_childDocuments_.review: WOW! Fobia St. Dinfna Hotel has been the biggest surprise for me this year.+ An intriguing  that unravels at a perfect pace and keeps you wanting to know more and push through the game. You will find lots of notes, some voice tapes and mini chapters used as flashbacks that complement the exposition of the main events, including some shocking twists!+  The  is, for the most part, polished and well crafted, reminiscent of Resident Evil 7, we have a first person perspective with shooting mechanics. You encounter a couple type of enemies, fight a few bosses and escape some chase sequences, giving the player some good challenges along their journey.The best songs happen during these intense moments, otherwise the soundtrack doesn’t stick out too much, serving just as background ambiences, not distracting but keeping the tension and atmosphere, combined with great sound effects such as rain, wind, thunders and more.+ The  is superb for the most part, the BIG focus of this games are . LOTS and LOTS of them, and I need to empathize this, because this is the factor that will determine if you will like this game or not. It reminded me a lot about Resident Evil 1 Remake, with just a slightly more complex map to navigate and with double the puzzles to solve. A huge variety of them, involving different mechanics and areas of knowledge for problem solving. You also have a special camera that can reveals different clues along the way.And now, onto the rough edges if this gem of a game. :- Some of the puzzles are OPTIONAL. A big number of them in fact. This creates a problem when the game presents to you new places, with new items and new puzzles to solve, to the point where you have a dozen of options BUT half of them will just give you ammunition or upgrade points. When mix all of those elements, the game can become REALLY confusing.- The items you can interact with should be highlighted or have a color code to help the player know what can they interact with or not. Since most of the areas uses the same palette, the environment blends with the key objects and you may miss some of them.- The flashlight can get a bit annoying when inspecting the surroundings. If you have it off, some objects will be very dark too see, but if you turn it on, it shines just in front of them, making it hard too see too. This is specially noticeable when inspecting inventory items or solving certain puzzles.- Some enemies can glitch on the terrain or have poor pathing.- Towards the last chapter of the game, I felt there was a bit too much of exposition, with lots of notes that break the pacing.Overall Im extremely satisfied with this title and will follow any future project of this team. Good job Brasil.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: While none of Fobia's flaws are bad enough to stop me from recommending it, there's still enough of them for me to say that I wouldn't buy this unless it goes on sale.The game hotel setting is fun to explore, and obviously takes cues from games like Resident Evil. The game also looks and runs great; I never had any performance issues. The puzzles range from so easy they may as well be pointless, so requiring to think for a while about the solution, so a bit hit and miss overall. The games length is good too, and I'd say most people will be able to beat it in about 8/9 hours. I don't like forcing players to beat the game three times to get all achievements, but there's lots to collect so there's some replay value.The game was not made in an English speaking country, but the translation is fine and the English voice acting is a little stilted but overall acceptable. The issue with the translation however, is that not all of the text is translated. Any documents you pick up, writing on walls etc. is still in Portuguese which breaks the immersion because everyone is speaking English and yet none of the in-game text is in that language. Yes, the text is translated to English when you click on it and there are a lot of languages to consider here (changing graphics isn't cheap) but it's a small thing that did annoy me.Navigation can be a problem because I felt the game often didn't prompt you where to go next, and the lack of a map that you could reference in the inventory led to me getting lost every now and again. The story line is basic and predictable, and I wasn't a fan of putting most of the actual story in the last 30 minutes. Still, the developers did make an effort on it and I appreciate putting documents and so on around to help you work out the story, so it's not all bad.Two problems I did have which really did impact my enjoyment were the boss battles and long walking sections. The boss battles are all terrible; you literally just shoot, move to another corner, shoot - rinse and repeat. They are boring as boring can be, and the same goes for the long walking sections. There's one in particular where you have to pick up pieces of a sphere, which went on for 45+ minutes and wasn't necessary. The entire section could have fit into a 2 minute cut scene.Overall, 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent horror survival. Would give this game 8/10 overall its really good with smaller flaws. Puzzles sort of OG resident evil. More than 1 weapon. Fantastic atmosphere and graphics (My old PC i-4770K GTX 1050Ti and 16 GB Ram runs this game excellent at 60+ fps on custom settings with only post process on LOW and Textures high and rest Medium)to make you feel like you are there. lots of nice things and lots of decayed bloody things. Voice acting is overall 6/10 its good sometimes and mostly meh but worth it. Although i love puzzles especially without spoilers and hints, this game does have a bunch of smaller (optional) puzzles that comes from nowhere with no reasoning.. Open a box with a key to find another locked thing inside with a code you have no idea how to find and wont try 1000+ combinations to brute force it. Or even when looking around everywhere you find something locked with a code that could be 5 digits or 8 and no clues around to figure out the codes. After a while when i got stuck or found things i wanted to open and simply had no idea where to go and no clues to go off of just search for answers on the net and get the codes instead of walking everywhere you have already been looking in the same places you already did. spare yourself that frustation if you want to keep a decent flow to the game. The game is not overly long its mostly retracing areas and puzzle solving that takes time. Love the implementation of a second reality sort of. (Mechanic ingame) For someone who likes an experience of horror shooter puzzle solving game this is really great. And no its not a shooter like the resident evil games where you prolly rack up 100 zombie kills or more. this is much calmer but still enemies where you dont expect and some times an enemy will spawn after you do certain things in areas you already completed and cleared of threats.Game does a lot of great things here. i got the game on sale for 12.49Euro and i am very strict with buying games especially if i dont deem them worth my time or money. this game is on the shorter end but worth the amount i payed for it. i think this game is anywhere from 8hours to 14hours depending on how stuck you are (puzzles) or the amount of times you go back and look for things. i am almost done with the game and i have spent 11hrs ingame playtime and i think 2 more hours to completion. i have tried to 100% the game as best i can on a first try. Pretty sure someone who wants to be done with the game faster and not 100% can complete the game in just about 8hrs IF you have the necessary codes etc ready from the net to progress without looking for clues yourself.Small tip for people who want to play this game without any guides or help. the very first "Metal Object" you get you need to save and keep in your inventory. Would suggest NOT discarding any items.. (The game has a marker on items like the newer resident evil when its done with its uses) You have a storage box to keep dumping items into with as far as i know unlimited storage. Excellent and i want more games like these and wouldnt mind 3x longer game with much more to explore and fixing some of the issues where it doesnt make any sense with puzzles. Only some have these issues the majority you have codes etc somewhere around the area.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I enjoyed Fobia. It's clear the team worked hard to create a tightly crafted experience, without too much bloat. Arguably the team didn't really get much wrong, the game functions well and there are few gripes on that front. But there are times where things feel a bit tedious/bland, which left me wondering if they needed to be a touch more ambitious.I ended up having to modify some of the game's config files, as there's an annoying vignette effect applied, without the option to switch it off. Additionally, the options to switch of motion blur,  depth of field etc would be greatly appreciated. I don't like having to "fix" games, because of annoying popular trends that many PC gamers don't subscribe to.In many cases, the torch made it hard to see items in the environment... I also found it hard to see some of the spider creatures due to how the torch works. Feels like the devs need to do a bit of a deeper dive into torch mechanics, to gain greater understanding on what makes a "good torch" in a video game.When it comes to the weapon upgrades, it's hard to know whether I should move on to the next area of the game or not. Having an obvious " 10 / X upgrades" count would defeat the point of secret hunting, but it could be handy to add some kind of "X out of X upgrade points" applied to individual weapons. That way, you could calculate the theoretical maximum number of upgrades you would need to upgrade all the weapons and deduce whether you're wise to search around before moving on to the next area.Another improvement would be to have some form of special highlight for memories or key items in the camera view, as the lighting/torch can make it hard to spot these items at times.Finally, unless I'm a complete idiot and missed something, I don't think there's a way to track the memory items you've collected. Due to the sections that drag on a bit, I'm not really motivated to go for a second playthrough, as I cant monitor what I've collected or the chapters/locations they were found in (and then deduce what I could be missing).The limited enemy variety and combat mechanics means the game feels like exploration was the priority. The claw enemies are relatively dumb and will charge towards you. Weapons lack feedback and the combat can be summarised as "shoot it until it's dead".Don't get me wrong, this is an indie team, so I know there are limitations on what they can manage within a reasonable time frame. But I didn't feel much reason to use anything but the pistol, outside of boss fights. Some form of limb destruction or block mechanic (e.g. Resident Evil 7), would have been appreciated.The initial flow of exploring areas of the hotel is great. But after a few scripted sequences, the main hall gets tedious to traverse, if you want to explore. There are also a number of locked gates that would benefit from the Dark Souls style "does not open from this side" approach, where you dont need to spend as much time navigating around long-sections to fully explore old areas.Complaints about traversal aside, the world has enough atmosphere to be enjoyable and the flow (outside of blocking off areas and few shortcuts), is decent. In fact, there were plenty more opportunities to add side rooms etc, but I get a sense that the devs were trying to be disciplined and not add too many areas.The ending felt somewhat abrupt and I don't really remember much of what happened during my time progressing through the game. Feel like there could be a few more narrative flags to help you take note of the key highlights, as your character explores through to the end. Felt like the story was just there to serve a function, but it didn't really matter beyond giving you a track to progress along.Outside of some of the cutscenes being tedious and the game dragging in places, I have little to complain about. Most of my complaints can be put down to inexperience and limited resources, where things just need some tweaking or additions to hit the mark.My advice to the devs - learn from this game, craft a sequel and I'm sure you'll knock it out of the park!

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, the game introduces an enjoyable and innovative camera mechanic that allows players to look back in time, enabling them to access new areas and solve puzzles. Speaking of puzzles, they are engaging and add to the overall experience. In many ways, this game feels like an immersive escape room adventure.Now, let's talk about the story. While it manages to be extremely interesting, it falls short in some aspects, leaving you feeling disappointed and confused. It seems like there are too many ideas forcefully blended together, resulting in logical conflicts. The ending, unfortunately, doesn't live up to expectations. However, despite these shortcomings, the journey itself is worthwhile and offers its own unique appeal.As for the gunplay, it's intentionally sluggish to reflect the main character's lack of weapons training. It doesn't feel out of place in the context of the game. That being said, there isn't much variation in combat, and the bosses could have been more memorable.Now, let's discuss the scares. While initially impactful, they lose their effect as you encounter them repeatedly. The lack of a genuine threat to the jump scares becomes apparent early on, diminishing their overall impact. This is a missed opportunity, considering their frequent usage throughout the game.Regarding the animations, they may not be visually appealing, but fortunately, they don't detract from the overall experience or break immersion.In terms of value, the game is priced reasonably, but I would recommend waiting for a sale to make it an even better deal. While it has its flaws, it still offers an engaging and innovative gameplay experience that's worth exploring.Overall, this game presents interesting mechanics, engaging puzzles, and an immersive escape room atmosphere. Just keep in mind its narrative shortcomings, combat limitations, and diminishing scare factor. Patience for a sale would be wise, but don't let these drawbacks deter you from enjoying the worthwhile journey it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game from an indie developer. A love letter to Resident Evil games, especially the later ones (first-person perspective). However, it isn't about how many zombies you can put down in 5 hours; it is more about exploring the surroundings and solving puzzles with some action and chase (similar to Nemesis or Mr. X from RE games) sequences here and there. There are two types of enemies (excluding bosses) and four types of weapons (pistol, shotgun, sub-machinegun, and revolver). The atmosphere is awesome. It really feels like there is no one to help you out, and you have to push forward on your own while these creatures lurk somewhere in the dark corners of the hotel—or is it just in your mind?Though, there was one thing I was disappointed about: the ending(s). I was like, "What? That is all?"All in all, I do recommend this game, especially for players who enjoy exploring and solving puzzles. Will you survive the phobia of Fobia St. Dinfna Hotel?

_childDocuments_.review: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel is a flawed, but pretty good horror, adventure game, so it’s time for the story. The St. Dinfna Hotel a beautiful place to stay in the city of Treze Trilhas, it was founded by a man named Christopher built over an abandoned mind that due to a collapse that killed 20 miners was shut down and the hotel built in its place or is that what really happened? After that incident Treze Trilhas has been plagued by by mystery after mystery and in the epicenter of all that is a mysterious organization called The Sacred Trail, many a reporter and investigator has tried to expose the truth and one amateur journalist Roberto Leite Lopes travels there to do just that, but finding the truth may put Roberto in a nightmare he couldn't possibly imagine, but can he do it can he survive and expose the truth or will his stay at the hotel be his permanent resting place.Alright the likes, the atmosphere is really good definitely helps set the mood for the scares as you wander around the decrepit burning Hotel dreading what could be around the corner, even if you've played the game and know what will happen the atmosphere is still quite strong. The graphics are really good and quite detailed with a nice use of color and shadow, the details are good from burning rubble to a broken sink still spewing water all of it is quite detailed to make the hotel look as decrepit and destroyed as possible.The levels in the game are very good if you've played classic Resident Evil games you know what you’re in for stuck in this big place where you have to explore, solve puzzles and then you get to like a hidden lab or something, but there's lots of detail in the levels that make it feel like it used to be a real hotel.The enemies and bosses are really good with interesting designs, especially the bosses each one having their own unique look probably the best boss would be this stalker/Mr X like character his design was quite intimidating and interesting wearing a gas mask, having this red flashlight that's hooked to his belt and having a giant claw like he's a tyrant, again it was quite an intimidating and interesting design.The music for the game was very good plenty of great soundtracks to listen too, the puzzles for the game were for the most part pretty good; a lot of them having a pretty good balance of hard but not impossible to figure out if you've read the notes and paid attention to your environment, although some of them could be quite vague later on. The story for the game is okayish at best a lot of it can be quite confusing, but there were some parts of the story I did like, especially when it came to the notes and diary entries.Now as you know I'm a fan of notes in games and this game has plenty of notes to read, also our main character keeps a diary and after certain point he will write his thoughts down. The notes and diary pages helped to expand the world making it feel real, especially reading the notes that belonged to the people that were killed in the hotel making it feel tragic.There's also collectibles which was nice as that adds a little extra to the story, but you can only look at the Collectibles in extra mode after beating the game for the first time. New Game Plus was fun I especially liked when you upgrade your weapon to its maximum you get infinite ammunition that helps with getting the last three achievements of the game.The characters in the game were good though the design can be a tiny bit stiff when it comes to faces, but it was not bad. I liked the main character Roberto he had a nice every man feel to him especially when dealing with the craziness, the story also hence that there could be more to him than what meets the eye though. The voice acting was okay it served the game well it's not anything to write home about though, but was okay and served the game's purpose.So is this game scary? Yes the game has really good scares, the game does a good job in balancing jump scares with intense and oppressive atmosphere and even if you've played the game three times like I have you can still get creeped out and jump. Alright the dislikes, the story for the game is pretty confusing I'll be spoiling it, but the bottom line is I just really didn't get it maybe it'll be explain better in a sequel. Some of the game’s puzzles can be kind of too vague, for the most part the puzzles had a good balance of difficulty which all it took was doing some exploration, reading notes and picking up certain items, but I feel as the game got closer to the end the puzzles got a little too vague.I also encountered a few bugs in the game one bug was that during the final level the game The Underground Laboratory there was a safe that wouldn't open even though I put the code in correctly.I also wish the game had a few more unique enemies in the game there's only two types of enemies the zombie looking creatures and these bugs, I would have liked a few more unique enemies also maybe two more bosses.And on these bug enemies I have to tell you that I really hated them they were so annoying especially when you're trying to get the achievement that requires you to beat the game without getting hurt, they are especially a pain in the ass at the final segment of the game were you trying to unlock this huge metal door and you can't see the bugs that well to kill them. I also would have liked a map for the game because it was quite easy to get lost.Now even with its flaws Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel is a pretty good horror, adventure game, it has a really good atmosphere, really good enemies and bosses and really good scares. So do I recommend this game? Yeah despite its flaws it's still a pretty solid horror game I just hope when they make a sequel they explain a lot of the things that I was confused about in the story. I also want to thank my good friend for giving me this video game thank you you snoot boopping kit.

_childDocuments_.review: Fobia St. Dinfna Hotel is survival horror game that is similar to the more recent first person resident evil games. You play as Roberto, a journalist who is trying to figure out the mystery and past of the hotel but end up being trapped in its nightmare.The story itself while decent can be very confusing. You don’t always understand what is happening or why you need to do tasks. You don’t really get the full picture of what is going on until the very end of the game. Even then it doesn’t really make sense. It’s not a bad story. It could just be told better with clearer understanding.The voice acting is passable. It’s not terrible buts it’s not great either. Some of the more intense scenes have the voice acting sound barely threatening or when injured you don’t sound injured or hurt. A lot of the time it sounds like they are reading straight off the script with no idea of what the scene should sound like. The graphics, sounds, and atmosphere are good. It always feels like something is going to happen or waiting for you around the next corner. You never really know when something was going to happen.The enemies honestly suck. The standard enemies in the games have terrible AI and will just stand there most of the time and let you shoot them. They have a lunge attack but most of the time they miss you, and they are weak and do barely any damage to you. You can take 6-8 hits before being in the red zone, so there no real danger of feeling like you could die.The bosses were terribly easy. One boss you could super cheese it and just stand in a corner and for whatever reason the boss would not go into they corner so you could just blast it with ammo until it was dead. The final boss was also easy.The puzzles…..oh man there’s so freaking many. Some of them drove me insane with the solution and constant running across the hotel over multiple floors to find something only to have to run all over the place again for its final solution. Not all the puzzles are mandatory to complete the game which is nice if you just want to advance the story. However you would never know that because the game doesn’t have a quest tracker.The game has its flaws for sure. It’s a bit easy in combat and a little over the top with its puzzle solutions, but I liked it and thought it was worth the time to complete it. I played this on a steam deck on mostly medium settings with max textures. The game ran at 60fps almost all the time.7.5

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough and boy am I glad I played this game. Sure it ain't super long and the controls can be a bit wonky but the rest is amazing. For such a small team they managed to make a game with fun puzzles, good story and fun gameplay. This resident evil like game is amazing if you need something new to play and it puts many recent AAA games to shame by actually making a fun game.Though the translation is excellent for most parts even for the voice acting, there are some places where it might be absent. The game is namely from Brazil and so some parts like clues can be confusing due to missing a slight translation. Example (not a real one to avoid spoilers): 01 D 02 E 03 D (D from direita = right, E from escquerda = left). On most notes in game you will have a translation of the text though the text on the assets in game will be Portuguese. The translation will be a transcription of the text but on clues that don't contain words but code it doesn't translate them. So bear that in mind when doing some puzzles. Most of them aren't super difficult but they do require you to find the right documents with clues to solve. The mechanic of having two different timelines which can be access by either looking through the camera or not is super cool. This does make it easy however to skip a clue and get stuck so be sure to go full on Sherlock Holmes and find the documents and items needed for the puzzles. ;)I definitely recommend it if you love survival horror games and it even has some nice features for those who wish to change the difficulty (adaptive ammo drops during boss fights or a journal which tells you what the objective is at that moment) I played with the adaptive ammo because I know I'm to trigger happy for my own good sometimes but left the objective disabled for maximum immersion. I'm just glad they added features like that. Not even all AAA games have that even though there are good examples of those that have it like Shadow of the tomb raider where some aspects of the game can be modified to suit your play style.All in all this game is really well made and a must play for those looking for a new survival horror game

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game as much as I could to garner a decent review. I aimed during my play-through to really try to get all the optional puzzles I could and collect all the memories (if possible) and so on. I did not accomplish this, but I'll get into that later. I'll preface this first since I am a very critical person when it comes to horror games - I do recommend that you play this game at least once. Although I did not enjoy it very much, I can easily see why others could play it over and over.The game overall...is a snore. I really tried to capture the plot and it's details as much as I could. The story was just dull and not well thought out. After about 11 hours of exploration and taking my time gathering intel on what really happened at the hotel and in the past, I was so exhausted trying to keep up I ended up not caring anymore. The plot became so convoluted and mismanaged that by the time I got my revenge on a certain stalker I had no clue what any of it meant. The camera being a gateway to another realm is intuitive!...but makes the game drag on literally twice as long as it should since you will find yourself going back and forth between the 8 (technically 9) floors of the hotel every few minutes - going from the 2nd to the 4th, to the 6th, to the 5th, to the.........you get the point. In fact, it made the game feel frustrating at times knowing that an item you need is in the alternate dimension, and you simply may have passed over it 20 minutes ago with the slightest hint that there MAY be an area where you were that required the camera. Yes, it is harder than RE puzzles, but to the extent that it is just intolerable (although this is an opinion) just makes me WANT to play classic RE games instead. The camera movement is awkward as well, aiming at enemies feels like you're dealing with Parkinson's disease as you aim at an abomination 2 feet ahead. The running is very slow, your character simply speed walks rather than actual running which makes exploration feel like it is going in slow motion. However, this I could look over simply because, honestly, the game is graphically gorgeous. Although the enemy models are a bit...questionable in design, the hotel itself and all it's areas are unique, packed with secrets, and amazing to observe and explore.The enemy AI is also decent, I never felt under powered or over powered (until the end of the game where you can 1 shot most enemies). They also can give a good jump scare every now and then. HOWEVER, and this is a big game no-no, all the bosses are absolute bullet sponges. The bosses are literally the shamwow of taking bullets to the head and still going like it all only dealt 15% damage total to them. In fact, I ran out of ammo so often and frequently fighting these things, I turned on the ammo cheat option for use during boss fights, and even then it was barely fun at best. The boss AI is also super aggressive at all times, so pile that on to the next thing - very small boss arenas - and it all combines into a huge angering mess that takes up 15 minutes of your life, or more if you die. My favorite sections of the game was when you went into the past and explored. Those moments were pretty scary at times, felt intense, and the running sequences felt great. Even the puzzles in the past felt more applicable to the game's overall theme - and they were far more memorable than everything else for me in the present timeline other than the cube puzzle.There is a huge benefit to beating the game, which is NG+ where you can eventually get infinite ammo upon fully upgrading weapons, which is beneficial if going for the other achievements that you really need infinite ammo for (no damage runs, no saves, or no healing for example). That being said, there really isn't much else to replay the game for. I certainly would not play it again for the voice acting which is miserable unless you're playing the past events in my opinion. Overall, the game is scary, and the puzzle are unique, with a beautiful environment to add on, but nothing about this game will pull you in (at least for me it didn't). I'd really only recommend this game if you really are into puzzles and exploration. My rating would be somewhere between a 6 or 7 out of 10. I would definitely like to see a sequel or just another game made by the same development team, just fixing all of these issues mentioned if they intend to do so.

_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming little mess of a game, and I love every second of it. Sure, you get a bug here or there, but it's actually rewarding to play. The game doesn't like to hold your hand. What it does like to do is to put you in a tight situation and go "gotem". But don't worry, when you run out of ammo casually dig through every single hotel drawer while squinting one eye. In the far back corner of the cabinet are maybe like 2 bullets. I do love this mechanic though. The game itself is very inspired by modern Resident Evil and P.T. among other things (including a silly pyramid head reference). That's not a bad thing in my opinion. Especially when you can feel the heart put into the game. This game was clearly made by big survival horror fan, and it really shows. Thanks for the cool game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: There's a certain amount of charm in this first person survival horror title but it is sorely lacking in some quality of life design. - The character moves like a drunk battlemech wading through tar. There are moments when your legs are trying to orient to your upper body position, especially when crouching (this all seems like something that shouldn't even be a consideration but it is) that makes movement feel very clumsy.  - There's a delay after certain commands and animations where your character will not respond to further similar prompts such as weapon switching. You might only want to pull the camera out for a quick look into the otherworld to open a path but you are locked into that choice for a while which gets pretty egregious in combat.- A canned animation plays when switching weapons. This is something that experienced devs do once when equipping a weapon for the first time and never again, you don't need to see it more than once and it gets in the way in combat when trying to use the right weapon for an encounter.- Unskippable cutscenes, very annoying when you have to keep retrying bosses aiming for the no damage achievement. EDIT: You can skip them in NG+ making no hit runs better suited for NG+, however if you were having difficulty with an encounter on NG you'd still have to watch the cutscene when reloading a save.- No load save button in pause menu, have to quit to main menu to load (again most annoying for above achievement).- There's a dedicated button for using the camera but you also have to have it equipped to a quick slot otherwise the camera button doesn't work so you essentially have to have it on 2 hotkeys. There are 4 quick slots and 4 weapons, plus the camera makes 5 things in need of quick slots; the inventory expands so it can hold all these which makes this oversight questionable.As I said there is charm here, the hotel makes for an interesting enough location to explore especially with the alternate versions of rooms when viewed through the camera. The premise is mysterious enough to keep me interested. Just be aware of the rough edges.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of plot and story, Fobia is pretty nonsense. What it does have in spades though, is mood and atmosphere. You basically wake up in this dilapidated hotel, and have to work your way through rooms and floors, simetimes in unorthodox ways. Almost like a maze, where you need to backtrack to unlock previously locked doors and passages. Very often accompanied by puzzles that span the layout of the whole hotel -- through  as well. Despite this, there’s always a sense of momentum and discovery here, which is great. It’s sort of what solidifies it in the “Resident Evil” genre or horror games. That, and all the monsters of course. It’s the type of experience where you’re all alone, locked doors are plentiful, and you’re only given a faint lifeline of health supplies and ammunition to keep you going.It’s pretty fun as far as these types of games go. And one with a surprising amount of  puzzles too, which I find very exciting. It certainly adds to the replayability of it.Recommended, if you enjoy horror games akin to the newer Resident Evil titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and have an RE sized itch that most games can't seem to scratch, you'll enjoy your time at St Dinfna Hotel well enough. RE7 style with enough differences to make it stand on its own. Combat is fine, there's some decent boss battles and an upgrade system to work through. There isn't a map, but it's possible that the game would have been too easy with one. You'll learn you way around pretty quick regardless. Only parts that really stood out to me as not-so-enjoyable were a couple of short flashback portions that served as a kind of interlude to the main story. I'm the type of guy that loves to wait for a sale on everything, but if you don't mind paying full price the game is long enough that you'll get your monies worth. Play the demo if you're really on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: A fun homage to resident evil games and interesting in its own right.  Plays very similarly to RE7 with a medley of puzzles and backtracking through a giant hotel.  There aren't a lot of monster types or monsters in general, but ammo is scarce so you need to be accurate if you engage and kill them.  There's several boss encounters as well, but basically the meat of the game is puzzles, story, and interacting with your camera that gives you clues that can't be seen normally.  A solid B+, quite enjoyable and worth your play.  The story is interesting but the end is confusing, so if you're not the type to let that ruin your day, I'd definitely recommend a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in all good faith give this a bad review. However, there's a reason I open with that statement on a positive review.The game has so much potential and is so close to being a really solid game. But it falls short due to bugs and fairly underwhelming gameplay/story.I put 14 hrs into the game, so I absolutely gave it a fair shake. Even did most of the side content.TBH the only reason I'm giving this a good review is because the potential it does have gives me hope the dev/devs will make something better in the future and I think they deserve support. I love these kinds of games so the more the merrier imo. Again this comes very close to being really solid.The main issue with this game is it's story (one of the worst/uninteresting I've ever encountered) and the fact the game wears it's influences on it's sleeves (Bioshock/Resident Evil for example) but doesn't come even close to being as solid as the games that inspired it.I don't mean this to be rude if the dev/devs reads this, I enjoyed the game enough to leave positive feedback but it all honesty needs a lot of work.This feels like a "practice makes perfect" scenario for the dev/devs and I look forward to their future releases.Having that said, the game is not worth full price $30. It plays closer to a $20 game imo.I'm torn between 3/5 and 4/5 for recognized potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Without being too technical I would say I had fun playing this. I liked the puzzles and the camera mechanics. I would have loved to see more of the camera bit (There probably was and is quite possible I missed them :P). It had elements from silent hill and resident evil that we all have loved. Ending could've been better but for me it was worth the time and efforts. It's not difficult and liked not having too many jump scares. They tried putting effort in the hotel ambience and I liked it. If you're not too picky on games and would like to play a decent game with puzzles and horror go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: If you've run out of old school Resident Evil to play then this is a solid alternative to get your fix.The exploration was a lot of fun. Progressively unlocking areas of the hotel and finding key items to unlock new doors and passageways in an intertwined map I just wish it had a way to track which areas you'd been to or areas requiring further exploration as it can become quite cumbersome to remember where you need to use your key items to progress. As well as finding where items are if you've missed something important which happens surprisingly frequently when you have 2 different dimensions you can switch between.I enjoyed the puzzles. They weren't too complicated and there was a decent amount of variety.The combat was basic but passable. The guns felt okay to use although the enemy variety was lacking. The game sets up the idea of shooting a specific spot on one of the enemy types although I very rarely found that it made a difference. The second enemy type caught me off guard almost every time to the point it was less of a threat and more of a constant jump scare.The story felt like it was trying to do a lot and I could piece together a large majority of it although it also felt like it was trying to do too much to the point that it's quite easy to lose track of all the plot threads which overall left me quite confused by the end. The game provides upgrades through upgrade points which you can spend on making your weapons better although I found that this wasn't a particularly engaging way to get these upgrades. I personally would have preferred some attachments which would have been dotted around the map instead. The game sometimes rewards you with context for the story through some puzzles although this can be quite an anticlimactic result and could have been more engaging with this system.As far as it goes this game is a good modernised old school style survival horror game that is surprisingly high quality when taking into account that this is an indie game of this scope. It's worth your time if you love games in this genre as games that are designed like this are few and far between.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. You can clearly see the 5+ years long of effort the developers put into this. I mean, the game has RTX but even though I'm running it in my GTX 1050ti, it still has very realistic (and impressive) reflections AND it runs on 70+ FPS with High Graphics configuration, which is absolutely insane, the game is so greatly optimized. Plus you notice a lot of details in the animations and graphics that lots of triple A games lack... largely.Storywise, i was actually very surprised by how complex and good it was. Gameplay was fantastic, puzzles were great, straight outta RE but with its own touch.Finally, as a Brazilian, thanks for representing our place in the game industry so beautifully, Pulsatrix! You might as well have marked our spot and shown how underrated we actually are. Thanks for making this game and congrats on the awesome work you put into it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant survival horror. Great graphics, level design and puzzles. The bits set in the past weren't as good as those set in the present, and I would have liked to see the camera utilised a bit more, but in my opinion this feels more like Resident Evil than RE 4-6 & 8. Not that they weren't good games, they just didn't feel like Resi games to me. Definitely worth a playthrough or two and hopefully the first of several Fobia games.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is certainly a rip off of the first person Resident Evil games, it does it well enough to where it is not completely irrelevant. The story may not make much sense, the puzzles may be unintuitive, and the gameplay may be repetitive and boring, but underneath all those issues is a game with fun exploration that is sure to please horror fans craving another first person Resident Evil experience, especially for the price. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who`s always enjoyed the exploration and puzzles in Survival Horror-games most, I really dig this game. It´s impressive how a rather small development team was able to pull this off, to recreate some of the biggest strengths of classic Resident Evil and Silent Hill and also implement some "modern" aspects of recent RE-games (especially RE7 and REmake 2). It certainly is not super scary (think of FEAR with a little bit of RE and Silent Hill) and the action is underwhelming for the most part (which isn`t that big of a deal as combat takes a backseat here anyway) but it gets a lot of things right and is an overall quite polished game. The PC version also deserves praise: the game ran almost flawless (60FPS for like 99% of the time, no microstuttering) in native 4k with maxed out settings (except Raytracing) on my rig (i7 4790k, RTX 3070, 16GB RAM). It also features DLSS btw.If you like classic Survival Horror-games and their focus on exploration, you should really check this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. It has a good story, cool creatures to kill, it's a survival horror and it reminds me of games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill.Would love to see this studio make a game like this with a story like Dino Crisis. They are really good with atmosphere and tension.Oh and totally worth the price tag for the effort put in.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Overall awesome game. Graphics are very nice and the game runs great (at least it did for me). Atmosphere is spot on and brings a lot to the game. Combat is good but not amazing, not many enemy types unfortunately. Your arsenal is pretty standard too; pistol, shotgun, machine gun and magnum. The guns are satisfying to use however and can be upgraded. The weapons are also nicely animated. Exploration, backtracking and puzzle solving are king in this game; so if you're looking for an action heavy game this may not be for you. There are tons of side puzzles not necessary for story progression that reward you with extra lore or supplies. The music was ok, not amazing but not horrible. The rest of the sound design is very good though. Voice acting is decent but has a nice amount of cheese to it. The story is appropriately cheesy and involves cults, old gods, weird science and ghostly phenomena.I'd definitely recommend it if you want an RE7/8 like experience with a bit of indie jank. Be sure to try the demo before you buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: A visually very atmospheric and impressive game. Everything in classic horror is offered what your heart desires. Raindrops hit the windows, the wood in the walls creaks ominously, simply wonderful. There are a lot of puzzles in the game, which I think is fantastic. Not a stupid nonstop jump scare, but also something for the brain. I love it. The first person gameplay is one of the best I've seen. The headbobbing doesn't bother me at all either, it rather gives me the feeling of being the actor in the game myself. The game is full of lovingly developed details, be it in the game mechanics or in the composition of the setting. In my opinion, the graphics and the atmosphere of this game could not be better. In any case, for me, Fobia is the biggest surprise of this year and one of the most beautiful horror games I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: A great game. I hope that a part 2 developed, but I hope they focus more on the factor horror and survival, because the game focuses on heavily on puzzles, and i do not mean that it is difficult, but the large number of puzzles does not create a balance with the factor of horror and survival. the game lacks a map with the player i know that maps are spread on all floors the hotel on the walls but as a player that you can open anytime you need. it may not be a big negative for some because looking the map on the walls makes the player immerse more in the game world.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just about done with the game. I enjoyed it until towards the end where I believe I am now. These are the things that have me on the fence:- Control Response: I'm playing with keyboard and mouse and there are times when I click my quick keys and it doesn't switch weapons or times where I'm pressing the left mouse to shoot and nothing happens.- Reload time, you can improve it but if it's less than level 3 I guess, there doesn't seem to be much of a difference - It does get less scary and more tedious when you're just running around blind trying to figure out where to go because there is no map you're carrying around as you do in *almost* every survival horror game (I know and have played the few that have no map or document saving) A map would certainly be helpful with the size of the levels you will go through for a huge chunk of the game.- the repetition of scares takes the fun out of the whole thing. I did enjoy to a point the graphics although I think with my settings I have to have, there's a strange black screen texture around the shadows. I enjoy some of the story so far, but I don't know what or why one enemy showed up randomly with no explanation  of weak spots or even what it is. _childDocuments_.review: First two hours gameplay: So far  I played about two hours of game and really liked it. I think creator of this game did a good job of story telling and keeping the mystery of the game well contained and interesting that forces you to keep playing it and find out what happened in this hotel.So far I mainly was exploring area and solving some puzzles and encountered couple of enemies. Puzzles haven't been that hard so far but they are unique and fresh. Enemies that I encountered also weren't hard to kill or avoid. There were couple of jump scares that got me but other than that the environment of hotel is very spooky that you always feel anxious in the game.The camera at the same time adds another dimension to this game that is really cool and unique but also makes it more scary to explore and find hidden stuff and clues, I really liked the idea. One downside to me was number of documents that I had to read to understand what is happened in this hotel and story of the game. Usually that's the less interesting part for me in any game to read documents to understand the story. But it's understandable for small indie teams to do this and these docs are optional to read but in order to fully understand story I recommend reading them.Visuals are really good and performance wise I just encountered some hiccups on loading new environment but other that that everything was smooth, played on cinematic level with raytracing and dlss on.I am going to recommend this game so far based on first two hours of my gameplay, will update if anything changes later, but so far so good and creator of this game did a really good job :)

about_the_game: Humanity has been destroyed - and it's up to Gori, along with his deadly but wise-cracking sentient hoverboard, F.R.A.N.K, and morose A.I companion, CH1-P, to slay the evil Adorable Army with lethal combos. Fuelled by insatiable demand, 'Cool-Toyz Inc.' created 'Ultra Pets'. The ultimate companions that never hunger, never require bathroom breaks and are impervious to the ravages of time. Little did anyone expect the mutation that transformed these perfect pets into twisted toys straight from your nightmares, hell-bent on wiping out mankind. Master explosive weaponry and devastating combos in an epic battle to prevent the Adorable Army from conquering the galaxy, and rescue Professor Y, their missing creator and only human who showed Gori and his friends love. Push your combat and platforming skills to the limits as you fight your way through twisted landscapes filled with environmental hazards, razor-sharp adult humour and a bone-crunching, pulse-pounding soundtrack. One of the last prototype synthetic pets, smuggled out of Cool-Toyz Inc before destruction, Gori is cute, cuddly, yet extremely deadly. Save the galaxy with a team of the unlikeliest heroes, from F.R.A.N.K and CH1-P to a host of unexpected allies, with a script packed with heart and adult humour that’s as razor-sharp as F.R.A.N.K’s blades! Battle the blood-thirsty hordes of the Adorable Army in fast-paced combat where your hoverboard is your weapon! Power slide, grind and spin to cause MAXIMUM carnage and high combo scores. Paint the town red with F.R.A.N.K’s blades as you slice and dice with gratuitous amounts of dismemberment - body horror and the most twisted toy designs you’ve ever seen! This cat has claws… and a devastating arsenal of explosives, razor-sharp weaponry and unlockable moves to lay waste to the Adorable Army in the most brutal and stylish way possible! From neon-drenched city streets and toy factories awash with deadly toxins, to twisted carnivals and the insides of arcade machines - each level is filled with lethal environmental hazards and mutated toys to push your combat and platforming skills to their limits. Use your extreme hoverboard parkour skills to explore every corner of the level for collectables that unlock radical new filters, outfits and fur-styles for Gori! Skate and slay out to an original bone-crunching soundtrack, with 48 songs bursting with energy across multiple genres. Play as a badass cat with a team of unlikely heroes Battle blood-thirsty hordes of mutated toys Explore multiple levels filled with lethal environmental hazards Master a devastating arsenal of explosives, razor-sharp weaponry and unlockable moves Use your extreme hoverboard parkour skills to explore every corner of the level for collectables Turn the town red with F.R.A.N.K’s blades as you slice and dice Skate and slay out to an original bone-crunching soundtrack The game contains foul language, excessive gore, and other adult content! Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like me, miss this kind of games from the xbox 360/ps3 era, this game is probably for you. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Gori is a comedic, fluffy gorefest that is a steal for 20 bucks. It will keep your adrenaline rushing for 6 hours as you decapitate unicorns (and other awkward creatures) on a claptrap hoverboard. And, who doesn't like cats? Gori made me realize how much I missed the golden late PS2 to early PS3 era of hack-and-slash games. Just like them, Gori is a very gamey game that is straightforward—simple yet effective. So if you’re looking for something like Alice: Madness Returns, No More Heroes, or Lollipop Chainsaw, you’ve found it here. Of course, escaping comparisons and innuendos to Devil May Cry would be impossible, as you chain together autistic combos.I've seen some efforts trying to describe what Gori is. Well, it’s exactly what its main menu soundtrack says: it’s a cat on a hoverboard fighting unicorns (humming). Or I’ll do you one better: it is the collective fever dream of Dante, Alice (from Madness Returns), Razputin (from Psychonauts), Tony Hawk, and the cat from Stray who met in a bar and got high together. Very effectively. Gori is a self-aware and lighthearted game with outlandish jokes, wordplay, and pop culture references. Sometimes it’s outright ridiculous and over the top. What’s better than a talking hoverboard? A cursing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hoverboard! Or for that matter, a Goldfish with a German accent claims to be a human. All with a Borderlands-esque character introduction screen.The game is incredibly fluid and easy to pick up, though it can be slightly challenging if you aim for 100% completion. The whole game feels ambitious but knows its scope very well, which is what makes it so good. Divided into eight chapters, you’re looking at approximately six hours of gameplay. I’d argue Gori plays it safe and executes nearly every hack-and-slash trick in the playbook, but it does them just fine. Without inventing anything groundbreaking, it immediately becomes a must-play.It’s a very artsy game, not only in its cyberpunk setting. It changes the atmosphere and constantly spices things up. There are levels that are eerie, giving those Alice: Madness Returns vibes. It runs very well and looks dope. Every scenery, every execution goods a make content for the photo mode. The soundtrack is packed with bangers, so it’s impossible not to agree that the composer snapped. Combined together with the art team they are a completely unstoppable psychedelic force. The gameplay doesn’t vary much as you progress further, but you can easily notice character progression in both aesthetics (visual changes to your hoverboard & weapons) and in terms of power as you go on an uninterrupted slaughterfest. The level design, once again, is simple but very effective, mostly designed to keep the flow going. The hoverboard is an OP ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that lets you wallrun, glide, and navigate the level through boosting. It keeps you busy and entertained throughout the entire game. Bosses are gimmicky but ultimately fun.I imagine Gori will find its own niche, but currently, I’d say it’s a bit underrated and I wish it could go mainstream. It’s hard not to love Gori, and while there are things I wish were better (such as combo chains, as you can spam your way out with fuel attacks), as a complete package, it’s better than the sum of its parts and it’s a blast.P.S. I also adore the skins and the fact that they give some of them for free. After seeing that, I purchased all the others to support the game. They’re all sick.★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast. It captures a feeling that I feel has been lost in the seriousness of a lot of modern games. It is chaotic and silly in the best ways. Slicing, smashing, and blowing up unicorns while riding a sentient hoverboard is a joy. Combat is brutal and gory with the bodies of severed unicorns flying about as you grind and boost on the hoverboard. On top of that, the game has a combat ranking system that encourages you to be quick and chain everything together. It's not a very long game, but the wild ride is worth it. I only wish the game had more upgrades to add to the chaos and put more variety into the gameplay. Right now, once you hit an early level, gameplay kind of stops evolving. The enemies and how you handle them does change, but the tools you use dispatch them doesn't. Additionally, I kept waiting for a new gadget or weapon or mechanic that sadly never came. But, hey, that's what sequels are for. All of this aside, I highly recommend giving the demo if you are interested. I know that I was very pleasantly surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: Not usually an action combat player, but this has me hooked! I can't explain in text how satisfying the combat is, but its amazing. The feeling of getting a great combo while slashing and skating through the air keeps me want to play more! Ch1-P is probably my favorite character, after Gori, I relate to his mood too much. Also, the cute purring had me from the beginning.. <3 Will recommend to my friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Gori: Cuddly Carnage

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I don't think I've ever seen a game that combines traversal with combat as well as this one.  Seriously.  Second, this game is heavily based on video games from the 2000s, both stylistically, mechanically, and thematically. The hover board sounds like what is instantly recognizable as a legally distinct impression of GIR from Invader Zim.  There's a pizza place called Tsunami but the S is so stylized it reads "Tunami" with sounds like Toonami. Unlike the games this one is based on, the combat actually works.  There are so many games from the 2000s that had cool level designs (like this game) fun characters (like this game) but where the combat just totally feel apart (I'm looking at you, Psychonauts.) but the combat here is excellent.  It did crash on me during the boss fight for the second level, but the game just released a few days ago (at time of review) so it's probably something they'll fix.

_childDocuments_.review: Gori is a really fun hack and slash game. This is literally Deadpool (2013) reborn. Its like Deadpool and Doom had a baby with Stray xD The game is pretty small-ish. There are only 2 weapons in the entire game; The slashing skateboard and a rocket launcher (also in the skateboard). Maybe an addition of an smg or something else would've been more fun (just a suggestion), so yeah it can get a little repetitive. But yes regardless of all that it does cure that itch to 'rip & tear until it is done' :PAlso do take the light sensitivity warning seriously. This game will feel like an acid trip.I would do crimes against Humanity for Gori xDAs for the pricing, I do think its great (atleast the regional pricing in my case)Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: (basically spoiler free review)I'm 30. I've dealt with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This is far from it. _childDocuments_.review: I feel like the best way to describe this game is "Alice: Madness Returns" for the current generation. We aren't getting Alice 3, but I feel like this taps into a lot of elements that made us want Alice 3. The combat and platforming are all very satisfying, though the combat doesn't truly wake up until about 1/3 of the way through but that's common in action games to keep ramping things up. The music is awesome, the graphics are great, the vibes are bizarre. The raytracing is a nice bonus, the game uses it liberally and it adds heavily to the color saturated neon look. HDR also looks great. Complaints:-This is the maiden voyage game for my new 4090 and while it runs great at 4k max settings with ray tracing locked at 120hz, there is still some obvious shader compile hitching that happens when transitioning over greater areas. Be nice if there was a more complete shader compilation than the brief one at the beginning, or some other solution.-My game crashed once so far, during Stage 2 boss.-Twice now random buttons on my controller (8BitDo Ultimate 2.4ghz) just stopped responding for a while, like 15-30 seconds. Weird. -The master audio slider doesn't seem to be acting as a master volume slider, but instead some type of dynamic range compression. The game sounded a bit thin and lifeless at first, but once set to 100% (default is 50%) the audio woke right up despite not actually getting louder. Game sounds fantastic actually, so it's weird to see this as the default option as it really stifles the audio presentation.-The option to adjust HUD transparency would be nice, though at least it can be turned off. It was kicking the auto brightness leveling in on my Sony OLED hard which could have been curbed by letting me adjust it to 20% opacity or something. Once you turn the HUD off though the crosshair goes away too which makes aiming rockets difficult. Luckily my display has the option to add a little dot crosshair, but the overall HUD toggle should not disable the crosshair or at least make them separate toggles. This games HUD is going to cause auto brightness leveling to kick in on any OLED display except maybe QD-OLED, so there should be more fine grain options to address this.-The HDR looked great, but some basic in game calibration settings should be present still.-The final boss isn't that cool and I wish there was an extra stage or twoNeutral on it personally, but the story is a schizo post. So make of that what you will.I'm surprised they are asking so little for the game. IMO charging $40 would have been more in line with the game. It's rare I like a thing so much I suggest you take more of my money. This is one of the best action games in years and, once you get settled in, actually frequently pretty damn funny. Maybe not belly laugh funny but what game really is? Bottom line you'll enjoy being in this world. This game is one patch away from being purrfect.Also you get to be a cat on a hoverboard who violently kills things.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just good fun. The characters, setting and dialogue are all awesome and pretty funny. The rail grinding I wish was a bit more forgiving, sometimes I press the grind button just a second too late, even though it feels like I'm above the rail. _childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully gory, cute and fun, retro adventure. A thing I didn't really expect to see nor play.++PROS+++ Gameplay is smooth and Gori controls very naturally on his board.  Light platforming and relatively easy, albeit repetitive combat keeps you engaged throughout alongside a good set of weapons that diversify combat further without overcomplicating the game. While it is no Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, it's a fine action game in it's own right.+ Plot is told via comics and some light cutscenes which I enjoyed but again, it's very simple. The world isn't very expanded and nothing really feels explored in it's entirety. The worst part is that the final boss IS hinted at but isn't present until the very last level which sucks. This isn't a condemnation either, it's just that I loved the world enough to want to see MORE of it which is good.+ Distinctly retro style mixed with some hard music makes this game feel like a beat-em-up Killing Floor, where you're just mopping up dozens of enemies effortlessly at a time.--CONS--- Game is rather short even at 100%, minus the difficulty achievement. 7 true levels, with an 8th boss level. There's also roughly 2 extra challenge levels per level but they are real quick and have pitifully low gold star requirements.- The game isn't very difficult at all and even on what I thought to be normal mode I was getting nearly every gold star and beating every combo requirement without trying. Wish some of those requirements were a bit higher to at least make it FEEL like I could fail.Overall I love this game, and I hope the hinted sequel happens.

_childDocuments_.review: A neon feverdream that is quite enjoyable and worth its price. I'll break this review into sections: story, graphics, and gameplay.Story: Its narrative is quite simple in all reality. However I did enjoy the comic style cutscenes inbetween fights and before stages. My wish however is that more characters were explained; the bear in the box where did he come about? origins of the company, more lore in general. I think the devs could have some fun with the story here and add a lot more context. But its fine as it is. Unless they intend to make a sequel. that'll be up to them.Graphics: Its not pushing the limits of unreal to say the least. However, its neon bright and gritty style is quite unique. I haven't seen a game like it before. I didn't notice any real texture errors while playing the game which is certainly a plus. Models were animated in a good fashion, however I would say some of the movements seemed a bit stiff. Overall good graphics.Gameplay: Here's the meat of the game. The 'Gori' bits. To start, right away I noticed that the game is... rather floaty. In a strange way its movement and combat reminded me a bit of Alice: Madness returns. Except its dodge mechanic is not that great, the only notice you have prior to an attack is a split second pair of shock symbols that appear and are rather hard to appropriately dodge to. only time I could get this easy was when i was going against one of the bosses but it still felt a bit off. For attacks there is a combo system. In a harsh way, I have to say this is almost useless. The attacks are rather laggy, floaty and regardless of difficulty feel like they do not hit hard enough on enemies. Only the heavy attack really stuns enemies and sometimes that doesn't even happen. Most of the time to chop down enemies health I was "spinning to win" (RT + X). The grenade launcher I have a lot to say about as well: While its charge shot certainly deals the hard hits to get openings on mini bosses, its ammo is abysmal in some areas, and it always left me stuck waiting for it to charge. Resulting in taking unnecessary damage or stalling out fights (in areas with the pick up this wasn't exactly an issue unless the pick up was placed in an awkward area) There were also a few strange glitches that occured where going in and out of aiming mode caused Gori to not be able to jump. While going back into sights fixed this, it should be noted that this was an issue that occured while on the game's hardest mode: Cuddly carnage.Cuddly Carnage also had the most errors out of all difficulties I played. I had a seamless playthrough on house cat. However for reasons I got fatal errors on boss fights and enemy fights with Cuddly Carnage. Resulting in the game to fully crash and close. If it wasn't for checkpoints, I probably would have a more negative opinion on the game. People also get this error as seen in youtube playthroughs so its not limited to my hardware. On top of this: several times I found my character softlocked in finishers, Gori frozen in place but still able to move around, and other strange glitches. While these didnt ruin the game for me, I have to ask that the developers of the game fix it as soon as possible as they can ruin the experience for those trying to 100% the game.Overall I liked the game: it was cute, cuddly and there was carnage. Pretty fun all well around. If a sequel is made I hope the  creators fix the issues and polish on what they have.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is my second ever review. I'm compelled to write this review as there have been so many disappointments in gaming in 2024, and many of the games I was excited for have failed to live up to the hype. Enter: Gori. I knew nothing about this game at all, it just popped up on a curated steam list. I saw the reviews, and for the price, had to give it a go. I'm only 2 hours in, but I'm confident in saying this is in my top 5 games of the last few years, maybe even my GOTY 2024. It's so refreshing, and most importantly, fun. No politics thrown in your face, no subliminal messages, just a hearken back to times when games were experimental, and fun was the only focus. It reminds me of a love child of Tony Hawks, Lollipop Chainsaw, and Devil May Cry. It looks and performs amazingly, but importantly for me, it controls *perfectly*. Very rarely does a game nail everything and leave me with genuinely no critcism, but this is one of those games. Good job devs, I definitely have my eye on your future releases!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game with generous gore which lends a sense of catharsis to the task of slaying an army of zombie unicorns. The fluid hack-and-slash gameplay loop married with light skateboard mechanics gives you a decent variety of combat options, yet doesn't get to be too challenging even on the hardest difficulty. The game regardless more than makes up for it with a wide enemy variety, a charming comic-esque art style, banger soundtrack, great level design with differing environments, and lovable characters. The humour starts off good, but doesn't go much farther than dialogue saturated with cussing; however, given the setting it sticks well enough. Also, kot.
_childDocuments_.name: Gori: Cuddly Carnage

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked:- No performance issues despite being an UE5 game. So much so it runs very well on an 8 year old PC- Very good and fitting OST- The game is geared towards fast-paced hack-and-slash gameplay- Combat and weapon mechanics being neither too simplistic nor too complex allow for having massive fun during enemy encounters- Hand-drawn comics used as a way to tell the story- The game doesn't overstay its welcome (in fact, after finishing it, it feels a bit short)What could be better:- Goldfin feels like American Dad's Klaus ripoff- Camera is a bit annoying at times- While enemy variety is good enough (at least one new enemy type is introduced each level), dog or rat-type enemies would be a welcome addition as a reference to the relationship between the species in real lifeOverall:Cute feline protagonist wrecking havoc, slicing and dicing amid neon lights in a postapocalyptic cyberpunk setting. Count me in!
_childDocuments_.name: Gori: Cuddly Carnage

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. The charm lies mostly in the writing (Goldfin is my favourite character) because the combat gets a bit samey after a while. I think it would've been nice if skating itself played more of a roll in combat, like boosting with the shield and so on.The game has two bad habits: one is springing multiple shield enemies on you at a single time, the other is spongey miniboss-level enemies who you need to politely wait for to make themselves vulnerable before you use your most efficient tactic of holding down the Tornado button until their health gets low enough for you to pull a Glory Kill.The boss fights are also pretty weak. On top of needing to wait for them to open up their weak spot, pretty much all of them needs to keep spawning the same random mooks that I've gotten tired of mowing down throughout the preceding levels.While the levels are fun with their own scenarios and setpieces, it's a bit of a shame that all they ever really amount to are interconnected battle arenas; for having a hoverboard, very little of the game demands any skating. There are platforming sequences but they feel automated and token, without even any inertia mechanics like going down slopes to build up speed. There was a huge opportunity here to marry unique mobility mechanics with the combat where mastery of both is required to master the game and  couldn't have missed it harder.But the levels are still fun haunted house rail rides, the characters bounce off each other in fun ways, and it's never boring. Except for the ending, where the game will ask you to do seven typical challenge missions just like the other seven you already did just to get another ending. Just feels like padding.
_childDocuments_.name: Gori: Cuddly Carnage

_childDocuments_.review: A late PS2/Early PS3 game in all the right ways. A short, sweet game starring the world's most radical cat and a foul-mouthed talking hoverboard that doubles as a blender, plus Marvin the Depressed Robot and Klaus from American Dad doing mission control. It's aggressively RAD in a way games haven't been in a long time and I want more of it.Platforming is a bit like boost-era Sonic, with you having a turbo speed button and a limited amount of fuel which must be recharged via grinding on rails or grabbing batteries out of dead enemies. Fuel also powers your turbo-blender attacks, which do insane DPS compared to trying to use normal button combos. Combat is kind of a character-action-lite affair, forcing you to juggle your ranged attacks, a few distinct melee types, shields and boosting around; it all comes together once you're actually playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games, where it is enough to watch the trailers, because what you see there is exactly what you get.The graphics are good, thematic, and vibrant. Maybe a bit too much so for some. A saturation slider might have been nice. The character models are also good (although Gori's eyes look weird when he blinks).The soundtrack might as well be the greatest strength of the game. It's like a creepy toy store version of Doom (2016), with a good use of leitmotif. Can also be listened to on streaming services.Combat is fun, responsive, and brainless, but in a good way. Enemy variety felt sufficient for a game with this length.Platforming is fine, albeit "loose". What I mean is that precision was never really required, and I think I never had to use both the mid-air dash and the double jump at the same time to cover a distance. Movement in general, felt satisfying.I have mixed feeling about the story. The backstory was good, and I liked how it was told using a comic book. The plot for the gameplay however felt disconnected from your overall goal. You spend most of your time building a weapon, whereas your main objective was supposed to be finding someone. This gave me the sense that the your are just given excuses for killing more. This became even more of an issue in the last mission, which I discussed here:  .The framerate was good, and I only encountered 1-2 bugs in total. What wasn't good however, was that the game crashed to desktop 4 times in my playthrough. I hope these are fixed by now.Gori Cuddly Carnage is a gameplay-focused game. And since the gameplay happens to be it's greatest strength (alongside with the soundtrack!), this is an easy recommendation. It is a relatively short game, but I believe, it's length is just right; making it longer would've been a detriment to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hack and slash your way through the mutated gore. You play as a bad ass cat, with your friend F.R.A.N.K., the blade wielding hoverboard. The "adorable" army is determined to destroy you, yet all you want is to get back what they stole from you.This game makes the world better. The video game industry is tired. We look at our big wall of games every way and see incredible titles. From DOOM to Slime Rancher, we see how creative developers can be. And we adore these games every day. But who would know that it's really hard to create a new lovable franchise?Please, don't over look this game. It looks shocking on the surface. But the flashy gameplay turns out to be an artstyle. The vulgar characters are easy to love. And this game is going to be a series. If you pass over this game, it's because your bar is too high. I promise that you will be missing out, and that some day you will regret it.

I can do better then that!' mentality - without punishing into a 'I'm just not good enough' mentality.
_childDocuments_.name: Gori: Cuddly Carnage

_childDocuments_.review: High on Lisa Frank. The purr-fect fusion of cute, vulgar, competence, and camp.Despite walking on two legs, Gori as a character is a great take on anthropomorphism. He can understand what people are saying, the intonations, and can only respond back with cat noises. But it's very realistic cat noises. He's nimble but unlike Stray, not to a handholded degree of perfectionism. The big blob CH1-P and hoverboard F.R.A.N.K both serve as a serious and a swearing comedic foil. The latter's immense cursing is censored at first, but you can unlock it with credits (lol)The enemies have a great deal of variety. You can’t attack all the same way, and what works well for once type of enemy will be parried with ease by another. The second level is an arcade, third level is like a nuclear toy factory, fourth is underwater themed, the fifth is some kind of doll house. Some concepts are intuitive, like the slicing and dicing, but in later levels you'll be gimping the grinding feature to farm for fuel, and there will be sequences where you'll run on empty for extended periods of time. Likewise, the glory kill feature can be abused when dispatching multiple enemies so you can be invulnerable and recover health.The semifinal boss is some utter playtime stretch and punishingly frustrating if you die (you go back to the beginning of the boss fight, and enjoy four/five/six "laps", not even stages). The final boss is much easier by comparison and the ending is bittersweet. Without spoiling it, let me just say Professor Y isn't as great as the game makes her out to be - and she's not even the antagonist.There are also some minor oversights regarding accessible wayfinding in the later levels, and being able to go in areas the developers did not account for. While these things don't break the game, they can be a bit unexpected as you may think you're going into the same area twice.Before I close, let me reflect a bit on a meta note: While I haven’t been a fan of their marketing partners (Alienware seems to have completely bungled its showcase featuring this game, both at IGN Live and at PAX), the game has really shined through as it's well designed, and the people who make it seemed genuinely invested in making it fun and engaging.Assuming you don't get stuck anywhere, you'll get about 6 to 8 hours of playtime for a story run and a few more hours of side content to 100%.
