_childDocuments_.review: I have alot to say about this amazing game! It shows alot of potential though sometimes I felt like alot of concepts werent explored too well. The game is fast paced and action packed and it kept me coming back for more everyday I had time to play it!   My complaints are few but they are there, although it can really just be boiled down to it being the first entry in its possible series. The arsenal feels very limited, even once you unlock Gori's full arsenal it kind of boils down to spinning and using rockets for the ranged enemies or heavy enemies to stun them, the bash is good for killing shields and gaining health from stunned enemies but in later difficulties the health you get from it is not good enough to warrant using it in a low health situation. Since the arsenal is so small it feels like alot of enemies really only have 1 or 2 approaches and especially worst in later difficulties where the rocket launcher's charge shot is your best friend if you even want to begin to damage heavier enemies. The game suffers a bit on humor since alot of the jokes boil down to "haha bad word funny" and even that started to loose its presence near the end of the game. Its not bad humor, it did catch me off gaurd a couple times especially with the manager in the 3rd level. Hearing a robot with a kids voice swear so casually was what got me lol.   There are alot of things I did enjoy aswell! The characters felt straight out of an early 2000s platformer with their whacky and often funny interactions with eachother! It is just a straight up silly and laid back game and thats something I am all for! The combat, even though repetitive, was still very satisfying and its made even better by the banger soundtrack which had a heavy doom vibe!  I could go on an on about this game but my point in the end of this is that its a game with a promising future as a franchise although it felt a little safe its a great example of how to properly plan and use project scope and avoid scope overload on your fist entry to any series. I do not doubt I will be seeing Gori again very soon and I am excited for the day I get to see the full potential of this franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Gori: Cuddly Carnage Steam ReviewI first played a Gori: Cuddly Carnage demo at the WASD Event last year in London. It was the highlight of the event for me, partly thanks to the welcoming crew from WIRED PRODUCTIONS, a big shout out to them all, and the 12 minutes of epic gameplay I experienced. It’s been worth waiting a year since I first massacred evil unicorns with a ginger cat on a foul-mouthed sentient hoverboard. God, I love video games. This is our review and I would like to give thanks to WIRED PRODUCTIONS and Angry Demon for the review code, and to you for stopping by. If you like what you see, subscribe cause it’s free. Storythe story here is pretty bonkers and felt like a hommage to an era when Care Bears and Furbies were at the top of Santa’s list. In this world,‘Cool-Toys Inc.’ created ‘Ultra Pets’, the ultimate companions. A minor mutation soon transforms the perfect pets into twisted toys straight from your nightmares, hell-bent on wiping out humanity. The Humans that are not wiped out escape into space. All that stands between the Adorable Army and Mankind is Gori the Cat, Frank the over-excited hoverboard and CHIP, the sorrowful cartridge. Together they go on an adventure to rescue their owner and put an end to the horrendous Teddy and his minions. The narration is cleverly broken into short comic book intermissions before the start of a level, and helps flesh out Gori’s back story and how the world was destroyed. I enjoyed the dynamic between the trio. Frank is the mouthpiece of the three and his wisecracking accompanied my many hours of gameplay.GameplayThis is an action hack-and-slash platformer, akin to games like Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. Level progression will have you traversing obstacles and defeating hordes of enemies. There are also chase sections, which truly put your hoverboard skills to the test. Gori and Frank’s synergy allows them to hover on billboards and reach new heights and speeds. Frank, is full of surprises, ranging from speed boosts, morning stars, blades and even a shield. If that wasn’t enough, he can become a bazooka that regenerates ammo over time. Perfect dodges slow down time, leaving enemies open to retaliation.The combat is sublime, with different combos and attacks to experiment with, and a score grading system akin to games of its ilk. Higher combos earn more money and points at the end of the battle, and they can be overwhelming but never feel unfair. There is an eclectic mix of unholy unicorns and other enemies. Most can be dispatched with good use of Frank’s arsenal, but use these wisely, as his energy is finite. The game has you carrying out a clever flow of killing enemies and grinding on rails to replenish Frank’s energy. It is not a game where you stay still. Combat is like playing Tony Hawks and DOOM Eternal in some ways, combining fatalities and stylish air time. Tougher enemies can be disposed of with a finisher that will drop health and battery packs. The end-level bosses were fun to battle and presented their challenges. The game's levels are quite diverse, each containing key fragments that unlock rewards within your hub area. It took me around 7 hours to complete the game, but there is still plenty to do afterwards. There are extra levels where you rescue good unicorns, and you can also replay levels to collect anything you missed the first time. Additionally, there are numerous cosmetic add-ons to customise the characters Gori and Frank. I felt that the game’s pacing and length were on point, without overstaying its welcome. Visuals, Audio and PresentationGori: Cuddly Carnage has a unique visual presentation, which has cities in ruins, juxtaposed with the colourful neon radiating from the special effects. The game allows for a photo mode and unlockable filters, and the developers have gone to great lengths to animate Gori facial expressions during combat. The game is fast-paced but if you slow down to take things in, you’ll see many easter eggs and details that the levels have to offer. The heads up display and overall presentation is colourful and easy to take in, and I did not experience any significant framerate issues in either docked or handheld mode on my Steam Deck OLED. I played on its default settings.I particularly liked the comic book story segments before a level, which I found fitting for the kind of tone the game was going for. It weirdly gave me Viewtiful Joe vibes, in the way the game was presented, with sound effect appearing on screen.The humour will not be to everyone’s tastes, particularly the amount of profanities and sex jokes thrown around. It not too overbearing but it has to be noted. Borderlands 2 fans may be more forgiving. The soundtrack complements the combat with metal and fast-paced music blasting during tense sections, and dark fair ground jingles can be heard here too.  The voice acting is decent, and aside from the swearing and jokes, there is a touching story about an unusual family trying to save the world and be together again. Gori only meows but he will melt cat lovers out there for sure. Conclusion£14.39 €17.59 $17.59 $22.88CAD $25.69AUS this is with the added 20% discount until 12th September. Gori: Cuddly Carnage is out on all major platforms and will also be released physically shortly.Angry Demon has created something greater than the sum of its parts. Explaining what this game is about, without people thinking you’re high, is a challenge in and of itself, but it’s so much fun to play. Fans of hack-and-slash score-attack games should grab this one. I truly hope to see this intellectual property grow and expand its universe. 9/10 Cat-tastic Hoverboard MassacreBrilliant PresentationGood LengthFun Unicorn Culling- Humour is not for some

_childDocuments_.review: Pawsitively Badass 😼+Addicting fast-paced hack and slash combat+Fun story lasting around 6+ hours to beat and around 20ish to 100%+ Tons of enemy variety and unique bosses to fight+Great platforming reminiscent of games like Sonic and Sunset Overdrive+Decent amount of unlockables and customization's to find+Fantastic soundtrack that could rival Doom+Well optimized for PC-Numerous bugs and the occasional crash but nothing game-breaking-Pretty easy even on the hardest difficulty-I can't stop making cat puns now lolMaybe I'm just getting old but games like Gori: Cuddly Carnage really take me back. Gori feels inspired by the edgy mascot platformers of the early 2000s with a mix of games like DMC and Sunset Overdrive. The gameplay while simplistic, is very fast-paced and addicting. It's one of the very few games I went out of my way to 100%. There's just something so cathartic about shredding through hordes of undead unicorns like a furry little meat grinder while jamming out to this games amazing soundtrack and it had me grinning ear to ear throughout my entire playthrough.The story itself is short but sweet with a cast of likable funny characters that will keep you invested till very the end. The game offers a fair amount of replayability however I think Gori would benefit greatly from adding some form of horde mode and/or online leaderboards. Also I should mention that I had quite a few bugs and some of the weirdest crashes I've ever seen in a game. Hopefully that all gets patched out soon. Overall while Gori is not a "purr-fect" game by any means, it's one where you can tell the developers put a lot of love and effort into making it. It may be a little rough around the edges but considering it's low asking price I feel a lot of it shortcomings can be overlooked and there is definitely a lot of stuff here to enjoy! I highly recommend giving it a try and can't wait to see what the devs have planned for Gori next!

_childDocuments_.review: Gori: Cuddly Carnage feels like a classic PS2 game, but in the best possible way. I’m starting to think it might make my top 10 games of 2024.Set in a futuristic world, you control Gori, a cat who is anything but “cuddly.” Equipped with a hoverboard, Gori not only glides around but also brutally and stylishly slaughters hordes of enemies. The story is packed with dark humor and absurd situations, making it both entertaining and memorable.The strongest aspect of Gori: Cuddly Carnage is its gameplay. It’s fast-paced, frantic, and keeps players constantly on their toes. The combination of hoverboard action and combat creates a sense of fluid movement and relentless intensity. The battles are satisfying and offer numerous ways to defeat enemies, keeping the game fresh and exciting. It reminds me of the best levels in Psychonauts and American McGee’s Alice with its floaty yet highly responsive and tight controls. It’s rare to see a modern game with such excellent air control.Visually, Gori: Cuddly Carnage is a delight. The game features a world filled with colorful and creative environments that sharply contrast with the bloody violence Gori inflicts. The character design is both charming and terrifying, perfectly matching the game’s tone. The game just looks incredible, with a late '90s to early '00s Toxic Avenger aesthetic. The attention to detail in the various worlds is staggering, showcasing the impressive creativity put into each level.The sound design is equally well-executed, combining heavy metal tunes with eerie ambient music to create a truly strange and occasionally scary world. The music sets an energetic tone that matches the game’s pace, while the sound effects emphasize the brutal combat. The voice acting is a bit hit-or-miss for me. Your sidekick can be quite annoying, but turning down the voices helped a lot. Gori, on the other hand, just makes cat sounds like meows.Gori: Cuddly Carnage is a breath of fresh air in the action game genre. It combines frantic gameplay with a unique aesthetic and humorous story, making it a must-play for fans of fast-paced action and quirky humor. While the game’s brutal style may not be for everyone, it undoubtedly stands out from the crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: Angry Demon Studio is one of my favorite indie dev teams, and it was pretty funny to see them go from two really good Norse folk horror games to a hyper-violent and silly combo-based action game. But they really pulled it off!The gameplay loop is really fun. It's all about maintaining long combos by slaughtering hordes of enemies while managing your fuel meter, which gives you access to the strongest moves. By having the protagonist on a hover board, there's a unique feel to the movement in combat, which is good since movement and chaining together moves is emphasized over complicated button strings. It's basically a 3D platformer mashed with a hack and slash. Admittedly, the combat might be a little too easy once you get the hang of the movement, even at higher difficulties, but it never stopped being fun. The visual style is also really strong. The enemy and level designs set on a future earth destroyed and currently ruled by evil toys are all fantastic. The story and dialogue were pretty entertaining too. Be warned, there was a good chunk of cringe in a lot of the jokes, especially with your hoverboard FRANK, but that doesn't really detract too much from the charm that the game oozes.Overall, it's fast paced and really fun platforming action game with a really distinctive style. Heavy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Gori: Cuddly Carnage is an adrenaline-fueled, blood-soaked, and surprisingly adorable romp that delivers on its promise of over-the-top action and hilarious mayhem. If you're looking for a game that doesn't take itself too seriously, while still offering tight controls and satisfying gameplay, look no further. What Makes it Great:- Killer Combo of Skateboarding and Combat:  The game's core mechanic of seamlessly blending fast-paced skateboarding with visceral combat is an absolute joy. Carving through hordes of mutated toys while pulling off stylish tricks feels incredibly satisfying. - Gori and F.R.A.N.K. - An Unlikely Duo: The chemistry between the adorable yet deadly cat, Gori, and his sentient hoverboard, F.R.A.N.K., is a highlight. Their banter is both hilarious and heartwarming, adding personality to the chaos.- Eye-Popping Visuals:  The vibrant, cel-shaded art style is a feast for the eyes. The game's world is bursting with color and detail, and the over-the-top gore effects are both ridiculous and strangely beautiful.- Adrenaline-Pumping Soundtrack: The high-energy soundtrack perfectly complements the fast-paced action, keeping you pumped up as you shred through enemies. - Surprisingly Touching Story: Beneath the carnage and humor lies a surprisingly touching story about friendship, loyalty, and revenge.  It adds an unexpected layer of depth to the experience.Overal: Gori: Cuddly Carnage is a delightful surprise - a game that's as fun to play as it is to watch. Its unique blend of skateboarding, combat, humor, and heartwarming moments makes it a must-play for anyone looking for a refreshingly different action experience.  Additional Points to Consider:The game can be quite challenging, especially on higher difficulty settings. The humor might not be for everyone, as it leans heavily into absurdity and gore. If you're looking for a fast-paced, visually stunning, and laugh-out-loud funny action game, Gori: Cuddly Carnage is an excellent choice.

_childDocuments_.review: is like some kind of trippy alt-universe version of the early  games if they never really existed, and were instead just fictional games in . Indeed, this is exactly the kind of game one can easily imagine Gaz playing in the background as she scowls at Dib.The action is fast-paced, the music is high-octane, and the colorful universe forms the perfect backdrop for the game's absolutely loony concept and cast of characters that include a hyper violent cat, melancholy spaceship, a hoverboard that is basically edgy Gir, and (later in the game) a giant German goldfish. There is of course also the human professor Y., but she's more of a story-only character than part of the actual game.And of course, like all truly good games, the story here is just a vehicle for the action rather than a central focal point. The aggressive slicing and dicing and bashing and shooting and.... well you get the idea, is what makes this truly worth playing. You have a modest, but polished, set of moves to work with. This is a very accessible game that does not ask you to master a hundred different button combos. It is distilled down to just the essentials and it snaps together very nicely without feeling overwhelming. You don't have a ton of tools: you have a few that work really well. Each one has a distinct purpose and each one feels satisfying. The only thing I found to be a little useless was the shield; I barely used it, but I wouldn't be surprised if there is some meta-strategy use for this that I am simply unaware of.Your targets for these moves are a decently diverse, if somewhat typical, set of unicorns. There's your standard useless fodder that exists only to be killed. There's a class of slightly-larger versions, one melee and one ranged, optionally with shields. Then there's larger "tank" variations of those. And there's also a few others like a flying unicorn that drops ammo and a purple one that buffs/shields other enemies. These are what you will be spending the majority of your time fighting, though rarely you will come across a tentacle-spawning dollhouse, a mushroom-type nightlight that must be bashed from the top for a basically instant kill, some laser-shooting hands, and some flying doll heads that drop brains. You also get numerous unique and challenging boss battles, plus some gimmicks in certain areas (like switches you have to trigger during combat), to break up the typical shredding.I will say, I wish we had gotten a bit more variety on the base enemies, or even just on their attacks. Most of them seem to have basically only one attack, and this can get just a tad stale during drawn out overly long fights. You spend a lot of your time hacking up fodder enemies, and I would have liked to see some more tanks. The larger enemies are pretty sparingly used, usually only spawning 2-4 of them per arena. To be fair, in their current design, this is good, because of just  they are. They can be a bit too damage-spongy, but you are rewarded for taking them out with a full recharge of your two resources: health and fuel (technically, you have a third resource in the form of of ammo but it recharges on its own). I think it would have been good to cut the bigger enemies' health and resupply values in half, but double the frequency at which they spawn. These are very minor gripes however, and certainly do not spoil the fun of grinding on rails and turning your hoverboard into a blender.Speaking of that hoverboard, don't let it turn you off if you aren't a fan of skating/driving games. This doesn't feel anything like that. The hoverboard here is nothing more than a justification for the gameplay (and an AI companion). Maneuvering it is not a difficult skill that must be mastered, nor something you have to directly control. It's very much just a way to put the combat on roller skates and foster the action. I might be showing my bias here: but the combat loop, with its emphasis on movement, mixing attacks, and "Gori" killing to reclaim resources, feels just a bit  inspired (and, without spoiling too much, the final boss definitely has an Icon of Sin vibe... you'll get it when you see it).All in all, the game remained thoroughly fun for the 8-ish hours it took me to beat it on the 2nd-highest difficulty, which at the sale-price it was introduced at I can't complain about. After beating the game there is still more to do in the form of good old fashioned high-score based combat arenas, and of course you can go hunting for all the cosmetics, upgrades, and unlockables if that's your thing, but again this is a gameplay-driven experience here. The main form of "extra content" is simply replaying the fights and mastering the game mechanics. This is very much about the journey; one of those games you replay simply because, well, it's fun to kill stuff, it needs no other justification.This is what games should be at their core: fun to . It puts the combat loop front and center. This will appeal primarily to players who value fast paced arena-style fighting above all else. If you're looking for one of those brain-off-reflexes-on smash and grab kind of games, if you want the sort of thing you can just go hog wild on and watch the carnage fly without much thought, a frantic and fun keyboard mashing clickfest of gore with a heavy dose of silliness and charm: pick this one up, get ready to slide and slash, stay cuddly... and stay Gori.

_childDocuments_.review: haven't had this much fun with (non-retro) area boomer-shooter since Doom Eternal...gorgeous visuals and style. exciting, intuitive and smooth controls. well-executed mechanics. unique narrative...and it features a feline as the protagonist. one (like myself) could not ask for more. I was expecting this game to be style over substance...something that looked way cooler than it actually was.  Nevertheless, i wanted to give it a chance because if it was even a fraction as fun as it looked in the trailer - it might be worth the investment of time+$. I was terribly wrong in my initial assumptions about the game.  It may actually be better than it appears in the trailer and i can already tell that A. I'm going to have a lot of fun playing this game. B. i'm actually going to finish. C. the replayability factor seems rather high and I would be very surprised if i stop playing the game once i finish the primary missions. Rather, i can easily see this developing into a "comfort" game...something that i can fall back on for stress-relief and mindless violence.  If this game LOOKS fun to you, then it likely WILL be fun to you. I'm having a helluva time with it. concerning the genre of the game:despite the visual style of the game being heavily inspired by the modern 'cyberpunk aesthetic' (neon blue and pink EVERYWHERE as the cyberpunk gods intended) i would argue that Gori: Cuddly Carnage actually falls comfortably within the genre of biopunk. (: focuses on the implications of biotechnology, such as synthetic biology, genetic engineering, and cloning.) due to the entire narrative having to do with genetically engineered pets, "toys" (despite their name, they, and Gori, are all GMOs), and other biopunk hallmarks.  I love the incorporation of the childish 'playground' aesthetic seemingly layered over a jagged dystopian metropolis.

A simple, fun, and insane story, AMAZING comic book style presentation, spot on acting, gameplay that was smooth, visceral and oh so satisfying, and unique bosses that test EVERYTHING at your paw tips. Nothing but respect for Wired Productions and Angry Demon Games for blessing us with this gem, and I HOPE we can get a sequel somewhere in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I have followed a lot of the development of this game, and been so excited for it to come out. I played through the main story for the first time without hardly putting it down, so I can safely say it has stood up to my excitement and expectations. ^0^ This game is definitely chaotic, crazy, and over the top, and if that isn't your style, you may not enjoy it. I also definitely wouldn't say that photosensitive players should give it a try. But, if you like bright colors and neon lights, fun movement mechanics, overdone crazy gore, and absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ creepy-cute enemy designs- then you'll probably love Gori. I really enjoyed the soundtrack, and the comic-book style flashback sequences. The story is very comic-book-eque itself, so it all pulls together well. I found the characters all enjoyable and well voice-acted, with a feeling of fun about the whole game that made me feel that everyone in the project enjoyed making it. Tiny details in scenery such as the graffiti in every area, and the labels on various items, were great accents to the fun and wacky environments. The difficulties go all the way down to a mode that even someone with slow reaction time like me could complete, which is a feature I always appreciate. The one trouble I currently have is that, although every other key piece was pretty easy to find, the third piece of the stage 5 key I simply cannot locate. Since they literally go 'here kitty kitty' when you're nearby, I'm truly baffled as to how I cannot find it. But, since that's my only complaint overall, I'd call this an absolutely smashing game debut.

name: Time Loader
detailed_description: Time Loader is a story-driven, physics-based, cute aesthetics, side-scrolling puzzle platformer with a twist. At the helm of a small robot, you’ll travel back to the 90s to prevent a tragic accident. Explore the house of your creator, solve brain-teasing environmental puzzles, acquire unique and powerful upgrades, and see the nature of common household items from an entirely new perspective! But remember: meddling with time has serious consequences. You may succeed in changing the past, but can you deal with the result of your actions? Gameplay Features: Subverted perspectives Even the most familiar objects look different when you’re the size of a toy car. Will you watch your every move or dive head-first into this dangerous new world? An arsenal to choose from Boosters, harpoons, screwdrivers… choose among dozens of upgrades to tackle each level and get the job done! Dynamic and branching narratives Don’t just relive the past: change it! Every choice you make will influence the story and may lead to a different outcome. So do us a favor: change the past responsibly! A complimentary dose of nostalgia Time Loader features music, references, and items straight out of the ‘90s. Relive your childhood or, if you’re too young for it, just gawk in awe at how primitive humanity used to be back then! Enjoy the relaxing atmosphere of childhood combined with the serious tasks you have.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is fine for what it is. A little remote controlled vehicle with a grabbing arm is put into a microwave-sized time-machine and transfered back in the year 1995. Your goal now is to destroy a toy, before an accident can happen. Of course, manipulating the past leads to other unexpected changes... So you drive left or right, jump, grab stuff, throw it (aim with right stick) and solve the problems that the game narrator tells you to solve. Everything plays in a 2D world, which is a bit stupid sometimes. Why solve intricate puzzles to overcome an obstacle, if I could just drive around it in 3D? Apart from that, it is a nice puzzler. Find your way through a house with a little robot (basically, just 2 wheels and a grabber).I encountered a serious bug during gameplay, though. After some time the stupid robot grabbing arm just didn't work any more. Or so I thought. The problem is the buggy joystick implementation (still in version 1.04), that leads to the grabber not working - or even worse - stopping to work during the game. Fortunately, there is an easy fix for this: Just disable Steam Input, and it works.Cute puzzler with a little dose of platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about my review until I reached the last section of the game. Using a Steam controller I found the Harpoon way too difficult to control. In some videos I've seen it show a guideline of where it's facing, but I didn't have one and repeatedly missed jumps despite having it right near the target. I had my fingers crossed that the game wouldn't make you use it repeatedly on do-or-die jumps ... and then that's exactly what it does at the end. You have to make several jumps with it in a row, and you have to wait several seconds between failed attempts. After a few dozen failures I found it too frustrating to control, uninstalled the game, and won't be finishing it.I did enjoy the creativity, soundtrack, and the graphics, but there were a lot of frustrations earlier too:- slow movement- lots of places where it's easy to fall and have to (slowly) redo some sections- interacting with some items unexpectedly lands you in the next section, before you were done exploring- it's really hard to visually recognize which "platforms" you can and cannot interact with- the puzzles were easy to figure out, but the controls / slow speed make them take longer than they should- saving / loading seemed buggy - there were times that I quit right after the auto-save icon went away, then was in a previous room when I came backAltogether I found it more frustrating than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting puzzle adventure game with an unusual character - a car with an arm. The gameplay is quite simple, we move the car, catch various elements of the environment, interact with it and overcome the different kinds of difficulties, leading to the goal. Ridles are quite simple, even a person who does not like such genres, or a young player will manage to solve most of them. Our main character evolves in a fairly linear, albeit in a satisfying way. You can see the effect straight away after upgrade.The game seems like a cool option for teaching your child to play slightly different types of games. Due to the time stamp of the action and pastel graphics, even the person watching the gameplay will not be bored. Especially those who were young in the 90s and know what the VHS is :)
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: For a game with time travel story you'd expect some consequences. Different outcomes. Shocking endings.Sadly, this is not the case with Time Loader.You will play Time Loader three times. Each one is your travel back to the past/present with insignificant changes. First, you do A-actions, then B-actions, only to... undo those A-actions. So much for the effort. It's all about platforming and pushing/lifting items. Entire journey is scripted and cannot be altered.There's a long sequence of unlocking a secret, which actually requires certain changes to be made in specific chapters. But again, it doesn't affect the story. Play Time Loader for its toy graphics and relaxed background, otherwise... ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a real little masterpiece!I would highlight three main aspects that took my heart:1. Control of a toy robot-loader. Despite the fact that this game is not AAA game, there is a breathtaking plot with a time travel theme (yes, not only Christopher Nolan can play with time well)3. And the most important thing is the vibe and atmosphere of the 90s. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that is just long enough and complex enough for a satisfying completion in a few hours. _childDocuments_.review: Cute little sidescrolling platformer where you control a robot on a mission: The robot's creator Adam had an accident as a little boy that left him paraplegic. But thanks to his keen interest in science, he has managed to build both a time machine and an agile robot that he sends into the past with the task of keeping the accident from happening. You control the little machine on its way through a 1990s household (with a few callbacks for anyone who was alive back then), making use of its unique flat four-wheeler design that allows for leaps and fitting through gaps. A little mounted arm can be used to grab and throw objects, which comes in handy sometimes. Every now and then, the robot gains extra abilities, e.g. starting electrical devices. These skills are necessary to make your way through the levels and to solve environmental puzzles, such as when you  remove obstacles.Controlling the robot is simple and intuitive, and there aren't any spots that require hard-to-master control skills. If anything, it's usually more about keeping your eyes open as to which paths you can take.As a bonus, since you ARE on a trip through time, there are multiple instances where you can take or leave an action that may have an influence in the future. This, in sum, will lead to one of three endings. No need to stress though, as it's usually pretty straightforward and all but one choices I found were OK to take (and that last one seemed to be irrelevant in the big picture).Another bonus: If you do explore and pay attention, you will notice secret symbols on certain objects that can be found off the main path. These plus some deduction skills and meta gaming can give you a fourth, secret ending.Verdict: It was fun enough and the aforementioned bonus features made the game more interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this must be a rough time to be a small dev team.  is a sidescrolling platformer that will inevitably be overshadowed by more impressive titles in the genre, through no fault of its own.Okay, maybe a  fault of its own. I spent - no lie - the entire game wishing I didn't move so dang slowly. Your little RC wheels  across the screen. The physics of your jumping are inconsistent, and you'll frequently need to retry jumps. Because this is a side-scrolling game in a 3D environment, you'll frequently run into cases of "Y'know, with just a little movement along the Z-axis, which the character is capable of in cutscenes, this wouldn't be a problem." I have no idea what the store description means by "dozens of upgrades" - maybe the logic is "a third of a dozen is still dozens." And bugs are still present - I had one CTD and needed to disconnect and reconnect my controller a couple of times because actions weren't registering.That aside - Time Loader is a "single-timeline" time travel story that mainly features physics puzzles as obstacles to platforming progression. The devs have taken great care to make sure you can't soft-lock yourself, which both is a blessing and a curse. I said in my review of  that you could effectively "Chekhov's Gun" your way through a level by interacting with all of the actionable objects you came across, thereby solving the problem before even seeing what the problem is - Time Loader has the same issue. If you can do a thing, you should probably do the thing.At the same time, some of your actions need to be so precise that I can't recommend this to newcomers either. I feel like more than half of players will find the gameplay too dull, and another eighth will find the platforming too fiddly. It advertises itself as "relaxing" and "nostalgic," but as an 80's kid myself, I need more than a toy DeLorean in the background to find myself gripped with emotion. The story didn't accomplish that either.The game teases multiple endings, as well as a way to get the "best" one. Look at the other reviews - see the ones with 2-3 hours? They beat  once. Those with 4+ may have gotten the best ending. At time of writing, only about 10% of reviewers found the game compelling enough to put that kind of time in.That's why I give this game my absolute bare-minimum thumbs-up of "it's okay." There is a game here. There is a decently original story. There are decently pretty visuals. The gameplay is... adequate. Passable. The puzzles are occasionally even somewhat clever.Honestly? If you're a Humble Monthly subscriber, or an Xbox Game Pass subscriber, or even if you just have an Epic Game Store account, I'd probably just wait until this pops up for free. Nothing in Time Loader made it feel like a "must play," and my free time is limited enough that even that makes me regret having spent my time on it.Tepidly recommended.

Time slows down when you throw the grappling hook, but not enough to make a difference. Stopping time completely would make more sense. I am sure someone will make a mod for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Well.. that was pretty awesome.After a good three hours I'd beaten the game with ending B and thought something like "probably a game designed for new gamers or even children" (despite the dark story); "yeah, was alright"; "Wished, there hadn't been so much guidance for the puzzles - made it a bit too easy" and similar.But then I had a look on the achievements and realized, that there was more. The next 3 1/2h I fried my brain and tested around to find all the stuff, I had missed. A short, but great story, pleasant gameplay and quite a few moments I did not expect in the slightest.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting story line, a very familiar BTTF vibe with a hint of Wall-E; and it is fun to play.  The puzzles, at times, are uniquely difficult, but not so difficult that you get discouraged. A very casual and laid back style of game play.  Controls are simple and easy to learn and use. _childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are easy to learn, the story is comical and the cartoon-y art style really makes TIME LOADER stand out. The different upgrades you acquire are well spaced out, realistic and fun. The story is short enough to play in one sitting, although there are 4 separate endings so if you want the full experience you will probably want to allocate ~5 hours total for this game.8/10 Overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: I love a metroidvania game, and while this is more of a platformer with metroidvania elements, I still found it quite charming.  The platforming is good, the design is fantastic, and the story is compelling enough to give you a good reason to be doing the things you're doing. _childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Short physics-focused platformer. Credit for the level of polish in the environments and the fun it is jumping around them with the robot. Points off for the puzzles that are rarely challenging, which was a shame - they missed a real opportunity here for more physics based puzzles, like a 2D Portal. The story was cliched and they could've done without it (and the alternative endings stuff). Pick it up on a sale for a couple of hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Time Loader is a story-based platformer. The game description calls it a puzzle-platformer but there really aren’t any puzzles, you almost always do the only thing that you can to progress the game. The controls are alright however at times they feel a little clunky.The story is your typical time travel story. A disgruntled man is unhappy about his life and he wants to change his past to fix his problems. Instead of going back himself he builds a small robot to fix the past for him. As expected things go wrong and now you have to undo all the changes you made while avoiding a time paradox.The game has 4 different endings, however you don’t have to play through the game 4 times to see all the endings. After beating the game once you can select a chapter to change certain key events that affect the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Well done, well thought out! Good time. Short game. The secret ending is lame (imo) and it takes away from all the stuff you changed throughout your gameplay so you don't get to see what you effected. but the A ending (which I would've gotten if I didn't do the secret one) is a fitting end. There are 2 other endings which are "sad" if you don't get the A ending. Just watch the other ones on YT after you see which ending you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a protagonist as lovable as they get (really hoping for my own rc time loader one day!).Puzzles are challenging enough to keep you interested, but rarely frustrating. Imagine a cute puzzler with a chill soundtrack and lots of Rube Goldberg type encounters.Plays extremely well on Steam Deck with only the odd graphical glitch, but never crashed or got stuck anywhere I shouldn't have been. Thoroughly enjoying my time with this one so far and I kinda hope I don't finish it anytime soon so I can extend the joy!
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Time Loader is a labour of love, the attention to detail, fantastic level design, physics, ingenious puzzle elements. Fabulous sound design and not forgetting the excellent soundtrack by Alexey Nechaev. Well done Team, I look forward to any future games you may produce. A short but sweeeeet adventure, with an option to return to chapters for  collectables or change events...I think. Just played through it initially.It would have been nice to have an option to turn off highlighted grab points and voice tips.P.S. Ignore my Playtime as I was in offline mode at some points so the game is longer than 79 Minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little physics based platformer. The climbing and jumping are good. Grabbing and manipulating objects can be a bit janky as well as aiming and throwing things. Some puzzles are little confusing as what to do where you don't know that an object can do something, and a little more variety could be fun like the power you get later on. the story is pretty meh and it is short. But its still solid. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Nice graphics, relaxing soundtrack, gameplay physics are OK, story and concept are cool. Cons: Way too easy. Spent too much time redoing the same sections over and over after missing a jump. Slow pacingThis game would have greatly benefited from difficulty levels. There is zero critical thinking skills involved and barely any gaming skills required.The "puzzles" are unbelievably easy. As soon as you come anywhere near something you need to interact with a huge graphic box with arrows pops up on the screen.  The entire game is basically hold left or right, occasionally pressing the jump key until you see a box appear on the screen, rinse and repeat. Its very obviously a children's game and that's fine but it could have been a much better game if you just let the player try to figure out some of the puzzles on their own instead of immediately shoving the solutions in their face.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the story and the fact that the little robot cares about adam, the game is good and fun to play, finding uprades and new gear was very thoughtfull and fun, as an adult I had a great "TIME" pun intended playing this and recommend this game as it has no curse words, the moments with the cat can be slightly frightning but thats more because of the music and sound effect in those scenes.The only thing I did not like about this Game is the: Pegi 16 rated Lord Of The Rings reference which kids will want to know where it's from and that can potentialy lead to them watching movies not appropiate for them, and kids these days have lot's of acces to the internet, which is the responsibilities of the parents however kids are smart and can circumvent a lot of parent controls so I would say it be wise for the Developer to remove that Pegi 16 rated reference and replace it with something else, that would be very helpfull for parents.And i would love to see more of these games and dlc's to acompany it, and more gear and upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little gameNot many hours are needed for completion, but the replay value is immenseYou control a little robot, sent back in time to save your creator from a debilitating accidentYou need to try and remove that which causes the accident to happenOn the way you will need to gather more capabilitiesTighten or remove screws with a screwdriver, or fix electronics with a soldering ironAlso, scattered throughout the game are glyphs, which you will need to collect to unlock the secret endingSpeaking of endings, there are three (not counting the secret one)Each one is unlocked depending on what you do during the gameThere might not be much to this game, but you will be replaying it many timesNot just to see all the different endings, but collecting the glyphas, and aiming for 100%

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first release version and got to admit that the game was almost perfectly polished. I encountered only two logical bugs during my walkthrough, both of them were remedied via loading from the last checkpoint, so it was no deal in both cases. I also saw minor funny bugs with graphics, but they were short-term and didn't spoil the gameplay. For the release version, it's a huge win, so all the credits go to the QA team and the devs who were patient enough to beat all the bugs before we players saw the final product :) As for the plot, graphics, atmosphere, mechanics and duration, I'll keep it short: all the aspects here are decent even for a picky player, but for me all of them are brilliant.I've been waiting for this game since Feb 2021 when I first played the demo, and I was def happy to be able to play the full game the same year. You did a great job, guys! Keep up the good work!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little puzzle/platformer, with a melancholy story of childhood and inevitability layered on top.  You play as a small robot which goes back in time to try to change the fate of your creator.Neither the puzzles nor the platforming are too difficult (except for a few control issues – more on that later), but this gives you time to take in the detailed world.  You explore your childhood home, visiting each room, and making small changes to accomplish your goal.  There are so many great references to objects from the 90’s.  Clearly there was a lot of thought and effort into designing the interiors, and I loved how the environments changed when visiting them in different timelines.I ran into a few frustrations with the controls, mostly around the throwing mechanic, but especially the grappling hook mechanic.  Luckily there aren’t too many puzzles involving those, although it did make the ending more frustrating than needed .  I also encountered a few bugs where I had to restart the level to fix a stuck object, or reset the state of one of the objectives.  For example, when trying to  I couldn’t advance without restarting the level.  Fortunately, there are plenty of checkpoints.The game is linear and actually quite short, though it looks like you can go back and try to discover all the secret items (I missed a few) to try to get a different ending.  This is a strong creative effort from a small team.
_childDocuments_.name: Time Loader

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of thought this took place in North America considering the NA SNES and outlet style.  But if that's the case then it's /ˈsɒdər/. The L is silent.Fun game.  I wouldn't call it a puzzle game though since the "puzzles" are SO simple.  You just move from one object to the next.  You don't setup any elaborate contraptions.  But it is fun moving around your environment.The only negative I have is the music.  They claim "nostalgic music" but it's nothing but slow droning music.  It gets a little synth wave at points but that's 80s, not 90s.What would have been a better idea is have the robots program time travel and download into different bodies.  In the past you have slow power hungry servos and wheels, in the present you have big dog style legs, and in the future you can hover.  Then make the ultimate story that the robots program acts as a virus and you have to double back and clean up your mess to fix the timeline.

detailed_description: Wishlist my next game- UVSU About the Game Toodee and Topdee is a 2D Platformer and a Top-Down Puzzler hybrid. _childDocuments_.review: Not for me, but still a good game.So, imo this game has some really good ideas but struggles with them quite a bit. Look at the achievements, only around half the people playing finish the first world (out of 5).Major points:+ Art style and animations are clear.+ Sound effects are wonderful, and the soundtrack is soothing and encouraging to help while solving puzzles+ Collectibles are rewarded for solving levels after switching characters as few times as possible (encourages planning ahead and out-of-box thinking)+ Collectibles are rewarded for  in levels with enemies, outside of boss battles. (Also encourages critical thinking)+ Clever usage of platforming enemies and moving hazards, temple world uses fire/water in interesting ways+ Difficulty settings were added in a post-release update, allowing you to get extra HP/invincibility, slow down the game's speed, and give Twodee extra jumps. From my experience these don't affect your ability to collect some collectibles. ~ Game puts equal amounts of emphasis on puzzle-solving and twitch reflexes*~ Co-op is turn-based, so it mostly exists to give you someone to talk to while playing an effectively single-player game~ No option to skip a level if you're stuck on a puzzle~ No guides or hints in-game if you can't solve a puzzle~ No option to reset the level to when you last switched to a character (such as if you accidentally put yourself in an unwinnable situation in the last 3 seconds)~ Story is lighthearted and doesn't take itself too seriously; it's charming, but I never laughed~ Around 100 levels with varying quality- Topdee gameplay can get confusing as grid positions slightly differ when switching between the characters.I would prefer to see a block indicator where Twodee's hitbox will be upon switching back to them when playing as Topdee. - It's entirely plausible to finish levels without understanding how certain mechanics work; the Thunder block is my prime example. Had to look up a guide to understand how it actually worked- Twodee's roles in some levels is to perform tight platforming, and making a mistake means restarting an entire level.- Boss battles are extremely frustrating, especially the 2nd world's boss; boss hitboxes can be a bit weird due to the perspective and result in deaths from attacks that don't always have a clear range. It's not super clear how to dodge enemy attacks; as Topdee a lot of attacks missed.- Enemies speed up dramatically when playing as Topdee, hampered by the fact that the AI becomes more aggressive- Collectibles are rewarded for speedrunning... in a puzzle platformer? With emphasis on puzzles? These basically require you to replay levels- World 2 is harder than following levels by a decent margin, to the extent I thought the rest of the game would be more difficult. Worlds 3 and 4 are more puzzle-oriented and forgiving with mistakes. *I think a lot of people are getting turned off by the game from this. In the first world alone, it starts to become clear that the game wants you to be able to pull off precision jumps and maneuvers with both characters. Now, I'm no platforming expert but I've beaten the main game in Celeste, and I'm no puzzle master but I've beaten both Portal games; this game doesn't have the same flow as either, though, and for a few main reasons. - Making a logical mistake as Topdee means difficult jumps pulled off with Twodee meant nothing, restart the level- Broke temporary blocks as Twodee, after solving a lengthy puzzle as Topdee, and can't reach the goal? Restart the level- Occasionally puzzles expect precision timing when switching characters or moving blocks with Topdee- Zero indicator a level has become unbeatable from placing a block in a certain position The worst aspects of platformers and puzzle games overlap here due to the game's nature. I honestly planned to write a scathing review after needing a guide for certain puzzles in the temple world (3), especially after one of the puzzles expects you to know that  While some levels shine really well (such as a stage where Topdee has to rearrange blocks to deflect lasers for Twodee, except the blocks are affected by gravity), other levels barely use the mechanic and simply have you switching back and forth to lure a pig to a switch or something. The levels aren't balanced; some are genuinely amazing and creative, and require you to think ahead without feeling unfair. Others expect players to know about mechanics that are never properly explained; these levels could probably be cut and the game would immediately be better. If the devs read this, I like your game quite a bit. But I genuinely think that making puzzles that don't require precision jumps or timing would be better, or making the levels more based on a player's reflexes. As it stands, the game straddles the line between fun and pure frustration for me, to the point where I have no plans to finish it. TL;DR: Look at achievements for how many people beat world 1.

_childDocuments_.review: When I came across Toodee and Topdee for the first time, which I can’t remember was due to randomly browsing Steam or when it was featuring its demo for a Steam game festival, I was intrigued. Well, it already got my attention with the title and it being a platformer, but it had a unique twist of switching between the 2D and top-down perspectives. And when I tried the demo to see how it played and how the levels will generally be like, I knew I had to keep my eye on it. And well, it’s now out so let’s see how it is.We start from the beginning, where we witness the creation of a universe where all the different perspectives games can be in reside in their own little worlds. The creator, Aleph, soon comes across some problems. The first being stability, which was solved by creating a Semicolon; and the second being the unintentional creation of Glitches, which Aleph created an assistant named Toodoo so these Glitches can be kept track of so they can all be fixed later and to help out. But as Aleph came to only needing to create one more world, Toodoo became worried. As when Aleph finishes up the last world and finally has time to deal with those pesky Glitches, Toodoo won’t have any purpose anymore. So Toodoo, determined not to be thrown away, steals the Semicolon. Causing all of the worlds to collide into one.And this is when two characters from two different worlds meet. Toodee, from the 2D universe, and Topdee, from the top-down universe, against all chances gets put in the same area and after getting the news of what happened from a newly born Glitch, they decide to join forces and find the missing Semicolon.The story here is pretty cute, well aside from the whole worlds colliding and terrible things are happening part. The dialog really hits that perfect spot for me where it’s cute, funny, and simple, but not so much where it harms the game either by being annoying or not properly conveying what it wants to. I looked forward to every cutscene as it never failed to make me smile as Toodee and Topdee talk to each other or to other characters.To find the Semicolon you’ll have to take advantage of both perspectives available to you by switching between both Topdee and Toodee. Both of them will interact with the world differently. Toodee is the platformer as he can jump across platforms and gaps, while Topdee can move boxes, but will need to use these boxes to create a bridge for gaps. Not to mention some aspects like boxes or the characters themselves will freeze once you switch to the other. The puzzles start simple, like having Topdee move boxes so Toodee can use them as platforms and grabbing keys to unlock walls, it does start to get more complex as more elements are introduced. Soon you’ll have puzzles that will require good timing to have a block drop and pause at the right moment, having you think about the order you do things in, or avoid deadly animals that go on a basic path for Toodee, but will full on pursue Topdee (and looking scary at that). And it will only get more difficult  and complex to get both Topdee and Toodee to that level-ending portal as you get more levels under your belt.That’s not to say that it suddenly dumps challenging levels on you. There are multiple worlds you’ll be going to which will introduce something new. It gives you enough levels to introduce you to the what’s new and giving you multiple scenarios so when those hard levels do come in, you’ll know what you probably need to do, but will need to figure out how to use Topdee and Toodee to get to your end goal.Toodee and Topdee really knows when it’s starting to overstay its welcome and I like how there weren’t that many levels in each world. Despite the interesting feature of switching between perspectives, I did feel times where I just wanted it to end and luckily those times came when I was nearing a boss fight.At the end of each world, you’ll get into a boss battle where you’ll be fighting corrupted guardians. These are pretty fun as you’ll need to learn their attack patterns, either by quick thinking or through many deaths, as you need to dodge attacks and find the perfect opportunity that will let the boss get damaged. Not to mention that these bosses will change up their patterns when they get hurt. Their attacks will affect Topdee and Toodee differently, so you’ll need to switch between who can handle it the best, and some attacks can change depending on which perspective you’re on, which can give you an opening to damaging them or a way to not die if the other can’t dodge the attack themselves without getting hit.If you are having problems, whether it’s because you have no idea what the solution is or just tired of dying in one hit, there are some difficulty options you can turn on like giving you more health, air jumps, and lets you carry heavy boxes. I do wish there was some undo button, especially for Topdee as it is easy to push a box in a hole without meaning to or switch at the wrong time for falling boxes, as it does get annoying when you get everything right and unscathed, but have to redo everything due to a simple mistake of going forward one too many. For that, I do recommend not playing this on controller, as it’s easier to make these simple mistakes, or try to remember to only use the D-pad as it’s a bit imprecise when you use the stick.Though, for those looking for more of a challenge (if some of the harder levels aren’t enough for you that is) there is another aspect that you might not notice until the end. There are actually three different challenges where the indicator is pretty lowkey, acting like it’s just part of the level decoration, until your attention is brought to it. And that are the ladybugs. There are three different ladybug colors that represent a specific challenge and they can be hard to get. All levels will have at least two of the ladybugs where it challenges you to complete the level with the least number of switches, represented by a blue ladybug, and complete the level as fast as you can before the red ladybug flies away. With some levels having purple ladybugs, challenging you to not kill any of the deadly animals. If you do get all ladybugs you will unlock a secret portal to secret levels for you to do and get an additional (secret) ending.Considering this game does have two characters working together, there is a co-op mode if you have someone to play with. I didn’t dive much into it, but it basically acts like if you swap controllers as you’ll take control of either Topdee or Toodee and you can decide if swapping can be done by both of you or just by the one that is active. And it might be even more helpful having another head to bounce puzzle solutions off of. Though probably not so much for the puzzles that require good timing.Toodee and Topdee promised a unique spin on platformers and it delivered. While it did straddle the line of staying too long and getting frustrating at times for me, switching between 2D and top-down perspectives to find a way to get past hazards and get both of them to the portal to solve the level was interesting and challenging, the boss battles were fun, and the dialog was delightful and funny. Not to mention the optional ladybug challenges that will make this even more worth it if you decide to go for them. If you like puzzle platformers and looking for an interesting twist on the genre, you can’t go wrong with Toodee and Topdee.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5h (19/20 achievements, finished the game) No. Yes (6 achievements). Yes (1 achievement).Toodee and Topdee come from different worlds. Toodee comes from a sidescroller, platformer world while Topdee comes from a top-down, block-pushing world.  combine both mechanics into a puzzle platformer with a bit of precise platformer element in some of its levels. It offers 100+ levels with some bonus and tutorial levels.- 100+ levels with a unique main mechanic in each chapter- Unique boss fights- Accessibility options to make the game easier- Some levels require insane, precise timing, especially the bonus levels- It's hard to precisely control Topdee to get what you want- Toodee hardly can jump after landing, causing issues on some levels- Cheap boss rush level at one of the levelsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650Despite coming from two different genres, the designs of Toodee and Topdee look similar in style. The only difference is from the perspective, where Toodee looks flatter, mainly because it's in a side-scroller view, while Topdee has more depth due to its top-down view. Since both of their worlds merged, the perspective of the level changes depending on who is in charge. Toodee's world is on the sidescroller view while Topdee's is in the isometric view. I like how smooth the transition between both perspectives is. That being said, the visuals themselves are decent, although I found the character sprites to be bland.I like how the game gives some background on how our two hero's worlds merged. There are also some references to basic programming in the dialogue, both in the story and in one character. I like how the latter one was designed, and how it actually makes sense for them to do what they do. The story itself is quite straightforward, but I like how each character and boss have their own personality.Since two worlds merged into one, you need both Toodee and Topdee to solve the levels. Topdee's world is top-down, so it seems that they can walk in the sky based on Toodee's perspective. On the other hand, Topdee has what Toodee doesn't have: jumping.Both characters need to cooperate to reach the goal. Topdee can help by pushing blocks for Toodee to walk on, while Toodee can help to drop some blocks since their world has gravity, pass through holes that can't be passed by Topdee, and destroy brittle platforms to open the path.The game has 5 main chapters, with 2 extras in it. The first 4 chapters have 20 levels with a boss fight at the end of each chapter. Each chapter will showcase a different main obstacle for you to try. However, I don't like the obstacles introduced in the latter half of the game. The levels in the first two chapters can be completed in several seconds, but some levels in the latter chapters might force you to spend minutes. Moreover, some of those levels, especially the one in the bonus chapter, rely too much on timing. I don't like precision platformers with hardly any room for error, and the last few chapters of the game are just that.Despite you having to be precise to finish the levels, the controls aren't helping with that. Topdee walks too fast, and it's hard to precisely control them. The thing is, they can push blocks just by slightly touching them, and it's easy to push them by accident. As for Toodee, while they are good for the most part, they can't seem to jump right away after landing, and there are times when they automatically jump when they are on the edge of a platform. I had issues on some levels because of it and had to resort to using the accessibility options for some since I couldn't seem to get it right.The boss fights are unique. I like how they are designed, especially since they require the cooperation of both characters to beat. The character switching is mainly done whenever the boss is changing on a certain phase, which is triggered by your character's action. It can take some time to remember the pattern and get the muscle memory to beat the boss, but I had fun beating them.However, I found the boss rush at one of the bonus levels to look cheap. Since the game mainly only has 1 health, you need to beat them without taking damage, but it can be hard to do so, especially since you have to fight 4 bosses in a row. It seems as if the developer is running out of ideas for a boss and put this feature in. I would appreciate it more if there is a brand new boss that I can fight, even if they have more health and are more difficult to beat.I finished the game in 9.5h with most of its contents unlocked. The game offers some sort of challenge by finishing the level below a certain time limit and switching characters as little as possible, which I did mostly through the accessibility option to save time. It isn't difficult to finish the game as long as you use them.The game offers an accessibility option for casual players. You technically can cheese most of the levels with it, except some that require you to use your wits. Despite that, you still can use the accessibility option to save some time on those levels. You can finish the whole game and get all achievements but one with these options.Achievement hunters need to suffer to 100% it, though. There is one achievement that requires you to finish the whole game without dying or retrying. You need to go from the very first level in the chapter to the last one, which is usually the boss fight, without returning to the main menu. You can't tweak the accessibility option for this and I just find it ridiculous to finish, especially since I had to retry a lot of times just to finish one level at the latter part of the game. I did try to finish most levels without accessibility options at least once, so I know that it's impossible for me to get this without spending tons of hours into the game, which I'd rather not do. The worst part is that there is content hidden behind this achievement. I know the content is trivial, but it still sucks.The accessibility options in  help to make me enjoy the game. It's a difficult game by nature, one which I don't like, and I had to complain a lot just to finish some of the later levels. Moreover, the controls make it hard for me to precisely move my character as I want. I still enjoyed it to some extent, but I don't think casual players should play it. Some levels require you to act fast, which can be an issue if you are not that good, even with accessibility options. The game is best for hardcore players who are looking for some challenge in both wits and reflexes.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the concept, loved the demo, but the game ended up being 90% platforming reflexes, 10% puzzle (or less). Not what I was expecting.Probably great if you are into Mario hacks, as this is structurally identical to plenty of one-screen-challenge hacks, where you die repeatedly until you do the trick right. To beat a level you need to do a lot more "I avoided the enemies and nailed the jumps right" than you need "I figured out the puzzle!" Other reviews (positive and negative) seem to indicate this is how the rest of the game will go on, only more so.So I'm getting a refund because that's really not what I was hoping for or expecting. The rest of the game is great; graphics and sound are perfect for what this game wants to be, and I even think the writing was fun and clever! (I think almost NO writing in games in fun or clever, so good job there.) I just can't get into repetitive precision platforming.7/10; do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the demo a while back, I was really looking forward to this. But right as the demo ends, the issues start. The demo ends with: here would be a bossfight in the full game, cya! But then you play the actual boss fight and its the most frustrating thing. You have to do the same tedious task 3 times and if you are ever hit during it, you can start over. So thats when I turned invincibility on. But after the boss fight come the animal levels which continue the trend of this being no longer about solving puzzles but about reflexes. There is one where you have to navigate a pike through spikes and if the pig dies you have to restart. Or the one where your topdown guy is stuck in a tiny room with a pig and you have to use the pig to press a button multiple times. So every time you don't react fast enough after switching you die. There even was one level that starts you in the path of a pig and you have 1/2 second to react before getting hit. Invincibility it is then. But the problem with invincibility is that afterwards there are no puzzles left. You don't have to solve anything in the later levels as everything comes down to reflexes and timing. So much for this being a puzzle platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a fan of platformers. But when i saw this game i was amazed by how cute it looked and how interesting the perspective change seemed to be. In the beginning, you have puzzles, very little reflex based levels and a ton of fun solving the maps. Eventually the reflex levels become more and more until the game is just not fun anymore. My friend and I have spent over 2 hours on the fourth world already and have still not made it to the bossfight in level 20. The levels are so painful that if we eventually solved one, we couldn't stomach another.The levels are one thing, the other is the collectibles you get for solving a level in a certain amount of time, only switching characters a certain amount of time and not killing "NPCs". Not switching too often and not killing enemies is often doable but we have not managed to get a single "solve this level in this short time" colletible (even with perfect execution on the solution) because that time is just so damn short. The later levels are so frustrating that i wouldn't even want to TRY and play them again for the collectibles. Worst thing is, that if you get all of these previously names collectibles, you unlock even MORE COLLECTIBLES for which you have to complete all levels AGAIN. I am even now thinking of letting the rest of the game collect dust in the depths of my steam library and never touching it again, all these extra challenges don't give me any more reason to try and continue, it even supports my decision to just never look at this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: for  with the theme "Combine two incompatible genres". The result was so good that the dev(s) went ahead and spent a lot of time to turn that prototype into a full game. I myself first knew about this game by playing it at Kongregate website, many years ago, and I'm very pleased with the fully complete game available on Steam.The gameplay is great. The soundtrack is good. The graphics are a gorgeous blend of 2D pixel art with little bits of 3D rendering. Still, the 3D effects are subtle, and blend in with the vibrant aesthetic of the rest of the game. I even believe some of those 3D graphics were built using nothing but 2D sprites.The writing is also quite good, with some meta jokes about the game itself and about game/software development. It's silly, but II think it's silly fun.The levels themselves are mostly well-designed, but some of them require "A-ha!" moments, and those can keep you stuck for a while. (I kept stuck with a tentative solution in my head for level 4-19 for weeks, until I gave up and looked up the proper way to solve it.) Some levels require quicker reactions, other levels require a restart if you make a wrong move (there is no "Undo"). Thankfully, all levels are short.The bosses look great and are very interesting to fight. Unfortunately, the boss fights are also quite repetitive and end up falling into the trap (or mis-design) of having a long invulnerable sequence followed by a short vulnerable moment. This makes the boss fights drag on and on while the player is waiting.The game also has many configurable options, and also a handful of difficulty settings Is the game too difficult? You can increase the amount of hitpoints, or you can make the game slower. These settings can ensure the game is playable to all kinds of players.In summary: I recommend this game. It's good and charming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty unique platforming experience. I found the idea really entertaining and intuitive with each world you progress through. I know this was just made by two brothers and you can sense their level of passion in a lot of the details especially with the story. The characters have tons of personality that makes for some hilarious moments during the cut scenes.As far as gameplay, I felt that the level design had an exponential progression in difficulty. Often times there is grace granted to players if they do make a mistake along the way. But as you get to later levels I found it painfully difficult to finish some of the levels. This had me looking up guides on specific levels and being shocked at how pinpoint accurate/perfect you have to be to get through levels. Also, prior to the 1.0.1.0 update in January the boss fights were unforgiving. A single mistake and you would have to restart from the beginning. Thankfully they included checkpoints and some other changes to make life easier on the players. This was honestly why I put the game down for a month until I saw the update that allowed me to beat one of the later bosses. Overall, I loved the concept, funny moments, and challenge the game brought despite wanting to break my controller at times. A solid 7.5/10 to me. If you like a platformer with a challenge and have a long weekend I'd recommend giving this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling perspective-swapping premise that's explored thoroughly in many fiendish puzzles.All the elements for a lovable retro-inspired indie game are here. Simply put, the music is catchy, the controls are tight, there's a simple yet charming story, and the sprites are appealing. I particularly like how enemies and bosses seamlessly shift between either perspective. There are plenty of mechanics that receive strong, hands-off tutorials and are then expanded upon in a satisfying manner.Although, it's a bit unnerving that a thoughtful puzzle game like Topdee and Toodee would have a death counter. The main thing that really took me out of the game was the repetition and precision required for later levels and especially boss fights [Edit: Boss fights now have checkpoints]. While bosses all had an excellent concept behind them, the sudden importance of timing was a jarring change of pace. Plus, it was frustrating to have to get the long boss sequences right all in one go. As the complexity of puzzles grew, so did my desire for an undo/rewind button. Thankfully, a generous selection of accessibility options let me tweak the level of discomfort I was willing to stomach. Still, that didn’t stop me from putting the game down after a few final less-than-stellar sessions.Overall, Toodee and Topdee is a great core concept with plenty of ideas to back it up, but it’s not yet ingenious enough to be wholly intuitive and captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: I happened upon Toodee and Topdee around a year ago while browsing Steam's upcoming releases, immediately tried the demo, and instantly put it atop my list of most anticipated indies. With a prototype designed for Ludum Dare 41's theme of "two incompatible genres," it asks: "What happens when a platform game and a top down game are combined?" The answer: bliss! It's everything I was hoping for, and more!The platforming genre has been around for forever, and I've played countless entries, yet it's still my favorite genre. But creating something unlike any other game in the genre these days isn't easy.  Toodee and Topdee takes a simple concept and iterates flawlessly with a boldly ambitious and unique approach. The clever puzzles evolve nicely, introducing tricky new elements and concepts throughout, ranging from straight-forward to mind-boggling. A level could take you 20 seconds on your first try, or 30 minutes and countless deaths. Without spoiling anything, levels - particularly towards the end - just keep getting crazier and crazier. The closing sections, along with the brilliantly brutal boss battles, create some amazing high points! The presentation is great, especially the sound design, and a silly humor pervades the entire journey. I followed the development a lot, so I knew some of what to expect, but it still managed to throw in plenty of surprises. My playthrough took me about 6.5 hours, but I'm itching to hop back in and master everything via the added challenges. I don't want to explain or say anything more.If you enjoy a puzzle platformer, I'd recommend going into this one with as little knowledge as possible. You just might find it to be something extremely special - or, like me, maybe even your Game of the Year!

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzle game was pretty difficult. If you're looking for a fun and easy two player game, this may not be for you. This game has such a pleasant art-style and I really enjoyed the banter between our two protagonists. The gimmicks of each world added onto each other in a satisfying way, and each level culminated in a boss fight that allowed you to flex your brainpower that got you to the end of each stage. World 4 was particularly hard for me, and I wish so badly that there was a hint system on some levels. Turning on the easy modifiers made it feel too easy and I felt like that would rob from the first time experience of solving the puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: A nice and polished puzzle game, where you have to switch, in real time, from a 2D platform to a 3D top down box pushing (Sokoban-like). You play with both characters at the same time, and deciding when to switch between the two is part of every puzzle.In these games the level design is a fundamental factor, and I can say it's well made. They also tried to not get it boring, with every level throwing at you something new or different, while putting some humour in the mix.Of course, it gets very hard in later levels.I wouldn't call it super innovative, as somebody says, but it's for sure unique in its own way.Fans of the genre shouldn't pass this one, while others... could.

_childDocuments_.review: What started off as a game-jam entry with a unique concept, evolved into a full game that looks fantastic and is both fun and challenging.This game is a hybrid of two game genres. The levels are quite challenging too.The animations, art-style and sprite-work is also some of the best I've seen. Especially the way 2D enemies seamlessly switch to Top-down mode.
