_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others You might have a lot of friends but few are the friends that can help you save the Universe.Toodee and Topdee is an adventure produced by two brothers, Gonen and Ori, that mixes action, 2D Platforming, and Top-Down Puzzling in a fantastic way, with a light-hearted sense of humor and a peculiar graphic style.The story starts at the beginning, I mean literally, the beginning of the Universe and how the planets were created by an Entity called Aleph. Each world was vastly different, one world was completely in 2D in which they could jump while another world was completely in top-down perspective where the inhabitants could move boxes. To keep track of potential errors, also known as glitches, Aleph created Toodoo, his right hand.As Aleph continues populating the Universe things started to get a little bit out of hand. To help restore order he created the Semicolon, which put everything back in balance. Nearing the end of this process, of creating new worlds, Toodoo realized that his purpose was reaching his final moments. He then decided to steal the all-important Semicolon.Everything fell into chaos with the absence of the Semicolon. This is where we meet our heroes Toodee and Topdee, that never should've been able to interact with each other because they are from different worlds. But, since their worlds merged together they now have to work in unison to retrieve the semicolon and restore the balance to the Universe.Gameplay-wise is where this game shines. Each stage is a unique puzzle where the player has to switch between both protagonist and their different perspectives to reach the goal. The fact that the player has to achieve this with just directional controls and one action button, makes it seem simple at first but you quickly discover how deep the rabbit hole goes.The devs made brilliant use of each aspect of the perspective and how they interact with each other in many intuitive ways. The player has to think beyond the perspective itself and combine both efforts to solve tasks that at first glance seem trivial for one character. Imagine having to jump off a box but being unable to move it, having to rely on the other character and their unique ability to reach that end.There are 4 Worlds, each with their individual theme, to traverse before reaching the hiding place of the Semicolon. Each of these worlds is characterized by 20 stages that increase in difficulty and complexity, culminating in an epic face-off against the Guardian of that realm.To help create the atmosphere we have to mention the soundtrack that fits like a glove and does an awesome job at conveying the appropriate mood for the situation. Especially the boss themes, they are all bangers.It is possible to enjoy this puzzle title alone or with a friend, through local co-op or Steam remote play. Personally, I would recommend playing this in co-op. Let's be honest, two heads think better than one and the added chaos makes for a good couple of giggles.Toodee and Topdee is a really fun take on the puzzle-platformer that adds that little something spicy to the genre. In every single new level, there is a new twist that makes things feel fresh and expand what the player has learned before. With 7 hours of gameplay, a lot of brain cells burned and a lot of screams of success I still feel the urge to replay certain levels. Definitely a title that is easy to recommend.Oh, by the way, the game doesn't end with returning the semicolon to its former place. There's actually more to find, you just need to pay attention to the ladybugs.This review was written in co-op mode ( Thanks Samusin! ).
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee features inventive puzzles that feels fresh from start to finish - each world introduces new mechanics, so it never even approaches "repetitive" territory. The music is catchy, and the graphics are colorful and fun. I enjoyed the programming jokes littered throughout the world as well. I wish it was a bit longer, but it's hard to fault the game when the experience is so tightly crafted.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one to review to be quite honest.As a simple yes or no I'd say yes, this game is worth playing. It's a really neat concept and has a lot of charm. The story works well with how it discusses making games through the eyes of those who are in the game.Here's my more in depth thoughts of it:So if you just want a puzzle game that explores these mechanics I think this might disappoint you a bit honestly. The first world is a lot of puzzles but I think it quickly delves into more execution tests than actual puzzle solving. If you're expecting that I think it can work, but it's a weird thing for this game to be. It also can become frustrating because of this, messing up a jump means you have to resolve the entire puzzle again. I had times I knew exactly how to solve the puzzle, but I just barely missed a jump and had to restart. The controls are good, but have a few quirks to get used to. The platformer character isn't quite what I expected, especially with some of the requirements the game wants, but it works fine. I think the topdown character had more issues for me. When you place a block it takes a second to actually put it down, which means if you want to place a block and then turn around this often means the block isn't put down in the right spot. It's something you can get used to but I didn't like it myself.The camera is probably the aspect that bugged me the most. Obviously the platformer camera is fine and shows the screen, but the topdown camera had some issues for me. It's at a isometric perspective, but it ends up making it hard to gauge the distance sometimes. Another thing you can get used to but I didn't personally like it.Spoiler stuff below:All in all it's a really neat concepts with some decisions I disagree with. But I bet others might enjoy those decisions, go ahead and try it yourself.Also if you're worried about length, it took me 4 hours without going for the extra content.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying this game. (Granted, I got stuck on one of the early puzzles.) The gimmick is unique. The platforming can be fiddly, but I can't really complain about that, because the Difficulty menu gives some generous options. Still, I would like to be able to bind a button to be able to toggle slowdown. And another button to hold to reset the puzzle. A lot of these puzzles, it's very easy to get into an unwinnable situation, and I'd rather not be forced to open the menu every time, especially when there are plenty of unused buttons on the gamepad.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, novel concept for a game, and it really delivers on the promise of the concept. Levels just keep introducing cool new things to do with the core mechanic of the game, and new ways you have to think to solve the puzzles. All of the levels are equally playable as solo or co-op, and the co-op is enormous fun.Many games with a new, novel mechanic don't actually work well in practice. The idea might seem cool in concept, but the gameplay ends up being tedious, unintuitive, or repetitive. But every level in Toodee and Topdee is genuinely fun and satisfying, and keeps showing just how many clever things the designer can do with the concept.Absolutely recommend this game to fans of puzzles, platformers, and lateral thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic puzzler! Unique mechanics, lovely aesthetic, all around banger!10D/10DAfter playing the demo for this game, I was wanting more and more. Dietzribi definitely brought it with the full release!Brilliant puzzles all around, with a smooth difficulty curve (with the exception of the last 2 puzzles, which will literally melt your brain). I had so much fun with this, I've started going back through and seeing how fast I can do each level after I had finished the game. It took me around 4-5 hours to finish myself. I won't give any spoilers for the game, but I can say that the puzzles always felt fresh all the way through.The game looks great, each world has it's own identity and switching between the different planes is a smooth transition too. There was a lot of attention to detail when giving the 2D-3D feel for each of the blocks and enemies. Character design is simple and effective, and the details of the extra characters were some of my favourite too (The "Glitches" in the game have actual code flowing down their bodies".The writing is funny, and the story is easy to follow. I loved Toodee's attitude in the game, and Topdee was a little naive sweetheart I fell in love with by the end of the story. A real feelgood vibeThe sound design is great, with variants of the soundtrack being played depending on who you are playing at the time, or even changing underwater. You can listen to the music however long you want, it's so relaxing and pleasant. Another one of my favourite OSTs from indie games!GOTY contender in my books! Definitely worth picking up, I highly, highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: There is 2 games in this game. One is the stages where you will use some platform skill but more often your puzzle solver skill like in Braid or in Baba Is You.Sometimes puzzles can be hard but still very pleasant.The other game is the boss fights. You will need a lot more platform skills. Soon enough it begins to be exhausting when you understand the mechanics to kill the boss but you are forced to redo the whole fight because of a little mistake that kills you because you cannot be hit once without be killed. Its' like a big difficulty wall compared to the stages.It's not like I don't like difficulty (I've done Celeste & Super Meat Boy), but in other games, the level before the boss fight trains you & prepares you for the difficulty of the boss.I ended up setting up the difficulty mode to add infinite lives for those fights and thankfully not spending 90% of my game time in them.I recommend you to do the same if you are in the same situation.Other than that, this 2D/3D puzzle game are really my thing and the universe is really sweet.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept with nice writing & characters - plagued by awful, annoying puzzles and a significant demand for skill.The tutorial and chapter 1 are great. Really fun to switch between characters and make them help each other solve puzzles. Sadly this is far as it goes because soon after (chapter 2 or 3) the game starts shifting into a strange direction. It forces you to abuse odd game mechanics, perform under strict timing, and generally work with very unfun puzzle mechanics. The game starts being too difficult both in terms of understanding puzzle solutions as well as pulling them off.If you look at achievements stats you can clearly see that the vast majority of players drop the game halfway through. Such a decline in completion is true for almost every game on steam, yet here the decline is much more severe than usual. Chapter 4 introduces the "control two characters simultaneously" crap (with a horribly annoying implementation of it as well) and look how much it affected the completion stats. People just drop this game past the first chapters!But I kept going until I've collected every ladybug in the game (extra rewards for completing every level very fast, with fewest swaps etc). Less than 1% players have done it. My reward? Unlocking the final challenge which is "beat each chapter in the game without dying or restarting". Not only I am already beyond annoyed of this game but I really don't think I have the skill or patience that is required to pull this off. I am not prepared to learn 21 levels at a time by muscle memory and play through them flawlessly - especially since the very last boss is ruthlessly difficult and inconsistent.I wish I never bothered to 100% the game. You shouldn't trust positive reviews of people under like 5 hours, they've never actually beaten the game to see how awful it becomes later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Topdee and Toodee is incredibly unique, its a great hybrid of platforming and top-down gameplay. But with 90 levels and some of them being extremely quick to complete the game feels short, most especially when paired with its $20 price tag. The most recent sale sells the game at $10, this is how I feel this game should be priced. I would have loved to see some form of a level creator and possibly a few more mechanics to play with. This would allow for so much longer play time out of this game. Each chapter introduces more different mechanics to play with but there can definitely be more. Maybe Toodee gets split from Topdee and makes the player compete with more 2D like puzzle mechanics etc.This really takes me Back to Battleblock Theater. There was a campaign mode with its own set of levels but where I would really put in my 100 hours was the Multiplayer and level creator. There was something very charming about spending hours working on a set of levels and then watching your friends die irl as they try and complete your masterpiece of frustration. But with this game you could do SO much more with that level creation, it really feels like a missed opportunity. Again, I love the concept of this game, there could just be a whole lot more done with it if only there was a bigger dev team or more development time. So for the love of god I would love a Topdee Toodee 2 if these features were included. But right now the game sells itself short and misses out on some large opportunities, its essentially a quick 4 hour pump and dump.

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a mind-bending 2D Platformer and a Top-Down Puzzler hybrid from indie developer dietzribi. Combining two incompatible genres into one game that messes with your perspective and features puzzles that will have you scratching your head for hours. The two brothers that makeup dietzribi, Gonen and Ori, have certainly outdone themselves on their first commercial project. Toodee and Topdee is a fantastic mash-up of genres that’s not only a quirky idea but one that actually works, and works flawlessly. The story beings at the beginning, the beginning of time, an empty universe where the only thing in existence is Aleph. A master of an ancient and enchanted language that can turn Words into Worlds. Over countless days and nights, Aleph filled the void with worlds. However, the worlds moved erratically and without a stabilising force. Aleph feared the life he planned to create would be in danger. And so the Semicolon was forged, placed at the universe’s centre to keep the worlds in balance. The worlds are now in harmony, orbiting the Semicolon at a calm pace. Aleph gives life to the first world birthing one of our likely heroes – Toodee. Then another world, different from the first, but home to our other hero – Topdee. Aleph also created an assistant called Toodoo to help keep track of all the unintentional glitches that were created so he can deal with them later. As Aleph nears the last world to receive life Toodoo worries, he will no longer be needed. Fearing this outcome, he steals the Semicolon, causing all the worlds to combine. Toodee and Topdee are pulled from their worlds or rather mixed into each others, they encounter a newly born glitch called – GLITCH. With Glitch’s help, they begin a journey to find the Semicolon and return the universe back to how it should be. The game is spread out across multiple worlds, each made up of numerous levels. The levels feature unique themes specific to their combined world. With each world being made up of two separate worlds, thanks Toodoo, there’s clearly something wrong. Toodee’s and Topdee’s unique talents are more than up to the task, but whether you can find the solution to each level is up for debate. Don’t take the game lightly, as there’s more than a few levels that’ll have you scratching your head for hours. As you may no doubt have guessed, both Toodee and Topdee have very different talents. Toodee is a 2D Platforming expert, it’s the only way he knows how to move, so expect all the usual move sets that come along with that genre. Topdee is a top-down kinda person, which allows for easy movement across the whole map if not for obstacles and holes that lead into the void. The transition between these two characters and their unique style of play is seamless. The fluidity with which you’ll be swapping between the two becomes almost second nature. It’s not possible to tire of the world tilting that takes place during a swap, especially when it’s presented in gorgeous pixel art. Best of all, though, you can experience this in glorious co-op with a friend.Credit to the developers in that none of the levels ever feels repetitive. Some may focus on one character more than the other for the solution, but both will always be necessary to complete a level. Some worlds even include other living creatures, like bats and pigs. These will also factor into the solution of a level, all the while trying to chase and kill you. Another addition and perhaps the most annoying of all (personal opinion) is Tookey. Tookey is a shadow-like creature that has a bird-like form, but the shadow aspect is the most important. Tookey will literally act as a shadow to whichever character you’re using, mirroring their moves exactly. You can, of course, manipulate Tookey with the surrounding environment, but the solutions will also require Tookey’s involvement, annoyingly. Not only are some levels impossibly hard, sometimes a solution is simpler than you think, but there’s even a challenge mode of sorts. On each level, there’s usually a red and a blue ladybird, sometimes a purple one, crawling around the walls. These actually correspond to a set requirement in which you must complete a level to get that ladybird. Red is speed, blue is swaps and purple is not killing animals. You’ll naturally achieve some of these requirements throughout a playthrough, but for a lot of levels, they add a new degree of difficulty. They’re also worth collecting because they may unlock some secrets, shh!It’s also worth mentioning there are a few options available to you if you’d like to adjust the difficulty. These options can greatly help speed at the process of solving levels, so might be worth looking at if you plan to get all the ladybirds. But note that the developer has stated all ladybirds can be obtained with the default difficulty options.Who doesn’t love pixel art, that nostalgic aesthetic of older consoles which graphically fidelity was in its infancy. It’s fantastic and Toodee and Topdee is no exception. Not only does the game look fantastic in its 2D platformer guise, but also the in world tilting top-down view. Not being talented in game design, I can not begin to imagine the work going on behind the scene to achieve this visual parity between the two distinct genres. Regardless, it looks great, and it works wonderfully and without fault. Throughout Toodee and Topdee the music is fairly generic, calm elevator type music. Perhaps by design, given the nature of the game, it’s probably the right choice. It certainly saved me from rage quitting on more than one occasion. The calm tones help make light of the tough puzzles, giving you the headspace to try at least once more before having to take a walk. That’s completely reversed when it comes to the boss levels. The music there is fast and frantic, making it that much easier for mistakes to happen. But when you know what you’re doing, it makes for a pretty satisfying beat to kick a boss down a peg or two. Toodee and Topdee is a fantastic mash-up of genres that’s not only a quirky idea but one that actually works, and works flawlessly. Describing how the game mechanics work really doesn’t do justice to the actual magic at play here. The fluidity with which you swap between the two characters is everything. It allows for creativity from both the developer and player that otherwise could not exist. The brother developer team dietzribi has created one of the best and creative games of the year!(Originally Published on )

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is an interesting spin of a puzzle/platformer. Each level is a single room that you can see all of. You can control two characters, one in a 2D world where you move right/left like a traditional platformer and another in an overview world where you can move left, right, up, and down. Each character has their own simple abilities that you have to combine to solve each puzzle. Some are simple, some are much more challenging. There are also challenges in here such as beating a time limit and to complete a stage without switching characters too often. All of the achievements are incredibly difficult to unlock if you really want a challenge. Movement as Topdee can feel a bit awkward at times, especially when you're going for the speed challenges, but other than that, it works great. The game's a lot of fun and feel fresh, something I haven't seen before. I definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The demo of Toodee and Topdee was streamed on the Scumm-and-Villainy Twitch channel almost 2 years ago and I've wanted to play the full game myself ever since. It took a while before I got to it, but I really enjoyed the experience. The mechanic is fun, there's a cute story, and the puzzles range from simple to challenging.I really, really appreciate the highly configurable difficulty settings, as my reflexes aren't great and things like the boss battles would end up being very frustrating if I had to restart them every time. I played with infinite health enabled, which compensated for my lack of platforming skills and allowed me to focus on solving the puzzles. Would love to see this kind of configurability in other games too! The only thing missing was the ability to "undo" something (though that would understandably be difficult to code given the real-time nature of the game) - such as accidentally pushing a block one tile too far, causing it to fall in a pit and having to restart the level.Having the 5th chapter tone down the difficulty of the puzzles a bit as the story reaches its climax was a good decision imho. It feels a bit like a reward for making it through the especially fiendishly difficult puzzles of chapters 3 and 4 and allows you to experience the conclusion feeling very proficient at the game (even if your skills aren't quite perfect, like mine).Most of the techniques required to complete the puzzles are learned easily as you play, and you quickly get to understand what each gameplay element does, with a few exceptions. That brings me to my only (very minor) complaint: There were a few puzzles that I couldn't solve because I didn't know of certain mechanics (for instance, Topdee has the ability to place blocks diagonally too, which is required in rare instances to solve a puzzle - this isn't telegraphed in the game) but the guides were useful for those cases where I really got stuck.All in all, I really enjoyed the game and the cute story. At first, the ending felt a bit sad, but I was happy to see that the developers hadn't left it at that :)

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful puzzle-platformer with a unique concept that's used thoughtfully and creatively. This game is a good example of using "show don't tell" level design with objects/enemies that interact with the environment in interesting ways. As a player it feels great when I figure out some of the interactions myself. The soundtrack is wonderful (to the point I bought it as well) with a nice mixture of lo-fi, nes-style chiptune beats, transitioning into a heavier, mind-melting chiptune-rock hybrid for boss segments with mind-melting tunes. I can't say much for the story, other than it exists (if you want a deep story-based game go elsewhere, this just isn't that type of game). Long story short, this game is excellent, and if it caught your eye and even vaguely seems like something you'd like, BUY IT! YOU WON'T REGRET IT!

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a wonderfully unique take on the puzzle platforming genre. The combination of two types of perspectives on games make for some complex yet engaging level design, where the player must think around the two views to figure out how to best solve each area. Then there are the boss fights which culminate each area's gimmick, which originally were tough as you had to beat each one in one go, but the later addition of checkpoints the in fights made them much more manageable.The music in this game is great to ponder solutions to, while the story is full of fun programming in-jokes that make for an enjoyable experience overall. The dev also seems very active as well, as they appeared during one of my streams during the game, which pretty much made my day! In short, I am glad I picked up this game and would heartily recommend it to anyone looking for a unique yet somewhat difficult puzzle platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful puzzle platforming experience.Toodee & Topdee was basically described to me as playing Super Mario Maker in editor mode, except editor mode is an actual character that has to deal with their own challenges.You play as Toodee, the platforming character, and Topdee, the top-down block-pushing character, alternating between platforming and block-pushing to navigate the two to an exit portal.  Each chapter comes with its own mechanics and trials to overcome, becoming steadily more difficult as the game progresses.  This game has the appearance of being good for co-op, but in practice, both characters are not active at the same time, but instead must be swapped between, like in Donkey Kong Country.  This suits the game better to a single player experience, though I do think there is still some fun to be had playing with a friend.The game starts off quite easy at first, and for the casual audience, I expect most will have a handy time throughout the game until perhaps the end of the second world where the difficulty starts to really ramp up.  However, I've played a lot of both puzzler and platforming games in my day, so I would have found most of these earlier stages terribly boring if it were not for the ladybugs the game employs.  You see, for the experienced player, the game uses two ladybugs, red and blue, to add extra challenge to every level.  The blue ladybugs look for players to use a minimal amount of swaps between character to get through the stages, while the red ladybugs look for players to play through levels as quickly as possible.  If you're good at these games, I recommend trying to collect these buggers from the very start, perhaps only holding back as you get to the more difficult third and fourth worlds.Coupled with the art and music, this game has a real level of polish to it, something about it makes it feel modern but also makes me wish it was part of my childhood.  The platforming isn't terribly complex, but is smooth and buttery.  The block-pushing is almost unexpectedly dynamic at first, but once you get used to the flow and getting those red ladybugs, it feels great to quickly pivot and place blocks with precision.And then there's the post-game content/secrets in this game.  I won't talk about them here, but let's just say figuring out the secrets to this game has pushed this game from being a simple quaint game to being something that made me really happy to play (though that last secret was a doozy, only get it if you're really into this game, like I was).I give it a thorough recommendation.  Most people won't be spending as much time as I did on it, but even a causal playthrough in 5-7 hours would be a treat to go through.  Thanks so much to dietzribi for making this game, I'll definitely be looking into whatever comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an incredible game. When I first saw a clip from this game on Twitter last year, I just couldn't believe that it was real. In fact, I was a bit concerned about how the game would work with the two styles, and whether or not it would lead to a compelling and exciting experience. That all changed when I played the free demo on Steam. Not only did the main gimmick of this game worked, it was phenomenal. I loved how I could be platforming one minute, then moving top down to move boxes in the next. It was unlike anything I've played before. Then I got the full game, and it was even better. It built upon what the demo included and really expanded it into a master piece. Everything from the Game Design, Art Style, Audio Design, and Story were all well crafted and well executed. The levels were so addicting and challenging that I just could not put it down. I recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of either 2D platformers or top down games, and looking for something fresh to play. I love this game so much, and it's easily one of the best games I've played in quite some time.

_childDocuments_.review: A meta game that doesn't just rely on "lol its about video games" to get by, this is a SERIOUSLY FUN puzzle platformer. _childDocuments_.review: So far I'm up to chapter 4 (Exceptions) and I'm really enjoying this 2D/Top-down puzzle hybrid. The characters are fun and the dialogue keeps a good story going. I'm surprised at how slick the two gaming styles have been merged and the complexity of puzzles that it creates. Each new world brings fresh dynamics and new challenges. Bosses are tricky but not impossible. The ability to quickly restart a level is a bonus.Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a retrospective on video games. No, it is a celebration of the concept of video games! It is the "Gödel, Escher, Bach" of video games.This game is a hybrid of a hybrid of a hybrid. First, a hybrid of a top-down puzzler and a side-scrolling platformer. But also a hybrid of an fast-paced action game and a slow, brain racking puzzle. But last but not least - it is a game about games about games.I would expect that combining all these would end up in an unbalanced mush of a gameplay, but here it is done with so much grace - with difficulty, while hard at times, always balanced and fair. Puzzles are coherent and communicative; platforming is challenging and not punishing. Bosses are all of the above together, actually creating a brand new type of gameplay, while keeping a very familiar feel (one of the bosses felt a bit hard for me, but that's where I granted myself extra few lives in the difficulty menu).Story is super unique and supports this type of gameplay. The story is also kind of a hybrid - the characters in the game are also the creators of the game (how is it even possible?). And the two main protagonists are going through the process of understanding their special role in this game, slowly becoming aware of their surroundings.All is left to say - Toodee and Topdee is a work of art, in one line with games like Stanley Parable and Undertale, which are aspiring to break the mere concept of video games. Toodee and Topdee is asking one question - what happens if you try to merge two things that should not fit? The answer is this delightful, beautiful game full of surprises, filled with great fun and challenges from the first intro levels up to the final scene.Also, I forgot to mention, great art and music that fit the theme perfectly.Do not miss out on this one! Play Toodee and Topdee today!

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a great game, although not the type of game I personally like, wanted nor expected going into itYou see, I watched the game's development on Twitter for a while and it was implicitly advertised everywhere as this kind of easier puzzle game that focuses on execution rather than figuring out what you need to do.And for the first levels it mostly holds true, the first 2 chapters were very fun to zoom through, and the game came out on my birthday and I had a lot of fun playing it.However! Starting from Chapter 3 onwards it mostly turns into this more mind-melting puzzle type of game. And it was not at all what it was advertised as! You can see that if you go back to the screenshots and the trailer, you will not find A SINGLE MENTION of the game's harder puzzles.(Okay, technically if you uncollapse the long description and scroll down a bit you can see the phrase "mind-melting puzzles", but 1) the gif attached is still a very easy puzzle 2) let's be honest nobody reads the long description anyway, that's just how Steam works)The point is - the game tries to combine moderately difficult puzzle levels with precision platforming sections (which I'm fan of the latter, you can tell by my profile pic haha)And there *is* an accessibility option to give yourself infinite lives and skip the platforming parts, hovewer there is *no way* to skip the puzzle levels entirely, as most of the time even having infinite lives to walk through fire won't help you too much (which I actively tried doing once the puzzles got hard, especially in the 4th Chapter when the shadow guy appears)If you personally enjoy the more difficult puzzle kind of game like Baba is You or Stephen Sausage Roll or whatever, then you will probably have a blast playing Toodee and Topdee. If you're like me, then you can still have a lot of fun playing through the earlier parts of the game with the more casual puzzles.Either way, I will not refund the game to support the developer. They did a great job, and I'm excited to see what their next project will beAgain, I don't have any problems with this game, except for its misleading advertisingP.S. dietzribi, please add a button to skip levels, or some other kind of help with the puzzles, it felt weird getting stuck on every single level for minutes after phasing through the first ones in a matter of seconds. so, yeah, please add that so i can see the platforming challenges the later parts of the game have to offer :D- Evoleo

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting puzzle concept. But the control scheme is totally ducked up. And the tight-timing platform/action aspect is just not mixed well with the big-brain complex puzzle theme.Most of the time I died because I want to <jump/grab>, but I hit the <switch> button, and vice versa. At first I thought this was my fault alone. But after playing a very first few chapters, I realize that this game don't require <jump/grab> nor <switch> so much (unlike other platformer games that I have to perform jump like 100 times a level). The issue worsen with the location of the buttons which is so close, [Z]/[X] on keyboard, or [X]/[A] on controller (why not [SPACE]/[TAB] and [A]/[LT/RT] instead?). Thus I have a hard time develop muscle memory of the correct buttons. When we actually need to pull it off (keep in mind that there're monsters chasing you at high speed), it's so easy to messed up.The button issue goes deep down than that. You see, the only action each character can do is jump or grab, exclusively. Initially, it might be a logical assumption to put both actions onto one button <jump/grab>, since when you are toodee you cannot grab, and when you are topdee you cannot jump. In practice, this design became a fatal mistake instead. For example, when the player is concentrating control toodee doing the platforming section, but need to switch to topdee for a sec, it is counter-intuitive to use the same button with topdee to perform a grab -- since many other game does separate these buttons. So if the player doesn't press that button but press another one out of the habit, it is a <swap> button instead! Now the player is given back to control toodee again, and immediately fall to their death because topdee forget to grab a box and build a platform... This problem will less likely to occur if the omni-action button was separate into two dedicated buttons in the first place.Remember that we are talking about a game that combine puzzle and platforming that every decision happen in a split second (if the game is not a platforming but just only a slow puzzle, then this design is more forgivable). So the buttons must be super clear in the first place. Each button should do one job and one job only. Not this messed up that not only confusing but also not allow any margin of error!The boss is also annoying, why our characters have only 1 heart by default? That's hardly fun to observe boss patterns. And the patterns is so darn long. Each time I died at a boss fight, I have to repeat the process of dodging attack like half a minutes before I can even land a first hit on the boss. And the boss needed to be hit three times in total! With the almost the same moveset!! What a wasted time of my life doing something so boring, so tedious.Know your audience. In fact, see the stat. I wonder how many people would turn on the infinite life and just play the game just for the puzzle alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee - Steam Version - v 1.0.0.4.The metagame is a boom of creativity and knowing on algorithmic thinking. In contrast it is an aesthetic promise above gameplay. The "cutscenes" are more the game than the player's experience. Is this an indie game for sure? In fact it is a game made by only two brothers. Despite of this the final game was in partnership with Super Rare Games publisher (based in London) mainly for marketing. In the press kit website content we can get: "The jam version received great feedback, and so Gonen and Ori decided to make it their first commercial project". I suspected that it was a game jam game, it has many compact features typical of a game jam game. You can search for the original Ludum Dare 41 entry -  and play the pre-alpha/alpha version -  .References/Legacy - Maybe FEZ by Polytron could be a strong reference in genre mechanics and small gimmicks. Also the integration of the ludic, the narrative and the music in Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP by Superbrothers and Capybara Games, with music by Jim Guthrie. The deus ex machina use is very frequent. We could see the similar plattform/puzzle level design in Master Spy by TURBOGUN too. But without a doubt the game is more based on other designs that appear a lot in game jam games.Characters - Personality traits - Toodee is rude in speech; Topdee is polited. Todee is cool, awesome, Sonic-like. Topdee is not too charismatic, indeed is very no guts. However we will see at the end of the game a very interesting change in the characters, like a monumental plot twist. The character design of the protagonists is cliché due to the fact of the cute/kawaii and super deformed form is in check nowadays. In the present we have other potentials in a impressionist way to explore pixel art without cute/kawaii/SD appeal - in other words we do not need forced face expressions and big heads to mark humanism in the small frame of pixels, it is not a technical problem today and we could explore other aesthetic markers (including doing it in tribute to retro games).The side characters are sort OK sort a little bland. The glitches and guardians could have more design in it. We feel a promise of lore and metagame network by the characters however it not happens. Need more ludo-engagement through the plot.Visuals - that kind of pixel art emulated in low poly 3D is a really solid tendency nowadays in indie development, see the searching for the tools picoCAD and SpriteStack in the present year that can "convert" 2d pixel art in a so-so-3D art (not voxel). In the game there is a magic feature with solidness - it is very impressive the change between the 2D (Toodee) perspective and 3D (Topdee) perspective and vice-versa in the dialogues scenes. It dinamizes the game! The game physics is a great topic! The cloud physics and art are very simple and fun.Thinking on the playability and the ludo-moto - the puzzles and the design of plattform jumps is well-constructed in a hard way. "Hard" here means a rather orthodox logic - straight. However the pig mechanics in not "hard", being an epicentre of playful creativity. The boss/guardian fights are well constructed in a cubic/kaleidoscopic point, very unique indeed - reminds me of some boss battles in Contra: Hard Corps (Konami, Mega Drive) that are very strong in singular gimmicks.Original Sound Track quick analysis in spontaneous notes:1 - Home - it is an normal almost chiptune dub lo-fi, just OK. A mix of idling  OK with a very OK;2 - Hello World - relaxaway - better than OK, but OK instead. More or less similar to the FTL soundtrack;3 - Jungle Kingdom - same of the 2 vibe;4 - Elementemple - Ok to good, but very 2010s in a bad way;5 - Exceptions - deep and frail in feelings, so so like FTL OST too. Very bad with drums (However in the game does not match!);6 - Error - sad, down, OK;7 - Return - not good. Tetrisistic but not well executed;8 - Ordalook - not good. Too fake desert soundtrack;9 - Yumbrozi - confusion, bad drums;10 - Korimlio - interesting - very good - eletric guitars!;11 - Ozraeen - more guitars! Nice! Drumba!;12 - Toodoo - very fast - not good - arrogant - horrible!;13 - Incompatible - good relaxaway track indeed. The best lo-fiist track;14 - Corruption - weak - fast and OK;15 - Ladybugs - the better OK track.The general feeling is that the music would be more interesting in another game and in another decade, maybe in the year of 2012 when the FEZ game was published. The same compelling and compulsory visual aesthetic of the game jams can be felt in the musical aesthetic. We can feel great aesthetic vices present in the inner culture of Ludum Dare jamers. On the other hand - we can feel de efforts of the integration between game design and musical composition near to the work of Jim Guthrie in Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP in some aspects, but far from something koshiroist.Localization - The short dialogues are well translated and the options of languages (10) are embracing considering the indie audience and the indie project. (it is worth remembering again that the game puts itself as indie and is made indie but has a connection with Super Rare Games).Optimization - No problems with standard emerging hardware. The minimum requirements stipulated is i3, 4 GB RAM - which is somewhat alarming considering the game is low poly and even the last few levels do not seem to weigh as much.Accessibility - The easy difficulty change in options menu makes it possible for people with motor restrictions or even people with little manual skills to play and enjoy the game until the end. The same goes for those who are not cognitively well-skilled at handling puzzles or those who do not like puzzles. Using a steam controller and testing the haptics feedback it is possible to say that the game is rotten in haptic design, there is only one form of vibration. There could be vibrations due to falls and other impacts for example as in Hollow Knight by Team Cherry - and that would not be that difficult to implement even for a small group of developers.Finally, the game is too short and the cost-benefit is not interesting when we balance the aesthetic promises against what the game actually is in praxis experience. Maybe the game needed another 1 or 2 years of development. It was not enough to transform the submitted game jam build for Ludum Dare. Could have explored more the metaworld with more lore and satyric and pythonesque plot and being more careful with mechanics and music. The balance points out that the Toodee and Topdee is not recommended since the negative topics outweigh the positive topics looking from the point of view of a player from an emerging country who will buy the game on Steam. Although there is no desire to ask for a refund - possibly a good update could come or a free DLC.Original full review - wasdtest dot com / reviewsMetacritic - leyaotangFollow my Steam Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: "Toodee and Topdee" is yet another of literally thousands of 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  In fairness this is probably one of the better 2D retro pixel console ported platformers out there, which is like saying this is really one of the best diseases one can possibly get. The gimmick here is that the 2D platforming puzzles are solved by switching to a 2D block placement mode, which allows you to rearrange the platformer level, which is incredibly pleasing to any console peasant who ever saw such witchcraft.  It's not going to do much to amuse PC gamers, unfortunately, because this is a console ported 2D retro pixel platformer, and that's a huge problem. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is most commonly used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.A strong argument can be made that construction kits like GameMaker Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer", dietzribi has done here.  These construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, and to make small demos to pass around with friends.  They're not intended to replace to actual work of real, professional game developers.  So it's inappropriate when amateurs try to use these for profit, without any actual, real game development effort taking place.  This doesn't result in products that have any real meaningful value for gamers.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game."Toodee and Topdee" has the ridiculous, laughable price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  That's right, the console devs behind this pixelcrap think this game is better than the entire Mass Effect Trilogy, better than The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, better than GTA:V, better than Skyrim, better than Red Dead Redemption 2, so they priced this higher than those games!This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a nice gimmick-y puzzle game about switching between 2D platforming and top-down puzzle solving. If you're expecting a lengthy game full of insane challenges, secrets, and a story with some kind of cool message, then this game probably won't be for you. But if you like unique gameplay ideas executed confidently and a story with a good sense of humor, this game does have something interesting worth checking out.The presentation of the game overall is perfectly serviceable. Everything looks like what some things should just look like, nothing is overly detailed, and it generally is just meant to be readable. Even sound effects and music are fine and not generally intrusive, but the soundtrack is mostly just forgettable. The best way to describe the presentation is understandable but nothing special or memorable, just good enough that information is clearly conveyed.The game itself is touted as a puzzle game, where its gimmick is that you have to switch between 2D platforming and top-down block pushing. If we look at the game purely from this perspective, it's basically a unique kind of puzzle game with a unique gimmick that makes it stand out.General controls for the platforming are just fine. I don't have much to say about it; it's generally tight enough that overshooting my jumps was my fault, however my only issues with the platforming controls is that some puzzles can feel a bit too precise at times, especially with some gimmicks making certain sections of the puzzles feel very cheap.The top-down controls are a mixed bag for me personally. Being able to rotate Topdee without needing to constantly reposition him was good, but the movement didn't feel very precise to me. I'll be fair here and say that I was playing this game with an Xbox controller, so some of the precision problems I have may just be a result of me using an analogue stick to play this game, but even then, I feel like sometimes I go in directions I wasn't trying to go in. It didn't feel like I was locked to 8 directions, it felt like I had full 360 movement, even if I know it's locked to 8 directions, partly because the controls are a bit floaty.Still, the game generally accommodate for the general lack of precision through its puzzles, which are mostly good. Some of them were decent brain teasers, and each world introduced their own mechanics that add a unique twist on the formula of switching between 2D platforming and top-down bock pushing. I do have some qualms with some of the execution-based puzzles, where one wrong move can entirely screw over the entire execution, and unfortunately, they appear more frequently as the game goes on. Thankfully, the majority of the puzzles were not based around finesse or execution and were instead about trying to figure out how to use the gimmick to solve the puzzle. Because each world introduces its own mechanic, they have a structure of the first few levels being about teaching the mechanic with increasing complexity, with the later levels in the world testing your ability to use these mechanics. For the most part, it works, and the majority of puzzles are really cool. However, again, the puzzles that require immense precision are a problem. One puzzle requires you to place falling blocks at a specific height while Toodee is meant to fall between them, and it's immensely frustrating to figure out the specifics behind it.This game also has bossfights, which act as the climax to every world. This is where the game tests your ability to use the mechanics you've been taught to beat the fight, and you have to hit the boss 3 times in order to beat it. Every time you hit the boss, the stage resets and you're asked to increase your pace. They're not terrible or insanely difficult, but they can get repetitive since the only way they get more difficult is by forcing you to be faster with your execution. Thankfully, there are checkpoints in the bossfights, so if you hit the boss and die, you don't have to hit them three times again in a row.All in all, Toodee and Topdee is a relatively short game that doesn't overstay its welcome. While more puzzles would be cool to have, at the same time I'm glad the game shows off cool mechanics and doesn't use them so much that they'd get stale. It does unique things with its mechanics, and it never felt like it was running out of ideas because the mechanics were taught, made more complex, and were done relatively quickly. I don't think games need to be long and overbearing with mountains of content; a long game means nothing if most of the game is bad or boring, and I'd rather have a short game that is consistently good rather than a long game that is mostly bad. And Toodee and Topdee is consistently good, to the point where I'd say it justifies its shorter length by just being a nice puzzle game.While I'd normally talk in depth about a story of a game, there really isn't much to talk about with the story of this game. Basically, someone stole an artifact called the Semicolon, which has caused worlds to merge, and glitches to appear, and it's up to Toodee and Topdee to find the missing Semicolon and fix the world. It's nothing special, just a simple justification for the mechanic, but it's rife with humor and self-awareness, and at times I chuckled a little because some of the jokes were well written. I wouldn't say it's worth discussing in depth, because everything is spelled out, and it's mostly the developers joking about game development.All in all, Toodee and Topdee is a solid puzzle game with a unique gimmick. It's a relatively short game you can beat in a weekend, and I fully appreciate that it used its gimmick and ended when they felt like they did everything they could with it. My last main gripe is that the final world's levels were kind of not good, since they emphasized the execution puzzles and added a kill barrier that forces you to beat the level at an unusually fast pace that's just straight up absurd, topped with the puzzles themselves feeling like they work better at a slow pace. Even then, I really liked the game enough that I think it's worth checking out if you like puzzle games with unique ideas and gimmicks, and I hope to see more puzzle games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: The trailer on the Steam page already does a great job of showcasing how unique the concept of switching between a top-down and 2D platformer can be. It's not a perfect game; there are a handful of quirks that stem from how a grid-based character and a freely moving character don't quite line up. The later levels get pretty challenging and demanding in terms of execution. There's no undo, which can make the execution-heavy levels quite frustrating. If you're not keen on action in puzzle games, this might not be for you. In the end, I respect games for exploring interesting combinations of mechanics, even if they don't make for a perfectly smooth experience 100% of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it at first, it's a super original idea with great puzzles.Unfortunately, it also contains unforgiving precision platforming combined with unprecise controls, and no undo button nor any way to save in the middle of a puzzle. In practice this means everytime you get the platforming ever slightly off (which is very easy due to the slippery controls), you need to restart the puzzle from the beginning. This means repeating parts over and over and over and it's just not fun.Shame because this game is close to greatness. It would only need a few tweaks. But as-is, I'm done with restarting the same damn puzzle over and over while managing slippery controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Quaint little puzzle game with cute visuals, a fun story I lost interest in, good puzzles and suitable amount of contenttoo much emphasis on dexterity and quick reaction times for my liking. Probably designed around the multiplayer which hurt the solo experience. The endgame is INSANELY difficult and hard enough with infinite lives. Music and sound are also weakGot this for free, but I wouldn't be spending 20 bucks on this. Wait till it's on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: I knew from the moment I saw the trailer that this game was full of potential, but now that I'm on the last, time-limited world, I can say without doubt that this is one of the cleverest puzzle games I've ever played. Each and every mechanic provides deeply thought-out play style for BOTH players. New worlds add new layers of complexity to the teamwork required to complete each level, and many of the later stages require real planning to beat.On top of the incredible stages, the bosses each provide a unique challenge in their own right. Requiring both players to participate, the boss mechanics often necessitate precise timing and planning as well, all while Toodee and Topdee are flying across the screen and dodging attacks. Between the stages and the boss fight, each and every world feels incredibly satisfying to conquer.This game is easily worth the $20 price tag, though it's definitely best enjoyed with a friend. If the creators ever make a co-op game again in the future, I will be the first in line to purchase (hint, hint).
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Do not play this game alone! It would be a waste not to share it with someone. It's not a replayable game, since once you've figured out the puzzles, you can't forget them. I wish it wasn't so!The cutscenes (of which there's plenty) are criminally funny and an absolute joy to voice act with your +1. The gameplay is super creative, perfectly challenging, full of twists, and delivers everything you could ask for with its premise of combining a box-pusher/sokoban with a puzzle platformer. You do the thinking, you do the jumping, you coordinate and learn the timings together, the gameplay loop is perfect and the level designs are fantastic. You'll die a lot, you hit restart, and you try again until you get it just right.Bossfights are super creative and fresh, pretty difficult but generous with checkpoints. It never feels unfair, but if you struggle, there are plenty of assist options, including infinite health. Some levels neglect the platforming, but since the puzzle solving is always a cooperative effort, this didn't really matter at all.It's a must-play. Grab someone who is willing to voice act their dialogue!! Friend, partner, brother, doesn't matter! Just somebody who likes fun, and maybe a bit of thinking.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game! The puzzles get a bit complex towards worlds 3-4, but as long as you're patient (and don't mind shoving mandatory blocks into holes by mistake a lot) they're fine. I adore the concept, and it's done wonderfully. I wanna talk about the ending, which is amazing, but it's better to experience it yourself.The dialogue is a little cheesy, but in an endearing way, and it ends up being really enjoyable. I finished the game about two minutes ago and I already miss Toodee and Topdee!
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and innovative puzzle game with a good sense of humor, but the "boss battles" are ridiculous and completely interrupt the flow of the game. If you enjoy getting killed over and over (and over) while trying to solve a puzzle, you'll love those "battles". Otherwise, you'll have to use the game's cheat system to skip past them. If it weren't for that I feel like this game would be great, but as it is it's definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is an excellent puzzle-platformer full of inventive ideas, charm and challenges!The concept of solving puzzles using two different perspectives that you can switch between on the fly is one of the most inventive mechanics I've seen in recent years and it feels fully taken advantage of: each world has it's one central theme that is explored through out it and it always feels like you're taking a new and fresh challenge.The graphics are great: they have a certain low-resolution charm to them thanks to the aliasing effect at play.The music is also great but most of the tracks aren't all that memorable: they are calm and not intrusive, allowing you to focus on the puzzle you're currently trying to solve.I won't spoil the ending but I'll just say it was one of the most creative, engaging and nerve-wracking final acts I've experienced in recent years, they've done a remarkable job.In short this game is nothing short of excellent and you should buy it, right now!
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game, but very disappointed in the final stage.Became far more about reflexes than problem solving, especially once they effectively became timed. Which turned it from fun to overly stressful. I still finished it, but part of me wished I'd have just stopped at stage 5 and never bothered finishing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Switch between control of Toodee (side-scrolling platformer, can jump) and Topdee (top-down puzzle game, can pick up and push boxes) to navigate them both to the exit.All up it's a pretty good puzzle platformer which I soured on a bit because so many later levels are more about timing than puzzling. The first half of world five in particular is horrible, and I hate to miss content but unlocking world six requires speed-running every level: thanks but no thanks.A very polished package with great level design, just do go in expecting as much dexterity as puzzling.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: , if you ever heard the expression “The whole is greater than the sum of the parts”, I’ll tell you that it describes this game very well.A boring platformer mashed with an equally boring top-down block sliding puzzler.It would be dull if not for the lovely graphics and great puzzle design.A simple adventure story with a programming motif that revolves around cooperation and visiting new and different worlds.You control both:Toodee who can run and jump like your average platformer hero.AndTopdee who can move from a top-down perspective, moving blocks about.The gimmick is switching between the two to solve puzzles and build a way for eachother to get over the obstacles that separate them from a portal to other levels.One more thing worth mentioning, is that despite the puzzle-y nature of the title, it also spots some difficulty in execution, some times requiring pinpoint precision or timing with your jumps, other times a certain execution sequence where maybe you're required to breack stuff and do many other things before a block falls down.You could see this as both a positive and a negative really.It’s a simple yet satisfying game with some bumps in difficulty here and there, it’s a recommendation from me especially since you can feel that the dev cared about this game while making it.However, consider also that the asking price of this game is around 20$ for what is essentially a neatly wrapped gimmick with little more and 5 to 10 hours of content at best, get it on a discount if you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and a well-thought out game! The puzzles can be frustrating at times but it is doable. The twist on the gameplay at the end is welcomed surprise! The characters with their programming themed personas and how they meshed into the story is very creative! This is a very unique game! Heart and soul were poured into making it and it shows! I didn't expect to tear up with joy and abit of sadness in the end but the journey was well worth it! THIS IS A MUST PLAY!
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a wonderful puzzle game with an almost universally appealing aesthetic and puzzles that are almost always intuitive enough yet difficult enough to make sure that you never spend too little or too much time figuring one out; it’s been a blast to play on my deck and I can’t recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This is an amazing puzzle platformer with great puzzle design, good comedy and stellar music, but going for completion is pretty tedious.(Spoilers Ahead)Toodee and Topdee is a cute little indie puzzle platformer with an emphasis on controlling 2 characters with different movesets. The game shines its brightest when the puzzles require juggling both of them which is, sadly, not always the case. I think Toodee and Topdee are on 2 different sides of the spectrum. While Toodee has fluid controls that allow for very fun platforming, there is very little interactability with the world, leading to having most of the puzzle solving done by Topdee, which on the contrary feels very clunky to control (mostly due to the fact that his movement is 8-directional, something that is understandable, but makes it annoying to dodge enemies that DO have full 360 movement).The main 5 worlds and the secret 6th are all very fun with stupendous design and great puzzles, I especially appreciate how the 5th chapter has a greater focus on platforming, which had been on the sidelines up until then, and how the 6th is based around niche tricks that attentive players would have already figured out on their own.Now, my biggest problem with the game is with its postgame content and achievements. The main source of replay value comes from hunting ladybugs. Initially you'll be trying to catch red ladybugs (awarded for completing a level under a specific time frame) and blue ladybugs (awarded for completing a level under what the devs think is the minimum amount of required swaps between the 2 characters), there are also purple ones, but those are few and far between. While the red ladybugs were rarely an annoyance or a challenge, the blue ones are really hit or miss. In most levels it's not too hard to figure out how to obtain them, but every once in a while you'll stumble upon a level where you go "I have to beat it in THAT little steps?". From there it's a coin flip on whether or not you can figure it out through experimenting or critical thinking (like in 4-2 where you have to learn that you can achieve different jump heights with the same portal positions by having them be at an uneven altitude), or you can only know by having some insider knowledge or finding the perfect strat for a boss fight. I remember distinctly when I had to look up the solution for the 4-16 red ladybug because I was stuck on it for 2 days straight, only for the guide to tell me that I was an idiot and didn't realise the invisible hitbox for a key was ever so slightly smaller on the bottom side. This left such a sour taste in my mouth. The ladybugs also make the already unforgiving boss rush on 6-10 even more unforgiving by having to take perfect lines and strats.Do you want to know what you get for getting all 206 ladybugs? You unlock 6 more special white ladybugs, one for each chapter. To collect these you have to go on the default difficulty settings and complete each world without dying once. I cannot stress enough how blatant this padding is. Outside of chapters 5 and 6, the levels are NOT hard to die on in the slightest, your biggest concern is accidentally moving a metal box in a corner and having to go back to the beginning. I can't lie and say I didn't enjoy chapter 5's white ladybug, but other than that, this is just inexcusable and obviously done to increase playtime (something that probably didn't even work, considering that the true 100% secret cutscene isn't even documented online at the time of writing).In conclusion, absolutely play this game, but please stop after beating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely, GENUINELY love this game. Its puzzles range from semi-straightforward to incredibly complex by the nature of the mechanic of the game being a little confusing (but in the best possible way for me.)The artstyle is really nice, the 3D effects being really really cool but maybe sometimes a little difficult to tell where things are meant to be when in control of Topdee (I suggest if you run into this issue, turning off the 3d effects is the best bet to make it more accurate). The "programming-humor" story is really funny and silly, and it got a lot of chuckles from me through the whole game. The music is also DYNAMIC depending on which character you're in control of, which isn't a "new" thing by any means, but I just love the attention to detail dynamic music gives. Oh yeah also the soundtrack IN GENERAL is amazing and i found myself humming along to it any chance I got (especially the elementemple music, GOD that's such a great track)There are some negatives I found in the game though:* There are some flashing light cutscenes in the beginning and end of the game, plus a mechanic in world four that flashes A LOT if fireballs interact with it without really any way to tone any of the flashing down (This can really hurt your eyes if you're anything like me, or even worse, this could potentially trigger epilepsy if you have that, so keep that in mind).* Some puzzles can be so complex and confusing that it can be discouraging if you make a small mistake, or leave you stuck. (I personally had to look up like two puzzles in chapter 4 for hints on what I was meant to do next)* There are some extremely intense and fast paced boss fights / fairly precise platforming segments / strict time limits for the first part of chapter 5 (For some of these things, I absolutely needed to slow the game speed down to 75% to avoid getting a panic attack. I do appreciate that the accessibility and difficulty options are there though).BUT despite its flaws, I still genuinely love this game, and saw it through to the end of the story. I'll be honest, this game might not be for everyone, as it can be a little frustrating in difficulty or complexity, and I've also found my fair share of small visual issues or even attempt-breaking bugs. That being said though it's an amazing and unique game that I think deserves a try.Thank you for making this game! -OriePS. I totally ship both Toodee and Topdee, no joke. :::}
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Really good! The gameplay is great, challenging towards the end but in a fair way. I kinda wish they didn't have dialogue. _childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, quite simply, brilliant. An incredible mix of puzzle solving and platforming that often allows for scenarios to be solved in unique ways. There have been several times where I've said "Oh, wow" upon figuring out a new trick or a way to get through a level. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem that transported my brother and me back to our childhood days of playing co-op games like Goof Troop on the SNES. _childDocuments_.review: Switching between 2D and 3D is not a new idea by any mean but the execution in Toodee and Topdee is top notch. The puzzles are clever and you'll be surprised by how many mechanics are introduced in this game.There are also some levels that require some level of execution as well. Whether you're gonna like it is up to your personal ability and preference. Personally I love it, especially the boss stages. There's something immensely satisfying when you can solve a level using the skill combination of both your brain and your hands.The only knock I can give the game is the lack of online co-op. Remote play together is ok, but it could be better.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is an absolutely fantastic puzzle plat-former. The platforming is fluid and responsive, the puzzles utilize the swapping mechanics well and make you feel like a genius when you solve them (especially in the later levels). The game looks and sounds great, with vibrant colors, bouncy animations, and catchy tunes to entertain you while you're experimenting away with the game's unique mechanics. I was surprised at how much I enjoyed the bosses in particular, which really test your skills in a way that the regular levels just can't. The story also surprised me with how funny and engaging it was, the ending was definitely the highlight of the game. The game took me about 5 hours to beat the final boss, but getting the true ending took me about 8 hours. Most of that was due to the fact that you need 111 of the games collectibles, the ladybugs. The game doesn't really tell you how to get these, but basically each level has at least 2 lady bugs. A blue and red one, blue ladybugs are awarded at the end of the level if you beat it under a certain number of swaps while red ladybugs are awarded for beating a level under a certain amount of time. A few levels also have pink ladybugs, which are awarded if you beat that level with out killing any animals. Getting these are really fun, and really showcases this game's speedrun potential. So yeah, incase you couldn't tell, I really like this game, and I think you should play it if you're at all interested in it or the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: It's been ages since I had so much fun with a puzzle game.Awesome concept and great puzzles.At some points the game would benefit from explaining a little bit more to the player, and sometimes it's annoying that you move something just by walking next to it, but overall I really recommend to give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: What a refreshing and interesting mix of 2D (Toodee) and Top Dimension (TopDee) where gravity, physics, perspectives and puzzles become one. Mind the Toodoo "paper person" (pencil pusher?) ..!One of the rare games I allow my 6yo/o kid to play; it really adds value, teaches something in a stimulating, amusing way.The great narration, polished cutscenes and beautiful graphics definitely add character to this brilliant indie title.Thanks, Dietzribi!@Dercetech

_childDocuments_.review: is good. It can be hard at times, but that just makes getting certain levels that much more rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: I love the novel concept, and it is functional on top of being compelling. Most of the levels are so cleverly designed, but there are a few infuriating ones that baffle me. The requirement to time the swap with such a small window of opportunity is absolutely ridiculous, and I'm known to have a keen sense of timing, so I can't imagine how other people felt about level 3-18, 4-3, or the bulk of chapter 2. I think if the animals and the falling blocks were so much slower, it would undo all of the frustration, but I understand this is probably not feasible as that would break some levels as well such as 3-16 (God knows how I beat that in my second try) and require tweaking the red ladybugs, probably among other things not immediately obvious to me.I had such a blast with the first and third boss. Discovering and executing the game plan for Toodee and Topdee was so much fun. Second boss was alright, but Topdee did absolutely nothing besides deactivating Toodee's hitbox, and if you're determined enough, you can even beat the monkey without using Topdee at all. I took pause after 4-3, so I can't comment much about the rest.Overall, I'd highly recommend it. It has exceptionally well designed puzzles and boss fights that make you forget you're playing a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nostalgia love-letter to the 2D and 3D retro games of the world... in one game. The developers knew they had a banger idea with this game, and they ran with it! You control Toodee and Topdee and can jump between 2D game play and 3D at the push of a button - it's ingenious and very well implemented.The music is one of my favorite parts of it. It's so chill and I can really relax to it. It needs to be more widely listened to on chill YouTube playlists and Spotify and whatnot - I know I'd listen to it. So if you enjoy puzzles and solid 2D and 3D platformers this game is definitely worth a go. I haven't tried co-op play, but I am sure it is a stellar experience as well. This is the Dietzribi brothers' first game, and you can tell they put a lot of heart into it.I remember playing this back when it was a demo in a Twitch stream and they came to support me. These are two passionate workers that ought to be more recognized in the indie scene. Nintendo themselves has done this already in getting this game on the Switch's eShop. I think that a level creator mode for this game would make give it near infinite replay value, although I understand that would be a ton of work to do. A few of the later levels are easier than the earlier levels before, but I can look past that as that can be a bit objective.In any case I appreciate all of the efforts here, this is a solid game, no doubt about it.

World 3 in particular has some really interesting mechanics,  but there's neat stuff to be found throughout and they definitely get a good deal of mileage out of them.Be warned that the first half of the final world (and a couple levels right near it) require some very precise timing and execution, so don't go into it expecting just a chill puzzle game.The dialogue had some pretty charming moments too, and most of the music was pretty nice.

_childDocuments_.review: it was OK. found the first 70% of the game very easy and the last 30% extremely tedious. great concept but the execution made me realize its pretty limited in its uses, and that speaks for itself in the relatively short catalog of levels/worlds/mechanics. this game was very held back by a lack of an undo button, but i can sort of see why it wasn't implemented.
