_childDocuments_.review: Before buying this game, I should warn you that it is not what it seems.This game is a very challenging puzzle platformer with a big emphasis on reflex timings and precision platforming. Most levels will require you to first make a plan of where to move the characters by taking turns between the two; and then to carry out the plan efficiently. This is challenging not only because the puzzles themselves are elaborate, but because certain puzzles demand a lot mechanical skill. Some of the puzzles may require upwards of 30 seconds to finish, and having to restart them several times due to mechanical imprecisions can become frustrating. In my opinion, World 4 is notorious for this. The game also rewards you with optional collectibles for finishing levels within time and turn constraints, in case you want to "100%" the game. In some of the puzzles it will be expected of you to use obscure mechanics that exist in the game but that will not have been explained to you in order to obtain these collectibles (as an example, as Topdee you can place a block covering Toodee and what will always happen is that when you switch turns, Toodee will clip above the block and not anywhere else). These mechanics are interesting to see in an extra world, but having them seep into the main game is not good, even if you only need them for optional collectibles, because they are very obscure and you don't need them to finish any of those levels; using them feels like cheating. I also found the time constraints to be way too tight in general.The other thing I wanted to warn you about is that this might not be a good co-op game. I haven't tried it out myself, but as far as I know, it works exactly like singleplayer except that each player controls only one of the characters. Given how tough this game is and how precise you have to be when switching turns, the co-op sounds to me like a hellish experience.On other aspects, the game is bland. It has an alright art style, decent soundtrack, repetitive boss fights (except the final), and an empty narrative that is only interesting in the prologue and in the ending. It is also short, even if you're going after completion, so I cannot recommend the game at full price.So why am I giving this game a positive review after bashing it so much? Figuring out most of the puzzles was a lot of fun for me because the quality of most of them is very good. Also, Toodee (the character affected by gravity) feels comfortable to control; and the last world was a very welcome change of pace. The game also contains some jokes related to programming and dimensions, which are funny by being out-of-context and breaking the fourth wall.TL; DR: Decide whether you are really into both puzzle games and precision/timing platformers, then get this game at a discount, for a singleplayer experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a super interesting title from start to finish, utilizing a unique gimmick of swapping from a side perspective, where you platform over gaps and obstacles, to a top-down perspective, where you move and place blocks, to solve a series of short puzzles. As the game progresses, new ways to approach puzzles are added, such as enemies and new interactive blocks.The game doesn't overstay its welcome, having just enough variety and being just long enough where the perspective flipping gimmick still feels as fresh by the end as it did in the beginning.The game has amazing presentation all around, with great pixel art and an amazing soundtrack.The only issue I had with the game is that messing up a puzzle can mean that you need to restart the entire level in specific instances. This is only an issue with a few of the harder levels, but it often wore me down having to redo the entire puzzle just to get to the one part of the puzzle I'm having problems with. However, this issue only comes up a few times throughout, and I don't mind it since the puzzles themselves were still interesting and satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: 100% steam deck playthrough. wow what a journey! this games mechanics are put together in a completely unique way. full play through took me about 12 hours. its a fun challenge and will make you think in new ways. i would say 70% puzzle game and 30% platformer. the puzzles were better than the platform experience. highly recommended and not just because someone told me. if you enjoyed braid youll enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer. The 2 dimensions mechanic works pretty well and new elements are introduced each world to keep it fresh. The final stages are quite challenging and the last bit is very unique. Would've preferred more upbeat music, and the dialogue could've been better, but those are minor things, overall it's a fun game, and there are also secrets to be uncovered.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Still only halfway through the game but thoroughly enjoying it. Really cool concept and the puzzles are really fun, and there's some pretty clever writing in the dialogue. You get a little bit of extra enjoyment if you are a programmer and get all of the puns and stuff.The art style is really cute and consistent, and I enjoy the soundtrack more than I even expected.The game also has a big deal of replayability with the 3 types of extra challenges: each level has collectable bugs (again, another programming related pun). Blue ones are awarded by using only a certain minimum amount of switches between Toodee and Topdee, which vary per level. Red ones are collected by finishing the level in a certain amount of time, and levels with enemies have an extra pink one, awarded by finishing the level without killing any of them.Overall, this is a great example of what makes indie games so good: they actually try to do different things and always remember the core value of gaming in general, which is being fun and entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: I've been out of the loop of playing puzzle games for a long time, but Toodee and Topdee was a lot of fun! The game revolves around the two titular characters switching the world's viewpoints. Toodee has a 2D platformer's viewpoint, able to jump and bound by the laws of gravity, while Topdee has a top-down game's viewpoint, able to pick up and push boxes and unable to cross gaps in the floor. The story merges the worlds of these two characters together and they must join forces to restore the universe, in a story punctuated with occasional boss fights and witty game developer in-jokes.The puzzles in this game get HARD. There's a couple tricky ones here and there in the first two worlds, but the worlds after that regularly have puzzles that can take you over 10 minutes to wrap your head around. I feel proud that I was able to beat the game without having to look up any solutions, but the settings menu has loads of accessibility settings to tweak the game and get the player past hard levels if they really need it.A couple other things! Each level has collectibles in the form of ladybugs, asking the player to beat level under certain conditions, which provide additional challenge outside of the levels themselves. They also seem to unlock some sort of secret, but at the time of writing I'm unsure as to what that is! The game has pretty memorable music, especially near the end. And the game's sprites make clever use of scaling to make the transition between viewpoints really smooth and satisfying. Overall Toodee and Topdee is a really clever and special puzzle game and I'd recommend many people to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

_childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is a fun puzzle platformer. I played it with my partner and I can't wait to see more.I really like the fact that you can switch between 2D and isometric views based on the character you are playing. This makes for some interesting puzzles when switching the perspective your brain is functioning in.  The artwork is cute and cheery. The music isn't a pain to hear. The bosses are a lot of fun too. _childDocuments_.review: Toodee and Topdee is honestly a weird game for me. Initially I played a large amount of this game through Remote Play but ended up buying the game myself to play it all through. I will say out of the gate that I think if you are a completionist like me, you probably will not enjoy this game as much and it will become quite frustrating at times. There are definitely some noticeable issues I've experienced with  the controls feeling incredibly slippery and not precise at times, which would be fine if the game wasn't constantly incentivising you to go fast due to each level having a collectable associated with speed. Other issues include incidents such as placing a block on the other side of a one block-wide gap rather than in the gap directly in front of me, or fire shooting through a solid metal block to kill me despite me needing to set the blocks up in such a way to complete the stage.I took some issue with both sides of the platformer/puzzler hybrid and found that the difficulty of the platforming sections felt alarmingly inconsistent at times, and the puzzle side of things had me saying on multiple occasions: "That doesn't feel like it should be the solution, but it works I guess?" which made completing levels often rather unsatisfying. I particularly remember two instances throughout my playthrough where I was given the solution of it being a mechanic I was entirely unaware of, and just felt annoyed about it.One positive thing I can definitely say is the soundtrack is very good. There were no tracks in particular I disliked, and I'd lean more towards saying I enjoyed most if not all of them during my completion of the game.These things being said, the game got me to play it through to the end, and to 100% it. So I guess it does enough right for me to feel it was worth playing. I wish there was honestly a third option for recommending or not recommending for an in-between. I'd say if you want a cute game and don't care about full completion you will likely get some enjoyment out of Toodee and Topdee. But if you are a completionist, this one's for the masochists.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game with a unique concept of knowing when to flip between different perspectives to complete each level. Most stages will generally take 30-40 secs to complete and are not excessively long (barring the last world). While you'll likely die a lot due to trial and error, it never feels like the game is punishing you too harshly with backtracking. The game definitely takes a curve in difficulty by World 3 (f*** you Elementemple) and makes you work your two brain cells. Take a quick break if you're really stuck on a level and you'll be surprised how you quick you solve it when you jump back into it.I will note that I found Topdee's controls a bit too sensitive at times and sometimes moves one step (or "block") too far. More than half of my deaths were him just walking into fire involuntarily (again, f*** you Elementemple.)   Bosses were hit or miss and sometimes took their sweet time during each boss phase. That said, each one did take the concept of the changing "2D/Top-D" perspectives and added unique twists to them.The overall game isn't very long (around 4-5 hours) but the ladybug collectibles help add to the game's length and provide an extra challenge. I haven't collected them all but damn, be prepared to play like your an AGDQ speedrunner for some stages. (Bosses are even worse where you can't collect them if you die once and have to restart :D)Any person that's a fan of platformers/puzzles should consider investing in this game whenever their's a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Developer dietzribi’s first title combines 2D side-scrolling platforming sections, with puzzle-centric top-down block pushing. The remixing of these two classic gameplay formulas results in a uniquely fresh experience! The controls are incredibly easy to grasp but difficult to truly master. Thankfully, its retro-inspired difficulty level was intentional. The developers include more contemporary accessibility options, for players who prefer a less challenging experience. I'd highly recommend this game to fans of puzzle games, retro-inspired titles, or anyone just looking to try something new. Everything from its top-notch pixel art, to its genre-bending soundtrack, makes Toodee and Topdee one of the most charming indie titles of 2021. _childDocuments_.review: This is surprisingly good. You switch between block-puzzles in a top-down view and platforming in a side-scrolling view, and the blocks take on different effects depending on which perspective you're looking at. However there are some really weird design decisions in this game that hamper the experience. I think the biggest problem is that there are mechanics that you're not properly introduced to. Certain blocks have properties that are never explained in-game, for example their interaction with elements. Wooden blocks are broken by lightning, but gravity-obeying blocks are somehow fine; you can push them through the lightning but you can't actually use the block to protect yourself; to do that, you need lightning blocks. I mean this is just confusing and makes otherwise simple puzzles take way longer than necessary. There's also boss battles which to be honest feel out of place, why is there anything reflex-based in this game? And the last issue that pretty much everyone's brought up, the lack of mistake rewinding, but it's especially annoying here because of all the precision BS you're expected to do. There's even a death counter in this game, like what the hell purpose does that serve? I mean it's like this game bounces between a puzzle game and Super Meat Boy. Overall a good game that has a few questionable decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: We've come to a point in puzzle-based video games where the greatest challenge is inventing a mechanic unique to the genre. Toodee and Topdee create its unique puzzles from the blending of two types of navigation: 2D platforming and isometric walking. Neither mechanic in itself is unique, they've been around since the beginning of games, but having characters from each method of movement tag in and out to get through 90 different levels definitely feels fresh and is a whole lot of fun. Toodee and Topdee begins with a quick rundown of how our two protagonists end up requiring the help of one another. Each character lives in a separate world that revolves around a semicolon, that is until the villain steals the universe anchor and plunges the world into chaos.  In order to retrieve the stolen semicolon and bring order back to their worlds, Toodee and Topdee work together to traverse the chaos and find the missing punctuation mark.The former moves through the level in traditional 2D platforming, while the latter walks throughout the level in an overhead isometric fashion. Topdee can pick up blocks and move them around in order to create platforms for Toodee to make it to the portal to exit the level. Each of the 5 different worlds all have a separate theme, whether it be animal avoidance or manipulating elements like fire and water.  The first 4 worlds have twenty levels with the final having 10 with a very unique twist. Mechanics are very easy to pick up and the difficulty of the puzzles increase at a steady pace. It wasn't until the fourth world where I had to set down the controller and really put some hard thought into how to make it out of the level. The last final worlds are particularly difficult and are great mental exercises for those who love a challenge. Speaking of challenges, each world ends with a boss that is pretty difficult in their own right. Beating the boss is less about figuring out a puzzle and more about timing the platforming and switching between the characters at the right moment. None feel impossible to beat, but they definitely require a few tries in order to really get the timing right for victory.If the threat of intense challenge feels too stressful, Toodee and Topdee has some of the best accessibility I've seen in a puzzle-based game. Different toggles allow for the difficulty to be lowered in different ways. Allowing Toodee to perform double jumps can get you out of a jam, or if you can't get the timing down, just turn on infinite health. Everyone will have an opportunity to finish the game on their own terms. In my particular playthrough it took a little under 5 hours to complete a single run of the game, but some in-game challenges do provide incentive to give it another go. Between the seamless mechanics, delightful graphics, and enjoyable humour in the writing, Toodee and Topdee is a whole lot of fun for folks of all ages. Score: 7.5 / 10Pros Colourful and vibrant worldSeamless blend of platforming and isometric mechanicsAccessibility options are terrificConsWorlds can feel a bit long near the endAchievements made clear early on
_childDocuments_.name: Toodee and Topdee

name: Mini Motor Racing X
detailed_description: Welcome to the world of Mini Motor Racing X! Strap yourself in, or strap on your VR headset, and jump into a nitro fuelled world where little cars mean BIG fun! Spanning across reclaimed ruins and scorched outbacks through to rain soaked docks and sunkissed tropical islands - Mini Motor Racing X will take you on a micro driving journey across the globe like no other. Tackle the massive career mode as you upgrade and fine-tune your garage of vehicles through four unique championships spanning the diverse landscapes offered throughout. Take the journey solo or complete the entire campaign with a friend via local couch co-op or online. Feeling more like a quick blast with more friends or some online randos? Tackle any of the 52 tracks in up to 4 player online races. Or, if you’re feeling extra frisky, try any of the multiplayer party modes on offer such as Bumper Ball or Micro Motor Racing! FEATURES: HUGE CAREER: Collect dozens of cars and race on over 50 tracks in hundreds of races with vibrant, rich visuals, day and night and in varying weather conditions. UPGRADE YOUR RIDES: Pump your hard earned winnings into upgrades to help give you the edge. PLAY IN FLATSCREEN OR VR WITH CROSS PLAY: Full support for VR and non-VR gameplay with multiplayer cross play between them as well as several other platforms. RE-IMAGINED FOR VR: Play the entire game in VR as MMRX has been re-designed and tuned for VR to bring the full game experience to life in new dimensions and with additional play modes. MULTIPLAYER: Online multiplayer with up to 4 friends for campaign co-op or competitive racing. SPLIT-SCREEN ACTION: Play couch co-op split-screen with up to four people or take them on in any number of competitive races. PARTIES ARE BETTER WITH FRIENDS: Take on friends online in several party mode games designed to bring out the worst in you. ULTRAWIDE SUPPORT: Featuring support for 4K and Ultra-wide resolutions. Please note that Steam users whom purchased 'Mini Motor Racing Evo' will receive 'Mini Motor Racing X' for free on their Steam account.

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this review when I spend more time with the game. I will also do a full video review. Anyways, I got this game because I already owned Mini Motor Racing Evo (as did 14 of my Steam friends). I got this game as part of a 2018 Fanatical bundle for only $3 USD. Of course, The Binary Mill didn't have to do this. They are a well-regarded VR developer that has two very good VR games in Gun Club VR (very underappreciated) and Rush. Most devs would not have thought to include the VR game for free to anyone who bought a prior game that was not well-received in Non-VR. Mini Motor Racing X, however, is not just the same game, but now in VR. There have been several quality of life improvements that make this game even better in VR and also Non-VR. They really didn't have to make this free, they just care about their customers.I haven't played the game much, but I am enjoying the career mode. It has a normal racing mode and also an alternate mode with all the power-ups and mayhem you'd expect in an arcade kart racer. You also have a ton of options on how you want to play this game. Want to use your motion controllers as a gamepad? No problem. Want to use your motion controllers as a hand where you hold on to the steering wheel? Check. Want to be in the driver's seat, first person view? Done. Want to play above the racing track and watch the little racing cars below you? You get it your way here.There's also all the graphical, sound, or comfort options you'd ever want. Plus there's different game modes from career to quick race. There's also this neat mode that plays a lot like Rocket League. You can also customize your avatar and also upgrade and unlock vehicles. The only thing this game needs is better multiplayer support. There are no lobbies for multiplayer (you just join random multiplayer groups and then vote on which map/mode you want). That's really my main and only criticism so far. It also doesn't have "wheel support", although it does support gamepads (VR and Non-VR). Lastly, I think the races & tracks may be a bit too short, although there's lots of variety with the number of tracks and being able to play day or night, along with some weather conditions. There's also different difficulty levels.The game ran smoothly. The sounds are okay for an arcade mini racer. The visuals are good. The art style and different track layouts fit with the game type. The different weapons and power-ups also feel good. The cars different attributes make them feel different from one another (better handling, faster acceleration, etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed on: GeForce GTX 1660 / Samsung Odyssey PlusSettings: Maxedtl;dr:This game is kind of amazing. (Also: THE MUSIC IS INCREDIBLE. It reminds me of Sonic Adventure and Crazy Taxi.)The real:I had been looking for a fun ‘little’ racer in VR. Not a throwaway game, but a game with actual content to it that I can sit down and play and really have a good time with. I bought Asetto Corsa with the assumption that its VR support was less than dreary, but that was a bust. I saw this pop up today and had to try it - and it 100% scratched that itch. =What is it?=A so-called ‘RC racer’, you basically race MicroMachines along a huge variety of tracks (the store page lists 50+ tracks and 100+ races, many are done backwards or in different weather to add gameplay) across four campaign circuits with either classic or new weapon-based gameplay modes (for a more Mario Kart or Twisted Metal feel), a quick-race and multiplayer quick-race, four non-standard arcade game modes, car unlocks and customizations… It’s all very overwhelming, to be honest, to see this much content put together so well in a VR package. The VR interface is flawless and well-executed, there are tons of comfort options and camera angles - and if you’re a masochist like me, you turn everything down and off so you feel every rumble. (It would have been nice to see WMR controller support modeled in-game, but it’s not a big deal, as I’m used to seeing Vive controllers by now anyway.)=How’s it play?=Exactly how you’d expect. I use motion controllers, and the driver’s wheel is responsive, the cars control like they’re RC cars (you have accelerate, brake, and boost, and that’s about it - brake while accelerating to drift) and it supports standard m/kb or gamepad through VR as well. The collisions are physics-based and its all extremely entertaining, especially in first-person. Stacks of tires will constantly get in the way and fly around as cars collide with them and each other, boosting around and into each other as they fling weapons. (It’s fun)I played two or three times online and didn't notice any lag. The Rocket League style soccer map is a load of fun. Offline everything is very polished and runs near-90fps for me (even at ~300% res scale to get a sharp picture), and even the more odd arcade game modes are a blast. (hmu if you wanna play online this game is seriously fun in VR)=Should I get it?=Yeah, I’d say so. It’s a free gift if you already own the game previously, but I’d say if you don’t, it’s worth the full price to support the devs. There’s a lot of content here; this is the result of the benefit of porting an already established game to VR. Bug-free goodness of a solid pancake game, but with fully enjoyable immersive 3D.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has improved a  since it was called "Mini Motor Racing EVO" [which has also been removed from Steam, so props to the devs for taking the game down and actually improving it].It's still not a perfect game, not by a long shot, and some (not all*) of my initial problems with the game have returned in this version. I'll list my issues off quickly, so I can get to giving this game's improvements the credit they deserve:-The corners of some objects (more often I'm noticing this with parts of the track itself now, instead of objects  the track) will still randomly catch your car while turning or trying to cut the tiniest little bit off of a tight corner, and you'll spin out or hit an invisible wall (this could be easily remedied by moving the invisible boundaries slightly further back from the edge of the track). Even in this criticism though, I do have to give the devs credit because it's nowhere near as significant of an issue as it was in the last iteration of the game.-The grind to level up your car is still a little too rough. It has been improved in later stages, but the early game is still a problem. I think raising the payout on races by about 100-200 (across the entire game) would make the game significantly more rewarding and less grindy, without ever putting you in a position where you're steamrolling the opponents. Another possible solution would be to increase the amount earned from money pickups on the track, because getting $50 for going out of my way to pick something up just doesn't feel worth it. Now if those pickups were worth $250, that'd be something far more interesting.And that's it for my old complaints, now for a couple of new ones before we get to the praise:-The final championship is dull af. I understand the grand tour vibe they were going for, but essentially making us race 24 laps on every track in the game just feels like padding. (6 laps per race, 1 race forward during day, 1 forward during night, 1 reverse day, 1 reverse night). The tracks aren't varied, long, or impressive enough that racing them in reverse feels like something new or interesting. However the Ai balancing of the final races has been DRASTICALLY improved, making the game far less frustrating to play. I actually reached the end of the final championship and was surprised when the achievement popped, simply because I was  the game to still be BS at the end. It wasn't, and I'm honestly really impressed by all the improvements that have been made.-The new modes are undercooked.--Bumper Ball is basically discount Rocket League, and that's okay. The biggest problem with this mode is that, unlike in Rocket League, there's no option to focus the camera on the ball, so a lot of the time your camera will get stuck (for various reasons) facing into walls, or in the opposite direction of where you want it to be, which isn't helpful when you're trying to play football with cars that still don't have  handling. Also, cars with sloped fronts (Supercar, for example) really struggle to get any purchase on the ball, so that's something that, I think, also needs to be fixed if that mode is going to be worth playing.--X Mode is just a combat racing mode which, again, is fine and welcome. the problems I have with it, are that you only get 1 power up per lap (as you start the next lap), and what you get is weighted towards what position you're in. If you cross the line in 1st place, chances are you'll get a Wrench. If you cross the line in 8th, there's a good chance you'll get a Twister (the whirlwind thing, can't remember the name I only saw it once while getting the final achievement, lol). I think having powerup pickups on the track (similar to how it's done in games like, for example, Mario Kart) would prove to be much more enjoyable and chaotic. Or maybe set it to a universal timer, similar to how pickups work in Rocket League's Rumble mode. I also think that it should be explained in game that pickups can't all be obtained from certain race positions,  the weighting should be pretty much entirely removed. That's just my opinion, though.And that's honestly all the criticism I have for this game. Not bad going considering the last iteration got a 1/10 from me, lol.Now, the good bit.Holy  has this game gotten better since last time.+The newly added camera options (and steering options) make the game significantly more fun to play and, although the constant twitching of the car (due to the handling of the cars in the game) messed a little with my eyes, it's still a substantial and welcome improvement.+The controls don't feel anywhere near as floaty as I remember them feeling, and I also didn't have any issues with vehicles randomly turning on their own. The controls still take a little getting used to, but I feel like what's there now is a stylistic choice, rather than undertested gameplay.+The AI drivers no longer seem to be so obsessed with ruining your day. Sure you'll still get bumped, but it seems a lot more like the other cars want to race now, rather than just wanting to specifically see you lose. Another great improvement.+The AI actually seem like they use the same boosting rules as the player now, which is a big improvement since last time. Any losses now feel substantially less cheap/unfair, and more the result of the AI simply racing better.+The game's in-game settings menus actually work properly this time!+In all the time I played this version, I never encountered a single crash (something that this game REALLY struggled with in its last iteration). I played it safe and closed the game any time I was gunna go afk, so I didn't really give it the opportunity to crash like it used to. But, either way, I still didn't experience a single crash, and that's also a big improvement since last time.Overall, I'm shocked by how much this game has improved.Well done on listening to your audience devs, and hopefully a few patches can improve what's here into something even better than it already is.Warmly recommended,7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ VR and non-VR version available.✔️ A lot of tracks (roundabout 50 with over 200 overall variations).✔️ Upgrade system✔️ Variation in game modes (Rocket League mode, King of the Hill etc. for a nice couch evening with friends).✔️ Charming art style and presentation.✔️ You can change camera to your liking (Third person, first person, bird's eye view etc.).✔️ Racing only mode or with items available.✔️ Soundtrack.✔️ Can be experienced in co-op with progress sharing,✔️ Price (Only 1,24€ / -90% off) during sale.❌AI is not the brightest and will use nitro randomly or boost into you in a corner.❌If you want to complete the game to 100% you need to experience tracks multiple times (Day-time, night-time, reverse etc.).❌ lackluster weapon implementation."Mini Motor Racing X" is a love letter to the good old "Re-Volt" times. After sinking in several hours, I can say that Mini Motor Racing X is pretty fun. From seemingly small options to many extras, it offers a lot. While I wish the extra modes were better and that the levels were more consistent, Mini Motor Racing X has earned an ongoing spot on my Steam library. Even its longer levels only take a few minutes, making it an ideal game to jump in and out of for just a few minutes. The core racing feels great, I truly can’t remember the last time I enjoyed an overhead arcade racer so much. There are a lot of good racing games, but none of them scratches quite the same itch that this one does. As long as you go into it knowing what to expect, I think you’ll have a great time. I completed this to 100% and the content it offers for the price it asks is insane:The game’s Career mode makes up the bulk of the gameplay in Mini Motor Racing X; you’ll race your way through championships, unlocking more courses along the way, in addition to new vehicles and upgrades. These can then be utilised in the separate Quick Race mode and Arcade mode (which features a mini-game called Bumper Ball, and is essentially the game’s inferior take on Rocket League). If you like collecting new items, you’ll find plenty here to be getting on with.From a technical point of view, Mini Motor Racing X doesn't make any major mistakes, which isn't surprising considering the modest graphics. You get a stable frame rate and fast loading times. A special feature of the game is the controls. By default, you control your vehicle from an angled bird's eye view. I had to get used to this change of perspective at first, but it fits well with the concept of the game. It makes you feel more like you're controlling a remote-controlled miniature car with the controller than actually playing a racing game. All this gives Mini Motor Racing X its own charm, even if the effect wears off comparatively quickly, hence why I changed the view about five hours into the game to third person. If you prefer, however, you can switch to other various alternative views such as a cockpit perspective. If you do that, the game controls very classically. This is where the metaphor of the miniature car comes into play again: If you drive it into a wall, it might have a scratch, but it simply bounces off and continues driving afterwards but who plays these kind of games because of realism?Mini Motor Racing X is an entertaining racing game that scores points especially with the consistent implementation of the miniature car idea. The game controls differently than the competition, at least in the standard view, and forces you to rethink, which can provide motivation in the short term. In the long run, however, the gameplay may suffer from a lack of variety, especially due to the short tracks and relatively familiar game modes. Nevertheless, Mini Motor Racing X is worth a look for racing game fans who want to see the genre presented in a slightly different way.Want to see more Re-Volt like games? How about... Re-Volt itself? Check out:

_childDocuments_.review: I received this product for free via .I played predominantly on the  with a gamepad, but also tried out motion controllers, and on desktop too.Mini Motor Racing X is a great and welcome entry for RC type racers in the VR space. Its easy to pick up and packs a nice amount of content. There is a demo available, and your progress from that is carried over to the full version - nice!One of the most  aspects for me was just how different it feels on desktop, the camera angles offered are quite different from VR and that really does mix things up. You tend to be more up close and personal on the desktop, with more camera movement, compared to VR which has you by default in a wider overview with a selection of angles which can put you trackside, or even further away!There are a good range of , from audio, graphics, controls, etc. 3 Difficulty settings, and to play with or without weapons.On the  side of things, I preferred playing with a gamepad (didnt try with a wheel, who knows that could be fun o.0) With a gamepad you can pick to steer clockwise/anti or have the car point in the direction of your stick. With motion controllers you can pick to steer clockwise/anti, or by pointing the controller, or by twisting the controller. When in cockpit mode, you grab the wheel with motion controller. I tried them all but happily went back to the vanilla thumbstick rotate, but options are always nice! ran maxed out 4K with MSAAx8 capped at 94fps (gsync) with such little GPU (2080ti) usage the fans didnt even come on. This thing could probably run on good integrated graphics! obviously takes a bit more, but entry level (GTX970) hardware should be fine. I played for a bit using 2 settings to compare data. Default SS (Steam has set to 150%), 90Hz with everything in game at default, which was high and MSAAx4 - with this the GPU was at about 30% usage, and didnt drop any frames. 2nd test was set to 120Hz and in game res scale set to 1.5 - with this the GPU was being quite well used, typically 80%+, and it held the frame rate at all times.A few things I would like to see added - Ability to play local coop with one person in VR and the other on desktop - Track editor (Which I believe its predecessor had :s)- Slightly wider detection range for showing track outlines. While you can jump about viewing positions during play, I preferred to stay putt, and if your car goes behind a structure you get the outline of the track, but it can be cut pretty closeThis is a lot of fun and an easy recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: I know I haven't played much yet, but this game is simply awesome. This review targets mostly the people who already know a thing or two about racing games like this. You know, the arcade top-down racers.Have you ever heard of Mini Motor Racing Evo? This game is basically an ultimate version of that game. They are pretty similar, but the devs took it and made it 10x better with tons of innovations alongside graphical improvements.Pros: - Awesome features that literally destroy the competition such as:- 20+ cars to choose from. Unlike the older version, they all have cockpit cameras with modeled interiors.- Detailed tracks with the return of remastered classics and new, fun tracks.- You can now choose from a big variety of camera angles. Adds a lot to the overall experience.- A whole new career mode with sick weapons alongside the classic one- A Rocket League inspired mode called Bumper Ball, and also a different mode called Micro Motor Racing which is also interesting-  Local co-op up to 4 players. WOOOHOO- Multiplayer, of course. Play with friends, etc.- More liveries for your mini cars!- You can refund your upgrades which was a feature the older one lacked (I think)- ALMOST FORGOT! You can change the difficulty in career mode. Believe me, the game gets really hard at times. Now you can make it easier if you are OK with it. Or make it harder if you are mad or something.ConsThey are minor details that I think would be better if changed.- No workshop (yet???)- 20+ cars is a good thing to start with... but none of those are new. All from the previus game. Which is why I want to consider this game something between a remaster and a sequel. Well, it was given for free to anyone who owns the previus game so I totally can't complain. If you are new to the series, the game not having new cars isn't even relevant for you so no worries.- Some tracks don't have detailed backgrounds. The few that do share the same background most of the time. This isn't a problem but surely makes the art style inconsistent.- Naming cars is not their strong game... cars are named like "sports car, hatchback, sedan". - Lack of licensing of TF2 and Portal which the older title had :( unfortunate but it's expected. The cars and tracks for these two still exist but they are renamed and the stuff resembling the games got removed. Both Fruit Ninja car and the map is still there though! That's all, I guess. This is a simple game. Totally kid-friendly and anyone can enjoy alongside them. Totally fun to kill time and play agianst friends etc.

If you aren't winning your car isn't upgraded enough. Or you are using the wrong car. You doing anything better, you if are driving semi okay. Will have next to no impact until you hit the high levels which unless you are particularly bored, have no other games, or are a kid. Probably won't happen.Some of the tracks are designed well enough even with the boring car feel that you can have a pretty good time. But likewise a lot are bland and just kind of time wasters.The battle mode or regular kart, game mode. Is wholly lacking. A shield, a mine, a rocket, and a wrench which bounces randomly, and a BS tornado. That is it. The game modes they have now would be fine for young kids. But the entire game is limited by the speed of the cars. The nitro which is in both game modes. Can't be made to spawn in a fair manner because everyone is so close. Because everyone is so slow. And the tracks are so short. That it is impossible to do. So what happens really. Is first place keeps getting the bulk of them. And no one can catch up because they are in first. And thus will stay in first. Unless you get hit with 15 tornado's. Which you might.The soccer game mode suffers from the same problem as the rest of the game everything's so slow and condensed that it's just a crap show.The game is like any other karting game. But if they only had 50cc karts. No 100cc no 150cc. Just 50cc.  You can have fun with it. But it's very limited by the decision to make slower cars and smaller tracks. And there really isn't enough content to make you want to keep coming back. If you've got anything better to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: It really is a great game, nothing else could add to what was developed, very nice graphics, excellent gameplay, a good number of tracks, cars and many improvements for these ones, and a good number of game modes, and view modes. I had fun and I liked trying the demo version, and I really enjoyed the game from the moment I bought it, it is totally recommended !!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: it's honestly not worth it. even on a sale. I recently played it with my gf and we both agreed that it's too boring and monotonous. also what's up with the ai being much faster than the pc? no matter which car you pick and with nigh perfect nitro consumption, the rubberbanding in this game is quite insane. it's honestly unfortunate considering you can play this in 4 player coop splitscreen but the gameplay is too weak to get players engrossed
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty sick if you like this kind of game. There is a good amount of variation and a solid creative direction behind a lot of the tracks. The UI is super cluttered and not very nice to look at in general, but the 3D artwork is pretty good. The controls are solid and responsive. The general gameplay is great (one again, if you like these types of racing games). A lot of these kinds of games have weapons forced on but this series has always had a focus on non-combat racing. However, it looks this entry does have an option to turn on some kind of combat racing.   I haven't tried VR yet but the game seems to have some performance issues (low FPS) in full screen but runs fine in windowed mode. Overall this is a solid game and maybe one of the better games in this kind of arcade-y "penny-racer" style. I would recommend this but the price may be *slightly* steep to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: A very unexcepted use of VR ! Very neat and well exploited !Several ways to play, with or without motion controller, it's very appreciated !Game itself is really cool with load of content, good cartoonish graphics, very well optimized (for VR), music are cool !There are just one point on which i have a reservation.Handling of vehicle is too much arcade to my taste. I know, it's an arcade game, but the driving lacks of deepness. No difference between asphalt and dirt, for example. In lot of courses, you can holding the throttle all the long of the track, without pressing the brake once. Moreover, the brake is almost of no use.But hey, I salute the overall work and the quality of the VR programming !If you like this kind of game and VR, you will love Mini Motor Racing X !!
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I typically enjoy the isometric view racer but this one just feels too off. I have two major complaints about this one that made me stop pretty early though.1 - The physics are weird. The AI can push you around no problem but you can't do anything to the AI.2 - It feels way too grindy. You don't get much money per race (Starting about $100-125 for a win) but upgrades cost hundreds of dollars. After just a half hour of playing, I literally couldn't keep up as I watch AI cars just go faster than my fastest cars. I don't want to keep playing the same level over and over just to get money to upgrade my car enough to stand a chance in the next races. The tracks are short, you can finish most races in about a minute, minute and a half, but I don't want to be playing the same tracks just to compete in the newer tracks. Looking at some of the other reviews, people are saying that when you do have enough money to level up your cars, that the game becomes entirely too easy too. I didn't get that far but at this point, I'm already done with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the cleanest and best-presented RC racers I've played on PC. Typically, these types of games resemble their counterparts in real life, and they're cheap & trashy. This has so many features I'm not used to seeing in an RC game, and plenty of content including tracks, cars, modes, etc.I don't even recall how I received this game, but I would highly recommend it if you're into kart racers and bite-sized games that you can pick up & put down quickly. I'd buy it again. And, it supports VR which based on the gameplay I would have to imagine runs pretty well.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I got this for free because I own the original Mini Motor Racing X. It's still pretty much the same Mini Motor Racing game but with more cameras which I wanted when I used to play this on an iPod back in 2011 and a new career mode called Type X which gives you weapons to use every lap. There is also an Arcade Mode that has new modes such as Time Trials, Custom Races, a Rocket League-like game mode minus also the flying and explosions called Bumper Ball, and a faster-paced racing that makes your car faster and smaller called Micro Motor.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motor Racing X is the upgraded version of Mini Motor Racing Evo, which I received for free due to having the latter in my library.Now, I'll start with the positive aspects. The game offers two modes, one where you straight up drive and the other one which adds a few items such as mines into play. The fact you can complete the entire game in co-op locally or online is certainly one of the game strongest points, and you can customize your car a bit. Another thing I really wish some more popular devs would implement is the camera modes, ranging from top down view, chase cam all the way down to the cockpit view.That's it for the positives. Sure, I could talk about how the game is colorful and stuff but that'd be trying to find beauty in the gradients of brown displayed in a steaming turd.Because boy, the negatives far outweight everything I just said.First off, the graphics look ugly. I don't mind dated graphics, but this is more of a poor design issue. The music and the engine sounds are pretty terrible as well.Second, the UI is atrocious. It feels like a mobile game and thanks to the kind user below, I now know that's because it is a port of a mobile game.Last but not least: the handling is bad and by that I mean . There is absolutely no complexity to it, as the car loses so much speed while turning that breaking is useless. By the way, cars shouldn't get on two wheels whenever you take a turn.In the end, even the items become useless. Not only cause they're so scarce, but also because the circuits are so damn tiny you'll spend more time fighting with the other cars masses just to stay on track than actually driving.It was a terrible game when it was called Evo and X isn't doing any better. Keep your money and save yourself some wasted time. Don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.Ingredients:1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter2. 1/2 cup white sugar3. 1/2 cup brown sugar4. 1/4 cup water5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon6. 1 pinch salt7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced8. 1 pastry for double-crust pieDirections:1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for free because being an old Mini Motor Racing Evo owner that got delisted on steam, thanks dev! This is essentially 2nd remake of Mini Motor Racing (still available on google play store and probably apple store).Pros:-Wide range of camera-Easy to learn, hard to master-Somewhat balanced cars that carries from vanilla game-New mechanics of weapons-Includes VR with good GUI-Runs pretty well on pc.Cons:-Ridiculous default level's difficulty (tune down to easy till you get good enough for normal)-All 3rd Party IP tracks (except fruit ninja) such as Team Fortress 2 and Portal 2 were remade to not contain the IP pricing again, but lost the original feel and appeal. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: You wanna play a racing game ? Run away, it's a straight adaptation from mobile gaming. The menus are terrible, the tracks are so basics your chemistry teacher will make jokes about it, the soundtrack is uninspired and the sounds effects pitiful.Run away. I paid 2€ for it and i feel like i was scammed.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 52 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing Mini Motor Racing X. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son found this game at Christmas, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game world and started playing but I was stuck on what you were supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he helped me. Loved it as it was the best time had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.Thank you <3
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- A surprising amount of tracks and feels varied and fun- Controls feel good- The CPU difficulty is challenging - The CPU can pick up the same items and money- The CPU will challenge and bump into each other, feeling like they are all competing with each other for 1st place- Music is decent- Fun modes such as soccerCons- The CPU pretty much just follow the same path the whole time and won't grab the out of the way nitros- No option to turn off the game in the menu (if there is it seems to be buried somewhere really good)
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: It's like, on paper, everything is right.  There really is a lot here and it isn't terrible.  However, it's like they manage to fail on the 2 yard line in everything that's here.  The RC pro-am perspective races are good, but they're on tracks that are too tight.  The battle rounds don't have great weapons.  It's like they get it, but they don't.  A reluctant thumbs-up.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Too twitchy even for a veteran F1 keyboard racer. I suppose mouse steering might be more manageable but i gave up already, for now.Maybe because of the low res i selected - 720 p, which made it too twitchy.Graphics and sound wise are geared for much younger audience. It's all fun over-sized & undersized graphical elements like small cars but with truck sized wheels. Selection of vehicles is fun too; you could drive a school bus or make it look like an ambulance with a different livery. All vehicles have a several choices of liveries for your preference. Of course the school bus was much harder to control than a sports car.Works under Windows 7 flawlessly despite what the store specified. Actually from what i read in the reviews and forum, some Windows 10 users had problems. BTW many older games has totally disappeared from the store including recent AAA titles. "Long life to you my Thane."Probably steers smoothly with a controller; die hard keyboard drivers should skip this.  for efficiency and stability.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: A boring slog through the same courses either reversed or at night time. In career mode you're either a mile in front of everyone else or struggling to keep up with one incredibly fast car. Upgrading your car becomes so expensive that you never want to try different cars. The game is repetitive and simple. It was nice to kill some time at work, but after racing the same course for the twentieth time, I'm done. I've seen everything the game has to offer and it's not much. The courses are all incredibly simple and short, no interesting alternate routes or course hazards, just a reskinned track with a few turns. It's a very boring game with little charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Mildly recommended.This is a pretty well made arcade racer. The graphics are good, lots of tracks, vehicles, power ups and weapons, local and online coop, VR and a career mode. It didn't pull me in though. It felt too reliant on boosting and drifting for my tastes and less on skill, plus most tracks feel claustrophobic. In the end, it's a fair price for the content and level of polish.

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun mini racer. I would not have kept for full price, but for 1.49, this is good to have around. there is a typical race option and a cart type fighting race option, which kind of lacks in weapons, but is still fun. Most races are under 2 minutes long, so that bodes well for me also. Wait for sale, but decent fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Mini motor racing x. -man this game is fun! for anyone looking for a simple but not to hard core drive sim, this is for you, sure its not your casual, Sunday drive type of stuff, but its the nice feeling of being behind the wheel and just GOING. racing on the track, hands sweating as you grip the controllers, the crowds cheering, you're on the last lap, enemy's on your tail, you skid the corner and victory, victory, victory!-The small excitement of even starting out with just the base cars is pleasing, every race feels like a challenge, wither it classic mode or the more X mode where you get power ups, items and other things of that nature.-Do I reccomend this game? Oh heck yea! its on sale all the time and honestly I bought this at full price, this game is so worth the money! good job devs and if you've got friends bring em along. nothing gets your gut busting then 4 players racing each other like old mario kart 64
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I revisited Mini Motor Racing X many years after first checking out its previous iteration, called MMR Evo. When I first started the game, the Campaign mode would always result in a crash-to-desktop, something that I was able to fix with a trip to the game's Discussions and renaming a library.While I cannot say with much certainty what has changed from Evo to X, beyond support for VR which I didn't test, the game still felt oddly familiar despite its generic looks, and overall lack of personality. Somehow, it manages in not standing out from the crowd in any meaningful way, and yet I could remember Evo suffering from the same malaise.Eventually I managed to stick around for a few tracks from the beginners' Campaign, but it never stopped feeling like slowly chewing through slightly damp cardboard. I can still have plenty of fun with things like Death Rally (not the remakes), and more in general, I had tons of fun with Horizon Chase Turbo, so I'm pretty sure the game's milquetoast-ness is the problem here.

_childDocuments_.review: Only played a few races, but this is one of the most polished VR experiences Ive had.  Switch between top-down "table-top" view and in-cockpit. _childDocuments_.review: FUN! - am an Old Gamer and miss the likes of Super Sprint from the arcades and the Atari ST - this is the very best up-to date version of it, while still being a laugh to play - no overly complicated car set ups - Just FUN to play, with the added benefit of VR mode too which is absolutly spot on. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Works fine with the HP Reverb G2 WMR but you need to utilize one of the custom HTC Vive controller binding profiles shared by one of the community members. Everything worked by default except the grip control which is required to turn the key on the main menu in order to start the race.This is a nice game to play for short bursts of fun but I could never play it for extended periods because it's one of the few games that makes me dizzy and nauseous after 30 minutes of gameplay. I'm not sure why it happens with this game but I don't have that problem with other VR titles. Maybe the short tight tracks, brightness and fast turns is too much for my eyes to handle. I will most likely play it less frequently than other VR titles because of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like the previous version which was Mini Motor Racing Evo, as it resembled a phone game.This one seems to be more interesting as it supports VR where you can control the vehicles from various angles, even hold the wheel from the cockpit mode.Would prefer less corners in the tracks and more 'meaty' crashes. Also, the track editor from previous games seems to be missing.Personally it is not my taste, but I think it is a fair buy for the price it is available right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying, i had to make my Partner buy this game as well to play with , as such i do not play solo, i play versus/Co-op.This game is amazing for the price, under £12 and so much content that it will provide hours, and i do mean hours of fun.So much to say about it hard to know where to start but i'll try : The races are short, but that does not hinder the game. They is a main game where you get to do Cups, but you got 2 different types of career , normal race career, or a career with power ups and weapons. Then inside the career they is multiple different cups to aim for, beginner experienced and such, and within those you can also change the difficulty from easy medium and hard. You get a good amount of cars to pick from and some livery's to change, along with customisation for your character such as helmets,gloves and even the steering wheel can be changed. Then you get to the race it self where you can play as if your looking like toy cars/micro machine style, or you can play behind the wheel of the car, giving you more ways to play ( replayability is high in this one).On top of the career you have arcade where they is a game like rocket league where you try and score goals with a ball, along with 5 other arcade style game modes. Stuff to unlock,the music is great. i mean come on, for a VR game this game is fantastic. easy 7/10 and i will be playing loads in the future with my partner and friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, even if the AI's favorite thing in the world is nitro bombing you into a turn. The devs have created weaponized nitro and the AI isn't afraid to use it. Multiplayer is also very fun, but sad to say you won't find anyone there. I really like the game modes though and wish it was active.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Played a lot on viveport and decided to buy on sale. Very impressive graphics in VR. Half a year with VR and this game is still in my top 5 favorite for visuals. It really looks like you are driving little Pixar cars. There is something about the artstyle and certain camera angles that makes this game visually pop. Really appreciate the large amount of camera angles to choose, far more than most racers. Without VR it would mainly be for kids as their first racing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Valve IndexThis is the sort of game that isn't really for me but as you can see, I'm recommending it.  Top down racers are perhaps my least favorite genre of video game and while VR improves the experience tremendously making it feel more like playing with remote control cars than ever before I still feel that way.  You can play it as a kart racer but the short tracks and somewhat standard items will leave you wanting more.However, this game oozes quality and charm.  You can tell it has a limited budget but the graphics are extremely appealing despite being optimized exceptionally well for VR.  That is one of the games other major boons, it feels made for VR despite having full support for non-VR users.  I've played quite a few Racing games with VR support but none of them felt as seamless as this one, the interface for all the menus is made exceptionally for VR and with multiple means of doing it, you can select your car with a touch screen or you can grab a remote and poke the up and down buttons on it to change vehicles in the garage... or instead of poking it with your other hand you can press the A and B buttons on the Index Controller.That is one of the best things about this game.  It has so many options.  You can play top down, third-person, or first person, with multiple views for each.  Then there's the controls, just including what I could access with the Index controllers I had the option to play it with traditional stick input, a virtual steering wheel (which by the way felt very good in first person), a virtual RC car controller (This was the worst one as there's no real world spring pulling you back to the center of the turning. The Haptics which work so well for the wheel aren't quite up to the task.), then they have tilt controls, and pointer controls.  Apart from those last two switching between controls is quick and intuitive making experimentation fun and easy.They have numerous party modes so you have plenty of stuff to mess around with if you start getting tired of racing.As a smart move for a smaller title, they allow you to play single player while in matchmaking.  Not just some bare bones mode but the full game, you can complete cups and upgrade your car while waiting for someone else to jump on at 4 in the morning.The two main downsides for me are the genre and the music.  The music isn't bad by any stretch but it doesn't stand out, it reminds me of a third party Wii game with very standard and safe themes.  Overall, this feels like a hidden gem in need of more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: A great racing game overall, fun for all ages!The good?+ The vehicles are unique and each is suited for different tracks+ Great soundtrack and generally good design+ Can be something to kill time if you've got nothing to do+ Hilarious when cars fly off the ground after boosting on a tireHowever, it still has downsides.- I can't hear my car's engine sounds- There's no unique music for day and night courses like there used to be- Speedway has no music and will break the pause menu- It's hard to find an online gameDespite all those, MMRX serves to be the go-to racing games for people like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are the most important part of any game.Unfortunately this an amazing game that has the worst control options ever. It seems to support many different control types but steering wheels or mouse (spinner) are a no go. It seems they are trying to see how much crap they can add without touching the major issues which would be fixed very very easily.Sad to see what I would rate as one of the very best arcade racer on PC (as a top down or with a wheel) left as just another game that i forget even exists.While I would recommend this game in general if you havent played the original, if you have played the original or want to use some different controls (to give the game something extra) don't bother. Everything is excellent except the controls which in certain circumstances essentially maake the entire game ruined.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: This instantly became the favorite game for our Oculus Quest 2. Amazing detail, lots of great tracks and vehicles. Great detail, very fun. So many options from views, like sitting in the car, to how you drive, like using an RC remote, using the steering wheel in the car or just the joysticks. Great game, definitely worth the $10. Would have paid double that for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simplistic 'go-kart' like racing game with a few additional modes like rocket league. It handles well and feels fun to play. The more simplistic game play, controls, and the upgrade mechanics reminds me a lot of Ivan "Ironman" Stewart's Super Off Road (an old DOS racing game with similar upgrades and racing feel). That game was a lot of fun too.My only complaint really stems from how 'heavy' CPU cars are in the single player. It feels like you're driving a cardboard box and have no weight while they're cinder blocks and smash you around like a rag doll. Some tracks like the country one in reverse is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because you get little to no time to get ahead before they smash you into last place. However - once you manage to get away from them, races become much easier as you aren't being thrown around everywhere.Still a pretty fun game anyways.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: This is an update of Mini Motor Racing Evo which adds VR support (which I will ignore as I don't have one) that adds a few tracks, and changes the cars balance a bit - now Formula and Prototype are much better than all the rest as far as I can tell due to the issue of "light" cars going over bumps (and even objects like tumbleweeds) flying in the air and being unable to turn effectively in maps like Ruins is far less conspicious, so you can just stick to them and win every map once you have levelled one or the other up.The extra maps look unique enough, but aren't especially interesting, so didn't add a whole lot. There is also a new X mode which causes everyone to get an extra (semi)-random item each lap completed, unfortunately this means if you are ahead you mostly get spanners (which can hit yourself after a while, but can be deflected off walls to try to hit following cars) and missiles (which fire forwards only), while the last two spots often get whirlwinds to hammer everyone else ahead with (and if you are first it homes in on you so you can't even dodge it). This is fine when playing multiplayer to keep things competitive but I would suggest avoiding it for the solo career as it is just annoying to try to win with getting hit once or twice every lap.Overall this is a decent enough refresh of the game even ignoring the VR element, especially if gained as a free upgrade from the previous version, that is less annoying than (particularly the physics of) the predecessor, but with less balance in the cars because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: A nearly perfect arcade racer and a remake that more than exceeds the original. I received the game free because I bought the original Mini Motor Racing Evo but I would have happily paid for it. This is arcade racing as it should be.It's a game that combines many classic elements of Super Cars, Super Sprint, Micro Machines, Skidmarks and Ivan Ironman Stewart's Super Off Road Racer but also allows you to race in first person and third person camera views as well as the classic top down view.PROS+ Lots of cute cartoony cars to choose from (Chibified Countach, Testarossa, GT40, Beetle & F1 cars are my favourites)+ Cars can be upgraded+ 26 tracks with day/night/forward/reverse variants+ Most tracks are great or excellent (Downtown, Grand Prix, Docks and Cliffs are perfect)+ Can be played quickly or for hours on end+ Feels really fast on upgraded cars especially when you Nitro+ A minimum of 20 Hours to complete all the championships (I would guess)+ Custom control options+ Music is great (and I say this as someone who usually mutes game music)CONS- Uneven difficulty scaling crops up occasionally- An upgrade system that will have you wasting 10% of your cash to respec into a car suitable for certain specifically annoying tracks (looking at you Countryside, Outback & Alpine)- Some grinding may be necessary to upgrade cars to be competitive (although Speedway is a great track to do this if you need to)- Does not have the track designer from Evo which is a damn shameNEUTRAL~ Adds an inferior optional Rocket League clone~ Adds a optional combat racing X mode that brings little to the game (perhaps fun in local multiplayer)~ Not all cars are useful, although perhaps if you want to limit a great player in multiplayer they may have some utility~ It adds VR so if you're Scrooge McDuck with a swimming pool full of cash, lucky you I guess?All in all I enjoyed playing this game 99% of the time. If you pick the Big Rig or Hot Rod early on and the Sports or Tourer for later races you should be fine, I learned this the hard way. Oh and don't forget to enable AUTO ACCELERATE! More games should have that option.Highly Recommended if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and entertaining game. It reminds me of those browser games I would play on  back in the day. It can get a bit repetitive at times but overall it's pretty fun. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Can't speak to the new VR mode, but the non-VR mode is just as much of a blast as the original game (Mini Motor Racing EVO) was. If you're looking for a fun arcade racer, and are willing to overlook some flaws, then this game is for you.Unfortunately there are several issues (some that carry over from the original and are still very glaring):For all its faults, the game still shines in a lot of areas. The tracks are memorable with a (generally) great and thematic soundtrack, and the core gameplay is fun enough to overlook the negatives. The game is still fresh, so hopefully it will see some love in the form of balancing (and crossing my fingers that the TF2/Portal licensing will be renewed, we'll see).(Haven't gotten around to the power-up "X" mode yet, but I will update the review when I do.)

_childDocuments_.review: [This review is from using the Valve Index]First off, despite my low hour count on Steam I have played this game for about 100 hours on mobile. I love the series and I thought why not give it a try in VR.I was BLOWN AWAY. This game has better menus and controls than most AAA VR titles. The interactive menus and booping buttons is incredibly satisfying, if you have a headset I would seriously consider giving this a try.I play a lot of Dirt in VR so I was excited that this had a first person mode. It's a bit of a vomet comet, HOWEVER, there are an insane amount of settings you can tweak to make it just right for you. On top of the amazing controls, there's a ton of content. If you end up liking this game, there's probably 50+ hours of content, and I mean that in all seriousness. It looks like a mobile meh, but I swear it's actually a mega masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Great little arcade racer, but doesn't take long to get through the championships. _childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed the Mini Motor series on iOS and Android, so when I saw it for VR, I got it as a fanboy, hoping to relive the experience but in a bigger format. After an hour (what was supposed to be a 10 minute test), I found myself grabbing my daughter and saying "look at this.... it is so cool!"The main career of this game is a series of small tracks, designed to be viewed from above (like RC racing). The multiple types of controls, teleport ability, and room scale view of the track give the classic game brand new life. But then, you can flip right into the cockpit of the car, grab the wheel, and experience the tracks from a truly new perspective.If you get motion sick, the cockpit view will be much more intense than the classic view. By default the developers help a lot with mesh on the windows and a little tunnel effect on high-speed turns. In the configuration, you can adjust the effects to your liking. However, I love the cockpit view: Suddenly, cute elements like the hippo become life-size surprising elements! Meanwhile the arcade drifting and handling feel very intuitive to me.Only one complaint: Could you please add a control sequence to reset the VR camera center?  If I accidentally slouch as a level loads, I find myself virtually smacking my head or putting the console out of reach. The VR camera center is reset if you restart a level, but a simple control sequence or menu option would be so much more convenient.[Quick update after my second 1 hour session: Whew... the behind the car view is great but gives me the sweats (the first sign I'm experiencing VR motion sickness). However, it's a great view because you can appreciate the art of the tracks yet have the ability to line up the tangents (especially with the steering wheel control).]
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Mini Motor X fixes all of the gripes I had with it's predecessor. Proper multiplayer, party game modes, new camera modes, and most interestingly, VR support. The best part is this game just showed up in my library, presumably because I have the previous entry. The only negative thing I could say about Mini Motor X is the removal of the track creator. But that is a small annoyance when the tracks created by the developers are so colorful and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Mini Motor Racing X

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! This is exactly the VR racer I've been waiting for! Well worth the current $20 price if you have VR.It's like RC Pro Am on NES, Rock'n'Roll Racing on SNES and Genesis, or BlazeRush (which only has VR on the Oculus store).Pros:+ Lots of tracks+ Lots of upgradable cars+ 1st or 3rd person VR or pancake+ Touch or gamepad controls+ Many ways to view the track, including a hot air balloon or blimpCons:- no key remapping* would be nice to have native wheel (G920/G29) support.* make sure you launch the game with touch controllers turned off if you want to use a gamepad.* works great on the Rift* shows Index controllers regardless* a wider variety of weapons in X mode would be nice

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to try to keep my disappointment and downright outrage at this cheap cash grab to a reasonable level, but that's going to be very tough to do.Pros:*Graphics*Accuracy of replica tracks*New compound is beautiful*SoundtrackCons:*Bike sounds*Compound lacking content*Physics are awful*AI is psychotic asf*Not enough new content/innovation for a passing gradeConclusion: this game is literally just Milestone delivering on their yearly game contract with FELD Motorsports. Milestone, i think, doesn't care about the series anymore, just their payday via the contract and people purchasing the game. They've never listened to our criticisms, such as tough blocks being an insta-crash, the track editor not allowing us to turn modules around, none of it. They don't care what we want, never have. This game is literally MESX3 with worse physics, a worse compound, worse AI and the same track editor. This game might be great for those new to the motorcycle genre, but for us vets this is torturous. Milestone doesn't deserve a penny for copy-pasting the same game a year later once again.

_childDocuments_.review: i like to clear things up and give an accurate review for the game in its current state. a lot of reviews are stating that the AI is to aggressive and the physics are terrible. i can confirm that the AI is no more aggressive then the AI of previous games in the franchise. the physics are different but not bad. the key to this game is you have to go slow to go fast. if you race on the track with the throttle at 100 percent all the time you are going to crash, not hit rhythms correctly, and be all over the place. there are parts of the tracks where you are going to have to break hard or in some cases just coast threw with your foot off the gas.  after you get used to the track you'll be able to go threw it perfectly most of the time. the bike does feel heavy when you first start the career. this is because you have base components on your bike instead of factory components. i recommend you select the real thing so you race the qualifying, heat, and main because this is the fastest way to earn credit to upgrade your bike. once you completely upgrade your bike you will be able to hit ever jump in the game perfectly. the second thing i recommend once you fully upgrade your bike is to complete the skill tree in career mode completely. this will make it easier to control the bike, this will be really useful if you are having a hard time with the physics of the game. make sure to check your journal in the my rider tab to see what challenges you need to complete to get more skill point to complete your skill tree as quick as possible. if you have any questions fell free to comment them and i will try to answer them to the best of my ability
