_childDocuments_.review: This thing is a mess. Not only are the devs incredibly lazy but also have absolutely no clue about the sport.You'd think that for a game that is mostly a direct copy paste from it's predecessor it would have the same features. Nope. For some unknown reason they removed the feature to copy the size and angle of the numbers on the side panels. Maybe they took the time to fix some silly little details from the last game? Also nope. The heat races are still set during the day, this has been a recurring thing since the first game and I don't understand how something so small can be glaringly left in the game for 4 years. They use a stock stadiums sounds pack as you can hear periodically between the crown noise a voice over on a loudspeaker saying "The ruling is incomplete on the field".Why is there a hockey buzzer both when the race time expires and the gate drops?This is the 4th game in as many years that the dev team has demonstrated a complete lack of knowledge or willingness to research basic aspects of a sport for a game that they want you to pay top dollar for.This is all apart from the physics and actual gameplay that you can read about from the other reviews.Do not waste your money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like getting restarted unexpectedly when you're in the middle of the track going under the tunnel? Do you enjoy when your rider pretends your bike is a skateboard and grinds endlessly (and uncontrollably) across a row of haybales, only to throw you off once you've reached the end? Do you  landing on peoples heads only to kind of "float along" on on top of them - just long enough to lose momentum and not be able to make the next set of obstacles? Then this game is for you!If you love things like:Then you're in for an .They missed the mark () with this iteration of the game. The physics are nothing short of trashcan worthy, with the bikes being unpredictable, which makes the rhythm sections being difficult to get consistent on. You can hit the same line two, three, four laps in a row - each time you'll get a slightly different reaction out of the bike. Sometimes you'll get thrown across the track, sometimes your momentum will be sapped on the jump face, sometimes your backend will kick unpredictably like you've hit some invisible lip.Back to those amazing haybales! To add a layer of fun complexity to the game, they decided to make it so you never know what to expect when landing on one! Sometimes, you'll skate across it, sometimes it will throw you off your bike like you hit a bomb. It's the excitement of never know how it will react that really  to this game! In the lead? Don't worry, you might tap a haybale which won't move, but  take you down!  This is a fair question. Well, for starters, you can land on them, ride into them, ride beside them, they will ride into you (and travel across the track to do so) and so much more! If you get too close to them? You're not making the upcoming rhythm section. Forget it. Meanwhile, about 8 of the AI riders will hit all the lines with ease! Passing you by, maybe floating on your head, who knows. It's pure excitement!It is what it is - not a good game. It seems like the idea of good gameplay was an afterthought. Who remembers "Supercross" for the PS1 ()? In that game, you could at least not clear one particular part of a rhythm and get going again. That is impossible in this game.If you screw up on a rhythm section? Unless you want to come to a complete start and downshift to first so you can  clear the next obstacle and double the rest of the way through... you're hosed. The AI will pass you for sure (or catch up if you're leading) - heck, your grandmother might even roll by on her electric wheelchair. You're riding 250 or a 450cc motorcycle - but if you screw up even a little, somehow that big powerful bike can't seem to manage to produce enough power to get 'back into a rhythm'. That is something you see all the time in real life - but yet in the game? The idea of different rhythms is . It's as if they designed this game around  - you either ride that line or suck forever.All joking aside? I think it's criminal how much they're charging for such a poor, poor game. I personally think they should be embarrassed to put out such a low quality game with so many bugs and unacceptable glitchy mannerisms. Thankfully I don't hear them pushing it much on the live broadcasts - and I can see why. The game is bad. If you get it for free? Okay, play it. If you get it for less than $10? Probably worth it if you really want  to play because you're bored out of your mind and you  hate yourself.If you're a reasonable person, looking for a good Supercross game that allows you to choose your own lines, craft a character you enjoy playing, has decent physics that make playing the game fun and exciting - this is not it. This game is not for you.If you want a game that is laughably terrible, but has names of riders you know? This game is still not for you. It's . I wouldn't be surprised if this was the last game of this franchise, because it's clear no one even cared to play the game they were making. No tests were done, no quality assurance. They just said "eh, some redneck sucker who drinks Monster will buy it - release it."Now if you'll excuse me, I have to go check on my grandmothers wheelchair and see what kinda tires she's running to get laptimes so low.

_childDocuments_.review: considering i got about 144 hours into this game,i have to say its a pretty good game but its got its flaws,such as the saving mechanic,i lost about 300 to 400 levels and more than 10+ million credits and about 5 to 7 championships due to the game glitching out my save and making me restart my entire game like its the first day i bought it,its pretty easy to get money and levels but after losing 144 hours of game time and the fact i haven't even touched multiplayer yet it becomes quite repetitive and i lose interest pretty quick,this is a good game if you wanna just pick it up and play for a bit then move on and play another game with your friends,besides the bugs its got a great bike and player movement,the seat bounce mechanic is amazing for hitting those tough lines that can make you at least a second faster on the track,i wish they would make the A.I a bit harder,i play on realistic A.I with advanced physics i seem to lap them about every race,and it would be really nice if they made it to where your bike has a chance to buck on the whoops to add more intensity to the game,but overall its a really well made game,nice tracks,amazing lines to hit,even the 2 strokes are fun to whip around,i'm not very fond of the compound track tho,it feels bland and dry compared to the compound we got in mesx 3,you can even install mods to give the riders 2021 gear,let you put factory graphics on your bikes and let you wear custom helmets as well,all of this is my opinion but for the full aspect of the game you'd have to try it out yourself,this is my first time ever leaving a review on a game so i hope it wasn't bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded this game within 45 minutes. Really wanted to enjoy it, and maybe with more time I would, but it feels like such a downgrade from previous games on so many fronts. Physics feel heavy and more challenging, but not nearly as fun or rewarding when you get it right, which is a bit counter intuitive. The graphics and sound are significantly worse than MESX2 in my opinion (They even re-used the same announcer sound assets from 2 years ago!). The career progression system is the same as always, just re-skinned into a skill tree system. The AI seem a bit faster than before, but they ride like you aren't even there and will push you around and ruin your lines, which is more frustrating than it is immersive. All in all the game just feels a bit lazy and not really worth the 50$.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is awesome!!! I've always been a fan of the milestone Supercross series! I've played and mastered all of them. The reason people are complaining about the game is because they probably don't realize that unless you do the training exercises and build your character stats the game will be really hard. _childDocuments_.review: Milestone is back at it again with their yearly release of another Supercross videogame. This year’s 2021 Supercross release is Monster Energy Supercross – The Official Videogame 4. The game has a few new features and upgraded visuals from its last release. Hopefully, it has high hopes to keep a Multiplayer player base with a couple of new takes on their Race Director & Free Roaming modes that will allow players to be free on organizing their own tournaments and allow players to play with friends outside of a timed lap based system. We’ve been asking to keep the pace to ensure the game can keep an online player base, and it looks like they listened to us; we’ll try it out.Other upcoming Milestone releases include MotoGP 21 (Apr 22, 2021 Release, and Hot Wheels Unleased (Sep 30, 2021 Release). All three of these upcoming games hope to put Milestone back on track for online play with other gamers who want to go fast and compete for a career on the tracks.After talking with the developers over at Milestone about their upcoming release of Monster Energy Supercross – The Official Videogame 4, it was great to hear that new features and a new system are in place to ensure things go up from here. We’ll breakdown what they have in store for us supercross and MotoGP fans.Breaking down the release of Supercross 4, there are improved physics that will allow the player to have assistance or go off on their own on a more realistic adventure that has been enhanced a bit from the last game release. In contrast, in the air, to the physics of terrain deformation while in the water or the fields that may not affect paly much while running over it after a race, but it goes down in the record that supercross 4 has more water physics than cyberpunk 2077. While the new features and cosmetics are near perfect for unlocking new things for the riders character and the career path is on its way to near-perfect to keep the player involved, the lack of a free-roam camera while racing instead of using different keys to look left, right, and behind would be a step in the right direction. And a rider stability upgrade that will keep your rider from flying off their bike when turning a little too hard or when barely grazing a tree/rock would be an excellent thing to see also.The new Milestone release of Supercross 4 is one of the best supercross games out there that gives the most realistic feel when the settings are right. The game has enough for a variety of skills and maps before even trying out any of the community releases. With a career path in view for USD 44.95 on release day, Monster Energy Supercross – The Official Videogame 4 is a must-buy if you’re into Supercross and enjoy the releases Milestone sends out. And with a final score of 9/10 for the game’s supercross realistic abilities, I can’t imagine what’s in store for the community with the upcoming game Season and future updates.You may find my full review of the game here:

_childDocuments_.review: Every Milestone Supercross has always suffered from two issues - the first is the format of Supercross is badly suited to a video game.  The second is the AI is so putifully, incredibly, staggeringly, mind-blowingly, shockingly GODAWFUL that the games are unplayable.Don't be fooled into thinking that all Milestone bike games are poor.  They aren't.  The MXGP games are always superb, and if you like dirt bike racing the MXGP games will not disappoint.  The problem with Supercross as a format, as opposed to MXGP, is that Supercross is a format that is finicky and technical, astonishingly physically demanding in real life (hence hard to reproduce with a gamepad), and has few long straights making natural pauses in a lap difficult to find.  F1 drivers users long straights to rest.  There is no such pause in a Supercross circuit.  Constant concentration is needed, which makes the skill of finding a rhythm in the laps much harder, so less enjoayable.This spoils the action and makes it more difficult and frustrating than MXGP games.  Milestone can do nothing about this - they don't make the rules or design the circuits for Supercross so they can't be blamed for the format.  Nonetheless, gamers will find it a lot less fun than the MXGP games.The other issue is entirely Milestones fault.  Here it is:The AI is shocking.The AI is awful.The AI is atrocious.The AI is woeful.The AI is shabbily, grottily, unerringly, shamefully appalling.There is no excuse for this.  Apparently Milestone hire out a specialist company for the AI.   Without a shadow of a doubt, Supercross has some of the worst AI I have ever experienced in a modern game.  It is so bad I'm sure someone, somewhere is writing a dissertation on 'how no to implement AI in computer games.'Words fail me.  I cannot describe how bad the AI is.  The AI is just so, so, so, so bad.  I cannot begin to explain how godawful bad it is.If you are thinking of buying this game, please don't.  Not until they fix the AI.  Just don't encourage them.

_childDocuments_.review: The best Supercross game yet. Definitely the best mechanics that milestone has had yet in any other their MX games. The only thing that i think still needs a little work on to make it feel and be more realistic is the whoops. In real life you dont just wheelie through the whoops ever single time being the fastest way in the game to get through them, so for realism it needs to be back and front wheel touch on each and every whoop and if you miss one, then your either going down or you get offset. Thats the main improvement that i think needs to be done but other than that, there's only minor improvements other than that, like the dirt itself and ruts being more of a game aspect instead of being able to just blow strait over them. It should be as the races go on the track deteriorates, which it does to an extent, but there needs to be more rut racing and balancing in ruts as you lock yourself in one and cross rutting for mistakes. I know that's more into the future for the amount of tech that needs to go into those mechanics but that's the ultimate realistic mechanics that still needs to be incorporated to get away from the arcade feel. i know Milestone is trying to appeal to everyone in racing games but if your using Monster energy fim supercross name, i think it needs to as close to the real thing as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend? Yes and no.Got MEXS4 after seeing now nice the 1st person cam was. One of the better first person cams out there for mx racing games. As usual milestone has done a great job with the visuals and sounds. Bike control with manual shifting and independent brakes always feels nice. That  said the game is not without its flaws. - The AI is faster, but just still terrible. Same goat trail, locked on their line, run you high, land on you and ride on like nothing happened bullsh1t I've experienced in all milestone games I've played. At times it doesn't seem like they play by the same physics.- The physics are questionable at times. Does the game even have a working gas gyro? Or a clutch? The whipping and scrubs still aren't there and often look quite awkward. Getting even a hair off rhythm will most likely have you ending up singling half a straight. Then there is the wheelie glitch...why is this a thing?-Is it just me or is rider lean is largely not animated?The UI could use some work. Things like the exit button and rider customization button are buried and not immediately easy to find. Then there are the odd glitches I've personally experienced so far like your riders hands disappearing and reappearing mid race when in 1st person view. Crossing the line in 1st - being in 1st on the track but having your position tumble down the race order to last cuz the game thought you cut the track somewhere but didn't bother to reset you.All in all I'm neutral on my position to recommend this game. Fun game despite it's flaws. I'm sure new comers to the series will enjoy the game-play and immersion. However,  ff you have all of milestones other games, I'm not sure this brings enough to the table to pay full price. It looks and feels great in 1st person...which was what I got the game for but the physics engine and animations especially could still use some tweaks to improve the feel of the bike.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. Going from SX3 to this doesn't feel like a downgrade like my people are saying. Physics feel better to me, the bike moves around more, sand feels better (thicker) and the tracks are all fantastic and feel great. Obviously the riders are going to be out of date with today as it's based on the 2020 season! The compound this year isn't great, not much to do there and the compound tracks aren't good this year either. They all feel too tight and small. Almost like they were an after thought. Although with COVID undoubtedly effecting this game I can live with it. The compound does looks good and is fun to explore but only for 5 minutes or so... The Career mode this year is much better. You feel like you're riding with a purpose this time which is nice. The addition of futures is good but feels more like a tutorial to be honest. The skill tree is a nice addition but it quite basic, however it is needed if you want to get faster as without it your rider is sluggish and well.. just not as good as if you were riding as a pro. AI are better than last year as well but still could be quicker. People saying they're aggressive are correct but personally I think it's a good amount of aggression. SX isn't a walk in park! There's likely tonnes I've missed but I wanted to give this game a good review as personally it was worth the wait and i'm having a blast playing it!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not entirely sure what to think. Sometimes the game is fun, other times I feel like I'm smashing my head against the wall. I generally don't leave reviews on games, but this one warranted it. And yes I know "They have to crank out a game every year per the contract blah blah blah".  Don't care, if you're a good enough company to sign up for a game delivery every year, you better have the quality control to make sure its good on release.Bad First: -The physics feel... super out of control. All tracks feel like mud tracks, you can land entirely on your side and not crash, and other times you land perfect and you just get skyrocketed off. I kinda of like the out of control feeling on certain tracks because you can ride super unconventionally and have good lines, but most often its garbage. Along with this you basically can never recover if you mess up a section, thats mostly realistic I guess, but I've seen guys seat bounce a whole triple after crashing in the corner before. Wheres the torque and clutch dumping in this? -Your character also just randomly pulls tear offs, you're blitzing a whoop section and he just pulls a tear off? Pulls a tear off the moment you case a triple. Yeah cause that's the best spot to have one hand on the bars.-The AI is AWFUL. Yes I get it, most AI isnt great but there's literally no thought from the AI. They are either just running into you at all times or they are just skyrocketing across the track. I'm not talking about a nice block pass with a little contact. I'm talking straight ram into you any possible chance. Usually wrecking your line which is nearly impossible to regain so you drop back like 20 positions because all the AI is ridiculously fast regardless of their lines.-Helmet cam mode feels like my helmet cam is attached to my gas tank lid. 70% of the screen is your handlebars. I like helmet cam mode because it feels better to play for me than 3rd person. When I play 3rd person I just get frustrated on how wonky and stiff it all looks. ride just sitting straight up all the time, robotic whips and scrubs. -These whip challenge events? The worst thing ever. You barely touch your joystick in a race and it counts as a whip, but ohhhh no, not in the challenges. You gotta do a friggin barrel roll for it to count in the challenges, and they give you jumps that are like 2ft high to do it. God forbid you get big jumps to execute your 900 degree roll for it to count as a whip. stupid. And if you get frustrated and wanna quit the event? too bad, no option to. You gotta ride out the time just failing over and over again in order to get back into the career page. Yeah yeah you can say "Just get better at it" all you want. Still not fun.-I wouldnt say its "bad" but the whole skill tree just seems kinda useless. I havent really noticed any significant riding improvement as you gain more in the tree. Really cool concept but seems to have fallen short.-Injuries seem random. You literally win a race by a landslide with no crashes and all the sudden you get a prompt thats like "you're injured, pay all this money or you'll perform worse". How? I just won that race and didn't crash... -There's no real incentive to win other than to win. What I mean is, you win like 2 races in the futures class and you have basically enough money to buy all the performance parts that actually do anything to the bike. After that you're just kinda swimming in money and there's no real effort to collect anything for unlocking parts to improve performance. Unless you just wanna buy everything to have it I guess.Positives:-The graphics are pretty good and they did a good job capturing a lot of the details on the bikes, tracks and gear. Its a very pretty game.-Just some of the refinement on the sounds and looks and feel of supercross. The buzzer for two laps left, the addition of winning gestures, some of the immersion stuff is pretty cool and doesn't feel as dry as previous games.-Some of the career mode options are cool, like being able to reach out to sponsors who aren't listed in your offers and ask for a ride. That's a pretty cool concept. The training stuff is pretty-Even though this was also in my negatives, I'll put the skill tree here as a positive. I think with some refinement in future patches this could be a really cool incentive to do the side "training" and offer up some unique advantages in the gameplay.-The tracks look nice and are a bit more scaled correctly. They are still in no way to scale realistically, but definitely better than SX3/2.-Although the physics feel out of control 90% of the time, what I like is the turning in this game. In SX3 it felt like if you pushed a corner too hard you'd just fall over and crash, this game it seems like you can be much more aggressive in the turns without that weird MX Superfly ice track feeling in the turns.I definitely feel more comfortable playing SX3, but then I have 100's of hours in it, maybe in a couple weeks I wont have as many complaints and I'll edit this, but for now, save your $49.99. I'm sure there's gonna be some patch that addresses a lot of the community complaints.Also, I really do wish one of these days the games would start your career on superminis though. That would be cooler than some joe just showing up to supercross and racing a stock bike. Maybe follow the whole thing of needing a certain amount of pro points to move up classes etc. Versus just completing the seasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my detailed review of the game. They need to go back to simple lists.3) The same stupid quirks still exist. Rather than typing in your dirtbike number, you have to select a range of numbers, then you scroll down and use the left/right arrows to navigate to your number. WTF.4) Physics might've gotten worse. It seems less realistic than before. The developers are unfortunately NOT motocross racers nor do they seem to watch/analyze motocross footage and apply that to their games.5) The graphics have not improved, the grind is still very real, and the same things you hated about the last 3 games are still alive in this game too.Now let's talk about the good things.And that concludes this review. Keep in mind that there are still several wonky issues with this game that I didn't mention but in order to hopefully save some people some money and headache, I'll let you know right now that it's another copy/paste.

_childDocuments_.review: UpdateI've played a few more hours and my opinion has slightly changed. I still say wait, but it's alright.The handling feels....ok. Some parts are really nice, like the sand sections. And you have to work harder to be precise. You cannot skim jumps anymore. While that is nice, sometimes it feels like you are penalized too much for being a little off. When coming up slightly short on a small landing I lose a little speed at times, and then other times I lose all speed and have to roll a lane. I could understand casing it, or a bigger landing, but I don't get it at times.The AI are insane. Not quite MX vs ATV has a beacon on you and will jump over a lane to hit you insane, but they bulldoze you frequently. And sometimes they don't seem to play by the same rules. There are huge jumps I've seen the AI pull from the inside that I struggle to hit from further out. Also, the train still exists. I wish the separation that exists in real life was in the game.I still don't like the career mode leveling. It would be nice to earn respect. Maybe have the AI race you a little harder when you're starting, but then only top guys race you hard as you level up. But the whole limiting your abilities is annoying. You're left wondering if the game sucks or just your rider. It's a poor execution and it feels like I'm being punished. And the new injury mode feels like a credit grab. "You're injured. Pay 10,000 credits to heal". Why? I don't recall my rider going down in the last race or any big hits.Overall, I give it a solid meh.Original:I feel like a rock going off jumps. The AI pushes you off the track. The rider feels disconnected from the bike in first person. Racing games that make your character trash and require leveling up are not fun to me. Consequently rider feels like he does whatever he wants in career mode. Neat premise working your way up, but terrible execution. I would recommend waiting until a sale if you really want it. This series latest effort is disappointing. And not that this one is a surprise since it's always the case, it would be nice to have an up to date season for once.

detailed_description: Discord Channel About the Game Red Barrels invites you to experience mind-numbing terror, this time with friends. Whether you go through the trials alone or in teams, if you survive long enough and complete the therapy, Murkoff will happily let you leave… but will you be the same? SYNOPSIS Set in the era of the Cold War, human guinea pigs are involuntarily recruited by the good folks at the Murkoff Corporation to test advanced methods of brainwashing and mind control. In a world of distrust, fear, and violence, your morals will be challenged, your endurance tested, and your sanity crushed. All in the name of progress, science, and profit. SURVIVE: SOLO OR COOP You’re all prisoners of Murkoff trapped inside their facility. You can choose to complete the trials by yourself or you can tackle them in a team of 2, 3, or 4 players. Coop is never forced when it comes to mandatory objectives but working together can be highly beneficial. Whatever the number of players in your party, it’s about surviving and getting out. Ultimately, your goal is to complete Murkoff's therapy and earn the right to be released back into society. In order to do so, you must complete the Trials and the MK-Challenges. Trials are immersive story driven therapies that take a certain time to complete. Mk-Challenges are shorter therapies occurring in modified or redesigned section of an existing map. HIDE OR FLIGHT In pure Outlast fashion, the core gameplay involves avoiding enemies, hiding from them, and trying to run away. Murkoff will provide tools you can use to increase your stealth capabilities, create opportunities to flee, slow down enemies, and more. However, you will have to earn those tools and work hard to improve them. The tools will allow you to Stun enemies Blind them See through walls Heal yourself and people around you. Murkoff will ask you to perform disturbing tasks in each trials or mk-challenges. Only after completing those, will you be allowed to exit the Trials or the MK-Challenges. CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION Customize and create your own trial patient. Your cell is your home while you complete the therapy, you can decorate it however you wish. Choose your tools, upgrades, and perks to fit your playstyle. Meet the Denizens of Murkoff’s Sinyala Facility in The Outlast Trials. Each one of them will try and help you get through the Trials in one piece! Think you’ll make it? INVESTIGATE You’ve been abducted by the Murkoff Corporation to undergo unethical experiments that will modify your psyche and behavior throughout the Trials. Collect documents and items that will help prove Murkoff’s malpractice against its patients. The Process: Break the Self: Murkoff aims to break down the test subject’s fundamental beliefs. Aspects of self-identity are systematically attacked. Like boot camp or indoctrination, the goal is to force a person to purge themselves of anything held sacred or taboo, the things that limit their behavior. The constant assault on identity, guilt and self-betrayal eventually leads to them breaking down. Build the Self: It’s a bad cop, good cop principle. The rejection of the old ideology leaves a vacuum into which the new ideology can be introduced. As the antithesis of the old ideology, it forms a perfect attraction point as the person flees the old in search of a contrasting replacement. This progress is accelerated as the new ideology is portrayed as harmonious and ideally suited to the person's needs. Collegiality and calm replaces pain and punishment. Just at the point when the person is fearing annihilation of the self, they are offered a small kindness, a brief respite from the assault on their identity. Salvation: Faced with the stark contrast of the pain of the past with the rosy glow of the future that the new ideology presents, the person sheds any the final allegiance to the old ideology, confessing any remaining deep secrets, and takes on the full mantle of the new ideology. This often feels, and has been described by many, as a form of rebirth. It may be accompanied by rites of passage as the person is accepted and cemented into the new order. The rituals will typically include strong statements made by the person about accepting the new ideology fully and completely, swearing allegiance to its leaders. Saluting flags, kissing other artefacts and other symbolic acts, all solemnly performed, all anchor them firmly in the new ground. Content and Photosensitivity Warning: The Outlast Trials contain strobing and flashing lights that could cause a small percentage of people to experience seizures when exposed to certain lights, patterns, or images. This game also contains intense violence, gore, graphic sexual content, and strong language. Please enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much to say about this literal masterpiece of a nightmare. Whether you've played the original single-player Outlast games before this or not is irrelevant. Outlast Trials stands above every horror game in the genre. The team at Red Barrels takes the coop horror experience everyone knows and brings it to the highest levels possible in terms of pure adrenaline-inducing horror, excellent animations & attention to the worlds detail, along with masterful audio that I swear will have you screaming wherever you play this.  So what do you do in this game? You are a patient (taken against your will) to essentially an MK-Ultra style mind control facility where the powers that be force you to undergo "Trials" that are meant to harden you and make you stronger in the face of pure horror & this game has so much of it. Each trial is a different location that has been turned into a grotesque extreme vision of whatever is being portrayed. Your job once inside is to do what Murkoff tells you & then get the hell out. Or die trying. Each character or enemy you encounter is intensely scary and satirical depending on who you get (I'm looking at you Coyle) with what I think is some of the best voice acting in the industry along with truly scary enemies physically as well.Nothing is scarier after running room to room and being sliced up with everything wanting to hurt you in some way and you finally find a moment of "safety" hiding in a barrel or bathroom stall and you hear Mother Gooseberry's singing muffled on the other side of the wall getting closer to you. Or hearing your friends screams over the radio as you hear them get brutally assaulted by "the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ man" as he chases them attacking the whole time. This game really is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. But in the best ways.If you want a truly horrific coop experience that looks so damn good you'll wonder why other games in the genre aren't even close, with sounds that are so realistic you'll be holding your breath to not miss what's coming around the corner, enemies that are so completely terrifying you'll literally be screaming running for your in-game life like it's real life, with levels that immerse you in every way so much so you'll think you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ smell it as the lighting, sound, darkness, and all of the wonderfully done set pieces and assets blend together into what I swear is an experience you have to see to understand. It is the scariest game I have ever played and in the genre it's the best there is. Are there some negatives to note? Yes. Quickly I'll say this game is the best to play with a friend or several (4 in total). Having your friends there, or even matchmaking while dealing with all this game throws at you is the most intense juggling act, and keeping everyone alive is so not easy. So if you're someone who solos games alone, although I believe you'll still have an amazing time it will not be easy and you'll come out of it like someone who was lost in the woods for 10 years trying to escape. Are there bugs? Some, but it's been less than 5 in the 60 hours I have played. Some were graphical and I think we had audio issues maybe once. I know some people might complain there's a lack of variety in the levels but dig this: there are I think 5 main levels currently (with the 6th coming in a month) but the replayability comes with the fact that they take those 5 maps and when they add new trials they'll reconfigure these maps and change them in totally different ways, sometimes unrecognizable with new enemies, different layouts, different objectives and for me the content has not ever lacked.Some stuff I didn't touch on that's still amazing about this game: The lobby where you choose your trial you get your own cell/room that can be customized with all sorts of awesome decorations/cosmetics from good looking to guts on the night stand (your choice) kinda like the Sims in Hell. All of the cosmetics are unlocked by playing the game. Each trial rewards you X amount of cash + rewards like clothing cosmetics which are great. In the same lobby you can also play mini-games like arm wrestling & speed chess (which happens to be like the best 3D chess game on the market for some reason?). I'm sure I missed plenty of good, and maybe even some bad but with this game coming out of early access soon it's already the most polished horror experience on the market next to something like RE: Biohazard but because this is a coop experience also based in reality I think this stands above that as well. It's so well done and I love everything Red Barrels has made here. Completely recommend this experience & I can't wait to play the Toy Factory level when the game goes out from early access which is soon. "The Goose is on the loose, the Goose is on the loose..."
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game that scratches an insane itch for a re-playable horror game.I find that Outlast:Trials really continues the dark, twisted world of the last two games - providing the player with plenty of gore, horror, and memorable sights that stick with you long after you're finished playing.The developers are brilliant, coming up with new content regularly, and having weekly changes to trails that add a different style of play every week. Making a "season" structure is something that they do, but it doesn't contain the usual pay-to-play/micro-transaction tactics of other developers - the season content has been promised to stay, even after moving on to the next season, and so you don't feel forced to play to make sure you don't miss anything - it makes it feel more relaxed in unlocking things through a season, and feels like you play because you want to - not because you're required to.I prefer playing most games single player, and this game doesn't disappoint for me. It has the difficulty dialled in greatly for single player, which was something I was worried about going into the game (I find being alone in a horror game scarier than online - the feeling of other players always takes away something for me). I put most of my hours in this game in single player, and although trails are substantially longer, they feel more immersive, and come with a much higher fear factor.The style of the trials are varied, and although it does follow a similar pattern per trial of sneaking around/hiding/problem solving, each play-through is varied enough that I haven't found it feeling too repetitive even though the maps are somewhat limited - with things changing out in each map per play-through for variety.I would recommend it to any horror fan who craves a gore-riddled game, full of jump scares, eerily good atmosphere, awesome realistic graphics, with an unheard of amount of replay-ability for a horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: It can be played by yourself or with up to three friends online. I highly recommend the latter. It is more action-oriented as there are more opportunities to fight back against the enemies you encounter, rather than simply running away. This makes the game more intense and exciting, but it also takes away some of the suspense and horror of the previous games.+ Fun and challenging multiplayer horror game+ Addictive arm wrestle + chess simulator+ Unique gruesome level design+ Great graphics and sound design+ More action-oriented than previous Outlast games- Long waiting periods w/ unskippable cutscenes inbetween trials- Some minor QoL issues can be frustrating at times- Not as suspenseful as previous Outlast gamesThe long loading times  each trial are a major downside, breaking up the flow of the game while making it feel slow and sluggish. I hope that Red Barrels can adjust this issue in a future update. That aside, I would recommend  to fans of horror games who are looking for a quick, fun and challenging multiplayer experience. It is a good addition to the Outlast franchise, but it does not quite live up to the high standards set by its predecessors. Yet.

_childDocuments_.review: As a dedicated fan of the Outlast series since its inception, I've truly enjoyed the depth and replay value the games offer. The Outlast Trials, in particular, has shown great potential with its engaging levels and thrilling gameplay. However, there are a few areas that feel repetitive and could benefit from some enhancements.Repetition and Variety:While the introduction of a new killer was a refreshing change, the game can feel repetitive with the same enemies—Coyle and Mother Goose—appearing in every level. Adding more variety in the antagonists would keep the gameplay exciting and unpredictable. It would be amazing to see a wider array of killers, each with unique mechanics and storylines.Endless Mode:Endless Mode has the potential to be a standout feature, but currently, it feels too similar to the main levels, just without the return to the sleep room. Introducing new and unique challenges in Endless Mode would enhance its appeal. Perhaps bringing back iconic locations like Mount Massive Asylum and classic enemies such as Chris Walker could inject fresh excitement into the mode. While this might deviate from the established lore, it would certainly boost the fun factor.Challenges:The challenges in the game could use more diversity. Many of them feel like recycled versions of existing levels. Adding a variety of new and interesting challenges, possibly with unique objectives and scenarios, would keep players engaged and motivated to replay the game.Main Levels:The main levels are well-designed and enjoyable, but there's always room for improvement. Adding more intricate details, expanding the lore, and providing clearer explanations would enhance the overall experience. Players love discovering hidden secrets and uncovering deeper narratives, so emphasizing these aspects could elevate the game to new heights.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun Solo or with friends. Love the art style and atmosphere and love the variety with each trial. Each enemy has a set behavior that can be learned and avoided. Pick ups and objectives are random so each individual trial never plays the same. Character customization is vast with a ton to unlock for your character or safe room. Meaningful upgrades that make traversing trials easier but not a cakewalk. Will continue to play for the foreseeable future as I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game provides the most accurate combination between stealth-horror genre and cooperative gaming, which therefore may be an optimal point of contact between both hardcore and competitive gamers. The maps' design is user-friendly, the complexity of tasks increases in proportion to player's skill development, and small every-level rewards such as talent points and customization items effectively maintain player motivation up to the very end. The plot, in turn, has become quite compressed and has acquired the appearance of the dictionary with lore notes. Nevertheless, the location and character design, scene staging and voice acting remain of tremendous quality and astonishing esteem for players. This is only enhanced once again by superb optimization and eye-pleasing graphics that don't overwhelm the computer's processing power. This kick-ass combination of details is transformed into an addictive gameplay that will keep you entertained for more than a dozen hours. That's why I highly recommend to try out this game even without friends, considering most of the playerbase is talkative and friendly. WP, Red Barrels!

_childDocuments_.review: does everything right and near-perfectly in a survival horror game.There is permanent progression through level-ups, skill and customization unlocks, which incentivises players to continue playing long after they've completed the final stage.Regular content updates such as new challenges, trials, maps and monsters encourage players to return often to experience something new.Players are weak, but not defenceless. Bricks, bottles and Rigs let players buy precious time to avoid enemies or slow them down. This rewards a more aggressive play-style compared to most horror games which rely too heavily on stealth. Due to offensive items, matches don't need to be unnecessarily prolonged and waste time.Mini-games let players occupy time while waiting for groups to form, players to join and trials to start. They also have ranking systems that give a sense of accomplishment, so players can treat these side activities just as seriously as the main game itself.Customization for characters and their cells give players the chance to display their visual flair and personality without the need for words. Want to show that you're a wannabe serial killer? Dress in the skin of your victims and display their body parts in your blood-drenched room. There are hundreds of individual items to unlock and buy and more are frequently added.Players can choose how accessible or immersive they want their game to be played. Show or hide all HUDs and indicators, or choose from a mix. You can feel more in control or feel more helpless depending on how much info you are willing to see on your HUD.Enemy designs are creative and each enemy character has a distinct personality, from the small grunts to the large ones and the prime assets which are the ultimate villains, each the centerpiece of their particular program. When enemies grab, beat, choke and toss you around, the first-person perspective puts you into the action and you feel absolute terror and fear.Sounds in the game are eerie, especially when you hear distant screams and nearby mumbling from unknown sources. Is it simply your imagination, or are there enemies lurking close by where you can't see them? The senseless ranting and menacing monologues by the enemies tell you there is no reasoning with them- you must flee or die. Every movement and motion has an impact, because sound is also crucial to the gameplay and scoring.The visuals are incredible. Everything is visceral and realistic, to the point where the player feels truly immersed in each location. The bloody set pieces and makeshift infrastructure show much attention to detail and every prop is well-placed and tells a small story in the overall setting. Spend time appreciating how objects are placed, why they are placed there, and you can see how each prop fits into the lore of each program perfectly. From the scratched writing on the wall, to how the mannequins are violated and posed, the player can almost perceive the madness of the world from the antagonists' minds.A well-optimized game that runs at consistent and high frame-rates even on lower-end PCs at maxed settings. Lots of settings to configure graphics, interfaces, volume and regional servers. Server disconnections or interruptions are as rare as to be almost non-existent, and I've only been disconnected twice- that was on launch day itself.A must-play game for all fans of survival horror, whether you intend to play solo or with others.

_childDocuments_.review: Outlasts Trials is a masterpiece that breathes new life into horror games. Developed by Red Barrels, this game invites players to an immersive experience with its adrenaline-filled moments and dark atmosphere. It's a chilling synthesis of horror and the fight for survival that will have you gasping for every breath.Visually, Outlasts Trials is stunning with its realistic graphics and detailed environments. Claustrophobic locations, labyrinthine corridors and dark rooms with dim lighting are perfectly designed to immerse players in a world of tension. As the atmosphere envelops you, your heart will race with every step and you'll eagerly anticipate what's around the next corner.One of the game's greatest strengths is its storytelling. You find yourself waking up in an experimental facility where you are a group of what you think of as test subjects, caught in the middle of the horrific experiments taking place. As one of the test subjects, mysteriously in danger of dying, you embark on a fight for survival. Your character's challenging backstory, combined with a deeply explorable story world, makes the game even more compelling.Outlasts Trials doesn't just rely on horror elements, but also tests players' intelligence. You'll need to use your strategic thinking to solve mysteries, sneak your way through and escape dangers. You have to be careful not to fall into cleverly placed traps and make the right decisions at the right time. As you face these challenges, it's almost impossible to describe the feeling the game gives you. Excitement and fear spread like fire through your veins, while at the same time you feel a sense of charisma that brings out your charisma.As much as the horror elements of Outlasts Trials, you can't forget about the charismatic characters. The game introduces a whole new icon of horror: sneaky and dark enemies. These characters create constant tension, with eyes watching you and dangers lurking in the background. Each one has a unique personality and a design that fits perfectly with the atmosphere of the game. You can have an in-depth experience by interacting not only with the characters you encounter, but also with the other subjects.All in all, Outlasts Trials is a breath of fresh air in the world of horror games. It's an immersive experience that will make horror fans' hearts race, take their breath away and keep them up at night. With its tense atmosphere, cleverly designed enemies and deep storyline, it's an unmissable opportunity for horror fans. However, be prepared for this experience, because Outlasts Trials will drag you into a real nightmare and offer an unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best survival horror cooperative game on the market. Outlast Trials is unlike any other horror multiplayer game you'll find. Outlast Trials provides a unique experience that equips you with items that you can heal yourself, cure yourself, pick up fallen friends, as well as defend yourself and strategise your next move. Admittedly, playing with friends yields the best experience for this game.The content is challenging, action-filled, with just the right amount of tension to earn and keep its place as a horror game. The objectives and puzzles are best achieved with a group who knows how to cooperate well. Since their previous updates, there are now daily and weekly tasks you can work through to earn additional rewards and a sense of progress beyond levelling, prescription and rig progression.I cannot recommend this game highly enough. If you love survival horror, and if you especially love cooperative horror games. You're certain to enjoy Outlast Trials.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is the pinnacle of what Outlast is. Every game in the series has always had their charms. This game is a very fun co-op game which can be quite scary at times. Although it looks and plays nothing like the original games in the series, it is worthy of The Outlast Trial. Different Variations of enemies Ranging from Giant Brutes, Main Themed Enemies, The Skinner man, enemies that drug you, and even Enemies that disguise themselves as other players to trick you.It has a very saw-like feel to the series with the Trials being the "Games" from saw. There is traps you need to avoid, Classes you can use to enhance your gameplay experience, being able to stun enemies, heal others, and much more. The Upgrade points that allow you to upgrade your class and also your character itself is insanely well done, The game is well balanced with barely ANY lag. Some enemies do stutter, and I only once did I have some issues with Server Syncing where I rubber banded and such. The fact the game can be played without others allows you to experience levels in multiple different ways.I was skeptical when they announced this as a Co-op game, but I think they actually nailed Co-op Survival Horror. What I appreciated about this game more than other Co-op games is that there is no microtranscations to buy more In-game currency for Cosmetics for your Character or your Room, and that makes me respect Red Barrels way more.The Gore has been upped MASSIVELY, and it adds to the world a lot more. I would say this is my favourite Outlast game of all time. -My only issues with the game right now is Stamina feels too short, I always find myself running out of Stamina way too quickly. And also the fact that Hiding mostly never works on enemies, even if they don't see me enter a hiding spot. Out of the 9 Hours I have played so far, only 1 Hiding Spot has worked for me. All in All, I do recommend this game to anyone who loves horror! It is a fun experience with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The arm wrestling game is simple yet effective. Players must time their button presses to exert force on their opponent's arm. The goal is to push their opponent's arm past a certain point before they can do the same to you. It's a classic game of strength The sudden shift from a terrifying asylum to a friendly game of arm wrestling provides a welcome break from the tension.The game adds a layer of competition to the overall experience. Players can try to beat their best times or challenge friends to see who is the strongest.The arm wrestling can also be used to develop the characters. It can reveal hidden strengths or weaknesses, and it can even serve as a bonding experience between teammates.The arm wrestling mini-game is the main focus of Outlast Trials, it's a well-executed addition that adds depth and variety to the gameplay. It's a fun and engaging distraction that helps to break up the horror.

_childDocuments_.review: The truly absurd and wonderful thing about O'Trials is how far Red Barrels is willing to go to shock the player. Every new trial that comes out, I always say to myself - "There's absolutely no way they'll be able to outdo themselves in this one." Every time I am proven wrong with extreme prejudice. I thought sawing a crucified man's legs off in the Orphanage was the worst it was going to get. Then I thought hanging a woman and crushing her head in the Courthouse was the worst it was going to get. Well, in the Toy Factory you cover a man in hot wax, bolt fake tits onto his chest, and... ok, I don't want to spoil it.Literally the only bad thing about this game is that the small size of the dev team means we have to wait a while for updates. It's an absolute masterclass in horror with an addictive gameplay loop. Co-op is fun and chaotic, solo play is immersive and tense. Atmosphere and music are stellar. Game is exquisitely optimized whilst still looking fantastic. Voice acting is phenomenal.This is a reminder you can sprint with the snitch cart.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is an adrenaline-fueled roller coaster ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. This latest installment in the Outlast series takes the horror genre to new heights, delivering an unforgettable experience that will leave you gasping for breath. While the game might have given me multiple gruesome deaths (including one that involved 10,000 volts to the nipples), it only added to the exhilaration and excitement of the gameplay.First and foremost, the atmosphere in Outlast Trials is masterfully crafted. The hauntingly detailed environments, combined with the eerie sound design, create an immersive world that truly feels alive with terror. From the flickering lights in the abandoned asylum to the bloodcurdling screams echoing through the halls, every moment is filled with an intense sense of dread that grips you tightly.The gameplay mechanics in Outlast Trials are equally impressive. The stealth-based approach forces you to tiptoe through the shadows, desperately avoiding the clutches of your deranged pursuers. The tension builds with each step, and the constant fear of being discovered adds a layer of urgency and suspense. The game's variety of puzzles and challenges keeps you constantly engaged, while the cleverly designed levels provide ample opportunities for both strategizing and sheer survival instinct.The graphics in Outlast Trials are stunning, showcasing the grotesque and macabre nature of the game's world. The grotesque imagery, while disturbing, is a testament to the game's commitment to delivering an authentic horror experience. The attention to detail in character design and environmental elements adds an extra layer of immersion, making every encounter feel all the more real.Despite the many gruesome deaths I encountered, including the infamous 10,000-volt nipple incident, the game always managed to draw me back in. The shock value of these moments, while intense, serves as a reminder of the high stakes and unforgiving nature of the game. Each death only fueled my determination to survive and push through the challenges ahead.The Outlast Trials also shines in its narrative. The story is well-crafted, with intriguing plot twists and well-developed characters that add depth to the overall experience. The game's immersive storytelling keeps you invested throughout, and the sense of mystery and suspense will keep you guessing until the very end.In conclusion, the Outlast Trials is a truly unforgettable horror experience that pushes the boundaries of the genre. Despite the many gruesome deaths I endured, the game's atmosphere, gameplay mechanics, graphics, and narrative all come together to create an intense and rewarding adventure. If you have a taste for heart-pounding terror and a strong stomach, I highly recommend diving into the twisted world of Outlast Trials and testing your survival skills against its horrors. Just be prepared to face some shocking moments along the way!

Yes, your team will drastically change the experience from smooth game to the worst possible struggle based on how good everyone is ^^So far though there is at least 3 programs ( big maps ) and 4 scenarios at least I think for each of them so if we take what I said about each staying 100% fresh for 2-3 runs and then get a bit more repetitive or familiar due to the same objectives or map layouts :That is still around 18 hours of fresh content Outlast Trials offers currently and there will be more maps and scenarios available!If you enjoy stealth / puzzles and perfecting your runs and games - this will offer many many hours above that especially that there is a PROGRESSION SYSTEM available to level up with and 4 different classes to maximize and try out their unique tools.

_childDocuments_.review: [Early Access Review]40 hours and 1 reagent released. This has been a fantastic experience from start to finish! Incredibly well polished for an early access title, The Outlast Trials is a wonderful new take on the Outlast formula and expands it further by including online co-op. The core gameplay loop is genuinely enjoyable and challenging. My only minor issues were with enemy detection being a little too sensitive, a bug that caused my and my friends characters to fall out of the map (only happened once so far tho) and the Deadly Prime Asset variation being a bit too punishing. _childDocuments_.review: At its heart, Outlast Trials can be compared to an intense, and deadly game of capture the flag.  You (and up to 3 friends) are dropped into a special zone patrolled by murderers and general wackos alike, told to make your way deep into enemy territory to achieve one main goal, and get back out alive.  While this main idea is easy to grasp, the execution of said goal requires a lot of running, a lot of basic survival tactics, and a strong stomach.  Like the other games in the Outlast series, this game does not pull any punches when it comes to gore, nudity, and general human suffering.  You will even be committing several atrocities of your own in order to make progress.  And this is all in the name of "rehabilitation."  This game definitely earns its age rating.What I liked:1. Levels are crazily detailed, but severely grotesque.  The lighting is awesome at times and even runs well at 1440 on my mid-tier rig.2. While the main objectives are identical for every session, the locations of important key items and traps are randomized.3. The game also automatically adjusts the number of objectives and the number of "crazies" that spawn in at a time based upon the number of players in the session.  The more players you have with you, the more chaotic the game becomes.  I actually found the game to be more challenging with 4 players than I did with just 1 or 2.4. Some of the challenge modes actually cordon off the main areas and force you into areas you could only see through windows in the main mode.  This brings a nice change of pace.5. If you sit and listen long enough, the bad guys all have some clever dialog and dark humor about them.  Most of them have very DISTINCTIVE personalities from each other.6. The netcode seemed to holdup pretty well overall.  I did not try the matchmaking, but the friends only lobby options worked just fine.  No one ever dropped unwillingly out of a session, and the lag was fairly minimal.7. Largely stable early access builds.  I've only encountered one bug out of the 35+ hours I've sunk into it so far, and that issue was easily circumnavigated (Tab/Escape menu wouldn't appear, which prevented me from reaching the program's exit button).What I disliked:1. It's late June at time of writing, and at this stage in the game's development, access to the final "mission", as well as the game's bonus "timed event mission," is gated behind completing the other three missions on the hardest difficulty level.  While technically doable, it's a VERY frustrating price of admission.  This is made all the worse by...2. ...there currently being only 3 maps available at the time of launch.  While this is typical of early access games, it's a bummer to have so few maps available when the existing content is this much fun.  I simply want more of it.  Please keep it coming!3. The screamers.  Good lord, the screamers are terrible on the hardest difficulty level.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: if you can justify the price on a short (less than 10 hrs) but extremely well polished experience, buy this game. If you're looking for extensive amounts of unique content that will keep you entertained for dozens of hours, avoid the game for now.It's a good game, extremely polished, runs well, no technical issues - it feels like what triple A games should be. The gameplay itself though is just 'decent'. Every mission is basically following a todo list of go to a location, grab an object, etc. The tasks vary, but always feel the same and get repetitive quickly. However, this can be excused due to the joy of playing a horror game with friends, which makes the whole experience a lot more fun. I am torn on whether to recommend it though. For the price, there is so little content available - with effectively only 3 unique missions and every other being a modified version (or even the exact same just more enemies). I almost feel bad pointing it out because the content that is available is incredibly well polished, but the truth is that the gameplay becomes repetitive and you don't get many hours of fun out of it. Personally I have had fun playing the game, mostly because of the co-op, and not having to deal with the BS that so many other "triple A" games include is a breath of fresh air - but it's kinda sad that it's got to this point.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is not just a game; it's a full-blown descent into madness, and it’s one of the most intense survival horror experiences you can find on Steam. Red Barrels has successfully evolved the Outlast formula, introducing multiplayer mechanics while maintaining the terror the series is known for. Here’s why this game is a must-play:The game throws you into the clutches of the Murkoff Corporation, forcing you to endure brutal trials in a grim simulation of psychological and physical torment. The gameplay masterfully combines stealth, puzzle-solving, and resource management. You’re not a fighter—you’re prey, relying on quick thinking and stealth to survive.The addition of co-op is a game-changer. You can team up with friends (or strangers) to face the trials together, but don’t think this will make the game less terrifying. Coordination is key, but the game still isolates you at times, ensuring the dread never leaves. If you prefer solo play, you’re in for a grueling challenge that feels more personal and intimate, though just as rewarding.The environments are incredibly detailed, with dim lighting, blood-soaked walls, and grotesque set pieces that make every step feel dangerous. The game excels in creating a claustrophobic atmosphere that keeps you on edge.The sound design deserves special praise. The muffled screams of other test subjects, the echoing footsteps of a chasing enemy, and the distant clanging of doors closing all serve to keep you immersed in the nightmare. Play with headphones if you want the full effect—and prepare to jump out of your seat.The enemies in The Outlast Trials are some of the most grotesque and fearsome in gaming. Each one has a unique design and behavior, forcing you to adapt your strategies on the fly. They’re not just monsters—they’re symbols of Murkoff’s cruelty, adding depth to the game’s already disturbing narrative.Multiplayer adds a new dynamic to the series. Working with others to complete objectives is thrilling, but it doesn’t lessen the tension. You’ll find yourself torn between sticking together for safety and splitting up to complete tasks faster—a decision that can lead to either salvation or disaster.The social aspect, including emotes and basic communication options, brings a slight sense of relief amidst the chaos. However, don’t expect comfort for long—the game is still relentlessly brutal.The game includes a progression system where you can unlock upgrades and perks, such as being able to heal faster or make less noise. This adds a layer of strategy and rewards multiple playthroughs. Cosmetic customization is a nice touch, letting you create a character that stands out in this horrifying world.The trials themselves vary in objectives and intensity, ensuring no two runs feel the same. With multiple difficulty levels and plenty of optional content, there’s plenty of replayability.The Outlast Trials is a triumph of survival horror, offering a fresh take on the genre with its cooperative gameplay while staying true to its terrifying roots. It’s polished, challenging, and unforgettable. Whether you’re a solo player or enjoy teaming up with friends, this game is a must-have for any horror fan.Pros:✅ Bone-chilling atmosphere and sound design✅ Innovative co-op mechanics that maintain the fear factor✅ Memorable enemies and intense gameplay✅ High replay value with progression and customizationCons:❌ Solo mode can feel overwhelming for less experienced players❌ Occasional balancing issues in multiplayerFinal Rating: ★★★★½ (4.5/5)If you’re ready to face your fears and endure Murkoff’s twisted experiments, The Outlast Trials is waiting for you. Just remember: survive together, or die alone._________________________________________

_childDocuments_.review: Below you'll find sections of the game that are the Premise, Level Design, Enemies, Graphics and Performance.Summary at the bottom for those who don't want to read the details and want to see the cons.This game's premise is simple, but effective and fun. It's entirely PVE with players having no way to defend themselves past their rigs, throwable bottles and bricks, hiding and running. You have your Rigs that act like abilities, Amps which act like secondary abilities you pick and choose from up to 3 at one time and help you fit into a specific playstyle and Prescriptions which are your permanent, passive improvements on your character's abilities. Such as breaking down locked/barricaded doors with 2 hits, instead of 3. Or having more stamina. The controls are smooth and responsive and you have the ability to slide, climb up to head-level objects, vault over waist-high objects, hide in numerous hiding spots and do co-op assisted climbs and gap jumps to take safe shortcuts. There is a selection of 4 rigs which majorly affect a player's approach to the levels.You need to complete a series of objectives in each level and reach extraction at the end. Player performance is individually graded based on a system that combines penalties from mistakes and bonuses from utilizing the items scattered around the levels, playing with your team or actions that are positive/useful. With higher grades, you accumulate more XP to level up, unlocking more Amps and tokens for prescriptions/rig upgrades/amps. A+ gives a big bonus to the cash rewards you get from trial completions and those are only used for cosmetic purchases. There is  in the game in any capacity. You buy the game itself and nothing more.The level design in this game is impeccable. Each Trial Environment (at the time of this review, there are 4) is very expansive and dense, with a unique theme and interesting Outlast-style twists on real-life locations you would see. The space is utilized very well, with many rooms intersecting each other. The layouts of the trials all make sense according to the buildings that they represent and their purpose. They're complex and interesting to explore, but may be confusing to some people initially. Along with the main Trials, you have MK-Challenges which are shorter, smaller levels with unique objectives and they revisit the same environment from the main Trials, but unlock different areas that you can't access in the main Trials and lock some others, essentially making a completely new layout. Some of those new areas in the MK-Challenges intersect with the main Trial's areas, too.While they are NOT procedurally generated (more on that below), they have a lot of randomization in them between sessions with some doors being locked or barricaded. Hiding spots being obstructed. Trap placements are never the same. Some objectives have different locations they can be at and are randomized each time. With the inclusion of variators which tweak different aspects of the levels, some doorways and windows can be entirely blocked off and that can really change the trials because you'll need to adapt to the layout on the go. The variators also affect a lot of aspects of the game. Enemy count, damage and aggression. Trap placements. Less/no item pickups in the level and many others.The levels are not procedurally generated and though that might mean it's not as replayable as a game with entirely random levels, it means that each level is VERY detailed. Every single room has attention to detail that is unmatched in other multiplayer games. Props fill the room with detail without it being nonsensical. Blood smears, bodies, writing on the walls and other decals add even more detail and tell a story. The texture work is also very, very good. When you look at the screenshots in Steam, it's exactly what you see in-game. There's very good environmental storytelling within each Trial and MK-Challenge. While the objectives will be the same and the general path would end up being similar to other playthroughs, the levels still retain replayability to a very respectable degree. The environments in this game are nothing short of perfect.They're made with love and care, without exaggeration.The enemies in this game are classic Outlast. Very aggressive and hostile enemies with unique, grotesque designs with a degree of real life plausibility.You have the Prime Assets, which are the main enemy and most dangerous enemy in the Trial. They are lore-important. They have distinct personalities which are very memorable.You have the Ex-Pops, which compose of the Normal Grunts, Big Grunts, Pusher, Screamer, Pouncer, Night Hunter, Berserker and Imposters. All of those enemies have their own unique weaknesses, strengths or strategies to deal with them. Their AI, however, is kind of primitive. They chase you in a straight line with no special movement over what the player can do like vault and climb and such. But still very solid with their pathfinding. Their animations are all motion captured and they are extremely lively, with animations like searching locked containers and quietly opening doors, closing them and even locking them sometimes. Their voice acting is very good, with Prime Assets being very charismatic and each variant of the Normal and Big Grunts having their own voicelines and mini personalities.The game is gorgeous and it runs just as good as it looks.The lighting in this game is the best I've ever seen with very fine and tasteful volumetric effects, shading and the night vision in the dark rooms looks gorgeous. The game's settings are very scalable to the player's performance needs and it includes DLSS and Ray Tracing for the reflections. But even without Ray Tracing, the screen space reflections in the game are very solid. For people that absolutely despise TAA, the developers have tweaked it so there is no blurriness or ghosting. If you're really low-spec, you can edit the Engine.ini file to disable even more things for performance gains, without being punished. No anti-cheat means the game runs easy and such modifications will not land you a ban.Even thought it's an UE4 game on DX12, the game pre-compiles shaders when you load into the main menu, so there should be no lag spikes or stuttering in the gameplay, unless you're really under the specs.The game is a very fun, very unique co-op experience that is very rewarding when played right with others. It has an interesting story, great visuals, great performance, very interesting music and a dedication to quality over quantity.I think it's worth the asking price. It's definitely worth it to try it. If you don't have friends that want to try it with you, the Discord is full of very friendly people who are welcoming and helpful. It FEELS like a community, not just other players.However! Red Barrels is a small studio composed of 50 people at the time of this review. Very competent developers, but the small studio size does mean that major updates take longer to complete, with a major update gap being around 4-5 months. This is still an indie game, even though the polish of it is something you'd expect from a AAA studio. The updates add very good, polished content and the team is not going to stop updates anytime soon. But if you're a person that gets bored easily, you'll be waiting for new content significantly longer than other popular games. If there are bugs that need fixing, they are very quick to respond with hotfixes, so game stability is still good, even though content updates are slow. Also,  the current scope of the game, there are re-used mechanics. Like completing MK-Challenge objectives by doing the same minigame or interaction to unlock the objectives. And recurring gimmicks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential. The first few trials you play are genuniely terrifying, far scarier than previous games in the franchise, but unfortunately its just the same thing over and over again, and the game quickly loses its horror and just becomes annoying.  There are three trials you have to get through before you get to the big final one. Each of these trials have 5 missions. 3 of these 5 missions are the exact same but with some modifiers. The other 2 are called "MK Ultra Challenges". These give you new objectives to complete and are actually pretty fun. Now even though there are 3 programs, there are only two main enemies. One only shows up for the first program, the other shows up for the final two. Both of them get annoying real quickly. The same annoying lines repeated for verbatim, and in the case for a specific one, "Mother Gooseberry", her screams become absolutely infuriating and just begin to piss you off.So, you make your way through the game, completing each of these three programs. You'll likely go from being scared of the game to just being bored and annoyed, because you're just doing the same thing again and again except with some extra modifiers that just make these missions more tedious. After doing all of this, it is time for Program X.Program X is the big kahuna. 10 trials, each providing you with a release token upon completion. You need 10 of these tokens to finally leave and beat the game.  I haven't reached Program X personally yet, I am only one mission away, but I did play it a little bit, and it is the reason why I am just done with this game. Program X is just all of the crap you had been doing before recycled one final time. Thats it. Just the same old ♥♥♥♥ recycled and made even harder. This game needs a lot of work before it will be worth its price. This game should be a 10 or 15 dollar game, not 30. If you can get it when it's on sale, then by all means, do so. It is a whole lot of fun for the first few trials you play, especially if you have a friend, but sadly that fun will fade really quick, and all you'll have left is an annoying and boring slog.
