_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Amazing game, great fun, i recommend you buy it, the most enjoyable horror coop game i've played in a long while. My one note is that the xp system could be slightly better as it promotes one playstyle - sneaking everywhere. Needs to implement a player kick from group system too :)  9/10 gameBefore I get to my very small complaint, I want to say the game is awesome, everything from the gameplay, sound design, the environments, moods just every single inch of this game is stunning. I will leave my original unedited complaint at the bottom.-Visually it's incredible and sometimes horrible to look at, graphically it's pretty flawless. The atmosphere is really heavy in a lot of places and the enemy design is so fitting for the world, everything from inside the trials and outside the environment really builds upon the world in an amazing way.-The game is in an amazing working state, I have had next to no issues with gameplay or the ai, only one minor incident with the Cop AI struggling with pathfinding around a door but it was funny you know? The gameplay loop it's self is engaging enough and i can see it being a formula that will allow for new maps and trials to come in the future which is really exciting.-I love how the customisation works, it's nice and simple and the way stuff unlocks is fun, you don't know what all the cosmetics are so just randomly getting them after trials is always enjoyable to see!-The sound and music in the game is super tense at points, with general atmospheric music as you explore the trials really adding a sense of dread and unease. On top of this the voicelines of the enemies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious sometimes, they're really well done and they add some quirks to the characters and bring them to life more. Every interactable object has a really satisfying sound to accompany it.-The Hub (Sleep Room) is really simple, not overcomplicated or anything and it is honestly perfect, it's really well designed. From the being able to see everyone's rooms, the 2 shops for upgrades, the arm wrestling table to pass some time quickly waiting for people and the design of the whole area, i couldn't imagine it being any other way.Now here is my unedited original complaint with the xp system.Games really fun, it's a good laugh to play with mates, however the levelling system is annoying and favours only one play-style. I am doing 75% of the objectives and taking enemy aggro away from friends which means i'm setting off traps and getting hit, so i'm walking out of every trial with a D- rank and my friends are B and above. I wouldn't be bothered about the grades as i'm having fun if it wasn't directly levelling me slower, my friends with less hours have now surpassed me in level and it's a quite annoying being punished for playing a certain way, a way that i find enjoyable and i'm contributing most of the workload, while my friends are crouching in corners.Update - i think a kick system is needed for the game as I was playing with 2 other friends and we got a random to join so we were a 4. We noticed halfway through the trial that this 4th was hiding in the main area, letting us do all the work, we assume so he can get a good grade. So we stopped doing objectives and have been sat in this game for about an hour and a half. none of us doing anything, we can't get him and this has gone on too long that we can't leave. So I am currently leaving for food and I'll see if he's left by the time we are back. Would be very nice to kick this person, so they aren't getting free +A grades for being a ♥♥♥♥. <3Update - He left, we won!

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5 hrs in on launch dayTHE GOOD: Graphics are lovely, game is totally playable solo, but a lot more enjoyable co-op. Took me around 47 mins to beat the first trial solo and maybe 15-20 with other players. Hosting/joining random lobbies is very easy and quick, I never waited more than 15 seconds to find a group of 3 other players to play with. The game incorporates a lot of cool puzzles for co-op play that makes sticking together rewarding. Everyone I played with was super friendly and constantly saving each other, dropping each other items when needed, distracting enemies, and reviving one another. There's a really good 'ping' system to alert other players of enemies and item pickups. Speaking of which, you can now pick up certain objects in your inventory of 4 slots, including healing items, lockpicks, throwable weapons, etc. You still can't kill any baddies in true Outlast fashion, but you can delay them long enough to escape. There's also a new 'backpack' system you bring into the trials with a refreshable consumable, some of them have distraction devices but I think everyone will stick to the healing one as a brick would do about the same as the others. Still lots of graphic violence and weiners everywhere, so I don't think anything got censored. There's a new store feature where you can buy things with the currency you receive from completing trials. I really like being able to change the cosmetics of your character, and the room customization is cool too, but I don't think anyone will ever have a reason to go to your room. After playing almost 9 hours I feel like I barely scratched the surface for what's on offer here so I'd say you're safe dropping the full $30.THE BAD: Long load times occasionally, got stuck in multiple infinite loading loops and had ALT+TAB out a few times to restart the game. Got booted out of like 2 games due to connection issues which can really suck as some of the Trials can take a LONG time. Lost many good men in some of the Trials I was in and it wasn't to Outlast goons. There's a quick communication's tab where you can say phrases like 'hello' 'danger' 'follow me' etc., but I think a cool store feature would be adding more lines you can swap out as the current options are pretty limiting. I'd love to be able to say things like 'GG (GT?), I'll distract them, run!' etc. I completed numerous Trials tonight but the only one that's marked as checked off is the first, not sure if that's a bug. The performance was pretty iffy on my end, but my PC is starting to show it's age (1070ti, i5) so that's to be expected. Some areas run buttery smooth but others are incredibly choppy, making some deaths feel cheap. There's a new sanity bar that fills up really quickly and when it hits its peak there is an invulnerable ghost that constantly spawns near you and drains your HP really quick...not too sure how I feel about that yet. No Steam achievements? Hopefully added in a patch soon.Overall I'd give it a 7-8 in the state it's in on launch. Really good for a PC launch in 2023 and has a lot of potential. With the grading system and stuff to buy with earnable currency I can definitely see this being more replayable than the previous titles. With some server fixes and patches I could see this being a 9-10/10.*edit at about 50 hours*So I've pretty much unlocked everything there is to unlock during early access, and I've had a lot of fun doing it. The gameplay loop is really solid and enjoyable enough to repeat, but I think there are some things that could bring this game from early access to masterpiece. A truly offline mode should be incorporated eventually, if it stays purely online then when the servers go down this game will be gone. I really wish there were a 2x multiplier for rewards or something similar for completing trials solo, it would incentivize players to try it a lot more. A steam workshop addition would add infinite replayability to this game. I hope more contraband and prescription upgrades becomes available in the future. Steam achievements are a necessity. Speedrun challenges for levels could add a whole new layer how levels are played. When you hit around lvl 30-40 currently you run out of new stuff to unlock, so some good ideas for new unlockables would be emotes, voice lines, shoes, songs for your room radio, etc. I'm still having a blast with the game but starting to hit a content wall at about 50 hours. Might take a break soon until the next big update. Great work Red Barrels!

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I had some initial concerns when starting The Outlast Trials. The game immediately throws you into an overwhelming and intense experience. After countless attempts to find reliable teammates in other games, I finally decided to give it a try with the one person who stuck around during my search. We were in the Final Exam for Project X, the ultimate level, and despite my lack of preparation, I had an incredible time until I eventually met my demise and failed the trial. (This was my first trial I experienced)Hoping to find some guidance or make new friends, I checked the Discord server, but unfortunately, I couldn't find any assistance from fellow newbies. Most players were already immersed in Project X and offered their support, but I wanted to experience the game organically, starting from the beginning and unlocking Project X once I had gained some upgrades and abilities. Through persistent use of voice chat and reaching out to as many people as possible, I managed to form a duo with someone who preferred using text chat as their means of communication. Later on, we found another player through the group finder, and within just two more games, we formed a solid team of four.Working together with new friends in this terrifying world was an absolute blast! As we communicated and familiarized ourselves with the maps, we progressed from Program 1 to Program X in just two days. The feeling of progression in this game is exhilarating and genuinely enjoyable. Unlocking a random outfit upon completing all of Project X adds a fun and unique element, as we all eagerly anticipated what the next person would get. This motivated us to not only finish our first release but also to be ready for the next one later that same evening.I've been searching for a game that emphasizes teamwork rather than relying solely on individual performance, and The Outlast Trials delivers exactly that. I now have a dedicated team that we regularly meet up with to play, and it's an amazing feeling. I'm eagerly looking forward to future updates and hoping for additional challenges or weekly variations in the maps. I'm excited and optimistic that this game will evolve into something the horror genre community can truly embrace and demand from their games.Whether you have friends to play with or not, The Outlast Trials is a must-play. When you start, I highly recommend investing in either Hide or Heal abilities and not bothering with x-ray. You'll be able to locate items and hear enemies just fine as long as your volume is turned up. Stay alert, be prepared, and most importantly, stay silent—Mother Goose is always listening.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is not a game that focuses on the story. It focuses on a scary Co-Op experience. There is a story though. Set in the era of the Cold War, you are a test subject, a victim of mind control and brainwashing, trying your best to survive the trials of the Murkoff Corporation, all in the name of science.If you have played the first and second Outlast games, don't expect this one to be as good story-wise. It's also a prequel to the first two games. If you are looking for a game with a good story, then this is not it.For a horror game, The Outlast Trials isn't particularly scary. Sure, you get spooked at times and can panic a bit, but it's nowhere near the same level of scariness and panic-inducing moments as the first two games. The surroundings consist of both bright and dark areas, but mostly bright areas, which is a shame, because it lowers the horror factor quite a bit.The gameplay is a lot of fun. You can play with up to 3 other players. If you choose to play with less than 4 players, or if you want to play by yourself, there are no bots to fill the empty slots. The fewer players, the harder the game. There are 3 therapy programs (levels of difficulty) that contain x number of Trials and MK-Challenges. A Trial is usually longer with more objectives, while an MK-Challenge only has one objective that can be completed quickly. In the first program, the maps have no Variators. Variators are introduced in the second program and are game difficulty modifiers that can adjust the gameplay through difficulty, restrictions, and some benefits for the player. For example, there can be more traps in the map, more and stronger enemies, etc. The Variators do not change though. You must complete all Trials and MK-Challenges in the first therapy program before you can move on to the next difficulty/program, and then complete all of the second program before unlocking the third. There are also a few weekly Trials every week, but those can be completed in an hour or two.For being a horror game with Co-Op, I think they have succeeded well with the Co-Op part and a bit less well with the horror part. It's a very fun game though. Very fun to take turns throwing bricks at the enemies to keep them stunned, while another teammate does the objective.After each Trial, you get an individual grade and a team grade on how well you and your team performed the task. The best grade is A+ and the worst is F. Higher grades equals more XP. The rating is determined by how many items you used to help your team, how much damage you received, how many soundtraps you avoided, etc. It’s not hard getting A+ when you get used to the game. When you level up or complete a Trial, you are also awarded Credits which you can use to buy cosmetics, and Vouchers which you can use to upgrade your Rig, Prescriptions (passive abilities) and Amps (player mechanic/equipment). Your Rig is basically an ultimate skill with a long cooldown, and there are 4 Rigs to choose from. You can switch between your different Rigs and Amps between Trials.My biggest problem with The Outlast Trials is the lack of content. There are far too few maps to play, and the maps don't vary much when you play them again, which makes the game repetitive and you get bored quickly. It's also easy to learn where the enemies spawn and how to counter them.It's not just that there are too few trials and challenges, but they can be very short as well. Some MK-Challenges can be completed in 2 minutes and Trials can be completed in around 20 minutes, depending on your team's knowledge of the game. There are many more MK-Challenges than Trials, so it’s pretty quick to complete all the programs.The game is not very difficult either, even on the hardest difficulty/program. The first program has 5 Trials and 10 MK-Challenges. The second program is basically the same, only with Variators. The third program has only 2 Trials and 4 MK-Challenges, which are also the same maps, only more difficult. I was surprised when I saw that there was so little content in the last program. We, a team of 4, completed all Trials and MK-Challenges in all programs on the first try. Once you know how the game works and play with other players that know the game, it's not very difficult, which makes it a bit boring in the long run.The Outlast Trials is a fun Co-Op game to play with your friends, even if it’s short. The game has a very good foundation, but it needs more content. It's still a game I recommend, and hopefully they will add much more content to the game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played all of the previous Outlast games (and by played, I mean I cowered under a blanket watching my husband play) I wasn't sure how well the game would translate to co-op. It's quickly become my favorite game this year. It's a game that rewards you for taking your time and planning your next move instead of rushing in and blowing through the objectives. The maps are so incredibly detailed and well done. The sound is phenomenal - the atmospheric sounds and the music are immersive. I appreciate that the voices of other players are affected by things like distance, psychosis, and being inside containers.  The game starts out reasonably challenging but progresses towards very difficult. Higher difficulties force you to come up with new strategies when you constantly have ex-pops prowling around your location. Once you get to that point though, you will have learned each enemy's behavior and quirks and you'll have figured out your load out.After almost 100 hours, most of the scare novelty has worn off but I do still scream occasionally when I'm unexpectedly pulled out of a locker or pounced on. The events have kept things interesting and give us a reason to run through trials again. We still haven't tackled ultra yet which I expect will make me cry all over again.   All in all, fantastic game from Red Barrels and I'd recommend to anyone who is a fan of horror games. Looking forward to seeing what else they create for us.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a lengthy review but I couldn't help myself!I played the beta back when it was available, and while we only had the first trial it was an absolute blast. Red Barrels really went all out with approaching Outlast from a multiplayer perspective and even with a full group of four players it is terrifying. I'm torn between absolutely loving the enemy designs and being utterly terrified of them, and they made sure to add all the small details that really bring these enemies to life unlike so many other horror games I've played in the past.Coyle checking the locker next to the one I'm hiding in, only to get visibly frustrated, leave the room and just when I thought it was safe I hear two light taps and he slowly opens the door behind me, or when Psycho (as I like to call him, gas mask guy) appears with his wonderfully maniacal laughter if you hit him twice with throwing objects he will go: "Alright alright you got me!" and scurry back to the 'spawn closet' instead of chasing you. Coyle obviously being aware that you are nearby but instead of searching he decides to take a smoke break while tapping on a glass door right next to your hiding spot. (This next one is during the beta) The big lumbering giant guy (I dont know what his name is) chasing us only for us to lose him between a hallway, rounding that hallway being chased by Coyle we spot him searching a tiny drawer for us and with all the commotion he gets startled and confused at how we got there, and then proceeds to join the chase.Its small moments like these that really bring to life these characters and you can see personalities within them that go further than just their voicelines and general demeanor. A really good example is with Psycho, who is very aware that he is playing this role of an 'enemy' in these trials, designed specifically to challenge the progress of the player. He clearly relishes in it, and when he comes onto the playing field so to speak he always opens with maniacal laughter. Its his time to shine and he is out there living it. Being that you get to know these enemies quite quickly throughout the typically long initial runs you gain this sense of cruel intimacy, you learn their patterns and behavior and you pick up on cues with how they behave, I mean Coyle can go on long rants about pistachios (yes, really.) and the bible and if hes into it enough you can sneak right past him without concern! While it is clear that the main 'big bads' of the enemy roster have a lot more work and detail put into them than some of the lesser knife or machete wielding enemies most if not all of them have little quirks or habits which, were probably so unnecessary for the developers to implement but in doing so, makes them feel so much more alive.You can really take advantage of the AI with the right tools, get out there experimenting! Same goes for any in world traps that have been placed, a good brick can fix most problems.I don't have the most insane pc rig, but its not super low end either, with a fairly aged 1060 6gb and an i7k processor (SSD + 16gb ram included) I managed to get a steady unwavering 60 fps (I only have 60hz monitors) on default graphics settings (which I believe is medium). For me these settings were comfortable enough that I did not need to change them, and somehow out of all games I actually need motion blur on or I get a headache, take that as you will.Small section but I really wanted to happily mention that I absolutely adore how they really gave every enemy true vision (as I'd like to call it). No weird can't-see-through-windows McGee here, standing in the light behind two layers of slightly frosted glass and you move an inch? They'll spot you, because you are still pretty visible, silhouette and all, even if they aren't entirely sure they still gotta check it out. Darkness is your friend in Outlast and playing between shadows and taking your time can help completely outsmart your opponent (as long as he isn't wearing his own pair of night-vision goggles...The map design is incredible, its very easy to get lost if you are panicked and they leave so many nooks and small passageways that you can escape to (or from, as enemies can follow depending on their size). Each of the 3 core Trials currently available all have their own stories, with 3 separate difficulties and two unique side-stories that you can also do. The replayability is strong in this regard. The 3 total separate 'stories' for each one also use different routes and might open or close areas you have and haven't been to, it really feels like a stage where they set it all up before hand real quick. I don't really want to spoil much about these and I've only played the initial difficulty of the three in the session I had before writing this review, perhaps I'll update it further as I put in more time.Back in the beta we didn't really get to modify much, and if we did I don't ever remember seeing it. However, the skill progression in Outlast Trials feels pretty solid, its a little weird having to spend a 'skill point' on being able to slide after sprinting, but as far as progression goes it does not feel out of place and comfortably scales the strength of your character with each unique unlock.As far as the 'classes' go, which are more so just tools, each one has their own upgrade path with some seemingly a little overpowered the further down the upgrade tree you go, however as I spent all of my points on the former skill tree section I have not experimented with any of the tools other than the one I chose as my first.From what I encountered? None, however I did run into a few janky movement issues but that could have been from the fact I was repeatedly cornered by a tall naked man in a bathroom stall (while in pure panic mode mind you).In the end if you are a fan of horror games, have been a previous fan of the last two Outlast games that Red Barrels released in the past or are simply looking for a unique experience you can't exactly find then I strongly recommend you give it a shot. It fits comfortably for solo play and really scales up the chaos with 3 more. The thirty dollar price tag feels reasonable for what content there is to offer and they will continue to add more Trials as development progresses. I've been on the bad end of previous early access title releases (where I've bought into EA on their release, which unfortunately would go sour), and despite my now innate uneasiness with trusting a lot of new EA titles I had genuine faith that Red Barrels would be able to deliver on a fun, engaging and outright terrifying new take on the Outlast formula, especially after getting a taste of it with the beta, and was more than happy to buy into whatever little ball of chaos this game is.I was about to give this some sort of #/10 but I've not played enough yet must play more so just yes for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I have managed to reach the end of content in just under 30 hours, that includes replaying some segments for no reason other than to get better at it. It is my estimation that you'll have seen everything in this game in under 4 to 6 hours minus the final mission and the rebirth cycle scenes. Between hour 6 and hour 30, you'll be replaying content you've seen before with different modifiers or you'll be playing the few challenge modes that the game offers, where you'll further explore the game's 3 core gameplay loops, namely; "Find Item, Bring to X", "Follow Wire" and "Find Keys." Any challenge mode may have any or all of these loops included, sprinkled with the Outlast horror that people are familiar with.It's interesting how this game is set up to replayed again and again, yet the trials lack replay value. Most importantly this is because there are no skip buttons, no quick replay options, and no significant differences in how you can approach the trial each time. It is good fun, but it's not as good as it could be. That's the caveat of Early Access players, I suppose. Regardless, one should expect the horror aspect to last no more than 2 to 4 hours. After that you'll have seen every enemy, jumpscare and trap the game has to throw at you. Once you're past the initial scare, which happens once you're familiar with what each audio cue means, the game mellows out to be an edgier Dead by Daylight, or Left for Dead without guns and zombies.It's not currently worth the price £25 tag, but it is fun. I hope we will see more trials soon to justify the game's cost. The Locker Hag will give you a rough reach-around for half that cost, and Mrs. Doubtfire will give you a lobotomy for free.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished The Outlast Trials a couple of hours ago and I can confidently say that this is one of the most fun online games I've played in a very long time. Quite innovative and fresh in every aspect. Considering I love Outlast 1 and 2 I was already quite familiar with the gameplay but I gotta say, the changes they made really made the gameplay fresh for me, too, which was a very welcome surprise. If I had to break it down and simplify it, the gameplay is essentially pretty much like Outlast 2, except you get to upgrade your character in every aspect. You get a rig, which is pretty much your power. You can get a stun grenade, x-ray, a mine and you can get a healing gas. All of those have their own "skill-tree" as I'd like to call it, even tho it's not really one. Each of those rigs you can upgrade to your liking with great benefits which genuinely help you in-game. Everytime you buy an upgrade you'll never feel like you just wasted your points. Then there's the normal skill tree. You can get general upgrades like more stamina etc. and it always feels good to upgrade your character. Later on, once you reach a certain level, you unlock amps. They basically give you a special passive power such as not making a sound when you walk through glass. Believe it or not, but that amp significantly made the game easier to play. Upgrades aside, I gotta mention the general gameplay. The gameplay is pretty much just run/ walk/ crouch around, find an object and then bring it to where you're supposed to. Sounds pretty boring right? Wrong. Even though this seems like it'd get tedious after a while, it really really does not. I've played the first map at least 10 times and I still enjoy playing on it. The gameplay loop is thankfully satisfying and fun enough to actually make you WANT to play another match, instead of feeling like quitting. The level system also greatly improves the quality of life of the game. Thankfully, the game got some RNG layouts, such as the secret room, which grants you a lot of goodies such as health increase, stamina increase etc. The rooms spawn is entirely RNG, from what I could tell, which is awesome considering you can't just run to the same room every match expecting you get OP stuff. Sadly, the RNG aspect is also kinda hurting the game in some aspects. For example: The enemy AI. Now I know that the enemy AI is not entirely RNG, which seems pretty obvious considering they immediately switch targets once a player starts to do the main objective. That is not bad per se, but it can and really does get annoying once you play a little solo. The overall game I think was structured to be played duo minimum, because some of the maps really are not as enjoyable solo as they are with friends. Doing the objective and therefore alerting countless enemies to your location can get very frustrating especially when they just decide to stick around and you gotta lead them away. The AI generally I don't think is something memorable. They're not really bad, but not really something that stands out, which is kinda sad really. I wish they decided to go for more memorable characters with smart and learning AI like in Alien Isolation. That I believe would've been a better step, but overall, the AI not being great doesn't take anything away from the game. Another thing that bothers me personally is that I always feel like all enemies know where you are. Whenever you decide to lead one enemy away, they never just start to look around in an area with no player, they just always stay in the proximity of a player and look for them there, even if you don't make a sound. I do realize that this is to make it more intense but after a while it can get really frustrating when you just wanna take in the atmosphere and try to look around. The Co-Op factor is easily the strongest aspect of the game. It's incredibly fun to look around with your friends or even randoms and hide and outsmart the enemy. Speaking of randoms, I've gotta mention that for some reason every random I've encountered so far was pretty great at the game. They always were very helpful and vocal, whether it was through the pinging system in the game or through the proximity chat. Those two aspects I'll talk about later however. When you play with your friends and you get attacked, your friend can save you from either getting incapacitated or even executed, which is really fun and feels satisfying, I love that aspect of the game. Overall it starts to really be obvious that this game was designed for multiplayer considering half the skills you can unlock are to save your friends in some shape or form. That is not a bad thing in my eyes, because this game was pretty much built around being multiplayer and being able to play it solo is just a bonus for all those who don't like to play with others. Proximity chat and the ping system are a MUST in this game. I genuinely believe that without those two aspects the game wouldn't be as fun as it is now. The proximity chat, if you decide to go with the open mic, is always fun to use. The only thing that I've noticed is that sometimes the things you say either arrive delayed or not at all? Partially the reason why I mention this is because as you stray away from your teammate, you obviously become quieter. After a certain distance you start to talk over a walkie-talkie. However, if you're next to them in a room you don't talk to them through the walkie-talkie, you talk to them normally, which can lead to very frustrating moments where your partner can't properly hear you 'cause you're very muffled. This rarely ever happens but I did want to mention it as it did get annoying at times. Now, if you're the quiet type and you don't really like talking, you can just use the in-game ping system. This is a great addition due to the nature of the game. You can ping objects and you can even straight up use voice commands. If you can't picture anything in your head right now think of the Left 4 Dead 1/2 vocals. They're exactly like that. Gameplay, AI and Co-Op aside, I obviously have to talk about the meat of the game. The story is very bare-bones, I'm pretty sure everybody knew that going into the game. However, I'd like to say that the atmosphere and the design of each level exceeds what they've done in the previous games. This game feels like the love child of a SAW game and an Outlast game. I can really dig that. You see all these fabricated locations and you can just feel that these places and houses were built by sick people to test you. When you walk around and look up you don't see the sky, you see that you are trapped in some warehouse. That realization when you walk around really hits. It feels very oppressing, scary and dark in the best way possible. I mean, think about it for a second. Think about the people who built these trials. That thought alone made the atmosphere of the game phenomenal in my eyes. The atmosphere in the game is awesome. It's not as scary as the first two, in fact, I personally don't think its very scary at all, but the level design is so good it really makes up for all of it. That being said, you do get scared. I can't begin to describe the amount of times I screamed when I decided to leave a room and suddenly run into some naked giant in the hallway. The game is scary at times! It just doesn't have scripted jumpscares, which I think was a good choice. I also quickly wanted to add that this game runs as smooth as butter. This game is really well optimized, you should give it a shot!Overall I'd say this game turned out really well. I'd give it a solid 8/10. Only things I'd love to see in the future would be new objectives on new maps. I'd love to see new maps with more traps too, and please not just with the regular door traps and such. Please give us actual traps reminiscant of SAW or something. Give us fun traps you gotta solve for the objective or you lose a finger or something, be creative!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly some of the most fun I've had from a multiplayer game in years. It's hard to describe the exact genre this fits in, but best try would be if Left 4 Dead and GTFO style "complete objectives to get through a level" mixed with more Dead by Daylight flair that it's only one big baddie (though depending on section, mini baddies enter too, there can be up to 5 I've seen at once). Take that gameplay then put the Outlast thematic on top of it. You have no means to fight back, but you can throw bricks/bottles, kick enemies off allies, etc. which is why the DBD reference.The game is over the top in it's horror thematic, like all Outlast's before, overly sexual, overly filled with gore, and no refrain from touching on religion. This isn't anything new for the game, but it can put some folks off if you're not ready for it.You can approach the trials solo or co-op, with 2, 3, or 4 players. The more players you add makes it easier and less scary (though there are location based voice comms and "fake" allies that can add some fun jumps if you aren't in a discord with friends.) The game is not balanced for solo at initial launch, it can be done, but it really becomes difficult. I'm not sure the higher difficulties are possible without at least one friend either. It's apparent at launch the balancing is made for multiplayer, though devs have stated they want it to be balanced for all sizes so that may be adjusted. The game is very easy to match make though, so no worries if you don't have a group. A con there though is that you can't select the level you queue into at this stage, only the party leader finally does, but if you get a group you stick with, you can completely multiple in a row as a party.This game is not as scary as previous Outlast titles. Period. It does have it's moments, even with 4 players, but it's not a jump scare game at all. It really plays into the strategy of a group, sneaking and hiding, and allies keeping enemies distracted while players complete tasks. And I feel like that's why it works for the Outlast series, they were never jump scare, they were "chase scare" - which this game still really gets at. It's a multiplayer strategy/chase game with hide mechanics and an Outlast skin if you really want to dumb it down. Also - I see a lot of "this game isn't scary at all" down votes... adjust your expectations to what you personally can handle as horror. I have a friend who had to refund because he couldn't get through the tutorial, but he doesn't do horror well at all. I can handle horror, though I do scare easily and find this game more thrilling than scary. I have had a few good jumps and really heart pounding chases though even with 4 allies. If you are a horror fanatic that is looking for the next scariest game and you're already desensitized to everything, this will feel very light horror to you. It is not Outlast 3, but it does connect to the story of the previous games quite well (and I imagine they'll keep building on that).All in all, the game is early access, but feels like a full launch. The AI of the enemies still needs a little love with a few bugs, it's early access of course with some kinks to iron out, but it's very well built out. There are only 3 "trials" but each has 3 difficulties and 2 smaller "variants" that change the layout and objectives - this culminates in a final trial if you complete all the most difficult of the 3 trials. There's a lot of room for replayability with character mods, customization, progression, etc. This is a game I'm pushing friends to get now as there's plenty to enjoy, and much much more to come from the sounds of the developers wishing to make this a a live service game they update, add to, and throw in subtle changes (and sometimes not so subtle).If you like multiplayer games and don't mind a little horror thematic, get this game. It's very, very, very good. If you are wanting to go in solo though like other Outlast titles, this may not be your fix. I still recommend though you try it and give the co-op a chance, you may find something you like to tide you over between now and Outlast 3. Or if you'd like to be masochistic, play solo 100% of this game, it's probably do-able, but don't expect it to be at all easy (as of launch, this may change with future updates because the devs have explicitly stated they want this to be able to be played solo.)This game has some serious potential and I'm already loving it. Wishlist it and keep an eye on it if you're uncertain, but if you get the game look forward to a good time with more to come.

Getting bashed and bloodied could be a little better, gory or more realistic, but I don't really mind because of how fun it is in the first few games. It's certainly got some similarities to regular outlast but its unique enough to not just be "Outlast multiplayer." However, because there is generally a lot more running and chasing than the other games you might get used to the natural jump scares quite easily, at least if you are playing with others it doesn't feel as scary. Certainly immersive solo but not that easy if you are not great with spacial awareness. Would recommend if you like phasmophobia but need a little more going on, or if you kind of like dead by daylight but aren't too into the pvp aspect. Would not recommend if you are looking to fight or just don't have friends. Surprisingly If you don't scare easily it might also not be for you, unless you like figuring out and doing easy tasks under pressure. However those tasks are really trivial so far... While its not super easy to solo the first few times, its not so difficult and as such also might not have as much replay-ability as dead by daylight.After some more play:Hmm... the content can be addicting, but I do hope we get more prime assets and theme mix ups soon. Otherwise features they've mentioned in the survey sound really cool. That might not be so much an issue if you don't play all that much. Another thing I've noticed is they really put a lot of attention to details I've noticed new things every single time I've played for 50 or so hours.I do have a few complaints about the screamers being everywhere with a really long range stun that lasts forever, I get it should be punishing with huge emphasis on sneak, but I think there is a point where it becomes false difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials is a fresh and exciting take on the series, building upon familiar core game mechanics and themes, but with a new coat of paint placing events in a series of cold-war era, Jigsaw inspired, rat mazes for the players to escape. The world building is phenomenal and the character/audio design fantastic.The game is one of the few I've played which manages to look great, ray tracing and all graphical settings on epic, without dropping fps below 60. In my 10+ hrs of game time I've experience fps stutters twice, both time they resolved themselves almost immediately and weren't serve enough to hamper game play. I've experienced no other technical bugs aside from some slight visual bugs when enabling ray tracing on reflections (which I turned off, but left the other ray tracing settings enabled on). I'm using an NVIDIA RTX 2080TI btw. The game is listed as early access but frankly it feels more polished than most AAA title releases.If you're a returning fan of the series you're gonna enjoy it. If you're new and unsure, check out a streamer first. But the game play is basically first person, 1-4 player co-op pve, solving basic puzzles while using stealth mechanics to avoid the bad guys. As a player, you can only run and hide, you can't fight (you can stun the enemies, that's about it). It's high stress and adrenaline pumping at times. Multiplayer definitely takes away an element of the horror tension, but adds a whole new dimension to the game and I highly recommend you play both solo and with friends using voice chat. Even just random people in your server lobbies or the outlast discord have been fun to play with and it does scale difficulty based on the number of players.This game is worth $30. It's a very solid base game with plenty of room for more content and the devs clearly know what they're doing. This feels like a passion project and I haven't had a single moment so far that wasn't enjoyable.Be advised though, it's very mature content. There's nudity, gore, extreme violence, foul language, suggestive themes, drug use, various forms of discrimination, bigotry - any disturbing content you can think of is probably in this game (just like the last two games). But I find it adds to the atmosphere. This content isn't just present to add shock value, but the events of the game itself revolve around this grotesquely caricature presentation of the world we live in. It's not afraid to get a little political but without pushing a political agenda, which is kinda nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Goofy early 2000's torture porn edgelord vibes taken to the point of comedy.Played solo, this is very much akin to the previous games, just in enclosed maps aka trials instead of an ongoing storyline campaign. Tense, creepy, horror game where you alternate between sneaking, running and hiding. Trials can have modifiers when played at higher difficulties or during weekly challenges or bigger seasonal events. Maps have randomised elements on what items are available where, as well as doors being locked that force you to take extreme detours and really alter the working layout of the map.While there's no full story mode, there's a background narrative that does build a little as you play, with several evolving endings when you complete the equivalent of a prestige system. Levelling up unlocks the ability to buy more permanent buffs (pharmaceuticals), upgrade your rig (power), and unlock more switchable perks (amps) giving you things to work towards as well as cosmetic options.Multiplayer is a riot. It's the same content but enemy numbers and objectives are scaled up for more players, and it becomes a Benny Hill comedy sketch as everyone runs several enemies around like crazy screaming as they go.It's far from perfect, with some very frustrating bugs, enemy AI can cause them to just stand right in front of an objective for minutes at a time, some of the combinations of modifiers are just plain unfair and/or unfun, etc. But as someone who frowned on hearing the next Outlast would be a multiplayer game, I was pleasantly surprised, and now I'm hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot more fun than I was expecting. I can see it getting repetitive for some, but I think the co-op aspect keeps it all fresh. Keeping a steady stream of new content, like maps and such, would solve that problem; I hope they do that. I wouldn't call the game scary, per se, but it is definitely stressful (in a good way); if you are a fan of the Outlast series, don't go into this expecting to be scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There is a bit of AI/animation/netcode jank, but considering the game is in Early Access, it is in a far better state than I thought it would be in - it's more stable than many AAA final builds. Overall nothing game-breaking, just minor inconveniences or lag.All in all, I recommend it. I would normally caution people on buying Early Access games regardless if I thought it was good or not. However, considering the absolute state of modern AAA gaming with releases like Redfall and Forspoken, I've changed my stance. This game runs pretty good on any rig, it plays without any major bugs, and it's fun: nowadays that puts you in the top 1%.

I have encountered a couple bugs with the pusher (gas guy) and sometimes the AI is a little more desirable however the horror factor really does hide it and the fact that the music alone can make you want to run for your bed helps hide any imperfections in the game.For an "Early Access Game" at £25 it is really good, it's amazing to see that teams with such high prestige in the games industry are not checking out using "Early Access" as an excuse to just leave us with the bare minimum and move on to the next thing, it's refreshing and I can't wait for more!

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to say that the aesthetics of the chess game are amazing. The slightly faded, off-coloured pieces fit the scene very well, despite looking like very nice pieces, especially with the gold accents on them both. The highlighting of the moves you can make when you select a piece, as well as blocking you from making moves that'd put you in check, are both standards; but where I think this game goes above and beyond is that it actually animates you and your opponent grabbing and moving the pieces with your mouse in real time. Some might say this can give certain strategies away that other online chess games don't, but it replicates the psychological side of playing chess in person that is very often overlooked in digital versions of chess. As for the people, a lot of them like to play, a lot of them just run around the map doing other stuff, or arm wrestling, which is okay, I guess. You're still gonna find players to match pretty often, but it's a bit frustrating when you don't. _childDocuments_.review: Great experience overall. For those who want to mainly play solo as I have, this game is still definitely worth buying. I feel like there's some nice mechanical improvements from the previous Outlast games while also still respecting their visions; the general feel of it resembles the original in a lot of ways which was great and  perhaps surprising given the length of time between this RB release and the first game (over a decade, so potential for many changes within the structure of the Red Barrels creative teams).The loop and progression is satisfying enough without being addictive. Familiarity, but plenty of new things to adjust to. If you loved poring over the documents in the first two games, the new ones that you discover throughout trials may help you connect a few dots from those in the first two games.The trial environments are super interesting in their own right, and I've really enjoyed learning how to progress through each one so far. They can get mildly repetitive, but you would be surprised what the modification of objectives and other parameters can do to give the environments a new feeling of life. They have clearly made a conscious effort to ensure variety, and this success varies but is generally acceptable from my experience.To summarise and keep the review (kinda) short: If you love Outlast, I think you'll love this. It's a bit of old and a bit of new and the result is quite impressive. Bring your friends into the mix and the possibilities for mayhem and fun grow even further with clear intent for cooperative playstyles baked into the gameplay. I have to say as well - being able to experience Outlast-style gameplay outside of the main instalments, but with changing environments, objectives and modifiers, is fantastic. Love the gameplay of the former titles, but say it's been too soon since your last story playthrough? Boot up this one.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn.Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.If you got this far, then you probably really care about the game so here's my real input. The game is actually really good, has its moments of fright, and is one of the best CO-OP horror games on the market right now. Having friends to play with is ideal, but there's a ton of people in matchmaking for the trials so there's no worry. I think we can all agree that the arm wrestling is the best part of the game

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, the devs keep iterating on the difficulty scaling and enemy ai, which for me have been the biggest problems since starting the game, and the current state as time of writing is pretty good in my opinion. The problem of the first mission being too hard for new players got fixed by adding easier mode, while we also received the psychosurgery difficulty. Combined with the mentioned ai tweaks the game now has a mode that lets even experienced players feels some challenge.The environments are the best part of the game for me. Each chapter has a unique theme and a main mission. Then the just as detailed but less visited parts of the map get used by setting additional mini challenges at those places. Going higher in difficulty, the maps that previously have been buildings open to exploration and free movement turn into mazes, that reward the therapy subject for becoming familiar with the layout, and being able to quickly think of all the possible paths to their destination.The monetization is extremely user friendly - all the new content so far besides a few cosmetic bundles has been free, which on one hand is good, but on the other makes me worry about how viable that system is for the longevity of the game after being used to other companies squeezing their player base dry.I can't escape the comparison of this game with Payday 3. Both are games I wish to succeed as a long term services. The difference is one feels like it's doing what it can to wrest the money out of me, while Outlast Trials feels like it's even afraid to ask for it after the initial purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is a first-person psychological horror survival video game developed by Red Barrels, serving as a prequel to the first two games. The game features four distinct character classes and skill trees, each with unique abilities. Players must complete tasks while evading monstrous enemies, using night-vision goggles to navigate dim-lit areas. They can only carry three items at a time and cannot directly fight enemies. The game was teased in October 2019 and is not a direct sequel to Outlast 2. The game was delayed to 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with a closed beta available from October 28 to November 1, 2022. The full version was announced in early access on May 18, 2023, for Microsoft Windows. The game's development team consists of around 40 people.

_childDocuments_.review: Having delved into The Outlast Trials, it's evident that this latest installment in the Outlast series delivers a gripping survival horror experience, though it is not without its imperfections. Whether it will resonate with you might depend on your tolerance for terror and your preference for multiplayer dynamics.The Outlast Trials excels in creating a relentless atmosphere of fear and tension. Set in a nightmarish Cold War-era experiment, the game masterfully blends claustrophobic environments with disturbing imagery. The visual and auditory design amplifies the dread, with unsettling sound effects and chilling environments that keep you on edge throughout your playthrough.A standout feature of The Outlast Trials is its cooperative multiplayer mode. Playing with friends adds a new layer of strategy and tension, as you must work together to survive the horrors of the trials. This cooperative aspect enriches the gameplay, offering both moments of camaraderie and chaos, depending on how well your team coordinates.The game introduces intriguing new mechanics in the form of various trials that challenge your ability to adapt and survive. These trials are designed to test your nerves and teamwork, presenting a fresh take on the traditional Outlast formula. The variety in trial objectives and the need for strategic planning make each session uniquely intense.The Outlast Trials boasts a grim and unsettling visual style that effectively contributes to its horror elements. The grotesque character designs and the bleak, dilapidated environments are rendered with a high level of detail, enhancing the immersion and heightening the sense of dread.While the cooperative mode is a notable addition, its effectiveness can vary. Finding a group of players who are both competent and communicative can be hit-or-miss. This variability can lead to frustrating experiences, especially when teamwork is crucial to overcoming the more challenging trials.The game’s design sometimes feels inconsistent, with certain trials and encounters feeling overly punishing or unfair. These moments can detract from the overall enjoyment, particularly if they lead to repeated failures that feel more like trial-and-error rather than skillful play.Compared to its predecessors, The Outlast Trials’ narrative can feel somewhat shallow. While the game sets a compelling backdrop with its Cold War setting, the story itself might not delve as deeply or meaningfully as some players might hope. The focus is more on the survival aspects, which can leave the narrative feeling underdeveloped.Some players might encounter technical glitches and performance issues, which can detract from the immersion. Frame rate drops, occasional bugs, and other performance hiccups can be particularly disruptive in a game where atmosphere and smooth gameplay are crucial. delivers a harrowing and intense survival horror experience, enriched by its cooperative multiplayer mode and innovative trial mechanics. The grim atmosphere and disturbing visuals ensure a tense adventure that is likely to appeal to fans of the genre.However, inconsistencies in multiplayer experience, occasional frustrating design choices, and technical issues may hinder the overall enjoyment for some players. If you’re looking for a thrilling, cooperative horror experience that will test your nerves and teamwork, The Outlast Trials is worth diving into. Just be prepared for a ride that can be as unpredictable as it is unsettling.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked outlast trials when it came out. But as the game has gone on, i've only felt the missions have grown more tedious, and have been created with the design philosophy of wasting my time. The last two new additions, which they've been able to crank out in a whole year, are filled with boring busywork that has some attribute attached to it that slows any progress down to a crawl. It's a total waste of time, and you can tell, especially with the newest "toy factory" mission, where there's a part where you just crank a wheel in an empty room for a stupid amount of time, for no other reason than to crank it. You could remove that puzzle, and it would change absolutely nothing. That's not my biggest gripe however.The level design is horrible in some moments. Things can be very confusing and hard to navigate through, especially with first time through a level. It takes forever to find crap you're looking for, and i know i'm not alone in this because my group of 3 were navigating through that new level and just hated the experience. I could also complain about how the game feels like it was made by psychos and genuinely grosses me out, and I consider myself rather tolerant of edgy garbage or intense violence. But this new missions just made me feel sick, i didn't like it. Really everything about it just sucks. I hated it. If you're the average person, you're going to run out of steam with this game in a couple of hours after you tried most of the missions with your friends. Otherwise, nah. Or you could be like those weirdos that like to grind out a bunch of virtual blue tokens hundreds and hundreds of times because they have nothing better to do. Play anything else i recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A tentative no, more of a "maybe".Whether the game is fun or not really depends on the map. There are some that are cool, where you have objectives that make sense and are laid out for you. And then there are some matches where you spend 30 minutes running in circles through the same eight rooms trying to find the objective in the dark. At first not knowing where to go is tense, but after a while it just becomes incredibly annoying.I really would not play this game with less than three people, preferably four. Not because it is intensely difficult, but because you need bodies to search for keys.In terms of looks it's a lot better than Outlast 2, which is best forgotten about, and the monsters aren't bad. It's just mechanically frustrating a lot of times. It's not scary, not at all, but if you can get lucky and progress through the levels quickly it's pretty fun.After a few runs through you have to start wondering what you're leveling up for, though. Once you play through a level once you've basically seen what you're going to see, and there's not really a lot of point to leveling up other than to make it generally easier. I just don't feel like replaying levels at a harder setting is really doing anything for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Played 34 hours (including beta) and can say it's extremely fun to play with friends. The gameplay is smooth as butter and the AI isn't stupid enough for you to be able to hide in a closet all game (cause some people just enjoy doing so for some reason), and not annoying enough to never loose chase if you turn a corner and try to use stealth. The only aspect that could be improved on are the progression levels and the items you can get by doing so, which I believe will be worked upon full release, so I'm not too worried about that. _childDocuments_.review: The graphics are great, the game play is smooth, and the replayability is up there. You can tell the devs really ironed it out prior to releasing it. So far no bugs or glitches have stood out to me during my first 6 hours of game play. I'd compare this to a higher quality version of games like Labrynthine, Devour, Lunch Lady etc. If you and your friends like those types of games then you will 10000% appreciate what Outlast Trials has to offer. It's pretty much a AAA game compared to those. Definitely fun with friends or just match making. There's an OK amount of content (3 main maps and a handful of different modes per) and a lot of reasons to keep you playing, but is it worth $30 right off at this current state? I'd say kind of. When the issue is wanting more instead of wanting better, it's worth it to me. I was looking forward this this, Sons of the Forest, and RedFall all year and this is the only one that wasn't a buggy, clunky mess. I appreciate that the devs really put time and effort into it which is sadly a rare commodity these days, and I trust them to keep adding more during the Early Access period. _childDocuments_.review: Fun and engaging survival horror game. Not very scary after a while, but the first Trial solo can be exciting. My favorite part is how satisfying the animations of everything are. Your character pops open a bottle of meds, takes a pill out into the palm of their hand, and swallows. Adrenaline shots are first stabbed into the arm and then the bottle is squeezed like toothpaste. Sliding, moving, jumping and hurdling over obstacles is smooth and satisfying. Your nightvision is simple and easy on the eyes. My only gripes are how excessive the "spooky" factor is put up. Eventually all of the blood and gore and evil capitalism vibes just get a bit much and no longer become scary but rather just gross and uncreative. I would love to see future Trials centered less around blood and guts and more on the psychological horror elements on their own. I don't need to see a guy getting chopped up to be afraid of the idea of going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Outlast fan, I got to say that this is very nice addition to the franchise. The game is fun, challenging and immersive. There's also a ton of stuff to grind towards, like new abilities, perks, customization items, etc. If you're the type of person who loves mastering games, this one is for you. Some other positives are the amazing graphics, the horrifying atmosphere, the gameplay, the social features and the enemy variety. There are some negatives though, like the lack of Programs (aka missions), the lack of a plot and the handling of the Prime Assets (aka the main villains). They don't feel that special and they don't have any distinct soundtrack like in the previous games. All of these problems are solvable and this is an early access title (at the time of this review). So, I believe that these issues will be addressed in the future. I recommend this game to any horror or Outlast fan.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast TrialsFor the first time in years i played a game that i had insane amounts of fun at. The game is being selled for €39.99 and i love the fact that Red Barrels didn't add any way of transactions in this game for cosmetics or anything at all, the only way to get good at this game and get cosmetics such as Cell Decorations, clothing and skins for your character is simply done throught grinding the game, leveling up and completing new Trials or even ones you've already completed which will still reward you with xp, Murkoff Dollars and level up rewards.Lore: The Outlast Trials take place in the year 1959 aka a couple years before the events of Outlast 1 and 2. The Murkoff Corporation conducts group experiments for CIA program MKUltra. You are a drug addict that lives in the streets and is one that the society wouldn't mind losing, so one day you find a poster/invitation to join the Murkoff Corporation Industry but why? When you join the doctors will make experiments on your body to change who u are to pretty much change society's point of view on yourself because they will understand that they lost someone important, and that someone is you.Gameplay: In my opinion this game finally brings something fresh to the gaming industry after so many years and tears of companies ripping off eachother and releasing the same broken games over and over (Battle Royales, Arena Shooters and much more). The game comes with a great Coop mode which i would say is honestly one of the best we've seen in any Coop title. You can partner up with up to 4 people forming a squad and taking on the Challenge of the Trials together. The game came out 18th of May this year and since then they've added new in-game holiday events such as a Halloween and a christmas event and on top of that brand new trials for people to grind. As of right now the game features 4 different and unique Programs with their own and different Trials and Program X which you can beat to earn your freedom (won't touch upon this Program due to spoilers). When grinding this game you can unlock different cosmetics, Amps which are small abbilities that you either Sprint for longer, bash through doors while running, slide while running, make no noise when you step on broken glass that would otherwise make noise to alert enemies of your location and many more that even can't think of cause we'd be here for hours. There is a feature called Rig's, there are 4 of them and each one has it's unique abbility for every playstyle aka Solo or Squaded up. Rig 1: Is a device called "STUN" which whenever you hit an enemy with it you temporarely stun them and disorient them. Rig 2: is a Mine you place on the ground that when is stepped on by an enemy releases a "BLINDING SMOKE" that makes any enemy type blind for a duration of time. Rig 3: is a "HEALING CANISTER" that releases a healing cloud around you for yourself and your teammates if they are close to you. Rig 4: is called "X-RAY" and makes it so you can see enemies through walls and ping them for you teammates or is also really good if you are planning to go solo in the trials. I'm not gonna touch upon what missions you do in the trials cause that is gonna spoil the fun.Characters and Maps: The Outlast Trials offer a huge variety of enemies, some more memorable than other but it is what it is, The First Trial you'll be mainly hunted down by "THE COP" who has a really cool design in my opinion and has a shock stick so he better not catch you roaming around. And the other one is "THE MOTHER" she is my favorite one easily, her voice actor did a great job and her design and lore is just pretty sick, her abbility is that she has a little puppet on her left arm with a drill in it's mouth so if she catches you then yeah. her lore is that she loves to skin people's faces and put them on Manekins and too be fair after you play Program 2 and 3 you'll realise that it's not only faces she likes to skin, super freaky and insanely cool at the same time. All of the Maps in the game are just way too good and really well designed to be honest, the game thus far has only four maps but even more trials so it's not one trials per map. this game has more content than what meets the eye at first. First we have the "Police Station", "The Fun Park", "The Orphanage" and finally "The Courthouse" until they realese more ofcourse.Soundtrack: The soundtrack and Score of this game is just way too based and knows exactly what it wants to be without it trying to be a certain way it can't. Huge congrats on the guy who made the entire Soundtrack and the orchestra.Verdict: The Outlast trials is as of right now on sale due to the holydays for about €21.99 and it's normal price is €29.99. In my opinion if you are a long time Dead By Daylight fan and you are looking for something new and more fresh of a horror experince, The Outlast Trials will do you just that favor. It's an amazing Coop game and even if you play Solo and have no friend you can still matchmake and find people to play with so you can make yourself friends and meet new people. This game is an insanely fun ride to go through even Solo or with friends and trust me, with friends? it's on another level cause this game is actually scary.I love the games that are paid and don't have a battle pass system or any in-game purchases at all because that's how games should be, because it also ruins all the fun. Someone could grind their ass off to get a certain cosmetic and someone else is just gonna buy it with real money to just flex it which really shouldn't be the way and i love that this game is this way.I'll give this game 10 because it knows what it's trying to be and the devs clearly know what they are doing, and let's not forget that the dev team is roughly around 100 people and when they made Outlast 2 they were around 20 people and just shows you what type of insane quality a team can put on a project if they are willing and passionate about it, Thank You Red Barrels.The Outlast Trials: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this is by far one of the most bang-for-your-buck-game out there. **DISCLAIMER** I will say the things that I enjoy:1.Progression in the game is very linear.2. _childDocuments_.review: As an Outlast veteran, I can say this is one of the best multiplayer games to date. The really long cutscenes and loading times before/after a trial make it tedious to want to play over and over again.All in all, I give this game a 9.5/10, I've never had so much fun or been this immersed in a multiplayer game before. _childDocuments_.review: After so many new co-op games being announced and then turning out to be generic Live service games with RPG elements, incremental progression, battlepasses and in general various strategies to ensure you will only be playing one game forever, Outlast Trials is a breath of fresh air and I can recommend it just because it is something different and incredibly fun. Hopefully this statement will not age poorly as the game leaves Early Access.To sum it up quickly, tense stealth horror game with satisfying progression. With a higher player count and more gameplay hours in, the scare aspect upon being caught quickly becomes replaced with pure chaos.For those on the fence, the tutorial showcases the core gameplay and almost the worst it will throw at you horror wise, I strongly recommend to buy, try (should take around 20 minutes) and decide whether you want to keep going or refund.After the tutorial you are put into a lobby with other players, where you can select the main missions of the game.These missions have slight randomization for the replayability aspect, certain doorways will be locked, items will be changed around, different hiding spots will be blocked off, however objectives and the general route will pretty much stay the same.In the same lobby you are also introduced to the game's progression systems, personal customization and the  arm wrestling minigame.The actual gameplay varies as in the first hours of the game, the horror aspect of the game will be heavily present as you get used to the game, the way it messes with you via the multiplayer aspect. You will be familiarizing yourself with the traps, the enemies and in general will take it slow and careful.10 hours in and with a high enough playercount however, the horror aspect wears off and the game becomes something akin to first person , The careful tense stealth gameplay now becomes a prelude to the chaos that happens when somebody gets caught, as all the players will start running away from the enemies, possibly into the traps, saving eachother from being attacked all while scrambling to complete the objective.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a really well made game, for a game in early access it seems to run and work better then most fully released games out on the market. _childDocuments_.review: This game truly surprised me. I didn't know what to expect from Red Barrels or how they would pull off an online version of Outlast, but they did it in style. Only activities available are arm wrestling and chess, yet somehow I still found myself spending a ton of time in the hub messing with randos, beating on tables. _childDocuments_.review: Red Barrels have once again outdone themselves with another great installment to the Outlast Universe. Outlast Trials has the same grit and horror that Outlast 1 and 2 were known and praised for, yet Trials steps it up a notch by giving players the option to experience this game in two ways: solo or with friends/randoms.This game's sound design and musical scores add to the scary experience and the enormous amounts of cosmetics you can unlock for both your room and your character are jaw dropping. The enemy designs are grimy and truly may shake someone to their core. There is also a good amount of lore for those who have enjoyed dissecting Outlast's files and dialogue in the first two games.The official release of the 1.0 version means an influx of new players but there are also a fair amount of old players returning. As someone who has gotten fairly deep into the game (although with only 1 rebirth under my belt), it was refreshing to find a lobby quick and to see that the load times have greatly improved.I was lucky enough to experience the beta testing and upon completing the tutorial and playing a few trials, I was roped back into this world and wanted to see more. If you like the original games and you want to see what it'd be like to experience something of that sort with friends, grab yourself a copy of the game.Let the trials begin!

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of Outlast. Ever since the very first game I've been a diehard fan, and this game continues to stoke and keep the fire alive inside of me. While it has a bit of a difficult learning curve in the beginning, you may think the game is unapproachable or too difficult. But give it a chance after practicing and watching some beginner tips, I promise it's worth it. As you level things only get easier, too.Fantastic game, can't wait to see what else they have in store. This is an incredibly strong entry for Red Barrels and I hope they keep this game alive.

_childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials is an outstanding cooperative horror game that exceeds expectations, offering approximately 15 hours of thrilling content in its current state. With engaging gameplay, a terrifying atmosphere, challenging stealth mechanics, immersive sound design, and impressive visuals, it successfully delivers a memorable and adrenaline-pumping experience. Whether playing cooperatively or solo, players can immerse themselves in the heart-pounding world of the Cold War-era research facility.While the game showcases many strengths, it's important to address a few areas that could benefit from improvement. The limited variety of enemies encountered throughout the game could be expanded upon to provide more surprises and challenges. Additionally, incorporating more incentives for exploration, such as hidden collectibles or optional objectives, could enhance the overall depth and engagement. Furthermore, introducing more complex puzzles that require creative problem-solving would add an extra layer of satisfaction for players seeking a greater challenge.It's worth mentioning that future updates and expansions have the potential to significantly change the content and gameplay experience, further extending the game's value and replayability. Despite these critiques, Outlast Trials remains a must-play for horror enthusiasts and fans of the series, offering an exceptional cooperative horror adventure that keeps players on the edge of their seats. Prepare yourself for a gripping and unforgettable journey into the heart of terror, whether you choose to face it with friends or brave it alone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy cooperative (or solo) survival horror games with a focus on tension and scares, The Outlast Trials delivers a solid experience. With plenty of updates and tweaks since it's release in early access, the game has definitely become more viable to play alone if you'd prefer to experience the isolated horror of it's predecessors. 🖤🦷
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials is a breath of fresh air in the world of multiplayer and a wonderful addition to the Outlast series. It's not so much as scary as it is fun, unless you're playing by yourself in some of the more challenging programs. There's a good amount of customization too, you unlock items by random upon completion of each trial and when you level up. Equipment comes in the form of "rigs", tools engineered to help evade or shake off the people chasing you, sometimes they make the game too easy though. But the trials will get more challenging I assure you. Personally, I think $40 is a solid price for the amount of content that is in store currently. It can get repetitive quickly, and it will, but that's where having friends come in! The devs have made it known they plan on pumping out updates as effectively as they can and I hope we will be able to enjoy this game for years to come!TLDR: Unique Gem, fun in groups

I don't know if it's an online issue or if it's just optimization, but it runs smoothly more often than it stutters.As for the aesthetics, the game seemed a little weird at first, compared to the other 2 games. Then again, you have to remember that this takes place in 1959 and suddenly it's almost futuristic lol.If you're familiar with the US Govt's intelligence agencies and their long legacy of criminal activity, then you'll feel right at home collecting lore via documents scattered throughout the levels. They're fairly accurate, as well, as far as blurring fact and fiction goes.There's a channel detailing the CIA from inception to present day, citing sources for everything, going through Project Paperclip, MKULTRA,  and even the gay orgies with J. Edgar Hoover and other notable men of prestige that the CIA's director threw for some reason. Check out EyesWideOpen on Youtube, it's an invaluable source and pretty fun to see how the lore of OUTLAST TRIALS fits into the history of the CIA.
