_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy is this game a mixed bag! Let’s start with the first thing though: this game is NOT a metroidvania in any stretch of the imagination. It’s a pretty straightforward action-adventure game. Now that said let’s just skip to some of the problems and even dealbreakers with this game. Problems. 1. The combat is stiff and very clunky. Now you may like this so it really depends but I would have liked it to be much more fluid and smooth. For me it took some time and many deaths before a learned it and in the end I can somewhat appreciate it. 2. There’s save points and check points. Now at a save point you can obviously save your progress (logic) and the check points are there to restart you when you die. But here’s the problem. You can only activate a check point once and if you choose to go back and save and then pass the check point again it won’t activate! You now restart from your save point. Now to  the real issue, let’s say you activate a check point and then you fight a boss. You may have a different setup for some bosses (different weapons, different magic you get what I mean) so you change your setup before that boss fight. And now you die and you go back to retry (from the check point) and you notice the all the changes you have made is reseted to what you had before so you have to do the same changes EVERY TIME after you die. The only way to save the changes is at a save point. This is infuriating to say the least. 3. The achievements are totally broken! I mean they straight up doesn’t work! If this is important to you move this to the “deal breaker” section. The deal breaker! Now this last one is an absolutely deal breaker for me. You see I started playing this game on my Steam Deck and I was planning on finishing the game on my PC once I got back home. But no such luck, the cloud saves doesn’t work. And I’ve tried everything under the sun the game refuses to sync up to my PC. This is the one thing that tipped me over for: “it’s a ok adventure game I can recommend to some people” to “nope! That’s one more technical issue I won’t accept”! So if any of my complaints is a deal breaker to you just stay away from this game or at least wait to a sale and/or an update…..maybe it’ll be good game in a couple of months who knows?

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by saying that I really don't want to write a negative review of this game, because parts of it are very good. The Art, which everyone has already touched on is one of the best uses of particle effects and lighting that I've seen in a 2D game, and the level design is, for what it is, actually very good. I did enjoy myself when exploring, both while going through the first time, and when going back for all the chests that I skipped (There's a reason to do so, it's explained in game). Unfortunately, I can't say the same about the combat, and for a game that is so heavily based around it, it's a deal breaker. To put it simply, it feels as though the players move-set and the enemies where designed for different games. The player has a simple move-set, with slow weapon swings even on fast weapons and a dodge that has I-frames but also a very long recovery, which indicate that the game is one based primarily around spacing and avoiding enemies with similarly long windups and cool-downs. Many of the enemies however didn't seem to get the memo, and attack so fast that in the time it takes for some of the player's slower weapons to swing, they can finish the recovery on their last attack, start up a new one, and finish it before the player can hit them. This more or less results in a combat system that encourages not skill, but finding the cheesiest possible strategy and then spamming it regardless of how boring it is to play, and make no mistake, standing out of range of enemies, hiding behind a shield while the enemies get killed by spinning swords isn't fun.Perhaps this kind of clunky combat would work if the game was based primarily around avoiding enemies, and indeed many horror games achieve success in this way quite well, but this game is a different beast, as it has fairly involved 2 or 3 stage boss fights, in which the sub-par combat is left to fend for itself, devoid of any good level design to hide behind.To compound this, the game has a fairly significant number of smaller design issues that make it quite frequently a chore to play. On that front, the rest of this review is just going to be list of my more minor issues and some of my ideas on how they might be resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to recommend. I don't usually review games I haven't beat it, neither for games I refunded, however, if the first few hours of the game doesn't hook you in, it's a bit hard to continue playing...This is specially the case with Lost Ruins. A game that visually looks incredible, reminding me of the Momodora series by Bombservice. Despite the great looking visuals, the biggest problem of this game is the pace. I'm talking about "constant open inventory" kind of games.In this game, there are a lot of things you have to be aware of, environmental things that can damage you, healing items that heal or cure effects, and so on. You can also use different weapons that vary your attack speed and things like that. Some enemies work better with certain weapons, while others are best approached with complete different playstyles.The game does not have any sort of preset switcher or ways to quickly switch things, as pointed out in other reviews that have beat the game. I stopped playing the game after my first hour or so, those hours were mostly going into the inventory screen to change gear and stuff, not much about actually playing the game. Every time that I had to do something on the inventory screen made the game feel incredibly slow.Some of the items I unlocked seems like they could simply be passive items instead of items you have to equip to have that effect applied to you. One of those items can be easily exploited, being a Ring that reduces your Max Health, but regens your health upon wearing it. I think there's also another negative upon wearing it that I forgot what it does now.Lost your health? Well, you can go to the inventory screen once again, equip that Ring, return to the game, wait for the health regen, go back to the inventory yet again, equip an item with a better bonus (since you won't be needing the Ring while at full health), advance a little to the room before you get damaged to something that you would prefer to get damaged instead of relying with constant inventory opening for every little thing in this game (as there's many different environmental damage types toward your adventure). Repeat the process.Even if you don't constant switch to this Ring (either play without it or play with it equipped at all times), you will still need to be constantly using your inventory screen to use specific spells to deal with specific things blocking your path, to defeat enemies easier, to heal yourself, and so on. No matter your playstyle, you will have to rely heavily on the inventory screen in this game, and with no way to quickly switch things, and no preset-loadouts, it's really hard to get the pace of this game flowing. The great visuals stop being your focus, and the letters of your inventory screen ends up being what's shown on screen most of the time, sadly.Your attack speed, depending on the weapon you equip, is also pretty slow. Your character goes into a complete halt when attacking. I wouldn't mind this very much if it wasn't for the constant menu-ing in this game. I really want to like this game, I really do, specially because of those great looking visuals, but it's really hard to continue playing after you realize what you'll be doing in the entire game:Opening the inventory screen every few seconds or so.The enemies are also unforgiving, as they can quickly drain your health due to the lack (or very little) invincibility frames. Combine this with things I have previously mentioned, you want to rely the maximum with your current arsenal, and the things you have obtained. Healing yourself with the Ring is a huge bonus and it's hard to overlook when so many things in this game can damage you in either fair or unfair ways.So yeah, this is one of those reviews that the writer wants to like the game, but just can't. I really really want to like this game, but, it doesn't feel like I'm playing a game when I'm constantly switching my arsenal instead of doing anything on it.There are also a few other nitpicks I want to bring up:- There's no way to disable voices in the game. These are tied to Sound Effects volume slider (you can disable Music and Sound Effects separately). This game doesn't have voice acting for dialogue, but your character will shout things when doing certain things like getting hit, being killed, blocking, etc., and it can get annoying after a while. I wish I didn't had to turn off all sounds to get rid of the voices / grunts that my character does when doing action X, Y, Z.- You can equip a shield that, upon successfully blocking, the character uses the same voice line when you take damage. This feels pretty weird, to be honest. It should either have a different voice clip or no voice at all. Just a loud "blocking" noise would be sufficient in this case.

_childDocuments_.review: In this action adventure we play a young girl who has been teleported to a castle. In the process, we have completely lost our memory. The castle is full of skeletons of other people who, according to the messages on their cell phones (with rather long-running batteries...), seem to have been teleported to this world just like us and tried (unsuccessfully) to find a way out. Besides goblins and aggresive animals that want to kill us, we also meet the sorceress Beatrice in the castle, who helps us find our way around. Soon we cross a fantasy realm full of monsters and hard-to-conquer bosses to find out how to get back to our old world.Lost Ruins is a 2D action adventure game in pixel style, in which we can attack our enemies with a variety of swords, axes and other medieval weapons. Soon we'll also learn spells to burn enemies or heal ourselves. The game teaches us to use the environment to achieve our objectives. Flammable liquids burst into flames when they come into contact with burning lanterns or fireballs, ice magic freezes waters. The game's focus is less on frantic jumping passages and more on combat and managing life,magic points, and our inventory. Cute characters, fluid movement animations, lots of items to collect (clothes, food, weapons, spells), an automatically drawn map and portals for fast travel make Lost Ruins a fantastic 2D action adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like MetroidVanias this will be neither Groundbreaking nor Mediocre. It is a great quality MV with cute animation, beautiful pixel art, fun and quaint characters, with a simple combat & progression system that rides the casual/accessible side of the genre, but still has enough there for vets. Its cruelly short however, at 20 hours I had completed both the Normal and "Boss Mode" difficulty options. And personally, I really wanted more of this clueless and naive protagonist but with all that said, in summary 'Lost Ruins' is a brisk romp of a MetroidVania that's fun whether you're new or at home in the genre. I'd suggest starting on 'Veteran' difficulty as there is something added onto the tail end of the game not present in 'Recommended' and 'Accessible' difficulties. As well as 'Veteran' feeling like the intended experience for such a comparatively brief MV. Grab it on sale if the length is a concern for you, otherwise I find the price and game itself perfect for what the developers intentions clearly were! Loved it c: <3

_childDocuments_.review: This review is going to make me a hypocrite. But hey, we’re all hypocritical once in a while, right? Oh well, here we go.This metroidvania is pretty heavy on the “-vania”: there are some really heavy RPG elements that, depending on your level of enjoyment of those mechanics, will make or break this game. Elemental damage and status effects abound here and only the right combination of equipment will make life easier for the player. Depending on the player’s gear, a puddle of oil on the floor can either lead to a quick death to the player or a helpful weapon against any baddies standing in the middle of it. At first, this caused me some really aggravating deaths until I started to get a better grasp of the system. Also, it might be worth noting that the menuing can be a little annoying as the player switches equipment in and out for different obstacles, but all-in-all it’s really fun.The story is pretty silly, despite some twists here and there. But the characters you meet along the way are pretty great. The psychotic butcher schoolgirl, the zombie fangirls, the katana-wielding goblin slayer: they’re all fantastic. On top of that, the enemies the player faces are memorable as well and each poses a different threat while being vulnerable to different damage types. This game constantly mixes things up and keeps things interesting.Where this game makes me a hypocrite is that it’s very linear – which is precisely the same reason why I didn’t like  and why I didn’t recommend that one. Any real exploration is locked behind sidequests, so if the player isn’t paying attention to those, there is no real reason to roam around the world. On top of that, items needed to complete those quests are marked on the map, eliminating any need to do any real searching. The thing that makes this game more interesting than  is that the limited exploration usually leads to a unique piece of equipment or a new spell or something. In , exploration lead to either a health pick-up, a stamina pick-up, or (eventually useless) money, and that’s pretty much it.  does it better, is what I’m trying to say.In the end, I really had a blast with this game. From the characters, to the maps, to the combat, everything came together to make this one a memorable stand-out. If you’re willing to muscle your way through this often-challenging game, you’re likely to find something you like in here. I know I did!

_childDocuments_.review: At first I loved this game, as I'm a fan of 2D souls-likes... that said, after a while it feels like a lot of cheap & unfair game play keeps coming up. Very disappointing, this is no Blasphemous or Momodoro. You die too often to situations where skill and reflex mean nothing. For example, you might do some tricky platforming only to be killed by a fireball from off screen while the devs clearly planned for you to be in a position where you can't avoid it, all after you just spent several minutes getting to that point finally! I'm okay dying repeatedly in a game so long as it feels fair, but this game subs clever design for cheap shots...Update: I've also noticed quite a few bugs related to button remapping. some labels don't update correctly for "back" if you remap the B button, for example. This sucks because the default layout is bad; it uses triggers for map and menu nav and bumpers for combat stuff... what?! So backwards. I tried to give it another chance today but now my L trigger brings up map even though it is clearly remapped for secondary attack in settings and reflects that on screen... So it says press LT equip but when I do the map opens. This sort of thing might be acceptable if the devs were updating the game and fixing issues, but it appears they abandoned supporting this game after a series of patches post-release and zero updates or community communication since.

There are lots of options for one-handed or two-handed melee weapons and different ranged and magic attacks. In addition to weapons, you can equip various items that provide huge bonuses to completely alter your build on the spot (or even between different phases of a boss fight).The first playthrough takes about 6-7 hours to complete. After that, you unlock additional difficulty levels, challenge runs (magic only and daggers only), and a Nier: Automata-like additional mini-campaign in which you play as three bosses from the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I think i want to like this game more than i did. I keep thinking ‘i like it but…’It's high point is definitely it's art. Fantastic pixel art and a good mix of nice lighting, effects and particles that are notably different resolutions but that still work together to be clearly readable in gameplay,  It dose lean a bit fan servicey in a similar vein as the shanty games for the bosses. Has a nice map to explore, with simple but enjoyable puzzles to break up the platforming and combat. An ok story, bit tropey but dint hate it.Gameplay it's a slow paced castlevania with sprinklings of souls like systems. It's core movement and combat felt good to me and i had a fun time playing it. Weapons each felt different and satisfying to use. A Solid variety of enemies to fight, simple but enjoyable bosses. The Magic spells you got were neat and the elemental effects looked nice and would have environmental effects. But it feels like it layers too many unneeded or unbalanced systems on top of this. I think it's health system is largely pointless as most damage you take means you die in two or three hits on normal anyway. With the items to heal largely being either heal for a useless amount or over a useless amount of time. so you have a good chance of insta-gibbing as soon as you leave the frustrating long item list menu regardless of the items you spamed. This also is similar to the equipment system, too many largely useless bits of gear, some that i think are broken or have wrong item translation descriptions.  with too few slots so i ended up just using the same items most of the game as it wasnt worth touching the system.It's save system also feels messy, with two different saves. A manual save point but also statues that auto-save when you walk past but you have no control over. Also it's unclear when these ones reset to be reusable. Meaning it can lead to frustrating repetition in sections with only the auto-statues as you cant control its use well. Also with death coming to you so swiftly i found the time to re-load is also frustratingly long too, i just felt like i wanted instant respawn/reload not what felt agonisingly long from death slowdown and wait for the prompt that your dead and want to re-load.I still enjoyed it over all apart from those issues. My first playthrough on normal was a solid 6-7 hours and it unlocked a bunch of modes on completion. Also seems like there are multiple endings and ways to play through, so it's got replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Wannabe H-game that confuses challenge with frustration.Story: 2/10Absolutely nothing compelling. You appear in a strange world, you fight bosses to find a way out. Very little is explained beyond surface details, and uh oh surprise twist except you definitely see it coming after playing the game for 5 minutes.Oh, by the way, you won't be able to see the real ending unless you beat it on Veteran mode. So yeah, have fun with that. Super fun and rewarding game design. Characters: 4/10 (9/10 for the heroine, 2/10 for just about everyone else) The main character is charming, but almost every single other character is dripping with the kind of art style you expect to see in adult-themed games. I recognize the talent, but it's also a bit ... gross. Some characters have interesting personalities, but you get a total of about 60 seconds worth of time for each of them.Three of the bosses are giant women that take up your entire screen, have massive and fully animated breasts, and "get embarrassed" when you do enough damage. Almost every other boss transforms to a second stage "party city skanky costume" form. How horny was the dude that made this? Good lord.Music: 3/10What music? There's maybe 7 tracks in this whole game. Some are okay, the rest are just ambient background noise.Sound: 7/10"Clunk! CLANK! CLANK! Clunk! Clunk! Clunk! Clunk! CLANK!"It's fine, but more variety would be nice. Some of the character noises are fun, though.Gameplay: 3/10Definitely my least favorite part of the game, and it's basically all there is to the game. To call this game "challenging" is inaccurate. It's intentionally designed to frustrate you. - If you attack in mid-air, you stop forward momentum. - Attack animations take forever to execute and recover from, while enemies attack with lightning speed and have massive windows for hitting you. - You don't get i-frames if you're hit, so some enemies can one shot you, by actually hitting you 5+ times in rapid succession. All you have to do is get hit that first time. - HP and MP don't regenerate unless you use items. There's no camp to restore HP and MP. You'll be able to cast a spell twice, and then have to spend money on items to cast again.- Status affects (which stack in higher difficulties) are overtly brutal, so you can play this game two ways: - - 1. Spend most of your time menu-ing to apply heals and cures.- - 2. Actually play the game, and just die. And then sit through all the cutscenes again.- When you die, the game makes you wait 5 seconds in slow-mo before letting you continue. Why? Because screw you, that's why.Graphics: I don't usually grade on this, and I won't start now, but...- The pixel graphics are very pretty.- The lighting effects are neat.If this game's for you, hey, that's great. But ultimately I'm just frustrated and disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't regret backing that game up.The art is absolutely charming and cute.The gameplay is decent and serviceable, with a lot of interesting interactions between elements and environment.At first I really thought I wouldn't like the combat with attacks that lock your entire character, including stopping air momentum, but those are the rules of the game and you play by the rules to see what's up.I think bosses, especially in Veteran mode, could benefit from having a couple more attack patterns.Some spells seem way better than others (the life leech spell makes everything way easier).My only gripe with the game is that it could need one more filter in the inventory (by type/element) and/or maybe the ability to put some items as favorites so they would always show up at the top of the list.Good items variety, interesting stuff happening, very interesting modes unlocked post-game.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Great metroidvania that even if it's somewhat short, has good survival mechanics that tests the player's creativity and skills.Lost Ruins, even though it's a metroidvania, it's sold as a survival experience, and as such, it should be tackled with a bit of patience. I see some people complaining about how the combat is slow, heavy and clunky, but I personally like it because you can feel the weight of the weapon you're trying to use, and it was done purposely so you build your character around such "flaws", like equipping a accessory that increases the attack speed of heavy weapons, or cast speed and/or cost of spells, and the game gives the player freedom to do any kind of build, as long you have the equipment to make it work. Early on that might be a problem tho, since you have to either buy the equipment or find it around the map.You can't grind out of any situation in the game or increases the stats of your character through items, like other games in the genre do, because it doesn't have a level up system, but the game has lots of checkpoints and save points, so it doesn't ending up being too frustrating and whatnot. I personally think there's way too many checkpoints in the game tho. I just think that the existence of shields somewhat broke the difficulty down a lot, which enables you to defend yourself virtually against anything, but it's not just aimlessly guarding, since you have to time the guard action correctly to defend (which has a pretty forgivable timing window), and elemental attacks usually pierce the shield (which you can mitigate or nullify completely with the right accessory), so it involves a bit of skill.Visual wise, Lost Ruins is beautiful. Every area has its own design and particularities, and the use of simulated pixels it's a shown of its own. I like how there's no reuse of enemy design, and how each enemy race suits the area which you encounter them perfectly, without feeling like out of place. The boss design is superb. A bit fanservicey, but it's great. I really like it.Replay wise, it offers quite a bit of content actually. The main campaign, which is divided into 4 difficulty modes, has two endings, and 3 extra modes are unlocked after finishing it for the first time, which may not contain anything new per se, it offers diversified gameplay and more challenges.Anyway, I really recommend Lost Ruins to the fans of the metroidvania genre. It may be somewhat slower early on, but keep pushing. It's really fun. It really is what I've expected, and a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute treat for the senses.The sound design is especially top-notch here. Someone spent time carefully planning overlapping sounds to not interfere too much with each other. Footsteps are responsive and sell the weight of characters and the surfaces they walk on. Ambient soundscapes pair well with any underscoring provided - and when there is silence it is with purpose! Actions and indicators are satisfyingly present with crisp transients and environment processing that's subtle but present... I know more and more games are taking sound design seriously these days, but when it's done right it's a treat and this game does it  right.Also, the visual detail is sublime for anyone who appreciates pixel aesthetics. We've got dynamic dithering on the dynamic shadows and dithering on the fade-out of the overlaying bokeh light effects in some scenes. Light maps paired with carefully applied shaders give a nice, glowy, rim-lighting effect when appropriate that doesn't distract from the pixel aesthetic. Animation is also buttery smooth with filtering turned on (feels a bit less polished with lower filtering settings, to me). Really, it's just plain gorgeous and does almost everything right where design rules apply. Might seem funny, but I think the least interesting visual detail to this game was the illustrated character busts seen during dialogue - and they don't look terrible or anything, they are just very static compared to the polish found everywhere else.Gameplay is pleasant. I'm still playing on the default difficulty and have only died a couple times. 2D platformers aren't usually my thing, but after I got accustomed to the jump height and distance I didn't feel like that was much of a struggle (yet). Platform edges are consistent and the fall speed (without any buffs) is just floaty and precise enough to be comfortable for most players to land where they want. It wasn't long before they started giving me equipment that impacted movement, so I suspect progression will unlock some variety to better suit player preferences.In classic, metroidvania fashion, progression and discovery work together to feel rewarding to the player. You expand your arsenal of abilities and equipment to reach new areas of the map that continue narration.It's a simple system, but resource management is critical. You have some room for error, but you can easily get killed quickly if you rush everything and avoid a methodical approach to most situations. So far, it all feels very well-balanced on normal difficulty.Animation, while very smooth to look at, may actually have been where I struggled the most at first. The first weapon you receive does not have an instantaneous attack, so there is a miniscule-but-present build-up time you have to account for while charging an enemy and swinging your sword. This was the most jarring yet fundamental mechanic for me to adapt to, but the game seems aware of this learning curve as you're given some fodder enemies to practice on (that can kill you, but at minor expense to your progression only) and literally the first item I purchased from the vending machine reduced my attack delay slightly. The silver-lining to the slow sword-swing was I noticed a visual-distortion effect on the trail behind the sword itself mid-swing that adds weight to the motion and eventual impact, even as the most basic weapon available. I think mastering the timing and distancing for effective attack strategies might actually appeal a bit to people that enjoy 2D fighters as I see some minor overlap. At the very least, it's not a game for button-mashing.Overall, I'm just gushing. Other reviewers probably have more critical takes on the experience that appeal to the more challenge-proned players. I'm not at all surprised by how well this game is rated on Steam right now; it's very competently made.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe the game in two words it would be cheap difficulty.Difficulty:Everything kills you in two hits, I died multiple times in half an hour but none of them because I didnt play well enough. Died because the slightly different looking ground meant that it was covered in oil so lantern I destroyed set it and me on fire. Died because attacking a lantern in fornt of you and then pressing backwards also redirects the flames backwards. Died because I used a explosive wand and wasnt far enough from the blast. Died because I didn´t pay attention to the ground pixels that represented spikes. Died because I walked into a finished and missed attack animation (girl launching two daggers with her arms forward into the ground).The combat is just as bad, slow and boring. Most enemy attacks have a higher reach so when you dodge them you are out of reach and have to walk back into them and then attack. This also means that slower weapons are aweful to play with. So in the end it boils down to dodge, attack once and dodge again.Items:The game has consumable items, in theory you could farm, stock up on them and face tank everything skyrim like it just isn´t worth the time and items feel worthless because you need multiple healing items to offset a single attack. It would have been better not to have them and get a rechargeable healing source.Some weapons are breakable and completely unecessary because they are often times weaker then your regular ones.For some reason you only have one equip slot for equipment even if one piece is a leather gaunlet and the other a pair of boots. Now it makes sense because most of the effects are powerful like +50% atk speed and a few other bonuses for one handed weapons but there are plenty of useless equipments too like floating in the air unable to move while doing an air attack.There are so many metroidvania games just play another better one even if this is by far not the worst one either.

_childDocuments_.review: First I gotta say that this game has a questionable power progression system that changes heavily based on player choice EX: You start the game with a low damage and meh attack speed that most enemies will straight up hit faster and stun lock you to death if you don't get the drop on them; now, you go from that to press 2 buttons and proceed to tank using your face while watching everything on screen dies and the change is either sudden or a slow power creep dependent on your choice which has a slight spoiler that I will mention near the end of this review.With that out of the way this game is very smart and it makes you feel smart. Every item has a purpose and exploration is rewarded handsomely. Items goes from basic RPG staples like extra damage and defense > to questionable if used alone > to kill everything without them touching you when combined > and up to self propelled demigod when used correctly EX: there are items that makes you immune to poison, doesn't do much alone but you can turn an entire body of water into a hazard that kills everything in it if you hit it with poison so..... equip the item, hit the water with poison and everything dies while leaving you unscathed. This is one of the many examples of the smart ways to fight that the game actively encourages you to do through seemingly brutal enemies encounters and there are many combinations of equipment, weapons and consumables that can be combined that turns a deadly encounter into a walk through the park and do not feel bad about using them as the game is quite generous with item drops. The enemies in this game have quite the variety in how they fight and what they are weak to, which make different areas feels unique and fresh. The bosses in this game are a hit or a miss since whether or not you explore and find items in the area can change the fight from darksouls level to kirby adventure so use your brain for the purpose of min-max cautiously to preserve the experience... I guess. There must be a better way to scale dynamic difficulty in my opinion though this game does it quite well compared to other games that have attempted it.Now for VERY IMPORTANT and VERY SLIGHT SPOILER and will DRASTICALLY increase your enjoyment of this game if you know about them so I recommend that you keep reading.At some point you will come across golden chests, these chests contain highly useful items that make the game's power progression feels drastically better and more fun to play BUT, right before you do the game will recommend that you do not open them while giving you vague reasons to do so. Here's the spoiler: the condition is that if you reach nearly the end of the game without opening a single golden chest, at which point the game will tell you that it is OK to open the chests now. After the grueling experience, you will be granted a "good ending" though to be honest all endings feels the same in terms of whether it makes you happy or sad, which is mostly happy-ish, though I would argue the "bad ending" feels better.So I recommend that you open every golden chest you can find and you will love this game as opposed to torturous beginnings, fun mid game and suddenly I'm playing Animal crossing with but with bloody ritual sacrifice with my enemies on the altar the end.TLDR: Fun. Niche because require brain usage, rewarding when brain is used, rewarding when explorations are made. OPEN EVERY GOLDEN CHEST. GG.

_childDocuments_.review: ThisGameIsGreat. Beautifully rendered out settings, sprite animations, pixel art is very high-calibur here. Some neat lighting makes it pop, too. Many difficulties. You get items to consume ( healing items typically heal X over Y amount of seconds ) so you need to plan accordingly. you can find weapons and magic, all wands , arrows, and grenades are limiteds use ( pay note of the amount you have left ) you can hold a few special items - like a school swimsuit that lets you move easily in water, and gives you some stat benefits ( also makes your character wear it, it's pretty damn cute ) The difficulty I chose is veteran - enemies kill me pretty swiftly, healing isnt easy to come by, and the boss was a masterpiece of learnign her patterns - you really gotta focus on that in this game if you chose a high difficulty. You embrace the game's mechanics - hunt out some weps, some magic - figure out a hidden item perhaps ( like the swimsuit I mentioned , optional to get and not in your path, you gotta backtrack for it )HUge map so far - writing is as good as it needs ot be, they aren't going for some deep philosophical mind bender plot. oh, and there's lots of cute anime girls and monster girls *so it's A+ materialgo buy it

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game!I remember being amazed by the pixel art from this in development a while back. I was surprised to have recently found that it was already out on Steam! The pixel art and 2D lighting look insanely impressive, and the gameplay does not do the art any injustices. 10/10 Game.First time playing through the game on the recommended difficulty took me like 8-9 hours, which unlocked a few other modes. One, 'Boss Mode', . Then, two that have you replay the game with some weapon restrictions; both of those were enjoyably difficult and taught two different strategies to overcome all of the challenges.After those runs I had most of the achievements and still really wanted to continue playing the game, so I decided to 100% it. The most daunting of the achievements was to complete the last mode 'Hardcore Mode' in which you have to beat the game start to finish without dying. I procrastinated that one until I had all the other achievements, but after I had done everything else, I knew the patterns for every boss and enemy, so though difficult if I died to something it was entirely my fault.After struggling through a Hardcore run thinking I was going to get my last 2 achievements I realized that one of the hidden achievements , so I had to do one more run through the game to finish off the last achievement.10/10 Game.  Art is good, Story is good, Gameplay is good, characters are good, there is a fair bit of replayablity, achievements are achievable, game is good.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a wonderfully animated anime-style pixelated metroidvania with a surprisingly elegant soundtrack that may feel short in the first run through, but provides replayability with it's numerous modes and endings to discover. Discovery is the name of the game here, as there are numerous characters to meet, weapons to find, and spells to learn.  It may not feel all that rewarding when it's all said and done, but it's impossible to deny that a lot of love went into this beautiful adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes my favorite "beat the game several times just to see all the endings"Well I did, and it was not worth it. Witch Mode was the only enjoyable run.24 hours to 100% the game which is including beating the save-wiping "hardcore" mode, which also generously gives you several items to cheat that mechanic.A single run is SIGNIFICANTLY shorter if you're not trying to be a 100% autismo like me.Calling this a metroidvania is like calling Euro Truck Simulator a racing game because both feature cars, Exploration is minimal, backtracking is only required if you want the gold chest items long after they stop being useful, and each one is pretty easily within teleporter reach anyway. 3 whole puzzles in the game one is "use chain lightning", the others being pushing anvils around.Magic is a joke, it's completely non-viable for more than half the game and in the latter half you just abuse invisibility to instakill things you don't like fighting. Fire is 90% of your damage, Chain Lightning the remainder. Ice spells have next to no use, Poison (and bleed by extention) is okay but misleading when used. Witch Mode makes this playstyle way more interesting as it turns a lot of garbage weapons into unconditional damage types so you can have electric oil puddles and flaming ice shots.Itemization is also a joke, half the accessories are straight worthless or detrimental, the others are just raw damage upgrades or REQUIRED just to make magic viable, most of which you don't get unless you open gold chests but this also instantly fails the questline related to it. By the time you reach the point where you're allowed to go back and open gold chests, you don't even need them anymore and may as well just continue on to kill the final boss.Weapons are... mostly a joke, you have basically two options:Yuri's wand for the entire latter portion of the game if you're trying to play a mageWhatever does the highest damage in a single swing of a favorable damage type, for the majority of a melee run this will be the Flame Sword, Thunder Hammer also gets some use. Shields will be your secondary weapon for the entire game because they are just that OP, block whatever and trade hits for free.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most frustrating games I've seen in recent years. It's not plain bad, because that would be easy - drop it and move on. But this game has a lot going for it - great visual style, a quirky but interesting story, and there's some good thought behind the part tactical, part arcade combat. However, the implementation of the combat is really trying one's patience - the laws of inertia apply to the player but not the enemies, dodge rolls sometimes avoid attacks and sometimes they don't, and it's quite easy to die from full HP to a two-bit mob at any part of the game. I was trying hard to put up with the shortcomings - but then about 50% progress, the game suddenly stopped providing new checkpoints, and that really did me in. The game became simply painful at that point. No.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I usually try to avoid negative reviews, but this time I can't simply let it go away. I don't recommend this game at all. You're probably attracted to the game because the character design, well, yes, it's well done. That's probably where the good things end.The combat is not good, your character is quite slow, this punishes you immensely at the beginning of the game when you have almost no weapons and magic, making it not a challenge, but a frustrating experience, which is the word that would describe this game overall: a frustrating experience.The soundtrack is just the same melody over and over, and if I listen to it for one more day I may go clinically insane, this paired with the extremely annoying high-pitch voice of the main character, and the frequent deaths can honestly ruin your gaming mood easily. Oh, and talking about the main character, is probably one of the worst in my 25 years of gaming experience, seriously guys... wth.And then there's the ending of the story that were two huge disappointments packed together. Hey, at least let me kill the b*tch, will you? To conclude, there are a lot of underrated indie gems that must be played, but there are also ones that are not even worth playing. This game taught me to be more selective now. If you're going to play this game I seriously recommend you to try that easiest difficulty first (which I never tried, but at this point it can only help this mess). If you're a developer reading this I apologize for the harsh review, but please know it was an honest one. A game should have a feeling of progression in both gameplay mechanics and difficulty, just putting a message at the beginning warning that it's a survival experience is not enough guys... have a blessed day.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent 2D dungeon crawler but I think some people over-look the "crawler" aspect of it.It's not a fast paced game and it tells you that right away, but think of it like Demon Souls first came out on the PS3; it was slow, methodical, and brutal and 'Lost Ruins' does the same.The graphics are fun without being too distracting nor is it trying too hard which makes for an enjoyable world to explore filled with interesting characters and enemies.One of my favorite aspects of this one is the environmental interactions. There were times when I was trying new strategies on bosses and enemies only to light myself on fire, freeze myself while half submerged in water, shocked to death, and none of them felt cheap because I brought it on myself and could have been avoided if I paid more attention.Give it a shot; I think its a fantastic game. It's some-what difficult, but not the hardest game out there and gives a great feeling of satisfaction as you progress through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game so far, playing on Hardcore for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles and man is it a kick in the balls. I don't understand the gripes against the slow attack speed some other reviews talked about considering one of the very first equips you get from the shop increases weapon attack speed by one.The shield is probably my favorite "weapon" doing hardmode though I wish it was an equip rather than a weapon that would maybe give a chance to negate melee damage taken, but that's fine and the Zweihander is a godsend for cheesing some enemies.Gold seems like a fairly uncommon drop so farming it is a chore, but considering some enemies are very, very generous with drops that recover flat HP or HP overtime makes it a non-issue to me.I'll update this review when I've gotten farther into it, but I really do enjoy the challenge of Hardmode. The behelit is a nice touch.Edit: Finally beat the game on Hard Mode, game becomes a little easy once you progress far enough to get a lot of the REALLY good item combinations, but it was still a really enjoyable game, the ending was expected; but I still greatly enjoyed it especially getting the reincarnation ending.I absolutely recommend this game, the start is a little rough due to melee speed, but once you learn to dodge properly and find better equipment you will find the game is much more enjoyable with the various item combinations.Final boss needs a buff though.

_childDocuments_.review: . Art is very good, map design ain't bad either, the graphics: color me impressed, they're well carely done, they even made shadows / light casts that change depending your height position / water surface reflections for a pixelart platform as this, minor details that... are rare and nice to see.   Oh man, I was UFF, this game punishes you! I was about to uninstall it and leave a bad review when I had like 10h of game but the game just wants you to keep going. It is hard, but why is it hard? Because everything is faster than you, the enemy reaction time is faster than your fastest attacks but there's a flaw, a horrible flaw that I felt poorly unbalanced... And would be the debuffs. Most all of enemies put debuffs such as poison / bleed / freeze. They do incredible damage, take long to go away and / or if you're playing on veteran + , these stack, meaning this, one blow will kill you on time if you do not constant spam heals. It does feel cheap.  HOWEVER!, once you understand that the game is made under this unfair conditions but at the same time you have so many weapons / trinkets at your disposal, you start to get the hand of it. The game makes you repeat a lot , you'll die a lot. It IS frustrating i'll tell you that.  Once you finish the game (I started on Veteran and finished it with the good ending) it will unlock new game variants and trust me, these are new fully experiences that remind me the games back then PsOne era. Too much to do, too much to try and feels nice to start a new game on any of these new modes.

_childDocuments_.review: Sidescrolling RPG with survival mechanics. I only recommend if you want to play hardcore mode with a limit on lives. Normal play would be better if it had limited saves like Resident Evil. Unlimited saving significantly lessens the survival aspect.Gameplay has good amount of interacting mechanics, abilities/items, and enemies. Story is charming but short, just like the game's length.If the game were longer it would be a highly recommend. Still a very good game and doesn't have any pretentious ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen some reviews outside steam stating how bad this game is. Is the game bad? no. Is the game good? not exactly. I would argue that the game is a good value at about $13 not worth $20.The gameplay is very choppy, lacks animation, and smoothness. Its not bad, but its like playing a Flash game. (I personally dont mind but it does show the value of the game). as a example look a the trailer from (0:37-0:41). Difficulty is okay as long as you know how to cheat the bots. There was a difficult boss and all I did was use a shield and wait. Items, and requirements will appear on your map which destroys the purpose of wondering around although it is still fun to explore and find ways to open chests.I love the way the game makes you think critically in order to solve problems and mysteries.It constantly puts you in a simple but effective system where you need to use either bows, magic, items to open doors, gates, or defend against enemies. The story is simple, you get  items that are useful and YOU HAVE TO use items carefully or else youll run out and live in hell. I do have to say, items are hard to navigate on your item slots, especially if you have lots of them. they are not sorted by Elements (fire, ice, electric, magic, physical) rather they are sorted by Favorites, Alphabetical, and by the recency of Item.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun to play and just kind of charming in general.Some people apparently don't like the combat much -- I thought it was great. I'm kind of old and slow and not that great at execution-heavy games, and this one just about hit the sweet spot for me. Just be a little patient, equip the right accessories, and you're good to go. Speaking of which, I really liked that the accessories were pretty powerful and synergise well too. It's not like dark souls (or other online AAA titles), where they have to nerf everything into the ground when people find fun combinations.Fair warning that the game is pretty short (could probably beat it in a few hours without issue). My playtime is from trying to get the achievements and different endings -- like I said, it's just fun to play.Also fair warning that you can find a school swimsuit to wear and the bosses have boob animations. If you don't think a game can be charming and also have those things, this is probably not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard difficulty is actually hard.  Although, what makes the game really hard is that, when you're jumping forward, if you attack, you stop moving forward mid-air.  This means you can't just jump at enemies to attack them before they get a chance to do anything.  It's annoying to get used to, but from a gameplay standpoint it makes sense because jump attacks are kinda cheesy.  You can still sorta do them, you just have to jump closer to the enemy and begin the attack when right above them.Graphics are good.  Playtime is long enough.  The Boss mode you unlock is not the usual boss rush, but actually replaying the game with 3 different boss characters that you can alternate between at will, there's new dialogue, and some things have changed.  I haven't tried the other unlocked modes, but based on the Boss mode they're more than some lazy attempt to squeeze more content out of the game.  Don't sleep on those other game modes.

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard to recommend this game because although there are not many good metroidvanias out there, this is almost not worth it. This game is extremely frustrating. The difficulty does not gradually increase or jump up and stay consistent. Some parts are just stupidly hard for no good reason.You don't level up. So you never do more damage unless you find better weapons. And you always take crazy amounts of damage unless you find an item that defends against ONE type of attack. Even then the other attack modifiers will easily kill you.The worst is that you have no i-frames when you get hit. This makes it so that even early game enemies can combo you to death if they hit you right and there is nothing you can do about it.For an endurance souls-like metroidvania there is almost no way to restore health. Save areas don't heal you. Health drops are infrequent or rare. You have to resort to cheesing two or three item abilities you find in the early game to heal yourself. It makes the whole exploration process unnecessarily slow and tedious.You often will need to buy items to have a fighting chance or even progress in questlines that give you much needed items. However, money drops are rare. And enemies don't respawn when you just go to an adjacent room and come back. When they do drop money it is only 1-5 gold. Every useful item you need to buy costs 90-240 gold. This makes the mandatory grinding suck.At least the character art is nice and the dialogue is a little funny. But due to the above mentioned problems, this game is hard to enjoy.---I went back and played 30 hours of this game to 100% it. My previous criticisms haven't changed much. I appreciate the care put into the game and all the extra modes. The heroine has different outfits. The dialgue changes based on the mode you are playing. And there is a hidden after-story. But in a way, those extra modes only confirm the previous problems of the game. The only way to win at combat is to cheese and abuse items/magic. When you figure out the trick combinations, you can blaze through anything. But it must be those combinations, otherwise it is like you hit a brick wall.A boss can be made trivial by simply jumping in one spot to dodge and using a projectile over and over again. Another will be made into a joke by simply using an AOE spell and running circles around her. That same boss will kill you in literally 3 seconds if you try any other approach because you still have no i-frames, she has no cool-down between attacks, and her status aliments stack. The combat system in this game is horribly unbalanced. You either find the cheese and it is really fun, or it is just grueling and you want nothing more than to play something else. It is not souls-like, just poor design.At least the bosses are cute. If you have a thing for giantesses, then you will get something out of this game there.This game is so close to being a great metroidvania, but the exploit-based combat just isn't that fun. Maybe pick this game up, maybe not. It can be really really frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: For a small team of devs I must say the game is quite fun. It is short but there is some replayability.THE STORY:The story is pretty straight forward with some twist and turns here and there which gives is a vague dark souls feeling because nothing is directly told to you and exposition so its fun trying to guess who the big bad is even if its nothing new its refreshing to say the least.THE ART:The art style is fun and animated very well. I have no issue with the over-sized pixels as it is more likely an art decision and not a limitation of the dev team. I've seen art styles where the characters have no faces so big pixels should not make or break how the game feels. Its all subjective so if big pixels bother you don't buy it.With that being said, the big bosses look awesome and are animated gorgeously.THE GAME PLAY:There is a learning curve here as to say the game wants you to learn how to play it not apply what you have learned from other platform games like it. The jumping, attacking, dodging, and hit boxes are essentially pixel perfect but they also have what Id like to call real weight to them. You are playing as a girl that is NOT a super hero, so she cant jump really high or dodge at super high speeds, her muscles are puny so swinging weapons would be cumbersome and there for by default clunky. Smaller weapons feel more natural and allow for better movement between attacks. Since your movement does not really allow for you to correct mistakes instantly you have to think about how you approach certain situations and what best weapons for the enemies present. The game wants you to think instead of mindlessly cutting through enemies with no regard to the gameplay at all. The gameplay is thoughtful.OVERALL:LOST RUINS is in my opinion a solid game, is it worth 20 dollars...Im not sure. The game is complete but short. There are some other modes that essentially add some additional hours to the experience but not truly any new content. However its a fun experiment i think. The small dev team did a good job capturing this particular genre of game and Im happy I picked it up. Hope to see more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews mention the combat being "clunky". Maybe this is just me, but I love Dark Souls 1, with its deliberate, methodical combat. Many would say it is much more clunky than its next installments. But I'd attribute it to a difference in design.This is more of an RPG for sure, and not a metroidvania. You don't really unlock any new movement mechanics, but more spells and items to broaden the combat playspace. The progression is fairly linear, though you do have forks that let you choose which area you tackle next.I'd give the game a try. I'm looking forward to an expansion of the systems-driven gameplay presented here.

_childDocuments_.review: A short metriodvania that delivers on what it sells: a hard side-scrolling dungeon-crawler with cute(ish) monster girls of varying attitudes. It's okay, I am not a fan of the mix of artwork and not a pure focus on sprite-artwork.While not the best sprite-work I have seen, it is certainly of high quality! It has the Shantae-issue of hip-shaking and nearly everything dressed in a school-girl's uniform. The music is there and it works to help the mood of each area in the game.This game is hard, and this difficulty comes from enemy damage along with a limited kit at the start of the game. As you explore and overcome, you gain various means to make combat easier along with managing damage and magic point scores.Unfortunately, this is where the Metriodvania qualities end as you gain no extra movement tools, and optional paths to loot either take dynamite(or a fireball spell), or a weapon/spell with long reach (Chain Lightning). Traveling the world is made very simple with a teleport system. The real challenges come from boss fights, but depending on your kit can also be made trivial.There is a very simple story here, with creepy implications later on. However, it loses marks from the extra artwork and dialogues you have with various monster girls through-out the game. There is plenty of environmental story-telling just from the sprite-work, but that is lost the farther along you get in the game. The dialogue takes away from the story by explaining the story, which ruins any interest in trying to figure things out yourself. I would have liked it a lot more if the story was told via exploring and looking around, rather than some anime cut-scene girl being glib and just explaining things.I like Metriodvanias, and a good challenge. I disliked the conversation artwork, and the lean on cheesecake character design. Tits have a habit of tarnishing something that was otherwise pretty good. Not to say that this is a bad game, nor a game to be taken super seriously, but it sadly does not marry its over-the-top presentation with its design completely.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the metroid-vania style of game, and I am a big fan of souls-like style games as well.Unfortunately this game is not it. I understand that this game was meant to be punishing, but more then the game being punishing, it just feels bad to play. The combat is slow on clunky. Your swings are attacks are not only slow, even with a "faster" weapon, the attack animation locks you in place for a few frames before and after your swing. This makes it so you will be unable to use your dodge for longer periods of time to let the enemies just hit you. The timing of your attacks and slows take a bit of time to initiate, slightly delaying everything you try to do and messing up your timing. A huge example of when you try to do an attack while in the air. It does not trigger until you are already back on the ground. As much as I would like to call this an oversight that be patched, it is an intended feature - based on an item that locks you in place in the air for an attack. Don't get me wrong, you could just buy a bunch of magic rods and spam cast your way through some areas, or even just ignore a lot of the enemies all together, and that is another problem I have. There is no incentive to kill anything. You are punished, whether you mess up or not, the combat is slow and feels terrible, the hit boxes are inconsistent - at times hitting you even in your dodge, the dodge is short, slow and inconsistent, and there is no reason to really kill most of the enemies.There are much better games to play in these genres, so I cannot recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 hours and got 100% achievement in this game, gotta say, this game is really fun but also kinna wasted some potentials for improvement.I love the pixel art style in this game, the character are cute af.The story is fine, nothing too special or bad either, it just doesn't have enough story for other characters in game, especially their past and future (yes, I do read all the journals in the game, I just feel they didn't tell enough). I wish the dev can expand more with the story and many other characters so the player can feel attach to them more, not just appear 1 time and then just never appeared again.The gameplay is really fun and easy to adapt, but when you get to half way of the game, you can just stick with some items that can help you pass the game with ease, even in Hardcore mode. And yes, this game is really short.The OSTs... Wdym this game has OSTs???Over all, this game suits my taste in pixel graphics, metridvania and platformer, but lack of OSTs and storywise of characters. I still recommend to pick this game up and try yourself to train your reflex, or maybe speedrun it.My rating: 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a pretty darn good metroidvania with focus on exploration and using your items/spells/consumables to your advantage. Game is also rather hard and you most likely will need some time to get used to it.Combat is slow and methodical, which can be bad for players that are used to lightning fast combat from other games in the same genre, but I personally very much enjoyed it, despite loving fast games. Your creativity is often rewarded and there is bunch of things that are borderline OP, but that's what makes it fun. Map size is decent, the game is a bit on shorter side tho. I was able to beat it in 6 hours on Veteran. Played the game once again for true ending, which took me like 4 hours. Story is... it's here, I guess. It has some cute moments, some dark moments. Some really dark moments too. Nothing that will keep me awake at night, but it's good enough.OST is alright. Some good tracks, some average tracks. Liked OST of the last area, very chill and melancholic.Art style I absolutely adore, it's great. You can unlock bunch of artworks for gallery mode and I must say, they are fantastic. Game is looking pretty cool in general, lighting system is fantastic.There is also bunch of custom modes, including boss rush mode, where you can play as 3 bosses in one character. Seems pretty fun, tried for a bit, can see myself getting back to the game later to complete it. Overall good package for its price, very much recommend to anyone looking for a challenging metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: A neat and slower paced Metroidvania with some genuinely gorgeous scenery and cute designs, and a lack of unlockable movement items that's present in most Metroidvania games that makes the exploration feel like you're always on the move. I ended up getting used to the lack of momentum in combat compared to similar games and the fact that you had to commit to every strike, felt like the cards were on the table right from the start in that regard.My biggest gripe was how intrusive the inventory management ended up being, switching weapons and accessories around felt like it took up more time than actually fighting at times, something that sticks out even more on the higher difficulties where a single trap can take away almost all your hp. Avoiding inventory management becomes its own gameplay mechanic in a weird way, and you learn that you don't always need to change your synergetic items around to adapt to a situation, but still an issue that could be fixed with something like an item wheel.That being said, the game is a fun challenge and feels like that kind of unpolished gem that's unique enough to give it its own charm despite its shortcomings, and I'll happily play through each mode available until there's nothing left to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Since there's no neutral option between a Negative and a Positive review i'll stick with a Positive one because even with some flaws here and there, overall this game was still a fun experience at the end of the day.So here are some problems from the top of my head that makes me not have loved playing this as much as i wanted to:First, here's the biggest problem of them all, the constant need to open the inventory menu every 10 seconds as you end up needing a different type of weapon in order to fight an specific enemy that's unfair or too hard with your previous set.Second, with the help of the previous problem, the dull combat gets highlighted further as you start to notice the tiresome pattern of opening your inventory, searching for a specific weapon in a mess of an order, dodge the enemy attack, kill them and then in the next enemy repeat the process, including switching weapons.Third, this is kinda underwhelming in my opinion, but the resources of this game are actually LIMITED, you'll get off a boss fight or a difficult corridor section and you'll reach a save point and feel safer until you realize that your HP and you MP don't recharge for free at all, never, the only way to recover basic resources is by either using weapons that heal you or buying potions, which takes us to the problem that you'll interact with a vendor and notice that you can only buy from him 20 bombs or something and then never anymore, it's gone, if you waste every dynamite in the game, then that's it.There are some other minor things that you can choose to nitpick in this game, but honestly i'm fine with the rest, and even with these problems i've stated, i've had fun and seeing the endings and the entire journey made me happy to have played it to begin with, it's a cool game to play if you like it's type, there's some very nice music tracks here and there, mostly to the ending parts, and the biggest seller of the game is definitly it's BEAUTIFUL pixel art mixed with some modern lighting and other post-processing VFX, just don't expect TOO much of the game and you'll enjoy it, that's all.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by a landslide THE MOST CLUNKY platformer I've EVER played!The combat system needs A LOT of work.- Weapon swings are stupidly slow. I actually cringed when I first picked up the gladius and tried it out. If you give a real life mace to a 7 year old, he's gonna swing it faster than the MC of this game swings a freaking gladius (which is designed for quick stabs btw, note to the devs).- For some bizarre reason, the devs decided that when somebody extends their arm forward whilst jumping forward, all of their momentum from the jump magically disappears and you drop down like a rock...Other than that, the game throws A LOT of cheap shots at you. For example: you're being conditioned to believe that your shield can block anything, including axe swings from orcs 10 times your size, or even explosive projectiles. Then there's that one random boss that damages you if you try to block it (which is a one-shot on veteran)...Then there's the bosses... The design is pretty cool and the fights are entertaining, but a lot of them are very cheap and unnecessarily long. The ice boss for example: you triggered it, see the blizzard, cool effects and everything, then you get ready to fight it, but oh wait, you get insta hit if you didn't instantly jump on a platform after you regained control.There are a lot of examples of such cheap shots. They're cheap shots because you're usually only going to get screwed over by them once.Then there's the hitboxes... oh boy... suffice to say, they need A LOT of work. Often times you will stab an enemy, with your weapon literally overlapping the enemy, but no wait, the game decided you didn't actually hit it and proceeds to hit you instead. Then there are hits that land half a meter away from you, that still bizarrely hit you.There's also the fact that they decided that the autosave shrines can't be re-triggered, so if it's right before a boss, enjoy having to keep switching your equipment around after every death, because there's no way to save again at the autosave shrines...EDIT:Beat the game, oh boy, does the game go downhill for the last quarter of the game. It seems like enemies are just being thrown at you in the cheapest ways possible just to slow you down as much as possible. You will end up just ignoring them and run past them, which will make things 95% easier. This last bit of the game was BY FAR just tedium and not enjoyable at all.The second to last boss is kind of broken (Kana), her attack hits you before the animation actually shows a slash, and her dash attack makes her invulnerable even a second after it's been finished.Usually in a game like this, when the boss uses a strong attack, it leaves them open for punishment, and Kana certainly shows that, what with the boss standing with her back towards you for like a second after the dash. But nope, she's invulnerable during that time.The boss before that (the spider archer), you just literally have to put a small rock on the button you assigned your shield to, and you will win the fight lol.The last boss was the most disappointing one so far. Very anticlimactic final boss, it relies exclusively on cheap gimmicks (summoning other enemies that heal her).EDIT2:Beat the boss mode, now this actually breathes new life into the game. A lot of the items you were used to in the normal run are now either "armors" or passives with different effects.The overwhelming clunk of the game still makes combat hell, but at least it's more interesting.All in all I'd give it a 6/10 until they fix the clunk.

_childDocuments_.review: A polished metroidvania which rewards caution and experimentation. Caters visually to the anime crowd but should appeal to a broader demographic of players thanks to polished mechanics, varid gameplay and high replay-ability.+ A good variety of different weapons, spells and equipment allowing for diverse builds and playstyles.+ Pixelated characters and vibrant particle effects come together to form an interesting visual style.+ Upon first clear, unlocks different gamemodes with new powers and limiters, further incentivising repeat playthroughs.+ Has a sense of humour and doesn't take itself too seriously. References other media without being obnoxious about it.+ Puzzles and platforming gives breathing room inbetween battles and helps keep the game fresh for longer.+ Map is on the smaller side, but shortcuts and secrets makes exploration rewarding.- Winged boots feel like they should've been part of the base mechanics and not an optional item.- Lots of menuing required for optimal play, switching between equipment constantly gets tiring.- Consumables are scarce early but become trivial later on, taking away from some of the challenge.- Assassin mode is a big let-down compared to the other modes.= Lots of suggestively depicted pixelated enemies, everything from slimes to harpies. May put some off.= Makes use of both sarcastic and dark humour. Some may find the dialogue hilarious, others unappealing.= Difficulty is high, at least for the first playthrough. Death is always near and caution is required.= Some bosses can be cheesed using clever tactics and/or item usage as an alternative to pure skill.= Crits are guaranteed from backstabs and not a random chance on any attack. Don't think it's explained in-game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off don't take any review seriously unless they've cleared it since they really have no idea what they're talking about. The first hour of the game doesn't present the entire picture. I cleared this in one go and got the 2nd ending as my first ending. Great game, amazing graphics and lighting effects. The difficulty is a bit inconsistent and sometimes certain later encounters are easier than earlier one but that might simply be due to the number of options you get in the game. Speaking of options, there's tons of loadouts and types of builds (predominantly bleed + hp regen, poison stacking, or glass cannon mage) and it made me switch equipment so often that I wish there were loadout options in the game since I'd be menuing so often. You could be changing gear every time you encounter specific enemies. Either way I had a lot of fun exploring and discovering new ways to reuse existing pieces of gear once new artifacts and equipment became available and allowed older equipment to shine. Speaking of exploration, this game is labeled as a metroidvania and while you can revisit older areas, there's no reason to do so because unlike other metroidvanias you do not unlock any movement or traversal abilities and everything can be obtained with everything the main character comes with. My personal complaint about the game is that magic is too inaccessible until the very end of the game unless you rely heavily on mana regenerating items which requires even more menuing. It's not until halfway though the game until you find your first piece of mana regenerating equipment (much earlier if you want to get the first ending). I also found that money drops way too infrequently (it's actually way too time consuming to "farm" gold) which makes purchasing consumables not worth it at all so you will want to save consumables for later encounters when it gets very difficult to avoid some boss attacks. There's also a sidequest in the game which involves acquiring some magic spells which will cost you a lot of gold so more useful purchases will be placed on the backburner because it'll set you back quite a bit. Some people have complained about the clunky attack animations and I can agree to some extent. Many weapons are considered "fast" but most enemies will frame trap you between their own attack intervals unless you go with "faster" or "fastest" attack speeds. Dropping straight down like a rock while performing a mid air attack is kind of annoying as well. As far as boss encounters go they are all difficult in their own right except for the last boss. Some bosses will destroy you so easily I had to rely on very specific setups in order to beat them asap.Post game content is also quite good if you want to replay the game. There are a couple extra modes like playing with specific loadouts and even playing as certain bosses which allows for unique game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Another Metroidvania game, although this one is more of a Meroidvania-lite game. Unlike others it is shorter with smaller maps with less power-ups needed to collect everything, at most you'd just need to buy a spell or two in order to unlock certain things without much backtracking needed.:The pixel art and animation is beautiful. Everything just flows to well and doesn't really hide itself in the background. The most important animations look quite gorgeous with all that extra care given to them.With it being metroidvania-lite the backtracking really is cut down, at most you barely have to go back to get other items be it for yourself or quest items for others. A lot of the times you just need to take the long way around or just need one certain spell.A lot of different weapons and accessories to make your own build as the game goes on, able to change it up as you grab new stuff to see what you find the most fitting.Beating the game once unlocks other game modes to spice up new playthroughs, all three of them varied in a way with one of them having a huge variance compared to the other two as it even has a bunch of new dialogue.:This depends more on how much you want to play this game, because it is short. One playthrough on average would take about two hours. Even 100%ing would not take that long if you don't idle, or do stupid things like me.Quests are kinda forced upon you, along with returning the reward. Should you bump into the character that gave you the quest, you'll be forced to give up the item even if you wanted it. There's also one questline that's the same thing three times and it just begs the question of why. He isn't even that important of a character, he is just kinda there.Combat first time around feels stiff, it takes time to adjust to it because your character swings it like they know how to fight, but don't have the stats to wield that weapon, and there is no leveling to fix this.Story is.. there. It exists, it isn't terrible, but I could of had the same experience with the game if it didn't exist. I'd say just experience the dialogue once if you want since it isn't very long, otherwise just skip through.:Dodge rolling is pretty weak in this game, aside from a select few moments, it often just puts you in a tough spot. The enemy is either ready to attack again when you just get back up or you rolled too much and were too far away for a counterattack. A lot of the time it is better to just jump around the enemy to hit them.Fighting enemies is pointless. This game has no leveling system and since only a few enemies have a guaranteed droprate of one item. The money they drop is pitiful and a lot of the loot they can drop is also pitiful. They can just drop nothing most of the time. So it is just better to not fight anything that isn't in the way or a boss.Overall it was a pretty nice experience. Really enjoyed the different game modes, especially the big one. Though I hope the next game these guys work on improves the system when it comes to combat, at least giving some reason to fight the random enemies, Also this game has the best Mimic design I've seen in a good while.

_childDocuments_.review: A Castlevania like game with waifus galore. You play as an amnesiac school girl that needs to get back to where she belongs. You will kill other school girls turned monsters that have lost the ability to reason. This give the game it's unique art design where there's a staggering amount of enemies you can get out of just that simple concept. That's all I'm going to say on the story because as short as the game is it is worth finding out everything yourself. The combats not much to write about. The standard Castlevania combat you know and love is here with armor and magic to add some variety to things. The game has several different modes to try after your first run. My favorite of which let's you play as the Boss'. While each run will only be about 3 to 5 hours it's still a fun game that's feels like it's worth $10 for the novelty of it.
