_childDocuments_.review: Oof, Lost Ruins is a Game alright.But in my opinion not a good one.This Game is kind of a Metroidvania Light with (badly implemented) Souls and "Survival" Elements and it just isn't fun, actually it is a frustrating mess.I can forgive that a little bit because after seeing the Credits, I think only 2 people really worked on it (disregarding the Localization Teams here) but if a Game is bad, it's bad.So the first thing you will notice is the extremely annoying sound the "Character Talk Box" makes. This is the first impression. Then you will notice good Pixel Art. It is just that, good, not the best ever but it kinda has it's own chunky style.The next thing I personally noticed was extremely annoying. I played with a Gamepad, but when I switched to my Keyboard (for opening the Steam Overlay or for going to Desktop) the displayed controls in Game would switch constantly (!) between Gamepad and Keyboard and the only solution is to restart the Game and also: NEVER touch your Keyboard while playing.Second thing I disliked (I at first thought the Game was buggy) was when an Achievement Notification would pop up but basically it only tells you, that you have fulfilled one step to get the full Achievement. Found it kind of annoying and also useless.The Music was also kind of meh. More bad than good. More annoying than hooking me. (You see where this is going? There is so much ANNOYING stuff here and that's not all, the worst things I will tell you about next.)I think this Game does not know what it wants to be, this is a perfect example of an identity crisis. - The Game has Souls Elements with slow and "deliberate" combat but it just feels clunky as hell. The Controls don't feel good. Then there are the enemies. Oh boy is this one frustrating Game. Normal enemies can be a pain to kill. I played most of the Game with a Zweihänder (yes, you write it like that) and the enemies are just unfair. The Zweihänder is VERY slow and in the time you attack, most enemies still have longer reach than you and can SPAM their attacks like CRAZY without ever stopping. Of course you are free to use other Weapons/Ranged Weapons/Spells, but everything feels kind of bad here.Then there are the bosses which are laughably easy. Every Boss has 2-3 Phases (Normal Phase, Big B**b Phase and sometimes a "funny" Phase were you can just kill them easily) and most of them have only 3-4 Attack Patterns which are extremely easy to counter. Also they take a ton of Damage and are down real quick.- Then there is the Metroidvania Element but the Game fails here as well. There is no real progression (apart from getting a LITTLE more health or getting new Items for new "Builds") here. No Double Jumps, no Dashes, no nothing. The Level Design is also extremely BORING and lazy. There are almost NO secrets to find and no branching paths and backtracking is also rarely if not ever needed. Basically you start on the left side, then go right aaaaall the way, then go up after a boss, go left aaaall the way, go up, go right and so on. This is the basic design here with VERY few variations (sometimes you go down also...).Platforming when it happens: Also bad. Either you are in a very small space and bump your head or you are outside and jump on a few platforms, it's not really needed here but also not very well implemented.I read some of the positive and some of the negative reviews on here and I actually agree with most of the negative reviews. Another thing: Savepoints and Checkpoints don't restore your health/mana, you have to consume items for that or just play like I did with a ton of regen-Gear.Storywise it's stupid. So is the dialogue. Just wow, what is that even? Can't and don't want to describe this.(And what's with all the big b**bs on the bosses?)Well, my first playthrough took 5.9 hours, only got 12/40 Achievements. In good Games/Metroidvanias/Soulslikes I would want to jump back in to get more Achievements and to see a different ending. Not here. I am just glad it is over. Especially because for some Achievements you have to torture yourself through the whole Game again, grind/farm a lot and/or play different Game Modes.I literally have 0 interest in that.So yeah, if you are a REALLY REALLY big fan of Metroidvanias/Souls-Adjacent Games and you need to play everything, MAYBE you will get a kick out of this, for everyone else who just wants a good Game: Stay Away!

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review I have beaten the game once without checking out any of the extra modes. I played the game on the recommended difficulty.The game is a well designed platformer offering a fairly linear experience. If you are hoping for a metroidvania that requires a lot of backtracking to look for secrets, look elsewhere. You can get most collectables as soon as you see them, any you can't usually revolve coming in from another screen.Combat feels mostly fine but it's not very well balanced. Early game some mobs can combo you to instantly kill you, but every boss felt like a joke to me. There is one boss I beat by standing in the corner holding down one button. The biggest strength of the game is the variety of weapons and other equipment. There are quite a few different weapons to choose from and I was regularly swapping around.The swapping sort of becomes an cumbersome though, the game feels as if it wants you to swap but the only way to do that is by pausing and changing gear. You get a lot of gear and some things are fairly situational. It can become hard to find what you want to use at times, the game could have definitely used a way to save loadouts or maybe let you favorite items.Finally for better and worse this is a very anime game. For no reason, lore or otherwise, some of your upgrades are just women's underwear with less than tasteful flavor text. I don't know why the +1 inventory slot upgrade had to be panties but it is. I know this kind of "fan service" can turn people off so I felt it was worth mentioning.I had fun playing the game, would play again. If you like the look of the trailers I think they do a good job of capturing the feel of the game. If you want an anime styled metroidvania platformer I would recommend Rabi-Ribi over this but the game was fun and I don't think I wasted my money.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This game's contains lewd enemies and boss characters designs, but is completely safe!This is very fun Dark Souls Metroidvania with a slow learning path with mechanics. You will die many of times learning how each monster attacks and learning the different stages in a boss fight. There are many different weapons, spells, items and equipment to combine that will help your with different areas in the game and for different types of gameplay.The only downside is you should save frequently for you cannot re-activate checkpoints to save recent activity, making you reset some progress that can be a little annoying, or needing to change equipment every time you respawn. A word of advice, start using your stat boosting items more often for a more fun experience. And If you want the true good ending, you have to play on veteran.This is the most fun I had with a precision style platformer, almost as much as Metroid Dread. This game took me 8 hours to complete on normal mode and there are post game content with different modes for achievement hunters, including post story for some of the boss characters. There's a lot of content if you're willing to put the effort into it and if you enjoy the gameplay.- 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Its not terrible but yeah it gets a lot wrong. Combat is awful, as you attack way too slowly and stiff compared to other enemies, you stop when attacking in the air, and almost every attack has a stupid status effect. The gear system is awful, as you don't really get new powerful gear from chests. Theres like 2-3 tiers of damage throughout the game and all weapons just change what type of damage they do. The same goes with items that you wear, that also don't allow you to equip to specific body parts they all just take up the same slot. So have fun going to the menu and swapping out equipment every 1-3 minutes, which is so much fun because we all play action games to spend 1/3 the time on the menu. Its clunky and you basically need to look up on boss fights what equipment is best to damage and limit their damage, which is the worst part of most MMO games and has no place here. You can choose different weapons but again it all is based on the damage type, and most of the slower ones are way too slow since you already attack slowly so it makes them almost impossible to use. Its not a true metroidvania although there are some secrets and some backtracking but its mostly linear and theres a lot of portals. It is stupid how you dont recharge mana and health at checkpoints/save points unlike every other souls game ever, which makes healing and getting mana a chore. Some of the boss fights are decent. The story is meh, mostly just weebo/boobah girl sh!t I didn't care about. The game is functional but its difficult for all the wrong reasons due to bad combat, bad weapons/equipment systems. But you could do worse I guess. 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game that plays equal parts as a puzzle and as a dungeon crawler. The main character is a school girl that plays exactly as you'd imagine one would in a world filled with monsters: weak and frail. Even the simple act of swiping your sword feels sluggish. Your first impression might be that the game is hard or unfair - and if you come looking only for an action platformer, then indeed it will be.The genius of this game comes from actually understanding the rules of its world and how the multitude of items you find interact with it. Once you get into that mindset and start experimenting, it quickly becomes obvious that there are simple and effective solutions for most things the game throws at you.The main story itself is short (5h-6h if you explore thoroughly), but once you complete it, there's a bunch of new game modes that unlock. Since doing a full run once you know what to expect is very fast (2-3h), these extra game modes provide interesting replayability. While the world and the bosses stay the same, the way the main character plays changes and so you again need to adapt.The pixel-art waifu bosses are kinda cool. The music is meh. The gameplay is definitely interesting once you learn the rules. All in all, I'd recommeng this title if you enjoy puzzles as much as combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: It is a slow, more methodical game. Yes you can just equip a weapon and trade blows but more than likely the game will hand your behind to you. It rewards being creative , like in the sewers the slime will trash you with ease but find the right item and you can electrocute while being immune yourself. If you are having trouble with a boss explore and you will find an item that will( if used correctly) make the boss fights easier. This game has quite a few different modes that change gameplay, from playing as bosses, to a rogue backstab style and even a mage run. These modes come with unique items that change how you play completely!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is fun, short, and morbidly cute. It has good combat that relies on game sense and precise timing... or extreme abuse of overpowered item combinations you'll eventually find. Early game can be punishing while figuring things out, but they give plenty of save and respawn points. This means you're never set too far back after you die from poisoning the water you're standing in. Again. Good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really play Metroidvanias but I really liked Lost Ruins. The combat system had a lot more depth than I expected and is completely loadout based. The items, spells, and weapons you equip at any given time define your battle style and can be freely changed between, even mid-battle. That last part does lead into a lot of menuing and switching between items to regen your MP/HP and respond to situations as they come up, which is my biggest gripe in regards to the game, as it slows down things a lot. Maybe hotkeys or the ability to create preset loadouts could help, but that still encourages switching loadouts extremely often, which may not have been the developers' intention. _childDocuments_.review: Ssometimes simplicity is what we need when it comes to our game mechanics. Though, we should not misinterpret simple for easy in all senses. After going through several suggested Metroidvania list I found this title would keep popping up as a must play in the genre. I saw that it was a short title so figured, to give it a try and see what all the fuss was with it. The game has an intriguing narrative if not honestly predictable from the start. It also plants may seeds of doubt in the player. Why I am doing this? Are they really bad? If you go through and collect the notes in the world and read the dialogue of the bosses and NPCs you encounter you will see that not everyone is who they are portrayed as. The gameplay is simple in you, have a weapon and some items and a couple of magic abilities. You rotate through and use them for environmental puzzle solving and combat. However for a Metroidvania the combat can be challenging at the recommended difficulty. Even the lowest of enemies can kill you in a few hits. You constantly will be going to your menu to find the item that will counter a condition you have so you don't die if poison or bleeding because you are losing a point per second and you only have 10 health and 20 points of bleeding. This simple but complex system feels like it can easily take you out of the game since you are constantly scrolling through menus in the middle of a fight. The game also seems to mess with you as you go, at least on Steam. After I beat the first boss, the achievement popped up "defeat every boss" but when I checked it wasn't completed yet. So instead it seems to be counting as you go to keep you guessing how close to the end you are. After finishing I can see that there multiple endings and new ways to experience the game. I probably won't play again since ai typically do not go for the other endings in these titles, but it's a nice touch as a single run can go about 5-7 hours depending how long boss fights take you. Overall it was a fun game, with some twist that made the game play feel rewarding. Oh and it has cute (though sometimes creepy) anime girls if that matters to you.

_childDocuments_.review: While Lost Ruins comes off as a tad fan servicey at times, I have to say that I enjoyed the game quite a lot even during the a bit over the top moments on some of the boss battles. The metroidvania exploration style in this is more castlevania than metroid. I found the exploration in the game to be satisfying with minimal backtracking unless you wanted to find rooms you didn't get into previously. True to form of the castlevania inspiration, there's a bunch of post ending content with different variations of gameplay and even a mode that lets you play as some of the bosses with different plot points & events occurring across the game after you have beaten it, making it feel completely different than your original run. I also very much enjoyed the pixelated art design and style of the in game characters. The actual character art does come across as being a bit lewd and that's cool if it's your thing, but it felt borderline for me at times. The level designs were great and didn't feel amateur at all. Only thing with design side of things I took issue with aside from the over-lewd was some of the music got noticeably repetitive. Very big into OST's and I enjoyed the tracks the composer worked on, just noticed some of the tracks looped more than others. A solid attempt for the first game in the series. The gameplay is very rigid and I did not like the loss of momentum on jumps and attack swings mid air, but after a few minutes of getting used to the controls, it played nicely and I enjoyed the tight platforming. The sheer amount of item choice & playstyles available to you gets a bit overwhelming for the length of the game. By the time you get into the swing of things, a new drop changes things up. Might be a design choice by devs and that's good as I was switching my weapons constantly as well as spells and equipment. The games also proper challenging and will make you change things up or "git gud" at times, after a few retries you learn the swing of things and can overcome pretty quickly. I would def put this up there with indie metroidvania titles like Momadora, Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth & Blasphamous that are under appreciated and shining examples of what pixel art games should look like. Def worth your time if you're a metroidvania fan. I am excited to watch Altari's next game, be it in the series or not. Hopefully wont miss their next kickstarter as I would have backed the project had I been aware. TL;DR Lost Ruins is a great metroidvania style game and worth your time if you don't mind the anime girls aesthetic as it can get a bit over the top on the fan service at times. Would pay 20-30 for the amount of content. I hope to see more from the developers when they are ready to release another game.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are amazing, cannot recommend enough. The game tries it's best to be difficult and challenging. But there's a difference between a game being difficult and being poorly designed. And poor design =\= difficult game(except you're in kaizo kind of stuff and you honestly believe that poor design is a part of difficulty). You know, there's this thing called "invincibility frames" in games. It's there for a reason, this reason is - when you are hit by one of the chaining attacks, you actually can survive. Not die because first attack stun-locks you and all next ones just connect. For some reason this game doesn't have them, so any enemy with a chain of attacks ultimately kills you.Actually everything stun-locks you. Your own animations lock you in predicaments all the time too. You can buy stuff. Cool. Except you need to grind like in "symphony of the night" 1g at a time but drops are less frequent and you're slow.Movement is extremely sluggish(like DS castlevanias), animations are too long and lock me as well, so if my attack does not connect, I need to wait for animation to end. _childDocuments_.review: This game had everything to work for me. This type of game has been done many times before so there are many examples to take pointers from. Yes the game gives you enough ways to deal with the enemies so that you don't have to keep doing it "the hard way".Despite all that, the combat just wasn't enjoyable. While in games like Darksouls or Blasphemous I found the constant battle with the enemy enjoyable and challenging, here I just dreaded it.The enemies attack patterns aren't hard to figure out, and the mechanics are simple enough to execute, so again, it's not that it is hard to deal with them, its just boring.Also close to the end the DoT attacks just get ridiculous, so unless you have the right item to deal with it you're going to either die or survive with very little health. Attacks in general by the end might just be insta kills really. _childDocuments_.review: Let’s start by stating some key details about this game: Unlike most of the 2D games I’ve recently seen, this is not a rouge-like game, but it is an excellent Metroidvania. Lost Ruins is not as innovative for the genre as others like Hollow Knight, but it masters what it tries to be while being a fun experience.   - The Combat: Personally, it doesn't feel as clunky as other reviews pointed out. There is a wide variety of weapons, spells, and relics that sure enough, if you choose right, may trivialize some of the end-game content; and although simple, due to the high variety of enemies and ways to face them, it feels very satisfying sometimes even needing to change all your equipment mid-battle. There are no death penalties unless it has been far too long since the last save point or tries the Hardcore Mode. The best part of the combat for me is something that I'm so tired of seeing in other Metroidvanias: Lost Ruins does not have contact damage with the enemies! You are not going to die because an enemy touches you; you’re going to die because they attack you.     - The Story: I had fun with it, it was okay; most people may call it generic. However, it always appears when you think you are tired of exploring or fighting, giving you time to rest precisely when needed. There are three endings to the regular story and one more for the Boss Mode. Additionally, if you read the notes and do the Boss Mode, you may appreciate the story more.  - Exploration and Sidequests: The world is not that big, but it has something in every part of it. Most of the sidequests you will clear just by playing, but some almost change entirely how you play the game, such as the quest that you can’t open any chest until the very end of the game. There are some puzzles to solve, and although simple, some are very fun.Boss and Enemies: every enemy feels unique, and the bosses are very cool to see their gimmicks. There is not much I can say other than go experience it, but there are some special things worth noting that I will be explaining in the game modes section.  - Game Modes: when you start the game, you have four difficulties. The first 3 are just difficult sliders such as HP and damage, and the other is the Hardcore Mode, where not only the enemies are stronger, but if you die, your save is deleted, and you have to start again from the beginning. Due to the difficulty presented at Hardcore, you will be forced to learn the mechanics the game offers to you as the player and the enemies, resulting in the need for a well-thought-out strategy. Additionally to these four base game modes, after you clear the game in any difficulty, you gain three new modes: Assassin Mode, Witch Mode, and Boss Mode; I recommend the first two for the players who want to test a new play style of the base game at its best. As for Boss Mode, it is an extension of the story where you play as 3 of the game's main bosses, making you understand their gimmicks while having more story and game to go for.     In general, I had an excellent experience with Lost Ruins, even going for the platinum. The game is simple, and it doesn't really try to innovate, But what it does is master that simplicity in a way that I’ve never seen before, creating a good time for both casual and experienced players.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is an excellent metroidvania, side scroller game.  Now this is the part where I talk about the story a little bit, but this is one of those games that talking about the story may spoil it for you so I'll just say it's about a young girl who has been teleported into a strange castle.Okay then the likes, the story is really good at first I thought it was your simple stop the bad guy story but had plenty of twists and turns and well-written characters that just made the story phenomenal, especially when you play the game a second time and everything in the story just seems to click together.The gameplay is really good it has a bit of a Dark Souls like feel to it, but with metroidvania-styled gameplay, it's tough but fair and when you die it is mostly your fault. It also has a nice balance of weapons and spells you can play with, you can also customize your character with different items to give them more strength or more durability or certain abilities. The weapons and spells are really good each one with their own unique look and power, some weapons and spells are better than others so this game gives incentive to mix and match to figure out which character build works for you. The pixel graphics are really beautiful, very well done with plenty of detail and nice little touches to it, I also love the character portraits it has a nice anime feel to it. The levels in the game are really good quite diverse with plenty of interesting locations to look at and explore, like a sewer to a castle to even a crypt, all of it well designed that makes you want to stop and stare at certain places in the level.The characters are really good very well written even NPC characters with little dialogue are quite interesting. I really like the main character because she's generally a very nice, very caring and considerate person, I also like this demon Merchant she's also really cool character and generally very sweet and caring, also I really like this Dragon maid she's super adorable looking.The enemies and bosses are really good each one with their own unique design and skill that keeps you on your toes, especially when playing a more harder difficulties. The music is really good with plenty of great tracks to listen to, that fits the game really well especially at the last level.The game also has quests by certain characters you meet which can give you better weapons or access to areas you couldn't get to before. Now the best things in the game is the multiple endings and different modes to play, basically after you beat the game for the first time you are given different modes like which mode, assassin mode and boss mode both the witch and assassin mode basically makes you play with a certain type of build. While boss mode where you get to play as three bosses you defeated and in that mode we get a completely different story which I found it quite good especially with the interactions of the three bosses. There's also different endings in the game which encourages you to play the game multiple times to get everything.There's also plenty of great references not just to other video games, but to anime and manga like in one scene it makes references to paper RPGs and berserk. The notes in this game I absolutely love as you know I like notes in video games as it can help build a story and these notes are very good they help build the world; these notes give insight to different characters and the villain of the game.Okay then the dislikes, alright there is not really anything to dislike about this game, okay there are some things but really they're just so small compared to how great the game is, but here are just some small complaints I have.The platforming can be a little bit frustrating sometimes like you could miss a platform after jumpping even though you were very close to it the platform. The final boss is a bit of a letdown I mean don't get me wrong the final boss has a cool design and she can be a bit tough, but I thought she'd have a second form like all the other bosses but no she doesn't even, not even on more harder difficulties she's still the same, like I said I found that to be a bit underwhelming and a little bit of a letdown. I also wish the game had some DLC to buy because I think it would do really well to have a soundtrack, pc wallpaper and art book for the game especially pc wallpaper.Alright now that I told you all this stuff, Lost Ruins is an excellent metroidvania, side scroller game. With a really good story, really good gameplay and really good characters and just so much more to love so I highly recommend this game if you like metroidvania games I recommend this game to you.

The characters, the monsters are pretty distinguishable and attractive. The graphic elements of the boss fights are top-notch for pixel-art game standards. The only downside, I think, is the environment design. It might get bored after a while, and some details and parts of the environment are hard to see.For the gameplay, it really challenges you with lots of traps, combos from monsters and bosses. The overall enemy AI is great, and it surely gives you a hard time battling through. The platformer elements and puzzles of the game is solid, yet somewhat easy at times.I also particularly love how the game offers you a variety of play styles, You can beat the game through brute force of weapons, or cunningly cheese the enemies from afar with bows, or backstabbing them with daggers, or wisely defeat them with a variety of spells that counter their weaknesses. Overall, the game has a great replay value. Finally, watch out for multiple endings of the game (3 of them, as I read online). So, if you are into cute girls with cute anime style, with a bit of a metroidvania and survival-style game, Lost Ruins is definitely a must-try!! Hats off to only 2 developers of this wonderful game!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fun game but has a very steep learning curve and punishing early game. There are a couple of achievements/endings locked behind playing on "hardcore" mode in which you lose your save file when you die and cannot manually save during the game (autosaves only). There is also an optional quest you have to complete to get an ending that makes the game much harder if you decide to complete it. I don't know if I will come back to the game to complete these.One playthrough is actually fairly short all things considered, maybe 5-10 hours if you are thorough, and only a couple hours if you speed through. Even so, the various obstacles, items, equipment, and magic that you encounter keep it a fresh experience to the point that no matter how far you get or how many items you have, if you use the wrong ones against the enemies you're fighting, you'll have an impossible time. Similarly, if you choose them well, a fight that seems very difficult will be a walk in the park. Some people have commented that the attack speed on weapons is very slow, but this is also a matter of choosing the right approach for the task at hand.You'll also unlock a few extra game modes after completing your first playthrough. I haven't tried these yet, but if you really liked your first playthrough this will probably keep things fresh for you and give you a chance to tackle the game from a new approach.Overall I would recommend this due to the interesting and engaging combat implementation (and some puzzle solving too) plus the cute characters and great artwork. The current price of $20 is definitely as high as I would go on it though. Ideally I think maybe $10-15 is a good price point (and I picked it up on sale myself). Still though, you'll definitely know if it's a game for you within 2 hours of playing, so you might as well give it a try if it looks interesting and refund it if it doesn't end up agreeing with you. I enjoyed it overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on a Metroidvania.It diverges from the norm in a few ways:- You do not heal at save points or checkpoints. You have to rely on consumable items, or gear you find later.- Enemies don't respawn. Except when they do. Not really sure what the criteria is here, but it isn't screen transitions or hitting a save point.- You do not gain new traversal abilities at any point. Walk, jump, and roll is all you get.None of this is necessarily bad, just unusual.Games had top-notch pixel art, is relatively difficulty, and pretty short at around 6 hours for a first playthrough.Sound is a bit lacking - the sound effects are serviceable, but even having just finished the game I couldn't tell you if it even had music. Definitely no voice acting.Gameplay is a little bit rough, but solid.Decent 7/10 game. Worth checking out, but not likely to amaze you.

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage. Just complete garbage. Which is why its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you have no I-frames and as such wave attacks by magic casters can hit you multiple times from the same attack. The game is labeled a metroidvania which is an insult to the genre. The map looks like a metroidvania map but you don't gain any new abilties or items that would let you access new areas. _childDocuments_.review: While the game is fun in some cases.  The storyline is a bit meh, and the exploration tends to actually be held back by the game mechanics itself.  There appears to be some basic concepts that I thought was a bit out of place for a dungeon/exploration/platforming game.I do think that the direct "drop" of the character while in mid air attacking plays in a cheap way to increase the difficulty.  The character should dedicate herself to the jump and while I think the jumps are sufficient, the attacks to bring a 90deg drop and wallstop mid air is an artificial cheap way of making this game harder.I also find another artificial difficulty in this game where there's very little money to buy items to assist.  This tends to create this "hoarding" type mentality and I don't actually use items or tools to help when it's too consumable.  I'll farm for items like chicken, and the difficult part is that I gotta teleport to respawn items.  This tends to get in the way of progress and also delays what is suppose to be just straight exploration.There are just straight forward game design flaws in this game, and at full price I would have never bought this game.  I do love the art style and I do love the characters, but the artificial difficulty bumps that are just due to bad and lazy level design is quite "annoying" to play through.  I will complete this game, but so far after maybe 5 hours of it -- it's a little uninspiring with the game mechanics. boss battles are fun at least, but the artificial handicaps get in the way.  The only saving grace is that respawns are close items are recovered when death occurs (eg it just reloads your auto save).Controller configuration gets annoying, I don't understand why the button configs on the controller changes the movement of the tabs?  This is a good example of lazy programming and not putting an extra routine in to properly map buttons to separate the way buttons map between menu and actual game play.(eg. I don't like spells on left or right buttons, so I move it to right button and right trigger, but now the TABS on the menu are mapped to left button and left trigger -- this is plain lazy for a game developer)I hope this gets properly patched and the devs look into making some of the gameplay mechanics better so that we don't get stalled by bad fetch quests and bad mechanics that artificially make the game longer and harder. One other item that bothers me is the lack of MP heal drops.  enemies tend to drop more health than mana recovery drops.  I tend to not even use spells if MP is used up since there's no way to heal and with the lack of resources (being unable to properly buy items without farming for hours) there's no reason for me to stick around and do anything or even look at vending machines.  MP heal drops should be a bit more often if you want players to use spells, also larger mp pool would be nicer considering you have spells that cost 12MP given a 20pt pool.  this is not even good if you don't allow for HP/MP recovery at autosave spots (which is also another artificial difficulty bump). Better planning and more enemy placements in a room would be nice - large empty room with 1-2 mobs with platforming is too little.  Even with no XP gains, it would be nice to just be able to do more.  Makes the inclusive fetch quests a bit more entertaining.  Also RESPAWNS, I gotta warp out and back to do a respawn, this is just meh.

_childDocuments_.review: The art is beautiful and the character designs are modest! That is all it has going for it though. The gameplay is super frustrating. I wanted to like it but it keeps making the experience feel cheap and unfair in most situations. I love souls-like, metrovania-style gameplay but this needs a new set of developers or someone from the Metroid series to help them design the gameplay. You will go through a level where you have studied the enemy movement and counted the pixels so you can come out unscathed, only to be killed by an off-screen magic attack that had no business coming into the screen. There is no real tutorial or any "lube" build-up in the gameplay. They just straight-up raw-dog and throw you into the hardest difficulty without learning proper weapon or magic management. Mind you, I played on "Normal". I cannot imagine the hardest difficulty. For normal, you already get hit once or twice and you are dead. I'm a Dark Souls fan but FromSofware are at least fair with their deaths. _childDocuments_.review: Although the crux of the game is lol anime titties there is a decent metroidvania in here somewhere. The art clearly has a ton of work put into it and is well done, and the music and sound design is pretty great too. However, the gameplay itself is absolutely frustrating - even on the easiest difficulty, some mobs can barely touch you, while others have instant death attacks, even at full health with stacked resists. This is made even more frustrating because there is zero sense of speed to the movement and attacks - you feel like you're moving in molasses the entire time even with the fastest things equipped, and as a result the combat feels super clunky and drags on. Magic is super over powered and I felt like many bosses (especially the last few) basically required a certain spell load out to spam in order to beat, rather than finding my own way to victory. Overall there's a lot done well, but it was too frustrating in the end to be able to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game.  Story is predictable, archetypical, japaneesie, boring.  The characters are stupid and basic.  The character portraits are sexualized as usual and also stupid.   The weapons are almost all boring and possess no individual noteworthy qualities,  Most of the magic sucks, as does casting it until the game is basically over.  Now for the good.  Thank god they didn't try to voice act this.  I do not like the grating voices these types of games assign to their characters.  The fact that it was text based meant I could stand to actually read the cutscenes instead of feverishly searching for a skip button.  There actually is a skip button, and you're not missing much by enjoying its use.  The bosses and enemies are all pretty fun to fight but the bosses can be cheesed really easily.  Like the spider archer lady is completely negated by a shield and summon swords and the ice lady by the fire sword and summonable fire orbs.  The visuals are very nice.  Pretty good pixel art.  Cool looking bosses.  To complete the map isn't too arduous and "how do I get over there" to get a treasure chest isn't a huge time sink for the most part.  Load up your favorite magical teleporting christmas throwing ham and... uhh, go ham on some demons!  Without elaborating much, the only real complaint I didn't already know I was going to have coming into this game was the magic system.  There are equippable accessories that give you constant MP regen you find very late in the game.  Otherwise, your MP NEVER regenerates at all unless you use restorative items which tend to be expensive to buy and somewhat rare to pick up.  The basic (lousy) spells give you up to 4 casts to exhaust your entire magic bar, and the useful ones as few as one or two casts. That's it.  The spells are almost all terrible.  Once you've gotten the two accessories that make magic use practical, magic becomes almost overpowered, one shotting just about any enemy and doing around 1/5th of a boss's health bar per charge if you exploit elemental weaknesses. I don't have a quick and easy solution for this problem.  It just feels like the game developers got lost trying to come up with the magic system, and it's not very good as a result.  You find new spells constantly throughout the game, but it never feels practical to use them at all outside of necessity to open a door or something until you find the items that regenerate your MP.  It would have been nice if there was a scaling up system where spells were either much more useful in the early game when casting them was extremely expensive, there was a very slow regeneration of MP by default, or even a system that regenerates MP for killing enemies so that the player would feel welcome to use it offensively.  Maybe this bothered other people less than it bothered me.  7 hours to 100% the map and beat all bosses with copious amounts of screwing around in the process.  Definitely worth the 8 bucks I paid for the game on sale. Conveniently, I'd give it a score of 8/10 as well due to the combination of length, cost, and enjoyment factor.  It's a pleasant game that, if you like to get-off looking at cartoon characters with comically inappropriate wardrobes, you'll enjoy even more than I did.  If the story in every anime you've watched or JRPG you've played has blown your mind, then you will love this game because it does not deviate even slightly from the common tropes of that genre.  At 10 bucks, it'd be a solid 7/10.  It is not worth 20 dollars.  Unless you're looking for your waifu or whatever the hell that means, wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: + lots of variety in weapons, armor, builds+ really nice soundtrack and sound design+ animations and pixel art graphics are great+ large world with multiple distinct areas- punishingly difficult until you get in the groove- poor difficulty pacing and balancing- lots of tools at disposal but most of them impracticalLost Ruins was advertised to me as a metroidvania but I never really got that feel. You don't gain new abilities or skills that open up previously inaccessible areas, the game's pretty open from the start and instead relies on puzzles and exploration to unlock new areas. The main idea of the game, is that you're criminally underpowered at the start and really don't know anything about the world. And you don't really learn much by playing: besides some cute and funny dialog, the story is really of no consequence and shouldn't be a reason to grab the game. It's a hard game, but only really near the start. From the beginning to the first boss, you'll struggle to make progress as you only have one equipment slot and your equipment selection is slim. Enemies hit hard and you lack many means to heal. After the first boss but before the second, it gets a lot easier, especially since you gain an extra equipment slot and can get a passive heal equipment. Shortly after you get a passive magic point regen item which is where the game starts to become trivial.Some of the later bosses I could do on first try without any difficulty because the tools at your disposal are so plentiful and powerful when paired with passive HP/MP regen: it's difficult to lose. Even the final boss, you could stand still and just regen and use up curatives to stay alive and deal damage without need for dodging or evading attacks. It really does get that easy.You have many weapons, spells, and equipment to choose from, but it's clear from the very start that speed is the name of the game, as enemies will stagger or be pushed back when hit. All enemies I could find could be stun locked, although the window for some of them is very slim, like the skeletons with shields. For the whole game I used daggers and a shield, and the shield honestly wasn't necessary. Using swords or hammers can be fun, but it's way too slow to really be effective unfortunately. But that's the whole shtick of the game, that attacks take time and need to be timed as an exercise of risk vs. reward.The soundtrack is quite nice. It's very muted, subdued, but very effective in setting tone. Each of the world's locations have their own track which repeats, but it's seamless and fits the locations well. The sound design in general is very nice: I noticed if I was on the left side of the screen, audio from my left speaker was more pronounced, being able to hear water dripping or footsteps clearer, and as I moved to the right side of the screen, the sound traveled with me, migrating to the right speaker. It's a neat use of spatial audio here.It took me a couple of hours to really get into Lost Ruins but I'm glad I stuck with it. It is extremely challenging in the beginning but you quickly get into the flow of things. I did a couple playthroughs and it took me 9 hours but I was thorough and did some achievement hunting, too. There's additional modes that unlock on game end which give you specific builds or restrictions which can make for interesting second or third playthroughs. I think the value is here, it just might not be for everyone. It's a cute game with clear love in it, but the difficulty can scare some away.Setting the Deck to 7w max TDP ensures a 60fps experience throughout. 5w is good enough for 95% of the game, but there are a handful of areas where the lighting or particle effects bog things down a touch. Experience on Deck is great, but cloud saves do not work properly. Your save data will not be available on both PC and Deck, only the system you started it on.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a beautiful game that captures a stotic since of tranquility in is playtime, offers challenging metrovania combat and a cast of strong female characters, that makes this game ultimately one that I would recommend. Earnestly, I actually didn't mind this and even enjoyed it since so many times in games Consumables felt kind of worthless, but in this game they might be the difference between saving your life or needing to restart back to your last checkpoint.The story is what I call "enviromental" much of the story is told through the pixel art on the screen,  and through your own imagination. There are words that fuel the flames of creativity but, if you take just the story that you're told, the words on the screen, it's a bit lackluster.When buying this game ask yourself: Do I want to play a game where I am a cute school girl fighting through a castle against other cute, deadly creatures that both look like they want a headpat and want to rip my neck off? _childDocuments_.review: Good example of a very fun game with a thousand flaws.The characters and bosses are all very stylish and the whole thing is a joy to look at.  The plot is predictable and not very memorable but it stands fine without it.  Exploring is a lot of fun due to the wild assortment of weapons, items, and accessories you can find.  You'll never feel like the game is wasting your time, because often what you'll discover is extremely useful for what is up ahead.  The huge assortment of practical collectibles and boss rewards gives a real sense of wonder and adds a lot of variety.The downside to this is that it leads to a lot of menuing.  When you have a hundred weapons and accessories with specific uses, you'll feel obligated to swap them constantly to be gaining full advantage.  There is no restriction on this, meaning you can literally hit an enemy with a DPS setup and then swap to a defensive one during an attack phase.  It slows the gameplay to a crawl.Additionally, there is a real problem with the combat in this game, in that weapon speed is far too overpowered.  The increased action delay on using a heavy weapon leaves you wide open, often getting your attacks interrupted completely since enemies tend to attack quickly.  Due to your very low health pool and relatively limited consumables, this is disastrous.  On top of this, faster weapons are better dps anyway, and you can often just stagger enemies and use your shield and counter, rather than trying to secure a larger opening.  It often feels like the optimal strategy is to force a boss into a corner and dagger them to death while spamming food.  The spell to slow projectiles also completely breaks half the bosses.I should mention that upon completing the game, you unlock a game mode that removes weapons entirely and gives you a Castlevania 3 (or more recently, Curse of the Moon) setup with well-defined characters you swap between.  This actually removes the issue of having to menu weapons, and since the combat didn't make good use of the weapon selection anyway,  the game just feels much smoother.  Menuing accessories and food is still a problem, but it's better.  I wish that the game had been built with this as the main mode instead.Despite all of this, the game is just fun.  A thorough playthrough probably runs 10 hours or so, but boss mode was fun enough for me to sink in another several.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought this was gonna be some Castlevania/Momodora hybrid but as time went on it started to feel more Shantae. And this is mostly due the writing and the enemy variety which I'm sure has been a huge inspiration.I'd argue that the early part plays like I mentioned, then turns into Shantae up until you reach the late stage (think clock tower) when it goes back to being your typical Metroidvania because this is when difficultly really ramps up. And like Shantae there is no way to level up, meaning you have to rely on your gear, spells, upgrades and most importantly your wits.If you know what you're getting yourself into and can deal with the difficulty (spikes) then the game is about 6-8 hours depending on how fast you rush it like skipping achievements or not, going for optimal builds or not. You can definitely do it in half the time if you so choose, but I choose to cheese half the game due to some glaring issues. Did I mention you get the option to cheese your way quite early on? You'd think that wouldn't the case but it is. It's so powerful in fact that it can easily carry you for 80% of the game once you realize it. It's bad game design no doubt considering everything else at your disposal and makes the game quite trivial and boring if you choose to use it. But that's what I did during my first playthrough. There's a few issues with spells and certain equipment later on as well which makes the game quite trivial to the point were weapons are kinda useless (other than for achievements). Normally you aren't really expected to be carried by magic often being a limited resource, but you can go ham quite literally if you so choose at a certain point. Often if not always you have to rely on some weapon build but it's kinda pointless and sad considering the arsenal at hand. A missed opportunity for sure. As for the the weapons themselves, you'd think they cause staggered damage of some kind in this game, but nope... you have your debuffs and that's it, while it's magic that does everything else. And oddly enough it's the opposite for enemies since they are all mostly melee while having longer range. Technically everything an enemy does will make you stagger and fall through platforms whenever possible.And now unto said glaring issues if you ask me at least, which can make this quite a bad experience if you aren't prepared, namely:- Konami/Capcom/Tecmo NES era enemy placement. Although not as bad you can get chain staggered by enemies which can lead to cheap deaths if you're not careful. So plan accordingly (if/when possible).- Infamous From Software animation locks and delays. I still think this is one of the biggest banes to game design since it crept into everything imaginable where it shouldn't have been in the first place. Weapons and spells in general have an overly long windup time which is slower than the enemy, and even with certain gear it becomes very tedious to the point where you can just match up to the enemy by deflecting them, i.e arrow vs arrow which is just bad game design overall. I'd treat the exploration part more as a stealth game, especially when you have access to spells and health/mana regen. Learn the animation cycles instead of relying on brute force unless you can of course towards the end.You'd think that after 35 years (Ninja Gaiden) that meleeing certain ranged enemies would be just as easy if not easier, but think again. Thanks to "brilliant" From Garbageware it now is the exact opposite instead. Jumping and stabbing, slashing or even shooting might as well not exist as a feature unless you like 100% vulnerability because potato. There are no iframes or forms of block unless you use a shield and then only a shield, because when you attack you are animation locked for that duration regardless if you hit something or not, tried casting a spell or not. You can by no means swap from attacking to blocking (even with a short delay) like in something "modern" like for example Ninja Gaiden from 2004 or Sekiro from 2019 which means that even if you hit an enemy you will mostly likely get staggered even if they die in one hit, because remember, they are faster than you and have longer range. Even older/other metroidvania titles have some form of evade ability like backwards step which was at least useful overall wheras the roll here is only useful for evading certain traps, boss attacks and finding secrets. And the best of all, even if we had that you still wouldn't be able to use it as intended due to said animation locks.Imagine if this timeline would've gone with Capcom or even Team Ninja instead. I'd love to see a DMC or modern Ninja Gaiden platformer but that'll never happen now. So thanks From Garbageware for making gaming worse once again.- The checkpoint system is EXTREMELY half-baked. Normal savepoints work as expected but the checkpoints are really bad because you can't run to the same one again after using it, which means if you did a loop of some area (which this game has A LOT of), you now have to travel further, often twice as long (even though we're talking seconds at most (but this adds up over time) just to use the next checkpoint. I'd almost argue they should've been removed or if you can then avoid them until you cleared the area, but then you end up in a catch 42 because you don't know what's ahead until you do which makes said checkpoint useless on your first run, unless you're really struggling or not saving that often..? if you're going for a second run on Veteran or any of the Modes then they make a lot more sense because you kinda know what to expect by then, but this is obviously not the case for first time players. If this game was stage-based then I wouldn't have complained but it isn't, it's a metroidvania. And if you have checkpoints you expect them to work all the time.It's not about being hard or anything but it's very tedious because you might die due to cheap death on the next room, AND EVEN IF YOU PASSED SAID CHECKPOINT, you now have to rerun the entire area even though you passed the checkpoint twice. And since the game has story bits it can mean rerunning the same part a couple of times which happens the closer you get to the midpoint. At least savepoints are placed next to boss rooms like you'd expect unlike some games which makes you rerun the entire thing to waste your time because reasons. Overconfidence can definitely kill your mood for the game if you end up in some deathloop because you're skipping mobs or forget about some traps when skipping about.To give a better example; time is limited (shocking I know!), so if every death costs about 1min, over time that can be (over) an hour lost simply due to having to rerun the place you just visited. And trust me, this will happen A LOT unless you go at a snails place. In worse games you get punished for simply sneezing because for some reason you can't pause the game whenever which can lead to a death. Why pause could exist 35 years ago, because I need to visit the bathroom or anything other urgent at any given point and not now is anyone's guess. Oh but thankfully you can pause whenever unlike some company's insistence on not letting you do so which is somehow a feature and quite widespread because potato? Thanks said company for making gaming worse! And if you think this was a great idea then I have a bridge to sell you.Music is okay and fits the game. A bit too atmospheric for my taste and nothing to write home about but considering the length (and price) does the job well enough.There's a few other things I'd love to mention but these would fit more unto a guide other than the things I really had to mention here. But for the asking price I still think it's worth it.

The game moves at an abhorrently slow pace, especially evident in the combat. Enemies tend to attack too fast for your slow attack animations to counter. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly player-hostile design, and not in a hard-but fair Hollow Knight way. The game features slow, clunky movement  affected by barely visible surface effects (like slimy, oily, or simply wet floors), and a useless dodge roll with a painfully long recovery that leaves you wide open. The combat is built for maximum frustration, with even the “fastest” weapons being painfully slow. Anything that deals any kind of damage takes a comically long time to deliver a blow, while enemies have no trouble spamming projectiles and lightning-quick attacks.Aside from some charming and well-animated sprites, the visuals are murky and hard to discern, so you often aren't even sure what hurt you. The game doesn't give you any way to heal or replenish MP early on, leaving you to scavenge a menagerie of borderline useless items that heal you a couple of HP at a time.And then there are abnormal status effects. Every, and I mean EVERY enemy gives you abnormal status with their attacks. Got hit by an insect - poison! Got hit by a goblin - bleed! Stepped into a barely visible puddle of water - wet (enjoy that 50% movement speed reduction for the next 5 seconds in a middle of a fight). All effects are unavoidable and instant, and all of them will absolutely kill you in seconds if you don't pause the game, open inventory, scroll to items tab, scroll down through a long list of confusing junk, and find the exact thing that heals this particular status effect. Close menu and get a new status effect right away.Despite how frustratingly difficult and un-rewarding the “normal” mode is, the game doesn't even deem it pertinent to give you an ending, as, you see – you only get endings if you play on “veteran” or higher. On top of it all, the game is confusingly horny, to the point where I feel like it was originally meant to be an H-game that got neutered for wider release.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reluctant to admit that I enjoyed this game since it was obviously made for weeboos, what with you playing as a short skirted schoolgirl that can find a swimsuit as an alternate costume, fighting other girls as big titted bosses (some of which are completely naked) in pretty generic dungeons with generic dark fantasy enemies. Not to mention, the generic amnesiac main protagonist seems to lack a moral compass as they go around slaughtering enemies while acting all kiddy and innocent. Ultimately, the game really doesn't even have an interesting story so I definitely think catering to weeboos was a central draw to it's presentation.Mechanically, the game shines with pretty solid effects and animations. The base combat consisting of your girl swinging swords in an arc of various timings based on the kinds of weapons you use adds some strategy to combat by forcing you to get the timings right, which can be a lot of fun, and there's neat gimmicks like pretty well done fire physics, all apparently done in the Unity engine. I'm not a big fan of all the status effects you can incur from so many enemies' attacks, and it's got that "Symphony of the Night" problem where it's not long before you find a sword that's guaranteed to be your preference over others, trivialising other loot you find which is the game's only real progress draw, what with the lack of a levelling system (which I also like). Being a Metroidvania game, I also inevitably came to points where I got lost, which is where I'm at now in the game. Lacking a real interesting story or characters that aren't terribly written under-aged waifus, I can't say I'm that motivated to move forward either. The smooth animations and pixel graphics do look pretty good, but the game might've been optimised terribly, as it bricked the computer played it on before I got the one I'm typing on now. 6/10 - I would play it again, and even recommend it to some, but there's likely better Metroidvanias that don't rely on schoolgirls as their draw, so thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I like and also don't like this game. It's hard to explain, so I'll be simple about it.You attack really slowly, so you have to plan your attacks in advance. Only problem with this is that you encounter new enemies pretty fast and their attack patterns are so fast that you can't react right away. Some have multi-hit attacks. For instance, I encountered some slime girls, and they were easy enough to figure out, but then I found a blue one and immediately expected something different, but wasn't expecting it to be a close range activated attack that hit SIX TIMES while I was in the air and could do nothing about it. At that point I decided that playing this game wasn't worth the effort, there are other, better games that do similar things, so I'll just play those. But that's not all the issues I saw.Second most egregious issue I found was that checkpoints and save points don't heal you - at all. You collect plenty of health resources and all from killing monsters and exploration, but... The items aren't very good. It's not forgiving at all. Even Dark Souls' campfires healed you, so what's the deal?Third strike for me was the fact that most traps aren't obvious at all. I could see where the spikes come up from the ground all over the place except one, and when I hit it, I almost threw up from how bad that design is.Ways this way could be better? Make those checkpoints HEAL you. Have mana replenish itself slowly automatically. What's the point of having fireballs if I can't use them on flying enemies when I need to? The enemies attack faster than you do, rhythmically. Either increase our attack speed, or reduce theirs. Heavy weapons suck and have arguably 0 use case, since they're insanely slow to use for all the power they've got, resulting in them being lesser picks.The only thing I liked about this game really was the artwork and atmosphere. Should have gone with Ender Lillies or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fantastic atmosphere. Whenever I boot it up, the title screen music just makes me feel like I'm in a dream. The art-style is on point, along with the OST and animations. Some bosses are out-of-this-world beautiful.The gameplay is very refined. You get to choose from a number of weapons that differ in size, speed and additional effects. Different weapons are not just slightly stronger reskins of each other, they are meaningfully different. I've seen people complain that the swing animation is too slow, but that is not a valid criticism: there are quick weapons with which you can outpace certain opponents, and there are slow weapons, which, granted, can't outpace some enemies but have some other advantage like range or healing or bleed. On top of that you have a bunch of magical spells, items and equipment that can help you deal with foes that do not go down easy to your usual build of choice.I want to point out separately that there are various ways to bend the environment to one's advantage, be that setting floor on fire or poisoning water. There is a lot of variability to how you can approach any encounter. There are also shields, and magic sticks, and veils and floaty boots and a lot of other stuff. And there are other very curious interactions that you should try and find for yourself.Exploration is quite good too. You don't have to visit every nook and cranny of the labyrinth to complete the game, but it will let you find: side stroies, interesting puzzles,  special weapons, special enemies and bosses, new scenery.  The game map does not feel empty in the slightest.The story is nothing special, but I did find it charming. The dialogues communicate the characters'personalities very well and the characters themselves usually have some nuance to them. Reading small pieces of lore lying about and talking to side characters made me feel connected to the world.The game does not waste your time. Save points are located in a balanced manner, they neither trivialize nor amplify the difficulty, there is a substantial challenge in getting from one save point to another and yet there is never an annoyingly long stretch of no save points.The game is also filled to the brim with content. After completing it once, you can replay it in hardcore mode or try for a different ending, or play a new story with different mechanic, or play it again with some restrictions. There are also a lot of secrets scattered around and a gallery to view your achievments.This game is quite amazing, I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10Finished the game in the default difficulty, not amazing but not bad either, I got this from HumbleBundle, one thing I'll say the game is worth 5€, the 20€ price tag is wild for me, this game if you don't want to replay it has a max 5-6 hours gameplay.This is a very small game, plays kinda like a metrovania but with an inventory and assortment of weapons that you have to use at best to take on every challenge, weapons do the same damage through the whole game and your character does not level up so you really have to choose the right weapon for the right job all along the game, this is where the difficulty comes from mostly.You can continue to play the game as you unlock 3 new modes when you finish the game the first time, but these new modes are just playing the game game with different conditions.It's a nice game to finish on 1 or 2 sittings.Biggest CON for me is Unity.. the game at some parts lagged a bit when there were some effects on screen, but this was mostly at end of fights or cutscenes, during gameplay it was smooth 120fps+.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to like this one as much as I did. While it unfortunately suffers from an inverted difficulty curve (where a lack of options and power at the beginning of the game makes the first few hours far more difficult than all that follow, even in repeat playthroughs), once it opens up, it feels empowering to find a new weapon or spell or accessory that suddenly makes some other set of tools viable.It does feel like some of the systems of the game go underutilized. There's a whole system where liquids like oil, poison, or water can spill on the ground and react with fire or electricity, but aside from certain traps, this whole system doesn't come into play too often. It might be possible to work this to your own advantage if you set up your equipment right.Altogether, a pleasant surprise. Worth pursuing if it looks like your thing, genre-wise.A word of warning:
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short game that some have called a Metroidvania. It feels like more of a puzzler at the beginning, but then you get equipment that can cheese bosses. As I am pretty low skill level, this was nice. Due to the low hp of your character, it seems intended that your repeatedly die and retry.Scaling: The game starts out quite hard, but then gets relatively easy. The hp scaling of enemies is too flat. While you can still die from a single enemy, the regular enemy battles are still pretty quick. Weapons/Spells: I like the variety. There's a multitude of ways you can get through the game after you've run the past the first area. However, there are significant issues the speed variation in the weapons make many weapons next to useless unless you really like handicapping yourself to hone your skills. The enemy reactions make many slower weapons unusable.  While it's intended that you use specific weapons/spells for different areas of the game, you can eventually cheese through with 3 or 4 after the first half of the game, especially if you pick ranged weapons. Bosses: I do like most of the bosses, and definitely died the first try on most phases, but felt some satisfaction in getting the timing down. It's weird that they have the order of the items from the bosses that they do. It definitely could have done with more balancing, but was still worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I want more of these games. This game plays incredible on the Steam Deck. It is so good that I plan on buying a physical copy for the Switch when it releases in July. I love the boss battles. The are numerous weapons to utilize in combat. It is fun to traverse the world. This game has minor side quests and puzzles that fit well for this game. There is a decent amount of variety of enemies and I haven't yet beat it. So far I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

Want to know more about the another story even though it doesn't exist anymore....
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10. Probably best described as a 2D adventure game. This is not your typical skilled action combat centric metroidvania. Not worth your time unless you have nothing left to play. Instead of going into every issue I have with Lost Ruins I'll summarize it overall. The game isn't broken but it puts forth the minimum effort to make just about every aspect barely passable. This genre is too competitive for these kind of entrants to be positive recommendations.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty well made for the content it gives, but the additional endings are pretty difficult. As for the 'clunk', the combat is slow but people are assuming it was made poorly or badly, just like many other games some weapons swing faster than others. The game becomes a joke when you use utilize magic as it just shreds bosses, and that is where the endings come in, aside from the free chest in the catacombs you have to beat the game without opening gold chests until a certain point. Overall, the art style is pretty impressive. The story itself isn't so serious and I would say it's probably on the same level of goofy as Rabi Ribi but slower and a little more difficult than Rabi Ribi's easier modes.

_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is just a joy.  The area, level design, and enemy mechanics work together perfectly.  For the first time in, maybe years, I never felt the need to check a wiki or a guide or google mechanics.  You just kind of experiment and progress.  It's a good time and a callback to the best the genre has to offer.The 'good ending' is even spelled out fairly early.  No hidden mechanics, no easily missable requirements, the game just tells you "Don't do X" and if you don't you're on the right track to the good end.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: The inventory is a pain in the a** to use, and you have to use it a lot. It's great that spells and weapons feel different, and that different enemies are susceptible to certain effects, and you can even cleverly use the environment. But the slow weapon selection takes all joy out of this, and the same goes for consumables and armor pieces. If the items were at least sorted by the effects they cause! Why there are two different mechanisms for saving is beyond me. There are  which let you save your progress permanently, and you can even manage multiple savegames for some weird reason. But then there are also these  that only act as a temporary checkpoint mid game. And they can only be activated once! So if you pass the same checkpoint again, your progress until then will not be saved! So when you die you often find yourself in the position of having to do a lot of busywork like talking to a character or picking up items again and again. It's just a frustrating experience.There's also no real sense of progression or accomplishment. There is no levelling (which doesn't have to be bad in and of itself, but it is in this case) and most items are utterly boring and don't have any advantage over the stuff you already have. Buying items is also almost completely useless. I could go on about graphics, combat, and other silly design choices, but these are the biggest deal breakers for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked the game.Clearing quests helps a lot with sustainability of HP and MP (f.e. that one bunny-like weapon, that regenerates MP when you hit it).Gameplay-wise it is entertaining. Encouters may be challenging depending on how quick you adapt to each new type of enemy and boss. Visuals are pleasant to the eye, that is if you don't mind pixelated anime-like style. I also enjoyed some of the OSTs throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't qualify that game as a Metroidvania, as the platforming elements, or the backtracking isn't complicated in any form.What makes up for it are the graphics and the "survival" elements in the usage of weapons, traps and environments that encourage the player to try, die and retry lots of different strategies.Game is quite short, but a completionist can close the tale in under 40 hours

_childDocuments_.review: fun little indie gamea bit short for my liking, but the actual gaming experience is pretty good. Boss mode is an especially nice and unexpected option. When I saw the name I thought it would be a boss rush of some sorts but no. No spoilers here:)Personally I REALLY like the art style, whether the avatars or the in-game pixels.In a word, totally worth the money(I want a sequel on Kana's love story pls)
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and somewhat short metroidvania, get it on a good sale :)+ Side quests, "secrets" and a few puzzles+ Multiple endings+ Multiple game modes (unlocked after beating the game and giving some replay value)- Difficulty isn't done well (I played on "Veteran").. Overall a bit tough in a good way in the early-mid game and a bit 2 easy late game (some late bosses are 2 easy cos u already have strong equipment and can even cheese them so to say).- Final boss is very boring and kinda weak + Nice weapon/armor/spell variety- Kinda short overall
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: surprisingly decent game but many small issues, rock paper scissor gameplay with the right weapon combat is trivialized and using wrong weapon will put you at massive disadvantage, art and animations are nice, the game is a lil sus do not let anyone saw you playing this, map design is pretty good but can be confusing to traverse due to lack of detail in map, puzzles are janky and no much explanation making a small mistake irreversible forcing you to reset the puzzle by leaving the area, you need to manage save files to make the game easier otherwise you may have to do things all over again and to manually save you need to travel to a nearby computer making it a little tedious at times.overall a pretty good game with several janks, a fun experience nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! I was put off by the negative reviews about clunky animations and slow attacks but it's really fine, there are items that boost attack speed and faster weapons. The magic and environment interactions are surprisingly deep for a kickstarter metroidvania. The art is great and bosses are all memorable, music is great as well. Not a great balance between punishing normal difficulty or face-roll accessible mode for your first playthrough, but once you get the hang of the mechanics and rolling behind enemies it's not so bad and gear selection for the area/boss you're in is vital. Pretty short but extended with special modes after beating the game, witch mode, assassin mode, and play as the bosses mode, and 3 endings. Hidden gem and quite a unique experience all together.
