_childDocuments_.review: I recommended this game, but give a warning.  Accessible (easy)  is too easy and the other difficulties start off too hard.  The difficulty curve is very steep and doesn't level out until after you gain a few items that give you enough health and mana to deal with the combat.  I did a single playthrough and loaded a previous save to get a second ending and pick up a few more achievements.  That all said I did enjoy my time with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: It's unfortunate that this game has been left in a buggy state, as it seems very enjoyable and relevant to my interests. Lost Ruin is a very difficult action adventure game that doesn't give the player the advantage of being able to level up. The player character is limited to the items and spells that she finds as she explores the castle she wakes up in. I got about 40% through before the frequent crashes became too much for me to bear. The achievements were also apparently broken, popping up on the Steam overlay several times as if I had completed them when I was no where close (popping the award for beating all the bosses after beating the first boss). I thought i could at least get past the crashes in compatibility mode, but I just got hit with another freeze. I'd be interested in coming back to this and pushing past the difficult game play, but not while having to deal with so many technical issues as well.e: I wound up returning to this game to give it one last try, and while it did crash on me one more time I was charmed enough by the gameplay the press on. I don't know that I can recommend the game at full price with its current bugs, but I don't think it's fair to negatively review a game that captivated me enough to pull me past numerous barriers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: People say this is a very hard souls like on even recommended difficulty and I have to disagree. While the initial difficulty is quite high, once you unlock a few accessories and find better weapons then the game is pretty easily doable in the 4 hours it took me to reach one ending. It seems there's a myriad of different modes and difficulties, so I'll explore them. But it really isn't that hard to get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Item/equipment management was pretty bad. Could have used an easy item swap mechanic ala dark souls. Game is technically a metroidvania but is kind of a hybrid and once you focus less on the combat/action and start playing it like a survival horror it takes off and you have an aha moment. The first 20% of the game is extremely hard for some reason. Early on it is more about item management than combat until a good chunk of the game is completed then it becomes pretty easy once you are able to equip a certain type of item which I wont spoil. There is lots of options for builds which I really truly enjoyed as each one presented different challenges and strategies for gameplay and were different enough to have much enjoyment from changing up my build every so often for fun. Straight playthrough probably 12-15 hours to complete if you do most of the content. I 100% the castle and defeated all the bosses and completed all the quests but didnt get all the items because you would have to grind for money to buy them all tbh. Some of the bosses are pretty easy near the end as well. I got this game on sale and I would play through again if I didnt have 1253125 games in my backlog. But it gets points for originality because it doesnt try to be castlevanaia it kind of does its own thing which is really cool. Also some clever design ideas and tricks are thrown in here and there that put a smile on your face like the designers were being pretty creative. (more games like this and less games that just try to copy older games) =) 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game, it's very short (i finish it 9 hours, but im sure u can finish it in less time) but when u want to play a good metroidvania with very smooth animations and and beautiful art (and a lot of waifus) this is your game.Also have re-play modes, and didnt try it but they are very interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this on the Switch. Hope to see similar titles in the future.* Several difficulty options to cater the different palettes. * Soulslike simple to learn but hard to master combat.* Weapons have different animations and unique abilities.* Equipment, spells and items with interesting modifiers.* Weapon, item and equipment synergies leading to different builds.* Anime girls all around. Sometimes cute, often grotesque.* Interesting boss mechanics. Bosses have a well-balanced difficulty.* Regular mobs can easily kill the player. Plentiful mob variety.* Dark and twisted story.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. Unique mechanics and design choices. Cute art. Not too difficult. And for those who are looking at this game specifically because of the metroidvania tag let me tell you that this is not a typical metroidvania in the sense that there is zero backtracking required in this game. This for me is a good thing because that is the one feature of metroidvania that I find a little tedious. This game is more accurately described as a mild action platformer. Everything in this game requires more thought and planning. If you think things through and use your items generously, then combat becomes pretty trivial. However, if you go in without a plan, don't use your items, or start button mashing, then you will die immediately. Definitely worth it on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it's a very good experience. Kinda hard and unforgiving even in recommended difficulty but it's really fun. If that's not your type then I don't think this is for you. Story is kinda normal, a bit predictable even. Soundtracks are okay. Lastly, the visual, well I bought it because of this very reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a solid metroidvania that seems too difficult at first, but once you play it for a bit and get used to weapon timing and enemy attack patterns, then it feels more balanced.  The game doesn't have the special moves or enemy soul collecting of similar titles, but what's there works well and the game is worth playing through a couple of times to see the different endings.  This has one of the more enjoyable boss modes that I can recall.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, to the point. The game play is just good enough to get you through to the end of the game. Story was mediocre but good enough to get to the end. Overall, that seems to be the theme of the game: just good enough to make it to the end. Worth playing but not worth the price. **Recommended only while discounted.**
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game commits many "sins" of 2D action platformers/metroidvanias:-HP/MP does not regenerate naturally, even at a save point-Attacks are clunky, slow and have poor hitboxes-Movement and dodging is slow and deliberate-No i-frames at all after being hit, leading to getting juggled by enemies-Air attacks stop all forward momentum-Checkpoints are single-use (until you hit another checkpoint)-Status ailments everywhereDespite all of these things, the game is actually great. It's designed to be playable with all these "downsides" so enemies are clunky and slow themselves, healing items are plentiful, and hard saves are frequent. You can eventually find items and spells that will allow you to consistently heal your HP/MP as well as deal some decent damage. The story is pretty good and it doesn't overstay its welcomeThe main character's idle animation is ridiculous though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a beautiful anime metroidvaniaRating: 8/10The anime art is really beautiful with a fitting soundtrack and some action. This game is for metroidvania fans or someone who wants to discover this genre.I think the story is quite predictable but nonetheless, it is worth giving a try.This game can be finished in under 4-5 hours but,for achievement freaks, I expect at least 1~5 replays and a couple additional hours. I might try 100% in the future but I'm not sure.It's pretty skill dependent and also you can choose the difficulty if the game is too hard but it was quite easy and linear compared to some other games.Pros:Beautiful anime artGreat soundtrackGreat entry level for people who never tried this genreShort gameCons:Nothing reallyNeutral: Replayability is to be desired but most of the time game like this you just come back out of nowhere and play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just not for me. The attack movement is so clunky and slow. This is by design so I can't say it is poor or anything. The game simply isn't something I found fun. _childDocuments_.review: Wasn't sure at first, honestly; there was some stiffness, seems generic, not a fan of the schoolgirl thing...but honestly this game is amazing.any issue with the animation or controls became just charming, the combat is actually quite a bit of fun once used to it, the mountain of weapons, spells, items, etc. that are available actually have an impact on game-play, much more than just "big number." the story is somewhat predictable but interesting, and the characters are charming. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely bad at this game, but it is very well made!The OST is good, the gameplay is challenging but not too hard, the artstyle looks very good and especially the character animations are really smooth. We are talking about 30-60fps animations. Big respect to the developers!A must play for metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely clunky controls, but once I learned that combat should be avoided and slow weapons are impossible to use, I managed to stick it out to the end. Nothing particularly interesting story or gameplay-wise, but the art is pretty cute. I'll point out the things that I found particularly egregious though. You lose all momentum when you attack, so I got killed or fell a lot by dropping like a rock straight into a pit until I got used to that. Items can get lost in the background art sometimes. Usually, it's just unimportant enemy drops, but I spent an hour unable to progress because a boss dropped a key and I didn't see it because it blended in and you have to pick up items manually for some reason. Finally, there are no I-frames when getting hit, so certain enemies can just wombo-combo you to death if you're not careful and that never feels good. Also the inventory menus are hard to read if you're colorblind.It's not the best game I've ever played, but aside from the rough edges, it's passable if you have ~5 hours to kill.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Really clicked with me with the combat, reminding me of Terraria's game-play: consuming items during fights, constantly healing, constantly switching items, constantly dying, and constantly being challenged, the constant good stuff. Honestly, this game scratches a certain itch I've had. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Stylistically unique, tad short but interesting game. Combat is very janky, sadly simple as that. Put together with focus on using consumable items rather then restoration and cooldowns it does not leave the best impressions initially.It gets better the more time you put in it but it does take a certain mindset to get a hang of the game. If you approach it expecting just another standard metroidvania only with fun pixel art style, you're gonna get disappointed and/or annoyed.Worth checking out still, I had fun with it and am willing to spend more time to complete higher difficulty and other game modes. It's nice to see devs succesfully putting a spin on old, set in stone mechanics or genres and ending up with something that actually works, as janky as the result might be.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game is suprisingly amazing for being an indie Metroidvania by a small studio. I went though the effort to 100% it and go for achievements, which is something I never do. I feel confident giving this an 8/10. It was only bogged down by minor pacing issues and balancing. I'm an instant fan of this studio now!Update: I have played this game for nearly 40 hours now and just 100% complete it. It is a very good game, but there is a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ involved in it. Enemies that die and you have to wait for them to explode to pass (or fire burning on the ground for 10 seconds straight before it goes out). There's a lot of messy stuff that makes the fun harder to get to, but it is still very fun.

Very much recommended!The "mix equipment" system is nice, but sometimes you find yourself changing the same set of equipments over and over. It would be nice if you could save "recipes".

I reached what I assume is the first boss and getting there was not enjoyable. HP recovery is very sparse and the enemy moveset has incredible range right out of the gate. Also no silly fashion endgame since gear does not appear to show up on your character.Maybe I'll start it up again sometime in the future on baby easy mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Reading some of the reviews I thought I was going to get filtered hard but I think the game on "Recommended" has the perfect difficulty, you just have to be careful, consider your items and use them, I'm one of those who hoards items and barely pays any attention to status, bonus modifiers and such yet I was constantly looking forward and gearing for the next challenge, I hit some walls ofc but checkpoints are plentiful as long as you prevail you will make it, if I did I'm sure you will. If you are struggling Shields and Poison are your best friends.Pixel art was gorgeous and while the characters only had like 3 portraits they were quite alluring on their designs, really looking forward from the devs if they have more projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is a metroidvania with souls like mechanics and quirky anime girls you may or may not care about. There are outfits and items you collect that benefit you (such as  a swimsuit so you can cast shock while standing in water without dying and oven mitts that protect you from fire). You start off with low hp (20 total). You recover your hp by using items that work like estus flasks, so you can die while healing. There are status debuffs, such as bleeds, that can instantly kill you.The level of difficulty and the time spent playing this game is mainly reliant on which difficulty you are playing (there are a bunch of them). IF you are playing on the default difficulty, be prepared to basically die all the time. the game is not "short". It's the same length as your typical metroidvania, and said length is based off game mode/skill/ familiarity.Having never played this before, I just downed the first boss and made it to the second boss in just under 2.5 hours. Most of this time was spent dying constantly.Fun game. A bit quirky with it's themes, but fun none the less.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. A little brutal at first but once you get the hang of the combat and how to use the correct weapon/spells the game seems to unlock. Attacks are queued similar to souls games. I went into this game thinking it would be more of a platformer but once it clicked with me I started to enjoy it more and more. Very difficult at times but the checkpoint system is perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game around launch but it slipped down my list of games to play, I should have played it sooner because I had a lot of fun with it.  For me it was better than some higher rated games in the genre.It may not be the best metroidvania game around and it can be a little clunky with the inventory but it does other things well.  The combination of skills like throwing oil and then setting it on fire or poisoning or freezing water to damage enemies was a nice idea.  Decent story, fun characters, plenty of different skills and weapons to mess around with.Game is a little short but the extra modes you unlock on beating it made up for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I like the way the girl moves like a 1930s rubber hose style cartoon character (especially Betty Boop) when she's stationary. I love the 1930s cartoon aesthetics.I wouldn't say it's the most noteworthy game I've played but the amount of items, different enemies and even game modes was decent. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a metroidvania with methodical combat that emphasises adapting your equipment and weapons to suit the situation. It introduces small yet meaningful changes to its genre, but the tedious UI hampers its execution.  The most apparent aspect of Lost Ruins is its visuals — a contrast of clean, anime-styled characters in a grimy, somewhat realistic environment. It’s a compelling aesthetic for those who like both styles. With its pretty pixel art and portraits in gameplay and dialogue, if you like what you see on the store page, you’ll like what you see in-game.  Lost Ruins also has adequate character animations overall — both in visual appeal and for gameplay purposes. The main character’s idle animation is incredibly animated, in two senses of the word. Environmental lighting is also subtly animated, giving everything a glow that makes enemies and your character easy to distinguish from the background. Most enemies have the appropriate wind up before they attack, giving you a fair chance to dodge and counterattack all but the fastest enemies.  However, similar to older metroidvanias, the main character’s attack feels janky. Every weapon has the same overhead swing at a constant speed, based on their speed stat, so there’s a lacking sense of heft in the heavier weapons.  In spite of its combat animations, combat is still interesting enough to engage in. While the weapon swing and movement are simple, the equipment you obtain over time are diverse and situationally useful. It’s a game that rewards adaptability; swapping to the appropriate equipment according to the environment and enemies you encounter will make fights easier. Whether wading through water or killing fast monsters, there is probably an item that will make obstacles easier to surmount.  As you get further in the game, overpowered combinations of equipment become available and I love it. After cautiously navigating every encounter up to that point, there was an incredible relief in simply rolling over every enemy that once gave me grief.  The need to frequently swap equipment, however, also means you have to navigate the inventory often. It’s cumbersome.  You have to press ‘down’ and ‘up’ to trudge through your extensive lists of items. Even though these are partitioned in helpful categories, these categories are each a single, long vertical column. Most of the items you’ll frequently equip or consume are in 4 categories: weapons, spells, items, and equipment.  You cannot skip ahead by jumping several items at a time. You cannot use your mouse. The only QoL in inventory navigation is the ability to change the sorting order and marking items as “favourites”. Though it’s better than nothing, the “favourites” feature simply keeps your items at the top of each long list, and still requires many button presses since you’ll likely want to keep several “favourites” (maybe six per category). Furthermore, when you want to try new items, it’ll take a while to find.  It’s a small frustration that grates on you as you keep playing on.  Fortunately, the game took me about 10 hrs to beat — including all side objectives, some frivolous achievements, and grinding for equipment and healing items.  Expanding on gameplay a little more, there’s the matter of difficulty. Having beat the game on “Recommended”, I would say I had a comfortably tense experience.  You can pause to heal in the middle of battle, but these are two key limitations that hinder such boring brute force. Firstly, the most common healing items regenerate 1 HP per second. Secondly, instant heals are expensive and tedious to obtain in large quantities. Not impossible, but tedious.  On the first encounter with a new enemy, you are given room to fight it on its own, allowing you to learn its behaviour and abilities. You are then continually introduced to new combinations of enemies, each addition a compounding threat to your life. Fast enemies allow slow ones to attack. Some hinder your movements. Nearly every enemy can kill you if you carelessly swing at them.   If you die, you lose your progress up to your last save point. In a strangely refreshing way, this classic way of handling death works well. Given the increasing prevalence of ‘running to your corpse to take back your money’ in newer games, I think I like restarting with all your money and items still on you. The consumables you spent before death will return, so you don’t have to worry about making subsequent retries unnecessarily difficult. Put in combination with the autosave point right before boss fights, I never felt unduly punished for messing up.  There is a hardcore mode, and new challenge modes unlock after beating the game, but I have not played them, so I cannot comment on those.  All in all, it’s rather . Lost Ruins’ most interesting feature as a metroidvania is that it rewards the player’s adaptability just as much as their skill with the controls. Yet, this very selling point is hindered by tedious menu navigation as you frequently swap out your equipment.  Its difficulty is well paced. Its visuals are as you see on the store page.  It’s not a must-buy, but you might like this.

_childDocuments_.review: So I got this as part of a Humble Bundle. It's a little pricey in my opinion, but $20 isn't bad for what it is. With the other options out there, I thought it might have been $15.The graphics are pretty good and things are usually easy to distinguish. As others have noted, a way to switch between two equip sets would have been nice, but once you get used to the game the inventory management really doesn't feel that bad. It's mostly the first playthrough that it feels a bit much. That said, the game reminded me quite a bit of Circle of the Moon, one of my personal favorite Castlevania games so maybe I'm just used to opening up my inventory to switch minor things around.I will say that once you get into the artifacts and how they affect your weapon swing speed, it honestly kind of hurts the game. Some weapons show up too late to be particularly useful and even "fast" weapons can feel pretty sluggish, so knowing your character's attack speed is pretty important. It makes some weapons kind of superfluous though. And that's kind of what makes the inventory more bearable after you have more experience with the game too: some weapons will just feel better or be able to do better things.Due to the dev's focus on survival, there are no quick refill points. You either have to spend an artifact slot or weapon slot or eat a consumable. The inventory sorts by newest by default, but it can also be sorted by name, so knowing that is also very helpful towards good inventory management once you understand what items cure or nullify certain effects.Enemies can be run past or cheesed in various ways (water has several cheesy things you can do to enemies inside while mitigating the effect on  your character through consumables or artifacts). They either drop consumables or pittances of gold, so don't worry about fighting every enemy. Bosses are where the combat really comes into play in figuring out patterns, openings, vulnerabilities, and even environmental hazards that you can take advantage of. Most of the bosses have two major phases: a player-sized form and a big form that has its own phases. If you know what you're doing late-game, the bosses with defined phases are pretty easy to cheese, which is kind of good if you want to attempt the Hardcore difficulty.Overall, it's good and can be beaten in a few hours. Once the game is beaten, you unlock a Castlevania-like boss mode and two modes that focus on spellslinging or crits that really remind me of COTM's extra modes. It's a nice little bonus that changes the way you play without making tons of changes. The major weapons and artifacts with effects that don't make sense for the mode (such as attack speed buffs in Witch Mode) get new effects thematically appropriate to the mode (like a casting speed buff instead) and become either active or passive artifacts instead of normal equips. I'm not kidding about a few hours per playthrough either. I've beaten it four times so far on different modes with only assassin and hardcore left.So it has balancing issues with its weapons and spells (there are a few absolutely amazing options and a lot of eeehhhh.... ones by comparison). I really wish the default attack speed was faster and didn't stop your forward momentum dead in the air. I also really wish there was some sort of more plentiful healing available that wasn't consumable or equipment based since that partially exacerbates the balance issues. The story isn't going to blow anyone away and it's a little ecchi at times with character designs. The music is balanced pretty low and is fairly lowkey "ambient sense of dread" for most of the game though there are a few nice tracks. That said, finding the little tricks to recover health or make certain rooms easier when attempting to collect most of the stuff is still fun. Finding the best boss strategies to balance out your damage and survivability was quite fun, like little puzzles, and environmental effects add a bit more depth that I appreciate. The extra modes add a bit more replayability to the experience as well. It is a little hard to recommend for $20 with its flaws and quirks, but it's a solid game built around map exploration and equipment combos.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little Metroidvania with only a handful of very minor stumbling blocks.As the biggest pro, the spire artwork and animation is consistently amazing. Light sources reflect dynamically on the characters which gives the scenes an incredible feeling of depth. Attack animations have a good amount of heft to them, though slower two-handed animations look a bit floaty instead of giving a feeling of 'gravity' to the swing arc. For enemies, all attacks are well telegraphed and simple to read.Combat has an odd mix of slightly floaty weapons with punishingly strict committal, though enemies are forced just as much to watch their attack whiff as you jab them in the back with a dagger, which makes the combat 'fair' for both parties, at least as long as you manage to keep it to a 1v1. Fighting multiple enemies at once is more often than not suicidal and sometimes you best choice is to run away or leave and reenter the room, resetting all still living enemies while dead ones remain temporarily disposed of (moving through enough rooms will revive all enemies in passed rooms). Weapons can feel somewhat floaty because one-handed and two-handed weapons are swung in an arc, but that arc has a steady speed throughout the entire animation, which can make especially slow attack swings feel very weak and weightless. Since being able to modify the swing speed through equipment is an option, I'm not sure if there is an elegant solution to that however.I think the biggest roadblock a lot of people will face getting used to combat isn't its grounded attacks, but the fact that attacking mid-jump will completely void all horizontal momentum, meaning that if you attack while jumping forward you will just drop straight down instead. This paired with how the game likes to place ranged enemies across precarious jumps makes platforming a lot more dangerous than one would expect from a very platforming-focused metroidvania.The typical solution to that of course represent magic and the disposable single-use wands that litter the environment. Magic is tied to MP which does not naturally regenerate, meaning you have to rely on consumables to refresh your MP or use equipment with provides you with some level of MP recovery. Wands are a reasonably abundant resource, but they are still limited in use, so they're best reserved for situations where melee would be too dangerous to commit to or open a handful of doors that require magic to activate their respective levers.For the minor stumbling blocks I brought up in the beginning, while combat is pretty fun once you get the hang of it, the game has somewhat of an over-reliance on status effects and DoTs. Pretty much any attack won't just deal flat damage, but also give you increasingly long stacks of bleed, burn or poison, freeze you in place, invert your controls, and so forth. On Veteran difficulty these can also stack repeatedly on additional hits, frequently providing you with DoT effects that exceed even your maximum possible HP. Most ofthese effects can be countered and even temporarily negated with consumables, but in the heat of combat it can feel rather frustrating to have defeated a a single enemy but losing several items just to counter the DoT and replenish the health you've lost just as the result of burning.Traps and trickery are our best allies in this game, learning which enemies are too dangerous to take head-on and how to bypass and/or defeat them without even allowing them to fight back are typically your best choices.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 This game is pretty good. (9/10 for me personally)The Story - itself is what i would say is the 'DMC3 effect' where in that it's entertaining as hell but has some surprising depth to it (and some dark messed up implications) that at some points gave me the feels.Gameplay - will be quite difficult for new players as it was for me but once you narrow down the mechanics it feels really good with all the weapons, ranged weapons and magic at your disposal. The variety of builds you can conjure up is astounding. Not to mention the amazing enemy variety that the game presents that will keep things not only entertaining but challenging as well. Likewise, the bosses really test your skills (and knowledge of mechanics as well).Visuals - are gorgeous and aesthetically pleasing.Loses points - due to the certain items being a bit too strong in that magic builds in the (very) late game are a bit too strong (for me personally). Inventory item swapping and usage (which you'll be doing a lot) can be streamlined further to lessen the monotony of it a bit. Finally, there should've been a new game plus for the veteran difficulty which in my opinion could've added late game enemies to the earlier stages whilst keeping your inventory so you can use all that OP stuff as well as your skill throughout a new replay. Maybe throw in even harder new enemies because why not?Conclusion,Instead of wasting money on some in-game micro-transaction, buy other games and experience something new. Lost Ruins is one of those experiences, simple and entertaining with surprising depth to it. Has its flaws yes, but it is an overall satisfying product in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A really charming game with beautiful, breezy pixel art, lush animation and lighting effects, endearing characters and character portraits, and an enjoyable, fairly mellow soundtrack. The storyline is straightforward and accessible, the finale is satisfying, and overall the game just feels very complete. I really loved the tremendous variety of melee and ranged weaponry, spells, and equipment with powerful and distinct perks - there's a lot more potential for buildcrafting here than you might expect in a typical 2D metroidvania.Combat can be a bit janky; each speed category of melee/spell attack feels a few shades slower than it should, enemy stagger thresholds are a bit inconsistent, etc. Difficulty and damage scaling occasionally feel off - some negative status effects last way longer than feels necessary and are particularly punishing.But these are minor annoyances, and ultimately I found they only encouraged me to dig into the game's diverse toolkit for creative solutions to trouble spots. Enemies who spam shields can be overcome with heavy weapons that ignore blocking; flying enemies who are impossible to target can be brought down with auto-strike spells like Chain Lightning; monsters with low stagger points can be crippled with Orb abilities, etc. etc. The game throws a lot at you, but always equips you with the tools to handle it. I found myself constantly switching up my loadout throughout the game's reasonable ~7 hour runtime. It was a great feeling that made for a varied gameplay loop, and I really credit Altari Games for engineering that.Lost Ruins might not satisfy people looking for a more hardcore experience or snappier combat, but I really enjoyed my time with the game, and definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a quick metroidvania with some gentler anime aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess you can say the game have an Isekai story, but sadly it is so simplistic and it have an OBVIOUS AS ♥♥♥♥ villain that you won't bother with the details. Well, to be fair it has a plot twist that could have been interesting…but let be honest, we are here for the action and the cute girls. So it is metroidvania with a classic save system! Normal to God save! YES! I like those so much! No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ autosaves and collecting your exp again trying to not die again. The start feels a little hard at first, but believe me when I say this: you will end up changing different play styles to suit your needs non-stop because it is so much fun! My earlier build was using a fast axe and a shield which with each block I healed myself, then I switched to magical swords and healing spells with armor/weapons filling my mana pool over and over again,oh and a demon bear doll that when it gets hit I get mana back. Getting back on track, another thing I liked a lot was the nice art of the characters when you had a chance to talk to them. I have big praise for some specific monster girls. My favorite from all of them is Jun. Ironically her reveal was also the biggest plot twist as well. A big negative I had (aside from the forgettable story) was the map. It is detailed enough to show you where you are going, painfully bland when you want to reach specific items. Also you can fail a mission if you are not careful, a very important one. If you are a metroidvania fan who also wants an extra challenge managing your loot and gear, and cute anime girls, "Lost Ruins" is the perfect choice.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little metroidvania! Recommended for fans of the genre who want something with some bite, or for those who like cute anime girls.Takes a little bit to get the hang of the rhythm of combat, but once you do it's pretty smooth and not too terribly difficult, while still having some challenge. Has a good focus on resource management that a lot of metroidvanias lack. There's a ton of build variety, it's very fun to play around with different gameplay styles and it's fairly easy to swap between them at will. The pacing of the game does lack at times though - the ability to swap equipment in the middle of combat is both a good and bad thing. It provides lots of flexibility, but also slows things down as there's no reason NOT to constantly swap equipment in the middle of combat as the situation changes, which really slows the otherwise fast-paced combat down. If you don't like fiddling through menus, I'd maybe give this one a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a direct reply to all the negative reviews saying that the combat is clunky.First: I am a total metroidvania noob. I just found interest in the genre a few days ago and this is the first game I am playing. I'm not experienced and also not a die-hard fan who plays every title that comes out.From those reviews, I get the impression that the authors went into the game expecting a hack'n'slay action game. And that is why they were disappointed. "Lost Ruins" is not about rapidly hitting your buttons and slashing though enemies.There ARE enemies that are easiest to defeat if you rush in and hit them before they know what is happening. More often than not though, you need to know what you are doing. Think of it as a beat'em'up, as if you were playing "Guilty Gear". If you mess up, the enemy can often get you in a stunlock and kill you no matter how many HP you had, especially if you face several enemies at once. At the very least, you will lose a lot of HP. If you know how you have to approach an enemy, chances are you can down him without losing any HP at all.Such was the case with the first boss, which frustrated me massively. It didn't help that I was playing the demo and that you couldn't skip cutscenes there (you can in the proper game). Once I found out how to kill the minions and then the boss, I am confident I can do so without getting hit at all. It's not even about hit zones or immunities, it's just movement and attack patterns.The game doesn't want to give you endless action. It's about ressource management and tactical combat movements. The gratification does not come from going in with guns blazing and slaying foe after foe, but from executing just the right movements in just the right timing. That's not to say the game has no speedrun potential, in the contrary. I'm sure you can rush through it if you perfectly memorized each enemy's patterns.Now the game HAS its downsides. Consumables, especially ranged attacks, are semi-finite. You get money and the occasional item from drops and opponents respawn, but mana does not regenerate (HP can, to an extent) and potions are really expensive. This makes me not use anything at all except for boss fights. There are also no quick-use slots for consumables so you have to enter the menu each time, and with a lot of very situational consumables you often don't end up using them even when it would be beneficial. Which is not a real problem if you can stand retrying a room over and over and are not playing hardcore mode or speedrunning.The characters are interesting and quirky and there is a slightly clichéd but entertaining story unfolding. I'm 3 hours in (2 more hours in the demo) and just facing the second boss, and I still like what I am seeing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  The art is absurdly good, and I found the gameplay enjoyable.  I do still have my gripes with this game though.  The story is bare bones and predictable, so if you're interested in amazing story and lore in games, you should look pretty much anywhere else.  The combat is interesting, in the fact that I have zero idea how 3/4 of it works.  I mostly just used melee weapons, however there are bows, a magic system, and items you can throw around to try and give yourself some advantage.  I can't really advocate for anything but melee combat, as I didn't use anything else, but from what I've seen, it's all well made.  I strayed from the others though, as the game kinda forces you into melee early on, and it's hard to break out of that when it works well.  The game is very short.  It only took me a couple hours to beat it the first time, but it has some replay-ability in a separate game mode and multiple challenge modes.  Overall, I'd give the game a 7/10, although maybe wait for it to be on sale since it's so short.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good at what it's trying to do, but definitely not for everyone.The game sets itself apart from most platformers with a veneer of player hostility in most of its design elements--weapons attack slowly, many weapons are single use, your dodge roll is clumsy, enemies deal brutal damage with quick attacks, HP and MP aren't refilled for free anywhere, etc.However, it's kind of a smokescreen. Healing items are showered on you as you go, the AI is braindead, and many of the items are gamebreaking (including items that grant infinite free healing/MP refills, negate all traps/bad terrain, and infinite use ranged weapons).Fortunately, none of that stops it from FEELING like you're triumphing over stacked odds and an unfair game. It's just hostile enough to feel good finding and using the stuff that's broken. You will have to proceed slowly and use your brain, but it's not actually that difficult except a few spots.Other stuff: Visuals are quite good with great monster design and great animations. Enemy design+variety is pretty good. Boss design is hit-or-miss. Despite looking like a metroidvania basically none of the stuff you gain are used for exploration or movement.

As soon as you get HP regen, you're set. Runes are broken, especially when you get the rune stone. The puzzles were honestly the absolute worst part of the entire game. _childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania that feels like it was made by a small team which has some truly awful combat.  You can equip one special item and two weapons, but early enemies are either slow and plodding or have ranged attacks that they let off in quick succession.  Many fights were 'hold shield to block projectile, move up, block projectile, move up, block projectile, strike, wait, block projectile, wait, block projectile, strike...'Arial combat causes you to stop moving and drop as you swing.  You can equip a special item to slightly help, but this is in place of better options like a damage booster.  Other items are misleading, such as a 'slingshot' not being a weapon but instead an item that improves the damage of a limited number of consumable thrown grenades.  Magic is already powerful and if you have MP you can waste difficult enemies. The thing that made me end up refunding the game so early on is the save system.  You can save at a small number of computer stations and you automatically save when you encounter a statue.  But you can't autosave at the same statue until you've saved at another one.  This feels like an attempt to make a slower, more deliberate form of gameplay but it feels overly restrictive along with the other issues.  It seems average at best and even watching a few videos showing where the story will go did not make me want to continue.  The cadence of combat just isn't worth the frustration to me, but I'm dead certain that it will 'click' for the right people and be an enjoyable (but too short) experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly simple action game that's somewhat on the short side but is bursting with charm. Visuals are top-notch. I especially like the giant monster girl boss art. Gameplay is pretty fun. The story however is predictable and nothing special, but there are giant monster girl bosses. More games should have giant monster girl bosses.Combat is quite good for how simple it is. Equip weapons and/or spells and press button to use. For the most part (boss mode has some special attacks when jumping) no fancy combos, special attacks when crouching, jumping or dodging, just swing your weapon or cast your spell. There's a fair variety in weapon and spell types with different attack speeds, reach, damage and status effects which when combined with the accessory system that allows you to further affect those offensive as well as your defensive capabilities leaves a plethora of approaches all perfectly viable. Experimenting with different builds throughout the game was pretty fun. Enemy design is done well and encourages that experimentation with various builds; you can't always just run up to all the enemies the same way, attack and back off, a somewhat common fault of more simple action games. The downside to the equipment variety combined with amount of different consumables is that you'll find yourself in the menu longer than you'd like to be. This hassle is somewhat offset by the ability to favorite items bringing them to the top of your list, but still can be an annoyance.

The first boss is probably the hardest, after that things get progressively easier due to the sheer amount of weapons options you collect.My main criticism would be that the final boss is a bit dissapointing, The game is about 8 hours long on the default difficulty, if you take your time, but I'd still say it was well worth it. _childDocuments_.review: This was a short and sweet but very entertaining game for me!  It is most easily compared to as being a Souls-like side scroller, where fighting even the simplest enemy takes a bit of thinking and patience, and save points are preset bonfires that reset the entire area of all spawns.You are given free roam very early on, to explore and find enemies in any order you see fit with almost no hand holding whatsoever.  It is a small content filled world with a lot to discover and a lot of interesting little sidequests to complete.  And the way you can build your fighting style can vary quite a bit.  You could go for quick attacking weapons with bleeds, slower hard hitting weapons, or numerous spellcasting builds to get through the game in any way you see fit.  Some things are a bit awkward, such as momentum loss when attacking midair, but they are all just the rules of the world you abide by to get through.  The writing and humour is charming, and the story itself is simple but fun to experience.Would recommend this game.  It has lots of replayability as well, with different challenge modes unlocking by completing the first run of the game, as well as multiple endings depending on how you do things.If anyone's interested in my blind run through, here is a let's play I recorded! :)

Give it a try, it's quite worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a fun game that doesn't overstay it's welcome.  As far as Metroidvanias go, it's not overly complex, which is something I appreciate.  Playing on "recommended" difficulty, I never had much of a problem progressing, but that's not to say it isn't easy to die, especially if you aren't careful or appropriately prepared.  Most encounters, including boss fights, can be made significantly less difficult by having the right combination of spells and equipment, so the game becomes less about overcoming difficulty and more about puzzling out the correct strategy.  Other things worth mentioning are the fact that check points and save spots are numerous and forgiving, minimizing the frustration of dying.  Also, the game is rather generous about marking stuff like treasures, NPC locations, and quest items on your map, and the fast travel system makes backtracking to find stuff you missed pretty painless.  There also seems to be quite a bit of replay value with the extra modes that are unlocked after finishing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a metroidvania that tries to offer combat that rewards throughtful use of tactics and cunning rather than quick reflexes, and though i think it fails in that regard i still think it's an enjoyable game.Simply put, there are too many OP pieces of equipment for the combat to ever significantly challenge the player. The only challenge comes from analyzing a situation and equipping whatever pieces of equipment deals with it. Player creativity is rarely required, mostly exploiting game mechanics. However, since death comes very easily, it still feels good to overcome the obsctacles Lost Ruins presents you with, even though it is usually in spite of its design rather than in tandem with it.Knowing this, what does the game get right ? simply put, it feels good to play; movement hits a good balance between weighty and responsive and weapons are varied enough to justify switching loadouts often. It's also pleasant to the eyes and ears, with a fitting if forgettable soundtrack and wonderful pixel art. Finally, the story is surprisingly enjoyable: it is self aware and jokey in tone, but the finale adds an unexpected layer of emotion that sends it off nicely.If you're interested in a metroidvania with slow, almost puzzle like combat, give REDO! a try. I think it succeeds in that regard much better than this game. Otherwise, Lost Ruins is a perfectly fine way to spend 7 hours exploring a good looking world and interacting with a flawed but interesting combat system. Some of the game modes you unlock after beating it are also very cool and let you get more bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously the game is very beautiful, great visuals/lighting, music and sound, lovely art style and characters with some meme dialog. That much you know. I'm waiting warmly for the anime~Has a cute story, with a twist that only comes by completing a specific quest. Story is a balance of being interesting enough without slowing down the gameplay too much, all the dialog scenes are skippable and they're not too long. Some metroidvanias suffer from too much forced story sequence slow-down of the gameplay but that's not a problem here thankfully. So you can easily just pick up and play the game for an hour without being bogged in some forced cut scenes that you've already seen 30 times or having to spam past pages of dialog and tutorials, this makes the game very replayable for me. This is so rare in modern games, probably as an attempt to pad out the playtime. With Lost Ruins there's a world and characters that are there if you want it, but its short and sweet, direct and to the point and also skippable. This alone is a huge plus for me.There's three endings and five modes, all of which are fun and unique. This is good because be aware that each playthrough is not very long. In 25 hours I have completely 100% the game, I plan to replay it more even though I've seen all the content.Gameplay is excellent each enemy has certain weaknesses and status effects they can inflict, the gameplay loop is almost Pokemon-like, at each screen you pause to consume some items and equip some loadout that is suitable for the specific weakness / strength of the enemies on that screen. Finding the optimal config for each screen makes it, in a way, more of a puzzle game than an action game. One flaw is that after some time it can get tiring to be constantly swapping equipment back and forth. You can mark favorite equipment that will stay at the top of your list, but it'd be nice to be able to save equipment configurations and then swap between them. Half of my playtime is spent in the menu manually swapping between 3-4 equipment setups. Also the sorting seems to keep resetting for me, I can never get the menu to stay in alphabetic sort mode for long.The game makes a solid attempt to balance all the playstyles that it offers, you can max bleed damage or dagger criticals or slow two-handers etc, some loadouts are strictly superior to others though. The game is also simply not that difficult so once you get a good feel for the controls you can choose your favorite build and beeline through the entire game with it if you want to, it will just be less optimal than switching equipment for each screen / area.There are many status effects and environmental reactivity, a lot of the fun of the game is discovering all of these. You can beat enemies in many creative ways if you want to.Both your character and the enemies are bulky and slow so this is more of a souls-like feel as opposed to other metroidvanias where you zip around the screen double-jumping with tight controls. You can easily die simply because you swung too early or you rolled one pixel too short or you misjudged distance and didn't land within your weapon's reach before you swing. It's not a flaw just be aware that's the type of game this is.In the normal mode magic is powerful and scarce for the first half of the map because your MP is so limited, in the second half of the map this flips and you suddenly have infinite MP. Because the map is not that long, the power creep feels wild, you very quickly go from helpless scared schoolgirl to an enemy-shredding god. Initially most healing items are heal over time, which is great, then you quickly get many instant-heal items. The game would be much challenging if instant restore items were more rare or didn't exist at all. There are also items that heal you over time when you're under some status effect, this makes for some cool combos but kinda makes the game too easy because you can exploit this. There are other items that heal you whenever you deal some type of damage to enemies, it'd be better if the game forced you to rely on those more or exclusively, meaning that you have to take a risk to restore your health, which is a little more engaging. It's weird that the game has this cool "you have to deal damage to heal" mechanic built-in but then invalidates it by giving you so many other easier options to restore health.I would love to see a sequel with a larger map and more challenging enemies / screens. The biggest "flaw" if there is any, is that there's simply so many cool weapons / spells / abilities / etc that don't truly get a chance to shine because there's just not enough truly challenging encounters. The health of enemies is pretty low, so there's no bosses that last more than 2-3 cycles and most enemies explode with one or two shots. This game would be a perfect candidate for some kinda lunatic mode DLC. Double the amount of enemies, double their health and make enemies a bit more mobile, and this would be a radically different game with way more opportunity to milk the different mechanics.As it is though the game is still a joy to play, absolutely worth the money, to me this is an almost perfect metroidvania. It feels like playing through an episode of an anime. Also what happened to poor Jun-chan ;_;

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be blasted for being basically a waifu-vania with how plentiful the amount of suggestive monster girls are the selling point of this game. Surprisingly though, game is about as hard as Momodora while still being forgiving as metroidvanias go, in a sense that with the right item combination in the right situation any level can become almost a cake-walk.And that's where I'm impressed by how well utilized are many of the equipments and weaponries you find throughout the game. Besides notable exceptions, many items in this game feel like they're perfectly made for their right purpose and for the right area, which makes the extremely limited equipment that you can use at once the more strategic  to utilize since there are many items that would make for outright broken hero thanks to clever damage stacking.The only main issue I have with this game, as common to any game I have with consumables is that if you're being too careful with the resource management you just end up getting through the game just fine without seeing much of other possible weapon strats, simply because they become less lucrative when, for the most part, melee can solve almost any combat scenario just as fine, and later on it even becomes possible to not run out of mana so that spamming magic from afar is totally an option as well.Not that I think the game's difficulty is any too easy per say, but rather that I'd wish there were more difficulties like witch mode or other creative ways to be able to experience the rest of the varieties in combat the game has to offer.All in all, game has an acquired taste in style that might put some people off due to excessive anime looks, but I'd still recommend this as not only a good metroidvania, but a metroidvania that actually felt different for a change.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. Have heard several people describe this as a Metroidvania - and while I can see where they're coming from, because it superficially LOOKS a lot like one, there really isn't this sort of "gain ability and backtrack a lot thing". Sure you can do that, but there's no required backtracking, though some enemies are easier to kill and some obstacles easier to bypass with later abilities.There's an elemental system with limited environmental effects (freezing/electrifying water, setting goo on fire, that sort of thing - but also things like "you recover HP when you set yourself on fire", "electrified water doesn't hurt you"). This can be quite fun to play around with as you discover ways to abuse this to your advantage.This is also generally how boss fights play out. While there's still the whole thing of learning patterns and what not, and technically you *could* beat all bosses just like that, the most effective way to deal with enemies is finding what combination of equipment and consumables works best, disable your opponents strengths and target their weaknesses. Again, to me that was very fun, but people used to some other games might be disappointed that fights are more about picking the best tools for the job than they are about super skillful moment to moment gameplay. Basically, the enemies are cheating bastards but you can throw everything they do right back at them.The game has a decent length for what it is, it took me about 15 hours to reach the true ending, and there are some challenge modes that unlock afterwards.If there is one somewhat disappointing aspect it would the plot - or rather, the lack thereof. The character designs are all pretty neat, but the characters themselves are all pretty one-note, and there's not really that much going on other than a bit of banter and then tearing each others throats out. Some of the characters have some more background or quirky character details, but it never amounts to a whole lot even if there's individually nothing wrong with it per se.Overall a pretty solid game, definitely worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost ruins is a adventure game that is basically based on dungeon exploration and boss fights.History(7/10): It is kind simple, basically, you are a student girl that has been summoned in a alternative world,inside of a dungeon  fully of monsters and traps and does not has any fragment of memory from her past life, so she meet beatrice, a mysterious girl that will guide you in your adventure and explain that each boss you defeat, you will be able to recover your memory.You will find some non hostile npcs, basically quests and merchants characters.I honestly miss a bit more development of our protagonist and the bosses, there are 3 main bosses that dont differ in development from the others, you just defeat them and..thats it,you wont find a complex background history about them.Gameplay(8/10): It is simple, if you learn to roll in the right moment, you will avoid almost all attacks from the enemies and does not have a variaty of combos,movement and etc. But it has a good variaty of weapons and equipment that have unique atributs that will be very useful in specific situations.And before forget to mention, this game has a long duration(+10 hours of gameplay) if you try to complete all story modes.Soundtrack and Art(8/10): this game has beautiful graphics and a simple but good soundtrack. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, if you expect some kind of anime boobie game this is definitely not it. There is some content you could say is a tiny bit like that but that just devles down to the anime aesthetics.What you will get instead is a solid metroidvania with more emphasis on surviving and managing resources. Enemies hit like a truck and your attacks especially the heavier weapons are slow. Means you have to actually think about how to approach every encounter. If not you might end up dying because of a lack of I-frames when you get hit.The enviroment can also be hazardous, so that is also something you gotta watch out for. Status effects are severe and will eventually cost you your life if not treated. There is magic and it's pretty fun to use but due to items being very limited too it is hard to maintain a proper mp pool (without the right equipment/items) for magic usage which again emphasises the resource management aspect. The pixelarstyle and overall tone of the game is amazing and i really enjoy the artstyle for the dialouge models too. And if that wouldn't be enough if you played through the game you also get access to more content that explains certain stuff about the lore (aside from the multiple endings).In conclusion, i definitely recommend this game to anoyne that likes a challenge and metriodvania style gameplay, especially if it's on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: highly recommend the game, it's a bit short but very fun, the interactivity mechanic with the enviroment and all the different item, equipment, weapons, and spell really allows you to cutomize your playstyle. The slower weapons that packs a punch really force you to plan your strike aheads and learn the pattern of your enemies, the small hp and mp bar combined with no limitation as to when can you open ur inventory makes traversing the world more of a resource management where you use specific items to deal with specific situation, especially since theres no heal spot so all healing or mana refill must either come from items or effects from equipment.the additional modes after clearing the game for the first time was a welcome surprise. assasin and witch mode locks you into only using only daggers and spells respectively, and the boss mode was a nice change where instead of changing weapons you now play as a three in one character.overall was a really nice experience
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game sits in a rather interesting cross roads of genres. In basic concept and overarching gameplay loop, it's a Metroidvania. You explore a series of rooms making up an interconnected world, defeat bosses and gain upgrades or adjustments to your kit along the way.That's about as far as the comparison goes however.The moment to moment gameplay is not like any other Metroidvania, it's combat and attacks are slow and seemingly clunky. The fastest attacks still leave you standing still for a good while, and while you have a dodge roll it's start up and recovery times mean it's not good for much beyond dodging an attack and disengaging, you'll almost always get hit if you attack to counter after rolling. The game is rather difficult initially as a result, though I did play on the Veteran difficulty for my first play through.However, this kind of gameplay is intentional, and the game is for the most part built around it. It's much less focused on the action of the gameplay, rather it rewards care in exploring the world and taking to careful preparation. The game lacks real upgrades to it, bosses drop stat upgrades or equipment slots rather than new abilities, and throughout the game you'll be collecting an entire variety of spells, weapons and accessories that can drastically modify your loadout and how you can approach situations. Early on the slow nature of combat made me gravitate towards the fastest weapon I could find, but soon I found that using a large heavy weapon was much more successful thanks to the range it gave me and the ability to control the fight by making enemies have to close the distance with me instead, and often times I could kill enemies in one or two hits. The game wants you to be slow and careful, and use the right tool for the job, and you'll be much more successful adjusting what your kit is depending on what you're fighting.The game does have a bit of a difficulty issue around this though. Being very stingy with money and offering no free heals, the early game is arguably the hardest part of the game as you lack the tools needed to properly strategize and play around the situations in front of you. The first boss was certainly the hardest for me, even with equipment that let me move quickly or heal in her arena, it'd certainly have been even worse if I hadn't explored before approaching her. However by the mid game, with the proper use of consumables and equip loads I was able to start killing bosses in only a handful of hits, with the final boss needing less than ten hits if you set yourself up to deal large amounts of damage. As well, magic started out as a valuable and scarce resource in the early game that slowly became my main method of clearing out mobs once I'd gained items to let me passive regenerate mana in the late game. While being able to fight only with spells was cool, magic is also incredibly strong and much of the game's moment to moment difficulty was diminished. On one hand I was rewarded for gathering and using all the tools I could, but I given the ability to simply roll over any non boss enemy purely with spells. Also, dev if you read these, please add some kind of loadout system, often times I had to menu through a cluttered inventory as I wanted to get the achievements for collecting items and it became rather annoying to swap everything out even with a favorite's system. As well, the ability to resave at checkpoint statues instead of having to leave to activate a different one is a much needed QoL change.Over all, I'd recommend the game. It's not a hack and slash, and shouldn't be approached that way. The art style obviously has a bit of a lewd anime girl trend in a similar vein to Shantae, but I wouldn't say it detracts from the game much and the overall aesthetic and featured art is quite good. There's not much to write home about on the story, it's alright with a decent twist at the end and some of the characters can be amusing or quirky.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game that can be cleared in a day or less. The combat feels nice and continuing is not too hard, but checkpoints don't restore health which means continuing is painful sometimes. One criticism I will level at the game is that if you want the best ending you have to actively refrain from opening chests that grant some very useful equipment, which means spending the majority of the game underpowered. While this is an appropriate level of challenge for the "golden ending", it takes the form of a side quest with no indication that this side quest is crucial to attaining said golden ending. Worse is that the reward is very mediocre gameplay-wise by the time you get it, so people who don't look up guides/don't care about the story will feel disappointed by this. Combat balancing is rather...iffy. As mentioned earlier, if you follow the side quest then you'll probably spend the majority of the game running away from enemies as there are no experience, gold can't get you good equipment (which is where most of the gameplay benefits come from). On the other hand, if you ignore said quest and open every chest you find, you will soon discover some very broken combo like infinite mana regen which makes most bosses a cakewalk. This can be achieved before fighting the third story boss. But if you're into min-maxing strats then this is an obvious buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes developers come up with concoctions for game ideas that sound fantastic on paper, but when thrown into the pot, mixed up and served create something... interesting. Lost Ruins is a game with elements of difficulty similar to what a player would expect from Dark Souls, with tight controls that work flawlessly and of course the spice of beautifully done pixel artwork and animation. Lost Ruins’ goal is mostly to present a difficult metroidvania style game, with an emphasis on combat, which the game is wildly successful at doing. The player is present many ways to dispatch their enemies from a good variety of melee weapons to throwable items and magic. Of course that's not all as you also have a variety of items that can alter the game mechanics such as giving you health back with attacks or allowing you briefly float. These types of items can vastly change your approach to combat.There is more here than running and gunning or just slashing away like a madman until things die. The player will have to actually really take care with their approach because this game is relentless. Don’t come into the ruins expecting to not die, because you most certainly will.Not only are the enemies and combat very thought out, but the level design had some consideration that shows. Some encounters with your foes almost are like puzzles with multiple solutions. At times there can be the very simple solution, but others not so much due to very creatively placed dangerous traps. Within the labyrinth in Lost Ruins you will find traps and hurdles in many forms. Obviously there are enemies, but we are talking about something very different. Elements such as poison toxins and oil on the ground that can slow you down, but even more alarming, oil can catch fire, burning you.  Also, even getting wet from water has its effects that the player must consider. These elements can be used to your advantage, so be vigilant in using your head as well as your sword.As far as story goes in Lost Ruins, there is a dash of it here, but nothing more than most would expect from a metroidvania title. More-so than not, the story-line is just there as an excuse to move you from point A to point B. Story is there, but don’t come in looking for some classic RPG depth as this is not that style of game.Although I have to admit, this type of game is not for everyone, there is a part of me that thinks there is something here that creates a nice blend that anyone could enjoy. Some players may find a little more struggle than others, but it isn’t so difficult that it’d be hopeless  for an average player to succeed. Lost Ruins is a fantastic game that not only presents a very well done gaming experience, but also comes at a very affordable price-point. If you are a player who wants the best bang for your buck, then you have just come across a stick of dynamite. Lost Ruins is a must buy in my opinion and from a development team we definitely want to keep in the development world.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and brief. Worth picking up on sale, for sure. I finished my first playthrough on hard mode after just a handful of hours, no guides or breaks needed.Enemies are varied, but extraordinarily simple. Most have exactly one unique attack; a handful of larger minions have two; bosses have, by and large, three per phase. Their art is well-styled and cohesive. All enemies have tells and consistent AI. The bosses are all young women that embody various fetishes, like slime girls, succubi, and a few other less-decent ones, but only the art plays off of that; the limited conversations and lore are completely nonsexual (with the exception of one comedic quest giver who exists to reference erotica from The Elder Scrolls).It controls like a classic post-SotN Castlevania game, with a few exceptions. The most notable is that swinging a weapon cancels all sideways momentum and controls. Startup and end lag is significant on most weapons, and you'll have to learn how to approach and disengage from each enemy individually. Back dashes are replaced with a Souls-like dodge with very forgiving i-frames and infinite uses.While I've heard complaints about the combat feeling slow or unwieldy, I enjoyed it. Some enemies or bosses are fast enough to swing twice before the slowest weapons can swing once, but they're rare. (Plus, slow weapons are going to be the least flexible -- why should you be able to tackle every threat that exists using only a greatsword?)While this game is tagged as a Metroidvania, you don't collect new movement options, there are no secretly-breakable walls, and the game is entirely linear with no necessary backtracking. Attack options (weapons and spells) are collected or bought throughout the game, including in one-screen optional areas that are barely hidden. Puzzles are simple and small.The developers also describe the game as "survival", but I disagree. Free, unlimited, unconditional regeneration is available before the first boss (for a toggleable penalty to max HP that you can switch off once you're healed), there's a checkpoint every third or fourth screen, and unless you choose the permadeath difficulty, you can simply treat the consumables as you always do: as things to be hoarded and unused.Lastly, I very much like the flexibility offered by the environment. Acid on the ground will poison you, but if you light it on fire, it will burn anything that touches it until it's exhausted. Casting ice spells in water will indefinitely chill it to damaging levels for both you and foes. Certain surfaces and regions are "sticky" and slow you down. It's all intuitive, and it's neither over- nor under-used.Overall, heartily recommended. It's a cute fusion of gameplay elements that doesn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after refunding another game for around $20, and decided I'd play this as a meme to stream to my friends. Then I kept playing it. Then I beat the game, then I started a new game, then another one. Needless to say, this game is really good, addictive certainly, with a gameplay loop that really gripped me.Lost Ruins is a classic dungeon crawl. The controls are clunky, which perfect encapsulates the idea of being a stupid high school girl swinging a zweihander around. However, the clunky controls are likely the biggest hurdle, and in my opinion they warp what seems like an action game into a strategic one. There are many weapons to choose from, all of which halt your momentum when you use them, forcing you to take it slow. If slow isn't your style, this probably isn't the game for you. You can also lobotimize yourself and make the game a cakewalk by using spells and exploiting weaknesses; there's nothing quite like fighting the first boss, getting annihilated, taking a step back and thinking about the nature of the boss and the arena, and then cheesing the boss to death by abusing the hell out of elemental combinations. This is replicated for most bosses, and even sitatuations, you don't have to bash your skull in and just "get gud", there's different strategies to try, and I managed to make the game a cakewalk before the halfway mark just by minmaxing my stats to godhood. Truly euphoric.The artstyle... look, let's not beat around the bush. It's anime, monster girls, and the like. I can't even pretend to do the "horny" joke, because I'm not a huge fan of the genre, but I will admit the farther along I got, the more tolerable, and even enjoyable the artwork became. This is a discussion on the artwork, as in still frames, if we're talking about pixel work, dear lord it's amazing. The Japanese anime thing might not be a selling point for some, but it's undeniable that if it could be done justice, they have gone above and beyond. You can tell that Altari Games really care about the game they made here.So, after having no lifed the game and nearly completed all modes, I can say this game is pretty dang good. I do have some minor gripes with it; for example, I was looking forward to the idea of unlockable characters after the game, and while I did get that, it wasn't really the length I was hoping. Again, what you get it well worth it, I just wish after playing all the modes there was more here, a compliment if anything, and a testament to my enjoyment of the game. Also the story is... not great. It's serviceable, but don't get this game if you want a branching story. The game seems to do best when it does the story of: "small snippets of messages left behind, you fill in the blanks" kind of story telling, the main story itself is nothing to write home about.Finally, this isn't a particularly long game. Once you figure out what works, the game is going to start breezing, or at least it did for me. Still, with the alternate game types you'll get around 10 hours or so, and even still something you could always boot back up to mindlessly play in the background once you've mastered it. Great game, would recommend, Witch mode is busted.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a triumph. The animation is gorgeous, evocative of an extremely well made doujin game but without the jank. There's just world's of choice for how you tackle the combat and puzzles, daggers, swords, magic, status effects, item combos that stack together for enhanced effectiveness, this is a game that begs you to try and explore all it has to offer you. The combat is tough, not unfair, but learning enemy patterns and your own range and speed is crucial to success. The game itself isn't terribly long, my first playthrough with tons of deaths and playing around with items came out to about 6 hours. But the end isn't the end, especially on your first playthrough. There are alternative modes, you can play as some of the bosses in a side campaign, and the variety of items and weapons invite trying multiple play styles.I came into this game blind, and at first the combat felt very slow and deliberate, but it doesn't have to stay that way. Before the first boss you've got access items which will increase your attack speed, weapons with various speeds, spells, one use combat items that pack a punch, and a variety of ways to tackle the problems the game puts in front of you. You get very few upgrades, basically those only come in the form of the artifacts you get from bosses and sidequests. In a normal mode game the max health appears to be 35, and you start the game with 20. Most of the growth in the game comes from your own abilities and experience with the mechanics. If that sounds particularly punishing, don't worry, there's an accessibility mode that eases the difficulty while still offering some challenge. In accessibility mode you're granted a relic at the start which heals 1 HP every few seconds, reduces enemy health and damage by 25%, gives you an extra item slot (VERY USEFUL), recovers your HP/MP at save points, and prevents bleed, fire, and poison damage from stacking. It's a big help!If I have one criticism of the game, I don't always love its sense of humor. The art seems very geared towards the male gaze, lots of big jiggling breasts, some of the artifacts are women's underwear, and for some reason the little hidden areas you'll find that add photos to the gallery all feature toilets. It wasn't enough to detract from my enjoyment of the game, but your experience may differ.For me, this game's an absolute 10/10, and I hope you love it too!
