_childDocuments_.review: Every time I see a pixel art game I think Jeez this is no game its art! So far this is no 1 and I have played lots of them like Blasphemous and Touhou Luna Night's . The animations and drawn art are fantastic ! Most of negative reviews is a result that people dont understand what this game is about. It's something different than classical metroidvania. Here it's all about survival. The main hero is weak and a little clunky but there are lots of useful stuff in this game spells, wands, dynamite , thrown items and consumables. And one more thing there's no dash button only dodge but it's quite easy to avoid danger for the first time and impossible to dodge second time cause of the delay. Also what people say about too slow attack animation it's not true you just need to pick up one impossible to miss gloves item. And one more thing love how the loot is placed in this game cause if choose the dead end path there are always a valuable items at the end of it. Love the game in general !  One of my favourites!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible!I've played the demo version of the game and I really liked it! Now that the full game is released, I'm never been so excited from a game ever!The visuals and pixel art are gorgeous! When fighting enemies, you have to be strategic when to swing your sword, throwing liquids and casting spells. And choosing the right equipment for certain enemies and bosses. Many complain about the combat being so clunky, but this mechanic makes it more challenging and I like it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a great game if you can get past the different combat.It's not twitch button like hollow knight, or most others. It's methodical, dangerous and deadly. And difficult.But I don't think it's bad. If you enjoyed a game like La-mulana, this one is definitely better. At the beginning of the game you're limited, but as you find more weapons, spells, and items you can switch up your build and approach things different ways. Don't feel afraid to farm cooked chicken to sell. Also you don't quite have to be incredibly sparing with consumables.Overall, I would say 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Lost Ruins pixel art is pretty sick. I was impressed. The environment is always a pleasure to look at whenever I enter a new area. The character designs aren’t half bad either.I found exploring the castle to be fun. I was looking forward to seeing the next zone and what it looked like. Seeing the different monsters and NPCs made it interesting too.Con:The combat is on the weaker side. I understand that it’s going for the slow, methodical combat, but I feel it falls short with most of the weapons. I feel that the combat is just flawed as your character’s attack animation is slow across the board excluding the knives which was what I used mid to end game. Monsters tend to attack faster and have faster recovery time than you with most of the weapons in the game. Often dodging an attack to land a hit yourself doesn’t work. This leaves you with only being able to land a successful attack if you out range them by a longer weapon, magic, or a bow. I was able to beat the game still so it’s not impossible.Overall I think you should play the game. Even if the combat could have been better, this game is a good one. Play it!Full Video:

_childDocuments_.review: The people complaining about the combat are living on a different planet."Wah, it's SoOoOoOoOo slow it takes like a FULL SECOND to swing your weapon!"The literal first NPC in the first five minutes of the game gives you money and sends you to a shop where you can buy a glove that makes you attack faster and do more damage. You can even get another glove later on and stack the speed upgrade. Alternatively, stop using gigantic hammers if you think they're so slow. Infact, why not use throwing weapons? Or a bow? Or magic spells? There are tonnes of options. You don't have to swing around a 500kg block of concrete."well what about the dodge? It doesn't even give you any i frames!"It L I T E R A L L Y does, you just have bad timing. I don't like saying "get better at the game" so I won't, instead why don't you use a shield? In fact, in the first hour or so you can buy a shield which comes out instantly, and on block it even restores your health. See, you don't have to get good if you don't want to :)I'm not even saying that the combat is great. It's fine. It's cool to use traps and stuff but it's nothing special. Calling it bad or awful or a dealbreaker is insane. These people are freaks. I almost didn't buy this game because of them and I'm glad I did. It's a fun game. Great graphics, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: A very neat little game. If you are only playing it from start to finish, the game shouldn't take you more than a couple of hours to beat, but it still feels fully realized and complete experience that doesn't drag on for too long. There are even special game modes for you to try out after completing your first playthrough. It is mostly a fun time to be had, and definitely worth checking out. I've seen complaints about the combat mechanics, and I think they're unfounded. It is intentionally made to be clunky and obtuse, but I think the same thing could be argued against most Souls-like games. It's intentionally designed to make you feel weak and cumbersome, and there's nothing wrong with that as long as you're willing to adapt.Speaking of complaints, however, I do have a few with this game. The side quests aren't very interesting to undertake, only giving you a little bit of dialogue and some items as a reward after completing some sort of fetch quest. Some of the bosses are a little too easy for my liking as well. There are some great bosses despite this, and I believe they would become much more dangerous on the Hardcore difficulty. Overall, there's a lot to like about this game, and it's definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Finished multiple playthroughs on normal, veteran, assassin and witch modes, and partially through boss mode, I can say that this game is very fun, great soundtrack and art. Interesting story, and i really like the boss fights, as well as the backstory behind each boss. This game makes you utilise your items and environment, rewarding creativity between different interactions between various magics, items and environmental hazards (eg. lightning and water)Don't be afraid to use items or you will find things much more difficult than they should be. The main part of this game is to use the effects of items and the environment to your advantage, instead of just stabbing everything to death. A very fun game for those who prefer to fight tactically, although not too difficult to just mash through everything with the right equipment/magic synergies as well.9/10 The game is exciting, and bosses are cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - A pretty unique spin on the metroidvania style of games, if you like hard metroidvania games where resources matter, combat and boss fights requires a little bit of timing and preparation, then be sure to give the game a shot. If you don't like games without a meanigful story and a little bit of fanservice then play at your own discression :DWARNING: This game will require you to load, die a lot, and learn enemy patterns in order to have the best outcome. Supplies tend to be scarce and save points don't refresh HP, so every time you save you have to make sure that you're ready to set in stone the exact supply/hp/mana situation when playing further. Grinding in this game is hard and not very efficient.So going a little bit more in detail from above, the main pull in this game at least for me is the fact that the game requires you to play it like a harsh survival game meaning - that resources are hard to get and what items you wear and where you wear them DO MATTER. Exploration is heavily rewarded with items that allow you to regain hp and mana when pushing through the game, each boss fight or enemy encounter can be significantly easier if you wear/collect the correct items and use the correct consumables in various situations. From the things that can discourage players giving this game a proper run or annoy them, would be the movement, weapon speed and range. The movement speed and jumping can feel very short sometimes and make you miss certain jumps and the weapons take some time to get used to, and the weapon you use may not be the end all be all to carry you through the whole game. This game sometimes may a feel a little janky and leaves little space for mistake without taking heavy punishment, but once you learn strategies and how to approach fights, the game really feels fun to play. The possiblity of having some interesting weapon/item combination is pretty huge and meanigful in this game, so it is advisable to tinker a little bit with it.The art style and graphics of the game are really appealing to me and you can feel that this game was made a little bit on the fan service side, since most of the bosses have a certain "weakspot" as their only hit zone, so if that's not your cup of tea then I would not recommend picking this up if you're easily offended by this kind of stuff.The story is the pretty basic, only redeeming feature is the fact that, like most of metroidvania titles these days, it has certain additional ending and a whole new mode of replaying the game which I will not spoil - but be on the lookout once you finish the game.For the price it is a pretty solid and complete experience, 2 playthroughts took me in total 13 hours to finish. I highly recommend this for people who look for some challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game start to finish. It's a challenging game,but finally beating a boss or clearing an area feels very rewarding plus the game has very good replayability with various modes unlocked after finishing the main game. There's also a ton of achievements to get after you're done with all the modes. Overall a really well done game with an interesting story.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I see most of the people reviewing here have hit all of the important points about this game, but I decided I would throw in my two cents anyways:First of all, I enjoyed it.  I'll first start with the items.  If you don't enjoy opening your inventory mid slash while in a boss fight this game isn't for you.  If it doesn't bother you then this game will be fun.  The thing about the items is that they're all valuable.  In most games you end up accumulating a massive load of items that just sit in your inventory and take up space.  That is not the case in this game.  3/4 of the way through the game, I had burned almost all of my items.  I think I had 3 or 4 things left in my inventory after like the 5th boss battle.  This means that items in this game are well designed and are meant to be used instead of just being random junk you just collect.  Except the toilet paper.  I ended up selling that when I had like 20 in my inventory.  I'm sure there are some cases where it could come in handy, but I never used it.The combat is unique.  It's slow and clunky and takes some getting used to, but once you learn the timings, it can be pretty fun.  You also learn that when timed right the hero's abilities can become kind of OP.  The dodge roll literally makes her invulnerable to damage.  If you walk into a room and see a pack of enemies you have no chance against, just nope your way through the room by rolling past them.  Just be careful to time your rolls properly or it's insta death.  Also her life steal magic spell.  OP.  No targeting necessary.  Just pop the spell and it will kill anything in the room (with a few exceptions).  All you have to do is dodge and make sure you don't get hit.  It's really effective against bosses especially once you get the wand that restores your mana.  The point I am trying to make is that combat is clunky, but once you start getting the right equipment and combos, your little school girl turns into a unstoppable demon slaying machine.  It's the feeling of starting off the game feeling weak and helpless and finishing off the game feeling like a beast that makes it kind of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: It got anime girls in school uniforms and swimsuits (not the adult content kind though), it got dungeons and goblins, very tough opponents that require to develop different strategies like switching between armor and weapons right in the battle, I really love the graphics … so what else can you wish for? _childDocuments_.review: A very fun game that at first feels like a "survival horror platformer" (you are basically a school girl handling a weapon), but ends being Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (due to gear and you getting used to the timing). The story is interesting and the art style is quite good. The music wasn't memorable but it did its job. You will have a wide variety of items so you can pick your preferred style. For my first run I didn't use magic at all because I felt it was too slow, but once you play the magic-only mode, you realize that it is also a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little metroidvania with a bit more work than expected for the last achievements (completing the game without dying more than 3 times is extremely hard, but some of the endings achievements are "bugged" and can get annoying).The combat start EXTREMELY challenging due to the limit amount of weapons/spells/equipments, but once you hit a decent combo (summon orbs + best friend + gladius + gladiator) you can start surviving almost whatever the game throws at you, and summon sword -> invisibility -> summon sword is BS with some gear.Additionally, have to mention that the game tends to go to hard on fanservice, in case that puts you off, but overall, quite rewarding once you get the hang of it.4/5 for me, 5/5 on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why people complain about combat. There is a difficulty setting. If you don't enjoy standard difficulty, you can always go easy.Combat is very intuitive and controls are very responsive. There are some issues with timings for enemy attacks, but this is a kind of game where you have to memorize each enemy's behavior anyway. It doesn't mean you can't beat an enemy you see for a first time - it means instead of rushing it you should taunt it first, roll away and see what it does. There are also countless ways of dealing with enemies besides facing them directly - there are items and traps. And it feels like developers designed every room thinking about players never facing an impossible challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I know the review says I recommend this game (and I do), but it certainly isn't perfect. It's well worth the $20 USD I spent on it, though.The storyline is pretty simple, but there's enough mystery to keep you engaged. The heroine just sorta appears, with no memory of what happened. Within your first few steps, someone named Beatrice shows up, and before too long she tells the heroine that the seal on her memory will be lifted if she can defeat the followers of the Dark Lady. Desperate to recover her memory, she embarks on her quest. The basic premise is simple enough, but as you play you find journal entries written by various people that either give you lore for the overall plot or the specific areas that you're in. That, along with the few NPCs that you DO find and do quests for, you get a pretty good idea of what the state of the world is. It's actually quite interesting to see what's going on in the world, and figuring out who the various NPCs who wrote the journals are.Now that the story is out of the way, let's talk about the actual mechanics of the game. Since the review is positive, I'll go over my negative comments first to help temper expectations about this game.Now that that's out of the way, let's talk about the things I like about the gameAll in all, I rather enjoyed this game in spite of its flaws, and if you enjoy the sidescrolling exploration experience, I believe you will to.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ok. It's not great. It's not bad, It's ok.The Good:You probably are looking through it because you saw the trailer and saw those big bosses with bouncy tits, let's not lie to ourselves. The trailer doesn't betray you. You'll see big bosses with bouncy tits.Most of the art is okay, sometimes it is even really pretty and quite sexy. The pixel art animations are also dressed with shading from real time light sources and particles and this compensates the non-purist pixel art wonkyness of pixels of different size.Also from time to time the music is really nice. It's not the best, but it matches the mood of the game really well.The game is replayable with fresh features on new game+, so even if its quite short, you can play again with a different story and different mechanics.The Bad:The game is bland. The story is bland.  The gameplay feels either wonky or annoying. The menues are... a hurdle. This is important because you'll be juggling passive items in the few item slots you have. No double jump and no dash make the controls feel sometimes slow and sometimes unwieldy. There are absolutely killer combinations that are extremely easy to achieve, a few for each zone. This makes some fights against bosses and some entire sections of the map so easy it's boring. There's some sort of environment system, if either you or the enemies touch the ground they might become wet and be further affected by electricity or catch on fire. While I'm impressed with the idea, I've found that I have not enjoyed it much. It felt mostly annoying when it was inconvenient (something that forced you to enter the menu to spend an item to become immune to the floor effects) or boring (entire parts of the map are submerged in water and you can destroy everything with an electricity spell, making these sections pointless)The metroidvania aspects of the game, for any experimented platform game player will seem too simple. The problem is not that the game is short (it is, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing) the problem is that the exploration is not interesting. I can't really put into words how simple the layout is, but it is amazing how the game can have so much effort put into so many things and the parts that are supposed to be the most important feel so unpolished.I'll be sincere. I'll only reccomend this game because I want these guys to succeed and make further games. I think they have the potential to do something amazing next. And if you enjoy the genre, you probably will want too, the game has a bit of soul, despite all its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. The art is amazing! 2. the combat is not nearly as clunky as some of the negative reviews would have you believe. I thought that all of the boss fights were fun. each brings something new to the table and it was quite enjoyable figuring out how to beat them.4. The story whale simple has plenty of wtf moments that will keep you interested. 5. Plus after you beat the game there you unlock 3 new game modes. over all a grate game for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals, plenty of checkpoints sprinkled through out so downtime after death is minimal and character/enemy designs are memorable. Controls and combat take a little getting used to but feel tight and responsive. Most enemies and bosses have predictable attack patterns that the lack of i-frames isn't really an issue. Enemies have weaknesses that can be exploited for quick kills and a number of item choices synergize to push damage even further.The additional play modes obtained after completing the main story give more context to the characters you meet and is worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this was a nice little game. The pixel art is gorgeous, and by far the best trait of the game. Gameplay is decent. Early on things are difficult and you have to be careful, but pretty quickly there are equipment and item combos that can exploit the AI.I wish the game was able to give more development to its story and characters. The story is fairly predictable, but still enjoyable enough. The characters that are there are well crafted, but some bosses literally show up for their fight with a gorgeous design, say nothing, and die. I would have been happy if the game was twice as long, and each designed character had dialog, or at least characterization.I hope this game receives some more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't touch on the art and music.. You don't need me to tell you yow amazing it is. But I will touch on the "polarizing" combat. Maybe actually give the game a shot before succumbing to the "OMG combat slow and bad. Other games better!1!!" mentality that many reviewers here seem to have. While the minority opinion, it is very loud on the forums.This game doesn't feel like Dead Cells or Ori or any other side scrolling action game because it isn't supposed to. Combat is slower and more methodical at the start. You need to block, parry, dodge, set traps and strategize those early encounters. Enemies are deadly and you're just an amnesiac schoolgirl. Go figure why it feels that way.HOWEVER, that changes pretty fast. You can become so incredibly powerful in this game. Virtually untouchable. You want a magic heat seeking bow that obliterates enemies off screen? Go for it. You want to be invisible and one shot backstab enemies with a dagger? Sure thing. You want to permafreeze enemies and blow them up with magic bombs? Also valid.It's a slow burn and you're a weak girl with little more than a sword you can barely swing. But the game will reward you for pushing on. Persevere and get stronger. It's worth it. The game is gorgeous and an absolute blast to figure out these unique builds.Try it for more than 10 minutes before making a judgment. You have 2 hours to work with here.

_childDocuments_.review: At this moment, I already completed the game, took me around 4 or 5 hours to complete, it's good, I had fun, but if there is something that I could complain is that the combat is clunky and annoying, this is more of a problem when you treat this game as a metroidvania, to put it simple, you should try this game as a survival, due to how the combat is design; the game is good, it's just that the combat is annoying

_childDocuments_.review: So I bought this game without knowing anything about it and I was... pleasantly disappointed?Don't get me wrong, the game is good, albeit slightly expensive for the playtime but it's alright.It has nice 2D graphics and nice jiggle physics.The game can be a bit boring at times because of the gameplay and the difficulty curve is weird since it's hard from the start but then gets way easier after 3 bosses.I have yet to properly finish the game but it's been a nice ride for the first playthrough.Would definitely recommend it there's a promotion.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much. I am usually someone who will only run through a game once and shelf it for a while. This game I have beat a few times and I still want to run through it yet again. I love the visuals, the controls and the all the ways the game lets you build your girl. The start of the game can be a little hard as you are still in your learning period and your gear is limited,  but once you are around the second boss beat, your choices really expand in what you can do. Magic may be a little overpowered around the time you get the good spells.I have seen some people complain about how slow some of the weapons can be, but I think it comes down to knowing when and how to use some of the slower weapons. Having beat the game using all sorts of styles, I can say that every weapon is viable to use. The only problem that I had with the game is that for a little while I could not get achievements while they were fixing some bugs around the release of the game, but that has nothing to do with the game itself.If you love Metriodvania style games with a dash of Dark Souls, then I honestly can not recommend this game enough! This is honestly one of my favorite games I have ever played on Steam! If they ever plan DLC or a sequel for the this game, I will buy it the instant I can!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far, do not expect a run gun n super reactive 2d platformer. This plays like a mix between a survival game and a 2d platformer in a good way. You are not OP. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and challenging with beatiful pixel graphics and particle/lightning effects. The thing I liked the most is combat. Some people might dislike it and it's understandable, since not everyone likes "clunky and slow" combat, but I personally enjoyed having to think about the way of passing every enemy encounter, including bosses. You can try out many stupid or op builds and since the game isn't that long it has potential for replaybility. I just wish there was NG+, but it might come in the future. Another good thing about this game are the graphics. Animations are smooth, particles look amazing, the lightning is beatiful and the enemy designs are of big variety. As for bosses, I will just call their design "interesting". The story is pretty simple, but that doesn't mean it's boring, but it has that stereotypical anime plot feeling to it. Some might like it, some might not. I enjoyed it to the point I decided to see all the endings, because I wasn't satisfied with just one (the game has 4 in total).Do I recommend it?Yes, but be prepared, that if you expect dynamic hack n slash game, then you can look for something else. But if you want a game that plays the same as Gothic, one of the classic games where at the start of the game you had to carefully choose when to fight and when to run then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing visuals!!! I really love the character design. Lighting, fluids and other effects are great, the sound is well defined.For the gameplay, I don't compare it to "Metroidvania" style or anything, I look at it independently and I really like it.You will have enough gold when you will realize that you can sell a lot of found items. Yeah sure not getting exp when killing monster can seem frustrating but I barely noticed it as it is the same for a lot of other games. And I don't feel the need for it, evolution through better equipment is cool too...For the combat system, as for any games which are not "assisted" you will just have to "git gud" and that's it. Personaly I think it is quite good, you have to calculate your moves because it is not fast paced. You will feel personal improvements.I like the arrows that bounce back on your shield (yes it is important)I like the variety of items/weapons/artifacts and their effects, there is a lot of ways to handle new areas and enemies.In fact, new areas/enemies will force you to change your gear and gameplay, it is refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: going to try and go in order of importance "played on recommended"The combat is hit or miss with people, it's not fast paced like touhou luna nights or dead cells, at least your character isn't. The bosses are more active but you can tell the game isn't going for a fast pace. That said combat is more methodical with a bunch of accessories, weapons, and spells to use. With more and more playstyles and synergy opening to you as you progress. There are weapons and spells with different hitboxes, ranges, effects, timing, and use cases for a few puzzles. I had alot of fun swapping my playstyle to fit whatever scenario I found myself in, trying to find what worked best. Enemy design and variety is good as well, and you can find yourself dying often if you don't pay attention to status effects and rushing in. The environmental hazards can be just as big of a threat as the enemies. If you swing a 2 hander over your head without thinking, you might set the room on fire. For movement you have the basics, single jump, and a roll. The platforming isn't anything special, but its serviceable (It can be annoying how a midair attack kills momentum, but you use it to drop on enemies, so eh?).The aesthetic Is good overall with tried and true pixles,  it's very anime in the dialog boxes (you get what you see), and the sprite work actually reminds me of shantae, which is usually expressive and... bouncy. There are some neat visual effects and lighting as well, which do their best to sell the environments, though some still fall flat to me (catacombs). But overall the game is visually interesting, and the intractable objects, platforms, enemies, and projectiles are all distinct. Plenty of variety in character design as well, though they don't really have a solid story to bounce off of, they're 1-D mostly. Music was serviceable, though nothing really stood out to me, at least not yet, I'm sure I missed somethings in my first playthrough. The metroidvania/exploration aspect are well done, the map marks locations you've been to and things of interest, you can even have a mapmarker. Your movement stays the same through the game as far as I can tell, and if you can't reach something it usually means you'll find a drop down or loop back in the following area. For exploring you are rewarded with items, most importantly weapons and accessories. Which are mixed and matched at your discretion whenever you see fit, making you more powerful the more you find. There are shops with usable items, weapons, and accessories. But money Is tight and items are expensive, so it still makes drops worthwhile. I didn't have to grind for anything I needed though, and eventually there are items that help there, in case you want to treat yourself to a lightning hammer. And the portals are spaced well enough that they don't feel cheap or overused.It is a game about anime things doing anime stuff, and if you're not into that skipping the dialog will get you back into the game fast. I think this game is worth playing, as long as your ok with a basic story, methodical combat, and dying thanks to your Hubris every once in while.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little Metroidvania that starts off very survival esq. where you must carefully approach each new situation you come across. Once you get the hang of the game the latter portion of it becomes a breeze: partly due to your experience at that point, and partly due to some key spells and artifacts you can find. It's not the longest metroidvania ever played, took me roughly 5 hours to explore basically everything and complete my first playthrough, but it has alternate play modes that unlock afterwards, such as locking you to magic or crit builds with some bonuses, or a special boss-trio mode.It's got cute little sprites and art, and music that's good but not going to blow you away. The presentation does it's job, blending the background and foreground together, with clear distinctive areas and music cues.

name: Ravenbound
detailed_description: Ravenbound is a fast-paced action game that combines the challenge of a roguelite with the choices of the open world. Master your combat skills, build your deck and beat the Betrayer in the mystic world of Ávalt. Grow stronger with every death You are a vessel in the service of the Raven who you help to restore its power in an effort to free the imprisoned gods of Ávalt. While each vessel is lost forever once they fall in battle, the strength they bring to the Raven is not. This allows you to come back stronger each time as you progress through this action roguelite. Explore a fantasy world inspired by Scandinavian Folklore Journey through the breathtaking island of Ávalt on foot or soar through the skies in Raven form. As you traverse this mysterious, Scandinavian-folklore inspired world, you will confront legendary creatures such as the towering Trolls, ruthless Hulders, and menacing undead Draugr. Build your deck to beat the Betrayer Progression comes in the form of cards and unlocks that you can find on your journey through Ávalt. In each lifetime new cards are unlocked, some by chance and some by player choice. As you grow stronger, so do the rewards. But be careful, each reward also increases the Betrayer's hatred which empowers her minions as it grows. Learn to master the varied and fast paced combat Learn to master the fast paced and fluid combat of Ravenbound to bring down the increasingly challenging and hostile creatures of Ávalt. By unlocking more cards you will expand your options as new armor, weapons and magical relics become available to you, granting you new ways to defeat the Raven's enemies with every lifetime.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy a lot of what this game is but there's one major thing that really puts it off for me. This game really punishes exploration. It's designed so you basically have to go to one or two areas, grab what you can, and go straight for the boss of each area. If you want to build out more or take out the 30-40 camps in each zone, you'll end up powering up the boss so much that they'll one shot you immediately. I'm not sure i've ever seen a game discourage any sort of exploration the way this game does. Why have an open world roguelite if you don't want players exploring the open world at all? The combat's fun, the cards are interesting to play around with, but the way it punishes you for wanting to go out and explore really, really sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I just came back to try Ravenbound out after not touching it since release day, and just about every problem with it has been addressed and improved.This was I feel the biggest problem at launch, requiring a constant online connection and a 3rd party account before you can even get to the main menu I'm sure turned many away, and the justifications given for it were weak, which is even more apparent now that they've removed those requirements and made them optional.I still don't believe there's a good reason for not using using steam's tools for the online features in favor of their own, and doesn't change that it was a terrible decision, but at least it's better now, I guess?There is a small positive gameplay impact for using the online feature that I'll expand on in a bit.Used to be the most effective way to deal with fights was to mash dodge when enemies are attacking and spam your own when they aren't. The iframes were generous enough that spamming dodge made you nearly untouchable. This also made later fights take a lot longer, because while you were clearing camps and empowering shards, you'd start getting more Hatred (the mechanic that buffs all enemies by a % permanently) and would be quickly outscaled when trying to increase your own power. So for me, enemies would end up having massive health pools, but could never touch me, so I'd just give them papercut damage until I got bored enough to reset.Now, all that has been reworked. Each stage gives you 6 hatred free chests and/or shards, and there's more variety to the hatred cards you can pull, so it's not just a flat stat increase for enemies if you want to chance opening a chest. The online player graves used to also give you hatred when you open them, but now they're basically a free card you can claim, which are not available if you don't use the online feature. So it looks more like an incentive to use their 3rd party account, which while I feel is still dumb, you can get some utility out of it.They also added a limit to dodges that have a relatively short refresh, but still gives you a reason to use the shield if you can't dodge. That would have been annoying before, because the shield had such a short lifespan and could run out even if you weren't blocking a hit, but it's been changed to instead absorb a set amount of damage before it pops, and is tied to your new posture bar. Enemies also have posture, and maxing it out opens them to a heavy damage attack (and seems to affect any enemy within the hitbox, which is fun with crowds.) Weapons also have a special attack with a cooldown now.Almost forgot, you traverse the map mostly by turning into a raven and flying really fast. At first you had to find a "raven tower" and run through it to take flight. People were annoyed and felt it inconveniently slowed the game too much. They tried adding more towers. Doesn't seem like it helped much, because now they've finally let you transform in and out of the raven at will if not in combat.It looks like they took a lot of feedback to get the game to this point, and it honestly feels far better. If it had released in this state, I think it could have done a whole lot better. But honestly, I still think it could have had more attention if they didn't require their 3rd party account to play when it launched.Seriously, nobody wants that, nobody asks for that. Don't do that again.

_childDocuments_.review: So after finally completing the game I can say I fully understand how to play and enjoy each and every runThe general strategy that majority fail to find out and what the game fails to explain is that the main strategy isChoose areaFollow blue objective to grab the manaUpon completing this this will cleanse nearby chests of hatred to allow the player to open chests without penaltyRaven up and look for the little light beacons coming out of camps (this means that it has a non hatred chest)Gather fragments and generally choose the free mana cards from the cleansed campsComplete the Green objective to get coinsUse coins to either buy a potion from the town (heals 100) or use coins to unlock a relic slotIf you havent empowered enough fragments. Empower fragments until you have one Hatred slot.Fight Warden Proceed to next areaEnjoy Ravenbound friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in how not to design a game.The core loop and mechanic in this game is to obtain shards, or open chests to obtain cards to upgrade your character with gear and passive enhancements.  Now, this is fairly standard stuff until you get into the other core mechanics of the game.There is a huge open world in this game that you can transverse as a Raven and the purpose for doing so is to find camps of corrupted creatures to battle, defeat and then obtain crystal shards from and open chests.  Three shards allow you to open a random loot table set of three cards of which you can only pick one.  A chest allows you to instantly pop up three random cards as well which you can only pick one from.  You can even find the death marker of another player in the world, and can obtain loot cards it offers. This is decent in concept and would make for a pretty good game loop except for one massive and game breaking mechanical design flaw.You have a mechanic called hatred in the game which is tied to a meter that fills up whenever you use three shards, open a chest or loot another players death marker.  Aside from the first time you respawn or enter a new bosses game world you get to cleanse only 1 area of hatred which allows you to open essentially three/five chests for random cards before you can never obtain cards without acquiring hatred that fills up your bar.So far, sounds decent right?  It is.  However, here is where the extremely poor game breaking design mechanic decision comes into play. You, the player are literally hard capped with how many chests and shards you can use before you literally cannot loot anything in the game world again.  It takes roughly maybe 6-8 camps before that happens.  The idea is that the game mobs will get more difficult the more hate you obtain, but the critical flaw here is that it is YOUR PLAYER that is hard capped in their ability to power up, find new cards, or even obtain money since the monsters themselves don't actually drop gold, you can ONLY get gold from cards in the game which makes you have to choose between money for healing (since there is literally no healing mechanic in the game other than via cards which use soul points or you buy it from a rudimentary NPC town merchant).  So, the game itself by design literally prevents you from exploring the open game world because you literally cannot loot anything or collect any more shards, which prevents you from growing your characters power before you decide to take on the world boss.This is absolutely a game killing design decision.  There is no way to lower your hate level until you defeat the worlds boss and even then it only removes ONE level of hatred.  A staggeringly poor set of decision on game mechanics.No player wants to be hard capped with what they can do in a game, especially when it comes to looting and growing in power, discovering more cards, being able to get money for healing and vendor purchases (you can buy three random cards from the loot table and pick one for 75 gold) and exploring an open world literally filled with camps that have chests sitting there shining a bright beam of light into the sky calling you to come earn them by killing the camp of creatures protecting it. Oh, you can still go fight the creatures, but NOPE, you cannot loot the chests or pick up any shards.  Thus, you cannot obtain a chance at soul/relic points (whatever they are called)  to activate the cards, and no you cannot obtain any more gold to either buy more relic slots to slot the cards into or obtain gold for cards, gear or healing. You're done, that's it, literally no more point to the world being there.  Instead, you better fly to the boss while you actually have the ability to give yourself full health (oh and he will be powered up since it is LITERALLY impossible to beat them without actually advancing and strengthening up your character with the cards., because the game design mechanic has determined that you will absolutely no longer be able to actually play any of the core game loop mechanics anymore because well, you filled up your incredibly tiny hatred bar...What happens when you die?  Well, you literally start off exactly where you were when you first started.  You do unlock additional weapon styles, new cards  and other minor things, BUT, you start out at the first boss again, even if you killed 3 of them, and have to do it ALL over again, capped once again with absolutely no carry over of active cards, no gold, no soul/relic points, nothing.  So, you  get to go open a maximum of around 12 chests or so before once again you are cut off from that core game mechanic and have to go try your luck against the boss.  If you die, rinse repeat. This is absurd and mark my words, unless the hatred mechanic is either removed or COMPLETELY revamped, it will do exactly what removing player progression ability and agency does; absolutely tank this games sales and ratings.The developers are killing their own game with their design decisions (oh and they deleted my similar feedback like this in a discussion form) , and I am sure it sounded good in theory, but life is busy with all kinds of responsibilities that take up your players and your markets time.  There are just way to many game choices out there that don't absurdly punish you from doing the things in the game the game was designed for!  Even Dark Souls allowed you to never be unable to loot the chests and monsters from the world you defeated in order to strengthen your character even if it did cause you to start over.  People do not want to be cut off from looting and improving their character and then forced to start at literally ground zero regardless of how many of the realms guardians you defeated and obtained their power. with the same limiting hard cap in play for every single run.The only hard cap that should exist in the game are the effects of hatred, not that hatred literally removes your ability to play 90% of the game and game world.  There is not strategic element here, this isn't strategy, this is punishment and terrible game design.  You cannot be strategic when all of the resources in the game are tied to a RANDOM loot table roll.  Stop talking about the strategic elements, they don't exist under your current design, unless the strategy is to kill your own player base and game.  I don't think that is your intention.How hatred should work if it MUST be a mechanic of the game:As hatred is accumulated, to a certain hard capped point, it increases the difficulty of the creatures and end boss in the given realm you are in.  I say the given one you are in as there is only one entire game world it's just you leave it and re-enter a different door for a different and harder boss and world camps once you beat a boss.Continuing on, once again as hatred is accumulated, the number of card offerings is decreased until the chests, relic shards or other players death markers only offer one card choice rather than three.Within the hatred mechanic, the player should absolutely have the ability to cleanse their hatred meter levels and decrease the power of the boss and other world creatures by taking on difficult and engaging quests to do so.  The game world feels so absolutely barren and meaningless without something like this.  There is literally only one or two generic quest offered in each game world and those once again result in filling your hatred meter.  Within 30-40 mins of playing you have zero purpose in exploring it because of the hard cap discussed above.  If, I somehow missed multiple other areas you can cleanse of hatred like you can do only a single time at the start of every venture into the game world then that is at least something, but I sure couldn't find any.Hatred (if absolutely necessary) should be able to flow back and forth and the player should NEVER be cut off from looting and improving their character.  Get rid of it, or revamp it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the hardest games to appropriately judge, specially in a short steam review. I am leaving a thumbs up, but that's cause the game appeals to me personally, I strongly suggest reading/watching reviews before committing to $30, it's a steep price and the game is NOT gonna be for everyone.It can't be understated how much this game does RIGHT for starters. I was thinking I'd hate the open world design for a roguelite game, but I ended up genuinely loving it, I was thinking I'd hate the floaty combat, but it turns out that it gives you an incredible amount of freedom in how to approach situations, without sacrificing how it feels once you get a bit better at it. The build variety is also genuinely good and the game lets you manipulate it in ways to get what you want and it also gives you an interesting risk/reward consideration with the hatred mechanic, where you can continue growing stronger before a boss, but that means the bosses grow stronger with you. The enemy design is actually good for the combat system, which is such a rarity with indie games, meaning that the fights remain exciting from the start of the game till the end of the game and you have REAL options when approaching combat situations and builds, none of which feel bad. But the negatives are also very negative.. The performance seems to be atrocious (I go in depth on weird things like memory leak issues in the video in this review)Ultrawide support doesn't really exist, GUI is all weirdALWAYS ONLINE???? I don't want my account on a mailing list tySteep price It's a really nuanced game to review. In order not to write a 50000 word page I've instead made an 11 minute in-depth review if someone's on the verge whether they want to buy or not, hope this review helps you figure it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is there. The foundations are there too. But the execution is... mid at best. This clearly needs heavy polishing. If it had been launched as an Early Access at 15 bucks we could have a nice game here that would evolve greatly if the devs listened to community feedback, but being launched as a 1.0 feels like a rush that shouldn't have been made, and doesn't justify at all a price of 30 bucks. If you want something similar to this that actually is fun go play AC Valhalla roguelite mode, which really feels what inspired this.EDIT 3: The game released two days ago and there hasn't been nor a day one patch neither a response from the devs, their twitter doesn't have any post other than a silly picture of a raven with glasses. No answer to the complains. No new info, anything. So yeah, keep up your hopes with this becoming a great game.EDIT 2: I'm seeing many people posting good reviews to help the game because they have HIGH HOPES OF WHAT'S TO COME. But aren't you guys forgetting this is launching as 1.0 and not an Early Access? Who is telling you there will be all those updates you're talking so kind about? Judge games by what they are, not what they will maybe be. If they make this into a good game in the future, you can edit your review afterwards, don't be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and make a positive review "just to help the score".PROS: + Good visuals+ Decent combat coreography (I'll develop further in CONS)+ Interesting concept of open-world roguelike experienceCONS:- Empty open-world. The game is divided into Camps with different difficulties and Villages (which I've just seen one at the moment). You move between these spots using a raven transformation that don't ask me why the devs decided that you can turn from raven into human whenever you want but to get into raven form you need to go to an altar which could easily be 200m away from your position, climbing up a mountain, or whatever. You can also use a grapple hook that is badly designed (YES, they did a grappling hook that is not satisfying to use more like a pain, tell me more about how to ♥♥♥♥ up one of the best mechanics a game can have). I've found myself more time running endlessly and pointlessly than enjoying the game.- Not really interesting combat, I haven't really unlocked any abbility yet (I suppose there are) but the combat is very button smashy. You have a parry that works sometimes, and a dash that sometimes and most of the hits don't have that big of an impact, so all in all the combat is flashy but for now it hasn't been really interesting since you can't really combo between heavy and light, and basically all you do is spam attacks until you can use your surge, which is an abbility that last less than a sneeze and increase your dmg output by some amounth that I don't even know. - The enemies always feel the same, no matter what enemies you face you will do the same all the time, you can dash unlimited times but even then you will sometimes get hit mid dash, and I don't felt a difference between fighting one human enemy or the other. There are no ranged weapons that I've seen, neither for you nor your enemies, not even magic casted at you, so every combat feels really samey. The boss fight I did wasn't the worst, but it felt like I did 0 dmg (Explained after this point) and he dealt a million to me. If you look up at the devs stream not even them after developing the game are able to clear the first boss, so there goes that. I suppose if you go with 0 hatred its more manageable but since I tried to get mana cards to try something the game supposedly offers, I ended up with a boss that was a power house (Even drawing only 5 hatred cards is already a +25% DMG and HP for the first boss).- Mana system is weird. If you don't find mana you can't use most of the cards you find, if you don't use said cards you become powerless. I don't know if there is a specific strategy to find mana but I haven't really seen it yet.- Hatred system. I found myself with no abbility to gain cards and constantly getting hatred (so I could try and find mana cards). In the end you end up with a lot of Hatred that basically increases Elite and Boss Dmg and Hp by 5%. - Shards and Card System. Instead of having an standard equipment system this game opts for a mechanic where you need to fuse 3 shards (which can be dropped by Elites and Bosses) or use a Hatred shard, which you get by unlocking Hatred Chests (that contains cards, which again you can't use if you don't have the mana for). If you do use any hatred shard for a fusion you automatically get a Hatred card which activates the effect mentioned before, one per shard used and they replace a card from your deck. And once a lot of hatred has been consumed one of this shard slots will always be replaced with a hatred shard until you kill a boss that unlocks ONE hatred slot. Stupid and pointless mechanic that makes your game unrewarding to play.- Account (?) Didn't have a problem with making one so I can play the game but it doesn't add anything and they sell it to you like IF YOU MAKE AN ACCOUNT YOU GET EXCLUSIVE REWARDS, when in the end if you don't make one you cannot play the game.All in all, I'll try playing more since I paid 30 euros and I really don't want to ask for a refund, and want to trust the devs, but this hour and something I played felt pretty lackluster.EDIT: After thinking about it I don't even want to hop back, that's the impression it left, so I've asked for the refund now that I can, and just hope that in the future I see some changes that make me want to play the game again. But thinking about it... the need of an account, 30 euros price, no launch discount, lackluster experience... seems like greed is the only thing that moves the game forward, so until I see something else I'd be better expending that on other titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Idea is nice, graphics and theme are pretty cool, but the execution is very poor.+ The world of Ávalt looks pretty, all the different biomes are pretty unique, dense forests, caves, ruins, mountains, exactly the nordic scenery you would expect.+ The card mechanic is nice.+ Flying around in raven form is pretty fast and smooth, but...- The open world concept is pointless, since you only travel from camp to camp in raven form (Ubisoft style, with a map full of markers). No point in exploring the rest of the world since it is empty. 90% of playthroughs are the same: clear the 'hatred' at the crack in the earth, clear the 3 camps around it, kill the warden, maybe do the sidequest for extra money. Everything else in the world is pretty much ignored, even the regular camps.~ The game seems to push you towards finishing a run in about 30 minutes, with time limit on  a limited number of rewards (blessings) per area. This turns the game into a boss rush type of game, so why can't I see the currently elapsed time in the UI??- Lots of game mechanics that are not explained, neither is the effect of buffs ("damage massively increased", by how much??). Devs should learn from Slay the Spire, just show extra info when hovering a card..- Combat is a janky mess, it's like watching viking Power Rangers dance around on your screen. Fighting a single enemy is pretty easy, but fighting a group is annoying as hell. You will be kiting the group around, hoping for a perfect dodge so you go into frenzy mode and then try to pick them off one by one. - Bosses suck, blocking and dodging is just guesswork.- Most cards and abilities are very situational, only affecting one specific type of enemy, so there's not much point in using them.- I don't see the point of half the skills in the skill tree, no respec possible.- The game recommends playing with a controller, but the camera is super stiff and movement feels weird. Mouse and keyboard seems a lot better.- Developer has a pretty bad reputation for releasing barely finished games and then abandoning it. I don't expect any future updates, devs already moved on to their next project.- One of the region names (Fornfjall) on the world map is incorrect...Finished the game after about 15 hours, level 42. Ravenbound can be entertaining once you get the hang of combat and if you don't mind grinding bosses multiple times to learn the timing of their attacks. Overall, Ravenbound needs a lot more polish and in its current state, I would not recommend this game easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Attention! THIS GAME FEELS MORE LIKE AN EARLY ACCESS THAN A FINISH GAME. Please be aware.If you wanna know more, here is my review:I really want to recommend this game, but sadly it is undercooked.Let me explain my reasons:"Good" things:-It is original.-Looks good.-The combat is fine.-The Card system is ok."meeh" things:-Dodging is all you need, you will spam that button a lot. The defense bubble worth it just for 1 or 2 enemies.-Broken SFX for main character and enemies, also there is no voice over for dialog.-Targeting feels weird, you have to press a button that will change to another objective, and sometimes it is not the one that you want to focus.-Is an open world where lacks of activities, there is not much to do aside of fight. Exploring is not rewarding. Still after 1.1- Skill tree added on 1.1 to give the illusion that the player is progressing.. but is just the old trait menu with some passives skills; the "progression and strengthen" is just a small portion of the skill tree, the rest feels like unlocks like  the old trait menu. Where the player Unlocks things like: Use the big axe instead of the sword and shield.And now you have a little plus like: "now your weapon deal 1 point more of damage" or "with perfect parry you increase 1% your focus" or "10 more hp".  Don't get me wrong, this is an improvement of how it was released, but still... is not something that hardly will make you want to grind for it."Bad" things: -The core loop is not interesting: Do blue quest, kill the enemies around it, do the One quest of the outpost, try to avoid hatred, fight the boss and Repeat! This is an open world game and it feels the opposite with this core loop. A pity and game breaking for me!-The open world feels empty. -33% of the time, is expended running towards a raven platform to be able to fly, so you can travel faster. In 1.0.3 they added more raven towers to solve this, but still feels that you are running a lot instead.My personal score is a 5 out of 10This is a hidden "Early Access", so please keep this in mind if you are planning to get it.I did a quick search about this company, and they are the one that made "Second Extinction", a game that is still in early access after several years... and today there are no news about when it will be launched. (Please, read the comments in that game)So, please, be careful if you want to buy the game.UPDATE:Played on patch 1.0.3 - The now can be selected, and we can play the game how we want. The game feel more generous with the mana, markers for the blue quest and hatred system it is not so punishing, but... the core loop of the game is not interesting at all.Played on patch 1.1 -The amount of cards have been increased, passive skills were added in a skill tree menu, now you have a new mechanic with keys: to help you to combat the hatred. The core loop still bad, is the same as the start.The only big thing is now you can play the game offline, this is a big deal if you are on a plane, train, car or their servers shuts down.I'll mention down below what I removed from the initial review due to updates, due to fixes an changes::-The game crash often. 1.0.3.-Critical NPC in outpost or some critical enemies sometimes just disappears, unable to do the "blue" quest during the run. 1.0.3- For each run, there is no progression.There is not much meaningful content to be interested with after a run. (No Mastery, Skill tree or Powers, there are cards that are not so different with the ones that you start ) skill tree added in 1.1-You need to play with an account, you have to be online all the time. Fixed on 1.1

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thankful that I got to play this game for free, because I feel £30 is way too steep for what it currently is. This game feels like it's still in Early Access, not a finished title. I hope the Devs continue to work on it and that it can fulfil its potential.I played less than 2 hours of this game and there's not much making me want to play more.The good:- Environment is graphically fine. Nothing special, but it isn't distracting.- Combat system rewards you for skilled play. Time your blocks and dodges for temporary buffs.- The mechanics seem semi-promising.The bad:- The card system. Why aren't these just regular "Pick your perk" type options? Why does 'mana' factor in? Half of the chests you open to get cards also contain cards which tank your mana resources so you don't even get to use the perks you just fought for. It's a weird system that doesn't feel rewarding in the early game and you seem to just get punished for opening chests anyway.- The world is a series of enemy arenas, it's not "open world". There's nothing in it. You can either traverse on-foot or you can find a ziggurat to turn yourself into a bird (with terrible inverted flight controls which have you speed up as soon as you start moving. Weird and hard to control.) but you might as well just always be a bird because there's nothing to see on the ground anyway. If the button to see the map markers was swapped with a button to turn yourself into a bird and then the markers were shown while in bird form then it probably wouldn't be so bad. Also what's the point of the grappling hook?- Fragments? The game tries to impress upon you the fact that these things have elemental affinities but how do you know or care what elemental affinity an enemy has? Does it become super relevant later on? A weird mechanic that I didn't get to find out the importance of but maybe it's important later on.- This game is so poorly optimised that it was difficult to stream at the same time. I'm running a Ryzen 9 5900X with 64GB of RAM and a 3080Ti. I do not experience poor performance with any games on high settings, even while streaming, but this game absolutely chugged my PC. You might not notice it if you aren't trying to multitask while playing, but every application I had open became incredibly slow while this game was open.Some Improvements I'd Like To See:- Better optimisation- Character Customisation from the get-go. Don't throw us into the tutorial area without giving us a chance to see that there are multiple potential Specialisations and Passive Abilities to pick up in the Meta tree.- More to do in the open world that make it feel like there's a purpose to exploring on-foot rather than by bird- Change the sprinting animation to look less goofy- Dynamic transparency on the environments. Not being able to see through leaves and branches while locked onto an enemy is frustrating.In its current state, I wouldn't recommend this game. Maybe I need to spend more time with it to see more of the good, but it's hard to want to open it again.I hope the devs continue to work on the game because I really like the concept and the combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought Ravenbound pretty much as soon as it was released as the style and format of the game looked very appealing to me. Unfortunately I gave up on it after 20 hours or so as the balance felt off to the point I found the gameplay incredibly frustrating. Coming back to the game recently, happy to say that the string of patches over the past few months have improved things greatly. The game feels better balanced, more fleshed out and less buggy. The challenge is still there, but combat feels better and the gameplay seems to flow more smoothly overall. I'm enjoying my time in the game now, and I think it'll be one I'll come back to frequently. It's a lot closer now to the game I hoped it would be in the first place.There probably isn't much point in checking out Ravenbound unless you are part of the niche audience that particularly enjoys rogue-likes. It isn't a full RPG and doesn't try to be. The open world doesn't add much to the gameplay directly and feels under exploited, but it does give the game atmosphere and a sense of scale, as well as some gorgeous visuals. Flying around it as a raven feels great. The game runs OK on my modest setup (i7-3770 / RTX2060), with framerates being good at 1080p, acceptable at 2K but poor at 4K. In the state it is in now, Ravenbound is well worth another look if rogue-likes are your thing.

_childDocuments_.review: The foundation is there and I think the game could become great one day, it isn't today though.I very much like the visuals and the combat. The block feels a bit unresponsive if you're mid-swing but the dodge is crisp and rewards you for perfect timing, animations are good and easy to read. Some of the bosses are incredibly quick for some of the weapons though and definitely needs some tuning.The reason for the "Don't recommend" is that the open world and roguelite mechanics are a mess and a half.It's a big open world and you're free to explore it, but there's nothing to find out there. Your exploration, such as it is, consists of flying to 2 markers given to you at the start of a run. One is a town that'll give you an objective to clear a specific camp and return for 100gold which will get you some healing, a random upgrade or 2 relic slots.The other marker takes you to a crack in the ground, in this crack you will fight a single group of enemies, killing this group will "open" up the surrounding camps (marked with light beams). These unlocked camps are important because of the "Hatred" system.The Hatred system is what is holding you back from farming, exploring, looting and, if i'm being dramatic, enjoying the game. See every time you get 1 Hatred, the elites and bosses gets +5% hp and +5% damage.As i mentioned earlier, some of the bosses are so quick that you are pretty much forced to trade blows with them and as you can imagine, that Hatred is going to doom a run pretty quickly.So how do you get Hatred? You get 1 Hatred every time you loot a chest in one of the locked camps. You also get 1 Hatred every time you level up after doing so 5 times, so level 1-5 is free, 6-10 is 1 Hatred each, 11-15 is 2 Hatred each. 15 is the maximum you can level up without killing a boss. Killing a boss effectively subtracts 5 levels from the Hatred system. So it's in your best interest to take the 5 free levels, go for the boss, do the next 5 free levels, go for the boss etc.I'm sure you can already see how this system will discourage you from doing anything aside from the free camps and the quest in the town.As an added annoyance: Equipping upgrades, be they gear or relics, costs Mana. Mana can be gotten from the crack in the ground which unlocks the camps, and from chests in camps, better stuff requires more mana. If you get lucky on a run and get really good upgrades, you might not even be able to use them because you can't afford to equip it.It's just a minor annoyance as it usually evens out, but it does happen alot that you're either sitting on excellent upgrades starving for mana, or sitting on an abundance of mana with nothing to use it on.Because of the Hatred and the Mana systems, the amount of upgrades you get are very few. Hatred will limit you to 5 levels and 5 chests, give or take, probably 4 of those chests will be mana. So realistically you're looking at 6 potential upgrades per boss to make your build. Keep in mind that the good stuff will cost you extra mana so more choices goes towards that or you can go pick up some hatred.Adding to that, if you get hurt and want to heal, you're paying for that through those choices (or the quest reward).While playing well, dodging, swinging and such goes a long way towards a run succeeding, this few upgrades makes a runs success feel very random.My conclusion: Don't buy the game, yet.In time it could well become something great, the foundation is there. The world is big and beautiful, the combat is quick and feels great (even if it needs some tuning here and there), it's such an interesting mix of genres, open world and roguelite. I really feel that Ravenbound could become something special.But they need to get rid of the Hatred system and give players a reason to explore the world. Right now it's not actually open world because there's no reason to leave the path laid before you, you go to the markers and the open camps, then on to the boss, anything else is at best wasting your time.I would love to see the game evolve and grow into the open world roguelite i was hoping for when i bought the game, but at the moment, it's just a roguelite with a lot of travel-time.Add the game to your wishlist and check on it in 6-12 months. As of right now it's simply not worth the price or the time and it saddens me.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option, I'd probably pick that. In the absence of it, not sure I'd recommend. Unless I'm missing something, I've tried out three weapons (s&s, dual axes, longsword), and outside of mildly varied timings on when the attack goes off and how much damage it does, there's not really much difference between how you end up playing them. You keep swinging, and because dodging/blocking can interrupt any action, you simply do one or the other when you see an attack coming. It leads to the combat feeling one note no matter what enemy you're facing. There's been no ranged gameplay so far, and no unique abilities to spruce things up in melee (the charged attacks seem mostly for gapclosing or guardbreaking, their damage compared to just light attacking doesn't seem particularly worth it).Maybe the remaining weapons bring something new to the table, but the three I've used don't feel as though they change combat in any significant way, and so I'm lead to believe the others won't change it much either outside of timings. The issue with that is timings only matter when dodging and blocking can't interrupt what you're doing. Why would it matter if I have a greataxe that swings slowly for big numbers if I don't have to commit to the swing? There's no risk in it.The camps so far also feel the same, everything camp I've hit, everything's using melee weapons, and all it changes is the timing of my dodging or blocking. I never feel like I need to disengage because dodging is unlimited. Three bandits using a longsword, greataxe, and dual axes didn't feel particularly different from a swarm of gremlins camp or the singular troll camp, because they're all just swinging their weapons and I'm just hacking away at them while I dodge or block 90-100% of what's coming in. Where are the archers forcing me to watch for attacks from off camera? Where are the trappers setting up area denial so I have to think about where I move? If this world has any sort of magical beings, where are the delayed explosions in an area, entangling vines, wasp swarms chasing me so I have to be aware of them while I fight off whatever I'm doing? If these things exist in the game, it shouldn't take me an hour and a half of relatively fast exploration/clearing to find any of them.World looks nice, running around it is nice, raven form is a neat idea to let you explore the relatively vertical land without too much frustration, same for the grappling hook letting you parkour up whatever you want. The randomized vessel traits/weapons is fun, though maybe instead of a randomize button to get a new set, make it a "create your vessel" button for an increased cost so someone wanting to try something specific doesn't have to potentially reroll 5-10+ times. I don't mind the mana/cards upgrade system, it's a necessity for balance and requires you to think about your character building a bit more than you would if it was just upgrade cards. It also means a lot more cards can be thrown at you without risk of the game feeling too easy from that perspective.As it's a combat focused game with pretty midtier combat, I can't recommend it at its current price. Wait for a sale and pick it up then.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is far from perfect, but a lot of negativity around it is either short-sighted or just outright wrong. I'll delve into these points further into this post. But if you need a TLDR -- Don't be discouraged by the negative reviews, this game is a diamond in the rough. I really do recommend it and I hope the devs keep upgrading and polishing it.Now, let's get into the details.Combat has a big misconception in the reviews: Both Block and Dodge are equally important and it's silly to think otherwise. Perfect Block makes you temporarily invulnerable, and Perfect Dodge gives you a temporary universal speed buff (attack speed *and* movement speed). Both of these things can be improved further with Traits and Relics. Against smart enemy groups or bosses with aggressive and irregular attack patterns, you need to combine both buffs to stay alive. Until that first boss goes down, the enemies may act dumb even in groups, but don't be fooled and don't get cocky. As you progress, they will get smarter. Moreover; Hold Light Attack to ready yourself for a stronger hit. You can cancel this into a block or dodge when necessary. This will help you avoid getting caught out by anything hard to stagger with a lot of health.The Hatred system does two things: It allows you to fine-tune your own difficulty, and it prevents overscaling your Vessel too quickly. Without it, the game would simply be too easy-- Runs where you get loot and upgrades so good you start one-tapping bosses would be every run. And you're not always forced to take Hatred Shards-- it's an *optional* way to Empower Shards at the drawback of increased difficulty. Maybe it can be improved, but Hatred is not a bad system. It's a *defining* feature. If you want loot without constantly scaling enemy health up; Just empower regular shards and cleanse beacons so you can loot chests without Hatred. The minute you build Hatred 1, go kill the Warden. As long as you don't Empower Hatred Shards, enemy health and damage will never scale upwards beyond base-- but the world base scales up every time you beat a boss.There *are* reasons to not just fly around in raven form all the time-- there are hidden loot and lore areas that you can't find via a marker while using Vision. You find them with your eyes. If those loot areas happen to be near a cleansed Beacon, then that's free loot without Hatred. That being said, I don't disagree that there should be more things in the world as lore is a one-time thing and not all bonus loot areas can be cleansed.As far as performance alone As long as your system isn't a complete potato and you're not trying to play on resolutions even most AAA games don't support, you shouldn't have many problems. (my GPU as of posting this is a GTX 1060 and my CPU is an i7 4790K and I use Medium settings. I do get frame drops but nothing unplayable. The only time I crashed was back during the demo and they have since improved the game performance.)

_childDocuments_.review: They need to remove or rework the hatred system entirely. Replace it with something like a "hero" system that makes the PLAYER stronger as reward for completing content. They need to let the player shift into a raven at any place in the overworld outside of combat. They need to remove the rng starting class mechanic and just let the player choose their race, weapons and passives.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: There are some really good things about Ravenbound, and it has its appeal, but it lacks the depth I crave in order to get a lot of play out of a roguelike. Not enough variety in builds and playstyles, not enough of a sense of variation from run to run.It's got the bones of a great game, but it just isn't done yet. But the devs have announced it's feature complete, which means it won't ever become the game it deserves to be.There's fun to be had, but not enough for me to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Slay The Spire meets Dark Souls; however, lacking depth both of those titles provide respectively.Reviews have described Ravenbound as an "open world RPG" - it is not.  This is a Roguelite title, where repeated deaths is a certainty, and luck of the draw is important.  While the world is gorgeous, it is not filled with quests, exploration, voice acted characters, and the likes that we see in an RPG. The real gem that makes the game fun is the incredible difficulty succeeding in combat based on cards drawn, weapon style, and player skill.Again, this game is not an RPG.  If you are looking for story and an incredible world filled with questing and adventure, then look elsewhere.  If you love Roguelite games with a high difficulty curve, then this is where you belong.

_childDocuments_.review: This game used to be very bare bones and not good the first hour of gameplay, which was quite discouraging. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I bought a while back but just got around to trying and I am enjoying it.  I am not sure why it has such mixed reviews (I haven't read them), but in my 2 hours of playing, I felt that it was a very interesting Rougelite/Soulslike game.  The controls (via XBOX controller) are fluid, and I had no crashes or bugs during my playtime.  I personally give this one a thumbs up.  It isn't as hard as many Soulslike games, but it is an interesting take on the genre mixed with Roguelite / Progression that carries over.   I personally recommend the game.   I like the style and flow.
