_childDocuments_.review: Game has infinite potential. If they fix the cons i'm about to share, this game will be one of the best. I can only hope they turn around and fix most of the cons so i can turn this review into positive.--- Pros ---- Progress: Steady progress every run. Power ups you get feel just enough (Not too much or too little).- Difficulty: Get punished for poor choices (makes the game challenging)- Power-Ups: Card system which let's you manipulate power ups. You can save cards for later if you don't want to your new power up right away.- Travel: Raven travel feels good and relaxing (Love the fact there is no UI, just raven). Trying to hit obstacles turned the bird around making it look smooth.- Playstyle: After a couple of runs, you can customize your starting kit to your preferred playstyle. Personally love the wolf character. He can sprint faster and destroy cards for extra DPS.- Freedom: You're completely free. The game doesn't tell you what to do whatsoever, to the point you have to keep playing to understand mechanics by yourself. Zero hand-holding.- Atmosphere: The game looks very cinematic. The switch between battle and travel is very appealing.--- Cons ---- Combat (Dodge): It's too generous. You can dodge 100% of attacks by dashing, just to instantly get a swing on the enemy, just to instantly dodge again. You can even Dodge mid swing, if you regret starting an attack. I sometimes find myself sliding through enemies 90% of the time while sometimes landing attacks. This way i can clear camps with little issue, just a lot of time. Adding a stamina bar would fix this issue.- Combat (Attacks): Too difficult to see whether you performed a heavy or light attack (they look almost the same). Too difficult to understand the impact of each attack (In terms of damage, stagger, debuffs).- Combat (Targeting): When targeting enemies, your camera gets locked on that enemy and you can only switch targets. Stopping targeting is not an option.- Controls: Seems like there is input delay (about 200-300 ms) when doing anything. It's possible to get used to, but the delay shouldn't be there.- Guide: While there is no hand-holding, the tutorial about the systems is very unclear. I had to look some of the phrases to understand what they mean. I still didn't figure out all of them. The game could use a mouse-over on key words to explain what they mean.- UI : Enemy stagger bar sometimes disappear. You can't see your health bar out of combat. Card interface/UI is too slow to reveal and navigate. The look of other menus look unfinished and lazy. In addition, finishing each camp will reward you with choosing up to 3 or 4 cards, which makes you feel like managing cards takes up too much time, because of the fact that menus are slow.- Sound: Some elements of sound stop working when playing the game a certain amount of time. Restarting the game fixes this. Things like steps, attacks, rain, UI sounds, music, disappear occasionally.- Climbing: Not interactive enough. You can throw a hook to climb hills and buildings but it's slow, hard to use, and just useless most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: First off i do enjoy this game, but there is far to many unenjoyable aspects to want to keep playing. I dont know why flight, your main source of movement, is locked to those lame bird pillars. I have to pick and choose my battles based off of how close they are to those because i dont want to run 500m to the next bird pillar. Also, many people mentioned the hatred aspect killing the exploration and i agree. There should be more ways to clear hatred so im not shoved into the boss fight because my hatred meter is full. Lastly, i would enjoy more rougelite elements that allow me to actually get stronger after every run. The progression between runs is very minimal and makes it hard to want to start a new run with the same tools as before.

_childDocuments_.review: Editing after most recent patch:They didn't fix anything that was actually wrong with the game and have announced that they are no longer working on it. Do not buy this game.I really want to like this game because it has done something that I haven't found in other roguelikes which is the idea of an "open-world". I just can't say it's ready to be played with how poorly optimized it is. The sound cuts out halfway through my run and never comes back, I'm not even sure if there's supposed to be voice acting because there is for the intro, then never again, and whenever I fight draugrs, my frames drop to 5 because of the fog the surrounds them. I've set every setting to as low as I can and attempted to adjust my computer to fix these issues, but nothing has worked. The combat seems like it works well, the flight to get around is simple and fun, and there's great diversity in the builds you can create. I would like to see more interaction with the world around you (including more pots because I've had run where I don't even find one by the time I'm fighting the second boss) and the addition of some new enemy types.This game is so close to being a great roguelike, but these setbacks are just too big to ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, polished world design with fantastic landscape and scale, yet when it comes to the meat of the game, I feel bored only 3 hours in. Now if you could take the game and instead of dying have respawn points, and safes to lock gear away, and kill that horrible card & mana system... then you'd have a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this, but unfortunately I just don't enjoy the loop.Main issues:- Combat isn't varied enough to make the rogue like replaying fun. - Bosses don't get harder they just get more health.- big empty map with only the same few enemies over and over- too much running around between everything. They give you the ability to fly as a raven to traverse the massive empty map, but lock it behind a handful of locations, so you end up running 1-3 min before you can even fly 1-3 min to the next location. Positives: - Grappling hook is fun- the few times you can fly a run is really cool

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few major things that really keep this game's combat from being really enjoyable.Poise is extremely awkward. It's hard to guess when a block will or won't interrupt a multi-attack combo. It's also hard to guess when bringing up the block mid combo will work.The game slows down a lot. I'm not sure if this is a performance issue with the particles or entirely intentional, but I hate it, it completely throws the timing off.Finally, I get the impression you need to bring the block up a couple frames before getting hit for a perfect block. This would be fine and normal with a regular parry window, but it's tight enough to be very, very irritating.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, while I do understand some of the negative points mentioned by all these negative reviews, some are either grossly exaggerated or very subjective. To me, it feels overall pretty nice and fun! Some aspects definitely need some work though and I hope to see lots of bug fixes and quality of life improvements in the future! Would recommend if you can stomach the price and don't expect an absolutely flawless game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game with rewarding yet challenging combat, and intriguing deck-building elements. The free-roam/open-world element is well done, meaning you can play at your own pace - I especially like the fluidity that the Raven brings to the game! If you wanted to like Dark Souls, but felt it needed to be a little bit more chill, and if you love Rougelites/Roguelikes, then you'll love this.I think the reviews are harsh - complaining about a Rougelite/Rougelike "...feeling a bit repetitive in some places..." is like complaining about an RPG having too many dialogue options. Besides, I wouldn't categorise this game as negatively repetitive. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Patch 1.1.3, Got all achievements (33/33)Recommend for those who looking for 3D Action with Roguelite/Roguelike element games. Not recommend for open world fans. I am not really into action game because my skill is bad, but just wanted to try it out since it is a roguelike game, I only able to beat the game in Normal difficulty once, which highly depending on my skills on playing cards to win. Transform to Raven is fun but you need to enter the Raven transformation spot to do that. I do find it quite annoying in some areas, where you are in somewhere low on the map, yet the nearest transformation spot is on a really high mountain, instantly feels like a walking sim to me, wasting a lot of time without benefit here. I really hope there is Raven transformation spot nearby every enemy spot.About Open-World, I don't find myself enjoy the open world. I walking or flying around the world just purely enjoying the view, nothing else, for those hidden stuff that you discovered, they are just for experience points for my skill tree to progress, it is not something like making me stronger in the run. Yes I do find some Sigil Key usage areas randomly on the map but Sigil Key is a very limited resource. I also can find some chests randomly on the map when I try to discover, BUT the chest is a Hatred Chest. In normal cases I would just avoid to open that since the game could become harder if I open it. So, in the end I feel it is just pointless for open world. All the enemies are not lure-able, they stay in 1 spot, lure further will get their HP reset, I would rather the game just let me instantly enter the arena and fight, instead of keep flying and running around, this also turning me down to keep myself playing as it can be really boring.Hatred system is not as bad as some reviews mentioned, maybe it is bad previously but I don't know about that since I just bought it on patch 1.1.3. Now Hatred system will give you 1 cursed (or punishment) card and 1-2 cards to choose, it could be useless but most of the time you can just nullify the curse as long as you have enough Sigil Key, you would only want to nullify the Hatred level curse in most cases, so as long as not keep getting the Hatred level curse, you can literally just spamming open the reward chests. In my opinion, current Hatred system is like surprised or unknown event in other card roguelike games where you want to try your luck out to make you stronger when you feel that you cannot grow stronger by constantly fighting enemies.There is a bug really making me angry, which is some entrance just got blocked by a door or stones, even though I am able to resolve it by exit to main menu and resume, it is so frustrating to do that because I would keep on running around first before I decided to try exit to main menu.I only able to beat the game in Normal difficulty once and I don't really feel like wanted to do a re-run unless I have the mood to play it, because I feel lazy to flying around such big map.

_childDocuments_.review: Like all Roguelites it is INCREDIBLY FRUSTRATING to lose a well-stacked character you spent an hour and half upgrading and having to start again with nothing, but this game is so unconventional and twists so many genres that I love it nonetheless.Here's a short overview of Ravenbound: There are 5 zones. You need to choose and beat at least 3 of the 5 zone bosses to unlock the final boss and complete a run. Before going to each zone boss you have the chance to explore the world, fight enemies, and do quests, to get new cards of weapons, armor, and perks to upgrade and strengthen yourself. However, the more upgrade cards you acquire before going to a zone boss, the more negative effect cards you acquire as well. You have to be judicious and efficient with what you do in the open world and can't just hang around upgrading forever. Get too greedy and and you might end up severely weakening yourself instead of getting stronger.It's clever, different, and I hate it. But as I said above, I love it too.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont know what the big problem is that people have with this game.  I have played a few hours and enjoy the combat and the game in general.  It is a little difficult but ím used to playing roguelike games and dying multiple times so i dont get too pissed off and emotional about it. Likes:  combat, visuals and gameplay loops.Dislikes:  i dont like the hatred system really.  Absorbing the hatred chests are so damning to the gameplay that it feels like the chests/camps are only area filler since you’re discouraged from opening them.  I dont like that the huge world is mostly filled with stuff you shouldn’t open… what a shame and i think a poorly thought out mechanic.Overall i like the game regardless and think it’s really fun and keep wanting to come back and play another round and see how far i can get or get a new unlock.I hope they fix the hatred system to make it so the huge beautiful world doesnt feel so useless and a waste of space.  You could reduce the map size by 90% because you only use a very small area to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's a pretty fun game that is receiving way too much negative reviews.Are there areas for improvement? Sure, there's definitely some fine tuning needing to be done, and I'm sure that after a few updates this game will be well worth the $30 (which in my opinion it already is but to each their own).The good:+ Huge world to explore+ Graphics are pretty nice+ Combat is fun + HUD is nonexistent so really immersive kinda like Elden RIngThe meh:+ Needs a bit more direction on what to do after tutorial + For 50 coins healing should be a full heal imo+ Wish there was a map to reference from time to time+ Enemies seem to heal while in combat if they fall out of their "zone" which imo is unfair, especially since I can't heal+ Would be nice if there were more weapons and/or let me switch weapons while in game+ Definitely could use more sources of mana or reward more mana from current sources+ A mini map would be chill tbh+ More enemy types would be fun, maybe some monsters, idk im still early into it so maybe this is a premature point+ A homebase would be cool, even if it's just a tent or something idk I'd just like a place that felt like mine instead of always roaming lolAll in all though really fun game that has a lot of potential but people seem to be really conflating their negative reviews and its unfortunate. In a few updates this game will be on point and (hopefully) after a DLC or two this game will be well worth over $30,P.S. I think there might be a bug when trying to clear the first Gale area or whatever it's called, the boss doesnt seem to have a health bar (not sure if this means he's invincible for some odd reason or if I can still kill him but so far I've lost the 2 times I've tried).

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Combat can be satisfying although enemies can be gimmicky- World is very pretty- Unique idea- Addicting gameplay loop- Interesting builds Cons:-Online account needed to play-Missing compass / way to navigate between places outside of generic markers-Need to go to a location usually 200-300m away to transform into a raven -Character is rng at start with trait / race / weapon being rng -1 Town per map (that matters) that has no real interactions or depth-1 fetch quest per map that has no depth to it -Each enemy camp feels almost the same except for a change in monster type-Chests seem to all give the same drops regardless of the enemies you beat for them / chest tier?-The difficulty scales a lot by having more enemies or very spammy or tanky enemies rather than actual difficulty-Boss spams the same move fast over and over again -Hatred system discourages exploration currently , just clear a few camps and the hatred free camps then move to boss-Many bugs -- Hatred level can stay the same after you have completed a run (latest patch 1.0.2)-- Enemies health doesn't go down sometimes but they still die somehow?-- Grappling hook has you pass through objects and is very finnicky feels like a last minute add-- Crashing -- Enemies from specific camps disappearing-- Invisible NPCs-- Tabbing out or using steam overlay changes game from fullscreen to windowed-- Unlocking more traits causes a bug where you get 2 weapon traits which bugs out the game--Game freezing during combatPersonal annoyances:-Raven sight is not nice to look at

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept game, but this game is really bored.First 3 hours, this game is fun, I mean the first boss fight. It has a little hard to fight but not hard like a boss in soul-like game. But after that second boss is really hard, it's hard and unreasonably. I think Dev want to make the boss like boss in soul-like game but this is a roguelike game.- HP Potion use 2 Mana, HP Potion is random card from root box.- Equipment use Mana to equip that depend on item quality.- Grinding is limited with hatred system and Mana root box is hard to find. Hatred system has 3 bar, I can farm Mana 14 - 21 point per bar (after done first main quest process, 3 - 4 root box and 1 mana box with not hatred (but it has minion around root box...). They will appear around area main quest done [big blue pillar] mana box has small blue pillar, item box has small white pillar) that it's mean I must fly around the map. I must fly around the map and run to the transform point because in this game you can't transform character to the bird anywhere.... It's not soul-like game, in Elden Ring or Dark Soul, you can refill anything at bonfire but this game you must grind again. If I die, I will grind again and again.- Even though the boss action and mechanics are easy to play but boss HP is the one of the cause that why it hard to kill. Long sword is really OP but only minion.- Other problem are game crash, target lock system and POV character and character sound.For anyone to buy, First time to play it's fun but after that it's really bored.For 17$ game, I think this game is not finish, I think Dev can make good more than.

_childDocuments_.review: I think people are little too harsh on this game. Does it have a few goofy game mechanics choices? Yes. Does it have occasional bugs? Also yes. But they aren't charging AAA prices and you still get a fun game out of it. The combat mechanics are satisfying, particularly as you play longer and unlock more stuff and the different weapon types. I think the game should have made everyone's first character start with a longsword as that playstyle feels much more similar to other souls-like games and makes the enemies feel a lot lot less like health sponges, which is a common complaint when playing with the default swords. The game starts to make more sense and opens up a lot more as people play more, though seems like a lot of people are dismissing it very very early on.As a sort of TLDR: I just got done beating Returnal and was looking for something else to scratch that live-die-repeat rougelite loop and this is working for me
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, however it doesn't come without flaws.The best features of this game are it's world and combat, and it emphasizes that a lot.TLDR; Is it worth to buy? Yes, but be patient.Combat:Fluid, parrying and dodging are satisfying.Could do with more weaponry options, and enemy AI can seem erratic, one time it can feel like a proper battle the other time it feels like they spam but one move, or keep dodging out of bound meaning they start resetting and slowly regaining HPThe world:The world looks amazing, flying around the stunning landscape as a Raven just to go sightseeing is worthwhileBut at the same time, it feels.. Empty. There's plenty of camps, vegetation and whatnot.It's that player interact-ability is really limited, you kind of just go to the village, do quest -> kill camps -> heal up -> kill boss-> repeat. Which isn't to say it's bad, because it's a lot of fun but having a massive beautiful open world to explore, give us ways to interact with it, more secret chests, parkour chests, resource gathering maybe to make into potions, or makeshift armour, or sell to get more gold.And that's really Ravenbound, the current gameplay loop is fun, but the potential it can have should be used and I'm eagerly awaiting what the devs will do as they're very open and transparent about development.

_childDocuments_.review: God I want to like this game, the style is great, the combat feels good and I can be a deer person.But dear lord in heaven the balancing is awful. The damage is low, the bosses are spongy, and the the game just feels punishing to play. Chipping away at a boss when I have a full damage build just isn't fun especially when they hit like a truck. I got 3 shot on a berserk build with over 1k of health. which makes me question what the point of taking that modifier is? The scaling is frankly trash even for a rouge like and apparently the new patch makes it even worse. I don't mind hard, but this game is that special type of hard where it feels boring. I don't feel like I've beaten a challenge so much as survived a war of attrition with some bosses. Also:Crashes are constant- Loot doesn't feel fun (you get punished by RNG by location of tear, chest quality and enemy type, and then get hate for it). - quests are repetitive and boring.- The always online isn't a deal breaker but it feels like if you're going to put players online do something with it. Saying 'oh its so you can see other players graves' just feels like a lie when plenty of games just make that optional and it adds basically nothing to the experience, cause why would I pick a grave over a chest???- WHAT IN THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DOES LUCK DO AND WHY DO I WANT IT?????Finally to the Devs, its fine to have your own vision but releasing a patch that makes a game that people are on the fence about even worse because you've been watching streamers MinMax builds may be one of the funniest things I've seen a developer do all year. _childDocuments_.review: This game is basically one big giant battleground where the objective is to fly around and kill various enemies to unlock cards and use them to enhance your weapon armor or abilities, however there are limits to this as the more goodies you unlock you get hatred levels which take away benefits you may receive.As someone who doesn't really care much for dark soul games i enjoyed my time playing this game despite it being 1 life each time round the combat is very entertaining and the wide range of choices and options on how to approach each round / boss makes the game fun to play.Pro's : fly around as a crow  - great fast paced combat with varying weapons - different choices to make enhancing gameplay throughout - beautiful landscape and world to explore - challenging yet not over the top enemies.Con's : combat becomes repetitive - the variety of enemies is very small making them predictable - each stage after killing a boss becomes harder making it practically impossible to not resist taking on board extra hate levels for increased enhancement. - crow gets stuck and is hard to control at times - despite playing on a RTX 4090 experienced stutters and massive frame drops while playing from time to time, though i imagine this will be fixed gradually overtime as the team working on this game have already made improvements.despite all this it is a very fun run through of a beautiful world arena that is worth experiencing once , twice maybe even 3 times plus depending on how much patience you have.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game has been fair – but I have experienced constant crashes due to memory leaks, upwards to 15 to 20 – this makes the game unplayable.However, If that is ever resolved… I have some issues with aspects of the design and implementation too.1)	Free roaming but lack of exploration or depth/reward: Yes, the world looks pretty and there are some hidden chests and such, but overall lacks depth and increasingly feels stale. I would of liked to have more quests (beyond just one!) and incidental encounters and story elements, etc. But especially more interesting loot. I would of liked to have healing potions dropped rather than having to burn cards for coin to buy a healing potion at the village I am forced to travel back to each time – there is no other way to heal. 2)	Lack of character development: Yes, you can earn legacy and unlock starting bonuses for your next pleb, buts that’s it. All cards are lost and you just start over. It is limited as you can’t even pick which bonus you want when unlocked, as it is randomised…. Coupled with that is the dependency on ‘mana’ a card-based meta-currency and 'hatred' that a times will bring your progress to a dead end due to blocking your means to pick up cards! I found this stifles development –  let me play the cards as I see fit when I am rewarded with them as i only have x amount of slots for upgrades and so see no need for mana or hatred.. In summary – its fair but middling and will quickly become stagnant in its current gameplay loop. It could have been so much more – but it is just so underdeveloped and bareboned.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to give the game a positive review cause I know there are people who probably gave it everything they had to build this game. Unfortunately, who ever made the call to put the game out, betrayed all there hard work.Honest Review. I played 26 hours, I beat the game on Tier one by using some slight cheese. Reason being, my graphics card is a 1060 3G and It looks like it can't handle the game. It seems to be being all the effects going off IE Fire lamps, Dust kicking up, fog, flash's, etc. So I had to cheese to make it though some part.But yet my computer can run ELDEN RING a ton better, no drop in frames or lag (this game slows down time somehow, it sucks in the middle of combat.)That being said, if this game was $10 or less and in Early Access, I would probably give it a positive review.$30 us a bit of a scam, if we want to compare it to other games that are leaps and bounds superior in terms of optimization and content.Pro's:- Open world is cool looking- Raven form feels great- Some Music- Some Armor & Weapons- I kept quiting only to want to come back the next day and try to make it work & beat it.Con's :1. Obviously unfinished product being pushed out for $30.2. Visual & game breaking bugs like quest givers being underground or items not working3. The game doesn't always detect when you complete an achievement or a challenge.4. Combat gets stale pretty fast do to the repetitiveness and realization in, this is it.5.  The roguelike RNG is more punishing then it is enjoyable.6.  No special moves, skills, etc.- More but getting to long. The game feels like a beta test. It seems incomplete. For all its assets, it feels empty.I'm actually surprised they were able to make such a big game but it feels, devoid of personality. Like the village NPC have personalities similar to anyone who makes a Roblox game. They stand or walk, you'll see a random text above there head if you get close " There's a storm brewing, better bring in the sheets" or something like that. The only voices things you get is the into animation, and the end animation. Cards being broken is upsetting. The legacy points is a mind bogaling system that feels super unfinished. You can UNLOCK like everything if you beat it in one run considering it give you 2 million when you do, even though you only need like 20k? And some stuff is unlocked though completing. And thats the whole " die again and come back stronger" system. like what? Your not any stronger, you just get a randomized play style you have to build around, if you want a modicum of success. again, feels like this was rushed out the door.THE COMBATBasic basic basic.The action combat mixed with the poorly done lock on mechanic is painful. Not only that but a lot of the NPCs jump back and will levitate on rocks, tents, etc. So it becomes very jaring. Super clunky mechanics at time for something so simple.Boring. The only exciting thing about the combat is you trying not to die and it raising your gamer adreniline.Other then that, it is very spammy. Your trying to stack Status effects on them, while dodging & blocking.I ended up building a ton of armor and spamming light attack to proc Stat effects last 2 boss's on Tier 1 run. At 120 armor, the damage you take is very forgiving and you get most back with gray health.Why isn't there any special cool moves to obtain? Something to make the player go " Oh wow, I want that?"There is literally nothing I want in the game. Only need. " I need to make this build work."THE ROUGELIKEMore like rougesuper-lite.The Card mechanic and the "Do it all over again" is the only thing that I see is rogueish. You can unlock traits but there are a lot of trade off ones and some that you would have to make sacrifices to RNG Jesus to make work. Like " When you cause weakness, 33% more damage & Stagger Impact." So now your searching for things to cause weakness. You might only have 1-2 things unlocked that do this. One might be from blocking, another from taking damage, OR if you Crit/Lucky . So if you do find any of those, then you got to hope you get items to make THOSE work. And because this means your now seaching for spacific camps to have a better chance of getting what you need, its harder, longer and drags.They system focused way to much on punishing and difficulty over fun and engaging. I know they are patching, patching, patching , patching but..... its 2023. You Should know by now that this is a dying form of development. I can only assume the team was put between a rock and a hard place to release this. But then again, they are the developers and publishers. I'll change this in the future if things get astronomically better.ATM I regret  paying $30's for this.Risk of Rain 2, Hades, Astral Ascent(small but good), Slay the Spire, Dead Cells, Inscryption, etcThere are so many successful Rogues out there, you really have to try to miss.I appreciate the bold new open world direction but it looks like all the funding went into that then it stopped.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: Unfortunately, the game play itself and the mechanics are first rather perplexing, and the combat itself is at best average due to the bug abuse / bugs. See your character fly around as you repeatedly press R1 and L1 or R2 and L1 for permanent invulnerability, stagger, and damage. Sure, I could just not do it, but it's funnier to do it. Example: This is a game that is meant to be Early Access and perhaps released in 2 years time, as it stands I can not recommend this game. It's more or less a "deck" builder that revolves around you walking around, unlocking the red beams of lights, then farming nearby monsters around the map to gain blessings, which will become your way of leveling up (armor and weapons)If you open a chest before clearing the area, it will reveal a "hatred" card, which will basically be a debuff and make enemies stronger while removing your ability to actually build any more cards which will shape your character, at that point you can't remove it so you would have to restart the game, which is a rogue like, with very little replay ability. It has an alright foundation, but there are too many blatantly silly things going on. Jump in the air and spam grapple, you'll hover forever, dash attack repetitively, you will be invincible and stagger enemies like crazy, there are so many other things.Among other things like water not actually being well... waterfalls or rivers. It's a layer that is covering up still water beneath it. Meaning, if you submerge yourself 100% you don't get pushed, because you're standing under the effect.

_childDocuments_.review: Full of game breaking bugs. Normally it might be excused for an indie game but it's unacceptable in a game where it can end your run and have to restart each time. Devastating attack doesn't work more than half the time, either it doesn't activate at all or the attack whiffs because of janky hitbox. Enemies resetting health because it thinks you're out of combat even though you haven't moved out of the area, only for it to start attacking you again the next second. Broken hitboxes in general for both player and enemies on any sloped terrain. Excessive fog blocking your view when terrain is uneven, only appears when fighting draugr. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, trust me. I really like the concept of a open world roguelike and the combat is decent, the graphics are good and I really like the animations at play here. The card system is not bad but there are some issues I have with it.Now with a roguelike that is open world, there has to be a mechanic that limits the amount of blessings and upgrades you can get so that you don't get overpowered and one shot the bosses, that's just common sense, I agree.With this game you have blessings, each time you unlock a chest or loot an enemy that has a read aura around it you loose 1 blessing. You loot cards which costs a certain amount of mana. When you start off you have 6 blessings, after defeating the first Warden you gain 5 more and I imagine 5 more after each Warden defeated. There is also a thing you must do before facing the Wardens which grants you a few camps to clear out which gives you a free chest with no blessing cost.The problem is that you need cards for new weapons, new armor, relics that increases stats or adds magical attributes like burning, bleeding, curse etc. There's a lot of things to improve but the number of blessings doesn't reflect that as well as it should in my opinion. After running out of blessing you will start to gain Hatred cards each time you loot, these Hatred cards can drain you gold, your mana, damage, armor, increase vendor prices, increase your Hatred level which makes enemies tougher.I feel like I'm being punished for looting because the amount of damage I need to effectively combat enemies and the Wardens is quite high. I'm sure there are builds that are very effective in the game but I don't wanna go for the "One build to rule them all" kind of gameplay, that's boring.I like the combat as I said but there is one issue. The enemies are fast, you not so much. You're fast but enemies are much faster and dodging and blocking becomes the only thing you can do at times. It becomes this dodge, attack, dodge, attack, dodge, attack. And enemies can if you don't time the dodge perfectly follow you while you dodge and hit you anyway, this depends on the enemy and what attack they use but some enemies are better at this than others.The skill tree is decent but limited in a lot of ways. Difficult to explain really without showing.There are multiple passive skill tree nodes that are just... Meh! Weapon class nodes which gives a bonus to something but locks you to a specific weapon type like two-handed weapons, dual-wielding, axes etc. There is one that gives you access to all types of weapons but there is a downside to pretty much every aspect of the skill tree, almost.Oh and no mage builds in the game. Can't go mage or ranged even in this game which is a shame.The "Folks" as they call it is basically your race and I love the design of them and they each have a specialty for when your "drain" a card. Draining a card is when you remove a card from your inventory without gaining the cards effect but instead you gain something based on your folk race. Either you gain gold, damage or mana. No matter which one you choose, you're gonna be missing something on the run.In my latest run I couldn't go on because I didn't have the gold to heal nor buy myself a Relic slot so that I could actually challenge the Warden. I was basically locked because of the race I was playing.I had the cards for a good build, I had the mana to use the ones I wanted but I couldn't because I didn't have enough relic slots and I couldn't get a card to unlock a relic slot nor did I have the money to buy a relic slot because I had gained Hatred cards that took away the gold I had.Gold can only be gained via cards and side quests, 1 quest for each area and that's only 100 gold which isn't much.I want to recommend the game, I want to like it but there are so many little things that come together for me that creates this issue with the game that I can't look past.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good-looking and challenging rogue-like with some unique ideas, but I think most players are going to find it too frustrating to be worthwhile in its current state. Enemies are very tanky and combat is floaty, with both the players and enemies sliding all over the place. Really the best way to survive fights involves sliding and dodging constantly, which gets a bit tedious. A weightier, more grounded combat system would really have been a better approach here. The difficulty is very uneven; the most difficult enemy camps can take ages to clear as you are forced to constantly kite the enemies apart in drawn out hit-and-run battles, and some enemies are simply such overwhelming damage sponges that you're bound to mess up before you can take them down. You can occasionally power up and get a nice run going through the use of the cards that you acquire by winning battles, but in the majority of my runs I never had enough mana to use any of them. Most of my runs also involved the game crashing to desktop at least once; this sometimes happens when you die, which erases any progress you made during that run. Not great!  I think with some additional bug-fixing and some very extensive balancing work, this could be a really great game. They've got the groundwork here for a really interesting and fresh take on the genre, so hopefully with some time and effort they're able to make this thing as fun as I think it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start off by saying I think that Ravenbound IS A GOOD GAME at least when it comes to combat and movement. There are several systems in here that don't make a lot of sense once you first start but once you change your mindset its OKAY. Hatred is the thing that people dislike the most, however it is completely possible to get to each boss without getting any hatred. The way that you are supposed to play this game, at least as far as I can tell is, cleanse the obelisk, clear the camps nearby and go do the town quest, if you haven't leveled up 5 times yet, go clear camps (without looting the chest, your greed will be your downfall) and by then you should have one locked slot with perm hatred and the ability to kill the boss. This works for all bosses all the time, if you're lucky your loadout will be good and it should be a fairly easy fight, if you're lucky.The problems I see with this game are two distinct types, bugs and balance. This game is buggy, town NPC will just vanish, music and other sounds stop at random times, game settings not sticking, items in the world won't be intractable, and most frustratingly of all the game will randomly crash (this happened to me 4 times in the first 1.2 hours of me playing, I lost count after that). Most of these are minor and will be solved if you close and reopen the game but the frequency of these happening is so frequent that most of the time its just better to live with it.The second major issue is luck, I know I said balance but it will make sense in a second. Luck is a fundemental part of this game, your traits that you unlock with the legacy points are not something you can select for a character for your next run, it gets added to the pool of possible options for your three randomly selected characters, you can spend more legacy points to reroll your 3 starters but ultimately you can't pick what you get. From there you get assigned two quests, one to cleanse a obelisk and the other to help the town, both these depend on luck, sometimes your obelisk will only have two camps nearby that give you rewards, sometims it will have 5 and the difficulty of the nearby camps is also random, so it may be 5 super easy camps or 2 really hard ones. The problem here is that the 5 camps that are easy will give you a chest every per camp and 2 upgrade points. thats 10 upgrade points and 5 pieces of gear straight away (technically 3 more gear cards because you can level up 3 times from 10 points), where as the 2 hard camps will still only give you 2 upgrade points and 1 chest each meaning you only get 3 total items for a lot more work. This makes the whole game feel kind of unrewarding for your hard work not only do your hours of play only get you random traits but even when you get a good loadout to start you could get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ quest that requires you to kill a hard monster for little reward or an obelisk that does the same which is a death sentence for most runs. Taking a moment to talk about everything else this game has to offer, the landscape is beautiful, the towns are pretty and have some nice variety for using mostly the same assets. The flight is super fun however it also comes with a downside that does change the pace of the game but, I will get to that in a second. The combat feels weighty and good, timing the dodges is a little forgiving but nice when you have a huge crowd of enemies your fighting and it allows you to close the gap for larger enemies like bosses and troll when they try to run away. Blocking isn't something I do to often but it is a completely viable play style and worth it if you'd rather facetank your enemies. Overall the experience itself is good but not great. I like this game and think that in a few updates it will likely be quite good and most people will be very happy with it, however right now it just feels unfinished, unpolished. The number of bugs and the overall unrewarding progression are too big of a hindrance for most people to be able to enjoy this otherwise great game. Lastly I want to touch on flight. It seems to be a hot button issue that most people think is good but how you get to do it is terrible. However after playing for a while I will say it isn't that aweful of an experinece but it does change the pace of the game in a way that does not fit well. Going to a launch pad is slow, even with the wolf folks who seem to run faster (maybe just a perspective thing) it is slow. This causes getting to the next combat experience to be significantly longer than fight itself, this means you will spend most of your time running or flying rather than fighting which for a fast pace action game is bad. Overall Ravenbound is a fairly good game that feels unfinished with a bad reward system. I do like it and will continue to play it because I enjoy it but I cannot recommend it in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: An update to my original review. Ravenbound is a completely different game now from when it first launched, with the addition of an unlocking skill tree, new ways to enhance a run with sigils, changes to the hatred mechanic and total overhaul of the traits and many of the cards. The environment is still gorgeous, although it is still vastly under populated with extremely static mobs, bosses and chests. With the changes to the hatred mechanic there is now reason to explore though if you want to go for a long play through to test a variety of more fun but slower build paths. The RNG on the cards is still extremely annoying and with the new update you can no longer abuse playthroughs by only unlocking cards you want as they are auto unlocked as you level up your account. The skilltree does somewhat make up for this as you've got a bunch of passive skills that help to make your run easier. There have been a number of performance fixes, with there now being far less crashes and bugs. You will still have a couple if you alt tab too much and during moments of high intensity, but for the majority of the time you won't have any issues. The game still lacks a fundamental reason to keep playing, the skilltree is a bandaid fix on progression, but even that will wane thin for many as once you've defeated the betrayer once, there is no reason to continue outside of speedrunning the game. Which I am having a blast doing myself but I do not think that it's the most common thing for the casual player to get involved in. The Devs are communicating strongly at the present time making changes based on player feedback and regularly hosting QnA sessions. Which is a positive start. I know many people will base their opinion of this game on how Second Extinction went and I can see a lot of similiarities in the starting process lots of feedback and implemented changes, will that continue we will have to wait and see. The game feels more complete now (although far from finished) and had it been launched in this state I think would've done a lot better, but it feels like it is currently on the right path only time will tell if they are able to keep up with the regular improvements. It still feels very much like an Early Access game but if you enjoy being involved in the development then the discord is a great place to communicate your thoughts/feelings about the game and it's direction. Overall, the game is in a reasonable state to change my review from negative to positive. However, the price is still too high in my opinion to buy the game outside of a minimum 20-30% discount with a 50% discount being ideal. But many positives so far and I hope to see them continue.

_childDocuments_.review: This game fills a need for me by combining the high fantasy and roguelite genres with souls-like diffculty. While there is still plenty of areas for the game to improve (included at the end of the review), I am happy to recommend the game at its current price point, and look forward to where the devs take it during early access.Pros:+ Great art style - the wold is vibrant and it leans into its Scandinavian folklore well.+ Fluid combat system; although there is an opportunity for variety.+ Innovative mechanic of transforming into a Raven to traverse long distances and allowing exploration very early in the game.+ The combination of deck building and third person combat is well done and enjoyable; however, there is an opportunity to help direct new players with energy management early on.Cons:- Game leans into the souls-like difficulty, however, the little direction the game provides may cause new players to leave before getting into the rhythm of the game. - The grapple system is interesting but isn't used meaningfully. There is an opportunity to add chests at the top of the towers to reward parkour/exploration.- Game crashes for me every hour or so (RTX4090 i9-12900ks).

_childDocuments_.review: There are good things about this game, the raven form is super cool and fun to use, I like the grappling hook maneuver system. However the game loop is not fun, the hatred system is still to frustrating, they did a minor change to it before I started playing but it is minor (you can unlock a few chests around a certain zone without getting hatred increase)The cons, this game reminds me a lot of Darkest Dungeon but not in a good way. There are to many stacking penalties, whenever you combine shards in game you increase your hatred, tough but would be fair if that was the only thing, however there are negative cards you can pick up. So not only do you increase the difficulty by raising your hatred and getting random debuffs like an increase in the cost to activate your cards, losing all your gold, or a decrease in your weapon damage. This creates a death spiral where if you start to do badly and start getting these things, you're going to be doing worse. The game is an open world but like most open worlds is suffers from the fact that if feels empty, there is so much space but nothing in 90% of it. If a game developer ever reads this I believe this is the main reason why people want to be able to activate ravenform at any time, not because travel takes a long time but because its insanely boring. I'm not just going to complain here but offer a potential solution, put some wandering patrols around that drop free stuff, health orbs, gold, cards that you can pick up without getting hatred or the risk of a negative card. You can make these groups larger than those in camp for some added risk but it would do a lot to increase the lived in feeling of the world. Wandering mini-bosses could also be added who if you defeat them reduce a percentage of your currently gathered hatred and maybe drop a cool card.Combat is the only thing to do in this game so another thing that would really add to the enjoyment is adding some puzzles, we have a grappling hook so adding a jumping section/puzzle where completing it earns you some free mana would add something to break up the constant fighting and give people options to enhance their game.The ability to start with 1-3 cards you've unlocked on past playthroughs would allow people to construct builds in game instead of having to pray to rnjesus that they get something they like or can use. I kept getting cards that would give me frenzy against burning targets despite having no ability to inflict burning. Having starting cards you could choose would encourage replaying the game to try out different strategies to see what does and doesn't work.As of right now I can't recommend people play this, I could keep at this and get good at the game and beat it, but I don't feel like my time is respected by the game currently so I have no incentive to get good at it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel obligated to post a review despite being only 8hrs in, given the wildly negative reviews the game is getting.It's great so far! Once I figured out some strategies to not get annihilated and streamline the run progression, it really picked up in pace and enjoyment. Got thoroughly stomped my first few runs until I figured some bits out.A few downsides. Some things aren't made apparent or obvious immediately. I've crashed three times in 8hrs of play. Lost audio only for my own hits, which made combat feel much less impactful for one run. And the world doesn't feel FULL, which seems totally fine to me given that it's not meant to be like an open world RPG experience, but I can get why that might be a turnoff for some people. That's about it, in my experience.It's got some neat systems, and the open world adds some nice flair to the otherwise relatively linear roguelite genre. Metaprogression is pretty solid via achievements for unlocks as well as a resource you gain just by engaging in the runs. Combat feels nice, once I got into the flow of the perf dodges/parries; I saw some complaints of people complaining about getting rushed by several mobs at once, but you can easily just spam or time parries to knock back all enemies at once The game's surprisingly forgiving by letting you regain some lost hp after each hit, too.Tip 1: Each race/class has a unique ability for breaking down cards. For instance, the ulfar (wolf people) can destroy cards in hand to gain +10% weapon damage; if you find yourself with a ton of cards and no mana to play them, just go ahead and crank up your weapon damage so you're getting some value.Tip 2: Some stuff requires holding down the button rather than tapping it. For instance, I was confused and mildly frustrated when I wouldn't pop out of raven form most of the time, but it was because I was mostly tapping the button instead of holding it.Tip 3: The towns are way more useful than I initially thought. You can heal roughly 50% hp for 50g, or expand your slots for 50g, or straight up buy cards if you're gold rich, or gamble for cards. Completing the side quests gives you a bit of gold, and humans can get gold for destroying cards.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because fighting seemed fun and challenging. But there are too many things that are broken right now and I've only played 7 hours at the time of writing this. A few things to keep in mind if you want to try this out:1. The game has a weird performance issue when it comes to the HUD on 4K monitors / resolution. I noticed that after a run and while leveling up, each time the level up bar started to fill, the frames dropped by 20. During this the game in the background is completely frozen and the only thing changing is the HUD. It's so weird that a HUD can cause frames to drop -- and you'll see these same frame drops during combat, because HUD elements displaying an enemies status such as bleeding, cursed, etc. are displayed above them and the text causes really bad lag.2. The combat is fun but the enemies can be unfair. I wanted the combat to be fair but hard like in Elden Ring but enemies will 360 target lock you, making dodging attacks seemingly unfair at times. You'll go to roll behind an enemy just to have them spin around and hit you anyways.3. You'll lose out on really good runs because of bugs. The game has chests, and you need to collect a certain amount of them to be guided to the boss. But sometimes those chests will be underground or behind a wall you can't open. I had one run end because the boss door opened by the invisible wall remained and I couldn't get into the boss room to fight them.4. Trying out new builds was fun but the game definitely looked like it was going to get repetitive and grindy really fast. There's I think 8 different enemies. You'll fight them over and over and once you figure out their cheap tactics (360 spin hits, etc) you'll be able to beat them pretty easily, and your build won't even matter anymore.5. The world is open but it feels so desolate and empty. I think this is okay for the price of the game and the fact that it's a roguelite but running and flying around the world eventually feels more like just getting from point A to B. In other words, the game could have just been a room based dungeon crawler where you go from room to room and you wouldn't have the weird environment bugs, underground chests, etc.TL/DR; 4K resolution performance is really bad because of UI text -- nothing to do with graphics. Enemies are cheap but easy to figure out. Builds are really fun but end up not mattering. Open world isn't really needed. Lots of run ending glitches and bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read the rest of my review, I want to say that I believe that this COULD BE a good game (hence the recommendation), and is currently just decent. The foundations are there, they're good, everything else just needs a lot of polishing.- This game is incredibly pretty, and it runs well. I get a stable 100 FPS on High settings (i7-8700 3.2 GHz, RTX 2080) and just flying around the world is a treat.- The world is expansive. It definitely feels like it had people living there, with various destroyed ports and structures around, and the numerous villages in the game which are a very nice addition.- The combat system is well made. The combat feels impactful, you have multiple weapon categories (all with their own stats and differences), status effects, guarding and dodging.- The card system that this game utilizes is big, with a lot of cards to unlock and use.- Decent enemy variety. It's nothing special, but definitely enough to keep me focused and having to switch strategies between enemies accordingly.- This game is very unforgiving. One misstep or mistiming of your dodge or guard and your entire run could be over. Enemies are tanky, hit hard and move fast, while the character that you play as can sometimes feel like they're made out of toothpicks if you get dealt the wrong cards. The newest patch doubled down on this.You also can't just top up on cards or coins or better weapons, as the game has a "hatred" system, which fills up over time as you get cards and eventually gives you debuffs for taking cards.- You get no meaningful choices. Everything in this game is RNG. From the character you play as to the cards you get. If you're a person that wants to hand pick their run and try out specific strategies, this game will not allow it.- No permanent progression. As a roguelite (and such a difficult one at that), I expected some sort of leveling up of stats or weapons that stay between runs. However, this game has decided to not take this approach, with the only unlocks being character traits and ability cards.- No explanation of mechanics. Stats such as luck, stagger impact or multistrike are never explained anywhere. It isn't said what they do or how they help. For example, there are "Blessings", and for my first run I expected them to do something special (like boost my stats), only to realize that the only thing they do is get rid of accumulated hatred.- The open world, gameplay wise, is essentially empty, with the only thing in it being enemy encounters. One of the developers has said on the game's discord that the plan is to add ambiance such as small animals, but I feel that there could be so much more, such as collectibles, side quests, puzzles, other ways to make money, etc. With such an expansive open world, it would be a shame to waste it.As many others have stated, this game should've been launched in early access, as it basically is in early access. The developers are regularly taking suggestions on their Discord, which is good, but the game not being in early access can be a bit misleading as it feels unfinished.There's  of potential here. If they balance this game right, implement the community's suggestions and take the game as a whole in the right direction, it could become one of the better games of 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: While the concept is interesting the execution is meh at best. This goes off of the hatred system (which i do not care for) simply the more you kill and collect the more hatred you increase when picking up the shards and you guessed it to RNG cards that possible increase stats or are trash. At the same time increasing bosses and elites output each time you have a shard of hatred which is nearly impossible to not have almost every time you open a chest. And get this once you pick enough shards up it locks a shard of hatred to you progress bar and can only be removed by you guessed it again defeating the boss whom of which if your like me is nearly 50% to 100% (those one shots are real) stronger due to excessive grinding from poor RNG. When removing hatred locked shards it only does so one at a time by the way each time you defeat a boss. In all the game feels unrewarding for combat and the want for exploration is not needed due to the punishment for shard collection via hatred system. The game itself needs to be reworked to be long term playable i would definitely wait a month or two to see if the devs listen to community or if this game will die like the many others before it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after a few updates and having played a bit more:This game is still broken ♥♥♥♥ and frustrate me so much... I regret so much not being able to refund this game.--------------I don't like to give negative reviews, I prefer to encourage devs to do better and hope for the game to become better... But unfortunately, I have to give a negative review for this game.I really enjoyed the first hour of gameplay when everything was new to discovered but the way the game lacks so many things, it died quickly...I would be more forgiving if this game had an Early Access tag and was cheaper but this is sold as a fully finished game and it is pretty expansive.First, like many reviews pointed out, you have to create an account and be online to play a single-player game. This is not a issue for me but it is good to know because some of the issue I have with the game comes from the game being online. I got disconnected a few times while playing.... which would not happen if they let us play offline.Then there are performance issues, I have a pretty good computer but sometimes, the combat is messy. The only thing you do in this game is fight, so it has to be pretty good and solid.. and to be honest, they are not too far from it but the current state as a fully released game is unacceptable. Let me explain.It felt sticky, like sometimes, your character would keep focusing on the same target even if I didn't "target lock" and I was looking at an other enemy. Also, I don't know if they queue user input or if it's the lag that does that but sometimes, I feel like my character keep attacking even after I tried to dodge or shield. This is a very fast paced game and the combat needs to be super responsive to be viable. Unfortunately, if I press dodge and it doesn't interrupt my attacks, it's a big nope.And now for the world exploration part. For me, it's a half win... they missed so many good opportunities with the world. They built a pretty world and you really want to explore it and use the grappling-hook to find secrets but unfortunately, there is nothing to find... Except for the same generic "cut and past" camp with three enemies and a chest.. there is not much more to see and that is sad to me. So many times, I tried to climb a tower or explore only to be let down by an emptiness.Even the town feel sad. The first I got there, the first two NPCs I encountered had the exact same face and look... I mean... it wasn't a big deal but for me, this was the first mark of laziness I saw in the world and after that, it just kept creeping on me... The world building is lazy.Let me finish this review by quickly describing a run: You get out of the main tower, you find the first crystal to break, find a few camp to kill and loot, get to the boss....The open world only makes it longer to achieve and gives you the impression there is more but it's all a lie.I might change my review at a later date if the devs fix their game but unfortunately, this is a full release so I don't have big expectations that they will... Should have know better, their other game have a review of "Mostly Positive"... but I wanted to like the idea of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank god that i got this for free, would never pay for this.If you are into vikings and such, get Valheim instead.This could have been a really nice game but they had to have different mechanics that just makes the game worse.Why even have the "Hatred" mechanics in the game? Remove it entierly and the game would be more fun than what it is now.Ravenform can not be used whenever you want, you have to run to a specific place in order to use it.Dont know why the grappling hook is a thing, you dont even need it at all.The world feels too big, lots of empty spaces.Always online for a single player game, thats bad.Not recommended, not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: Would've given this game a positive review if this was early access or if there was a roadmap for continued development. From what i can find this is the full game and its simply half baked in all the systems. Hatred is a weird system and doesn't feel balanced in either direction or really necessary. The combat is either incredibly easy or just unstaggerable, unparieable, and spammy enemies come up. So it feels wildly unbalanced and like all the options the game gives you with stagger, block, and dodge is reduced to just dodge and even then the hitboxes are wildly inconsistent.Enemies are either barely an inconvenience or god himself and sometimes 3 of god himself.Open world is empty and while beautiful doesn't bring anything meaningful to the table.Most of the world feels useless because you have to clear this large rock boss room to not take hatred for opening chests in an area, but you only do that once per world and it only covers like 4 out of probably 45 camps in the world.Most of the systems just feel completely useless because you can just rush the stone room, get like 4 augments and almost complete the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after many more hours:I recommend this game. Big Learning Curve, first several hours are a pain but once youre past 5-10 hours it all makes much more sense and its actually fun. I just wanna jump back in and try out new builds and mess around. Yes, the game has tons of issues and wonky mechanics. It also crashes every hour at least once on me but its good. If the Devs listen and fix some stuff, this can be amazing. Honestly it is like a game in early access and should have released as one.btw, the only reason I continued playing is because steam did not want to refund me the game and I wanted to get my moneys worth.Original review after around 7 hours:Oh Ravenbound. How excited I was for this game. I even tested the beta, gave some feedback to the devs and was hoping for something to waste my time on.But even time wasted on this is too much of a waste.Ravenbound has a few very good things, lets talk about those first.+ It looks visually stunning. Good Job, the game looks great, cranking up graphics really makes this a fantastic looking game.+ Good Concept. and... thats kinda it.So why is this game something I cant recommend anyone?- Heavily Repetitive.God, after already 7 hours it becomes so repetitive. Theres just no depth to the combat. Its just RT/RB spam and dodge spam. Nothing else. Its honestly just boring. Restart your vessel, cleanse the area, collect the non-hatred chests and go to the boss, move on to next area and die to some wonky camera stuff or an enemy that suddenly is so strong it nearly 3 shots you. Rinse and Repeat- No feeling of progression.I dont know if its just me but I just dont feel like Im making any progress. I unlock more cards and traits and all of that but... I just continue to get the low bad cards and there's no real guaranteed progress. No permanent stats increases to make your next run easier, nothing. I dont understand it tbh.- The Hatred System... is just so contradictive? Here, kill enemies but... you will make the boss stronger if you collect too much. So how do you become stronger without giving the every enemy a buff that keeps on stacking. I cant even track how much stronger all enemies became cause theres no indicator. - No proper Ultrawide support. Ye its 2023 and I cant play this game on my Ultrawide without some issues. Either the whole game is stretched from 16:9 to 21:9 or the UI is just cut off halfway. I did mention this in my beta-feedback but obviously it wasnt fixed.Now that I think about it, I mentioned multiple issues in my beta-feedback that are still persistent and werent worked on.This game could have been really cool, but sadly some people couldnt wait longer and had to release it as quickly as possible. I like the DEV team, I am in the discord and they're cool people and I hope they will take all the feedback in and change the game for the better.If I could, I'd still refund it to be honest. Just not worth 30€ right now.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: My initial review was posted when the game just got released. It was in an alright state but with good improvements the game could be better.However after that, the game got worse and worse, systems scrapped, changed for worse, and lastly they pulled the plug and stopped updating the game after a few months.I'll leave the old review below, but in the current state I do not recommend this gameOld review:After playing for a night I can safely say that this game is not as bad as the reviews make it look.If i were to make it into a Pros and Cons list:Pros - Combat, while not very deep, is very fun. Enemies dodge, block and backstab, you are going back and forth between playing passively when you haven't been hit and aggresive when you have been hit and it feels great!- The game looks pretty good for a developer who has 3 titles to its name- Unlocks are plenty and give more options the more runs you get into.- Enemies are suprisingly varied in their attacks. The deeper into a run you get the more interesting their patterns become.Cons- The tombstone system feels worthless. Why take 1 negative, for 1 card. When you can take 1 negative for 3 cards and keep one?- Many things are not explained, not even in the compendium. What is luck? What is lucky? Or for example how legacy can be used to unlock new traits and weapons (I thought it was only used for rerolls up untill hour 2)- Effort in terms of visuals seem to be incredibly misplaced. Why are towns detailed to the point where they have working elevators and detailed housing. But the rest of the overworld is left to look generic and plain? If the focus is on camps and towns, just let players turn into crows when out of combat and ditch the idea of exploring the world by foot.Lastly not really a + or - but this game is 100% more a roguelike than a roguelite. As far as i know, there is no progression that actually makes you stronger from the get go. You unlock new cards, new traits etc. but they aren't strictly better than what you have at the start as far as I can tell.All in all, do not get scared by the (currently) 37% positive reviews. Most are issues with controllers, account logins and other small things.With a little bit of polish and some fixes this game would be great already.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this in beta originally and got sent a key. I would not have played this game otherwise after what I experienced in the beta, this game is not worth the money. I played this release version a bit but aside from the first area and boss being a bit easier (or maybe I just got a lucky run, tbh I think I did), it feels exactly like the beta, which I did not like.Bandit camps, the game. The only way to gear up in this game is through obtaining and playing (if you can) cards, which are random and are not guaranteed to be helpful based on what you currently have equipped. Don't have a bleed build setup yet because you never got a weapon that applies bleed (OP af but tbh it's necessary)? Well here's three cards to choose from that boost your non-existent bleed damage. Need more than 20 armor? Here's a card that changes your current 20 armor for 20 armor, so now you have 20 armor.The more you clear bandit camps, which is the primary way to gear up, the less you are able to gear up since it slowly removes the amount of cards you can draw (max of 3) per chest or through consuming fragments from elite enemies. Each time you lose a card slot and consume fragments, instead of drawing three cards to choose one from, you draw two and enemies get a free +5% to their health. So while you just obtained yet another unusable card the enemies get a guaranteed upgrade. If you don't kill the area's boss soon enough, eventually all your fragment slots can be filled with "hatred" instead so you keep losing the potential to get better cards and increasing the enemies' health.Longsword is broken in a good way in that it infinitely staggers lower level enemies, which is nice since every enemy is a damage sponge. Gold is pretty much pointless aside from healing or maybe getting another useless card.Fought a Troll, got it to half health, but its main attack has it jump backwards. It jumped backwards enough to get out of its camp range, which caused it to stop taking damage, heal to max, and ignore me to reset back to its original spawn position. So I had to start the fight over again.Sometimes I feel like smaller dev studios just hype themselves up just for creating something, how did no one stop anywhere in development and think "maybe we should make the game fun?"

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let all the bad reviews discourage you from buying this game.The vibe is amazing and the combat feels really smooth.It's a open world ROGUELITE, so don't expect the open world to be filled, it has a certain amount of camps everytime just like a normal roguelike.You can choose from there what you want to invest time/health/curse into.If you play safe and only take non-cursed stuff, you will get less debuffs, less money and you get to a boss within 4-6 camps.You want to risk debuffs and get loot? You can do that as well and take 20 camps in the same area.It runs great on a normal PC, mine is far from good.It does have stuff that I'd like to see change and maybe the price isn't worth it right now.But I can see this game grow a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a lot of fun in the game so far. The only thing I would like to see is the option to scroll the camera further from my character. I see people complaining about no character creation.... It's because your character is technically "The Raven".. Not the vessel that gets randomly generated and dies to empower you. The premise of the game is that these vessels continue to die in order to make your next vessel strong enough to beat things that your previous vessel could not. You WILL DIE... A LOT... It's part of the games design.If you have ever played the game "ASCEND: Hand of KUL" it is similar to that game. It was an old game that technically wasn't multiplayer but was always "Online" because other players deaths in their world impact your world in certain ways.This is the same for this game. When another player dies somewhere they leave "Hate" in your world in the form of a gravestone that you can cleanse and loot for cards. The game would not work offline because of this feature.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow us to see fragment names to build towards what we want;Allow us to see the name of the mobs more clearly when flying so I can choose what camp to clear;Allow us to discard fragments we picked up so we can free a slot in case we find other one that fits more our build;Allow us to "blacklist" some cards so they don't appear on a specific run to increase the chances of others being drawn;The Hatred System just don't work on the current concept from what I understood (which is not a lot due to how confusing it is). I need to clear a mana node to free 4 chest from hatred right? But what about the whole world? I want to travel and see it. The game itself tells us to choose our camps for the fragments we want but most of the time i cant see mobs names... neither fragments names... Am I supposed to only pick the ones I want? What about the chests away from the node? Am I supposed to see them and just ignore? It is counter-intuitive. I see chest, monke-neuron activate, I grab shiny; and gets punished...This review is from a new player pov, the hatred system breeds confusion and kinda scares people away. _childDocuments_.review: The first impression was pretty bad. Uncomfortable camera controls. Awkward tutorials where you're not entirely sure what you're doing, Clumsy double-jump with a grappling hook into thin air for some reason? Attack moves are so detached from terrain that it's a challenge to break some clay pots. Then you turn into a crow and miss the entire flying tutorial while trying to steer.The combat is kinda impressively bad at times. Things fly around, it's hard to say what moves enemies are pulling. Animations are detached from the scene and enemies jump through objects. Hit boxes all over the place. If you don't quit at this point and play a few runs, it kinda starts getting almost interesting. A lot of stuff isn't explained, but you can piece things together to work out what the actual gameplay loop is. The synergies you can assemble can be pretty wild and you can get amusingly OP. Can get kinda fun. Then you get bored after a few more runs.There's probably something pretty cool in there, but you have to dig it out from under a lot of very rough and often buggy content. Having a good run? How about boss doors get stuck...

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty fun but a couple things I cannot get over. The game heavily punishes you for taking your time. It would honestly be better if there was a separate game mode where you could play the game as it is now and another without any sort of time difficulty increases. Another thing is the Betrayer boss fight, this is probably the worst boss fight I have ever done in any video game. The great thing about fighting and overcoming bosses that are difficult in most of these souls likes is the fight is at least fair, when you lose you can look at it objectively and see how you can improve. This guy has has no downtime and a overly bloated health pool he will beat you in attrition alone, you will develop carpal tunnel before you beat him. Other than that UI bugs in every run so far. I've had Hatred Cards stay stuck in my Vessel screen not allowing me to see what my third card is when choosing. And this last run I ran into the quest markers not removing themselves either after an area was complete or the chest/objective was complete.

There's also little incentive to go beyond your hatred limit in terms of exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: "RavenBound. <3It's a Rogue-Like or Rogue-Lite open-world game with a vast and stunning world, RPG elements, and frenetic action.However, there is a system called Hatred that creates a debuff when you explore and conquer camps that were previously dominated by creatures and beings that work for the game's villains.This system takes away the best thing about the game, which is exploration.Exploration in the Rogue-Like genre is not commonly used by companies, and typically, games in this genre are based on quick matches with a maximum of three exploration options.Although RavenBound invites players to explore, the Hatred system takes away the exploration, leaving players with just over 20% of the game to explore, since each slot locked by Hatred adds more power and life to the boss and elite enemies of each run.It doesn't seem like they have reached the refined point where the common gameplay of players who bought the game and the desire to make a different game come together and peacefully coexist, bringing balance, dynamism, and action to the game.It's important to keep in mind that the invitation of RavenBound is exploration with the Rogue-Lite or Rogue-Like style.This HAS TO END right now...-Too much time is expended running towards a raven platform.We need to introduce other transformations to run on the ground, even if there is a cooldown period.-The Hatred System needs some tweaking.If I play and kill too much, the boss gets buffed?What the heck? More kills should mean less boss power. That's not too hard to see.At least remove those blocks on artifact slots.-You need to play with an account and be online all the time.No, please, no. Do you want to learn something from our gameplay? Okay, I'll let you see my gameplay. But don't ever make this an obligation. Never. This is not an MMORPG; this is an indie single-player game.I'll play it the way I want. At the first opportunity, I'll get this game from a torrent, so I can play offline or not be bound to a server..."

_childDocuments_.review: Early negative reviews might turn you away from this game and they're somewhat justified. The world (though huge and beautiful) is quite barren and begs you to fly from outpost to outpost in order to engage with meaningful content. However...While I had one crash in 2 hours, when I started the game back up and hit play, I was right back to where I was when the game crashed. Minimal loss in game time, little to no loss of energy (combat is aggressive but fun and rewarding), and I'm honestly looking forward to beating down more bandits, draugr, and trolls. Also, the world is gorgeous and my bias towards gaming with friends leaves me wanting some kind of multiplayer.If you're a fan of roguelike/lites (this feels more "like" than "lite" despite the unlocks) & you want something in your game library that's engaging and can easily stem the tide of boredom, Ravenbound might be worth your time!(devs: don't let the negative reviews get you down. Keep up the good work. You folks are killing it!)
