_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:The game is a huge amount of fun, runs well, combat is easy to pick up and hard to master. Worth the money. It has bugs at time of writing but they are being sorted patch by patch.Honestly, this is an absolute gem of a game. I do see the issues that some people bring up, but the core game play loop is amazing and addictive for me.The main issues at the moment are the bugs! These are not "game breaking" but there are some "run ending" bugs that will make you want to pull your hair out. That being said at time of review 24/04/2023 the devs are already putting out patches and I have little doubt that these bugs will be crushed very soon.Most of the bugs can honestly be fixed by a quick "quit to main menu and jump back in". This is extremely fast, My PC can do it in less than 10 seconds. That being said, I am sure the Devs are still working to sort them out.COMBAT:The combat in the game feels really great, blocking with perfect timing and dodging too. Both have their uses to either make you invulnerable for a few seconds or boost your attack power for a few moments. They do both have their use!If you actually understand the way the cards stack and the way you build, the enemies are not just health junkie tanks, this game manages to tread a very fine line between too much health and too easy.Some of the attacks in the game feel extremely BS, when you are fighting 10 guys in the dark and can barely see anything and they are all spamming attacks at you causing you to semi-stun lock... it can be frustrating. I am still learning though.ISSUES:Please god EXPLAIN some of the stats in game. Give me some information in the lore book or anything. I could very well just be thick but I have absolutely no idea what luck does in combat and what being "lucky" in combat means.... it boosts loot rarity but how does that support me in combat?Some of the attacks from the enemies do feel SLIGHTLY out of time, this is a bit more rare and it could very well be me being bad but the combat sometimes just really feels slightly off with the perfect block/dodge. I have made it to the 4th boss so I don't think I am that dense but sometimes I will get the perfect dodge (confirmed by getting a buff) and still take damage.My last issue is the biggest one and it is honestly a good issue to have. The map is HUGE with so much to explore but each stage of the run allows me to clear maybe 10 - 15 camps while trying to keep hatred low. I so badly want to explore this map and clear every single camp! It is a big ask but please can I have a sandbox mode where I can just go around clearing all the camps, the map is so beautiful!OVERALL:This is a fantastic game with a harsh steam review score. (At the moment MIXED). This in my opinion is an extremely fun and engaging game, well worth the asking price! It has some bugs that will be fixed as I have trust in the devs. If you are at all interested, I say give it a try. It is challenging and you can't just brute force your way through, you have to think and plan your build as you go.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having fun playing this. It's got satisfying combat and the ambiance/graphics are amazing. It can be a little overwhelming for me when there are a ton of enemies (end up dodging/blocking so much that it's impossible to find an opening to attack), but that's just part of the combat.Speaking of the strategy, the encouraged strategy is very unusual from any other game. Once you get used to it though, it's not so bad. Just never open corrupted chests. Only gain cards through essence drops or cleaned chests. Sometimes that will leave you a little thin on loot, but it's always been a better choice than opening a corrupted chest.Unlocks are okay, with the common 'card system' problem of ending up with a card pool that's over saturated with stuff that doesn't work well together, making it increasingly unlikely that you'll get things that pair well together. That said, a lot of the better items that you unlock are good enough on their own to be worth it. One annoyance as a result of this system is rolling gimped characters starts happening fast (characters with two weapon traits, e.g. "This character only draws swords" paired with "This character only draws axes").There have been issues, but the developers have been pretty good with timely updates, especially for the more serious problems.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys games with Souls-like combat, I was disappointed with this game. The difficulty level was simply too high, but not in a way that was enjoyable or rewarding. Instead, it felt frustrating and made me feel bad about myself as a player. The game lacked the balance needed for a truly enjoyable experience.One of the biggest issues with the game was the lack of checkpoints. It felt like progress was constantly being reset, and any progress made was erased by the next difficulty spike. This made the game feel like a slog, rather than a fun and engaging experience. I found myself becoming more and more frustrated with each failed attempt.Additionally, the game lacked the ability to make meaningful choices about the character. The character felt static and lacked depth. The game would have been improved if there were opportunities to make choices that impacted the character's abilities

_childDocuments_.review: So, after 35 hours in this game I'm still unsure how to feel. I love this game and I hate this game at the same time. Ravenbound has a lot of unused potential, but still you can have a plenty of good time with it. I would like to recommend it to everyone (and I will), BUT at the same time I don't want to. In the end you should decide yourself.To start with pros and cons I just wanna say that some +/- could seem like a contradiction, but there really is the feeling of some mechanics that they are bad and good silmutaneously.Pros:+ Visuals (Graphics and models, environments and overall world looks fantastic).+ Card system (You do your builds by drawing and playing cards and that idea is pretty original in the game like this and there are lots of weapon, equipment and relic cards).+ Combat (Combat is fluid and pretty accurate).+ Races, Wpn classes (there are 3 playable races with unique traits and multiple weapon classes).+ Grapling hook (You can traverse high places with grapling hook that feels pretty good).+ Gameplay loop (In its heart it is great and enjoyable, but other aspects ruins it a little).+ Achievements (It is possible to get them even without advancing to higher world tiers).Cons:- Combat (It's button mashy and repetetive after few hours).- Wpn classes (There are only close combat weapons that feels pretty much the same. No magic, no bows. Shame.).- Grapling hook (It feels pretty good, but it's pretty much useless, cause you have no reason to climb high places most of the time).- Audio and visual bugs (sound looping, NPCs not spawning etc.).- No spellcasting even when magic is present (as mentioned before).- Hatred mechanic (the mechanic that punishes you for drawing too much cards basically, so if you want to pimp your build, you will suffer.... a lot.).- Drops (in my case the game crashes 2-3 times for aprox 4 hour-long session).Additionally the post launch patch made the game much harder even when it was already pretty hard AND they even didn't fix all the issues and bugs. I've collected all achievements and I feel like the game has nothing else to offer and I have no reason to play it until some content update, which I hope it would get. If the game was an Early access I wouldn't be so strict in my review, but it is fully released title that could stant some more work.Did I enjoyed it? Yes.Is it worth your money? If you can afford 30eur for a game without hesitation.... Yes. If you can't wait some more time or get it on sale.Why to hesitate? You never know if the devs will continue to work on this game, but I hope they will.Once more: The game has a great potential that will hopefully be fullfiled sometime. I will continue to edit this review with every major update. In Ravenbounds current state, my rating is 5/10 with a lot of place to improve and potential to climb much higher. The devs are pretty active for now so hopefully they would stay that way.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game so far. The loop is a little straightforward but it's fun. I'm enjoying build creation each run. My current play time is 3.8 hours and so far, it has crashed on me 11 times. On the bright side, the game recovers from a crash decently. _childDocuments_.review: I keep playing this game but I wouldn't recommend it for most people. As long as the gameplay is challenging and engaging, I stick to what I bought, especially because this game is in the AA price range so I want my money's worth.Overall this game makes me think of an openworld Hand of Fate. Not grandiose, not terrible, just okay, and that's also because I don't think I am very demanding.Misses:- lack of polish (no voice acting, missing vfx)- tutorial is present, but omits a terrible amount of information (like what's the precise difference between "orange" and "red" camps? You have some armors that protect you against specific enemy types, but you only unlock the lore entry for this enemy type once you've beaten it, so until then you don't even know against whom your armor is strong against. What do the symbols mean under each card's mana cost? All of that information you'll have to figure out because the game can't bother explaining these to you, which is sad because it would probably give people the desire to actually build their vessel in a specific way.- performance (game crashed twice for me)Design points:- weapon types actually don't matter at all, they have barely different movesets but that's it. It would have been nice to for instance say that greataxes generate more stagger whereas twin axes make people bleed. Attach an existing status effect to each weapon type would actually have people think about the synergies of the vessel's trait with what weapon type they're starting with, instead of just different moveset, basically just aesthetics.- the grappling hook is useless and could have easily benefited the game with some simple additions: what if you could get a relic that doubles your next damage after you've hooked to someone? another relic that brings people to you instead of you to them? etc.- boss camps: Some "red" camps are actually bosses not elites. The game doesn't say or give any reason as to why you should beat a red boss rather than a red elite since it would result in the same treasure chest. I just did a "red" troll camp with two trolls and steamrolled them, I then moved to another "red" troll camp right after, same run, and I ended up in the arena with the bigass troll wielding a sword and I just got one-shot. Why should I beat this guy if the chest is of same rarity?- In terms of traversal the hook is useless, period. Almost any need of the hook got overwritten by the distance covered by jump sprinting. I would keep the jump because it doesn't break the flow of movement instead of the hook that keeps you in the air for one second doing nothing while it's looking for a point to latch onto that most likely you would be able to get to without the hook anyway. There are some towers in the open world, what if the "Hatred" was so strong around these towers that you wouldn't be able to go in raven mode, and would need to do some grappling hook up the tower to free up the corruption on this tower, which would have a camp at the base and give you a free chest just like the towers of hatred?- the "alternate attack" for weapons doesn't change anything at all. The only quality to that attack is the guard breaking ability when you hold it, which applies to all weapon types, again nullifying the potential differences weapon types could have. What if twin axes alternate attack (pressed, not held) would build up a bleeding gauge, while the great axe's whirlwind looking one could build up staggering easier?- it feels like the team spent a tremendous amount of time on the open world performance, graphics and traversal in raven mode, which are all great. Moving around as a raven is pretty satisfying and you can feel the speed spikes greatly (especially when gliding after nose diving). For the benefit of the game I think more time should have been spent polishing combat and cards/traits than the open world.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting a few months for this game to release. Looked promising, but failed every step of the way. Refunded my purchase after an hour. _childDocuments_.review: It's far from a popular opinion, but I hated Elden Ring. I put over 200 hours in on PS5, in an effort to overcome the combat system and the abusive arc, only to have myself feel like I was being put through a shredder. It wasn't . This... this is .There are always a PILE of things I wish for in a game. But this is hands down in the ZELDA classic vein. You can feel the love and intention the Developers put into everything.Is it perfect? No. But as an avid Action RPG (focus on the Role Playing aspects) this has me hooked. It has excellent mechanics, a smooth character controller, and isn't trying to eat my skin every six inches. There are things I don't love. I think the Camera controls could use some refinement. The hard lock on characters should be moveable to a new target, and lock on at a greater distance. Some of the movement physics issues others have mentioned need work. But seriously... Kena was too linear and too short. That was 50$. Elden ripped my face off for 60$. Let's not even talk about the 80$ mess that was Forespoken. I love my action games. I love TCG systems in those action games. (Yes I'm one of 5 people to play Baten Kaitos all the way through). And I love my Indie Games. I'm 4 of 6 years into developing my own full scale title at the time of this review. I've spent thousands in the last five years for games with AAA ratings which didn't offer half of this attention to detail and careful craftsmanship. As a Roguelike, I expect they can just funnel content in as the game ages and matures. I think they should have set it as an Early access, and let it mature without the Production 1.0 judgement.Listen, I've waited three years for this game. And I don't regret a penny of the money I spent on it. I am incredibly excited to see where the Devs take it.Do I  Yes. But will this sit on my Steam Deck and be something I casually master and get my face melted by over the next six months? Yes.Buy it. Play it. Love it. Let it grow. And let's cut the elitest nonsense out of our vocabulary. Sometimes a small studio produces something which is just... FUN... and I think SR has done that here. If you don't want to give it a chance that's on you. If you want this to succeed, Offline is a must. I would also recommend that you go back and create something special for your Beta Testers... anyone who tested the game should get a free copy or at least some nifty Tester only loot. And be public about your goals for the title for the future. People knowing it's a living creation, and not a cash grab will help tremendously in the days to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I can no longer in good conscience recommend this game. It had such great potential to be something awesome but the consistent instability and bugs encountered simply make this a chore and not a game that is fun. If you are lucky enough to play a round you are in the minority, every few camps the game will crash, I have had to delete and re-install it to get it to work only to lose all progress and still after a few days the game is unplayable again.  After my last round it awarded me a ridiculous amount of the currency (1 Million+ when normally you get a few hundred to 1000 tops). Now the game will not even load and I am stuck in an infinite load screen loop until my PC's memory get maxed and the game crashes again. This game should be labeled early access or maybe even pre-alpha at best.  It is not ready for consumers and is unacceptable that it was released in this state. Posted my original review below to show how excited I was and forgiving at the start.Original Review:I am obsessed with this game but...it is buggy!First off I want to say I highly recommend this game, don't judge it by reviews, try it, play it! I am a huge fan of the roguelite/roguelike genre and Ravenbound is a truly great iteration and take on it! I think this could be a top tier genre defining type game and one I plan to keep playing for a long time...if improvements are made.I have been having so much fun with this game (14 hours in so far), I have been unable to stop playing...even with all the crashes. To be fair it needed at least a few more months of work before releasing.(Speculation) The game feels rushed and maybe that is due to the amount of bigger games coming out in the next 2-4 months that this was the only competitive window they saw?Pros: * Amazing core game-play loop, keeps me coming back again and again.* Fun and fast paced combat.* Easy to learn but hard to master each of the weapon types. * The mana/gearing system is a cool.* Unique characters.* Really great open world design (regions, camps, map in general).* Boss fights are hard but fair.Cons: (most of these issues can be reset manually by closing the game and restarting but that's annoying)* It crashes...a lot and always in combat (The day one patch did alleviate this but it has crashed 3 times today already on me.* The audio design seems to struggle with what to play at any given moment, sometimes its the great music other times it cranks the sound to 11, other times half the sounds stop working and your left with muffled noises.* The blue tear objectives sometimes just don't have any mobs to clear (exiting the run and rejoining fixes this but that should not be a thing).* The open world is not worth exploring since there is nothing in it...I mean nothing at all, no coins to collect except in the tutorial area, no roaming mobs to fight, nothing aside from a random vendor here and there you just go from one camp to another.* Missing a few core roguelite/roguelike features: (Suggestions really)** Let me have a trait that just gives me 100 coins at the start of each zone so I don't have to do the side quest in each zone (I always do the side quest to get 100 coins in case I need to buy a heal).** Let me have an option/mode to hand pick or swap a trait or weapon at the start (with how many there are its going to be tough to play the ones I want to try)** Add a mob pack here and there that will heal me a little so I don't have to fly back to town which could be on the opposite side of the zone.** If your going to make the side quests take me to the same location/camp every time at least pick one next to a raven point so I can quickly get back to town.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Promising Roguelike with Room for ImprovementTL;DR: Ravenbound is a visually appealing roguelike with enjoyable combat, but the perfect dodge mechanic and the permanent hatred system can be frustrating. The story is easy to overlook, but the atmosphere and setting are well done. Worth a try if you're interested in the genre, especially if the developers plan to fine-tune and expand the content.I've played Ravenbound for 30 hours and would give it a 6.5/10 overall. It's a single-player roguelike game with pleasing graphics and an art style that I find very enjoyable. The sound design is good, but it can get cluttered quickly, while the music is solid, earning an 8/10 in my opinion.The game's controls feel really good, and the combat is fun. However, I experienced some inconsistency with the perfect dodge mechanic, which was frustrating when facing difficult enemies. The game's main mechanics revolve around a hatred system to prevent players from overleveling and steamrolling through bosses. While the temporary hatred feature works well, the permanent hatred aspect can be limiting and may deter players from experimenting with different builds.The story is easy to overlook, but the game's setting and atmosphere are impressive. While the variety in camps and enemies might not be enough for some players, I find it satisfactory for a roguelike game. Character race options are interesting, but there aren't many memorable character interactions.Ravenbound has decent replayability, but the limited end game builds and certain mechanics might hold it back. At $30, the game is worth it if the developers plan to fine-tune and expand on the current content. If not, it might still be worth a try if you're willing to spend the money.Let me know if you have any other changes or additions you'd like me to make.

_childDocuments_.review: Alot of people are giving this game a bad wrap. let me just start with, this game is not super easy to understand, alot of mechanics go unexplained unless you look into the codex to figure out what they do or how they work. Another thing is that, yes the game is janky, but at the same time the game just came out and its from a studio i myself have never heard of before now. my point being that the game is going to crash here and there... that said, this game handles crashes better than any game I've ever played before. I've played over 4 hours at this point because i didn't want to give a review without giving the game a chance and at the time of this review there is still alot i havent seen or done but i can say that many of the negative reviews i read are understandable. The majority of negative talk about how the mechanics are sub par, which i already mentioned above, and the combat is repetetive and button smashy. The combat, at first, feels very button smashy but it does require you to engage your brain, many enemies in the game are chunky and hard to kill but that makes for a requirement to dodge or block, some enemies also have multiple attacks to roll catch, or in other terms hit you after a dodge. Another point I read in other reviews is the the only way to power up is to gather too much hatred but thats just not the case. At the beginning of the game it very much seems to be the case, lots of the worthwhile cards take more than 2 manna and thats hard to come by, alot of the time you cane find boxes, as long as you search for them, that give you a card that gives  3 or 4 mana at the cost of 1 hatred shard. On top of that the main objective literally tells you that there is a monument that gives power without giving hatred, it doesnt tell you in the mission objective but it also gives 5 mana and it cleanses some of the chest and loot boxes around the altar so they dont punish you with hatred shards anymore. TLDR: Most negative reviews dont give the game enough time to get a better understanding of in game mechanics, if youre looking for a new game, ravenbound is pretty good option for the forseeable future, aslong as you give the game enough time for you to get into the flow  (P.S.) Devs, if you read this just know that even if right now people arent liking it that much doesnt mean that the game should be dropped, as a matter of fact, the game has the potential to blow up if support is continued. Please dont give up the game is great and has more than enough potential

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's fine, I've not had any issues with it, I will say that my rig (though not top top of the line because I'm not touching the 40 series RTX cards until a better hardware config is available), it's a decent rig nonetheless, RTX 3080, 64 GB of DDR4 and a Ryzen 9. Most games I play, I can play with graphics maxed out and the video card fans don't even hint at turning on. I started playing this with graphics maxed out, and the fan kicked to life. To many that's not that big a deal, but, given that fans have lifespans, and that heat degrades circuits, it's  a bit of a big deal, especially when it's one game in particular that makes that happen.Now, that said, that's just me wanting to prolong the life of my video card as much as possible given that good RTX cards are hard to come by without bowing a knee to a fragging scalper, and doesn't really have anything to do with the performance I've noticed itself. With things set to max I was still able to enjoy the game without any noticeable loss in framerates. My monitor is an AW3423DW which is qd Oled with an curved screen and 21:9 UW screen at 34". I was unable to test how exactly high the framerate goes because I need a new USB C - Display Port 1.4 cable, as otherwise, the monitor locks framerate to 100 hz via HDMI connections which disables g-sync. That said, at 100 hz framerate, the game ran smooth and everything looked nice. it was a bit odd, though, because the game started Windowed at 1980x1080... other than that, this is an apex game, IDK if it's required, but, when you first load the game, you will be asked to sign in with your Apex login. IDK if that does anything special yet, although it appears that it unlocks other player's graves to loot. As far as gameplay, currently got into the open world and started playing. I, decided to drop this review a bit earlier than I usually do specifically because I'm confused as to why people are saying that the game world is barren. Okay, sure, the starting area doesn't have much in the way of friendly villages, but, unless they made the mistake of walking on foot instead of flying via ravenwing, there's a decent amount of things to do right after the tutorial area. Keep in mind, that this is a roguelite. It's meant to limit the amount of villages you start with as that's something you work towards, but, the main focus isn't on those villages as much as other things. Honestly, I was reminded a small bit of Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild the Viking-esque furry/humie roguelite edition. Don't get me wrong, it's not like Breath of the Wild in a derivative (or arguably inspired) way like, say, Craftworld, however, there are a few parallels nonetheless. I cannot compare this to Dark souls or the Bloodbourne because, although I like the earlier stuff from From Software like the Kings Field series and the Armored Core series... their recent games bore me because they're designed for "hardcore" players who ruin the prospects of other people wanting to buy those game because they think "git gud" is an excuse to be crap human  beings and call other people who don't "show that they're hardcore because they don't conform to being 'hardcore'" "casuals".... that type of baby in teenage or adult skin can bugger off while people like me who actually have been playing video games since as far back as Atari 2600 and 5" floppy discs, have devoted a decent amount of time (most probably more time than they've been alive) playing games. Oh, wait, sorry, this is supposed to be review... whooops, rant over. I would not say that this game is a *scoffs* "souls-like" as there were games that were similar before Dark Souls and Bloodbourne were around, and, imo, they were better. What I can say is that this game is melee combat focused so far, each run inhabits a new body but your character, the raven soul, inhabits that body. between each run there's a meta-currency to apply to unlock new features, like new traits, one of the two furry classes (look, it's not that I hate furry's, I just can't stop saying the term when it's prevalent in a title), new weapon styles etc. There is no regular inventory mangement like you'd expect from an ARPG, instead you're given cards to choose from after collecting the soul fragments of fallen foes, every 3 fragments gives you a card which can have mana. Mana is important because it's how you equip better gear or add a feat. As stands, from what I can see, if you're a min maxer you'll either love it or hate it depending on the type of min-maxer you are. If you're the type that wold load up Icewind Dale and click the reroll button until you get the "perfect number of points" so that you can dump a stat and make another stat queen, you'll probably not like this style of progression. However, if you're the sort of min-maxer who conceptualizes a certain type of build, and goes out of your way to grind some extra stuff to make that build as broken as possible, you'll probably like it. If you're just playing the game for the game without expectations, you'll be just fine, just keep in mind that you don't equip new items, try them out, and then get to revert to what you had previously, because that's not an option, so, you've got to think through if the "upgrade of gear" is actually an upgrade, because, if you pick it, but were building your previous gear up, those upgrades from the previous gear will be gone too. So far, the gameplay loop is decent, and there are a few unique systems, like the way mana and soul fragments are used in lieu of xp, and how when you open a chest it's to get a new card, not a new item per se. Another unique system is hatred. Every chest or player grave that you loot gives you some hatred (unless you cleansed the surrounding area by beating a mini-boss), that hatred comes in 3 tiers which, when you go to load up the cards for a soul fragment give boosts to all elites and bosses. If you absorb too much hatred, one of those tiers becomes unlocked, and, as a result, you permanently lose a loot choice and bosses/elites permanently gain a boost with each chest you open unless you pay someone to cleanse you of that curse. It's pretty unique, and, although that is a bit frustrating to deal with, definitely makes you want to think carefully before looting, or, search for the local baddy which permeates the area with hatred to kill them so you don't have to deal with it. Is there more to the game? yes, IDK what as I've not got that far, what I will say is that, so far, the game does seem to be worth the asking price... Oh, and, no Denuvo, so, that's further reason I like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's a beautiful open-world game, with rogue-like and souls-like elements to it. The characters you play as only get cooler as you progress through, and it does get easier as you learn to telegraph enemies. I've already died multiple times, and each death is just a fresh start as all of your previous decisions are wiped away.Not for the impatient, but definitely for the adventurer! I do hope to see minor improvements to the game, but overall it plays spectacularly on my PC. Most of all, I am already craving to see more content like weapons and card additions. The enemy types presented so far are both interesting and slightly challenging, but I do hope to see more variations as I progress further through.Lastly, this game does take some grinding. Racing to the boss fight before clearing some of the surrounding objectives is NOT a good idea. Take your time, kick some butts, and then when you feel like a super hero, go try the boss.All in all, worth the wait. 10/10 game and worth the full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Seems pretty cool so far, I think once I get the hang of "where to find what" I will last longer, because apparently attempting red beams off the bat is a bad idea lol. The cards and hatred add some unexpected variance to keep things fresh, only thing I find odd is that the world is empty unless it's a point of interest. Even tossing in the odd lower level monster or something would be a welcome change /shrug. I'll update after I put more time into the game.After about 12hrs, I'm leaning towards a pass on Ravenbound.-You pretty much HAVE to follow the same routine each run, and travelling just wastes time.-The 3rd boss seems to be the end of normal combat and the start of Pro-Skater, since if you miss even a few slides, you are done. I had a really OP setup that gave close to 1000%  damage and it was still just taking small chunks off the boss, so either broken or stupid lol-There's rarely a reason you'd want to open a red chest since it's benefit will hardly if ever outweigh the boss buff you get hit with since the scaling is so whack, apparently 5% means the boss is indestructible lol-Why are you fighting 5 or 6 enemies at once? They all try hitting you and I know you can ground slide all over the place but you can't avoid the ones all flying through the air off screen or out of camera view.Neat ideas with the cards, and hatred. Red chests might as well not exist, traversal is beautiful and game runs pretty good for the most part, but travel is a time killer, this could have just as easily been a 2D overhead map that you just clicked to go to the points of interest, since there's no reason to even fight the majority of the things on the map unless they are sitting on an unlocked chest or a specific rune.I was pretty excited to try this out when I was given a key, as I never got the chance when it was in beta. It's fun at first but the scaling in both camp sizes and ridiculous boss fights just border absurdity. So it's being hung up and maybe in a year or five it will be worth coming back to try out again. Also F the need for online in a single-player game, the saves aren't even server side so it's going to be open game for save scumming...
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: how would i rate the game in it's state ? i'd give it a 4/10i like the concept of the game, openworld mixed with roguelite elements is sweethowever, the game in it's current state despite being release as a non early access game is... basic and need a lot of improvementsthis is where i'm mixed, you start with basic equipment, which is fine, but  equiment you'll get will always be about getting more mana, to get more dmg or more armor , but because of the limited mana (if you're lucky) you won't always be able to equip the cards + you'll eventually get hatred which will make the enemies stronger, , that health issue can be a bit anoying when you don't evolve correctly cause of the randomnes in dropscamps (which is the main part of the game) can be a bit anoying as they are repetitive (always 2 elites and 1 commun most camps depending of the difficulty of the camp)the enemies are attacking as long as they're not staggered which is anoying when hitting a basic enemy and not seing him twich after being hit also you can get stormed by those 3 enemies as they will non  stop attack you , making the fights anoying as you'll have to look at the animations of the enemies to guess when they'll attack as perf block makes you invulnerable for a sec, perf doging buffs your attack, but perfect doging an enemy can also lead to death as you're not invulnerable after the doge (the enemy can strike multiple times in a row which made your perf doge useless, you'll get hit if you attack and you can't guess it)the game looks great, the open world comes with biome variety (snowy regions to desert and forests)i didn't had any particular visual glitches but one where the vessels would blink ? before starting a runi'll try to update that sectionfor now one that was pretty anoying but not run endingi turned to human form and simply vanished, unable to control my character, but the camera, hud didn't apear and the enemies where attacking my possition when i would have appeared i guess, to fix that i had to go back to the main menu and resume (thank god i did not had to restart the run)the game loop is, go to village, get quest, go to camp, kill, get loot/mana +risk hatred if you want, go to side quest, kill, go to marker, kill, sell cards to get money, buy hp back, prepare to attempt to kill gardien, repeatfor now i don't see much content, the animations seem basic for the movements, the grapling hook could be better, the camps could use a bit of variety, the enemies could use a nerf (lower hp and dmg or give the players a way to easily heal) addding attack markers or hints so the player can see and react instead of having the enemy attacking from behind the camera as you lock onto another, avoiding dmg when you perfect dodge and the enemy attacks you three times in a row (still with the no hint problem, it's poker for now)reworking the combat behaviors when there are many enemies so it's not just mashing strafe and attack button and hope for the best as you're constantly getting attacked for nowi'd love to see the game hatred reviewed (not big changes, just values added according to your difficulty level, 1-2 % on normal, and more on higher) just so casual players and people that just want to chill can enjoy better the game without the difficulty rising too fasti was hyped but still see ravenbound as a demo for now and not a fully perfected game, at best i'd say early access but the fact that the game is not marked as early access, scares me for the future of the game (game said as complete when it could be improved wich would basicly become repetive and just turn the game into one of those game you play and forget about)

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a blast with this game. I enjoy that getting better means actually getting better vs just getting better stats. It has crashed on me after death about every 3 runs very consistently. Hopefully this will get patched soon. I know there are a lot of negative reviews but I think it's very fun. Give it a shot if you are interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Because of price and the big potential this game has im giving it a thumbs up.The combat is spammy but thats only because it rewards it which should be tweeked. The open world right now looks great but just feels you could of just had a map and instant travel. The RNG cards are simple but make the gameplay fun.6/10 for me but im hoping they work hard on adding more to this game and could be a real gem
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting ideas, and definitely has potential. But the implementation is not really that great. Especially the character control feels strange to me - it's like the character is floating and the combat feels weird since you just keep sliding around, which makes the feeling of floating even worse and the combat much less interesting than what it could have been. I hope it can be a much better game with some nice updates in time! (But until then ...)
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure I did receive a free copy to stream (so take this review as you will with that info). Right off the bat I want to say I really enjoyed the game! I'm a big fan of roguelite games that have a story and a level up system that persists even after death. Some people have mentioned they've had issues with their game crashing? This is something I did not experience personally as the game was rock solid. I like the card system that feeds into the RNG, I enjoyed the fast paced combat, and thought they did a great job on the environment. I do wish there was voice acting in the game to push the narrative even further. I also hope they'll add more weapons to increase the variation of combat. Overall enjoyed the game and plan on playing more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is simple but fast-paced fun that rewards reaction time and paying attention instead of just mashing buttons. The world is gorgeous, though a fair amount of it does seems a little empty - easy and quick to get around in raven form, though. You can choose to play it safe and only clear "cleansed" camps, or try to get even more power while empowering your enemies by clearing camps within the spread of hatred.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to other players because the rouge-lite loop is fun, the movement can be satisfying, and the build-crafting for the various skills feels frustrating and rewarding at the same time.I would however not recommend getting this game at this moment...Main reason being frequent crashes to desktop.Secondary reasons being a poor general user Interface and soundscape that negatively affects accessibility.Tertiary reasons consisting of a cumulative number of minor issues and arbitrary gripes, ranging from incomplete control//key customization, and codex/guide entries, to long distance traversal feeling empty, and wait times for menus or in game "cutscenes" feeling repetitive and immersion breaking to the gameplay.My thoughts are overall that the game needs more time to be fleshed out, it has a distinct "Early Access" feel to it that'll likely sour the experience of most that play it at its current state. It has potential to offer a lot as a more casual rouge-lite, but not without TLC, which the developers has the potential to give based on my experience leading up to this release.I am cautiously optimistic about the future, but not confident to call it a 1.0 release.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Ah damn im not gonna lie i was waiting for this game for quite a while, testing it out while demo was active i had a lot of fun, looking at gameplay without any expectations and criticism cuz it was still only beta/demo.But here we are quite some time later in the future, the game is out and:-For the first hour of gameplay ive encoutered some bugs where npcs wouldnt load-Big ass open world is def there, too shame its empty, i mean okay there are some building some dungeons and mini bosses, but im going to be honest here and its not fun really to run into one location - fight 3 enemies, run into another location fight 3 enemies - fly to another location and guess what fight 3 enemies-combat is pretty fun but sometimes even if i use shield or dash it does not really count idk whyAnyway game in my opinion has huuuge potential but its lacking some stuff for sure and you can feel it right away even with not hunddreds hour inm i might change my opinion later with some nice chunky uptades to it
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game and I can see the developers listened to feedback about the mana system (its easier to acquire and equip gear now), however I will warn you that that I have had multiple issue where it windows and my controller doesnt work, one time I spent 45 min on a run then it windowed and broke (would not stop guarding) resulting in me not being able to attack or dodge and I died. This has been such an anticipated game for me that I still have hope that it could be made into a great game. For now I would hold off buying at the full 30 dollars, unless you come from a country where you can get it for 15 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Attacking, dodging, parrying, flying, overall the whole gameplay feels really good. The enviroment and visuals look really good aswell. The only negative that pretty much kills the game for me is that like 95 % of the cards just offer more damage and nothing else. The rest just offers status effects, coins and stuff therefore every run feels the same with the weapon beeing the only difference.If you just want to enjoy nice combat and dont care about cool card synergies that might get a little out of hand then this game might be for you otherwise I wouldnt recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky game to review.. I like it, or more importantly I like the concept of it.. I played it in Beta and didn't like it to begin with.. I was expecting an open world that was alive as a modern open world should be.. not open world with camps where monsters are.. this was raised by me in the beta and several others.. on the surface this seems to be a very shallow game with little in the way of gameplay and I was turned off by the experience.. however the concept drew me back for one more run.. It wasn't until I had a lot of runs under my belt that the game and its features started to open up, I gave feedback on the beta early based on my experience and.. I ended up really liking what is here, the card system, the different vassals their unique abilities, the card drops.. you really have to play this game a lot to appreciate what is here.. I feel there will be lots of people like me that won't like what is here at first glance.. but given time you will learn more about the game.. I can't tell you to like it, but I can say you have to give it time before you can appreciate it, and yes that's long after your 2 hour refund window..
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game that is on to something that could be great.Had issues creating the account because the sign up button would not work when i started the game.Controls and movement are a bit weird, had to play with the keybinding a bit.Enemies can block with their weapons, but you only get a block that reminds me of the one in super smash.Open world that looks great but feel a bit too empty.I like the card and upgrade system, makes it a bit more challenging.Also the hitbox seems accurate but enemies swing very wide so it can be very punishing.Fun but hope it gets a bit more worked on
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty fun, it's a little rough around the edges and combat can feel a bit floaty sometimes. But I'm having a lot of fun with it, and will probably play through it at least once. The lack of voice acting and very minimal sound fx makes it feel a bit uncanny though. wouldn't need full voice acting but some jibber jabber or at least some sort of sound during dialogue would be nice.The text box UI and interactions with NPC's also feels very unpolished.But If you like this type of game. I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: I'm afraid unplayable for me. I'm on my last group of enemies in a zone and the game just keep crashing. Restarted 10 times, crash mid fight every try. This didn't happend in the beta. I was glad to see some things brought up by the beta testers got fixed and/or changed for this release but alot of things didn't. Until crashes gets patched I'm gonna have to pass on this, it's such a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: lots of potential but needs some work, camera controls (controller) seem a bit off, I think the response curve might be wonky or the stick deadzone might be too high, it's hard to tell without any options to adjust them. early game progression is a mess, there's a reason hades gives you the first upgrade for free, really need to revise how mana is earned it's far too rare early on.put some more time in to see if it got better, it did not. some more issues: combat is far too spammy, enemies have very inconsistent reactions to damage, sometimes you'll be able stun lock and keep up your assault, other times they'll just attack straight through the damage. on top of that it's often very hard to see attack telegraphs, especially when fighting groups. most of the time you're only hope is to get a couple of cheap hits in whilst dodge spamming. always online requirement coupled with bad first impressions probably means this game is doomed to be shutdown at some point. progression and upgrades are controlled through restrictions and rng, you find upgrade cards, but now you need mana to use them, you find mana cards, but now you need more upgrade slots, all of which comes from the same rng card pool. so if rng isn't on your side you can't progress. I've changed my mind about it having potential, too many of these issues are baked into the core game, i'd be extremely surprised if it can be fixed before the servers are pulled.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying it so far for what it is. I have only had 1 crash so far and that was then i was alt tabbing while the game was loading. Aside from that, performance has been smooth. I do agree with other comments that the open world is pretty bare, but I also try to see it as other rogue like games. Other games, you go from room to room and kill the guys, get loot and go to the next room. Here instead of going room to room, you have an open world that you fly to whatever camp you want to do next. Same concept, different execution.The combat does seem pretty basic though with a few combos that I have figured out. I still recommend it for those who like rogue-like games
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. Been waiting for this to release for a long time. Sure the game isn't perfect... but its also day 1.... have you seen the quality of AAA games on day 1 lately? They are Literal garbage... This game has minor bugs and some clipping issues but the more people that play and report bugs/issues the faster the issues get fixed and the better the game gets!This game offers a challenging and unique open world rogue-like style. On my third or fourth death, I went to the snow biome and completed several achievements easily. For those of you who have played more challenging open world games like Elden Ring and other souls games - this is right up your alley. Lots of evasion, parrying and some luck.If you can't handle dying a lot - then don't play this game. The game is meant to be extremely hard from the get-go and get easier the more you play... so if you can make it to run 3 or 4 - you can get play styles and have more fun. Don't just give up after 30 minutes to an hour... thats not how this game works!Have already recommended this game to several friends and will continue to do so!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh I was unaware that it was a roguelite when I bought it, I saw Systemic Reactions and just got it. And I am glad that I did. The graphics are beautiful and super vibrant, the world is quite expansive so there is a lot to explore. The combat at the beginning is rather simple but I'm sure as you progress there will be some changes. It's simple enough yet challenging enough that you can enjoy it. The card system and having to manage mana to use the cards is a very cool idea for a game like this. A cool combination of a roguelite/deckbuilder/fighting game. The music is very nice and the story so far is quite interesting too.Only cons IMO is the lack of character creation but that may come in the future, and a world map.All in all I could say for the 30-ish minutes that I played its definitely worth it. A solid 8/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Fear everything and nothing for death brings you closer to victory in this challenging open world action-roguelite. As the Vessel of an ancient power you must use steel and skill to complete your mission in a dangerous fantasy world inspired by Scandinavian folklore.

name: The Unexpected Quest
detailed_description: An adventure game with strategy and management elements in a medieval fantasy setting - drawing inspiration from classics such as Warcraft 3 and The Settlers. Embark on quests, hunt down treasures and manage your resources as you build, battle, cast magic and brew potions to bring order to a world on the brink of disaster. Strange creatures living in different locations await you. Some of them will help you, others need your help, and others will take a liking to your head...or, rather, your fresh brains. You will visit quiet villages, snow-capped mountaintops, impenetrable forests, and foul-smelling swamps. But one thing will remain the same - adventure awaits you everywhere! Collect everything that isn't bolted to the floor! Dwarves don't mind work, but they won't lift a finger on an empty stomach. You can't build a working mill out of mud and sticks, so you'll have to search for the appropriate materials. Keep food stocked and resources plentiful and your world will expand! Build bridges over turbulent rivers, build docks in the swamps, repair buildings, and build new ones! Mills will provide food, sawmills will provide building materials, forges will improve equipment - and you can always sell the surplus at the market. Many building styles and colors await you in the game. The citizens of the world have always had many problems to overcome and quests to embark on. Try to help everyone you can, and reap the rewards of your labours. You can also always count on what's most important: sincere words of gratitude*. * Computer game characters don't have real feelings or minds. You can get much further with a kind word and a sword than you can with a kind word alone. Hire experienced soldiers, upgrade their armour and weapons, fight, and conquer. Whoever said the pen is mightier than the sword has never been on the receiving end of a Claymore! And with the ‘Tales’ mode introduced in the latest update, battles will be more exciting than ever. Choose from 3 difficulty levels as you play the two initial chapters dedicated to battles. Not enough food or materials? Are your soldiers dying from their wounds? Did the workers decide to create a union? Magic items and potions will remedy the situation! Save up your gold, complete quests, and plunder chests. There are many ways to get magic items!

_childDocuments_.review: I can answer all your questions in two sentences:- No it's not like Warcraft 3 or The Settlers but more like a time management game (without the stress of a timer)- Yes it's a ton of fun!This game really makes me miss playing games like Warcraft 3 or the Majesty. And I love the art style!EDIT: To be honest... I am a 36 old father of 2 little kids and omg they are so annoying sometimes I almost get crazy. This game really helps me to relax in these situations as the music is so calm and the gameplay is easy but still fun. So if you have kids and they go on your nerves you might check this game out, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay yes I hit the thumbs up. And that's technically because overall the game isn't really that bad.Here are the worst things about it.-It's way too simple for an RTS-It's overall quality is cheap-And it's probably only 3-4 hours of gameplayBut why did I say yes? Because it's a fun simple stupid little time consuming game that's not even asking for that much money.It's a little fun, kind of addictive and it's an easy inexpensive way to waste a few hours of your time when you've got nothing currently better to do.Overall I liked it, but just be prepared for what you're getting into.If you want a more in depth look with some legit gameplay then check out the video on my youtube channel (link below)But overall it's not a bad little game. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the RTS and the graphics, and the building and clearing objects were fun but combat needs a lot of work, It's frustrating building multiple combat units only to find out that they're all deadlocked into 1v1's, and by this I mean if I send my swordsman to fight another unit, that unit HAS to be a swordsman as well, so you can't use archer + swordsman onto one swordsman, and you can't have 2 swordsman fight 1 swordsman. The combat is the same with all units , Mages vs Mages/ Archer Vs Archer, another thing that is good to know is that the healers don't actually heal, you have to craft potions to heal up injured units. At the time of writing this I can't genuinely recommend this game to anyone, and concept wise I was really hyped up for it but I'm willing to give it a shot again after a couple patches/updates to it
_childDocuments_.name: The Unexpected Quest

_childDocuments_.review: 6-10h 3/10 1, there is chapter selection No You don't need a guide 2 on Astats No No No No No No No difficulty option NoThis is a fun time-management/light RTS game. In the beginning, I saw some elements from games like the "12 Labours of Hercules/Hermes" kind of games. You need food, wood and gold to build buildings and recruit fighters, for those resources. You'll need to build production buildings and have the workers collect up those resources. Later there are some more RTS mechanics involved but it's always a very light form of RTS.The game has 8 chapters, the first 3 are very short and function as a tutorial for the rest of the game. Each chapter has some new mechanics to make things a little bit more complicated. I really disliked the time mechanics in chapter 7 but the rest of the game was a lot of fun.You also have to manage your inventory. You can only have 6 items active, which includes the weapons for all 3 fighting characters, some items to give more resources and you also want to have potions with you. There is a chest in which you can store a lot more items, but those aren't active and you can't easily access them while in a battle.The achievements for this game are for the most part very easy. Almost all achievements you'll unlock just by playing through the game. You might have to look out for the snowman in Chapter 3 and cleaning the beach in Chapter 6 but if you miss those, they are right at the start of the level, so you can go back to that chapter later and get them within a few seconds of entering that level. The hardest achievement in this game will be to get 3 stars on each chapter. To get the 3 stars you have to complete all the main and side quests in each chapter, open up all the chests and the hardest part of all... your workers and fighters aren't allowed to die. For this one, I suggest saving the game before you try to fight a risky enemy and if somebody dies, reload a save file from before he died and try again. You can see on which chapter you have all the stars, so if you missed one, you'll know very easily which chapter to replay and get that missing star(s).I enjoyed this game a lot, it didn't overstay its welcome, it kept me intrigued enough to keep playing and finish the game, which took me around 10h to fully complete but I should note; that includes some idle time when something IRL work-related popped up, where I'd have to tend to that and also me replaying chapter 4 because one of my workers had died, without me noticing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unexpected Quest

_childDocuments_.review: This is not strategy game! Not at all! So don't expect anything similar to Warcraft 3 or The Settlers.This is just casual time management game and that's the truth.So with that being said, is that game bad? Not, it's quite fun, but I give it thumb down only because misleading description - I don't approve such practice.And as time management game, this one has some fresh ideas, so if you like casual games with zero difficulty level and just want to relax, you may try it. _childDocuments_.review: Quite short but very enjoyable game!No challenge and no time pressure, just complete the objectives while methodically clearing the map by clicking to collect resources and items (both usable and with passive bonuses), construct buildings, hire units, buy upgrades and battle the monsters in the most casual and relaxing way possible.A couple of nuisances are present. For example, inability to cancel a single item collecting request (you can only cancel all requests at once, so if you made 10 proper orders, then made the 11th but realized it's a dangerous one, you can only cancel all 11 orders and will need to make those 10 clicks again). I've also encountered a bug (?) when items dropped near the main building were stacking upon each other instead of being placed in a 3x3 grid like usual (I think it was level 7). On top of that, powerful items with passive bonuses appearing frequency seems to be weird: for example, I just got the one that gives +3 to A, B, C and in then +4 to A in a really short time window and these do not stack (inventory is limited, so managing your items is probably the only "hard" aspect of the game).The biggest letdown for me personally, and this is actually not the first time it happens: the last level. As if the inspiration was squeezed away completely or the time constraints proved to be too tight. There are 8 campaign levels in the game and their complexity rises gradually, like really nice. Early levels can be completed in ~30 minutes, while the late ones can take 1 - 1,5 hours.So, level 7 was rather big and took me about 1,5 hours. But then comes level 8, which was very small, very easy (even by the game standards) and very quick with a big cliffhanger in the story. I mean fine, whatever the cliffhanger, but why such abrupt change in the pace? The game is already quite short, so I was expecting the last level to be at least as "complex" as the level that went before. But nope, quite disappointing.Nonetheless, I can still recommend the game if you'd like to play casual clicking and resource collecting medieval game for a couple of evenings!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game is really casual. It's great for those that don't want to think and just chill. Grab this game on super special if you need a break.In this game, you gather resources, which you can use to clear paths, buy workers and soldiers, and upgrade your base. You basically just click on the resource that you want a worker to gather and off they go. As the game progresses, the maps get larger and slightly more complicated, which means that you need to apply a bit of strategy of how you can tackle the map. You can also pick up side quests from characters on the map, which require you to gather unique resources, which are unlocked behind barriers. You can also pick up items and equipment that can give you boosts to resource production or your army.The graphics aren't amazing and the game isn't particularly large or complicated. But it's fun and I kind of want to play more. Things get interesting from Chapter 3 onwards, so play a bit until then.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a real-time strategy (RTS) before, The Unexpected Quest can serve as a stepping stone, a baby's first RTS as it were.If you want to see my first impressions of The Unexpected Quest as they happened, check out my video. This game exists in a strange middle ground between something that's not quite a mobile game but also isn't an RTS. You just click on objects that your units can interact with: gather resources, build buildings, fight enemies, perform upgrades, etc. The challenge, for lack of a softer word, is in optimizing production to finish missions as quickly as possible. Sending your workers to a task within an enemy's range will cause them to flee, so failure barely exists as a possibility. Each mission will score you for not losing units and completing side quests. The story is passably fine but a bit too lengthy for the format. Some might appreciate that, I suppose, and side quests within missions have lengthy writing that you can easily skip over.The problem is, who is this game for? Young children? People with disabilities who can't play a traditional RTS? I'd call The Unexpected Quest "baby's first RTS," but I'm not sure there's quite enough real-time or strategy to even fit it in that genre. Don't get me wrong, there's nothing explicitly bad about The Unexpected Quest, and perhaps there's a niche of people who will enjoy this game. But it's certainly not for the average gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Note well: this is not really a combat game.  If you're looking for hack-and-slash, try elsewhere. I love the strategic gameplay--for everyone who said 'this is too easy', there's someone like me who prefers it on a more laidback level than  (e.g.) Dark Souls!I bought the game yesterday and got so caught up that I've just sunk seven hours into finishing it. Has to be something there.However, I'm a little annoyed at the ending.  Spoilers: I don't mind cliff-hangers, but I'm disappointed that the last chapter had only just got going when it suddenly ended in a dramatic cut-scene. _childDocuments_.review: While GRID Legends is a clear improvement over GRID 2019, it still leaves some stuff to be desired.From the way the story and career work to the driving physics, GRID Legends has definitely improved many aspects of gameplay making it a much more interesting game to play, but it's still not enough.The story mode makes no sense. First, it doesn't respect what you do. There's a narrative and it will follow it no matter if you just barely managed to achieve the objective they give you or if you do far better. Second, these dumb rivalries make no sense. Rivalry in older GRIDs came from teams that were just really fast, this "bad guy" trope just feels stupid.Just give us a good career mode with the features from GRID 1 like sponsor and team management and add a few more interactive features if you want.Enough of these "Drive to Survive" stories that disrespect what the player does.And, speaking of the career mode, it's still very shallow and boring. All you can do is just race in a series of events, complete X amount to unlock the next level and that's it. No sponsors, no team management, no true involvement. Just race a car and win.TL;DR on the driving, corner entry is the only place the car is willing to rotate, after that all you get is understeer if you don't use the handbrake. It's a terrible mix of "realism" and arcade where you only get the worse of both worlds, clunky drifting paired with chronic understeer.My main problem is how the driving still suffers from an identity crisis.I could ignore all these issues with how the gameplay flow was designed if the driving felt good, but it sadly doesn't.While it's definitely improved from GRID 2019, they seem to be taking "baby steps" instead of trying to do a bigger overhaul, which it needs.At first I thought the problem was just the tyres retaining too much grip when skidding, but it's more than that.The tyres feel like they have a delayed grip response, they don't react immediately to the angle the car is going and this results in a very strange mid corner understeer. The problem begins when the tyres "wake up" and realize they don't have maximum grip anymore and your car gets locked into a line, like a train on rails.From GRID 1 to Autosport, the cars were always happy to rotate more through a turn if you kept turning, it was a matter of controlling the car through the entire turn, not just in the moment you start turning.That felt far more rewarding and fun to learn, Legends on the other hand treats steering like a quick-time event, press and hold the button at the right time to do the corner successfully.Using the handbrake is the only way to get the car to rotate mid turn. Most cars will benefit from using the handbrake around tighter turns and this can really ruin the quality of the racing because drivers can just get away with missing the braking zone by just pulling a quick drift.Then the actual Drift mode is pretty disappointing. The cars feel extremely awkward and in a very strange way understeery, which isn't good for a drift mode.They also suffer from the skidding grip problem, being far too grippy to actually properly drift.It doesn't come close to how nice and natural drifting was in GRID 1 or Autosport, or even GRID 2.I wouldn't buy this game for drifting.The UI looks and feels like garbage. This game's main menu feels like Forza Horizon's pause menu, tabs with tons of garbage under them. Sucks to navigate, sucks too look at.Codemasters was once known for really cool looking yet easy to navigate UI, this is the furthest you can be from that.The online feature where you join a race halfway through is cool, but I think you don't get your car's upgrades when you start driving meaning other players will get an advantage for that first race.The driving physics just sucks for online racing anyways, promotes dirty driving and aggressive moves just for the sake of having cool looking crashes because that's all people seem to care about these days...With the massive discounts you can often find this game on it isn't a bad buy. $10 seems about right for what this game's worth to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I am one of the few lonely souls who actually completed the career mode (different from the story) and I don't see much written about it here, although this is where 90% of your playtime is supposed to be sunken into. So let me lose a few words and explain why I ultimately gave this game a thumbs down. I'd say it's decent. Handling and physics are good, great car list, good sounds and graphics, fun tracks with a few exceptions. In general it's a solid racing game all around. For the most part, no. The progression is incredibly blandly designed, sponsors matter very little once you have completed all of them, there are still no management systems, you are stuck with one single team mate and overall it is detrimentally grindy.In essence, the career is a glorified version of Grid 2019, which was pretty much universally disliked for being too simplistic. Legends' career still is a far cry from the complexity of the first entry and ultimately a shell of its former self.- You are disincentivized from using any other cars than the ones the game initially gives you for free. In order to unlock all events, you need 39km of mileage on one car of its class to unlock a final event required for completion.- In addition to that, often times your car will not reach the required mileage to unlock the last event. This means you basically drive in circles on Indianapolis over and over and over again until the mileage target is hit.- Instead of management aspects they opted in for boring stat upgrades for various things. You are stuck with one mediocre team mate, sponsor objectives are as interesting as "drive 90km" and money is basically never an issue. The most management goes into how to waste the least amount of time.- 95% of the career is either regular circuit racing, elimination or time attack. The game does have other game modes - such as drifting and multi class - but they get used only a small handful of times over the career. It's bizarre how the variety is there and just doesn't get used. Needless to say, it gets boring fast.- The career is split into four "chapters" and in order to unlock the final one you need to 100% complete the third one. Coupled with the two points I have mentioned above, this was mind numbing. Tracks also repeat themselves an insane amount at this point. The game simply does not have the amount of content to warrant 40+ hours of play time.- Countless of UI bugs, tracking errors and AI inconsistencies.- The finale is the wettest farts of wet farts. Just a combination of eight races you have pretty much already done. No significant money reward, no bonus car, not even a credits roll. It felt like the game never ended.All in all, it is a fine racer to pick up on sale for less than 20 bucks. Play the brief story, dabble a little bit into the career, try out the cars you want to try out and then move on. Multiplayer is basically dead on arrival so that's sadly all your getting.

_childDocuments_.review: is a hostage to its own history, struggling for years to repeat its 2008 outstanding accomplishment. Many things are, again, wrong with , but many are right as well. It takes notes of its long-lost success and polishes all that worked out well in 2019's disappointing reboot to a shine.What excites me about  is the addition of a story mode. Driven to Glory is a classic underdog tale, styled like a fly-on-the-wall documentary, where an unknown driver races their way into the big leagues, endures hardships and rivalries, and finally becomes a victor—with your help, of course. Let me get this straight right off the bat: it's cheesy, unengaging, and predictable. But god, doesn't it make me want to smack that smirk off Nathan McKane's little face, the series staple top dog. He finally has a face to go with his name and is immediately thrown into the bad-guy role. Not because he’s arrogant or dressed all in black, but because he enthusiastically tells you all about the new restaurant down the road that lets you choose which lobster you want to kill for dinner.McKane aside, what goes on between the talented cast is a hyperbolic, factitious drama that drags down their decent performance. However, the bigger issue here is that you can't steer the story in the desired direction, even though you're the one behind the wheel. You're expected to finish early races in the middle of the pack, then slowly make your way up the rankings, but if you’re good enough to turn in podium finishes left and right, this sort of messes up the plan. The narrative blissfully ignores that fact and continues as if you’re still fighting for recognition.Bah! I'm putting too much on a circuit racer. I'm glad it gave me a simple goal to strive for.With the story's fluff and pomp out of the way, pure racing can take the center stage back.  hews close to arcade racers thanks to its smooth and forgiving handling, while the simulation elements remain shoehorned as always. On the surface, it looks about the same as its immediate predecessor, but under the hood, it drives far better; things have clearly changed. From electric jaguars, to outrageously-bouncy stadium trucks, to modern-day tuners, the wide and wild line-up of autos and classes all feel different to control, though none are difficult to learn. New camera positioning gives a better sense of speed, and more tire grip ensures your ride is more responsive and stabler than before.You can grind your gears (pun intended) in the career mode, the stretched version of the story mode but with too much gated content. Elimination and drift return after years of absence, while the rest of the game is relegated to the usual circuit, sprint, and time trial races. You're stuck with replaying already-completed events and discouraged to take different vehicles since many of them require upgrades that require both money and a few dozen miles on the odometer. Until you have enough of both, progress is halted. Talking of upgrades, they boil down to tweaking just a few aspects of your machine. As for the mechanic and teammate improvements, they are as basic as "haggling over better prices" or "less faulty driving". Perhaps too basic, but they do add a bit of depth.It builds out the reboot's paltry levels of track variety, too. London and Moscow are the new locations that take it to the streets among the ever-present San Francisco, Tokyo, Paris, and Barcelona tracks. If you're looking for road tripping more than circuit racing, the fictional Strada Alpina, set in Italian Alps, takes the high-speed content galore to new heights. For more freedom, Race Creator allows you to mix and match over a hundred track layouts, cars, and rules as you see fit. Organize crazy multiclass events that see you globetrotting in dinky little machines against big rigs, in hypercars alongside vintage GTs, day and night, rain or shine.As seen with the upgrades, technicality and other adjustable aspects of the vehicle are drastically simplified. Teetering a bar for gear ratio, springs, dampers, and a couple more are all you get for the tuning system; no numbers or units, just a "soft" or "firm" option to describe how you’re modifying the car. Not only that, damage and deformation lack the previous strong detailing. Bumpers and bonnets bend just a little and come off only after a string of intense crashes, while parts like tires seem irremovable, even in open-wheelers. At least, mechanical and terminal damage has been kept.While you're bearing with the slew of career events, realistic opponents make up for other hiccups. As long as you're on their good side, they let you blitz past. Bump them enough, and you bet they will race you just as angry. They'll go bumper-to-bumper to defend their lines and outright slam into you to keep the lead. This is the nemesis system! To balance out their ferocities, they are programmed to be as fallible as you. Tires falling off, engine malfunctions filling up the field with smoke, and cars spinning out around corners, in unscripted sequences, make for spectacular accidents on their part.Aggressive AI, coupled with the highest difficulty, makes it feel almost impossible to get in the lead compared to the next one down, which can often be easy.  suffers from unbalanced difficulties; however, the abundance of customizable settings allowed me to make a mix of expert and hard options and find the right spot for a fun yet challenging experience, whereas anything above medium was excruciating in the previous entry. In terms of multiplayer offerings, the game supports cross-platform play with up to 22 players on the grid. You can come up with many different scenarios using the Race Creator, friends and strangers can hop in even mid-race and take over any AI drivers, without interrupting the match in any way. They can even tag along with you in career mode.Glossy paint shines in the blooming sun, rain puddles make glorious reflections across the tracks, and fireworks sing as they breach through prominent landmarks. All cars do look the part too, making the whole package a visual delight. On the other end of the audiovisual department, engines roar, and crashes are deafening. That wonderful, grating crunch of bumper-to-bumper action is as audible as it is visual. The few songs in the rotation are sweeping orchestral melodies with tightly-produced drums and electric guitar underneath that elevate the races quite well.My  kept this motor purring on the highest settings at 1080p, 60 FPS. Although some of the bugs I encountered are already ironed out with patches, nemeses behave inconsistently on occasion. Sometimes, a clean pass might tick them off. At other times, blasting them into a fence won't register a thing. may not do much to stand out, though on-track carnage and off-track narrative turn it into a well-oiled machine compared to its despised predecessor. As one of the only two purchasable options left in the series, it's obvious where your money should go.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid legends is an arcade style racing game with beautiful graphics and quality content. In Driven to Glory game mode  you'll be closer to understand the backstage of competitive racing by witnessing the rise of a new racing team and the various challenges and rivalries they encounter along the way. The game also features a career mode where you can progress in a more traditional way,starting with easy events and gradually unlock higher tiers by earning reputation and completing objectives. To name a few : circuit races ,time trials elimination and endurance races,there is a lot of cars and unique events to unlock which will keep you busy for a long time.  Pros:- Driven to glory features live-action footage,interviews and behind the scenes footages, the unique events such as sudden mechanical failures or team orders or unexpected weather changes keeps the gameplay fresh - Stunning graphics,the visual fidelity is a significant highlight with realistic lightning,diverse landscapes,beautiful and detailed car models- Accessible and satisfying handling for casual players,a friendly hud and user friendly menus- Dynamic objectives and rivalries,the inclusion of custom objectives and rivalries makes each races more unique and significantCons:- Inconsistent AI behavior ,sometimes it's too easy to win races- It's missing something to leave a mark and be memorable, i don't know what but that's how you feel after you finish itMy review scoreStory - 10 Gameplay- 9 Graphics- 10Sound - 9Overall - 9.5Conclusion -  Solid racing experience, great game modes and lots of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite me having most of my hours in GRID 2 of all the GRID games, I undeniably love GRID as a franchise.
