_childDocuments_.review: Bears in space is some combination of Doom, Ratchet & Clank, Borderlands, and the more recent High on Life but doesn’t do any of its influences all that well.Gameplay is very doom/bullet hell inspired and while fun at the start, quickly becomes repetitive and more of a nuisance than anything. Guns and their upgrades are directly influenced by R&C but ultimately feel barebones at best in comparison. It takes forever to get the gun upgrades and with dozens of them it would be a massive time sink to try. Enemies are really generic and most just have a variation on laser ball attack pattern. It’s not the worst gunplay I’ve ever felt but it certainly won’t be bringing you back. Also, I hope you like destroying purple boxes because that is one of the pillars of this game (yet even in this area it feel less satisfying than R&C).Story/characters are…rough. The ultimate main story is a bit of a meme the whole way through and feels extremely disjointed at times. It also drags on for way too long for what it is trying to tell and ends up feeling like a chore that never ends. One level after another that feel repetitive and derivative. The characters while there are a few bright moments, are mostly annoying to listen to and frankly uninteresting. It’s just joke after joke after joke and it devalues them the more the game goes on. This is compounded by the terrible voice acting of the main characters’ partner and various other NPCs you meet along the way. They don’t do a good job of selling the stereotypes they are trying to poke fun at and have a pretty underwhelming delivery. I know this was made by a small team but it doesn’t change the fact that it is still bad.The world levels themselves are varied at least but are again too large, empty, and bland. It feels like you are going through a game still in alpha and most of the visual clutter has yet to be added. Lighting feels really washed out too with a weird low contrast haze look. It’s not fun to look around most of the time and if you don’t care about the little secrets scattered around, would probably prefer to just run through most of it. Those secrets can be fun but most of them are just on the nose 2 second jokes that honestly feel pretty lazy.As for performance it ran fine for me on a 7800x3d and 2080ti but was surprisingly maxing my gpu, odd for a game of this low visual fidelity. There are some major performance dips when a bunch of small enemies are killed in succession. Overall I would most likely give this game a mixed rating if there was one because I can see some people enjoying enough about it but I’m going to err on the side of don’t recommend. It just doesn’t do all that much well and feels like a watered down soup of multiple other games. Maybe pick this up on a deep sale and give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really ever leave reviews but this game was so much fun I feel obligated to.About a week ago I saw a vid about Bears in Space pop up on youtube, part way through that video I saw what was obviously a Chron-o-John, I immediately turned off the video and bought the game and have hardly been able to put it down since. Bears in Space is in many ways the game Serious Sam 2 should have, could have been in a perfect world, and then made it 10x better. At least that's the most direct comparison I can think of for the overall feeling of the game, but there's so much more. The weapons are fun and creative, there's a ton of them and they are really satisfying to upgrade the next version. The rocket launcher is downright amazing it feels perfect. There is a ton of side stuff, secrets, eastereggs, and even some mini games, all of which I really enjoyed and even though there is a lot, it never felt like anything was 'getting in the way' The gameplay is really fun, the enemies are good and there is no 'super annoying one' at all, your character moves and jumps and shoots just right and there is nice variety between the different levels.I loved the story and characters, they are funny without having to rely on being foul or edgy or overly self aware, its just nice solid comedy very much in the style of the classic Lucas Arts adventures, which the game contains several great references to, among many many other things.My biggest fear while playing was that it was going to be too short because I was having so much fun but thankfully it went on just long enough to hit that sweet spot before feeling like anything was dragging on. I will be going through to replay it and find the rest of the secrets, and there are some very nice features to make replaying levels enjoyable: enemy multipliers, weapon upgrades you would probably not have gotten to the first time around (there are a BUNCH of weapons) and of course the secretsThe secret locator item you can buy at the ingame shops on each level gives a little light up beeping when you are close to a secret, enough to be helpful without that feeling of shame that comes from looking one up or getting a hint. Really really really one of the nicest features in a game like this is on the Level Select screen there are different checkpoints you can start the level from and it actually shows which secrets/collectibles are obtainable from that checkpoint on.(Ex: If you are missing Trading Card #5 and you mouse over checkpoint 1 or 2 it will show you can get it from there, but when you mouse over checkpoint 3 the Card #5 will be red, meaning you've gone too far, so if you just need to collect that one you can start at checkpoint 2 to get to it quickly) If I had to find a gripe with something it would be that it uses checkpoints instead of quicksaves, and there are some limitations in backtracking, but it is definitely designed with replayability in mind so thats more of a directional choice than a flaw, and maybe one of the reasons I had so much fun was because I didn't get caught up in quickloading over and over to save myself 1 extra rocket and a little health for the next area.Bears in Space is great, really great, definitely buy it, can't recommend highly enough. It's pure magic and I hope they make more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive how much a small team was able to accomplish.  The scope of what they tried to do is huge, but the level of polish on the final product is low.The game can be boiled down to two things: FPS arena fights, and secrets that mostly take the form of little comedy skits.  Some of the comedy lands, and some of it doesn't.  It's a toothless brand of comedy that aims to be wacky without poking fun at anyone or anything in particular.  There's joy to be had in exploring a level and discovering these details, but that joy is severely tampered by levels filled with invisible walls, and arbitrary one-way gates that prevent you from traveling backwards.  Will going down that path take you to the next secret?  Will it be an invisible wall?  Will it take you to a one-way door that stop you from secret hunting?  It's a gamble every time.The only way to get back to secrets you missed it to replay part of a level, which is a chore, because the shooting isn't very good.  The game features about 15 guns, which is 10 more than it needs, and each arena is an exercise of moving methodically from health pickup to health pickup, clearing out spammy enemies as they tick down your health.There's effort and creativity on display here.  I hope that the team involved keeps at it, learns from what worked and what didn't, and takes on another project of a more manageable scope.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd much prefer to be excited about Bears in Space given the 'small team many years' disclaimer the game starts with, but it is just a passable boomer shooter where secrets in each generically-themed level come with a tangential bit of lukewarm comedy.Bears in Space isn't particularly funny. A lot of the humor stems from short, spontaneous jokes or zany character introductions. When it tries to subvert gaming tropes, the bit is done predictably. Very few of the jokes are diegetic, which misses the unique potential of comedy in an interactive medium. Bears in Space is also very happy with how funny it thinks it is. Comedy is of course subjective, but if you've found yourself wincing at the meta and self-congratulatory humor in Borderlands or High on Life, well, this is the same domain. Bears in Space isn't particularly fun. It's a skeleton of a boomer shooter. There’s a double-jump and air-dash. Melee on 1, pistol on 2, shotgun on 3, SMG on 4, etc. You've played this before. The weapons, even the assortment of barely functional comedy guns, feel slippery and lack impact. The basic guns have crazy bullet-spread problems. Enemy types are generally homogeneous alterations of gumball machines and the smattering of tiny projectiles that fill firefights is visually unappealing and moves unpredictably.Within the narrative of Bears in Space, there isn’t any interesting stakes or build-up or comedic continuity or reason for the things you do. The only recurring characters of significance are the twelve-packs-a-day bear in your head and the merchant. It’s no surprise then that the lack of structure leads to throwaway “well that was something” scenarios that break the pacing of gameplay and sabotage the integrity of the comedy.In the end, the comedy doesn't carry the game well enough to justify putting up with the gameplay and vice versa. Unless the genre's basics are enough to get you going or you're a tuber looking for some easy riffs, Bears in Space isn't worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Another case of too much of a good thing. While it starts off very promising with almost Serious Sam levels of action on screen it will then constantly stop you in your tracks with cutscenes, character interaction, attempts at quirky humor or annoying puzzles.  This could've been a really solid 5 to 6 hour experience but after having played 10 hours with another 5 massive levels remaining filled with constant distractions I'm ready to throw in the towel (I even rushed through the last few levels I played, oof). I can forgive the subpar combat but the nonstop regurgitating of the same comic sans fueled shtick gets old fast and while I understand that I'm just not the target audience for it, life's just too short for me to bother with this any longer... Very disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: For all the love and personality that's baked into Bears In Space, the actual gameplay experience leaves me with two elephants in the room that are keeping me from recommending it. First and foremost, this game is in dire need of optimization. I'm not normally a stickler for performance, but in a genre like FPS, every frame counts and there were several places with a lot going on that made my computer chug. I was often struggling to stream this at 720p on low settings and I don't think it helped that a game of this scope was a 20 GB download. Second, even when things were running smoothly, enemy hordes were often super messy. Between enemy movement and shot volume/spread, it was just too much for me to deal with on normal difficulty. Maybe with some extra tuning, this could be a great game, but for now, as much as I want to praise what's good about it, I'd approach with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: While the basic idea could aappear appealing, it comes out as a budget High on Life.Most of the humour is based around the low-brow mean-spirited absurd nonsense of 2000s Cartoon Netork and Adult Swim productions, including the high reliance on references.Hoiwever, either the jokes drag on too long, or you see them coming a mile away and they take literal minutes to get to a predictable punchline, or worse, they fall absolutely flat, and most references are so on the nose it's actually painful.The cutscenes are unskippable even when replaying levels so you'll be wasting your time re-trudging to the same unfunny gags you already suffered through.Exploration is not encouraged due to a linear level design with tons of invisible walls that make explorable areas confusing and frustrating.Gunplay is extremely middling as none of the guns really feel good, either due to robot hitboxes being too narrow or some guns working in uninituitive ways. The amount of XP needed to level up guns that can is often way too high as well.The Respawn option should have been on by default instead of being a toggleable setting and the customizable difficulty accessible anytime while playing feels like a crutch, just like respawn, to compensate for the design flaws.The characters are either uninteresting or grating, nothing makes sense but in a bad sense.While the retro-futuristic 60s aesthetic is good, too many levels have a dull grey dominante as a base tone which drags down the visuals.All in all, I can't recommend this game in its state. I have no doubt the developers' hearts were in the right place, but the result is a low-brow frustrating mess that drags on terrible jokes and messy gunplay.I don't mind either low-brow humour, references nor absurdity and exotic guns, but here the combined result is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Bang for your buck Boom Shoot goodness with at least 100% more Bears. Bears in Space is a Retro FPS that combines both faced paced FPS gameplay mixed with Bullet Hell qualities and a large humorous tone. Created mostly by 3 people in the Unreal Engine 4, it follows the story of Maxwell Atoms as he's one day from retirement on a boring prison ship until they're attacked and in the chaos fused? with a talkative bear called Beartana or BT for short. From there they go on a absolute wacky, robot slaying, adventure all across over the place on a quest to get back to Earth. It's such a nothing plot but has so much rich heart and humor that you're just happy to be on the ride to see what's next! Gameplay of Bears in Space follows a more linear style with having arenas for combat and platforming and miscellaneous segments between the arenas. The shooting is pretty solid a good variety of enemies with various attack patterns, movement options, and a absolutely absurd amount of weapons. Like there's so many weapons that you need 2 weapon wheels to even see all of them. They range form the workforce FPS weapons like Shotguns, and Rocket Launchers, to novelty weapons like a Anvil and Rubberband launcher, a almost useless Carp Spraybottle, and Basketcube Launchers to name a few. The amazing part, is that all of these weapons are useful in one way or another. While yes, the sheer amount does mean the game has a large weapons bloat, I think it does a decent job separating the workforce and novelty weapons. Like for example the Gamma Launcher which is basically your rocket launcher is more useful but the Tri-Shoot can be a replacement if you run out of ammo. As going the sheer variety of robots is insane even by Episode 3 you're still getting introduced to new robots that have different attack patterns along with the earlier ones. Futhermore all of these weapons are upgradeable, which are tracked by getting kills with each respective weapon that has a upgrade tree unless stated otherwise. While the upgrades are nice to make your early game weapons still useful, the grind to get them can be a bit long such as the one for the pistol.Now the level design is one so notable it needs more elaboration. As stated earlier Bears in Space's levels for the most part are mostly linear hallways connected to arenas or set pieces with secrets spread out inbetween with a handful of exceptions. The difference of this compared to what you normally hear when a Retro FPS has linear level is the absolute sheer length of these levels. With few exceptions most of the levels can take 20+ minutes to beat and they're typically stuffed will with combat encounters, moments featuring humor, variety or both, or just normal secrets. Throughout these levels are a currency known as Vicbucks which you spend at Vic's. A robot who is more than glad to sell you new weapons, along with things like health, armor, and ammo refills as well as a really useful secret detector. You're also given a handful of Tool "Weapons" which effect either your movement options or affect the environment during platforming segments inbetween fights. It's a notable enough mechanic that you even have a weapon wheel for it. As for all the side modes to provide variety, they often take the form of idea adjacent to FPS gameplay, like becoming a Light Gun shooter, Basketball, or other minigames in the FPS style. Otherwise it's either themed arenas or simply jokes. It's a amazing blend that also helps that the humor is pretty consistent. Often making jokes at FPS game tropes, general pop culture references, and just humor that rarely becomes annoying through a full playthrough. There are also Trading Cards hidden around like these humorous secrets but they kinda are just there as a collectable rather than being something interesting. As the story is really just an excuse to go on this wacky adventure, I'd rather take a look at the style. As Bears in Space has a wonderful Retro Spaceage-like style. From the colorful environments, to the design of the robots and weapons, the game absolutely nails it's visual style. Even for me who had to roll back on some of the fancier effects for performance the game still looks and runs mostly great!  This is even more notable with how big the game is. As assets are reused very rarely, and when reused are often for a specific callback to a joke or fitting within a different level's theme. It can be jank at times but still consider that all of this was mostly made by just 3 people. The music also really well done, having a variety of themes for each level as well as music made during combat to really amp things up. Overall, Bears in Space is an incredibly unique FPS game that's stuffed full with content. You can easily get around roughly 15~ hours on a normal playthrough and it's not that particularly hard to get 100% so you could easily get up to 20+. Really the most annoying parts about 100% is that, due to the way the levels are constructed, you have to rely on specific checkpoints when revisiting levels. Which can be tedious if you have a secret that's hidden between these warps. As other than general grind-ness for two other achievements, I'd highly recommend going for that 100% as you'll get to see everything the game has to offer. As a whole it's a great game that's easily worth the full price of 20$ for how much content you get, that is something I cannot say often for most games!

_childDocuments_.review: Do not be fooled by the game's presentation.It's "DOOM in stupid" with tons of side events to shake things up.Enemies can (and will) destroy you by flooding the entire combat area with bullets and explosions.It is genuinely challenging on medium difficulty.As for the jokes, humor is obviously subjective.Most of them didn't land for me, but moments like "We got ourselves a little security" and then showing a tiny bouncer did get a chuckle out of me. It's dumb, it's on-the-nose, and the game knows it. My only gripe is the projectile-based combat. It takes quite a bit of time for your bullets to actually reach the enemy. And they move around a lot. It feels like more than half your shots end up missing because of it, making for a very unsatisfying experience. I highly recommend enabling a small amount of aim assist in the options menu to give each bullet a little bit of "magnetism" (yes, even if you're using a mouse). It makes a world of a difference.Like so many other games, it's seems impossible to get a solid 120+ fps out of this one (usually an engine/optimization issue).Once things start exploding, it can drop all the way down to the 60s.Therefore, I have to lock the game to 60 and use frame generation software to at least have it look like a 120 fps game.If you're a 60 fps person, this does not concern you.

_childDocuments_.review: If the devs are reading this, just want to add that I was blown away by how good the writing is, it's truly great comedy. My advice would be to understand why all these reviews liked Bears in Space more than High on Life and build on that (keep doing what you're doing, and embrace/widen the gap between the competitors)When I played High on Life a couple months ago the jokes were a bit too edgy and crass in that game. I would often get annoyed by the humour in High on Life, or cringe at it, or both. Bears in Space is a lot more modest with it's jokes in a smarter way, even if the jokes themselves are really silly and goofy fun. To put it into perspective, Bears in Space has a wide range of humour but it particularly has more old-fashioned 90's/00's type of humour (think Leslie Nielsen's parody movies like Airplane/Scary Movie) relative to high on life being strictly more ultra-contemporary (rick and morty, etc.). I think Bears in Space will age a lot better because of that alone. Bears in Space had me actually laughing out loud more times then I can count. My only 1 single negative/criticism is that the game was too long (22hrs, could have been 30 on higher difficulty setting and exploring more). It's great value for money, but the issue is that it certainly risked the humour getting dry and old. Some jokes/sequences were repeated a few too many times. Personally, I didn't mind, I actually thought it was funny to see the repetition, but I could see how others may have grown a little tired of it. Putting the humour aside, the gameplay also got a little tiring- not a lot, just a little! But a small part of me was glad the game was over when it finished, the robots and gun noises and all the ADHD chaos just gets physically tiring. Short and sweet is a virtue in game design in general, and in comedy too. The gameplay itself is still very fun and relaxing to play in general though. Despite complaining about the game length, the devs did such a great job at adding in new guns, gameplay, new mini games, it really was phenomenal and I have huge respect for them. It's a solid 9.5/10, a genuine GOTY contender for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Let the records show I almost never write reviews for games. While that probably doesn't really hold any weight to you I hope it at least communicates that I was impressed with Bears in Space. I don't think I've ever played a game from such a small study with so much heart and polish, and I honestly think it will be a difficult challenge for it to be knocked out of my top 5 games of the year. THE STORY:BIS's most standout characteristic is its incredibly funny and smart writing. Almost every cutscene and joke brought a smile to my face and several even made me laugh out loud and had me thinking about them even when I wasn't playing the game... at least the first time I saw them (I will elaborate later). The over arching story doesn't really matter, which is brought up several times, because BiS is really about enjoying the moment. Its story is kind of a sketch, comedy game  filled with tons of pop culture references both recent and older. Every secret is more or less just a bit that rewards you with Vic bucks to upgrade weapons, but most of them are very creative and some have ridiculous amounts of efforts put into them. BiS is absurdist humor, think Dear Sister or Aunty Donna, at its peak.GAMEPLAY:BiS is a very competent modern, boomer shooter/Bullet Hell most of the time. You have a double jump and dash and enemies all fire large amounts of projectiles in unique patterns. BiS features a VERY large enemy roster, and it truly astounds me how every one manages to be unique and many use the bullet hell formula in very fun and creative ways especially the late game ones. These projectiles also deals large amounts of damage. I played on the highest difficulty and it is possible to get mowed down from Max health and shields to dead in a couple seconds. That being said health is pretty abundant the difficult is staying alive to get to the health. However, to be honest I'm no shooter god, and I probably averaged only 2-3 death every level (which are usually about an hour in length). To combat the large enemy roster you have a similarly large arsenal, 25 guns and several grenade types, and many of the weapons can be significantly upgraded by getting kills with them. Are all of the weapons good? No. A few of them are gag weapons that do at worst decent damage, but they all have their own fun or interesting quirks, and I enjoyed switching to at least one of them in every fight or so. Completing secrets and destroying boxes around the map will give you money to buy weapons, ammo, armor, etc. You may have noticed I said BiS is only a shooter most of the time. Several of the secrets and gameplay sections will totally shake up the gameplay style changing to be like Mike Tyson's Punch-Out, Galaga, House of the Dead and more. As I said early it truly astounds me how much work and love this small team was able to put into this game.THE BAD:I think BiS really only has one flaw, which I hinted at earlier, and that is seemingly padding out its run time when it is already a decently long game. The smallest way this is apparent is in the number of kills required to uipgrade guns. The main arsenal takes around 1,500-2,000 kills with each weapon to fully level them. While there are a lot of enemies in the game, there is not nearly enough to upgrade them all in a single playthrough if you're are also working on your special arsenal. This is especially frustrating, because if you die the kills from your previous life are not saved. Even if the weapon upgrades in a fight it will revert back if you die. This seems to me to be an intentional choice, because there are certain things like secrets that will save progress when you die. Now to combat this you can go back and replay level with your current arsenal to get any secrets you missed and grind kills. However, this brings me to the MOST egregious example of padding playtime. Cutscenes are mostly unskippable. You can slowly "skip" some of the dialogue in most cutscenes, line by line, but it is not uncommon for them to have entirely unskippable segments.  If you replay a level you will have to watch these each time. To make it even worse checkpoints are almost always BEFORE them, so if you die you will have to watch them again. Checkpoints are also often far-ish apart meaning you can actually have to watch two or three cutscenes again if you die. The absolute worst example of this in my playthrough was a cutscene where a guard walks a ridiculously long distance to set off the alarm. I died in the fight after it 2 times, so I had to watch that guard walk the ridiculously long distance 3 times, and let me tell you the first time it was pretty funny, the second wasn't funny and the third was very annoying. Broadside if for some reason you're reading this, please for the love of Vic at the very least just put the checkpoints at the start of fights.FINAL THOUGHTS:Like I said I absolutely think Bears in Space is worth anyone's time, but I think it's probably best played just to enjoy the ride. Play on the normal or easy difficulty, and don't sweat trying to get every collectible and secret your first time. That is the exact opposite of how I usually play games, but I still loved my time and after taking a break I truly look forward to coming back to finish up what I missed. The game was clearly made with an unbelievable amount of heart from a small, team that is made of truly talented writers and game designers. I genuinely can't wait for what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: People are absolutely sleeping on this one. I have not beaten the game as of writing, but I have played to the "Carnival" level, which seems to be at least halfway to completion by my best guess.To start, the humor is not for everyone, its not edgy, but clever about how dumb its being like something out of "The Naked Gun" or "Airplane!" with alot of sight gags and reference humor. It is far more subdued with how often they crack jokes compared to something like "High on Life" where they would throw 30 jokes at you a minute with like 1-5 of them landing. Its dumb in a tasteful way for lack of a better term, though if you don't like getting riffed at by a bear woman who sounds like she smoked 40 packs a day since conception, maybe turn the voice slider down.That being said, the gameplay is fantastic. Movement is fast and responsive, and the level design encourages a lot of platforming and out maneuvering your foes who are primarily various types of robots. They all gib satisfyingly into multiple pieces upon death, spilling oil and bolts everywhere. I've encountered about 8 enemy types so far (not including bosses) and the only one I actively dislike fighting are the small ankle biter robots who come at you in swarms (They're very fast, but you can outrun them).Now where this game shines is in the weapon variety, level design, and quality of life features that encourage replayability. Maybe I'm misreading inspiration here, but Bears in Space seems heavily influenced by the older Ratchet & Clank titles. You're given access to a staggering amount of weapons. I'm talikng 20+ unique firearms, melee weapons, and throwables, and not a one feels out of place. Every weapon ends up being useful in different situations, however there is at least one weapon that seems like it was placed there as a joke. Also a legally distinct Unreal Flak Cannon is in there. That is the only one I'm gonna spoil, because they are all a treat to discover. Continuing with the Ratchet & Clank comparisons, 90% of your arsenal has an experience bar that fills on kills. When filled, your weapon evolves. These evolutions are all accompanied by a physical change to the model, as well as an additional firing mode or enhanced weapon statistics (Damage, rate of fire, projectile size). The last 10% of weapons do not upgrade, but are usually found in secret areas on levels and can be missable.Missable weapons are not too big of a deal to me simply because this game has several quality of life functions that make hunting for secrets painless. Your overall character, his arsenal, and any relevant gadgets for level traversal you find are ALL saved to your profile, and level select is unlocked from the very start of the game. This effectively acts as a New Game Plus mode that is always on. You could play for 10 hours, decide to start over from a level of your choice, and keep your entire progress. That includes Arsenal, upgrades, and level traversal gadgets. It's such a breath of fresh air from having to redo an entire game just to get to a fight you wanted to replay with your new toys.And the levels are all fantastic, 20 minutes long at minimum with tons of side objectives and secrets that actually give you permanent additions to your character. It doesn't go as far as Ratchet & Clank did with how expansive the side paths are, but often you'll often leave the critical path to find a mini level of its own off to the side. This is also where most of the reference humor tends to be.I don't want this to get too much longer, so I'll end with this. This game feels like a true labor of love. A shooter with the speed and precision of modern standards, harboring the soul of a game from the mid 2000's. It's fast, fluid, clever, and well designed. A hidden gem that shines so bright, I'm floored that it doesn't have 10x the amount of reviews it currently does. Broadside Games has crafted something truly special here, and I wish them nothing but success in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Superb and hilarious game. Writing and game design (e.g., the anvil launcher) that actually has me laughing. An excellent game that I've been thoroughly enjoying. I'm only 3ish hours in and I know I've missed a bunch of stuff in terms of secrets, already want to replay the game and find out where I missed things. Highly recommend! 10/10UPDATE: 10 hours later I'm still loving this game. I think the only thing I'd like to see is a slight economy edit: maybe enemies should drop very small amounts of v-bucks on death. Just a thought. I'm finding myself completely shocked by the sheer breadth of material in this game. It's massive and full of unique 1-off moments that aren't copy pasted. Like they just made special and specific assets for this ONE scene, and that happens over and over. It's wildly impressive, especially after playing a lot of shooters (e.g., High On Life, Halo Infinite, etc.) where the reused assets make one-off moments impossible. The wig system for enemies is endlessly engaging and funny. Movement (in air and on the ground) is especially enjoyable. Scripting and scenes are fantastic. I've only run into one bug so far (when battling a special character in a hidden underground temple, after beating that character it wouldn't move to a specific area to let me progress) and it only set me back 3 minutes. It has superb pacing and even better writing. It's so absurd. I also really appreciate how you're the bad guy here. I think a worse game would try and have a redemption or moral moment for your characters, and although this game does introduce those moments it insists on subverting them and ridiculing the attempt at a moral turn for our characters. I am very impressed at this because I find it's really rare in any game (whether from this decade or the one before it). So often we're fed this stuff that wants us to take it absolutely seriously and only to laugh at brief moments of poorly written jokes. Bears In Space takes a very clear and firm stance AGAINST such seriousness. It is very much, through and through a game that exclusively is dedicated to having fun and NOT being taken seriously. I think some people will find it difficult to get into because of this, and I had to adapt myself as well. There were scenes where moral choices are given to the character and I was always actually thinking about what the "right" (i.e., moral) option was. Eventually I remembered that the game IS a joke, that taking these moments seriously actually detracted from them. I was constantly reminded that regardless of MY inclination as a player, the game itself was made with the express intention to make you laugh and as real (actually real) escapism from the seriousness of life, other games, etc. Only in the absurdist realm can we actually have a real escapist moment, where you can seriously forget and move past your daily foibles. This might be taking the game too seriously, but I really want to impress how impressed I am with it. It's a fantastic achievement in writing and expression that does what it sets out to do. It never feels hollow or corporate, and while not every joke lands a surprisingly large number of them do actually make me laugh. It's not highbrow, if it tried to be it'd be going against itself. It's an achievement insofar as it goes through with what it wants to be, it succeeds at doing literally one thing. And this achievement, in my opinion, is as phenomenal in its craft as other games where narrative achievements have been accomplished. In a very real sense RDR2 and other narrative games (Umurangi Generation, Disco Elysium, etc.) that succeed in crafting actual stories (and not just merely being bogged down in surface level politics, and this isn't to say that deep and gripping political narratives aren't also craft--only that there is a dreadfully large body of literature which fails in every way to get past a merely shallow political critique) are simply the other side of this coin. We need to support games that know how to write, we need to support good art. And although you may not be in the mood for a deeply comic experience, you should be able to recognize that it is, through and through, an achievement for these developers to have made. I cannot recommend it enough, it's quite literally a breath of fresh air to engage with.

_childDocuments_.review: At a glance or in screenshots, Bears in Space comes across as a cartoon-y pseudo-boomer shooter, employing that love-it-or-leave-it style of bullet-hell projectiles and breakneck speeds. I personally find these to be precisely my cup of tea, but I will also be the first to admit that it’s a niche genre that is quick to alienate some players. You need a strong hook to draw people in, and Bears’ hook has the weight of the ursine behind it. And it’s a roar-some good time.Pulling one hell of a juggling act between FPS, platforming, and brawling mechanics, Bears also throws in a comedic tone that permeates every part of the game – jokes and references come at a rapid pace, lurking behind every corner and often waiting out in the open to be discovered. Where some games opt to add a splash of humour for a lighthearted experience, your time in Bears will be spent submerged in the funny juices, with set pieces and characters all playing their part to cook up punchlines of all kinds. In the quiet moments between gun battles, you are free to poke around the massive environments seeking riches – but the real money makers are in-game challenges that quite often involve some kind of micro-skit of silliness.At one point as I leapt nimbly from platform to platform, I noticed a rock plateau within jumping distance. I landed and was greeted by a robot wearing a tank top who lived his life one quarter micron at a time. He explained we were racing for slips, the first to return from DEATH MOUNTAIN will be the winner – and the winner takes all. I climbed into my vehicle, and the clock ticked down. The race started, and my opponent immediately blasted into a rock face like a missile, spectacularly exploding and leaving me to awkwardly putter around death mountain and back to the starting grid. I exited my vehicle and was greeted by a robot in a stunning wig, who happened to be the wife of the apparently deceased ‘Vince’. She was looking for him, and sincerely hoped he wasn’t somewhere living his life one quarter micron at a time. I didn’t have the heart to tell her, so I quietly collected my prize money and slunk off.This is a precarious path to tread, given that such a care-free approach to the game and its narrative could leave it feeling disjointed and disconnected – but the re-use of characters and consistent callbacks all get channeled through our protagonists, Maxwell Atoms and the space-bear Beartana, to keep everything familiar and comfortable. To be clear, the narrative ticks exactly as many boxes as it needs to, introducing our titular heroes and providing their motivation, but that is where the heavy lifting really ends. This is a tale about problems, and how liberally applying bullets and bear paws can solve them, not life-changing lessons.The game also revels in traversal and platforming options, with a familiar standard of hovering platforms and precarious falls. Some of these will move, others might only be active for a short period of time, others will predictably fall after a period of time. With a double jump AND an air dash under your belt, getting around these is a fun time – but the developers at Broadside have been mindful to those that might not vibe with their time in the air up there. Implementing a unique difficulty option to actually opt-out of the challenging aspect of nimbly leaping around, additional platforms and surfaces will become available in the game world to reduce the gravity-borne anxiety. It’s a truly unique addition, and well worth seeing mainstream adoption for games moving forward. It means that all of the playspaces within the game are carefully curated to any who wish to inhabit them.Many of the more arena-like spaces would look right at home in classic titles like Unreal Tournament or Quake 3 Arena, the clear inspiration put on display for any who remember the thrill of blasting across a battlefield via jump pad and raining hot death on whatever mook still had their feet planted on the floor. Even with the cartoonified proportions and style is unmistakable – and magnificent. This is similarly echoed in the run ’n’ gun sections of the game – though the inspiration clearly switches gears to feel more like Serious Sam – with your way forward now a stellar lightshow of ballistic orbs and rushing enemies. Pushing forward feels like running headlong into a garden hose set to JET (every bit as fun as those summer days as a kid), the deft understanding of what made old school titles fun beautifully captured and remade in Bear’s own image.When the game does throw down the gauntlet, you’ll often find yourself leaning forward in your chair to increase your power level. Bosses in the game follow the same formula of creating a swarm of bullets to dodge and hazards to leap over, but they have the added dynamic of a unique arena that comes with special gimmicks to utilise. In these spaces you will often leverage your latest gadget to impact the fight, giving your considerable firepower a short pause to massage your grey matter, solving a miniature puzzle to gain the upper hand.While Bears doesn’t take itself super seriously, it still has an immense amount of self respect. It would be incredibly easy for a developer to write off any real care for mechanics or pacing, leaning heavily on the immense supply of gags and skits (or memes, as the youth would say nowadays) to have the end product just get slapped with a label of MEME GAME and see some middling success as YouTuber content bait. This game has a funny Fast and the Furious Easter Egg! Johnny Knoxville is a robot in this indie game! The thumbnails make themselves. But the brains behind Bears have taken careful consideration to ensure that the title exists as a sum of many unique parts to make a glorious whole, while also working to make it brilliantly accessible to anyone. There is a sincerity behind the game that is commendable, and deserves recognition.Broadside Games’ Bears In Space is an anomaly in the sense that it is like many things, but there is really nothing that is truly like it. As a first-person shooter, it is a chimera that gleefully gobbles up facets of so many other classic games – not just shooters – to create a girthy gameplay experience that can change at a moment’s notice to deliver something completely out of leftfield without giving the player mechanical whiplash. Yes, a moment ago you were casually shooting robots – but this is the Virtua Cop-esque shooting section. And a little later we will do the fishing minigame, okay? On paper it would read like the scribblings of a madman, but in execution it all ties together beautifully into a medley of frenetic fun.

name: Children of the Sun
detailed_description: Burning with anger, THE GIRL wages a one-woman war against THE CULT, taking them down cultist by cultist, bullet by bullet, until she reaches her true target: THE LEADER. Along the way she will unravel the dark truth about this mysterious order and the atrocities committed by them in the name of their master. In this tactical third-person puzzle-shooter you assume control of one bullet, guiding it through increasingly complex and challenging levels to kill cultists, trigger traps, and reshape the environment. Every shot counts and ruthless precision is rewarded. Taking down THE CULT is deeply satisfying; doing it with style even more so. PLAN YOUR APPROACH Tactical sniping, puzzle solving, and light stealth collide in Children of the Sun to create a third-person shooter like no other. You only have a single bullet to complete each level, but you can re-aim on impact, curve around obstacles, accelerate to break through armor, and more to really make that one crucial shot count. RITUAL MURDER Lose yourself in a dark, twisted tale of revenge as you hunt down the nefarious CULT. Children of the Sun accompanies its unique one-bullet action with an evocative, mystery-filled storyline that unravels as you exact your revenge on the people who made your life hell and relentlessly pursue the enigmatic LEADER. KILL, KILL, AND KILL AGAIN Children of the Sun is lethally replayable by design. There are multiple solutions to each level, encouraging creativity and experimentation, with a satisfying scoring system that rewards accuracy and efficiency. Then, you can check the online leaderboards to see how you stack up against your friends and the rest of the world.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those rare instances where, while short, Children of the Sun feels like the perfect length for what it is. It isn't so short that I felt I didn't get anything out of it, and it isn't so long that I started to get tired of its base mechanic. Really knows when and where it should be freshening things up too. If you're cool with getting 3-4 hours out of it, this is totally worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, we have another Devolver Banger here.How do these kids today say? This Game is a mood. This Game is a vibe.So, what is Children of the Sun?It is basically a puzzle Game, simple as that. A very, very short one at that (I will get to that later).When you mix in the Vibes of the Movie "Mandy" with the Slowmotion Sniper Cam of Games like Sniper/Sniper Elite, put in a little Visual Style of Killer 7 and the Bullet Curving Mechanic of Games like Singularity/Bulletstorm/etc. you get Children of the Sun.I won't discuss story here, because it is basically just a backdrop. It's setting the tone. Has that Cult-Revenge-Movie-Type feel to it.Story is told without Voiceacting but in stylish animated Comic-like sequences that look pretty good.The violence in those Cutscenes is just another moodsetter.Regarding the "Music" I have mixed feelings. It is just droning and a little experimental, just a tiny bit of guitar and drums and doesn't have that many tracks.Don't get me wrong, for the mood this Game wants to convey, it is pretty decent, but I wished there was more.What do you do in Children of the Sun? You position yourself (the Game can be played with just one hand, only the mouse, which is pretty chill), mark some enemies, shoot a single bullet and eliminate every enemy whilst curving, speeding and directing your bullet through the level.You are the bullet as soon as you shoot. And you try to get a good score. That's it! This is the Game.Steam said it took me ~3.5 hours. And thus I arrive at my "criticism". But it's not really that. On one hand, the Game doesn't overstay it's welcome. For Achievement and Leaderboard Hunters, there is replay value though. But on the other hand, it really is way too short for 15€.Before you start flaming me regarding the topic of value in Games, I know, this is probably just one movie in the cinema and I got my moneys worth. But it is hard comparing this to so many other Games on the market that offer the same and sometimes way more value for way less.It's not like I got poor buying this, 15€ is not that much. But also it kinda is.To be honest, I am not even quite sure on how I feel about the value for money thing here. Also I don't want to start a discourse. Still, this is a fun little Game. Also you can shoot dudes in the d***.Short Game, short review, cu...

_childDocuments_.review: I randomly saw Children of the Sun in the store and impulsively bought it to test it out, and I really had a lot of fun with the game! It's a short 3-4 hour experience that really does everything with the rather simple concept it's presenting, and each level has a new unique idea behind it, which I really enjoyed.In Children of the Sun, you play as a sniper trying to eradicate a cult with just one  bullet per level. This starts rather simple but the game adds complexity to how you can control the bullet over time, so that it becomes a fast-paced puzzle where you have to take into account which enemies to target in which order and how to reach the next one from each enemy you hit, without there only being only one solution to each level.For me, this game really felt like something you could 'master' and improve your understanding in and it's a lot of fun and you feel very cool doing it the whole time. There are ranked boards per level for people who want to improve their scores, and a short story that gives the game a clearer direction, which I found intriguing enough to keep me playing, but wasn't too drawn out, which I honestly really appreciated.What really stands out about Children of the Sun is the vibe. The music, sound effects, VFX, animations, color schemes, fonts and other visual elements create such a fun, distinctive style that makes the game ten times more engaging than it already is. It's really *such* a blast to play through the levels.There isn't that much negative to say about the game - I occasionally found actually *finding* the enemies in a level a bit annoying; I wished the game would have been a tiny bit longer, maybe with some less complex and intense levels in between the last levels; and if you are prone to motion sickness this game is probably going to be very bad for you; but that is about it in terms of issues I had with the game.One thing I really liked is that the tougher enemies that the game introduces aren't just harder to kill for the sake of making the game harder to beat, they actually change how you have to think about the level and where to move your bullet to, and for me, they added more fun and didn't feel frustrating to beat which is a first for me because I usually think it's really annoying if an enemy has an amor set or a shield, just so that it takes longer to beat them.Children of the Sun isn't really the type of genre I am usually into, so for me personally it probably won't be a game that I would list along my favourite games, or anything like that, but it's still one I had a lot of fun with, and one I would absolutely recommend other people to also play!

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll admit that the other user reviews I’ve seen here sum this game up better than I can, but I still wanted to throw a positive recommendation into the pile. Yeah, it’s the love child of Sniper Elite and SUPERHOT that was forced against its will to watch Mandy maybe a few years too early. I mean that as a compliment, this game’s insane.You play an unnamed girl avenging the murder of her father from a psychotic cult leader by, mild spoilers here,  The final mission is an interesting challenge, but most people will probably see the end credits in 4 hours or less, and in my experience that was while doing the challenges on the first go. If you don’t mind a short but very sweet puzzle shooter that also looks like a lost horror game from the 90’s, then give Children of the Sun a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely nails the grindhouse aesthetic and story even if the storytelling is very fast paced with blink-and-miss glimpses of flashbacks to understand Girl's motivation to kill a cult leader. The story ending has a nice dark twist, and in general was reminiscent of Midsommar at times. The sniper puzzle shooting is very satisfying when you figure out the solution, and has great audiovisual feedback. It's very accessible too, just needing the mouse as you move from left to right on a plane to deliver the killing shot that will dart from target to target, and you can leverage blowing up the gas caps on cars or birds in the sky to get better positions. The progression in enemy types pairs well with the abilities you develop like slow-mo, redirecting your bullet, and kaleidoscopic weak spots on enemies. A nice feature is once you've tagged the enemies, their positions stay even if you fail, which means you're not wasting time and can focus on optimising the route for your bullet. Overall, there's a certain dark and vengeful mood this hits along with the killer girl grindhouse aesthetic that makes for an engaging sniper puzzle shooter that doesn't lose steam by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet and not at all what the negative reviews seem to think it is?This game is great, and coming from someone who typically *hates* puzzle games, this is so, so far from random chance lol. Trial and error, sure, but not to the point of frustration? Apologies if this tickles anyone the wrong way but you have to be really really forcing yourself to do something a single way to be stuck on any level other than the final few for more than 20 minutes. Doing the challenges is another story but that is supposed to be more complicated, the main game itself is very enjoyable, straightforward and interesting. I'm always a fan of games that full send on one weird, niche concept and thats definitely what happened here. I would say getting this for under like 10 bucks is worthwhile, thats 2 beers out at a bar in todays economy and you can just play this game with a six pack in the fridge for a little bit more money and a lot less awkward exchanges with strangers. I appreciate the art and despite some jank to some of the animations the style is just oozing off of every corner of this game. Mechanically I really liked how it did feel like it was going further and further to push you to use all the mechanics at your disposal, there was quite a few times where I had the "let me cook" going in my head for a stupid strategy that ended up being not so stupid. Chaining headshots and getting enough distance to penetrate armor or angling it just right to bounce off certain things is very satisfying. Its a very fair thing to say that a game wasn't for you, but reading some of the negative reviews (aside from the one that had issues with flashing lights, which, fair) really just came across like all those Elden Ring DLC reviews. "The game didn't roll over for me and actually made me try/think a bit, 0/10" like get out of here lol. The people complaining that you "cant find any of the enemies" have to be blind because I AM colorblind and still found the enemies fairly easily on my first go of each level. At most you had to reset once but if you mark them with the middle mouse button they stay marked on further attempts, so I really don't know what the complaint was. Sorry the puzzle game didn't bend over and let you first time every level?If you want a unique, brief experience that does its best to really go above and beyond on the style while maintaining quality of the substance, Children of the Sun is a great time. If this seems interesting to you, pick it up and try it and just keep an eye on the refund window to see if you want to hang onto it and go for all the challenges and whatnot. I had a good time, and assuming you arent a whiny baby, you probably will too!

_childDocuments_.review: A visually arresting sniper/puzzle game where you telekinetically control a single bullet that you use to kill members of the cult you escaped from. Every time you hit an enemy, you can redirect the bullet from that point, so it's initially all about figuring out the order to kill them so that you can continue to play connect the dots with your targets, but it eventually layers on more powers for you and more challenges to overcome in enemy types. It's so aggressively styled in every aspect of it, from the eerily colorful visuals to the unsettling soundscape to the frankly kind of edgelord story beats (the game was originally pitched as "I Just Killed a Man and Now I'm Horny" so that can kind of give you the vibe it's going for). It's all so singular and of a piece that it just feels like a such a complete package. I beat it in 3.5 hours, and it felt like they got about all they could out of the mechanics presented. Some of the puzzles were thrilling, requiring quite a bit of timing and precision to pull off.It's definitely not for everyone (stylistically, thematically, or gameplaywise), but I loved it. Laser focused in every aspect to communicate a ver specific vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty unique one-shot sniper game that has you hitting multiple targets by turning the bullet and slowing down time or aiming in specific ways to get all targets with one bullet. The color palette and story telling is also interesting. Sometimes it's a bit finicky to control the bullet and hit edge cases, but generally it's straightforward. Also the last level is a bit of a difficulty spike, but overall this one is short and sweet.

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie this game had me raging for a bit, but not to the fault of the game but the one mistake I kept making. The mechanics in this game are very simple but so well put together. The game is very concise and fairly short but allows you to replay the levels to increase your score toward the leaderboard. The story says a lot about the plot of the game without ever saying anything and it works to ground what type of world the main protagonist must suffer through to bring justice. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. It's short and to the point. You're out for revenge and you have the power to control the direction of your bullet as if flies through the air to take down your targets one by one as you track down the leader of a cult. It's fairly short and easy to finish in only a few hours and get all achievements in.As you go through the levels some enemies will start wearing body armor and others using strange powers to block your bullets unless you hit them in the right manner. Most of the challenge I'd say comes from just trying to find every enemy you need to kill in each level. Thankfully you can mark them once you find them so you can know their positions the next time you try.The only downsides I'd say it once you finish it once you don't really have much of a reason to play it again unless you wish to try to increase your high score in each level to rank up on the leader boards but sadly the people at the tops of those leader boards have such massive numbers that I'm guessing they somehow cheated. But maybe I'm wrong, I don't know.But still it's a pretty fun and decent game that doesn't over stay its welcome.Would recommend buying whenever it's discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot really cool aspects that make for a really unique experience.  Attributed to the story, it come off as intense or heavy but in actuality, its a really nice and chill puzzle game with that dopamine hit you get from sniper play. This can be work friendly game because it is fundamentally a casual puzzler you can play on mute BUT to really get you money's worth, I think you wanna play with sound.  Not that the music is good or anything, it's just that sound really adds to the experience. Its fun that the game changes things up by adding pac-man, fishing, and car chaser mini games.  Surprising and fun for a game that feels really linear. It's also super stylish, with retro PS2 graphics.  Something about the cut scenes really remind me of twisted metal 2's which is really enjoyable and keeps you looking forward to them.The cult story is fun...and very adult... but its non-linear reveal keeps you engaged. BTW fun story: there was a family that lived across the street from me growing up that had been part of a cult.  The father had to chase down the cult in Europe and rescue his 1st wife and her/their(?) son.  He was successful in the rescue and they all lived in this house...with a new wife.  Looking back at it, musta been a weird situation... cause you know the dual wife thing... and I don't know if that was his biological son... cause you know, the whole cult thing.  BUT he was cool and we were BFFs.

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is the most violently fun connect-the-dots game I've played so far. The controls for the game feel great and precise, and the levels are well-designed and thought out, making for interesting gameplay. The story is kind of take it or leave it and kind of irrelevant, but it's present enough, I guess.My main gripe with the game is that, even though in the trailer there's an amazing song playing, the game pretty much has no OST. For a game whose art style leans heavily on the more artistic side over quality, simply not having any music really breaks away from the mood. When I compare this game to Hotline Miami or Katana Zero, not having any form of OST or even the song from the trailer present just feels lackluster.I'd still recommend the game but just wish it had music.

_childDocuments_.review: Children Of The Sun mixes super hot and Sniper Elite as you fire as a Sniper and then using your powers you take possession of the bullet itself and guide it towards your targets The core concept evolves during the game as you gain the ability to curve the bullet's trajectory in midair and also increase its velocity, all while enemies adapt to your new found abilities. All of this helps building puzzles that both challenge the player and allow for flexibility.The game bolsters a comic book playstyle as well as a twisted narrative that as you go through the ranks of a cult in the search of their leader, everything controls pretty smoothly as the whole gameplay requires only mouse movements.Targets in vehicles will have you consider timing and armored enemies that require maximum velocity to penetrate demanding that you also manage distance when all these enemy types are in play it becomes quite a challenge to keep all these elements front of mind but never did the puzzles feel unfair.By first marking all enemies and planning through your slaughter, you can build different opportunities to wipe all life from each scene, all ending in a beautifully drawn path that your bullet took.A full playthrough of Children Of The Sun Will run you roughly 4-5 hours but there's room for replayability through pushing your rank on the level specific leaderboards.

_childDocuments_.review: Very stylish game with depressing atmosphere. The psychedelic visuals are complemented by oppressive music and sound design. The story is told by the series of stylized slideshows, showing the main character's past. I love the way the authors decided to explain the main mechanic of the game.The main gameplay is pretty straightforward and engaging. Imagine a rifle with a controllable bullet (like from Singularity or Bulletstorm). This feature is exaggerated by a thousand percent. That's the whole game!As a concept, this sounds very cool and promising, although the gameplay sometimes feels very monotonous.There are a handful of mini games between the main levels, but they feel out of place. I can understand why they are there, but... I don't like them.Anyway, try it out yourself! You won't regret <3

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a bloody puzzle shooter where you have one bullet and more than one enemy to kill, but you have a secret: Jedi girlboss powers. You can redirect the bullet every time you hit someone and even slightly bend its trajectory as you go. The game is pretty short and the puzzles aren't TOO hard but the replay value comes from optimizing your runs and trying to climb the leaderboards.Also, as a lore/story guy at heart, I really liked the way the narrative is delivered. Every few levels you're dealt a short, frantic, cutscene (not in chronological order) that gives you a piece of the puzzle and an insight to The Girl's mental state and why she decided to go on a one-woman rampage against the cult. Good game, very fun, well worth the price IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: The discourse around this game and discoverability has kind of taken away from people talking about how absolutely brilliant it is. Plays like a cross between Superhot, Killer7 and the Nikita missiles from MGS. Vibes absolutely off the charts - neon and shadow painted together across an original, unsettling art style, and grimy, fuzzy audio that put me in mind of a cross between sound design from some of the best modern horror films (Hereditary, Sinister) and Tenderfoot Tactics. Though I'm more interested in the wordless narrative (indirect echoes of Sagebrush), loads here for high score type folks as well. A genuinely fascinating and original game, loads of fun to figure out and execute the levels, and I want to put it on my wall and my stereo. Strong recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the demo enough during Next Fest but unfortunately Children of the Sun proved to be entirely style over substance. What starts off as a neat little sniper puzzler with a Killer 7-esque aesthetic devolves into trial and error, tedium, and wonky hitboxes. In some levels you aren't even able to see every enemy initially so you straight up gotta trial and error it. The later mechanics the games adds feel more like annoying gimmicks and the last level is just an absolute slog and I just gave up because I couldn't find the last damn enemy in all the visual noise and didn't feel like repeating all that ♥♥♥♥ over and over again just to find them. Easy skip and I regret I'm probably past the refund window.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a puzzle game where you play a magic bullet. Every target hit lets you redirect the bullet. At first the puzzle is simply how to thread the needle and navigate the environments, choose the right targets in the right order to complete the puzzle, murdering a bunch of cultists. But soon it starts to introduce new wrinkles, blowing up gas tanks, using birds and fish to help re-direct your bullets, but then you start being able to bend your shots trajectory, or outright change the direction your bullet is being fired mid-shot. It's a really weird but cool puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game with a hella aesthetic, and the supreme feeling when you finally get the path Just Right can't be denied.That said, I often spent more time looking for my targets than trying to set up my pathing -  even with their yellow outfits, they're easily missable, especially with all the also-yellow fires and headlights about the place. It can get frustrating, but not so much that I ever considered giving up.It's a short game, too.In short, it's a game that's probably worth fifteen dollars, but if you were to buy it on sale, it wouldn't be anything to be ashamed of, either.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat real-time puzzler with some tactical flavoring. Equal parts game (mechanics, game play loop, level/mission areas) and art (color palette, soundtrack, impact of visual violence). It's different without being inaccessible and while it starts out very simple, the end is satisfyingly complex. Crucially, it doesn't overstay it's welcome: I spent about 6 hours actually playing, including my achievement hunting. Easy recommend for those who want something different, or maybe something quick (some missions/levels can be finished in as little as one minute). This one definitely hits the mark; thumbs up across the board.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)As a long-time fan of tactical shooting games, I was eager to dive into Children of the Sun, and it did not disappoint. It was my first ever third Person "puzzle" shooter and i really enjoyed it. You can control the path and speed of one single Bullet and Essentially, you need to pause, pivot and plot your single shot to kill every enemy on each level. I honestly dont think its that much replayable but i definetly had a lot of Fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: pros:- unique concept of being able to telekinetically control a sniper bullet to take out entire outposts- gameplay is very tactical and makes you think a lot. which targets you prioritise shooitng at first, which targets to shoot last(so you can always use them to reposition your bullets). where you shoot. for example, you can shoot a guy in the head for some points and more re-aim(a mechanic which lets you reposition the bullet 360 degrees before firing again) chances or you can shoot the car exhaust next to him to even more points and potential multikills if other men are near him. - new enemy additions and mechanics are rolled out at a very steady and comfortable pace. it starts off simple but gets quite deep as the levels progress with armoed enemies you have to powershot, gravitational arc enemies, which sometimes call for the use of the re-aim mechanic to hit, etc. - simple controls- creative levels- ranking leaderboard system gives you something to aim for even if you've already beaten a level. incentivises efficient play.- the game is very fun, which is most important.cons: - poor optimisation. lots of stuttering and it looks very pixelated even on 720p setting.- the story feels disjointed and the snapshot sequences roll by too far for you to even get an idea of what each sequence is about. - at the start of each enemy, you're meant to tag the targets before sniping but due to a combination of the pixelated muddy visuals and how dark the levels are it is extremely hard to make out where each enemy is. - whilst it is beneficial that a ranking system exists, it is only tied to leaderboard positions instead of giving you preset medals/ranks on top of that for each level(like in neon white for example). the medal or level rank system feels more tangible and motivates you to perform better and come back to perfect each level. overall, i think this is a very solid and unique game and the positives far outweight the negatives. i would give this game a 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like it.I love these tactile puzzle games, but I just can't get past the chaotic visual noise and clutter of this one.  I appreciate different/unique styles and I don't mind rough around the edges, but it felt like too much effort was put into being edgy that it just came off as forced, and it ended up being distracting enough that it took away from the actual game.   And this is the one and only game that has made me physically uncomfortable. I'm not normally sensitive, but the flashing visuals combined with the music actually made it an uncomfortable game to play for me. I even tried removing all the blurring etc and gave it another shot, but it still ended up being more style than substance, which wasn't worth the literal headache.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet with a gorgeous art style and super fun gameplay. Story follows a young girls quest for revenge on a cult and its leader for the abuse and suffering they inflicted on her and her family. Story is mostly told in cutscenes accompanied by music with no dialogue and between that and the levels themes you get the idea of whats going on. Each level is like a puzzle and using your one telekinetically directed bullet you chain together targets as efficiently as possible. There is a leaderboard and score for each level giving it some extra replay value especially if you like a little indirect competition like that. Music is good, very atmospheric and there's a grunge-y tone to it which I really liked. Visually the game is gorgeous, like a comic book come alive and the aforementioned cutscenes themselves have a very "high quality, stylized comic book" art feel to em. Excellent game, don't miss out.

_childDocuments_.review: ok this is so good, I wanna explain why but I just like it a lot and I might come back to add more details but I love it so much i was calling the protagonist "똘끼(DDolki)" which means something like insanity in korean and i think it fits her but I love this a lot. I was looking forward to buying this since a few weeks ago and I was so glad to finally get it. I am happy that I don't have to regret it(11/29 KST)(came back to this 12/01 KST) if you expect to see a huge plot twist, or somehow a ‘long enough’ game , you will possibly find this underwhelming. I will just ramble on here but, I first gotta make clear that I’m not bothered by the “short” playtime, and the bullet having its casing. Plus I LOVE girls. I need more silent girl protagonists like Chell from portal 2, or customizable characters from Far cry 5 and New dawn.<narrative>It feels just about right, no unnecessary complexity or dragging. and I would say it is too short if it is missing what's important, which in this case, it doesn't. No surprise I was literally glaring at the credit role to figure out artist's name HAHA I know there are other games that has cultist theme, with so called graff or psychedelic style arts(including Borderlands 3), but this one is remarkable. _childDocuments_.review: Recently, I have become immensely bored of puzzlers and especially of shooters; respectively, both have become stale and boresome, either from personal fatigue or industry trends that prevent us from a little thing called innovation. But in my short time spent with it, I never tired, never bored of whatever the hell  is. Shooting into Devolver's vast, and often unpredictable catalogue enters a stylish vengeance story that feels like some bastard child of  and . And, do I f*ck with it? Absolutely.The short explanation is this, you have been dealt a bad card in life by a bearded hippie, and your vengeful plot is to viciously (very stylishly) murder his hordes of followers with an absurdly beautiful efficiency. But why is that so cool you ask? Because you do it with a single bullet and f*cking telekinesis. You weave through heads like it's a fine art. It's so cool. So rad.  I shouldn't have to explain anything else, buy the bloody game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would summarize this game as "what would happen if Suda51 was asked to make a Sniper Elite style game, but he was just coming off a week-long SUPERHOT bender".Tightly designed, incredibly evocative, and just plain fun to play. The rules start simple enough - you have one bullet that you can re-aim after a legit impact. As the game progresses, you start to get new abilities, alongside increasingly more difficult challenges to overcome, such as body armor or deflective shields. Even though a slight mistake can end an attempt, it has that Hotline Miami/Katana Zero thing where restarting takes no time at all, so you're encouraged to explore and experiment.Definitely worth the full asking price, but if you see it on sale, GRAB IT IMMEDIATELY. This game deserves all the love.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Children of the Sun. I'd consider this more a puzzle game then a sniper game. You are given one "shot" to kill all enemies on the map. As levels go on your gain different ways to interact with your speeding bullet to influence it different ways toward your targets. The concept holds well and the new interactions are great.My only issue is the sound design, a few times it can be very grating on the ears. There is also level "X" which blasts you with sudden flashing colours and I was not ready for that! I feel for $15 if you know what you are getting it's worth it. But I would recommend finding that under $10 deal for a good "I really got my money worth" feel. I did 100% it in 4 hours, but used a guide to help understand each levels clue. If you decide to go in blind, some of those clues may be difficult to figure out and prolong that play time to a fair bit. Don't over look this, it set out to do something and it pulled it off well!

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White: Sniper EliteScout an area, plan how you're going to take out everyone, screw up, improvise, try again, and come up with new ideas for improvement. The core Hitman gameplay loop, boiled down to a 30-second speedrush of you flying a bullet to its destination, paired with the joy of competing with your friends' scores, is the most easy to pick and play pure fun coming out of a sniper rifle I've seen.With a 3-4 hour story mode, and another 1-2 hours to finish up the optional challenges that each level has, it's wonderfully paced and very respectful of your time.
