_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is described as a "puzzle-shooter", but the experience reminds me more of the first phase of infiltrating a base in a stealth-action game. Each level sees you circling around a location, tagging enemies, noting patrol paths, and observing environmental hazards that can be used for extra damage.Once you take the first (and only) shot, Children of the sun reveals its main mechanic - telepathically guiding the bullet.  Sometimes everything will go according to plan, but even if it doesn't, you can often improvise a solution 'mid shot'. This mix of planning, timing, and thinking on the fly is incredibly satisfying.The level design is great throughout. New mechanics are introduced every so often, and each level has a different focus. Some are tight spaces with more obstacles, some are more spread out, some focus on enemy movement, etc. Aesthetically, the levels echo a variety of dingy, real-world locations where one might expect cult members to be hanging out.The presentation is excellent. Art style is exactly what you would expect from a game published by Devolver: lo-fi assets, stylised violence, and surreal environments. The music has a similar vibe, contrasting ambience with noisy bit-crushed drones. The narrative is incredibly brief, consisting only of 15 second cut scenes at the start of each level. They look nice though, and give just enough context to make each level fit into the story. The game is quite short, around 3 hours (probably 5 if you want to complete all the optional challenges). Overall this is a positive as the core mechanic never becomes stale, and the game is well suited to replayability.Levels also have a scoring system (and leader boards) based on factors like time, multi-kills, headshots, distance covered, and number of bullet redirects. Experimenting with unorthodox routes can improve your score, similar to how alternate routes and skips can improve your times in Neon White.Other cool little details:- Footsteps are a 'note' rather than a sound effect, and the pitch increases if you move faster- The main character's head spins as you move the mouse cursor on the level select menu
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: - There's a boatload of style poured into every nook of Children of the Sun that transforms a collection of (mostly) mundane locations into a surreal hypercolor world- Levels primarily take place during dusk, dawn, sunrise, sunset, twilight, or really anytime during the day that the light isn't simply bright or dark. Even when it's not those times, it's often cloudy or raining. Combined with the, shall we say, "aggressive" approach to color saturation, everything seems dreamlike- The screen flashes magenta and red to punctuate every kill, then fades to gray as you take aim again. This color fadeout also occurs whenever you use an ability, making it easier to hone in on the neon orange baddies- The OST is fine, I guess. It's hard to be enthusiastic about ambient drone music. It just sounds like someone falling asleep playing acoustic guitar accompanied by a depressed chainsaw- I did think the little bass kick that coincides with each kill was a neat sound design choice that contributed some additional flair - Children of the Sun is primarily a vibes game, but I'll at least explain the plot setup. The titular murder cult is growing rapidly, turning members into slayers of nonbelievers. Our unnamed protagonist's family is swept into the Children of the Sun, but not long afterwards, her father is killed for an escape attempt. Time for revenge!- Also, she develops psychic powers that let her control bullets like Yondu and his arrow in Guardians of the Galaxy. That's a fairly important detail- That's about it for the story. Some plot details are revealed in animated comic book style vignettes while other lore is dropped in short interstitial levels. These generate the vibes- Those vibes are mostly just unnerving and abrasive. It veers too far in the edgelord direction. The game makes a cringeworthy association between murder and sexual arousal that ruins the mood. A game that lets me be a horror movie slasher for a few hours can be a fun little power trip, but I'm not trying to get weird with it- Choices like that shine a light on the rest of the artistic decisions. Are the visuals so "punk" and the music so impenetrable that it's just trying to be edgy? That choice of Olde English font for the "DEAD" title card that flashes on the screen to end each successful killing spree seems pretty suspect now- In the end, the vibes really just serve to highlight the "killing" half of "revenge killing". At some point it goes beyond punishing those responsible and derails into school shooter territory- But I suppose that if you can stop rolling your eyes at the vibes long enough to concentrate on the gameplay, you'll see a pretty interesting concept. It's a sniper game enhanced by the protagonist's psychokinetic powers- Each level sees you choose a sniper spot by walking either left or right and firing off a single round. Then the real action begins- Assuming you hit your first target, time will slow down as your bullet hovers in the air. You then get to aim again and repeat until everyone's head has been ventilated- You'll occasionally get access to additional stage-locked powers as you progress. Some levels allow you to temporarily slow time in flight to influence your bullet's direction, useful for correcting aim or curving around obstacles. Another sees you Tokyo Drifting your bullet in slow-mo to hit impossible shots through cracked doors or open windows- I'm split on whether I agree this is a puzzle game or not. It's a puzzle in the same way billiards are: you have to sequence properly and think at least one step ahead if you want to get everything in one go. However, you can't see all enemies or shootable environmental objects simultaneously in some levels, so it detracts from the ability to plan out a solution in the way a puzzle would- Let's just say it sits somewhere between pool/snooker and limited FPS with psychic powers- I don't know that I want to replay the game owing to the weird vibes and the fact that I earned all the achievements (which were fun things like situational kills and trick shots). There's a high score system built into the game that rewards things shot economy and low in-level time if you want to compete, but maximizing efficiency sounds like work. I already do that 40+ hours a week- That said, this will be a very short game if you're simply playing through. If you ignore achievements and the scoreboard, you have maybe 4 hours of content awaiting you- I found myself liking the level design more as the game progressed, but somehow my enjoyment kept waning. Initially, the bright colors, revenge story, and cool concept had me going. Every level introduced new and interesting obstacles (trains, car chases, kill-gated energy shields, etc), but the gameplay never really evolved- In that way, the game eventually stops teaching you new tricks, and it doesn't give you enough tools to invent or learn new ones yourself. Every level just feels like a variation on a theme rather than a new stage- Ran just fine on a Steam Deck. It would have been far easier with a mouse, but I wanted to play on the couch. The slow-mo accompanying every skill makes controller aim quite simple, at least- . Children of the Sun is a conceptually interesting game that keeps cutting itself on the edge on which it's trying to balance. An additional skill or two in conjunction with a vibe retuning would have made this more enjoyable. The concept is neat and the achievements are fun, but the rest felt lacking

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game dearly. It's not a long ride (4.9 hours to complete it achievements and story-wise) but there's replayability in taking different paths and approaches. I didn't find it challenging with the exception of one or two shots and would have liked more of a challenge from it, but the difficulty isn't what makes it great. The story is conveyed simply and is compelling. The visual style throughout is cohesive and excellent. The mechanics are fluid and intuitive and it feels great to play. I enjoyed solving each level and especially had fun piecing together the last one when I thought I had run out of space but found exactly what I needed with maybe a second to spare. All in all, this game was fun to play and rewarding to beat. I'd highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I. Am. Obsessed. Children of the Sun is a terrific puzzler, just dripping in the most heinous of vibes. I had high hopes for this game's sniper mechanics, and I am glad to say those hopes were surpassed.It starts out relatively simple: try to find the right out to shoot a handful of guys. I will say, it was during this phase that I wondered if this game really had meat on the bone, or if it was just a cool premise with evocative art.After the first few missions though, the puzzles began to evolve at a thrilling rate. The number of missions I ended breathlessly triumphant over clever geometry and mechanics make me positively giddy.There is also, like, WAY more content than I expected? I went into the game knowing that it was about 4 hours long, but those 4 hours are just so DENSE with fun. The missions don't take long, there are a ton of them, and not a single one feels perfunctory.Basically: This game is TIGHT and pristinely polished. It's a game where you can feel the developers' fascination with their own premise, and the result is sublime.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cautionary tale of being a child and joining your local community organisation and having a good time...Until one day when your father tragically dies in an accident while handling a hunting rifle. In addition to the mental powers of telekinesis, which you had already, you gain the powers of mental illness; henceforth allowing you to not just bend the trajectories of bullets, but also the ability to callously murder your former friends.Journey back through your happy memories of the spiritual community you once inhabited, murdering everyone you met along the way, until you can finally murder the one man who gave you your powers in the first place Gameplay wise, it's pretty fun, it gets pretty puzzling as far as murder sims go.Vibe wise, I kinda felt like a school shooter the entire time because of the way the game celebrates gory death after gory death.There's also a scoring system and leaderboard if you want to engage in a phallus measuring competition with friends or strangers on the internet.Worth buying on sale. Took me 3 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where the developer came up with a cool mechanic (you control a forever-ricocheting bullet), came up with just enough story to make the mechanic cooler (revenge story against a death cult), and made exactly the right number of levels to do a bunch of cool stuff* without getting repetitive. Absolutely worth the $15, because nearly every minute* of its 4-hour runtime is interesting to play.*There is one exception. All of the main missions are rad as hell, but there is one mandatory minigame right around the midpoint of the game that is extremely clunky and poorly designed. I beat it in less than 10 minutes, so I don't think it's a deal-breaker considering the absolute bangers that the rest of the levels are, but YMMV.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: In 2024, your 'Connect the Dots' now includes murder because of the woke. I am having a lot of fun with this game and the challenges in its levels, as well as its wonderful art direction with the colorful artworks during cut-scenes and the flavorful visual effects that pop up as you play the game by merely shooting someone or going as far as building up immense momentum to the point that your bullet domes a guy so hard it creates a black hole energy visual effect. _childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle shooter where you're basically given an open field full of bad guys to kill, you'll be able to survey the area, tag the enemies and then take your shot but the moment you take the shot is when the control is shifted to the bullet itself and it's up to you to maneuver that single bullet throughout the level and kill all the enemies because one shot is all you're getting. It's a simple idea executed well enough to keep you engaged till the end with some new stuff in there to keep things fresh.The story is a simple tale of revenge which is told through brief cutscenes before and after each level with beautifully unhinged artstyle showcasing the grim aesthetics, moreover there's no dialogue or soundtrack just silent white noise in the background coupled with the gritty visuals even during the gameplay. The story is easy to piece together and the ending is satisfying asf.Overall, this is a fantastic game which is very short but I'd rather it be short than overstay it's welcome I guess and there's no replayability apart from the challenges. One minor nitpick is I wish it had the same bone crunching sound effects when you killed an enemy like in Sniper Elite, might have elevated the experience more. Regardless it's a great game and I can easily recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like simple games if they have something cool about them. Could be a nice core gameplay idea, or interesting style or story. Even before the proper rise of indie games, there were super low budget PC and console games. Series like “Simple” from D3 Publisher or the “SuperLite” from Success even gave birth to niche but popular franchises, most notable being Earth Defense Force. When I first saw Children of the Sun, I thought of such games and was hoping that it could have that “something cool”, whatever it is. But after the quite short playthrough of the title and just one day passing, I’m already struggling to remember the game.At its most basic, Children of the Sun is a puzzle/sniping simulator. While you can move around the target area on a rail left or right, it’s there to let you analyze the location and choose the position for the shot. Once you shoot, you have to kill every target on the map using that one bullet you shot or you fail. How? Well, every time the bullet hits a target, it stops and lets you aim at something else, while the rest of the world is moving at extremely slow speed. So your job is to figure out the most optimal way to ricochet from one valid target to the next in one go, while eventually a couple of additional mechanics and concepts get introduced. Oh and while also attempting to complete level challenges that are hinted in the subtitle of the level.It’s a very neat concept and I do believe that there can be a game built entirely around it, but Children of the Sun ain’t it. The most “difficult” levels tend to be that way because the game might intentionally obfuscate information from you or require you to wait. It feels artificial, not as a fun extension or evolution of the base idea, but something stuck on top of it just so you spend more time in the game. Same goes for the few levels that work differently and include weird gimmicks. It all looks clearly inspired by works of Suda51 (there’s even a hotel called NMH in the game), but has less style and substance then the games of his people actually like.By the time I was finishing this incredibly short game, I was already forgetting it. There are not that many bad levels or moments, although the very last cutscene of the game bugged out for me, but there’s just… nothing outside of the neat base concept. Perhaps, you might be interested in playing it just for novelty sake, but I doubt you’d care much about it after it’s completed. If you even bother to complete it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It's an overwhelmingly average game. It's short, overpriced, has very little in the way of interesting wrinkles. The scoring system is obtuse. It's a one-and-done kind of game. Get it on a deep, deep sale. It has no real story, no interesting twist. The main mechanic is simultaneously what you'd expect it to be and frustrating to deal with in time, especially when you're trying to do some trickier guided shots. The deflector cultists are weirdly inconsistent about when they'll get their shield back up meaning you lose a lot of runs to trying figure out if you've made it back to them in time. It's just... exactly what you'd expect, and it somehow manages to still disappoint. My playtime is literally how long it takes on average to complete the game. No joke.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the tl;dr: Another argument for a mixed rating.  I recommend the game as long as it's at a significant discount (It's $19.49 CAD at time of writing, sale price of $15.99 CAD).  Knowing what I'd get I probably wouldn't have paid more than $10 and even that's a bit much. First, I love the concept.  This sort of game is exactly the thing I like in a sniping game.  Marking the targets one by one by circling around, with the twists being that you can only fire one shot.  Making clever use of the environment and abilities to make sure your shot hits is quite enjoyable.However, the game doesn't really do much with this.  Early on you get a couple of ways to increase maneuverability, giving you more options, but the game's idea of ramping difficulty is making enemies harder to hit.  Some literally can't be marked before shooting (thankfully marks stay between attempts), some enemies have directional shields, some enemies are armored (which require a significant distance to kill and shots hitting them end the attempt instead of deflecting off), and some have a temporary defense that regenerates if you take too long to get at them.  The latter levels were more exercises in frustration as an increasing number of armor and shielded enemies meant the game became significantly less open in its design, effectively forcing you to take one of a handful of effective paths.The game is also way too short for its price.  It'd be one thing if it didn't outstay its welcome and was masterfully crafted, but towards the end it definitely felt like the devs were scraping the barrel on finding ways to make the levels more difficult.  There's also no replay value unless you're the kind of high-score leaderboard fiend.  My playtime included trying to complete every challenge the game gave me and have an unbroken score combo at the end of each level, and if you want to just play to the end it'd take maybe half this time.

Or even better, in a future patch, allow an accessibility setting to disable flashes and things of that nature.SEXUAL VIOLENCE WARNING: Additionally, there are traumatic sexual encounters that the main character faces in this game that should be listed in the Steam store page as a content warning. _childDocuments_.review: You will probably like this game.I'm truly happy for you if you do, and hope this game succeeds for the developer's sake too.But there are a plethora of reasons why it isn't for me and I try to enumerate four of them here:- I didn't gel with the art-style. It's just ugly, I am sorry. I get it's supposed to convey a message and deep meaning, but the meaning I get from it is: Everyone is as ugly inside as they are outside and I should play a game that is beautiful instead.- The story didn't grab me. Don't get me wrong, the premise is great and maybe I missed some form of gripping intro that introduced the characters in a more appealing way, but "Murder dudes all wearing the same shirt because someone you know committed suicide" doesn't feel that compelling to me. I'm not the fashion police. Just look at my face. I have no style either, I can hardly blame them for their poor choice of jerseys to wear.- Everything feels restricted, you move around in one direction only, almost herded like a stray sheep, I don't feel like a sniper at all. Do I have much choice? I don't feel any meaningful impact the moment I force my bullet to move in a different direction, because there is mostly just one obvious target that is next.- It's supposed to be lonely and depressing but after each level you are pitted with a score-board and you are pittied against a gazillion of players, all been there, and done that same thing with "BetaEdgeLord9000" having a 0.05% better score than you for reason that aren't visible, or even remotely transparent and this makes it feel too close to real life.So the game tries to be as ungamey as possible while being too gamey.Sorry, I really wanted to like this game, but it's not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is the purest example of something being "artsy-fartsy". It tries so hard to be artistic, yet comes across as pretentious and feels like it was pulled out of the creator's back end.Based on its Steam tags and description, the game tries to sell itself as a tactical/strategy/puzzle shooter. Well, as a combination of Hotline Miami, Superhot, and Sniper Elite, you would kinda expect that. But in reality, it doesn't have any parts where you would actually have to use your brain. It's extremely easy, even if/when you want to maintain combos from the start of a level till its end. Basically, you just click on each enemy's head, one after the other, and watch them die.The only parts where I had a bit of fun were some of the very late levels where every mechanic (faster bullets, hypnotic and armored enemies, bullet redirection, etc.) got introduced. That means 20-30 minutes of fun in a game that is 3 hours, and only 3 hours because 1 hour of my playtime was wasted trying to find the remaining enemies on some levels that were placed in some strange places. I guess the "highlight" of this game is when the main character sits down on the toilet, tells into the camera that she is horny because she killed a guy (yes, this really happens), and after that, you have to play possibly the worst mini-game ever concieved by a human being (you have to rotate a head with left/right mouse clicks to pick up ammunition in a top-down maze and avoid other heads).I received this product for free, yet I still want my money back. Or my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I'm a sucker for indies and games that get me thinking. This is one of those games. My highlights: The gameplay. For a game about an assassin who takes it upon herself to enact revenge against her abusers, this game is exceptional at getting you into that mindset. You become methodical, choosing who will be your first victim and who will be your last. I got deep into trying to figure out my position and the trajectory of my bullet especially in the later levels. You get into the girl's mind so easily, its terrifying in a way just how calculating you can become. This isn't a game where you can willy nilly point your gun and it will automatically hit, you have to make sure that one bullet counts or otherwise have to restart a level all the way from the top. Which brings me to my next point--Don't buy this game if you're looking for a full comprehensive game. This is a game where the story supports the mechanics rather than the mechanics supporting the story. Its a fever dream, you will never get the full details of what is going on, but maybe...that's what the developer is going for.To sum it all up: get this game if you want to feel like a calculating, stone cold killer aiming to wipe the floor with everyone standing in your way.

_childDocuments_.review: Figuring out how to guide a single bullet through all the enemies in each level is a decent concept and it tries to add new elements to keep it interesting throughout, but even for a 3 hour game its gimmick gets a bit boring fairly quickly. Whatever story it was telling here I didn’t really get much out of either, but the stylized cutscenes were cool at least
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential, but ultimately disappointing.  This would be a mid-review if such things existed on steam.Love the art, atmosphere, and the core concept is really promising. However i feel like the levels from the mid-game towards the end are really lacking. The orb-enemies are more annoying than anything, and takes most of the fun out for me sadly. I would love to see more levels with more interesting mechanics. I also couldn't get into the new endless mode, as it felt like the enemies were coming just way too slow after the first 3 enemies (may be skill issue on my end, idk). Overall, I quite enjoyed much of my time with the game, but the lacking endgame levels, short runtime, and no substantial story makes this game not worth it for me, even on sale, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: not only is it audiovisual perfection, but its done in a way that enhances the gameplay. theres a visceral punch when you kill a cultist, everyone stands out from the environment except for the sniper you play as, and the cutscenes have a really characterising scratchiness. the gameplay is already really fun and engaging, but its everything surrounding it that elevates this to a must-play. they should teach about this game in colleges
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A surreal, smart, and really fun action/puzzle game. The main mechanic of controlling a bullet mid-flight is intense and makes for some interesting challenges. The story is a disturbing grind-house revenge tale, adding to the deeply dark and surreal vibe. It's like if you dropped acid and played sniper elite while listening to a harsh noise album with a cult documentary on in the background
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A fever-dream combination of arcade and puzzle game built around taking out an entire level of baddies with a single, telekinetically-controllable bullet. Full marks up front for originality, but the grunge-psychedelic presentation and open-ended puzzle design merits a lot of credit too. It's one of those games where you can choose whether you want to merely do well enough to progress or zero in on perfecting your performance on a particular puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Hunt down a cult using a sniper and superpowers Its super stylish with short barely decipherable cut scenes are mesmerising Pretty short but very memorable and definitely worth a play New enemies and powers are added over the course of the campaign to add complexity It can be frustrating when you cant find the last enemy but oh so satisfying to thread the needle and wipe out the map the Overall a good time with only the last 2 or 3 missions being a difficulty cliffThe strange achievement structure means you can 100% the game without finishing the last level - all that's needed is to complete challenges that not every level has
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me quite a bit, it has a very unique shooting mechanic and is very fun to play. It is a short but intense game. I recommend doing the secondary objectives of the missions, you have a little more fun as it becomes more difficult and at the same time you get all the achievements in a short time.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be played in a very short 2-3 hours.I can't even classify this for now, because I would have played it further anyway; but if it had just become repetitive boredom, it wouldn't have provided any more challenge.For 15€, I expected a little more in terms of visuals.I liked the atmosphere itself, and the level design.But the whole thing looks very rough and lumpy.There could have been a lot more work on the effects and 3D sets. (Not to mention the textures.)There is only one main character, at least his animations could have been worked out better. Ah. *sighAnd that's exactly why I don't understand why my computer is so stressed while playing.The fans don't spin up that much during 3D rendering.So I can't imagine what this much power is needed for in this simple game, since there's no need to calculate brutal AI behavior, there's no physical effect at all, and the levels aren't huge and everything in them is completely lowpoly.Although I know game developers aren't really interested in optimization these days, I'd rather get my money back for it when it seems like they only did half the job.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I love or hate this game. A horribly mini-game and a slog of a final level really soured it for me; I would have much preferred to have had 3 hours less play-time but all of it be fun. I guess recommend overall, just because it's so unique if you are interested in it it's the only game in town.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; highly stylized puzzle shooter centered around a grindhouse-esque story about a cult. Absolutely get it when on sale if this sounds fun. I really wanted to love this game but it fell flat in a central way, enemy design. The games art style is gorgeous, the colors the low polygon models the vibe is just right. The cinematics in between levels convey the story effortlessly. On that front there is nothing to complain about just stellar execution. The main mechanic of the game is nothing new but interesting you control a bullet and can steer it's course including fully changing it's trajectory when hitting and eliminating a target. This gets expanded upon in later stages of the game when weak spots are introduced. These charge a meter when hit allowing to change trajectory of the bullet in mid flight and so the games comes together: "You have one bullet only to eliminate all enemies in each level." This works great on paper and for the first couple of levels but then the game absolutely fails on a crucial part of execution: enemy design. The game introduces armored enemies that can only be killed using charged shots from a specific distance as well as enemies that create a deflecting barrier that steer your bullet away. On paper this still sounds fine but it simply isn't fun. While initially the game allows you to solve levels in multiple ways by the end of it there is basically just one way that is viable and it simply is not fun anymore. I've played roughly 2h to get to the last level of the game and by the point the game lost me as I was going through the motions. Yes I know how to finish that last level but it is simply not "fun" or "entertaining" at that point. It's tedious and boring and that is imho the worst a game can be, tedious.If the game did something else with it's enemy design and the mechanics of the latter half of the game it would be amazing but as it is, it is simply not "fun" after a certain point and that is very disappointing as every ingredient necessary for this to be a cult hit in the indy sphere is there but it's just not quite working.Get it when it is on sale and play until you had your fill it is absolutely worth seeing.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: this game is just fine. some of the levels are very fun, some levels you will spend 15 minutes bashing your head against because the game will assure you you will hit a shot it will then count as a miss. im also not a big fan of the games art direction and all of the sound in this game is super loud for some reason, even on 50% volume. this game isnt bad enough to leave a negative review, but thats about the best compliment i can give
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Not the kind of game I was expecting, but a peculiar one indeed. More of an "High Score" game, but the twist of killing all your ennemies with one ball is entertaining. I loved however the little puzzle inside the missions, where you have to kill the ennemies in a precise way, not knowing how... until you find it! Short game, but interesting in a way.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is quite short, with the intention of you replaying levels to try to score higher points, or pickup secret achievements. While there's nothing wrong with it, I might suggest picking it up on sale, given the cost.Cost aside, this game is a fun little arcade shooter, where you control the bullet and ricochet around a map. There's an puzzle element to this game in identifying the best order to hit enemies in; however, given the length of the game, you can figure it out pretty quickly most of the time.The graphics aren't anything to write home about for this game, but they're perfectly serviceable for an indie title. As for the story, it is kind of there, but the game has virtually no dialogue, and tells that story through brief still shorts between levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)Kill two birds with one stone is now a puzzle game.The goal in each map is to clear the targets with a single shot, considering lines of sight and body armor. You are also given three skills to aid you in this task. While the idea seems fresh, the execution is quite flawed, as the real challenge lies in finding every target; once you do, there is very little puzzle left to solve, as most approaches work. The campaign feels like a demo, the length is slightly over the 2 hour refund window, and it leaves you thinking that a lot more could have been done. Worth at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting experimental game. Controls are minimalist, you can only move the character on a fixed rail that surrounds the scene by moving the mouse left or right, then aim and shoot with the mouse buttons. Still, it works pretty well as a concept, each level is a puzzle where you have to figure out how to kill everyone with a single bullet by re-aiming it after each successful shot, plus there's an optional challenge to clear for each level. Albeit short, it's quite a fun experience with some really trippy - though somewhat crude - visuals.The price tag is a bit high for its duration, so I recommend getting this on sale. Hope to see more levels or game modes added in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, it’s alright. I’ve seen a substantial amount of people describe this game as ‘Sniper Elite but on acid’, and I’m just gonna come right out and say that those people have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea what they’re talking about. The only similarity to Sniper Elite is that the camera follows your bullets, which any braindead idiot can figure out ten seconds into watching the trailer.Movement is restricted to clockwise and counter-clockwise rotations around the perimeter of the map, and NPC pathing is heavily scripted, so the solutions to each level are somewhat limited. You also only get one shot per level, which you then control using some kind of telekinesis, so the game’s more about coming up with and then executing a plan of action rather than improvising or being tactical; something which is explicitly stated three seperate times on the store page. Said page also states that the game has ‘light stealth’, which is just a straight-up lie. There’s never any risk to your character, and the only way you can fail a mission is if your bullet hits something other than a cultist. Due to the nature of the game, there’s also no bullet penetration, so multikills are unfortunately impossible.The entire game is coated in a layer of artificial sharpening, which cant’t be disabled, and despite being fairly well polished, it still suffers from hitbox issues and has a tendency to crash. You eventually unlock the ability to change bullet trajectory mid-shot, but you don’t get full control over the z-axis, so often I would send a bullet up into the sky and then have to reset the level because I wasn’t able to re-aim it anywhere near the remaining targets. This feels like more of an oversight than anything else, but it’s still one of the few problems that I feel needs to be addressed.There also seems to be this notion that the final level has some sort of massive difficulty spike. I really don’t know where that idea came from. It didn’t even crack my top three, and it was actually one of my favourite levels overall.To paraphrase a couple of other players, this is basically Connect The Dots meets SUPERHOT, with the story and aesthetics of Mandy. If you’re buying it because someone told you it was like Sniper Elite, you can go ahead and tell them to ♥♥♥♥ right off. It’s worth noting that I was able to finish the game with all of the achievements in about four hours, but if you’re one of those people who care about price:length ratio, there is some degree of sandbox content offered by the leaderboards for each individual level.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the kind of  "abstract" style Children of the Sun has, it's very atmospheric throughout the whole game. The story isn't like a masterpiece but it's good, especially the ending is very interesting. Overall my whole feeling about this game is that while it's not a masterpiece or something that will stick in your mind forever, it is very sleek in its presentation and well polished. One of the things I appreciacted the most was the soundtrack, which is adaptive and really adds a whole lot to the experience. It changes from suspenseful when you are searching for a spot to take the shot from, then quiets down if you stand still, until it gets loud when you take the shot. I adore the very bass and distortion heavy sounds it has. Gameplay is fun and gets expanded upon gradually by adding new mechanics, if you love puzzle games, something with an unique and dark atmosphere and don't mind if it's a short-ish game, by all means get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, the story its strange but interesting, the gameplay is really well made every shot feals like an important desicion, even if youre without an idea and tring to ricocket to maybe hit the cultist, its like every game where you are a sniper, just now you have habilitis that made this game really much better, the sound effects help enormously, every hit you made is recomforting, the only thing i have to say is that the difficulty scaling is quite strange since i got stuck in two levels but those levels wherent the last ones, over all 10/10 i would recoment it, just try it in discount if the price is too much, i was able to pass it less time that i expected, but the achivements are quite fun so i use some 2 more hours
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Children of the Sun today. I want more of it.The ending completely blindsided me. That doesn't happen very often and it impressed me - and while it does work as a full stopping point, I would not at all mind knowing what happens next. There aren't very many words in this game; there really didn't need to be (complimentary) as the art does all of the lifting. The in-game stuff is great, but the disjointed comic cutscenes are especially my jam. Gameplay-wise, this is for sure a puzzle NOT a shooter. You walk around a perimeter, mark your targets, plan the route of your bullet and send it, bend it, accelerate it into a cultist's face and then curve the sucker up into a passing bird so you can get a good angle on the gas tank of a car some goons are leaning against on the other side of the map. Want a NG+ or a DLC or sequel with some QOL features and some more options. Let me split bullets and stuff. Get wild with it and let us go in slowly with just the knife, maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what the gaming industry is meant to be all about, developers trying to be innovative and different! And even though Children of the Sun might not have longevity, it sure has captured my imagination.If you look closely to the visuals you'll see that the graphics are pretty basic all round, but that is overshadowed by the psychedelic art design. Everything from the colours, lighting, sound and definitely the story projects a surreal atmosphere that, even though might not be for everyone, sure is original. But not as original as the game play. The mechanics of moving around and shooting people with a sniper rifle are simple, but the overall premise plays more like a puzzle game. You have to really think and plan each move before stringing together that one 'magic bullet' shot. I did start to find the process a bit tedious after a few levels, but this will definitely appeal to perfectionists out there, as there plenty of avenues to tackle each level.Whether you are a fan or not, games like this deserve praise for originality. And since the price is so cheap, especially when its on sale, it is well worth giving it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun little puzzle game. A simple objective gradually blooms into a powerful swathe of abilities against increasingly complex targets. While your score might take a hit on time, this game really rewards taking a moment to plan out your shots at the start. Took me about 3.5 hours to beat, but definitely has room for me to go back and experiment to improve my scores.This game is a poster child for "I want shorter games with worse graphics made by people who are paid more to work less and I'm not kidding". A short game with simple visuals that was incredibly fun to plow through.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended "puzzle shooting" game dripping with atmosphere.This review was written after completing 13 missions and getting stuck on the 14th. I've heard the game is short, so I may be near the end. That said, I wouldn't consider the game too short if it ends within a few missions.Each level sees you, The Girl, scouting out and marking enemies, then shooting a single bullet that can be manipulated mid-flight to kill all of the targets. It's a simple concept for sure, but it's a very satisfying game play loop. Each puzzle has multiple solutions and there are scores/rankings to chase if you are so inclined. I'm not much of a "score player", but I will definitely be revisiting earlier levels again to experiment with different solutions regardless.One of the major strong points of this game is the presentation and atmosphere. The graphics are stylised in a kind of lo-fi, grungy, almost comic book aesthetic. The cut scenes are told in a frenetic motion-comic style and they break up the levels well.If you enjoyed Killer7, I reckon you'll get a kick out of this. It feels almost like a "Killer7 Side Story" with the limited movement, graphical style, and messed up plot. If you haven't played Killer7, play this first as it's more approachable, *then* fix your life and donate your soul to Suda51.This game won't be for everyone, but if the idea of a "puzzle shooter" is appealing and/or you really like the graphics, it might be for you. It's well worth the price of admission and you won't find anything else quite like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It is a rather stylish, fun, and simple “puzzle-shooter” game that narrates the short and perplexing vengeance story of a woman who uses her power in a very singular way: to control a bullet.The art directions excel with their beautiful illustrations, recherché use of colour, grunge-like design of the environment, and overall execution.The core mechanic is simple to understand, and its iterations benefit from the creative and challenging (but fair) level/puzzle design.I like it and recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Another weird and trippy indie game published by Devolver? Sign me right the ♥♥♥♥ up!In , our unnamed protagonist embarks on a path of revenge against the cult that ruined her life. All she has at her disposal is a hunting rifle, a single bullet, and the uncanny ability to control the path of that bullet.In gameplay terms, each level starts as a fairly standard sniping game where you position your character, line up your sights, and take the shot. However, when you hit your first target, time slows down and you get to re-aim where the bullet will go next. This turns each level into a puzzle, where you have to find the optimal route and have the bullet hit every enemy in a single, unbroken flight.Most levels also come with optional secondary challenges, each presented as a short riddle. This adds a couple of extra layers of difficulty since first you need to figure out what the riddle means, and then how to actually execute it in-game.As the game progresses, you'll pick up a couple of new abilities that will let you control the bullet to an even greater extent, which in turn means the puzzles become progressively more intricate and difficult.Audio-visually, Children of the Sun feels like a lost piece of PS1 media in the best possible way. The models are simple and effective, the color palette is moody and subdued, and the sound design further amplifies the intensity of the vibe. The story is told through fragmented and disjointed comic-book-style cutscenes, but there's more than enough there to get a pretty solid grip on what's going on.I do have a couple of relatively minor complaints.There are a couple of moments where the game tries to be a little too "edgy" for my taste, but I guess that's down to personal preference. The riddles for the secondary objectives vary wildly in difficulty, and I'm not ashamed to admit I had to consult an online guide for a couple of them.Also, the game could stand to be a little longer - as of the writing of this review, the only replay value it has is if you want to get one of the achievements tied to the secondary objectives or climb the ranks of the leaderboard.With all this in mind, Children of the Sun presents a pretty solid puzzling experience, especially when you consider that most of the game was made by a single dev. It's pretty cool to know there are people out there making weird games like this, and I'm 100% here for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: The concept, style, and execution of this game are great.It’s a very unique puzzle shooter that is really fun, It’s short but is sweet.Really cool, dark, and brutal visual style and music Only real downside I had is that most of the levels are very easy and are meant to be replayed for faster times and finding short cuts.I would have preferred longer more challenging levels like the final level of the game. It’s the best level in the game and feels like it really pushes its concept to its full potential. It ends just as it starts to get really good leaving you wanting more out of it.Hopefully we see more of it in the future in the form of DLC or sequel. Or even a level editor so it can live on with a community. I’d like to see it’s concept live up to its full potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. I beat it in about 6-7 hours and there is definitely a replay-ability aspect to it if you want to go back and try different solutions to the levels. The game is all about sniping enemies and planning your attacks. It's a puzzle sniper game. I love the aesthetic. When I fail a mission I always feel it's my fault and not the games, so the controls are superb.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, maybe a bit too short at my taste but well done. The artwork and story are quite good and complementary, levels might be a bit too easy at the start but the last ones are really good, the last and one a bit before in particular. Also fun to platinate though it might not always seem clear at first glance. Overall great, hope to see some more one of these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: What a painful ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ experience. This is recommended to masochists who like games that hurt, as you will hurt a lot when trying to 100% this thing. It’s for this reason that at every opportunity, aim straight for the face. It relaxes some of the stress—especially stress accrued throughout those funky mini games. The story is okay—you can really take it or leave it—but the immersion and intensity of the gameplay does make up for these small grievances.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: The audio and visual effects are amazing, every action feels powerful and the short cutscenes are unnerving in the best possible way. Also just overall a very good game. Can be played like a puzzle game if you just want to get through it, but rewards players for acting quickly with points multipliers if you're the kind of person that likes speedrunning and high scores. The only thing I would add is the ability to see your friends scores on each level, so that you could compete with just your friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece of an indie game. It is more of a puzzle game than an action game (considering this game can be played with one hand), so there will be lots of trial and error and thinking. But it also allows you to yolo once you master the mechanics and are more comfortable with them.It's concept is pretty unique. Although it does remind me a lot of SUPERHOT (which I also really enjoyed).Everything is just right about this game. The "puzzles" aren't too hard. The dialogue is minimal (thank god). I loved the cutscenes and the story! The game's length is perfect for the price. The difficulty is perfect. The achievements are perfect (you can easily 100% them if you try).The "intermission" missions are interesting, fun, and a nice welcome break from the normal bullet puzzle missions.They style, artwork, title of the game, and mission names/phrases are amazing and very well done.The tutorials are short and sweet and nicely integrated.Basically nothing in this game overstays its welcome.Perfect, bite sized game! High recommended.Historians should study this game as a lesson on how to design a game properly.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I like everything about this game, except the absolutely infuriating "pac-man like" level which I despise with every fiber of my being, which is made worse because of the random crashes this game for some reason has on my computer.Even though I can run every AAA game I've installed for some reason this amazing indie has crashed my computer more times than I died to the final boss of the elden ring dlc.I had a crash so bad I even lost all my progress pretty close to the end...That being said the aesthetic is awesome, the puzzle gameplay is really rewarding the overall game-feel is really engaging. I just hope I can play it fully without freezes or crashes in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a really unique sniper/puzzle game that feels like a bit of an acid trip as you take down a cult. Did I pique your interest?There's not much story here aside from some minor cutscenes before each stage. There's not even a single word of dialogue. But what you do see is interesting nevertheless. You get to see a cult taking over and harming its own members as you go on a revenge tour to take the cult down.The game play is rather simplistic in nature. You can only run left and right. In fact, this whole game can be played with just  a mouse. You move around in a circle or maybe between two objects if you can't fully encircle an area. Mark all the targets in the stage and find your ideal starting point. Once you take a shot and hit your target, time slows down dramatically and you can change direction of your bullet. You get one shot and you have to take down everybody in the stage to advance. Most stages have a challenge for you to strive for as well.You'll unlock some minor abilities and find new enemies as you progress. You can curve bullets, speed bullets up, or even redirect them without hitting anything provided you fulfill the requirements. You can also aim for birds flying around the level to give yourself a new vantage point. The game is short and sweet but it's really unique. I finished it in about 3-3.5 hours and had a blast all the way through. If you're looking for a unique indie game, this is a must play.One recommendation, if a dev is reading this, is it would be nice if you added an option to restart from where you shot at what time you shot instead of always forcing you to the starting point. The last mission for example, I would always rush to the far right side and immediately take a shot. It's a minor thing but I think it would be a nice QoL to just let me retake the shot from the same spot and time instead of running to the same position over and over every time I retry.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very cool game. A mix between hotline miami, superhot and Rip Van Winkle.I'm not a competitive guy so I haven't tried hard to have the best score and all the achievements. But I think this game deserve more atention and allow players to create their own levels and challenges. Try it! Very fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I especially recommend the demo, which gets deep enough for an accurate sense of the full game. I had the sense when playing that there was only one intended path, but watching better players than me do crazy things with the signature mechanic really opened my eyes to its possibilities.I was disappointed the music wasn't as fun as the trailer (was there even any music?), but the game played as promised. Except for the last level, I was pleased to be able to play at a very slow pace, leaderboards be damned.There are some minor quality of life improvements (options for unmarking targets, disabling HUD, showing fatal distance, minigame skip, etc) that could make this an easier recommendation, but I am not optimistic based on the dev ignoring the low-hanging rebindable controls fruit the community has been asking for since before launch. But if those aren't dealbreakers and you like the style for a bizarre and violent puzzle game, the price is right on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: What you would get if Robert Rodriguez made a grindhouse story about a girl taking revenge on a cult. Armed with a sniper rifle that basically is Yondus Yaka arrow, the gameplay consists of finding the optimal path to take everyone out with a single bullet. Simple premise and pretty basic gameplay, This is much more of a puzzle game than a shooter so the replayability is limited but the presentation, sound design and graphics oozes style, That alone is what got me interested and the gameplay is compelling enough to make you stay, just wish there where more of the game. First half of 2024 have been amazing for indies and this is no exception. Very solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: is a unique and fun puzzle game about a girl getting revenge on a cult with a sniper rifle and powers that allow her to kill 20 people with a single bullet. From a gameplay perspective, once you shoot, you are playing as the bullet (and it's casing, which I assume is the result of a European developer lol). It has a very unique and unsettling art style, which combined with the music creates a really compelling atmosphere for the game.There are many different ways to kill all the enemies in a level, but there are specific challenges on most levels that require you do at least one specific thing, usually prompted by a vague sort of riddle that is fun to figure out.The game is not too long, it took me about 4 hours to beat. I recommend it for anyone who likes puzzle games and doesn't mind violence.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I got very controversial feelings after finishing the game. On one hand we have curious mechanics and on the other hand - very disturbing both visual and sound design. If you're not afraid to experience seizures when exposed to certain lights, patterns, images and weird audio accompaniment, then you wil have a chance to enjoy playng it.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great game. Easy to learn mechanics and fun game play. Art style is unique and when you figure everything out it feels great.Two minor critiques. - Every once in a while there was a hidden person that was maybe too hidden which caused me to fire aimlessly to figure out where they were.  - Having the two powers on the same button caused some issues for me. It was manageable but did feel awkward.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Stylistic, enough mechanics to keep the game interesting, and a short enough timespan to get through it all.While I never really like the idea of my score on a leaderboard, if you're looking for replayability, you could do a lot worse.The story is angry, concise and so well established that I understood without a word needing to be said.There's a trick or two to some of the levels making for a really fun experience overall.If you're looking for a neat puzzle-type game and want to revenge-murder your way though, I can absolutely point to Children of the Sun.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A cheap, short, grimy and grungy sniper puzzle shooter you can beat in about 5hrs, I even 100% the game on my first and only run lol, challenging aswell and great if your looking something interesting concept wise or a fan of Hotline Miami.For its length however, I'd wait for a sale, but other than that its a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet puzzle-shooter game where you brutally kill everyone with one bullet, bouncing from head to head. The presentation is amazing, with the animated cutscenes being gritty and loud, making for this intentionally disorienting feel. Gameplay is very punchy, with your one bullet having the impact of a freight train. You have to connect the dots between everyone on the map, flying your bullet from person to person. While there are some routes that are obviously better than others, CotS gives the opportunity to return to previous levels and try different routes, and maybe increase your score on the global leaderboard. Later on in the game, where you unlock more ways to manuever your bullet, it only adds to the punchiness. Definitely enjoy <3Audio works well. While the music isn't nothing super standout, the sound effects is where this game also shines. You FEEL the sound of the bullet whizzing through the air, picking up speed. You FEEL the impact as you shatter some random dude's kneecaps.Recommend from me <3
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are saying the game is too short but I found it to be the perfect length.The difficulty the game scaled with was perfect.After figuring out the controls each level took some thinking but never made me feel stuck, and on the late levels where it took quite a few tries it was so satisfying to feel that accomplishment.We need to stop evaluating the price of games by their playtime because many you pay for the experience and with Children of the Sun that experience is worth every pen you'll spend.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A rather odd, dark, creepy & specific  game in which you play a cult victim seeking revenge with a sniper rifle.Don't get fooled by the simplicity of the first levels where you get to discover the first gameplay twist (you get to use telekinetic powers to control your sniping way more that you would expect); this mechanic actually goes deeper and deeper as you progress in the game. Interestingly, soon enough, some of your enemies will display powers too.The game has a very , but I didn't bother because it's my kind of short games. Last levels were very enjoyable, and revisiting the game to 100% it with achievements is really extending it in very enjoyable ways. Be wary, there are some elements of narration that definitely warrant a trigger warning here. Lastly, this whole Hotline Miami-vibe short sniping puzzle game is definitely worth it in my opinion, but I wouldn't buy it above 15 to 20 bucks tops for 3 to 4 hours of enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game for what it is. It's a little janky and rough around the edges (bullet momentum felt inconsistent to me personally), but by the time you throw your bullet around the map, you do get that great puzzle solving brain juice. It's pretty short if that's a deal breaker and I think well worth the time to play for an afternoon!
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the sun is a nice little game with a unique concept and excellent art direction. You play as a women who wants revenge by killing the leader of a cult. You do this by shooting them, but you only get one bullet, and as soon as you kill one person you can change the direction of the bullet to kill the next. Repeat until everyone is dead. Seems simple and for the most part it is. Later on the game introduces some enemies you need to kill a certain way. Even still the game is pretty easy. I struggled a little with the last few levels but for the most part it's strait forward. I would recommend doing the challenges. There's one per level and they add a little extra difficulty. (F*ck the train one though). Sometimes it can be tricky to actually figure out what the challenge is as it doesn't outright tell you what to do, but you can figure them out.     The story is basic. I think. It's a little hard to tell what is going on with the Acid visuals and quick cuts but it's not the point of the game so i wouldn't give it much thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This project is seeping with creativity. Rother & crew knew exactly how many tweaks and abstract flourishes to spread out of the course of this 4~ hour experience to keep you intellectually satiated. Elicits the like of Elfen Lied and the work of Panos Cosmatos in the best possible way. Monstrous supernatural strength, dwarfed by horrors of grounded systemic violence, used to violently disentangle the organs of your oppressors in a way that parallels but never Fixes the parts of you that are never coming back. Except now you're feeling that rage yourself, every time you hold down left click to speed your bullet up, every time you're thrown into a level after being reminded of what hurts and who hurt you. There's something that clicks with this kind of detached trauma in gaming, a bit too well.I feel compelled to say that there are moments where this game is seemingly edgy for edgy sake. It's difficult to make that distinction in an action/revenge game as hateful and as violent as this, but not every line works with the greater picture imo. The vast majority do however, and the stylization of the formal and informal gameplay mix splendidly. If there's one word to describe this game, it is execution. A bold visual style. The strategy that defines the core gameplay loop. And, well, the in-game method in which you progress level to level. I'm not sure how else to spill it: this game rules. You really should use keyboard and mouse by the way. I was stuck to controller until the very last level. Switching was the difference between night and day. It turns out the combo system is entirely usable at your lower "skill levels", it just wasn't intended for the longer turn speeds inherent to controller. Please use keyboard and mouse! And it should be noted that, unfortunately, Sleigh Bells is not featured in the game. God does it fit perfectly though, whoever put those songs in the trailers Gets It.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: More like children of the FUN. This game is incredibly inventive, fun, and beautiful. My literal only 2 complaints are that this game needs a level editor because the core gameplay is so awesome I would love to have more levels, and Chasing Lies is a great concept but the physics are super wacky and dumb. Also, the light strings in the last level should not have collision with bullets. But seriously, this game has one of the best ~4 hour campaigns you will ever play.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper rifle scoring puzzle game ??? Hell yeah !This game was a blast to play. The idea to combine a sniper rifle, puzzle elements and a scoring system is genius. The levels where you have to figure out the best way to headshot every ennemy in a row without spending too much time aiming to avoid losing your combo are where the game truly shines. _childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a beautiful game consisting of a series of levels in which you must strategize how to kill every enemy on the map with one bullet infused with your telekinetic powers. Once you're familiar with all the mechanics and their limitations, the game achieves a nice flow. However, about the time you enter this flow, the game is over. I typically value games based on whether or not I had one hour of entertainment for every $1.00 I spend. One day, this game may cross that threshold, but it will take a concerted effort on my part to be a completionist of the game's Steam achievements and probably then some after that. This being said, I still recommend this game, and put it in the bucket of unique gaming experience worth paying a little of a premium above what you might usually consider. In my opinion, this game will be one I turn to when I want a quick gameplay session without much investment on my part.

The game introduces new mechanics quickly and wastes no time adding more layers to each puzzle.-->Playing with mouse is recommended for precision, it is a sniping game after all.-->A keyboard is entirely unecessery for Children of the Sun.-->Playing on steam deck is possible, but joystick controls make precision more difficult.You can beat the game in 4-6 hours, allthough the challenges and leaderboards may give you additional playtime.It's a short, but great experience that makes you wish for a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: Very mildly short game that doesn't over stay it's welcome; for 14.99 certainly worth the pricing paying full dollar (I got it around 11.99 on sale). If you want a weird experience keeping your toes tight. Play it till the end in a single go if you can, this is a perfect game that captivate's the raw energy the style this very game going for. Not only is it fun, very much re-playable after you beat it! You want to gain every achievement or get your mind off things quick by a simple hard game? This game perfect, with discovering new outlet's to take down your cultists foes.Mind you the biggest con of this game is the leader-board, Why?    Well put it simply this game tries really hard to be in-a-way arcade based; this is where you will noticed you and your friends (or everyone around the world) will end up with the same high-score (and lower rank) as you continued each level. Those that are on-top, ones that got the higher high-scores by hitting every target precisely; will find themselves being number one "IF" they are the first to get it (in general). Now the problem isn't the High-Score itself isn't hard to gain. Hard but not impossible (certainly fun); just do not be surprised if you ever gain the highest score like everyone else landing a lower rank. As much the game does it's best to be arcade base, one of the weakest qualities.To get to the point you will be below the leader-board even if you got the same number as the one who got 'THAT' SCORE first. Meaning the score-board works but only those who got the score first to be top rank above everyone. So you will never be number 1. You will likely end-up being number 2 or 1000+ rank like everyone else. IF by a chance you do land to be RANK-1, your friends can managed the same score as you only to be below you. Counter-Productive to be honest. Just be aware of this. Everyone kinda ends up with the same consistent high-scores.I figured this important to point out, since I do nothing but played arcade based games (old to new); while some may get turn off by this minor issue. And it is minor, however I don't personally mind it since that's not why I love playing Children of The Sun. Very simple yet still hard, does not insult you & every level was given a lot care & thought into it. Rare to say, I loved every level in it's own right! The game get's harder as you go, that make's the game very balanced how it handle's level design. I ended up respecting every bit of it.Highly Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a fascinating blend of gore and strategy. With a lower poly art style and stunning 2D artwork, the vibe of the game is immaculate, as well as the narrative that is woven in with each level. The mechanic itself, playing as a psychic sniper that can control the bullet after being fired is unique and in application, extremely fun. Being able to be strategic and figure out exactly how to carve the best path for your bullet leaves you feeling both satisfied and smarter for the next level. It continues to improve on the idea and integrates new ideas well. It was a solid experience overall, and I plan to continue to play and see how I can better each path.

_childDocuments_.review: I really dig "Children of the Sun". You play a masked sniper - whose look reminded me somewhat of the movie "The Crow" - on a mission to wipe out some kind of religious group. The details are hazy, as the plot is presented through a bunch of confusing cartoons. That's fine though. We've learned from "Hotline Miami" that context is not a necessary pre-requisite, but a seasoning. "Children of the Sun", unlike "Hotline Miami" is not a franticly-paced action game. It's a strange kind of puzzle piece, where you guide one single bullet from enemy to enemy, sometimes bending time and space to land a perfect head shot. Through a liberal use of slow motion, it gives you ample time to consider your next move. The catch is that you have to nail all the enemies with one bullet, and the bullet can't touch anything that doesn't bleed or explode, or it's game over. Is that sort of ridiculous? Oh yes. Is it great gameplay? Duh! "Children of the Sun" does its premise justice, and fully delivers on the potential of its central gimmick. Its grungy aesthetics, noise-filled soundtrack and ridiculously violent gameplay hit just the right spot for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept. Easy to understand puzzling rules that require minimal complex input (the entire game can be controlled with the mouse) but at no cost to abstract thinking. You are, essentially, tasked with mastering navigation of 3D environments using your bullet, maximising your kill efficiency (based on distance and hit location), timing your special powers, and positioning your ballistic in such a way that you can iron out special enemy types.As said, very basic concept that's handled very well; just the right simplicity to be easy to learn, yet enough depth to maintain interest in the long term.My only grievance (other than selfishly wanting more content!) is that I think the last level, while a climax, is also a fairly significant difficulty spike and regresses the flow of puzzle solving to a fairly trite trial-and-error. Especially if you kinda suck like me. Because there aren't really any emergent factors of the game. It's not like fighting a boss over and over where understanding and learning is half the battle, and reactivity to how it fights each time is another. The level plays out the same way every single time, as it should as a puzzler, but with a high difficulty failures equate to a fairly boring repetition of play.But that's just a minor grievance and specific to my own skill level and what I perceived as an end game spike. Otherwise the game's good, simple ♥♥♥♥ that's strong on paper and in execution. I'm not going to stick with the game to master leaderboards. But I'm glad it's there, and the it was worth my time nevertheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Sleazy, kinetic assassin puzzler. Through all the grime and grit, there's a really thoughtful loop here. Use your powers to kill all the bad guys with one shot but... how elegant can you make it? That "elegance" is such a delicious counterflavor to the grim story and graphics. _childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles and shooting games don't usually go hand in hand naturally, but Children of the Sun has somehow stuck the landing. Constantly testing your patience and problem-solving skills, one bullet is all you have, it's also all you ever need.I loved the visuals above all else in this game. The gameplay is a lot of fun and challenging (if you care a lot about high scores) but it does sometimes lack a certain polish in terms of the bullet's hitbox. Overall, the game is rather short, if I did not care for scores or achievements, I'd likely finish it within two hours or less. The price is something to be desired as well unless you're the type to be on the top of every leaderboard in each level, you may wait for a worthwhile sale.Even if I won't play Children of the Sun again anytime soon, my four hours experiencing this visual treat was more than I could ask for.

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is really cool, it takes a simple concept and does it really well and despite being a short game it oozes style and is definitely worth checking out.You play as a sniper that has one bullet to try and take out many enemies in an area, only you can control the bullet somewhat during flight and redirect it every time you hit a target.So to start with you scout out an area, tagging enemies and possible targets as you go. Then you choose a moment to fire, a target to hit first and you have to work out how to hit every target with this one shot.It took me a little over 3 hours to clear every stage and get every achievement so there's not much left to do outside replaying the levels or going for high scores on the leaderboards.The style, atmosphere and storytelling weren't really appealing to me but it's nice to play something truly unique, a game I didn't spend long in but it certainly left an impression that I won't be forgetting for a long time.If you're happy with the short length of the game and intrigued by the action puzzle-like gameplay I would definitely recommend checking this one out. If the game gets a sequel or a follow-up that has a larger scale, I look forward to playing that too.
