_childDocuments_.review: The One Shot, One Kill aspect of sniping has been a mainstay within video games for some time, dominating the hyped expectations of First Person Shooters.  But the OS,OK method is not just a medal to be awarded on a flick in a multiplayer lobby here: the one bullet in your gun is your one opportunity to slay all your enemies in front of you.  You must kill them all in order to maintain your secrecy and continue your mission.  But how do you kill multiple people in different places with one bullet fast enough to avoid alerts?  Telepathy.  Telepathy and a lot of Hate.You are THE GIRL, fighting a past plagued with atrocities and trauma brought through THE CULT that she joined and was raised in, is out to kill THE LEADER, a mysterious long haired aviator-donning man who set THE GIRL on her path to vengeance.  The plot of Children of the Sun is offered in sample sized, overly-saturated, schizophrenically-paced retraces that take the syrupy feel and transitions of a Killer7 and inject the 4-day-bender concoction Post Void would leave you to deal with.  It’s hard to piece everything together but the reasons to kill these cultists are not needed when you’re given your ways to dispatch them.Wielding otherworldly powers, THE GIRL uses her trusty sniper with one bullet, and when your initial bullet hits your first target with a Sniper Elite-like onboard camera from firing to contact, you’re brought into a first person view of the bullet and can send that bullet wherever you see fit.  This allows for impossible angles to become routine and no cultist to feel safe as each enemy will bleed soon enough.  All shots must connect with either an enemy or an environmental hazard, explosive or aviary, or the mission must be restarted.  The angles you’ll be expected to hit are going to feel absolutely nutty at first but the end result within the game’s 2-3 hour campaign will stretch how far one bullet should be able to go.Preparation is the name of the game.  Movement and firing is handled exclusively on your mouse, no keyboard needed.  Guiding your mouse left and right will navigate THE GIRL around the layout on another Killer7-kin railed path to gain different angles.  Once enemies are in sight, you can mark targets that will show different colors for different styles of enemies which will be highly necessary to map your kill path based on who needs what and where.  It’s a very simple control scheme that feels smooth and effective even with juggling multiple different aspects of combat in the later levels.As you get the hang of guiding your bullet through multiple people, a steady stream of extra ability becomes available.  Guiding your bullet mid-flight, accelerating your bullet to supersonic speeds, changing your bullet’s trajectory mid-flight without hitting a target: the creativity and collective ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you can perform with these inclusions makes the initial entrance of a level feel like an insurmountable task and by the end of it you wonder how these cultists ever stood a chance to your genius.  The overexposed neon red of the blood splatter to whipping your bullet 180 degrees to the next cultist running in fear of the bullet with a mind of its own setting its eyes on them and complete your mission with a cacophony of noise, colors, and dopamine is more addictive than whatever this cult was providing.And you’ll need each and every inch of power you bring to your bullet as the cultists did not come to lie down to you.  The beginning missions offer a pedestrian outlook of the farther reaches of THE CULT, but later levels bring in riot-shield wielding enemies, heavy armor soldiers that require a supersonic bullet to kill, and praying shamans that can curve your bullet out of harm's way, only to be vulnerable for a short period of time.  Each layer provided to your arsenal is another layer THE CULT recognizes and defends against, and starts really stretching your brain for the best possible outcome to murderous victory.Throughout Children of the Sun’s 26 levels, 21 level-specific optional objectives help push the envelope of what’s doable within each area.  These (to my knowledge) aren’t necessary for any post-credit extras but they are worth a good chunk of points as each level, outside the mini-game and plot-specific levels, is scored based on time, amount of shots/paths taken, limb damage, multikills, and more.  The scoring gives a much needed injection of replayability for the competitive bunch as the amount of meat on the bones for its campaign might not be enough to satisfy some.There are a few levels in between the puzzle-based shooter that serve as breaks in the action, most are plot related points that help provide a needed reset on the tense action, but there’s just this one 2D mini-game where you have to collect bullets on a rudimentary map before you can hit these roaming targets and there’s walls in the way and you are constantly moving and can only turn in wide rotations and if you hit a wall it reverses and mirrors your direction.  This game is miserable and half broken: you and your enemies can go through walls, the patterns for the enemies leave very little wiggle room, and it’s just not a very fun sidestep from the game’s main attraction.Most levels are very well done, especially the car chase mission is ludicrously entertaining, but the very last level of Children of the Sun feels like an ankle-snapping misstep.  With all the different enemies seen throughout the game and all the different abilities provided to your bullet, The Temple requires you to remove two tiers of multiple enemies of multiple calibers and there’s less creativity to muster through this and it succumbs to hitting “the line” and praying your angles are correct.  It took me nearly an hour (and a night away to vent frustrations) to map and hit the correct path for this level, which was nearly a third of my total playtime.  I get they wanted this grand finale but it doesn’t procure the vivid imagination the previous levels did and provided more of a sigh of relief that it was over than the dopamine-soaked “A-ha!” moments peppered through beating previous levels.But you know what’s the sign of a good game?  After finally finishing the last level, I want to go back and pull my scores higher and hit the rest of the optional objectives because that rush of pulling some serious shenanigans on dirty cultists with a .50cal bullet and some revenge-filled ingenuity is a rip-roarin’ way to burn a couple hours.  With its syrupy, saturated presentation and some real smart puzzle gunplay, it’s easy to angle our bullet past Children of the Sun’s mistakes to combo some hours in pure delight.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it through. There is demo available, I recommend playing it before buying. If you like the demo, you'll like the full game as well. Anyhow, review time. Controls are so well thought out that mouse is all you need. This really doesn't get any simpler, although keyboard is also supported it's not needed.  Story is the game's weakest point. Evil cultists killed parents, must revenge, also can use telekinesis on the bullet for some reason... Or the whole cartridge, in this case. I assume she shoots with her telekinesis as well and the gun is there to help with the aim. The story is told between missions in chaotic comic format without any text or speech. Except in one level. I don't know, the whole story seems stale, it really doesn't have any meat in it. Blocky old school 3D graphics from early 00's when Voodoo was the leading GPU in the market. Kind of reminds me of Superhot for some reason. You have one bullet you can re-aim after each successful hit, or in mid-air if your power meter is full. You can also speed up the bullet. Some enemies have armor that requires you to shoot at full speed and in later levels; a power field that forces your bullet out of it's trajectory, but leaves the cultist vulnerable for a brief moment. You have to kill all the enemies with one bullet; if you miss you die for some reason and have to replay the level. You get a score after each completed level. Completing levels more efficiently brings more points. Pretty easy, only the car chase managed to frustrate me a bit... Until I realized I'm supposed to blow up the cars. 4-5 hours, which seems to be pretty much on the nail. Any longer and it would overstay it's welcome. Force fields get easier when you realize you can just graze them with the bullet from the middle, doing this will speed up it's flight. It also gets through terrain with the force field push, which may or may not be a bug. The game doesn't explain why you have only one bullet. Perhaps telekinesis works only once per day? Also, you can remove your mask during missions. This doesn't seem to affect the game play at all. 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a very short, but interesting . I have no idea why people are calling this a shooter. It has a gun and you shoot it; but if that’s all the criteria needed to be a shooter, then that means Telltale’s The Walking Dead would be one too.There is a pretty basic revenge story to follow as you play the game, but it’s told in a very stylized way with very little dialogue and it covers some pretty dark themes. It’s mostly told with flashes of 2D comic panels that have a really cool graffiti art style to them. Unfortunately, I don’t think the 3D sections of the game quite capture it as well and it ends up looking like a weird hybrid of a low-poly retro style and a 7th gen game when you’re playing it. The environments are pretty great for the most part though. Everything is dark, dingy, and surreal; and the soundtrack compliments it very well. I love the synth beating to the pace of your footsteps as you find the right spot to take your shot, I love the cymbal crash every time you hit a target, and I love the loud and heavily distorted droning after you complete a level and see your bullet’s path across the map.There is a a good amount of variety to the game. New abilities, target types, and other challenges are introduced throughout the entire game up to and including its final level. There are only two levels that have a frustrating difficulty spike, one of them being a weird Pacman-like minigame instead of an actual level and the other being a vehicle level where everything is a moving target, but the rest are just challenging enough to be satisfying to figure out.My biggest complaint I have with this game is just how short it is. I really liked the puzzles and I wanted more after I was finished. I would’ve liked to at least have a level editor or something, a la Hotline Miami, to give it more replayability. Even without it though, I can see myself revisiting this game often in the future to try for 100% and climb the leaderboards.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and stylish puzzle shooter with a very unique premise that’s brought to its full potential throughout the game’s runtime. The grunge cell-shaded art style, mixed with the lack of score, and the pure brutality of the gameplay all helps sell the cold and harsh revenge tale this is going for. Really great game, wish it was maybe a little longer or had a bit more variety in enemies, or maybe even a few more mini games or unique levels to break up the pace, but the amount of replayable on display here from the sheer amount of ways you can tackle each and every stage is beyond satisfying and I can absolutely see myself replaying this endlessly, if not to grind the leader boards.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly enjoying my time with Children of the Sun. Completing some levels feels incredibly satisfying, and on others, I'm chasing high scores, aiming for the top 40 or even breaking into the top 10 with a newfound strategy or realizationSome scenes are designed to evoke discomfort, which is fine since you have to feel good about the protagonist going after the enemies and it serves its purpose of making you hate them more. One area for improvement, in my opinion, is the clarity of the scoring system. While playing, I've noticed that understanding the mechanics behind scoring isn't as straightforward as I'd hoped. You'll find people with 3 times your score on simple levels and wonder what they did. Consulting the tutorials and manual, you won't get more information than your intuition will tell.When I turned to YouTube gameplays from tryhards, I was told about hidden scoring mechanics, but I'm hopeful that as more players uncover them, the community will share guides and additional info.In summary, Children of the Sun is another solid release from Devolver. I'd rate it a 9/10. And to Vinny, if you happen to read this: I'm coming for that #1 spot on the silly minigame you took from me >:c

_childDocuments_.review: ~ 2.5hr of content. Solid game, great art style, and tells a solid story without a single word of dialog.The only frustrating part is the final 2 levels, where you can tell they made them purposefully more difficult so you can't do the whole game in <2hr then refund it. I wish they would've just had fleshed it out with more content, but it's expected if this is a developer's first game.As with most puzzle games, you can't replay it or play it endlessly. The leaderboards are pretty much useless for normal players since points are deducted based on how many tries it takes to do the level and how long you took to do it, meaning that one person who grinded the speedrun strat for each level makes it to the top. My recommendation is to keep the leaderboards as friends-only. I would rather see how they ranked as they played through the game.Overall, a wonderful first game by this developer and I look forward to seeing what they make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, when I went into this game, I thought the game would be a sort of 3rd person shooter... little did I know that it would be a Hitman sniping mission, but better.The mechanics revolving around your bullet and the whole planning and executing your plan is very enjoyable. It's basically a sort of arcade-y version of Sniper Elite where the very elaborate "you have hit this specific part, of this specific limb, of this specific body part" is simplified to just "head", "arm", "chest" etc. You may think that it's to it's detriment but no, it helps the game as it focuses attention more onto the story and the puzzle mechanic. This brings me to my next point.The puzzles in this game are very well thought out and not as straightforward, especially the later levels. You may think that the 3 abilities unlocked would make the levels easier and it does to an extent. However, the majority of the levels are made extremely difficult by either placing enemies in annoying positions to get to, or placing annoying enemies to deal with in positions that prevent you from getting an easy dub. Especially priests, screw those guys.In conclusion, the game is fun as hell. the story is compelling, art style is super pretty, the minigames are fun, the extra birds given to help reposition you are good, abilities feel impactful and ACTUALLY REQUIRE A BIT OF SKILL to use, and the final challenge being a "do everything in one shot" is actually very hard.All in all, if your a fan of puzzle games and don't mind getting frustrated, then this game is for you. Hell, even with some levels being super hard I managed to complete the game in 3 hours.Good luck, and happy hunting!

_childDocuments_.review: Children of the Sun is a puzzle shooter stripped down to just the core puzzles and the aesthetic. The style is very minimalist and psychedelic, the plot is barely there and follows the jumbled chronology of your protagonist's crumbling mind, the levels themselves contain lots of "errors" that quickly become too obvious and drastic to be anything but either magical or psychosis on the part of the protagonist.And it works! The puzzles are what's on display here and they're good. Everything else works towards communicating how broken the protagonist is. The puzzles are truly unique and very satisfying... and the plot communicates a story about how our need for control damages the people around us. There's so little here but everything works because they put the thought into making sure it was put together excellently.And the price! It's so cheap! Well worth the cost of entry. If you want shorter games with worse graphics made by people who are paid more to work less and you're not kidding... this is a game for you.

Very punk/grunge with incredibly inspired set pieces. - no real downsides (besides the difficulty I mention below), I just want more of this game, world, and art!Word of warning/encouragement: the game does get harder and more complex. _childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. The idea is novel, the music and art fit the game well, and the mechanics feel very smooth (I saw that the dev mentioned how hard it was to get the camera to look right, which makes sense considering how natural it feels). It definitely makes sense that Devolver is publishing this game - it's the exact sort of stylized, hyperviolent and well-executed game that is typical of stuff they publish. The game is kind of short. It is only 15 dollars, so 4.5 hours out of it works to 3.33 dollars/hour, which isn't that bad. Plus, it's primarily a one-man project. I think the main issue isn't its length but the challenge of the early levels - they're all kind of easy and go by really fast. The game only felt actually challenging at the end. Shifting the difficulty spike a little earlier would fix most of this game's problems. Overall: solid game, 8 to 8.5/10. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a great puzzle game. To me, it's reminiscent of Superhot - takes an interesting FPS game premise, makes it a stage based puzzle game, gets in and out in like two hours. Each stage has some number of enemies standing or walking about, and you’re a telekinetic sniper who, once they shoot the bullet and hit someone, can redirect and reshoot the same bullet to hit someone else, so the game is about chaining headshots by finding out lines of sight (with more mechanics as the game progresses). Great style and visuals, satisfying puzzles, slick presentation for the solution of the puzzles, and a fun high score contest if you want it. There’s some little things that can be annoying, like having to walk back into the position you want to shoot from if you lose, or trying to find everyone in the level (that's part of the puzzle), but it’s minimal, and the game is satisfying and definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle shooters, and this is a wonderful addition to the genre. It's fun not just figuring out the level but maximizing score. There is some absolute insanity that can be pulled off with proper planning and scouting of the level. I am doing my best to not just finish this game in 1 day, but god do I want to.I will be following Rene Rother's future projects whatever, and wherever they may be. Click some heads, stop the spread.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty short, so maybe it's not worth the 15 bucks, but it doesn't overstay its welcome. There is just enough of it with interesting mechanics to leave you feeling satisfied. You also have challenges on certain levels, so there is a bit of replayability. If you want, you can wait for a sale, but the game is definitely a thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say this first: this has now become one of my favorite games!The story is dark and cinematic, not wasting a moment on screen, leaving you breathless with its dark imagery.The gameplay loop is the right mixture of challenging and enjoyable, making you consider every angle for the perfect shot. I couldn't help but binge-play this game up until the end. The way the gameplay evolves over time left me thoroughly impressed, as for each obstacle the game throws in your path, its array of tools helps you overcome it.While sadly short, I enjoyed every minute of this game and will gladly return to see how far up the leader boards I can climb and obtain all of the achievements. I highly recommend this game, and if you're unsure, try out the demo to see if this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game. Excellent use of a few core mechanics, and doesn't overstay its welcome. I beat it, though I didn't 100% it, and am happy it ended where it did. This is a beautiful single sitting game, with some space for people to hone their skills and master it if they really want, and I'm pleased with it. It was worth paying full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Very few games have I replayed the demo for them before they came out like I did for this one. The gameplay is addictive with just the right level of challenge to keep you satisfied. The game is short, but I feel like it is the perfect length for what it is. Plus I foresee coming back again and again to get those last few challenges I need.This game feels like the closest we are ever going to get to a "Hell Followed With Us" game, the vibes are very similar.Also at time of writing this, I have the high score on the car level, so I may be a tad biased.I recommend this game highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Children of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Very good puzzle game, very good killing game, very good dopamine game if you enjoy arcade high scores. Everything about this game is better experienced knowing nothing going into it, don't look up explanations, guides, or how the scoring system works. Trust me its much more fun figuring it all out on your own. This is a puzzle game after all

name: Goodbye Volcano High
detailed_description: Features Fully voice-acted and starring Lachlan Watson ( The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina ) Meaningful choices: Make difficult decisions to navigate Fang’s life and friendships Stunning hand-drawn art and character animations—feels like a playable cartoon Written using the storytelling engine that powers Heaven's Vault, Sorcery! and 80 Days Goodbye Volcano High: a hybrid cinematic narrative/rhythm game/coming of age/interactive movie visual novel experience The world’s about to explode. Just in time for senior year. Just Fang’s luck: they finally figure out what they want out of life, and now the world’s about to explode. Ok. So the world’s ending—do you tell your crush your feelings? Fix your messed-up family dynamic? Write the best song ever ever ever?? Try to do it all? Goodbye Volcano High is a story-driven, choice-based cinematic adventure game about personal growth, acceptance, and the power of community. What will you do at the end of an era? Decide Who To Be Your choices shape who Fang becomes, and determine your gameplay experience. Discover what the future holds as you play through your final year at Volcano High. No pressure... Chosen Family Values Get close with friends, family, acquaintances, frenemies, crushes (crushes!?!). Figure out how you’re gonna be there for your loved ones when it matters most—it is the literal end of the world, after all. Nurturing relationships builds affinity and changes the outcome of your gameplay. Don’t Let the Apocalypse Get You Down Put all the shit that’s hard to say into your music with an interactive rhythm and lyrics system. Choose what you want to say in your lyrics and then perform those original tracks throughout the story. Dino Minigames & Prehistoric Interactions Immerse yourself in Fang's day-to-day through interactions and conversations. In-game dinosaur-themed social media and interactive one-offs make you a part of Fang's life.

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High has some good things and some bad things, it has very, very pretty backgrounds, it has a pretty nice soundtrack... and that's it.The story is very, VERY average and very, VERY simple, the characters were boring, there was almost no conflicts between then and when there were, they were easily solved, the choices in this game are... almost no choices. Nothing of what the game let's you choose will influence in the game, maybe you will unlock a different photo in a gallery, that's it, no matter what you cannot change anything, in fact sometimes it tricks you and makes you believe you have multiple choices and then the game removes those choices and forces you to take one choice.Or maybe the three choices the game is giving you will make Fang say the exact same thing in the end, because you have almost no control.The voice acting is terrible and I don't mean the voices, I am sure the voice actors and actresses are pretty good, but it feels they got no direction, like nobody told them how they should express themselves, this is extremely noticeable on Fang, the main protagonist.Besides that, the price is extremely expensive for how long is going to take you to beat it.Not recomended, not even cheap honestly because it was pretty damn boring, I'm sure you can find a fun game with similar characters for free somewhere else, ahem ahem.... those who know, know what I am talking about.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished episode two as of writing this review, which is when the audition for the battle of the bands occur. So far not pleased with the various technical issues, lack of common visual novel features, and odd decisions in regards to the available gameplay alongside choices with their effects on the characters1.) Technical issues-The lip syncing is off and often characters will speak over themselves if you happen to skip dialogue rather than just transitioning to the next audio line-Characters will sometimes just slide across the screen, no bobbing either for their model to indicate walking either-Some odd clipping issues noticeable for background characters, especially if they have feathers or wings-Setting UI elements will overlap with each other depending on resolution that you run the game2.) Lack of common visual novel features-There's no pause or next for individual scenes that aren't dialogue of characters talking. If there's a scene of characters walking or a background you like in particular that you want to look at, you can't view it longer than the time it takes for the next character to begin speaking-No save feature for choices or to repeat branching sections. You can exit back to the main menu and continuing will reset you at the start of the scene. Perhaps when you finish the game there is a scene select, but no option to choose from what episode or point in the episode that you've already completed -Can't view previously said dialogue for characters said or for text messages in a scene in case you'd like to listen to it again or missed something specific. Text messages in particular don't allow you to scroll back up while texting and finishing the text messages will cause you to immediately exit regardless if on auto-text or manual. That may be another bug-No fast forwarding text, in fact depending on the scene occurring you'll be unable to skip at all while whatever action or individual line of dialogue the character is saying on screen. This is very inconsistent3.) Odd decisions -You don't need to pay attention to anything involving the music gameplay section aside from the middle notes that you input using arrow keys or whatever it may be on a controller. Every other portion of the screen like the WASD notes or QE prompts can be ignored completely without any loss to your success meter. Your success meter is also extremely easy to fill, so you're able to ignore most of the song without penalty and then hit the last few notes once you hear it starting to wind down to succeed. Failure doesn't offer much either since the song still plays and is sang well and while the characters listening may state that it's not as good as it could be, it's still worthwhile and pleasant. This is very apparent during the audition when I failed all the notes to see what would happen and was rewarded by being entered into the battle of the bands with barely any acknowledgement towards my mediocre performance-Characters don't really change their behaviors based on your attitude. I was curious what would happen if I was cold and distant with Fang to see if that had any impact on others willing to assist myself or the rest of the band. As it turns out it's very minimal. Granted, it's still early in the game at chapter 3 out of what I assume is 5, but for saying that choices matter with only small flavor text being provided early on doesn't feel genuine. I imagine if I were nicer to Naomi then maybe I wouldn't need to have Reed finally take his year book photo in exchange for my device to be fixed, but based on everything else it feels like that was scripted to happen regardless. -Pauses and some acting. For the most part, the cast do sound like awkward teenagers which is great and definitely fits the setting. Unfortunately, there's segments that a second take feels like it'd help a lot. Particularly Trish and some of the background characters when they talk. The quality sometimes rivals that of someone you'd found on fivver to do a quick line or two. In addition, the pauses for either jokes or the awkwardness of the situation to linger are too long and makes it seems as if a transition is about to occur before you find yourself being pulled back into the same scene. This could also be a bug since I've noticed the length varies widely and possibly could be loading the next portion of the scene. The other mini-game like clicking on fellow students in the assembly hall or finding your device under Fang's dirty bed are extremely basic and easy to skip entirely by accident by either backspacing or clicking on an option that also happens to be overlayed with such said device in question. The UI, for mouse and keyboard at least, is rather annoying to deal with too when going through settings and photographs of moments since the mouse movement controls where the screen moves across the options while scrolling does as well.Overall disappointed with what I've experienced so far and will be refunding. Perhaps when on sale and patched further I'll consider picking it up again, but $30 for a visual novel that's been in production for four years releasing in this current state is far beyond what is acceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: I have anticipated this game since the moment I saw it and have been listening to the music on repeat as it released so trust me when I say this one is a difficult one to write.::The good::The voice acting is great. The writing for dialogue is also pretty darn good, and comparatively much better to other VN type experiences I've played. The whole story feels very immersive and I was completely lost in it while playing it all in one sitting. The representation is great and not ham-fisted. Very accurately emulated present day social media. The build-up and pacing is also very well done for a 5-6 hour experience. The visuals are wonderful. Whoever was illustrating the scenery and interiors went absolutely wild on them. And the music ! Finally got to play and hear the tracks I've been listening to all this time and they were so good. Absolute highlights of the game.::The not so good::~ Technical ~For a game that consists entirely of animated sequences and VN style choices it felt kind of jittery. Sometimes it felt almost as if the game was buffering between the delivery of lines, leaving odd pauses between the delivery and kind of throwing of the flow of things. Sometimes lines would skip automatically without any input being pressed.The animations sometimes also felt kind of buggy with some things occasionally not loading in at the same time as everything else or looking kind of laggy.The lip syncing during musical segments was pretty good but didn't seem like the same level of care was put into it outside of those segments.Seems like it was just missing that final level of polish in the general feel/flow of things.~ Mechanics ~At times the rhythm game didn't feel super responsive or the most sync'd with the music. Could have been a latency issue? It also felt like juggling moreso than a lot of other rhythm games. There is two different mechanics in the game you have to tend to at the same time which is 1. quite difficult, even for myself who lives on rhythm games. and 2. sort of takes away from feeling intertwined with the music. I was kind of hoping to be able to get into the zone and vibe along with the music a bit more but it really did require 100% of your concentration juggling these two elements haphazardly. This is also important to note as some of the most important montages of the game occur behind the rhythm game UI which is almost unwatchable as the game demands 100% of your attention if you don't want to mess it up. I had to ask my friend who was watching me play what happened during the final montage (and if I want to try see it again I have to play the entire game again).The game also lacks the ability to replay segments or even have save slots which shoots replayability in the foot quite a bit. Committing to playing the game all over again just to go down a different path with a character is too much of a time commitment, especially when there's no going back if you pick the wrong option and end up in the wrong branch.~Narrative design stuff ~Feels like there could have been a few more solo heart-to-hearts with the main characters of the game. I haven't replayed it to go get closer with other characters yet, but so far with the characters I was close to there was still so much I wanted to hear them speak their mind about and open up to me about. Like we are all about to die maybe? Please tell me what's on your mind! It felt like the final pivot heart-to-heart/piece of exposition you get at max character affinity wasn't quite there.And finally . I can say with certainty that I would have look past all the other shortcomings and would have written this as a recommendation if more care had been put into the conclusion of this story. Unfortunately with this huge build up it creates throughout the game, it kind of drops the ball on it at the end. The ending isn't as abrupt as some other narrative focused indie titles that released this year, but it does still feel a little out of the blue. It was a bit of an "oh" moment when the credits rolled. Its not a bad game. It is abundantly apparent how much love and effort has been put into this by an indie team with looming delivery dates and expectations to live up to. And I want to give this the thumbs up especially since there seems to be a clear co-ordinated effort to talk badly about it right now. But the end just made me feel kinda hollow and its hard to come to terms with that just being how it ends after all the anticipation.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:>I liked the art style, the characters generally looked good (except when they face forward, then they can look a bit weird). Some of the backgrounds were genuinely pretty>The songs were very competently done, they were great to listen to>I loved the L&L segments, they were cute and funny>I did genuinely like Fang, Naser and Sage as charactersNegatives:>Pacing - there were some significant issues with pacing, namely that it was a bit all over the place. The game starts off at a glacial pace with next to nothing happening for hours, but once the pace picks up, everything goes by at a million miles an hour, with everything and the kitchen sink being violently squished into as short of a timeframe as possible, followed by the whole thing coming to sudden screeching halt. Not ideal.>Storyline - setting aside some obvious issues  , the storyline didn't make too much sense to me. It started off with Fang being a little overbearing when it comes to following her passion, trying to go pro with her band, which Trish isn't overly pleased about - it seems to be heading towards a 'moral of the story' type situation in which Fang learns to be more considerate of her friends' needs... but then by the end, all of that is simply thrown away and everyone ends up doing what Fang wants anyway, rendering literally everything that happened before that moment pointless. I'm not really sure what the devs were going for with this one, if I'm honest.>Sometimes certain characters will behave in psychologically impossible ways, which ruins any immersion to be had - Trish spends most of the game avoiding Fang and voicing her displeasure with constantly having gone along with whatever Fang wanted, leaving her with no time to pursue her own hobbies and interests, but then at the end she suddenly does a complete 180 and is perfectly happy to go along with what Fang wants. What...? Why? It makes no sense. >The ending itself is horribly unsatisfying - it happens very suddenly once the storyline finally starts going somewhere, leaving me unsatisfied, like 'oh... that's it?'. Ultimately, nothing is resolved  which is extremely unsatisfying>Choices - something that genuinely frustrated me was that sometimes the game gives you certain options, but when you try to select them, the game simply doesn't allow you. What the hell? If I'm just going to be forced to play the game in whichever way the devs personally want, then why bother even giving me these options that aren't actually options?! This is not good game design. Similarly, sometimes I am literally given a singular option - what's the point of that? Why not just have the characters advance the storyline/dialogue/whatever without any input from me, if I don't have any actual choice in what happens next? I genuinely hate this mechanic. Speaking of choices, the fact that you only get one romance option in the game is a bit disappointing - I'd like to think that when a romance mechanic is implemented in a game, you'd get more than one option for who to choose in the end >Characters - most of the characters were very one dimensional, just having a single thing to distinguish them in any way (e.g. Stella does tarot, Trish likes insects, Reed likes L&L, etc.); no interesting backstories, no real personalities beyond having that singular interest and/or being neurotic beyond belief, often barely reacting to what's going on around them, all speaking like 20-something year old tumblr addicts, which can get grating sometimes. I found it difficult to get invested in most of the characters and care about what happens to them at all, which is unfortunate.>The rhythm game segments were annoying - you don't press buttons in a way that would match up to the track, you just randomly mash whatever buttons appear on screen with no rhyme or reason, which often come with sound effects that don't match the track either and ruin the sound. It's doubly annoying that sometimes there are things worth looking at going on in the background (such as the endgame memory montage), but there is seemingly no way to view them outside of those segments>'Generous timing' mode (or whatever it's called) is anything but - if you stink at rhythm games like I do, or otherwise like to think through your options a bit (turning off auto advance doesn't always work), then you're still going to end up with nowhere near enough time to react quickly enough to whatever's going on. Sometimes it felt as though that option was non-functional - I toggled it on, but nothing seemed to change>Bugs - ignoring any visual bugs (I've seen much worse in other games), sometimes the game would randomly freeze - I would push the button to advance dialogue, but nothing happened. I had to restart a few times because of this. Sometimes dialogue would get skipped altogether for no apparent reason, or voice lines would cut out. I also noticed that my settings didn't get saved, so when I restarted I had to change my settings againAll in all, I'm rather disappointed - I think there was a lot of potential for this game to be genuinely good, with a cast of complex, relatable characters and a good storyline... but it was let down by terrible pacing, having no actual choice, a confused storyline and dull, one-dimensional characters.I really wanted to like this game, but it fell short on so many things, I could not in good conscience recommend it to anyone, especially not at the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay but... just generally mediocre and disappointing. :\Some spoilers below so beware.The character development, writing and sequence of events were kind of off for about 70% of the game from the start. It is only when you reach the last couple of episodes is when the writing improves, the characters and their bonds develop a lot more and things get more interesting.I'm not sure but I believe most of your dialogue choices don't matter save for a handful. It's really weird that a visual novel does not have impactful choices throughout its story. There's even times where you want to choose a dialogue option but they do this whole effect thing around it that forces you to not be able to choose. I guess because they want to show the character hesitating to say a specific thing... I get the idea but I think the execution was weird and kinda dramatic in a dumb way.Another big gripe for me is the music QTE's: You literally cannot fail them. I played through this game and intentionally tried to fail the music QTE's just to see what would happen... and nothing. You progress normally. I see literally no reason to include QTE's if they're not engaging, not fun and if you cannot even fail them in the first place. Just why?The ending was definitely emotional, but it's quite a generic ending nonetheless and they missed out on the opportunity to make it a bit dark by showing the meteor or its impact. Not trying to sound sadistic or anything like that, but they designed this whole game around the inspiration of the dinosaurs and the meteor that caused their extinction... but they copped out on that and made the ending ambiguous. I was secretly looking forward to that. :P Oh, and yes there's literally only one ending. One.The artstyle... I'm not sure. At times I'm okay with it and others I'm just weirded out by it. I can't come up with an opinion for it... just something isn't right. Maybe I just don't have something for anthropomorphic animals. I don't think it's bad in-general though. :o I also always liked the little doodle-y style when you're zoomed out on some of the scenes, it was kind of cute!I know I'm being a bit critical here, but I will say there are actually some good parts in the game. The music is great and I do love some tracks from Worm Drama. I also really did like the last couple of episodes and how things developed. It really fleshed out the characters and the writing was pretty good. I enjoyed them!However... that's really it. It's hard for me to come up with plenty of good things to say. I think there are many visual novels that are worth more, both in time and money. It's certainly not worth 30$. No, I won't really talk about the other game everyone is talking about since it's not relevant to this one in my opinion.If you do like this game, power to you and I fully respect that. I just feel really disappointed since I actually was waiting for the game. I wanted to play it as a joke and for a bet with friends, but I secretly also wanted it to be really cool and interesting... that wasn't the case unfortunately.If you want to get it, my advice is to wait for a big sale. If it were up to me, I'd price this 5$ tops.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I am sober, it hurts to say this but I am not satisfied with the game. First of all, 1 play through is about 5 hours. With achievement hunting it could be double or triple that, but for a base price of basically $30 usd is a little steep. To add in my impression that this game's content is more of a kinetic novel than a visual novel, even more so. I like the characters, the music, voice acting (even if its a little awkward and choppy at times), and most importantly the story. However, as a game I wish there was more to it. The 2 main systems, affinity and rhythm game, do not impact the story and/or needs more work. To start, affinity might as well be non-existent since the ending is pretty much the same and choices pretty much only affect what scenes you see. The poorly implemented rhythm game feels like a watered down version of a description of OSU. Not only that, doing good or bad does absolutely nothing for the plot. I know very well I missed about 80% of the notes and yet still come out as victorious? I am now wondering, if I do another run, what changes if I dont hit any keys at all during music segments. Art is subjective so I won't go in on that, but my biggest issue is the ending. Personally, I do not like endings to be well...open ended. Yes, one could say that its an artistic choice to have it that way but I have taken quite a few art classes so I know a poor excuse when I see one. I genuinely feel its a cop out to have the ending like this considering the lack of player content. At least give me an ending so I can have some form of closure. I really want to feel ok about recommending this game to my friends, but I just cannot. Again, there are things I do genuinely like about this game and its sad to have them overshadowed by current flaws. Hell, for a game marketed as a visual novel why is there no option to save progress? I will not ask for my money back. Just know that me paying the basically $30 usd was a form of trust and now I feel disappointed and betrayed. My lesson is learned.

_childDocuments_.user: Phil Swift, He Who Mends All
_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRIf you like pretty pictures, nice music, and cute characters doing cute things without caring much of the narrative behind it, you'll probably like this game. If you care at all about following a cohesive narrative and exploring a world and the characters that live in it, you will probably not like this game.SPOILERS WILL BE AHEAD. READ AT YOUR OWN DISCRETION.The Good -The backgrounds and a lot of the non-animated art assets range from great to downright spectacular. Most of the music is good, if a bit repetitive at times. The romance between  is adorable for the most part. The social media sideshow stuff is pretty funny, even if a decent chunk of it is just copying and pasting other viral tweets. The rhythm segments are decent and the other mini-games are serviceable. The Bad -Character animations are often too stiff or, paradoxically too floaty. Voice acting leaves a lot to be desired for some characters, especially the main character. There are occasional visual bugs with the characters and backgrounds and audio bugs with voice lines. The Ugly -The writing. Almost all of it is some combination of complete nonsense, directly contradictory with itself, pointless, or woefully underdeveloped. The setting and world are not thought through in the slightest. An asteroid with an "electromagnetic atmosphere" (this is not a thing) is disrupting cell towers and power stations (the amount of radiation needed to penetrate the Earth's atmosphere to cause this would sterilize the planet instantly) right before it is discovered eight months before impact (this would be approximately 250 million miles away). All of civilization, despite starting down imminent and complete annihilation, continues to run smoothly up to and during the end, minus the occasional interruption of utility services. Nobody really seems to care that the world is ending, and they would rather spend their final moments watching some up-and-coming high school band live out their dream of being famous instead of doing literally anything else with anyone else. The asteroid, despite being a constant and very literal threat, is only spoken of as an abstract 'bad thing' by pretty much everyone (except for Naomi during a single scene), and only makes itself known when the plot wants to do something 'cool', like turn the lights off so Fang can do a solo. The narrative's pacing is mindboggling. The first quarter of the game takes place during the first two or three weeks of school (September), and then it skips straight to April for the rest of the game with literally nothing in between, stuffing the last three quarters into the space of a month or so. None of the conflicts or plot threads that are alluded to or started in those first couple of chapters are developed in the interim, so it's essentially a seven month void of time where nothing happens, and everything picks up where it left off in September. Despite giving themselves an entire eight months to work with, they decide to only use a around six or seven weeks of that time, and despite only giving themselves this much time, they pad out the runtime of the game with a tabletop gaming subplot that has no bearing on the story and serves zero purpose. It is not used as a medium to develop characters, ferment conflicts, or otherwise advance the plot, and is pure spectacle. It's very nice spectacle, but it's spectacle nonetheless, and it feels like the developers had a cool idea for an epic thing and didn't care if it ran in parallel to the story instead of intertwining with it. Choices rarely matter, and when they do it's usually only for a single scene before putting you back on the railroad. At no point is there a culmination of your choices to decide some final section of the game; it is always the same, minus a few minor details like Fang's outfit. Even the main romance, one of the more focused-on plot threads of the game, is decided by a single choice near the end, and no matter how dismissive and rude you are to , you will always be allowed to choose to be "more than friends" with them. The game's main message of not trying to push people into sacrificing their dreams for yours is completely thrown into the garbage at the ending, when every single character comes together to follow Fang's dreams. There is a ton of friction - mainly between Trish and Fang - about the nature of the band they play in and what Trish actually wants to do with the time she has left, but she ends up going along with all of Fang's desires to audition whenever they want, and then play at Battle of the Bands and Caldera Fest anyway, despite saying multiple times that she won't do it and that she wants to spend time doing other things. The game's romance plot is all over the place. I did say earlier that I thought it was adorable, and it is - on the surface. It starts with an out-of-the-blue text from an unknown number confessing a crush right after the news of the asteroid is revealed. There is a seven month void of time as described earlier, and this mystery texter is still anonymously texting Fang, and only offering to meet in person at Battle of the Bands. Fang is chided for "making Naomi wait" and not paying attention to the signs that were supposedly there the entire time. Naser comments that Naomi "isn't exactly subtle" yet there was apparently no offer to meet in person during that seven month time skip mentioned earlier. It's bizarre that Naomi plays that game for that long, and even more bizarre that Fang goes along with it for that long. If there was some sort of deeper reason for Fang to be so obsessed with a mystery texter it could have worked, but nobody brings it up except once right before the Battle of the Bands. The individual characters are pretty bland and uninspiring, and their interactions leave a lot to be desired. They usually stick to one gimmicky trait that defines them, and are either poorly explored or not explored at all. Sage likes cooking, Stella likes tarot, Rosa likes plants, Reed likes tabletop. Trish and Naomi are a bit better, but they don't really have character arcs to speak of. Trish ends where she starts - playing in Fang's band, despite the entire story suggesting she wanted to step away from it. Naomi is a massive dork which is kind of cute, although the game leans very heavily into all the dorky things she does. The largest sin this game's narrative has is that Fang is not a character in a setting, Fang IS the setting. Every single character and the world itself bends to suit Fang's needs. There is no reason for society to continue functioning up until the day of Caldera Fest. There is no reason for Trish and Reed to spend some of their final months, days and minutes supporting Fang's desires to the bitter end when they themselves don't care much for it to begin with except for in the best of circumstances. There is no reason for thousands of people to turn out to a concert at the end of the world instead of spending time with their loved ones, and there is no reason for such a venue to even be functioning at that point, hacked together or otherwise. There is no reason for Naomi's weird stalker texting to successfully woo Fang, and if anything it should turn them off completely from that level of spergdom. There is no reason for any of this to happen if you assume that characters have their own independent thoughts and desires, but if every character is a set-piece that exists to supplement Fang's world, it starts to make more sense, and essentially makes Fang a Mary Sue. Except worse, because even Mary Sue's need to follow  rules that the world lays out. Not Fang. TL;DR;DR: Every single swing KO_OP took at making a compelling narrative was a complete miss. It took them three years to write this mess. All they have to provoke any feeling is some heartstring pulling when the pretty characters get obliterated by a meteor.

_childDocuments_.review: To those who haven't got a clue what's going on, Snoot Game was made after GVH was revealed but before it was released - Snoot was initially a whole anti-trans thing by some 4channers that became a full parody game under the dev name Cavemanon. GVH was released by KO_OP after Snoot. Wani was released by Cavemanon after that, as a standalone they could sell. I played Wani before knowing any of this, then Snoot, then GVH. Here's my rundown.Not knowing any of the drama while playing I Wani Hug That Gator, I didn't really get the feel that it was anti-trans. There was a lack of any queer characters or mentions, but it wasn't out of place, as it's a pretty focused story about art, disability, and the right way to support those you love. Wani is one of the most relatable things I've ever read, and has affected my life even more than Night In The Woods. I cannot recommend that game enough.Most of the beef is about Snoot. Snoot Game is definitely anti-trans. This mainly manifests in Fang being extremely hostile about misgendering in initial scenes, then falling into some odd, mostly swept under the rug "they're just confused" arc and changing back to female pronouns. I've heard that some of the original writing was much more troublesome, but was dialed back by the others on the Cavemanon team, and any anti-queer sentiment seemed to have been squashed by the time writing started for Wani. Most likely, others on the team were much less vitriolic, and a shift in the fanbase to include a lot more trans furries put pressure to can the 4chan brand hate, as Wani was their own IP they could sell and money could be lost by alienating fans. As for the game itself, it's worth a slog through if you're willing to put up with the edgier 4channer thought processes of the main character. More worth it if you're from that side of the internet. Under the gunk, there's actually a solid story about realizing there's people around you, going through things just the same as you. If only the anti-trans elements of Cavemanon fully understood that for themselves...As for GVH, There's a couple odd plotholes, but the story and characters were gripping enough to keep me fully engaged for the straight 6 hours it took to play... and left me with a pretty big hole in my chest. This game is a metaphor for  and nailed the feeling of uncertainty and doom one feels not only about graduating high school, but also jumping right into the age of the aforementioned metaphor afterwards. There's inspiration, love, and a pit of pain to be found in this story, and it does tell it really well through the moments the characters have with each other. Nearly every scene has its part to play in showing you how the characters are feeling and dealing with the change around them. However, there WAS a change in writers that you can feel in a few parts of the story - those aforementioned plotholes. It's not enough to throw the story off its tracks, but it does mess with the pacing a bit. The tracks are total bangers, and the action of the music minigame reflects that feel. The animations and voicelines are usually great, but do suffer a bit of QA oversight every once in a while. The UI is smooth and nice to look at, and I'm a fan of being able to see your relationships at a quick glance. The people at KO_OP did great work with this one, and I highly recommend it... but probably on a sale, as it is pretty short.When it comes to the split in communities, there's good and bad in both. I've plodded around the different discords, and there's a lot of bad blood there, as the particularly hateful types from Cavemanon's fanbase have raided anything and everything KO_OP numerous times. It's gotten to the point that any mention of- or indication that you're into- either Wani or Snoot will get you straight up attacked and likely banned on the KO_OP discord. I can understand being on edge after some heavy 4chan raiding, but some chilling the hell out is in order, especially when one joins the server just looking for fanfics and gets freaked out at over a profile banner. There's a couple good fics to get recommended on the KO_OP discord, some good fan art and a neat tarot card bot, but otherwise not much substantial happening over there. Mostly just people fangirling over the characters, sometimes a good convo or real talk starts up.As for the Snoot Club discord, there's a total mess of 4channers throwing dung in the general chats, just avoid those unless that's your cup of tea. There's a pretty good selection of fanfics and a few fanmade games/mods to get recommended, pretty killer fan art and more chill conversations in the production chats, as of the time of this writing. Worth a check if you're desperate for story continuations or copefics after reading Snoot or Wani.I can't recommend stepping too far into either community unless you're really needing some extra fan content. TL;DR, It's a fustercluck of racist and transphobic 4channers pissing off a bunch of quick to anger queer kids who don't know that the only way to win against a troll is to block and not engage. Even lurkers like me get sucked into the drama. My advice: enjoy the games, move on if you can, dig for fics if you can't.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sure is something.As of right now, I've only played through the first 3 chapters and it's been... an experience.I went into it already knowing quite a bit about the game and a lot of behind the scenes stuff surrounding it, so my expectations weren't big, yet I was still kind of disappointed. I've been trying to believe in the devs to polish the game out and give them a chance but this is not it, to be fair.I've read through a couple of reviews here already and I see a lot of them talking about technical issues, controversial stuff mostly, including the "fan"game, but here I want to focus on the story and how it is presented so far. There will be spoilers, in case you care.I haven't seen the whole story yet, obviously, but I think I've seen enough to give a common evaluation. Overall, the story and theme consistency have been decent so far, but I cannot say that for the general plot. Going through the story feels awful and really confusing. That is because this game has a really bad habit of having no transitions between scenes and chapters AT ALL. Don't get me wrong, sometimes going from one scene to another without a transition suddenly can be good, but when transitions are not present at all, is when it becomes a problem. And I'm not talking about just visual transitions, but the more subtle ones as well. For example, a lot of times we see one scene happen with a mini plot that plays out for like 5 minutes and then it just moves on suddenly. Without any kind of transition or anything. The game took "show, don't tell" a little too seriously. There is like, barely any telling. There shouldn't be a lot, obviously, but there still should be at least a little bit. All of the scenes in this game are treated as short stories just barely connected together to form a plot. You move on from one dialogue with one group of people, to another without ANY EXPLANATION.There is no visible goal in the game. One scene ends abruptly and another begins. Nothing was set up for the new scene in the previous one, it just began and now it's happening. What the hell is going on? Can someone tell me please? It would be great to have Fang, at the end of a scene say "Hey. I should do X now and talk to N." And then the next scene in question begins and they do exactly that. But that never happens. The plot just moves on seemingly with no goal between very disconnected scenes. It feels like a slice of life mini-comic or a 4koma, except it tries to be a connected plot, failing miserably. Multiply all of that by like 3 because of technical issues like lip syncing and janky, obviously repeating animations that completely take you out of an otherwise pretty fun world.Now, to the characters. The only ones I kinda at least a little bit feel something towards are the main group, which technically is great! You want your players to like the main characters, but the secondary characters all feel very weird and frankly out of place or really supportive, without a spine of their own. One exception for that is Naser, who feels like a foil to Fang and honestly their clashes as siblings with two opposing mindsets are pretty entertaining so far and make for an actual story between them. So far the only thing I'm genuinely interested in seeing play out in the future, along with the whole asteroid thing. Naomi is trying to be an important character, who is obviously Fang's mysterious and secret admirer. At the end of chapter 3 it's been pretty much confirmed with the cutscene, but there are some hints dropped before. Now, that might be a red herring, which I hope it is, because this "mystery" already performed a whole summersault into absolutely evaporating itself.Let's talk about this "mystery" then? My biggest gripe with the story so far. This is set up in the very beginning of the game and to be frank, the setup was pretty good, but not what follows. Before the game I've only played the PC demo which featured the setup for this mystery, and honestly, it was the only hook for me from the demo. The complete and utter suicide of this mystery, however, is insanely disappointing. The secret admirer is openly setup, with giving the player an opportunity to form an opinion on together with Fang immediately. You can choose to ignore this stranger and move on, or reply and be excited to your friends about it, or any other combination of the options. The next time the game re-introduces this stranger, however, the player is not given a choice and Fang just replies to them. Not only that, but they completely warm up to the stranger like immediately and start sharing personal feelings and talking to them like an old friend and... that's just completely stupid objectively and an out of character thing for Fang to do. They start sending the stranger hearts, venting and stuff. From my experience with stories, stuff like this is usually explained by the main character "being bored" or "whatever" but here even that is not present! The player is not given a choice as to whether Fang talks to the stranger or not, they just do. And they always form a bond. And no, it's not impacted by how you immediately reacted to them. Then, in the ending of the next chapter, the stranger is very clearly revealed (they try to be subtle with it but... anyone with a pair of eyes will get it). I don't know how this plays out further, but I can't imagine it being worse than it already is, or getting any better.A little filler section about the D&D parts of the game. Or how they call it in this universe, L&L (I can't remember off the top of my head what it exactly stands for, but I think it's Lizards and Loot)? I'm quite into D&D myself and once it got mentioned I couldn't wait for the actual gameplay to see and judge it. Well anyway, the sections are actually pretty good. Way better than the actual game, honestly. The one bad thing about them is that Nerd from the Boyfriends webtoon looking ass character. Thankfully he's not a recurring character in the actual plot, at least not so far... He is really annoying and, uh... Preppy. Wonder if that was an actual inspiration because WOW they are similar. Don't ask me how I know. But other than that, I guess there isn't a lot to say, but these D&D sections are kinda a highlight of the game and funnily enough usually happen at the tail end of a chapter, sort of as a reward for going through all of THAT.As for the themes, the game chooses a very safe route and goes for a theme that is very relatable to it's target audience. The whole growth and change thing, anxiety and pressure from the last year of school thing, overall the whole coming of age stuff and whatnot. Due to my personal circumstances the theme is really close to me and the release date for the game is actually quite humorous considering everything. I'd say it nails the theme pretty good but it's a pretty easy theme that is overdone a lot, done through and tested, especially in settings like this, so personally I don't see it as much of an accomplishment. Especially considering how the whole plot and story actually play out... really just makes it worse and downplays the theme.Overall I think the actual story is quite decent and worth experiencing, but not for the price of 30$. I myself am pretty torn with my opinion on this game, but I cannot in good faith really recommend this game to anyone.-A little update since I've played through the entirety of the story now.To me it feels obvious that they've put everything into the ending, it was actually pretty good. I also stated that Naomi was sort of a nothing character but I think she kinda redeemed herself in last like hour of the game, but I still wish she got more screentime. And that's kinda what it sums up to: the game was extremely slow, yet didn't take enough time with the story and characters. A lot of the sections were really about nothing or just Fang.

_childDocuments_.review: "Is this game good?" Sure, it is a lot of fun. The story is really nice and I had a good time."Is the VA any good?" Nothing to say about it, it is clearly good. Even if the big space between dialogues ruin the immersion, the voice acting itself is pretty good, not gonna lie!"How's the music?" It's amazing! I can highly say that it carries the entire game by its own. "Was it worth it?" Now, I don't think so. For 30 bucks, this game is really expensive for a 8 hours long game, when all you have to do is pick a choice and do some rock band from time to time. The lack of multiple ending and of impactful choices really makes the game unpolished. It's like asking for some cookies, and the chef only gives you the dough. Like, of course it's good, but that is certainly not what you asked, especially if you paid a lot for it. Some people say that Snoot game or I Wani Hug That Gator are much more compelling and better visual novels. It really depends on people's perspective, but I agree with them at some point. They both have multiple ending, a lot of character development and with some nice art on top of it!So, only buy this game on huge sales, like 50% off or something. Other than that, try Snoot game and I Wani Hug That Gator, two really good visual novels made by Cavemanon!Note : 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to give this game an honest chance going into it, but after having just completed it, I cannot ever imagine seriously recommending this to somebody. This is one of the least interactive games I've ever played - of the 5 hours I played, maybe one of them was actual gameplay, and the rest was cutscenes and dialogue. There's also a disgusting amount of padding in the form of the D&D campaigns the characters play - in which, for whatever reason, the developers decided to go into great detail. The rhythm game segments were decently fun, I'll give you that. But for the price this game is asking? Just go pick yourself up a real rhythm game, you'll spend less, have more fun, and definitely sink more time into it then the pitiful 5 hours this game has to offer you.

_childDocuments_.review: For context, I played Snoot Game first. It was a great time, seriously.It's a shame that it has to so viciously undercut what Goodbye Volcano High actually is though.  I can't speak for everyone's experiences with all those apparent lgbt+ things, I never got much of that in my playthrough, as though that would take away from anything.But I did very much get a story that runs parallel to things like Night in the Woods, just with different end points.  Where NITW tells you to hold on to anything at the end of everything, GVH says its ok when you reach that ending, to share your moment with the world in spite of that finality.The heart and soul on display in GVH is why videogames are an art form. Not everyone will draw the same conclusions from what they see, not everyone will value what it brings. But you're doing yourself a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disservice if you think the devs didn't pour everything they had into this experience. If you vibe with it, you'll fall in love like I did.The only thing I genuinely hate, is that it's over, and I won't get to see my friends again.  I miss them so much already. But what we had was beautiful and I'll cherish it forever.  Thank you KO_OP.

_childDocuments_.review: It's mid and inoffensive, honestly that's what I expected, but it is not worth $30. It should be $20 at most, but I dunno, it's just not that great nor terribly ♥♥♥♥.There's things I like, the backgrounds representing Volcadera Bluff are actually very nice and pleasant, sells the coastal town vibe very well. I did like a lot of the music, maybe it's just my all over the place taste in music, but I enjoyed it. And the D&D inspired sections have some of the best art direction in the game IMO.The voice acting is good, I didn't really have issues with anyone's performances, I dunno what else to say about that.Now for the spicy takes I think a lot of people that enjoyed the game will tune out I'm sure.There's much better story based games out there with good LGBT representation, if you're looking for it, that are far cheaper like, Night in the Woods, VA-11 Hall-A and maybe more I am forgetting I dunno.And if that's not why you're here and you want a more tightly written story that probably involves these characters or a similar setting, as generic as it sounds and I can hear some people groan and start typing a massive ♥♥♥♥♥ fit about it, play Snoot Game or the original option without the anit-fangame baggage, the I Wani Hug That Gator demo, here on Steam, by the same devs as Snoot Game. Honestly, the story starts off fine and then just kinda speeds up fast by the third act, like the devs desperately want get this over with, despite that, it feels way longer than it actually is with a lot of the tolkien #Relatable dialogue that so many writers nowadays feel the need to just, drop in here and there. Like the devs really didn't want to go on for to long either because they didn't have any confidence they could do a longer more tightly paced story or they were afraid whatever audience they were going for wouldn't have the attention span for it.I also got a problem with the choices or sometimes lack there of, they literally blatantly tell you to your face multiple times in the game with choices going static and graying out "No, no, no, you can only choose this choice and only this choice because ♥♥♥♥ player freedom". Like, if I want to be a complete edgy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ let me be one, it honestly comes off as smug and pretentious on the developer's part, like they're saying they know better than the player, at least TellTale and even David Cage games let you be a huge dickwad and not care.The rhythm game sections are...just boring. You can literally miss one or two notes and still get a 90% score or higher, its literally just for show. I get it, this is more about the story and such, but so is Night in the Woods, a similar story based game that I can tell influenced this game a bit here and there, except the rhythm game sections in that are an actual challenge and have a proper score system based on how well you do and you don't even need to do well to progress. My point being the challenge should be there for people that want it, I mean hell, they already got accessibility options, just make the mini game as it is now the one of those on by default and let people turn it off for a challenge, can even make achievements for it.The animation, hoo boy, it's kind of a mixed mess. The puppet rigs for the characters freak out often just spazzing for like a second really took out of the story the few times it happened. The lip syncing is, certainly not great, but not horrible either. Honestly despite the start of this paragraph, the animation is fine, it got the job done and from what I hear is leagues better thant whatever the ♥♥♥♥ was going on in the demos and especially the 2020 PS5 Showcase trailer, but I kinda expected less jank from 3 years of work.I overall don't think this game is awful nor do I think it's amazing like I'm sure Twitter addicts are all saying, it's just mid and not that memorable in sea of games just like it and to me that's a far worse fate than being so ♥♥♥♥ it's funny or just plain bad. Still I feel somewhat grateful for it birthing Snoot Game, even it was initially for spiteful means, that game did touch a lot of people emotionally, I know it did for me and it certainly helped advertise this game better than whatever KO-OP was doing for advertising. Truthfully, whatever KO-OP does next I have hope it's better and goes well for them, I can see beyond all the BS and see it's a team that really wants to make great art and I appreciate that, but man this just ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let's get to what the game does best first. The music, it is phenomenal. In fact, I was disappointed by the amount of times that I actually got to do the song writing and rhythm sections. You get to play about five songs throughout the story and each of them are down right amazing an fun to do. There were so many times when the story got choppy and I wished that I could just have Fang sit down and practice her music instead, but it unfortunately never really went that way.The animation was all around very good as well, there were some hiccups that I saw in the cut scenes, such as Fang having an extra thumb in one of the talks with Naser. But despite the small flaws you can nitpick out, you can really tell there was some love put into this game. Which is why it disheartens me so to write this next part of my review.The story. The main, integral part of this game, felt all over the place and confusing. At the start of the game, you are told that the scene you see is 8 months after the start of the real story. But then it feels so contradicted by the fact that scenes jump from one to the other, with no real sense of timing or pace. During my play-through I really tried to befriend and compromise with each character as best as I could, and yet, there were moments that felt random and disjointed. Some characters would be upset with my actions for no apparent reason, and it felt like scenes were cut from the final game that were necessary to tell the tale in it's entirety. I truly feel this game could have been so much better if the story line was just the slightest bit more sensical.Despite all this, I really did enjoy the game. It was a pleasant story that told the tale of a group of great friends, supporting each other through the toughest of times. And with this, a meteor is coming soon, and we're all going to die. So I'll say to everyone, Goodbye Volcano High.
