_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game on another level.The interactions between characters felt realistic and and the rhythm game segments felt like they had a lot of stake, and of course they did but I felt so tied into the story that if Fang lost, I lost.I also love how the game ends. (SPOILERS AHEAD) Once the story has reached its end everything gets put together, and you understand how they all grew as people and where they go from here. I really like how they didn't have a "big kaboom" in there too, it opens up possibility and really made me think. When I saw the credits I was shocked, (in a good way) because I was expecting some sort of sad farewell from them. Now, I don't even know if they died!!!! The teacher had said there was a chance it changed course, so I believe there is a possibility they survived. _childDocuments_.review: Emotionally powerful, well written, great game. A lot of care and love was put into the narrative and is a strong storyabout dealing with a potential catastrophe while navigating your queer series of friends as everyone struggles through it. As someone who went through the pandemic and felt a lot of this, it's hard not to relate to their struggles. The rhythm sections take a bit of getting used to but are very well handled. It's worth replaying, as well, to see what you didn't get to, so the game definitely earns a sense of replayability. The core story here is dealing with a lot, it's a rough ride emotionally if you've been alive the past four years and have a shred of humanity in you. If the themes are hard to deal with, skip, but otherwise, it's so great I cannot help but recommend it even if it can be hard on you emotionally.You'll see a lot of reviews here that are jokes or just dumb transphobes and homophobes trying to push their hate game, but this is something that is real and sincere and scares people who are terrified of the idea of opening themselves up a little bit. It's kind of funny in a pathetic way, and if you're one of those people, get a life, or go play AC6 you scrubs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definetely worthy of attention. But I will point out the major points for those who consider or doubting to buy this game:Story (7 out of 10)Story is about teenagers in front of their big life, their dreams and fears. Meaning, it's the usual teen drama. There's a dream of becoming a cool band, of wanted something more, of wanting to be accepted, of the fears of the end. The reason I give it 7 though is because the story is linear. It variates on background characters (if you see them or not), but overall, it's the only story and nothing will be changed in second and more playthrough. It's just my opinion, but I believe games like this should have at least two endings.Gameplay (7 out of 10)Mostly, i's like an anime. You just watch the story, occasionally pick answers in some scenes. These answers only affects how close you be to background characters and if you will see their story. Also, there's rhythm game segments during songs. Gameplay is not comlex, more like Visual Novels, but it still require your attention. If this game would've been longer than 8 hours, I would've give it 5 points, but game is short enough for not getting tired of such gameplay and actually allow you to relax during it. But, still, not much action and involvement of a player. Not best, but good enough.Music (10 out of 10)Music is always about taste and being subjective, but for me it was straight into heart! I loved it! It's calm, vocals are calming, instrumental goes through soul and give you so much vibe! All the people who were responsible for songand music part outdone themselves. I bow to each one of them, it was beyond perfect.Sound design (7 out of 10)The most conflicting part of the game for me. Voice actors did the bomb, Their voices made this game awesome. But sound designers kinda messed up in some places. Like, a lot. Always there's either cut of beggining of the sentence or it's ending, you literally hear how it was cut off. Also sound effect on voices, when someone was, for example, speaking on mic - background noise from the microphone is simply cut off. And it ruines the atmosphere. It's sad, especially, when vocie actors did great.Visual (8 out of 10)Another subjective thing, like every form of art. For me it was good. It's simple, eyes not tire from looking through it. Through every story I noticed only one fail - in club episode with blackout, when Fang played solo on acoustic guitar, in final frames they stay with electro guitar instead of acoustic =) Overall, good job, I won't scream like this is a masterpiece, but it's a job well done.To sum it up, even if I point out some cons, music won this game for me. I recommend to play this game to everyone, just because of music. Just try to read through story and admire art, it may catch your eyes more than mine. KO_OP studios, you did great, I definetely gonna look for your other projects. Good job, guys.

_childDocuments_.review: What a way to tell a story. This game had a lot to offer aesthetically, from both a visual and audio standpoint. Each track is mesmerizing and follows the theme of the narrative to a tee. In addition, there's a lot of detail to each character's design. Not only is the main cast beautiful to look at, but even each of the background characters have their own flavor to them. In general, the amount of detail in this game is astonishing. From the representation of LGBTQ+ to the realistic nature of the dialogue to the well-thought out scenarios for each high school character. It was fitting and charming. Much of the key moments in this narrative brought upon a plethora of emotions, showing you the real impact this game has.I unfortunately have one complaint and it is the bugs. On a technical level, these bugs can hinder your overall experience a bit. Random dialogue lines are skipped and I even encountered a major glitch in the rhythm game in probably one of the most impactful scenes. I'm sure they can be patched, but that's the current state of it.TLDR: Snooty gay dinos coming of age with great music and i love them

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone, YaOldBuddy here with a review on the game Goodbye Volcano High. Goodbye Volcano High is one of those games that show me why i love story games and when choices are around, how impacting they can be. They'll allow us to choose what we we want and how we feel about situations and GVH is exactly that. It felt nice feeling like you are apart of the story in a way but the way you choose the options, you choose it for the main character called "Fang". You get to see so many different sides of how the story could potentially go and makes you eager to know them.- The Story is pretty well made, nothing feels too cheesy and the story is willing to give you a good time and gets you into the mood of how the situations end up being.- None of the character comes off as too annoying or act like they aren't fitting to the story or the cast overall, they were all pretty well put together to be apart of a cast.- The Artstyle, the enviornment and the scenebuilding overall are wonderful. I cannot express how many times while listening during the story, i tried to look around as much as i could to find small details or simply watch how beautiful the enviornment was or how well drawn everything was. It is impressive how much work KO_OP's team put into this.- The Gameplay is put very well (of course recommended more with controller). The decisions didn't seem bad and quite fits to the decisions you would have to make inside the game. As for the Rhythm gameplay... You have to press alot of buttons and use the joysticks at the right moment like you were hitting the drums, that gameplay felt very smooth but can be abit confusing at first. Either way loved it!With pros, there are of course a few cons. Though they have not been too impactful for the gameplay and the story.- Whenever a character gets to a next position, it kinda snaps to a next position which i found abit odd and sort of uncomfortable.- (Not sure if intentional) The mouth movement of the characters is sometimes abit too slow and doesn't catch up all too much with the dialogue.My Personal opinion to this game is going to be as following: The game deserves the money as funding with all the work the team being KO-OP has put into it. It was a meaningful story, alot of attention to detail and overall the characters, environments and the emotions that wakes up within you. (A little overdramatic from my sides but i dont care, i love this game!)One thing i loved about this as well is that the game wasn't afraid to show it's nature sometimes and kinda also the reality of situations. They've shown how people would act even through a dire situation. People would still be meming around, paranoid or still acting like themselves, just like the internet would. Another part of the game is the LGBT-Q like aspect. If you don't like that part, it's too bad. I love how the game really loves to support the groups and allows you to hear it from their side and i support it. No one should worry about who they really should be.This was my review on Goodbye Volcano High and my last words will be: This was a pleasent experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second of this game & cried twice. 10/10. This is on par with The World Ends With You & Night In The Woods (My two favorite games) IMO. I fell in love with the characters, soundtrack, and everything when I started playing it, and I decided to 100% complete itSure there's only one ending, but the game makes up for it with a lot of different conditional scenes. It's absolutely not an issue like some people will make it seem.For example, as you progress, certain choices raise your affinity with Fang's friend group, and it all culminates into the beach conversations at the end of the game. During the D&D portions, your rolls also change the outcome of them.I liked how the game handled topics like transitioning, preferred names, and family acceptance as it hits very close to home with me, especially Rosa's beach conversation (which i linked earlier), where she talks about how her family is handling her transition, which is adjacent to how things are with my mom's side of the family and me. The way Reed uses his D&D sessions with his friends as a way to distract himself from his insecurities was pretty neat too.The voice acting is a little spotty in places near the beginning of the game, but otherwise it's great, and they got some AMAZING VAs for it.PLEASE play this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have major expectations going into the game since it was hard to get a read on it, but I liked the character design and general art style. The demo didn't grab me, though I still wanted to give the full game a shot.The phrase "this is competing with Pizza Tower for my game of the year" probably sounds nuts. That's where I'm at with this game after blitzing through it on release, the character writing really resonated with me and it's been stuck on my mind since finishing it.This is very much a straightforward coming-of-age drama with an eccentric twist for the sake of an overarching metaphor, and you're probably on board with that or you're not. Even if the offbeat art style and heavy focus on queer characters isn't your thing, you might still get something out of this if you enjoy media about the messy struggles of becoming an adult.Aesthetically, this is a really impressive production with an animation system similar to those in western RPGs, with characters blending between combinations of pose and expression sets. While it can lead to some janky moments and rough state transitions, it allowed the devs to get really ambitious with the story scope while having full animation (outside of a few D&D parody bits) for the characters. The top-notch music and voice acting do a lot to flatter the presentation as a whole.What I think will be more divisive than the art direction is the commitment to putting you in the main character, Fang's, head when making dialogue response choices. Options can take on funky effects to convey the mood of the response, some might disappear completely if Fang changes their mind mid-thought stream, or require an extra set of button presses when it's something hard for them to say.Sometimes, when Fang is in very emotional situations, none of your choices for dialogue will be what you would want to say, because you're restricted to Fang's mental perspective. Some players won't be a fan of moments like these, but those limitations help to illustrate the main character's flaws and limitations as a person.The choices made over the story mostly manifest in the conversations available near the end. There's not a lot of room for affecting the main events of the story, though the ending hours hit so hard that I don't mind the lack of variance.Despite the weird atmosphere around the game's release, and the lack of many release day reviews, I do truly hope more people give it a chance. I was really, really impressed with the writing and presentation. These characters and this story are likely going to stick with me for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, perhaps more than I should. The characters resonated with me and I enjoyed their company. I would love to be able to spend more time with them. I really enjoyed the story that we got. They left me, the audience, wanting more, so I say good job to the team who brought this together. Additional props to the voice actors. I thought they all performed excellently.But I won't lie to anyone here. This isn't much of a "game." It's more of an animated narrative experience with the facade of a game built around it. All the "game" elements are completely superficial. Personally I would rather see this story done as an animated mini-series because all the "game" stuff didn't really add much to the experience for me. The rhythm game sections were fun, but if you can completely fail them and not affect the story in any meaningful way, then I don't know what else to call them other than superficial. Why engage the player if it isn't going to matter? Is that some meta-narrative thing? If so, I don't buy it. Personally I wish the devs kept this bun in the oven longer and used the time to make a better game experience because they nailed all the other aspects of this product.I would recommend this game to people who are just looking for a good story and maybe a casual gaming experience at most. I'd put this game up there with Night in the Woods and Beacon Pines.Also the soundtrack that you can buy separate from the game holds up if you liked the music from this game. It's a welcome addition to my playlist.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that the only reason I wanted to play this was because I loved Snoot Game. I know the two are unrelated but that's what got me here.Goodbye Volcano High is not a bad game. I did enjoy my time playing the game. It was a fun, unique experience. The music  was nice. The game touches some heavy subjects and handles them decently. I will say that the replay value is not there for it as much as it is with Snoot Game (since it has different endings, bonus chapters, and a secret bonus scene/picture)---Potential Spoiler Warning----Positives-I like the direction for Fang's voice.-Characters are enjoyable. Even Sage to an extent.-Fang.-Customizing the band logo and posters was a neat touch. -Nice music. Decent jams that are changed depending on lyric choices. I like that, that's cool.-I like seeing the schools, and the Lava Java. The jungle/tropical feel was great.-The conversations feel somewhat natural for their age.-I will say the RPG sections were a bit silly, but had a nice flavor to them. The Dinogang -Sage, Stella, Rosa- really need to shut the F up though. Reed is best DM.-Nice dino desgins, but could use some work. Naser does look a bit silly with his hair. Just leave it bare scales if you're gonna go that route.- (Spoiler) The ambiguous ending is a nice touch, despite the fact I'm left unsatisfied. It leaves room for a sequel if they decide upon it. If they do they need to make it longer for sure.-It's an lgbt game that doesn't lean to heavily on the fact that it has lgbt characters or interactions.-I like the world exploring. Needs more of it though.Negatives-What really goes against this game is the length. It's too short. I feel like certain characters of the Dinogang really didn't have time to shine.-There are some story contradictions.-They have wings but I have you rarely see them fly/use them during the game. -The music the ban plays is nice but it doesn't feel Battle of the Bands level of winning.-The choices don't really matter in the end friendship pervails in the end regardless. They do have effect on the flavor and certain events of the story, but the train chugs along nonetheless. This could be dont on purpose as that is a certain aspect of the story. Storywise it makes sense. Gameplay wise it is unsatisfactory.-The ending is ambiguous, which is fine, but there should definitely be a better ending, or a nice little extra scene if you get all the friendship points. If they could establish during the story that the expected collision percentage of the asteroid has either increased or become a definite (only implied it has) would help. There are only implications that it has done so, like with the indefinite school closure. _childDocuments_.review: (Disclosure: I was given a "special thanks" credit.)This is one of those games that, if you're receptive to the kinds of characters and stories it's striving to present, it's going to stick with you. I had been following this game since it had been revealed in the PS5 showcase stream back in June 2020. I thought it looked okay at the time, but I didn't think it'd so thoroughly root itself as one of my top five games of all time.Visually, it looks like no other game out there. It looks like a 2D animated television series, with the kind of lighting and detail you'd expect from an anime. The character animation is 2D as well; the characters are both emotive and fun to look at, bolstered by some truly superb voice acting. Many of these characters are some flavor of LGBT+, and each of them feels like they were made with love from people who have lived their experiences. Complementing all this is wonderful, catchy music, whether it be instrumental tracks playing through a scene, or beautiful songs played during the rhythm sections. There are a handful of visual hiccups and sometimes stiff animation, but none of it so damning that they break the game or the immersion. The choice-making mechanic takes the genre in a great direction by giving visual cues on the emotions behind every choice, so it's always clear where the character's headspace is. This is coupled with additional mechanics of "Resistance" (you need to hold extra buttons to confirm an emotionally difficult choice) and "Hesitation" (if you don't fully commit to a choice, you might lose the opportunity to make it). They work so great at integrating the narrative into the gameplay that I'm shocked that other narrative games haven't tried them before. There are also rhythm game performances sprinkled throughout the story, with a simple but engaging gameplay format that always makes me look forward to them. There are also photos and flashbacks you can unlock as you play, but not every photo can be earned in one session; you WILL need to play through a few times to see everything this game has to offer.But narrative games live and die by their story, and that's where this game truly shines. There's a real emotional weight to the struggles the characters face: trying to plan for their futures when they might not have one, while also figure out who they are to each other as their lives slowly fall apart. In a genre that typically makes all your choices so powerful that they write out multiple endings based on what you do, this game paints the illusion of player control over the narrative, and then rips it away over the course of the story. This game could ONLY have one ending -- they're dinosaurs and there's an asteroid, after all -- but your choices influence everything leading up to the end. Certain scenes can play out differently based on your actions, or you might unlock special scenes based on who you befriend. Through all this, you get a compelling story that leaves an impact on you. It's quite hard to do a rhythm game at the end of the world with tears in your eyes.Goodbye Volcano High is a beautiful, thoughtful, memorable game that strives to show what this genre of games can really accomplish. I wholeheartedly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best representation I've seen of queer friendship in any piece of media I've consumed. It is a visual novel in disguise with some game element strewn in with dialogue choices and of course the musical performance minigame. But in contrast to more traditional visual novels, it's more animated and is also voices. It feels more like a Telltale game in that sense.I particularly love how the dialogue choices reflect in the main character you play as, Fang. Sometimes you need to do additional input to say something that would be difficult for them to say, and sometimes an inner monologue appears if you try to say something rude. The dialogue option changes to that inner voice which I found super interesting.The musical performance minigame is great. There is not a lot of them in the game, but unlike some other games, the minigame is challenging at times and feels satisfying to play. It also helps that the songs are pretty good.Some negatives about the game is that sometimes the animations feel a little stiff, and the voice line deliveries feel offbeat at times. The game also seems to be pretty linear and present you with illusions of choice sometimes. But they feel like nitpicks since the rest of the game is pretty amazing.It's a breath of fresh air for queer gamers to see themselves and their friend group represented. It's not every day you get to see a main character of a game be non-binary and get to finally see yourself represented.

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially hesitant to try this game after hearing about the discourse surrounding it, but even after playing the other titles that this game is compared to, I'm extremely glad that I gave it a try.If you're looking for the same level of humor and intensity as the other titles being talked about, this definitely won't have the same impact; but, I found that while GVH has a very different focus and atmosphere going on around it, this story still has a great amount of moments that range from adorable to heart wrenching. That said, I did feel that some of the relationships developed in this story didn't have enough time to be fully fleshed out. Overall, I found the story was perfectly fine for what it is, it just depends on the kind of story you want and how "raw" you're expecting the emotions to really get.I will also say that the soundtrack is AMAZING. I don't tend to listen to this genre of music too much, but I've found myself listening to every song on repeat. Dabu did a fantastic job and it's hard to believe their only other works on Spotify are Dwarf Fortress and Winding Worlds. Brigette Naggar was also fantastic!I know this review sounds like I'm just glazing the devs, but I feel that overall I'd probably give Goodbye Volcano High a 7.5/10. It's not perfect and I think the weakest aspect of this story is the dialogue and how the cast delivers a lot of her lines. I'm no expert on VA recording, but I think the pacing and emotion could use a lot of work in terms of how the characters act around each other, it just seemed very stiff, which is surprising considering they have some good cast members in this project such as Rengoku from Demon Slayer. I really wouldn't have known he was in this if I hadn't looked it up, he just sounds that different here. To just end on the part that people can't help but to focus on... Yes, there's a lot of LGBTQ+ representation in this game. However, I pretty much never felt like it was just being thrust into my face and when moments DID pop up,  I appreciated how the story handled it. A lot of it is more about the characters in this story just happening to be who they are. Hell, it's not even clear for a lot of characters if they even have ANY romantic feelings, let alone for any specific gender/people. It's just a part of who they are, which I think is a good way of normalizing such things.

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High was my very first Visual Novel, and it was a thoroughly enjoyable experience for me. I marathoned it over the night. I just couldn't stop playing it until it was done. I'm really not the type for Visual Novels, but I felt compelled to give this one a try, and I am certainly not disappointed. It was just a lovely, sweet, positive experience.I encountered a few technical issues while playing, like characters being abruptly cut off while speaking in a couple places, and a couple screens that I could not progress through, but I was so invested in the story and characters that it didn't really bother me at all.Also, I just really want to say that while I finished the game in about eight hours, I am not disappointed. I thoroughly enjoyed those eight hours. While I definitely want more of Fang and their adventures through life in Pangea, not every game can or should be one you can play every night for several hours for a week or three without exhausting its content. It's actually refreshing to be able to have something digestible that I can just enjoy for a night or two and move onto other things I would like to do. It would be quite tragic to have this story overstay its welcome. People really do seem to forget that making a game is a pretty extraordinary amount of work and a notably lengthy process, especially for small independent development studios. Try to temper your expectations in a world of disgustingly monetized forever games. I personally have little desire or patience to play 100+ hour RPGs anymore.As for that anti-fangame, pay it little mind. It can't ruin such a good and lovely thing. Fang is perfect just the way that they wish to be. <3Keep up it KO_OP! Just keep doing your very best!

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game last night, wrote a mini review just before 2 hours to put up my thoughts before the 2hr mark of no return where I could no longer refund the game. I took the day to do a run through of the story to completion (Story not achievements that comes next). Anyways, I'd like to start off the review by saying that I've come to this game AFTER completing the parody romance Visual Novel Snoot Game, I love SG and find it impossible to get through this review without mentioning it since GVH is the reason that we have SG and as such I'll often be comparing and contrasting GVH with SG and IWHTG (another romance VN from the same developer, set in the same location as both SG and GVH). A lot of that community jokes on GVH about how terrible this is, and I assumed so too after seeing numerous reviews, memes, and just playing the masterful storytelling that SnootGame had to offer and for the most part my original thoughts for the first 2 hours remained mostly unchanged. I'll begin with everything I dislike about the game. Stella, Rosa, Sage, and Trish are still insufferable, however Trish became less so later on in the second half. The biggest let down to this game is that it is a choice driven narrative game with only one ending, and one that comes wayyy too quick. It took me 25 hours to complete IWHTG with its' 4 endings, and this I can complete in 9 hours total, only having to start a second run to get scenes I missed during L&L, that aside, with the right choices you can essentially complete this game in less time, getting every achievement but 2. There's many visual bugs, visible seams on almost every character, in one scene you could see the cutofff of Fang's model because it was too high from the bottom of the screen, in another scene Trish came into view and flashed between 2 different facial expressions in a single frame, and many examples of subtitles not lining up with what the VA is saying, in one scene it gave the sentence a different tone and meaning. Sound issues is smaller, mostly being audio line timings being off, the front or back end of the line being cutoff by .5s not massive but got annoying fast. Most of the characters feel very cardboard and one dimensional, the choices (or lack thereof sometimes) you make feeling like they have little to no impact, being there's only 1 ending there's no impact to your choices, picking options they like only give extra scenes for you as you fix up your relationship with your friends. The relationship system being another very annoying system I'll leave for elsewhere. It seems like I had a lot to gripe about with this game but, I still don't hate it enough to not recommend it. The music is fantastic, I loved every music segment, the theme is great, the inclusivity is great, the romantic side-plot was a nice touch, even though they ruined the mystery of it so fast, and Fang. Fang is wonderfully written as a character, I only wished that there were more choices for you to say, or that in certain places the option you picked better relate to what is actually said. This is nowhere a bad game like most people made it out to be, nowhere near as good as SnootGame and IWHTG but it's not bad by far. Would I recommend this game? Yeah, on sale, the price tag is a little high for what you get out of it. Would I recommend you play Snoot Game or I Wani Hug That Gator instead? If you're die hard in love with this game and came here for the lgbt inclusivity and just are apart of the "woke agenda" that the right wing (get it?) keep vomiting about, then, no. SG, while fantastic, heartwarming, heartbreaking, and at times soul crushing, was made by a bunch of 4chan /v/ideo game board NEETS. It makes jokes that make me cringe even though I used to be the same. If you're not faint of heart, can handle a few crude jokes at someone's expense, then go play SG, it's free, it's fantastic. IWHTG however, I recommend to anyone. The devs realized how good SG was, and improved upon their formula, still giving you a devastating and beautiful story, but making it more accessible to people who don't spend minimum 5 hours a day on 4chan. It made me into an emotional wreck for 2 whole days after working through all 4 endings. TL;DR: Goodbye Volcano High has a myriad of minor visual and sound flaws, and suffers from 1 dimensional characters at times as they stick to a script instead of feeling like fluid characters. But it's redeemed by the music, Fang, the theme, art, inclusivity, romance, and Fang. Feelin a light 7.5-8/10 but I recommend going to play I Wani Hug That Gator instead (Snoot Game too if you can handle some crude 4chan humor)

_childDocuments_.review: After recently viewing and taking in other opinions and realizing that my original review was somewhat impulsive, I've come back to rewrite my original review and update my score based off new information (i played snoot game)Overall, no matter how much I wanted to give it a higher grade, no matter how much I loved the trailer or the community or the soundtrack, . The story is touching, the message is great, and somehow relatable, no matter how slow interactions may be. The graphics (especially backgrounds) are stunning and AAA studio-like , the music is ear-gasmic, the overall dialogue is mid-quality, and while the game does leave me wanting more, it delivers on what you expect, although I would not be opposed to something like a prequel, or a small DLC including more.Goodbye Volcano High is one of the only Visual Novels I've actually played and finished, and throughout, it was about a  experience. Going into the game, it's hard to pretend that you don't know what's going to happen in the grand scheme of things, but the character's emotions, no matter how slow the interactions may be, do take the game to another level. Navigation of LGBTQ+ themes, Seniors "leaving the nest", knowing the end is coming, balancing life and friends, etc. is good, however, a big problem that myself (and others) have noticed is that .  They're almost lying to you in the beginning by telling you that your actions have major impacts. As far as gameplay goes, it's a standard VN experience: Choosing different dialogue options, knowing which choices influence your relationships with the people around you, special mini-games for special actions, etc. The music sections are relatively boring and easy to get through, and I do wish the "health" system fell slower, as missing 1-2 notes gets you below half pretty quickly. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, does this game have it's beautiful moments, but also does it have it's very, very ugly moments. During certain times, it feels like a AAA studio show or movie (which would be unbelievable if it truly happened), but other times it feels like a PowerPoint slideshow with voice-acting. There are times where the lip-sync did feel very limited and desynced, and the animations can be somewhat repetitive and cliche, but other times where it felt unbelievably high quality.Holy, again, ♥♥♥♥, does this game have a great soundtrack.  the music is genuinely really good and I wouldn't be surprised if I heard it on the radio. I had slight audio stuttering issues, but it seemed to resolve itself (First World Linux User Problems) Oh boy, the dialogue. Like the other categories, there are times where it feels like I'm genuinely hearing the dinosaur's VA's talk as if their whole world just shattered before them, voice breaking, stumbling over words, etc. But other times, it can genuinely be a dumpster fire. Subtitles not matching with their lines, skipped lines entirely, from time to time the dialogue feels like it was written for a B-Movie/high-school film project. A few options for simple accessibility, like wider spacing for songs, customizable subtitles, etc. Negative points, however, for making subtitles neccessary. I found no way in settings to turn them off. Also, there are no subtitles for lyrics within songs. As I referenced before, this game has almost entirely LGBTQ+ characters. Fang is nonbinary, Reed is gay, Sage is transgender, etc. Sage and Fang have a talk at about the midway point in the game that is very touching, as they both talk to each other about the struggles of not being "normal" and how their family perceives them. If the whole game had this level of writing and character development, it would be an easy 10/10. However, after about 5 minutes, the conversation is over and the game continues as if nothing happens. This won't take away from my Diversity rating, however. GVH has almost no replayability, which sucks because to get a 100%, you need to play through the game several times. Choices barely matter (as stated before), sections become a slog to get through, and the only thing that really changes is where you choose to go in L&L (GVH's version of D&D). Small comment, but Linux support is okay as it runs on Proton X11, however I did notice a few crashes whenever I completed a chapter (probably Steam achievement ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ breaking stuff) and  (take it with a grain of salt, I barely did much testing).Oh boy, Snoot Game. If you haven't played it but have played GVH, . It adds to the story in ways GVH barely did, addresses much, MUCH darker themes, (TW: ), has dialogue that feels like people wrote it, no voice acting :/, mod support, and 4 DIFFERENT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ENDINGS. Your choices genuinely, finally matter in gigantic ways.  It definitely has it's questionable moments, such as the main character starting out somewhat biphobic/homophobic (and a weeaboo), but getting the ending screen genuinely feels like you've watched someone's life play out in front of you.

_childDocuments_.review: (Update 28/08/2024)I immediately update the review after I finished the snoot game♪  ♪Ok, so my thoughts on GVH is it's kinda good enough for me, even though I started playing with a biased mindset at first. But it turned out to be pretty okay. I still listen to the OST sometimes because it’s really great, and the story isn’t that bad either. Still acceptable. However, I wish there were multiple endings.I’ve tried finding videos of each song on YouTube, but there’s only one video with all the songs compiled together. I’m surprised no one has uploaded individual tracks. Should I do it myself?One of the main issues I had was collecting achievements. It's a pain to replay the game from the start every time (it took me five times in total). Please consider adding a chapter select feature, a menu option to view photos, and, most importantly, a menu to play any song. The music is one of the best parts of the game. At least let us play it whenever we want or watch the songs with background visuals without the minigames.We know you can do better than this._____________________________________________And now, here’s my review of Snoot Game.I literally cried after finishing the last bonus chapter. All I can say is that the story of SG is absolutely beautiful. I never expected a game to make me cry on stream, but the emotions were just overwhelming.I didn’t cry right away at the ending in Wani, but I do cry later in some point in my life because of the game. However, SG made me cry instantly. Maybe because of my emotional state? SG and IWHTG will always hold a special place in my life.In terms of writing, GVH can’t come close to SG. But hey, at least GVH led to the creation of SG, right? Even if SG was made as a parody. Can we all just stop hating on each other?Conclusion: I did not hate GVH or say GVH is a bad game. But SG is just too good to compare. For people who love visual novels, I recommend trying SG after completing this game. It will be worth your time, I promise. (Or you can try SG first. It’s all up to you.)(And below this is the old review. Just wanted to keep it here.)I’m playing this first before starting Snoot Game.The OST is really good. I love it!I’ll move on to Snoot Game after I achieve 100% completion in this one. However, getting 100% is quite tedious because you have to restart from the beginning with each playthrough (and I have to do it three times...). _childDocuments_.review: **SPOILER FREE**Genuinely the best story-rich game I've ever played. I think its better than anything Telltale made, better than Until Dawn, and even better than Detroit: Become Human. I think its well worth the 30 dollars and even well worth buying the soundtrack tooGameplay: There's definitely not as much gameplay as in most games like it, but what it has gave me chills. The concert segments were a fair challenge of hand-eye coordination and felt incredibly satisfying to play.Music: The music is definitely one of its stronger elements; each song you play is magnificent and the background music really helps set the scene wherever it takes placeU.I.: The user interface is pretty barren; not being able to check your decisions or go to a chapter select is pretty drab, especially for a game like this. Hopefully they add those features in later. Aside from that, no complaints. I've never had any  bugs or things not work when they should with the U.I.Characters: All of them are fantastic. They're likable, relatable, and understanding. They're true representation of friends and you want to see all of them succeed. There is the issue with character models being used repetitively and some lip-syncing issues, but they're not bad enough to ruin the game for me.Story: My favorite aspect of the game is the story it tells and how well it tells it. Almost everyone knows what its like going through your last year of school and how difficult it can be no matter what plan you have for the future. You get so many perspectives on how school life is for so many characters which never seem forced or unnatural. I especially love how open-ended the game is. Some things happen with little explanation, and even the ending doesn't seem to be completely final, but that's what secretly makes a story great. It keeps you talking about the game, wondering and drawing your own conclusions. Why did this character do this? Did this end up happening in the end? Though it may seem unsatisfactory, its one of the most important parts of writing in my eyesOverall, I think the game is next to perfect, and the problems I have with the game are very minute and easily get overshadowed by the greatness the game has in store. Can't wait to play this over and over again

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10I'm usually not one for these type of "your choices matter" type games but this one really hit the spot and gave me a great experience that I couldn't put down. Yes, people will meme on the whole "lmao dino emo has long face" but there's a lot of heart in this game that tackles topics that for myself really twist the knife and hits close to home. [GAMEPLAY]The choice decision mechanic which is a small function but had me find myself relating to the protag more and kept catching myself hesitating around the options as the timer is ticking down and realized that this is what it would feel like scanning through every way a conversation and the options that make you hold on your choice made me think "Wait....Should I really say this right now?" which I found wonderful. The small segments that take a back seat are really charming and make it feel like you can really craft your own little journey with your silly dino pals. While the rhythm game segments are pretty basic, its pretty much holding in one direction while playing OSU which at times creates too much to focus on but also good because of that. Playing an instrument is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard and does help give that feel of rushing to try and not mess up so its love/hate in my opinion. the ""Dino Twitter"" mechanic personally was my favourite, it was great to play with friends and end up doomscrolling to see what the other characters are talking about with some scarily accurate tweets which was hilarious. Overall the side content outside of the visual novel style is a little rough around the edges but really did make me smile and gave me a great experience so its not just constant talking and figuring out the best route. The social link mechanics were a surprise to me (Not spoiling it) and added some lovely charm to my playthrough that I didn't expect.[VISUALS]The art design is amazing in parts with some absolutely stunning background work and once you get over the long nose face thing the designs of each character really warm on you and shows each person's own personalities. There was also an incredible amount of detail to the background characters which could've easily just been shapeless blobs but make the world feel lived in (If a dev is reading this by any chance please point out your background character to me so I can draw you some fanart please and thankyou). some of the animations are a tiny bit janky and made it feel a little rushed but when the scenes of full animation for main story beats hit it looks wonderful. Great work art team overall! [BUGS]While its only day 2 it is still important to remind everyone that there were a few issues I encountered, main one for myself being that the keyboard and mouse support felt very rushed out, keyboard UI prompts look like they're still in alpha and clash with the other fonts, trying to make changes in settings using keyboard and mouse just won't apply them so a controller is a must even with the support being an option. There are some pretty strong animation/pop-in bugs that show up throughout playing which is probably due to optimization which will need work, there's some subtitles that don't match with what a character is saying as well as some poor sound design which will just cut off character's lines mid talk so feels like you accidentally skipped a line. While all these issues are frustrating it didn't take away from the time spent but does pull you out a little if you went as in depth as myself so worth knowing at the current time.[VERDICT]Overall I didn't expect much of this title but was really surprised with how fun, silly, sad, anxiety inducing and beautiful the story took me. While there's some launch hiccups it doesn't fully break the game (From what I played) it doesn't take away from the experience as a whole. If you're looking for something that takes you through the anxiety of a new change in life and the fear of change while also cherishing those small moments with friends then this is for you. If you're looking for a standard visual novel that goes through the same beats then I suggest not trying it out or play the demo and feel like its for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High is a strange and beautiful idea.On the one hand, it is simply a solid high school drama, exploring conflict between friends and the notion of growing apart, the nature and pursuit of one's dreams, and of course, a bit of romance, because... can you even call it a high school drama with out a sprinkle of that? ;) The game wonderfully captures what one often struggles with at that age, one's sense of identity, their place in the world, the trajectory of their future, etc.And yet, by making the characters dinosaurs and adding in the factor of impending doom via the incoming meteor, they do something truly interesting. They manage to juxtapose a story about looking toward the future - and all the uncertainty, fear, and excitement that entails - with a story about facing mortality, about accepting an end. Having the cast of characters face both those struggles at the same time makes for a wonderful, unique story.The story aside, while the game is largely a visual novel, there are some rhythm-based mechanics. They were challenging enough that I was able to enjoy them, but not so hard that I ever got too overwhelmed. That said, there also weren't many instances of doing this, so I wouldn't count it among the main draws for the game. I also would have liked the ability to retry a song right after completing it, but I don't recall seeing any such option. That's likely intentional considering actions and choices seem to impact the story, so I can't criticize it for that really...  but... I still would have liked the option hehe.The art style is solid, a simple sort of comic style. Like something you might see in a webtoon. It works well for this story. And the music fits the tone well.Overall, I think the game is wonderful. Its premise is clever and unique and excellently executed. And it pulls it all together without overstaying its welcome, taking about 6 hours or so, I believe. I'd definitely recommend it, especially on a sale. I also have to give a special shout out to an aspect of the game I found quite clever and endearing,

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High is not really a perfect game. The reused animations kinda bugged me after a while and the small dialogue audio issues could be annoying. All of that is definitely noteworthy and all but I still highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend this game!The writing is amazing and not only managed to bring out a variety of extreme emotions in me but also typically kept me in the main character's shoes; Fang is in this sweet spot of controllable and out of control that is very understandable when and why things slip out of your grasp, but also allowing you to have a fair bit of input and customization over their own fate. Granted, I'm saying this with only ONE playthrough, so if there are any behind-the-curtains shenanigans going on that make that sound weird, that's probably why.The setting and main story concept feel pretty fresh without being too out of left field for my tastes, and the idea of the world coming to an end with characters who all varying opinions about the imminent disaster was as depressing of an idea for a story like this as it was emotionally engaging with the current state of the world as it is.It's a real shame that this game went through all the development troubles it did thanks to various things, not including the pandemic delaying the release on the game far past the time people were interested and aware of it. I personally think it rivals Night in the Woods for character focused story games with furries in them. I really appreciated this game just for existing, even before I played it.It's genuinely worth your money if the game's description sound enticing or affects you in any way. If you're seeing this before the game awards are up, vote for it for Games for Impact, seriously!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game since its announcement in 2020. I did not know what I would be prepared for going into this game. Once it finally came out and I was wondering just what this game was going to be like, I didn't expect to emotionally connect with the writing and the characters the way I did. This game's themes of escapism and LGBTQ characters hit hard with what the characters are going through as well as the excellent voice acting on display here. I became so attached to them by the end of the game, and found myself laughing at their awkwardness and funny moments, but also being proud of their development by the end of the journey. In the course of 7 hours, I went from wondering just what this game was like to feeling something for these characters.The rhythm gameplay is also excellently incorporated into the story and the pressure that the characters were feeling. Granted, I didn't fully understand at first that I didn't have to time my analog movements with presses and instead hold them in the direction the notes were coming from. But besides that, the gameplay was pretty easy to pick up. I genuinely felt the same anxiety Worm Drama was feeling when they were first doing their audition because of the fact that you couldn't just redo performances and had to give it my all just like the band was. There aren't many games that can make me feel the same way as the characters were feeling. I felt like I was them at that moment, feeling the same pressure on stage to do my damndest to impress the crowd.There is some jank in the game that could have been polished a bit more. Some voice lines skipped for me automatically without touching anything. I don't know if this has been patched or not. If it has since this writing, ignore this. Some voice lines also don't match the subtitles, and there are occasional typos, though the latter issue isn't unusual for visual novel games, so it's not a big deal. The resused animations, despite the very detailed expressions, can get a bit repetitive and noticeable on occasion, but it didn't distract me too much thanks to the quality of the art direction. In general, the occasional technical issue here and there didn't detract much from what was there for me to enjoy and be engrossed in.When checking out other reviews and general reception for this game, I was disheartened to see the amount of bigoted hatred from people that I'm willing to guess haven't even played the game, or prefer Snoot Game because of its transphobia. To be clear, I'm not talking about the people that have played the game and have legitimate issues, I'm talking about the many, many people who just hate the game as its concept for being a furry LGBTQ game. There isn't enough recognition for a game like this, which is why I'm writing this review. I can't imagine how the developers are feeling having to read all of this hatred after working so hard on this game. I would be crushed in that position. So to people that hate the game based on it being a furry trans game, a big ♥♥♥♥ you to you, you don't deserve to appreciate this gem.To those who are on the fence about this game or are just influenced because of what bigots are saying, do not listen to them. This game has so much to offer in its writing if you're willing to listen. It saddens me to think about Goodbye Volcano High likely going under the radar and hated for being something that isn't straight. I implore you to give this game a chance, if you like visual novels and want a story that might stick with you, I think you'll find a pleasant surprise here.And if the developers are reading this, thank you for your hard work on this game for these last 3 years. I know there were lots of delays, but the years paid off so much in the end, and I'm so happy that the game turned out the way it did. I'm afraid to think about how the ugly reception to this game has affected you, but I want you to know that your work wasn't in vain, it is being appreciated by people like me. Try your best not to listen to the bigots who hate the game for not being what they want. I think you made something really special here, and I can only hope that in due time, Goodbye Volcano High gets the recognition that it deserves.

And these characters somehow manage to convey those feelings, again and again.I also can't make this review without talking about the music. OH MY GOD, the music is so good. Even if you are not into that kind of music, you have to admit it is amazing. One of the only games where I happily bought the soundtrack. Does it have some bugs? Yeah, but I am confident that they will be patched. You can tell it's a bit rough here and there. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Goodbye Volcano High isn't a "good" game, but it's far from a bad one and is definitely worth your time if you get it on sale. I should preface this review by saying that I came into GVH as a Snoot Game fan curious to try out the original. While I didn't find GVH as moving/relatable as Snoot Game, I'm endlessly grateful to the devs for bringing these characters to life.I'll start with the bad -- Goodbye Volcano High is really rough around the edges. From animations being janky or pop-ins occurring after cuts to the lip syncing being off for most lines of dialogue, it definitely lacks polish. These are all issues that I believe can be addressed with a patch (or number of patches), but regardless it's something worth mentioning. The pacing in certain sections also feels a bit off -- the game gets a lot of hate for the D&D parody sections, and after having played through the game, I totally get this. There are three in total, and while I think the first one is cute and fits well into the story, the second and ESPECIALLY third feel like complete departures from the main story. I just wish this time had been taken to further develop character relationships or expand on the subplot with Fang's parents. My biggest gripe with the game is that I feel the writing in act three (basically everything after the Battle of the Bands) doesn't work super well. Characters seem to make out-of-character choices (and part of the issue here is that I don't think the player is given enough context to the pre-existing relationships between the characters, ie before the events of the game take place) and I found myself truly baffled by some of the dialogue. I was always rooting for Fang, but I wish we could have made more meaningful choices that could affect their relationships at the end of the game, like Worm Drama breaking up or whatever. I think multiple endings could potentially help this issue, but ultimately act three just doesn't work for me.All that being said, I did enjoy my time with Goodbye Volcano High. Seeing the characters I know and love from Snoot Game being brought to life with voices and animations was super cool, and the soundtrack is stellar. Not my type of music really, but it does a great job of creating a rich atmosphere that I liked spending time in. The humor was also . . . surprisingly good? Like the in-game "twitter" feed has some straight bangers -- there are also a ton of great references in the game to all sorts of pop-culture stuff from Critical Role to Berserk. And, at the end of the day, while I found all of the characters to be a bit too soft, I did enjoy watching them interact with each other, for the most part. Screw Trish though, somehow both SG and GVH managed to make me hate her. Is this game worth $30? In its current state, absolutely not. $15, though? I'd totally recommend it if you're interested. While due to the lack of multiple endings I don't think GVH has a huge amount of replayability, I'm definitely going to do a second run at some point to try out the different dialogue (and L&L quest) options. Hope this review helps someone out.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review having just finished Chapter 4, which according to achievements, is about half way through. NO SPOILERS. Figured I would write down early thoughts. Will update after completing. I'll also mention I have no knowledge of Snoot Game or whatever it is, nor have I read any of the drama regarding the developer, so my opinion isn't affected by that. I am reviewing only this game, nothing else. I see many other reviews, particularly the negative ones, bringing these things up, and I don't see the relevance.I also have no idea where the narrative of "4-5 hours of gameplay" is coming from. I'm five hours in and just hit the half way point. I suspect these people are skipping all the dialogue or something.Positive things:Fully Steam Deck compatible out of the box. Literally zero issues. Resolution and controller settings worked perfectly. One of the smoothest Steam Deck games I have ever played, even better than most "Verified" games.I love the characters. They all feel like different people and all act realistically. They all have different opinions on actions and all feel real. The writing is fantastic.The method for picking Fang's responses is really interesting. Some tense situations have a timer for picking a response, and you quickly have to choose what they are going to say. Alternatively, there's some situations where a particularly strong option is available, and if you move over to it, Fang's thoughts will gray it out and replace it with why they changed their mind on it. It's a very cool way of showing what Fang is thinking without directly telling the player. I also like how the UI designates extreme responses; anger is on fire, sad is broken in half, etc.The story, so far, is remarkable. I was a little hesitant about a game where the plot entirely revolves around teenage children in high school, because I just didn't think that could be all that interesting, but I was wrong. The school aspect isn't a major focus; it isn't like Persona 5, for example, where going to school is a major mechanic, it's more of a background setting here in GVH. Instead, the story revolves around the personal interactions between Fang and others, and to me, it works very well.There SEEM to be a huge amount of alternative paths. I am only half way through my first play through and I am already excited to do a second play through with different choices. I am unsure how much they actually change later in the game, but that's something I'll update my review with later.The rhythm sections are really, really fun, especially on controller. Think Night in the Woods, but more complex. I'm a big rhythm game fan, so this clicks with me really well. Love it.Negative things:Encountered a couple of minor bugs. One situation I simply couldn't advance the game because my A button input wasn't being accepted. It worked in menus, but not the game. A quick restart fixed it. There's also been a handful of graphical gliches with characters not lip syncing correctly, but over all, very minor issues, and far less bugs than any modern AAA game.There's a point in the game where you are playing an in-universe version of Dungeons and Dragons called Legends and Lore (or L&L). These were... dreadfully boring. There's nothing happening because it is characters-playing-characters, so none of the choices (as far as I can tell) matter, since it doesn't actually affect the characters in "real" life. I don't get why this was added. Thankfully, this is a very small part of the game, and since the dialogue literally doesn't matter you can skip most of it if you wanted to.Fang has a full-on fivehead. It's honestly a little distracting sometimes.Two of the achievements require rolling a nat 20 and a nat 1 in L&L. Given the dice is random and I have not found a mechanic that allows me to influence it, these have the chance to be very, VERY annoying achievements to get.Overall:So far, I am absolutely loving GVH. Highly recommend, even as someone who typically has no interest in visual novel stuff. Night in the Woods is one of my all-time favorite games, and GVH is scratching that itch really well.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly, truly wanted this game to be great, but for the amount of time and money this game received, it is not. As a visual novel, I've played better, even some free ones, I have also played worse. For the rhythm music sections, I have also played better free ones, but I can respect how they tried to mix up the gameplay style for these segments, even if I feel it was a bad execution in practice. Coupled with a bad choice of engine, Spine2D, for 90% of the character appearances, which can lead to some real Cronenberg moments, and other general technical issues, the game just... honestly wasn't there.There is also some inconsistencies in writing, issues with continuity, and some discussions that don't really make sense based on previous discussions. Also the game, as long as auto-forward is turned on, play itself almost entirely. A few moments it won't autopick an option after a timer elapses, but 99% of the time it will as long as you just check in now and then. And the music segments, it does not matter to the story at all if you perfect every note or miss every note, the story moves on regardless. Honestly, the choices don't matter beyond maybe a *smidge* of some character backstory, but even then, not really. It honestly seems like certain parts were kept from different levels of the development hell the game went through a bit of, and it led to a mishmash of writing. The quality just kind of bounces around, and it feels like the good parts were things that were there from early on and got to really get the full polish. And then there's some other bits that seem attached to those kinda haphazardly.Also the voice acting is... not the greatest, especially not when trying to match up with the lip syncing. No one seems to have any real emotion at all, which is actually fair to matching how their body is lacking in, y'know,  They tend to just stand there with their arms at their sides, arms half-bent, or arms crossed. There is next to no body language for anything, no  physical or verbal, which is a shame and really detracting from the game.The rhythm game segments, as I mentioned before, I respect trying to take a new spin on that type of gameplay, but it was only good on paper, not in practice, I feel. It doesn't feel crisp or smooth, and a lot of rhythm games you can kinda play almost by following the beat of the music and just really  with it, but not this one. It tends to get a bit... busy with it, especially in the latter half of the songs, which has the unfortunate side effects of making it hard to focus and really notice one of the actually good parts of the game, some of the static CGs or animated segments that aren't done in spine2D. Some of those are actually really good and it's a shame I couldn't actually look and enjoy them if I wanted to do the rhythm game.Now for some of the good parts:As I mentioned before, some of the static image and non-spine2D animated parts actually look really good and can be adorable or actually add some of the few moments of characters having emotion in this game. The background art is almost always really crisp and good, which is kind of jarring with the spine2D character models. Know how you can tell when a rock or a bookshelf is gonna move in the older cartoons because of the animation quality difference? It's kinda like that, but all of the time.The music is actually pretty decent, I'm probably going to be listening to some of the songs now and then, I am especially a fan of the live version of Don't Call.Honestly, I was really hoping this game would've been great, I really wish I could love it, but I just can't say that, or really actually recommend it to someone.  On a good sale, maybe, but honestly, it's a 6 hour game and it took me over 13 hours to beat because I had to keep taking breaks from it, it was an honest slog some of the time. So again, hesitant positive because of the lack of neutral option. It is a solid /10. It is positive and not a negative review specifically because I can respect that there was an attempt and in the parts that are good, they  genuinely good. Sadly, such parts are rather few and far between what is otherwise a rather mediocre experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Making a game about anthropomorphic dinosaurs is about honesty. An uncompromising vision, it essentially disarms the creator. They're dinosaur people! It's strange! But the creators like dinosaur people, and they made no compromises. Everything they have is all there for you. I don't believe anything was held back. On first glance, maybe you're put off by how the characters look. Maybe you're a part of the crowd who believes would be better if the cast weren't LGBT. A parody game made specifically to attack this one, is perhaps the greatest endorsement of Goodbye Volcano High's authenticity. It's a perfect contrast. Openness, versus hatred masked in parody and comedy. There is no fulfillment in a negative identity like that. Just play this game, don't bother with the parody. This game provides an ineffable insight into the creator's world. Whether drawn from experience, or invented from desire. A high school full of dinosaur people allows us to engage authentically with the media, and in my opinion, connect with it like few other games. In the game, you're put into the shoes of the main character Fang, a non-binary teenager. Through them, you meet friends, play in a band, and try to keep it all together in the face of the apocalypse. Nothing particularly astounding or supernatural happens. Despite the setting, the game very much could have been set in modern day and accomplished the same plot. And the plot itself, is where I would hold some criticism for the game. Not every narrative beat truly hits the mark, although this may be partly because of the branching narrative aspect of the game. Goodbye Volcano High is extremely concerned about the "how" it conveys things. The characters speak with one another? It's animated and voice acted. You need to select a dialogue option? The text blinks and shifts during stressful scenes. You design your band's logo, posters. You play a rhythm game each time Fang plays on stage. When your friends text you, you see the messages on your phone. And, putting it all together, it works beautifully. I really love this game, especially the music. There's something special about how it all comes together, and I think it really displays that furry/anthro art brings something to the table, all on its own. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: CONTAINS SPOILERSTo start with what I liked:Starting from the pause screen, I like the smaller elements that really add to the aesthetic and charm of the game, such as the way the character's relations to Fang are shown. Having it resemble rings that orbit around Fang really helps to add in the aesthetic with the planets and especially the meteors. The Twitter tab was actually rather enjoyable to pause and read through periodically throughout the game, but I do have some minor critiques of it to discuss later on. Then of course there was the pictures tab, it serves it purpose, however for this too I have some comments to address towards it.And when it comes to the UI choices made with the dialogue options, I absolutely LOVE what you did where some dialogue options will be prohibited for the player to choose based off of the past dialogue choices. Where to prevent certain options so that the player can only play the character they have at that point made themselves to be is such a small touch which really goes far for my immersion and enjoyment. As well as just the general visual design of the dialogue, it helps to convey the tone of what the player would pick which is another one of those small touches which go far.Critique:The Twitter tab, while enjoyable and funny to read through, really served no major purpose in the game. Which I feel is a major misuse of this system. Something like this could have been used to help establish context and worldbuilding around the asteroid in ways the main narrative couldn't, serving as a way to answer some player's questions and curiosities about the apocalypse, as well as the main cast. Like maybe Fang could scroll through a post from their parents which helps the player better understand them by providing them more depth, or a post about some random guy explaining how exactly the asteroid works in a way predicated on general fearmongering which was retweeted by Reed, serving to both better explain the asteroid and characterize Reed for those who want to read through it. Yet it mainly is used to tell a joke here and there (which I enjoyed, don't get me wrong) when it could have been used for so much more and just strikes me as a missed opportunity. Also, I wish there was a sort of indicator (especially when replaying the game) for how certain dialogue options affect certain relationships. So that when I'm trying to replay the game and make it so I can get access to the special Naser moment at the beach, I can know either beforehand or afterhand how the dialogue choices I choose will affect the relationship in a good or bad way. I can't even tell what dialogue choices affect relationships, which is really annoying having to pause the game to see if his orbit changed to reload my last save or not, like even a "Naser will remember" this will help. As a matter of fact, for a game based heavily around its replayability, it has been made rather difficult to replay. No way to check how you influence relationships, no way to have save states to scum for all the other endings, hell, there isn't even a way to fastskip through dialogue this is anything short of spamming A. Having to replay the entire game piece by piece in order to achieve everything is going to be a massive turnoff for people trying to replay the game, and lets say you end up coming near the climax and you only realize then you chose the wrong dialogue for Rosa and aren't able to have that moment at the bonfire with her? Enjoy replaying the game again, and you better hope you figure out what the correct things to say to her are. This is just really not player friendly, and I hope something is done about this sooner or later. And to list my complaint for the photos tab, I really wish there was a black backdrop or something when you select to look into an image, as sometimes its impossible to read what is said underneath the photos as the white blends into other pictures. I have to scroll down all the way after selecting an image just to read what it says, so I hope a quality-of-life fix can be done for this too. Also, assuming that my following critique was something intentional by the devs and not a bug on my end, this game has several segments that have no music, when they really really should. Like the transition from that one purple teacher character (forgor her name) to the logo customization screen is really jarring with how all the music and dialogue cuts so abruptly. I feel like a good solution to this would be to either have some music, or to have that Ms.Purple's dialogue be muffled and echoey so it still feels immersive with the scene. This also goes for mainly every segment when Fang goes on their phone, there should be some music, or if people are supposed to be talking, muffled talking in the background, because it really pulls you out when everytime Fang hops on their phone the entire world stops (think of the scene when they just got done having the fight with Trish after the comp and they are in front of Sage, Rosa, and Stella).When it comes to the writing, it's a mixed bag, but overall it's rather enjoyable. I say it's a mixed bag because sometimes it has it's moments, like sometimes the dialogue can lose itself and have certain tangents overstay their welcome. And as a much bigger issue, sometimes dialogue can really handfist exposition to the player to the detriment of my immersion and enjoyment of the story. A good example of this is some of the first words of the story where Naser calls you "sib". I get you want to explain to the player that these two characters are related and that Fang is enby, but dear Raptor Jesus did you have to do it in the most unrealistic way possible? I'm sorry if I'm being rather aggressive on this point, but it's always a pet peeve of mine when siblings call each other bro/sis/sib in a story, and I truly believe that information could have been conveyed in a much more subtle way (like they live in the same house afterall it wouldn't take much to convince the player they're siblings). Another example of them being handfisty with exposition is when Fang and the gang first talk about BOTBs to one another, doing it in a "As you know" fashion, but at least there the blow is softened by the writers using as a way to characterize Trish and Reed. Luckily for the most part the writing seems to grow out of this by the latter end of the story, and is much more enjoyable for the majority of the game. However, another big complaint for the writing from me is that I wish they better fleshed out Fang's parents, who serve to be a relatively important plot point near the end (despite being shrugged off in the scene immediately after its revealed how they won't be coming home for CaldFest, although that issue could simply be attributed to the pacing). Like it was hardly relevant in the main story as it was and it simply doesn't possess the buildup the climax wants you to believe Fang's parents have. Bugs:There is A LOT of them. Sometimes dialogue skips by itself. Sometimes limbs go ragdolling and characters look how they aren't supposed to in scenes. The whole shebang. I know this game has been brewing for nearly 4 years now, but I would have preferred a few months, or even a year more, just for it to be released in a finished and polished state.I have so much more to say, but my wordcount is running dry, so let me sum up my thoughts. Overall, the narrative and gameplay help to greatly accentuate the themes of the game, while it loses its footing here and there, it's still stable enough to keep you in for the ride. However, due to the current state of the game replaying it is another hell in of itself.My final take is that this is a game worth buying. But just not right now, it has a lot of issues right now that need fixing that I would wait until after they are done to be considered worth buying. But I truly enjoyed this game, and will be following along KO-OP for their next games.

_childDocuments_.review: i had waited for this game since it's announcement back at the PS4 announcement and had been following it on and off each time i was reminded about it (albeit from unsavoury parody imo) after finishing it i had been thinking of how to review this and i think i will go point by point like many other reviewers do. first ever in depth review so what could go wrong right?now, this game took a looong time to come out (pun unintended) and some will hold that against the team but my counterpoint is: indie dev team that not only increased their scope, but had a LOT of unwarranted hate and even a 'fangame' riffing on the characters themselves. then covid happened AND a bunch had been re-written during the lockdowns, making this take at least half of the delay it had. now to talk about the game itselfthis is high school seniors leading into college, and even though no one expressively states their age. it is safe to assume all are teens, keep this in mind regarding choices, because the writing is ON POINT with their personalities, teen cringe included. the pressure, uncertainty and relationships felt so authentic that i felt a LOT of it, even as someone not easily swayed like that.there are a couple of moments where i think knowing more about the friend group's history for me to make certain decisions. but that's also probably the overthinking adult in me talkin'Think Telltale, except visual novel kind of setting with Musical gameplay sections.this is a combination that i haven't seen much if at all. but it was done well and authentically.i was honestly looking forward to each music section because honestly the way the inputs were done for them, i'm not a rhythm master or anything, but the difficulty was juuust right for me to feel tense but also have a lot of fun, hoping to not mess up too much. you can turn down the difficulty however if that's your speed. also i couldn't help but bop to the music whilst playing these sectionsexpressions....they are conveyed very, very well, and i have no idea how, but it's definitely aided by the voice acting. the graphics are more artistic than powerful, BUT there is varying visual bugs across a few that don't last long enough to take away from the experience. lip syncing seems to be lacking a bit. but that's all i gotta say about thatit is a fairly short game, but that doesn't mean it's not worth the price, as it's budget is definitely on the higher side and the writing was done so well and authentically that you don't feel like anything out of character happens, some choices seem like an always lose situation, but think of it like this: you are playing as the internal thought pusher, not the decision maker. like how you have multiple thoughts and one sticks out to you to play out. what you control in this game is what thought sticks out to fang to play outthere's a good deal i missed out on because of said choices, so chances are i'll do several playthroughs in my spare time, but for now i say it's worth it for even one playthough.fan of VNs? get itFan of Telltale, but want less harsh consequences? get itlike music with a lot of feeling behind it? get it
