_childDocuments_.review: The mix of visual novel and rhythm game serves GVH well. The rhythm game: the mix of directional arrows controlled by analog stick with the face button inputs scattered across the screen is inspired. You really feel like you are doing two things at once without it being overwhelming. Plus the music is really good!The visual novel stuff is really good too. This is a game where the dialogue button's text does not match up what the character actually says, which annoyed me, but it makes some sense when there's supposed to be subversion in how the game presents dialogue options. There's a few tricks, like options cycling around to represent Fang's uncertainty. And the game will lock you out of some choices if you hover over them but then move away, representing Fang's hesitancy (this is something you can turn off through the options menu).In the end this is a story game. And the story is kinda great. There's a chunk of it that's a little weak because the meteor stuff is pushed to the back and it feels like the drama could come from any YA fiction but eventually shows its teeth and the drama becomes gutwrenching but also very human and affirming. It's worth checking out.

Some technical issues were present, like visual pop in when a scene transitioned; lines of dialogue being cut short, and I think I seen the beginning of a romance scene with Stella after I already was with Naomi, and some kind of relatability/retry menu would be nice for the chapters/music performances, but these are all things that can be added with an update. _childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely so beautiful. Sure, there are some bugs that need to be ironed out, and a few choppy transitions, but the writing hits so close to home. _childDocuments_.review: Right so, just finished game. For me clocked in at 6 and half hours. So what do you get out of it?You play as Fang, a (taradactal? been awhile since dino class) Teen aspiring to have a Music Career and go on tour with her friends. _childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet (Beat in about 5 hours). I can see the comparisons to Night in the Woods and they are justified, similar edgy teen slice-of-life tone and also has rhythm game sections with a few songs. Speaking of songs, I do like that you can choose your own lyrics, although I still think the replay value here is somewhat limited as the player's choices don't seem to have a huge impact on the story otherwise. I think the main problem is that the game simply wasn't long enough for me to create bonds with the characters. There's a big cast here, so I find it faces a similar problem to Mass Effect 2 in that there's all these great characters but barely any actual dialogue with them to get to know them further. I do also feel the LGBT elements were ramped up a little too high, while I'm supportive of the community, this does come across as a little in your face. I heard others mention technical issues, but I didn't find it much of a problem. A couple freezes but nothing serious. I enjoyed the L&L sessions most (potential future dlc?), and while this game definitely isn't for everyone, I quite enjoyed my brief time with it. But I'm not sure it's worth the asking price considering how short it is though and the aforementioned lack of replayability.  If you like these types of games and can enjoy the unique tone it's worth picking up though.

The character designs are great, and Fang's is probably one of my favorite of all time. _childDocuments_.review: Does this game have technical problems? YesDoes this game have overall problems with writing and character development? YesDo your choices really matter? You should already know an answer to this question based on how many games have used that phrase in the pastIs it worth playing? If you are not discouraged by the questions and answers above, then go for it, you will not regret it.There are some technical issues, I am not gonna list all of them, since other people did that. There were two things that bothered me the most. First, some dialogues are skipped, I needed to check if I have not accidentally pressed a button on the keyboard. Second, something went wrong in the process of audio mix for most of the dialogues, often when characters stop speaking it sounds as they have not given the track time to naturally fade away but just cut it right in the moment when the line ends.The only real struggle I have with the story is the ending, which stands against the message that this game wants to tell. Overall, story is not perfect. But it does not need to be, it is still enjoyable and emotional and left me in this sad/empty state after finishing it. 30$ for a 7 hour experience is a bit much, but honestly I had much more fun than in other AAA titles which take waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay more hours to complete and this game reminded me of what I love about short games. It was not the best and most perfect, but still it was a great ride for me and I will go for it again, after the devs will patch it up. Although, if you cannot ignore some inconsistencies or flaws with storytelling and it bothers you, I would say skip this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: When first seeing the announcement trailer I knew I had to play this game since I'm a big fan of narrative / decision based games like Life is Strange, any of the games Telltale has been making etc.I didn't watch any of the following trailers since I try to keep going in as blind as I can into games that interest me and having said that a lot of the narrative in Goodbye Volcano high is treading known paths of stories that deal with similar situations.But even if the game goes through very similar story beats as other stories in that genre I had a great time from start to finish. The characters felt earnest and the voice performances where great across the board.There was a lot of charm and love crammed into this project at every opportunity. There were a lot of small animation details that surprised me. For example the different animations when Fang is texting with their friends on the phone added a lot of personality. And those small details are everywhere.The first time you'll see the credits is around the average length I'd say for games in this genre (5-6 hours)and while I ended up wanting more when I saw the credits it wasn't because I felt the game was incomplete but because I loved the cast and wanted to spend more time in that world.But when it comes to what is in the game. Well it delivers an at least to me emotional story with a great cast.(Sorry for not going into detail here but I want to keep it spoiler free)When it comes to downsides for this game. I ran into a couple of bugs where sound wouldn't play (fixed it with restarting the game) or sometimes inputs wouldn't work. Though that was fixed with changing between fullscreen and borderless window in the options menu.As someone who played a lot of rhythm games some of the input prompts felt weirdly clumsy and unresponsive. But since the focus is more on the narrative I didn't really bother me that much. I had 1-2 instances where I reload a safe cause I though the input for one the prompts wasn't really working. (When you have to push both analog sticks down at the same time) But after getting a feel for the required timing it was fine.Overall I feel I can safely recommend this game to people who enjoy games like Life is Strange or telltale games and I am really exited to see what the team behind this Goodbye Volcano High does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High is a sweet mix of a VN / Rhythm game with wonderful characters / visuals, and a compelling story that intrigues the player as the passage of time goes on with the impending event behind everything. Thoroughly enjoyed my time with this one. Reminded me of times I've clutched closely in my life but also of bracing through the unknown, inevitable hard decisions in life. Truly a wonderful a game in its own volition with memorable characters / setting. Must play for a nice story!
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! I loved it. Great dialog, fantastic voice acting and downright incredible production value, to the point it felt at times like I was playing an animated TV show. The story is moving and carefully crafted so you don't hate the characters even if they argue or make dumb choices. There are a surprising number of fun creative choices you get to make in this game, alongside the usual 'communicate your feelings' dialog choices you would expect. Also, the music rules. The length of the game is 6-7 hours, which I think is the right length for a story like this one but keep it in mind if that is a factor before you buy.The only negatives I have are small missing features or technical problems:The game sometimes hangs for too long between shots. This can lead to awkward pauses in the dialog.There is also sometimes pop-in when the game switches shots, causing a background element or character to show up a few frames later than everything else in the shot.Finally, there was one instance where I paused the game and audio broke, which I fixed by quitting to desktop and reloading my save.Speaking of saves, this game has no save slots, or manual saving at all. Not even a chapter select screen. You just have one autosave and that's it. Very odd.Overall: The story idea and characters alone warrant an 8/10. Voice acting, music, and stylistic flourishes bump it all the way up to a 9.5/10. The minor technical issues and lack of save options hold it back just a little, but hopefully the devs will fix these problems with a patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game at a 75% only because i had a few problems with it. But i will say none of the problems took away from the awesome but sad Story. It hit so many marks with me, from how i used to feel growing up, to how i feel today. I did a play through all in one sitting and took a little under 7 hours to beat, There isn't much of replay other than to get 100% the songs for the Achievements. In all the game makes you connect with the main dude. If you used to be a no one, someone who cast aside, Didn't follow in the footsteps of there parents, the game will speak to you just, like it does with me.But for what i would say would break the game for some people, -I had it skip over dialogue on it own some times mid way through or right at the start and jump to the next. and there is no way to look back to see what was missed.-The Animation was either slow not synced right or just not there for talking, moving, etc.-There are many times when the game just loses all back ground sound, You'll be talking to someone with music in the background and then it just disappears and its all gone. leaving to a very awkward conversation between you and the NPC.-The biggest thing i have a problem with. There is not a single point where you are given a moment to pause to put the game down, not after days or in between what is going on in the world. It just goes and doesn't start from the beginning to the end. -There is no Save file meaning. if you mess up on a song mid way through the game and what all the achievements you have to restart the whole game over again just to get said achievement. That goes the same with all the in game choices (IMO you shouldn't go back to change a choice and you should play it all in one go. but i know people can't do that).

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy it but there's some glaring technical issues and 'rough around the edges' bits that I'd really wish weren't here after 4-5 years of development and multiple delays, none of it was bad enough to ruin my experience but y'know you hate to see it in a $30 game, especially one as simple as a very linear visual novelgood: I really like the characters, the story, the designs, the music and the voice acting, everything that's 'important' is done right IMO, you should be able to tell if it's to your taste just by the trailersbad: stuff like character sprites flipped horizontally without respect to text printed on the clothing, jittery animations (I understand there's a bit of artistic choice going on here but there are points where it really doesn't feel like an artistic choice), sometimes a background would take a second to actually render, and some characters have audible mic noise in their voice lines so you can hear when the actual audio files begin and end. again none of it's terrible enough to ruin the game, but it does stick out. edit: also the game really poorly communicates the passage of timeanyway I cried at the end ♥♥♥♥ you guys I like the stupid gay dinosaur game

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't play games like this, but i was hooked when i saw it on the steam store. Mostly because of the unique setting and the wonderful music this game has to offer. The band/artist? "Dabu" is, from what i have researched, the source behind most of the songs you will hear in this game...and they are really good! The animations are great, the voice acting can be an up & down but overall i think they did a good job with this game. I'll update my review once i finished it!Edit: I have now finished the game and i overall enjoyed the short but sweet story. I just wish that there were multiple endings.

This game had me crying, laughing and shaking. Not a lot of games can make me do all 3, but it takes a really good one to do so. I adore so many of the characters, the art is beautiful and the soundtrack is filled to the brim with bangers. ♥♥♥♥ any haters. WORM DRAMA GANG!!!

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 story was great, characters were awesome, ending was perfect, game play want to hard and not to easy, i highly recommend you go in blind with this game to get the full experience the only thing keeping this from a 10/10 is the damn mouths my ocd brain cant help but see them not 100% line up but that's just me im a perfectionist and see all the mistakes people make that doesn't mean its bad and i got over 90% on all songs my first try so that made me happy give it a try im sure you'll like it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Now that it's been almost a year since the release, and I've had time to play through this completely as well as with friends and get new people into the game, I feel like I can leave a better review.Goodbye Volcano High isn't for everyone, both good (just not a fan of the gameplay style) and bad (queerphobic), but I HEAVILY recommend giving this game a shot. It doesn't try to be some grand story, it doesn't glamorize its characters or fit them into a cheap box, there isn't some attempt to make every single line a standing ovation. KO_OP treats its characters like they would any real person. I won't spoil much about the story, as it's something that loses some of its impact (pun intended) if you already know a lot of the story beats.They don't always talk with absolute clarity, their motivations can be confusing, and some things they say or do don't always make sense. But they're not an oversight in this case. They're an integral part of the story and the characters, and the dialogue and delivery are both much more like what you'd hear from actual people. Despite all being dinosaurs, they're all very human.There's also no big, crazy story going on beyond the asteroid that's hinted at in the demo and the middle chapters, just Fang and their two closest friends trying to win the Battle of the Bands before summer while figuratively making it through in one piece.There's more focus on the characters and how the little details can get in the way of being friends sometimes, and it doesn't portray anyone as perfect. Not even Fang, the character you play as. The people who call them selfish or a jerk tend to miss the point that this is part of the overarching story and Fang's character arc, and they don't always see that for different reasons.And besides the art direction being really unique, offering an almost 3D style done completely with 2D art and an entire system for both movement and characters talking, the music and sound direction are incredible. It's worth listening to the soundtrack alone from this game, especially if you're a fan of genres like Shoegaze (which seems to be the main inspiration). You'll also find some familiarity if you've ever played games like Dwarf Fortress, as its soundtrack is made by the same person, Dabu.For the voice acting, despite feeling a lot more human and personal, there's still some real talent behind everything. It doesn't sound like 90s high school movies, where the actors and actresses are more obviously in their late 20s to early 30s; I personally forgot these were even adults doing the voice acting. Especially Fang's voice actor, Lachlan Watson (They / Them), someone who's appeared in the Sabrina the Teenage Witch reboot and the Chucky TV series. You get to hear their singing voice in the soundtrack too, which they NAIL. Brigitte Naggar's singing isn't anything to scoff at either, though!There's also Allegra Clark, someone you might recognize from Apex Legends and Jujutsu Kaisen; Ozioma Akagha, known for some live action shows like Delilah; Mark Whitten, a voice in Spider-Man 2 (the PlayStation game) and the Demon Slayer movie from 2020; Sarah Elmaleh, someone you might recognize from Hi-Fi Rush; and more, such as Abe Bueno-Jallad, Dee Revilla, Jensen Trani, and Dahlia Salem, the last of which was an actress in Paul Blart: Mall Cop of all things. (The last part isn't important, just funny to mention.)(If you are just here for Goodbye Volcano High itself, this next part may not be relevant to you, but I still recommend reading it.)The last thing I'll mention is this: If you have any amount of respect for queer people, regardless of what group or if you are in that group yourself, I recommend staying VERY FAR away from both "Snoot Game" and "I Wani Hug That Gator!", as both of them are by the same person: Cavemanon, a common 4chan user (the kind you hear about on the news, not the kind that stopped the cat killer) much like almost everyone on his team.The first game was made completely as an anti fan-game, started and ultimately released years before this game was much more than its reveal trailers, containing some really vile content that doesn't just include very blatant transphobia. All of its endings are centered around the transphobia, though, and one of the "downer endings" specifically turns Fang into a literal school shooter (in a FULL SCENE, graphics and all) just for not being detransitioned. The other "downer ending" is not nearly as graphic, but is still based on not being detransitioned. The other game does not have much of this, likely because Cavemanon and the people he worked with knew it would likely not fly a second time, but the beliefs, views, and even outright hatred is still a part of its design.Cavemanon himself, and by extension a lot of his fans, are - for lack of a better description - exactly what you'd expect from the "bad side" of 4chan. In particular, they're quite fine and adamant to dox certain people over Goodbye Volcano High (especially Wolf Nanaki), and Cavemanon has made multiple long-winded post about his "traditionalism" and how Snoot Game is explicitly MEANT to be as queerphobic as it is.When it comes to "I Wani Hug That Gator!", there's a certain chance that artists who make content surrounding it (especially art) may not know these things about the previous game and Cavemanon, and you may have some luck warning artists about said content. But when it comes to Snoot Game, I would almost not even bother due to how blatant it all is. Which is a shame, as there is a very large and disappointing amount of queer people who are fans (or "fans") of these games, not knowing or caring that the creator very publicly despises them for who they are.If you're all the way down here, and you read all of this, I'm glad you took the time for it. If you're all the way down here and DIDN'T read all this, imagine I'm throwing bean bags at you.Worms Forever,Dreamless
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review:
In times of change, what do we owe each other? 

Goodbye Volcano High, a cinematic, choice-based narrative game set in the final year of school for a bunch of dinosaur teens, on the cusp of graduation and the rest of their lives.

You will follow them as they struggle to make their mark on the world, figure out who they're going to be, and try to find love, all before time runs out and they're thrust into the world of adulthood. But what they don't know yet is that time might be about to run out for real. In a time where we're all feeling a little lost and scared, and not sure what happens next, we're hoping that the story resonates with people.

name: Alone in the Dark
detailed_description: Alone in the Dark weaves a chilling tapestry of psychological horror and Southern Gothic charm, reimagining the iconic game that set the benchmark for the genre. We invite you to join us on a journey into madness, where each encounter could be your last. With each step you take closer to unravelling Derceto's mystery, the eyes that watch from the darkness grow hungrier. Every bullet means the difference between survival and an unthinkable end. The next door you unlock could lead to a nightmarish realm offering nothing but slashing claws, grasping tentacles, and frayed sanity. Journey to interbellum Louisiana, where an era of decadence hides a darker tale - of escape from past traumas and an intolerant society, into the waiting grasp of something darker, something that has patiently lurked for impossible eons. This is Alone in the Dark as you've never seen it - a skillfully-woven narrative of Southern Gothic elegance and eldritch madness that pays homage to its legendary origins while taking the next step forward in survival horror storytelling. A Haunting Tale of Mystery and Madness Step inside Derceto Manor, an asylum shrouded in intrigue, guarding a terrible secret. Client Emily Hartwood and private investigator Edward Carnby embark on a harrowing quest for answers; Emily to the mystery of her missing uncle, Edward to the toughest case he will ever face, and both to questions they dare not ask themselves. This re-envisioned classic invites you to explore an unforgettable single player adventure rich with suspense, frights, and revelations that will test the limits of your imagination. Featuring Hollywood Talent Experience some of the greatest acting survival horror has ever seen through the performances of award-winning actors Jodie Comer (Killing Eve, Free Guy) and David Harbour (Stranger Things, Black Widow) in their first videogame roles. Jodie and David’s immaculately captured likenesses breathe life into Emily Hartwood and Edward Carnby, lending a deeply personal aspect to Alone in the Dark’s story that demands it be played twice to get the full experience. A Tribute to Horror Pioneers Rediscover the essence of psychological horror in a game that respectfully nods to its 1992 origin, the game that established the survival horror genre. Alone in the Dark is your gateway to an experience steeped in the atmospheric dread of classic horror, with next-generation storytelling and gameplay. A must-play for fans of twisted tales, nerve-wracking exploration, and desperate combat. A Story That Challenges Reality Envisioned by Mikael Hedberg, acclaimed writer behind modern horror classics “SOMA” and “Amnesia”, Alone in the Dark’s intricate web of mystery delves into themes of trauma, faith, evil, and abandonment. Whether you choose to brave the nightmare as Emily or Edward, you will uncover secrets that defy everything you thought about videogame storytelling. Explore Derceto Manor in this reimagination of Alone in the Dark, a love letter to the 90’s cult classic horror game. Return to the roots of psychological horror and experience an atmospheric journey worthy of the game that started the genre. Dive into a world full of sounds that make your skin crawl with a haunting, yet mesmerizing doom jazz soundtrack. Enjoy the thrill of desperate survival in a world where reality starts to crumble, evil lurks in every shadow and ammunition is scarce. Experience this nightmare from either Emily Hartwood’s or Edward Carnby’s perspective and unearth the dark secrets of a gothic mansion. Immerse yourself in a deep psychological story that goes beyond the realms of the imaginable, by Mikael Hedberg, cult horror writer of SOMA and Amnesia. See Emily and Edward brought to live by the Hollywood talent of Jodie Comer (Killing Eve, Free Guy) and David Harbour (Stranger Things, Black Widow), who lend their voices, their appearance, and their formidable acting skills to the protagonists.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is splendid. The surroundings and characters constantly give you the impression that something is off. The story was complex and unfolded progressively throughout the game. The action sequences could have been done a bit better (maybe introduce a first person mode when shooting/encountering monsters).
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Really good gamePros- Creepy atmosphere, the music and ambience sets the mood nicely both in the calm and creepy areas - Sound design, guns actually sounds impactful- Story, not bad and needs play throughs with both characters to get it all- Puzzles, playing on unassisted mode and it was really fun figuring out the more difficult ones, although some are very easyCons- Melee has little feedback, weapons just swings right through enemies - Can't store pick ups like Molotov's and bricks only hold them and move very slowly until they are thrown-  Some bugs, like after defeating 3 enemy monstrosities with a shovel and taking a victory hit from the hip flask like a hardened PI only to get legs stuck in a child's bike and had to reload
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, puzzles and atmosphear. Combat is a bit janky but not as bad as other reviews paint. The audio adds to the mood and makes it even creepier. If you like Lovecraft, you loved Eternal Darkness and in general you like psychological survival horrors, this game is definetely worth it. Just don't expect a game like RE, it's more like a mix between RE and Silent Hill (though Eternal Darkness is the closest)
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an enjoyable survival horror experience with good enemy design and level design. The game also has pretty good feeling combat as some of it its strengths. However constant visual stuttering and bugs plagued my first play through. Whenever I entered a new room I would experience noticeable visual stuttering. I would suggest you setup a frame counter to determine your lows and then cap your frames to that minimum in Adrenaline or NVIDIA control panel. This game has really nice looking graphics, featuring highly detailed textures and great looking character design. Props to the voice acting and dialogue as well. I will say that solving the puzzles in this game is too tedious to be fun though. Finding the correct combination/code requires serious effort as you have to back track to find key items and search through files for clues. Compared to the joy I get from puzzles in Resident Evil games, this game simply can't compete.The combat feels good in this game and the gun play feels fairly accurate. Ammo and healing items are fairly sparse which fits nicely with the survival horror genre. However it is worth mentioning you will probably get stuck on objects throughout your play through and have to re-load your save to get unstuck.  I wish they would fix these bugs as it really ruins the experience. All in all I'd say it's worth a play through, but maybe wait until it's on sale. I really don't approve of this game selling for the price of a triple A game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: its ooookkkkkkkkkk. lol there's a lot of negative things that I really think they could have done better, but there's also a lot of moments that felt really great. I feel like they should've pushed things further because there's parts where it certainly DOES go there, but then just kinda pulls back. It's a decent experience. Wait for a good sale though for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a "lovecraftian detective" story experience, not a survival horror game. As a reimagining of the original game, I enjoyed it very much, but don't expect Resident Evil 2 Remake level of quality. Don't expect a shooter either, the combat is too wonky. i. e. this worked best for me: meet monster, run away to throwables placed in the level, throw them at monster, then shoot it once from afar, then sledgehammer to the face when it is up close. And then continue with the story...
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I recommend the game for fans of walking simulator type games The strong advantages of the game are as follows+ great atmosphere of the world referring to Lovecraft's writings+ visually impressive locations + motion capture of the game characters+ story told Elements correct, but giving a feeling of underdevelopment-  the game is relatively short, I play slowly and admire the views the passage of one character took me 10h - locations are linear- the storyline is linear - good, but repetitive puzzlesWeak aspects that caused negative feelings for me as well- not pleasant combat model, the character is sluggish, the combat strategy for each enemy is the same- Character control, sometimes the model would freeze, and it was necessary to load the save- Almost identical plot of both characters
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are overly simplistic, often involving just picking up an item and placing it in an obvious spot nearby. Combat is disappointingly poor for a modern game. It feels like most of the budget went to hiring actors, but it hasn’t improved the story quality at all. Only play this if you're a die-hard Alone in the Dark fan—otherwise, it might ruin your nostalgia for the series.Thank god its short!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome. Great atmosphere, puzzles, character depth, storyline and plot immersion. True homage to the original early 3D polygonal PC games that I loved back in the day, completely reimagined as a modern AAA title. The ability to play as these two actors (with different story experiences) is so cool. The 3D modelling and voice acting is particularly noteworthy. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Great throwback to 90s era survival games. Now let me preface this by saying that the game, especially combat is clunky but I personally think that is part of the charm of it all. The combat is the WORST part of this game so if that is your only focus skip on by, but I loved it start to finish clunkyness and all and thought that it was a great throwback to the original Alone In The Dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This is about as great of a re-imagining/remake of the original game. The combat is the only thing I would fuss about. It's not the worst, though it shortly lost any enjoyment half way through the game. The melee combat felt "meh" mostly just swinging wildly in the air(But this Carnby just never took pirate sword fighting lessons ^_^). Otherwise the real key selling points are the story and great motion capture/voice acting. Also seems to have a good extra replay value worthwhile to play both characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first game of the series.Great atmosphere, very good jump scares, the story is a bit confusing at times but I think that's exactly what you have to get involved in with this game. Combat mode could be a better, playing time a bit short BUT I can highly recommend it to anyone who likes dark stories with a certain amount of horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic AA horror game, albeit with some flaws. The game is 100% overpriced and should not be $60, especially with the ridiculous performance issues and multitude of bugs. I also can't justify that price with the lack of unlockable content. $40 would've been the perfect price for this game.(AN EDIT: The game has been patched to remove a lot of the bugs, and the shader cache issue has been addressed. Please take this into account - I appreciate their devotion to making the experience better.)Moving on from those criticisms, I wholeheartedly loved this game. The story is fantastic, classic Lovecraftian fare with a delightfully confusing story that feels rewarding to unwrap and digest. The characters are fun and well-acted - David Harbour particularly breathes a lot of life into Edward Carnby. The combat isn't fantastic or super engaging, but it's serviceable - combat is not typically what I go into survival horror for, so if it's functional I'm alright with it.(Silent Hill 2's combat is pretty bad, after all. And that's a perfect game in spite of it.)The atmosphere and tone are also fantastic. The soundtrack is perfect, and I found myself very immersed throughout the game - Derceto becomes very atmospheric once we approach night-time, and I adored the atmosphere and oppressive mood of the French Quarter, Hateful Mound, Cemetary, and Sunken Temple areas. Spoilers ahead.Some nitpicks: I wish the Dark Man were more present as a gameplay enemy, as I enjoyed the gimmick of him draining your health in the Toroella level. He could've been a lot scarier if he showed up more often outside of cutscenes.I also am mixed on the Ghouls, who aren't too differentiated from each other and all have the same "bones, gore, and mud" aesthetic. I do wish some more classic Lovecraft-type monsters, like the Deep Ones or the original games' zombie chickens, had appeared in some capacity. I also wish the big ♥♥♥♥♥♥ who appears at the end of Hateful Mound and in Emily's 4th chapter had gotten a proper boss fight.Finally, while I'm not too bothered by it, I do wish both routes had conformed with each other more rather than the Resident Evil 2 Remake style "both routes are their own canon" kind of deal. There are elements of the story that fit each route differently - the Dark Man and the Jeremy cutscenes feel much more natural in Emily's campaign, while Edward's route generally fits the slow reveal of the cult and Grace's character better. Part of me wishes the game had gotten more development time to flesh out each route and present them as "two sides of the same story," rather than "the story but with a different character."Overall this is a great survival horror game if you understand its scope and what you're getting into. I would love it more if they 1) patched out the bugs and frustrating graphical stuttering, and 2) lowered the price to a much more reasonable $40.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, but not that great. The atmosphere and graphics are good, but the gameplay is boring a lot of the time. It can be exciting when you have to handle a lot of enemies at once, but that doesn't happen very often, and the AI isn't very good. The story isn't the best either, and you often wonder about what the hell is going on. Still, it's an okay horror game worth getting at a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this title represents b-class psychological horror games. Puzzles were decent but weak combat didn't save the day. However the investigation like reading the notes was interesting same as puzzles since those were logical. Had to say that the second playthrough was much more fun than the first one. I believe it helps to enjoy the game when you know how to play the game right, heh.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Outstanding psychological horror with some mystery thrown in the mix. Some of the controls can be a little clunky on controller but its not game breaking. Hopefully a patch comes soon to fix alot of the stuttering, I don't get it all the time but I still get it occasionally and its quiet annoying. The story is very compelling and makes me want to come back for more. If you want a good horror game that makes you really think get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first entry to the series, so I'm coming in without nostalgia for the earlier entries.This game feels flat, bland, and overall unpolished in a way that really makes me wonder why it has mostly positive reviews at the time of writing.It oozes Resident Evil clone to its very core, though whether it was because of less funding, a smaller team, or a less experienced team, this just feels like a cheap imitation of what it wants to be while selling itself as an equal.This is a full price game, and price tags set expectations. The general animations in this game are bad, at times the facial animations can look like they were animated by Tim and Eric, the environments range from uninspired to okay, the dialogue is mostly uninteresting, David Harbor's performance is lackluster, his character design looks goofy and he just doesn't fit the role in my opinion. Then there's the combat. The combat is easily the worst aspect of this game.Melee weapons just don't feel satisfying to use. It looks and feels like a unity asset flip where you just float the weapon around rather than swinging it. It doesn't have any sort of weight or impact to the hit. Melee weapons also break very quickly, which in most games mean they are a precious commodity and can be used to stun, break a grapple, or overpower an enemy or two until it breaks. Not here though. It gets worse if you don't have one because aiming at something close to you is so imprecise, making it significantly more difficult to hit than something far away. Even while using a gun, it just doesn't feel satisfying. Compared to Resident Evil where it would throw a decent amount of enemies at you, forcing you to make a quick decision of target priority and stunning with head shots, Alone in the Dark only throws 1-3 at you at a time. Shooting enemies does not stagger them and your dodge lets you evade damage and clip straight through enemies. In fact, combat is rarely, if ever, even mandatory,  leaving it pointless to engage with combat at all.. You truly can just skip fights altogether if you want. When a core aspect of the game is given such little care or attention, it proves that this is not a $60 game.There are a whole bunch of puzzles in this game, and they aren't too bad. Some are really easy, some are frustratingly obtuse, but overall okay. If you select to play on "modern" mode rather than classic, the game will give you hints towards puzzles. Some hints are barely any help at all, others will outright tell you what to do if you haven't solved the puzzle in 3 seconds. Even so, these puzzles are not enough to carry this game.I don't recommend even thinking about picking this up for more than $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only chapter 2 but it's already clear this is an excellent survival horror game. The mansion, the keys, the collectibles, the music and presentation, it's all very engrossing and far beyond my low expectations. Also happy to report the game runs well on midrange hardware, beyond the shader stutter which is not as bad as I expected. Performance feels very much like the Dead Space remake. UPDATE -I was only an hour or so away from finishing this enjoyable survival horror game when I saw a subject line in the discussions - "NO NEW GAME PLUS OR UNLOCKABLES??" - and after looking into that and confirming it's true, my enjoyment comes to a full stop. Just shocking that a developer making a survival horror game doesn't understand the element of "here's a toy or two for the second playthrough". Why include 2 playable characters if there weren't reasons to replay.There are a lot of issues with the game I was enjoying as worthwhile symptoms of a lower budget game. The story is interesting enough but some dialog requires a lot of suspension of disbelief, the puzzles are hit and miss and the player is prone to getting stuck. These issues go from charming to infuriating with the understanding that the developer did not bother to include a reason to replay the game. They are just annoying flaws now, not fun quirks to be dealt with as you scour for secrets and unlock goofball stuff in a second or third run.I was on my way to give Alone In The Dark a glowing review but now I am frustrated at my own 40 dollar discounted GMG purchase. Absolutely not worth more than 30 dollars. Shocking disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: its pretty mid in all regards. not to say its bad but it def doesnt live up to the hype. the combat doesnt feel great, the puzzles go from literally just an actual puzzle to some random ♥♥♥♥ that is basically "finger♥♥♥♥ it till something happens". a lot of the time you will find a missing part in one room, then the thing it goes to literally in the next room. graphics, story, atmosphere... its all acceptable. if i were you id wait for a few bug fixes and a sale
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: hmm tough to say i give it a 6 maybe 7.5 out of 10.  Positive notes the game looks great, the sound, voice acting is very solid.  Moods, music is great. Attention to detail is very good as well.  Sadly, i kind of felt bored.  nothing new, everything it feels like I have done before. This game kinda does not know what it wants to be.  Is it a resident evil original game ?  A resident evil 4,  The old school alone in the dark ?  Well kind of a blend between all of them but nothing stands out.  The puzzles were just ok, I cheated on them honestly because the story was just not that great.  Kind of dragged on and on like this review lol.   Anyway, i forced myself to finish the game because I knew it was short so that helped me with the last 2 hours. Id suggest if you love these types of games which I do get it.  It has high production value,  but the guns, gameplay just does not make you want to play more and the so so story just makes you want it to be over.   Short game worthy it just do not expect a resident evil or deadspace, or the cutting edge alone in the dark like it was back in the 1990s.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good game, don't get me wrong, but in it's current state I've had to reload a certain section 5 times as I keep getting stuck within different barrels and walls. Until an update is released to address these collision issues, I just can't recommend playing it. _childDocuments_.review: A bit more mixed, as my experience playing through had highs and lows to be expected from a lower budget remake of a beloved survival horror staple. I LOVE how this game looks in every aspect.Music is solid.Cons:In my experience, the audio mixing during the final boss was awful. When transitioning to an otherworld section, I was spawned into a wall and had to reload to fix it.Game ran well at 4k 60fps on my 3060ti, but there is a stutter here and there that seems to be a game problem. _childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a "Thumbs Sideways" option for Alone in the Dark 2024.This game does a lot right, but also a lot wrong.PROS:- Puzzles range from all difficulties. They start out easy and progressively get harder and I love that feeling of progression.- The game gives a unsettling feeling which is great for a horror game.- Characters are gimmicky but in a charming way. Some people might say its lazy writing but I found it charming- Derceto Manor is fun to explore and collectibles are interesting (if you read the descriptions that are tied to them)- David Harbour does a good job with what he is given. Felt like I was playing Hopper from Stranger ThingsCONS:- Combat is VERY janky and frustrating. Feels like they kinda threw it on at the end of development and didn't put a lot of time into developing it- Every time a scene changes the game TANKS in frame rate. Most of the game ran at 60+ fps but every time a scene was changing, it would drop down to single digits at times on my NVIDIA 4070TI- Only 4 enemy types and none of them are interesting- Few missions bugged out for me and had me having to load either old saves or outright rebooting the game to fix it.Overall I think I would give Alone in the Dark 2024 a 6.5/10. Fun game for an initial play through, but not one I plan on going back to for a 2nd run.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edward|NG|Normal|Old School][Emily|NG+|Old School]+ The story is quite a bit steeped in Lovecraft mythos, just like the original. I thought it was pretty great, but recommend a first playthrough with Emily for a clearer picture, especially if you're not familiar with Lovecraft lore. Other than that, it's an intriguing mystery encased inside an atmospheric 1920s setting with a gorgeous aesthetic and a great mood and feel. It's mainly what carries the game in spite of some of its flaws. It has some jumpscares here and there, but I wouldn't call it scary overall. It relies on its eerie mood and atmosphere much more than on outright scaring you directly.+ The environments are gorgeous, both Jeremy's memories and the Derceto mansion itself, and the lighting is often stunning. Congrats to the lighting artists for sure, great stuff! The game showcases pretty great usage of Unreal Engine overall, especially for a AA game and talking strictly about the visuals; performance is another matter entirely >.<+ I thought the voice acting was excellent across the board, all fitting with the 1920s era and helping create convincing, mysterious characters.+ Puzzles were pretty great, well balanced in difficulty (at least for me), never frustrating but almost always satisfying to solve.+ I kind of like the decision to not be able to pick up throwable items (bricks, molotov cocktails). It forces you to pay attention to your surroundings, keep their locations in mind and have some spatial awareness of where you need to move to gain an advantage on the enemies. It adds a very slight tactical element to the otherwise generic combat that I appreciated.+ The gunplay is serviceable, guns have decent kick and feel good to use and aiming is snappy.- Melee on the other hand is very janky. There's no impact to your hits, so sometimes it's not even clear if your hit actually connected and the animation work involved really doesn't sell the action.- The final boss has some pretty awkward movement and animations as well. Again, the key word seems to be janky.- Some bugs were encountered in my two playthroughs, small visual issues and the main character getting stuck in collisions occasionally (only once with a reload required). Nothing game-breaking though, and no crashes.- Performance-wise, the game is a stuttering mess. It stuttered constantly across two playthroughs, on sudden camera movements, traversal, and transitions to cut-scenes. It's very likely not only PSO related and, with Unreal being used, it can be quite a number of things, but it's definitely frustrating and negatively impacts the experience (and ruins a jumpscare or two). I'm pretty tolerant to poor performance, for me it did not render the game unplayable, but I could understand how it would for others.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad per say, but it has serious flaws that made me decide not to finish it. Its worse flaw is that it performs absolutely awful. It was literally unplayable for me at launch due to the frequent stuttering, and it's still bad even after the patch. So much so that, when I shoot an enemy, the game freezes because it can't render that basic blood effect apparently (lmao). I can't aim because of the lag, cutscenes are frequently broken, and sometimes my character just disintegrates the fabric of reality. In addition to this, the combat is awful. The revolver Edward gets is so weak that it is practically unviable (I didn't play as Emily, so I don't know if she gets something different), melee is awkward with your character moving with every swing in a way that is sporadic and impossible to control (leading to you circling an enemy rather than hitting it),  and enemies can and will stunlock you in a corner where even dodging won't really get you out. The game genuinely made me sick to play, which is not something any game has ever done to me before. I think it was the bizarre effects the game has, down to subtly moving the camera when zoomed in to a puzzle. Turning off most of those effects allowed me to play the game without getting nauseous, and it may be some sort of problem unique to me. Regardless, I still want to warn any future players about this.The game is very overpriced. It should cost at most 40 USD, but instead the game is as expensive as a AAA game. Get it on sale if at all. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The short review:A third person adventure set in the jazz filled streets of 1920's Louisiana, that combines voodoo with the cosmic entities of HP Lovecraft. Mixing melee and shooting with survival horror, exploration and puzzle solving. Passable fun, but so, so, soooo "mid" in every regard bar the quality of its story-telling which is weirdly compelling. And even then it is just more Lovecraftian stuff at a time when Lovecraft is overused and dull. I don't regret my time playing it, but on the other hand there's nothing here that hasn't been done better elsewhere.The long review: Alone In the Dark was one of the earliest examples of survival horror, if not the first to be fully 3d and so give even more tension to the player through that level of immersion. It was one of the inspirations behind the creation of Resident Evil, and ever since that has been its cross to bare. It may have created the genre, or propelled it into gamers awareness. but here is a young upstart that just supercharged those expectations, and then did so again in a different way with Resi 4. From there the likes of The Evil Within and Dead Space took a look at what Resi did, and then said "hold my beer" before super-duper-supercharging the genre.Along the way a barely known game was made called Silent Hill, followed by a hardly remembered sequel of low quality, and bam! Suddenly AITD with its Lovecraftian horror was, like its inspiration, old-hat. In 2008 the series was reborn with the same name, but with a markedly different setting and approach to the horror genre. Personally I think its a very brave (though ultimately a bit wonky) attempt at innovation, and still is, to my mind, the most ambitious AAA horror ever released. Which was a very long-winded way of getting around to this remake, and the slightly disappointing end result when compared to competitors in the genre, or its previous entries that share the same name and legacy.The basis for this 2024 remake / re-imagining is sound;  as a template the mix of combat, exploration and puzzling is as tried and true as ever. Every single one of those horror contemporaries did exactly the same thing. The problem for AITD is that they did it better.What are you hoping for from this game? It's a third-person adventure with melee combat and shooting. The melee and dodging is basic, and weapons break quite quickly. For all its flaws Callisto Protocol did this with a smoother flow to the action, and whilst its technically reasonably sound, at a design level this is no more sophisticated than the playstation 1 days of standing there mindlessly whacking enemies. Do you like shotguns in horror games? I'm sure you do, you know, those shotguns where they obliterate parts of the enemy in a shower of gore and feel super-satisfying to shoot because of that very thing. Well....the shotgun here is sh*t, and the only reason that isn't really disappointing is the fact they eventually give you a tommy gun and that is a beast.Overall the shooting is okay, but nowhere near the slickness or intensity of Dead Space and Resi 4 Remake. Its fun, yet objectively its nowhere near as much fun as them. The narrative and reality-warping set-pieces afforded by cosmic horror are doing a lot of the heavy-lifting here, rather than in the game-play department which is fairly average.Stealth isn't something this game does, even when it does. Its basic and generally so short and easy as to be mere padding. The same can be said for the one vaguely memorable chase sequence that occurs. Again, these are nowhere near other games for intensity or execution, and sadly being pant-sh*tt*ngly terrifying just isn't something the game ever manages.Fun? yes. Weirdly intriguing due to its dreamy story-telling and odd plot? yes. Scary? nope. Thrilling?....??...I guess at around the half-way  point it picks up in intensity, but.....er...noooooo.To me it was a game I mostly enjoyed, yet could never shake off the nagging thought it could have been so much better. A pulse-pounding stealth sequence here (of proper merit, rather than the cheap efforts provided) and  a heart-attack inducing chase sequence there (like Cthulu Dark Corners Of The Earth did around 20 years ago!!!!), and this could have been amazing.Could have, would have, should have, but....uh...didn't. In the end this is a fairly safe reboot, and one that will probably be more appreciated by those unfamiliar with the games it shares its name with. Whilst this is obviously much better technically than the 2008 release, I am 100% sure that precisely none of it will stand out in my memory in years to come the way that games does. I don't want to be too down on it, as I am quite jaded and experienced in many years of horror games, but even now a mere few hours after finishing it I struggled to think of what I could highlight in this review. It's not bad and its slightly better than average (compared to, say, The Suffering or Cold Fear), but a great action game it is not, and it isn't scary or frantic either. Your mileage may vary of course, but even as a genre newbie I can't see this being frightening unless you have a very weak disposition. All that remains is whether the story grabs you, and to be fair that is its strongest element.

_childDocuments_.review: An Alone in the Dark game but your never "Alone" and never "in the Dark". Missed the mark on what made the original from 1992 an influence for the industry. _childDocuments_.review: As a developer of another Lovecraftian game, I would say that this is a perfect Survival Horror game (not an Action Horror like many modern games). It involves exploration, puzzle-solving, and survival. The combat isn't perfect, but it's adequate for the genre. The Lovecraftian elements and story are well-executed. Overall, it feels like a return to the roots. Remember, the very first Alone in the Dark (3D) was an inspiration for the Resident Evil series. So, in a way, the cycle has now come full circle. Please also keep in mind that developers have deadlines tied to funding and contracts with publishers. They've done their best to deliver a good product, but it appears there's still a need for optimization and additional QA. Hopefully, Pieces Interactive will fine-tune this, and the game will garner enough sales to become a classic in future. Let's stay positive, as games like these are hard to come by these days.

_childDocuments_.review: It's refreshing to play a title clearly made with love, with respect for the IP it's based on, that comes to you complete with no microtransactions and no in-game store. This is a really fun survival horror game with good writing, great voice acting, and a balance of humor, horror, and fun. It's not a perfect game by any stretch, but it's been a while since I played a single player game that felt as well-paced. Personally, I wish the puzzles had been a bit harder, but I saw some critic reviews saying they were too hard, so I suppose that means they're in a pretty good spot. There's some jank when interacting with the environment, and combat isn't smooth (but that's a survival horror tradition at this point). The game is perhaps a bit pricey for what you get, but still worth a buy now if you love the genre/David Harbour/Jodie Comer. If you don't, once it's on discount it'll 100% be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all releasing this on the same day as Dragon's Dogma 2 and the HZD: Forbidden West PC port while charging 60$ for it is crazy. Makes me think that people in charge of selling, marketing and distributing this game are not qualified for their jobs.With the above out of the way, tldr: Janky lovecraftian "Resident Evil" with less combat and more emphasis on puzzles and story. Just in case you don't know the original AitD come out before RE1 and kinda inspired the whole survival horror genre. - Environments and architecture are pretty great. Post-WW1 art deco aesthetic never fails to be beautiful, the places you visit have a lot of detail and flavor. - Voice acting is good to great. Lots of charming old timey accents. Every written note is voice acted too and even with different voices depending on the author. - Facial animations are the worst aspect of the game's visuals, stiff faces, dead eyes. They are bad even by janky mid-budget game standards which is a shame in such an otherwise moody and atmospheric game. Ironically NPCs seem to have better facial animations than the two playable characters.- Jazzy night club lounge music is very enjoyable and fits the game's aesthetic well. The horror related sound layer is pretty good too, there's almost always something clicking, scurrying and tapping around you during the horror segments, pretty unnerving with headphones. - Story is a fairly standard lovecraftian affair but it's well written and the characters are compelling, creepy and fun even if you don't get to know them that well. The game relies more on atmosphere and tension than gore. - Combat is....fine. Handgun, shotgun and tommygun, what else you do you need, right? There's a flare gun too but it comes late and is barely used. If you play on hard you might need to rely on the environment (throwable objects and such) and melee more or just run past some enemies. There's a dodge move that's pretty spammable and makes it relatively easy to avoid damage. You should get AitD2024 if you: like 1920s southern US decor and mannerisms, like Lovecraft, like puzzles and moody atmospheric experiences. You should avoid AitD2024 if you: hate puzzles, need a high variety of weapons and enemy types, can't stand janky gameplay or animations. AitD is enjoyable but its gameplay systems and produciton value are too thin for 60$, I really think THQ shot themselves (and more importantly the devs) in the knee with the pricing. I mean Resident Evil 4 costs 40$ for ♥♥♥♥'s sake.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Alone in the Dark, despite having very low expectations due to lukewarm critical reception. Having played through it twice I can say that the reviews were quite unfair, since many compared it to the Resident Evil remakes, which had much bigger budgets and were overall very different games.My favorite thing about Alone in the Dark is its atmosphere and setting. It goes for this jazzy, noir movie feel and pulls it off perfectly. Its not particulary scary, but it did succed in building tension and unease, that reaches a very satisfying climax at the finale.Main marketing point was of course the leading duo with David Harbour as detective Edward Carnby and Jodie Comer as Emily Hartwood, which I considered a waste of budget before game release, but I must admit that their performance greatly adds to the experience. Unfortunately the other characters are a bit underwhelming in comparison as they are not as well rendered and their actors can't match performance of the main characters.I played entire game twice, back to back with both characters to see the differences between the playthroughs. Gameplay differences are minor and each character gets only one, about an hour long sequence unique to them, but the cutscenes and the story perspective are very different. I really enjoyed that, but I wish the gameplay differences were more substantial and if I had to choose, I'd prefer one playable character in a longer game instead.Gameplay wise its pretty standard third person horror with over the shoulder perspective. Moving around feels good, but sneaking and combat are pretty janky. I found stealth to be nearly useless throughout the game as its way too slow and combat animations often got in the way of gameplay, with some weird hitboxes and both me and enemies getting stuck in environment. It didn't happen too often, but it was pretty jarring when it did. Actual shooting feels good and punchy, with strong recoil, which discourages going full auto and makes you consider every shot. Melee on the other hand is just plain bad, with its stiff animations and weird delay between hits. I played on Hard which made enemies more resilient and resources very limited, amplifying the survival aspect in this survival horror.Outside of combat you'll be exploring very nicely rendered and diverse areas, with many puzzles to solve along the way. I did not expect the kind of location variety this game threw at me and I suggest avoiding any spoilers, its really worth experiencing yourself. Puzzles mostly consist of jigsaw puzzles, deciphering codes and finding numbers in environments. They weren't too hard, but I found them satisfying and nice change of pace.Overall I highly recommend Alone in the Dark to any survival horror fan out there. Its criminal that this game didn't get the acclaim it deserved. Sure, its a bit janky and short, but it more than makes up for it with great amosphere, story and level design. Unfortunately Pieces Interactive, the studio making this game is no more, since Alone in the Dark failed to meet sales expectations of the publisher. This is a sad reality of game development, where solid, niche games like this get overshadowed by money making, soulless abominations like First Descendant or Once Human.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre project that relies on a once-glorious title from the past, back when computer games were crafted by teams of creative geniuses. The graphics are dreadful, and the game design issues are even worse. The narrative, filled with flat characters, clashes with the use of real actors' appearances. The plot and its presentation are laughable. Boss battles are atrocious, and the puzzles are inconsistent, just like the rules for interacting with the game world. Overall, this project retains nothing from the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the devs were given more time to polish and expand but whats here is solid AA material. It got rushed because of Embracer's BS but hopefully the devs can keep making stuff like this.The "visible seams", so to speak, are the jank of the melee, and the lack of variety between enemies and campaigns. _childDocuments_.review: When you consider how every sequel and reboot of the 1992 classic Alone in the Dark has only been passable at best, it is a thrill to finally have a game that does one the originators of the survival horror genre justice.The story and characters remain engaging throughout, with plenty of great vocal performances throughout, and the remade Derceto (and the other locations you visit) look great. There's also some brilliant period-appropriate music throughout, while the combat is... serviceable, though not a big focus of the game.If I have complaints, I'd say that it's a shame Carnby's and Hartwood's campaigns are almost identical. There are differences in cutscenes and part of chapter 4 plays out differently depending on who you play as, but for the most part the two protagonists tread the same path. Just a minor complaint, as that was also the case in the original and a lot of games that followed in its wake, but it's still slightly disappointing that there isn't more difference between the two.A bigger complaint is the price, which I think is too high for a game that is pretty short and I would consider mid-range. Mind you, with Triple-A games now costing over sixty quid these days, the £45 mark is probably the kind of price we can expect from middle-tier games these days.Still, if you're a fan of survival horror, or you're a fan of Alone in the Dark who's been burned by previous entries, this return to Lovecraftian form is absolutely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: To the point================A criminally overpriced mediocre revival of a beloved horror franchise. Get it on a deep sale or not at all.+ cleared on hard difficulty +Good Stuff==================- Dercetto is a great setting for the game, I really did enjoy exploring it and it game me strong Eternal Darkness and RE7 vibes. It's a shame that they didn't make it a little more 'funhouse' like with secret passages etc. The dreamland environs are also really great looking and atmospheric but they're just too small with one of them being a proverbial straight line.- The soundtrack is very authentic, if not poorly paced. The Jazzy tracks for the cast is very fitting but they have the habit of coming on at very weird times. Like right after spitting in Cthulhu's eye probably isn't the best time for an upbeat mardi gras style song.- I know it's a collect-a-thon but I did like the Lanappe and finding them throughout the environs. The first set you unlock gets you a powerful gun so I was hoping each would give you something neat but 90% of them are just dumb text blurbs, I mean at least give us some upgrades or something.Bad Stuff===================- I know Embracer group will never read this but how on God's green earth do you greedy slimebags get off charging $60 for this game?! I could name a handful of indie survival horrors with more love and attention to detail in the first 30 minutes then this title has in its entire run time. I guess it doesn't matter since you shuttered the studio immediately after the release of this game but you are the sickness killing gaming- The story is truly awful, when looking at an A and B scenario like Resident Evil 2, you can at least say with certainty that while you don't have all the answers after playing a single scenario, that you were compelled to at least try the other. No such drive here, the story barely has time to breathe jumping from one dull and predictable moment to the next which is a shame because I actually liked most of the characters, but everything's is so rushed and jumbled. Why did anything even happen in this story? Who knows or cares?- The combat, at least on hard, is completely terrible. Enemies are bullet and melee sponges and react to your attacks like a brick wall. They also make no sense damage wise as the early enemies take around 5-6 bullets to kill but these small crawler enemies in the end game take 7 or more.- There is a stealth mechanic that teeters between 'completely useless' with you being spotted immediately or 'super broken' walking in front of idling enemies without them even reacting.- The enemy variety is not great. There are roughly 4 humanoid and 2 bug enemies that all move and attack in bear identical fashion. Also having them completely in plain sight near constantly kind of removes any feeling of fear or dread.- The bosses, again on the hard difficulty, seem near unbeatable. I was throwing bricks at the final boss after running out of bullets early. They have obvious weak points but attacking them doesn't seem to do a whole lot more then attacking them normally.-There are just a ton of janky bugs in this game, enemies will sort of slip and slide around while trying to find you, sometimes melee attacks will clip you into walls or, when running from something, you'll run on top of an invisible obstacle and get stuck until the physics engine pushes you off.- This one is particularly brutal : The character movement. You character is painfully slow making exploring the various environs a chore, even worse when trying to evade enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised to see the steam reviews are only mostly positive. I'm going to try to review the game not as a reaction to disagreement, but on its own. I played the game on hard, switching to standard midway through; and played on the "old school" puzzle style. Overall, I really enjoyed the game. It takes inspiration from Resident Evil in exploration and a bit of The Last of Us in combat. The puzzles are solid and very solveable, I only had one that I got caught up on and I did not need to look anything up. The sound design and the lighting were absolutely immaculate. Seriously, the sound design is a huge highlight. Actors did a great job. 99% of all animations were fluid and great. Story was very interesting, lovecraftian spoiler stuff also super cool. . From what I can tell, there are multiple endings and different things for which main character you play, so I'll definitely be doing at least one or two more play-throughs.Below I have some criticisms, but anything not mentioned was pretty great!Bugs: I only encountered minor 2 bugs in the entire game: Water making flashlight light wonky, and getting stuck on some geometry (quickly resolved by messing around or reloading from a rapidly set autosave). Performance was steady and high throughout on maximum settings, but I have a very good PC. PC Portage: Some of the default buttons are weird, and it was a little confusing to figure out what button to heal and switch weapons was at first, since its shown with a D-padCombat: It isn't the focus, but plays an important role to prevent the player from feeling comfortable. It completes that role well, but the combat is a bit lackluster-  the melee combat in particular. I also wish that you could hold a throwable without having to hold Q and move at a snails pace. That said, I found  very satisfying, intense, and generally really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why I continued to finish this game. Had barely motivation to keep walking forward. In times of RE and SH remakes, Alone in the Dark will stay in the dark. The setting is interesting, the story dull and bland. Gameplay is a combo of RE and SH. The 2 main characters are not fun at all to play. Sure, they don't win the game character beauty contest, but come on can you please make this any less mediocre? Either way, the game flopped hard and was not fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the 90´s, Alone 1 and 2 were one of my favorite games. The mechanics were new, intriguing, and the atmosphere was unique! Even with the 3rd game, although the setting wasn't my favorite. But by 2008, I felt it had lost what made the game so appealing. The modern take made it, paradoxically, more like games that were inspired by the first 2 or 3 Alone in the Dark games.All that to say, I am a nostalgic fan of the saga just exited by this game existing.Now after playing it, so far... although I don't have the latest gamer PC, I can play with settings in high mostly, and it runs pretty good. Had to make some minor changes while playing to make things go smoother, but nothing too drastic.My favorite part is that the 1920/1930 atmosphere is back! The attention to detail, and the love for the original games really shows. Also a big fan of David Harbour so that added a bit extra to make this game one of the best remakes I have played... so far.As a nostalgic fan I have to say I am very pleased.

_childDocuments_.review: WE WANT A REMAKE OF THE ORIGINAL - NOT THIS!!OMG... What in hell did you do to one of my favourite games from my childhood!! I played this game the year it release in 1992 and recently replayed it. Still an amazing game with era appropriate levels of jank.THIS "re-imagining" is NOT Alone in the Dark. All they had to do was to make a Resident Evil style remake of the original and expand and improve where needed and you would have had the beginning of a bright future for this franchise - after all, this game quite literally inspired Resident Evil...PROS:- Beautiful Graphics- Jodie Comer made a good EmilyCONS:- NOTHING in this game is remotely scary or provokes even a slight sense of tension or unease- The plot and story were absolutely terrible and made no sense- The entire game should have been set during the night. Light does not = scary...- Decerto kinda looks like Decerto. But not faithful enough to the original- David Harbour is NOT a good choice to play Edward Carnby (where was the moustache!)- Shooting is passable. But melee is atrociously bad...- Throwable implementation was horrible- Enemies were laughably unscary. They didn't even make sense within the story!- Soundtrack missed the mark. Jazz?? In a horror game? Seriously???- Large portion of the game not even set within Decerto. Other dimensional travel WTAF??- Having Decerto as a lived in space instead of a deserted and haunted space was the biggest mistake here. Decerto was supposed to make you feel trapped and Alone in the Dark. Not hanging out with folks for dialogue that never helps develop the plot in any kind of way!I could not even finish this game. Its like Bloober games got their hands on it. So now its all supernatural themes with rooms changing around with a completely nonsensical plot.I am so damn sad that this is where this franchise finally landed. PLEASE someone just remake the original "FAITHFULLY!!!". And in case you wonder what that looks like... HERE:- A Resident Evil style Lovecraftian inspired survival horror experience- Decerto is a COMPLETELY deserted, decrepit, old, evil and horror filled mansion- A story based on the occultist pirate Captain Ezechiel Pregzt who's spirit still haunts the house in search of a new body: namely yours...- 2 Characters only - Edward & Emily.- Arriving at dusk, you become trapped within the mansion! As night closes in you have to find a way to defeat the evil or die Alone in the Dark...- Set the game ONLY during the night.- Puzzle solving and door keys to find of course!- Now use modern graphical technology with ray tracing and make this a gloomy, scary and horror filled experience where Decerto resembles a house that should be condemned. And fill it with scary as hell monsters including the undead crew of Captain Pregzt who still serve their Captain.THAT'S HOW YOU DO ALONE IN THE DARK "THE REMAKE"
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: While the game might not be as polished as Capcom's RE Remake series, from what I've played so far it's been fun. It apparent that they've taken heavy influence from the Resident Evil Remake games,But saying that the original Resident Evil game took heavy influences from Alone in the Dark. The gameplay is very similar to the mentioned Resident Evil games, so if you're a fan of that you'll feel at home with this. This game does take a more investigative approach as to how to solve the puzzleswhere you need to read some of the notes lying around to gather enough informationto form a conclusion to a solution. The game definitely has a more 'Noire' feeling as well. So it doesn't take place just in the mansion. As the story unravels you'll visit different placesbased off of the "memories" of your uncle via a talisman, as he's being potentially possessed by a 'Dark Man' which you'll read know more about throughout the game. And those areas are essentially 'twisted' memories of places that he remembers, but somehow the people he knows appear in those places too, being *Alone in the dark* with otherworldly monsters.The game can be spooky, the audio design's pretty good and the surround sound is nothing to complain about either. A short and sweet review, it's a recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: It really drives that old school survival horror adventure gameplay, with a reality-bending story. It will depend if you enjoy that type of gameplay, yet it stays true to it. Quality story and characters. Explore, investigate and find objects. There's both ranged and melee combat. It's not scary horror, but more an investigating thriller. It brings back an old game to modern standards. I don't have any performance issues with it myself and can run it smoothly at 4K HDR with 120 FPS (Epic settings) when using DLSS (Quality). I have V-SYNC disabled, but am using a G-SYNC monitor. Some people complain about stuttering however on different PC specs, so check your hardware and use the latest graphic card drivers. There was also a patch released right after the game first launched, so update it.
