_childDocuments_.review: Having finished Carnbys side of the story my verdict is mixed, it's a solid modern survival horror game, however i feel that the game missed several aspects of the original series that made it so unique. This game does not feature any traps like you would run into in the classic games, the varied and unique enemy design has also been foregone for more generic monsters. (RIP to the ballroom ghosts and animated armor displays, they will not be in the game)In the very least they retained the melee system with breakable weapons and plenty variety to choose from.Most of the puzzles i found to be well designed apart from 1 that had me stumped for a little while (It's the warehouse safe, if you know you know)When it comes to the environments they are beautifully crafted and truly a feat to behold, however i also at the same time feel it doesn't quite evoke the same mood as the classic games do, but perhaps that's just not possible with the graphics used. The caves under Derceto are for example not used in this game.I will also make a short note regarding the use of celebrity actors for the main characters, i find that it somewhat detracts from the experience as i can only see the actors and not the character they're supposed to embody, i also wish they had used carnbys classic look redheaded with moustache and all.All in all i do still recommend this game if you enjoy survival horror, but do bear in mind that the "horror" part in survival horror is rather weak in this game, and it is what i would consider rather loosely based on the source material and retains mostly the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a truly impressive reboot, while also remaining faithful to the groundbreaking original. I honestly feel it isn't getting the credit and player-base it deserves.Alone in the Dark follows Edward Carnby and Emily Hartwood as they ominously arrive at Decerto in search of Emily's missing uncle; tell tale signs of dark curse linger over the Hartwood family. The story kept me intrigued throughout; clues such as letters or diaries flesh out the lore, while also being voice acted too. Puzzles and lagniappes further clue the player in on this world but never directly illustrate just what on earth is going on, which keeps the suspense alive. Just like the original, Lovecraftian themes are woven throughout.Now we have talked about the story, what about the graphical might that brings this world to life?I must start off by stating just how well modelled the Decerto mansion is, it oozes atmosphere and I had great fun exploring it. Subtle jazz music plays at points, while each and every room feels believable, it seeps that 1920's/30's Great Depression style. The mansion isn't the only place you will be exploring however, I won't spoil it, but it perfectly varies up the pace and adds variety. In terms of character models, David Harbour and Jodie Comer have been mo-capped in their respective roles; they both look great, unfortunately, it is where the other character models fall down as they definitely do not look as good as the two main protagonists. However, this did not sully my enjoyment because everything else looks honestly top tier.Gameplay wise, you will be solving puzzles with combat sprinkled here and there, where as this ramps up in later chapters. Combat is fine albeit nothing groundbreaking, my main enjoyment of Alone in the Dark came from its narrative and puzzle solving. The length of the game is around 20 hours for absolute full completion, in my personal opinion I have feel I have got my worth but this my vary individually of course.My final verdict is that Pieces Interactive have done a damn fine job and I hope they get to make a sequel and continue the franchise, sales makes games now but Pieces have proven they are passionate about Alone in the Dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a very solid game and I enjoyed the experience throughout. Though I never expected it to set the world on fire so to speak (and it doesn't) what we have here is an incredibly faithful, true reimagining of the 1992 classic. Those who have played that game before will clearly see the intricate ways how scenes from the original game have been taken apart and put together in new and exciting ways. It has atmosphere, it has charm, it has quality. It's all very Lovecraftian in the best of ways. As far as downsides go, there is really just the one. The combat really is quite bad. Luckily, for about 95% the game knows where it's strengths lie and uses combat very sparingly and at just the right moments. The only really bad thing about the game is the ending encounter. It is so frustratingly difficult due to the restraints the combat puts on you that it can get increasingly tedious and results in the fun getting sucked right out. I had to resort to changing the difficulty to easy just to stop me from haven an increasingly bad experience. Of course this immediately resulted in the encounter being such a cakewalk I could practically finish it with my eyes closed. Seems like a balancing issue. So, not a good way to end your game, even though the story round up is quite satisfactory.Overall though? It's good. Pick it up if you like survival horror, Lovecraftian adventures and early 20th century sleuthing.

_childDocuments_.review: I will echo another reviewer and say how awful it is that all involved in making this game will have no chance to ever improve on it further. There is so much greatness here that just needs some refinement.Back when this released, I was smart enough to watch a gameplay video and was instantly hooked. In my younger years I was an adventure gamer - easily spooked and slow to react, but fascinated with the creepy, the mysterious, the atmospheric. AITD, in all its disturbing and slow-moving glory, appeals to both my younger self and who I am today. I love nothing more than uncovering a story buried in history's annals.Each environment is crafted with so much care and love, right down to the period-accurate push-button light switches. Even with very little to find, the rooms and larger locations give off something so complete that it doesn't feel especially disappointing when you unearth nothing more than a box of 3 shotgun shells. After all, you're in another world, and you don't simply pick up and pocket everything in real life, right?I enjoyed all actors' performances, though I will say that the dialogue could sound extremely anachronistic at times (more on the anachronisms later). Much has been said of the high-profile actors and motion capture being ultimately wasteful - and this may be true - but it contributed something especially absorbing to the cast.On the topic of much being said, I've also seen a lot of theorizing, wondering, and general confusion around the story. To me, that's the perfect sweet spot for a mystery/horror game. I would be disappointed if I were looking to find out who killed Mr Ratchet on the Orient Express, but - we're in a world where nothing makes sense, on purpose. I was so thrilled and fascinated to ponder the little details and obscure facts that I learned; it only made me wish there were more. While I didn't buy the Director's Commentary DLC, I may well do so in the hopes of learning even more.My only real issue here, wrapped as it is around all this amazing experience, is with the combat. On easy mode it's bearable - two or three shots to kill most enemies, and they stand around kind of swaying for a few seconds to give you plenty of time. On New Game+, which I tried for about half an hour, it takes seven shots for a basic enemy; you find boxes with only one bullet in them; a melee weapon will break after killing only ONE basic enemy; the amount of enemies and their speed are increased; and all of this is only emphasized by the awkwardness of movement and the way the hit animations will keep you in some kind of stun lock, unable to aim and sometimes getting stuck on the enemy instead of fleeing. Very quickly I found myself wondering how I should even deal with it - stealth was obviously supposed to take precedence, but what do you do when you have one bullet left and three enemies just burst out at you? The answer is, go back to easy mode.More minor, but just as important for me, are the anachronisms dotted throughout the game. They're mostly in the dialogue, not necessarily in the word choices but just the way characters phrase their thoughts and choose to speak. I wasn't expecting an actual 1930-accurate experience, Mid-Atlantic accent and all, but it was strange to see how well-done the written materials were in comparison to the spoken word. On some occasions, the dialogue even felt vaguely disconnected from itself - I think that may have been on purpose, though, given the themes; the more you go along, the more you feel that everyone else is living in a different world than yours.And also...the music. Striking as it is, evocative as it is, it did not mesh properly with the world of the game. I'm speaking specifically of the "film noir" jazz sprinkled throughout. That style simply did not exist in 1930 (plus, there are so many old records from the 1920s that could have been used for diagetic music instead of random classical pieces). If I may digress:In general, I've found that the 1920s through 1955 or so are compressed by the public consciousness into flappers, fedoras/trilbys, a couple of gangsters saying "see?", Marilyn Monroe, Frank Sinatra, some Casablanca, and WWII-era things like Rosie the Riveter and maybe some pin-up photos. The issue is that all of those icons had their own time, their own era of sorts - flappers in the 20s, that portrayal of gangsters in the early 30s, Marilyn in the early 50s, and so on. Squashing it all together is how we get Henry Mancini scoring a game set in 1930.So: for someone who doesn't know the details of those periods, it's a game with old-fashioned technology, co-starring a detective in an old-fashioned hat, and featuring some cool jazz music because that's what old-fashioned detective movies play. And if you enjoyed it for that reason, then I'm glad - I just turned off the music and had fun playing some of my own. (Plenty of old late 20s records have been digitized, so it's easy to pick songs that don't sound like they'd be in The Shining.)I was lucky enough to not encounter any major glitches, even on my older hardware (on which it runs very well with mostly medium settings and the blessing that is the Pre-Load Shaders setting turned on). There was some stuttering, which I understand is an issue for many players, but it didn't render anything unplayable.Ultimately I was totally captivated by this game, and even without New Game+ I remain so. If you are willing to look past some quirkiness - and maybe even put more effort into the combat than myself - to get a strange, vaguely disturbing and sometimes very thought-provoking experience, then I highly recommend it. Thanks to everyone who worked at Pieces Interactive for putting their hearts into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal story, written by the same writer as Soma, an absolute love letter to the original games, has some great references to the original games. This is not a full survival horror so don't expect some form of deep inventory management, its considerably more on the slow burn side with plenty of complex puzzles that require deep thinking, some are more nonsensical but they are 100% solvable if you pay close attention to the details between the lines.Combat may seem more on the clunky side if you focus too much on the comparisons between Resident Evil 4, You are not Leon S Kennedy, you are Detective Carnby or Emily Hartwood, You don't roundhouse kick zombies and parry chainsaws you fight with the same technique as anyone would just wildly swinging a pipe
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is an enjoyable horror title, notable for its smooth mechanics, interesting setting, and curious mood. While the gameplay won't be surprising to anyone who has played Resident Evil 2, the gameplay consists of a combination of exploring moody mostly-linear environments and puzzling around an ever-changing mansion. There is combat that is shallow, but never annoying, and the focus on a limited selection of melee and ranged options adds tension effectively.The standout feature is the atmosphere and tone of the game, which renders Louisiana of the the early 1900s in a wonderfully swampy fog. The music and writing combine to create a languid feeling of unease, and yet there are moments that are slyly funny, too. Overall, I recommend Alone in the Dark. The experience is more subdued than Resident Evil, which I compared it to earlier, but that difference is not without its charms.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ... ok. That's it. I often heared about it that it is the best Alone in the Dark Game since the very first one.I got to say I haven't played any AitD game before this one, but if this game is the best since then, then go_d damn the series must be bad.So what are my problems with the game:-the game is like never scary, not even close-the story is a confusing mess-combat really isn't great, quite clunky, especially melee-technical problems:   -performance is very unstable, stuttering is quite common   -sound issues-it's barely a survival horror game, you could even argue it's not even a true one which is kinda funny when people often say the og game was the very first survival horror game. _childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Love it. Old-school handmade (semi-realistic, but it shows it's handmade and not photogrammetry) graphics, well acted voiceovers, good animations. Great Weird Tales style Lovecraftian atmosphere. Puzzles are easy, so you don't get stuck on them all the time. It's exactly like I like it, an adventure game.It's not a puzzle game, and not a shooter, so if you were hoping for something like RE4 meets Mist, then it is simply not that. It is more like a walking sim where you have to shoot an occasional monster or do a very simple jigsaw-puzzle.As for bugs - got stuck in geometry one time. Thankfully the games autosaves like every 10 meters, so no biggie.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, there is no incredible variety regarding the enemies and there are really few boss fights, but the visuals are great, the puzzles are neat and the story is really intriguing. For me the game was at its strongest when it started shifting between dimensions, leaving me with this major puzzle: trying to piece together what is happening in this place. I for one had a great, yet admittedly short, time with this. Definitely would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game. It's modeled off the remakes of RE2+3 (which those originals were modeling off of AITD, a cool twist). The combat feels good and punchy, but ultimately the enemies aren't very scary and neither is much of anything in the game. Loading screens are minimal. The game does suffer from the occasional stutter. Going through doors when you are trying to backtrack is, sigh, slow - they really should let you barge through doors like in the RE-makes. Also, it feels like there are still a couple of bugs with the map/collections that are annoying, as it is very easy to find yourself locked out of a collectible because it wasn't clear it was required to be collected at a certain point. Then in future chapters, some doors are arbitrarily locked for no other reason than, literally, who knows, so the rooms with remaining items are still inaccessible but very much obvious from your map.But, this game shines with the puzzles. They should have never included a directed mode, as it basically solves every puzzle for you, making the greatest bit of content in the game simply bypassed for the sake of appealing to a wider audience. It is best to just play unassisted, and enjoy the beautiful environments, solve puzzles, and be happy that you finally get to play as Jodie Comer (David Harbour too, I guess...)!I would love to see a sequel with these 2 characters in it!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks pretty good, both graphics and design, and the sounds and music are very well done as well, but that's it. Way too many problems bring this down to no recommendation level as far as horror is concerned.The story's not very interesting. The way it's told, the premise and the setting somewhat are, but it's really just your standard Lovecraft plot, to keep it spoilerfree. There's a bunch of characters that get introduced and seem interesting at first, but then you barely ever meet them and they end up being mostly irrelevant. It's also kind of sad they apparently blew a lot of budget on two Hollywood actors for the protagonists and then don't give them much to work with. For instance, at no point during the game do they give the impression they think they are in danger or at least somewhat scared. Mild surprise from time to time is the height of emotional reaction you'll see.Which brings us to the main problem with this game: it's simply not scary. It's not missing it by much, because the game is moody and well presented, but it's still missing the mark. Big issue for me was that during your exploration of the mansion, you're never really in danger and you know it. Sure, there are one or two instances in which realities overlap for a short moment, but it's not enough to make you feel unsafe. What the game does instead is that you get teleported to rather linear combat levels somewhere else at fixed moments in the story, but unfortunately, the combat is so poorly done that it's more annoying than intimmidating. What little horror the game manages to build up flies out of the window the moment you need to lift your weapon against a monster for the first time. Those looking rather goofy, doesn't help much, either.The other main aspect of the gameplay are the puzzles. While the puzzle density is adequate, the puzzles themselves never go beyond the type of generic videogame puzzles you've solved a ton of before. In addition to that, the protagonists tell you how to solve them without asking or warning, even with puzzle help turned off in the options.So overall, this game is one missed opportunity after another. It has it's heart in the right place, but never lives up to its potential. You could have an entertaining time with it regardless and enjoy the atmosphere, but the actual game is mediocre at best and especially as a horror game, it is a failure.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre, Janky. Those are the two things that come in mind after finishing the game with both characters on hard combat difficulty along with old school guidance difficulty. While this is certainly a better game than the memeable disaster from 2008 it feels unpolished and almost unwilling to commit to being a horror game.As mentioned above there are two characters Emily Hartwood and Edward Carnby, after a brief intro scene you get to choose which character you play as but unfortunately the execution here is less than stellar as both of the characters play through the same core storyline and gameplay segments. Although each character offers a slightly different perspective/version of the events through cutscenes along with some minor changes related to their personal storylines and a brief unique gameplay section in the penultimate chapter of the game but around 90% of the gameplay content you experience remains the same regardless of the character.This is also reflected quite heavily in the playtime as for example my first playthrough as Emily took me around 6.5 hours and my 2nd playthrough as Edward took me only 3 hours 18 minutes which included watching all the cutscenes. That being said I very much preferred Emilys version of the story as I felt it worked better with the core narrative and its themes.So what does the game do well? Environments are one of the highlights and there are quite a few areas that are gorgeous, cutscenes are well directed, voice acting across the board is quite good and puzzles managed to strike a good balance between too easy or too tedious although there are a couple exceptions and issues with puzzle repetition.Unfortunately Alone in the Dark really falters on two important fronts combat and horror, former simply feels unpolished due to lack of proper fit feedback, half baked melee system, bad enemy animations and overall boring enemies that pose very little threat. The latter on the other hand suffers from myriad things that prevent you from really getting immersed in to the game: Gameplay flow is often interrupted by cinematics, game often wrestles the control of your character away from you for a brief moment such as to load a scene, dialogue or if it needs you to focus on something etc.In addition to that sound mixing also is of the variety where loud equals scary which I often find to detract from the atmosphere as I personally find it more annoying than scary. This in combination with a recurring looping audio bug where some sound effects stack on top of each other leading to an ear splitting cacophony took me out of the game quite a few times.Aside from that I have to admit that the narrative as a whole did not really work for me, much of it felt derivative and a bit too much of a been there done that especially when it ends up repeating some of the mistakes that many games borrowing a little too much from H.P. Lovecraft do but at the end of the day your mileage may wary and some may find the narrative to be compelling.What about the PC port then? I would say it could be described as functional but with some issues such as traversal/loading stutters and with some oddities like displaying a HUD element with dpad icon when you are playing with KB/M or things such as assigning holding "I" as a shortcut for opening the map instead of using a separate key such as "m" for it. That being said I don't feel like Alone in the Dark is worth recommending at its current price point as it is a short and unpolished experience with little to none replay value. Horror enthusiasts will likely end up playing the game either way at some point as most of us tend to play a lot of horror games regardless of their quality but for those new to the genre you can get a whole lot of actually good horror games for 60€/$ instead of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little rough around the edges, but overall it's really good. Feels like a bit of a hybrid of Alone in the Dark and Eternal Darkness, with gameplay that is obviously inspired by the RE2 remake, but with some additional mechanics like melee combat. It's the kind of survival horror game that you used to get back in the early 2000s, and IMO it's the best Alone in the Dark game.Now in fairness, some of the mechanics are a little undercooked such as stealth, and combat is... okay, but not great. The weapons sound great and have punchy animation, but enemy hit responses are a bit flat. The puzzles are sometimes a bit rote. These aren't deal-breakers, but they are areas that could be refined.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Alone in the Dark, ending the game with both characters and enjoying some of the bonuses I get to the conclusion that "professional! critics went to hard on this game. It is a good game, with puzzles, the combat while a bit flawed and simple compared to other games of the genre, but enough to be entertaining. In general I think this game have some bugs that could be avoided and some little details that could be polished. In general this is a good game and a very good reimagining of the classic. I got entertained all the way through and the level design was good.  I am glad I gave this one a shot and ignored the critics that really want to standardize the industry rather to consider classic and different experiences fairly. I recommend for all survivor horror fans, it's a decent entry to the Alone in the Dark series and a great improvement from previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the technical issues (stutters and sound issues) I am having a great time with this game. It really shows that it's an homage to the first 3 games. I guess you need to have played the originals to appreciate this one fully. AitD 1 and 3 were some of my favourite games i played as a kid and this one sends strong vibes. Some complain about the combat, I think it's just right, Carnby is an alcoholic, out of shape and Emily is no girl boss so combat is clunky and slow. However you don;t have that many encounters if you want to play on the normal difficulty (there's no point in being masochistic in this game). Story is pretty straightforward, not something to write home about but I like that the characters are well fleshed out, diverse personality wise and everything is voiced (including ingame books and papers). The puzzles are not that difficult and just like the original games, it's mostly about fetching the thing to the other thing to make some other thing work. It's just a relaxed experience you can probably finish within a day and feel entertained, we need this kind of games every now and then.UPDATE: after beating the game, i can safely say that it's a game worth playing. I miss the time when games were made like this, no bull***t, just have fun. No chasing upgrades for weapons, no stats or leveling up to make you grind stuff, no meaningless side-quests, no open world and so on. The game respects your time and you can beat it in under 10 hours on each character if you take it slow. Honestly, for me this is well worth the 60$ price, i don't judge a game on world size or how long it is, I had plenty of fun for that money and that is what a game should be, fun. Really hope for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely wonderfull love letter to the atmosphere, themes and ideas from the original series. Lots of easter eggs, absolutely banging soundtrack and atmosphere is to die for. The game FEELS like a slow burn 70s horror movie in the best possible way. The story, the way it is presented and all the notes and lore are very well put together, smartly written and very engaging. If you like story driven games, get it.Yes, there is some jank and bugs, but nothing that would hamper the enjoyment of this lovely, lovely game.The game quicksaves all the time, there are no achievements tied to playing on hard difficulty so it smooths over the fact that the combat is trash and some bugs can clip you into stuff.EDIT: Patches fixed quite a lot of the technical issues the game had.

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC!!!At first I was a bit worried on account of some of the reviews inclining towards the negative, but after buying and playing the game for myself I can confidently say I LOVE THIS GAME. The environments are MESMERIZING, so much that I'm spending way more time in every room and level than the story strictly requires, just for the sake of gazing at the rich and  impressive surroundings.By the way I very much appreciate the "calm step" at which you can walk through the various environments and still speed up if you want with a very realistic looking jogging animation. So much better than those games where you can only run around like a wet hen.The story itself, although somewhat linear (most doors and rooms are locked and cannot be opened until the story has progressed to a certain point), is nevertheless a great combination of gameplay, detective work, storytelling and unexpected twists so it never gets boring and you'll constantly discover and experience new things.  Granted, the combat is somewhat basic and I don't like the fact that the MC pulls out a gun at the most inconvenient moments (this is because drawing weapon is tied to RMB as well as to ordinary UI exit actions which should have been separated, meaning you keep holstering your weapon over and over again, but that aside). Combat is nevertheless satisfying enough not to be disappointing. Gotta say I love those huge gunpowder sparks, nice reload animations and the sounds aren't bad either!!  I do have some doubts about the replayability but since every one of the two characters is said to have their own unique gameplay I'm looking forward to replaying the game from the other perspective as well.Great classic horror game with a wonderful 19th century feel to it, and if you pick it up on sale for let's say 30 bucks you'll have a great time without any regrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to Alone in the Dark during its first remake when they gave Carnby a mullet and I loved it since then, so it was agonizing watching an old beloved get turned inside out over the years. As such, I went into this very skeptically, which pleasantly surprised me, in a good way, but there are a few things that need to be said:- When playing with a controller, the Tommy Gun has WAY too much recoil. This is not too much of a problem for most of the game, but the final boss is nigh impossible to kill with a controller because of the bad gun controls- When new areas get loaded in it's VERY obvious something's about to happen because the game immediately freezes for a few seconds- Cutscene camera work is odd, like the way it's done makes scenes feel like they're starting in the middle, as if like you missed a part of the scene before the characters continued - The story; to avoid spoilers I will simply say the story felt somewhat disjointed at parts; like there are plot points that come and go and feel like they don't connect with anything else happening and the final segment of the game feels like it comes out of nowhere since the game spends all its runtime pointing you in the opposite direction. I get they probably did this on purpose so the final chapter gets you good but the execution was a little lacking. The good: - If, like me, you're someone who has seen this series get dragged through the mud all these years since the first remake, then rejoice that this is a MASSIVE improvement over everything that came past the 2001 remake. - It's not as tense or as scary as that entry, but it has its moments and the team definitely made good use of the story's Eldritch inspirations to draw up some good ideas and create some really nice looking areas. - As is the norm with horror games, there are many puzzles and most of them are really nicely done, requiring you to actually pay attention to documents and clues to get how to solve them. I will admit though, I struggled a little to understand how the talisman you get at the beginning works.- Narration; it's obvious the team put a lot of effort into this one, as while the scene dialogues are a little odd at times, every single document you find in the game is fully narrated for that extra point of immersionOverall, if this was sold at the price of a AAA title, I'd have some issues but even with all the jank, at its current price tag, it is a good deal for the amount of content you're getting. I loved my experience with this, especially since I've been starved for some good Alone in the Dark content.I will update this once I do the other scenario as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the mainstream critics out there are unjustifiably dragging this game through the mud. While it's not a perfect game, it accomplishes the survival horror experience these developers sought to make. This may not be a AAA experience, but resources were put in the right place - engaging story, lore, asymmetric combat, atmosphere, puzzles requiring thought, and environments oozing with meticulous attention to detail. Not to mention several unnerving moments throughout that blend in with the overall story seamlessly. Optimized well with only minor, occasional stuttering and bugs, such as getting stuck on random assets. That said... $59.99 is WAY too steep for an 8-12 hour experience with little replay value, especially when compared to other games such as Alan Wake that launched with a $49.99 price tag. Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but unfortunately it doesn’t really do the original justice at all. Even if I hadn’t grown up with the original, I’m not sure I’d find myself being that impressed. I really do like the art direction and music, but gameplay-wise? This is hardly survival horror. Extremely linear and scripted enemy encounters remove any sense of dread you would normally expect from the genre…Not to mention its almost complete lack of replayability. (Unless you are a completionist, there aren’t any worthwhile reasons for collecting every lagniappe on repeated playthroughs.) It’s a shame, because I was really pulling for this one; however, there are just too many great competitors to really recommend, even when considering the budget.Speaking of which, I also wholeheartedly disagree with the “pretty good for AA” argument. Robocop Rogue City released this year and had great gameplay. Within the genre, games like Crow Country and Signalis prove that you don’t need a huge budget to make a great survival horror experience. Unfortunately I’d say skip it unless you can get it for half the price or lower. I’m hoping we get another reboot attempt - I doubt this one will get a sequel. Maybe one which emphasizes and expands upon what made the original so great and groundbreaking for its time.

_childDocuments_.review: Sum up  of the game "our gonna need some keys". Its worth playing but I would wait for it to be on sale. It only took me like a day to beat it so it is worth a play through but not $50.00.  It has a lot of silly glitching, nothing that kept you from playing (at least not for me)  but there were some hairdos and  bottles that were doing an Irish jig. The aiming is a bit atrocious but it didn't keep me from moving forward. Meh its a nice game to play when you want a break from other more long term commitment games. I got it cause I needed a break from BG3 and I like the actors they picked as the main characters. All and all it is another entertaining game if your looking for something small and weird. Pro: It actually was a smooth playthrough despite the fact it was a mystery. I notice a lot of mystery/puzzle games make the mistake of getting you lost and confused as to what to do next. You often will end up spending a considerable amount of time retracting steps and spend more time trying to find out what you are supposed to be doing that you can't even enjoy the game. Not the case here, everything was pretty straight forward a even when I had moments of confusion they only lasted a very short time before I figured out exactly what to do and got back to enjoying the game. Cons:....why the hell is this game $50.00? The play time is not there my dudes, and ya it was interesting but like it wasn't something that blew me away with visuals. Also when I shoot at something directly I expect it to hit none of this role me a 1d20, I swear it would miss even if I had a direct hit like 20% of the time. Good thing there are bullets available at almost every 20 meters. Side note: This is a good game for people who want to play horror games but get to scared to play horror games. _childDocuments_.review: There's some bugs, particularly with collision detection, but thankfully very generous checkpoint placement will help you out there.I mean this sincerely: this one is a 9.5/10 for me. The story is so well told. The pacing is superb. It's not just another Resident Evil clone like The New Nightmare or too ambitious beyond its means like Inferno. This is -just right-.I'll be writing up a full video review in the near future, but if you're at all a fan of old school adventure games -and- survival horror? If you miss puzzles actually being cleverly designed in games? If you crave for something that truly feels like it's both a modern title AND something ripped straight out of the 90s in the best ways? Play this. Absolutely make a point to play this. Between the two protagonist's unique stories, solid scenario design, and brilliant performances bolstering an already solid script... a few glitches and a bit easy of a final boss fight are worth overlooking.

_childDocuments_.review: Look. Clunky? Yes. But I gotta admit, the atmosphere, music, acting, and characters hit. I think this is pretty well done. I, like many others, would like a patch or two to clean up some issues. Overall, I got it on sale for 30 bucks. In my opinion, no brainer if you like horror. I am playing on the hardest difficulty and it can provide a challenge in some cases. It gives no hints on what and where to go, less items to scavenge around the levels. Its fun! I do wish the devs came in and cleaned up the stutters when loading a new level or area. You'll most likely see it early on. As the game has gone on, I see it less. Still, kills immersion. _childDocuments_.review: Items disappeared in my inventory in chapter 2 leaving me to run around for hours before I finally googled it and realised that my save is knackered.Some of the puzzles are very abstract, it is very easy to make an early false assumption with the medallion that can leave you stumped for a long time making the wrong connections. Both times that I had to use it I just brute forced it and got lucky, then when finally googling it I realised how it's supposed to work.Game hitches constantly when moving around the mansion, not too bad to be game ruining like my first point but slightly annoying.Overall I don't want to finish this game, and you should get it on a deep sale and be prepared to Google things for some of the abstract puzzles. I don't want hand-holding but for some of the puzzles you do need to make some mental leaps in logic, which is unfortunate. How the medicine bottles look like a snake is beyond me.I also respect the fact that all of the inventory items are voiced, but some of them are so long and read so slowly that I wouldn't be surprised if you start skipping them.I don't recommend this game, but I may not be the target audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly let me tell you guys that no i haven't played the original but i have heard of the game before. Recently i was interested in the game after i saw some Alpha gameplay footage & it made me intrigued as i'm a fan of 3rd person shooter horror games which includes puzzles as well. The lovecraftian tag made it more interesting cause i love the works of H.P. Lovecraft, i have always loved games like Call of Cthulhu, Sinking City, Sherlock Holmes Awakened, etc. Now coming to the game itself it's a good Remake of the original, it reprises the spooky environments, Ghastly enemies and adds a cool detective formula to it. The combat is your regular 3rd person over the shoulder shooter where you use Pistol, Shotgun, Tommy Gun and Melee items to defeat monsters just like Resident Evil but the combat is kinda clunky with the player getting slow due to heavy recoil. We get to solve lots of cool puzzles but it suffers from heavy backtracking.Can be played from two different perspectives who are Edward and Emily with different outcomes but overall the Story and puzzles remain same. People who love horror and solving puzzles with bits of lovecraftian atmosphere this is the game for you.The performance of the game is very good, played for 2 hours and didn't encounter a crash, it suffered from heavy traversal and shader lags but currently they fixed it with the latest 2 GB patch and the game runs great! The graphics itself are pretty ordinary but the character models and lip syncing is top notch! I give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated game in my opinion.Sure, it has its flaws and quirks, and you definitely feel that this isn't a 100+ Million Dollar production. This isn't up to the standards defined by games like the RE2 Remake regarding presentation and overall production value.That said, this game oozes with atmosphere and tells a compelling story, with some mysteries and twists here and there. The general gameplay-loop (consisting of exploration, puzzling, exposition/story/cutscenes, and combat) was highly engaging for me and I basically finished the campaign (played as Emily; 6.9 hours (nice) for my playthrough) in a few sittings. You just want to know what happens next!Graphics are fine, although performance (mostly traversal-stutter) and pop-in surely aren't ideal. There's some good variety in locations and the lighting sometimes really looks spectacular. Of course, there are weak points, like the character models (other than the protagonists, those look actually quite good). All in all I actually think this game looks quite nice and the graphics set the mood perfectly most of the time.This is a slower-paced game, with lots of stuff to read, some dialogue, and quite a lot of puzzles (which are mostly good, but it falls flat for a few). Movement speed and combat are also rather slow, but that's not a bad thing. I should mention that this isn't really survival-horror though, so don't expect to have to deal with inventory management, crafting, and resource-scarcity!If you enjoy a narrative-heavy mystery-horror-thriller and don't need that last bit of polish in your game, I highly recommend this one. Not quite sure why the critics score on both metacritic and opencritic are that low; user scores paint a different and - in my opinion - more fitting picture though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great AA game. It's got some jank to it. The controls can feel a bit clunky, but generally the gameplay is solid. The The creepy atmosphere is solid. It's all very traditional in many ways. A great callback to survival horror games. Reminds me a lot of Signalis in that way. Having great fun so far. This is comfort gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would give this a 7/10 off of what I've seen so far. This isn't a REmake2 or 4 quality title, nor is it as scary as them, but it is a solid first step in the right direction for this battered & beaten series.It still offers some good scares & atmosphere, it's southern gothic noire aesthetic helps it stand out, the story is an engaging mystery with replay value & Decerto has been remade with an interesting history & even has some Spencer Mansion DNA. A fitting evolution. However these would be the CONS of the game.. Melee is janky & poorly implemented . The use of real life actors likeness for the leads creates an uncanny valley effect when compared to the rest of the cast which begs the question, why not do that with everyone?. The framerate has a habit of hitching & there's stuttering during transitions. Some people have even reported crashing but thank God for the Manuel save system. $100 (AUD) price tag is too high for what's on offer compared to another rceent THQ Nordic release, Outcast A New Beginning. $60-$70 would have been more fitting.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing the game, especially exploring the different locations and the temple in the middle of the desert. The puzzle that involved redirecting the lights through mirrors was a fun challenge. However, I did notice that the graphics in the cut scenes could have been improved. In my opinion, the in-game graphics looked better than the rendered cut scenes. I'm not sure why the developers didn't spend more time refining the cut scenes, especially when you compare them to games like "A Plague Tale" and "The Quarry". These games have much better skin, hair, and lip sync with the characters. Despite this, I still found the game enjoyable and finished it in about 8 hours. Now, I'll replay it as the female character in the story. Oh, I almost forgot! Every letter and piece of evidence you find is well worth it to read it to its fully extent to connect the fascinating story behind the manor where the story unfolds. Similarly to Alone in the Dark 4: The New Nightmare, the story combines the spiritual beliefs of the locals that used to inhabited the area. Overall, I give it an 8 out of 10. If you can get it at a discounted price, I would recommend giving it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! Such a fantastic love letter to the original AITD trilogy with lots of fun callbacks. (I see you, Slaughter Gulch Script.)It's 100% a survival horror game. Action feels a little on the clunky side (which should feel familiar to fans of older games of the genre like the PS1 Resident Evils, the original Alone in the Dark games, Silent Hill 1-4, etc.) I say this with love, but I know this can be a turn-off for some players.While it isn't fast paced, it is a great horror story with some fun twists and layers to the mystery that I fully enjoyed. I plan on playing through at least twice more, as there is lots of content to unlock, and each character can unlock story beats/items for the other character's game. These unlocks and progressing through both stories help you learn the full truth of what has and is happening at Derceto Manor, and your part to play.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: It's "We have Alan Wake 2 at home" (but endearingly)This is a solid game with a little jank. A nice psychological horror with less emphasis on dark and dreary environments, jumpscares and gore, and more focused on the bizarre, occult, and atmosphere. Despite having two big celebrities act as the face of the product, the game has a nice personality of its own that I enjoyed. It has a rich 1920s theme across a variety of totally distinct environments and locations, with pleasant music, gorgeous visuals, some interesting characters and a plot I found interesting. Seriously the environment artists knocked it out of the park with this one.There's a fair bit of dialogue going around about how this game flopped and how they should have put the money used to hire Jodie Comer and David Harbour towards more solid gameplay and mechanics. I think there's some merit there but personally I think having these two people act as the main characters is pretty cool. While they are great actors, I feel like they fall a bit flat at voice acting most of the time. I'm not sure if this is just a lack of direction or experience (Acting and Voice Acting are totally different ball games) because there are a few moments where they put on great performances. The other voice actors in the game do alright, but nothing to write home about imo.The gameplay focuses around third person shooting and melee combat with dodging, while including items like bricks and molotovs that you cannot carry, but throw at enemies in close proximity. I think this is a nice system that allows you to conserve resources in a few different ways while not being an inventory-management based game. I felt like the shooting was a little off, but overall works just fine. Melee combat is floaty, lacks weight and was just unsatisfying however. The item throwing is a nice idea that I think works well. I didn't really find myself bored of the combat throughout.I felt the puzzles were pretty straightforward, with a few more puzzling ones in there but I felt those ones were perfectly balanced in their difficulty. I wish that clues and solutions to puzzles could expand beyond the room they are in, especially those that take place in Decerto. This would have shaken them up a bitI'm mostly writing this review because I think this is a quaint little gem of a game and that the studio deserved better. Because they made something good

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the Alone in the Dark series. I'm a fan of survival horror. I think both Jodie Comer and David Harbour are great actors. Based on this, the reboot of the series with these two in the lead roles should be a great game, right? Right?Unfortunately, things aren't quite like that. But everything in its own time.Alone in the Dark (2024) is an old-school survival horror game, another installment of the series that actually created this genre back in the distant 1992. Everything that makes games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill hits is present - puzzles to solve, strange places to explore, hordes of nasty enemies to defeat, with your weapons and ammo being more than limited. So far, so good.But here come the small unpleasant details. The game is endlessly linear - until you find the key to room A, you can't proceed. Until you solve the puzzle in room B, you still can't move forward. There's no freedom of action, everything happens in a precisely defined order.The puzzles, which are an important part of games like this, are too easy. In fact, only one puzzle took me more than 10 minutes, mainly because the slightly strange controls didn't allow me to focus the telescope faster. If for some reason you still struggle with the puzzles, the game gives you more than obvious hints.The story is very pleasant, I won't deny that. Starting as a noir from the beginning of the last century, it quickly leads you to a world filled with madness, paranoia, and more than enough references to the works of Lovecraft and Stephen King. If only it were a little more interactive, instead of completely linear. You can also experience it in slightly different ways through the eyes of two main characters (you choose who to play with at the beginning).Which leads to the battles. The shooting itself is done in an extremely clumsy way, and hitting anything is a matter of skill and luck. Adding the limited ammo, the fact that your characters are mega clumsy, and the enemies - quite fast, and the rare healing items, the overall impression is quite unpleasant.The sound is, well... okay, let me put it this way. All the moans, creaks, closing doors, and other sounds that are supposed to create atmosphere are great. Add some dark jazz, totally suitable for New Orleans at the beginning of the 20th century, and it gets even better. The voice acting by the supporting characters is also on point.And here comes the huge surprise - both Jodie and David sound half asleep, without any emotion, and it's more than obvious how much they hurried to get their paycheck and break away from the studio.Bad.Graphically, the game is quite pleasant, from the crumbling psychiatric clinic in New Orleans, to the infectious swamps of Louisiana, through the ancient Egyptian temple to the abandoned Arctic station, everything is beautiful, detailed, and frightening. But, unfortunately, there's still a "but", the expressions of the main characters are just as devoid of emotion as their voices.Regarding the enjoyment of the game, I admit - I enjoyed it. And solving the story room by room and page by page, and solving the puzzles, albeit easy. A few times I jumped out of my chair at well-directed "jump scares". A few times I laughed at the exchange of lines between Jodie and David, albeit spoken with a tired and bored voice.The game is still worth it, especially considering that there hasn't been a new Silent Hill in years, and the Resident Evil games are getting further and further away from the genre's roots with each new installment.But it could have been a lot better with just a bit more...i don't really know what. Time?Rating: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I'm a big fan of older survival horrors like the earlier Resident Evils and Silent Hills, and the 4th Alone in the Dark, although I never played the original. I've been reading through the other reviews and personally I can't say I've had a load of the problems other people have had. I'll agree that the story isn't revolutionary in any way, but I think it's because this type of Lovecraftian setting and story has been done so many times and in so many mediums it's hard to do something new whilst preserving the expected tropes. I've just started reading Lovecraft myself and it's brilliant to see some of the details from the books used in game. I've also found all of his story's so far to be more about building an atmosphere than action so I suppose the game captures that pretty well too. I'd say it's a solid story with a couple of unexpected twists, although the final act does seem to come upon you suddenly. That said Emilys story is the better of the two. The game does nudge you towards playing as Emily first but as I'm more familiar with David Harbour than Jodie Comer, and Carnby was the main character in the first 5 games, I went with Carnby first and it was the wrong decision. Playing as Emily the supporting characters are more forthcoming with information, Emily's unique sections are more interesting and the whole story felt more cohesive. Carnbys story is better with the information you get in Emily's story. Looking at some reviewers play times it looks as if they've only played one half of the game, and the weaker half at that. I'd also say Emily's story has less technical issues than Carnbys. Graphically I think it looks good and runs as at a pretty steady 90fps on my 5800x/2080/32GB rig without any issues, compared to something like Alan Wake 2 which struggled to hit 60fps for the majority of the game.Gameplay wise It's what I want to see from a survival horror; recursive exploration and some decent puzzles without being too action oriented like pretty much every Resident Evil game and remake since 2004.The puzzles vary from very simple pick up item, turn around and place in slot to some that will require cross referencing a couple of different items in the room and one or two documents you've discovered that will have you scratching your head for a few minutes. To counter other reviewers complaints:> Cost Vs time. Every survival horror I've ever played has cos whatever the industry standard was at the time and taken 6-10 hours for your first playthrough (12-20 for two characters) and 2-4 hours for subsequent runs. This game falls squarely into the middle of those brackets based on my own play time. > The aiming works fine. Yes it's a bit slow and if you fire in succession too fast then your character will be affected by recoil and the second shot will go wide. Similarly if you're moving whilst shooting your accuracy goes down. Adjust how you're playing and you won't have any issues. After all you're not some superhero with special forces training, you're a couple of normal people up against the unexplained, CoD level responsiveness and accuracy should not be expected. This was the design philosophy of a lot of older survival horror games and it's nice to see it back again. Anyone else who played those older games should know what to expect. Personally, this is how I want my survival horrors to handle. > If you get headshots on enemies (and you actually land them, see above) weaker enemies go down in 1-4 pistol shots, stronger enemies in 1-2 shotgun shots. Not broken as some have said. > There's actually 8 enemy types in game. Sure they all look similar and it may not be as varied as the original, I don't know, but its not as bad as some people make out. > Getting stuck on objects. I'm pretty thorough with exploring and I only managed to get stuck in the scenery three times in two playthroughs so make of that what you will, but it's nothing a quick save and reload won't fix. > Grapical issues are minor. My GF got some speckling in a few areas on her PC using DLSS to upscale from 720p to 4k, playing it myself at native 1440p I had no issues. There's one cutscene where the character rubber bands for a few seconds right at the start regardless of who you're playing as but other than that I can't think of any problems in 2 and a bit playthroughs. The game could do with a little extra attention here and there as far as graphics and collision detection go but compared to the state a lot of games launch in nowadays it's incredibly minor. All in all I think this is a great start to resurrecting a classic series and hope they do the rest of the series, particularly a remake of New Nightmare given my nostalgia over it, and hopefully eventually a continuation of the series seeing as the 2008 and 2015 games pretty much killed the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Another decade, another attempt to revive Alone in the Dark. I’ve recently replayed and covered all of the previous games in the series (excluding Illumination, because who cares). The inspiring original trilogy that shaped modern action adventures, but aged poorly. A much simpler first reboot The New Nightmare that nonetheless did several incredibly ambitious things. Overly ambitious Alone in the Dark from 2008, that attempted to reinvent the genre but failed miserably. And now we have a third game simply titled Alone in the Dark, except this lacks any ambition of the previous entries.Alone in the Dark from 2024 is a mostly linear horror themed story driven action adventure game. That serves as a new reboot, a “reimagining” of the original game that directly references this fact in its cosmic horror “nobody knows what’s real” plot. But design-wise it is completely unlike any of the previous entries in the franchise focusing far more on said plot than the gameplay.Mechanically, this is another game taking Resident Evil 2 (2019) as a reference. Except, it only covers the controls and combat, while completely ignoring the rest of the gameplay experiences of both new RE2 or the previous games. As a result, this game doesn’t fit the core pillars of survival action (let alone survival horror) and lacks any meaningful exploration, while the rest of the pillars are underserved as well. There’s one central location that you get to revisit between the almost entirely linear levels which pretends to behave like a typical interconnected survival horror spooky mansion. But in reality even the “exploration” of this location is on rails and the game constantly closes and opens paths in such a bold way that even the most egregious examples of this from Fatal Frame look tame in comparison.But hey – not being a survival horror/action isn’t a bad thing and Alone in the Dark doesn’t have to fit the limitations of a genre to be a fun game. This title focuses on being a story driven experience and to give it credit – the writing for the characters and character performances are genuinely impressive. The writing feels as if something that came out of the Lovecraft novel (minus the racism) and some of the cutscenes are really well directed too. Unfortunately, the plot itself is extremely dumb. It gets caught in its own delusions and attempts to be “meta” and in the end loses any sense of direction or point to it. I mean, sure the storyline of the original game wasn’t particularly interesting either, but that game was released in 1992 and also had a lot of other cool things going for it. While the only thing this new game seems to have is the storytelling.The rest of the game aspects range from barely functioning to potentially interesting. Combat is not good, but it’s also not the worst even within the limits of franchise. Plus it tries to spice things up with the throwable objects and Alan Wake dodge, which are fun additions. Puzzles range from exceptionally primitive to obtuse in an unfun way. The idea of unlocking secret endings or scenes via collectibles is curious, but collectibles themselves can be hidden in an unacceptable manner – like in a tiny spot just few steps from an invisible trigger that blocks you from being able to grab it. There is no meaningful resource management and the ammo/health pickups system is incredibly silly in its execution.Then there are also countless bugs and poor design decisions. You will constantly get stuck on decoration objects and it more likely than not will require a reload of the last save. Animations break for characters and enemies. Sound may suddenly break and you will get a cacophony of noise in the background or a character line will be unvoiced. Map breaks all the time adding confusion to the already frustrating pixel hunting, as pickups may not be interactable unless you’re standing at a specific angle. Collectibles and items may reappear when you’ve picked them up already, sometimes infinitely. Occasional interaction spots appear when they shouldn’t. There are several spots where you can completely break the sequence of events without even realizing it, which breaks the script of the game… The game is in a genuinely unacceptable state and some of these issues could’ve been identified and designed around very early in development.Yet, despite all of this during my first playthrough I was relatively positive and hoping that the game will still manage to surprise me in some way. But no there is simply no ambition in this project. No cool systems like in AitD 2008, no non-linearity like in the original, no wild mechanics and plot points like in the AitD 2 and 3. Even The New Nightmare, for how closely it followed the Resident Evil formula of the time, did genuinely inventive things with the flashlight and created two unique playthroughs for its two characters, with unique locations, story and puzzles. While Alone in the Dark 2024 is completely linear, its story is almost exactly the same between characters and there’s just one mostly insignificant and uninteresting location close to the end of the game that differentiates one character from another. There’s nothing inventive here, nothing unique or interesting. Just a rehash of things you’ve seen done better before.So while I originally considered getting all secret endings in the game, I just stopped during my third playthrough. Alone in the Dark from 2024 is short, I was about half-way through, rushing through everything on easy and in just about an hour or so I would’ve been able to see more of those secret things I’ve already unlocked… But then the thoughts of spending even five more minutes with the game became so suffocating that I had to stop. And will most likely never play it again. If it ever gets properly fixed so thousands of its bugs are gone and you see it at a huge discount, maybe it could be worth one playthrough. Just to check the dialogues between characters and have a simple linear walk through this title. But until that happens I would not recommend it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: - The idea of a reboot of the saga is a success.- The game recreates an atmosphere of terror and mystery that keeps you in suspense throughout the game. To be clear, the mansion setting is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.- The story is intriguing and keeps you hooked until the end: if you're a Lovecraft fan, don't miss it.- It's very replayable: it has five different endings, although Edward and Emily's parts are very similar for most of the game they have some differences that make it worth playing with both of them.- It has some really memorable moments.- Levels are well designed and offer a good challenge....... although there is one level in particular where you have to run away because there are infinite enemies and they don't tell you anything: it's a notable design flaw.- They shouldn't have spent money on the roles of Edward Camby and Emily: it would have been better to use that budget to enrich the game and polish it more.- Some of the puzzles are repeated too often, and are somewhat difficult to solve.- The combat system is too basic, and when the enemy gets too close it becomes almost impossible to survive.- It has several bugs, which don't detract too much from the experience, but are not understandable. For example, I got stuck (literally, unable to move the character) several times, forcing me to reload game.Putting on a scale the good things on one side and the bad things on the other, the good things win by far, but unfortunately for some media the bad things usually outweigh the good things, unless you are a fan of a certain saga. It's true, this Alone in the Dark has a clumsy combat system, but its atmosphere is of honours and its story is remarkable, and just for that alone it's worth playing it.- 8/10.The truth is, I don't understand the bad press that the game has had, because I loved it. It's true that it's not at the same level of the greats of the genre, but its budget is much lower. I hope they make a second part.If you're a fan of survival horror you should give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Mitigated.Starting by what made me playing it and enjoying that time. It is splendid.The 2 main qualities of this game are its visuals and its narrative. Despite fabrics are hard as rock, the rest is simply beautiful. With well crafted stages, splendid lights... It is a Call and serve the Mythos without a doubt.Story is just great. Atmosphere is fantastic.It is verbose. A bit too much. You do not have to read except for 2 documents and probably due to a bug since the plethora of other lectures is voiced. Well voiced.But it comes to a point that having to listen without doing anything else breaks the game.I did jump a couple of lectures because I wanted to play instead of listening.I did stop the voice sometimes because it is just faster to read yourself and I wanted to play. Not to listen books after books. notes after notes.It comes with glitches and bugs. Some visual glitches, nothing game breaking but damageable since the game rely a lot on its visual. Especially with lights that may become strange while entering or leaving a space. Some sparks that are appearing in the back of the character.And some bugs that obliged me to restart a save. It happened multiple times. I could not take hatchets that come in boxes. Objects that are for the least mandatory not only for fighting.It brings to the saves. Automated and manual. No limited slots but limited times. For some reasons, you cannot manual save any time you want... And you will reappear at precise points of the map. With all you have done such as already collected stuff but not reappearing where you saved. A bit disappointing, especially the first time.Controls are rough. At least playing with a controller. Not really responsives.  That does not serve the coming point.The worst.What reproduce the game at best from its sibling from the 90's is the combat. It is different but it reminds this feeling while you had to turn on yourself to adjust a shot. Sometime a creature is right in your reticule, you are not moving, you give a shot and you are still able to miss it... Disappointing.It is still acceptable because the game is good and fights are not too punitive. Fights does not require extra action for most of them and when it does, it is manageable.Except there is an ending boss. One that split  offspring, minions. I stopped here. I find this too painful for the moment considering the lack of polish around the controls.Frustrating because it is the actual ending and I would like to see it.This dev choice was definitely not a good idea considering the fighting mechanic quality. On top, it starts with a video that you cannot skip... Expect to watch it a couple of times.That really bores me.This last point by itself makes me wanting to put the thumb down.I keep it up since I really enjoyed the 11h of game before that.I also want to replay it with the second protagonist to see what changes. But without seeing the ending... Not sure how I am going to handle that. A cheat maybe if there is one.Regarding its price, I bought it on sales. I wanted to buy it at day one but when its price came out, I took a step back. Playing the game confirmed it was the right choice. It should have been released with the 34% off proposed today. Because of its length, including the time you have to listen without playing, and its lack of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has common unreal engine 4 shader problem.It will stutter even with rtx 4090,but i am able to fix this with old knowledge.1-You should increase your shader memory to ''unlimited'' under  nvidia 3d settings - or amd control panel or asus rog software etc.2-Delete all files under C:\Users\yourusername\AppData\Local\NVIDIA\GLCache  and DXCache too if it's there.3-Delete all files that can be deleted under C:\Users\yourusername\AppData\Local\Temp4-Delete dx cache via typing ''storage'' to search then select temporary files - tick directx and clean.5-Force game to use dx12 with adding -dx12 to steamlaunch options or game exe.6-Match your fps limit with your display and use vsync.7-These should %90 reduce your stuttering but if you still suffer stuttering ,try using ddu tool and delete  and reistall your graphic drivers when your windows in offline mode.This will temporarily fix your issue with micro stutters,weird trace in air like using DLAA when moving camera (even while it's turned off) and render issues.It's more usefull on cards with big vram but you still need to repeat delete cache steps when your shader cache starting to bloat again.

_childDocuments_.review: Since last year, I have been eagerly waiting to play the new  reimagination. It was initially supposed to come out before my birthday, and it would’ve been a great, spooky season release. But I’m glad to have waited longer because it was worth it!Either playing as Edward Carnby (David Harbour) or Emily Hartwood (Jodie Comer), the story follows them as they head to Derceto Manor. Emily has received a letter from her uncle, Jeremy, telling her to stay away. Avoiding her uncle’s warning, she heads to Derceto and hires private investigator Edward to help her. However, they find her uncle missing when they arrive, and the staff seem reluctant to help them. Where has Jeremy gone? Why are the staff strange? What secrets does Derceto hide within its walls? It’s time for us to be alone in the dark.Before playing this remake, I decided to play through the original 1992 game to get an idea and feel of what I might be getting into. Honestly, I am pleased I did because it helped me appreciate this game even more. Throughout my two playthroughs (Edward and Emily's campaigns, respectively), I could spot the various easter eggs and references from that first game, such as a secret hidden memory in the attic and collectibles or items that look like those found in the original. Furthermore, so much detail was included in this game, and it’s impressive. Graphically, this game is stunning, which is always a plus. The narrative is quite interesting and kept me engaged as I went along; plus, I enjoy Lovecraftian horror. Just like  or , some puzzles aren’t too complicated but do take some real thinking.As I write this, I want to add that the game still has some stuttering issues. It didn’t ruin my experience with the game, as I encountered it minimally, but it is noticeable when it happens. With this being a survival horror-like experience, there are sections of combat. I didn’t hate these portions, but the only critique I would give is that the reload speed felt a little slow to me, although it did seem realistic. I do recommend playing through each character’s campaign as they aren’t entirely the same experience, just playing as different people. Some neat differences exist (unique cutscenes, unique sections, collectibles that can only be found as each character). It is worth playing through a couple times, trust me.This is an excellent game; there is so much to love about it. I really don’t understand the negative reviews. It felt like a true  game. P.S. Loved the casting!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was a solid entry, albeit dotted with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here and there. There's a good balance of exploration, solving puzzles and combat. I think the developers got the pacing spot on and I never felt like the experience got repetitive because there's quite a lot of different locations from ancient tombs to murky swamps. It really nails the environments and atmosphere which have a very Lovecraft / Gothic vibe. Apart from exploring the mansion, it is a fairly linear journey and there's not much going off the beaten track but I was OK with this. The combat was satisfying enough for me, not brilliant but not awful either. It does feel very old school in a deliberately awkward way. Lobbing Molotov cocktails could of been designed better - it's very hit and miss if you're not aiming but maybe that was intended. The ammo placements in a few sections weren't very balanced either and there's a level with an unnecessary amount of flare gun ammo prior to a mini boss fight. During this fight, and after you've beaten him, you can't go back to replenish your gun with all that ammo because the path has now been blocked off. The voice acting is really good, as is the modelling of Emily and Edward. The other characters aren't as polished but they still compliment the main protagonists. I can't fault the gloomy jazz music which is perfectly fitting and assists the game's spooky atmosphere. I say spooky, because in general it was quite tame on the horror. The puzzles varied from easy to normal which I mostly found a breeze on 'Old School' mode, although there's one that's not clearly explained which took me a while to figure out. There's some nods to the original AITD series like a sudden switch in camera view and subtle things like the way Emily leans forward to push open  double doors. I just wished the developers had included some comical kicking and slapping which was present in the earlier games. I encountered quite a few bugs. Some interactivity not working properly and mostly getting stuck on objects. It could certainly do with some more play testing but nothing was really game breaking and was a matter of reloading a save.I had a lot of fun with this game, coming in at around 10 hours and I hope there's a sequel but with more improvements. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: After one playthrough and about to start my second, i've enjoyed Alone in the Dark for the most part. There were a few times I got stuck in game geometry and had to reload. Asset loading causes very noticeable stuttering and hitching at times (even on a high end machine and SSD) and combat feels like an afterthought with poor camera control and enemy responsiveness that can lead to you being wombo-combo'd in a corner with no way to heal, which doesn't feel too satisfying.The story, character performances and atmosphere save this game though. I hope the dev team learns from this experience and can build on this base while smoothing out the issues to polish this game and perhaps work on others in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a mixed bag.i enjoyed it thoroughly but there are many aspects in which i am disappointed. firstly the mansion looks incredible. secondly i enjoyed many of the puzzles as simple as they were.i appreciate the setting immensely. the story for what it is, is fine. the characters and delivery are phenomenal.the music is especially noteworthy as it has almost a twin peaks vibe, very lynchian. theirs jazzy notes that are period appropriate but also some synths to pad out and add atmosphere very good stuff.the fact there are 4 endings and 2 characters adds to replay-ability but also lends itself to some issues.the lack of unlockables for beating the game multiple times is SEVERELY disappointing. many old games especially from the era this game hails from have many secret unlockable weapons and even if they didnt they had a lot of variety and the setting lends itself to some really interesting possibilities but theres only 3 weapons (4 if you include the character specific weapons) but there in itself leads to my main critique of the game. there is no real sense of progression. now many people critique modern games having to have skill trees and level ups ect ect but resident evil and evil within had gotten these systems down perfectly and lend themselves to their own criteria- one being realistic and one being fantastical.resident evil gives way to progression by allowing you to find weapon attachments and allowing you to stow resources away creating a satisfying gameplay loop leading to a nice skill ceiling. the evil within allowed you to upgrade your chracters skills and craft ammo leading to a need to scrounge environments.with resident evil 4 and other modern survival horror games: inventory management makes for moment to moment and emergent gameplay.not only does alone in the dark hamper itself with a lack of ANY of these systems refined and easily transferable from a series that has more than 20 years of experience but it actually spits in your face by carefully managing exactly how much ammo it gives you. alan wake 2 did this and it made for a system thats easily game-able. it takes the control out of the player and keeps it in the developers hands. so there are containers everywhere and depending on how much ammo you have it spits out what you need. your Never struggling or surviving. you always have exactly what you need for each scenerio. its predictable and frustrating. the level design is great but as i have said the combat doesnt just stop with the way the systems work with ammo, progression and player agency but it also physically lacks feedback as well as the enemy variety being very lack luster. when you shoot it feels like a pellet gun and the enemies have very poor animations.the combat very quickly loses any fun factor.the gameplay is imo extremely dated whilst also having bad tropes that modern survival horror games seem to persist in. linear levels that look great but lack any need to explore. alan wake 2 suffered from this as well.there are difficulty options but even those are lack luster, one being guided and the other "not" i say not in quotes because even with it off you are told exactly where to go no matter which section and the map literally tells you when your done with a room. in resident evil this is good because of the progression systems which allows the game to be a lot more mechanically driven and difficult. this game stays largely the same throughout. so if im so down on everything involving gameplay why do i still recommend it?because whilst the gameplay is bleak the setting and atmosphere is really good. especially so if you have appreciation for the setting it takes place in, the south.it has a wonderful atmosphere that all but saves the game. the art director did a great job and if it wasnt for him this game would be really bad.the story isnt anything to write home about and can be predictable depending on what ending you like.derceto is phenomenally crafted and interesting, but with the lack of gameplay elements to keep players invested it seems to be a one and done game, unless the story itself supremely interests you. TLDR: game-play is lack luster and mechanics are too simple to be considered a "survival horror" game but, the atmosphere and soundtrack make up a suitably enjoyable overall experience. the story is ok but the ascetics take it home.notesresident evil has got the blueprints down perfectly evil within 2 also perfected the systems a more fantastical survival horror game should have.the reason silent hill gets away with being so poor mechanically is because the atmosphere and story.this game is jsut barely passing the mark.it falls in an awkward space because it doesnt have the mechanics of resident evil and lacks the compelling stories of silent hill 1-4 that has had fans in forums discussing the game for 30 years. the only saving grace is the art direction. is that enough to recommend a game? i dont think so.so in my notes i wills say stay away until a sale.there a lot to like but the gameplay is out of touch and seems to ignore the improvements capcom has strived to make.
