_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ After her uncle disappeared from the Derceto's mansion, an asylum deep in the Louisiana countryside, Emily Hartwood hired a private detective. As they drove towards their destination, she explained that Jeremy Hartwood was possessed by something or someone that he refers to as the Dark Man, who is constantly watching his movements. She also mentioned that most members of the Hartwood family go mad and kill themselves before their time comes. But Jeremy didn't kill himself; instead, he hoped to find a cure with the new method of the Derceto's mansion owner, Dr Gray. However, in his last letter to Emily, he made some accusations that the entire staff of the asylum were part of some cult, and then he disappeared. It's time to discover the mystery of Alone in the Dark.Alone in the Dark is a third-person Lovecraftian psychological horror adventure game developed by Pieces Interactive and published by THQ Nordic on the 21st of March on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS5 and Xbox One Series X|S.The game has five chapters and will start with a fabulous cinematographic scene. Then it’s time to choose who to play as. Carnby, the private detective, was my choice. If you decide to play as Emily, I understand the game will lead toward the same path but have different commentary and cutscenes. You can play the game with or without hints. If you choose to play without hints, you'll have to figure everything out by yourself. The gameplay and the character's animations are beautifully done and so smooth. All the locations you visit are visually stunning. In almost every area, there will be things to pick up along the way, such as clues regarding the story and puzzles, ammunition for your firearms and objects you can use as melee weapons, such as pipelines and sledgehammers. There will be locked areas and locked chests; you might find a key for them while playing on your current chapter. But, more than once, these areas or chests will be accessible further down the track in upcoming chapters. What impressed me was the voice-over and the atmosphere in the game. You hear sounds in most places giving you the impression that something is there or that something is about to happen. It made me jump several times. I knew that something was building up, but when it happened, it was not where I had expected it to be. I would classify the puzzles as average; while a couple of them got me thinking, most were pretty straightforward. Yes, some puzzles will require additional objects to find within your surroundings, but on several occasions, you won't be able to complete these puzzles straight away as some of the objects won't be available in the current chapter. The puzzles with the medallion are also pretty easy when you gather all the information required. I was slightly disappointed with the fighting and enemies I encountered in this game. There is not a great variety of enemies, and they are easy to dispose of. Even the last two bosses were surprisingly easy to kill. There are objects lying around, such as briks and Molotov cocktails, that you can throw at enemies.  I liked that!  These objects helps damage them significantly, and can also be used to distract them.  You can easily dodge enemy attacks and use the melee weapon if you are close enough. Sure, melee weapons deteriorate pretty quickly, but if you have enough ammunition and keep dodging until you are out of reach, you can turn around and start shooting at them.  For my first experience with a game of this series, I must say that I enjoyed it. I need to go back and play Emily to see the difference between the two characters' perspectives and to finish collecting all the clues. I have been very thorough regarding clues, so I imagine the other collectables will be discovered while playing Emily. The graphics, soundtrack and voice-overs are excellent! The game runs very well, and I haven't experienced any issues apart from the mouse sensitivity at the start of my playthrough, which was an easy fix by adjusting it. You can play the game with a gamepad, or if you are like me, the mouse and keyboard are just fine. The game is translated into 16 languages, but the full audio experience is available in English, French, German and Japanese.  I think the initial release price of $99 AUD is too high for what you get in terms of gameplay.  $69 AUD feels more appropriate.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics and voice-overs+	Well-designed levels (chapters)+	Intriguing story+	Stunning atmosphere all the way through+	Able to play the game through two different characters +	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Lack of enemy variety-	Combat is far too easy, including bossesAlthough a rather short game with a lack of enemy variety and manageable combat phases, Alone in the Dark has stunning graphics and voice-overs, a chilling atmosphere, well-designed levels, and well-structured storytelling.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much better than you probably think. Try it. It might  very well be the best AitD since 2001  or even since the 'classic' era, and, obviously, infinitely better than that 2008 catastrophe.  Admittedly, i remember vividly only the very first game (c'mon, it's been, like, 25 years ago when i last played the old AitD), but this one is very good.You need to understand though, that this is NOT a AAA game, so don't expect Alan Wake 2 or RE Remakes level of presentation or polishing, and it doesn't have the inventory management system - it's more of a adventure\quest type of  game with some combat sequences. And it's not a cheap travesty either, because while playing you actually see that the developers very much cared about the game, and spent the (humble) budget money wisely; don't be fooled by "professional journalists" opinions and the underwhelming PR campaign. So, what CAN you expect?+stellar voice acting and dialogue+enveloping authentic "bookish" atmosphere+solid writing and story +good level design and detailed environment -combat system is janky - this is where the limitations of budget really showing.-the game relies a bit too much on a puzzles of one particular type (when you need to restore a right picture or order of things)note: i've beaten the game once, playing as Edward (as per canon), but planning to make another run as Emily (as per canon, of course).As of now, solid 8\10, or even 10 if you're a fan of the old AitD.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark was a pretty good surprise and honestly better than I expected.It does have a good variety of environments and those are usually really beautiful. I like the Lovecraft inspiration and the vibes from Louisiana. The story and music are both pretty good and the pacing is actually nice, so I never got bored.It's essentially a mix of survival-horror (especially in Hard mode) and investigation. The mansion isn't as threatening as in the original, but after all this is a re-imagination and not a remake, while still being really respectful to the original material in general. There's a few bugs/issues, and the combat is clunky (shooting is fine, but the rest meh, I didn't like throwing items). I recommend to adjust camera settings because the default ones aren't the best and make the combat even worse imo. It's not an AAA and it's sometimes obvious, the presentation can be a bit rough at times, but it does have a soul.In the end, Pieces Interactive did a good job and it's a pleasant surprise to play an Alone in the Dark that's not only pretty good, but also closer to the first game than whatever we got since AitD 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review (again, and I promise I'm not bipolar):I've been waiting for this game, LITERALLY, for 32 years. Was the wait worth it?30 minutes into the game and I was absolutely in love. 6 hours later, I'm not in love anymore. And I'm more disappointed than I could imagine. Tho, I finally decide to recommend the title, in order to try to resurrect the franchise.Why this change of heart?The beautiful thing about Steam is democracy in reviews. You can speak the truth about things.This game isn't what I was promised, and that's a huge disappointment. I'm a true fan of the original series from Infogrames. I grew up with those games.What's wrong with this title? It's only halfway of what I expected it to be.The game itself is the remake I could have expected in 2005 to 2010. This game arrives 16 years later.Gameplay is poor; there's not much to do, most of the places you interact with are empty. Why? Door and area discovery feels like a bad copy of Resident Evil, when Resident Evil series are, in fact, a copy of the original AitD. Go to this point to get the key for the other point. I'm missing a lot of puzzles/riddles here.I read some reviews saying the puzzles are easy. That's true. As a hardcore gamer, I've come to realize that the "democratization" of videogames for everybody has made puzzle designers hollow and a little lazy. I'd prefer challenges and things to make you think more, and let bad players check out walkthroughs and videos. Why does everybody have to play at the level of "not very smart" people?Combat system: I understand what they intended to do, but they didn't achieve it. The movements are clunky. Not organic. The characters are considerably slower than they should be. If you have no weapon, you can't use your fists or feet to try and fight, so if you break your melee weapon, you'll be in trouble (just reload the game if the enemy is covering the only exit). It seems they didn't pay attention to this department. 3/10.Enemy AI: It's ironic that in the era of Artificial Intelligence we have to witness enemies with a super simple pattern: run into you and attack you straight forward. There's nothing close to variety or strategy here. The distraction system by using interaction with elements in the environment could have been way better. Not a lot of variety in monsters.I had to put sensitivity at 2 out of 10 because this game seems not to have been balanced for PC gamers. I have to put my mouse sensitivity at the lowest setting because it was close to impossible to aim or move the camera with precision.Graphics are truly fine. 7/10. But visual bugs are killing me (specially clipping).Very good plot/storytelling: Will give it 8/10. Tries to capture the original smell.Derceto is beautifully designed. This is one of the GREAT areas of the game. The art direction is incredible; I have to say this is the best thing. 10/10 for this.Sound design is great. I'll give it a solid 9/10.The music is fine, but it abuses jazz; I think a more "ambient" or "atmospheric" soundtrack would have benefited the game. Or even a revival of the old school games from Infogrames. 6/10.Collectibles feel unnecessary and like a "classic thing" that doesn't suit this game. I guess they realized, upon finishing the adventure, the little it has to offer, so this way they were able to add 40 extra items into an "empty" game.In the bug department:Some clipping issues that should have been solved by the year we are in.You can trap your character in several spots of the terrain. It seems the mapping hasn't been carefully tested.Some game crashes so far (not a lot, but 4 crashes in 6 hours... that's a lot).At the end of the day, my feelings are that this is another nail in the coffin of a great franchise because the games that were released after the original ones have been disappointing one after another. Really average. This franchise deserved a good development time, and it seems this game needed another year of cooking or some extra employees.OVERALL? 6/10 - I guess I'll have to wait another 32 years for a good remake.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but with this game, I just had to.Because it`s way better then I expected it to be - the trailer was a little misleading in my opinion, I almost didn`t buy the game, because the trailer didn`t click with me - the game was different than what I expected after the trailer - and in a very good way.The graphics are awesome and stunning at times - the game oozes with atmosphere.Voiceacting, Sound and Soundtrack are great. Puzzels are not too easy but also not too challenging.Fighting mechanics are... ok - not the best, but good enough for this game.The only thing, that REALLY felt underdevelopt, was the "throwing"mechanic - you don`t really need it, so it`s no big issue, but it isn`t the best thought that went into this game.I loved the original Alone in the Dark - back in the day when it came out, and the remake has a kind of similar feeling - it even pays a little "homage" to the original at some point.Its at least a 7,5/10, maybe even a 8,5/10 - maybe it`s not for everyone, maybe it`s not mainstream, but I had a hell of time with it and enjoyed it very much.I would recommend Alone in the Dark - definetly when it`s on sale and even on full price.btw - there are 2 playable characters and as far as I can tell (first playthrough with Edward, now second playthrough with Emely), even if the "basic" gameplay stays the same - you`ll get different cutscenes, depending on with character you`ll choose - different enough, to justify playing the game with both characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a game developed by Pieces Interactive and published by THQ Nordic and is a modern retelling of the 1992 classic game of the same nameThe game offers some really pretty graphics and a nice aesthetic, although some ugly textures here and there, it is pleasant all the same. The combat however is absolutely horrendous, worse than The Sinking City, in my opinion, and suffers from the usual cliches you find in horror games which throws my immersion right off - if you're looking to be scared or spooked, this isn't the game for youThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game with some repetitive puzzles and boring walking sections but an okay-ish game nonethelessThe story isn't that much interesting and I really tried to enjoy it but just didn't, I must say I preferred the manor sections over the other-world sections, as they didn't heavily rely on the broken, boring and clunky combat unlike the other-world areas and emphasised more on investigating and looking for clues And having the story from two different angles  have been interesting, but rather than actually running with it and making the two different characters experience two different stories, they just did the usual thing of having roughly the same story told just with different cutscenes and dialogue options, not what I wanted when they were marketing it as having two different stories toldAlone in the Dark overall, however, is a okay-ish "horror" game to play in short bursts but if you're expecting a coherent modern retelling to the 1990's classic, this ain't it...

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I used the recommend button, I'm more on the neutral side regarding the game.Yes, the game is a good survival horror, but after playing so many Resident Evil games, it feels a bit outdated.The story is fine, I enjoyed the main characters and every other character from the game. There are a great variety of locations with the mansion being the core one. The design of these locations are beautiful. The graphics are nice. The game is well-optimized I'd say. There were 2-3 times when the game were stuttering a lot, but a PC restart fixes that. Not sure why.Now, for the worst part of the game, the gameplay. The enemies are not that interesting and they are pretty repetitive. There are only two bosses in the game, both at the end of the game, one after another.There are only 4 guns, and you can't upgrade them, but considering the lack of variety of enemies, I think it is fine.Some of the puzzles were nice, but I didn't like that a lot of time the item to solve the puzzle was in the same room as the puzzle. The game is pretty short, you can beat it in under 8 hours, even if you try to collect everything. I played on standard and didn't die even once. You can play with two separate characters. Each character have separate cutscenes, a small exclusive mission and that's it. Basically the story doesn't go in parallel like in RE2. There are just two different stories depending on the character that you choose.I can't say that I didn't enjoy the game, so if you are a survival horrors fan, you should definitely play it.I still look forward for the Alone In The Dark 2 remake, if there will be one.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've gotten to and started chapter 3 which is roughly the halfway point and I have decided to write a short, but hopefully useful, review. First, lets mention performance. My system specs are an i9 7900x CPU, 32Gb RAM,7900xt GPU, NVME storage. I've been running the game at max setting with no upscaling at a native resolution of 3840x2160. The frame rates I have been getting in the game have been 80fps for the most part. However, some ares have seen my frames drop down to around 60fps for no apparent reason. This just shows that some areas of the game need some additional optimisation which I'm sure will happen at some point. The more egregious issue though is stutter. It's not consistent, but it does happen whenever you enter a new area/room and can overstay it's welcome. I have also had to restart a couple of times due to getting stuck on the terrain. All of these things can be fixed with patches, so if any of this will bother you, you should hold off on buying until it's been patched. Now onto graphics and game play. Graphically, the game looks about 5 years old. It is nice overall, with a nice atmosphere but has some very ugly spots and seems to be missing shadows in many places. Reflections look very UE4, which isn't saying much. Character models look basic. I would advise not to compare this game to something like Resident Evil or Alan Wake 2 when it comes to graphics and you'll be happy with the overall look. How the game plays though is where it will definitely be make or break for many. It plays like it's 10 years old. Your walking speed is slightly too slow, but you can jog everywhere. Stealth is just doing a half crouch and moving even slower. Combat has no feeling to it, especially the melee combat. Gun combat feels clumsy. When you look into what the developers were going for, that is a true spiritual recreation of the original Alone in the Dark, then I would say that they nailed it. Unfortunately that's also it's potential downfall, as what has been released feels old and dated, especially if one attempts to compare it to any other game within the horror genre released in the past 10 years or so. I will undoubtedly finish at least one play through of the game because I do think it has something worth playing, but there is no getting around the fact that is does feel and looking rather old and dated. It also feels like it was put together by a small studio with a very limited budget, which when you look, it was. Maybe it all makes sense.

Also  My favorite part of the game was the  Overall I enjoyed it! Sad to hear that the studio has been closed but I am glad the devs put out New Game Plus for us.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Alone in the Dark became the legacy name it is, it was a video game my 11 year old brother installed on the computer. When the game began, I was so amazed - 3d  MY HOUSE???? The technology at the time was great even though it is quite humble in todays standards, even in the regards of the tech at the time.. BUT, the important thing was the vibe and feeling it created. The game unique in every aspect with the gameplay and the puzzles. I would open the door to a bathroom and suddenly some strange and eldritchian tub monster is killing me, I punch knight armor and now it is alive (I suspected it would). So anyways, nostalgia ramble aside I think the big question is: IS THIS GAME ALONE IN THE DARK, AND DOES IT GET THIS VIBE RIGHT?Well, yes, and greatly so! It currently (mid 2024) full price, and while it doesn't feel like a full price game as far as cinematics and razzle dazzle, the story, characters, gameplay, and puzzles all feel like a full price game. There were moments that scared me, moments where I was eagerly exploring the mansion, moments where I enjoyed the characters.. it was great. 8/10, on the border with a bullseye for what I wanted out of the game. There's new game plus to get the full story you must play both characters as they have their own journeys. All in all, I think users should go in with a A quality expection instead of AAA. This game really is on the exact path it needs to be. I would buy a sequel on launch, and I think the team did a 10/10 job, this franchise has been cursed and it is so nice to see something meaningful and not a name grab. You did it and it is appreciated, it brought me new nostalgia memories.

_childDocuments_.review: This gioco is very tanta robba.Don't trust review mentioning bad combat because that's completely false. If you like games like the first Alan Wake or Resident Evil 3 remake, the combat is quite similar to those with the sorta precise dodging and works well enough that you can get through the entire game without firing a single bullet or taking a hit.The story is quite nice: not exactly horror, more like noir mystery. It's definitely refreshing compared to other games that try to overdo the horror theme and end up being extremely predictable with their jump scares or horror tropes.The only real cons that are worth mentioning are some collisions getting you stuck on map props, but you can in 99% of the cases just save, reload, and you're good to resume.Very recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine. It's honestly nothing special or unique. It's more of a mystery game than horror, but the story is mostly told through documents that you have to pause the game to listen to or read yourself. Without them the story doesnt make a lot of sense. With them, the story makes more sense but it wasnt for me. The combat is clunky and not needed for the majority of the game and then the final boss fight depends on it. Lastly, I got stuck on objects several times while playing the game causing me to restart. Hopefully it'll be fixed in a patch. I recommend the game only if those things dont bother you or you can get it via a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a Lovecraft fan? You are going to absolutely love this game! It is the best Lovecraft game I have played in years and has so many Easter eggs you will constantly find yourself smiling. If you are a survival horror fan, it's a great expansion to the genre. The story is short, but playing through it twice gives you the whole picture and will take you about 12-14 hours.  Highly recommend playing this, and hoping for a second one

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished a playthrough with Emily and will probably start a playthrough with Edward in a little bit, it's not re-inventing the wheel or anything like that,  but this is still the best Alone in the dark has been in years.  The world building/ atmosphere, is especially a highlight,  the game is at it's best when it's building up tension and you're solving puzzles/ discovering lore. The music is creepy the story is interesting. It's a bit of shame that the combat feels a little clunky at times, to the point where when fights break out the game kind looses the sense of being creepy. The handgun feels like it has little impact, the melee weapons are imprecise and the throwables would be a lot more fun if you could carry them with you, I understand the idea was probably to lean more into the horror and make combat feel more deliberate and a last ditch effort to put you in the shoes of the character, the thing is, clunky gameplay takes me more out of the game, than and slight deviation into action for the combat.... regardless if you like survival horrors, especially the puzzle solving elements and dark Gothic world building, it is definitely worth your time

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat this game with one character, Edward, and loved every second of it.I took my time exploring everywhere, reading all the notes, getting involved in the story and it took me 8.6 hours to complete.Positives:+ The voice acting is top tier excellent, great cast+ The smooth jazz music is beautiful and haunting while playing, sometimes gives a Twin Peaks Vibe+ The art direction is gorgeous, beautiful original environments+ The puzzles were well balanced and original, not too difficult, did not need a guide+ There are many references to the old Alone in the Dark games and also Resident Evil, which was fun+ The story is really deep and interesting if you read through all the notesNegatives- Not much enemy variety, or enemies in general, the game is 80% exploration and 20% fighting I would say- The combat controls are old school, not many weapons in the game- Could have used more boss fightsThis is a mature well made game, with an emphasis on exploration, story, and art direction. (Not on combat)Overall I loved it and give it a 9.5 / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark COULD be a good game.   It has an interesting story, with some good voice-actors, beautiful environments and lots of Lovecraft lore to tickle my fancy.  But the bugs, forced tedious combat and clear content-cuts to the game just aren`t worth it for their asking price.      The game is a slight (and I mean SLIGHT) re-telling of the original Alone in the Dark.  However, in this version, Emily Hartwood's uncle didn`t commit suicide in his manor. This time, he is missing at a mental hospital that was helping him.  Aside from some names, a few easter-eggs and the key/door progression, nothing else is similar between the two. This story is a whole new beast.  You play as either Emily Hartwood or Private Investigate Edward Carnby, who was hired by Emily to help find her uncle who went missing at Derceto Manor, a place where the wealthy can seek treatment for their problems.You manage to convince the staff to let you investigate the manor, resulting in you diving deeper and deeper into the strange and unusual supernatural, with it blurring fantasy and reality.The story for Emily was pretty interesting, with it having her face her own demons (both metaphorical and literal), but nearly everyone is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to her, usually dismissing her or even giving thinly-veiled threats.   Even Carnby is dismissive of her most of the game, and she is the freaking client!But the game has you visiting various places with different themes, with some truly cool looking monsters to deal with, and with the lead-up to the final boss going freaking balls-to-the-wall crazy, which I loved. <3  As I said before, the story is pretty good, it just sucks that it is being bogged down by so many other issues.Combat is REALLY bad in this game.  And I don`t just mean it`s not fun either. I mean it is really broken. Monsters on normal difficulty will take an entire pistol clip to kill a single one of them, assuming it counts the shots hitting them to begin with.   If they get too close to you, you will just aim your pistol in some random direction and fire there instead.   It takes 2 shotgun blasts to the chest to kill one of them as well...   And I am still talking about the FIRST enemy types in the game.  Good luck trying to melee or even shoot those little beetle bastards when 2-3 of them are rushing you at once, while they can literally drop your health to minimum in a single headbutt.Melee weapons break easily too, often right after killing a single enemy, which forces you to use your range weapons up close again. The game "encourages" you to use stealth and use thrown items as decoys while you sneak around them, but that is also broken.  Because while you are sneaking, the moment you pick up a brick to throw it, you automatically stand up, causing you to become detected.    Not to mention nearly all the monster infested areas are these long-narrow corridors with objects and corners you just get stuck on randomly, resulting in the enemy hitting you and pretty much stun-locking you. Most of the time the monsters are scripted to spawn in on you, already being agitated, so you can`t run from them or hide. The game forces you to fight.  They will also chase you indefinitely, unless you manage to get up a ladder or a door to close between you (which you can`t manually do)There is a dodge function, but it only works half the time. Good chance you will just dodge into an object or the monster itself and get stuck. Enemy damage is REALLY weird. Sometimes they will hit you for a small amount, and sometimes they will knock you down to barely alive, even if it is the same monster doing the same attack.  The whole system is just designed to bog down progress and force the player to keep back tracking to pick up melee items, just in order to progress.  I nearly quit the damn game, it was so bad...Puzzles are OK.  It is 90% finding the lock-combination with the last 10% being "make a picture in the grid".   Nothing at all like the original's fun puzzles.  It usually devolves into "find clue 1 so you can get combination B.  Now go to puzzle X and enter in Combination B using the notes from Clue 1".    Was never really engaging.    Yes, everyone knows the character models look kind of "meh".  Voice-acting is pretty good though, although it becomes clear that they all were reading their lines alone in a booth, and never actually recorded dialogue between 2 real people.    They seemed to have given an honest try though. Models are still bad though.Each character is unique and SEEMS to have a personality, but you don`t get to interact with ANY of them enough to actually start caring.   There is one character called Ruth that Emily is apparently really attached to and wants to be best of friends, but there is no reason WHY Emily acts that way.  You interact with Ruth maybe 3 times the entire story.    It feels like they cut A LOT of content, which really sucks, because I was actually really interested in the characters.  I WANTED to learn more about them.  Why are they here? What is their connection to manor and the missing uncle?  Are they good or are they bad?      The first question barely gets glossed over in a literal document you find in the game (which is easy to miss). The other 2 questions only get answered right at the VERY end of the chapter, and you are essentially just being told by the devs to "just roll with it".They were doing a good job with the characters when they ARE in the game, but they barely are there, which makes it moot. You literally could take out every side-character from the game, and it wouldn`t have made a difference in the end.  This game has a few bugs.  I never crashed or T-Posed, but I had gotten permanently stuck between two chairs or on a strange object, requiring me to have to reload a save more than a few times. Loading between areas has some REALLY bad stutter issues. Usually I don`t mind, but not when I am being pursued by a monster or trying to watch a cutscene. You also get stuck on a lot of small objects littering the scene. I wanted to edit the options menu, which resulted in the UI showing the options menu, but the game still thought I was on the main-menu which caused some pretty interesting errors.  Would give it a ~Meh review, if Steam would let me.  I tried REALLY hard to love this game.  And I mean REALLY hard, but I just cant recommend it.  It feels VERY incomplete in a lot of aspects.  If they halved the asking price, I would probably recommend it then, but currently, I cannot.  There is a bit of a gem hidden in this game but there is just too many bugs and bad design choices to let it shine.I played the game as Emily and beat it within 10 hours.  (found all the hidden goodies)The story is pretty interesting, with more than enough Lovecraftian vibes to it.  Voice acting was good, but I really didn`t care (AKA never got a chance TO care) about the people themselves.If you grab the game, I STRONGLY suggest playing it on Easy mode, just to save yourself the headache.  The freaking combat...  It is horrible.  I mean...REALLY bad...  It isn`t hard, just freaking tedious.  I nearly quit playing it because how quickly weapons break, how much ammo is needed to kill a monster and how narrow the corridors are which makes fleeing nearly impossible since you get stuck on the smallest objects.Also, don`t grab it for full price, until they fix the bugs and issues.  I enjoyed the game, but it is not worth their current asking price.I did nearly ♥♥♥♥ my pants the first time I pointed my gun at "The Dark Man".  THAT is how you do a villian! Now, if you excuse me, I`m gonna go play the original Alone in the Dark now. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: So, let me start - as someone who has never played the original, or any of the sequels, I can say that I have quite enjoyed what they delivered. The Game has heavy inspiration from some other big horror games out there (e.g. RE4R, Silent Hill...), but manages to utilize it's own mechanics in a different approach. The Game is, as far as I have played it ~6hrs long, which is quite okay-ish for a hefty 60€ price tag. Would I recommend it? Definitely, yeah!Alone in the Dark manages to grab your attention by slowly piecing everything together, even with several clues/notes about the story. You can choose between a modern and old-school playstyle, with the only difference being on how much clues you get for solving puzzles (old-school has less, as the name says). The graphics are good, controls sometimes feel a bit wonky, but if you got used to it, it's not a problem for the rest of the game. The only thing which threw me of quite a bit is getting stuck. The game has big problems with calculating the players hitbox, which can lead to getting stuck at stairs, doors and tiny tiles such as barrels & wooden planks (I had to reload a total of 13 times during my playthrough!). Other then that - Get this game if you're looking for something fresh in a survival horror game, since it's not the stereotypical zombie-ressource-gathering-slaying type of game, which is the general market audience atm. Great job, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A very sweet game. Strongly recommended for anyone who enjoys mystic mysteries and themes of the occult; very enjoyably written and directed, not a masterpiece but it sits comfortably above most games nowdays. Don't get the wrong idea with the game's metascore, Alone in the Dark is far from mediocre, though it came out with some performance issues, so take that into consideration.They say the original was "A Virtual Adventure Game Inspired by the Work of H.P. Lovecraft". Now, I've read my fair amount of Lovecraft time ago, but I can't really say I'm that much a connoisseur nor act like I have any sort of superior understanding of what that feller has gone on about, but at the level I'm at, I think this game gets it. Then there's at least the dozen people I counted on the internet that proudly presume they themselves know all about my man Howard, and they confidently claim this remake *really* gets it, so... if you're into Lovecraft, I guess you wont want to miss on this one.Performances felt at least a bit goofy and overly dramatic at first, but after a while it stopped bothering me, it made the game feel awkwardly campy, which actually intensified the scary moments when those came, at least in my experience. Not necessarily a strength nor a weakness, but an adequate and charming quirk.Something else that felt awkward about the game was the very noticeable fact that every character's face model was wholly made from scratch, except for the 2 playable protagonists. It gets a bit distracting once you realise the only real pair of faces are Emily's and Edward's, and everyone else is a fake, but admittedly this also ended up contributing to my unease, since it actually achieved a sort of odd flavoured uncanny valley effect.Combat and locomotion is very serviceable for the kind of game it is; very reminiscent of The Evil Within, for anyone who played it, which you'll know it's not very deep, but it's also not painfully basic: it does just a tiny bit more than the rudimentary, which makes the type of loop that gets old very quick. Unlike The Evil Within, however, Alone in the Dark's combat is a lot more spaced out and well considered in its pace, and the game is shorter, so as a whole it's actually alright.Whether you consider the original a PC Adventure Game or the very first Survival Horror, neither genre can be conceived without some nifty puzzles; in this game, however, they're in fact quite unique for either genre. What I mean is, puzzles in Alone in the Dark are not the type of obtuse "use monkey as wrench" nonsense we've come to expect from the PC adventure genre, but it neither has the sort of mechanical rubik's cube puzzles that characterise Survival Horror. Puzzles in Alone in the Dark lots more resemble irl Escape Room problems, and quite literally are in most instances, with coded locks, safe boxes and even lasers, and with passwords always hiding in some hidden meaning behind a note, or literal writings on the walls. It was actually really cool, because coincidentally I invited my girlfriend to sit along while I played it, and she loves escape rooms more than anything, so she had a ton of fun both watching and being able to participate. Between her and her experience with ERs, and me with my love for SH, we thought the puzzles were dope, I'd say they're of moderate difficulty overall, some easier some harder.Generally, I like to play Survival Horror adjacent games in company because they're great for 1 controller 2+ player gaming, since while the person with the controller always plays the combat, everyone else can participate in figuring out where to go next and how to solve puzzles. Often times I'd much rather play them alone, in part because I tend to develop a sense of intimacy with SH games, but also because I don't want to lose the chance of being actually scared, if that were to happen.Surprisingly, while I played it with my girlfriend watching, this game was actually able to spook us both, even when in each other's company, and even being that my gf isn't easily scared by most media she's experienced. At times it was almost to unbearable for her in fact, and me being the one playing, I can't really say I had as bad of a time as her, but what I can say is that this games' subject matter and imagery managed to unsettle me way more than I anticipated.Now, note how I referred to "Survival Horror adjacent games"; this is not without reason. As a survival horror purist and for everyone else like me, I must say this Alone in the Dark remake is NOT true survival horror, but it's still similar enough to be enjoyable if you play it with reasonable expectations. Saves aren't an integrated game mechanic, there's no resource management besides ammunition limits, and there's not really a "survival" game loop of any sort. There's combat sections and exploration moments, the former sometimes bleeding into the latter to keep you from ever feeling too secure.I played it on the "Hard" combat difficulty and "Old School" guidance difficulty; yes, there's 2 difficulties to choose from, and I believe the hardest of these make a very satisfying experience, at least for someone used to the genre. Keep in mind both my experience with survival horror and my girlfriend's hobby of solving irl escape rooms when evaluating how difficult this game might be for you. I also can't say for sure everyone will like the puzzles, since we all have different thought processes; I'll just suggest, and if you've been to escape rooms you should know, to remember to always try the simplest possible solution interpretations first, and if they fail, only then begin overthinking.The navigation and exploration in this game was good, the Derceto mansion can be very ornate and baroque in some areas, and the many more sights there is to see are jaw-droppingly beautiful. The progression is very metroidvania-esque, as expected, but often times I felt like the backtracking was very well planned out not to feel like a chore for players less accustomed with survival horror, and the place is not as big as, say, the RPD or the Spencer Mansion, so it'd never take that long to go from corner to corner if it ever came to that.Lastly, if you're smart, you should already know the 2 campaigns aren't parallel plots, but rather 2 different screenings of the same story: not like RE2's A and B scenarios, but rather 2 A scenarios, more similar to what happens in the first Resident Evil. In my opinion, the development of the story and plot make more sense when playing with Emily, so I'd advice playing with her first for a better first time experience. Not that Edward's doesn't make sense, I just think Emily's makes the better movie, but they're both good scenarios, each with their different cutscenes, character interactions and even some stages unique to their own.Once again I say that I fully recommend it, and I'm very glad this remake came out the way it did. I always felt like Alone in the Dark deserved better, and it's good to see it come together this well.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played all six previous AitD games (plus the two prologues) this certainly does look and feel like an Alone in the Dark game. It is quite possibly the best AitD game out there, only rivaled by The New Nightmare, and a worthy heir to the original which by today's standards is incredibly janky. And let's not even talk about AitD2, 3, 5/Inferno/2008 or, God forbid, Illumination.I can understand the combat is not for everyone, considering how janky it is, but I had good fun with it. The atmosphere was on point and the whole game has this weird, dream-like feel to it that I enjoyed. The transitions from one world to another are made incredibly well. Of course there are also bugs, like getting stuck on objects, sound glitches and general stuttering. Hopefully the game is updated to run better in the future.Thus far I only finished Carnby's playthrough but I am excited to go through Emily's story as well soon enough. Glad to see this series brought back from whatever limbo it was in.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A nice pulp-y romp, highly recommend. Made with plenty of love and references to the other games. I know the old media it's referencing, girlfriend knows the other games in the series, together we had a great time seeing all the love and faith poured into it.Unfortunately, AA games don't sell well, and the company got immediately axed, so no patches to the classic Alone in the Dark jank, but it's perfectly serviceable... just remember to save occasionally in case you get stuck behind a chest or something. Other than that, enjoy a great Resident Evil-like. Or, given Resident Evil was based on this series, enjoy an Alone in the Dark-like, I guess?Also, I played through with controller, girlfriend (AitD superfan) played with mouse+keyboard, both worked fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game fully expecting to regret it - it's a modern reboot after all, though I hadn't played the original. Bracing myself for a horrible flop, I booted it up cursing my weakness for the man with the naughty-named cat. By then end of the first hour though, I found the game really growing on me, and by the end I felt it to be one of the better Lovecraftian games to come out in recent times. I certainly had a better time here than in the Sinking City, or in the actual Call of Cthulhu game itself. When I say Lovecraftian, I don't mean the modern application of the term in which the tentacled Mythos provides content for a shooting gallery - this actually feels much more like something the man from Providence might write. The story feels like a classic scenario from the Call of Cthulhu TTRPG - you get an unsettling letter from an estranged and possibly insane relative, so you and your PI comrade run off into the swamps to find the isolated nuthouse he's trapped in, impolitely tooled up with firearms that aren't really called for by the situation. Like in the tabletop game, by the end of the tale everything is on fire and it's not really clear whether the investigators managed to make anything better. The combat is a bit clumsy and unrefined, although the shotgun sounds and feels surprisingly good, but then horror games shouldn't really be about fighting anyway. I do think there might be a bit too much combat if anything, though it's nothing like the amount found in Resident Evil. They do have the sense to keep most of the violence in your strange visions and out of the house itself, which is a good move as they've done a good job making the place quietly creepy and it'd be jarring to keep discharging a tommy gun in the parlour. I liked the sudden transitions from the "real" Derceto to the dreamworld locations - sometimes you'll open a door and find yourself in a warped version of the mansion, or even somewhere else entirely, and these moments are often as visually striking as they are surprising. It's a good kind of jarring feeling that helps put you in the shoes of the protagonists; the house has a wrongness to it that you can feel as they do. I did find the acting in places a bit wooden - surprisingly, the Carnby/David Harbour playthrough was a lot worse for this, and it was a pleasant relief to move onto the Emily/Jodie Comer storyline where the interactions between characters felt a bit more natural. The supporting cast vary in quality but generally aren't bad. The puzzling was actually very good - there are plenty of clues and hints in the notes you find while exploring the manor, and some of the puzzles actually require you to read and reread documents and work things out for yourself, but they also aren't so obtuse that they'll drive you to look things up. It's quite old-school, and quite refreshing in an age where games fall over themselves to solve puzzles for you. The secret endings are an excellent addition too - after running through both the main storylines, they make the game worth coming back to and offer significant changes to the outcome. Finally, I have to praise the addition of New Game+ in the most recent patch, which lets you start fully-armed and ready to look out for the sneaky alterations added especially for this mode. I couldn't say from experience how close the game is to the original, but for me I'd gladly play a sequel if by some miracle it ever came about.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, sprinkled on top by some jankiness. Very enjoyable if you're into horrors with cryptic story and a fair bit of reading to piece it together.I'm currently halfway through my second playthrough. I wish I could say that Alone in the Dark is an amazing game.And it's very close to being one! However, despite looking nice, having great voice acting, solid gameplay, good music, there's always a feeling that the developers didn't have enough time and/or budget to give this game the final polish.For every great thing that I found in Alone in the Dark, there always was some jankiness to counter it. Nothing gamebreaking, mind you. But always noticeable enough to wonder - what happened?Here's some examples.Main character models look terrific! And their animations are top-notch. Most of the side characters are great too. Some are good... but then the others look like from 2010. Like Juan in Taroella; the writer Cassandra; or Lottie. It's very jarring seeing them alongside superb and highly detailed and extremely well animated main characters' models.Overal music score is great! However, couple sections I could only describe as cacophony. I guess it's suppose to be "scary". But as someone who doesn't get scared by horror games (except phychological ones, which this is not), I just find it annoying more than anything.Ranged combad is good (for a survival horror game, keep in mind!). Shooting is solid, weapons feel right and have nice punch to them. Dodge is responsive, so you can always get out of harm's way quickly, reposition and take aim again. But at the same time melee is all sort of jank and nothing more than spamming 1 button. So I just almost never use it. Fortunately, the game gives more than enough ammo to keep me stocked up all the time.Environments are very detailed with tons of various small props. Some scenes are super cool to look at, with lots of effort and artistry put behind them. But whoever worked on lightmaps did a very poor job - seams are everywhere on smaller objects, some shadows look like a total mess or bleed through onto neightbouring geometry, making objects look muddy.I like smaller details of characters reacting to their envioronments like looking around or putting their hands on guardrails.... but at the same time half of their fingers clip through at weird angles every time they do it.Once at the very beginning of my first playthrough I got stuck in a wooden box. So I had to reload from checkpoint. Fortunately, the game saves very often, so I "lost" about 4 minutes of gameplay. After that I just kept to clearly designated gameplay areas and didn't try to test the boundaries of where I could squeeze to. So it was smooth sailing henceforth, and I haven't encountered any issues with collisions.Now, I started my review by saying that I'm playing through the game for the second time. And that's because despite some jankiness to it, as mentioned already, I really enjoyed my time with Alone in the Dark. However it is worth mentioning that if you're not into reading (or listening, since EVERYTHING is narrated in here, but can be turned off) journals, book pages, notes and documents for clues to piece the story together, this might not be the game for you. Because by the end you gonna be very confused about what is going on.I really like the dialogues in this game. They are very very nicely scripted and feel real. Well, if you take into account that it all takes place in a loony bin. What I especially liked is how different it feels to play as different characters.At the start we are given a choise to play as Emily or detective Edward. Playing as the detective, people around you will act respectful, cautious, reserved. Playing as Emily, however, completely switches things around. Characters are more hostile. Some men act like real creeps, whether intentionally threatening or not. Others act patronizing and condescending despite having good intentions. Devs showed man-woman power dynamics of early 1900's in excellent detail that feels realistic. And speaking of second playthrough, playing as either Emily or Edward feels different enough to make the game feel fresh even second time. Dialogues are completely differet. Some events take place in different order. Some scenes and levels are totally different. And the story pieces together more by having different perspectives.What I find weird, is that in Alone in the Dark by default players will get a good ending. And you'll have to work to see bad endings. Which is totally backward to how it's usually done in video games - good ending serves as an incentive to put more effort into the playthrough to unlock it.All in all, I really enjoyed Alone in the Dark, and I hope the developers will make more games like this. But maybe with a bit more polish next time.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Alone in the Dark (1992) is a masterpiece. It introduced 3D animated polygonal characters in pre-rendered 3D environment with fixed camera. The charming frames are very cinematographic and thrilling, art direction is top notch still today. It's the father of Resident Evil but gameplay was quite different. You shot two or three zombies/monsters at all. The main gameplay is based on puzzles. The very good story is inspired by Lovecrat Mythos.No other titles in the franchise came close to the first one. Unluckily it's also the case for this new rendition.Let's see the reason why.1) Stuttering is the real protagonist of the experience. It's really unnerving. It depends on software, not on hardware, I own beefy PC.2) Too many hard weapons and shootings kill the atmosphere, the story and the protagonists. You cannot turn Alone in the Dark into Resident Evil, very bad move. Combats mechanics are really really ugly, old school, a bad old school! The final boss is really a nightmare because of the flawed mechanics. Very unnerving. Still in 2024 you find bullets and weapons scattered on your path or through the rooms of the house with no reason at all!3) Story has completely no sense, very ugly! The usual re-heated soup based on the assumption that the protagonist is mad, so everything is possible even if it has no sense! It's like to have no story at all! Still in 2024 you discover the not-existent story by reading documents, diary pages and letters scattered through the rooms of the house with no reason! Ridiculous! Very very bad, very disappointing! It looks like they wrote the bad ridiculous story with no inspiration, as willing to destroy the franchise. And they succeeded! I think there'll be no more AID games. 4) Puzzles are there but are forgettable, nothing special. Plus, in 2024 you cannot develop a game as you were in 1992, where puzzles have completely no sense in relation to the story. They have just an end in themselves, just to make you play with your digital toy.A few positive things: lot of references to the original first title, the attic, the knife, the tree, etc. even a few sequences with fixed camera!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. It is like Resident Evil meets Evil Within. The only problem is the last chapter (chapter 5). It felt way too short and rushed. _childDocuments_.review: Decent game with an interesting story. It is worth playing through with both characters since there are story changes with different cutscenes with each. Also, not all collectibles are accessible with one playthrough. You need to get all of them to unlock all the different endings. The best part has to be the story. It was definitely more interesting than expected. However, the two main issues with the game are performance and combat:I noticed stuttering when loading new areas on 3 of my computers I tested this game on. They range from lower mid tier to high tier gaming computers.  It isn't bad but can be pretty noticeable at times. Especially if you are running the game with an older CPU. I noticed some bugs here and there but not bad and nothing game breaking. Hopefully patches improve things in the future.In regards to the combat, it is passable but can be quite annoying. Especially if you play on the higher difficulties. I can't speak for the hardest difficulty but on the standard one (recommended one) the enemies tend to be bullet sponges and can kill you in a couple hits. The melee attacks feel like you are just wildly swinging a weapon but it kills things. Also, when you go to zoom to aim your weapon it completely shifts the camera super close to your character. Basically removes your peripheral view so you can only see right  in front of you. Pretty annoying when you are in fighting multiple enemies at once. Setting the game to use the max FOV didn't help either. Overall the combat feel unrefined and kind of outdated but it works.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading this review keep in mind I've only finished the game as Edward Carnby. Apparently this game warrants two playthroughs with both characters, but from my understanding the only differences are a couple of different dialogues and a different level in Chapter 4. I didn't feel like playing through it a second time, reasons below.As a lifelong fan of the series, I feel somewhat relieved that this game is possibly it's final dying breath. Finally, after 20 years, we get a proper, true to brand, Alone in The Dark game. It's a very underwhelming experience, yes, but it's a proper send-off to one of the most influential horror franchises in existence. While this is certainly a relief, it's a mediocre game nonetheless. It was a surprise to see David Harbour as the main protagonist of this game. And we got to see Harbour at the peak of his capabilities here - which, sadly, doesn't sound too promising, as he's not a very good actor. As I expected, his acting was very bland and monotone. He played a detective that was extremely invested into the plot, endangering his life multiple times to see his investigation through, yet he sounds disinterested in everything. AITD was never famous for its voice acting and the characters have always sounded dead inside, so it wouldn't be a problem if it wasn't for some phenomenal voice acting on other characters, specifically Cassandra, Emily and Maccarfey. It's weirdly inconsistent and anticlimatic. At least his face, and the faces of the other characters, were well made. No uncanny valley there. In terms of presentation, AITD is very aesthetically pleasing. The graphics are semi-realistic and they are a perfect fit for the premise. The lightning is beautiful and I've stopped a few times just to admire the sunrays entering the dark halls through the windows (the Library looks amazing!). Cutscenes have some nice animations, too, they're fun to watch. The sound design is great, they've used some of the same techniques as the first Amnesia and Dead Space games did to keep you on your toes at all times. Music is great, reminiscent of Deadly Premonition, a bit too much at times. I just wish these tracks were available on Spotify. Combat serves its purpose, but that's about it. It's very easy, gunplay is okay, dodging is buggy at times but otherwise all of it is okay-ish. I don't have a quarrel with any of the systems here but they're not exceptional either. It's not a shooter so it doesn't matter too much, combat sequences are few and far between and they're easy even on the hardest difficulty.AITD is filled to the brim with puzzles, maybe 2 or 3 of them are good. Pretty much every single puzzle in the game is some sort of a mosaic where you have to rearrange parts of it until it forms a coherent picture. Gets boring pretty quickly. They're simple and I've had more fun figuring out which key fits which lock. What the game does well is it's ability to guide the player without making it feel like the devs are holding their hand. This type of games especially has a big issue in that regard - oftentimes the games either treat the player like they're an idiot that has to have everything done for them OR like they're Einstein and they don't need any sort of guidance, ever. AITD reaches a fine balance where everything seems to flow naturally. I never got stuck and I always knew what my current objective is but at the same time the game didn't treat me like I'm a big dumb baby. Storyline is weird. It's good but feels somewhat incomplete. I don't mean plot holes or anything like that, it just seems like it's missing a few crucial pieces that would make it feel finished and less underwhelming. I've played through this game with my girlfriend and when the credits rolled we both just thought  There was a lot of potential here, especially with , but it goes to waste because the whole storyline seems vague about everything as if they didn't want to get into too much detail to avoid creating plot holes that they would have to fix, if that makes sense. They could have messed with the player's head at so many occasions because it's a perfect premise for it, but they opted for a safe and simplistic route. Oh, and you know how every game set in this time period has this alcoholic traumatised detective as the main character? And the game usually reveals that they've done something horrible? This part was the most underwhelming of it all; not to spoil anything but Carnby really doesn't have it that bad, I feel like 0nlyfans chicks have more plausible reasons to be traumatised with their lack of a parental figure than this dude. So the short character arc didn't convince me, maybe Emily has a better one.All in all, as mediocre as it gets. First true AITD game in 20 years and a proper bullet to the head to my beloved series. I'm glad it dies with this game instead of that horrendous shooter "Illumination".

_childDocuments_.review: Like Evil Within, only a good game.I'm saddened by the fact that this project got lost in the mix pretty quickly. In my opinion, it's one of the of the best games of the year. In the story and narrative part for sure.Let's just make a couple of points things. The combat gameplay in the game is rather mediocre. In this part, it may be inferior not only to triple-A products, but even to many indie projects. The puzzles are not the most inventive and, in some places, even too obvious (however, is that so bad?), though they're still pretty functional and well placed in context (most of them). In general, the B-game's flaws are present, and there's no getting away from them.But there are two things in the game that are very high quality and made with creative ambition - the story and the audio-visual environment. The plot is very interesting and requires, in addition to attention, quite substantial analytical work. It won't just be given to you as it unfolds. This is the game in which reading all the notes is not only desirable, but also necessary. And they are written very well. The plot is imaginative and layered, you will have to put it together like a puzzle, but, I assure you, it is a very rewarding pastime for a person who likes story-oriented games.On top of all this you can overlay an excellent art design, which compensates for the technical simplicity of the game, and just excellent soundtrack and sound design. Aesthetic enjoyment of the game is quite easy to get: there are signs of the era, local context (hello New Orleans voodoo), and a good figurative assemblage of the tone of the game as a whole.After passing the game, if you have been following the story closely, there is a good aftertaste. And despite the fact that the storylines for different characters are not very different, the game still creates interest for you to return to it at least one more time (here I should mention that I myself have finished the game five times). By the way, the length of the game allows you to make repeated playthroughs a rather tiring event: the first time, if you will meticulously explore all the nooks and crannies, it will hardly take you more than 10 hours. Further passages will become much less time-consuming.Of course, I can't miss the fact that our favourite Howard Phillips Lovecraft is fully felt here. The game is permeated with his moods and tone as much as possible. This is one of the best games on the works of the great escapist and digger of the depths of the terrifying.As a whole, this game is more than the sum of its parts. I can absolutely recommend it to fans of good stories and tight atmosphere, especially if you're willing to put up with some rough edges in other aspects of the game. Just remember that some effort will be required here.I could say quite a lot more about the game, but I'll stop myself, as I realise that a little bit of what I've said here might bore the reader. It's a shame that the sequel was reportedly not given the green light. I would have been very interested in returning to this universe. I believe that the creators have a very worthy reimagining of the legendary series, which became the progenitor of the whole genre. I believe that now the return to the series will not be soon, but I hope it will not die at all, because as we know:‘That is not dead which can eternal lie, and with strange aeons even death may die.’

_childDocuments_.review: Generally I quite like this game, if only Steam had more than a good/bad scale it might have been easier to give a more precise rating. As it is now I think the good outweighs the bad.The good stuff first, the mood, the atmosphere, the time and place, the clothing style, I love it. The story also feels fair enough, there's a lot of 1920's pulp fiction, quite a lot of H.P. Lovecraft, the Black Pharaoh, Shub-Niggurath, and other cultist themed content. Though the story is quite linear if you start thinking about it, there's little or no room for free exploring, but it's still good because of the mood.The bad part however is the technical aspect. The graphics are great on epic settings, though they always feel quite blurry, even with motion blur turned off. The problem is the lag, which is enourmous, while at the same time the character for example turns lightning fast, in fact so fast you loose track of which direction your looking in, and where the enemies are. So both too fast at the same time as extremely laggy, makes the combat rather frustrating when you're facing more than one easy opponent. Add to this that the combat itself is rather hard to actually do, and some actions would preferrably require a third hand, or a few extra fingers per hand.And then there's also the minor technical things, like animated video sequences not stretching to the same width as the actual playing screen, giving you large black borders on both sides of the screen, or photo mode not filtering out the mouse pointer, but those are minor things that can be photoshopped away in the streamlibrary. The major issue is the lag and the challenging combat system.And then again, I actually came for the story, not for the combat, so I wouldn't actually mind even more simplified combat. I have enough other combat focused games anyway, but not enough good story-games.

_childDocuments_.review: Story is decent and the atmosphere is phenomenal because you get to travel to a few open (but small) open areas besides the mansion.The sounds and music tracks are good too (The music is alright but not too memorable) and you get to play with two characters and each one has an overall different interaction with all the residents in the mansion, that and the multiple endings you can get by collecting specific items (Game tells you which set of items) make it worth for replaying.But i can't recommend this game due to the lack of polish; there are bugs where you can't pick-up melee items even if the prompt appears, poor animations (You can't clearly tell when an enemy is about to attack oftentimes), sometimes enemies slide all over the place, sometimes you can't pick up collectibles unless you look at them in specific angles (even if you have plenty of space to pick them up), that and the technical stutters in cutscenes.Bats and enemies that look like ticks somehow can teleport like goku and grab you even if you're behind them, and there is a glitch where after solving the final puzzle the game will freeze a couple of seconds before playing a cutscene... But i didn't found game breaking bugs in my two playthroughsAll in all i say this is a good game but the state in which it came is far from desirable

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game with EmilyWould recommend - 8/10While the game felt a bit janky in its controls and combat, which is fine for an AA title, I enjoyed it very much and would recommend it. In regards to price, I personally don't think it delivers beyond AA quality to justify the €60 price tag.As a comparison, Dragons Dogma 2 is an AAA title costing only €5 more.Pros:- story- pacing- writing- voice acting- puzzles- environmental design and atmosphere- gun combatCons:- Forced aim-throwing mechanics- Melee combat- Potential game breaking bug - see side-note belowI rather it would have let you pick up x-number of bricks and molotovs separately, and let you throw them as needed Melee weapons with such low durability made it hardly worth being in the game, I ended up ignoring it for the most part unless I needed to smash a wall in.Side-Note (no story spoilers):Near the end is a seemingly game breaking bug when playing on PC keyboard, when you pick up a key in the back of a room, the screen showing the key seems frozen. No input action will close that popup and you will not be able to continue.There seems to be nothing you can do to pick up the key and continue.If you own a controller, there is a work around, plug in the controller and press B for secondary action (xbox, no clue on PS5)If you play on PC and do not own a controller this might be preventing you from completing the game.The only reason this is not a negative review for that is that there is a workaround but just barely.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original back in the day but do not remember it at all. I also never played any releases of the game since then, so this is my first step back into AITD in decades. Being a veteran of FPS's and RPG's, I was looking for something different.As other reviews state, the combat is pretty wonky.  It isn't noticeably in the early stages of the game, but comes into play later.  Having played NES back in the day (and other systems of the 80s and 90s), I was no stranger to reloading and replaying levels, bosses, etc.  So the wonkiness of the combat wasn't too frustrating for me.Another review stated that the items you pick up and where they are used are very close together and I found that to be true.  The graphics are awesome, albeit a bit stuttery at times (I'm running an i9, 64GB RAM, and a 4080FE).  But if you can play through those issues, it's not too bad of a game.  Great acting, engaging storyline, lots of puzzles to solve.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a decent game that is a bit stuck in the old school mechanics. The game does a very good job setting up an interesting story and atmosphere, and (light) puzzles provide needed breaks from exploration. Unfortunately, as many have already pointed, combat gameplay is lacking. It’s not terrible, but is stuck in the past and does not really add value to the gameplay. Arguably, the game may have been better if it skipped combat altogether (or limited it to a handful of scenarios), and focused even more on puzzles and exploration. Having said all this, this is a solid 6-7/10 game with an interesting story in a genre that we don’t often get these days. It is definitely worth checking out on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw that a new Alone in the Dark was about to be released, I was all but excited: the original Alone in the Dark (1992) was, alongside Wolfenstein 3D and Doom one of the very first games I ever played. I relished Alone in the Dark 2 and 3 as only a fanboy can, yet with the turn of the century came the first Alone in the Dark reboot with which I never connected. Then came the second reboot in 2008 which I never bothered to play. Thus, I was highly sceptical of any new entry in the series, and I had little hopes that this would be any different.Now, having done every single achievement in this game all I can say is: thank you, Pieces Interactive, for offering a nostalgia trip like none other.As befits a proper Alone in the Dark reboot, we play as either private detective Edward Carnby or Emily Hartwood – motion captured and voiced by none other than David Harbour and Jodie Comer respectively – who make their way to Derceto Manor in Louisiana to look for Jeremy Hartwood, Emily's uncle. What ought to have been a routine visit to check up on the elder Hartwood turns into a search as the pair learn from the mansion’s cadre of suspicious characters that Jeremy has gone missing and is nowhere to be found. Soon, our protagonists find themselves in the midst of an interweaving plot involving them, the missing Hartwood, the unlikely inhabitants of the mansion and twisted entities from beyond that plague the mansion. For true to its predecessor's fashion, Alone in the Dark 2024's Derceto is filled with monsters that are either heavily inspired by Lovecraft's writings or directly taken from the late writer's lore.Enemies invariably takes us to combat, which draws heavily from the Resident Evil series – themselves arguably disciples of the original Alone in the Dark. Thus, ammunition is a scarce commodity throughout the game and much more so are medicinal canteens that replenish your lost health. Melee weapons have a limited durability before they break, which makes it impossible to melee your way through the game to save ammo. Some reviewers have found the combat to be rather clunky, which I do not entirely deny. Rather, I make a case for it being spot on with the game’s overall feel, for making it a seamless shooter would have utterly detracted from the nostalgic feel of the game.For the game is all about nostalgia: it is filled to the brim with references and nods to the original games ranging from collectibles to easter eggs  which, while not entirely following the original storyline, do ground the newest game’s story on that of its illustrious predecessor . Even the weapons are a throwback to the original Alone in the Dark titles, albeit the game arguably draws more from the second, rather than the first game of the series in this regard. There is, finally, something that I cannot put into words, which is the overall feel of the game: Derceto and the whole story truly feels like an Alone in the Dark title, from the puzzles, to the aesthetics of the mansion, everything reeks Alone in the Dark. For those of us feeling extra nostalgic, there are also the DLC included in the Deluxe Edition which allow us to swap our character’s skins for their 1992 equivalents and even includes an 8-bit filter to make the game look straight out of the ‘90s. If anything, my biggest complaint is that we should have had a DLC that swaps the current OST with that of the original game (the monster theme from the DOS version is something I seriously missed in this game!) and we could also have used ‘90s skins for the monsters as well (there is no beating those skeletons walking with their arms stretched).That is not to say that the game is perfect: as stated, combat feels a tad stiff at times and there is the occasional frame drop every now and then. Graphics have also been heavily criticised, albeit unfairly: the game might look like a title from the early PS4 era, but that is nothing wrong per se. First, not all games need to be AAA lookers to deliver a solid gaming experience. Second, Alone in the Dark 2024’s price tag accurately reflects this. My only qualm would be that, while I did find the game’s length to be spot on, I ended up wanting for more (I would not have extended the main story, but I would definitely like to have a DLC of sorts at some point). Yet ultimately, none of these aspects detract from the game’s enjoyment.For in the end, Alone in the Dark (2024) is the ultimate love letter to a genre-defining classic: it is a touching, beautiful tribute to all of us who hold the original game dear in our hearts. Many may claim my review to be biased and written with rose-tinted glasses; a case could be made indeed for my being lenient with the game’s weaker aspects out of nostalgia for the original 1992 instalment. Yet the opposite holds true: I was (and still am) absolutely critical of every Alone in the Dark title that came after the original trilogy and my bar was impossibly high in terms of what I expected of a new instalment in the franchise. Yet Alone in the Dark 2024 delivered far beyond what I dared to expect: for the 20 or so hours that took me to 100% this game, I journeyed back in time to my kitchen’s PC, sitting on my father’s lap while my mum cooked dinner behind us, completely oblivious to the hardships of adult life; a journey back to a happier time; an easier time. And for that I cannot help but be grateful to the developers.9/10TL;DR: Nostalgia trip like no other. Will transport you to the ‘90s and hard. Has some minor technical issues that do not significantly detract from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere and Setting:The 2024 reboot of "Alone in the Dark" delivers a chillingly atmospheric experience, setting itself in a noir-infused 1930s America, embracing Lovecraftian elements that perfectly blend the eerie with the historical. The Southern Gothic elements provide a perfect backdrop for the unnerving narrative, enhancing the game's ability to unsettle rather than outright scare.Gameplay Mechanics:The gameplay mechanics pay homage to the original while adapting to modern expectations. The introduction of melee weapons that degrade over time and clunky yet thematic gunplay adds to the survival horror feel, reminiscent of the original's challenging encounters. The incorporation of modern controls, such as jogging and varied actions, brings a refreshed feel to the navigation and interaction within the game's world.Puzzle Design:Puzzles in the game maintain thematic consistency with the setting, though they occasionally veer into the arbitrary, asking players to make leaps in logic that may not feel entirely grounded in the game’s world. This could be a minor setback for players who prefer more intuitively designed puzzles that clearly tie into the storyline.Narrative and Storytelling:The narrative progression is a standout feature, rich with Lovecraftian themes of cosmic horror and the fragility of human sanity. The transformation of Derceto into an asylum, while a departure from the mansion setting of the original, offers new storytelling opportunities and maintains a strong narrative thread that is both creepy and engaging. The game’s approach to horror focuses more on psychological tension rather than relying heavily on jump scares, which is a welcomed direction for players who prefer suspense over shock.Audio and Visuals:The audiovisual presentation of the game is compelling. The soundtrack’s southern jazz influences mesh well with the time period, enhancing the immersive experience. Visually, the game leverages Unreal Engine technology to produce detailed and realistic environments, although there are occasional technical shortcomings in elements like depth of field and glass rendering.Player Experience:The game's design seems well-suited for consumption in short sessions, allowing players to digest its intense atmosphere and complex narrative in manageable chunks. This pacing could be particularly appealing to those who value story and atmosphere over extended gameplay sessions.Overall Impression:"Alone in the Dark" (2024) is an exceptional entry in the survival horror genre, effectively blending traditional elements with modern enhancements to create a deeply atmospheric and engaging experience. It stands as both a tribute to and a reinvention of its namesake, promising both newcomers and fans of the original a richly layered exploration of horror and narrative depth.
