_childDocuments_.review: The first Alone in the Dark in a long time that do the originals justice.Some highlights for me are:- Resource scarcity which is well balanced and made me give it a second though before wasting precious bullets.- Amazing atmosphere and art design with great detail throughout.- The sound design is great.- Snappy menus which provide some great quality of life features.Now, having played through the game twice. It's not without its faults. But the issues are the type that can be resolved in a future patch. And those are:- I ended up getting stuck on terrain more than once - and in one case it even resulted in a game over. The constant asset streaming and loading between - The combat is satisfactory in the case that it does what it's suppose to - but not much more than that. It provides some basic combat mechanics which can feel stiff and the soft lock on mechanic can cause troubles when attempting to target something else than the game expects you to.- The constant asset loading between rooms can sometimes cause major stutteringWith an interesting story, to-the-point puzzles and, although basic but functional combat, this game have have shown that the franchise have the chops to be a modern classic when it focuses on what made the original great.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept trying to play Alone in the dark from 1992 and it was a very tough game to get into. this remake however pulls you right in and its a worthwhile fun experience, especially if u like Lovecraftian stuff. the actor for Jim Hopper from stranger things adds an extra charm to the detective character and i've enjoyed every step of the way. most are saying the combat is bad but if u think about the old game compared to this and the resident evil remakes, this games combat is just fine, its unique and does not make you feel like a super hero that can just shoot the leg or arm and gg, it actually takes planning and use of the environmental objects and deciding to use ammo or the durability of your current melee weapon as you can run out of all those things and then you will have no way to fight back (but it doesn't often come to that). the story is a great retelling of the first game with allot more depth and character, the atmosphere of the game feels like an actual Lovecraft story where anything can happen. and the 2 characters seem to have very different playthroughs allowing replayability. any bugs the game has had are actively being taken care of as one i mentioned was fixed within the first patch. overall its a greatLovecraftian horror game that really improves upon the original.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with a video reviewStream Review of Alone in the Dark - a non-ideal project with a fascinating plot Alone in the Dark, a remake of the 1992 project, from Pieces Interactive and behind the publisher THQ Nordic, has reached the release. This mystical story will take players to a mental asylum, full of mysteries and secrets. Today we will tell you about how the game turned out and whether it is worth our readers' attention.Deserto InvestigationEmily Hartwood is agitated by the content of the letter from her uncle Jeremy Hartwood, so she hired a private detective Edward Carnby and together with him went to a mental institution. Upon arrival at the Deserto estate, the heroes discover that a man is missing, so they decide to conduct an independent investigation and uncover all the secrets of the place. It is obvious that not everything in the asylum is calm, so Emily and Edward will find themselves in the thick of things.The main roles in this adventure were played by Hollywood actors Jodie Comer ("The Last Duel", "Killing Eve") and David Harbour ("Very Strange Things", "Hellboy"), who not only successfully coped with the voicing of the characters, but gave them humanity and literally brought the characters to life with their voices.Graphics and optimization problemsAs we mentioned earlier, the developers did a good job of recreating the atmosphere of a mystical thriller. In addition to good work with light, they managed to recreate the house really "alive". There are many objects in the corridors, the rooms are filled with various things of the inhabitants, and the otherworldly dimension is often shrouded in fog.The graphics, unfortunately, are not very modern, but everywhere you can see a lot of details that enhance the immersion. Screenshots do not fully convey the picture, and players will have something to pick on. The musical accompaniment was typical for the genre: not intrusive, without memorable compositions, but with high-quality sound effects.There are also claims to the realization of some animations - it is noticeable that the developers did not have an unlimited budget, so they could not refine every aspect of the game to perfection. For example, the heroine is waving her hands in the air while climbing through a narrow doorway. There are enough such nuances, though they almost do not spoil the impression of the process.But the optimization will obviously upset gamers. On a PC with RTX 3060 in the first third of the game there are constantly sharp drops in frame rate. Most often they are connected with the launch of cut-scenes. It is likely that the developers will fix this problem in the nearest patches, but it can spoil the perception of the game. It was not possible to test the game on consoles, so the state of the project was evaluated only on a stationary "machine".Sometimes heroes can get stuck in some object and only successful dodging to the side will allow to get out of the "trap". There were some critical errors, for example, scene freezing or door opening error, so we recommend to save in manual mode sometimes.Alone in the Dark turned out to be an exciting and good game, but only without taking into account the optimization problems. Besides, a small timing of five-seven hours per hero will allow you to saturate yourself with the story and not get bored in the process. It justifies its not-so-high price tag and will definitely be a good adventure for players for a couple of evenings.Pros:An engaging plot with colorful characters;Gameplay in the best traditions of Resident Evil remakes;Thoughtful environment and entertaining puzzles.Cons:Optimization and bugs spoil the overall picture;Not the most perfect graphics.Final score: 7.5 out of 10Verdict: Alone in the Dark can't be called a masterpiece, but it's a very solid game that will definitely be able to find its audience. Especially well it reveals itself in terms of the plot. We recommend it for familiarization in between bigger projects.

_childDocuments_.review: An unfaithful "remake" that's steeped in mediocrity.I was a child when I first played the original Alone in the Dark, too young to actually beat it, but I loved the setting and the atmosphere. I'm not a huge die hard fan of the original to the point where I remember every detail, but I remember enough to even question if this release could even be called a remake.The only thing I can say that's the same is the setting, main character names and the overarching Cthulu-mythos story. However, the progression through the mansion itself, the enemies and scenarios are so completely different you can't really even say you're playing the same game.The original title was the prototype for what the survival horror genre would become: paced exploration in a maze-like mansion with various puzzles to solve and backtracking to be had. It was a short experience that didn't overstay its welcome. AitD 2024 is a strictly linear experience that drives you from one dull set-piece to another as an incredibly forgettable story is doled out over the course of 7 or so hours which ends up feeling way too long for what it offers.The atmosphere of the mansion is solid in the beginning, you see somewhat familiar locations from the original to tickle that nostalgia but within the first couple hours you realize that nothing actually happens in the mansion itself. All of the enemies are located in these "pocket dimensions" that you travel to through a talisman and often take place outside of the mansion itself. There are twisted versions of the mansion, but you know that while exploring the normal mansion itself you're always going to be safe. It completely kills all the atmosphere the game tries to set up. Also, the "exploration" and "adventuring" from the original is completely non-existent here: this is NOT a game with any exploration like the original and it's 100% linear. This is the most disappointing thing about it and the game doesn't do anything to hide the fact that it's a straight shot. "Puzzles" mostly come down to finding a key that's sitting in plain sight sometimes right next to the lock it needs to be used on. I can't count how many times I had to open a door or box I just found only to learn that the key is sitting in the same room, or just one room over. Some puzzles require you to figure out codes or match images but the game spoon feeds you all of the answers. There's nothing to solve when the answer is sitting right next to you in a conveniently placed note.The gameplay itself is awful, combat is a completely slog, there's about 5 or so enemy types and there's even a horrid stealth mechanic that you're better off never engaging with (seriously running from enemies is the best option). Unique one-off enemies like the original are gone. The game is more action than horror and none of that action is satisfying.The sound design and voice acting are really well done I have to admit, all pieces of text have some sort of VA that will read through it, however in order to listen to it you have to stay on the inventory menu and some of the notes are long so it totally kills the pacing. You're stuck on the pause menu either reading it yourself or listening to the VA. However, I will say that some of the direction for the VA is absolutely baffling, especially David Harbour, he sounds completely indifferent to anything happening the whole game completely phoning in much of the performance.I played through the game once and won't ever bother doing so again for different endings or seeing Emily's story, I read it isn't much different anyway so I have no interest.Lastly, I played this exclusively on an OLED Steam Deck and tried maxing out the FPS by dumping nearly every graphic setting trying to hit 90 fps and the game still struggled often. There were times were the Deck would choke down to 40fps depending on the environment.I wouldn't even buy this on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing both scenarios I decided I can recommend this game, just barely, with a lot of caveats.The good:- Puzzles are fun and I had no bugs or issues associated with them.- Environments look great. It's obvious that a lot of work went into them. I stopped to look around a lot and admire the attention to detail.- Two scenarios to play through.- Multiple endings.The bad:- The game lacks polish, which is evident in the following:   - Combat is the worst part. Once you learn how to kinda work around it, most enemies are fine. But one enemy in particular was quite frustrating and made the section they were in unfun. Every animation has a kind of wind-up - turning, running - and it feels awful. You can get stun locked in corners if enemies reach you (this happened to me during my FIRST encounter and it was immediately apparent the combat was more than just janky). The melee lacks impact. If you attack enemies too soon, seemingly before they finish their appearance animation (like coming up out of the ground), they will appear to take damage but actually won't, which caused me to waste a lot of ammo and I had to start waiting extra long to make sure they were "ready" to be killed (that unfun section I mentioned). Sometimes the cross hairs don't show up.   - I got stuck in collision a few times on objects along walls. Nothing game-breaking, just had to wiggle free. There was also a room that had collision remain in the middle of the room for an object that was no longer there.   - A couple graphical issues. Very bad lag when going to new areas or loading cutscenes. Bad graphical glitching during one particular part where an object that was appearing was flashing rapidly until its animation was done.   - It feels a bit short for full price. Wait for a sale.I hope the developers fix these issues in an otherwise fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark wasn't what I expected. _childDocuments_.review: It's not going to be for everyone, but I'm pretty sure this game was made for me specifically. If you enjoy lovecraft and survival horror and you know your video game history you already know this is a remake of a game from '92. THE VIBESWhile it's lacking a bit in polish, it's suitably spooky and mysterious and the sheer attention to detail in the environment makes me giggle like a doofus - there's subtle references to horror literature all over the place if you look. The sound  design is insanely well done and all the little directional noises make my brain feel itchy.THE GAMEPLAYIt reminds me of the spirit of the era the original is from - go from room to room trying to solve slightly convoluted puzzles with not too much assistance. Some people will find this boring, but I liked getting dunked on by lucasArts era point and click games and it feels very much like that.THE COMBATIt's clunky and slow, which is the exact kind of combat you want to have in a game like this - running and gunning is for action heroes and you're playing as a woman with no combat experience or an alcoholic P.I. who can just about aim down his iron sights.TL;DR if you like classic survival horror, enjoyed the new Resident Evil remakes, and also happen to love getting bullied by retro point and click adventure games, this one's a surefire win.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind that I've never played the original, so I was pretty much going... alone in the dark with this one. The voice acting was superb, the atmosphere was excellent, and I found the gameplay itself really nice and simple to follow. Loved the weapons you gained during the journey as well. They got me good with some of the jump scares as well, which made me feel like I was more on edge during my playthrough. The game isn't without its problems, though. Despite being out for a long time, I did still suffer some stuttering issues from time to time, but nothing game breaking. I also chose to play Edward because I wanted to play as David Harbour, however, when I began playing Emily on my New Game+ (great option btw!), I felt like her side of the story made SO much more sense from her perspective. Going in with Edward in the first playthrough was exceptionally confusing from his side of things, and I felt like his reactions were very underplayed when going back into the real world. With Emily, it just felt more natural coming from her, that I actually wish I'd played hers first and THEN Edward's (so if you're planning on playing through both stories--which I do think is a really good way to get the WHOLE story although it's also not something REQUIRED, then I definitely recommend playing Emily first and then Edward). Outside of that, I really enjoyed the game, and the 90's nostalgia feeling it brought with it when it comes to games like Resident Evil or Silent Hill. I got it on sale, was worth it and I recommend. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few short years ago, who would have thunk that in the year of 2024 we would see two remakes of survival horror classics, modern revivals of outdated classics that not only plays to the nostalgia factor of the original fans but also brings them to modern audiences with all the technical improvements that accompany a modern game. The 2024 remake of , which comes from Mikael Hedberg, responsible for  and , is an ambitious homage to the original classic that birthed the survival horror genre. It brings a well-loved story back but with a modern twist, updating the haunting setting of Derceto Manor and infusing it with fresh visuals, better sound design, and quality voice acting from a strong cast (that includes Jodie Comer and David Harbor) and a 3rd person over the shoulder camera that has become synonymous with these kind of games. However, while their is much to love in the game, it occasionally falls short of the high bar set by recent horror remakes such as this years incredible revival from Blooper Team of the  classic considered by most, myself included, to be the scariest game ever made.:The game's story, following either Edward Carnaby or Emily Hartwood as they investigate eerie occurrences in Derceto Manor, brings a nostalgic charm with an updated sense of dread. The setting is well-crafted, using shadows and lighting to play with tension, while subtle cues in the environment offer a true sense of a haunted mansion. The choice between two protagonists with different perspectives adds some replay value, though each storyline sometimes feels incomplete or somewhat lacking in depth and I would liked to see the developers give more of each character a different through-line to the end because a lot the game is the same for each protagonist you choose except for their backstories which play out throughout the course of the adventure but aren't nearly as compelling enough. The story itself feels like a classic horror tale with a few unique twists, but it doesn’t break new ground, which may leave genre veterans wanting more.:Visually,  looks good for the most part. The character models and the overall design of Derceto Manor look fantastic, with intricate details that convey the era’s dark, Gothic atmosphere. However, occasional frame rate drops and texture pop-ins disrupt immersion, particularly in areas where smooth graphics would have heightened the horror experience. Enemies are not nearly varied enough, though some designs seem less inspired, borrowing heavily from familiar horror tropes.:Combat, exploration and puzzle solving make up the core gameplay, and  largely sticks to its roots. Gunplay is straightforward but can feel very stiff at times, echoing the feel of older survival horror titles. Resource management remains essential, forcing players to weigh their options and conserve ammunition carefully, which adds tension to encounters. However, the controls, when in combat, do feel clunky (especially after coming off ), and the AI lacks the complexity that would add real suspense to fights. Some puzzles are cleverly designed, adding a break from combat, though others feel repetitive or are too simple for seasoned players.:The sound design is among the game’s best features. Ambient noises, creaking floorboards, and haunting sounds fill Derceto Manor, building an eerie atmosphere. The musical score shifts from subtly unsettling to intense during key moments, amplifying the tension.The 1920's jazzy soundtrack is also a joy to listen too when the game is not trying to scare you. The voice acting is commendable, with well-delivered performances by both leads that bring depth to the characters, though some dialogue feels a bit melodramatic and underwritten. :With two main character storylines and multiple endings,  2024 remake offers decent replay value, especially for those interested in unravelling the full story. While I had an absolute blast playing this game I am cognisant that newer players to the genre may find their impressions vastly different due to the games somewhat clunky and unwieldy combat mechanics. Some may even find the horror a little too predictable. For me it captures the classic horror vibe but without the polish of some of the better titles in the genre, so know what you are getting into before you purchase.: I found  (2024) to be a satisfying trip down memory lane for someone who experienced the original back in the nineties but that it lacks the polish and innovation that could have elevated it. It does justice to the original's eerie charm but doesn’t quite capture the groundbreaking quality it needs to stand out. For fans of classic survival horror and those looking for a solid atmospheric experience, this is a worthy addition, but don’t expect it to redefine the genre.

The game allows you to play as either Edward Carnby or Emily Hartwood, each offering a slightly different perspective on the story.Story: The narrative is engaging, following Edward and Emily as they investigate the mysterious disappearance of Emily’s uncle at Derceto Manor. The story is filled with supernatural elements and psychological horror, keeping you on edge throughout. The performances by David Harbour and Jodie Comer add depth to the characters, making the unfolding mystery even more compelling12.Technical Performance: While the game is generally well-polished, there are occasional bugs and glitches that can disrupt the experience. However, these issues are relatively minor and don’t significantly detract from the overall enjoyment of the game.Secrets and Hidden Loot: Exploration is highly rewarding in Alone in the Dark. Finding these secrets often requires keen observation and a bit of backtracking, but the rewards are worth the effort. The game’s world is rich with lore and hidden details that enhance the overall experience12.Final Thoughts: Alone in the Dark is a solid entry in the survival horror genre, offering a compelling story, atmospheric visuals, and rewarding exploration. While it has its flaws, the game’s strengths make it a worthwhile experience for fans of horror games. If you enjoy a good mystery and don’t mind a few scares along the way, Alone in the Dark is definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not sure what all the gripes are about. There’s some stutters here and there when entering a new location, but many games do this. It’s not immersion breaking by any means…it’s just there.Graphically the game is great. It’s a beautiful game to look at. Texture work is not CP2077, but it’s not trying to be. It’s more than acceptable. Facial details are good enough to where I can easily tell who the actors are. That’s all I could ask for.Level design is well done. One of the little things I noticed is that items like radios are actually plugged in. They’re not just sitting randomly in places. You can tell placement of objects was a focus.Lighting is beautiful too. No, it’s likely not RTGI, but there’s plenty of games that have that. This game doesn’t, and it doesn’t need it. What it does use is perfect.Voice acting is top notch. They paid for talent, and they got it. Nothing, so far, has seemed “phoned in” like Danny Trejo in Far Cry 6...my GOD!Speaking of voices…they have notes…but you don’t have to read them. There’s voice acting for those too!! My biggest pet peeves in story driven games, is when the lore and story is pushed upon you with notes you have to read. I’m sorry, but I’m playing a GAME. Why on earth would I want to be reading a book? Lol.So far I’m loving the game and I look forward to digging into it some more. Don’t worry about the naysayers. Right now, it’s just cool to hate the game. It’s not perfect, but  none are.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:  * Interesting story that sucks you in    and drives you to keep playing in    order to find out more* Great atmosphere - I didn't find it    scary but it evoked a feeling of    suspense and dread in terms of    things that have and can go wrong* Thought provoking puzzles* Solid voice acting from the cast* Scarce ammo* Great exploration- just like in the   First Resident Evil mansion* Somewhat reminiscent of Silent Hill   with dream/memory sequences* Cool Lovecraft Outer God reference:   The Thousand Young* Fully voiced journal entries that are   read to you with the sound of a type   writer - very 1930s Noire    AtmosphereNegatives:* No gun/character upgrades    (probably due to limited budget)* combat was ok but could have used    more engaging mechanics.* Monsters not too difficult but they    do quickly sneak up on you and    corner if you if you aren't careful.* Game stutters and freezes a little    during cutscenes (this may be    dependent on your hardware).  The   devs will probably fix this. Verdict:  It's the best Alone in the Dark game I've played.  It's worth picking up if you're a fan of survival horror.  Don't miss out and get this game now.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:-Fantastic atmosphere, music, and voice acting!-Many fun references and Easter eggs to the original AITD game and some Lovecraft lore-Puzzles are pretty fun and unique to the game, although a lot of them are fetch quests and keys-Fun gameplay and replayability!-Perfect for fans of AITD, detective noir and pulp stories, and Lovecraftian cosmic horror!The Not-So-Great / Room For Improvement:-Both characters have almost the exact same path to follow in the story save for a small section in Chapter 4 where each of them has a unique plot point. Carnby and Emily are completely different characters with different reasons for being in Derceto and I feel like their paths should've been more personalized, but perhaps this was due to time constraints or budgeting. -There's one default ending for both characters and the only difference is some dialogue. To get all the other endings, the player has to find and complete certain sets of collectibles and sometimes has to perform certain actions in the game AND in actual cutscenes - all of which requires having to do research to even know what needs to be done to achieve these endings; which spoils the surprise. I kind of wish that there were options in the game where players could choose what happens either through dialogue or opening secret doors/performing arcane rituals; this would keep the element of surprise while also adding more replay value for players!-There's a feeling that I'm on a tight track and can't explore very much, I mostly go from A to B.-All of the background characters have wasted potential; they've got such interesting designs and personalities and it was a disappointment that I couldn't interact with them more. Especially Baptiste, Lottie, Ruth, and MacCarfey; they had great potential for being partners. But I suppose the developers wanted to maintain the feeling of suspicion and isolation. -The game is a bit laggy, sometimes movement stutters to a pause and I worry it could cause a crash but thankfully it hasn't ever crashed on me. But I always make a point to save, just in case.++++I remember playing the original AITD back in the early 90s, it's very near and dear to me since I have a lot of memories associated with the game and the blocky 3D graphics, the eerie soundtrack, and the haunted house with so much history and intrigue. The puzzles, the death traps, the zombies and the mole/bear-monster things that could be karate kicked more efficiently than using the rifle with limited ammo...There are many horror games, but THAT game could stand on its own!Granted, these days it is considered very dated and the controls were clunky and hard to use; but it set the tone.I never imagined that it could receive the remake treatment after nearly 32 years, so of course I had to buy it and see how it was reincarnated using modern tech and gameplay standards. I may be biased, because I loved the original Alone In The Dark so much and this newer version is very ambitious, but I really enjoyed playing this game and I've replayed it to experience every single ending - at least five times. Oddly, the game never really got old for me, I do have some parts that I favor more than others, but it's a strangely dark cozy game if that makes sense. I also improved and got faster playing through each time as I started to memorize some of the puzzles and got a better sense of direction. So, this game does reward you for repeated visits. AITD here ticked so many boxes for me; it has a classic detective noir feel to it, with hints of pulp fiction, actual exploration in the Louisiana bayou, The French Quarter, and more! It also has a more tasteful interpretation of a mental hospital/retreat without shaming mental health or traumatizing the player, that's an added bonus. It does have some elements of horror, but it's more of a dread type of horror instead of scares, without actual jumpscares I'm also pleased to report. Another aspect I really enjoyed about the game is the use of a talisman to travel to other locations, it is probably the most authentic and magical feeling of being transported in a Lovecraftian setting I've seen so far!As for action in the game, I'm happy that the developers were able to find a good balance so that it retains that survival horror-like feel without it being an actual shooter type of game. The original game didn't have an emphasis on fighting, it was always about playing it smart and figuring out how to avoid or outrun enemies or disable traps, which might disappoint some action fans. But, hey, you get a cool Tommy Gun!I could go on about the game but I think I've left enough here to give players an idea of what to expect; I don't want to spoil any of the fun surprises!Alone In The Dark is a pretty good game, not perfect, but certainly NOT regrettable! If you're unsure, you can always wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: POST-COMPLETION REVIEW UPDATE: Yeah, I ABSOLUTELY recommend this game. At about 10 hours for Edward's campaign, I didn't feel that it ever overstayed its welcome once. I took my time looking for all of the collectibles in Edward's run, so I feel I will most likely spend about the same time with Emily's. The ending isn't anything that I saw coming at all and was a great climax to what I felt was already a very enjoyable experience. To add on the my original review, if you enjoy Lovecraftian horror, the classic Resident Evil trilogy and Alone in the Dark remake from the early 2000s, you definitely need to play this. I give it an 8.5/10!Probably about 4ish hours in so far and I highly recommend. I don't agree with many of the criticisms about the game other than occasional performance hiccups, personally. I think trying to compare this to a huge title like RE2 Remake or RE4 Remake is doing the game and yourself a disservice. This is a slow-burn horror set in an early-1900s, southern gothic Louisiana setting. It's much more akin to the original remake of Alone in the Dark than it is the remakes of RE2 and RE4. It has a ton of atmosphere, great music, a fever dream story, and has some genuinely tense interactions. The combat isn't horrible, however, I don't think this game's intention is to focus on flashy combat, but to focus on the looming dread in the silence between fighting whatever monster is about to attack Edward or Emily as to make you antsy to shoot or beat it to death as fast as possible before it kills you. If you like the original Resident Evil trilogy and Alone in the Dark titles, I HIGHLY recommend buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I want to say that I think Alone in the Dark was a tough choice of a game to remake. The original AitD is built upon a very cliched concept: it's basically just a straightforward story about a haunted house. It's remembered for being innovative at the time, and for having some pretty memorable puzzles (it was much more of an adventure game, than an action one, after all), but looking at it from 2024, when we've been having a great horror renaissance for a few years now, it's just not that special. Later installments (like AitD2, 3 and eventually The New Nightmare) mostly were just trying to throw more cliches at AitD core to see what sticks (ghost pirates, Weird West, generic curses/witches/talismans, etc.).How do you remake something so basic? Well, I like to say it's not about the core idea, it's about execution. They could've played it straight and just make a horror game about a haunted house, and then try to elevate it with memorable monster designs, good scares, high production quality and, most importantly, doing . Because the main draw of the original AitD games was, really, how they were doing new weird things, offering unique challenges, how there was never a point where you could say "all right, I've figured this game out, I know what to expect now." This is not how things went.Alone in the Dark 2024 offers a pretty basic story about a haunted mental asylum and about madness, with a bit of a Lovecraftian theme. Unfortunately, there's very little depth or elegance to its narrative or presentation. Yes, the game is pretty, and I do like the new Derceto, but ironically, that's not where you spend most of the time. Most of the time you'll be walking through a series of mysterious locations created by the wild imagination of a madman. Well, that doesn't sound too bad, does it? Unfortunately, if upon hearing "imaginary horror worlds" you're expecting a lot of trippy visuals, shifting architecture and mind-bending surprises, you'll likely be disappointed. Instead, you'll travel through a bunch of fairly realistic places, occasionally populated with one of 4 possible enemy variants. It's not  per se, but there's also almost nothing surprising happening.The voice acting is great, and the noire tone permeating dialogue and cutscenes is very well doen and kind of captivating, though, but the story grows more and more confusing as it progresses—and I don't mean "confusing" as in "the protagonist is going mad and you don't know what is real and what isn't", I mean confusing as in "messy and haphazard."The combat is very much "we have Resident Evil at home" (which is ironic, considering the original AitD invented most things that RE1 was). It tries to follow in the steps of the recent RE remakes, but suffers from being extremely basic and a bit clunky on top. All encounters are just "run, point and shoot", with enemies that don't really require any unique tactics (and like I said, there are like only 4 variants). There's awkward stealth (that the in-game tutorial keeps reminding you about), that is very slow and almost never valid. There's also some run-of-the-mill melee combat with quickly deteriorating weapons, and also a lot of throwing things a-la The Last of Us—but  you can't carry the throwables on your person, instead having to throw them immediately upon pickup, which means almost every location in the game is mysteriously littered with rocks and molotovs.There's also a dodge button that I only found out about in the last couple of hours, by checking the controls—the in-game tutorials either don't mention it at all, or do it maybe once (despite always reminding me about sneaking). On top of this all, the movement doesn't feel particularly responsive, and the character can rather easily get stuck or stunlocked by enemies.Oh, and the final boss is basically .Finally, one of the biggest sins of the new Alone in the Dark is that it's just not scary. And yeah, maybe I'm not easily scared by games, but there are plenty that make me nervous or uncomfortable. To be truly scary a game has to surprise you and subvert your expectations, and this just never happens in AitD.Alone in the Dark 2024 is not a terrible game. It's pretty, it tries to do its own things, it feels like a labor of love, it features a lot of references to the older titles. But I cannot in good faith recommend it when we have games like Alisa , SIGNALIS , You Will Die Here Tonight  and many others that, while smaller in scale and budget, just  it.

_childDocuments_.review: The grandfather of all survival horrors is back! It's a bit of a bumpy ride in parts, but it's strengths certainly outweigh the flaws.+ A triumphant return to the setting, feel and themes and of the original game+ Interesting characters and witty writing+ Intriguing story with enough twists and turns to make you want to keep playing+ Fantastic soundtrack and sound design+ Beautiful visuals and varied environments+ Memorable setpiece moments+ A lot of care put in the optional narrative content. Instead of having to read you can have the game read the notes to you n the voices of the characters  - a huge for the visual impaired and something more games should do.- Several puzzles re-use the same mechanics, which becomes repetitive down the line- The item puzzles are very easy- No matter which lead character you choose the campaign is largely the same- The combat lacks depth and strategic options- The scares become predictableDespite all it's shortcomings I think it's definitely a title worth playing. It doesn't revolutionize the survival horror genre, but it doesn't have to. I thoroughly enjoyed the story, setting, the quirky characters and the wonderful soundtrack - so much that I was compelled to finish the game in one sitting - something that I very rarely find myself doing.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the originals but had heard of the games.What caught my attention with this game was an article in the news paper about Jody Comer and David Harbour playing as the main characters.I'm glad this appeared on my radar as its an incredibly well crafted horror game that tips its hat more than once to games from the 90s yet feels incredibly modern in its presentation.Visually the game looks amazing. The characters are a little stiff in their facial performance (but that is most games - it's just something you notice far more here because you are familiar with the actors likeness). The environments are so detailed and so well crafted. It feels very polished in that regard. The sound design is also incredible. Sound in this game adds a rich texture to every environment. You open an old iron gate and you can hear the springs clicking in the lock, or floorboards creek convincingly as you walk through an old house. It's something that really stood out to me in how much attention to detail there was and this combined with the fantastic visuals make this game incredibly immersive and incredibly eerie. It's not a jump scare game (although there are certainly a few moments). More of a slow psychological horror. I found myself just feeling a great sense of dread the deeper i got into the game. I love the backdrop of New Orleans and the time period this is set in. The actors performances are fantastic. The game mechanics revolve around you solviing investigations while exploring areas.The combat has been criticised but as you get into the game you realise it's absolutey fine. You have guns. You can pick up mele weapons that have limited durability. You can dodge. Then there are objects around the level that you can throw but can't carry around easily. This certainly feels a bit awquard until you are used to it - but essntially it means you need to keey your eyes peeled and take note of where these items are. Then when you encouter enemies you can run to one of these items and throw it at the enemy. Since the molotov sets them on fire it becomes an essential tactic. Once you understand it the initial jankiness turns into more of a strategy. I kind of like it. Especially as you get further on int the game and have encounters of multiple enemies at once.You can tell a huge amount of love and effort went into producing this title. For me it's an instant classic. Something i'll go back and replay a few months down the road. There are two main characters and you can do a playthrough with each that offer some differences to the narrative and dialogue.This isn't resident evil and nor is it trying to be. It's something else. Something more approachable and casual. I hope that the developers get a chance to flesh out their ideas and put out a sequel with expanded content and story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is why reviews ♥♥♥♥ out by main stream "game journalists" are not to be taken serious or of useful in any capacity. About 5 hours into the game so far and it is great (as far as I know, the game split into 2 scenarios and each scenario is 7~8 hours in length). Not a masterpiece but something memorable for sure. Not AAA quality but it doesn't feel cheap, definitely a solid AA experience. You can see the effort that the developers put into this game. Atmosphere is creepy. Ambience SFX and creepy BGM are great. The tense BGM everytime you have to sneak past enemies or something is happening or about to happen is just awesome and makes you nervous.The story is very interesting, with lots of voice-acted story notes to pick up. Everyone is doing a great job playing their characters. The pacing is great and it just hooks you into the story of a dark, mysterious and creepy paranormal mansion.Puzzles are not easy but not holding your hand either. They're interesting and do give you a challenge that makes you think before you solve.For a full old school style survival horror, I suggest playing it on the highest difficulty with old school style option (less environmental clues) where the game shines the most. I'm having a great time so far, a very solid AA game.What can make you dislike this game:+Movement & combat: -This game has an old style of survival horror combat feel to it, like 90s and early 2000s. It felt like I was back as a middle school kid playing RE code veronica. -The movement of the character feels pretty heavy like a real human with weigh. When you turn around in modern AAA games, your character is very snappy, like, doing a 180 quick turn and just run. In this game, when you turn, there is a short period of turn animation, plus heavy body moving sfx, so you can feel your character being sluggish. And when you run, your character doesn't burst into a sprint either, they slowly speed up into a run like real human. Many will call this "janky" but I think it's just design choice. I don't hate it but if you're too used to super soldier characters in modern FPS or stuff like RE4 Leon, it may put you off in this game+Game performance:-As of writing this, the game is pretty demanding in the VRAM department. If you have GPUs below 12 GB of VRAM, you will experience fps drop in some scenes. I didn't have fps drop in combat so it's not really a problem. When I don't have fps drop, my frame rate is pretty high and the fps drop episodes are also short (1-2 sec)-There is also something wrong with frame pacing. It doesn't feel smooth even  though my fps is 120. Lower the mouse sensitivity and aim sensitivity really help but there is definitely something weird going on+PricingThis game is great but not $54 great. It has good quality but still at AA level. So if you're buying this full price, you may feel like it's not worth it for the content it offered. This game is about $30~$40 top.

_childDocuments_.review: While being a fairly short game and pretty middling, even mediocre on certain fronts and the price of admission is a fair bit higher than it ought to be for a majority of people. Alone in the Dark is filled with a ton of spirit and passion for the Survival Horror genre and the original game of the same name. It's definitely worth a trip as a survival horror fan but people who aren't as into the genre or setting are not going to find it worth the price point.The story is best left hands off in this review, i will say that it is absolutely critical to the experience. It's a fun little horror story heavily invested into lovecraftian mythology. If you enjoy that sort of thing, it's definitely something you'll have a good time with. The voice acting is pretty solid across the board but rarely you'll find a few blemishes. The main duo of David Harbour as Detective Edward Carnby and Jodie Comer as Emily Hartwood are pretty solid. David in particular feels perfectly cast for a role like this. However what really shines is the setting. Decerto is a really cool place to actually explore and take in the atmosphere, it really does a lot of the heavy lifting of the story at times. It sets itself apart pretty solidly from similar romps into the time period and really adds to the Film Noir sort of vibe it's going for. If you like a sorta Supernatural Horror LA Noir vibe, you'll enjoy it. The game isn't strictly stuck in Decerto and there are some cool places you get to explore that definitely add to a few elements i've talked about before. The music is great as well. I can't get into other specifics without spoiling certain story elements but the game does a really solid job of keeping a mystery going, it just needed the rest of it to be better.This is where i gotta stop with the outstanding praise. I want to emphasis that i like this game, it's got a lot of heart but it doesn't redeem it's flaws. Outside of blemishes that i will talk about shortly, the game is trying to leaning into it being a Survival Horror game of old as opposed to new. If that's intentional or not, i don't know. I played on Hard without Hints. You die really really fast and your weapon aiming isn't consistent, melee combat feels sluggish at times if you don't take care of yourself, at first i thought this was intentional similar to games like Silent Hill or Call of Cthulhu. This isn't the case. The game breaks pretty heavily with excessive use of the dodge button, the iframes you have on the dodge are just too many. Melee Combat at the start feels very desperate but you will barely use it by the end of the game because your arsenal expands to the point that you never truly run out of ammo like you do early on in the game. The game does a good job of at least giving you SOMETHING to work with if you really are swimming without a paddle but this runs counter to Survival Horror as a genre. Ammo should be valued and it is for the most part at the start but by the end, it's just too much. It makes everything much too easy. Alone in the Dark is a very easy game but in equal measures comfy. It's like sitting down in your bed and reading dracula but lacks that gameplay tension that it's inspiration draws from. The original Alone in the Dark was absolutely brutal in it's gameplay and wasn't afraid to kill you on the slightest mistake, it makes sense why it really did work back then. Puzzles. The game has a fair amount of them and without hints they do indeed sometimes lend a cerebral challenge or require investigating what clues you do have but there are just as many that are fairly brainless. Decerto itself feels like a place that gets more and more closed off as you continue on through it's halls, it feels less and less focused as you go on which is a pretty huge detriment. Finally, the playtime. You will all likelihood, beat this in under 9 hours on a first playthrough. There are secrets and story shift to encourage replays on both characters but it's just too little compared to games that do this much better.It's a lack of consistency i have issue with. It doesn't feel consistently challenging the whole way through and gets easier as you go to the point that it completely deflates the tension the game is going for as a horror and then ramps back up with the climax almost to a jarring 0 to 60 in 30 seconds sort of way. It definitely has it's moments, it definitely has parts where it shines but ultimately it makes Alone in the Dark a very mediocre game with regularly glimpses of true promise. I can't recommend this game for most people at this price point unless you're an absolutely diehard survival horror fan, love Alone in the Dark or really want a fun lovecraft story to play through. In that case, it's a recommendation. I wish i had a mixed recommendation option. However if this price was eventually discounted at say £20 to 25. I could absolutely recommend it for even lukewarm fans but the price point is just too damn high.

A REALLY disappointing entry to the Alone in the Dark series. I know developers like watering down horror games to appeal to more people but this has been watered down so far as to completely remove it. Its not a horrible game by any means but when using the 'Alone in the Dark name' you expect scares and plenty of atmosphere and this game has neither. _childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. If I could, I would give it neither a yes nor a no because it is pretty much just mid.The game runs bad even on a good pc.There are lags, items refuse to be picked up and you get stuck on stuff easily after an enemy hits you.The worst or best thing about the bugs are the enemies who either see you a mile away or don’t see you even if you stand right in front of them.Also there are soundbugs after killing an enemy which results in them playing their dying sound over and over again…The puzzles are always the same. Either do a puzzle after finding the missing pieces, find a code for a safe on the other end of the map and run through the map again without anything good happening for a long while.I started singing sea shanties while doing my laps like a good errand boy to make the experience more fun.The story was confusing and the interactions between the playable characters gave me a headache.Especially the way they try to tell the story through articles and documents which seem endless. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I loved it, as an old fan.I've played Alone in the Dark 1 fairly regularly since I first got the demo around 1992-1993 from a dial-up BBS. The last time I played it was a few months ago. I never had much interest in any of its sequels - instead, I always wanted the Virtual Dreams series it was meant to be a part of. Yes, instead of the Edward show, we were going to have a variety of new adventures, settings, and characters. Along those lines I think I'm one of the few people who always saw Emily as the protagonist and read the intro text. Edward was a snake who called himself "the reptile." Seriously, he was just there to loot Emily's uncle's place.That we've gotten a reboot where again Emily is a focus and hers is the story that's the strongest? Oh boy, thank you, that's really more genuine to the original than I ever expected. All the details reworked in new ways was a real joy too, from the dark man to the Astarte to even the spiral dagger. And what they did with the tree, A+, that was awesome. This is making me wonder again where Frédérick Raynal would have taken it, had he kept control. I loved hearing from him in the director's audio!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Alone in the Dark (1992) and there's a few things in common, and quite a few that are different. Same protagonists and setting, while the story and mechanics are quite different.THE BAD:- Combat is pretty frustrating and not really fluid because of mouse acceleration.- You can't remap the Z and Y keys to go left or right in puzzles (for QWERTZ keyboards).- It's difficult to explore everyhing and solve all the puzzles, as sometimes you just get into a cutscene and can't go back, by just opening a door for instance.- The performance of the game is pretty bad on PC. You can tell tis unoptimized, as you get huge frame drops in certain areas, and then its back up again and no problem.THE MEH:- The survival aspect is pretty basic with just health items and ammo to manage, and there is no inventory screen to manage. It's not good or bad, its just very basic.THE GOOD:- The story itself is interesting and fun to explore- Voice acting is also pretty good from most characters you meet (and there's quite a few)- There's some similarities or "nods" to the 1992 title, which are nice if you know the original gameThe game was about 10 hours long for me and overall a pretty good experience. _childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that my experience with the original Alone In The Dark is minimal, so I can't compare this remake to the original. The game has some performance issues in the form of stuttering when loading new areas. I played it on both windows 10 and linux. On windows 10, the stutters were noticeably worse.You play as either Edward Carnby or Emily Hartford and you goal is to find her uncle Jeremy who's in Derceto, a sort of upscale mental institution. The game follows Capcom and Konami's shift into the third person, over the shoulder perspective over the classic tank controls. This game can be divided into two parts that you will switch between. Exploring Derceto gives you the more open, survival horror experience of looking for keys and other items to progress. While in Derceto you will experience little to no combat. Periodically, you will enter a kind of Silent Hill "other world" that is linear and you will encounter monsters. I find this to have a pretty good pace. Exploring Derceto is the most fun, in my opinion, and the "other world" segments don't overstay their welcome so there's a good balance of both. There's no inventory management, however your resources are capped. You can only carry a certain amount of healing items and ammo for each weapon.Now I'll go through some problems. This game has a fair amount of jank. While sprinting, I frequently got stuck on furniture and other items decorating the environments. Sometimes I was able to use the dodge feature to get myself unstuck, and other times I had to reload my save. I experienced a bug with audio glitching and crackling after the game's first update that was solved by loading an earlier save which luckily wasn't very far from my last one. Combat is hit or miss. You have an array of weapons including fire arms and melee weapons. The latter are found frequently as they break after a few hits. There are throwable items like bricks and molotav cocktails. You hold Q to pick them up and aim, otherwise they get thrown instantly. This is a problem as enemies are fairly fast and it's cumbersome to have to slowly turn yourself around to throw things. This is exacerbated by the fact that there is no quick turn. The enemies themselves are very bland and samey. There are four kinds. The first two are humanoid and they're fought the same way and act similarly. The third is a weak, but annoying flying type. The last and worst is a small spider looking thing that takes WAY too much ammo to kill and deal a ton of damage. Finally, the final boss of the game is frustrating. I should mention that I played on hard mode, so this may not be a problem in lower difficulties. The boss is large and it's second phase is inside a decent sized room. It periodically spawns far too many enemies. If you can't kill them quickly, they'll overwhelm you and you will get cornered. Occasionally the boss gets too close and will not allow you to see anything around you.In conclusion, it's an enjoyable game but it's not without its quirks and frustrations. I would recommend it to any fans of survival horror

I cannot emphasize enough how much all elements fit into a perfect picture. I only wish the two stories completed each other instead of being mostly separate experiences. Even after overwriting my save, I STILL cannot access the locked doors because they key I am supposed to have, has vanished again and won't unlock any doors. In order to get this again, I have to start over entirely and "follow this walk through, step by step" per the game devs. Instead of fixing their game, and one of the most recurring issues this game has seen, we're told to pull up a walk through and follow it step by step to ensure we are doing exactly what they intended we do--meanwhile, the actual prompts from the game don't give any information regarding this and do nothing to guide players to ensure it doesn't happen.I do NOT recommend this unless you genuinely plan to have a walk through up and running for your entire save to ensure you do not accidentally grab an item that was available to grab in chapters 1-2, but you're not supposed to grab until Chapters 3-4 in a specific order, so you don't end up soft locked and having to restart. _childDocuments_.review: This game was given to me as a gift for my Birthday, and frankly - Can't say enough good things about it. Like it so much that I am making a review now just to make sure others see it and give it a shot. SO ! Here is a short Pro and Con list.  Pros:The game FEELS like it should. While the 3rd person movement is not near as clunky as the original Alone in the Dark, there is a small level of jank that makes absolute sense. It belongs and it is not punishing, at least not at the start.The Voice acting with the notes and characters are well done ( minus a minor gripe...Looking at you Hartwood! ) . While its huge and different from the original, it stands on its own as what Alone in the Dark should be. The story driven atmosphere is even more so amazing now as it was years ago. As someone who normally just skims the side lore and goes on his way, I found myself putting down the controller and letting the notes be read to me in cinematic flare. Its not Alone in the Dark A New Nightmare or the crap movie that was made as a cash grab / tax breakThe Music - I could gush on that opening menu theme forever. The games sound and everything just push and pull everything where it needs to be. And when you find a certain tree at the start of the game that beaters of the original game KNOW what the heck it is? The sounds around that are. fuggin. amazing.The Cons:Granted, I am just a 1 hour and change into the game but I can gripe about a few things.The Spirit of the Original game is here but is lost ever so slightly. While the original game had its fixed items in fixed spots and a whole house to explore, it is replaced with random loot locations for ammo and booze ( or nothing at all )  and with some new locations you travel between that will allow you access to other rooms and key items to help you explore the main house. Its a little odd but its minor in the grand scheme of thingsThe character selection intros. Hearing a small quip about the characters ( i say small but it was like a 2 min long voiced dialog the characters voiced themselves )  when I was making my choices just made us understand the characters a little bit more.  Another minor gripe though!Emily Hartwood has no southern drawl! Big ooofsters! In the original game with her intro you could hear that southerner twang, but now she lacks that and since they do a lot more talking this time around I already miss what it could have been. But again, another tiny gripe. Sound Volume: At times when i find an item and your character says something ( In my case Carnby ) its like he is a mile away talking to you, I am unsure if me turning down the master volume did this , but still everything else is at a decent volume and my sound settings are untouched other than the master volume so things should balance out but it seems the speech is just that much quieter.  Final Minor Gripe though!So far, all my cons are just water under the bridge. I havn't had huge frame drops on Epic settings and my PC is far from top of the line, and it runs smooth like buttah! Did you play the original game? Did you see / play the horrible AitD games and wished you could go back to the simpler times? This is as close as you can get with out some emulation friends and I can not recommend this game enough!Edit: 8 Hours in, and I have changed my mind, I love the new way the game plays rather than being only in the mansion. The Story so far is great!

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark 2024 is a thrilling return to the classic survival horror genre that delivers an unforgettable experience. From the moment I started playing, I was captivated by its perfect blend of spookiness, challenging puzzles, and compelling storytelling.The atmosphere is incredible, with eerie environments and a haunting soundtrack that kept me on edge throughout the game. The developers have masterfully crafted a world that feels both menacing and immersive, making every shadow and sound a potential threat.The puzzles are well-designed, offering just the right amount of challenge without becoming frustrating. Each puzzle felt like a natural part of the story, enhancing the overall experience rather than detracting from it. The balance between exploration, puzzle-solving and combat kept the gameplay engaging and varied.Story-wise, Alone in the Dark 2024 holds a gripping narrative that unfolds in unexpected ways and shocked me a few times. The characters are well-developed, and their personal stories add depth to the main plot. The game's pacing is excellent, keeping me hooked from start to finish.Overall, Alone in the Dark 2024 is a must-play for fans of the genre. It successfully combines elements of horror, mystery, and adventure into a cohesive and enjoyable experience. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or a newcomer, this game is sure to provide hours of spine-tingling entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in The Dark (2024) is a game destined for cult status. It's design is old school, it's rough around the edges but has had clear loved poured into it by a passionate team.Let's go over some important con's:.It's combat is extremely simple, at times I wished that there were just more enemies to feel like a threat..It's pretty jank at times, while I didn't encounter any stuttering or crashes on both my playthroughs, my character got caught on scenery about six times total. Most of the time a few dodges forced me out but most of the time it was a reload..The price point, it's a very pricey game for what it is. Your millage my vary but I'd suggest waiting for a discount.Now with those out of the way, I can now explain why this game has wormed it's way into my brain like the voices of an old god..The atmosphere of both Derecto and the many unique locations you'll explore are second to none, complemented by a fantastic score. Doom Jazz needs to become it's own genre at this point!.Jodie Comer, David Harbor and the rest of the cast put in great performances, but special praise I feel should be given to Jodie Comer playing such a traumatised and broken character in Emily. Her story goes to some dark places that really affected me.The plot goes deep, if your ready to scour the game for documents and clues (each read by the writer), you'll build up a tangled web of lovecraftian horror beneath the surface of this detective story.I'm so happy with this game, with a bit more polish from a clearly talented team, I'm sure we'll see more people enjoying what is a labor of love and reverence for the 1992 original.

And here's why ... monsters appear at unfait places pop up through solid brick walls or one and a half inch right behind you (completely out of sight of course). You're not able to walk backwards and so getting some distance and aim at your opponents. Instead of this, your character turns and slowly sneaks - his back towards the monsters - away. Melee attacks are simply a pain in the ass as the characters spins and turns while hitting a monster and pretty soon, the latter is in your dead spot in your back. _childDocuments_.review: LOVELY SETTING VS DISAPPOINTING GAMEPLAYThe atmosphere, the setting, the music, and the characters, are well built and developed. I have to say that the action is very limited, and beside a few tense moments, the whole experience was a captivating but disappointingly quiet piece of cake. The puzzle parts were so easy that sometimes they could have been skipped; 90% of the puzzles have their solution right beside them, which really takes a lot out of the experience. The past title had more enigmatic parts, and to find the solution you often had to look around the whole place, sometimes unloking a door or a mechanism far ahead in the game. For instance, if you have to pull a broken lever and you are missing a part of the staff, it's very unnecessary to put the broken part right beside the machinery. You could have just let it whole, nonsense in being able to repair it with zero effort. Maybe you could add - I don't know - a kind of glue or some ropes and nails to piece it back together, having them scattered somewhere over a dangerous place, or in some hidden compartment. That's what it's missing so badly from the game.Fell off short in the finale as welll.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of classic survival horror games and can get this game at $30 or less, I think you'll enjoy your time with this game, but it's a very short, limited game with nearly no replay value. My first playthough took about 6 hours with exploration, and I spent another couple hours as the alternate character. I don't want to say much as to spoil the game, but the atmosphere/art design and lovecraftian elements are great, the mansion was well designed, there's a good variety of locations, and the combat has just enough to make it feel more modern while still retaining a clunky feeling(I mean this as a compliment).David Harbour is...fine, if a little flat at times, and if they could've gotten the game's production cost down and lowered the retail price by not hiring him, they should've done that. Once you beat the game, you do unlock a NG+ option(which was added as their last update), but otherwise there are NO unlocklables outside some collectibles that track between every playthrough. No new modes, weapons, costumes, upgrades, filters, anything. This is a HUGE letdown and practically kills this game's longevity. For many, this will be a one-and-done playthrough, as the second character, while having different dialogue and interactions with certain characters, is practically identical.Still, if you're a fan of the genre, and don't mind a journey back to simpler time, this is a well made game, for what it is. Just don't expect a lot of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing similar to the original is the name.  It's a totally different story, a very convoluted one.  The graphics are pretty nice (though VERY unoptimized), the sound quality is really good (quite uneven, some parts of the game/sound effects are arbitrarily louder or quieter than others).  Some of the puzzles have very bad logic and require you to think in a very obscure way.  The exploration is nice and interesting.  The map could have been awesome if they would have made your character in the map menu an arrow, instead of a dot so you could see which direction you're facing, therefore the map is terrible and confusing.Thank God the combat system is secondary, because it is ABYSMAL.  Absolutely God awful combat.  Clunky and awkward, and your character always feels "heavy" like you're trying to run in a pool, where the harder you try, the worse it gets.  Both the controller and M/KB sensitivities are weird and are either too sensitive or not sensitive enough, which makes combat that much more of a chore.  Headshots don't seem to be any different than body shots and picking up a throwable object renders your sensitivity so slow, that if you're not facing the enemy directly when you pick up a throwable, you've left yourself open to getting hit a bunch by the enemy.  You can't put down throwables either.  You either have to use them, or lose them.There is no inventory system, infinite resources, which makes the game lame and doesn't impose caution, or logical thinking, you can just "Rambo" everything and still be rewarded with plenty more ammo.The character models are quite bad, they look VERY dated.  Maybe they should have spent more resources on the game itself instead of the voice actors.  I would much rather have a game with great mechanics and bad voice acting rather than good voice acting with terrible game mechanics, and that's basically what this game is.  No more than a barely playable "Book on tape".

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is an interesting, if a bit shallow, survival horror experience that's missing some conventions of the genre. There's no crafting, no inventory management and the combat is very simplistic. If you're hoping for modern Resident Evil-like experience, you'll probably be disappointed because combat isn't really the focus here. There's a much greater emphasis on exploration and puzzle-solving. What AitD does really well is world-building and atmosphere. Exploring Derceto Manor and interacting with its eccentric inhabitants is a lot of fun and you'll visit a surprising number of locales through your playthrough(s). The story is engaging, if a bit confusing, and won't offer the kind of closure that some people want. However, that's pretty standard for Lovecraftian narratives so it's better to just enjoy the ride and not worry so much about the destination. Playing through as both Edward and Emily will provide more insight into the characters and lore, as each character has unique dialogue, cutscenes and a couple of exclusive levels.Overall, I enjoyed Alone in the Dark, though it almost feels like more of an adventure game than a survival horror game. That said, playing on the highest difficulty does provide a lot of tense moments, as resources are much more scarce and enemies much more dangerous. Either way, if you're into Lovecraft and enjoy creepy adventure games, AitD should be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: As a remake of a cult classic survival horror I feel this game is already in need of a remake. The graphics aren't terrible but they're nowhere near up to standard for current gen, I'd say the game looks as if it from 360/PS3 era if not slightly better. Animations are clunky at best with most gameplay mechanics. I imagine many minor problems that I experienced during my playthrough will be fixed with a patch soon, however this doesn't mean that the game is good, I've definitely played worse but I feel like this title deserves a lot more.Some of the puzzles are enjoyable to solve but many of them are very simple and just involve finding a key for a door and a few of the puzzles are extremely unnecessary like the item you require to solve a puzzle is literally next to the solution.Audio notes are a nice touch at first but grow old very quickly and listening to someone slowly read essays felt like a third of my playthrough. _childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a what I would call "Survival Horror Light".There is no item management, no need to conserve ammo or healing items and no need to avoid enemies (at least on Standard difficulty). But with its interesting setting and characters, great environments and awesome sound design Alone in the Dark is still a good game that never gets boring during the 7-8 hour playthrough. I encountered only very minor bugs and stuttering so in this regard I cant complain. Combat is slightly clunky but otherwise fine.My main issue with the game is that its too easy on Standard difficulty. The combat is no challenge and the puzzles are generally rather easy (and too similar), although a few of them are a bit more challenging. There is unfortunately no need to conserve ammo since as soon as you start wasting it, the game spawns ammo everywhere so you will never run out. As I already mentioned, its a "Survival Horror Light" experience , not really comparable to something like RE1 Remake or Tormented Souls. If you are looking for a challenge this is not your game.There is certainly room for improvement but overall I had a fun time during my stay at Derceto Manor and I hope there will be a DLC or even a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an Unreal Engine 4 and there is no shader pre-compilation step. So guess what? Shader compilation stutter, even on high-end hardware. It's minor, but it's all over the place. Considering all the release delays, considering that pretty much every other dev learned to add the pre-compilation step, it's just atrocious. The stutter is very typical: you get it when traversing and coming into a new scene, even if it's very light on graphical detail. You run around, you come back to the same place - no stutter, as the shaders are already compiled (on the fly, which is causing the stutter). You go into a new area - stutter again. I've went from highest to lowest settings, the stutter is there. My specs are way beyond the officially recommended ones, the same PC can run Avatar at 120 FPS and maximum settings. Smooth AF. Needless to say, Avatar looks much better in general.Furthermore, you can run the game at higher frame rates (say, 120), but real-time rendered cutscenes are locked to 60. Not ideal. There is stutter in the cutscenes, too. Not in all of them, but in some for sure.Oh, and here is another horror. It's possible to change keybindings, but they are limited, reflecting the number of buttons on a controller. So, you can switch weapons with 1, 2 and 3, but for the fourth weapon, you have to hold 1 instead of just using 4. Even if remapped, you have to hold the button. Same goes for opening a map: you can't have a separate map button, instead you have to hold the button that opens the "investigation" menu. So little effort went into this port.Just a bit of reminiscing. I've played the original Alone in the Dark in 1992. It was the best game I've ever played at that point. It looked amazing and boasted a game design that I haven't seen in any game before and not in many after. It was very Dark Souls by design: you were dropped in the middle of a horror, and there was not artificial guidance. The game was non-linear and you could finish it in several ways. The puzzles were clever and a lot of the things were missable, making the game fun to replay. I've played the same game many years later, and it still looked and played great, even though low-poly models started to look a bit funny. It was still an immersive and scary experience. The 2024 version is not a remake or a remaster, it's a very loose reimagining. It's also not even close to be as impressive as the 1992 game was back in the day. The design is very limited - you are often locked into a very linear path. Puzzles are a joke. Combat is clunky.Update: just a few hours after the release, there was a patch sized over 2 GB. Didn't fix any of the problems above. You know what it did? Locked away the paid DLC which accidentally slipped into the initial release.Alone in the Dark is priced at EUR 53.99, which includes a temporary release discount of 10% from the EUR 59.99 price. For this money you can get either a brand new better game, and a lot of them are being released around the same time - Dragon's Dogma 2, for example - or a bunch of better older games.OK, Horizon Forbidden West just came out. Priced at EUR 59.99. This game runs at all maximum settings at 4K and 120 FPS. No dips whatsoever. It looks photo-realistic. It's not the best game out there. I've played it on PS5 a while ago and got a bit bored, as I thought the writing too mediocre, but it's definitely the pretiest, that's why I bought it again, this time on PC. So, priced the same as Alone in the Dark, looks several times better, works significantly smoother, has a bigger world and more things to do...

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished the game.I really enjoyed it at the beginning, but the more I played, the less I liked it. Let me summarize my impressions, keeping in mind that the game has a AAA price tag of 59.99 Euros. I'll list everything important to me in a game, from top priority to least priority.Story -> 7/10.I can't say it's an exceptional story, but it's good enough. Honestly, it's the only thing that kept me engaged in the last two chapters. Otherwise, I would have dropped the game.Gameplay -> 5/10.Atmosphere & Characters -> 7/10.Technical State & Optimization -> 6/10.I didn’t encounter any bugs, but the controls and combat feel pretty clunky.With an RTX 4070M, 32GB of RAM, and an AMD 7745 8-core processor, I was averaging 40-50 FPS. Honestly, the graphics aren’t impressive. The locations are small, and the graphics are average. I don’t see any reason why the performance should be this poor.Level Design -> 4/10.Graphics -> 5/10.For a AAA game, the graphics are very average.My overall score would be 5.6/10.Unfortunately, I can’t recommend this game at its current price. It feels like a good indie game with a small budget, not a AAA title. Its real value is more in the range of 10-20 Euros.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to see what THQ could bring to the table after the disaster that was Inferno and Illumination, but I think it is safe to say the franchise is at this stage... cursed... or in need of a developer that has a larger budget.The game drops frames rapidly from one room to the next, even with DLSS on, it can drop anything from 30 to 60 fps, and cut-scenes can be a hot mess as it stands on launch. So optimisation is clearly an issue, at least for now, which I'm sure can be patched up in time. Running into my first combat encounter, I ended up trapped down the corridor and had to restart, which was quite annoying as I couldn't simply navigate around the enemy. It does feel like a few mechanics have been added since the initial release of the trailer, and they don't quite fit right, for example, running down the stairs. (you'll see what I mean) The game does look stunning, and it does remind me of a third person Resident Evil 7 set in the 20's, albeit this is essentially a remake of the original game. The sound design is quite nice, some parts reminded me of the early AITD games, and some tones in the music reminded me of the New Nightmare entry which is always a personal favourite. Sadly as it stands, I can't recommend this game with the issues from launch.
