_childDocuments_.review: Very mild recommend, the game is split up between exploration and combat zones without much overlap. The sudden transitions between these two can be cool, but overall the combat feels really bad, I'll go into why that is but if you're down for exploring the mansion with light puzzles and a story that has cool concepts with a weak execution, then go for it.I know it's Survival Horror and believe me, my expectations for combat were low, but oh man. The three ways of dealing damage were guns, which work ok despite some astoundingly bad collisions at times, melee, and environmental thrown objects. The melee involves getting close to the enemies and the poor hitboxes aren't exclusive to the gunplay, I would constantly get stuck on enemies or the terrain, exacerbated by the enemies pushing me. There isn't great feedback for a heavy or light hit (the difference is holding the attack button without a clear "fully charged" animation) and I got stunlocked by enemies more than a few times. For the environmental throwables, they're a cool idea that do appreciable damage, the incendiary ones especially, but are positioned oddly. Once you pick them up you're stuck in slow "throwing" state that can only be broken by throwing the object and thus breaking it. The notification for interacting with these is also really particular and there were many occasions where I could not get the prompt to show despite staring an object down. The enemies are also pretty bland, there's either dudes that are straight forward or bugs. The bugs later on have ridiculously high health and I was convinced it was a bug itself.I won't go too far into the story,  but it's psychological and takes a lot of literary inspiration that it doesn't really do much with. I played the Carnby campaign and his backstory really stood out as being a bland take on a predictable formula. The rest of the plot fares better, but has better ideas than execution. On paper, Silent Hill meets pulp horror sounds perfect, but outside of cool environments it doesn't add up to much. Voice acting is hit or miss, though normally the former. The lead 2 actors are a big exception, David Harbour sucks in this and he looks dopey, I didn't like playing as him.My favourite moments were like Song Of Horror lite, if that adventure game-style aspect appeals to you and you're ok appreciating a framework for what it attempted rather than what it amounted to then go for this game, probably on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than I expected. It has a pretty good grasp of survival horror. I expected something that would eventually devolve into a big dumb action game and so far it hasn't done that.There are a few negatives that I think anyone should be aware of.First, the combat is incredibad. I'm not upset that they don't let me blow the enemy away like I'm Rambo. I'm upset that you can't transfer momentum into enemies while moving. So it's not only possible, but common, to get trapped against a wall if you get hit once in a confined area. If things like this had just been re-contextualized (for instance the enemy grapples you or pins you to the wall) it would work really well with the fact that it's a horror game. But since it feels and looks unintentional, and all you can do is sit there and wait to get hit a few more times, it really undermines any dread that could come from those kinds of situations. It's not "Oh my god, if I get hit here I'm done for." it's "Oh my god, I missed. Just kill me already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."Secondly, some of the puzzles have very ?-pilled design. Without spoiling anything, there are some puzzles that take less time to brute force than it takes to find all the clues to get past them. Like maximum time to brute force of like 90 seconds. 6^3 combinations at a try rate of 3 per second is like ~70 seconds and that's if you have to try literally every possible combination. You can just cycle through them by flicking the dial without even paying attention so it's even possible to just get the answer accidentally without trying. There's no reason to look for the clues. That really doesn't feel intentional.Lastly, this is not a negative for me, but it may be for some people; This game is a goshdarn book. There are alot of documents to read and alot of them are very important. There are voice-overs for all of them if you don't feel like reading but there is like 20 pages of mandatory text in the first 1hr of the game. I like it. but I know that some people may hate it.All-in-all this is a good game. It's much better than I expected or hoped for.Looking forward to more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's talk about it.Pros:- Atmosphere is great- Puzzles are challenging and rewarding- Game looks beautiful- The story is.. very interesting. For sure keeps you playing- Obviously the live actors are awesomeCons:- I have a new gen gpu and this game still runs poorly. Very framey an stutters.- The frames and stutters on the boat level are almost game breaking- The monsters on the boat level phase through walls and can attack you- The controls for combat are pretty clunky. Best not use melee and keep things at a distance.- The controls in general are clunky and hard to get used to.- Price tag for game, considering all above listed issues- There are 3 or 4 total variations of enemiesOverall:This is fun. It is. If you love survival horror and are looking for another title this is exactly that. The atmosphere is cool and the live actors are great. The puzzles are  challenging with not too many clues. I fear, however, if you are not a die hard fan of survival horror, you will not be happy. The reason being, there is A LOT you have to overlook even though this is fun. The poor combat, clunky controls, and constant stuttering is almost too much to deal with. On one level in particular, it got me killed 3 times because enemies were floating and phasing through walls. This, coupled with the lack of variety of enemies, and the full $60 price tag? Would not recommend. The game functions like a $30 game. If this was the price, I would have had no issues. Helldivers 2 was $40, and even though in a completely different genre, the point remains. I cannot see how the price is justified for all the issues.

I still love it, still am hopeful the series continues from here, and will easily rate it 8/10.)

_childDocuments_.review: (mini-review).Alone in the Dark is a re-imagining of the venerable, 1992 cult horror game.  Set in the early 1940s, against an Art Nouveau, Call of Cthulhu-inspired backdrop, Alone in the Dark uses the threat of foreboding, cosmic cataclysm to generate much of its anxiety and dread.  The game has atmosphere, unsettling monsters, a unique visual style and two well-performed lead protagonists.  The graphics, are good, if albeit plain and the game, while stuttery at times, is, for the most part, stable.  Gun play is good, melee is a bit of a miss and the bosses/puzzles are a combination of both.  Interestingly eerie environments abound.That said, be aware that Carnby's play through covers everything you need to know about the title and Hartwood's own play through not only adds little in the way of new content but it is also filled with woke narratives that detract from the story. Ultimately, the game feels like a AA Resident Evil-inspired remake of a comparable survival horror IP and its 10 hour campaign is well-worth 15-20 dollars. To date, the developer Pieces, has has been shuttered by THQ Nordic.  Don't expect additional content or additional Alone in the Dark remakes any time soon.A nice, solid little diversion in the same vein as the Resident Evil and Silent Hill remakes.7.5/10.Buy on sale.

And the most important... this game has no HORROR inside, it doesn't have screamers, it doesn't have horrific monster design, it doesn't have feeling of the last medkit and last bullet in your weapon.The puzzles are stupid, the fights are stupid, I am stupid that was waiting it so much all this time. The dissapointment of the decade for me, and it can't be fixed with the patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I run a 3070ti with a trash CPU and at 1440p on High settings I've maintained close to 100 fps with minor frame hitching around new areas and cutscenes. Negative performance reviews are overblown. The game is quite polished, playable, enjoyable, graphically sound. The real thing that needs a patch will be object collision, as the player model has a tendency to get stuck on furniture, particularly in combat.Other than those issues, the writing is better than Resident Evil, frankly. This story is just more interesting. The voice acting is really good all around, the puzzles are great. It's shaping up to be short, sweet, and the extra gameplay filters and 8-bit graphical options were frankly worth the cost, I can't wait to replay the game in full 8-bit. In addition, the Southern Gothic charm shines through with an EXCELLENT soundtrack, campy noir, and a fun setting in Decerto Manor. It weaves a tight modern horror game with very obvious retro influences I really enjoy and which do set it apart from other modern action-horror titles.I would have liked more focus on hardcore survival horror, as it is definitely more of that creepy action game (think Alan Wake 2) than a more horror-influenced, Dead Space-esque experience, but I don't think the game loses much as a result.7/10, I personally find it worth the full price, but think if you can snag it in the $39.99 range you'll get the most bang for your buck and it'd justify the purchase outright.

_childDocuments_.review: The kind of survival horror jank you would come to expect in the likes of Deadly Premonition 1&2 or The Sinking City. If you haven't played either franchises, think Resident Evil 2 but Lovecraftian and with plenty more reading and just plain bad, but ultimately passable, combat. I chose Carnby for my first playthrough, which means I got David Harbour's okay performance, although that could be attributed to some lack of direction. Jodie Comer seemed to have put a bit more into it from the few scenes I came across with her.The game does seem to encourage you to replay it from the other character's perspective, as it supposedly gives you "the whole story", but since it might imply replaying and re-exploring a lot of sections, it might be for the best to let it simmer down a few days before going back. Will likely update the review once I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Die hard old school survivor fan here (silent hill, RE days).This remake is a mixed bag for me. There are better titles out there and I would not recommend it:Atmosphere is here, initially (in the mansion), but it soon becomes mundane and it no longer has any substance. It may seem like an open environment, but the game is very linear, forcing you to complete certain objectives in a certain order. Combat is terrible and clunky.The off-world chapters are boring: get from point A to point B, watch some cut scenes. Return to mansion.Puzzles are okay - most of them don't require item finding and just figuring something out on the spot. Wanted to finish the game, but I just could not get motivated to complete it even though I am 80% of the way through. Zero inventory management. Hardly any exploration. Game just drags on and gets repetitive as it progresses. Wait for a deep discount if you want to give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: first...the issues. its a bit buggy. i often found myself stuck on object geometry like cars, street carts etc. and unable to move which can only be fixed by death or reloading. Melee weapons often fail to switch and sometimes the game thinks you already have one when trying to pick one up, meaning you need to die, reload or progress to a cutscene to be able to pick another melee weapon up again. Hit registration is questionable at best...Some enemy animations are broken and can create a bit of unfair difficulty (mostly lookin' at you spider/water flea enemy...) Loading into new areas and returning to Derceto causes brief frame rate drops. And lastly, sometimes after reloading a save, items lose their interaction icons but can still be interacted with. this can usually also be fixed by reloading, dying or progressing to a cutscene.In spite of all of that, the game was insanely fun with an interesting and off the wall story, a unique cast of characters and well detailed environments. It's well worth getting into, even with it's existing issues. I had a completion time of about 9 1/2hrs with Carnby on normal and there's still another character for me to play through the game with.TLDR; Game is good,but has some annoying bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Gem of a game, a beautiful love letter to classic, exploration-heavy survival horror with absolutely insane quality of writing and voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: After watching many a negative review on release day i hopped into Alone in the Dark with some worry as to what i might find ahead, but much to my delight Alone in the Dark is an excellent noir/lovecraftian horror which with time i believe will become a beloved cult classic. I completed my first  play through as Detective Carnaby portrayed by David Harbour of stranger things fame and he did a truly excellent job with voice acting and adding some extra quality to the character. The story though short is very well told with engaging characters and some very well designed puzzles. The gameplay is equal parts the evil within, silent hill with a dash of feeling like Indianna Jones in some parts of the game. I did speed through the game a bit clocking in my first character completion at about 6 hours, but this was 6 hours of all killer no filler and i hopped straight in again to check out Emily's perspective who was barely seen during my outing as detective Carnaby.Performance throughout my play was flawless and i thought the game looked beautiful in parts. Enemy encounters is where the game does falter with some janky melee combat and the throwables were very poorly designed in how you utilise them, but as a huge fan of old school games like the silent hill series and games of that era i could let this slide. A great game that i see myself coming back to again and again, particularly one for my fellow horror heads out there.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the 3rd attempt at rebooting the classic Alone in the Dark franchise. In my opinion, this is the best attempt at doing so. The game pulls obvious inspiration from the recent Resident Evil games, which is ironic because those games took inspiration from the original Alone in the Dark. It features 3rd person gameplay that combines exploration, puzzle solving and combat through a large mansion called Decerto in 1930s Louisiana. The story is based on the original Alone In the Dark, but the lore has been heavily expanded upon. The game isn't as polished as the bigger budget Resident Evil games, but that's OK. Overall, I'd recommend this for fans of the Alone in the Dark franchise and survival horror games in general, or those looking for a Resident Evil style game set in the 1930s. I'd also recommend picking this up to support the developers, who shut down due to the game's low sales. This was a game made with a lot of care and attention, and they deserve our support.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I'm really liking this so far. I love the setting and the spooky old mansion. This game oozes ambiance! I also like how apologetically old school it is in it's design and controls. Reminds me of the survival horror games of the past. I'm a firm believer in the maxim that horror games don't always need the best controls (like Silent Hill 2 for example) and this seems to hold true here too. The movement and combat is pretty janky, but that's alright for me so long as the story keeps me entertained... and it is! The acting is actually really good, better than what you usually get in games, suffusing the characters with plenty of, well, character!I'll update this later if my opinion changes, but for now I'm really glad this series finally gets a respectable release.Edit: I'm mostly through the game and I want to update my review. I'm still really liking it, but it's definitely one of those games where some things came out much better than others. First off, the things this game gets really right is it's story & characters, it's graphics, it's setting & mood, and it's voice acting.While graphically, it's not the most advanced game out there, the art design looks great. They particularly succeed in the little details. Every level is packed with little inconsequential details that really add depth to the game. For instance, when I go into a new room in the mansion, I love walking around and seeing all the little stuff they added to help flesh out the characters that live there. Someone really thought about every corner and it shows.As far as the story goes, I'm loving it. It's a wonderful tribute to the Cthulhu Mythos. The writer (who for the record is the same guy who wrote SOMA) really did his research. I particularly loved that he name drops the Unaussprechlichen Kulten, my favorite of all the fictional books that inhabit the Cthulhu world. Furthermore, the character writing is particularly strong. At first I was a bit put off by the changes made to Edward Carnby as I remember him looking more like how he did in the original AitD trilogy, but the voice acting of David Harbour brought me around. As a matter of fact, none of the voice acting for any of the characters are phoned in. They really landed a solid cast.SPOILERS Now, the parts that this game could have improved on... The game itself is pretty basic and I get the feeling that they ran out of time on a lot of stuff. For instance, the first time you run into the Dark Man it's kind of a joke. He just sort of wanders about aimlessly. You can just run right on past him with very little consequence. If you stop moving and just let him look at you, your health starts dropping, but you'd have to intentional mess up to have this happen. I have to figure that they wanted to do something more here because the level design suggests there was to be a game of cat and mouse, but alas they were unable to provide it.There's also a surprising lack of enemy diversity and the enemies that there are get repeated quite often. And they aren't really scary. And they don't really seem to have much to do with the world itself. For a game that so frequently makes use of the Cthulhu Mythos, you'd think they could do a little better here. At least something that resembles a Mi-Go makes an appearance later in the game.Really, it feels like the gameplay design team ran out of time and just had to patch it together at the last moment. This kind of thing is frustrating because you can see the indications of a potentially much more elaborate game, but alas it was not to be. It has me wondering what we could have gotten if the team had another year.All and all, I still strongly recommend this game. Yeah, there's a lot it could have done better, but I can't say that I'm not having fun. Sure, there was clearly a much bigger game planned, but what there is is a still a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: My daughter and I honestly enjoyed the game.  I've always liked David Harbour as an actor and felt, in my opinion, he did a great job with his character.  We didn't think the story was very gripping though.  I wish they would have stuck with the original story of Jeremy Hartwood.  I didn't like how he was actually still alive and how we "chased" him within his own mind.  In the original game, Derceto was built by a pirate named Ezechiel Pregtz who heavily studied the occult and extend his life unnaturally.  He was eventually killed and his spirit lived within a giant tree in a cave beneath the mansion.  Jeremy Hartwood had killed himself in order to prevent Pregzt from possessing him.   From what I remember, Pregzt then targeted Carnby.  I found the original story to be far more interesting.  This remake attempts to be more psychological but at no point did I feel confused as to what was going on nor was I vested in the story.  I finished the game because I just wanted to finish it.  I do definitely recommend the game when its on sale though.  Pretty short.  Only took me 17 hours and I'm not good at these games.  A good player could probably finish it a little quicker.  If you're looking for something to keep you busy for a couple of hours here and there and you're into psychological horror, it's a good choice.

It's not actually all that common in the game, and when it does happen you will at first think it is merely lame and janky. However by the final boss (or the first time you get stunlocked to death by a basic enemy that took you by surprise or becuase Carnby became glued to some obstacle in the scenery) you will realize that it is indeed total, utter ass. Liked everything else though.

_childDocuments_.review: While I would’ve preferred it fixed camera perspective, there is really a lot here that screams classic survival horror seasoned for the modern pallet.Combat.I personally am enjoying the not quite right feel to the combat. It does a beautiful job of making you feel anxious and unsure of the outcome of Indie individual altercation, which makes you fear even the possibility of an encounter with something dangerous lurking around the corner. I’m working on my camouflage belt in Krav Maga, but even as a white belt, we were introduced to weapons training: firearms, knives and improvised weapons like sticks. I am a brown belt working on black in Brazilian jujitsu, but I still vividly remember how strikes, being spun around or even just falling to the ground were extremely unnerving and would often paralyze. The four human stress responses to new situations are fight, flee, freeze and fawn. Our protagonist are a concerned relative and a private investigator neither of which is going to have extensive fire, arms, training or experience, utilizing them in a stressful situation. Playing as a vulnerable female, it makes perfect sense that she randomly readies her weapon, places her finger on the trigger and uses it for appointing device. The lack of trigger discipline demonstrates a lack of awareness of the four basic rules of firearm safety. I laughed so hard at the beginning of the game when she declares that she hopes he has a gun so that he can wave it around in a psych ward and get coherent answers from people afterward. Somehow, the developers have been able to encapsulate all aspects of the insecurities, apprehensions and incompetency that anyone, even trained, can exhibit under extreme stress.Atmosphere.While creeks, footsteps and closing doors are typical implementations to make a location feel lived in or alive, I can’t sing the praises high enough for the unique implementation of audio logs for individual notes and objectives, and I only wish that all items would be given an audio clip just to make it a complete immersive feature. The difference in feeling and emotional impact between someone involved in the project reading a description or prose and a random gamer, trying to the potential relevance of unfamiliar text which popped up on the screen, is identical to the difference between a professionally recorded audiobook, read by a trained voice actor, and a overwhelmed, novice volunteer reading subject, specific jargon from a college textbooks for a blind student Recording from their living room.Bug:Fortunately, there is a dash or dodge button. My solution to the problem of being able to walk into objects has been to rapidly press the Dodge or Dash button, while spinning the character, a little further clockwise or counterclockwise. I assume this was done to give more of the perception of limitless exploration. It seems like some of the assets have one particular angle that well allow your character to clip into the asset and that same angle has to be found to get out. An extremely minor annoyance yet it is still there and you should be aware of it as well as the cause/solution potentials.I will add to this once I’ve actually finished both campaigns, but Whats here is a definite a full throated, controller clutching recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the original trilogy and I can happily say that the 2024 version is worth it. It may have some flaws here and there but it is AMAZING.I took my time playing through both campaigns and damn, it was a fantastic experience. Gonna replay it soon to get all the achievements, YES SIR ! The game FEELS like it should. While the 3rd person movement is not near as clunky as the original Alone in the Dark, there is a small level of jank that makes absolute sense.The story is awesome. All the areas from the game are well-detailed.The Voice acting with the notes and characters are well done. David Harbour and Jodie Comer did a fantastic job. The same goes for the other actors as well.While it is huge and different from the original, it stands on its own as what Alone in the Dark should be. The story driven atmosphere is even more so amazing now as it was years ago. As someone who likes to explore and get more of the side lore. I was very pleased and impressed. I found myself putting down the controller and letting the notes be read to me in cinematic flare.It's not Alone in the Dark A New Nightmare or the crap movie that was made as a cash grab / tax break.The Music - BREATHTAKING. I could gush on that opening menu theme forever. The game's sound is top notch. I'm glad we get the soundtrack with the deluxe version.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly I never played the old Alone in the Dark games, or any of the questionable 360/PS3 era games, so was fairly new to me overall playing this bad boy.As a fan of Lovecraftian horror, it's honestly a damn delight, especially with a few key aspects coming straight from the source material, such as entities or creatures. That being said, the game DOES it's own interpretation of some things, namely a lot of the enemies outside of one particular boss, but it's still pretty fun nonetheless.At the time of the review, there ARE some noticeable fps drops at times, I noticed them mostly when the the game was loading in another part of the map, the transitions between the real world and the "nightmare sequences" and some during the boss fight at the very end of the game, but otherwise? Honestly pretty solid launch.Keep in mind, this isn't a triple A budget game. Sometimes stuff looks a little odd, like some of the facial animations, or things like the running and or reloads, but unless you ONLY want to play hardcore polished games like Witcher or Red Dead, might be a bit of a miss for you.One thing to note as well, that in order to get the most content out of the game, similarly to Resident Evil 2, you need to play as both characters, so that's at least two guaranteed playthroughs, with each lasting around 8 or so hours if you don't try and speed run things.Overall, I genuinely enjoyed this, and I can only hope that it performs well enough to either get a DLC, or a sequel at some point down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: All around a good game with great atmosphere. It is very reminiscent of Resident Evil. Very similar style and atmosphere.I notice how others mention stuttering and performance issues. Which I noticed as well at first. But after tinkering with just turning off motion blur, chromatic aberration and enabling v-sync, as well as not enabling FSR. I noticed that the stuttering almost completely stopped. Only very occasionally will I get a hiccup. So still a bit of poor optimization on the dev side.For reference, I have an Intel i7-1200, AMD RX 6800 XT, 32GB RAM, and it’s on a 980 Pro SSD. Runs it at max settings.I can’t say this will fix everyone’s issue with the stuttering as I’d imagine most know what they could tune to resolve the issue. I hope at least. But for me, I have almost no issues after doing the above that I mentioned. Just a very minor hiccup here and there. Nothing too problematic or annoying to break my immersion of the game.Overall, if you’re interested. I think it’s worth it. Considering most games these days are absolute cash grab garbage. I will say this one is a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the OG Alone in the Dark games, but I've seen a lot of media talking about it and seeing it's gameplay. I personally think this is a fantastic recreation and modernization of a retro classic. The setting is amazing, the soundtrack is fitting, the entire atmosphere sucks you in and makes you intrigued. The melee feels weak in a way that it just doesn't have a good punchy feel behind it, but I can look past that since you rarely need to engage in combat anyways if you're quick enough and can press dodge - also I mean the guns feel just fine and punchy. The best part of this game though comes down to the world building and it's ability to really make the character feel like they are barely holding on and living a alternate life all of a sudden - fighting the eldritch horrors of the mind while everyone is just spectating. It's a very well done Lovecraftian style horror story imo. This game lands in my top 5 of 2024 easily, and if you need a totem to understand where that is - the other remake isn't on that list.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original game, and are familiar with the various entries into the series after, it's clear the developers took the time to really integrate a lot of the lore. It's a clear re-imagining of the first that does it justice, just without the obnoxious instant death mechanics for things you couldn't know beforehand and that expands on the Lovecraftian lore the first used in its story. The environments are moody and scary and the story is certainly original, if often told in notes found throughout the game.That said, it's not without its flaws. The game practically points you in the directions you're supposed to go with its placing and camera angles after events in Modern mode, aiming with a controller is awkward, and the enemies are more obnoxious than scary. Worse, the lighting is hard to adjust properly depending on your monitor and the environments don't have consistent brightness, so things can go from dark to overly bright near instantly.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like it could be a fun game. Early enemies seem to be a rip right out of the newer RE games. Several performance issues for PC. In 3 hours I've experienced many hitching issues with artifacting and screen tear issues with V sync off. Had to turn Vsync back on to get rid of the horrible tearing effects. Clothing artifacts happening a lot which in turn is causing the actual hitching of the game. Almost a rubber banding effect with clothing, neckties, etc. Needs a decent patch or two. Then, should be fairly awesome.EDIT: 4/7/24- Game has gotten a couple of patches it seems and honestly runs a LOT smoother than at release. I havent' gotten any of the game hitching rubber banding effects from articles of clothing that seemed to hitch the game badly. This NEW AitD game takes all the original ideas of the first (1992) and makes them much better. Going back to the Cthulu mythos and monsters and music and setting is ideal. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait to play through both stories (Emily first, then Edward, though you can do them in any order) before I left a review.First, I love this game. I was lucky enough to not have the bugs that others experienced, my only issues were a few instances of getting stuck on geometry (where, as Emily, I was able to dodge and eventually free myself, and as Edward, luckily had an autosave just prior to reload and replay.)The structure of the game reminds me a fair bit of the Resident Evil 2 remake, in that your map expands as the game progresses and you do not have all the keys at the start. (Also like RE2R, items are "Archived" when no longer necessary.)  If you played both sides of RE2R, you're familiar about how the beginning of Claire & Leon's stories are very similar, but they differ significantly later in the game (with Leon having the Ada story & Claire having the Sherry story.) That is also the case in this game -- the dialogue and cutscenes differ between Emily and Edward in the beginning, but they each have their own story to address as well later in the game.If you enjoy southern gothic aesthetics, this game will be a feast for your eyes. The sickly yellow tones, the iconic buildings with galleries so associated with New Orleans, swampy shacks, it's all here. The environment team did an incredible job, and truly, hats off to them, they nailed the assignment.Also on the "good job you!" front, the audio team. Though not quite as intense as Alien Isolation (but really, what is,) the audio team succeeds at making you feel like doom is imminent. There is excellent tension created just from what you hear.The downsides, which truly are me reaching for complaints, begin with the combat. It is not as fluid as similar games, and the melee combat in particular could have stood to be polished a bit more. There is no "lock on," so you'll be SURE you'll hit the enemy and then stop just shy and GET hit instead. This is made all the more obvious by the fact "opportunity" items like rocks & Molotov cocktails DO have a lock-on system with enemies, even though they are found in-world and you cannot carry them with you.Additionally, the game is fairly short. One playthrough (Emily or Edward) will average about eight hours if you aren't rushing & are actually looking for collectibles (which you should absolutely do, as that does impact your game.) If we go with two playthroughs for a full experience, that's about sixteen hours of playtime. For me, personally, the price was more than worth it because I am a huge southern gothic horror fan & was anxiously awaiting this game since they announced this reimagining in 2022. If the initial $59.99 price tag is more than you'd be willing to pay for 16 hours, perhaps wait for a sale.Overall, this game is everything I wanted it to be and I'm very pleased. I would absolutely love more stories in this beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone whose always adored horror story games in old spooky mansions, I'm so glad the genre hasn't died and Alone in the Dark doesn't fail to deliver... At least not yet!Already I'm immersed in the quiet yet pervasive solitude of the manor, opening clues and stocking up on bullets... I have a feeling I'm going to need them! What I like so far is the simplicity of it (I'm not keen on overly complex UI menus), yet I appear to be collecting parts of forbidden knowledge and access to greater things as I advance. I liked at the start, it shows you three samples side by side of a dark shadowy scene, medium and bright scenes - So you can adjust your personal level of brightness and contrast to suit the range of environments you'll be exposed to.Although I do admittedly have a high end PC, I've not come across any performance issues at all so far. The game runs very smoothly and I am enjoying the atmospheric lighting conditions and high end graphics.I did have one clunky sticking point for my character early on (a fallen over plant pot in the first open area), but I managed to get free of it eventually.Lots of locked doors you need to find keys to, lots of clues and as I've mentioned, wholly immersive. I've gotten half way through Chapter 2 now and have had to kill quite a few creatures. I don't like that they just throw you into that - No warm up, no training, no easy first dude... They take quite a few shots to kill and I did die a few times already, mostly because I felt thrown into the deep end a bit.You can creep around a lot of them, or just run away - Means you don't need to fight everything. But go figure out your controls first if you can! The "opportunity" brick you find to distract the enemy - I haven't figured that out yet, or made it work to my advantage and I've been playing a few hours already.I am enjoying the balance between clues, puzzles, exploring and then the world of fighting creatures... It's a nice mix and keeps things interesting! I'll keep playing and return with more!!

_childDocuments_.review: The haunted house formula has been a mainstay in horror games arguably since Sweet Home (1989), mainly because video games allow for a completely different approach to places than movies or books. In video games, the player is free to explore every nook and cranny - and in turn must always choose to step into the dark basement himself. Whether it is the police station from Resident Evil 2, VtM: Bloodlines' Hallowbrook Hotel or Thief's Shalebridge Cradle: These locations stick with the players, searing their floorplans into the brain. Derceto in the original Alone in the Dark from 1998 stands among the greatest examples of the haunted house, codifying the genre and freeing the way for the aforementioned classics.This game is not an example of that genre, however. Whether or not you will enjoy 2024's Alone in the Dark depends on whether this is a dealbreaker for you or not.The 2024 reboot sends you away from Derceto frequently - and when you are there, you are never really Alone in the Dark. Derceto is the place where the interactions take place, where the story is continued. While the classic haunted house is explored, 2024's Derceto is a rather linear experience, a starting point into other eldritch locations. Locations that simply bleed atmosphere, yes, locations that Lovecraft himself chose for good reason, but this approach takes time and attention away from Derceto itself (here reimagined as an eerie clinic, although it still retains its roots in more than one way). It is a horror game, but not so much a haunted house as a theme park.For my part, I did enjoy this new iteration of Alone in the Dark quite a lot. I had just finished Resident Evil 4's reboot and while gameplay-wise everything about RE4 is better than AitD, the absurdity of the plot made it hard to finish. I will not return for a NG+. Conversely, I finished both playthroughs of AitD within three days, because I loved exploring a new iteration of Derceto, loved the characters, loved the atmosphere, the inclusion of Lovecraft's Cthulhu mythos, the allusions to the 1992 original. From Weird Tales magazines scattered about to a bust of old H.P. in the attic, from finding the old Indian Blanket again to in-jokes about AitD 2 and 3 - this could have been a masterpiece. Sadly, it is held back by other factors.The technical issues, for example, almost made me refund the game. Stuttering during transitions and cutscenes, repeated crashes to desktop - this game is badly optimized and suffers from it. Strangely enough these problems only occured in my Carnby playthrough. Then there is the combat, a clunky affair, more of an annoyance than a challenge. Some of the puzzles add nothing except for stretching game time. And while the story is compelling, its ending is weak and unsatisfying - in fact, I prefer the secret bad endings, because they fit the bleak tone so much better.Do I still recommend it? That depends. Fans of the original or of Lovecraftian horror should definitely give it a try, with the aforementioned tempered expectations. It is a solid Gothic horror tale and the actors - Jodie Comer and David Harbour especially - do a fine job. Get it in a sale, though, because you won't help the developers: Pieces Interactive was shut down after this game did not sell as well as expected.I would have played a sequel, if it ever came to that. I guess that is as much a recommendation as one can give.Final verdict: 7 of 10 Indian blankets.

_childDocuments_.review: Another case of 'I hate leaving negative reviews, but this was an atrocious mess and I want others to save their money.' THIS is why we don't spend an entire dev budget on a pair of actors. A beloved franchise with yet another failed reboot, because somewhere up the chain, someone decided to force a dev team to work with half the resources so that a couple Hollywood B-listers could phone in wooden performances while the game falls apart around them. What started with an interesting premise devolved quickly into an absolute disaster of pacing, storytelling and design. When the game wasn't stuttering (which was rare), it was STILL clunky and unintuitive to control. Every motion--walking, reloading weapons, using weapons and using health items--is done at a snail's pace, and ALL can be animation cancelled easily and accidentally, meaning you can end up taking a solid 10 seconds to reload a gun or drink some health if you aren't careful. Yes, that's right, because these base actions take roughly 5 seconds each to complete. So a slight misclick--or believing the game dropped your input so attempting to redo it (because it happens ALL the time) means you will accidentally interrupt the animation and double it's length. What's more, reloading and drinking health items both cause your character to stop running and slowly strut instead, and if you are forced to dodge or run--you guessed it: animation cancel. I won't get into the story because it was such an absolute mess. I am a firm believer in the 'show, don't tell' school of writing, and while cosmic horror is one of my favorite subgenres, this was an abysmal attempt at knitting together a bunch of unresolved, nonsensical plot points vomited at you in an exposition dump that would put most anime to shame, with the watered-down glue being 'but it's cosmic horror so we don't have to make any of this stuff add up!' Pass denied. Sorry.I was so excited for the first 2 hours of this game, And had zero desire to finish it, let alone do a second character's full playthrough. I am so let down that I will likely not see another Alone in the Dark entry in my lifetime due to this complete flop of a reboot.

_childDocuments_.review: That was fun.Okay, so, I never played the original AitD, so I can't really compare them. The only other game in the series I've played was A New Nightmare, and Emo Carnby was a major turn off to the game, even aside the game breaking bugs I kept running into. THIS Carnby works a LOT better, and I really enjoyed playing as Emily.Gameplay: 6.5/10 paws.* For what it is, this game's gameplay isn't bad. Some of the responsiveness feels sluggish at times because the characters turn more like real people than the whole spinning in place thing a lot of games do. They don't get moving too fast, and they aren't masterful gun-totting badasses. That's actually kind of the point, though. It makes combat feel a lot more like something to be worried about. Still, some of the jank in interactive points is... well... jank.* There are guns, and you will have to use them. Ammunition is sporadic. There are melee weapons, and you had BETTER use them. THERE IS A DODGE BUTTON AND MAY THE HIGH PRIEST CTHULHU HIMSELF INTERVENE IF YOU DON'T USE IT.Sound: 7/10 paws.* Overall I liked the sound design. It was nothing special for a horror game, but it wasn't bad at all. The voice acting was, by and large, pretty good.Story: 7.5/10 paws.* Harder to follow than I expected and on the surface it feels like you are touching on several different stories at once. In a way, I think it _IS_ touching on several things at once. Though it lends to great future setup, and feels right for the what it is, it does give the game a less cohesive narrative. Once you get under the surface all those branches of story start to make a lot more sense, although I do feel that some of it requires some VERY in depth prior knowledge on the players part with Yog Sothothery to grasp some of what's happening.* Something I found fascinating was just how absolutely hardcore they went on getting ...well... who the dark man actually is... RIGHT. And they DID. They got him spot on. It was glorious.* There is a thing at the end of the game. It is absolutely, exactly right. I adored this depiction of it. If you don't know what I am referring to... play the game and remember that dodge button. You're going to need it...Additional note: 12/10 paws.* Game has an option to play as a woman without her just being a re-skin of the male protagonist. I know that's not a big thing for some people, but I have been having to make do with main characters I just cannot step into the shoes of in a lot of big games for so long that when that isn't an option I find myself not bothering with the game at all. I loved it, and I loved Emily's character, and the backstory of hers hiding behind the scenes hit pretty damn hard, and actually did explain a few things. That said, I actually liked this enough that once I go get myself another coffee, I actually am going to go back in and play through as Carnby, because I am actually kind of curious and halfway like the guy already.I went back and played the Prologue too and thoroughly enjoyed the (EXTREMELY) brief stint playing as Grace. I think I'd play a whole game from her dissociative perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not in good faith recommend this game due to the amount of bugs experienced. I am constantly getting stuck on small objects that cause me too load old saves. Getting stuck is exacerbated by the dodge mechanic that will put you in this scenario more than actually dodging. enemies straight up clipping through walls or disappearing all together. every time I rebound the button for the opportunities, the game would bug out and not let me use anything. I do not believe that this game was actually finished on launch, and bugs are not the only problem. there are multiple sounds that just absolutely do not match what you are actually doing. the first time i encountered the sniffer all of the audio came out of the left channel until the cut scene was complete. There was also an area near chapter 4 where you climb down wooden vines, but the game clearly makes metal ladder sounds. On top of all of this the combat is absolutely not finished. the small ground enemies towards the end of the game are almost impossible to hit with melee weapons, resulting in a waist of ammo as they take almost 7 handgun shots to kill. Even if you do manage to hit them with a melee weapon almost every enemy will deplete an entire melee weapon making them almost useless. I hope they fix these issues, but i just cant believe that people are still getting away with releasing games that are this far from being finished.I will change this review if these problems are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Not Alone in the StutterOutside of clunky combat and bad optimization - plays good, somewhat interesting too. I can`t write full review until you guys fix your shaders loading in this console port.And after latest April patch game still ran poorly, I cannot believe how much went into this game budget and how much into the actors. Let`s go with the pros:I loved the game, it is a fun adventure, a fresh look at the classic first Alone in the Dark game. Atmosphere is awesome, music is nice, environments are decent and have the same vibes as original one. At the core moments it held me nervous and engaged. Collecting and reading stuff to make story connection is very well presented and narrated too!!! Puzzles are nice as well, and you really have to think a bit first playthrough. All and all, I hope game gets polished and perhaps gets a DLC or a sequel to make the other two game remakes happen. I haven`t regretted buying this and completed all the achievements.Secret endings are neat little way of having expected outcome that is not very clear to achieve at first glance. Now cons:Combat. Is. OK. Not good, but definitely better than the OG AitD game. But often monsters felt just tedious and clunky, not challenging, and even worse - animation is not often reading what can happen next. Stutters/lags. Still are there, still break immersion, still hope that will be fixed because it made me feel that broken immersion at the times...Collision - hope they fix it, I was mad that randomly stuck on some objects just because I dashed into a magic pixel and could not hop off the object.Animations and transitions - here`s the deal. I understand it is not interactive kino with press button to make choice. But many little things here could be more polished and done better. I had weapons stuck under feet, Emily standing on a book, dorky movements of the sliding monsters... Plain sad. And last, but no least for me, was the chapter 4. It feels so rushed that probably I`m not the only one feeling it. You basically jump into different places, then the boat segment is just a joke, same as the winter one. That`s why I feel that some stuff could be expanded on. OH and now I remember the worst feeling EVER. Since our characters are doing stuff in parallel, I am very sad to see that their scenarios are exactly the same and we get almost zero insight on what the other character did while we were investigating. I hoped that I will visit a bit more different places, or do different stuff, like resident evil 2 A and B scenarios. Lost opportunity if you ask me. Overall I`d say it is a 7/10 experience ruined by lack of QA, bug fixes, animations improvements, stutter removal, and maybe making combat and story feel a bit more rich.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to love Alone in the Dark back then and slowly forgot about it in profit of what Resident Evil brought to the genre quickly after. Is this reboot a revival of the 90's? Absolutely not. Is there still a vibe of Alone in the Dark? Yes, somehow you'll find that weird dark folklore stories mixed with its own dose of cosmic horror for sure. It has its own visual & audio directions that are quite strong, and while the game offers a way to explore two variations of the whole story with both character, I've finished the game filling I've got enough of one playthrough.I think the dev did a decent job but at some point there are some series that should just sleep for good and let the space for new ones to rise. I feel that people would have been less harsh on that title if it was not owning the 90's legacy of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw the trailers for the game and it looked...rough. I love Lovecraftian games, have always wanted to hunker down and play the original Alone in the Dark, and the reviews weren't all that bad, so purchased at full-price.The first enemy convinced me they missed the mark; I spent an hour shaking my head in disappointment, but it consistently began chipping away at that initial impression until I found myself really appreciating it.  The combat becomes fun, the story becomes compelling, and the cinematics get more convincing.This is by no means a flawless game, but sets itself apart as one of those increasingly-rare sleeper-hits made with enough money and passion to be ambitious. Its charm may just be elevating it to a top spot in my favorite games list, alongside other imperfect gems like the original Nier and Hellblade.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:Finished the game as Emily. Everything stated below still stands as the game was awesome throughout. I will say the combat ended up generally better than I anticipated when I first wrote the review. That being said, it's still not going to be for everyone, especially those looking for action horror.Original Review:I've only played the first few chapters as Emily so far, but I want to take a moment in my review to talk about the impressive art direction and visual design. I am a huge fan of horror movies, and I find that the most effective films have great cinematography, lighting, and sound design. This game has really perfected those three elements so integral to the horror experience. As an example, I recorded a moment during my playthrough that had at least four light sources with different color temperatures that gave the scene a richness and depth never really approached in even the most cinematic games.Additionally the sound design and the soundtrack are both impeccable. The jazz music, ranging from timely to chaotic and creepy (just watch the trailers), and the sounds of insects scurrying from or swarming the light, the creaking of doors and walls and branches, even the sound of footsteps squelching in mud or dully shuffling a floor above all add up to incredible immersion.It's so rare to find a game with both a strong sense of design and the willingness to stick to that design so thoroughly, but I'm glad this game does it. It's the only thing the game does perfectly, but playing it, you find yourself wishing other games would take this approach. How much better would the modern classics of the genre be with this level of style and execution?To that point, this game could also be improved in places. For the most part combat has been adequate, though sometimes excellent. It's occasionally frustrating finding yourself in a corner with no way out and the camera clipping in ways that make you just wait to die and try again. For every moment I've had like that however, there has been a moment of sheer panic, fleeing and spinning frantically to launch a brick or bottle at my pursuer and land a quick headshot or hatchet swing before running for my life toward the next environmental opportunity. That's where the combat shines, and it's certainly how the game is meant to be played, at least by me. That sometimes means dying, at most a couple of times, until you know where the exits and throwables are, but mostly the auto saves have been just before the fights so far.But you should play this game for the atmosphere not the action, since that's what it leans hardest into and where its greatest strength lies. On a 4070 I'm playing it in Cinematic in 4k with HDR on at 60+ fps, and I find myself stopping and taking screenshots or recording video at least twice an hour, because the game is really that beautiful. If atmosphere is important to you in horror games, you owe it to yourself to experience what this game does well, even if that means plodding through a few moments of things you may think it doesn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like giving a negative review, but after playing for 10h, the negatives outweigh the positives.This game does not excel at anything. Every aspect of this game goes from  to , it never achieve greatness in any department.Which is quite a shame, because at first glance, the game does not look too bad. I mean, the visual of the game is quite good and some of the environment is nice to look at. The UI/Menus are also good looking too in my opinion. Lastly, the voice-over is also not bad.However, after playing for a while, the problems will start to show up...The story does no seems to make much sense, it also does not help that the characters interaction is often pointless and provide nothing to the story.Every enemy don't react to your shots or your melee attack, it feels like you are bashing a moving brick wall. Speaking of melee attack, it does not feel good at all. Your character seems to never focus on the enemy, making the whole thing hard to lend hits.Not bad by any means, but there is not a single track I can remember of.There is a lot of physics bugs in this game where your character can get stuck in furniture or wall. This happened 2 times when I was playing this game and I was forced to reload my last save.The door physics/mechanics is also annoying. If you enter a room and decide you want to go back, you need to wait for the door to slowly close before you can open it again. It gets annoying overtime.There is also a lack of polish on scene transition at times, meaning that the game should have a black screen to load things of, but no, for one second you will see weird animation or repositioning of characters that you are not supposed to see.After starting the  mode, all of this issues was too much (especially the combat) and decided to give up. The experience was starting to get more frustrating than fun, unfortunately.I wish the devs would have spend more times polishing the combat, the story and the characters, because the game could have been something great. It has potential.

_childDocuments_.review: You're probably aware that this game is sort-of a mixed bag, so giving an opinion is quite risky.I, for one, enjoyed it immensely. The puzzles were great with a handful that do require your full attention, the manor and levels are extremely well designed (and quite diverse as the story progresses), the music and sound design is top-notch and story-wise? If you're looking for a good Lovecraftian game, you're in for a treat! And the lore of HPL is used exceptionally! Combat is passable; at times it feels janky and could use some fine tuning but in all honesty I never found it frustrating.Yes, there are bugs... A lot of them! Surprisingly, in my first run, I didn't experience any, but during my second I actually stumbled upon all of them (clipping issues, audio glitches, getting stuck on objects, missing objectives etc). Stuttering is there and quite persistent, but afaik I'm playing a Unreal Engine game so it kinda comes with the territory; as gamers we don't have to put up with it but it's hardly surprising!I sincerely hope the devs put in the extra effort to polish this game because there's a solid experience to be had despite the techical flaws. It won't break ground (graphically or story-wise) but for those of us who played the originals this is a loving homage not just of the AitD series but for 90's Infogrames games (Shadow of the Comet, Prisoner of Ice). Definitely worth playing!

_childDocuments_.review: "Alone in the Dark" (2023) is a revival of a series that has always held a special place in my heart. As someone who has been a fan since the original 1992 release, I approached this reboot with equal parts excitement and trepidation, hoping it would capture the magic of the early games while updating it for modern audiences.**Story:**The story is where "Alone in the Dark" (2023) truly shines. It stays true to the series' roots with its blend of psychological horror and supernatural mystery. Set in the haunted Derceto Manor, the narrative feels like a love letter to fans of the original games. The plot, filled with twists and chilling moments, captures the eerie atmosphere that made the series iconic. The characters are well-developed, and their backstories are compelling, adding depth to the overall narrative. The dialogue is well-written, with enough nods to the original to satisfy longtime fans while still being accessible to newcomers.**Graphics:**Visually, the game is stunning. The developers have done an incredible job of bringing Derceto Manor to life. The attention to detail in the environment is impressive, with each room and corridor dripping with atmosphere. The lighting effects are particularly noteworthy, playing a crucial role in creating the game’s tense and foreboding mood. Character models are detailed and expressive, adding to the immersion. However, there are occasional issues with frame rates and textures that detract from the experience, but they aren't enough to overshadow the overall visual excellence.**Sound:**Sound design is another area where the game excels. The eerie soundtrack and ambient noises work together to create an unsettling atmosphere that keeps you on edge. The voice acting is strong, with performances that bring the characters to life and enhance the story. The sound effects, from the creak of a door to the distant wail of something unknown, are perfectly executed and contribute significantly to the horror experience.**Gameplay:**Gameplay is where "Alone in the Dark" (2023) stumbles slightly. While it successfully modernizes some mechanics, there are moments where it feels clunky and outdated. The combat system is serviceable but lacks the fluidity seen in other contemporary horror titles. The puzzles, a hallmark of the series, are well-designed and challenging, though occasionally they can be a bit obtuse.**Final Rating:**Overall, "Alone in the Dark" (2023) is a solid return to form for the series, despite some gameplay shortcomings. As a fan, it’s a joy to see this beloved franchise back in the spotlight. I’d give it a solid 8/10. The story, atmosphere, and dedication to the series' legacy make it a must-play for any fan, even if it's not without its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: excellent game in my opinion. I usually don't buy games at release, but this one was worth it even at full price -10% launch discount. people compare it to resident evil, but I think it's its own thing. there is much less combat and more exploration. the locations all have great atmosphere! just make sure to disable all the hints and markers. graphics and story are great too. i couldn't get into resident evil 4 remake at all and had to refund it, but i loved this game.performance is fine for me with a 3080 in 1440p using dlss and everything on epic settings. shader compilation stuttering sucks in the first few minutes and why is this even a thing? can't it precompile the shaders? however, the major problem for me were the lag spikes during combat. if you turn quickly and want to do a melee hit, odds are that the game hitches for half a second. it's not a hard game so you will likely survive and it doesn't happen all the time, but it's annoying. i'm also fine with the game's length. _childDocuments_.review: Is it perfect? No.Does it lack some polish? Definitely.Was it fun? Absolutely. Since the game's combat is not as fluid like Resident Evil, my recommendation is to play on 'easy' with all hints turned off. That way you will enjoy the best Alone in the Dark has to offer, while the worst will not be as frustrating. Sincerely hope that this little gem of a game will do well sale-wise, because I believe this studio has enough respect and love for the originals to remake them with the care they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Resident Evil 2/3/4, Silent Hill 2, and Alone in Dark in just over a month.  Alone in the Dark was the one I thought was going to be worst, and was the one I loved the most.  The voice acting in this game is excellent, the audio logs I listened to in full. The notebook narrator recapping things as you went along is great.  I loved the focusing to see items/points of interest mechanic. After playing several survival horror titles in a row I appreciated how streamlined this game was in comparison.  There were some rough spots, some visual glitches from time to time, but nothing game breaking or even really distracting. I don't know why this didn't catch on more, or get better reviews, but this is a sleeper hit for 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like writing these reviews, but I was pretty disappointed in this game. A new Alone in the Dark game in the style of the recent Resident Evil games with a story by the guy who wrote SOMA seemed like such a no-brainer and I was really looking forward to it, but in the end it fails to deliver.The game is way too linear and has none of the interesting exploration from RE. When you find a key or important item you use it almost right away. Sometimes in the same room. Neither the story nor characters are particularly interesting. Or rather, they had the potential to be interesting, had they been more fleshed out. The Dark Man is so nebulous as a villian that it's honestly hard to care about Jeremy or his problems. The combat is so close to being good, there are a few encounters where you're juggling melee, ranged and throwable items, and it all comes together in a satisfying way, but the rest just boil down to shooting at enemies walking towards you at a snails pace (or getting stuck on geometry). The graphics and animation are good enough, but for a $60 game that feels like the bare minimum these days.Also it just isn't spooky enough. Where are all the crazy mindscrew moments that made SOMA so memorable? Like half of the levels take place in the daytime. At the start of the game you arrive at the mansion at dusk, but why not have it be at night and raining straight away to set the mood? Alone in the Dark. It's right there in the name. Yeah, I don't know. Maybe this game would be worth it at around $30, but I can't recommend it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark 2024 may not be the best survival horror game you've seen, but in the current generation, where the genre has become rare, it's something better than nothing, and for sure, it's way better than the newer action Residen Evil games.The story telling has some weaknesses; it's like it's missing so many unanswered questions about the past of characters and their purpose, like why the maid attacked you aggressively with her knife when you wanted to peek into the kitchen?The action gameplay is very simple; you probably won't feel a lack of ammunition, which is the main feature of survival games. You can cross the enemeis or hit them with bricks or molotoves. There are only two bosses near the end of the game, and they are not challenging even on hard difficulty.Some puzzles are great, and some are just straight-forward due to the lazy design of the levels. It's like in many places, you face a locked door or locked safe, but the key to open it is just placed in the same room or the next room.BTW, despite the issues the game has due to the lazy design of the story and levels, it's still a survival horror game and worth getting if you like the genre, so I'm giving the game a  score.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! It's the first Alone in the Dark game I've played start to finish so I can't say much about how loyal it is to the franchise but I simply love this game. I played it on easy mode because I was more interested in the story than the fights and let me tell you, I was still on the edge of my seat! Great story telling, art is beautiful, voice acting superb and great replayability...for at least one more time because it really pays out to play both characters!There are many collision, streaming, freezing and visual bugs in this game. I thought I ran into one blocker which only turned out that one thing that was optional so far, was indeed mandatory. I am fine with the amount and kind of bugs in this game though. Nobody is perfect...and it ads to the everlasting feeling of one can never be sure if it's reality or the slow loss of sanity...

_childDocuments_.review:
Deep in the 1920's south, Emily Hartwood's uncle has gone missing. Together with private investigator Edward Carnby, she embarks on a journey to Derceto Manor to uncover the secrets of this mysterious place and the circumstances of her relative's vanishing. 

Return to Derceto Manor in this reimagination of Alone in the Dark, a love letter to the 90's cult classic horror game. 

Encounter strange residents, nightmarish realms, dangerous monsters and ultimately unveil a plot of rising evil. At the intersection of reality, mystery, and insanity, an adventure waits that will challenge your core beliefs.

Who can you trust, what will you believe, and what will you do next?

name: Embracelet
detailed_description: Are you looking for a heartwarming, relaxing game? Look no further! Exploration, puzzles and an exciting story in a unique setting Embracelet puts you in the role of Jesper, a Norwegian teenager who lives with his mom in the city. One day he is handed an old bracelet by his Grandfather who grew up in a fishing community up north. This bracelet has powers - strange, mysterious powers! Jesper is given the task to unravel the mystery behind the bracelet. Where does it come from? Who does it belong to? And why did his Grandfather leave the island and his old life behind? EXPLORE A BEAUTIFUL, NORTHERN NORWEGIAN ISLAND SOLVE PUZZLES USING THE MAGICAL BRACELET MAKE FRIENDS AND CHOICES THAT CAN AFFECT THE OUTCOME OF THE STORY With its gentle difficulty level, intriguing story and beautiful soundtrack, Embracelet is a game for anyone who enjoys unique, heartwarming video games. Embracelet is made by Mattis Folkestad, one man team behind the award-winning adventure game Milkmaid of the Milky Way. Playtime: 3-6 hours with different endings. Best played with a game controller, like an Xbox one, Dualshock or Nintendo Pro Controller in a sofa or a comfy chair.

short_description: Travel to northern Norway, solve puzzles using a mysterious, magical bracelet and make new friends on your journey to discover the past - and yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: An enchanting adventure game about the coming of age of Jasper.  He visits an island off Northern Norway where his grandfather grew up and meets all kinds of interesting characters.  Along the way, Jasper learns about the ties of family, loss, guilt, love and friendship.  He also finds the owner of a bracelet his grandfather gave him which has 'magical' properties.After a slow start, there is lots of action.  Reminded me of the Famous Five books but with older teens.  There is a bit of violence and sexual innuendo, so not for young children...suitable for pre teens.Achievements are pretty easy to get, but you have to replay the game to get the second ending.  The game took me over 6 hrs to get through, but it still is a bit pricey, so buy on sale.Graphics were simple, music was good, but the controls were clunky.  Controlling the main character on keyboard was a nightmare, but I believe those on controllers has similar experiences.   Puzzles were casual and simple.  There are no stressful areas to overcome, but there is quite a bit of backtracking involved.I loved the environment of the Norwegian island which was lovely and refreshing to see.  Recommend for those who enjoy non-combat adventure with a sweet story.  7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is very chill game. It's a story driven game about a boy who's given a magical bracelet and it give the boy some supernatural powers. He travels to the small fictional island in Norway to find what happened to his grandad and his adventure begins.On the way he finds friends and spends some time with them. There are some humorous scenes, sad moments and even some thrilling action. Nevertheless the game is very relaxing. All the main characters are really lovable but maybe there's not enough time to fully connect with them. I wish I could've spent more time with those two friends to know them better.There are some light puzzles where you need to move some objects or push a button. Mostly gameplay consists of running around, helping people and talking with them. This is how you advance the story. It's a short game with multiple endings. They're not very different though.Running back and forth could be boring sometimes but overall it's an enjoyable experience.Graphically the game is very minimalistic but it has beautiful art-style and even with these low-poly graphics some scenes look stunning.Game runs perfectly well but that shouldn't be surprising considering the graphics. Should run smoothly on any PC.Unfortunately there's no ultrawide support. It could benefit from cinematic aspect ratio. But what can we do...The soundtrack is pretty nice but at some point it starts to get a bit repetitive.There's no voice acting but there's not much to read either. The dialogues are pretty short consisting of two or three lines sometimes extending to several lines.Overall a good and enjoyable game for those who love story driven and relaxing games. Not a masterpiece by any means but it's way above average. It's short but tells an interesting story. Get this on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: *** Recommended ONLY if you have a controller and can deal with platforming ***This is a better glimpse into a North Norwegian coastal community than you could hope to get during an actual vacation (source: I live here), combined with a solid story-driven puzzle adventure revolving around a mysterious, magical bracelet. The solo dev has come a long way since "Milkmaid of the Milkyway", and thankfully he's abandoned his atrocious attempts at rhyming. He's clearly familiar with the northern landscapes, everyday life, joys and struggles that he portrays in a natural and nuanced way. The game is pretty for having low-fi graphics (that I'm generally not a fan of), the soundtrack is good as far as I can tell (unfortunately played with some background noise and without headphones), the puzzles are alright (you use your magical gimmick to fix stuff), difficulty level very casual I'd say so far*. Most importantly for me, the island feels like a real place with real people. It's a mostly chill experience, though I think a content warning for (general content, not essential for the plot afaik) is warranted. I also would have appreciated an option to disable that hip new jumpy text thing that's supposed to express the speaker being emotional. *HOWEVER, this game seems to turn into a surprise platformer towards the end, requiring dexterity with controls and timing. Thanks, I hate it. I guess it's ok if you're used to platformers and have a gamepad, probably still doable though a PITA with a keyboard. My clumsy self tried and failed over and over again before I got too frustrated and abandoned it. What a shame :( TL;DR: If you love puzzles, I don't know if that's reason enough to play this game. If you love story-driven adventures , this is a solid one. If you love Scandinavia and/or the (sub-)Arctic and feel like spending a few hours in Northern Norway, this is probably an excellent choice with a gamepad and platforming skills. * * * I collect chill and story-driven games in my curator .

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this. I'm a complete sucker for coming-of-age stories. It's the nostalgia of being a teenager and feeling all of these strange over-complicated emotions despite not having to worry about anything all that more complex than school (although, Jesper does experience some loss). But also being able to experience it in the framework of exploring a beautiful Norwegian island, making new friends, rather than, er... walking around an American mall, sipping a smoothie, with friends you don't even like, because hopping on a boat to a remote island wasn't an option. I only wish the island in Embracelet were bigger, that there were more folks to meet, more hangout sessions with your two new friends. All interlaced with even more magic and mystery. Maybe more complex puzzles, although the very light puzzles were fine. I could envision this game being so much more - but it was a chill three hour experience, and I have no real complaints. It was a delight.Also, Jesper is a bit of an environmental terrorist, which made me laugh, but I don't think I was supposed to??

_childDocuments_.review: A gentle, touching, atmospheric puzzle-adventure with nice writing and music. Fans of games like Night in The Woods and Oxenfree will feel at home, though Embracelet is shorter and less substantial than both. Fans of point-and-click adventures will enjoy it too.For those who are worried about this game having platforming or action game elements: There is no jumping or shooting here (no jump button, even). I don't remember any challenging action sections. I didn't need to use the sprint button unless I simply wanted to move faster. There were no timing-based movement sections where you'd fail or die if you didn't move quickly enough. I was never in danger of dying though slow reactions on my part. In fact, I'm not sure if it's even possible to die in the game. Arguably, using the bracelet itself might feel tricky for some users because it's mildly reaction-based, where you press a single button when two moving circles line up, but there's sufficient build-up beforehand and I only missed a few times. There's no penalty for missing, you just try again immediately. I played with an XBox controller and everything worked smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a narrative driven adventure game about a 17 year old boy discovering the mysteries of a mysterious bracelet on a small island in the North. It's a charming experience made by a one man team. I haven't played their previous game, but as a fan of story driven adventure games I had to give this one a go. Embracelet is longer than your typical indie "walking simulator" taking about 3-5 hrs compared to a typical 1-2, and it uses its time wisely.  For the majority of the experience your left to your own devices discovering mysteries at your own leisure. You can choose to pursue further on particular topics, and solve problems from the handful of island residents. It reminded me a lot of "Boku no Natsuyasumi" (My Summer Vacation) series with how your spending your vacation in a quiet small island with a lot of the sound effects just being the sound of birds or the wind. It being an adventure game there are puzzles and dialog trees to click through and Embracelet does a decent job on both. A majority of the obstacles in the game can be solved by using the power of your bracelet which has the ability to move/push/destroy objects. None of the puzzles are particularly challenging but they do provide some thought to keep things engaging. I do wish there was more to the bracelet with every action being executed with a timing button press. As for the decision making its very simple dialog trees with a majority not changing much of anything, but create some nice flavoring to the main character, Jesper's personality. There are two endings but they seem entirely based on a simple hangout session you may have between one of your friends. Embracelet's biggest problem is it's lack of time cohesion, which sounds silly on the surface, but does create in a sudden jolty narrative experience. Jesper's time on the island is planned to be a week, but the entirety of the first day is a huge chunk of the game with the last third suddenly shifting between days without any awareness. A simple title card or scene of Jesper going to bed would add a lot. The only other issue being that the games narrative swerves into different directions so suddenly. The final outcome of the mystery is interesting but it happens all too fast that it left it feeling a bit too abrupt to my liking, and if you can ignore some silly story beats that require "don't worry about it" you are still left with a solid experience.Overall, I'm really happy I played Embracelet. I couldn't help but be drawn into its charming little world. It's a well written story with a endearing little cast. Despite the hang ups I still recommend the trip out into the quaint little island in the North. PROS+ well written branching dialog+ Fun open ended exploration and puzzle solving + endearing small cast of characters+ Beautiful Soundtrack creates the perfect atmosphere + Satisfying lengthNEUTRAL+/-  The bracelet mechanic is really basic and doesn't ever do anything new CONS- Inconsistent sense of time- The final act happens so suddenly and ends abruptly- Jasper gets stuck on terrain a lot when highlighting objects8/10
