_childDocuments_.review: A Visual novel, that would have benefited from a voiceover if not for the fact that it's a long game with loads of dialog. Love, life, death and regret, and even, you know when boys prefer boys. Sabotage, espionage and vandalism interspersed with a side story all about the threats to our beautiful planet fill out the plot. Something for everyone.  Don't let the simple boxy graphics put you off, very good controls and puzzles.The back story follows multiple young people all trapped in circumstance. You must play a part in telling their story. Sure you have to make choices, and some choices and some objects you interact with change the way the story unfolds, but in the story arc it's pretty classic, twists and turns some predictable others not. Very much about having fun and some fantasy and magic lightens the mood of what is otherwise a deadly serious story. I missed a fair few items in my playthrough, and this may be one of very few games that I have time to play through a second time.If you enjoyed this game, you can find other much like it here

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet commits "the deadly sin" of being an adventure game "day dreaming" of being a platformer, but it doesn't irk me too often. The story is touching and intreaguing. Themes like illness, loss, poverty, centralization and sexuality are handled with care and dignity; without becoming ham-fisted. A trio of one-dimensional, brutish and cartoonish antagonists stands in grinding contrast to the generally nuanced writing, but most of the character relationships feels natural, and the charming, quirky townsfolk are quite familiar for anybody growing up at the  Norwegian countryside. The branching character and story paths feels organic and believable, for the most part (I would have traded an "action-movie cliché" sub-plot for more hi-jinks and bonding moments with the main characters). Embracelet is a sweet game, with a simplistic but endearing artstyle and solid soundtrack. It's not "perfect," but has personality and charm.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my. I loved Milkmaid to bits. So I was highly anticipating Mattis' next title. Pretty early on in development I was really disappointed by the choice of the artstyle and the way this game controls: 3D environments and direct character control instead of beautiful pixel art and a point and click gameplay. Now that I have played it I certainly understand the reasons for this choice, since in some parts it does add to the immersion, but all in all I gotta say, I did not like the graphics all that much. They serve a purpose, but all in all the world feels like big chunks of polygons, without much detail, sadly. And don't get me started on the way the character controls. Early on while playing this I almost dropped the game because the character will walk in a circle and continue to walk for nearly ten seconds on one spot when you simply try to access a hotspot you stand right at a second time. It's infuriating.I also think the story does not make a lot of sense either and to me the explanation for everything in the end felt very lackluster. Still it is engaging enough to make you continue playing and wanting to discover more of the world you're in and how the relations play out.However, I did like this enough to actually finish the game. It has the same magic and spirit that made me love Milkmaid so much and I think I'm falling in love with Norway thanks to Machineboy's games. It's hard to put a finger on what it actually is that makes this game shine despite its flaws, but in the end it doesn't matter: it just shines. Must be the love that has been poured into it from its developer ;)So thanks for another trip into your beautiful world, Mattis. I am looking forward to your next creation.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished *Embracelet* by the developer who did *Milkmaid of the Milky Way* and really liked it.  This is one of those slow paced story games that left me a bit teary at times.  The main game mechanic for actions is clicking/hitting the button as two circles match up, and your can set the difficulty level in Options.  I had mine set right at the middle and only missed when I wasn’t paying attention.  Easy to play with a controller but doesn’t seem like it would be too difficult with keyboard/mouse.    There are things you need to do to move ahead with the story, but there are optional tasks too.  I found I missed one of these, but could get that in another playthrough.  I was going slow and it took me 5 hours to play.  Playing again to experience things I missed and choose a different ending would go faster.  There are three endings.  Only one autosave though so one would need to start over to get all the achievements and the different endings.  I thought the game was just beautiful and was very glad I played it.  I hate to compare games because the stories told are very different, but if you like the pacing and focus on story in games like *To the Moon* or *Last Day of June* you would likely enjoy *Embracelet* very much.  There’s a demo, so no reason not to give it a try.  I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a sweet narrative adventure in the vein of Life is Strange. You play a teenager who finds a magical bracelet and heads back to the fishing village where his grandfather grew up to learn more about the family history and discover the origin of the artifact. It's set in Norway, which is not a common location for games, and that makes it feel a bit special. The characters are all kind to one another, and although the bad guys are a bit over-the-top, the obvious villainy gives it a bit of a feeling like a Famous Five story or Tintin or something. You know the baddies will lose and you're going to make it through just fine, which is exactly the way a light adventure yarn should go.The most annoying part of the game is the controls because you cannot control the camera and sometimes it swings around to really inconvenient locations that lead you walking back in the opposite direction you were just walking in. There is an especially egregious section near the end where the camera keeps swinging around and then you fall off the thing you were standing on and have to walk all the way back round and start again, over and over. I almost threw my keyboard out the window, but I'm glad I persevered because aside from the annoyance with the controls the story is warm and comforting. If you're looking for a bit of escapist fun, and like the sound of wandering around an island in the fjords helping people, Embracelet is a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a narrative and expressive 3D adventure in third person view with low poly graphic style. It was developed by Mattis Folkestad, founder of the one man studio Machineboy in Norway; he composed even the soundtrack. It is commendable that an indie author has ventured into the difficult task of developing a narrative and expressive game with few financial and human resources; that’s the reason why the game is worth of our attention. Let me say that the experiment is totally successful. I’m very happy that Mattis submitted a copy of the game to my curator page on Steam; it’s very rare to receive games as good as this one. You can play it also on Nintendo Switch.Embracelet tells the “bildungsroman” of 17 y.o. Jesper living in Oslo with his mother; he has never known his father, who died before Jesper was born. Jesper is in the middle of an adolescential crisis, he is no longer interested in school and has no friends, his beloved grandfather is seriuosly ill and is going to die. Before to die, grandfather gives him a magic bracelet, with the power to manipulate the world around him, and a mission to accomplish: travel to Slepp island where grandfather lived when he was young and unravel the mistery of the magic bracelet. In the past Sleep was a thriving community based on fishing and tourism; now it is almost uninhabited, and voracious oil companies are compromising its delicate ecosystem. In Slepp Jesper will meet Karoline and Hermod and together they will have an unforgettable summer full of incredible adventures, friendship and love that will change their lives forever.Superpowers, adolescence, coming of age story, loss, friendship, love, family, ecology, narrative game… Does it ring the bell? Obviously yes, Embracelet is clearly inspired by Life Is Strange. However they are two completely different games and experiences. It has even something of Oxenfree (adolescence, magic elements and comics ballons) and of Night In The Woods (existential crisis, the decadent town of Possum Spring and comics ballons). Mattis Folkestad could not rely on motion captured actors; he did a great job by animating every single hand drawn character in the hand drawn game world. Mattis worked as cartoons designer in the past, I found on the web one of the project he worked for: Embracelet comes with a lot of divinely animated NPCs; the intense human relationships that the player establishes with the characters are the real strength of the game. Not by chance the title comes from the verb “embrace“. I didn’t think it was possible to get attached to characters and places just sketched in a low poly style; yet at the end of the game there remains a sense of nostalgia for not being able to experience new adventures with your virtual friends in the fascinating low poly world. The hand drawn visuals are magnificent, able to create a contemplative atmosphere and make you forget the low poly graphics or, maybe, just because of the low poly art! The beautiful soundtrack helps to build a pleasant, peaceful, poetic mood. Divinely written texts and multiple choice dialogues help to estabilish strong and empathetic relationships with the characters. As consequence, the absence of acting voices is not a limit: while reading the comic balloons, it seems to hear the voices of the characters!Gameplay comes with a weird feature: you cannot control the camera. Usually we are used to control camera with the right stick in 3D games. Here the camera is programmed to follow your avatar Jesper so that he is always at the center of the frame. Outdoors or in large places, camera is executing programmed “dollies”, following Jesper from behind or from the side, from near or from afar; indoors or in small places, camera position is fixed but it is programmed to rotate for following Jesper. So you cannot rotate the view, visual is determined by programmed camera following your avatar movements. At first I was perplexed by this feature, then I realized it allows the author to determine always the best view, just like directors do in movies; at the same time it integrates with the player’s freedom of movement. In this way the aesthetic beauty of the view remains consistent throughout the game, it’s a good compromise of cinema and game! It helps a lot to build the beautiful contemplative and expressive mood of the experience. You can see the best result of this technique in the “running for love” interactive sequence. Thanks to this technique the game switches seamless between gameplay sequences and cut scenes. Maybe here cut scene is the wrong term; you have sequences where you can control Jesper, and sequences where you cannot control Jesper; transition is highlighted by the upcoming of two horizontal black bars at the top and at the bottom of the screen, just like in movies. However animations are built in game engine, there is no visual difference between interactive sequences and not-interactive sequences. AI moves Jesper from the position where you left him to the position programmed by the author. Everything is so smooth and seamless. To say the truth in some scenes you can still interact, you can select the different options of multiple choice dialogues or use the superpower of the bracelet or do other limited actions; maybe the best term is scripted sequences. I wrote here about the need to find new techniques for managing the camera as result of player’s interactivity and programmed AI such to grant always the best view; and even of the importance of scripted sequences in interactive narrative. Embracelet is a good achievement in the right direction. Some commentators complained about the programmed camera movements; in my opinion the programmed camera works fine, provided that player follows the peaceful and slow mood of the game. If you want to run, go fast and play in a hurry, the slow camera struggles to follow Jesper and place itself in the right point of view in short time. My suggestion is: enjoy the contemplative and peaceful atmosphere of the experience, give time to time.Continue here:

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, chill coming-of-age adventure game set primarily on a northern Norwegian isle. The title follows Jesper, a 17-year-old kid from the city who is gifted a mysterious bracelet by his grandfather shortly before his passing and goes off to his grandfather's childhood home to discover its origins. Along the way he meets and befriends two similarly-aged-youths and explores the secrets of the island and the bracelet's past. Embracelet is an overall chill title, largely being somewhere between a walking simulator and a point-and-click adventure title with no time-intensive or pressuring portions. There are some latter segments that require a small amount of platforming, which while forgiving when making a mistake are a bit frustrating due to the controls not being well-suited to precision movement. Achievements are relatively easy to obtain, though there are ending variations that require another playthrough to acquire. Jesper also does on occasion notably get stuck on the environment and ends up teleporting to his intended pathing destination, which is a little jarring but both infrequent a serviceable solution.The game's narrative, its setting, and its artistic direction, a gorgeous and vibrant low-poly style, are its strongest points. The narrative is much as any coming-of-age title, but Jesper and his interactions with others carry a genuine and realistic weight to them that is appreciable in a genre often decorated by excessive melodrama. In simpler terms, it largely reminds of a very chill and calming young adult novel. The setting is refreshing, taking place in what is very distinctly rural modern-day Norway, and the art style helps provide a simplistically minimalist but vivid and rich depiction of it. The one of the two biggest weakness of the narrative, though, are that there is a distinct lack of time cohesion given that game's plot seems to begin to jump from day to day without abandon or notice at a point despite Jesper only going to sleep once on his week-long trip. The second weakness is that I feel a bit more time could have spent with the various characters of the island, though that is more of a compliment to how I much I want more from the narrative rather than it feeling empty or unfufilling. A bit more structure to the overall narrative and a few additional moments/ interactions/ etc. with the cast would go a long to improving the narrative, but the narrative that is there is strong in and of itself.In the end, Embracelet is a title that is refreshing and enjoyable experience that I have found myself coming back to every now and again (to the point where I have bought it both on Steam and on Switch). It is not a revolutionary title by any means and certainly does hold a few faults of its own, but it is overall a fairly high quality game made by one person and one that I will sooner say positive things about then otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely experience this was, an absolute joy to play! Embracelet is a game about growing up, finding your own way, making your own choices and finding people that you want to keep in your life, and all that wrappeed in a beautiful story about visiting Slepp, a remote Norwegian island. I was genuinely surprised by the amount of gameplay and story (~4 hrs for me) there was, and none of it felt like filler or drawn out content. I also can't believe this whole game was made by one single person; I applaud them for it! Definitely recommended if you're looking for a fun and wholesome game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, engaging, and fun game which I would recommend to anyone looking for a casual, story driven game that they can get through in one sitting (providing their definition of 'one sitting' is somewhere up to 5 hours, which is about how long it took me to complete).The game has a number of different endings, which is good, but it's not really a game I would consider super replayable, which is less good, because if you want to see the different endings, you have to replay the game.There were a couple of times during my playthough that I had no idea how to advance the game, so I wandered around in circles interacting with everything I could, but I also forgot that there was a button I could press that highlighted objects of interest until I was almost finished with the game, so I can't rule out that it was my fault.Overall, I really enjoyed this game, though. Check it out if you get the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: First i would like to say i REALLY enjoyed playing this game.Both the story and atmosphere kept me immersed to the very end.Also the attention to details as querky as they might be made me smile on more than one occasion. Like the "buss for tog", the old coin slot machine, which i guess you need to be of age to remember, the doorbell and not at least the outgoing personality that is so typicals for northeners .Highly reccommended

_childDocuments_.review: A new addition to the growing genre of "teenager visits island", with some kindred feeling to Mutazione and Oxenfree, though stylistically more along the lines of Wide Ocean Big Jacket.It's at its very best when it's just about the atmosphere, people and landscapes of Northern Norway. Less so when it tries for "action scenes", deeper lore, or awkward platforming. Wide Ocean knew to stick to what it does well, whereas some choices here are a bit less fortunate. Still, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this to anyone looking for a nice 3-hour vacation up in the fjords.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful solemn game with simple but unique functions that differ from the adventure genre norm. Camera shot vistas that are breathtaking, music filled with mellow goodness, and a story that tugs at the heartstrings. Another wonderful solo-effort to inspire budding generations who want to create their own message in a videogame.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible adventure, full of heart and charm.  Note that a previous reviewer is wrong, this is perfectly playable with a mouse & keyboard (just change in the settings before you start the game).Lovely graphics, a beautiful piano-led orchestral soundtrack, and a rich story with excellent characters.  I will remember this one for a long time.  My only complaint is there are some dodgy camera angles, but you soon get used to this and it doesn't detract at all from what is a superbly directed story and a well-flowing game.  The puzzles are simple - but I like that. I loved this from start to finish, taking around 4 hours total to complete.  Possibly my Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely enchanting! A coming of age drama on an island in northern Norway. With beautifully written characters, a picturesque landscape and a thrilling story (subtitles available)! With just under 4 hours a little on the short side, but there was not one minute of boredom...If you came here and actually took the time to read the reviews, chances are very high that you will like this game a lot. Don't be afraid of the platforming sections , they were pretty easy to master...
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy, different and heartfelt game, Embracelet will feel a bit generic and shallow in the beginning (edit: to be clear, I refer to the introduction here, before he reaches the island community and the game really starts), but it's well worth your time. The depiction of Slepp, a remote northern Norwegian island community, feels authentic and helps set the game apart, and the music, which was composed by the developer, helps set the mood, too.The game clearly draws inspiration from Night in the Woods (the speech bubbles are an obvious homage), and manages to capture some of that game's charm and atmosphere, while also exploring the "struggling hometown" theme in its own distinct way, while telling an interesting story along the way. My main story complaint is that the characters could have had more depth and personality, and the dialogue feels a bit stilted at times.The pacing mostly holds up, although there are a couple fetch quests that feel a bit drawn out, and some platforming sections with at times awkward camera angles and tricky controls if you use WASD instead of a gamepad. Most of the puzzles are pretty simple, but there are a couple fun and challenging ones. The game is played in 4-5 hours, about the length of a Life is Strange-episode, and the story is beautiful.If you want a game to relax with, with an interesting story, you should give Embracelet a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Nice story, nice environment and characters.Really casual game, with somewhat engaging gameplay.However, what matters is the feeling of attachement to your character and those around him, you go on an adventure with many different feelings. Even some good jokes in there, maybe especially relatable for those from Northern-Norway.Most people could enjoy this game if they gave themselves time to play through it. Took me 4-5 hours, missing some extra tasks.

Jesper's life changes when his grandfather gives him a magical bracelet, capable of changing the world around him. We fell in love with this game immediately because of its atmosphere, emotion, and great writing. Please see my video for my full feelingsThank you

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is an adventure game set in Northern Norway - a unique coming of age story about love, loss, friendship and family - and a magical bracelet with mysterious powers. Embracelet is a puzzle adventure game with a gripping story, gentle and satisfying puzzles, exploration and a beautiful, orchestral soundtrack. You play as Jesper, a Norwegian teenager who lives with his mom in the city. One day he is handed an old bracelet by his Grandfather who grew up in a fishing community up north. This bracelet has powers - strange, mysterious powers. Jesper is given the task to unravel the mystery behind the bracelet. Where does it come from? Who does it belong to? And why did his Grandfather leave the island and his old life behind?

name: Cult of the Lamb
detailed_description: Cult of the Lamb: Unholy Alliance Crusade through dungeons, slay heretics, build your cult, and seek new powers together. But there’s more. As well as the addition of co-op play, the Unholy Alliance expansion also adds new tarot cards, relics, buildings, fleeces, follower traits, follower quests, and other secrets to discover! Double trouble Experience the entire Cult of the Lamb campaign in local co-op, with one player inhabiting the role of the Lamb and the other taking on the mantle of the Goat. Enjoy new 2-player twists on existing minigames like fishing and knucklebones, and choose from a selection of corrupted weapons, tarot cards, curses, and relics as you embark on co-op crusades. Cult of personality Unholy Alliance adds a huge number of new follower traits, making your flock more diverse, unpredictable, and charismatic than ever. Cultists can be insomniacs, bust law-breaking friends out of prison, enter a catatonic state after the trauma of a resurrection, or become afflicted with a curse: and that’s just a tiny handful of the quirks you’ll encounter as your cult grows. Power play Take your crusades to the next level with Unholy Alliance’s godlike selection of new relics and tarot cards—some of which have been designed with co-op in mind. The Lamb and the Goat can swap weapons, deal extra damage when fighting back-to-back, or deal a critical hit if their attacks are in sync. Solo players also get a heap of new powers and abilities to play with. Cult of the Lamb: Sins of the Flesh The Lamb must lead, and Followers must follow in Sins of the Flesh, a free content expansion for Cult of the Lamb. As your followers indulge in worldly pleasures, choose their prideful customizable outfits, and treat them to a gluttony of vacation juice, you might find that life may hatch from an egg. Alongside a new levelling system, new mechanics, new quests, and improved quality-of-life features, the Lamb has uncovered a new combat weapon to blast the heretics of the Old Faith. This power can be yours if you yield to the Sins of the Flesh. Sins and Disciples New progression systems add more depth and complexity to managing the Cult of the Lamb. By following the sinful path, your followers will delight in gluttonous rituals, vain buildings, and wrathful doctrines. Invite your most loyal Followers to the inner circle of Disciples, a revamped levelling system of Follower progression. Better Cult Life Shiny poop, baneful brooms, and bigger, better buildings improve busy Cult life. Shiny poops have special effects, like yielding fruitful crops and adding XP to your broom. Levelling up your broom will make chores faster and more effective. To improve automation, there’s also a new tier for the Janitor Station and the Storage Structures so your Followers will take better care of themselves. Ready, Aim, Fire Blast heretics away with the new Blunderbuss weapon. When loaded, it fires big damage in close quarters to bring a new combat playstyle for your crusades. If you charge it up even more with a heavy attack, you can aim to snipe enemies from long range. Outfits, Options and Offspring! Each of your cultists can flaunt their Follower fashion at the new Tailor building. Once unlocked, each cultist can wear their own outfit, with 23 different styles to choose from. But your Cult is getting even more unique. When two Followers love each other very much, they might find an egg. Nurture the egg for it to hatch, then care for the offspring until they're ready to pledge allegiance to your Cult! Cult of the Lamb x Don't Starve Together Don’t let the Lamb starve in this crossover update with Don’t Starve Together! We’ve cooked up a whole new game mode, new themed decorations, and a new follower form to satisfy your hunger. Survival Mode The ails of mortality plague the Lamb in Penitence mode. Eating. Sleeping. You will learn how your followers struggle to survive. But a simple bed isn’t enough for a great leader. The Leader Tent is the perfect place to get your beauty sleep. An Arachnid’s Allegiance Webber arrives from the world of Don’t Starve Together. Can you unwrap the quest to convert them to your cult? They just don’t starve! New Crossover Decorations From homages to the Deerclops and Pig society, to base necessities like the science machine and alchemy engine, you can customize your cult with a whole set of decorations from Don’t Starve Together. Cult of the Lamb: Relics of the Old Faith The Lamb must keep their Cult flourishing, their Followers faithful, and their power unchallenged as they crusade in this free content expansion, Relics of the Old Faith. It adds brand new ways to spread the gospel of the Cult of the Lamb with powerful new abilities, exciting new characters, and thrilling new challenges. Delve into the shrouded history of the Lands of the Old Faith as the Lamb fights to conquer those who would question their power. New Cult buildings will appease your Followers while new combat abilities will smite opposing heretics. Uncover the secrets of the Old Faith so you can be the God you want to be in this massive content expansion! New Combat The expansion brings a deeper layer to dungeon crawling for new and returning players. With powerful Relic abilities, heavy attacks for each weapon class, and dozens of items to find, the Lamb will unleash delightful devastation. New Postgame Another challenge awaits after completing the main story. Revamped dungeons, mysterious characters and challenging boss encounters are in your new quest as the God of Death. Along the way, you can unlock Follower forms, fleeces, unchosen doctrines and more. New Challenges Put your skills to the test with several new challenge modes for combatively competent Cult leaders. Boss Rush, Permadeath and other unique challenges await after defeating the final boss. About the Game Cult of the Lamb casts players in the role of a possessed lamb saved from annihilation by an ominous stranger, and must repay their debt by building a loyal following in his name. Start your own cult in a land of false prophets, venturing out into diverse and mysterious regions to build a loyal community of woodland Followers and spread your Word to become the one true cult. BUILD YOUR FLOCK Collect and use resources to build new structures, perform dark rituals to appease the gods, and give sermons to reinforce the faith of your flock. DESTROY THE NON-BELIEVERS Explore a sprawling, randomly generated world, fight off hordes of enemies and defeat rival cult leaders in order to absorb their power and assert your cult's dominance. SPREAD YOUR WORD Train your flock and embark on a quest to explore and discover the secrets of four mysterious regions. Cleanse the non-believers, spread enlightenment, and perform mystical rituals on the journey to become the mighty lamb god.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. So addicting to play. The cult community building and the rough-lite dungeon crawling parts of the game compliment each other so well. I really like how you can choose what portion of the game you wan't to focus on. You can either view it as a rouge-lite first and view the cult building as something to use your loot in and to upgrade your abilities; or you can view it as a cult building game first and view the rouge-lite portion as a way to gather resources for your cult. Very good concept executed very well!

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is the perfect game for anyone who's ever wanted to start their own religion... or just really likes possessed sheep. The randomly generated world and roguelike elements keep things fresh and challenging, and the ability to collect and indoctrinate followers (including other animals) adds a whole new level of strategy. Plus, the ominous deity you're trying to appease is just the right amount of creepy. I laughed, I cried, I convinced a cow to worship me. 10/10, would start a cult again.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best way to describe this game isyeah it did a lot of everything, but none of it well enough.This game has so much potential with updates and patches but as it is now, for a rogue lite I feel it pales in comparison to the ones that come before it. The art style and soundtrack really carry this one.I had a wonderful time playing it but I can just FEEL, it could have been and still can be so much more refined.- Still riddled with bugs- You should not have to hold 'e' for every action you do- Combat feels clunky even with a controller- some weapons and curses clearly feel so much better than others- Most tarot cards are useless and are gimicky (i.e. roll into enemies to do damage or poison them on hit, they do not do enough damage to dent any enemy in the game)- There is a clear winner when it comes to which cape is better (hint its the yellow and white one, the rest suck)- Base building is incredibly clunky and the terrain layout is weird, sucks you cant move your shrine.- Loyalty and the entire cult member management system feels flat and everyone feels disposable, no real punishment for anything.- Commandments you get too quicky imo- No reason to fully upgrade your base / cult level because you can finish the game well before that- most cult upgrades are useless (i.e missionary, confessional, etc)This one is the biggest one for me: Post game I dont feel like i have anything to do, and for a rogue lite thats the biggest downfall of all.Played on Hard difficulty aswell just as a side note.- The difficulty scale wasnt really with how hard the game got but more with how little health you had to work with which felt very artificial. There wasnt enough of a sense of progression in difficulty at all.- The bosses all felt so easy, especially the bishops which were supposed to be these godly terrors, beat the final boss in 2 tries while the 3rd bishop took me 4. Just... man.I still enjoyed my experience, id rate it 7/10 (closer to a 6/10 moreso) because i was just ATTACHED to this while i was playing it, i woke up with an itch to play it again.Id pick this up on sale. TLDR

_childDocuments_.review: Someone looked at animal crossing new horizons and said, "there's not enough demonic cult activity in this game" and I absolutely love them for it. Keeping tabs on followers while crusading is quite nice, as now the followers can kinda 'take care of themselves'. My one problem with the game is the fighting. _childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a roguelite action game part community management game and while both are undeniably fun and engaging to do, Cult of the Lamb feels like it eventually runs out of steam rather than both elements combining to create a game climax of sorts. Regardless, Cult of the Lamb does what so many of it's kin fail to do. Be a game that creates a story in of itself. Your dwarf fortress, your Stardew Valley's, Issac's and Risk of Rain's. Cult of the Lamb deserves to be held in a regard as high as it, even if it doesn't quite have the depth of any of those.The Roguelite experience will range on luck, your personal skill and the difficult you set at the start of the game. Most of it functioning as an expedition of sorts rather than an endless plundering of loot as time progresses outside of it. Affecting the community management portion of the game. Try not to stay out too long lest people start starving or someone revolts against you. It's when you start mak decisions that affect the other side of the coin that the game gets addicting. Do i go this path and get extra wood that i can use to build a lumberyard or do i get fertilizer for my garden? Maybe get extra coin so i can unlock more tarot cards to empower myself during a crusade? (your standard roguelite run) You always need bones for rituals and crusades are your primary source of that, so always be expected to dive into this from time to time. The combat is very simple, if you've played Binding of Isaac with it's heart system then it's very similar. You have varied weapons and they function differently in swing speed to suit your personal playstyle on dodging/attacking. They come in different variants, like lifesteal on kill or summoning ghosts on kill that unlock as you progress. I don't entirely know how to feel about it to be honest, a part of me wants to say that it's fun because it is but it's also very shallow in places and outside of making decisions like what tarot cards you choose during a crusade or which route to go. It's not that exciting. The community building aspect is frankly amazing, think animal crossing except you treat your villagers like subordinates. Fodder for the fire but with a friendly smile. Food can be an issue but don't worry if someone dies. You can feed their body in an act of cannibalism and with the right upgrade it can be a great boon. Sacrificing your followers is common and necessary as they do eventually get old and die. So you're incentivized to sacrifice or murder them because dead bodies are bad hygiene. Bad hygiene means followers get sick. Sick followers mean can't work on my several effigies of the dead deities i slayed last tuesday. Holy god these people have hygiene issues. Let me tell you. Some of them actually ENJOY eating poop. I can literally serve them a bowl of poop and they will go to town on it the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ animals. They'll be little ♥♥♥♥♥ at times and kick up a fuss because they are "Hungry" and "need food to survive" or they'll be "Upset" that their "friends" were sacrificed to the being above which was totally necessary dude. I spent the points on making sure there was a toliet installed then spent the points on a prison so i could prison the people who kicked up a fuss bout it. I labeled all of my followers after food items, because i would brutally murder them and then use their corpses for food. I HAD a farm it's just like bro. Once you go for cannibalism and you see the upside to cannibalism. Well, you can't hold back. Old people are meat dude. Who even CARES? You can literally resurrect them anyway! That guy you just ate for dinner? Yeah i just brought him back to life. His name is Mince because he went into your lasagne. You can fish which takes awhile but it's worth it in the early game. Easy meat. I'd love to clutch on cannibalism any day of the week but there are a lot more fish in the sea than people who'll literally die to be in your spaghetti carbonara for you. If you're annoyed at certain villages for pooping literally in front of the toliet, you can just send them away on a mission for a few days to get new followers or meat or whatever.So i literally had a quest where Mince my boy wanted to prank another dude, Beef Burger. I'm so influential that i can make people eat poop so you can see where this is going. I tell Beef Burger to eat poop. He literally eats the whole bowl without a hesitation. Hell, he drops everything he is doing just to go and eat that bowl of poop for me. The real kicker is after getting him to eat poop ANOTHER time. Mince decided he enjoyed eating poop too, he ate it all with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ smile on his face. Beef Burger got eaten, so like you know how that one ended out. I resurrected Mince many times and he's my second hand dude.Another one. I have this old dude. Meat. He's a simple old dude, he was originally fodder that i was going to use for more food. Now you have cooldowns on sacrificial rituals and i needed to get rid of old people. So i had him fight a younger dude, Stew. Here's the insane thing. This 54 year old pig managed to murder a young rabbit dude just with his bare fists. I blinked stupified and then just said screw it and put Stew to death for humiliating the concept of one of the oldest known meals in human history. Alright, so i'm like "damn so what do i do now, he's still an old guy.". There is a meal in the game known as Deadly Dish. Now this thing has a 75% of killing the follower, but gives you resources upon consumption. It also gives you faith if your community are cannibals but i digress. HE SURVIVES THE 75%. I say ♥♥♥♥ it i'm just gonna wait until the cooldown is done and ascend this guy. He dodged death TWICE and i just had to ascend him. Dude has several other followers named after him as a second name. Hopefully this gives you a taste (heh) on what you can expect out of the community building in this game. It's an experience to behold and is well worth the price of admission.  There have been plenty of elements i've not spoiled in this review and there are plenty of surprises to be found that are just best found yourself.My only big downside with the game is that it doesn't feel like there is enough in it. Not in the way that you'd expect though, i want more dammit! It's like having a really nice meal and wanting seconds. Cult of the Lamb doesn't have seconds but holy god do i want some. Cannibalism optional. Expand the roguelite system a little, it feels like there could be more done there but keep rolling with the mad stuff here. Give it a sequel or expansion, i don't care. I just want more.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I'll just come out of the gate and say it like it is, is this game hard? No not really, at least compared to most other roguelites this game is fairly forgiving and on the easy side. Is this game even a roguelite? Yes but I feel like the main appeal is the base building moreso than combat, as the split seems at least 50/50 between the two gameplay loops.However this is not at all to say I disliked the game, in fact it was very enjoyable. While it can be very easy to breeze through the game if you are experienced in other roguelite/bullet hell games while taking few deaths or hits, it is still a very enjoyable game for someone like me, who tends to get bored of base builder games and I even found myself wishing I had a bigger base to build more stuff. Case in point being that if you are a fan of the roguelite or builder genre then I recommend you pick this game up, not only is it cute but the gameplay isn't too bad and even if you're a hardcore roguelite expert you might still enjoy the time you spend on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game. At first I thought I thought some mechanics or repeated sounds were going to annoy me but it feels like they took that into consideration and instead I find myself adoring all of the sounds they make. The mechanics I thought I'd find annoying are actually more fleshed out than I realized. I was even on edge on the art style at first but now I believe it is a perfect fit for this game and wouldn't have it any other way.I rarely ever find myself going into a game and thinking "I should beat this on the hardest mode!" but I've enjoyed all of this enough that I am going to be playing a save for Med, Hard, and Very Hard each. I don't think I've ever played a game and knew for sure that I don't regret a penny spent within 14 hours of playing aside one other instance.If I had to make any complaint it would be when the heals drop just out of my reach to grab but it doesn't happen much (maybe 2 times so far?) and hasn't costed me a run either. With all the fixes I saw them doing I have high hopes that it will be patched one day if that isn't suppose to be there. From what I have seen this game has the potential to be the kind of game where it gets repeated content updates to add more. _childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is one of the best roguelikes I’ve ever played. I love all the aesthetic aspects of it: the art style, animations, and audios. The cultists are very cute and charismatic. As for the gameplay, it’s as good as it is hard sometimes! But don’t despair! You also have a good sense of progression. As long as you persist and take care of the cult, you’ll feel you are growing in power and things start to get a lot easier, as all good roguelikes should be.My favorite aspect of the game is dealing with your cultists and their interactions with you and among themselves. It is incredibly fun, even more so when you stream it due to its Twitch integration. However, dealing with your cult itself can be really time-consuming. You can’t simply go on your runs without fearing a total disaster when you come back (believe me!), so you must make sure things will sustain themselves when you are out there. It was not so easy for me; I would have liked to go on more runs, but I felt stuck with the cult sometimes.The game is almost perfect, but I’d improve task management if I could. Maybe if we had a menu showing your followers and their respective tasks, and the possibility to change roles through it, that would make things easier.Cult of the Lamb is updated very often, and most of its new content is delivered for free, which is amazing! I’m glad this game exists. Thank you so much to Massive Monster and Devolver for this gem. You can count on me as your faithful cultist! ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: You are a Lamb who was excecuted, and brought back to life, and now you’re a cult leader, seeking revenge upon those who killed you, and free the one who brought you back.Cult of the Lamb is a cute game with cute character designs, and it’s weird how well it fits with it’s dark theme (sacrifice and death etc).It has nice soundtracks, and it’s combat mechanics are just smooth, it feels really good to play.The gameplay alternates between hardcore fighting and chill cult management. You can easily forget about life for hours straight while building, upgrading, preaching and playing god on your cult.I never used it, but it has a nice Twitch integration, you can name your followers after your real Twitch follower’s usernames, and they can vote about decisions in the game. It’s the closest thing to really playing with the chat.From the beginning it’s very addictive, it has a nice progression and an interesting enough New Game +, making the monsters harder, and adding new moves to the bosses, a new gamemode and depending on your late game choices, a more complete conclusion. it’s worth playing.It’s very creative the fact that each character has their own fictional language, for us it’s just some random goofy noises but it makes sense in that world. I played only on Extra Hard and it was challenging, maybe I could’ve 100% it way sooner on easier difficulties.Where the game really shines is your freedom of choices, what kind of cult leader you’ll be, and even having so many possible solutions for the same problems, for example: Your followers are hungry. You can: harvest berries and cook something; go fishing; unlock upgrades that let you make food out of grass; make a feast ritual; make a ritual where they will not eat or be hungry for 3 days; decrete that cannibalism is acceptable so they can eat dead followers meat... it gives you a lot of autonomy and freedom.Thre are different possible gamestyles with your fleeces and curses, whether you want to play like a mage focused on using curses, or maybe equip a berserker fleece that makes your hits 10x stronger but you die with 1 hit of anything. There are a lot of options and each one is very different and fun to try.I’ve been wanting to play this game so bad, and it was really worth the price.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb you did it again! This might as well be the best game I have ever played in my entire life! So what the rouge like elements are really easy even on the harder difficulties. So what if the majority of the bosses in this game are just some cute blob that occasionally shoots stuff at you and then leaves after you do one tick of damage so that they can spawn 20 enemies on you. I simply could care less. The thrill of having my own cute animal cult and killing them in the most horrendous ways possible makes up for that completely and perfectly satisfies my narcissistic god complex!!!! You can to anything you want to those lemmings. Feed them poop and grass, extort their entire life savings out of them, make them kill each other for your own amusement, and once they are dead, you simply bring them back to life and start all over again. No matter what I do to them they still love me, and that's more that my parents ever did for me. So basically, you should buy Cult of the Lamb, Developed by Massive Monster, Published by Devolver Digitial. Even if the game is shallow it still brought me joy in my empty husk of a life, and hopefully they like... idk update the game to make the dungeons a tad bit better

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 15 now. My son got this game from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 12 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his controller. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelites are now a field so crowded that you need something special to make it genuinely captivating to repeat dangerous dungeons over and over and over again while accruing incremental changes. Cult of the Lamb’s answer to this is to lace the game with irreverent cult humour, add a light city builder/social manager layer to break the monotony and to make every character into a whimsically cute cartoon animal. And what do you know - it’s the most fun I’ve had with a roguelite since Dungeons of Dredmor and stands head and shoulders above most entries into the genre.I was going to leave the review there but I do have to elaborate slightly on the actual cult simulation side of the game and simply compliment how much fun it is to manage your little flock of faithful followers, controlling their daily lives according to your whims as they spend their days toiling and worshipping (and with the latest content patch, happily sinning) for you. While the action sequences are great, I found the cult simulator sections in-between so engaging that often I found myself more excited to spend more time with my little guys when logging on. The micromanagement isn’t burdensome and can be relaxed to cater to the player’s needs (and I do recommend toggling on the setting to stop time in the village whenever you go into a dungeon) so it never overstays its welcome - and in fact, I could imagine enjoying an alternative version of this game that fully focuses on this aspect in greater detail over the 50/50 split is now. It’s a lot of great fun and nicely breaks the tension between the more intense dungeon running.

It becomes pretty clear, pretty quickly, which ones are best, and the combat is not expansive or interesting enough to keep me going, and the camp management also fairly quickly turn into "Get back from dungeon, do a feast, preach, empty outhouses, go again".The TL:DR is that it's fun. If you need a good game to play for a few days it's a great fit, but it gets repetitive fairly quickly, and I'm left with a feeling of "It needs... more". I was doing the well-known perusing of my owned games to pick and play one, and rather than finish it I'd rather write a review, and if you can't keep my interest long enough to complete a game I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been describes as a cross between Animal Crossing and Hades however I don't think it does either one of those game styles very well. The crusades, while only 10 minutes long on average seem meaningless when it comes to your settlement with a combat system that leaves you unsatisfied. The weapons don't offer much in terms of changing up game-play or strategy. You either attack once and then dodge or attack 2 or 3 times with a faster weapon, then dodge. The tarot cards don't change how the game is played either. It never really feels like anything is improving. Also a lot of the rituals and devotion perks just don't matter. Overall it just seems like you simply build things because you can, or perform rituals because they are there, without it really mattering or effecting game-play. Despite the pleasing art style of this game, its lack of variety makes it not worth it to me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a roguelike, and its barely a roguelite. There is no meaningful decision making. The pathing options, the order you unlock them in, and the 'benefits' they provide are virtually meaningless. The combat is basically top down old school Legend of Zelda with a dash of bullet hell. There is almost zero variety in enemies, weapons, perks, and abilities, and there isn't any synergy between any of these things. The sensation of having an incredible run and hitting the lottery and crafting the perfect build is completely absent in this game because there are no builds and no variety with which to even craft one. This game is basically what you would get if you allowed a 12 year old to design Hades, but they were much more interesting in making an even less challenging version of the Sims instead. Don't waste your money. It's not fun and its barely cute.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of those rare games with religious themes. Given the complex nature of religious aesthetics, this game has no doubt nailed what it promised to deliver: the hypocrisy, the fanaticism, the blasphemous practices associated with cults, all of it. However, when it comes to its gameplay, I couldn't help but notice that the developers did not invest as much efforts as they did on aesthetics; it's repetitive and out of balance.It felt as though the developers had a plan to flesh out its gameplay but halted it in the middle; the game still has a great potential for more gameplay elements, but they are simply not implemented yet. This was a bit sad for me because the developers did everything they could to deliver the aesthetics, writing, and worldbuilding, for all of which I had zero complaint and full scale satisfaction. Only if the gameplay was fleshed out, the game would have a phenomenal climax, but in its current state, I can't help but say the game feels rather anti-climactic. and labor-intensive.That being said, I still do recommend this game for general audience, because it perfectly captures the gut-wrenching creepiness of cults in its art. You can also get a rough idea on how hundreds and thousands of people could go insane and do insane things just by playing this game. If you ever found yourself clueless on newspaper articles about some cults doing crazy stuffs just like I did, I believe you would have a quite enlightening experience playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable lamb running an adorable little cult, and stabbing things along the way. Had high hopes going into this considering the hype, and was not disappointed. As a usual cozy management/story type gamer, I was hesitant to see what the combat would be like for me, but (as someone who played entirely on Easy difficulty) it was quite enjoyable, and I found myself improving at the mechanics while enjoying the ride. I definitely will be revisiting this when new content is released.The game ran mostly fine on my potato of a laptop, but a couple bugs did present themselves. There was about a 1/8 chance that I would have to relaunch the game due to it giving me about 1 frame every 2 seconds, but the relaunch fixed this every time. A couple times I was left sitting in an empty combat room waiting for enemies to fall from the ceiling, which they eventually did, but after an uncomfortable amount of time. Lag spikes did occasionally occur especially in the cult compound after reaching 15+ followers, but generally did not affect my playtime experience.All in all, amazing game, great soundtrack, story, and mechanics. A little buggy, but mostly a welcome experience :)

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Graphics }---☐ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☑ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ MS-DOSBeautifully hand-drawn graphics that really support the game design. I found myself constantly really looking at the level design. While repetitive at times (each dungeon doesn't vary that much), the effort built in is something really beautiful. Reminiscent of The Binding Of Isaac, but better. Small tips are given within the design. Unsure what the next room might be? If there are a star and moon, it's a tarot card room. If there is hanging swords and weapons, it's a weapon room. There isn't so many hints that it ruins the surprise or risk of moving into another room, but it offers a fun little extra to an otherwise great experience.---{ Gameplay }---☐ Very good☑ Good☐ It's just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don'tAnimal Crossing meets dungeon rogue-like, and exceptionally integrated. You need to go into the dungeon to find followers, who will then build your devotion, which allows you to return to the dungeons stronger. But on top of that, to keep your followers happy, you need to explore dungeons for resources to bring back to them until they can sustain themselves, and even then, you are still required to trawl dungeons for ingredients for food and buildings. A really well layered approach that doesn't ever feel like you're just grinding a dungeon for materials. There is always multiple things to do at once, and consider before leaving. On top of that, while you are gone, your little cult will suffer deaths, hunger, etc. So you also need to be aware of how long you are spending in a dungeon. Really clever.---{ Audio }---☐ Eargasm☑ Very good☐ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ I'm now deafSoundtrack is fantastic. Really complements the game. I really loved listening to it, and there was enough variety to not be bored.---{ Audience }---☐ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☐ GrandmaSacrificial murder, non-monog marriages, and having to clean up the vomit of your followers after they've seen a dead body and proceeded to ♥♥♥♥ themselves, only to be impressed by their own poo, truly an experience for a cultured person such as yourself. From the *sheepish* look you give yourself cleaning up poo, to hosting a ceremony in which you give your followers psychedelic mushrooms so that they trip for 2 days and love you, whatever you're into, this game has it.---{ PC Requirements }---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computerI have a decent, but older gaming laptop, very very occasional framerate drop, but nothing that broke the game, or frustrated me. I can run CSGO at 60fps perfectly fine, so something a little better than a PC that can run that and you'll be cruisy.---{ Difficulty }---☐ Just press 'W'☐ Easy☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Significant brain usage☐ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsI played on medium difficulty because I like myself. The game was challenging, but never throw-your-controller. Deaths are reasonably punished, but I never wanted to turn it off just because I lost. You need to be able to learn to dodge accordingly, and think about weapon timings. Probably closer to The Witcher than Skyrim, but honestly, once you get the hang of it, you're only going to get punished for timing mistakes, not random ♥♥♥♥ falling from the sky for no reason.---{ Grind }---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leaderboards/ranks☐ Isn't necessary to progress☑ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ You'll need a second life for grindingThere's a bit of grind, but it's supplemented really well with little side quests that make you feel that the grind is at least building towards something reasonable. Drops are consistent, and there is not a heavy RNG element.---{ Story }---☐ No Story☐ Some lore☐ Average☑ Good☐ Lovely☐ It'll replace your lifeThe lore is fun, Haro is cool, would be nice to have a bit more, maybe a compendium or gallery in the game you could access inside the tent. _childDocuments_.review: Enter the mysterious world where salvation assumes an enigmatic form and the distinction between dread and devotion becomes hazy. This journey is a fascinating fusion of strategic base-building, roguelike aspects, and a story that draws players into a pleasantly surreal universe.The game's charming pixelated visual style immediately captivates you with its vintage charm. But underneath its benign exterior is a world full of sinister whimsy. As a recently chosen shepherd, you are entrusted with creating and overseeing your cult that celebrates survival against the advancing darkness rather than villainy.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a drop of water in the ocean, but this game absolutely nails the vibe. _childDocuments_.review: Adorable colony sim with roguelite elements. Inspired by the classics, (Zelda series, TBOI and a bunch of other Devolver games), but also achieves so much. Lots of versatility when it comes to gameplay, you have these Binding of Issac-esque arenas with destructible environments and varying sizes and difficulties of enemies paired with these bullet hell driven boss fights, of course, sprinkled with those aforementioned roguelite elements. Then you head back to base and now you have a cul-, I mean, colony, to take care off, making sure they get fed, get some good shuteye, get them to praise the lord, become sacrifices and of course make them work for a living in your base. You can also travel to different areas in this small map that provide you with a gambling addiction, a fishing addiction, a shopping addiction and maybe you'll even find some cool secrets along the way. There is nothing all that bad about this game, it's really good and has some replayability to it. If I were to complain about something, it would probably be the boss fights, they all play the same up until the final fight; a lot of it is just dodging the same attack patterns while also avoiding the boss' peons, not really all that difficult despite how menacing the game makes them look. It's a small nitpick for me, I just really enjoyed the versatility on display but thought this could improve for maybe a future installment or a huge update. Cu-, Colony of the Lamb is truly amazing and offers a lot of bang for your buck, this will be another gold standard for roguelites in the indie genre. Praise the Lamb!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely simplistic combat combined with a colony management aspect in between runs - but without any strategy, only the micromanagement part of colony sims. It does have a somewhat unique artstyle and setting, but it leans on that too heavily, the "little kids' cartoon meets Lovecraft" gimmick (think the woodland critters from South Park) can only carry the game for so long without gameplay - I was already bored out of my mind after ~1 hour of playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's a solid dungeon crawler with a good amount of depth. Mixed with a good gameplay loop of exploring to get resources and heading back to your cult to use them and level up. It's fun, there's a good amount of depth here, it looks good and doesn't pull you out of the game to explain how to have fun playing the game. It's just good. I kind of wish it was a bit more difficult sometimes as far as the cult sim bits go. Seems very easy to get everything you need and there's not a lot of difficult once you get that ball rolling. In fact, it seems the game just keeps making the cult sim parts easier without really adding more challenges or some sort of ramping difficulty. The dungeon crawling has a story mode, but also an endless-type run you can do.  Both feel challenging and rewarding. I'd say a solid 8/10: It's fun, it keeps you engaged in a loop, it's aesthetically pleasing without overdoing it's themes, and it's focused on keeping you entertained and having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's all I have anymore. I got it as a gift, my wife thought it was cute so I got it for her on her switch. At first it was fine, we would fish together, discuss who would be the next sacrifice, and brainstorm our base design. Now, it's all I desire. She won't even look at me anymore, all she does is resurrect her favorite followers and imprison the rest; I've found my true calling as a farming aficionado, with a surplus of seeds and plenty of poop to go with it, but sometimes I can't help but wonder, 'Was this the right choice? Can I bear the burden of this divide between the one I call my true love? Can we ever recover from this tragedy that's befallen us?' I can't even remember our anniversary, or her maiden name for that matter, but when we're asked for the names of the followers in our cults that love to eat poop the most, you'll get a dossier in MLA format, peer reviewed, of how General FatNuts or Squag Jr. III prefer grass-fed shid over meat-fed shid.also amazing soundtrack 12/10 plz come out with DLC, and people have this game crash for some reason? all it needs is like 4GB RAM must be a skill issue idk

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the game a lot -- there is a lot of ground for emergent narratives, the combat has a nice feel to it and if it stops being as fun, there are a ton of accessibility options to play around with to make sure it never becomes gruelling unless you want it to. Really, the accessibility options for so many aspects of the game are what impressed me most, as they let you tweak the experience to be what you want it to be. The narrative is pretty straightforward and linear but clear, revealed bit by bit so you gradually build up the overall picture from the puzzle pieces. so when you understand the story, it feels earned. The humour the developers approach the game topic with pairs great with the art style and the mechanics. The only thing that bugged me was having to grind a little for a couple of achievements that required certain rooms generated for the adventure map. Since the maps use random number generation, it can sometimes happen that the rooms will take a lot of time to spawn. But other than that, I thought CoTL is a fun and enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Aww yiss, knucklebones!"I saw an old trailer for Cult of the Lamb and was immediately fixated on the curious combination of cutesy art style and dark occult subject matter. I expected a management sim where you build up your cult, manage resources, affiliations and more.What I wasn't prepared for was the hack-and-slash gameplay that felt like bargain bin Binding of Isaac!So, safe to say, I didn't know what I was getting into with Cult of the Lamb.You are the lamb, the last of your kind, and about to be sacrificed to ensure a sealed-away entity cannot return to the mortal realm. You escape, however, and begin raising a cult from which to draw power from so you can defeat the bishops who stand in your way, all in service of a dark, bound force that bides its time and awaits for you to release it.The game is split roughly in half between a passable exploration and combat game where you take on randomly generated maps, fight enemies and collect temporary upgrades, and a cult management sim where you recruit followers and order them to work or worship, generating resources with which you can build up your little cult village of cute animal people.As the game starts it feels fun and quirky and full of energy and potential! The first occult rituals in which you and your adorable animal followers cheer and chant as blood-red runes throb and stir is a promise of something truly unique ahead. However, in trying to be two games at once, Cult of the Lamb falls flat with both of its halves, and what might have been a march to success turns into a stumbling trot to mediocrity. The combat quickly begins to feel samey and the unpredictable nature of equipment you are provided can make some runs feel tedious and annoying while providing very little in way of rewards. Likewise, the cult management quikcly starts to feel like repetitive busywork. Upgrades somehow feel like they unlock both too slowly, but also too fast, since you can unlock everything worthwhile quite early in the game, leaving you with just minor incremental gains that don't feel worthwhile. The cultists themselves, adorable, colourful and embedded with special character traits, turn out to be very simplistic cardboard cutouts that generate side-quests for the player to deal with, many of which revolve around juvenile humour about eating poop which feels out of place. Like a joke a developed came up with early on and refused to give up no matter how inappropriate it ended up being to the final themes of the game.Where Cult of the Lamb truly shines is its audiovisual aspects. The quirky music combining vocals and ambient instruments, the wonderfully creative 'voice acting' of some characters, the colourful and cheerful character art and all the gorgeous little animations that really bring to life the variety of characters, especially our protagonist the Lamb. It all just tickles the brain in all the right ways! Time and time again I found myself smiling and bobbing my head to the tunes.Sadly the audiovisual glory cannot uplift the mediocre gameplay enough for me to really recommend the game. The first few hours I was hooked. Around the 6 hour mark I felt I'd seen all there was to see, and when I finished the game after about 13 hours I was sad to admit I had been right. On top of the underlying issues with the games flow and design, I suffered of a number of bugs that caused the game to get stuck as events did not load or menus did not open, forcing me to return to the main menu or to start the game again. The Twitch integration felt especially broken, and I disabled that around the halfway point of the game.A special mention has to go to the little dice-based minigame of knucklebones, which was far more entertaining than it has any right to be, and the keepers of the lighthouse and their hilarious chanting I couldn't help but mimic whenever I visited them.In conclusion, Cult of the Lamb is a wonderfully creative idea that had potential to be two great games, but it ends up stumbling and never reaches the greatness it deserves.Playtime: 13+ hours (Single playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 9Audio: 9Story: 6Gameplay: 4Overall: 6

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt one of the most fun games I have ever played.The combination of roguelike dungeon crawler + colony management makes for one of the most satisfying gameplay loops I have ever played.Genuinely, every dungeon run has me more excited to build up my cult, and building my cult has me excited to go back into the dungeon.Having 100%'d the game, including post-update - the pacing of the end-game and post-game is excellent. If you REALLY love cult of the lamb, you can easily sink hours and hours into the game.It's one of the most polished games - ever. The art, music, UX, and systems in the game are unbelievably polished, and that absolutely does not go unnoticed. The only "issue" I have is that the game feels too easy, but there's a lot you can do in game to mitigate that and make it feel at least decently challenging. Regardless, it's a lot of fun.Cannot recommend this game more.

Honestly I think a lot of the positive reviews are people in the same boat as me who were so excited and impressed by the first few hours. Once you really get into it though literally every part of this game is insanely shallow. The combat, leveling, colony simulator stuff, it's just all done so bad.Another disappointing part about this game is that it feels like it borrows from every other game in the roguelike genre (with some especially big influence for binding of isaac) and then does nothing new with those concepts. They borrowed ideas, and just made them worse.The art and animations are amazing though. The gameplay is just very disappointing. Buyer's beware for this one, the positive reviews are largely based off initial impressions and don't reflect the the quality of the game as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It is less than the sum of it's parts, and is definitely NOT worth $25.The game half-asses it's Rogue-Lite and Resource Management/Stardew Valley-esque gameplay and both end up feeling not very fleshed out. The better of the two should definitely be the Combat, but it's laughably easy and I found myself not dying until the 2nd boss while playing the hardest difficulty.The Fishing minigame is ripped straight from Stardew Valley but is also less challenging. I was able to catch every variety of Fish after visiting the one Fishing spot the game offers three times.The art style and music is very charming and effective but it does not justify the lack of depth this game has. Sadly, it will still sell well because it is a quirky game with a high-level of polish (at least in the art department) which is being published by Devolver Digital. They are also marketing it very heavily, which did succeed in getting me to buy the game.There were also several glitches I experienced while playing and several things which should not have passed game testing. The Shrine despawned from my game and I had to restart my game. Thankfully, I was able to use the same save, but it did take me out of the experience when all of my Cultists were sitting on the same tile where the Shrine should be while kneeling. The game seems to be hard-wired to inform the player of every time a Cultist eats a Grassy Gruel even when they have the "Grass Eater" trait. This led to me receiving a prompt 15 or so times telling me a Cultist ate a Grassy Gruel, but it was fine because they had the Grass Eater trait. I know that they have this trait and there is no need for the game to tell me every time a meal is eaten that has it.Some of the elements, like Sacrificing Cultists, also seem to have little purpose or be superseded by other gameplay elements. I was able to max my Devotion (or whatever word they have for levelling up weapons and Curses) nearly every time I checked my Temple, mitigating the use of Sacrifice. It also incentivizes sacrificing high-ranking Cultists in the tutorial, but these Cultists would be better suited for joining you on your missions or going on missions.I wanted to love this game, having highly enjoyed Hades, The Binding of Isaac, and Stardew Valley, but it feels like it tries to do too many things and few-to-none of them are done successfully. Knucklebones I did really enjoy. It reminded me of Caravan from Fallout: New Vegas but you didn't need to read an instruction manual to play it. Even in Knucklebones, which was my favorite part of the game, there was a pretty severe oversight in the "How to Play" section. It read "Match Dice - When dice of the same number are placed in the same column, multiply their value." Logically, this would mean placing two 1 dice in the same column would have a value of 1, and two 6 dice in the same column would have a value of 36, because 1 times 1 is 1 and 6 times 6 is 36. However, this is not what happens, and instead adding additional dice of the same value multiplies the value the dice would have by 2 for the first additional die and 3 for the second. This means that two 1 dice equate to 4 in the score, and three 1 dice equate to 9. This was just a really dumb, not game-breaking oversight, but there should be no incorrect information or confusion in a "How to Play" section that has about 4 sentences in it.Overall, there is not enough depth to justify the $25 price tag, and while the game has a great sense of style, the gameplay is too shallow to keep player interest. It is also lacking that extra level of polish I would expect from a game that is being marketed so heavily.

Overall, this game felt to me like it was two separate games that were being developed for the mobile platform that they ended up combining because they didn’t have enough substance to fully market either, and they somehow got the idea that they could pass off the amalgamation as a full-on indie PC game.  I purchased it on sale with DLC (it just adds cosmetics) for around $17, and I still feel that the price was unjustified after having played it through. _childDocuments_.review: The Cult of the Lamb must be rallied once again.. many of the acolytes have been in hiding amongst the populace.. once you've rallied them, I will give you further instructions..Cult of the Lamb is a surprisingly very fun city builder mixed with a roguelike where you spend half the game building a nice little town of cultists, and the other half going on crusades into different parts of the world and obtaining new loot to use in leveling up your followers, your cult and your own abilities.The cultish aspect of it is quite cartoony and really flows well with the atmosphere and you are given a surprising amount of choice within the game of how you want to run your cult! You can be a fairly nice leader and treat your followers well, even to the point of bringing them back from the dead after dying. The opposite is also a possibility, where you can sacrifice your followers to increase your powers and abilities as well as cannibalism and several other side effects and dark rituals. Even allowing you to take them with you on your crusades!Combat and controls are very smooth and surprisingly fluid in the crusades, the boss battles are very reminiscent of Devolver Digital's previous games like Enter the Gungeon and Hotline Miami, often seeming like Bullet Hells. However despite the bosses being bullet hells the life system is fairly forgiving and gives you a set amount of lives that allow you to take more damage before you die.Speaking of dying, during a crusade has no negative effects outside of losing some of your resources you obtained during the crusade, which I like a lot! It allows you to keep playing even if you die without too much punishment.However this game is not without it's faults, it blends both the city building aspect and the rougelike elements very well, but there are a few nitpicks I have.1: Some QoL changes to allow blessings to be more easily done would be appreciated. Smaller cults are easily manageable however in bigger cults of 10+ people it becomes tedious hunting down everyone to bless them. 2: This one comes down to personal preference but after swinging your weapon you become immobile for a short time. You can still roll but you are locked in place for a tiny amount of time, leaving enemies to hit you. It's likely a balance thing and doesn't break the game for me, but it does feel a tad clunky after a bit.3: More choices! I love the fact your not locked into being an evil or benevolent leader and I would love to see more variety in choices you have for running your cult. Your current rituals and choices of boosts for your cult give you a great bout of variety, but each option gives you around 4 choices total to pick from. It's understandable because the boosts together are already quite big, it just feels a bit small.Overall I love the game! It combines roguelike and city building without leaning too hard in either direction. The adorable art style doesn't feel out of place and after playing it for a decent amount of time, it's actually a lot more tame than I expected so the art style makes it stand out even more! There's plenty of cultist imagery to go around but it's surprisingly a lot less gory than I was expecting. Not that that's a bad thing, I actually really like that! If you are looking for a fun game that has city building and roguelike elements with a cute art style, pick this one up! I'm just starting out but so far it's easy to pick up and play without being too easy or too challenging on the Normal difficulty, I can easily see people trying many different routes on the higher difficulties. If you are looking for something with advanced multi-layered city building or long runs into a roguelike environment with permadeath, this game isn't quite like that and you may prefer other options.It's very nice and simple while still having enough depth to keep you playing even after you get the mechanics down. The level of customization for the followers is great too! I liked it a lot more than I thought I would and if you are thinking of picking it up, give it a try! There's plenty of fun to be had starting your own satanic animal crossing village.
