_childDocuments_.review: A cutesy game with a casual cult-management side as well as a dungeon rouge-like combat side. The management portion of the game is pretty lightweight, you have to keep morale and food to acceptable levels while progressing through the building tree and completing objectives to appease your cult members. You unlock augments for your cult doctrine over time, though they don't impact the gameplay too severely. The cult members are fairly autonomous day to day, which is useful since the game's time continuously ticks away, no matter the activity.The cult system is fine, but it's pretty shallow. Not a bad thing persay, just doesn't allow for much replayability. Then there's the combat sections in the dungeons which are pretty fun, if punishing. You roll a random weapon and ability for every floor of a dungeon, and you gain cards throughout a dungeon giving you minor bonuses until you eventually die or live to kill the boss at the end of the floor, unlocking the next floor. It's a satisfying enough system, if a bit repetitive. Recommend the game if you're a fan of the aesthetic and casual management games, look for a decent sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from perfectly picturing how I hope my dream will turn out once I start my sect and go live in a commune, there's one thing I love about this game.Poop.Poop is central to your economy. Poop is vital. Human waste acts as a fertilizer, which is a direct indicator of crop quality and growth speed. At mid-game, you unlock the latrines and the fertilizer silo, effectively streamlining the process of putting your excrements to work. But we can game harder: berries are your most reliable source of food in the early game; you start with a few bushes and seeds are abundant during crusades. Now, the "berry meal" is a low-tier meal listed as having a 15% chance of having a follower poop themselves directly upon consumption. It is listed as a negative feature, but it isn't: use that newly-generated poop to grow more berries, to feed more followers to collect more poop. And since some followers are coprophagic - and produce more devotion when sick - you can feed them meals made out of their own feces to increase their piety towards the Red Crown. Such is the glorious history of my poop cult.I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: ...I'm torn on this one. I like the dungeon delving a lot. It's got a snappy, sword-and-spell combat system with just enough delay so you know it's inspired by "Dark Souls" at least a little bit. You fight your way up to harder and harder bosses, and the combat keeps evolving. In between runs, you come back to your little cult and manage your flock. And it's silly and light and fun--you have to manage their beds, their food, their messes. Early on, when your cultists number small enough that you can count them on your hands, they feel like your chosen few.But after maybe a dozen in-game days, the wheels just kinda fall off. :/ The dungeons start to feel repetitive, and the whole time you're being sent messages about how your cult is falling apart without you. As the cult gets bigger and bigger, your followers feel less like individual creatures and more like another resource you have to juggle. I've spent entire in-game days putting up beds, inspiring followers, rebuilding resource generators, giving sermons--bored out of my skull because I just want to go on another dungeon run. And that's not even getting into the tacked-on fishing minigame, the not-that-deep Knucklebones dice game, and the other two regions which are even less interesting...It feels like the two halves of the game should play nice together, but they kinda... don't. In the end, I think it was only fun for Twitch streamers, who could laugh as the follower named after one of their subscribers begged to eat poop or sacrifice another subscriber.

_childDocuments_.review: An ok rogue-lite dungeon crawler and a mediocre base-builder rather awkwardly stuck together. The dungeon crawling element (á la Binding of Isaac) both moves the story forward and gives resources that are used to grow the titular cult, which in turn leads to upgraded abilities for the next run through the dungeon. It's fine as a game-loop, but not novel or exciting. Which sums up all the mechanics of the game actually - decent and reasonably well executed, but run-of-the-mill. I guess that the huge interest it's gathered is mostly down to the aesthetics of cutesy characters committing Loftcraftian horrors. But if you don't think Happy Tree Friends is the greatest thing ever, then this game has little to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot and adore the idea. With some tweaking, bug fixes and content updates, this can be an amazing game. It's short compared to other roguelikes but I still recommend it for the unique experience it has. It's especially good as someone's first rogue-like, the game doesn't expect you to sink in weeks and replay it several times just to experience everything. It has a nice difficulty curve (alongside difficulty options) instead of killing you at the beginning 50 times 'till you learn enough. This can be downside as well for people who expect this to be a rogue-like similar in difficulty and length as others.I love the game's artstyle, the combination of cute and dark is so great. The fact that they can make sacrificing, death and cannibalism look so normal and not disgusting is impressive. The doctorines you can pick from were sometimes funny to read with how morally grey they can be or how you can make your cult think something that's normally 100% wrong to be completely OK. This game knows what it is and I like it. I just wish there was a bit more flavour text with NPCs or followers.Monster designs are nice and I like the variety of forms your followers can have. Being able to decorate your base also adds more charm to the game, I rarely decorate in games but for once I did. At the time of writing I did have a visual glitch where some of the tiles I placed would briefly be the wrong tile for a second when coming on screen.The music is amazing, there isn't a single song I dislike. The effect that's done on the music when you're hit makes taking damage more impactful. Sound design also is good.I enjoyed my time with it. The combination of going on a rogue-like adventure and building your cult works pretty well. Everything you do while exploring can directly impact what you're gonna do at your cult. You can't spent too much time in both as you need resources for your cult and can't leave your cult alone for too long. It's a good balance.Combat is simple but enjoyable. I did expect a little more weapon variety but the ones that are here do all feel different to use. Room layouts could use a bit more variety. It did become better later on with environmental hazards and having some enemies come from the ceiling (I like it when games that use 2D art in a 3D world do stuff like that). Should also note that I really appreciate there being an arrow sometimes that indicates the direction a monster is attacking towards, makes things not unfair.The base building isn't super complex but that's a good thing for this game 'cus you're not always at your base. Upgrading things to get more automated feels good, not everything can be automated like keeping faith high but that's alright as it gives you some time pressure while crusading. Just seeing everything run well in your base during the final hours of the game is very satisfying.Watching the followers do anything is charming and you feel more powerful as your cult grows. I do wish they had more impactful triats, it's mostly very minimal and doesn't make them too distinguished from each other. It's also not too difficult to keep them satisfied (at least on normal difficulty, can't say for the harder ones yet), I didn't get a single one to turn against me. The random quests they give you are nice, there are a few that aren't worth the effort but others are funny like a follower randomly asking you to let them eat a dish made out of follower meat. I like that some of them have an actual quest line to go through.I do find it weird that there is no penalty for waiting with indoctrinating a new follower. You can just find new ones and let them wait 'till you're ready to have more in your cult or have them replace one who just died. It would be interesting if there was some sort of time limit or downside to letting them wait too long.The game's default difficulty is not as hard as other rogue-likes, it was a pretty smooth and casual experience to me. The game's also a lot shorter than other rogue-likes, no need to replay 50 times to experience most content. Can be both good and bad depending on what you seek in a rogue-like. This game seems ideal for people's first rogue-like or those who seek a more casual rogue-like. I personally enjoyed a more casual rogue-like for once after playing several ones that kill you for taking 1 wrong step. Definitely will replay it on a higher difficulty and try the Twitch intigration as that seems like a good time.Progression is a bit too fast in some regards. I spent a moderate amount of time in my cult and despite keeping my follower count around 7-8, I quickly gained doctorine tablet pieces and levels for the lamb. I got all doctorines before beating the 3rd area and had the lamb fully powered up at the start of the 4th area. Loyalty seems to either be leveled too quickly or the impact of their levels is a bit too much. Having them give a tablet piece each level makes you get them very quickly, perhaps some cap on either loyalty level or doctorine tablets that only gets increased by beating bishops could help.The cult building does have a well-balanced progression as I never felt far ahead in it as the amount of devotion you can get at a time is fixed depending on your general cult level and extra devotion generation from smaller statues and such.Even if I have some criticisms for this game, I really like it despite encountering some bugs. I do think this game has plenty of potential for further content updates, even paid DLC. So I hope they take a similar approach to other indie devs like Motion Twin and Klei with post-launch support and paid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: 20h 5/10 1 Yes, I used  No Yes, one achievement is missable. Win a game of Knucklebones against Rattau and win. I would recommend doing this the moment you find him No No No No Not really, beating all the bosses at least once without getting hit might also depend on a bit of luck No, you can play on the easiest difficulty and still unlock all the achievements NoThis game had a lot of hype around it when it got released and I totally understand why! what an awesome game. Who would think about combining a rogue-lite with a management kinda game? , another awesome game from  had a bit of city building kinda stuff on the side, but it wasn't as well integrated as the management aspect is in this one. Here you have to run a cult, decided on different subjects your standpoint, and make your followers happy, while still not breaking their trust in the religion. I decided to go for them being happy when I sacrificed somebody, but that had as a downside that they would freak out when another member died of old age, which was kinda stressful at some times when my sacrifice and ascend here on cooldown and somebody got the status "old". Another of my decisions was to get a ritual where everybody can eat, which made feeding my cult easier, but later on when doing longer dungeon runs and being away for a few days that they would have so much hunger.. while the other option was to let them not get hungry for 3 days, not sure I choose the right one for my playstyle there. It is great how much influence you have on how to run your cult. I also enjoyed the rogue-lite part a lot, getting ingredients from the dungeon, and beating bosses. There were also quite a lot sidequests, some in plain side, some others more hidden. Overal I just had so much fun and couldn't stop playing. Don't think this is a cute game btw... because it really is not. The art style might look cute but man you can be cruel. I'm glad they went with this playstyle, I think it would go too dark otherwise. I would also recommend reading the dishes you can make, and not just making them without reading... I almost got a game over screen because I killed all my members by accident, aka not reading that I gave them poison. Many of the achievements are very straightforward and nothing to worry about. There is one missable achievement around Rattau and playing Knucklebones against him. If you do that just as soon as you can and win, then there are no other achievements you can miss out on. You can play Knucklebones quite early in the game, so if you did miss it, you can easily start a new game. The hardest achievements for me were defeating the 4 bosses without getting hit. You can redo those fights but especially the last one gave me a hard time. This was very frustrating because on my first fight against that boss, I got hit in the last 5 seconds of the battle, otherwise, I would have gotten it already without really trying. I would recommend waiting with those 4 for later on as you'll get things that make it a bit easier. I used  to get a better idea of how to accomplish this. The only reason I say above that completing this game is a 5/10 is because of those 4 achievements. Otherwise, it would be more like a 2 or 3 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of he Lamb has elements of a colony sim, a city builder, and a roguelike hack&slash. Pros: The style is cute, the controls are precise and responsive, the story is mildly interesting, if only for the witty mix of adorable and macabre.Cons: all the mechanics of said genres are simplified to a point where there is no real strategy or even play-style differentiation. Choices don't really matter much. Press the same buttons, repeat the same boring tasks and do it for enough time, you'll get there. Quickly starts feeling like a chore. In the end it feels more like an idle game than any of the genres mentioned.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: A polished settlement simulator / top-down adventure game with an appealing aesthetic with quite a bit of dark humor throughout.I think the game is well-made and worth the money for people who enjoy this kind of horror-esque macabre tone, but it's just not my taste.--I went back and did the post game. I'm now at 58 hours of playtime instead of just 8. I feel uncomfortable that it's required to permanently sacrifice followers to finish that portion, but I guess it's fair since you *will* get a replacement follower after you finish the zone. So I guess one can think of it as offering a new body to replace later.Overall, I think the game is really good, but it *is* kind of a horror game and has quite a number of uncomfortable moments, no matter how hard you try to play it as a friendly cute and trustworthy lamb.And no, you can't bang your favorite disciple. The lamb will be forever the last. (You can hook up your favorites with the other characters though.)I don't know how intentional it is, but a lot of the cult-specific elements of the game do feel kinda like subtle social commentary. When I birthed my first new follower in-cult and saw how quickly the loyalty bar was going up, I nearly screamed. And then when I realized how fast loyalty goes up when taking care of them as a child I had the moment of "Wow, that's just like when I was a kid! Wait. WAIT. SHOULD I BE DOING THIS TO A KID, UHHHH THIS FEELS SLEEZYYYYY" and then next thing I know they've joined as a full time follower and already level XII, darn close to the max. In hardly a tenth of the time it took to get other characters to that level.Also, if you get tired of the fishing/repair/cooking minigames, or if the battles start to drag on, go into the options and turn on all of the auto-fishing and change the difficulty and whatnot to whatever feels good. There is no penalty for it, you can genuinely just customize the game to be whatever is fun for you... except the cult stuff, the cult's gonna cult no matter what you want.

It feels fun to play, to come back to occasionally, and it makes me hope for future updates and etc.Taking care of your followers on a harder difficulty beyond Normal is truly careful and perfect. _childDocuments_.review: I´ve played 100 days in this game and just finished the main story. I was even contemplating to get all achievements but I won´t and here´s why:- there are maybe 10 aspects in this game which are actually unique- of these aspects maybe 3 are fun (the fighting, the dice game and caring for your cult to an extend)- a lot of times it´s repeating the same 5 things to advance in the game- without the arbitrary hurdles to advance the actual game would be maybe 2 hours long depending on your skill- you can´t leave your cult alone for 1 minute which prevents from playing the actual game instead of babysitting everyone. - a lot of mechanics get introduced way too late in the game, like for example the sin mechanic. You need way too much to unlock everything and it takes way too long to get the necessary amount.- there are many bugs which feel so frustrating. One time 2 of my cult members were drunk and shortly before they sobered up and I went to bed they started fighting. So I woke up and one of them died. Or for example half my cult just get stuck on the spot while trying to head to their beds. You have to talk to everyone to unfreeze them so they don´t get to be tired the next day.- way too many actions have the same button mapped. I butchered way to many dead members because I missclicked or used my cursed instead of selling the old one.- why is the "y" button used twice on the rhythm game? - fishing feels useless because the amount of time you need to fish every available fish that day takes too long and the reward is compared to other methods too little- the game feels in almost every part too easy and when you get damaged it feels undeserved (for example the mob just spawned in or you can´t see the attack because the environment obstructed the view)- on the topic of difficulty: how should I know at the start of the game what difficulty level I should pick? yes you can change it later on but I gain nothing from it so for what reason should I put it anything higher than normal? And if you want a challenge, the more reasonable modes only get unlocked after clearing the main story and even for that you have to start a new save- caring for your cult feels like work after some time. Had a chain reaction once because I had 3 newborns who ♥♥♥♥ everywhere which made my other members throw uptl;dr - the game is a min-max simulator, still has a lot of frustrating bugs, way too many repeating parts and important mechanics come in way too lateThe game wants to be way too many things at once. To juggle everything at the same time hinders the fun. Save to say I still could find some enjoyment but because of the things listed above it´s sad to see what the game could´ve been...

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's Hades.Except it's actually Hollow knight.Except it's actually Don't starve.Except it's the binding of Isaac.Well actually it's all of them weirdly packed into a single product. There are essentially two sides and pretty fundamentally different games packed into to this. There's a resource gathering micro and macro management building sim and a rogue like top down combat experience. When it comes to the resource management gameplay, It's possible to do nothing but idle and watch your followers gather resources and handle their little village while you have to at times do things like cook for them and hold sermons (at least initially). As the game goes on you need to do less and less for them to just manage themselves. By around day 40ish of in-game time you're going to be overflowing with resources and have essentially won the resources management part of this game. The upgrades also end way too fast for there are way too few of them.The main thing this game is marketed as is as a rogue-like fighting game. It's ok but seems almost secondary considering you can live almost entirely without it and just grind the second half of the game until there's nothing to do anymore. What the rogue-like part provides is mainly story content. The story is pretty meh. At first it's interesting and kinda cutesy-creepy but after that initial reaction sets off all the cult stuff just becomes normal. Plenty of replayability though for the game makes you do the same missions again but on a higher difficulty after you're done with the game's 4 worlds.The game also has some glitches, like getting softlocked from follower interactions, but reloading the save seems to fix it so nothing too gamebreaking. Also the credits have all the discord mods in them which genuinely made me laugh.Generally speaking it's very addicting but gets stale after a while. My final verdict is a solid 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed the first few hours of this game a lot (I really enjoy the aesthetic and concept), everything feels a little bit too shallow to say Cult of the Lamb stands up to its peers (Stardew, Oxygen Not Included, Hades, Isaac, Dead Cells).For the rogue-lite side, the game's combat mechanics are satisfying enough, but the lack of diversity and control of your build throughout runs really started to wear on me towards the end. I never really got comfortable using the dagger or claws weapons compared to the axe or sword, so whenever I got a run that started me out with those I would be tempted to just exit the dungeon and start over, since you only get a few weapons drops throughout runs and there's no guarantee it will drop a weapon you want and not a curse. It would have been nice to get the choice between two or three weapons and curses at the start of each run. On top of that, I was pretty disappointed with how same-y all four of the dungeons felt, and how certain enemy designs kept getting re-used (you have an entire dungeon just dedicated to spiders theming, and then re-use spider mobs in the underwater dungeon too?). I also disliked how the layout of objects in dungeon rooms really made spaces feel cramped and difficult to see enemies at times, but could have forgiven that if there were more variety in runs. As it stands, you really dread the idea of dying at all in this game since it takes a multiple runs to clear each of the four dungeons already, and every run makes you feel like you're spending resources instead of making your character stronger. That brings me to the colony management side of the game, and how the two halves link together. In all, I really was expecting another "tier" or two to the various buildings of the game. This game lacks what you might call "late game" upgrades to the colony that makes you feel like they're becoming self-sufficient. Even with the highest tier to farm upgrades, only one farmer can work per station at a time for some reason, so if you really try and maximize the amount of farm tiles you can fit into a given farm station, your colonists will constantly need help keeping up with watering, harvesting, and fertilizing even at the very end. I also felt like the missionary trips were very unforgiving and not really worth it, with the rewards being very low given the length of missions and high chances that even a powerful colonist will die during them. Really, the entire colony system starts to break apart at the seams towards the end, as managing a colony of 20 villagers (the minimum to unlock the final boss fight) will give you a massive amount of busy-work. Each day felt like the same loop of sermon, confession booth (I couldn't be bothered to talk to each colonist every day to get a loyalty boost, so daily confessions was my compromise), pick up resources from the farm, drop off seeds/fertilizer, bury dead bodies (colonists die really quickly of old age in this game, further making me question the point of leveling up colonists), cook meals, rinse and repeat. The lack of ways to delegate this constant feed of busywork makes it always feel a little awkward crowbar-ing in a dungeon run into a given day, since it took me almost a full day to complete a given run. This made the "infinite dungeon" system to replaying dungeons feel useless, as by the time I finished a single pass my colony feed already would be blowing up with tasks to do. Again, this all felt very normal in the first few hours of the game, but I was really surprised there was no relief even with a fully unlocked tech tree and colony tree. Then as soon as you unlock the final item of the tech trees (I did this at the tail end of the third dungeon), you start to accumulate gold instead of faith points. I suppose they had to do something with your faith buildings, but this really made dungeon crawling feel even less justified as before it was the only real way to get gold (beyond the unbalanced missionary system). It also made the "gold cave" late-game area feel completely useless, since there was no real point investing gold in the well there when you already have more gold than you know what to do with. I also didn't really need to sacrifice my followers there, as all it did was unlock the final trinkets needed to get the last fleece in the game, which I already knew I was never going to wear as the buffs seemed super under-powered (hence why I chose it last). I was expecting some kind of "ultimate fleece" or something to unlock for getting all of them, but that didn't happen. I've asked myself after finishing the game with such a sour taste in my mouth if my gripes all come down to there not being enough content in this game, and if I just unrealistically expect every game of this format to be a 100+hour experience to feel satisfying. And while it's true that I was disappointed to feel like I had exhausted this game's content just around the same time as I would start really sinking my teeth into an Oxygen Not Included save file or Stardew farm, I think there's more to the problem here. Even a relatively short "economy simulation" game like Game Dev Story can feel satisfying from beginning to end if the tech trees and different mechanics gel together nicely. I think the problem here is the game never really felt like a cohesive experience.It winds up delivering the worst tedium and busy-work of colony simulators in early game, with no satisfaction of surpassing those growing pains through tech trees and late-game buildings, and the worst repetitiveness of replaying dungeons constantly like rogue-lites, without the fun variety of builds to make you enjoy having to play through essentially the same dungeon over and over again. As it stands I would say this hybrid just doesn't quite work, and to stick with the other heavy-hitters that preceded Cult of the Lamb to get your fix of the different genres on display here. Definitely a jack of all trades, master of none situation.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Good Game DesignCotL is two games in one the likes of which many have been made before but all to often these titles are shovel ware rogue lites that all feel the same. This game really tries to innovate the genres whilst master crafting the experience to feel immersive and ultimately fun.The game consists of base building and the binding of issac style dungeon crawler and both feed off each other. Both games feel really fun with beautiful top tier artwork and snappy animations whilst you craft your experince throughout. The cult theme really works here and is a pillar of much of the games great humour. Maybe this theme isnt normie friendly enough for the masses I'm not sure but arent we all sick of dnd fantasy themes or done to death simplistic sci fi rogue lites I for one am and CotL is super refreshing by contrast. Given the games clear replayability factor and the price I think this is a no brainer in terms of recommending and buying at full price and I would not be surprised if this game makes it into the top 10 games of the year at very least for art direction which for me is a 10. Overall there are moments in this game to which the medium of video games is truly emboldened in its ultimate form. The graphics the music the feel of combat all sing in unison triggering the buzz only video games can give you when all your senses are being stimulated. I have had no bugs up to now and tbh this game feels alot like something you would see made in Nintendos gold era it has that level of a quality feel to it but with a darker tone which I love alot. Like drdisrespect says its a snooze fest out there in the gaming world so love it or hate I recommend giving cult of the lamb a shot its at the very least trying to stand out from all the terrible games being shoved out right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early review, but it's day one and people are going to be looking at this game and I feel like three hours is enough for me to give you an impression, especially since this game is a roguelite. It's really enjoyable so far. The artstyle and the animations instantly welcome you into this creepy cute world. And it holds you with snappy fun combat and engaging cult management mechanics that are simple enough that they're not overwhelming but deep enough that even early on I've had to think about where I wanted to go with things. Within the first the hours I cleared out the first of the 4 major bosses and have amassed just under a dozen followers. It was hard to pull myself away from the game, I played these 3 hours in one go and wanted to play more but I'm starving so it's time to get lunch after I finish typing this up. This game has a lot of Hades in its DNA from a combat perspective, it's more simple at least at its surface but each combat encounter has kept me engaged. And what's surprised me even more is that the cult management mechanics have also been very engaging. Each run has something going for it because you're progressing your cult on some axis or another. It's not a roguelite where all your progress is washed away each run, if anything, each run no matter how far you go will only serve to further your efforts. I'm really enjoying it. I might edit this review after actually beating the game, but for those of you looking to see if this is the game for you, I'd absolutely recommend checking it out based on what I've played so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a very grim yet charming entry in the "roguelite" genre.You take the role of the Lamb, a creature tasked with operating a cult for an elder god being.A very fun mix of town building, resource managing and dungeon crawling awaits. It never gets too much, with the "rogue" parts of the game being bite sized and taking about 10 minutes to complete (with an option to extend them, should you wish to do so.)The game operates on a day-night cycle that can sometimes get a little repetitive with tasks that you should be performing every day, such as holding sermons and greeting your cult members, however it never got to the point where I would skip these tasks on purpose, as they don't take very long and give you nice perks.As your cult grows you gain access to more difficult areas and a wider variety of decorations and functional buildings, as well as unlocking perks for your members and new rituals to perform.Should you want to switch up the gameplay a little, the game allows you to change the Lamb's pelt, which gives them different buffs/nerfs, such as stronger attacks in exchange for taking more damage.The story is simple yet engaging, and there is a lot of post-game content to keep you glued to your screen.The developers have an update roadmap available, so there's always new features to look forward to. The mythical "sex update" is on the way at the time of writing. I can't wait~.All in all, a very fun game and worth the pick up both on and off sale.Also, there is a fishing minigame. Also also, you can, in fact, pet the dog.

_childDocuments_.review: "Cult of the Lamb" is a captivating and eerie experience that defies expectations with its charming yet unsettling blend of gameplay elements. At first glance, its adorable art-style and whimsical music draw players in, but beneath the surface lies a rich tapestry of dark lore and occult themes that add depth to the experience.The music in "Cult of the Lamb" sets the tone perfectly, enhancing the game's atmosphere and immersing players in its eerie world. From haunting melodies to upbeat tunes, the soundtrack complements the gameplay and adds an extra layer of immersion.Visually, the game is a treat for the eyes, with its vibrant colors and cute character designs. However, this charming exterior belies the game's darker undertones, which gradually reveal themselves as players delve deeper into its lore.One of the standout features of "Cult of the Lamb" is its plentitude of mechanics and activities. From managing your cult to exploring procedurally generated dungeons, there's always something new to discover and master. The game's variety of gameplay mechanics keeps things fresh and ensures that players are constantly engaged.What truly sets "Cult of the Lamb" apart is its juxtaposition of cuteness and creepiness. While it may appear lighthearted on the surface, it delves into themes of cultism and the occult, offering a surprisingly deep and thought-provoking experience for those willing to explore its darker side.

_childDocuments_.review: *Played on Steam Deck*Pros:- Incredible, one of a kind, art style- Really great balance of farm-sim and rougelite- Farm-sim elements are really well fleshed-out, albeit shallow compared to dedicated farm-sims (deliberate choice)- Rougelite elements are very well done. Can be challenging on higher difficulties, but really rewarding.- Game is silly in very enjoyable ways, does not take itself too seriously- Great music- Dungeons have replayability as you scale- Great minigamesCons:- Main story could be a little longer- Gameplay forces you to dungeon dive, which forces the game to be shorter than if you mainly stayed with your cult- Farm-sim elements could be slightly more fleshed outOverall:Highly addicting game in which you lead a cult. Half your time will be spent dealing with your cult/farm and the other half diving dungeons for materials/tackling the main story. The combat is not too difficult, but overall rather rewarding. The dungeons do scale as you get stronger, which makes for a continuous challenge.Advice to anyone thinking of buying/playing:Don't rush the main story. Spend time developing your cult and farm. _childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb can be described best as a half Rougelite half managment sim that in my opinion combines really well into each other. The two gameplay styles really blend well into each other. The rougelite elements remind of Hades, you get a random weapon and a random projectile each dungeon run with different attributes and each room will have a random benefit and each run ends with a boss fight that typically grants you a new follower. Combat is pretty simplistic but otherwise enjoyable. The cult and base building element reminds of Animal Crossing, feed your villagers, treat their needs, gain faith points and become stronger through them in the dungeons. Building your own religion in your own image is mighty fun too in my experience. The synergy boils down really well. Game also has a lot of nice and fun side content minigames to partake in. Game can clock you about 9-15 hours depending on how much you focus on the base building aspect as you raise your total follower count. Easily one of the best games to come out this year. A pretty good buy for its price too.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 10/10Total Content: 8/10Visuals: 10/10Audio: 9/10Story: 8/10To start, the game has an absolutely incredible theme. The 2d, cardboard-cutout artstyle combining Happy Tree Friends with Binding of Isaac is super original and fun, and the music is good enough to be memorable but subtle enough to not be distracting. Plenty of customization as well, with follower forms, decorations, fleeces, etc. I'm a big fan of the "Sims" sort of speaking you hear from the characters, and the subtitling is done well and is never intrusive. The gameplay is incredibly solid, with half being very similar to Isaac, but less in-depth. Going through stages and collecting followers, resources for your cult, finding tarot cards, etc. is very entertaining all the way through the end of the game. The other half of the gameplay, being your cult management, is similar to Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing in a way, but with a dark twist. Plenty of ways to make your cult your own, from changing the way followers look, to assigning jobs and setting doctrines. I would prefer there was more to upgrade, as you do run out of things to do later in the game (nearly at the end), but it's still very enjoyable. (STORY SPOILERS) The story isn't very deep, but it works well and kept me interested all the way through. Defeating the heretics and collecting their power to free and eventually overthrow your deity was a fun process, and felt like you were genuinely making an impact in the story. This is made even better with certain moral dilemmas such as sacrificing certain characters for your own gain. If they add DLC, I'm curious where they'll take the story.One of my few complaints is that there is a big power difference between a few of the weapons and curses. Mainly, the dagger is nearly worthless compared to the axe or sword, which are significantly stronger and have superior range. Some of the curses are just objectively better than others, being able to be aimed precisely or automatically tracking enemies. This is somewhat minor, but it is disappointing seeing a dagger at the start of a run. An absolutely amazing game, with great gameplay, visuals and audio, and a theme you don't see in a lot of games. If you're a fan of roguelikes and/or Stardew-esque games, definitely give it a shot, as it's well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: ARGH THAT ENDING WAS SO SATISFYING I BEAT HIS ASS... *ahem*So I somehow went into Cult of the Lamb not realising it was a roguelite/like, simply because I don't pay attention to any gaming news. I thought it was going to be a farming management sim, which... I suppose technically it is. But the roguelike elements are the core of the game and are great fun. You get that real adrenaline rush when you survive something you didn't think you would. The only thing I would say is that the combat feels a little sticky on keyboard and mouse, but the game does explicitly recommend you play it with a controller. The side quests are a complement the main mechanics greatly since they tend to be things you don't have to go out of your way to do. The management part of the game is simple and not overwhelming, and, despite the games' themes, it does allow you to be a... somewhat nice cult leader.The art is incredible, the dev team very clearly had a strong grasp of the aesthetic they wanted. It fluctuates smoothly and naturally between extremely adorable and outright terrifying. Each world is unique and had a different vibe, but all conveying danger. I would say that the bird cultist designs do freak me out a lot more than the monstrous cultists designs because uh... why are their mouths uh... there? Separate from their beaks? On a more serious note, I do found that sometimes the levels/rooms got a little cluttered, causing me to lose health just because I didn't see one tiny thing in the tall grass, which I'm sure is by design but was also incredibly infuriating.The characters are fairly unique in design, but they do kind of meld together in terms of personality, falling into the binary of 'this one won't kill you' and 'this one will'. I don't feel it matters too much though that the characters felt same-y, because the main plot revolves around the Lamb and their mission anyway; the characters who help you SHOULD feel kind of disposable considering what you're setting out to do.Music is fantastic, and so was the sound design. I could very clearly pick out when I'd gotten hit, and I could hear if I'd forgotten to do something at the cult camp before racing off.I'm still coming down from the adrenaline from the final battle, so... Yes. 10/10 game, absolutely would recommend anyone who's even a little bit interested in it to give it a shot.

Now that I'm done with the story I don't see myself coming back too often just to check on my cult and work through the same dungeons again. Longevity of a game comes from replay-ability, and while I could restart completely, there's no bonus to that. Great game, but more of a one and done.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the bugs which can be fixed and hopefully will be fixed I gotta say the game is rather shallow.First the three big positives: Art Style, Music, Theme & Presentation, those are incredible and put together so well that I gladly spend 23€ for the game.The gameplay itself feels like they've half heartedly glued together Hades (The Dungeon Crawling Part) with Oxygen Not Included and Don't Starve Together (The Village System / Cult System).First of all the Major Problems for me with the Dungeon Crawling.- The Dungeon Crawling Upgrade / Tarot Cards are just useless out of 36 cards there are only 3 useful ones which will help you in the run itself.What's the point of adding cards like "Enemies drop Fish", "Harvest more resources" (in the dungeon)? Feels like those effects should be something unlockable through something in the cult system and not upgrades in the dungeon itself.They only dilute the pool of the 3 cards that are useful for a dungeon run.While other cards are even counterproductive, the bomb Tarot card made me go paranoid since I didn't know if the bomb was my bomb or a bomb of an enemy, the faster movement speed made it harder for me to position myself in a game about positioning.At 10 hours in I've just stopped picking up any cards.- The Combat is boring and to easy.You run in hit the enemy once run out, repeat until the enemy is dead.I just started using the golden fleece which gives you more damage for each enemy killed until you get hit, to fasten the combat up.To talk about the easy part (very small spoiler about endboss mechanics) I gonne use the last boss as an example: it's partly a bullethell boss, so dodge bullets get in hit get out.Except there are barley any bullets to dodge, it feels like they had more bullets since the arena is quite big to manuvere but removed 300% of those bullets at some point in development, it's as if they've tried to develop the difficulty for small children.The Village Part / Cult Part:-The building part is that there is barley a building part there is maybe 5 total buildings you build and then upgrade through them to level x while some of the levels are literally just filler and don't add any value to it.Like as an example there are sleeping bags > tents > houses, the upgrade from bags to tents is that tents don't crash as often as bags. That's it nothing more, there is no real value to upgrade to tents. - Running the cult itself is also very bland & very micromanaging there are two things you have to watch out,  followers believe and their hunger.For the believe you just do a sermone each day and a ritual every few days. For the hunger you just cook every few days.So a daily day in the cult is sermone > bless your members > collect devotion > either cook or do a ritual > go into the dungeon repeat from step 1.That's all there is sadly, I expected a lil bit more.Weirdly enough I managed to get all the upgrades there are in the game by hour 9 so the other 10 hours I just dungeon crawled and did the quests.In other words 10 out of 19 hours I barley engaged with the cult mechanic at most feeding my followers and doing a ritual like once every 3-5 days. I'll defininitley return to the game once the endgame has been added hopefully they add more systems to the Cult System and actually engaging bosses with those updates but at the current time I would only say buy the game when its on a deep sale for like 5-10€.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not want to say it is a bad game, but sadly you still can't make it clear enough with the first look at a review. Obviously the red deters people from even reading your reason why you do not recommend it, because they automatically think you saying it is a bad game.That out of a way. CotL is a great game with steep flaws, breaking the very game it wants to be.I just do not recommend it to others because of those reasons. I came in more for the Rogue like aspect and a bit of a mix in with the town building and managing.Sadly you spend the most time in the game managing your town. You could go out more at the beginning of the game, since you do not have to do that much in town, but you won't get far, since you are not leveled enough for that challange. Later on you are forced to constantly take care of your folk, otherwise they starve and poop themselves in the grave in no time. And that is exactly what i absolutely do not like about this game. The moment you decide to go deeper into the dungeon, you pretty much are setting yourself up for complete failure, since you most likely will lose people or even destroy your cult.So you are forced and yes i mean FORCED to look every run for around 10 minutes after your members before you can go back in another 5-10 minute round of doing what you came for. Or at least the majority. That being said if they add something that does give you a ability to not have to be worried about your people for a while so you can actually play the game the way you came for.. this review stays as "negative" even if it is really just that i do not recommend it.Still. It can be fun if you manage it somehow. But if you mess up once it is all the more frustrating. And frustration is not why i play games. Life is frustrating enough for me.I will obviously update my review, should they do something about this issue. I just hope they aren't putting it in a paid DLC or something.Edit:Something i forgot to add. Difficulty spikes hard quickly. To a point where enemies become absolute damage sponges. Even a good build won't get you through there. So you can spend 5-10 minutes on a boss simply because he takes way too many hits to be killed, while you yourself dodge everything perfectly. It's not the end of the world kind of a problem obviously, but as mentioned above... it is extremely frustrating, leading you to end the game simply out of exhaustion. I do not want to spend 10 minutes on a small boss, just because i did run into the same level a few times too much. You should implement a feature that slowly makes the enemies weaker again over time, so you don't end up with enemies at a level you can never reach, just because you enjoyed Darkwood so much.

_childDocuments_.review: The comparisons to "Binding of Isaac" are obvious to me, though I'm pretty sure it's two different companies.  There are strong comparisons, and I'm going to make them.  If that doesn't make sense to you, you can skip a lot of this review, get the overall picture and understand I like the game.  Bosh!  What efficiency!So yeah, I like this game. I've clocked in significantly more time on my streaming account.  But I marathoned this over the weekend on this account instead of doing work I needed to do from home.  I SHOULD BE ASHAMED OF MYSELF.  YET I AM NOT.Your quick summary:  It's a twin-stick shooter.  Which is to say you look down from above, navigate your character around, dodging attacks, while attacking in any arbitrary direction.  You can go left and attack right, or up, or whatever pleases you.  One stick is for moving, the other for shooting.  Just like Robotron: 2084, if that means anything to you.Much like "Binding of Isaac" (BoI), it's got a pixely art style.  Each map is broken up into a handful of individual combat arena rooms, which usually fit on the screen and rarely take up two.  So combats are short, sharp, and can be pretty fast-paced.A lot of BoI gameplay leans into a lot of bullet-dodging.  Most every enemy has an attack that fires shots, be it in a pattern, or at the player, or whathaveyou.  So awareness of the whole screen and good positioning was key.  Here, in this game, there are fewer bullet attacks, per se (one boss notoriously excepted), but the enemies are more likely to go engage you in melee.  Since most of your attacks are also melee, that's fine.In terms of gameplay itself, it comes off with markedly more nuance:  your character has much more agility, much more rapid movement, requires appreciating your weapons' reaches, and deciding if you can stunlock an enemy long enough that you can finish them, or disengaging before you get hit by that or another foe.  Unlike BoI, you've also got a dodgeroll move with a fairly generous invulnerability window, so it's possible to disengage pretty quickly if you're observant.That said, healing is a limited resource that requires the random generator to be working in your favour, so the best bet is to not get hit in the first place.BoI aims to be kind of gruesome and, if you will, really edgy.  It fits the theme of the game in a way, but that sort of bleakness is taxing.  This game generally comes off as cute, except when it doesn't.  Animals are smiling and cheerful, and then can look scared, or hurt, terrified, disgusted.  They murder each other.  They get swallowed by eldritch horrors.  Many of them are coprophiliacs, some few ask them to make a "special meal".  Terrible things happen to them, and sometimes you're the agent of that terrible thing... if you want to.  You can be nice, but the world isn't.It doesn't get really graphic about it, at least. Dismantling a corpse might make little giblets fly out, "hams" as the missus would put it. The more gruesome things are implied rather than explicitly displayed.  But even still, invest the slightest thought about it and it's kind of perturbing.  That, in my lofty opinion, makes it far worse than BoI, which just tries to slap you in the face with it.The Twitch integration is amusing, where viewers can sign on and make a critter look however they please (subject to what you've unlocked), and then puts their banner atop the critter so you always know it's them.  If you like your viewers, this makes the game personal.  If you're callous, well... hah, you can always make them fight each other to the death should it please, or turn one into meatshakes to serve up to the others.  Later, I'm told, will be a coop mode.I haven't finished it yet, and I'll likely be streaming this game off-schedule, mostly during the weekends.  There's room for more signons.  In that public game, I can't help but be nice.  In my private game, well... you probably don't want to be there.  Pop on by, the missus and I are usually up to something droll when we're on.  .  I always put the links down here because advertising is hard, and I like people who like to read (especially what I write), so clearly you're my kind of person.I forgot!  When the game isn't about slapping enemies upside the head, there's a whole commune to take care of.  Raising crops, cooking basic meals, sweeping up after the little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, building up buildings for them, giving sermons.  It's one part violence fighting, and one part farming sim.  Over time, a lot of the farming stuff can be automated so you don't need to do it yourself, though the early all-manual parts are a bit irksome.Anyway, the missus enjoyed watching me streaming it, and I'm having a fine enough time playing it.  And if you're given over to mulling things, I'm sure there's a lot in here you could think about.  That's worth the price of admission right there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really torn on this game, I was looking forward to since it was first previewed, I loved the art style, tone, and general vibe of the game, And all of that is still here.My main issue with the game is it took me around 12.5 hours to beat, which isn't a issue in it's own right, But around 8 hours into the game, I effectively reached "Full build" as far as my in game character would go (Meaning i couldn't upgrade my rougelite side with weapons and abilities any further)which makes the cult side of things effectively have no link to the rougelite side of things, while also letting me breeze through the rest of the story i had left with the best weapons in the game, When at full build there's also a fair bit less incentive to actually push your cult as well, As the only real way that matters is in the form of converting your followers to demons to assist you in dungeons.It really is a shame though, Because the base building side of this game was fantastic.. It's primarly what i focused on before, and even after reaching full build (Partially why i got it so fast i imagine) It's great seeing the cute little animations of your followers working, and seeing them slowly get more and more levels to them is a huge appeal to the game, It's just a shame this aspect, and the rougelite seperate so fast.Overall though the game is still a good one, It's just a very short game, with bad pacing contained within. I'd probably still recommend this game on a sale, And a lot of my issues could potentially be fixed with future updates, Don't let me stop you if you think you're fine with paying full price for a 12-15 hour game, but ideally wait for a sale, or a major content update.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the lamb is a very cute game, with dark tones. On paper, things like sacrificing your followers and chopping up their bodies for food sound very dark, but the game somehow manages to make it look kinda cute?As for the gameplay, you go from room to room, kind of like binding of isaac, until you beat the final boss of that area. On your way you can collect different kinds of weapons and cards which give your character certain perks.Weapons are pretty basic, it either hits hard but slow, fast but barely puts a dent in your enemies or somewhere in the middle. There is no such thing as combos, just hit 3 times and the attack animation resets again.You get a certain amount of projectiles, a decent variety of them too. I would say atleast 7.The all have different things and I think ill leave them for you to find and use.Cards are the main appeal to combat for me. They give you perks like getting projectiles back faster, gaining a heart, doing poison damage on hit. I was honestly kind of sad to see such a little amount of them and they dont impact the game too much with a few exceptions. For people that look for a system like Binding of Isaac, where you combine a bunch of items to get the most ridiculous builds, look further. Cards are really basic and do not stack together.Bosses are fine, if youre used to Hades or The Binding of Isaac they shouldnt be too big of a trouble.The final boss was very easy compared to the bosses ive faced before and the ending was rather dull?Kinda funny but thats about it. They'll probably expand on the post-game through DLC and im definitely looking forward to that.The game has you collect followers and resources to expand your cult. As you expand your cult you get more and more silly things to do. Again the themes are dark, but done very cutely. I had a blast using every type of ritual, setting up different laws like: Cannibalism (we all know what it does).This part of the game to me was very fun, but a bit too simple. I hope they allows us to have more options for our followers because right now theyre either praying, or working.Id like my followers to feel more special rather than another pawn. Make them stand out somehow!Overall paying $23 was definitely worth it. It isnt anything mind blowing, but its a nice game that is worth spending your time on.To me, the game perfectly represented what I eventually got and I think the price also perfectly reflects what I expected to get. I'd give it a 8.5/10.If they allow me to interact more with my followers (give them jobs kind of like rimworld but more basic) it wouldve been a 9.5

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute.Combat is not too technically demanding, but you are rewarded for skill and timing.Dungeons are procedurally generated, unfortunately not a lot of variation in combat room layout; .A decent variety of enemies whose patterns and movement seem internally consistent, feels good to learn and improve for each enemy.The other half of the game (the cult building part) is a resource gathering/management sim that can augment your combat stats and abilities.Overall the game feels like a fusion of the aesthetic of Binding of Isaac, the town/resource management of Darkest Dungeon w/ some elements of a mastery system in Rogue Legacy, while the combat is reminiscent of Bastion. _childDocuments_.review: Let me get this started by saying, that one, I haven't finished this game (I probably will if only to get my money's worth so expect an update to this if i feel it need be) and two, I'm a little ♥♥♥♥♥/causal when it comes to games, for example I played on normal difficulty for this game which i hear doesn't really mean much. I have a hard time getting me motivated to challenge myself and I really like management games, so when I heard that the rougelite elements are shallow (they are, and it's so boring i didn't want to play, unlike hades, a game i didn't get far in nor is really for me I but really really enjoyed when I played it) I was like sure, the management is said to be better so surely the management should be at least decent!It's not. It's really not.To start with a dumb nitpick, there's a lot of decorative blueprints but the area is so small and limiting in how you can build (not to mention it's just a boring square) that I knew it'd be pointless to decorate unless a follower told me to. Second the dialogue repeats itself a lot with the characters with quests, really hitting home how you're doing the same ♥♥♥♥ over and over again, which is fine but I was hoping at least the traits would change that bc so far the traits have less of impact on gameplay than ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wobbledogs (a mostly idle game in which the traits don't even do much there). And the moment I realized how little traits there were was the moment I realized how shallow this game is.All the cult stuff do was make me wish they did more with it than just generic rituals (why not make it so you can make it like a commune? with characters becoming friends or foes, even getting together and having kids ANYTHING to make it so I wasn't mad every single time the game told me two characters became friends like that means anything. or making the doctrines ACTUALLY INTERESTING and not something i choose then ignored or something i choose and broke the game in half like the grass perk) I also had no problems with difficulty at any part of the cult until they forced ♥♥♥♥ on me, which was then dealt with in 5 seconds. It means nothing and I don't even know if difficulty even changes that, but from what I can tell it doesn't.Now, as I write this review I realize I'm only nitpicking instead of talking about the larger elements of the cult sim part, and the reason is that it's just going through the motions, eventually you just do the same thing over and over again, at first it's fun bc it's all new but the moment it stops being new is the moment I wondered why I was even playing or why I even bought this game (and why I was stupid enough to buy the overpriced dlc pack). Sure it's serviceable and it works (i heard it's glitchy but besides from the game saying a dead character got old I didn't get any) but here's not even any added charm such as a variety of dialogue, types of quests, or even just silly animations, interactions or actions the cultists can do. The whole thing simply just exists and it becomes a chore fast and is just grinding so you can beat the dungeons faster.There's not even a good way to manage your cultists from what I could tell and if there is I didn't notice bc it didn't even matter, it just goes to show how useless the cultists actually are. And it doesn't help how they get old so fast that I dreaded leaving the cult bc i knew if i went into the boring dungeon i would have to leave to get back to town and bury my cultist (i don't sacrifice or resurrect unless prompted and choose more "morally good choices" aka I handicapped myself and it didn't matter except I wasn't dummy broken, just bored).Anyways there's also rougelite stuff and the combat is pretty boring as I mentioned, room layouts that don't really mean much, enemies that just are there and are only hard if you get the stupid dagger (aka it's rng if the game goes faster or not and not in an interesting way, in a "oh it's just slower and more annoying but still the same thing and it's only hard because I get impatient" kinda way). The cards barely matter, some weapon types are useless (the vampire barely did anything for me) and the bosses don't even let you do anything cool (i drained the health of a boss to half, thinking I skipped an enemy wave phase until it just went right to that phase without me even having the CHANCE to get a hit in so it doesn't reward me for doing good).If anything this game is just a thing to play if my ADHD decides it just wants to do something that doesn't take too much thought, and even then it bores me. The most fun I had after the first few hours was playing the dice game because that has more variables and dept than the rest of the game. If you want a management sim play rimworld or oxygen not included, if you want a rougelike play hades or issac. It's not bad though, it's good just not great and honestly it makes it worse because it now falls in uncanny valley, though this could all be turned around with updates, however in its current state it's just mediocre and not worth the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and cute, Cult of the Lamb couches the terrible dynamics associated with cults in a cutesy art style with plenty of non-characters for you to grow attached to and/or murder in your quest for power. _childDocuments_.review: Alas, despite its phenomenal presentation, Cult of the Lamb is too shallow to garner an honest recommendation from me, and, forced to a hard Yes or No, I find myself leaning negative here.This game knocks it out of the park when it comes to the superficial - it's visually distinct and full of very crunchy and punchy effects.  The combination of combat-roguelike and colony sim is intriguing, and the game is absolutely effective at ... much like any cult worth its salt strives to be.Would that the similarities had ended there, but, also like a cult, a hollow existence awaits those who delve deeper into the game.  Every system introduced into this game, though many appear interesting at first, turns out to be disappointingly shallow.  The upgrades to buildings/tech offer little variety and are underwhelming in terms of any actual feeling of .  The combat upgrades are even less inspiring; you get new weapon types (insofar as just adding Poison or Crit to existing ones is ), you get new spells (which I found unsatisfying to use), and there's little else worth mentioning.  These are arranged into a truly meager tree, with little apparent reason for its hierarchy and no sense of customization, since you must take nearly every option from one tier before advancing to the next.  Doctrines and Rituals are probably the most interesting systems, but these too lack depth, and don't feel very balanced or tuned for good pacing.It feels strange to say about a game that, outwardly, seems so polished, but Cult of the Lamb felt almost .  It's not that you can see any gaping holes at a glance, and it's not that anything is evidently ... Rather, what's not done here is the expansion, evolution, and finishing touches that allow good ideas to mature and coalesce into great games.   It's as though there were a few solid brainstorming sessions, and the resulting high-level ideas were developed, arranged to look as enticing as possible, and released.  With such excellent alternatives in the roguelike genre, it's hard not to feel that this approach is in some way a deliberate cash-grab rather than a true attempt to make a game the best it can be.The shortcomings are not immediately apparent, and there are procedural obstacles (tiered trees and mandatory repeats of the same combat area) which do little other than extend playtime, so many who might've gone for a quick refund will remain enticed just long enough to make that impossible.  I wouldn't refund it myself, as I did have some genuine fun here, but the more I think about this game, the more a thumbs-down feels like a correct response.

_childDocuments_.review: To me this game is cute and has an original idea but does not feel finished nor polished. I find that there's a lot of depth and thoughtfulness lacking in how the game is played through, the combat, and the city building parts. For example, you can easily max out your city half-way through the game and the city does not really offer anything of value to your character, except for some starting gold on your runs, and overall the city just feels like a useless chore. The higher level characters in your city don't really matter, nor does placement of buildings, very little of consequence. The robes that your city unlocks are mostly all disadvantageous except for one of them. I started the game on the highest difficulty with no prior knowledge/online looking and beat it in 17 hours, and there's no real interest or incentive to play it again, or any new quirk. For me other games exist that do both the combat/playthrough and city-building parts in a much more satisfying and interesting way, even if you have to play a separate game for each.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb combines an action rogue-lite with settlement management, an amazing art style, humour and music. You are the Lamb, chosen by The One Who Waits to start a cult and conquer the lands from the four bishops of the Old Faith. You start off by gathering followers from randomised runs into the territories of each of the game's bosses and build your cult, managing follower's needs like food and shelter, using their devotion to improve your skills and upgrade yourself and your cult. The action element of the game involves you going through randomised runs of the aforementioned bosses. Each one offers new enemies and materials to collect. The gameplay is quite simple. You get an action roll and a weapon and spell each run which can change depending on what you find whilst in each dungeon. The slight variance comes in the weapons, each playing slightly different and each now coming with their own special attack. Hammers are slow but high damage, daggers are the opposite and so on. Once you've cracked the rhythm of each enemy, runs become degrees of success where no hit runs are rewarded with more materials at the end. The cult management side of the game is where a lot of my own gameplay came from. Followers are 'saved' from the runs into the wilderness and then pop back at your base ready and ripe for indoctrina- er, I mean re-education. Followers are fully customisable and come with a variety of perks and forms. Followers can then be sent to work within the cult to farm, gather wood, stone; with the new update, Sins of the Flesh, followers can now cook and brew drinks. The amount of followers you have directly relates to your own power and the rate at which you can unlock new zones and upgrade through the tech tree, so keeping them alive and happy is a priority.In upgrading your temple and cult, you gain access to a choice between abilities. For example, after gaining a point in your cult you can choose to either sacrifice followers, gaining more devotion, or holding a funeral for already departed followers (followers can age and will actually die of old age, which is also affected by cult perks). This does bring some replayability to your games to see what the other effects do, but in my opinion some are objectively better than others so there won't be that much variance. The update I mentioned before, Sins of the Flesh, added some new features namely a new resource, Sin. Getting these Sin points involves making your followers do sinful acts such as dancing naked round your bonfire, competing in fights to the death and also engaging in cannibalism. Followers can also now 'couple' with each other and produce children born and raised in the cult, letting you choose their perks. Outfits for your followers were also added. All of these made for really great additions that  out some lacking parts of the game. Overall I love Cult of the Lamb, it's gorgeous, cutesy art style juxtaposed to it's grim themes make a really fun and engaging theme. Shout out to the soundtrack by Riverboy also, firmly one of my favourite OSTs! Do you want to become a cult leader? ...

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this is another in a long line of "light roguelike with another game tacked on" that's been happening over the past few years like Boyfriend Dungeon and Going Under, where it doesn't really commit to either idea well. The actual roguelike combat ("Crusades") have incredibly poor balancing issues, and the cult management is bland and uninteresting.On crusades, you start with a random weapon and spell, with additional affects as you get upgrades, except that if you get two that apply different effects, only one applies, and if you have multiple sources of the same effect, like poison, they don't actually do any extra damage. Why would I bother with a poison weapon that does 5% of an enemy's HP when it takes 3 swings to kill them with a normal weapon? On top of this, the weapon "upgrades" feel completely meaningless, granting a 0.1 damage increase per level. Most enemies still go down in the same amount of hits when you go up a weapon level, and if you go back to cleared zones for faster clears, tough ♥♥♥♥, the enemies all got stronger so any upgrades you got are not useful.Invincibility Frames are another glaring issue, they exist, sure, but their timing and the brief stun on hit makes it more likely for you to get hit multiple times. This is best exemplified with the fly belching frogs, when they jump on you, damage you, then burp out 20 flies and damage you again in less than half a second.Spells are either long range missile attacks that do good damage, or short range AoEs that do next to no damage, and require you to be right up in enemy's attack ranges.Then the simulator. It's just boring. Oop, you gotta get these supplies to build your structures that give you a 5% boost to building more structures! You wanna get a slow trickle of them over time with the buildings? They only last like two days, so you don't even break even due to the gold cost. Rituals feel super niche like Ocean's Bounty, or the one where you automatically build all incomplete buildings, and just feel kinda lame.Leveling followers is just tedious, and as you get more, you can't spend all day dancing and bribing them, or else that's ALL you'd do. I let my faith deteriorate to the very bottom after doing an extended run of the first area, but all it took was a single day of rest and a meal my worshipers liked and then it was back to full. It felt like the decisions I made to micromanage the cult on a daily basis didn't matter beyond doing one routine task, and not a variety of methods.Overall, it's cute, but that's about it. Definitely not a $25 game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is okay. It's not a bad game, but it's not a rougelike/rougelite. It's a beat em up.You'll get boned by the perspective in combat a lot. A lot of the combat you'll notice is just kind of clunky. It's not responsive enough for you to make the most of your own skill set. You'll find yourself getting hung up on certain actions or weird delays in button presses. You currently can't rebind controls unless you use big picture. If you do go with a different controller scheme in-game you'll actually have an action conflict mid-game, as in, you'll use your curse when you try to recycle weapons/curses found in dungeon. There's still weird slowdowns during gameplay that require the game be restarted to be fixed. The slowdowns happen both on my desktop (a strong computer by 2022 standards) and laptop (midtierish by 2022 standards).You can change the difficulty midgame which is great for anyone looking for an easier/tougher game.Luckily, the visuals are cute as hell, the cult mechanics are decent, the side-stuff is okay.Marred by a lot of bugs in the beginning but at least so far, the devs seem to be active in keeping up with it.Currently, I don't think there's enough content to make it worthwhile.Wait till DLC comes out or maybe on sale, but I cannot say the value is there when compared to games with similar price. If you're looking for a game to play for a bit while you're traveling or something, it's okay, and you will likely enjoy it for a bit, but after a while you'll start to notice the lack of polish on the mechanics. The game is propped up by its ridiculously cute appearance and pretty novel cult system, but in the end, it's just okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, lovely art style, an okay game, and an interesting mix of genres.I wouldn't recommend it though, not unless it's on a 65% or more sale. The cult mechanics are interesting for a couple of days, but soon turn into tedious tasks.The "colony management" part of this game was an interesting idea, but poorly thought through. Having followers do the work for you is well enough, but there's no depth to it. The rebuilding aspect, where buildings collapse after x time, feels like a shoddy attempt at trying to get you to farm resources.The quest mechanics really bug me, especially the follower ones. Followers will give you quests that you literally mechanically can't complete. And you can either decline and take the penalty right there, or accept and take the penalty later. The quests also took away from the concept of choice in the game. I didn't *want* to use brainwashing on followers, but I had to because it blocked a quest line. I didn't *want* to marry my worst colonist (or really any for that matter) but the game decided to give me a follower quest to do it, that I couldn't afford the penalty on at the time. May have to Henry the VIII that marriage.If you're interested in side-quests and somewhat inclined to do all the tedious chores around your base whenever you're there, you'll progress through the development trees faster than through the dungeons. Having cleared dungeon 3 twice, I already had all the weapon/curse upgrades, and only lacking two of the buildings.The dungeons are are fun mix of hack-and-slash with a hint of bullet hell on some enemies. Navigating through them uses a map system like Slay the Spire, which means your choice about which path to take does matter. After a very short while the dungeons feel horribly repetitive. New enemies appear, new weapons and items appear, but mostly it's just a copy of generic item/mob A or B.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for the first few hours. The art design is flawless, the music is catchy, and the gameplay loop seems engaging without a lot of chores to do even in the city-builder mode. It doesn't take long for the under-cooked ideas to set in, though. For example, each dungeon run, you're stuck for a while with whatever weapon type you happen to roll at the beginning. For me, the gloves/gauntlets are basically unusable and the hammer is manageable but not really fun. For you it might be something different, but if you roll a weapon you don't enjoy, the first part of the run is probably ruined for you. You just rolled a "not fun" on the gameplay die. As more tarot cards and curses are collected, the chances of drawing the really useful ones for your playstyle actually goes down; you're punished for acquiring things and committing upgrades. The overall progression of the Cult is paced poorly, too. I am not the type to track down endless collectibles and side quests, but I had every major upgrade unlocked less than halfway through my play-through. You can see that my play time is only 17 hours as of writing this and there's nothing new for me to do. Other annoyances show through and reveal the team's focus was probably on getting a cute game out for YouTube and Twitch to fawn over rather than crafting a smooth experience for players. Cult members stack up on the map and make it impossible to interact with the one you want. The animation for acquiring a new cosmetic decoration can't be skipped and just led to me mashing keys impatiently to get back to combat. Nothing ever really changes despite collecting dozens/hundreds of things; the permanent upgrades to the Lamb are not impactful, so managing the Cult is mostly a waste of time (the only ones that actually help are the central ones that upgrade weapon level and the ones that upgrade the amount of mana or whatever it's called). And so on.It's a cute idea that needed more time in the oven or more competent game design. The art is great, especially the simplified facial expressions. But it's not really worth playing more than a few hours; I only finished it so I would feel comfortable reviewing it. I recommend waiting for a deep sale to buy it at single-digit prices. It's a fancy mobile game at best.
