_childDocuments_.review: With having played this game for quite a bit, completing all the achievements and done pretty much everything it has to offer, I really wanted to give it a thumbs upButThere are just way too many softlocks and bugs. Now, I have to mention that I play on a PC with a standard keyboard and mouse setup. My computer isn't weak by any measure, and the game should, in theory, run into no issues at all. However, compared to some controller gameplays I saw on YouTube and the fact that after the demo was published players requested the option/feature to have mouse controls, I feel like this playing style is a bit left behind by the developers. I've never experienced in any game, even in the first weeks of their release ,to be softlocked so often. The most reoccurring one is when I press the windows button, exit, and go back in the game again, my cursor is stuck in the upper left area and cannot be moved anywhere else until I don't exit and reenter again. Furthermore, this doesn't only happen when I quit with windows but also when sometimes traveling to a new area. For example, in the very beginning of the game, when we are led to the old temple ruins, this softlock always happens. Another thing I noticed was that the longer you play the game without quitting, the more likely you will encounter bugs. Generally, after half an hour of gameplay, I tend to encounter at least 2 bugs of various types.Although, bugs are not the only thing where mouse + keyboard users feel neglected. Sometimes you can use the left-click to accept certain tasks etc., alongside the button F; sometimes, you don't. The same goes for the movement of items or interface interactions where moving the mouse doesn't do anything, rather you are forced to move with your keyboard. The most egregious example of this is building. There, you can't use the mouse  and have to solely rely on WASD to move the objects and F to place them. This is incredibly annoying, since the grid we are placing the items on are very finicky and nailing the desired position might take a few tries. This overall discouraged me from decorating my base further because it is a nightmare of a patience game.In the end, I know the dev team is small, and truly, they have done a tremendious work for this game. It is fun, has a lovely art style, and a good enough story, however they should have thought about accessibility for other playstyles a lot more. With its current state, it feels like mouse and keyboard gameplay was a fast bandaid on the issue, yet not truly tested or given the care it needed. It probably was done due to time pressure, and that's understandable. Even then, I will have to not recommend this game to anyone who is not playing with a controller (and even then, you may run into bugs quite often) until all of these are fixed.(P.S. English is not my native language and while I tried my best to articulate my opinion the best I could if you run into something that makes you scratch your head grammar wise or contextually, I apologize)

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be one of those games we look at in the future and say "yea that was great. we need more." Though not truly simple it quite feels like something simple. actually feeling like a day to day life of cult within some aspects, while other aspects is great game. I can rather easily and happily say that it feels like a mix of binding of Issac and Animal crossing while keeping an intense uniqueness especially in art style that makes up for any mockeries, even to the ideas of "furry". Though each of those two games falls short, but this one builds and fixes what downsides i may see, the chores actually feel worthwhile in this game, you can see the people happy for what you do, but then the endless runs actually do affect your game making running feel like a worth of time. Now the game itself is fun, the community too is really quite nice (i am on the discord too). And with how down to earth and followers the Devs are with updates and such it does make it feel like a fun thing to be apart of within the communities. note i personally don't talk much but i do read the stuff.  I currently am breezing through extra hard and it feels perfectly for what difficulty it has. the combat is great, the movement is great, the controls, too, are great.  In the trailers there is a rather good cartoony artsyle, but in game itself it has a really well developed and consistently cute chaotic look to it. Each of the follower forms looks great but the part where you can customize more than just color makes it a very easy thing to make a cult of exactly what you'd like, whether you want a cult of your friends, horridly cute monsters or other.. chaotic wants. The cult itself especially with all the decorations and doctrines gives you the ability to actually customize your cult. Vegan tree lovers, Terrifying cannibals, or a prison of sinners, it is actually something you can well customize.  It almost feels like an A/B story game, where on one side you're hunting for retribution but the B story is going down into your character as you, a leader, will be. how different the vengeance of hunting the people who slaughtered you and the ideas of "these gods are bad" while also giving you the choice to be a good or bad god for your own followers is a grand fun thing to play with from a story point. Plus the lamb is cute as hell and i can dress him up

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this out when it was a free demo on Switch, and I wasn't really convinced either way. But really, this is an aggressively mid at best game with a lot of nasty traits, mainly animal cruelty that is really excessive, gross, and needless. You also can't avoid it easily, and you can't really avoid it at all if you want to unlock everything, so that's delightful. The presentation isn't super tight, but it's serviceable. The story isn't good, but it's acceptable. The intro isn't too indulgently long, but there are plenty of places where you'll be annoyed by how long it takes to do a sequence as a walking simulator that for some reason they thought would be a great idea to open with. The controls are okay, but they still feel unacceptably floaty for a game that should be polished to this level.It doesn't do anything exceptionally well. It's not that much fun to play. There's clearly a fixation with grossness and cruelty that it barely slaps a perfunctory cutesy aesthetic on, but it isn't enough to cover up how really unpleasantly nasty the developers seem to be. This says a lot about them, and I can't say I'm going to look at the publisher very kindly either.There are great ideas here, and some of the music is really inspired. But the game isn't, and it tries to sell on outrageousness, which it really doesn't have much of, and cuteness, which it doesn't really have at all. It's not cute. This is another case where the personality of a thing can make or break that whole appearance. It's cool if you like it, but I can't imagine being someone who does, because it seems like the kind of cultists you get that are cool with eating poop. I'm not impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: For a roguelike game, there is little to no replayability, for a colony game it leaves alot to be desired. There is still alot of issues in the game that aren't addressed.  Combat really isn't very fun, it gets dull pretty quickly.  The colony part has its charm for awhile but gets really dull.  The colony tends to just do whatever they want sometimes, not because they are lazy or don't want to but because of bugs requiring you to restart your game to fix.  The game can be literally be completed with basic structures, feeding them grass everyday.  There is no priority system for your followers such as a list, you just have to guess or remember what you told them to do.   Tiles disappear in your "base" which gets really annoying when trying to design it.  The build mode is a headache if you are trying to make your colony look nice, the blue tint in build mode hurts my eyes after awhile (yeah I know thats a "you" problem), moving around the grid in build mode is really jank at times, having to reopen the menu everytime to change the tile you're placing instead of having a action bar at the bottom you can drag stuff so you can place things quickly is really annoying.  The crusade part of the game gets very repetitive after awhile because the rooms repeat themselves so much with little to no variance.  While the game had its moments of fun, the bugs and bland moments overweighed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will segment this review into two parts, the quick part for those who want to know if the game is good or not and the bigger part.Spoiler free partSummary: I would recommend if you like dungeon crawlers and roguelike gamesCult of the Lamb is a dungeon crawler (binding of Isaac or enter the gungeon) combined with building strategies (timberborn). And this combination is to my surprise well made and fun. Theoretically, you can dump the base building if you don't like it but I can assure you, you will like it. Combat is swift energetic and can be quite challenging (depending on which difficulty you're playing). There is some story but I would say it's not that big but the devs say they're working on it. And finally, I would like to say the "simple drawn" graphics are just amazing. That's what I like about indie games, they're unique style of art and in this scenario, it works wonders. (when your cute little lamb performs a ritual where you sacrifice your cute little cat follower and your other followers start clapping and cheering it is just wonderful XD)The long analysisThe base building aspectI generally like this experimental combination of genres, but I must say I enjoyed the vision of the cult growing for like the 2 or 3 locations and didn't really bump into: "You need more cultists to open this door" but at the end of the game you need about 20 cultists to progress, so I needed to grind. There are rituals and other things but I really did not pay much attention to them (that doesn't mean they're not fun but I enjoyed more the combat side). But that's just me.The dungeon crawler aspectSo in Cult of the Lamb, you go to crusades for materials and to kill bosses to progress in the main story. I really like how different the scenery and enemies are in the four parts of the game. There are many playstyles you can choose, you can have a "mage build" or just depend on your demons to do all the work or you just hack and slash, That is for you to choose (if the RNG and cards are right). There are four weapons you can get at the start of your crusade and all of them have unique playstyles and abilities for you to master. So the crusades don't get repetitive and every crusade is unique in its own style.All in all cult of the Lamb is a great game and you should play it, or I might send some very hungry fellow your way :).Short story, Spoiler alert

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having put a lot of hours into this game, there's one thing that I really need to warn people about: It is incredibly hard to see what is happening on the screen in combat.The colors of each zone's background, terrain obstacles, and enemies are all extremely similar. Especially in the fourth level, where everything is solidly blue. Worse, as you level up you are able to get an increasingly number demon followers to assist you -- who clutter up the screen even more, especially directly around you. You know, where you might like to be able to pick out enemies.The fighting areas are for the most part incredibly small, and hemmed in by tons of scenery which is, you guessed it, basically the same color as everything else in the zone. The entire game is so cluttered it's a wonder your character can move (and if there's enough rocks on a screen, maybe it can't! although you can get a random tarot card to dissolve these and it's only more troubling than the rest of the clutter in a couple scenarios).There are ways to cheese through the levels, but at this point I feel like I am no longer playing the levels in any engaging way.I bought this on sale and I would tell past me to wait until it is further on sale. Like $8 or something. If you are thinking about playing this and haven't played Hades, go play Hades: better weapon selection, better level design, stunning colors, more responsive combat system. Fewer cute animals to sacrifice and no farming. Nevertheless! Unfortunately, if you are looking into this game you've probably already played Hades.

_childDocuments_.review: I already bought Cult of the lamb on Ps5... and for my friend... and for another friend... the point is, I want people to experience this game. Its incredibly fun and perfect for those into cuteness juxtaposed with dark and sinister themes. Game play is addictive, well balanced, and satisfying. Creating your cult the way you want it is so fun. Do you want it wholesome loving, or twisted and brutally violent? Do you want to work with your followers, or have them with for you? I can play this game over and over and still find value in a play through.I do have some criticisms though.The new weapon the Blunderbuss is really bad. It feels incredibly weak and can be very frustrating to use. The reload mechanic makes sense, but it gets really annoying when I run out of ammo and try to shoot, just for the reload progress to reset. It sounds really fun on paper to try to time your shots and keep a rhythm to your attacks, but if you mess up once, you lose all momentum. That on top of its pitiful attack damage. ON THE CONTRARY, the blunderbuss is ESSENTIAL if you use the Fleece of the Berserker. Its actually overpowered with that fleece. The range keeps you safe from risking getting hit, and its ability slowing down time and increasing the range makes any battle room a breeze. With that said, the blunderbuss needs to be reworked a little.The alcohol addition feels tame. Its very funny and I get enjoyment out of it, but it feels useless at times.With all the new building additions the size of your cult feels very tiny. I constantly have to rearrange. I'm thinking of doing another play through without decorating my cult, which sucks to say because you can make some really cool looking cults. A size increase would be more than welcomed.Overall, this game is great. Every update gets me excited. The developers obviously care for their game and continue adding additions that fans love. If you don't have it, I would recommend doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: When I launched this game for the first time, I played it non-stop for like 7 hours stright, which hasn't happened to me for several years at this point. This game is VERY addictive, and you can easily see why: the animations are satisfying, the colors are lush, the whole gameplay loop of running through dungeons and bringing stuff back to build your settlement just feels so smooth and natural. The settlement shenanigans quickly become the more important part, given that they lead to more of both upgrades and fun moments, but the combat segments don't feel lackluster either, they are pretty fun and challenging at times. The game doesn't go too deep with its systems, but the main story isn't long enought for this to take a toll on the experience. The only gripe I have with the game is the fact that some combat strategies seem obviously inferior to others. It feels like some of the weapons and spells simply exist to dillute otherwise a very powerful loot pool so that you don't constantly get fireballs and crit weapons to plow your way through the rooms. This power level divergence is a necessary measure, but I still feel like the weapon/spell pools could use some tweaks so that discrepancy isn't between getting the better or worse stuff, but rather getting stuff that significantly alters your playstyle in a way that is still viable. The game is otherwise fantastic, and it is super engaging all up until you beat the final boss. This is when the post game content starts, and it gets kinda repetitive/grindy, as you essentially repeat everything you've done in the main plot but with a difficulty modifier. I feel like counting the post-game content as a full-fledged downside would be unfair, but I cannot just omit it either. Overall this is a great pick if making sacrifices to the eldrich gods while cute animals ♥♥♥♥ all over the place seems like your type of pastime

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, enjoyable experience that casually meshes town management mechanics of games like Animal Crossing and a much less depth-filled rogue-like ARPG titles. If you are looking for in-depth combat and synergies similar to Hades or Binding of Isaac then you may wish to look elsewhere. The game is a balancing act of combat-lite experience used to break up the cult management aspect of the game. The town management is the core of the game experience. It is well designed and fun to play though some looking for in depth combat like over Rogue titles will be disappointed (it is rogue-lite in nature too). I don't feel like it was a bad choice and I welcome the casual feel as it is a very well-balanced design decision, that keeps the combat from feeling too developed and others will be turned off of. The main aspect is time management and town management with combat feeling like a seasoning thrown into the recipe. Just the right amount though some will not like the lack of depth in that regard. The cult options are vast and while I can't say that options may feel one sided at times where one outweighs the other, the game feels casual enough of an experience to let you build as you wish yet not so inconsequential that your choices don't matter either. It's so much fun to craft your cult and the town they reside.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly charming and fun rogue-like. Meta-upgrades and a big focus on managing your own cult with lots of fun ways to interact, design and manipulate your followers. A mixture of never having the same run of battling enemies like Hades and managing your cult, money and food similar to Stardew Valley.The story may not be that intricate. It serves its purpose and keeps you engaged in wanting to find out more about the world, though. Side quests, secrets and seasonal content included. The best part: The devs are not even done yet. Even though there is already an immense amount of fun content to play through. Their Roadmap shows two more big updates. It's gonna be awesome. A must-play for every rogue fan =)

Once you've got the basics set up it pretty much just runs itself, and what you're left with at that point is a mediocre Hades / Children of Morta style game that lacks interesting weapons or skills. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Cult of the Lamb, I was thoroughly impressed by the game's engaging gameplay mechanics and unique aesthetic. The blend of strategy and simulation gameplay is executed excellently, allowing players to manage their own cult with a range of options and decisions that impact the story and gameplay experience.One of the most impressive aspects of the game is its distinct art style. The graphics are colorful and detailed, with the dark and whimsical tone of the game perfectly captured through character and world design. The sound design also adds to the game's immersive atmosphere, with an eerie soundtrack and unsettling sound effects that enhance the overall experience.While the game's difficulty can be challenging at times, I found it to be a satisfying and rewarding experience overall. The cult-building mechanics are robust and offer plenty of opportunities for strategic decision-making, making each playthrough a unique experience.In conclusion, Cult of the Lamb is a highly enjoyable game that stands out for its engaging gameplay mechanics, unique aesthetic, and well-crafted narrative. Fans of strategy and simulation games will find plenty to appreciate, and the game's overall quality and attention to detail make it a standout title in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game.I'm one of those people who enjoys the serotonin boosts that come with achievements. Especially if I manage a 100% game completion. However, a lot of games have a tendency to make achievements somewhat...unachievable...for the very average, not so good gamer like myself.Cult of the Lamb does not do that. It is the absolute perfect balance of grindy, fun, and achievable. It doesn't lock achievements by difficulty, number of runs, or anything of the sort. Absolutely everything is achievable as long as you're willing to grind for it. And, honestly, this game is so fun and so beautiful that grinding does not feel at all like a chore. It feels welcome and enjoyable.I wish more games would make their achievements easier to, well, achieve. Seeing that 100% next to a game is so incredibly cathartic, but as a (relatively) low-skill gamer with not a lot of time, it becomes frustrating to continuously fail. For example, Destiny 2 is another one of my favorite games, but the seasonal light level grind is so exasperating that it makes me unwilling to play the game. There needs to be a balance, and Cult of the Lamb has achieved that balance.I love love love love love this game more than words can describe. GOTY in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its up-front warning on load, this game actually does  require a controller to enjoy, and works better than most games of the genre when it comes to KB&M support: UI elements have hover effects, your lamb aims in the direction that the cursor is pointing, not the direction that they're moving, and it's possible to navigate through menus using just the mouse.It's not perfect, though, and doesn't quite meet the high-bar that  established; the lamb doesn't  the cursor, so it's hard to see where you will be attacking, and the movement systems will occasionally conflict - for example: placing buildings doesn't really work with the mouse, and you need to half-and-half with the keyboard to place things correctly.  KB&M still feels like a 2nd-class citizen, but it's definitely not unplayable.The gameplay itself is fine - if you like rogue-lites then there's no reason you won't like this one!  The base-building aspect is functional but not super satisfying - but it doesn't detract from the game at all, and sets a nice pace between improving your cult and going on subsequent runs.The art style is really nice, but can make it quite hard to see what's going on - but never to the point that it's frustrating (at least on normal difficulty).
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: The Awesome:- Catchy music.- Fantastic art style that pioneered and innovated.- Addicting gameplay that mixes classic roguelike elements (though very simplistic) with a twisted version of an Animal Crossing village.- Simple story that has just enough substance to stay engaging without being too distracting.- Just the right amount of content for you to want to see all of it without it becoming too repetitive.- Post-game content (somewhat similar to Terraria's Hard Mode) that gives you additional 10+ hours of gameplay and story.- Almost flawlessly executed local co-op, virtually seamless and 100% completable with a friend from the start to the very end.- Two additional game modes with increased difficulty as an incentive to replay the game one or more times.    The So-So:- Lack of depth to combat: you wouldn't want to stay longer to experience more of it.- The roguelike part of the game is much weaker than the village part: there's little to no variety from one run to another.- The cult depends on you way too much early game.    Though flawed, the game is very charming and unique. Its edgy-cute aesthetic hit just the right string in my soul, making it one of my favorite games ever. Highly recommend it.

Players will find themselves emotionally invested in the outcome of their cult and the fate of its members, creating a sense of attachment and investment in the story.The game's innovative gameplay, charming art style, and captivating story make Cult of the Lamb a standout title that is well worth playing. _childDocuments_.review: Sozo? More like RIP Bozo.Say No to drugs, kids.Bit of a rant further down.Been playing since Launch day. (Pre-ordered)Good game for a rogue-like style. _childDocuments_.review: I don't understand this game. And I kinda feel that developers don't understand it either."Farm" part of this game seems fun at first, even though it is a bit wacky. You cannot automate most of the operations and some of them become tedious. Why can't I rebuild my mines/lumber mills straight away? Why do I need to empty their chests (that takes tangible amount of time, especially if you already did it a couple dozen times), go to the building post, select the building in the interface, drag it over half the town a place it? And I even can't upgrade it straight away - I need to wait for it to be built. Ugh. There's a lot of stuff like that - and you can't skip most of animations you already seen for fifteen times. With game getting more laggy and slow-loading with every passing day it became the very reason I decided to stop playing it - and to post this review."Rogue-lite" part of this game is lacking. It's fine, it's sometimes fun, but it's just a bit shallow and... Repetitive? I have ~500 hours in Isaac, I know my repetitiveness.And the strangest part of it all is progression. It was fine for the first ~10 hours - I felt like I'm moving somewhere. But then I unlocked all character perks even before beating the second boss. Like.. Okay? By the time I started attempting the third one I already had everything upgraded to the limit. "Farm" became obsolete whatsoever, there were no reason to keep my followers happy and, well, alive. Half the game was over even before I reached any conclusion on the other part of the game. I don't understand what was the intention for that.And all of that doesn't consider the fact that the game is really buggy, to the extent I never expected from such type of games, especially the ones being tested by content creators for weeks before release.Best part of this game is the whole "cute satanism" concept and you can easily get all of that from their trailers and maybe one short letsplay. Apart from that, I wouldn't recommend you spending any more time (or money) on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very approachable with a varied enough gameplay loop. Aesthetic is beautiful, and there's enough going on in the world to make it interesting. Progression is paced very well, and exploration is rewarded. I can't not play it for a few hours whenever I pick it up. It'll be one of a handful of games I actually bother to 100%.The only real complaint I have is the animations. The visuals and audio are all gorgeous, but there are a lot of animations in the non-combat portions, almost all unskippable. They were enjoyable the first hundred times, but taking care of the daily tasks once you get a bigger cult going takes way longer than necessary.All said, I highly recommend this game if you like the aesthetic and/or genre. It's one of my all time favourites and has an incredible amount of charm to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really cannot say enough good things about this game. I am not into dungeon crawler games. Hades held nothing for me. But this game? Freaking golden. It's got base building, interactions with followers, farming, and in so many ways you can choose your own path and craft your own cult following. It's not all sacrificing of followers if you don't want to play that way! I see so many people playing that way, but I did not feel forced to do too much of that and so my enjoyment of this game is through the roof. The balance of this game is like a really, really good D&D experience. The sound design is perfection. The game art is unique and appealing. The fighting and weapons are very well balanced and includes LOTS of different styles of fighting! The different weapons require you to strategize your hits differently and I find this both challenging and continually engaging. I have not beaten the game yet, but I am very close and I am eager to see how this story turns out. I can't stop playing this game! Way to go, devs! I applaud you!

_childDocuments_.review: For a casual game that doesnt try to be a rogue like, its fine. Its really fun even if I feel like a lot is still missing.Followers dont have personalities (SPOILERS: and even the final boss loses his personality when he joins your cult)Its definitely worth the 25 bucksIf you sell this as a roguelike however, its lacking A LOT. The game has a lot of blue balling when they lead you into something and then just end. There are no secret bosses(all the bosses in the game are very similar to each other in general), no secret zones, nothing. Even if you beat the major boss of the area, the game lets you continue further into the dungeon, just to have the same things stand in your way. No new enemies, resources, bosses or anything worthwile.Same with little events like the gold statue during dungeons or certain NPC's, you always expect something cool to happenlike a secret boss but its always really underwhelming.Game in general is pathetically easy, you got so much space for the final phase of the final boss where just NOTHING is going on. Also the fact that theres only 5 weapons and no crazy combos is just kinda lame. Just making it sometimes do poison damage isnt a new weapon to me. The game just needs to go the extra mile and it would be one of the best, hopefully DLC will add that.As a standalone game for the price its great and fun! But it keeps trying to sell itself as a roguelikes, which it just doesnt deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is an action, rogue-like, funnily dark dungeon crawler with a mix of strategy. Developers Massive Monster have made a cracker of a game that a lot of people are going to thoroughly enjoy when it releases on August 11, 2022 on PC, Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch. Firstly, I would like to get this out of the way before I dive into the review. I generally do not like playing this type of genre. Endlessly hacking this and that to get more items to then hack more things is not something I enjoy when it’s packaged in this way. Plus… I’m generally not good at this genre of game. So going into this, I had a fair amount of bias. But, I’m quite happy that I put my ego in my back pocket on this one. Cult of the Lamb is not only interesting, but it’s also fun and engaging.You play as an adorable lamb who has been given a second chance by a locked-up powerful being know as The One Who Waits. You’re charged with getting revenge, freeing the chained-up powerful being and creating a large cult following so they can be worshipped. There are four other ruling bishops/cult leaders who are getting in the way of this goal and your job is to crush them. There’s a lot of religious-like text and speech which delves into prophecy, how to treat followers and how the world is governed. You also get hints that the being you are serving is bad, but you don’t care because the other four bishops killed you and your race off.One thing that stands out is that the game is brutal in the sense that you can sacrifice your followers, let them die or even force them to work even if they’re sick. While playing through the game, the background narration is encouraging you to manipulate your followers as you wish. However it is also in your interest to keep them alive so you can make them farm and worship. In-game you’ll need to gather wood, mine stone, farm food and produce money. You set up an altar which your followers will pray at, and based on the level of your town, you’ll get town upgrades or perks for your character. The more you keep alive, the faster you will grow!There are two ways to kill your enemies; using a melee weapon, which has different attack abilities such as poison or life-steal, or spells, which can be targeted or have an area of effect. On top of that, you will get perks from cards and by using rituals to get things like extra health.The town’s progression is based on levels and it has a tree-like structure. It’s fairly easy to figure out what you need to build – just make sure you place similar things close together. For example, the followers can’t water certain plants if it’s not next to a farm placement. Building the town is not a side thing you can dismiss but a large part of the game. You will need to not only hack your way through enemies but also tend to your town and followers.The combat is fun and easy to manage as it’s all based on your keyboard, and there’s no mouse involved. The different melee options, spells and cards you’ll receive through the game allow you to progress whilst it gets harder and harder. This all adds up to a balanced and well thought out game.The artwork throughout Cult of the Lamb feels unique and well suited to the style. The town is bright and bustling, whilst dungeon-crawling areas can be menacing and quite dark. The style also matches the cute/adorableness of the lamb whilst showing the dark side of what is actually going on, and the power struggle. The sound is also just as good and matches the style, with satisfying chopping and hacking sounds to the soft coos of your followers.Overall, I REALLY enjoyed this game and once it releases later this week, I will continue to play it to enjoy the full scope of the story. It balanced base building, resource management and combat in an enjoyable way. It’s one of the few in this genre that I will continue to play.This review utilised a Steam key provided by Devolver Digital and Cult of the Lamb releases on August 11 on PC, Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch.#roundtablecoop

_childDocuments_.review: The game  is pretty nice.Artstyle and tone speaks for itself.Gameplay-wise it's very enjoyable and addictive. Combat is pretty solid, plenty of collectibles and satisfying progression. It also has a New Game+ kind of version with increased challenge. For comparison I beat almost all regular bosses on my first try, but the NG+ versions usually killed me more than I'd care to admit (though I was using the double damage mantle)The game is not without its flaws, however. This is a warning and contains some spoilers. If you value your playtime and sanity, just do the bare minimum for your cult, enjoy fighting through the 4 zones, beat the game and then go for the bad ending so you do not have to deal with the post-game or the late game cult management.My main complaint is that the cult management side of things has a lot of very tedious and annoying things about it. I'd go as far as to way it's terrible towards the later stages of the game. The cult mechanics require extreme babysitting even on normal difficulty. There's many daily routines you have to do to keep your cult happy and nourished, and even after you manage to find ways to automate it, there's still many repetitive daily chores to maintain faith and increase loyalty that you will spend 30% of your playtime doing the same 3 things over and over and over and over. Also, unless you make the right choices early in the game that allows you to completely freeze hunger and faith for a few days, you are barely going to be able to leave your cult for 6 minutes without ♥♥♥♥ hitting the fan. Having elders in your cult is basically a ticking time bomb. You go out on a "Crusade", get notifications that 1 or 2 elders have died. Sure, you think, your cult has positive attitudes about death, so they'll be fine. You come back to a cult with 0 faith with a couple of them having turned into dissenters which need to be imprisoned and reeducated. Now imagine this scenario happens basically every 15 minutes of gameplay. It just feels bad. Sure I can use fasting and brainwashing on my followers to prevent that from happening for a few days, but I feel like the drain is way too fast on basically everything, even on normal difficulty.Devotion from your followers praying is both extremely grindy and wasteful. If you have even a few followers praying to your statue the statue will fill up every 1-2 minutes and your crusades last 6-10 minutes, which is almost as long as a single in-game day. Why is this important? Well, you can only get 170 devotion from the main statue, and there's like 100 things to unlock, and after a couple in-game weeks the price of these new unlocks becomes in the several hundreds. In return the game gives you a few buildings that can hold... 10 devotion each.On top of this, Cultist's levels are represented by the loyalty meter, which gives you bonuses in a few different areas, BUT raising loyalty is extremely tedious and time consuming. There's like 5 daily interactions you can do with a single follower once per day, and a ritual that can raise all of them at the same time, but even with all the daily babysitting and investing all your time and resources into increasing one follower's loyalty, it can take you as long as 7 days of devoting half your playtime just to max him out. There's some ways to raise the loyalty of multiple followers at a time but each of them except a ritual amount to a 5-10% daily increase to the next level. These followers also have life expectancy, and usually they do not live longer than 20-30 days inside your cult. There's ways to extend the life expectancy or even make followers immortal, but these range from rare to extremely rare. And to get these, you have to go through the vicious cycle of going on a crusade to kill a boss, come back to deal with the disasters that happened to your cult when you're gone for 6 minutes, and then repeat this all over again for the next 5 hours of playtime to get maybe one of the items that will extend or immortalize one of your followers.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb combines dungeon crawler and base builder into a pretty fun package. Spared by an imprisoned god, you are made into the new leader of their cult. You build up a dark empire full of adorable creatures that decide to follow you after you rescue them "because of the implications" if they don't. The art style is fantastic. It's very unique in a horrific-cute sort of way. The character design are again unique and weird. They all talk like the old N64 Rare games with just noises instead of speech which works well in this twisted world.The overall gameplay is fairly shallow; but engaging. In the dungeon crawling sections your options are a basic attack, a dodge roll, and your "curse" which is a unique ability, most of which are ranged attacks. You progress through a short 5-10 minute dungeon, fight a boss, and then return to your cult. The dungeons are fairly easy on default and I would recommend going up a difficulty from normal if you've played a lot of games like this (switchable on the fly). I died a few times, but never felt like progress was impossible or that the enemies were unfair.After a "run" you're teleporting back to your cult where you indoctrinate new members, give dark sermons, preform rituals, upgrade various perks, and assign duties to your followers. Again, every part is easy to grasp but engaging. When you've got your cult in a good place, it's back to the dungeons. There is also a bit of exploration of the overworld where you meet other strange denizens of the realm for various side quests and unlockables.  What this game is not is an endless rougelite. There is a clear ending, and while there are some sidequests to do afterwards. and there is a sort of endless mode, that's not really really the point. I beat a couple of the post game bosses which were basically just another mini boss and had no real desire to continue the "endless mode"; didn't feel like there was a point and the combat and weapons are not deep enough to really encourage experimentation. The constant swapping between dungeon crawling, cult management, and exploration of the overworld keep the game interesting. The day-night cycle gives a sense of  progress and urgency. You're constantly thinking about what to improve on in your cult and what you need to harvest from dungeons. I thoroughly enjoyed Cult of the Lamb, and recommend it to anyone interested in dungeon crawlers and base builders.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a load of fun. When I heard there would be a sim game with a Cthuluesque (cyclopean? eldritch?)  veneer, I knew I was in for a treat regardless. I didn't think I would be getting some of the snappiest roguelike brawler mechanics I've seen in a long while on top of a very addictive sim game.The roguelike portion of the game is very fun. All the weapons feel unique and have strengths and weaknesses to each. My personal playstyle preference meant I usually went with the dagger or sword to have next to no lag and dash around, taking full advantage of iframes. Some slower ones make more sense if you want to be a caster or tank. One really nice touch is the tunic system. This gives you challenging powerup mechanics to play around with and lets you lean further into your favored power fantasy. My favorite was the one that offers you an unlimited stacking damage boost for every kill you don't get hit.Bingers, beware: the sim game will keep you saying, "just one more day." I was surprised but satisfied with my progress in the sim portion of the game: it might need some tuning. I was left feeling overpowered by my endeavors in the sim game. My gain in the sim outpaced the brawler by merely talking to and maintaining my villagers/tasks consistently every day/night cycle. Nonetheless, some of the random events that happen later in the plot still gave me a scare. Pay attention to your progress in the brawler half of the game for more than a few days/night cycles, or you'll max out the sim too early.Lastly, there are the plot and aesthetics, which I will lump together because they are so closely intertwined. The story is good, if not predictable. But the aesthetics are striking: they are simultaneously macabre and adorable. I've heard many concerned that the cuteness coupled with cult-like violence might be off-putting, but that's not what is happening here. The blood and gore are not over the top. Moreso, this game is just dark: more Nightmare Before Christmas or Billy and Mandy than Happy Tree Friends.All in all, this is my favorite indie game of 2022. If you liked Stardew Valley, you'd surely be hooked by this too!

Preheat the oven to 180C. Grease and line two 20cm sandwich tins.2. For the cake, place all of the cake ingredients except the boiling water, into a large mixing bowl. _childDocuments_.review: Before I talk about it-I'm not a huge fan of rouge likes, I tend to gravitate to "rouge likes" like Risk of Rain 2 and Deadlink (which I highly recommend if you're into rouge-like fast-paced shooters). _childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a quintessential game in the genre of hack n slash roguelikes/lites. Progression in the form of managing and maintaining your cult is a lot of fun and serves as a good break between runs to increase your power, grow your land and cult, and progress through the story. My only critique is that the amount of un-skippable micro-cutscenes is a little ridiculous. I wouldn't be surprised to learn that by the end of my playthrough, multiple hours of that time was spent waiting for these animations to finish. Pretty much every interaction in the game has an animation tied to it that you have to sit through. Be it collecting a dozen loyalty rewards from your followers after sermons, picking up a god tear for the umpteenth time, handing in said god tears, performing the same ritual you use every 3 in game days to maximize whatever progression point you are working towards at that time, picking up any item in runs, etc etc etc. These animations are well done and fun to sit through once or twice, but they grow old fast, and a lot of them you will have to watch maybe even hundreds of times through your playthrough. It's very repetitive. After the first time, they just become pointless time sinks that should be skippable. Some of the most egregious examples to me were definitely having to hand in bulk amounts of god tears, picking up the 3 god tears that drop at the end of post-game bishop runs (I don't need to watch a Legend of Zelda chest cutscene for every tear I pick up oh my god) and collecting loyalty rewards. Despite this, Cult of the Lamb is still a fantastic game. If you've played games like Hades, you'll probably like this one. Part of me just thinks that it could have respected my time a little better.

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating and engaging game that blends elements of a rogue-like with a management simulator."Cult of the Lamb" is a challenging and rewarding game that will keep you hooked for hours on end. The gameplay is fast-paced and exciting, with a wide range of weapons, abilities, and power-ups to discover and experiment with. But what really sets "Cult of the Lamb" apart is its innovative management system. As the leader of a cult, you'll need to recruit and manage your followers, build and upgrade your base, and make important decisions that will affect the fate of your organization.What's more, the outcomes of your rogue-like runs can have a direct impact on your cult, either positively or negatively. The management gameplay is incredibly intuitive and easy to pick up, even for players who are new to the genre. The graphics are bright and colorful, with a charming, cartoonish style that perfectly complements the game's quirky premise. The sound design is excellent, with a memorable soundtrack and a wide range of sound effects that bring the game world to life.Overall, I highly recommend "Cult of the Lamb" to anyone who enjoys management simulators, or just unique and innovative gaming experiences. It's a game that's easy to get lost in for hours on end, with enough depth and complexity to keep even the most hardcore gamers engaged.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the cave-exploring mini game in Stardew Valley? Now expand it to the full game and add some cult elements then you get Cult Of The Lamb, a hybrid dungeon crawler seasoned with base-building, and of course, cute animals doing questionable things. As a recently sacrificed Lamb, your death is postponed by The One Who Waits for he has another plan for your life -- a servitude of freeing him in exchange for your immortality. Now you must build a cult and smite all the heretics standing in your way. I cannot stress enough how much I love this game. From its cartooney artstyle and bopping soundtrack, to responsive control and balance between two genre, these elements blend together well. The cute-things-doing-horrible-things Happy Tree Friends style is just the cherry on top. The game does have some issues regarding pacing and minot bugs, buy ultimately they do not hinder your enjoyment for this cult classic. I highly recommend it.Again, I really love the art direction and  addicting soundtrack. For a roguelite, I hardly get tired of either one. You just have to experience these kind of feeling yourself.Dungeon-crawling and base-building are inherently different genres of video game. It's nice to see Massive Monster manages to strike a balance between the two, and create a sort of "shifting mind" gameplay. Dungeon-crawling offers tight combat and resource hunt, while Base-building gives you the freedom to customize your cult. If you are tired of combat or simply being frustrated by roguelite element, you can take your time to manage your "insert base name", tending some crops, constructing dome decorations, fulfilling the needs of those little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mean followers, and conducting various concerning rituals. And vice-versa, if you are itchy for some fighting or running short of some supplies, feel free to throw yourself into the holy crusade for your cult and smite those heretics. I know this isn't a revolutionary idea since almost every MMORPG has some sort of personal quarter or others of similar design, but as a core gameplay loop I think Cult Of The Lamp does a great job.→Those  I mean followers know your love towards them so they keep exploiting it but they are your  I mean followers and you love them so much you will fulfill their needs anyway.→You ever just play Knucklebone so much that you forget that you have a cult to tend to?→Really cute animation.→There is a dedicated "Baa" button.→Interesting and equally questionable side quests.→So many followers' forms for you to choose.→The noise NPCs make, I love them!This is my only issue about the game. It seems like progression and unlockable upgrade system need some rebalance. For my experience, by the time I reach the third dungeon I have already unlocked two-third of the upgrade system for both the base and the arsenal for crusading. I know I did compliment the dev for finding the balance for dungeon-crawling and base-building, but the progress-and-reward ratio need some adjustment. Because I already have most of upgrades unlocked, I find my self replaying later dungeon less than I do with earlier levels. Instead, I focus more on taking care of the cult and other minor stuff, which could be a good thing since there are several things to do outside your cult.→Tarot cards should always draw one offensive and one utility/defensive. I don't need extra resources gain or map reveal when I really need more firepower.→Sometimes, talking to a follower who is in the middle of dropping resource will cause the camera to focus on the follower instead of The Lamb, even when the interaction is over.中文小簡評→你以為這是邪教模擬器？不！這是幼稚園模擬器。你得幫你的信徒煮吃的、把屎把吐、滿足他們一堆詭異的要求。(我全部都做了因為我太愛這群小渾蛋。)→可愛的畫風、可愛的動畫、一聽即上癮的配樂、可愛的東西做可怕的事情。→Roguelite地城探險和家園系統能找到平衡點。→諸多信徒模樣可供你隨意更改。→遊戲節奏似乎掌握得不夠熟練，到第三座地城我已經解鎖三分之二的東西，→希望抽塔羅牌時可以抽一張攻擊型和一張防禦型/功能型來選，有時真的很需要火力加持而不是顯示全圖或資源加成。

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Quest Builders (It’s not a dungeon crawler but the management systems and religion references resemble both titles)Moonlighter (Has similar system of going to dungeons at nights and managing your shop during day)Dave The Diver (More polished gameplay and minigames and much more easy management system) Fabulous Fear Machine (Meta jokes of some dark occult appears in this game as well)Palworld (The pal system and the pleasure of being evil the way using pals resembled pawn system to me)The Cult of the Lamp is a merge of dungeon crawler, craft and crew management game. The game presents pretty solid setting using religious themes with a satire telling. The conflict between cute visuals and vile attitudes of the characters actually works pretty well for the theme. Also, this blend makes the setting more fun to consume. The game starts with a scene of our dear lamb being a sacrifice for the elder Bishops. The lamb, who is also the last of its kind, has been chosen for this ritual and being victimised by the followers of the bishops. Right at the death moment of the lamb, the forsaken Bishop (One Who Waits) occurs in front of him and tells our character to rise and get revenge of him. Then our character comes back from death and slays the followers. That way our lamb starts its crusade against the bishops and we start to collect pawns to create our cult. With this basic premise the game sets our goal to kill the bishops and manage our cult.As you can guess from the explanations above the gameplay consists of two separate parts. At one hand we are going to crusades against other cults. This part plays as a classic isometric action title with some bullet hell challenges. In these crusades our character can carry one weapon and speel. There are several types of weapons in the game. Also, few of them have some little gimmicks to vary the gameplay. But the most obscure difference between them is attack speed, damage output, and weapon reach which is kind of dull for this kind of gameplay which requires repetitive gameplay. This dullness presents in the skill department as well. There are few skill types. To decrease this issue developers tried to give some spice with adding some weapon and spell upgrades such as having a critical hit chance or poison possibility on hit that you can get during the cult management part. Also, there are tarot cards you can collect each run that gives some advantages to you. These tarots cards and weapon upgrades actually bring good variety for gameplay, but they’re not enough to keep the gameplay fresh after a while.Each bishop has their own biome and their own three followers at their service. In each crusade we choose a bishop’s biome, that way we start to explore a randomly prepared map. These maps have some similarities to the ones you can see in Slay the Spire. This is a good addition to gameplay. Each stop in maps provides you a place to explore, shopping spot, healing spot or another event to explore. This way the difficulty of the runs or the materials you can get during each run changes depending on your choice. Bishops have servants (Mini Bosses) three for each. Which makes plenty of variety on the boss section, and worth mentioning.The management part of the game has similar mechanics most of the same types of games has. You gather pawns and materials during your crusades for crafting new things and building a cult. Then you gain some buffs for your crusades. Each pawn has their loyalty and they also have a life cycle. To implement this life cycle, they included a day-night cycle. This also increases difficulty for the management, so some might like this. There is a build tree for you to get new upgrades, but you need to have some Devotion as a currency. The need of Devotion increases with each upgrade you make. As a result, it becomes tiresome at some point. This issue occurs for every element of the management part. So later the game suffers to let you get upgrades for the next run. As a problem these blooms during the mid game at most. During you have some decent number of pawns you realise you need to lookout for them, and to do this and go into another run you realise you need to automize some of the things like making food for followers. But it’s not that simple if you haven’t spent your devotion on this department. You also have a church to pray, do some rituals and some other things that can give some buff your cult, village management or crusades. Lastly, the team behind the game makes a decent thing to update it constantly with free contents. They added a kind of New Game+ mod after beating the game. Also, last update lets you make babies in the cult, so it doesn’t need to add anything more. Right? Jokes aside it’s definitely a fun addition and the team knows what goes nice with the theme. Another thing is there is a dice mini game that has simple rules and likeable that you need to play at least once if you played the game. In the end I really recommend this game to people who did like run based games, and want some flavour, to vary the game and do some other stuff in a single game.

_childDocuments_.review: The fighting is fun, although you have to get used to aiming where you hit with your mouse instead of simply clicking. Once you keep that in mind, though, fighting feels very satisfying and although I hate grinding, I love doing the extended dungeons to see what loot I can get. It feels even more worth it because each bit of loot helps with the base building, and I love making my pretty, little village with its nicely aligned roads, houses, and sections. One is my town building section, one is my neighborhood, one is my farm and work building section, and one is the religious quarter with the temple and the graveyard included. I have flowers and statues and lights, and my villagers like to sit by the plants and read happily, and it makes me so happy they're enjoying it.This is a great mix of rogue dungeons, building your arsenal, and managing a village. I do tend to play on easy mode because I'm not a good fighter but I still really enjoy it. I like that you can choose between being good or evil or in between; I always play a good leader. And, the DLCs are all great, too.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have only played this game for a little while (about 2.5 hours), it is clear that it's an enjoyable gaming experience, complete with adorable and detailed artwork! I cannot wait to see what's to come. You have to be able to appreciate a bit of dark humor, as you are playing as a sacrificial lamb brought back to life by "the one who waits" (a devil-like deity) in order to build his cult of followers. You must fight your way through enemies of the Old Faith (including the four Bishops who sacrificed you in the first place and are the Bosses) to save followers and convert them to your cause. There is an exploration and combat aspect, but then there is the "farm game" aspect of tending to your followers, collecting items to build various things to help your cult, completing quests they give you, growing and cooking food, giving them sermons and blessing to raise your faith, etc. There is actually a lot more to it than it might seem on the surface! I am curious to play through the story and learn more and see where it goes!  So far, I would absolutely recommend this game if it appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Recommended.This game feels like a mix of Binding of Isaac roguelite design, mixed with a bit of hades/bastion gameplay and Dont Starve artstyle. Its fun, doesnt take itself serious, has good enjoyable combat, and is overall quite good. I do not regret buying it on release.The few downsides are:1. Its very easy to get "op" in the village part, making it almost impossible to lose. Some things (like money ritual) are incredibly overpowered. A lot of buildings arent really needed, as their function seems to require base game to be harder than it currently is.2. Performance is good overall, but stutters quite a bit in lategame, when you have a lot of followers in the base, or when you have a lot of fervor drops in the dungeons. _childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good! But it isn't without its flaws. The Roguelike gameplay is very shallow. There aren't any sort of "builds" to aim for. Rather, every upgrade you receive does the bare minimum to affect your gameplay (ex. 1.25x attack speed, two extra hearts, 1.5x speed up, etc). It feels like the Roguelike is more of a time-progression mechanic rather that a fully fleshed out experience, as when you come back from a crusade, your followers may have lost faith, gotten sick, died, etc. If you're picking up this game solely with the expectation of a deep, variable roguelike, I would look elsewhere.The most enjoyable part of this game for me was the Follower management, but sadly, it is also lacking in depth. You can't edit Follower traits when you convert them to your cult. They come with predetermined traits. You CAN however employ cult traits via doctrines that will be given to all of your Followers, but as far as direct Follower customization, you're restricted to name and form. Relatively disappointing; by the end of the game, I wasn't changing anything about my new recruits because at the end of the day, it doesn't really matter. They really just act like another warm body to extort for their dedication.One thing that doesn't make too much sense is the resource collection, and setting up resource collection stations for your Followers. When you create a mine, for example, you get a short period of time where a Follower can harvest stone for you. This is great, but the station itself actually breaks after a short time. It costs stone to create the mine, so by the time the mine self destructs, you're barely net positive in stone. I had the biggest problem with lumber, and I was constantly making lumber mills just for them to break and leave me marginally better off than before. I don't understand why the resource stations would break, especially later in the game when they become more expensive. I've given it a lot of criticism, but I genuinely enjoyed my time playing. The doctrines you can enforce, the rituals you perform, and the boss fights you take part in are all great. The game has a ton of charm, which I think is its biggest strong-suit. The dichotomy of these cute little animal creatures praising a literal demon is very funny, and the characters themselves are adorable. They knocked it out of the park in the art direction department.There doesn't seem to be a ton of replay ability at this time, so I don't foresee myself continuing to play. But hopefully they will continue to add to this game, especially in the end-game department.

_childDocuments_.review: Published by : Developed by : Cult of the Lamb is a games made by a fantastic indie studio Massive Monster, you'll play as The Lamb. Sacrificed to the old Gods and resurrected to take your vengeance at the Bishops who sacrificed you, with the power of the Red Crown and The Lost Flock that is your Cult, Cult of the Lamb.in Cult of the Lamb, the core gameplay design is divided by 2 Gameplay core which is Roguelite which is called Crusade and Colony Sim Building to build Your Cult. : in this mode you will have to fight your way through procedural generated Dungeons, every time you are starting a run you will given 1 main weapon and 1 skill (Cursed power).Between those stages in a run you will eventually encounter new weapon or new skill, sometimes you will encounter harvest items, new potential Cult Recruits, Interesting NPC, new Tarots card. Levels in Dungeons is always random and changes everytime you'll start one and you need to finish it 4 times and wins against these mini-bosses before you get to face to face with each of the 4 Bishops who sacrificed you.  : Cult Building is another core mechanic of the games you'll need to progress in order to continue through the story or helps you growing up your power for the Crusade. In this mode you will have to Indoctrinate different kind of cute animals, these Followers will helps you build your power through Worship and Farming, when Followers worship The Lamb statue they will give you Devotion which can be used to upgrade your Cult buildings and the Church Devotions is useful to upgrade your Lamb basic power and talents, these can be deliver via Sermon once for each day or through Rituals which can be unlocked by Doctrine and these Doctrine also affected by Church Devotions. Farming for rocks and woods will helps you upgrade your buildings and ways that you can manipulate or encourage your Followers to give your more devotions. With all this there is a catch however, all these Followers animals they all have their owns daily necessity such as Bed for sleeps. Foods for hungers, and well... Toilet. It seems at first glance all of these design seem to be like a chore but actually thats the Fun part, imagine having a bad day at your office and then you'll going home and play Cult of the Lamb to satisfy your inner masochistic desire. In Cult of the Lamb you can do ANYTHING to your Follower, from sending them to prison or just straight murdering them if they revolt against you. Harvest their cold rotten body and scraps those meat to feed the other Followers you hates, and occassionally sometime your Follower without no clear reason... they wants you to feed them scats... (LOL its true)Will you become a Savior of the damned with a Hope to bring Love and Peace for all the Living Beings. or Will you become a Tyrannical Lord bringing Destruction and Misery through Order and Cold Hearted Evil.the choice is yours to make my Lamb.Cult of the Lamb have a good sound design from every strike of the Blade or the Hammer your Lamb strike through the enemies and the hitting sound is truly well made and well thought, combine that with an excellent piece of Chill Lo-Fi beat between Dungeons and your Cult Base. This games truly makes you feels at home with the peoples you want to be with. All these excellent Soundtrack is made by a talented composer called River Boy (Kudos to you my friend! i grew up playing on the river oftenly when i was a little girl~)in Cult of the Lamb, you will found many NPC with unique looks and small lore attached behind them, this will helps you unlocks new Tarots card or other stuff such as Decorations, Follower Form, or Minigames (Knucklebones, a games of roll and dices and Fishing games)the games have this unique mechanic where your action suggested by The One who Awaits (they who resurrected you) should you obey them or not will makes the Final Battle being affected by it.Cult of the Lamb is filled with interesting NPC that it reminds me of a games called Undertale where these NPC is made with deep thought and unique ideas before they greenlit it. I'm glad to inform you that this games have a very quite good perfomance and can definetly run on any hardware older or modern PC, quite a few settings of the games from Texture, Bloom, Depth of Field, it seems to supports High Resolutions too, although the games maximum framerates is at 60. At the current time of writings. Cult of Lamb is still plagued by micro-stutter, heavy stuttering, crashes, and softlocked to progression or gameplay. Although... i'm glad by the grace of The Lamb the devs still adressing and patching the games with updates and hotfix once in a few days.-  : Cult of the Lamb can be finished under 10 - 20 hours or even faster like 4 - 8 hours if you are already knows what to build or the enemy or boss pattern during Crusade.-  : again Cult of the Lamb can feels very short with the amount of content it offer, if you are not reluctant to devote your heart in Colony Sim building mechanic. You might not enjoys this games because 80% of this games is based on Interacting and Building your Cult in opposite to 20% of the thrilling Roguelite gameplay of Crusade-  : for the amount of price (see below) you purchased and support for this games. Cult of Lamb offer a variety and exciting ways for you to enjoys your Cult growing and finish or progress the games in your owns pace.-  : as an indie games. This games truly understand how to price a games with its length and multiple ways you can finish it... Unlike so many Indie games where the fun and the value is not on the same page (I'm looking at you Stray) -  : River Boy... you sure not Jesper Kyd long lost brother ?-  : Cult of Lamb without a doubit is a hybrid of both Hades and Animal Crossing but somehow able to translate both games into a very Fun games! without the chores and the artificial difficulty of both games as this games featured multiple difficulty and encourage you to finish it with your own pace.-  : that must be the fastest in-game credits i have ever seen in video games... WOOW! for a small studio like this with small lists of team you can achieved probably the BEST indie games of all time without needing a comeback like No Man Sky.Cult of the Lamb truly is an emotional ride for me and as a Video Games have found a special place in my heart forever. I have been battling with my Depression and Suicidal feelings for long, medicine won't works anymore and i have been called several times for psychotherapy session to address the kind of illness and struggles i have daily, but Cult of the Lamb as a video games. Truly bring an enjoyment and messages for all peoples to keep trying their best in their life no matter what the situation is, just like The Lamb who keep trying the best to get back up and found the place The Lamb wants to be.With this oppportunity i want to thank all the entire team and staff that involved in the development of this beautiful games Cult of the Lamb. From the bottom of my Heart.Thank You Massive Monster, i am rooting and looking forward to all of your future projects and developments because i know you have made Cult of the Lamb with so much passion and love for all of us and your hardworks pays. Once again Praise The Lamb! and for everyone who reading this humble and far from perfection reviews i made.Thank you and i hope everyone have a long good life ahead filled with Blessings and surrounded by peoples who always love and cares about you.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and wow, what a good time! The theme and game play are top notch. I really enjoyed the balance between base building and combat. The battle mechanics were really fun with random weapons at the start of each crusade that is further randomized with tarot card pulls and idols. The boss fights have different mechanics that require the player to remain agile, so there's no tank and spank setups. Lastly, the art work is really nice. Hats off to Devolver! I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boi - this game is any eeeasy recommend!This is part Animal Crossing, part Hades style dungeon crawler - combat is fairly straightforward, the spells decently varied in utility - but what will definitely sneak up on you is how well the game balances the cult management systems and incentivizes you to evenly split your time between going on runs and running the cult at homebase.Also - the contrast between the cutesy characters and the eldritch abominations you end up slaying makes a for a game that'll definitely stuck with you for a while ~Edit: the new update made the endgame incredibly fun to chase - 11/10 game, definitely a must buy

_childDocuments_.review: I think I was too harsh previously not recommending it, despite its honestly small issues and nitpicks it's still a fun game with an amazing style and incredibly cute. If you like management games moreso I would recommend it as it's a lot more of the game than the combat imo.Previous review:Very surprised I'm rating this game down, after about 10 hours the game just stopped being enjoyable for me.- Over half the progression gets completed in less than 10 hours, makes half the things you do feel pointless- Managing your followers is cute and fun at first but just gets boring and annoying after a while, especially the further you play- The combat is incredibly shallow, there are barely any diversity in items, weapons, ect- Some of the upgrades are worded poorly and made me pick the wrong one, and these are irreversible- Feels like I'm not allowed to play the game and I instead have to spend 80%+ of my time getting food- Using actions on followers takes far too long to make it really worth doingThis game has an outstanding visual style, looks super cute and cool at the same time, at the start I was thinking this would be one of my favourite games, playing it more reveals how shallow and boring the game is unfortunately.If you get this 50% off or more then it can be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Hades had a baby with Stardew Valley  that’s really into Lovecraft Novels. Cult of the Lamb combines the fast-paced combat of Hades with the cozy, addictive life-sim elements of Stardew Valley—only this time, you’re running a cult. The game’s base building and resource management keep you on your toes, while the eerie, yet strangely adorable art style makes everything feel like a twisted version of Happy Tree Friends. It’s a wild ride where you’ll be balancing time management with fighting your way through dangerous dungeons, all while keeping your followers in line.The combat strikes a perfect balance between fun and challenging, never too easy but rewarding. This unique blend of action and management creates a one-of-a-kind experience that feels both chaotic and satisfying from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Very good. Ended up over levelling a bit by focusing a lot on the town-building aspect, but it's nice the game lets you progress however you want be it more dungeoning, or more town building. Because of my focus on the town I noticed I didn't have a lot of the issues to do with faith, hunger, etc that I have seen from other playthroughs. The combat is super fluid and fun, the spells and weapons are interesting. I did have some issues with early achievements and unlocks because I started playing from the demo before continuing on the full game, so I would suggest either just playing the full game right away (if you even think you might enjoy this game you most likely will), or if you do play the demo then start a new save file on the full game when you buy it to avoid any issues. The art and music are also both amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive cult-management roguelike.Pros:* Sacrifice cult members - Why? Because they're old or I felt like it, and they liked it!* Management of cult members doesn't feel like a chore* Easy to understand the concepts from building, fighting, managing, rituals, everything* Are you starving? Don't worry we just fasting* Different levels of difficulty* Cute animals that go bi beep blip blop* Different varieties of rooms and powersOther things to do: Simple minigame for gambling coins, fishing, screaming at your members, rituals, building and decorating your place.Cons:* Preferred weapons than others, but maybe this can  depend on your style as well* Short game. Possibly the longer you play this, it will fall off but those first 20 hours tho...* Not much to do once you reach the end, maybe start another game with higher difficulty, but other than that idk.According to the developers, there are active updates, so perhaps there will be more added in the future, but for the first 20 hours of playing this so far, it is highly addictive and I sacrifice sleep for this. This game is on a good path especially when future content gets released and hopefully is of high quality as well. If this goes on sale, it would be worth the grab. I bought this full price and no regrets whatsoever. Good and unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I didn't buy this on release is because I often find dungeon games near impossible to play due to my disabilities. I bought this first for my partner as a gift. I tried playing on easy mode and was pleasantly surprised to discover I could actually play and win, but I was still having fun! Even playing on my laptop with damaged keys and a slightly wonky older mouse instead of with a controller is both possible and enjoyable! The accessibility settings are also really good, and include less common options like dyslexia friendly fonts!As far as game design goes, I cannot describe how in love with the sounds I am. The details are so amazing, the music is already becoming some of my favorite music of all time, every little noise is so perfect and cohesive! The aesthetics are similarly well crafted and consistent. There's also a healthy balance of tutorials and learn as you play, with the more nuanced and complicated mechanics being explained simply and clearly.TLDR I am absolutely in love with this game because of it's design and my ability to play despite my disabilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, addictive, and fun. Every time I start playing this game, I end up staying up much later than I should because there's always one more thing to do. I love the art style and the fighting mechanics are very smooth and satisfying. I also get too emotionally attached to some of my followers because of how cute they are. The only problem is that I encountered quite a few bugs. For example, my game would sometimes freeze while I was in the middle of a sermon, leaving me unable to do anything, even save. Once or twice, the game also glitched during a crusade and I was unable to go to the next room. This seemed to happen when I decided to go backwards to a room I hadn't been in yet before progressing. For me, the bugs weren't a huge deal, I would just recommend saving as much as possible. Crusades are generally pretty short, so making up lost progress isn't too painful.Overall, I'd say that this game is a good buy. I've had a ton of fun playing it, and it's a great way to waste a couple of hours. All hail the lamb!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the critics are right and that neither half of this game - the rogue-like half and the base management half - are stellar knockouts. However, as someone who doesn't review and critique games for a living, I found both sides of this game to be engaging and fun. It's easy to get caught-up in managing your cult and doing "one more thing" for multiple in-game days and then it's also easy to get wrapped-up in the combat and wanting to do more than one randomized run at a time. I like the charm and aesthetic of the game. I like the sound and music design. I can see where the game could be better or longer but overall I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing this game but I feel it’s being uncritically praised and ultimately wouldn’t recommend it if someone asked. It has good bones but them bones are very bare. Biggest problem with the gaming is pacing: before I beat the second of five bosses, my cult was essentially running on autopilot, my decrees were completed, and someone was asking me to eat poop for the third time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a charming roguelike game where you’ll have to create your own town with the local cult of adorable woodland creatures. Running your own cult is just as fun as it is chaotic, and the game gives plenty of opportunities to customize your cultists, grow and expand the base and impose your mighty will.The mechanics are a brilliant balance of dungeon crawling and cult building that feed into each other perfectly. Even though combat is easy to master, it’s rather fun with a good variety of weapons and curses to play around with. The art direction and soundtrack are standout features, creating a unique atmosphere that's both creepy and cute. Overall, Cult of the Lamb is a unique experience that fans of roguelikes or management sims should play.8/10 (Great)

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 - great game! overall the game is as adorable as it is unsettling, a unique mix of genres and themes that come together very well.i love the art style and over all aesthetic of the game too. it nails the balance between its cutesy cartoon vibes and its demonic set dressing. some elements of the game was also similar to enter the gungeons which i really liked. with that being said - game still has a few bugs but I do have faith in the DEVs that they will eventually fix them.

_childDocuments_.review: first of all, the art style is AMAZING. It's the perfect blend of cute and sinister, occult and cartoony. it's really unique and i love it. now on to what i like and dislike: Like:The combat is interesting, the base building mechanics are fun, and it's really just great to have your own cult.Dislike:Some of the mechanics aren't explained very well, and I wish it was easier to deal with dissenting cult members. maybe you get tools to deal with that later on but early game it's incredibly frustrating that I can't really effectively deal with dissenting cultists. Overall I'd strongly recommend this game! It's a ton of fun and the art style really brings it up to a whole other level!
