_childDocuments_.review: I've finished all of the game and achievements, but I can't bring myself to recommend Cult of the Lamb. I had high expectations since the idea seemed pretty fun and fresh, but all in all this is a mediocre dungeon crawler with a farming system for your hub.The fighting system is quite okay, but the power ups could be better/make more of an impact on your playstyle. What's really annoying is that your town continues to develop in the background, so that many of your followers at the beginning will keep getting hungry, angry, or sick from you just going for a simple normal dungeon run to get ressources you need for them. There should be a shop to trade ressources and there's just nothing to do with all of your money and ressources after you get past some point in the game.Also, I think the release definitely could have used some more time for polishing: Apart from several bugs which could still be considered teething troubles, the game just seems very poorly optimised and made me suffer from some very extreme lags during some activities like cooking in my town and even in dungeons while things were being built in my town despite using a very stable PC setup.I am afraid I must say I'm mostly disappointed that this game may have come out a tad too early. It's not completely bad and was fun at times, but I think with some more feedback from testing it could have become a lot better than what it has been released as.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game with a cute design, fun features and great soundtracks. It is a lot of fun but still pretty buggy.When I played the game back in summer 2022 it was soooo buggy that I had to turn off my Nintendo Switch during many crucades because my game froze. Fortunately that's not the case anymore. But now there are other game-breaking and annoying bugs which weren't there before or I was fortunate enough to not encountering them til now. My first save file is completely fine, no bugs at all. The second is absolutely bugged. The first bug came up when I had to give the first surmon after building the temple. My character froze and cancelling the sermon didn't cancel it entirely. So I had to restart the game for 3x in total. At the third trial the sermon worked as it should but I noticed that I didn't get the faith symbol and it wouldn't appear after leaving the cult and re-entering it or restarting the game. So I will never know the status of my followers faith, not even if I check the cult menu. I also noticed that my followers never have any requests like hiring old people or sick people or wanting to eat a poop dish or throwing someone into prison. I had 1 or 2 requests at the beginning, but they stopped after a certain point but I can't tell when maybe when I upgraded the shrine. Another thing that disappeared are notifications about collapsed sleeping bags or tents. My game never told me when a follower turned old. I also got the bug that I can't build on certain spots because the game thinks that there's something there already. So either there should grow a tree (but it won't) or the game won't register that a tree got destroyed. I was excited to see that there's a new system: the sins. But I really don't like how slowly your followers generate sins. So I don't really play with it cause it feels like an annoying chore.So that was enough negativity. What I really like about the game is the fact that you can choose on how good or bad your cult will me. The doctrines bring a lot of variety for rules and rituals. I also really like the fact that there are accessibility settings like a fond for dyslexic people (only in english though), auto fishing, auto crafting, auto cooking, the ability to pause the cult's time while being on a crusade and the ability of having infinite health and infinite fervour. All those settings are great for people who might struggle with reflexes, so they still can enjoy the game. It is also nice that you can change the game's difficulty in the settings.  It would be great if we could get an update to upgrade the plot we got because it gets crowded pretty fast in the end game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> A great base-building game with some roguelite elements, cute and detailed art, bizarre humor and multiple secrets that will give you quality entertainment for ~20h. Do not expect replayability value though.-------------------------While I had a great time with this game, I kinda wished I had more information about it beforehand so I knew what kind of game I was exactly playing, so here it goes: Cult of the Lamb (COTL from now on) is a base-building animal crossing-ish game with some roguelite elements set in a bizarre, cute but satanic world where you establish your evil cult in a quest of imposing over different heretics. You do so by growing your cult with members (workers), resources and expeditions. The order I described COTL is relevant. When I purchased it, I expected some roguelite game with a base-building feature that would define my perma-upgrades. Instead, it works the other way around: this game is 80-90% base building and is complemented by some basic roguelite mechanics. It did not sabotage my experience at all but if you're expecting to find a next roguelite to dig into, this might not be the best option.In terms of base building content, COTL has become my small addiction for the past week or two. Progression is well constructed and you constantly feel the urge to keep doing stuff to slowly but steadily improve your cult. In general, resources are connected to the strength of your cult, and at the same time, a stronger cult will deliver more amount and faster resources. These are all connected to the game's cultist nature, since you strengthen your cult by raising loyalty, reciting sermons, doing rituals, and such. Other resources are related to new members, basic crafting materials, farm materials, etc. The game also features strategy and risk/reward situations by having potential negative outcomes (e.g. disseases, death by aging, members revelling, etc) and forcing you to mind your resource management better.In terms of roguelite elements, it has a bit of everything but the overall presentation is extremely simplistic. Layouts resemble the ones in The Binding of Isaac, being rectangle-ish, but with much less variety. Floor structure resemble the one in Slay the Spire or Inscryption, but without the same weight. Upgrades during runs resemble Hades in the shape of a multiple choice scenario, but options are much more limited. Combat follows a quite basic structure of a hack-n-slash where you spend most of the time rolling and attacking, while using magic (aka Curse) here and there. Compared to the entertainment value of the base building concept, these expeditions felt very generic and not very interesting, as runs felt very similar one another. But yet again, do not think of it as a roguelite.As a final warning for that, keep in mind that the game presents very little incentive for replayability. While progression of your cult is very solid for the most part, you quickly step up during the second half of the game and you eventually reach maximum stats without much trouble, with no way of getting stronger. At that point, you will complete the game and won't touch that savefile ever again.Overall, if you are not really looking for a roguelite game as a core and simply look for an entertaining game with funny, bizarre elements, great visuals and a length of ~20h, COTL is definitely your game. Despite not having replayability value, it gave me good quality content and it surely deserves a shot :)

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Satisfying, quick paced, accessible, and most importantly FUN game. I would recc this to pretty much anyone that has a passing interest in roguelites and base management.Pros:-Accessible! There are plenty of difficulty options to customize your experience, and even on its hardest difficulty the game is not unconquerable.  -The game incentivizes fun. If you want to be world’s most awful cult leader, you can do so without judgement. Heck, you can customize your cult’s teachings to get the most out of it in the same go!-Snappy and quick. Combat is fairly simple with an attack, a spell, and a dodge roll, but it stays fresh for far longer than I was expecting! Slashing at enemies is fun, and they telegraph their attacks clearly, which keeps the fights feeling fair.-Cute artstyle. Everything in this game looks nice, cute, or culty! There’s plenty of decorations you can use to spice up your base as well.-Great minigame! I’m talking about knuckle bones – the fishing minigame is par for the course as far as I’m concerned. Knucklebones is so fun for how simple it is!-Good music. I spent about 3 days listening to ‘Saviour’ and ‘Anchordeep’ on a loop, and I do not regret it!-This game hits that ‘popular appeal’+‘indie vibes’ sweet spot. It’s got poop and murder and cult stuff, but its imagery is rounded and soft to the point where I’m expecting to see Follower Plushies within the next month or so. Cons: -Very little replay value. I love this game, and I have started a second save on the highest difficulty to get more time with it, but outside of a second save file and 100%ing the game there is not much here for repeat playthroughs. Even the ‘endless’ mode you get after defeating the boss of an area is not truly endless, and ends after about 4 loops. There is ( as of right now ) no way to have a run through all of the area’s one after another. -Probably a little too easy for experienced players on the recommended difficulty. Even on the highest difficulty I had no trouble making rapid progress. -You always start with a random weapon. Doesn’t seem like a big deal at first, but if you’re trying to get every achievement or trying to kill a boss you’re having trouble with, getting stuck with a weapon-type you hate is the worst. There is a skill to circumvent the penalty of dying to get a ‘reset’ on your starter weapon, but it takes time and is irritating. -Followers quickly become a resource without personality or depth. They all have unique abilities, but outside of a handful of events, they are interchangeable. The ability to name and customize them sadly plays into this.-Typical base-building pitfalls apply. Getting resources and farming starts off as a necessary chore until you figure out automatization – at which point the entirety of it falls by the wayside. Once you hit a certain amount of resources and side-quest progress, managing your base becomes something you do out of your own volition rather than a necessity. -You’re forced to pick your rituals before you have a clear idea of what kind of ‘build’ you would like to make. There is no way to switch to another ritual, leaving you with a couple of cult-abilities you cannot/will not use because they do not fit in with the other rituals you chose later/earlier on.  -… It ends. I was having a blast with my followers, and I was using every resource available to me, because all of them were fun to interact with. And then I hit the end of the skill trees, and I no longer ‘had’ to do anything, even though I badly wanted to. Though I’ve listed a lot of cons up there, they are minor nit-picks in my eyes. This game isn’t perfect, but it is FUN! It’s priced just right – where you get a steal of a game when it’s on sale, and exactly the kind of fun, engaging experience you’d expect when putting down the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the lamb has one major design flaw that holds it back from being a good game:The core gameplay loop is only half fun.The management of your cult compound; talking to followers, sacrificing them, feeding them poop, THAT'S fun. I like that.The dungeon runs? I could do without.They are just so... boring. Every weapon FEELS the same, every room FEELS the same, you BARELY get any kind of randomised upgrades so every RUN feels the same. Rogue-lites live and die on variety between runs and so when every run feels the same it starts to get old FAST.Add to that the fact that the maps are so colourful and move around so much (grass swaying in the breeze, fires crackling, etc) that it makes it harder to tell when an enemy is telegraphing an attack, so you get hit quite a lot unless you spam the dodgeroll button like a maniac, but spamming imputs takes you out of the moment and just adds to the blurred, dreary haze that is the dungeon run portion of the game.All in all, I would prefer if that part of the game, the dungeons, the combat, simply weren't there and we JUST did the base management stuff.Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played Don't Starve or Don't Starve Together and wished that you could get NPCs to do some of the tedious work around your base and gather resources for you so you don't have to? Because that is basically Cult of the Lamb.The biggest difference is that you personally don't actually need food or sleep, only your cultists do, so failure to manage them won't result in a game over, it mostly just sets you back in time. You unlock more and more buildings as you progress, and as you unlock buildings it unlocks jobs your cultists can do, so over time the things you have to personally oversee becomes less and less and more streamlined to deal with.Taking care of your cult is pretty easy, it mostly just involves making sure they stay fed, manually sending them to "sleep it off" if they get sick, or imprisoning them if they start to dissent. The other half of the game is the roguelike dungeon crawling. Every dungeon run you start gives you a random weapon and a random spell, and you may upgrade or swap weapons and spells multiple times throughout a run, as well as picking up a bunch of different buffs from tarot cards and relics you find along the way. The only thing you actually have control over is your Fleece, and aside from your starting one that does nothing, all of them have bonuses and negatives to using them, so you can sort of change your playstyle based on what fleece you're using. My first unlocked fleece, and favorite until end game, was damage focused and gives a stacking 5% damage buff for every enemy you kill, but you lose the buff if you take any damage and you take double damage from attacks. At end game though, you get more hardcore versions of the starting fleeces, like one that makes you do 10x damage but you only have half a heart so you die in a single hit without mitigating factors. My favorite end game fleece though makes it so you don't get weapons at all and instead makes you a full on spell caster, letting your power regenerate over time, your spells cost less power to use, and you get a full bar of power every new room you enter.Steam says i've played it 26 hours, which is hard to believe it has taken this long, but I had finally finished the post game content, although to be fair, the post game content is mostly just running through the normal game a second time with everything a little harder but using overpowered new fleeces to make it not even matter.All in all, I enjoyed the game. I bought it for $15 on sale and its definitely worth the price for me. I didn't bother with the DLCs because they only add cosmetic stuff like follower skins and new decorations, which I didn't care about at all and still don't regret not buying them.That said, i'm probably done with the game. There doesn't seem to be a whole lot of replayability, and you technically have to play through it twice to really finish up anyway. At this point, there is nothing left for me to do but run the dungeons over and over but I don't get anything useful or interesting as a reward anymore (since I have already got all the stuff I want) and the runs aren't unlimited anyway because theres only a finite number of rooms until it ends each time, there is no infinite run possible to see how far you can get or anything like that, which is kind of disappointing.Either way, I think i'm done with it, but i'm glad I got it and got to experience it. Cute game. I'll come back and check out the new update that is in the works and supposed to be coming out soon, maybe it'll add more fun stuff to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with I love this game. I played it when it first came out and have started a new save every time there has been a big update. The game is so unique and the characters are all likable in different ways, which a lot of games lack nowadays. Even the so-called 'villains' of the game have aspects I enjoy about them.The gameplay is very well thought out, and I recommend it to anyone.As a solo-player game, it's probably one of the best games out there, as it's an easy-to-play enjoyable experience.Now, going onto the reason for this review, the multiplayer update.First of all, I appreciate the developers for making the updates free to play, without the need to purchase any DLCs to enjoy the new content. I would have gladly paid for new content but I think this gives the game a huge advantage over other games.Sadly, I do not enjoy the multiplayer. I like a lot of the new additions to cater to a second player and to work together, but I think by not making it split-screen, or allowing players to join from their own PC's (they only have local co-op), it makes the game extremely harder to play and less enjoyable. Keeping your eye on your character while the screen gets smaller or larger, compared to where your friend is on the map, is extremely hard. We've lost focus of our characters multiple times, and have died multiple times because of it. The screen changing sizes is very annoying, if it was one constant size or split screen it would be much more enjoyable. There are aspects of the game I enjoy, I feel if they just changed that one thing from multiplayer it would be a lot more enjoyable. I do love this game though, and I 100% recommend it to anyone, solely for solo game play. Which sucks cause I was excited about this update.

_childDocuments_.review: it's hard to say no to this despite there being a couple softlocks that guarantee a fail early on in the game, plus some useless mechanics/items here and there. overall, the game has so far provided the cute veneer over its sinister atmosphere and plot, which i've found more entertainment in than disappointment. i'm unsure if i'm swayed to this opinion because of the roguelike crusades that bear many similarities to the binding of isaac, a game which i have sunk over 800 hours in and enjoyed playing. either way, i have to say that the rest of the game is quite enjoyable, although tense or anxiety-inducing at times provided the frequent feeling of being stuck in a hole or weighing two negative options. there's also some things you can do to cheese your way out of extra negative consequences, like repeatedly interacting with dissenters whenever they try and broadcast so your cult doesn't get influenced and they leave without issues, or even sacrificing the only cult member who's against sacrifices to avoid it being a problem in the future. the latter is more reasonable and feels like a logical solution, but the former thing feels like an exploit. there are some weapons the game provides you in certain locations for crusades that are almost utterly worthless to use, like a hammer in heket's realm. not only is it slow, but it has a massive delay which renders use against projectile-hurling enemies or flies to be incredibly tedious and risky. it's a matter of rng determining whether that's possible, and i wish there were some exceptions for which weapons you could encounter in certain realms given these enemies nullifying their strengths and their overall usage. the game's difficulty increases at a rather consistent level, which i appreciate. you get used to the increase each time, or else you suffer consequences. there's a lot of strategy to it, and instead of brute-force, that's exactly why i think it's done quite well, and is another reason i recommend this game.as for followers, it feels like some variants die older than others, or maybe i encountered a coincidence that felt too good to be a coincidence. their mouths are all pretty much the same, and don't match their face or species very well in some cases. it'd be nice if they matched their head, but it's not the game's focus so i don't think they'd be bothered to do so. overall, it's got some issues here and there, enough for me to recommend against it, but i'm choosing to recommend it because it appeals to me in a couple ways while also doing some other things incredibly well. it's hard to make a game so well-liked while having problems people will constantly be wondering about and hoping to be fixed, and that's exactly what they did with this game and its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but I just can't get into it. That's not to say this game is terrible, but there are big flaws.Battles feel repetitive, and it doesn't feel as satisfying as some other rogue-likes, primarily Hades, to complete a full run. Runs feel either too hard or too easy, and there just isn't any in-between. Controls in this game feel too simple as well. There's an attack button, dodge, and that's it. Fights in this game consist of repeatedly mashing the attack button and dodging the occasional projectile or lunge forward. Enemies, with the exception of some bosses, feel too easy to beat. Collecting food during runs can also be tedious even on normal difficulty where you have to constantly be collecting it as your main priority for keeping your cult alive. The perks that you earn in the runs feel too simple and easy to get.The other half of the gameplay, which is actually taking care of your cult is alright, albeit serviceable, but it doesn't feel deep as I want it to be. That might just be because I haven't played much of the game. But I don't enjoy a lot of this game which makes me sad because I really wanted to like this game.Cult of the Lamb just doesn't know the kind of game it wants to be. It wants to be many things, yet succeeds at neither. If you're looking for a rich rogue-like inspired by Hades that has inticing gameplay, Cult of the Lamb isn't it, and the other side of the gameplay doesn't exactly deliver either. Sadly, I do not recommend this game. There are far better rogue-likes out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda cute in an eldritch kinda way, it's pretty well made all things considered, and the loop is engaging. It's just that it could've been a lot better like bringing in the cult to the rougelike aspects outside of their needs bar being essentially a time limit. You can explore all you like in the rougelike sections and bosses but your cult will die if you don't get back soon enough. However aside from one or two perks you can get that'll let you kill your cultists for power the cult merely exists to unlock weapons/curses and stages. Once everything is unlocked the cult is basically useless. The funnier part with the cult base building is that it's almost entirely self-contained. There are upgrades which can help automate certain parts of upkeep, but nothing that will really elongate the rougelike timer the cult is. There is one structure that can let you bring cultists into dungeons, but that's basically all the cult is. A timer, unlocks things, and maybe bring a little help if you really want to. The rougelike sections themselves aren't that deep either. You got a dodge roll, weapon attacks, ranged curses, and some basic passive upgrades like slightly more damage and situational slightly more damage. The weapons can mostly be boiled down into 2 weapon types, heavy weapons that kill in one or two hits and lighter weapons that you swing a lot and try to kill with multiple slaps. That boils it down a bit, but realistically that's all you need to know about the weapons. If you like the aesthetic it's fine, but compared to other roguelikes it's far from the best. If I had any recommendations for changes it would be to integrate the cult and the dungeons together. Maybe ways to send cooked food from in the dungeon or ways to get power from specific individuals at a shrine or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: One of the masterpiece I played for quite long time in the industry. Well designed, well balanced game play  with  engaging art and music.  Cult of the lamb plays with human moral behaviours during game play as how you approach decision making to cultivate a flock, deciding who lives, who dies for what reason. Voice lines are awesome that is in another cultic language which makes it very fun and interesting to hear. Fights are not monotone, there is always something new coming up your way. At the same time it is not complicated. Many surprises on the crusades that pushes you to grow your flock and look after them even better.General game play is easy to grasp, controls are good and the camera interactions are engaging. Animations are very good as well, I personally find some of them too long when you start to reach end game. UI is innovative, I personally like heavy meta perception indicators of what happened during game play, usage of UI art is clear yet still super fun. General UX is good with a lot of options including accessibility. I played the game with mouse and keyboard. It is sometimes confusing to have primary action on right mouse button, such as gaining fervor from shelters, graveyards. Collecting poop interaction can also be better. Final boss fight is pretty good but still in normal difficult can be more balanced I feel. It is a bit hard to finish with 5-6 hearths in normal difficulty. The game is quite polished I just encountered 1-2 minor bugs which is reported.Thanks for making it.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but I would give it 3.5 stars if I could. The gameplay that is there is pretty good, but once you start to understand the game's mechanics, it's practically over. Most of the other reviews are accurate with all of the positives of the game. I would still recommend it, but be warned its a pretty short game.The game can be beaten within 8 hours by casually playing through. I would say it would take most people 12 hours to beat the game. If you care about collecting everything it'll probably take most 16-20 hours. Then there's nothing else to do, the only re-playable content is the combat which is a simpler version of Binding of Isaac.The game is like a short nice infusion of Stardew valley and Binding of Isaac. I enjoyed the game for what it was, but i'm hoping the game gets extra content added in to make it a 5 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a beautiful, addicting game. It definitely has it's own cute charm to it. The animations, artwork, and vibrant colors make the game look wonderful, but also simple in a way (I can't describe it). The game-play is very engaging, with a wide range of things you can do that will keep you hooked. It kinda has everything for everyone. There are a lot of nods/references towards religions, especially Christianity, which can be sensitive to some people. I doubt this would be a problem though, as you're literally getting what you paid for! A CULT SIM!I also find the combat somewhat mediocre, but it is still very engaging and fun. _childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review right after finishing the final boss and completing the game.Cult of the lamb is an incredibly strong contender for my game of the year, the game is amazing, the amount of thought and detail that went into every aspect is admirable and i loved every second i spent with the game.That being said it is not perfect and i do have some issues.Those being:- I do not care about my followers, after the 50th entered my camp and kicked the bucket i stopped bothering to bury them and just started cutting them up to sell their meat- The loyalty system is goofy and can be abused real fast (i didn't have a single follower leave because i could just do a serman and go about my day)- Difficulty spikes are weird, from boss 1 - boss 2 the phases they go through are wild, one of them is a generic fight while the next is a bullet hell - Collecting blueprints is more of a chore than something i want to do; in the game there are blueprints that unlock customisation items for your base, issue is everytime you get one you have to watch a 5 second unskippable animation of the lamb celebrating this blueprint and putting it into their book this is pretty annoying and a skip button would have been nice.That's all, i love this game, give it a try it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Artistically beautiful, soothing music (and overall audio design on point) and simple yet well balanced mix of roguelike and followes management. _childDocuments_.review: I've got mixed feelings about this game. (PLAYED ON MEDIUM) I'll start off with the good points:- There is always something to do, food, catching fish, side quests, refining mats, earning loyalty with followers, rituals. The list can go on.- Art style remind me of "Don't Stave" a lot, but this feels a lot more polished. Which is good.- LOTS of weapons (Hopefully more coming soon! Even though it's just released)- Secondary attacks, packs a punch. Especially when you get the seeking round (You'll know when you find it) - Boss battles are unique too the that particular boss. Which is refreshing and annoying at the same time, so you don't get used too the attack pattern :D- "Cloaks" As I like to refer them as. Really change your play style. Depending on what kind of "build" you want to go for. I was running, 10% damage for each enemy you kill (Had it as far as 1030%). But, it resets on hit, as well as you take double damage. So, pick your poison? - Added benefits after killing each main boss, are always nice. Which are passives, that you go into every run. Don't do the sacrifice one as much as I should. But considering how long my followers have been with me. I've got attached :D- Tarot cards, which you pick up during a run. Give you really nice benefits to help with your run. Had 9 from one run? Which made it quite easy to run though 3 levels of one boss room. Which you don't have to pay for, which is SO good early game.- Money was no issue, during my play time. I did have an issue with expanding my bass and upgrading building though. But, get the mind controlling spell, then the "follows donate too you". You're rolling in it.-That's all I can think of at the moment. Will add more, if I think of anythingBad things, from my play time. -Game feels VERY unstable during my play time. Lags too 1 FPS, when going over too a new day (I have got a full base, day 100ish and playing on Ultra) Lot of enemies on the screen? Lags, which makes it hard to fight enemies when not trying NOT to get hit. Since you've got a 360% damage bonus... Boss fights wan't an issue with the lag though. So, no idea...- Invincible and invisible enemies. Only had this once. But, it was very annoying since I was in second stage of a run. :D- Big bad boss fight, wasn't that hard? - MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR YOUR FOLLOWERS. 40 follows, which I have to go up to individually and tell them too do this job instead. Since I need this certain material. Or, claiming the loyalty bonus from them. Good luck if you've got more then 2, UGH- No REAL use for gold, late game (I know you can make golden bars. But, with 200 gold bars and nothing to do with it. Seems pointless) - Give us a way, to FARM grass. I won't mention how tedious it is. But, you need grass, to turn into poop. Which then can be used in your farm, to fertilise the crops. Which makes you harvest them faster.- I don't know what's wrong with my game. Tried restarting my PC, checking for bad files. Nothing. But, I can no longer load up my save that I've been playing for 28 hours. So, I won't play until it's fixed. (I'm not redoing everything, to get back to where I was on a new play-though) This game, is an AMAZING game. But, it still needs work. I know, it's only been released for 2 days. But, these things needs to be addressed. It is well worth the pick up, if you want a chaotically fun game, which will keep you on your toes when it comes too combat, and having a Farmville life back at home. _childDocuments_.review: recommend FOR NOW and only if you find it cheap on a 3rd party site. i can tell they are beginning their descent down the very same slippery slope most successful games do. the dlc is going to pile on more and more and so are the FOMO rewards (we've already got several and they're twitch prime "rewards" with no way to actually earn them). all the while, the game is getting more buggy and less balanced as they focus more of their effort away from a good experience and more towards how to profit more.if relics of the old faith, the new content update, is anything to go by, there is no hope future updates won't just completely crush what balance the game has left, and it already invalidates every doctrine you decided throughout the main game by offering to let you buy all the other ones (even if you don't want them, once you start deciding, you must pick one. so much for trying to design a cult in a certain way)

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a fun filled adventure from start to finish! It took the familiar aspects of the rogue-lite genre and implemented it's own unique spin on it with the cult building/management system. _childDocuments_.review: Not a huge fan of games with roguelike elements but cult of the lamb was a real blast to play. The artstyle is amazing, the overall theme very enticing and fresh. The game basically consists of two parts, building and managing your cult and its buildings on one hand, going for dungeon runs on the other. The management part is pretty relaxed and has activities and minigames such as farming, deckbuilding, fishing and miniquests from your followers. The dungeon runs consist of several stages with occasional minibosses throughout and final bosses at the end of the run. you gather ressources here and all sorts of bonus loots plus character abilites. It's fun to go on these runs, even if you're not the biggest fan of this roguelike system.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good and fun game!The first time I saw the game, I didn't expect it to be so successful and so fun. ( especially because a mode for co-op was also added )The game is still quite short if you want to play it only for the main story, but if you are a fan of games where you have to build a base, go to dungeons and at the same time be an unpaid babysitter because the animals in the cult you need too much attention, you have found your ideal game that you won't get bored of anytime soon!So what are you waiting for? _childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is good. I played for eight hours on release day alone. It is addictive, the game play loop is extremely satisfying, and the art is beautiful. If you gun down the main story it is a bit shorter than I'd like, but there are plenty of ways to get distracted to keep you from reaching the end too fast.However, and there is a however, this game has been horribly buggy at release. It feels like an early access game despite being marketed as finished. I have no doubt it will be fixed, in fact they fixed one of the larger glitches the morning after release, but it is still sad that it was released in this bad of a state. If you are thinking of buying this game, double check the forums and the patch notes first.There is a fun game here, and I believe it will be patched to near perfection, but as of me writing this I would not recommend you start playing. Yet

name: Achilles: Legends Untold
detailed_description: 𝐆𝐀𝐌𝐄 𝐅𝐄𝐀𝐓𝐔𝐑𝐄𝐒 Arena Style Co-Op. Action RPG with souls-like combat style. A variety of enemies to battle, each with a distinct combat pattern. Weapons, items, and skills that offer a unique playstyle. An open world ready for exploration. Over 20 hours of gameplay. A proprietary GAIA (Group AI Action) system that governs AI cooperation within the environment. Achilles: Legends Untold is an action RPG featuring souls-like combat mechanics, set in the mythical world of ancient Greece, where you assume the role of the fearless warrior, Achilles. For the best gameplay experience, we recommend playing with a controller. FIGHT AND LEARN Dive into a world where mastering combat, from defense tactics like blocking and evading to a wide array of attacks, is the key to success. If you fall in battle, rise again, enhance your hero's skills, try a different tactic, and venture forth once more. CHOOSE YOUR COMBAT STYLE Select your ideal weapon, from wielding a one-handed sword and an axe in the other, to the might of two-handed swords. Equip a set of powerful special attacks, craft a handful of grenades from gathered ingredients, and charge into battle. FACE UNIQUE CHALLENGES Engage in battles against foes utilizing an innovative GAIA (Group AI Action) system. Your adversaries exhibit unscripted interactions with one another, enabling coordinated attacks, often making strategic use of their environment. DEVELOP YOUR CHARACTER Harness a wealth of skill points to expand your hero's capabilities, offering a multitude of character development options. EXPLORE ANCIENT GREECE Roam through meticulously crafted locations inspired by Ancient Greece. Ascend mountain passes, venture into the deepest dungeons, and battle for survival in otherworldly rifts.

_childDocuments_.review: The bar wasn't set too high regarding gameplay depth but basically everything is very well executed. For less than 20 bucks, this is a very good game. It's basically Wolves of Midgard in Greece.+ Fully voice acted, some lines are lackluster and some are repeated over and over, but overall very good+ Great soundtrack+ Decent graphics and awesome performance (levels load in 1 second)+ Different weapons for different fighting styles (swords, axes, two-handers, spear + shield)0 Pretty simple and repetitive combat system but the sound and the gore make it fun- Some items and equipment stats need a lot of tweaking/balancing in my opinion. Most throwing weapons are completely useless at the moment. On the other hand, two-handed sprint attack ("wirlwind") just plows through everything and makes the game too easy.- Simple, slow (and boring) skill progression systemCoop is only for dungeons at the moment but it works well. Coop for the whole game would be AWESOME.

_childDocuments_.review: Get up young princeDon't let a stone take my glory. There are no pacts between LIONS and men. You will wander the under world deaf, dumb, and blind, as the fool who thought he killed ACHILLES. HECTOR! HECTOR!! HECTOR!!Man Troy is one of my all time favorite movies from the 2000’s. Glad they made a game based off Brad Pitt.Before that Skyrim guard took an arrow in the knee, there was Achilles, the man who took an axe to the heel!It truly feels like a tougher and more badass Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like if Diablo II, Champions of Norath, Baldurs Gate Dark Alliance, and Titan Quest had a love child named Achilles. Achilles is a fun challenging arpg, with a great skill tree, crafting, and storyline. The game is a lot of fun. I thoroughly enjoyed it. There is plenty of action, as well as lots of places to explore. Enemies will give you the challenge you're looking for. The game is STUPID addictive once you understand the mechanics and know what to expect. Playing in the hardest mode makes it challaging and rewarding. The movesets are basic and the armors are not amazing but the story and the gameplay are great. Soundtrack is badass. I love games that have a good soundtrack and this game definitely delivers on that. Kinda reminds me of the first time I played Hades. Achilles will not have a million things to do… but the things it has, it's extremely good at.I loved the Diablo fused with Dark Souls type gameplay.  Brutal (souls-like) and forgiving (wide open world means you can kite the hell out of strong enemies and get really surgical with your strikes) at the same time. Loved the various weapons, as well. Especially the 2H sword, and the spear+shield playstyles. There’s also enough loot to keep me engaged but it’s not overbearing like Nioh. The lack of armor is only a slight negative as you can still obtain armor just not on a “loot” based system.The combat is awesome. Violent, brutal, and gore-ish but definitely not spammy. The combat style is almost entirely melee, but totally fluid and rewarding. Each weapon style has its moveset, and on top there's a few assignable "skills". The in game weapon system is simple. It’s scale based like Dark Souls. If you know Dark Souls this should be easy. The element system is also like any other souls game where Divine damage is better against “evil” or “Undead” and Dark damage is good against the opposite. Enemy variety is good enough for the stretch of the game. I was hoping to encounter a few more other Greek mythology creatures (like Gorgons, and Pegasus) but it’s still great nonetheless.Overall for me it's a very enjoyable game. You'll get overwhelmed at first with the amount of mobs you encounter but once you understand the mechanics of those mobs and know how to deal with them you’ll find it so fun. So far this game has been a blast to play. Great visuals, great skill tree, ancient Greek mythology... what's not to like? If you're looking for a fantastic action RPG adventure with a touch of souls-like gameplay then this is the game for you! Homer Would Approve.Finally, you can pet cats! Brad Pitt would be proud.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No. You are Achilles. You came to Troy to raze and plunder it. Many ships arrive on the shore, with hundreds of your soldiers. You jump on the shore - and you are alone. All alone. Sometimes you see a dead body on the ground, and sometimes you encounter a single enemy, or two. Later a bit more, but that's it. You fight them. And this is the core gameplay. Close quarter fights against small groups of enemies. Center on an enemy, attack him with 2 different attacks, use your shield, dash... and not too much more. Learn a few new skills later, throw a grenade. Enemies just attack you on sight. You have to watch your stamina, and the game plays a bit like a soulslike... So you kill a few enemies, sneak into Troy, and get killed by Paris. And here the story starts, because the god of the underworld, Hades, asks a few little favors from you, or he will let you rot in Tartarus forever. So you agree, and you are sent back to the land of the living. Or wherever you are sent, because the first enemies are a lot of clumsy skeletons. Rest at shrines (bonfires) to get healed, and most enemies get revived. When you die, you are revived at the last shrine. Collect enough fate (experience) to unlock some new skills at a shrine. Die and collect your fate before you die again or it is lost forever. The sourroundings are looking nice, but you can interact with nearly nothing. You cannot destroy anything, there is not much interesting stuff to loot (some healing potions...), not many secrets to find, and even small obstacles cannot be pushed away/destroyed/climbed... sometimes you find a ladder to climb or a door to open. That's it. More or less. A bit... boring. Furthermore, you see your sourroundings in an isometric view, but unfortunately you don't see very far. This is fine for the close combat, but awful for exploring. You maybe see 10 meters in all directions, so you can run past nearly everything that is close to you, just because you do not see it. Only at fixed points the camera switches to a more panoramic view to show you a bit of the sourroundings.The game is in Early Access. What is here already works... but it ends after Chapter 1. Chapter 1! I mean, huh? Where is the rest of the game? You have to wait another year for it and may get it then, if you are lucky. Ok, maybe they will release the planned missing four chapters as soon as they finish them. I am not against Early Access, but in the last months I saw a lot of Early Access releases which did not contain a lot of content. You may get lucky and receive a large game in the end, like it happened in King Arthur: Knight's Tale. Or you may have an unfinished trainwreck after the devs abandoned the game. Is this worth paying a little less than the finished game will cost? Your choice. I was close to downvoting the game, but I think that this would be a bit harsh because it works fine and as long as you enjoy the fights, it is fun. It can become a good hack and slash game if it receives the planned updates. The conversations are fully voiced and have subtitles. The subtitles are often different from the spoken dialogue, though. Gamepad works fine, my PlayStation Dualshock 4 controller even shows the correct buttons on screen. Ultrawidescreen is supported.Classic hack and slash game in Early Access. Contains chapter 1 (of 5 planned)...
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: First of all who the hell comes up with this 'souls-like' nonsense, I've seen it time and time again in many different games but the only 'souls-like' mechanic is portal/checkpoint/bonfire where you can level up and where you can rest and reset all enemies. That sure as hell isn't definition of 'souls-like' but whatever I just wanted to address that.About Achilles ... is it a shovelware? No! Is it awesome arpg? No! It's actually fine enough game which is actually kind of a unrefined gem where the first thorough playthrough takes about 20-25 hours- music fits nicely the setting- it's UE4 so it looks nice- every line is voiced even though the delivery might be janky and whoever voiced Achilles tried to do Aldo Raine impression (and tbh it's not a bad thing)- there's fair environment variability (2 big maps and 3 small ones+some cellars and dungeons)- good weapon and overall equip variety- variety of enemies is also good enough for a game with this price tagThinking about it I don't really have something really bad to say about this game, yes it crashed on me once but that's about it. Story is fine, combat is fine, there's couple of bosses that have well visible attacks unlike Lillith in Diablo 4 and the game (depending on chosen difficulty) will most likely hold you by your nuts until you find a blacksmith but after you level up a bit and upgrade your equip you get from mostly 1v1 fighting to aggroing whole groups of enemies and cutting through them like hot knife through butter.So good job devs, you've delivered a game with fair price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold is like a narrowed down version of Titan Quest with some souls-like elements. Don't expect this to be Diablo. It's still pretty fun! Also pretty clunky.+ Best part of the game is the hack and slash combat. Lots of different weapons to pick your favourite playstyle: swords, axes, 2-handers, spears, shields, you can even dual wield! Special attacks, parries and dodge rolls give a nice flow to fights.+ Inventory and crafting is pretty nice, you don't need to think about managing anything. You get to take a limited number of items with you, the rest is automatically moved to an invisible stash and you can replenish items at bonfires. Too bad the throwing weapons are not all that useful.+ Map design is pretty nice, but the graphics look a bit dated.+ The game boasts an "intelligent group AI system". I noticed that sometimes one soldier with a shield will kneel and then another soldier does a leap attack off his back, that is really cool! Still, enemies still have very predictable movement patterns, making it easy to time hits as they approach you.- My current build is completely overpowered, an upgraded 2-hander that can drop every enemy in a spin-to-win attack, which makes other items and skills useless. I recommend playing the highest difficulty.- Sometimes the aim is off and your swing misses an enemy completely, which is annoying because animations are pretty long and it increases the risk of getting swarmed.- You can get stunlocked by a group every now and then, but you'll learn to move around it.- The "skill tree" is pretty low effort: it's mostly stat points with a few abilities here and there, no way to build a unique character with it.- The voice acting is mediocre and the dialogue is just dumb.- I was hoping for more enemy variety and monsters from Greek mythology, not just random dark fantasy creatures.I had a hack & slash itch that needed scratching, this game does a decent job at it.It's not amazing, but at this price point it certainly is entertaining.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this at the beginning because I think that there is no element in this game that is done simply well, but I still wouldn't want this comment to be misunderstood as negative. My goal is to identify areas that require improvement in the context of future productions (which I strongly count on)◉ ➝ When I only fought 2 bosses on the first day (playing for over 4 hours), and most of the time I was an errand boy, bringing item after item, while being sent back to some corner of the world each time, the level of frustration kept increasing, and I questioned whether the game is actually worth playing/finishing at this point. ➝ An important element of souls-like games is the  Here, unfortunately, there was no separation of areas and quests into specific sections, that would end with an encounter. I was wandering around aimlessly for most of the game, and towards the end of the game I suddenly had boss after boss, making the entire experience a complete mess.➝ Unfortunately, there is also a , which in my opinion are the most important element of the souls-like genre. Outside of the fight with the chimera, these are rather bland. There are no fireworks or more advanced attacks, that would require specific behavior from the player. Unluckily, nothing happens in these fights, and the whole thing is devoid of challenge. I had the impression, that I could close my eyes, and repeat a sequence of random attack and dodge, and I would still finish this fight without any major problems.◉  A huge part of the game is unpleasant and unnecessary running, which constantly forces you to fight the same opponents that you see hundreds of times. I would definitely prefer to see smaller, but more refined locations. This is a very big problem for this game, because it negatively affects all important elements, and I assume that a lot of hours, which went into making that ,could have been spent on many other elements.◉ There was definitely a  here. I collected several of them, which looked rather poorly, and actually took away the dynamics in combat, due to their laborious animations. A game based on Greek mythology has a huge potential. Without messing with the plot too much, we could consider adding non-equippable items/perks, that would give us different abilities, often associated with different gods and, consequently, the elements associated with them. I think that many players would like to see an attack related to Zeus' lightning, rather than some basic dash-pierce spear sequence, without any "flavor"/effect on it.◉ Visually, the game is basically decent.  This makes the entire game look a bit slurry. Some locations also need to stand out a bit more. Too often I had the impression, that I was looking at the same thing over and over again, but with some post-processing added in the form of a red or blue tint.◉  It seems to me, that the game unnecessarily switched between simply distributing base statistics, and perks that modify the gameplay in some way. I would prefer it to be either a simple statistics-based system, or, if you actually wish, statistics with a lot more modification options than you've made.   Apart from the fragment of the constellation, that introduced changes and bonuses for the usage of a shield, we basically had a few, single, insignificant perks that were part of that system. An interesting idea, but unfortunately it doesn't look very good, if it is only implemented in such a small part.◉ The player controller still requires some polishing. Combat can be clunky and a bit annoying◉ Rift clearing definitely too long and with too many mobs. It introduced an almost irritating "level of difficulty", i.e. running and kiting several dozen opponents, one after the other◉ Boxes blocked with the requirement to destroy 3 rune-stones are crazy. A concept that's good for once, maybe twice. Hiding basically half of the crates behind it is some sort of gameplay paranoia, that constantly calls into question the point of exploration. Not to mention, that many of these runes required the use of a shield (which, let me remind you, is not a mandatory element of the equipment)◉ I think that in a game of this scale, randomizing the items found in the chests is rather unnecessary. I would prefer it to be something planned by designers (items placed in specific places)◉ Selling items individually... well, I believe it's some kind of oversight, because I don't know how to comment on it :DAfter playing for 1 hour, I could say I've seen it all. During the remaining 11 hours, I did not experience any changes that would offset the sense of fatigue I was experiencing. Other soulslike creations do not turn their systems on their heads, but because they don't have to due to attaching importance to: With these things, they are able to keep the player's attention and not cause a feeling of monotony throughout the entire playthrough.--Not sure if any developer is gonna read it. Sorry for being such a pain in the ass, but I hope that these can help you in your upcoming games.

_childDocuments_.review: In Greek mythology, Achilles or Achilleus was a hero of the Trojan War who was known as being the greatest of all the Greek warriors.Achilles is an ARPG hack and slash which actually pays tribute to Greek Mythology and true to its roots is fully voice acted as well.This is not a triple A title by any means, but I am actually having more fun, yes that's right more FUN than in some triple A titles as of recently.Graphics are decent, combat is kinda Euro janky at first but with skills and advancement starts to feel better, smoother if you will.Skill tree is a little different with spells thrown in to the mix as well, but fairly easy to understand.Story is not bad, but we are not necessarily here for that, but still interesting never the less.Works great with a controller my preferred way of playing, at this price point you will get your monies worth plus, with cards, achievements and all the bells and whistles.P.S. _childDocuments_.review: Devs have done a lot of major patches since my original review, and even reached out to me to let me know, so I think that's really awesome and shows the hard work they've put in this little gem. So please give this game a chance, and I'm definitely excited to see what they come up with next! <3   I'll be honest, I played the first 15 minutes or so, put the controller down and said it wasn't for me, even though I LOVE Greek mythology (which was what drew me to the game in the first place). I actually opted in to refund the game, unknowing that I'd had it over the time period limit. And let me tell you, I am THANKFUL that I didn't commit to the refund. I thought hell, I've already paid for it, I may as well play more of it, so I did. Following this tale of Achilles was well worth it, and the length of the game is also decent, too.  Look, there are some little things here and there that make it janky. The voice acting isn't AAA, but it's not a AAA game (and I'm pretty sure the same dude did the majority of the voices). Sometimes the shield doesn't aim the way you want it, so I'd use my keyboard instead when necessary. But overall, the game was definitely worth the hours of play. The world itself is gorgeous, as to be expected with anything Ancient Greece. The range of enemy types as well as weapons is good, too. I'm so thankful that I didn't end up getting my refund, because once I gave it a chance and let the story progress, I wanted to see it through til the end. It was a little hidden gem with a pretty damn good price tag to it, too. I had a lot of fun, loved the writing of the story, and enjoyed the fighting style. Really well done. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not recommending this game for two reasons. 1. The player is easily stun locked, by swarms of enemies (anything more than two). It's not like a souls game where you get one enemy to deal with. IMO being able to be stun locked as a player is the dumbest mechanic on the planet. 2. The stamina pool and regeneration rate is way way way too low (even maxed out) you'll find yourself with out any stamina to attack or doge. So on top of getting stun locked the player can find themselves in situations where their surrounded by enemies, and unable to move away (either by stun or lack of stamina; or even worse getting stuck on the environment) Areas of less of concern but still annoying terms of game mechanics, The enemies have this attack which the player cannot block, which they are quite fond of using it aaaaa lot. The wolves use it as their opening attack and you won't see the notification icon until it too late. The wolves also don't stick around to fight either, they circle you like a wolf would. However the players walking pace is too slow to catch them and running uses stamina, which you'll run out off instantly. The attack animation will get interrupted, but attack speed isn't a parameter which can be upgraded or made player aware in the weapons menu. Aside from that, the graphics and animations are pretty good, the story is a little meh; but good enough to keep you engaged. The camera, especially for a isometric game, is pretty good. However those game play mechanics makes the game very very frustrating at times; enough to make you want to find a trainer and cheat.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to like this game, but is just not worth it. I've spent 14 hours more than anyone should because i am one to usually end a game before giving it a review, but Achilles: Legends Untold doesn't deserve this just like i don't deserve to keep suffering needlessly by playing this dissapointment of a game;The premise of the game is simple: you are Achilles and you died at the Trojan War but were given a second chance, resurfacing in Greece 10 years after the end of the War to find everything is bad.The gameplay is a mixture of ARPG with Souls-like, with a stamina bar for rolls and attacks along with a "fury" bar for your weapon skills. The game tries to do a lot of different things, but none is particularly deep so there's a very limited crafting system, with some enemies dropping resources needed for some one-use items. Later on there will be some "rifts" that you can choose to close, but they are basically very small arenas. There will also be this big monsters from another dimension that you can hunt down to get skill points, but they are all the same. Achilles  also has a Star-sign attribute system (something which reminds me a little of Grim Dawn), but it is horrible: the star signs used in the game are neither the classic >GREEK< ones, nor something interesting (like the 12 tasks of Herakles/Hercules).The game have some pretty sites, but they are few and far between, most of the time just being some sort of "generic Greek ruin" or another. Enemy design is very dull and repetitive, and after the first few hours (3-4) you will have seen most of what the game has to offer. The enemies are divided in: human (different kinds of soldiers), then wolves,dogs, and lions (just reskins), Cyclops and Gryphons (these two are the only two Mythological monsters you will be facing), then Big Soldier Statue, skeleton, Big Skeleton, plant, Big plant, Bug, giant scorpion. The enemies might have different skins, but mostly just behave the same.The story of the game is dull and manage to be even worse than the gameplay, with atrocious voice acting from most of the cast, forgetful characters, uninspiring design and too much "not now, i will explain this later" going on. If anyone knows what "foreshadowing" means, well, this game doesn't understand the concept of the word, making everything too obvious all of the time.Not every game has to have a great story, and that's fine, but the fact that Achilles TRIES TO make it all that much worse. It even tries to give you some choices by letting you decide to either execute or spare some boss enemies.I think one of the greatest disappointments of the game is that it tries everything, accomplishing nothing. If you want a Greek Tragedy, Greek mythology enemies or anything remotely connected to that, you WON'T find it here. If you want a weak, but serviceable story also, you won't find it here, instead you will find something written by a 14 year old boy who skipped History lessons and never managed to grab a book, with all the male characters trying to force some deep, rough voices and a very buffed, not crippled Hephaestus.The "GAIA AI", which is supposed to make the enemies interact between each other in interesting ways (one of the major selling points of the game) rarely shows and, more often than not, it's poorly implemented.I see this game got a lot of positive reviews, but i also noticed by all of the VERY RARE ACHIEVEMENTS that i got from the game, and that are just mostly story progression, that most people didn't even manage to finish the first part of the game.Keep your distance or check this game some years from now. Achilles has a lot of cool ideas that are just VERY, VERY POORLY implemented.One of the good things about all of this is that i did manage to get a lot of friends from removing this game from their wishlists, because no one deserves to throw their money away at this poor attempt at a game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were to ask someone what the greatest story ever told was, you are very likely to get a whole slew of answers, ranging from the classics like Moby ♥♥♥♥ and Huckleberry Finn to modern day classics like The Cat in the Hat...  Hey don’t hate Dr. Seuss got a lot of people through their childhood.. Giving us things like Green Eggs and Ham, and The Grinch..  Sure he also had some questionable beliefs and may or may not have created some questionable drawings for his books, but most of them are still classics..  Anyway, getting back on track, one of the best stories ever told will surely be the Iliad and the Odyssey, two books interlinked with each other and written by the same man..  Homer.. Not the slightly below average intelligence Safety inspector who chokes his son, but the man responsible for all those great movies we watched about the Trojen war..  One of the main characters of the story Achilles.  A conflicted hero of the Greek army considered to be one of the greatest warriors of all time.. Slayer of Hector, the Trojan Prince and greatest Trojan Warrior..  Also slayer of numerous other notable Trojan soldiers..  Done in by Paris and his lucky arrow..  Forever to be associated with your heel..  This story -  takes the tale of what happens after Achilles stops being polite and starts being real... Ok, that’s totally not what happens, he dies and strikes a deal to work for Hades (yes that Hades) back from the dead and ready to reap souls, collect some scraps.. kill a bunch of stuff,, chew bubble gum, cash checks and crack necks.. Achilles wants to drive a range rover... (ok not really) Not to mention slay some legendary heroes or not if you’re feeling generous..   Gameplay - Achilles legend untold models itself after the Souls series, although not nearly as difficult or polished.  The combat features the things you’d expect from a souls like, blocking, dodging, light and heavy striking.  The game also has a co-op option, which I didn’t partake in before writing this review so I’ll abstain from commenting one way or the other on that aspect..Pro’s  Playing as Achilles is something I never knew I needed to doDecent graphicsFairly fluid and smooth movements Difficulty was fairly good, although needs to be tweakedCon’sHad some issues with Fatal exceptions, seemingly fixed with the latest patchno achievements or trading cards, although game is early accessSome minor graphical and sound issues although it’s early access so...Conclusion The games price of entry is 19.99, a fairly reasonable price for the content delivered, with the game being in early access it could be a doubled edged sword like other games in the past, ALTHOUGH, this game seems to have lots of bells and whistles which aren’t normally included in games which sputter out in early access,, but the potential is there like with all early access titles.  That’s one thing to be weary of when making your decision... BUT the game itself is fully functional with only minor bugs here and there, nothing too concerning.. Things that would be nice to see in future updates, aside from additional content, achievements (we love to show off hits), trading cards (Achilles, Hades, Hector, Paris, Trojan trading cards,, yes please).   So I’d recommend picking this game up, giving it a whirl, and enjoying a game which will have you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an isometric hack and slash that feels like a union of Spartan: Total Warrior and Dark Souls with fun combat and itemisation that sees you wielding weapons with different playstyles, as Achilles in the Underworld after dying to Paris in the siege of Troy. A very interesting premise with a low budget presentation that is at times quite funny, for example when two characters clearly voiced by the same guy are doing slightly different voices and talking to eachother.The enemies in the game call you bastard all the time which is a little degrading but it is what it is. I would have personally used the ancient Greek word it comes from- nothus, which means the same thing. It just sounds a bit more Greeky than a bunch of people calling me bastard in Greek accents. A bit off putting.The combat really is fun. Achilles does a lot of moves iconic from the Brad Pitt performance in Troy, and there are plenty of different moves to try out with each weapon. I actually wish more ARPGs would do combat like this, where you feel like your character is actually fighting and doing combos, instead of just waiting for cooldowns to pop so you can flatten or explode everything on the screen instantly.That's why I compare it to Spartan Total Warrior more than I do other ARPGs like Titan Quest, although it feels a lot like that too at times.Thanks for reading my review you bastard

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This is just an initial impression. I will update this review as I get more time in and more updates are put up.So far the game is rather good and the gameplay seems satisfying.I was playing on the lower of the 2 difficulties available at the start.A few observations so far:1) Combat works well with a controller. Strong and normal attack. Block. Dodge. Run. But also abilities like a 'Spartan Kick' stereotype that pushes people over and a shield throw. All worked quite well.2) Leveling works with shrines you unlock. They allow you to upgrade skills & rest. A bit Dark Souls-like in that you collect life essence / souls to buy skills with.3) The skill tree seems varied and large. Special abilities, stat boosts etc. There seem to be several builds possible at first glance.4) After only an hour of play I can't judge the weapons yet but there is clearly a crafting system and you can find weapons in the levels and equip them.5) The story so far is nice. Troy, Age of Mytholoy, Titan Quest, Classical Greece slammed into the Troy era (so very Homer). The Gods are alive. There are supernatural beasts to fight but also bandits, hoplites etc.6) Levels so far look good. The game is beautiful. I like Achille's design and armor.7) I fought Hector and Paris so far. Judging by how these played out, the basis is there for some rewarding and more complex boss battles later on.Initial impression: Very promising. Hopefully they keep upgrading it. A very promising hack and slash / dark souls / loot & XP grinder game with an awesome theme.Update after some more playtime:1) Loving that they use a system of soul recovery but also have you collect soulshards you keep like in Dark Souls. Wouldn't mind a few more of these drop. Ensuring the pain of a loss of trying to push through is a bit lessened. Overall I like it.2) Good elements of Dark Souls but so far they thankfully don't overdo it either. It is after all partially an action hack and slash rpg with loot. So it looks for a nice blend of Dark Souls skill meets loot and level-up fun. 3) New boss fight I bumped into was challenging but far from impossible. Satisfying for averagely skilled players like me that struggle with hardcore Dark Souls but can appreciate an actual challenge.4) Unlocked some more weapons. I'm liking the selection so far. Love the Classical Greece inspired weaponry so far.5) There seems to be a decent variety of enemies from human to supernatural.Update: Got up to the part of the story released in Early Access.So far I like it a lot.Good combat, fun leveling.I'd love to see more visual/cosmetic variety. (unlockable in game!)And more fun sidequests.Main story is interesting. I get the impression the story will let you side with one of 2 Gods based on some choices you make. Not sure. But if you can go down 2 paths (or more) and thereby unlock other story content & weapons (ideal for replayability!) that's awesome!Update:Probably my final version of the review.Fully released. I gave the game another playthrough.Though not on a hard difficulty. I also did it in 2 or so sittings. So my memory of the early story part may be a little bit blurry. Still my criticism and praise won't be very influenced by it overall.The Story:The final story we got is both better and worse than the pre release version.I rather liked the teasing of picking Ares or Hades. The early interactions with Hades there etc.The story was massively changed (may always have been intended as such) and now focus on helping Hades stop Phobos.It works although i preferred a lot of the earlier story structure, the sequence of some plot events etc.Overall the storyline is satisfying though. With a fitting ending.A few criticisms though:- the flaws of Achilles though a crucial part of the plot are not that explored. HOWEVER I spared everyone. IF memory serves there was a bad ending teased that may dig a bit more into that.- It felt a bit rushed near the end. I feel the game could've used another map maybe fleshing out your 2 main support NPC's. And a map digging into Phobos's realm.Gameplay however is good.A bit of Titan Quest / Diablo, a bit 3rd Person Hack and Slash (traditional) and a little bit of Dark Souls mechanics. Play it at a lower difficulty and it plays more like a hack and slash looter and play it at a higher difficulty and it leans a bit more into the light Dark Souls mechanics. In short you can play it chill and you can play it a bit more stressfully.Upgrades and weapons are pretty varied with an interesting skill and build system with plenty of options.There is a decent amount of side activities and things to unlock.And a chill run will allow you to dive into New Game + at a higher difficulty, digging purely into the challenging combat while having unlocked a lot of the fun stuff.I Can definitely recommend this one.I wouldn't mind seeing them use this system for a Sparta themed action rpg in fantasy greece. Especially really early Classical Greece or Persian Wars era.Mixed in with a good dose of Greek and Persian myth.In any case as stated well worth picking up.If you're unsure wait for a small discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles the Angsty Teenager - is a fun game, in dire need of polish. The combat, especially against larger enemies, is great. BUT there are bugs and frustrations aplenty, chiefly the following:1. The targeting system is very poorly suited to this game. It was probably shovelled in for the  sake of (craft-able) throwables, but both crafting and throwing are superfluous, so we now have three half-arsed systems, instead of one good combat system.2. _childDocuments_.review: It's just OK for that small price. The idea of taking mechanics and a combat system like in Dark Souls only harms this game. I immediately turned off focusing on the target because it works terribly, it switches to the wrong enemy and constantly jumps.And in general, this seems like an unnecessary mechanic in the game. Because in this RPG genre, when you have a lot of enemies on the screen from all sides, the last thing you will do is focus on any specific enemy. This is the main problem with the combat system in this game. It was specifically made around focusing on one target, like in Dark Souls. Some of the hero's abilities are directed and without focusing on one target, you will simply use the ability past the target, even if the enemy is standing in front of you.But if you thought that for a normal game it’s enough to simply turn off focusing on one target and choose non directed abilities, you’re very mistaken.. Without focusing on the target, it is also very easy to miss with simple attacks, because the hero does not hit the nearest target, as in similar RPG games. The hero simply attacks ahead of himself. Therefore, you need to try hard to ensure that your hero is directly in front of the enemy at the moment of impact. I would say that the combat system is the biggest disappointment and biggest problem in this game. Just remove it from the game, make it like Diablo or Titan Quest and this game will shine with new colors and be 10 times better.Next, the looting and items systems. The game has a huge number of secondary items, such as bombs, traps, weapon oil, potions, and many other resources. And all this is useless. I beat the game using only healing potions, simply because everything else in the game has no value. And also because using all this is completely inconvenient, since it is again implemented like in Dark Souls, with crossbar buttons which you don't have time to use in the action battle and, again, you need to focus the target first.  Also, switching a huge number of these items causes difficulties, because only 4 items can be placed on the panel. They can only be changed through the inventory. It would be good to display the second panel by holding the button, but for some reason there is no such feature in the game.There is no value in different weapons either. During the entire game I changed weapons 2-3 times and it was just for fun. I essentially beat the game with the same weapons, without even really upgrading them. Played on medium difficulty. Many identical points of interest on the map - basements, chests, improved chests with search for keys. This gets boring by the middle of the game and you simply ignore them, not only because of the same type, but also because of the lack of value in these activities. There are also Metroidvania elements here; you cannot open some of the chests without receiving an ability that is given later during the story. I had no desire to go back and open it.  There is little variety of enemies in the game and they are often repetitive, especially in the second half of the story. I guess this can hardly be called a problem, given the overall length of the game and the small size of the world. The developers tried to make a good game, but for some reason they decided to build it around the mechanics of hyped souls-like games, which negatively affected the final result and only made the game worse. In general, I would rather rate it between good and bad, but considering the price of the game, the fact that I am a fan of ancient Greece and a more or less good story, I am more inclined to give a positive rating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isand I highly recommend it for everybody, especially for those who own Steam Deck!The game is strongest where it should be - in the interlocking mechanics that make it hard to tear yourself away 🔥 an example of such a gameplay loop? You have a task to complete, so you follow the marker. When you reach it, you decide to go a bit further to reach the checkpoint. Upon reaching the checkpoint, you decide to explore the nearby basement. There, you find a weapon that you want to try out, so you continue on, past the checkpoint. There, you level up and realize there's a side quest nearby, so you go for it. After completing the quest, you're close to another checkpoint, and why not unlock it? Especially since you feel your character growing stronger and sense their power. Words might not capture it fully, but the gameplay is incredibly immersive 😀Other strong points?-full voice acting-pleasant music and sounds-diverse landscapes and locations-the atmosphere of mythological Greece permeates from all sidesWhat could be better? Playing Achilles: Legends Untold is an exceptional fun & adventure, but the potential for a sequel to elevate the experience even further is undeniable. The game is great, but individual elements could be deeper. The graphics are OK, but no one will be picking up their jaws from the floor. The progression system is OK, but more skills and the ability to diversify builds would be welcome. The weapons are OK, but no one would mind more equipment and its features. Quests are OK, but it would be nice to have choices as well. Don't get me wrong - none of this hinders the game because it plays great. It's just that with a bigger budget, more time for production, and lessons learned from the first part, the creators would likely make a global hit. Achilles: Legends Untold is practically made for it. The game runs ultra-smoothly, both in terms of FPS and due to the fact that transitions between locations take a maximum of a second. Well-distributed checkpoints allow for both long and short gameplay sessions - but it's more likely to be a long one because the game is as captivating as a swamp! All buttons are perfectly mapped, and one doesn't have to ponder over the controls. Just fantastic!My recommendationSee you in ancient Greece!
