_childDocuments_.review: Even though it's still in the early stages of development it is a very good game to play. It combines many elements from Soul games and ARPG games like Titan Quest and Diablo, which is not a bad idea. The environmental design is very beautiful with a lots of potentials for improvement. The only thing i don't like is that there is no map in settlement areas. That means if i die it's very hard to retrieve my lost "souls" because i just don't know were to look for them. Another thing i noticed is that when i use a poison resistance potion i still get poisoned the same if i don't use it. I suppose that is because it's still in early access.My conclusion? I will continue play this game because i am a big fan of greek mythology and it has a lot of potentials to became a very good and solid Soul/ARPG game.Waiting for the next update!
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself plays well. Combat is smooth-ish, sometimes not fluid but not enough to be painful.My only gripe would be the buffs/potions used to enhance weapons during combat. They do not last anywhere near long enough for a player to gain an advantage from using them (so I don't use).Also the harps that enable extra chance for loots drops from enemies, again, don't last long enough to gain any advantage from using them.Other than that, the game is decent. Story line is intriguing & spins a different narrative on the gods & their in-fighting.Interested to see where this game goes from here
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Still Early Access, but already a very good game. If you like Titan Quest and always wished a more active combat system with melee weapons: here's your game! That means: in addition to the two attacks (one normal left-click and a slower but heavier strike via right mouseclick) there is also the option of active shield defense and two evasive maneuvers (one smaller step back and a dodge roll). There is also the option of throwing your shield for a ranged attack.I am just missing an option to throw a spear and hope something like that will be added to the game later! Would be especially interesting since it's actual fighting technique for ancient times to first throw a spear and follow with your melee weapon. I definitely prefer that also in effectiveness than just throwing a magic shield, losing your only protection (even if you get it back easily) ;-)Conclusion: I already hope that, like in TQ, many more DLCs will follow, extending the current ancient world!
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice surprise !Gameplay is super fun and smooth. Maybe you guys could try to implement some secrets inside boxes you have to hit.And maybe some randomly generated armors / weapons ? Weapon usage might be a good idea for difficulty as well if you plan on relying on crafting (which i guess is the case, but not reached yet)It seems that you guys really used nicely the 3 dimensions, as some area use nicely the verticality  in dungeons. I would recommend as well to try maybe to add secret drop passage with hidden balcony.I feel like the stamina comes back a little bit too fast in hero difficulty (or maybe we just have too much to begin with, i personnaly like it really level depedent), otherwise it's quite well balanced.Skill tree seems quite decent, and level size is really nice. Really nice souls / titan quest mix.Just need some optimization for some fps drops depending on levels. Still recommended, and i will be impatient for full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing. I've always wondered why there aren't many games about Achilles.I've expected the game to be based around Trojan war rather than this fictionalized story, but it is still pretty good. Story is fine, graphics are good, dialogues could be better but it's fine and even voice actors did a good job. Of course game has bugs cuz it's in early access, there are many things I'd point out that I would like to see more (cutscenes for example) but I won't bother too much.All in all, very good game, it's worth the money. Objectively 7/10, but since I love Achilles, I have to give it a 10. Keep it up :D
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this game only has that many reviews. Dark Point Games is a developer (and publisher) that clearly is here to make a statement, this game lacks of very little, though beware, it is not for the faint of heart.It is best described as a fusion between Titan Quest and Dark Souls. Uh?!? You read me right. The view is isometric, à la Titan Quest, there's loot, not as complex as in an ARPG, but enough to expend your gameplay in a way that best suits your preferences and the mechanics are very much like a Souls-type game. I never thought this could work so well in isometric but this title is proving it certainly can. The environments are vibrant, well distinguished, you have mini-dungeons as you'd expect in games such as Diablo, enemies should not be approached all in the same fashion and certain combinations of enemies will give you a harder time, but with patience, timing and strategy, everything can be overcome. However, death is very much part of the experience, again, like other titles of it's genre.Right from the beginning, the game does a great job pulling you into it's story. While it is nothing you wouldn't have seen before, the narrative is well delivered and at good pace. Dark Point Games did pull the stops to not let the plot feel like an half-ass'ed effort, for a game where one could be forgiven to have done so, however they carefully crafted the storytelling. The sound design is very clever, you feel the environment you find yourself in. SFX are as immersive, as they helpful, guiding you through assaults, assisting your timings, etc. Best played with a headset by the way. Quite frankly, I sound biased but really, this game exceeded my expectations and already it had caught my attention a while back. And last but not least, this game is so reasonable in it's asking price. It really is dirt cheap for the quality it offers and the quality of gameplay, the variety in skills, weapons, build, etc.The one part that I can't comment on unfortunately is the Co-op but from having loaded a game, it would seem that they are unique layouts meant to be played with someone, however you can still carry over your progress to your main game, that is the impression it gave me.And so, this would be my one disappointment, which is a bit obnoxious as I haven't played the part, but nothing leads me to believe the main campaign can be experienced as a multiplayer game but it'd be SOOOO COOL. Imagine playing any Souls with a friend, how would you approach certain bosses, how would you deal with encounters, how differently would you both build your characters to make the most out of your playthrough?I hope the developers consider making the campaign fully playable in co-op, especially as this game is very difficult, though that's not a negative for me, quite the opposite in fact.Don't sleep on this title, give it the 2 hours and refund if you think it's not for you but honestly, it's much more than I expected it to be. And last but not least, I will address the length of some of the reviews I've read, apparently, the developer is working on adding more, YAY! However, I couldn't stress this enough, this game is undoubtly a "quality over quantity" kind of thing, let that sink in.Brava, Dark Point Games, brava.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this is a great game. The cutscenes are a little underdeveloped, like animations when characters are speaking, but, the gameplay definite makes up for that. Honestly it's the best action rpg I've played in a long while. The combat is awesome. It would help having a minimap and such, but I know it's being worked on - it's early access. I didn't go into it expecting it to be polished. But thus far the gameplay has me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: For EA this game is far more polished than most larger budget games. For a top-down action RPG with some souls-like elements, I think they've nailed a great foundation. I love the combat and difficulty (though could be more difficult IMO). With some added content, polish, and more skills this will be a great release. I only hope other top-down ARPGs take note on what Dark Point has done so far. Keep up the great work DPG! Look forward to your finished product.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I review this game well...i'm saying like a 7.1/10 so far. The one thing I will tell you is, obviously it's in early access! I get that! Still. with all that said, I think this game has a lot of potential!
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: First of a quickfire review of the game can be found here: Achilles Legends Untold lets you take charge of the greek hero, equipped with a light and heavy attack, an abundance of weapons, a huge talent tree which gives basic attribute buffs and new skills, and a third ressource called fury to dish out heavy hitting special attacks and/or using your shield like Captain America would, as a throwing bomerang.This game provides you with a huge open world to explore without a lineal path and the lack of any sort of map makes it even harder to simply follow the main story questline. Luckily Achilles comes equipped with a "turn left here" - navigation system which can be used to move in the right direction if you ever feel stuck.Does this game has flaws?Yes. Can they be fixed?Yes. Are they typical early access flaws?Yes.Should I stop that question/answer shtick? Yes.Final thoughts, if you like souls-like combat, a meaningful talent tree, open world exploration and looting/upgrading fancy equipment, you should definitely check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: For Early Access game, looks fairly good.Ancient Greek theme on point. Combat mechanics are decent.Different enemy/monster types are good.Skill Tree has enough variety to go different ways/play styles.Enemy AI still needs some work.All in all 7/10.Looking forward to seeing finished game and other content.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: great idea, decent game, quite a bit of jank.Changing the idea of hack'n'slash from mindlessly slaughtering millions of monsters to carefully planning every approach works really well in this genre. It has a lot of Dark Souls elements: stamina system and relatively low health, souls we gather from enemies or bottles that are used to upgrade our character, shrines in which we rest or respawn after death, and enemies that respawn if we do. And it fits really well. Graphics are good, for a genre, and we have dynamic camera that can both give us great shots of ongoing battle and sometimes be a bit of a nuisance. Music is decent. Writing and voice-acting is nothing special, personally i find it pretty low on the list in those games anyway. And I do like the game set in greek mythos.Now, as it is still in early access it definitely has some problems. Some will require just minor tweaks, other might be problematic.One thing that was bothering me is the lack of map. While the game takes many inspirations from the DS series, in DS we could freely look around, to not get lost or notice places we want to explore. Achilles doesn't have that. In this way it's more like metroidvania games, like Hollow Knight for example. And without any kind of map (even simple, static, without showing where our character currently is) it's easy to get lost or just miss some things.The other thing was aiming with mouse. For some reason the character aims at a different angle, than it's supposed to, while it should look at the pointer. With fast attacks it isn't very bothersome, but for heavy attacks and shield blocks it's a nightmare.And sometimes there are frame drops for no apparent reason, which in this type of game is quite an issue.Minor issues I've found so far: - during the first boss fight on the bridge, boss spawned underneath it. Could do anything, had to teleport out and try again (which was successful then) - sometimes the sound of unsheathing weapons still plays even though the enemies are dead - big scorpions walking sound is waaay too loud - not exactly a bug, but menu managing for every single bottle of souls is a bit annoying - in some places text doesn't match the voice, and is displayed in weird paceDespite those issues, the game was fun so far, there is a lot of potential in this, and after some fixes it will be definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game wholeheartedly, but by no means it's not without it's problems. Movement can be a bit clunky and hard to get a hang of it, but when you do its very rewarding. The climate of this game is really good, it's mainly what seperates it from other dark-souls-likes. The skill tree is fun to explore. The worst thing is that its only the first chapter, but its still enough to be worth its price. I know it will get better with time. Don`t listen to the nitpicks and try it yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game! I like the graphics. Imitates hot Mediterranean sunlight. That was a nice touch. For early access, not bad, had no problems running it.The game is very playable so you don’t waste time and can dive right in. Once you go with the flow, you can enjoy just the right level of challenge to enjoy every success. I really like the general climate of ancient Grece, and the way it was interpreted for the game. It’s not accurate, sure, but it doesn’t have to be. It’s just supposed to be fun and playable :)Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game,  especially like exploration; killing the undead help me relax after exams. The combat system is particularly well made; the opponents are not the strongest, but being careless you can assemble a large group that will be a problem, which balances the game well. The character development and combo crafting system is solid. For me, one of the biggest discoveries this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good game with ancient Greek theme. Gameplay is fun and sometimes can be hard (you've to be focused all the time or you will die), but its not Souls level of difficulty. Graphics, animations and voice acting are decent.Cons:- lack of map - when you die and want to get back to your body for lost souls, sometimes it's hard to remember where exactly you died, which wasn't a problem in Souls games- frame drops - it's far from game breaking, but game needs some more polish. In some areas you have like 80fps then you move few steps and it drops to 40-50fpsGame is cheap and I definitely recommend to try it out. It's cool action rpg with Soulslike mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Overall its a good game with very interesting mechanics, there are flaws in the games like MAPS!!! please include them in!. other than that the stamina and dodge mechanics is a new add to this genre of game. its relatively hard to play the game for a casual gamer like me... game engine needs to be further improve for smoother gameplay..controls are abit laggy idk if its a game feature or not... the input lag is quite visible esp when using blockgreat job for the developers working to bring this game and idea forward... its great afterall..
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Greek mythology meets Dark Souls!This game is a lot of fun and poses a good challenge with lots of rewards and upgrades. If you enjoy Greek mythology and hack and slash game-play, you'll enjoy Achilles. Despite some rough voice acting, the overall narrative is interesting and serves as a sort of epilogue to Homer's Iliad.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game ! Reminds me of Dark Souls, Titan Quest and the movie Troy. Hacking and slashing is fun although a bit different than lets say Diablo so it takes some time to get used to. Graphics and sound are pleasing. Sometimes the game can get a little choppy  with frame drops but all in all great work. 8/10, will play some more.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game, but it needs work. Achilles: Legends Untold is a uncut gem. It tries to blend together the isometric camera of diablo games as well as difficulty and combat style of soulslike games. Sadly the combat animations don’t feel as responsible as in FromSoftware title and maps/enemies don’t fell as polished as PoE or beforementioned blizzard’s title.  The game has good Greek mythology inspired story with additional twist which allows devs for setting up a interesting campaign for the protagonist.As far as for early access title the game is worth recommending. Can’t wait for the game to develop into the masterpiece it could be.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game! It is obvious that there are still many issues to iron out, but the concept is solid, the visual side is very appealing and, judging by how active the developers are (just look at the number of updates and information they provide), I am confident that Achilles: Legends Untold will move confidently towards becoming a complete, bug-free game. As for the gameplay itself, I can definitely see myself spending many evenings with this game :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: So this is Dark souls with Titan quest. I must say its addicting and it really gets hard at times. The combat is very different than any other games so it will take some time to get used to all the dodges and parries and blocks. You really need to use the skills to go past certain areas. For the price its really worth it but get ready to be frustrated when you die over and over again. Dont put a bad review because its hard. When you learn the movement its really smooth and you can fight 7-8 enemies at the same time. This game is in early access so there are quite a few bugs and you can get stuck at places but just exit the game and log in again and you are back to normal. I hope they add more to the questline in the game , it has a lot of potential. It took me 11 hours to reach the last quest playing solo so far but it says its not available so I think its only the beginning. The world is huge to run around and you have a feeling of open world when the different parts connect.There is smithing and materials and interesting skills so you can occupy yourself for some more time if you want and not do the quests, i just played the story back to back.I really enjoyed this though and looking forward to moreEdit: I just read its only the first chapter in early access of five in the full product so thats really awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed playing Achilles so far. Combat is challenging, but when you win there is a lot of satisfaction involved. Graphics and animations are really pretty and it's nice to stop for a while and appreciate the surroundings. For an Early Access Product it feels really good and I will wait for finished product with anticipation for even better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing a lot of mixed reviews.....Tbh I like the game. Runs pretty smooth on my PC, prefer using controller over keyboard (found the key mapping to be weird....who makes ctrl the block button??????) but anyway, yea I like it. Does it have a ways to go until I would consider it "complete" sure, it feels like a game thats about 70% finished. Needs some polishing and what not but it'll get there. I think my biggest gripe is how much stamina is used for each swing, or how weird the enemies are in terms of responsiveness, and the occasional buggy spawn shrines but w/e it'll get fixed....for less than $20 get it now so you can beat it later, it'll be worth it 10000 times over for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly cool, especially the graphics, especially especially for it being an early access. I am not a good player and while true, I have died a lot, I still had fun.I played this game with my friend. First we played on our singleplayer saves and grinded some mobs (she got to lv 20, while I reached only 14). Later we switched to co-op. Here no issues. Just start your own game, invite a friend and voila you can play together. Or better yet survive the boss and laugh at your friend who died shielding you :) .Good times.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold is an isometric action RPG game, greatly inspired by the souls-like genre and old-school hack&slash games. The players will venture through many unwelcoming locations, battling legendary creatures and trying to piece up the story of the world. The game is a bit lighter on the "souls" side, as the studio wanted to create an easy-to-learn but hard to master experience. Because of that, Achilles: Legends Untold may be enjoyed by the souls veterans and new players alike. And if help is needed, just summon your friends to play together in jolly cooperation, and explore various dungeons together.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

name: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes
detailed_description: Return to the battlegrounds of Bersia in Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes, the sequel to the Xbox cult hit Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders, updated into HD for modern PCs. Command new units across seven new campaigns, each featuring a new playable character. Medieval mayhem returns! Orcs and ogres, vampires, and knights - command them all in this epic conflict of steel and strategy! Enhanced for modern PCs: - Game controllers support (a gamepad is recommended for optimal experience) plus an all-new mouse & keyboard mode. - Revisit classic battlefields in widescreen HD (including ultrawide support). - Rock on and ride out, accompanied by a high-powered metal soundtrack. Bigger, badder, better than ever: - A massive new game in the Kingdom Under Fire saga. - Seven new playable characters, each with their own story-driven campaign. - Lead from the front as a half-vampire count, an ogre warlord, or graceful dark elf. - Command new forces, including powerful elemental creatures. - Call in airstrikes and artillery and watch the battlefield burn. - Conquer fifty complex new missions, plus an endless range of random battles. Become a master of war and wield the battlefield as a weapon. - Defend the high ground and ride down into your opponent’s ranks. - Lay traps and ambushes in forests, or smoke your foes out with fire arrows. - Call in air units to pummel foes with cannon fire or their own plummeting hulls. - Pay heed to the elements. Wind and rain can change the course of a battle. - Cast powerful magic and call on artillery. Scatter your troops to avoid reprisal. Master seven new heroes, both light and dark: - Lead the charge as spectacularly powerful new characters. - Lash your enemies as a half-vampire, or crush them as a massive ogre. - Crush your foes with powerful new combos - Build your army with monstrous new troops and powerful support units - Assign allied commanders to your forces, each with their own abilities & magic - Lead, fight, hunt. Master the tactical map and remember: One hero can only go so far. Reforge your soldiers in the fires of war: - Explore the continent across two different eras of the explorable campaign map. - Build your perfect army. Lead regiments of humans, elves, orcs, and more. - Loot, level, and grow powerful. Evolve your troops into new forms and master their skills. - Re-write the rules of battle with powerful combat magic, supportive and destructive. - Command the elements with Fire Wraiths, Ice Maidens, Thunder Rhinos, and Earth Golems. The battlefield calls to you once more, commander. Your troops stand ready.

_childDocuments_.review: My all time favorite game finally made it to Steam after many, many years. A port I stopped hoping for long ago.The game runs perfectly with a controller. (I am using an Xbox One controller)There is no multiplayer (yet?) and the Custom Game is a thing. (Create your own mission)For the new players, this game is a kind of RTS (Total War) meets Dynasty Warrior. You've got troops that you can upgrade and gear up in your missions, including your chosen Hero that you control on the battles. This game is old. It came out back in 2005 on the original Xbox and it's still looking pretty great despite the age.Anyway, thank you so much again for bringing this game to Steam. That was an instant buy from me.PS: Some campaigns can be real hard, be warned. :)   Might update this review eventually as I progress through the game..
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to fix your save slots. Delete the save game by pressing tab on the keyboard, then you'll get a prompt to delete it. Hit yes, then manually save over that slot.Step by Step Process:1. Start New Game.2. Get through intro mission.3. Press home on the keyboard.4. Navigate to save game.5. spam enter through all the save slot message spam BS.6. Press tab on the keyboard.7. Delete the "damaged game."8. Save over slot.From there you should be able to save and reload your game. It's an odd ♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the port.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell this is good guys. It seems to be on par with the first KuF port. The controls feel good (if you're using keyboard like me, HOLD TAB to issue movement and attack commands to your currently selected troops, and HIT TAB to switch between troops, this should help you a lot when you are starting out) though a controller is recommended since all of the onscreen buttons are for the controller.I've only played the first few levels but the single player and skirmish modes are here and available to play. For those hoping for multiplayer - I DO NOT see it as an option on the title screen. But for those like me that are here for the single player and skirmish modes only - the game seems to have all of that in tact. So I am pretty excited to play this game again. I am currently playing the game on a NON-gaming laptop and the game runs smoothly without issue, the game runs well during heavy combat and troop movements  - so that is great.  I just want to thank Blueside for putting this out. I believe that KuF has some of the most unique game play even years after the original xbox games were released, and I hope to see more Non-MMO KuF games in the future. I would gladly support them. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Save your money and frustration, find a way to play the Xbox version.I don't write Steam reviews, but something is wrong with this port. I bought this in a bundle with Crusaders, which was fine, but this game has so many strange problems that ruin the game. I had to write something to warn people.The pathfinding is the worst. You can try your hardest to get units to just go straight up, but instead they will take a hard right, run in a few circles, go up left, then die because they were getting slaughtered by archers the whole time. This goes for retreating from battles too. Your units will not go in the direction you're telling them to escape and seem to just pick at random where they'll go. You will not see this in the Xbox original.Archers also don't behave as they should. Normally archers when told to attack will attempt to back off and continue to shoot at enemy units as they close in. That just doesn't seem to happen in this port. It's actually kind of useful since the enemies have more archers than you and they will just stand there and let you attack them instead of trying to run and shoot. Sometimes they run, but it's still not the expected behavior from the Xbox version.Damage is just off, units will die way faster than they do in the Xbox version. I felt like Ellen's first mission was a bit harder, but I figured I was just not used to the differences between Crusaders and this, but no. Booting up the Xbox version you'll notice that troops inside of units die way faster, they seem to get damaged faster as well, and it's not the passive damage mechanic that everyone in the Steam community is talking about. Your bar will go from red to empty in an instant unlike the original Xbox version.There's also minor audio and visual glitches, like the mini-map not being properly transparent in the fog of war zones. The dark elf death sound is just off, it sounds like it's cutting out a half a second into the sound then repeating itself. In menus or the map screen the annoying PC control pop-up keeps showing up and making a noise every time it does. Even if you turn the visual pop-up off the noise persists with an annoying clunk every second or so while you're trying to listen to the dialogue. There's gotta be more, but I just can't think of them.I beat Ellen's campaign and stopped part way through Walter's. On the mission where you're supposed to escort Leinhart. The pathfinder just ♥♥♥♥ it's pants so hard I had to restart the mission multiple times and take like an hour of time to beat a simple mission. That's when I got the Xbox version to confirm to myself that it wasn't this bad. Turns out I was right. I'm playing through the Xbox version now and haven't seen any of these problems. This is just a butchered port. Do not buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the KUF games on the original xbox, you will love this. Because for all intents and purposes, it's pretty much the same game. While the store page calls this an HD version, this pretty much only applies to resolution and even then just barely. Hell, even fonts and UI elements have had absolutely nothing done to them for this release, and look grainy and muddy as all hell. There are absolutely no graphics options or enhancements whatsoever, the draw distance is just as low as it was on the original xbox (covered by the classical ever present thicc sandstorm / fog / snowstorm), the framerate is limited to 30fps, you get the idea. And to top it off, although they mention they have implemented a keyboard mode for this re release, it's keyboard controls are about on par with dark souls in terms of being absolutely so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrendous and unintuitive that you may as well not bother with keyboard and mouse. Its the classical stereotypical asian-dev PC port where you kind of wonder why the hell the devs even bothered, given the improved experience you get of this port is marginal at best compared to emulating the original xbox game. Keys are rebindable, but the game was built from the ground up with a controller in mindNow you may be wondering why after that amount of scorching i would still recommend this game, and it's because if you have a controller (i wouldn't know, i dont have one for my PC), the game is truly amazing and there is nothing quite like it before or after it's original release. One thing that i really have to give the game credit for is it's implementation of multiple campaign , each with it's own viewpoint, playstyle and story and timing in the overall story for each game. _childDocuments_.review: KUF: Heroes is a semi-RTS mixed with some hack n slash based in a dark fantasy world. It consists of 7 campaigns, each taking place around the events of the previous game (Crusaders), so I recommend playing that first if you haven't to get a better grip on each campaign's story.Presentation - Not too shabby, especially when there are hundreds of troops on the map at once. Models are nice, with a large variety of human, dark elf and orc troops. You can see some of units raise their weapons when approaching an enemy troop. The maps and environments themselves are... decent; sometimes a map would literally just be a flat desert, though you'll mostly be focusing on fighting anyway.Music - A metallic treat for the ears. IMO much better than Crusader's soundtrack since I happily gave myself a migraine from all the head-banging.Gameplay - Very solid and feels great to play on the PC using a controller (a huge plus since it'd crash a lot on the original XBOX). Again, highly suggest playing Crusaders first because Heroes lacks a real proper tutorial, so the learning curve is a tad steep. You engage in skirmishes in a board and control a hero troop, plus any additional troops you wish to bring along. The troops you control are groups of units instead of single units (think of Total War). You control your troops in a semi-RTS mode and go into a Dynasty Warriors-esque style mode when your hero troop is in battle with another troop, and your other troops always stay in RTS mode. The campaigns consist of two factions: humans and the dark legion (dark elves and orcs). Both factions have different unit jobs such as infantry, archers, giant eagles and giant scorpions. Each job has strengths and weaknesses you need to learn in order to crush your enemies (and not get crushed yourself). After each battle you can level up your hero and troops, buy gear and hire mercenaries for more troops.Story - Not too bad. Each campaign takes place before and/or during the events of Crusaders and serves to fill in some holes and enrich the story. Voice acting is shaky aside from Morene and Rupert, but personally I find the cheesy quality to be enjoyable. Overall, a great and fun mix of RTS and hack n slash. I give it 8 dark elf butts out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! This is what you are missing if you like other RTS games like starcraft, warcraft, total war; more of a third person look at commanding multiple troops in a chaotic style battle!I would like to say with all due respect, to ignore the reviews saying this game was never meant for a keyboard. I have played other RTS games on console (starcraft 64, war hammer xbox360, ogrebattle) and can confidently say they would all be better utilised on the pc. If your take is the controller than by all means, play to your desire.In any battle the first thing I do is press space. The map mode is your ultimate tool for movement, controller or keyboard. I do not suggest moving your troops in the third person mode ever. You will be confused and lose track of where your troops should be, as well your rider units will be best utilised when on a multiple rout. with that said, im not gonna tell anyone how to win their war, but I use my riders alot. If you use riders too, then the SHIFT key will be your best friend. I keep the natural WASD and right hand on mouse for the whole battle. I only find myself in My heroes combat mode maybe 15% of the whole skirmish. Your gonna want your heals consistent, your riders riding, and your support supporting. It's chaotic because its meant to be, if you find yourself overwhelmed, it's because you're supposed to. Position is everything, thats why your map mode with the space bar is so important. keep your archers behind, your infantry infront, and your riders ultimately controlling the skirmish, by being everywhere. Have fun and die well!

Ensure you have two wizards with different magic. I usually have Earth and Lighting, but Fire is always a safe bet. The support troops I will have one Cavalry squad. _childDocuments_.review: This is the game that made my childhood.I always wanted to fight in the middle of a great war, inspired by the scenes made famous by the Lord of the Rings trilogy.  If you have a love for strategy, armies of swords, and an album of metal rock to accompany you into every heated battle, this game is for you.Some may compare it to Dynasty Warriors and I say that similarities only go up to the genre of hack-and-slash.  Unlike Dynasty Warriors which involves an overpowered singular hero (the player) mowing down an entire army of cannon fodder soldiers, Kingdom Under Fire places great emphasis on the player's ability to not only control their hero, but the squads of units that follow them.  Soldiers are not cannon fodder - losing them and upgrading them can mean life and death in a battle.  If not careful, players can fall prey from simply charging into the fray without considering the layout of the incoming enemy force.  Cavalry is ideal for charging down foot soldiers, but die in seconds when inpaled by enemy spearmen.  Archers must be positioned to avoid melee and so that their arrow don't get hindered by trees.  Believing that your hero can alone take on the entire world is hubris here.  Strategy and game awareness go hand in hand here.  Simple soldiers can do damage to you, underlining the notion that you are more of a leader than an overpowered hero with ridiculous amounts of mana.  You are closer to Aragon leading an army of men rather than Lu Bu simply mashing the attack button to effortlessly make the world bend to your will.When it comes to story, Kingdom under Fire follows the tales of 7 individuals, each with their own role in the war raging across their continent.  Fans of the previous game (Kingdom Under Fire: Crusaders) will recognize many of the faces they walk next to here.  Newcomers don't have to play the previous game to get the full experience of Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes, while doing so gives you greater insight on the story.  Each character boasts a unique backstory, an individual set of moves and playstyles, and a faction from the religious Ecclesia to the vampire-ruled Vellond.  The world is at war, you play characters from different sides which give more perspective to the war in its entirety, and finishing each hero's campaign unlocks a form of New Game Plus.  Story stages throughout the map are unlocked, allowing the player to replay these levels with the heroes they've completed with.  If you love crafting your ideal army, making them stronger with better upgrades and skills and unleashing them in a map of battles you once conquered, all the more reason to complete all seven.For all those who have a knack for hack-and-slash strategy that is different from turn-based gameplay and Dynasty Warrior overpoweredness, I strongly suggest giving this game a whirl.  Enter a world of men, elves, dark elves, dwarves, orcs, and vampires who all fight for supremacy over the land.  Fight across snowy mountains, scorching deserts, and wide empty plains where the environment can be used for or against you.  Command a colorful cast of heroes whose stories you'll wield against a colossal tide of intrigue and impossible battles.  In a kingdom under fire, men go into war.  Heroes lead the way.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Crusaders is so much better than this game. Just play that. There's nothing of value here.Main issues are the game becomes repetitive much faster than Crusaders, because to get through all the campaigns you'll have to keep starting and restarting, and every campaign ends in like 3 hours, each, (If you're wondering about my play time, I just left the game on) so you never adapt or switch up classes or feel attached to your army through a long hard campaign like you do in Crusaders. Also all the stories (So far) are ether genuinely awful, boring or just fine because they limited themselves to being a prequel (Mostly). Every addition to this game has a draw back:There's now a skirmish mode! - you have to set up both players armies for a specific general, and the game does not save them if you turn the game off.There's new units! - 4 elemental monsters that can be picked by both factions (So there goes the asymmetry), that are so expensive to level up, die so fast when you use them and are so hyperspecific at what they are good at, that you ARE NOT using them, ever.There's skirmish maps in the campaign to grind - Did people want this? You couldn't grind at all in Crusaders because it was 4 well designed linear campaigns. It used an entire campaign to tutorial you how to beat the hard campaigns. (Even if you're scared of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up your build, just have a general on a longbow unit that can cast heal). Plus the skirmish maps themselves are just large, flat, empty maps with enemy units scattered around with their AI turned off... and they're in everyone's campaign.Speaking of which! Let's just rank the campaigns, so if you're determined to not get Crusaders instead for some reason, you'll at least know what to expect (No spoilers):1. Walter's - Amazing opening level that has you genocide a village screaming for you to stop, as you then hunt down the fleeing refugees (Someone mod this level into Kendal's campaign! as a reveal mid campaign). It is horrifying and well executed... rest of campaign's alright. This is 1 out of the 2 campaigns actually taking place during Crusades, so you know exactly what happens because Kendal's campaign in Crusaders is about hunting down Walter. So the impact's kinda lost, and they reuses an important cutscene that is meaningless to this game because what happens only effect the characters in Crusaders... 8/102. Ellen's - It's fine. It's the tutorial campaign. It was a good first impression 6/103. Cirith's - This was stupid. I haven't finished it (Burnt out from the game), but from what I have it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid! You're companions consist of a poet who uses paragraphs to wax poetic about how hot you are, and some gremlin girl who only cares about shiny things. They also turned Cirith from this carefree cynic, in Crusaders, into the most turns to camera "Can you believe this?" kinda character. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid! 3/104/5/6. Leinhart's / Morene's / Urukubarr's - I never played them and probably never will. I am interested in how Urukubarr's is the hardest campaign, but playing that requires me to play Morene's... which requires me to finish Cirith's... eeeeeeeeeeeehhh....7. Rupert's - I know I said no spoilers, but... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Who asked themselves, while playing Gerald's campaign, how Rupert got the alliance between the Dwarves and Elves, while you were defending the keep? was it the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that asked for the skirmish maps!? You know EXACTLY what's going to happen plot wise, so they tried to focus on the character of Rupert. Turning a meathead with a heart of gold, volunteering on a suicide mission to escort emissaries to forge an alliance to save his comrades, into Partick Star from Spongebob. He spend the entire campaign forgetting what he's doing, has zero urgency, constantly getting lost, crying about how stupid and useless he feels, and repeatedly getting drunk off of dwarven ale (Because it was mentioned off hand in ONE LINE he said during Crusaders, to humble the people congratulating him for saving their lives). I ♥♥♥♥ you not, the emissary who's your companion, leaves the party to forge the alliance without you. But you save his life at one point so he tell Rupert "No, see, you were useful all along. I guess we both have our strengths and weaknesses. Ha ha ha!". This is the most "derivative filler" campaign out of all of them and one of the worst pieces of content I have ever had to endure. _childDocuments_.review: Played these as a kid on xbox and beat them..Start with female knight campaign. It teaches you the game and has super fun levels early on and is the most forgiving. The game has a few bugs that may discourage people from really giving it a shot, but if you work through them, the game is such an amazing experience. Controller is probably the best way to play it, but I am using mouse and keyboard now since im not on xbox anymore. It works fine. Game really takes some patience. You cant just hop in and start slaying, you need to take a good 10mins and learn all the controls. Im only 4hrs in, and it all feels natural at this point. So you can and will adapt to mouse and keyboard. Learning and adapting to the controls is the hardest part, but takes the least amount of time.The game allows you to customize your soldiers, characters, officers and more with different stats abilities, roles, skill trees etc. It has a medium difficulty that eventually ramps up to quite a hard game..and I love that...Call it the dark souls of large scale hack and slash/rts combat. This is a Niche game, but for those that enjoy this stuff, i cant believe how well its held up from 2005. The scale is still very large, the game play still very fun. You wont steam roll this game in a few hours like a call of duty campaign, expect it to be long, trial and error combat on missions and clock in at over 100hrs before you see it all. The hack and slash part is basic like dynasty warriors, except all the AI are actually moving around and fighting each other at a quick pace so it feels more dynamic. The Rts part isnt anything overwhelming either, yet some how it remains challenging and in depth enough to be very entertaining. Each campaign has an actual story with voice acting, and theres a lot of it. Bugs...this thing was not remastered very well aside from the graphics. It has small annoyances for instance, when you go to save your game, you have the game tell you all 50 save slots are corrupted and have to delete one and then save your game. F10 is the start button and menu button yet on most PCs f10 does something else so you have to juggle it some. You use alt to look around but it also freezes/pauses the game when you let go of it after looking around, and a few other things that can be annoying. Youll have to keybind some stuff to your mouse to work around some kinks. If the game wasnt so long and so good, I would tell ya not to bother with it, but it really is worth putting in the time to get it smoothed out and then play.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with an interesting world. The interaction between a real-time strategy and Dynasty Warriors-esque combat was an cool idea for the time although the more you play of this game, the more you'll realise how much better it could've, and should've been done.The game will take it relatively easy on you up until you get halfway through Ellen's storyline (who's storyline basically acts as the tutorial and warm-up to the mechanics of the game.) After that though, you BETTER know the in's-and-out's for optimising your troops and your characters or you'll quickly find this game to be a nightmare to trudge through. There's no New Game+ either so unfortunately if you intend to try and explore the game after finishing the story, ya gotta do it from square one again.The soundtrack is absolutely awesome. It's metal and chaotic and it complements the craziness of the large-scale warfare of this game perfectly.The voice-acting is kind of a mixed bag. There are a lot of big names like Robin Atkin Downes in there and there's also a lot of unheard-of voice-actors who are giving it their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ A-game on some of the minor characters and if that ain't admirable work, I dunno what is.It's worth mentioning, this game originally came out for Xbox Original and PS2 and was only just recently ported to PC this year so as you can imagine, it's kinda buggy. A.I. is often dumb as bricks, sometimes your character will dance around doing what you want, etc. Thankfully the devs are actively patching this game the best they can, which is honestly more support than I was expecting. Any other dev team contracted with porting this game might've just shoved it out the door and forgot about it, just focusing on their payday. I mean, it's an old game from a bygone era that even back then not a lot of people likely heard of, who's gonna care if it's buggy, right? Well thankfully that isn't the case, the devs seem to actually care about this game and it certainly shows.

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning of the end for the KuF series.Many people are claiming that Heroes and The Crusaders have survived the test of time and look beautiful in 2020. I can tell you that if you try to determine what's going on in the battlefield without using your mini-map 80% of your strategic gameplay time, you won't be able to even tell what is going on 30 meters past you because of the dumb vision fog that's intended to have the original Xbox have the game run on at least 30 fps. You must squint real hard to try and see the outline of a swamp mammoth on the middle of the map.  You literally can't see anything but shadows. They supposedly remastered and improved the graphics, but I've yet to see any difference between the original and this port.Also, this port is one of the worst you will ever have the disgrace of touching, this being the main reason why I make this review. This should be enough info to steer you away, however if you'd like to hear why I hate this game so much, then read on.I do not trust myself to give you an unbiased opinion on TC, but I can for Heroes. Here's my quick story explaining why:I never touched Heroes back when it was on Xbox. I only ever knew The Crusaders existed, and for my 10 y/o self, that game was more than enough to have hundreds upon hundreds of hours invested into it. When I learned Heroes was a thing was because a friend lent me Circle of Doom which was, in turn, their first game into the KuF series and I decided to Google the series. He didn't like TC, I didn't like CoD, none of us knew Heroes was a thing.Years later, I found a Heroes original copy on a BlockBuster at less than $3 bucks. It was used. I tried to play it on my X360 only to find out The Crusaders was backwards compatible, but Heroes wasn't. I still have it on a shelf, massively disappointed with Bluebox, Microsoft and Phantagram for that fiasco.2 weeks ago, I saw this released on Steam. I was beyond ecstatic, so I bought it on release. After finishing The Crusaders completely, I went immediately to boot this up. From the moment the main menu theme started playing, I knew something was wrong. It wasn't even similar to TC. I brushed it off as nostalgia bias, so I played a custom game. Accidentally chose Morene. She sounds like a teenager now, instead of a cold-hearted vampiress. I ignored it, so I went to boot up my first campaign as Ellen. 5 minutes in, I almost Alt+F4. The voice-acting is terrible and the OST is straight out of place for a game like this. I was amazed at how they went from good-great voice-acting in TC to literal anime English-dub quality in Heroes.I'm 2 missions in on Ellen's campaign now and I can't continue. It's legit torture. I had to watch gameplay videos at this point. Here's a breakdown of all the things that completely ruin this game:- The English voice-acting was done by a band of teenagers who tried really, really hard to sound like grown adults.- The music was composed by a starved high-school band and a rejected composer who were paid with 5 loafs of bread and were ordered to try and do their best. They couldn't decide on whether they wanted to make it orchestral or heavy metal, so they made it both.- Ellen's campaign and Ellen both as a playable Hero and as a character. She might be the weakest, edgiest, most pathetic trash can in this game. She takes years just to kill a single orc that's 2 levels above her troop.- The writing was very likely made by a fan who was tasked with making interesting backstories for the secondary characters in TC and ended up creating a fandom that includes all of their favorite anime clichés and excellent choices in dialogue, like saying "Uh", "Ah", "Agh" and the rest of their favorite interjections ad nauseum. They also changed the personalities of many characters just so they would fit in their fandom.- ^ They were also in charge of the translation for the subtitles for Heroes and The Crusaders. They weren't that great in that regard.- Actually, most of the new heroes suck. They are largely useless on the battlefield and are boring to play.- The camera is awful. If you have it high to see your surroundings, you get a isometric view of your character and can't see what's in front of you nor what you're hitting. If you lower it, your character blocks half your screen and you can only see the current enemies that you're hitting. How they managed to break something that worked in it's predecessor is beyond me.- I wanted to try out multiplayer because it was apparently the best feature in the game. It's been removed. Both from TC and Heroes. No one knows if it's ever going to be implemented.- Game is capped at 30 fps because the engine would otherwise break.- The developer for both ports has stated multiple times on the forums that they were not given enough time to implement many features from the original games. Therefore, they were cut from the PC port entirely. If you see the state of the game, this comes as no surprise. Example: The mini-games that unlocked after you beat Regnier and Kendal campaigns respectively in The Crusaders are gone.10/Rupert's manlet voice in Heroes. I want to cry.

_childDocuments_.review: Update June 27th, 2020I have finished Walters campaign here my thoughts and what I encountered. First off, the game still has issues starting up. While it's gotten better it still takes me 3 to 4 tries to get it to work. This could differently deter people from buying the game. This needs to be fixed asap the only reason I put up with it is I'm a superfan of the series.During Walters's second campaign mission, I really took my time to max my experience using cavalry to get mass SP and using Walter to throw meteorites out left and right. Once I felt that I had gained enough XP, - 7000 is the cap - I escorted the dark elf to the ancient heart only to have the game glitch out and not let me finish the level. The ending since would not trigger and I was left with a very frustrating amount of time wasted. This also needs to be fixed. It worked the second time but I no longer felt like taking my time so I just grabbed the elf and completed the mission gaining almost no XP or gold. Also, the pathfinding on this mission is totally screwed. I've only encountered this issue on this mission so far but I had to really guide Walter because If I issued an order to move more than say a 2/5ths of the map then Walter's troop would freak out and start running backward it was really annoying. I did not encounter the map glitch again where the movement map failed to return to normal which is very nice.All of the other missions for Walter went smoothly I just had one hell of a bad experience with mission two. I can say that I enjoyed the experience and had lots of fun reliving my childhood; however, I do not see this game lasting very long if multiplayer is not somehow added because not very many people are going to even notice this old game during a steam summer sale I don't see today's generation getting the same enjoyment out of this that I do. There needs to be something added to hook them in or to keep it going longer. Once I complete the campaign and there are no achievements or multiplayer I'll shelve this game. I don't really care about modding this game because the player base for it is so small it seems like a waste of time.TLDR:This is an old game from the early 2000's it has some bugs but the story, heroes, and gameplay are extremely good. The game is worth 20$ and then some there is no multiplayer at the time of this review however custom games can be a great way to waste time if you are bored. Just don't be surprised if you have issues getting the game to work the best things take a little effort to enjoy to the fullest. June 24th, 2020I've only played a few minutes and had some difficultly getting the game started; however, I managed to get it up and running and it's everything that I remember from when I was a child. I played Walter first and standing there at the start of his first mission that ominous music playing it took me back to my childhood love it!However, I cannot let that cloud my mind I give it a 10/10 for nostalgia. But, it took me 20 minutes just to get the game to launch and I also experienced a map glitch where the movement map got stuck and wouldn't retract making the mission impossible to complete without a restart.This is my super basic review I'll edit this to be more in-depth within a few days' time.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes is the standalone expansion pack that adds 7 more campaigns to Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders that take place before, during and after the base game filling in the plot holes with even more heavy metal Medieval High Fantasy violence that we know and love. Ellen of Ecclesia's story explains how she joined Hironeiden and Gerald's unit, Rupert of Hironeiden's story explains how he formed an alliance with the Dwarves & Elves for the much needed reinforcements, Walter of Ecclesia's story talks about his visions leading to the war, how the Ecclesians got into trouble with leadership as well as internal conflict leading to their late assistance of their allies then their eventual end at Nowart starting the Age of Darkness event, Cirith of Vellond's story explains how after Lucretia's campaign she meets her sister to join her unit to retrieve the Ancient Heart from the Patriarch but they end up in life threatening mishaps, Leinhart of Vellond's story talks about how he annexed Hexter but was forced to deal with rebel Kaedes Dark Elves with his newfound allies before joining Regnir's unit in the end after losing his castle, Morene of Vellond's story talks about how she attempted to retrieve the Ancient Heart but failed leading to King Waldemar's compromise and who is leading Kaedes rebels revealed & Urukubarr of Hexter's story details about how he united the Ork tribes to become the strongest WAAGGHH! We don't just get new campaigns but we also get powerful new Elemental units for each element (Ice Maidens, Fire Wraiths, Earth Golems & Thunder Rhinos) and a reworked XP skill allotment system that you can reset an officer's unit XP to reuse it to switch to another unit path or use that experience on another unit although it also limits how you can skill up due to having a flat upgrade price rather then a per level basis at least you can respec whenever you want. We also get custom game mode with a great degree of customization to make fights the way you want with a good amount of maps to combat at like Total War except with Kingdom Under Fire RPG-RTS-Musou system to make fights as varied as possible from what skills to what unit type paths to what hero leads them in greater numbers. Sadly no multiplayer yet like the original Xbox version and ideally you still use an Xbox controller cause if you want challenge wait till you reach Urukubarr's campaign cause you'll need those quick reflexes there as the stories get progressively harder to test your strategic & tactical limits. A worthy expansion pack that's more of the same which is fine cause its a ton of brutal bloody fun with some new units and some changes here and there. If you love the base game like me and want more simply get this expansion pack you wont be disappointed! Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on the original Xbox. Along with the first one. It's not exactly a LONG game. But It most definitely will take time to complete. The mechanics aren't very deep admittedly. But what IS there is very fun to tinker with. The combat has a lot to offer. It's an RTS light/hack and slash. I fell in love with the story and it's characters. They all feel very unique and fairly fleshed out. _childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend playing this after you've played KUF Crusaders. If you like that game, you'll find lots more to like in this classic Xbox gem as well. One warning to those who haven't played this game before: In the two starter campaigns (Ellen is the obvious first one, Walter is also considered "easy"), there are missions that are MAJOR difficulty spikes. You'll probably know when you find them, Walter's comes very early in his campaign, Ellen's later, but they can be extremely frustrating. I'd recommend looking up strats online, because you don't want those 2 bad missions to put a halt on the otherwise excellent experience of this game. It's challenging, unique (both this and KUF Crusaders have a formula I've never seen replicated), and fun, and has excellent cult appeal with it's iffy voice acting and heavy-metal fantasy vibes. I'd even suggest skipping Walter (once you've played Ellen you can jump to a few others) so you don't get bogged down and miss out on the otherwise terrific experience of this game. One problem with the port though: pathing can get seriously fudged up. If you notice you unit struggling, give them short direct move commands rather than long and queued ones. Hasn't been game breaking in any instances, and honestly helped me cheese the gonzo hard Walter mission when the AI unit you have to protect got stuck running in circles for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED REVIEW: This is one of my childhood favourites and I couldn't wait to play it. I initially gave the game a thumbs down because the developers basically used players as their QA team. There were many errors at the launch of the port from not being able to actually get to the title screen to some pretty bad pathfinding issues. I said I'd change my review if they fixed them and they have - in quite a timely manner too.Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes is a good game, it's fun to play and mixes it up with lots of playable characters. I think the script was originally translated from Korean so it can be a bit janky in the English translation but the dialogue isn't the worst.The gameplay is where its at. You command your own group of troops as well as plan the strategy for all your units. It's great tactical gameplay that allows you to get involved with the action rather than just viewing it from a top-down perspective. It's a shame there aren't more games like this. It's a shame the developers took the franchise elsewhere with Circle of Doom (A hack and slash with no strategy) and Kingdom Under Fire 2 (An MMO with some limited strategy elements).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game in desperate need of patching, stat. Some allied units won't move and thus missions cannot advance. Some mission objectives fail to register as completed, meaning missions cannot advance. Also, and I'm not sure if it's just me, even the easiest heroes have missions way more difficult than I remember (and I just replayed and beat most of the Crusaders earlier, so I know I haven't forgotten how to play this game) to the point where some of these missions feel impossible. I will thumbs it up under the condition that I assume patches will be pushed because they were pushed for Crusaders. If you like strategy games (and especially Dynasty Warriors) this is a unique little gem of a game that nobody's ever replicated. Including its sequels, for reasons I don't quite understand.

name: Source of Madness
detailed_description: Source of Madness is a side-scrolling dark action roguelite set in the Loam Lands, a twisted Lovecraftian inspired world powered by procedural generation and AI machine learning. Take on the role of a new Acolyte as they embark on a nightmarish odyssey. Uncover the cosmic secrets of the Loam Lands and The Tower of Madness, the moon’s mysterious Citadel. The horrific monsters you face are never the same, concocted with procedural generation and animated using a neural network AI Explosive close-combat magic, labyrinthine environmental exploration, powerful loot management and a skill tree filled with abilities, classes, and spells Rendered in a beautiful AI assisted art style, the fascinating world of the Loam Lands reveals a deep arcane lore as players uncover its many secrets

_childDocuments_.review: Has art style and physics are very reminiscent of games like Hammerfight or Swapper. Definitely has that indie "jank" feel, many would consider charming. Just about everything is physics based, so cloaks are flowing all over the place, and it almost seems as if your torso is getting led by your lower body. Not necessarily a bad thing, but it might be for some people. Environments look nice, if a little bit too dark, and the monster design is more creative than the usual for Lovecraftian games. The 2d overlay onto a background does create some muddling issues however, as it can be challenging to understand exactly what you're looking at. That may be intentional, since it certainly would make sense when dealing with eldritch abominations, but often I just found myself unsure if I was looking at a corpse, an enemy, or part of the background. A slight outline to separate foreground from background, and maybe a bit of cleanup on the actual units themselves (to see appendages vs the core vs whatever, just see what's connected where) would go a long way toward improving the clarity of the game.I have noticed a few graphics bugs here and there. After resizing from 1440 fullscreen to 1080 windowed, text in the controls menu is cropped on either side. Going to the graphics menu again shows the full screen resolution, despite that clearly not being the case. Minor bugs that will likely be fixed early in the EA, but I would rather provide a thorough review I'm only a little bit into the game, but the story is fine. Nothing amazing, but not really problematic. Nice to deal with Yog-Sothoth, since he doesn't come into play too often, and the narration is well done. I was a little put off in the very beginning however, when you're first walking past a handful of survivors. All of them comment on how they are insane, and how it must suck to not be insane, but this just feels lazy to me. These cosmic horrors break minds, show them what they cannot comprehend. Having someone who's very psyche has been shattered walk over and say "boy golly I sure am insane" rubs me the wrong way. As overdone as it is, I'd much prefer to see some becoming cultists/prophets, rambling about what turns out to be a future miniboss, or crying absolute incoherencies, begging for salvation that they know cannot come.I brought up above that the physics had that jank indie feel to them, and that it was a matter of taste. The controls have that similar style, but there are a few points that are much more black and white.  You aim with your mouse, and can cast spells with left and right click. Despite aiming with the mouse, however, you cannot normally cast behind you. While sometimes I have been able to hold right and shoot to the left, propelling myself forward a little quicker (spells have knockback on you), I'll also be fighting an enemy, back up, and suddenly be shooting in the direction I'm moving instead of where my cursor is. UPDATE: I have learned that this is the result of releasing your spell button before the spell actually casts. The spell only targets the cursor when the button is being pressed. Otherwise, it just faces directly forward. I still haven't figured out how to control the item direction though.Holding a cast will use an "Ultimate", with a cost associated with it. This is fine, but I can't really tell what that cost means. In fact, using the ultimate will often require you to just be spam casting the primary ability for a while first, then suddenly it will charge and come out with the big hit, as if it were the final part of a combo. This is likely a result of my misunderstanding the spells, but the complete lack of any real tutorial beyond "hit left click to cast" indicates that this may be a recurring issue.As of writing this, I have just finished the first actual boss, . The big stand out problem is that this is another roguelike that has plenty of stats to juggle, but doesn't bother explaining any of them. Clarity is a MAJOR issue. I might pick up a ring that applies Chill to targets on crit. What does Chill do? No idea. I would find a helmet that gives "Affinity to Nature". I have no idea what that means. There is a poison debuff in the game, but outside of the green pools, good luck finding out what applied it. You have a tiny debuff icon on the bottom of your screen, but it seems to cycle through 6-7 times before it goes away, and mousing over it shows nothing. As stated above, I still have no idea how to determine when an ultimate will cast, or what those little pips mean. As far as I can tell, there's no real way to find out what something will do without buying it, and even then you're often left in the dark.Hopefully, this will all be fixed early on. It's pretty easy to do, just involving updating tooltips. A bit more concerning is the actual combat. Mostly, it involves finding the rings you want to use and holding both mouse buttons while pointing at the opponent while kiting away. At first, I thought that melee might be broken. Enemies don't do damage on collision, but instead projectiles and periodic "swipes" with a glowing appendage. Knowing this, it should be easy to just dodge when you see the swipe, right? Unfortunately, the vast majority of my damage taken is the result of the crazy physics catapulting an enemy onto me, and just getting stuck. The blink/dodge won't get you out of the mess, often doing nothing at all, and moving is futile. Unless something is done about this, I think most sessions are going to end in frustration.In addition to the bug fixes and clarity overhaul brought up above, improving enemy confrontations would be great. Enemies seem to be procedurally generated, but at the moment that just results in incoherent blobs rolling over to you. Sometimes they have "phases" that occur when their health drops to a certain point, losing a number of appendages before continuing their chase. Instead, encourage the player to slice through these tendrils and arms. As far as I can tell, this functionality currently isn't in game (although it's nearly impossible to actually target a body part given how floppy and erratic enemy movements are), but even if it is, it certainly isn't clear to the player. Double down on the "shambling horror" aesthetic A foreground character was a coffin with long spindly legs. I was actually pleasantly surprised seeing it slowly patrol the area, only to realize it wasn't anything I could interact with, and I haven't seen anything of the sort since. Throw giant spidery monsters at me with 7 joints per leg, jerkily approaching at quick speeds. Let the player slice through their legs, causing them to tumble down as they continue their approach. If the creatures are procedurally created as I believe, the devs clearly have a method of locomotion that is indeterminate of the creature's shapes. Hopefully this isn't just "apply a force vector in the direction of the player", because that would allow you to transition from "walking" to "crawling" or "rolling".  This game is absolutely rough around the edges, but it's also an enjoyable experience under that. I'll tentatively recommend it to anyone who's really into roguelikes, while the rest should probably wait until a polish pass goes through.: I just finished what's currently in the game, and balance needs a bit of work. The ACT 1 boss was absolutely 0 threat, but took 5-10 minutes to kill. If you're having any trouble, just run double blood rings and heal your way through the entire game. At the moment, I have no desire to go back and play some more, since there's not really too much to experiment with. Very few effects interact with one another, just boiling down to "do X% more damage on Y spells". Will see later.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovecraftian rogue like game where you play as a cultist fighting against the monsters of other old gods.Pros-* You can unlock a variety of mage classes, the first one very quickly.* The art in the game is really well done and unsettling. * The real star of the game is the physics. The randomly generated monsters, with ragdoll physics can be a lot of fun and hilarious. I've had mini-bosses fling themselves into the air with such force that they just never come back down. It's also a lot of fun to bounce across the screen, using the pushback from explosives and shotgun blasts for additional jumps, keeping out of reach as some poor abomination flails impotently in your general direction.* The variety of weapons and equipment seems pretty good. I wish I had more control of what I get. You don't really do "builds" thus far, you mostly just hope you can find a couple of good weapons. The monsters get higher level with each new zone, so you'll need to replace each weapon every few zones, and you really hope they you don't get stuck having the replace two good weapons with two less desirable ones, with better levels. But two weapons that you actually want is a lot of fun.Cons* The levels are procedurally generated, so you quickly just start seeing random clumps of level tossed together to be jumped past. Apart from looking for hidden doorways, you quickly give very little regard to the world itself, since you already know there is no deeper meaning, besides random geometry.* The monsters are procedurally generated, usually ending as some kind of tentacle monster with any number of random abilities and traits. Since healing is very limited, you generally stay far away from each one, since you don't know if it'll suddenly blast you with poison, or explode on death, or deal contact damage, or who knows what else. So you just see them as random lumps to be blasted apart and avoided. They typically arent that hard and most of the time I get hit is when they do something unpredictable, like fling themselves at you from off screen at 95 miles an hour. Again, since you know that are randomly generated, you don't see any meaning or artistic value in them.* Small community. It just isn't that big of game, fanbase wise, so there isn't a lot of information out there. No real tutorials, faqs, guides, or explanations of game mechanics.* The physics get wonky. You get a teleport/dash to help move and avoid enemies, except sometimes you'll get snagged on the enemy and get hit instead. So even rolling past enemies with well times dodges doesn't reliably work. If your going to get hit, you might as well as mash that blink ability, but it certainly isn't reliable like in other souls-like games.
