_childDocuments_.review: Another very solid piece of work from Zeboyd, if you liked their previous post-Xbox arcade games, you'll likely enjoy this one as well.  This is a shorter game than Cthulhu Saves the World or Cosmic Star Heroine; clocking in an 6-8 hours for a first playthrough.Zeboyd games have always had a flimsy 4th wall, but this one goes far beyond any of their previous offerings.  You the player are an active participant in the story, which makes things quite fun.  The story blends Shakespeare, magical girl anime, and high school relationship building together with a large dose of humor.The map graphics are a bit plain, but still very servicable and very varied between the different dungeons.  The menu, character art, and battle sprites are extremely well done.  The battle sprites and character art in particular show a lot of character.  Sound and music are top notch, sound has always been good for Zeboyd games, but this title really shows a huge improvement.  The soundtrack is wonderful and I strongly recommend it when/if it becomes available for purchase.Combat wise, it's fairly similar in design to how Cosmic Star Heroine and Cthulhu Saves Christmas operates.  Each character can equip up to 7 skills, most of these exhaust after one use; then there is one defend which reduces damage for a turn and recharges your exhausted skills.  There are no chaos skills like in CSC, so you have full party build control.  Imogen is forced in your party at all times.  In most of the game, you'll have a forced party, which will be different between dungeons.  This makes you alter your strategies for each dungeon, but it can make some dungeons rough when you have little to no AoE damage, especially on higher difficulties.  Late in the game, you will get the ability to select which three party members to bring along out of the full compliment of characters; so you can create a specific party build with complementary skills.Like with previous CSH/CSC titles, there are also items, which are 1/combat skills any character can use; unite skills that get stronger as the battle goes on; and the Hype (Hyper in previous games) system where every few turns a character's skills get stronger.  Different in this game is that equipment is gone.  Here, you get traits which unlock as you gain levels.  These traits (aside from the first one Magical) give you passive bonuses or modifications to skills and a set of stat boosts.  Each character can equip 3 traits which helps customize that character's role in the party.  This feels a lot like a collectible card game, and reminds me a bit of creating hero builds in the original Guild Wars.  Synergy between skills on a single character and synergy with other party members is quite important to making combat easier.I ran the game on the "normal" difficulty (second choice), and it was pretty solid.  I could easily die if I didn't pay attention or used my party synergies and skills inappropriately.  The last boss got a bit tricky as well.  Like with all of Zeboyd's other games, foes get stronger as the fight goes on to discourage turtling strats, so you will need to play fairly aggressively.  Luckily like CSH and CSC, you are at full power for each fight so there is no risk in going all out each fight.The final aspect is that between missions, you have interactive scenes with your fellow characters.  There are only a few places during these scenes where you have to choose between options on what to do.  This is unlike CSC's wide array of choices.  Note that there is some combat that can happen during these scenes, you'll have a fixed party for these for the most part.Criticisms are fairly minor overall.  I feel that full party customization is unlocked a bit too late.  Loot in this is a bit more boring than in previous games, it's mostly similar items (which are still good as they can fill in gaps in your party's skill set) and backpacks that allow you to carry  more items.  Leveling is more important, as the replacement for equipment, your traits are almost only unlocked by leveling up.  Map design is good but doesn't feel as creative as some of CSH's dungeons; and the graphics of the maps are a bit more plain when compared to the excellent battle, sprite, scene, and UI art.Overall I feel it's a great game and one of Zeboyd's best entries to date.  Almost anyone who likes 2D turn based jRPG's, especially those with the theatre or magical girl themes, will enjoy this one.  The short nature of it is a nice change of pace from the long epics that many jRPG's are; and the more humorous and whimsical nature of the game is a nice departure from the grim nature of many other jRPG's.  Those with familiarity with Shakespeare's plays will probably get a kick out of the silliness, obvious and less obvious references, and the humorous "translations" that are available whenever any early Modern English is displayed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun RPG that gets straight to the point. _childDocuments_.review: This is everything a short RPG should be. It has a joyfully broad and deep skill system that it throws you right into and constantly adds interesting, meaningful abilities to right up to the end. On Challenging mode (the second-highest difficulty out of four settings, which you can switch between any time), there were virtually no trivial enemy encounters the entire game. Because the system doesn't include stock-able items and refreshes everything after each battle, the game expects you to make full use of your party's plentiful abilities with each encounter. This is a major part of why the regular battles are more fun than many RPGs' boss battles. The combat is exhilerating and immensely satisfying, even by Zeboyd Games's exceptional track record.At first glance, the game appears very trimmed down compared to what's typical in an RPG, but make no mistake: the battle and skill progression systems are as deep, rewarding, and fun as any 50-hour RPG's. The game is short, but there is more fun to be had per minute (and more laughs to be had per minute in the script) than any other RPG I've played. Don't think of it as being trimmed down or shortened: it is in fact highly concentrated. If you're looking for a sprawling, epic, emotional story played out over real-world weeks, this isn't that, but I highly recommend changing your expectations and giving this a shot anyway. If you ARE looking for a deep game that you actually have time to finish and makes you laugh a lot, this is exactly what you want. Although the ending is more abrupt than would be ideal, it will still put a smile on your face.I haven't even touched on the premise yet, which is singular and delightful. If you enjoyed studying Shakespeare in school even a little and have at least heard of Sailor Moon, you will have a blast. And if you love either or both of those, this game was made specifically for you. The "modern translations" of the Shakespeare and Shakespeare-esque dialogue, which you can press right to see on each applicable line, manage to be genuinely semantically helpful, illuminating on the subtext of the plays, and side-splittingly funny all at once.tl;dr: 10-ish hours of tremendous, satisfying, fun JRPG combat and laughs galore. It doesn't have everything you would expect from a JRPG, but what it does have, it has in spades, and this MORE than carries the whole experience. Must-play.EDIT: I had included a bug FYI here, but they just patched it!
_childDocuments_.name: This Way Madness Lies

_childDocuments_.review: I have thoroughly enjoyed every game by this studio, and this is no exception. The combat isn't quite as polished as Cosmic Star Heroine (their previous game), and it's way more linear. The story is a lot more light-hearted though, and it's definitely funnier as a result. The entire premise is just hilarious, and it's an absolute blast to go through the story. The sound track is just one amazing song after another, which definitely helps.Personally I prefer the more serious tone and deep combat system of CSH, but I still had a great time with this. If you've played any of their games before you pretty much know what you're in for. If you haven't, and you have even a passing interest in JRPGs, buy this game, play it, and then buy every other game they've made and play those too! Their games are seriously the best indie JRPGs out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Another wonderful RPG offering from Zeboyd Games!  Shakespeare meets "Sailor Moon" this time around with their great turn based battle system carried over from Cosmic Star Heroine & Cthulhu Saves Christmas.  Very fun all around and worked perfectly on Steam Deck without having to make any adjustments (only to resolution in-game).  Highly recommend like all their games!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun turn based rpg with humorous take on both Shakespearean literature and modern internet culture. Combat is very similar to Cosmic Star Heroine. The story is mostly linear, but there are a few choices that can be made that decide which brief events take place before getting back to the main story. The music is great. Each of the magical girls get their own intro theme.

name: Fashion Police Squad
detailed_description: Calling all officers! I've got a Fashion Crime in Progress and I'm mobilizing all Fashion Police Squad members. Grab your Belt of Justice and your Tailormade Sewing Machine, we've got some Fashion Justice to dispense! Fashion Police Squad is a humorous Retro FPS where you fight against fashion crime using attire enhancing weaponry. Clean the streets of socks in sandals as Sergeant Des, and experience a single-player story full of fabulous characters, dazzling encounters, and fierce runway shows! Pit yourself against all kinds of Fashion Crimes, from saggy pants to neon brights Utilize a specialized weapons arsenal, including weaponized Sock Gnomes Jump, climb and swing your way around Trendopolis to uncover its secrets Fight against the biggest, baddest bosses in the fashion industry Solve the mystery of the resurgence of Fashion Crime and take out the villains at the top Each fashion crime has a fashion solution, and you'll need to choose between your weapons carefully to fix each fashion faux pas! Each enemy needs something, be it a splash of color or all the seams taken in, so you'll need to switch to and use the right weapons for the right situations! Picking the wrong weapon will do nothing to your enemies, so time to choose wisely!

short_description: Even at this moment, our fashionable city is under assault. Baggy pants, dull suits, sightings of socks with sandals. A message needs to be sent, and it needs to be sent in style... Time to serve some good ol' Fashion Justice!

_childDocuments_.review: It's more than a boomer shooter. There's an interesting twist: you need to always use the correct weapon against a given type of enemy, otherwise it doesn't do a thing. You can't fix a bad fitting dress with a paint gun. It ups the difficulty quite a bit, but trust me - they made it work.Obviously the concept is ridiculous, and the game embraces that fact. When "fixing" an enemy instead of hearing a death scream, you hear the announcer say how amazing the refashioned person looks: SEXY! DEBONAIR! DAYUM! FIERCE! And of course you get to see their new self standing there, thankful and much happier. It doesn't get in the way of fighting, as the "reformed" criminals are almost invisible when there's still danger around.This light tone lends itself well to humour and classic memes. And by classic, I do mean classic. Since it's a boomer shooter, it contains some "boomer memes" (this is a misnomer, but let's just roll with it). Make no mistake: whoever made this is well-versed in the language of the early internet and uses that knowledge to make ridiculous mishmashes which, when combined with creative and fun game design, create some incredibly memorable and fun moments.I need to stress this here: normally I  memes and pop culture references in games, they just yank me out of whatever immersion I had. But here they not only work, they get away with insane levels of meme saturation. It's just that kind of a game.It also breaks some conventions of the shooter genre, but it does it with gusto. Your weapons (except the ultimate one) have unlimited ammo, and only one of them requires reloading. Your melee attack isn't so melee, it actually has quite a bit of range, and it's main utility is stunning. Exploding barrels contain glitter, so they hurt your enemies, but heal you. And there is no sprinting, instead there's... making the floor slippery.Okay, this part actually sucks. In order to move fast, you must use a specific weapon to spray water on the floor, and then "slide" on it. It doesn't really work so well; what makes things worse is that there are some platforming/parkour sections which require you to use this. I fell so many times because I just couldn't get the feel for it. Luckily, the most annoying of those sections is an optional challenge, so at least there's that.Oh, and some people are complaining about the belt swinging. I don't know, I found it cool. Maybe they made it easier? I think it works just fine. You don't have to use it all that much, anyway.Finally, something that I really liked is that even though the game's protagonist is a male fashionista, it doesn't contain  direct LGBT references. I don't mean it in a homophobic way, though - quite the opposite. I think it's ridiculous that we associate good fashion sense in men with being gay. This kind of mindset hurts all men - straight and otherwise. If I want to slay some puss while wearing high heels and a red overcoat, let me. Okay?I think the game's great. It's pretty, it's fun, it's got good humour, and there's some really good music, too. I've played most of the game on Hard difficulty ("You reap what you sew") and I had to lower it towards the end because the fights got a little too tough. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this one was surely a breath of fresh air in this stream of "boomer shooters"! No blood, gore and guts here, it's all glam, fashion, style and silly light hearted references packed in a neat set of varied missions and accompanied by an amazing OST worth the price on its own if you are a fan of SEGA-style music with a funky approach, in fact, if you like that sort of piano/grand jazz/keyboard synth ultra melodic songs that glue to your mind, this is for you. Indeed, sound design is just as prominent as the visuals here.Anyway, quick mechanics rundown: your character is extremely agile and fast, there is no dash but there is a melee weapon used to hop and climb to greater distances. You get a small set of weapons (including one that let's you jump further ahead and move even faster) and they are arranged in a system where each one needs to be used on different enemy types to stunlock them or deal damage, that is until you get the equivalent of the BFG (which the devs kindly provide infinite ammo for if you clear the game). Each weapon fits a certain purpose and they will not be effective against certain enemy types. This is telegraphed both via audio and visual cues so you are quickly told you need to switch weapons.Now, things get extremely chaotic and challenging once you face enemy waves with enemy combinations that require you to move around and switch like a madman until you fashionize all those terrible criminals. Each time you eliminate a target an Unreal Tournament/Devil May Cry 5 style loud voice will scream phrases and that already elevates the game above others. It just oozing style and I loved it so much more for it. It's a good way to accompany the combat! Again, it may not be the wailing of demons and electric guitars and an angry armored dude but it sure is a learning experience on fashion words in English, heh. At the end of each mission you are evaluated by the amount of secrets, swag (basically, armor items) and enemies arrested for that sweet-yet-OCD 100% completion goal. These tallies are done incredibly well in a silly fashion parade style, with bosses getting their own special screens.The story is kind of a spoof full of references (not gonna spoil) and certainly not quintessential to the experience although I would certainly love if the next game contains even more voiced dialogue (only the intro is voiced, the rest is what I can only describe as Banjo Kazooie noises), although the delivery and writing could make or break it. Having all enemies voiced is also great as the quotes they spew are just as ridiculous as expected, chockfull of memes that keep the arenas engaging.While for many it may not reach the heights of some of the new torch bearers of this new old school era like DUSK or Ultrakill, the style is extremely well done, entertaining and packed with enough humor to get a special highlight. My only gripe was that a few of the encounters are confined into extremely small arenas for the amount of enemies you face and that gives you little room for maneuvers and there were a few performance hiccups using the melee belt, other than that the game ran smoothly on my PC.I really hope the devs are working on a sequel that refines elements and ups the ante or just brings us more joy and fun to cut it up a bit with all the disembowelments and violence. Sometimes we just need a break from that with some colours and laughter. Props to the devs, hats off and suit up!It's not a terribly long game so even aiming for the 100% should be doable. Very recommended and if on sale, even more recommended but also get it with the OST! It comes with FLACs which is always a huge plus!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what it appears to be - a catwalk of stylish ideas rekindling an old flame with a plethora of fresh twists. It's almost unbecoming how long it took me to connect. I wasn't feeling it until a multitude of mechanics finally clicked together. It's a slow starter, but I think the devs acted wisely by introducing them gradually instead of making a mess. After a couple of hours, I could see the full picture and caught myself deeply engaged with the systems in place. Now, let's dispense some judgement on this proudly judgemental game.The story takes place in Trendopolis, a leading city in fashion, dizzying heights, and breakneck chases. Gazing at the vibrant vistas from the rooftops, I felt like I was visiting a town from Transport Tycoon. The striking colour palette is seeping juice and the pixel art is meticulous, emanating craftsmanship. On top of that, the game periodically delivers cool gags, brilliantly spoofing bigwigs like MGS, Wolfenstein, CoD, even old-fashioned racing games. And not by making some feeble references but through well-made playable sketches that fit into the world aesthetically and don't overstay their welcome.Aside from aesthetics, FPS emphasizes its story and characters. The protagonist, Sergeant Des, is trusting and confident, he even gets a clever little character arc at the end. His fashion sense resembles that of M. Bison. Cosplay is all the rage, I suppose. His partner officer Haley is featured prominently by partaking in most conversations. She plays a role of a level-headed and strict archetype, talking sense into Des, yet she doesn't come off as condescending when doing so, being a loyal and respectful companion. Soon, Deep Coat enters the picture, bringing with him a voguish mystery that unfolds throughout the playthrough, culminating in many hilarious payoffs.Looking holistically, the story is gratuitous nonsense played for a joke. The game is aware of the fact, treating its characters and twists with sass, paying more attention to its clothing puns all three-and-a-half fashionistas may fully appreciate. I can't help but respect this tailored approach! If anything, this commitment to the thematic throughline is impressive. Only a niche audience could make the most of it by recognising all the nuances, yet the game was made to be enjoyed by everyone. I did, and I'm a notorious fashion criminal. Despite the inherently divisive subject matter, FPS never gives off any elitist vibes. It's too nonchalant and cheerful for such antiquated notions.The beginning levels are flat, lacking in branching or environmental interactivity. I also wasn't happy with unlimited ammo, because it made me almost indifferent to secrets, which, despite being inventively tucked away, don't contain interesting items to find, only your old health and swag (armour)! Vital stuff, just unexciting. But I forgot all about it when the game began to open up. Its map design always stays straightforward, however, soon I gave in to the sheer charm of its crazy ride through the beauty of surreal absurdity. I adore the abstract set pieces like that Transport Tycoon city, a subway with inventive platforming fights, bathhouses with labyrinthian wardrobe hells, and a colossal cruise boat boasting vent tunnels coated in gold.Every environment is thought-out, full of imaginative challenges that wouldn't fit anywhere else. Fun acrobatic elements with good air control as well as many hazards get introduced later in the game. They range from traditional explosive barrels to trampolines and poles to swing from by using the Belt of Justice as a grappling hook. Thus, platforming in search for scissors to cut ribbons Des "can't possibly get past", your analogue of cards and keys, never feels like a chore. Finally, someone tackled that ancient trope in a manner most fabulous! In the same manner, the game makes sure to entertain you between battles while doing its best to diversify gameplay scenarios.With those getting more exciting the more stunts like jumping from one side of the metro station to the other over electrified rails you get to perform. Not to mention several intense challenge missions and these wonderful spoofs of classic franchises presented in hands-on, interactive ways. Take the gnome-shooting sniper segments with "unfit" and "hair" bullet types. Although I sucked so hard I kinda hated those, I must admit they're solid. But I loved the other ones a lot, be that a lightning-fast vehicle turret segment or VR speedrunning parkour levels. None of them felt superfluous, enriching an already saturated game even further.It's a non-violent game, by the way. Des doesn't kill, he fashionizes his grateful victims. You still shoot people though! Spilling no blood or gore, but the paint clouds, resounding thuds, and impactful feedback compensate for it. Refashioned enemies keep standing and it would've been a problem if they didn't become elegantly transparent during fights. And some fights they are! Local boss battles, for one, are some of the most complex engagements I've ever seen in a shooter! This is where the game's playful nature goes truly wild, letting its mechanics shine, and the best gags get introduced. Normal brawls don't lag far behind. FPS is one of these classic Doom-like shooters that, while having dedicated arenas that lock you in, constantly drips intermediary side gigs that can be just as layered as the main attractions.Each encounter forces you to correctly assess your ever-changing predicaments and rapidly swap guns according to your targets' overlapping weaknesses. It's a quaint take on rock, paper, scissors. But these tools aren't glamorous enough. Instead, get your hands on an assortment of thematically coherent guns that put commitment to the themes on display. Use the Belt of Justice as a stunning melee option, a paint shotgun to brighten up the day, a sewing machine gun shooting buttons and grenades, and sock gnomes for special occasions. A water cannon deals with loud and oversized garments and can be also used to spray soapy water on the floor in front of you to run faster and jump further. Finally, the Ultimate Fashionizer shooting vacuum-packed wardrobe rockets crowns this humble but effective collection. To boot, every weapon gets a cool secondary fire.By refashioning people, you fill the Fab Meter to slap some fashion sense into them with your Fab Slap Glove. Basically, it allows you to skip an odd fight in style. But it won't always be that easy, you'll have to learn your enemy. The criminals represent a range of tacky stereotypes, possessing unmistakable shapes and easily distinguishable sound cues. From suitcase-tossing office drones and jumping Karens with pepper sprays to nefarious scooter bastards or beach dads in speedos, and every one of them demands special treatment. To underline how complex it gets, the beach dad first demands the use of sock gnomes to get rid of the armour, then a grenade to blast off the speedos, and a quick button-up to finish him off, all in this exact order. Here's how a myriad of little quirks come together to form a hardcore and highly entertaining combat system. Des is quick on his feet and slick, being able to lash his way out of trouble in most circumstances. I had to use everything in my arsenal, jump, swing around to survive, and did it make me feel good! This game carries a bright spark inside, giving it a special kind of cheerful energy strong enough to light up your mood and make your worst day a little bit better. Mopeful Games, thank you sweethearts for being as you are! Be that your first and last creation or one of many, know that you did a swell job, you magnificent hype beasts. Your game slapped my frumpy cheeks happy.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I have to make this review just for people who might have similar expectations to me. This is definitely not a bad game, but I feel in various ways it's a letdown for me. I don't do reviews too often overall but these problems definitely added up in the later levels of the game. I'll just do a pro and con list because it's pretty simple. Pros:Great visuals and localesFun humourA set of mechanics that initially work wellSecond boss has a lot of cool segments if a bit tediously longCons:Mechanics become overwrought and tediousVisibility on screen of enemies is a genuine problem when too much is going onA later enemy absolutely tanked performanceVarious minor bugsPlatforming segments become jank and unpredictableSniper sections, which I feel are rarely enjoyable but are certainly out of place hereI wish the devs well, I think this is a creative game. But to anyone buying this expecting a more typical retro shooter experience, this is really not that game.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't recall how I blundered upon Fashion Police Squad (its title a clever backronym for the game's own genre), but I was so baffled and intrigued by the concept that I felt compelled to pick it up.This was the correct decision.FPS is a zany (and very much tongue-in-cheek) homage to the camp world of haute couture and the unique feel of retro FPS games (which seem to be having something of a renaissance of late, for some reason?). It was a blast to play, even if some areas were very challenging (and not always for good reasons)--but that, too, falls squarely within the purview of retro FPS games, does it not?If you are expecting a finely-polished game with dazzlingly precise play and mechanics (such as, say, Ultrakill perhaps?), this game is not that--but fortunately for you, those games do exist. If you're willing to have a hilarious time catwalking through an FPS with quirk pouring out of its gills, however, FPS is probably an excellent option to play.As a final note on value (as that seems to be a key consideration on Steam), FPS's main campaign is fairly short, and would be shorter still if some of the areas hadn't seen me need to retry them more times than I care to admit (again, some for reasons of legitimate difficulty, while others, distinctly less so). There are side challenge one-off missions you can undertake, usually for more drip, but that isn't everyone's cup of tea. I completed the story and a couple of the side missions in under 7 hours, if that helps you calibrate.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who likes a great atmosphere, or a good FPS.   Not only is Fashion Police Squad a great unique entry in the FPS genre, it's one filled with character and heart. It's easy to look at the subject matter and the surface and see only a game that may be a gimmick of some sort, but that would be a big mistake. The action is great, using the gimmick of specific weaknesses to force you to focus on particular enemies, while you're dodging enemies left and right. I played on hard difficulty, and even as a veteran of the genre I got a good challenge here, dying a reasonable amount but not to the point of horrible frustration. This is all in the backdrop of clever jokes and a great atmosphere: the game does a fantastic job in setting the stage and you really appreciate the level of detail put into the parodies and references. It's a colorful game with a fantastic soundtrack and great sound design, and it's definitely a game that you'll want to put your full attention into.Really, a lot of my complaints are small: dealing with specific rooms with enemy design that feels a little too cramp, or needing a tweak or two here with the movement on the belt swinging. A bug or two that would cause me to reset a level's progress, but in the big picture, they don't add up to overshadow the game's great pace, design, and overall fun factor. Great for new or veterans players, it's definitely worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Duke Nukem style boomer shooter.  Rather than having ammo pickups, the enemies can only be defeated with certain guns, more of which unlock as you progress.  This keeps levels cleaner, allowing you to focus on the pixel artwork and play style rather than hoarding ammo for the super powerful weapons vs. using it.  The sprite work and pixel art are top notch, with a great nostalgic soundtrack.  The writing is funny, coupled with the many video game references and pop-culture spoofs make this a game worth playing.  The game is rather easy, even on the hardest difficulty, but that doesn't make it not-worth-playing.  People have definitely been sleeping on this game.  I am excited for FPS2.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I've played long enough to defeat two bosses and I can comfortably say that Fashion Police Squad (FPS, haha) is a magnificent game reminiscent of the shooters of the 90s. Where Quake and Doom gave us blood and violence, the Fashion Police Squad gives us comedy and the freshest fashions.The game sports a small but diverse group of enemies, each one sporting a different weakness for you to exploit with your arsenal (and subsequent alt fire modes). Movement is quick and responsive (Especially when swinging with the belt, maybe even a little too fast). Characters are fun and quirky with a silly story line to follow that's littered with Easter eggs. The game even sports side missions as challenges, although it should be noted the only challenge is to really just get to the end. (I haven't found a mission that challenges me to beat a time or something).The game also sports secrets hidden away in little nooks and crannies on the map. Looking through the collectibles in the menu, I can see several things grayed out. I imagine that there might be incentive to keep replaying after my first completion of the game but I'm gonna take my time getting there.Overall, I'd say if you're a fan of the 90s shooters and you like to laugh easy then Fashion Police Squad will be just the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll be the first to admit that I have an awful fashion sense. I can’t properly match colours and my style is basically using the same set of shirts over and over. But you know, I’ve never actually been able to CONFIRM that my fashion sense is awful… until I played Fashion Police Squad. Now, I can safely say I have evidence! Jokes aside, the concept of a shooter that has you helping people become more fashionable (according to societal standards anyway) fascinated me to the point I knew I had to give it a shot - and I’m really glad I did!—--Despite the joke in the first paragraph being sub-par at best, it is based on . Fashion Police Squad is an  that doesn’t take itself seriously (and is all the better for it). Words are replaced by their more fashionable counterparts (“Get your sass over here right away!”, S.W.A.G team outfit instead of S.W.A.T, etc), a gun called “2DYE-4 Elite”, a title card introducing new enemies and what fashion crime they’re committing (you can see the one for the Tourist in the steam store page pics - I can also safely say I unfortunately have committed some of those crimes myself and am currently deeply ashamed), and enemies even explode in a dance when beaten, forever thankful to you for saving them from their existence as a fashion criminal!Everything in this game revolves around fashion.  You might notice that so far, I haven’t really mentioned the story, but there’s a reason: for me, the story here serves as mostly a platform for this thematic and charm to build upon. While it’s serviceable, and , the themes are what stuck with me. And those manifest everywhere: the story, the writing, the gameplay… The game even has tons of gaming and pop culture references and parodies! This is why I mentioned that  The graphics, UI, everything is carefully crafted to convey the old school feeling, right down to the main character’s face looking left and right on the bottom of the screen, in a direct reference to DOOM. You can clearly see each enemy’s fashion crime reflected in their model, as well as their “fixed and fashionable” versions after you beat them. The soundtrack, while not very varied within each level, makes slapping (literally, thanks to a certain power up) some fashion sense into people an absolute blast.But I think when a lot of people try to get an old school shooter, the main thing they’re looking for is quality gameplay. Is the game just as good in this area? Well… not quite.  As you play through Fashion Police Squad, you unlock several weapons to aid you in your fight against unfashionable beings. As you play through the game, you also unlock several of said unfashionable beings. The thing is,  For example: the aforementioned tourist needs to be attacked with a gnome that removes his socks. Said gnome, however, deals 0 damage to a Dull Suit - the game’s first enemy type that rocks a gray suit and needs to be colorized.Effectively what this means is that, when you reach arenas, you’ll have quite a few different enemy types thrown against you, and most of your weapons (save for an end game exception) will only be effective against one or two and deal no damage to the other enemy types. This results in you having to constantly swap your arsenal around so that you can deal damage to whatever you’re facing - and if the wrong enemy type walks in front of your target, tough luck! Better reposition yourself or change weapons because that enemy will now block all damage from the weapon you were using. While this didn’t bother me much, it did become worse when combined with the level design. The thing is  One, for example, throws gas that lingers around an area. If you find that enemy in a corridor just around a corner, you might just end up having to back away and wait for the gas to clear before you can pop back around the corner and keep shooting. The gas also visually clutters the screen a bit. Now imagine yourself in a small arena full of different enemies, some of which gas part of the arena, set fire to another part, and you have to keep jumping around madly and swapping weapons while trying to avoid AOE zones… It seems fun, and it often is, but it can be very frustrating to deal with as you’re simply not left with much room to dodge or maneuver.Due to that, some rooms may feel harder than intended, but overall, playing on the second hardest difficulty, I didn’t have too much trouble - it was just challenging enough, even if some of the said challenge felt a bit frustrating because of what I mentioned above.  The most common are platforming sections that have you flying around using your belt (yep) from pole to pole and another weapon that allows you to artificially speed your character up temporarily. While I did have some problems jumping while under the effect of said weapon, in general, the platforming is pretty fun. There are also other ways the game shakes up the gameplay, but I’ll leave those as a surprise.In terms of glitches and the more technical side of things,  (or at least ran well at max settings on my system - rtx 2060, i7 8th gen, 16gb ram, nvme ssd), but I did run into a few issues. Most were pretty minor, such as doors being a bit tough to interact with if you’re right in front of them. The only more major issue I ran into was in a late game arena. In an arena, you get locked into a room with a bunch of enemies. However, on this specific occasion, I got locked OUTSIDE of said room. It was an issue because I needed to get through the room to progress, and couldn’t kill the enemies. I ended up using a late game AOE weapon to fashionize my enemies through the door, but I suspect restarting the level would also have worked (I’m lazy though and didn’t want to lose progress). All in all, I had a blast with Fashion Police Squad. I think anyone can agree that, even if the gameplay is not for them, this game is certainly not lacking in style! If what you read here seems interesting, I also have great news:  so there’s really no excuse to not check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: This game... is hard to rateFor starters, i really enjoyed this game in the beginning. _childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like Fashion Police Squad. It's not a bad game by any means, but I don't think its really a game that really grabs you.I played the Demo earlier this year and I really enjoyed it. There weren't many huge changes I noticed, and you get the first 3 missions, which is pretty substantial. If you enjoy the Demo, you'll probably like the full version.I think there's a lot of good stuff in FPS, especially if you like the tongue-in-cheek campiness and sillyness. I wouldn't describe it as 'laugh out loud' funny, but it's a good lighthearted romp, and it's not super difficult either. There's a good weapon variety and they all have two different modes, and you have to use the right weapon on specific enemy types. Unfortunately, none of them feel particularly great to use, and I really don't get much of an emotional response from defeating enemies. It's not the lack of gore, but clearing even through groups of enemies isn't super satisfying. It's kind of hard to articulate unless you've played the game.The first two sets of levels send you through urban environments and they're pretty good. A good mix of long and short range combat, and wide open arenas for you to deal with groups of enemies. Unfortunately, the third chapter sends you into cramped subway tunnels, which is a real bummer unless you really like corner peaking enemies. The enemy variety is quite good, and you have to use the correct weapon to take them out. But, most of them are just medium ranged enemies that throw things at you, making them all blend together, even if you have to use different weapons on them.Fashion Police Squad doesn't exactly ignite much passion for fashion in me, which is a real shame. It's got a lot of style, good music and great tone that doesn't take itself very seriously. Unfortunately, as much as they add to the core combat loop, I think it just doesn't feel as satisfying as it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 7th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Finally, someone arrests people wearing Socks with Sandals. Fashion Police Squad looks like a Boomer Shooter, and it has a taste of that.  Players will end up fighting fashion crimes, whether it’s people who have been turned gray, wearing neon shirts, or ill-fitting suits.  Players will shoot them with a dye shotgun, a sewing machine gun, or sock gnomes.  It sounds insane but it’s actually quite funny with tons of great moments and it’s also well written.  I found myself laughing multiple times.At the same time, this is a humorous take on the shooter genre, but it does have some issues.  So far every enemy is only weak to a single weapon, so if you shoot someone wearing a bad suit with the dye shotgun, it does zero damage.    In addition, the difficulty here more comes from the number of enemies than specific enemies themselves, and I’m sure the absurdity of it will wear off eventually, definitely not yet, and probably will last the full first playthrough, but it feels more like a joke that’s great the first time, but you’ve heard it the second time.  Pick this up if you want a refreshing boomer shooter.  This is unique for what it is, and honestly, I feel compelled to play more of it just to see what else it’s going to do. _childDocuments_.review: A real cute and different FPS game. Before this game I had no Drip, now I'm swimming in it! Love the belt whipping Pootie Tang style! Game play is pretty cool! Its got lots of fashion stuff that you use for weapons and it only works on enemies that require that particular weapon and gets pretty crazy, so its kind of like a memory game being you need to remember what weapons do DMG on said enemies. This game might not be for everyone but its a cute game if you are looking for something different to play that doesn't take itself seriously and like FPS games. So, Throw this one in your cart if you want to feel FABULOUS!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best drunken purchases Ive ever made! This game really had me in giggles when I realised I was the fashion police with a paintball gun! whats not to love... completed the game in record time then had to play a re-run to see if I could beat my score (because reasons) I do recommend this game, its like the old skool Doom, there will be times the game sticks and you fall off platforms but pretty sure you have like unlimited lives so it doesnt really matter haha (plays well on the 521gb steam deck)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game stylish and unique? Yeah. It's pretty cool that way and I can tell that it's made as a labor of love. I like all the references being thrown around and the inventiveness to the the world and writing. The pixel art is also rather inspired with all sorts of little flourishes.But some gameplay in this game is janky. The platforming feels pretty good while it's just the belt grapple, but once you throw the DRIP water gun into it, yeah, I start to hate it as you lose traction and can't quite see where you're going as you aim the water at your feet and often have to cross large gaps with long run-ups while enemies chuck projectiles that can knock you out of your jump.The combat arenas also get very cluttered and visually messy. With enemies having immunity to everything but the right mode of the right weapon and spawning right on top of you most times, it can often feel annoying, particularly getting to later levels.I guess for those much more experienced with boomer shooters, this will be something with a refreshingly new palette with more of a puzzle aspect to enemy encounters, but as someone slightly more casual, honestly, I'm having a bit of trouble loving it. I find it hard to recommend in that way. For most people, I'd just watch someone play this. You can appreciate its good qualities at that distance without frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, how I wanted to enjoy this game.People loved to level the complaint that doom eternal "forces you to change weapons for enemies".I never agreed with that and found myself to get a long just fine with using whatever gun or tool felt good to use.In FPS every enemy is hard locked into only taking damage from whatever gun(s) the game wants you to use. And some of them just aren't fun.Late game has an enemy that requires you to throw 5-7 gnomes at them, wait for the gnomes to whittle down a bar of health/armor, then switch to the first rifle, use its alternate attack which is a sticky bomb, THEN hurry and attack the enemy with your rifle before the timer from the sticky bomb ends. ALL while dodging a huge mess of projectiles, aoes, and enemies bumping you on scooters and sometimes chaining you up.Not to mention the dubstep enemy which is a bulletsponge with an AOE that covers the entirety of the ground of whatever arena you're in. This enemy can only be damaged by ONE gun.Except for the rocket launcher which they give you at the end of the game almost, but then they also only dole out the ammo for it when they specifically want you to use it.If you end up buying this, don't be surprised if by level 7 or 8 out of 13, you're feeling "I'm just over this". Level design is barebones to nonexistent. The jokes are just cringy and NEVER. STOP.There's only 5 weapons. 1 is a throwable used for only 2 enemies and isn't fun to use. 1 is the rocket launcher which you don't get til the last few levels and barely get to use.Also the final boss is an absolute joke. It's not hard, not at all, but it's an absolute slog and just boring. The final boss took me about 10-15 minutes, and that's because I would have to wait for an npc to deliver me THREE ROCKETS AT A TIME. The three rockets would do about 15% of the boss' health, then I'd have to wait until the npc came back. Rinse. And. Repeat.If you played the demo last year during the steam fest, I'm not being hyperbolic when I say you've witnessed the best the game has to offer.There's sooooo many good boomer shooters available right now. Do not waste your time with this one. Do not let the immediate style fool you. Buy anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: An original revision of the now-ubiquitous boomer shooter formula. Fashion Police Squad builds on a sunny, blithe atmosphere with plenty of memes, jokes, and trendy fads thrown in, as opposed to the usual dark, horroresque setting of its peers.The gameplay is, perhaps, the best part of the game. Each weapon and tool at player's disposal can only hurt specific enemies, which are weak to it, arranging a complex rock-paper-scissors ruleset to follow. It takes some time to memorise and get used to the weapons and the enemies that they counter, which leaves you rifling through your weapon menu mid-fight, while at the same time dodging dozens of projectiles; because of this, it gets quite hard later on even on lower difficulties.Sadly, the game is incredibly short at 16 levels total, and can be beaten in just about 4 hours, and also feels a bit low on content overall.Otherwise, Fashion Police Squad is a fairly worthwhile experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This is close to a master class in pacing. Every time I was starting to get bored or it felt stale, a new mechanic/weapon/play-style was introduced. Has some of the freshest boss fights in the genre. If you are tired of the circle strafe bullet sponges, this has you covered.  Plenty of grade a cheese to go around in the setting, enemies, and dialogue. Fun stuff.Biggest complaint is some truly frustrating platforming sections in a first person shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just adding a note after  finishing the game, my thoughts are largely the same, but I'll say that things do get even better as the game progresses, especially the music and levels, the final boss was really fun too, with its only fault being that his twist required a quick text tutorial halfway through.Only played a few missions so far but I decided to make a review after Mission 8's boss.It's a really fun shooter, the gameplay is genuinely great, there aren't a lot of guns but they all feel pretty unique and one even plays into movement in a fun way, movement feels really nice during fights and thanks to the design of areas and the enemies I'd say that moving around feels better than in games like BLOOD. Enemies are fun to fight and encounters are pretty well thought out when it comes to the mix of enemies you face at any given time.Now what made me really love the game, was its humour and presentation, and Mission 8's boss sealed the deal, the game is pretty absurd as far as setting, plot and humour goes, it's very unapologetic about the writing it has, it's a constant stream of references and absurdist humour that is rare for me to enjoy but that really worked for me here due to the way the game's presented, the  character sprites really sell all the enemies and their fashion crimes, the locations are varied and look lived in, the sound design's pretty good, the mob's dialogue is pretty funny and the music's pretty nice.The only real downsides so far were a couple of bugs that had no impact on gameplay, and using the belt to swing around the map can sometimes be annoying because of slight bumps completely ruining the swing. But overall, it's a pretty fun game, fairly unique too despite the saturation of the "boomer shooter" market.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I am one those people that loved the forced weapon swapping in Doom Eternal. Using just a shotgun gets old fast. So, what if you did that but made the game be christian friendly by focusing on horrible fashion choices that you must correct with your "weapons". This is the only non-violent fps I think I've played. The humor and genuine challenge knows not to overstay it's welcome by constantly being goofy and giving you new ways to play the game. I love defending the award show from fashion crimes by sniping their cringe away. Ok, I lied, it's not family-friendly, their is an enemy that some people might not like but was the best surprise and made total sense it being in this game. It's not hard to think about what fashion kink it could be.If you want to become fashionable:
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Started out liking this game. Very funny and clever writing and the music is great. But the more it went on the more I hated it. The gimmick of needing a specific attack for each enemy is unique in the start but as more and more complicated enemies pile into confined spaces it becomes insufferably horrible. trying to juggle whatever super specific attack you need for one enemy as all the others bomb and smash you into the corners. I turned the difficulty down more and more as the levels went on until I was dying on easy mode to the hoverboard enemy near the end who does entire arena wide damage, which is un-avoidable, and also buffs the health of all the other enemies. If the combat wasn't total ♥♥♥♥ it would be a classic but it tried too much bs all at once and the whole game suffers for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying this game is fantastic!  Probably one of the most unique FPS games I've played in a long time as far as the theme goes.  Fashion Police Squad is a very vibrant game full of memes, funny villains, terrible puns and god tier style.  It controls well, and plays smooth and fast paced.  The enemies get progressively stronger throughout the game, and beware the Karen, she will be back, and in greater numbers.On a technical level the game overall runs great being a doom-esque clone style shooter, the characters are well animated in pixel style and the weapons feel good to use.  The only criticism I have is there's a bit of a rendering issue when travelling fast using the belt whip between buildings on the 2nd set of levels, though I was lucky enough to have the Dev visit my twitch stream who confirmed they are releasing patches for little bits like that so this will probably not be an issue now.Overall, this game is fast, fun, colourful and has a fantastic grasp of humour making it an absolute delight to play.  Add all that to a fantastic low price and you have an absolute gem.  Get it in your steam library now!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: genuinely great time with some fun mechanics. It's worth the money, even if most of what I did enjoy was just the humor and overall sense that the developers had a good time making this. with that said, the game does have problems, mainly with the combat. It feels great initially, but as it expands and introduces mroe guns and enemies thinks start to become pretty grating from a nice little challenge to a bit of a slow drudge, until it finally ends up being sadly a slog to get through, especially the mission before the final boss when there are just so many enemies packed into an area that the only solution is your fake rocket launcher. Trying to outmaneuver enemies or just trying to be better at avoiding attacks just turns into deal with more enemies faster simply because it's an impossibility  to be able to avoid all of them. There was even a bug with the ||gimp suit enemies with whip chains|| where trying to use your grappling belt to swing around would force the nearest enemy of that type to teleport in front of the belt in the air cancelling it out. This sadly makes the game at it's best when you aren't actually in a traditional fashion fight and instead is worth it more for the boss fights, special level segments and the comedic writing. Platforming as well wasn't as well thought out as I'd hoped and instead was simple platform hops with a "run" introduced later and a grapple that acts more as a spacer for the platforms.Overall worth your time, lots of creative things to love about the game but not enough of that same thought put into polishing and refining their gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprising little joy of a game. Fast paced combat that requires you to rapidly switch weapons to take care of enemies. While the level design is not particularly inspired, the combat variety and just strange weirdness that the game comes with makes up for it. Well worth your time and some cash.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Doom but its running on LGBTQ+ engine. Since the last Steam Next Fest, i have played over 40 demos and this game outshined a lot of them. I have been excitedly waiting for the day it gets released and i'm really glad to say that it really delivered. Fashion Police Squad is a brilliant and fresh take on retro shooters. In it, instead of mindlessly killing people, you have weapons to fix peoples fashion crimes. Each gun has a different use case and because of that, the weapons don't feel stale to use. It has one of the best pixel arts i have ever seen in a game and the environments, characters compliment it beautifully. The story is not really memorable and some might find the writing cringy but i really think you will realize how much it suits the game itself. Though the game is mainly a shooter, it is also a really solid platformer. Each level ups the ante bit by bit and thanks to the creativeness and uniqueness of most mechanics, the game just keeps getting better.  I have almost nothing bad to say except i had some fps drops in my playthrough that didn't necessarily break my immersion.  The game is short but super sweet since it has no fillers. I'm really looking forward to other projects this team puts out. I think this game is well worth the price you pay.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Level design bad.Weapons novel but mediocre.Premise novel but wasted.Writing the quirky millennial variety, aka insufferable.Enemy design bad. Enemies spam attacks in an annoying way and don't signpost their attacks properly.Combat annoying. There is too much visual noise to mentally grok what is happening on screen. Combat encounters bad. Arenas too small, fights devolve into attrition instead of a tactical dance. It's basically bullet hell where you have to race to kill everything before they deplete your health. The devs are aware of this, because you always get tons of health pickups after each fight as a bandaid to the bad design.Levels are long and copy/paste areas, making them feel tedious.Game tight and visually/technically polished, but mediocre in gameplay execution. I not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who's a fan of FPSes will appreciate and adore the hilarious satire in .Prior to release and having played the demo, I was concerned that the main mechanic of each enemy requiring a specific way to be defeated would drag the game down but that was not the case at all; with only four weapons, there is overlap between which enemies are affected by which weapons so there's more freedom than you might think.It's a really creative and ingenuous game with genuinely good humour in it. I'm really happy with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the first six missions, it's safe to say this game is an absolute banger as Des would say!This game is full of great humour, but I like that it's not the only thing it has to offer. The gameplay is very snappy and smooth which makes busting fashion criminals extra satisfying. There are some really creative enemies here, and I especially like the bullet hell type of dodging mechanics that they have implemented on a first person shooter with great success.My biggest gripe with these kinds of games is usually the difficulty being too easy, but I feel like after playing on the second hardest difficulty the challenge feels just right. I'm not steamrolling through the levels too easily, but also not getting frustrated stuck in the same spot for an hour. I will definitely have a second playthrough after this one on the hardest difficulty though. I also like that there are a lot of design choices here done with speedrunners in mind!There are a couple things that I didn't like and some missed opportunities with the weapons and enemies here and there, but no major complaints so far. This game really performs above what I expected going into it.This game costs less than a pair of designer socks and has a lot more swag, so I would definitely recommend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced fun fashion action. A great FPS experience that doesn't outstay its welcome, with new mechanics, environments and horrifying fashion crimes behind every corner. The soundtrack is banging and the pixel art graphics are great, but my favorite part is the writing and the story that's full of jokes.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like that one, but i wasn't convinced, despite some good, interesting ideas. First of all, there's the obvious: the unique setting, universe and concept of "fashionizing" enemies instead of killing them. Then there's the combat: you can't use any gun you want on any enemy, you gotta choose the right tool for the right foe. While it's a cool gimmick during the early fights, i don't think it holds up really well in the long run. Because the devs wanted you to play in an overly specific way, there's absolutely NO versatility in there.  For that reason, i don't think there's much replayability either, and there aren't much secrets to be found anyway.And i can see the Doom Eternal crowd come and bring the good old  back up... but i completed the campaign on the hardest difficulty so i think i actually could, in fact, get used tot he gameplay and master it.  Somehow, i think that the "very hard mode" is what ruined it for me. I can think of a dozens of situations when a lighter difficulty would have made things much more fun and less of a hassle. So if you end up getting it anyway, i advise you to stick to "hard" mode (or whatever its in-game name is). That could mean less bullet-sponges, and less annoyingly unfair encounters.Would that be enough to redeem the whole game? I'm genuinely not sure. Fashion Police Squad has some of the most obnoxious and pesky enemies i've ever encountered in a boomer shooter. That's probably done on purpose but it really got on my nerves, and you can't get rid of this. Same for the constant rhythm-breaking narration through dialogue pop-ups. Sometimes, the NPCs don't even have anything relevant to say, they just interrupt you to tell something like . Speaking of this, F.P.S. is barely enjoyable to roam. It holds your hand way too much through bland boring levels. I can think of a few surprisingly good platforming parts. Same for a few specific mini-games. 2 out of 3 bosses were also nice. Alas, even if it has its moments, FPS don't shine often enough to earn a positive review in my opinion. Aside from those few parts, the rest was often drudgery to me. My review may sound harsh to some but it's not exactly a bad shooter, you can give it a try if it's on sale or if you got it the monthly Humble Bundle. But otherwise? I wouldn't put it in the boomer shooter priority list.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a really fun concept and design, but i agree with the other viewers that it gets to be too much having to use specific weapons only on certain enemies and having mobs of all the enemy types flying around. Aside from that I think its really fun, but the magic gets beaten out of you by the frustration of having to shuffle a bunch of weapons to not die
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing idea!The fact that they took  a pretty worn out idea, shooting demons, shooting aliens, shooting terrorist that recycles for 30 years and make a very funny and interesting spin makes this game stand out so much.The presentation is 11/10, so funny, so vivid, so full of personality, this game stands on its own, the graphics are an homage to very old 2D shooters with enemies having only the front sprite and turning towards the player at all times.The music is really good, very funky, very catchy and the sound is very crisp making you identify easily which enemy is attacking from where and what to do.I had an absolute blast with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a boomer shooter wrapped in delightfully humorous pixel art aesthetics. The game’s narrative is quirky and engaging, ensuring a light-hearted experience throughout. I had enjoyed various fresh gameplay elements across the gameplay. What I like the most may be the Boss fights designs, which are particularly well-crafted, offering challenging and inventive encounters that highlight the game’s creative spirit.However, the level design occasionally misses a stitch, especially in later stages where cramped spaces become cluttered with diverse enemies requiring specific weapons to defeat. This can lead to moments of frustration amidst the chaos. Fortunately, the game wraps up quick before any annoyance can wear thin my patience. Overall, Fashion Police Squad is a stylish, fun-filled shooter that's well worth picking up for a quick and humorous blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. Great concept, great humour, great art. But I just can't stand having to swap weapons all the time to tackle different enemies. Coming back to the game after forgetting what weapon is for what crime is just painful. Although I do understand the logic of not being able to fix a badly fitting suit with an underpants gnome or whatever. If I can slap and belt whip all the crimes no matter what they are, why can't I just shoot them? Also what is with the annoying pointless jumping and parkour sections between each arena? You took all the worst lessons from doom eternal. I just want to shot stuff game stop getting in your own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those classic shooter games that nobody asked for, but needed to play!PROS: fun and imaginative twist on boomer shooter design; quirky and creative presentation; fast-paced; amazing selection of "weapons"; top tier humorCONS: some platforming was a pain in the assCONCLUSION: All in all, Fashion Police Squad is a fairly humorous parody of internet and video game culture, wrapped up in an entertaining boomer shooter package. It confidently showcases smart game design knowledge with its sharp controls and engaging gameplay. You’ll chuckle at its dialogue, be thrilled with its gameplay, and take glee in fixing fashion errors that may cause you genuinely to roll your eyes in real life. Who’d have thought making your enemies stylish could be so much fun?
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is what you would get if contestants of Ru Paul's Drag Race were tasked with creating a new Duke Nukem game and someone overachieved that assignment. The hilarity of the theme was expected, but I'm most pleasantly surprised by how good this strafefest feels to play. To top that off, everything is just juicy, impactful, and stylish on the audiovisual side. FPS (I see what you did there) manages to feel both retro and fresh, forcing the player to not just blast away but employ the full arsenal of fashion weaponry. While repetitive at times, the game flows nicely into the next humorous story point and presents you with new enemy types. Simply fresh & chic!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A very wacky and non-violent FPS with plenty of cloth-related puns to go around.The game had me chuckle quite a lot at some of the puns and jokes going around as well as keep me on my toes with just how intense the combat can get with the various badly dressed perps act as they're introduced along with new gameplay mechanics to spice things up.Highly recommend it if you're looking for something that's a lot more lighthearted and non-violent than what you usually see in FPS games.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun concept, great style, but by the final 1/3 of the game, the enemy encounters become unbearable slogs. So much of the combat encounter design sets you up to take gobs of unavoidable damage, then "apologizes" afterwards with health drops to build you back up.Having to switch weapons to deal with different enemy types is a potentially interesting idea, but in practice, it literally ruins the game by the end. Being swarmed by different enemy types in a tiny space (like a rooftop) creates situations where you're simply trying to race against your unavoidable health drain.If there were better defensive options to help with crowd control while switching through the different weapons, then it might have worked. As it is, it doesn't.Play the demo, that's by far the best part of the game. If you're insistent on playing the full game, stick with a lower difficulty, even if you're usually an "Ultra Violence" FPS difficulty player.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a lot of fun, but can at times get brutally punishing with enemy combinations in the latter half of the game. At twenty bucks, this is a steal, and overall won me over with the game's sense of humor, charm, action, and really well-designed boss battles. Overall a winner, but I'd recommend playing on a lower difficulty at first to get the hang of the weapon juggling before pushing into something more punishing. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Oh the common thread that is people complaining about gameplay loops being too hard despite the arsenal you're presented with during the late game. It's Doom Eternal all over again, lol.Stop throwing away your rockets and take advantage of the fact that you can clear dozens of fashion crimes at once with them. Utilize that sweet whip to escape from the scooter bros constantly pummeling you. Know which weapon to switch to and which targets to prioritize, etc. Boomer shooter 101. Are we really still complaining about games being too hard? Come on...In short, get good.6.9 hours in and the story has been bested. Game was amazing and hit all the necessary spots. I'm looking forward to 100% completion of the game and thoroughly enjoyed how much effort was put into it. The demo had me worried the gameplay would fizzle quickly but it kept delivering and kept me wanting more. Although it ended too abruptly, I'm still looking forward to revisiting levels and secret/achievement hunting the levels all over again. Game absolutely shreds with style and class. Wonderful change of pace to the average boomer shooters that have been dropping.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: + Good, over-the-top humor* Story with text-only dialogue- Too much mixed enemy variety with need for dedicated, necessary weaponry and skills (quickly became too much)Personally, I disliked the text-only dialogue, and the the variety and necessary weapon and skill management, remembering, and swapping quickly became cumbersome and annoying - and even more so after not playing for a while, you have to remember again or try and re-learn.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Initial premise and ideas are very clever and funny, the first few levels are very charming and fun but later on it isn't nearly as fun.But late to mid game it drags on way too much, and even all the charm in the world can't save it from being annoying.-Inconsistent platforming, especially with the whip, this gets super annoying later on-The guns are all fun when you get them but later on switching between 5 guns to find the one gun YOU NEED is so annoying and tedious-Later game spams so many enemies, especially really annoying ones, the Gimps who prevent you from using your whip with levels designed with it in mind and chainstun you-You get a really OP rocket later on but it kept clipping on geometry and wasnt very usefulThe demo when I played it was so much fun, the first few levels are but It's so boring and annoying later on and it saddens me because I love the premise, humour and characters. I think im on the final level, the boat and I just can't complete this, it's no fun at all.If any of this interests you try it for an hour or close to two and if you feel like it's not as fun or it's beginning to frustrate you dip out and refund it imo, or buy it on a big sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Any goodwill the game builds up is ruined by the final boss.  Terrible design choices abound:* Damaged only by one weapon?  Check.* Damaged by the only weapon with limited ammo?  Check.* Drops for ammo are random?  Check.* Attacks are quick and difficult to avoid?  Check.* Health drops are also random?  Check.It's like they forgot they were trying to make a fun parody of boomer shooters and decided to punish anyone who stuck around to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: - The main game loop of having to switch weapons on the fly to accommodate to criminal's needs never got stale. I had a blast trying to parse out all the different enemies in an encounter and strategize my priorities and everything.- The movement in this game is really fun. The belt grappling hook is fun to use, and the water gun—despite taking some time to get used to—was really fluid to use.- This game is hilarious. Simple as that.- Encounters in this game felt like they were just the right difficulty. Sure, I died sometimes, but it was never enough to make me get frustrated . I played on the second hardest difficulty, for those curious.- Surprisingly, the over the top and almost amateur voice lines never got old. They really add a lot of character to the game and I don't think I'd quite enjoy it as much without them. There is an option to disable them if you get tired of them, though.- The small platforming sections in some levels are well designed and fun to go through.- The characters are all enjoyable; from the main characters to even the enemies.- Sock Gnomes feel almost shoe-horned in as a weapon. I never really enjoyed using them, aside from maybe throwing them at the music person to ruin their beat drop.- The Fab-Slap, as funny as it is, always feels like you get it in scripted places. It almost takes some of the magic out of it when you're suddenly faced with like 50 enemies but you just so happened to get 100% fab moments before.- Overall Rating: 8/10 (Great)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about Fashion Police Squad, but to me, there's equally as many things to dislike as well. I was going to go on a huge rant and list the extensive list of bad points about the game, but then I realized that I would also have to list the equally long list of good points about the game (to give a fair review), so I won't be doing that; it would take too much time in a written steam review.I'm still giving a cautious positive recommendation because the game clearly had a lot of effort put into it and it is polished. And also, the lead designer is clearly an OG who has played many of the different classics (even from different media), as evident in the many references imbued in its gameplay, writting, art and even sound and music. So you've gotta respect that repertoire and influences.Just be aware that this is not a traditional FPS (for better AND for worse), it is more of a "gimmick" humorous niche game where the core gameplay plays second fiddle to the main thematic and narrative, and to be honest those 2 elements got old rather quickly because when every little thing is a nod or reference or pun (no matter how clever or funny those are) it gets overwhelming. It is a unique experience for sure, but it rapidly overstays its welcome and those 5 hours to complete the game went on for longer than I had hoped. Get it on a deep sale and see it for yourself; by the 2 hour refund mark you'll have a decent idea of what the game is all about.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of like a family-friendly Doom Eternal, you'll find yourself having to use red guns on red baddies and blue guns on blue baddies time after time, especially in later areas where you're locked into arenas with waves of spawning enemies.I regret playing on Hard, it was fine for the earlier levels but around level 10 it became a considerable struggle to keep advancing. You have a fixed amount of health per area outside of pickups and there's no way to come back from low HP, like in Doom Eternal. You just have to not get hit. This wasn't helped by readability issues: guns and fire effects taking up a large amount of the screen often made it difficult to tell what I was shooting at which is a very critical element for the 'Simon Says' nature of this game.That all said I enjoyed my time with Fashion Police Squad. The protagonist, Des, is genuinely funny and likeable in a sort of dorky himbo kind of way, and it managed to be pretty consistently funny at times, even though some of the jokes were just terribly groan-worthy. Like a Power Glove joke in 2024? Come on. If you're like me and you play basically anything that looks like a boomer shooter, you'll get a few hours of enjoyment out of this, but its contemporaries like Forgive Me, Father, Dusk and Ultrakill do outshine it slightly.One final thing I wanted to touch on that isn't bad or good, it's just weird: 90% of this game you could give to a child to play, there's no blood and enemies aren't killed, and there's only a little risque humour... but then in the final few levels gimps and flashers turn up which was just weird to me? I'm not a prude or anything but it just confused me lol
