_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Video review: The genre, which many like to call "Boomer Shooter", has never been as vibrant as it is now. And vibrant is the watchword when playing Fashion Police Squad for the first time, which despite being an FPS doesn't have any gore elements, nor will the objective be to finish with the species that are on the other side of the barricade. A title that is full of references, not only to titles that made this genre so beloved, such as Duke Nuken, but also to films like The Wolf of Wall Street, or to Drag elements such as the highly acclaimed Death Drop, when the game is charging and even when pressing the special skill button and even the finger snaps from Nintendo Direct showcases. This was one of the cases that caught my attention on Twitter for its creative and colorful side in terms of presentation but also in terms of gameplay. It's noticeable that the Mopeful Games studio put a lot of time and attention into every detail during the adventure. While the story isn't the deepest, every line of text lets the characters' personalities shine through, and there's even drama to keep things spicy.The player will take on the role of Sergeant Des, a policeman dedicated to fighting the wave of fashion crimes that is ravaging the city. The streets are full of people who have various problems in terms of their clothing, which, yes, are present in our daily lives and which, among them, are multiplied by examples of tourists wearing sandals and white socks (please don't do this), clothes that are too tight, the Karens of this life, &c. After playing this game I will keep an eye out for these situations! Watch me!As I mentioned there are no moments of gore or any kind of violence. Well... there are times when it is possible for us to throw a good b*tch slap in the face of clothing aggressors, however, all weapons are somehow related to fashion and affect specific enemies. The 2-Dye-4 Elite gun is perfect for solving crimes of monotony of colors against the gray suits of businessmen who throw suitcases at us, but it is completely harmless against, for example, bigger cases and when I say bigger I mean in terms of stature, since there are lockers (gym bros) in suits that don't fit the shoulders in the best way. In this case, Tailormade will be called to the noise to mend the stitches of a once-giant suit. All weapons have a different but very intuitive flow from the first contact with them. It should be noted that the water weapon makes it possible to wet not only enemies but also the ground and thus make the character move faster. This is a viable option for traversing the map faster, but it also makes it easier to reach platforms further away.I found myself often looking for the right button to pull the right weapon to fight the fashion crime that was in front of me. Yes, because playing in Hard mode is not easy at all. I had to repeat several sections as they were filled with waves of enemies that seemed endless. At certain times there is a need to cross the level again in the opposite direction. Not being exactly the same thing, since the enemies presented in a second round may even be different from the previous case, but there was a need to do so to add some game time to a level that seemed to be small.When it comes to level design, the colorful maps, which get more interesting as the story progresses, invite your exploration and become even more interesting due to the amount of secrets hidden in each corner and that reward the player with a poster of the character dressed in very special ways. What about a He-Man or a Harry Potter in a fashion game?Whether you understand fashion, whether you're a fan of Pop Culture elements, or on the other hand you don't understand any of these subjects, Fashion Police Squad manages to grab the player for the fun of its easy-to-recommend gameplay and still delivers a few laughs in between.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lovely take on the classic Boomer Shooter in a very "Yass queen slay" kind of way. Had this came out back in the day of Doom's original inception, it may have been seen as the Weenie Hut Jr. of Doom games, but what you'll find in this game is a colorful world full of fashion, fighting, and fun. This genre is not typically a game I would play, and playing at Hard in an attempt to prove something to myself, I definitely found myself whelmed by everything coming at me. Regardless, I was having fun in the chaos of it all, correcting fashion crimes the entire way. The writing is witty, and more than worthy of an audible nose exhale of humor. My sole gripe about the game is that I, myself, have difficulty playing it for more than an hour and a half or so at a time before feeling significantly motion sick that I have to lay down and take a break. Either way, I enjoyed my time with the game and it certainly gave me thoughts and ideas about what I wear next time I step outside my door.

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw this game back in 2020 and was really, really excited to play it. The devs were posting it on Reddit and I was so hooked by it. Now that it's been two years and I've finally had the chance to play it, I would say that it's worth picking up, but it's definitely got some problems I'm surprised made it in the final release.The good news is that it IS fun. There are lots of puns and references to catch. The art style is clean and readable all the time. The bosses are really creative and have several phases. They are definitely a standout to me. The guns and enemy variety is good too, for the game's length, and really show how committed this team was to this goofy concept. The only real downsides are minor, but they're easily remembered when it's a relatively short game that's largely banking on the idea of the game, not so much the mechanics themselves.I had some annoying visual bugs during a platforming section (whole sections of the map would flicker, or disappear completely), which was already a low point in the game to me because the platforming felt a little under cooked. I kept falling straight through the platforms I was supposed to be landing on. It restarts you back several platforms too (not the one you just jumped from, but like three or so platforms back) which is incredibly irritating and I can't imagine why it's like that. The platforming almost always requires you to spray the ground with water and use it as a boost which means if there are several platforms, you have to constantly stop and spray the ground. I get the idea and I think it can work for some locations, but nearly ALL the platforming does this and it just absolutely kills the pacing.You also have to swap weapons CONSTANTLY. This may bother some people.Some QOL features could be implemented. Like, how about letting me turn off all dialogue for levels I've already completed instead of making me rapid fire jam the E key. Let me turn off all tips. That kind of stuff.Some areas toward the end absolutely overwhelm you with how many enemies there are. I was really shocked at how aggressive and challenging some of these little moments were. And you may restart fairly far back, which can be a huge bummer. I guess it isn't too much of a complaint, but more of an observation. Because I fully expected the game to be a breeze from start to finish.Either way, yeah it's a fun game. I feel like you sort of know if you'd like this game or not just from the concept and a short video.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: So to be perfectly honest I don't like picking a thumbs up or thumbs down for this one, but if I had to pick I guess I'd prefer to stay on the positive side. I've not finished this game as of writing, but I've played enough that I feel hard pressed to say my thoughts on it will change by experiencing *more* of it. Fashion Police Squad is charming, it's got a vibrantly self indulgent personallity and a sense of humor so *eh* it almost makes me chuckle. The game itself is fine in concept and it plays well enough to be... palletable... but that's about it.Everything in Fashion Police Squad is *almost* good. Weapons *almost* feel good, movement *almost* feels good,The visuals *almost* look good,The gameplay is *almost* fun. But the entire experience reeks of a lack of polish that it desperately needs. It's difficult to put into words but everything is just *slightly* off in a way that makes the entire experience difficult for me to enjoy. It gets an A for effort, and like... a C- bordering on a D for execution.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an underrated gem of a game. If you found this on your own, you struck gold. If you found out from a friend or other source, they struck gold and are sharing it with you. This game has one of the most fun gameplay loops I've seen in an fps shooter game. When I got this on the steam summer sale 2024, I thought it was going to be just another first person shooter game like any other, but OHHHH NOOO I was wrong. It may not be plot heavy but that's a good thing, as the game rarely interuptts the player's pov, but when there is a plot, it gets even better. People may not like it because one weapon may only do damage to specific groups, but that makes sense. It makes sense because if you saw a big coat, would you smear makeup on it and say that's fixed? Neither would I! and if you said yes, start thinking. This is a great game, with good times packed into it. The ending left me sad too, so that's an accomplishment. I'm a heartless being who can rarely feel sadness, and this game's ending made me sad, one, for the fact that it was over, and two, for the fact (insert important character here) (spoilers)! This game was made with love, so I'm going to buy the soundtrack when the summer sale 2024 ends, for full price! If you haven't bought this game (and read this whole review), go buy the game and try it for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique 'boomer shooters' I've played. The fashion puns and theme can be a bit over the top, but that's part of the charm. I found myself genuinely laughing at some of the bizarre enemies and situations. The soundtrack is sufficiently retro, and punctuates the fights well. The guns are all solid-feeling, the movement is surprisingly good, and the game can be beaten in easily 8-9 hours on the middle difficulty, and 100 percent completed in 10-11. Short and simple, something too many games lack. Your enjoyment may vary, but for me this is a solid 8, maybe even 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is filled to the brim with fashion, style, and creativity in almost every aspect of the game. This was a complete joy to play through. Some of my personal highlights are.Presentation has so much personality and charm. The world is well thought out when it comes to it's main idea revolting around fashion. Everyone's life is full of fashion choices and design. This is reflected on some details like the billboards advertising certain trends of meme, and clothing. Whole companies are designed around a certain martial and style, which is really nice. The enemies you fight in this game are based around super ugly fashion trends and bad choices. Like socks and sandals, dull business suits, weird things and such. You can even fight Karens that complain to you the entire time which is just wonderful :) The pixel art and world graphics blend in with each other really nice and even work together with one another to create great visuals. The music is also really high energy to suit the absurd nature of it all. Sound effects every time you deal with the un-fashionable and some of the weapons are so satisfying and rewarding to the ear.The boss fights in this game are super creative, have super fun  gimmick, and their design in terms of fashion really does a good job in what to expect of that said boss. For example you get to fight a loser discord moderator. Now take this and imagine some of the stereotypes that center around that, and chances are, you know what the boss fight will look like. Super awesome design.Now for some of the things I thought were pretty in the middle.Level design is a mixed bag. On one side, you get levels that greatly paced, visual variety and surprises. Alongside awesome set pieces that are creative and add on to the fashion world. But on the other side of the bag, you get the subway levels which are super tight, cramped, and a barrage of foes in a artificial way. These levels don't create a good game play loop at all. And or some are bland that they don't really add on to the world and absurd adventure. Also from time to time, there will be some platforming  sections sprinkled through out the adventure. I personally liked them because they created variety from the shooting action. However sometimes, it's really easy to overshoot you landing on small and narrow platforms. Something to just note on.The weapons you get through out the game are pretty normal, but with the fashion flare and absurdity that is super great. But you have to use certain weapons against certain foes in order to defeat them. You can't mix match the weapons you want to use. I personally feel this is a pretty artificial way to create combat variety. There could be other ways to better this such as gimmicky arena design, and or special hit boxes or elements of the world. They kinda do this with fire hydrants to make you're first weapon stronger for a small amount of ammo. They should be more of this rather then selective weapons for selective foes. The only thing thing that I don't like about the game is the way they handle special challenge levels. out of the three challenge levels, two of them are bland, boring gimmicks, short, and out of place with how it was put together.  However, the last challenge level is fantastic, thrilling, and well...challenging. I wish the other challenge levels took the same approach but add in new ideas and gimmicks in the mix. The last challenge level certainly have great foundations for future challenge levels with great ideas waiting to happen.Overall if you are looking for a family friendly shooter with plenty of fashion charm, awesome presentation, creative bosses,  good level design (most of the time), and fun ideas, this is certainly a game for you. If you look through the screenshots of the game and don't like the fashion tone of it, chances you won't like it, since the game entire identity centers around the latest fashion trends. But other then that, this is a super great and humorous time to be had. I would personally give this game a 8/ 10. It would be closer to a 7, rather then a 9. This game is short, but never over stays it's welcome. A stylish game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr- recommended with caveats- the general premise for the game is great, but the execution in places leaves more to be desired, and at worst, is frustrating. while i will expand on the negatives below, i still generally enjoyed my time with the game and look forward to what comes next from this developer.** i do want to note that the devs are currently patching the game to address many of the things i complain about below. since i have 100%ed the game already, though, i am unlikely to revisit this game again any time soon to confirm which of my issues below have been addressed, especially since this is already a 'recommended' review **level design is unremarkable (with a few exceptions) and fairly sloppy. there are a few different locations, and they all make heavy use of modular assets. i want to clarify that i think there is no harm using prefabs/modular assets, especially as a smaller indie team with a limited budget, so long as things don't feel copy/pasted often. things did feel copy/pasted often though. a lot of this is noticeable because assets don't line up, there is z-fighting, you can see/fall into the void, or you see the unrendered insides of assets. i normally don't care much about these things, but it was so common i started to notice it more and more.difficulty balancing is all over the place. some levels and encounters are ridiculously easy, while others account for 90% of my deaths and required my to grind/save up for a super skill to get through. the main issue with difficulty was limiting player movement in tight spaces with a lot of enemies and/or enemies who have attacks that are near impossible to avoid in a small space (karen gas cloud, for instance). i think part of why enemy encounters in games like doom and quake work so well is down to the positioning and choice of which enemies to combine in an encounter. it doesn't feel like the same attention to detail was utilized in the majority of the encounters for fashion police squad.negatives aside, i really liked the premise of the game. it definitely fills a void in the "boomer shooter" "retro fps" market and gives visibility to characters and ideas mostly unexplored otherwise. the colors are bright, there is some charm to the story, and the character art in particular is well done. i appreciated some of the movement mechanics too (even if i found them a bit inconsistent) like the belt of justice for swinging and the wet'ones for increased ground movement speed. in summation, i think some of my late game frustrations have unfortunately colored what was, for the majority of the game, an enjoyable experience. recommended if you play every new retro-styled fps or you are looking for something a bit different and you have some patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Among the flood of titles in the current boomer-shooter renaissance, we have Fashion Police Squad. This yassified version of Doom sure has style in spades, but is almost completely devoid of substance.As Sergeant Des of the Fashion Police Squad, your task is to rid Trendopolis of heinous fashion crimes. To this end, you'll use a variety of weapons and gadgets, such as a color sprayer that can liven up even the dullest gray suit, a sewing machine gun to combat those baggy fits, sock gnomes that will devour offensive footwear, or a water gun that will cool off even Guy Fieri's signature fiery outfits.This setup serves as a solid basis for a retro shooter. As such, the "combat chess" mechanics are on full display here - after the tutorial, you'll regularly have to fight groups of enemies, dodging and weaving to avoid incoming damage while strategically deciding who to take out first.It's a shame, then, that this aspect of the game isn't all that well thought out. While the combat is pretty solid, with fluid movements and snappy controls, it lacks the creativity and problem-solving prevalent in actual retro shooters. Each enemy can only be defeated by one specific weapon, with later, more complex, enemies having two or more health bars, where each has to be whittled down separately.Also, there's no sense of experimentation and discovery where you find a new weapon and have to figure out how to use it effectively - each is just given to you at the exact moment you find a new enemy type.The game also features extended platforming segments, as a way to mix up the flow between fighting sequences. However, figuring out the timing can be pretty tricky, making these segments more frustrating than fun.The pixel graphics are simple but effective, with the appropriate amount of effort given to details to ensure environments don't feel dull. The cinematics are done in a comic book style, with character outfits and poses clearly inspired by Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (which, in turn, was inspired by fashion magazines of the time, so I guess we've come full circle). The music and sound design are serviceable for this type of game, but nothing to write home about.So I guess the final question is: what does this game actually want to be? The shooting and platforming are solid, but not great. The graphics and sound are serviceable, if unremarkable. There is barely a plot, with the script relying heavily on lame puns, outdated references, and clunky dialogue to get by. And finally, the vibe is a bit off - it feels like the creators have a genuine understanding of fashion and style, but the game has a watered-down satirical tone where you're not sure if they're being sarcastic or earnest.The way I see it, either go fully down the boomer-shooter route, where we don't care about the plot, but the shooting and platforming are polished to perfection, or pick a lane for the story (satirical or earnest) and focus on that, while leaving the mechanics solid, but not spectacular. The way it is, Fashion Police Squad is stuck dangling in the middle, like an ill-fitting suit no one wants to pick off the rack.

_childDocuments_.review: Every so often a game comes along in a genre that upsets the apple cart and does something truly new. In the shooter space, that is a little rarer than in others. Fashion Police Squad is one of those rarities.On the surface, it looks like your typical linear story blastathon. But dig a little deeper and you'll find one of the coolest single-player shooters of the year. It's got great level design, clever writing, and enough dad jokes to keep you laughing over the course of the game. The mechanics are a nice mixture of everything from Bulletstorm to Bionic Commando. Save for one or two frustrating horde moments, I rather enjoyed my time with this one. If you love the FPS genre and want something different than the old school 90s kill everything experience, or the contemporary army themes and battle royale games popular today, check it out. Everything about it feels new, and it makes what should seem like a one note sight gag work really well over the course of a substantial campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Slight recommendation. Main issue is the first person platforming. It's not very comfortable and slightly missing a jump is frustrating. The belt swinging mechanic is good but it's easy to make a mistake. Long jumps are another problem area where you'll probably miss a few. The platforming doesn't get any better by the end. I was annoyed with the game many times.Also, the game becomes challenging by adding more projectiles which would be fine but they stick you in these really tiny arenas with no where to go. So good luck dodging everything. This is less of a problem and the enemies are interesting since they all have a unique way to defeat them. But with switching weapons so much it can feel like you had no choice but fail.This isn't like other first person shooters and one one hand that's great because we need something different. On the other hand it sometimes feels like the developer didn't take any of the important lessons from them either. Still, it's has good shooting and the humor is pretty good. I didn't get tired of it but that's very subjective. There are a lot of memes so be warned of that.I liked it enough to finish it and it's an interesting short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: "I fell into the flames... and bounced back!"I love the way this game does comedy; most comedy games I play typically do the "stand-up routine approach," where you listen to funny characters go on as you experience standard gameplay. In this game a lot of the big laughs come from the little things. Its hard to describe, but the game knows when NOT to be funny in some ways. The enemies you fight don't tell jokes, but they're intentionally cheesy and over-the-top in a way that makes me giggle.Gameplay wise, Doom Eternal is clearly the biggest influence. Here though, its ride or die. Every enemy has a very specific weakness. It really depends on what you're looking for in the gameplay. If you're into freeform player expression (finding a favorite weapon or an unconventional approach to a problem), you will be dissapointed. HOWEVER I personally enjoy a highly tailored encounter. Combat is less "which weapon do I use" and more "where do I go, and who do I take out first". By no means would I consider it mindless.Lastly I have to hand it to some of these bossfights. FPS games used to be infamous for godawful bossfights but more and more these days I've been seeing exceptions to that rule. These recent boomer shooters, with over-the-top movement, weapons, and enemies, certainly lend themselves better to fun, personality-fueled bossfights then the gloomy shooters of older decades.These DJ enemies tho.... I'm sure the pro players will tell me to get good at the game, but boy do I hate them. They're not even voice acted either so they were especially disappointing!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoyed this retro styled first person shooter that has an emphasis on the comedy and having the right weapon to solve any fashion faux pas from a multitude of enemies. There are so many fashion puns and references/nods to other games to at least bring a smile with the cheeky writing and voice/sound design. Fashion Police Squad also introduces new mechanics throughout the game that does not overstay its welcome, from a turret section with drab suits on flying boards and long limousines to a fashion sniping session to correct guests' fashion disasters.There's a lot of secrets to find throughout the game to unlock, so it encourages some replay of the levels to find it all that will unlock more outfits and visual treats. That being said, the platforming is a hit or miss as it requires some finesse with a certain weapon in order to progress. Each level will progress in adding more enemies to an arena to encourage movement and prioritize your arsenal (the belt whip will get a lot of use to keep opponents at bay). There are challenge levels as well to test your mettle.In addition, the music is very catchy and fits the mood of the game very well. The audio is very top notch with some endearing low quality voice lines from some enemies to give them character. The announcer letting you know when you have stylized your enemies is also a cherry on top of this cake. Boss fights are very distinct and memorable too! This all comes to a head for the end of a level where you get to see all the defeated foes strutting their stuff on a walkway.Fashion Police Squad is not a long game, but it was a welcome addition to my library that leaves quite a fashionable impression, which has been missing from the retro first person shooter genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty unique concept for an FPS. Rather than killing people, you need to fix their awful fashion, for example, coloring in a grey suit or fixing someone awful hair-do. It was pretty fun for a few hours but honestly the weapon switch mechanic really annoyed me and I wasn't able to finish the game past level 9. I may come back to this game at a later point.I'd still recommend playing it, but just know that some of the later gunfights can be quite disorienting, when several enemy types are attacking you and you need to switch to the correct weapon type in order to even deal damage to them.Lastly, even though I find the concept unique, these type of games are ALWAYS better when there is some blood & gore and unfortunately, this game has none of it.Final rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game of 2022. The game mechanics are a real breath of fresh air. Each enemy can only take damage from a specific weapon. Some enemies take two different weapons in a certain sequence to defeat them. The result is an exciting dance between weapon switching, choosing the right firing mode (each weapon has an alt fire) and targeting the right enemy at the right time. At times, the intensity can be Doom-esque. The game certainly is challenging if played at the right difficulty. Just when you feel like you've seen all that the game has to offer, a new mechanic, weapon, or enemy is presented that shakes everything up. Some sections had me seriously impressed with their uniqueness and creativity. It's evident that so much thought and care went into creating this title, nothing feels lazy or sloppily put together. Absolutely check this out, it runs great on Steam Deck as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unique! It resembles a strange mix of Doom and Spiderman, and it works very well. The weapons are designed so that you'll need to use them all, adding to the experience even more. It's clear the developers were passionate about this game, and the story is hilarious and doesn't take itself too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of boomer shooters, big fan of movement shooters, not a big fan of movement shooter elements in a game that's built mostly as a boomer shooter. Everything about this game is fantastic. The art style is what immediately got me interested. Gameplay is fluid and fun, fun storyline, infinite pop culture references, etc. The ONLY thing I'm not super fond of is the movement shooter elements like sliding around with the bubble gun or swinging around with the belt, but only because this is a boomer shooter at heart. Boomer shooters are slippery, that's how they're supposed to feel, but these elements feel just a little TOO slippery when combined with other elements, which can make some sections of the game a little frustrating at times. It's definitely nothing game breaking, I would still highly recommend this game.You can really feel the love that the devs put in and if you've got $20 to burn, I'd recommend you pick this game up over that $35 wingstop order that you're having doordashed to your house rn you slob
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a fun throwback shooter with the gimmick being that you have to use specific weapons to defeat certain enemies. The game is paced really well and constantly introduces new enemies and weapons right things are starting to become stale. The story was pretty enjoyable as well considering how ridiculous the concept is, but it does just about everything it can with the premise of fashion cops taking down criminals committing fashion crimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

Certain enemies can only be damaged using certain weapons and it creates some strategy. I just wish enemies would eventually disappear after you resolve their fashion violation. _childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best retro fps games that i ever played, it feels like old doom mods but with more fashion (haha), humor and graphic stuff (npc fading in combat is a very clever idea). has an amazing soundtrack and these kill voicelines make me laugh every time. it's simply an amazing game, i enjoy every bit of it, truly epic and funny
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Really original FPS. Clearly inspired by DOOM with tons of stuffs borrowed from the Super Nintendo era (most of the voice/effects could be taken from Street Fighter IV or Turtles In Time).  What makes this game so original, is that you're not fighting demons or monsters, but people with an awful taste in fashion (like people wearing socks with flippers, or Karens..). Only a Finnish studio could come with such a weird concept 😄The sense of humor is top tier. One particularity in the gameplay, is that ennemies are only vulnerable to one specific type of weapons or ammos. This is quite an interesting approach at first, though it get a little bit frustrating after the mid-half of the game, because you constantly have to switch between weapons. Despite this little annoyance, I absolutely recommend this game, especially if you are looking for an original 16 bits retro FPS that doesn't take itself seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend playing the demo, you'll have one hour full of laughs. After the demo the game just repeats its own formula.The humor is great, the gameplay is meh.It's quick paced first person shooter gameplay but it's all about picking the right weapon for the right enemy type all the time.The level design reuses the same assets in every area so every part of a level looks basically exactly alike and you would be lost all the time if it wasn't for a mission marker that you blindly follow non stop.The exploration could have been interesting but the secrets are way too easy to find and there is no real reward besides a picture to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: By far, this is the wildest first-person shooter I've probably ever played. For how ridiculous it looks, though (and trust me, it really is), the way the narrative and theme of fashion is integrated into the game design is incredibly clever. Every weapon works in a plausible way to fight a plausible fashion crime and the general moment-to-moment gameplay is solid as a rock. Fellow gay DOOM fans, take notice.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad offers a refreshing twist on the classic "boomer shooter" genre, injecting it with a vibrant and quirky personality that sets it apart from its predecessors. As Sergeant Des from the Fashion Police Squad, players are tasked with eradicating fashion faux pas from the streets, wielding an arsenal of weapons to combat crimes like socks paired with sandals and uninspiring business suits. Here's my detailed take on this stylish adventure:Let's start with the gameplay, which is where Fashion Police Squad truly shines. Unlike traditional shooters, FPS introduces innovative mechanics that tie directly into the fashion theme. Each weapon is uniquely tailored to address different fashion crimes, keeping combat fresh and engaging throughout. However, I must admit that the chaotic combat sections towards the end of the game were a bit overwhelming. With a barrage of enemies and constant weapon switching, it sometimes felt like a fashion frenzy that left me scratching my head in disbelief.Moving on to the visuals, Fashion Police Squad delivers with crisp, colorful graphics that perfectly complement its vibrant setting. The attention to detail is commendable, with each character and environment exuding personality and charm. However, I would recommend turning off pixelated text, as it can be a bit challenging to read.In terms of audio, the game doesn't disappoint. The music sets the tone effectively, while occasional voice acting adds an extra layer of charm to the experience. Despite the lack of extensive voiceovers, the humor throughout the game is undeniable. Even as someone not particularly well-versed in fashion, I found myself chuckling at the witty dialogue and quirky scenarios.Now, let's talk about the final boss fight, which, while exhilarating, can also be a tad frustrating. Balancing the intense action with strategic gameplay proved to be a challenge, but ultimately added to the overall excitement of the showdown.Overall, Fashion Police Squad offers a fun and relatively short gaming experience, clocking in at around 5-6 hours. Its humor, innovative gameplay mechanics, and vibrant visuals make it a standout title in the genre. Despite some minor frustrations with combat intensity and readability issues, I thoroughly enjoyed my time patrolling the streets as a fashion-conscious sergeant.Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and challenging! Well designed enemies and weapons to counter them. Some decent movement tech even though I wasn't always happy to do the platforming. The game kind of fell apart for me near the end as there finally became too many enemies and guns to say I was enjoying the mechanic of enemy weapon-type immunity. DOOM Eternal style enemy spawns also became really really tiresome by the time it was over. Really exhausting final few segments. Still, the gameplay is slick enough that it easily gets a recommend from me. I enjoyed the references and humor but it may not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A slightly shorter but incredibly fun, robust experience of a boomer shooter. Puzzle-based gunplay never gets old thanks to regularly introducing new spanners into the works, every boss fight was interesting (especially the second one - with all the different game styles, I had a dumb smile on my face the entire time), and I think it has to be said how welcoming a shooter is in this space that doesn't take itself ultra seriously and just has fun. This was a fun, light-hearted game in a sea of overly grim and crunchy contemporaries and it didn't outstay its welcome either. I think the only thing that I didn't like were the gimp enemies, who were more annoying than threatening and harmed the flow of combat (instead of rewarding rapid responses like a lot of the other enemies do), but besides that, a home run of a shooter and one I can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A fun doom clone that doesn't take itself seriously. Makes references to older games movies, and memes. Visuals are good, game play is nice until the end. Boss fights could be better as the last one felt more like a chore than anything exciting or challenging. When you kill the final boss you feel free than accomplishing something. At a certain point in the game, enemy spawns and types feel cheap and irritating. Also, some enemy types tend to glitch through walls during fights. But overall, it's a fun FPS game to play if you're wanting to take a break from anything competitive. Would recommend buying on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Got this from Humble and it was a good game but sometimes too challenging. I almoast gave it up because of the chaos which was caused by too many different kinds of enemies which need to be killed by different weapons and the unavoidable attacks all the time. My Fab gloves were waisted a lot of times until I figured out there is a problem with the keyboard layout and other keys are activate this special power by accident too.. not just the one you set.Usually about 24-30 hours game play is prefered for me to complete a game.. It was really exciting at first how this game is doing FPS without killing enemies.. just making them fashioned. :D+2 for the style and atmosphere-1 for too many different kinds of enemies and some of them are really a pain to defeat..-1 for combat system feels too slow sometimes compared to the amount and speed of the enemies. Some weapons should do more damage.-1 for upgrade system, there is nothing like that.. only a few clothes can change on the game.. but nothing else..-1 After a while it becomes too hard because of the reasons mentioned above..-1 for FAB power bug, it toke a lot of time to fogure out why it is activating when I don't want it.. and didn't press the key..7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah.I'm going to say that at the time of writing this review this little gem has made my day.At the moment we are going through a interesting time for FPS games. On the one hand you have massive super black-hole budget games like COD and such kinda just spinning the wheel BUT on the other hand you have had loads of smaller games like this one that are just an absolute joy to play.This game takes itself zero percent seriously and embraces the silly ass plot and style of its theme. _childDocuments_.review: After playing for the first two hours, I can safely say that this feels like a true love letter to retro gamers, fans of Doom/Duke Nukem and to people who loves puns. This game just oozes with style! And goofy jokes.Playing on the second hardest difficulty had me on the ropes before I started to grasp the different combinations you can pull off with the weapons. Some enemy types are frustrating, but the level design and different movement mechanics, like the pole swings or the fashion slap, give you just enough versatility to make split second choices that let you stay away from being worn out (aka dying). I'm not gonna let you in with all of the weapons I already unlocked, but Portal fans should love the water gun. *nudge nudge*I'm really looking forward to playing this more and trying to speedrun through some of these first levels.If you are looking for good vibes while playing a 90s styled FPS game with well written, modern humor and fun game play, this should definitely be in your radar!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this game, it was just a few little things that ended up making this a frustrating instead of fun game.Pros- Great music/aesthetic- Unique weapons and ideas- Very interesting story had me chuckling a few timesCons- The average enemy damage is a bit too high, it became constant in the later missions that I had to absorb a number of hits because it takes a bit too long to dispatch the enemies- Weapons are a bit too one note, it's good to promote weapons having certain strengths but it gets tedious having to switch every 2 seconds because the 10 enemies on screen all need different weapons to cause damage- Platforming is often frustrating, not so much the whip grappling but the sections where you need to use the water gun it just isn't my idea of fun in an FPStl;dr A interesting but flawed FPS game, pick up on sale if any of the points sounded interesting to you otherwise I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Decent "old school fps". I say in quotes because of two things which heavy deviate from old school fps. First is the lack of quick saves which for some reason a lot of newer old school fps do. But more importantly every weapon except one has infinite ammo which I really disliked. This is such a simplifikation.The main aspect of the game is that every enemy can only be damaged by one or two certain weapons, and stunned by certain others. It's an interesting idea and means the game has a unique selling point. But if you really think about it, this just limits the way you can play the game. (Btw. there are just 5-6 weapons in the game.)A very subjective point is the theme of the game which is all about fashion which is kinda cringe imho. Still the humor isn't bad here. The look is mostly pretty nice, the soundtrack is dope and the gunplay is mostly pretty decent if you can overlook the fact that the game really ristricts which weapon you are supposed to use against which enemy.The game also consists of surprinsingly quite a lot of platforming. Those mechanics are pretty decent.Lets talk about balancing. I played on the highest difficulty and let me tell you that the game isn't that hard most of the time but has some huge difficutly spikes, even unfair at times, especially the boss fights. (In fact I couldn't beat the final boss on the highest difficulty.) The lack of quicksaves and the fact that checkpoints are sometimes too rare can make this frustrating. On lower difficulties the game should be all right, I wouldn't recommend highest difficulty though.

_childDocuments_.review: i dig the everything cause werk buut i hate that youre pigeonholed to specific weapons for every enemy. like if youre using your weapon right it should work. i really don't want to give it a negative but i kept falling into a hole and didn't really care enough to figure out what i needed to do next through like youtube or gamefaq.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad makes me really, really wish there was more nuance to Steam's recommendation system. I played the demo a month or two back and liked it enough to buy the full game day 1. The first few levels dole out more of what I liked from that- fun, peppy music, a concept with heart and soul, bright and joyful visuals, and some fun takes on the classic FPS arsenal. Things start to go a little sour with the introduction of some later enemies leaving lingering damage effects that add visual clutter and slow down a game that feels like it should flow much faster. The latter in particular, introduced just as the levels switch from fairly open urban environments to tight corridors and often fought two, three, or four at a time alongside other enemies, lead to deaths that feel cheap and unearned. This brings me to another issue I'm having that wasn't immediately apparent from the demo. Most enemies can only be damaged by one or two weapons in your arsenal, forcing you to switch weapons frequently.  Giving every weapon unlimited ammo sidesteps the potential problem of a lack of ammo leaving you unable to damage certain enemies, but not every weapon feels impactful or satisfying to use- meaning that fighting certain enemy types (looking at you, Guy Fiery) feels like a chore. I'm about 40% of the way through the game at the time of writing, and having an increasingly rough time of it- I really want to love Fashion Police Squad, but I wish I had watched some more in-depth reviews before purchase. I hold out hope that some tweaks to enemies or weapons may improve the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "Beautiful Art, Innovative Premise, But Tedious Gameplay."Fashion Police Squad boasts a visually stunning art style that immediately draws players into its vibrant world. With a premise that promises innovation, it's hard not to be intrigued by the prospect of enforcing fashion laws amidst such captivating visuals. However, as engaging as the game's presentation may be, its gameplay mechanics leave much to be desired.The concept of dispatching enemies with specific weapons initially seems like a novel twist on traditional gameplay mechanics. Yet, in practice, it becomes a cumbersome and frustrating ordeal. Rather than embracing the fast-paced action one might expect, players find themselves bogged down in a repetitive cycle of trial and error.Each encounter feels like a chore as players scramble to locate the correct weapon for each foe, disrupting any sense of flow or immersion. What should be a seamless blend of strategy and action devolves into a tedious exercise in micromanagement. The beauty of Fashion Police Squad's artistry is sadly overshadowed by the clunkiness of its gameplay.Ultimately, the game's potential remains untapped, obscured by its own design flaws. While the foundation is undeniably strong, Fashion Police Squad falls short of delivering the captivating gameplay it promises, leaving players longing for a more streamlined and engaging experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but I just could not after playing 9 missions.I've basically stopped playing after the second boss, which was a tedious experience at best - over 15 mintues of running chaotically.My review is nothing new - other reviewers pointed out those points good.In summary:+ nice graphics+ good music+ meme-like humor related to fashion - meet your tailor, socks and sandals, etc.- combat system is just not there - on that in a moment- level design is incomplete- story is unengaging after some missions - I do not care what happens So, "combat" system. You have 5 "guns", I've only got 4 due to dropping the game- paintball shotgun- sewing machinegun- gnomes- water soap gunBasically you have n types of enemies and an enemy can only be hurt by a specific gun/s. During first few levels its ok, but later on when you have a cluster♥♥♥♥ of enemies in small rooms you need to switch guns like frantically and the visibility is bad.In conclusion - good premise, poor execution. It's a very repeatable game that's more tiring than fun in the long run.You have some character customization when it comes to powerups but that's not really making any change in the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes everything I love about retro Shooters and adds  a pinch of that 90's SEGA Dreamcast era flair to it. This game has a style that sets it apart from your standard shooters and runs with it to tremendous success in my eyes; It has vibrant colors, a funky Chip-tune soundtrack and I cannot wait to take down the fashion crimes out their. I highly recommend this title to any and all.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I actually disagree with many of the reviews saying this game "starts great and goes to ♥♥♥♥ in the end." The game is tedious and rigid 60 minutes in, at most. I would say the greatest strength of "boomer shooters", arena shooters, arcade shooters, what have you, is the expression they allow the players. This strength is found in many of the shooters I love, from Doom '93 to Ultrakill. Fashion Police Squad, however, removes all of this expression by reducing the game to a series of concurrent rock-paper-scissor matches. Each enemy is taken down with (usually) a single weapon or strategy. If you use the incorrect one, you are entirely ineffectual. This proves to be incredibly limiting and boring, as well as occasionally irritating when you want to take care of a high priority but can't get through the wall of enemies only affected by your flaccid melee. If the game drops off after the beginning, then seeing the end is not worth the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A funny and clever take on the classic FPS genre. There is a lot of interesting ideas however it still needs some work, specifically when it comes to pacing and balancing encounters. The game will just lock you in a small space and spawn a dozen enemies at once, and unless you happen to have your ultimate charged then I hope you enjoy being attacked from all sides at once by enemies that each require specific weapons/tactics to beat. The worst of this was on the rooftops during the beach level, I died at least a half a dozen times during one encounter because there was literally no room to maneuver without either eating tons of damage and/or being knocked off and taking damage. It's just cheap and goes against how the base combat mechanics are setup. There are other issues as well but the claustrophobic enemy spams really soured the experience for me. Overall I'd still recommend it, though in its current state maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Gay Doom featuring Doom Slay Guy.Great boomer shooter with amazing soundtrack and beautiful pixel style.Unlike most shooters, it is also a puzzle game having to use specific weapons to defeat specific enemies.But the funny dialogues, aesthetics, and a bunch of video game meme references. You will have a dazzling time
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliantly dumb fun game. I am honestly surprised that the tacky fashion jokes did not get old; maybe they will for you, but they didn't for me.The shooting action, sadly, is the weakest part. Even with the incredible boss fights, the major issue lies with the enemy weakness system. Every enemy has weaknesses and immunities, with nothing in between. this means that every attack will either have no effect, or a regular effect. As a result, you'll be forced to constantly switch out weapons, and if you've ever played Borderlands 2 in higher difficulties, Fashion Police Squad does it worse.Exploration in this game is quite superb. Using the belt melee attack as a grappling hook was very enjoyable.This game's saving grace is the incredible boss fights. There are only 3, but all of them are amazing, and honestly the 2nd and 3rd were incredible fun that I highly enjoyed.All in all, you are getting what you paid for, a ton of dumb jokes with mixed gameplay and some really strong redeeming qualities.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid boomer shooter FPS. Cool art style, the humour can be hit or miss, but it's never super distracting or too in your face. You'll probably get a neat chuckle out of somethings. Mechanics are cool, lots of enemy variety and having to swap weapons to deal with different enemy types. Grappling is also super fun.Overall solid indie FPS, well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is NOT a generic 2.5D Doom-clone shooter. While on first glance it may appear so, it isn't that. It is heavily inspired by Doom Eternal, even upping it a notch. Gameplay while chill at first, quickly ramps up in difficulty forcing you to swap weapons to defeat different enemy varieties. It gets as sweaty as Doom Eternal, and that is a good thing. It has actually challenging platforming sections where you can swing by poles using a whip - Prince of Persia style. And yes, the platforming in this game is definitely a notch or two harder than Doom Eternal. But if you got through Mario, you shouldn't have troubles with this one. If you're thinking, "meh, another 2.5D shooter with a cartoony art style where you're not even killing enemies?", trust me - you'll get over that bit quickly enough, because the gameplay is very enjoyable. All in all, a solid shooter, that punches way above its weight, and is an under-appreciated gem. Has good replay value as well, and I see myself replaying the game again when I'm older. I was starting to get tired of 2.5D Doom clones that are aplenty these days, but this one plays very very different. You won't be disappointed with this game if you enjoyed Doom Eternal.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A sillier retro style game that has a lot of fun mechanics and weapons to play around with. Very unique in terms of it's premise and just how wacky and difficult some of the later encounters can get, especially with a gorgeous art direction.Some later levels feel like they get a bit more challenging in weirder ways I'm not sure how to explain but otherwise most of the combat encounters are balanced in terms of difficulty and skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: One of those rare cases where I was actually thinking about a game outside of playing it, and being excited to start it up again. Humor is bearable if you're above the age of 12 and have the capacity to use more vocabulary than the word "cringe", and ramps up in difficulty greatly towards later levels. _childDocuments_.review: Just not good.Presentation wise it does a good job of looking the part, but when you derobe it all you find is a dusty copy of Doom Eternal and several crusty tissues in the pockets.One of the major issues with this game is that it ONLY wants a specific weapon to deal with specific enemies. In most cases it does this by making every other weapon completely ineffective, that's fun right? Swapping to a shotgun because an enemy literally requires it, and not because you tactically benefit from it overall. Simon says gunplay. Barf.Outside of the MAKE SURE YOU SHOOT THEM WITH THIS gameplay, maps are pretty linear and sometimes involve swinging over pits with your belt, but it's never more than point A to point B type stuff, enemies don't require you to swing around even when the opportunity arises because strafing will usually be enough.Secrets reward you with either armour or the same picture of the main character in a different outfit over and over...? Thanks..?Look, I don't know if a prerequisite to liking this game is wanting to ♥♥♥♥ the main character, but it sure as hell ain't making me want to look for secrets lmao.You get an ability to instakill enemies for about 20 secs every so often, but it's not very fun. You just click and he teleports and defeats them. That's the only other mechanic you have apart from shooting. Shooting enemies with the specific gun the game wants you to that is, did I mention that yet?Difficulty wise, what difficulty? Just bash it onto hardest and I promise if you're semi decent at FPS games you'll have absolutely no issues. Enemies don't hit hard and all your guns have unlimited ammo soooo...It's just so much style over substance. Quite a lot of freezing you in place mid level to read dialogue too, cos that's what everyone wants, to stop shooting and read jokes based off old memes and other unfunny ♥♥♥♥.It has a vision but needs less slack on the belt because it's trousers (pants for yanks) keep falling down, and it happens so often I've stopped laughing and started rolling my eyes instead. Couldn't recommend this game unless you've exhausted the entirety of the Steam boomer shooter catalogue and can't wait for more.Edit: oh yeah, it runs pretty poorly too in a lot of cases. Under 100fps on a 3090? What?

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and competent Old-School FPS subverting the old Doom and Duke Nukem tropes by making you "help" enemies instead of slaughtering them. This little twist helps with some clever gameplay gimmicks, such as having each enemy be vulnerable to only one or two of your "weapons".The tongue-in-cheek nature of the narration with its puns and constant easter eggs makes it highly enjoyable, even in the significantly harder last few fights of the campaign.The platformer set pieces and overall traversal mechanics fall short, however, with some weird hitboxes... But nothing annoying enough to actually impact the overall experience.The game is short, with some challenges to complete after the main story ... But since you can basically turn the game into a very easy mode with story rewards, I wouldn't count on it that much to boost the playtime.Nonetheless, I recommend it. It's a pretty neat indie shooter with a really fun premise ! :D

_childDocuments_.review: Got it from a humble pack.As far as the theme goes, it commits to the bit and hams it hard, and I think it does a good job even if I can't say I enjoyed it. The game certainly has style!It's not a bad shooter. It runs fine, the movement feels fine, the grappling hook is fun. If you're big on advanced movement tech: look elsewhere. The actual shooting part unfortunately feels like a chore.The enemy weakness gimmick is unique but not that interesting, since it takes all the decision making out of combat. No longer do you need to worry about conserving ammo, or what guns work best on what enemies, or even target priority since some weapons (looking at you, belt and sewing machine alt-fire) have cooldowns long enough to force you to target something else. The only real choice you have is to press your berserk button if it's real dire.But that's not even my real gripe. No, what kills me is that the secrets are pointless. You get.... character art of the player character in bad fashion. I get why, if weapons are strictly gated behind progression because they only work on certain enemies and you don't need ammo, the only thing you can put in them is healing. And the game doesn't need more healing. But it's still such a downer to know that looking for secrets is basically pointless! Admittedly I may be more secret-hunting oriented than your average boomer-shooter enjoyer, but still.This game didn't do it for me, but I would pick it if I needed a boomer shooter for a person who didn't really play videogames. It's straightforward, not that hard, the game tells you EXACTLY what you need to do, and the tone and style would probably help sell them on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why this is rated "Very positive".For 20 bucks you basically get a roughly 2 to 3 hour "pseudo" boomer shooter. I've played for like 20 minutes, 2 missions, but I'm just, sadly, bored to death. The game has about 12 missions or so. Let's be generous and say each mission takes 15 to 20 minutes (it's more like 5 to 10 for the early ones), so this is how you end up with about 2 to 3 hours, maaaaaaaybe 4 if you're stretching it. That's already a very short time to money ratio. There aren't any other modes than the campaign. You may choose a higher difficulty, and it's nice they're all unlocked from the start, the question is just ... why?This is one of those games that isn't offensively bad, it's just... why would I ever spend 20 bucks on ... this? Something that is essentially a glorified student project. The art style is ultry generic Pixel Art (think old school Doom, more colourful, but with duller environments), the combat and traversal is uninspired and slow, there's not even a "run" button, and your guy is pretty slow by default. The weapons are your standard fare, but with a "twist", because they don't kill, you see? The shotgun shoots coloured pellets, the Tommy Gun basically does the same, a beam of light sucks the colour out of things, while a belt whips some fashion sense into people... There's more I'm told, but I have no real intention of finding out I'm afraid, because each weapon only ever works on one enemy it seems, which means constant switching for each and every one of them. The enemies themselves don't really present a danger either, and their portrayal is "mildly humorous" at best. There's dudes in grey suits, super energetic "bros" on city scooters, bigger dudes in loose fitting suits, baggy pants users, you get the drift. You'll likely encounter way more fashion sinners, but they're not really interesting in combat.In fact they seem to just be haphazardly thrown together with little thought for the various combat arenas, but such a combat arena should be carefully curated, so that enemies complement each other. But they don't. The suits guys throw suit cases, and due to the weird graphics style and projectile speeds and the fact you need to hit them up close means you get hit every once in a while, but the baggy pants guy just stands there as a sort of "don't come near me or I'll ... bubble you"... yeah. While the scooter dude is just zipping around the arena, occasionally crossing your path... yes, this is just the beginning of the game, but if you want to grab the attention of people who are not toddlers then you gotta do better, I'm afraid.That basically leaves the "story", which is equally as yawn inducing. Some conspiracy is afoot, of course, and your fashionable police squad has to get to the bottom of it, with the help of a mysterious figure in a trench coat. There's nothing of interest here, it's just a vehicle to get you from arena to arena, from mission to mission. You could just as well remove it entirely and the game wouldn't suffer for it much, especially since it keeps interrupting what little actual gameplay flow there is. Every time I was feeling like I could actually almost enjoy the game it stopped me dead in my tracks to give me more exposition and tutorials...And the soundtrack just mellowly plays along without pumping you up. I have no idea who this game was made for. It's not for the "modern" shooter audience, it's not for military shooter fans, it's not for "boomer shooter" fans, it's not for serious players, nor for those looking for levity, because ultimately nothing fits together. It won't appeal to "moms" and it's certainly not interesting to little kids, because they won't even get 10% of the references (meaning you gotta be older, like in your 30s/40s, to somewhat get the humour).All of this is to say that it's on its own not a terrible game, there's just no point in playing it, even for free, because there's a vast amount of infinitely better games out there. A very good comparison imho would be "Forgive me Father", which costs just as much, has more content, a more interesting art style, every level is very different, enemies are actually complementing each other and pose a serious threat, the music is great, the story even is more interesting, and the gameplay is pretty damn good. While that one's a horror themed game, it's got the same niche idea. So if you want to make a retro shooter about fashion ... that's surely possible, but take a look at FMF and copy that game if you must. And yes, I understand that both games came out almost at the same time, but still... one clearly had more interesting ideas and executed them better than the other, so the question remains why? Why is a game about fashion among the blandest in the genre? Wasted potential.Maybe a sequel could fix this. Longer, more varied and interesting missions, more interesting art style, better combat and arenas, more tailor-made weapons instead of the standard ones in every shooter, but they shoot coloured pellets instead of bullets, a more pumping soundtrack, story bits that don't interrupt gameplay and is actually funny and clever, instead of full of dull word plays. Funnily enough this game about non-violence is rated ages 16 up for "sexual innuendo". Can't make this ♥♥♥♥ up, probably because of the exhibitionists in the game?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid boomer shooter with a lot of style. Its aesthetic contributes a lot in keeping the game fresh and interesting throughout its playtime, but that's not all it has going for it. The mechanics are on par with other classic-style boomer shooters such as the original Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. There are many different types of enemies who can usually only be hurt by one weapon type, forcing the player to remain engaged in combat and making good use of each weapon. The difficulty starts to ramp up in later levels, which I'm sure tryhard boomer shooter enjoyers will appreciate. The only complaint I have is that health items can be a bit sparse, making some combat scenarios even more difficult, especially in the later parts of the game. Overall, though, this title is a lot of fun and worth playing if you're a fan of classic boomer shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Just about style people! It's about damn Technique!Fashion police squad may seems like another boomer shooter with a lot of pop culture references, but actually is one of the finest experiment of the FPS genre.Let me explain: the game take the basic notions of the FPS genre like weapons and enemies, then it reduces them at the most basic function. After all said and done, it ''rebuilds'' them in a way that is actually pretty unique and yet simple and familiar: to each enemy,  a weapon ( or two). Seems trivial, but instead of simply following the ''structure'' of the most FPS ( boomer shooter or more modern ones), this game takes the very idea that started the whole genre ( basically, the entirety of the thought process behind doom) and  starts from there. If you think about it, how many games do this? not just adding some novelty to an already seen combat system, but instead to build from scratches an ''idea'' of FPS gameplay? Maybe I read too much into it, but I swear this game is damn awesome ( and fashionable).Furthermore, Fashion police squad manages to insert something more ''modern'' like platforming, weakest part but still done in a very clever way ( and even with this gameplay mechanic, the devs. managed to create a completely new way to ''run'', or better yet slide, for an FPS ). Plus... It's non-violent: all you do is fixing clothes! Besides that, Story and Design are a blast and funny as hell ( and, again, rather unique having an FPS on the fashion world, and even having jokes about it without being offensive), while the soundtrack is fitting and pretty good ( Actually, I loved the bit theme, but I see how this is more of a personal taste).So, worth it? YES. without a doubt. This Boomer-shooter enter with full honours into the pantheon of the games considered pillars for the FPs genre and gaming in general, and also a masterpiece among its peer... title that this game ''wears like a glove'' ( YAS, manage to insert that joke).

_childDocuments_.review: Been excited to get my hands on this one. FPS seemed like a fun satyrical boomer shooter, and it did live up to those expectations. Howevr, by chapter eight I started to loose interest a bit.There are a couple different weapons you unlock throughoput the story, and each has their own secondary attack. This is what caused my enjoyment to wain as obviously only certain enemies can be hurt by certain weapons or attacks, and as you get deeper in you come across some that require one weapon to start doing damage, then the special attack of it or another in order to finish them off. I'm not talking the boss battles, I mean the standard horde enemies.Which leads to the other issue: Artificial difficulty inflation through large hordes and weapon management, sometimes in tight spaces that make dodging pretty difficult. I'm running this on medium to just enjoy the story. I planned to do my second run on insane (as I normally do), but much like Dread Templar it doesn't feel like I need skill or a good strategy to survive, but rather whether or not I'm worn out from the amount of bullet sponges coming my way come the next wave and care enough to move on. Much like the other title I mentioned, I'm struggling to do just that.On top of that FPS just tries to cram too much into the story. Sniper missions is one thing, but when you reach the android boss you have to pay attention which weapon or alt fire to use to wear him down long enough to enter cyberspace and do these mini combat games to advance to the next battle to knock off another chunk of health. In those mini-games you'll find nods to classic titles like some platforming akin to Mega Man 2 (even has similar sound effects). It's fun, but it just interrupts the flow of the main story.Thankfully that's about it with the gripes. Fashion Police Squad is a good game overall that just does too much to the point it starts to lose focus on what made it so much fun at the start in the first place on top of increasing the hordes that progressively eat more of your ammo with each passing chapter. If that's siomething you enjoy then FPS will more then likely kep your attention from start to finish. However if you want more than just a war of attrition each mission then you'll end up checking in about half way through like I did. I'm stuck in the middle with recomending this or not, and given I'm starting to forcing myself to finish process I have to lean towards it being a no.

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous Doom, I guess. Fashion Police Squad's more interesting aspect would be it's limited weapon types/alternate-fires and how each corresponds to a specific enemy type. You correct their fashion crime. A paint shotgun brightens outfits, a sewing machine gun tightens loose, ill-fitting ones, etc. The aesthetic is bright and vibrant, the tone and plot irreverent, really stands out compared to other boomer shooters in this regard.Where I find Fashion police Squad falls flat is its platforming, level design and enemy placement. You can use your melee attack, a belt, like a whip to swing across various pitfalls and a water gun on surfaces so you get as movement/traversal speed bonus, but the level design for these platforming sections starts to become more frequent, clunky and frustrating. Where Doom had monster closets that would open usually on armor or health pick-ups, Fashion Police Squad likes to spawn enemies out of thin air in its combat arenas. Less annoying at the start but by the tenth mission I was just sort of done.I don't even want to bother trying to face tank the rest of the campaign, there's literally so many other boomer shooters out I'd rather just play one I actually enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad (or FPS, nice!) is a breath of fresh air for the arguably over-bloated realm of old school, “boomer shooter” genre. A colourful, light-hearted twist to a game style that is almost exclusively filled with endless violence and gore that also adds its own novel twists to the combat. While the most hardcore purists may find it’s challenge a little lacking and its length rather short, Fashion Police Squad is undoubtedly one of the best titles for people who dislike FPS games to try and get into FPS games with.For even the most die hard fans of the old school FPS games it is hard to deny one fact: the genre is now becoming over-saturated. While in 2019 it was refreshing to see high quality games made like they were in the past finally come out after years of bland military shooters, by mid-to-late 2021 the concept of shooting hundreds of satanic aliens in some hyperviolent, sci-fi environment was worn well past its welcome. Even if you added something new to the gameplay it was still the same gore-soaked mass of 1994 to 1998 gameplay. To stand out now takes something special!Fashion Police Squad (FPS) bucks the trend mostly in terms of its aesthetics. Gone is the brutality and in its place comes a far more wholesome affair: You are a member of the Fashion Police and in this alternative world setting you go around solving crimes against fashion on the streets of Trendopolis. Rather than blow people away with lead, you use your dye-based shotgun (2DYE4) to colour bland, grey suits in, or you use the tailormade assault rife sewing machine to correct ill fitting suits, and so on. While it can be said that a change in settings does not affect the core gameplay underneath, this change in aesthetic and setting does at least make it stand out from a rather large crowd these days, which in most cases is enough for some. More so, it can be said that the more light-hearted take can be attractive to people who previously disliked the violence and gore of other FPS titles. The SNES-but-3D visuals can help this even further. If there is someone in your life who may like FPS games but are put off by the gruesome and gritty nature they have, show them Fashion Police Squad and you may have a convert!Aside from the look of the game, FPS does have a couple of quirks up its chique sleaves to make it stand out. The primary factor is how combat functions. As described above, weapons are… tailor made (I’m sorry) to fit their enemies. The 2DYE4 has both a primary and secondary fire mode, one spitting colour in a shotgun spread and the other as a lightning gun colour drain. Against the first enemies, dull suited men and over-saturated bros on scooters, each fire mode will only work on the appropriate enemy. Dull suits will not be affected by the secondary fire as they have no colour to drain, and the scooter bros are already too colourful, so the primary fire does nothing. As such Fashion Police Squad takes the “combat chess” of titles like Doom Eternal and enhances them to the point of exclusivity; it is not that some weapons are more effective than others, it is that you  use the correct weapons on enemies. This may sound inflexible, but the general combat is never too hectic that it becomes unmanageable. There are some slightly rough situations with a couple of enemies though. For example, there are socks & sandals wearing German tourists who do a hitscanning camera flash at you, blinding temporarily and doing damage, and the only way to combat them is a “sock gnome” that is thrown out like a grenade. On occasion these enemies are placed in high spots, meaning you must climb up to get them, all the while soaking up any damage that they pump out. Bar this though most enemies are fine to deal with and have the usual threat assessment other good quality FPS games have.Tying into the combat are the bosses. I’ll keep this short as there are very few in the game, but all of them are fun combat situations, demanding you change up how you fight them as the fight goes on. While bosses are usually a low point of these types of games, thankfully FPS here has some fantastic battles. So much so I’d argue the second boss fight is worth the price of admission alone!External to the combat the general movement and level design is fairly run of the mill. Levels are linear paths with occasional, optional secrets to find along the way. While it occasionally does branch out into alternating paths and there are “key hunts” so to speak of, it is very hard to get lost here. The only confusing moments are likely to occur with the occasional first-person platforming sections, swinging about from flagpoles and bouncing about on shop awnings, but even those moments are solvable with a little observation.So are there any major issues with FPS bar the above ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? There are a couple of oddly demanding moments on the hardware when I noted the game dropped below 45fps, but these were few and far between. Similarly, the options are not bad but a little limited in some areas. Max FoV being 100? FPS limits capping at 120 before unlimited? Hardly world ending stuff, but a little limited. Indeed, the worst element I can think of comes maybe in the game’s length with only 4 chapters clocking in at about 4 to 5 hours. The time you spend in game is absolutely wonderful, but I can’t help but want to play a chapter or so more! Irrespective, these are a couple of loose threads on an otherwise immaculately tailored product!So do I advise Fashion Police Squad? Without doubt! It may be a little short and lacking in the brutality (both in theme and gameplay) for the hardest of the hardcore FPS aficionados, but as a fun little jaunt? It is without doubt one of the most enjoyable little distractions I’ve played this year!
