_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews for this game seem to stem from a misunderstanding of what it is. So before buying think carefully about whether or not you would enjoy a: Short (~2-4 hour) FMV style game with a strong mystery theme and a handful of (not-especially divergent) choicesThe plot is really what you would be buying this for, this game has a particular story to tell which is interesting and fun to watch unfold. But the game only has few hours to tell its story so match your expectations of the number of divergent plot points accordingly. There is not much 'game' here so if that strikes you as a let-down then this is not the experience for you.  However, if you are looking for a quirky, fun 2~4 hour 'movie with choices' experience with lots of twists and turns to keep you interested then you could do far worse than this and I would recommend it if that sounds like something you'd enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good, although not great FMV game where you play as a young man who wakes up in a hotel room.  He has lost his memory and, as you progress through the game, you (and he) piece together what led to him being there.I will say little about the story, except that it's made more exciting than it otherwise would have been by the use of a time-loop system.  The sci-fi element and the mystery surrounding it is the best part of the game, since the other mystery that features, which I will not discuss, is a run-of-the-mill story.I generally like time-loop stories, and this one held my interest, not least because I had no idea where it was going for quite a while into the game.  The producers cleverly created red-herrings and surprises.It's right, in my opinion, that the developers kept this game short (at around two hours play) for what they had.  Even at that, some of the individual scenes are very dialogue-heavy.  And it slows down the pace of the story without adding anything interesting to compensate.  Some of the dialogue should have been trimmed and the game could have used more twists and turns.The best modern FMV games like Contradiction: Spot the Liar, The Shapeshifting Detective, Late Shift and I Saw Black Clouds either kept the dialogue short, or had much of the longer scenes with sinister (or otherwise interesting) characters, in order to maintain interest.  The producers of Death Come True should have taken note of that when making their game.Depending on the choices you make, you will see two characters who act strange or suspicious.  Sadly they don't feature in the story much.  I would have liked to have either seen these two more or had more such characters, just to add a few more surprises and interesting moments.While the acting is decent, the lead actor looks to me to be quite a few years too young for the role he is playing.The ending theme is awful, and is the sort of theme you often find at the end of modern horror or thriller films - totally out of place.Overall, Death Come True is a good, but flawed game.  It's not as good as the best ones but it is better than The Complex, At Dead of Night and Dark Nights With Poe and Munro.  Basically, if you like Late Shift or I Saw Black Clouds - games where your interactivity is limited to making choices to advance the story, then you will probably like this game too.  Oh, and if you like time-loop stories, then I wholeheartedly recommend the game.  Enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is a short yet fun FMV game. It's more of a thriller movie then a fully fleshed out game something like Immortality which I'm really eager to play. The gameplay itself is pretty straight-forward, you're presented with various option as the movie plays and each choices leads to different path or bad end. There's 2 major ending in the game and I can say it's fairly easy to get both of them. The game is a choose-your-own-adventure genre and It took me about 3 hours to finish the game fully including all achievements and the collectables videos. What I like about the games are it's cast, casting Kaji Yuki as the Navigator is definitely a great choice. The actors definitely did a great job portraying their roles and it works well with the game design.What I didn't like however is it's plot. I felt like it could've be more fleshed out and involved other characters instead of it's awkward plot dumping session we have in the middle of the game. It does make sense to a certain degree but it's just not for me. The short duration of the game aside, the asking price of the game is questionable at best. I don't think it's worth if you're getting it at full price. Overall I think this game is definitely a mixed bag for me, it has the potential on the story and it's FMV design which I enjoyed but it's let down by the overall duration of the game and it's price. I'll give this game . Definitely try it out if you like FMV games or mystery in general but only during discounts

After less than 3 hours I had found all secrets, unlocked all achievements, and the entertainment value was not THAT high. You may still enjoy it if you enjoy interactive movies but there are plenty others that I would recommend before this one; Erica & Late Shift to mention 2.You may still enjoy it, but it's nothing close to what I was expecting when Danganronpa was mentioned in the Blurb.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun experience, though one with very minimal interaction.  This is quite like the old FMV "interactive movies" of the 90s.  You're not really in control, you're just occasionally branching down a short - and usually deadly -"what if" before continuing the story.You're sadly not going to find a twisted web of twist upon twist upon twist like Danganronpa or Zero Escape fans might expect, but it's a pretty solid 2-3 hours of entertainment
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: A short "choose your own adventure" style game - well, more like a movie with a few branching paths. Still thoroughly entertaining and while it is not a deep mastermind adventure like Zero Escape or Danganronpa (which this game keeps getting compared to due to the composer being the same), mostly due to the limited amount of characters, it is definitely an entertaining 3-4 hours until you have seen everything. It has the perfect length and does not overstay its welcome.Huge bonus for the great soundtrack (again, expected from the composer) and the "Off Shot" and "Making Of" videos which show some glimpse into how movies like this get made; I always love watching these kinds of videos. For the price it may be a little steep, but I would recommend it for at least 25-30 % off if you like experiences like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fairly short interactive movie with not many choices, so if that's a deal breaker fair enough. If you're still interested then this is great and worth your time.Production values are fantastic, whole thing looks really good from start to finish. The story is engaging with some nice scifi twists in there.However what I really liked the most is some clever design. The choices you have to make to succeed are often telegraphed through clues in the dialogue that makes it feel smart rather than arbitrary when you make progress, the villain's motives are well thought out in a way I wasn't expecting and while there isn't many choices I feel the entire game is built around leading up to a final choice that is genuinely meant to be tough as you could argue in favour of either routes.I'd love to play more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of an interactive movie than a game, and a good one at that.The good: It's FMV! Interesting plot, nice visual effects. Not a low production value experience.The bad: Except the last choice, the choices are more or less meaningless.The ugly: Some minor characters have little to do with the overall plot. They move the story in strange tangents that make the viewer scratch their head as to what the whole point of including them was. Overall they weaken the experience IMO.Worth it if you like FMV games / mysteries / Japanese media. Takes about 1.5-2.5 hours to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed this game and I really liked the whole premise of the game. I won't spoil anything as I feel that experiencing this game without spoilers is the best experience and I'll respect the creators of the game's wishes not to spoil the story. The entire time the story of the game keeps you on your toes with many plot twists and red herrings. The game puts many hints on how to continue on in the game and it's quite easy if you were paying attention. There are a few downsides. There are only 2 true endings. The choices throughout the game doesn't really matters to get either of the endings as it's quite linear, the only choice that dictates the endings is the final choice in the end scene. They also don't really allow you to save throughout the game as the continue element is part of the story. The good thing is that they give you a skip forward and back so that you can skip over stuff that you already seen, the only time you will really need it is the 2nd run for the other ending. Finally, there's not much replay value for the game after the 2nd round. Other than that it was a nice experience like I was watching an episode of a J crime drama. The entire game with an entire replay of the game with fast forward for the 2nd run of the game to get the other ending and the deaths I missed on the 1st round was around 2hrs according to steam.I would highly recommend getting it it's around the price of a movie and is basically an interactive movie. You get around 2hrs of game play with behind the scenes plus some extras, which is quite nice to have and not forgetting the ending theme is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this mostly out of support for the creators. This game is not for people looking for an in-depth experience nor for those that want the same experience as the Zero Escape or Danganronpa series.Death Come True is essentially the next logical step for visual novels - that is to say, DCT is a movie with diverging choices. In a similar vein to Netflix's Bandersnatch, DCT will play footage automatically until certain points, where you can make a choice that affects the story.The story and choices that you make aren't the most in-depth nor are they the most compelling. I feel like if I weren't playing with someone else to bounce ideas off of, the game would get bland very fast. That said, I enjoyed the time we spent deliberating on the mysteries of DCT. I think the devs and writers took too many cues from modern moviemakers, as a lot of the heavy plot points are telegraphed so hard that it was difficult to not see the end result from a mile away.That said, I did enjoy the time I spent playing through DCT and for its price point, I don't think its much of a stretch to call it an interactive DVD movie. If that's appealing to you, or you just want to support Tookyo Games' newest title, pick this one up, possibly on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but I'd be lying if I said it didn't leave me disappointed. Death Come True comes to us from the developer of the Danganronpa series and is a FMV mystery title. As the story plays out, the game will occasionally prompt you to make a choice where you then witness the outcome of your decision; like a Choose Your Own Adventure novel. However, that's where my primary criticism of the game comes in. Despite the illusion of choice, DCT is actually very linear. Usually you are left with deciding between one of two paths, but making the "incorrect" decision often leads to a quick Game Over and the option to continue the game at the last branch in the story line, so you can make the other choice and advance. It doesn't always play out like this, but in the interest of avoiding spoilers, I'll ease up on getting more specific. Also, this game is a lot shorter than I was expecting. In 3.4 hours, I earned all the achievements and witnessed all the branching outcomes. Granted, there is a fast-forward option that I used to bypass scenes that had already played out in a previous playthrough, but I still wanted a little more meat on this bone. So, why do I recommend it? Because it's not a bad game. The story is interesting, albeit not as mind-blowing as I was hoping. Just know that you're getting a bite-sized, Black Mirror: Bandersnatch-esque experience and not much else. With experience in the Zero Escape and Danganronpa series' prior to playing this game, it's conceivable my expectations were too high. Nevertheless, I look forward to the seeing what Too Kyo Games comes up with next. But as it concerns DCT, I recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the FMV genre and loved everything about this game.  Great story, high quality acting, and easy navigation system. Fun fact: The lead actress is a well known Japanese actress whose film credits include Kill Bill and Battle Royale (2000). The game is about the length of a movie and plays like a Chose Your Own Adventure Book which limits you to minimal options at critical decision points.  You can fast forward throughout the game and I was able to complete the story and experience all the alternative options (and secure all the achievements) in under 3 hours.  Having paid for some of the "cheaper" FMV games from Chinese developers, where the acting or navigation was sketchy at times, I don't mind paying more for a higher quality experience, so the length and cost of this games was not a deterrent for me.Highly recommend it.  Fan of FMV and of Japanese culture in general will greatly enjoy it.  I hope the developers make another game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short FMV interactive movie from director Kazutaka Kodaka, the creative mind behind Danganronpa. It's about as long as a movie (took me 2 hours to complete) and should be completed in one sitting for the best experience.I really loved the story. It starts out as a stuck-in-a-time-loop thriller and throws a lot of twists and curveballs throughout the whole experience. It always kept me guessing.Production values are really good for an FMV game. Acting performances are also above par for this genre. Good work.While "gameplay" is limited in a game like this, the interactivity that IS there adds a lot to the story. It would not work as well as a movie. That's what matters, the interactivity enhances the story.I'm already looking forward to what's next from Kazutaka Kodaka.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: is a "choose your own adventure" styled FMV game. But honestly I'd describe it more like an interactive movie with a bit of player choice here and there. I think the appeal of purchasing this "game" is to experience Kazutaka Kodaka's writing through this mystery thriller. I think DCT was generally entertaining throughout with some emotional moments here and there. However it felt a bit weak compared to the Danganronpa games in terms of the overall narrative development.I think maybe due to the short run time it feels like the plot is a little undercooked and variousnarrative elements could have been explored a bit better and in more detail. However what is presented here is still a very fun ride with some suspenseful twists and the setting especially at the beginning is enthralling. The length to finish an entire run is about the same amount of time to watch a feature length film at about 2 hours.  - The acting performances, the entire cast did a good job in selling their respective roles and adding to the tension of the story. - The cinematography, whoever did the camera work did a good job capturing the scenes and helped add to the atmosphere of the game/movie. - Sound design, generally speaking I thought the SFX and BGM selection did a good job adding to the suspenseful nature of the film while also adding moments of silence when necessary. - The simple but stylish UI that didn't ruin the immersion of the "game". - The concept, I really like these sort of "butterfly effect"/"groundhog day" type premises. Also having the protagonist as an amnesiac works well here as you get to learn things alongside them as the stakes become more clearer. I'd say this was for the most part executed well in this "game". - The story, while not totally disappointing felt a bit weak/rushed towards the second half of the adventure. I'm not sure if it was due to time/budget constraints but that portion felt a bit underdeveloped compared to how strong the beginning felt. It's just odd that the pacing at the beginning felt strong in getting the viewer invested in the world/conflict only to be rushed in the second half to one of the possible endings. Also there's an info-dump in the second half of the adventure that's suppose to explain certain "sci-fi" elements that felt a bit lazy and off in it's placement within the story. This overall point is more so a mixed one rather than a straight up negative one.- Length, for an FMV "choose your own adventure" this was pretty short, I don't expect a game like this to go on for hours since at that point it would feel needlessly padded out or bloated at the expense of ruining the pacing, but it could have been a bit longer to address certain underdeveloped narrative bits. I.E. Character development, and pacing the ending better. *(As an aside I do not mind short length games, if the experience is tight with no fluff or bloat then that's great, at the same time if it feels like there are underdeveloped aspects or wasted potential I'd notice/mention that too. The overall quality of the experience matters a lot more to me than length)- Weak side characters, I can't say who falls under this category otherwise I'd spoil some things, but you'll know them when you see them. They're a bit disappointing in that they add little to the overarching narrative aside from some minor screen time appearances in some scenes.Overall I think this is worth experiencing if you like mystery thrillers, however I'd advise waiting on a discount to purchase this. While good, I think this could have been better if Kodaka would have spent a bit more time on the script and perhaps paced the ending a bit better since that portion felt rushed making either possible ending you come to a little underwhelming. I'm hoping that Kodaka tries something like this again, and the next attempt will be a more solid outing because this had so much potential since all the ingredients were there, but unfortunately fell a bit short on the execution. Regardless if you know what you're getting yourself into it's still worth the ride despite the flaws just probably not at full price.Side note: if you get all the "deaths" you can unlock extras like some behind the scenes footage shoots of certain scenes of the game and more of the news bits if you're interested in that content.

_childDocuments_.review: I 100%ed the entire game in 2.5 hours, so keep that in mind. It's EXTREMELY spike chunsoft, but with fewer characters. The death special effects were... not good, but in a hilarious way. Someone gets stabbed with a sword in the armpit. I liked it because I love morbid plots but I'm not a fan of jumpscares. There are 16 bad endings, and 12 of them are unique and spectacular. There are two possible "true" endings, and both are bittersweet.I would've liked more Spike Chunsoft humor. _childDocuments_.review: I think in a perfect world, I would just judge this game on its own merits and recommend it as like "eh, it's fine", but that isn't the world we're living in. We're living in a world where this game is made by Too Kyo, and a lot of the people who would consider playing it are people like me who reflexively purchase anything and everything in the Spike Chunsoft/Too Kyo sphere. In that context, the game is lacking.It's a "Choose your Own Adventure", but there aren't really meaningful branching paths. It's more like "Pick not the right path, enjoy your immediate unique bad end". Because there's really only one linearly correct path, the whole story ends up not being super mysterious, at least not in a way where I had a lot of time to speculate about the mysteries before the game just straight up told me.Another thing I consider an issue is its length. I don't particularly have anything against short games, but a 2.5 hour FMV CYA is coming dangerously close to competing with just watching a movie unless there's something very gamified going on it. I would say this is not such a game.If you are like me, and you bought this game because of the developer and the other games flagship members of the studio have been involved, I don't recommend because you'll be disappointed. If you just want to play a FMV adventure game, I still don't really recommend but it's at least a thought.

_childDocuments_.review: This was... ok. The live action l think actually HURT the game. Especially given the story and world of the game (it'd be spoilers to say why l think that).It took me 1:50 to beat the game. There are two endings, l only got one, but l don't really care to get the other one because the game basically tells you "hey, this is what the ending A or B will be like, pick one". Around the 1:10 mark l had figured everything out and it was basically just me waiting for the characters to figure everything out.The live action made it so there were so few characters (because it's harder to work with actors than just animate 3D and get voice actors). This meant some characters would be underdeveloped. Like there was this really fun character (Nene) who was only there for like a couple minutes. This is much unlike in a game like Danganronpa, where someone can be an unimportant character, but they still get fun times with the personal time and speaking with them during the slow parts of the story. _childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is an FMV adventure/mystery game written by the mind behind the Danganronpa series, Kazutaka Kodaka. The story revolves around a young man waking up with amnesia in a hotel room. Bizarre events are happening within the hotel, including debating with his own identity and purpose there, the protagonists goal is to try to discover the source of the weirdness by replaying events slightly differently each time.As an FMV, the scenes play out until certain choices are asked from the player. Some actions will lead to bad endings, others will progress the story. There are 2 branching main endings that are mutually exclusive, so the game must be replayed again to see the other. Luckily, once you've gone through it once you should know both how to quickly reach the end, as well as which choices to select to see more of the bad endings. There are no manual saves, but this is due to a design choice that makes sense once you reach the end, but skipping ahead during a scenario is very easy so this was not an issue in the end.Every bad ending awards an achievement, an in-game medal, and unlocks bonus clips of behind the scenes footage of the filming process. It's worth to go out and reach them all to earn those extra bonuses.The total length of the story is about 3 hours, including the seeking of all alternate endings. The bonus clips will boost to around 3.5 hours of total content to see. The performance and effects are very good in my opinion, the plot has some twists here and there, though the player can piece together the greater picture as more clues continue to present themselves. It was enjoyable for what it was, worth checking out in a single sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off with saying that I enjoyed the game for what it was, but for how long the game was, I don't think the price of 15.99 is worth it. Which is not a problem, but was jarring to see at first. The cover art is also misleading as well, since only 4 people are important. 2 of which you actually spend any time with. You barely spend any time with the main villain and you will be dying a lot for a multiple of reasons that I won't name here.Which that said, I enjoyed the story and was able to follow along with the main plot just fine. The opening created an air of mystery that kept of building that I couldn't help but keep playing to see what happens and how things play out and I was satisfied with the good ending. _childDocuments_.review: While Death Come True is inoffensive, it doesn't offer a lot new either. IMO, FMV Games only have a couple ways to stick out due to their format, their interactivity and their story. Well, to start with interactivity, there is little user choice here. When the player does get to make a choice, it is usually a binary between "right answer" and "wrong answer", and wrong answer will zip you back to the decision making point so if you want to see everything you should probably pick the wrong option. Getting things right is basically just a question of "did you pay attention", rather than taking any kind of thought or trial and error, which makes it just keep flowing. There is something to be said about making it easy to continue, but it shouldn't come at the cost of feeling like player interaction doesn't matter. There is a reason the game opens up asking for people to not stream it or post a playthrough up front, it's to "prevent spoilers" because the game wouldn't lose anything if it was a movie. So how is the movie? It's fine. It doesn't do anything that blew my mind, but it's not terrible either. Coming from the creator of Danganronpa I expected more. It's not broken, it isn't terrible, it just isn't special either, so I'd find it hard to recommend. If someone wanted to check out FMV games I'd point them to Contradiction! or The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker before I'd point them to Death Come True.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an easy mark for FMV games, but this one really disappointed me. All choices are binary. There is only one correct path through the game. Some choices aren't even choices; if you pick "wrong" you just need to pick again until you get it "right." The finale is a 20 minute exposition dump with almost no interactivity. This game has zero replay value. All I can say in its favor is that the actors are fine and the premise is mildly interesting. But overall the game is a slog to get through and you have to play it all in one go or it starts over. 1.5 out of 5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give Death Come True a thumb up, but unfortunately this interactive movie that barely qualifies as a game has been a disappointment. Read the summary at the end if you want a tl;dr.Let me explain. First of all the gameplay element is very light. Every scene in Death Come True (DCT) is acted out by real people in live action. The game is closer to a visual novel but in film form, than say interactive adventure games from Supermassive or Quantic Dreams like The Quarry and Heavy Rain where you can fully control the characters’ movements and is able to interact with multiple objects within a scene to trigger branching paths. However, what makes good visual novels a game is that choices are consequential and branching story paths and scenarios are distinctly different and have substantial length. This is not the case for DCT where one can finish under two hours, and it is more linear than it first appears to the player. The general gameplay flow goes you view one scene, at the end of it you make a choice among two or more actions (except the first scene serving as a tutorial where there’s only one choice). Where DCT falls short is that there is only one story scenario, you either pick the action that advances the story or pick from the rest of the actions which immediately results in a very brief dead end scene or an invalid choice where the protagonist goes “that’s wrong, pick from the other options”. Granted some of these dead ends can be rather humorous, but they are not enough to make up for the illusion of choice.Okay, so how does DCT fare as a film? In my opinion, a B movie. The story and premise is uninspired and the central ideas have been explored many times over past decades in much greater depth and sophistication. Those ideas were used quite shallowly in this game and without spoiling too much, I’d say this is a murder mystery crossing the Matrix minus the action, with gaming tropes like reloading a death, like in Re:zero. There are flashes of the quirkiness and ingenious absurdity from director Kazutaka Kodaka who created the Dangaronpa series, but the script is mostly mediocre and forgettable. The dialogue can be quite corny at times, like when you watch a live action adaption of an anime. Sometimes real people saying anime stuff just don’t work. Video quality is not very good either, the game being ~5gb and 1.5-2 hours long means you can expect Youtube 1080p quality with visual artifacts. Visual effects, music and sound, and the acting are not bad but nothing to write home about, aka mid. I feel like most of the budget went into hiring the actors, many of whom while not A listers are likely familiar faces to people who watch many Japanese films, TV shows and anime, like Chiaki Kuriyama from Battle Royale and Kill Bill, or Yuki Kaji who is primarily a voice actor with roles like Eren from Attack on Titan.In summary, what I liked:+ Recognisable cast.+ Ability to fast forward and rewind right from the start. Important because you can only have 1 save and you can’t do chapter select until you have 100% the game, meaning if you want to redo an early choice you have to start over.+ Extra footage, behind the scenes, blooper reel, like you would find on a movie DVD. Some of them are funnier and more interesting than the main story LOLWhat I didn’t like:- Lack of gameplay and meaningful choices.- Mediocre story and writing.- Short length.I bought it heavily discounted during a sale, and even then I find it debatable if it was worth my money.My score: 4.0/10

_childDocuments_.review: Since I got all the achievements for this game I'll try to leave a complete review.  I loved the female detective, I thought she was a great character and I wanted her to prevail, so I played this over and over to get all the scenes.  The gameplay mechanics were perfect for an FMV game.  It wasn't complex and didn't get in the way of the story.  As you played, you unlocked behind-the-scenes footage.  So once you finish the game, it's like having a movie on Blu-Ray with a bunch of extras that you can skim through to enjoy the experience more.  Very rewarding.  The good ending was very satisfying and it ends like a good Japanese movie.  Made me want to see more!Something I really liked about this game is that you often have to fail and end the game to move forward.  You can't play a 'perfect' game.  Dying is a part of it.  A lot of FMV games, when you die, you think you failed and you just have to try again, and not die, and that can get tedious.  When you realize that dying in this game means you're progressing, you don't mind playing again and again.  There are just a handful of characters, and they all have great twists and turns to their story. This is one FMV game where, like a good movie, I'll be revisiting this every so often.  When I played it though, I was compelled to play it nonstop because it was so enthralling.  I think you'll like this a lot if you enjoy this genre!

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True" is a thrilling and innovative interactive movie that keeps you engaged from beginning to end. The unique premise of waking up in a hotel room with amnesia and having to piece together the story through various choices and interactions with characters creates an immersive experience that feels like you're a part of the action. The acting and production values are top-notch, and the twists and turns of the plot keep you guessing until the very end.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously loved this game. I think it's my new favourite. The OST is phenomenal, the story while mystery thriller fans might be able to figure out early what happened the process and how and why it all happened is very interesting still. The story while easy enough for detective fan veterans to solve was not cliche imo. There is only two ending's both are good choices to have for end game I'm glad they did, as both are bittersweet endings which I personally love those kinds. Fans of Danganronpa will see a LOT of familiar elements in this game. What's really cool i think they did was once you finish all of the death's you witnessed you get extra behind the scenes content videos to watch. What I especially loved about this that Danganronpa fans will be surprised by is there was zero gore to the game. While in my younger days I was all for the edgy bloody stuff, I'm really glad they stuck to the approach they did with this keeping things clean without sacrificing any of the overall feel. I really hope we get more games like this from the same people as I've played or watched almost every FMV out there and to me, this is THE BEST one. Acting 10/10Plot/Story 8.5/10Character development 7.5/10Soundtrack11/10 Overall10/10, cannot recommend enough!

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into it expecting it to be a fun little 2.2 hour or so movie experience with very little interactivity or branching paths, I think you'll enjoy this. The acting is great, cinematography is solid, and special effects are neat. The mystery could have been stronger, and Kodaka reused ideas that he'd already used in the Danganronpa series, and even more recently, a bit in Akudama Drive, but overall I found the experience to be interesting and engaging. The thing I was most disappointed in was how little Jiro Sato (the news host) was in the base game, but I think he has a bunch of videos in the extras I haven't checked out yet. I don't necessarily think this is worth buying for the full $15 price, especially because people are used to getting more bang for their buck out of a "game," but I just think of it like I bought a mid-priced DVD from wallmart that caught my eye, and I'm pretty satisfied with it. I will say that I'm not too supportive of how strongly they're enforcing copyright strikes on videos about the game though. I think everyone loses in this scenario, and people not being able to post videos or create discourse about this game probably has something to do with the fact that I've never heard about it until today, despite being a pretty big fan of Kodaka's work (with the exception of World's End Club)

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is an interactive movie. The premise is simple at first, it plays like a choose your own adventure; you make choices, you die, you wake up at the start of the game retaining your previous knowledge, and you go through the game making different choices. The the game takes a hard left turn and gets really weird. The story is wonderfully weird and twisted and there are some pretty great deaths, but the game is quite short. You can get the true ending and most, if not all, of the deaths in a single session. I would say the game is definitely worth it if you catch it on sale and you like weird FMV games, but it's harder to recommend at full price due to its brevity. I was thoroughly entertained the entire time, so it was worth it to me, but everyone has a different idea of how long a game should be as compared to the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Something about the "You wake up in a room" genre has always fascinated me. Perhaps it's how there's an instinctive need to find out what's happening that motivates you and the character to work in unison to learn out the truth. And coming from the creator of Danganronpa, this game has quite the pedigree in that genre. Sadly, that's most of the game's appeal. It's a rather small story all things considered, clocking in at about 2-3 hours of play and there's not much happening. No grand reveals about the world the game takes place in, no big conspiracy and only a few meaningful choices to make. On my first playthrough, the game felt much bigger than it really was because I was somehow avoiding all the random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths. And that's a shame because the random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths are great, and the game knows it because finding all the deaths is the way you earn achievements and bonus extras.But on the other hand, in this genre I would normally expect the random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths to be part of the interlocking mystery and they just aren't in this game; they are just completely random and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. More than one of the characters in the cover art only show up in one scene to kill you in what is basically a complete coincidence (to the extent of creating a plot hole once you know the big secret), almost like the story is trying to punish you for not following the aggressively linear story. But hey, it's the creator of Danganronpa, aggressively linear stories seem to be their thing.Definitely a recommend: The mystery is fairly interesting and the characters are fun to engage with for a while, but it's not a game changer and you'll probably never come back to it once you've beaten it.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this is more like a Novel moreso than some of the other FMV games out there. It's a very interesting story with twists and turns and lots of epic Shots (Great lighting and Photography/Directing) as well as clues that keep you guessing about things. I think anyone looking for a Murder/Mystery FMV Game is going to be pretty pleased with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: The Steam page lies a bit by saying it's the "first interactive film of its genra", because it really much is a simple FMV game.The gameplay is pretty simple : watch a video telling you what happens, make a choice, see the consequences. Sometimes your choice will lead you to your death. Sometimes it will further the plot. Sometimes, it will do both. Even though the gameplay is very simple, I really like the fact that the death routes are not synonymous with bad choices.The game does not tell you this, but you can bring the menu out by left clicking during a cinematic. There, you can rewind, pause, or skip forward the video.Each time you discover a new way to die, you will earn a "Death Medal" symbolizing the death. It's like an achievement menu. Earning Death Medals gives you access to extra videos.You have two main endings. If you play your cards right, you can see every scene and earn every Death Medal in two playthroughs. It takes about 2 hours to reach one of the two endings, and 4 hours 100% the game if you skip the scenes you already saw, not counting the extra videos unlocked by the Death Medals. Yeah, this game is really short.This game is an FMV, so talking about difficulty is a bit weird since you are bound to finish this type of games as long as you don't re-do the same mistakes. Even by this standard, this is a very easy FMV. I dodged like half of the bad ends simply because I have enough brain capacity to remember what worked or did not work a few minutes earlier. There are only two times when you have a time limit to make a choice, and they give you plenty of time to make up your mind. There are no real puzzles, and the few moments when you have to investigate, the game will tell you when your choice is wrong and ask you to choose something else.As I said earlier, the game is really short, and it shows in the story. The mystery around the main character's amnesia and presence in the hotel is solved pretty quickly, especially if you "play it right". You pretty much understand most of the truth after 1 hour, and the next hour is spent solving the main problem of the game and discovering the last missing pieces.I would have loved to see more of some characters. Maybe, this way, the game would be longer. You can see 7 characters on the game's poster (if you count the monster in the foreground), but only 4 of them have a real importance to the plot. The others are pretty much cameos. Getting to learn more about the 3 others would have been nice.Still, the story is the true strength of this game. Even though the story points are a bit "classic", the game uses a combination of those classic tropes and presents them to the player in a well written and articulated manner. Sometimes, you don't need to have something never seen before to write a good story. You just need to know how to write in an interesting way.The worldbuilding is alright. Nothing grandiose, but tight enough to be coherent and to not destroy your suspension of disbelief.Finally, your choices, good or bad, have an influence on the story. Well, not that your choices matter in the classic sense of the term : in the end, you are railroaded into a single course of actions, and the story doesn't change wildly depending on your choices. No, what I mean is that this game is a bit... meta. The story does take into account the fact that you can make "bad" choices. You'll understand once you play it.I can't tell you much more about the story, because it is such a short experience that you can easily spoil it. You'll have to believe in my words when I say I liked it ;)Another point where this game is pretty good. They really outdid themselves on this, if I compare this game to other FMV games I played before. Each character is really recognizable with nice costumes and "character design" ; they all have little something that makes me think about manga/anime characters. On some characters (especially Nene), you can see the influence of Danganronpa, the author's previous work. The SFX are nice. Contrarily to other FMVs where they have a nice interface and that's it, SFXs were used in the videos as well to enhance the visuals and accentuate the "abnormal" aspect of the situation and are pretty clean.There are also some really nice, pretty cinematic shot compositions. Instead of just filming someone talking in front of the camera, like some FMVs do, they took some filming techniques from movies and applied them. If you ignore the occasional choices you have to make, you really feel like you are watching a movie.Also, this game has one of my favorites Game Over screens.You can feel that this game is experimental. It's really short, the gameplay is barebones, and it uses classic tropes in its story. It's nothing grandiose, and it does not try to be more than it is. Still, it does what it does pretty well. I especially liked how the story was told to the player and the visuals.Because of its short nature and its quality, playing this game feels like playing a very polished proof of concept. It was a nice experience, I had fun, but I found that it ended too soon. If the studio makes another FMV game, I would love to check it out - juste make it a bit longer ;)If you want a nice story, are looking for something easy to play and/or are searching an interesting 2-hours movie, I think you will like this game.And the ending song is a banger \m/

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is just like any choose-your-own-adventure book, with the wrong decisions leading to imminent death. However each death awards you with collectible death medals which in turn unlocks behind-the-scenes videos. As for story, the beginning 30 minutes are really good at keeping your excited and tense. If anything the endings are the really enjoyable part of the game. Death Come True's real weakness is it's inflexibility to develop the story beyond the "correct" path. Many times I felt the story was going to make a twist but instead I was murdered in less than a minute. It's a real same since it leaves it's interesting side characters to appear for less than two minutes.[v]Verdict[/v]If you decided $16 is worth it to support a rookie game company by all means. _childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: really good story telling but short, actions don't affect the ending which is a bit disappointing but it does offer up alternative 2nd endings. _childDocuments_.review: Very short game.  Looks like it has lots of choices and branching story points, but at least 90% of the choices are meaningless and lead to the same path, near identical alternate results, or just plain out not letting you choose the choice and make you reselect the single right choice.  The game is definitely a linear story with the only true branch being the final choice at the end of the game.  Also the title screen shot is a lie.  Theres only 3 characters in this story.  The others appear for all of 30 seconds and are gone and done with, totally irrelevant.That said, I recommend this game/movie. It just felt like a concept demo and too short to be something awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that price-wise it is quite worthwhile. It is indeed more a little bit longer than a movie-length experience but not really as long as a full-fledged game. Nonetheless, It was very interesting to see the history and mystery unfold. Sadly due to the limited time and resources, and additional routes, I guess it could not get more complex than it was, but still was enjoyable. I think the format does work and would be quite interesting to see in a multi-part series where the history and mystery can unfold in more complex ways. The acting had a little bit of issues here and there, but I only had more issues with one scene in particular, the others were worthwhile.  Sadly if there was one I totally missed any Danganronpa easter eggs. Would love to hear an official "pupupupu" somewhere hinting at something that we know it is not the case. Even if it was only for the hype and a nod to the fanbase.

name: Cassette Beasts
detailed_description: Check out another turn-based title About the Game Adventure. Battle. Transform. Collect awesome monsters to use during turn-based battles in this open-world RPG. Combine any two monster forms using Cassette Beasts’ Fusion System to create unique and powerful new ones! Welcome to New Wirral , a remote island inhabited by strange creatures you’ve only dreamed of, nightmares you hopefully haven’t, and a cast of brave folks who use cassette tapes to transform for battle. To find a way home you’ll need to explore every inch of the island, and record monsters to your trusty cassette tapes to gain their abilities! Transform into monsters...using retro cassette tapes?! Faced with the constant threat of monster attacks, the residents of Harbourtown, New Wirral choose to fight fire with fire. Record a monster to tape, then play it back to take on its form for battle! Fuse monster forms! Getting close to your companion has benefits–while transformed you can combine your strengths to gain the upper hand in battle! Any two monster forms can be fused to produce unique, fully-animated new fusion forms. Explore a rich open world Certain monster abilities can be used in human form. You’ll need these to help you get around, solve puzzles, and locate dungeons. Glide, fly, swim, climb, dash, or turn magnetic! Take on the Gauntlet – a never-ending battle mode where you’ll face fearsome enemies for precious material and glory! Travel alongside a diverse cast of human companions Never fight alone! Form bonds, spend time together, and help your selected partner complete personal goals to become a better team. The strength of your relationship determines how well you’re able to fuse! Master a deep battle system Take advantage of elemental chemistry to apply extra buffs or debuffs alongside your attack, or even alter your opponent’s elemental type! Play with Friends Team up with a friend in local multiplayer to explore, transform, and fight together! Party up with Online Multiplayer to trade monster tapes, challenge your friends to 1v1 battles, and team up to take on powerful Rogue Fusion beasts for great rewards!

_childDocuments_.review: The creature collector genre feels like a tough place to develop a game with Pokemon being the massive behemoth that it is. Hard to make anything without somebody just saying "You're just copying Pokemon!!"It's so great to see devs exploring this genre more, and doing it very well at that! Cassette Beasts is easily one of the best creature collectors I've ever played, and I'm including mainline Pokemon games in that. Story, mechanics, creature design, humor, graphics, everything is just top notch. And the soundtrack is just stellar. This is such an easy recommend to fans of the genre and anyone interested in something that feels fresh but also scratches a nostalgic itch at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring the world is fun, the creatures are (mostly) well designed with fun names, the story is heartfelt and the music might be considered good by people with other taste than me.The combat isn't half bad until you figure out how to abuse the mechanics. Then it gets completely boring and unsatisfying to play.Also this game is lacking essential QoL-Features like sorting stickers (the abilities you can assign) is very barebone (for example you can't sort by their affixes), you can sort the bestiary but not explicitly look up creatures in it and such things.The hassling with the stickers is especially tedious and time consuming if you want to try out different strategies multiple times.If the keybinding in the menu were consistent that would've been also nice. (Pressing 'enter' at save doesn't save ,it merely closes the menu)It only crashed once but at a very unopportune moment.And worst of all: One creature that is inspired by a salamander is referred to as a lizard even though they're amphibians. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts: it's high time we dispel the notion that it's merely a Pokémon clone. Developed by Bytten Studio, this game offers a fresh and exhilarating take on the monster taming genre that stands tall on its own merits. Here, we'll dive into what makes Cassette Beasts so unique and why it's a complete masterpiece.A Unique Twist on Monster Taming:At first glance, some may draw parallels between Cassette Beasts and the Pokémon franchise. After all, both involve capturing and battling creatures, but Cassette Beasts distinguishes itself with its innovative "cassette" mechanic. Unlike Pokémon, where you simply capture creatures, in Cassette Beasts, you capture abilities and splice them together to create your own unique monster hybrids. This adds a layer of strategy and creativity that sets it apart from the traditional monster taming formula.A Riveting and Fast-Paced Story:One of Cassette Beasts' most outstanding features is its gripping storyline. From the moment you step into this pixel-art world, you'll find yourself engrossed in a narrative that unfolds at a breakneck pace. The plot is full of unexpected twists, complex characters, and thought-provoking themes that keep you invested from start to finish. It's not just about capturing monsters; it's about uncovering the mysteries of the world and your character's place in it.Challenge for the Experienced Gamer:Cassette Beasts doesn't hold your hand. It offers a refreshing challenge for those seeking a more demanding gaming experience. Battles are strategic and require careful planning. The variety of cassette combinations and the dynamic AI make each encounter a thrilling puzzle to solve. It's a game that rewards skill and strategy, keeping even seasoned gamers on their toes.Visually Stunning Graphics:The game's pixel-art style is a work of art in itself. The attention to detail in every environment, creature design, and character is astounding. Cassette Beasts manages to evoke a sense of nostalgia while still pushing the boundaries of what pixel art can achieve. It's a visual treat that enhances the overall immersion in the game.A Masterpiece in the Monster Taming Genre:In summary, Cassette Beasts is nothing short of a masterpiece in the monster taming genre. It successfully distances itself from the Pokémon comparisons with its innovative mechanics, and it offers a captivating story, challenging gameplay, and stunning visuals that set a new standard for the genre.While Pokémon may have laid the foundation for monster taming games, Cassette Beasts takes bold steps in its own direction. Bytten Studio's creation deserves recognition for its dedication to delivering an unforgettable gaming experience that stands tall on its own. Cassette Beasts is more than a clone; it's a genre-defining title that has undoubtedly earned its place among gaming greats.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recomend this game, but there are just so many little amateurish mistakes in this game.- moves don't tell you if they can be equipped to a specific monster or not until you open the three sub menus to equip it.- game has box stacking to reach areas as a mechanic, but the boxes have weird physics and sometimes your character chucks them up on a cliff so you cant retrieve them- If you swap from a low health monster the game doesn't remember this and will spawn you in as that low health monster in the next fight.- No tool tips for abilities or status effects so you need the wiki open to know what things do if you don't remember from the first time you saw them.- Flee is easy to accidentally hit, with no confirmation pop up so you can often just flee from fights accidentally. Happens very often when your trying to capture a monster since the buttons are right next to each other. The one time you REALLY DO NOT WANT TO FLEE..It's death by a thousand paper cuts. None of these are game breaking on their own, but there are just so many of them that it slows the game down. I really hope they do a quality of life update so I can recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts to me is the perfect Pokemon game, but it feels unfair to call it that since the game ends up sharing so little with Pokemon by the end besides the loose idea of "catching monsters" to use later.  Be warned if you are looking for more Pokemon exactly as you know it this game will not be for you, but if you want to try something wholly new with the genre give Cassette Beasts a try!If you just are looking for a random opinion I highly recommend this game without caveat, but if you want a break down of how this game differs from Pokemon games I will be spoiling most of the games mechanics while trying not to touch any story or specific secret spoilers.  This game has a lot in it, but it is good at giving you the information concisely when it is relevant (it doesn't all seem this overwhelming in game).  I am sure I will be forgetting to mention some mechanics here, but these are what I found to be most relevant to playing the game.If you are curious how the game differs from Pokemon it has a lot of the fat stripped from it replacing it with wholly new mechanics and ideas.  Gone are the random differences in individual mons (for the most part).  No more IVs, EVs, Natures, or Abilities. Any mon you catch will start the same as any other of the same species.  Similarly levels of individual mons are removed for the most part.  In its place is a mechanic of "stars" (basically levels), where each star grants a new move and at 5 stars the mon can evolve if possible.  Stats are only changed on evolution rather than on star gain so there will never be a need to grind up newly caught mons to try to match the rest of your team.  The leveling up system is not gone entirely though, instead being tied to the player instead, so a sense of progression and the ability to over level still exists.  If you want though you can change the way that other npcs level scales to the player in settings.  That might be one of the greatest strengths of the game, an absolutely fantastic UI with so many quality of life features.The game is choked full of great QOL of features:  you can see what abilities do while you use them, status changes and types are visible on the mon itself during combat, a very helpful tutorial message (can be turned off) pops up the 1st time a new effect happens, the type matchup chart can be pulled up in combat, healing items are replenishable for cheap but capped on how much you can hold, fast travel is unlocked from the start and has a hotkey, dialog animation and move speed are quick, the location of interesting events are marked on your map when an npc mentions them, moves can be removed and added on the fly (even switched between mons that can learn them).  There are so many impressive QOL that it is hard to remember them all.  I know I will struggle to go back to other games that lack them.The game isn't just refined Pokemon, it has new takes on some of the tropes of the genre.  The game has unique types, with some familiar ones from other monster training games.   The big change to typing though is the interactions.  There are no super effective/not effective moves, instead all interactions with types are more complicated then that, often giving a debuff/buff on interaction or rarely even changing the type entirely.  For instance a fire move on a plastic mon turns the plastic type to poison type. Another fire move on the now poison type will set it on fire giving it a damage over time effect for 3 turns.  The type changing element of the game is a core mechanic, every mon has a unique sprite for every other type it could be.  Shinys in this game are instead one of these type changed mons, equipped with unique movepool as well as a different type from what is normally found.  The way moves are learned is also a big departure.  All moves can be removed from any mon and added to any other mon that is compatible.  There are also passive moves which function in the way abilities do in Pokemon.  If you miss grinding out catching Pokemon for better stats the closest equivalent for that here is a chance for moves to have extra (generally not very significant, or a restriction on using to its fullest) effects on them.  Any time you gain a new move you have a chance to have an added effect on it, with shinys having a boosted chance.  Finally another departure is that the game focuses exclusively on double battles, as well as fusing together of two mons to create a temporary stronger mon.There will of course be a lot of comparisons to Pokemon, but the game stands on its own in many ways as well.  The game's focus is on traversing an open world while gaining abilities to solve puzzles and unlock more of the world.  There are many boss battles, separate from trainer battles, quests, and environmental puzzles throughout the world.  There is no universal currency, instead the game has a theme of recycling and raw materials are used in place of a currency.  Items are only obtainable with the relevant material and more of it can be found through breaking down similar items, battling monsters, finding chests, or completing quests.  Perhaps the last big selling point is the "romance system".  As the game focuses exclusively around double battles you will spend the game with one of several partners growing closer with them as the game progresses.Ultimately this game won't be for everyone.  I personally love the mon designs and art direction, but I know for some people the differences between this and Pokemon's style will be an instant deal breaker.  Additionally you aren't really catching mons, but rather transforming into them.  In practice this changes very little but I know weirds out some people. The game focuses more on story than the original Pokemon did which will be a mixed bag for some people.  To me this is a game that takes the mechanics of Pokemon, refines it to perfection, and then creates a world out of it that the creators seemed to have truly put a lot of love into.  Despite all of my comparisons to Pokemon I think this is a game that stands on its own apart from it, and if anything is helped by comparing the two.  I would highly recommend giving this a try if you have ever hoped Game Freak would try new things or even if you just like the style and tone of the game.  It is a perfect Steam Deck game and should be coming to Switch in late may if you would prefer to play this handheld.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest take on a non-Pokémon Monster RPG I've ever played and it's not even close. To those who play that series but don't know what to expect from this, it's basically a double-battle focused RPG where you and a partner (who you also control) use monsters to fight wild monsters, other "trainers", and large boss fights.This game nails:-Its characterization and writing, which ranges from sad and relatable to hilarious and uplifting (and it's not afraid to talk about more adult themes)-Its gameplay, where it dips into a vast pool of Passive Equippable moves that you can stack on top of each other to produce tremendous and wild results-Its Type Chart, that blends pure advantages with status conditions and stat boosts to make Typing always feel worth its effort in learning-Its soundtrack, which is LOADED with strong combat music and great emotional gravitas (although the overworld themes are a little bland by comparison, I must admit)-Its world design, which heavily emphasizes PLATFORMING and puzzle solving, but none of it is difficult to learn and by catching new Beasts you get more abilities to traverse where you areSo if any of the above sounds remotely appealing, get this game. GET IT. You will not regret it at all.My only regret is this was gifted to me! I'd have bought it for myself had I had more money at the time... but I'm all in on any future paid DLC, because this game and its studio more than earned every penny they can get.10/10 would fuse again.

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, this is really good. The art is great, fusion is a perfect mechanic, I love the music, I love the writing, and it outperforms Pokémon all the time (I say this as someone with a lifelong obsession with Pokémon). Hence so many stars.On the other... it has problems. Mostly quality of life problems that should have been solved during user testing. And they're not that big a deal if you're playing the game once, only a few will come up, especially if you don't do the postgame. But if you love the game, and really want to engage properly, and get 100% achievements, they discourage that which is sad. It honestly feels like the game is fighting you sometimes... 1. Menuing: No easy way to see which types of beast learn which stickers. When adding stickers to tapes, your position in the list of stickers is randomized after clicking, which is disorienting and makes rescoping your beasts really tedious and difficult. Also, sorting only applies at the time of sorting. So if you sort alphabetically, and then get another sticker, that will be put at the bottom of the list instead of alphabetically, unless you click sort again /every time you unequip a sticker/. This is a huge problem because you always want to be rescoping your beasts and this means you're scrolling for so long to do this basic aspect of gameplay! It discourages builds and making cool beasts which is really sad. 2. Saving: If you reset to use a ritual candle, a priceless item you would be a fool not to savescum (see currency balance and cruel and unusual achievements section below), they make you wait 4 real world minutes before anything spawns again. This is vindictive, especially when considering the achievements list. Once you've bought a game, you should be able to "cheat" if you want. You paid for it.3. Currency balance: Fused material is immensely scarce and valuable, to a mean and stingy extent. For example, you only get 75 fused material for 100%ing EVERY CASETTE BEAST TYPE IN THE GAME. That's 1.5 ritual candles, for doing something many could consider definitively "completing" the game. After spending 0 fused material for the entire game (which involved never upgrading my character) I had 100 after completing the main game. So, 2 candles. And after that they dry up. For doing long "raid boss" equivalents you get... 1. So that's how you farm it. 1 by 1. Meanwhile all other currencies like wood accumulate in massive quantities you couldn't spend even if you tried, with no way to convert them to the only useful currency. To make this even worse, the same currency you need for these candles (which are obligatory to 100%) is the one used to upgrade your character. So if you want to 100% achievements, something only possible with several candles, you can't upgrade your character once or you're wasting resources that will literally take hours to grind to get back.4. Physics: Physics in this game is nasty. You get caught on corners, the obligatory platforming segments (especially the one with Alice) are very frustrating, where endlessly respawning enemies keep knocking you off platforms... doesn't help that stamina is lower than I would like, even in the postgame. Honestly, this is probably Godot's fault, but it goes to show that the engine has limitations. Also, your partner who follows you everywhere haws a hitbox, so you keep bashing into them and they keep knocking cubes off buttons which is very frustrating. 5. Text speed: Text speed is slow, and there are strange pauses in loading text when characters are talking (within the same text box onscreen) that make it unclear when the text is going to end. I couldn't press to skip, because I kept accidentally pressing through dialogue options because the load speeds were so irregular and sometimes characters would say short things. I would like text speed options. Again, a minor complaint, but it would be nice...6. Cruel and unusual achievements: See section 2 and 3 for why these are cruel and unusual, but honestly what a nasty grinding postgame to get 100%. Literally hours of grinding to get 1 of the item that gives you a chance, and if you use it, what do you get? Possibly not the thing you need, unless you save scum. But the game tries to thwart that at any turn. I can't imagine authentically getting an astral traffikrab (hyperspecific achievement) without savescumming, but even with that the game is fighting you and giving you "time out" wait periods between resets like you are a misbehaving child.tl;dr: good game, but some fixable flaws make it frustrating at times, and the nastiest endgame grind I've ever encountered

_childDocuments_.review: When I play a game for 20 hours in two days, usually it gets a positive review. So don't be surprised when I give this game an absolutely glowing review while I'm still honeymooning with it. I'll probably write a more in-depth review later that only I will really read, but the main thrust of this is me being baffled that I'm the first one on my whole steam list to have played this. What's wrong with you people? College changed you.I don't usually push out review like this, but this game is 50% off at time of writing and I felt like I was going to try the game and refund it if I bounced off of it. Instead, yesterday was a blur where I did nothing but play this game and occasionally rose to eat and drink.Why should you play cassette beasts?Cassette beasts is like if Digimon loved you back. Somehow basically every gripe I have with other mon-games has been addressed. And that's hard to lead with because Cassette Beasts isn't a subtweet of a game, it's something that clearly takes inspiration and lessons from other mongames and then takes that ball straight to the net. This game was not meant to carve out a niche like Temtem or made to be bitter and edgy while eating nintendo's lunch like Palworld. It stands alone as something unique and special, a lighthouse of a game in between oceans of disappointment.-Simplistic type matchups that lead to the game turning into rock-paper-scissors? Not in Cassette beasts baby, while there are type match-ups they lead to unique and in-depth interactions that tip the battle in your favor but don't guarantee a win. It pays to learn them and they can be part of chipping away at tough fights, but they aren't the major deciding factor for most fights, rather just a little bag of chips that comes with the meal.-Weird leveling system that makes you stick with like 4 mons and leave the rest of them in the dust? Don't worry about it. The game uses a system that makes even the most route-1 pidgey-lookin' mon that you have in your box at least passable in a fight. The evolution system is a bit weird but it's easy to get used to and the way it's set up leads more to having a big book full of mons that you can assemble different parties out of rather than a few staples that you always use. Also because the evolution system doesn't take multiple hour grinds for every mon, I ended up clearing the finish with around 80% of the mons collected. Even if they will be in my pack forever.-Static environments and boxed in quests? Try schmoving around an enormous 3-d world with quests you can tackle in any order you like. The game gives you the ability to bullet-dash very early on and with the physics engine at play you can do really wacky stuff with it. I think I've already sequence-broken a few times on accident based on some level gaps.-Divides its attention better than its contemporaries. Breaks the mold from pokemon more and isn't as hobbled by random jutting MMO aspects. Plus, the artstyle is better. Yes, I am bitter.-Parting from other mongames that leave story swinging in the breeze, Cassette Beasts' video-gamey plot is made very flavorful by the many different fun characters and interesting small twists in its structure, along with one or two legitimate little beats that make the story more than just a glorified gym leader hunt. Plus, the undertale-style shirt-tearing ending, while a little clumsy, did succeed in making a sentimental little bozo like myself get misty-eyed. If I had it my way they'd inject a couple more decibels into the ending because it's such a showstopper.Also, the game has a bunch of really cool other stuff.-Companion characters ahoy! So far I like all of them but one. Meredith you are too much of a drip and I have already pledged my heart and soul to Kaleigh. Even if her name is spelled like that. She's irish, okay? It's fine. This is fine. It's fine.-The way the game uses music and its artstyle are amazing. The first time I played I spent a while just hanging out in the Harbourtown cafe listening to the amazing vocal performances.-Just oodles and oodles of charm. I love that the healing item is a pencil you use to re-spool  your tape, I love the stupid pun names that some of the mons have, I like that you can just camp in an area where you're grinding or hunting for a bootleg (shiny, kinda), I like the fact that the "team rocket"-like in this game is actually just- well it's really good but I won't spoil it here, I like the way the vocals for the soundtrack come in when you fuse- it really feels like they added a bunch of small details that nobody would have even thought to ask for.It adds up to create the same wonder and exploration that I felt when I first played pokemon all those years ago. To paraphrase youtuber and cool-sounding guy Steak Bentley, "Less de-constructive and more re-constructive. Bringing back the magic, but a little more honest, because you're a grown-up now."In leiu of a rating, that's just my pitch for why you should play Cassette Beasts. If you feel let down by any of the larger mongames (pokemon, digimon, etc etc) or even if you love the genre and can feel how tight the constraints can feel on it, then you really owe it to yourself to give Cassette beasts a whirl. It is abundantly clear that stem to stern this game is built with love for its genre and a sincere desire to make a worthy successor to the ailing old throne of Mr. Pikachu himself. Fantastique.Edit: I finished the game, came back to do some more undisclosed edits, and give this game a 9/10. Yeah, hoss, get it in your steam library. Grab a copy for you and that one neice you don't really talk to but could use a fun, mostly wholesome game that takes the bad in the world seriously. Get it burned on a series of 14.35 discs and seal them in your wall so that it will survive the great gloaming. Get it tattooed on your firstborn child's head in a language they don't understand so one day a wise old shaman will caress his finger across the scalp of your now-adult progeny and catch a Springheel. Or just play it, that works too.But, one caveat.If you are my sister, don't buy it. Look I'm not good at christmas gifts okay

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised the heck out of me with the demo (now unavailable) so much so that it's an easy day 1 purchase for me, and I played it straight to finish, which I rarely do now with games as an adult, maybe playing it on the Steam Deck helps hah.The combat is turn-based and is interesting, you mostly have a partner with you and you can change the type of beasts that both characters could become leading to a dynamic mix-and-match strategies. Each cassette that holds the beast forms have a set of stickers, those are the aggressive, passive and support moves that the character could use and each stickers have their own rarity with additional effects on them, leading to the possibility of creating some very interesting (even borderline unfair for the enemies) strategies. Main feature of this game is the fusion mechanic which combines both beasts that your character and your partner currently equipped into 1 mixed beast, combining both their stickers move pool and stats. Love every time this happens as the current soundtrack switches to vocal version and it just fills me with that feeling of "LETS GOOOOOO".Enemies of various types like beasts, bosses and other characters can be very challenging and requires you to switch and try other strategies, especially the bosses and some character fights when they also fused with their partners. The bosses are some of the most unique designed characters I've seen especially when you first see them in your fight.This the only game where I feel like I want to go out and record the bootlegs version of the beasts, they're like shinies in Pokemon but with a different type than their original version with a look that matches that new type, this leads to creating more interesting combat strategies and there are mechanics that makes the bootleg hunting/grinding easier.There are end-game contents and even new game+ contents and gives you the ability to turn on some challenges like a cassette is permanently destroyed if it gets defeated and randomizing all of the beast locations.All and all I completely love this game and I highly recommend people to at least give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: There is absolutely some initial clunk, but this game takes wild and unexpected swings for something that could've just stuck the formula and been a perfectly normal pokemonlike.There's Shin Megami Tensei and Digimon DNA mixed in. There's a working physics engine. There's a vocal version of seemingly every song in the soundtrack. There's surprisingly deep lore. You can fuse every gad dang pokemon into every other gad dang pokemon. I don't... I don't actually know why they did that. That's a monumental amount of design work for a payoff that the average player is barely conscious of. And the whole game is like that.Cassette Beasts is casual and cozy. It's got heaps of sidequests, Legend Of Zelda style puzzles, and mons to catch. Character customization is weirdly deep, and you can peel moves off of mons and put them on other compatible mons, and this includes passives and specials. The move list is also bonkers wide, and a *lot* of them aren't just +damage +type stuff. Every tenth move I see is metagame defining in its potential. Not to mention type interactions aren't just plus damage. There's an unhinged number of them, all with highly specific effects, and STAB bonuses don't seem to be much of a thing, so you can aim for really wide coverage with your movepools.Or you can leave move slots open, because some moves scale their effects based on the number of open slots.It's good.Now, on the downside, the game does start a little slow. Before you've gotten a few mons and acclimated to the way combat works and gotten some traversal abilities, map exploration feels clunky. This improves, but you have to be willing to get over the initial hump. Also, the game's cozy tone is not always... completely cozy. There is *stuff* going on in the metaplot that is extremely compelling, but less nice than you'd expect from the genre.Ultimately, I'd say Cassette Beasts feels like a weird DS monster catcher rpg that never quite took off, but developed a strong cult following ten years after launch. If you like specifically that type of game, you're going to have a *phenomenal* time here. If you're just looking for a pokemonlike, this is still a good one, but be prepared to spend the first few hours getting acclimated.Edit: Rolled credits. Holy crap this was made by like three people, publisher and voice cast excluded. Also Yuri Lownethal is a voice in this? What a weird gem of a game. Definitely a bit neither-fish-nor-fowl with its pokemon color palette and SMT tone, but it takes some wild swings and hits more than it misses. Strong recommend if you like monster catchers and you're looking for something cozy.
