_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is cute. Cassette Beasts is one of those cute RPGs and if that’s what you’re looking for, you probably won’t be disappointed- but I can’t say why the “probably” without spoiling the ending.The concept rests on you as the main character being isekai’d to a new, very small world- but in a subversion of the trope, nearly everyone and everything on this new world has been isekai’d there. And, in typical fashion, your main quest is to leave; but it’s not long before you find out that the rules of physics here don’t quite apply, which is how you wind up monster collecting and transforming using Cassette Beasts.I’m not good at video games, and guaranteed some Pokemaniac would know the optimization of it all better, but for the most part: the designs are fun, the branching paths for remastering (evolution) are easy to find and understand, and most monsters have some level of merit to using in battle, at least for a casual playthrough, so you can really play around with making a team out of designs you like rather than optimization.Speaking of optimization of team and strategy, one of the nice things that this game lets you do if change the AI difficulty and the level scaling right from the get go; I chose to leave them be, as I overall thought they presented a good challenge, but as I said before, I’m not good at video games, so I didn’t want it harder or easier. Still, it sometimes slaps you in the face; I mean the basic plotline at around level 65, and in doing post game, I almost immediately got a new quest, only to be slapped in the face by a level 100 boss. And it wasn’t the only one. (The level scaling is nice in regards to the other mini bosses and bosses you face, though.)Speaking of the monsters and gameplay, finding bootlegs (shinies) is not horrible in this game. Upon its completion I had around two dozen. The chance in a normal encounter is 1/1000, but the post game is far more helpful, giving you an item that makes a bootleg a guaranteed encounter (though what kind specifically is only partially guaranteed; getting exactly what you're looking for takes work in quitting and reopening the game). For a while even this was frustrating, since the item is only one use and it costs 50 of another item to farm, but in the end, not horrible. The fun thing about bootlegs is, unlike shiny pokemon, bootlegs are more than just a special color; they actually change the element of the monster from its typical state for a bit of fun!The battling system is mostly simple, but can get complicated as times; there are so many status conditions (and elemental internations that cause status conditions) that, after 70 hours of gameplay, I still don’t remember them all. But the setup makes it far from impossible to win despite this. One of the largest issues I have is the map; the characters are 2d on a 3d map stylized to look 2d artistically. I enjoy the art the the cheesy 80s/90s getups, but sometimes moving about the maps can be a pain; it’ll turn at sometimes unexpected times and has more than once messed up my direction, and there are places you can get… Stuck isn’t the right word, but not not-stuck. At my 8GB of RAM speed (not high, but you don’t need much to run this game) the map would also load for me if I went from one side to the other, in basically the same longitudinal position, which includes of the middle of the main town and in the middle of a puzzle that requires running back and forth so I got it over, and over, and over, and over again. Now that I don’t need to run in the same places 500 times it’s not so bad, but that part was grating- especially with enemies chasing you into encounters and disrupting you. Let me do the damn puzzle!One thing that befuddles me is that I can be roaming the map at level 105 and lvl 1 enemies are still trying to chase me for a showdown. They do get in the way sometimes. Fast travel is useful, but feels inconsistently placed sometimes.Throughout the game, you’ll get six partners that tag along with you (you can choose who one at a time and swap whenever), and five of those six partners are romanceable (the sixth one is not for a VERY GOOD REASON, but I’ll leave that out of this portion). It’s very much a side item to the game and mostly for the achievement, but all relationships have hearts- which is odd, because hearts are about the overall relationship level, not the romance level. You have the option to begin romancing any of those characters at their respective five-heart cutscenes, and you can have each character romanceable at the same time, but can only be in a solid relationship with one. Fortunately, there’s no damage to friendship if you don’t choose romance options at any time. The conversations are fun, and you get either little snippets or dialogue when you rest. The snippets repeat randomly and are based on your relationship level with someone. Dialogue is unique, only occurs once, is a great way to learn about characters and feel a passage of time in the game, and has new dialogue based on different plot points in the game. Unfortunately in the post game, these eventually wear out, and the post game can be far longer than the main game. It just felt stale after a time.There are 123 achievements and they’re all doable. Most are storyline related and the rest are not difficult. The longest I spent on one that wasn’t story related was 4 hours, and that was just due to awful, awful rng luck (trying to get a Glitter bootleg). 100%ing this game is not bad. A couple of them (catching all monsters and getting them all to five stars) can be cheated a bit with the DLC, since “doing them all” is hardcoded by number, so I got the achievements before I did thanks to the DLC (the DLC is fun by the way, if a bit odd in its initial mechanic, I’d say worth the money).(Warning for ending and postgame spoilers.)My biggest issue with the postgame is that- unless I’m stupid- it’s not really explained where the orb fusions are coming from or what their purpose is. Me being stupid is a distinct possibility, though.And now the ending, the sore spot for many: the second you arrive on New Wirral, your goal is to leave. And that’s what the end of the plotline is: leaving. I, like many others, expected the moment where everyone decides to stay. And then, when that didn’t happen, I waited for the moment after the cutscenes where they somehow found a way back.It doesn’t happen. In the end, your friends say goodbye, if you had a romance it breaks, and you all leave on good terms, never to see one another again. If you play after, in the postgame, you’re teleported to the moment before you make this decision, and can carry on in New Wirral (you can start the post game without doing this anyway, from what I understand). This decisions was controversial, to say the least. I saw people disappointed with it, saying it was against the spirit of the game, and I felt the same- until I realized it was entirely wrong. Sometimes plans change or life throws you obstacles. Sometimes you’ll make unlikely friends that will help you through it. But the plan was always to go back home, to friends and family and loved ones; you either don’t see your New Wirral friends again- and they all want to leave- or you don’t go back to your friends and family. You can’t ask them to stay for you. Not everyone or everything is meant to stay in our lives, but that doesn’t mean we don’t grow because of it, that we aren’t affected by it, or that it’s not worth treasuring.Overall, this game is a solid 8.5/10, it was fun, and I’ll miss it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play at times can be a blast but it can also get pretty chaotic. First and foremost the world is quite tiny for an open-world type. The  in-game music varies from awesomely original to filler I've heard in every other small indie game of varying type. Status effects are chaotic, to an insane degree(there are 98 according to the wiki). The game will at times explain them but when suddenly there's a dozen little indicators in battle it's not easy to follow and the game is so new it's not viable to find a competent guide to provide some much needed in-depth explaining. The scaling is confusing too, how is it that I trampled a trainer 5 levels above me but am obliterated by something 2 levels below? there's not much that's intuitive to the in depth battle mechanics and the learning curve is STEEP. That being said if you like a lot of chaos maybe this game is more your speed than it is mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. Its one of the best monster catching pokemon-esque games that doesn't image itself as a direct pokemon clone. What I love most about the game are the quality of life features. When you make a game using gameplay already set in stone, like turn based rpg elements, you don't want to keep the terrible qualities that come with them that other indie devs don't seem to understand.For example, cassette beasts allows;-your entire party to gain exp (even when they're knocked out)-levels are based on your player character's, so all your monsters share the same level.-you can't one shot this game's version of shinies-you can adjust difficulty and level scaling to let grinding or main gameplay to be less annoying-your moves are able to be swapped in and out to other monstersThe only problems I have with the game is mostly to the menus. Giving multiple level up items to your characters or monsters takes too long when you can only give them one at a time. Or how there isn't a system or menu to know what moves each monsters are allowed to have instead of relying on hope. The story also had problems that is prevalent in other trapped in new world need to return home, but I won't spoil the obvious. The notice board grind to complete 100 quests was also mind numbing on the way to 100% the game, but overall Cassette Beasts was the most fun I had 100%ing a monster catching game like this. Overall 9/10 for a clean experience. Fountess gang rise up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a cool game. _childDocuments_.review: Traveling around the map is needlessly tedious and restrictive making going anywhere that isn't a warp a chore to get to. combat is very slow and some battle feel like a slog even with a elemental advantage a good handful of the later fights are not fun because of how long they take. it does have it moments though, it feels very satisfying to do a strong set up and blast through a team or even knock out a trainer before they can even get to their next cassette. Multiplayer is disappointingly half baked with the only thing you can do with another player is rouge fusion battles. other than that you can only see them on the overworld. Most of the creature designs are good and the moves potentially having special effects is cool and can completely turn a fight around. it's a very unique idea that is executed very well but the combat left a lot to be desired as i mentioned. I can see the appeal with the game but i find it very mediocre for the most part. if you're looking for a creature collector i would try something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a highly enjoyable Pokémon-style game with some extremely fun mechanics such as the monster fusion system that can result in some seriously goofy combinations. I was not expecting it to be as good as it is and had fun with some of the jokes the game has. The sticker system allows for moveset customization that's limited solely by what you have in stock and you can freely modify your Cassette Beasts to enhance your strategies or strengthen the individual beast. Cassette Beasts rewards and encourages creativity and it's a game I plan on keeping installed for awhile so that I can beat up wild Fusion monsters whenever I feel like it (I really enjoy seeing all these monster combos).
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Continuing the train of great reviews,This game is awesome. if you are looking for something to scratch that pokemon itch while being new. This is it! i have played Temtem, Nexomon, Cronomon, etc. and been looking for something like this for a long time, while those entries are excellent, few scratch the whimsy and wonder of catching new cassette beasts like this one! YES they evolve, DO NOT look up their evolved forms, as each is honestly such a wonderful and cool surprise! Really took the best elements of pokemon and Digimon here. after a few hours i can solidly say the experience stays the same throughout. the open world idea combined with powers by catching certain cassette beasts is awesome and is a solid throw back to metroidvanias which benefit HEAVILY from this genre when combined.  The battles require technical planning, and elemental advantages have a twist that really leans into using elements to win. the boss fights? I wont get into those because they are so neat but i appreciate the weirdness here too! it pays off as the bosses all feel mechanically and thematically different.In short, please try this out. either on Xbox game pass or here. you will not be disappointed with the charm, atmosphere, and technical game play of this title!

_childDocuments_.review: This masterpiece of a game should honestly be about 10 dollars more then it is. There is so much content, so much diversity in the monster designs and ability combinations. The story especially the companions story arcs are very well done. Here are some pros and cons for people who are on the fence about buying this game.Pros-Good amount of monsters (120) (baby forms and evolved forms are well stated and all useable)-Good character customization-Companions are very diverse and likeable-Story is quite strong for the genre type-Traversing the map in the mid game is amazing-Bootleg (shiny) hunting is fun and extremely rewarding-Combat and Music are unforgettable and revolutionary.-Very rare that you will have moves similar to other people once you find the upgraded versions as they role with numerous random affixes.Cons-Traversing in the early game can feel like a slog until you get some of the abilities.-Swapping companions can be annoying because they take one of your monsters with them until you swap back (should be getting adjusted)-As of right now multiplayer is very limited ( Mainly local, remote share play, no battles or trading)-Sometimes hard to know what you should be doing next due to the vast amount of freedom the game gives you after the tutorial.-Unlocking fusion with some of the companions takes longer to unlock then I would like.-Will consume your lifeOverall solid game and I'd give it a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Pokemon?  Into action, adventure, grinding, and exploration?  Well, if you like any or all of that, plus an extra heap of nice music to go with it, this may be the game for you.+++Pros++++ The overall concept and most of the execution is great+ The game looks decent and the music fits it+ No crashes or bugs encountered so far+ Varied selection of monsters, stickers, and companions to customize your play+ Almost a casual game, but you can get yourself into trouble if you don't pay attention---Cons---- Would like a bit more variety with the music - each monster form has its own unique music since they are "taped"- At the outset the pacing seems a bit slow & grindy, as you have to repeatedly return to a rest spot to heal yourself; you can only carry a limited number of items that heal/repair your monsters/tapes, but not you - the number carried can be upgraded eventually though===Conclusion===While I haven't played any Pokemon games in over 20 years now, I doubt the formula has changed so much that my experience with it would be irrelevant.  This game is cut from a similar cloth, but gives you more freedom to play around with your monsters.Monsters can evolve after awhile, but you also have the ability to customize them via the use of stickers that you apply to the cassette tapes - the higher their level, the more sticker slots they have.  Then, you also have the ability to temporarily fuse you and your companion's equipped monsters into a unique monster - prior to playing, I thought you could permanently fuse two monsters to create a new one that joins your party, but that isn't the case.  Too bad, as I would have loved a breeding/fusion system that allowed for that, but oh well.I wasn't sure what my reaction to this game would be before playing, but I'm pleasantly surprised.  There are a few things I'd like to see done differently, but overall it is quite fun.  Oh, and it plays flawlessly on the Steam Deck, so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those magical games that appear once in a long while. I found it by chance and tried the demo, and on the very first few minutes I was already very interested on it. And then I learned a bit more about the setting, and then the first vocal track dropped.... And I fell in love with the game immediately. And the more I play the game, and unlock new stuff to do, it gets better and better.I won't spoil anything of the story, nor the setting. All I can say is that it has such a great mood to it, and some unexpected contrasts at some points!Gameplay-wise, it's not just a Pokémon-like game. It has a lot of unique twists to the formula, and also has some cool mechanics probably inspired by other games as well. Like Persona's Social Links, essentially you can get closer to your NPC partners and know them better as time goes, also making your Fusion stronger.This game does so many things great that a lot of monster collecting games should do as well. The difficulty is very customizable. And I'm not saying like the usual "make the game nuzlock mode". I mean you can actually make the AI more challenging, which I love it.No random encounters by walking in grass a few steps. You can actually see the monsters in the world. This should be a staple in every monster collecting game, in my opinion.tl;dr, This is one of the best monster collecting RPGs I've ever played, even with my little play time it's easy to tell that. Fantastic soundtrack; great mechanics; not just another Pokémon-like; very cool story and setting that keeps me interested of learning more, side-quests, an interesting open world that doesn't feel like it's constantly railroading you, and many more.I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: i first heard of this game by watching alpharad gold play it, thought the artstyle was super appealing and immediately bought it after watching that video, something i have never done before after watching a let's play. being a fan of pokemon my whole life, i was really drawn to this game, moreso than any other monster collectors besides pokemon (and maybe yo-kai watch). i'll list what i think are some really strong parts of the game and some parts i think are a bit weak (while trying to spoil as little as possible). i played this game completely alone so i can't comment on the coop though.stuff i liked+ a lot of focus on human characters. i love the human characters in pokemon so this made me really happy to see.+ music is really good, none of the songs i actively dislike or got bored of. i couldn't find some of my favourites on youtube so i bought the ost just so i could go back to them any time i wanted+ as i said above, the artstyle appeals to me a lot, as well as the monster design. the fact that there are 14k+ animated sprites with just two full time developers is nuts (a vast majority of them do seem to have been procedurally generated but what can you do. it fooled me otherwise a couple times at least)+ the world feels massive, in a good way. in a similar way to how old pokemon games felt massive as a kid. new wirral feels as expansive as i thought unova and sinnoh were as a kid.+ the gameplay took me a bit of getting used to but i still really like it and there's tons of really cool saucy stuff you can pull off. sometimes i'd go into a fight underleveled but with a creative strategy and come out on top and it made me feel really proud for coming up with it, a feeling that i've only gotten from pokemon in the past.+ didn't mess with it too much since i don't like self inserting in rpgs but the character customizer gives like the perfect amount of options such that it doesn't feel too daunting. plus you can change anything at any time. ++++++++++++ the difficulty options are AWESOME. they're kind of tucked away but you should absolutely turn them up. scroll to the gameplay section of the settings tab. didn't feel the need to grind ever on the max setting and every battle was even. there is an order the game lays out certain tasks in, but on the max level scaling settings you can completely ignore it and it's so so so COOL.stuff i didn't really like (might be a bit nitpicky but i do think they're worth airing out)- the overworld puzzles have some janky physics which can be frustrating at times. sometimes i felt like i was supposed to use a moveable object as something to stand on top of but whenever i did the cube would convulse. multiple times during my playthrough movable cubes flipped over or sent me flying, which just became an annoyance whenever it happened. i'm sure these issues could absolutely be fixed in a patch, i hope this part of the review ages poorly.- my game crashed once on an older build, but given the fact that this happened to me only one time and the game has since received new patches, it is likely that they fixed whatever caused me to crash.- i found one of the partner's quests really frustrating, because you're locked out of using a core gameplay mechanic with them until pretty late into the game, especially . it's not the end of the world, it just means that using this specific partner is the hardest to use, so i'd suggest not using  unless it's to work through their quest.+ these issues do not retract from all the positive things to be said about the game, so i really hope this doesn't come across that way.overall for its price i think this game is a steal. every year or so i run into an indie game that knocks my socks off, and this is the most recent one to do so (it's also the first pokemon-like to do so too). i 100% recommend this game to anyone who likes pokemon or just any kind of jrpg. i'm writing this before i play the dlc so i'll write a review for that too when i'm done it. you *can* access the dlc any time after you buy it but i intentionally avoided it so i could just focus this review on the base game. i also tried to avoid being too specific about gameplay and characters and music because i think it's worth experiencing yourself, instead of having some person tell you about it. you can tell this game was made by people who get what makes pokemon work and what makes other jrpgs work, and put their own creative spin on it that also works.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially purchased on switch, but this game has not only been my favorite game of 2023, but one of my top 3 games of all time. It's like a monster taming game but instead of taming monsters you transform into them with a cassette player!This game really just wants the player to have fun. Fully customizable AI and scaling (even customizable mid-playthrough!), with perma-death and randomizer options after beating the game once, and the main puzzle of the game differs each time you make a new game. This and the other options allow for a unique experience even on your 2nd, 3rd, or 20th playthrough! So, even if I uh completely accidentally solved the main puzzle so early on that I was completely confused as to what happened and why (as I couldn't even do anything with solving it until later) it actually took me a while to solve on my second playthrough due to it being completely different!There is a local co-op feature, but I haven't gotten to use it yet so I can't really comment on it. However, there is an online multplayer and PvP update being heavily worked on and planning to release early this year, so there's that to look forward to! As far as characters in the game, there are several characters and you can improve your relationship/bond with them. There are some cutscenes and light romantic events that can happen if you select the right options when you are close enough to a character, but they are entirely optional so if light romantic elements don't interest you, you can just avoid them. It has a phenomenal soundtrack, fun and unique designs, complete customization, many huge Quality of Life features, (stickers are SO NICE and have INSANE competitive potential(for those who've played Pokemon, think of one-time-use tms but then you can take the move back off the creature and get the tm back to put on another one, or just take off a move that was part of its learnset and make it a tm)), and many unique and fun features! I mean, the typing system itself is actually really fun! They made a freaking typing system FUN. I didn't even know that was a thing I could enjoy so much until this!!!I will absolutely be trying to get all the steam achievements, and while the Bestiary is able to be completed, I probably won't truly complete it as the  do have their own section. On top of that, it keeps track of all the  so uh yeah good luck if you truly want to 100% this game!So yeah, that's my semi-spoiler free review for this phenomenal game. I would pay $60 for this game if it was priced that high- I cannot recommend it enough for those who want a monster taming game suited for an older audience!

_childDocuments_.review: So when it comes to creature collector games, I’ve only really focused on Pokemon and SMT/Persona. For some reason, I’ve convinced myself that any other creature collector game that aren’t these must be garbage somehow. I’m happy to report that I was completely wrong. This is definitely one of the best games I’ve played this year by far.It’s like Pokemon but you transform into the monster rather than summon it. The difference is that if your monster form goes down, your player character is exposed to attacks. If your character goes down, you’re done, even if you have more monsters in reserve. Another key difference is the fact that you can equip up to 8 or 10 attacks on a monster. That must seem like a lot to Pokemon players, but there are no “abilities”, instead you use those slots to equip passive abilities, thus, giving you greater control over the build of your monster. And yes, you can have multiple passives, unlike Pokemon’s one passive ability per monster. Then there's the battle gimmick, which is fusion. Two of your monsters can become one to unlock a new super attack, and combine move/passives pools into one huge monster with much higher stats. It's fun, and it's impressive what they've done to make all fusions look like the monsters they're fused from. The story is also more mature than your typical Pokemon story. The music is absolutely god-tier. Nothing else to say on this. I wish more games had soundtracks this incredible.Now the negatives, the post game, if you want all achievements, is a terrible horrific grind. You do randomly generated quests in order to get “fusion material” which you need a lot of to get the last achievement (around 450 or so, if I’m not mistaken). I think your most recent Pokemon games handled the post-game content much better. Sword/Shield’s Dynamax Adventures are tons of fun, Legend’s Arceus various post-game side quests, and even Scarlet/Violet’s meager post-game (I haven’t played the DLCs for this one yet…) far outshine the disgusting mindless grind this game has. Which is unfortunate as every other part of Cassette Beasts is better than most Pokemon games, in my opinion.I do hope I get to play a “Cassette Beasts 2” one day. This was far too fantastic to just end like this. There’s DLC to this game, but I haven’t played it. It’s not required for 100% achievement completion, and I heard that the new music in that DLC doesn’t have vocals, which is a huge deal-breaker for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is an absolute gem of a game, seamlessly blending nostalgic charm with innovative gameplay mechanics to deliver an unforgettable experience. From the moment you boot up the game, you're greeted with a vibrant world teeming with personality and possibilities.One of the standout features of Cassette Beasts is its unique cassette mechanic, which allows players to transform ordinary objects into powerful creatures. This mechanic not only adds an exciting element of discovery and experimentation but also serves as a clever homage to the beloved cassette culture of the past. Whether you're turning a humble toaster into a fire-breathing dragon or transforming a cassette tape into a lightning-fast cheetah, the possibilities are endless and endlessly entertaining.Cassette Beasts is more than just its inventive gameplay mechanics. It's a beautifully crafted world filled with memorable characters, breathtaking landscapes, and secrets waiting to be uncovered. The art style is a delightful mix of retro pixel art and modern flair, evoking a sense of nostalgia while still feeling fresh and contemporary.The game's narrative is equally captivating, weaving together elements of mystery, adventure, and humor in a way that keeps you hooked from start to finish. Whether you're unraveling the secrets of the island or forming bonds with your quirky companions, every moment feels meaningful and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, first and foremost, a Pokemon-like that RESPECTS YOUR TIME.Want to try a different moveset? Freely swap moves around between any/all of your monsters. At any time. For free.Tired of hoofing it around? Fast-travel's enabled from the very start, go nuts.The combat is also interested in more strategic depth than just plain STAB and type weaknesses. Strong type attacks against weak types inflict nominal maluses on the weak type, and weak type attacks inflict nominal bonuses on the strong type. I say "nominal" because type shifting moves are incredibly common and used by just about everyone, so what appears to be a bonus inflicted on you NOW can rapidly turn into a malus if you're not paying attention!Also, the soundtrack SLAPS.And the writing is good as hell.And might also be linked to Lenna's Inception which is also fantastic in its own right??Basically buy this game, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, fantastic, fantastic game!To compare this to Pokémon is to do Cassette Beasts a disservice. Pokémon feels to me as though it has lost its heart and soul. This game plays not like a Pokémon made for kids or to print money but a game made for all ages, and a game made out of love and passion. I'm so ashamed of myself for sleeping on this for so long. I bought it back when it came out and just never got around to playing it until now. Ironically enough, I kind of put it off a bit thinking it would be “yet another Pokémon clone.”I'll be transparent and say I haven't finished the game, but I'm on track to doing so. It runs well enough on Steam Deck and utilizes the Godot game engine. My playtime has been split between playing on my laptop and playing on my Steam Deck. I leave it set to 50 Hz on Steam Deck, and leave all other battery settings at their default values. Turn off half rate shading if you're using DeckyRecorder. HRS seems to cause some sort of flickering in footage. May cause epileptic episodes if you open footage without realizing you've left HRS on. Steam Deck does get frame drops, and they are noticeable, but due to the nature of the gameplay, they are not game-breaking. I did get some crashes, and I think my issue was limiting the wattage to 13 instead of leaving the limiter off. I have been unable to recreate the crashes after setting wattage back to default. I don’t have an OLED model Steam Deck to compare, but the fans ramp up quite a bit on the old 512 GB LCD model Steam Deck.Cassette Beasts is 100% what I would call a wholesome and cozy game. It's got some creepiness and some cuteness. It’s got a good amount of diversity. It’s got some heartfelt moments, and some good potential for character development. There’s been some really clever moments that made me go “Huh. That’s interesting,” as well. I think I still have quite a bit left to do, and I've been stumped a couple of times. The game could do with some more hints or giving more guidance on what you're supposed to do next at certain points. It just kind of started to slow down at one point, and I ended up wandering around until I stumbled into what I was supposed to do. This actually happened a couple of times during my play sessions.There’s some really good music in certain locations and boss battles of this game as well. I was in a cafe at one point and was suddenly hit with some music that took me aback for a moment. I wasn’t expecting that kind of vibe from this game going into it. As a music lover, I can’t help but love the record-themed stages. The first boss encounter had a really good song, as well. Not quite the kind of music I was expecting from this game, but definitely not disappointing by any stretch. I find the fusion and cassette/recording mechanics to be really interesting. They’re a good twist on the monster collector formula. Type matches and mismatches, abilities, buffs, and debuffs all feel really good to me. They’re fun to play around with, and they make sense in this game’s world. I really like the way the leveling system is implemented as well. I never felt like I was hindered by the beasts I wanted to use. Your beasts level up, evolve, and all that good stuff. However, your player character also levels up. That’s the interesting part. There’s a lot to play around with here, and a lot of interesting twists on the monster collecting genre. It’s really not “just another Pokémon clone.”To just describe it as “Pokémon but better” or something along those lines is to do Cassette Beasts dirty. It’s so much more than that. It’s a love letter to what made those classic Pokémon and Zelda games great. It wears its inspiration on its sleeve, and it does it in the best way possible.Pick this one up. Buy it on sale if you want, but I think it’s worth the full asking price.Edit: I beat the game.  I'm now playing the DLC. Cassette Beasts is definitely worth the asking price. So much so that I've gone back and purchased their previous game, Lenna's Inception, as well.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.4.24 UPDATE: I would recommend adding the "List of Redeemable Codes (Past and Current)" guide by Sky to your favorites. Here the devs drop limited time codes that get you free bootlegs. When a new code is posted to the guide, you simply go to your mailbox in your room or the Cafe, put in the code and you get a free bootleg instantly and sometimes an additional item. The codes generally last a few weeks before they are deactivated. This is a nice feature because getting bootlegs is definitely a grind. And now you know what the mailbox is for! ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've had a lot of luck when trying out new genres the past couple of years.  Cassette Beasts was no exception.  This game constitutes my first JRPG and first Creature Capture game (nope, I've never played a Pokémon game). I must admit this game has been a ton of fun. The music is quite catchy and the main song is very peaceful. It has an "I ❤️ the 80s" retro theme with its pixelated graphics, limited voice acting and character wardrobe. None of which took away from the gaming experience in 2023. The gameplay is enjoyable with plenty to do on a large map... you can even play with a friend!  Most of the tasks are fairly straight forward, but if you want to 💯 the achievements you will have to grind to find at least one of every bootleg type, obtain a copy of every beast and obtain additional info on every beast (there are a lot of beasts, evolutions and fusions). You can adjust the difficulty to your preferences, but I found the default to be very enjoyable.The price is extraordinarily reasonable. At $19.99 you can feel good picking up this game at full price... on any sort of discount, it's a steal. In fact, the devs could have fairly priced it at $24.99- $29.99, but I do appreciate the lower price point. I haven't said anything about the story or gameplay. Both are interesting and engaging. Most of you are better gamers than I, so suffice it to say,  "you won't have much trouble naturally figuring out some of the less obvious elements as you progress through the game." ... battle strategy, chemistry, how/ where to find bootleg beasts, etc... and for the things that weren't intuitive to me (like how the heck do you beat a ghost!? And where on New Wirrell is that gold coin??), steam guides and youtube videos have been a big help.This one's a 10/10 for me. It's not a perfect game by any means, but the devs have given it a ton of love and it has been a real treat to play. I strongly recommend you give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially passed this up as being just another pixel-art Pokémon knockoff, but after seeing a glowing review for it, I decided to give it a shot - and I certainly didn't regret it! Rather than just aping the Big P, it very much provides a fresh take on the Monster-Taming genre, and while it's not without its flaws, the execution is truly excellent. The music is AMAZING, and utilizes dynamic mixing in a way I really wish more games would. Despite the 'kid-friendly' design of the monsters, the story's quite deep and mature, dipping into philosophical and psychological concepts. The characters are well-executed, with your various companions all being fully realized individuals that you find yourself wanting to get to know better, and not just grinding rep with for the sake of boosted abilities or achievements.Now, I DO have to point out a couple of drawbacks, though they don't detract enough to make that thumbs-up waver. Firstly, while the game being moderately challenging isn't a bad thing, the way it often blindsides you in one way or another feels rather unfair. You may sometimes be plunged into harsh boss-fights with no warning, and even fights that ARE thoroughly telegraphed may turn out to revolve around some gimmick or trick that you just don't have an answer to in your current lineup of monsters. In the end-game, the loss of resources you suffer upon death is rather insignificant, but early on it rather stings... and of course, once you ARE in the endgame, it's quite possible for you to create your OWN gimmicky trick-builds, murdering any and all challenge the game has to offer.Second, there's the... ugh... *post-game*. It's a GRIND. Just... a HUGE grind. There's some actual interesting stuff there - extra monsters, extra features, more interesting characters, new types of mini-bosses and so on, but most of it is gated behind a ridiculous grind that just requires you to collect 'Unstable Matter' by either doing hundreds of endless, randomly-generated radial quests, fighting tons and tons of endlessly respawning minibosses, or refighting the main storyline's bosses over and over and over again for hours on end. The later option, for those curious, is the most efficient, once you have the right kind of depraved gimmick-build to effortlessly annihilate them - but it's still a dull, mindless slog.Still, despite those flaws, Cassette Beasts remains a very worthwhile game to play, and a fine example of what monster-taming can be like when you stop trying to just imitate Pokémon -  and if you aren't a completionist obsessed with 100%'ing games, the post-game grind is at least... *manageable*.

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a wonderful game that does a great job of capturing the feeling and aesthetic of Gen IV Pokémon, with a battle system that is focused on taking the basic concepts of combat in Pokémon and expanding them in intriguing, unexpected ways. Tied together with a light story that essentially functions as a framework in which the game operates rather than being the driving force, this game is both cozy and challenging, simple and thought-provoking, and a great time from start to finish.It really feels to me like the developers have a great deal of appreciation for what makes Pokémon work so well - one of the things that really annoys me about some romhacks and fangames is the sense that the developers of those always think they can do things a lot better than Game Freak, whereas with Cassette Beasts, it feels like it simply takes inspiration from the basic framework of combat and goes in a fresh, interesting direction. The core of battle is type interactions, which are a lot more varied and diverse than in Pokémon, relying on basic logic for you to ascertain how elements will interact with each other. I was discovering new interactions as late as the final part of the main mission, and I'm still not completely sure I've seen it all.Party management emphasizes experimentation - monsters don't have their own individual levels, instead your player character levels up directly, giving every monster a common base power upon which you can build, and making all of them at least a little bit usable in battle from the moment you acquire them. In place of levels, monsters have a separate leveling system that grants more move slots and default moves every time they level up, though movesets are completely customizable at will via the use of HM-like move stickers that are infinitely reusable. It all just feels very thoughtfully considered, more about creating a satisfying environment for player experimentation than, I don't know, being difficult for difficulty's sake.The story is sparse, and the somewhat non-linear mission system can sometimes leave you feeling a little directionless, but all it takes to get on the right track is to just open the mission list, pick a mission, and start pursuing it. Eventually, you'll narrow the list down to just the core path, and doing the other missions as much as possible first will allow you to properly scale up to match the increasing difficulty of the main mission. The art style is very, very charming, using sprites for characters and 3D models for the environment - very Gen IV Pokémon, as I said before. There's an unsettling aspect to some elements, too, hinting at a darkness at the center of the world you're thrown into, and the variance in art style for the characters related to that core mission is one of my favorite things about the game.This is a game where it feels like every element comes together extremely well, in the service of ensuring the player enjoys every aspect of it as much as possible. It's not perfect - fusion feels like little more than a gimmick, there's an ambiguity to some missions that makes it hard to figure out what exactly to do at the mission marker, you can inadvertently sequence break and get rolled pretty easily even with your partner party member warning you when you're underleveled for an area - but it does a lot of things well, very well, in fact, and it's a game I had a blast with from beginning to end. Worth it at any price.

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a fresh take on a genre full of Pokemon Clones, this game isn't Pokemon, and honestly, it's better for it! Then dive in, Even better if it's with a friend.Cons-Low CustomizationSlight Loading Issues (nothing game-breaking just a small shudder when the game is having trouble loading in an area)Slightly Repetitive Fusion designs (which are due to the small dev team but still need to be stated)Pros-Amazing Story, Well Written Characters,Great Music,Awesome Monster and Boss Designs,Fun Exploration (that gives the same sense of freedom as 3D Open world games despite being top-down)Loads of unique Play-styles and Strategies for you to try and find your groove with!Cassette Beasts is one ride it'd be a disservice to miss out on, Just don't go in with the expectation of a game exactly like Pokemon and enjoy Cassette Beasts for what it is, a really Good Game made by Devs who really care.I Rate Cassette Beasts a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: With the review scores being the way there are, I am wondering if I ended up with the wrong version of the game. It had so many blatant issues that I am more than a little surprised so few people would mention them here. So, having played through the entirety of it with a friend, I may as well try myself.To at least start off on a positive note, the game does look and sound nice. The artwork and designs, as well as the music in the game, are pretty good. It did give a good first impression, but that is about everything the game really does well. Everything else feels like someone's first attempt at designing gameplay.The combat tries to offer some complexity with various type interactions that cause different buffs, debuffs, and other effects when certain typed attacks are used against others. This sounds neat in theory, but was so irrelevant for the entirety of the game that it may as well not have been there. The observant player quickly notices that a high speed and damage stat are all that really matters, at least early on. It's easy to one shot at least one enemy in a given fight before they get a turn in, far more effectively minimizing damage than any amount of defense or utility ever could.Once you get into the late game and have more stickers at your disposal (The game's version of monster abilities that you can swap between monsters), the game completely falls apart. It is trivial to equip your monsters with combinations of stickers that, in our playthrough, one-shot almost every single fight (Including bosses) before enemies even got a turn in. So the game either breaks the moment you experiment with it, or you restrain yourself and stick to uninteractive loadouts all the way through, there is, unfortunately, no fun way to go about it.Even when you are obliterating your foes, the game is still adamant on playing out every single action in order. Did you proc five random attacks and the single enemy died after the first? The game has to let you know the other four ones all failed, in order. Attacks with type advantage need to inform you what debuffs you put on the enemy even though they are already dead. Multi-hit attacks play out all of their attacks every single time as they whittle away at corpses. There is no way to speed up combat or skip animations.Fusions were a neat idea in theory but became obsolete the moment you get them, not to mention that they effectively delete multiplayer for the duration. Hopefully, your friend doesn't mind sitting out if you ever plan on using them. Either way, they effectively combine the stats of the fused creatures, as well as their ap. In execution, this is pointless because you are also down to one action per round, making anything but spamming high ap attacks a waste of your turn. Even then, the strongest attacks are ones that trigger when creatures are swapped in, meaning you are far better off even damage wise to just never fuse and rely on your passives.The UI in this game is an absolute atrocity. You have 14 different elements attacks can have, and can then roughly categorize abilities into melee attacks, ranged attacks, passives and utility. Guess what options you have to sort them? Alphabetically. That's it. Have fun scrolling through your list of stickers from memory as you flip through a list that can only display ten at a time.Swapping out party members means they have to take the creature equipped to them with them. Had a new party member force your current one back into town during a story quest? Have fun running back and swapping around monsters for a few minutes in order to get back the monsters you were currently planning on using. Someone seems to have understood the general concept of puzzles but didn't actually bother trying with the execution. There are some overworld puzzles that were interesting, requiring you to pay attention to the environment and figure out a solution off of those hints by yourself. Most of the main game puzzles, however, are obvious the moment you look at them, and simply require you to go through the motions for the bland execution, making you wonder why they are even there in the first place.This is exacerbated by the fact almost all chests in this game contain garbage. You get good stickers from shops/leveling up bootlegs (The game's version of shiny monsters) and good materials from overworld rogue fusions, quests, and bosses. As far as I remember, the contents of every single chest in this game have been pointless materials you would also drop from every random encounter ever.The game has made the curious decision of attempting to go for a character relationship driven narrative while also rendering you a silent protagonist. You have occasional response prompts that are usually something along the lines of "Yes" and "Yes but in yellow". No dialogue options in this game matter, except for possibly romance confessions when reaching maximum relationship status with a given character. Naturally, they are head over heels for you after expositing their life story and struggles at you, while you blankly stared back like the soulless automaton that you are. The meta-commentary we haven't paid much attention to, but it is more than a little on the nose with one boss being the incarnation of capitalism, while one of the enemy factions is a group of landlords that are literally just vampires. This was roughly on the same level as the quest to stop an evil cult. You don't really know why they are evil, they aren't actually doing anything in the game that is shown to you, or even mentioned to any significant degree, but it's a cult, what else are they going to be?This game certainly felt like wasted potential. The gameplay didn't really change after five or so hours in, but we wanted to push through to the end to see if combat maybe gets more varied somehow. As far as we could tell, none of the bosses have any mechanics that require you to interact with them, safe for a singular puppeteer that has effigies of your team on his side, requiring you to pay attention to where you place your attacks, lest you suffer recoil. Had the game tried to do more things like this while keeping some semblance of ability balance, perhaps it could have been something.

_childDocuments_.review: (The following review is based on the 1.5.0 version of Cassette Beasts, but not taking DLC into account. These feelings are still accurate as of me writing this review, but praises and criticisms I have exclusively with the DLC are not included here.)I had heard quite a few good things going into Cassette Beasts, and the game's launch trailer really grabbed my attention, but I was not at all prepared for how the game would blow every single one of my expectations out of the water. Cassette Beasts manages to pay homage to its inspirations while crafting its own special experience from that foundation. As a longtime Pokémon fan, I pretty quickly picked up on the gameplay, but was pleasantly surprised at the many individual components that make the game unique. Instead of a MP or PP system, the game uses Action Points that you accrue over the course of a battle that can be spent on moves of varying amounts of power- it's more akin to something like Boost Points in Octopath Traveler. This makes it so that both weak moves and strong moves have their place in battle, which I really like! The game primarily focuses on 2v2 combat, and the synergy you build with the various partner characters you join up with over the course of the story translates very well into the gameplay, especially through the headlining "fusion" mechanic that spices up the combat significantly─ you'll have much greater firepower, but can't take as many actions per turn, which is a fun tradeoff. Moves and passives are contextualized as "stickers" that can be freely attached and detached from monster tapes at will, making experimentation and strategization easily some of the most streamlined I've seen from an RPG. My only minor point of criticism is that by endgame the sticker list is a bit of a pain to sort through to find what you want, but the filter tools make this a little less frustrating at least. As a lover of turn-based combat, I was thoroughly impressed.The characters and story felt very fresh and engaging, especially for an RPG of this subgenre. I'll keep my thoughts here as general as I can to not spoil things. Each of their backstories and personalities added something to the party, and the optional romance mechanic managed to enhance the experience without taking anything away for those who aren't interested (except an achievement unfortunately, but that's not too bad). As a nonbinary person, I felt very at home with the options included for character creation, and seeing LGBTQ+ representation in the game itself was really awesome to see. Everything regarding this feels really natural and well-written, which I love. The Archangels and what they each ultimately represent slowly build an interesting narrative over the course of the game, while each being memorable in their own right, utilizing various art styles that feel foreign to everything else in the game's world. There's a nice balance of lightheartedness and more serious subject matters tackled here, and overall does a good job of keeping a positive outlook throughout without needing to talk down to its players when the going gets rough. The story pacing felt very good, which can be hard to pull off in an open-world experience where things aren't always done in the same order, so I appreciate what the devs and writers were able to accomplish here.The visuals really land in this game in every aspect, from the chibi overworld, to the adorable talk sprites, to the unsettling-yet-badass Archangels, and of course, the fantastic animated monster sprites. To the untrained eye the inspiration is obvious, but it goes a lot further with it than its inspirations by every monster having animations for dealing and taking damage, as well as many of the "asleep" animations being a lot more visually interesting than just having closed eyes. Oh, and reminder that just about all of this applies to the 19,000+ fusions too. Some procedural generation was obviously needed to reach that monolithic number, but amidst the recent controversies around AI art, it's really refreshing to see this pulled off with 100% organically drawn and animated components. Oh, and of course, the monster designs themselves are fantastic. There's a very lovable quirky feel to each one, while having a flavor entirely of their own that you can't easily find elsewhere. The more mature subject matter allows for some really fun names and designs that wouldn't fly in more family-friendly monster-collecting RPGs without losing any of the aforementioned charm at all─ shoutout to Skelevangelist and Miasmodeus, among others.The music is absolutely stellar. The vocals kicking in during battle themes when a fusion happens appeals very heavily to me as an enjoyer of dynamic music in video games. There's some nice motif reusage present, as well as a good amount of lyrics with multiple meanings that were fun to experience. Same Old Story and Arrow of Time will be on my VGM playlist for a long time yet to come.I could go on for ages about all the other things I love about this game, and I'm sure there's some things I'll kick myself for not mentioning here later, but honestly the best thing about Cassette Beasts is the gestalt of the game experience rather than any of its individual aspects. It's not very often I see a game so well-balanced in its strengths, and whether you're a casual Pokémon fan, a monster-collector RPG fanatic, or just want a fun turn-based experience in general, you can't go wrong with Cassette Beasts.

_childDocuments_.review: "Can you feel it? The lack of wind but abundance of air?"This game is quite honestly my game of the year. It's fun, engaging, non-restrictive (A big thing I'll get into in a moment), and does well in establishing it's own identity in a well saturated genre.It introduces some very interesting Quality of Life changes that Pokemon-likes would really do well to implement. I was worried at first that the catch mechanic was a bit handholdy because technically a beast can't die while you try to catch it. But as the game scales up and the monsters/legendaries get harder to catch, you realize that its not easier than your usual "throw ball and pray" strategy. It's actually much riskier and more challenging as you risk your character (not your beast, your actual player) being 1-shot.So that already put the game at a solid 9/10 for me. But what really pushed it over was the ability to play with whatever combination you want. The way type advantages are done make them easy to either abuse, work into your strategy, or ignore. The concept of STAB seems to be removed in favor of bonuses over other typings. For example, instead of Fire critting Grass for super effective damage, instead it guarantees a burn even on a skill with no innate burn attached.Water "extinguishes" fire, causing a drop in damage, both ranged and melee, etc.Baton Pass players like me will love the setup capabilities of this game, as buffs and debuffs are applied to your character, not your tape. So you can have a tape (The "Pokemon" are called tapes) that, at start of battle immediately does 3 buffs, then on your turn, swap them with your sweeper.You can build almost any tape in any way you want, save for some stickers (the "TMs" are called stickers) that cant go on some tapes, giving you an incredibly vast pool to play with. This game is amazing and I haven't stopped playing it since I picked it up. I wish there was PvP or some form of online so I can see the teams and mons other people have come up with.Solid 10/10 for me

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up playing Pokemon, this game is an absolute joy to play. I have a real soft spot for indie games, and this is no exception. The passion for making a great monster catcher game is evident.The battles were challenging at times, especially if I stumbled into an area that easily countered my two main beasts I ran for a while. It pushed me to swap out and try other combinations and led to some really neat combos! The story was cute and I enjoyed playing through it. The main story took around 24 or so hours for me to complete at a leisurely pace. There is also a number of post-game/late-game challenges you can complete that I'm sure will keep me busy for a number of hours more.While I don't think I'll push for 100%, as I don't want to grind that hard for getting a bootleg (like a shiny) of every type, I definitely am going to shoot for a completed bestiary! Also, the move bad joke is one of my favorites and always gives me a chuckle!So, if you want at least 20 hours of enjoyable gameplay, I can honestly recommend picking it up at its current full price as it is worth every penny!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR. After getting all the achievements, I can say it's a very fun monster taming game that brings it's own unique (and also quite complex at times) ideas to the table, though it's not worth going for 100%.Story:While there is a main story to follow that acts as a hook from the beginning of the game, this game actually splinters off into multiple stories that usually focus on one character. The strength of each story really relies on said character but luckily the main cast are enjoyable and fleshed out enough carry them. While not super deep, I for sure enjoyed their presence and I assume it's a just a matter of taste as to which ones resonate with you (with Felix being my absolute favourite). The monsters:The cast of creatures are extremely important in any monster taming game and this game delivers with 121 fun designs (not including bosses). They are packed with personality and I can see each of them having fans. In addition, both of the starting tapes are a great choice, simple at the start but help to really show off the uniqueness of this games remastering (evolution) system.This remastering mechanic is also fantastic as it can give you extra choice when evolving. You can either pick blind and have fun with your new team member or google it to see what your options are. Either way, more player choice in how a team ends up is always a good thing. It also means that even if players pick up the same monsters, their teams and strategies could end up completely different by the end of this game. The one drawback of this system is that some of these split lines have one far more cryptic one, meaning the likelihood of you finding them on your own is quite slim.I do however wish there were more of them. 121 seems like a reasonable number but a good chunk of them are split evo lines. The most blatant example of this being the cariviper line taking up 5 whole slots in the roster. Overworld gameplay:The overworld is a small yet open map that allows you to go anywhere you can reach. At first I absolutely hated exploring it as it felt like a slog. This was until I managed to gather power ups. Once you have all of them, running around the map is extremely fun but for those first crucial hours of the game it feels quite bad sadly. In terms of interesting locations, this game is almost nothing but. With how small the overall map is, there is almost no space for time filler, each section of the grid having at least one interesting thing to look at, find or explore.Battling:This games battle system will either be a blast or overly obtuse depending on how much you want to memorise. Instead of focusing on big numbers for it's type chart, certain types can dish out either positive or negative to what they are hitting. This makes for a farm more dynamic system about a mounting wall of effects, buffs and debuffs that you have to worry about rather than "me use strong move knock out opponent". While fun this system is also quite exploitable once you get comfortable with it. Many an archangel was taken down on my playthrough through a combination of leech, poison and burn. If this was a multiplayer focused game this could be a massive issue but since it's not it's just fun to see how much you can cheese challenges that you're facing.Stickers are the equivalent of moves and abilities in this game, each one can be added, peeled off or replaced with a compatible move. This gives the player a great amount of power to customise each of their team members, helping them to feel truly unique. They are also pretty easy to get your hands on so players are encouraged to play around.During each battle, you team up with a picked partner. Having fights be a 2 vs 2 (or maybe even more with swarms a summoning) allows for a great deal of strategy in regards to targeting and switching. It also gives more support oriented beasts a time to shine (seriously, despite having a zero ap attack as it's only attacking move blossomaw was one of the most reliable team members). You can also use the type chart to your advantage if you're prepared enough.AP is this games version of energy or mana or power points. This is an extremely balanced energy system that feels rewarding to engage with. Many other games would have it deplete and then force you to do nothing to gather it back whereas in this game you can almost always do something meaningful with the ap you have access to.Player base stats are also a fun addition, this can be tweaked to help boost traits that benefit your overall party or battle plan. During my playthrough I gathered a quite raged attack heavy squad. This would be a bad idea in other monster taming games but for this I was able to lean into this by investing my players current melee attack into ranged for an extra kick when attacking. Postgame:Unfortunately, once the main story is done, it feels like the game runs out of steam. There are extremely fun elements. I loved the  but every fin part is surrounded by a sea of grind. Want to bootleg hunt, 50 fused materiel per ritual candle. Want to continue the fun story lines, not until you've beaten another 4 rogue fusions. Prehaps shortening the postgame would have made it far more fun to go through but as it is, it and some of the achievements tied to it are not fun. Artstyle:I know gen 5 pokemon is very in chic right now so I imagine most people are absolutely gushing over this games 2d pixel sprites on simple 3d surroundings. I can't say I disagree with them, it works quite well. Where I think this game shines is how it clashes with it's bosses. The archangels all have a completely different artstyle that helps to make each of them feel unique and alien. Bootlegs:As a final addition (and as an avid shiny hunter in the pokemon games) I wanted to mention bootlegs. They're a 1/1000 chance of happening and they completely change the monsters type. This is such a fun addition to the formula that helps them feel unique for their regular counterparts. It also means you can hunt the same one multiple times and have completely different feeling monsters. You could probably do a run with only one type of monster if you were crazy enough. I addition, this is the only way you have access to a natural glitter type which is a fun addition that would have been to mechanically crazy to have as a normal type. If you did somehow read this far into the review and plan on getting into the game, if you find yourself with an astral traffikrab during your playthrough, consider yourself blessed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews (even though I should), but I feel this is one of the times I would be mad at myself for not leaving one. This review is SPOILER FREETL;DRGameplay loop/core mechanics: 9.5/10UI design: 9/10Controls/settings: 7/10Environment design: 9/10Music/sound design: 9/10Creature design: 10/10Partner deisgn: 8/10Character customization: 8/10Final score: 9.5/10Long Version:Gameplay: the gameplay is fun, though I am biased as a big pokemon fan. That said, this isn't just a pokemon clone. It more than feels like its own game in the same genre rather than a re-skinned pokemon game due in part to the evolutions but also the characters you travel with. Objectively I couldn't give it a 10 due to the tedium I know some people will find if they aren't into the completionism like I am (which is also a problem people have with pokemon to be fair), but personally I love it so subjectively I would. The only complaint I personally have with the game is the difficulty scaling. Its open world so if you go too far forward that's on you but some of the special monsters in the base area are unreasonably strong. There were a few times I nearly lost to a special in area 1 but blew a special in area 3 out of the water by comparison even with type advantages and solid strategies. UI design: the various UIs are non-intrusive and generally easy to navigate. You can get to any of the menus from either a shortcut or the default menu button, so one or two inputs. The layouts are for the most part intuitive with the exception of the settings menu which requires you to press the FN button plus the arrow keys to swap pages. The battle interface is easy to read and understand, and turn indicators are more subtle but for the most part effective. The selection menu in battle is very clever but also clearly labeled to avoid any confusion which is nice. There's no flee prompt, and while it would be nice not having one isn't really too big a deal in my personal opinion.Controls/settings: it's a pretty standard control scheme (WASD to move, space to jump, shift to dash), and it can be customized. The only weird choice is the "page up" "page down" option, because I have to hold the FN key in order to use those keys rather than just the arrow keys. And from what I can tell you can't assign the regular arrow keys. The customization is a little confusing as it's the only place that requires you to use the mouse which isn't intuitive when everything else can be done keyboard only. But when you figure it out it's not really a hassle. I can't remember off the top of my head if it has controller support, but if it doesn't that would be the other thing I'd dock points for. Controller support is a big thing for me because it allows people with disabilities to have a better experience with the game.Environment design: in terms of visuals, I really love the aesthetic. It's cute but not overdone. The environment doesn't distract from the characters in it too much, things that are interactive are not made so painfully obvious they distract you but also don't entirely blend in with static environment pieces either, and for the most part the sprites align everywhere they should. The physics can be a little weird but all things considered it's very smooth. The amount of the world that gets loaded doesn't lag anything on my computer and having only 1 loading boarder in the whole overworld makes it far less intrusive which is a big plus in an open world game. The loading screen itself only takes a few seconds at most, so it doesn't really throw off the flow of exploration. The only difficulty I had was one that just comes with the design by default. Navigating a 2D sprite on a 3D plane can make platforming a bit confusing but as you play your understanding of exactly "where" you sit in the world gets better, allowing you to make more precision maneuvers. The map itself is big enough to be initially confusing (in the way that encourages exploration), but small enough to be learned and navigated which is a different kind of rewarding.Music/sound design: It's just good. Plain and simple. The individual themes of each area are unique but all follow a more relaxed overall theme. The choice to include lyrics is apparently a controversial one but I quite enjoy it, and they only appear indoors. It does distract from the reading at first, but after you hear it a few times it fades into the background almost as well as plain instrumental music. Other times the lyrics are a very nice surprise. Voice acting isn't AAA grade which is expected but as far as indie games go its one of the more smooth implementations, and it's quite light-hearted which fits the theme of the game very well. Personally I think the voice acting here feels much more fitting to the game's atmosphere than the more "big industry standard" style of voice acting. The dialog is not fully voiced but the vocal interjections generally do a good job conveying the tone of whatever text is on screen. The battle cries of NPCs are a little funny. I'm not sure if they're randomized or if maybe I just had a bug happen but a character that was very clearly supposed to be a male figure (he was a reference to a real person) made a much higher pitch sound when he saw me.Creature design: in terms of aesthetics I love the creatures. It gives me the same excitement I had when I was a kid playing the pokemon games for the first time. They're full of clever references and cheeky nods to so many different things I had fun trying to guess them all, Each new monster is unique and interesting in its own right, and makes me wonder what it might become, if anything. And the main mechanics give you so many forms to discover, meaning you'll really have to be doing your due diligence if you want to see all of them. And speaking of; mechanics wise, I'm actually quite impressed. This is where it differs from pokemon the most in my opinion. Because of the way the move system works you really can turn just about any of your creatures into a powerhouse who does not stop to ask for directions. They won't be invincible, and no one strategy will work for all occasions, but you can very reliably make a team of just your favorite monsters and you can get to most places and win most fights just fine. They're all versatile and balanced enough to hold their own if you take the time to build them up. Even unevolved forms can bring you pretty far into the main game without needing an absurd amount of knowledge about stats and mechanics.see comments for part 2
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: - Very interesting combat system with unique elemental reactions.- Fusion feels VERY AWESOME to do. Every combination of monsters leads to a unique fusion result. - Exploration with Pokemon HM-styled moves are taken to another level with the abilities being used in creative puzzles. - Very cute mix of 2D and 3D. - Game has a very good feel of atmosphere, whether it be relaxing or spooky.- Simple story line and subplot that feel a bit rushed at time but still do enough to be charming. - Very flexible monster customization system.- Tons of optional and post-game content. - Phenomenal soundtrack. The vocals even kick in when you fuse in battle!- Rewards you for paying attention. Quest markers don't tell you everything and it's a joy trying to figure out the puzzles and riddles on your own.- Boss fights aren't too hard, but have gimmicks to keep them interesting and are very visually intimidating and memorable.I'll be honest as someone going through a rough time i've teared up multiple times at how good this game is. If you enjoy Pokemon, Shin Megami Tensei, Persona or you're looking for an adventure in general, Cassette Beasts should be the next station you make a stop at.

_childDocuments_.review: Though the narrative and gameplay elements can feel flimsy or rushed at times, and the fusions are frequently a little disappointing visually (personally speaking only!), I had a genuinely wonderful time with this game.Most people are right in calling this baby's first SMT game tbh. That doesn't make it any less enjoyable!The overall theme, gameplay loop, monster designs, and music were fantastic. The ending definitely emotionally ♥♥♥♥♥♥ me up a bit despite it not being anything crazy. If you're looking for a Pokemon style game, this isn't it. This really doesn't play or feel like a Pokemon style game *at all*, this is absolutely MUCH more SMT. If you're looking for a pretty light Digital Devil Saga type experience, I'd highly recommend this game even at full price! The game is moddable and there's quite a few really great QoL mods too.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I go over the game I'd just like to say this: I never played any monster tamer before, pokémon included. This is my first entry into the genre. I do know a few bits and bobs here and there, but I don't have any actual first hand experience of any other monster tamer. Take of that what you will when reading this review.I did not expect Cassette Beasts to be as good as it is; the gameplay is (for the most part) fun, innovative, and easy to understand, it has a great artstyle, and an AMAZING soundtrack. It is overall a VERY good game. If a non-pokémon player like me likes it, I'm sure anyone who DOES play other monster taming games will love Cassette Beasts. Easily an 8/10 for me, my 2nd favourite game of all time (so far).Overall, the gameplay is very good at the start, but after you beat the main game and get to the post-game content (yes, there is post-game content) it starts to lose a bit of it's magic. As for specifics, I'll put them in bullet points here:That's all I'm gonna say; there is still a lot to the game, but I'd rather not spoil too much.The story is pretty fun. Each character/companion has their own quest with their own storylines. The characters themsleves aren't one-note; they feel like real people, and are fun to listen and talk to. The ending is pretty underwhelming, but I suppose it's all about the journey, not the destination. Again, won't spoil too much, but rest assured that it's a good story that might even get a tear or two out from you.It's cute and very pleasant to look at, ranging from the character portraits to the pixel art. The team have done a phenomenal job on these.The beast designs are both unique and random, ranging from a sad water tap to a cat with a flat screen for a head. If you like weird and fun designs, you'll like this game.The soundtrack consists of 80's/90's synths and rock. Some of the tracks even include vocals, which slap REALLY hard and still give me goosebumps everytime I hear them. Think Persona 5; just instead of jazz it's electric guitars and synths. It's really good.The game does have options for same-sex romance, along with the option for your character to have they/them pronouns. I'm indifferent on this, but maybe you might love/hate it. I'm not the one to really judge either way.The community is small but welcoming. The people in the discord server are a great bunch of lads and are really supportive. The developers even also talk often in there. As far I see there is no toxicity at all.That's all I got to say; great game, I highly recommend it if you like fun, innovative gameplay, or even for the artsyle/music alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful experience, and I can highly recommend it to anyone who is even remotely interested in RPGs. The mechanics, writing, music, characters - all impressively good for what I would typically expect from a "Pokemon-like" game. It is basically a love letter to what Pokemon could have become in a world without greed. I plan on returning back to this some time from now to complete my bestiary and experience the post-game for sure. Will definitely be attempting to full clear achievements on it, it's that enjoyable!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Pokemon Infinite Fusion and Persona combined. Cassette Beasts is that plus the single greatest soundtrack I've ever heard. Even if you find turn-based combat boring, the music will have you hooked. Controllable AI intelligence and scaling pushes this into a 10/10, can and will recommend to anyone.
