_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is an interesting take on the mon genre (monre) that passes more often than it fails when it comes to presenting a cohesive experience.Major disclaimer: this game might resemble a popular mon game series. This game, while borrowing elements of that series, is absolutely NOT like that game in the least. You will be mercilessly obliterated in your battles if you think it is. Prepare for shenanigans. We're entering romhacklike territory.Pros:- Colorful monster designs are inspired and not at all derivative or overly generic (glances at temtem). You can definitely make out each monster's visual influences even when they're smushed together with other monsters, or evolved ("remixed").- The sticker system presents an enormous amount of mix and match potential for almost any pick you go with. You might find yourself favoring other picks over your starter as more choices are made available to you.- No monster breeding means that you can just obtain one tape of any given monster and not have to endlessly fish for optimal stats or moves. (glances at temtem again)- You still have a reason to acquire more monster recordings because you can use extras for materials or fishing for more stickers. If you like collecting things, there's no shortage of hoarding here.- Gameplay is quite challenging. You will find yourself often on the back foot because new faces and gameplay elements can turn a situation on its head very quickly. On the other hand, you might just find a way past the problem just as quickly as things spiral out of control. Sometimes the problems are the solutions?...- Music, as a core theme of the game, is the game's strongest element and continues to impress at every turn, as long as you're into the aesthetic it is presenting.- The only thing that gates you off from advancing is the main story and unlocking new modes of overworld movement. Everything else is your choice as you see fit, no matter how reckless this is.Cons:- The visual aesthetic is somewhat muddled, even given the context of the multiversal trash pile that the game world is set in. This makes it sometimes difficult for the theme of "80's/90's americana I guess???" to get across through these limitations.- The game somewhat suffers from romhack mechanical overload, which misses the point of the most popular mon's pick up and play style. (Of course, since this is a common problem to have, you mostly have yourself to blame if you go searching for somebody else's take on the monre.) This is somewhat alleviated by the fact that the game does take the time to explain new mechanics to you when they happen, but oftentimes you'll get bogged down in multiple pratfalls when some elemental matchups cause numerous status effects to pile up in a chain reaction that can feel somewhat discouraging when you get penalized two or three times by different things that happen from one mistake. Of course, it is somewhat evenhanded in that some mistakes can actually result in benefits for you, but all of this is happening by accident and makes the experience vary greatly between players for no other reason than luck of the draw from your previous choices. This can make counterplay and mitigation difficult to perform on the fly.- Having so many choices can easily lead to choice paralysis. This is even more of a problem if your monster has multiple evolution paths, and then on top of that we find out that stickers have rare variants that are better and have additional effects. Thankfully, given how flexible the game makes everything, if a choice doesn't work out, you're not super committed to it forever, or even in five minutes of resourceful thinking.- Materials are somewhat of a chore to farm early on until you get your footing, since most fights are never as simple as you think they would be, and there's no settings option to skip attack animations.- If you eat ♥♥♥♥ because you picked a fight a bit too big for your britches, you will lose a significant (to a new player) amount of resources, and then the game salts the wound by autosaving afterwards. It will also give you some healing items to help you, but if you went into a fight that killed you so fast you couldn't use them (action economy is extremely tight in most battles), it's somewhat unintentionally insulting, and you can't even hold them if you were already holding the maximum amount of healing items when you were wrecked. Although you can't lose anything that isn't replaceable, this can be extremely punishing to newer players who just wanted to see if they can beat a new challenge that they can only sort of guess how strong it is because enemy sprites are all roughly the same size in the overworld. Losses should have been scaled more towards relative player levels rather than a set percentage for the entire playthrough if the players are encouraged to take risks in a very off the rails experience, as there are no backsies if you fall down a hole filled with angry monsters or catch the attention of anybody dangerous.- Battles are somewhat skewed in favor of your opponent (romhack syndrome part two), because the assumption is that you know what you're doing, except you don't if you're going in blind. Yes, breaking them over your knee is easy once you do know what you're doing. May the fates help you if you don't though.- All of the above elements leads many players to have to consult the wiki in fear of putting their foot in a beartrap, which seems somewhat counter to the game's presentation of a wilderness where freedom is king. This is definitely not the kind of thing you can pick up casually, which leads me back to my original major point; most mon games seem to favor mechanical complexity over being easy to pick up, and it's weird that players and developers think that mainstream mons are overly simplistic and that being easy is a negative thing.That being said, I can still recommend this game because they actually make this sort of design work for what they're shooting for, instead of being somewhat aimless like many romhacks. The design is tight enough that it can work with what its given, and that effort has largely paid off. The main thing you should be asking is if this kind of thing is your wheelhouse. Thankfully there's a demo for that.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of indie games that take a genre and make a masterpiece out of it, the I cannot recommend this game highly enough!The style is fun, whimsical and full of character. The music is incredible, the characters are deeply likeable and the monster designs are great. But the mechanics is where this game really shines!Other turn based games focused on creature collection can feel grindy. So this game ties your level to your character (and your companions never seem to drift far behind) so you can switch monsters without worry. This leads to more experimentation, and cleaner gameplay while still giving a sense of progression. The only grind I experienced is the post game, but by that point you're in too deep and its an excuse to stay in the world a little longer.The movement options given based on certain tapes you get don't feel like "Get this to do a specific thing to progress" but rather a constantly used part of your arsenal for traversing the world, tapping into experiences found in metroidvanias.The type matchups feels fresh through usage of effects dependent on the matchup, leading to more creative uses and strategies forming. (Like attacking your own beasts for the buffs, or strategic switching)The fusion mechanic feels great to use, and the addition of adding vocals to the soundtrack makes it feel amazing even when against a level 8 enemy.I feel like I have a whole bunch more to say but who's looking at steam reviews for an essay, so all in all, highly reccommend

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with pokemon so long ago, played every game, but slowly became jaded with newer entries. They didn't capture me quite the same- like somehow the "charm" they used to have lessened each time. The stories felt cheaper or more surface-level, new mons more lazily designed. I think for me, part of this was the transition from 2d to 3d. Cassette Beasts wasn't something I expected to love- my first thought was that it was probably another relatively uncreative ripoff with a new gimmick to make it stand out. Boy, was I wrong, and I'm so grateful to the friend who pushed me to try this.I have never written a review before, but I feel compelled to now. I am obsessed with this game. You can really feel the passion the devs have for it! It's innovative, it's original, and man, is it fun. The beasts are WAY more interesting than those in any other monster collecting game I have experienced, and at times, even more than Pokemon itself. The sprites are SO beautifully done and are EXACTLY what I would want out of a modern monster collector- they feel nostalgic but fresh all the same. The environments being 3d while the characters are pixelated/2d did throw me off a lot at first, as did the background music lyrics which were horribly distracting, BUT thankfully the devs added the ability to switch them off in the settings. With time, the mix of 2d/3d didn't really bother me at all, especially given everything else I love about this game. The inclusion of completely new element types (such as plastic, a personal favorite) and their unique interactions with one another made the battle gameplay feel much more energized. Being able to collect rare moves and switch them between beasts is also a huge plus, with different rarities carrying a variety of randomized boons such as +ignores walls or +% chance to activate at the beginning of battle. The "fusion" mechanic is really fun as well, and combines ANY- and I mean ANY of the beasts together in battle for one super-strong beast with its own unique sprite. Shinies, or "bootlegs" as they are called in CB, come with more than just a palette swap. They are more likely to learn rare moves, and can be ANY element- something that can completely switch the way you use it vs. its standard-type counterpart. If you are a shinydex collector, you have the opportunity to find FOURTEEN bootleg versions for every beast, EVEN legendaries! Finding bootlegs can be super addicting, and they spawn at a MUCH higher rate than pokemon- although it isn't so high that they lose their value. You can still go for hours without encountering one.I do wish the characters themselves felt more fleshed out. It would be nice to have character-specific activities (training with Eugene, writing poetry with Viola, drawing with Felix or playing fetch with Barkley, perhaps?) and more character-specific date events. I also think there is opportunity to add additional cast members, even if it's post-game. Frankie and Sunny come immediately to mind. My hope is that these things are expanded upon in the future. And I must say, the future of this game looks bright!Tl;dr- if you are jaded by monster collectors and are on the fence, absolutely go for it. I bet it'll exceed your every expectation like it did mine.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm stuck on whether to actually recommend this. The savvy type will see the overwhelmingly positive reviews and raise their eyebrow, sending themselves off to the negative reviews section because they know that even if they don't agree, they'll at least get a review with any semblance of critical thought*, because it's the only part of the review section meant to be about reviewing rather than as a marketing hype machine.That's the audience I want to reach, so I'm leaving this in the negative category.I want to preface this with saying that I haven't beaten the game. I'm going to tally that against the game, because it doesn't earn it's capacity to utilize it's own open world to control pacing. It very quickly feels like the majority of your time will be spent dodging very low level enemies who partially scale (at recommended settings) their stats (but never enough to facilitate an actual challenge), while ambling across a psuedo-samey puzzle-box like map structure, turning the game into a maze to navigate just to get to an area that you've either been in before to complete a quest, or a new area, probably to also complete a quest.The problems compound with it's structure working against it, the game has no method of guiding you to appropriate challenges or to appropriate points to reduce the inane backtracking. There are ways to fast travel but the methods of unlocking the places you can fast travel to feel almost arbitrary (One area is unlocked on the critical path, one is unlocked in a character side quest!). Couple this with meatgrinder battles that will slowly chisel you down and you quickly start to feel that the pace slowly simmers down between the interesting moments, as you check the map every few fights and backtrack to a rest point (bonfire, which you can't fast travel to) before moving on to fight more meatgrinder battles and dodge fights on the overworld and spam the run button when you fail to dodge....The interesting moments are whenever you encounter a new monster. Take that as damning praise against the rest of the game. This game shoots pokemon's "elegance in simplicity" design philosophy in the foot by pushing complexity in designs without straying from a core idea, rendering their more complex beasts instantly readable despite having more to look at. The game is a *bit* too reference heavy in it's designs to always completely land for me, but it's mostly drawing from historical or urban folklore that ends up being underutilized in the wider space. It's a matter more of preference whether that hits you or not, rather than the idea itself being trite. These little guys are consistently great, and I definitely appreciate the ubiquitous  artificial human creations (plastic in particular) becoming a natural element to draw from lean that alot of these designs utilize. It's real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unfortunate that the devs decides to put these good design philosophies in a game that's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hipster it's competing with YIIKOkay, that's quite an exaggeration. It's not....nothing is YIIK. This game wants to push itself as profound, and boy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ howdy do you feel it. You fight "trainer" battles with philosophers popular with the "i am smort" crowd, the fusion mechanic of the game always makes the obvious "lol its like sex" joke that I'm mostly mad at for starting to do it after I started taking the piss out of it, there are people in the game people call vampires that are actually just landlords, one of the bosses is "inspired by the concept of consumerism", you get the picture. I'm not one of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ conservative idiots who thinks "politics should be out of games", but you need to face the fact that you aren't leftists, like most liberals want to act like they are. You certainly don't earn the capacity to put Karl *♥♥♥♥♥♥♥* Marx in your game, I don't care for how briefly. The characters are very aggressively uninteresting, and flip between being daydreamy psuedo-philosophers, snark factories, and their character trait. Sometimes two of those at once, how's that for character depth!?That certainly doesn't stop them from talking to you until you think they're cool. Dialogue isn't...well it isn't Planescape, but there's enough from there that when I realized I'm completely uninterested in these people that I felt the attrition from spamming the skip button, much like Monster Hunter.That leaves battling. People are saying it's innovative. Sure, it is. Is it *good*? I'll tell you when I need to use it. I'm at around level 40 (side note: your level and therefore mon stats being attached to your character defeats it's own purpose when you need to level up your mons to get moves that allow them to compete anyway, unless you spam TM's, which isn't ridiculous because it isn't expensive, but it should be noted), and power has overwhelmingly consistently been the best strategy. If you don't know how it works, (although you've probably read another review that explained it but I'm just being thorough), instead of types interacting through varying levels of damage output, they interact through a series of buffs or debuffs depending on the type (single, there are no doubles except fusions) of the monster and the type of the move. A fire move hitting a wind mon will create a wall for the wind mon that will block two attacks is a fairly frequent example. A fire move hitting a grass mon will ignite them, giving them a dot. Like I already said, however, I've fairly frequently been able to brute force my way through because an enemy doesn't have the capacity to nuke me, and I always will have more mons, which, as someone who frequently plays hardcore nuzlockes, made me appreciate the pokemon battle system alot more than I did before. Man, I didn't realize until writing this review how much of the game I really considered a miss. I'll play to finish and I'll update the review with how I feel if it's changed, it's possible the characters might grow on me, or the battling gets genuinely involved, but, really I'm just playing through to see all the monsters this game has. Even the ones I like less were still absolutely great, I can't emphasize enough how much I like them.side note: the overworld has puzzles but theyre in the same league as botw, i didnt wanna dedicate a full paragraph to saying that lol*Edit: i checked the negative reviews section after i wrote this, boy was i wrong lol, i'm pretty sure this is the only thing resembling a review down here. hell there was a moron talking about jewish marxist propaganda lmaoEdit 2: The lead singer in the tracks of this game sounds disturbingly similar to Hayley Williams

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I'm one of the developers of Godot Engine, the game engine used by Cassette Beasts. So I'm naturally rooting for it to be a success that helps outline how versatile Godot is :) Still, I'm playing this on my free time and reviewing it from my perspective of a player fond of indie games.I'm only a few hours into the game so far, but what I've seen really ticks all the boxes for me. Fun and refreshing monster collection gameplay, amazing art direction and OST, and a pretty engaging story. I picked up the game for the first time when it released yesterday and I've had a hard time stopping playing to go to sleep at a reasonable hour ;)I'm eager to see more of the game, and I'll aim to update this review when I do with more in depth insights on what I enjoyed or not. But so far I love everything about it!Oh btw I'm playing on Linux, and it runs great, both on my laptop and on Steam Deck (where I'm going to play it through).---Edit after 20h in-game: Yep, I still love it. It actually gets better after a few hours when you really dive into exploding the overworld, and start recording or "remastering" (evolving) some of your more experienced monsters. You get access to new skills which make the combat a lot more interesting, as well as progressively getting more possibilities to navigate the overworld, unlocking new areas and secrets.I got to find my first 3 bootlegs in the wild, which are slightly more powerful versions of the monsters with a different element, and those quickly found their way to my favorite rooster :)There's overall more content than I first expected, seeing how I haven't beat the game yet. The overworld map didn't feel very big initially when I started exploring it and discovering big chunks in a short time, but it's actually pretty satisfactory.I'm having a lot of fun capturing new monsters, trying to find bootleg versions of them, reading their witty descriptions - Djinn Entonic is my favorite - and experimenting with different play styles.I'm a bit overwhelmed by the sheer number of monsters I now have available, combined with the "stickers" system to assign skills, which makes me feel like I might have to spend a lot of time micro-optimizing the assigned stickers whenever I change the composition of my party. But I mostly play casually and don't bother too much, I'm still powerful enough to go through most areas, and just need to be a bit tactical on big boss encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 11/21 Nominated Best on Deck. Good luck!Cassette Beasts very quickly shot to the top of my favourites list after just a couple of hours with it. If you're like me and you played Pokemon for years, but didn't enjoy the more recent entries for one reason or another then this game might just fill that void. I find that with a lot of monster collecting RPGs (Nexomon and TemTem, for example) I'm always wondering when my monsters are going to evolve because I'm so used to the conventions laid by Pokèmon. It's a bit grating, finishing a battle, levelling up, and... Nothing. There's no wondering in Cassette Beasts: The system that developer Bytten Studio has in place—a star ranking that raises with each battle until it hits level 5 and then your Beast is ready to evolve—is perfect. I also liked that some monsters had branching forms. Progress feels good and the fact that you can remove and reuse moves at will to build the perfect moveset is brilliant.If any of the following interest you, I would suggest picking it and it's fantastic OST up:*An example of that last one is Rock versus Grass. In Pokèmon, sure, one would do extra damage to the other, but in Cassette Beasts, Grass striking Earth means the Earth type will get seeded, providing your Grass Beast with HP regen. Say whaaaaa? Some of them are just logical: attack a Plastic type with a Fire move and you get a Poison effect as a result. So cool.I could go on about how area progression is unlocked by acquiring new Beast forms to unlock over world abilities and how great the writing is. I could gush about the pixel art style and how wonderful and vibrant the world is. I could tell you all about how this game breathes life back into a tired genre.  Instead, I'll urge you to top off your Steam wallet and get this game. It is definitely a labour of love and well worth the asking price.

The characters are cute and endearing but they just don't go deep enough for me to really be invested in the story enough to want to go on eitherMain problem with this game is a problem I have with leveling systems in general. You're doomed to always be overleveled by the end if you do any amount of side quests. I just don't like stat-increasing leveling systems outside of roguelikes because of this.7/10 Nothing really wrong about it, a lot of interesting stuff but goes on too long for it's own good and becomes uninteresting to me

_childDocuments_.review: When PalWorld came out, I heard people talking about other monster-collecting games and this game came up quite a bit. It happened to be on sale at the time, so I picked it up. It's a good time, overall: the elemental mechanics are generally satisfying to use (and eventually break across your knee), the music is decent (the combat tracks are a highlight, though admittedly I am a  for tracks that add vocals at times of hype), and the artwork is all really good. I have only a couple nitpicks about the main game:- The comedy is really hit or miss. For me it was more misses, but there were some good moments.- The ending kinda sucks.- I only really found myself interested in Felix's story, and the Shakespeare references with Viola seem comically out of place.The post-game and 100% experience, on the other hand, soured me on it a bit.-Once you get into a potential rhythm of how everything works, you realize just how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long each combat is. Pokemon, for all its faults, has an option to turn off battle animations for a reason. I installed mods to speed up combat 5x

_childDocuments_.review: someone really thought "what if instead of capturing pokemon in a little ball shaped capsule, you recorded them to cassette tapes, and you transformed into the creatures instead of them fighting FOR you"originally pirated this game because over the years, I've become wary of all the monster catching games that try to cash in on pokemon's success without having enough to the game to really stand on its own merits, but I proceeded to buy this one on Steam after finishing it cuz this one's the real dealit's got its own type matchup chart, with buffs and debuffs specific to the type interaction, rather than just damage boosts, all battles are double battles, and the game does have its own equivalent to trainer battles, there's level scaling, and unlockable randomizer/nuzlocke modes after you beat the game once, has an explorable open world with similar progression to pokemon Scarlet/Violet, in that you gain new abilities from certain creatures, which help you explore more of the world, move customizability is far more variable and accessible, "shinies" in this game are more than just a palette swap - they're a palette swap, but are called "bootlegs" and can be any other type that that creature normally isn't, banger OST, cool characters, and most of allYOU CAN BE GAY
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing this after 100%It's probably my favourite creature collector of all times. I've been searching for a long time for that Pokemon-but-with-a-twist formula and Cassette Beasts has really scratched that itch for me. It is currently my favourite game of the genre. The gameplay is awesome and very fluid. Upgrading monsters is not very grindy (unless you are going for all achievements) but it still has a degree of challenge to it. If you are familiar to games similar to Pokemon, you'll understand right away that this game brings something fresh to the genre. Overall 10/10 from me. The soundtrack...man. It is out of this world. Greatest soundstrack to a game I've heard in a long time. It is one of the only ones I've actually wanted to buy (and I'm also listening to it on Spotify, for free, which is saying something). I wanted to offer as much support as I can to the artists and the producers. You can also buy a real cassette with this soundtrack, but you have to hunt those stocks though. It took me almost 70 hours to 100% this game. You can probably do it in less time but I took my sweet time. I highly recommend this game. It is a steal even for the full price, compared to the content it gives.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: With 25% of all players having progressed to late stage achievements that take many hours the percentages speak for themselves.I really wish I could write these comments without referring to Pokemon but I just can't. It's a "catch em all" em up and there's just no getting around that fact. What most people will find surprising is that this small (just over 600mb) game by an indie development team is far superior to any of the other games of its genre. It's also pretty amazing in an age where games can be close to 200GB exactly how much can be achieved with vastly lower use of data space. The graphics are typically cutesy made from a combination of pixel, voxel, and cell shading. I'd refer to them as Zelda-esque but there are also areas that can remind you of Mario 3D without the full rotating views. In fact much of the game is centred around working out how to get to certain areas so there is a fair amount of puzzle element to the game. Combat will be instantly familiar to anyone who has played a catch em all before but the range of moves and custom skills on offer here far surpass any others. The music is also very pleasant - not something I usually take a lot of notice of. Add to this a fairly large cast of characters and companions, rpg like questing and multiple quest threads, and you have an absorbing and fun game that is worth every penny of its asking price and some. What a sublimely designed game! 95%This should absolutely be entered in the end of year awards.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the atmosphere, the graphics and the music. But the game itself just isn't for me. Even with level scaling turned off the battles are a grind and the puzzles just aren't interesting due to the sometimes janky physics. I would have loved to like it enough to finish it, but I just can't put myself to see it through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a fantastic RPG and I cannot recommend it enough. Though the Pokemon influence is obvious, at no point was I left feeling like the game wanted to *be* Pokemon. It has its own distinct identity and style. The music, the monster designs, the graphical style, even the twists on the gameplay all give the game a distinct feel that left me feeling like...well, I was playing Cassette Beasts instead of Offbrand Pokemon.I'd also like to mention that the game itself is surprisingly earnest and sincere. If you're annoyed anytime something resonant is undercut by jokes or sarcasm or silly references, you're not gonna find much of that here. There's plenty of funny, silly or just plain bizarre things to see, of course! But when the game's story touches on something serious, it takes itself seriously. And I really appreciate that in this day and age.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most competent creature collector games on Steam.Pros:-Type advantages are handled in a very refreshing way. "Super effective" attacks debuff opponents rather than just doing more damage, and "resisted" attacks buff opponents instead of just doing less damage.-The action points system adds strategy to movesets and encourages a balance of low and high AP moves.-Party characters are fleshed-out, having development arcs instead of being one-note personalities.-Soundtrack is PHENOMENAL. Town theme is very cozy, while the battle themes get you pumped up. AND THERE ARE VOCAL TRACKS, which is really cool.-The theme of cassettes is maintained very well, potions and revives are tools to rewind cassette tapes, like pencils.-Monsters stats are tied to player level, so it's easy to swap out teammates without worrying about grinding.Cons:- While most of the spriting and animation is good, some are a bit off- Only one attacking animation per monster, whether doing melee or ranged attacks- There is little structure in terms of progression, so it's easy to be a bit overwhelmed with all of the quests that require explorationOverall, this game is an easy 9/10, and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants something that shakes up the classic Pokemon-esque formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is an iteration on classic Pokemon that improves on everything that made those games excellent.Combat is more strategic, the catch mechanic has an excellent risk/reward system, mistakes while leveling don't exist, and all the monster designs are fun and inventive.The music is an absolute banger, cover-to-cover. The art and narrative are consistently solid.While family-friendly, the game never condescends to the player.No distasteful cash grabs or perverse monetization. Just good vibes.A modern classic!
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is one of the few creature collection games that doesn't just steal from the Pokémon formula. With distinct enough ideas to stand on its own, the game stands at about 20 hours to complete the main story. It includes post-game content too so you can definitely get several hours more out of this.The battle system is unique and encourages more tactical thinking, and with an AP system it doesn't punish the player for using stat-based moves or switching casettes, as doing so can store up AP for more powerful moves. You can also more easily make your favourite beast your main cassette, as the sticker system makes it easy to give them powerful moves.The game runs smoothly even on lower-end devices and I've never encountered any glitches. I absolutely love this game, and the critique is sparse. Here's a few things that could improve the game for the developers, but in its current state I'd still highly recommend it.The amount of different types makes things confusing at times. The game gives you a guide, but it's a hassle to memorise it. Being able to see what moves would be weak / strong against your opponent would go far. The game actually does have this feature but only for major bosses. Bringing this into every fight would be helpful, especially since certain moves actually boost the enemy, so using the wrong ones punishes the player a lot.As well as this, the beasts have symbols to indicate their type instead of words. This becomes a little more inconvenient when the type-tapes you use have words. Putting the symbol on the tapes description too would be very helpful in avoiding confusion.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of review, I also have 100 hours in the Game Pass version of this game, after which I decided to buy the game on Steam.Cassette Beasts is a creature collecting game which naturally leads to the first question of: How does it compare to a game like Pokemon? In my opinion, Cassette Beasts does its own unique spin on the genre very well, and I'd argue as an avid shiny Pokemon hunter that the bootleg system implemented in this game is superior, which is where I'd really like to take this review as someone who is a big fan of having a huge grind to chip away it, this game really scratches the itch. There are 14 types in Cassette Beasts, and every creature can have a bootleg of any type, so for example a Traffikrab is normally a Plastic type, however you can find a bootleg Ice Traffikrab, or Fire, or Astral, you name it. Each creature has a section of its bestiary entry dedicated to showing which bootlegs you've acquired of the creature. On top of that, creatures can also fuse together with each other, and all 128 creatures can fuse with all 128 creatures (so yes, even itself!) to form over 16,000 possible fusions. Which are also recorded in the Bestiary. So yeah, if, like me, you're a lover of the grind, and a fan of this type of game at all, this game does an amazing job of giving you a lot to do. Of course, if you're not a grinder that isn't to say the game isn't good, it's fantastic regardless, and absolutely worth your time. I just wanted to talk a little bit about the full completionist nature of the game as it may encourage some masochists like myself to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts had been sitting in my wishlist for a while, mostly out of fear that another upcoming monster taming game would be underwhelming. IMO if a game can put a nice spin on the genre and actually attempt to face the BEHEMOTH that is Pokemon, hats off to them. Giving Cassette Beasts a chance was a great gamble-Story: 7/10The type of open world game that throws multiple objectives on the map and is like "go do all this to complete the game" which isn't my really my cup of tea, but really fun nonetheless-Art: 9/10All the character portrait art and promotional art is phenomenal along with the world and creature design, but the open world sprites felt... off, for lack of a better term. (only when exploring the map, not during battle. Those sprites are nice)  -Monster Design: 7/10   At the time of typing this I haven't completed my Bestiary, but all of the monsters I've encountered have really charming designs. The game kind of loses me at the fusion mechanic though (Granted I know for the sake of game creation they could give every possible fusion it's own hand made sprite, but some of the fusions look a tad goofy)-Soundtrack 1000/10This soundtrack goes HARD! and its only supported by the fact the the music gets more dynamic if you engage with the in-game mechanics. the same mechanic also applies to the mellow town theme. being instrumental as you walk around town, but entering a building ramps up with vocals for an even soother tone-Combat: 9/10Made me think more than in Pokemon. Instead of individual moves having a use amount, you build up spendable points each turn that you can use on said moves. Instead of types just doing more or less damage to each other, they have specific reactions with the games chemistry system, which makes battles less of a mash A simulator. There's also and essence of resource management since you can only hold a limited number of healing items. Now I can't just buy a million revives and beat my opponent via war of attrition-Misc Notes  -The companion are cool and all have pretty compelling stories that are really grounded in the setting. Although some companion quests take you to late game before you can fully utilize them  -The mix of 2D sprites in a 3D environment could be jarring to some people, but I think that's what makes it charming  -OMG the boss designs are so cool and I wish I could ramble about them but its definitely something a new player should go in blind to  -The open world puzzles aren't the most attention grabbing, but they are a nice break from constant questing/leveling/farming and who doesn't like some free goodies
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. It's not as crunchy as Siralim, but it makes up for it with engaging puzzles, innovative gameplay, and a delightful story. The combat is fun, the difficulty is solid, and bootleg hunting is more addicting (and rewarding) than shiny hunting ever was. I took 50 hours to beat Cassette Beasts my first time, and I was running into new mechanics every few hours. I cannot commend the devs enough for doing what Gamefreak and others have failed to do in the past years. The creators of Cassette Beasts put their entire heart and soul into this project, and it shows. Grab this game now, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: The blend of Persona-style monster-fusion and open, online Monster-catcher/Pokemon style gameplay are novel and enjoyable. However, the music, character designs, and on-rails hand holding bog down the experience somewhat. The designs and music are inoffensive, but they aren't particularly gripping either; the use of lighting and shadow on the models, the shapes and proportions of the monsters, as well as the cadence of a lot of the music makes the game suited for more relaxed, but also less focused, engaging, or cohesive world feel. Worth a play if you want a cool spin on the Monster-catching/Pokemon formula, but not if you want a really cohesive one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that's relatively close to Pokemon and Digimon, but also utilizes the 2v2 format? Look no further! Cassette Beasts breathes a lot of new life into the genre! At first I didn't know what to think, but after spending a good chunk of time with the game, I've grown to love it a lot! The references to hit pop culture from the 80s is also phenomenally done! (Spoiler free of course!)One twist the game offers is that instead of catching the beasts you find out in the wild, you transform into them with your cassette player! In a way, it reminds me of a Digivice from Digimon! *insert nostalgia vibes* Funny enough, the game bares more resemblance to Digimon; there are different paths that your beasts can evolve on (some beasts even have 3 remaster options). Monster types even vary a lot, especially when it comes to mixing monster combos for new and strong fusions (a similar aspect for Digimon with DNA Digivolution as well as Pokemon Infinite Fusion, you can utilize both movesets within the newly created beast)!Story wise it all fits nicely in its package; flavorful and memorable characters, twists and turns applied, and subplot tied in with main plot! I have to hand it to Bytten Studios, I don't get attached to a lot of games, and this one really sealed the deal for me on numerous factors! It just hits all the right spots!Ratings:Story: 9/10Nostalgia: 10/10Gameplay: 10/10*insert shameless plug* If you're curious about the gameplay, I happen to have a playlist made for the entire story!Though I will say, if you want to check the game out for yourself, definitely pick it up! I would HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who enjoys Pokemon and Digimon, as well as other monster catching/taming games! While the game doesn't have multiplayer yet, it will at some point once the Piers of the Unknown free DLC comes out (there's no confirmed date just yet, but hoping this year for the 8 player multiplayer update)

_childDocuments_.review: Y'all are inevitably going to compare this to pokemon, and I'm not even gonna pretend that my lifelong love of those games isn't exactly why I bought this. Which is a damned shame, because this game really isn't quite that. I mean, nothing much manages to have the sort of charming monster design and style that pokemon has, but this game feels like its more interested in making a name for itself on other strengths, namely being a really  little JRPG, and I'm not sure how else to describe the vibe of this game, but I absolutely love it.Like, you meet NPC companions, and they all just kinda give off this same, really charming vibe of "We're all in this together" that meshes well with the setting, and just gives the game cozy feels. It captures the  you're looking for in a game trying to capitalize on your nostalgia for older games in its genre without actually trying to  the same as those games in a really masterful way I've never seen before.But it's polished and modern and just  in a way that alone makes it worth recommending. It's got good  and  behind it, despite me coming in skeptical that the cassette thing would be more of a weird retro gimmick from a decade before I was born, but no, it's just , at least from the first few hours I've seen.And the turn-based combat going on has strong pokemon vibes but is clearly trying to make for its own identity- the type chart (which the game hands you as an item early on, and you're free to check in battle, thank god) is mostly built around free status conditions, positive and negative, rather than big damage buffs, and it's a solid take. I'm having fun.Strong recommend on a game I was half expecting to refund when I bought it, tbh. I've been disappointed in enough retro-styled games like this that want my nostalgic-for-old-pokemon money that I was going in skeptical, and was proven soundly incorrect.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing Cassette Beasts entirely, I have to say this has been one of the most refreshing and entertaining sorts of monster-catching game I’ve ever played, as the charm, aesthetics and music all work together perfectly to create something that goes far beyond the gameplay itself in terms of the meaning and messages that are conveyed in the game. While I won’t go into too much detail to avoid giving spoilers to anyone that hasn’t played it through to completion, I will at the very least say that the gameplay, story, soundtrack and deeper meaning behind the game and the events that unfold within it are likely to keep me coming back for more playthroughs. The gameplay itself very much is reminiscent of franchises like Pokémon, of which I am a long-time fan, so the combat felt familiar enough for me to easily grasp the combat system, but still felt complex in its own right and different enough that it was fun to learn how to make the most of my adventure throughout its world, with plenty of new mechanics that can help to make each and every beast in the game unique and worth learning about and experimenting with. The combat felt incredibly engaging on a regular basis and really demanded my attention to make the most of every fight, and the way that enemies scale in power to make them a challenge to handle even in later parts of the game really helped to keep my attention focused on getting as much done in the world as possible and making the most of every single monster that I could get my hands on. The story takes a simple trope of waking up in an unfamiliar world and makes it feel fresh and colorful in the wide cast of characters that you come across over the course of a journey, and I can’t say that I was ever disinterested in the adventure, both in term of NPCs and those that are playable in the course of the game. Everyone feels like they’ve got personality and just enough background to make them all stand out distinctly, and they all mesh together well to create a gaggle of characters you feel invested in learning more about and how they have come to find themselves working for the betterment of all around them in the world the game takes place in. You honestly will grow to feel attached to them all as the game progress, and that attachment to them, whether it be heroes of villains, helps to make the game stand out from others where the characters in a game might only relevant for short periods of time here and there.The soundtrack of the game if perhaps one of the most standout features and something I highly recommend also investing in if you’re looking for something totally original that goes far beyond the sort of music you might otherwise expect from a game like this. The music is just as colorful and vibrant as the world the game takes place in and really helps to keep you engaged mentally as you make your way through your journey, with tracks that help to set the tone wherever you might be in the game. The fact that vocals can even come with the music is highly impressive and is something I normally would expect to only see in a high-budget video game production, so the extra effort that was taken with the soundtrack there is more than appreciated. Lastly, I just want to briefly mention that the game is much more than just a game in its existence, as it offers fresh perspectives into the way that our world interfaces with the world the game takes place in and fiction as a whole, and I was not expecting for it to really hit me as hard as it did. Not only are there emotional moments that really serve to tug at the heart stings in how you can relate to the characters, but what they represent in this world and what meaning can be gleamed from the events that unfold in it proved to be profound to me, and highly enlightening in regards to how the dreams and thoughts of people everywhere can create things greater than our expectations might otherwise ever imagine. There’s so much more I could say, but at the very least, the game is one that will leave you thinking about its events long after playing it, in ways too numerous for me to truly mention. As a whole, I can’t recommend this game enough and honestly found it to be a thrill ride with plenty of secrets and messages within it that everyone should give a try for the sake of experiencing it and the amazing adventure it presents for all those that choose to delve into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've completed the story at this point and my stance on this game is largely unchanged. I've touched up my review a bit to elaborate on some things I was too brief on but that's about it. I will say that the final boss is at least decent in the first phase, though the second phase ends up being a glorified cutscene which is pretty disappointing. The ending is also really abrupt, which didn't really bother me but will probably upset anyone who actually likes any of the characters besides Viola (whose character motivation is clear and consistent enough for her behavior at the end to actually make sense) and Barkley (who is a very good boy).----From a raw gameplay standpoint Cassette Beasts is a pretty good game, and if that's all you're after then the current "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating is warranted. It's not perfect - I have issues with some of the UI (too many button presses to perform basic tasks, no confirmation window for irreversible actions like sending party members to storage or fusing) mechanics (unlocking new fast travel points / shortcuts is much more annoying/tedious than it needs to be, Eugene's fusion unlocking at endgame when he's one of the starter characters is baffling design) and balancing (Coaldron is such a mess that it can't use its own level up moves, meanwhile stack 7 Random Starters and a 10AP attack of your choice on a glass cannon and you'll auto-win every fight forever) - but it's overall a refreshing take on the mons genre that's mechanically solid enough that I wanted to keep playing until the end of the story in spite of the rest of this review.The writing however is a  miss. Some other reviews mention woke elements, but honestly they aren't that bad. You have a 3-choice pronoun selection at the start of the game; a bunch of characters with neon hair; and a partner lineup with 1 white (female, Irish) character, 1 ambiguous character with dyed hair, 3 black characters, and a dog; but that's as far as it goes. It's the  that gets me.Several of you have already pressed the jester award button just from reading that much, but if you haven't, please hear me out. There are random philosophers as NPC trainers throughout the world who spout one-liners related to whatever they're most famous for saying, then they lose all relevancy forever because they're just NPC trainers. Most of the partner conversations that weren't utterly forgettable were full of navel-gazing, the main exceptions being Viola (who actively refuses to navel-gaze and is the most based character in the game because of it) and Barkley (who is a dog).The society of New Wirral is pretty clearly trying to portray socialism...or more accurately the quasi-socialist  that so many modern liberals think is cool. If the game's portrayal of "socialism" functioned on more than an aesthetic level, or if it wasn't trying so hard to deliver a message rather than just being a good vibes "all-in-this-together" society, I wouldn't be nearly as scathing as I'm about to be."From each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs" does  mean "you can do what you feel like and if that's sitting at home all day every day nobody will bother you about it" but that's sure how the game treats it. Similarly, in order to seize the means of production  but New Wirral is a disorganized blob of vibes that subsists off of interdimensional detritus and expects a single pumpkin patch to feed everyone. This admittedly works, but only because the pumpkins are video game enemies that respawn faster than you can kill them. New Wirral also straight up  (probably because all the landlords are literally vampires - yes, it really is that unsubtle) and instead relies on barter and favors, which is technically possible in the world as shown, but only because the canonical population is less than 1000 people, everyone who might possibly have less than pure intentions is cartoonishly obvious about it, and the island gets a constant influx of basic resources and refined goods for free so nobody has to bother with things like "infrastructure", "manufacturing facilities", or "supply chains". Even electricity production gets waved away with vague comments about an "energy field"! The only reason this society lasted a full century is authorial fiat, which means the whole thing stops being applicable to the real world and the message is shot in the foot.I think the best summary is that the game has an entire dungeon and boss fight that's all about lecturing the player about the emptiness of consumerism and the need to spend less time and money on hollow things like...video games...when it A) costs $20, which might not sound like much, but the take only needs to be split between 2 people and most games with this heavy an anti-consumerism message are either less than $10 or explicitly give a sizable chunk of profits to charity; and B) will take most players at least 20 hours to beat the main story, while still having a bunch of postgame content + a randomizer mode specifically designed to encourage people to play the game forever. Again, this game has "go outside" as one of its core messages.I hang out with  and they aren't anywhere  as insufferable as this game can be. And their arguments are occasionally somewhat convincing, too.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a creature-capture RPG with  a great soundtrack, likable characters, and of course, a great lineup of cool monsters.Most characters carry cassette players. Wild monsters you encounter can be 'recorded' to cassettes, and characters physically transform by listening back to the cassettes.Battles are turn-based, and use an energy system for moves. More powerful moves need more energy. You get a little energy each turn.All monsters have a type. Some are elemental, like fire, water, wind, etc. Others are more modern, like plastic, glass, and metal types. Types have advantages over others, but it goes deeper than just "does more damage." When a water attack hits a fire type, it 'extingushes' it, giving the fire type a debuff on its own attack. But if a fire move hits a plant type, it causes a guaranteed burn status that does damage every turn. These are just the absolute basics, there are plenty more type interactions that cause various buffs, debuffs, or status effects.Possibly the most innovative feature of this game is the ability to temporarily fuse any two monsters into a gnarly new beast during battles. You also always have a swappable companion to accompany you on your adventure.I really like this game, and I highly recommend it. It runs great, looks great, and most importantly, it's fun. Also, 20 bucks is a steal for the amount of content you get.

_childDocuments_.review: Very forgiving, relaxing, comfortable creature collector. The best part of the game for me is how it allows you to customize your creatures however you want basically whenever you want. There are interesting moves (stickers) that are passive or interact with other moves- whether it be by type or order in the list. You can swap these and any active moves at will. Your creatures can be as deep or as shallow in move or partner synergy as you want. You can go back to any zone, you can avoid pretty much any fight, and every monster is accessible. The whole game is accessible. It really doesn't punish you and frequently rewards you.I'm honestly just taking my time with it and not reading any guides on meta or game completion. I would recommend you do the same! Don't worry so much!I would recommend the game just because of the Cafe song "Wherever We Are Now" by Shelby Harvey and Joel Baylis (It's on Spotify).I would also recommend the game just because of Kayleigh

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts feels like a game made by true fans of the genre. Everything about this games is just so well done, if you’re a fan of Pokemon or creature collectors this is an absolute 10 out of 10 experience and a must play. Definitely a top contender of my personal contender for indie GOTY. Unlike the other games in the genre cassette beasts gets going really fast with minimal handholding, just the occasional text bubble of how mechanics and type matchups work as there are some very interesting typings here that shake up the formula. Combat is fast and never feels like a chore of endless grinding. Me and a friend having been playing through it side by side on the hardest difficulty for reference and it’s still not overly challenging for veterans of these games but I always appreciate it when games let you decide your own difficulty or just make the game brutal as I love a solid, rewarding experience. The only thing I wish was that the game made one of its unique mechanics, fusions, a bit more of a requirement on the hardest difficulty. But I’m pulling at strings here as that is nearly a nitpick if I must say one thing, and that never detracts from the experience. Exploration is fun, and fast as the developers implemented a ton of movement mechanics that make exploring the world feel incredibly satisfying. Being a game called Cassette Beats and probably by reading some of the other reviews you’ll come to learn that the soundtrack here is absolutely fantastic. Lots of great tracks at all the right moments make the experience so so much better. The tender vocals of the track that plays while in town really just bring such a sense of belonging and warmth, and if that’s not your cup of tea they give you the option to just play with the instrumental soundtrack. Trainer captains, this games equivalent of gym leaders, bring along more intense tracks with hard hitting guitar riffs that really amplify the moment. It’s all just done so well. Had another friend watching a stream in the discord who began singing the music as he also found it so enjoyable to listen to. If this game pops up on your steam recommendations you would be doing yourself a huge disservice by passing up on it. And I mean that wholeheartedly. I know a game like cassette beasts won’t be what every gamer is necessarily looking for and that’s okay. But for those looking for an absolute indie gem in a sea of games that either waste your time or are just utter hot garbage, this is the exact opposite. A true masterpiece of an experience and the team who worked on this should be regarded incredibly highly. I for one will be patiently awaiting a well deserved sequel and if you take the 30ish hours to get through this I’m sure you will be too. TLDR: Overwhelmingly positive reviews don’t do this same justice, if you even clicked on this title just do yourself the favor and add it to your cart. It’s easily worth so much more than the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review by saying that I loved this game. I wouldn't play 90 hours of it and 100% it if I didn't really enjoy my time with this game. That being said, I'm an overly critical person and this game is certainly not perfect. So the good: It's essentially a 2-dev game with custom artwork for all the combinations of all 128   and it's really neat that they put such care into the art. The art itself is also unique and distinct, and the tailored lyrics to the situation your character is in is really interesting to see a game do. The type mixes are confusing, but they're at least scientific, and hey - I liked that it was grounded in more realistic chemical reactions than arguably a lot of creature collector games. Alongside all that, the story itself was engaging and compelling and I haven't enjoyed a creature collector game story in a good ten years. It was mysterious, and kept me wanting to learn more and play further. And it was never easy to guess what would happen. The archangel designs contrasting the game's aesthetic was also a really cool feature, and the bootleg versions of creature types and sticker TMs really gave you a lot of customisation for your teams, along with the fusion. This game was an enjoyable game. But it was also incredibly frustrating, and here's why. I'm gonna be brief: There's a lot of late-game crashes that increase the more you use your sprint/dash. The game cannot load in the world as quickly as you can sprint, and even the "loading in the rest of the world" jarring, out of place loading screens do nothing to help the loading issues. And if the game can't load it in, it either completely stops your character with an invisible wall or hard-crashes your game. The character relationships are ok but ultimately disappointing - The characters are kind of boring, get better as you get to know them but even then, they're pretty mid, and spoilers: but none of the relationships are meaningful nor ultimately matter because you - and the characters themselves - leave it all behind, even with a romantic relationship. Which is weird, because you get the excuse "I can't go there" but then the dog can, so why can't anybody else? Another complaint is that the game  favours Kayleigh, and you lose out on a lot of early game lore, dialogue and flavour-text about your situation and even game mechanics if you ditch Kayleigh and go with Eugene or someone. Which is nuts, because the game is barely voice acted, so it wouldn't have taken them much to adjust early scenes for other companions. So the whole relationship/romance system is there, but ultimately feels hollow. Speaking of hollow, the stickers/TMs and bootlegs somewhat trivialise the gameplay. It ended up being very min-max, with the "strat" being Glitter Kephri with Headshot and Random Starter, or a normal Kephri with "type-change" support that trivialises the types. I enjoyed the fact the game gave you that level of customisation because it gave me the freedom to choose beasts based on aesthetic choices, but kind of killed the incentive of trying out different beasts, because why would I bother when I could just change the sticker? The end grind is also pretty insulting. I finished the main story in 50 hours, and only realised there was "more" after seeing the achievements. The "more" is a handful of quests hidden behind fetch&carry "townboard" quests that have you running across the map (that loads in really slowly!) doing busy work in what is essentially radiant quest padding between levels. I had very much checked out of the experience by the end of the grind, even with the ritual candle "exploit" to speed up the process. It felt like a really lazy way to create extra content when it started really strong with unique quests, especially as this grind was only accessible at the very end. If you'd let me do these missions throughout the entire game? It wouldn't have felt half as terrible. But I found myself struggling to boot up the game for such a grind, which sucked, because it was so strong before that and the cracks started to appear.Anyway. It's not a bad game. It has flaws, but I enjoyed my time with it, and it's definitely worth the price, and an incredible job for a two-person team. I'll keep an eye on their future games for sure, and I don't regret my time with this game - but I'm content to uninstall this and never touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: So many great things to say about this game. The artsyle, music, and monster designs are all so fresh. I don't like to compare games to pokemon but this is exactly what I want out of a pokemon game. It has this great 2D/HD style with lots of nice bright colors that pop. The world is fun to explore and has you unlocking abilities that open up new areas and let you explore the world in different ways.The music is so relaxing and calm when it needs to be and then in the heat of a boss battle, you get this awesome soundtrack that picks up in pace. I love the small snippets of dialogue that some of the characters make during text scenes. It helps to give them a bit more personality hearing what they actually sound like.The monster designs are all so different and quirky with funny combinations that you can fuse together throughout the game. I wish there were even more but the fact that you can fuse any 2 leads to thousands of combos so I understand why there can't be more.This game has a semi-open world that expands as you unlock more traversable abilities. You can do any line of major quests (fight bad guys, progress story, fight the "gym leaders") and there are lots of fun side quests with supporting characters. This is one thing that pokemon scarlet and violet failed at providing as it was "open world" in the sense that you could go anywhere, but it was not scaled properly. With cassette beast, it felt like almost anywhere I went, I could handle myself but there was still a threat if I wandered too far or for too long without healing.I really enjoy the combat system. It's almost always double battles so there are lots of unique strategies and combos to try out. The leveling system in this game is also a favorite of mine. You level your character and a monster simultaneously. The monster provides base stats on top of the character so you can switch to a weaker mosnter to level it and it won't be totaly useless. The moves can be swapped out and stored in a move bank that can then be put on another monster that is compatible. Overall I found it to be a mechanic that was  unique and time saving when I wanted it to be. I'm close to finishing the game. The story has been unique and has a cool cast of characters that make me want to complete all their story lines. The monster designs are great and I love trying out all the different fusion combos. For the price, this game is a great pickup and you won't be disappointed with the amount of content you get out of it. If they were to ever release more content or another game along these lines, I would pick it up in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna be real with you reader, Cassette beasts is an incredible experience, it does with 2 dudes and a modest budget what the most profitable franchise ever made couldn't with a bottomless budget and 160+ devs, it made a world I genuinely love just being in. New Wirral is not some modern 8 hours to travel from one end to the other open world filled with areas that serve zero purpose, every corner of the map every single area has things to do, not an ounce of space is wasted.The gameplay reminds me of Atlus's digital devil saga games crossed with Nintendo's big yellow money farting behemoth Pokemon. The elemental chemistry system feels like a genuine evolution of the old type effectiveness of yore, instead of just rewarding smart move usage with larger damage numbers Cassette beasts decides it's more fun if each type caused unique positive or negative statuses to the attacks recipient, like earth moves crippling electric's ability to hit multiple targets or poison moves being burned up as fuel by fire types causing them to gain increased energy generation. I could gush so much about the intricacies of combat but I think I've said enough.Now the soundtrack, god this soundtrack is perfect it enhances everything to such an absurd degree, the theme of Harbor town turns what would be a cute but not incredible little jrpg town into one of the coziest towns in gaming that I am just happy to be in. The battle themes are no slouch either special mention to "Same old story" and "Your inception" the latter being tied to one of the coolest pieces of fanservice to those who played Bytten studios previous game "Lenna's inception" another great game in it's own right.Look I could keep just gushing forever but please just play this game it deserves so much love, Bytten studio should be so proud of their work here because they've made something truly beautiful here and I look forward to anything they make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Not every monster collection game is a Pokemon knock-off and this game proves it! There is a lot more depth to this game since all the "type interactions" are status effects both positive and negative; no extra damage just because you picked the right type. The ability to rip moves from one monster and place onto another is so convenient as well to design your perfect moveset. The companions are great for helping set up combos and I appreciate the thought put into their backstories. Well, except Barkley, but come on, he's a cute-ass dog, what's not to love? All in all, much love for the story and monster development. Cannot recommend enough![EDIT]: Played through DLC and still fantastic. Very much enjoy the new monsters and stickers. _childDocuments_.review: This is without exaggeration the perfect monster-catching game. Fantastic art and monster design, an absolutely killer soundtrack, and progression that's insanely open-ended without ever feeling boring or aimless. The characters are amazingly likeable, the plot has a surprising amount of depth to it, and the world is just wonderful. I was hesitant to pick this one up because monster-catching games lost my interest many years ago, but whether or not you like the genre PLEASE PLAY THIS GAME. There's so much here that speaks to the level of love and dedication the devs have put into this game so if you're on the fence, just give it a shot! If you're anything like me, you'll be blown away.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looked forward to this game back when i first saw its trailer- and i had no regrets of it. Is it groundbreaking? No, but it certainly does quite a few different things to set it apart from other creature collecting games. One of the biggest being how type advantages do NOT dish out extra damage, they interact/change things. One example being how fire type attacks against a poison types cause the burn status effect, or hitting a plastic type with a fire type move turns it into a poison type. It forces you to be strategic and plan out how you use the creatures you capture on tape.Oh yeah, you turn into the monsters you capture.Anyways, onto the rest of the review. Otherwise this will get much longer than it should.Story/lore?Good for what it is and certainly had my interest. Leaves me wanting more in a good way. And i'm not afraid to admit i shed a tear toward the end after everything i did. That is all i can really say without spoiling anything.Characters?Different and none annoying- especially the companions you can get/choose from. They reach have a certain leaning toward certain stats, encouraging you to use certain monsters with them, but they do have a certain monster they like and get a 10% stat bonus from using that line. Showing they have a preference based on their character.Gameplay?This is one of those games where over leveling only does so much. It helps, but not as much as having a good build to counter the foe- especially when facing the bosses of the game- all of whom fight in a completely different manner. I will not spoil how they fight, as i found it very tense and satisfying to find out how each battle and plan accordingly. If you do not like overleveling, you can change the difficulty anytime on the settings. because they do scale up based on difficulty settings... Scarlet and Violet- take notes!Soundtrack?Love it. I love the vocal and non vocal versions of them. While i disagree that the vocal versions are somehow distracting, there is an option to turn off the vocals so you only get the music. Up to you.Replayability?After clearing story mode the first time, you unlock a custom mode where you can go full on nuzlocke mode, randomizing the monsters, typing- even the moves they learn. There is also a local coop, but i am not sure how that plays out. But it is there at least.Are there flaws?Some people have complained about crashes and bugs, but the only time anything like that happened to me was when i fell through the map- but that hardly set me back as i was put right where i was before that happened, so no harm done. I personally didn't have any issue with the game otherwise, but that might be the result of me being pretty casual. Some of the achievements do appear a bit... grindy, for the more dedicated sort.Verdict?If you really love creature collecting games in general or even an rpg where you can formulate your own strategy and ways of battling- i give this game a big thumbs up. Certainly feels like it has more love and effort put in than the last few pokemon games as of late- especially on release.

_childDocuments_.review: Review in short:"Cassette Beasts has a better story, theme, world building, level design, soundtrack and ideas than any Pokémon game in the last decade. An extremely solid game that goes beyond being just a 'Pokémon-like'."Info on how I played:* Played on PC* Played in single playerPro:+ Amazing OSTs+ Simple but effective character creator, with everything (also name and pronouns) that can be changed any time during the game+ Optional Quest Log+ Special types interactions+ Visible enemies on the world; no random encounters+ Original beasts' designs and names+ Difficulty settings+ All cassettes in the team gain exp+ Original mechanics (capturing beasts, world movement skills, fusions, ...)+ Good level design with shortcuts; well done open world with Metroidvania mechanics+ Interesting world building+ Good characters+ Post-game content+ Huge replayability thanks to special New Game options+ Unbelieavably huge amount of unique beasts sprites for fusions; each pair of beasts has one for a total of more than 16kCons:- Cannot remap joypad's controls- Captured bests go automatically to the "box" and cannot be added directly to the party- Cannot add pointers or markers to the map- Cannot skip or speed up animations, making battles against many enemies incredibly long- Completing the bestiary requires heavy RNG-based mechanics and some unclear ones- Bad handle of sorting/filtering of moves- Bad handle of re-ording beasts between the party and the "box"Miscellaneous:* Pokémon-like, but more JRPG* Cassettes' level is tied to evolving; in battle, it is the character's level that matters* The game is not all "happy and colorful", but has some relatively creepy parts and designs. It's NOT a horror game, mind you, but it's not a kids game either.* Strongly altered status-based combat system* [Minor spoiler] In order to finish the game, the player is required to solve a riddle which is "unique" to each game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't stop. It's so fun and the soundtrack is great. This is NOT a pokemon clone, to all you idiots that think pokemon has a monopoly on the taming genre.. Combat adds enough to the turn based formula to be compelling. I really enjoy the type advantage bonus' not just being an attack bonus. Example: Instead of water just doing more damage to rock type, it erodes it and provides a debuff for future attacks, or Electric on certain types providing a conductive debuff that makes all your follow up electric attacks chain to all conductive enemies. Turning earth enemies to glass type with certain attacks.The interactions with your followers are fun. Exploration had me hooked the majority of my time so far. I went to bed last night humming along to the soundtrack. Seriously A+

_childDocuments_.review: This really is a love letter to monster collection fans. The amount of QoL in Cassette Beasts compared to other games in the genre is frankly embarrassing for other publishers. Visuals: 8/10Sound: 9/10UI: 8/10Gameplay: 9/10Replayability: 10/10Your tapes (monsters) rank up to learn new moves and eventually remaster (evolve) into more powerful tapes. These moves are applied as stickers that you can freely peel and replace onto any compatible tape. There is a unique shiny system in this game known as bootlegs. Any monster can be found as a bootleg of any element. Every monster has effectively 14 different elements that you can find; the color changes to match the element as well. When you factor in fusions (any two tapes can fuse into a unique monster during battle) you end up with a staggering amount of possibilities. Also it’s open world with overworld monster sprites (including bootlegs), abilities, and unlockable fast travel.Do yourself a favor and pick up Cassette Beasts. I’ve played exclusively on Steam Deck and it is a fantastic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Monster-designs are super creative with a lot of variety.World/Dialogue/Story is at least good enough. Didnt blow me away, but wasnt bad either.Music is awesome, especially the different battle themes always pump me up! Inside buildings there is even singing. Which is nice, if i wouldnt have to read A LOT of dialogue at the same time. Its distracting, but strangely fits very well in any other case. If it really annoys you, you can turn vocals off in the options.You can take 1 partner with you, you can take 6 different monster forms with you, each monster has around 8 different attack/skill slots, there are many different elements, buffs, debuffs, attacks, skills and you can temporarily fuse 2 monsters to combine all of those into one powerful monster. There are seemingly endless possibilities to form your own strategies!For example, hitting my wind-monster with a weak fire attack creates a wall that blocks ANY attack 3 times, which can be stacked up to 15 times. Sounds broken, but there are multi-hit attacks and many other skills which counter such walls and many bosses will also use very effective combos for themselves.Sometimes i had strategy-planning-sessions for several hours and i enjoyed that a lot! If you are not into that, there is a wide variety of difficulty which you can choose in the options!If there is one thing to criticise... its the loot. it seems randomized and mostly its not even worth it going for those chests. Also, the open world didnt feel as good as i had hoped. Maybe because the map is a bit too small? But those things are probably just me saying "Give me more!"If they make a second game with the same formula, i wouldnt complain at all, its almost perfect as it is!

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game expecting a half decent Pokemon clone. What I got instead was one of the best monster collectors I have ever played. This game may invoke ideas to compare it to Pokemon but make no mistake, this is it's own beast of a game.The elemental system is was of the most fleshed out and well thought out I have ever encountered. Rather than a simple strong or weak, every element uniquely interacts with others to completely alter the tide of battle, like using fire on a plastic type melts the plastic turning it into a poison type, or hitting air with a fire move causing a surging updraft putting up a defensive wall around the air type. This system is fine tune, dense with customization, and just begging you to break it open with a hammer.The monster designs are absolutely endearing with so many that I couldn't help falling in love with. Hell this is the first Monster Collector I've played where I DIDN'T feel compelled to keep my starter because of how many options there were, and I mean that in a good way. Combine that with the unique bootleg system, and this truly is a game just desperately begging for an online battle mode. I can see a meta forming behind the scenes already.The bosses were an absolutely treat, with several of them being permanently stuck in my head. The side quests and partner characters are all deeply interesting with some very relatable and realistic worries. I felt compelled to do everything and meet everyone. I plan to get all the achievements now at this point.The music is the real stand out here though. Every track in this OST is mesmerizing. Lyrics dropping in and out based on the context of the situation, a heavenly voice that draws you in... I found myself unconsciously singing along every time I went to the cafe to manage my team.If I have to give anything negative about the game, it's that as it currently stands I do it a "journey is greater than the destination" type situation as the game itself including the final boss were absolutely fantastic, I did find the main story ending to be less than satisfying, especially given the game does have a romance system in place, but I feel like it didn't really contribute much once I chose my partner. All things that can be rectified with DLC, Updates, or anything else honestly. 9.5 / 10 from me. Recommending it to whoever I can.
