_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a Pokémon game that treats you like an adult, both in its relatively mature themes and its gameplay. It respects your time - dialogue and menus are a breeze to cycle through, you can reference a type chart at any time, and the world map is intimate and easy to navigate with a great fast travel system.This philosophy even carries over to the battle system, which features a replenishing per-battle SP mechanic that eliminates the migraine-inducing "run back to town just so I can use this one move again" loop. Grinding is also practically non-existent as levels are tied much more strongly to your base characters than the titular beasts, putting you in a great spot to take on the final boss as soon as the option is there.Also, refreshingly, the playable characters are all grown adults who you can romance no matter your gender identity, and they all have interesting backstories you can unravel by spending time with them. This is backed by some great, though admittedly sparse, voice acting, a feature The Pokémon Company seems to write off as a mortal sin.I'll admit the creature designs leave quite a bit to be desired, and that's really where Pokémon still reigns supreme. You're probably not going to be drawing any of these beasts in your notebook while you're bored in class or a meeting, but I'd overall describe most of them as "pretty cool."And it's difficult to get completely invested in this world where every inhabitant seems really uncomfortable with the idea of Cassette Beasts existing in the first place; a far cry from the majority of Pokémon's population falling in love with - and often dedicating their entire lives to - a wide cast of cuddly companions.If you're an adult who's felt disenfranchised by Pokémon's inefficient hand holding and laser focus on the younger market, definitely give Cassette Beasts a try. You'll get a short and sweet RPG monster-collecting experience that gives you a firm handshake and buys you a drink. Just don't expect a juggernaut universe that becomes your next personality like its grandfather before it may have done for you back when "2nd recess" was a regular part of the daily itinerary.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible spin on the monster catching genre that I think really needs to be experienced.While there are a couple things about the game that I've had issues with, such as somewhat clunky menus with regards to switching around party members, I cannot stress enough that the rest of this game is actually close to perfect.The gameplay is satisfying, it's fun to come up with ridiculous strategies and watch them play out live, and I found myself getting giddy even when I lost, because it meant that I'd be able to come up with something stronger and come back twice as greater than they had thought.I adore the characters.  Every single one of them is a joy to adventure with, and the ones I can't take on adventures with me, I so desperately want to. (But that's what workshop mods are for. >:3)The bosses in this game.  Hoooooly crap.  I'm going to restrain myself from talking too much about these because they are genuinely so much better experienced blind, but just know you're in for a treat.  The concept is ridiculously cool to me, and the execution is FLAWLESS, with the caveat of a couple of them being pushovers, but they still come in swinging with incredible designs and just the general rush of being in the fight.The soundtrack is flawless.  There's not even much to say outside of "I HAVE BEEN LISTENING TO THESE SONGS ON LOOP SINCE I STARTED PLAYING THE GAME" and I think that honestly says what it needs to.I have only had this game for around two weeks and it already means the world to me.  I HIGHLY recommend it and would LOVE to see more people get into it.  <3

_childDocuments_.review: This is more akin to a casual strategy game. Due to the nature of the game, rather than over-levelling, you must employ strategy. When you are at an advantage or disadvantage, the game will show you through visual triggers. Changing your forms is necessary for some of the trainer battles; otherwise, it makes no difference if you're level 25 and your opponents are level 5 you can't overpower them. You're going to lose do to them apply an array of different negative effects, at a high amount damage.It does provide a consistent amount of progression, which is nice and the ability to fully craft your beasts. Don't like what their current abilities are? No worries. Rip those stickers off and slap on some stellar ones in their place and customise with super rare and uncommon variants to empower them even further than before. You can find these from the merchants that restock their stores every night/day. So gathering resources from beasts and quests help set you up for more powerful stickers to make the following battles even more trivial. It's enjoyable to theorycraft.Building your relationship with your companion allows you to fuse together, this alone offers so many different types of beasts a new visual appearance. The possibilities are endless. Find a glitter version? That'll also effect it's color. Joy! The game is worth the price and is very cozy. However, it may be a bit too slow for those who want a more fast paced game experience, since you can't really "run" just dash every 3 seconds due to the annoying stamina meter, which makes sense for the gliding, but not for the dashing. It makes traversing new areas take up some unneeded time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Personally don't feel this is a satisfying co-op game as the mechanics often push you to take away control from player 2 to fight more difficult battles, and rarely does a second person make exploring the overworld more interesting, but instead you just force one another to follow eachother as the AI would anyways. The only real advantage that might be gained from co-op would be if one person is better at platforming than another, then they can carry their partner through certain zones. Otherwise, it's a pretty fun creature collector with a lot of experimentation that sets it apart from something like pokemon, but I think a lot of the experimentation just falls flat. I still found myself exclusively relying on passive effects and pure damage abilities, usually ending battles before any status effects became relevant. The type advantage differences are interesting, for sure, but in the endgame they become somewhat irrelevant, I found. There's a somewhat unique currency system, but the economy quickly becomes irrelevant because you have so much and there's no need to buy anything, at least if you ignore the post-game currency grind which is exceptionally tedious and most things to buy with said currency are mostly useless. The game is also really stable, and the only bugs I found were pretty minor.1. Me and my partner both got launched either together or individually into "space", but quickly came back down and nothing of consequence really happened.2. Occasionally on starting the game it would be stuck to 30 fps, but a restart or resting would cause the game to run normally again.3. You can use certain items in the overworld without depleting a stock of them by switching to a different subsection of the inventory after using them. I essentially had infinite items due to the aforementioned currency surplus, so this only saved me some time going to the vendor, really. The story is pretty stock-standard from what I saw, which is fine, and most of the character relationships are pretty 1D and after a while I found myself just skipping all of the dialogue. Maybe there's something more, but whether there is or not didn't really affect my enjoyment, I didn't buy this game for a gripping story, and a lack of one wasn't missed.The post-game content seems to be what the game really wants you to engage with, but it ends up being just a bunch of "radiant" quests that revolve around killing x things, talking to someone in a location, or killing a boss. There are a few post-game quests that have something more, mostly story, but mechanically they were also just killing a boss.I did enjoy my time with the game, and as someone that hasn't been able to finish a pokemon game, even the ones I really enjoyed as a kid, for the past decade or so, it's a fresh enough take that it's worth a try if you're interested in a different take on a similar formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Personally not a fan, and it's mostly on the art end.I can't get past the art style - it's very deliberately the way it is, and it's definitely competent in areas, but that way personally really doesn't do it for me. It's emulating B/W - B2/W2 era Pokemon and how that integrated pixel art and 3d, but just kind of falls short of the mark. Everything is just too mismatched. The trees especially I found distractingly poorly rendered. Anything that isn't 3d or a beast is very flat. Again, it's deliberate, but I really did not like it. The 2D art portraits for the characters are adorable and polished but needed to be pixel art or not there at all. You just have mismatched pixels, 3d and 2d all layered on top of each other. I try not to let visuals bother me too much but in this case it spoiled the experience to the point I didn't feel motivated to play - and combined with a tutorial area and writing I didn't find gripping, it killed my motivation to continue.My opinion is pretty subjective though. This game isn't for me but that doesn't mean it won't be for you - if you like the art style, give it a go. I wish the creators all the best and think the idea in concept is excellent - just not for me. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have yet to fully sink my teeth into this game, but as far as I am, I am very impressed.  For reference my experience with the monster collecting genre is that I love Shin Megami Tensei and have played pretty much every single mainline and spinoff outside of the very new ultra generic anime ones I have no interest in.  I have played a lot of the Dragon Quest Monsters games and find them very fun.  I enjoyed Pokemon Gen 1 and 2, no rip against any of the others, but the series evolved the gameplay mechanics at a snail's pace over 20 years.  I'm also not as interested in it's 1v1 chance based mechanics as I am in more party based broader strategy type stuff.I gotta say, I really like that this game feels flavored by Pokemon instead of weighed down by it.  The creature designs are very cool and feel original, also it's incredible to me that there seems to be a sprite for every fusion in the game (above and beyond, THANK YOU!).  The way typing works with it's different status effects based on types attacking each other is much, much more interesting to me than the flat damage boosts of Pokemon.  This should go without saying, but since we are in the modern age of games: I also greatly appreciate the very hands off approach to just let the player play the game and the broader quest objectives where it will highlight an area on the map instead of just putting a marker saying "it is exactly right here!".  These things give it a greater sense of exploration and adventure.  Granted I haven't played a modern Pokemon, but I also think the exploration abilities enhance the gameplay and are way more seamless and interesting so far than Pokemon's HM's.  Another really cool feature of this game is that everything is modular in that the monsters skills are all stickers that you can just hotswap around and try all kinds of stuff.   They really wanted you to be able to customize your group and main characters stats to be however the hell you want them and negate time spent grinding and farming.  Not to say it's entirely removed those aspects, but it has made them fun and reasonable.  I also think the music and art style is pretty damn cool.  It has it's own vibe and I think it's pretty cool how during the music the lyrics kick in situationally like in character action games.  Plus, if you don't like lyrics in your game music, you can turn them off in the options menu (I generally don't prefer them, but the game does them very well imo, so I left them on).Overall: Cool game, good game design, well worth the money.  I would buy whatever this developer makes next based on the gameplay decisions in this game alone.  Good job guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette beasts is a game that's flawed, unique, and also really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard to write about.Let's get this out of the way first- yes, I recommend cassette beasts, and yes I like it a lot, but it comes with an asterisk. Oh, and yes, it's also pokemon but actually good. This game sets out to do a lot of things, but it sometimes misses the mark, and on at least one occasion, misses it pretty hard. This review is going to be rather harsh on the game, but it comes from a place of genuine love for the game. Some of these points, especially quite a few of the negative ones are just weird little nitpicks that bother me quite a lot for reason, so be warned. Cassette beasts gets to sit along side games like CONTROL as games won't play again, not because I don't like them, but because they had a big impact on me and I want those memories to remain untainted.And so, without further adieu, let's actually talk about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.The Pros.- The music. THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MUSIC. This game's soundtrack is great. If I had to, I'd place in in A tier. A little higher than DMC5 but lower than Laika Aged Through Blood or Alan Wake (which are high A to S tier imo). Some of the instrumentals are pretty forgettable, but the ones with vocals are excellent and a majority of the instrumentals are, bare minimum, good (or great at best). I listen to the ost on a semi regular basis, and considering how that was one of the game's selling points, at least for me, it knocks it out of the park. - Elemental interactions in this game are good. Instead of having Pokemon's system of "Oh this pokemon is middle aged type and takes x2 damage from midlife crisis type attack", they actually put ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ EFFORT INTO IT. Take notes, Nintendo. Instead of a binary damage multiplier or whatever, type advantaged advantaged attacks can buff, debuff, or even change the type of the target or attacker. Fire type attacks might cause metal type creatures to melt, but could also cause healing mist if used on a water type. There are tons of factors to consider, and these kinds of interactions can easily trip up even prepared parties.- The story. It was interesting enough for me to keep playing, and was the driving force behind playing the game. The climax was satisying and well written and I really enjoyed it. There are some really cool ideas , but unfortunately, not all the ideas and writing sticks the landing, as I'll go into detail later. Regardless, the story is good, and the writing is leagues better than what you'd see in any other game in the creature collector genre.- The Cassettes. I just really liked it. It's cool and unique, and even if it's mechanically the same thing, I still like it a lot.- The Character portraits. They're good. I really like the art style for them.Eh- The game was easy, aside from a couple spikes in difficulty. It's not a huge deal. I'd glad I don't have to spend too much time with the combat system, but I think it's something to note.- The graphical style is pretty standard as well, nothing special. The pixel art didn't really stand out as anything interesting, but not every game has to be Rain World or Hyper Light Drifter. The art was charming, but there's still room for improvement. - The movement. This goes without saying for top down rpgs, but the movement was eh, even in a 2.5d space (which I liked the inclusion of). There are movement abilities you get, but aside from the dash and wings, none of them felt decent, and of the dash and wings, only the wings truly felt good. But you only really use the dash and wings, so it's not a huge deal. The movement isn't bad, it's just okay and I thought I'd mention it here.Cons- The big portion of the review where I dump my issues with the otherwise good writing goes here. I didn't like the characters in Cassette beasts, well not all of them at least. To be fair, while I did get everybody but viola to max relasionship level and saw their special cutscenes, I didn't romance any characters. I liked Kayleigh, though felix was fine, and was either neutral or disliked most of the other companions. It's a baldur's gate situation where they added too many and as such, some ended up half baked. I think it would have been better if they just had 2 or three (plus barkley, because yes) and focused on giving more time for them to develop and expand upon the characters.  The game has tonal issues. Dealing with both a serious and light hearted tone can be hard, and while skilled, the writers didn't pull it off. Sometimes it felt like they were trying to keep the light hearted tone for the sake of being a "pokemon like", and as such doesn't quite fufill being "Pokemon for adults". It's certainly a mature game, and there's some super cool stuff, both light hearted and not, but the light heartedness feels a bit forced. I don't think the game should have been serious all the time, but I wish they'd actually dive into the darker or more serious and grounded aspects of the world and characters that were mentioned  and just brushed over. It is a testament to the writing, however, that I really do want to know more about this stuff though.- The illusion of choice. This is a minor one but the game often offers 2 or more choices for dialogue and they're both the exact ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ same thing but worded slightly differently. It just feels a little condescending. Offer us choice or don't. Just don't pretend you're doing so.- The combat was pretty eh. Not much to say here, it's the boring standard affair. Things do become interesting once type advantaged attacks are thrown into the mix though.- Fusions look ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ugly. It's not a real gripe but i thought it would be funny to put it here.- This is less of a con and more of a missed opportunity. A lot of the designs for monsters are solid, but forgettable. I wish they did something unique and go with some more music (or any design that fits with the cassettes) inspired designs. It felt like they went with what was familiar rather and sticking with the general theme. As a result, the cassettes kinda felt like a nice bonus rather than being at the forefront as the title implies.Anyway, thanks for reading. I live in your walls. BYYYYEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE

_childDocuments_.review: Simple combat with a lot of depth. A very nice variety of monsters with almost all of them having evolutions and some multi-evolutions. Sadly that is the ONLY good thing about the game. I would love to say I finished the game, but unfortunately I did not due to the lack of a lot of QoL settings that should've been implemented at the start. I have some personal issues with the RPG/metroidvania elements of the game I will highlight, but they aren't really deal-breakers (mainly with chests).Note: to keep things simple I'll be keeping terms common. Skills are known as Stickers. Monsters are known as Cassette Beasts. I'll be using skills/monsters for the terminology.1) A lot of my time in this game is spent watching monster attack animations which take forever to go through and wastes/pads the time by a lot. Let me explain this. There's a move in the game called "Multi-Smack" that attacks a monster 3-5 times (similar to multi attack moves in Pokemon like Fury Swipes, Pine Missile, or Fury Attack). If this attack causes a monster to faint it will continue the animation fully until it's done. Let's say Multi-Smack hits 4 times, but the monster faints after 1 hit. The animation will still play out for 3 more hits despite the monster having 0 HP. Another interaction that wastes time is when you attack a Wind enemy with a Fire ability it creates an Air Wall that would block attacks. When you do this even when the monster faints, it still creates the wall unnecessarily wasting time again. There's a ton of these type of time wasting interactions in the game that unnecessarily pad out the time.2) Speaking of padding out the time, combat has no speed up or skip animation feature in the settings. When combat is naturally 2 v 2 with slow animations AND monster skills are unnecessarily padded out, the lack of a 2x speed really drags things along. 3) There's a lot of annoying features with the UI that would come out as a laundry list. These are things like: - Moving monsters in and out of the storage taking way too long and having far too many buttons to press to do so.- No filter feature and/or search feature for skills (TM/HM moves from Pokemon, and there is a VERY long list of skills when you play the game).- No manual map markers so you're expected to remember every treasure/hidden cave location- Swapping party members forces the party member to take your monster instead of being sent to your storage. What this means is that party members will ALWAYS require you to put a monster that you don't want with them in order to swap them out with another party member. This is exacerbated by the lengthy storage system UI I highlighted on my first point.- There's a lot of prompts that don't force a check. For example, you can flee and there won't be a button asking "Are you sure you want to flee?". Another problem is you can accidently recycle cassettes (the poke balls of the game) with no prompt given mid combat. I accidently recycled all of my early game cassettes because I didn't know I was unable to catch a monster in the early game.4) Chests don't feel rewarding at all. As far as I can tell you can obtain every skill/passive at the start of the game through traders. There are upgraded variants of skills (so say an upgraded version of "Multi-Smack" that increases the damage or gives the ability +1 more hits), but it's completely RNG based so there's never going to be a guarantee you'll get what you want without grinding hard. This is why monster level ups and chests feel pointless because every skill is available at the start. Going back to a chest that required a certain ability you can access to only find a useless skill makes me not want to bother exploring the game. Personally I think chests should give reroll options on rare skills or the ability to upgrade skills to make them more worthwhile, but I digress.These issues really started weighing down on me until eventually I couldn't bring myself to continue playing the game. I do not know how far I've gotten as there aren't really any big indicators of progress in the game. I've unlocked the second half of the map, but I'm a completionist so I was grinding level ups on monsters to see their evolutions. Cleared half the bosses and 5 of ranger captains.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start this rather negative review off I just want to say I am genuinely upset that I have pressed the thumbs down button for one of my favourite game series (questionable choice to many, I am more than aware) but it's truly how I felt after the credits started to roll. I sincerely hope Eerie Guest Studios (developers), tinyBuild (developers and publisher) and Steel Wool Studios (DLC developers) can redeem this game as soon as possible.Betrayal:2 days before the release of Deluxe Edition the short and long descriptions of this game were drastically changed to remove any mention of the neural network AI and highly anticipated locations such as the Golden Apple Amusement Park that were promised to us when pre-ordering this game back in April.Price and Game Length:This game is absolutely not worth the price it is being sold at in its current state especially considering the main/base game can be entirely completed from start to finish in roughly 2 hours.Artificial "Intelligence":The main selling point of the game: The AI, is quite frankly atrocious to play against. They lose you incredibly easy if you go anywhere remotely abstract such as on a bookshelf or a bed, they often pause when they get close to you as they are trying to calculate your next move rather than simply grabbing you and they all have such a limited set of tasks that you can often see them loop if you leave them be and just watch them do their tasks for less than a minute.Puzzles:The puzzles for this game are much friendlier than the ones seen in the original Hello Neighbor however to that game's credit at least those were rather creative. For the sequel at least 50% of the puzzles ended up being a "solve this combination" (number or colour) or "use scissors or a crowbar to access this".Marketing:On the official social media accounts for the game, we were given a little glimpse of a weather system that (according to the Ex-Lead Game Designer during a Steam Q&A that happened on the 4th of October) was (this is not an accurate quote but merely what I can remember him saying) fully functional, when I played the game myself it NEVER EVER showed up during gameplay, only for a few seconds in a scripted cutscene... There are numerous scripted/fake screenshots on the store page: You cannot pick up paint cans and chuck them at any of the neighbours anymore but you could in the Beta, there is no key to pickpocket off of the back of The Mayor in the game and the visuals look MUCH nicer in that particular screenshot than what we actually get.Deluxe Edition Content / DLCs:As of right now both Back to School and Late Fees are incredibly unpolished: Countless visual bugs, both of their intro cutscenes give absolutely no direction as to what your goal is and there are no save points in either of them so if the game crashes (which it more than likely will as the DLCs are unstable) you have to start over! Hello-copter is sluggish to control and the grappling hook often doesn't function properly.Conclusion:In conclusion, this game should have been in the oven for at least another 6 months. There is still some hope for this game in my heart as they do have a feedback channel in their Discord server that they are allegedly reading through and will be taking everything on board. I am giving this game a rating of 3/10.Thank you for reading.- AidanEdit:Just to clarify to those in the comment section: I pre-ordered the game back in April in order to gain access to the Beta which actually has a lot of the interactions with the AI that I wanted which were stripped away in the Full Game. When you would boot up the Beta it even reassured the customer that being able to interact with boxes and also properly breaking windows would return for the Full Game and neither of them did so that's unfortunately yet another lie to add to the list.

(I am not counting the Flying Camera as a DLC because it is ridiculous, who in the world is going to use that in the game...)Finally, the pricing... oh boy...The normal game costs only $40 and $60 for the Deluxe (Which includes the DLC). If you are someone who has bought and completed the normal version of the game and paid $36 for all the DLC on the store... _childDocuments_.review: To all who read the reviews BEFORE buying, please just... don't get this game. It's not worth the $40 USD markup that the game has. If you do want to play the game however, all I suggest is that you wait for a steam sale cause as I said, this game isn't worth $40 USD. Now, onto my review on the game and why I think it's not worth getting...(notice! there are some spoilers below, however the TL;DR summary is spoiler-free at the bottom.)First of all, let's talk about the AI. The main selling point of the game that implements the stealth mechanic of the game. Let's just say that it's not the best... When the AI sees you & starts chasing you, the AI will most of the time have stutter-y movement making it easy for the player to outrun the AI. That's fine not a big deal right? Well let's talk about hiding in the game. If the AI sees you go into a closet to hide in, they will pull you out. However, if the player turns the corner and then immediately hides in a closet, then the AI just gives up and goes back into wander mode. The AI also has a very short attention span, which means if they don't see you after walking like 2 rooms, then the AI just goes back to the wander phase. If the AI is supposed to be "revolutionary", then the AI should at least check a hiding spot in the room where they AI last spotted the player (something like outlast). Speaking of hiding, sometimes you don't even need to hide at all. If there is a simple obstacles such as the player standing on a bed in a room, then the AI does not know what to do and simply stands there waiting for the player to drop off of the bed. Sometimes even crouching for a bit behind something makes the AI go back to it's wander phase and sometimes the AI decides that your time is up and automatically does the animation where the AI catches you. Speaking of which, sometimes the AI just decide to be unfair and catch you when you're out of the AI's range. This is because the developers were too lazy to add some countermeasure like jumping to get to the player when the player is in a place where the AI can't path-find or reach which makes the game even worse than it is. Now, speaking of the AI in the game, with all the characters in the game you'd expect at least a different AI with everyone right? Well not really... with all of the characters in the game, all of their AI stays practically the same. If the AI sees the player while the player is on the AI's property, then chase them. That's all the AI is except for Mr. Otto which all is different is that he occasionally shoots at the player when in chase mode & Mr. Peterson in the finale which his movement speed is heavily increased. The developers stating that their AI is revolutionary and all of that is a flat out lie to the consumer.Second of all, let's talk about the puzzle point of the game. The puzzles to say the least are not fun... at all... Trying to figure out what goes where & trying to find the necessary things you need to progress just feels like Hello Neighbor 1 again. There is zero guidance of what you must do or how to find the necessary things to progress. It's just a constant scavenger hunt on grabbing items in the most random places. I had to use a guide on my first play-through because I was stuck for TWO HOURS on THE FIRST HOUSE. Maybe I'm just really blind and don't observe my surrounding but when stuff is just in the most unnecessary & random places, then the game stops becoming fun and starts getting tedious.Third thing, let's talk about the controls. As far as controls go in the game, they are pretty solid. The controls mostly act like the Hello Neighbor 1 Alpha 1 controls where you only need to press the pickup key once instead of having to hold a multi-instance key to pick up items. The movement in game mostly sticks faithful to the original Hello Neighbor however the only complaint I have is that you are just really slow even when sprinting. I understand that this is supposed to be a stealth game and not a "outrun the threat like hello neighbor 1" game which is why the player is really slow in the first place, but if the developers altered the speed just slightly, then in my opinion, it would be a lot better because getting to other places wouldn't be as tedious. However, I don't mind the speed. As far as new mechanics go such as being able to grab onto ledges & the inventory system, I say that they're also pretty solid. The only thing that I would complain about is the sliding. If you start sprinting and hit the crouch key while sprinting, you'll do a slide. I personally found this really annoying in some circumstances & overall didn't really like it. This is a stealth game, not a first person shooter. I don't see why the sliding is necessary at all.Final thing, the story... The story is in my opinion just bad. The entire plot of the story is that you see the neighbor keeping his son away, you crash into a barn, the neighbor knocks you unconscious & now you decide that you have to save the kid. Sometimes you would go unconscious during the story and wake up back in the building you first woke up at where the TV screens show you your next objective. Overall, the premise is that the keys to the museum that the neighbor has his son inside are in different houses for just no reason. The game states that the story of this game is a story on how Mr. Peterson becomes "The Neighbor" but I feel that the story isn't exactly that. If I explained the story wrong and if there is more to it, then I do apologize considering that I never really looked into the story that much. I just went and beat the game.OVERALL the game is just like how it turned out in the first game. It is the same deal where you have to go on a tedious scavenger hunt with items in random places & having to solve un-fun puzzles with an AI that is bad.Before going onto the summary, I do have one more thing to state about the game, the crashes... oh my god the crashes... you can crash at any point at any time for no reason. I've had the game bug out on me and would not let me past a loading screen when I was at the final part of the game where you get locked up in the neighbor's museum meaning I had to fully make a new game and replay the entire game through again. However playing the game with knowledge on where everything is cuts playtime on a run to like 20 minutes.SUMMARYtl;dr The game is not worth the price point. The AI isn't very good. The puzzles in the game are not fun and are tedious. Finding items to progress is just another scavenger hunt like HN1. Controls are semi-decent & story isn't the best either. I suggest to either wait for a steam sale on the game before buying or don't get the game at all.RATINGSAI (Main part of what makes the game a stealth game) - 4/10Puzzles - 2/10Controls - 7/10Story - 4/10Extra RatingsPhysics - 6/10 (You don't get flung when doing anything in the game anymore however physics are still clunky)Aesthetics (deco, enviornment, etc.) - 7/10 (big improvement in looks compared to the first game)Achievements - 2/10 (all but 3 achivements are just playing the game normally.)Hopefully this steam review is somewhat helpful to anyone. This is my first time actually making a lengthy and legitimate review on a game instead of making a joke review.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; false marketing, mismanaged development, not worth $40 for the standard edition (nor $60 for the deluxe edition)It's been almost a year since the game came out (damn, time really does fly, doesn't it?), and the game has received 9 patches as of November 25th, 2023. I decided to rewrite this review, as the original version had some wrong info and I thought that I should fix it up a bit.Before jumping into the review, I would like to give some context on my relationship with the Hello Neighbor franchise as a whole. I have been a fan of Hello Neighbor since October 2016, when YouTubers were first finding out about the game and making videos on it. I was a fan of the franchise up until the release of this game, for reasons I will talk about later in the review.In this game's promotional material, many features were advertised - a neural network AI, a large open world to explore, sandbox gameplay elements, and many more. However, literally NONE of these features were included in the game, and they still haven't been added nearly a year after release. The AI we got was not a neural network, and it instead was a slightly upgraded version of the AI from the demo, which itself was a watered down version of the AI in the Alpha 1.5 version. The "open world" consists of a few streets, and all of the important locations are right next to each other. The spooky museum with the titular Neighbor living in it is placed directly next to a bright and colorful bakery. Also, you can't even explore the open world until after beating the final boss level (which, might I add, was made over the course of a single week by one person). The only post-game content was a simple puzzle that rehashed elements from the game's main locations, and it wasn't even there on launch!The worst part of all of this was that the game was originally intended to have the marketed features. Nikita Kolesnikov is the creator of the first Hello Neighbor game, and he served as lead game designer, creative director, and composer in both the first Hello Neighbor game and it's prequel, Hide & Seek. However, in October 2021, Nikita was mysteriously removed from the development of Hello Neighbor 2, as he was no longer lead game designer and his creative director role now meant nothing (it is important to note that in April 2021, a new composer was hired so Nikita could focus more on developing the content of the game). The new lead game designer was Alexus Kravchenko, who had worked as a level designer and senior game designer since September 2020. However, despite supposedly playing a major role in the development of Alpha 1.5 (which is considered by many as the best version of Hello Neighbor 2), Alexus decided to completely change the game's direction and scrapped literally ALL of the marketed content. However, not only did he not tell the fanbase what the new direction of the game would be, he did the exact opposite and lied to people in the official Discord server about what content the full game would include.On November 14, 2022, less than three weeks before the game launched, Alexus announced he was going on a "sabbatical". However, people noticed on his LinkedIn profile that in actuality, he had quit. On November 29, 2022, two days before the release of the deluxe edition, the game's Steam description was changed to remove all mention of the neural network AI, open world, and other marketed features that ended up not being in the game.The standard edition of this game is not worth the $40 USD price tag. As for the deluxe edition, it's an EVEN BIGGER scam. On top of the issues with false advertising, the deluxe edition contains 3 DLC packs; 2 of them are new levels and the other one is a drone. The drone was actually FREE TO USE in the game's public alpha builds, so the fact they're charging money for something that was free in an early build is really scummy. However, the other two DLC packs are even worse. They were designed by Steel Wool Studios' non-VR team, AKA the same guys who made FNAF: Security Breach. All of the same issues from the base version of Security Breach apply to the DLCs, though with the extra factor of being even more glitchy than the base Hello Neighbor 2 game (I didn't mention the game being buggy in the previous sections of the review, since it's really a given for Hello Neighbor games).HALLOWEEN UPDATE: The new section with the Guest (the crowman) is even worse than the base game. The layout of the new area is somewhat similar to the two public test builds of Hello Guest. However, the Guest is a sped-up version of the regular AI instead of having his own unique stalking AI. Because of the way his AI is set up, along with there being no safe areas and the Guest always spawning close to you when you die, this section is filled with constant deaths with the feeling that no progress is being made...OH WAIT! It's not just a feeling - whenever you get caught, large chunks of the main puzzle get reset, forcing you to go through the tedious process AGAIN! And God forbid the Guest manages to catch up to you and kill you while you're riding the minecart to the church, because if that happens, it is borderline impossible to progress because of the Guest spawning so close to you.All in all, do not buy this game. The game is only really worth $20 USD, yet they're charging double (and in some cases triple) that amount. If you want to play an actually decent Hello Neighbor game, then please just go play Hello Neighbor 2: Alpha 1.5. Not only is it free here on Steam, but the AI is actually pretty good, the puzzles are unique & fun to solve, and there is an actual open world that you can explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly the most disappointing thing ever. This is the Security Breach of this franchise. I actually feel bad for the poor lower-level developers who worked so hard on this game, and had no say in how it turned out, only for it to come out like this because of... design choices.First of all, the Guest, a.k.a. Birdman, isn't present in the game, despite being the mascot of HN2, seen in Hello Guest and the HN2 Alphas. Why is he gone?And speaking of, the Alphas are nothing like the finished game! The Alphas had a certain charm to them, and why waste time adding so many cool and unique features into the Alphas, when you don't have them in the final game? For example, the Alphas had a really nice crowbar animation when taking off planks, and it's not even present in actual game, which I may add, cost forty dollars more than the free Alphas. How is an Alpha more polished than the full release of a game? The conveyor belts, the fire extinguishers, the wires, the ropes, the Guest... oh my god, the bird! He used to drag you back to his house to *chuck you out of a window at Mach speed!* That was cool! What happened to that guy?And the game is nearly shorter than the first game, even without a guide. The game ended on such a weird cliffhanger, and the final segment was unexpectedly short. I feel like this game is trying so hard to have a theory fanbase around, similar to FNAF's, but... it just doesn't work. The ending makes zero sense, and I feel like they don't even actually have an explanation for this. I could imagine the devs watching a HN2 theory video, thinking, "Oh, that's cool!" learning the story at the same time we fans are. The ending concludes with a "Well, shucks, you beat it! You can now play as Luigi!" wall of text, accept you can't play as Luigi, and you're left with immense sadness at the fact that you cannot play as Luigi. (More on that later, you can't play as Beatrix either).Speaking of story, this series's story was actually pretty interesting and entertaining, and I, a mere fool, was excited to see how this game could expand upon it. People added in the Alpha, like The Guest, The Man in the Hat, and Beatrix, as touched on before, are not present. You can't even play as Beatrix in this game, which perplexes me because it would have changed barely anything apart from the player's character model.The Alpha's had an interesting mystery behind it, with the twist being that you now have to save the Neighbor from the Guest. In terms of story, the Guest could have been an adult Aaron seeking revenge on his father for his childhood trauma. The Alphas seemed to have taken place far into the future, making a story like this possible. Any story would have worked, anything that's not: "Secret Crow Cult! Better watch out for the Baker!" There are so many more things that could be mentioned here, like nearly ever frame of the earlier trailers for this game allegedly being scripted, and the neural network AI that allegedly isn't even present. Look up any video on YouTube about Hello Neighbor 2 if you want to learn more. I'm leaving this review here not because I hate tinyBuild and the developers, but because I'm genuinely saddened and only want to see this series thrive. Hello Neighbor 1, despite everyone hating it, was near and dear to my heart, and was a nostalgic part of my childhood, watching Youtubers play it and the countless mods made by fans of who only did so because they loved Hello Neighbor.So I'll leave here a quote uttered by many parents around the world at some point in their life: "I'm not mad, just disappointed."

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of, if not the biggest, the worse disappointments I've had in recent memory. Considering its length alone, IT IS NOT worth 40$ already.The only improvements over Hello Neighbor 1 is its polished artstyle and music. The puzzles range from too easy to a little hard in difficulty, and the AI itself is somehow even worse than Hello Neighbor 1. The story ends on a cliffhanger with tinyBuild promising updates when the game should have been finished in the first place. All of the achievements (Except for one.) are just literally progressing through the game unlike Hello Neighbor 1 where you had to do other things unrelated to the main objective. The game is also terribly unoptimized.The worst part about it is the deceptive marketing following up to this game's launch. tinyBuild promised a neural network to be utilized in full game but there wasn't even one and they changed the wording of their Steam description days leading up to the early access launch to make it not hint at a neural network. One of the mods within the Discord even tried gaslighting about it. The fact that the Guest was promoted on their cover art and only showed up for a few seconds on screen and was never explained makes no sense. They also switched the game from being open world to linear. It's obvious that something happened in 2021 that shifted the direction that the game was going for and tinyBuild should not double downed on what they showed earlier in 2021 when they released the beta and announced the release date for full game.I've been following this game with interest since I played the prototype in early 2020. I was excited for this ambitious project. This was supposed to be their chance at redeeming the franchise. It disappoints me immensely that it turned into wasted potential. Please do not support this type of development/marketing and refrain from buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the stupidest games I've played in a long time, and that's saying something. Not only is the entire story nonsensical theory-bait, far more than the first game, but it's also just not fun. It's a ridiculously short, unpolished puzzle game that gets easy to softlock. I softlocked myself for two entire months. After repeatedly asking for support, I was eventually told to send my save in. Only after doing this and discovering the save they gave me was just another softlock, they told me that they were apparently incapable of giving me the single item that popped out of existence. I was encouraged to replay the game to see all the cool new features they added. So I did, and it's aged like fine milk. The AIs have all turned from annoying nuisances to killing machines with super-human hearing and infinite vertical reach. Any challenge that the game used to have has been replaced with just omniscient idiots. The only thing the devs seem to have done between now and the game's launch is add filler content. I finally finished the game this time, and it is the least satisfying theory-bait ending ever. It's just a cliffhanger, followed by a literal wall of text saying to wait for the next game. Believe it or not, I wanted to like this game, considering I kind of liked the first game. But this is just ridiculous.Pros: ????Cons:- Stupidly easy puzzles- AI is worse than ever- Ridiculously short- No good content has been added since the release despite developers stating they would- Stupid, theory-bait story- Barely any competent developer support for the many bugs

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that I have to give this a thumbs down. I LOVED the first game and considered it a breakthrough. It was monumental in its novelty and controlled insanity. This game is  just a shadow of the original game. There’s no dreaminess, no surrealism, not a single thing outside the box. You spend your time solving obvious puzzles, looking for obvious things out of the ordinary, and it’s just so saddeningly LINEAR and predictable. I’m so disappointed. I pre-ordered this game — something I NEVER do —  because I was so awestruck by the original. I played the beta and was cautiously optimistic. But then this. THIS. This tiny, bland thing. Remember in the first game those creepy side quests, going through the grocery store and the school, thinking, “What the HELL is this???” There’s none of that. At all. In fact, there are things that seem like puzzles but aren’t anything at all. Remember the ending to the first game, how out of this universe it was? Nothing like that here AT ALL. This was just so damn LAZY. So obvious. So disappointing. Don’t buy this game. Just okay the first one and pretend this one never happened.

However, i will compare it to the marketing that was around it for the last 3 years.Complicated story: False  The story is extremely simple. In fact there is no story but some camera footages that work as transitions guiding the player to the next locationNeural Network AI: FalseThough better than HN1, the Al is exrremely simple without any elemnt of complexity. Its not neural network and nothing in the video breaking down the AI in HN2 was implemented.More characters than baker, major, taxidermist: FalseIn fact there are 2 more which are found in DLCs and do not take place in the main game. There are just 2 extra levels. AND the farmer, a character which was mentioned in the first devlog, never made it to the game.Amusement Park: FalseEven a few days before release there was this question in the game's description: "Why does this man with this mustache visit the amusement park every night?" However, no amusement park at the end.Guest: FalseThis is a true surprise. The character that followed the deveopment of Hello Neighbor 2 from the beginning till the beta stages did not make in to the game. Its so weird that the guest was featured in the beta trailer in December 2021 and after some months, the trailer was extended adding the guest in more scenes of it. The guest is also on the official game's keyart but not in the game. This is a true scam.Interactive pinboard: False"Uncover the big mystery in Raven Brooks":FalseThere is no mystery in raven brooks. At the end, you do not even uncover it. The game is unfinished.I understand that while developing a game, things change. Some things may be removed and some other perhaps added. However the game's development was anounced on June 2020 and after 2,5 years, the outcome is a simple game that can be beaten in less than 3 hours with an extreme price for it's value. If it was like 15$, i would recommend it just for the puzzles and the whole vibe but the price is currently too high. I honestly don't believe that this was Hello Neighbor 2.... :(

_childDocuments_.review: (UPDATE ALERT!!!] There have been multiple major patches to the game released and they've improved the game A LOT! I'll wait to rewrite this review until we enter the new content phase.    I quite liked this game. The story feels very interesting, especially if you've played the other games in the series. The game also feels a lot more straightforward than the other Hello Neighbor games.    The Story Mode is definitely a highlight but it has been for me in pretty much every Hello Neighbor game. I am pretty much hooked on the story of these games and books. The plot is very interesting and I definitely recommend waiting to play this game until after you've played Hello Neighbor and Hello Neighbor: Hide and Seek. Those two games are pretty important to understand this game, especially Hello Neighbor: Hide and Seek. Although I liked Hello Neighbor's plot, enjoyed every segment of the game (even Act 3) and really enjoyed how it followed Nicky's journey to get over his trauma, the game's plot would definitely fail to make sense to anyone who didn't do some research to figure out exactly what's going on as none of the Hello Neighbor games have any dialogue, despite the animated series and books having conversations. The game didn't explain much and although Act 1 and Act 2 were pretty self explanatory, Act 3 and Finale wouldn't make much sense without you looking for information outside of the game. Hello Neighbor 2 improves this by making the game a lot less based on symbolism and a lot more straightforward, if you see something happen in this game, chances are it's really happening and isn't symbolism, there are nightmares that you have when you complete some nights but they are almost immediately revealed to be nightmares when you wake up after them.    The game is also still being constantly updated. They've been releasing new content updates for a little bit now and so far each one has added something new and fun to the game! Patch 1 added paint cans and Patch 2 added bear traps! They respond to bug reports quite fast and get patches out the door along with new stuff to play with! Say what you want about the issues with the game but I definitely respect everyone who had something to do with this games development for not just taking the money and running, they're actually trying to fix the game and make it a better experience for players.    This game got heavily criticized on launch for being extremely buggy but I didn't run into any notable bugs in my playthrough. The only bugs I encountered were in the DLC, Back to School really only crashed once and although Late Fees is really buggy, Back to School and the Hello-copter more than make up for that. I did see that a lot of the bugs are platform specific so I guess the Steam version just isn't as buggy as the other ones, especially after the newest updates. The point here is that the bugs aren't as big of a deal as people are making them out to be, at least on Steam.The game features an open world and it is definitely one of the best parts. There is a whole town with multiple different AI characters you can see and each of those AI characters have places that you can break and enter into. You can mess around with the AI and use things like paint buckets to pull little pranks on them. The world sadly doesn't have citizens that walk down sidewalks and stuff which makes the world feel a lot less alive than I was hoping it would. You can however hear people talking in the random houses that aren't part of the story which does help with making the world feel a little more populated, it's just a little weird that you're the only one walking around the streets. The characters also never leave their respective buildings which is quite sad as I was hoping that the AI would have routines that would involve them going to different places around town, like the cops going to the bakery to pick up more donuts or something.    Speaking of the AI, the AI is certainly good, but as far as I can tell it isn't the neural network system that was hyped up before release. I suppose I'm fine with it if they cut it due to not being able to finish it. I'd much rather get a less advanced AI than one the barely functions due to not being finished. I also hope that after patching all of the games major bugs, they begin working on finishing the neural network AI and implementing it into the game as I would really love to see how the AI gets better over time. The AI still isn't that bad and usually behaves like you'd expect it to. The AI can do cool things like sitting down by the fire, placing bear traps, sleeping and looking for shortcuts to get to you. The AI is pretty much the AI from the first game but with quite a few improvements added on. The AI is definitely cool, I just wish it was better because they got everyone excited for a much more advanced AI, and then couldn't get it in the finished product.    The game also definitely isn't finished, it'll take you about four hours for the average first playthrough and $40-60 feels a little bit too expensive. However I'm not that angry about it because at the end of the game they say that they intend to come back and add more content in future major updates so I'm hopeful that there'll be more and more added on to the story mode over time, or at least new DLC levels that add more stuff to do. There is also a free roam mode that is unlocked after completing the story mode that allows you to just mess around with the people in the free roam world and that is definitely a good feature,Although it doesn't seem like there'd be much to play around with as there are a total of five different people you encounter, it somehow still manages to keep me entertained for hours simply running from house to house messing around with the citizens of Raven Brooks. You can explore the free roam world and interact with every AI powered NPC you encountered during the story mode. There are paint cans and alarm clocks  you can use to play little pranks on the AI and the world is graphically amazing as wandering the streets at night and looking at the lights with bugs flying around them shining on the reflective water puddled street is beautiful. The fun in the free roam mode is always there as breaking into people's houses and messing around with them will always be fun!    The main letdown right now is the lack of screen-time that the Guest gets. The Guest was hyped up as the scary antagonist for this game for a while in promotional material however he only gets about three seconds of screen-time in the intro cutscene. I sorta believe the Guest's three seconds are there just so that it isn't false advertising as the Guest literally appears nowhere else despite him being a really cool idea for an enemy and being a big presence in pretty much all pre-release builds except the demo. I'm not super angry about this one either though because at the end of the game they say they'll come back and add more stuff in major updates so I"m hoping that they'll add some more story or a DLC where the Guest can finally get his chance to shine.    Overall I think this game is awesome. It makes the story way more straightforward which makes it way less  complicated for people who just wanna enjoy a blind playthrough, however the story's main plot points depend a lot on the player having played the other games in the franchise, so this game definitely isn't intended for newcomers. The free roam world is fun to mess around in, especially with the AI powered citizens living there. The game is lacking content, but the content that's here is definitely high quality and there is more on the way! I think that you'll have a good time with this game, especially if you're already a fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: (IM WRITING THIS AS OF PATCH 3) Although we were entirely mislead by the alphas with the guest being an antagonist, I still do find this final build to be great in its own ways. _childDocuments_.review: I came in with low expectations and was pleasantly surprised by the graphics. However what seemed perfectly in place for a game as disgustingly awful as this was the lack of story. All that is needed to know is that this game doesn’t have one. It  has no ending, or even a solid idea of what it is doing. Each character seems to have something going on with them, but it doesn’t get brought up or explained. It is one of the many faults of this game.Another would be the A.I. that this game claims to have. The characters suck at walking or chasing, each time they turn they must stop and redirect themselves. There’s hardly a way to properly interact with the A.I., as it tends to forget you exist fairly often, even failing to chase you for very long when you’re inside the house. It’s too easy to escape them, they don’t have a way to thwart you. The hunter and the neighbor have traps, but that is the limit to what they are capable of (minus the literal gun the hunter holds). There isn’t a real progression of difficulty, because the neighbors can’t properly navigate the house. They can’t jump, climb, or reach you in certain places. Each character shares the same A.I., never changing to present new forms of gameplay, merely walking around doing chores until they see you and must try to catch you. The chase scenes offer no real entertainment, as the A.I. either loses you immediately, or chases you until you’re out of their line of sight. They don’t take the time to fortify the house or learn from what you’ve done, they just return to their regular routine. It ruins what the point of the game is. Even with the patches that have been done post-release, they fail to make the A.I. actually smarter, they just fill it with other useless functions that don't improve it whatsoever.The scenery is certainly beautiful, and it has a great artstyle that has improved what the previous game tried to accomplish, but that doesn’t work when things are clipping through each other very noticeably. The interactivity with the neighborhood houses to collect items is a nice touch, and the promise for more things to explore sounds promising, but it can only be effective if it’s done right. No more releasing things in a broken and unpolished state, it doesn’t belong in a finished product. Ask anyone who plays video games, the lack of polish is the biggest threat to a game. You can certainly have clipping in a 3D video game, but not when it’s something as controllable as a donut box on the table, or the literal dirt from the ground clipping into the lower floors of the hunter’s house. It should have been fixed, but for whatever reason it hasn't.Whatever happened to the alpha versions of this game, I really miss the concepts they held. Using generators and battling a much more advanced A.I. held much more promise than fighting an enemy that checks hiding spots during the chase scenes. At least the alphas had a cooler villain. A return to that would have done the game some good, but the puzzles have this simple formula with hardly any variety. this only gets worse the bigger the house is.This game heavily relied on post-release patches. It added things that certainly improved the game, but also showed the flaws it held from the beginning. We should have had a game like this from the moment we were given early access, not four patches later! The DLC got the worst of it, as it has so much less focus put onto it, and it shows. It's not even fun to play, as it seems to take inspiration from the first game, and look how it turned out.At the end of the day, the A.I. should be the main focus, along with the story of the game. Give the characters a story that is explained cohesively, rather than with hints that don’t give a straight answer. It only frustrates those who don’t want another FNAF theory knockoff, what we want is an advanced A.I. that learns from you and thwarts you. The devs seem to recognize this, so why isn’t it featured? Just let the characters have their own personal abilities and locations that make them unique, as there are plenty of ways to make a game successful without the need for a theory video.

_childDocuments_.review: This game only does a couple things right and a whole lot wrong, however I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy my time with this game.This game is definitely a large step up from the first game in the series, streamlining a lot of the puzzle elements which allows the game to become less confusing with what you have to do next, while still keeping the challenge of the puzzles, however similar to the first game, the game doesn't give you much hints to work with and the hints provided are sometimes very vague.The story itself is very short and unfortunately like the first game, is still extremely vague and ends on a irritating cliff hanger that makes no sense.This game also has been giving a lot of criticism and backlash for the sheer amount of false advertising the game commits, with the main antagonist who was in all of the advertising leading up to the launch of the game, being the bird creature, only appearing in a cutscene for less than 3 seconds. they had additionally completely removed the promised "Neural Network AI" that was so heavily advertised, however when the game had released, this AI was no where to be seen and the AI we were provided with was buggy and functions poorly. To give credit where its due however i will say the AI in this game is leagues better than the AI in the first game.I personally love the idea of going to multiple different smaller houses rather than going to one massive obnoxious house that is so convoluted and frustrating. It keeps the game fresh with each house you visit.Here is a quick pros and cons list of things done right and things done wrong:     Pros:The graphics are absolutely gorgeous, love the cartoonish artstyle, it leads the game to being extremely distinguishable and left me constantly admiring the game in all its glory. No more awful parkour segments! parkour still exists however its much less extreme and the games engine is actually designed for it now, instead of being forced to stack glitchy boxes to access areas you can now climb to high places which really helps the flow of the game and makes a less irritating experienceAI while still not great, its definitely an improvement from the first and unlike the first game, the neighbors are actually now a threat now that they are more realistic and the houses are much smaller in scale.Animation in the cutscenes are beautifully animated and charmingCons: An extremely high end pc is required to have a smooth experience at max graphics, I was forced to turn the majority of my graphics down to medium despite my pc being fairly high end (luckily despite being on medium graphic settings, the game still looked stunning). I had to cap my frame rate to 60 in order to have a smooth experience. Even on medium settings I still experienced frame drops quite frequently, most of them were only slight frame drops that weren't too noticeable, however areas such as the cafe and the museum were most noticeably bad with my frame rate, leading to drop to 50 frequently.The overwhelming amount of false advertisement as previously discussedPoor AI as previously discussedConvoluted and underwhelming story as previously discussedDespite the beautiful scenery, the map is quite barren excluding the different neighbors houses, there lacks anything to do in the map except go to the neighbors houses. Terrible DLC which doesn't even function correctly, I haven't bought any of the DLC due to the fact that they dont even work correctly according to the internet, there is also a DLC that you can buy that has a item you can use throughout the game which costs FIVE POUNDS which is extremely overpriced for a item that is pretty much useless and shouldnt be paid DLC.    The game for what you get is extremely overpriced, I refused to pay the £40 price tag, I ended up using the website CD keys to get the game on sale for only £15 which I believe is a reasonable price for a game of this size.In conclusion, as Foekoe says in his review of the game, If you ignore all of the bad choices and terrible false advertising, then the game by itself while not scary in the slightest, can be quite enjoyable. I personally had quite a lot of fun with the game, being a long time fan of Hello Neighbor since 2016 who got disappointed at the terrible full release of the first game. This game definitely is a step in the right direction and with some improvements and major adjustments added, I believe the extremely unique concept of Hello Neighbor which was ruined by the first release can finally thrive through either this game with added updates as they promised they would, or through a third game which TinyBuild will hopefully fully focus on  and attempt to make it truely great.My personal rating for this game would be a 7.5/10 which I am aware is an extremely generous rating and with the current state of the game shouldn't be that high of a rating, however I cant help but enjoy this game for what it was. If we exclude my biased and personal opinion of this game, overall I would rate it around a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with good things.This game has good graphics, great music and great art style. The art style and graphics are much better than HN1. That's it.Now I'm going to talk about bad things.This game is buggy.The parkour sucks.The game is really short. It took me 2 hours to complete the main campaignand 1 hour to complete the forest part. I didn't watch any guides or other stuff.Now, I'm going to explain, why Hello Neighbor 2 is a big scam.The devs promised us many characters including Guest, the guy with a hat, police officer 1 and 2and many other characters. Guess what, they didn't add these characters except the police officer (1) andsome characters from the Beta. Even the guest wasn't in the game. Well, actually he was in the game, but heappeared only for 3 (!!!) seconds in the beginning. Now, he is in the game, but the devs added him a YEAR later, after the launch day. Again, they promised us, that everything will appear on the launch day.They also promised many locations, including the abandoned park from Hello Guest (Pre-Alpha for Hello Neighbor 2). They didn't add. The mentions of all these characters and locations were removed from the store page.The game is missing mechanics from the trailers and presentations. It's even missing some mechanics from the ALPHAS, including the moment when the Guest grabs you and throw you out of the window. It's much better than getting caught in the "full release".The story isn't even completed. Again, they promised us a compelete story and other stuff.Btw, the story (for now) is pretty bad. !!!SPOILERS!!!You must help the neighbors son to escape the neighbors house (Museum).You solve all these puzzles and in the end, neighbors son just returns to the neighbor because his sonloves his father. Then you get hit by someone and you're being dragged away. That's it.So we did everything (solving puzzles) for nothing. Really bad story.!!!SPOILERS END!!!At last, I want to talk about the AI.The devs also promised us a NEURAL NETWORK AI. Guess what, on 4th December 2022 (two days before release) they removed any mention of neural network AI. The neural network AI was a huge part of their marketing campaign. _childDocuments_.review: The game is quite enjoyable, with engaging puzzles and minimal bugs. However, this doesn't overshadow the fact that the price is unjustifiably high for the content provided. The term "not that buggy" applies only after nine patches and numerous hot-fixes. As someone who has followed the game from its prototype phase, I must point out that it lacks many features promised in the alpha versions and promotional materials. Despite these issues, I was inclined to give a positive review, hopeful that future updates would address the current shortcomings and integrate elements from the unreleased Hello Guest game. Unfortunately, this did not happen. We are left with an unfinished game, with more broken promises than content. While this title is an improvement over the original Hello Neighbor, it cannot overshadow the fact that the game feels half-baked, as if it's handing you the recipes and expecting you to finish the cooking.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: It was my fault that my GPU got so hot. I got some case fans and it went from around 90 to 75 on high. Spoilers will be covered in black boxes.Let me start off by saying I really wanted to like this game. I had been so excited for a sequel to the first. But I couldn’t bring myself to enjoy it.First of all, I almost caused permanent damage to my GPU while playing through, even to the point where I was trying to finish it as fast as possible so that I could let my PC cool down. I have a Radeon RX 5700xt which is very capable of running this game, yet it only ran at 30 fps on max graphics. When I was playing it on high my GPU was literally reaching 90 degrees Celsius. Even turning it to medium the game looked like garbage and still ran at 86 degrees. Second of all, the game was EXTREMELY short. As you could see, I beat this game in 6 hours (at the time of writing) and I just uninstalled it because it was so bad. I had to use walkthroughs because of how difficult the puzzles were but there were literally only four acts like the first one and they were all very short.  Then when I beat the game it just put in in free roam with nothing else to do except get caught by the characters. Third, the story kinda sucked. It was the typical “Neighbor has child in basement, open basement through a million puzzles, go into basement, game ends.”  The ending was ok, but the last 5-Minute task was literally harder than all of the other puzzles. Somehow all of the characters (except the police) seemed to be working with the neighbor, and  which was kinda weird as it would probably get you in more legal trouble than what happens in the beginning. It also ends on a complete cliffhanger and . As for bugs, there weren’t too many game breaking ones like in the first one except for little things like me being able to grab a picture through glass without breaking it. The AI does tend to freak out sometimes though.So in the end the game is really not worth $40 for 6 hours of playtime. Not even $20 on sale IMO. Unless you can speedrun it and refund it in under 2 hours you’ll probably be disappointed as there is nothing to do at the end and no reward.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be honest, when first going into this game- I didn't think It'd be good in the *slightest*. Hello Neighbor 1 for years now in the Indie game community has been the laughing stock and prime example of how not to make a game. But to be honest, this is a really good game. The puzzles are really well thought out, maps pretty good, graphically it's beautiful, the story is... kind of nothing to be honest, but the other benefits outweigh that. I don't like Tinybuild as a company though. For literal *years* the fans have been waiting for the all so holy "Patch #10", but it's seeming at this point- to never come. When HN2 first launched, it was a buggy, incomplete mess, which over updates- got better and better! But it's still lacking content that they promised *ages* ago. And I really don't think we're ever going to see that content, because now we have HN3 announced, more episodes of the TV Show (which I don't personally like, but some others enjoy it.). I really want to recommend this game, as it's not half bad. It's enjoyable. I'd even say It's *good*. But tinyBuild, for the love of god- Stop making promises you can't deliver on. If we get Patch #10? Great! But the fact that we've had almost zero communication throughout all of this is absurd- If you can't do it, just say it. Stop giving people false hope for something that will never come.

_childDocuments_.review: okay, here comes a honest review from me, about the game.- time.the game can be finished under like an hour if you know what you're doing and not rushing, but attempting to enjoy it. I'm reviewing the standard edition.- alphas. this game, just like the original HN, is not like it was in the alphas. especially, it's not like Hello Guest was. it is NOT Hello Guest, let's say it has nothing to do with that game. so if you're expecting something similar after playing the alphas and even, the beta, you might get disappointed. I hate changes, especially unexpected, sudden changes. it literally frustrated me, to watch the development progress, and my final feelings are a bit bittersweet and mixed, because I do know, what the game could've been.- AIthe AI knows less actually, than in the beta. however, it will do it's job, don't worry. I'm comparing it to the beta only for now, since it is the closest to the final release. the AI has different tasks for each sequence, and it doesn't do much more. for example, when you enter the mansion for first time, all Neighbor will do, is to walk from A to B and look around, and maybe walk away for a while. later, as you progress, he will sleep and walk from C to D. not more. positive point is that stealth is actually required this time, but sometimes the man will notice you from the other end of the house and catch you from a distance. he can. but it doesn't do daily activities, it is programmed to be aware of your arrival and chase you if necessary. sometimes it just stares. a lot of people will complain about the final battle, but I personally liked it. the mentioned "lack of daily activities of the AI" is maybe just my sadness, I enjoyed just looking at the AI and experimenting with it. Because of this, the randomness of the game is more limited, than it was in HN for example..as far as I know, neutral network - where the AI learns from each player - was taken out too, but I'm not complaining, rather take it out, than release it in unstable and not tested state.- story and characters.let's start with the cutscenes; one way or another, I'll never get over them :D they were nice, but a bit short, they just served as transitions and only as that. if you were as deeply into HN as I am, then you'll also experience lack of symbolism this time. the story is fully understandable, if you did read the books, because this game partly was based on them. but just partly. rather on the books, than on the first game, which is supposed to be the base, because this game is titled "HN2"the characters kept the good balance, however [Neighbor and Aaron, I mean. we didn't really get to know the rest, not even the journalist, who I will not call Quentin, because he is nothing like the old one]. they weren't like in the books (thank god!) it was the good and healthy balance that your character needs if you're a story creator. credits to whoever forced them to be like this. the original message of HN and especially, Neighbor did remain - for now. he isn't a villain and I will say this until the day of my death. :D - additional thoughts.you can't interact with as much items as you could earlier. and after you finished the game, you can explore the map and that's it.for me, the puzzles were a bit similar in the houses, and I'm someone, who has a hard time memorizing numbers....yeah. visually, the game looks nice, the artstyle isn't that close to my heart, compared to the original HN, but it's still fine. also, the puzzles are much easier, and more straightforward, than they were in HN.- but.why am I still recommending this game then, despite it has flaws? because it does have flaws. it often crashes because of nothing, or freezes, despite I have the recommended card. you can get stuck at places, where you run for shelter. not gonna mention small things, like clipping etc-it's not an issue now. so?I recommend it, because I know how much work, effort, RESTART from scratch, dreams and cancellation of plans were put into this sequel game. I followed the development and sometimes struggle of HN2 in the past years. people were pushed to the background, others left, others arrived. this game had insane deadlines, again.I really do hope and wish the best for Eerie Guest Studios - they have some really great and kind hearted people, whose talent shows since the very first version of HN. ***this game franchise doesn't deserve the hate it gets. if you're still reading, then at least once in your life go and try it out yourself if you can, and do not listen to the reviews of random people. try it yourself. and maybe you will like it. I'll sign, that not everyone may like this genre.the original HN was ahead of it's time, an unique game. I'm saying this for sure.
