_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, pretty good in fact but not great. That being said its "Early Access" so expectations still exist.For starters the game is as others are saying, its a Rimworld type functioning game with a different look and feel.Cons It's the look and feel that both brings it up and brings it down. Being more immersed visually creates the feeling to have a mental and emotional need, this doesn't give that (yet). There is no real story or end game goal and by that I mean the experience is at the moment very short lived, what you get 1 hour into it is what you get the rest of the game so far (speaking of the gameplay itself here). That would be the main con in my opinion but again EA so its to be expected at the moment.Combat is an area the Devs can really put more work in on future updates as it is well to be frank pretty bad. The Draft system as it is "should" be a secondary system for the active combat. To make effective use of turrets you pretty much have to create an uncomfortably large power grid that clutters the space making TD the secondary combat system atm. The taming is indeed involved in the combat however its pretty unreliable simply being an accessory to the draft system. Resource and space "balancing" are also currently more of a chore than a fun part at the moment (specifically when trying to be organized and optimized), this due to terrain constraints such as empty craters from debris sites that remain once the debris is cleared, which some Terra forming functions being implemented would greatly help while staying (realistic).ProsThe modding support, there is a lot to get comfortable with and can just as easily make the experience better as you can break the experience however, it provides a lot of capabilities. Everything that is currently in the game feels and looks unique and drives the exploratory nature as you play.The variety in resources, and equipment are amazing, in fact having this variety is currently what drives most of the  current replay ability as each map seed creates a different look and feel with scarce open plains to densely resource filled maps. with different resources available on each seed.The Seasonal effects and time spent within each greatly help the current depth of the game and what it can be.ConclusionIf you like games like Rimworld, you will like this game and will probably spend countless hours on it even in its current state. Devs are active and consistently working on the game so there is more to look forward to with an already good game. Just understand the game is EA its lacking in areas but excelling in others.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, this game is surprisingly good.  I Bought it as a diversion and expected to play it for a day or so then get bored, as that is what usually happens when I get an EA game.  Instead I just keep loading it up and just can't put it down, even thinking about how I can make my colony more efficient when I am trying to sleep. I haven't had a single crash and the only "bugs" I have run into are the ones attacking my colony and trying to eat my survivors.  I don't usually give either positive or negative reviews unless something seriously stands out.  For this game it is a positive. I made a thread about a very minor QoL improvement I felt would benefit the game.  I half expected to just see the "thread moved or deleted" message as I accidentally put it in the wrong forums.  Instead one of the devs responded that he liked the idea and would send it to the rest of the team.  This is an Early Access review and the devs are maximising the benefits of early access to make the best game they can.  We seriously need more Early access games where the target audience is listened to, instead of being told what they want and banned for daring to have an opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is deceivingly fun for a good amount of time. It seems to have some pretty good bones, until you get far enough to realize that the advancement in the game suddenly hits a dead end.Then you notice how wonky, basic, and downright terrible the building is. Trying to build a second floor is a nightmare. Want a staircase inside your base to the second floor? Well, too bad; you can't build a roof over it, even though it's a 1st floor staircase and you're trying to put on a 2nd floor roof.The amount of gear in the game is just way too basic. It feels like a alpha version of a game as far as gear goes for your survivors. Then there is the way the game eventually forces you out. Enemy waves don't cap. They just keep getting bigger and stronger. You're forced to either die or leave the planet. Players want to play their own way. Let them.Then you get the minor grievances like how the Gujo bird goes extinct in the first year as they attack things tougher than themselves and don't respawn. Getting poultry can be a serious pain. Crafting times for simple things like a single piece of electronics is ABSURDLY long. It takes way entirely too long for your people to work at their work stations. When you get an electric smelter you can only put 10 iron scrap into the thing at a time. It spends more time waiting for someone to transfer to and from it than it spends actually smelting because the inventory space on it is so low.The game is fun, but once you get to a point you'll suddenly feel like it's a half-finished product.

In this game it takes you probably 3-5h until you don't need to do anything and slowly grind to the ending.I will follow this game, based on the other games it will get a lot of DLC's, I hope with free content updates.. for now I liked the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Rimworld then you'll probably really like this game too. The gameplay is just like it, but this obviously has better graphics, and they have the same base price. I haven't played it as much yet, but I was immediately hooked, time went by quickly when playing, and it's one of my new favorites. If you haven't played Rimworld or any other colony sim then I can also describe it as being a bit like playing the Sims, but they're surviving on an alien planet they crash landed on. You have the survivors build a shelter, scavenge, chop down trees, mine rocks, observe alien life, gather and hunt food, craft weapons and clothing, build a proper cabin/base, research new technologies, make better food, alcohol, go out and explore, etc. Your survivors do get attacked by alien bugs every now and then, so it does also play a lot like a tower defense. _childDocuments_.review: I like the varied maps to start out on.  I also like the character selection with pro's and con's of each character. Combine that with mission difficulty choice, this game should be able to accommodate to a variety of player skill levels.There is just one feature that may be usefull that I wish the game provided. _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I bounced off Rimworld despite loving the concept, and found this an easier gateway into the colony-sim-with-random-attacks genre. Stranded is more intuitive to play, has a better UI and tutorials, and you start out  more basic - building scrap metal shelters and a campfire while you gather the resources and research in order to start constructing a base.Liked: Choosing from a pool of designed characters, each with their own traits, likes and skills. The ability to add modifiers like a larger team size or increased walking speed without it affecting most achievements. The look of the game. Sending people on expeditions in hot air balloons. Finding new survivors. How happy my survivors were to get carpets and musical instruments and tea and cake. Didn't love: The waiting around. Once you set your team's priorities, they quite happily get on with life and there's not much for you to do until animals attack or you have to answer the radio. Nights are particularly slow - this game really needs a faster max speed. It was disappointing that interactions between survivors were so shallow and they mainly seemed to dislike each other. The animal attacks also felt tacked on and boring (playing on normal difficulty). The game just... doesn't quite have challenge in the right places. I mean, tea and cake and carpets just a week after crash landing...I had a fun, if sometimes idle, 30 hours with it, and will probably have a go on harder difficulties to see how much that changes things. It gave me the courage to go try Rimworld again, feeling more prepared for it, and ironically bounce off just as hard as I did the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Game isn't really playable in its current state. Reason being, this game is desperately lacking a priority system. For games like this it is a must and the Devs simply just did not put on in. I spent the entirety of Spring and Summer waiting for my people to deconstruct old stockpiles and move them inside, but they thought that harvesting cloth from our farm was more important. Due to this, I lost several supplies and food and this set me back to the point that I couldn't even begin to research the items I needed. I'm also not able to get them to observe the insects I've killed before other creatures eat them. Nor will they go back for the hide on the ground after hunting and butchering an animal. There isn't even a way to take control of the characters and force them to pick certain items up. _childDocuments_.review: Ignore the haters who claim  is Rimworld and then hate on it for all the reasons it is not Rimworld -- after playing eleven hours.  RW is a fine game, but if the haters try to go back and play RW, they will wish it was more like SAD.  Part of the genius of  lies in the struggle to get your survivors off the planet one-by-one.  Attacks from local megafauna increase in intensity and frequency, so you find yourself always calculating how quickly you can evacuate, who should go first – and who should be the last person standing to hold off the worst attacks.	  This game mechanic creates a real sense of urgency and tension as each survivor bids adieu.  It’s nothing you cannot handle, as the game supplies you with a variety of automated turrets, traps, fortifications and weapons. 	  Ideally, you reach a point where your defenses do all the heavy lifting.  It can be great fun to watch as your flamethrowers and traps dispatch several hundred bugs without you so much as lifting a finger.	  But to get to that point, you have to collect resources, build up a food supply, establish a power supply, work your way through a research tree – all the things you associate with a first-class survival simulation game.  If you have dabbled in the genre before, you will find much familiar in SAD, but the beauty of the game is in its accessibility.	  Even if you have never played a survival sim, you can have great fun learning the ropes at the easier difficulties as you ponder tackling Insane/Chaos mode.	  The downsides include skill degradation, which the game never warns you about.  If you have a survivor who specializes in, say, research, but you give them tasks on occasion to help build up a secondary skill in crafting, e.g., you can come back just a few days later to learn that they have lost all those crafting points and more, because they are not constantly using the skill.  You never lose a skill level once you attain it, but any progress toward the next level can vaporize.	  Steam discussion threads are full of folks who complain about travel times to distant places.  The most obvious response is that it is not an exploration game.  After you crash land, click and drag across wide swaths of the map and all the resources in the highlighted area will be revealed.  If essential resources are not relatively handy, pick a new seed.  There are ways around any shortage, but especially if you are just beginning, you might want to minimize the challenges.	  And then there is the micro-managing.  If you set up the Activities schedule and the Priorities menu reasonably well, and you are playing on easier difficulties, everything will get done eventually.  I would suggest that this is actually the most fun way to play the game.  But let’s just agree that efficiency is not your survivors’ strong suit.	  When one of your survivors almost, but not quite finishes scavenging a wrecked spaceship, and instead of completing the task decides to meander back to camp to eat a fruitcake, the temptation is to jump in and direct the survivor back to the wreckage.  Odds are some other survivor is already heading out to finish the job.  But you have to be a certain kind of person, that I am not, to just let things unfold, however inefficiently.	  Finally, allow me to praise the online community, which is extraordinarily helpful and generous with its time and wisdom.  Flin Fredstone, Bjorn, tommy_b_schmidt and many others are the unsung heroes of this game.  The devs are a pretty constant presence on the forums as well, which is always a good sign.	  I have replayed the game numerous times without a single glitch and every playthrough has been different and uniquely challenging.  There are many different seeds, different teams that you can choose, different biomes, and two additional scenarios (Military Outpost and Sow and Sell), not to mention an active modding community, that make the game almost endlessly replayable (although if there are glitches, mods are almost always to blame).  I appreciated that the achievements could be obtained, more or less, just by playing the game.  Beware, though, that a Perfect Game with all achievements can become imperfect when they add content and new achievements, even after the full release -- and after you have moved on to some other game.	  This is one of those rare games that appeals to casual gamers, but as well to those who prefer a game into which they can invest many hours.  There is always one more thing to research, one more fortification to build, one more preparation for winter.  So feel free to blame me when you look at the clock and are surprised to see it is two or three in the morning.  Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this to support the development of the game.  It is quite developed for an early access game.  The game can be quite challenging or much simpler depending on the seed you select for your world build.  Some fine tuning needs to occur on the degradation frequency of certain components and items.For 25 hours in - I can honestly state that I have enjoyed it thus far.  It is very playable at this stage of development.  If you like base building and resource survival games then this should work out for you.Pros:- Good research aspect- Built to have the player invested in their survivors.- Tailoring tasks to individuals strengths and weaknesses.- Survivors become for efficient with each task they preform over time.- Combat is straight forward without becoming cheesy.Cons:- Equipment/structure breakdown frequency.- Time to craft certain replacement parts cannot keep up with the need, especially in the energy resource department.- If your world seed does not have certain breakthroughs (i.e. research) that can be found you can have quite a struggle, such as not being able to make fuel.- Survivor relationships need work.Overall, I have found nothing game breaking but certain aspects make goals hard to obtain until the Devs smooth things out more.  I would recommend it in this state although I am certain it will improve the longer it is being developed.

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game, its ok. Visually its very good, its like getting rimworld but with a good graphic engine and 3D camera.For what ive tested so far the game is not super hard, except for the energy management that is a real nightmare. I have 25 wind generators and 18 solar panels for 5 colonists and im constantly having shortages. I have 2 freezers, 2 fridges, 1 electric furnace, the advanced research table and 2 automatic turrets, i dont think i need a nuclear reactor for that, but it seems so. Must be like in Tropico, where you need 20 nuclear plants to provide power to an island with 2000 people. Another problem is the extremely short durability of any item you make, you need new clothes and weapons every few months, and thats alsot not very realistic, and annoying.The random animal attacks can also be annoying and ive suffered 4 in a row, with like 10 seconds interval between one and the next, and this is also not ok since you take ages to recover from any injury. The tutorial teaches you fences are useful to funnel enemies, but they arent, mad animals will constantly destroy the fences, even metal ones. The randomness is a little annoying and i would like to rely on how many animals i see in the map instead of having random spawns of 10-12 mobs every few minutes combined with local animals getting mad and attacking too.The time the colonist spend working seems super short, they usually leave tasks about to finish for stupid crap like taking a walk, when they can just finish it in seconds, but no, i better stop, take a walk and then i finish this critical stuff i have to build for survival tomorrow better when im more relaxed. Some resources are for some reason absent in some maps, like not having a single cloth plant in miles around the base and having to resource only to making bark leather.The tailor must be broken because making clothing takes like weeks for 1 garment alone. Equipping the whole colony while making one jacket takes like 4 days, not ok. They really need to speed up tailoring A LOT, and i mean like 3x or faster than current speed. Its not ok to build a wall in 5 seconds and take 10 real time minutes to build 1 garment when you need a full gear every season with the stupidly fast durability decay.Another little fail: When you manage to get the radio and build everything related like the antennas, the animals get angry, but if you turn off the radio antennas and the radio table the animals keep attacking as if they were active. I would like the animals to stop being angry if i turn them off.The random chance to get a new survivor landing near and auto joining is super low, ive only got it in two games and one was like 2 days after beginning and the other game she joined after like 2 years. The only other survivor i got was from a balloon mission. Hard to increase population.Needs lots of balancing in the durability and speed of some tasks, but its a promising product. EDIT: seems they fixed the tailoring speed, i tried it and its still too slow, i think they sped it up by 10-20% but needs double speed or more, not a slight increase.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is the colony sim I have been looking for, for sooooo long. I have a thousand hours on Planetbase, Factorio and Frostpunk, but I have 100% completed them and all challenges. There is nothing left to do. I have tried other games in search, currently addicted to Sons of the forest which is a phenomenal game I might add. However I need something with more over sight. THIS GAME, is the perfect colony sim. It has all the best parts of all three of those games. Personal and base management oversight, skill building, researching, tower defense against hostiles, scavenging, seasonal challenges, exploration and more. I am 7 hours in, and I am straight hooked. This is a game I will play for years and years by itself, and in between games when I need to zone out and refresh. Two thumbs up for gameplay, graphics and play style. If you are a simulation fan this is the game for you. Like all good sim games, scavenge fast and build a defense around your base as soon as possible because you will get attacked relentlessly and repeatedly. My other advice is to get some heavy clothing ready in the fall, stock up food/ration packs, winter will hurt.

While they have added robots and drones to help with some of this, it still would be nice to see vehicle building to maybe get to those really far-away wreck pieces and whatnot. _childDocuments_.review: You've crash landed on an alien planet... lets explore ... asymmetric pedantry!What do I mean? Well you can micro manage your survivors; you can tell them not to eat raw meat, duh!. you can tell them how to prioritise farming, scavenging, crafting and other tasks so that they act (fairly) autonomously. You can even tell them not to eat any other survivors favourite foods! (I'm guessing that by default they're fairly self obsessed and don't give a hoot about anyone else, go team!).But Ken, my favourite psychopathic team member (he likes observing death , +6 happiness, that's not worrying is it?) can't seem to go to the shelves and choose a thermal jacket (crafted days earlier by Vivian) when the weather starts to turn - or can anyone else for that matter.Ken is unhappy (-6 happiness because he's cold), this is more than counterbalanced by the fact that he has nice 4x5 tile bedroom (+18 happiness). Kens got his priorities right!No he hasn't, Ken died 10 days later from hypothermia because I had the game on fast forward, desperate to believe that he could dress himself appropriately from the choice of over 25 different items of clothing without me telling him to do so.Why Ken, why? If you can prioritise your daily tasks and eat when you're hungry - why can't you dress yourself when you're cold?I would like to think he died happy - because I told everyone else not to eat his favourite meat stew, but now it's going bad because Ken isn't around to eat it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a "meh" category.It's not bad, but it's far from great.  It's  current Rimworld.  It's closer to Rimworld during the early alpha days (I backed Rimworld on Kickstarter).  It has an end-game.  You can win it.  But . . ..The "colonist" AI actively fights you when you try to fight.  It loves to spam massive hordes of enemies to zerg-rush your base.  And your non-drafted colonists will actively "go for a leisurely walk" right through the horde.At least, unlike AColony, I didn't die within one second of starting a map.  But, being able to successfully win a game (evacuating a total of 6 survivors) on my second game . . ..And let's talk about those survivors.  Sure, they have pretty art for each one, but, they're all pre-made characters with pre-made baggage.  And those are the only survivors you'll get to see.  You can't make your own.  And with the Denuvo Malware, you won't be adding your own, anytime soon.This game  Rimworld.  It wants to be, but it isn't.  It's not a bad game.  It's pretty, but coupled with Denuvo, I'd say go play Rimworld and avoid this until they remove the bloatware  it goes on sale.  It still needs an epic amount of work to approach Rimworld.  It's not a $35USD game.  It's a $20USD game.  With Denuvo, it's a $5USD game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is to Rimworld what many might claim Rimworld is to Dwarf Fortress. Better graphics, but severely parred down. There is nothing in this game you couldn't find a more in-depth experience doing in Rimworld instead. Add to the fact you can only have 8 total survivors and things like a basic inventory system for survivors to carry meds/food/bandages and it sort of seems like this could should've stayed in Early Access with the promise to continue expanding on the foundation it's built here.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review for post early access launch.Stranded: Alien Dawn is a colony survival builder game not unlike Rimworld.  It has 3 game modes that all center around building a base strong enough to survive wave after wave of giant insect swarms:Crash landing:  You crash land on a planet have to flag down passing ships and escape one survivor at a time over the course of a few months.  (So you have to build a base that can basically defend itself.)Military Outpost:  You have to build and defend a relay.Trading Outpost:  My favorite game mode.  You start with up to 3 survivors and a dream: Buy the planet.  Any members past your initial set must be hired, and they will leave if you fail to pay their wages.  You get credits by trading with passing ships, with each transaction costing you 50 fuel to send the trading pod up.I do recommend it, but the game is lacking features that other colony survival games have.  For instance, although it is a 3D game, this game does not let you build multi-story buildings unlike "Going Medieval".  As far as Rimworld features go, it's missing the ability to auto deconstruct old/damaged clothing/weapons, the ability to teach dogs how to haul, basically any relationship features save for marriage, a more fleshed out priority system that lets you prioritize workbenches and probably a few more that aren't coming to mind at the moment.  That said, I played through every game mode and enjoyed it.  Plus the game does have mod support.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Banished that improves on it in several ways.  It benefits from shrinking the scope to a small group rather than a village, while increasing the depth of the crafting system tremendously. Be as primitive or advanced as you'd like, but achieving a balanced sustainable home base is satisfying and worth the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: So I have put about 150 hours into this game since it released onto early access.  For an early access game I found it surprisingly well fleshed out.  It is early access and I look forward to seeing where this goes. Currently you kind of get the same old grind of things after a bit. Not Much Story even among the character interactions which is an area I hope that they develop.  I Do think that this is intended in order to create a lot more interesting goings about and add some variety to it on playthrough. It has a lot of potential and is enjoyable in its current state. The Things I did find after 150 hours is that this game for me gets a bit too repetitive and it is my sincere hope that the developers finished product will have extensive modding support and more depth to its characters and social interactions among a few other things. If the mission is to survive I did not find this much of a challenge and would like to see a bit more attention paid to the logistics of managing the survivors.  I Spent the majority of the game on the highest fast forward setting and easily overcame the few pickles i found myself in managing my survivors.  Its worth buying and supporting the devs and i sincerely hope they put up a roadmap.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Denuvo and their weird choices on the EULA aside... This is one of those "I wish there were a neutral button" reviews. This game was REALLY fun initially and I am hesitant to post a negative review after only paying $30 for 30 hours of entertainment but I probably won't play this game again after getting to a point where the micromanagement of ridiculous tasks started impacting my ability to enjoy the rest of the game. This was sad because I really was having a good time to this point.The main source of my frustration is from the wear and tear mechanic, or more specifically how to avoid that mechanic. You'll find yourself manually un-equipping and reequipping items constantly in this game for various reasons since there's no interface which allows you to automate this that I'm aware of. Your futuristic weapons have no option for repair or recharge and for some absurd reason even if never fired while equipped will break within a few years. The same goes for your synthetic high tech armor, and presumably just about anything else you can wear in the game. So, you're left with a decision to either remove them manually after combat (season or weather change etc) or watch them wither away. I can understand a straw hat made from hay lasting a year but a pistol or a set of synthetic armor being destroyed after 3 years is pretty silly.This mechanic would not be a huge deal at all if switching gear was easy, reliable, or if there was a way to automate it but as it stands it takes way too much time to do this and it snaps me right out of any immersion I had going on at that moment. I realize they have to create scarcity but this is just not a well thought out way to do it in my opinion and a very simple solution would be to decrease the decay on items which make sense. There is really no danger from the combat (for the most part) in the normal difficulty mode so I'm assuming this is their way of balancing it a bit once you start getting better items but it just makes for a frustrating experience.The rest of the game is a solid 8/10 so if you don't mind micromanagement on that scale you'll probably like it.

_childDocuments_.review: As we may know top down games that focus on survival have been hit or miss with their building mechanics over the years. The progression from "stone age" to the what I call "the advanced age" is not too short but not too long. In fact it is satisfying when you do achieve the next step with the survival journey. I would recommend this game as I put 200 hours into it but felt something more like 80! Great game I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Got this at 35% off, and it still wasn't worth the price. Could have been a thumbs down, but there's nothing egregious about it.It's an ok little game. More sane and playable than Rimworld, but limited in scope and appeal. Controller support is a huge plus, and I was able to play this from a couch start to finish (thanks for that devs).  I guess you could replay this over and over, but I feel no urge to what so ever. It well done, reasonably stable (got one freeze deconstructing a complex building) and polished enough.  It's not AAA at all, but still gives you a decent experience although a fairly blend and generic one. The characters are uni-dimensional, no voice, no real story, nothing memorable. This made me appreciate Riftbreaker, which left a stronger impression in the same style, even though it was a small game too. _childDocuments_.review: Good game for EA. Lots of good mechanics in here, good graphics, and the unique traits of characters are good. I really, really look forward to the full release.That said, there are weaknesses. The AI and tasks need significant work. When you hunt or butcher an animal, the task excludes the hides. The butchering character won't go back and transport them. You have to either manually designate it or hope whatever character you have on delivery duty gets to it before it rots.The characters also forget tasks, or interrupt themselves. It's frustrating to have someone doing a task, hit an anything or relaxing hour, drop the item, do whatever else, and then start a new task instead of continuing what they were doing, because if you weren't paying attention you'd never know that now there's some resource sitting around rotting.Research breakthrough being tied to Seeds instead of randomized is a weird choice, as well. Effectively, it encourages making a Seed list (I think there a few that are starting), list all the starting area resources, all the breakthroughs, and then people just picking the "best" start for the gameplay they want. To me, randomized would be much better.Resource uses aren't really balanced either, which I can sort of understand, but you wind up with the mushrooms being a holy grail resource since it's food, healing, and with just being under a roof it lasts forever. Find a seed that gives you hay cloth and with two crops you have food, clothing, and healing covered, which is a huge chunk of the resources you need covered. A bit of balance here is needed. Maybe giving the mushrooms a shelf life and some sort of drying research to extend that, like with pickling.Fruit bushes are another bumper crop, but goes bad with no way to preserve it besides freezing. Maybe some sort of preservatives research, with the action of making preserves be an active task (like crafting a weapon or clothes)?Overall, a good start to a game that gives me good hope, but balancing and AI improvements will make or break it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me a bit down the middle. For one, I'm sorry, but its hard not to compare this game to Rimworld. Very similar concept and mechanics with even early Rimworld quality of life mods being implemented off the bad. If you own Rimworld its hard to look at this and think its worth the investment for the same thing. Like wise if you're on the fence between the two games it really comes down to preferences. Stranded: Alien Dawn is a bit more simplistic in that there are less mechanics and modifiers to worry bout, but that maybe a good thing. The game also has clearly stated goals to work and strive for which is a big plus if you've played Rimworld and just... couldn't get into the whole 'make your own fun/goal' concept while keeping the core concept and gameplay loop you're looking for from it.With that said, combat is downright boring with rush and sheer numbers being the only things the AI can do. I honestly hate how the enemy just sort of... "manifests" into existence wherever they want. Pawn is walking down the road and suddenly they're surrounded by 200+ bugs that just teleported on top of them from the lord in heaven himself. You can sort of control combat by just having the front gate open which seems silly, but I get the AI is really basic so whatever. Like Rimworld, while the game is fine out the box, there is just SO MUCH to consider while playing that the game is going to sink or swim based on its mod community. Off the bat needed mods. Improved storage and batch crafting mods. You need a tone of electronics for everything late game and just like with Rim's components, one at a time isn't going to gut it when you need like... 50.With that said, I can see how this game's more focused goal and easier to digest maps can appeal to some and why they would want it. It reminds me a bit of D&D and Pathfinder. Pathfinder had some good ideas to streamline the game and make things more simple by combining the huge skill tree. Stranded: Alien Dawn does the same thing to Rimworld, like literally, but....some people want that. Personally, I'm not done with all the achievements and personally I feel like I've seen everything already and getting a tad bit bored by by 6th back to back bug invasion on Outpost with no time to repair. Well whatever. Not a bad game if that's what you're looking for. UI is a bit cumbersome. especially when you start dealing with the varying heights and just very specific ways to click something to get it selected.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games you'll either love or go not for me.And if you do love it (like me) be prepared for a lot of "where did the time go?" moments. There is a bit of micro managing and waiting for something to happen, but over all there's enough game play for me to make those periods bearable. There's also a lot of resource juggling while keeping everyone from having a massive meltdown. Which when it does happen is often quite entertaining.Like most games in this genre', there could be a few QoL additions to reduce the micro managing. Like being able to mass select bulldozing items, Or not having to bulldoze constructions instead of simply upgrading them to a better version. But I think this might be intentional, since much of the game play is managing a limited labour pool of 4 survivors and a massive amount of tasks to do. Still it makes for a lot of selecting/clicking...But don't get me wrong in the end I do highly endorse the game if it's in your wheelhouse.

_childDocuments_.review: In this video game, you find yourself on an exoplanet with a hostile environment where various random disasters occur. The game is planet-side, where you control a team of multiple survivors. In different game scenarios, you have access to supply pods, rescue pods, or can trade items with passing spaceships. While you are on the same exoplanet, you can visit different biomes or ecosystems, allowing you to play in various planetary regions that impact the gameplay experience.During each playthrough, the in-game environment is procedurally generated, ensuring a unique experience every time. The game uses the same engine as "Surviving Mars," giving it a visually realistic simulation of an exoplanet survival-focused game style.This game offers a diverse gameplay experience in each playthrough due to multiple different scenarios, biomes, procedurally generated environments, and varying resources. The research and tech tree variations also add depth to the gameplay."Stranded: Alien Dawn" is particularly interesting for older players due to its deep and complex planning and strategies required to coordinate your team of survivors in the harsh exoplanet environment with alien wildlife.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so while I would recommend the game it's game so moderate - serious kinks. For example, your survivors seem to prioritise carrying out tasks over caring for themselves. _childDocuments_.review: There is a lot going for it but it is still early access for a reason.  Vital things are extremely difficult to obtain/craft such as clothing and electronic parts.  Even after getting the appropriate resources and having maxed out settlers producing these items it can take several days to complete.  This is pretty bad considering it can take a few days to each items to break so by the time a settler creates their first pants, everyone is already walking around in their underwear.The interaction between settlers are also lacking.  They can fall in love but that's about it.  No friendships/rivalry/etc.  There is a wedding arc but they can't use it at the moment since it is buggy.  Lovers also do not have a way of sleeping with each other which is odd since they get a daily penalty for not sleeping with each other.  I figured they would just remove it for now until they add that possibility.This game is a better copy of Rimworld in terms of graphics but it fails to compare to it in terms of content.  Once you get to the end game content, it's a grind to get anything done.  Oddly enough, it gets harder to survive the more advanced your group gets. After more content becomes available and things get finely tuned, this game is going to be amazing.  I will happily support this through EA and hope they don't take that support for granted.

_childDocuments_.review: The game, as it stands, could be likened to a basic version of 3D Rimworld, yet it lacks the same level of charm and variety, featuring only a single type of enemy. The available DLC adds some unusual features, but these don't quite elevate the game's overall appeal.Its mechanics are reminiscent of tower defense but are hampered by an underdeveloped technology tree. The game also seems to struggle with realistic portrayals of electricity, physics, and technological progression. For instance, players transition from using primitive bows to constructing AI-controlled machine gun turrets from mere scraps, which feels disjointed.There is potential for improvement in future updates, ideally focusing on enriching the game without relying on frequent, revenue-driven DLC releases. It may be more prudent to consider purchasing this game during a significant sale, or to wait until it undergoes further refinement and thoughtful development.

_childDocuments_.review: As another user has pointed out, they have a very crappy End User Licensing Agreement. They really can do whatever they want and they even outline rare circumstances where they reserve the right to do so, this sounds reasonable in theory but in practice the developers are always holding your copy of the game hostage in a manner of speaking. Anyway since I am stuck with the game now I will have to get my moneys worth out of it. Are you ready to hear my thoughts developers? I hate that I cannot rebind the alt key to my side mouse buttons, for anybody with a gaming mouse like me your thumb is probably resting on those side keys while playing.. games like Dyson Sphere Program allow me to rebind it and IT'S NOT AS IF THERE IS A CONFLICT, THIS BUTTON IS NOT IN USE IN GAME AT ALL AS IT IS.Also the time options should be on Q and E respectively, why on earth is the default controls set to the - and + keys? I wouldn't even care if you just copied Oxygen Not Included and its approach by having the TAB key use fast forward, pressing repeatedly brings it back to the previous options.Now let me say what I am honestly thinking here. In the tutorial you get to observe a mushroom and simultaneously set a craft on the work station. WHY ON EARTH DID IT TAKE LONGER FOR THE GUY TO OBSERVE THE MUSHROOM THAN THE DUDE WHO HAD TO GO CRAFTING? I'm not mad here, don't mistake my caps for that or hostility/negativity.. it's just baffling that in a pre-defined circumstances such as tutorials that this can happen, it could even give off the impression that if general observation is this slow the game is going to be a real slog all the way.There's also a light flickering through the trees that really, really breaks immersion and I toggled some settings off but it didn't change it. I will again investigate it later but I'm not holding my breath I can turn it off. This review is IMO rather fair unlike the EULA. _childDocuments_.review: Mostly by-the-numbers survival-management game with actual full controller support and great base mechanics, hindered by non-sensical updates and even more non-sensical DRM. And no, it's not an online game, it has DRM for no reason at all.If you're the kind to play long hours and mouse + keyboard become a pain, you probably love the "Full Controller Support" tag, and know the tale of seeing it and going "hmmmmmmmmm". Well, it's not Tropico levels of controls streamlining and ease-to-use, but it's great.Aside from that, the good twist that some games of this genre only started doing now, Stranded AD already does, which is the character selection. Instead of the "randomly generated peeps with numbers that either make-or-break-the-game or make-no-difference-because-we-don't-want-to-kick-the-player-in-the-nuts", you choose between different pre-made surviors (or leave it to fate), and it's then a matter of covering your needs. When they like a task, they get happy doing it, and sometimes just can't do it. It's a great start.Different than most of the genre, it also focus not on continued survival, but you do have an end goal (different on each scenario). Good amount of difficulty options to tailor how things will go until then, and survivor combinations and how to approach things will help keep the replayability high.Development went really well out of Early Access, with set goals and roadmaps. New game modes got added, mod support got implemented, and more importantly, several quality of life features got introduced that reduced micromanagement. It's still a personal pet peeve of mine that doing micro to battle is LEAGUES beyond not doing it, and this wasn't nowhere touched so far, so this might be a heavy turn off for those who prefer the management side more than the battle (but there is a "pacifist monsters" option).New DLC dropped, and I was anxious to try it and give a bit more of support for a game that is on the cheap side for the amount of content, but the update came with changes that did nothing but create more busy work while making no sense at all, creating artificial difficulty for the sake of it. Given that, and the fact that the developers have not even bothered addressing keeping a DRM on a single player game that is doing nothing but being a pain on players with poor internet connection, I'll just change this from positive to negative to steer away anyone hoping that things would have changed for better after launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan f this game. It really is just a re-imagining of RimWorld. It feels a little less fleshed out but it has big enough skill trees and enough scenarios to keep you busy. If you've not gotten Rimworld full edition yet on sale, get that. If you have and you're looking for a prettier adventure this fits that niche nicely. I've had great fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Five hours in and I'm having mixed feelings.  To be sure, the game isn't bad, but there are some issues.  It really does remind me of when RimWorld launched, which is appropriate since so much of the gameplay seems directly influenced by that game.  Also, very similar to RimWorld, modders have stepped in to shore up, modify, or add completely new components to the game - allowing people to really customize their experience - if not for this, I'm not sure how I'd feel about the game overall.As I haven't progressed that far into the game, or the tech tree, based on the gameplay videos, this won't be a comprehensive review or a final judgement on the game.The game has a lot of good points, but most of those are based on the similarities to RimWorld.  I don't think I need to elaborate on that too much.The things I feel that need a bit of work are the pacing, speed control, and setup options when starting a new game.  The pacing feels a bit slow overall and even when changing the game speed, the highest speed feels slow.  My survivors go to bed and it still takes awhile for night to pass - it isn't like we're talking minutes, but compared to RimWorld it just seems slow and considering how progression overall seems slow, it makes the entire game seem to drag.  Then there are limited options when creating a new game.You can enable or disable raids, but you can't actually change the frequency.  Because of this, the raids appear to follow a set pattern, which just makes it seem like the insects have a calendar that they follow for attacking - "Uh oh boys, we've got a raid on the calendar for tomorrow - let's go kill some humans!"  I'd like options for changing the frequency of everything from storms, raids, weather events, etc.  From 0 to however many days (to set the random frequency), but raids must be y days (again, 0 to whatever) apart at least.Anyway, if you like RimWorld, there is a good chance you'll like this.  It isn't a one-for-one copy, but if you've played RimWorld you will immediately recognize a lot of its influence.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Haven't bumped into any bugs, but the AI could be improved upon. It's annoying to watch the survivors go back and forth instead of going in a straight line. I've had survivors run a good distance just to spend two seconds on a task and then take off before they finish the task... annoying.  I think the game is adequately challenging on the harder levels, but is mind numbingly slow on easy mode and since the attacks are rare you have a hard time getting resources from the critters since they are sparsely populated on the map.I would like the ability to prioritize the activities and crafting tables so I can control what all my survivors are focused on.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  If you want a chill, no-challenge little game where you set people to do stuff and then basically walk away, or if you *really* can't stand the Rimworld graphics and don't mind playing a much more simple version of that game, then this may fit what you're looking for.I'm not totally sure how to rate this, but I've enjoyed my two playthroughs a bit, and it's only $30, so I think it deserves a thumbs up.The problem with the game is that it's really easy/simple, and it's really a one-time play type of game.  There really just isn't that much to do.  I won the first time I played (easily), and played through a second time when they added animal taming, but that really didn't add much to the game unfortunately.Basically, if Dwarf Fortress is college, and Rimworld is high school, this game would be early elementary school (but with okay graphics).  If you have never played any games like Rimworld, then I assume Stranded: Alien Dawn will provide some challenge and a lot of fun.  If you've ever played Rimworld, then this game will be a complete breeze and just a relaxing, semi-boring little builder game with some farming and crafting, and some attacks by animals that you will dominate.Also, I highly recommend NOT playing with the random survivors option turned on.  To me, random survivors seems like it should be the base way to play the game (A spaceship crashed, but in this game you get to pick all of your survivors?  That should be an option in my opinion, and if you choose your own survivors you shouldn't be able to get achievements or something).  If you go with random survivors like I did on my first playthrough, you start with each of the survivors having a railgun sniper rifle which is the best weapon in the game (there are only like 5 weapons, although you can research "advanced" railgun sniper rifles... *snore*).  With 4 railgun snipers, you basically don't need to build defenses until the 2nd or 3rd year, if even then.Anyway, the game was fun to play through, and the second time was okay I guess, but I don't know if I'll ever play it again unless there are a lot of major updates that make it more interesting.  I had been looking forward to this one for a while, so it's a bit disappointing that it's so simple and easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok, I just expected more. It gets really slow at a certain point where you kinda have to build Mechs in order to scout out the map... exterminate bug colonies, rinse repeat. Then researching that technology gets a little bit dull and I cant imagine that it gets any more challenging from a survival standpoint other than the fact that the game just evolves in to a tower defense as you progress. I've put a lot of hours in to Rimworld, and I think the reason there is because there are so many permutations and weird stories that come up in that game - thats what keeps me coming back to it. In Stranded : Alien Dawn, that is not the case though. You don't really get the suspense of different interactions and strange permutations of neighboring tribes... endless moments where random people could join or leave. S:AD has a very static approach to forming your caravan and embarking on your journey. Its less chaotic, sure but its definitely a bit more boring to play this way. In S:AD you will only ever encounter the static characters that you can choose your initial group formation. The interactions those characters have is not all that interesting, and accessing the log of what conversations happened, what their preferences are or what makes up their personality is a little cumbersome and not as rewarding by comparison to something like Rimworld.But if you're the type of player who has never experienced a Survival Sim Base Builder, this could be a good entry in to your series. If you're veteraned up from your experience in Rimworld, you'll probably find this game to be a bit more like the "diet coke/walmart" version... If you are a hardcore Rimworld enthusiast and play with various mods, creating religions, experiencing all that RW has to offer - you'll find this game super boring.Like I said, its ok though. The graphics are pretty fair for a 3D adaptation. I'm 20 hours in and I feel like I've experienced all this game has to offer, make of that what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game, the trailers looked real good. Got in and immediately realized it's optimized about as well a horse trying to pull a train. The game constantly chugs and stutters. I was willing to put up with it but then I realized how bad the gameplay is. It's very hard to know which units will do what task when instructed, and every task is clunky and the UI is not helping. Half the time I was instructing my people to do something, they'd ignore me and just stand around doing nothing. What made me get my refund was the combat. You have to select each individual unit, "draft" them (preventing them from doing anything non-combat related), and MANUALLY instruct them to fight. Not only will they not defend themselves EVER unless you instruct them, but they run away in all random directions. I couldn't even find one of them after she had ran away to the far corner of the map. Stay away from this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying Stranded: Alien Dawn! I have not encountered any bugs aside from the ones to make soup with so very playable for an early access title. I like the multiple avenues for research and the challenge when a tech you want isn't available yet (but was on a previous play through). I find the game modes and difficulty levels challenging enough that I have not chosen the worst of the survivors to start the game with. A must buy for those who enjoy this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: If the Sims were crossed with Borderlands and Project Zomboid (but in proper 3d and without zombies...yes okay it's a stretch but it's that isometric vibe).  Very addictive and can be quite brutal, luckily autosave comes to the rescue.  Takes forever to get anywhere what with the constant staying alive mechanic, keeping your survivors happy, and trying to amass resources.  I'm nearly 30 hrs in and have only just unlocked automated turrets - game changing.  Finally I can get on with developing instead of barely surviving one mass attack to the next.  Brutal and frustrating, but ultimately very satisfying when you start to thrive.  Not a game for just dipping in and out of...
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously as an early access game, this still needs a lot of polish. What they do have is pretty solid however, and with a few quality of life improvements in the control aspect, and some actual interesting things to discover out in the terrain, they may have an amazing game on their hands. Being able to manage things like individual schedules, and what they prioritise, is really cool. If you like resource management games, crafting, settlement building, survival or even The Sims, you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a game similar to "Lagoonia" was and I have finally found it. This game is amazing! Love the ability to research and build my little colony. I would highly recommend this one to anyone that likes exploring, gathering and building. I also love that the game drops new resources/spacecraft for things you can't really find on the land.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Another survival game, that has breathtakingly annoying rot cycles asynchronous to useless growing cycles, based on seasons that only serve the threat of winter. Another survival game with uselessly exaggerated damage by use. Another survival game, in which whatever attacks has x-ray vision and therefore spends more time doing random buildiong damage than hunting targets in the open. Another survival game, in which its protagonists whine, that their Chardonnays doesn't have the universally accepted serving temperature - 20 days after crashing into an alien world. Reason enough for yet another meltdown. Hoo-ray!Stranded Alien Dawn looks interesting and could be fun. It isn't. It is just another game, which tries so very hard to be Rimworld, but instead of a presenting a nifty, fresh idea or three to lift it above the classic template, it does nothing more than falling short in direct comparison. There is not enough novelty in this game to make it interesting, even if and when its wonky base game loop is fixed.A tip to the developers?Survival games should be 4X - explore, expand, exploit, and exterminate. SAD, like so many others of its kind, is merely 5R - rot, repair, replace, riot - and ultimately repress.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Update on April 9, 2023: Newest update made the game fun and interesting again. Started a new colony with the newest update which added a few new twists and items. A lot of the previous game breaking issues seem to be resolved now so game is playable and enjoyable again. Comment on March 12, 2023: This game was great until the most recent patch. Now batteries stopped charging properly, leading to them slowly draining til you no longer have batter power every again, furnaces and 3d printer queues don't work, unable to move items, game frequently freezes. If these issues are resolved I would come back to update my comment but right now this game has drastically lost my interest. I would love to play more but I don't forsee myself playing much with the latest patch issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not saying this game is high budget 3d Rimworld, but it's high budget 3d Rimworld. I'm not saying that's a bad thing, I actually enjoyed it for the 115 minutes I played it out of the maximum of 120 you're permitted before you cannot return a game, but it's... lacking.Instead of randomly generated colonists, it has pregens, there is a colonist limit of 8, of course it has none of the good mods, and while it has a number of refinements I legitimately do like, at the moment it's simply not worth the 30 dollar price point.I might take another look come the spring or summer sale, but for the moment, I'll just stick to Rimworld to meet my Rimworld fix.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Initial review: ~8 hours. Edited review: ~14 hours and completion of Crash Landing scenario on Medium.I can definitely understand why some people have given this game negative reviews. It is a very, very slow-burn of a game. In the first few hours, at least on the scenario I played, although I was enjoying it, I just didn't feel as though I was really progressing much, mostly because there's a ton of setup. With only 4 survivors to start out, there is a lot of micro-managing that needs to be done, between observing crops and animals to see if you can grow/tame them, keeping food stocked up, gathering resources, taking care of aggressive mobs, researching tech and then building up your base. I also noticed, again in this specific scenario, that getting extra survivors is incredibly rare. In my ~14 hours I managed to trigger 1 special event that got me a 5th survivor, which was definitely helpful and sped-up progression. Now, I do have to mirror some of the negative feedback here. Tweaking the "assignment panel" and setting priorities based on what my survivors are best at, still led to certain things not getting done and a lot of manual "go here, do that". It seems like the game only wants each survivor to do 1 or 2 specific tasks and stick to them, but it's simply not possible when you've only got 4 guys and a ton of different tasks (some of which probably shouldn't be considered tasks) to do. It also feels like certain tasks within a specific task-type have higher priority (which you cannot see or change) than others.Also, because of how tasks are categorised and divided up, in some scenarios, 3 survivors will all be doing parts of 1 thing. For example, you'd think cutting a crop, replanting it and then taking the produce to storage would be 1 complete task within "Farming", but it isn't, it's actually 3 different tasks (Cutting, Farming, Delivering), which all have their own priorities (and therefore survivors set). Meanwhile, crafting items and cooking are done on a "what's first in the list" priority system, so you'll constantly need to tweak what you actually want your survivors making. Also, when I say "craft until 3" and those get crafted, why doesn't it get removed from the queue instead of staying there with "limit reached" on it? Small thing, but can make the menus cluttered. Once you progress through the research and start getting into electricity, you might think a lot of these tedious tasks would end up no longer being an issue and therefore streamlining gameplay. Yes and no. For example, the drones (a much later research) do improve gameplay, as they will handle delivery of resources to/from storage (only the delivery), however your actual electrical grid can be very fiddly to set up. Although at the start, it can be as simple as slapping down some wind turbines and solar panels and then linking everything up with power-poles, some tedium creeps back in when you want to start setting up and automating things, especially base defenses, as they can be a massive power-drain. Changing circuits on any electrical equipment is a task that a survivor has to complete and turning a switch on/off is also a task that a survivor has to complete. Therefore, constructing a bunch of turrets, linking them up to a switch and having everything set to specific circuits can still be a lot of manual "go here, do that" for a survivor. It's even worse when the switch is off (so the turrets are too), then you get a raid on your base and need to select a survivor to manually go and turn the switch's state over to activate the turrets. You can only get true automation when you've further researched the various sensors and have then spent the time linking everything up to their respective circuits and such. You then think you can relax and let your survivors get on with tasks that matter, like feeding themselves and researching/crafting stuff, but what then happens is that electrical equipment constantly breaks down and needs repairs - and I do mean constantly. By the time I was finishing up the scenario, I had about 20 carbon wind turbines and I am not joking when I say that every ~30 seconds, one of them was "malfunctioning". For some of the tech, this can be a major hassle, as you'll need 1 of your survivors permanently stuck to the soldering bench making CPUs or some-such to keep up with the repair demand. That is unless you get lucky and keep getting them from passing ships (when you've got the orbital radio set up), or from expeditions.As for the combat stuff, I'm on the fence. It felt a little tacked-on to pad-out play time. From what I can tell, the amount of enemies that will raid your base depends on your stockpiled resources and researched tech. It starts out with a couple of raiders, then ramps up to 10s of them and then 10s of multiple different variants. When you've only got 1-2 survivors kitted out and any good with combat (and no turrets yet), it can get hairy pretty fast. In my playthrough, I had a raid of like 80 enemies and had 3 of my 4 survivors bleeding out and fainted, while my commando was on an expedition; Needless to say I wasn't prepared to lose 6 hours of progress and my entire base, so resorted to some "sneaky" methods to stop that from happening.In regards to the whole "managing morale" mechanic, it's going to depend on your selection of survivors. In the entire ~14 hours I played, I only had 1 meltdown happen and it was my crafter/carpenter who was constantly moody because of... well, I don't really know why. He was fed, warm, clothed, had his own house with bed and fireplace, was constantly getting happiness from the leisure items... but nope. After his meltdown though, he gained a ton of happiness through his supposed self-enlightenment and then was never moody after that. It basically became a pointless mechanic about 4 hours in honestly. Don't overwork, sleep-deprive or starve your survivors, slap down some leisure items and give them a warm bed and you're set. A note should be made here that the selection of survivors is not balanced. I get that these are meant to be "real people" and therefore all have different skills and tolerances, but the fact is that there's a handful that make a scenario a walk in the park, while the rest of them are pretty terrible. Setting difficulty to easy but picking terrible survivors will make a scenario harder than if you played on hard-mode, but with the "OP" survivors - it's just a bit silly. I picked Greyson, Nova, Melody and Laara (Paulette joined later) and outside of the previously mentioned poorly-timed raid, I didn't have any issues. Lastly, the "end game". The end game of the scenario I played through was essentially sitting around and waiting for the next spaceship to come through on the orbital radio. The game does slow to a crawl at this point, as the more survivors you have leave, the less stuff you can get done in a given day. The best practice is to make sure you have stockpiles of everything (especially food) and have done all the research, so then it's not a big issue if someone suddenly gets rescued. For me, Nova popped up on screen telling me to leave her till last, possibly due to the fact that she had every skill at max level, thanks to an expedition she went on, or possibly due to her innate ability to completely avoid meltdowns. It is definitely best to leave the most resilient person till last, as others can become lonely and experience meltdowns because of that. Overall, despite the visible flaws, I am still enjoying my time with this game thus-far and I am glad I got it from Humble after eyeing it up for quite some time. It's definitely a case of needing to enjoy this genre and slow-burn type of game though.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun survival, colony base builder.A Rimworld-lite, Banished-lite, fun and relaxing game to play in an interesting setting with good variety.I find myself coming back to this title regularly, and sinking another 5-10 hours into a base.This aided by nice variety in planets/environments, and the added replay-ability offered by different game modes.Lots I would like to see improve, but their formula works, and works well, and the setting it what helps deliver it to one of my favourite games of it's type in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Game was ok on the release, but there is no new content since April, don't recommend to buy -- abandoned by the developers.Valid point about the game is the finished product, but with the great mechanics i would like to see more replayability, with no bugs or so. Just feels like small version of something great.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, i've just finished the game! My last guy left the planet during an attack that he would probably not have survived ! Very addictive and not so easy. Really loved it. A few, small bugs (only a few days after the release of the early access !) but nothing serious and a very rich game. In a word (or little more) you select 4 survivors (out of 20 I think). They escape from a crash and will have to survive on an alien planet with only their bare hands. So choose wisely ! They don't have to same abilities. They'll have to cook, make their own clothes to survive fierce winters, houses, fields etc. You may even marry two of them which would increase significantly their mood (and you'll see that it is VERY important!). The second part of the game is the toughest from my point of view : you'll be able to contact vessels that will be able to rescue your survivors, one by one, diminishing slowly but surely your already small team. And to my point of view this is the most difficult part of the game (especially when there's only one left).This game is amazing and will put you through the most opposite emotions in a very short period of time. You're totally free to build everywhere you want the rooms and buildings in the shape you want (no second floor to buildings though but that's not a problem). So think well : not to lose time, no to disregard the well being of your team (temperature, distractions, dry and clean clothes, good and diversified meals, a nice living space), and you'll have to organize weapons to take care automatically of unfriendly visitors (bc even when there's one or two left, you'll have hords of enemies running to your precious devices).  Then yes, I do recommend this game 100% !
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much everything I ever looked for. Like Rimworld, but without the crappy graphics, and it feels more immersive than Going Medieval. What the game sorely needs though is to add a character customization for at least one survivor. This would allow for more playability with the already included survivors, as their dynamic often means picking niched characters, and it's kinda boring. It also need to implement more interaction between the survivors, as it is right now it's just a lot of arguing.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This one is perhaps my favourite survival sim. Rimworld is much deeper, but Stranded is prettier. It's a complete game with enough challenge and also an ending. This game has some replay value, but sadly, not enough. There could easily be much more variation in the flora and fauna, it's just a matter of DLC. But I feel I have played this game through enough times now. This still has so much potential, but I believe the devs have shipped this one and forgot about it. Anyway, it was worth the 100 hours I put into it. This could have been a true masterpiece, but capitalism says no.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: There is most definitely a good game in here screaming to be let out but i dont believe it will ever be realised (thats why after my first review [left below] I kept trying to find it).Rather than focusing on big updates the devs clearly need to focus on getting the basics right. Pathing is still a joke.two examples Hunt far away killing multiple animals the survivors still wont collect all of the items (of the same type) meaning multiple inefficient back and forth.Planting a perfect square/rectangle field where the fertility is the same through out does not result in clearly efficient planting of straight lines but zig-zagging random patterns that make no sense what so ever.And again as mentioned before attacks seem completely out of kilter with your ability. Again i love a challenge but sending scorpions on day 30 when all i have is a pistol and bows and arrows makes no sense.The only reasonable explanation is the devs expect you to behave in a certain way any any variance means failure which makes for a disappointing experience.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original review (left after the first patch):Attacks are Totally Unbalanced after the last patch.While i love a challenge the new attacks are totally over powered. I always felt that at 1 every 5-7 days was a bit much but now they are totally overpowered (Hell i have one save with three major attacks in a week and one set of hungry visitors - you cant recover with that frequency). While the fix addressed some of the issues vomit, craft time, too frequent malfunctioning and added a bit of variety to the attacks over all its done more damage than good. The most frustrating part is while a fair few early access games tweak the balance with regular patches over the first week or two it was three weeks before the first patch that has wrecked the game and days later still no word of anything to resolve the screw up.There is a fair amount of potential in this game but being so slow to address the issues gives me little hope it will live up to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable game - I cant believe this is only just released in early access, it's miles better than other more established games in this genre.  A well thought out research tree and loads of content already!  I love the turret defences, they feel powerful and work well with sensors.  The game even has an ending to work towards at your own speed.  Great visuals and atmosphere, cant wait to see the finished article.. Worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate its an early access game - Bad Storage Management, Lack of prioritisation, Missing a lot of simple content which could make it better - Not to mention the amount of bugs encountered (no pun intended) - Its promising game but unfortunately they need to fix a hell of a lot things before I would come back to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: One of my biggest issues with this game is the fact that AI/pathing, often you will find your characters standing around not knowing what to do when they are already assigned for certain task, it seems it takes them a little bit to calculate and realise what they should be doing leading me to manually assing them to their tasks which is rather annoying as this happens really often. The game has potential to become rimworld 2.0 yet it will require a lot of work still, I might check it out after a few more updates and patches. In the meantime I can't recomend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is not what i'd call easy or intuitive, you need to go through the tutorial at least once and i recommend watching several people's play through from the beginning either on twitch or you tube. However that being said this is a very fun game once you get the hang of it. Also the developers are listening to the community and making QOL improvements as well as implementing new features consistently which is always a plus. There is also just something really rewarding about playing a more difficult survival game and doing well in it! If you like survival games then this is a game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Paid $50 AUD. Played for 6 hours. Still wanting to play, so I guess it's good? It's easy to pick up. I think the draw to it is the taming animals options. It can get very hard during Winter.I do think there is room to improve though. I think paying $25-$30 would be more appropriate. I would like to see some kind of PVP option.I would LOVE to have more A.I given to the animals. It's pretty good though! Just enhance the grazing, hunting, sleeping. Give them all a little life. Maybe even show them getting playful. Currently good though. You see them hunt/graize and sleep. I found it hard to set priority tasks. Could be me. But that could be done easier. You can prioritise in sub catergories, like what clothes you're making before other clothes. _childDocuments_.review: After sinking a decent amount of time into the game, I've come to the conclusion that while I enjoy it, it's definitely got some quality of life issues. The gameplay is rewarding, the end game gives you a sense of accomplishment, and you're incentivized  to keep on exploring even after you think you've seen it all. Having to micromanage every little aspect of my survivor's lives get's pretty boring, pretty quick.  They *should* be smart enough to change clothes when the weather changes, cook food when there isn't any, or automatically defend your settlement, but they don't do any of those. I wish there was a job priority screen, that way I wouldn't have to dedicate one survivor to cooking non stop.  Either food production needs to increase (maybe 4 or 5 meals per action), or prep time needs to be cut in half. I hope the devs keep up with the game, and keep adding to it. This has definitely been a fun experience despite the steep learning curve to learning how to micromanage properly. Very late game, I feel like I'm playing asset manager instead of a survival sim since I have to manually tell every person what to do.  For instance, I managed to tame a few dogs and they had puppies.  And while I get the allure of it, preparing meals should be a higher priority than training those puppies every time one is born. I know the game is in early access, so finger's crossed they stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, don't get me wrong, but it has too many unrealistic concepts, such as humans melting down because they're a little tired (not exhausted, just not fully rested, and well-fed), as well as taking hours to traverse short distances adds to the unrealistic feel of it.   I can buy into the 48 day year given it's a moon, but the concepts of physics and chemistry are obviously alien to the engine developers. No understanding of material.  Elements don't decay, for example (although they may oxidize). It's just designed to make you spin endlessly in circles.They added a rule to allow for faster movement, however the standard engine hasn't been updated with the correct values. I'm sure there's a player base out there for it, just not any that are familiar enough with physics to care/notice the difference. Water is not a concept here, but rather a given, so if that aspect of survival is part of what you were looking for (I was), then keep looking.It's good for obsessive builders, if you can tolerate the rate of breakdowns (the false economy concept is baked in as far as that goes - nothing lasts longer than a couple of years).

_childDocuments_.review: A new take for a single player survival game that is refreshing.I'm really looking forward to further development and additions to the game.Still on my first go and used default difficulty but if there was a setting to make some of it random I chose those.  And overall it is still a bit to easy.  Random survivors having rail guns is likely why.  I think it would have been way more difficult without them and I'll try a new game later.Graphics is good enough.  Sound is ok but with a minor cooking bug where the mixing of ingredients doesn't stop unless you scroll away from camp then go back.
