_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would rate this game around 3.75/5. It is fairly well balanced and the idea of it is interesting. However there is very few reasons to keep playing after few missions as there is nothing new to try or discover. The only survival aspect is the random attacks, which after a while are quite easy to handle even on insane difficulty (or whatever the hardest was called). Depending on the mission and the planet there are few different strategies and they work every time. So once you figure them out (which shouldn't take too long) it tends to get a bit less interesting.Besides that the biggest flaw I found with the game is the AI. For example, you can queue tasks to your characters but unless the task fits their current schedule they will ignore it (in that case the queue gets cleared after last completed task). This results in annoying amount of looking after your characters (unless you clear the schedule and giving them free will to do whatever they wish, which also has its problems). The AI also lacks in the tasks the characters are about to do. They might stat traveling to the other side of the playable map to gather resources (and only pick a handful before turning back, leaving rest on the ground) when their energies are extremely low. This results them either turning back before they get to their destination or dropping whatever they were carrying and returning back. There are so many bad things about the AI that  I could go on and on about it.Depending on the mission (crash landing, military, trade) and the planet grassland, jungle, desert you end up pretty much always defending your base (unless you activate the game rules for peace when there is no need to defend). You start your missions by selecting your characters (unless you choose to opt in for random ones). Each character have their own traits (at least I found that many of them are absolutely useless and I would never pick them for a mission). You can have up to 4 characters to start the mission with (6 in military).In crash landing and military you need to research certain technology to allow you to build a specific building or buildings. Then keep them powered and defended until the end. In crash landing you need to contact ships in orbit to have your survivors be rescued one by one. In military you need to defend long distance communication device for a certain amount of time. In trade mission you need to gather enough money to buy the planet rights to yourself (maybe the easiest mission when playing in grassland or desert, where you can get carbon, or whatever its called). After few trades your done. The planets well have their differences but they affect very little on how you approach things. Whether you need to focus more on winter or summer clothing makes really no difference (and this is pretty much only a factor on the harder difficulties). There is less wood to be found in the desert, but then again there is more stone, it affects a little your initial building strategy, but the impact is has is so minor that it's barely worth mentioning. There is also different moons which apparently have some kind of a factor to the game, but apart from the chaos moon I really didn't notice any difference, so to be honest, I don't even know what the rest are supposed to do.I wouldn't pay the full price for the game, but if you find it on sale and don't mind micromanaging your characters then I would go as far as to recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid survival / base building / crafting game. I hit unrecoverable issues on my first three tries, such as not having researched something that I needed for my colonists to survive later on, through to animal attacks that overwhelmed me due to poor defences. Because it's hard it takes a long time to progress as you spend a lot of time recovering from attacks or events, such as illness, cold snaps, winter, food shortages, emotionally challenged colonists and so on.My only criticism would be that the crafting takes way too long, for example, by the time you've crafted enough shirts for your survivors your other items would have started to decay. It def needs some balancing or a more forgiving mode, but even without that it's a really solid game for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions are very positive. The tutorials and included hints/tips where uncommonly good compared to what I see in most games I normally play. But that said there is a learning curve, especially as to what is the best way to spend the early days. Importantly you start with only 4 persons and there is an obvious limit to their ability to do all the tasks you would like them to. Do not bite off more than you can chew.I belive that some gamers will  complain about stupid AI, hopeless pathing, to much or to little micromanagment, «sims functionality» building options and so on. A loud minority will probably shout for different survivor camps and much more focus on combat and warfare. The latter should be ignored, there are tons of combat/war-games and it is a bad idea to destroy a very good survival game by trying to include mechanics that most likely will not work anyway. My advise to devs is to keep the balance more or less as it is in the game today. It is my impression that the devs intend to have a solid survival game then develop multiple scenarios. That is probably a good idea.So far I have not seen any serious bugs, but that may be because I have focused on  finding the best strategy for the initial phase. The only really annoying thing so far is the repeted request for feedback in the form of handing out stars to different aspects of the game. Do not get me wrong, feedback is important but to be useful it should probably be a bit more text based. Just to rank with stars seem to be quite  pointless – i.e what would 4 stars  indicate, compared to what?If you like challenging survival games that includes base building, short and long term strategy/planning and much more do give Alien dawn a try.  The only serious risk is that you will get to little sleep to be useful at work in the real world :)

_childDocuments_.review: OUT-%$%@ing-STANDING game.  Seriously amazing.I bought this game in early April 2024, my initial reaction was "Oh no, God please no, it's one of these mobile games where you build a town and wait for energy, and they're going to try to micro-transaction me, etc.." and I couldn't have been more wrong.  I did the tutorials (which, during the first one is where I had that thought), and then jumped right into the gameplay after about 15-20 minutes.  This game gives you all of the elements!!  It has exploration, city building (well, base building), combat, and people management like The Sims, except there's not a bunch of LGBTQAAIP+-=1234 nonsense thrust into, and it's actually GOOD.  I'm in the basic crash landing mode or whatever still, I haven't even touched the other modes, and I already feel like I got my money's worth out of this game.  I've played for 38 hours, and I'm fairly certain I paid less than $38 for this game, at WORST that's $1 an hour, and I'm just scratching the surface of this game.  EXCELLENT, EXCELLENT game.  Some suggestions:- Make the amount of stuff that the settlers can do in a day "more" relative to the length of the day, or add automation to more tasks.  By the time I get my base to the point where I should be able to branch out and do some other things, my settlers are all completely engulfed in "handling" tasks, and can't actually get anything else done.  OR perhaps make a droid that can perform handling tasks, much like the drone that does transport.  That was a genius addition to the game, more like it would be welcome. - Make mech cores craftable, even if they're ridiculously expensive.  I want to build a mech and I'm near end-game, and I still have zero mech cores.  I have 2 settles always scavenging and going on expeditions and can't get the RNG to give me one.  Please remove the RNGness of mechs in survival mode (or whatever the base game mode is called).  Once again I LOVE the game, awesome job, just some suggestions that would greatly improve it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little ambivalent about the game. I really like the graphic presentation and realistic look of the worlds and people. The user interface is clean and easily understood. I like that there's an effort made to create a pool of characters who are individuals with unique traits, which really adds color to the game-play. But there are some aspects of the game that need work, and I don't think the "Tame and Train" game mechanics impact this at all: Once you understand the game mechanics (build a shelter, research and plant crops, defend your base, research a bit of the tech tree, explore and find a radio, talk to passing ships, get your people rescued one-by-one) nothing really changes, which limits the replayability. Changing locations and crew members in different games gives only minor variations, but your strategy to get your people rescued doesn't change from game to game. The challenges are essentially linear and consistent each time.I like the game, but I feel like I've already seen everything it has to show me.  Some ideas that might change things up:- More in-depth character interaction/conversations that affect relationships (characters can elect to leave your base and go it alone if you anger them sufficiently). Right now you have no control over character relationships--you're just a spectator.- Multiple methods of rescue (sometimes you can get your people out all at once, or in groups of more than 1).- Provide a "No Rescue" option where you have to create a self-sustaining colony (right now essential resources are finite and wouldn't support this mode). This would provide more value from the tech tree research; about half of it right now is unnecessary to get rescued.- Other camps of survivors, providing conflicts over resources and supplies.There are other things, too, but right now the basic strategy is too consistent.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game because it is a building survival game.  The challenges are good.  Though the manufacturing speeds are slower than they should be with the day clock speed, even with higher levels in that area.  Making a pair of pants, primitive as they are, should not take all day with higher levels.  Also, a more logical path should be followed when picking up items for transport, as I watched someone bob back and forth from one end to another instead of picking all the items up in one area at a time.  Another item to note is that these people seem to be hardy as they were traveling in space and you have to be fit, both mentally and physically.  Having any kind of meltdown should be few and far between.  In the tips that show up when someone is having a meltdown, it says that giving a direct order can break the meltdown, but everything is grayed out or red and marked with having a meltdown, so no attempt even works.  The infestation of aggressive animals are too many and ramp up too quick and they show up out of nowhere as the migrating animals have a more native path to attacking your walls, though they do just spawn randomly.  These animals should spawn more naturally and roam and find your settlement versus just popping up at random intervals and they really should not ramp up with each attack.  Another things is explorations.  These messages keep popping up, but a balloon is required to go.  If a balloon is required, then the messages should not pop up until you can build one.  Please fix these little issues.  Otherwise this is a great game and I will continue to play to see the improvements and enjoy watching the survivors and what they do.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it; The devs are improving on Rimworld and doing a good job.  The thing I don't like is the overly constant mental breaks.  I fully understand that I need to research and provide things to stop the mental breaks, but it's happening too often (as it does in Rimworld) and needs to have a option to adjust the frequency.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game and I am hooked.  As many others have commented it is like a 3D version of Rimworld (which I really like). In some respects the character AI is far better. For example your resource gatherers will skin/chop/farm/mine stuff and then take it straight back to the base/storage (unlike Rim).  There is base layout and tower defence planning required along with people management (you have to keep them satisfied otherwise they throw a tantrum and do own thing for a little while until they calm down).I like the fact that the research tree can be slightly different in each playthrough although that can make it harder for some scenarios (the fuel and power breakthroughs are key).  There is a Scrabble-bag of characters of which you can choose 4 to start off with all with different traits (some negative) and you may be joined randomly by others during the game.  It's early access and does have some minor issues particularly storage and I have had 1 game crash during 60 hours of play. Overall it is very polished and has a lot of content and depth.  I cannot wait to see what the developers will add in the future.  Definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Do not recommend.Played about 13 hours with no issues. New update drops, game won't run. Tried uninstalling/reinstalling, no luck. It appears to be something related to Denuvo - I had no issues with it previously, but of course there's no way to roll back to a previous working version.This is what happens when you prioritize releasing an unnecessary DLC over maintaining a stable base game.Sadly it's too late for me to refund. Learn from my mistakes, just pirate this instead. The concept is fine: Rimworld Lite with a lot of the depth stripped out, but in 3D.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible colony builder/survival rts. Yes, it is very similar in mechanics to Rim World. However, it has enough differences to be its own game. _childDocuments_.review: I don't really get why this is so highly rated or popular... _childDocuments_.review: This is a good game but i think it could do with a few tweaks.One thing that needs to be addressed is the ability to tell your crew to do something and not wait for them to figure it out for themselves, basically if you drip feed them things to do then they will be ok but when a lot of things need to be done then it starts to suffer as important things like cooking get left by the roadside for other tasks so everyone just ends up eating raw veggies. _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn is a enjoyable colony management experience because of all the elements that need to be managed to be successful. As a player you have to dance around keeping each colonist needs met. Be it Rest, hunger, happiness, and relaxation all while dealing with seasons, disasters, illnesses, social traits and attacks.Through all of this stuff you need to explore the local area and expand your camp while doing research to accomplish your goals. But you also need to skill up your survivors so they can do more complex tasks like build more advanced things and go on expeditions. I found all of this to make an enjoyable gaming experience.The game has an odd performance problem that does not seem to have anything to do with how big you build a colony. The game just has some unexplainable performance drops that seem Inexplicable. it seems like the day / night cycle has a problem during the winter season. During the night time it's too bright and in the morning their is an abrupt drop in light.Colonist interactions with each other are more often negative causing a problematic happiness drops.Negative happiness events stack but positive ones do not stack.Some colonist traits are unnecessarily annoying. More specifically rest recharges at half the speed for one colonist. While another is constantly vomiting because of an implant.Overall I like the game and the issues are not enough to get in the way of having fun with this one. Thumbs up for me.

_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for the base game, with no DLC, and no mods.I had a lot of fun with it and finished all the scenarios. For my first two scenarios, I played on normal and then later on hard difficulties as I learned the ropes, and I had the occasional challenge but it was mostly relaxing. It felt like the game wanted me to beat the scenario and move on rather than see how long I can grow a base for, primarily by eventually giving the player too much to do with a limited number of survivors.Having finished Crash Landing and Trading Outpost, I thought I'd seen all the game had to offer; a very competent 3D RimWorld clone (yes, it's impossible not to mention, many of the mechanics are 1:1) where the content is kind of limited by comparison, but that's understandable given how long it's been out.But then I wanted to try the last base game scenario on Chaos Moon/Insane difficulty, just to see how bad things could get, and it was like I was playing an entirely different game in the skin of the original. I say this in a positive way; to pass Military Outpost I spent a few hours looking up guides and inspiration, and I felt like I had to fully make use of every mechanic in the game to stand a chance. I eventually understood how to build a proper killbox - I'm not a fan of the necessity of it, but it's satisfying to do while you're still figuring out the details. The ball kept rolling after I'd found some stability, but interestingly, there was never a lull in the game. At every point, there was another objective I was trying to accomplish, like crafting mech cores, dealing with a massive unexpected metal shortage, et cetera, and I would often have to micro-manage the tasks to make sure the most important aspects were finished quickly. I never felt like "oh, I'll just let it run on auto and it will get done eventually".Celebrating the first New Years' Eve after barely making it was amazing. I didn't even need the extra mood for the survivors, I also did it for me, and thought "they deserve it after what they've been through". When I finally won, I felt very good about it. It was a challenging, but satisfying experience. I wish there was more in the way of base customization, weapon options, strategies for dealing with hordes, but it's a very solid core. If you liked RimWorld, or colony management games in general, you will probably enjoy this title. It also has enough things it does differently so that it has its own identity.As far as cons go, the AI pathfinding can get janky sometimes and I've had survivors get perma-stuck opening/closing a gate, as well as trying to repair an unreachable object by grabbing resources, walking for a bit, then giving up. This can be manually solved by finding the offending object, but it can be very frustrating for a large base.Also, the way the AI prioritizes tasks for survivors can be infuriating. Salvage operations will sometimes be stopped a progress pixel away from completion, meaning a full walk back later, and building will usually be done in the exact order you placed things in. This sounds reasonable until you have a hole and a missing gate in a wall during a raid because they kept on building the wall. There's also a lot of quality of life stuff around inventory management that just isn't there.The music is great, I just wish there was more variety.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: I cannot recommend this game currently, There are good ideas here & there, but balance & such just make the game kinda annoying and makes you think "Man, i should play rimworld."So this game has a few problems, one is your colonists just eat..so much food. You pretty much have one colonist Always making food and the others just inhale all the food in one day until you need to, once again, make more food.Colonists joining seems to be a stupidly rare event. So good luck if you have a colonist die.Map generation i kinda wish you could see a rough map of where you are before you make the game. More than a few times i have joined a game & i am in a sucky area.'Observing' seems to serve no purpose..at all. Sure, You observe a tree & you learn how to plant said tree. But early game? _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, with a lot of promise as it gets further built out. Some have called it a 3-D Rimworld, but having never played Rimworld, I can't speak to that. I would call it a combination of Sims and Banished/Dawn of Man, but the survival and combat are more sophisticated than the latter (and, obviously, set on an alien world in the future). Despite being early access, there is a lot here already and I had loads of fun playing it to the end-- nothing felt unfinished, though there's currently only one alien world, so replayability is somewhat limited. I hope in the future they build out the structures/furnishings some more, especially the fortifications-- it would be nice to have some electrified fences and/or something stronger than just wooden walls, especially when you have carbon nanotube structures-- and add the ability to manipulate terrain. It was annoying not being able to extend my building the way I wanted because the land next to it was ever so slightly higher and not on the same level. Being able to raise/lower terrain would also add a very cool element to base defense because line-of-sight is key, though you can partly address this by building elevated floors.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! Haven't encountered any issues across my first play through at all. Content is strong and there are lots of opportunities to create your own scenarios, so the replayability is massive. The different survivors all have their own story and their own skills and weaknesses, so the number of combinations you can have, with different end goals and game rules makes this game an absolute bargain for the price. Easy recommend and will be playing this a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that feels like a strange mix between Kenshi and The Sims. It is in no way perfect, and has some pacing issues but the biggest issue the game has is definitely the "combat" which could have been exciting but instead is just tedious, frequent waves of brainless insects which only really results in breaking the tempo and distracting you from the more fun aspects of the game: Basebuilding, resource management and colonist care. I played through two different scenarios, one on normal, one of insane, and it is definitely much easier than other similar games. I recommend this game if you like the colony survival genre, but I suggest you play on a high difficulty and turn off aggressive animals in the game rules for the best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Rimworld 2.0, in 3D. There is already an active modding community, so if you feel something is lacking rest assured there is or will be a mod for that purpose.That being said, if clothing could be automated, that would be great. Also, devs, please allow for some sort of slider for the invasions; might just had been the moon I was under, but getting four invasions in seven days killed a run dead. What I am waiting on is a mod like the one Rimworld has for customizing your people; their traits, background, age, etc,. and making custom scenarios. Biggest time sink by far is going to be just waiting on research and observations, so plan around that if you are struggling to get a footing down. Finally, I will say this game is completely doable solo on insane, which is always my test for survival games. Just takes a lot longer. _childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Only thing that I see can improve play is if the survivors can research and build generators, solar panels, balloon, circuit boxes, etc., they should be able research and build a land/wheeled vehicle (electric or fuel base) that can get you to other areas on the map quickly to either hunt, observe or harvest. It takes way to long to walk to a destination and back to complete task not near the base camp.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good idea but fails to ultimately deliver.  If the game drops to around $15 its worth a purchase.  If you're looking for a base building game managing survivors, this isn't it, its a "get off the planet as soon as possible" type game and that could be okay but the longer you play the more likely the game mechanics will eventually overwhelm you and you will fail.  Its a good idea but the game has too many quality of life issues and the team is not interested in addressing most of those problems.  There are tons of issues with the AI and efficiency that have been present for over a year with no real attempts to fix it.  Like really dumb things like exhausting themselves by taking on tasks they can never complete (too far from base etc) and not sleeping or doing jobs in a way where they will walk across a field to pick something up instead of the pile right next to them, and many other frustrating issues.  Things break too quickly, can't repair, your characters wont equip the right items for replacement, you will micromanage your people where you shouldn't to make up for the poor AI programming, bug waves and aggressiveness are proportional to your base size, upgrades are a distraction that will consume the most precious resource in game (time management).  Variety is lacking.  Read the discussion boards and you'll see many of the same types of posts complaining about the same things without it being addressed or fixed.For $35 there's plenty of other great base building games I would buy before this one that don't have these challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not playable in it's current state.I won't go into full detail, but here's the following issues I have with it:- Survivors idle frequently, and when "drafted"(controlled by you) still refuse to do tasks- Building is really bare, you cannot specify if you want certain walls open, or even add doors. You're left with U shaped buildings you have to stack onto each other in order to make some semblance of a base.Wait a little while until they figure out what to do with the building system.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this game is Rimworld with some Kenshi trappings. It does a good job of transitioning Rimworld's gameplay into a 3D space, but loses a lot of the charm that makes Rimworld such a wild ride to play. The game also fails to capture the spark of either of the games I mentioned, it lacks the depth and absolute insanity of Rimworld, the gameplay is inferior to RW, and it doesnt utilize the 3D aspects of the world in a way that would make it live up to Kenshi, with the structures you can build being relatively simple with very basic base defenses and no usable Z-axis in building to take advantage of height.The colonist are also inferior to those in either game, with much simpler skills and quirks than RW, and lacking the depth of stats and customization that make Kenshi's characters such an interesting thing to play with.All in all, if you want a simpler Rimworld with prettier graphics, I'd say go ahead, but if you have played either RW or Kenshi, or you want something with more depth to it, go back to them for another playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked playing Rimworld then this is Rimworld in glorious 3D, so what's not to like? The mechanics are essentially the same, albeit dumbed down somewhat. At 86 hours I'm about out of content but I did spend about 40hrs just making concrete so your mileage may vary. _childDocuments_.review: In its current form, the game looks unfinished. A lot of mechanics are not tuned properly. _childDocuments_.review: I don't think it does great injustice to call the game Rimworld Lite 3D. In many ways it reminds me of Rimworld Alpha 14 version, which was the first one I played. Which is not a bad thing, I really loved the game already. Because I had played Rimworld a lot, I was suspicious of buying this game, fearing it might fall short in comparison and would just make me want to play yet another hour of RW. But no, I was pleasantly surprised. In gameplay it feels familiar enough but the 3D world makes it an experience of its own.The 3D part in Stranded: Alien Dawn is really well made. I mean the game is beautiful and atmospheric. Besides, there just aren't enough games where the discovery of manure is the most important thing, and gives the player feeling of fulfillment! I hope they'll add human vs human combat. It's ok to fight the bugs, but it would be just awesome to have gunfights in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: We crash landed in an awful place and after much discussion, we decided to make a move towards a large shoreline.  It was difficult as everyone suffered some form of mental break while relocating.  We just barely got our first building up before winter hit which was a good thing because our clothing was in tatters.  Fortunately, Quinn was quite the intellectual and breezed through some planetary research, unlike Laara who was struck by lightening twice in the exact same spot....what are the odds.  unfortunately those two lightening strikes destroyed what little intelligence she had, but she still managed to plant a small plot of what she called buttermelon.  The local wildlife began to get just as desperate for food as we were and while Jack tried to kill them all, he took a gutshot from one of the horned buffalo like creatures and was carted off to his bunk.  Quinn had just managed to load an exploration balloon and decided the best course of action would be to explore and maybe come back with another survivor who might be able to help Jack as his situation had become quite dire.Laara decided she was going to hump it back to the old camp where she had left a few medpacks thinking she might make it in time to save Jack.  probably not the best decision as that first camp was a long hike that had driven more than one of the survivors a bit loony on the way.Meanwhile, Emilin stayed behind and made pancakes, thinking the best way to cure a man of anything is a good meal.  She might have been right as she was a fine cook.  in the meantime, Jack grew much worse developing a serious infection and it looked as though he had only a few hours.  As Emilin worried, Jack died.  ♥♥♥♥.  Well, she did what she felt the others would have done and prepared him a gravesite while stripping him of his gear.  Where the Hell were the others anyway!  Just then Laara stumbled in and saw that Jack had died and went berserk as the long hike had been too much.  Emilin offered her some fresh pancakes and this seemed to calm Laara down a bit, she was a fine cook afterall.Where the HELL was Quin!  Emilin checked the pantry and noticed the stores were low.  While there still were a good number of animals infesting the garden, eating everything in sight, she and Laara decided they should't risk getting gored.  that's when Laara said it.  "We should butcher Jack"  After all Emilin You are a fine cook, I think you could even make Jack taste great.  The decision was made and Emilin and Laara behan butchering Jack.  just......as........Quin.......returned.Jack had just burst in the door and said "I have them, I have the meds!"  As he ran into Jack's room, his eye's widened as he witnessed the horor before him.  "Holy Hell!"Once Quin calmed down, Emilin prepared a special stew that evening.  Everyone's spirits rose as they toasted over the stew.  Quin sat back and said quietly, "Emilin, you sure are a fine cook"5 Stars.

_childDocuments_.review: First impression after a few hours of play - it's (obviously) like Rimworld, only not as good in almost every aspect.Pros- It's a simplified and less difficult take on the DF/Rimworld genre. That will appeal to people.- Variety in the fauna and flora, and I like how they need to be observed before you can discern their full usagesNeutral- Graphics are okCons  - Ugly UI- Repetitive gameplay loop- Few emergent stories- Survivors lack personality in comparison to other games - Rubbish sound effects- nonsensical (gamey) technology barriers - why would you crash land on an alien planet yet forget how to construct buildings? - Far too derivative of other games in the genre. Struggle to see why you'd play this over Rimworld As for an overall verdict, it's closer than the above lists would suggest. Had I played less than two hours I probably would have refunded. However, I don't feel the same level of regret as I have done with other games with a similar number of cons. Despite its many issues, I have found myself wanting to play S:AD again. Perhaps, with more time, it will grow on me. So it's a no for now but it may change in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, fun, challenging colony sim, makes you really think about building placement and considering moving camp entirely, which is an interesting dynamic not usually present in these type of games that tend to encourage hunkering down in one place on the map. Careful management of your survivors is available to you without needing to manually tell them which tasks to do manually through a "priority" system. A con of this is that if you don't carefully manage them, they probably will prioritize themselves poorly and starve everyone to death. Would like the ability to create my own survivors similar to something like the Wasteland series, with a choice of perks and ability bonuses.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptionally enjoyable survival base builder, with three unique campaigns (in the base product) (and three unique biomes) that each have their own unique starting conditions and victory conditions, even if the overall gameplay tends to boil down to the same moment to moment activity.  It is generally a relaxing game that has enough challenge to keep one's focus but not so much difficulty that it becomes frustrating.The graphics are serviceable unless you really want to zoom in on characters or the environment, mostly being clear on what you're looking at (some small plants look very similar to one another), and there is a distinct look of all the given materials in the game.The 'give general order but allow autonomy' mostly works, with the characters going about the task that needs to be done, and while there is a system to readjust what priority each of their tasks are, the default system is generally workable if a bit uneven.  Characters might interrupt a task to do something else, like stop transporting an item to have a meal because they're hungry, but then won't resume the task; many items will be left lying around unless task priority is shifted considerably.Characters can be drafted, specifically for combat, but there is little finesse in this area, mainly it's best to gather all your people together and have them well equipped and then send them at a target; characters have to be manually controlled to fall back, most enemies don't have ranged attacks so they merely charge at you and cover is generally only buildable; I've not had a situation where I could get to a ridge that oversaw an area and then rained fire down on enemies who would have to take the long way around.The drafting doesn't allow for precise control of non-combat actions, which is a bit frustrating particularly when you have an item you want a survivor to observe (the means by which you learn about them for resource extraction), but that item might be very far from the base so you want to have them properly equipped and make sure they do THAT task and not try to retreat to base to relax, or sleep, or eat, or whatever.  I suspect this is to prevent the sense that one must micromanage your people for optimal outcomes, but there are fringe cases where it would be nice to have this option.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of other people, I was looking for a Rimworld-like colony sim in 3D and this certainly fits that description. It's much more streamlined and focuses on smaller groups of survivors, at the cost of some depth that you would have experienced playing Rimworld. Multi-floor building is quite cool and it makes the 3D part seem like it actually matters.I think there's still some room for improvements, for example I wish some resources were more granular (a sensor shouldn't cost the same number of CPUs as an automated turret imo) and that energy generation had more options (you are almost entirely dependent on renewables, fuel based sources don't really scale well in my experience).Overall an excellent entry into the colony building genre, and the game continues to be updated.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fantastically fun game (10/10), like a higher-res Rimworld but with fewer people to manage. The game isn't stingy with the amount of resources that you get per trip (e.g., chopping trees, mining rocks, etc.). Lots to do in a game but probably the best part is the construction. Lots of freedom in building houses or warehouses or combinations. The only thing I would like to see in this game is a bit more customization with the starting game and end game goals. I'd really like to have the option of playing after the end game goal has been reached. It'd be great to be able to play the crash landing scenario but have the option to do galactic trading. The modding community thankfully has that sort of thing covered. But what I'd really like to see is something like establishing other outposts on the same planet where you could transfer resources between outposts. So once you have one area functioning really well, you can recruit another team to establish a new base and set up a trade route between them.Really, a fun game well worth it. I really look forward to seeing how this game will develop in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Alien Dawn is a breath of fresh air in a gaming landscape that has felt somewhat stagnant in recent years. It’s a true 5-star gem, offering a unique blend of survival and strategy that stands out among its peers. _childDocuments_.review: :Finally, we're at the point, where I can say that  surpassed any other colony survival management simulation game Steam has to offer. With the latest free update (and DLC that comes with it) you finally can build multi-floor complexes. At this point  won't lose to any other game in terms of graphics, features, optimization and moddability. And in some cases, it even surpasses them. Moreover, some existing frameworks (such as detailed body status/information for humans and robots) imply that there are much more things to come.An extremely powerful modding toolkit is supplied along with the game, that allows to modify everything or even implement completely new features. Considering, that most of the logic is handled via LUA scripts, almost every part of the game is open for tinkering.And presence of Denuvo? Frankly, for all the attention, love and care game receives from the developers, the presence of thy Denuvo in thou game can be forgiveth.:I can tell with clear conscience that developer, Haemimont Games, lived up to expectations with release of modding toolkit. There are some bugs and issues to resolve, but main step towards infinite replayability is already done. By the way, all unpacking instructions for Surviving Mars are totally suitable for Stranded: Alien Dawn as well, thanks to both games using very similar engine.:Seems like developers (and publisher) decided to heed the voice of reason and add proper modding tools with Steam Workshop support. Hence, my decision to change my own review into positive one, because  deserves to be modded. When modding tools will get released (at 28 February, 2023), I will check modding capability of the game. And if it is as huge as Surviving Mars, then I will leave this positive review as it is. Else, I will review it again.:Denuvo? No modding (despite game being very modding friendly, because it uses same/similar engine as Surviving Mars). No modding? Don't bother to buy it. It will die out rather fast. _childDocuments_.review: AKTUALIZACE RECENZE: Hru jsem nakonec rozjel. Musel jsem ale nainstalovat externí program Intel extrem tuning utility a podtaktovat procesor. Další radou co jsem našel na fórech byla deaktivace E-jader, to jsem naštestí už dělat nemusel. Verdikt na hru neměním. Mám i9-13900K takže z mého pohledu relativně nový a výkonný hardware. Musím li tedy používat programy třetích stran, abych hru rozjel, nemohu ji s čistým svědomím doporučit ke koupi.ENG version translated with the help of GoogleREVIEW UPDATE: I finally got the game up and running. But I had to install the external program Intel extrem tuning utility and underclock the processor. Another piece of advice I found on the forums was deactivating E-cores, luckily I didn't have to do that anymore. I do not change the verdict on the game. I have an i9-13900K so from my point of view relatively new and powerful hardware. So if I have to use third-party programs to run the game, I can't in good conscience recommend it for purchase.Původní recenze:Hra samotná je v jádru zábavná, jedna se o jednoduší Rimworld s atraktivnější grafikou. Bohužel asi po odehrání 15h začala hra zamrzat, interval se začal postupně zkracovat na současných cca 10 minut hrací doby před zamrznutím a pádem na plochu. Řešení na fórů nepomáhala (vypnutí autosavu, snížení grafiky). Sledujte zda přijde aktualizace, která toto opraví.  Informace o zamrzání hry jsem našel na fóru už v říjnu minulého roku a problém je zde pořád. Takže občasným informacím od vývojářů, že problém řeší uvěřím až uvidím výsledky, pak i změním hodnocení. Do té doby zvažte nákup, chyba se začala projevovat daleko za hranicí času pro refundaci. Hra mě pře zamrzáním velmi bavila, ale v za mě tedy hru v současném stavu nedoporučuji.Original reviewENG version translated with the help of GoogleThe game itself is fun at its core, it's a simpler Rimworld with more attractive graphics. Unfortunately, after about 15 hours of play, the game began to freeze, the interval gradually began to shorten to the current approx. 10 minutes of playing time before freezing and crashing to the desktop. Solutions on the forums did not help (disabling autosave, reducing graphics). Watch for an update to fix this. I found information about the game freezing on the forum already in October of last year and the problem is still there. So I will believe the occasional information from the developers that they are solving the problem when I see the results, then I will change the rating. Until then, please consider purchasing, the bug started showing up well past the refund time limit. I really enjoyed the game despite the freeze. Therefore, I do not recommend the game in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. Some more work needs to be done, but it does indeed feel like a 3d Rimworld.As for some gems of other reviews:Denuvo? It's right there on the store page in a bright gold box! "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper" If you don't like this, don't but the game. Contact the developer and let them know why you aren't purchasing it. Or decline the EULA and refund it through Steam. If you explain why, support is generally really good about refunding for DRM that you don't agree with as long as you are under the 2 hour limit."Denuvo has been criticised for high central processing unit (CPU) usage and excessive writing operations on storage components, the latter causing significant life-span reductions for solid-state drive"No. I've played this and other recent Denuvo games on a nearly decade old CPU. Denuvo related processes don't use more than 2% of it. Any modern hardware isn't going to notice it (5800x for example). SSD wear? ((citation needed)). _childDocuments_.review: Ajánlom mindenkinek, aki szereti ezt a stílust, de...A játékban rengeteg apró hiba, "csukás" van még, amire lelkileg fel kell készülni.- A karakterek hajlamosak abszolút módon figyelmen kívül hagyni a napi beosztást, és addig dolgozni, amíg vagy össze nem esnek a fáradtságtól, vagy idegösszeomlást kapnak a stressztől.- A feladatok automatikus elvégzési sorrendje abszolút logikán túli. Lényegében az elvégzendő feladatok keletkezési sorrendjét követi akkor is, ha az azt jelenti, hogy 3-szor szeli át a teljes térképet oda-vissza a karakter/robot/szállító drón.- Az építkezés, épületek felépítési működése (statika, hozzáférhetőség, terhelhetőség) abszolút kretén módon áll össze. Egyáltalán semmi köze sincs a valósághoz, illetve a praktikumhoz. Példa: Egy asztal fal mellé lerakható, viszont ha ezen falrész ablakot is "tartalmaz", akkor már ez nem kivitelezhető.- Ha átépíteni/modernizálni szeretnél egy épületrészt/elemet, hát borzasztó nagy türelem és aprólékosság kell hozzá, mert az átépíteni kívánt rész kijelölésére nincs egyszerű "egy adott típusú elemet kijelölök" mód.Még messze nem volt módom minden aspektusát a játéknak kipróbálni. De nagyon kellemes és szórakoztató számomra. A grafika jó, a zene élvezhető, s bár egy idő után monotonná válik a játékmenet, de remélem a jövőbeli fejlesztésekkel ezt orvosolják majd a készítők.I recommend it to anyone who likes this style, but...There are still a lot of small errors and "loopholes" in the game, for which you have to be mentally prepared.- Characters tend to completely ignore the daily schedule and work until they either collapse from exhaustion or have a nervous breakdown from stress.- The automatic execution order of the tasks is beyond absolute logic. Essentially, it follows the order of creation of the tasks to be completed, even if it means going back and forth across the entire map 3 times on the character/robot/transport drone.- Construction, the construction of buildings (statics, accessibility, load capacity) is put together in an absolutely cretinous way. It has absolutely nothing to do with reality or practicality. Example: A table can be placed next to a wall, but if this part of the wall also "contains" a window, then this is no longer feasible.- If you want to rebuild/modernize a part of a building/element, you need an awful lot of patience and meticulousness, because there is no simple "I select a specific type of element" way to select the part you want to rebuild.I haven't had a chance to try every aspect of the game yet. But it's very pleasant and fun for me. The graphics are good, the music is enjoyable, and although the gameplay becomes monotonous after a while, I hope the creators will fix this with future developments.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn - A Thriving Oasis on a Harsh WorldStranded: Alien Dawn, Haemimont Games' colony sim on an alien planet, is a thrilling blend of base-building, resource management, and survival against a vibrant, deadly world. As the leader of a group of survivors stranded after a crash, you'll face the unforgiving elements, alien predators, and your own colonists' anxieties as you struggle to establish a foothold and unlock the mysteries of this strange new home.Strengths:Captivating Planet: The procedurally generated world is rich with diverse biomes, each teeming with its own flora and fauna. From lush jungles to scorching deserts and crystalline caves, exploration feels constantly rewarding, uncovering new resources, hazards, and lore snippets.Intricate Survival Mechanics: Hunger, thirst, disease, and even mental well-being play a crucial role. Every decision - from building priorities to resource allocation - feels impactful, forcing you to carefully balance short-term needs with long-term prosperity.Character-Driven Gameplay: Each survivor has unique skills, personalities, and relationships, creating a dynamic society within your base. Managing their moods, assigning tasks, and utilizing their strengths feels deeply satisfying, fostering an emotional connection to your colony's well-being.Evolving Research Tree: Unlocking new technologies opens up gameplay possibilities, from advanced farming techniques to powerful defenses against the planet's threats. The sense of progression and constant improvement is addictive, driving you forward through challenges.Engaging Story and Lore: The narrative unfolds through environmental storytelling, research fragments, and survivor interactions. Unraveling the secrets of the planet, its former inhabitants, and the cause of your crash keeps you invested and fuels the desire to explore further.Weaknesses:Steep Learning Curve: The game throws a lot at you early on, with complex systems and menus. Newcomers might feel overwhelmed by the multitude of mechanics and resource management intricacies.Combat Can Be Clunky: While tense and strategic, combat can feel clunky at times, with pathfinding issues and imprecise aiming mechanics occasionally frustrating.Late-Game Content: After establishing a thriving colony, the late-game can feel repetitive, lacking clear goals and new challenges to overcome.Overall:Stranded: Alien Dawn is a deeply rewarding colony sim that thrives on its intricate mechanics, diverse world, and compelling survival narrative. Despite its learning curve and occasional combat limitations, the constant struggle against nature, the evolving society within your base, and the urge to unravel the planet's secrets keep you hooked for hours on end. If you're looking for a challenging and immersive experience that blends survival with base-building and captivating exploration, Stranded: Alien Dawn is a must-play.Verdict: 4.5 out of 5 stars - A stunning survival sim with captivating world-building, deep mechanics, and a thriving colony to nurture. Be prepared for a steep learning curve and some late-game repetition, but the overall experience is richly rewarding and unforgettable.Bonus Tip: Don't be afraid to experiment with different survivor roles and specialization. Their unique skills and needs can unlock creative solutions to tough challenges. Also, prioritize research and exploration; knowledge is your key to survival and success on this alien world.I hope this review helps you decide whether Stranded: Alien Dawn is the right game for you. Happy surviving!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought on impulse and was pleasantly surprised. At the time I'm writing this (Oct 2022), the game is in Early Access, but despite this, it runs stable and plays well.Graphics are nice, they don't stand out, they don't distract, there's enough details to be worth zooming in and having a look. Perhaps most surprising is the stable performance, whether I play at 2k or 4k, I get to enjoy a stable 60fps.I was skeptical if I was going to like the premade characters, but ultimately I do like them. I find it very pleasurable to watch my survivors hustle and bustle, doing their chores and tasks. Sometimes the survivors priorities seem a bit off, and can require some micro-management. But this also helps build stories. Like when Katina almost let Hann bleed out after he rescued Rita from a swarm of bugs, because getting some sleep was more important. Or that time Rakha regularly got frustrated by having to do all the construction and kept going off to punch a pole or going off for shooting practice. And speaking of stories, when your outpost fails because your survivors died, you'll get a timeline with important moments, a really nice touch I enjoy.At the time of review, content overall is limited, but what's available is great. Clearly the team went for quality over quantity, and hopefully there will be more tech, more research, more ... well more of everything. The biggest downside to this approach, for the time being, after one solid successful playthrough you've basically seen everything there is. There are some randomized research options and expeditions events that change based on a random seed, but it's really nothing major.The gameplay is built with a focus on reaching the victory condition, and some mechanics are scaled around that, making an endless play somewhat difficult but not impossible. Though it's possible that this too will see some change, being in Early Access.The developers have also blessed the community with a great community manager, who's actively working on gathering feedback and communicating very respectfully with the community.In summary a great start and so much potential!

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Alien Dawn is your typical early access colony manager, it has the minimum amount of features and a twist where there is an "end" where you build up and then build down to have your people escape one by one. It isn't finished, so if you are not a fan of "Early access" just wait for it to come out. It is on the right track and not feature complete.The good:The build system is pretty good. Looks like the one from the Planet Coaster, Planet Zoo etc which is pretty good. The mechanic of "building down" at the end is pretty cool. It isn't done yet, there needs to be more automation in place, but it is a new twist to your typical build up.The bad:Not very replayable. The characaters are static, and the maps are not procedural. A single playthrough should do it for you.The map is kinda too big. There is no way you'll use it all.Scale is small, you never really get more than 10 survivors. Game isn't "done" yet. but it is on the right track.The ugly:Nothing really. It is a pretty good game with a good future.If you are interested in the game, but haven't played Rimworld or Going Medieval I would recommend playing those first, they are better games (at the time of this review) but this game has future potential and is a pretty good game. I would just recommend Rimworld or Going Medieval over this one at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, some simple questions that will quickly answer if this game is for you:If you , then this is not for you. Go watch the show, it's really good!If you  then this game might just be for you! With a few caveats...What  does well is present the Abyss itself as the true antagonist. It's going to get you killed, a number of times, and often in quite unfair ways, but since you've seen the show (unless you were lying when you answered my questions), you already know that!The game somewhat requires that you take a trip through an extended tutorial and recap of the start of the first season of the show, seeing Riko and Reg trek it all the way down to the edge of the second layer, just past Seeker Camp. This part of the game is quite slow, and it removes some of the more interesting mechanics that the proper game provides.Honestly, I was almost giving up on the game at first. The roughly 4 hours I spent going through the tutorial was somewhat painful. When I realised that there was no point to painstakingly collecting a lot of the things the game tells you that you CAN collect, I ended up running through a lot of the environments, opting to save them for when the real game got started. This was a wise choice! Because, oh wow, there's a lot to explore, find and collect in the game proper.Jumping over to , the  part of the game, things immediately become a lot more interesting. You start things off as a young cave raider with a grand goal in mind: Become a White Whistle and reach the bottom of the Netherworld! Sound familiar? Of course it does, you are essentially a stand-in for Riko, and your journey through the Abyss very closely matches the journey in the   and  of the show, ultimately ending at .On your way, the game presents an original story that the author of the manga was deeply involved with, making it by and large canon (with a bit of creative freedom in some regards). It kept me motivated to keep going, as I absolutely adore this world and its strange inhabitants, but the real meat of the package is of course the world itself.The Abyss is a huge, sprawling network of caverns and vistas, streams and waterfalls, settlements and wastelands, all spread out across a number of layers. Descending down is captivating. Ascending is always treacherous and sometimes literally lethal due to the curse. The deeper you go, the worse it gets. This draw, the mystery of the depths and the perils of returning from them, is truly captivating.Gameplay wise the loop consists of venturing out from Orth, the surface town built around the edge of the Abyss, and collecting artefacts to bring back. You complete quests along the way, and combined with the artefacts that you return (or make equipment out of), you slowly level up. At certain story points, you will be able to upgrade the level of your whistle, the badge of designation carried by every cave raider. The higher the level, the deeper you can go. It also comes with the benefit of making the strains caused by the curse of the abyss easier to bear, as well as unlocking the ability to fast travel in deeper and deeper parts of the Abyss. A daunting trek back from a deep layer suddenly becomes a piece of cake once you are experienced enough.Visually, the game sports a very stylized design, very closely matching the look of the anime. Characters are rendered very close to their 2D counterparts and all feature the original voice actors from the show, at least in Japanese. The beasts you encounter and the many different foods you consume over your travels are both also rendered with extreme attention to detail to the canon of the show. There are even some new environments spread through the layers you can explore, adding even more depth (pun intended) to the Abyss.Ultimately, this game is a true love letter to the show and its universe, and while the task can be somewhat daunting with a slow start and a pretty harsh difficulty spike when going deeper the first few times, I can only recommend it wholeheartedly to anyone who is a fan of the series. It’s not perfect, but the good parts by far outweigh the bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend this game ONLY if you're a fan of the manga or anime. But wait for it to go on sale. If you don't know what Made In Abyss is, don't bother. There's quite a few REALLY annoying problems with this game right now and hopefully they'll get patched. One of the most confusing decisions by the dev was to lock the full game behind an approximately 3 hour tutorial story that is an abridged version of the first season of the Anime. Which would be FINE except it's executed in such a hamfisted way. Reg, your companion in the Tutorial, has some of the worst AI I've ever seen. He constantly gets stuck, aggros everything and dies, has only one dialog line which he repeats every few seconds for no apparent reason and, in one quest that involves the need to analyze specific enemies to complete, Reg seemed to be hell bent on killing the enemies before I could complete the process. During the tutorial, much of the game's meat and depth is either locked off from you or not explained very well. I was 3/4 of the way through the last mission before I figured out one of the ONLY things you can craft during this portion is food, something that would have made the previous 3/4 of the game much easier. You could spend hours wandering around in the Tutorial collecting relics and crafting components, but the game doesn't tell you this is all useless and wasted time. The goal of the tutorial is to just get through the story and with the exception of some basic food, you can't use any of it. Once you complete the tutorial / anime rehash, the game does expand a great deal. There's a few skill trees for crafting, fighting and cave raiding. You're free to explore wherever you want and do whatever you want. This is all fine but you're going to get annoyed real quick with a couple horrendous problems. The worst is some of the most frustrating enemy spawning I've ever encountered. They spawn wherever you're not looking. 3 squirrel looking things? Kill them and they immediately re spawn behind or beside you just out of view. This also happens when you're climbing, which is incredibly problematic because you use stamina to climb, and also to swing your weapon. So continuously spawning enemies are kind of a game breaker since you either have to take damage or use stamina to fend them off and probably fall because you run out of stamina.  This is also incredibly bad because attacking enemies contributes to your weapon degrading and breaking. You can burn through one very quickly fending off non stop spawning enemies and find yourself defenseless after you run out of crafting materials. EDIT: Now that I'm more than half way through the game's main campaign, I can add a bit more. The rapid spawn mechanic is apparently by choice. After you spend too long in an area, low HP enemies spawn rapidly to push you along. There's apparently an item that temporarily pauses this mechanic, but it's still an odd choice given how much the game wants you to take your time and explore.  What the Deep In Abyss mode does get right is the sense of danger and careful planning it takes to successfully dive and make it back. Your inventory is extremely limited if you stock up on survival items and doesn't leave room for valuable relics to earn money and experience when taken back to town. But you need food and weapons, not to mention your clothing which takes up a significant portion of your available inventory. Weapon degradation is a real problem if you go around attacking everything you see. So the game pushes you to avoid conflict in this manner and encourages you to pick and choose your battles.  The more weapons you take to compensate for the degradation and breaking, the less room you have for other stuff. The Deep In Abyss mode has incredible potential. The sense of depth and scale translates very well to the real danger the Abyss presents. If you go down to layers 3 or deeper, it's a huge commitment to return with the valuable relics you can find. There's no shortage of exploration and secrets to find. The crafting system is just deep enough to make it challenging without being too complex.  Unlocking new parts of the skill trees gives you access to things that make delving easier and less time consuming in the upper layers. The environments are unique in each layer, which is nice. But the graphics don't get any better the deeper you go. There's just enough to convey the terrain and that's about it. I still stand by the reccomendation ONLY if you're a fan of the series. It's worth the playthrough to explore the Abyss yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: is not the game that an amazing series like  deserves. It's janky, buggy, unpolished, and frustrating in several ways. That said, it's the only  game we have for now, and for those of us who have already watched the anime and read the manga, it's the only other official content to tide us over until the next volumes and seasons come out, which could be years from now. And despite the jank, it's not a terrible game--there are some things I really like about it. But still, I struggled with whether or not to recommend the game, and ultimately decide that I can recommend it, but per the previous disclaimer, only to huge fans of the series who can wait for a sale and tamper their expectations.The game is split into two parts, "Hello Abyss," which is basically a tutorial that recaps the first half of season 1 (), and "Deep in Abyss" in which you create your own cave raider and work your way up from being a lowly bell rank to a legendary White Whistle. Hello Abyss can be finished in about three to four hours, but it's barely worth playing unless you want the achievements. It's missing a lot of the mechanics that make the rest of the game interesting, and the retelling of Riko and Reg's story is abysmal. It doesn't do the anime or the manga justice at all. While they did at least get the same voice actors from the anime, the developers didn't license any of the animation or music from the series, except for a few intro scenes. Instead, they rely on poorly animated in-engine cutscenes that lack any of the emotional impact of the anime. I think this entire section of the game was outsourced to another studio, and it really shows in the lack of quality throughout. Deep in Abyss is much better, and it has kept me hooked on the game for 40+ hours despite all of its faults. In this mode, you do the actual work of a cave raider: preparing for your trip, delving into the abyss, collecting as many relics and other materials as you can carry, and trying to make it back to the surface alive while surviving the threat posed by primeval creatures and the curse of the abyss. I found this gameplay loop quite addictive, and though it does get repetitive--especially towards the end of the game where leveling and crafting become very grindy--it always feels like there's more to discover, and the story of your OC cave raider's progress is intriguing enough to maintain interest, though by no means excellent.The effects of the curse/strains of ascension are mostly well done. The first and second layers cause only minor inconveniences. But in the third layer, . The fifth layer effect is a bit disappointing: it should have been more like how it's depicted in  where it , but instead it just .Other reviewers have described  as being a difficult game, but I think this is not quite accurate. It's not hard, per se, but it can be very . It's possible to get stuck which can cause you to lose hours of progress. You can delve too deep and end up not having the resources to get back. You can also follow a path downward only to later realize that there's no way back up that path if you didn't put a rope out beforehand. In most cases, there is an alternate route available somewhere, but finding it can be easier said than done.Make sure you save frequently and keep multiple different saves at different points! It's good to keep rotating saves so you always have the option to go back to a "safe" spot.Also limiting the difficulty is that enemy AI is practically non-existent. Contrary to how the primeval creatures of the deep abyss are portrayed as vicious and cunning in the anime and manga, enemies in the game mostly just stand in place and rotate around, casting attacks at random. Most of them will also leash if you get more than a few meters away, which means you can always just run past them (and usually should do so to conserve resources). The most dangerous and annoying enemies are the flying and climbing ones that harass you while you're trying to scale cliffs; the  are especially aggravating. Exacerbating this is the fact that most enemies respawn constantly without end. Apparently, there's a mod to disable that; I can completely understand why many players would want such a mod.There are a handful of forced fights in the game, including boss fights with  at the bottom of each layer. These fights are generally not hard either, but they can be aggravating due to resource management: if your weapons break and you don't have the materials to craft new ones, you can't fight back at all. Your only option at that point is to reload your previous save.There are several noteworthy bugs in the game. For example, you can exploit the stamina mechanic when climbing by standing on top of (most) relic nodes that jut out from walls. You can also exploit it when descending by dropping off the wall (neutral jump instead of downwards jump) and grabbing back on, which uses no stamina. Sometimes you can fall off a wall from a height that should be deadly, but inexplicably take no damage. If you excavate while on a wall and end up with too much weight, you'll fall off, but if you're quick enough, you can pause, discard some items, and you'll be able to grab back onto the wall before you fall to your death. I doubt any of these things were intentional.Weapons break far too easily, perhaps even easier than those in . Durability systems in games are often irritating, but I don't mind them so much when they suit the gameplay and the experience the game is trying to evoke, which is certainly the case with ' theme of survival in a hostile environment. But a 2kg metal pickaxe shouldn't shatter into pieces after whacking half a dozen rodents. Strangely, excavating relics and resources doesn't reduce your pickaxe's durability, and in fact you can even excavate without a pickaxe in your inventory at all.The role that relics play in the game is disappointing. They're effectively just glorified vendor trash and crafting materials. I do like that selling relics is one of the primary means of leveling up, given that that's what cave raiders are known for. But there should have been at least some relics with real gameplay effects (sun spheres don't count.) I was excited to finally unlock , but even these don't have any unique animations or effects. This feels like a major missed opportunity. It also could have helped explain why . is not a bad game, but it's certainly not great either. And that's a shame, because  is excellent, and the game could have been too with more care and attention to detail, and perhaps a larger budget. The core game is solid enough that I enjoyed my time with it. But I still wouldn't recommend it to anyone who isn't already a big fan of . I really hope that one day the franchise gets the high quality game it deserves.This was abridged due to Steam's character limit. Full review here:

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the deal...It has potential. The game is good if you grab the spawnrate-fix mod from . If it's on sale, it's a steal. It could be so much better with more work, and there's a ton of cut content that didn't make it to release.I've heard that the devs aren't looking at any future contributions to the game -- likely aside from bugfixes. Hopefully this isn't true, or at least the devs change their mind. Aside from that, the intro questline can't be skipped but it takes maybe ~2-3 hours if you cruise through it. No resources will carry over, so just blast your way through to get to the real meat and potatoes of the game.The custom-player mode is where the good stuff is at. Some advice and tips:-Main quest progression gates available depth (and occasionally adds some larger primeval creatures to the maps), so prioritize the main quests first.-Stamina is incredibly important while going up walls, so don't be afraid to rest on the rocks sticking out. You don't want to see your character get turned into goop after a fall.-Going up via the waypoints takes HP and Hunger, going down usually just takes Hunger. Eventually you'll unlock fast travel to take you down to the newest depth, which is much more efficient time and resource-wise, and back to Orth.-Packweight is the most limiting factor of the gameplay-cycle. Free up some weight at the itembox in your room by dumping items you don't need. You'll always be gathering more of whatever you already had. Just some food, medicine, and your tools is the ideal pack.-Armor is far and away the best thing to work towards. Always make that your primary goal; the quests can wait.-Rope isn't as valuable a resource as you might think, but it doesn't hurt to have. You can always make more.I've been loving my time with this game so far, hopefully others can look past its flaws and see the beauty underneath.

_childDocuments_.review: Made in Abyss is a fantastic anime, one of my recent favorites. So I was pleasantly surprised to see this pop up on Steam, the series has the potential for a fun video game.Given the atrocity that was the Re:ZERO game developed by the same studio, I expected just another straightforward VN-adventure hybrid. Binary Star is much more than that though. There are still VN segments, but the gameplay takes priority here and there is a full slate of stuff to play around with.Crafting food and equipment, using various tools to get around, taking in the many different areas of the Abyss, unlocking abilities on the skill tree, hunting down artifacts - it is a much higher-end production than I was anticipating and the studio has done a great job building a solid foundation.Unfortunately though, that is just the foundation, because the game takes a massive dive in quality once you get to how the actual loop works. Instead of evoking that feeling of exploration and wonder that one would expect to come with diving into the Abyss, the overall feeling I had was one of monotony. This is because the vast majority of quests are simple fetch quests, “go here and kill this” quests, or “go here, talk to this person, and come back” quests.You would think, “okay, but these fetch quests give you an opportunity to explore the Abyss” and yeah, you would be partially right. The problem there though is that once you’ve seen an area a few times, it becomes a bit boring to head back there for the fifth, sixth time to do something menial like collecting five bird eggs or fishing for material to craft a certain dish.This becomes especially annoying later on when you have to trek through like four or five different areas just to get to your objective only to have to trek all the way back at the end. I quickly realized I was spending roughly 90% of my time just getting to where I needed to be and that most of that time was spent trekking through the same areas that I had already crossed through in the previous five quests. This is the bulk of the Binary Star experience and it is a massive disappointment given the great base that the game starts with.Little things add to this disappointment too. Item weight, limited backpack size, equipment durability, and the fact that if you run out of stamina your character literally stops in place until the stamina bar regens to full. Sure, there’s an excuse for realism to be made there, but this is an anime game and a lot of these mechanics are blatantly anti-fun.The combat is the most dead simple thing ever, with your one button attacks that only expand beyond that with the skill tree that just makes the combo string longer. The lock-on is a bit finicky, the hitboxes are usually way larger than they appear, and most fights boil down to simply hitting an enemy a couple times, rolling to the side, and repeating.The game is basically divided into two parts: “Hello Abyss” and “Deep In Abyss”. The former is the “proper” story mode that tells the story from the anime and allows you to play as Riko and Reg. That said, the entire thing only adapts up to the survival training with Ozen - episode eight from the first season - and it took me just three hours to clear. I found this mode to be a vastly inferior method of telling the Made in Abyss story for what it does adapt.After completing that mode though, you unlock the full experience: Deep in Abyss - or the game mode that most of my earlier complaints come from. This mode allows you to create a custom character and tells an original story with said character. Sounds cool, but the story itself is just there to link things together and isn’t really a strong point. The rest of it is as I described earlier.The graphics are what I would expect from an early PS4 or even PS3 game, with bland textures and boring world design. The music is a bit better, but honestly nothing can compare to Kevin Penkin’s work in the anime and I guess I’m just disappointed that we couldn’t get something that at least tries to be that good.I ran the game at 4k 144fps, max settings on my RTX 3080 Ti with no performance-related issues. That said, there are some bugs worth mentioning, including voice playback randomly stopping after alt+tabbing and NPCs getting stuck in the terrain when moving. That latter one happened A LOT and it comes with an equally annoying sound effect of someone rapidly hitting the ground.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is a decent game bogged down by some incredibly tedious quest design. Exploring the Abyss can be fun, but not when you have to do so dozens of times in the same areas just to complete simple fetch quests. It’s a shame, because the studio did a fairly good job building up a solid foundation. It’s just that they didn’t know what to do with said foundation and we get a filler-stuffed experience as a result. Maybe one day we’ll get something to build on this base, but for now, Binary Star is unfortunately an easy pass.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!
