_childDocuments_.review: Okay hear me out..I genuinely understand the negative points people are bringing up. HOWEVER, despite all of this i think it is a game absolutely worth checking out. Especially if you love Made In Abyss. - The general gameplay is very nice. It's your typical exploration, survival, crafting esque game and it's so much fun to explore!- The custom story (story where you create your own character and become a cave raider) even has it's own storyline and you get to see the characters everyone came to love from the show.- The visuals are actually pretty neat. From the models to the surroundings it all works really well together.- So much exploration potential!! You can just run around for funsies and bonk whatever creature comes across your path. Though some might eat you instead. You have a weight limit to your inventory (which can be upgraded) which forces you to run back home and go at it in a new run (aka. this isn't just a 2 hour game, you can spend alot of time on side quests and just explore for fun).- Learning about the creatures is hella fun. You can analyze each creature you come across and learn more about it in a journal you keep with you.- Whack control layout. That is completely true for the keyboard control. I genuinely don't understand how they came up with these settings  the good thing is that you can easily just change the keybinding and set them to whatever suits you most. Playing with a controller is a bit more comfortable though a few buttons are still questionable but then again you can still change the keybindings.- Not worth the money. I have to kinda agree on this one. I paid 60 Euro and was a bit bummed after playing for a bit because i thought that i wasted my money on barely anything fun to play.  i think alot of people haven't played too far into the custom story, got bummed out that Riko and Regs gameplay was so short, or just didn't quite expect what game they got themself into and it turned out to be a  game they don't necessarily enjoy.- Janky, Buggy, Unpolished. That is true. There's a few lil things here and there that just don't function like they probably were intended to. But it happens to the best games out there.- Creature spawn is insane. That is true as well! In certain areas you will literally be swarmed by creatures trying to attack you, even if you just stand around trying to eat something or heal yourself. There have been a few times where i got frustrated because i kept falling to my death because a moth touched my arm. If you make use of your Mail Balloons though you will be fine and it will be less frustrating.- Too Slow? I guess if you like fast paced games this is not for you. The beginning is pretty slow, having just become a red whistle you will be forced to simply struggle along and run back home after getting a scratch on your knee. But that changes as soon as you start going to the 2nd and 3rd layer.- Side characters talk TOO MUCH..... that was something i struggled personally. Whenever you have a mission that requires someone to join you on your journey into the Abyss, they will talk to you. All. The. Time. Whenever you pick something up they throw 3 sentences at you in a row.. I want to pick my flowers in peace leave me alone please.If you like exploring an unknown world, learn about it's creatures, survival + crafting, and have a little bit of patience? I think this game is worth checking out. If you're unsure about it's pricing.. wait for a discount :)8/10 recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that has all the elements in place to be great- a large world to explore, crafting, survival, talent trees, quests/side-quests, and best of all, being placed in the world of Made in Abyss.Sadly, the execution fails, and the game is marred by terrible design decisions. I don't know if there was zero play testing, if people were afraid to give feedback during development, or if leads were too arrogant to listen to that feedback. It's unfortunate, because it's not a case of needing more budget. They could have played the game for five minutes and seen how the game's systems get in the way of enjoying the game.It's a grouping of several small issues that on their own can easily be overlooked, but combined make gameplay truly tedious. Like companions repeating the same two lines every 3 seconds (no joke, you dont get more than a couple of seconds of silence at best before they repeat the same lines on a loop). The ability to place 99 custom map markers, but will disappear once you go to town (lol, seriously, why?). Enemies that respawn a second or two after killing them, combined with low weapon durability and limited inventory space. Slightly different from the last point, flying enemies that spawn infinitely around you when you've been in an area for ~5 minutes (again, combined with durability and inventory space make this quite tedious). Apparently this was actually patched a few months ago, I can't even imagine what it was like before.As can be expected, maps are quite vertical, meaning you have to deal with the curse every few seconds. Combine this with the plentiful climbing, where every 5 seconds of climbing you have to pause for ~7 seconds so the curse can fade. Now add in the infinitely spawning flying enemies swarming you while climbing, your weapon durability, and the limited stamina.Those who know the story upon which this game is based, know that this world is brutal. I expected difficult and unforgiving gameplay. Instead, the game is actually really simple, the only difficulty comes from the tedium of these mechanics and the jankiness of the game. I feel like I'm not fighting the creatures inhabiting the world, nor the Abyss - instead I'm fighting the developers and the game itself. It completely breaks immersion and it's such a shame.When I saw Spike Chunsoft made this game, I was both excited and fearful. Some of my favorite games are by these folks, but from my experience, action games are not their forte. I knew what I was getting into, I knew this wasn't going to be triple A, and quality would not be high. But it didn't need to be for this game to be a success.I will continue to play in the hopes that the game gets better, because ultimately I still love the world the game is based on, and I'll update if things change. However, at this moment, the feeling I get from this game is disappointment in such wasted potential, especially because a lot of these issues could have been fixed so easily, and should have been identified immediately within just a few minutes of playtesting.One last note: If you decide to pick up this game, I would seriously recommend skipping "Hello Abyss". It's not a difficulty setting, and despite what people say, it's not a tutorial either. It's a barebones version of the game that offers a highly watered down version of the first few episodes of the anime, and where basically none of the systems are in place. You will be punished for exploring, and for looting pretty much anything you find. You will likely spend a huge chunk of your time managing your inventory and deciding what to throw away. Reaching the Seeker Camp made me want to cry from how sad one of the fights was, and the cutscenes did not do the story justice. I was ready to uninstall after completing that, and thankfully I decided to give the main game a try (and if after this rant of a review I'm still thinking that the main game is a drastic improvement over Hello Abyss, just think what that says about Hello Abyss).

_childDocuments_.review: Middling recommendation, with several CAVEats. (Ha!)If you've seen the show, and thought the world and especially the Abyss were fascinating, there's a lot to like here, albeit mixed in with a whole lot of budget problems and sometimes weird fanservice. Note: I didn't really care about rehashing RIko and Reg's journey in a slightly worse way, so I only played the other game mode. It's got a number of tonal issues whenever you're talking to anyone, is my main critique. Riko, the incompetent and frankly insane loser who technically flunked out of orphan school for committing suicide, is now some sort of weirdly legendary character. Everyone assumes you've heard of this amazing person and her incredible exploits, despite her being... pretty much a nobody in the anime. And often it feels like people don't take the dangers of the abyss seriously at all, even when they're supposed to be professional cave raiders. Even Riko knew it was dangerous in the anime, she just didn't care. But you'll see even black whistles be totally nonchalant about everything.There are also bloody stumps of cut features all over the place - for instance, a lot of characters will, after completing a specific quest for them, have some dialogue in the vein of "Give me a call if you ever want me to join you on an expedition!" It's pretty obvious a lot of planned features were designed around and then awkwardly torn out. The whole game feels buggy and unfinished, in an old-school Obsidian kinda way. My favorite bug is when you kill a boss with a weapon, the weapon breaks, regardless of its durability level, including relic weapons. Thanks QA! (I'm joking, I know they didn't have the budget for a QA department)The game requires a mod to be enjoyable - play it for a bit until you see what I mean, then go get the "disable constant enemy spawning" mod. Otherwise you can never stop and look around, which is... weird in a game that you're mostly playing for the scenery.With all of those out of the way... Yes, I really like this game. For all of its flaws, as an exploration/survival game, it's fantastic. I've never seen a game where a weight limit was as harsh or as necessary, because what you don't necessarily realize going in is that this is not an action game, or an adventure game. It's a hiking sim with mountain-climbing elements. I'd say 90% of your time will be spent either slowly trundling into some increasingly dangerous place with your comically oversized backpack OR climbing a rock face (the remaining 10% of your time is spent managing your inventory). You aren't an action hero, and while combat is often necessary, you are MUCH better off running away or otherwise avoiding fights most of the time. Your weapon won't survive more than a few swings, and weapons, especially GOOD weapons, are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HEAVY. You can only carry a few, unless that's the ONLY thing you bring with you. In many ways it forces you to think carefully, consider the dangers of a course of action, and treat things with a lot more gravity. Especially gravity, because boy will gravity kill you a lot. And I love that slow, careful exploration. It's where the game truly shines. It's not perfect, there's a number of things I'd change and places where it's held back by various concessions (mostly to budget, occasionally to accessibility, annoyingly frequently to tone-deaf fan service). But I can't think of a single game like it, really. So, if you are...1. A fan of the show,2. A fan of slow-paced, grounded, careful survival/exploration,3. Willing to overlook bugs (as well as insects) and a blatantly incomplete game,then I would give it a somewhat muted recommendation. I like this game a lot. I don't think it's  good, but it does certain things uniquely well, and those things are pretty great if you like them. Pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game.  It's imperative that I inform you that you should only be buying this game on sale if you value your quality/$ metrics.  That said, it should at most be worth $30 if you don't want to feel robbed.  The 60 hours I am shown to have put in was the time I spent completing the game, so there is quite a bit to do if you also factor time into your tolerance for pricing.You should also know that "Hello Abyss", the first segment of the game, makes up well less than 10% of the time you will spend to finish the game.  Don't over-invest yourself in playing "Hello Abyss", because "Deep in Abyss" is what your money has been spent for.  At this point, the game thankfully no longer demands you to unlock "Deep in Abyss" by playing "Hello Abyss" first as many initial players had to deal with.  If you want to determine whether or not to refund, "Hello Abyss" is a red herring mode that will inappropriately represent what the game will be like, and it may take long enough to time you out of the refund period; play "Deep in Abyss" from the get-go instead if you listen to this and are still unsure if you'll like the game.Deep in Abyss is a delving simulator based on the world of Made in Abyss.  Yeah, I said SIMULATOR.  Don't expect fun, streamlined action and adventure all the time.  The game is amazing at delivering an experience of the day-in-day-out delving job where you brave the wild and seek out relics to sell back in Orth.  The journey down will be a chore, and so will the journey back... at least until you start getting promoted and can fast travel amidst layers.You will manage hunger, stamina, weapon durability, cargo weight, and the curse of ascension traversing the Abyss.  You will make judgments about fighting or avoiding creatures.  You will plan out items to bring with you and seek resources and/or food ingredients to pick up and craft/cook with on-site to facilitate your excursions (if the show/manga didn't make it clear that eating is an essential aspect of survival, the game will force-feed you the wisdom one way or another).  You will revisit some areas multiple times, especially if you have charted it as an optimal route to where you need to go next.It will feel like a slog at times, and that's probably what actual delvers in the world would feel; dare I say, that could be considered immersion of its own kind.  If you value the idea of eating some humble pie and immersing yourself with that sensation, Deep in Abyss shares a bit with old-style Monster Hunter games (note: the versions BEFORE World and Rise) in how you can identify as and take pride in being a successful delver through the act of careful preparation and work applied using what you've learned through experience.I didn't care so much about the jank of the controls (arguably appropriate to approximate a delver's struggles in the Abyss, but I cannot anticipate whether or not you will be frustrated), the general graphical quality, or such.  Even the parts of the game that others despise (constant butterflies and birds for daring to climb, the third layer, etc.) I considered part of the trial of triumphing over the game, and everything is achievable.  I did like the ambient intensity of the music (I didn't expect electric guitar bits, but they worked where applied), though Kevin Penkin's work might have added a bit of beauty to the setting.  All that said, I found the value of the game was in the experience of operating as a mortal delver and the journey of improvement and progress until I obtained my white whistle.  I enjoy struggles like that.The game terminates at the end of the 5th layer.  One can hope that a future release of an MiA game will elaborate upon the qualities of the game, objectively improve graphics and interactions, and add in more dangerous trials in the 6th layer... perhaps even the 7th layer (if it takes THAT long), but I was quite satisfied with this much.  I might even start a new playthrough sometime, but, for now, I recommend the game for the MiA fan who already knows the story and wants to see how they'd fare in the Abyss.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, when I heard that Made in Abyss was getting a game I was extremely excited. Thinking about the world and themes of Made in Abyss, I couldnt help but feel it could be turned into an awesome game. The unique monster design, the many environments of the abyss itself, and the lingering threat of the Curse of the Abyss seemed like it would lend itself to a one of a kind gaming experience. I didnt even want much of a story, just for the devs to let me live in that awesome world for a while. But WOW, this game has dropped the ball in a big way. First off is graphics and performance. The game is not pretty, it is good PS2 to bad PS3 graphics at best and the performance is meh. Anime and JRPGs in general dont tend to be the prettiest (final fantasy excluded), but with a unique design that is crisp they can shine (Persona). Unfortunately they did not manage that here, with the models often being fuzzy and so little effort made that the dialogue wasnt even synced to the lips in some places(like not even an attempt, just a gaping unmoving maw). Its not particularly ugly, but with the pricing we should expect better.Gameplay, the core of any game. This was particularly what excited me about a Made in Abyss adaptation, there was so many unique mechanics to utilize. However, what was implemented is frankly trash. Movement is slow, bulky, and your stamina drains in about 5 seconds. I'm sorry, but you play as a kid right? Right? Why on gods green earth can they not run for more than a few feet without having to catch their breath like a 75 year old chain smoker? Oh and by the way if you let your stamina empty you have to stand still catching your breath while monsters maul you or push you off a cliff for an instant kill. Fighting in the game is slow and bulky, you are super weak, and there isnt really unique loot for killing monsters. Honestly I dont even know why they bothered to make a fighting mechanic at all? You. are. a. small. child. The entire show and manga is them scurrying around hiding. The only times they really successfully kill anything is via Regs Incinerator, a fancy tool, or using a trap. It would have been far better to make the monsters actually scary(Which honestly I dont know how they made them not scary, they are horrifying in the books and show) and improve the movement and sneaking. Instead, the monsters behave like dynasty warrior mobs that just keep spawning and slowly swinging at you. Lastly we come to the absolute WORST gameplay implementation that was done. The curse of the Abyss itself.The idea here is that if you ascend, you get sick. Its really a simple concept. The problem is how the game tallies exactly how many meters you have ascended since you last sat and had a little break. It isnt calculated by using the relative depth of the map(IE lowest point in the past 15 seconds is 500, if player crosses 485 they get sick). Noooooo, that would make to much sense. Instead they make it a sum value of any and all ascension you do. As a result if you are on a path that is roughly even in terrain, but has small bumps that cause you to rise and fall a few times as you go over it, you could easily get sick and puke your guts out while walking in a straight line. This makes traversing basic terrain infuriating as you just start getting sick out of nowhere. But thats not even the worst part. No, theres an even more egregious sin committed by the devs. In the level design they DEMAND YOU ASCEND. They literally will make you rappel down 80 meters, then walk 20 more, then climb right back up or higher on the other side. Problem is that you have to stop and take a little nap stuck to the side of the cliff like a Koala every 5 meters or you start puking! Oh and by the way to refill the hunger you just puked up you have to cook. To cook 90% of the meals you have to have salt. And its never explained where you scavenge the salt. Im sorry, but If I am starving in a death pit I dont need to season my freaking chicken!!!! Getting back to the level design, I just cant imagine any dev going "yes lets force the player to climb extremely slowly and take breaks every 5 meters for half of all the levels! What a brilliant idea!". I know this was one hell of a rant, but its honestly just such a shame to see so much potential ruined right outta the gate. I hate to say it but I didnt really enjoy any part of the game. I just tolerated it out of love for the franchise. I do have one more major point to make though, and thats the pricing.60 dollars, the price of a triple A game. That is an INSANE PRICE TO PAY. This game would barely be worth 30. I would NOT recommend buying at full price. Honestly the gameplay holds 0 lore you are missing, so just watch a video of the cutscenes on youtube if you love the world of Made in Abyss and want to consume all the lore it has. If you find it on a steep discount and want to try, sure go ahead. But be wary, the mechanics are made to infuriate. Might I suggest a stiff drink to help it go down? I certainly needed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest. I REALLY enjoy this game,  This is a game I would never recommend this game to another person in good faith. At times it feels like there was a meeting where, as a joke, everyone pitched the worst possible mechanics, but instead they weren't actually joking and they did it.When everything is on point and you're in the flow, you really get immersed in everything, truly making you feel like you're a cave raider! When you've been down in the abyss for quite awhile and you manage to arrive back in Orth by the grace of everything, it is such a wonderful feeling. Coming to understand the Abyss like a second home and navigating it like such is satisfying because you have to have it beaten into you. I really adored getting hands-on with a world I deeply enjoy and interacting with my fan favorites from the source, all while on my own little journey to the bottom of the netherworld. that's also the same issue with this game. It tries its very best at every possible moment to remove as much fun as it can. The infinitely spawning enemies makes combat a chore and something you actively avoid, not because it's dangerous and not because of weapon durability, it's just because otherwise you'd be constantly fighting the same enemy every time you turn your camera! Combat is literally something I only engage in as a means of getting more food or because I have a quest(s) that requires me to kill X. You would think in a game about adventure and exploring you would actually be rewarded for doing so, correct? Sike, you either: death, a dead end, a waste of time and resources or, at the very best, a marginal one-way shortcut. Actually, exploring would only really serve to get you lost unless you've already unlocked  I would genuinely love to sit down to a conversation with the person(s) responsible for the mechanic where every annoying flying enemy (the butterflies and birds) hunt you if you're on a stage for 4+ minutes. Some of those stages are HUGE and time-consuming to get through unless you know in advance the EXACT route you intend on taking, otherwise enjoy not being able to climb because they WILL spawn directly on your head and you can not hit them because combat while climbing is jank or they will stunlock you because you have to wait for the curse to disappate. On the topic of the curse, it is by far the BIGGEST letdown! ANY amount of elevation and the curse starts to hit you, enjoy the uneven ground that will also start accumulating, making it so every few seconds or so you basically have to sit there for 8-10 seconds twittling your thumbs while you wait and repeat until you reach your destination. Alternatively, you can choose to sit through the animation of throwing up and sprint for a good while, since you will not get hit by the curse while you're recovering from its effect.I'm only on the 3rd layer right now, so I haven't beaten the game at the time of review but I honestly doubt my opinions would change since my issues from the core mechanics and loop of the game. I'll probably put more playtime into the game and 100% because I'm that kind of person but I very highly doubt I'll ever think about coming back after that or really even fondly thinking of the game, which is honestly a shame because there's a lot of potential if the game didn't try it's hardest to make you hate playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Made in Abyss (Manga/Anime) series, boy are you in for a treat. This game plunges you deep into that beautiful world. It scratches that "if only the Manga/Anime could spend a little more time in expanding each layer" itch. Along the way you'll not only get to meet, but quest with many familiar faces.Ok now for the not so great, although the game was released this year, the graphics seem quite dated (you can find better graphics on a PS3 title). If you're playing on mouse and keyboard, good luck. This game was clearly made to be played with a controller. For a game that allows you to jump into each layer of the abyss to explore and hunt/scavenge/gather, it sure is frustrating that there's a persistent gameplay mechanic built-in to push you out of every area after 5 minutes. Having to deal with constantly spawning 1hp mobs that harass you after barely exploring 1/4 of a new area has to be my biggest gripe throughout my playthrough. (Glad to see there's a mod to disable this). Weapons have durability and you'll find yourself breaking (broken weapons are just instantly deleted) many all throughout the early to mid-game. Thankfully though, by late-endgame, weapon durability is no longer a significant factor to have to play around.Now, if you can get past the graphics quality and the irritating mob spawn mechanic, the gameplay loop is stellar. Diving into the abyss, exploring new layers, mining relics, gathering resources, harvesting mob parts, deciding what to keep/toss cause you're overburdened, realise you're low on food/health/poisoned, before climbing back all the way, hoping to make it back to the surface...rinse and repeat. Each tier of gear and weapon upgrades feel impactful, and can easily turn previously perilous layers into a stroll in a park. As you progress through Red to White Whistle, you are rewarded with very nice quality-of-life buffs like curse resistance and the ability to teleport back to the surface from a previous layer at the cost of hunger and life. Despite the mob spawn mechanic, I was able to complete the game progressing at a relatively comfortable and casual pace (umbrella might be the best relic in the game imo lol).All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed the game very much and to be able to travel down the same paths taken by the Manga/Anime characters, this is very much a must-play for any Made in Abyss enjoyer.

_childDocuments_.review: Good ip, poor game designBeing one of the top fans of Made in Abyss, I bought this game immediately, but quickly got disappointed by the several factors in the following:1. Ridiculous Key bindsIn most 3rd person RPG games, you click left mouse to attack, right mouse to aim. In this game, left clicking your mouse is Crouching, and right clicking does nothing. You hold Z key to aim, and press X to attack. The worst part is you can’t change the key bind to your mouse in settings. Left shift is supposed to be sprinting and Q or E to open your inventory. No. You need to press TAB to craft and open the full inventory. You sprint by holding left control. I haven’t even complain that mouse wouldn’t work in selecting anything except a few option buttons. Instead of scrolling down with your mouse wheel in menu, you are forced to spam W and S or Z and X keys to go up or down and left or right on the panel, respectively. By the way, spacebar always closes the menu, ESC is useless just like left mouse.2. Reg’s AI is profoundly defective. He is controlled by an AI that has a health bar and would respawn after losing all health. Sometimes he helps you to neutralise threats. But most of the time he attacks any hostile monster even if they are passive, he could’ve just ignore them. But he decides to attack anything and wastes health. Then by the time you need him, he’s always on his way to respawn.Sometimes he is stuck in one place. He can’t climb unlike Riko with spacebar, and decides to stomp around. If you don’t have any food supply, ignore him and move on, because trying to lead him will waste your hunger bar. 3. some map design flaws that would trap you forever if your hunger bar is empty. First, you lose hunger when you enter the next map. Second, In the reverse forest, there’s a spot on the only path that you must climb. Climbing costs you hunger and stamina. And when your hunger bar is empty, your stamina bar is also empty. That means you can’t climb or use weapons. And to recover your hunger, you need food. There are barely any food in this map and only by hunting the birds you have a chance to loot 1 egg from 1 bird. You need 2 units of eggs to craft 1 unit of food, and each unit will only sustain a couple more times to attack and steps of walking. Then you might want to rely on Reg, and he is not reliable in the game.Conclusion I really want to ask for refund but my play time is well over 2 hours. Console version is probably better speaking of the controls. Whoever makes the steam version has never played any RPG games on PC. If you have bought this already, you have paid a premium well beyond any of the triple A games. At least not worse than bf2042.

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately wanted to like this game. But I cannot in good faith recommend this to anyone, fans or otherwise, of Made in Abyss. To start off, the game has two modes. You play as Riko and Reg, two of the main cast of the anime, as they descent to the second layer of the Abyss. Completing their mode is considered the "Tutorial", and you make your own original character child and experience what cave raiding essentially would be in this world. That is a fantastic setup for what could have been an anime aesthetic punishing-but-fair action game with Tsukushi's messed up mind making up about 3/4 of the monsters you'll encounter in the game. Instead what we get is a crash course in bad game design and budget restraints causing a developer to pad game time with arbitrary meter management that becomes next to impossible near the end of the game.-It sure is Made in Abyss-Moments of actual awe and wonder as you reach certain areas and get to explore places from the manga-Side quests are generally of the "Gather 50 in X zone of Y Layer", for every zone of the layer, or "Kill Z monsters in X zone of Y layer"-The design of the layers feels like most of the budget was put into layers 1 and 2, and they ran out of money to finish the game.-If you navigate the world, you will eventually NEED to ascend in order to continue going down, whether a walk up a hill, climbing a tree, or scaling a cliff. The Curse of the Abyss introduces a very fun and exciting mechanic where you have to stop moving for 30 seconds in order wear off so you can continue to ascend. This never improves and there is no resistance stat like cave raiders develop in the Anime's canon.-Enemies are spawned constantly behind your camera. This can become exceptionally frustrating when you're navigating sheer cliffs.-Related, Moths and other flying enemies spawned behind the camera can navigate into your model, causing you to be stuck in place until you fall to your death.-The durability of your weapons is just slightly too low to not be frustrating.There may be more but this is what has come to mind. Finishing this game was exhausting and I wish to never touch it again.I've beaten the game, 100% achievements, and I did it in spite of the game and its poor design choice, not because of the game being enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. many complain about the mob spawning but there are mods to turns that off if you don't like it. I personally do not mind it too much. it is occasionally annoying when you are climbing something and entity collision causes you to spaz out and fall to your death, but the easy solution to that is to just kill everything as you ascend or descend. This game is hard and it is quite unforgiving, but to me it felt fair. Do be warned though, it is very easy to soft lock as going down is significantly easier than going up. ALWAYS save manually at the orphanage/orth before going into the abyss and NEVER overwrite that save in the abyss. If you soft lock and overwrote your orphanage save, then you'll have to restart the entire game. Now soft locking isn't a negative here. It feels intentional and makes sense. It's basically if you are careless and do not give any thought to how you will ascend, then you will obviously get stuck. There is a lot of content here and exploring, gathering, and combat is pretty fun. There are 2 campaigns. the first one is ~5 hours and follows the first  of the show. Its very restrictive and simplified. (no skills, no xp, no storage, no tool durability, no infinite enemy spawns). That first story is okay but mainly serves as a 5 hour tutorial. I'd recommend it, but if you do play it, you really have to commit to it since deep in abyss mode is MUCH better. deep in abyss is ~50 hours to beat and has a lot more. All the content is unlocked and is much more unforgiving. The deep in the abyss mode is its own unique story, but equivalently follows . So I'd recommend watching those first if you are interested in the show. IF you decide to do deep in abyss first and skip the 5 hour "tutorial" campaign, then, fair warning, it will still give help, but it will be ROUGH at the start. I've seen many reviews of people doing that and giving up because they don't understand food management, combat, and ascending. I should note this game plays like a souls-like version of don't starve. Story wise, its kinda eh. the story has good potential, but character development is very much lacking. However, it does expand on the world building a bit. You can make and eat basically everything in the shows and movies. And you can learn more about how promoting to higher whistle ranks works and, learn about some of the relics. Anyways I love this game.  If you like made in abyss, then I highly recommend. and if a brutal don't starve souls-like sounds fun then give it a go. Just heed my warning. You need to play cautiously. always make sure you have a return route and a save back at orth in case of soft locks. There are mods to turn off the infinite mob spawns. Be aware of the insane difficulty spike in the 3rd layer. There are often multiple ways of descending and ascending: go on short scouting adventures to find them!

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 30 hours in, in the Deep in Abyss campaign, here are my thoughts.I would only recommend this game if you're a big fan of the anime, like I am. You're going to need to have a big place in your heart for this show to tolerate the downsides. But if you do, then you're going to have fun._DOWNSIDES____________-Enemy spawn rates are ridiculous. I was able to avoid ground enemies spawning by facing away from a cliff, because they spawn when you're not looking. However, when you're climbing, flying enemies spawn like crazy and it gets pretty egregious. Climbing takes stamina and so does swinging your weapon. So you can see where the problem lies. I did find, though, that just sitting at a shallow cliff face and waiting for them to spawn and striking them down is an easy way to get a hold of bug meat, which can be crafted into food that refills stamina.-Glitches everywhere. Most haven't been game-breaking fortunately. It's mostly visual.-When you run out of stamina, you stop dead in your tracks. It can get really annoying really quick.-Weapon durability is waaay too low.-Unable to sort your inventory. You can put things on your item ring but, as far as I know, you can't sort in the inventory screen.-Can only fast travel after you get your blue whistle.-When cave raiding with other characters, they say one line on loop every 30 seconds or so. It gets old fast.-The Hello Abyss mode in general. It is not a good retelling of part of the first season. The only improvement made is that there isn't any fanservice, something I'm very thankful for. I ended up speedrunning it to get to the Deep in Abyss mode.-General lack of polish_UPSIDES____________-Once you get to Deep in Abyss, you're able to go anywhere and do anything. My favorite part of the show was the world so it's nice to be able to explore and interact with everything.-Analyzing creatures makes an entry in your notebook that gives you lore about them. It's very nice.-The Deep in Abyss story is intriguing. You can only level up your skills to the next whistle rank when you reach it in the story, and the fact that white whistle is listed gives me that bad feeling of foreboding like the anime does.-Some of the side quests have a lot of charm. There's an early one where you find a mail balloon holding the last letter of a delver and he wants it delivered to his family. I won't spoil it but what happens when you do deliver it is really nice.-Though I listed the fast traveling in downsides, part of me actually likes having to go through the layer to get to where I need to go. It feels like an expedition.-Going into unknown territory feels actually dangerous. It makes good on the sayings that the abyss is treacherous, even in the first layer.-You can customize your delver at anytime!-More Jiruo content. Love that guy.-It took some time, but the graphics are actually kind of nice when you get used to them. At least the first layer.-There is some genuine love put into this game with the amount of detail in some places, like the notebook, food choices, gear, and Deep in Abyss story._SUGGESTIONS FOR POTENTIAL PATCHES____________-Fix the enemy spawn rates and weapon durability. Please please please.-Fix the myriad of glitches.-Don't make the player stop completely when they run out of stamina-Add inventory sorting-The ability to walk around a portion of Orth or Belchero

_childDocuments_.review: Game really feels like an alpha build. Doesn't even have it's own game icon, just the standard unreal engine ico. And I'm not saying that just because of the graphics, but because the game ends prematurely. It makes sense I suppose, since the manga has not been finished, but they're selling it as if it is a finished game, and they're charging $60 for it!The game is split into two parts:Hello Abyss, which serves as a sort of demo that concludes at the end of the second layer, and Deep Abyss, in which you go back in with your custom character to the end of the fifth layer. So, what is going to happen to everything with the sixth layer onwards? Will they be released as DLC?You only control one character, Riko or your OC, and sometimes you are followed by your compatriots. They're pretty strong, but there is no limit to how often voices are played causing them to repeat the same voice lines over and over every time. You will quickly mute the voices to save your sanity, especially when you start hearing them in the cutscenes. You know how Sonic Adventure ripped most of the voice lines from dialogue in cutscenes? Same thing here.There is some intrigue in the design of each area, that will probably not be appreciated in Hello Abyss, as you are constantly being forced to "go to the objective marker", even while your supply of items is dwindling. You see, when your hunger meter depletes, your stamina is gone. You cannot climb and you cannot fight, and past the first layer which has berry trees, there is no natural food source anywhere else that doesn't require stamina to get. It is all produce from the primevals. Prioritize food (and weapons because you can't fight w/o them either), or find yourself trapped with nowhere to go but down.It's not until Deep Abyss that we have a bit more free reign, though there are still some moments like this. Not too many compliants about the skill point trees, but a lot of the combat-related perks are just useless. Your emergency dodge roll is just too inefficient to be useful. It cannot roll through enemies, leaving you to get sandwiched by hordes, and it has helped me dodge attacks a grand total of zero times. When you're able to dodge, you're able to run, which is always the better option, because enemies are not that bad in this game. A lot of the elite types enemies are very strong and can easily kill you in one hit, but can easily be kited or stunlocked and they have a very limited set of attacks, to match your weak and clunky control, I guess. As such, most of the bosses you face don't feel like as much of a threat as they should be.It squishes the manga's story into the game, though some are done through the perspective of your custom character and feel like there's less stakes because of it. Despite all the brutality and the potential death of major characters by your hand, all of the lewd parts from the original work are only told in passing. Licensed game, this was bound to happen.I won't lie and say I didn't like it. I had fun. Most of my enjoyment comes from my interest in the story's world, and I want the media to be exploring and learning more about that world. But I can easily see some critic playing this for 5 minutes and immediately hating it. Can't say I'm surprised considering the devs started from making a visual novel. The expectations placed on something like this was just too high for them to surmount. But an attempt was made. I truly do wish them luck, you did your best mates. For 60 dollars though? Absolutely irredeemable.I feel really bad having to say these things... Tsukushi, please don't hold it against me...Would anyone else be willing to work on making a Made in Abyss game, I wonder?

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such a disappointment. It is NOT worth the price, even on a sale I would say stay far away from this game. The tutorial mode where you play as Riko and Reg is horribly laid out, and does not do a good job at explaining the core mechanics of the game. The mode where you play as your own cave raider has moments of intrigue, but is ultimately held back by the technical issues and wildly irritating design decisions. I'll give you an example - You need to begin climbing back up to the surface after a successful cave raid. Because of the fact that enemies never stop spawning, you have had to use up all the durability of your pickaxe or knife. To craft another one, you need animal bones, which are only obtainable by killing certain creatures. To kill said creatures, you need some kind of weapon, like a pickaxe or a knife, and there is no way for you to fight back whatsoever without a pickaxe or a knife (until later in the game where you can obtain ranged weapons). So you are effectively stuck, and have to restart the entire cave raid because the game's own mechanics go out of their way to softlock you into restarting and losing all your progress. It just feels like a giant waste of time. The original story from what I played was alright, but nothing special. I'd say just stick with the anime at this point and to not trust these developers in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, since I’m a big Fan of the series. The setting gives a great potential for an interesting and challenging game, but the implementation of the developer is less than mediocre.The graphics are verry dated, which is a shame since the unreal engine was used. While I don’t have a big gripe about the visuals it mostly shows that the game also came out for Nintendo Switch (which isn’t meant positively). The character models are mostly near the original but other points, like the looks of other clothing, are just bad. Why do I need cat ears on my helmet where I mostly fight some deadly creatures?While the graphics can be called last gen, the technical implementations are even worse. Animations don’t match with the movement. Animations interrupt other interactions. Hitboxes are truly a bad joke. The menu is atrocious and also the item wheel is kind of pointless if it gets cluttered by every item you pick up (even if the item isn't usable in the first place). You will get stuck in most places and the geometry of some climbable walls is so badly designed that you either cand get through or loose grip for no reason. Fighting feels sluggish which is caused by the bad animations and also the badly implemented fighting in general. While the game puts lot of focus on fighting enemies the fighting system can be described as mostly rudimentary. You have an basic attack which can be upgraded but only gives you more combos. The targeting of enemies must be hold and rolling is by double tapping the sprinting button. So for some fights you’ll need 2 to 3 buttons pressed at the same time for focusing an enemy, attacking it and rolling away. Sometimes the attack will trigger more attacks then pressed. Also, the Sounds are mostly repetitive. Some voice lines will repeat endlessly and will get on your nerves, especially for the companions. The English dub is ok but nothing to brag with.Gameplay is mostly repetitive. You’ll go down the abyss, get some gathering quests here and there and fight through enemies and find some relics by excavating on certain spots. Besides your health and stamina you have an fullness meter. If the fullness gets empty your stamina will no longer recover and you aren’t able climb or attack. The maps are mostly small and traversing from one map (not layer) to another will either deplete some of your fullness or fullness and health. Also you can shorten the way down the abyss but you will allways need to ascend through all of the layers to get to the overworld. While climbing, jumping or walking slopes upwards you will catch the curse. If you ascend to far you will get the curse corresponding to the layer you’re in. The implementation of the curse is somewhat right from the lore perspective but feels mostly harsh in game. Ascending roughly 10 metes will give you the curse. However this is also true for getting up a couple meters and descending afterwards. The counter of catching the curse is cumulative. Some areas are hilly enough that you’ll catch the curse while running straight a line. Also while climbing you will have to make rests for depleting the curse counter. This is especially bad in the 3rd layer, which is mostly climbable walls. While climbing or walking through the areas you will get attack by smaller enemies which will respawn infinetly and also can teleport. This means that most enemies will spawn or teleport in right behind you. This happens also while climbing, so enemies constantly try to attack you while pausing for the curse to stop. The Weapons have durability and will get destroyed. So fighting might not always be the best solution. Besides a crafting system you ‘ll need to manage you backpack that has a carry limit and too low for the most time. Your carrying weight will only be shown while browsing in the menu. So you will have moments where you will fall of the cliff for excavating an relic and getting overweight.The Hello Abyss campaign tells the original story of Reg and Rico, while being altered very much. Dialogs and also whole scenes are altered. It feels like a family friendly summary of the manga, which is odd for the gorier Death scenes. Yes the anime and especially the manga have some problems, but the mor darker side and the horrific pictures are missed completely by the game. While trying to copy the sound of Kevin Penkin (composer of the music for the anime) it completely misses the mark and often it will struggle to set a mood also it feels very repetitive after some hours of game time. I might be a bit harsh here for being a composer myself but it feels mostly off and uninspired, especially with the work of Penkin in mind.All in all the game feels mediocre at best which is an insult for the asked price of 60€. I really wanted to like this game and while playing there are some glimpses of an interesting and fun game but those sparks of hope mostly get killed off by the more than lacklustre technicalities and phoned in mechanics. I wonder what another game studio would have brought. Having gathered experience with this game it will by my last game from Spike Chungsoft. Oh, what a shame! I hope there will be another chance for this this IP by a better game studio.

_childDocuments_.review: First. off. I will say I 100% this game. By that I mean I literally did everything this game has to offer. Every quest, every item, every enemy scan etc.BUT! I will say this game is not worth the 60 Euro they want for it. It's rushed, with bad AI and barebones features, and I had a blast with it.The Good: You will have fun with it when you start out at first. It's unforgiving and will punish you with no remorse for the slightest mistake. The exploring part is what really shines, and juggling your weight limit to fit that one extra thing you really wanted makes it very addictive.The in-between: Combat is kind of meh. So are the quest who mainly consist of fetch quests or kill X of this creature (the latter going up to insane quota's). You get relics you can slap on your gear, but it's very limited on the variety. Until Endgame/Postgame it's mainly poison resistance or broken arm/leg resistance. Only after you beat pretty much everything do you get interesting stuff like HP up, crit up etc, to put on your gear.The Bad.The AI is hurrendus. Both the monster AI and the human AI. The human AI can't even navigate the maps and keeps repeating the same stuff every 2 seconds. The enemy AI has no concept of danger either. There is an area with a large laser that's part of a puzzle, where I without problem farmed birds flying into said laser trying to get to me. Some areas have invisible bumps stopping you in your tracks so you have to jump over them. Also I have died a few times to me trying to step over a dead enemy and the game decided the corpse and my avatar can't be in the same place resulting in me getting booted off the platform to my death. The animations are pretty bad too. bipedal enemies have no girth to their step and looks like they have wheels attached when they run around. Game was obviously rushed out the door for a fast buck which is a shame since the good stuff is really amazing. All in all it's worth getting when it's on sale, but don't you dare pay full price for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to fans of the series.  Through gameplay it let me see the world of Made in Abyss in a new light.  I didn't know I  (But perhaps grab a simple mod to remove the 'hurry up' mechanic which felt completely at odds with the rest of the game for me.)Although I bounced off the game at first, I gave the game another chance and got completely immersed in the experience it was bringing.  This is the story of you being a young cave raider, who slowly but surely learns how to dive into the abyss and survive each layer.  Bit by bit, learned experience by learned experience.  Building up your accumulation of knowledge and skills so that you can go deeper and deeper.And the game manages this through very simple gameplay mechanics and basic graphics.  The game does look like a 'budget' title (the character models look great and accurate to the series's style though), and kind of plays like one too, but it does so much with what it has.I was absolutely stunned at times when entering a new area and seeing what lay ahead, which really goes to show how well the game fosters the atmosphere, dread, and wonder of exploring deep into the Abyss, even with its simple visuals.  Discovery was a constant reward, and wanting to see what was next kept me going forward.In keeping with the survival emphasis of the series and setting, preparation is key to success in your cave dives.  If your only weapons are about to break you'll have to avoid enemies instead of fighting them.  If you run out of ropes you may need to turn back.  If you run out of food (and didn't think to bring enough salt to make more food) you may be a goner.  The logistics of having enough food and supplies to reach your destination  are super important, showing the challenge in traversing the Abyss, and is what I would say is the basic gameplay challenge of Binary Star.Combat is super bare bones and most things are very easy to kill.  Oddly I found that the weapon durability in this game added to the experience, since, while you can almost certainly defeat any monster in your way if you have to, you'd prefer to avoid conflict just to save on weapon durability.  Avoiding unnecessary encounters seems very appropriate for being a cave raider.  Also, your durability is restored when you return to Orth, which greatly took the sting off of weapon durability to me.Each layer brings its own challenges for you to encounter, become familiar with, and then surpass.  By the time you reach a new layer, you have gained mastery over the previous one.  This is through player knowledge, like learning routes, knowing what kind of supplies to bring, how to deal with enemies, etc.  and also through skill upgrades you've unlocked or gear you have crafted.And then you step into that new layer where new, different struggles await you, in ways that were thematic and never felt forced.  Each layer of the abyss feels so unique, and full of (murderous) character.  I found myself having a new appreciation for each layer in turn, and the difficulties Riko must have gone through when traveling through these areas... and even more appreciation for what regular cave raiders (who don't have a Reg with them!) have to deal with.If a video game representation can create that kind of new perspective and appreciation, then I would say it is very successful.In summary, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with is this game, and hope that anyone reading this finds the same joy in this game's charms that I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Until you've gone real deep in the abyss and gotten down to your last weapon and are struggling to get enough food to make it from map to map you wont feel that sense of conquest, but when you do clawing back from being on the verge of having to give up that's what makes a real cave raider~don't let the simple look of the game turn you off while its not super souls like i would say it can be even more punishing then souls if you are unprepared, there's a real sense of achievement once you learn what you need to be proficient at cave raiding going deep on a raid and being able to make it back is really rewarding~and a big tip, there is a hidden timer when ever you go into a map like a grace period of sorts enemies wont spawn around you or while you climb if you are fast :)(all the negative reviews talking about the endless enemies spawning just don't know how to use the crouch button.... literally everything will stop coming after you once you crouch and move less then a centimetre away from them... and in some cases its actually helpful when you carry a lot of salt like these negative reviewers xD you can use the bird meat and the eggs to keep stocked up on food :Palso yes weapons have durability you aren't meant to mindlessly Kill EVERYTHING you use your weapons with purpose either for a big enemy that's in your way or to gather food from things that can also drop bones and you will need a few hard rocks from the mine-able nodes to keep making hatchets that's what i use to farm for food also killing the butterfly's that spawn when climbing walls isn't always the best thing to do, try to move left and right moving sideways on walls uses less stamina then moving up or down when your going up ropes you use stamina going up but if you stop moving your stamina will regen you can smack away the flying enemies if they are a bother while rope climbing)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most surreal gaming experiences I've ever had in my life. It's not often I come away from a game that is clearly rushed and unpolished with loads of issues and kind of loving it. So where do you really begin with a game that offers such a unique experience?Presentation:This is probably the element of the game with the most extreme ups and downs. Visually it is absolutely nothing to write home about, fidelity is often low and many of the monsters have a distinct "unfinished" quality to their appearance. Notable examples would be the Orb Piercer and Madokajak (don't worry, we'll get to them.) But the designs are at least faithful to the manga and anime, if not as well realized as I would like. Which is not what I would say about the voice work which is quite good. The entire anime cast reprises all of their roles with quite a lot of dialogue for characters we rarely saw in the anime, it helps bridge the gap and make the experience feel more authentic despite the shortcomings in other areas.Which is a perfect time to bring up the music. No, it is not composed by Kevin Penkin, yet it still is pretty damn good with a number of memorable tracks from the Orth and Orphanage themes to the surprising rock piece that was composed for the lower 3rd layer. It doesn't carry the emotion of the anime's OST but that music is very specific to the show and its content. In short, it's good but don't go in expecting to be moved to tears.Gameplay:So this is where the game really comes into its own as a wild experience. This is a semi-rogue lite dungeon crawler built around learning how to dive deeper and deeper until you finally hit the 5th layer (I'll avoid specific story spoilers.) Each layer comprises of a number of levels, separated by loading screens. Likely because they lacked the time and resources to fully build out a seamless open world. So it's kinda like Stalker, actually it's a lot like Stalker and I might sound like an insane person for saying that but hear me out. Each delve can start from either the very top of the Abyss or from the top of any layer you've unlocked through story progress. This is important if you're looking to collect specific relics for any equipment you might want to create. You have your health and hunger to manage along with a weight system that limits the amount of gear you can carry and you will carry A LOT of stuff on you the deeper you go. Which leads me to what I would consider my primary criticism of the gameplay. There is a fast travel mechanic that allows you to return to the top point of any layer from anywhere excluding the 5th, this is obviously designed as a means to avoid either extreme softlock scenarios or make trips to farm relics less of a pain. But personally I would have preferred either a passive gathering mechanic for layers you've explored or reduced costs on gear but zero upward fast travel. My most memorable moments in this game were before I knew this mechanic existed and I fought from the 4th back to the surface, using every single resource I had to get back up. That's the magic of the gameplay here is knowing how easy it is to go down but every step carries the knowledge that you have to go back up at some point. It challenges you to push yourself and your knowledge of the game to see just how much progress you can make before you hit your limit. Every enemy encounter, every accidental fall, every time you ascend just a bit too quickly and you are afflicted by the curse, it drains those very valuable finite resources you need to escape. I will not go into extreme detail on the combat but it is relatively simple. Weapons have durability, weight, and damage. In increase in one generally means all of them go up as well, with some exceptions. Your goal is rarely to fight every monster you see, that's the fast way to doom a run by wasting resources on things you can just avoid. But it's also important because it's how you collect some of the many resources that are used for crafting both topside and in the Abyss itself.Now... we have to talk about the tutorial. It's bad.The tutorial in question is the introductory campaign called Hello Abyss. In it you play as Riko going through an abridged and slightly different set of events up until they depart from the Seeker Camp in the manga. This is extra weird as an introduction if you have no idea what the hell is going on in this setting because they do not explain a whole lot about the world and if you're already a fan, you've seen this before. I've seen two versions of this story, a third was not necessary. The acting carries it since you get the authentic Riko and Reg experience, but remember, this is supposed to be teaching you how to play the primary campaign. Yeah, this is still meant to be the tutorial yet it does not teach you about:(This is not an exhaustive list)- Fishing- Most of the crafting- Ascending sickness- Weapon durability- Ranged combat- Injuries- Status effectsIt's kinda awkward to be forced through an entire 3 hour segment that holds your hand but also tells you very little that's super important for later. I can see people going through it partly and jumping ship because it also hosts some of the worst production value and some truly wretched QTE's that feel REAL CRUSTY. Those moments are the closest it gets to shovelware, which thankfully are rare. But they suck serious ass.Conclusion:Obviously I recommend this game but it comes with caveats. Is it worth 60 dollars? That's up to you, I bought it full price and didn't feel like my kidneys were stolen but that's up to how much you end up liking it. If you get the same number of hours out of it that I did, you'll likely come to the same consensus. It's glitchy, unpolished, the performance ranges from acceptable to kinda awful in some areas, there were notable frame drops in several areas that weren't shockingly bad, but still jarring when you consider this game is not exactly pushing technological boundaries. If this game ever had a sequel I would hope that similarly to Stalker, it continued to build on a series of mechanics that are genuinely interesting but just need some help to really shine. It's good, but it could be great.Also there's Nanachi, therefore, 10/10. 🤣

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one, I can only recommend this to Made in Abyss fans, or people that like continuous kicks in their nutsack, because the Abyss is unforgiving.The game stands a bit above mediocre for me, I have a good time with it, but thats mostly thanks to mods and cheats, Im not gonna sugarcoat it. Things break way too fast, you collect a bunch of things to craft a weapon, and its gone within 10 hits, durability increases with higher gear, but the craft material to usage ratio doesnt feel worthwhile.Some of the OST is hit or miss, Im disappointed we didnt get Kevin Penkins masterpiece, but copyrights a ♥♥♥♥♥, so please dont ♥♥♥♥ on the devs for that, (music can be replaced via mods.)Overall its a rough stone, which can be upgraded by a dedicated community, to make the edges a bit less spiky. Definitely get this on sale, its a 40€ game.

_childDocuments_.review: It really is a shame. A fantastic concept and a world of endless possibilities held back by dated gameplay, repetitive quests and an undeniable lack of enthusiasm from the developers. I wish this game was made by someone who actually loved the source material, or at least gave a damn about making fun video games... both would probably be a good start.You'll find plenty of reviews criticizing everything that's wrong with the gameplay, so I'll spare you the details - if I had to keep it brief, I would say it is simply irredeemable and would have needed a completely different approach from the start. No amount of small fixes here and there can make this enjoyable to any greater degree. The combat sucks, the movement sucks, the survival aspects weigh down your enjoyment at all times - but then again, people will tell you that's the whole point of the game. I played most of this with a mod that disabled the incredibly annoying, endlessly re-spawning enemies and still only barely made it through without gauging my eyes out. This game is not hard. It's not difficult. It's tedious and boring. Every time you feel like you're close to finally feasting your eyes on something exciting, you're instead met with drab visuals, comically bad camera work, rushed animations and a frankly stunning lack of graphical detail for a game released in 2022. I mean damn, I know it has to run on the Nintendo Switch, but that does not excuse completely empty sky-boxes, totally flat lighting and some of the most shoddy texturing I have ever seen in a supposedly reputably produced video game.My playthrough felt very disjointed, I kept triggering and completing quests out of order - I have no idea why or how that happened, but it was a major loss of immersion for me. It's very strange how most quests that contribute to the story-telling in the second half of the game are side quests - it doesn't really make sense to me, they shouldn't be optional. It's so easy to miss big quest branches accidentally or play them out of order.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness has an identity merely by association with the show. If you replaced all the characters with generic people, randomized some of the levels and called it something else, this game would have a 4/10 rating at most. Objectively, it has very few redeeming qualities, and even the fan service is so few and far between that I just can't bring myself to care. This game will do the bare minimum to string you along and then proudly serve you a big plate of nothing at the end.Considering nearly 13% of all players have completed this game in its entirety, I am probably yelling at a brick wall with this review. Must be some degree of masochism involved... ...and yeah, sure, maybe all the trouble was worth it... to hang out with Nanachi...

_childDocuments_.review: The tl;dr is that if you like methodical exploration and Etrian Odyssey, you'll love it.Without the tl;dr, this game could be seen as niche... and it absolutely is. Because it's based off of an incredibly niche sort of manga. It's difficult at times, does not stop you from making mistakes, and you are completely capable of soft-locking yourself. So git gud.The core gameplay loop is similar to the Etrian Odyssey; you have your destination and purpose in mind, you load up on supplies you think you need, you add more because last time you forgot something, and you anticipate the perils you may encounter. Then you dive down, deeper than I went on your mom right after prom but before graduation.The scenery and music fits completely as your death child slowly devolves into a rage child. Faced with untold horrors that normies will never comprehend and the creepy madness that comes from knowing not even a strategy guide will help you, your rage child devolves into some form of pit beast. A little bug-eating shin kicker that says they can take three adults on at once and come out with barely a scratch. Since this is Made in Abyss, I'll let you interpret that as to what seems more canon.The story is pretty bare bones but that's because your Norman Fetus is playing the role of Norman Reedus, which is to say that your journey is your story. You largely lack narration because you whispering to yourself "how do I get out of here alive?" is all the narration you need. Your journey is the plot, with your failures and growth being the rising arc. Your victories from each dive-each one deeper than the last-are the climaxes to that particular chapter.At the time of writing this, I've put in 32 hours and have obtained all achievements. And my verdict? It's too easy. If you're used to the EO series, you're a veteran before you realize it. Taking breaks when it comes to moving up and carefully planning out whether or not you should fight mirrors the plunges up and down the various Yggdrasil labryinths. Break dancing on the razor's edge becomes your bread and butter and it dawns on you that most adults probably were neutered because they simply lacked the testicular fortitude to risk life and limb for the sake of exploration. Then it dawns on you that your lovecraftian potato hasn't entered puberty yet so the notion of testiculars is a far gone dream. It wasn't about fortitude. It was about grit. It was about that need to know what lies beneath. It was about how a child is a smaller target to hit and can crawl into tiny spaces that adults can't so you're technically playing on Easy Mode until you turn into some gangly, spindly-armed monster that has to worry about some myth called "taxes".Also it has wider lore on the setting you don't see from the manga so if you like the series you'll like this even if you suck at the modern hobby known as "video playing". It used to be called something else but multiple websites once told me on the same day that gamers were dead.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game you play for the story, or if you want to have a leisurely time from beginning to end. This is a game where you test your mettle against the dangers of the Abyss, and the Abyss is not afraid to gobble you up whole and spit you out in a gory mess. The game might frustrate you and seem unfair at times, but the Abyss is not a place that you can take that lightly. You have to approach it methodically, making sure you progress while not biting off more than you can chew. Each dive is a balancing act between your equipment, resources and wit. The deeper you go, the harder it is to return home, but the deeper you go, the greater the rewards might be. The more rewards you bring back home, the more your character grows, which lets you delve deeper on your next trip.The game is not without its flaws, and it's not everybody's cup of tea. The story is bad, the new characters are non-existent, most of the interactions with characters you know from the anime/manga are ripped straight out of the source material most of the time, except your OC is shoehorned into it. The game has a very janky feeling to it, as if it wasn't completely finished. The game has a hidden timer that will start spawning agressive enemies on your ass if you stay in one area for too long, which will frustrate you to no end the first few trips, but it's something you eventually learn to play around. The game has two modes, a tutorial mode (Hello Abyss) where you play through a part of Riko's and Reg's story, and a main mode (Deep in Abyss) that contains the meat of the game. The tutorial limits your exploration and teaches you bad habits that will come back to bite you when you begin the true playthrough with the main mode, which might leave for a pretty sour first impression, especially considering that Hello Abyss is mandatory to complete before you can play Deep in Abyss.However, the level design is excellent, the game is challenging in an unconventional way and the sense of progression you feel as you grow your character and descend ever deeper into the Abyss is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has jank, a lot of jank.The combat for the most part sucks there was really only 1 fight in the game I found enjoyable.This is because the combat animations look and feel slow and dull on both your part and the enemies.There are skills that alleviate this but they are mostly towards the end of the game and really aren't your priority when playing.The way the story is told feels odd and slow because of the animation quality.A big number of quest are just fetch quests that on the face of it don't really have a point.This game however does survival in the abyss very very well, it's probably the most I've ever enjoyed a survival mechanic.This is because of the way the game uses the abyss to set an asymmetry in your objectives.Going down you need resources to descend that is: weapons, ammunition, healing, ropes, fish bait, poison resistances, food, etc...Going up you need: space for relics, much more food for the ascent, gas balloons to reduce weight, mission goal materials, etc...All the while you can't stay in one place for too long or creatures will begin to come after you costing you even more resources to deal with.The end result is a fine balancing act where you need to judge the amount of resources you're willing to take down into the abyss to use to bring up (the generally heavier) relics to sell/hand in. Bring too much and you need to go up early or waste your resources to make room for more relics, bring to little and you're likely to die from hunger.Adding to this is the crafting system that perfectly fits into the survival mechanics as a means for adjustments when things go wrong, as they inevitably will.If a weapon breaks, you can scavenge resources to make a new one, if you run out of food you can cook creatures of the abyss to keep yourself full, if you're out of ropes you can make new ones.With crafting becoming more important in the deeper layers where you pretty much have to accept that you won't be able to take all ropes or food you want while still coming back with a size-able haul, so instead you bring down salt, sugar, etc... things that help you cook food but weigh much less to make it possible eat on the go in the abyss.The game also carries a skill system and its pretty important to level up your skills appropriately so you don't get stuck as it allows you to craft more things, carry more things, ascend or descend more easily etc...I earlier mentioned how there where quite a few fetch quest just thrown about, I suspect these large quantities of fetch quest were put there so that even without consciously going after all of them players are still likely to clear a few and gain skills to level up.Originally I wasn't going to recommend this game to anybody because the initial game-play section following through the story till the end of the 2nd layer, was long arduous and boring as it failed to communicate the game's best features well making it hard to recommend even to the right target audience.However upon recently learning that they had actually removed that being a requirement to play 'Deep abyss' I decided to write this review.Overall I would recommend this game to those with a niche interest in survival elements if they want to see survival done in a novel and interesting way and can handle some jank here and there.As I stated at the start, there is jank in this game, a lot of it, but I was able to tolerate it because I think the developers succeeded in making a game that communicated one crucial aspect of the manga. That being that in the abyss the biggest danger isn't fighting monsters it's finding ways to survive in the abyss and its tough but with careful planning and quick thinking you can get through it.I think that's something the developers can take pride in. A more successful game might have made them more money, but this game will stay with me. The niche it struck has given me a unique experience that's left me with that all too nostalgic curse of being so engrossed in a game that once it ended the world felt a bit hollow because there was no more for me to play.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I played this game through on the Nintendo Switch first. I purchased the Collector's Edition physical copy on Switch and it was worth every cent, despite the game having many flaws. Played over 120 hours total. This game offers many things to do besides the main story if you're interested. There are a ton of side quests and the exploration is considerably vast. The main story is interesting enough and most of that has voice acting, which is pretty good. I'd say the exploration is the heart and soul of the game. It's fun to gather for crafting as well. Cooking, crafting weapons and making gear is all pretty straight forward. There's also fishing if you can get the respawns to leave you in peace. This game was a mess at launch and I would honestly say that despite a few patches, it still needs work. Though it's definitely much better now than it was on release. Spike Chunsoft is known for releasing buggy games and never fixing them, so that's nothing new. The respawns aren't quite as egregious as they used to be, but things will still spawn right on top of you and behind you when you turn the camera. The moth brigade will still be sent in if you even look at a climbing surface, which is pretty anti-fun but manageable with a little skill and patience. That's what this game requires more than anything: patience. If you can learn to be patient and not get frustrated, you will find tons of enjoyment in this game. I've seen a lot of people stating that "you will love this game IF you're a Made in Abyss fan." I had never even heard of Made in Abyss before this game and this was my GOTY for 2022. This game got me through some stressful times last year when I had a pending court date and thought I was probably going to jail each day for over 3 months while waiting for court. Not a great feeling. Luckily, things worked out and I avoided doing time. This game really helped me forget about the stress of my court date, so for that I am grateful. Anyway, I've also read some things about the graphics supposedly looking bad and I couldn't disagree more. In my opinion, the graphics are beautiful. It's the perfect aesthetic for an anime game. I'm not sure what people are expecting a game from a manga to look like. Not everything needs to look like Elden Ring or God of War. I grew up with the NES, SNES, Genesis and Sega Saturn, so to me this game looks incredible. People are a little spoiled on graphics nowadays. This game looks fine. I wholeheartedly love the music so much. No complaints with the soundtrack whatsoever. The piano bits while at the Orth screen are hauntingly beautiful, much like the Abyss. So, maybe I'm an oddball because I'm one of the few that the GAME actually got me into the ANIME. I had no idea what this was and had seen some preview videos long before its release and just knew I had to play this game. I do not regret purchasing this on both Switch and PC. Doing a second playthrough now on PC, settings on max, 90+ fps. Just gorgeous. This game (to me) just rules and I love it very much. I have a special place in my heart for this one because of the times it got me through. Plus it's fun as hell.
