_childDocuments_.review: So, a review of this game, a game declared dead on launch by a few, and mainly reviewed by people who haven't finished the game or given it a chance. For anyone who is needing an honest full review of the game, here it is, because lord knows this game needs a full review.The Bad: The worst problems of this game seems to be one thing that made layer 2 hard for me. It's, to put it bluntly, the fact enemies under you can cause you to stop climbing or rappeling and essentially kill you instantly. Half the time I get some form of grace fall protection, still a bit annoying. The Good: You have a fully fleshed out game that gives good incentive to use the cooking system, get used to carrying salt because it will save you. There were very few times I felt the game was impossible. Even in the worst parts of layer 3, I found ways to survive the madokajacks and escape many situations another game might make impossible for me. The want of greed versus returning safely is measured well, and until I completed the game it scaled very well in terms of difficulty. Older parts that were extremely hard became easier, and newer parts maintained the challenge to keep things alive. The deaths being unique was a very eye catching detail, and each layer having different curses was a wonderous surprise to me, especially given the accuracy. The crafting system was robust enough to allow me to survive on my surroundings quite well, and older weapons dont get phased out, they become more staple parts as you use older and outdated weapons to defeat enemies without wearing down your good weapons. Free repair on return to Orth was a godsend, and the reward of bringing relics or doing quests for exp pushed me to do them. The game works really well with this, and a lot of time youll find that it has a lot to offer.For anyone complaining about fast travel, you can access it in the map menu using Q and ascend levels. This helps reduce any slog id find before. It is based on whistle level, so your newest layer is usually not fast travelable. A good solution for something that may throw off balance. The map system also works wonders, and allows for some good tagging of areas.Spoilers ahead now, Ill be reviewing the plot of the game.The first bit is very nice. Raul dying was something genuinely not expected and I thought it was a cop out till I found out he was actually dead. Good on them for establishing stakes. The game works the fine line between humour, cute, serious and heartfelt very well. Tiare is a good foil for the character, and Detchaunga's reveal got better as I played. It wasn't handed to me and I felt good when my worries were rewarded. Bondrewds a fun fight, though most of the later game is dominated by strafing with explosive shot. It will be your godsend. Tiare's feels lacking but the emotional impact was noticable. Most characters are fleshed out very well. Detchaunga's postgame fight was great, never thought id hear a villain threaten to taxiderme my character. Postgame is quite good and opens up even more content, something I'm still playing with as its a very fun game for multiple dives. Good story and plot, like the ending slide.Also, meeting Nanachi when I tried to kill myself threw me for a loop. Very well done with the Nanachi meeting. Also, Reg and Riko's side quests are very fun. Besides that, the game gets my recommends. The people making this game stayed very well to the show and offered even more, giving me an experience I was glad to be apart of. May make a guide at some point, who knows.Besides that, all around worth what I payed for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would actually half-recommend this game. If you want to buy it, don't buy it at full price. When you first start playing, you need to finish a "tutorial" of sorts, which will take you between 30 minutes and an hour, depending on if you skip through the story (It is just a retelling of the anime's plot up their descent in the third layer, I would recommend to skip through the story, and rush to objectives to get it over with as soon as possible).After that, you can play the "Hello Abyss" mode, which is the story of your own character. This story is nothing all that special, but it is worth reading the dialogue in my opinion.In terms of gameplay, this game is quite clunky. There are a lot of systems present; such as: Skill tree, equipment durability, weight, hunger, armor, general resource management, I-frames on dodges, multiple weapon-types, side-quests, multi-layered platforming and so much more. But compared with other games in the same price-range, these systems are just unpolished. As an example: Dodging requires you to input the sprint input twice to execute; and since you have I-frames tied to that roll, the timing to react to enemy attacks is quite awkward. Speaking of enemies; almost every enemy in this game has very predictable attack patterns and can be cheesed easily, and those that can't, can be beaten easily with ranged attacks. Hitboxes in both enemies and terrain are really, really sloppy and will probably lead to a lot of unnecessary deaths. This would not be as bad as it is, if the game wouldn't already punish you hardcore for venturing into the abyss unprepared. Though that is probably the strongest side of this game; the options in the skill tree (which you will unlock more of as you progress through the story) make it clear that interaction with environmental hazards and resource management are your biggest concerns. Getting more powerful through the skills you unlock and the knowledge you earn throughout your time with the game also feels incredibly rewarding. It really is a shame that this game will probably never get any updates, additional content, or for that matter even patches for the abundance of small flaws, but it really is just a fun little game. Though I always think that pricing this game like Monster Hunter: World or Elden Ring is kinda ridiculous. I have 100%ed this game after about 60 hours, and I really think a game should give you more bang for your buck for this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like backtracking for hours on end? Watching all your equipment break but being locked in a forcefield that forces you to fight to the death with opponents you could otherwise avoid? Is your favorite activity running three steps and then running out of breath, then being surrounded on all sides by enemies that deal barely any damage but stun lock you in place until you die? _childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of this series and don't mind that this game is basically a cave raider power fantasy, this is a lot of fun. The timescale of the story beggars belief, in that you go from a red whistle to a white whistle in what feels like a couple weeks of cave raiding. I really feel that some time-skips would have mellowed the experience, but they probably didn't want to do models and animations for child-PC, adolescent-PC, and adult-PC. Understandable. The game also has you complete several feats that feel deeply excessive (. You also wind up collecting a number of relics that you have no business having (). The original story doesn't add much to the world, the game is primarily a vehicle to explore the locations and characters established in the manga/anime. If you're looking for something to let you do new and different things inside of the Made in Abyss universe, this game will disappoint you.Gameplay-wise, learning how to strategically navigate a cliff face so that you can recover your stamina part way through a climb or descent or planning out the optimal return route from a few layers down feels like you're personally progressing as a cave raider with your own little tricks and strategies. Eventually though you get stamina perks that make climbing mostly a breeze, and you get fast travel from higher layers when you progress through the Cave Raider Whistles; both of these changes kind of trivialize a lot of learning and hard work you do before unlocking them. Taking a risk on a climb you're not sure about, but managing to get where you want without falling feels very cool, meanwhile perking to the point that you can just free climb from the bottom of a cliff to the top without any strategy is boring. Combat is kind of a snooze once you get the hang of it, especially if you employ some of the better options available to you. The only enemies I really struggled with were . When I played at release, there was an annoying issue of mobs spawning in ridiculous numbers once you'd been on a layer for a couple minutes; I do not know if that's still the case, but I used a mod to decrease the spawn rate to something less unreasonable, and it saved me a lot of frustration. Some may complain that I removed the combat difficulty I complained the game was lacking, but even with the insane spawns it wasn't difficult so much as incredibly annoying. After the tutorial section, all weapons have durability that decreases with use, so the extra mobs were just a logistical problem that'd artificially inflate how long the game takes to complete (i.e. with weapons breaking much more often and having to carry many more weapons that eat up your carrying capacity, having to do more trips to the same locations). I don't regret at all modding the spawn rate down a bit.Atmospherically, the game captured the Abyss very well. The portrayal of most of the major landmarks was great, especially in the first layer and Ido Front (did not like how they did  at all though, felt cramped and not how it was in the manga or anime. The soundtrack was a miss for me. I just turned off the in game music and played the anime OST instead.Overall I enjoyed it. I'd give it a B grade.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first things first,before you even think about touching this game please do yourself a favor and watch the anime.So with that out of the way, lets go to the game review.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is in its wholeness a maybe 3/4 finished game. Some mechanics leave out mutch to want, sutch as the enemy AI or the combat system. The game itself is split into 2 modes: “Hello Abyss” and “Deep in Abyss”.“Hello Abyss” is following the story of Reg and Riko as seen in the Anime until the second layer, where you get familiarized with your surroundings, game mechanics and the rules of the Abyss. So it is advised to first play this mode to gain a deeper Understanding before heading out on your own, since Reg out there babysits you.“Deep in Abyss" follow`s a new untold story which in general is in my opinion 6/10, so not the worst and not the best. Here you dive deep (Pun) into the Abyss up until the 5th layer. The difficulty of this mode is directly proportional to how good you know the limits of the game, since there are things you are never directly told. And now the problems of this game, just to name a few:- auto save will never have your back- routes are not clear so you have to find them yourself (which is a good thing since it encourages exploration, but you will likely just die to the same stuff again)- you can get easily soft locked- your tools break way to quickly- some ingredients are always required and if you run out of them, you can say goodbye to your run- infinite spawning mobs- generally ascending in the 3th layer- farming relics for armor/ weapons, some required relics are so rare you will likely only see them in 1/5 farming runs (talking about you ugly bayblade)- the bosses in general are way to easy compared to the rest of the game- your inventory is full nonstopJust to name the ones that come to mind.But the game is still enjoyable when you use community mods sutch as “Decreased Item Weight”, “Reasonable Quests” etz. These you can find on steam guides or on the official “Made in Abyss: Modding Community” Discord. These can mitigate these issues, and without them the game is really good.With all of that said, when this game does something good, you really notice it.- The music, OMG the music, if you like the Made in Abyss soundtrack you will love this one, I cannot stress this enough the music in this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful.- the way the Abyss is portrayed as this lonely, cruel, unforgiving  place- the voice acting is just like in the Anime - large variety of food, relics and weaponsAll in all, I would say this game is worth playing a solid 7/10.  But it`s not worth 60$ get it in a sale!The Link to The discord:

_childDocuments_.review: Things to fix:- The game was unplayable for me (and for many other people) without the no-respawning-enemies mod. Make it an option in the menu. I'm seriously sorry for the people playing it on the consoles. Constant swarm ruins the experience of exploring and the game in general. Especially in the beginning, when you aren't used yet to the clunky controls and item wheel and you don't know yet, that you should run away from enemies, when you have no weapon equipped, otherwise they'll just keep stunning you and kill you, before you'll be even able set a weapon on the item wheel.- Keyboard and mouse controls are awful, even after rebinding. You can't click anything in the menus. You can only confirm with mouse what you've chosen with keyboard (it works like enter press, which is useless). Make the menus clickable. Operating item wheel with mouse is terrible.- NPC followers talk way too much, repeating the same lines over and over again. It's absurd that it was implemented this way.- "Increase gathering speed" - change the description to double loot from gathering or something (same with other two farming skills).- Seeker Camp is so empty - nothing to do (at least at first), nothing to buy, no restock when you first arrive there, which feels unfinished. I was quite disappointed, when I first arrived there.- Corpses disappear too fast and sometimes it's hard to dismantle them (especially in butterflies case) - you often can't loot them before they disappear, especially when you fight many enemies at once. What is even the reason to make them disappear so fast? Make it 2 or 3 times longer.- Weapon crafting system for all except basic weapons is broken. Farming good resources is not efficient enough. Everyone just crafts high-end weapons once, swaps them before they break and comes back to town for auto-repair. I don't think this is how the system was intended to work.- No real reward for filling notebook. Put some milestones to make it worthwhile.- Add tutorial on fast travelling up (back to surface). It's hard to find and the rules are not intuitive at all.- Sorting settings in the inventory are temporary, make them stay.- Sygnalize that the character is running out of stamina more clearly (deep breathing, more/earlier sweating).- When you try to talk with Kiyui, the onversation often triggers with Shiggy instead, because they stay to close to each other.- Lower the requirements of quests for killing 30/50/100 the same type of enemies, which have like single respawn per map.Things to consider:- Make the possibility to fight unarmed, when all your weapons break. Even if it's very weak attack, it would help newbies.- Make better weapons more durable versus weaker enemies (can depend on their HP or something).- Killing big/tough monsters doesn't give enough reward (no good enough loot, no achievement).- NPC followers getting stuck at objects. I know they reset after some time, but it makes the game feel more buggy than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who want's this game I definitely reccommend. The game has two story modes. One where you play Riko and Reg on their journey through the abyss. The other where you follow the story of a nameless cave raider.I definitely reccommend doing Riko's route to learn basic controls and how stuff works before doing your own thing. The game captures the essence of the anime perfectly. The whimsical beauty and danger in the abyss is beautifully captured. The death scenes are brutal as well and each creature has their own death animation (except small ones like the vines and tiny birds and the flowers)The customizations have variety and unlike most anime genre's this one even has different skin complections. You can give your character heterochromia eyes as well.You will feel immersed in the story and feel like an actual cave raider.The game will make you beg, plead, cry, laugh, and puke.I am addicted to this game, it is weirdly peaceful yet terrifying leaving you on the edge of your seat.DEAR DEVELOPERS OF THIS GAME:Here is some stuff I feel like they should add however to make the game play more enjoyable.- More save states. You only get three save states and an auto save. Meaning if you wanna make different characters and play them all at once, you can't really do that. And you can basically kiss your sweet ass goodbye and have to restart if your soft locked and don't know how to navigate somewhere. -Speaking of navigation, a navigation on and off feature would be really helpful to new players or those who don't have an internal navigation irl skill. -Some of us like playing for the story and scanning everything while others might like the challenge. I think this game would be so much better if they had a difficulty setting. -Multiplayer. Imagine it. You and your friends helping eachother navigate the abyss. It would not effect the story as the characters will only talk to you, but it be really neat for layer 3 when you run out of supplies and cant fast travel.-Speaking of fast travel, if the developers can't make the fast travel easier by making us fast travel to layer one when we are on layer 3 as a moon whistle can we at least have it where there's a call for help thingy with a consequence like losing all our items from the trip or something? Or maybe also have a feature where we can fast travel sections instead of just the entrance to the layers we unlocked? Just asking.This game is a masterpiece and was worth every penny, they really did capture the essence of the abyss and the dangers it has, and the developers should be proud of themselves for accomplishing this feat.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game was a lot of fun. There are a lot of easy things to dismiss it for, and you'll see plenty of them in negative reviews but the nebulous term "buggy" is not very fair as I encountered very few bugs and none game breaking, the gameplay is solid, even if the game is on the lower budget side, which is what most people throwing out this term probably mean anyways.The most fun part of this game, I loved scoping out the map, learning to route to areas, and manage your resources to get there, it can be pretty engaging, then you do not have fast travel on the deepest layer you're allowed to go, so you have to make it all the way back up.Its also an RPG, there will be collecting materials, crating items, doing quests for people etc. I did not find collecting materials excessive like many rpgs can be, so I enjoyed that too.The story: Its servicable, nothing groundbreaking and there was a few parts I wondered if it could be considered cannon. However, there is a lot of lore to learn, all the monsters, a lot of interactions with the npcs and such made me excited to learn more and progress the story. (since I like Made in Abyss)The combat is okay, I didn't think it was all that fun, sometimes you will hit things and it does no damange, honestly its really medicore. Many of the boss music enemies are a joke and easy to defeat also.Lastly, there is the "reason-this-game-has-mixed-rating"  The first 2-4 hours is a different game mode that showcases little of the best parts of this game, its basically a run to the next cut scene mode, you also are exposed to the ai companion system the whole time, which is borderline broken, and they repeat the same lines over and over. Really a worst of game showcase.It is also 60 dollars.. for that I got 46 hours to fully complete the game. On the other hand, its obviously not the highest budget of game. Take that as you will but I am not going to take an attitude of condemnation for that and the amount of engaging time I received.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually at about 30 hours due to offline play. all spent in freeplay mode. thank you for allowing us to do that now, spike chunsoft. Wonderful game. Just about everything i could have asked for as a fan of the series...The Abyss in all it's grotesque and wonderfully gory glory. this is also the PERFECT steamdeck game.The Gameplay: Slow burn but fun to explore. it takes about 8 hours of playtime to get to the second layer during free-play though it has up to the 5th layer playable. Each has a similar amount of content to the first, except for the third layer for reasons obvious to most fans. Each layer being split into 9-15 Zones rather than being one large progressively loading map. Each "zone" has a Health and Food cost to advancing, though going down costs no health, only food.The integration of the Strain is good. Probably the best way it could have been done game-play wise and not be very annoying. The Gripes: As if the Strains of Ascension and the curse of the abyss weren't bad enough, as you start climbing, flying enemies will spawn to pester you on your way up. Terrible idea. though i suppose that's the point. usually a new one will spawn every 15 meters of climbing, though you do eventually get a weapon that is designed specifically to swipe away these enemies. The Netherworld is ruthless. There are also the unfortunately many ways to soft lock yourself. (starving at a teleport point, with no food or no ropes to scale or descend a cliff-side too tall to climb. no weapons available to collect more food or defeat enemies with. on and on.)Weapon durability really is an awful trend to have become popular. Thank you, Breath of the wild. Many of the beginner weapons will break after killing 2-3 large enemies. you can likely get 10-12 small enemies; but considering the exponential cost of these weapons, their massive weight meaning you can't bring many, and the scarcity of materials to craft them in the field. Very poor decision. The Character Customization menu is lacking, having just a singular, androgynous body type to play as, with your choice of hair, flesh tone, beginning attire, and eyes. it is still quite charming to make your own Cave Raider, even if they are not heavily customizable Your raider only has one voice, regardless of playing in the EN version or JP version, and does not change with gender. Many of the Primeval monsters are adequately intimidating, the split jaw most of all. The progression is fine, though by the time you are a blue whistle you will have unlocked all the Red Whistle perks with enough points to also fully complete the blue whistle tier and into the Purple. And boy does that grind to blue whistle take a long time, as stated previously.The Voicework is... adequate I suppose. The story serves little purpose here; the twists and turns all being somewhat obvious to veterans and non-veterans. The big hole is why you and I are here and it is wonderful.good game. worth 60$? absolutely notworth a 65% off sale? absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing this game for round 2 hours I have reached the point of obtaining Lyza's whistle and can some up my thoughts so far.The parts I love about this game are the mechanics, the world/level design and the art style, the guy who said this looks like it came from a playstation 2 must of forgot to put on his prescription glasses because this is around similar quality to Genshin considering the anime cel-shade artstyle. The game is slow paced, which for a new player has its advantages so you can easily get use to controls, change settings and get use to any quirky mechanics. The curse fits rather well, being able to subdue it by standing still for a short period so you dont fully succumb to its effects.I love the fact this game takes into account with things such as stamina, hunger and weight capacity, gives that extra thought of strategy, item management and planning (of course it isnt for everyone).Some things however I have a slight gripe over. The character animations during cutscenes feel too stiff for my liking, im aware some anime based games go for this, however for something like Made in Abyss would recommend making them more lively, another gripe is the effects, an example being when Reg is electrocuted, it is a camera shake and not much in terms of visual effects which is a slight let down. Another aspect is again things such as cutscenes and the eventual dialogue sections, they are ok, however has a more graphic novel base which I again believe doesn't fully fit this game, mostly since I would of expected more animated and 3D aspects such as in Riko's room.One major point I do not like is the price. This is mostly because yes I have not played the whole game yet so not fully sure if it is worth £50, however I can say it feels more like a game worth £20-30 at best.There are more positives and negatives, however those are minor, the game has only just released and like all games will have teething problems and critique will sure come pouring in (on the basis people actually leave HELPFUL criticism and not half arsed angry responses). I'll be sure to leave another or update this review the further I go along, however I do still suggest giving the game a chance

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, a "mixed" (at the time of writing) overall result perfectly defines this game. It's an incredibly niche title priced at $60 which had me incredibly worried, but after watching a no-commentary playthrough and skipping around to try and avoid any game-spoilers, I immediately knew I was going to love it. And allow me to get this out of the way, do NOT spend more time than you need to on the tutorial/Hello Abyss mode. Nothing carries over and in my opinion, was overall implemented poorly.You should be experienced in the source material before getting into this game. The manga if you can since you get all the extreme details that they couldn't air in an anime, but the anime is also great (personally my top #1).The exploration is exciting. I love knowing that the deeper I go, the more difficult it will be coming back up. I love the preparation involved. I love trying to estimate if I have enough supplies to continue onward safely or if I need to turn back. I enjoy having to bring backup weapons and measuring the efficiency of swinging my pickax at a certain enemy is worth it at any given time.I kind of wish the curse of the abyss was a bit more involved. Maybe less harsh, but harder to avoid? It's not the worst right now, it pressures you to play a certain way and that's okay to me but I think it might be more fun if it had a more thematic mechanic than a punishing one.And of course the respawning enemies. I've found a few tools that either scare them away, keep them preoccupied, or make them lose aggro, but none are foolproof against everything. I'm definitely having more success in this department than other players here, but I'd still agree to tone the respawns down just a smidge.They got all of the original JP voice actors on board. This is what made it an instant-buy for me. I'm not a seiyuu fanatic, but if there's a voice a character has been given in one piece of media, you can't change the voice and expect everything to workout. I'm so glad they decided this, even if it's probably what made them price the game at $60. Remember Tales of Vesperia? lol...The combat is serviceable. Standard 3rd person combat with lockon, invincible dodge roll, limited durability weapons, and some unique item-to-enemy interactions (such as throwing meat/sun relics/fruits into a group of monsters).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to address the countless gameplay/video/audio issues. The story alone made me determined to write this negative review, and the story alone made me hate these 2 companies developed and published this game.This part of the game represents first 8 episodes of Made in Abyss season 1. The main story line follows the anime, where Riko and Reg depart from Orth and go to seeker camp. The main story itself is just fine as it is, yet a lot of small details have been dropped. Nat's back story and Lyza's back story are completely nonexistent. Basically what builds up all those minor characters are dropped. All minor characters are made in a forgettable way, all small emotional beats are dropped. The originally touching and disturbing story is stripped down and became as bland as is could be.This part of the game represents a new main charater Aki's story (I'll address the new main charater with their default name "Aki"), where they join Belchero Orphanage as a new cave raider and strive to become a white whistle.The whole story is about Aki becoming a white whistle. In Made in Abyss lore, a white whistle is a life reverberating stone which is made from a human being. The sacrifice must have strong emotional tie with the owner of the whistle and must be willing to sacrifice everything in order to continue their journey into the abyss. Without a strong emotional tie, the life insignia on the whistle will not be compatible with the user's thus cannot be used to activate relics. The curse must be applied to the sacrifice during the transformation as it is what makes the transformation possible. So, the BSFiD story should at least present that "strong emotional tie" through it's story, and a tragic final sense where the sacrifice suffer the curse and transform into a life reverberating stone. But that never happened.There're 3 other cave raiders joined the Orphanage in same time period: None of these new characters received any proper character building. They are just there, doing insignificant things from the start to the end.Tiare is a child infested with terminal illness, sold to a wealthy foreign relic collector by his parents. He wants to delve into the bottom of the abyss before he dies. During his days a cave raider, the only thing that he did with Aki which can possibly build up the said "strong emotional tie" is spending 2 days being trpped in a cave in which they had some dialogue about their dreams and made a brief promise about becoming white whistles together. After that, Tiare enters his missing-in-action state until the end, he only appears a few times with very little dialogue which provides little significance in character building. At the end of the story, before the altar of Ido Front, Tiare appears as the final boss of the main story, revealing his knowledge about life reverberating stones. Then a duel happens between these two, the stronger one shall become the owner and the weaker one shall become the whistle. After losing the duel, Tiare transformed into a life reverberating stone during a brief conversation, no curse applied, no transformation scene, only black screen with subtitles. And Aki makes their last dive with Tiare in thier hand. The BSFiD main story ends.This is all you can get from the advertised BSFiD original story. No character building, no emotional beats, no memorable moments, only a lot of fragments from manga/anime glued into the so called original story and some awkward boss fights with known white whistles. With a 3A price and a top tier anime title and "supervised by Akihoto Tsukushi", this is not what one can expect. I personally take it as a scam.I have 2 more entries on my blacklist:

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that even as a huge fan of the franchise, I waited until this game was on sale for $30. At this price point, i was very pleased with the game. The title for this game could literally be called "Made in Abyss: Inventory Management" and it would perfectly describe this game. I did not mind this however. Past the 1st two layers, it is an art trying to figure out the least amount of equipment you can bring to maximize how much you bring back to the surface with you. It really grabbed the feeling of the abyss when you over extended and were scrambling around just to find food and you couldn't find your way back to the surface.My only real gripe with this game is lack of a post game. After you complete the main story of Deep Abyss, you will be able to get even higher tier weapons and armor....there is just literally nothing to use them on. You should be strong enough to kill literally anything in the game prior to this, and there is no reason to go back with the new gear and 'grind' just because. There is 1, sort of post game boss that I won't spoil here, but I was able to kill it with maybe 2 healing items on my 1st attempt. The other "post game" quest is pretty clearly one that they considered haveing much earlier in the game but just threw it in at the end. Honestly, if they just added some new bosses or quests in an update to let me play with the new gear this game would be 10/10 for the league this game is in (this is not an AAA game).Sound design and aesthetic are amazing (that BGM at the end of the 5th layer). I don't expect any dlc for this, but I'll keep wishing.

_childDocuments_.review: For people who aren't big fans of the series, . Or unless you are an idiot like me who is hoping that if the game does well enough before the eventual discount, the bigwigs with cash who funded the project will figure that maybe people want to play an actually good game based on Made in Abyss.So as you would expect, this is not a good game. It is not the worst game either. It is an okay game that is plagued by jank, questionable design choices and the dullest combat system this side of the Pecos. I like the weight management that you have to take into consideration, as well as planning for expeditions unless you want to be a dumdum like I am who keeps miscalculating how much food you need when going to do several missions in one go, and the trip back home is a race against the clock because there are walls to climb, like 5 units of food left in the system and several Madokajackasses just swoosh right in on you when you are trying to do the world record of climbing the Great Fault just so you can get to an area where you can fast-travel from. Assuming you get food from the rodents you meet and brutally slaughter with what tools you have left.For an Unreal Engine game, the graphics aren't that great either from what I expected, but it isn't the worst I've seen either. The third and fourth layer locations are pretty neat, but it makes me wonder how much better this game could have been.But anyway, my protip is this if you buy the game: Consider the mod that removes the infinitely spawning enemies. Play the game first and see how it is with those in, and then make your decision. I gave up after 20 hours and realized that the game experience had gotten a lot better for me when I removed those damn things.Second protip is: Sneak as much as you can. The enemies have barebones AI and as soon as you crouch slightly, it's like you cease to exist because they have no object permanence, as long as you are not right next to them. The only exception so far to this rule that I've seen are Orb Piercers, because ♥♥♥♥ you they make the rules in the 4th layer. Anyway, as long as you don't kill everything that crosses your path, you save time, your weapons and most importantly, your food that you need to climb back up from the hellhole that is Abyss.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't do actual reviews, but it seems this game is extremely misunderstood. The Hello Abyss "story mode" only lasts around 3 hours and is just a basic tutorial. Is it a worse way to experience the anime's story? Yes, but it's not supposed to be a replacement. Though, it is a dumb decision to make it mandatory. This game is good, but it does have issues. Some monster spawns are unfair or constantly respawn and some tasks in the game do feel redundant, but simply changing up your route and exploring more makes it a lot more enjoyable. The graphics are fine. I don't understand what people were expecting of a 3D made in abyss game. Some Areas actually look outstanding Heaven's Waterfall for example.Combat is basic but enjoyable. You have your basic one two combo with pickaxes or hatches, but using a gun or bow to switch up your play style makes it more dynamic.Exploration is this game's main drive, and it's done very well. The layers are intersected in smaller section that you can traverse through which you have to travel through multiple times. Some People say it's annoying, but I think it's a good way to portray the game. Making a route each mission to get the fastest to a task is actually quite enjoyable.Tldr: This game is pretty good, even though it does suffer from issues, but I think it's unfair how this game is being treated already.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a long review because Made in Abyss deserves my full thoughts and feedback, but I also made a heavily cut down TLDR at the end.First things first: this is a game for fans.Let's not pretend like if this game wasn't about Made in Abyss it would worth anywhere near this price tag. If I'd imagine never hearing about the anime or manga and played this game, I would've stopped playing after an hour to refund this.When you first get into the Abyss you are welcomed by the "PS2 graphics", even on highest options the game really doesn't look like a full price 2022 game by any measurement.Especially annoying are also butterflies and birds which will interrupt you while climbing, which you will do a lot. There doesn't seem to be any timer for them to respawn after you killed them, so you will permanently have to outrun or -climb them or your durability will suffer.Which gets me to the next point. Your weapons have a very limited durability, together with the never-ending enemies I usually had to bring 3, 4 if not more weapons, really bringing your backpack weight to its limits every single expedition. I have heard the devs are working on a patch which should "fix things", but that one has not been released yet so I can't say how much it will actually end up fixing.Now one might say this is all just part it as this is meant to be a survival game and I have seen enough content hidden in the games files to fully believe that this game was supposed to have A LOT more when it comes to survival. Managing sleep and other biological needs on top of just food. Even just food, name cooking, was supposed to be a lot more in-depth with cooking minigames for example. Point is though, as fun as all that sounds, it's not actually in the game. Just good ideas which at some point just got cut from the game.Everything does strongly lead to the feeling that this game is just... unfinished. There's even more to this like certain gameplay things that just don't make sense. One example being the unlocking of "combos" for melee combat, but after every hit you have to wait a little before enemies can take damage again. So if you actually use these combo attacks, all you do is waste your very limited durability. Combat in general is really just existing for the sake of existing, it adds nothing and could be removed from the game entirely without losing anything important. I have also just walked into a dead end with missing visuals for a wall. Food is also completely unbalanced with 3 or 4 different dishes being the only ones you will ever want to use. Which is so sad because there actually is a good variety, but I still would not be able to name you more than 6 dishes at best!And finally, my by far most hated thing about this game. Nanachi barely is part of it. This is Made in Abyss ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, how dare you give me just 20 minutes with my favourite character at best?? At worst you could even just accidentally miss Nanachi entirely! I can very begrudgingly see that this is due to how the story is designed, but this was extremely disappointing. That is the one thing about this game that is completely irredeemable.Oh well. Making it through all the bad things, there are still things making this game worth playing.As you might notice pretty much immediately: The game uses the same (Japanese) VAs. I did not check all of them, but I know for sure that the voices I'd consider important were done my the same people. This does a lot in making it feel familiar and really makes you feel home in the series.I don't know if this game is considered canon outside the main story itself, but it might as well be. People act as you'd expect them to, the creatures of the abyss look and behave as you'd expect them to, the world itself generally does capture the feeling of the abyss.The story also fits well enough. There's nothing really unexpected and I wouldn't want there to be anything unexpected. Anyone who has seen the show will know what's coming when they encounter Ozen or Bondrew. (Side note I appreciated seeing just how toweringly huge Ozen really is. Never really realised that with her 230 cm (7'6) height, the children really don't even go up to her hips.) Thankfully this game has not fallen into the trap of trying to make something totally new with the story and missing the source entirely and that is all I would've asked for anyway.As I started in the very beginning, this game is made for fans. That in mind, it does its job. I do really hope there will be one or two updates to fix the worst, most annoying aspects. Other than that, I do generally recommend the game. Anyone who didn't immediately press buy after hearing about "the Made in Abyss game" and is any hesitant, do yourself a favour and wait a for a sale, then spend the money you saved on things that support this series better. A fair price for this game would be 1/3 of this price, 1/2 at best. Then you'll be able to really enjoy your ~40 hours without worrying you wasted your money.TLDR: This is an okay game which does a decent job appealing to the community who are just grasping for any MiA content they can get their hands on. I do generally recommend it, but the full price is ridiculous. Unless you REALLY want it immediately, wait for a 50% sale.Also, the amount of time with Nanachi is extremely disappointing, just somewhere between 1 and 20 minutes. I hope someone got fired for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not be like me, don't play this game. My god... it started well (after getting trough the Hello Abyss mode, wich is terrible), the first layer is pretty fun overall and i liked to complete it troughly, the game was rough, but it was fine at the moment, the story seemed interesting and i kinda wanted to see what would happen in the deeper levels. But as soon as i got to layer 2, i started to get tempted to just drop the game (and i did for a while)Basically, this game is the gathering sections of monster hunters, except it never gets better, it gets worse, A LOT worse, and the few fights you have are the most basic stuff you can imagine, this can't compete even with some ps1 games fighting systems, Soul Reaver had a better combat system than this. The main problem is that yes, the abyss is relentlessly hard, but not in a fun or fair way. In layer 2 you constantly had to go back and forth narrow bridges, where you would get pushed from by things like... an enemy death animation, a little bug that you killed, and even if you were pretty away from it, it would push you a little, but enough to make you fall and die. Or sometimes it was the lock on system, your character would move on its own while attacking and that would send you flying over the edge. And the thing with this game, is that even when fast travel gets unlocked, you still have to backtrack a LOT in areas that are seriously annoying to traverse.The game also has a horrible habit of making infinitely spawning enemies, and most of the time you just have to run away, because even mini bosses dont have worthy loot most of the time, they'll drop the same thing that the tame beast that you can kill in 1 hit can (only SOMETIMES they'll drop something unique), but the most annoying thing are bugs like the moths, wich infinitely appear when you are climbing and attack you. Now, they do little damage, but they can easily poison you in 1 hit, wich will make your life all the more harder. So you have to attack them to get them off, and that will lower the durability of your weapons... wich is Breath of the Wild levels of bad, but unlike that game, here you don't find weapons around, you have to craft them, and sometimes (like in layer 2) you simply don't find the things you need to craft said weapons! so your only choice is bringing the weapons with you to begin with, wich is annoying too, because your weight limit is VERY tough to deal with, and weapons are some of the most heavy stuff you have. So it's very common that you'll simply run out of weapons and have no way to defend yourself against these infinitely spawning enemies.So you think you'd just be able to run away from all enemies... but you can't, because of the curse of the abyss that wont let you ascend fast. I know this had to be there for accuracy, but its implemented in a super annoying way, when you are climbing and the previously mentioned infinetely spawning moths come to you, you can't just hurry up so you don't have to kill them, you have to stop and wait or else the curse will trigger, so you have no choice but killing them, and again, i can't stress this enough... weapons can hit like, 15 times before they break, even these small moths are a heavy toll to pay.So that was hard enough, but i pushed trough, i made it to the third layer and... yeah, i just couldn't keep going. In the third layer, first, those moths get replaced by 1 hit kill minibosses that can easily snipe you when you are trying to climb and kill you in one shot (AND AGAIN, remember you can't climb too fast or you'll get hit by the curse, so you are forced to stop ascending. You can try jumping to the sides to dodge, but ALSO you have to deal with the stamina meter, and in the third layer the sections you have to climb are VERY large), and to top it of, when you get inside the caves in that layer, they are ABSOLUTELY PITCH DARK. You seriously can't see anything at all, i found myself just pushing myself to the walls and looking at the horrendously confusing mini map trying to make my way trough. It's terrible, and to make matters worse! you usually have a light in your helmet, that isn't great, but would have helped a bit in this damn place, but guess what? in preparation to the third layer, i went above and beyond and made a relic armor that was the best i could access at the moment, i had to grind a lot, fish a lot and make some of the most annoying backtracks, but i made it, i had my relic armor and i was ready for layer 3 and then... turns out the relic helmet is the first (and so far only) helmet without a light in the game! so yeah, i was pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ here. There were torches to be made, but i had no idea i would run into such a dark place, and boy... backtracking out of that place was impossible due to the previously mentioned minibosses that attack you while climbing.So i just uninstalled, this was no fun, i regret not seeing the whole game trough, i would have liked to see where the story was going, but my god... this was just too bad, the physics were killing me, the saves are limited to items you need to craft, and backtracking was just too awful... i do not recommend this at all, even if you are a series fan.

_childDocuments_.review: i like it but i would wait until it's on sale. playing the "hello abyss" mode almost turned me off of the game, but trudging through it was worth it for the "deep in abyss" mode on the other side of all of that, which is way more interesting and fun compared to the "hello abyss" mode. that mode is the "main course" and gives you a lot more freedom to explore the abyss however you want, and there's lots of fun progression, a skill tree, crafting recipes... i find it pretty fun! it's definitely very casual though -- which isn't a bad thing.there's a couple bugs here and there but nothing that felt game breaking to me; also, using a controller doesn't seem to swap the on-screen icons for controls so i've found myself failing a couple of the randomized QTE. some mechanics can be unusual to learn at first but once you get the hang of them your experience in the abyss is a lot smoother (like buying lots of ropes because they are not permanent fixtures)all in all, i do enjoy it, but i would heavily suggest waiting until it's on sale unless you've got money to burn. $60 is not deserving of the quality of the game (especially since the world's visuals are kinda...lackluster, albeit the first layer can be pretty at times) -- but it's the exact kind of quality concern you would be familiar with if you've bought games that use anime or movie IPs in the past.(footnote: i have an unhealthy obsession with the bunny)

_childDocuments_.review: Sad I have to say this, but the game is a disservice to its source material. The music is alright, if forgettable. The character design is pretty neat, but the environmental art and backgrounds look too simplistic. Perhaps that has to do with console restrictions. The control scheme however is horrible and unfixable if you don't use a controller. The default keybindings were unusuable for me and you seemingly cannot bind mouse buttons, which is something i for the life of me can't understand. Having to rewire my brain to just be able to play is already a serious negative, but i eventually got used to it because I wanted to see what waited for me. Or maybe I'm a masochist.What really is the biggest shame though is the introductory mode called "Hello Abyss". I have no idea what they were thinking locking the full game behind a surface level recreation of the show. A bad one at that. You are railroaded down a series of events from the first episodes of season one, often altered to fit the limitations of the game design. You are locked out of most survival, crafting and open world elements and effectively forced to play a 3-5 hour tutorial without actually being taught anything that isn't taught to you in what i would call the actual game. Enjoy watching Reg get stuck on the terrain or uselessly stand around, however. Neither does he have particularly great pathing nor any climbing animation, which means he will do whatever while you climb, appearing out of nowhere behind you once you're past obstacles he cannot traverse. Man, they really did my boy dirty. Maybe he never got over having that stick...well, nevermind. I don't know if this behaviour extends to the other characters from the main game mode since I haven't gotten very far in it yet. But it wouldn't surprise me.Once you've managed to grind through Hello Abyss, you are finally allowed to play "Deep in Abyss", the "actual" game. You get to design your own character with some nice, if few, customisation options. Then you are thrown into the game amongst a group of fellow apprentices into the world of Orth. You get to take quests, buy and sell stuff and apparently engage in an original story. I can't tell for sure, because I haven't gotten very far in. To tell the truth, while this mode seems to already be worlds better than what came before, my motivation has already been sucked away by the mandatory retelling of season one. And even without that there might just be an alright game waiting for me, certainly not a masterpiece.In short: Not worth it even if you are a diehard fan of the show/manga. And good luck if you don't own a controller. Don't drop the asking price of 60 Euros or whatever your regional equivalent is on this. Wait for a considerable discount, and pray to Ozen that they abandon forcing you to play Hello Abyss.

_childDocuments_.review: Had this on my wishlist for a long time and always wondered how a video game in this anime setting would be like? Don't let the cute art style fool you, this game is a brutal, violent, survival game. You have to gather, craft and manage your inventory and be prepared for any situation or else you die in cruel various ways. Some of which are animated and you get to see your character die in horrible ways.There are some bad parts of this game in its current state.This is a switch game with low budget, so expect alot of jank. I remapped the controls of keyboard and endured it just fine. On the pc the quick time events are on keyboard even if you have a controller plugged in. _childDocuments_.review: There are two modes; Hello Abyss and Deep In Abyss.Hello Abyss: Incredibly faithful to the original anime in the way the characters are presented, the styles, the actions are almost frame for frame perfectly replicated with the 3D models and the architecture of the abyss is incredible! You play an overall weaker character but it is a great way to learn some of the major mechanics you are going to be using within the Abyss on Deep In Abyss mode. Also Riko can die in many exciting and unique ways, which is a unique and nice touch to really drive home the gritty reality of the abyss.The story follows up to about halfway through the first series of the anime where they descend into the vertical wall. So as it stands don't go into this expecting to get the full series of the anime in the game.HOWEVERDeep In Abyss: You control your own character and take them through a harsh, gritty reality that is unforgiving from the outset. You start out on your first dive, weaker than even Riko, and from there you spend your time growing, completing quests and gaining experience as a delver. You will easily surpass Riko after a few dives. With a story supervised by Akihito themselves, you know it's going to be a fantastic and brutal story that doesn't hold back.Controls: Both keyboard and PS5 controller are a joy to play with. It claims to have partial controller support but in reality the controller support is 100% there and is not a problem at all.Gameplay: Crafting, surviving, trying to work through the curse of the abyss, and reach the bottom of the netherworld. All enjoyable as you try and get past some incredibly dangerous and scary monsters. There is a large amount of inventory management in the early game which seems like it will become a bit easier as a skill allows you to carry a bit more. Just try not to go up too fast or you will be risking your life in unnecessary situations that would be child's play otherwise.Graphics: There has been some mention of the graphics not being "the best", but I personally enjoy them as they are VERY close, if not an exact copy in some areas of the anime, and really gives a lot of depth and feel. I enjoy it thoroughly as it's like I'm playing the anime, and that's what I came here for.Sound: A very important part of the abyss, sound has been crafted very well, from the game's OST, the songs, the ambience around you, and having the original VAs reprise their roles for ENG and JP is truly a delight. Every line I have encountered is voiced and it truly adds a feel to the game which makes it more exciting.Lore: There are little bits of bonus info in the game that explore bits of lore here and there that really add to the knowledge gained in the anime and manga, so if you want get as much knowledge as possible the game is a must.Replayability: The Abyss itself is a great replayable device, but there are lots of secrets hidden everywhere, but no "collect these golden eggs to get X" or "Korok Seeds" item mechanic, which is a boon, but also a shame because finding broken mail balloons could have been a chance to add in a few bits of extra lore by being able to read old delver's stories and could have just made the abyss itself feel more alive.Conclusion: This game tries very hard to master many different areas of the game, and does well. While there is less from the Hello Abyss mode as originally expected, it's a tutorial, and Spike Chunsoft has clearly focused 100% around the quality of the game, and it shows in many ways. There are tiny bugs that in all honesty should be expected based on the terrain of the abyss.Score: A resounding 9/10 Crying, Broken and Totally Helpless Children.It's brilliant, and beautifully crafted. There's a hope that there might be some DLC in the future, but even without it the game is a gem. I truly am enjoying the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't worth this price. (90 CN). As a title like "Made in Abyss", people expect the vast and huge endless adventures that the anime gave but this game doesn't provide that, hence the negative reviews and mixed total ratings. Let me get these few things out of the way:The story of this game is from the first season of "Made in Abyss" and it was executed perfectly. They kept you enthralled on going down into the depths for the story and to see out Riko's story. The game mechanics isn't far off from the realistic approach and kept you feeling human by having these survival features like food and crafting. I enjoyed this very much and was one of the reasons why I even bought this game.The second portion of this game I found just as entertaining as the story, if not even more. It's all about what its like to be a Red Whistle, the progress of gaining experience and what its like to be cave raider. It's fun, it has the basic RPG features. However that's all it really gave the player. Go fetch like quests to gain EXP to get skills on the small but useful skill tree. In conclusion, it's not for everyone and the price is WAY high for what you get. People's expectations were high with that title "MADE IN ABYSS, they wanted more but got a predictable RPG game. But for me I don't mind it. I LOVE this anime and game itself. It's so cool to view the perspective that Riko had in the anime and manga. To play it is such a cool experience, seeing the creatures, layers, relics, items, and visuals. Put that all together and for me its doable, playable and dare I say entertaining. Just please be considerate about the price, would you like to walk Riko's path in this cool interactive anime? See all the iconic characters in season 1 all for 90 (CN) dollars? It's quite obvious for me and I didn't even hesitate when the game came out. I wanted that and I'm a satisfied customer.     But that's just me.

_childDocuments_.review: I may change my opinion if I decide to pick the game up at a later date, but as of right now I have no interest in playing further. I love the Made in Abyss series, but this game doesn't do it much justice.I'll start off with the good; the artstyle is very fitting for the series. It's simplistic, but that's by no means a bad thing, as the don't necessarily need to be insane for this type of game. The music is also nice, a bit repetitive in the orphanage/menus, but that can be overlooked, Spike Chunsoft tends to have that sort of issue with many of their games.My main gripe is with the janky ass PC control scheme, you're able to rebind most of the overworld controls, but the menu scheme is utterly impossible for me to get used to, and considering how much time is spent in menus, it just drills into my brain how unintuitive the controls are, like who in their right mind binds L/R navigation to L-SHIFT and L-CTRL?? Not to mention space being the return key. Though Spike Chunsoft have a pretty abysmal track record with terrible control schemes I feel.The other thing i have a problem with is the linearity of the relic collection, at least in the "Hello Abyss" mode, as each relic is marked on your map, and you NEED to collect all of them to progress to the next area. This makes it feel less like i'm a cave raider exploring the abyss and more like a stupid little baby who can't do anything without their hand being held all the way. Maybe "Deep in Abyss" is different, so take my opinion with a grain of salt, since i just can't bring myself to play any more as of right now, but these are just my two cents from what i've played.

_childDocuments_.review: A tricky recommend, but if you love the series then you know exactly what level of punishment and suffering to expect, and you'll get it.It was tough to stick with, the biggest issue is the interface, menu upon menu with frustrating keybindings and you need to spend a huge amount of time in said menus.  The introduction mode is semi-necessary for the game mechanics and is a nice recap of some of the series but is kinda dull to play.Getting into the meat of it, the first few hours are not very engaging and you'll die a lot to basically everything, the controls are clunky, the mechanics are oppressive, the game doesn't seem that fun, and losing progress is frustrating.  Yet, I stuck with it, mostly due to a friend also playing at the same time and story-swapping made everything more engaging. Before long I've cranked up tens of hours and really immersed in how trivial the early stages feel while on the edge of my seat spending hours trying to make it home after a very deep dive.It's still an awkward clunky mess as a game, quite a few bugs to be seen, but it's made VERY well within the themes of the show, the character models and JP voice work are on point, they've really given each layer their own unique feelings of terror and progression is both very slow, makes very little change, but all the difference at the same time.  Weight is the most frustrating mechanic but it's fun that it gives you plenty of things to consider and balance that you won't realise you need to until later. Rather than a lot all at once, which speaks to some good game decisions in there.They also put far far TOO much love into the different ways to suffer, the death animations are brutal, the cherry on the cake is the later curse consequences though, excellently implemented!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically like writing negative reviews, but the fact this came out from a beloved franchise, and was so hyped up only to have a mixed rating hours after release speaks for itself. TLDR:The anime was beloved for it's artstyle and visuals, which as you can tell from the trailers is not at all reproduced, but I was willing to overlook that. what I was unwilling to overlook was the gameplay. This game feels unfinished, and clunky in almost every aspect. I was really looking forward to this and am incredibly disappointed. Don't waste your money on this triple A cashgrab game for $60 when this is significantly worse than any good indie game. I refunded the game, so I don't know what's in the second story (you have to complete the reg/riko story first), and I don't know how deep the game goes into (edit: apparenttly the first mode only goes until ozen, so not very far)controls:The first thing I noticed going into this game was that despite me using a controller it only displays the keyboard controls on screen. There is no way to change this. Also when you change your controls it seems inconsistent on what it changes (for example I mapped crouch from a to left stick press, and warping from place to place was changed with it, but menu navigation was still a) This is only mildly annoying though, or it would be if it wasn't for quick events.quick events:The way the game incorporates you into the story is through quick events in it's many animated scenes is through quick time events. This was really frustrating on controller because it flashed your keyboard controls, and I don't even know if the corresponding buttons on the controller even work, I found myself dropping my controller and rushing to my keyboard to press a single button before coming back to my controller. Additionally, it feels really lazy to have QTE in an action exploration game. The premise was to play through the experience, but when every major scene is just a cutscene with a QTE or a visual novel, it doesn't feel great.exploration:Not all games need to be openworld, but this one really needed to be, the entire premise is exploration of an unknown world, so when I see loadingzones every few minutes that cost your resources to traverse through it disappoints me, and it isn't as if this was done for memory issues, it uses ps2 graphics and has incredibly small areas. On top of this the world (at least in the first mode) is incredibly linear, to the point where if you try to enter loading zones you're not supposed to you're simply not allowed.Curse of the abyss:The ENTIRE gimmick of the franchise is belittled into a waiting mechanic in this game. not only are you required to ascend multiple times, whenever you do, your screen gets hazy and you have to wait for it to go away or lose half of your hunger.  This makes the game feel even more slow, while also essentially trivializing the ascent.inventory:Oh god, why? There is a cap on the amount of weight you can carry before you lose your ability to use items, sprint, climb and many other things. This doesn't sound bad in concept but effectively it means that not only are you throwing away items regularly which never feels good, but since you can't tell how close you are to that limit, you are almost certain to have moments where mid-climb you collect something, reach that limit, and fall to your death, or mid combat collect something, and fall to your death. etc. I even had a scene where I was told to run from the crimson splitjaw at the beginning and I was just waddling away unable to open my inventory in that moment to throw something away to move faster.Combat:The combat is really clunky. I found myself regularly unequiping and reequiping my weapon just to be able to use it, and even when I could, you only have a standard attack. It's really easy to get stunlocked in place by multiple little enemies and just die unable to get away because you can't roll past them. I found myself just relying on reg to kill most things for me.Reg:I was under the assumption that you'd get to switch between reg and riko, this is not the case. Reg is just an npc that runs around attacking things, and dies over and over again. Luckily there's no consequences for him dying, but it feels so underwhelming, to the extent that I think it'd be better if he just wasn't there at all. He also get stuck on rocks just trying to follow you.Hunger/Stamina:The hunger system is something I would want in this game in concept, but it just feels tedious, the only purpose of it is to give you a consequence for ascending in losing it. when it's empty you lose your stamina. Stamina really only matters for sprinting and climbing, meaning that it again is tedious. Additionally, unlike other games, when you run out of stamina, you stop completely in place for a few seconds, making you question if it would have been faster to walk.Death:if you die you simply restart the area you're in. Not a very big consequence, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. I however got to a point because of being stunlocked multiple times that being annoyed by restarting and losing my progress.Monster Dex:You can spy on creatures you see to add them to the monster dex, assuming reg doesn't kill them while you're scanning them. It seemingly has no purpose and only tells you what layer they're on, despite you leaving the layer to never come back. I might have missed something on this one.Pros:The story, while mostly being the anime again, does have some new content, with new creatures, and new areas to explore. If you're really into the world and can overlook all of the glaring negatives this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: So i've completed the "Hello Abyss" story line arc - also to be considered the tutorial imo.I'll say that so far as a videogame, not too impressed. I picked this up because I am a big fan of the anime. Unfortunately playing through the brunt of the main story there does not appear to be any extreme sexual content, even to the level of the source material, unlike others in the genre, and the price point is fairly steep too. I would moderately recommend the game if you enjoy the MiA source material or are a fan of other classic ryonage.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This sandbox's greatest flaw is the ambition left unfulfilled. Best played blind, with infinite mob patch, without using fast travel. Also only worth maybe $40 maximum. The game is overall a very "fun" experience. Take that statement with a grain of salt, as progression, scaling, crafting, and difficulty are completely busted. The first and last third of the game are actually quite easy, with the middle section having a ridiculous difficulty spike (mainly due to environmental factors). Crafting has no linearity or direct progression whatsoever (excepting some weapons and items), and you can clearly tell they had planned on more materials being available. The Hello mode acts only as a extended tutorial, and bad retelling of the source material. The Deep in Abyss mode, seems slightly more original as an almost direct rehashing of the original story with common anime tropes. Additionally, the only interaction you have with Riko and Reg is playing the same mission, twice, almost identically, besides which character you run into first. In fact, the only truly fleshed out feeling part of the game is the first 2 layers in the Deep in Abyss mode, these make up the peak of the experience. The rest feels like they've simply stretched those concepts to reach the fifth layer, but in an unwilling fashion. There are clear artifacts from ideas Chunsoft never managed to implement. The companion system is utterly broken, and dialogue in the game alludes to a much greater depth that was simply truncated and left in a quarter-finished state at best. Crafting supplies work in this same fashion with end game items being referenced as needing more complex materials, but still taking the older items. Even in the advertised screenshots you can see multiple alluded systems that were never implemented: A compass, a hunger/thirst system, a fatigue/sleeping system, temperature management, a mount(?), and a clock. The game doesnt even have the clock. If the game had managed to fulfill these ambitions, it would not only be the greatest anime-game adaptation ever, but also probably game of the decade. Instead, now I'm left hopeless this is the best game adaptation we'll get and its a sad shadow of what it could have beenEssentially you need to view this product in a different fashion. This is not a "game" per-se, its a sandbox. It does not provide anything outside of the source material, so if you hoped the game would get you more insight stop that now. What it does do and does excellently is build a world for you to explore and goof off in. It also conveys the brutality of the abyss in a very compelling way. However, the gameplay feels a disconnection from the actual expected feeling of exploration so here's some advice on how to best enjoy this sandbox:Chunsoft decided to inhibit exploration by adding a an infinite stream of enemies based on time spent in a level. Patch this out. Additionally, while the fast travel does very much help cut down on the unnecessary bloat feeling, it detracts from the adventure and should only be used sparingly. Some complaints might be made about the possibility of softlocking, and while this is true, the only real reprehensible softlocks are after the game autosaves you into a scripted encounter. Standing there, staring at a turtle, you must return to your last manual save praying it was recent. Guides help to avoid this, but also detract from the exploratory aspect so also use sparingly. Save often, watch your equipment, and just take your time and explore.Overall, I could say I had fun, quite a decent amount. Hello Abyss mode lasted about 3 hours, and the Deep mode up until white whistle about 27. There is no endgame context except grinding, so experiences may very on length. Is this product worth $60? Absolutely not. The product is definitely worth it around $30 as long as you dont expect the game to be much more than an a beautifully brutal sandbox.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game, but it's begging for a more polished sequel. My thoughts on the mangaka's uncomfortable treatment of child characters notwithstanding, this game captures the feel of the anime perfectly and fleshes out what little we've seen of some layers within the Abyss. Gameplay is serviceable, but seeing as I *want* more of it, I'm confident that a few tweaks to the Deep in Abyss mode formula would make it stellar. Fantastic sense of atmosphere, coherent / interconnected gameplay systems, and a lot of resource management fun to be had.The worst I can say is that expeditions have to planned out *perfectly* before you set foot in the Abyss to minimize annoyance. Note that I said "annoyance" and not difficulty, because frankly, the game's difficulty flatlines once you memorize all the petty tricks its level design throws at you. You climbed down a wall and forgot to set up a rope? Well time to throw your character off a cliff and restart! Oh! You forgot to bring salt, can't harvest any in the abyss, and entered a zone shortly before running out of hunger? Better restart the expedition in its entirety! This game is full of that stuff.Unfortunately, I want to reach the bottom too much to give up, so I'll keep persevering.

_childDocuments_.review: If you watched the anime more than once and really enjoyed it, you will enjoy this game.Disclaimer:  The Riko/Reg portion is basically a long tutorial.  The character creator mode is where the full game actually is.Combat:  Good - Relatively simple hack&slash combat.  It can have issues with awkward hitboxes but the lock on targeting system helps make it alot less frustrating than other similar games.Audio:  Very Good - The music matches the mood and keeps the feel of the show.  The new JP voice talent (didn't listen to the English VAs) does a good job matching in with the established characters.  There are a few audio clips that lack diversity in the gameplay and can get repetitive but it isn't as glaring as I've seen in other titles.Visuals:  Very Good - Though it isn't going to win industry awards for it's models, almost everything about it fits the show extremely well for style.  I was impressed with how little clipping I see and the models, even at range, rarely glitch visually.AI:  Okay - The ally and enemy AI have a hard time.  They will occasionally get stuck on terrain and they won't always be able to track your character well.  It's really the only objective flaw I'd point to for them to fix.Overall Gameplay:  Very Good - Setting aside the Riko/Reg portion (which only has limited parts of the game's system open to it), there is alot to enjoy.  The game-play cycle of dive and return feels solidly fun.  The overlapping progression systems allow for growth in free-play adventuring while keeping it connected to "story" questing for bigger progression moments.  Managing inventory on the journey, hunger/fatigue, and planning for the inevitably harder return ascent provides genuine challenge.Bias:  I will tell you, I tried to be as objective as I could in writing this.  However, I didn't realize just how much I would enjoy this game until I got a good way into it.  Now if you'll excuse me, I'm off to 100% this thing.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was taken aback by the jankiness, it's definitely a niche game made on a budget for a specific audience. Some of the regional price differences are also pretty absurd. Over time it has won me over.The initial tutorial campaign is not very good, as it doesn't explain things very well, highlights the screwy follower AI a lot, and does little to prepare you for the main course. It's not very engaging and doesn't bother completing the storyline. Unfortunately, it leaves you ill-prepared for the main game as you are left clueless to a lot of mechanics and their importance.Once you get past that and start figuring things out, it's pretty chill. Skill point upgrades help alleviate the initially limited backpack carry weight, torches can be used to ward off a lot of hostile fauna, and it is decently challenging and paced. The intent of the game is NOT to just fight everything you see, but carefully choose your fights to preserve items and move through areas efficiently. As you progress, you get some fast-travel options too. It stays fairly true to the source material.Graphics range from serviceable to somewhat ugly in certain biomes, it's honestly closer to 2000s console games than 2020s ones at points. Sounds could have more variety, but a lot of the music is okay if not particularly memorable. UI is made for consoles, if you're used to it it's okay, but nothing exceptional.Overall it is a middling game and unintentionally hostile by not explaining well how anything works. If you can figure it out, it gets a lot better. It reminds me a lot of older Japanese games, if you enjoy that particular genre of grindy RPGs it makes a lot more sense and is more tolerable. Best played with a gamepad of some kind.
