_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'm gonna start with DON'T GET THIS IF YOU ARE NO FAN!The game has 2 sides right off the bat;1. The prologue, where u played as Riko with Reg as your companion.2. The main game, where u create a character of ur own.So, with that being said, I'm gonna review both.1. The Riko & Reg is basically a prologue, to introduce and teach you about the mechanic, combat and gameplay of how the game should be played. It is based on the anime where Riko and Reg dived the Abyss down into the 2nd layer and met Ozen. Now, pay in mind, the anime itself is GORE. And the game also similar. Just think of it similar to other souls-like game, u DO NOT ENGAGE every single enemy coming at you. U will die. Besides in the anime, Riko & Reg mostly just run away every time they see monster. Reg cannot fire his arm cannon, Incinerator as freely, EXACTLY LIKE IN ANIME. So don't expect u can blast it all the time. The prologue ended when Riko & Reg finished their training given by Ozen where they then dive into the 3rd layer.2. I just recently reached 2nd layer after 10+ hours in playing. I take my time by exploring, crafting, cooking, etc. Basically, if u ever played Outward, Skyrim, Witcher, Dark Souls, and the likes, well this game is not much different. I actually got so hooked up, because this game is so related to the anime where we're no superhuman or superheroes. We don't have the shout like in skyrim nor we can cast sign like in witcher. U are a teen who have enough courage to challenge the Abyss that filled with monsters, equipped mostly ur guts. Tread carefully. Do what the prologue taught u. Don't engage every single enemies and run if u have to. Enemies spawn immediately, but that doesn't mean they will chase u down everywhere if u run away. U can duck to evade their alert. With each step, the curse of the Abyss is stalking u in every corner. U need to craft weapons from looting dead monsters or excavating the rocks. U have to cook to fill the fullness level. Weapons have durability, so watch out for that too. SAVE UR GAME! It is crucial to save often, cuz u don't know how things gonna turn. Graphics:Let's NOT compare to the current AAA titles. Pay in mind, this is an anime game and they have their own style. Which, IMO it is actually very good and much better compared to the anime itself.Sound:Can be improved, but overall not that disappointing. Music is calm and chilling in the orphanage, in combat is very tense.Gameplay:Mind the curse. It's everywhere. LITERALLY. But can be avoided by simply running away or ducking or eating food.Combat:Enemies adjust with how far u go. The deeper u are, the more challenging the monsters are, just like how it is stated in the lore. U can always run away if u wanna skip them (just like in other games), unless it's a quest.Mechanic:Not much different than other RPGs or souls-like game. U need to loot, craft weapons, cook, heal, etc.VERDICT: Overall the game actually very enjoyable. I'm gonna continue my journey to become a White Whistle! Will update my review once I'm finished the game, maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: I love MarulkPlease keep in mind before reading the actual review that I got this game for around 18~ US dollars due to regional pricing difference, and my first playthrough is done with two helpful mods. The mods I used are Beardmo's lore friendly skill and description (fixes inaccurate translations), and Heatnixx's curse rebalancing (basically improves the curse system). I've fully completed everything in the game aside from insignificant side quests with no story from the , and admittedly, there are some parts here and there during the early game which feels a little tedious, but after that the game becomes really enjoyable until the end. It is worth noting that this game can be very punishing and brutal on the player if one were to get too careless, so it might not be the best game for people who are looking for a very casual experience. While the overall experience is enjoyable, the combat system has one major bug, which sometimes cause rapid consecutive hit to not deal damage, so don't expect too much from combat in this game. Allied NPCs also tend to do funny things at times due to how their AIs work. Despite that, the game really shines when it comes to exploration and just immersing in the abyss. You are free to roam inside it and do as you please whilst being mindful enough to make your next move. In other words, the game becomes extra enjoyable if you are patient, and inversely so if you wish to rush in without thinking, as aforementioned, the game can be very punishing. You'll also learn more tricks such as  here and there as you become more familiar with the game, enhancing your ability to explore even further. As for the graphics, they are simple yet captures the beauty and the theme of the game perfectly, so you won't even need a high-spec computer to even run the game! Unless you want to put on the best shadows graphic setting that is, but the second best setting still looks nearly as good without killing your fps. In conclusion, the game is very appealing if you are someone who wish to explore a mysterious world of the abyss and is willing to bide their time doing so while not expecting too much from the combat system, and thus, I recommend this game (with mods) for people who are interested and have similar regional pricing. P.S. This game is even more enjoyable if you just so happen to be a masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up: if you like Made in Abyss, easily 4/5, if you have never heard of it, 3/5 or lower with skill issues. They left a lot out and phoned the ending in, but the Abyss is cool and exploring is fun. I write a lot so I know most won't read all this.I'm a fan of the series and was waiting on this game a long time. I had high hopes for it and enough of them were met that I gladly gave around 100 hours of play. My initial impression was phenomenal, tho by the time I felt like it was finished my opinion had dropped. Still, it's one of the few games I 100%, and achievements aside I honestly sought out a very deep exploration of the game chasing unknown codex entries just for the sake of knowing.[Atmosphere] The netherworld is stunning and mystifying, horrifying as it is beautiful. You travel deeper and deeper and feel like you can but barely see the edge of understanding. Stopping simply to observe so often, taking in vistas and primeval creatures, attempting to trace a path further or understand what exactly the obstacle was. Invited often to have questions about what you're witnessing, from "Where have I gone?" to "What danger am I in?" and the most intoxicating to me was wondering when discretion should temper curiosity. I got to see basically all the death animations... the game has a disarmingly clean and cute style. The first fall to my death was a shock, and the brutality is waiting, always. A deadly serious world that at once does not want you in it but tempts terribly. [Gameplay Loop]Play is nicely broken into downtime and time down there. First journeys, into the beginning of the game, into new areas, into new layers, toward new goals, will cause pause from the sudden onset of risk against reward. Harsh experiences will inform what equipment is missing, and how terribly you miss it. Gain some veteran insight only to go to the next layer and face down bewilderment, anxiety, and especially lethal greed all anew. I remember the first full traverse of the second layer as a harrowing firewalk and then a breathlessness as I reached the awe-some last area and turned back from pure fear. Bravery got me to the terrifying third layer, and darkness and hurry caused me to get lost... for three hours. When I resurfaced, the disbelief after that trial had my love for the game blossom. The setting labels adventures into the Abyss as "dives" and that word is a wondrous mix of choking pressure balanced by the rewards of breath and wonder. Personally, I never truly wanted for the resources to go down, just the resources to go further. [Execution] (Spoilers)With such atmosphere it's so strange that the game struggles with its own motive of getting you to play. Genuinely, exploration is reward itself. Just seeing the Abyss invites you to explore it, and not seeing the bottom tempts you to try and find it. This doesn't require "quests" but the game most definitely does give those to you. There is a line of a main story, scattered side quests, and a slew of filler tasks like digging or killing an arbitrary number of times which give you experience for levels for skill points. Side stories are character related, usually helping someone in a slight pinch or in horrible danger. The main story is concerned first with your whistle rank and how to rise to the top, and then shifts to your more personal adventure on your way to the deepest point you can reach. The people around you are above average to annoying. The more main a character is to the source material, the better they are to experience in game, but if you aren't familiar they will just be slight standouts. I never cared for the people as much as I cared about the Abyss itself. The finale is underwhelming and predictable.[Completion] (Very Spoilers)This game is not finished. Around the midpoint, I started to feel it. There are parts the game acts like are there, or should be there, and are not. Mechanics, stories, and places. A bad strike is survival gameplay. The third layer extreme temperatures, and equipment can be cold weather, but there's no mechanic in place. Don't fall and don't get eat and don't forget to eat, survival is not an issue in this survival-themed game. The first third of the plot is dense with attention, like setting the world up, illustrating how cave raiders gain real experience from novice to veteran, and making connections between you and your character and who and what they know. This becomes noticeably flimsy as the game goes on. Your fellow orphans are dear at first, but later forgotten except as quest vehicles...  It was shallow and forgettable. A stain on the atmosphere is that by the fourth layer, parts of the world begin lacking. Lasers that you can redirect, that would be puzzles, but aren't. From one dive to the next, an area had a different layout, another has monsters as platforms to different places. Interesting touches that showed the development knew how to make it more than it is. The worst was Ido Front. Much of the game is natural with sparse ruins, but here is a ruined city! I desperately wanted to explore, but it is just two hallways and a boss platform. I was upset. [You take your Last Dive? It goes nowhere. There is no sixth layer, just clear data. I played a little more, but I was let down. Would that I could see what this game was meant to be.The are glitches, like characters that won't shut up when they dive with you, or monsters that spawn immediately off screen and infinitely so. But, there are mods. Or, you can mute the voice volume and not kill everything that moves.If you aren't selective with what you collect, you will spend a lot of time pausing and discarding, and that process is clunky.There are a lot of food recipes, and few of them are useful. There are a lot of armors, and most are useful for balancing defense with weight. Money was never ever a barrier. Hanging on to relics for later use was.Nanachi The cutest character is Marulk.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a meta comment. It's hilarious that steam lets people review a product that they haven't even expired the refund window for, isn't it? Let alone the fact that most people seem to complete the Riko compaign and bail. Losers.Second, my opinion. The game is fantastic, though not without its issues, and its difficulty is rather unforgiving and if not for the per-area autosave this would be irredeemable, yet as you get into the custom character campaign the world of the abyss truly and in full actuality opens up to you. The journey is long and hard, and beyond the beaten path is little in the way of money, but the adventure you take every time you step into the abyss is never less daunting so far, nor is it something to take lightly. The repetition is expected, and the way the curse works is fine if you aren't stupid enough to vibrate like a hyperactive idiot expecting nothing to happen. As you progress further in the game your movement becomes more fluid and you unlock more abilities which allow you to progress further and further, easier and easier with each step. But make no mistake, there are negative things about this game like the constantly respawning mob harassment, or how it forces you to use up durability on all of your weapons with seemingly no alternative way to make them leave you be.The way the world is crafted is like an old monster hunter map partition rather than open world, and this restriction has given them a staggering amount of focus in crafting each and every area to be incredible in detail and feel. The abyss truly feel more and more terrifying and surprising every time you go deeper, and my only real complaint is that I will never be able to experience this for the first time again. It's hard with no hand holding, like games should be, with a beautiful design and aesthetic that serves the world of Made In Abyss justice, truly and fully. I can't wait for my next dive.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the manga and anime so I am enjoying it for the most part. Give a quick run downGame is split into 2 halves, the quick run through of the anime which acts like a tutorial and then where you get to be a character and go cave raiding. Its basically cave raiding simulator, which I have found fun.Regardless of if you are a fan or not, deffo worth waiting till its on sale. Really no point for the price it is. My review is going to be based mainly on the second part, the own character thing which will cover some aspects of the first, but not all, but I think thats more important for the meat of it. Also, I have only reached the second level, so I dunno how much of what I say changes further onPros-Fun exploration. The levels are interesting to explore, along with creatures there to fight and research/-crafting is wide range as well as skills allowing to unlock more. I do have to say though they are blocked via whistle level which can be a lil annoying if you havn't progressed the story enough to unlock them. -Easy grinding mechanic to gain money and skills. Easy guild quests and also relic selling meant I got pretty high up in level and money without having to worry about stuff.-Stealth can allow it easier to avoid conflict, especially when you are only trying to get from one place to another and weapons are low.-Characters. For the most part, I like them, I enjoy having them around and gives a lil bit more immersion to the game.Cons-Enemy spawning when climbing/standing still. Mainly this happens when you are trying to recover from the curse of the abyss. Its managable but rather annoying when 2/3 spawns each time that you are there, with no choice but to wait.-The negative curse design. If you are constantly going up and down, it seems to tally it, so even if you have gone up one meter, if you have been going up like that for a while, you will be hit with the curse and have to stop before progressing. This can be very difficult to do on bumpy terrain which have you doing this.-Fight locking. This happened recently but I was suddenly in a fight with some mobs and all my weapons broke. I had no way of crafting replacements. I had not intended to suddenly be in that situation, so I had to give up as there was nothing that could be done.Nit picks-Where is the quest? Sometimes, they don't tell you where the quest is and you are expected to either know where abouts it is, or aimlessly wonder until you find it. For those who want to progress, I can imagine it can be annoying, but I rather enjoyed stumbling on them.-The map is not entirely useful. With the quest markings not really showing until you are in the area itself, but also figuring out how you are meant to go down the layers or what areas lead to where. -NPC don't shut up. If you have an NPC following you on one of your cave raids, they are saying the same 3 lines over and over again, with about 5 seconds apart at the longest.-Storage. Granted, as you level up your ability to carry more increases, but this feels like its just to carry the weight of your newer higher level equipment, so in the end, you still are only left with a small size to carry everything.Final thoughtsDespite all the bad things I have said, I am still enjoying the game and have spent hours playing it, just generally being a cave raider and wondering around exploring, getting data on the creatures and plants that are down there as well as the story that the creators are trying to tell. But unless you enjoy the original content this game is based on, I think you may struggle with it a lil with all the negatives that it has. It's only because I am a fan that I continue to play and enjoy it. So my recommended is with huge *. I recommend it because i have a bias to liking the original content, so will continue to play and enjoy despite the issues. Oh and quick tip for those getting it. First half of the game, just do whatever the missions tell you to do. Its not for exploring or doing, your just playing out the first bit of the anime.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* If you're a fan of the show, you'll LOVE everything about the game. Very faithful, and so great to see a game that's actually a worthy counterpart to the movie/show it came from.* The environments are amazing. I cannot stress this enough. So many areas I entered were so breathtaking, even despite the.. less than stellar graphics. Actually, the design as a whole. The areas, the enemies, all of it of course a testament to Akihito Tsukushi's crazy creativity.* Feedback loop is pretty nice. Dive, level up, dive deeper, level up more, etc. The pacing is generally pretty good, with only a few parts feeling a bit slow.* The game autosaves at the beginning of every floor (and at certain key moments), which is REALLY nice. Because you'll be dying a lot. WARNING: This also contributes to softlocks (more in the Cons), so be careful, and always carry a balloon or two to counter this.* The music! It's fantastic. It can be a bit repetitive on certain layers, but the most played themes are some of the best ones, so I don't mind.* I never struggled for money, not even close. So feel free to buy arrows, experiment, and just buy food instead of feeling like you have to farm it or save it.* It's just plain fun. Overcoming the challenges of the Abyss itself, learning map routes, collecting treasure, levelling up, and most importantly, just *surviving* in the Abyss is so rewarding.Cons:* The softlocks... You're a few floors down and your weapon breaks and you forgot to bring another or materials to craft another? You're pretty much screwed. You can't kill more enemies to make more weapons, nor for food. So unless you can make it back with what you have, you're screwed. And you may go a few floors or dozens of minutes before realizing it, resulting in losing a good chunk of time. Though this is a learning experience.* It's.. quite janky. Lots of odd collision, very small hiccups, visual glitches (mostly minor, except one area), and general wonkiness. It's not like some Early Access games I've played, but it seems like almost all of it could be fixed with a single patch, but I wouldn't count on it. In 60 hours, I only encountered one bug that actually affected me, resulting in me randomly losing the items I'd gained on a dive (but not my progress, oddly enough), but reset me to my pre-dive inventory. So I lost my treasure but got a bunch of supplies back. All in all annoying, but not the worst.* It's difficulty is almost entirely derived from one thing: The Abyss itself. Which is fitting. Most enemies are not that tough, though your first encounter with certain ones might be a.. learning experience. Even the boss fights are mostly unceremonious (which is actually nice because it sucks being roped into an unexpected boss fight and stressing about progressing). With the exception of one enemy (more on this later).* The graphics aren't fantastic. Doesn't bother me much, but it might to some. But I feel this game is similar to Xenoblade (Wii) in that respect. The graphics were.. well, as good as it could be for the Wii, but it more than made up for it with the stunning locales and area design.* Inventory space. It's not the worst game I've played in this respect, but it's not great. You spend a LOT of time chucking stuff to make space. Which makes sense for the genre, but still it'd be nicer if you.. just didn't have to do that. Also, more powerful weapons and armor as you upgrade get *significantly* heavier, so most of your upgraded inventory space is eaten by heavier equipment.* FREAKING MADOKAJACKS. They are the bane of my existance. They are the worst enemy in this game, and possibly in any game I've ever played. The trick is to save energy and space for about 2 jumps in any one direction (usually vertically) and as they swoop in, pick a direction, double jump, and hope for the best. Fortunately, most climbs are only plagued by one or two swoops at the most. But still. I'd wager at LEAST half of my deaths in this entire game are due to them.Tips:* SALT. NEVER LEAVE HOME WITHOUT IT. About 20-30 is what I usually bring on dives. Being caught without it deep in the Abyss is almost certain death.* If you're not opposed to modding, there's really only one needed. There's one that makes the survival knife have only 10 damage and infinite durability. Some may argue it's a bit OP and takes away from some of the challenge, but personally, I feel like it just takes away from a lot of the frustration, so I highly suggest it. And to anyone hesitant about the complexity of modding, it's literally just dropping a single file into the game's folder. That's it.* Poison arrows. Always keep a dozen or so of each type. Poison is incredibly powerful, and some enemies can die with a single arrow (albeit, slowly).* The amount that food heals/feeds is important, but of equal importance is the weight. Keep this in mind. And stock up on boiled eggs, incredible bang for your buck.Score:8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say I am a massive MiA fan, I have always wanted the anime to get a game since it feels like the whole whistle mechanic came directly out of a game and I was very much looking forward to this release.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling Into Darkness is not a very well polished game. It will not stun you with great graphics and the gameplay is not smooth like a Dark Souls title. It is, however, a good Made in Abyss exploration game and those who watch, and always wanted to explore the Abyss will get to do so here. This game might frustrate you with clunky gameplay but  it will still leave you craving for more due to the respect that was give to the source material and world.The game is divided into 2 game modes - Hello Abyss and Deep in Abyss.First lets look at Hello Abyss. This is a mode that has you, the player, follow Riko and Reg in the main story of Made in Abyss, this is usually standard fare for anime titles but don't go in expecting to go all the way from the Edge of the Abyss to the Sea of Corpses. Hello Abyss functions as an extended tutorial and it tries to give new arrivals an idea of what the story in MiA is, it takes you to the end of the Second Layer. Everyone who has seen the anime will know where the drop off point is in the story from that alone. That said, it does not do so gracefully. The game is not the most smooth and polished piece of software out there and it shows, you will see and feel how clunky it is, it serves as an ok tutorial and a very subpar introduction to the story of Made in Abyss. The main offenders here are the jank and the noticeable lack of Kevin Penkin's masterful OST, replaced by a mediocre score with weird choices for sound design. I do not need a "you got this item" sound queue every time the game shows me a relic. All in all this is the weakest segment of the game, which is a shame since it will be your first interaction with it as the game will not allow you to play the Deep in Abyss mode until you complete Hello Abyss.Now lets dive into the meat that is Deep in Abyss.The main game is this part. Mind you, this does not invalidate any of the previous criticism. The game is still clunky, the graphics are still ok at best and the sound design still suffers. However, here is where the game actually gets to do what it was meant to do. While in Hello Abyss the crafting/gathering/equipment side of things was present, it felt off and Deep in Abyss is the reason why. There is no need to explore, forage and collect things in Hello Abyss because the story is linear and your main goal is to progress the story and get a general feel for the mechanics of the game. In Deep in Abyss is where you HAVE to gather, you HAVE to collect, you HAVE to manage your inventory and complete requests, progress your skills, equipment and rank as a cave raider and this is where the game makes up for all its short-comings. The Abyss feels big, not as massive as it would be in real life, of course, but definitely big and confusing as it should be. The progression of your character and rank feels fun even if limited and the game's original story helps move things along. The curse Mechanic is an interesting concept that is somewhat decently applied to the game, but the execution could be far better and the combat is no Dark Souls or Elden Ring but it is serviceable for what the game is, just don't go in expecting Souls-like fluidity.All in all Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling Into Darkness is a mediocre, barely serviceable action adventure game for the wider public. For a MiA fan, however, it will scratch that itch of wanting to explore the Abyss even if just a bit. I do recommend muting the game's musical score and playing Kevin Penkin's superb OST in the back, that was when it most felt like I was in the world of Made in Abyss, exploring.This is a game for the fans, and only for the fans, willing to overlook many of its flaws to have a shot at diving into the Abyss, explore, collect and go from red whistle to an experienced cave raider.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this by saying DO NOT GET THIS AT FULL PRICE it is not worth it no matter how you cut it. Anyway, this game has so many dumb design decisions that cause this to be one of the most frustrating games ive played in recent memory. Decisions including (but not limited to):-enemies constantly spawning 1 meter behind you outside (and sometimes inside) your view, interrupting whatever you're doing without fail. From what i've read, apparently theres some kind of timer that starts as soon as you enter an area that causes this once it hits 0. So the game wants to rush you along, why also telling you about not taking risks and taking your time exploring???? -the depth system doesn't really work properly. The game tracks the curse by how many meters collectively you've ascended in a short period of time. which means you can suffer the affects of the curse just by jumping up and down for a few seconds, which is dumb and doesn't stay true to the original work. Also, there is no way to gain resistance to the curse in some way, so you will be climbing up a few meters, waiting 30 seconds for the curse to wear off, then climbing some more, then stopping and so on for the entire game. With this in mind though, it could have been worse, they could have stayed true to the anime and forced you to endure the curse whenever you were making your return trips which, while accurate, likely wouldn't have been fun to deal with at all. I suggest maybe tying curse resistance to your whistle ranks, it would better show that you're becoming a stronger and more experienced cave raider and be a bit more in line with the source material. With that curse resistance, you'd be able to ascend more before you'd have to take a pit stop or maybe even reset the curse buildup quicker on the earlier layers. It's not perfect, but it's better than what we got.-softlock cliffs. Some cliffs you climb down from can lead you to not being able to get back up, due to the stamina limitation, as well as needing to spend stamina fending off the dozens and dozens of butterflies that spawn right behind you whenever you climb. I'm not fully opposed to having something like that, but having progress completely halted because of it? No. There also points at cliffs where you can use ropes to rappel down cliffs quicker and without using stamina which can solve this problem. Unfortunately, not every cliff has those, and if the cliff you just dropped from didn't have a rope, you're screwed. The problem is can be remedied with upgrades to stamina efficiency while climbing, but that's way further down the upgrade tree, so you'll be suffering for a while before you get that.-exploration is very limited. Rather than actually traversing the abyss and seeing what down there, the majority of what you're going to be doing is fetch quests and other errands for people. while these quests could be used to try and push you to new and unexplored areas, most of the time it's going to make you backtrack to an area you've already been countless times to collect some grass or something.-the story mode is pretty much a very watered down version of the show that stops around the halfway point in season 1. It gets the important stuff across i guess. surprisingly, didnt have a problem with the constant spawning of enemies outside your view, but that may be because you have a very overpowered partner that kills everything he sees.-"the actual game" mode is a more expanded version of story mode where you get to create your own character. you get more stuff to craft, you can earn skill points to learn new abilities and recipes, all that stuff. The story is kinda just filler to get you from point A to point B, Im indifferent on it.-MAYBE the game will get updated to fix some of this stuff, but given how these things went through playtesting and into the final product with no one realizing how bad it really is to play, I have my doubts. So until then, don't buy, or at the VERY LEAST don't buy it at full price. 20 bucks tops

_childDocuments_.review: An Open letter to Spike Chunsoft.*Ahem* Dear Spike Chunsoft, As you are well aware, this game is seen as "Mixed" by a number of the community. However, I believe that this game is more than that, and is truly worth the time, if you wish to give it. The attention to detail in relation to the source material, it's all there. Personally, if horrible things weren't happening to orphans, it just wouldn't be MiA. However, while the game is good in its own right, I do have some complaints...Okay just one complaint.The game is fantastic, the Abyss draws you in and keeps you coming back (if you've the stomach for it of course.) so much so that I, someone who barely plays modern day games, kept coming back, and aside from the story mode, I have every achievement as of this review. The music go harder than it should in some places, and the atmosphere hit that sweet spot of being just daunting enough to make you want to turn back and take a break, while being tantalizing enough to keep pushing forward for that sweet SWEET Dopamine. However, we must address the elephant in the room, or rather, the twelve and a half foot flying rat on layer three.THAT'S RIGHT, The Madokajack, I'm talking about the Madokajack. Seriously, Satan's birds must be stopped. This is a plea of war against the wall watching sky dwellers. I BEG of you, please PLEASE patch their hitboxes in the future so we don't get knocked down while HALFWAY IN A CAVE. Seriously, I'm trying to climb inside the safe zone and suddenly a KC-135 Stratotanker sized monstrosity hits me with little warning besides the ominous music.As such, I beg the devs to please take another look at the rats and perhaps reduce their size ever so slightly, beyond that game's a solid 8/10. It has some slow moments, and random bandit attacks are kind annoying, but if you like pain, you'll love this game. Bought it twice so I could get the collector's edition on PS4.Update: I now have all the Cheevos.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Made In Abyss, you will most likely enjoy this game. To preface this review, I downloaded mods that disabled the infinite spawning mechanic and replaced the soundtrack with the anime soundtrack, so I won't mention them as negatives since they can be fixed. Overall, I recommend this game with a few caveats.Pros:- Exploration and survival elements are solid. There's nothing quite like traversing and conquering Lovecraft's Brutal Hellhole of Loli Abuse and cooking up a storm as you run out of stamina on a cliff and turn into a blood stain on the floor, just like Ozen said!- The Deep in Abyss mode is a good idea for a Made in Abyss game like this. Instead of rehashing the main story poorly (I'm looking at you, Hello Abyss), you get a simple and believable story about joining the Orth orphanage and taking various jobs and requests while fulfilling your own goal of becoming a White Whistle and making connections with fellow cave raiders and returning characters.- The graphics are commonly referred to with scorn, but I like the janky PS2 graphics. Makes me feel young again.- The difficulty can sometimes be unforgiving. When you travel down the Abyss, you'll eventually find you made an expedition unprepared and you'll have to start it all over again. This can easily mean wiping a good 30 minutes of playtime, but I enjoy this aspect because its as punishing as the Abyss is always made out to be and it makes the preparation phase of the game impactful and thoughtful.- The progression system is fine, you upgrade your whistle rank and get more abilities when you do. Nothing too in-depth, but it works and opens up for more options and areas within the Abyss as you climb the ranks.- It's Made in Abyss. Seriously, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MADE IN ABYSS game. C'mon.Cons:- The partner system is extremely buggy and aggravating to the ears. They constantly repeat lines and cause noises to glitch out when they get stuck on a slightly elevated piece of dirt. Very annoying and takes you out of the experience when you have to take someone along with you.- The main story (Hello Abyss) where you play as Riko and Reg, while not necessarily untrue to the source material or poorly written, is a slog to go through since all of the cutscenes are boring to watch and the best aspects of the game are not present in this mode at all. Worst of all, you're forced to play through it to get to the real game. This essentially makes it a 3 hour long tutorial, and a poor one at that.- The enemies are generally slow and dumb, making most of them a nuisance at best. Its rare for an enemy to actually scare you or challenge you after the first time you encounter them and learn their moveset. Some are a complete joke, like the Inbyos.- $60. Enough said. This should REALLY be a $40 game at best. But if you love Made in Abyss, then money is no object.TL;DR Too expensive and rough around the edges, but Made in Abyss fans who have been waiting for a game where you can traverse the Abyss and abuse your loli will be satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so bad. I was living in the very definition of a cope since I spent the same amount of money to buy a girlfriend and take her out to dinner at a nice restaurant. I have been a very big fan of Made in Abyss for a good while and was very much looking forward to getting a new perspective on the universe and hoping to learn about certain artifacts or aspects that were less touched on in the manga/anime. There are a LOT of issues with this game but there are some things that I enjoy and want to speak on those first.The nostalgia aspect is very nice. I know people clowned on the graphics but that's actually one of my favorite things about the game. It had a very nice PS2 feel and it actually brought me back to playing games in my room all night long. The colors were nice and just very warm and nostalgic for me. I know many people would disagree with that statement but personally it was something I really enjoyed and am glad they leaned into it as much as they did.Another thing that I really enjoyed was the fact that it ran very smoothly. My computer is good but nothing special and I was streaming with consistent 240 fps, no frame drops, cuts, skips, anything. This is a small thing but it's something great about the game that needs to be recognized. I'm trying so hard to give this game as much credit as I can...One of my biggest problems is that there is nothing new to experience, but instead just the first 16 chapters retold in a visual novel-like manner. This is one of many nitpicks I have but I'm especially disappointed that the team did not even finish off at the end of chapter 16, which is (in my opinion) one of the best scenes in the entire show/manga since it not only gives much needed support to Ozen's actions, but also beautifully shows the very important connection between Lyza and herself, strengthening the connection to Riko. I assume this was done to save money from having to rig Lyza's model and get the spoken lines in. Understandable, but leaving off right before a very cathartic conclusion of an arc just strikes me the wrong way. Another thing I’d like to point out is the actual world in the abyss. When you think of the abyss, you imagine a vast, beautiful biome of incredible creatures, beautiful flora, and amazing views. Instead, what you get is a few bland creatures with simple attack patterns and seem to be placed haphazardly using a dartboard. The creatures don't roam or explore their own environment, they stick to their box and attack the player if too close. Instead of being able to walk through the amazing city of Orth, seeing the houses for their glory, you’re stuck in specific rooms that you essentially fast travel to. It really is unfortunate to see such potential of a great steampunk cityscape get underutilized in this game.This segues into another gripe I have with this game. The fact is it's way too linear for it to even remotely feel like the abyss. An important sliver of the horror in the series is the vastness of the landscape. Something touched upon in the 5th layer especially. In the game, it feels like you’re on a set path where you can't get lost in. At least personally speaking, the idea of getting lost in the abyss and trying to find my way out sounds so intriguing since you get to put yourself in the eyes of Riko and Reg, though this is just a personal preference. I do, however, stand by the fact that the linear aspect removes a large chunk of mystery and horror from the abyss.I really hoped that I’d see models of the artifacts and whistles in greater detail. I was quite upset when I found out that the physical objects were reduced to jpegs on the screen. I really think it took away all the power that these insanely important items hold. Having Habo come up to me, giving me Lyza’s whistle, would have made much more of an impact than being transported to a VN style cutscene with a white whistle jpeg.There are a lot of smaller things that don't really fit in a whole category alone but are still important things to mention. These things include: Poor combat system, recycled lines from the anime, terrible controls, boring fetch-quests, story ending too soon, and the cooking system feeling way too underutilized.I do want to note that this is just the Hello Abyss mode, but being forced to play this before you start another mode that’s advertised is such a hassle. I also did not want to continue further because I knew I wanted to refund the game and get my $60 USD back in my account. If a game like this is going to use the anime story so poorly and as a tutorial type section, it at least should be interesting and even a little challenging.Needless to say, I am extremely disappointed with this game and I seriously hope the dev team makes real improvements to this game because it’s a great concept and could be such an incredible horror/exploration game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not enjoyable. For starters I was excited for this game before launch as a fan of the anime so when I saw the $80 price tag I assumed the game would be extremely well polished with interesting mechanics and story. What I found was exactly the opposite.For starters, playing on a PC was a nightmare. The controls where badly managed. For example, I have a mouse with the usual left and right mouse buttons but also two buttons on the side. The only button I was able to use in gameplay was the left mouse button. The other buttons wouldn't bind to other actions in the keybind settings. moving on to the mechanics. there is nothing complex or interesting about them. the mechanics are straight out of your average rpg or adventure game. there's nothing particularly bad about the mechanics, but they seem out dated since you could probably find an adventure game from the mid 2000s with similar mechanics. Since the mechanics don't try anything new or ground breaking it makes the game feel stale. Moving on to the story, the tutorial which doesn't tell you its a tutorial, follows the story of Riko and Reg from the manga and anime. Its basically a shot for shot and line for line remake of the anime but in a game format?? which handles the story much worse. despite this, I was actually enjoying reliving the anime in a game format. I was so excited to get to the deeper layers to get to the more interesting story lines like Nanachi and Bondrewd. And wouldn't ya know it, the tutorial stops right before you enter the third layer which was very disheartening.Moving on to things I enjoyed about the game, the soundtrack was very good. It reminds you of Kevin Penkin's score from the anime but yet the songs aren't just copies of said sound track. In other words, they did something original while still paying homage to the source content which I think the game could have used a lot more of. additionally, despite some low polygon walls and cliffs, the scenery and creature design is beautiful. the art style and its relation to the game once again reminded me of the anime. In the anime, the cute, cartoony art style fools you into thinking the show is for kids. thus when the gore hits it subverts your expectations. I experienced a similar phenomenon in the game. Once again the art style draws you in as cute and cuddly, but the game isn't afraid to show some horrific death scenes. I also appreciated how they didn't stick strictly to what was shown in the anime but also added some new items like a hunting bow and pistol. Also, part way through the tutorial there was an anime opening style credits sequence that was really hype.Overall, there is something in this game all though it is buried deep below layers and layers of issues. If you haven't checked out the anime or the manga don't even consider buying this game. You wont understand anything so go read/watch the series then come back. If you do decide to come back be prepared for an unpolished mess of a game that OCCASIONALLY has some high points.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to give the most real review I can for this.Overall:The game is not bad. I would give it a flat 6.5/10The developers did try, but a good portion of the game falls short.The Good Parts and Effort:- The cutscenes are great. The cutscenes actually follow the story down to a T. With a few exception but most are minor.- The Side story for your custom character is actually decent. I found myself more interested in it than the canon storyline.-Canon storyline is pretty decent. Mostly regarding the storyline.The Bad Parts and Improvement Areas:-Combat is very basic. Just one attack kills most stuff or does nothing at all.-Stealth is next to useless in most early areas. It does work but when it does work, it works TOO well.- Some storyline areas are a bit odd. Ozen's library is WAY too small for what the anime potrays. If the idea was to make it seem claustrophobic, good job, but it makes the atmosphere terrible. -Riko's storyline is OP. In other words, Riko is given so many materials + Reg, that it makes the custom character mode seem odd. If they didn't force you to play Riko's first, this point could be removed, but playing it first gives you the wrong idea for the game. One final addition so it doesn't have to be another point, Reg is  OP. Not as an ally, but as free rope when traversing the abyss. When playing custom character, rope is paramount and often needs to be built up over multiple runs.- AI Can be avoided easily at all costs. This point is slightly moot when doing the custom character route.Keeping is short Overall:Game is not bad for a first entry to the franchise but a bit disappointing for such a great show.Worth $60?Hell no.Get it on sale.If you are desperate, go for it but don't expect anything life changing.Is it worth a try? Perhaps. I would say its a bit like a easy mode animal crossing. If thats your thing. Dive in.Enjoy ^^P.S. TO THE DEVELOPERS:If you want to fix this game, two easy points;- Stop enemies from randomly, continuing to spawn around the player, i.e. hummingbirds and ferrets. For some reason these are the only enemies I've noticed so far that do this. Very annoying and seems unnecessary.- Make "Hello Abyss" Mode optional, not mandatory, it gives the game the wrong vibe. Deep in Abyss is MUCH better overall as an introduction.I'm sure there are other points that need to be fixed but these were the GLARING issues I found during playing. I hope ya'll can fix em! :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't seen made in abyss, don't play this game. There are too many cut corners and bad design decisions that keep this game from being worthwhile for an average player. If you are a made in abyss fan, don't get your hopes up, while it does have its moments, much of this game's unique story is quite predictable, and the abyss itself can feel quite shallow due to how much of a chore it is to actually explore, with endlessly spawning enemies and a half-baked combat system putting a drag on the fun. Of all of the design decisions, the absolute worst offender is the curse of the abyss simply being a wait timer instead of an interesting mechanic to play around and having to think about, which is just the worst since it could introduce so many cool scenarios, but it was all thrown away. A lot of this game is simply rough around the edges, with everything from environments to enemies just feeling a touch unfinished. Another year in development and this game could be leagues ahead of where it is now, but as it stands there are too many flaws to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying this game only costed me 20 dollars, so my opinion is based around that pricing.Well it's what you'd expect from an anime game, down to the cringe indulcing name, but still on the upper end of anime games.Editing to add: The game displays Keyboard inputs when using a controller, but that can be CHANGED with a setting in the Options menu. It is NOT a bug, just a really odd design choice.• GRAPHICS: The graphics are fine, they look certainly better than the PS5/Switch, but the lower areas are just hastily modelled. They're very lazy and empty compared to the areas of the 1st layer. The same can be said about enemy models. Some look really interesting while others look like low poly junk.Cutscenes are fine I guess, I skipped most of them because I just recently rewatched Made in Abyss.• GAMEPLAY: It's the best part of the game. The game is basically a bunch of interconnected dungeon maps, similar to old Monster Hunter. There's two modes; Hello Abyss and Deep In Abyss.-Hello Abyss- Nothing short of a glorified tutorial, where you play as Riko while Reg walks around behind you one shotting everything within a 30 mile radius of you. It's thankfully very short as the mode itself is extremely garbage but it's something you can easily get through in an hour. Hello Abyss ends right after Seeker Camp.-Deep In Abyss- This is where the meat of the game is at. You MUST complete the Hello Abyss gamemode first to unlock it. You play as a CaC who slowly progress their way through the Whistles rank by doing repetitive fetch quests in the Abyss itself. It may sound boring at first, but the gameplay loop of it coupled with the dangers of the Abyss itself makes it for a very entertaining time. It is a bit clunky but it does help feeling like you're a child in an otherwise very hostile environment. Some areas are really annoying when it comes to the amount of enemies and how unavoidable they are, while others are more chill and relaxing. Enemy AI is also very basic, so don't expect them to be anything more than farmable hazards.Deep In Abyss ends at the 5th layer, so if you were expecting to transform into a Hollow or a Narehate, you'll have to wait for the sequel, Made in Abyss: Trio Of Solitude And The Stray Soul, or whatever other cringe name they decide to come up for it.It also has an endless spawner after 7 or so minutes which seriously harms an otherwise relaxing experience.If you were expecting some sort of survival mechanic, DO NOT BUY the game. All the survival meters you see on the screenshots were REMOVED. There's NO SURVIVAL MECHANIC, the screenshots are outdated from an alpha dev build or whatever and I have no idea why they're still on the store page. The only thing you have is a food meter that you need to keep full since traveling from one map to another costs you food and health.• Audio: It's decent, but the voice acting is abysmal and the creators either ripped the acting from the anime itself, since I remember everything they said from the sub, or somehow managed to have the most phoned in performances ever.Riko is the only character that portrays any sort of emotion, everyone else feels like they're reading off from a book while being very bored. On the bright side, I found it quite amusing when I fell off a cliff as Riko, only for Reg to let out a mildly disappointed "Damn it."There's also the huge annoyance of lines being overly repeated. Your character will grunt the exact same way everytime you do a specific action, and all the gameplay lines from the Hello Abyss mode are ripped straight out of the cutscenes, and OH MY GOD do they repeat. You will hear Reg saying "Are you ready?" and Riko replying "Of course I'm ready!" OVER AND OVER. Same thing with every other line they speak while playing.Overall, it's a decent experience. I enjoy the first season of Made In Abyss a lot and I've enjoyed the game so far. I personally wouldn't pay 60 dollars for it, but at the price I got it for I can't really complain. Steam really needs a neutral option when it comes to reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game despite some issues that come down to a lack of polish.Pros: - Original story different from the anime/manga, but follows the universe faithfully- Looks beautiful despite the limited graphics (you can tell it was build for Switch then ported to higher-end platforms)- Tons of content, will keep you busy for 30+ hours easily- It is a hard game, so people who want challenge will be served, and mods exist to make things easier for those who prefer an easier approach (it will still be hard though)Cons:- If you want the anime/manga story, you will be disapointed, as that part is only a very short tutorial- A gamepad controller is required, mouse&keyboard is rough- No odd-resolution support like 21:9 (you will get black bars on the sides), again, built for the switch first- Game balance is rough in some aspects, an infamous "respawn timer" causes ennemies to spawn at your feet non-stop after a while, making the game almost unplayable in early levels, but thankfully there are mods on PC that can fix that.- Lack of polish in general. On top of the clearly rushed balance mentionned above (early on it is hardcore, then a single skill can completely change the way you play the game and obtain resources), other issues that are not game breaking can be annoying like the very limited amount of sound effects for human characters, or the inaccurate combat mechanism, or some animation glitches that take you out of the immersion. Mods can fix some balance issues, but not the core gameplay.In my opinion, worth the price despite the flaws if you are a fan of the series, especially on PC as the community is hard at work with mods both for QoL improvements / bug fixing and add-ons. If you go into this game blind though, you may notice the flaws more than the amazing universe it's based on.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: They patched it so you can skip the "Hello Abyss" prologue. I recommend skipping it if you already watched/read Made in Abyss.The reason why people hate it at first is because the prologue is essentially a 3+ hour long tutorial that is missing the several key RPG mechanics that the OC mode has. The game actually starts for real after you beat the Riko/Reg prologue (when you reach the end of the second layer, no you don't need to play all the way down to the fifth layer). On top of the lack of RPG mechanics making the game feel stale and linear, the Riko/Reg prologue story is of course also very monotonous if you've already read the manga/watched the anime.Once you beat the prologue, you actually unlock the fun RPG mechanics, and exploring and combat feels much more exciting and fulfilling. You're incentivized to explore and find relics to gain EXP, which you don't need to do at all when you're playing the Riko/Reg prologue. You have a catalogue for all the relics, monsters and characters in the world, showcasing Tsukushi's expansive world building. You have to genuinely think about how to get around and explore since you have limited resources. Reg's cable arms are OP on purpose, and the introduction of weapon durability makes you think about avoiding needless fights, especially considering you don't gain EXP from combat, but instead gain it from quests and relics (aka, exploration). I've only done the first layer on the OC character playthrough but it's 10 times more fun than the prologue. Rush through the prologue, and give the OC mode a shot. You'll be surprised.>>> EDIT (after beating the game):Pretty good, yet very disappointing in some areas.The World+ Good adaptation of the Abyss.+ It's great experiencing what it's like to be a Delver who actually has to regularly climb up from the Abyss (and not have Reg). It is rewarding to actually come back from a hard and long trip.+ 1st and 3rd layers are full of verticality, detail, and have intricately connected paths. Definitely the best areas in the game.- 3rd layer is a tad bit TOO difficult. There is no smart way to deal with the flying monsters. You cant bait them using squirrel meat, as depicted in the anime. They are also not affected by paralysis or electricity effects. Ascending requires you to know how to stay out of their aggro range with horizontal distancing, and vertically dodging them once you're forced to get close.- 2nd layer, especially the Inverted Forest, is an incredibly linear, uninteresting slog. Also filled with lots of potential soft-lock scenarios due to how it's set up with the main story (unexpected forced combat scenarios in a game with limited resources)- 4th layer is very disappointing. 4th layer's Goblet of Giants is somehow linear and very short, despite being such a key location in the series. It should have been the area with the the second steepest verticality. - To double down on the 4th layer, the Eternal Fortunes Garden was nothing like how it was depicted in the manga/anime. Too small and too dark.- 5th layer feels empty, not just in environment, but also because majority of the enemies are docile. The only difficulty is ensuring you have enough salt to cook since the food/HP requirements from travelling are (rightfully) very costly in this zone. Also the floating water bastions above Ido Front are not supposed to be purple energy blobs, devs.Gameplay+ Difficult and very punishing.+ Exploration requires planning with supplies and travel routes.- There are soft locks (and even hard locks if you manage your saves badly) depending on how poorly you prepare.+ The limitations on fast travel based on your Whistle are great, and make sense thematically. + Combat is serviceable (aside from melee combos not damaging some enemies since they receive i-frames during some stagger animations).+ Durability and repair system creates an intricate resource-allocation game between your weapons and food. - AI is non-existent. Boss battles are all a joke, especially ones that rely on movement.- To double down on the AI as a seperate point, Bondrewd's boss battle is the most disappointing thing in the game."- Infinitely spawning Mobs could have been handled better. Sometimes it comes in clutch if you need food though.+ Relics provide a great gameplay loop to level and make money in the 1st and 2nd layers, and give an incentive to explore.- The Relic gameplay loop is less enticing in the 3rd and 4th layers before you are able to fast travel, since it's incredibly difficult to ascend and the rewards are not worth the effort.- Relics are essentially just generic high-tier materials used solely for crafting generic high-tier weapons with better stats, they do not have unique gameplay purposes like you would expect from the lore. Even if they were given subtle stat-increases similar to Ozen's Wedge, that would have been great. Relics are definitely the biggest let-down in this game. Everyone I knew were looking forward to seeing what unique special-grade, 1st-grade, and 2nd-grade relics we could use.Curse of the Abyss+ The symptoms from the Curse of the Abyss are very well balanced and is thematically accurate. It even has its duration scaled based on your Whistle, which is a cool way to simulate the Delver's tolerance to its symptoms based on experience. - However, the Curse system isn't entirely accurate to the source material. You accumulate the Curse whenever you increase your elevation by any amount in the game (even if it's small, consecutive bumps in the terrain which move you up-and-down just by a few inches). In the manga it's more of a hard threshold once you reach a certain distance (~5 to 10 or so meters). - In game the intended strategy is to wait for the Curse to alleviate before pressing on, which could be interpreted as bearing with the nauseating symptoms, but doesn't make as much sense for the 3rd, 4th and 5th layers where there should be unavoidable consequences. It's clear it's for the intended gameplay design and would have been too punishing, but I would have welcomed a change that forced you to push through with the Curse symptoms when ascending, instead of outright avoiding it.StoryDecent. If you know anything about the series, you already know how it's going to end. The original main villain was meh, but his boss battle was actually the only decently designed fight in the game. I was also hoping that the story would have been completely separate from Riko and Reg's adventure, and at the very least were slightly linked indirectly. Once your character starts interacting with Reg and Riko, you stop believing that your character could exist in the world. The game quickly starts feeling like your generic self-insert fan service anime adaptation.The post-Reg ruined state of Ido Front doesn't make sense, especially considering you meet with Prushka in this game, and Nanachi and Mitty are still chilling in their hideout.Speaking of Nanachi, the secret way to meet her took me for surprise. I wish there were more secrets like this in the game.OVERALLCool game. I'm a huge Made in Abyss fan so it was worth the time. I'd say any Made in Abyss fan should try this. It's not polished enough to be full-price though, I'd wait for a sale. You will definitely get your hours worth though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Made in Abyss, this game is a great way to immerse yourself in the lore and setting. It is presumably non-canon as there are direct contradictions even within the game itself (with basically two versions of the same side quest at one point). The graphics are spot-on for the art from the anime, and the world is just as terrifying and brutal as you'd expect. Load times are almost instant on my system. Suffer through the hello abyss mode (don't bother wasting time gathering or fighting anything that isn't required, just go to the next objective marker), which serves as one of the worst tutorials in gaming history and shouldn't take too long to complete, and play the real game.The game feels like it was made to be a vita/switch/mobile game, PC port controls are not good at all (are we sure this is a UE4 game?). This is not a good starting point if you're not familiar with Made in Abyss. There are several glaring flaws in the gameplay and game design itself, mob AI is awful and has very limited aggro and leash ranges and predictable attack patterns, making some enemies that should be terrifying to even look at the wrong way seem like minor obstacles and annoyances that just try to get in your way. The storytelling is very brief and feels incomplete, leaving huge gaps that you're expected to fill in for yourself. There's a lot of wasted potential here, but ultimately it's an enjoyable experience excluding the cliffs, looking at you madokajacks. And who can forget  infinitely respawning 1HP mobs that will often phase into existence out of nowhere and that are there solely to prevent you from standing still? Or fishing. Which isn't absolutely required to progress or even upgrade gear as once you hit the fifth layer you can just gather scales from mobs and required combat sections are fairly limited throughout the game and can be done with gear you purchase from stores.100% achievements, though nowhere near 100% on quests, items, mob/character gallery took me 33.1 hours. _childDocuments_.review: There is no way i can compile on a short review how much this game is broken or is not properly done: bad economy system, dull souls-like fight mechanics that feel extremely simple, tremendous item and mechanic restraints everywhere, some of which could be easily fixable... and many, many more, all of this that leave a trully frustrating game. Very little of the game is properly constructed and is clearly half done (the last level is clearly unfinished, it looks like a testing developing area). The game really feels as if it had been developed under extreme time constraints, low budget, unexperienced game developers or any of these combined. It was also most likely not tested at all since so many problems are evident in both existence and solution but still remain on the game. The soundtrack is all over the place, it's composed of short tracks which don't really fit the environment and since they quickly loop they become annoying. As for the story: First of all I'm a huge fan of Made in Abyss, if you have never seen it and wish to experience it, I'd strongly recommend to go watch the source material, dont take it from here for the first time. In this game, Story is composed of two different campaigns, one follows part of the descent to the abyss of the two main characters, the other one is the story of a new character (you) that gets in the abyss recently. To put is shortly, the main campaing is the tutorial with no new events compared to the source material and the secondary campaing should be considered the main game. The overall theme of the second campaing is basically a non-cannon fanfiction that drastically changes the events of the original source. On this regard, there are good stories, bad stories, and then there is whatever Made in abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is... like the rest of the game the story is half done and i swear to god at some point I sarted wondering if time travel was involved in the later stages. Even if you can step over all these game limitations and commit to go througt the game, progress on it comes at the cost of spending A LOT of time on it aswell, but every now and then the game feels slightly satisfying to play. I must add, i am actually on a second playthorught and i have started enjoying this game for what it is, it's a 5/10 at best, but it really feels that if this game had had 2 aditional years  of development and tested it adequately, it would have been an astonishingly good game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game includes Hello Abyss mode and Deep in Abyss mode. Hello Abyss closely follows the same story as the first half of the anime. The actual gameplay is a cakewalk, only one fight was challenging and that was because Reg glitched out before the fight on the first attempt, once he participated it was trivial again. Reg is invincible and will destroy any enemy without consuming resources, possibly needing to recharge if he gets too much damage. Just watch the anime, it's a better experience than Hello Abyss.Deep in Abyss is the better part of the game, it doesn't appear to have the same problems.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Made In Abyss fan this game filled the desire for more content from this series. But even for a fan I can only recommend getting this when it's on sale like I did. The game has a lot of fun simplicity like exploring, discovering, combat, meeting characters from the series, going through a new story by the author himself, and more.----------The game is not as difficult as most reviews like to let on. I beat it without any mods and had very little issues with the spawning enemies. But, you will find yourself inevitably having to restart levels whether it's because of being under prepared or running out of items mid level. Main issue I had is I don't know why all the cool cosmetics, skills, whistles, and weapon (the blaze reap) are after the main game when there is really nothing left to do. It really makes me wish for a ng+ or some type of dlc where you go to the 6th layer just so you can get to use them more. There are def a lot more game play issues that can be discussed but I'm too lazy to list them. ----------Overall I enjoyed the 61 hours i put into this game and getting all the achievement's. I would have liked more from a MIA game but this will have to do for now.3/5

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I like the concept, but no.The control scheme is atrocious, especially in menus. Stuff like 'ESC to confirm, SPC to cancel', or having a mouse that does actually nothing except having LMB mapped to confirm (aka, if you click on something, it instead confirms whatever was previous selected with WSAD). That's exceptionally crappy levels of console port, right there.And, of course, absolutely no key rebinding options.Ingame controls aren't much better, combined with a weirdly stiff animation and movement system (i.e. characters halting and pausing half a second before doing a 20cm hop). Combat seems a bit weird, too, but I haven't played long enough to see whether there's more to it that would be considered redeemable (given other reviews, I wouldn't count on it though).It also took me less than 2 minutes of actual gameplay to run into the first bug (glitched out dead mob that kept attacking me after dieing), so that's promising.I won't necessarily diss the game for it's graphics or dialogue quality, because the animation is in the end meant to imitate an anime, and the dialogue is run of the mill visual novel stuff (with decent voice acting, to be fair). But it definitely won't win any prizes.So, as much as I liked the setting and the anime itself, the game just seems like a horribly messy console port cash grab on first glance. And with Steam Refund policy being what it is, a first glance is all you get before I got to make my choice.

_childDocuments_.review: If you do like the series in general , i'd recommend you not to try it despite liking it . The world setting is based on the source material which is what really interests me the most to play this game . Despite that , i'd say if you're here with no prior knowledge to the series whatsoever then i don't recommend you to try it , There's a lot of issues with this game that is clearly not polished even at final release :-The combat feels sluggish as your animation lag is so bad that you barely can dodge attacks from the monsters . I have experience in monster hunter and despite that it's still pretty tight to even dodge attacks as monsters dont leave too much opening . Speaking off there's a bit of a cheese in the game where you just hit the monster once repeatedly to keep them stunlocked . Now comes the second problem .-Weapon durability is very bad design wise . I understand its a resource management game but with that limited durability you are forced to just not fight at all and run from monsters which somewhat kills the fun in the challenge . The worse thing is that small enemies have infinite spawnrate whenever you're like climbing or running around and will attack you . -Remember that cheese from earlier? The cheese is actually very limited to how much stamina you have so its not like a forever stunlock kind of thing its limited to your weapon durability + stamina . But im not complaining about stamina for the cheese but mainly for climbing (I'm talking about you 3rd layer). The stamina has basically gatekept me from ascending in this game for like hours and hours and its annoying every time you try to climb and you almost barely reach the top but ran out of stamina and fell down . At one point , i had to grind food just to be able to climb back up and boy that wasnt fun .While adding to that if you are trying to ascend which 60% of the game if you hit halfway through the game you are going to ascend a lot , makes climbing even more stressful especially in the 3rd layer where there's just a big wall sticking out with one shotting monster that will try to attack you as you climb and then if you climb up you'll get hit by the curse or die getting one shot . This by far is the worst part of the game for me . -Coming from a guy who played monster hunter a lot , i find it very disappointing that when you kill big monsters (like the splitjaw from the anime in the 1st layer if you remember that big snake thing) , they actually don't drop special materials . It'd have been cool to see armors based on the monsters which would've added more depth into the armors in the game or even weapons . I distinctively remember that in the manga there was like a description for one of the birds called Hammerbeak , it says that the head has a part that supposively works like a flint. Would've been cool if that was a thing in the game but nope . They only drop either bird meat or egg which i find disappointing too as they just remove some of the cool aspects of the original material . All and all , i don't recommend this game .

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the manga, so I thought I would enjoy the game. I absolutely love this game. It's a lot of fun and there's a lot to do and explore! I would, however, recommend buying it on sale; it is NOT worth the full price as it still plays like a buggy beta build.Pros:Going through different layers, beautiful level and monster designs, exciting gameplay. A lot of the mechanics do follow the game. I know that the curse of the abyss is a pain for a lot of people, and it's definitely inconvenient, but I love that it was included because it fits the universe. You get to see a lot of main characters, and go on quests with them!Cons: This game's mechanics are NOT well done, and the game is so hella glitchy it isn't even funny. There are instant kill enemies who WILL kill you even if they don't touch you. The jumping mechanics work about 75% of the time. The PC controls SUCK; this was developed for the Switch, so if you have joycons it's a way better experience. The AI is probably the most broken aspect of the game; they're pretty useless and get stuck CONSTANTLY. They also have extremely repetitive voice lines that basically play back to back to back. There are also REALLY annoying useless moths and bugs that infinitely spawn to make your life harder and use up your weapons, but there are mods to remove them. Interesting: This game is not forgiving and will punish you for bad choices or improper preparation. This can make it a pain in the butt, but it's also very in line with the real story. If you take on the wrong enemy, you'll die. If you aren't prepared for a delve, you can get soft-locked and unable to get back to the surface. You have to approach this game with a trial and error mindset. I've found this game about as unforgiving as Dark Souls. I like the difficulty because it suits the universe, but I did get stuck in certain areas with massive learning curves for hours or days. It was really rewarding when I finally surfaced.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly ignore anyone who only played Hello Abyss mode as it is just a retelling of early parts of the anime and is INCREDIBLY limited (you can only go to areas the game lets you and alot of the mechanics aren't available) it functions as a very basic tutorial, with it missing many things (including weapon durability which I will get to later) and a taste of the original story.tl.dr. Absolutely worth it (at half price) if you love Made in Abyss but you'll probably want to give up at the 2nd layer in the Deep in Abyss mode unless you're a masochist (it goes to the 5th layer). There are some mods to fix a few things (without necessarily making it easier) but I can't exactly recommend a game that needs to be fixed by the players.This game is only for people who really love Made in Abyss and even then I'd only recommend if it's 50% off or more (~$40AU or less) so while I personally have played the game for 48hrs, (I installed the mods I mentioned after exploring, but not completing, a majority of the 2nd layer as it simply wasn't very fun trekking all the way up to the first layer with barely anything done) in the 2nd layer in Deep in abyss mode it goes downhill as far as enjoyment factor and good game design, the creatures are a non issue (which is very disappointing as the hostility of the abyss just isn't there) you can walk (literally walk no running or dodging needed) past them unless you need a resource from them and then they are, for the most part, very easy to kill.The difficulty at this point comes from your entire hunger bar emptying in a couple minutes (2nd layer dives take over 10 minutes) and weapons having ridiculously low durability (5-10 hits depending on the weapon, it takes 1-2 hits for a small creature and like 5 for midsize one, you'll need multiple weapons for some of the larger creatures) plus an incredibly small inventory limit compared to the resources needed to complete a raid, which on their own wouldn't be the worst (it should be a punishing place).It's completely fine on the 1st layer as you can get away with carrying 5 of a weapon and just replace them as they break because it's easy to get resources to do so and a particular creature is constantly dropping food and weapon resources. ( one of the mods I installed replaced the weakest weapon, a hatchet, with an even weaker, essentially unlimited durability hatchet which allowed me to go down longer and made it so I didn't require 6 or so weapons just to get the food I needed to survive) It's when you get to the 2nd layer that things go bad you can no longer just kill enemies for food 90% of food drops need salt so make sure you have plenty of that and getting back up from the low 2nd layer to the 1st layer requires more than a full hunger bar as it is consumed to move between areas as well as the constant drain (just going to the 2nd layer costs 20%).With incredibly weak weapons the fact that creatures tend to drop either practically useless food as it doesn't restore enough to travel between some areas and you lose half of what it gives getting more food from one of the easyish enemies to farm for food, the other one that seemed somewhat worth farming dropped bone FAR more often than meat which you can use to make more weapons, assuming you're carrying enough stone, but you don't get enough to keep up with the rate you'll break them or if you do you'll run out of food/hunger which instantly empties your energy meaning you can't swing your weapons anymore (you can use ranged weapons without stamina but they break in ~5 shots and are far more difficult to craft) this can make getting back VERY RNG dependant, it's not only a massive jump in difficult from mostly mindless exploration on the 1st layer to planning things out far more carefully and having to contend with the RNG on the 2nd layer this makes a very poorly designed game.After the 2nd layer is the worst of all 5, the 3rd layer is a massive hole with some tunnels in the sides of it, you'll spend most of your time climbing here so make sure you have some stamina resupplying food to get back to the top when you want to return to town, this wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the flying creature that lives on this layer that is very difficult to avoid and, at this point, near impossible to kill and very much not worth killing yet, so make sure to have a save close to any climbs needed to make it back up, they aren't generally a problem on the way down (though they can occasionally get you, it's rare) it's trying to go back up that really sucks.Completing this layer without mods would be awful, as the food and weapons to resupply the food you'd need to return to town would prevent you from achieving much, unless you want to bank on finding an abandoned bag that gives you weapons and/or food.After the 3rd layer, particularly since you can fast travel past completed layers once you get the associated whistle, the game is pretty fun again, the 4th layer is probably the best,  it's scenery is personally the most enjoyable and exploring felt fun, though it does introduce the worst enemy (this one is the only one that cannot simply be walked past but you can generally sneak past without much difficulty)The 5th layer has fairly boring scenery but it does give a bit of a harsh feel so it doesn't detract from the experience, the only thing I found worth doing on this layer is the story, but the story was kind of interesting so it's atleast worth finishing from this point and shouldn't take too long once you've hit the 5th layer.
