_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet of this review: If you're a fan of Made in the Abyss world/lore and this game is on sale for 50% off or more I'd recommend getting it!This game has two different game modes: one mode follows the season 1 anime and is considered a tutorial since it's quite short. The second mode allows you to create your own character and delve down to the 5th layer, starting out as a red whistle and progressing all the way to white whistle. You spend time in "town" and then go back out to the abyss to collect relics and try to descend deeper. If you're familiar with the anime then the dangers of the Abyss shouldn't surprise you; you might be admiring the view of a flower-covered hill until a Corpse-weeper swoops down, bashes your head in and carries you off to it's nest to devour you. I honestly have really enjoyed slowly exploring the world, and you do need to take it slow as the game implements weight limits, requires you to climb back the way you came to return (depending on your whistle rank), and the curse of ascension. I would recommend that you download the mod for this game to eliminate infinite enemy spawn timer, as I find it extremely annoying, but your mileage may vary. I would love for this game to be more easily modifiable (like be on the steam workshop) because there's so many features that were cut that would be wonderful to have (weather, camping, character statuses, etc), but honestly I still really enjoy the game. The Bad: I'm not sure if it's due to my computer but in some maps I'll have an instance where my FPS drops to 1 and I need to wait about 10 seconds for the game to resume. The enemy AI isn't very good, and the infinite spawn timer is annoying AF. Combat is a little clunky, but that also may be because my combat skills are low.

_childDocuments_.review: if you can get it for ~$10, go for it. otherwise dont bother.  the actual game is only about 4 hours long, painfully stretched out by making you go through each floor 1-5 times before you can progress to the next one, and giving you almost no inventory space/equipment durability to force you to go back and forth over and over. fast travel mechanics dont unlock until they arent of any real value. the first half of the game is a poorly made rehash of the first season of the anime, except almost every "cutscene" takes place in visual novel style, with 1 or more character models just standing there staring at your screen, delivering lines in the most lackluster "i dont want to be here" manner. its also completely effortless, and not any fun whatsoever unless you simp REALLY hard for the anime, and somehow dont mind this terrible version of it.  the 2nd half of the game is the actual game, but its designed more around disrespecting the player and wasting your time, then allowing progression. it was very clearly NOT tested to any degree, as certain areas of the game are borderline impossible to get through without cheating, following a video guide, or already knowing the single possible path to take to progress. 2nd half has an enemy that will poison you, and said poison will never stop until youre dead, UNLESS you first found the secret cutscene to find nanachi AND finished her long, 15 step fetch quest. otherwise, youre screwed, and will soon be dead.  combat is trash. you have just a single basic attack, and after leveling up a skill tree you get access to a basic 2-3 hit combo and/or charge attacks. either way though, you just spam the 1 attack you have from the 1 weapon thats worth having. theres no sense of wonder or exporation, and dispite what some of the other reviews say here, the areas are absolutely nothing special looking. on average youre looking at early PS3 graphics, and early ps1 gameplay.  worst of all, the entire game is a bug filled mess and very clearly had NO QA testing done. every single map has dozens of spots where you can be walking along and...BAM! stuck in an infinite falling cycle because of poor geometry. the bug enemies have a strange quirk to their model, where if you touch them they are treated like a bicycle ramp, and youre sent launched into the air and to the side. and said bugs are EXCLUSIVELY placed in spots where touching them flings you off a cliff to your death. the entirety of layer 3, like literally every single inch of that map was very clearly not tested at all.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness does not try to win you over. It doesn't try to be convincing by existing as a game a casual player would be comfortable in. This is a game that aims to be a specific way, and it accomplished that excellently. Games are about the gameplay, not the graphics. And I tell you, the gameplay is high tier.At any moment of the game, you risk dying. It is tense. Without preparing enough, you'll be stranded and lose lots of progress. Frustrating for sure, but that's why it's amazing. You're efforts are rewarded because they matter. Harsh consequences for mistakes. This game forces players to slow down and pay attention to how they play and what they are doing.A tip when looking at other reviews, there's two types of negative reviews: 1, They simply do not like the game and point at what makes it good as a negative. 2, legitimate complaints, as there are issues with the game. It is our choice to deal with the jank to enjoy this gem of a game.  Not worth 60$, at all. Buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this for 60% off and it's worth it all in all, otherwise the full price would be too much even for a fan of the series.Hello Abyss covers the main canon story up to Riko and Reg leaving the 2nd layer and departing down to the 3rd, after 3-5 hours of that as the tutorial to the mechanics of the gameplay you can then play Deep in Abyss where the our main non-canon story starts.There's a lot of problems i have within the game such as the Telescope being useless af when it doesn't allow you to scan the creature even if it's 10x zoom and the creature is in full view, vague skill descriptions such as advanced gathering having "faster gathering time" instead of "double gathering drops" making me think it's just physically faster to gather stuff instead of doubling drops so i only picked up the skill in the end-game, can't say much for PC controls since i used a controller.Otherwise, problems such as certain terrain being a one-way path or maps getting reset rendering your ropes useless and you can't go back and have to Give Up your current cave raid because you ran out of food and salt because the 5th layer is basically the incarnation of gluttony eating up your hunger bar; can all be seen as the harshness of the abyss and merely my unpreparedness for the cave raid.Other minor annoyances is that the character you make only has 2 voices, a male and female child, which led me to believe that they could voice what we are saying but whenever our character talks they just go through an animation with no dialogue or audio on what they're saying and you have to see the reactions of the people you're talking to the make out what you said.Dorothea and other characters like Mio in the Caravan Fleet is kind of wasted on since there's only dialogue changes depending on the main quest you're currently in or what whistle you have (aside from white, no one talks about white aside from one guy and timeline is messed up when you get to post-game) or giving food everytime you want to buy something and get kicked out of the Caravan Fleet whatever choice you make.Really wished you can talk to Dorothea about Riko since Also, i don't know whether this is a bug or a feature but i have They should add more than 3 save slots even if i don't use them.Stand on shiny relics for stamina, worked especially well in the 4th layer.I still hear the sounds of the shiny relics even after closing the game...Still a good experience though, ob.Capital of the Unreturned DLC when....?

_childDocuments_.review: An unforgiving adventure into the abyss that manages to be decently faithful to the source material. A flawed game, but a comendable effort considering the overall quality of most games based on anime franchises. This one is not quite Dark Souls, but can be quite challenging until you get the hang of the climbing mechanics, resource management tricks and commit to memory every stage layout to be able to navigate in-and-out efficiently.For people that haven't read/watched the source material... I would say skip. You can go in blind, but the game will probably be rather mediocre for you, and there are better options for the money out there. For the series hardcore fans it's worth it on sale....You have to have some endurance for this type of game tho, as some of the "difficulty balancing mechanics" can be a little... offensive, like the tendency for the game to spam annoying critters any time you start climbing a rope or wall. There are mods to solve this, but imho it makes the game "too easy" because other than making you fall to your death the game doesn't really have any proper way to kill you since the combat is completely lackluster and exploitable in your favour once you know the enemy you're facing.

_childDocuments_.review: While watching the anime, I was always thinking that MiA had everything for a good videogame; the core concept of cave raiding, the strain of ascension, the whistle tier system, the flora and fauna of this world and most importantly the Abyss itself  seemed just perfect for a game. I wanted to explore this world for myself so badly, to climb the ranks of cave raiders and to create my own adventures. And then they actually made it possible!Coming from a developer who, best to my knowledge, never really made games like this (Chime Corporation) and the publisher Spike Chunsoft (whom I love, but again, not for this kind of games) I was a bit skeptical. I was afraid this game would turn out to be some low quality spin-off akin to a flash game.Fortunately, I was wrong. This game was made with love and I'm certain the developers wanted to give us the experience we were dreaming of while watching the anime / reading the manga. The story is even supervised by the creator of the manga, Akihito Tsukushi himself!The game has two modes: "Hello Abyss", a sort of tutorial / warm-up mode and "Deep in Abyss".The former focuses on Riko and Reg's story (~3-4 hours) until they reach the Seeker camp in the 2nd layer. A lot of people complain about this because they wanted to continue the story of the anime.I personally don't understand the frustration. We've already seen it and the game wouldn't be able to reproduce the same awesomeness of the story. When I said that "I" wanted to experience the Abyss, I didn't mean through Riko, and I think most people understand me here. She is her own character and her story is already written, let us have our own.Also, towards the end of Hello Abyss I even started to dislike it. Following their story meant linear progression, no exploring, little crafting, no leveling but it ended just at the right time. They taught us enough to begin our own journey.Deep in Abyss starts with your customizable character becoming a red whistle and going on their first dive. The game quickly introduces the main cast and a little handholding later you're free to progress and explore at your own pace, which is the beauty of this game. The new story itself isn't anything mindblowing, especially if you watched Dawn of the Deep Soul things become pretty apparent pretty early on, but it's still good and fits in the world well. It's a decent story but the game's main appeal is the cave raiding, as it should be.It's surprisingly good honestly. I was expecting way worse from this studio but I'm pleasantly disappointed. That said, it still has problems, just minor ones. Gathering resources is quick and easy, you'll never need to go out of your way for some plants.Excavating rocks may yield you common, well, rocks, or relics. Mining will be your primary source of relics which you can sell for xp + money, or craft armors and weapons with them later on (which I highly recommend).Fishing is really good in this game, but still fishing. You see a fish in the pond, throw your bait close to it, it bites. Quick and easy. That said, unless it's required for an armor set or quest, you really shouldn't spend much time fishing.Hunting primeval creatures for food is relatively easy (just bring salt, for the love of god BRING ENOUGH SALT). Side quests that require hunting have the well known curse of getting too tedious too fast. I'm talking about "kill "x amount" of "y creature"". Yeah, they are there but a lot of them are not even worth it for the XP. You can get enough XP from other sources, so don't feel obligated to complete them all, there's no achievement for it.The controls could be better. I used a gamepad for my playthrough (I used mouse occasionally for ranged weapons) and remapped nearly every button. Maybe because I have other preferences from other games but I just couldn't get used to it, but since you can freely remap them it's fine I guess.You dash holding down a button. Dodge is the same button. "Kinda like Dark Souls, eh? Cool!" THINK AGAIN! You need to DOUBLE PRESS the button to roll. This may be my single biggest complain with the game. Some enemies require quick reaction time and double pressing takes a lot of it.Also when an enemy dies you were locked on to, it would be nice if the game automatically targeted the next one that's close to you. Otherwise, the combat is decent.The cave raiding itself is quite enjoyable and the level design is perfect in my opinion. I was afraid it would suck but they actually nailed it. The verticality is good. The thematic resemblence but uniqueness of individual areas inside layers is just awesome. The loot placement, enemy spawns and everything else, I didn't find a single problem. I was so afraid in Layer 1 that they made this amazing map for they first part of the game to reel you in and then you'll only get generic levels after that, but they kept it up till the end.You'll be climbing walls a lot but for me it was fun after figuring out the exploits.There are not many gimmicks, and virtually no puzzles. It's a wild environment, not a pharao's tomb.The leveling system is okay I guess, and the whistle tier progression is satisfying as with every new whistle you can unlock more skill for either combat, crafting or cave raiding. I love that skill tree, it's very well done.I heard there were more survival mechanics, kinda wish they weren't cut. You only have to worry about hunger and status effects really (including broken arms / legs but easily managable). This reminds me, there were critics who said this game was too hard, and there were some who said it was too easy. Fans of the original works know the Abyss is unforgiving. I personally enjoyed the challanges and never really felt like I was too comfortable either. It kinda works like this: first time you explore an area, you don't really know where you are going and try everything. This puts you in much more danger than later on when you're running through the same area you are already familiar with and I guess thats all right.The strain of ascension is very well implemented.This game is very easy on your pc. I have a midspec machine and it ran this game 60fps on epic quality the whole time. Honestly it feels like this game came out in the PS3 era. That said, the textures are not at all ugly, they create the perfect cartoon world for this game. The characters are rather simplistic as well but you'll get used to them. The 2D art for the items and creatures / plants are very nice though. I'm not usually critical of graphics so can't say much more.All in all, It satisfied my yearning for adventure in the Made in Abyss world. I would recommend this to anyone who loves the franchise and wants to experience the thrill of cave raiding, and for survival game enhusiasts who want a fun time. Waiting for a discount is always recommended.Small addendum:I forgot to say this but if you're like me and cringe at every word english dubbers say in anime (no offense to them, I just can't stand it) fear not, this game has japanese dub you can turn on in the options menu. It also makes companions more tolerable as they talk a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely rough around the edges, a more mid-budget game, but I really enjoyed my time with it. I would say that enjoying Made in Abyss does help, and especially if you always wanted to explore the Abyss.The game is a difficult RPG / Survival game, kind of. You have to manage stamina, hunger and health, and explore the Abyss from the first to fifth layer. The Abyss is truly unforgiving and hostile, but also beautiful. You have to climb a lot and navigation is a constant puzzle. Climbing up hits you with the curse - but it mostly is boring as you just "wait" for it to disappear. Not sure if it could be done better as a game mechanic though.There are 2 modes, the "Hello Abyss" is really just a tutorial though and follows the manga/anime story only until the third layer. In "Deep Abyss" mode you make your own character and truly play the game and explore at your own. There is an original story to follow, which is nothing great honestly, but good enough. There are cameos and lots of side quests, also none of which are stand-out. Some side-quests also are super grindy, requiring hundreds of creature kills - you don't have to do them though.The progression and eventual mastery is really fun. You keep improving as you rank up and get better equipment, and it is fun to look back how difficult the first layer was in the beginning when you now explore the fifth layer.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky but lovable. It seems that most of the negative reviews are from people who didn't even bother giving the game a chance. This game is clearly made with love despite the few hiccups, and the developers understood what makes the abyss so enchanting.I had a rocky start and some frustrations along the way, but the more I played this game, the more I started getting attached to it, and at this point I adore it. I've played it for 57 hours so far (and I believe I might be nearing the end), so to me, the game is worth it, provided you play it with the spawn rate fix mod.Let's start with the basics: Don't expect a AAA game nor an engaging combat system, and play this if you're already a fan of the series, because the story might be difficult to understand with no prior knowledge of the world. The game has 2 modes: "Hello Abyss" and "Deep in Abyss". The first one acts as a 3-hour "tutorial" and retells part of Riko's journey (but ultimately I found it quite boring). The 2nd one is where the real game takes place, so you can skip or speedrun "Hello Abyss".While this game is clunky in terms of controls (you can remap them though) and may contain a few broken features (which can usually be fixed with mods), it is excellent in exploration, the main gameplay loop is fun, the characters are lovable, the music is really nice, and you can learn many interesting things about the world. Even some side quests feel meaningful because they allow you to spend time with your favorite characters.Overall, a solid 9/10 if played with the mod I mentioned. The negative reviews feel misleading and harsh, because my experience was better than I expected. If they ever make a DLC or a game that covers the remaining layers of the abyss, I would definitely buy it!I'm off to go say hi to Bondrewd, thanks for reading!(PS: You don't know true peace and cozyness until you've found Nanachi's Hideout)

_childDocuments_.review: Short version - Imperfect-but-soulful, if you're a fan, pick it up (when it's on sale).'Binary Star' is not without its share of bugs, flaws, and weaknesses: The tutorial (Hello Abyss), in particular, feels hastily thrown together and I recommend skipping it unless you want the achievement, and the main game could have benefited from fleshing out the combat, skill-tree, and adding in a few more survival mechanics, but overall it's such an endearing, comfortable, and soulful game that it's easy to overlook its shortcomings. The fundamental gameplay loop of delving, exploring, treasure hunting, and trying to survive the ascent to cash in your haul and upgrade your gear for the next sortie is incredibly satisfying, especially when your well-laid plans inevitably go awry on the way up and you're forced to think on the feet. The plot is mostly window dressing for the setting and the gameplay mechanics, but the new characters are nice enough, and the story does work in a few good moments, and works in a lot of dialogue and details from the series along with some fun cameos from familiar characters. If the game is even remotely on your radar it's probably because you're a fan of the series and you're looking for an excuse to spend some more time in that universe, and at that, the game excels. While it's not worth paying full price, if it's on sale for $20-30 dollars you'll absolutely get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: If I didn't know better I'd think there was an early access label on the game. The second part/game is really corny but fun for the first two layers, but then the story kind of drops off and the game just slams what is possibly the hardest part of the entire game in your face in the form of the third layer. After that it's just several floors of grinding though. There's almost no story outside a few tidbits on the fourth layer. The game just sort of expects you to want to get to the end without really giving you any driving factors to keep going. Sure there's sidequests, but after a while sidequests just start feeling like unnecessary chores to extend your playtime (kind of like fishing for better armor), and you realize you're already capable enough to just keep advancing to the next stage using the profits from quests you completed accidentally and relics you bring back between dives to fund further trips (I realized this shortly before getting my black whistle). At that point Bonedaddy's quest just feels like a punch in the 'nads, you know?It's a fun game. I would only buy it on-sale since it feels half-finished, but it's worth playing.EDIT: Oh right, and make sure to use Japanese voices.

_childDocuments_.review: To start I would preface this review by saying that in my personal experience I think Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is a good game that is very enjoyable. I feel that the overly negative reviews focus too much on the few negative points that the game does possess, and completely disregards the many positive aspects of the game. The game I think is a solid 7.5/10...maybe an 8/10 if I am feeling generous.To begin, there are two modes. Hello Abyss and Deep Abyss. Hello Abyss is meant to be a tutorial, and is completely optional. It is simply a faithful adaptation to the anime up to the end of layer 2. You play as Riko, and you have your travelling companion Reg to help you with fights and act as a never-ending rope. It's a good way to acclimate the player to the general mechanics of navigation, resource management, preparedness, etc. You don't get to keep any of your progress when Hello Abyss ends, so many people just end up skipping this part. If you are confident you don't need a tutorial, and don't feel you need to see the first few episodes of season 1 in a video game adaptation. Hello Abyss is an easy skip. I should mention here that Reg does get stuck a lot in Layer 2, AI pathing is awkward at best. Plus there is a lot of repeating dialogue that happens every few seconds. It gets really annoying, and I think this is another good reason to just skip the tutorial.Onto the meat of the game, Deep Abyss. This is where you get to control your own character, and go on your own adventures into the abyss. This is clearly the best part of the game and is the main mode you will be playing. There are tons of quests to do, both main quests and side quests. There are skill trees, an abundance of items to collect, multiple zones in each layer to explore, wide variety of enemies and side characters, recipes for food items, clothes, weapons, etc. There is a lot of content here that you will find, and the gameplay loop is both entertaining and engaging. Much of that comes from the exploration of the abyss itself. There is so much to discover and see in each layer. A variety of pathways you can choose, new and interesting enemies, plenty of things to collect and loot, areas to discover, and other things. Indeed just exploring new areas is extremely fun and rewarding. As you complete the main quests and layers you will get promoted to higher ranking whistles. With these you can fast travel to previous layers you have completed, depending on your progress in the main story and what whistle you have. This is a great time saver as you won't have to start at layer 1 and go all the way down to a deeper layer.  There is a lot to talk about, but it would involve going into spoiler territory.In any case, there are some negative points to talk about as well. Combat and odd development choices to name the biggest two. Combat is very simplistic, and outside of just whacking enemies with your weapon. You have a dodge, that must first be unlocked. Nothing really special here to talk about. Hit and run mechanics are useful. You have ranged weapons too, but otherwise combat doesn't vary a whole lot. Sometimes dodging doesn't work when it is supposed to, and the hitboxes of some enemies are bigger than the enemies themselves. Sometimes there are "lingering hitboxes" from attacks that visually should not be there. There are some features in the game that could have been explained better. For instance, you can make climbing easier once you unlock the lunge ability. Game doesn't really tell you that. Yes it's in the skill tree, but you won't know how useful it is until you unlock it and try it for yourself. There are shortcuts in certain areas that you will begin to see in layer 3. You have to do something to unlock them, usually pushing a rock. But unlike the ropes you have used before. These shortcuts will reset once you leave the area. Not the layer, or the abyss itself. When you leave that specific area, things will return to normal. For no logical reason. This can strand you in bad a way, but there is always a way out if you look for it, and find it. I suppose an argument can be made that parts of the abyss are canonically ever changing, but there are some shortcuts that not even this is a good explanation for. I will also talk about enemies spawning behind your back after you have been in an area for an extended period of time. These will be flying enemies that will harass you constantly when climbing or just running around. Most of the time you can crouch to make them disappear, but you can't do this while climbing. You either have to beat them up as you climb upwards and your durability on weapons will suffer plus drain your energy, or let them wail on you as you sit waiting for the curse effects to disappear. I can understand why they are there. The developer wanted to keep tension high, and force the players to make difficult decisions. Though I feel a better way could be found.In addition, small gripe on my end, but there isn't a way to customize the clothing appearance of your character. For example, one of the skills you can spend skill points on is increased backpack space. Which you will obviously want as how much you can carry will always be a constant concern. This has a secondary effect of changing the appearance of your backpack, neat. But at some point it make your backpack's visual appearance huge, like visually massive. It covers 3/4 of your character from the back view. It literally looks like your character has become a backpack with legs. It's actually ridiculous to look at. I looked for a way to change my backpack appearance to something less goofy, but the option is not there. For the rest of my adventure I felt like I was "Backpacky The Explorer". Odd development choice if you ask me. I also liked the look of some gear sets, but they had worse stats. There is no way to equip one set of armor, but have the appearance of another. Fine I suppose, but at least let me change the appearance of my backpack.I think this is where I will end my review. There is much I could say about it, but this is the basics I feel that will help other people make a more informed purchasing decision. For what it's worth, I think the game is good. Get it on sale for sure! I want to see more from this series, and this is a good...start. Definitely needs improvement, but I am looking forward to the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all sorts of jank, but behind all of the glitches and questionable game design is a generally addictive and unique game.It's a difficult game, and it's more than happy to throw you into inescapable scenarios if you didn't think to prepare yourself properly. Half the time the difficulty is challenging but fair, and during those times it's a lot of fun. Unfortunately though the other half is filled with artificial difficulty, the biggest issue being aggressive enemy spawning in many locations. This would be fine in any other kind of Dungeon Crawling game, however this game actively encourages you to scan the environment and take your time - this is a lot harder when enemies are spawning a couple metres away every few seconds if you dare move the camera slightly. This might sound like a trivial issue, but when you're in the mid-to-late stages of the game trying to fight a difficult boss, smaller enemies will  spawn just out of sight. They'll make you flinch, then it's game over.However if you have a calm temperament and don't mind losing progress due to some unfair circumstances, you get a unique innovative game. The locations are beautiful and varied whilst the soundtrack gives off an ethereal vibe - The Abyss has the perfect combo of awe and horror. The gameplay loop of exploring further and further into The Abyss collecting relics to sell back at the surface is addicting, and each time you descend you take on more risks until you inevitably bite off more than you can chew.Honestly I think this is a great game, just don’t expect it to be a polished experience. Also if you're a fan of the manga/anime, you'll appreciate the extra lore.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews deceive you. Most of them were written during a time where the game forced you to play its inferior "Hello Abyss" Gamemode.With that being said, the game features 2 Gamemodes. The aforementioned "Hello Abyss" is meant as a "Tutorial" in which you play as Riko and Reg on their way down the Abyss. Nothing you do in this gamemode carries over to the "Main" gamemode "Deep in Abyss". Do I still recommend playing Hello Abyss? Yes. But don't waste your time collecting stuff (especially Relics, they're useless in this mode). use it to get accustomed to the gameplay. The game will get tougher from here on out.Let's talk about the main gamemode now, "Deep in Abyss" has you create your own cave-raider who enlistens into the Belchero Orphanage to eventually become a White Wistle. This gamemode is where the game truly shines. The Abyss is unforgiving and even the first layer can prove deadly if you're ill-prepared. Collection and crafting equipment is fun and the skill system which is tied to your whistle rank, forces you to delve deeper and deeper to unlock more content. Many of the characters, monsters and areas from the Anime are in the game as well. I was surprised when I found the spot where Riko initially found Reg during the first episode, and standing in front of the deep chasm of the third layer gives a feeling of dread.Who is this game for?The gameplay loop kind of reminds me of Monster-Hunter a bit, with the exception that it's not (always) about hunting large monsters. You use the City Orth to equip and buy goods (Weapons, Clothes, Food, etc.) to prepare for a dive, accept quests from the Guild and other NPC's and then dive down, carefully planning to be able to make your way back.. if you can't make it back to the city from down below, you'll lose it, so plan in advance.The game has a tiny but very friendly and dedicated modding community that's hard at work fixing smaller issues.There's Mods disabling the countdown enemy spawners, replacing the ingame OST with the official Anime OST, reducing weight of items and increasing durability, allowing for more character creation options and much more.I just recently got this game on a 50% discount and I don't regret my purchase at all. It plays well on the Steam Deck and on my PC and it has me hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: It hasa lot of ups and downs. A lot of downs but if youre a die hard fan like me who can see past the imperfections of this game it is quite enjoyable for some. The glitches should be addressed and wish the save feature for the balloon was an option so I don't have to leave my computer on overnight til after I get off work. The storage space starting out is quite horrible. I have to constantly craft and eat and drop stuff and the eating speed is rough if near enemies it won't let you finish it if you get hit consistently. And the time it takes for the layer movement effects having to stop less than every minute if I'm climbing up a tall wall. Again, overall I enjoy it quite a bit. It is tasking and tedious when it comes to farming and grabbing HEAVY relics and crafting but because I love the anime and manga so much, it doesn't really bother me as much as it does others and hope people who love the anime can see what the creators of this game were trying to accomplish and how big of shoes they had to fill. Graphics, voices (except for reg...hes very puppet-like and emotionless in here for some reason knowing these are the original voice actors), designs and originality of the art and music and atmosphere it gives off like in the anime. If I were to rate it, I'd give it a 6.5/10 for the lack better acting and not really any facial changes in certain lines and scenes of any of the characters, the length it takes to level up past a red whistle not letting you increase your backpack space which makes it difficult to craft and carry several things causing you to run out of something when you really need it and the amount of time wasted sitting in one spot waiting for the layer curse to dissipate. _childDocuments_.review: When I first watched Made in Abyss, my biggest thoughts about the show was that this franchise would make the best freaking game ever. The world is amazing and beautiful, and the story is captivating, but definitely room for more exploring and world building. The characters are pretty memorable and awesome too!Onto this game. This game was not what I expected at all. When I thought of a Made in Abyss game, my mind immediately went to a Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild style open world exploration game where you would have to venture into the abyss and follow the main storyline as Riko and Reg until the end of season 1 or when they got to the entrance of the 6th layer after the 3rd movie. (However, now that we have season 2, integrating some of that would be pretty cool as well.)This game is NOT that at all. It's semi-open world where there's not that much to explore and you're always having to travel between areas through hubs rather than it being completely open. The saving system is both a blessing and a curse (no pun intended) where I either forget to save, override my old save or some other mishap (It's a skill issue, I know). The crafting is a pain because I don't know where to find some of the resources needed and the game doesn't tell you anything, I always need rope (always have rope), navigating a new area when you can't fast travel yet is the biggest pain and if you're ill-prepared for a adventure into the abyss good luck getting back. I wish the combat was a lot more snappy and not so slow, especially for the bosses and mini-bosses where I want to move around and spam my attack button. Don't even get me started with the keybinds for M&K. I would personally use controller, but you can't navigate the menu's properly (unless they fixed that). I mostly bought this game because it was a Made in Abyss game which is something that I had always wanted. I kept playing because it is fun even if it is annoying sometimes, especially if you like the franchise and that is why I am recommending this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not recommended to people who are unfamiliar with Made in Abyss and looking for an entry point to the series, or fans who want a game comparable to the anime in terms of quality.  It is only worthwhile to play if you are deeply in love with Made in Abyss’ world, lore, and characters that you want to see more of them after you watched the 1st season anime.A few glaring issues are gatekeeping.  First is the $60 price suggests this game to be something it isn’t; my advice is to wait for a sale.  Second is the ridiculously overtuned infinite enemy spawning that is a deal breaker for many players, myself included.  The solution is to download the mod that removes the infinite spawning, while the overall difficulty of the game remains unchanged.  Lastly, don’t expect a stellar original story from this game… The plot certainly has the series’ signature cruelty, but its narrative is way too incohesive to enjoy.What this game does well is to present a gameplay loop that is faithful to the original source.  The process of the main character going into the Abyss, obtaining relics, and coming back to the surface alive is the main loop of this game.  Resource management is the key to any successful expedition, and the player is rewarded by carefully planning ahead, dealing with the enemies and terrain accordingly, and finally bringing back as much relic as possible for money and exp.Another notable mention is despite the game’s PS3-ish graphics, each map and area has an overabundance of the mysterious, alluring, and dangerous atmosphere as is mentioned in the anime and manga.  With the exception of Layer 3’s maps being a massive pita, every other map is a good tourist trap and should be explored fully.TL;DR: Buy this game when on sale if you love the Made in Abyss series enough to overlook the various faults it has and enjoy the aspects it does well. Also use the mod to disable infinite spawns so this game is actually playable.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Buy if you like Made in Abyss and want to experience the Abyss in some way, pass if you don't.I was on the fence whether or not to buy this game, and after reading the top review, I had decided not to. A few weeks later though, I heard a few good things and thought "Why the heck not?"I'll preface this review in that if you're not a fan of Made in Abyss, this game probably is best passed. It's nothing special if you're not interested in the story, and it's not going to make you interested in the story by itself.If you're a fan, I feel the game does a good job in representing what the abyss in Made in Abyss is supposed to represent. It's dangerous if you're not careful, it's tedious, and can be repetitive. That's likely what a cave raider in the MiA universe experiences. Going down and up the same paths in the abyss to find the ideal path, trying a different path and realizing you might not have the supplies to return, picking up a relic only to find you have to throw something out to bring it back.The downsides:* The price of the game is AAA for something that's not AAA polished.* Graphics aren't the best; there are areas where tiling is obvious, or the texture chosen doesn't quite fit. It's an anime game, so the graphics aren't going to be realistic, but they leave something to be desired. * Enemies spawn off camera depending on how long you're in an area. It can get quite irritating, but there is an item that keeps them away.* Relic "nodes" are almost too obvious, the locations don't change, and the variety of relics is limited.* Quests boil down to either kill quests, fetch quests, or craft quests.The positives:* Inventory management is essential, as is proper planning prior to and during a delve.* The areas have some variety to them, and are interesting to explore.* The music is rather catchy* Enemies can be extremely deadly if you're not careful* Fast travel is limited based on progress in the game. I recommend against using it for immersion purposes.Overall, I enjoyed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The ugly news first: animations and landscape models are very mid. Anyone that has played the game will tell you the Inbyo boss fight is embarrassingly bad, and this is true. Boss battles also feel a bit clunky and not dynamic because of the status animations and movements. I also had no idea how to proceed in the 3rd layer at some point, but the game assumed I would have unlocked a stamina upgrade by then, which made me able to climb a certain wall and proceed. This oversight took me a while to figure out.The bad: You  N E E D a spawnrate fix mod. I've poured almost 30 hours into this game and didn't need the mod for the first 10. But some creatures can respawn WITHIN 2 FEET OF YOU and will hit you to push you off the wall you're climbing or bridge you're crossing. This infinity nearby enemy spawn is useful to avoid any softlock you might get yourself into and helps you farm materials faster, but it can be a real nuisance. Use the mod to fix it and turn the mod off when you feel like you need enemies to spawn faster.Another bad is some mini-bosses also feeling clunky. However this is not a huge issue, since ONLY the early game mini-bosses feel like that, and in the early game you should avoid these guys like the plague, and by the time you can deal with them the clumsiness isn't an issue anymore.The good:Many reviews get this wrong. THE MAIN GAME LOOP AND HELLO IN ABYSS ARE GOOD if you ask me. Hello in abyss is a 3-4 hour long tutorial where you play as riko and reg. People were very happy hello in abyss could be skipped with the new update, but you will be completely and utterly lost in the first layer of the abyss if you skip it. The main game loop for the first 30 hours in the game is somewhat like this:>Complete main story quests in the lowest layer you have access to.>Gather relics and turn them in to improve your gear.>level up, unlock the next layer and repeat.Something else that's really important that reviews don't mention: The sound design.The sound effects are satisfying, the music does not get stale after hearing it for hours while exploring, and even 30 hours into the game I keep discovering new music tracks during new types of combat and in new areas. Every BGM is fitting for the area you are in, and doesn't get repetitive as quick as most BGMs do.Another thing that a lot of reviews don't mention is RELIC SYNTHESIS!! You can make INSANELY strong weapons using relics, but crafting these is a skill tree unlock late into the game. However, at this point you still have 8+ quests to gather a certain amount of materials and research in the first and second layer. I had abandoned those quests assuming they were boring filler content, but you need some first layer relics to create your first relic weapons.You might get where I'm going with this.If you end up playing the game and progress, you will VERY likely start fast traveling to skip traversing the first layer on the way down. This is where those "filler" quests come in, the game cleverly has some half-completed quests waiting for you in the first later, along with relics and certain items you need to craft weapons which only appear in the first layer. I've not yet finished the game but I'm assuming when I unlock higher level crafting recipes, I'll start needing to use 2nd and 3rd layer relics and so on.I already poured many hours into the game, I've seen what made people think its bad, but I've been having a blast. Unlocking a new layer to discorver, holding 8 different maps next to each other to plan out a route, taking that route, making sure you dont starve, making sure you dont get hit by the curse of the abyss, fighting off pests and creatures, all while you're killing some rodents to make food to keep yourself alive. This part of the game gets very immersive and despite not having good graphics or animations, it is really fun in my opinion.VERDICT:If you love the made in abyss franchise or don't really care about graphics then yes this game is for you! If you're not so much into exploration in games and want a challenge you should definitely wait for a sale. As you can tell even most negative reviews have at least 20 hours into this game. Even though some parts don't look good or are visibly rushed, the game is **BIG**. Despite the content not being worth the triple A price the AMOUNT of content definitely is.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, This review is meant to help new interested people to answer the question "is this game worth $60?" and a simple tutorial of basic functions, I will give my opinion and a simple no-spoiler review, let's get started.		Hello Abyss: this is a basic introduction save that goes through the general story of the show, it is very short and introduces the main functions of the game. This part is not as strong as the main gameplay and has no effect or continued story (aka you can't level up as Riko and you don't get to explore or do much besides basic functions). All in all, it has its hard moments but is a really good tutorial for people. Personally, I recommend speeding through this part and getting to the main game (unless you want to learn the story, which is amazing and you should go watch the show if you like this part). Again this will only affect that specific game mode nothing in the rest of the game is affected.	Deep In Abyss: alright so this is the main game of well the game, you can pretty much go anywhere at the very start (after the required story mission). The story in this one is actually really good with new characters and lots of gameplay, This part of the game is where you can level up your character with quests and collecting relics to turn in. Now onto the actual gameplay and game aspects! Deep in Abyss gameplay: Collectables: in the game, there are 2 pick-up items (different kinds of material that all look different but are functionally the same). 	Plants: along the ground, there are many different plants that you can pick up, with different uses in crafting and quests. 	Rocks: on the walls, there are two kinds of rock that do different things, Blue sparkles: if a rock is sparkling blue it will give either a crafting material for weapons or a normal relic, Red sparkles: if a rock is sparkling red it will always give a relic with a chance to give a high-grade relic. On every level, these rocks will take on a different look but give the same type of loot (if you look into it you can find a thing called rock standing too). Enemies: This is pretty simple, there are a few kinds of enemies that give different things, but they all generally give the same loot depending on the area, Again this is spoiler-free so I won't tell you the enemies, but I will give advice on that there are small weak enemies, and large big enemies (and subsidies that are more medium). The small enemies mostly give meat and nothing else, but the bigger ones give more materials. Unfortunately, you don't get multiple drops, if you kill something you get a chance to get something out of the pool of their drops.Equipment: simple, you get a helmet slot, body slot, leg slot, glove slot, shoe slot, and backpack slot (keep in mind the backpack slot cannot be changed or removed throughout the game only upgraded through skills). some pieces of clothing can have a ruin equipped onto them that gives you a substat that will help with specific damage or statuses. next weapons, bow, gun (yes there is a gun), pickaxe, and machete, these are all simple and can be crafted, the higher whistle level you are the higher one you can buy/craft (if you unlock the weapon crafting skill required). there are different ammo types too but that's not important, weapons have durability and can break, but will be replenished IF you can make it back to the surface before they break. Skills: you have multiple different skills you can progress into, most high skills are locked and will unlock when you get a higher level whistle. You have Battle, Cave raiding, and Crafting, pretty self-explanatory.Quests: you get main quests that appear in the quest section, and side quests to complete that you get from the city after unlocking a layer/going to a new layer.	Food: what do you want from me? you eat it and depending on what you make it gives back health and hunger, you can craft or buy it. but a little hint you didn't hear from me FOOD IS LEGIT THE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO HAVE... so let's get into why	movement: you can jump, climb, sprint, attack, collect, and climb ropes, if you don't have hunger up even a little, you have no stamina, if you have no stamina, you start moving extremely slowly and can ONLY jump. Food goes down fast. way too fast, so always have food on you. Layers: so far there are only 5 layers, no spoilers though so you'll have to figure it out by getting there, (Big warning for level 3 though, just be prepared)Characters: No spoilers... duh! but I wanted to say that the characters are well voice-acted, true to the original story, and very fun to interact with. One thing you will find very early on is that anytime you pick something up they will say something generic which was annoying at first but really funny the more I played (but that might have just been because I was happy to finally do something other than suffer) Difficulty: Alright so right off the bat you will already know from other reviews this game is MEAN, if you die you will be sent back to your last auto-save (it saves every time you enter a new area, aka. gold rings) and you will lose everything you collected in that level. Fighting some enemies can be fun and quick, but some are impossible to fight whether you can touch them or not. the enemies WILL spawn infinitely in certain spots, which can get extremely annoying, but if you go into an area without much food, DO NOT mod this out of the game (this is my pure opinion, I could handle the worse parts of it which I get into soon), in curtain places if there was no infinite spawning I would have lost hours of gameplay because animals are a food source, and no food = no stamina = no climbing = absolutely f**ked. climbing can be brutal and some small enemies will spawn and body block you off your climbing killing you instantly, some can fly and instant kill you, and others can knock you off the side without giving any benefit of food. Do not be ashamed to turn it off it can get really really annoying. A problem I had was controls, throughout the game I did not use the lock-on feature once for a fight, why? because the game wouldn't let me equip it in a more convenient spot. changing controls is fine but major controls like left click or right click, it would not let me change, and I had to put major keys like q and e on attack and pick up (again no re-binding of left click for me so I couldn't change it to attack) running out of food with no hope of animals nearby is a game over, so I suggest keeping a save file near the beginning of the layer so you don't lose everything.Conclusion: Alright so we have talked about most of the functions and gameplay, now then, the true question... in my opinion "is this game worth $60?" A triple-A price indeed, So my verdict? no, I don't think this game should be sold at $60, BUT I absolutely love this game, as hard as it can be it is fun gathering, the skill system is perfect, leveling up is fun, and getting a new whistle and new main quests are fun, and the difficulty in my opinion :does not need to be changed at all: Why? it stays true to the show, the abyss is a literal hell hole that will kill you in the blink of an eye and it does, a lot. It is very infuriating at many times, but I learned and grew and so did my character showing just like in the show, how whistles grow and get better at exploring, and the game captures this absolutely perfectly, amazing game system, amazing gathering system, great fighting mechanics, and if you're familiar with the show there are so many new experiences and moments that just shinned through the pain. I personally have fallen in love with this game, it's a lot of fun learning, it's a lot of fun collecting, and the pain of failing only felt SO MUCH BETTER when you finally figured out how to survive and get back. The ending was good, and it was fun all around, But! back to my answer... Why did I say no, if I love this game so much? well... (continued in comments)

_childDocuments_.review: Well having played this game for 47 hours and getting all achievements I have some thoughts. The game is good (if you like the show/manga) and is worth playing just to experience certain things in a slightly more hands on way. However you must play through a neutered version of the first half of the season of the anime which lasts 3-5 hours before getting into the good stuff. Afterword you get to customize your torture orphan and start your bloody descent. There are many neat concepts and fun creatures to fight, although enemies constantly spawning just off screen can get tiresome. For an example you can make relic gear similar to that of white whistles, and there are even full on boss-fights with very nice rewards. However there are some major downs, the game is nicely stylized to be similar to the anime and manga but otherwise has looping textures and some wall textures are passable at best, combat is fairly simple even with max level combat skills and most enemies can just be stun locked by basic attacks. I would say in spite of this that some of the late game areas are very good looking for the graphical style, and the boss fights while cumbersome are fun and not stun lockable making you have to actually try. Over all I suppose I would give the game a high 6 or a low 7 if you like the show/manga and probably a 4.5 if you have no interest in the world or characters. (I hope as the story progresses the game will get more content also)

_childDocuments_.review: The best way i can review this game in a way that captures its charm is through a story. I'll try to sum it up in a TL;DR at the bottom in case you may find this long winded.I can see why reception on this game is mixed. It's incredibly unfortunate the first three hours is a poor tutorial that doesn't really give you a proper idea of what the meat of the game is. After clearing the forced story mode with Riko, That restricts your ability to truly adventure, which is supposed to be the main appeal of the game. You can finally start your adventure into the Abyss with your own character and experience an original story. Just like the anime, Don't let the look of this game deceive you. This is very gameplay over graphics. The gameplay is, much like the abyss itself, Unforgiving. Without including any spoilers, I went on a dive and made multiple mistakes along the way without thinking anything of it. I threw out salt to make room for more treasure, Didn't manage my food correctly, and had dived too far deep into the abyss, running out of food and resources (because i threw away my salt, i couldn't properly produce more edible food) to actually be able to make it back to the surface. I had lost 1.5 to 2 hours of progress roughly after taking another 30 minutes to realize that there was no way for me to make it back to the surface.In this moment, in any other game, i probably would have dropped the game. Yet, Despite my bitterness, each of my long term mistakes started to click in my head as i realized everything was my own fault, and such mistakes are what a careless cave raider would actually make if they became too complacent or overconfident. For some reason, this felt acceptable and kind of genius. I didn't know my character was for all intents and purposes dead until it was way too late. In this instance, the abyss had claimed another Cave Raider, and i had no one to blame but my own hubris. Now I have to start this whole dive over, but now i'll be better prepared.TL;DRThis game is not for everyone and suffers from a bad first 3 hours that misleads you on what the game is actually about. This game past those 3 hours is incredibly unforgiving, but thats how it should be if the devs TRULY wanted to capture the dangers of the abyss and how being prepared is the defining edge between failure and survival in the Abyss. You can lose large chunks of progress if you are under prepared, and this game will not hold your hand. I give this game a 9/10, but if you just read the TL;DR this game probably isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a ton of fun with this game. After the Reg and Riko tutorial mode, the real game is a fun, pretty standard, RPG-style game where you level up your character and go on deeper and deeper cave dives as you do. It's been a blast to play through the different layers I've seen in the show, interact with the characters, and get that satisfactory feeling of progression whenever I complete a long and dangerous cave dive deeper than I've ever gone before.The controls are a little clunky but after rebinding some keys/buttons they're not hard getting used to. The graphics aren't impressive but they're enough to make the world look very pretty and true to the anime - think Breath of the Wild, not impressive but they do a lot with what they have.Some minor bugs here and there, but nothing game-breaking.I've seen complaints about the gameplay but I disagree. The punishing aspects of the game are there for a reason. The curse of the abyss is a huge part of Made in Abyss and can't be removed, the durability and respawn systems are there to encourage you to complete your objectives in a timely fashion. The abyss is dangerous and it's a bad idea to stay in one zone and think you can just kill everything. And when you overcome these challenges and get back to town with a bag full of valuables to progress your character, it feels great.Overall, I recommend for anyone who's a fan of the show and doesn't think the gameplay mechanics talked about would prevent them from enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a diehard fan of the series, and just love the world of Made in Abyss in general, you'll be wonderfully charmed by this game. That being said, it's as tough as a soulslike and frustrating a lot of times. Super immersive for the world, but not really good for casual fans of the series. I don't know if it's really worth $60, but I've already got 29 hours in it upon writing this review, so maybe?
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: As many have pointed out, the first mode "Hello Abyss" is rather dull and off-putting. As a fan of the source material, I really dislike how the story was butchered. Don't really need to talk about the graphics much; everyone agrees they suck. The reason I would recommend this game is for the second part, "Deep in Abyss." Its an original story by the author of the manga, and the game really opens up to allow tons of exploration and customization. Mind you, you will probably have to remap the controls to your liking, cause the default pc controls really aren't well planned out. Well, that, or get a controller.With all this being said, though I am having fun, and would recommend this game to anyone who is willing trudge through the first part, I can't excuse this price. I recommend to wait for some sort of discount. Only reason I got it at $60 was cause I wanted to support the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Rough around the edges with many things feeling unfinished, but has a lot of good content and is very fun once you get into it.If you are a Made in Abyss fan, definitely try it out if you can spare the cost or it goes on saleOver 95% of the game occurs in the Deep in Abyss mode after the 5-6 hour Hello Abyss mode. It becomes a very different game after that with skill trees, quests, additional weapon types, clothing, relics, levelling and more. It took me 5 hours to clear Hello Abyss, and 60 hours to clear Deep in Abyss excluding most of the side quests.It was really fun to see familiar characters interacting with each other and doing quests for them. I loved to see new areas of the Abyss and learn about the creatures within, filling a bestiary with information on everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of awful in many ways, but I'm still having fun playing it.My biggest issue is how the curse doesn't really seem to matter that much, and you just avoid it pretty much entirely just by pausing every few seconds when ascending--I'd love to see a mod that tried to change that, but it might be challenge to do without redesigning a lot of the game...
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty jank and not worth full price unless you're a big fan of the IP.That said, once you get through the pretty awful and barebones tutorial mode 'Hello Abyss' (I just ran through the last quarter or so to get it over with, you don't need to gather/craft anything not required by the main quest) and reach the second mode, 'Deep In Abyss', it becomes far more fleshed out. It's clear that this mode is where 90% of dev consideration went.In this mode, the game gets a lot more open ended exploration wise, and the real game loop actually begins (explore, look for relics, craft/manage resources, track a path back to Orth, sell/appraise relics and level up, improve gear and repeat but getting a little deeper each run). The difficulty ramps up, and there is also a new story written by Tsukushi for this mode that is surprisingly compelling with several easter eggs and character interactions for the fans. There are still issues with this part of the game as mentioned in other reviews, like the spawn rate of trash mobs and the weight restriction, but these can and have been modded. Looking at the patch notes for Chime's other game on here I'm not holding my breath for an official fix.Overall I would say give this a chance on sale if you have a tolerance for jank, are an MiA superfan, or both, as there is a genuinely fun game here with some interesting mechanics I haven't seen anywhere else, that decently evokes the feeling of the anime. Piss meter restoration mod when?
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am really enjoying it. It does have a really slow start and long tutorial.. and there are definitely some QoL things I would change. I would definitely also change the spawn rates for enemies and how close they spawn to you. That is honestly probably the most annoying thing in the game. Other than that I would say this is mainly an exploration survival game, and its actually pretty hard once you get to Deep in Abyss mode. Lets of prep work to do before each dive into the abyss, because you really can easily become soft locked down there and have to start completely over if you stay down there too long and are not prepped to be down there that long. Once you get to layer 3 you really start feeling how open and big the game is. Slow start, and some weird design choices, dated but still surprisingly pretty graphics at some times. Over all its way better than I expected it to be. Lots of reviews judging it far too early. Also if you don't like games with a lot of gathering, crafting, and survival elements, you probably will not like this game. If you like the show then you know the Abyss is brutal, and they didn't change that here.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: It's really an excellent game. Makes you as if you're in Abyss. It's not an easy game and you may game over for multiple times, but it's really what'd happen in Abyss. I also like the story very much. Still in Tier 2, but looking forward to meeting to Riko later.  Another thing I enjoy is the detailed description of the ecology (and different items) in Abyss - it completes the anime and manga. People complain about how annoying part of the game is, but I'd say that's just small problems and the point is to enjoy the world of Abyss.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: I had bought this game day one and had done quite a bit in the couple of hours. The tutorial is around 3 hours long and that does end up putting people off but once that is done you get into the real meat of the game. It is amazing how it pulls you in and invokes you on exploring the abyss as we have always wanted from those who have watched the Anime. It does require some polish though and the AI is very aggressive but you can turn that into an advantage easily. I do recommend a sale but for someone like me who wanted to jump right in there. I can recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: The real game starts after the "Hello Abyss" game mode and it's quite enjoyable, you play as your own character and slowly rise in the Whistle ranks and descend deeper and deeper into Abyss. The game isn't for everyone and I would recommend for a average person to get it on a discount but for a fan of the series it can be a treat.

I will not be asking for a refund, as there is still more for me to do in the game; but if you are looking to buy this, wait for it to go on sale.Next, the """Tutorial,""" Hello Abyss. _childDocuments_.review: Lots of bugs and bad design choices can make this game incredibly frustrating. However. The sense of satisfaction from accomplishing a goal is very strong in this game.  Little touches, like the save function being an in-universe item (that doesn't function if you don't have a clear view of the sky) add to immersion.  The early sections of the Abyss with poor lighting and boring platform-hopping give way to some rewarding scenery as you get deeper.  The community for this game is one of the better ones I have ever seen, and the games first mod fixes the problems with endless spawning mooks.A lot of people have complained about how easy it is to get softlocked.  They are right, it is really easy to find yourself trapped with no choice but to give up and lose hours of progress.  Once you realize that is reality and start meticulously planning every piece of equipment you take on your dives, the game completely changes.  I genuinely have fun laying out all the salt, light hatchets, torches, and mountains of boiled eggs.  Setting a weight goal of my pack depending on where I am headed and what I plan to accomplish is completely engrossing.  Even with careful preparation, it is still entirely possible to get stuck so you never really relax.  As you get stronger whistles, you become able to fast travel out of earlier layers and that sense of danger is lessened.  I still kinda miss the terror of climbing out of layer 3 once the last of the salt is gone, hoping I have enough supplies to make it back and cringing as I discarded hard-earned relics to make a little more room in the pack.I don't know if this is what Tsukushi was thinking when he imagined the Abyss, but it sure does feel like I am lost in Uncle Lovecraft's Funtime Murder Hole.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Made in Abyss, its my all time favourite manga and anime. While this game is well made in some aspects like music and atmosphere. the game itself is not worth the triple A price. The graphics are mediocre at best and the recurring audio cues and voice lines from any partners you have (Reg, Nat etc) trigger every time you scavenge an animal or a plant which does get annoying. The game also does not help you much, I had to go into the control settings to figure out I had a headlamp to use. Please wait for this game to go on sale or have a reduced price if you really want to play it, it is not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is a great game that suffers from some very questionable design decisions and brutal difficulty – the „I want to waste your time” kind of difficulty, which will put off a lot of people. If you are not into that, you most probably won’t enjoy it. It’s not buggy nor glitchy, but it’s very unforgiving and may be downright unplayable without at least minor modding.The first big problem is the game mode selection, which sounds good at first because it makes it seem as if there is more content in the game. The reality is that the original story-based game mode is really a form of a tutorial for the main mode of the game. All shops, crafting and leveling are very limited, which you are not told. The real game gets unlocked after beating this 3-5 hour „intro” based on the original story. This also makes it seem as though the game is very short. The length of the main story is already listed as 4 hours on some websites, which is false, as this is not the real game mode but just a sneak peek into what’s to come.Once you get to the „Deep Abyss” mode, which is the actual true gameplay of Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness, is when things get real. The difficulty ramps up in a crazy way. Hp, food, stamina meters, bag capacity, limited fast travel, curse of abyss and worst of all: Infinite enemy spawning behind your back after 5 minutes of exploring will all be things that will accompany throughout the journey. Thankfully, there is a community made mod that removes the Infinite enemy spawning, which for me personally, was what made the game playable. If you’re planning to get the game please get it for your own mental health. The devs have posted that they are looking into bugs and game balance so maybe this gets fixed in the future by them, but we will have to wait and see.The gameplay loop itself can be fairly enjoyable. You set out to explore the abyss, each layer divided into multiple areas. You harvest supplies, kill enemies, navigate cliffs and so on. The game follows a main story quest and also offers a lot of side quests, both randomly appearing as well as available in the guild location in the city. Once you set aside the game’s issues it will be a great experience for any anime/manga fan for sure. In the game you can explore up to and including the 5th layer and meet many of the characters from the original story on your journey. Beating the whole game took me about 40 hours. Then there’s also a good couple hours of ‘endgame’ content, you can keep leveling, getting gear upgrades, and there are actual optional side quest lines including characters from the original story.All in all if you can get over the punishing difficulty there’s a lot of fun to be had here, especially for enjoyers of the original material. The general reception wasn’t that great so you can probably expect discounts soon. Get it then, if you’re on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: Very tentative recommend. I was going to recommend against this, but, I instead opted for a "yes". I have only gotten as far as beating the retelling of the anime, and I looked at it and said "is this it? this is meant to show off what the rest of the game is like?"After I beat it, I immediately jumped to the other mode to see. It has much more available...which I've yet to get to, and may change this review later but. The game clearly has much more available I've yet to try, and the tutorial (the OG anime story) made the worst of potential impressions for the rest of the available content.Otherwise, it's a fun game with a bit of repetition. I was able to go almost 5 hours through it nonstop.  I did experience a semi-soft lock toward the end where I didn't have any salt to make food with, and because travelling between two zones costs food...well, yeah. I'd run out of food, not be able to craft more, and be locked. So I had to go into Cheat Engine and edit my food value to 100. This was partially my own fault, 'cause I'd craft a lot of food and just keep eating it for fun (I was joking with friends while looking at the eating animation), and ate way more than I should've. Still, should've been opportunities later on to craft more food that wasn't egg and bug recipes (if RNG favored me)

_childDocuments_.review: You're initially made to play as Riko and set out to do bits and pieces of her 'story' if you could call it that. It's basically just an hour or so long tutorial without an actual tutorial.The actual 'game' starts after you finish that tutorial which so far? It's a bit of a mess, the curse system becomes a major pest  instead of a major mechanic of the game. Even traveling up small inclines would have your threshold fill up, or simply jumping in place like a gremlin which was funny at first.Just writing this down for friends and such. It has potential, but nothing a patch will fix at all. Probably would have been great if it was just all Riko and Reg with QTE's like Asura's Wrath at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Came back to change my review like I promised. The graphics are so bad I can't believe I don't get motion sickness from this. (From someone who puke after 30 minutes on minecraft.) The keyboard bindings are horrible, you can't change it to bind with mouse. I've had my left pinky on the ctrl for the entire time running. Z for targeting is basically useless to me, as you won't have a finger to press X for attacks while running on WASD and Ctrl. I've seen people mentioning the enemy spawn rates, sometimes they're helpful, but with the fast travel doesn't worth the two cents it implements. You can only fast travel to the start of each layer after you obtain a higher rank than your current depth, which doesn't make sense because you'll be doing tons of exploring in the new area and not the repetitive quests. It's not about making the game easy. Traveling back up to a certain location doesn't sound that illogical to implement. Imagine coming up and having to go down again to a point in-between, who does that?Games at this price should at least have 30hrs of play time full of content. The game makes up for this by its horrible amount of gathering quests to prolong the time you have to spend on this game. I don't even see an open world game this bad. The hello abyss mode was horribly executed, such that they only explain the tutorial to you in the second mode after you trial and error yourself what skills Riko already possessed. It's blatant. After you spend your three hours replaying a bad version of the anime getting amazed all your imagination in 3d only to find it stops at layer 3 you can't refund the game. Had I been able to see all their horrible quest system had to offer I would've stopped playing 30 minutes in.I'll add more but this doesn't worth 60 bucks. I've seen people say 30; I'd say 25 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've gotten a chance to play the deep abyss mode my opinion has changed a lot from my first impressions on day 1. The hello abyss mode (story mode) really didn't put the games best foot forward and left me very disappointed. If there is a hack or something in the future that let's new players skip it I would recommend doing so and go right to the main game (deep abyss mode). I can't say much about the quality of the game mechanics and gameplay because I dont play rpgs and have never played a game like this before but I can say that I have been having fun with it so far. I know people have been upset with the graphics but I knew this game was coming out on switch so I didn't have high expectations in that department. When comparing the graphics to a switch game like pokemon legends arceus I think it holds up suitably. My advice for new players is to not play this game unless you have seen at least the first season of the anime. Even though the game trys to explain to you the story in hello abyss mode it does a horrible job and will spoil the beginning of what is an amazing show.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll leave this review short and sweet. This game is severely misunderstood. Frankly if you haven't made it past the admittedly obnoxious tutorial, you shouldn't be allowed to review.Here are my criticisms:Characters look fantastic*Some* locations look great.*Some* locations look like ass, aka they are out of a wii game.Tutorial is nonoptional and is around 2-3 hours, which is why this game got a surge of bad reviews on its release. Keybindings for controller on PC are strange, but you adapt. Curse mechanic is there which I understand is the series's staple, but I think it'll frustrate people new to MiA.After the tutorial the game is much more enjoyable with lots of creatures to see, characters to meet, and relics to find. I saw someone complained the character creator is limited but I thought it was okay. Its about the same as Animal Crossings. While the abyss may not be pure open world Skyrim experience you are looking for, it offers a sort of rogue-like Metroidvania experience that I personally find satisfying. You might find a special grotto, a rare relic/creature, etc!Overall, I think this is best for Made in Abyss fans. If you like the anime and can get past the tutorial, you will probably like this. Seeing the characters and creatures come to life is really cool, and exploring the abyss at your own pace is fun! Whether you decide to pay full price for it is up to you, but I think it's worth playing whether you decide to wait for a sale or not. Ps, The company that made this game said they won't be releasing DLC, I figured that's worth mentioning. I wouldn't be surprised if a mod or too comes out for the game though.

_childDocuments_.review: Take the Dive of Your Life! Made in Abyss, the breathtaking manga and anime series by Akihito Tsukushi, is getting its first ever video game adaptation! Experience the Anime's Story - The story begins with Riko and Reg's meeting in the first episode of season one. This marks the start of their great adventure, and together they travel to Seeker Camp in the second layer of the Abyss. Experience the awesome power of the Curse of the Abyss, as well as the astonishing, legendary entities known as primeval creatures. Prepare to glimpse the world of Riko and her friends. Experience a Brand-New Story - Another story takes place many days after Riko and Reg depart for the Abyss. The world’s sole remaining, unconquered chasm, the Abyss, is the stage where many adventures are born...and disappear. Those who appear in these stories are mesmerized by the power of the Abyss and aim for the bottom of the netherworld. The story about to be told is of the adventures of a nameless Cave Raider in the Abyss.
