name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef
detailed_description: Join the Discord! About the Game Prepare to charge Luteus Prime For many centuries, the planet of Luteus Alpha has been producing much needed materiel for the wars raging on in the Armageddon sector. Many are drawn to the planet, and so is the great Warboss Ogruk Gutrekka. Upon arriving on the planet, Gutrekka took your most precious hair squig. Filled with vengeance you’ve sworn to do anything it takes to return your hair squig, and prove who is the strongest! And so your adventure on Luteus Prime begins. Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef is a hand-drawn 2D action adventure taking you on a wild ride of dakka, gore and explosions! Krump your way through the hive city of Luteus Prime; battle Humans, Orks and Genestealer cultists; and ultimately retrieve your luscious hair squig from the hands of the Warboss Gutrekka! Who’s ready for Waaagh!? Game Features: Classic 2D side-scrolling goodness, filled with intense action, funny one-liners, screaming deaths and comical dialogues! Choose your class, picking between four distinct characters, each with their own unique toolkit true to the Warhammer 40,000 lore. Inflict chaos with an arsenal of weapons at your fingertips. Expand your armory with up to twenty different weapons. There’s no such thing as having too much dakka! Unleash your Waaagh! at the right time! Wreak carnage and rain destruction on those puny ‘umies. Challenge the mightiest empire in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Become victorious, bring the planet to its knees and lead your very own Waaagh! Earn hats by destroying compelling bosses, completing milestones or exchanging Teef at the Mekboy shop. Teef are collected by tearing through the story. Beautiful hand-drawn scenery gives an incredible sense of depth to a side-on world. Break up the action, and immerse yourselves in engaging cinematics. Set foot on Luteus Prime in single-player mode, or get a party together of up to four Ork Boyz and have some fun together! Multiplayer is available both online and in local co-op. Brawl it out against your rivals in an all-out epic battle to decide who is the baddest Ork in the warband! Up to four boyz can scrap it out in the arena, both online and in local PvP. Get your socks rocked off with an amazing heavy metal soundtrack, composed by Deon van Heerden. Yes, there will be explosions. Like, a lot of them!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very short for its price, and while it can be described as a 'good' time rather than a long time, it is still very overpriced. Even farming kills in multiplayer for the last achievement only took me about five hours; the campaign was 2.5 hours on the hardest mode. I think for the price, it should have more content. That being said, it is very true to the lore in the 40k universe and one of the few games that accurately portrays 'Orkiness'. The soundtrack is one of the best I have ever heard in a 40k game, so that is well done too. There are still crashes; in my five hours, the game got locked twice, and it quit with an error in multiplayer once. This game still needs more patches. I hope the devs fix it soon.Overall, good to pick up to kill a few hours minus the bugs for a rip-roaring good time. But it ends too quickly. Pick it up on sale if you want it, not for full price. I give it a 7 out of 10 until the bugs are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'z reallly torn on dis. On da one 'and I'z zoggin grate dat wez gots a proppa game, da humor iz grate, da muzac is great and iz fun. On da uva da classes lack diversity with the storm boy and beast snagga being the two most different with the storm boy having a jetpack that can light enemies on fire and lets you evade over a longer distance while the beast snagga has a throwable explosive melee and an attack squig bomb. The Weirdboy and Flashgit don't really have anything going for them. Some of the guns are fun, the laser shotgun especially since it can fill up the entire screen with lasers, the flamer feels nice, but over all most of the guns lack punch and feel like someone tried too hard to balance them so they end up kinda weak. I feel like this game could benefit greatly from a level up system and adding more variety to the classes. The game is fairly short, which isn't bad since it's a fun little story, but I also crashed multiple times during it. I guess I'll recommend it since it would probably be a lot more fun with friends and because I feel like it's so close to being a fantastic game like castle crashers but its just missing something.Now I'm just going to kinda list some ideas I had playing that I feel might help.As I said before some sort of level up system so that as we progress we can feel ourselves getting more powerful and rather than just picking up boxes of teeth having enemies drop them.What I would really love to see is mixing up the ults so that the classes feel more unique, like having the weirdboy do some psychic nonsense, the beast snagga goes berserk increasing melee damage and attack speed, the storm boy jets around and the flashgit can keep the unlimited ammo. Just some ideas

_childDocuments_.review: People who view any game purely in a dollars to hours ratio are dooming themselves to picking up dinosaur ♥♥♥♥♥ forever.  Me, for the price of purchase, I got an absolutely brilliant soundtrack. That soundtrack also came with a fun game, by coincidence, and that game came with a hit of nostalgia for Flash and the old websites that hosted Flash games.  RIP in peace, Flash.But this is a game site.  So let me tell you about it.  You want an executive summary?  Platforming combat.  Really combat, with a side order of some platforms, but there's no tricky jumps to make.  You're an Ork. You don't do jumping puzzles.  You shoot things.  Dakka is the solution to every problem.I say it's like Flash because every character has this chunky kind of animation that looks like several discrete pieces are rotated, but nothing is ever really deformed.  Flash did a lot of that.  Here's an arm piece, there's a head, maybe two torso pieces, and you rotate them around to make it look animated.  And, usually, the animations are really overdone.  This is no exception.  It's the flashiest flash animation since a site that sounded like "congregate" but with a K.In the Warhammer 40k universe, well, most everything is dour.  Really, every last faction except the death-killer "undead" robots... and the orks.  The orks are ramshackle, live only for fighting, and they'll fight each other if there's nobody else to fight.  Nothing else enters into the equation. And then they talk in goofy but gruff cockney-esque voices and... honestly, I could go on, but it's enough to say they're an entertaining faction, a rare bright light in a world full of soggy concrete hallways and for-the-emperors, and I had my fill of that a long time ago.Is this a short game?  By the time I wrote the review, I'd completed it.  I enjoyed it, I grinned like an idiot at a few of the cutscenes, I shot a lot of boyz, beakies and other assorted oomies, plus a couple spiky boys and extra-armed oomies.  I'm quite satisfied.  I could do the PvP mode but likely never will, and the odds of me replaying this in coop are vanishingly small.And I don't mind one bit.  Like I said, the purchase price was the soundtrack.  The game, for me, was the extra.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game from a really good creator. If you've played Guns, Gore and Cannoli you just need to know this game is that same dose of goodness except in 40k flavor.For those of you who haven't known fun yet i can describe the game as thus;you're an ork thats obvious, the gameplay is pretty straightforward which is good because as an ork you are pretty damn stupid.There are several weapon categories to choose from and you can carry 1 of each type furthermore you can choose between 4 versions of each said weapon each one with different effects, some minor some major.You also get some bare bones class options as you can play as 1 of several types of character.These different characters only get a few minor differences between each other. Namely grenade type and melee weapon, despite how different the skin of each class might make you look its sad that you only get these minor changes between them.Now while your ork is great and all and has his own fun personality you get to ride along with its the enemies that really steal the show with their variety and designs. If you're a fan of 40k you'll be able to easily recognize not only each faction but each unit type even, the fact that i can pick out each type of proper unit  easily is testament to how good the art design for this game was, there was some real love put in here.Sound track is nothing but constant bangers with fantastic heavy metal tracks pushing you through each combat, one might wonder what kind of music plays during down time but thats irrelevant as downtime is NOT orky and therefore not worth even considering.The cutscenes (which are unfortunately pre rendered) are really fun and well animated. This team has come a long way from the GG&C's stiff newgrounds tier animations. The entire adventure feels like a fever dream told to you by a drunk ork in some dive bar. Its constantly over the top but not in a way that ever yanks you out of the game.I've had some crashing issues with the game but hopefully these will be addressed soon.I had lots of fun, its worth getting for the simple asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're in need of not just a game to play with friends but an actually good one too, look no further than:WGGHH!!!!While some might complain it's short, just like I tell my girlfriend, it's not the size that matters, it's how much fun 1-4 people can have with it that matters. A huge benefit of the size of this game is the fact that you get to try out new weapons against fellow orcs, chad space marines, and mechs at a fast rate before you can get bored. That’s when the final boss shows up and feels lackluster compared to earlier ones, a classic example of bigger doesn't always mean better, I'm talking about boss size here. Speaking of killing, you can friendly fire, which is a way for a co-op game to be in the upper echelon of amazing co-op games, so I would highly recommend it if you have these things called human friends. There's even a combo for co-op play: where one shocks and stuns with an AOE lightning gun, and the other chainsaws freely without risk of dying unless they are immune to stun, which I “never” experienced. Unlike lazy games, here modifying your weapon changes how it functions, not small percentages. Your shotgun can be turned into basically a flamethrower, a laser scattershot bouncing off walls thing, or a beefy big quad shotgun that takes forever to reload. Each variant of pistol, rifle, or rocket has a use case, so try them all out. My personal favorite weapon is called a “deathbeam”. Apparently, the game and its bosses are lore accurate or so I'm told by my Warhammer friend that gifted me this game trying to convince me Warhammer is amazing. I'm not sold yet, but this game is on the right track and is easily approachable to anyone not aware of the universe. It's more humorous than other ones I've played and the story is simple. The orc boss steals your cool hairpiece, you need to retrieve it. If you’re not convinced this short cheap game is worth getting, there is that short highlight video posted above that also showcases how metal the soundtrack gets at times. Also, there are specials from classes you choose at the start of each level and the one I picked happened to be more deadly against us than our enemies, so I don’t want to talk about it, I’m not mad, just embarrassed.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence on whether to give this a thumbs up or down, but will ultimately give it a thumbs up for just the sheer love and passion these devs have given to the orks. If you are a ork fan, this is a must buy. If you are a warhammer fan, this is on the upper scale for warhammer games and has some great fan service you'll likely enjoy. If you are just a regular gamer looking for a fun "castle crashers but with guns" type coop experience, then you'll probably like this game too as the gameplay is really fun, boss fights are intense, and the music is top tier. However, I have some warnings. First, the game can be pretty buggy (especially for coop). Between playing this with both my friends, we had disconnections,dying as we killed the boss caused the game crash, people failing to spawn, and one instance where a leman russ boss disappeared half way through it's boss fight. It's not down right enough to kill me loving the game, but it is common enough to be annoying. Second warning I gotta give is this game is SHORT. You probably can finish it within 2-4 hours, and while you can find teef to buy new weapons and hats, you'll probably get most of what you want in your first playthrough. I admittably haven't tried the verse mode yet so that might add some more value, but I still debate if this would be worth $20 (though these days video game skins are worth $20 so I guess there are still worst ways to waste $20). My recommendation would be wait for a sale and see if any friends would like to play it with you. Then you can do a single and coop playthrough. Despite it's issues, this game was a nice short, but really fun and funny experience. It's just got too much charm and WAAAAGH for me to hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is great, the art style is lovely, and the game nails the Ork humor. The only downsides are a handful of mostly funny visual bugs alongside one annoying bug where an elevator wouldn't come back up when a coop friend used it resulting in me dying just to keep playing the level and the coop campaign disconnected me and my friend multiple times and seemed mildly unstable at others resulting in lag.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong this game is amazing! Satisfying gameplay, excellent voice acting, a simple story to follow, and amazing soundtracks (Same guy who also composes Broforce apparently). This is entirely perfect for an Ork game. That being said however I wouldn't recommend this game for the reason that it's just too short.You can beat the game's story in just about 2-3 hours, even on the highest difficulty. After that, there's not much you can do other than multiplayer. Sure you can go and find all the secrets in the game, unlock every cosmetic or achievement, or play on a higher difficulty......Which is essentially playing the game's story again. Overall, Gameplay, voice acting, levels, and soundtracks are great! But content-wise, It's too short of an experience to justify its price. I would recommend this game however if this were to receive some more content or DLC (I doubt that would happen anytime soon.) or if you find this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop is basically running around shootin' or krumpin' things with yer mates, and pretty much flying though the who's who of the 40k universe. The action is exceptionally smooth, and the gunplay is lots of fun. Often times you find yourself beaming a big ole smile (like your Ork) as you mow down wave after wave of enemy.The weapon choices are exciting, each costing a fair investment of teef, and dramatically changing how you approach encounters. I enjoyed trying different weapons, seeing what worked and just generally switching between them to be the most annoying ork possible. Not sure which was my fac , but it kept the loop engaging, and made it fun to stay at it, even for a couple of hours at one sitting.The game's pacing is fairly fast, and while it never gets truly adrenaline-pumping, it's engaging and there's always a squig to find, humie to krump or shootin' to be done. On to the negatives (boy, there are more of these than I'd realized)- - I realize this game has just released, but I've had persistent issues with restarting from checkpoints whenever the entire team goes down. The loading screen does show up, but the bar tends to get stuck at about 70%.- There are also times when moving pieces of the level (trains, conveyor belts etc) are in different places for different players. This makes it difficult to keep your dakka in one place, and in tougher sections could even get you kilt.- The classes fail to distinguish themselves throughout the entire length of my game with my friends. There were certain sections where we even tried to deliberately play into the roles to get that synergy out of them , but it was almost always better to just improve movement and learn boss patterns.- The objectives at certain parts are poorly signposted, we often spent a few moments at the ends of each level wondering what to do, only to realize that the entire party needed to go to the far right, or needed to group up in a chamber or on a lift.- One slightly more thorny issue is that imo the campaign mode doesn't fit the price tag (and I blame GW's licensing cut). There's maybe 3 hours of good waagh to be had, and without any further fun game modes or story to play through, the player experience just ends right there.- Finally, there was an odd bug we had with one of the players on our team (who picked Evil Sunz) who just straight was invisible to us for most of the playthrough. It was incredibly hard keeping track of where he was, and without discord to help, we'd have spent hours trying to group up in the right places to progress the level.Overall, I'd give it about 7/10, fun, cute, and a great introduction to 40k through the eyes of the best faction (fight me), but ultimately lacking the oomph to follow through.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Castle Crashers meets Warhammer 40k. I imagine this is how all Orks view their lives in the 40k universe, horrific and maniacal violence but filtered through a whacky, cartoonish filter. In fact this whole game might be viewed as an Ork fever dream, seeing as our special green space thug solos a Genestealer Cult, an Imperial Knight, a few Space Marines, some Primaris ♥♥♥♥ and a Gargant ALL HIGHLY IMPROBABLE but whatever I don't care, you don't play an Ork and expect to be tactical and realistic.The game is very fun but it is also very short. Online multiplayer is not that active and will likely be completely dead going forward. I would wait for a sale if money is important to you. But if you love Orks and want to enjoy a decent 40k game that's not turn based ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the 100000th time (you can count them on 1 hand), then this might be your jam, I certainly enjoyed myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good warhammer game, compared to multiple others!Classic platformer-shooter gameplay, variety of bosses and 3 enemy factions overall (imperium, orks and genestealer cult), also there is a pool of guns and classes to pick from. I enjoyed writing also (Guy Haley is one of the script authors - you could've heard the name if you read Black Library books) - game has a set of good jokes, while staying ridiculously true to wh40k canon! Game is relatively short - I finished it in one evening, but it definitely was a good time, giving me a challenge on highest difficulty. Overall - a musthave for a warhammer fan!

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef is an enjoyable and entertaining game, especially due to the delightful Ork humor that permeates the experience. The gameplay itself is decent. However, the game does fall a bit short in terms of length. After my first playthrough, I completed it in about 3-4 hours. Extending the gameplay by an additional 2-4 hours would have made for a more fulfilling experience.One notable issue is the game's tendency to crash, particularly during boss fights. Given the game's relatively short length and the fact that it is 2D, these crashes become more frustrating. Despite this, most of the boss fights are well-designed and some are exceptionally amusing. Unfortunately, the final boss does not live up to expectations, proving to be extremely easy and somewhat anticlimactic.

_childDocuments_.review: After Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2, I was looking forward to this game more than almost any AAA title in recent memory.However... Everything is worse, and I mean everything.Movement: You don't move as fluidly in this game, the double jump is lower, and the dash doesn't seem to have any real benefit while in a combat arena aside from getting away from groups of enemies, whereas in GGC2 it was integral to reach different platforms.Weapons: You hold 1 pistol, 1 machinegun, 1 shotgun, 1 rocket/grenade launcher, and presumably another couple of types. While it seems like you would want to be switching depending on the situation, it's more likely you'll find a variant you prefer for handling the stages, and then switch to an appropriate one when coming across the boss challenges. They all have infinite ammo, which seems fun until you see what effect that has on choice and game balance; gone are the decisions you'd make between squeezing the last few rounds out of your favorite weapon or holding onto the ammo for a tougher encounter.Art direction: Everything is shades of brown, grey, black, and yellow. The lack of detail in anything, including character models, but especially the foreground, makes moving through the world incredibly boring. You'll see the same graffiti a half dozen times in the first hour of playing the game on the same surfaces and wonder what the artists spent their time on.Sound: The MC doesn't say much, and what he does say is repeated far too many times to be interesting to hear. Vinny from GGC was a stereotype done right, with interesting and funny things to say which don't boil down to only being angry and saying waagh. Also the sound effects for guns and things getting hit are soft, no impact. And the music is barely there, a droning bass that doesn't really go anywhere. Where is the rock? The drums? The metal?Story: Orks are dumb and the story is silly, which is 100% totally fine. What isn't fine is how redundant the events are. An ok intro to the story leads to a lot of WAAAGH and nothing else, and you'd expect something else, anything else.Enemies: They still run at you, and the still shoot at you, and they still die and lose heads and explode, but for some reason it's not as satisfying. Also, their bullets travel extremely fast, too fast for your eyes to sometimes tell in between the zoomed-in action and samey backgrounds.Level design: GGC2 had so much detail and inspiration in the levels and their design in concert with the weapons and enemy placement that Shootas just can't reach. Compare the first levels of both games back to back; one filled with verticality, introduction to your main abilities, and weapons, and see for yourself just how much was lost here. I don't understand how you could go from a city with awnings, which let you enter a building from multiple floors, and snipers to some boxes with a single snipers above some "spawnboxes" of enemies and not tell you are doing something wrong. In fact in the first level there are engines dangling above enemies, but you cannot shoot them down; there doesn't appear to be any stage interaction aside from exploding barrels and ripping a dozen-shot heavy gun from its mount.After Guns, Gore, & Cannoli 2, I expected better, but what I got was much, much worse.If you loved GGC2, do yourself a favor and pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas, Blood, & Teef is a nice short game where you play as the only race that's having fun in this universe the orks. The story is simple, you want your wig back from the guy who shoved you out of a plane, along the way you'll kill the imperial guard, gene stealer cultist/tyranids, the baby crocodile you flushed when you were 6, space marines, and orks who look at you funny.The gameplay is 2d platform shooter, and your given the 20 guns to do it and 4 dinstinct...ish(I'll talk about them soon.) classes to kill anything to get your wig back and be da boss. The game can be beaten in about 4-5 hours (3 i your just stupid good), but it's got some fun replay value if you wanna kill an afternoon. While this game can be played with friends it isn't required to have a fun time.Now some flaws with the game, other than it's short run time, but (I want more) isn't really a flaw. I just lied to you, 20 dollas is a lot for 4-5 hours if you don't feel like replaying it. The classes are also a mixed bag. The, Flash Git, Storm Boy, Weird Boy, and Beast Snagga all use the same guns with grenades and melee being different. Now those grenades can make the difference since the weird boy's can stun, and melee isn't really encourage except for the beast snagga because it isn't a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ melee it's a spear that explodes you throw(and it's good). The flash git also sometimes doesn't use ammo when he shoots and uses molotovs. You will notice a difference when you play a campaign with one and switch9I beat the game with flash git and wondered why it felt i reloded more as a beast snagga before i realized), but they still feel a little samey since they all use the same guns.Said guns can sound a little weak other than the shotgun, but they get the job done and the music should be blaring loud enough you won't mind hearing it more than your guns. The only real downside is the short time and class semi-diversty in my opinion. Oh also I'm sure some lore guy is pissed one orc did so much, but if 1 orc beating an imperial titan gets you angry more at the lore than the fact you beat a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ titan why are you here?(I barely know the lore other than tid bits here and there so no warhammer bias.)Personally if this game gets some dlc that lets you play more( I wouldn't mind fighting the kreig, the tau, or really anyone if i can shoot more.) I'd say buy it. As it stands get it's on sale, or you have a little extra spending money, or you love this type of game. Certainly get it if you want to play with friends because why WAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGH alone when you can WAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAGH as a group?

_childDocuments_.review: A short, fun action filled run n' gun that can be appreaciated by fans and outsiders of the Warhammer community.My review to Shootas, Blood & Teef after 60 hours of playtime: Story: It's obvious that the story is more of an afterthought than the focus, but it works lorewise, because player with no knowledge of the 40k universe find themself in Teefgrabba who cares only about fighting and his mcguf... aem I mean hairsquigg and 40k nutters can enjoy all the easter eggs and inside jokes. Powerscaling is completly off though. Yes, in a book some Orks and a buggy killed a Titan, but they didn't just shoot it until it dies, meanwhile a single Ork in this games mows down Tanks, Knights and White Scars like nothing. I feel like we give it a pass just because it's "whacky Ork game" which brings me  to Asthetics: The cartoony artstyle can be called...controversial when the first trailers dropped. But from Hammer and Bolter to the 40k mobile games I'd say it's not the worst. It definitly helps that we play as the comic relief faction that allows a lighter style in the grimdark of the far future to work. I personally call it the "pyrovision" effect, where a brutal and violent world is shown cute and funny through the eyes an inhuman character. But outside of 40k compatibility it's a solid and strong art direction. Especially the Knight, good work converting this overdetailed monstrosity while still being able to see it as such. It's going to age like fine whine the coming years and will keep its character. I only have a few nitpicks with scaling, f.ex. how big a regular guardsmen is compared to Teefgrabba. Now finally to what we came for: Gameplay: Not many have played Roguesides other games, but I did so let me tell the following: This game feels like Guns, Gore & Cannoli 3. A lot of enemies, obstacles and set pieces have been slightly altered and been used from Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2 and implemented, which isn't inherently bad. They fixed a lot of issues I had with this game, f.ex. the lack of weapon feedback and the sheer amount of superfluous weapons ,like 4 automatic weapons that all feel the same and just overcomplicate the weapon wheel.The weapons in Blood & Teef feel amazing. The sound, the kickback, the enemies reaction, way better than the Cannoli 2 roster who all felt like the tanks of Wii play. The change to from 10+ weapons to 5 weapon slots with 4 options each was a great change to make the combat flow more smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost a good game. The animations are basically Flash from the early 2000's, but whoever set that up really enjoyed making the cartoony look. The music's annoying Metal more often than not, and I turned it off.The problem, as with so many games like this, is all the little stuff.1. Control loop feels mushy and unresponsive. It's like the controls are polled only once every quarter-second or something. It's hard to do a double-jump sometimes, and as that's integral to gameplay, well.2. Gunplay isn't very good. The problem here is that I think they balanced the weapons for multiplayer, which does not work out for singleplayer, at all. There are weapons that just feel useless, like the saw- its damage output and hitbox are both tiny and wrong. There are weapons that feel like they were nerfed into oblivion because they worked too well in four-player free-for-all, like the Zzap Cannon- it's useless for SP. There are weapons where I'm really not sure why they were allowed to suck, like the Deth Beam and the Squig Launcher, the Sticky Rokits, the Quad Shotgun, etc. These all feel like things where nobody tested the feel in single-player properly before release. Very few of the weapons you buy feel like genuine upgrades, other than the totally-broken Guided Missile that allows you to clear whole sections by shooting off-screen. It's like, in a game that's basically supposed to be silly good fun, the developers just kind of forgot that balance in a SP title isn't really all that important, beyond making the player feel challenged. There were spots that weren't terrible, in terms of boss fights and arena challenges, but if the weapons had had more crazy, punch and silly side effects, this could've been so much more than it was. The AI's pretty bad, but it's largely OK, because there are plenty of enemies to kill. The game relies on numbers and bullet sponge enemies for the most part, and they gradually get harder and harder, while also showing up in huge numbers. The final boss fight is kind of a joke, but it's fine, at that point I just wanted to be done.3. Level design, visually, is OK. I'd say that enemies blend into the world a bit too well for this style of game, but overall, it's fine. The art's great in places, copy-pasta in others. Some of the areas feel really well-designed, but quite a few feel like somebody was rushing to meet deadlines.4. The sound design, with the music off, is barely passable.5. There's a Dash that's 99% useless. I don't know why it's even in the game design.6. The boss designs range from meh to excellent. However, they tend to have too many fights where you grind a shield or spend the whole time jumping and dodging while your guided missiles sloooooowly kill the enemy. Other than the final fight, there aren't clever weak-spot mechanics or other things that keep something like this entertaining.7. There are a few really interesting enemy mechanics, like an Ogryn with a shield, that never get used again. 8. The game's terribly prone to crashing at the oddest times. I'm pretty sure it's a memory leak or malloc, because it often happened during boss fights, cutscenes or when switching levels. However, the developers didn't leave any crash-reporting in the build, so it's a silent crash-to-desktop with zero explanation.9. I haven't played it multiplayer, and honestly, after seeing the weapons mix, have no desire to. It's not tight enough, and the controls would be a serious problem, even if the weapon balance is right. My theory remains that they made the classic mistake of balancing it for MP, and that's why SP feels so bad... when practically everybody who buys this will play it SP. Ah well.Overall? This could have been better than "ok, I guess". For the asking price, it's not, even though I got it on sale. Dear developers, instead of quietly abandoning this to go work on something else, come back, do a polish pass on the balance and feel of SP so that Easy is punchy, responsive, fast-paced and fun, Normal is a bit tricky and Hard is moderately brutal in places. As things stand, I had zero desire to play this on Hard or play it past seeing the end, because I'm guessing that enemies get 200% base health and do twice as much damage, which will make all the weapons that already felt weak and boring feel even worse. Since there isn't a level editor and there's no way to mod it, it's a dead-end title for me.This is a game that could've been fixed up mainly with tuning- everything from how quickly the control state polls to how the weapons feel. There were so many things that felt like wasted opportunities, like the Squig Mines that felt powerful-ish, but were so awkward to use that they needed to be much better to feel right.At any rate, this isn't the worst thing I've ever played. It's just so much more meh than it deserved to be, and it was entirely fixable. Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing pretty regular crashes on Linux under Proton, just like the native Windows users. Besides that, the gunplay just doesn't have the impact to match the otherwise gorgeous art. Both the player character and enemies are pretty spongy and there's no real sense that anyone's scored a hit. Even the rocket launcher is disappointing. See Streets of Rogue, Nuclear Throne, or Enter the Gungeon for how to make a rocket launcher feel powerful in 2D. For a game that focuses on shooting, having anemic shooting is a pretty serious flaw.Besides this, there are some frustrating bits of bad design: often in a level I have to hold a button or key to activate something. This takes me out of the shooter trance just like the timing-based platforming sections in 2D Sonic games take me out of the speed trance those games are known for.This is so disappointing because I desperately want to love this game. The aesthetic is absolutely on point, and I found myself chuckling pretty regularly while playing. The background art, the incidental voice barks, all of it really sells the Warhammer feel. It's a shame that everything else feels, well, like I'm playing with some cheap, hollow plastic figures and environments. If this game was a series of action figures, I'd be quite upset to receive them as a Christmas present.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas, Blood and Teef came out of nowhere as a game. Me and my friend were amazed with how charming and fun the game was. It had a surprising variety of weapons in it and an ASTONISHING amount of enemy variety, like: Guardsmen, Commanders, Commissars, Scions, Ogryn, Grots, Orks, Nobs, Killacans, Sewer monsters, cultists, genestealers, space marines and more! There's a lot of cool references in the game that are a delight to see.The story is pretty simple and short, but it was still good fun. Took about 2 hours to beat with a friend.In terms of difficulty, it's not that hard. Has some moments that might be tense, but it should be manageable.Had some crashes, but they weren't too problematic on my end.For achievement hunters: very easy completion. There are some are some really useful guides in the community tab if you need help with it. Took about 7 hours to 100%.8/10, would love to see more like this in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the shortest games I've ever purchased.Took me less than 2 hours to complete the game for the first time and about 5h to get all achievements.Gameplay itself is just holding down left-click, switching weapons to not reload and spam WAAAAGH! whenever it's available. Difficulties are a joke as well, hardmode is what the actual "normal" difficulty should be and anything below that is just a walk in the park. Checkpoints are overly generous as well.Bosses don't feel unique and more like bullet-sponges.Replayability is nigh to zero and the "PvP" mode is just tiny arenas with 3 different objectives (TDM, KOTH and CTF) with no incentive to play them whatsoever.And most importantly, the game is RIDDLED with bugs, and I mean that you'll at least encounter a few every playthrough, if not even gamebreaking ones (not being able to progress, enemies getting stuck, bosses bugging out so they don't take damage/move, etc.).Don't spend your money on this unless it's on sale for 80% or more.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time 40k fan I can say that the story of this game is exactly what I wanted from an Ork-based shooter. Your boss stole your hair, so you gotta murder everything until you get it back.The gameplay though is atrocious. Firstly having more dakka is not enough, you have to manage constantly switching weapons to deal with specific enemies (which is inherently anti-ork). You'll want to ensure you've practised quick switching from explosive, to projectile, to energy weapons as you'll need to do it a lot.Secondly the platforming is extremely slow. You're not incentivised to move quickly and rip and tear like you would expect, instead you have to advance, wait for set pieces, hunt for teef (which is infuriating as it's the only way to get unlocks because apparently killing a baneblade isn't valuable somehow), and then slowly but surely move through a level. This is made so much worse by the multiplayer input lag. You're expected to react to timing windows which are always out of sync if you're not the host.Thirdly there's no real melee options. We're Orks! All the artwork in the game shows choppas, but your piddly little melee weapons barely tickle enemies. Where's the melee classes?! If they come later in the game I'll be disappointed as they should be in from the get go given by default most Orks use their sluggas to get close enough to krump.Lastly the class and clan system is pointless. The variety between each class is so minimal as to not really be relevant to the average gamer, and selecting a clan offers no real bonus other than looking different which is incredibly disappointing.As a final note: the best way I can describe this game is that it feels like a generic, poorly-designed, lacklustre shooter platformer that was bought out and had 40k material taped onto it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I had fun with the campaign mode, and loved the Ork flavour of this title, the campaign's length (beat in about 3 hours of casually playing) and gripes with controls make me not recommend this game at its current price (10% off). The movement isn't great, guns feel weak after the opening minutes of the game, you can't hold down the firing key and keep shooting after reloading, the burna weapon tree doesn't inform you about their overheat mechanic, and the enemy types aren't that varied. Some later combinations of heavy enemies are harder than boss battles to deal with. Default controller bindings are rather odd as well (namely jump being LT on XBox controller).Despite all that, it's still a fun time, but not for full price.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 Preheat the oven:Place rack in the middle and preheat the oven to 400°F.2 Assemble the pie filling:In a large bowl, gently combine the rhubarb and the strawberries with the sugar, tapioca, salt, and orange zest. Let sit for 10 minutes.3 Roll out the bottom crust and fill the pie:Roll out one disc of pastry dough and line the bottom of a pie dish with it. Trim to 1/2 inch from the edge. Transfer the filling into the crust and spread out evenly.4 Roll out the second disc of pastry dough and place over the pie. Trim the edges to an inch from the edge of the pie dish. Tuck the top crust edges over the bottom crust edges and use your fingers or a fork to crimp the top and bottom edges together. Cut slits in the top for the steam to escape.(If you want, for a nice glaze on your pie, use a pastry brush to brush a thin layer of egg white or cream over the top of the pie.)5 Bake the pie:Place pie on the middle rack of the 400°F oven with a baking sheet on a lower rack to catch any juices that might spill over.Bake for 20 minutes at 400°F, then reduce heat to 350°F and bake an additional 40-50 minutes longer (50 to 60 minutes longer if doing a 10-inch pie). The pie is done when the crust is nicely browned and the filling (that you can see through the venting holes) thick and bubbly.6 Cool and serve:Remove from oven and let cool on a rack.Serve warm or cold. If you do cool to room temperature, the juices will have more time to thicken. Pie can also be covered and stored at room temperature for up to 2 days or refrigerated for 5 days.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game ever since I first heard of it. Playing a WH40k game starring as one of the not so usual Orks seemed real fun to me and the Demo showed, that they encapsulated the Ork-Feeling quite well. Now that the game is released, it feels a little unfinished to me and so I am disappointed. Of course, you can not demand an overwhelming amount of game time and deepness of a 2D-side-scrolling shooter, but completing the campaign in 3 hours total game time is a little too less for the price.On top of that, there are still several annoying bugs in the game, ranging from regular crashing the game, to checkpoints not correctly saving your progress and enemies that behave wired and are thus easy to fight. This seems to be the case in some levels more than others, leading to the final boss beeing waaaaay to easy to beat, even on the hardest difficulty, especially compared to other bosses in the game.Overall it is a good, but still unfinished product that I'd not recommend getting into at the moment, until they did fix some of these issues or the price has been lowered.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very ok.  The biggest disappointment for me is the lack of upgrades or progression. This is simply a linear game with not much to do after you beat it. I've unlocked all the weapons and tried them out and there is only one that I will use. Most of the others either pale in comparison to the one, or they are just unusable because of the spread (or lack of range). Literally one gun that was "good". Everything else to unlock is just cosmetic, IE, hats. Just not enough, and the hats do no boosts, or anything. The gameplay is fun for the most part. I found the bosses irritating because it is just a pattern over and over again and they have too much health. Very bullet spongy.  In between that was fun.  The game allows you to carry 5 different weapons, but switching to them on the fly isn't really an option. You are forced to use a weapon wheel or click the appropriate button but I haven't played enough to even know which weapon type is in which key slot.  The game doesn't freeze when you use the weapon wheel (tab, and it opens if you just click it once, it isn't a hold situation) so it doesn't really allow you to switch to an appropriate weapon based on the enemy. It crashed once for me, and booted me out of another game (both offline). Was surprised that there wasn't more to the game, but I should know better being that it is warhammer.  Glad I got it over half off.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game through on normal. I waited until it was discounted during the skulls event, I'm glad I did so. The game play lacks, no weapon upgrades, no continuous game play, and no one is on the multiplayer servers anymore. If this game was 2-5 dollars or if they added more content maybe I'd re visit this review. I would like to try the multiplayer, but it's impossible to do so without friends playing. I wanted to recommend this to a friend so we could play, but I'm not. There's not enough re-play content to ask someone to spend money on it. On a good note, I feel like there is a lot of potential for this game, and hopefully the developers go through and tune it up a bit. I do love the animation and the overall feel to it, the sound track is amazing, and I feel like it does capture the Orks very well.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give a decent Warhammer game a negative review seeing as there's a metric TON of trash ones, but sadly this game just isn't for me.I'll leave this disclaimer: If all you're looking for is a game where you can roleplay an Ork dakka-ing humans mindlessly all day, this is the game for you and you'll love it. For me though, and in 2022 the era of progression gaming, I need more. I want to customize my Warboss's mech suit. I want to choose the territory I go into, with pros/cons and rewards/negatives for each territory I invade. I want to customize my guns and unlock new parts for them. I want to customize my ammo. Hell, I want to customize my ork!There *is* a VERY limited progression system in this game. In the time I played (50 minutes) I had unlocked the ***entire*** progression system. Woo. So after this all I had to look forward to was grinding humies into paste endlessly over and over. For some, that will be enough. For others that want progression, customization etc it will not be enough. I am of the latter category.All this being said, I wish there was a "neutral" option instead of yes/no on Steam. _childDocuments_.review: What a great short game.You can really tell a lot of nerdy love and care went into these designs of the characters and backgrounds, going so far as to directly reference the actual sets that you can buy with all the weapons, characters, enemies, its a very nice touch. Shame that the Mek workshop, although accessible throughout the game at every checkpoint, shows up once? I guess we just carry that thing on our back the whole time.The game play is good, and its fantastic that it has the option for four-player local co-op. Although I played it alone, I imagine it would be way more frantic with more people. But I have a real bone to pick with the designer of the achievements, for gods sake (although I guess Gork/Mork's sake would be more fitting) stop adding "challenges" that are just kill x enemy 1000 times! Nobody enjoys that! And designers please stop adding sewer levels into your game, nobody cares if it's thematic, just skip it and get to the cool set piece we know your teasing already, fans know whats coming (as you're not too subtle with your symbolism) and others are just bored trudging through killing just straight up rats. Padding is padding and this would be a much better overall experience without it.The weapon selection is fine if exactly what you expect, although a certain weapon trivialises most boss encounters it's cool and dangerous to use so i'll give it a pass, it is great that there is no out of place rpg mechanics strapped in, and you're as powerful when you start as when you end, just with more weapon selection. Trying the weapons out is a fun experience.Overall, I'm pretty sure that even if I wasn't nerding out over all the references it is a silly good time through and through. I would recommend, 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright.The game crashed on me one time on my playthrough, and it takes a while to load at the start, but other than that it runs well... just don't expect it to run in ancient laptop though, the game is a heck of a lot more demanding than it looks.As for the story? You play as an orc that gets bullied by another orc, he even rips your hair at the beginning, and that jumpstarts the whole quest of getting your hair back. Then nothing much happens, you fight a number of warhammer factions along the way, but all of it feels fairly incidental? Is good, because the characterization of the orcs is really well made, and the dialogs are really funny; but the overarching plot is not really anything to write home about, it's just an excuse to play around as an orc and hear that same orc taunting "humies" and wanting to smash things and the like.The gameplay is also fairly mindless, but fun; it has three difficulty settings and they're properly balanced -hard is hard, easy is easy-, so on and so forth. As you progress through the game, you get teeth (or "teef") that you can use to get upgrades and hats, as you play through the levels you get checkpoints where you can buy these things, or alternatively change your equipment; strangely though, you cannot change your hats here, only your weapons, if you want to change your hats you need to back in and out of the main menu. Which is a bit of a hassle, but whatever, is fine...I think the real problem is that, unlike previous titles from this developer (Guns, Gore Cannolli 1 & 2) the game doesn't really evolve that much when it comes to its levels or its set pieces. For the most part you'll go through the same looking stages, killing a number of random enemies that more or less behave the same way. It's fun, but it's nothing that really feels meaningful or impactful in any way, it's simply okay for what it is.A problem that I did have with the weapons, is the fact that the guns have some fairly abstract images to refer to their stats, as well as some minor descriptions here and there... the issue is that even if you are to follow these images for what they -might- appear to be; a lot of the times the weapons don't seem to have accurate descriptions, nor correct stats. Like they give you a rocket launcher that's supposed to have a really good fire rate, and you buy it, only to then use it and realize it has the worse fire rate of the three available in the game... It's just stuff like that, that makes the game a tad bit annoying.The game does have some cool bosses, all based on emblematic characters from the Warhammer universe, so stuff like that is really nice.Like many have said, the game is short -about 4 to 6 hours depending on how much you explore and your difficulty of choice-, but I think for what it is, they game is fine. I already think games are too long anyways; like I've mentioned, I think the game not really evolving much and just kinda reiterating on the same concepts is kind of what prevents it from being more than a decently fun time. I really like the orcs, and the combat is fun, but there isn't that much to it other than that.It's fine, get it on a sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: FINAL VERDICTIf you love the Warhammer universe, orcs and stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-ups, this game is for you!OVERALL 9/10Stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-up fun! Worth a replay and it has fun 4-player multiplayer (real-time Worms)!GRAPHICS 9/10Simplified, cardboard cutout-style art reflects Warhammer orcs' simplistic mindsets. Some excellent set pieces such as the imperial knight (giant robot knight) and the temple of the gene stealer cult. Even though the environment was a war-torn wasteland there was enough visual variety to keep the visuals interesting.SOUND/MUSIC 10/10Powerful on-point sound effects and the soundtrack bring the action to visceral, pulse pounding life! It took me until the ending cinematic to figure out that the music the orc band was playing was the theme song of the game ("SHOOTAS, BLOOD AND TEEF!"). They should have put it in the trailer.CONTROLS 8/10Using a controller I had some issues with aiming the snazzgun (it kept drifting up and down) and since there were so many important commands I had to map dash to a button instead of a trigger so I had to keep letting go of the trigger buttons to dodge (dash). You also walk and jump forward very slowly. Other than that very easy to control.PLOT N/AShoot-'em-up so not much of a plot to speak of; the warboss steals your topknot and you have to fight your way through swarms of guardsmen, tyranids, orcs and space marines to get it back.GAMEPLAY 9/10Fast paced stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-up fun!That being said, I would have preferred more weapons and for them to be slightly powered up (eg. the burnastikk should have more rounds, perhaps 6).I also would have preferred the weapons to do more damage or for enemies to have less health. Large battles turn into a bit of a grind with even minor enemies soaking up damage as you dodge back and forth for what feels like forever. I would have preferred more enemies with less health that dropped like flies to really emphasise the Warhammer aspect of the game. Boss battles with little enemies running around were somewhat annoying as you had to spend quite a bit of time being distracted by the small fry.MOST OF ALL I WOULD HAVE ENJOYED HAVING A SQUAD OF AI BUDDIES (BOTS)! IT WOULD REALLY BRING THE SINGLE-PLAYER CAMPAIGN TO LIFE.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell if I enjoy this game because it is a 40k game, or if I like it on its own merits.  I suppose it's more that it is a 40k game where the player gets to play as an ork.  Plus, I like retro video games, and the 2D run 'n gun is one of my favorites.The first thing that struck me with this game is the long load times.  While I don't have a powerhouse PC, I wasn't expecting the game to take a few seconds to boot up or load stages.  The filled me with a little concern.  And that concern was warranted, as the game is a little buggy, and I have already had it crash on me once.  With several times it threatening to.  The game play itself is 2D side scrolling twin stick run 'n gunning.  It's certainly not the best I've ever played, but it's far from the worst.  My biggest grip would be that even with the strongest guns, even the weak enemies take multiple hits.  Which further slows and already relaxed pace run 'n gun.  My next issue is the weapon wheel is a little clunky to use.  So I just cycle through the weapons instead.  Which is also frustrating as if I had the option to not take certain weapons, pistols being one of them, I wouldn't.  Just to make cycling through easier.  Speaking of weapons, Shootas, Blood & Teef have a bunch to pick from, but I found myself only using like three.  And of those three, I use one weapon 3/4 or more of the time.  It's too much of a pain to cycle through what the character carries and the carried weapons are by category leaving most of the load out at the save points.  To be sure, there weapons that work way better versus some enemies, scorcha vs. rats for example, but whats in hand and melee are work well enough to not want to bother.The game offers a fair amount of movement options from double jump to dash.  I try to include the dash in my play, but much of the time jumping and moving seems to be enough or better to avoid enemies and/or their attacks.  Perhaps mastery of this is more suited to the higher difficulty settings.  I probably won't ever know.Do I find the game fun?  I certainly did when I played the demo and the first portion of it.  The game isn't becoming more fun the further it goes on for me, but I also don't think the fun factor is dropping off a cliff either.  I think the more I play it, the more it goes from a fun game to a pretty fun or okay game.  And I can't separate how much of that is the 40k IP carrying it for me. As I am a 40k fan, and the story is entertainingly funny to me.So, I don't know quite if I recommend it or not.  I'm glad I added it to my library warts and all.  However, reading over my review it doesn't sound like I cared for it much.  So I'll recommend it if you like 40k and retro game genres like run 'n guns.  But caution anyone that isn't much of a fan of either.  Hopefully, the game's technical side gets tightened up in the future as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and really fun sidescrolling shooter.   Playing this actually reminds me of my childhood days playing browser games.  I played a lot of stuff like this, but made with with flash animation and a budget of a ham sandwich.   But I think that those cheap old games worked the same way this one does.   The levels are short, sweet 5 or 10 minute affairs.  Pretty much every level you'll have enough drops to unlock a new weapon.  Just simple challenges, fun guns, no long grind, no microtransactions.  Just pure, innocent game design.   It's actually shocking how refreshing that feels.  The story setup is great, you're on a quest to take down your old warboss who betrayed because you have a shiny fing on your head and he's da BOSS!  So takes it right off your head and pushes you out of your craft.   And rather than dying tragically like some lame hero of the imperium, or succumbing to corruption like a thrall of chaos, you simply shake off the landing, pick up your gun and start krumping your way back to the git.   I couldn't write a more orky story if I tried.   This game is great.   Buy it, sale or full price, it's firmly worth the money.  I'm confident that if you've liked games that are similar before, or this game is catching your eye, you're about to have a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes, but with a few asterisks attached.Shootas, Blood & Teef is a 2D platformer/shooter where you play as an ork who was wronged by his warboss and now you want revenge. You fight your way through an imperial hive world's battlefield full of imperial guardsmen, orks, gretchen, and even some interesting factions you won't see coming. You fight some bosses along the way, and eventually you get your revenge... but it happens way too fast!You can see my playtime in this review. It's about 3 hours long, and not much more than that, unless you want to go achievement hunting. So I wouldn't say the game is worth it at retail price (19,99€ at the time of writing).There's also the case of the humor. This is a 40k that does NOT take itself at all seriously, but on the other hand, it's a game about orks, it probably  take itself seriously, considering what the orks are like. If you like your 40k games gritty and dark, this game isn't going to give you that, but if you like the zany kind of humor that the orks can provide, there's lots of laughs to be had in this game. If you can find the game at a discount, 30% or more, I'd say it's worth it, but not at retail price.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Warhammer has a game in just about every genre these days. Lol. Actually, I don't think there is a match-3 Warhammer puzzle game yet, so somebody needs to develop one!                                                          Ok, I digress.  Shootas, Blood, & Teef is a multiplayer (it has local co-op) run and gun where you play as one of four classes of orcs attempting to take a gasoline plant from humans. Each class has a couple of minor differences (such as what their grenades do, what melee weapon they have, etc). The variations are subtle but noticeable.  Along the way the you collect "teef" (or teeth: orc currency) which allow you to purchase a handful of new weapons at every check point and the main menu (divided into types: pistols, shotguns, rifles, explosives, and another kind that unlocks later after picking up a flame thrower). You can also buy hats which are purely cosmetic.                                                                                                                                     *The game's graphics, while simple, are good and fit the game's humorous tone.                                                                    *I would say that the music is symphonic metal. While it is subjective, I like the energetic sound track and       feel it fits the game well. Weapons and explosions sound appropiately boomy and voices are sprinkled       throughout.                                                                                                                                                                  * The controls are tight for the most part; however, sometimes my brother, nephew, and I had trouble        quick swapping weapons.  We had to push the button a couple of times.                                                    * The game is a little short, but there are three difficulty levels and you can select stages individually to        collect any "teef" missed (it shows you the total "teef" of each level and how many have been acquired        on the level select screen).                                                                                                                                                          I purchased this game on sale, but honestly, I would have been happy with it even if I paid full price.  Also, it does work on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: TL;DRShootas Blood & Teef is a straightforward, 2D platform shooter that manages to be a fun, funny, brief experience. _childDocuments_.review: A very well executed, if brief retro-style sidescrolling shoot 'em up Pros:- The setting, visuals and atmosphere have been recreated with the utmost care and love. It's clear the developers understand and care for the world- Very simple, but very functional gameplay: there are no upgrades, no stats, no puzzles or even platforming challenges, it's nothing but non-stop action from start to finish- Very tightly designed: you have basic movement controls, a melee attack, a grenade, 5 different weapons and 4 different character classes to choose from. Each function is designed with a specific purpose, allowing for slightly different gameplay styles. There's zero fat.- A wonderfully colourful, expressive artstyle that's just the right amount of goofy, and the visuals are always extremely clear and easy to read.- There are tons of easter eggs and funny background details for fans of the setting to find. Be on the lookout for motivational posters, they're very funny- Relentlessly fast pacing, there's never a dull moment- A kick-ass soundtrack that fits the game perfectly- 4-player co-op is available, but I finished this game solo so I can't comment on its quality muchCons: - Very short. I cleared the main campaign in less than 4 hours on normal difficulty- Very linear. This game would really benefit from some exploration elements. Though with how tightly the game is designed, I can't really say what you'd put behind that exploration- There are no transitions between levels, and very few cutscenes to establish context. When you defeat a boss for example, the game cuts immediately to a loading screen and drops you into the next level within seconds, giving no time to adjust to what just happened. Many times I was confused if I was even at a new level, or just continuing the previous one. Given how short the game is this isn't a huge deal, but it's jarring nonetheless- There's basically zero exposition or explanation of anything. Things like what a Waaagh is, what the Imperium is, why there are aliens in the sewers, what the white armored big guys are are just things you're expected to know- The pricepoint. $20 is simply too much for this game, no matter how tight the experience. If the game were half that, I'd recommend it without reservation. As it stands now, you're best off waiting for a sale.Despite its (literal) shortcomings, this game makes up for quantity with quality. It's clearly a labor of love and passion.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely satisfying {if short) arcadey game with a quirky art style that seems to actually reflect well how the orks view the world of 40k. If you wanted grimdark 40k to be less grimdark This game fits it well.There's fantastic attention to little details (mushroom calanders? lol), the storyline is suitably orky (and crazy), and the various bosses you fight have some of the most hillarious intros I'd not seen since borderlands series. Guns are suitably fun to fire and all the unlocked guns are typically sidegrades of each other so you don't have to unlock everything to finish the game. Co-op play is fantastic as well. The ragdoll physics are hillarious. My main issue with the game is that it crashes very often (at time of writing this), in my playthrough I counted it crashing about 4-5 times. And while the game is fun, The solo/co-op is rather short. Would be nice to have some extra content post-campaign as well such as a co-op horde mode or challenge/ leader board modes (e.g. an arcade mode with scoring similar to Gears of war)Also there's friendly fire with the melee attacks, beast snagga spears and explosions. Your melee attacks do feel rather weedy and lacking impact (even when you're swinging a tankhamma as a stormboy it can take a few hits to kill most mobs!) which is quite un-orky. Despite all this, overall I'd still recommend this shooter if you just like a bout of mindless mayhem and watching things run about in flames.... now time to go paint a mushroom tattoo on one of my ork minis....

Some information were shared with players, a part of soundtrack (which is really, really good to be honest!) was presented and game finally arrived.And I cannot say that this game is "especially bad" or "superb." because it is somewhere in the middle. What You going to feel from the beginning is the fact that this is, as previously mentioned "Guns, Gore & Cannoli",  an indie game that tries to be AAA title on license and fails because of it. What need to be mentioned is fact that it has less to offer than "Guns, Gore & Cannoli" and "Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2" and at the same time more to offer. Yes - this is a paradox that is hard to easily explain without playing the game.What You need to know is that, that game shows exactly how Orkz from Warhammer 40k Universe "thinks" and "works" and how they "see the world around them". If You expected "serious game" because "" then prepare Yourself to look at very nice and humoristic look into that grim universe. You'll be surprised how well it suits this universe.And one more thing - don't buy this game at full price, show some respect to Your own wallet and buy it when price goes down or when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Art, sound and especially voice acting is great but the gameplay is very mediocre and the game itself is super short.Gameplay - Very basic and doesnt require any thought, you run through the levels too fast to even notice and there are very abrupt stops and starts, youre fighting a boss and the split second its dead you get a loading screen and then you spawn in another level.Graphics - I like the cartoony artstyle and the animations are good, especially mechs and such "shake" in a very styalized way which fits the game. Screenshake is way too strong but can thankfully be turned off.The screen is cluttered with visual "noise" and its really hard to tell whats going on, differentiating between your teammates attacks, your own attacks and the enemies attacks is basically impossible. When we played we died very often without understanding what killed us, sometimes rockets/bullets/lasers fly straight through you because theyre friendly sometimes you die because theyre not.In general its hard to tell whats going on.Sound - Voice acting is really good and I was surprised by the music, theres one rock track with vocals which is really good but weapon sounds are very meh, no punchiness in explosions or dakkas.Cinematics - Theyre humorous and well animated but the video files are compressed beyond whats reasonable and there are a lot of artefacting and pixelation.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas Blood and Teef is a simple game, and it's meant to be. It's a classic 2d sidescrolling shooter like Contra or Metal Slug, but painted with the 40k brush. And what impressed me most was just how much this game gives as far as detail.To go without spoilers, your enemies will range far beyond the standard affair of orks and guard and Space Marines. As a tabletop player, I found myself shouting out in surprise whenever a new enemy showed its face, many which have either rarely or even never had a video game representation before. Seeing these often overlooked factions and species was extremely refreshing.Of course, the gameplay itself is great. It's fast and simple, with tons of options for weapon loadouts and, not to mention, classes. You can choose from Stormboyz, Beast Snaggas, Flash Gitz, Weirdboyz, all of which have unique actions and looks to them, different melee attacks, different grenades, and overall feels. Combine this with a total of five weapon slots each with four weapon options, the game has a ton of replayability.I will say that the game is on the shorter side, but with its arcade-y nature, it is very easy to pick up and just run through a level or two with an entirely new loadout. Half the fun is going back and trying a level with a new class and new loadout, and seeing how it performs.Overall, this game is simple fun, a very fitting soundtrack, and probably my most enjoyed 40k game so far. Of course, that might be the ork in me being biased. Either way, I absolutely must give this game an obligatory-

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I've played it exclusively on Deck. It's everything I ever wanted from the basic premise. Shoot 'em up and with Orks. An orky perspective on things without being annoyingly grating. Fun background details are included like what the posters say, the shrines to Old Bale Eye / Yarrick, and the hand drawn elements are charming. The music punches above its weight and feels appropriately epic in high intensity.  I'm usually one to just play a campaign on easy and finish, but I've already started replaying.  The only downside in gameplay is that some minibosses feel harder than the main bosses, and you tend to explode more barrels than intended. The playable classes feel mixed. The Weirdboy seems the obvious worst of the four as its main effects can be replaced by the Shokk pistol, the Stormboy's hammer is a little clunky to use but makes up for it with his dash attacks, the Flash Git is the general best for the small chance of not using ammunition, but the Beast Snagga is my favorite because using his explosive spear is so satisfying as it rewards good placement and can help pierce shields and take down large beasts.  The variety of enemies feel healthy and never tiring. I wish they could've kept every enemy they had considered in development, like the Big Mek instead of choosing the Killa Kan, but that's just life in videogames. The weapons are generally fine. It capitalizes on what I considered a missed opportunity for the tabletop and put the Boomstikk on Infantry. The self damage weapons feel a bit hard to use in practice. Game never crashed for me.  The multiplayer seems a bit bare due to a bit of a lack of a playerbase but I hope that starts getting better, or I just start exploring LFG threads.  Maybe the game is too "indie" for the price for some but for me it was an instant purchase with no regrets.

_childDocuments_.review: Cutscenes and voiceacting are great,the story fitted well.Nice concept overall,The enemy varietie was fine and the portrayal of the 40k universe is cartoonish yet faithful.BUT The gameplay is repetitive,you have not enough guns and varieties,cant upgrade ork or nades,despite having too much money to shell out!Autoaim on controller makes it stupidly easy,but the ai  has it as well so i had the feeling you could not dodge all attaks,which is not intended anyway.Most parts are too easy,but the game is not deep or fun enough to bother changing the difficulty to hard.You could just run past most enemies,but that would make it really boring.I quit at the stompa fight(i think its the last one) because the autoaim kept correcting my aim which made me not hit the weakpoints( blieve it or not!) so the fight took forever and i quit and deinstalled after my second try.Felt like a waste of time in the end ,so dont waste yours ! O yeah and it crashed 5 times in almost 3 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a BLAST - WAAAAGH!It is highly addictive albeit being disappointingly short - but with great replayability value if you find some friends to play with. Online lobbies are still rather empty, but since the game is rather recent and fresh while it is certainly a niche game, this is not very surprising. Sound is great (although still buggy). The music is a BLAST (WAAAAAAGH!), sounds are convincingly accurate and fun to listen to, while the voice-overs hit the spot. The mechanics are easy to learn and not that hard to master, but coop-wise it is rather limited for its' short story, that entangles you nonetheless. If you're into WH40K, you might enjoy this for its' humourous approach and accurateness of lore, while still being an orky game. Guns and skills suit most play styles, and while class differences (there are four) are subtle, you're invited to play around with them, especially with friends or co-players. Other than that, the game has an active discord server. It's been active since the demo release 8 months prior to the release of the original game (I myself joined rather late), but the devs are listening there as well. It still has some flaws and bugs though, since progress is stored per machine and not per account, so some unlockables are unavailable if the game is played over various computers. To summarize, the game is well worth the money and is a great game to play, especially in local coop. Get krumpin'! WAAAAGH!

_childDocuments_.review: This game "gets" the orks in 40k and the sense of humour you need to have with these characters. Some parts of levels that you can walk on are obscured by other layers of artwork, but it doesn't affect game play too much.

_childDocuments_.review: played the beta, played the full, and ive even played other games from the devs, all i can say is that its a good game, hard to find ppl online, and the story is short for 20$, but honestly this may be the best w40k orks game that exists, if they add more stuff to make online more lasting the game would be a definite 10/10, but the lack of replay-ability makes the game lack luster at times.im still leaving a positive because the game-play is awesome, and i have hopes for the future of the game, but be aware of the problems the game seems to have before you buy it, because 20$ is a lot for a 3-4 hour game...still with all that id say its a good game overall, twice so when compared to half the piss that is other warhammer games, its not perfect and has a lot of room to improve, but its not the worse game ive ever played, its even enjoyable, i did have fun playing this game! witch i cant say the same about 90% of games from warhammer. lastly when compared to GGC and GGC2 there's a lot of things learned, i love the UI changes from GCC, miner things like how your ammo and health is over your head rather then on the corner of your screen, whale GGC2 had your health the ammo was still difficult to keep track off, not that that really matters, sense ammo in infinite in SBT, witch i dislike because it makes it easy to just spam the better weapons for the entirety of the game, along with this, i have noticed a visual decline from GGC2 and SBT, with the art of GGC2 being HD and having an almost 2.5D look to it by using art techniques, this is absent, and i understand that SBT is meant to be cartoony but so is GGC2...overall, when compared to there old titles they have improved mechanical elements like UI and some game-play bits, but the art has seemingly suffered abit in return...with all this i would give the game a 6.9-10, should you buy it? yes, but i would wait and keep an eye on how this game evolves if it will, and understand that if your only in it for the story your only gonna have like 3-4 hours of game-play...and that's on the hardest setting....

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little game, but quite a few bugs. Crashes seem to be frequent on boss loading, and progress/weapons seems to be saved locally rather than cloud based. I played for a while on my switch while my son used my PC, when I came to play on my PC and he on his, I had all of his weapons and he had none since he hadn't played on his PC at all. The elevators are pretty horrendous in multiplayer too, very glitchy.Worth the price tag for the comedy value with friends, if you don't see the value in that then don't buy it expecting a long and involved game, because it isn't one. A decent amount of effort went into the art, voice acting and references, which I enjoyed. Very true to 40k and Orky as hell.The good weapons become obvious quite quick, swapping between all 4 is simple and intuitive and the special ability keeps you ripping through. I do think the Flash Git is my personal favourite for the neverendig bullet spray.

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts out fun and hands you new weapons at a fast pace.  Then....it doesn't any more, the enemies get spongier and spongier, you get no real ways to deal with them...Most of the weapon options are pretty rubbish, there are points where you need to switch weapon loadouts but can't, weird level transitions, just all manner of hair pulling annoyances piled up on each other.Plus points, it is a rare humorous take on the 40k universe and its humor stays amusing throughout, with loads of references sprinkled through the levels.If they could have kept the frenetic starting pace going this would be a definite recommend but unfortunately it ends up as a slog.  Only really recommended for very hardcore 40k afficionados.TLDR No Bloodaxes dont buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming and fun. Though not terribly long, the amount this game gives you for its price is very reasonable and fair. _childDocuments_.review: It's a delightfully silly take on the only faction in 40k that is having a good time. After campaign is done, you are done, and from everything i have read its about 3 hours long and thats not a whole lot for the money.Limited weaponry options are also a slight bummer (no upgrades?), this is because most weapons feel like they dont bring anything to the table and or are just bad/feel bad.All in all, for the little i played a fun romp, but pretty expensive for what it is (and i hope it gets more content, game modes mostly).

_childDocuments_.review: First Impressions: Fun movement and Weapons, but the enemies are a little buggy. _childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it simple, I would say this game is a *SOLID B*. A fun and short game.I was getting alot of enjoyment out of playing this game. Most of the bosses were fun, the shooting felt good, and the humor was on point. Worth playing if you love the Orks, Warhammer, or games like Metal Slug or Alien Hominid. Getting into it, there's some issue I have with it, having played the game single player. 1) The auto-aim for controller is on by default. You can turn it off but it seems to turn back on when you go to main menu.2) The game has crashed 4 times for me. Shocking for a game with little requirements to run.3) You can't increase or decrease controller stick sensitivity like you can with the mouse (at least from what I could find).4) You can remap the controls to your liking. The issue being that the weapon wheel and next weapon function cannot be tied to the same button/key, even though by default they are the same button (Y/Triangle). Same with the interact function or etc.5) Maybe a little too pricey for how short it is. 6) At times it felt like the regular enemies were harder and tankier than the bosses. I found myself yelling "JUST DIE ALREADY!" alot. 7) *SPOILERS* ---> There were 3 moments that I thought were frustrating or unfair. The 1st being the elevator in the Imperium. The 2nd being the 2 Killakans. The 3rd being the final boss. Each of these moments felt like taking damage was unavoidable. I hope these issues are addressed by the devs in the future.
