_childDocuments_.review: As a dedicated gamer always on the lookout for new adventures, I eagerly dove into Sons of Forest. Unfortunately, what I found was a jumbled mess of half-baked ideas and missed opportunities.Let's start with the story, or lack thereof. Sons of Forest promised an intriguing narrative centered around parallel universes, but what it delivered was a convoluted mess that left me scratching my head in confusion. The plot felt disjointed and poorly executed, consisting of post-it notes and parallel universes with little rhyme or reason. Instead of feeling engaged, I found myself struggling to care about the world and the characters.Adding insult to injury was the abysmal pacing. The game cruised along at a snails pace, with little to no narrative peaks to look forward too. The cutscenes were also abysmal, and actively made my enjoyment of exploring caves and bunkers worse, as I came to dread the extremely boring and narratively nonsensical cutscenes. Even worse were the lackluster boss fights, which felt more like tedious chores than epic battles. Each encounter was a repetitive slog, lacking the excitement and challenge that should accompany such pivotal moments.And then there's the ending, or lack thereof. After slogging through hours of lackluster gameplay, I was hoping for some sort of payoff, some resolution to the questions swirling around in my head. Instead, Sons of Forest chose to leave me hanging, dangling on the edge of a cliff with no satisfying conclusion in sight. It was a cheap move that left a bitter taste in my mouth and soured my overall experience.But it wasn't all doom and gloom. One shining beacon amidst the darkness was the base building mechanics. While the story may have been a disappointment, I found myself strangely addicted to constructing and customizing my own little corner of the world. There's something oddly satisfying about erecting walls and turrets to defend against the hordes of enemies that plagued the game.And let's not forget about greg. After a long night of battling lackluster bosses and grappling with a nonsensical plot, there's nothing quite like curling up with a nice pot of greg to warm the bones. It may not make up for Sons of Forest's many shortcomings, but it certainly helped take the edge off.In the end, Sons of Forest is a game rife with potential but ultimately falls short of its lofty ambitions. With a weak story, poor pacing, and lackluster boss fights, it's hard to recommend this title to anyone other than the most dedicated base builders.

My only side note is if this sounds good to you, this is exactly what it is.  The original Forest was a really tight game, that felt like the perfect length.After a while I just ran out of steam.  The story doesn't feel like its going anywhere.  The new characters don't really do anything - you can give them tasks or weapons but there's little interaction beyond that.  There's more enemy types but many are just annoying spear/arrow/bullet sponges that return again and again and again.  It's The Forest with Quantity, but sadly just doesn't feel like Quality. They go through their  fighting animations, jump around a bit, then you bluntly just stab them in the face with a spear (or multiple) before they die.You can even just stand in a lake and watch them drown themselves as they try to get to you.Literal ARK AI with animations that look nice.You can find a golf cart that has no sense of gravity whatsoever, as you can scale any surface, even if it's on a 90 degree angle and you can't use your map, get fall damage or anything else, even as a passenger.The "knight" hover board being a "try to steer me without hitting a tree" mini-game, but at least you can use your map on that one as well as a few weapons.In the multiplayer side of things, almost literally everything is client-side. From loot, to resources, to storage.Even some enemies.There is a lot more to say about this game, so I might update the review later if I think of anything.For now, I recommend you don't buy this game at all and leave the devs to actually make the game, although I got the feeling they blew their budget on graphics.4+ years of development, a bunch of money from sales and early access sales and we get this.*Corrected some grammar and spelling mistakes.

Upon trying to even make a start in the game, I was greeted with problem after problem and I won’t be trying to play again until there is some sort of major update fixing these issues: *Game not starting after clicking start*Player not being able to do ANYTHING and having to quit and lose progress. *Major Sound Adjustments and so that players can simply turn down “main menu music” and not all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ music. Like why is it so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loud?! This was the start of all the triggering lol. It’s not hard to pay audio engineers to level everything out nicely. Some sounds would be stupid loud and others too quite… giving us players 3 volume settings to adjust. Nice. *Game spoon feeds players, revealing all cave locations, removing that satisfaction you get from finding them hidden away. *Food doesn’t need cooking and water doesn’t need boiling. Boring. *terrible optimisation for PC gamers who have normal PC’s and not a $6000 setup. I was getting 40 frames in a forest area with everything on low and have a RTX2060 6G. With AAA games these days coming out bug free, and being free to play… this just isn’t it for the $44 price tag. Yes… they probably have a smaller team and budget. But they had years to perfect this, and just slapped “early access” on the title. So that makes it all okay doesn’t it? No. Hopefully the game runs smooth and is actually playable and transitioned into a more entertaining SURVIVAL game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game somehow is worse than the fist one which was also a mess. A bigger map that amounts to a sea of empty set pieces. This game really feels like a walking simulator at times. There's less enemy variety in this than the first one and the caves are more linear and uninteresting. The story is pretty much non existent and full of holes.I think my biggest complaint is there is literally never a single reason to build a base and use any of the advanced crafting mechanics. Food and water is everywhere and I can't build anything at my base that will  help me out in exploring. No forge for better weapons when you get better weapons in caves. Maybe you need to grow food to make specific dishes for buffs on harder difficulties but I never struggled for food. They introduce a sleep meter which can also be bypassed entirely with energy drinks and energy bars so no need to build a nice house to get better sleep. A lot of little things are just annoying for no reason that just feel like the developers have never learned from any other video game or their past mistakes. I think the worst part is that the game is so close to being good but falls flat. The world and the aesthetic are so interesting but don't get explored or resolved in a meaningful way. Kinda like the show Lost.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is a survival horror game that serves as a sequel to The Forest. As with its predecessor, the game is set in a similar environment but comes with a variety of new features, including improved graphics, a new storyline, and more advanced crafting and building options.Based on reviews and feedback from other players, one of the main criticisms leveled against Sons of the Forest is its increased reliance on exploring and gathering high-tech items. This has led to some concerns that the game may feel more like a scavenger hunt rather than a true survival experience.In contrast, The Forest was praised for its focus on survival mechanics, such as foraging for food, building shelter, and managing resources like water and energy. While high-tech items were present in the first game, they were not as integral to the gameplay as they appear to be in Sons of the Forest.Moreover, some players have noted that Sons of the Forest's greater emphasis on high-tech exploration may make the game feel more linear and less open-world than its predecessor.In summary, while Sons of the Forest has introduced new features and improved graphics, it has shifted its focus away from survival mechanics and towards high-tech exploration. This may be less appealing to players who enjoyed the emphasis on survival in The Forest.I intend to update my review of the game as it continues to receive further updates.

_childDocuments_.review: So far it seems vastly inferior to the previous game. If you don't already own it, get the first game; if you already own The Forest, just go back and play it again.Graphics and graphical detail are much improved, sound is nice, apparently there's now guns , different seasons etc. but so far thats about it for the supposed positives.....-Story is somehow even more non-existent/ disjointed than the first game-Enemies are still massively buggy and just unconvincing. Despite the fact this is not only the second game in series; but has also been out for years and past 1.0 for 8 months. You can fail to survive the first 48 hours 6 or 7 times, finally build a base before getting killed, think you've succeeded the first challenge......nope, 8 enemies will spawn from nowhere, glitch straight through even multiple layers of wall and just 1 tap you while you're in inventory or build menu :(-Cooking pots seem to only spawn in 1 or 2 places amongst an enormous map. Drinking crystal clear, free flowing water from mountain springs makes you instantly sick and degrades your max health by 80% . If you play with survival elements on hard, you either have to cheat and look up cooking pot locations, or survive solely off blueberries for several days; you'll find dozens of grenades, C4 , golf carts and electric scooter things in that time, but source of purifying water? the means to open canned food? anywhere that isnt crawling with dozens of enemies? nope.EDIT: *New building system does not 'have potential' its just plain crap*,  in early game its just cumbersome and confusing. Little to nothing in terms of meaningful tutorial. A basic microscopic cabin now needs not only the same overinflated number of logs as it did in the first game, but you have to spend an extra 20 mins positioning the camera to show the option, which allows you to cut various full size logs into different shapes and sizes. Seems like it might be worth it, until you realise the inside is so small you cant even fit a fire and a bed..... Go free form/advanced building? even worse. Randomly wont let you place where you want, as it decides you're trying to lock onto another pillar 10 ft away. Build walls, but if they arent flawlessly connected and aligned as if done by a career architect, the option to build a roof never appears. Want to line defensive spikes flush to a wall? nope, game decides you must surely want some weird diagonal support beam going down into the ground, so thats the only prompt that's allowed. Game would flat out not let me even attempt any type of roof for my first base, so I started again. Built a a straight angled rectangular house, built roof beams/support frame...... wouldnt let me place anything between the supports..... so I can have the frame for a roof, but I cant have an actual roof ?!? Trash system.Imo/ TL:DRSons Of The Forest still feels like an early access beta, or a polished concept of their future plan for a sequel to 'The Forest' . If Endnight seriously consider this a mostly finished game, I'm bitterly disappointed. Requested refund given the broken state of the game, but was denied as I was generous enough to give the game more than 2 hours to prove itself, unfortunately its trash and a waste of money.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is a really good game. Unfortunately it was postponed many times and appeared in Early Access, but it turned out very well. Since the game is not finished at the moment, but is still being worked on, there are also many bugs and glitches. Among other things, that you can play through the game in 10 minutes, sound bugs, animation bugs, missing textures, etc.I play this with friends and for some reason I have unlimited shots in my pistol and when we place logs we can spawn unlimited logs.The map here is 4x larger compared to The Forest.What I like about the game at the moment is the variety of building and the building system. Also the AI ​​companions that make the game easier. There are new enemies, animals and new weapons etc. From today's point of view I think the graphics and implementation of the game are good. I really enjoy the game, not only exploring and fighting but also building and hunting. The game is being improved and the developers are also listening to the community, which is why they have not only added hotkeys compared to the predecessor, but even more. The added animations for building, eating, drinking, etc. are great. Chopping down trees not only looks better, but is also faster. I also like the seasons and the reasonably realistic day and night breaks.Unfortunately, the story is not well implemented. I hope that it will be finished, because some things are not revealed and throw a lot of theory into the room. There are many bugs, but they will be fixed.Unfortunately, the AI ​​cannot be taken into caves to fight or explore. The opponents are a mystery to me. Sometimes they do little damage and then suddenly they do a lot of damage. I find the in-game repair tool redundant as I couldn't fix anything that was broken since it can now be disassembled and moved. I also think there are fewer mutants compared to its predecessor. I hope this will change over time.Despite the problems, the game is really worth it. I'm having a lot of fun playing and I'm excited for the upcoming features and updates. The price is optimal and in addition to the records that the game has already set, I also give a clear buy recommendation.Sons of the Forest sold over 2 million copies in 24 hours and had more concurrent players (415,000) than any other released game. That is even five times more than the predecessor, which reached around 70,000 in the past few months. They even made it straight into the top 3 most played games on Steam.Keep it up!

I feel like I have committed atrocities that would make a majority of people question my character.  The older I get, I feel like certain freedoms are stripped, not only physical freedoms, but mental as well.  I was able to peruse these wares in real time.  I started with the best intentions, and soon realized that the leash was off.  After I ate my first man flesh(accidentally), I realized I regained my will to pursue different avenues of this wondrous entitlement.I feel like I have been dug out of the cemented earth.  Unearthed, unscathed, I arose anew into the arms of the sun.  I no longer feared the tribals that littered the land.  I was an animal myself.  I realized that life was filled to the brim of possibilities.  I started slow, almost cautious.  It's as if my parents were silently looking over my shoulder, but alas, I had not a care in the world.It comes in waves.  The hunger, not just for sustenance, but for trying new obstacles.  Armed with my newfound hope for the future, I built wondrous things.  With my comrades, my family, I built ungodly things.  I enhanced the human experience.  Every spear thrust, every lively spark of my stun rod, further drove me into madness.  A madness I embraced.Building only filled a small void, although creative, was enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in it's own right, and casual players can expect like a good 30 hours out of it. It's graphically stunning, the best looking and performing unity game i have ever seen, by a very wide margin in both areas. (Your performance will suck if you don't configure texture quality right though, i think 6-8gb vram for high settings)I absolutely recommend this game, it's great, you won't regret it.If you compare it to the first forest however, it falls short in certain areas. The biggest issue is that this barely qualifies as a horror game anymore, sure it has some creepy monsters, but the designs of the monsters in the forest were original and maybe even thought provoking, the designs of the monsters in this game just felt kinda generic. The monsters in the first game each had a story, the monsters in this one, simply put, don't have a story. Not to mention the scale, the monsters in the first game were big, the monsters in this one tend to not be much bigger than humans, it takes a lot of the terror away.I suppose this is done because instead we just have more of the monsters but more generic monsters vs fewer unique monsters, I know at least  I myself would enjoy the latter far more than the former.The cannibals in the original game were scary as hell for most of the playthorugh, in this one they're a nuisance at best.As for the story, the plot in this game is rather convoluted. a lot of critically important things are left entirely unexplained and some things just plain make no sense (why is all canned food cat food?! there aren't even cats! and that's just one minor thing...). It seemed like they were originally going to take the plot in a certain direction then midway completely changed their minds and made it something else instead, but left a lot of major things that could only be explained by the abandoned plot in the game anyways without making up any new explanations for them.The build system, in the original game the build system was a bit tedious, but endearing, in this game it felt only tedious to me.Possibly the worst things though were the unicycles and gliders. The unicycles allow you to move at ridiculous speeds and jump from any height without taking fall damage, and the gliders can climb indefinitely so they're more like airplanes than gliders. it's op as ♥♥♥♥ and ruins a lot of the survival elements in the game, you never have to prepare for a journey when you can just fly anywhere on the map in a few minutes without any danger. Then fly right back when you're done. This was probably their biggest mistake, the glider and unicycle seem only to be there to make the game more friendly to casuals, but it's a mistake. The golf carts are fine though.There were some things they did better though.The island is bigger (but sadly less dense with 'stuff'), the caves are much better designed, the story thrives on mystery, you play as a guy trying to unravel what happened on the island and it's a ride and a half trying to puzzle it together.So in a nutshell, i'd say this is a worthy second installation of the forest, despite it's flaws i would still call this game a masterpiece but when compared to the first forest, some of the things that made people really love it haven't been given the attention they deserved from the developer for this one. I hope the third installation will give us the best of both games.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me get right into this and start of saying that this is very fun and a lot more polished than I initially expected from Endnight saying this was going to be early access. Myself, my brother, and lots of our friends have already been kicking it into high gear with finding items and trying to get through the game.Below is more or less a bullet list of things I find awesome about SoTF.- The quality of life improvements: Base building is so much more fun and immersive now.- Sharing items: In both multiplayer and singleplayer you can share items with Virginia and with Kelvin, but in multiplayer I believe this function really shines in contrast to The Forest. It is a lot easier and more streamlined than having to pull out a tray and put an item on for each item you want to share.- Gameplay: Overall, a big improvement from The Forest- Environment: I think that they did a lot on making the world look a lot nicer and more in-depth than the previous game. That being said, one of the things that still wows me is walking through snow leaving trails that stay there for awhile, as well as the dynamic seasons and weather.Those are some of the more positive points I have for SoTF. However, that being said, I still do have a lot of things I hope that the devs take into consideration (considering they opened this for Early Access for people to provide critique on their works)While I do enjoy the game, there quite a few issues that I think the devs really need to address, many of these we have noticed and while we find funny and ludicrous, definitely have to be fixed as time goes on.1. Guns & Ammo: Guns are definitely by no means a bad addition to SoTF, but I got SoTF to have a realistic and hardcore survival horror game not to be the Doom Slayer with a 12 Gauge Shotgun. I think the damage is up to par with what i'd expect from a shotgun or 9mm pistol, but I think that the issue isn't the damage as much as it is the fact of ammunition being so plentiful that ammunition for guns is easier to find ammunition for a bow or crossbow. This is an obvious issue regarding balancing and I think as much as it is fun right now, it can lead to a slower level of replayability for the game as time goes on. Guns should be a reward for a lot of hardship and survival, but still something you need to use sparingly.2. Audio: Alright so this is something I am sure they will fix in the next update, but I am going to include this here anyways. The audio can be really neat, but really bad and broken at times, this is especially noticeable with the wind in which it will become choppy and robotic at times and also incredibly loud even with AudioFX turned way down. Again I am sure this is something they plan on fixing next update, but I am including this one anyways.3. Stability and Performance: I do not know if its just my system or if it is a common issue (though based on the response from friends and my brother it seems to be an issue across the board), but I get severe frame loss that does not relent. It is pretty odd that a game that would appear to be less taxing than a game like star citizen, I get less frames in than the latter.I have a lot more I could include, but I think these cover the biggest issues I am having with SoTF. Again, I am well aware that this game is in early access and there will be problems. But to the inevitable commentators who will mention I am judging the game too harshly since it released early, I have this to say to you: Early access is designed for criticism and critique of the game, that is why devs even bother to do early access. So if you are going to waste your time commenting to me that this is "early access so it is going to have problems" then just don't.I still recommend people to get this game, but just know it does have problems and factor that in before you buy it. I believe that Endnight will 100% turn this into one of the greatest games of 2023 right alongside Hogwarts Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person that likes survival games, I was SEVERELY disappointed in this game. There's obvious issues like the performance issues and some settings running BETTER at higher modes than lower ones, but I was willing to let it slide because I love 7 Days to Die and that game runs pretty poorly even on high-end systems.I never played the original Forest game so I can't say whether or not this is a downgrade from it's predecessor, but the world felt dull and empty and navigating the inventory and menus felt clunky as all hell, making this feel more like a bad PC port; not to mention the notebook being nearly unreadable with DLSS enabled (which also made little to no difference in performance, may I add). The way the inventory is laid out makes it where half the time I picked something up, I didn't even realize it even went in my inventory until I moved the camera way off to one of the sides (the inventory feels like it trying to interpret mouse inputs as controller inputs too), I have no clue why they didn't just use the traditional grid-like inventory screen that any other survival game uses or just let you manually place items in your inventory instead of the confusing mess it is now. The combat felt comparable to ARK, but far less responsive as if I was lagging even in single player anytime I tried to use the spear or axe, and what this game seems to consider "POIs" would just be standard world generation elements in other games. I came across an NPC that had 3 arms and 3 legs, but it had no way for me to interact with it so I tried killing it, but even then I couldn't do anything with it so why even bother adding them aside from "cool lore lol".TL;DR this game had a TERRIBLE first impression on me as a survival game player and feels like a bad PC port of a console game with a lifeless world and rushed combat, saw what I needed to see and refunded before the 2 hour mark. Most likely won't be purchasing again unless something major changes about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't going to review so early but after reading other reviews I feel compelled to.My main point is that SotF is not RELEASED. It's early access, and it's early access for a reason. Those who played TF in early access will remember how full of bugs and borderline unplayable it was when it first entered early access, and Sotf in its current state is still leagues beyond what TF was. Comparing the two seems incredibly unfair to me, especially given Endnight's proven track record of dedicated updates, communication and feedback with their community. I have high hopes and faith in the dev team that when SotF does reach full release, it'll be just as if not more polished than TF. With that being said, here's what you can expect from playing the game as of right now: - Bugs, obviously. That's the point of Early access. - Missing features that exist in TF. Features that will more than likely appear as the game goes through update cycles. - Chugging on lower spec machines. It's borderline unplayable for me if motion blur is on, and the low graphic preset is the one that functions best for me on my ancient machine (still gorgeous though). - A functional, if rugged survival experience that doesn't hold your hand with tutorials (yet) and largely lets you trial and error your way through the new crafting system while being pounded on by enemies with new and more unpredictable AI (frustrating). + Tonnes of new features like a 3D printer, peaceful mode off the bat and companion characters (I see you Virginia and I clocked your name). + Kelvin. What a funny little guy. Can't wait to see him shine properly. + A banging soundtrack. + A functional, if rugged survival experience that doesn't hold your hand with tutorials (yet) and largely lets you trial and error your way through the new crafting system while being pounded on by enemies with new and more unpredictable AI (thrilling). If excitedly waiting for new updates, finding new bugs to play around with and exercising your abundant patience sounds great to you, buy SotF and contribute to the inevitable shiny full release that'll come. If it doesn't, watch people who do have that kind of patience play it instead. No shade. It's not a full release and your expectations should be adjusted accordingly. Massive kudos to the dev team for breaking Steam without even having a full launch. I hope Endnight are proud of themselves!

_childDocuments_.review: The game had its scary/freaky moments for the first 2 hours. Until you actually die for the first time, and realise there are 0 consequences to it. You spawn either in the closest enemy camp, the bottom of the ocean, or inside a blob of slime, pull out your knife and untie yourself. Just to find that your backpack with all the gear is conveniently placed either at your feet, or the nearest shore  (you are also immune while picking it up). The enemies are super predictable, and attacks are so easy to dodge that you can just sidestep.The survival elements are non-existing, you're always thirsty, hungry and lacking sleep, but the only thing you notice is a slightly smaller stamina bar, which hardly makes any difference except if you are running long distances - of which there are a ton. VAST empty areas, with the occasional camp or point of interest, just to realise that you stopped by these points of interest in the wrong order, and you need a tool found at one of the other points. Back to running for 15 mins.Freezing? No problem, just the slightly smaller stamina bar once again.Building a base? Sure, go ahead, but there's really no point in it whatsoever. Enemies will simply open doors and make themselves at home regardless. Build a fence you say? Sure, but now Kelvin is stuck inside, as there are no gates, and the only exits you can make that actually keeps people out is a rope over the fence. The NPCs doesn't understand this, so now they are useless.I have also experience a game-breaking bug where my mouse in the inventory completely disappeared, and as you have no quick-equip buttons, I couldn't pull out my weapon. This happened inside a cave. Luckily I was playing in two-player coop, so I could just follow my buddy and revive him over and over while he did all the fighting. Couldn't really quit out, as that would have deleted multiple hours of savetime, as the only way to save is at a tent or a bed...I really don't understand the hype, and why this has received so many positive comments when there are a ton of survival games out there that makes every aspect of survival so much better. Heck, Minecraft has a more realistic survival aspect than this game. I only wish I had realised sooner what an extreme waste of money this was, as I'm past the refund limit. Here's hoping something major happens soon that makes this game playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Fight Demons.This game goes absolutely, stupidly hard.You wake up after a helicopter crash on an island, technically you're here to save some rich ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and his wife.But there's nothing stopping you from going full psychopath, eating people, building effigies out of your enemies corpses, downing entire bottles of prescription pain killers, eating random berries and mushrooms just to see what they do to you or fencing off half the island with a giant solar powered electric fence.The possibilities are as limitless as your capacity for chronic and sustained cruelty! The combat is just great.Enemies hit like run away trucks, but so do you. One good swing can take a man's head clean off at the neck and you have a cattle prod to slow him down while you line up your swing. Or if melee isn't your style there's plenty of range options. Flaming, exploding and toxic arrows. Thrown spears and rocks, grenades, IEDs, Molotov cocktails a 12 gauge shotgun and a 9mm pistol. Even a slingshot if you're feeling like role playing Denis the Menace. Building takes a little getting used to, some aspects have changed from the first game and its not all for the better.The survival guide is organized better, but some recipes are gone. You can no longer craft boats for example and building fences requires you to place every single individual post rather than just drawing a magic line on the ground and bringing logs to it.Personally I like these changes, but some players might feel annoyed not being able to lay blueprints before hand or they might take issue with the overall slower pace of building. I personally felt boats, while cool in concept, were overpowered in practice and should have been cut. There were no threats on the water and you could easily build everything essential to sustain yourself on a single boat. In general, once you get past the whiplash of having to relearn a few habits the new system is better overall. There's lots of new stuff to try building, better storage options and new traps.I do wish we still had the catapults. They were tough to use sure, but I don't think they were beyond saving the concept was really cool. Just give them a better range of travel!To help with the slower pace of building your dream house you have Kelvin! A deaf mute who... Uh, might have a serious brain injury...While he is no good in a fight, he is extraordinarily gifted with construction!You can't pre plan your custom buildings, but you can still lay blueprints out for storage and decorations, then give Kelvin a command to go and pick up everything needed to finish building them. If you don't have supplies stocked don't worry, he's perfectly capable of sourcing basic supplies like rocks, sticks and logs on his own!He can even be ordered to refill your supply caches, repair damaged structures or clear out trees and when its all done he'll take a janky dynamic break. Sitting in chairs, near fires or (pretending to) eat from food stores. Oh yeah, Kelvin also doesn't need to drink, eat or sleep. So don't even worry about giving him a bed or dog house.He's great, when he's not clipping into your lap when you're trying to sit by the fire. Spelunking and exploration as a whole remains mostly unchanged.Caves are still spooky, mutants are still creepy, cannibals are still everywhere.I think the map overall is bigger, there are definitely more places of interest and things to discover so get out there and have fun!  I think the best part is there's no random generation, everything is still uniquely crafted so you never get caught out by bad RNG and every area has its own little story to tell. You find desiccated settlers in the oldest caves, cannibalised campers on the surface and massacred maintenance men in the bunkers.  You also have vehicles now, which are stupid fun and just a little janky. They love to do flips when you crash, can ford any river or drive straight through a lake and will literally render even the toughest cannibal down to their essential parts if you hit them at any real speed.Also whatever demons that were hobbling the original game's performance have been excised completely. It looks better than ever, sounds just as good as before and preserves almost every meaningful aspect of the game play while running flawlessly. Everything a sequel should be.Discard the bits that didn't work and enhance the things that did.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Sons of the Forest is enjoyable and positively iterates on the first game by adding new weapons, tools, and a better building system. However, it currently suffers from a lack of content. You can think of the game like a sandwich with no meat in it: the bread and toppings taste good but the product suffers as an overall due to missing an integral part. This is true for both the story and gameplay/progression. I played in multiplayer on normal with two other friends. Completely unfinished and confusing; less motivating than the first game. I get that the game is in early access and that the story of the first game was slowly put into the game after multiple updates. As it stands now, there is a solid beginning/intro cutscene and an ending with nothing in between connecting the two. My friends and I felt like we stumbled into the middle of the story or missed a large part of it when we had begun the ending sequence: nothing was explained and there was no continuity – new things appeared out of nowhere with no previous introduction and no explanation for their being there. I was also not as invested in this story as I was in the first game: I wanted to save Timmy and take revenge on the island and the cannibals in the first game. In Sons I am not motivated to escape the island other than for my own survival which is trivial. Sure, there is the setup for the story which is that we are a private military investigating the island after some mega-rich dude and his family disappear on it. I do not care about these rich people. I have no personal vendetta against this island other than getting off of it as soon as possible.Spoilers: As it stands, all we do is wander around, read some emails (most of which don’t matter at all) and somehow bumble our way to the final portion of the game with no feeling about it. Sure there’s that rich family we have to find, but who cares about them? My character has no backstory with them other than being employed by them. Hopefully Endnight will greatly expand upon the story in future updates. Crafting is cool and about the same as last game, but the animation which plays every time should either only play the first time an item is crafted or be a toggleable option. The building system is a nice change, but I could see it getting tedious after a while, especially with the setting up of large log walls and needing to chop every single point. The biggest issues with the game right now are the lack of punishment for not having enough food/water/sleep, the incredibly forgiving death system, and the speed at which you are introduced to new items and weapons. These issues all play into one another. there needs to be a bigger reason to stay hydrated/rested/fed. Sure, it reduces your maximum health and stamina but that does not have much of an effect on moving speed or attack power. Food and drink are so plentiful there is no reason to hunt. My inventory was constantly full of scavenged energy drinks/bars, canned food, ramen, and so on. My friends and I were able to walk around the entire island separate from one another to every point of interest without hunting animals or running out of food once. We did this 3 times without ever needing to stop and hunt/cook food.  We only died in cave fights, and this respawned us at the mouth of the cave with all of our items directly next to us. Only bad thing was that we burned through meds, but we could just throw our heads against the wall and push through, or simply run past enemies. The game would’ve lasted longer and been a lot more engaging if we had to plan out our approaches and risk losing items/progress. I like them all, but you get them way too fast. The shotgun reduces the game to easy mode except for in the final segment. The fact that every cave with every item is also marked on the gps and available from the beginning of the game also exacerbates the issue of finding equipment way too quickly. As a result of this, the early game crafts are neglected and serve no purpose. I have no reason to use the slingshot, or craft arrows, or use the torch after the first 30 min of the game.Because of the ease of survival, forgiving death system, and speed of finding new powerful items, there is no incentive to build a base and the game is easily sped through.Also, the west of the map is where everything happens, hopefully the POIs will be dispersed and added onto. Also, bunkers are cool but not as cool as caves, and the caves could benefit from more vertical layouts. Alsox2, the dead construction men everywhere detract from the horror atmosphere as they look like they died minutes before we got there.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Currently this game has no point to exist, i understand its a Early Access Game but this game is not what i expected the sequel to be. Just like the the first game there is no point to build anything you can just leave and rejoin a save and everything will just respawn. In Multiplayer you can just save with logs and rejoin an have more logs. There is not a single hot key item besides holding inventory, at least give us one for at least one weapon. When you pull out your bag it looks like a roblox animation. This game just simply isnt what i expected, i expected it to be a military version of the forest. Maybe like overrun military bases all over the map besides the cave labs. They put so much time into building but again these is no point you can just run to all the caves get everything and win. In my opinion if feel like we lost more buildings then in the forest one if anything. (No log sled, no area marker besides gps marker, no gazabo, etc)Story: Little to non-existent even after i read all emails and papers.Kelvin and the graphics are the only good things about this game, except you should be able to mark things he shouldn't chop down. Even though there is little to no optimization for lower end pc's this last part will most likely get fixed.In conclusion even though this is early access and ive witnessed the forest one from launch early access to release, this this not looking good for the sequel. If anything this game should of been delayed by another year and only opend for free early access for people who owned the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Remove the markers from GPS and reduce resources everywhere.The gameplay itself is extremely solid and genuinely a great time with friends. The actual survival element is fun and they did an excellent job expanding building.However, outside of that the game feels like a rail track that does not incentivize the player to actually experience the survival and base building aspect.. All the key items are basically crammed in to one small portion on the map and it's all marked on your map from minute one. So you're basically just holding your GPS out the entire game walking from point to point. Every point of interest in the game is marked on the map and overflowing with resources and materials, so there is little reason to set up a base. My friends and I spent a few hours building a camp but once we had started 'exploring' we never had any reason to go back. The larger map should make players think about setting up multiple settlements around the map but because you are given SO much food and resources there is no point, so you are just riding along the guided path to the end.The story is extremely underdeveloped and left every one of my friends confused as to what the ♥♥♥♥ they were thinking by the end of the game currently. It's not like the story from the first game where you discover pieces that all fall in to place by the end. Nothing makes sense in this game, though I heard that they are still working on the story. But it begs the question why they would put the end of the game in its current state. Its extremely unsatisfying.If I had to put up constructive criticism I would say the major issues, aside from the story which from I understand they are still working on, is they need to spread out key items across the rest of the map. Flesh out and implement more than 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ caves, and remove the markers on the GPS. The game gives you beacons you have no reason to use because everything is marked already. Don't outright remove the GPS because with such a large map it is genuinely helpful. But having everything marked from the moment you launch the game really steals the experience for players to explore the world. Lastly I would reduce the resources and food you get everywhere, energy bars, MRE's and soda aside there is always a river close by and way more animals than there ever were in the original game, even on the hardest difficulty survival and resources were not an issue at all.Hopefully with more development and some changes to some of the mechanics my friends and I can put as many hours in to this as we did The Forest, otherwise I think this game will just suffer from sequelitis and be DoA outside of the sandbox element.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Review edited after 29 hours in game.The game is in Early Access, with the devs saying they were going to be in EA for another few months to polish the game up. But SotF doesnt need polish. It needs another half of a game.SotF has been in development for like six years but it just.. doesnt show in game. The plot is half-baked and barely there, the island is huge and beautiful but feels empty.Nothing gets explained, nothing is fleshed-out, nothing connects or makes thematic sense. They took 'Show, Don't Tell' and decided to neither show nor tell anything.It was... so.. so dissapointing, to wait for years and spend money on something that showed the only worthwhile parts in the trailer.And the decision to make Virginia's clothes see-through when it rains is just...it just reeks of misplaced horny fan service that feels real gross, especially when applied to a character like Virginia, in a game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Played then finished the game in co-op (3 players) a few days after release, we had a very good time.Gameplay is solid, game is beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: Disappointing SequelIn my opinion, this sequel is a missed opportunity. The developers repeated the same design flaw from the first game, making the inventory system overly complicated and hard to navigate. This time, it’s even worse due to the sheer number of items you can collect.Another major flaw is the unnecessarily massive map. The inclusion of a GPS system that pinpoints exactly where you need to go takes away any sense of exploration, reducing the game to a mere walking simulator.The base-building aspect feels completely redundant and unnecessary for progressing through the story, only serving to slow down the progress.  Gathering resources needed for base building is incredibly tedious, requiring you to run back and forth like a headless chicken.The AI is dull and predictable, with enemies seemingly spawning out of nowhere, which makes the cannibals feel disconnected from the world. Switching between tools or weapons is cumbersome and disrupts the game’s flow.The story itself is, in my opinion, poorly executed, with a confusing progression that left me disoriented. Overall, I wouldn’t recommend this game and will likely not finish it. To me, it feels more like a walking simulator with some action and survival elements tacked on.

_childDocuments_.review: As I write this I have just shy of 3 hours of gameplay, which admittedly may not sound like a whole lot. However, during my time playing I have grown quite frustrated. I understand that this game is "Early Access," and has newer features compared to the last game. I will more than likely update my review once the game fully releases, but for now here are some of the issues I currently have with this game. 1. If you are playing Single-Player, you are at a severe disadvantage when it comes to respawning. In Single-Player when you die for the first time, you are teleported to a nearby cannibal camp where you have to break free, grab your belongings and escape. What's frustrating is that when you break free, you are able to be "one-shotted" and die immediately. You might think, "Well, that's no big deal, I'll just respawn again." WRONG, after your second death you will be prompted to reload from your last save game, which could've been God only knows how long ago. So, enjoy that.2. Kelvin, or "Robby" as he is listed in the game files (more on that later) can be both extremely helpful, but can also ruin hours of gameplay. By this I mean, if you're building a base in a tree, there's a good chance that this ai will begin chopping down the tree you've been building in for 2 hours, completely ruin any work you did, and then give you a thumbs up before sitting on the ground. So, for now I suppose the only fix would be to not build a base in a tree, or just be very mindful of what this Kelvin guy is up to.3. Speaking of Kelvin, it's important to note that he is not immortal. He can be "downed" quite easily by cannibals, and you can revive him pretty quickly. That is, if he isn't down on top of a tree stump. That's right, if he's downed on top of a tree stump, tough luck, better reload your save because he's as good as dead! Which brings me to my next point.4. There are no console commands without the use of mods! Listen, I'm not THAT old, but these new release games closing off access to the debug menu/console commands are honestly ridiculous, why make me jump through hoops just to access something that I should have immediate access to? I only looked to see if I could access them in order to revive Kelvin, which even when I went into the game save files, didn't work. There is "supposedly" a way to bring him back, but I tried it, I followed the instructions exactly and now my Kelvin is completely gone. So, my tips for you if you're going to play this Early Access nonsense would be: 1. Build a shelter/set up a bed and save as soon as possible. 2. Apparently you can burn tree stumps to get rid of them, might want to do that if you care remotely about Kelvin.3. If you do care about Kelvin, keep an eye on him and exactly what he's doing in order to gather resources. 4. Play Multiplayer I guess? Again, I'll probably update this later on as they work out the bugs, but as of right now, I can't recommend this to people. Just go play the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: I've played both The Forest and Sons of the Forest since Early Access.I like what they did with Sons of the Forest. It has some cool new content to explore, new gear and the story was expanded upon. It's a pretty game as well, it wasn't as well optimized in early access, but it has improved a lot and can be played with a stable framerate, even without DLSS.I do have some criticisms about the game. The combat feels less balanced compared to The Forest. Sometimes your hits dont have an impact on the enemies. Once the enemies are armored up a lot of the primitive weaponry becomes practically useless, as the enemies dont really react to hits anymore, until you've destroyed their armor. In late game you have to depend on firearms, bombs and traps, as primitive weaponry no longer does the the job well enough.I recommend playing at custom settings, in default the gameplay just feels very off. You try to build or explore, and enemies appear and harass you. You just fought a boss or a large group of enemies, and more enemies appear. I recommend changing the enemy aggression/spawnrate to low. It feels less spammy that way.The building system is a neat concept, you can build things and mix and match, take off parts of your buildings and re-arrange. It feels like a massive chore to build things in this game that aren't coming from blueprints. The blueprint system of The Forest felt much better, although the ability to take off parts of your structures after you built them is a neat feature in SOTF.The world is way too large. 4x as large as the map of The Forest. At that point I feel like there could be a fast travel system. You put down a GPS marker and you could fast travel to that spot in the future. Could be like sleeping where some time passes and you need to eat and drink again. It's not just the size, but just how empty the world feels. Caves have the same problem here, a lot of walking, not a lot to see except for enemies here and there.Lighting in this game is pretty, so is the sound design. Both are a bit flawed though. Lighting could use more brightness in the shadows, especially in caves. Sfx themselves are well made, no complaints there, the sound mixing however could use more work. Some sounds are too quiet, other sounds are way too loud.I've played the story in early access and watched the rest of it on YouTube, and I didnt like it as much. The first game was somewhat nuts as well, but SOTF is even more nuts, you see a lot, but a whole lot is not really explained all that well, even if you read all the notes.All in all a good game, a little rough here and there, could use some improvements here and there. I hope the devs can add lots of interesting things to explore on the island, maybe flesh out the story even more.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is an exciting and immersive game that is sure to provide hours of fun and entertainment, especially when played with friends. The game's multiplayer mode is a joy to experience, as it allows players to work together to explore the mysterious forest and survive its dangers.One of the standout features of Sons of the Forest is its intricate and well-designed hunting system. While some people may find it a bit repetitive or lacking in variety, the system is nevertheless engaging and requires skill and strategy to master. Players must carefully track their prey, set traps, and use a variety of weapons and tools to take down their targets, making each hunt a unique and rewarding experience.While the game's graphics and overall design are impressive, I have noted that some of the idle animations are a bit lacking in detail. However, this minor flaw does not detract from the overall quality and enjoyment of the game.Overall, Sons of the Forest is a fantastic game that is sure to appeal to both casual and hardcore gamers alike. Its multiplayer mode is especially enjoyable, and its hunting system is both challenging and engaging. While there are some minor issues with certain animations, the game's overall quality and entertainment value make it a must-play for any fan of survival games.

_childDocuments_.review: A LOT of gamers these days confuse their feelings with constructive criticism of a game, because of that we end up with games like this.I am NOT a developer: but how can you tell me they are when you make a schematics for a tree house make it and then you tell your NPC go gather logs and cut the tree that is your house (I know its fixed but why was there in the first place)how there is an NPC that bring you dead squirrel (or some other item) drop it for you and go under the map.You can't take all kinds of cool mechanics and just put them in the game, these things don't even have to be tested they are more close to common sense.Sons of The Forest introduces some cool new ideas to the formula, but doesn't quite hit the mark. It doesn't really hit any marks compared to the first game. It's massively incomplete, and lacks any meaningful expansion on the roots of the first game. The positive standouts are definitely the graphics and the addition of AI companions to assist you across your journey if they do there job normally. The game looks good, but once you get past that you begin to realize how shallow the experience actually is. The game is "early" "access" So its okay to put out 3-4 hours of game content for 30$ knowing that it took them 4 years to get this 3-4 hours of content when they had a previous game that they could take from. - The combat system is a huge let down. I was hoping for an expansion on the melee system from the first game, but instead they added guns which I don't think is a good direction. I mostly used the pistol and one shot everything but the shotgun is hilariously overpowered, and you'll never run out of ammo because you can just farm ammo spawns. When you know you're in power in a combat situation, there's absolutely no chance of you being scared or getting tense. The shotgun gives you this power. - The world is so empty, there are barely any point of interests, and the point of interests you find are all the same with the same useless loot. I spent more than half my time playing walking through the woods from point A to point B with no interesting landmarks in between ahh wait actually there was a pooped ponds randomly.- Base building is totally pointless. We spent a lot of time building a base (like 20h 2 people just chillin) only for us to leave it and never return until we finished the story. While the new building system is intuitive, it takes way long to achieve the results, even like a simple wall. The UI for placing the logs and stuff is very limited itself. There's no snapping On/off option when you need it. Placing sticks and logs becomes very tedious after a while.- Caves in 'The Forest' were dark, deep, confusing, a pain to traverse, had verticality and connected you to other parts of the world.Here we get one entry, almost a linear path, a one-way exit point around the back (not marked on map). Furthermore on the caves they are so much more empty besides just enemies after enemies to get to the thing at the end and leave.- Hunting animals for skin is pointless now because they took out all the cool items you could make with themThere is a lot more stuff but i thing this for now is enough... in this review I put as much effort as the developers for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Only 15 hours in and have already seen just about everything this game has to offer. It falls short in almost every category. The new building system is really cool and works good for the most part, but there is a lack of different types of buildings. No defenses for your base other than walls. But at the same time you don't really need them because you can go days without seeing an enemy near your base. Also, your base is pointless. I probably spent half of those 15 hours building a base with friends and there is really no point to it other than just having fun building different structures. You can easily just travel the world and you'll find plenty of food and an unlimited amount of water almost anywhere you go. There is almost no survival aspect at all.Kelvin (the AI helper) is a very cool addition but he is buggy and can sometimes hurt you more than help. The best thing i found for him was to fish if your base is right beside a river and he catches about 2-3 a minute so you'll never run out of food. He is also good for getting logs and sticks. He can honestly be a little OP if someone is wanting the true survival experience. There should be an option to turn him off. I guess you can just never tell him to get stuff but then he just gets in the way and will jumpscare you from time to time.The story is just flat out awful. I dont even know what it was. You can realistically beat the game in 5 hours or less. I truly hope they add more to it including more enemy types and a boss fight at the end because there isnt one. The caves, while visually they look great, are also not as good as the first game. They are all just linear caves with only 2-3 enemy types in them. No puzzles or special gear you need to traverse them like there is in the first. (other than a rope gun that is extremely easy to get.) There are also less caves. The map is apparently 4 times bigger but it seems like there is less spots or POIs than the first game, so in the end its just a lot more running to get from cave to cave. Overall, the game is visually stunning. Im very pleased with the graphics and animations theyve added. It does take a pretty good toll on your PC though. Im running an overclocked i7 9700k and a RTX2080 gpu and still only getting around 60-70 fps on medium settings (playing on 1440p ultrawide)They have a really good base for the game but sadly in its early access state I just cannot recommend it until more is added. Basically just a base building and running simulator. Im excited to see what they add in the coming months.This is also my first steam review so apologies if its not layed out great.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, the game is a solid upgrade from the first. Building and crafting is extended upon with more variety and more grinding in a lot of cases. Obviously some players may find this irritating and time consuming but I don't feel like it takes away from the experience too much. After all, the fun of the first game was partly due to finding a spot to plant roots, defending it from whatever monster comes your way, and then expanding the area you're in or moving on and finding a new spot.I have no problems with the graphics, the game is gorgeous and a definite improvement from the first; I have no complaints whatsoever there.My big, main, GLARING problem with the game, is the story. Specifically, the end. Because my god, Endnight are showing that they do not know how to plot a suitable, well thought out or comprehensible ending to their games.So the starting plot of the game has you arrive at the island hosting the titular forest in search of the CEO of PuffCorp, Edward Puffton, his wife Barbara Puffton, and daughter Virginia. The helicopter you are in crash-lands on an area of the item and you are briefly accosted by a man holding you at gunpoint before knocking you out and the cutscene ending, leading to the actual gameplay starting. One of the first things you can do upon starting is to assist a guy that was in the same helicopter as you. His nametag reads Kelvin and he becomes your assistant throughout the rest of the game, accepting commands ranging from building a fire to following you around with a boombox radio like it's the 80's again.The problem starts, like in the first game, with too many plot threads that the game tries to clear up before the end, with extremely mixed results. We get threads related to the island (What was Edward Puffton doing here? Why did he go missing?), the characters we meet  and the various encounters we have on the island . As the story goes on more and more get added  and a few DO get resolved, but the general lack of payoff and the unexpected introduction of new elements  leads to the largest attempt at tying up loose ends since Star Trek Voyager's finale.We get to the end of the game, where more and more threads are getting dropped out of nowhere  which leads to a bottleneck and then sudden release plot and story and "answers" of everything all at once  that just feels extremely unsatisfying and to be honest poorly executed.This is the exact same problem that occurred in The Forest. Endnight added all of these tasty little tidbits of information, to which most people's expectation would be that they get answered in due time. But they don't. And it's really quite disappointing, because it sours the ending of what was otherwise a good sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of the classic horror movie "the Descent" and what it would be like to crash landed on a hostile cannibal island. The survival elements take a bit of getting used to and you feel like a fish out of water when you first crash on the island. Much like Arnold in the predator, you start to become one with the environment and emerge a more ruthless and efficient cannibal killing machine. Once they respect you, you can generally find your way unimpeded. The cannibal AI is a lot of fun to mingle with. Trying to stay neutral with them for as long as possible at first was interesting but sooner or later things will get ugly. A fantastic title solo but I imagine playing this with buddies would be an absolute blast. Melee combat feels really good and the dismemberment is a nice touch. If you enjoy Subnautica but wouldn't mind more horror, combat, and defence elements this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, don’t get me wrong, Sons of the Forest can be a blast when you’re playing with friends. The building mechanics and physics are genuinely impressive. But here’s the thing, it feels like the building part is its own separate game, while exploring and finishing the story is like an afterthought. It’s almost like they took two different games, slapped them together, and hoped it worked.For a game that’s under 20GB, it’s a visual upgrade—but honestly, it feels like The Forest with a bigger inventory and slightly shinier graphics. The story? Uh, what story? In the first game, at least there was a clear narrative. But in Sons of the Forest? I’m pretty sure the plot is just a bunch of random scenes mashed together. It’s like the devs were like, “Let’s add a time-traveling subplot at the end because, why not?” At this point, I wouldn’t be surprised if they suddenly reveal that it was all a dream, or worse, an elaborate prank.It’s an alright game if you’re looking for co-op fun, but as a sequel, it leaves a lot to be desired.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: This was clearly a technical and graphical enhancement over the previous title. Everything feels better at a surface level. Crafting, combat, movement and even the inventory are all clear improvements over the original. It was also nice to see more enemy variety through the game.  this game manages to fall flat in execution of these improvements. None of the building mechanics provided any meaningful advantage in any way, nor are any of them required for progression, so why would I do them? It's more fun to simply explore and find progression. However the only issue with progression is how linear it is. I'll find 3 caves before I find the 1 that contains the item I need to make any progress. ON top of that, the larger map this game has is actually a determent because all it serves to accomplish is more wandering around for the correct cave. Even if you manage to map out all the correct caves to visit, getting around the map takes far longer than I would like, with no way to alleviate. So I ask you, if the building system is meaningless, and the exploration and story feel bad because the bottle-necked linear progression and ridiculous treks across the map, what is there left in the game? My friends and I were close to beating the    before we even bothered to try making a base of any kind, and when we did, it all felt pointless. We built a tree house, we built a cabin and we built some water and food collection. Issue being that none of this did anything. A cabin was just as effective as pitching a tent in the middle of nowhere, and we managed to have more than enough water and food just by exploring. So what benefit was provided by stopping to make a camp?It feels weird to say, but I think this game could benefit from adding some grinding. If I have to spend an extended amount of time killing cannibals or hunting, it may actually incentivize me to build a base. They could probably also benefit from a bit more depth to the crafting tree that would utilize buildings in a base, as well as something to make traversing the map a bit easier. Fast travel seems against the spirit of the game, but I can't think of a better solution.This game tries to do both the survival crafting thing, and the story thing but it fails to interweave them in any meaningful way, so it just ends up falling short of them both. I would look at a game like Subnautica (specifically, Below Zero) for an example of a similar game of this genre that has managed to pull off this combination successfully.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I said I would not recommend this game to people, due to the lack of variety in activities, very little endgame content, and poor community cultivation. I am happy to say that 2 of the 3 issues have been resolved, and it is clear they will be adding even more content to keep you active. There are still some small issues, like poor controller support, and just minor jank that never got ironed out, but it is not enough to warrant a bad review.I will say, that I think an emphasis needs to be made on creating a more active and connected community. Games live on for 2 big reasons: Open source code, and community cultivation. Endnight already said they will open up modding on full release, but the community for this game feels fractured, despite evidence of a large base. I think Endnight needs to add better matchmaking, and make it easy to find groups of people that are in the stage of the game you want to be in. The official discord needs overhauling and moderation so that activity is encouraged. Lastly, there needs to be better tools for server hosts/owners to police and control their games, so that trolls and griefers get filtered out as fast as possible.I love this game, and all I want is more community. I am on the verge of starting one myself if Endnight doesn't start doing it. I want to play with people, but it is so hard to find groups. This game would be in my top 10 games of all time if they made it easy.P.S: FEMALE. PLAYER CHARACTERS. Seriously Endnight there are a lot of women who play this game and they still can't play as themselves.

I have notes:-The map is monumentally larger and simultaneously so, so empty -and exploration is largely just a big fat waste of time. -There isn't an easy mode to this game. On the lowest setting enemies shrek you like you're on the hardest setting of the first game. -Caves are more empty, less dangerous, less spooky, and overall less interesting/fun to explore than the first game. It's almost as-if a good portion of the game was generated by a program rather than hand-crafted.-There are ten thousand too many deer.-I miss spear-poke-staggering enemies.For most the upgraded visuals will be enough and they'll be happy. I was hoping for something with a bit more meat and a bit more depth even if I did have fun playing it for a bit -I experienced burnout in just a couple days of play while I have hundreds of hours in the first game, so make of that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has soooo much promise and I have had fun with it at times BUT I just can't bring myself to recommend it in it's current state. The reason? Too many enemies. And no I don't mean it's too difficult or that I don't like difficulty (I do). You are CONSTANTLY being raided by enemies no matter what you are doing. You may decide that you want to spend 10 minutes building a base but you can't because a hoard of enemies will constantly interrupt you over and over again, destroy the structures you are building and then if you die, and get revived, you are INSTANTLY downed again because enemies will continue to attack you before you regain control of your character. The amount of enemies is ABSURD, and it ruins for what could be such a good survival game. There has to be pockets of peace in the game so that the player can catch their breath and start exploring other aspects of the game such as building and exploration, but those aspects become non existent when you are bombarded by combat situations every minute.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I enjoyed the first game, I was surprised at how little there is to actually do in Sons of the Forest. Updates throughout early access have slowly made the game artificially more difficult, while enemy AI hasn't improved in over a year, developers have removed armor and ammo sources, and even reduced the effectiveness of some weapons. Electrical system is largely incomplete and low-function, Kelvin's AI still doesn't allow him to swim after nearly a year, and Virginia is still a hit or miss when it comes to being friends. The "new" lumber system simply makes building harder and cutting down trees is mostly the same.Sons of the Forest lacks the love that was put into the original game, this game is NOT ready for full-release.EDIT 04/22: As time has passed since the "1.0 Title Update" there have been multiple updates still adding features and mechanics left out of the base-game. As I stated, the game is not done, and the developers at Endnight Games have now proven that. This game is *still* in beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly was really excited about this game and the first 4-5 h were great but I got very disappointed.  Pros :- Graphics are stunning, the world is crazy beautiful and immersive. - Building feels very hands on and intuitive once you get the concept. - Cannibals do a good job at making you feel observed everywhere you go. Cons :Where to start..- No keybinding for inventory- Island is huge but no exploration is needed as EVERYTHING is written on your GPS- The caves are underwhelming to explore, very linear and so little of them.- No incentive/need to build anything as you can just run from cave to cave/basements and never run out of food and drink- Story was just underwhelming I don't know I was hyped about this game but it feels like everything went into developing the island but not so much about the story and content. IMO it needs a looot more cave especially for an island this big. A redesign of the caves with more verticality and complexity. A balance in difficulty making a requirement to build up and defend yourself. A little bit more of story and not being spoonfed all the exploration. Its still early access and much can be improved hopefully.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off as a positive, this game looks phenomenal. Visibility is great and the graphics are superb even in rain and water. Outstanding work done by the team. The adjustments to how cold works and when you get cold is a much welcome change, likewise to the lack of blood washing.On to my gripes and first-completion thoughts done in multiplayer.Much fun and excitement was had during playthrough, but very very bitter taste left in my mouth after finishing this game under 5.5 hours.Item number 1: Nerf the babies                          Just Kidding                          Actually do it though                          I begAbsolutely no motivation or reason to settle down and build a base. Despite me and my friends loving to build bases in The Forest, here in SoTF, we finished the game without cutting down a single tree. Due to the lack of speedy movement within the much larger upscaled island. It is very hard to justify building a base when the second you want to go somewhere important you have to run around for minutes on end. That being said the stamina and movement has been greatly improved since the previous game (despite the base movement being much slower).The UI has also been greatly improved for inventory. HOWEVER, the movement within the inventory feels sluggish and the inability to hotkey equip weapons and items makes switching weapon annoying, to the point where we would be running around for minutes on end with an item we don't care about, or putting us at a disadvantage as the inventory switching is too slow. Needing to hold down the button for inventory to access the quick inventory makes little to no sense.The building menu is small, annoying to navigate, and lacklustre compared to the previous game. However the new mechanics for building are amazing and I can't wait to see how this is expanded upon with new buildings. Honestly, words cannot express how pleased and amazed I am with the building mechanics. Only gripe is when a log is cut down to a quarter and removed, it can't be placed back in the corners of a log, and thus, loses almost all of its purposes. Again, as in my first play-though, I find it strange that the lady in blue only spawns after building and due to my friend killing her within seconds, I am unable to comment on the inclusion of her.Speaking of buildings, the map doesn't feature nearly any interesting landmarks which provide subtle and interesting hints of lore, besides the odd cannibal camp, where we interestingly see mutants tied up and tortured. Furthermore, for a billionaire island a lack of a mansion and excessive underground bunkers demonstrate a seemingly un-linked narrative and world in certain areas similar to the first game, though a noticeable improvement has been made. In terms of bugs I have noticed a few audio issues and clipping but no game breaking bugs that have hindered the playing experience or immersion.Guns are too OP and we played on the hardest difficulty.For a story I couldn't get enough of in the first game, the only thing I can about remember from this game, is golf balls, or lack there of as read by the emails.Main Summary:Story felt bland, short, disappointing and didn't expand upon the first game.Characters were non-existent despite being in cut-scenes and playing as one.The Island, despite being one of the best looking in any game ive played in a very long time, felt unpopulated by any meaningful structure / exploration chance mainly due to movement/time taken to travel, further hindered by GPS/Map almost pointing you away from the freedom of exploration.Inventory was a breath of fresh air, but is slow and an irritation to use.Building is downright awesome. Though quarter logs are useless once taken off a building. And UI for building book is small, sluggish and lackluster.I have alot more I could say about this game, but I'd rather not bore you to death. I may or may not add to this once playing more, and actually give some better feedback. This is a first playthrough feelings/hottake i guess? XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most fun games my wife and I have played co-op in a long time.  There's just something serene and peaceful about exploring a really vast area with all sorts of hidden secrets and discoveries to be had, meanwhile stocking up supplies to last through the winter.  And finding all sorts of new and exciting ways to cook and prepare the bountiful selection of deer, rabbit, and tasty humans.  Raw is delicious (just ask Virginia), but dried foot and finger jerky is great for when you're hiking across the island, or have a nice steaming bowl of Greg on a cold winter's morning.  Just remember folks, friendly fire is not friendly, so do your relationships a favor and don't hit your partner with sharp stick in the back of the head... I mean, we all know you were just trying to spear another baby, but you have to wait your turn!  Plenty of babies to skewer.Just one thing I'd like to see different.  Babies should be a good source of meat.  I mean, we can enjoy a bowl of Greg, so why not a plate of roast suckling baby.  Mmmmmmm.

_childDocuments_.review: For far too long, the indigenous people of The Forest have endured terrible suffering at the vile hands of rich colonists from the aviation industry. Innocent families have been forced to live in constant fear of being bombarded with deafening aircraft, brain-damaged tourists, endless hate speech and incorrect pronouns. What once was a virgin paradise they could call home, now has been left brutally violated, chopped up, eaten out, and covered in toxic luggage.Peaceful mutant inhabitants have faced a relentless barrage of violent oppression and vicious persecution ever since the privileged invaders descended from the sky. They are repeatedly mercilessly misjudged, misgendered, and mistreated. Getting roasted in front of their friends, rudely left hanging, or being served up a flat stew has become common practice. The fully clothed bigots not only have the audacity of exploiting their distinguished culinary traditions, but have even begun appropriating their renowned decorative culture. Surrounding themselves and their stolen property with The Forest's beautiful diverse people and animals in the hopes of appearing more inclusive.. They're not fooling anyone.How much longer will this cruel onslaught of atrocities last? The time has come for justice to be served. We must expose and prepare the despicable savages who have wronged the brave mutant natives to no end. If only our barbaric society could be as harmonious as theirs, the world would be stunning. In tune with nature and brimming with exquisitely bare people who come in all shapes and sizes. We should all aspire to one day be able to identify as them. Next time you set your crooked feet on their sacred land, drop your filthy clothes and humbly apologize to each one of them. Bow down and offer them the reparations they so ravenously need.
