_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished, buggy, and inelegant in some weird ways, both in what new it brings to the table alongside stuff unusually missing compared to its predecessor. I don't think it's reasonable or fair to expect Sons of the Forest to be literally exactly The Forest 2.0; Endnight clearly wanted to steer some game systems, design tropes, and feedback loops from the last game into oblivion in favour of newer ideas that serve similar functions but require a different approach to the meta, and that's very welcome. But I cant help but shake the feeling that it's missing 'something'.That being said, many of those 'somethings' are stuff that I figure will be patched in over time, or already have been in some degree. New items and construction complexities. More interesting NPC/cannibal reactions. What's there is already really good and interesting as a foundation or framework, and there is a positive feeling that Endnight are filling the gaps to flesh them out.And what's new and functioning is really cool. The base system needs work to deepen options, but the build freedom via the new system is fantastic. I love the seasons transition, even if they feel largely inconsequential with exception of Winter. The game is loaded with gorgeous visual cues and tricks, and oozes atmosphere and feel. The core identity of The Forest is absolutely here, and it's been an absolute joy to jump back in.I think, long term, my only worry is the quality of the cave systems. The crew I play with haven't explored all the caves, but only one really stood out. And it was great! It was super long, moody, and tense. Really captured the feeling of the original game. But the rest have been remarkably short and forgettable. I recall the devs talking about more complex cave systems, and I just don't see that here yet, and I'm not 100% convinced it's something they're patching in.Either way, a better "early access" game than most early access games, and a really solid foundation for a sequel to The Forest. Some stuff works better than others. Some stuff feels unfinished and fixable. Other stuff maybe undercooked or underdeveloped and not sure if it'll get fixed. But nothing that, in my opinion, detracts from the experience as a whole and what it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed my limited time with the game so far and would actually recommend it, to an extent. As someone who almost never experiences the "rampant issues" with game that everyone seems to always talk about, this is a negative review simply because of the wildly differing experiences people are having with the game.I will say, having played the original all the way through again recently, this game is in a way better state than the original in a variety of ways. The pure survival aspects seem way better tuned so you're not on the brink of death at an given moment because you can't seem to find food or clean water anywhere. Admittedly though, Sons definitely feels overtuned in terms of food at times and the fact that you never have to boil/purify water in any way seems a bit odd considering the the original was. Building, gathering resources, and just the overall play experience also feels way better here for the most part.Now then, the negative stuff. The addition of helper npcs like Kelvin and Virginia are really nice, when they work... When tasked with doing something, Kelvin will regularly stop at random times and just sit at your campfire for sometimes days. When told to stay in place, he will eventually also just start wandering in your direction and has nearly died numerous times in my playthrough because of this. Virginia is an interesting case. You don't ever really actually interact with her, instead she just becomes friendly one day. You can give her your guns to help defend you, which is pretty nice. Especially considering she doesn't even need ammo. But just like Kelvin, even once she's friendly she'll just run off with your gun sometimes or even just not shoot at the enemies.Now, my biggest complaint with this game is the enemies. Like I've seen mentioned in other reviews, there is very little variety in the mutants. Which is odd considering just how more kinds of basic guys there are now. As far as I've seen there are only 2 types of actual mutants: the finger ones and the twin things. I've seen people talk about there maybe being more as you get through the story, but it really doesn't live up to the variety in the original game. The actual combat itself also just feel rough. It's actually a bit better than the original, especially considering the variety of weapons you're given to play around with. But, it seems like every enemy in the game is able to one or two shot you on both normal and hard. In fact, the only difference between normal and hard that I've noticed is that enemies have more health and  there's more patrols wandering around when playing on hard. Was this the case in the original? Actually, kind of yes. But the thing about the original is that armour actually did something. One creepy armour in the original lasted for a few hits against the final boss's one shot attacks. All the armour I've used in Sons seems to last maybe one hit to even basic enemies. I honestly don't know how I would change the combat balance, all I know is that it just feels off right now.As far as glitches go, like I stated at the beginning, I haven't really encountered many. Most ones I can think of are pretty minor: some weird interactions while using the sled, building free furniture, bodies turning invisible when picked up, etc. There are only two major ones that I remember finding. One was being able to duplicate logs when being rejected while trying to place them down as a wall. The other one was being able to push someone through the map in multiplayer just by standing on their head. The only one that could be considered really game breaking was the clipping through the floor and even then we were able to fix that pretty easily. But, looking at other people talk about glitches, there is a good likely hood you encounter some way more annoying stuff than I have.[Edit] Almost forgot to mention this: this games map is absolutely huge and amazing looking. But, there are a lot of caves that just feel like nothing and are just one room with really basic supplies that are found in droves all around the rest of the map. Because of it's size too, it just takes forever to get places. All you need to fix that is just some for of alternative transportation. Like, there's the sled but all that does it get you down hill faster (when it decides to work properly). Someone else mentioned in their review adding something like a mountain bike, but you could also just add a way to maybe fix  up one of the hundreds of golf carts scattered across the island.[Edit 2] They did add the hang glider literally today, but haven't used it yet.All in all I really like what's already here, I just want to see it become even better and really be able to live up to the legacy of the original.tl;dr - I don't hate the game, it just has some flaws to iron out before it can really be considered amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: (Updated review)The forest is in my top 5 favourite games of all time and easily one of the best, if not the best survival game available on steam. Sons of the forest was an extremely anticipated sequel that me personally and clearly the rest of the forest community have been waiting for since most people beat the first game.I am immensely disappointed with this game as the game feels like a quick cash grab from end night since people had stopped buying the first game so they had no revenue coming in.When i first loaded into the game with friends, (that's after 15 mins of just trying to get into the game let alone play) i was initially blown away by the visuals and was impressed, until i started playing and my vision was cleared from hype and i realised how poor this game is compared to the first.The game is a literal walking simulator, and there are no other forms of transportation available in the game apart from the rope gun which is a big downgrade from the zip lines in the first game. When the map is 4 TIMES the size of the original game, at a minimum a form of transport should be included as a standard (the sled does not count since it is only downhill). The game feels like a giant linear space giving no incentive to explore because there is nothing in the map apart from the same caves over and over, but most of them you can't even get through because 85% of them requires a key card! There is absolutely ZERO sense of direction so for new players it will be a nightmare walking around the map for hours looking through cave after cave just to find they are in the wrong one because it requires a key card, or go to a green ping on the map that requires a shovel. Oh did i mention you have to figure out yourself by checking every cave which one has the rope gun on top of all this just so you can get said shovel to open the same hatches in the ground over and over?Many things from The Forest are missing in the second game hilariously enough (even though the game is double the price) from small quality of life things like the spear bag, stick bag etc, up to the point where you can't even build DOORS OR GATES WITH LOCKS so cannibals can just walk into your base freely.Building is a massive downgrade in the sequel since over half of all the blueprints from the first game are just non existent (that includes all cannibal traps by the way) up to the custom building that has been replaced with the new clunky time consuming mess of placing each individual log yourself, and that's after you manage to get the snap point to align up. There are still annoying holes when you build a roof so at least there's one feature back from The Forest.The new inventory is horrible, like the player has just thrown the items you acquire onto a tarp and stuck some cheap amazon led strips to, so you are left to search through your inventory hoping to find what you're looking for. And do not get me started on the backpack hot bar being removed that is just pathetic considering how much larger the inventory is in comparison to the first game.The only thing i have not had a problem with is the optimisation, while not perfect could still be improved, but look at every other review that lists a bug and i guarantee you i have experienced all of them.In conclusion, at this current state, the game is just a watered down version of the first game with less features and an even worse story line  and a bigger map with nothing else new to uncover, just the same repetitive walk round look in funny hole in rock find item and go into another rock hole then boom game finished. Until this game gets the features back from the first forest and the god forsaken bugs are sorted out, i can strongly advise you to stay away from this game until it is out of early access, and maybe then they'll lower the price so you actually get what you pay for instead of overpaying for a lack-lustre title as it sits currently.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing Sons Of the Forest, and I'm sure I'll be picking it up again soon.Graphics and audio are fantastic. (Audio in caves is particularly great but horrifying.)Base building is an easy skill to learn but a hard one to master. Picking the right location, and building an aesthetically pleasing base that can keep unwanted guests out can be a little tricky.Combat  doesn't feel clunky at all and while there is a bit of a learning curve, once you get used to it you shouldn't have too much trouble dealing with whatever the game decides to throw at you. Usually.Kelvin is great at gathering resources for you, and Virginia is an absolute beast with a shotgun. I do wish you were able to interact with them more though. _childDocuments_.review: Whilst a promising title, I cannot recommend the game in its current state. The constant, never-ending enemy attacks on your base of operations are a headache and disallow you from focusing on building, in addition to scaling based on your base size, regardless of the level of equipment you poses on your person, often leading to overpowered enemies and subsequent deaths. With early-game equipment, even a single enemy can be challenging and dangerous, and as the numbers grow, the game is virtually unplayable, as surviving combat becomes unlikely,Speaking of the building system, it is quite different from the original game, though does still have some similarities. Whilst the inherent idea of the changes to it is quite nice, the practical side of things makes for tedious gameplay and leads to frustration in the many occasions where the system refuses to cooperate with the player, e.g. when constructing in water or on cliffs.Furthermore, I really despise the inventory system, which was miles better in the original Forest. The system Sons of the Forest uses is far less smooth, and leads to confusion due to the whole inventory not being visible at a glance, and requiring you to search for items by moving the camera; which in turn doesn't always respond to your hopes and wishes, leaving you frustrated and without the item you are searching for. Changing in and out of the inventory is also prone to FPS drops and rendering issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons Of The Forest, the sequel to the forest, brings a similar approach to the first game. However, it suffers some underlying issues like the first game, with even worse stacked on top of it. The sequel's map is different yet similar to the first, only major difference, is that its incredibly huge. There are seasons and varying changes that happens throughout the time you play, other than that the map is incredibly barren and empty. This is an incredibly massive flaw to any open world game, it lacks any true reward for exploration for players and it is an easy way to become disengaged with the game itself. The GPS ruins the fun for discovering things, and 9 times out of 10 you cannot access what you find and the game shows no hints towards getting any item (shovel, keycard). The gargantuan map has very little content anywhere you go, with only some tiny camps and maybe a cannibal camp if you're lucky. It constantly encourages looking at the GPS and simply going to hot spot locations scattered around the map already marked for you. Walking to each and every spot is incredibly tedious with no random events and no landmarks to be found. The caves found are only filled with loot, unlike the first game where there were cave cannibals to be found in almost each and every one. The loot is always stale, and there is such little reward for what travels you have to take to get there.That being said the building, and the crafting systems are honestly very satisfying. You interact and make new buildings and tools and you watch it all happen, I found this mechanic incredibly fun and really cool. However, making bases and buildings and putting the effort into creating any actual home feels very pointless, as the map is so big that by the time you want to go back home its at least an actual hour to get there, there is no raft, no glider, no nothing to get you around like the first one. This with the lack of interaction with the environment creates nothing but a tedious and non-engaging travel around the map.With almost 8 hours in, the enemies still remain the same, and you're constantly being harassed by crawler cannibals, with a selective few upright and large cannibals, On day 12 there has been almost nothing new to look forward to around the map, with only finding one conjoined twin mutant creature found only once the whole time.A lack of a hot bar or any sort of quick way to pull out any weapon makes fighting the cannibals all the more frustrating. And if you do die in the game there is little to no consequence, you simply wake up, cut yourself down and then bam there's your loot right in front of you. All in all, the sequel is like the first game but honestly worse, with the only things feeling updated is the building and crafting mechanics being more interactive.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: I am aware of the fact that the game is not finished yet.However it is not even a beta.It runs smoothly and I only had a few bugs like a completely red screen or weird animations.But what really pisses me off is the lack of innovation and content.-mutants are the same or less varieties than before (again babie mutants, the normal ones and the crawlers, ...)-if you are cold nothing happens and you can literally run through the mountains in a pink pyjama.(no joke, there is a pink pyjama)-you can be tired without hard consequences-there is so much food on this map you can eat like 20  racoons and 30 deers every 10 meters. Its so easy they could remove the need for eating and drinking altogether, because it makes no difference. It also makes building traps or growing crops completely useless.-water everywhere, no need for rain collection or smth-a  lot of structures and items are missing (big bonefire, rain collector, pouch for sticks, pouch for berries, ...-no infections, you dont have to wash off the blood anymore-after 10 min you get 1000 weapons-shotgun too powerful (one shot everyone) must be nerfed or mutants must be stronger/armored or less ammo-everything is marked on the map, there is no need to explore-you could craft a speer in the first 2sec and win the game-storyline makes no sense and is far too crazy for my taste-basebuilding is still not necessary, you can build a stick bed for saving  and thats itthis gamedesign is so bad you can carry EVERYTHING with you and it won't slow you down. Everything you ever need is in your pocket and thats why you don't have to return to your base ever.-the seasons are irrelevant and the winter is no challenge-the AI is not much better than before. in fact they dont scream to alert their mates anymore and they removed some other stuff. It doesnt feel like you fighting against a tribe, but more like a few drunks in the woods-they also removed the mutants from patrolling the map with the light during night time-nobody is talking, not even the cinematics are with voices.-no punishment for death, you respawn, pick up your bag and nothing happened-no bossfights, everyhing is happening in cinematics-you can run for few km and dont encounter any mutant. if you see one you just keep running and nothing happens. like i said before they are not dangerous and can easily be avoided/killed-the fights are the same like in the first game. you hit them, they fall and you finsish them off.-no shortcuts for weapons or tools, you have to get out your backbag in the middle of a fight-they copy&pasted half of the laboratory-some mutants look blurry-there are animals missing in Sons of Forest 2 (e.g. lizzards, snow bunny, ...)-the mutated woman is just another unfinished part with 0 impact to the game-the whole game feels like a reskin of the first game, no innovations and far less content now-the caves are linear and very simple you go in at A and run straight to exit B-they removed the stick markers, but you dont need them because everything is so simple-i dont like that they give the player a handheld GPS. What happened to maps? Its so much better for the atmosphere to use maps and find new parts of a map and stuff like this. Its not possible with a handheld GPS. A big map is better for planning what to do, mark stuff on the map with little pebbles....would be so much nicer.-stamina is far too high. you can run, fight and cut down trees for hours.-there is a radio playing in every 2nd camp, but they did remove the walkman of the first part where you could find tapes, put them inside and learn more about the story or listen to music-loot still respawns after the map is reloaded, completely destroying the balancing(you dont have to restart for loot anyway because there are camps with 20 ropes)-you can cut a piece of meet out of a seagul and it restores as much hunger as a part of a deer?!-since you don't have to craft clothing for winter time or for the mountains, there is no need to hunt deers, because they dont benefit the player. Just eat 2 squirrels and don't bother with hunting big animals. They missed out on so many possibilities to make a great game that I cant recommend it and this point.

_childDocuments_.review: 50+ Hour Review: This game is recommended at $29.99, BUT I would never pay over. In a summary, majority of the budget and attention for this game went into the graphical detail and experience. It almost feels like they made the above-ground open-world experience part of the game first, and rushed everything else. Big open world with not a whole lot to do.  The world and visuals are BEAUTIFUL! There are lots of interesting mechanics that play a part in the open-world experience that can make your game play interesting. However, this game seems to be lacking everything else the original Forest did. It could be because of early access, but I don't see how it can be adjusted. The caves are super small and do not take much to get the required tools needed to progress through the story line. [SPOILERS] Once you get the shovel, you pretty much unlock the rest of the world. The problem is it feels too quick and easy, especially when it took only 3 caves to do that. The cave containing the shovel is the last cave you will ever explore, all the rest for some reason are just loot caves with little to no reward. The original game had MASSIVE caves where it could take you at least an hour to just explore. When I first launched this game, I was overwhelmed to see the GPS have so many caves, but ended up being a disappointment. Bunkers carry the rest of the game, with all but 4 being crucial to the story. The story itself is very very weak. All the sudden characters start getting involved with no real introduction. There just doesn't seem to be a lot of content besides building bases and fighting cannibals. Don't get me wrong, the game looks amazing and is very fun the first many few hours, but very lacking in terms of content to the original game, even as an early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited since November 2019 when the teaser trailer came out. Now that it released in 2023, it is very good. The building is greatly overhauled with deciding how to set up beams of tree logs instead of constant blueprint. The ability to split the logs in half to make floor and working on a roof or splitting them into stumps. The game has more damaging enemies now that you have access to guns and how you progressively get a bigger and better arsenal. The mutants are interesting, scary and creepy in their designs. They get less worrying to fight when you get better weapons. The inventory is greatly improved from the last game and you more room for resources, food and items. Little sad that you can't work towards greater inventory space. But makes sense in way that you are apart of the army this game. The graphics are beautiful and makes the game stunning. Seems that tried getting a smooth and great experience to the player base graphics and animation wise. The story is pretty bland, but the story doesn't need to be a great adventure and movie like. The objective is quite simple, Find and rescue a billionaire on an remote island. Since this is sequel to The Forest it isn't really a surprise that you crash and end up stranded on the island. The ending is quite interesting in a way but also confusing. there is things given to you but not really explained. Concluding the review of the game is must say that there are somethings that they removed which was great in The Forest. Traps are minimised to two and certain things aren't explain as well as they should have been. There are no hotkeys anymore, so you can't quickly switch from weapon to weapon or to heal fast. But can probably be they wanted a more *realistic* take on inventory? The game is great though, I had a lot of fun playing for the first time and it was really relaxing to build and take me time with building or just exploring. -Overall score: 7/10 -26/02/23

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game after about 14 hours of playing.Positives:- Building mode has been a huge improvement over the original mode.- The new weather system really helps the world feel more alive.- NPC brings a nice change- Looks nice graphically. Especially with the changing seasons.- Lots of weapon options.- A 3D printer is a very good addition. But I feel we need more options in this printer.- The addition of GPS is much appreciated and makes navigation much easier.- Sharing/passing inventory items to member collaboration is a great improvement for teamwork.Negatives:- Caves without dead ends immediately appear shorter and less dynamic compared to the original. (For example, previously, you'd use a climbing ax to navigate a very deep cave.)- Not all original mutants are present in this game. And the mutants in this game are nowhere as threatened as in the previous ones- Imperfect World There are many caverns that are completely empty and serve no purpose apart from providing secondary resources.Bugs:- Spoiled food can still be cooked and will turn into "cooked" food that can be eaten as normal.- GPS tracker does not use any of the custom icons. They will always be on the radio icon by default no matter what you choose.Virginia can sometimes disappear and not be found. Not sure why this is happening but it seems random.Calvin's IQ is laughably bad. For every right thing he does, he breaks five more. It's just a liability and you'd better tell him to rest until the end of the game so you can get the achievement. I feel it would serve a better purpose being able to help you in the fight as Virginia is.- Multiple items will be attached to your hand when you press it in the middle of the animation. _childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game. The Forest was fun, creative and interesting, combining both solid gameplay and provocative back story/script.  Early reviews of Sons were mixed, so I waited until v1.0 to give the team a chance to finish the game.  Unfortunately even after waiting the result is an unenjoyable mess.  The map is huge and extremely repetitious, so it's *extremely* tedious and boring getting anywhere, even with golf carts or the glider. Likewise, building an interesting shelter is incredibly tedious due to the need to collect huge numbers of rocks and logs.  Kelvin is supposed to help with this, but everything involving him is tedious (including having to redesign my structures so he gets stuck).  Crafting is tedious and pointless. Victoria could have been an interesting character, but instead copies the cliche swimsuit-clad-girl-with-a-gun trope and has no personality, backstory, etc.  More generally, the plot is an afterthought and full of dumb holes (like characters popping back to life).  The final credits are completely un-subtle about setting up a third game, but this franchise needs a reboot/rethink not another game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Right look, I want to recommend the game, honestly I do. But it's overly difficult and not for reasons you would expect. Difficult to the point of frustrating.Building is a pain in the ass. The game has wildly esoteric rules on how you can and cannot build something, and working around those rules is just jarring. I can make a triangle slope but I can't fill it in? Why? I can make an equilateral triangle and fill that in but it looks awful.If I have stairs, due to the random nature of what is and isn't load bearing, if it gets damaged or destroyed good luck repairing it. I can't place diagonal logs inside an already built square to remake the stairs without taking apart everything above it. Good luck if you have a tall building.I can't place a log over a gap and then support it afterwards, so to build an overhang, you have to build from below, then use a strut, and then remove the supports below. Makes kind of sense, yet that only works if you can measure the distance from below. If you're in a treehouse? Good luck, there's no way to build extra platforms with the template if it's too high.Oh and how often do structures get damaged? Causing your entire base to fall in on itself? All the time. Why? Well what's that? A caterpillar enemy that can phase through walls and destroys almost every structure it comes into contact with? Why not? Sure, just destroy all the work I've done for the past 3 hours because building is so irritating and farming logs is tedium.Combat also, is painful. I don't mind the game being harsh with spawning enemies, but my god I need a breather sometimes. I'm in multiplayer, and I get knocked out, so I wait for someone to pick me up. They're struggling too so they pick me up and run so I have the chance to run too. Nope, I can get knocked out again in the getting up animation. Why? I'm already low health, give me some time to make distance and at least TRY and gather my bearings. Gaining health is already very difficult, so letting the player have a few frames of invincibility at least until they actually have control of the character again is not unreasonable. Also besides the fact that most enemies can annihilate your health in 2 or 3 hits.It's just, very eh. It's very very rough. I know it's early access but, it's not really an excuse. The triangle fill in building thing is absolutely basic. Valheim did it fine very early in it's life, why can't this?I can only recommend it once they polish off the building system, and rework the combat a little. In any other case I'd simply recommend Valheim over this any day.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Early Access, and maybe I'm spoiled with amazing games like Valheim but nonetheless, I am pretty underwhelmed. Melee combat is very unresponsive and feel sluggish, hits just don't connect well and it's always very unclear when a mob is dead or just moving around by inerta or squirming. Many other things are confusing, there is no way to see what you're supposed to do other than map markers, which don't become crossed off when visited. The story is also very underdeveloped and the ending is like watching a movie without sound. Sound in general is also quite rudimentary, you hear mobs like they're inside your head although they may be 5 meters away from you. We were 3 people who played it through in 20 hours, and at least 5 hours of that was spent base building, revisiting caves because of crashes etc. We all had the feeling at the end like "Okay.... that's... it?"I don't think it was worth the 29 EUR tbh. It may be much better in the future but I also don't really see the replay value as the map and story is predetermined, you don't have character building, skills or stuff like that.

_childDocuments_.review: where do I even begin? As a huge fan of the original The Forest, I had incredibly high expectations for this long-awaited sequel, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint!First off, the visuals are absolutely stunning. Every detail, from the lush greenery to the dark and ominous caves, is incredibly immersive and really transports you into the game's world. And let me tell you, that world is even more expansive and engaging than ever before.The gameplay itself is simply mind-blowing. With a whopping 21 hours of gameplay, there is no shortage of content to explore and enjoy. Whether you're sneaking through the forest to avoid hostile enemies, or gathering resources to build your own fortresses, there is always something to do and discover.Despite some minor performance issues and a few bugs here and there, "Sons of the Forest" really does manage to deliver an absolutely incredible gaming experience. The level of depth and detail put into the game's story, world-building, and character development is truly extraordinary, and it's clear that the developers poured their hearts and souls into this game.Overall, I cannot recommend "Sons of the Forest" highly enough. If you're a fan of survival games, or just looking for an incredibly immersive and engaging gaming experience, then this is the game for you. It's an absolute masterpiece, and I can't wait to see where the developers take this franchise next.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, a big step up from The Forest, but gameplay wise it feels like a step back. Upping the difficulty from Normal might help, but survival is so trivial that it's basically a non-issue. Food and water is abundant. Shelter takes about 20 seconds to create if you need to sleep or pass time from night to morning. Most of the above-ground encounters I've had are non-hostile or at least very avoidable, turning the entire above ground part of the map into a walking simulator. I trudged through the snowy mountains with zero preparation and wasn't punished for walking in normal clothing through the snow for a whole day, nor for simply camping under a stick and a piece of foil.Basically, it's a survival game where survival is a given. That mostly leaves exploration to find caves to go underground, slowly progress the story, and fight the more aggressive enemies down there. Frankly, it just isn't enough.That said, this is in Early Access, and there's a lot of promise here. I wouldn't be surprised if 6-12 months from now I delete this review.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's beautiful, but the story (among other things) definitely leaves something to be desired.The game is absolutely beautiful. Definitely one of the best looking games I've seen in a while. You can pick a nice, scenic place to build a house and just stare at it; it's amazing. This game has an atmosphere like no other. The cave atmosphere, the nature atmosphere, it's stunning.The building is very robust. You can build just about anything, and it's so much more gratifying than the original game because  placing each and every log on that house. Plenty of options, and you could easily make this game a sandbox.Kelvin is useful. Set up a log holder and tell him to go get logs and fill it; he will, albeit slowly. He's still better than nothing though, will take out some of the tedious work of the game.You get a second chance when you die. From what I've seen, the first death in a day will lead to you being sent to some sort of capture point, whether it be in a cave bubble or strung up at a tribal camp, it's not over when you die. However, when you die the second time in a day, you will be forced to load a save or restart.The inventory system, crafting animations, and weapons are far better than the original game. There's animations for drinking, eating, crafting, reloading, shooting, all of that. Adds another level of immersion to the game, for sure. The backpack-holding-up-thing that replaced the keybinds system is better too, in my opinion.The caves aren't as rich as the first game. They're extremely atmospheric, which is awesome, but they have next to no depth. No ropes or anything like that. They're also not interconnected, to my knowledge at least, like the first game's caves. The enemies are also quite annoying, which I suppose could be intentional, The AI isn't all it's touted to be. It's definitely interesting; the cannibals won't attack you immediately and will instead watch you and observe you, and they will also mourn fallen comrades sometimes; that's all I've seen though. Kelvin, while useful, can become a liability. He often doesn't follow you and will lag behind you, and you'll have to wait for him (you can leave him too, but then you miss out on what he's actually useful for). He cannot defend himself either, so do not expect him to help you out in firefights.The whole tribe system is quite underwhelming. Yeah, they're there. Yeah, there's 7 foot tall dudes that want to beat your head in. More was expected, though. The game is fairly straightforward, and the story isn't deep. The performance isn't great. It's a pretty game with tons of foliage, and that takes a toll. But the optimization leaves something to be desired too. 32GB of ram and a 3070 OC only getting me 70fps on high WITH dlss? Come on.Currently, The cons outweigh the pros. This means i'll give the game a negative review. If anything changes or I feel I should add anything, I'll upgrade this review.

_childDocuments_.review: "Sons of the Forest" isn't just a game; it's a masterpiece that transcends the boundaries of typical gaming experiences. From its breathtaking visuals to its immersive gameplay mechanics, every aspect of this title is meticulously crafted to deliver an unforgettable journey into the heart of darkness.One of the most striking features of "Sons of the Forest" is its stunning graphics. The game's lush environments are rendered with such detail and realism that you'll often find yourself pausing just to take in the beauty of your surroundings. Whether you're exploring dense forests, eerie caves, or abandoned structures, every inch of the game world feels alive and teeming with atmosphere.But "Sons of the Forest" isn't just about looks; it's also about gameplay that keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. The survival mechanics are deep and challenging, requiring you to scavenge for resources, build shelter, and fend off the horrors that lurk in the shadows. Every decision you make feels meaningful, whether it's choosing how to approach a dangerous encounter or deciding which upgrades to prioritize for your character.Speaking of encounters, the enemies you'll face in "Sons of the Forest" are some of the most terrifying creatures ever seen in a video game. From grotesque mutants to sinister cultists, each foe is uniquely horrifying and poses a constant threat to your survival. But despite the danger, there's a sense of exhilaration that comes from facing these challenges head-on, knowing that every victory is hard-earned and well-deserved.Of course, no review of "Sons of the Forest" would be complete without mentioning its captivating story. As you unravel the mysteries of the island and uncover its dark secrets, you'll be drawn into a narrative that's equal parts haunting and thought-provoking. Every twist and turn keeps you guessing, and the emotional depth of the characters ensures that you'll be invested in their fates until the very end.In conclusion, "Sons of the Forest" isn't just a game; it's an experience that will stay with you long after you've put down the controller. With its stunning visuals, immersive gameplay, and gripping story, it sets a new standard for what gaming can achieve. Whether you're a fan of survival horror or simply appreciate a well-crafted adventure, this is one title that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is gorgeous: graphics, building and combat mechanics, interacting with enemies and realistic friendly fire are a treat. It's an enjoyable game if you're into exploring for days, building a base, getting spooked in caves and finding out there's always an enemy spookier than the first one you've met. I've spent days playing, exploring, reading notes and fighting all enemies throughout the forest and across the island and never had any clue about any storyline or whatsoever. Suddenly, I came to the point of the story ending, without knowing what it actually was about.It just doesn't add up to each other, from golfballs to cubes. I get the whole fresh storyline and different take on the game, but I wasn't invested in the story as I was when playing The Forest. Clues don't add up and just add more confusing information, which adds up to more confusing information. TLDR: Sweet game for fun foresting/exploring/hunting nights with the homies, not so great storyline. Would still recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is a sequel to the first part of the game. I can say that the second part is very realistic. After playing "The Forest", I can tell you that there are more options available. The developers have experimented with building mechanics, and almost anything can be constructed according to your preferences.There are two levels of building difficulty: the first is for prepared structures that require you to simply bring the necessary items, similar to what you did in the first part of the game. The second level is more realistic, allowing you to build as if you were constructing in real life. My boyfriend and I built a beautiful house on a spacious plot. However, as we found it monotonous, we finished the game in just two or three hours. There are also other tasks available, each with its own unique approach. The plot is a bit unclear. We discover the stones of youth, which turn the remaining humans into creatures seeking to harm us. There are two possible endings to this story. I won't say which one is better, but in one of them, we are taken away by a plane. There are also good and bad versions of this ending. There's also a secret ending, or we stay on the island and never return home. Choose the ending that suits you best.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this is an indie game made by a team of about 30 people or so, SOTF was alright to say the least. I know most people enjoy this game mainly for the building/creative aspect, but my review will be focused on things outside of that. Gameplay wise, there were some finicky mechanics here and there. It felt awkward trying to be precise when building. For example, trying to align logs together or cutting them up into pieces. Driving that motor unicycle thing was annoying, and maneuvering the golf cart took a bit of time to adapt too. Some UI elements overlapped each other which interfered with tasks I wanted to perform, some even sharing the same hotkey for some reason. Like for example: trying to pick up cloth from ziplines vs. trying to ride the zipline, or picking up your pot vs. adding more items into your campfire. Transitions into cutscenes felt abrupt and made the story feel a bit confusing too.  I feel like I would have enjoyed the story a lot more if players could play as Timmy instead. I wanna know what he was doing on the island. I wanna know HIS story. I'd feel so much more relevant to the plot if this was the case. In the first game, we literally played as Timmy's father. The game left us off in Timmy's perspective and his pursuit to find out who he was and where his mutations came from. Kind of sad to see a character with so much potential go to waste like that. However, I do like the two new characters, Kelvin and Virginia. I think it's great having two companions to help me on my journey. Again, I just wish there was a better way to integrate the MC and even Kelvin into the story. Kelvin's AI could use a little work tho.Also, spoiler alert:At the end of the day, I think what the game mostly needs right now is some polish. And it's only been a year since this game came out. I know the creator spent a lot of time to flesh out the first game, especially during the first couple years after launch. Because of that, it became one of the most reputable survival-horror indie games out there. I can only assume that this is what SOTF needs as well-- is just more time for refinement. Unfortunately right now, I would have to say it's not worth the $30 price tag. And because of all the downsides I mentioned earlier, I wouldn't recommend this to a friend. Solid 6/10

Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I cannot recommend this game on the 1.0 launch. Here is exactly why in a bulleted list why (Spoilers)TLDR: - Travel is slow even with vehicles (doesn't feel like the game respects your time)- You are punished for killing enemies instead of rewarded- The open world can feel very empty especially before you get the re-breather/shovel(which good luck finding those without the wiki)- You can only save at a campExpanded for those those on the fence about the game and for the devs if they'd like to read (love the devs btw, every game just isn't going to be for everyone)1. The map is huge and travel is slow (I am aware of the golf carts and glider)To expand on this, no one wants to have to run 30 minutes north, get excited that they are about to find something new and then realize that they need a shovel... this was one of the worst feelings and totally killed the exploration spirit. "Should I run to the next GPS marker... nah its probably something I can't even interact with yet... guess Ill go kill some more stuff.. oh wait that will make the enemies stronger..."2. You are punished for killing enemies... the new scaling enemies makes it so now when you kill an enemy you feel like you screwed up instead of feeling like you accomplished something.3. If you miss a key item in a cave you have no way of knowing it so that you can go back and find it. For example, with the re-breather in the cave up north, I felt I had explored the cave and continued onward to the next cave. This limited what items I could get as I ran/drove/flew around the map trying to find the re-breather (which you need for multiple other caves). This was extremely frustrating until I finally looked it up online (feels bad man) and realized it was in a cave I felt I already explored. To be fair, the path is probably obvious to the majority of people but it was not for me.4. Still not a fan of the saving system, wish it was skyrim style (especially with the long distances)For these 4 main reasons I cannot recommend the game in its current state. I did "beat" the game when it was originally released on early access with friends while this attempt I am describing was solo.

_childDocuments_.review: I could talk for hours about this game, but I'll try and keep it short. I want to start by saying I have had so much fun playing it, exploring its ins and outs and getting invested with every new update it releases, however, I am very disappointed with a lot of the decisions EndNight have made regarding the story, progression, combat, building and so much more.I started playing this game from the day it first released in early access, and the very first thing I noticed was that half of the tools, content, animals, diversity and survival mechanics from the first game, The Forest, were simple non-existent, and to my surprise, are still missing in the full release state it is currently in. The way they decided to slowly add in some of essential elements in each update was so disappointing, it didn't feel like anything new was actually being added, and at the same time not getting the satisfaction of using the classic tools from the first game as they still have missed so much content from it. To give some examples, The Forest had so much variety and diversity in the materials the player could gather to craft certain things. It created incentive to explore as to craft a certain item, you had to travel to a certain spot on the map to where that plant grew/animal spawned. Sons of The Forest has not even a speck of this. apart from the map being ridiculously big, there is absolutely no point to explore it as there is simple nothing to find. All of the places that proggress the story are marked on the map, meaning you can just B-line it to those spots and not bother about the rest of the map. There is no unique place where a certain plant only grows, there is no spot where a rare animal only spawns that skin can be used for a unique special tool. what only can be found is a couple of digging sites and caves, which only usually contain a blueprint to a structure or a story item. Yes one could argue there is an incentive to explore to get all the artefacts and blueprints, but to me it feels more like a chore rather then appreciating the journey because I know there is no change in the scenery. Biomes would have been an amazing addition, with different types of trees and plants that only grow in that spot or something like that. I'm gonna stop yapping how I think you get my point. The building: an absolute chore. It is so tedious, inaccurate, time consuming and repetitive that I see no point in it, and plus, there is no incentive, once again. The game can be 100% completed without building a base. there is no requirement for it, and because its so frustrating I just don't bother. again, I could go into so much more detail about this.Story: just... no. it's so bad. there is no emotion, no character personality, its random, disjointed, and one of the poorest written I've seen. The Forest had an AMAZING story because there was depth to it, layers, a timeline, events happening that lead to other things changing, and EMOTION. the first game had no dialogue, but it worked so well because the animation was done so well in partnership with music. yeah I'm not a fan of this one's story haha.Combat: ehhhh it's mid. once you learn each enemies weaknesses and how to balance your stamina it's pretty easy, however how the armour works is horrible. if you misjudge the slightest thing you can loose pretty much every single piece of armour and have absolutely no control over it. Again, I could go into much more detail.over all this game can be fun, and its visually stunning, the graphics are incredible and as a whole it is very immersive, however it lacks incentive to literally do anything. The story is garbage, the sound design is also pretty bad, the helicopter crash intros are a joke, it is literally the worst cut-scenes with lagy animations, they go for far too long, no suspense, and terrible sound effects. The combat is rough and feels janky 75% of the time, building can be initially fun but then just gets annoying and repetitive, and as a whole the game feels so unfinished. I would not recommend this game if you are looking for a updated, expanded version of The Forest, what you would picture a sequel to be, but this game is not that. Also the survival aspects of this game are nearly not even a factor, all the food and water you will ever need can be found everywhere, and that is literally the only aspect to the survival mechanics (I'm exaggerating, but that is how it feels) I recommend playing the first game, The Forest, for a real horror survival experience with exploration and a genuinely good story. anyway I'll shut up now

_childDocuments_.review: Another situation where I wish Steam had a middling review option. I do like this game and I do recommend it to fans of The Forest. Just not at its current price point compared to the available content. For years, The Forest has been the game I use as an example of Early Access done right. The latest patch release of Sons Of The Forest inspired me to throw my opinion out there. I was a huge fan of The Forest and have walked many friends through the story and caves. Sons Of The Forest has a lot of improvements over the first while also taking a few steps back in some areas. It feels pointless to list all these issues because just like the first game, its Early Access. They are all subject to change and will most likely be fixed up quite a bit a year from now. As it stands, there is currently no reason at all to build a base aside from testing the games functions and your own creativity. However, my biggest problem is this extremely strange approach to Early Access they've taken this time around as opposed to the first game. The first game released onto Early Access with one cut scene, a handful of items and craftables and grew from there to encompass a feature complete game with a solid story for those who were interested in finding it. The story elements here in the sequel are as deep and interesting as the first game. The issue stems from the fact the story and its elements are fully completable from the outset, bugs and all. In my experience this has put quite a damper on my excitement going forward because I already know exactly what is going to happen for the most part. I'm sure they will add in little twists and turns here and there as the details to the story are further developed but it can't change the two available endings. Both of which are currently nowhere near as peak as the first games available endings in my opinion. The cut scenes as they exist now, aside from the opening cutscene, are extremely jarring. Sound and dialogue seem to be missing and the animations are very stilted and awkward. This is just a symptom of a bigger problem. The problem being that this game should have just released when it was ready. I don't believe there was any reason for this game to launch in EA aside from laziness and it sort of shows in the game and patch releases. If you play and complete the game, it becomes glaringly obvious that the developers are well aware of the game they are making and where it is headed, but for some reason they insist on dragging out its development time. The latest patch which came out just prior to writing this adds a few new items, a couple cave extensions and some new craftables. Having completed the game already, knowing that I do not need these new items or mechanics to complete any gameplay or story elements is a huge disappointment and is not bringing me back to play more. At this point only the full release will bring me back for another playthough and thats sad. The Forest was EA done right. Almost every patch had me coming back to find new items and experiment crafting as the story progressed, patch after patch. A perfect example of how this was done properly in the first game was the patch that added the climbing axe. Before the patch, the player could find walls in caves that were clearly there to be scaled with some sort of tool. These caves had items the player either wanted or needed to complete the story in both the sense of item progression or plot progression. Sons Of The Forest has none of this. The only item you NEED to complete the game is a cosmetic item that currently holds little to no plot value. For fans of The Forest, I recommend you hold off until the game is more feature complete so you don't burn out your curiosity like I did. For the curious and uninitiated I give the same advice. Pickup the original The Forest in the meantime. Sons Of The Forest needs more time baking in the oven before its ready.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game quite a bit in the first couple months of its life cycle, then took a break and let the developers add more stuff & fix a lot of game-breaking bugs. I didn't really feel compelled to write a review during my first two months with this game since, despite being new and fresh with a massive upgrade to the graphics and an expanded arsenal of weapons, this game felt lacking in a lot of areas compared to The Forest. There were so many basic QoL elements of its predecessor missing in this game at the start, not to mention the fact that it ran very poorly and there was an abundance of bugs.6 months later, I booted up the game again to find that the devs had indeed listened to the feedback from the community, added a bunch of our QoL suggestions, and even went back and added alternative options for previous updates that were not received well by the community (i.e. the patch that forced containers to be finite). Lots of new builds and items to mess around with and even new caves & overworld settlements to explore. I also heard they revamped and expanded on the main questline. The game really almost feels brand new again -- the beauty of Early Access when you have competent developers. I'm not going to say the game is perfect by any means, as some of the same issues are present in the game (i.e. dropping frames every time a group of enemies spawn near your base to try to raid it). But solid progress has been made by the developers and I appreciate their commitment to this game.I am very much looking forward to the finished product of Sons of the Forest. It absolutely has the potential to go far above and beyond The Forest's end result.

_childDocuments_.review: This game will have mixed opinions for sure. I see some reviews complaining about less content or lack of tutorials. Some even say Early Access is not an excuse. When you buy an early access game, you are the tester, period. Having limited content helps us focus on whats broken so the Devs can concentrate on fixing before they add more. Creating a tutorial on something that isn't done would be pointless. B is your tutorial for now, or if you are unable to figure it out, "let me google that for you". This game is about experimenting with different combinations of materials and learning the mechanics as they unfold.The world is very nicely done and feels like a proper successor. The cannibal behavior is buggy but you can see where it is heading in a superior way. I chuckled when a cannibal walked up to my log and started dragging it away deeper into the woods. They do become hostile and can be over whelming if you aren't prepared. The Devs did provide an option when creating a new game to turn off enemies as well as damage from thirst and hunger so that you can learn the mechanics as they are.Yes, there are plenty of bugs, maybe a couple game breaking depending on your last save. SAVE OFTEN! I had a save file that didn't load, but I restarted the game and it loaded fine. Sound is glitchy as well. That sudden scream in the woods right in your ear that makes you jump every damn time....This is based on single player game play. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Endnight has already added 10 bindable hotkeys via hotfix prior to their first update.  Huge plus!  I am changing my review from 6/10 to 8/10.  Having beaten the game almost twice now, I think I was overly harsh in my initial impressions.  The game has bugs but it is very playable.  While there is no log sled in the game, ziplines allow you to send logs both downhill and uphill, which is a huge plus.  Simply set up a zipline where you want your logs to go and you're good to go.  The story is a total mess, makes no sense, and is entirely incomplete, but the gameplay and world are solid experiences that make it worth playing even in its unfinished state.ORIGINAL REVIEW: I'm going to give this an honest review.  Huge fan of the Forest - couple hundred hours in it at least.Aesthetically speaking, top notch.  Great upgrade graphically and sound wise.A lot of mechanics feel unfinished.  To ship a first person survival game without the ability to use hotkeys (1, 2, 3, 4, etc) for your weapons is borderline unforgivable.  I shouldn't have to use a cumbersome "hold+select" menu to switch between just two weapons.  The Forest had hotkeys, four of them in fact - it wasn't perfect, but it worked.  This is a no-brainer that they totally dropped the ball on.  Core combat mechanic that isn't there.The move away from prefab blueprint building appears to give the player more control over custom builds, but it also makes the building process substantially slower and more labor intensive.  Perhaps my friends and I haven't figured it out yet but mobs will push doors to your base right open and walk in.  Not sure if there's something we're missing but a defensive wall with a door in it is pointless.  The previous title didn't allow mobs to traverse through doors, why would they now?  We had to devise a platforming puzzle to enter/exit our base which rendered the new NPC close to useless.  It took me a while to figure out the building system in the first title so maybe I'm just slow but having to resort to scouring youtube to figure out how to keep mobs out of our base seems like it should be unnecessary.The new crafting mat design is god awful - having to move your cursor around to push the edge of your screen to reveal more things to select - who's UI idea was that?  Please take them out back to the woodshed.  Crafting now takes twice as long as it did in the first game due to the fact that not everything is right at your fingertips and also that there's now an animation that plays every time you craft something, locking you into longer crafting mat times while enemies roll up on you.The rest/food/water (particularly rest) mechanics need tweaking.  Hopefully that change will come quickly or I foresee a lot of mods stripping the mechanic out entirely.Caves feel spooky and there seem to be way more types of mutants, so that's good.  None of us care for the change to the lighter - it is now a UV-type glow instead of a yellow light from a traditional lighter.It seems like there's a lot of potential but it honestly needs a lot of work.  Many gameplay differences from the first title feel like a step backward instead of what they should be - a step forward.  I honestly expected more from Sons of the Forest after 2+ years worth of delays.  The title was very clearly stuck in development hell and there must have been at least one design pivot by the development team.6/10 for right now.  Not great, not terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: I was blown away by the incredible atmosphere and graphics. The game's haunting environments and realistic sound design create an incredibly immersive experience, and I found myself feeling genuinely scared and on edge throughout my playthrough.The attention to detail is impressive, and the new crafting and building mechanics add an exciting new dimension to the gameplay. The controls are intuitive, and I found myself easily able to explore the world and experiment with different building strategies.However, there are a few areas where I feel that the game could be improved. Firstly, while the building and crafting mechanics are fun to use, I found myself wanting more structures and traps that are specifically designed to work against the cannibals. This would add a new level of strategy to the game and make it even more engaging.Secondly, while I understand that the game is still in early access, I did encounter several glitches and bugs during my playthrough, which sometimes detracted from the overall experience. I hope that these issues will be addressed as the game continues to be developed and refined.Despite these minor issues, I believe that Sons of the Forest is an excellent game with a lot of potential. The game's atmosphere and graphics are top-notch, and the new mechanics add an exciting dimension to the survival-horror genre. With a few tweaks and improvements, this game could become a true classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy it? Yes, absolutely.There are still a LOT of things missing which we know from The Forest, which should be added within the coming updates. Next Update is only like 10 days away or so at the time of this review. The Graphics are absolutely beautiful.Story is too short yet, but more Cutscenes and Story progression was announced to be added later anyway, so don't expect the best story experience yet if you finish the game early.I really hope they add more traps, since right now there is no real use for them. They don't kill the cannibals/mutants and the choice of 2 (plus the option to put sharp sticks in the ground) is not enough. The new building system however is just awesome. I really enjoy this.There is no more 1-4 Hotkeys, you attach stuff to your backpack and hold i-key for a quick inventory. You got to get used to it, but it actually is kinda cool and adds realism.Realism is great, though still alot is missing. I guess they will add Hard Survival again, which is NOT in the game YET. No calories system, hunger and thirst damage is off on Hard Mode (you can activate it on individual difficulty). You can drink any water from any source (except from the ocean ofc), hope they will change that once Hard Survival makes its return. Still a lot of bugs, but I've encountered nothing game breaking.I still lose myself in this world for hours and hours and hours. This game is no disappointment. Any negative reviews you will find are either people who didn't play The Forest, who can't deal with the realism/difficulty or who simply expected more finalization from an Early Access Game. The latter is just dumb, but patience is a virtue.I don't regret buying this and will most likely still play this game in the next coming months, especially once the Updates hit. Love it!Hope you found this helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Would like to say fist and foremost, THIS IS NOT THE FOREST. Meaning that, if you enjoyed the build-a-base and hold out game play in that one, this plays different. You should come in with different expectations. From what I can tell this is run-and-go style game. More details later.You start off as a merc trying to find a billionaire's family. You get a little dossier before crashing onto the island where the game begins. Playing one in single player and once in multiplayer, I've been dropped at two different locations. One on a beach, and the other in the mountain with different cut scenes both times.Pros:New AI NPC. His name is Kelvin, his eardrums ruptured from the crash. You communicate with him through pen and pad. IDK how his AI is, because both play through's I immediately killed him. You have that option.You inventory is expanded immensely! Also crafting is more intuitive now (albeit the taro tent)GPS Tracker. From the beginning you're given a GPS track to track your fallen comrades/clients. This will point you towards the story more or less.AI overall improved. The animals aren't full-blown stupid and running into you (so far in my play through). The cannibals feel so much more human! They aren't as aggressive with you at first, but they seem more curious. Once you start overstaying your welcome they start harassing you, trying to sort of shoo you away from areas of interest/camps. They don't chase you down to the edge's of the earth either, they'll lose interest quickly unless you provoke them. When in combat, they normal enemies are slower, but they come in more numbers. Don't expect the 1-2 random ferals, you'll frequently get groups of 4-6.Crafting is slightly easier. They UI will tell you when you have a new crafting recipe both on screen and when you open it up. I think this is an overall plus. I enjoy knowing when I can create something new, and not always check  in the inventory to see what different recipes are available.CONS: Multiplayer has some issues. Performance was great in single player, but when I hosted a session I had major issues. My friend also experienced bugs where he would be locked in an animation and had to quit out to do anything different. Multiplayer needs help.While things seem more user friendly, there is still things I couldn't figure out and find in the options menu. I'm not sure if it's me of a bug. When you pick up other GPS Locators, I could cycle through to show what type of tracker I wanted, but couldn't figure out how to set them down.Animations were still a little hit-or-miss especially for the pitching tent animation.DIFFERENCES:As I mention previously, this is a different game than The Forest. Please come with that expectation. It is my belief that, because of the tarp and the new behavior with the AI, you are not meant to bunker down. You need to be on the move. The cannibals won't attack you if you leave when they arrive and they will come to check you out frequently. Please have this in mind.As of now I haven't been able to make a raft. I don't think sailing is what the developers had in mind. Water is suppose to be a challenge/barrier not a get-out-of-jail-free card.Berries are nerfed quite a bit. There seems to be more plants that you benefit from in this game, the additional nutrients they bring are not significant. ♥♥♥♥ farming you need to hunt.Caves, so far have not been harmful in this game. I found three. 2 were great in providing added benefits (find the 3D printer!) one I didn't have enough to explore it. This is a double-edged sword. On one side it's a relief from the dangers outside. On the other hand you don't quite have the same "Descent" feeling as you did in the original game. Don't go in them expecting a challenge.Overall I'm happy with what they put out for $30 and hope they continue to work on this one and polish it up more. Please do not abandon this like you did with The Forest!

_childDocuments_.review: This is more-so a mixed review as there are things I've liked and disliked and things I haven't fully experienced yet. Most of my time has been on default Hard options in a multiplayer server. I will be continuing to play the game and my review is likely to change as updates roll out.Survival Mechanics-There virtually isn't any, somehow they've shipped a survival game with less nature survival features than its predecessor (outside of the addition of what appears to be a lite clothing system for the snow biome I have yet to experience). To me this feels like the most unacceptable part, it's a survival game and after the first couple days you can have a structure and infinite water/food depending on where you intend on basing.Water is just a free resource generally across the map via the water streams, there is no opportunity for collecting & boiling water from the ocean as far as I can tell (I could be wrong). You can make a water collector but it feels like an empty necessity if you're constantly around running streams. Food is the standard kill something cook it and its incredibly simplistic. Even eating raw meat and/or human meat feels as though there is no consequences. Additionally, once you explore a couple caves or a POI the amount of food (and water) resources you're carrying on-hand can survive you for MANY days completely negating the need to trap fish/small animals. As I mentioned before, there doesn't appear to be any negative effect for eating human meat either so on Hard since you're going to get a raid every day or so you can just chop off limbs, put them on a drying rack and infinite food source the cannibals. Your stamina degradation is incredibly easily managed by continuously drinking water or eating via the sources mentioned above. Having an empty sleep bar also doesn't visibly or noticeably impact my character (I could be completely missing something when it comes to this as I don't let it stay empty for long or often). The what I believe to be strength leveling up mechanic also generally just feels shallow.Exploration / Story-You can find GPS trackers to mark POIs but the game already gives you a bunch of POIs for free so you almost instantly feel like you're already being told to go to specific places rather than explore for yourself. Perhaps this is the intention and there are many more hidden places, but it just makes what I felt like was a key part of the initial playthrough of The Forest unexciting.The environment is quite well done and in many of the areas you feel almost nomad like traveling through a dense forest and want to stop and enjoy the scenery, until you hear that screech behind you and remember you're always being watched.I haven't fully explored the map or every POI and my experience with the story is limited so I won't go any further into details.Construction / Animations-This is easily the most impressive part of the game, I was locked in for quite a few hours just experiencing the animations for various things. Manipulating logs, sticks and the various other construction items feels quite immersive. Free building is incredibly good and while building on slopes can get a little wonky it's not a deal breaker. My friends and I kept joking it really did feel like a "pioneer / lumberjack simulator", especially early on.Some of the animations appear to have performance issues and while not entirely immersion breaking are slightly annoying. I will explain this more below.General Issues / Bugs-The AI pathing can get pretty atrocious. The mud covered cannibals that crawl around on all fours have multiple times now been locked in a path where they run in circles around a small tree that would only yield sticks. Virginia also has numerous times run into my home (while running away from my presence) and then gotten stuck running into a corner to then flail around the house looking for the exit.Kelvin himself is quite useful provided his task area is clear of a structure, he has numerous times now walked into the side of my house or another structure and just infinitely walks there into you remove the blocking item(s) (which in some cases can get quite inconvenient). Additionally getting him to drop logs can put him into a "spin cycle" where it reaches too many logs in one spot as he groups them and they'll roll away. He'll then continue to grab the same logs over and over again and drop them 2 feet away.Water physics with logs is laughable (actually, it caused comedic effect the first couple times my group saw it). I assume this is why we're unable to build boat houses like The Forest. They just bounce incredibly high and appear to be on ice skates when pushed.Optimization is an interesting topic, the games minimum is a 1060 or recommended 1080. I'm on a 2080 with high/med settings and can rarely pull through 60fps (out in nature). A buddy of mine is on a 1060 and was generally playing on sub 25fps for alot of the time (even on all settings as low as they can go). Logs in water also seem to cause FPS to nose dive though this could've just been coincidental.This is yet another game where Hard = bullet sponge but mob 2 shots you (if unarmored). I personally dislike bullet sponging especially since a brute - not sure if they have a specific name, incredibly large guys with skull mace - takes ~14 arrows to the head but can get lucky once and stunlock and kill you.Weather doesn't appear to be entirely synchronized when playing multiplayer. There was a few times where one of my buddies (we were at one point 4 players) would mention they were in what felt like a hurricane, while some of us had light rain with clouds or in some cases just a sun shower. This appears to be an issue across the board with all weather forms.The intro is awkwardly quiet, no screaming and light on voicelines. It just feels like a pantomime of a helicopter crash. I can't complain about this too hard since the previous game was also like this, was just hoping they'd perhaps try and flex some lite voice acting muscles for the sake of immersion and overall impressiveness.TLDR-Overall SUPER impressed with the construction and animation systems available for use, the immersion these can provide is quite enjoyable. Incredibly underwhelmed by the natural survival mechanics, somehow it has less impact on the gameplay than the previous game. More general issues and performance problems than expected for a project that has been in development for many years with a base game to take ideas from.I haven't fully experienced the game so some of my criticisms may extend from not knowing about a feature or lack of experience in a particular area of the game.I understand the game is Early Access and can be fixed or adjust so hopefully I can keep the review updated to reflect my opinion accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty fun but very short lived for $30. Played multiplayer and we had nearly no problem running through all the caves in the game. I had several bugs where I would pull out my backpack and the game would then replayed the sound effect every 0.1 seconds and then it would drop frames until it was just frozen in the matter of 2 seconds. Had to quit and close game completely to fix as just leaving and rejoining my friend didn't fix it. Also had another bug where after encountering a cut scene the game wouldn't let me pick anything up or open my backpack and to get back to the location I would have to travel a large distance again and I was just not in the mood for running simulator.Section TLDR: Game breaking bugs found in Multiplayer that require full game restarts not just disconnect and reconnect to fix.So besides bugs we also have caves marked on the map but not all of them are caves to explore. Several are just resource caves that have a few wooden boxes in their one room. Super annoying when you hit the point where you already are max on every piece of equipment. You can get guns and attachments like flashlight and laser sight but be warned they suck. They cover the iron sight so you can no longer aim down sight and for the crossbow you're guy doesn't aim it straight ahead he has it pointed down to the left so the laser just doesn't work on it since you have to aim down the sight of the gun to get the laser pointed in the right direction but by doing so your entire view is blocked by crossbow and the laser sight device placed on the iron sight.Section TLDR: Caves are either explore-able caves or resource rooms and Gun attachments block iron sights and just suck in general.Guide book also sucks. The first game's building was by using a book and flipping through different tabs and having several options on each tab. It was quick to flip through. This one gives you a book where you have to switch which hand is holding it to change what you want to build and its a press and hold to switch hands. Then to flip through the book you get tabs that aren't really labeled well for what they are and you get two images of things you can build before clicking to go to the next page so you have to spend more time flipping through pages looking for what you want, not to mention possibly having to switch which hand the book is in as the piece you are trying to build may be in the other section. Also some recipes you need the item in your hand instead of in the book. Campfires need sticks in your hands to craft instead of in the crafting book like everything else is in it.Section TLDR: Crafting is split up with no hint as to what you need in your hands to craft and takes a long time to find the one thing you are trying to craft.NO ACTUAL STORY. Game had this random guy in green jacket just show up and no explanation of who he is.Full TLDR: Game is just not in a good spot. Bugs that are game breaking, features that weren't thought out for ease of use or simple functionality, and cave systems that were enjoyable experiences are now a coin flip if they are an actual cave or just a pointless resource room.
