_childDocuments_.review: Sons of The Forest, unfortunately, falls short in many areas. Firstly, the game lacks content, making it feel like an incomplete experience. Additionally, it reuses the same biome as the previous game, giving a sense of deja vu.The survival mechanic in the game is also underwhelming, lacking the challenge that many players expect from this type of game. The building mechanic, on the other hand, is overly realistic, which makes it feel like a chore rather than an enjoyable activity.The story in Sons of The Forest feels rushed and poorly executed. It fails to keep players engaged or invested in the game's world, and the ending is particularly disappointing.Finally, building a base in the game feels like a wasted opportunity. It doesn't offer much variety or excitement, and it's not enough to redeem the game's other flaws.Overall, Sons of The Forest feels like a game that was rushed to market without enough attention to detail. While it has some redeeming qualities, the lack of content, poor survival mechanics, and underwhelming story make it a difficult game to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very fun, namely the first 20 hours or so. At the moment, the late game is black and white -- either fun and engaging, or terribly boring.To start, the core gameplay is awesome. The combat feels good, and engaging groups feels threatening, challenging you to manage your resources properly. There are some major balancing issues, though. You can be stunlocked by one hit, only for your get-up animation to finish and to be hit again ad infinitum. There's a respawn mechanic where you awaken captive in a cannibal (or cave creature) camp. Picking up your bag will oftentimes lead to a similar stunlock issue once your animation invulnerability is up. Some hits feel like they should stagger only for you to get hit due to their incredible and unapparent poise. The cave creature camps are terribly unfair (pleb git gud) and the loot is lacking. As for the cave creatures, I think it is balanced for multiplayer play, because they are bullet-spongey and great in number. There are ways of dealing with each that take different approaches, but again, it feels more balanced for play that isn't solo. One too many losses in the cave led me to erecting a tent after each room and save-scumming as to not lose 45 minutes of progress due to one stunlock or mistake.The building is phenomenal. It is by far the greatest part of the game, alongside the crafting. Getting a base with walls, decorations, traps to deter would-be player-ingesters, and establishing self-sufficiency is very satisfying. Not to mention the help of our miraculous helper friend Kelvin, whose work ethic would make him successful in any workplace. There's not much more to say other than that it just feels really good.Exploration feels good for the first hour or two of it. The points of interest are usually quite exciting, offering loot and tool upgrades that make them worth visiting. But there is a glaring issue with the map size. It is simply too. freaking. big. Running across the map is cool in your first expedition, maybe. You are cautious of the enemies around you, excited by the cannibal encampments and ambushes and remnants of a more civilized populace. You feel farther from home than ever, making you apprehensive of every encounter. However, once you learn that the campsites hold excesses of ropes and cloth, you the act of running becomes incredibly boring as you pass practically every sign of life in preference for a B-line to a blip on your map. Needless to say, when a game has me looking at my real life phone while holding Shift+W, there is an issue. Any form of transportation would be a welcome addition.EDIT: This review is getting updated because they've added exactly that! Currently there are two modes of transportation, the hangglider and the Knight V. The knight V is a monowheel type vehicle and let me say it fixes ALL of these issues I've had. In it's current state, I would  call the Knight V unfair, because it's just too silly to fly up and off mountains at Mach 1 and survive the 900 foot fall. But honestly, I don't care. It makes the process of getting across the map even enjoyable as the mechanics of it are well implemented, and it's just too much fun to ride with friends.This review was a Yes before this update, but man have most of these complaints faded.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most disappointing £25 I've ever had leave my bank account, even as an early access game this was beyond pathetic, the game feels extremely bare-bones, almost as if this was an alpha test release for the game, not an early access. - The only improvement from The Forest 1 is the building, in my opinion, which there's no reason to even take part in because there's absolutely no reason to build other than "to just do it".- There's no way to quick swap between weapons without opening your inventory to select a different one so you're locked holding on to one item, unless you want to die while looking at your inventory, which is always fun. - Game feels more like a running simulator than a survival game. Out of my 11 hours of play time I'd say a solid 8 hours MINIMUM is spent running from one cave to another, trying to figure out which one we had already been in and which one we hadn't.- Even when playing on Hard difficulty, there was no difficulty. Swing at an enemy and it staggers until it dies, it just takes a long time.- Supplies are THROWN at you whenever you go in a cave, you'll "struggle to make ends meet" until you find your first cave and then all of a sudden, you have more supplies than you can make use of and they can last you until the end of the game quite comfortably.I could point out more but I don't want this to go on for longer than it has to.DO NOT get baited by the flood of "positive" reviews, of which probably at least 95% of them are all meme posts, nothing related to the game what-so-ever.As the game is right now, solid 4/10, maybe a 5 if it was cheaper. Is it the worst game? No, but it's definitely not the best either. In all honesty I'd say wait for a good... year? of updates, might be worth looking in to by that point.Also, don't make the argument of "But it's an early access game, what did you expect?". I've seen plenty of early access games with far more content than this game offered and for a fraction of the price.

_childDocuments_.review: And by this I mean, that it is a decent game and it has a lot of the elements what made The Forest so great, but somehow it falls short what it was aiming to deliver in the first place. And this is especially true for the story.In the first game (The Forest) everything is a mystery right until the very end when you discover the labs, within the artifacts and what they do and suddenly all pieces fall in to place and make sense. The crash landing, your son being taken, how the mutants came to be... (except the cannibals, those are never addressed). Of course what the artifacts are, where they come from, etc... are still unknown, but you have the sense of accomplishment in the end. You feel like that part of the story is irrelevant in the conclusion.Here the game tries to focus more on the artifacts and the mystery around them, but things are detached, vague and meaningless at best. You piece some parts of the story together about the Pufftons and the guy who smacked you in the face in the beginning. (Don't know why he just didn't killed you by the way...). But all these tiny nuggets of lore are meaningless. Too small and too vague to make sense.The funny thing is, that on the Island you visit places with information source galore. Books, laptops, papers, etc... but the few little things you can actually pick up are just some pieces of paper of an email printout with 1-2 sentence saying absolutely nothing.It feels like the game tries to be mysterious whilst you are constantly denied access to sources of information along the way.The hows and whys are detached as well. On one hand you know how the mutants came to be on the Island, but then you ask the question why are there unmutated cannibals? What is the relationship between these mutants and the ones from the Forest?Nothing gets answered.And the ultimate culmination of the story. Absolute garbage, uninteresting, unresolved mess, with meaningless cut-scenes.Another disheartening experience in terms of the story events are that the triggers happening over and over again. Like when you get near a military camp where a chopper takes off when you get close. Now that animation happens every time. It just doesn't make any sense and completely breaks the immersion.One of them is useful for maintaining base gathering stuff.The other is dumb, can't shoot proper and you cannot tell her anything to do.Anyone else you encounter means absolutely nothing.The guy in the beginning (the main villain so to speak)? You see him 1-2 times, but no interaction, no meaning, no cut-scenes where he tells  you some info. Just an empty shell that has absolutely no context.Timmy? The same. Appears out of nowhere, does absolutely nothing, tells you nothing and overall a useless character in the plot. Him being there does nothing to the plot.Crafting is the same concept as in the first game, but besides giving you more resources and such, you can't really make more things. For example you can't make rope, whilst that is an essential for bone armor, so you scour the points of interest for respawned resources.Or sticks... You can't go and chop up a log to make sticks? Or that there are items you can have hundreds of it, like the cloth piece, but you can only have 6 rope or so?I am pretty sure 500 pieces of cloth is going to take up more space then 5 rope.And then there are the things you can't even throw away, like animal heads you picked up, or the human arms, legs and head you picked up. You can only throw the human parts away, when they have become rotten, but animal heads don't rot?It's insane how certain things just don't make any sense whatsoever in the menu system.So this whole situation makes the gameplay kind of awkward. The story revolves around an event that happens at a given point in time. A point which can be as far as you want it to be, because there is no countdown, no sense of urgency, nothing. This makes the story and the survival and building aspect of the game mutually exclusive and one has to suffer and give way to the other. In this case it's the story.You could spend years on the island not even lifting a finger for the sake of story progression, which just doesn't make any sense whatsoever.Bumping in to Timmy at a big door, trying to open it, then going away to for X  (where X >= 1 day) amount of time and he is still there doing the same thing, just standing and contemplating about what the key to the door is. Or perhaps meditating about his poor life choices.So from a story standpoint a simple explore, uncover and solve kind of game type would've been certainly a better choice. The old Farcry game comes to mind. Punch it with a time limit and you have something great. Sure it's not replay friendly, but this isn't either.From a survival aspect, it has a lot of boxes ticked, except for a few, which sound silly. Like the rope thing. Not being able to craft such a necessary item just makes the game dumb by cheesing the respawning of resources.It was fun playing with a friend, but ultimately a letdown compared to the first one. I am a big story guy and if the story sucks, or the delivery of it sucks, I just cannot give it a thumbs up.And this story, or at least how it was told sucked big time. It completely made me lose interest in whatever comes next. I like some mystery, but when you go through a game and you just don't know what the hell happened in it and you come away from it more dumb... Then it's a bad game.It's just a rushed, hot mess. Or at least it feels like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest throws you headfirst into a thrilling survival experience that surpasses its predecessor in almost every way. The game is a massive leap forward in terms of visuals, gameplay mechanics, and sheer scale, offering a truly immersive and challenging experience. This game throws you into a world that feels truly alive. The dense, lush forest is a breathtaking sight, teeming with life and danger. You'll find yourself navigating its winding paths, carefully avoiding the treacherous caves that hide within its depths. These caves, however, are not just obstacles, they're portals to hidden secrets, ancient relics, and terrifying encounters with the creatures that call them home.The world is filled with a constant sense of unease, as you never know what lurks around the corner. The constant threat of cannibalistic mutants adds a layer of tension to every interaction, every step you take. You'll need to be constantly vigilant, crafting weapons and tools to defend yourself and explore the world.Speaking of crafting, the game now takes the system to a whole new level. You're not just building basic shelters anymore. This game allows you to create elaborate fortresses, complete with defensive structures, traps, and even working electrical systems. You can build bridges, rope bridges, and even ziplines to traverse the terrain. You can even customize your base with furniture, lighting, and other decorative elements.The crafting system is incredibly detailed, allowing you to combine different materials to create a vast array of items. You can gather resources like wood, stone, and metal from the environment, then use them to craft everything from simple tools to advanced weapons. You can even craft special items like torches, bows, and arrows, which are crucial for survival in this unforgiving world.The game offers a wide range of functions that add depth and complexity to the gameplay. You can:Build elaborate bases: Construct defensive structures, traps, and even working electrical systems.Craft a variety of weapons and tools: From basic axes and spears to advanced bows and firearms.Explore the world and discover hidden secrets: Uncover ancient artifacts, gather resources, and encounter unique creatures.Manage your hunger, thirst, and health: You'll need to eat and drink regularly to survive, and be prepared to treat injuries and illnesses.Interact with the environment: Cut down trees, mine for resources, and build structures.Customize your character: Choose your clothing, weapons, and tools.Play in single-player or co-op: Experience the game alone or with friends.The world of Sons of the Forest is a place of constant discovery and challenge. You'll need to be resourceful, adaptable, and brave to survive in this unforgiving environment. But with the right tools and the right mindset, you can overcome any obstacle and build a thriving base in this wild and wonderful world.But while the gameplay is top-notch, the plot feels like a chaotic mess. The story, while intriguing at first, quickly descends into incoherence and frustration.  Many players have criticized the pacing of the plot in Sons of the Forest. They feel that the story unfolds too quickly, making it difficult to understand what's happening and leaving them feeling less engaged than they did with the previous game. Some reviews even mention that the story feels like a joke because of the rushed pacing.Here's the breakdown:Pros:Stunning visuals and immersive atmosphereDeep and rewarding crafting systemEngaging and challenging gameplayVast and detailed world to exploreImproved combat mechanicsCons:Confusing and frustrating plotUnclear objectives and lack of directionOverall, Sons of the Forest is a fantastic survival game that excels in almost every area except its plot. If you can overlook the narrative shortcomings, you'll find a deep and rewarding experience that will keep you hooked for hours. However, if you're looking for a game with a compelling story, you might want to look elsewhere. In my opinion. Game is 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original story and endings in The Forest but boy, this game had a rushed story and maybe should have been delayed further. Some of the new crafting elements are interesting, you can either make blueprints like in the original or you can utilize the free crafting system which is fun. The graphics are also pretty, seasons are a thing. Enemies (cannibals especially) have interesting behaviors and the AI is pretty good. I can even forgive some of the early access bugs like weapons getting stuck to each other or eating your canteen if it gets equipped to a hotkey.However the story is just...so rushed and confusing. You get 2-3  cutscenes during the entire game, maybe one line of dialog, no reason for your character to know any of the existing characters but your character just kinda goes along with things anyway? Even reading the emails and viewing some cameras you get a teaser of what is going on...but then BAM you get hit with an ending with no end boss, no challenge (you can literally just run to the end past a few mutants). You're left wondering what happened, who are these people, what happened to these people, why should I care. Hopefully they'll be working on more story fixes/adds when getting out of early access so that things actually make more sense. Very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: When compared to The Forest, it feels so much better. Having AI to help you build, and being responsible for their well being, adds an extra layer of difficulty to just navigating the island. Not only do you deal with cannibals and mutants, but you have to also make sure your buddies don't die in the process; taking precaution also rewards you with achievements as well. For anybody who hasn't played The Forest, this will feel more difficult; you won't know much about building fortresses and weapons, or catching food to sustain yourself. Caves will add a layer of immersion and shock, as you'll see the "mutants" and realize you're in for a ride. Keep in mind that the game is still in early access, but the changes will be drastic from The Forest.My favorite is the bugged out red cannibals that spin wildly when killed.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, let me tell you a few things about this game....It's like a time machine that takes you back to those golden days when you and your buddies would scream, swear, and pray to the gaming gods not to get eaten by cannibals. It's like a horror movie marathon, but with more gaming and less popcorn. So, buckle up, gamers, and get ready to relive your worst nightmares... in a totally fun and twisted way!Now, I know it's still in early access, but trust me, this game brings a lot to the table. It's like the old The Forest game, but with some serious improvements. The visuals are decent, but be warned, this game is a resource hog. If you don't have a decent PC, this game will bring you more frustration than joy. So, unless you're a glutton for punishment, invest in a good rig.My advice? Play this game with friends, because let's face it, you don't want to be the only one getting eaten by those cannibals. It's always better to have someone else to share the fear and terror with. Plus, when you're huddled together in the dark, you can always blame each other for making noise and attracting those pesky cannibals.So, grab your buddies and get ready to face your fears. Who knows, maybe you'll come out alive and have a few laughs along the way. Or, you'll all end up as cannibal chow, but hey, at least you'll go out together.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible! If you played , this game is just that but better in a whole bunch of ways. The building system is super satisfying / innovative. The world feels like it's own place and oh my god the graphics are amazing. The graphics come at a cost of performance but it feels like a fair trade off considering how much you can interact with the beautiful world. The game is being updated (with actual impressive content updates) about once every 2 weeks. I think the amount of content in this game is definitely worth the price at this point considering I still have a lot left to do with a nice amount of hours logged so far. The one major complaint I have so far is that the combat can be somewhat clunky. Sometimes hitting enemies wont really impact them because they're mid-animation or they've just been hit right before. Playing on hard can feel like a bit of a slog and I'm not a fan of increasing enemy health on increased difficulty. I'm not a huge fan of the fact that enemies respawn in a cave so quickly so that if you take a lot of time to get through them sometimes you end up making no progress as the enemies respawn faster than you can kill. Also it's kind of crappy that simply saving and quitting causes loot to come back, giving you an easy way to cheese getting a lot of valuable resources. At this point, I wouldn't recommend playing your first world on hard (maybe I just suck).Overall this is a huge recommend from me as Endnight has made one of the most beautiful world that feels alive and inspires exploring and experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much the best a survival game can get. The game drops you onto a cannibal and mutant infested island and gives you the complete freedom to do whatever you'd like. It can be pretty tough at times, but you are able to customize your difficulty in whatever way makes it a more enjoyable experience for you. You can change enemy health, how much damage, indestructible structures, and tons more.The graphics are beautiful, and the attention to detail is top tier. The seasons change. Summer is bright, green and lush until you get to slowly see the leaves change color, Certain crops stop growing and eventually snow begins to fall. You leave a path in the snow where you walk. Freshwater lakes freeze. The amount of small, more obscure realistic physics I noticed while playing was amazing. It really feels like the devs thought of even the tiny things that don't matter much but increase the immersion a ton.The story is optional. If you just wanna survive on the island forever, build a massive base, you can do that. However, I found uncovering all the clues and the mystery extremely exciting and interesting, especially after playing the original The Forest.If I had to make one complaint, although a very minor one - it would be that certain, small areas of the map feel a bit empty. But this is contrasted by the amount of things to do, and other portions of the map that are very well done and fleshed-out. So trust me, do not let this deter you from playing the game as this is simply me just nitpicking.There are very few survival games who knock it out of the park the way Endnight Games does. I have a lot of trust in them, and am really hoping for a 3rd installment of this series. This has easily become my favorite survival game, and easily in my top 10 games of all time. It's just a must-have experience for gamers. Very much worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a massive improvement from the first. Building is super unique and fun.  Weapons feel super clean and smooth to use. Some items from the first game that were not brought over are deeply missed. For example. Transporting logs from one place to another used to be easily done using a log sled.  Considering this game is in early access, I have high hopes for the future of this game. I will say that the "endings" are underwhelming and the final area of the game feels empty. A lot of the weapons are bunched up in a single room towards the end which seemed a bit underwhelming. I wished that they were more evenly placed or discovered throughout the game play.  I have only came across a few bugs while playing the game which includes but isn't limited to player models being warped, hard stuck in between objects, brief pauses, floor and roof building, items vanishing in inventory etc. In general, the game is worth the money and the hype and I can't wait to see future developments.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the Forest. I finished it a number of times, both endings. I went back to play it because I loved the building mechanics, the use of animal hides, the weapons you could make (like the slingshot). When I heard about the follow up I was excited, I counted down the days to the game release. Then it was in early access and I could play it. And I hated it, why the sudden reliance in "finding" weapons and items that in the first game you could make? Yes it's a beautiful looking game, the graphics are superb. But where is the fun in "finding another gun"! Why the need to rely on guns at all? Kelvin is fun to work around for some of the game at least, but then he just gets in the way and is virtually useless as he won't fight anyone. Virginia has unlimited ammunition for the guns you give her - wtf! Yes re-arming an npc can be a pain in some games, but that's just one of the tasks you need to do to complete the game. But Virginia being able to produce unlimted ammunition for the shotgun, the rifle and pistol. That's not immersion breaking - much!I wanted to love this game so much, I feel guilty that I don't love it. But I've realised that I'm trying to play through the game, not because I want to, but because I feel I have to. The devs put so much work into it. But it's not the game I was hoping for, it's not even close. Why remove the old style building mechanics - I loved being able to just throw resources at a blueprint and it took them - none of this oh so stupid "you have to do all the logs first, then the stones, then ....". That is so frustrating. So are the constant animations - yes splitting a log in half to make a floor was brilliant the first time I saw it - but the hundredth time or the thousand'th time - especially when you could be killed by the mutants while being forced to watch an animation - hell no!So for anyone who loved the Forest, I wish you luck with this game, maybe it is what you want. But for me, it's over, time to uninstall a game I have no interest in trying to finish. Anyone who loves survival games but didn't play the Forest. Well I hope you like it.

_childDocuments_.review: “Since no one with a positive review is willing to explain why, I guess I will.Right off the bat, visually, this game is jaw-droppingly phenomenal. The lighting, presentation, and atmosphere has been brilliantly re-captured to ensure older fans from the first game feel like they are returning to somewhere that feels oddly familiar, yet holds many new and unique encounters we have yet to discover. The colors, especially the greens, pop in just the right way to further emphasize the seemingly calm and collected forest during the day that can quickly change into a dark and unsettling nightmare by night.Endnight has again hit the nail on the head with the combat. Considering the old system of charging up momentum to land attacks worked exceptionally well, it's understandable they did not try and reinvent the wheel. Combat has been expanded and smoothed out just enough to keep it feeling fun, fresh and different. Landing hits is just as satisfying as it was in the old game, and mastering these techniques is especially entertaining with both new enemies and their original, upgraded counterparts. As far as interaction mechanics, the inventory system has been cleverly improved, and Kelvin is a genuinely cool addition to the game. For other friendless losers such as myself, having Kelvin around is good company. Interacting with him is intuitive and straightforward, and losing track of him isn't a problem with the GPS you get right off the bat. Starting off with some way to orient yourself in a map that's five times bigger than the first game is also a welcome change. The "quick inventory" while you're on the move is a welcome upgrade as well. The crafting menu has also been improved, separating custom buildings from presets, which makes it easier to keep track of what you can make using custom buildings. Unfortunately, the garbage control scheme returns so for the first five minutes into my new save I was making the game playable instead of... playing the game.But holy smokes the building is 1000% better than the first game. You still have your already mentioned presets for use in a pinch, and you have the massively improved custom building. Instead of laying out where you want everything to go all at once, you get to pick and choose as you create your desired structure, which makes it way easier to manage your resources while making it, and also allows you to make changes as you see fit. This is a huge step up from the previous game, and it's great.I see some complaints with the performance but I personally had no issues. With the medium preset my game ran at a rock solid 75-80 fps, which is perfectly fine for a game like this. Survival games don't need absurdly high frame-rates; what's more important is certainly the frame times and consistency. And my game would rarely drop frames, it again stayed at 76-77 fps with little deviation.I think that's really this game in a nutshell. The first game, but with pretty much every mechanic getting upgraded and reworked in a positive way (for the most part). There's some reused sound FX throughout the game which I thought was a little disappointing, but there have to be some expectations with a team of just 30 people. People get wrapped up in the fact that visually it competes with triple-A games, but those same people forget a tiny team of 30 put this together, and they are only asking for 30 bucks, which is a steal for a game with this much visual fidelity and replayability. Not to mention the oncoming free updates that will only add more content. It's certainly okay to be critical of a product and point out its flaws, but with expectations in check, this comes out as a pretty solid game”

The concept is there, it's just right now it's not great. The story is idek, confusing as hell. The ending was just absurd (again didn't understand it). There are a lot of bugs in this game that people don't really talk about it. The gameplay at first is actually pretty fun. However, the more you keep on playing it, it just gets way too repetitive and annoying. Same thing with the mechanics. It's cool at first, but later on I just don't want to see the same damn animation over and over again (For example, making a tent). Also, the map is so huge which means lots of stuff right? Nope, it's a huge map with a whole lot of nothing in between key points of the map. The game is basically a walking simulator just to get from one cave to the next. Also, building a base is the most useless thing ever if you're playing to beat the game. Building a base just wastes time, and you're never gonna use it again. Caves are super boring in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is an excellent sequel, offering an impressive sandbox full of bizarre creatures, places and loreThe first thing you'll notice is how beautiful it looks. From the moment you step into its world, the game's exceptional lighting, both outdoors and in the eerie confines of its caves, sets the stage for an adventure that's as visually striking as it is tense. It could easily be the most gorgeous looking Unity game on the market right nowThe gameplay offers a rich variety of activities, including building, exploring, fighting monsters and collecting loot. For those who enjoy crafting and constructing, this game is a base builder's paradise. The building mechanics are intuitive and rewarding, making it enjoyable even for players who typically avoid this aspect of survival titles. I don't usually like building but Sons of the Forest had me hooked. I was constantly placing new blueprints and running around collecting resources. It was really fun and satisfying, and you can see your progress in real time as each stone or stick you place will be accurately displayed and inserted into your structureSet against an intriguing backdrop that blends body horror with sci-fi, Sons of the Forest features a world filled with creepy enemies and anomalies. The game's lore is fascinating, weaving together elements of cults, alien artifacts, and alternate dimensions. This kind of world-building encouraged me to delve deeper into the story, looking up additional information onlineThe enemy designs are truly unique and disturbing, especially when it comes to some of the mutant types. The AI is impressive, with companions and foes alike behaving intelligently. Your enemies climb trees, interact with one another, they fake attacks on purpose to throw you off, set ambushes and use tactics. Each monster or cannibal has it's own distinct attack patterns and personality, and it's fun to figure them all out. Your allies can help you defend your base, build structures, point things out in the environment, collect food and building resources. They are optional and you can always "dispose" of them if you wish, but I loved them and they even have their own ending cutscenes as wellThe dynamic environment, featuring changing seasons and weather, further brings the world to life. And it actually impacts the gameplay as well, as you will need to craft or find warm clothes and make shelters so you don't freeze. The game also runs surprisingly smoothly, with excellent performance in 4K using ultra settings, and no crashes or glitchesIn terms of equipment, Sons of the Forest offers a wide variety. There's a dozen weapons, which can be further enhanced with attachments, as well as throwables. The armor system makes a return as well, allowing you to both craft and harvest things to cover yourself with. But that's just barely scratching the surface. There's tons of gear you can craft, 3D print, find in caves and bunkers, and even further enhance it with a special type of device. I must admit though, that there were tools and gadgets that I never used. Such as the masks, or the electric weapons, or the slingshotThere are also a handful of vehicles, which really help when it comes to traversing the island. The hang glider and the electric unicycle being my personal favoritesAlso, even though not much is known about the protagonist, I think he looks dashing. And has some of the best hand models I've ever seen in a videogame. Whoever modeled and textured them deserves a raise However despite its many strengths, Sons of the Forest does have some drawbacks:For instance, all the gameplay animations are fantastic. There's literally a separate animation for every single thing you can craft or discover in the game. They're quick and snappy, and always seamlessly transition into gameplayBut the cutscene animations often feel off, with incorrect pacing and a lack of anticipation that can break immersion. Coupled with: a horrendous field of view, clipping meshes, strange motions or facial expressions, and missing sounds, all of which can detract from the overall enjoyment of the game. I thought that was just part of the Early-Access experience, but it seems like they barely touched them up for the 1.0 releaseI don't know why they even bothered hiring Shawn Ashmore, as he's barely in the game, and none of his scenes look motion captured either. So they got a Hollywood star for a couple of minutes of artificially sped up audio. It really made me think that the whole "cinematic" part of the narrative was an afterthought. Something that they put together out of necessity, rather than genuine desire to tell a story. The narrative, while interesting in premise, is kinda shallow and not well-delivered, making it hard to follow the plot. I really dislike this disconnected Dark Souls breadcrumb type of storytellingCombat can also be a little awkward, often boiling down to who can tank more damage rather than requiring skill or strategyThe soundtrack, is less impressive than its predecessor, focusing more on short stingers than memorable melodies. No more hauntingly beautiful main menu tracks, and no more tense combat music. Though there are some really catchy radio tunesAlso I don't know if this is a pro or con but - I never felt scared or intimidated by anything this game had to offer. There are some scripted jumpscares where a hanging skeleton or whatever falls on the floor in front of you with a loud thud, but that's not horror. Maybe it's not meant to be scary, because I always found myself pushing forward, into the danger, I wanted to see moreOverall, Sons of the Forest excels in creating a visually stunning and immersive survival experience. Full of interesting monster designs and curious anomaliesIts strengths lie in , , and . Which far outweigh its shortcomings in cutscenes & storytelling. For players looking for a rich, atmospheric game with plenty to discover and build, Sons of the Forest is a standout title worth playing

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the forest... we waited for you for a very long time! Although the game is in early access and the story is not finished yet, the game is incredible and the developers implemented some original mechanics and ideas into it.I really love Ke(L)vin! He is an amazing friend and companion that helps you with gathering logs, sticks, food and building shelters <3. I'm really attached to him and one of my favorite moments in the game is with him. One of the red cannibals attacked him and I got so angry that I equipped my machete and jumped over the enemy. When I killed the cannibal I got very proud of myself and then I saw behind me Kelvin who was dead by my anger over the red cannibal. The game has a long journey until it gets out of the early access as there's not a lot of content currently added when compared to "the Forest", but the developers are tirelessly working on the new updates and the results look to be promising. _childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game are the graphics at a solid 7/10 - they make you want to actually go outside and go camping or snowboarding, both of which would be better uses of your time than playing this game.If you want to bash zombies, build a fort with your friends, and have a great time doing it, 7 Days to Die is a better game.If you want to immerse yourself in the characters' story, Fallout New Vegas is a better game.Both of those are more rewarding to play - you get very little for playing this literal walking simulator.If you enjoy finding/crafting ammo to dispatch the enemies with, that's as much of a reward as you'll get, because the melee combat is rudimentary, and at best, spammy.SotF devs if you're reading this, congratulations, ya got me! You have successfully tilted me off the face of the planet with this game.Feel free to go through my game list to see what I like playing, but I cannot recommend anyone buy and play this game, in all of its entirety and bugginess.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE AFTER PATCH 15: As announced by the developers, the game will be released in full version on February 22nd, unfortunately the system on which the game is based (the survival part) absolutely does not exist and no content has been released regarding it. Sons of The Forest will not receive any more content updates until release on February 22nd and only bug fixes will be released. IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR A SURVIVAL GAME DON'T BET ON THIS ONE, THE SYSTEMS ARE MEDIOCRE, NO SURVIVAL AND THE MAIN STORY IS RIDICULOUS. THERE ARE MUCH DEEPER GAMES THAT DEFINITELY DESERVE MORE, LIKE THE FIRST GAME. REALLY DISAPPOINTED.“We set out to make the ultimate survival horror simulator" Yes sure.I have to be quite critical of this game, for me it's just all graphics and little gameplay, a lot of content is missing and how it is structured now only leads to boredom, even playing with friends. Many contents and systems are missing compared to the first chapter, all points of interest are marked on the map, there is nothing to explore since the game already tells you where to go and what to do, survival mechanics are practically absent, seasons they do not cause any diversity on the environment or on the player, except of course for the snow. There is nothing to build except for modular constructions (but again, build and then do what?), prefabricated and absent decorations. Every loot on the map respawns, and doesn't give any in-game challenges (you can reload your save and replenish loot as much as you like). The enemies are almost useless and stupid, there are no variants or new mobs or major innovations. To date, with update 2 there hasn't been anything to make me play this game again, they even added the final boss in the story which is nothing more than a demon already present but only enlarged in size. I sincerely feel cheated by these developers, and counting that this game had to come out last year I'm very hesitant about its future development, moreover it had to come out as a full game and not in early access, in that case what would we have? Nothing.There would be much more to write, but given the situation I also avoid writing a novel, for those like me who are able to see the situation, will understand the problems I have reported. Avoid discussions on the game page if you are an adult, they are all rude kids or adults who have never grown up.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the game is no longer in Early Access, I'm going to be brutally honest. The game is cool. But it's far from a worthy sequel to The Forest. _childDocuments_.review: Even for early acces, quite litteraly unplayable due too missing simple base mechanics such as for example quick selecting weapons/ tools, dodges...The npc you get is a nice addition but he is a total goon, gave him the assignment to finish a structure - he chopped it down instead.Hityboxes are scuffed and so is damage taken, 25-30% damage from a hit of one of those baby mutants in the start cave? the damage they can tank is also quite weird, they wont even die after sitting on a molotov, yet those big tank looking cannibals die from 3 arrows or one axe swing.Softlocks afer respawn.Respawn points are fixed locations, and cant seem to be changed to your base.Building mode did get some polishing when compared to the forest 1 and is slightly better, gathering materials goes quicker due too the density of the forest you are in, which is nice, the map itself is also quite good looking so those are definitely an upgrade. yet one swing from any cannibal will still break your structure and drop all of the materials regardless of having 1 log in it, or missing one log to completion.Journal doesnt show what berries/ plants you discoverdas in Forest 1.Not possible to place landmarks/ marks in the GPS.No option for riposte/ parry but the cannibals can.Whatever you build, is constantly under attack. _childDocuments_.review: Well It has not even been out for 24 hours yet and i have 12.3 hours already... So I guess I would have to say I 100% recommend this masterpiece of a survival game. It is the perfect sequel to The Forest, the combat mechanics and the building mechanics are simply amazing and it is such an improvement from the previous title. The enemy AI is great, they are smart and the various types are amazing. I killed a cannibal and a female one came running and started crying over top the body and accepted her fate as I shot her in the back of the head with a 9mm. The Fact that in solo you can now have allies that can help you out is simply amazing and its even better they still exist in multiplayer. The Guns are really fun and honestly overpowered but you cant just make ammo you have to find it. Now aside from how amazing I think it is from the previous title there are many bugs and kinks, such as it needs to be optimised, there is a lot of random log and item duping from doing simple actions. The building may be an amazing and better difference but it still needs some work it feels a bit jank at times and multiplayer has plenty of bugs (for people connecting not as much for host) such as sometimes the game will bug out and players cant place objects or they cant interact with objects. Kevin likes to no clip through things and pick up objects out of thin air and create them as well. There are probably many more bugs but this is all i can think of so far throughout my play through but you also have to remember that this game is early access and an indie title.Edit: My first save broke after 13 hours and I had to restart, so afterwards my friends and I started a new save and accidentally beat the game in around 4 hours without finding much lore pieces.

_childDocuments_.review: Was playing multiplayer with a friend and some genius at this games company decided to allow you to manually wipe your character progression every time you join a multiplayer lobby. It asks whether you would like to continue with a saved character and gives you a yes or no prompt, with no chance to get your character back if you delete the save you will literally lose all your characters progress and have to unlock everything again. Considering the idea that this game relies on progression that it tied to items that you unlock and carry with you along the way it doesn't make any sense that you can accidentally delete hours of progress before even loading into the game. That's what happened to a friend of mines and it killed our play through. It is basically a button that asks whether you want to delete you game progress, for god knows what reason, why would anyone wish to delete their game progress on a multiplayer server that they join?I am honestly still astonished that it's even an option so watch out if you have any friends to play with because clicking the wrong option leads to a character wipe that is unable to be found again.

_childDocuments_.review: After 2 years of delays. this game is unfortunately terrible. I loved the original game. The atmosphere was absolutely unlike any other game and exploring the massive CONNECTED cave system was thrilling and terrifying. The enemies weren't very diverse, but that didn't matter. All the claims this game made at improving upon the original fell short beyond marginally better graphics, a dynamic building system, and a (unnecessarily) larger map.The graphics are there for the most part (I don't really care about them but some do) aside from the rock textures. The moon was pretty and the trees and foliage looked nice, but nothing that is better than any recent releases going for that style. But the sound quality... is just unbearable. Enemies sound like a whining rodent that sometimes grunts. They don't react appropriately to getting brutally assaulted. THE WIND SOUND. jesus christ the wind is so loud. At 30% sfx volume my ears were raped anytime a breeze blew by. Every sound scales very poorly if at all with your distance. It is impossible to ascertain how far a cannibal or flowing water is based of the sound, as every audio bit just gets slammed right in your ear like its inside your ear canal.  I could maybe excuse the glaring sound design issues if the exploration or story was compelling. They are not. The open world might be 4 times the original map but its 10 times as empty. 60% of me beating the game (no guides) with my friends is just running across empty forests scattered with copy paste villages every 15 minutes. The caves are just linear in and out systems, some just being a hole with loot (JUST ROPE SO MUCH ROPE) and no enemies or anything of interest despite the mark on your map. Their are 4 mutants that you will likely encounter, and not once are you ever forced to kill one. The story is actually laughably bad. Two cut scenes with almost no buildup or context and some printed emails, most not of any relevance. if you were considering this game for a compelling story turn right around. It is a complete joke, after the final cut scene we just laughed asking ourselves "is that actually the ending for a game we'd been waiting for for 3 years?" The cut scene itself is just funny, at the end of the game the conclusion feels like watching spongebob on 10 benadryls.The greatest (not that great!) strength of the game is not the combat, it is the peaceful survival. No fast swap option makes engaging cannibals a nuisance. The shotgun is hilariously broken, one shotting everything and making them rag-doll. I love the inventory space, its a nice expansion of the original,. The building feels like legos and kelvin is a helpful guy. Anytime we started having fun something would remind us of just how early access this game was. They should've just delayed it again, the state it is in now is embarrassing and disappointing from such a respected development team.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is an awesome first-person survival horror game that kept me on the edge of my seat throughout my gameplay experience. The graphics are absolutely stunning, and the open-world environment is expansive, allowing me to explore every nook and cranny of the island.The game's storyline is intriguing and kept me engaged, and the new mutant types and boss battles provided an exciting challenge. I particularly enjoyed the improved AI of the mutants, making each encounter more intense and unpredictable.The game's crafting system is also top-notch, allowing me to craft a variety of weapons and shelter to survive the harsh wilderness. And let's not forget the co-op mode, which is a blast to play with friends and adds a new level of teamwork to the gameplay.Overall, Sons of the Forest is a fantastic addition to the survival horror genre, and I highly recommend it to any fans of the genre. With its improved graphics, expanded open-world environment, and engaging storyline, Sons of the Forest is a must-play game for any survival horror enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: Vintage chocolate chip cookiesIngredients150g salted butter, softened80g light brown muscovado sugar80g granulated sugar2 tsp vanilla extract1 large egg225g plain flour½ tsp bicarbonate of soda¼ tsp salt200g plain chocolate chips or chunksMethodSTEP 1Heat the oven to 190C/fan170C/gas 5 and line two baking sheets with non-stick baking paper.STEP 2Put 150g softened salted butter, 80g light brown muscovado sugar and 80g granulated sugar into a bowl and beat until creamy.STEP 3Beat in 2 tsp vanilla extract and 1 large egg.STEP 4Sift 225g plain flour, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ¼ tsp salt into the bowl and mix it in with a wooden spoon.STEP 5Add 200g plain chocolate chips or chunks and stir well.STEP 6Use a teaspoon to make small scoops of the mixture, spacing them well apart on the baking trays. This mixture should make about 30 cookies.STEP 7Bake for 8–10 mins until they are light brown on the edges and still slightly soft in the centre if you press them.STEP 8Leave on the tray for a couple of mins to set and then lift onto a cooling rack.RECIPE TIPSFREEZING THE BISCUITSIf you’ve frozen the biscuits, take them out and arrange them on a lined baking sheet. Once defrosted, pop them in a medium oven 190C/170 fan/gas mark 5 and heat for 2-3 mins to crisp up. Don’t leave them too long or they’ll dry out.STORING DOUGHYou can keep the uncooked dough in a sealed container in the fridge for up to two weeks. Simply take some out, dollop on a lined baking tray and allow to come up to room temperature for 5 mins before bakingThe game is really good to I just figured i'd give you my cookie recipe first so you could have some great cookies to enjoy with this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The improved graphics from "The Forest" and attention to detail when it comes to game features like crafting is just a mask that hides the true bug fest this game really is. Not only is this game littered with bugs, but it runs like complete garbage and the world is lacking and empty. When it comes to a survival game, I expect very little: an immersive world and basic survival mechanics. Sons of the Forest has every feature a survival game would have, and not a single one is polished. The forest in this game is anything but immersive. Its repetitive, boring, and empty. I could walk for hours and not find a single point of interest, which should not be the case for a mysterious forest with billionaires that have gone missing. The forest in this game just shows how bigger isn't always better.The enemies/cannibals in this game is a joke. In the first game, The Forest, the cannibals felt alive and unpredictable, filling the player with fear and paranoia; however, Sons of the Forest fails to implement the same feeling. Instead, the enemies just surround you or your base in intervals of what seem like 10 minutes and they just attack, making it impossible to maintain a base without disabling destroy structures. Having to be nomadic in Sons of the Forest's map is boring and frustrating. The enemies are not alive, but rather just npcs with the sole purpose to annoy you.This game is borderline unplayable with the bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Needed a few more years in the oven. Multiplayer is buggy, and i mean BUGGY. I'm talking phasing through the floor, being entombed in a ladder, textures clipping everywhere, the works. However the worst part is the saving, no one seems to be synced up in their saves so whenever me and my friends boot into a game all of us are at different points of progress and we have to spend an hour catching everyone up and getting to the proper locations. The game is also very poorly optimized, on minimum settings i'm still only getting 20-30 fps, and this drops seemingly at random. The AI on your "companions" will break at random, on the tenth day Kelvin ceased any function and could not complete any task assigned to him. The tracker you place on Virginia bugs out as well, leaving dozens of map markers. The game is also missing many features from the first including rainwater collection and the log cart, so you'd better enjoy walking from logs to your house for hours, and walking to a river every time you need some water. Speaking of walking, the game designers seem to absolutely love it because this map is huge and barren. Get ready to spend hours trudging through the grass just to get a couple small items. Some of the caves don't even have anything in them, and the helicopter crash, despite being marked with a special icon, has absolutely nothing in it. Night is dark, sometimes unreasonably so. Your torch, flashlight, and lighter seem to only illuminate about two feet in front of you, and this turns to zero when you are sprinting. If you dare to open your inventory for more than three seconds you will be immediately jumped by the army of cannibals that just spawned behind you, and they will camp your corpse so that you cannot get up when revived. Building a base serves basically zero purpose as you will be constantly under assault for no reward, and you can simply go cave to cave until game completion.TLDR; don't buy this until 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where do we even begin with Sons of the Forest? On one hand, the game is an absolute feast for the eyes with its stunning visuals and expansive, beautiful map. You'll encounter all sorts of new enemies and have the pleasure of discovering new weapons and tools that can make survival a little easier.But then there are the cons. The new building system is a bit of a double-edged sword - sure, it's cool to experiment with, but it comes at the cost of losing a lot of the old content from the original game. And while the new weapons and tools are exciting to find, they can also make the game feel a little too easy once you've got your hands on them.To make matters worse, the crafting system has been severely limited. You'll find yourself missing out on useful recipes like increased inventory capacity and materials from animals. And don't even get me started on the story. It feels like one big fetch quest, with locations so far apart from each other that you'll spend more time running than actually playing.The cutscenes are a bit of a joke too. This is supposed to be a survival horror game, yet the cutscenes feel like concepts and are downright laughable. And if you do manage to slog through the story, you'll be rewarded with an incredibly confusing ending that leaves you scratching your head.Companions are supposed to be helpful, right? Well, not in Sons of the Forest. They feel weird and annoying, and when used, they can break the game entirely. And despite the huge map, it feels empty, with locations full of items you can't even pick up because your inventory is already full after just a few hours of exploring.Oh, and let's not forget the artificial blocks in the story. You'll find yourself searching for a single shovel on the entire island just so you can dig a few inches of dirt and progress the story. And what about all the misc and clutter items lying around? Plastic buckets, working boat engines - your character can't even pick them up or use them!All in all, Sons of the Forest is a confusing mess of a game. It's got some great moments, sure, but they're buried beneath all the issues and frustrating mechanics. Play at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I've played for over 300 hours and I still want to like this game...but I can't. And I was a big fan of The Forest and I love builder survival games, in general. My favorite aspect of the game is the building and I've spent most of my time doing that. But it's super buggy, wildly inconsistent, and way too convoluted for what should be simple concepts. When something as simple as building a staircase with walls requires you to 'place a piece, remove a piece, place a piece, trick it, remove a piece,' there's something fundamentally wrong with the mechanics. And you can only learn that through a google search because the game sure doesn't tell you how to work that out. Sometimes you go to place a piece and nothing gets placed but you still expend the material. Sometimes you place something, then go for an adventure or supply run, come back and pieces are missing...yes, even with structural damage turned off.The story is very interesting, but short in comparison. The graphics and audio are beautiful but I get the sense that the dev team cared more about making it look pretty than working and playing well. I would rather them sacrifice graphics for quality mechanics and a building system that doesn't randomly break for no reason, making hours of work feel wasted and being a real design killer. It's a really sloppy system for how good it looks and it's a shame.My real distrust of this game started shortly after buying it. Keep in mind, I had been eagerly anticipating this game and had been hearing that the game would be a "completely fleshed out game" at release. When it dropped, I was not aware that, a week before release, Endnight changed their tune and said they were bumping it down to EA (likely due to mismanaged funds, greedy fingers, and an unrealistic deadline). So, I start playing it thinking it's a complete game only to be sharply let down. To top it off, it wasn't even close to a complete game at that time. Since then, Endnight has added quite a bit of stuff to the game (some of it kinda cool but honestly unnecessary) while seemingly ignoring all the major mechanical issues that more than a fair amount of people complained about. To my dismay, many of those issues persist today in the "Full release" of the game.The AI for Kelvin and Virginia are sometimes helpful, but mostly they just get in the way or they eventually geek out and start doing really dumb behaviors, like walking into a wall for 40 min because the AI can't comprehend that stepping 2 feet to their left will solve their pathing issue. Kelvin...ugh...It's almost better if you just let him become a cannibal chew toy. It's better than sending him to go gather logs and then he proceeds to walk 3 miles away to cuts trees when there's fairly dense forest just outside the base. At that point it's faster to just ignore him and do it yourself. Once you get the zipline gun, Kelvin pretty much becomes obsolete.  And the AI's affinity for getting into places that they can't get out of is...impressive! I can't even begin to explain how Kelvin manages to turn every door he walks through into some kind of weird out-of-phase ghost that gets lodged into the wall.All I'm saying is, for a "complete game" it feels like it's still in EA. I'm super disappointed in Endnight for playing dirty marketing tricks with much less than truthful advertising and then passing off this, Still unfinished, game as a full release. For the amount of time they put into making this game, it should, at very least, be mostly consistent mechanically. I don't see it reaching that milestone any time soon, if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: A highly anticipated game that I feel didn't live up to its expectations. While I understand that it is early access, there are many inherent flaws to it that will take some creativity to get around. The scale of the game is too large, with a beautiful but mostly empty and uneventful map. The caves are, for the most part, separate, and are very easy to clear in quick succession. To account for the scale of the game, additions made for ease of travel have severely dampened the difficulty, and in my opinion, the charm of the game. Firearms are very easy to get and even on hard mode, ammunition is plentiful. There are literal electric unicycles (the Knight V) that barely drain your already large amount of batteries, and I hope to god it's just a placeholder. They allow you to bypass literally every danger in the game with no risk. The threat of cannibals and mutants feels almost next to nothing, even when the more dangerous ones come around. Cannibal interactions feel far less special and more like an inconvenience, which feels like a total waste of how intricate their AI is. The map is too large to care about their borders, and the game is too easy to care about making peace. Another huge difference is that because the survival aspects were so easy, the only focus was the story, which was very short and unmeaningful. However, I don't ever recall caring much for the story in the first forest, as I was too busy and immersed in actually surviving against an ever growing threat while finding myself moving towards more and more drastic measures. This was even after maybe my fifth playthrough of that game. None of that was felt in Sons of the Forest, unfortunately.Overall, me and two friends had completed the game twice after exploring literally everything, and built a very sizeable base under 20 hours total. One of these playthroughs was even before the Knight V was even a thing, and where we got guns late due to not knowing where they were.However, there is a lot of good to the game as well and I won't pretend like I didn't have fun during my 18 hours of playtime. Despite the bugs which I imagine will be fixed over time, it has a very good core. It looks great, the building is fun, AI interactions, despite being far less consequential, were still fun, and it is absolutely a great game to play with friends. Hopefully the game continues to grow and become far more fleshed out over time, but until then, I cannot recommend it in its current state if you're expecting the same survival horror of the first game or an immersive and difficult experience. This game should have stayed in development like so many other games that are being rushed to release nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: Survival gameplay and building is a ton of fun. The combat is fine. Overall a great co-op experience with friends. However, the story is incredibly lackluster. Even finding the notes doesn't do much to clarify things. Both the level design and the storycraft are significantly downgraded from the previous game. Also, the lengthy animations for simple actions can be overbearing at times, specifically discovering things like name cards in bunkers that the character inspects for a literal 10 seconds before letting you exit the animation or getting trapped in the slow pick-up-backpack animation when respawning in hostile areas (which can result in you getting instantly downed again depending on the area). The animations and physics for vehicles were really clunky and made most vehicles unpleasant or disorienting to operate. Also the minibosses were significantly harder than any boss in the game, making big moments in the story fall flat. Overall, the game is still a lot of fun for co-op. But in terms of singleplayer/story experience, I was left a little disappointed. I still recommend it at $30, but these are my criticisms to anyone curious about picking up the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm amending my review for some clarification because I feel like I wasn't really specific enough.For starters, the story:I've seen a few reviews say the story of the original Forest game was bad and predictable, but I think those reviews missed the point. Sure, it was predictable in the sense that you have to save your son, and that seems to be the surface level takeaway everyone reviewing *this* game had for some reason.There's a lot of things in the original game you need context clues to figure out. You don't just get your hand held through the story, you have to find a bunch of clues that point to the bigger picture.Sons of the Forest is similar, and my original takeaway was that there was not enough to explain the ending.This isn't really the case. I think the problem with Sons of the Forest's storytelling isn't that it's tacked on, but rather it all happens too quickly. I think in regards to the story and gameplay, having the caves and bunkers marked for you immediately is too much, especially in co-op. When you have a partner, as long as one of you manages to stay up, you can just keep a loop going of reviving your friend no matter what difficulty you're on.This makes it so you can blow through the caves incredibly fast, and if you're with the wrong group, you'll probably miss a lot of the clues that point to the story because you're breezing by so fast. The artifact is actually really interesting, and the cannibals presence is also really cool, but only if you're not rushing through things. Is this the game's fault? I think the blame can be split: When you found a cave in the original game on your own, you didn't want to rush it because it felt like you discovered something massive, even with friends. You knew going into that cave meant your exploration paid off, but Sons of the Forest spawning you in a radius of 5 separate caves removes the feeling of discovery and I think it pushes you to just want to rush through and get to the next cave.I'll chant the chorus with everyone else and say this: The trailers really did make it seem as though the story was complete, but it's still lacking context. Most people speculate the young man and old man in the bunker were Timmy and his Dad, and they were right, but the confirmation doesn't come from the game telling you, it comes from the game files referencing them as such, and Obelisk Studio's art station saying the same thing.The "bad guy" is never addressed, and is literally called "badguy" in the game files, and I'm pretty sure their head model is just a multiplayer head, and not actually a uniquely modeled character, which muddies things further.The surrounding elements, such as the new artifact and the cannibals, as well as the missing persons you're sent to find seems to be answered, but everything else feels pretty unfinished.Now let's talk map size:This'll be a quicky but it needs to be said - the map is bigger but doesn't feel like it. Someone said in another review it feels like the same amount of landmarks but with more walking and I couldn't agree more. There's a lot of empty space without collectibles, camps, or enemies other than mud people jumping from bushes. I guess this is good if you want a lot of space to build without getting close to landmarks, but by and large this feels more like a walking simulator than the original game, with less sprint speed.Combat and AI:The combat is pretty much imported straight from the original Forest, so it was never bound to be super good. You can parry attacks now, but it seems hit and miss. The hitreg seems pretty wonky, especially when you're attacking things on an elevated surface, and enemies seem to dodge a lot more than in the original game. To me it feels like artificial difficulty, but I guess the guns balance it. In my opinion, the guns are really fun to use but it feels like they're a bit overpowered, especially in co-op when your ammo is essentially doubled or even 8 times the amount. In co-op, dying doesn't seem to have consequences. In single player dying twice will make you officially die and have to restart or reload your save, but in co-op you'll die with your items right next to you every time, essentially making dying pointless. It's more annoying than something to learn from, because there's nothing stopping you from just cutting yourself loose, dying, then cutting yourself loose again until you're free from whatever camp you spawned in. Dying in caves also makes you respawn in said cave, so even less consequence when you're exploring underground.Companion AI seems a bit wonky right now. First playthrough Kelvin was stuck underwater for like an hour walking in circles, and Virginia kept taking off her GPS tracker. Second playthrough I spawned in the mountain, and went into an ice cave. Kelvin got stuck in the ceiling, then eventually clipped instead the ceiling and either couldn't get out or died, couldn't tell you which. Virginia also got stuck underwater a few times.Conclusion:I haven't even mentioned the things like log sleds being missing and no gates, but I'll call it here. Playing Sons of the Forest, in my opinion, seems ultimately frustrating. The combat has hardly been improved, companions seems to do what they like no matter what (tell Kelvin to stay and he'll end up following you in 20 minutes anyway), guns make things too easy and ammo isn't terribly hard to find, albeit blasting giants with a shotgun is gratifying, a lot more running than the first game, etc etc.I'll still be playing the game, I'll still be enjoying certain moments, but overall I can't recommend it for a while. I don't want to call Endnight liars, or the trailers misleading, but I was under the impression early access at this point meant ironing out bugs, not missing whole features. In fact, I'm pretty sure Endnight said they went EA for bugs specifically, not because there were missing features.PS: Somehow in my first playthrough my friend and I experienced two separate endings. I had Kelvin, Virginia, Timmy and Dad with me, he only had Timmy, Dad, and Kelvin. How is that even possible lol

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving Sons of the Forest a negative review not because the game is bad, but because the game should be further progressed than where it is now based on the development history of the game. If this game was meant to be released a year ago as a full game, one would think it should be much more fleshed out than where it is now. It's hard for me to recommend Sons of the Forest for anyone right now in its current state. The game's scope was either too large for the team to deliver based on the timeline they were looking to hit or it was released about 2 to 3 years too early.While the building and survival aspects of the game is very functional and playable, it does have a lot of problems that needs work. Things like desyncing and duping is a huge problem that can make the game really unplayable.The exploration and story of the game needs to be either expanded upon much more thoroughly or redone entirely. Essentially, exploration in Sons of the Forest is an illusion. It does NOT exist in the way it does in The Forest in that you have a linear path. If you had a map to draw out what is available for you to explore, it would look like a map right out of Final Fantasy X or XIII. You also cannot access the next progression point without a previous key item and you get stopped quite literally at the entrance of any interest point. This is unlike The Forest where you can go into certain cave systems and get locked out of progression deep in that exploration.If you take out all of the walking on the surface of the game and only include the exploration portion of the game involving these caves, there is only about 30 minutes to an hour of content. When I say that this aspect of the game is undercooked, it is extremely undercooked and I feel the team really either needs to redesign what they currently have or rework it in a way to better match what they had in The Forest. As of now, what is available to you should not be released as a final product, it is a massive step backwards. If all you want to do is build a base, you can spend hours on that easily and be quite happy but the game is lacking many of the same building options you had in the original game. Sons of the Forest also has kind of a pseudo grid system that I wish was in the original game, but at the same time, I don't. The game is kind of in a weird in-between state between having a lot of strictness so you can better align your structures, but it also doesn't have enough fluidity to build what you want. You can easily hit the limitations of the building system in both ways and I almost much rather have them go extremely hard in one direction over the other. An example: if you wanted to build a wall flush against mountain side with a weird cliff or slope, the game kinda stops you when it breaks the grids if it clips into the wall. Whereas in The Forest, you had a much more fluid system and you could kind of clip building items into the walls of the game so you can make a much more interesting base without having the game tell you no. I think I would be more okay if the game allowed you to clip an item into an existing surface if there was a connection point for that item to connect to. As of now, if there is any clipping at all, you'll be restricted from placing an item. But I digress. Overall, Sons of the Forest can be enjoyable. But unfortunately, I was more disappointed than not. I'm sure that with time, the game will be great. But compared to The Forest and even Valheim, what's here is really underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: With 45.4 hours plunged into Sons Of The Forest, I've not only embraced survival horror but also discovered an unexpected source of cringe-worthy cuteness: Virginia. And let's not forget about Cool Kelvin.Kelvin, with his laid-back attitude and knack for keeping calm in the face of danger, is like the chilled-out counterpart to Virginia's adorable awkwardness. He's the epitome of cool amidst the chaos, and his presence adds a cringe-worthy level of relaxed charm to every situation.Whether he's cracking jokes in the midst of mutant encounters or effortlessly wielding weapons with his smooth moves, Kelvin's coolness never fails to impress—albeit accompanied by a cringe or two at his cheesy one-liners.Sure, the mutants may be terrifying, and the survival challenges daunting, but Kelvin's chill demeanor makes it all feel manageable. In a world where screams echo through the forest and danger lurks around every corner, he's a reminder to take a deep breath and keep cool under pressure.In conclusion, Sons Of The Forest is a rollercoaster of scares and awkward giggles, and Virginia and Kelvin are the cringe-worthy duo that make it all worth it. After 45.4 hours (and counting), I'm still as terrified (and embarrassingly charmed) as ever, and I can't wait to see what adorable (and cringe-worthy) moments await with Virginia's sweetness and Kelvin's coolness by my side.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the original The Forest for a bunch of hours, I was eager to jump in and have a great time here.  Man, if disappointment was cake I'd have one hell of a cake.I'm sure by the time the game reaches the full release I'll improve on some of the bare-bones feeling of the game, and hopefully improve it all around.  Until then, I'm going to have to step away and play something else.So why'd I stop so soon?AI is miserably awful.  Kelvin might as well be a little mini base destroyer.  At first it sounds awesome to have him assist you in building your base.  Who wouldn't want some assistance in gathering trees or other items?  Well, no idea on how the AI decides what trees to chop down - but nothing beats watching them turn their axe on your almost built log cabin instead of the tree next to it.  Nothing quite so exciting as having your almost built house be felled in a swoop by Kelvin.  Or is it Klevin?  I don't remember, because to me he was the base destroyer.  What else did he do?  Set things on fire.  If I wanted to cook, he wanted to be in the fire.  It was so bad I tried to have him follow me across the island so I could leave him there.  No dice, he got lost about halfway and somehow ended back at my base.Crafting somehow feels like it's taken a step back from the original, making it more cumbersome and annoying to deal with.  The new map, using GPS, is awful and the map making markers(at least early on) requiring the GPS trackers to set up is terrible due to the short number of them found.  Maybe there are more, maybe not. I don't know.Swimming will often leave you wondering why you can't get out of the water, or wondering if you've forgotten how to swim upwards.  Despite your best attempts you just won't do it.Combat is about the same as the original.  The environment is beautiful, and I look forward to eventually coming back to it.. But man, first impression is a solid dose of disappointment.
