_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not like SUPER impressed so far. Visually, yes I definitely am - it's a HUGE improvement from the first game. AI seems to be a lot better too, so I will also give it that. But everything else feels like it has fallen short. I know they're still working on adding more but it's crazy that there's some MAJOR things that have yet to be added/complete. The caves for example, most of them are just small one room with a few crates of supplies because they haven't finished them. The caves were a huge part of the first game and one of my fav aspects. Granted there are a handful that are complete for the story line, but it feels weird and hallow going to the empty ones. Multiplayer has been fairly buggy, like falling through the map as well as getting stuck in a position and not being able to interact with anything - therefor having to reset your game. Which may not be a huge problem, but if you are like me and hadn't saved in awhile - you lose all that progress. Also, if you want to build a treehouse and you plan to keep Kalvin (or Kelvin) around, well be prepared to have one or the other. The man does NOT let you have a treehouse. Breaks it every single time. Also, it's weird how little crafting recipe's there are. I was excited for the improved crafting/building (which it has) but you can barely build anything. Yes you can make whatever house/base you want but if you want to fill it with things? Not much. Can't have giant gardens, can't have gates and you have TWO options for traps. I miss my birthday traps from before. Obviously they (hopefully) are going to be adding all that was in the last game and more - but I am a wee bit bummed by the lack of options. All in all, it's still fairly fun and I don't regret buying it (yet) and am eager for all the updates they plan to have. I will reserve my final judgement for when it is finished. I just absolutely loved the first game (even with all its quirks and jankiness) and waited patiently for this sequel. Obviously this is just my opinion and it's from what I have experienced so everyone's will be different, but just a heads up for all. Take it with a grain of salt. ultimately this game just doesn't feel quite as satisfying as the first. I feel you aren't quite as rewarded for exploring, especially the caves, and building doesn't seem that necessary - unless you want to for fun. You can basically be good with what you have in your inventory and just live out of a tent. Cannibals haven't felt like that much of a threat while on multiplayer - the first game felt like it made it harder and harder every time, whereas this game the threat never gets bigger. Really hoping the updates improve upon these things. As for the game in it's current state - it's fine and has been somewhat fun with others. 30 bucks isn't bad for what it currently offers. if you're on the fence, I would wait for further updates before buying. Otherwise, get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand this an early access title but at it's current state I have to leave this review as NOT recommended overall.Performance issues aside, the game is very fun with friends. Being able to grab a GPS and roam around this larger new map was admittedly alot of fun! It's just a shame that after a few hours you start to notice the same enemy variety over and over as well as when exploring the land it's just a lot of running without actually seeing or finding anything from 20+ min at a time. I haven't tried it on SOLO but I can imagine it being much more difficult and horrifying. The game starts you off with an NPC who helps gather supplies for you and is a nice addition to the gameplay and gives you a nice companion if you are running this SOLO (especially for beginners to the series). However, there were many times when he would either get stuck on a  structure I had built or he would seemingly go out of his way to dismantle any of my previous houses to get materials for my newest build (which is insanely annoying). It got to the point where I had to put him down in order to keep a house standing longer than 1 day. And sadly once he's dead, that's it. As for the rest of the gameplay, I feel the inventory system, building mechanics and combat have been improved from the first in many ways. The inventory is now much cleaner and faster to sort through and use. Gun play still feels janky, but any form of melee feels fun and hits feel weighty. My only issue is the fact you get a GPS with infinite battery and it literally shows where you need to go in order to find clues to finish the story and/or find new weapons/key items to progress. I felt this took away alot of the mystery and exploring that was present in the first game (and also added ALOT more play time to anyone's first playthrough).My only real complaint with these new additions is the crafting mechanics. I was saddened that with this new build mechanic they did ended up removing A TON of blueprints from the original game to sort of force the player to use this new custom building mode (which I am not a fan of personally). It's a bit confusing to get the hang of and it takes alot of trial and error before you truly get the hang of it. I just prefer the simple "plot a blueprint down here and go get the materials needed" type of building and it is nice they brought some of that back, I just wish there was more.When it comes to the story? I haven't 100% gotten to the ending yet in my playthrough, but I have had a few friends already complete it within 8 hours of gameplay....which is INSANE to me compared to the first game which I felt took more around 15 to 20 hours to complete the story on a first run through. From what I can say without spoilers is that the story feels rushed and un-finished in many aspects. I truly hope the devs implement more creatures to find, more cave systems, and maybe more weapons to liven up the combat before it's full release. For my final thoughts I would say that my overall feeling towards Sons of the Forest is disappointment. I have been following the developer updates for this sequel for years and every new peace of info we got made me incredibly excited for its release. However, seeing that it was another early access title immediately made my blood boil. Thank god this isn't a full-priced game at the moment, but it's sad they didn't just wait to release this as a finished game this time around since they had all the player data they could ever need from the first game's 4+ years of early access. This entire experience just feels half-baked and rushed out the door. I do truly hope that Endnight Games can make a comeback and fix all the issues I stated above before the final release because if not...I will have to keep my rating of "not recommended" which I really don't want to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in 18 hours, multiplayer with three friends and our good AI companion Kelvin.Sons of the Forest is a squeal to The Forest, a survival horror game that was really fun and enjoyable, and worked around the genre well. The difference between these games was that The Forest slowly got updates overtime, including an ending to the game when it didn't already have one. SotF being a squeal, means that the team has a basis to work off from, a formula which allows them to improve on after their previous game, which was a success.So whats the main issue here? Well to begin, despite being early access, this game was due to release only in a few weeks. My trust with Endnight Games comes from The Forest, but this does not guarantee that SotF will follow the same path of success TF has. Early Access is not a reason to excuse the multiple issues SotF has, when these issues were resolved in TF.For the survival aspect, this is VERY mixed. On the one hand, free build was fun when it came to building a home. Understanding what and how to use logs in this game felt creative, and it definitely is something Endnight can improve on. This comes at the cost of multiple building options in TF not returning, or being awkward to even use. Walls for example, should have the player feel safe, serving as a barricade. Buildings walls in SotF takes too much time and effort which was done better in TF.There were seasons in the game, winter, which lasted a few days then never came back again. Me and my friends survived 28 days, with winter lasting around like 5 days. Other than that, nothing else, and winter never came back. Either seasons need a bigger impact, or winter needs to allow dis/advantages more, and be more frequent.On a positive note, Kelvin was a very much appreciated addition. His AI was a bit wonky at times, but he's a companion that I loved to have on my journey. He has some bugs, but Endnight has something good with him. He's the best part of the game.Then the story...what happened here? To keep this spoiler free, the game starts off interesting, then feels like it doesn't do enough to justify the ending. The ending can make some sort of sense, but it leaves more questions than answers, and it's not handled very well. This is much more of a "find the information to appreciate the story" type of game, but even knowing some information, the story doesn't work. I will say this, Endnight definitely has something, so that "something" needs to be "compelling".Finally, the bugs. Yes, the game is in Early Access, which is why I find it important to harp on how this games bugs brings the quality down. Some bugs can be fun, like sometimes when you build shelf's, the wood you use won't be consumed. Some ragdoll psychics bugs out to be funny, ok! You know what does suck? Having the host of the server save the game, then starts falling through the floor, FORCING us to cheat just so he could reposition himself on the platform so we could continue on in the game. This is UNACCEPTABLE no matter the game, Early Access or not. A line has to be crossed, and being forced to cheat just to continue with a playthrough crossed it. Alongside that complaint, no Auto Save was the worst, and is a feature that should be at the very LEAST be a toggleable option, and is a QoL feature that is normalized in games nowadays. One of my friends crashed a few times, and lost a lot of progress. Two of my friends clipped right through the floor near the literal end of the game. Me and my friend got animation trapped and were forced to restart, and the result of these occurrences losing a lot of time as a result. Autosave should be a must have due to the bugs in this game.As much as I enjoyed this game, I cannot advise you purchase the game based of what it is now. Sure, its Early Access, and I admit due to Endnight's work on TF, I have some trust that they'll improve on the game. But it's current state, you should only purchase it if you enjoy the limiting building features it has, which sadly, isn't enough to sway my opinion on the game, as much as I enjoyed some buildings aspects.It's not good when I felt relived that the game was over, and my friends who joined me feel the same. I try to understand Early Access and give developers chances due to Early Access, but due to Endnight's history on TF, I do not have enough tolerance to endure the negative aspects of SotF. The positives are there, but the negatives outweigh the positives, even for Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard of Sons Of The Forest, I was unaware that it was a sequel to a previous game. I had no knowledge or experience of this franchise; I was simply enamored by the stunning graphics and the action displayed within the game trailer. I played through and fully beat the game while it was still in Early Access. I recently played through and beat the game in its full release, as well as having played and beaten the first installment of the franchise, The Forest. Comparing these two games, as well as my experience in Early Access, Sons Of The Forest has truly risen to being a vastly superior entry to the franchise. The story and world building has been fleshed out, with cutscenes and items that contain lore throughout the world. As mentioned earlier, the graphics have had a major upgrade. Perhaps what makes this game so entertaining and unique is the addition of the two companions that accompany the player during the game, that being Kelvin and Virginia. They make the world feel less lonely, while also easing the weight of tasks such as harvesting, by helping to gather resources. The cannibals that inhabit the island also are far superior. There are different types, and they even have different facial expressions based on their activity. Each encounter feels different due to the varying types of cannibals. The Forest franchise is very enjoyable and different from most survival games. The franchise blends the horror and the survival genre brilliantly to create an amazing game and experience! I would recommend this game to fans of both genres.

_childDocuments_.review: 10th March 2023: I've not had chance to play this new update, but I will AND I'll update my rating accordingly.Looks nice, played ok, but just like a takeaway it left me unfulfilled.Ultimately it's a disappointing survival experience. Methods for survival are limited - because the sole purpose is to follow the story. Water collector? Gone - got to drink from a stream until you get to a 3D printer (yes, a 3D printer) and even then carry two 3d printed flasks? Nope - apparently that breaks a fundamental law of the universe or something.You can build, yes, but you can't really 'craft' anything. Essential items have to be found through the storyline - for instance, only one shovel has ever been brought on to the island apparently and that selfish bugger who had it took it with him to his demise. How about clawing at the dirt with your bare hands? Nothing that requires a shovel is deeper than 6 inches. Nope. You must get the shovel, lest your podiatrist beats the ever loving crap out of you I guess.Keycards. Think Doom, but over 9 square kilometres. 3 keycards which each open a different area. Again, only one of each on the entire island. Now, that's fine but it's just indicative of the reasoning behind a lot of the 'logic' behind SOTF survival - it is just 'busy' work, for the sake of it ('it' being the e-longlongman-longation of the story). There are buckets, for goodness sake, on the beach when you first spawn in. Can't use them at all, not even to store small rocks or berries (let alone water). Want to store those small stones? Can't drop them - build a set of shelves and carefully store them in neat cairns of 30. I mean, what the hell...If you're coming direct from The Forest you'll probably love it. If you've played anything else in between then you're likely to be very disappointed because like the discoveries that require that shovel, it's all very shallow.They (Endnight) could draw out the survival aspect by allowing a full tier of rudimentary equipment, from diy glue, duct tape, water containers, cooking equipment (to actually cook actual combined meals), stone/scrap metal tools, leather etc that could provide many hours of initial gameplay before you get in to the story - setting up camps at tactical locations around the map as you explore, for example. Not only that, it might also provide some replayability because as it stands, within 10-20 hours the story is over and there's nothing left worth doing and no reason to play again - the story will be the same and so will the limitations. (disclaimer, I have not played multiplayer).My opinion: wait for mod support - if it arrives (modding tools and workshop support) then have at it - the location is superb and empty - ripe for filling. If mods can bring proper survival crafting (gear, food and even more prefabs) then this could be a prime blank canvas. As it stands, unless they're going to revamp the story arc I can't really see what else they're hoping to bring to the table, other than a few fixes, dedicated servers, optimisation, a fricking turtle shell water collector and rafts. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - will no one think of the rafts?!If you want to sling Endnight 30 bucks and it's nothing to you, then by all means do so. If it's going to be a choice between a week of good meals and plain pasta and ketchup then don't. Hell, if it's a choice of another game or this one, then think carefully. If you're still undecided, stick the $30 in a jar, hide it under your bed and find it around September time.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright fun game.Building thing is more interesting than in the older title The Forest because we are more "free" to build like we want and can add/remove part on the fly to change things. Quite a lot of small trick involved when you build.Zipline are easy to use and make moving logs arounds way more easy.Kelvin is fun to have around, giving him order. HE sucks at cutting down tree tho, so when you want to gather logs you want to cut down tree and leave the pickup for him. Just don't forget you are limited by 50 logs pieces of any kind on the ground on the whole map, outside of stored logs.However having a few more option could looks cool, like small stone wall and the like. Right now you build with logs and that's it.Trap are costly unless you keep reloading your save (that respawn the very little amount of material you can find), but you can freeform build spikes by placing a stick on the ground and sharpen it. And it's super cheap & deadly.Sadly, caves aren't as interesting as in The Forest from what I can see. Unlike the previous game you aren't often going in at one entrance and going out somewhere else confused. Probably because of the sizeof the map. And I miss the more confusing inside layout.And we still can't see anything insides caves when you play solo. Most weapon require two hands so it's total pitch dark (100%full dark) in a lot area where you need to fight back mutants that run/jump around all the time super fast. Your only option right now is building line of campfires as you explore the cave and fall back to them as soon as you aggro something. And don't bother with flares, they are only good to throw down in some further area to see how many of them are waiting for you - they don't stay long and barely light their surrounding, with a flickering red light that reflect around.And honestly I really don't see the appeal in this, it's not scary or fun. Building tons of campfire isn't interesting and doesn't feel "right", and staring at a black screen doesn't feel "right" either.However some part of the caves have some small lamp laying around, sometime it's enough.While it sound quite negative I still have some fun playing. If the game was more costly I might have not recommend the game tho. Some more polishing might help a lot but thing like the cave will probably never change.

_childDocuments_.review: Visual Upgrade, Gameplay DowngradeTLDR: Wait for further development or sale (I'd say $10 is a good value for this game in its current state), and don't play without friends. This game would have sucked if I was playing solo, I only had fun because of the shared experience with friends. I'd wait until this game gets fleshed out a bit.1. Enemies stay the same, either too hard in the beginning or way too easy about half way through the game2. Building is kinda pointless when all you need is a tarp and a stick for a tent3. Inventory is a pain, crafting system would benefit from a recipe book and auto-fill items. Who wants to click on your leaves 10 times for a crappy piece of armor that you need ten of. So if you wanted to make 10 leaf armors you would have to click 100 freaking times on a leaf.4. Building on the last point, armor pretty much sucked. I didn't notice a difference between the armor variation. I assumed the bone armor would last longer than leaf armor, or provide more protection, but I think its just cosmetic at this point. That being said, what's the point in the tech armor?5. World is big but empty. Pretty much the world consists of really linear caves (about half that only consist of one room full of junk), copy paste bunkers, 2? points of interest, and crappy cult camps where you re-spawn. There's a cool giant mountain that's pretty useless. Oh and a singular life raft that holds no significance once you explore it.6. Weapon balancing sucks. There was one weapon I found a few hours into my play-through that was clearly the best melee weapon in the game. Why use anything else when your weapons don't break?7. Bows are useless, and you have a VERY loose idea of where you are shooting. Effective out to about 10 meters against standing targets. Side note, I'm not sure I've ever seen a compound bow without sights until this game.8. Gun attachments are hilariously useless. Gun flashlights are worse than the starter lighter. Lasers force you to hip-fire because your stupid character mounts them ON TOP of the gun, blocking your sights. I can't believe there wasn't a red dot sight because why can you mount a laser ON TOP OF YOUR SIGHTS RENDERING THEM USELESS.9. Molotovs felt like they did nothing. Cool they burn for a bit but they're still alive and attacking you. 10. THE SOUND IS HORRIBLY MIXED. Opening your inventory is stupid loud, and don't even get me started on the environment. The wind and rain make you feel like you are in a tornado because of how loud it is. The shotgun is awfully quiet, and pistol suppressors only work on your end. If your buddy shoots a silenced gun, you still hear the loud gunshot. 11. The story is dumb and and the ending is bad. 12. COMBAT. You don't even have to fight. YOU ARE FASTER THAN EVERY SINGLE ENEMY in the game. There are no cultists with bows or ones that throw rocks at you to fight from a distance. Why fight when you can just runaway from every fight.13. Jackets/Outfits don't really serve a point, with the exception of the wet suit which lets you swim faster. When winter rolls around, who needs a jacket when you can just run around with a torch. 14. I played this game on normal difficulty, because I hadn't played the first game in years. WHY DO YOU SPAWN WITH EVERY LOCATION MAPPED OUT ON YOUR GPS? What's the point of exploring when you already know where to go?15. Too many rope spawns. I can't recall outside of the first in game day where I didn't already have the maximum amount of rope I could carry. I swear just about every single box you would search would have rope. I really don't understand what the wait for this game was. For a game announced late 2019, and assuming production started earlier than that, what took so long for this. Its basically just a graphics upgrade and a new map, but with a ton of features removed from the game. Feels more like a crappy DLC than a new game.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands, I would argue this game has less to offer than The Forest. Story-wise, I had no idea what was going on. There was exposure to the story by engaging with the world, which was good, but then you'd have cutscenes with random NPCs that you'd never met before and none of it made sense, and then the end just came out of the blue jarringly and I had no idea what had just happened or that the game had even just ended. I was just left completely confused.The crafting is good, pretty much what you'd expect, but with seemingly much less variety than in the first game. No crafting pouches, quivers, or anything like that. There's only 1 hide (deer hide), and it can only be used to craft an armour that is basically made obsolete by constantly coming across creep armour. You're pretty much discouraged from crafting by always coming across easy food resources that don't require cooking, or by always getting medicine. You can play the game without feeling the need to engage with many of the mechanics because the game is always trying too hard to make sure you have enough of everything.I'm aware that this is early access but I did hope for more at this stage than what was offered, something at least on par with the first game. I wouldn't recommend it currently for anyone looking for an experience on par with the first game. I hope to replay it in a few years and be able to recommend it, especially at the price of £25.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest: A Hauntingly Beautiful Dive into Survival HorrorIntroduction:Sons of the Forest, the highly anticipated sequel to The Forest, brings players back into the unsettling world of survival horror, blending elements of suspense, exploration, and terrifying encounters. As a long-time fan of the horror genre, I eagerly plunged into this eerie wilderness to experience the next chapter in the unsettling narrative crafted by Endnight Games. Here's my detailed review of Sons of the Forest, a game that goes beyond jump scares to deliver an atmospheric and chilling adventure.Graphics and Atmosphere:From the very beginning, Sons of the Forest captivates with its hauntingly beautiful visuals. The forest is rendered with a level of detail that immerses players in its unsettling ambiance. The play of light and shadow, coupled with the dense foliage and eerie weather effects, contributes to an atmosphere that is as atmospheric as it is terrifying.Character models, animations, and environmental details are all meticulously crafted, enhancing the overall sense of realism. The game's lighting design plays a crucial role in creating tension, casting long shadows and illuminating the mysterious creatures that lurk in the darkness. The overall result is an environment that feels genuinely alive, in the most unsettling way possible.Gameplay Mechanics:Sons of the Forest retains the survival mechanics that made The Forest a standout title while introducing new elements that elevate the gameplay experience. The crafting system is robust, allowing players to build elaborate structures for defense or exploration. The sense of vulnerability is palpable as you scavenge for resources, knowing that danger could be lurking around every corner.The introduction of new tools and weapons adds depth to the gameplay. The bow, in particular, becomes a crucial tool for stealth and survival, emphasizing the importance of careful planning and strategic use of resources. The dynamic day-night cycle and weather conditions further add to the unpredictability of the environment, creating a sense of constant tension.Story and Exploration:Sons of the Forest weaves a mysterious and unsettling narrative that unfolds gradually as players explore the island. The game introduces a compelling mix of environmental storytelling, audio logs, and visual cues to piece together the events that led to the current state of the forest. The sense of isolation is heightened by the enigmatic nature of the story, leaving players with a constant desire to uncover the truth behind the horrors they encounter.Exploration is a key component of the experience, with the island offering a variety of environments to discover. From dark caves filled with ominous echoes to abandoned structures that hint at the island's troubled past, each location tells a part of the story while offering new challenges and horrors to face.Horror Elements:Sons of the Forest excels in delivering horror that goes beyond mere jump scares. The game relies on a combination of atmospheric tension, unsettling visuals, and a haunting audio design to create an experience that will leave players on the edge of their seats. The creatures that inhabit the island are both grotesque and terrifying, and encounters with them are pulse-pounding experiences that test your nerves and strategic thinking.The horror elements are not limited to the creatures alone; the game introduces psychological horror elements that play with the player's perception and sanity. The result is an immersive and psychologically intense experience that stays with you long after you've put down the controller.Multiplayer and Cooperative Play:Sons of the Forest introduces a cooperative multiplayer mode, allowing players to team up with friends to face the horrors of the island together. The cooperative experience retains the tension and atmosphere of single-player, while also introducing strategic elements as players work together to survive.The seamless integration of multiplayer into the core experience is a welcome addition, enhancing the replayability and offering a different dynamic to the horror. The shared experience of facing the unknown with friends elevates the emotional impact of the game, creating memorable moments of both terror and triumph.Technical Performance:In terms of technical performance, Sons of the Forest impresses with its polished visuals and smooth gameplay. The game runs smoothly on various hardware configurations, and I encountered minimal bugs or performance issues during my playthrough. The attention to detail in both the visual and audio aspects contributes to a polished and immersive horror experience.Conclusion:Sons of the Forest is a triumph in the survival horror genre, delivering an atmospheric and chilling experience that goes beyond the conventional jump scares. With its hauntingly beautiful visuals, intricate gameplay mechanics, compelling story, and relentless horror elements, Endnight Games has created a title that will linger in the minds of players long after they've left the forest. Whether you're a fan of horror games or simply looking for a truly immersive and unsettling experience, Sons of the Forest is a journey into the unknown that is well worth taking. Brace yourself for a thrilling and terrifying adventure that redefines the standards of survival horror gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: An entirely new experience from the makers of the 'The Forest'. Sent to find a missing billionaire on a remote island, you find yourself in a cannibal-infested hellscape. Craft, build, and struggle to survive, alone or with friends, in this terrifying new open-world survival horror simulator. Experience complete freedom to tackle the world how you want. You decide what you do, where to go and how best to survive. There are no NPC's barking orders at you or giving you missions you don't want to do. You give the orders, you choose what happens next. Enter a world where nowhere is safe and fight against a range of mutated creatures, some who are almost human like, and others who are like nothing you have ever seen before. Armed with pistols, axes, stun batons and more, protect yourself and those you care for. Feel every interaction; Break sticks to make fires. Use an axe to cut out windows and floors. Build a small cabin, or a sea-side compound, the choice is yours. Pluck fresh salmon directly from streams in spring and summer. Collect and store meat for the cold winter months. You're not alone on this island, so as winter rolls in and food and resources become scarce you won't be the only one looking for a meal. Co-op Gameplay - Survive alone, or with friends. Share items and work together to build defenses. Bring back-up to explore above and below ground.

name: Turbo Overkill
detailed_description: ' Turbo Overkill is the best Tony Hawk game in years.' - Fanbyte 'If Sam Raimi's Evil Dead movie made the Chainsaw Arm an iconic piece of weaponry, wait till you see the leg chainsaw.' - Sportskeeda 'Turbo Overkill isn't just one of the best boomer shooters on the market right now - this is one of the best games on the market, full stop.' - Superjumpmagazine Half-metal, half-human, all murder machine Heavily inspired by some of the all-time greats like Id's Doom & Quake , and Apogee's Duke Nukem 3D , with stunning cyberpunk visuals, Turbo Overkill is the most savage FPS ever released by Apogee. You play as Johnny Turbo, augmented with hidden arm rockets and a chainsaw that extends from your lower leg allowing you to slide-slice enemies wide open. In this Blade Runner -meets- DOOM hellscape, Johnny returns to his hometown of Paradise and finds its entire population possessed by Syn, a rogue AI, and its army of augmented minions. Desperate for enough money to outrun his past mistakes, Johnny takes on the impossible job of destroying the greatest AI ever created. Rival bounty hunters want to claim the prize first. Nothing is easy in paradise. Turbo Time, wall-running, dashing and grappling hooks, oh my Turbo Overkill takes over-the-top to never-before-reached heights. Activate Turbo Time(™), a new form of slow motion with a twist. Build incredible speed by wall-running and dashing. Slide on your chainsaw leg, eviscerating foes and opening up bosses for critical damage, and go car-surfing on the hoods of flying cars. Blast away with the Twin Magnums, which lock-on and instagib several foes, the Boomer Shotgun and its attached grenade launcher, or the Telefragger sniper rifle, which teleports Johnny inside an enemy before they explode from within. Race through two dozen stages packed with secrets, bonus arena stages, and white-knuckle combat puzzles. Find game-changing collectibles to unlock punishing modifiers like triple-monster-speed and insta-kill. Combine all of Johnny’s weapons and powers to outsmart, outgun and outrun the corrupted legions. TL;DR: o Kill a boss, get its augment (special power) o Play Spider-Man with your grappling hook o One-up Duke Nukem with your chainsaw slide-slice kick o Kills = cash. Use cash to install augments, upgrade your weapons, and add new abilities in your talent tree o Be a ghost runner while wall running o Attack from above riding the hood of your flying car like a kung-furious badass o Mini-rockets built into your robotic arm? ✔ o This. List. Will. Grow. Wishlist the game to see it happen Don't quote us on nuthin' “ Turbo Overkill is fast, frenetic and ferocious—excess personified,” said Sam Prebble, one half of Trigger Happy Interactive. “This is the game we’ve always wanted to play; making it is a dream project. Relentless enemies, extremely deadly and fun weapons, speed and precision above all else—if you love Quake III Arena , modern and classic DOOM , or Apogee’s legendary first-person shooters, you’ll feel right at home in Paradise.” “As the guy who helped launch the shooter genre with Wolfenstein 3D , Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem 3D, Max Payne , and Prey , I haven’t been this excited about an FPS since the golden era of Apogee/3D Realms,” wrote Scott Miller, founder. “ Turbo Overkill is a sandbox of fun and original gameplay ideas that come together like a night of melty hot pizza and your favorite cold, frothy brew. Playing this game made me a Turbo Lover all over again.”

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, fun fast paced pumping action, really awesome visuals with an interesting aesthetic. The attitude of the game and the tightness of the controls make it fun to play both narratively and through gameplay. Most shooters in the genre are focused on bringing back the feel of other games, where Turbo Overkill certainly stands strong on its own two legs.Also big ups for the demo, it ended up convincing me that this was a great title to pickup and support while in development. More games need demos!

_childDocuments_.review: If you love first person shooters, buy this game. No need to even think about it. The gameplay is 10/10. The graphics are 10/10. I played almost to the end of the game with it on its lowest settings, and really appreciated the artstyle and retro feel. Then, I realised I'd been playing on the lowest settings and turned it onto the highest and was blown away. This game is simply gorgeous. The sounds are 10/10. The voice acting is fantastic, the weapons sound beefy, the soundtrack gets the heart racing. The story is 10/10. It'll make you laugh, it'll make you cry, it'll change your life. Just buy this game already. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in early access, its one of the better shooters I've played in the last few years. Feels like the perfect blend of boomer shooter and modern, taking from games like Doom Eternal with fast and fluid movement and ultrakill with its pixelated aesthetic. Sick music carries you through all the ultra violence as well, dynamically changing from a more subdued sound during exploration to the heavy beats during combat. Its also hard, even on the normal 'regular joe' difficulty, but not unfairly so. It simply demands that you learn its mechanics and use them to your advantage. 8 base levels make up the chapter currently available, with two more chapters on the way. However, there are secret levels to be unlocked based on the collectibles (tapes) found in each level, for those of you out there who like such things. Other collectibles (chips) unlock modifiers which can be enabled on all other levels, such as one which adds a big head mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I had very high expectations for  as I've seen it appear on many "Best of 2023"-lists. And while it starts off very strong, taking a page out of the new wave of Boomer Shooters reminiscent of DOOM 2016/Eternal, it does unfortunately fumble the ball and severely outstays its welcome.Episode three just becomes a constant slog of the same encounters spammed over and over again complete with a boss rush sequence at the end as well. By the time I was done, clocking in fifteen(!?) hours on the highest difficulty, I was completely drained. After the credits rolled and seeing the other modes offered in the main menu I just couldn't fathom why anyone would want to bother with the Endless or Arcade options. It's far from  mind you and does plenty of good such as the frenetic combat itself, the epic synth-wave soundtrack or being able to upgrade Johnny Turbo's abilities to your own liking and playstyle. Sadly though the positives are buried beneath far too much fat that  needed trimming. And while I understand its odd to complain about there being 'too much content' I feel like a snappy retro FPS like this could've been much more enjoyable at half its length. I would even go so far as to say it would  its replayability if it was shorter. However even some of the levels themselves just drag on and on and I shudder the thought of having to go through all of it again just to uncover the remaining collectibles. Its core mechanics are certainly fine and when you're chainsaw sliding into multiple enemies right into a jump pad and unleashing an auto-missile barrage at the height of your jump in slow motion, seeing enemies below explode in a mess of gibs and health drops before grapple-hooking into another foe on the periphery of your vision it definitely hits that endorphin rush. That said when all the chaos unfolds even the visuals themselves can become an assault on the eyes what with the exaggerated cyberpunk aesthetic and areas where the colourspace devolves into a saturated fluorescent mess. It all adds to the feeling of exhaustion which makes this game difficult to recommend. Ultimately  is a prime example of "too much of a good thing" and dilutes its own experience by artificially padding its length. So get it cheap, play the first episode and then decide if you want to stick with it. According to the achievement completion rate many of its most vocal fans certainly haven't...
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best modern shooter you can find. Certainly has the best movement in an FPS I've ever experienced. Double jump, triple jump, sliding with a chainsaw that deals damage to enemies, sliding midair, wall-jumping, wall-running, grapple hook onto environments and onto enemies, rocket and shotgun jumping, and using a sniper rifle that teleport you to enemies. This game has is it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ all. Levels beside being well designed, have all these gorgeous backdrops and vistas to look at, and progressively get more aesthetically absurd and just insane to play. They're also populated by an incredibly diverse set of enemies and mixed with both challenging arenas and just fun enemy encounters. Even the bosses are great and memorable, and all the weaponry you find feel sooo good to use.Great game and a guaranteed good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: The Boomer Shooter Genre has had a lot of entries in the last few years since Dusk came out on the scene in 2018. This game is definitely a worthwhile addition to the genre especially when the devs are so kind to just sell it for less than $20. The weapons feel great, the levels are huge, and the art design is pretty damn great. This feels like a genuine work of love and I'm excited to see how this game shapes up before full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I barely understand why people keep calling this a "retro shooter". Does this look like Quake or Duke Nukem to anyone? If you travelled back to 1996 and showed Turbo Overkill to someone who had  just got done slaying Shubb-Niggurath, they'd either keel over dead from shock or think it was a greater technical marvel than the time machine you just pulled up in. Understand I'm not criticising Quake or Duke Nukem, I just want to make the point that this game's no throwback; it's bleeding edge stuff.The game's got loads of, for want of a better word, gimmicky mechanics.  But the incredible thing about them is that they're all useful. Grappling on rockets, grabbing enemy missiles with the plasma rifle alt-fire, telefragging with the telefragger, the chainsaw leg, of course, are all usually one possible answer to any problem. Moreover it's all incredible fun that I only stop playing because it's so intense.I could wax lyrical about this game for much longer than I have already, but I'm quite tired and I can't recall ever reading a Steam review that was over three paragraphs long myself, so I'd be hypocrite to ask others to do so. Wholehearted recommendation for Turbo Overkill from me, it's a wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an advocate for players who love fast movement and combat. You can move at lightning fast speed at will. You can combine weapons and mods to your hearts desire on a canvas of enemies and arenas that let you express yourself through speed and gunplay as simple or creative as you want it to be. There are mods that push your abilities to the next level, and the graphics and art style are a love letter to the cyberpunk genre. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: We live in a time when small studios can make masterpieces using free game engines and when high-budget large studios just stagnating and make crappy copy-pasted games every year. Turbo overkill is great example of cool action game that shows that games must be about fun and gameplay, and graphics with other stuff are secondary. Turbo overkill just delivering to you a LOT of fun and gore action in low-poly, but, nevertheless, stylish graphics. Level design is good, platforming is breathtaking and sometimes a little annoying) This game gives you exactly the experience you are expecting. And difficulty settings are very ajustable. You can lower it through your run if you like to, but actually I like it playing on high difficulty. At the same time, the highest difficulty settings (last option), in my opinion, is for mazohists or tryhards only. So if you do not like to die and restart every 30 seconds - select something less challenging.UPD. Just finished the game. I can tell you that I literally hated some levels and wanted to change my review to negative very badly. When you think that they can not make your playthrough harder - you are wrong - they can. Sometimes it became just ridiculous. At the end I cached a game-breaking bug and have to restart level because of that (it broken the checkpoint so necessary event was not triggered). Final battle (I used only infinite ammo modifier and only at final levels) was so hard that I maybe restarted it 50+ times. I can not believe that I managed to beat the game at Serve Me Pain difficulty. After all, it is still very good game and it was worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible high octane, balls through the wall, hoverbike riding, chainsaw sliding, rocket launching, secret level unlocking, orbital bombardment having, funny as hell boomer shooter with a an ost full of absolute banger after absolute banger, and a surprisingly engaging story for what it is. It's not perfect, the final couple levels drag on a bit too long, and I kind of wish there was another difficulty preset in between 2 and 3 (skill issue I know but there we're a couple moments in the third act that felt a bit too punishing for my taste, but then I switch it down to 2 and it's too easy). Still, this is one of the best boom shoots on the market and if you're a fan of the genre this is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid 7/10 game. It has a solid story, and I especially liked the "dialogue" in the thrid chapter. The music is enjoyable and the visuals are fine too except for  human animations in cut scenes.Now to the gameplay. For the most part, it's good. You have a wide range of wepons with alternative firing modes, even some parts where you fight in vehicles. But there are issues. Two of the weapons IMO are complete garbage: the minigun, which is just completely outclassed by the double ARs/MPs and the double barreled shot gun, which does deal decent damage but its reload makes it unplayable in most situations; and its secondary fire is just bad. Another thing that was very annoying, is the enemies damage output. There are some attacks that can 100 to 0 and you will be like ??? what ??? In tight arenas where you have to dodge a lot of stuff you will sometimes end up infront of strong enemies and exactly that can happen -- you instantly die.There were only a few bugs I encountered, the most comon one was getting stuck somewhere after a chainsaw slide. The only game breaking bug was in the last level just before the last boss, I jumped of some lift and then found a secret which caused an autosave. I could not get up to the boss arena without noclip cheating.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, after 4 hours, I think I have to throw in the towel on this mostly excellent boomer shooter. It was a good ride.The good:The guns.That brutal slidekick mechanic.The cyberpunk vibe.The dark synth soundtrack.Smooth performance. Will likely run on a potato.Difficulty levels.The meh:The upgrades. A bit stingy, to be honest. It's depressing seeing so many vending machines that allow you to affix upgrades, while getting so few upgrades to actually affix.The precision platforming.  I got stuck bouncing over and over again trying to get to this ledge and then finally I somehow made it! - but then didn't know where to go, made a wrong jump and then couldn't make it again.  After 15 some minutes, of bouncing like an idiot on a launchpad in a section that really shouldn't be that punishing, I called it quits.Also, the levels can be quite large and can sometimes be confusing.The verdict: It's a great homage to shooters of old. But if you don't like very challenging platforming sections, be warned. Even on the easiest difficulty, you'll have to deal with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Chaotic and fun I played on street cleaner difficultyEach episode improves a lot on the previous, I wasn't too impressed with the game on the first episode but as you go through the second the game becomes great and keeps going up from there.Sometimes it's a little TOO chaotic enemies can 1 shot you very quickly some of the platforming is kinda lame and most bosses aren't too impressive but aside from that and frequent minor glitches the game is an easy recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: If you like (2016) Doom and Doom Eternal, you will love this game. Combat has that same feel of managing your weapons (ammo and which is most suitable for a target) and managing your risk with distance. Distance management comes in two parts like Doom, the first being that some weapons are better at close-range while others are longer-range. The second part is replacing Doom's glory-kill system with a chainsaw leg which allows you to slide through enemies to deal damage.Upgrades are pretty good for weapons and you as you can feel the difference as your body has limited slots for personal mods, making your choices have an impact. The level designs are also very clear and each episode is unique. My only real disappointment would have to be that by the time I reached halfway through the last episode (Episode 3) I had run out of things to buy with all my money. This is a bit of my own fault as I used a mod to collect all money when they drop and another to make things cheaper as soon as I could. I believe the upgrades and mods would likely have been paced adequately otherwise. Great pacing and doesn't take itself too seriously while still having a solid identity and themes. Very nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute recommendation , Turbo Overkill is one of the finest examples of indie games done right. There is barely anything i don't love about this game. Its a nice shooter platformer, a great action game and one of the best boomer shooters ever made. The action and combat is super fast, very enjoyable, challenging and overall just really fun. It has a retro aesthetic while maintaining a modern looking design, the level design is just superb. Nothing but praise, I just love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced action, and filled to the brim with charm and love for the genre. The game features an outstanding soundtrack, and an incredible arsenal of weapons, each of which is super fun and satisfying to play around with. The only criticism I would have is that the game goes on a little long, as some levels can go from 30-40 minutes each in playtime, but that isn't to say I didn't enjoy the ride the whole way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal shooter which does a fantastic job adding in new and surprising elements. Level design is top notch, sound design is excellent, visuals are some of the best in this genre; only complaint is that some of the weapons can feel slightly underwhelming. I'm thinking of the pump action shotgun specifically which lacks substantial sound design and feedback as a result. Small gripe, but became apparent through playing. Absolutely adore the game, fun and pithee, a joy to play!EDIT: 1.0 full release here, AMAZING! 10/10. I love this game, it's got to be one of the best shooters of the last 10 years. It's solid in every way. Just finished the game and am ready to do a full playthrough again. Only game in recent memory that I've had that feeling with was CULTIC.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: A hesitant recommend. Probably more of a "mixed" review. This game had me at having a chainsaw leg, and there were alot of positives, but I will start off with the negatives, because this game had quite a few in my opinion, and I feel like these will be the most helpful to discuss.Turbo Overkill is brutally difficult at certain points, and some sections are agonizingly long. A few of the boss battles will have multiple stages, and some rooms will have multiple rounds of spawning enemies. When you think you are done and free to leave the room, the game is like, "But wait, there's more!" It just makes the game very exhausting. I thought Doom Eternal was tiring, but it at least knew to not waste your time as much as this game. I even reached a point while playing this where I was skipping past entire areas of enemies because I didn't feel like wasting time or ammo.Alot of the enemies take forever to kill, and many of them, in my opinion, were quite annoying to deal with. The drones only being able to be killed from above, the electric enemies, and the homing missile ones... The levels in general feel like they take forever to complete. In the last third of the game, it was taking me close to 30 minutes per level. It doesn't help that their layout can be confusing (there's no map), and the game only sometimes gives you waypoints. For someone like me that does not have much spare time, I didn't appreciate this.The thing that made me almost stop playing the game is how I kept accidentally locking the game from progressing on the last level, so I had to complete the beginning of the level at least 3 times before resorting to mods because I lost my patience.- the Destiny-like U.I. where you have to drag the cursor to select things in certain menus. Dear Game Developers: please stop doing this menu design. It's a time waster.- Some of the audio logs are very long. Thankfully you can close them out if you don't feel like listening to them, but there were a few where I was like "Man, they're still talking?"- No punctuation at the end of alot of subtitles for dialogue.- Definitely is a bit too inspired by Doom, specifically Doom Eternal, especially the HUD with switching weapons, the sound of things being done recharging, as well as the level design in some ways. There are keys you have to collect to progress sometimes, and there's an alternate fire for every weapon.>> On Doom, you have VEGA. On this game, you have SAMM (whose voice actor is not as pleasant to listen to).>> Late in the game, like in Doom Eternal >> The game could have done more to differentiate itself as something new."Wow, that's alot of bad," you might be saying, "Did you mean to leave this as a 'not recommended'?" (I look at how long my dislikes section is) Well... I do still like the game overall. I just won't play it again. Some things I like...The chainsaw leg was very fun to use. Sliding around with it, having lots of floors that are conveniently slanted to use it. The speed at which you move without sliding feels good too, and I don't feel like I'm going too slow. One thing that Turbo Overkill didn't take from Doom is not having a BFG9000 equivalent. Instead you have the Ion Cannon, which feels very different, and is very fun to use. I do like the story overall, I just wish there was more of it in the game, and that it was more in-depth. While Johnny has an interesting background that I wish was explored more, Maw was definitely the most intriguing character for me, and I am always drawn to arcs where . The cutscenes with action in them are very impressive in my opinion, and are very "creative" with their violence. Some of the level designs are "eh", but the more cyberpunk-looking ones are very cool in my opinion. The music is hit or miss for me, but there's a few tracks that I like as well.I guess in the end, this is a borderline recommend. If they do end up making a sequel for this, I will definitely consider trying it. I just won't be playing this again. Way too exhausting.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best retro-style shooter released this year, but it has its caveats. Its gameplay flow has more in common with Doom Eternal than something like DUSK, which you may have seen from other reviews, but it does have enough retro elements with its level design to somewhat warrant the label of "boomer shooter", particularly in the earlier levels. Weapons and upgrades are doled out at a brisk pace, so there's always a sense of progression and becoming more powerful. Your chainsaw leg is available from the get-go, however, and it is by far one of the most enjoyable aspects of the game. The story is...there. It's not particularly strong, but you're probably not coming to a game called Turbo Overkill for writing on par with God of War. It does become surprisingly prevalent in the second episode, and Gianni shows up, as is mandated by his eldritch contract to appear in all retro shooters, but it more or less serves as a backdrop to take you on your various fits of extreme violence. My main grievances with the game lie with the pacing of the last three levels, particularly the third to last and second to last. Throughout most of the game, the pacing of the level and encounter design maintains a delicate balance between providing unique scenarios that start out bonkers and escalate to really f***ing bonkers while knowing not to overstay their welcome. A mech section towards the middle of episode 3 is a standout moment. But the last three levels are long. Much longer than the rest of the game. By the time I was halfway through the third to last episode I was ready for the game to be over, but it gets dragged on longer than it needs to. The second to last level is a boss fight, and I found it to be quite enjoyable and paced just right. Until it had another phase. And then another. I won't go into specifics due to spoilers, but a specific weapon is needed to permanently damage it, and I found the method required to be finicky at best, and didn't always work when it was supposed to. Those two levels are really where most of my problems lie with the game, and only because they aren't as markedly excellent as the rest. Overall, Turbo Overkill has enough style and substance for any modern retro shooter, and it's impressive that such a small team could make something so meaty. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is absolutely insane for what it is. I tried the demo and let me just say, I instantly fell in love. I have never been more satisfied with a game purchase in my life. It's a mix of all the games I adore. If you're a huge fan of DOOM, Ultrakill, & Cruelty Squad, need I say more? This fast-paced shooter will most definitely stimulate the ♥♥♥♥ out of your brain. The soundtrack is a BANGER too so don't miss out. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe how frenetic this game gets even in earlier levels. The combat is amazing, all weapons have such good synergy, this is a badass simulator through and through. I have no clue how my brain is capable of understanding and reacting to everything on the screen, but the feeling I get is beyond amazing, can't wait for the full release even if it's just more content, as it stands the game is already well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: There is a very convincing free demo which will show you the core features. This made me buy it shortly after i finished the first level there, after i browsed through the settings, after i was able to rebind every key how i like it, after i snapped into the atmosphere of the game from the first nanosecond. I dont regret the purchase and i think this product should have a higher prize. The purchased version had even more options: An FPS limiter, 2 more keys to rebind, enhanced cutscenes, of course more weapons and augments, every level had a secret level and there were level modifiers to collect...It is an awesome product and the demo is worth looking into.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic retro-graphics movement-focused FPS, that lasts maybe three or so levels too long, which is apparent by the completion achievements. There are some stellar and memorable levels in the game, including a couple at the very end, but you'll be feeling that new enemies aren't really introducing changes to the gameplay loop anymore by the middle of episode 2. Running from enemies in these arenas is easy enough, so you can usually avoid their mechanics, intentionally or not, by just running in a big circle around the edges and prioritizing your targets from big to small. It's still a great game though, and I'd wholeheartedly recommend it even if you wouldn't end up finishing it. It absolutely deserves a spot among the best of the throwback FPSs released in the past decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Easily a 10/10 game. An immediate must buy.-The weapon balance throughout the campaign is extremely well managed. -The enemies are varied and interesting to fight. -The arenas are varied and never overstay their welcome. -The bosses are actually fun to fight in an fps.-The movement is incredibly satisfying-There aren't any shoehorned political agendas.-The characters are fun, sometimes humorous but never annoying.      All things considered, it may be the best fps I've ever played. It's certainly in the top 3. I eagerly await what the developer does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "modern retro" FPS games I've played so far. The game is not holding back and gives you all the tools to go completely berserk. Movement is extremely fast and smooth, you're jumping, dashing and zooming through the level, if not slashing through lines of enemies with your chainsaw leg.Levels are nice and varied, ranging from tight corridors to open futuristic cityscapes. Enemies are not that much of a challenge on their own, although there are some tankier ones. It's the arena style battles that can get pretty challenging, where hordes of enemies come at you in different formations.The guns are nice although the double barreled shotgun feels a bit useless compared to the other guns and the rocket launcher is pretty clunky. It generally does not really matter which gun you use, which means you can take every fight the way you want. A little more game design could have been put into that, as in the new Doom games. It's still a lot of fun to wreak havoc with this arsenal.It's clear the developers don't take the game too seriously and want to deliver the most wacky, fun experience they can. I think they succeeded at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This is less an in depth review, more a reaction after one playthrough of the EA version.Turbo Overkill is absurd! There have been some really great FPS titles released in the past 2 years that have capitalised on the return of the old school shooter. Some great, some not so great, and then there is Turbo Overkill. This is potentially better than Dusk in the long term if the devs do not soil the bed mid way through development. Think an almost perfect mix of Doom Eternal minus the complexity, and Ultrakill minus the boxy, arena focused level design. It moves well, the shooting is fun, the levels are a joy to explore and it has a superb sense of place.The only real criticisms I have of the version put out thus far is the later levels are not as well signposted as they could be, plus they suffer from a degree of visual overload which can make a certain platforming section over a speeding highway seem too much. Aside from that there are some bugs that cause visual artifacting / you can see through some walls and there is the fact some enemies can shoot through walls.Bar that, stick this on the Wishlist asap. This should be, if all goes well, a top 3 game in the mass of all the mass throng of old-school shooters that have appeared over the past 5 years.UPDATE: I've just played chapter 2 and I am amending my prior statement that this is a top 3 game. Bar Ultrakill, this is the best FPS game released in the past 5 years. It is not flawless as some of the more interesting spectacles like the motorbike section are a bit wonky, plus there are still some bugs with the level design, but the general way that Turbo Overkill plays out is so top tier that I cannot recomend it enough! As usual, wait for the EA period to end, but once it is out in full, get this asap!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: i thought this was going to be another run of the mill boomer shooter but this is THE boomer shooter mixing the fluidity of the modern with the style and substance of the past the traversal and arena style of doom eternal with a killer story with a mix of hit scan and projectile based enemies allowing you to skilfully bullet dodge like the the 90's shooters we all love a sleek visual style dripping with neon awesomeness reminding you of something like blade runner or akira (cyberpunk) some of the dialogue is a tad immature very borderlands 2, DMC but it kinda fits as your running around killing people as a cyborg with a chain saw leg and flipping off cyber street punks music is amazing and voice acting is kick ass so enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never write reviews. In fact, I think this might be my first one, but I'm not sure. I absolutely wanted to support this game, as it completely blew me away. This is one of the best shooters I've ever played, up there with Doom Eternal. The pacing is amazing, the weapons feel and sound perfect, they constantly add new elements to the gameplay, the soundtrack is superb and the game looks fantastic. If you're into shooters, I'd advise you to give the demo a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Old school FPS in a cyberpunk world. Wall running, jump pad, car shooting, chainsaw slides... Great game!Turbo Overkill set a high standard retro FPS should be. If you are familiar with classic 90s FPS you won't find this game a stranger. Game offers regular firearms from pistol to dual machine gun to rocket launcher, and part of the player character's body for melee weapons, a chainsaw on the biotic leg is extremely convenient, slide to use it and the faster you run the more damage it does. In each level there are vendor machines for ammo and upgrades, similar to Cyberpunk 2077 you can insert chips to each limb for boosts. My favorite is to gain 6HP for every enemy you kill by the chainsaw, this quickly turned the game into a racing game. There are more chip options like extra wall jump, higher damage, but when I finish the game I do not find chips for head and left arm, maybe more for future development. Like the Doom games, hidden collectables (tapes and chips) scatter everywhere, well hidden and fun to find. It is said to find all to unlock secret levels, I haven't done that yet but would love to in the 2nd run. Colored keys for colored doors, but with no map  offered and no way point occasionally I lost my way, a way point is given only when you are on the right path sometimes. Each level contains a relatively big map with many floors, players will revisit places so it can be confusing. I only assume enter a place with prawn enemies is the right way.Level design is great. Map is complicated and allows the player to explore almost everywhere. It is nice, I feel like I'm off the map some time but eventually know it is supposed to be this way, players are given more freedom to move around in combat.5 difficulties and I choose the 3rd - Hard mode. I play FPS often and know what to expect, I read it gives enemies x1.3 speed and x1.5 damage output, after beating the game this is exactly the challenge I want and not too overwhelming. A bit hard at the beginning but once you know the game it is fun - keep moving and dodge bullets, control your position in the air!Another thing worth mentioning is the action part. Double jump + up to 2 wall jumps +dash + ladder grabbing turns this FPS into a challenging ACT game. I LOVE games to test my controls of jumps and landing, this game is so right for me. In two maps I do long and precise jumps (one in the chamber with chainsaws and the other one on top of cars next to a moving train) so challenging I thought I was on the wrong path. So rewarding just to beat the level.I finished in 7 hours, I cannot wait for future levels, card drop and achievements. 10/10 recommend at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Really is engaging in numerous ways. Level design is quite clever and maps, enemies and weapons are all very good. The best thing about this game is the variety in the maps and the size of the game is very good also with many levels to complete, each one getting more difficult. Overall the game is a lot of fun and just what shooter fans would love.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Part boom shoot, part character action FPS, this is the cream of the crop of the retro shooter genre. The gang's all here: incidental combat, lock-in arena fights, exquisite level design, an appropriate(ly cheesy) OST, and a story line that gradually matures past the usual drivel over the length of the campaign. You don't  get a super shotgun, you get a super shotgun with a grenade launcher. You don't  get a railgun, you get a railgun that can telefrag people on command. And most importantly you don't  get a chainsaw, you get a chainsaw for each limb. Turbo Overkill lives up to its name for better and worse. It's balls to the wall action from start to finish, but the finish line is about an hour or two past where it needs to be. Even so, it is well worth your time and money. You'd be doing a disservice to yourself as an FPS fan if you don't play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely insanity, literally one of the best games I've ever played. I never even thought it could be possible to have such a fluid motion while gaming; this really exerts everything from me. After 20 minutes of playing my hands almost hurt because I'm strafing, dashing, aiming and jumping so hard. It's soooo much fun!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: First I gave it a negative rating: the game is very nice and fun playing(chainsaw leg, alternate pistol-fire, smooth movement, quick save, fragfest), but in the 5th mission I suddenly lost all my savegames; usually I wouldn't start over again, but I did this time, speedrunning through the missions I already knew. The only con was that savegame issue( besides, some saves are not accurate)
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Heartily recommend this one. I didn't feel so at the beginning, it starts off pretty slow in a generic cyberpunk theme that I didn't really care too much for. It did have memorable levels and the gameplay was alright enough to keep going. However Episode 2 is where the game really comes together, the difference with the previous episode is like night and day. By this point the gameplay starts to be quite similar to nu-Doom (think lots of fast-paced fights in arenas with tons of movement options and plenty of verticality). Might not be for everyone but I loved it. Some amazing songs in the soundtrack start to pop up as well. I did see high praises for its pacing, I don't know if I really see it that way as it is *mostly* arena fights for the remainder of the game, with the occasional (well done!) vehicle section. But I can't complain.I think towards the middle of Episode 3 the game starts to run out of steam a little bit. It does manage to have bombastic set pieces in this episode but the gameplay loop itself stops throwing new elements in the mix by this point. It is compensated by a terrific penultimate level priming you for the final battles to come.FPS fans and certainly those who liked Doom 2016 or Eternal will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game, but either I'm really unlucky or it has A TON of soft-locks, doors and scenes not triggering etc.When it is fixed certainly a recommendation, but it's so frustrating being stuck multiple times, then looking up a video and seeing something has just not triggered :(Edit: Also, given up at the Maw fight. Why the ♥♥♥♥ would you put checkpoints BEFORE cut scenes?!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: So, so, so good. The gameplay is smooth, the guns feel great, the movement is fluid. I have not dumped this much time into a game over such a short time for a while. Every weapon has it's place and doesn't feel underutilised. The music, graphics and gameplay add up to be my new favourite shooter.However, I do have a couple of issues:It is incredibly easy to skip cutscenes accidentally.
