_childDocuments_.review: I have slowly played this game over the last few months, playing a few levels then taking a break just to keep it fresh. I was enjoying it a lot until Chapter 3. The gameplay itself is wonderful, good movement, forgiving platforming and solid shooting. Your compatrion S.A.M.M. is solid, and the ultimate evil is decent. The reason why this isn't a positive review is simply off of the ending of the game. The last 2 levels are simply just a test of how long you can hold down your finger on a trigger and avoid damage. You have to kill the second to the last boss in 3 separate rooms, the first two times you have to drain his health bar 5 separate times, followed by a tank version at the end with a massive health bar. While just shooting a boss and dodging bullets would be a fair fight, you end up having wave, after wave of enemies to deal with before you can deal more damage to the boss. The final boss is worse, there is no health bar, you are perpetually swarmed by enemies, and this is after you have had a 4 timed arenas that are incredibly obnoxious and laid out poorly. I attempted the final boss many times before I gave up after the transformation. This game had so much potential, and turned into simply a button mashing bullet hell, almost as if the devs ran out of solid ideas to finish the game. I doubt I will go back and try and finish the final boss again, it was annoying and frustrating just to get there, and to continue to reset at the beginning of the fight, after the previous boss would allow you to reset whenever he lost a health bar is brutal. Sometimes, you can finish a shooting game without it being abusive to the player with how much they have to do to simply finish it. What is the point of selecting difficulty levels when the end of the game is just a slog to kill everyone and spend an eternity fighting bosses without health bars?

_childDocuments_.review: The gist: One hell of a wild ride, but not without some problems.The pros:-The presentation is one of the best I've seen in a shooter. Bright, popping colors, an absolutely killer soundtrack, and some breathtaking setpieces and cutscenes make it a treat to watch.-The game loves to one-up itself again and again with the upgrades. Your killsat gun turns into a nuke. Your shotgun turns into a long-range sniper rifle. You go from one chainsaw leg, to having every single limb be chainsaws. Even your pistols turn into damage-dealing monsters that work great with the bullet time powerup.-The vehicles (for the handful of segments they're used) feel genuinely powerful rather than a forced gimping, usually with powerful machineguns, regenerating health, and a very strong secondary weapon on a rather short cooldown.-Most boomshoots have one or two secret levels for every batch of levels. Turbo Overkill has a secret level for EVERY level, giving you a lot to do even without specific completion points.-The voice work is stellar, barring maybe the Teratek Executive getting rather grating.-Johnny is already a highly mobile character at the start, with a fast running speed, dashes, a fast slide-kick, and double jumps. But by the end game, you'll have more movement options than you know what to do with.-The skill ceiling for how the weapons and movement pair together is absolutely insane.-E2M8.The cons:-The weapon balance gets kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the endgame. The chainsaw gets so powerful you're gimping yourself by actually shooting anything less than a Leaper, and the single assault rifle is insanely powerful for how plain it is - accurate at longer ranges, lots of damage per shot, and a ton of ammo basically makes the plasma gun obsolete. (It doesn't help that I couldn't seem to figure out how to get the projectile catcher to work - skill issue on my part?)-Levels are long, especially if you're going for completion. For most of the game it's negligible thanks to the wonderful set design and movement, but episode 3's levels in particular can be real slugfests with waves upon waves of spongy enemies; and the later levels have enemy counts that push towards 1,000. It feels less like a test of skill and mastery, and more a test of endurance.-E3M7.The overall package is wonderful enough for me to recommend it, and I consider it an S-tier boomshoot up there with the likes of Dusk for its energy, presentation, and its total embrace of over-the-top carnage that a game called "Turbo Overkill" ought to deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: A Dazzling Fusion of Cyberpunk Chaos and Hilarious Mayhem.Turbo Overkill seamlessly blends the adrenaline-pumping chaos of cyberpunk aesthetics with healthy does of side-splitting humor. This game is a masterclass in delivering non-stop action and explosive gameplay. From the beginning of the game to the very end, Turbo Overkill thrusts players into a world where bullets fly as fast as the witty one-liners and cutscenes. The game's humorous undertones are woven into the fabric of the experience, adding an extra layer of enjoyment to the already exhilarating gameplay. Turbo Overkill keeps the fun every single second of the playthrough. The level design is a standout feature, offering a rollercoaster of never-ending changes that keeps the player engaged. The narrative takes on twists and turns with amazing boss fights and challenges. Visually, Turbo Overkill's graphic style is really cool. The cyberpunk aesthetic is executed with precision, immersing players in a vibrant, dystopian world filled with neon lights and futuristic landscapes. The music perfectly complements the fast-paced action. Turbo Overkill is a flawless combination of action, humor, and stunning aesthetics. It's a refreshing addition to the FPS genre that not only meets but exceeds expectations. Whether you're a fan of cyberpunk or just crave a game that delivers unbridled fun, Turbo Overkill is a must-play for any PC gamer. Highly recommended, this game is a triumph in every aspect, setting a new standard for the FPS genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the core design, Turbo Overkill is one of the greatest FPS ever made. It's design, weapon roster, movement, world ; it's all so immensely fantastic and creative and well made. Aside from the Uzi after it's level 3 upgrade  (seriously, I preferred it at level 2. WTF) and the entirety of the plasma gun, I used every single weapon frequently depending on the situation. The upgrades push weapons in and out of viability too in cool ways ; upgrading the shotguns was such a fun moment, pushing them from very underwhelming to extremely fun and powerful.   Unfortunately, and it pains me to say this, a lot of small blemishes knock the game down from new genre titan, to just a very good fps. The game lagged very inconsistently ; in some areas I was on max graphics without a hiccup, and in others the game chugged at minimum graphics. I also got stuck in geometry more than a few times, and tutorial popups and the recharge notification for the chainsaw arms would often just... not happen.Money is very oddly balanced. I played on the middle difficulty, Street Cleaner, which turns off buying ammo and health in shops. So I just consistently had WAY more money than I could possibly use. I bought almost every upgrade as soon as it became available with money leftover. Even cutting zen gain to 2/3 would make the process of saving up for upgrades way more fun. The damage attacks do feels very lopsided. At max health and armour, I could take dozens of bullets, or two enemy rockets. Frequently against big enemies my health would jump from full to near dead in a single hit, and the game's feedback on these attacks wasn't strong enough for me to generally figure out what I could've done differently. The Sloths, Technopedes, Rammers and Teddies were some of the worst offenders. And there were a lot of small things where I just went "HUH?" Like how single armour fragments don't charge you above 100 armour, but single health point vials do ; and how easily I voided out when looking for collectables or hit an invisible wall in the car stages. The game is lacking polish in a lot of small ways. Despite all that, I still wholeheartedly recommend TO. The movement and guns are joyous, and the story was a blast to see. I hope trigger happy games consider patching some of the game's issues, so I can update this review to read "Chegg. Charms. Chenis. Game of the year"

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so, Turbo Overkill.You might be wondering about that title. "Turbo Overkill? Tf is that goofy ahh name"Let's say, it totally lives up to the title.You're a badass called "Johnny Turbo" who is tasked with cleaning up Paradise because of a virus that has gone rogue called "Syn" and just happen to have a CHAINSAW attached to your LEG. Syn, is eventually planning to corrupt all that's left of the earth. It's the ordinary "save the world" kinda deal but it's presented in an interesting way and doesn't get in your face most of the time.While on the topic of story, may I add, the voice acting is actually AAA quality, I was surprised by it.On the gameplay side, yeah, it's pretty much all you could ask for. Fast movement, fast weapon switching, all that goodness. Let's address the elephant in the room first though.The CHAINSAW LEG. If the concept of that alone doesn't get you sold on the game, then don't worry, this ISN'T even the best part.You can use your slide to shred through enemies as a melee move, which gives you an enourmous boost in speed, and the faster you go, the more damage you deal. This move ALONE is SO. MUCH. FUN. You essentially gain an extra dash while in air, allowing you to DROPKICK the enemies with it. I REPEAT, YOU CAN DROPKICK PEOPLE WITH A CHAINSAW LEG.On the other side, we have the actual weapons.You start off with the dual wielding magnums, which while yes, they're a pretty much an FPS standard, they have an alt fire lock-on mode that is devestating towards most small opponents, sometimes even wiping out a whole room. The alt fire does have a cooldown, and here is when the weapon switching comes in. To surpass the cooldown, instead of being a sitting duck, you can switch to another weapon and fire that instead. And an exploit comes to mind "Can I switch back and forth to fire the magnums' alternate firing mode wiping out everything?"No, you can't. You can use the normal firing mode, but not the alt one. This, is INCREDIBLY smart. It encourages weapon combos really well, and not only encourages you to play stylishly, it's FUN to play stylishly.The shotgun is just that, a shotgun. It has an alt firing mode where you can charge up an electric grenade of sorts that deals a lot of damage, killing small enemies, or stuns the bigger ones, making them take double damage. It can also be used for vertical movement,  since if you fire it under yourself while midair, you will be propelled into the air higher than normally, granting you an extra jump. Same with the super shotgun (or rather in this game, a literally SAWED OFF shotgun), it just deals more damage while consuming more ammo. The alt firing mode launches a sticky grenade that can easily disintegrate large clusters of enemies, sorta like the normal shotgun's alt firing mode, but weaker, although the sticky grenades are way cheaper, making you think if you should use one or the other.You can also swap between the SG and SSG to deal massive amount of damage, but this requires pretty good hand coordination and aim.There is the dual wielding machine guns as well, that are incredibly powerful if it lands in the proper hands.It's a DPS MACHINE, and melts anything in it's way (Just like another weapon we'll be talking about later), while being innacurate. If you're not a fan of the extreme innacuracy of it, you can get the alt firing mode, which combines both of them into one, heavy damage dealing, accurate machine gun, and while it's way slower, it's way more versatile.Onto the minigun. It's pretty much another flavor of the machine guns, but it's way less accurate, and fires like a gazillion bullets per nanosecond. It also deals more damage per bullet, which makes me call it the Incinerator™.On the topic of that, it's alt firing mode, is a literal FLAMETHROWER, which is a very close range but insane dps dealing weapon (They made the flamethrower good, forbidden!). I like to pair it with the slide to basically disintegrate opponents in tight spaces/hallways.The rocket launcher. It's pretty fun to rocket jump with it though, and it does have a very satisfying sound effect when you hit the enemy with your lethal shot. Also can be paired with the shotgun and sawed off shotgun swapping. The alt fire is you holding up 4 rockets to release them all at once. It's pretty damn devastating, and when paired with [REDACTED] it's an instant kill.You also have a missile launcher arm, and it's just the magnum alt firing mode on steroids, pretty much a nuke get out of jail free card weapon.There is some other weapons I won't mention because of spoiler reasons for episode 2 and 3.Pairing all these weapons together creates a great balance of stylishly comboing weapons together to create the perfect F U C K I N G MURDER MACHINE.The soundtrack is one of the best fps OST's I've listened to in a while, aside from maybe ULTRAKILL, and you should give it a shot. It won't dissapoint you, and I think it's really underrapreciated.This is my shooter of the year.Anyways, so, since I don't know what to do with this review anymore, Imma just debunk a couple stupid points brought up by the community (WIP)"Movement is too fast, I can't get used to it"Okay, if you're coming from a military shooter, I understand what you mean, but in about 30 minutes of gameplay you're already used to it with how much control the game gives you. I often see people complaining about falling off bridges because they were "too fast". _childDocuments_.review: After playing this game I'm convinced that Sam Prebble is one of the most astute, discerning FPS designers ever. As a voracious consumer of FPSes, I've played most shooters since the year 2000. Even my favorite games have objective mechanical drawbacks, but I think this game has the least in my experience. All mechanical aspects are fine-tuned to perfection. TLDR; Buy the game if you like fast-paced shooters. If you're invested in the state of FPSes and care about where they are going, buy this at full price! The quality and quantity of content you get for this price is unthinkable. Now let me attempt to provide some long objective analysis/evidence to back my statements above.MovementFast-paced shooters that follow the doom/doom eternal design philosophy (movement shooters?) are enjoyable due to fluid movement first and shooting second. The movement in Turbo Overkill is fluid, intuitive and very forgiving. The level design also never gets in the way. You'll rarely get stuck on anything or miss a jump. Some reviewer on youtube put it best; The game "operates at the speed of thought". The controls are so smooth, that if you think of something, it will seem like it happens automatically. Seriously, the quality of the movement mechanics and control in this game cannot be overstated. The design philosophy of this game is to the liberate the player by giving them all the tools they might want and more. You have a double dash, double jump, doom 2016/eternal style full directional control in the air, "chainsaw leg slide". You can double dash and then do the slide to cover more distance. The jump, dash, slide all cover a generous distance so you can zip across an arena quite easily. You can add an augment to the jump to reset your double jump when you hit a wall so you can essentially get 4 jumps if you want. If that isn't enough you also get a grappling hook in episode 2. Everything else is given to you in episode1 IIRC.You can also selectively wall run during certain fights. The wall run and ladder climbing in this game have zero jank and zero fighting with the controls. Sadly, I can't remember any other game executing these basic things this perfectly. Using the chainsaw slide gives you health/armor back. You can insta-kill fodder enemies with the slide so you can quickly get health/armor back and focus on the tougher enemies. This brings us to combatGunplay/Combat loopAgain, the philosophy here is to give you a large number of tools (probably more than your need) and let you loose in the combat arena to approach combat the way you want.I view player freedom as an equally valid choice as compared to the more restrictive, but also fun, doom eternal approach. Turbo Overkill seems to be inspired by Doom 2016 in some ways here. You get a varied arsenal of course. An alternate fire mode on all weapons. For example, the double barrelled shotgun launches grenades. The plasma gun secondary has a microwave beam and a mode that "catches" projectiles so you can throw them back at enemies!  You even have a gears of war style hammer of dawn weapon! In episode 2, you have a sniper rifle that teleports you to the enemy if you charge it up! This game borrows the best tools from every shooter you can think of and integrates them in a well thought out, intuitive way into your toolset. Since the player has so many tools at their disposal, the game has to be balanced such that the enemies are large in number and hit hard. I did become over-reliant on a few guns due to all the chaos (for me it was the chaingun and rocket launcher). However, the number of enemies that spawn in will deplete your ammo fast enough to cause you to switch your weapons reasonably often (yes fast weapon switching and animation cancelling is possible but not required!). The enemy types are quite diverse and pose different types of threats. The enemies' movement and attack patterns plus the level layout makes it fun to discover a valid set of tools for the job at hand while you're flying around the level. Like for example is the level big and easily traversable such that I feel confident enough to dodge projectiles so I can charge up some rockets and then unload on the heavier enemies? Are there obstructions in the way so that I can use the plasma microwave beam and quickly dash behind around a wall while taking out a chunk of a heavy enemy's health? One thing I found interesting is that you can kinda take a quick breather mid-combat and control a small space around you for a moment (YMMV). This gives you a second to strategize movement and weapon selection unlike Doom Eternal where I felt like the noose tightens when you pause even for a second. Maybe I'm just not good at Doom Eternal but I mostly ended up using the guns the game pushed me to use rather than really strategize (no knock on Doom Eternal, I loved that game). Level Design/ProgressionThe levels are designed to loop in on themselves and are largely big and open. Generally you won't feel claustrophobic or feel like you're getting stuck on objects. There are exceptions to this, but I found those exceptions tolerable due to the fluid movement. The number of secrets in each map are always the same and they are fun to find. Enemy types and weapons are trickled out to you slowly over the game so that you can get familiar with each of them before you fight them in tandem with other enemies. There is some buildcrafting with augments that you can add to the protagonist. But you can equip a ton of augments at once and some are clearly more impactful than others so most people will end up with similar builds. This is good IMO because it gets you back to the action quickly rather than keeping you crippled by indecision in front of an upgrade kiosk. Not much else to be said. It works well. Can't think of any big drawbacks here. MusicSubjective. I would buy this OST. I'm not into this type of music (death metal is more my jam), but this music fit so well, kept me entertained and mildly moving my head throughout all the levels. I occassionally listen to the soundtrack while doing other things as well. Not much game music makes it into my daily playlists. Visual Aesthetics/Art DesignGenerally each section of the level is unique and structure differently enough so that you don't feel like it's all a bunch of similar looking spaces separated by corridors.  The levels are fleshed out in terms of background art, especially the paradise city locations. There are some memorable locations that will stay in your memory. At the same time, there are some levels that felt a bit samey either compared to other levels or sections within the levels themselves. The art style of the levels was cool. The enemies were ugly and I didn't like how they looked. I'm not good at analyzing this aspect plus much of it seems subjective so I'll keep it brief. I don't like pixellation in 3D. I prefer colorful 2D sprites like in Duke Nukem rather than the brown and gray 3D models in Quake. Turbo Overkill was like a blend of the two art styles to me.I loved the cohesive art style of Doom 2016 and I wish someone makes a game like this in that style!Summarily, I would say the aesthetics were functional in the sense that they communicated a sense of place. They didn't bore me, they didn't wow me. No complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a hard one to write. I'm giving it a positive review, but only because the first two Acts are amazing. Things taper off really badly from the beginning of the third all the way to the end.  Pros: -Banger soundtrack-Excellent visuals-Good variety of enemies (this is also why I said this is a hard one to write)-Weapons and their subsequent upgrades feel really impactful (most of the time). -Being able to upgrade yourself with augments was a fun ideaCons:Have you ever played a game where you were sitting there like "This is really good, but I really wish it was over already." That was me for the last half of this game. It became an absolute slog to get through some of the arenas because they were all filled with the most bullet sponge enemies in the game. Each arena would have no less than 20 bullet sponges that severely slowed the game down. It wouldn't be a problem most of the time, but in Act 3, pretty much every room is an arena with a ton of these enemies. I ended up doing the bare minimum amount of kills I needed to progress through most of these areas because I didn't feel any incentive to kill them. If anything, forcing me to fight them probably would have made me just shelf the game and never come back to it because it becomes that much a bother. The last two missions are really what's leaving a sour taste in my mouth the most out of anything, though. The second to last mission is...Just stupid, in my opinion. You fight the same boss across three phases, but the first phase has four "phases" and the second phase has three "phases" and the last phase I guess has two "phases" because you get teleported away for a little bit to fight another arena. Confused yet? Because I sure was when I didn't just put the game down and walk away after I finished it. The last mission was kinda BS because you have to do the same exact thing 4 times at 4 different terminals. So, 16 waves of enemies plus fighting the environment plus fighting a timer. Then it's another multi-phase fight with a bunch of nonsense (enemies that constantly respawn, unclear directions other than "destroy the layers") that would have been better condensed to two banger phases without all of the fluff. Neither of these fights felt satisfying. I actually felt relief when I finished them so that I never have to fight them again. I think it's funny because I think even the devs realized that the player would start getting annoyed and had the voice actors throw little things in there like "JUST ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ END IT ALREADY" and "HOW MANY MORE LAYERS DOES THIS ♥♥♥♥♥ HAVE?" It's either that or they really didn't realize how much of an absolute slog the last Act was going to be. Now, with all of that being said, all of the areas in Act 3 were super cool. I just personally think it's the weakest Act of the whole game because of the bullet-sponge spam and all of the fluff. All-in-all, if I was just reviewing the first two Acts, I'd give this a solid 10/10. The last Act brings it down to like a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cool and fast paced, and you get to kill robots and AI. It has plenty of options and accessibility options as well, . It seems to only be missing a HUD size option (It's REALLY small) and a game speed option (the game is REALLY fast, and can be hard to react to things as fast as the game demands).My major gripe, however, is that the game is HORRIDLY UNOPTIMIZED. It's clear they are going for a Unreal Tournament style of graphics, but the game pushes GPUs unnecessarily harshly, doubling the heat of my RTX Card by merely being launched. And from what I can tell, it seems that it's all operating overhead. Changing the graphics options and resolution did not improve or reduce performance whatsoever, and only changing the max framerate made a difference, indicating unoptimized code and/or scripts.There are countless more "graphically advanced" games out there which don't push hardware nearly this hard. There is simply no excuse for this.This game needs better optimization before I can recommend it to anyone with low end or even mid-level computer owners.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is an absolutely amazing, action-packed shooter with amazing callbacks to the older years of FPS. The weapons are smooth, the levels are stunning, and the story is quite interesting. It gives me personal feels of "Cyberpunk meets Doom meets Ultrakill." It's a weird mashup, but Turbo Overkill does it perfectly.Now, my only complaint is the cutscenes. Turbo Overkill suffers from the Doom: Eternal "mini-cutscenes to show you important things" style. I personally greatly dislike this in video games, as it feels way too hand-holdey. I'd prefer to just go around and find the item myself, especially with Turbo Overkill's maps. They aren't big enough to warrant such a cutscene, and when they are we get a directional marker. The full on cutscenes aren't much better. They are made very well, but their sound design is very, very subpar. My experience is mismatched audio syncing, underwhelming gunfire (ex. shooting both Ripper and Maw in cutscenes), and sometimes even underwhelming in general (a good example is when your leg stops working and you manually saw off an enemy's head. It feels weak.) I could also nitpick about other things, but those aren't anywhere near as important (or warranted) as the cutscenes. If they fix these in the next update, then I'd easily say that Turbo Overkill is one of the best FPS arena shooters ever released. It's hella fun, and you should buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Cyberpunk First Person Shooter where you can chainsaw slide through hordes of enemies, shoot rockets and grapple on them, Telefrag into enemies to taverse the map, become Chainsaw Man and and throw enemy (and your own) prjectiles back at them. I could leave it at that and would just recommend you either buying the game or checking out the Demo! But I won't, cause there is so much more to love about this game.First off,  24 Levels (AND THE SAME AMOUNT OF SECRET LEVELS), each of them visually diverse in different environments. It's all Cyberpunk Themed, you travel through severs, over rooftop, a toxic wasteland, through a powerplant and later on even in space.The levels are overall really well paced, you got mostly swift and fast combat encounters, some bigger and longer arenas that are broken up with some platforming section which never last too long.The combat is really tight. You got over 9 weapons, each of them with purpose, there is nothign that doesn't feel useles, except maybe the Minigun at times, but even that one has a super good Alternate Firemode. Most enemies are running around shooting at you and while their behaviour doesn't overall change, the variety comes from the projectiles they throw at you. Some projectiles are threatening for different reasons, which is somethign you gonna particularily feel on Murder Machine, the highest difficulty where you end up dead in less than 2 seconds for some enemies. I spent most of the time playing on Murder MAchien Difficulty with Triple Enemies just for the fun of it. That Soundtrack is also top notch, though it really start bopping starting from Episode 2. Anything else? Oh yeah, there is also and Endless Mode, which is great fun and a Level Editor! This game is through and through a full experience, and one of the most fun shooters around.My personal GOTY in a year where ACVI comes out and actually has to match this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an action packed adrenaline rush. I've been following it since it's early days and the way this game has evolved has blown me away. The amount of variety the combat provides via weapons, utilities, and environment makes every encounter heartpounding. Combine that with the aggressive synth soundtrack and you've got a bombastic experience. The story is largely just a framework to hang the amazing set pieces and colourful enemy designs at you, but this isn't the type of game where you focus on the story or characters much (although you and your AI have some nice moments even if you're a silent protag).I would say my biggest criticism is the rooftop vehicle levels. While I applaud experimentation and even enjoy the other vehicle level on the cycle, the rooftops felt a bit slow disjointed and is probably the only time I really got lost in the game for an extended period. I don't like offering criticism without suggestions, but I'm not too sure what to say. I love exploration but this section didn't really feel like it rewarded it. I'd say maybe make that section on rails (have the AI drive the car while you shoot) or put some notable stuff around the map for straying off path. Granted I may have missed what might have already been there which if so that's on me. But if you love FPS and intense action you must give this one a chance, the first two acts are incredible and I eagerly await the remaining epsiodes!

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is well deserving of its success, being a true bargain for the amount of content it provides.Paying homage to the sci-fi/cyberpunk genre with several on-the-nose references to films like Robocop and The Terminator, It does not shy away from its inspirations. Respectfully and masterfully, it delivers an experience that is a cut above the rest in a long list of retro style shooters sweeping the market.Yet despite all this, I must stress one important criticism I have, in that it suffers from a lack in moderation. The game runs a bit too long, culminating in a finale that left me exhausted when it was all over. I think after the 10 hour mark, my brain felt like it was just spinning a bare-tread tire in place in an attempt to cross the finish line.In summary, Turbo Overkill is a testament to what indie developers are capable of, but ultimately lets their passion for game design get a bit carried away. Still, I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY REVIEW:You have WAY WAY more and faster mobility options than in Doom Eternal(DE), (FFS, you get full air control, double jump, and double dash) right when you get started, but to compensate, in the hardest difficulty, most powerful attacks one shot you, or at least cripple you even at full stack. But, unlike all those noobs saying this game has random deaths, I assure you EVERY high-damage enemy/projectile is loudly/brightly communicated, you just gotta learn  what that the beep from a syntaur, the wooshing rockets from a sloth, and the mace notification from a ram, those massive bright blue slow projectiles from splits, the clinking grenades of a , etc all mean and how you ALWAYS could have done something differently 1 or 2 seconds ago to have saved yourself via foresight alone(no hindsight).As for weapons, there's not as much underdogging of weapons as in DE or D2016 (the starting pistols will be highest DPS weapon in the game, even more than the token based SATELLITE BEAM gun). AND each and every weapon is SO distinctively unique(the least of which is a machine gun that switches between brrrr and fshhhhh).Coming back to movement, most enemies don't lead your trajectory while firing projectiles, so you always gotta get creative with your movement if you don't want to go back to the LOS that has 5 fatal rockets coming at you and eat them all. I actually find this quite entertaining because yes, for one enemy, you can just run a circle around them and they can't do much against it since they don't lead their projectiles, but you put an arena full of enemies, all with different types speeds and methods of attack, and *chef's kiss*. Now THAT is a movement shooter, you gotta think fast, get creative, spam your cheggs and dashes(unlimited, and refresh on jump pads and grapples respectively) and most importantly, NEVER go back to the same angular LOS of an enemy sloth as 0.5-2 seconds ago.You're also welcome to pick not murder machine and just go to ham on every super, heavy, and trash mob you see with your cheggs. Or smash your buttons with no consideration of anything and go braindead on a second playthrough with my least favorite augment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a retro First Person Shooter similar to Dusk or Amid Evil, where player character Johnny Turbo must fight through hordes of Human and Cyborg enemies to stop a rogue AI from taking over the world.•	Movement speed is very fast.•	Good weapon variety including magnum, assault rifle, shotgun, double barrel shotgun, minigun, rocket launcher, plasma rifle, sniper rifle and ion cannon. Most weapons have a secondary fire mode.•	Your leg has a chainsaw attached, which lets you slide through groups of enemies, instantly killing weaker enemies. This can be upgraded to restore your health and armour with each kill.•	You’ll also gain a slow motion ability which is very useful for dealing with more dangerous enemies. Killing enemies during slow mo will make them drop ammo pickups.•	Customise your playing style by equipping upgrades such as increased maximum health, triple jump, and nearby ammo/health pickups being magnetised towards you.•	Level design can be annoying at times. This is one of those games that has lots of small platforms where you’ll need to jump, double jump, air dash, double air dash, wall run and grapple hook over bottomless pits. Thankfully the airborne gymnastics is fairly lenient (there were times where I felt like I missed a jump but the game decided it was close enough). But sometimes the level layouts are confusing and I’d spend a few minutes trying to figure out where I’m supposed to go next. And I lost count of the number of times I accidentally fell off a small platform while trying to shoot enemies.•	Hard difficulty is nicely balanced for an experienced FPS player during episodes 1 and 2 (each episode contains several levels), but episode 3 at times felt a bit too much. I got through it, but it was less fun. Most encounters involve being trapped in a small room with not much space to dodge and even less cover, while having to defeat multiple large waves of enemies. Eventually one of the rocket launcher wielding enemies would spawn right next to me and kill me before I had chance to react, sending me back to the start of the first wave. Probably more enjoyable on normal difficulty.•	I also want to give a special mention to the final level, which has several encounters where you have to defeat multiple waves of enemies within a strict time limit, or you’ll die instantly.•	Boss fights are mostly just bigger waves of the same enemies you’ve spent the whole game killing, while occasionally shooting the boss between waves.•	Story is nonsense. There’s not much of an intro to explain things and there are several occasions where NPCs refer to past events that I’m not familiar with, which made me wonder if this is actually a sequel to a game I never played. (I don’t think it is).•	Voice acting is fine.•	I finished the game in just under 17 hours.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes or framerate.•	Default field of view is too high. I don’t think I’ve ever changed my FOV in any game before, but everything looked really weird while I played through the first level. After consulting the forum and changing FOV from 90 to 74, everything looks normal.Turbo Overkill is a good game that fans of retro FPSes should mostly enjoy, if you’re in the mood to just turn off your brain and shoot things. Worth buying on a small sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This is THE most fun shooter I have ever played!The fast action is god-tier and litteraly all guns feel powerful and have their place and when the enemies line up nicely for you, just slide through them and slice them up with your chainsaw-leg. Even the pistols you start with are good and towards the end become one of the most powerful weapons with temporary massive damage that instagibs the fodder and 2-3 shot kills most other enemies. The second to second action is litteraly the most fun i've had in a shooter.I thought before i bought and played it that this game left alot to be desired in terms of graphics, but let me tell you its as pretty as it needs to be. The character modles are are low detailed but the only time you will notice that are in some short cutscenes. Combat moves so fast you wont be able to tell enemies are low poly, and the guns you hold i think look quite nice.The soundtrack is also so damn good and fits perfectly with the grity cyberpunk theme of the game.I do feel like i have to give one negative criticism of the game. Several times and definitley more than would have liked I had no idea of how to get to the next area. It felt like they intentionally hid the the intended path forward in counterintuitive ways. _childDocuments_.review: Fast paced non-stop action. If Ultrakill and Doom: Eternal were your cup of tea, this is an easy sell. I played on the 2nd highest difficulty and had a pretty comfortable time. 3 hours to complete the first episode. Love the biopunk aesthetic.Now since I'm a critical person I'm going to do what I do best: ♥♥♥♥♥. The checkpoint system is awful. I'm guessing it's based on crossing a line on the map. However, the game has you running around like a maniac so chances are you're going to cross one mid combat multiple times during a playthrough, so you respawn in the middle of a previous fight. There was also a situation I ran into during a platforming section where a switch opened a shortcut in case I fell. The check point however, flagged before I hit the switch the first time. So I respawned, fell and found out the switch hadn't been hit.The weapon balance is a little off. The Chainsaw Leg and the F-U Rocket are too strong for things that doesn't cost anything to use. With the augment upgrades the slide turns the melee enemies into health and armor refills, any encounter with them left me with over 100 health and armor. The Rocket with the damage upgrade can gib what's supposed to be the episode's big bad enemy, and it can target multiple other enemies along side it. The harder encounters ended up being situations with a lot of smaller enemies I didn't want to use the rocket on. The game's abundance of bright lights can be an issue as well. Enemies with bright lights on them don't really stand out in the environment that is mostly bright lights. I didn't even know where my crosshairs were most of the time, I just went with the wall of bullets approach. The stores feel superfluous. On higher difficulties especially you can't buy a whole lot. The weapon stores were for a 1 time weapon upgrade, and the general store sold augments that you then took to the near by splicer vender to install. The weapon upgrades could just be included, they're available at the first store after you get the gun anyway. The general store and splicer vender could be combined, so you buy them and install them at the same place. You would also get to see the nifty video demonstrations were you buy the augment.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this game has great gunplay, reminds me heavily of ultrakill or DOOM, there are a few glitches that I have come across and I will list them-Whenever I click continue it for some reason brings me back to the fourth level even if I am currently on a higher level.-whenever I slide into a wall I sometimes get stuck for a little whileAll in all a pretty great game, that deserves some recognition.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great retro shooter. Movement is crisp and abilities make it incredibly fun to zip around your enemies juggling guns and alternate fire modes. Exploration is encouraged but not required, you can usually just find your way by looking for the next enemies or ammo. I have gotten stuck a couple times not knowing where to go; sometimes it's easy to miss the hints in such a fast-paced game. And the driving section is borderline unplayable if you usually use inverted controls, as they don't invert during flight. Had to take that section extremely slow because of how ingrained the y-axis is in my brain. Those two qualms aside, definitely recommend this. The movement is really close to perfect and overall it's just a really great, fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute blast.  Everything you've ever looked for in a Boomer Shooter except this is way more than that.  For it's genre it has all of the usual: retro graphics, high octane fast and furious, tons of enemies, bloodbath, find the secrets, find the exit and so on.  What separates it is that it incorporates a lot of today's gaming but in a much more streamlined, simpler way consistent with the game.  The game takes place in a corrupt, Cyberpunk world and your job is to clean the bad element.  In addition you also have a score to settle.  It's a nod to Cyberpunk 2077 and Ghostrunner.  It contains RPG elements similar to it and it's complexity is relative to the game.  Weapons can be upgraded, your character has a skill tree you build up as you go along and there is a story to follow.  The weapons look great, they sound great, the overall game looks really good and it all just fits so well.  There are definitely some challenges in that the game is very vertical for lack of a better word.  Moving around involves a lot of ultra high jumps, running on walls, a lot skillful maneuvering.  This aspect I wasn't crazy about but all in all I am having a great time.  Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Intelligent level design, best use of a chainsaw in games since Gears of War, best use of a middle finger since Postal, best tower of Sauron since LOTR and on top of that a banging soundtrack.In a year with System Shock, Atomic Heart and Trepang2 you'd think this game would have steep competition. But Turbo Overkill outshines them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good not great game. The look and feel of the game is cool. The enemies, although of decent variety, arent that cool to look at and do get repetitive with how long the game is. Theres a decent amount of guns with alternate fires, even if most of them are pretty standard fare. The movement in combat as well as platforming is what takes the cake for this game. Its a shame you unlock things too slowly especially the grappling hook, as having multiple movement tools feels excellent.  The levels are pretty boring and generic "grey alley/ grey building" except for some levels in Act 3. For some stupid reason when you've selected a difficulty when you want to switch it mid playthrough at the beginning of a level you can only go down in difficulty for some inexplicable reason, maybe the dumbest thing I've ever seen.The game is really long for a shooter and can at times overstay its welcome but is still pretty fun throughout, just maybe play it in doses. It is dumb how upgrades are specific to a specific limb, as you should be able to slot in something for your legs, and not be unwilling to use it on the R leg because you already have 2 really good upgrades for that leg but your L leg upgrades suck but there's nothing you can do about it, as it makes no sense. A couple bosses are a bit gimmicky but provide a good challenge, although its stupid they all use the lazy respawning waves of enemies trope to artificially inflate difficulty. Overall its still a good game and its amazing such a small group of people made it. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: From the creator of Total Chaos, a horror Doom mod that's become a modern classic, we get Turbo Overkill. But don't let the developers previous Doom fame let you to believe that this is a derivative doom clone, what we have here is something crafted with lot's of love and passion. Turbo Overkill's first episode is a very solid first introduction to the game and its world. The game wears its sci-fi and cyberpunk influences on it's sleeve and you'll find lots of references both in the levels and in the story to popular movies and games.The level design is all incredibly well crafted, and it throws in some variety in a few levels just when navigating the cyberpunk cityscape starts to become a bit repetitive. There's a lot of enemy variety in episode one although a few can become tedious to deal with later on. The game starts off as a fair challenge and can grow to become pretty difficult in the last 2-3 levels. There were one or two difficulty spikes that seemed to come out of nowhere but hopefully the dev's decide to balance to those out in the future. Overall what's here is great, Turbo Overkill doesn't feel like a halfhearted attempt to mimic the first person shooters of days past so much as put it's own spin on that tired formula. Give this game a spin it's absolutely worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is excess incarnate. For years I have wanted a game like the new boom-shoots of today to take on that excessive, in your face game design of old. Something along the lines of Serious Sam, Painkiller, Ninja Gaiden 2, etc. A game that only kept getting crazier, harder, and dumber with every level. This game is exactly that. The game lures you in with it's low-poly cyberpunk aesthetics, but worry not, as its choc-full of chainsaw limbs, space-lovecraftian nightmares, over the top combat, and much much more. Can the excess get to be too much sometimes... yeah. While the game is one of the best in its field overall, the final hour of the game is just back to back bad boss fights, but it's the only stain on a game I think is otherwise amazing. I just love games like these so much, play it when you get the chance please.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Took some getting used to the controls and movement, but after a couple minutes I was cruising and blowing everything to kingdom come. The progression from easier enemies to harder ones is as smooth as you can get you never feel cheated out of a win you feel like you messed up and just need to change up your strategy or your augments. One of the most fun games I played this year can't wait for what's to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to describe just how much this game does correctly. there is not a single weapon, enemy, plot point, boss fight, level or piece of dialogue that feels redundant or wasted. every upgrade has a purpose, every weapon is a beast capable of downing gods and every story act is an escalation worthy of the name overkill. the only thing limiting you in this game is your own skill and your own imagination. if you have any interest whatsoever in arena-fight to arena-fight design similar to nu-doom or painkiller? I am of the personal belief that this game is nearly perfect, and with some polish and a bigger budget it would have even outshone doom eternal. if anyone ever manages to top this, they may well have to create a perfect game out of necessity. where can you go up from here but to heaven itself?
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME HAS AN AMAZING AMOUNT OF GAME PLAY AND LEVEL AFTER LEVEL, OF THINGS TO DISCOVER AND VERY GOOD BADDIES TO FIGHT AGAINST.  LOTS OF GUNS AND ROCKET LAUNCHERS TO USE AND THE ABILITY TO BUY EXTRA AMMO ETC.VERY COLOURFUL AND PRETTY INMPRESSIVE FOR A PC GAME, THE LEVELS HAVE LOADS OF VARIETY AND ARE VERY PLAYABLE.THIS IS ONE HELL OF A GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a wickedly fun Retro FPS that oozes charisma! I don't remember the last time I had so much fun playing a shooter! I don't have a lot of time to play games on the regular these days, so it's nice to have something I can jump into and play in short, fast paced sessions. For full disclosure, though, I do know the main developer on this game personally (he's almost a one man show, believe it or not!), and have worked with him in the past, so there's probably a bit of bias, I admit. We were never afraid to tell each other when we thought each other's work was crap, though, and I think most people would agree (especially based on reviews!), that he's made something special! Bravo, Sam!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game.  It's extremely fast paced, lots of guns, lots of ammo, lots of interesting enemies (which is a massive point in and of itself), and fun maps.There's a dodge, a fast paced slide, a grapple, a double jump, some wall slides, teleports, options for wall grabs, the list goes on.  The combat is fast paced, guns have alternate fires, and I found myself using almost every gun in most situations.  The enemy designs are all well done and it's nice to see some really new kinds of enemies that aren't just the stock standard.  Story is fine, too.  Music is phenomenal and map design is fantastic.I played on No Pain No Gain.I think there's only three points I'd dock it for:1. There's just too much money.  I'd bought every upgrade and gun type way before the end of the game.2. There's too much ammo.  I was frequently maxed out on just about everything.3. The difficulty for the first 2/3 of the game is very easy.  Like, way too easy.  Then it ramps up really fast and gets really hard.  The final stretch of the game was super hard in places (in generally a good way!).  I just wish the whole game had been more difficult.  Not sure I'm a fan of the final two bosses either as I was mostly just getting killed from one-shots.I still whole heavily recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This might sound like an obvious overstatement, especially since I'm writing this after 4 hours of gameplay, but..BUT, this might be one of my favorite games ever.Since I love both doom and cyberpunk this feels like a suspiciously perfect fit for a goofer like me. The inspiration is very obv to a point one might say this straight up just IS doom, but no,... its so much better.It's funny doom with both the weapons and movement on steroids. It's set in a world controled by a ROGUE AI, which is also like doom slimy tendrils virus thing. And most importantly, you have a chainsaw leg. Yes, a chainsaw leg with which you can slide super far while slicing a dicing enemies. I havent gotten there yet, but you can literally shoot a rocket and grapple onto into with your hook. You can wall run, double jump, have 2 charges of dash + you can chainsaw slide all you want. So yeah, take doom, add cyberpunk story and character cyberware customization, add funny and add retro FPS look and thats what this is.Also it's apparently been made mostly by one dev. This game is ridiculously awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Holt cow, this game is on the podium 100%. I was skeptical at first, I've never liked any games like this. and I still don't. but this is the one outlier. For a game so satisfying and smooth, it also is pretty funny. everything feels balanced, and if it's too hard for you, there are different difficulties. Also, I was expecting 6 hours of gameplay, but no this is 20-24 hours. and every second is just as good as the last. there is ONE thing I don't like: a single enemy on the second hardest difficulty can one-shot you if you have 200 health and 200 armor. you'd think "Oh well, that makes sense, it's the second hardest difficulty, and it's probably an advanced enemy." you'd be right. I'd completely agree, but the only problem is there is no sound cue, and it's a fast-ranged attack. that pissed me off for like 10 minutes but that's it.  everything else is so perfect and satisfying. And as far as I know, there aren't really any ways to cheese anything. you can play any way you want, i loved this one gun, and it brought me through most of the game, but then my friend hated that gun and did a different gun I hated that brought him mostly through the game. and if you don't like guns at all, you can get a powerful as heck chainsaw leg, that destroys everything. It fits whatever playstyle. Also, voice acting is great. play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game that has a very strong doom eternal influence. I'd put it in my top 5 retro fps games. Other titles would include Ion Fury and Cultic. I'm playing it on street cleaner difficulty and getting my ass kicked in the first episode. Sometimes navigating the maps is a little too difficult and unforgiving for my taste. I am a casual player so most people into retro fps games probably won't care. I really don't want to have to drop the difficulty to beat the first boss. All in all its a great game that presents a good challenge. Has awesome style and the soundtrack is perfection. I hope the retro fps genre never dies.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: WOW!!! This game is awesomely WICKED!!!! I can't even describe how excited I feel  as I just beat the game (I also sat through the credits, nice end bit Devs). Huge shout out to a friend for gifting me the game a long while back! The combat is very fast paced as you swap between multiple weapons and lash out a barrage of bullets and rockets and laser beams and even chainsaw attacks towards hoards of enemies. The graphics are amazing as I especially love the art style. It gave me retro game vibes as I looked closely at the textures. Additionally the story itself is just amazing and had me hooked from the beginning! Definitely a must grab game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best Boom Shoots I've played in the last decade. If you're a veteran of the genre or looking to get into it, I cannot recommend this game hard enough.The entire weapon arsenal is a joy to use - nothing gets put into the 'worthless' box for a majority of the game. There are times where a weapon may be tucked away or neglected for a bit, but it will always have a use at some point. Barring a couple enemy types, the game has no "this weapon counters this enemy" - allowing you to play the game however you wish.The OST is an absolute banger, the second to last boss has the best tracks in the game. They do reuse assets in their level design, but its used/reused so incredibly well that unless you're really looking hard for it you may not even notice. I didn't notice myself until it was pointed out to me!Overall, amazing. 11/10. Play Turbo Overkill!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Extremely fun gameplay++ Amazing visuals++ Amazing levels and setpieces++ Banger soundtrack++ Insane cutscenes+ Chainsaw Leg+ Cool vehicle sections+ Many weapons and augments+ Good voice acting* OK story-- Game was completely broken on first start up-- HORRENDOUS audio mixing in some cutscenesThis game was a blast to play through, for the entire time. The gameplay and flow in combat are addicting and a lot of fun. On the audio-visual front the game is pretty insane as well, combining unique and memorable visuals with a banger soundtrack. The chainsaw leg is one of my all-time favourite melee weapons and the vehicle sections were a nice change of pace as well. The negatives are related to stuff which should be easy to fix (but for some reason are not): The first start up is pretty broken, with the wrong language selected, after which I had to look up a guide to fix the game. The second is the HORRENDOUS audio mixing in some cutscenes, where the music deleted my ears, while everything else was drowned out.All in all the game is very worth it's asking price, just maybe wait for a patch to address the issues first.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: First review I've posted in a while. Perhaps everyone will tell me to "git gud", or more likely nobody would see this, but my opinion the game should have finished with the Maw boss battle. I really liked the game up until that point, and honestly the entire last level should have been scrapped or thoroughly redone. That was so frustrating and the game went on way longer than it needed to. If it wasn't for that last level, I would have loved this game, but that last level left me with a pretty bad taste in my mouth really. Aside from that, this game is quite epic, especially one level in Episode 3 where you are fighting in space, that was epic. _childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill takes the “Boomer” shooter to the next level. This is the best iteration of classic first-person-shooter fun I’ve played yet. Surpassing both the classics and the modern entries. Everything about this game is just top-notch. The level design is both great and varied with lots of different locations and some crazy ideas. Searching for key-cards never gets in the way of the fun, because it is always pretty clear where to go, sometimes even guided by markers. There are quite a bit of Ghostrunner like parkour elements in the game but the movement controls are way better executed than in most other FPS games, so that you always feel in full control making these sections fun instead of trial and error frustration. Enemy variety is great as well and boss fights are fun. There are even vehicle sections that are also a lot of fun. Even more fun are all the weapons and upgrades that the player obtains during the gameplay. Each weapon can be enhanced for alternate fire modes and more punch. All of them feel great to use and it is difficult to find a favorite. There are also character upgrades that enhance movement, damage types or give you more money, health or armor from dead enemies. Tons of stuff to play around with and find your own playstyle. All of this is presented in super stylish low poly graphics with fantastic special effects and tons of environmental variety. Dark back alleys, sprawling cyberpunk cities, chromed skyliners, moving trains, space stations, pest-infested sewers, you name it. The 15 hours ride never gets boring and there are also five different difficulty levels to fine tune the player experience. Last but not least the absolutely brilliant synthwave soundtrack that pumps the adrenaline into the veins during intense firefights deserves a lot of praise as well. Overall a tremendous game that is a steal for the asking price. Get this ASAP if you are even slightly interested in frantic FPS, cyberpunk or overly stylish video games.

_childDocuments_.review: While Turbo Overkill has retro-inspired aesthetics, I'd compare it most directly to Doom Eternal in terms of gameplay. The ballet of both combat and movement abilities, switching between different weapons, using melee takedowns to recover health, armor, and ammo, and using environmental interactivity to get around the combat arenas works beautifully. Unlike Doom Eternal, fights aren't as prescriptive and there's plenty of room to approach them in your own way. The graphics are beautiful and sound design and music are top notch, the game runs well and I encountered very few bugs and glitches in my platythrough.If there's one criticism I would have it's that like it's id inspiration, some levels overstay their welcome a bit. Overall though, this is a strong recommendation and top contender for my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Took a while to get going, but it was worth it. During Episode 1, the gameplay is nothing special. When Episode 2 rolls around and you've unlocked most of the weapons/mechanics and the levels occasionally force you to fight in arenas, that's where the game picks up. That's when it starts to feel like Doom Eternal gameplay. Otherwise, it's too easy to just kite/funnel enemies and kill them without much difficulty.I will say that the Chainsaw dash is also a little OP, especially when you've unlocked the perks to get armor and health per kill. With no real limit/cooldown to using the Chainsaw dash, it was a little too easy to fly around the map killing dozens of trash mobs and getting health and armor. In many cases, it was more beneficial than using my weapons. I feel it should be another tool in the arsenal, but not a primary means of offense.The music also became noise after a while. It's always going at max intensity even when there's no action going on. Eventually I had to mute it and play my own music. What did me in was a bug I encountered in the final series of boss fights where the Cyber Maw boss stopped spawning after reloading a checkpoint -resulting in a progress blocker. I didn't care enough to restart the whole level to fight the previous bosses again just to get my progress back, felt like I saw enough of the game at that point. I might replay the game down the line when the game has less bugs.Despite my complaints, there is a lot of fun to be had here. When the game is at its highs, its insanely addicting. It is clear the amount of effort that was put into making the game fun. The game also has a lot of charm, humor, and homages to 80s/90s content.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag. At its best, it's probably the best modern boomer shooter I've played. But at other times, it feels really half-baked. The difficulty is absolutely all over the place in a way that doesn't feel deliberate. I think a little bit more polish and play-testing would have gone a very long way.All that being said, I'd still recommend this game because it absolutely nails the most important things: weapon design and enemy variety. The guns look cool and feel fun to use, and there's a ton of different enemy types with varied behaviours. I also enjoyed the frantic movement - it's not exactly what I was expecting but it's fun and it feels right at home with the over-the-top cyberpunk setting.Finally, I have to shout out the almost perfectly placed checkpoints. This is, I think, the only boomer shooter (old or new) I've played where I felt like I could actually rely on the checkpoint system to put me back at a reasonable, fair save point when I died. It makes the game feel like a genuine challenge rather than a test of my ability to resist the urge to save scum through difficult fights. The game still does have quicksaves, so that might sound like an insignificant thing, but it had a huge impact on my enjoyment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, let me start with the good, I LOVED the setting, combat was solid, movement was spot on, weapons were all fun to use maps were great and well designed. The game is long so you definitely will get your money’s worth out of this. However, I wish Steam would incorporate a “neutral” rating system. I am one of the unlucky players who suffered from a severe audio bug that muted all ambient sound effects, the only way to resolve this was going back to windows and enabling “Loudness Equalization” in your sound properties. I couldn’t play this game for months because the audio was so broken and the devs have yet to acknowledge thew issue, it was only the help of another Steam community member that led me to the workaround. The other reason I would give this a neutral rating is EP1 and EP2 start off so damn strong and fun but then you get to the first Maw boss fight, this just completely ruined all the fun I was having. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ STUPID. Even worse EP3 which has some really great moments was over shadowed by them doubling down on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculously dumb boss fights (Maw and SYN). It was just not fun anymore and I just wanted to be done with the game. It’s really a shame because this game was leaning towards “Perfect” to me until these eye rolling anti-fun boss fights. I hate that ♥♥♥♥. This multi-phase, multi layered, puzzled boss fights that go on and on and on and on ruin games for me. If the devs make a sequel, please for the love of everything just stick to the basic FUN of the game that you had going in EP1 and most of EP2 and ditch the overly complicated boss fight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.It's not a bad game by any means but the issues I have with it keep me from recommending this game unless you can score it for really REALLY cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: For a quick review this game is great. It is like Quake 1 on steroids with a 80's vibe and some more story and cutscenes. It progressively gets better and better as you play the game too. Highly recommended to buy. I will continue to see what these devs make next like is upcoming Total Chaos game.For a longer review, this is probably the best boomer shooter I have ever played. The creative talent knew what they were doing.There are negatives, certainly not game breaking listed below,The collectibles need to be taken out the game. It goes against everything this game represents which is fast and furious gameplay. If you want to provide unlockables make it to where it compliments the gameplay like killing enemies or finishing levels within time limits. I am surprised the creative talent made the collectibles to where it will slow you down searching for them. This was a mistake. If you want us to explore the world you created, viewing the already well designed levels is the prize, not some artificial collectible. I will not scour the levels or will I look up YouTube clips to figure out where they are. I will not go back and play the game again in different ways because of not having the collectibles that I missed the first time I played it. At the very least just give us the collectibles after beating the game.Other smaller issues include,-I would like the option to move the weapons more to the side of the screen to not obstruct my fov,double-barrelled shotgun shooting too slowly,-levels can be a bit lengthy,-the fog, and the onscreen effects while having 30-second power-ups need better perfecting, hard to see what was on screen, I wanted to play with the fog on but it made the game hard to see.-Too much explosions while shooting enemies blocks my vision of seeing the enemies being hit with my bullets, this takes away some satisfaction from hitting my enemies. Make the effects shoot to the sides or something else so I can see the damage I am doing-I would like pvp multiplayer at leastEverything else is great though such as,+I constantly used all the weapons provided with the exception to the double shotgun cuz of its slower shooting capacity,+the game quickly gets better and better as you play+graphics and sound top-notch,+plenty of weapons and enemies,+the vehicular shooing sections did not overstay its welcome,+pretty lengthy game for being a boomer shooter, 15-20 hour game,buy the game, i'm looking forward to seeing what else the developer is making...would be great to see some sort of old school zombie survival horror game by these guys.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I wanted from a movement shooter, it's got tons of weapons, weapon combos, enemy variety and most important of all... MOVEMENT, there is a LOT of movement in this game, no other game I've played has such movement, you have a grappling hook (mid-game) that allows you to grapple on enemies and certain spots in the map.Not only that, the game also allows you to dash, chainsaw slide + dash (Yes, you have a chainsaw on your leg that allows you to tear enemies while sliding and that is also interesting) and gives you an arsenal of devastating weapons, no weapon is useless in this game, they all allow you to frag a lot of enemies at once.Dare I say that this game is the best movement singleplayer shooter I've played, yes, Ultrakill is good and it's also awesome but Turbo Overkill is just way more frenetic and the weapons are more devastating and simpler to use, it's all just mindless killing combined with hyper aggressive movement and air control and that is exactly what I want, it's really relaxing in it's own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ this is some impressive stuff. In its best moments it can give Doom Eternal a run for its money,The combat loop is excellent, you fly through the arenas at breakneck speed and use your whole arsenal all the time. None of the weapons and powers ever feel redundant and unnecessary, the balancing act is *chief's kiss* The pacing and set pieces are *almost* always top-notch too: there is something sick and distinctive in every single level. Even the vehicle sections are totally amazing, the bike and the mech ones especially.And it looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous, and it's mostly one guy project, are you kidding me?9/10===============================I hated the last two levels tho. They are the definition of an overkill (*ba dum tss*).The penultimate boss arena just drags on and on and on and on, way past the point of not caring. 12 stages. 12 gоddamn stages. With annoying platforming in between and Nihilanth-style teleportation to the separate arenas mid-fight. And *now* you decided to start punishing players for jumping-into-the-abyss, in the penultimate level, seriously?And there is the final level, when the game out of nowhere presents the most annoying gimmick in the entire thing - time trial fights. I was screaming at the screen at that point. And there is the sensory overload endless final boss after that. Your cute companion S.A.M even complains about it in game. Guys, if you felt the need to lampshade it - maybe just tone it down a little bit, huh? All of it left me exhausted in the end, and not the good kind of exhausted. And that a shame, the game this excellent deserved better send off than "thank god I'm done with it".

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: computer crashing issue has been fixed, my highest recommendation i could give on this game.original review:this game is genuinely amazing but equipping certain chainsaw augments straight up shuts my computer down. i'm only not recommending the game that causes such a massive issue like this but i know they will fix it. this is just a warning to new players that this could happen, and will instantly recommend after its fixed.TLDR: games a wonderful 9/10, but this game loves its most miserable unfun thing, maw.                                             !!!potential spoilers ahead!!!Review: you know that meme of a drawn horse being perfect all the way to the end being a child drawing? thats this game full stop.I think this game is genuinely amazing. super fluid, i feel in control of almost all my abilities, and that bike combat is so smooth, i haven't played a game with a better hoverbike since like perfect dark. the music matches the tempo of gameplay, most the weapons i used almost throughout the entire game, and also the pistol stays relevant for once in a shooter!there is genuinely so many small things i love in this, between small upgrades to your character making you feel more powerful all the way to the very end, unique designs, weapon utility, and enemy pool. i love most the arenas, this game never ever lets up, unless it needs to. at the beginning i was struggling, but by the end i was doing so good that almost nothing way that much of a challenge (dont worry though, if you stop moving they will absolutely kill you, its still very challenging).the hoverbike level by far had to be one of my favorite missions,  its just near perfect in everyway.its graphically beautiful, while keeping the aesthetic of what an old quake shooter wanted to look like, almost like how n64 renders were what Nintendo wanted you to imagine the blocky characters to look like on the system. and the music is a straight banger, i've listened to the so much out of the game, like i did with dooms music. the color pallet stays consistent, only the ladders are hard to find sometimes though. here are some things i'm iffy on, that doesn't really ruin anything but still takes me out abit. the car, its nice, but its kinda clunky, i kinda wish it had just a little bit more polish on the maps its in. cutscenes also feel way too floaty, and kinda weird (i know its a really small team making this and these don't effect the gameplay but i still wanted to mention it). some weapons don't really flow too well, like the ssg, i just feel it doesn't really warrant it in here, that being said i did use it alot, comboing the ssg+sg+ssg+rockets, but on its own just kinda felt weak.  the sniper while really cool just never really worked well outside jut hip firing (ill get back to that) its still a wonderful weapon, but the crosshair is kinda bad for sniping in this game being so small. the assault rifle upgrade though? overpowered. literally best weapon, dealing so much more than anything else, the only gun that can make noticeable chunks on boss health bars(ill get back to that as well) it just became my most used gun, with using the others for rotation clearings. the venders, you cant mute their voices and it was irritating hearing them after awhile lol. also i'm not sure if there's any sort of map, but i couldn't find it, and some places could really use something like one. turbo time also while nice i used once and then forgot it ever existed. just abit too many things in this game, but you know? _childDocuments_.review: It's impossible nowadays to play a arena boomer shooter and not compare to Doom Eternal or Ultrakill.I finished the game on the second to last difficulty, so my review is based on that.Turbo Overkill is super fun. You have more weapons than you can count, with many variations.They twist your gameplay all the time. New power ups, mods, vehicles, abilities, transversal moves. You can customize your experience like in Ghostrunner.Also, many movement options. Double jump, slide, wall run, grapple, rocket launch. You can grapple your rocket? Also there's a telefrag sniper? This feels like Quake on crack with ADHD, just go nuts.Game progression is good and will not make you feel overwhelm. Everything is gradually introduced to you.Story is good and the voicelines are funny. There's also many references and homages to other games and pop culture.The arenas are fun and well balanced, but the map design sometimes make you feel lost like a metroidvania game.There could be more interaction between your weapons and the enemies. Some enemies are just bullet sponges and could be more fight while in air. Also I hated every single homing missile enemies. Anything that explodes deals too much damage and sometimes you don't even know why you died.Game runs well on my PC. Loved the retro-cyberpunk-synth/vaporwave style.8/10 waiting for Turbo Overkill 2.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Turbo Overkill is a fantastic love letter to the retro FPS genre, the story is oddly charming with likable characters despite largely being an excuse for 'go here and shoot anything that moves', the soundtrack has no right that good, and most importantly it's just good old fun.However there are some flaws I had with my hours with Turbo Overkill. Some enemy types can feel quite bullet sponge-y, some levels can drag on for a bit more than they should, some checkpoints can be wildly inconsistent with the amount of enemies you're expected to fight through again, and some of the boss fights go overboard with the amount of phases they have.Overall it's a good time. Good hunting, sir!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insanely fun.  It's on par with Doom (the new ones) in terms of feel, satisfying gun play, control, and near-meditative immersion. The music is fantastic and encourages you into a sublime flow-state of play.  I've enjoyed the hell out of my time in this but there's one gaping flaw in this whole picture.  The boss fights!  The actual challenge aspect of it is really fun and well-realized, but starting a multi-stage fight OVER AND OVER AND OVER from the very start is annoying at first, hateful after some time. The boss fights get progressively more terrible and annoying as they go on. The Maw one (the third if I'm counting correctly) is particularly egregious. No more slowdowns, god knows how many stages, and music which was cool at the start wearing out its welcome.  Oftentimes the AI loads in with a damage ray that contacts you instantly no matter how fast you dodge.  At least let us re-start at individual stages, don't take away powers we expect to have, and consider having an option for allowing quick-saves in games.  The main gameplay loop is so much that it's staggering how bad the boss fights wind up being.  I'm not complaining about difficulty of these, I'm complaining about things being taken away from you which you expect.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, the game's great but... Little things all around just don't make me want to continue. Having ammo for the guns just slowly kills the diversity of weapons I want to use. I often find myself traversing the same place three or four times just to figure out what I'm supposed to be doing. The horizontal movement is on crack, but the jump feels pathetic. Often, the chainsaw slide will miss/get stuck on/do no damage to enemies and cause deaths for no discernible reason. Most of the time, I don't understand what is actually damaging me, how much it's damaging me for, and how worried I should be. 50% of enemy projectiles look like homing missiles. 25% are grenades. That last 25% are ??? Augments, at least where I am in the game, do not feel meaningful. It's... chainsaw slide gives you a little bit of survivability, and then everything else is more damage, more damage, more damage, you don't have to pick up currency anymore and useless. Currency is often annoying without the augment. Falling off the map, needing multiple passes just to pick it up, and after all the effort you buy the gun upgrades, the augments and feel like you have nothing to buy but ammo anymore. While I don't think the game's for me in particular, it is a fantastic retro-esque movement FPS with great music, enjoyable firing mechanics, and maybe a story upcoming. If you're looking for something to get away from the CoDs, the Battlefields, and the other boring sequel umpteenth franchises, look no further. Slide right into the action.
