_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is probably a better Doom 2016 sequel than Doom Eternal.In terms of formula, it's basically the same. Dash/jump/run around arenas and kill things, move on. But it's rare to find a game THIS carefully and what feels like intentionally made. Both difficulty and the options given to the player escalate slowly and almost until the very end. Be it new weapons, other abilities or augments for the player. And when you get the feelings things might get scale, the game throws something new at you like a (also very well done) vehicle level. The game stays fresh from start to finish and it's all killer and no filler. Both soundtrack and voice acting are stellar, especially Gianni Matragano and Jon St. John who might have done the best job of his career so far. Negatives would be nitpicks. One or two fights felt like unusual difficulty spikes in the curve. One fight especially took place in a room that felt far too small for it (alhtough I think that was intentional). Some arenas provide you with power ups which I sometimes overlooked. They weren't really hidden, just not placed right in front of you and when you enter an arena and the battle starts you don't really have much time to look around, except for the most obviously placed items. The big spider-like enemies with TVs for heads have a rocket attack that can be easily dodged if isolated (not so much in a frantic fight), but I felt it hits way too hard if it hits. And sometimes, albeit rarely, I had a problem finding my way going on... but never longer for like 30 seconds. Overall though it was just a stellar game, crafted and realized by VERY talented, skilled people.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is another hyper-fast boomer shooter, which have been coming up a lot recently - Ultrakill, the new DOOM games, etc. So what makes this one different? Well, firstly, the style and story are actually fairly interesting. The grungy, cyberpunk aesthetic city is dirty and gritty, but also it's full of life and has a real feel to it. The environments all feel like true places.Additionally, the gimmicks that it comes up with are fantastic and unique. I use "gimmick" here positively - I don't want to ruin them here, but there are constant new ideas and ways the game interacts with you.And to top it all off, there's the traditional New Blood seal of quality - movement and gunplay feels amazing, everything looks great despite the low resolution, and the minute-to-minute gameplay is so much fun. The guns are fun to shoot, and the enemy encounters are built for the perfect challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill puts you in the cybernetic shoes of the titular Johnny Turbo, your not-so-everyday space merc that gets tangled into a struggle for controlling a powerful AI called SYN. Things do get out of hand really fast, and Johnny, willing or otherwise, will have to save the planet (and perhaps the galaxy as a whole) to ensure his own survival.It’s a story centered around the topics of greed, lust for power and all the other wonderful traits oh-so-common in us fellow humans. It’s not deep, nor complex, but it’s alright considering the genre at hand - if anything there’s an amount of lore and info superior to what could be expected from an old-school shooter to begin with. The quality of it is more than passable, with some highlights descending (ascending?) into the macabre and bizarre, of course peppered with coarse speech befitting lowlives, mercs and other scum inhabiting the neon-lit dystopia of Paradise.Tremendous care was put in building levels, not only on a functional design standpoint, but visually, too. The retro aesthetics, featuring purposefully washed-out palettes and low-res models, blend superbly with all the modern tech goodies as real-time lighting, physics and advanced effects. More than a few times, stages will have dynamic, evolving backgrounds where battles play out, destruction happens, and mayhem usually ensues. Despite its fast pacing, Turbo overkill lets its art direction be appreciated and enhanced in smart ways.In general, levels have a linear but wide structure that develops throughout multiple height levels (exceptions apply), and can even become quite complex. Most environments feel spacious enough to take full advantage of the diverse mobility options at Johnny’s disposal - options you will have to use, if you want to get all the various secrets and Easter eggs scattered in the most unthinkable recesses of this crumbling colony. Other than achievements for the serial pain seekers, secrets unlock interesting gameplay modifiers and secret levels for each chapter, so they’re definitely worth your time. For the rest, levels play out in the classic old–school fashion, which features color-coded keys, switches and at times objectives to clear, arenas to conquer before being able to proceed. The crown jewel of TO, combat is extremely fast paced, high-stakes and surprisingly deep. Only a few hits from stronger enemies will be enough to demolish you on the higher difficulties, but there are ways to counter that: a fluid, intuitive movement system comprised of sliding, dashing and jumping allows you to combine these features into acrobatic evasion, often granting you temporary i-frames that negate damage - even more so with specific upgrades. Your arsenal features weapons with multiple fire modes, each suited to specific situations and moddable with upgrades which alter, even significantly, their functioning. The bread-and-butter of combat is, however, Johnny’s signature chainsaw leg, a lethal slide-based melee weapon that will be critical to staying alive, as it’s one of the few ways to generate healing / armor from foes with the right upgrades - and since on higher difficulties medkits are only dropped from kills, you’ll need that a whole lot. A selection of gadgets, both offensive and defensive, will also be unlocked, like the micro-missile implant raining destruction on your foes, or the Turbo Time, slowing everything (including you) down and dropping extra goodies from each kill. Temporary upgrades boosting damage or even granting invincibility can be sparingly found in the more difficult arenas and sometimes bosses; you should save them for when crap really hits the fan. The arenas are challenging but fair, and feature multiple waves of enemies as customary. The checkpoint system is fair and respects your time while not being excessively forgiving: it strikes a great balance, and there’s also manual saving, although not at the higher difficulties.Boss fights evolve as HP goes down, and usually feature additional mobs in-between phases (and sometimes alongside the boss itself) - normally, a boss fight relying on “adds spam” would be a sign of bad design - however, in this case, Turbo overkill uses such enemies to give you a chance for recuperating HP and Armor, so it’s actually something to look forward to. Killing enemies will always drop coins, in turn used to buy Augments for both your cybernetic body and weapons. You’ll be able to decide your own “build”, and assign the augments you prefer to focus on offense, defense, utility or a mix of all these combined, based on each augment’s passive trait. Some of them can’t be bought, but are instead found in TeraTek crates, opened only with a secret key well-hidden in each level. Weapons are instead upgraded in a “straight” manner, gaining new functions and always being better versions compared to the previous one. It’s a compelling system that makes it worth it to get 100% kills in all levels, as well as secret-hunting for keys or money stacks, because you’ll definitely need all the cash to buy augments as soon as possible, on higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: I came, I saw, and I kept sawing – and to think I almost skipped Turbo Overkill, figuring it was just one of the dozens of retro shooters that seemingly get released every single month these days... It is not! Instead, , and it should get way more attention than it’s getting at the moment! If you give this game a chance, it will utterly steamroll you with its countless awesome gameplay ideas, intricately designed lengthy missions, beautiful set-pieces and even a proper story that ties everything together without detracting from the gameplay side of things. .Turbo Overkill follows the high-mobility shooter style you may know from games like  or, more recently, . In stark contrast to id Software’s most recent release, however, . No forcing the player to use insta-kill buttons because of a ridiculously limited ammo capacity, for example – Turbo Overkill gives you all the tools you need, and then some!In fact, I think that ‘excess’ is the defining term I have in mind every time I think about Turbo Overkill. And I mean ‘excess’ in the most positive way possible! From boomsticks to orbital lasers, from grappling hooks to micro-missiles and from slow-motion to double-chainsaw berserk mode, . It even throws some vehicle missions at you – and manages to make those feel awesome instead of limiting, to boot!Level design is another area of Turbo Overkill best described with the word ‘excess.’ Sure, 25 missions spread across 3 episodes may sound like a pretty standard number, but , making me feel like I played double that number – with not a single dull second to be found. And I’m saying that as someone who tends to get a little tired of non-stop action after a while. Turbo Overkill held my attention throughout by  over the course of its 25 missions. And while I felt that , the fact that I never ran into a wall of frustration or boredom speaks volumes, as far as I’m concerned. And on top of its campaign, the game also has secret challenge maps and a feature for downloading user-created maps. Once again: ‘excess’, but in the most positive way possible!Perhaps surprisingly, another thing that kept me fully engaged with Turbo Overkill throughout were its story and the deliberately garish ' meets ' setting. Sure, the main plot about stopping a megalomaniacal AI isn’t exactly Shakespeare, but  – a genre where many devs notoriously just handwave all of that away. Turbo Overkill manages to have its cake and eat it too, as .At the end of the day, I’d be seriously surprised if Turbo Overkill doesn’t become a true shooter classic in time. ! Perhaps, like me, you’ll end up falling in love with a game that you almost skipped because you took a look at it and thought “just another retro shooter, I guess...”

_childDocuments_.review: The game start off simple - short levels and basic weapons that you know from all other shooters. The only gimmick you have is the chainsaw leg which is very useful because you can replenish health and armor with it. Given all that you might think that this is just another retro FPS... But then it just start giving you more, and more, and more...Weapons have secondary modes which can be completely different from the main mode (electro-burst on shotgun, grenade launcher on sawed-off, flamethrower on minigun, gravity gun on plasma gun etc; reminds of Painkiller) or you can unlock upgrades that add something new to the gun.When you get used to the game's basics it opens up, starting with a flying car section. Levels become bigger but not a chore to traverse because you also become faster (as a player and as a character).And it doesn't stop there. E.g. you get to jump on speedy cars and trains, ride through the whole city on the bike with miniguns and chainsaws, jump around the space from one ship to another and then ride a robot.The level and arena design is great, looks like new Doom games. It's hard to get lost, the game always show you where to go without relying too much on objective markers.Visually it's gory techo-body-horror stuff. The graphics are pixelated but it's noticeable only in static. The music is also great and fitting, hard stuff during the fights and more ambient when you just run around.All in all, this is the best FPS of 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Very stylized, extremely quick gameplay with a large variety of weapons that have alt fire uses. In the second episode the options you have feel like a scan-tron to combat tests. exploration is rewarded with secrets and collectibles that get more and more obscure to find. I really enjoy how episode two gave even more upgrades to its weapon arsenal. One critic I have is that the fights (really only in episode two) can go on for a very long time and if you die at all you have to do it all over again. I understand it is a skill check to move further into the game but some encounters feel excessive. Still a great experience and it's not even finished in its development!

_childDocuments_.review: THE LAST SET OF BOSSES AND THEIR COLLECTIVE 100 FREAKING FORMS CAN SUCK MY CYBERNETICALLY ENHANCED COCHLEA!!!In short, first few levels are fun but after that, continuing this game started to feel like a chore, sucking out all the variety and action out of it.Then the game starts feeling like a Doom Eternal clone that forgot to implement the glory-kill health mechanic as a constant feature. What is more, unlike Eternal, quite a few weapons seem tacked on or their mechanics just a gimmick. You will even feel compelled to bypass most of the spongy enemies (and in fact most of the game) by abusing the chainsaw slide with the according augments. Enemies can pulverize you from off-screen in mere seconds.Art Style seemed competent at first, but soon things just became a shiny neon mess, especially when equipping any powerup.A Story is present...Sadly it gets dragged down by the horrendous overacting in the found audio logs, that try to be endearing like many cheesy 80s / 90s action flick but are just grating.Oh and the final cutscene sets itself up for a big final choice, but abruptly ends on a cliffhanger. What makes it worse, it shows you that no matter how much effort you put into defeating any previous boss in the game or how heavily any character gets mutilated, nothing is of lasting consequence, the stakes are non present and they can simply bring back any anyone, especially the most annoying characters which should definitely have stayed dead!But the Music is good!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Some are calling it a boom shoot and I would say that is not totally accurate. That being said, I think that most faces of boom shoots will enjoy this.Thing I love about this game: arena style combat, it is constantly introducing new enemies/weapons/upgrades/etc..., The combat is fast (like this game makes Doom Eternal feel slow,) the writing.Get this game! For some reason, it is always the rocket launcher, the next shots sends me flying, or the sniper rifle, that is only really useful as a travel gimmic rather than an actual weapon.Same thing happens when you run out of ammo..Also constantly hitting the floor in front of you, with the rocketlauncher, even though all the other weapons clear the edge just fine..
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game since Act 1 and seeing it evolve since then has been a real pleasure. The way the game consistently adds new mechanics keeps the gameplay loop fresh without making it feel overwhelming. Couple that with some of the smoothest movement in a shooter and great selection various weapons to play around with you get some of the best FPS combat of all time. At its peak when you are in the zone dodging everything, dishing out insane damage, all while flying through the air almost never touching the ground you will feel like a god. If you're only ever going to play one retro/boomer shooter make sure it is this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I hate to give this a thumbs down but I just can't groove with this thing. I may return later but I can't even bring myself to finish the levels currently in the game. The world design and general feel of the game is great but there's also a lot of annoyances that crop up after playing for even just an hour. The world design was what originally drew me in. The sound design and animation work on the weapons is superb, and the skyboxes are really a sight to behold. Lots of great secondary fires too, really love the pistol lock-on. Also, the chainsaw leg is obviously a blast. One of the best melee weapons in any shooter ever. It's tons of fun in the right levels and feels great to rev it up at high speeds. Unfortunately, level design is confusing and not full of a lot of clear indicators on how to progress. I spent a lot of times in these levels trying to track my way around and without a map it's very easy to get lost. There are also a lot of levels that require you to move very carefully too lest you get instakilled. Which is obnoxious when one of your most useful tools is the chainsaw leg which uncontrollably rockets you forward at 900 miles an hour. To add to the annoyance; good luck identifying any silhouettes during combat with this many particles flying around. It's excessive and you need to sort through a lot of visual noise in order to find what you are actually looking for. I can't tell you how many times I got killed by something I just could not see through the gunfire and explosions.To add to this, weapon damage and enemy balance is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Everything either does too much or too little. The double barreled shotgun in this game is an insult to all double barrels but it's alt fire does a ridiculous amount of damage. The SMGs feel way too inaccurate and do too little damage to be viable in a room with more than 3 enemies. The pistols too, that primary fire is so situational that the pistol is just going to become your occasional room clearer with the secondary fire. Enemies attacks are so fast and do so much damage even on just the hard difficulty that you can't afford to waste a second not putting enemies down which just invalidates so much of the current arsenal. The rocket launcher is pretty much the only thing that feels right, although even that feels like it should have a minor damage buff. It's a good base, but so many of the design choices and current balance of weapons makes everything feel off. I'd love to see the full release of this game dial in the level design a bit more, trim off a lot of the fat (Like seriously they don't need to be 30 minutes long). I would love to see a complete re-balance of the weapons and a visual overhaul to make enemies and their attacks more visible. I love dark cyberpunk aesthetic as much as the next guy but this is also a super fast shooter that requires split second reactions. And for godsakes get rid of that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dated upgrade system.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome! If you like action FPS you owe it to yourself to get this. I could get into details on why its so great but I don't think I have to. A good action FPS is one that flows and pulls you in, making you do cool stuff just because you feel like it. That is what this game does, the level design, the enemies, the weapons, your abilities, they all come together beautifully. Bonus points for having boss fights that do not suck and pretty epic scenery.My only gripe, and I'm nitpicking here, is the vehicle sessions. They are few and far between (thankfully) but imo they don't add that much. If you make the main loop super fun you better have vehicular combat to match it or it will feel like an interruption instead of an addition.But its a really small gripe. Go get this game, its superfun!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of low res textures it's more like "we have Doom Eternal at home" than a retro fps. Generally fun movement and shooting but has some problems (awful compass, some underpowered guns and laggy weapon wheel = too many weapons, half baked shop system that feels out of place, not really enough environment variety to support a third episode). Some things could improve with patches but just slightly above average.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane. Absolutely phenomenal. Probably the best combination of everything boomer shooters have to offer: ridiculous movement speed, sliding, dash, wall-running, grapple hooks, slow-mo, and much more. And each weapon is satisfying, visceral and functional - the upgrades make them go even further, in ways that will genuinely surprise you. The game never stops changing, throughout.Seriously, if you love games like this, then this might become your new favourite. Definitely not perfect though: some cheap deaths occasionally, and some of the boss fights have somewhat frustrating design. The story is interesting enough to follow, but not remarkable. It's also a much longer game than you might expect, which isn't a bad thing, but it can wear you down by the end. The aesthetic of this game is fantastic, and it evolves more as you progress, with each new 'Act' creating a massive shift in your surroundings. I couldn't even believe this was the same game I was playing at times! Other than one MAJOR frustrating part in the final level, and a few other minor gripes, my experience was significantly positive. I HIGHLY recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Top 5 FPS games I've ever played....and I have played A LOT. Think this actually might be my favorite...its just good fun....and it gives you what you want out of a boomer shooter, super satisfying all around. Music slaps, movement is great, great level design, gore, upgrades keep things interesting throughout....can't say enough good things about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe how amazing this game was to play. Not only is the combat extremely satisfying, and the upgrade system and mods very engaging, but the story was also very gripping, and kept me wanting to play more. Triple A games keep blundering about not knowing what the ♥♥♥♥ to do while this game completely blows anything they've produced out of the water. aside from some annoying bugs this is a 10/10 must buy for any shooter fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: So after beating turbo overkill on the 2nd hardest difficulty (my save got corrupted for the hardest difficulty like 9 missions in and i wasnt gonna go through all that Again on the hardest) i must say: This is an amazing game with niggling flaws at best.Its fast, but fast in a precise way, you must cut through the chaos like a scalpel with machine guns, and ALWAYS KEEP MOVING. the weapons have great synergy, the coolddowns on the special attacks are tuned just right, the violence comes quick and punchy. if you like doom eternal, quake, shadow warrior 3, this is just the game for you. now for the niggling flaws...it relates basically to just my view on the boss designs in the 2nd act, ripper and maw, having an over reliance on TURBO TIME, a slow mo ability that gives you health and ammo when youre in it. I didnt much enjoy having to wait on cooldowns to replenish my resources...but i do have a suggestion, on the bosses, if you land the chainsaw kick it replinishes your ammo by 30% and health by 15. it requires skill, allows players that want to treat this like quake matches on steroids that treatment, and doesnt get in the way of turbo time still being part of the bossfights. also with MAW, in the second phase he hits me in startup when all the visuals are still loading in, so maybe just give him some delay there? its been awhile since a game caused my fingers to ache (doom eternal being the first and last game to do such) so i can day WELL DONE for getting me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: It's indie cyberpunk DOOM Eternal without the chainsaw handicap and more mobility. There's a good variety of enemies, weapons all have specific purposes and at least one alt-fire mode, the movement systems are excellent and have good customization options, the level design is fantastic, and the bosses are all well-designed with unique mechanics. It took me a while to power through the first Act because it just felt like a long tutorial in a tediously by-the-numbers cyberpunk aesthetic cityscape, but Acts 2 & 3 have a crazy amount of environmental and aesthetic variety. In fact, despite looking like a low-brow boomer shooter on paper, this game addresses cyberpunk themes better than most other recent games in the genre and slowly adds more biopunk and body horror elements.There's a lot of bang for your buck here and it's definitely better than most nu-boomer shooters I've played. The only objective problems I can think of were some high tier enemies having too much health, enemy explosive weapons doing too much damage, and some bosses being a slog because of lack of checkpoints. This all might've been just because of bad difficulty scaling though because I was playing on Hard. Definitely worth picking up if you enjoyed Doom Eternal's design but thought it was missing parkouring chainsaw legs. Overall, Turbo Overkill was a blast and was much better than I expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Post completion of first EP TLDR: Orignally gave it a recommend but now changed my mind. Meat of the game is still fun but all the issues i've mentioned before is even worse. Core mechanics and features need to be cleaned up, bugs need fixing, and some missions reworked.The core foundation provides a lot of potential but everything else on top of it harms the game. Still early release, so things may change.6.5/10Gameplay : Core loop = good but game mechanics don't work well together or not thought out well enough.Graphics : GoodMusic :  GoodStory : Arena shooterBeat EP 1 on level 4 difficulty. Previous TLDR: Meat of it is decent enough to recommend  the requires a lot more finesse in game play, control, and even basic necessities. If these particular things arn't fixed, then my review may change---- : Visually very cool and works well. Stylized, so don't expect the most realistic anything.B/c it leans heavily into the Neon cyberpunk style, don't be surprised when you start having difficultly seeing enemies. Take bloom, neon backgrounds, neon gunfire, neon enemy gunfire, gore, retro visuals, and your very fast default movement speed, don't be surprised if you end up having difficulties seeing what you want to see or end up spraying into a blob of enemies hoping for the best.I turned off gore, bloom, and some other stuff.: If you like EDM, you will like this. I am an enjoyer of toaster music so no issues from me.:Turbo does not fall under the same lane of Doom Eternal but more along the lines of classic-esq modern arena shooters like Ultrakill and Dusk.Movement is fast and there is a lot of action so you won't stay bored. The foundation is there but everything on top of it needs improvement.The big issue is weapons. They are boring and need better identities.  is basic starter weapon. Alt fire is kinda cool but the issue is that its not that good against heavy enemies while very good at light but you usually would want to use the chainsaw slide in order to get health and armor back (if you have these upgrades). Goto "long range" weapon.: Very boring across the board. DPS weapon with Alt fire is a single smg for long range engagements. Why use SMG when magnums can do long range engagements? Why use uzi for DPS when you got machine gun? Needs better identity: Always fun in arena shooters. Alt fire is a stun grenade that stuns sometimes. TBH don't know how its suppose to work. However, it feels bad to use due to animation lock. Maybe i'm bad but there been many times i missed due to only wanting to quickly fire it but didnt fire soon enough so it does the next animation. There is no cancelation, so very often don't shoot when you actually want to shoot. This should be reworked to mach how there is an option for the doublebarrel in settings to make Alt fire just load in shots when left click fires.l: Bigger shotgun. Alt fire is also a grenade but now it bounces and sticks. Pretty fun : Machine gun. Alt fire turns to a flame thrower which is kinda cool but not sure the purpose of it is thou. Doesn't destroy heavy enemies fast enough compared to shotgun/doublebarrel combo and you should chainsaw smaller enemies for resources or to save ammo. Maybe make a fire a damage debuff or something. : Rocket. You can weapon swap combo with the shotguns and rocket but ammo issues make it difficult to do.Below i go into deeper detail: Arena Shooter: Below i'm just going to rapid fire bunch of issues that really should be addressed. - : Saving in this game is buggy. At my 3 hour mark, i was at Level 7 but when i pressed continue, it brought me back in the middile of 5. After level 8, for some reason it changed the difficulty to 1. Just needs fixing.-  : Fixed in recent hotfix. - :  IMO probably the biggest thing that needs improvement. This is just my take but: AMMO = ALLOWING YOU TO PLAY THE FUN PART OF THE GAME. Completely backwards thinking where you are not provided enough ammo despite the action scenes getting bigger. PLUS higher difficulty don't have access so buying ammo DISPUTE PROBABLY USING IT MORE. Compounding the bad weapons, this feels very bad. I use up all rocket and shotgun ammo having alot of fun then i have to waste my time using the boring weapons. Plus later levels you at literally fighting previous bosses as mobs. The amount of enemy health you need to clear is so much higher. In theory weapon swap/combos and stronger weapons will counter this (and thats a good thing/weapon swap=fun) but you dont get the ammo to do so.Make the weapons better AND give more ammo AND allow the ability to buy in higher difficulties. -  : Man i think the SMG/Machine gun is so boring to use. Not helping that you drain through shotgun and rocket so quickly. Like i mentioned above, ALT fires need to be reworked to be more interesting. Weapons need better niches and identities - : Higher difficulties should not have faster bullets, it should have higher bullet damage to reward good movement. Faster enemy bullets = less rewarding to movement which is in contrary to Arena shooters. Unironically hiding behind and using the magnum auto targeting and cover becomes viable. - : I die a lot in these types of games b/c i play like a spider monkey on the verge of overdosing. Mixture of movement, weapon swapping, and close range encounters. The issue is when I die alot but get spawned about 2 set pieces behind. IMO makes no sense.-: The car level should not be in this game. Not only is it not fun, its contrary to every other game system. When i'm playing a RTS, I don't want to suddenly start playing a rhythm game. Plus the map on this level is not good. I remember spending about 10 mins trying to figure out where to go, then learning there is a small section of water that blends in with everything else you need to go through. And then i have to restart the level in another part of the map b/c the "do no pass" red walls wouldnt go away so i had to play this boring level AGAIN.-  : I only use the chainsaw leg b/c i attached the armor+health upgrade or for movement speed. The chainsaw leg needs to be better. Not only are you putting yourself in a disadvantage position by running into enemies that can kill you pretty quickly, you get no benifit out of it. Why use chainsaw when you can use flamethrower? Why use chainsaw when a grenade does the same thing? Like i mentioned, the ammo/health upgrade is the only thing i use b/c it at least provides some benefit to the cost. How about making this built in so it gives other upgrades more time to shine? Overall it needs an identity other than "Chainsaw leg is a chainsaw". Make the game work with the coolness of the concept.- : Everything i mentioned above compounds each other. Only a few cool weapons -> use more often -> less ammo -> forced to use boring weapons -> not funMeat sponge enemies -> use stronger weapons -> less ammo -> later levels have 10x more meat sponge enemies -> no ammo -> not funIf more EPs come out, i will play them and maybe change my review. I did have fun with the game  these issues became a consistent issue, making the holistic experience sour.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta be the negative Nancy here. Mainly because the highest difficulty "Murder Machine" is so ridiculously unfair, it's crazy:No quicksaving, even though the game has quick saves otherwise, no health or armor pick ups except from some enemy drops (Like WTF), most enemies (even the weakest ones) can one-shot kill you, or at least take away most of your health in a blink of an eye, enemy projectiles are either hit scan or so incredibly fast and numerous that it's either impossible to dodge them or completly luck based.Because of the no health or armor pick ups basically your only way to get back health and armor is by having certain implants and then doing chainsaw kills. This is fine when you have low tier enemies to kill but not when there are only high tier enemies left.I played a lot of old school fps and I usually play my first run on the highest difficulty and sure it was hard at times, but never as hard and unfair than in this game.What pisses me even more off, is that this game has an achievement for beating the game on the highest difficulty (Unlike for example Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal or Doom 1 and 2 in Doom 3 BFG Edition which all have ridiculously hard highest difficulty but thank god no achievement for beating it). And despite all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I managed to beat most of the game on it, even though a lot of the fights took me like 50-100 tries, maybe even more. Yeah, was very "fun"But then you get to the boss fights which are even worse. And for some reason the devs thought it was a good idea to include 3 bosses just in Episode 2. Episode 1 had 1 boss fight which is more than enough. I managed to beat the first boss in Episode 2 but the other 2 are so extremly unfair I couldn't beat them. Honestly they would be doable if they would at least include check points after every boss phase, but that would be too fair I guess...So, what did I do: Well, during the game you collect tech chips in secret areas. And each of them varies the game which you can activate through the main menu. Some of them make the game even harder but some are basically cheats, like insta gib (which for some reason works on some bosses but not all), infinite ammo (which isn't even needed as the game gives you way too much ammo) or infinite turbo time. Thank god those cheats do not void the achievements, so after having tried those bosses way too often, I decided to use them at those points.I "love" it when a game is that hard you basically have to use cheats to beat it...Yeah I get it what some of you might say: just lower the difficulty. Yeah, fair point but in my opinion a game on a highest difficulty should still always be fair and doable if you properly learn the game (which I did).But what about the rest of the game:Well, honestly the rest of the game is mostly fine but still far from perfect:-some of the weapons are so weak, like the super shotgun (which is a crime in itself), the chaingun or the plasma gun, basically after some upgrades you just need a few weapons to effectively kill enemies, namely the regular shotgun (only for alt fire), the assault rifle, the rocket launcher and sometimes the sniper.-soundtracks: some of them are really good, others some annoying techno bs-the devs tried to include a story but that was so boring and generic, they might have just cut it entirely, same with the characters, all but Sam were super annoying, sometimes dialogues are even pretty cringeSo is it all bad? No, of course not. At least the non-boss fights are mostly quite fun if you ignore the underpowered weapons. If you don't care for achievements or beating a game on it's highest difficulty, this is a decent old school fps, otherwise it's just pain and because of all the pain this game gave me, I have to rate it negative. Cry about it.Honestly the best way of playing the game is to play your first run on the second highest difficutly unlock all upgrades and collect all tech chips. Then if you care for the highest difficulty achievement, just use the cheats to beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a hell of a time up until the final level which contains 4 timed challenges. _childDocuments_.review: By far one of the best indie singleplayer boomer-shooters out there.Turbo Overkill is more than a love-letter to the retro-FPS genre; it's a game made with soul and passion, and this becomes clear after every passing episode in the game: the tools in the gameplay soundbox, the soundtrack and the scope of the story keep growing larger until the end. It. Just. Keeps. Getting. Better.In addition to excellent gameplay, this INDIE title features plenty of fully-voiced cutscenes (skippable; usually placed at the beginning of levels or during key boss fights).Side note: in Early Access/throughout the game's development, there were a couple of levels/areas that just didn't 'click': the final boss of Episode 1 and the motorcycle level in Episode 2 come to mind. The developer took the time to rectify these levels in Early Access all the while developing the masterpiece that is Episode 3. This developer clearly CARES about their product.This game is a STEAL at this asking price. Buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters I've ever played. Obviously a lot of comparisons will be drawn to Doom and Ultrakill, but I think this game outshines them. It's not hard as all heck if you play on a reasonable difficulty, but the high difficulties are suitably punishing. Every gun has at least one alternate fire mode which I freaking love. Every single level tries to introduce something new, whether it's an enemy, gun, ability, etc. Graphical style isn't just a novelty, it really helps with environment design and the feel of the combat. Every head explosion and insta-gib is very punchy and crunchy and feels like there's impact to your shots.The story actually has me hooked. Very little is revealed about our protagonist, and he can't speak, but I need to see this story to it's conclusion as I feel the bad guys are owed some serious payback. Most importantly, the soundtrack is banging. Every stage has it's own theme, and there isn't a single bad one. Furthermore each stage has a 'Half-way' or 'Third-of-the-way' point where the music shifts to an alternate version of the same track, usually just after you've acquired a new way to spell "♥♥♥♥ you" in your enemy's blood all over every nearby surface, so it ramps up the feeling of increasing in power ten-fold.Some detractors do exist. The game has differing versions of 'kill-floors' some of which actually mean instant death and some mean you get teleported back up in real time. It varies by stage and area, and it's fair, but nonsensical. The hardest difficulty can sometimes be a case of 'stop moving for 1 second and you die' but I'm enjoying the hell out of it and the checkpoints are mostly decent. There's no way to track WHERE the last few enemies are on the map if you're aiming for 100%. Everyone spawns in with a loud noise and a flash of light and will attack you relentlessly, so they're easy to see, but every so often you'll miss one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the corner of a room he blends in to. So far though I think 100% enemy kills is just for bragging rights. Lastly, and sad to end on a downer, the chainsaw bike is not as fun as you might expect. It's a cool feature but feels like a rollercoaster with no safety brake, not a part of the game you can master like the regular combat, It's only made one appearance though, so not a major impact on the experience.*Edit: they changed it to a hoverbike. It now handles 10x better and the entire level was revamped around it. This developer really cares about making this the best experience for it's community.

_childDocuments_.review: Been following the development of this game since its announcement and was excited to finally get my hands on the game after the open beta and wow was I not disappointed.Not only can you tell how much effort was put into the shooting but damn did they really go hard when it comes to the sliding, seriously the chainsaw leg is the best tool in your toolbox and they didn't waste a single opportunity to allow you to rip enemies to shreds with its overpowered wrath. Theres barely any need to dash once you use a speed upgrade on the leg, it becomes a third dash when in the air and is a massive speed boost in combat, letting you dodge damage while one shot killing all the annoying, squishy enemies while also farming health.truly a new classic weapon, im in love.The upgrade system is a welcome change of pace from many of these new age classic shooters, I had to sit and really think about my choices when selecting new upgrades with most being useful and only a few seeming useless, for my playthrough and build anyway.I only encountered a few bugs in the game, most of which were me chainsaw sliding through the map by accident or getting trapped in a corer while sliding needing to rocket jump to free myself. the only bug that had me worried involved the car, if you reload a save from either dying or loading a quicksave you find yourself in a random room, but if you press the key to leave the car you just teleport back to where you were, weird one there.Anyway, cant lump much more praise on the game, level design: SICK, enemies: SICK, weapons: "Can destroy entire rooms" SIIIICKCant wait for the full release and dont regret supporting this game, truly one of the greats!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game and must play for single-player FPS enjoyers.Clearly borrows many things from other shooters like DOOM Eternal, even down to replicas of certain level set pieces, but in most cases Turbo Overkill improves the borrowed designs and does them better (I'm glad Glory Kills were not copied). Calling this a retro or boomer shooter does not fully entail that this game actually has very modern and innovative things going on, in some parts maybe even the most modern.Thoroughly very well rounded and clearly well gameplay tested product, but there are always things that could be better. While soundtrack is superb, gun and combat sound design was the weakest point in my opinion. Combat and projectile visual clarity and seeing what actually hit you is other thing, and in combination with lacking precise combat sound design, these can make it seem slightly unfair at times, as this game can be "rippy" how quickly you can die.Even thought the game is about AI Syn, enemy AI is not particularly impressive or dynamic, but it's not the worst either. Gun and chainsaw balancing is often brought up, but I didn't think it was that big a problem. There are many great guns and gun combos available, and weak chainsaw would probably end up being more annoying than powerful one. Also I understand pace changing with vehicle segments, but I wasn't too fond of these when general movement is so good in this game, that I only wanted to leave the movement limiting vehicles behind. Replayed all levels in hardest difficulty and cleared leftover achievements. Game still held great on second playthrough, although I'm glad that I didn't do hardest difficulty on my first playthrough, as it would have definitely diminished my thoughts about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I have nothing but good things to say about this game. It's fun, it's challenging, and it's pretty much everything I could ask out of an indie first person shooter. It takes some of the best elements from Doom Eternal, Quake, Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon, and the rest of the cyberpunk genre to present one of the best games I've played in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: The short'n'sweet intro goes something like this: it establishes who you are (a cyber-badass), what you're here to do ( purge), then you dropkick your chainsaw leg into some cyberdude's face and off you go into neon-soaked rain. It only gets better from there, trust me!In a nutshell, we're talking a fluid -  (always a boon) in a deliciously dystopic cyberpunk setting (yup, still gettin' better). Speaking of getting better, a lot has been said & written about its chainsaw leg. You see, not only do you move across arenas quickly, you also turn a whole mob of trash into red chunks (as well as the customary pickups) while you're at it. ... and it still gets better with the weapons roster which is Syn-damned fun to use. _childDocuments_.review: It was a fairly fun and well made game at the start. I really enjoyed the pacing and the story-telling. However, after half-way point story completely derailed and branched out which was quite confusing and made me forget about the entire plot.Then a lot of one-off mechanics were added, like flying car, motorcycle and mecha sequences that serves pretty much no purpose other than "why not".But the worst offender was the quests becoming mindlessly repetitive. You can easily tell the developer looked for a way to prolong the lifetime of the game to increase play hours, which is understandable. However, the way to achieve this was simply gimmicky and diluted the whole experience. Simply put, one mission is divided into 5 different parts. So instead of "shoot corruption to clear the path", it becomes "shoot corruption in 5 different spots to clear the path". This essentially makes you do the exact same thing 5 timesThis method gets exponentially worse in further levels where each of those objectives get their own branch of several other objective. For example, you need to destroy a terminal in 5 different locations. However, when you get to the terminal, you need to "kill" each terminal 5 times before the mission is completed. So what could be one mission artificially becomes 25 different mission.Apart from that, boss fights also become repetitive, where one boss has 3 phases and each phase has 5 separate healthbars. So you have to kill the same boss 15 times. You get the idea.The game was cool at the start but it overstayed its welcome. The meaningful part of the game is basically half the length of the entire playtime. If not for that problem, it would be quite a pleasant experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk is an interesting and often misunderstood genre.What seems like a fascinatingly bright and colorful aesthetic at first glance is often underlined beautifully with social commentary and thought-provoking propositions both subtle and upfront. Beneath the superficial gloss of neon paint and shining lights, you will often find biting criticism of politics, corporations and capitalism. Dig a little deeper, and you will find yourself pondering more abstract quandaries; how much machine can you be, before you cease to be human? Does the thought experiment of Theseus' Ship apply to human? A well-written cyberpunk setting can leave those that engage with it thinking; about the self, about one's life, about where we're headed, where we came from, and about the nature of man itself. A masterpiece will have those that engage with it asking questions the game never directly proposes upfront. This game in particular poses one question about humanity, and so I  ask:Why on earth did it take us  long to name a man , strap a chainsaw to his leg and give him a crouch slide that turns people into red goo?The story premise is as simple as it could be; you're Johnny Turbo. Your left arm is robotic, your right leg is a chainsaw, and you get paid off to put a stop to the machinations of the AI Syn, whose major plan is to merge machines and man into one being. To this end, bio-cores have sprung up all over Paradise; a dystopian, neon-lit city of artificial pleasures galore, where flying cars zoom by at blistering speeds, where night-time is illuminated by billboards and bright signs, and where the horizon is a glowing mess of advertisement boards the height of skyscrapers. An already dystopian city, giving off a seedy vibe, and yet it pales in comparison to the future Syn has in mind for humanity. Throughout ruined buildings and along the brightly lit city streets, you'll encounter its increasingly nightmarish minions everywhere. These range from human thugs spliced with somewhat minor augmentations and brandishing conventional firearms or having their limbs replaced with limbs or guns directly all the way to more-  creations; barely humanoid mounds of flesh hopping on all fours and dispensing lethal amounts of electricity, augmented people ripped in half and still animated by the power suit strapped to their bodies and towering, worm-like technopedes armed with rockets and an ocular laser beam bolted onto a quadrupedal platform carrying its immense bulk around.Naturally, though, a game like this couldn't just let the enemies outdo a man like Johnny Turbo on the weaponry front, so you bring to bear your own little arsenal of augments and guns, the most basic of which are a pair of akimbo pistols with a homing secondary firing mode that, if charged for a sufficient amount of time, will vaporize lesser enemies in an instant. A lot of conventional weapons are present and accounted for even in Early Access; shotguns both pump action and sawn off, sub-machine guns, a minigun, a rocket launcher, and all come with an optional upgrade adding a secondary fire mode that you can spend your hard-earned money on. Could I interest you in an electric blast upgrade for your shotgun that stuns most enemies, leaving them vulnerable for easy dispatching? I don't have to, it's on the house, go ahead and give it a go.How about that twin minigun, bit too reasonable for your taste? How's about you pop off those barrels and use it as a flamethrower instead? With how close and personal the fighting tends to get, you'll appreciate having the option.Now, for the important bit; would you want to pay 2500 dollars for the ability to throw away one of your akimbo SMGs? ...Well, you should, because it comes with a lifetime supply of backup SMGs to pull back out in case you want to sacrifice accuracy and damage for spraying and praying again.And all of that isn't to speak of the upgrades for your cybernetic limbs that can further tailor your playstyle; do you want your chainsaw leg to be your main tool of engaging? Pop an augment in that increases the movement speed when sliding; damage is based on speed, so you're less likely to get stuck in hordes of enemies as you plow through, too, as a little benefit. Or you use it for sustain, and make it recover health and armor with each enemy killed? Perhaps you're not overly fond of the chainsaw leg in general; why not slap a mod in that makes you send out a shockwave after falling for a certain distance?There's plenty of options and they're all amazing. Combat simply feels good; the weapons are nice and meaty, movement feels great, enemies hit hard but always seem fair and manageable. Whether you blow someone apart with a sawn-off shotgun blast to the face or slice through a group of weaker enemies with a crouch slide like the Reaper through a field of wheat, feedback is nice and meaty. In short, despite only having one episode out so far, the game is already  promising; and not in that unfortunately common Early Access-way where it's an "everything is off but the idea of the game is nice so might as well give it a thumbs up I guess, hope it improves"-sorta deal, no. Things feel , they feel . You can tell a lot of care and effort went into making things feel good; it's a very inspired game, with a team that knew what they wanted to do, and by Jove, .It is  one of the best throwback shooters I have seen so far.Also it features a man called Johnny Turbo.Did I mention that? Because that's worth a recommendation alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when games used to be fun? This one does. At first I wasn't enamored because the enemies were a little mid, but it turns out they aren't supposed to be Halo elites- they're just fodder for your many, many toys. They just keep giving you cool explody toys and all the room in the world to play with them.Great map variety, and design. One problem I usually have with these retro shooters is that I'm often getting lost due to samey level textures and no map. Not here, the directions are always plain as day because either bright neon doors aren't open yet or enemies are spawning in X direction. This keeps the momentum going and dodges a common pitfall.Speaking of, the movement in this game is ridiculously cool. You have a chainsaw dash that is omnidirectional, plus two jumps and two dashes you can use in the air, plus other goodies I won't spoil. And the level design lets you use ALL of it. You are soaring through the air blowing up baddies and the devs don't care if you ever touch the ground again.Story is a fun backdrop for all the killing you're doing, but what they nailed is the constant escalation. You are always going to more and more ridiculous places and killing bigger and badder dudes. Vehicular sections are fun and don't overstay their welcome.The one issue I had is that some bosses are small and so fast that I have a hard time hitting them under normal conditions. Other than that it's an incredibly good time. Game just lets you have fun- a must-buy if you like retro shooters with an emphasis on mobility

_childDocuments_.review: One can compare this to many games (dusk, necromunda: hired gun, EYE divine cybermancy, doom eternal, ultrakill) but honestly it seems to beat out all the competition by incorporating their elements into a more cohesive and fine tuned experience than any of them. I think this might be the best first person shooter made in modern times be they retro inspired or not.Movement is fast, fluid and responsive and the speed is insane. The best thing about this is that the levels are clearly made with this mobility in mind being very large scale and accommodating to the mobility of the player. Often times you'll find yourself backtracking through levels finding other paths thanks to how non linear they are, running into newly spawned enemies guarding a door you previously weren't able to open.The way the game handles these enemy encounters is great too, rarely ever do you run into anything you could call a bullet sponge, instead most of the difficulty comes from evasion and quantity of enemies and it allows you to fully utilize the movement freedom you've been given, including a chainsaw-leg-slide boosted by rockets that can one-shot hordes of cannon-fodder. In-short this is a fast game about flow where a couple hits of enemy fire can mean the end in mere seconds. The weapons at your disposal are entertaining, each having an alternate firing mode to switch to that greatly alters the behavior of the gun. Some even feature three firing modes.The game also features an upgrade system that allows you to add behaviors and traits onto your body parts through cybernetic augmentation. These are meaningful and tangible effects that really influence how you play the game and change things up. An example is the ability to wall jump, another is adding extra chain explosives to the rockets from your rocket glove.Vehicle sections are placed evenly throughout the campaign and do a great job of breaking up the pacing by switching up the gameplay a bit, they're very entertaining.Graphically the game is serviceable, looking just about good enough for them to be able to carry the visuals through often solid and other times downright inspired art direction and the game runs very well.The story is simple and the tone is campy and over the top, being mostly there to set up the gameplay but it does escalate further and further as a relatively local conflict balloons into something much grander in scale.The music ranges from solid to great being made up of mostly synth/rock blends and during the final third of the game it incorporates orchestral elements that work surprisingly well and are somehow reminiscent of lotr and the matrix trilogy. Definitely get it, even not on sale, if you're at all a fan of fast paced shooter action you'll probably love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best single player shooter since Doom Eternal (Even though there's barely been any since). I've played a lot of boomer shooters in the last few years and this is the best one since Dusk in my opinion. This game nails the movement and shooting. The movement is very quick with the double jump and double dash. The arsenal of weapons feel great to shoot and i looked forward to upgrading them as the game went on. I like the art style and cyberpunk aesthetic the game has and it has a cool soundtrack accompanying the gameplay. The levels themselves are pretty good overall, there were some that were outstanding like the end of ACT 1 and i like how big the scale is in a lot of them. As for negatives i thought the story was pretty throwaway and the game overstayed it's welcome around ACT 3 because there wasn't many new ideas being thrown in to keep the engagement high. Overall i highly recommend to any fan of shooters. 7/10 (Good)

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic shooter and an amazing modder success story. I've been following Sam's work for sometime now and seeing him graduate into the indie scene with this bombastic shooter is amazing. In early access this is already buying as it stands, nevermind that there's almost twice the initial level count in secret levels, many unlockable features that change play style considerably, and that this is one of the greatest of the new wave of retro shooters. Dripping in charm, oozing with violence and pulsating with style, this is an indie shooter you should buy not only to support the work of a hobbyist-turned-professional, but for yourself - because god forbid you never get the chance to experience Turbo Overkill first-hand.EDIT: Turbo Overkill is my game of the year. _childDocuments_.review: Do you like Doom: Eternal? Do you like Cyberpunk? This is what happens if both of those games had really sloppy drunken sex. It's fast, it's brutal, but it just feels so good. The combat is turbo charged, with a dash and double jump system similar to Doom Eternal. You be launching off jump pads and switching through a massive arsenal of weapons regularly. Every weapon has an unlockable Alt-Fire mode, and all of them are just straight up badass. I won't say they're all necessary to make it through the fights, but they're all so cool and fun that you'll want to use them anyway. That is...when you aren't sliding around on your chainsaw foot like a cyborg motorcycle from Hell, grinding everything in your way to meat chunks. I would say it is on par with Doom: Eternal in fun factor, but it is a tiny bit more dumbed down. There isn't quite as much resource management or target prioritizing here. But I think that's okay, it's just a mindless shooter. Get in, kill hordes in 2 seconds flat, get out.The level design is fantastic, with big open areas that utilize verticality in the most fun ways, as well as tight corridors that make it all too satisfying to line up hordes of enemies and chainsaw them up. There are 3 video tapes and 3 blue chips in every level, and they're well hidden without needing you to scour every single pixel of every level to find. I haven't found any secret doors, and while that may be a bummer to some, I found it refreshing. I hate having to mash the E button while I face grind into every wall in games, so not having to do that here really lets you focus on the ACTION.Last but not least, the aesthetic and general vibe of the game is perfect. It's gritty and dark, while having the perfect amount of 90s game cheesiness and badassery. Your characters name is Johnny Mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Turbo, and you have a chainsaw for a leg, and you are sent to a city called Paradise to destroy a rogue AI named Syn. You're not getting anything too out of the ordinary here, but what you're getting is masterfully done for what it is. The noises, the voice acting, the billboards and posters on the walls...it all looks like it was ripped straight out of a 90s game and I couldn't be any happier with it.I love this game, I logged 7 hours into it after launching it for the very first time, and plan to log many more hours. I'm especially excited for this full release because there is a level editor and I'm hoping this game picks up and the community makes a slew of amazing custom levels!! I would say at sale price right now ($16) it is an absolute STEAL. Even at the planned $25 though, I would say it is worth it. You're missing out on an absolute GEM if you don't pick this bad boi up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite genres, so I really wanted to like Turbo Overkill but I just couldn't get into it at all.Experience:I breezed through the first handful of levels in 30 minutes without any challenge from the enemies, the biggest obstacle being the environment which all blended together which killed the pace when back tracking was required.Core Mechanic:The sliding mechanic is a nice idea, but in my experience it was WAY too OP, and given your seemingly unlimited arsenal there just wasn't any friction; I was plowing through the enemies with no issue but also without much satisfaction.Aesthetics:I also bounced off the aesthetics which felt really unfocused to me; a cute robot on the walkie talkie, a military guy smoking a joint on the main page, the borderlands inspired vending machines and the enemy design all felt like they were pulled from different IPs in a way which, for me, didn't come into an interesting whole.imo new age movement shooters like Ultrakill, post void and Chop Goblins do this genre right; simpler and more focused. Turbo Overkill just didn't scratch that itch for me; simply ending up with a load of cool mechanics and ideas crushed together into one over produced and scatterbrain package.

_childDocuments_.review: This *has* to be the most adrenaline-fuelled, manic, massively over-the-top thrill ride you can play today.   Whatever mechanic you like in your FPSes, Turbo Overkill's got it but polished to absolute perfection.The wonderful thing about T.O. is that if you can dynamically adjust the difficulty by pre-selecting the difficulty level and then adjusting it with tech chip mods. For example, I played at "standard" (aka Street Sweeper), and it was a nice challenge for a Doom/Quake/Duke veteran, with lots of high-speed combat in tight hallways and huge spaces, but I was picking up hidden "tech chips" along the way.  Collecting all 3 on a level gives you a game-altering tweak that can help or hinder.  If you fancy seeing what it's like playing as a porcelain teapot, sure, there's a mod that makes you die on the first hit.  But, if you've already done a level and want to replay it to get an achievement or missed secret, or you're finding a level too hard, there are mods that can make you pretty much invincible.  There's one that lets you play in slow motion all the time. There's another that gives infinite ammo, and one that makes all enemies insta-gib.   Even the most uncoordinated granny who's never seen a mouse before would be like death itself with those three tech chips.After I got about halfway through the game, I got a little fed up with hunting for ammo, so I turned on "infinite ammo".  By the end of the game I found my reflexes slightly too slow for the last few levels, so I turned on "infinite Turbo Time", which made those levels passable.But, be warned:  This game is friggen un-put-downable.   The levels are one long hyper-intense smash-fest at warp speed set up to give you maximum changes to rock like a god.   Anyone who played doom and tried the -turbo 250  command-line switch will know what I'm talking about.  The game just feels like it's running at a million miles an hour... But, like in Max Payne, as soon as you kick in Turbo Time (bullet time), everything slows down to a wonderful anime-like action sequence.  You can take your time lining up shots. You can speed over chasms and drop a few grenades down, or pop a couple of rockets into the mouth of a big beastie, and then land safely on the other side before spinning around and nailing a headshot at the sniper on the ledge above you...The really big warning is... if you play it long enough, when you go into the outside world, everything feels like it's in slow motion. I found myself driving almost too fast and needed to force myself to slow down.    This game is so FAST, and just so INTENSE, it makes your brain run at 250% doing jumps, leaps, shots, rebounds, dodges. It all feels so natural as well. The controls are beautifully set that you find yourself executing a ballet of perfect death, a whirlwind of chainsaws and miniguns, leaving just a fine red mist behind you.  So, when you turn off the PC, step out into that big blue outdoors, and you're "just" walking along, it's like in futurama when Fry drinks a hundred cups of coffee and he can see the flapping of a hummingbird's wings.   There's even a loading screen hint that says "If you want to know what Turbo Time is, drink 100 cups of coffee".. It's *EXACTLY* like that.   The weapons are AWESOME.   there's no "BFG" so to speak, but the Ion cannon comes pretty close, making the full standard set of FPS weps from Melee to OP exotic complete.  The sniper rifle that lets you telefrag enemies has so many brilliant uses,  it's an interesting twist on a mechanic I've never seen before.  The grappling hook can be used to wonderful effect at dodging and leaping, just like it did in Quake 2 Capture The Flag...Simply put, the devs have sat down and written a list of all the epic things they loved from Duke, Doom, Quake, Quake 2, Halo, Doom (2016), and a myriad other games and said "What if we put just the best stuff in, and leave out the filler".The music is absolutely gorgeous.  Some of the levels have their own themes, and the game itself has a theme that ripples through the pieces.   Taking on an army of mutants in Turbo Time while a thumping techno track blasts from the speakers... Listening to the bullets whizz by my ear in Surround Sound, listening to the distant explosions of monsters that just caught my rocket volley to the face...  It's all so wonderful.  There are also challenges and arenas you can test out your skills on.   Some of them are immense fun.I can't recommend this highly enough, but there IS a lot of bad language.  a profanity filter would be appreciated with possible alternate dialogue for anyone who doesn't appreciate the F-bomb being dropped all the time (not the wrist-cannon mod).  I often had to pause the game when my kids were anywhere about, lest they hear someone's dropping S- and F-bombs like confetti.I'm a completionist, so I've hunted all over for the tech chips and cassettes, hence the 60 hours playtime. I reckon a speedrun would be about 10 hours, with a solid playthrough  being about 30.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game that has weaponized movement as well as this game and it is absolutely phenomenal to play! Once all of the movement upgrades have been unlocked gravity is more of a suggestion as you weave around the map like an angry hornet bisecting enemies with your chainsaw leg. The weapon selection is great for an old school shooter, and there are some fun and unique options thrown in, like a telefragging sniper rifle or an orbital laser(that works everywhere). All of them served various niches and felt well designed and satisfying to use, although I'm not exaggerating when I say I killed at least 80% of enemies in the game(hardest difficulty) with the cheggs. Not only is sliding around cutting people in half a blast, but with the right upgrades it's not only viable, but one of the best weapons in the game! Also, you can grapple onto your own rockets!Level design was nicely done, and I appreciated all the platforming sections, it would've been a tragedy to have such beautiful movement mechanics and not get to flex them. Speaking of which I would 100% play a version of this that was just platforming too, love me some first person platforming! There were a good variety of areas and the developers did a good job of exploring some fun locations while still fitting the cyberpunk theme. The  freeway/train fight, fighting through a debris field in orbit trying to escape the planet, and Vector-4 where all some immediate standouts as far as cool locations go. Few games can make going this fast this fun! I would strongly recommend this one if you have a need for speed, or just want a quality retro shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, unfortunately not amazing.It does feel like style-over-substance, and it's noticable how there is a big coverage by Retro-FPS community in reviews, but almost 0 activity afterward, like in guides, let's plays and the like.I do, however, want to congratulate the small dev team for delivering a finished and good game to the finish lineI'll be honest, it took me quite a few attempts to "get" the game. I did find the game boring, frustrating, or tedious at first, even thought to leave a negative review.But then I decided to just get through to the end, and in the end, it clicked.I could not shake of the feeling of kitchen-sink design, that it's unbalanced and doesn't fit together well.I learned to stop caring and just go "chegg goes brrrr" and found the experience quite enjoyable.If you come expecting the tight and smart design of Ultrakill, lower expectations. Don't feel weird if you forget that you have certain guns/abilities/upgrades and use the same 2-3 guns on anything that your Chegg (titular chainsaw leg) does not outright instagib.Weapons do feel really kitchen-sinky, like anything goes, doesn't matter if it fits really.Like after 50h I still don't really know what's the tactical difference between two Uzis and Twincendiary Machinegun. And the flamethrower mod of above-mentioned gun? Game doesn't really give you great feedback on how much damage fire does, it sometimes obstructs what you are trying to burn, and also has confusing death animations, where grunts stay upright burning, and it's not clear who's dead, who's burning, and who managed to escape the flame.And same-ish problems occur all around your arsenal, they aren't designed to interact with each other really, there are only few clear interactions with questionable utility, like grabbing your rockets with plasma rifle. Oh yeah btw, how does Plasma rifle really fit in? Why, again, would I use it above my 2 machineguns, and it also has this meme-beam, at least it's not as bad as in Doom Eternal, maybe it's projectile grab is somewhat useful.Arsenal feels like it tries to copy Doom Eternal, but shares it's pitfalls.I only found useful altfire of Magnums, altfire of Waster shotgun, Boomer shotgun and Uzis, ah also maybe Rocket LauncherSee how I mentioned altfires? Because the primary fires feel like trying to kill an ant colony by shooting individual ants with a slingshot.I just overused the OP chainsaw leg and didn't feel good about it, as if I was playing wrongEnemy design is also at times questionable. For me it felt that either I would mainly receive inconsequential chip damage, HP rarely being lower than 80, but then I would catch some stupid and unfair attack that would 1-hit-kill me outright, with almost full HP/armor(main offenders being Sloth's rockets and armored flamethrower dudes).Higher difficulty settings only make this problem more noticable, and in general feel untested, unbalanced and lazy(yeah, hehe, x6.66 damage received, funny number, ah also way faster projectile speed, have fun catching instakill rockets with your head, no hp/armor pickups BTW)In order for me to start enjoying the game, again, i really had to start ignoring these issues, turn the brain off, and just enjoy blasting whatever

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent and very underrated boomer + story-shooter. Similar mechanics to Doom Eternal or Ultrakill with its unique art- and visual style set in a depressing Cyberpunk/Blade Runner world named Paradise. As a street cleaner, your job's cleaning the city of the so-called Syn virus. The story is good enough and becomes attractive over time. The game is divided into three chapters underlined with varied gameplay passages and levels. Clean movement and shooter mechanics with cleverly designed guns, all fitting for different situations, are building up to a solid gameplay foundation. Paired with a chainsaw leg, you will find yourself dominating a large horde of enemies while listening to the banging soundtrack surrounding it. Upgrades for components of your body can be bought and applied, along with purchasing a secondary gun mode for each one. Thanks to the well-thought-out level design, the game always feels fresh with new ideas, armory, and gameplay passages. Overall, it is a great game, with the only flaw being the music banging 24/7 instead of only in fights, making it feel more like background music. Give this game a go if you like other fast-paced shooters or shooters! Such a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: If Titanfall 2 and Doom Eternal had a baby, this would be that game. Combat is fast-paced, never overstays its welcome. Enemy variety is diverse, with boss fights being fun and well-spaced.Everything feels very punchy; pixellated gore and absurd visuals in low-res create a visual masterpiece that is just as big of blast to play as your micromissiles. The soundtrack is phenomenal, too; every level has at least a decent track, with some exceptional ones like Sunset Synthetica. Turbo Overkill is a 10-12 hour FPS experience; try it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is easily the best FPS game we've had since Doom Eternal, full stop. It almost doesn't feel like an indie game just because of how quality it is. It's movement is so smooth and so fun it puts most other movement shooters to shame. Tons of crazy weapons and enemies, and the chainsaw leg mechanic is really fun to mess around with. You can tell the guys making this just wanted to make something awesome and they succeeded in my books.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy Turbo Overkill? 100% yes! It's easily one of the best FPS game of the past five years, especially if you love Doom Eternal or Ultrakill then it's a no brainer. But that doesn't mean it's flawless, actually, not only it's flawed to the bone, it's also a buggy mess. Plus, 19hrs into the game, my save files got corrupted and lost all my progress. Fortunately though Sam Prebble, the lead developer, was kind enough to sent me a save file on Murder Machine so I could continue my game without starting again.In my opinion the worst part of TO is the checkpoint system, on Murder Machine you can't save and load, so on numerous occasions the game spawned me surrounded by enemies and it goes without saying that on MM they kill you with one or two hits, so it's pretty annoying. I believe that the Ultra-Violence difficulty on Doom is more balanced than MM is here, it's not a matter of "git gud" the game is just "♥♥♥♥ you hard" and doesnt care. In general, balancing is a huge issue.Last, the final two missions (TeraTek Showdown + Final Purge) are the worst levels in the game. Repetitive and boring, letting the game end on a sour note. I'm sure that in time the devs are gonna patch most of the issues, but there's no patching for those two missions, they are just bad and waste of time. It seems they run out of ideas by the end.I don't want to sound negative towards the game, I love it, but since I played it on the highest difficulty I got some tough love for it. Turbo Overkill has excellent gameplay, fast gunplay and the best OST of the year!9/10 (maybe a ten if they patch the bugs and balance MM difficulty)
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but this game is too damn good and too damn underrated for me to not write one. Turbo Overkill is an absolutely phenomenal game, and while it does have its issues, they're very minor or hardly affect the main gameplay at all. The gameplay itself is amazing, and if you want a good ass movement shooter like ULTRAKILL, this game is amazing. To summarize everything, the gameplay is amazing, the story is good(albeit a bit flawed, I still enjoyed it nonetheless), the mechanics are amazing, the graphics are straight up beautiful, enemies are fun to fight, and there's endless content in here! Literally, there's an endless mode, but there's also a level editor, secret levels and "tech chips"(basically cheats that you can activate) that you can unlock in every level, an infodex, custom difficulty which just got added, achievements, and a great campaign that's a blast to play and replay through. As of writing this review, I've unlocked 100% of the achievements, and I've got to say, Turbo Overkill nails what makes a good FPS fun! Highly recommend this underrated GEM of a game! My only issues are that the level editor can be a bit jank at sometimes(e.g. not allowing me to use the "save and play" button properly to playtest or freezing on the loading screen when trying to leave) and that parts of the story are a little lacking, but I can't really think of anything else wrong with it! BUY THIS GAME
