_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a title I've had my eye on. Getting more into point-and-click titles, I found the art style charming. The characters looked to expressive. How the story just seemed like two kids getting lost with adventure. A tale of whimsy and imagination. And while that is there, this title sadly falls flat.The music I think it was quite nice, but the star of the show is the visuals. The two main characters are expressive and standout. You can immediately tell each of their personalities simply by looking at them. As you make your way further through the game, each area feels unique in it's own way. Why the visuals are such an important aspect to the title is because of one thing: imagination. You really feel like you're exploring with the two and apart of their 'world'. How it pulls you in and makes you forget that all of this is just the two just having fun together outside. The visuals really hold the experience.The story is not really anything to write home about, but that's okay. Two kids completely being taken in by their imaginative play and needing to get back home. It's short, sweet, and simple. And sometimes, that's okay as you explore the world being crafted.The gameplay is the thing which pulls the game down. It's a point-and-click, but I find myself wanting more charm from what those games can offer. What is here is nice, but the game makes me want more. The puzzles are rather simple and don't allow the player to really look at that they have. There is no examining the items you get for thoughts from the characters. You can talk with characters, but there is no dialogue. It's scripted, usually telling you what the character needs to move on.Lastly, there are 15 chapters, but it really makes the whole experience feel more shallow. The reason are the levels are all fairly small. Each section is made for simple puzzle solving. The visuals and whimsy beckon you to explore the world these kids are playing in. And yet the game doesn't want you to explore. The game puts you in small spaces where it's hard to get yourself stuck. The puzzles are simple and leave you wanting, even near the end of the game. Everything just feels more flat when the game invites you in for so much more.Lost in Play is not bad. I wouldn't recommend it for a starter point-and-click, but would say it would be good for someone who knows the genre and doesn't mind something light. But the price just doesn't justify it. For $20, it's a game that needs makes me yearn for something more. I wanted more interactions with items, or at least commentary to hear the main character's thoughts some more. Hear them talk about the world, talk to the characters. The game just leaves me wanting. If you are interested, I would say pick it up once it's on sale. However, there are other titles for the same price which don't leave me with the feeling of dissatisfaction. Not bad, but something that is close to being something special.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like this sort of game, this is the sort of game you'll like. The attention to animation detail is fantastic: it would have been sufficient for the chicken to throw the nail in the air and catch it in her mouth, but having the chicken throw the nail in the air, catch it in her mouth, glance at the nail-shaped deformity now in her throat, push the deformity down her gullet with her wing, and then belch? That's dedication to craft. Small touches like this are ubiquitous. The puzzles are thoughtful and fair and primarily require that you pay close attention to the environment. As you play through the game you'll progress through self-contained scenes and leave the previous scenes behind, which eliminates tedious backtracking, inventory bloat, fruitless 'inventory to object' experimentation, getting lost, and other not-fun aspects that often plague point-and-click adventures. There's no padding--the design is tight and purposeful.  In addition to puzzles, there are a few mini-games (no action/reflex games). None are optional and some might be surprisingly challenging but not frustratingly so (YMMV), and there are zero penalties for failure--just hit 'retry' and give it another go. Most took me several tries, but each is fun and quite winnable.The voice acting--despite the characters speaking gibberish--is magnificent and frequently hilarious. Lost at Play is a winner all around.

So just be sure to help your kids pass the difficult parts... assuming you have what it takes to beat those nasty Orcs in cards!

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful little game!You play as a brother and sister (one or the other depending on the chapter, it switches often as generally one needs the help of the other) in their adventures which take place in their dreams for the most part. I found that the childish dreamy atmosphere was extremely well rendered, it's like the video game version of a (very good) children's book. The design is beautiful and consistent, the narration is poetic (everything is explained without resorting to any text or dialogue).In terms of gameplay, you need to solve puzzles to progress, typically there will be several interconnected puzzles at once. _childDocuments_.review: Lost in  Play is simple yet fun. With just enough challenging puzzles to feel rewarding. The story is chock full of imagination and adventure. From the moment it started it immediately drew me into the world of the sibling's imagination. And even though we experience their real world journey only briefly I thought it was a great way to ground the story in reality, if just for a moment.The game's point and click mechanics aren't complex. With each chapter you're clearly presented with goals for progress, which is something I appreciated. Albeit, this game wasn't very long, and it didn't need to be. The worst thing a game can have is filler for the sake of filling time. And if you ever hit a roadblock there's a hint system in place that can help you out of the various situations you're in. _childDocuments_.review: In a word: delightful! This game had the perfect balance of old-school adventure game charm and slightly trickier logic puzzles, as well as a fun little story that tied it all together. With its Over the Garden Wall vibes (I see you, frogs and cone hats) and seamless gameplay, Lost in Play is definitely worth getting if you love solving your way out of tricky situations. While classic LucasArts games will always be a favorite of mine, I love how Lost in Play created a slightly less moon-logic heavy game than classic adventure games tend to be. In Lost in Play, there are many chapters, and each chapter of the story has its own goals, its own puzzles, and, most importantly, its own objects. You're not going to be carrying around a quarter or a screwdriver from scene 1 throughout the entire game, wondering when it's going to become useful. Instead, whatever you collect has relevance for that scene only, and objects that need to be combined automatically do so in your inventory--yet the inventory object puzzles still require a little thought! Nothing is so complicated that it's impossible; I didn't need in-game hints or walkthroughs, making this a very welcoming game for newcomers to the adventure game genre. Because you're working within a limited space, there are really only so many combinations to try before you have your Aha! moment.On that note, the design of the game eliminates annoying backtracking, which is fantastic. While sometimes the beauty of an adventure game is finally realizing the unique connection between one object from one side of the map and something all the way on the other side, you know what ISN'T beautiful? Walking back and forth between them. Walking to every location trying to figure out where to use that roll of tape. Trying to combine every object in your inventory until you figure out exactly how the hell the game wants you to use them (and sometimes trying twice, because it really seems like that gum and that piece of string should go together!). Lost in Play has NONE of those problems. It leapfrogs all those hassles by creating fairly contained environments; you won't be wandering back and forth for long before you know what to do.And then there's the puzzles--by which I mean, occasionally you'll need to play a minigame/do some kind of a logic puzzle to escape a monster, persuade a character to give you an object, etc. If anything, I'd say the minigames and puzzles are a few steps above the rest of the game in difficulty, making it just a LITTLE off-balance. I'd say that in the narrative and the exploration scenes would be very friendly to younger players, but some of the puzzles and games get quite a bit trickier! If kids are playing this, these might be a great place for an older sibling or a parent to help. The minigames and puzzles are extremely fun and satisfying to play, though--I'd play a whole game of just these puzzles.This game is definitely worth your time if you want a fairly easy, relaxing game with a sweet narrative that still requires some thought. It's just the right length, too--you can finish it in 1-2 sittings, so it doesn't overstay its welcome or get boring. It's also incredibly easy to get 100% achievements, which is deeply satisfying to me as someone who loves a checklist. Definitely give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: So...I really wanted to like this game.  I'm a point and click game creator, I love the genre, and as others have said, the visuals are stunning, the characters adorable, the whole setting and concept is charming.However - about 2/3 of it is just bad game design.About 1/3 of the puzzles were good, well signposted, not flat out easy but just enough of thinkers to feel satisfied when you solved them.  Classic point and click adventure stuff.Another 1/3 were moon logic puzzles, what I call "guess what the author was thinking" puzzles, based either on actions you'd have no logical reason to take, or game functions you'd have no reason to assume existed (go back to -50 on the time puzzle, pan sideways at the keypad/guard puzzle).  The creators clearly knew how to signpost, they just failed to do it at enough critical moments to be really frustrating.The final 1/3 were the constant, constant, unskippable mini-games.  I'll be honest that mini-games in a point and click are a pet peeve of mine - they're usually unnecessary padding, "stretch the game time to make it feel longer" filler material that has no bearing on the plot.  And the creators here stuffed their game full of things exactly like that.  I only saw an option to skip a couple of times, and believe me, I looked.  After that I was trapped into non-plot-related games I didn't want to play, using a hint feature that often barely helped, and constant searching online for walkthroughs.  I nearly quit for good during the card game, and at the frog-tile puzzle at what should've been the climax of the game.  These things aren't satisfying to win - it's a slog that leaves you feeling like "oh man, finally, that's over with".There were also several "unnecessary extra step" puzzles that creators can solve easily with simple variables - if you have the inventory item a NPC is looking for, don't make the player character shrug like they have no idea what the NPC is talking about (like at the void door/pitcher puzzle).  Trip a variable so the player produces it automatically when the NPC asks.  For experienced point and click players, it gets an eye roll and some unnecessary extra clicks to complete the puzzle.  For inexperienced players, it's a "wait, what?  Am I still missing something?  I better go wander around pointlessly pixel hunting."I think the whole thing is so frustrating because it clearly had the potential to be something amazing.  The creators have art, animation, sound, and some puzzle design on lock.  If they'd spent extra time planning and designing better, it could have been a masterpiece.

The game is kind of split up into several hubs/levels where within each hub there is lots of point and click inventory style puzzles with an overall goal, mostly its to find various items that will allow you to proceed to the next hub. There is also several small mini-game style puzzles thrown in as well as some interesting movement based puzzles. Nothing too difficult, game flows along nicely.- Nice music- Lots of humor.- Great performance, 120-fps through-out.Cons- While the game is mostly playable completely with just the mouse there were a few mini-games were keyboard was required. Its strange because the first mini game I came across you could actually click on the on-screen representation of WASD but in subsequent games this didn't work so its possibly a bug.- There is voice acting, I'm not sure if its a real language or just gibberish and while it is very charming and I suppose fits the theme very well I still would have appreciated English voice acting for more immersion.Overall highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: "Lost in Play" is a FREE mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as a paid product, as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.This mobile app is admittedly charmingly animated, but that's the only good thing about it.  Simple, dumbed down puzzles, a mediocre narrative (at least it has one, I suppose), some okay-ish cartoon artwork.  But the games themselves, this being basically a collection of minigames, are underwhelming and somewhat dumbed down.  The characters also talk in Simlish, the gibberish that EA uses on The Sims, so there's some hope these mobile devs will at least get sued for that.  Scamming PC gamers is probably something they'll get away with, consequence free. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this mobile app?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $20 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  If you really want to play this, grab your iPhone, it's free.  Don't pay for it here. Charging PC gamers TWENTY BUCKS FOR A FREE MOBILE APP is disgusting.  This is a scam.  Just who do they think we are?

And if you get stuck, then there is always a very helpful hint system.Lost in Play is a gem for those seeking a relaxing yet engaging gaming experience. With its nostalgic nod to classic adventure games, it's a delightful journey that both newcomers and seasoned players can thoroughly enjoy.Recommended on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a traditional point & click adventure with a charming art style and endearing sound design. All of this is told with beautiful art.Some in the Steam comments dislike the fact that this game has such a high review score and have intentionally given it a negative review just to mention that fact. Ignore them. You will enjoy this game, even though it is simplistic. The puzzles are varied and some are fiendishly difficult. Highly recommended, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: CHILDHOOD WONDER   I am not really a fan of point and click games, I’ve got nothing specific to complain about the genre tho. For some reason, these games just don’t sync with me, Disco Elysium is a very good example: Good story, great gameplay, interesting protagonist as well as multiple dialog choices, and yet, it’s accumulating virtual dust in my Steam library. So that makes me wonder, why I’ve loved Lost in Play so much? What kept my smile throughout my entire playthrough? Spoiler alert: The answer is probably something cheesy like: “It reminded me of my childhood days.”  You play as siblings Toto and Gal, both embarking on an epic journey with lots of puzzles, visual spectacles and silly jokes. Throughout my short, but rich, 4 hour playthrough I've explored: a goblin camp, a haunted cave, a big desert, the open ocean and, of course, a living room. This game is the perfect example of quality over quantity, you will never get bored or feel like the game is not respecting your time.SIMPLE PLEASURES  The game is quite simple and it is filled with a variety of distinct puzzles for you to solve. Most of them require you to collect specific items based on the necessity at hand. But don’t assume that this is another one of those “Fetch” quests, the puzzle variety is quite extensive and there are a lot of mini games at play to keep you entertained. Every puzzle is unique in its own way and I was quite impressed by some of them. Luckily, the puzzles are not the only factor that will keep you entertained.  Certain games will never look outdated even after decades of its release. That’s the result of a good art direction, the visual presentation of a cartoon-style 2D game is timeless and won't go out of fashion in the years to come. And even if it did, I would still consider it a worthwhile experience.  Overall the game is quite polished and bug free, the performance is excellent and it works great on the Steam Deck, but there is definitely some space for improvement. The mouse and keyboard controls sometimes feel rather clunky and unresponsive, I highly recommend playing this game using a controller. Some specific puzzles are also frustratingly non intuitive, which made me lose a few minutes looking for something that was never intended to be found.VERDICT  I loved this game so much that I even got my wife to embark on this adventure with me. Its the perfect game to have a great time with your family and be reminded that even adults can get lost in play.Highly Recommended

The game's puzzles are mostly logic-based, and require the player to use objects and the environment in creative ways.Lost in Play features a variety of unique and memorable characters, including a talking fox, a giant robot, and a magical bird. The game's world is also beautifully designed and full of interesting details.Overall, Lost in Play is a charming and enjoyable point-and-click adventure game that is sure to please fans of the genre. It is a perfect game for players of all ages, and it is sure to put a smile on your face.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawlessly polished and relentlessly charming, Lost in Play deserves your attention for its imaginative storytelling alone. _childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is an adventure puzzle game where you play as a sister and her brother as their imagination soars. The game seamlessly transitions between the two in real life and their imagined world, in which a box with crayon drawings becomes a monster, a bicycle becomes a magical flying dragon, and video games become important puzzles that must be solved in order to defeat the big bad and rescue your friends.The game consists of progressing through chapters, where each chapter gives you access to a few screens, and you must utilize objects and NPCs in each screen to solve puzzles, win at mini-games, and ultimately complete a goal. In this way, Lost in Play is very much a point-and-click game, yet it is best played with a controller to walk around and interact with the world around you. I had a grin from ear to ear throughout playing this game. Every animation is adorable and relatable, every dialogue is cute and delightful, and every puzzle and mini-game is original and entertaining. The gameplay can certainly be considered quite slow, with many unskippable animations, which does hurt replayability, but I never once wanted to skip those animations on my first playthrough.Ultimately, given the short nature of Lost in Play and the limited replayability, I think the price is ever-so-slightly high and would recommend waiting on a sale, but would highly recommend this game nonetheless to anyone looking for some childlike fun in their life.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem, a thrilling quest that deserves a solid +8yo rating. From start to finish, it captivates players with its remarkable features. It has everything - nice graphics, amazing soundtrack, characters, imagination and good sense of humour of the authors. Humour plays a significant role in this adventure, with the authors injecting clever and amusing moments throughout. It's delightful to encounter unexpected laughs that add an extra layer of enjoyment to the gameplay. This lightheartedness balances perfectly with the intriguing story, which keeps players engaged The story is interesting and fun. The quests, while not overly challenging, strike a satisfying balance between entertainment and brain-teasing. Most can be completed without too much difficulty, but there are a handful that present a delightful challenge, taking even the most experienced players around +5 minutes to crack. It's a testament to the game's design that it can engage both children and adults alike, allowing everyone to participate in the adventure.Speaking of children, this game stands as the pinnacle of quests created specifically for younger players. In fact, it's the finest kids' quest I've encountered in the last 10 years. This glowing review is not just the opinion of a single individual but the collective sentiment of four individuals who found immense joy in playing the game. With unanimous agreement, they awarded it a perfect 10/10, solidifying its status as an unforgettable experience. Kol ha-kavod! Waiting for Lost in Play 2)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that will remind you of your childhood. The game follows two siblings, who play around the neighborhood. We experience the world as they see - trough the eyes of their imagination.The artwork is splendid, looks and is animated like a well made cartoon for children. The voice acting is done trough jiber-jabber, with animated chat bubbles that show you everything that needs to be shown. Outside of menus the game uses no words. Everything is communicated trough images and sound. The presentation is splendid trough the whole game, with no cut corners, and some surprising elements later on. As this is point and click game (that is perfectly playable on a controller) there are puzzles to be solved. One would think that with a game that looks so cute and childish all the puzzles would be no-brainers. But I actually found them all to be unique, interesting, and they usually require thinking to solve them. You might even get stuck on some. There's build-in hint system, but I've never used it. It's never really hard, but it respects your intelligence and perception just enough.The game is joy to play on a controller. The interface is quick to use and snappy. When you stand within the range of an item and choose something from the inventory it's used instantly, without additional confirmation, which works really well. Every action you do, including wrong ones, is animated. It's just gorgeous. There's also tons of minigames and riddles that take you to a separate screen, which also play very well.It takes about 4 hours to beat, which is just perfect for this kind of the game. It never gets to a point where you would get tired, and it will take you 2-3 evenings to beat. The game changes between both playable heroes, and they both get their time to shine. They are just siblings who play together, and it's warm and fuzzy.This is a game that took me back to the time I was 7 years old. Steam should have double thumbs up, even if it would be just for this game. Imagine it's what I gave this game.

The Gravity Falls esthetic is pretty neat and though a tad easy, the game is very enjoyable.However... The story of the game is that two kids lose themselves in their play fantasy and need to find a way home. So, there is no real narrative to follow here, the various set pieces basically could have been done in any order and you're playing these mini-episodes. Now some of the journey home is done in montages... and that comes across at "look how much bigger the game could have been, if you'd just given us more money at kickstarter". With a pretty steep price and only about 4 hours of playtime it tastes like you just sucked on a greedy middle-finger.Yet, on what we got, we can't complain. So, it really comes down to how much money you want to pay. I would easily recommend it at 10€, but I payed double. Also don't trust trailers or screenshots on what seems playable. It feels like buying a pig pizza and after paying the delivery guy eats 3/4 of it, leaving you with a kid's size pizza. But at least it is delicious.

_childDocuments_.review: First two hours gameplay: I am not usually fan of these point and click games but after seeing the art style I gave it a try and I am glad I did. This game is so charming and challenging at same time, you can't find many games that have these both qualities. Some of the puzzles were really hard and need to look carefully around to find a hint, there were moments that I went crazy and wanted to stop playing because of some of them but finding those hints and solving puzzles were really rewarding. name: Override 2: Super Mech League
detailed_description: Override 2: Ultraman Deluxe Edition Override 2: Ultraman Deluxe Edition includes the main game, Ultraman Season Pass: Containing 4 super-charged Ultraman characters – Ultraman, Bemular, Dan Moroboshi, and Black King. About the Game The gigantic robot brawler is Mech-ing a super-charged comeback in Override 2: Super Mech League! Seven years after the Xenotypes that invaded Earth have been eradicated, the giant mechs that were once the planet’s defenders are now their entertainers in global mech battle leagues. As a new pilot of these repurposed weapons of war, climb the ranks and represent your Club with a tuned-up roster of returning and new mechs, each with their own unique abilities, moves, and super-charged attacks. Override 2: Super Mech League is playable both in single player and multiplayer campaigns for up to 4 players locally and online in stages set all over the world. Start as a new pilot and propel yourself through the ranks in a deep and robust Career Mode. Join Mech Leagues and earn reputation by competing in Arenas located across the globe. Duke it out with a tuned-up roster of returning robots and new mechs across various versus and co-op game modes of up to 4 players online and locally. Defeat your opponents using an arsenal of unique moves including super-charged ranged attacks, metal-busting combos, or an arena-shattering ultimate attack! Career Mode: Fight in Mech Leagues and soar to new heights, aiming to be the best mech pilot. Represent your Club and work together with its members to earn Influence and rewards! Ranked Rumbles: Two Mechs enter, one leaves. Battle through the competition and climb the ranks to become a legendary pilot. Mech Mania: 20 playable robots including brand-new mechs with unique abilities, skill sets, and Ultimate moves. Hazardous Arenas: Competitive fighting grounds that include dynamic elements such as geysers, lava pools, and platforms that encourage strategy and unexpected outcomes. Upgraded Game Modes: Pick your playstyle across match types including 1v1, 2v2, free-for-all and several games such as Xenoswarm, King of the Hill and more. Expansive Customizations: Unlock a slew of cosmetic items and attachments for your mech of choice in the Garage.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic Arena brawler that hits every itch I could want fighting as a giant robot.  However it is very apparent it will be falling short just as its predecessor did.Override 2 was my hope at finally getting a player base that Override never had, however it appears the same lack of marketing is taking place so the player base will be non existent within a week or 2 just as the first, but that isn't even the most upsetting part that I was let down by when trying to enjoy Override 2 with my friends.The game has the new league system which is great! However, they added in 2v2, and multi person battles to the leagues but don't allow you to actually play in those multi person games with friends.  You and a buddy wanna go fight 2 other people out there in the world? Sorry, you can't.  Override 2 only has 1 way to play with your friends, in a private match versus scenario.  You can't group up and play against other people in the world you can only play in your small circle.  You also can't even unlock any items when playing with your friends unlike the first, so no fun cosmetics or new mechs are being unlocked if you ever want to play with your friends.Override 2 gave me tons of hope and joy again, only to crash it all down realizing they learned nothing from their first mistake of a game, and even dug the whole deeper removing any way to play a "party" brawler as an actual party because you can't even queue any games with your friends.Final quick point - you can't change any controller bindings in the game only keyboard bindings (the game being a console port to pc) which is kind of a joke of a setting to be missing on release at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Put it short.Game looks great, sounds great, weapons are actually nice addition now.And thats all I got from this.The joy I had from playing the first game does not exist in this game.This game has been dumb down, at it shows. Seems more like a "Cash grab" over thought out development. Seeing how the previous game used several years while this took.. what... 1?Here are a list of all the wrongs I found in my short but quick decision of "Keep or Refund" playtime.- There are now only 4 attacks. All tied to the attack buttons. Previous game had 8. No more Charge, or having combos. Only "This button does THIS specific move, and this does that specific move".      Sure you can do combos, but... the combos are eh...- Maps are super small- No more overheating. So all the attacking can be spammed.- No more special bar. Only spam.- Ultimates are now not tied to the players health, and more on "who can stand in the special charge circle the longest", which would been better if the maps werent 3 feet bit and if it was removed for charging your ultimate instead of a "king of the hill" thing.- No more Party controlled mech. Which is what I wanted from the Pre-release version of the first game.- The amount of new mechs are so small, it could have been a DLC for the first game, and probably played better.- No more Hover, and no more sprint either.Overall. GG on not building upon what the first game had for it, but remove tons to make a cheap "console arena battle game".For its price, its nice, but compared to the first game, or even all the previews and demo videos of the first game, nah fam.Hard pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna keep it simple: Pros: - Looks great and sounds great - League Mode is a nice addition - Mech variety is still wonderful - Ultraman (Even if it is Netflix Ultraman which is trash) - Throwing and the added air game - Ultraman Cons: - Loss of the original games controls (Or no option to choose between them) so now the game feels incredibly generic and not much like a mech game.- The grind to unlock mechs feels terrible and wasn't needed. - Loss of any sort of story mode (There was potential here for a story about the league and the people you meet in it, a new pilot, anything.) - AI clearly hasn't gotten any smarter. - Environmental destruction feels lesser since things just explode now instead of fall to pieces. - Maps are incredibly small and bland, they do shift and change at least in certain levels but it doesn't help the levels feel large. That would be better if the arenas weren't so small and cramped. - Always online. - Attacks feel so incredibly weak, ultimates especially just feel useless.- The heat system was a great way to prevent abuse, removing it outright not only makes things feel less mech but also opens things up to violent spamming. - Not much in the way of cosmetics. This game is disappointing in almost every single way compared to the first. It feels like something they should have tacked onto that than a proper sequel. I was looking forward to them building on the first game to make something truly amazing but that is clearly not what this is. I wanted to like it so much, and while there is fun to be had...just play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mech League (SML) takes the entire game in a new direction. For the uninitiated and return players, I will outline the differences from my experience. I will try objectively list differences with my opinions on the changes listed separately. I would recommend both games, though SML provides more content and would be recommended first.It is important to note that the fundamentals of fighting have changed since OG Override. In both games, each arm/punch and leg/kick was individually assigned to the shoulder and trigger buttons. This was a distinguishing feature in playing like a lumbering mech.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't wait for this game to come out.  I loved the first one.  the previews looked great.  the game looked faster and way more slick.  but when I started playing I realized that they had taken all of the things that made the first game out.  the unique way you control your mech was replaced with a much less intuitive faster simpler brawler system.  you no longer feel like a huge mech just a generic brawler like every other brawler.  they gutted the games mechanics.  here is a few of the features the first game had this one doesn't.  Co op where each player controls a different part of the robot.  feinting. parrying. flying. charging hits.  mech pilots and characters. a compelling story.   this game is a hollow imitation of the first game with no understanding of its success or its failures.  we needed a better marketing campaign to bring in more players to help the matchmaking which is an issue in this game already.  we needed you to refine the mechanics you had already in the game not take them all out and reduce it to a button mashing simplicity.   much of the game is luck now no skill is needed.  additionally the stages are bland boring and infuriating.  the ground moves on almost every single level.  I've already had opponents get stuck in glitches because of moving parts.  a lot of time you are fighting the game rather than your  opponent.  you can't choose which modes you want to play as they are presented at random.  you have to unlock mechs and cosmetics slowly and in a trivial fashion.  There was so much potential for this sequel but its clear the developer doesn't know what they are doing or what audience they want to appeal to.  stuck in a limbo between casual brawler and fighting game.  its clear that modus is in desperate need of better leadership.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I cannot recommend this game.  Though it is technically a sound game (at least for me) it just lacks so much the original game had.  Story mode is gone, now replaced by league which is default PVP.  You can press a button to force AI to be your opponents instead but it's weird you have to do that every single match in league.  The option to set if you wanted to go online or not would have been nice.  The only real sense of progression is earning cash from performing tasks during battles and earning short term sponsors.  You then just the use money to unlock basic customisation of the 'mechs and that's it really.I can see it being more fun as a 4 player party game but even the cooperative 3 players controlling 1 'mech has been removed.  The maps seems very small compared to the original game and the combat feels more streamlined which sounds good initially but now you can't do things like charge your punches and kicks or do double punches for example.  Everything just feels like a compromise to add a few more 'mechs and some Ultraman crossover content.This could have been the next war of the monsters but it just doesn't reach that level of chaotic fun.  Hits feel very weak, being knocked into buildings doesn't have the spectacular impact you would expect and matches can be over so quick it kind of ruins the fun.  4 player brawls are just button mashing madness, the AI is wonky in these matches as well being either super quick to react and pummel you with rapid combo's you can't counter very easily or they are braying dullards, standing in a huddle waiting to be punched into oblivion.For the price it is clearly a budget title but I can think of better games with more going for them for the same price.  Maybe worth a sale and if you can get some friends to buy a copy each it could be good for the party atmosphere.  Otherwise it just isn't worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the first game, but this one basically ruined everything that was good about it. I genuinely don't know what the developers were thinking. Everything is now hyper focused on PvP combat, but the combat is so much *worse* than the first game? If you *must* buy this for to feed your collection addiction, wait until it's 80% off....

_childDocuments_.review: Override 2: Super Mech League is an extension of Override: Mech City Brawl.   For those who have not played Override: Mech City Brawl, Override is cross between Pacific Rim and Rock 'em Sock 'em Robots.  Override 2: Super Mech League is mainly about your Mech fighting other Mechs.  It's a fun game and I would advise everyone to but this game.  After you have purchased Override 2: Super Mech League, you can also buy the Ultraman DLC.  I have been a fan of Ultraman for years so I was looking forward to buying Override 2: Super Mech League along with the Ultraman DLC.  To be honest, I feel that Override 2: Super Mech League should have been made a DLC to Override: Mech City Brawl.  Making Override 2: Super Mech League a DLC as well as the Ultraman DLC would have allowed players from Override: Mech City Brawl to enjoy this experience.   Again, I would give this game 9 out of 10 stars!
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I get it. It's not the same as the original, but that's okay. The original was a fun, story-driven homage to Pacific Rim. It had wonderful characters and the slow, methodic slapping around of enemies was great! However, it clearly didn't sell well and as much as that really does sadden me (it's a lot of fun!!!) I can understand why: modern fighter fans don't want slow. Modern fighting games have to be lightning fast, otherwise the snobbier players will dismiss it. Instead, we need to look at the sequel for what it offers, not for what it 'should be.' It's fun, frantic, and fast while still carrying a sense of weight to it (though I admit I feel like there should more oomph to each hit. The visual feedback is kinda weak.) The storyline is pretty much a throwaway but who cares? It narrows its focus to try and become easier for people to jump into for a few couch multiplayer bouts. While the original's combat is awesome for a single-player "kick some kaiju ass!", it was just too much for people to take in for a quick brawl with a buddy. Overall, don't hold the sequel right up against its older brother and say "You're different. No sir, I don't like it." Instead, enjoy it for what it IS: a shallow but mindlessly fun WWE with mechs.

_childDocuments_.review: Completely different game from the first.the first game was like a test run not bad but needed more time to mature through the likes of a sequel and then we get override 2 a different game from the first in too many ways and just like the first it feels like it is a test run that needed more work before release both games are like tech demos... they are playable no bugs or glitches from what i can tell graphics are good (better in the first game) gameplay can be fun at times but mostly dull most fun is had with 2-4 player splitscreen especially because the game has no community but as long as you have friends/ family its a non issue however this game ditches the story mode that the first game had in place of a lazy league mode that tries to force online on you and since there is no community you wait for long periods of time for it to stop matchmaking (cant stop it unless you go offline on steam) to fight bots anyway. they also just straight took away customizations from the first game feeling like they are trying to add them later as paid dlc sleezy.... speaking of sleezy devs have a habit of releasing the game and dropping it after release they did it with the first and quickly did it with this one they are no where to be seen dont expect balance patches or qol gameplay changes to advance the game further.+++split screen up to 4players (wouldnt be worth buying otherwise)+big robos+graphics+decent sized roster some missing from the first game though+- different from the first cant say is any worse or better---missing a lot of customization from the first game--no story mode (was in the first game)-forced online for single player league content with no way to silence annoying manager-lazy bare bones gameplay mechanics with little thought put into it especially for a "sequel"-want currency? prepare to grind forever although not much to buy with it anyway unless you like hats-still no playable monsters until season pass completes you will get 1-combos are too simplistic, lockon is atrocious and jump button is more like a very short hop-stages are extremely small compared to the first game-dash button doesnt cover much distance and no run button means people are glued to your faceboth the first and this game could have been amazing or great but both ended up being mediocre at best.dont buy it at all especially without dev support but if you must buy get it on a deep sale 75% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy Override 1, but wish the controls were a bit more fighting friendly? Want some midair combos? Want to play as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ULTRAMAN?This game has stepped up its...game...considerably. More mechs off the bat, a passable League play mode with progression and an an over-talkative cookie-cutter agent, great local multiplayer and plenty of other game modes to satisfy. The league can be played offline or on, a nice touch, and the graphics are above par for any indie fighting game out there.This is one to keep an eye on, to scratch that arena battle itch. It's definitely tighter, more fun overall than the first, and a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how people tested this game and didn't find the issues I have in the first 10 minutes of play time. There is no way to play online with friends outside of private matchs. Why would this ever be a thing in a game that allows you to do 2v2 in the "Leagues" Mode. This game is supposed to be a party brawler but you can't play with a party unless you're fighting your friends. You get nothing in-game for fighting in a private match. No currency, no progression, no satisfaction. As much as I like Override as a whole, I can not and will not recommend people buy it when there is no cross-play at launch when the player base is already small, no party system to 2v2 with friends, and no incentive to play private matches when you get nothing for it. Maybe Override 3 will finally make some good changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Vastly inferior to the previous game.There's no costumes, instead you get "armor" that costs an arm and a leg per piece. It's literally cheaper to buy an entire other mech instead of a full set of armor. Not that you want it anyway since none of it carries the personality or character that the costumes in the previous game had.Through the campaign you play through the different game modes which are...randomized. And no, you can't go through the menus to stick to the game mode you prefer. This is also an online-only game, meaning you can always come across someone who will completely wreck your day when you just wanna indulge in some power fantasy by spanking bots, like I usually do. I lost my voice screaming at the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.Oh yeah there's no charging attacks anymore, which I feel makes the gameplay overall less fun because it eventually boils down to mashing buttons. Especially with three or more players, which is already the majority of the gameplay modes.All the characters and pilots are gone too, instead your character is some nameless nobody who wants to be the best that no one ever was. Which is disappointing because that completely nullifies the best part of Override, the fact that each and every mech is full of such character and charm, you'd expect it to be full of loud stereotypes and stuff like that. But no, they're just rolled off an assembly line.♥♥♥♥ Override 2, I don't care if it has a cross-promotion with Ultraman. They should have just made Ultraman DLC for Override 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems really good, mechanics are expanded drastically from the main game (now having various aerial attacks etc)I feel the game might be a bit unbalanced for now, since lock on for projectiles seems to basically ignore jumping, making projectiles pretty hard to consistently dodge (especially day 1 when noone is super good at the game yet). This paired with the endlag on blocks seems to make zoners very strong. Right now I've been playing Atlas, who has some good movement tools but for bulkier characters this might prove even more of an issue.Only downside would be that I feel almost scammed by the lack of single-player content. The "leagues" aren't a "career mode" or "single-player mode". They're just online games though you can press Y to cancel them in order to fight a weak AI. I don't know if they have matchmaking based on player rank, but I hope not since you can way too easily raise this by just fighting AI and there doesn't seem to be a way to move downwards. Other than that there doesn't seem to be any sort of matchmaking.Overall a good fighter to play with friends across the world since this game has roll-back netcode, the 10% launch sale is a good time to get it since single-player is very shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game because I loved playing the first one with my friend a lot but they have changed the core gameplay to much to the point it just feels like a different game. I can see why people would like this game more over the first one with how quick the combat is now but it has gotten rid of some fun mechanics like charging up punches and kicks and being able to feint with them, the parry system, and flying. It feels like they are tying to go with a more brawler type fighting game and less of you feeling like a humongous city destroying mech fighting another humongous city destroying mech. I really liked what they had going in the first one I wish they kept on going with that formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh I'm disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: Lots of camera bugs to work out but that added to the retro feel however they do need to work on getting the camera figured out. The hit detection was also a bit off sometimes imo but those are my only real complaints. As a silly 4 player mindless beat up your friends game it does the trick I just wouldn't pay full price for it in it's current condition. I only played a little bit of the free weekend and even then the servers felt slow and I was unable to get a 4 player match up without CPU but I'll probably buy this game if they polish it a little. Even as a local coop or a remote play 4 player split game it would be fun if it worked just a little better but if you are used to fighting with the old Gamecube style camera angles you'll be fine here.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game, but it seems to be poorly optimized, at least on my end. The game is laggy even when running about 100FPS, and slows my PC down to a crawl. Either way, there is no cross-play and very little marketing was done, so the playerbase will likely not grow from its peak now. The combat feels good, but I hear there is a lack of easy ways to play with friends, which just makes the lack of cross-play hurt even more. I'm sure if the optimization/framerate issues are exclusive to me, but it may be wise to wait for a steeper sale if you're looking for netplay matches.EDIT - I fixed the performance issues by locking it to 60FPS, but the single player content is weak and the playerbase is already quite low. It seems like it's better to wait for a sale, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on release after enjoying the first one a fair amount. The developers made some questionable design decisions with Override 2, particularly with how you unlock currency for cosmetics and characters. The mechanical changes were fine and felt like a way of giving each character a more unique fighting style, but they seemed to have leaned into the concept of this game being more online-focused than its predecessor. However, just like the first one, Override 2 never found a dedicated player base. My friend group tried to revisit this game in 2024 through any of the online multiplayer, but found that we couldn't connect to the game's servers. It's unlikely that the developers will revisit this game, so I think it's safe to assume this game is completely dead with a significant portion of its content unavailable to new players.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much a single player experience, and this is not designed to be played as such. Unlike the first game where you are on a mission to defeat invading kaiju, you are "back" to the league fights that were mentioned in the first game. I personally enjoyed the first one because I didn't want a Robot Jox experience. I wanted a Kaiju fighter in the vein of the classic War of the Monsters (I had it on PS2). This game has a shallow fighting system that offers no strategy. You just start punching buttons and hope you land your hits. Kind of like Rock'm Sock'm Robots.I mentioned that this is not meant as a single player experience at the start. I said that because this was meant to be played against other players. However, because this game did not have an audience, it has no competition. There is not much of a story it would seem in the initial go except for "Hi, I am your agent. Let's go fight a bunch of people to be the champ". That is it.Honestly, I rather play the first one (which I have on Xbox) or the classic War of the Monsters over this. Of course, there is also Gigabash, and that one is a rip roaring good time.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is improved, and is slightly more intuitive than the first one. There's also a lot more characters, and there's less of the goofy mech designs. Unfortunately, that's about the only improvement. The overall experience is actually worse because there's less modes available. _childDocuments_.review: Fun, fast pacer arena brawler with a good roster of characters that are diverse enough in abilities to warrant being separate but still similar enough that you can pick up any of them with relative ease. Also the graphics are pretty solid too and there's a decent amount of modes to play. However its not perfect, not a lot of people on matchmaking, and CPUs in versus are really easy even on higher difficulty. I'd still recommend the game if you're looking for a unique arena fighter though, especially since progression in the league mode feels really satisfying. Might be better on console for easier local play though

_childDocuments_.review: It's well rounded and complex enough to not get boring right away. Plenty of variety in maps and mechs and has local multiplayer, which is few and far between these days. The things I would mark negative about this game are just design choices in certain settings, like how customization works, and not enough camera options.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good time. I played the first Override and had a blast. I haven't played Override 2 long, but I already love it. The game looks, sounds, and feels amazing to play. There's a variety of mechs and stages, the OST fits the setting and genre, and the controls and movements feel fluid and rewarding. After a long day I enjoy a good session of smashing buildings and beating on AI opponents. I don't typically enjoy playing fighting games against random human players, so having the options to play the Versus mode with/against friends/AIs or the League mode against AIs is great. My only gripe so far, and it's a minor one, is that I have to press F3 before every League match in order to play against AIs and not be matched against human players. I wish there was a setting or switch to enable/disable AI or human player matching while in League mode. Other than that personal preference, the game is solid fun. The "cos-mech-ics" for the mechs cover "cool" and "silly" options and are all able to be earned by playing the League mode. So far I haven't had any bugs, errors, frame drops, or other irregularities. In an era when many games are broken on launch it's refreshing to play a fun game that is built and polished well. I won't make any claims about netcode as I have yet to - and probably won't - use the matchmaking system.

name: Nexagon: Deathmatch
detailed_description: Fight battles in a televised tournament in a completely destructible environment where losing means death and winning means freedom. Recruit an unstoppable team of cracker-jack combatants with varying fighting skills and weapons and construct an impregnable fortress of defense, laden with deadly traps and devastating weaponry. Traverse an unforgiving arena collecting rewards and infiltrate the enemy’s stronghold with the intention of destroying it... Happening the years following the brutish skirmishes near the Orion Nebula, a strong feeling of general well being seemed to permeate even into the darkest corners of parliament, where a wild and daring decision concerning the treatment of prisoners was made; a chance for freedom that would supply the Galaxy with an extraordinary new form of entertainment ... THE PIT. Delivers the full package of character building, strategic resource management, and a never-before-seen depth of real-time tactics!! Story Since the late 25th century, Earth's population has skyrocketed, and the face of our blue planet has been transformed into a complex grid of concrete, polymers, and steel. Oxygen trickles into the atmosphere by virtue of precious biospheres that dot the skies in a suspended fragile mesh several miles above the surface. Humans toil and commute alongside the masses of alien races that have since inhabited Earth's centers. Together they have concocted the most voluble and copious of environments known to mankind since the Garden of Eden. At the turn of the fourth millennium, pessimistic speculation led philosophers to believe that Earth was bound for troubled times and that great suffering would engulf the helpless inhabitants. As usual, they were wrong. In fact, in the years following the brutish skirmishes near the Orion Nebula, a strong feeling of general well being seemed to permeate even into the darkest corners of parliament, where a wild and daring decision concerning the treatment of prisoners was made; a chance for freedom that would supply the Galaxy with an extraordinary new form of entertainment ... THE PIT. Features Nexagon is real-time 3D tactics with a refreshing twist on action/strategy gaming. Strike out into a completely destructible environment, where every structure, weapon, building or otherwise, can be entirely obliterated. Design and manage your own persistent, editable base of operations, build defensive structures, traps, weapons, and lavish gardens to please the crowd and protect your investment. Purchase units that gain experience and undergo physical changes over time, becoming more powerful from match to match. Battle your way through 3 separate divisions of enemy contenders, increasing your network value to one day compete in the ultimate fight for freedom … the Nexagon. Gain extra credit supporting your network sponsors through the use of billboards and control of advertising locations. Earn sufficient credit to buy some heavy hitters who will send smaller enemy units crashing into buildings or flying right out of The Pit entirely. Take control of stationary weapons and send mortar fire raining down upon your rivals.

name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch
detailed_description: Six years ago, the Machine Legion invaded and colonized the Torch City, which was originally inhabited by animals. Rayton, the former soldier in the resistance war, has been living in seclusion since then. After his friend is forcibly arrested, Rayton reclaims his mechanical fist and steps to his journey fighting back. And he never expects that he has been involved in a bigger scheme between the mafia, the rebellion, and the legion. Exploring the Metroidvania game world with a dozen of areas with distinguishing vision themes and level designs. Earning the rewards by conquering the challenges of combats, puzzles and platformers in countless chambers, tunnels and shortcuts. Interconnected and automatically loading game map makes the detailed Torch City more convincing and beautiful. Mastering the Fist, the Drill and the Whip, depending on the situation of the battlefield, switch your advantages between the long hits, the high damage and the wide range, taking every enemy standing in front of you down. Dozens of enemies wielding their unique weapons challenge you with exquisite cooperation tactics, and various bosses with totally different combat patterns provides you never repeated experience. The combining of the dieselpunk aesthetics and the oriental-style architecture constructs the core visual style of Torch City, exposing the world with the intense conflict between the furry animals and the mechanical army from their appearance to the nature. Powered by Unreal Engine 4 with physically based rendering and extremely detailed textures, presenting a gorgeous 3D visual performance and pushing the genre to a whole new level.

short_description: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is a Metroidvania action game featuring exploration, intense combat and challenging platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun, and very pretty looking Metroidvania. Definitely worth a playthrough if you like this genre. It took me about 37 hours to 100% it.Most of the game isn't terribly difficult, but a lot of environmental challenges are unforgiving. However, the master level martial arts challenge and final boss are extremely difficult and are, by far, the most challenging parts of the game - even on normal. The few critiques I have are:- You can't see what your moves are unless you're at a repair station.- Drinking carrot juice takes far too long and is extremely clunky, which is weird because the rocket item that uses the same mechanic is vastly more responsive.- There aren't enough fast travel location and there was no reason to have a subway system and a "teleporting" system, they should have stuck with just 1 of those, or given the subway more spots to travel to.- Putting the teleportation device to the main town inside Urso's attic(?) was an annoying choice. Especially when you couple that with the fact that once you leave Urso's attic to go to town you have to wait for the town door to open every single time you go to it from Urso's.- The combo system, while kinda fun and interesting, is sorta pointless since you can't use them on anything except low level normal enemies. More difficult enemies and bosses will just ignore your combos and special moves while hitting and interrupting you. Learning the master combo is completely pointless since you will never ever be able to use it outside of that challenge.- The Underwater portion needed more polish. The fact that you are forced to only use 1 fist type the entire time underwater seems like the mechanics weren't fully fleshed out. The underwater fighting isn't intuitive at all.- There are a lot of enemies that fight dirty or just take way too many hits to kill. The ninja frogs are a huge offender. They do look cool, but we never learn why there are a bunch of frog and wolf-like robots that are the enemies.- There are some mediocre treasure chests that take a ridiculously long time to get to. It feels like the secrets in this game could use a tune up. Sometimes you'll spend a ton of time navigating to a secret room only to find 20 coins in a chest.I would still recommend this to anyone who likes Metroidvanias because it is a good one, it just needs a little more polish.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on . I am about 2 hours in, and I am loving it.  OK, so I am 12 hours in and I did NOT expect like 30 to 40 % of this game to take place UNDERWATER...It is fun to use your drill to propel yourself around, but it gets old rather quickly, and there are plenty of underwater traversal and combat sequences, where your options are limited. I still have a very positive opinion of the game, but I think it could've cut down on this. I mean, it gives you so many great options for both combat and traversal, yet takes those options away for a large part of the game, which I think is frustrating. Other than that, the review stays as it was before.F.I.S.T. is a 2D Action Metroidvania, not unlike Guacamelee, with heavy emphasis on traversal and combat. The premise is very simple: you play as a bunny with a giant mechanical arm, and are trying to rescue your friend from an oppressive force.The arm is your main weapon and it allows you to perform all sorts of crazy wrestling moves. Combat is tight, responsive and the animations and audio-visual feedback are just insane. The second weapon I unlocked was a Drill, and that is even more over-the-top, as it allows you to perform tornadoes for huge AOE damage. There is also quite a nice amount of depth to be found, as you can switch freely between your weapons, to create stylish combos and toss enemies around, like in Devil May Cry (although the game does NOT have a style meter, that rewards you for switching up your tactics).Outside of that, the usual metroidvania stuff is there, exploration, opening up new areas, backtracking, finding secrets/upgrades etc, I am sure you know the drill. What I commend the game for, is that the upgrades that you unlock in order to open up previously inaccessible areas are actually woven into your general gameplay, rather than just being one-off keys. I found so many metroidvanias underwhelming, because you would unlock an ability/tool that can only be used to open a door, and that's it. But not in F.I.S.T., as here you will learn to do a Sucker Punch, that allows you to break-through doors, as well as send enemies flying. Some minor gripes include an over reliance on ranged enemies. Thankfully projectiles are generally slow, and you have enough movement tools to avoid damage, it's just a little repetitive to always have to prioritize the same enemies in every encounter. There was one boss which I also found to be a little frustrating, but I did manage to learn its patterns, and checkpoints tend to be generous enough (although I found no way to skip the intro cinematic to the boss, which became a little annoying on repeated attempts, even though it was less than 15 seconds long).Should I have a major shift in my opinion as I play through the game, I will be updating my review. But for now, this is a  for any action game fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed F.I.S.T. that much that I chose to 100% it.It's my favourite metroidvania that uses the combo-combat you find in fighting games.  Probably because I dislike those systems and F.I.S.T. allows you to get by without needing to really master much of it.  It's also arguably the nicest looking metroidvania to use a 'somewhat' realistic 2.5D artstyle (Grime and The Mobius Machine being some other examples).You end up with 3 different weapons that attack in UP/Down/Left/Right directions and have 3 buttons to attack (X, Y and B) that can be combined with different directions, though many attacks require you to train and unlock them.  You can pretty much get through most of the game spamming X and using the 'press and hold X' attack with your starting weapon, though you will fare better if you can throw in a bit more than that.F.I.S.T. is a high quality release that gets most of the basics of metroidvanias right while looking quite nice as well.  The map is for the most part what I want out of a metroidvania map.  Areas in different colours, anything I missed marked.  ..Except for the collectable Posters.  Fortunately the one I was missing I could look up online and locate it that way.  They are quite easy to walk past, plenty of other posters in the game are just background scenery which contributes to not always spotting them on your first pass.The fast travel points are a bit spaced out which I can imagine irritating some players, but I found it fine, but then I don't mind a bit of a hike.It rates as an A- for my personal enjoyment.  To get any higher than that it would've needed to:1.  Draw me into its world with great music like Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom or Astalon: Tears of the Earth.  The music in the game is perfectly fine, it's just less my style and kind of quiet in the background, perhaps I should've increased its volume.2.  Provide more non-linearity.  The game did have plenty of places to backtrack whenever I got a power, so I can't fault it too much, but I think everything had to occur in order (Of course, don't quote me future speedrunners!)and 3.  ..I suppose I never cared much about the bunny and his story.  It was perfectly serviceable as a plot and world, but it didn't capture my imagination all that much.Basically, F.I.S.T. does almost everything right for a metroidvania while at the same time just not appealing to some of my tastes to become an absolute favourite.===================== =====================  Aeterna Noctis |  Astalon: Tears of the Earth | Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom | Hollow Knight |   Blasphemous 2 | Cathedral |  Afterimage | The Last Faith |  Elderand | Ori and the Will of the Wisps | Doomblade^ |  Ender Lilies: Quietus of the Knights | Depths of Sanity | Environmental Station Alpha |  |  Blast Brigade | Haak | Biomorph | Turbo Kid |  Alwa’s Legacy | Steamworld Dig 2 | Islets | Blasphemous | After Death | Pronty^ | Mortal Manor* | Escape From Tethys | Outbuddies DX* | Monster Sanctuary | Elliot Quest | Rebel Transmute | Moonlight Pulse |  Haiku, the Robot | The Mobius Machine | Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown | Ultros |  Lone Fungus | Ghost Song | Death’s Gambit: Afterlife | Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night | Kunai | Kingdom Shell | Axiom Verge | Rabi-Ribi | TEVI | Treasure Adventure Game |  Flipwitch | Infernax | Plague of Yamorn* | Column on the Sea | Jrago* | MF-01 Aerostrike^ | Laika: Aged through Blood | Xanthiom Zero | Carrion^ | Chasm | Wuppo | The Mummy Demastered | Momodora 4 | Momodora 5 | Catmaze | Castle In The Clouds | Omega Strike | HunterX | HunterX: code name T | Aggelos | Midnight Castle Succubus | Sheepo |  Ato | EldritchVania | Cookie Cutter | Elephantasy | Rusted Moss^ | Grime | Moonscars | The Messenger | Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth | Iconoclasts | MindSeize | Ebenezer and the Invisible World | Luna’s Light* | Tales of Kenzera: Zau |  Castle In The Darkness | Alwa’s Awakening | Nitrojet* | RIN: The Last Child* | Pharaoh Rebirth | Yoku’s Island Express | Guacamelee! _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I personally wouldn't recommend this to someone who wants a fulfilling metroidvania experience.I understand where all the praise for this game is coming from. It is gorgeous, and it really nails the dieselpunk aesthetic. From a visual standpoint, an overall experience, this game is a 10/10.Unfortunately, once you start paying attention to the gameplay, it becomes clear that there's a disconnect.  This game has everything a metroidvania should have, on paper at least. It's got the distinct areas, the unique movement mechanics, the unlockable abilities, the boss fights, the traversal puzzle rooms, the secrets and backtracking, etc. However, in practice, these elements don't really mesh together well.For one example: You get three very unique weapons by the end of the game, but their full use is locked behind memorizing combos. Most combos aren't even useful in most encounters, so you end up with this unfulfilled potential of weapons that you use to do the same attacks over and over. Another example is the boss fights. You can tell that someone(s) put a lot of work into the boss animations and movesets. However, they must not have worked very closely with the people working on the main character's movement abilities. The first 3 attempts at most bosses have you end up getting stunlocked to death just because you didn't anticipate one of three different juggling attacks that the bosses trap you in. A final example is the map layout. There are a lot of unique areas, but in most cases, you're only going to go through each once. The story will throw you into an area, you'll go through it in a relatively linear fashion, beating enemies and solving puzzles as you go, and then you'll leave 90 minutes later with a new ability and a couple of collectibles. And that's the last you'll see of the area. Even though the map is all connected, the access points between areas are almost useless. If the story doesn't throw you into a new loading zone, then the transporters around the map become more convenient to get to. You have to be very motivated by 100%ing the game to get you to backtrack through old areas. These are specific examples, but I don't think they are solely responsible for what's lacking in this game. I really think it's just the case of a new studio putting out their first game, and trying to figure out how to make things work. They've definitely gotten their art department locked in, but their game design team honestly just needs some more experience. I think this would have been a more enjoyable experience if they had narrowed the scope a little bit. I would have loved this as a 6-8 hour game. Once I got 10 hours in it started to drag.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to think that Chinese game studios only made gatcha games and rip-offs of better games made in other countries. Then I played FIST. What else can I say? It's a masterpiece among modern Metroidvanias, easily up there with the likes of Bloodstained, Guacamelee and Axiom Verge. The map is sprawling without being confusing, the combat system is in-depth while being easy to pick up, and the story is a compelling tale of corruption, betrayal and heroism in a dieselpunk world inspired by early 20th-century China. _childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say that this isn't a bad game by any means. I think this game has a good foundation. But there are multiple problems with the game that lead me to say that I would want them to do something a bit better than this. Firstly, the story. It's rushed, all over the place, and lacking the character development to make you actually feel something about them. One minute, Rayton is being praised for his heroics, and the next, he's being bashed for being stoic and dense. Lady Q and Urso do not have enough time to be fleshed out as individual characters to have a meaningful impact on the story. The same with Cicero. This guy is seen, what, 4 times in the actual story!? 5 maybe? And out of all the characters, I probably was the most interested in his backstory, which we got basically NONE of. Without spoiling anything, I just feel like he was one of the most underdeveloped characters I've seen in a while. And honestly, the same could be said for the main character, Rayton. Like, he's a "rabbit hero," while having no flashbacks to his heroics. We're just told he's one, and given one scene that's supposed to prove it. We don't see enough interactions of him that aren't business. He's just bland. Boring. The ending is rushed and empty.In terms of gameplay, there are pros and cons. The combo system is actually pretty good, especially with the weapon-switching from Fist to Drill to Whip. The ground and aerial potential of combos is impressive. The problem? There are a lot of bosses in this game that either armor through your hits, or are unable to be launched into the air, making these "master combos" largely useless. The final boss is about 3x harder with the Fist and the Drill, mostly because of the parry that takes off 3 health bars from you, plus the fact that you can be parried MID-COMBO. The Whip makes the final boss a joke. Insane damage, hardly any combos. Fights where you can launch bosses and do combos are actually entertaining, but without that? Fights are just stale. Use the best weapon and do the same optimal combo that can't really be punished because of the whip's range. The Drill honestly becomes largely useless after the Whip is obtained.Collectibles are fine. No issues there. I did a Normal playthrough, but didn't 100% the game (only managed to 98% it), but did like the Plant Seeds, Posters and Data Disks. Platforming was also for the most part, pretty good, though there were times that were scuffed in the hovering sections. Not going to mention PC specific issues because by their own admission, they are still attempting to optimize it.All in all, I think this is an ok game with a subpar story and decent gameplay. Personally, though, I wouldn't recommend it. I just feel like after beating the game, I'm left unsatisfied. Hell, the ending is just like dumping a bucket of water on an already dying flame. It was a complete letdown. But hey, just my opinion here. Platforming: 8.5/10Story: 4/10Combat Gameplay: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Metroidvania 2D platformer with a steampunk theme. Plus there are fuzzy wittle animals! I loved those games so I'm counting that as a plus. - You can move faster by dashing and it doesn't drain energyCons-Attacks are slow and easily interrupted by an enemy hit... if you don't upgrade/are slow to upgrade combos the fights will become very repetitive-Areas within maps look very similar making it easy to get lost or become reliant on your map tool for orientation- Much of the first part of the game requires travel by foot between maps, which can become tedious and "transports" aren't an option until you exit the 3rd map- I don't notice the music and in a Steampunk themed game, I think I shouldI definitely enjoy this game. Is it worth the money? I'm leaning towards yes, but the jury is still out. But it's available to demo so you can see for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I currently wouldn't recommend FIST, I think that will change if the developers can patch out a lot of the bugs and glitches.Several crashes, graphical glitches, entire areas turning into slideshows for 30 seconds at a time (settings didn't matter), and a really poorly thought out control system mar what is otherwise a pretty good time for the most part.The "training" section is a great advert for how poor the controls are when set against what they were attempting to achieve.  If you can't complete the "training" (for combos you literally will not ever, ever use no less), you cannot complete the game 100% as one of the missing shards is tied to completing the "training" challenges.  With a parry system so horrendously implemented as to be completely useless (you need to face toward an attacker, then push toward them at the right time on an analogue stick), you are going to get hit an awful lot in combat, and often stun locked.  It goes down with a special dash later, but it is still nowhere near fit for purpose especially when it really seems to be a core part of the combat.  There's no block either, with you having to attempt to parry attacks from both melee and from ranged attackers while you go.So I'm currently writing the review with the 2nd final boss fight still to do, and the "Master" level of the training challenges.  I don't think I'll be bothering with them to be honest, with the main reason being the convoluted control system.There is a really good fun time in here, it just needs some polish.
