_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a great game, but I'm hesitant to call it a good Metroidvania.Each area the game takes you through is fairly linear, and you'll only revisit them if you want to get collectibles or data disks (used to unlock some moves).  Otherwise you never need to return.  There's a few areas midway through the game you can 100% complete on your first pass.I find the combat system enjoyable, but I question some design decisions.  It's a gambit every time you go into to attack, because you don't know if you'll interrupt your opponents move or not.  Many attacks from enemies will just super armor their way through and hit you anyway.You start with a dash, but not really a dodge.  You can't dash through enemies until you get a VERY late game upgrade, which personally made combat flow much better not being body blocked by enemies.  You aren't given a block / parry ability until about halfway through either.  I've played games with a similar parry mechanic, so it wasn't too out of left field for me to figure out, but it does NOT like analog sticks.  I had to swap my movement to the D-Pad on my Logitech F310.  From there parrying was actually pretty easy.  But just like with enemies super armoring through attacks, sometimes parrying will stun the enemy completely, and other times it will just negate damage.  Early on you also get a charge up punch which is shown that it can be used as a counter move against a bosses rocket punch, but it's never utilized again after that.Storyline wise it's better than most Metroidvanias.  My only complaint is that if you press the confirm button too soon in a conversation where action is happening, then you'll go from talking to punching without seeing what triggered it in between.Eventually you get a hang of the combat and find what combos work well for you and steamroll most enemies.  Some of the bosses can be challenging, but not anything too rough.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Important:I played the game on SteamDeck. I had to reduce nearly all settings to "low". This way the combos were not lagging etc. but maybe this was also the cause for some strange effects.COMBATThe combat is pretty nice. It starts easy with same easy enemies and will get harder later in game. Also "old" locations will be upgraded with heavier units. The only thing I didn't like about the game were the enemies who can shoot. I am not sure if it was only coincidence, but it somehow always felt like the enemy is exactly knowing where you will land with your character and shoots at exactly this position.In some cases this is really painfull since you cannot even move. I had situations where I was hit by multiple enemies in different combos in a row and believe it or not: I could not even stand up and was killed. These moments made me nearly smash my controller.BOSSESThe bosses are a huge pain. If you get angry really fast due failures ... then avoid this game. Some of the bosses are such a pain, you will curse the developers and all gods you know. But in the end ... the solution is to memorize their patterns (for this you need many tries) and learn to dodge or counterattack. But using the SteamDeck it was sometimes only luck if the controls did what you told to do.And you also need to learn the combos. If you use them correctly, you sometimes can instant kill a boss. _childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical when I first heard of this game, but being such a fan of the metroidvania genre I had to try it out. What got my attention from the get go is the art direction. This game looks fantastic! All of the modern graphical bells and whistles, packed into a side-scrolling platformer featuring anthropomorphic animals — what's not to love? The world looks and feels lived-in; a fictional China if the population were a bunch of furry animals, and with a surprisingly high level detail of from neon signage to in-game decals, it's the small things that deliver the love and dedication the developers had for this game. Not to mention how many different biomes it has (it has several), the world will keep you going back to reference the map more times than expected. The cast of character's designs are spot-on and memorable, voice acting and animation is well executed. Even the NPCs were given enough attention that they feel like they're part of a cast rather than just random placeholders in the map. F.I.S.T's gameplay however is its strongest suit. The action lends itself well to a controller and has enough weight that you feel Rayton's punches land. There's a certain satisfaction that you get if you manage to run a difficult combo and execute perfectly. I'm a sucker for that, that's for sure. There are a few instances when the moves didn't register as I wanted, but not too often that it broke the experience for me. The difficulty in the AI is good: not super punishing, but not push-over easy, and the variety of different enemies kept me wanting in anticipation for the next one. The tedium of grabbing all the collectibles was made lighter by the many varied enemy instances that it didn't come off as boring or taxing. But if its gameplay is the high point, the main story falls short and is something i'd consider pretty generic; typical hero narrative, with a supporting cast that don't really do much. As memorable as Ursus the bear is or Chuan the red panda, I wish they had more involvement in the narrative as I would have loved to see them in more scenes. That said, I wish they worked Lady Q's character more into the game. Despite that, I still felt the story to be compelling enough for a 20-hour playthrough. Lastly, the sound design in this game was amazing. The SFX they used for the attacks, enemy soundbites, ambient sfx of traffic and chatter were all top notch. The music perfectly complimented the action, and it almost took a life of its own with all the orchestration and jazz licks that you are able to sample as you play through the game. I thought that the voice acting (except for Rayton's stoic performance) was pretty good, and the cutscenes — particularly the fight choreography — are gorgeously made. Overall, I think this game is one of the better metroidvanias I've played in recent years. I'd for sure be on the look out for future DLCs or sequels, as I'm sure this wouldn't be the last to come out of the studio. A definite must-try for casual gamers, and a sure-buy for fans of the genre. An easy 8.5 out 10 carrots.

_childDocuments_.review: The China Hero Project is an interesting initiative, a few years ago Sony’s Playstation division decided to sponsor and help new promises from the chinese indie scene and quite a lot of projects appeared from that new initiative, the most recognizable were “Lost Soul Aside”, “ANNO: Mutationem” and “F.I.S.T. Forged in Shadow Torch” which is the one that I will be reviewing. I must confess at first I didn’t give it any attention, yeah, it looked very promising but it wasn’t in my radar, that was until game released and I started reading about it and damn, everything looked really good, so, after completing it at 95% (save, no achievements) and 18.5 hours of gameplay I think I can safely say that this is the surprise of the year for me.Is this game worth your time and money? Let’s find out.We play as Rayton who lives in Torch city, a place under the Iron Legion’s domain, an authoritarian regime. Rayton refuses to be part of the resistance as he lost a lot in the big war that took place prior to the regime but that changes when the Legion takes his friends as prisoners and he must rescue them. In the process they will meet Q, a mysterious feline warrior that tries to protect something that the Legion wants at all cost, the Spark, something ancient. The more we get involved in this, the more we will discover about the spark and the true intentions of those mechanical enemies.I’m going to be completely honest here, the story is flat, it’s a mere instrument to keep you busy going from one place to the other as most metroidvanias do, it is not a bad story at all, however, I don’t think it’s deep or interesting enough to highlight it because this game truly shines thanks to two main factors, level design and gameplay loop. Characters aren’t bad but once again, they are flat entities that at the end of the day won’t matter that much as everything is very straight forward, this doesn’t mean this is a bad thing, not at all, it works perfectly for what the game wants to accomplish and in this case the story is what it should be, the main line to follow from beginning to end.In the same way characters seemed to be built specifically for gameplay purposes. The cartographer, the seed boy, the vendors, Urso for paint upgrades, etc… At the end of the day all elements are part of a mechanical system that works perfectly to make this a very fun and engaging experience.While I said that story is not that interesting, I must say that visuals are over the top for a game like this. Is this level of detail necessary for the experience? Hell no but holy smokes, this game is truly beautiful.Torch city and nearby areas have a very distinctive visual style, it kind of reminds me of a mix between Hong-Kong streets in the 80’s combined with a dieselpunk style, a mix between classic real world style with a mechanic heart on it. The streets are fully detailed with 3D elements in the background to give you the sense of depth even though it plays like a 2D game, the main hub of operations, which is also a street but with interiors fully modeled, is STUNNING too as it’s the most visual intensive area, those background streets look phenomenal. In general I would say they nailed every inch of the map to create a cohesive and interesting world.Animations are something that sometimes are a bit weird, specially when characters are talking and in-game cinematics are running, but in general in-game animations are responsive and really well done. Visual effects like particles and dashes are also really well done, in general I would say this game has a really good visual level, way more impactful than it needs for the kind of game it is, however, this really helps us to get immersed into this world and this journey.I won’t comment on level design just yet as I think it makes more sense to talk about once we talk about the gameplay loop as it’s a very important element.What about sound? Well, music in general is really great, in fact once you explore each area at 100%, the cartographer will reward you with a music disc to listen to those tracks, each area has a different music track and I must say that they are really great. When it comes to voice acting, I played this game with english dub and the cast did a really good job, although there were a few lines in which I think two different members dubbed the same character for different lines? The one that I noticed the most was the cartographer when rewarding you, I don’t know why the line in which he shows his appreciation sounds like a different person, nothing bad just weird hehe.Anyway, let’s jump directly into the juicy stuff, gameplay loop and level design.Torch city is an interconnected labyrinth full of tunnels, hidden spots and alternative routes that you will be unlocking the more abilities you unlock. There’s a room there you can’t reach? Keep going and once you get a new ability try reaching it again, this is how it works with metroidvania games, backtracking is required in order to unlock all content and trust me, there’s a lot to unlock; Seeds, Data disks, posters that will unlock paint jobs, locked boxes that require special keys and mysterious shards that you will need to find. All those elements will be hidden but they will come in handy for upgrades and to unlock even more content. Don’t forget about HP, SP and side effect bar upgrades, they look like capsules and you will need 3 in order to get an upgrade, most are scattered around the map while others require special things (like buying them or getting them via activity completion) this will come in handy, trust me.Once you unlock all three tools from your mechanical fist, you will get access to a ton of movements which once unlocked will make the combat experience and the traversal something really great. Let’s start with traversal, once you unlock the three main movements that are needed to completely reach all places of the map things will get fun, why? Because movement becomes something dynamic and not only that, exploring the map is in general fun as it will make you move constantly, it’s not about straight lines but jumps, coordination and in general a fun route.When it comes to combat, things can get ugly for our enemies, at first our movement set is quite limited but it won’t take long until we start having upgrades that will make each combat something spectacular, a combination of movements and an upgraded SP/HP bars is something that by the end of the game you will truly appreciate as things will become dynamic and fun, you can also switch your weapon in the middle of a combat, however I don’t think I would recommend doing that, try to learn each tool by their own and master them. My favorite without any doubt is the drill, that tool is brutal as heck, and executions with it are amazing.As for the PC performance, I didn’t have any problem although I think it might be a bit demanding but can’t say I had a bad experience as my performance was perfect all time, no drops, no stuttering, in general a very smooth experience with everything at max.In conclusion, F.I.S.T. is a very solid and stunning metroidvania that might not be in your radar, but trust me, it is very worth your time even if you don’t want to complete it at 100% although I would say it won’t be a hard thing to do if you enjoy movement and traversal, in general I would say that, while it doesn’t really create anything new, it refines the metroidvania formula and does a very great job.I seriously hope you have an amazing experience with this game as I did, Rayton and Torch City need you.

_childDocuments_.review: To the people complaining there is no exit button; its in the game settings menu like so, so many other Chinese/Japanese games. Yeah I know its not how we do it in western games but its predictable.I have a short amount of playtime as of this first posting, but the TL:DR is, this is a combo-based fighter game in a metroidvania world wrapped in a anime-style story. Gameplay holds up and is challenging, if you expect to dead-cells your way through this, think again. Enemies will stop you in your tracks, you can't roll or dash through them (at least not yet, at my stage of the game) and so you *have* to learn which attacks clear which mobs best. And when you nail it, its awesome. When you don't, you will get clobbered.My only real gripes are, not being able to turn off motion blur completely, DLSS settings being vague, and.. the music is pretty good (especially the level-up skills menu lol) but.. the tracks are *so* short. They loop after a very, very short time and with an obvious fade-in. Given how long you might be in an area, or paused, I think the soundtrack should have room to breathe and set the tone but *the tracks are so damn short*. Why? Is it stock licensed music or did they just tell the composer to only write like 1-2 minute long loops (that don't even seamlessly loop, but probably could if they didn't have the fade-in every time). Just, an odd choice for a metroidvania which usually have elaborate area soundtracks.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game really blew me away... i'm generally not that into steampunk and certainly not into antropomorphic animal characters but this game is just too good to miss out on! It exudes charm and attention to detail in every single area... Environments and characters feel lively and the backgrounds burst with personality thanks to everything that's going on such as people getting extorted by crime gangs, cars driving by, machinery buzzing and pipes leaking. The whole city feels alive and the whole experience is incredibly immersive because of it. I got sucked into this game for 3 days straight, doing pretty much everything the game had to offer bar a few things. I'd gladly count it among my favorite metroidvania's of all time along the likes or Ori, blasphemous and haiku the robot. It really is because of games such as these that MV's are my favorite genre, and i can't wait to revisit this one later down the line. If i haven't convinced you yet to pick it up i'll go ahead and discus each aspect in more detail but suffice to say that i really think this game is worth your time and money, even at full price! Now to get into the details;I say this for every metroidvania but level design is the most important aspect for a MV to get right. I'm glad to say that FIST is pretty much a ten out of ten in this department. Not only is the map absolutely ENORMOUS, it's also filled with secrets, collectables, side routes, shortcuts and all the other metroidvania goodness. I'm not gonna say i rushed this game but i went through it at a steady pace and it still took me 15 hours to fully explore all the areas. The mapping screen is super usefull and clear to help with backtracking, so navigating and 100%ing the map was an absolute joy as well as being worthwhile with usefull upgrades. The movement in this game (which is imo the second most important aspect for a MV) is also super fluid, so all the wall climbing, grappling and platforming around the map was super fun, even in combat.Combat itself is also masterfully done with a robust and indepth combo system that allows you to chain lock enemies once you've mastered it. I never played street fighter or smash games but this is how i imagine they feel like. The combo's are diverse with satisfying animations, particle and sound effects. Each one is also usefull so you're not just sticking with one but instead are actively encouraged to keep mixing it up. Enemy variety isn't that high but each one is a joy to fight, there's some especially nasty ones that can quickly take you out if you're not carefull. Enemies are also mixed and matched often to create a large variety of encounters, despite the small assortment. There's also a dozen or so bosses to really test your skill, most are doable but some took several tries without every feeling unfair. The final 3 bosses especially were super well crafted, and without giving away anything there's even an ori style escape to test your quick thinking and reflexes!If level design, movement and combat in a game are this good it's already a great experience so visuals are sort of like the cherry on top. Once again the game knocks it out of the park here with high quality models, textures and lighting in every nook and cranny. I'm normally not that big on 2.5D but this game looks absolutely gorgeous. Like i mentioned at the start it's also chockfull of little details that make the city feel alive and breathing. There's also a very large variety of environments, from flooded caverns, to power plants, abandoned miners, ancient temples and bustling streets. This game has it all. The music isn't that memorable but it felt like it fit with the whole tone and mood of the world very well. Sound effects are great, they really add punch to your attacks and the voice acting is superb. Sadly the english VA is missing for side dialogues but for all the main story related stuff it's there and it's very well done. Especially the main character rayton, who has this satisfying gravely voice.Speaking of Story this is one of the areas where the game doesn't stand out as much, it's decent and doesn't detract from the otherwise great game but it is relatively predicatable and not as interesting as it could've been. The writing is mostly pretty good, apart from one sorta cringey side character, but most of it is borderline cliche. Still this doesn't matter to me because the world itself does half the storytelling, and it does that extremely well. Lastly there's bugs and performance and while the game does have a little bug here and there, the quality and polish of it all is too high for those few bugs to hamper the experience. Performance is smooth once it gets going, but loading in a new area can cause a big framedrop (down to the 20's) for several seconds. However once that's loaded in the game stabilizes and the lag is gone, even when returning to areas once they've loaded in during your play session.i can hardly say anything negative about the game and the things i can say are understandable little flaws or nitpicks. I know this review is full of superlativs but that is for good reason. The game is all around extremely well made, and an easy recommendation to any fan of sidescroller, metroidvania's or steampunk. It's one of the best games i've played this year and has earned it's place among the favorite games in my library. I think scoring a game is a flawed concept but if i had to this would probably be somewhere between a 9-9,5/10. An easy recommendation even at full price, and a steal at a sale, don't miss out on this one folks!

_childDocuments_.review: The new metroidvania about a rabbit with a huge mechanical fist that puffs out robotic invaders literally embodies the "hurricane gameplay" thesis, reducing the parry value to about zero. This is one of the few drawbacks of the game, but parrying here is the thing that you really do not want to use, moreover, this ability appears quite late and you no longer want to retrain. The game very skillfully forces you to be fast, mobile, constantly strike, get away from attacks with the help of dash, predict the moment of the attack, use special attacks in time, disrupting possible damage from the enemy, make long and most deadly combos. Parrying does not fit here at all, especially when it is performed in such a very peculiar way. Fighting enemies here is incredibly fun, you arrange crazy brawls on the screen, throwing enemies with your fist, pulling and pushing them with your drill, predatory whipping them with a whip, or even combining all three available styles. It's a real adrenaline rush, it's a decent challenge to player skill, it's fun.But no matter how fun it was to fight with ordinary enemies, the main thing in such games is the bosses. And they decently hit you in the back of the head. Almost each of them makes you experience a gamut of emotions from "It is impossible to kill him, I want to remove Steam" to "I figured out your secret, scoundrel, well, now you will get it in full, my fist rules here." Bosses are varied, fights with them are very entertaining, there are also hidden bosses that you may not even meet in the main plot. The main opponents here really feel like the main ones, the completion of some important segment of the path, and not just rotten blockheads to fill the time. The design of the levels is competent, I just did not like the levels with swimming at all, and the pace of movement is too slow in them. Yes, you will have to do some serious backtracking to find all the collectibles and improvements, but this is not particularly forced. The game is insanely pleasing with its visual picture, so juicy that you want to drink it like juice. The plot is sometimes too dramatic, but keeps itself within the framework of a completely competent story, in which everything must end well, which is a pleasure.The game has a lot to offer both the hardcore player and the amateur unfamiliar with the genre. She is fast, angry and cheerful, abundantly wetting the rusted gears of spinal reflexes with adrenaline. Unambiguous positive recommendation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty ok! Has moments of genuine coolness mixed in with bits and bobs that could do with an improvement, and a couple small things that are very frustrating to boot.The story itself is ok. It's not going to win an award by any means but it'll take you on a simple enough journey.--Pros.The setting is truly wonderful. The 3D backdrops for this 2D side scroller are gorgeous to look at at times - and the way the lighting is utilised just makes for such immersive scenery. I hit a hanging light by accident and the thing threw itself around - lighting the character and the environment dynamically as it moved. There are enemies that use the 3D space nicely as well, so it's really cool.The character models and designs are memorable, unique and the main char Rayton is so damn fluffy.The premise and utility of the fist strapped to your back is really interesting and unique.The soundtrack by Caisheng Bo does the job well, with a couple of the songs truly slapping. (you'll know the ones)Once you unlock yourself a couple of abilities, navigating the world starts to genuinely become a fun experience.--Cons.Parrying never really felt reliable. Using the joystick you have to tap in the direction of the projectile or attack to parry, rather than just having a dedicated parry button a-la Sekiro. Hold that direction button for too long and you're no longer parrying. Just felt a bit clunky.There's very little diversity in foes. Expect 5 or 6 robotic mob types, and bosses who are regular enemies with a couple extra moves and a health bar. You'll fight the same baby blue bomb throwing tank at least 4 times in the story, and then you can expect most bosses to have a double boss or a mob rush encounter later into the game.Localisation. Expect a few incorrect words here and there. Some of the speech is hokey as hell, and when it's not stiff it's very basic. There's a lot of "saying the same thing but from multiple characters" repetition. Also some pretty strange turns of phrase. There's a bunny collecting seeds who will ask you "Did you find it? The seed in the glass?" Referring to "it" like it's a singular seed, when no, there are loads of them to find in the map.A few instances of odd 3rd person declarations, particularly from Urso. Sometimes they'll use other character's names as if they aren't in the room - despite talking to said character directly. A paraphrased example: "I should really take Rayton out some day" - Urso, talking directly to Rayton. Just weird and a bit unfortunate, but hey, it's fine. It took me out of taking the characters seriously a little bit, but it's not a deal breaker.Traversal. There aren't very many fast travel points. Expect a lot of map checking and back tracking.Plot Twists. They were not handled well. Saturday morning cartoon level "mwahaha"ing threw me thoroughly out of the experience.A major personal gripe that did bring nothing but annoyance was a dummy training set of challenges. Screw wasting time on that. I have better things to do than grapple with inconsistent controls and unforgiving time windows.All in all this is a game i want to like, and in some ways do. But not without a robotic fist sized dollop of "could be better." Still, for the first outing, this is a fine experience if you like metroidvanias, moreso you're furry trash like me. :3

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania that goes heavy on the visuals. Some areas provide more of a challenge but its certainly not the focus of the game. Had a fun time exploring and finding secrets/collectibles but it became a chore later in the game. Even with fast travel points, backtracking was a pain. Otherwise, this is a fun addition to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks fantastic - especially the animal people, I'll give it that. But during my two hours I found the world uninteresting, and the combat was so awkward it drained all my will to continue.It feels like the enemy designer and the combo designer never talked to each other. Enemies are fast, have quick attacks, their projectiles are slow; it feels like combat perfectly suited for parry/dodge-heavy gameplay. But you can't really "dodge" (you can dash, but it's just a large, not very fast move), and parry - once you find it - costs points which also are used by the healing potion. On top of that, your movements are slow semi-combos that feel hard to execute. So you'd think you're a juggernaut, one/two-shotting bad guys, yeah? No - they all take far too many hits; you almost don't want to engage them.Then there's the issue of enemy variety. All enemies are robot troops, except there are also those annoying robo-frogs. Those are a total pain to fight due to, again, them being quick and agile while you're slow. They come in big and small varieties, but are essentially the same. The robot troops I saw three types of: sword, gun, and heavy axe. Sword and gun feel almost exactly the same, heavy axe are a little tougher and resistant to pushback, but otherwise also the same. I feel like a good metroidvania should have decent enemy variety, and perhaps there are more enemies later on, but I'll never know.Another thing that defines a metroidvania is "ability locked doors". The fun comes from figuring out which tool do you need to open this passage. Here, it's not only marked on the map, but also a popup shows up telling you exactly which ability you need to use to open this door, no matter if you have it or not. There's no way of turning those popups off. Taking away all my fun from experimentation is what it does. They appear more than once, even after you've learned that those doors can be opened with this ability, insulting your memory.The music in the first area is so repetitive, it almost drove me crazy. The (English) voice acting is alright. What's great is the clear attention to detail when it comes to backgrounds; a lot of work must've gone into that. The characters also look stellar in all their furry glory, retaining their animal characteristics while displaying human-like expressions. Excellent work. That said, the first thing you see in the game is a cutscene where a shapely catgirl runs away from some drones, while breasting boobily doing parkour. Lots of effort on display. Too much, perhaps; I'd rather have the game played well - I know of other places where I can look at catgirls breasting boobily.Don't get me wrong; there are far worse games out there. If you don't care about the metroidvania aspect and don't mind clunky combat, the worldbuilding seems somewhat interesting - during cutscenes at least. However, there are also far, far better experiences if you look for them. Hope that helped.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely my GOTY 2021. An excellently executed metroidvania beat em up with well designed areas, great feeling movement, super fun (and challenging) boss fights with gorgeous graphics to boot. The soundtrack is also quite nice, and I found it extremely fulfilling of my need for a fun fast paced metroidvania.The story is pretty simple, about a rabbit named Rayton who, when his big bear friend gets thrown in jail, decides it's time to fully un-regime his city from a bunch of robo-soldiers oppressing it and break his friend out of jail with a big mechanical fist that he wears like a backbling. You get some other weapons further into the game, each with their own movement ability that makes the platforming more interesting, with an excellent interlacing of both combat tools and movement tools at the same time. The depth of the combat in this game is quite high, with optional combo challenges that are even quite useful in learning creative ways to juggle between multiple weapons simultaneously, and with a boss rush unlockable post game and a massive myriad of collectables that are cleverly hidden throughout the map, 100%ing this game was a blast. For some reason i've read people thought there weren't reasons to revisit previous areas, but there are plenty of secrets and items that you can only get with later power ups, so I don't know what they were on about.My one criticism of this game personally is only a warning that the combat may be a tad difficult late game for people who aren't that good at beatem ups or combos (or parrying, woof some of those later bosses). If you worry about "getting juggled and having to use the same moves over and over (because you don't want to learn the combo system)", this game may be a tad tough for you. If you enjoy fighting games though, it might be more up your alley. Overall, this game is a 10/10 for me, a shocking sleeper hit that doesn't get talked about enoughI also found it quite funny that they introduce the cat woman like she's going to be some kind of relevant love interest but rayton visibly doesn't care because he'd rather fight an entire army for one of his male friends, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrying a giant fist on your back as you go about slapping mechanical constructs sure sounds like a fun premise. So let's see if this little rabbit is hiding a butterfly underneath his paws, or is it perhaps something more fetid.Perhaps my IQ isn't high enough to fully comprehend the complexity of this cheesy and predictable story set in a dieselpunk furryverse, but I do know that the glowing thing everyone wants is orange. And what is orange? That's right - an orange...also carrots. Hence the hero bunny, Rayton, wants to find it, so the villain bunny, Cicero, doesn't. Conflict ensues, friend becomes foe, and only one will have the orange thingy.Orange aside, the furries are bland and forgettable. None has any depth to their motivations which ultimately makes them flat. Heck, the main baddie is on screen for 10 minutes and is severely underused, as is his connection to Rayton. It should have received more attention than a  Also, Rayton is a pretty forgettable protagonist. Ma man goes from "" to "" in two seconds. All it took was his friend getting thrown in prison. Cool. But what about all the people who lost their lives before that? Guess that just wasn't good enough of a motivation for our great hero.And even if the game is fully voiced and ripe with cutscenes, the writing made sure all of it went to waste. There was some cheesy dialogue, so that's nice. But I did love the performance of the English voice actor for Rayton. My man channelled his inner Christopher Daniel Barnes during impactful moments.Ah, childhood memories.As a Metroidvania, you know what to expect; Lots of backtracking, barred off areas inaccessible just yet and plenty of unique abilities and weapons for you to find and try out. But, a couple of crucial missteps drag the whole experience down.Since exploration is a crucial part of the experience, it had to be good.  It was fun to hop around Torch City thanks to the game's fluid animations and amazingly responsive controls. But, the world is utterly lifeless. I like the dieselpunk aesthetic, yet so much of the map is just useless empty space. I couldn't even be bothered to hunt for the many secrets, finishing at a measly 76% completion. They succeeded in conveying a sense of scale with the map design, but so much of it is empty that made exploring tedious. It's simply too big . And the area design didn't help either. While there are some standout areas, like the streets of Torch City under the jurisdiction of the Rat Gang, most of my time was spent traversing bland, ugly and empty pipes and caves with zero personality.Nevertheless, everybody is aware that exploration is not a core part of a Metroidvania and thus shouldn't be fun. If the combat is good, then there is still hope. And it is good. Indeed it is. I love the combo approach and had fun mixing weapons mid-combat to continue my slapping of the enemies iron cheeks. To help you do that, you have the  and . Each weapon does have its own unique set of moves and advantages over the others. The fun comes from switching them on the fly during combat, chaining together devastating combos. But, the  are not that useful for bosses or mini-bosses. So I stuck to ? And these special moves deal tremendous amounts of damage but need one bar of  to use. However, you needn't worry about not having enough of it; Besides some enemy drops that restore it, slapping enemies around with your light or heavy attacks recharges it. So get to slapping! And these special moves are obtained from the games pretty extensive skill tree. You'll need  alongside the game's currency to unlock skills. Sadly, there are no new moves in tier 3, as those picks just add more damage to these moves. But let's talk about my main issue with the combat - , you must first  to reach you, and just as it's about to boop that little bunny noes of yours, then you . This single design choice made me loathe combat with more than one single enemy. It just doesn't work when you are getting ganked. Also, the parry window is small, and there is no specific animation to let me know if I even attempted the parry. It'll either work or not. And that's how I'll know. Wonderful.And now we move to - . There are four unique pieces of equipment you'll utilize to rid Torch City of the Machine Legion - a  (yes, there is a second parry option for whatever reason) and . Now, these items should complement the combat. But not here. No. Instead, let's limit the player by having all of the equipment use the same . Why use the rocket shotgun or the exploding puppets and risk running out of health potions during a boss fight? This problem isn't as terrible during your clashes with the mobs because of a specific skill that regenerates one EP bar per execution. But yeah, during boss battles, using anything other than a health potion is not a sound financial investment.Yet, a few rays of sunshine still managed to slip through these cumulonimbus clouds.Platforming and puzzle-solving were quite enjoyable, even if they lacked variety or challenge. It was more like a fun distraction as I made my way towards another group of mobs in need of some good ol' fisting. Speaking of mobs, their variety, visually and gameplay-wise, is excellent. At first, it might seem like you'll fight the same two enemies, but as the story picks up pace, new enemies start showing up, all with unique movesets and skills. , making some sections quite challenging. The samurai gave me more trouble than I'd like to admit, mainly because of the god awful parry implementation I ranted about earlier. Besides smashing mobs with my giant fist, . They have a great variety of moves, and as the fight progresses, they become stronger and adopt new attacks, ramping up the challenge. But, I do have an issue -. Some show their point of impact and range, but some don't, leaving you to take it like a man first and ask questions later. And since the parry system is awful, I had to die just to see the full scope of the bosses arsenal. But, I still did enjoy fighting the bosses once I knew the whats and hows of their moves. And lastly, the game's soundtrack was surprisingly good, with certain boss tracks getting the juices flowing. I also loved the jazzy background tune as you stroll through the Rat Gang controlled streets of Torch City. I just have a soft spot for some good ol' jazz.So while my 15h adventure in Torch City wasn't a steaming pile of rabbit droppings, it also wasn't entirely enjoyable either. Too many poor design choices hold back what could have been a standout title of 2021 and a damn good Metroidvania as well.

_childDocuments_.review: F.I.S.T is an...interesting...metroidvania. I mean, I logged 20 hours into the game and I've almost 100%'d it, but I'm not sure if I'd be stoked to play it again.I really like some parts of the game! The art direction for the game is absolutely fantastic, does a good job at immersing you in that dieselpunk type setting for the most part, and has areas that, while they blend together a bit too much, are all nice to look at. The combat is..alright. I love the idea of more combo-centric mechanics, but it is admittedly frustrating to do them sometimes. It takes a LOT to stagger bosses in the earlier parts of the game, and you don't have the tools to efficiently evade their attacks yet so it can often feel frustrating to try and pull off a combo you think you can cancel out of in time, only for the boss to armor through the attack and pummel you into the ground. Not a lot of the bosses are terribly difficult, but some of them took me more than a few tries to beat.  I will say that I had a lot more fun with the bosses later in the game, as at that point you have several weapons to pick from and switch between on the fly for some cool chain attacks.Exploration is a bit lack-luster. There's only really 2 unique collectibles to the game, which are plant seeds and posters. The former works similarly to grubs from Hollow Knight, though the rewards are pretty much just money and Data Disks that you can use to learn new skills, and the latter is weapon skins. I personally don't really mind the lack of collectibles for FIST, as the game doesn't really place too much emphasis on it, but for the size of some of the areas in the game I was disappointed with how much of it was just kind of...empty space.The music is pretty good, I think they stick out just enough to not be too "ambient", and there are a couple that I'll probably listen to outside of playing the game. Now here's the biggest issue I've had with the game. The technical side of stuff. Take this with a grain of salt, as my computer is pretty good, but the graphics card is a bit outdated. I could run the game at 60 with graphics set to medium (they're set to that from the start), and ran into a lot of issues outside of framerate, mainly that textures would pop in a lot along with some lighting which was a little annoying but not experience-ruining, however there were several instances where I'd enter a room and it would just be...completely empty except for a gray background until the room fully loaded in a couple seconds later. For the most part, like I said, I like the game. I'd definitely recommend it on sale, but make sure you have a good computer as I feel like the recommendations for it are undershooting just a bit, but that's just my thoughts. Gorgeous art, good music, alright combat (a small thing I didn't note but the story is just kinda meh), and some technical issues, I'd say it's like a 6-6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game so far, my favorite Metroidvania-style game since Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.The thing this title does very well that makes this sub-genre of 2D Platformer so appealing to me is giving players little glimpses of areas that you're unable to access until later in the game, when you've unlocked more of the games powers. That was something I loved about Castlevania: Symphony of the Night as a kid, and I also loved about Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night a few years ago. It sounds simple in theory, but it requires smart game design to achieve since you must construct the game in a way that allows you to backtrack while not feeling like you're actually backtracking. You do this by unlocking these Dark-Souls styled shortcuts that connect the world, and it's something this game did time and time again and I loved it.This game is also HUGE based on what I've experienced so far. The combat is solid and there are tons of skills to unlock. Combat was also refreshingly challenging at times in all the right ways. Story and graphics are great in my opinion, and the sound design is also notable, although I'm no expert in that arena. I was happy with the voice acting even though the main character Rayton, a rabbit/bunny with a giant robotic arm attached to his back, takes himself a bit too seriously (at least in the English voice acted version).My only real gripe with the game is there seems to be a screen tearing issue for me, even with V-Sync turned on. I looked for a solution online that recommended a couple ideas but so far, no luck.I hope more people become aware of this title so that maybe we can get a sequel someday. I recommend this title if you're into this style of game. I took a chance on it and was extremely happy I did.

It COULD use some better located warp points and more of them, especially later in the game to backtack missed items or secrets.  Bosses are a challenge, but nothing controller throwing. _childDocuments_.review: A really fun game. If you love Metroidvanias you'll want to check this out at least once; it contains a very stylish world and your character has a lot of maneuverability that makes exploring fun and intuitive. The graphics are great, the English voice cast is excellent, and it has a simple but satisfying story.  My main criticism is that, in order to unlock the game's most powerful move (and get 100% completion), you have to do combo training. The combos can be VERY hard to pull off, especially for people with disabilities (getting the timing right, the lag between switching weapons, having to press multiple buttons in quick succession), and it's very unlikely that you'll actually use the combos when combating enemies. The actual combat can range from very satisfying to very frustrating (some enemies take too long to kill or deal too much damage; there is no way to block damage and you don't get the parry ability until later in the game). There should be an accessibility feature that makes combat and combos easier to pull off (activating slo-mo, simplifying combos, health bars for all enemies so you can tell how long it would take to beat them, etc.).As for technical issues, I did run into a few crashes, though thankfully I didn't lose any progress, and they didn't completely break the game. Keep in mind I have a more high-end PC so people with a lower grade computer might have more trouble. Overall, yes this game needs a little polish and better accessibility, but is still an ultimately enjoyable and worthwhile experience and I'm glad I checked it out. The devs definitely show promise and I'd like to see more games from them.

_childDocuments_.review: A quality metroidvania, but not without some noticeable blemishes.Pros:- vast, diverse and beautiful setting you can easily find yourself be immersed in- a more fighting-game, combo-oriented fighting style than in other metroidvanias I've played- the story is OK+ - I wish the setting was developed further however- an easy to use map that does its job properly (not a given in recent metroidvanias for whatever reason)- varied, fun bossfights (special shoutout to last three boss fights)- no bugs of any kind - the game runs smoothly and without any issues on my PC without any dips in framerate or whatever- perfect price for its content and length- no overused, somewhat outdated nowadays mechanics like dropping your coins on death or whateverCons:- the focus on comboing hits diminishes the moment you obtain the whip which more or less breaks the game and makes the game sans a few bossfights a breeze- underwater levels - I've seen other reviews complain about them as well and I think the general issue is the fact that your moveset is much more limited underwater, there aren't many enemies and the platforming with limited, sluggish movement can get pretty difficult at times. Once you die you respawn way back and have to begin again. The underwater levels are also very vast for some reason- Ancient Complex - kudos for trying out something else for this location but I haven't enjoyed it at allAll in all it's a solid metroidvania, whose staggering amount of content reminds me of another quality Chinese metroidvania, Afterimage. Perfect for its price, no need to wait for a sale in my opinion. Patiently waiting for a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: Another pleasant surprise from my adventures into genres and franchises I normally wouldn't play but decided to give a shot. This game has a lot going for it, but you can tell it's indie due to it being rough around the edges. Graphics and character models look great, little bit of ray tracing here and there really make the anthropomorphized animal world really pop and come to life with a nice variety of different environments, enemies and things to figure out. Enemies and bosses provide decent challenge, but button-mashers beware as combos and proper timing to dodge and land hits become crucial in the endgame and for bosses.Voice acting was actually mostly pretty good, which was surprising considering it's a foreign game. Localizing from another language can add obstacles and challenges that aren't always present when working with the native language and voice actors, but of course, the performance that seemed to lag the most was the main character unfortunately, while the other problems with voice acting seemed to be due to writing/translating.Despite some stutters here and there and a crash or 2, I enjoyed myself more than I thought I would and went after all achievements even after spending an hour and half on the final boss (felt like I was playing Sekiro again, though I admit I was just being sloppy and impatient trying to beat the game before midnight).

On top of that the icons dont grow if you zoom in. So i found myself going closer to the TV...... Charakter Movement is flimsy. This design with the fist on the back makes you move very strangely. Found myself dying to some simple traps after 12 hours of gameplay just because I had to use my very short omnidash through some lasers. Which brings me to the lategame progression. To make it still hard this boss teleports a lot, attacks in both directions, could counter your attacks with a killing blow and telegraphs all his attacks the same way. _childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why this game flew over my radar, but I am glad I dig it up from my dusty video game piles. FIST: Forged In Shadow Torch is a well-made metroidvania focusing on action. Combat feels tense, and the combo is really satisfying to pull off. The art style may not be my taste, but I cannot deny the effort the developers put in to make the level gorgeous to behold, especially the stylized china town that is Joffre Street. Even though the levels aren't inter-connected like the others in the same genre, the game still delivers the core features of a metroidvania. But most importantly, Being an action-oriented metroidvania, the game offers players a decent of tools to create their own combo. The main draws here are the three primary weapons players gain through progression: Fist is the big mechanical arm strapped on our protagonist's back. It is the default weapon and also the most versatile one out of the three. The move sets of Fist are great for both starting combo and bridging the other two weapons. You can easily knock down or launch enemies for more combo options. You can even throw weaker enemies to create some breathing room; Drill focuses more on linear damage. Its multi-hit nature can easily stun-lock enemies for quite a while but the move sets lock you in place. Therefore, it is best to use this weapon as combo finishers; last but not least, Whip is a pair of grappling hooks. While the normal attack cannot flinch enemies like the other two, the speed and range can easily make up the gap. Being a grappling hook also allows you to grapple toward your enemies, forcing the downed ones to stand up. What makes the combat the most interesting is that you can freely swap between the three weapons. Attacks are cancelable and they can seamlessly connect with each other. It is always satisfying to pull off the more complicated combo in combat. These power take time to gain, however.Dual-purposed abilities are my favorite in the recent metroidvania. I am glad FIST: Forged In Shadow Torch get this idea right. The three weapons are the best example: Fist can punch button on doors and break ceiling vents; Drill allows you to glide, moves faster underwater, and opens fan lock on doors; Whip lets you grapple on to drone to reach higher places and close electric fences. Even though most of other gating abilities in this game are common trope, it is more important to see how they interact with the levels. Platforming challenges in each area aim to help you familiarize the tools you just get, and these challenges are satisfying to complete. The developers certainly takes time and effort to refine the mobility players have. With a few abilities gained out of order, you can even sequence-break some secret areas without proper tools, which is something I always cherish about in metroidvania.→Story is quite decent.→Love how well the characters are animated.→Many hidden items in each area. →Weapon paints have a lot of nice reference and easter eggs.→Enemies variety are lacking.→I wish the levels are more inter-connected.→You can only throw enemies left and right. At the very least you could and should be able to throw mid-air enemies downward.→I hate that any interaction with NPCs always close the menu, forcing me to interact with them again.中文小簡評→遊戲體驗很棒的類銀河系惡魔城。→最重要的一點，不獸控制啦！→雖然這種類寫實畫風不對我胃口，但不得不說一些場景設計真的很好看。→戰鬥主打連擊，三把武器各有優缺點，能夠在連擊中自由切換，打出你心儀的Combo。→三把武器同時也是關鍵技能，能解鎖更多機關及完成特定跳台挑戰。→其他關鍵技能雖然了無新意，但最重要的還是製作團隊如何在關卡設計中反映玩家取得技能後的機動性，這點我覺得做的很棒。→故事還不錯。→關卡藏有許多隱藏區域及道具。→武器烤漆有一堆致敬彩蛋。→敵人種類重複性高。→各個關卡並沒有相互連接。→只能把敵人往左往右丟，無法上拋或下砸。→很討厭每次跟NPC講完話後互動選單會直接關掉。

_childDocuments_.review: This is an OK game but it suffers from the same issues as Ori in that there is very little reason to go back to each area with each of the unlocks other than to just collect things.  Sure those things can be useful but they are in no way hindering you from completing the game.  this is an incredibly linear experience considering its a metroidvania.  This is very much a game on rails with just collectables locked behind abilities.   The enemy diversity is non existent, theres about 6 different enemies which just have colour swatches changed, sometimes with an added hat to tell the player they are stronger.  This hat is only different per type of enemy.  The combat and movement mostly feel fluid, so long as you dont do any advanced combos (which is actually ok, because there is pretty much no standard enemy which can withstand a standard combo and mini / bosses dont flinch or ragdoll in the same way leaving advanced combos useless) until you go to do the combat challenges and you suddenly realise that the combat is actually very clunky.The story is ok, the cutscenes are fun.  the non-cinematic cutscenes are jarring to say the least.  the text appears at a different speed than it is spoken, and the characters movements are scripted to be timed with the conversations.   So if you skip any text box at all then characters can start teleporting from point to point as you have also skipped their movement animation without realising it.  Also the subtitles often start with the last line of audible dialogue.At no point in any game ever should there be a collectable in the literal room before the final boss which requires a turn in.  this means about 20 minutes of back tracking and then again to get this collectable, turn it in in the safe zone and then return to finish the game.  I don't know if you get returned to the safe zone after beating the boss as once the credits finished rolling the game crashed and I wasn't going to do it again just to check.  all in all i got 96% on first play through though I don't know if this includes the collectables i gathered but didn't turn in.  I certainly had no where else to go on the map and nothing more to collect, so I'm assuming it doesn't.  in which case, 100% collected and completed and 4% not turned in.  all in all, its a fun game.  it just has some things I don't enjoy and have found other metroidvania games to have done better.

_childDocuments_.review: Update/TLDR: So - after another extended underwater section (and the promise of many more!) and the terrible combat, I've had enough; This is not a good game.--- F.I.S.T is a very loose game adaptation of a 1978 movie [citation needed], but instead of Sly Stallone we get a fluffy bunny with a giant mechanical fist attached and an action hero movie rasp, and instead of a story about unions and the mob we get a bunch of generic dieselpunk fantasy twaddle. So yeah, not very faithful furry version of the story. It takes the form of a metroidvania game- I'd say this is an attempt to create as pure a metroidvania experience as possible. It's hard to explain, but with most games you get the feel that it's a game first, and then it fits into a genre; Here it feels like the reverse is true. This gels with my opinion that it's a pretty uninspired take: technically very competent, but in the end kind of soul-less. As a game, it's mostly fine - a 2d platformer with great technical presentation that quickly gets its hooks in with the typical genre exploration and ability progression. Combat is a low point, as the dodge move does not grant invincibility and does not go through enemies. Later on you get a parry move, but it's mapped to the same stick as movement so it's very fiddly (and to me, next to useless.) Exploration is OK. The areas are varied and have the requisite secrets and bits that you'll need to backtrack to later; The map tool is pretty good, marking down everything you run into with clear icons; The main problem is that a lot of screens feel empty, and while varied, they're mostly some variation of city street or military facility. The art style isn't very striking, but it does manage a few cool vistas - the 3d is very well made, and there are a lot of graphical bells and whistles (ray tracing and such.) Because the plot and the characters are pretty bland, and the game as a whole feels like a retread, it's the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the points of friction that stand out. Underwater levels or multi-stage boss battle difficulty spikes. The fact that you can't skip some cutscenes. Backtracking through a ton of empty screens to an unexplored room, only to find a handful of coins. The combat. It's not enough to offset the core draw of the genre, but... I don't know, even what's good in it feels very rote. Like a technical team flexing its muscles, an engineering exercise rather than an artistic one. I'm certain that's not true, and hope that the team proves me wrong with whatever they chose to do next. It's a generous game in content, with tons of things to do and places to go, and it's got a ridiculous amount of polish; it's just a shame it doesn't make more of an impact, and that the annoyances are so pronounced.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, one of the better Metroidvanias I’ve played.Pros:+ Combat is fun, with satisfying combos. I especially liked using the drill.+ Difficulty progression felt very steady throughout. Every time I felt like I was starting to master an enemy type, the game would introduce me to a new variant of that type, forcing me to adapt. The challenge was always solid but nothing ever felt too hard.*+ Gorgeous semi-realistic graphics & aesthetic.+ Furry characters.+ Main theme music is a banger.Cons:- Healing uses the same gauge as several other functions that could be useful in combat (namely ranged attacks, a parry ability, and a decoy dummy). Because you’ll probably want healing to be available as much as possible, those other functions will barely ever be used, if at all.- I occasionally encountered a glitch that caused some of the buttons on my controller to stop working temporarily.- Ending is a nothing-burger.(*Except the mechanical core boss. _childDocuments_.review: 5/10: The Good, The Bad, The UglyThe Good - Has nice graphics and environment. The backtracking is pretty decent and the platforming and puzzles are pretty good. The level diversity is pretty vast and the use of weapons as secondary equipment are pretty clever; like the drill turns into a helicopter and a propeller for underwater levels. The Bad - Most enemies are pretty easy until the bosses and then its die a couple times, learn their attack patterns and call it a day. That alone isn't such a bad combat system but the way the boss fights unfold sucks. There's never any reason to switch between weapons and pretty much all boss fights follow the same system... get 2-3 hits in, run, evade, repeat until fight is over. It becomes very systematic and tedious making most of them forgettable and boring.The Ugly - Combat just ends up feeling cheap. Often I'll start out attacking the boss and getting 1 hit in just to be turned around the other direction on the immediate following swing . You never have a chance to use your more powerful, unlocked chain attacks cuz the enemy will just hit you, so its more cheap hit and run tactics. And the worse... F*ing STUN LOCK. Prepare to be stun locked and incapacitated a lot. Game just turns you into a punching bag so often that it hardly feels fair or like your skill set means anything. Personally, the game just feels cheap and lazy after awhile. Any game that relies on Stun Lock to add to its difficulty is just more lazy bs from uncreative crap devs imo. Sucks. I really was looking forward to this game but its combat is just so stiff and mechanical that it lost all appeal & the fact that some enemy attacks are so fast paced and the input feels so unresponsive at times just ruins it.  If you're into Metroidvainia style games you'd probably enjoy this, but if you're a casual gamer I'd pick up a gamer that's higher on your "To Buy List"

_childDocuments_.review: Really great metroidvania game.2.5D: 2D gameplay on 3D engine. Two difficulty settings.Beautiful graphics and relaxing music, large locations that differ from each other, well crafted.Nice story where steampunk meets furry creatures and one tough brawling bunny, with voiced characters.Fighting is done very well, smooth and responsive, no issues, really nice finisher moves as well.Should take you around 13-16 hours, and it's not too difficult.The downsides:Master Wu training is the most difficult and frustrating part of the game. It's not required but most powerful skill in the game is gated behind it (and few achievements)Lots of travelling back and forth, especially when you get new powers. There is a fast travel system but it's not that easily accessible (ie. one per location) so you still spend some time getting to it.Had a blast with it (excluding Master Wu part)Definitely recommending.

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem, surprised this one didn't get more attention. Extremely enjoyable, snappy "Metroidvania" set in a creative, well-fleshed out world inhabited by interesting characters. I was consistently surprised by all of the little details that brought this world to life. Combat is good and responsive, choose between 3 different weapon types/styles that can be insta-swapped to make your own combos. Lots of secrets to hunt down and skills to unlock. The only downside I encountered was the rather abrupt, "Okay, but what happened after?" ending, no real New Game + to speak of (if you want to unlock further secrets and such it must be done by loading your last save before the final boss) and some janky custscene animation that often would not sync with dialogue. Aside from those minor downsides a real quality title, must-play for fans of the genre, would buy any sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best metroidvania to release in 2021. FIST doesnt do anything groundbreaking but it does almost everything right in regards to the genre. If youre looking to scratch that itch you cant go wrong here. It has great combat, nice graphics, some solid platforming and the game paces really well. One thing I didnt like was some of the secrets you find is just extra coins, imo they should have gotten rid of shadowboxes and replace them just to make those secrets more rewarding. You can really style on enemies in regards to combat but some just dont have enough health to go crazy on and some bosses wont allow you to go off so you just need to stick to a high dps bnb instead of trying to juggle. If you like fighting games you might enjoy this system, combos arent too hard,you dnt need to master them and the training mode trials gives you some good ideas, my biggest issue was getting confused with the weapon switching since you cant really map anything besides your movement or attack. There also a decent difficulty spike for the last 3 bosses outta nowhere. Just parry stay patient and use a high dps bnb I just tried to do any combo that ended in the down special with the fist. I didnt really care for the story but its passable, dnt really play this genre for that but I'll give them the nod, I didnt really care for the zootopia type animals but it makes for a really nice setting that feels alive with some history. Theres full english voice acting in this game which is impressive since this was made by chinese developers, they even sync the lips and it sounds good. The only reason why this game didnt get as much praised as it deserves was probably because its chinese. This might be the best recent metroidvania I've played since blasphemous and bloodstained. I personally would rate those games higher but this doesnt lag far behind. Definitely deserves more love and will go down as a solid staple of the genre. You cant go wrong here.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this one came out of nowhere and ended up being one of my favorite metroidvania's in recent memory. In a genre that is stacked to the brim with certified classics I wouldn't go so far as to say this one's in the top 3, but it's at minimum top 10, easy. For a relatively lower profile release, I was shocked at how gorgeous this game is. If you have a high end gaming rig, this is easily one of the best looking games in the genre. The graphic fidelity did come at the cost of some stutters as well as odd texture and environmental pop in, but overall this one is a stunner. The overall aesthetic here I would describe as furry Final Fantasy 7.  The city the majority of the game takes place in reminds me a lot of Midgar, with it's haphazardly built slums and opulent entertainment districts. The game also bears more than a few thematic resemblances to FF7 as well, with the main character being a jaded former soldier reluctantly called back into action to aid a resistance group in fighting a tyrannical organization that is despoiling the planet. I don't usually comment on music quality, but I have to mention it here, as this game also has a really damn good soundtrack.Combat and exploration are both excellent as well. The movement here is just perfect, not too slippery, not too clingy, just right. Wall jumping and dashing through the environments is felt fluid and precise, and I never encountered a situation where the character felt out of sync with my inputs. Combat is simple on the surface, but the multiple weapons, special abilities, and pop up moves allow for some incredibly robust combos. My only complaint here is that you have almost no ranged options and are almost always up against dudes with guns. There is an upgrade to your dash that allows you to pass through enemies and projectiles, but it's withheld until the very end of the game. I really feel like this should have been the default, and it would have made a lot of the encounters with multiple gun users feel a bit more balanced. Overall this is a great game and 100% worth it at full price. While it won't dethrone something like Shovel Knight or Bloodstained, it's definitely up there with games like Shadow Complex and the Strider remake as some of the best of the genre. Unreservedly recommended to anyone who enjoys metroidvania's.

_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a fantastic Metroidvania.  It follows all the classic tropes, sidescrolling, wall jumping, large interconnected map revealing goodness.   FIST takes place in a depressed, Steampunk world, that is being torn apart by a war between the Furtizens (anthropomorphic animals) and Robots.  Do not be put off, there is no odd "furry" stuff, I found the characters and the character designs to be creative and fun.  FIST brings a few top tier characteristics to the table.  The first, and one that is pretty obvious if you have seen screencaps/videos, is that FIST has stunning graphics.   The art is badass, and the engine is super advanced and modern, with support for heavy ray tracing.  All of the environments and characters and fur look terrific.  Another feather in FISTs cap is its combat systems.  You eventually unlock 3 main weapons, that are all interesting and fun.  The combat can be difficult, and your crazy juggles and combos and parries are all needed to survive.  It reminded me of a Platinum game at times, which is high praise coming from me.  FIST has all the requisite secret areas, and backtracking with new abilities to find hidden collectibles, and remains fun and challenging throughout, and lots of difficult bosses and sub bosses, to really test your mettle.  I really enjoyed all my time with FIST, it was never a chore, even when I was stuck on a tough room or boss.If there is one negative to FIST, is that it has a little technical jank.  The game would crash out pretty consistently every 30-60 minutes if ray tracing is on high, in addition to weird noise on the edge of the screen that you are moving towards.  Textures can load in a little slow, and the game can get choppy at times, even with vsync/gsync.  I do not think these issues are related to my setup, as I saw many similar complaints online.  These technical issues are the only mark against an instant classic.  I hope we see a sequel!9/10

I haven't finished it as I write this, but I can't find any negatives to it so far. Graphics are rock solid. For a platformer, its gorgeous. I like this better than Ori, and other games of its ilk. The mechanics are also solid in this with sufficient weapon variety. The Metroidvania elements to progress in the maps are pretty cleverly done too...nothing really seems contrived. The story is OK...while I can't bag it, it's pretty simplistic. Bunny boy is an old war veteran and tasked with taking down one of his fellow former ally soldiers who he thought was dead. He's not, and apparently he has bad intentions. As such Bunny-boy (Rayton), needs to talk some sense into him...through violence, and needs to ally with people who are less than reputable to do it. Honestly...as I write that, I'm thinking...HMMMM it's not actually bad :). The voice over work is good. I need to stress, I don't like platformer games too much. I really didn't like Ori 1 or 2 (beat them...bought them because of the hype). I also didn't like Hollow Knight at all. I liked Salt and Sanctuary though (mainly because of the boss battles, and the subdued puzzles). Basically, if you are more into combat, and less into puzzles, you'll probably like this. _childDocuments_.review: I am strongly recommending this game, with a few caveats that need attention.This game gets almost everything "right" and by that I mean the vast majority of the game is impressive as hell. The graphics/animations are well beyond what I expected in a metroidvania. The sound design was also exceptional, specifically the ambiance and sound effects which built both immersion and impact, respectively. The environments were detailed and beautiful. The story included cutscenes/cinematics which I wasn't expecting either, and added some depth to the characters and aesthetic.The abilities, while a bit vanilla (double jump, dash, wall climb) and predictable, were still fun to obtain and the process in which you do felt well-paced and definitely gave you incentive to backtrack, which you'll be doing a lot of.Speaking of which, navigating the map is a relatively easy feat, since main objectives are marked in or out of fog of war, and the paths are somewhat obvious. You won't be finding any wall chicken here, but there are some breakable entrances you might overlook. The mechanics are one of the areas where the game diverges from your standard metroidvania, but it's a good thing. You collect plants to turn in for rewards, eat noodles for temporary health pools, and there are a good handful of secrets scattered throughout the game that are entirely optional but could even open up new areas. The weapons, abilities, and items are diverse. Some are much less useful (imo) than others, but it still gives the player a little extra agency that often lacks in this genre.While almost everything about this game was enjoyable, the parts that weren't were, in my case, severe detriments; to the point that while I spent most of the game feeling a 8 or 9/10, the last few hours felt like a 5. If that sounds harsh, let me explain why.The controls can be clunky at the worst possible times. Namely, drinking a desperately needed potion. There is an animation lock/delay when trying to do so. If you're not perfectly still a half second or second before drinking the potion, it won't register the input. This meant death for me more often than not.  While most of the platforming felt responsive and smooth, switching weapons was also a pain. There is a mini-game where you are required to switch weapons mid-combo, and I simply gave up after a handful of attempts after the weapon swap wouldn't register.Navigating the map is simple, but tedious. This is a minor complaint, but since the game goes a lot harder on the platforming than most in the genre do, going back through a spike maze with double jumps and air dashes gets annoying on the fifth run because you finally got that new movement ability. This game also loves lasers, and Meatboy-style resets if you land on certain ones. The underwater areas, one in particular, I just flat out avoided at the expense of a few plant seeds because I just didn't want to deal with the teleporter location, traversing multiple areas, then swimming slowly through a lengthy area while hiding sporadically from a mechanic that is fun the first time and only the first time.Lastly, but possibly most importantly, the one aspect that infuriated me the most was the last hour or two of the game, as a whole. The last major dungeon is a total slog. The puzzles are boring and irritating at best. Without spoiling anything, the puzzle was a snooze fest but took a while to complete. They also added a lot of "let's just absolutely annoy the player to literal death" enemies that would snipe you as you were carrying a puzzle item, or prevent you from hitting a switch several times. It was an exercise in patience and tenacity, not enjoyment.But that area is nothing compared to the last 3 boss fights. I won't spoil anything, because I don't have to. The combat and boss fights in the game went from a comfortable challenge to a soulslike disaster very quickly. Regardless of the "get gud" lifers or people that just don't find games difficult in general, the difficulty scaling exploded. Until that point the scaling felt relatively natural and organic. You fought a boss that was maybe a 3/10 on the difficulty scale, then a few sections later a 4 or 5 tops. This went from 5 to 9 on the first of the three, then an 11, then a really strong desire to uninstall the game and never look back. Shame.The solution to this conundrum was listening to the players and adding in an Easy difficulty. Now, while I appreciate the devs doing this, here's what you ended up with:Easy: Too easy. The game is basically casual at this point. You'll rarely, if ever die, and bosses are a joke.Normal: Well balanced. Fun. Then basically go ♥♥♥♥ yourself for the last three bosses.Was that the right call? Probably not, but everyone should still play the game. I spent a lot of time on the negatives but it's because I am coming out of the game fresh and I felt blindsided. I want to both encourage other metroidvania fans this is a must-have, but also prepare y'all for the moment when the game suddenly decides to turn into a soulslike and maybe go ahead and get a replacement controller ready to order.

_childDocuments_.review: Where The Ascent is an exemplar of cyberpunk, F.I.S.T. is a prime exhibit of dieselpunk done right. With antropomorphic animals mixed in it, of all things. And it works nearly perfectly.  The game is metroidvania, featuring puzzles, exploration and fighting with combos. Abiliteis, comboes and gadgets are unlocked and upgraded as the strory progresses. Overall, movement and combat are very fluid and responsive, with the sole exception of weapon switching, which made me give up on advanced combo training. I played with a controller, as recommended.  The graphics and animations are gorgeous. The envinronment practically screams dieselpunk - there are factories, slums, military bases and neon lit streets, and it all looks like reimagined and more fantastic version of 1950s, with East Asian flair. On occations there are more natural areas, like caves, mines or snow covered mountains. The backgrounds have almost same insane level of details as in The Ascent. The characters are animals and it is fully acknowledged in story. They look great and they are excellently animated, especially in cutscenes.  I have played using original Chinese voices, which were good and added to the atmosphere. The music fits with the era that inspired dieselpunk - it is a selection of jazz that underscores the film noir feel of the story.  The story and dialogues are fairly interesting and I enjoyed them. As noted above, there is a heavy noir feel to them. Sometimes the translation is a bit clumsy and on a few occations the text did not fit into the dialogue window.  Overall this is an excellent and enjoyable game with a unique atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics, design, animations, weapons, movement, map / exploration, secrets - everything is great, a real treat for metroidvania fans like me. The voice acting is fun (I recommend the Chinese original with subtitles; nothing comes close to a badass rabbit with a deep Chinese voice). For me there's only one downside: the combat. I never really got into it. It's okay if you only fight one or two enemies, but the moment there are more the mechanics didn't really work for me. In my opinion it's a bad design decision to add parrying as a skill rather late in the game; I found it hard to integrate into the fights, especially those with many enemies. That's because there're a lot of combos in fighting which prevent the enemy from breaking free - but enemies also use combos and once you're hit you cannot recover but must endure the whole combo. So, if you miss the first parry you are locked into an animation and get a beating - rather frustrating. If you're fighting several enemies, I found it impossible to block on all sides; in the end I sometimes parried by accident, but I rarely used it on purpose. Even later in the game you get the ability to dash through enemies and attacks, which I found to be a lot more useful. So, I won most of the harder fights because I leveled up to the max and dashed a lot. Simply put: Other games do combat better. The biggest frustration was not being able to get a 100% because I was unable to complete the fighting challenges which earn you an item to open one last door, get one last skill, complete the map, and get the last poster. None of these are essential for finishing the game, but as any metroidvania addict knows, you don't want to stop before reaching a 100% ...But the fighting challenges require you to complete ridiculously complex combos, including several weapon changes in midair and what-not. I already failed the first advanced training (not for lack of trying) and after I learned there're also master challenges, I knew I wouldn't waste hours and hours in trying. I found the timing required for the combos simply too tight. Surely there are hardcore gamers who like this kind of challenge, I’d have preferred if this weren’t tied to completing the game a 100% but rather as an achievement for masochists.Despite the complaints: A beautiful game I had almost 30 hours of fun with and I can absolutely recommend it to fans of the genre.7/10
