_childDocuments_.review: This game has stayed within my interest scope for quite some time. I've opened the page couple of times, read through reviews and postponed it to a "better discount - then we're talking. Maybe. Don't know. Should I get this?" shelf.Finally I've downloaded a demo, played a bit and decided that it's not that bad, so why not grab a copy? Should you get one too? Let's see...The game looks amazing: the characters, the backgrounds, all the small details and cut scenes. Visually it's gorgeous.Movement system is high tier too: once you unlock all the stuff that allows advanced navigation - the game really blooms.Abilities themselves are very well done and demand using all of them on a regular basis, which is a huge plus IMO, as recently I played too many metroidvanias bloated with different skills/abilities/features that are implemented just to be used once or twice and then vanish completely.Combat... Combat is: let's put it this way - not for all. It uses combo system, and personally, I never used any of those combos that are taught to you by your martial arts trainer. Simple ones are quite enough. Think of Guacamelee  style combat, yet more primitive and less diverse. Still well done and satisfying overall - yet I see where some people may find it non-perfect. Level design and backtracking - great, yet with some flaws. I still hope that I will get the ability to teleport between save spots in the endgame, as navigating around can be quite tedious. The world is full of puzzles, secrets and challenges all of which are fun to discover. True, some respawn logic in challenges and other minor details are not very well thought, but that's just a small issue along the way. The  that may turn people off is the developer's attempt to make the game more diverse by adding sections of gameplay that break out of the core game mechanics. I'm talking about stealth mission (there will be a level where you lose all your gear and will have to sneak through), some underwater madness (where the game starts to feel more like Eco the Dolphin), etc. And it's clearly a love/hate situation - either this will entertain you, or you will be completely turned off by it. Personally I found it frustrating first, yet now, looking back - that added to the overall experience and I think the game benefits from such sections. The music... Well, I can't say anything  felt close with my heart, so yeah, it's there and it's not bad. Matter of taste. (Though the starting city location tune... That's a weird melody choice) This is a great metroidvania with astonishing visuals, good movement/ability system and fun exploration.Some people may find it frustrating due to complex, yet not perfect combat system & random change of game pace in custom levels, such as stealth mission/underwater exploration, etc. Personally I think this is a great game and do recommend for all genre enjoyers! Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game does have a lot of PS2 energy, and I mean that in the nicest way. The characters all look nice, they have decent voice acting, and there's a lot of love put into the world. However. I reached a section where I rode slowly on an box for several minutes, not actually being challenged, but was forced to in order to recollect my gear after a Supposed-To-Lose-Fight. There were no enemies, no real challenge, and, let me emphasize, AN INCREDIBLY SLOW MOVING BOX I HAD TO RIDE. There are clear issues when the game wants to play unique animations during dialogue, with the occasional long pause between dialogue lines so that the fighting animation can load or something. Also, while the voice acting isn't bad, it suffers from a really awkward translation it feels like. Cicero, a character whose reveal is supposed to be a surprise, is mentioned earlier by another character as being someone you have to fight by your training Master. Your attacks all feel like they have slightly less range than they actually do and the fact that you can hang in the air and keep hitting without gravity applying feels strangely stiff? The longer I played, the more my interest petered out. And that's despite the game having lots of hilarity there - the animal people are called 'furtizens', there's a character called Wang selling a drink called 'Pump', and the cat lady has a lot of breast physics that just seem so out of place. Altogether, not the worst time I've ever had, but I don't want to play any more than I already have.

_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a Metroidvania with Spectacle fighter type combat. I like Metroidvanias and I like spectacle fighters, so I really enjoyed playing this game. I would've likely enjoyed this game a lot more if it took advantage of the spectacle fighter combat aspect better….. But more on that later.As I mentioned, FIST has spectacle fighter combat. So instead of simply spamming the attack button in something like Castlevania, you're using a mix of light attacks, heavy attacks, SP attacks, and switching between different weapons. SP attacks do lot of damage, but they take SP. You recover SP by doing regular attacks against enemies. So you're encouraged to master combos which incorporate both regular attacks and SP attacks, which is great.There's 3 different weapons in total, and there's a few hours in between as you get new weapons, so the game is nicely paced in this regard since you have a decent amount of time to master each weapon before you get the next one. Whenever I got a new weapon, I really enjoyed incorporating it into my combos, and it was really fun to master combos that used all 3 of the weapons! In addition to your main weapons, you also have 4 "sub-weapons", which cost EP to use. You can use these weapons to either heal, parry attacks, throw out a decoy, or shoot homing missiles. Out of all the Metroidvanias I've played, the offense aspect of FIST has to be one of the best I've experienced.While it would've been fun enough to do cool looking combos on enemies all day, the developers were also able to make the game challenging. Regular enemies are challenging through a decent amount of variety in what they can do such that you have to approach them in different ways:	• Some enemies have ranged weapons who'll be able to attack you before you can reach them, forcing you to dodge	• Some enemies can randomly disappear mid combo and attack you from above	• Some enemies have shields that can only be broken through certain attacks	• Some enemies are in the air and shooting at you from far away, forcing you to do some mid-air combos to reach them	• Some enemies "charge" at you with super armor, so if you try attacking them, they'll tank through it and hit you	• Some enemies can enter a "counter" stance where if you attack them in any way, they'll parry the attack and hit you backIn addition to having a decent amount of enemies, you're quite often going to be facing multiple enemies at the same time. Every so often, you'll enter "arenas" where waves of enemies will keep spawning, such that you can face 4 enemies at once. So combat definitely never feels like you are one-sidedly comboing enemies to death. If you were only facing one enemy, you could likely infinite combo them to death. However, since you're facing multiple enemies, you have to master dealing as much damage as possible in the shortest time possible so that you're never in one place for too long and can move onto the next enemy as fast as possible. So not only is the offense aspect of FIST really good, so is the defensive aspect.In regards to the bosses, they all offer a decent challenge. Bosses can basically be split into 2 types. "Humanoid" bosses can be juggled in the air every so often (they have super armor for a few attacks) while "Heavy" bosses can't be juggled in the air, but after doing enough damage to them they'll be vulnerable to a ground combo (or every so often they'll just stand around doing nothing, at which point you can go ham on them). Apart from these categories, bosses for the most part feel very distinct from each other and so whenever you face a boss, you have to master their moves and how to dodge them. While bosses are reused every so often, it's very rare. Most Spectacle Fighters are a series of combat encounters one after another with pretty much nothing else. FIST on the other hand is also a Metroidvania, which means there's a decent amount of platforming and exploration. The platforming is pretty decent, especially later on when you get the whip weapon and air dash at which point the mid-air platforming sections are really fun. The exploration also feels rewarding. The rewards are basically stat boosts to your HP, SP, and EP bars. While this is nothing new, it's particularly designed well in FIST since you HP, SP, EP bars are very tiny in the beginning. For example, your SP and EP bars start out at 2, so exploring and increasing these bars by 1 feels huge. Not only that, but you can find "data disks" by exploring, which allows you to learn new combat moves, which is always something to look forward to.While I found the non-combat sections of the game a decent way to change up the pace, one thing I really didn't like was that this game has a lot of underwater levels (emphasis on a LOT). I generally don't like water levels, but in this game it's even worse since when you're underwater, you can't do ANY combos anymore. Not only that, but the enemies you face are a lot more simple, needing only like one hit to take them down. I really wish all of the underwater levels were replaced with more land combat encounters, since I didn’t enjoy any of them.One last thing I'll mention about the combat isn't exactly a negative, but more like a missed opportunity. As I was playing the game, I felt that FIST was a great game, but it didn't quite reach the levels of something like Hollow Knight, where you really have to master the combat and bosses in order to succeed. Then near the end game, I reached a room with an "arcade machine". By interacting with the arcade machine, you could face bosses that you've previously fought all over again if you wanted. Not only that, but there were 3 "tournaments" where you faced 4 bosses in a row, with the last 2 bosses always being ones that couldn't be found in the game. These "hidden" bosses were basically Hollow Knight level bosses where they were really challenging and really required you to master them before you could beat them. I really wish these bosses were spread out in the game instead of all being saved as an optional thing at that absolute end of the game, since the difficulty curve would've been a lot better for it.There's a story, but it's fairly lackluster. You play as a rabbit who's in a town that's run by machines who are bad and you have to stop them. These machines are after something called a "spark" and if they get it, they'll be unstoppable which is really bad. The problem is that the game does not explain at all about WHY these machines are so bad. So while the story is really pushing me into caring about wanting to stop them, I really don't because I am never shown the machines doing anything particularly horrendous. If anything, I kind of find them funny since every so often the machines make jokes. They're kind of too "authoritarian", but that's about it. I also didn't care about the protagonist all that much, since his only goal seems to be to stop the machines, which is really generic. Since I didn't care about the antagonist nor the protagonist, I didn't find myself engaged with the story.Overall, I really enjoyed the gameplay of FIST. There's very few 2D spectacle fighters I've played, and after playing FIST, I wish there was more of them. Hopefully if I play some in the future, the developers will know better than to put underwater levels in their spectacle fighter :P

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot, in good conscience, recommend paying money for this or any other video game published by Bilibili. The reason for this is that the publisher is extremely unethical. They fired an entire dev team (for NEON ECHO) without compensation just because their EARLY ACCESS game didn't make enough money... then proceeding to keep that early access game on the store despite it no longer being under development anymore. Prior to this, this was the most promising roguelite platformer under development.Update: I have now played this. In short this game is 30% cheaper than prince of persia the lost crown and it's basically prince of persia the lost crown but around 30% worse.The good about the game is exactly the same as the good with prince of persia the lost crown: large size, high end graphics, high end budget, voice acting, and so on. In addition it has a proper english translation despite being a non western gameThe bad things are also similar to those of prince of persia the lost crown but in addition it has the following issues:- very serious performance issues related to asset loading in two biomes, the hub biome and the underwater base biome.- 20% of voice acting is missing- The combat training is impossible, unlike prince of persia the lost crown. This also means it is impossible to obtain the final ultimate optional ability, which means it is impossible to defeat the penultimate boss on normal difficulty (but funnily enough the final boss is easier and is beatable on normal).- Unlike prince of persia the lost crown where it is possible to customize the game to your own playstyle with charms, there is no such option here and if you can't get used to DMC style combat then you are screwed.- This game has some of the worst backtracking I have ever seen in a metroidvania, it even goes out of its way to make it as bad as possible with the treasure chests that require a skeleton key, so even if you find it you still have to backtrack to it with a key later on (and these are usually really far away from warp points)On a neutral note, like all chinese video games this has bad writing but compared to all other chinese video games I've played this actually has the best writing and translation I've seen.Anyway I recommend just getting prince of persia the lost crown instead. You get what you paid for, especially if you buy that on the switch.

Every boss had some style or mechanic I liked.They were fun to figure out and a defeat wasn´t devastating. There is always a checkpoint near.The newly added Boss Rush is nice. It showed me what I have learned so far and that the first bosses are easier now.If to easy: switch on some or even all of the handicaps.Or see that there are even meaner versions of some of them.As hard as some bosses could be, I would wish me one or more harder difficulties.Just to spice it up a bit for the game outside the boss fights.Would I recommend?Yeah, go for it. Combat revolved around three weapons—fist, drill and whip—that each brought their own combos and fighting styles while also serving as tools for navigation, from the drill's gliding to the whip's grappling. Switching between these weapons mid-battle was possible for more complex combos, as well as adjustment to various enemy types and scenarios.It wasn’t the most interesting metroidvania I’ve played, but it had its moments with the combat, puzzles and decent amount of challenges. _childDocuments_.review: I picked this Metroidvania up on a recommendation, and the game largely lived up to it.The first thing that must be said is how gorgeous it is.  It's apparently the first/only game of some (indie?) Chinese studio, but the art easily feels AAA.  Of other indie Metroidvanias I've played, only Bloodstained comes close, but this goes above and beyond making its strictly 2-D gameplay feel like a planar slice of an immersive 3-D world.  In many places, interactible stage elements swoop in from foreground and background, and maps are crafted to give the feel of fully 3-d cities and rooms.  The only complaint I've got about this incredible scenery-fest is that on slower computers it definitely occasionally lags, and fuzzes in elements as it loads their low-detail meshes followed by their high-detail meshes.  Once or twice a day during my playtime, it would lock up entirely (<1 FPS) for a second or two, but as I played it usually settled down.It's worth a look for that alone, if you're more of an indie gamer looking for some eye candy in a genre not known for it.  Beyond that?  Pleasant but not a stand-out.  The difficulty curve was reasonable after some big early-game spikes; I took out most bosses on my first or second pass, with a few (including the final one) stomping me flat until I learned their patterns.  The basic enemies are dangerous in numbers, too, but the game is very forgiving -- you don't lose anything on death.  The automap is *exceptionally* friendly, marking many (but not all) collectibles and all unopened doors, so your backtracking is low-guesswork.  Quests are strictly go-here-fight-boss with a side order of acquire-collectibles, but the midgame has some branching story points keeping it from full linearity.  The story didn't particularly grab me (old grizzled war hero gets pulled back into his old life when bad guys intervene) but the English translation and the voice acting are solid.The gameplay is smooth but with some noticeable flaws.  Movement techniques are tight and pretty forgiving -- I appreciated that double-jump plus dash was sufficient to let you sequence break some areas -- but the late-game grapple has some counterintuitive auto-snapping (prioritizing targets below you sometimes??) and several of your moves have startup frames which can lead to false starts and failed activations.  (Also, I only discovered AFTER the final boss that you can continue to drink healing potions by keeping the trigger held down, instead of having to go through the startup animation each time.  That would have made several tough fights easier.)Similarly, the combat/combo system is deep and intricate -- but is both held back by poor controls (most of the sample combos you're shown in martial arts training switch mid-combo between your weapons, and the only way to cycle between your three weapons is L1 or L2, and if you hit the wrong trigger and cycle the wrong way, you're dead in the water).  Meanwhile, combat has a Souls-like pace of finding an opening for slow attacks which don't always stun-lock the enemy; most of the enemies have ranged attacks and you're almost entirely a melee character; and you don't even get an invulnerable dodge until the next-to-last level, so for most of the game you're relying on short strings of basic attacks in between madly jumping to avoid projectiles and dashing out of range of big enemy swings, greatly limiting the actual utility of the combo system.  You can lay down some serious hurt with your SP-consuming special attacks, though -- especially after upgrading them to more powerful versions with your in-game currency -- and it's always satisfying clearing a room by unleashing a special or two.I'll admit it, I largely played the game because furry, but I think there's plenty to like here beyond that.  I listed a lot of its rough edges above, but when I wasn't getting broken out of my experience by them, this was decently engrossing gameplay and a visual feast.

_childDocuments_.review: Six years have passed since the Machine Legion successfully invaded Torch City. The furizens (anthropomorphic citizens) left after this invasion live in constant fear. There is a resistance that thrives in the shadows, but for most they just want to be left alone, hopefully to live their lives the way that they can. In F.I.S.T: Forged in Shadow Torch, you will be taking on the role of Rayton, a former ace soldier who is pulled back into the conflict. You will not have to go it alone, however, you’re going to have a mechanical rig that starts with a very intimidating and painful metal fist. This is a Metroidvania type of game. It’s all about conquering different areas of the world, with the world being filled with platforms, obstacles, and enemies. There are of course hidden goodies throughout the game, as well as additional tools that you can use as you get further into the game. As you progress through the game you’ll also have the chance to spend currency on upgrading your moves to help better put the enemies out of their misery. I know that the storyline of the reluctant hero thrusted back into the spotlight to try to take on the world by himself is a very well worn theme, but I have to say that this game made it entertaining and interesting. I cared about the other characters in the game, I felt the pain of the main character, I felt as if the developers cared about the story. To be honest, the crowning achievement of any good story is that the player is left wanting more, and I indeed was left wanting to know “what happens next?”You’re going to end up with the fist, a drill, and a whip as your arsenal, and each has their own special talents to help with accessing sealed areas. They also give you different modes of attack be it with range, speed, or abilities. I did spend most of the game using the fist, but I will admit that there were certain parts of the game that relying on the fist alone will not equal success. There are some other limited use items that you’ll gain throughout the game, but to be honest I mostly had it on the carrot juice (think of it as health potions) so that when I screwed something up I didn’t immediately die. From start to finish this game took just under 11 hours and I have to say that most of the time it was jam packed with fast paced action. Sure there were a couple of areas that made me want to pull my hair out because I mistimed a jump, or I failed to get clear of an enemy when I was trying to heal so death came to meet me, but that was part of the game, and something that I learned from. There is some backtracking that you will have to do throughout the game, sometimes to continue the storyline, other times to go back and gain access to previous areas that you didn’t have the right skills to access, but for the most part you’re going to be revealing more and more of the world. There are a couple of “warp spots” but to be honest they kind of confused me and so I didn’t use them unless I was trying to get back to town.This is a solid game, I basically played this game non-stop from start to finish. I kept coming back for more, and that of course tells you that this is a game that you need to have in your collection. It also doesn’t hurt that the environment looks gorgeous throughout the game, even though you’re only truly side scrolling through the game, the background adds so much more life and depth to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As Metroidvanias go I would say it's slightly above average?  7.5/10?  Most things are decent/good with nothing being overall excellent.The environments?  Good looking enough.  There's a lot of 2.5D effects in the game and they're generally used well.Characters look ok.  They're all some kind of animal and the fur effect looks kind of sketchy on medium settings.  The animations look quite good on the other hand.Music is passable.  Some tracks are catchy, many are forgettable.The combat system is a high point.  You have a few weapons at your disposal, with various special attacks that can easily combo together so the skill ceiling is a lot higher than just button mashing.  Bosses are pretty fun as a result.  Your damage output and damage sustained is rather high so you can end up dead quick, or take out a boss in one extended flurry of combos if you stagger them and don't miss.  The parry once unlocked has a forgiving window and is useful.  Your "MP bar" can be used for healing potions or various attack items, so you can choose a risk vs reward kind of situation.Map traversal feels good.  With your combination of wall jumps air dashes and double jumps you get around very quickly.  The pacing of the map expansion is ok, and secrets are split between "have to find them behind secret walls" and "Need an ability you don't have yet come back later."The story is mediocre.  You won't really care about what is going on.  The voice acting is shockingly decent, but the script translation/localization is quite bad.  The sentence structure is often stilted and you'll note characters suspiciously repeat themselves in slightly different ways a lot, a hallmark of bad localization.Worth playing?  For sure.  Price isn't bad either.

_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended! Personally my GOTY of 2021! The combat mechanics are really varied and fun to implement in actual gameplay. It has everything a good metroidvania should have, such as distinct areas, platforming, puzzles, character growth and so forth. The visuals such as character design, animation asset and environmental design are all beautiful! There's even a JOJO reference!For the life of me, I couldn't figure this out, but the game was almost always chugging or underperforming for me even with specs that should have been good enough to handle it without issue. Having said that, that's a personal issue and I won't let it affect my review.As much as I love the game, it's not perfect. The aforementioned features don't always reach their peak potential as most situations don't particularly lend themselves to using your full repertoire, there aren't a TON of reasons to return to an area after getting everything (or most of everything),  and the English localization is lacking in that it can be confusing at times and downright redundant. These may sound pretty bad, but the cons did not outdo the pros. I love it, but it could be better, like  most games.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: It's... good, yeah! Not great, and I have my gripes, but, I enjoyed it! Beat-em-up style combat, which isn't my forte, but between the three different weapon types and a few subweapons (that I never really used much) you have a lot of options, the platforming feels pretty tight, the map is large but not overwhelming and most areas feel unique, the graphics are pretty well polished (though I had to turn some settings down to get this to run on my machine but whateverrrr)And I don't have any big nitpicks or issues, just... a lot of smaller ones. The game does look beautiful but it's kind of... samey, in its drab color palettes and mechanical fortresses, only a few areas stand apart and none of them are that striking. The weapons are all pretty good but it feels like each new one handily outclasses the previous one... and you get the drill like an hour and half into the game... and then don't get the whip until over halfway through, right before the end of act 2, so it doesn't feel like you get enough time to use it? There's also some pacing issues, namely a LOT of slow-moving elevators, platforms, unskippable cutscenes on boss retries, kind of sparse fast-travel points meaning backtracking can get annoying, in a lot of ways it just feels slow. Tack on a -ton- of reused enemies and bosses - the first "boss" you fight, uhh, prepare to see him a dozen more times, same with the ninja frogs - and  it did get a little exhausting by the end. Also, way too many water areas - one may have been fine but there's like, three or four water-heavy zones and a lot of them happen pretty close together too so it again gets, exhausting. The plot is a footnote but it feels... awkward, maybe as a result of the translation, but even then... sometimes stuff just -happens- and doesn't land with emotional impact, and the game kind of ends in a weirdly inconclusive location and eehhh I just wasn't that invested. Also, as a furry, the word "furtizen" hurts my soul.It's not that I have more problems than praises, just that what the game does right is... pretty standard and not particularly worth praising, it's all-around a good time, a strong 7/10, y'know, just, could be better too!
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic metroidvania. Great weapons and combo style fighting with a decent story. This is a definite must play for any metroidvania fan. Pulling off some really cool combos can be challenging but well worth the effort. I still need to go back and find the rest of the collectibles. I feel it's worth the full asking price so if you get it on sale you are getting a great deal.For Deck owners:It plays pretty good on the deck. It does have a few graphical glitches once and a while but nothing game breaking and sometimes when I would put the Deck to sleep and then pick it up later the audio would get a little static sound to it. Restarting the game would fix it so I do recommend closing the game out when taking a break.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Decent Metroidvania very pretty. Combat could use damage numbers but its lite on rpg elements so I understand why it doesn't have them. Enemy variety is starting to were thin lot of "recolors". Story isn't bad and the world is genuinely interesting. 4/5 decent game pick up on sale if you like Metroidvanias
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Beaten it and it's genuinely one of the best metroidvanias I've ever played. Absolutely worth it. Excellent really challenging boss fights and tough platforming sections. There's even a hidden fighting game mode if you want more combat scenarios. I wish there was an unlockable hard mode. There's only Easy and Normal. Beat it on normal and found it to be a fair challenge. Some tedious puzzles in the ancient ruins level and a little too much swimming, but a strong final boss fight. 8/10Haven't beaten it yet. This is more or less a first impressions. This game rules. Easily the best combat system I've experienced in a Metroidvania yet. Think Devil May Cry if it was a Metroidvania. There are a plethora of unlockable moves across all three equipable weapons that allow you to string together insane extended combos using classic techniques like juggling and weapon swaps mid-combo. It's extremely satisfying and fairly challenging. You gotta time your attacks and dodges just right. I would've really appreciated a style meter or combo meter to encourage more aggressive play, but that's just me. The game is gorgeous and runs smooth even at 4K with ray-tracing enabled. There is some stutter when loading into new areas unfortunately, but once you're in, there's no slowdown thankfully. Environments are highly detailed, atmospheric, and full of depth. The game isn't exactly linear, but you always know where you need to go and are rarely lost. You're encouraged to revisit areas and branch off the beaten path to unlock additional upgrades, items, and money. I prefer this approach, as I hate getting lost and having to backtrack constantly. Thankfully, backtracking isn't a chore thanks to the game's excellent movement controls and abilities. It's not quite as fluid or as fast as Metroid Dread, but you'll have no issue rapidly navigating through levels and possibly even sequence break the game unintentionally. If you're looking for a complex story with cryptic Soulslike storytelling, this is not that kind of game. The story is corny in its serious tone and it doesn't bother me. I found it amusing and enjoyed the voice acting featured here. I'm really enjoying this game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a competent metroidvania, but there are far better ones out there. Get this for 10 dollars or less, I honestly think Dust, An Elysian Tail is a better anthropomorphic style game/ metroidvania.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid metroidvainia, it has some kinks, but what is there is enjoyable combat and great platforming that for the most part feel very fair.It does get a bit overboard toward the end. Combat gets a bit too spamy and some of the platforming loses what earlier sections did much better.A 80+ % run will take you about 16 hours to complete. Just enough.Special mention has to be given to the environments and how the world connects. This is often an issue in metroidvania games, but in FIST this is highest class. Might be the best I’ve ever seen. It really doesn’t feel like you’re playing a metroidvania game in the sense that the environments all make a logical world-building sense.For example, in a game like Indivisible (which is a game I really like) there will be so many parts, platforms and such that make gameplay sense, but no sense whatsoever in terms of the space and environment you are in. FIST does this extremely well, the environments are truly a treat to unfold.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game recently, here are my thoughts on it.- Gameplay 8/10Pretty original metroidvania in that aspect. It focuses heavily on melee combat, and the 3 weapons are really inventive and have a pretty good sense of weight / power. The platforming is solid and the fighting is pretty challenging in a good way. The combo system takes a little while to get used to ; commands are queued so it punishes mashing.- Art style 9/10The backgrounds are *gorgeous* and the machines' dieselpunk aesthetic works great as well. The Iron Legion design is really good, and while I wouldn't have chosen such a realistic style for the furry characters, it works. Well except for Lady Q, whose whole design is "I'M A GURL" with exaggerated curves and big anime eyes that look out of place. Also not sure why half the furry characters have a tail and the other half doesn't.- Sound design 6/10The soundtrack does the job. The voice lines get a bit repetitive after a while, and can someone get this poor rabbit some coffee please, he sounds like he's reading his grocery list.- Writing 3/10The big weak point of the game, it feels like they focused exclusively on gameplay and the story was added as an afterthought. Which is a shame, because the lore would have been so fun to explore.The characters and story are, unfortunately, pretty flat and cliché. You have the old disgruntled war hero, the fat comic relief bear, the old martial art sensei, the best friend turned traitor, literally Catwoman, and yes they're written exactly like you'd expect. Funnily enough, the most fleshed out and attaching character is an enemy NPC, the Legion's Head of Personnel.- Overall 7/10If you ignore the story, FIST is a great dieselpunk metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Definately one of the best platformer games I have ever played. Good story, graphics, mechanics, physics, and runs smooth. _childDocuments_.review: A good metroidvania. _childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game design is backed up with solid combat and tight controls (and a pretty impressive sound track in my opinion) all help make this game stand among the top metroidvanias of all time. Upgrades are dolled out at a very sparing, even pace and feel well-earned. Secrets are slightly concealed (although the map can give you good hints) and often blocked by a satisfying and difficult challenge. The characters and worldbuilding are a little sparse, but there is plenty of game to enjoy to keep you craving the next area until the very end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in ~16 hours and got 100% completion.The game is a lot of fun from start to finish, the combos that you can pull off are so satisfying - or you can just power punch everything and still have lots of fun. I wouldn't say it was an easy game, but it wasn't that hard either. I think it could be kind of difficult at the start, while you're learning enemy moves and hit-box sizes, after that the game is smooth and rewarding. Boss fights are specially fun.Amazing graphics and scenery, really knowing how to create the atmosphere they wanted.The only weak point of this title is the story. Character motivations aren't solid nor interesting, the development of the story feels more like an excuse for making a playable universe rather than actually tell a story. I don't see this as a big problem, though. The mechanics and visuals compensate for the lack of good storytelling.A very satisfying and visually pleasing game. Don't expect a great story and just enjoy the mechanics and looks of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: All around a pretty great game so far. Not the most incredible story but gameplay and graphics are great. Voice acting is good. _childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: System and Setup:Windows 10 64bitIntel Core i9 10900KNVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 SUPERLG 27inch 1440p 144hz monitor 27GN850-BThe game launches without trouble, although there were some unfortunate technical issues that brought down the experience. I can run the game maxxed at 120fps. Beyond that, the game starts to struggle to maintain its framerate.Notes:- The largest map I've ever seen in an Metroidvania. My first run took me around 20 hours, which feels absurd for a genre I usually associate with 10 hour playtimes. - A combat system based upon three main weapons that can be switched mid-combo. Fans of Guacamelee, or Character Action games will know what they're in for.- The game graphically looks nice, when it's behaving properly.- The English translation is often awkward to listen to. A native English speaker should've been hired to proofread and edit the script.- Poor optimization for PC. The loading stutter is a constant annoyance, and textures in the environment and Rayton himself will constantly flicker black seemingly at random.- The game doesn't have a mini map, which means that the player will have to constantly pull up the map screen to avoid becoming lost.- The game is nice enough to highlight locked chests and plant collectibles when you get near them, taking the frustration out of relocating them when you have the abilities and/or keys to get them. The game's map also tracks the percentage of an area of the game you've been to. However the game only tracks how much of an area you've seen and not if you've gotten all of the collectibles or upgrades from that part of the map. Posters are also not marked. This adds some annoyance to the game for completionists who don't want to have to use a guide or a video for help.- The ending was a little bit abrupt and I would've liked if there were at least one or two other scenes in the epilogue.Despite the game's flaws, FIST is a great Metroidvania game and fans of the genre shouldn't overlook it.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: As a die hard fan of the metroidvania genre, I absolutely loved this game. Its fresh game play and inventive environmental elements reminds me a lot of how it felt to play Shadow Complex for the first time, more than a decade ago. Same engine from Unreal with many feature improvements applied over time. Highly recommend you try it if you're a lover of this games!!! The only minor complaint I have is that the  combo training challenges at high levels of difficulty can be insanely frustrating to pull off. I'd prefer if TiGames would remove the beginner, intermediate and master training challenges and give you the mystery shard after beating the three individual weapon challenges.While TiGames indicates the game is still being optimized on PC, it runs very well and only has a few minor hiccups from time to time with assets failing to load quickly enough. The hardware I used to run the game was the following at 1080p and max settings with motion blur set to the lowest option.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good! It takes a lot to stand out from all the Metroidvanias everywhere all the time, but this one manages to do it in style.  Combat, music, worldbuilding were all excellent.Seriously, I've had more fun beating people up in this game than in the last NetherRealm Studios game I bought.  Can't wait for a sequel/DLC.The game is also pretty light on backtracking, so you only need to backtrack a lot if you want 100% completion or if you need to find combat upgrades.  But if you reeeeeeeally want a challenge, you could just try powering through the game without upgrading combat.  It's all up to you.Chinese voice actors really hit it out of the park too.  Though I'm kind of disappointed that the final boss wasn't Winnie the Poo.

_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvanias typically attempt to specialize in either movement or combat, and let the other be a secondary mechanic. FIST is the rare one that excels at both, and it's equally fluid whether you're juggling enemies in melee or dashing around between jumps. The map design is expansive and the game is beautiful though unfortunately even on a 2070 it chugs at times with crippling lag that requires a restart to fix. This primarily affects the hub area but there were times during underwater sections where I'd have to downgrade my graphics to minimum settings to get the game to run. The translation also isn't flawless, with odd disconnects between subtitles and spoken dialogue, to say nothing of the jarringly inconsistent quality of the voice acting. These are relatively minor quibbles though, and FIST is an incredibly solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: An all around decent metroidvania with fun game play, good graphics and nice atmosphere. The upgrades are meaningful and enjoyable and the exploration is quite fun. My biggest criticisms of the game are that the story is generic and forgettable, and that the difficulty is very imbalanced. I played through 80% of the game on normal and had a good time, but the last part of the game goes berserk and I actually had to turn it to easy to finish. The final 2-3 boss fights are orders of magnitude harder than anything else in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: the game is very nice look and has alot to do and can keep u busy for hours and been really enjoying it so far and highly recomend this game at first i didnt think i would like it but i had a blast learning all the areas and collecting stuff in game  i wanted to thank the team who made this game its amazing
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me start by saying this is 100% worth it. Metroidvanias are my favorite genre of video games because their sense of progression is sooooo satisfying and F.I.S.T. nails it on the head. If you like Hollow Knight, you'll like this game.Combat is tight and challenging, music is on point, graphics and atmosphere are great and the story is....meh.The collectibles are always worth it making exploration very nice and the map is clear and concise.I do have 3 major complaints that I will list below if the person reading this cares.1: The fast travel systemHoly sh!t there needs to be like 2x more fast travel points. Like most metroidvanias, there is a ton of backtracking and this game does not make it easy to 100% most areas endgame when you have the proper abilities to go back and get everything. Most of the time, the only fast travel station is on the opposite side of the map as opposed to that tiny thing you missed earlier in game. 2: Huge expansions of underwater Need I say more? Underwater sections in video games are usually bad and this game is no exception. 3: The last ability you get *spoilers ahead*I hate writing spoilers in reviews but this boiled my blood and must be said. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: This is a splendid game and I highly recommend it if you enjoyed playing the Ori games.What I liked:- Beautiful graphic and art, even if it's a 2D game, don't underestimate it ;) - A story, yes. I'm tired of games without a story or putting just one enigmatic scene and rolling it out. - The abilities and varieties. Some games have nearly the same abilities but this one has some cool ones.- Map design and connections, it's a blast to travel through and discover secrets, most of them are accessible through unlocking abilities or some platforming. You don't need to go and hit every wall ;) What should be better:- Nothing really stood out or was annoying, I'm looking forward to the next game from this studio <3

_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've seen so far, F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is a textbook metroidvania game with a very atmospheric steampunk/dieselpunk aesthetic. I have to say I was initially skeptical about the anthropomorphic characters (I mean, they are even called "furtizens"), but the story and dialogue are actually quite intriguing and have kept me playing this game for days, with no signs of me getting bored of it. As for the gameplay, the combat is smooth and responsive and there is plenty of exploration to be done and hidden areas to be found, just like I would expect from a good metroidvania. I have seen some criticisms towards the combo system in the game and in all honesty, I am beginning to see how all the combinations for the different weapons can become overwhelming and difficult to remember. I have mostly stuck with a couple of skills/combos so far and it has worked out OK though, so it doesn't seem like the game NEEDS you to remember all of these combo combinations.All in all, if you are a metroidvania or a steampunk enjoyer, F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is a must-buy in my opinion. And again, don't let the furry characters dissuade you from the game! You'll get used to them pretty quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to prefer exploration focused action adventure platformers, aka metroidvanias, to be about the exploration. By now we’ve seen so many games of this type emphasizing one or several building blocks of the genre that there’s plenty of choice for everyone. F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch, the first major release by the Chinese-based TiGames, is a metroidvania focusing on action, story and somewhat realistic architecture. So in a way it works like a mix of Shadow Complex and Guacamelee! and does a good job at it.At its core, F.I.S.T. has everything you’d expect from a brawler metroidvania. It has incredibly fun movement mechanics so the world exploration is fun, with infinite wall jumping, dashing, double jumps and other unlockable skills, with most of the fun basics becoming available almost from the very beginning. It has a fun arsenal of melee moves and skills that gets expanded with new weapon types and more combo possibilities. You can also switch weapons on the fly, juggle enemies in the air and later even unlock a parry skill. There are also skills and upgrades that you can improve or buy as all defeated enemies drop money, which can also be found in containers all around the map. Which you, as always for the genre, will not always be able to explore in full on the first go, as you will be lacking skills. However, if you’re really good with the skills you already have, you can get some unlocks early and avoid the later backtracking. The only thing, somewhat common for modern metroidvanias, that is missing here is a new game plus mode, which is a bit of a shame.All that said, while the game certainly has all that, and also looks pretty good, it doesn’t always know how to use its resources right. Combat, for all of its moves and skills, often feels sluggish and either tedious, when fighting normal enemies, or way too chaotic when fighting some bosses. There’s a noticeable inconsistency in input latency, probably also tied to the general performance issues this game has. Though, even with that, the “training” that you can go through to unlock more moves and collectibles, feels completely pointless, as you won’t be pulling those cool combos in the actual gameplay – simpler enemies either die fast or are easier to deal with more consistent simpler combos, while bosses cannot be juggled at all. And some can block or even parry your attacks, with no clear tell or pattern, which throws your combo off and can nullify your special attacks, that have a cost to them to pull off.The story and the world also feel inconsistent and at times rather poor. Maybe some of the story issues can be written off as awkward translation (and it does sound literal and weird more often than not), but even without that, I can’t see it being interesting either way. It’s a pretty simple tale with stock characters either way, it’s just that the characters are all anthropomorphic animals. Not all of whom even look right, which is also a thing – visually the game can be stunning, but at times it’s a poor clash of styles. Not helped by the usual Unreal Engine 4 issues with sprawling interconnected worlds, like stutters (especially with Ray Tracing), texture pop-in and bland late 2000s look of more metallic areas. The music is often a miss too, with the very first location track being the worst offender and the best example of the issue – it’s not a bad track, but it’s short, repetitive and it soon becomes annoying.Even the exploration and platforming are uneven. For story reasons, for example, the game can suddenly teleport you away from the area a few percent before you fully cover it, so you’d have to specifically backtrack to it to get those last parts of the map. And this happens a few times. Some of the platforming challenges are a bit obnoxious and the difficulty of platforming in general is rather uneven. There are a couple of more puzzle-centric areas and those are almost never good, as the puzzle itself isn’t difficult, but the execution can sometimes be annoying to do. Luckily, there’s genuine variety in mechanical focus from location to location, so it’s rare that you’d get annoyed for too long.I enjoyed a lot of my time with F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch but most definitely not all of it. It’s also worth noting that at the moment of my playthrough I had to occasionally go to the main menu and reloading the save to stop the game from horribly lagging, which might be an issue with ray tracing in one of the areas. But this wasn’t the reason for plenty of the annoyances I had with the game. If you’re in a mood for a metroidvania with a melee action focus, but also really fun movement and you don’t mind a rather poor story that’s mostly unskippable getting in the way from time to time F.I.S.T. is a cool game to check. It’s not great, but there’s enjoyment to be had out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap what a breath of fresh air! I loved FIST. I used to be a huge fan of beat em ups when I was younger, like those old crash bandicoot wii games were my favorite. FIST felt like a huge trip down memory lane for a game ive never even played. I was a huge fan of the combat system, and the parkour sections of each area. If you want that upgrade, you have to work a bit for it. I love that. I really hope FIST gets DLC or even a sequel soon.

Platforming can be challenging but not all that hard. Huge map, lots of exploration and secrets. Biggest gripe is the fast travel system is dumb, there was absolutely no need to include the subway, and being forced to fast travel 3 times to get somewhere just because you have to take the subway is needlessly tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts with a great story and immediately you start your first mission.  Every mission is unique and challenging as each boss fight is too.  The map is diverse and BEAUTIFUL.  Each area has a unique vibe and great music.   Once I start playing, its hard to stop!  SO GOOD. _childDocuments_.review: What I like:Very classic Metroidvania. It implemented all the key concepts of metroidvania well: weapons, abilities, upgradables, collectibles, story etc. Oh, did I mention fluffy characters? The control is quite smooth and fluid.What I don’t like:Lack of content. ~25 hrs and I'm 100% complete, collectibles, achievements, all of them. So in terms of play time, it is more like an Ori game, and much less than Hollow Knight.Lastly I believe some negative reviews around the combat system are unjustified. One review claims two of the weapons are useless. That’s because he hasn't learnt to use parries.The combat system is very advanced and similar to DMC, in the sense that it has jump cancel, aerial combos, weapon switch, special moves etc. I can already imagine hard core players doing crazy combos and shredding the bosses. If anything, the current “normal” difficulty is too easy that players do not need to learn any hard combos to complete the game.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Very reminiscent of Shadow Complex but instead of guns its built around more of a combo driven melee system that is really fun. There is a lot of variety of combat styles, tons of secrets, story is actually good. It feels like a AAA production game. Music is great. Puzzles are fairly straight forward but plenty of incentive to run around and find all the secrets like any good metroidvania should have.There upgrades aplenty. You have secondary weapons and tools. You can customize the look of your armor by finding old movie posters that can be painting on your armor. Combat isnt a simple spam attack. It is timing and combinations of different attacks. You can chain different weapons together for bigger combos. You can also parry and counter attack enemiesThis game as far as metroidvanias go is a 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: 5 hr in, a decent metroid game i guess (the only metroidvania game i've played extensively was hollow knight). Character development felt a bit slow to me as I've only unlocked a few abilities so far. The checkpoints in the game are placed a little too scarce for my taste and there is a lot of backtracking if you want to 100% each area which can be a little tedious. _childDocuments_.review: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is probably the worst title a game could ever get.  It's as if the developers sat around trying to brainstorm the worst name for their game possible.  Aside from the title, the game is great.  I really enjoyed it.Th game plays a lot like the Ori series of games and mechanically it is smooth and satisfying.  This is a metroidvania set in a steampunk setting.  The art direction is wonderful and it performed relatively well with a few occasional hiccups in FPS.  All I did was turn off Ray Tracing (didn't see much of a difference, anyway) and it then ran smooth with no issues.  The only slight annoyance I experienced with the game is its fast travel system.  A metroidvania is the type of game where you will want to backtrack to previous areas to locate power up's, collectibles etc... so you would think they would implement a fast travel system that will allow you to do so with ease.  but no.  You have to plan how to get from one area to another... taking multiple fast travel options to get to your destination as there is a portal system and a subway system that take you to different parts of the map.That being said, it feels like taking the subway to a destination and then getting on a bus to get to where you want to go.  It's realistic, I'll give it that.Mechanically the gameplay, platforming and battle system are satisfying and well designed.  The battles are relatively challenging and encourage you to stay on your toes, read the enemies moves signs and perform actions accordingly.  Button mashing wont, for the most part, work much in this area.  I finished this game with about 15 hours of game time.  It's not the longest title nor is it short.  I would say it doesn't outstay its welcome and leaves you wanting more... which is what a good title should leave you with.  I would say its worth 20 bucks.If you enjoy metroidvania's, beautiful graphics and tight, challenging gameplay, you'll love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I been playing metroidvania games for some time now and most of them end up as decent games that are fun to play through.  is one of those types, it doesnt have some inovations but it still enjoyable expirience. The strongest parts might be  which allows a lot of enemy juggling and weapon swapping mid combo (similar to Devil May Cry series) and . City presents before you in face of dark streets and underground labs created in dieselpunk style. Music contains multiple genres that covers mood pretty well, be it jazz, electro or orchestra. Cutscenes looks nice, but you may notice lack of polish here and there, such as twitching or missing smoothness in some animations.  - being average at best. (there is lack of memorable characters) - game starts with a single weapon and allows you to upgrade it to unlock new moves which you can combine in long and fun combos which only becomes deeper and more complex with new weapons and gadgets. Learn to parry and switch arms mid combo and you will be untouchable. I see lots of potential for speed running this game.I hate underwater levels and this games under water level is no different, I died the most in this area.I really hope F.I,S,T. does well enough to warrant some DLC I want more.The name gets some questions when discord displays it. _childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: If you like metroidvanias then this is a game for you. Literally everything you could want out of the genre plus more. Has your typical explore new areas until you have to come back later with more tools to explore every inch of it. A good amount of upgrades, collectibles, and customization. The best part though has to be the combat in this game. Reminds me a lot of DMC or Darksiders. You have a lot of freedom to make your own combos and extend them as you want. Dash and abilities that use "mana" can cancel any move on the spot making for some really fun and difficult to pull off combos. Also the story is pretty good. A story you've heard before but with the atmosphere and setting in FIST you can really get immersed into.  After the ~18 hours i played (no afk) i feel content putting it down for now. Completed the map 100%, did the fun side challenges, but there is still more i plan on coming back and doing! I would easily recommend any fan of the genre to buy this at an price because im certain you will enjoy FIST.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Good story, but on the shorter side unless you choose to spend time searching for all the stuff.Replayability seems good, because it can be on the shorter side, but not great because of a very linear story.The combat is good and responsive, but not too hard (playing on the NORMAL setting) and the exploration is fun and satisfying!The abilities are also fairly original and very fun to play with! Also combos are a real thing in this game.I give this game a  7/10 because it is a bit unpolished in certain areas, such as some of the dialog and some animations during cutscenes and such. Also a few minor bugs in the time of writing.Absolutely  music! 9.5/10 (wish for more tracks).The ambiance is just right for this type of setting, and it really feels dire and empty where this is appropriate and relaxed with smooth jazz where the dangers of the world are none.This has huge potential to become a classic tbh. Great fun to just mess around, but also good speedrunning potential I think.All this with great graphics too!All in all, I recommend this game for those who really want to play a metroidvania, but are a bit scared or confused of the concept. It's hard to get lost and the important bits are handed to you. I haven't really tried the easy setting, but I imagine this opens the game to those not interested in hard combat as well.This game really ticks off a lot of boxes

_childDocuments_.review:
Six years ago, the Machine Legion invaded and colonized the Torch City, which was originally inhabited by animals. Rayton, the former soldier in the resistance war, has been living in seclusion since then. After his friend is forcibly arrested, Rayton reclaims his mechanical fist and steps to his journey fighting back. And he never expects that he has been involved in a bigger scheme between the mafia, the rebellion, and the legion.

Exploring the Metroidvania game world with a dozen of areas with distinguishing vision themes and level designs. Earning the rewards by conquering the challenges of combats, puzzles and platformers in countless chambers, tunnels and shortcuts.

Interconnected and automatically loading game map makes the detailed Torch City more convincing and beautiful.

name: Wolfstride
detailed_description: Wolfstride is a role-playing game about three former partners-in-crime coming to a turning point in their lives. When they inherit a junkyard mecha called Cowboy, they reunite to enter the planet’s most elite mecha competition: the Ultimate Golden God Tournament. Each member of the team lends their unique experience as they prepare to outwit the best mecha opponents from around the world. Between dog-mechanic Duque, mecha pilot Knife Leopard, and jack-of-all-trades Dominic Shade, the core crew’s got just about everything covered. That is… until their simple mission to make money unfolds into a deep, slow-burning exploration of their complex lives, the dark choices of their past, and their inevitable fate. The hangar is Duque's domain. Repairing damage between battles is just the beginning. Swap out parts, install upgrades, and add new weapons to improve Cowboy and perfect the custom loadout designed to beat your next opponent. Take the role of exiled former Yakuza, Dominic Shade, to explore every quirky corner of Rain City. A half dozen establishments introduce a kaleidoscope of characters, each offering support, a job, or a biting insult to your journey. Enter the arena to fight it out in giant robots one on one. The turn-based battle system rewards preparation and strategy. Move carefully to get in the best position to attack and keep the enemy off-balance. Target attacks to wear down your opponent or go on the defensive when the fighting gets too hot.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride is a story-rich turn-based strategy game. The store page already tells enough of what the game is about story-wise. In short: You're a team of three who wants to win the Mecha world championships. On your journey, you will experience a lot more. There is actually a lot of story outside of the tournament, subplots, and whatnot. It feels like a visual novel to some extend. Almost everything is voiced in the game and the voice-acting is great. The story is interesting and through it resembles animes/mangas it doesn't feel as "over the top". This is the other big thing, next to the story. Battles are turn-based. Your Mech has five different HP bars. Two for your arms, one for your head, and one for your body. If your body's HP reaches 0, you lose. The same goes for enemies.Your attacks and defenses vary based on what you've unlocked and selected.There are different attacks from throwing a car, to shooting guns, to hitting your enemy with your fist.Also very important is your movement. There are seven tiles in total. Some will give you or the enemy +5 on attacks if you're standing on it. You have to move up to 2 tiles each turn and push the enemy away.Then there is a bar next to your mech. It fills up over time. Fully loaded, you can use it to heal yourself, strengthen your attacks or restore your arm/head. The story progresses. You're (almost) free to go wherever you want. There are many different places to visit, jobs to take and people to talk to. Most of it is story-based but you can also do jobs to earn extra money. Jobs are like mini-games.  Anyways, you will have to do missions each day in order to progress to the next day like getting X, talking to Y, buying Z, or battling in the arena. You will unlock new abilities and parts for your mech and fighter like new ways to attack, defend, new special abilities, and better parts to make your mech better overall.For many things, you will need money. Like, after every battle, your mech will be destroyed (to some extend of course) and you need to repair it. For that, you need money. You get money after battles AND by doing jobs.   Wolfstride is a unique story-rich turn-based strategy game. It takes some time to get into it and it's not mainly a TBS game but when it comes to the battles, it gets quite tactical and interesting. The story is well-made, the voice acting is very good and the overall atmosphere thanks to the wonderful art style is great. Moving around the world is quite annoying and feels unnecessary but doing mini-games can spice things up if it gets too monotonous. Overall, Wolfstride is a great game. It hasn't the addictive gameplay-loop as other strategy games have but it's a very interesting game. It's also VERY cheap considering the asking price so I definitely recommend it to fans of story-rich, anime-like strategy games!
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: This game... is unpolished in some aspects. Typos, bugs and visual oversights mostly, but the long pondering dialogue does also tire me out after a while.But I will still recommend this game. I've beaten it, gotten all of those stupid fricking collectables and sat through every bloody cutscene. Worth it.This game has a place in my heart. An underdog action story, it is painfully honest yet whispering pieces of lore in my ear and leading me to search every corner and nook and cranny (even though most of it is empty). _childDocuments_.review: This game wants to be good so, so badly. I wanted to love it, and I really tried. It would have been leagues better as a straight-up visual novel -- the mecha combat actually kind of rocks, but the endless walking, the back-and-forth busywork, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you have to put up with really starts to grate on you. It's also a perfectly fine and cool little story, but just like the gameplay there's simply too much nothing. It smacks of student art, someone's darling, and there are plenty of aspects here that should have been reined in or straight-up killed. By the end credits I actively didn't like this game, and that doesn't feel fair given how much I enjoyed it in fits and starts. All that said, I'm glad I purchased it -- this game is exactly the kind of art I want to support.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really sorry but: no.The idea behind this game is awesome, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome: There is this cool black and white "manga artstyle" in a world somewhat inspired by Cowboy Bebop, Gurren Lagann and others where you get into Mech battles.I do enjoy games that are more like a novel than a "traditional game" (like the Persona series, Phoenix Wright, 999 or Aegis Rim) so I don't have a problem with this genre.When you start Wolfstride/Corona Black it really delivers what was expected from the trailers and screenshots here on the Steam Store, but after 2 or 3 hours it goes downhill really fast. Soon everything that was interesting disapears and you get throw into 15+ hours (I'm not even joking look my total gametime here) of:- Bad filler content with tons of endless dialogue where the voice acting doesn't even fit the reaction in the character portrait.- Grinding for hours and hours some very bad minigames that don't even reach the minimum standards from an average free mobile game at the Playstore. To add insult to injury: these minigames always have some weird bug going on to take away any good impressions you had about this game previously.- Slow and unorganized amateurish menus were you can't sort it or use a shortcut to quickly jump to the end of a list.- The "virtual combat" is just another empty grind (because you need the damn pineapples) that makes you bored and tired to the point you don't want to see any other fight again... which is a problem because that's the main feature of the game.- You just can't fast travel to places of interest, instead you have to spend a lot of time walking aimlessly through an uninteresting dead world just to check if there are some new events going on in the bar or elsewhere.- When you want to skip the annoying animations (when you press start button) the game instead display a prompt about "people who skip animations don't value artists!!" as if an ugly piano animation at the bar (which never changes throughout the entire game) is something to be proud of. Maybe I got so annoyed by the things I said earlier that even the little things started to add some weight about what I don't like so I'll stop here.In the state it is now (Feb 2023) I would never want someone I care for to go through what I went here when I decided to play this game from start to finish, so I'm not going to give it a positive review.In the future if they do a revised version where they remove a lot of the useless content/filler (making it a shorter but better game), with minigames worth playing and A LOT of quality of life updates for everything... I'm sure there is a great game under all this rubble.

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings on this game are... strange. I'm - at least in theory - its target audience. I grew up watching anime, so I should be eating up all the references this title is packed with. And I genuinely love the concept! However, it's a very, VERY flawed game.For starters: playing through this game's story felt very much like reading a first draft of a novel. There are so many plotholes and story elements that either come out of left field or get introduced only to disappear for the rest of the game. The game's economy is a mess as well. Money is basically useless, especially during the late-game. And don't even get me started on the whole pineapple system. It's good in theory, but the amount of grind required to max it out is insane. All this could be fixed by simply making pineapples buyable in the game's store.Speaking of the store - it's basically useless as well. It only updates during specific moments of the story. And out of all the items that become available only 1-2 are actually useful. The rest is fluff.I think this game's biggest issue is the fluff. There's a whole lot of walking the same paths to the same places in a (pretty dead) world. There are days where there's literally NOTHING to do, except grind. No story progression, no interesting events, nothing. Which is especially annoying given how much of this game's story remains unfinished/unpolished. All that empty space could've been filled with story beats and development. Instead, it remained empty.The fighting system is interesting enough, I suppose. The game is VERY easy though. The only actual challenges are some of the basement bosses and virtual battles bosses. The actual story-related fights are painfully easy at times. The only fight that I actually lost once was the final boss of the game; and I wouldn't exactly call myself an expert in turn-based combat.Overall, this game has a really interesting concept that ended up falling flat. Some aspects of it are enjoyable (like some of the characters and the combat) but most of it felt relatively unimpressive.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Good idea, mixed execution, needlessly grindy and needesly long in terms of going from a to b. If it were by me I would give them a second chance to make a sequel and improve on many of the points below, it was made with love and care so I guess it deserves to be considered at least, but its not perfect (And I would struggle to call it totally good) or for everyone.The GOOD:ART: Stylized and well done, monochromatic works, would have liked some splash of colorsMusic: Good overall, underused songs, overused overworlds and main themes, good vibesStory: Original, mostly voiced and very proffesionally, it tries to do things with the gameplay and be coherent in the world it presents maybe to its detriment on some aspects, the characters are if not good at least they are done sincerely.Gameplay: Fun when it is balanced, flexible and feels like a mecha fight, the world has its charm, you control the pacing somewhat wich can make the game go slow or fast depending on how much you try to interact with everything everyday and how fast unlock things by grinding.The badArt: Underutilized assets, no gallery, no personalization.Music: the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mangoose drums are annoying as ♥♥♥♥Story: Sometimes it feels juvenile, it treats themes that need more developing, drops stories with no consequences many times, its a mish mash, if you overlook the amateurish there´s heart on it.Gameplay: Not enough, not focused, it should have way more mecha fights integrated and as a part of the game, and you seem to play minigames in order to be rewarded with one meager decent fight, prone to be either overprepared or underprepared. Needlessly grindy with the friends system and the minigames being locked behind upgrades that you get from friends.Conclusion: I wrote like a lot and i couldnt post that so have this, it is a game made with heart that i wish made a sequel with an overhaul, it is A game, the story wanted to be everything and barely got somewhere by the end, the gameplay is good if you play on a balanced curve of difficulty, wich i dont know what it is because everyday i played with FOMO trying to upgrade as much as I could as soon as i could, you have roughly 40 days to slowly get there, play a little bit everyday and it will be more enjoyable than trying to complete it in one go.I would recommend this if you like anything resembling gurren lagann or if you can mix the ingredients of what this offers in your head and derive pleasure from it.The bad its not because there was negligence, I feel it needed more time than what it had avaiable and it was a passion project to either do it now or never, I hope a sequel comes someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler-free review:One of most underrated gems I have found on Steam!Wolfstride is a unique game that's not what someone would exactly expect.Let's talk about design first. This is considered a turn based strategy game, however that's actually only a tip of the iceberg.The graphics are what is considered a mix of colorless pixel (16 bit?) and 2D animation using so called "motion tweens" and some special effects, all of them being very well made. There are not many if any games out there using such combined art style.Now for the gameplay core - the turn based part happens during mecha battles, however most of the time you are spent running around doing errands. There is cash that's mostly grindable in the form of minigames where you can purchase things, mainly upgrades for your mecha. One could say that's about it and that it becomes repetitive and boring, but there are details here worth mentioning.Plotwise the game is very story rich. It gives lots of attention not only to the main character but others as well. There will be backstories to unfold while facing the present that's filled with both comedy and drama which will make you want to progress further down campaign. You roam around map for around 63-ish days straight and you can either only focus on essential objectives, or use your time to try and see if there are any new character interactions each day and speaking of, there's a huge amount of dialogue (it's skippable though) within this game and what's really amazing is that almost EVERYTHING is voiced! Each character has its own voice, done in a proffesional matter where you can perfectly tell their expressions.Another great plus would be the soundtrack as it provides perfect atmosphere that often shifts from chilling into thrilling.There are some small flaws (like no sign of the controls list as I've discovered you can walk instead of run with the shift key) and some minor bugs here and there but overall this is one of those games where developers put their hearts and souls into making this one of a kind masterpiece, regardless of how little popularity it has.

_childDocuments_.review: I had my eye on this game for a while, and oh boy what a treat it was.The characters are all awesome and memorable, the story is pretty neat and entertaining and the artstyle is beautiful. It has that old school anime feel that I really dig. Specially loved the character design and the whole monochrome vibe!Soundtrack is pretty cool, and dear lord the voice acting is just superb. Most of the game is voice acted and every character just fits so well, they did an amazing job and I loved every bit of it.Gameplay is pretty simple overall, you run around talking to people and can do some mini games to earn money, which in turn you have to spend into uprading your mech for the next battles. It all revolves around that!The mech battles are turn based and pretty cool, and although they start a bit slow at the beginning of the game they can be figured out pretty quickly and aren't that hard after a while.The game's length isn't too short not too long, but if you want to do everything, such as some side-battles you can squeeze a bit more out of it!I had a great time with Wolfstride and it goes straight to my favorites!
