_childDocuments_.review: As a game, Wolfstride isn't particularly compelling. The gameplay loop is weak and boring, the world isn't particularly interesting and the story is a convoluted mess that tries way, way too hard to find any semblance of sense in it's overly contrived, neverending monologues.However, there are some glimmers of good in this. I struggled a lot on whether to recommend this game or not, but I did settle on the thumbs up. Let me explain a bit on what this game is about and where its strengths and weaknesses lie.Wolfstride is mostly about one thing: mech battles. In a black-and-white world, Shade and his friends are trying to climb the top of the mech leaderboards; in it for money and fame. This could and should have been the story, but sadly, it is very overencumbered by a Yakuza backstory, abandoned plot-threads, happenings that are never explained or elaborated on and a story-telling that tries way too hard to be edgy and meaningful. The game suffers from monologuing (with good voice acting, though), characters that come out of nowhere and disappear just as quickly and a bad habit of never explaining anything until the very end - and even then, I can think of three or four things that happened that I am left with no explanation for, as if I just dreamt them.The explanations and elaborations at the end of the game should have come much sooner as it would have made the entire game more compelling. It would have shed further light on the characters and their motivations and would have given me a reason to care about what is happening. Instead, for most of the game, the characters have almost no background or reason to do whatever they do. which is a shame.The actual gameplay loop is probably the weakest part of the game. It essentially consists of two parts: errands and mech battles. The errands are needed to get money and pineapples (to develop the relationship with characters). Sadly, the errands are getting very repetitive very quickly. The game never actually elaborates on what the pineapple rule is - if there is a limit on how many you can get from the errands, when or how you get them, etc. - so it all seems (and probably is) very random. There is no need to develop the relationship to max with all characters as it doesn't give any additional story or background, but you do get some good items and such, so it's sad that the system is so unclear. The world is very small and you have to pass the same screens dozens of times to walk to your destinations.The mech battles are fun at first but are, aside from one or two optional battles, WAY too easy. The ideal strategy is quickly figured out and so you can spam the same moves over and over on the enemy's chest (the only part that needs to be destroyed to win) and no one will ever stand a chance as long as you buy the best parts for your mech whenever available. The mech battles themselves are not very exciting (though pretty flashy, at least) and you can't skip enemy moves, so sometimes you just gotta sit back and watch the enemy do its thing for up to a minute.So, this all sounds pretty negative - and, frankly, it is. A weak gameplay loop and an extremely backloaded story with many nonsensical happenings would kill almost any game. But here is the thing: you can tell that there is SOMETHING here. The game isn't trying to be edgy or deep for no reason, there is actually a story being told here, with an actual lesson. It's a bit clunky and backloaded, as mentioned, but there is something here and sitting there watching the end credits after all the explanations and goodbyes, I can't help but feel that it wasn't so bad, if only it was told in a more interspersed way THROUGHOUT the game instead of leaving the player in confusion. The characters are cool; the style of the game is undoubtedly amazing, reminiscent of mech anime; the pixel art is simple, but nice; the soundtrack is fitting, if a bit repetitive; the voice acting hits the mark most of the time, especially Shade; and the general idea of the game is unique with some flashy, if mostly easy, battles.This game could have been amazing, and all the ingredients are here, but they are either not fully ripened or are put together in the wrong way. Having finished the game with its emotional ups and downs, I wish it was more than it is, and I am left with a weird mix of wanting more, but also being satisfied by its ending. If nothing else, it is undeniably unique in its execution and setting, and maybe sometimes, that is just enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much going for it, and I could easily see it really connecting with certain audiences.  It just wasn't for me.  I don't mind over the top, generally speaking, I think over the top is great, as long as it's fun.  This game succeeds in being stylishly over the top, but isn't always fun to read or play. The rule of cool has been followed to great effect, but the line between cool and cringe becomes blurrier the more extreme you go.Here the presentation, while clearly an amalgamation of 90s mecha-anime, Cowboy Bebop (and its musical influences), Redline, and film noir, meshes together into something uniquely appealing and fresh.  The cinematics and sprite work are top notch, and I think I get the most out of this story when it's showing, not telling. I genuinely wish that this excellent stylistic blend were in a better game.  The team at work here clearly had vision, and their creation has lots of heart.  I would honestly go so far as to call this game an artistic masterpiece, and I wish I could watch an anime based on its world and characters.It's where the game starts telling, not showing, that I begin to lose interest.  I think the monologues of the main characters are moody and insufferable.  That's a personal preference thing.  It's just, with the game working so hard to tug on my heartstrings via these ham-fisted deliveries, I find that I care less about what happens to the characters overall.  It doesn't have to be shakespeare, it just really feels like it the emotional beats are obligatory pit-stops that are just as trope laden as the games visuals, but unlike the visuals, they don't add anything to the game overall.  The humor is also grating, a lot of it just didn't land with me, but I totally appreciate them trying to add some fun to the story.I think the premise is unique, and there is a lot of potential, but the gameplay is unfortunately not diverse enough to keep me coming back.  It boils down to farming for money to buy parts that let you snag an easy win in a fairly rudimentary combat system.  It all looks and sounds gorgeous, I just wish that the gameplay were anywhere near as dynamic and cool as its presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultra-stylish monochrome  high-tech low-life sweary  mech team RPG extravaganza with a lovable cast of misfits, excellent presentation and a flair for the written word.I really liked the demo, but as one of the devs told me, there's an awful lot more to the game than the demo implies. Sure the simple but highly strategic turn-based mecha-rumbles from the demo are present , but even they have more drama to them than what I played before I bought it. The biggest suprise is that this is a full RPG/adventure with V.N elements and you'll be doing a hell of a lot of other stuff as well as fighting: Quests, conversation, repairs, upgrades and mini-games in a story based mix are all as big a part of the game as the beautifully realised combat. Cool pixel art and very professional anime/manga style illustrations work wonderfully in tandem to conjure up a Cowboy Bebop influenced ambience, not to mention the music, which is insanely catchy in places and some of the best I've heard in a game.The intro is impressive and really sets the scene for this engaging and highly amusing tale.I may add more to this review as play continues, but as of now, first impressions and an hour and a half playthrough have left me suitably chuffed with my purchase., especially at the low price point it's on offer for. It's a quirky game and perhaps not for everyone, but I can see this becoming a cult hit.Edit, I never mentioned the voice acting, which is AAA quality and beyond!

_childDocuments_.review: This game's kind of a mess. An enjoyable mess, but a mess.Things start out very promising with top-notch voice work and art design, and what mech combat the game tantalizes you with is great. However, the story does a little too much tripping over its own feet; while the writing does an amazing job letting you feel like you're experiencing a vignette within a larger world, too much of the central plot is left at loose ends or unresolved. Pacing is also all over the place, with large stretches of time left as "free roam" where you're "free" to experience side activities that are like No More Heroes' repetitive minigames, but worse. Except you're going to have to do them in the early game so you can buy upgrades for your mech. Later combat encounters also won't be even half as difficult- balancing is all over the place.In summary, great audio, great art direction, good combat system, and a story that's all over the place. The team's training robot is also perhaps the most annoying character I've encountered in a video game, to the point where when I streamed some of this on my Twitch, I refused to listen to any of his voice acting unless chat redeemed points to force me to do so. It was that grating.

_childDocuments_.review: Reader, do you remember the 2011 film, "Real Steel?" Wolfstride is like that 2011 film, but less stupid. Your giant robot fights in a syndicated giant robot boxing league to climb the ranks in order to win enough money to rid the main characters of their crimeful regrets and such while you, the player, learn about all those crimeful regrets and how the characters are coping in the thin hope that this is their opportunity to start again.The robot fighting takes the form of a turn based rpg *kind of*. Before and after these robot fights, the player equips abilities and gear to make their robot's numbers bigger than the enemy robots'. That said, there are dimensions to this battle system that are unique to the genre. If you, the reader, takes nothing else away from this review essay, then I think the combat mechanics of Wolfstride are very good and rewarding, if, and maybe not only if, you like turn based role playing games.This game is like potato and kimchi pizza: there shouldn't be any possible way that these ingredients, combined, should be palatable, but this product is shockingly good.The setting of Wolfstride sounds like a 2004 weeaboo's idea of what 2017 could have looked and been like for no better reason than it sounds cool. And, honestly, it is very cool. There is a consistent sense of aesthetic and purpose to the presentation of Wolfstride that knows how to toe the line between cool and obnoxious. This is nowhere more true than in the presentation of characters. They are anime archetypes, yes, but archetypes carefully discerned by a mind that knows where the charm of those archetypes ends. The teenage side-kick character is youthful without being naive, extroverted without screaming in the player's face, and moody without acting bi-polar. There is a surferbrodude, but he's not a doofy, "you're telling me a shrimp fried this rice?" air head for comedic effect. The protagonist is probably the most archetypical; by the end of the narrative, he pushes the self-absorbed brooding attitude too far to make him all that interesting to think about. However, most of the time the characters manage to be wacky, but not too wacky, and just relatable enough to not tip into narcissistic over-sharing.This isn't to say that the narrative is perfect. The pacing of Wolfstrider can be weird. Chapters and sub-plots sometimes feel incomplete. Story beats will be introduced, briefly explored as expositional pieces or conflicts, and then tepidly forgotten or un-dramatically resolved. This happens often and can read like a paper-back with pages missing. There are elements to this story that don't mesh with the overall tale, and it attempts far more than in needs to the detriment of its immersion. Further, I'm not confident there was sufficient time for story editing before release. Characters will allude to activities or events occurring in one time-frame but then, inexplicably, these events happen the day after, which is jarring. In the current build, there are chronic spelling, punctuation, and script errors that happen just often enough that I don't feel I'm being a prick-book-and-word-liking person for noticing and criticizing these errors.Wolfstride is like an rpg of only boss fights and no random encounters, which is pretty great. The collective point being that Wolfstride's combat is very simple to understand if you can read and do 1st grade math. The complexity introduces itself in the tactical aspect of terrain control. Even though there are only 7 spaces, matches are won and lost depending on how well the player can control space to the benefit of their robot's strengths. The mandatory robot fights typically aren't too complicated. You're given a general idea of an opponent's fighting style, and the challenge becomes countering whatever their gimmick happens to be. However, if that sounds too simple, understand that opponents will rarely commit entirely to a single gimmick, and you never know exactly what they can do in combat. You learn opponents' move-sets in the middle of combat, which often prompts the need for predictive problem solving and risk assessment. Sometimes, one opponent's arm part can be more threatening than the other. You may not be able to destroy that part before your robot takes critical damage. It may not be smart to attack the arms at all and, instead, focus on their cockpit which protecting your attack options. The simplicity of Wolfstride's combat opens the door to nuanced match-ups, and these mechanics are mixed-up enough to become rewarding, yet fair, tactical scenarios. I will note that enemy A.I. can be stupid. The A.I cycle through their programming rather simply and often fail to take advantage of obvious tactical advantages. They will ignore terrain bonuses to jump back and forth to no benefit for themselves. They will execute commands in sub-optimal order and lose out on game-changing opportunities when attacking. This isn't egregious enough to ruin the challenge of the combat, but you do get the sense that your opponent might not be able to read or do 1st grade math. There are optional challenge fights you can take any time in between obligatory matches. These challenges feature pilots with better equipment and move-pools who probably can read and do 2nd grade math. This creates a satisfying loop when crafting your giant fighting robot. You may feel that your last obligatory fight felt too easy, and then take on a challenge fight to test how well you've thought about basic addition and subtraction. Maybe, you're uncertain about your preparations before an actual robot battle and want to test your theory crafted kit in a fight without consequences to better understand and identify flaws in your strategies. Wolfstride offers a rewarding challenge that never feels too straight-forward, daunting, or obtuse. There are other game-play elements outside of the combat, and they are easily the weakest part of Wolfstride's design, but not bad enough to quit playing the game. As much as I like looking at Rain City, it doesn't offer enough optional content to make me feel confident that said content is worth leaving the robot HQ, rather than just skipping to the next day if I have nothing robot fighting relevant to buy. The game suggests, at its outset, that there will often be side-quests to pursue, but I'm pretty sure there's only one in the entire game. Shops stock new robot fighting equipment very rarely, and these pieces of equipment are usually inferior to pieces you can get through other means. There's a bar full of guys who are mean to you, and they will say the same mean thing to you every time you talk to them. One dude just says, "..." and I hate that man but kept talking to that most hated man everytime I went into the bar just in case he had something more thought provoking to say than actually nothing. Wolfstride is an anime and video game inspired indie turn based rpg that refreshingly restrains itself, mostly, from making the mistakes of other anime and/or video game inspired indie turn based rpgs on this platform. It mostly shows restraint where others flop, despite occasionally tripping on its own prose. The whole package clicks in a unique way that made me avoid the same comparisons to Cowboy Bebop, Ashita no Joe, or TTGL that I'm pretty sure every games journalist has made in their reviews. Because like yeah I've watched anime and I get it but Wolfstride really isn't similar to any of those things aside from how a football is similar to a bird because they're both round-ish, brown sometimes and people will look at you weird for throwing them as hard as you can into a wall for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: A heavily stylised game about a bunch of misfits slowly but surely crawling their way from the bottom to the top. The battle sections of the game let you experience feeling almost completely powerless, totally dominant and everything in between.98% of the game is voice acted and is done very well. The dialogue does have a few typos that are a bit distracting considering how accurate they normally are, but it's not enough to detract from the effort that's gone into it.The story is overall done well, but feels a bit rushed at the end and goes off the rails. However, it is still satisfying.The game play is an eclectic mixture of turn-based mech battles, odd jobs and exploring the town. Mech battles seem to have occasional glitches where the enemy becomes incapable of attacking, but these tend to occur in battles that don't matter too much. The odd jobs are interesting distractions. The challenge battles you can take on really are challenges, but overcoming them is incredibly satisfying. This stays true to the end with the final mech battle - though I only had to repeat it once, it was still a close match.The animations in battle truly lend to an atmosphere of spectacle, with each of them being named, landing with satisfying clangs and pushback, and conveying the power and weight of these machines. You can get some truly powerful moves, but don't neglect the lesser ones, as you need a variety for each limb and part. I favoured a defensive build.Overall: Wolfstride is not a perfect game and it took me time to get into it. But, it absolutely has heart. Like the ragtag team that it follows, it does its best and absolutely deserves your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride is a refreshing and unique blend of style, coolness and madness. The graphics and music are just sooo good. The swift animations fit perfectly and just make it so natural and yet at times so suddenly... "POoW!". All the Art in this game is very well achieved, genuine and inspired, but the SOUL of it all, it's the story... It's a ShatTered Soul, and when looking back into this experience it may feel like a story of random unrelated episodes that are hammered together into one shape/Shade using the power of craziness. Should this even work!? It does, because it achieves those levels of funny and extroversion we got used to watching and loving on very famous and successful animes.It's fragmented, but honestly, it doesn't really matter - first, because it becomes its identity, and second, because it causes so many emotions, and it's carried by a voice acting that is insanely good - it really brings the characters to life and the feelings to your throat.This one is special (just like Raw Fury likes them).Wolfstride starts us off with tastes of mental insanity, comedic dog threats and feelings of wonder at the brutal impacts of mech metal bashing. While we are distracted, it then develops a story with a good amount of deeply emotional moments that will make you forget this is supposed to be a Mech fighting game - and I'm not so sure it really is, but it is... maybe, YOU find out!It's ONE CRAAAZY RIDE! Go play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's style is great, it's like a real visual novel. It's also full of twists and turns, going between funny scenes, slice of life sections, emotional backstories, and tactical mech combat that is quite fun. The game is also fully voice acted!A couple cons are the fact you have to run everywhere, which adds time to the game and gets kind of annoying, as you don't want to miss things that could show up each day. Additionally, it starts up pretty slowly, so be prepared to ride out the intro for a while.Edit: Just finished the game, and I think one part near the end got a bit off. The huge rant I understood, but the section after could've been a cutscene maybe? Otherwise it was a fantastic, fun ending with more twists and turns just when it felt predictable.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: A bumpy but extremely enjoyable ride. More of a visual novel with proper gameplay than anything else, but there is so much to like about Wolfstride. The No More Heroes like structure moves along the plot, going from grinding minigames and sidejobs to upgrade your mech and get new attacks for these fun clashes against other mechas. Initially the premise is super entertaining, but sadly, you eventually will encounter loopholes within the combat system, and its very easy for the daily tasks to be very grating, and the money grind tiresome. More when initially, you lack some useful upgrades that ease the small roster of side jobs that allow getting more money.But what completely carries the game is not this repetitive loop, it's the S tier gang of deplorable underdogs starring the show, expressive portraits, soundtrack and the magnificent voice performances of the cast bringing these loosers to life. There is so much personality, charm and character on offer. I don't think this type of game is for everyone, but damn I had a really good time with this one, and I believe it deserves more attention for being a neat little game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is less than the sum of all of its parts: a visual novel with only a single choice (barring a minigame in the middle), an RPG system that, due to the lack of parts/skills, essentially solves itself for you when you reach gear-check battles, and a story which clearly seems to have been padded to give players who don't get into a repetitive loop of chores more time to grind the money for those aforementioned parts when they appear (the story starts referring to timers which are 2-3x longer than the plot tells you, undercut as soon as one minute later).It's not good. Nothing in it was worth my time and the final chapter was actually some of the worst of it because everything was visibly falling apart by then.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game, but I ended up requesting to refund it. The concept is fun; meet new people and face your past all while preparing for turn-based mecha fights. All the interactions between characters are full voice-acted, and the art is fun and beautiful. However, these things weren't enough to distract me from the horrible slow progression of the game. When you start the game it tells you that you have around 63 days until something (they don't tell you what it is at the beginning), and while you get to decide when to end your days once you've completed your daily tasks, it still feels trivial, if not just down right tedious. I think part of this is to blame on the unnecessarily long travel time between locations. When you want to leave one area, you have to run out of said area, then into a small cut-scene like hallway, and THEN you get to the actual map where you can pick your next destination. None of this would be a problem if not for the fact that your character is fairly slow considering the distance they want you to cover. Overall, the pacing of the game was not for me, but if you can handle the slow progression then you might like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Granted I've only played for 3 hours about and finished the first chapter;Game looks awesome. Whoever said that greyscale couldn't fit perfectly has no clue what they're talking about. Honestly I was a little unsure about the mixture of pixel based sprites for the overworld clashing with the animation for character portraits and mechas, but it looks fine and all the animations look excellent in their own right.I love the music. From the intense music leading into a fight, to the actual showdown itself, to the chill music walking between areas, I've had my volume turned way up since I started playing and I'm yet to regret it.I can only speak on the story from the first chapter, but the characters are enjoyable enough, and you really do get that feeling of working with a total scrap mech. Especially if you played the demo previously, you're painfully aware of how limited your pilot's capabilities are originally, as well as how unimpressive the machines stats are, which leads into this incredibly satisfying and thrilling feeling of getting stronger as you progress. I can imagine that some people might not take to the mini-games, or complain about the amount of story between mech fights (so far), but honestly I really appreciate the pacing. The build-up allows fights to feel more significant, and it causes the mech fights themselves to be refreshing and exciting when you get into one.This review may be updated as I play more, but so far, absolutely loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: A story-driven game about a group of misfits being gifted a mecha called Cowboy and then trying to climb the ranks of a fighting tournament with it. The dialogue can be lengthy sometimes, but the story was great, the characters had depth, and the turn-based mecha fights were fun and satisfying. You play as the protagonist, Dominic Shade, who manages Team Cowboy. Throughout the game, more of Shade's backstory will reveal itself, showing the player how he ended up reuniting with his close friends, Knife and Duque. Players can customize Cowboy with different kinds of parts that each have their own drawbacks and advantages, and the pilot, Knife Leopard, can equip various moves and stances, allowing the player to develop their own mecha-fighting playstyle throughout the game. Almost the entire game has high-quality voice acting. It also has a unique and stylish art style. Overall, Wolfstride was an experience that was like no other game for me, and I believe that it's a highly underrated indie gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one slow ♥♥♥♥♥♥ burn. It starts really low-key, with not a lot of options and with a story where you're just kinda milling about, getting to know the cast and see how they interact. It's really comfy, and the voicework is top-tier (I even kinda like Peepoo; I laughed like a jackal when he dipped his voice into his actual range for a moment and revealed he was putting on an extreme falsetto), and the writing is great.I was gonna drop it because it really did feel too slow for me, but I stuck it out for about the four hour mark; it was absolutely worth it. The game picks up around day 9, when suddenly two really big things change: 1) Virtual battles open up, and 2) you have an intense, emotional vignette with a character in a junkyard that let me know that this game was absolutely no longer messing around. From there, it's a hell of a ride. I'm not gonna be done with this one for a while.The presentation on this game is also absolutely divine. For such a small team, they managed to pull together some excellent voice talent for this *fully voiced* indie RPG (already a ridiculous feat, made better by just how GOOD it all is). The amount of polish and pure love put into both the pixel art and the anime-styled art grew hard on me over the hours. At first I was a little skeptical of the black and white art direction, but it really came together once I realized how they were using it very intentionally to tell the story.As I approach my middle age and I find myself looking back on my earlier years and how I spent them, I realized while playing this game that I'm asking the same kinds of questions these characters are. Because of that, I think I'm gaining an appreciation for looking forward and moving on. Lemme tell you, trash; It's a feeling that wouldn't be anywhere near as strong without an experience like this one on the record.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the very definition of a flawed masterpiece. It overstays its welcome, having a runtime of about 25-30 hours even though the open world is tiny, which will inevitably result in you traversing the same environments a few dozen times. It takes too long for you to even get to the first proper fight (about an hour!), with two scripted ones before that. The voice acting is a mixed bag, with some of the characters having some pretty fantastic performances while others sound bored out of their skull all the time. Some of the gags and character interactions miss the mark completely and come off as annoying rather than funny.But when it comes to everything else? This game It oozes with style, with the visuals and sound design being nothing short of stellar, especially during fights. Giant metal fists and bullet casings fly around in something that looks taken out of a manga, all accompanied by punchy mechanical sounds present in even the damn skill selection menus. I'd also be amiss not to mention the fantastic soundtrack, giving every opponent a distinct feel while complementing the action.But it's not style over substance. The gameplay, while not terribly complex, gives you enough challenge and freedom to develop builds and strategies as you get accustomed to the game's systems. My only gripe is that at the start of the game these fights occur with too little frequency, forcing you to explore the world and take in exposition instead of letting you punch robots in the robot-punching RPG. You eventually unlock some optional challenges that can be taken on at any time though, making the problem go away entirely.Last but not least, is the story. I don't even know where to begin with this (in a good way). Things start off a bit confusing, with your mecha getting wrecked on a fight and your protagonist Shade being involved in some shady stuff (wait, was that the joke all this time?), but that's all seemingly pushed under the rug pretty quickly, giving way to the straightforward goal of climbing the ranks on a tournament. It does take a while to get going, but the story eventually starts taking twists and turns you almost certainly won't see coming, something that gets more prevalent the more you play, and that's... actually a bit of a problem.See, while the story is, and I'm serious here, some of the best I've seen on a indie game, I can't stress enough how long it takes to get going, which isn't helped by the game's length. During the first 10 hours or so, the dialog can get mind-numbing at times, and I wouldn't blame anyone who decides to drop the game at that point. There can definitely be a whole lot of appeal for a story that starts off simple and slowly shows its true colors, a layered puzzle whose size you couldn't even grasp at first, but the writing and pacing just aren't enough to sustain that process.I don't regret the time I spent playing Wolfstride. If anything, the game's so damn stylish that I kept coming back just to see those cool animations and whatever fancy move my opponent would use next. If you want to see big stompy robots beating the crap out of each other, make yourself a favor and buy this. The story is just the icing on the cake (or maybe the center, considering how long it takes to get to it... but then... ah, whatever).
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wondered what it would be like to own a giant mech? Pretty cool thing right? Being able to hop inside cockpit onto the pilot seat, take the controls and feel the ungodly power of each hit you land, thundering shock of every punch you take. But what if I told you it would come with elegantly stylized monochrome world view, existential crisis and crippling debt you have 63 days to pay off? Welcome to Wolfstride and hop on the ride "trash", it won't stop till the end!Game starts with a cutscene and jumps to turn based combat prologue that gives us a look on our main protagonist and his supporting cast. You're thrown in shoes of Dominic Shade, conman, ex-yakuza and professional liar. Don't have much on you besides killer smile, stylish suit, cool sunglasses and pack of smokes. Accompanied by ever optimistic friend and mech pilot Knife Leopard (AKA Pineapples) and ever grumpy dog man who happens to be great mechanic Duque (AKA Wizard), Dominic is set to make cash enough for the trio to live comfortably. Things go bad extremely fast as his latest money scheme goes bottoms up, debts are piling up and past catches up to him. Trio of friends decides to place their bets on one last gig - the UGG Mecha tournament in Rain City and in the end maybe even save the world?Wolfstride's world is sharp, anime-stylized mixture of giant robots, over the top characters and pixel art goodness. Mecha designs are striking (even if game doesn't exactly show them clearly due to forced perspective during fights),  characters have certain flair to them, portraits and still shots are full of neat details and it's clear some mecha centric animes were an inspiration. Animation of giant robots during combat is awesome, bold lines of the designs, attack names, anime speed lines, it all adds to the spectacle. Between the fights we observe the action from the side and we move around the world in very pretty pixel art. All of it is dipped in monochrome sauce with few exceptions, which helps the game to elevate it's style further. I'm a sucker for good looking games and Wolfstride artists did really great job here.There is nothing spectacular here in matter of exploration, between fights we travel the city as Dominic, do sidequests and minigames during each day. There is no free roam, map is divided into 6 sections and we pick them from map menu. Once picked we can run around and look for things to interact with and characters to talk to. As the game progresses we can unlock different minigames that can get us money to buy new pilot moves as well as special parts for our mech, which has pretty deep internal customization. We can't customize the look of Cowboy, but it's possible to swap head/chest/arm plates that increase the HP of each part, add different frames that increase base damage and ammo count, operating systems which increase damage of attacks in certain range, engines that increase moving range, mainframes responsible for extra action points and lastly cores, that govern healing efficiency. Game is divided into 63 days and has a rythm of few days rest>fight>few days rest giving player time to repair their huge chunk of iron between action. Full playthrough took me around 30 hours which is pretty hefty for the price value. There were few minor bugs here and there but nothing a restart couldn't solve.Combat is a slightly different beast, as we ditch the pixel art graphics and go into full comic and anime style. Giant robots are placed on opposite sides of the ring, represented by a lane at the bottom. Each turn player and the enemy are able to close or gain the distance with MP and do  attacks with AP, some also require ammo, which can be reloaded infinitely with certain actions. Before fights make sure to pick attack moves, defense and repair skills as well as stance that affects generation of morale based bonus damage. Each stance has specific conditions to generate morale and 100% means bonus damage to next hit. Healing works similarily as it is generated passively between turns and on 100% it's possible to repair or restore destroyed parts. Speaking of parts - each mech has 4 targetable parts: head, arms left/right and chest, which if you destroy wins the fight. Destroyed head robs you or enemy from ability to direct blows, losing arms locks up certain attacks. Haven't mentioned it yet but game is almost entirely voice acted and cast really makes the story feel alive. My favourites are Dominic and owner of the nearby junkyard Hog, guys are pouring their souls into it. Favourite female characters - Joy, Moonshine and Aunt ZZ. Supporting cast, male and female, are also really good and fit their roles. Combat noises are rich, you hear impact of the blows, gunshots, horns of thrown cars at you, explosions after destroying parts. Even moving mech around has nice "thud!" to it. As for music it's a pretty interesting mix of rock, country, blues, somber rock ballads and some few genres I can't exactly put my fingers on. But overall, it's solid soundtrack and you may find to pick a favourite song or two.And we finally reach story, which is probably the only thing I had a gripe with during my Wolfstride playthrough. Characters are mostly likeable (except for one VERY annoying robot) and it's pretty good tale about trio of friends on larger than life adventure. The thing that irked me was how unfocused it all could become. Along with main story we are introduced through game narration to additional plot points and they all go... nowhere? Even in main story some events happen without rational explanation. It gives a feeling of a Kickstarter game that didn't exactly reach every goal, so some loose ends got left dangling, although that's most likely not the case. Pacing of the story is also hurt by overusage of monologues. Never been a fan of characters talking at each other, even if they get a pass because of emotional situation. People don't talk in lengthy monologues. But when dialogue is good, the game gives off a bit of that Tarantinoesque character, maybe thanks to overall pulp, over the top vibe and extensive yet not overbearing usage of swears. This may be the first game that gave me that "maybe I'm getting too old to understand this" feeling due to plot construction, it may just be me though. "Immature grown-up RPG" may be the best summary straight from the devs. Overall it's a good story that touches many subjects like redemption and coming to terms with your past to be able to look into the future. The ride to the end in those 30 hours was good, albeit bumpy at times.To sum up, I think you, dear reader, should give Wolfstride a chance if you like VNs and/or giant robots. I'm no VN veteran but I enjoyed my 30+hours. Voice actors carried their roles admirably, audio and graphic style elevated the whole experience above the "style over substance" story beats at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, trash! It's time for a Midnight Strut Session!WOLFSTRIDE is the underrated gem of 2021I've been looking forward to this game since 2020's Steam NextFest where they release the demo. As a big fan of Mecha, this game was on my radar as sson as I saw the premise. The game plays like a well-written visual novel with mecha turn-based battles and minigames thrown in to help immerse you in its world. The build diversity you can have with your mech surprised me as it is so deep and varied with how much you are allowed to customize. Each of the minigames are fun in their own ways and offer rewards you can then use for your mech battles. The last bit of of interactive playing is collecting pineapples and raising your NPCs friendship. You do this by giving them said pineapples to submit them to the almighty tropical army of the pineapple god. This is one of the only downsides as the amount of pineapples needed is a bit much so farming pineapples feels tedious after a bit.The story of this game while starting out very slow becomes this over-the-top adventure that actually made me teary eyed at the end. The moral of the story is fairly simple, but the way it is told really moved me. All the characters within the scope of this story are somehow amicable and refreshing to be around, yet they all encompass tropes we've seen time and time again. Shade is such a goof yet badass character. He really reminds me of Travis Touchdown from No More Heroes. In fact, much of the story iterates some of the themes or atmosphere of Travis Strikes Again which is a plus in my book (you should definitely give that one a try too!).The soundtrack for this game by Isadora Penna is sooooo good. I am big on rock and dirty sounding guitar and this soundtrack is all of that and a bag of crisps. There is still tracks that sound more mellow that are very nice to listen to as well. Some of my favorites on the soundtrack are Wolfstride, Trinket & Killer, Shade, Wormageddon and See You Around, Trash. Give them a listen on whatever streaming service you use to see if you dig it.In the end, this game was a blast that I will definitely give a replay in the future. A solid 9/10 that went under alot of people's radars. I hope more people play it.Like you, trash!

_childDocuments_.review: A good visual novel with turn based mech battle action. There are two things people need to know before jumping into this game, though - you'll be spending a lot of time grinding minigames to raise money to upgrade mech parts, and there's a specific game you need to grind a lot of in order to get best-in-slot gear. The story missions are fairly difficult if you don't bother and only use store-bought gear, which I would say is a decent demerit.While the voice acting is *excellent*, the tone of the script is less so. There's a character named Peepoo who is as annoying as you would expect, and there's several cutscenes that go on for about 3x longer than they should, even though you can tell the VA is great and they're doing their best to keep the momentum going. As long as you have a good amount of tolerance for some weirdly overwrought melancholy and weeb-ery, you'll be able to see the story through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there, Kiddo! Have you ever wanted to play an ANIME?  Ever wanted to go on Hours of Filler-Episode style adventures followed up by heart felt story arches that you remember for decades? WELL THEN WolfStride IS FOR YOU! WolfStride is  like playing an anime like Space-Dandy or Cowboy Bebop, but with Mechs. Turn based combat, and minigames akin to No-More-Heros. Some Straight out of the 2010's anime craze style game. 7/10. Frag-a-Jam.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Fun game play mechanic concepts. Satisfying progression/leveling. Rock-em-Sock-em Robot fantasy fullfilment.Cons: Worst narrative of any game I've ever played. WAY over the top characters constantly avoiding questions in seventeen scenes before finally answering with emo responses, and repetitive dialogue/downright annoying voice lines. There's a character who has robot turrets and says PEEEEE all the time, or an announcer who calls everyone trash every single sentence for nearly every single fight. Who came up with/approved this? Also, the game play loop gets repetitive since you only have three strategic options. 1. Blitz a kill. 2. Neutralize enemy offenses/defenses to grind a kill. 3. Take out the head to mitigate their focus damage then blitz the kill. (this last strategy is required like twice all game, so I'm being generous including it.)I think a sequel could be very promising if these concerns are addressed, but as is I would say I feel more frustrated than satisfied by this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily, one of the best story driven games i've ever played.No really, the story being simple, and eventually evolving into something stupidly over the top, just to end up with me trying to hold my emotions to myself cause of the really special ending. And the fact that reading the entire thing, playing through it, and having fun with all of it took me around 30 hours just shows that it's a good time sink. Absolutely amazing voice acting, absolutely amazing characters, absolutely amazing graphic style, absolutely amazing jokes. I hardly know what else i can really say to describe them without spoiling the game. Though i can say that the fighting in this game gets slightly stale after a bit, and when you unlock a move that gives you special meter, and steals it from your opponent so you can heal faster and they cannot do it all, and the entire fighting kinda falls apart to the point that if you're not losing instantly, you're winning. But nontheless that i've had a blast building a great moveset i liked and riding on it till the end of the game.Also to think that the "Power of Christ Compels you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" line was the single reason why i bought it, and ended up with genuinely thinking this is one of the best games i've ever played, is kinda funny.I can't write good reviews, but that was an amazing ride, and great fight in giant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechs, that turned into everything i wasn't expecting and made me love every second of it. Buy it, Play it. Become Trash.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part it's a fully voiced visual novel with light gameplay elements to keep you actually engaged. You run around between various locations to find the next piece of story and then return back to your base. It has some extremely pointless padding in form of running down a 10 second street every time you go somewhere, but it's not too bad overall. It can be ignored with a bit of tolerance. Outside of that you get a few mech fights of turn based combat as big events in between doing small tasks to progress the story.I would say the trailers "slightly oversell" how good the animations and the voiceacting is as in the game there is a bunch of repetition of different faces etc, but being "slightly worse than how bombastic awesome the trailers looked" still makes it awesome at the minimum. Thus you are casually playing through a super stylish visual novel with endeering characters and plenty of laughs to be had. The gameplay is basically non-offensive and somewhat enjoyable busy work whilst the game delivers a bunch of amazing and interesting characters to listen to. WELL WORTH the money in my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't take this pseudo JRPG in stride...I can safely say that Wolfstride is unlike any other game that I have ever played. Are there others like it out there on the market? Most assuredly. But none have as much thought or attention to detail put into them, if you ask me.I won't be providing any kinds of spoilers here, other than to say that this action-packed visual novel perfectly encapsulates the experience of playing an anime protagonist with a shadowy & tragic past. Everything from the visuals, to the exchanges of dialogue, to the story and setting and the relationships between the myriad of characters that comprise it all — it all coalesces into something akin to perfection.Even if you're not a fan of the various series that clearly inspired it ('Trigun', 'Cowboy Bebop', 'The Big O', 'Outlaw Star', 'Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann' and 'Cannon Busters' just to name a few), I'm still going to highly recommend this game. It's got everything you could ever want from one of its kind; heart, humor, action, suspense, drama, and big effing robot battles! (And who doesn't love big effing robot battles?)But perhaps the best thing of all is the value. This game is only 15$, when in reality it ought to be at least thrice that. God tier levels of work have been put into this thing. The voice actors do an outstanding job of propelling the narrative forward in ways that a lot of diehard otaku would say was impossible to do outside of Japan. The visuals make you feel like you're playing something produced by Madhouse or Studio Trigger, who have produced some of the most famous anime of any generation, past or present. And that soundtrack?! Oh, man. It's the icing on the proverbial cake!So, yes, I am going to recommend Wolfstride to everyone that I know. Raw Fury and OTA IMON have teamed up to deliver a must-have gaming experience. 5 out of 5 stars.Well, what're you waiting for, trash?! Get in that cockpit and punch Earth in the face!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. The vibes are immaculate, the main cast give me strong Cowboy Bebop vibes, and they all really grew on me with time. The art is just fantastic, too.It manages to be both funny and genuinely emotional, without those stepping on each others' toes, and while the main character can be very melodramatic, it's not like the game is unaware of that. (Thankfully not in the way that it gets constantly quipped about to the point of getting grating.)It's not perfect - the pacing - of upgrades most specifically, but in general - can feel a little wonky. Trying to get money and max friendships with people requires an excessive amount of minigame grinding. Our perspective character's long melodramatic rants about how awful he is can get a bit excessive, and even the chunky, satisfying main combat of the game can fall prey to you figuring out a dominant strategy, making it easier than it should probably be... but none of these things stopped me having a wonderful time. It's a game that I can definitely see not everyone completely vibing with, but it resonated with me, and completely sucked me in.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride was basically love at first sight for me.  I love mecha, and it's tone and presentation press a lot of buttons for me.  I'd recommend to anyone, especially anime fans, because it plays like one at times.Gameplay is divided between walking around town doing various chores for mech parts, and occasional battles to put them to use.  I was playing Persona 5 Royal before I started, and while the structures are similar, Wolfstride is a little more concise, meaning I haven't been able to put it down.It isn't a perfect game.  There are supposed to lose fights, and minigames you can't win until you get upgrades later on, two things that always annoy me.  The story can also feel like it drags on, especially when characters start to repeat themselves over and over in soliloquies, which happens a few times toward the end.  The climax isn't very satisfying either,  the game alludes to  a big bad from pretty early on, but by the time they actually show up the fighting is done, and the focus of the story shifts from the stakes of the mech fighting in the real world, to one of the character exploring their own psyche and learning to forgive themselves.   Guess the structure isn't the only similarity to Persona.  There's even a pinrapple based social link system, now that I think about it, though the rewards feel a little lack-luster, most of them being things you can buy eventually anyway.  The rate at which you get pineapples is also abysmal, which leads to an absurd amount of grinding on minigames, which would've really put a damper on things if I didn't know how to use cheat engine and just give myself all the pineapples I could ever want.Wolfstride, though flawed at times, is the most fun I've had in a while, with a great cast of interesting characters.  Except for Peepoo, a deliberately annoying sidekick character.  His voice is like nails on a chalkboard, and he's a one trick pony who tries to say vulgar things but whose programming only lets him say 'PEEEEE.'  I skipped through most of his lines, and resent him being in the game.  Until he was introduced, I loved everything about it; and the game is still amazing around him, it just gets derailed for a little while when he shows up, and feels a little grating whenever he makes a lame, uh, 'joke.'If I seem hard on the game, it's because it was close to perfection for me, but that makes the few, minor flaws it has stand out much more.  It's still a solid 4/5, an 8-8.5/10,  I'm hoping for a sequel that goes a little more in depth, and actually explores some of the plot points it set up and then ignored.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has fun characters, nice music, and gorgeous sprites, so I can forgive it for being a little too entertained by poop jokes (seriously, cool it with those if you ever make a sequel). It's jarring, too, because this game does have some legitimately beautiful moments (e.g. the last LAST fight) and some jokes that felt like they earned a chuckle out of me, so this type of juvenile humor feels kind of forced and out of place when juxtaposed with the rest of the package.Ironically, this line of criticism doesn't apply to the character named PeePoo, who ended up being one of my favorite characters. You could tell the voice actor was just having so much fun with this character the whole way through.One part of this game that I really enjoyed was the way characters talk to each other. Every one has a nickname - Shade, for example, is also Shado, and Catman. Knife Leopard is Pineapples, Duque is Killer Hound, Zee is the Witch. A lot of times in stories this gets really annoying, but I feel that they did it in a very endearing way in this game.On the topic of voice actors - for this level of production, I was very pleasantly surprised by the entire cast's voice performances, with the exception of some lines sprinkled throughout that were clearly recorded out of context of the lines surrounding them. There are also quite a few typos, as other people have mentioned, and I wish that they would go back and fix those. That said, I definitely appreciated the moments where the actors adlibbed just a bit to make the characters sound more natural.It makes it even better, then, that all of these lines are accompanied by a myriad of beautifully-realized portraits, with all sorts of crazy and awesome expressions. Some larger, more intricate images are used in the more impactful moments of the game, which made me wish that there were some sort of built-in gallery for me to see them again later.There are all sorts of little things in this game that bugged me, including actual bugs. The biggest of which was a glitch which caused me to be completely unable to play the game. Luckily, support was very quick to get back to me on this issue, and I've published the fix I used to get past it in a community post. There were also a couple of smaller issues, like how the "money ticking" sound will sometimes start to loop infinitely. However, none of these issues were common enough for them to bog down my 25 hours with the game.There were some design decisions I wasn't a huge fan of, such as the way pineapples were done. This system did have some fun moments come out of it - such as a character telling you the pineapples made his heart stop, which teaches you the Cardiac Arrest Punch move for your mech - but I didn't feel rewarded for maxing out all of the characters. Even just making the pineapple god say something funny would've been nice; an achievement would've been appreciated as well.The arcade is another area I felt this. I was very excited to see the arcade grow as the weeks when on in the game, but I maxed out all of the upgrades in the first 3 days of discovering it. I kept coming back under the assumption that there would be more (the hint for the place says I can hire more people, but I never got that option), but there never was. These are very small things, obviously, but it's the type of thing where just a little bit more would have gone a long way.Finally: gameplay. This is the part of the game that I think is best enjoyed if you know what you're getting into. I'll just be blunt here: most of this game is waking up in the morning, walking to every NPC you know, talking to them, and maybe doing some side-jobs for money and other goodies.If you're hoping for mech battles galore right out the gate, you'll probably be a bit disappointed by the "slow start". There are lots of opportunities to play them to your heart's content later in the game, but the early game is all about getting the world and characters established. The mechs themselves are wonderfully brought to life, with gorgeous animations and punchy sound effects.In the end, Wolfstride is a very captivating story with really fun characters that are all unique and pretty well performed. If you let it, it can really pull you in with endearing character moments and hilarious mini-games .

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of heart and style, and the substance isn’t bad either.If you couldn’t tell, the game is in black and white, and that is an intentional stylistic choice. I would say that it would look a lot better in color, but fret not, there are a few twists and turns in terms of this design decision. And the game does a lot with its extremely limited color palette.The voice acting is very solid, pretty much every VA does a great job of portraying a single character, even some of the NPCs who don’t particularly matter to the overall story. This has a lot to do with the script, which makes each character distinct and unique, but the voice overs really hit this home. Wolfstride is an underdog story at its core, but there is other stuff happening in the background, and when it hits its story highs it hits them pretty hard. There is a really cool sequence about half way through the game that I wasn’t expecting, just fluff, and it is done in a really engaging way that makes you appreciate what the writers were doing with these characters.But I can’t say the entire script is perfect. Certain events happen with little explanation, some plot threads seemingly lead to nowhere, and certain characters have a tendency to either philosophize ad nauseam or go on melodramatic rants. One character in particular is written to be both incredibly annoying and lovable, and you may alternative between those extremes from scene to scene. I do believe some of the imperfections I mentioned are actually done on purpose. Wolfstride’s writing is quirky, so is the lore, to say the least. Overall though, the story is just rewarding enough to make the journey to the end worth it.You’re probably wondering about the gameplay though. The core mecha combat is really good, especially getting new parts and moves to customize your playstyle. To its credit the game gives you a lot of versatility in terms of how to approach each fight, and when you get your core together, you will feel like a badass. The problem is that it takes a looooong time to get there. The beginning is very slow and doesn’t have a lot of action, but once you’re reaching mid to late game, it’s almost nothing but a metal on metal, robot punching fight-fest. You will initially face off with some really basic, beat-up junkers, but gradually move on to some really powerful and very cool-looking opponents.There are also several minigames, and for the most part they are decently fun. The game doesn’t tell you this, but you won’t be getting high scores on those minigames until you progress further and unlock certain helper items. The main problem with Wolfstride though is that the world is kinda...empty. You’ll spend the majority of the game running in game-time through the same empty streets to talk to a few NPCs, grind some cash, and then do it again the next day. It’s not super daunting, but it does get old after you’ve been doing it for a while. There’s also some grinding involved with a certain mechanic, but if you wait until a little past the game’s mid-point, it becomes significantly less time consuming.Would I recommend this game? Oh yeah, overall I think it is pretty great. But try the free demo first if it is still available, see how you feel about it. For someone who likes giant robots and tactical combat there is plenty to love. Just remember to do what Foam Gun asks you to do. And talk to Barbara, she loves you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll edit this for a bit more detail later but for right now: Wolfstride is an absolute banger, The game's style alone would be enough to recommend it as an artistic indie game. The music, tone and art design are all stunning. The game wears plenty of hats and the DNA of a diverse group of sci fi elements are kicking around inside it.  Gurren Lagann, Pacific Rim and Cowboy Bebop are the clearest inspirations for the world and story, but the art design has that sleek, design-heavy stylistic flair to it that I associate with the likes of Persona or Dangan Ronpa. That's not to say there's nothing original in Wolfstride, it's a wildly creative endeavor. But it wears its inspirations on its sleeve and they come together in this bombastic, beautiful game.And it is a game. This is no walking simulator or glorified puzzle game. There's a lot of gameplay to be found in customizing your pair of cowboys (mecha and pilot both) and the combat is tactical and hits a good level of challenge where it's punishing but with a proper build and strategy few mistakes spell an instantly lost battle. I won't get into all the details of gameplay, particularly since at 5 hours of gameplay I am still unlocking new systems. Suffice it to say that underneath the flair and highly competent story and characters there is a genuinely interesting and play heavy RPG.The game's not precisely flawless. The indie heritage shows in a few rough edges UX-wise, mainly regarding the locations of certain menus and the travel times from location to location and the dialogue can be a bit unwieldy at times. There are also a minor handful of bugs I've run into but nothing gamebreaking and the developers have already begun to address the worst of them. Honestly, my biggest criticisms are largely nitpicks and not anything that I think would turn a player's experience of the game.In short,  the game's stunning. Zany, nostalgic without being unoriginal, and deeply engaging. Especially given its extremely generous pricing I can't recommend this one enough.  So give Wolfstride a shot, peopletrash. I didn't regret it and I'm confident anyone who's gotten far enough to read this review won't either.

_childDocuments_.review: rocks!What a game, what a wonderfully energic and stylish game.A funny/heartfelt/bombastic Visual Novel, bundled with a cool and competent turn-based combat.Explore the city, meet people and do odd jobs to scrap together enough money and parts to fix the mess of a mech you call "Cowboy" for the next big fight.Artstyle goes quite strong, good music and dialogue to boot and quite a lengthy game too for the asking price.Imagine the battlefield as a 7 squares line each mech occupying one space.The game builds around this concept by having abilities that can only target up to a certain range or over it, you can move, push your enemy, be pushed by them, buff yourself, use and recharge your ammo for special attacks and access a special move once a bar fills up.Your mech can be customized to fit multiple playstyles you may have in mind.When not in fights you’ll be doing some minigames to earn money for the upgrades and repairs you oh so desperately need for the next fight.A gangster with a heart of gold, a gruff canine mechanic, and a free spirited hunk wish to enter the mechfighting world tournament with their busted up, prototype of a mech......an incredible story ensues.In the early game the fights are sparce and far between, leaving much more space for the visual novel to set stakes and characters.Conversely in the late game is just a mad rush of a fight after the other with little time for the story and the little that there is while flashing out the world of the game a little ore is inconsequential for the characters and main narrative.Many things are left unexplained or narrative arc are opened and never closed or abruptly ended in a hurry to wrap things up.These are still minor complaints; I still thoroughly recommend this game because it deserve every ounce of praise.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, Wolfstride is a ride. The steam page's own description puts it best when it describes itself as "an immature grown-up RPG". The art is obviously incredible and the game knows it. I've never seen a story's final act try to cram more crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ into it and I mean that in the best way possible. While Wolfstride suffers at times from some slow pacing but the game had enough charm, style, and intrigue to keep me hooked and in the end it all paid off. Its influences shine through while still feeling like something totally original, albeit not without its flaws.             The Mech Battle system is unique and interesting enough to serve its purpose for fights but I didn't feel encouraged to swap around moves and parts often like the game has in mind as customization felt underwhelming at times. There were also a surprising amount of days with nothing special to do besides new dialogue for the characters. I do think the driving force of this game is the ride you get pulled along for with its cast but I think the surplus of days with nothing special going contributes to the game's pacing feeling a little weird at times, especially when there's inconsistencies about whether or not there's narration after the day. However, on the note of the cast, I'm not sure if I've ever seen an indie game with more character bulging out of its voice acting to the point I couldn't see any of the cast the same without it. Wolfstride's characters are its heart.                  With those flaws being said though, I think they're fairly easy to overlook once you get into the flow of the game. For an Indie debut I think Wolfstride is incredibly impressive and I'm a bit shocked to have not seen anyone online talking about it. I think OTA IMON has shown a lot of promise with this game and I'm excited to see and play more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game at the end of 2021, and I feel bad that it took me this long to play it.If it has the name Wolf in it, I'll always take a look. Glad I did!This game is a story that many of us have experienced in our lives. Ok, maybe not with mecha, or shady pasts. Just getting on in age, and feeling like we didn't accomplish much. Not knowing our path, and living with regret.The main characters in game, are in their mid 20's, to early 30's, with other characters being far older than that.So for many of us, the "time limit" as it were, hits home, and hits hard.Let's break down all the good stuff.-Beautiful sprite animations, as well as great detail 2D art for our characters and mecha.-Grade A voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not big on mecha games tbh. Never have been. They tend to be rather...soulless to me. Mech battle after mech battle after mech battle with a story that's either a quick paragraph between menus or a relentless deluge of background details with no greater present story than "You want to be number one".Wolfstride...Wolfstride is different.Wolfstride is a game that at surface level, maintains the 'rags to riches' story I mentioned above, but uses it as a base to bring together a bunch of troubled characters and give them something to believe in again. And honestly, characters are where Wolfstride shines. Every single member of your team, every citizen of Rain City, hell every opponent you face on your rise to the top has a level of complexity and care put into them that makes you love, laugh with, laugh at or hate them effectively. Combined with the distinct artstyle of the world and solid soundtrack, it creates a world I wanted to truly absorb and enjoy as much as possible. Chatting with the crew in the hangar, grabbing a drink at the Midnight Rider, doing odd jobs at the Crapyard, they all make this place feel like a living world instead of a glorified menu.And the mech fights are nothing to sneeze at either. The anticipation between each fight is intense as you scramble to prepare your mech with the customisation system which strikes the perfect balance of being deep and complex enough that any playstyle can be used, but it's never so complicated that it feels overwhelming and intimidating. The fights are intimate, strategic and brutal. You're not chipping away at someone in a metal suit that moves like they're on the Moon going "pew pew pew" with a toy laser. You're getting in there, breaking through their defences and shoving a 10 ton fist RIGHT UP THEIR...chest. It feels cathartic and impactful, like a boxing match between two heavyweight champs. Just a relentless slugfest between two mechanical titans and I love it.Now I won't call it perfect. There are a lot of story moments that take 10 lines to say what could have been said in 2 and while the story itself is great, there are elements I wish were explored more relating to some of the side characters. And there IS a mechanic that I swear was trying to go for it, but it ended up just being a way to get some cool parts and bonuses for the gameplay, which is nice, but...man the potential was there. Also the game's not as funny as it thinks it is. The humour hits true in a good portion of the game, but there are moments where the comedy falls flat, 95% of the time due to one particular character who deserves to be punted into the sun.Those issues and some minor spelling and grammar errors aside, Wolfstride is an excellent time. An immersive, living, breathing world with some amazing characters and thrilling mech fights to be had that's just shy of being a bona-fide classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this game isn't what you probably think it is.  It looks like a turn based mech combat game but it's not.  It has turn based mech battles, one on one arena matches, and they're fun.  The mechs look good and you can customize not only the mech equipment but the move list for your pilot.  You can make a bunch of different, and effective, builds.  That part of the game is great, and the black and white art looks nice.  If I were to rate the mech fights on their own?  Easily 8/10.  But that's the problem, the game isn't just about the mech fights.It's also full of tedious, repetitive tasks.  Loaded with rather poor writing and way, way too much dialogue.  There are several rather annoying characters with very annoying voice acting, one in particular that's just plain ridiculous - they were going for a character like Claptrap but they missed by a country mile.Then there are the minigames that are very boring and feel out of place.  There's also lots of pointless running around from one area to another.  The story is boring.  Too many cut scenes and voice overs that I can't seem to skip or speed up.  Just one thing after the next that's annoying, pointless, and/or tedious.There are glitches in certain parts of the game.  The display in the virtual combat arena starts to act up and you can't see where each mech is positioned, and that's pretty important.  I also managed to get stuck while walking from one area to another, no idea why, and I had to exit and re-start to fix it.The single biggest issue is that the first 3+ hours is annoying and boring.  You have to power through hours of boring story and annoyances in order to get to the mech battles and it's painful.  The first few hours should grab the player and make them want to play more.  If I hadn't read some forum posts that say that the game does get better I would have given up and that's a massive problem.Wolfstride is a beautiful, disjointed, and tedious mess that I wish I could recommend but I simply can't endorse a game that I have to force myself to play in order to get to the good parts.  8/10 for the mech combat and overall art/style but this is a 2/10 for the rest resulting in an average of 5/10 which is simply not good enough, folks.

_childDocuments_.review: (Explanation - Received as a Christmas gift.)Rating - No More Heroes if it meant something, out of 10Overview - What a wild, strange, F'd up unbelievable ride.Story - You play Dominic Shade. for the most part, as you get handed a giant hulking key to the future with metal fists from a departed friend. Deciding to take part officially in the world-wide tournament of mechs, you claw and kick and drag you way through countless fights against all odds as the Player is slowly fed introspective bites and info on what might be really going on here.  If you can put up with a small handful of spelling errors and incorrect text, it's perfectly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fine. And everything is voiced (Altho Shade talking about the Mangoose stopped being spoken)Gameplay - 4 Body parts to slap metal hands on and shoot! A single plane of movement that you can take advantage of!  A ton of parts to equip to your mech to adjust all kinds of options! A long list of offensive, defensive and support moves to swap around! And then slaving away Shade's life trying to make money to afford most of that cuz Fight money is piss lmao.  It's really fine tho. Combat is very fun ( I will vehemently agree with anyone calling "that move" broken. You know the one).  Feels great to hit things. You see battle damage in both directions. You can disable and break parts to kill access to one's actions.  The jobs are all fairly quick. You get good cash as you rank higher, too.  The game's also intelligent about "point of last return", and gives you the option to go back and make stacks of cash if you didn't think ahead.  Speaking of, the game is very forgiving in general about this, and tells you about the make-or-break spots before they happen.Pineapples are a currency as well for basically Bond Points, and don't come frequently enough I feel. Plus, could have used flashier moves? Just a few.Music - Hooh. If a person came up to me and said this was the style of music that'd be playing as they took me, it'd be 48 hours before I ever remembered what gender they were.  This music was amazing. Every track has energy and mood and often times I sat there just listening to it in-game. Plus you get the Mangoose, who took me way too long to realize he drummed a beat to how fast Shade moved. Or didn't. Art - You  might be initially taken aback by the 6-bit pixel art for the "world" portion. It's totally irrelevant. Each  mech is amazingly well-drawn, and every action is of similar repute. Everyone's profiles do a great job of portraying the current emotion or goal of the discussion.  Not to mention, I'm fairly certain Shade's smoke trail from his cig is entirely random. So there's that marvel. Cast - We're talking about a pendulum being flung across the Mohave Desert. From borderline try-hard cool guy Shade, to two specific individuals who are utterly NEXT ****ING LEVEL insane.  We have super heroes. We have mobsters. We have hitmen. Possibly abyssal beings. A llama. Yes a llama. Secondary gameplay section -  I'm a bit torn on this part. I feel like I could have used some visual mods to Cowboy over the course of the game? Also, maybe like a NG+ or just some sort of "Endless".

Some of the locations like arcade, underground, and midnite rider also feel underutilized. The game has the oddest fast travel mechanic, which causes pointless backtracking between locations. This becomes even more evident when you are going around the map, trying to trigger new events.The soundtrack and the mech combat are ok, while the voice acting and the art style are top-notch. Wolfstride takes tons of Inspiration from Cowboy Bebop and Gurren Lagann, but all it learned from them was to be complex for the sake of being one.
