_childDocuments_.review: I sunk 30 hours into this game, I 100%-ed it and unlocked every achievement. And yet, I cannot recommend this game in good faith. I'm gonna get heavy into spoilers in my review, so here's a short little tldr for those considering buying this gamePros: Incredible, if repetitive gameplayIncredible, if very repetitive musicIt's fully voice acted, and the VOs did an absolutely fantastic jobThe writing is incredibly hit or miss, but it hits a lot of the time and manages to be funny, charming, and gets you to care about (some of) the charactersThe art style is greatThe cons: Everything elseI realize that enjoying a story is subjective, but the contrivances are strange, almost nothing is explained, and when some are, you'll have wished they didn't even bother. Genuinely, don't play this game for the story. Watch the movie they ripped off instead! Redline is an incredible movie, one of my favorites, and so I was excited when the stories were eerily similar in the beginning. You can tell when they stopped plagiarizing and started writing for their own. Watch Redline and enjoy the gameplay. That's as much as you can get out of this game.Spoilers begin now:This is very obviously a character based game. There is an overarching plot, but it's there as set dressing and to provide motivation for the characters. The overarching story is confusing and kept insanely vague, so all you CAN do is focus on the characters. If you go in looking for character development, you'll find it in spades! Except for the main character, Shade. Shade starts out with Homestuck sunglasses and a chip on his shoulder, and from the getgo he has this "I'm too cool for all this" facade that is, at least I thought, intentionally grating. His friends provide enough buoyancy to offset his terrible vibe. The people around Shade grow and change and turn into legitimately better versions of themselves throughout the story, but Shade stays exactly the same the entire game. The other characters, and even Shade's own memories try to get him to improve himself but he resolutely refuses time and time again. Until finally you reach the ending, and you get a completely unearned 5 minute cutscene where he throws himself a pity party and then says he's changed, and then roll credits. The ending leaves such a bad taste in your mouth that it'll make you gag I swear. We even get a fire emblem type "Where are they now" type thing in the credits, and 1, we don't get to hear about the world at large, which is very strange considering the ending is the start of WW3, and we don't get to see what happens to our opponents, which is so disappointing. And in this “Where are they now”, Shade says that after this whole braveheart speech about how he's changed and he's better now, he says point blank that he's going to continue acting the exact same way. It’s such a gut punch.The second half of this game ruins the good will it establishes in the first 10 times over. 100 times over even. The story flies off the rails completely, none of your questions are answered, and it just keeps promising and promising that something interesting will happen, and it never does. At the end, a character we've never seen before shows real life footage of the American Military, makes some good points about the world that they live in, kills you, and is never mentioned before or again. He just kinda comes in, proves himself right unequivocally, and then the game is over. Who the hell is this guy? We never know. We never get answers to almost all of our questions. Who is GW? Vague hints and a big fat nothing burger. Why'd he kill himself gruesomely in front of his friends? No clue. Who is Godworm and why does he have a cult? Not only is that not answered, it's not even brought up. He paralyzes your best friend and you have no clue who this guy is, and then you have to read in between the lines and infer that he's somehow related to this universe's United Nations? Who blew up that oil tanker? NO CLUE? Why'd Shade make a deal with the devil? Because he felt weak I guess? What was the deal? THEY DON'T SAYAnd for the cherry on this sh*t cake, the big one we've all been waiting for, why is Shade in this mess to begin with? What exactly is the inciting incident of this story? Well I'm glad you asked, you see Shade's friend got shot, and Shade fired back, and f*cking missed, and just hit a random dude. That's the rock solid foundation this house of cards is built on. I swear to god I lost my mind when I found out this is what Shade had been whining about the whole game. Just a hollow vapid character, with a quirk that does not work, and with zero growth.It blew my mind that this was the direction they took the story. You feel like you missed something CONSTANTLY, but believe me, you didn't. It just doesn't connect, and doesn't make sense.There are a ton of smaller annoying things too, like the gameplay outside of the fights is grinding minigames or slowly running through an empty, way too big map to check if people have no dialogue or items for you, which 90% of the time is absolutely not. The difficulty is a joke. You have to stop yourself from killing your opponents on the first turn by ending your turn early if you want to hear the second round midfight dialogue. You have to intentionally handicap yourself to make this game have any semblance of difficulty (except for the penultimate mech fight, which is by far the best in the game).There are two characters who will be etched into my sh*t list for the rest of time, those being: Mary the niece of ZZ, who at first seems to be a genuinely interesting character until her writing turns batsh*t crazy and she becomes a "lol isn't she so random" type of character. She'll say literally anything, which makes her dialogue mean nothing. Genuinely "the narwhal bacons at midnight" type drivel. And then PeePoo, the robot that trains Knife, your pilot. Do you think the word Pee is funny? Well then you're in luck, as this character will say this a million f*cking times. You see he's comic relief, and his programming won't let him swear, so he says Pee instead of a swear. If you liked that, don't worry, that is his entire dialogue for the rest of the game, with some hackneyed "silence meatbag" trite garbage thrown in for good measure. Every single character besides Shade, Mary, and PeePoo are brilliant, vibrant characters that are brought down so far by association with these three bones hidden in this game's meal.This game is like a crossbreed between a siren and hydra. It draws you in with fun gameplay, cool mechanics, stellar voice acting, and incredible characters, and then suffocates you in bullsh*t. For every good joke there's 5 bad ones, for every fun fight there's an hour of tedium, for every genuinely sick character there's a gigantic segment of Shade wallowing in self pity, or PeePoo doing his tried and true one and only joke over and over and OVER AND OVER AND OVER. I cannot over-emphasize how f*cking sick I got of that one grating joke, sprinkled in between genuinely great writing, just enough sour the taste of the whole thing, it's that prevalent, and that annoying.And here we are, at the end of my inane ramblings. I wouldn't get so worked up about this if there wasn't something truly great hidden in here. It's just hidden pretty deep. This game truly had one of the worst endings I've ever seen. The entire game you're strung along with the promise of answers just around the corner, and in the end you're left with the answer to only one question, and it's so stupid you wish they didn't even bother giving it to you. This game is so close to being truly great, but it falls short in so many ways. Genuinely, as a retrosepective, I give this game a 2/10. If you asked me 10 hours in I would've given it a 8, maybe a 9. It falls off hard, and it never delivers on what it promises.If I had to describe this game in one word, it would be: Disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real mixed bag. Some great art, great music, decent voice acting, some interesting bot building/combat mechanics. There's a good sense of progression through earning currency and building up your bot and making design choices.Unfortunately, the writing for this game is miserable. The story is mostly just Cowboy Bebop as ordered from Wish™ or Temu™- a ragtag band of miscreants are broke and try to raise money. But the characters lack any sort of defining or interesting characteristics, they're all just generic anime tropes. You've got the mysterious broody guy, who isn't interesting enough to care about his mystery or why he's brooding, the energetic young femme type, who's an extremely poor fill-in for Radical Edward. The tough grumbling old man who just wants to get the job done. But they're all missing the uniqueness to their presentation and stories that makes those characters so good. And the addition to the crew is an absolutely intolerable robot, who's only gimmick is screaming PEE and POO and PEEPOO throughout every line of dialogue. I've played about 16 hours of this game, and that character alone made me start skipping the voice overs. And he talks A LOT. I've usually got a strong tolerance for 'annoying' characters, but this one in particular is so constantly present and annoying that it's made me stop playing the game. I've stopped playing for a couple of months to give it some space and see if I could come back to the game to finish it out, but honestly between the dry narrative that feels imitative of a pile of good anime without doing any work to make it unique or stand out, and "PEEPOOPEEPOO PEEEEEEEEEEE!!!!!" Defining what this game thinks humor is, I can't even bring myself back to barrel through it.A lot of heart here, a lot of good art, interesting mechanics, silly mini-games (even if the game design does lead to lot of aimless wandering)... Just having a completely generic story take up a lot of your gameplay time, and then bogged down by functionally a screaming child every other line of dialogue means that it's hard for me to recommend this to anyone over the age of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride is the perfect game for a young male teenager, whose maybe struggling with depression, and isn't sure how to deal with it in a culture where men aren't as allowed to talk about feelings.  However I'm a trans female 20 year old, who has not, in fact, struggled with depression, or caring about my masculinity.Wolfstride is a mixture of minigames, interspersed with fun mech combat.  It has some of the best voice work in a video game since Night of the Full Moon or Hades, and a good story to go along with it too.  The biggest flaw, and what kind of spoiled the whole game for me, is it's Pineapple system, of giving people pineapples to advance your relationship with them.  So, wanting to complete all my relationships, I had to absolutely Grind SO MANY MINIGAMES, to get enough pineapples.  And I didn't even get anything good for getting them completed.  So, so long as you don't do what I did, you'll have a good time.That all said, I can't understate how important this game could be for a young guy trying to make sense of himself and his masculinity.  It's a game which very much addresses and discusses masculinity, what makes it appealing, why toxic masculinity can be harmful, and how to find a healthy way to be masculine.  It also talks about the unique ways depression and masculinity, which is refreshingly unique.  Again, most of these themes, don't speak to me ~specifically~ very much, but it's so easy to imagine someone who'd love this game.Altogether, Wolfstride is a fun game about mechs punching each other, the broken men who pilot them, going on goofy adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you play a game or watch a show and you can tell the people who worked on it loved making it? Yeah.As a fake persona fan (the real ones never play the damn games), this game does an awesome job of taking the daily task + turn based combat formula, putting it into a good redemption story and making the whole thing fun and exciting all the way through. It's short (for a jrpg), but I think that's the perfect length for this kind of story, it never felt dragged out or hastened. Every single voice actor did a phenomenal job, honestly, I'd say voice acting in Wolfstride is up there if not even better at times with voice acting in shows like FMAB, Baccano or Cowboy Bebop. Crude jokes really help, but even so, the game does do a good job of balancing being serious with stupid fun. Also, stupidly fun, the OST is an absolute jammer.The combat has some cool moments, though I do think it could be a bit more difficult at times, the big importance in this game is preparing the mech and the pilot instead of actually executing tactics, but some people do prefer it to be that way. The gameplay overall is pretty simple, as for me I like it, I really prefer focusing on the narrative, characters and story in the media, but if you're looking for a Tengen Toppa Titan Fall 2 then you'll be disappointed. Although I would still say that although the gameplay isn't revolutionary, the developers knew what they needed to get it to do and they did a solid job on it. Plus, simplistic gameplay works well for the slice of life type of world it achieves, at least for the most part.The Art style really makes this game work. The grayscale works for the tone, the characters are expressive, some cutscene shots are just so phenomenal I feel like I need to invest in a thesaurus so I could stop reusing the same words. If you like games with a focus on how they convey the story, like gameplay that isn't too complex or experimental but knows what it's doing, and some awesome music, artwork and voice acting to make the plot work even better than it already has, you're gonna have a good time with Wolfstride.I have been gifted this game by a friend, but I will definitely buy the OST and the Art collection, now that I have finished the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but Wolfstride is, hard for me to describe. One the one hand it wants to be a visual novel lite, with rock'em sock'em robots thrown in. It has glaring issue that need to be buffed out, but from the discussion board it looks like mileage may vary. So I guess the good, Voice Acting is decent enough and the visuals do their part. There's a okay story in here, but sadly it is buried under the slow grind and pacing that it may turn a lot of people away.I want to add more positives, but so far that's about it. I will admit I haven't completed the game, but will do so. Once completed I'll come back to update if there's more to add. So there's a relationship system, that's fine and all, but it's increased through pineapples. Look I like pineapple and all, but if someone dumped as much pineapple as Shade does upon me I would get a restraining order on the man. To note, pineapples seem to be rare in the Wolfstride world and this dude is finding them left and right. I'd be questioning how he acquired them. Also, you get them out of a trash heap. Yes, there's Bounty's Hog Yard which is a trash yard. Shade is passing these out to people, the heck is wrong with this man. The big issue is pineapples are hard to get, but there are mini games that give them more than others. Which ties into the other issue I'll get into, but lets wrap up the relationship system. So each level you level up one of the many characters they'll give you useful items(sometimes). Though once you hit max level(level 7) that's it. I feel like the Persona games felt more rewarding, in Wolfstride it just end and is never brought up again. Like I just busted my butt to get you these rare fruits and once done that's it?So Pineapple god dude implores you and once done just throws you to the waste side. No thanks for helping spreading the magic of pineapple to the people. No reward from him once so ever. I like to tell this dude where to stick the pineapples. Anyway, the system become moot once each character is maxed out. Which I finish doing by like day 28. Which now we can talk briefly about the mini games.So certain locations have mini games and you can't get the highest rewards until you get certain items that help you do so. At least that what it should do, but the time and button sequence for the cat bathing game feels impossible to wash all 26 cats, even with the item upgrade you get. I'm sorry I don't use and Xbox controller and use a PS5, but it's kind of hard to press B when it's X on the PS5. Please have mutiple controller support. Yes, my memory suck and visual add would've help by having the button match the controller I'm using, but this is a personal issue. Though, the Dev could've made a little effort to have more then one controller supports for mapping.Then there's the BDSM bike mini game, now I couldn't even get more then just money from it. I couldn't get the first reward box even with all the upgrades. It's literately sitting a hair breath under the line for the first one. So unless there's more upgrades further down the road this mini game is also unable to get everything. The two that are by far the best are in Hog's Yard and with the upgrade very doable. Which I just focused on Junk hunt and Junk Mining for the time I was grinding for pineapples.Now here's the issue with the mini games, once you maxed out everyones level with pineapples, they become moot. Why? Because, you've gotten so much damn money you don't need to do them anymore. By this time I was take very little to no damage that even needing money to repair my bot became moot. I've bought or was given all the upgrade up to this point. Bought everything at Paradise Arcade. Bought Everything at the convenient store(with the rare exception it gets restocked for story purpose). I have over 150k+, why we need to do life risking robot battles again?So there's a VR game that allows you to have back to back robot battles and I got all the prizes at day 33. The only challenge I find completely RNG and unbalanced was Mongoose. Which will move into my next talking point, mech battles, but first, Fudge this fight. He literately gets like 3-4 attacks per turn, has an attack that can push you from one end to the other end of the arena squares, and undoes all your puny damage like you've done nothing at all. Oh, lets not forget the attack that allows him to speed from one end to the other after he knocks you back. How I beat him came down to sheer RNG and luck.So onto mech combat, you get AP(Action Points) and MP(Movement Points) the more MP you have over your opponent allows you to go first. So here's the balance issue I see, most of the opponents you fight have not only high damage with armor reduction, but it cost them as little as 1 AP to use. While most of you decent attack have high AP, High Ammo cost, poor range, cool downs, and crap damage. I'm sorry I'm barely do without moral boost with a 2AP, 2 Ammo, and cool down 40-60 damage and these guys are getting crazy attack that I don't see require any cool down and 1 AP for 45+. Maybe I suck at the combat system, but even when I do win I notice how garbage Knife Leopard's attack skills are. How in the heck has he managed anything. Even with all the skills bought up to the point I'm at(just now entering the underground), its been a slog. Not to mention you don't get enough recovery. I get maybe 1 recovery every other round, but my opponent has like 2-4 after just 1. How unbalanced is this? Like challenge is fine, but I feel so damn handicapped at times it makes me not want to complete the game. Yet, I expect the fights in the underground to be even more one-sided. I've read people complain it's, "Too easy and didn't even break a sweat." Well hold on there mister masochist who probably chews up and spits out Soul's games like they're childs play. Not ever gamer out there can be a dang perfect as you, okay. If you're so good why not tie one arm behind your back, blindfold yourself, and wear ear plugs. Maybe then games will sort of feel like a challenge. Seriously get tired of the, "Git Gud" attitude of people. I want to have fun playing a game, not be frustrated. If I want to deal with garbage I'll go outside and deal with real life.Anyway, sorry about that rant, but I know people on the internet will use that tired saying everytime someone has difficulty with a game. If the Dev makes another game like this I think having a challenge mode for those more interested in the story or heck, just having an issue beating a battle can change the difficulty. It's just sad to see game mechanics become moot. Area's at this point are empty and devoid of purpose, like the hospital. The location gets used once and it is never used again(to my current knowledge). The road that leads the hospital serves a little more purpose and there's a area you'll have cut scenes are and is used for the relationships, but beyond that; that's the only purpose it currently have. The Arcade is moot, which is sads as the Dev could've put possibly some mini games to win prizes, but it sole purpose, making money you don't need.The Crapyard(the S fell off) was cool, but ZZ generally loses her purpose, because you bought everything useful from her shop. Like, why do we need to get her every battle? Heck, I can't even pet the kitties, 26 cats and none pettable. Beyond an interesting story with helping her, I really having a hard time seeing why the main cast needs her. The general store has a Gacha machine, but beyond a box of information, no further interaction. Seriously, you put a Gacha machine in the game and I can't spend money on things? The heck is wrong with you. At least it give me some reason to come back to the general store over time. Anyway, guess I can't leave a though full review as I seem to hit a character limit for it. I hope the Dev fills in the world a little more in future games, the void and moot mechanics just leave things empty.

_childDocuments_.review: I try not to leave negative reviews. There's enough negativity to go around already. But after about 10 hours of Wolfstride, I think I'm ready to pack it in, and I'm really disappointed that I feel that way. I have a ridiculous amount of hours in BattleTech. And turn-based tactics games are my jam. You'd think a turn-based mech combat game would be perfect for me. And that's exactly what I thought I was getting when I played the Wolfstride demo. But the reality is that this game is more like a visual novel bloated with irritating characters, a needless story, and a collection of extraneous mini-games. It's almost as if the developers knew that there wasn't enough meat on the bones of the core gameplay and decided to punch it up with all kinds of other nonsense. The mech combat at the core of the game is solid, even if it gets extremely easy pretty quickly if you grind out expensive parts and pilot moves. And the visual style is exceptional. I have to give credit where it is due. But everything you're forced to engage with outside of the fights is just a slog, even if you attempt to skip every cutscene. 10 hours of entertainment for $15 is a pretty good deal, but considering the mech combat portion of the game was *maybe* a third of that, I can't recommend it. It's a real shame too. If there was more depth to the combat, and if it took center stage, the game could have been fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna wirte a super in-depth review about the game, but just know that I adore it. It was incredibly enjoyable to go through and it stayed on me mind for days on end when I wasn't playing. It's hard for me to get that feeling lately. Below I'mma list a bunch of flaws, don't take it as "i hate the game because of this" but rather "I love this game and wish these didn't marr it".I do have a handful of gripes with some stuff the game does, like not enough mech variety, progression being locked by story points (like, you get your last few upgrades when there're like a couple hours left) and LOTS of dead time. _childDocuments_.review: The vibes of Wolfstride are immaculate, and there is some potentially delicious meat on the bones of its combat system, but the opening hours do a surprising amount to stop you from getting to the good part.The opening days of the game are extensive fetch quests, running along long empty roads to and from locations to characters that are an equal split of charming pastiches of classic anime characters, and some persistently unfunny characters that threaten to never stray from their 'bit'.There's a robot named 'Peepoo' with an intentionally screeching voice that replaces random words in their dialogue with 'pee' or 'poo' like a Smurf. They're also set up to be a persistent member of the main cast. This is probably 'the joke' of the character, but it's just not funny or pleasant, just loud.You do get a carrot dangled in front of you - introductory combats are fun and tactical and the next one feels like it's *just* around the corner, but there's more fetch quests and Peepoo to bear before you get there. I took a break from the game at the introduction of an Elite Four of characterful silhouettes that would have me Pokémon-playing, Tournament Arc-watching, No More Heroes-loving butt absolutely thrilled. But there was just no real guarantee that their writing would be any more engaging than Peepoo and I... just couldn't bring myself to come back to it.If you're an old-school anime fan with a taste for Rick & Morty or Family Guy at their more puerile moments you'll get along with Wolfstride solidly. I'd still recommend playing with the voice acting off.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wolfstride" is a RPG/Anime-Visual-Novel set in an alternative present where mech-fighting-sport is a thing. You take on the role of Dominic Shade - a former mobster - who got entangled in shady business and struggles with a ragtag cast of characters to get some cash and get even with their pasts. The game focuses heavily on storytelling and it delivers. The writing is consistent, sometimes good, even very good, but some jokes are hit and miss and things can drag into cringe-worthy territory (There are a LOT of pop-cultural references - to anime in general, "Cowboy Bepop" in particular, a lot of side notes to bands like "Ween" and "Beck" and serveral game franchises - some are implemented quite good, some not so well). The visual art and character design is top notch,  the pixel art still delivers, but is not that fleshed out in my opinion. Some places and scenes also feel empty and rushed, but the overall atmosphere manages to smooth this out. A big thumbs-up for the voice acting - almost everything is voiced and they did a great job! The game has a very slow pace in terms of gameplay: You socialize, prepare for the battles, are going places, talking to people and doing errands which are presented in mini-game-fashion (which can be offputting to some). There is also a lot of backtracking. The turn based mech-fights are fun, cinematic, original, strategic and intense, but the overall power progression and the balancing have a strange curve.Overall "Wolfstride" has its rough edges, but it is a quite unique experience and definetly a work of heart! A nice and hefty underdog package for everyone that likes a stylish piece of media!
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Hold onto your pants because I have a review as usual my friends, so as usual I'll do my short version, Wolfstride is a game I heard was a slowburn and ya know what? It's half right, the gameplay takes a sec to get to the actual good parts and meat of the game itself but characters? Story? If you're a lover of these things you'll be eating out of this games hands like a half starved dog ready for a full course meal and a heavy petting session, as a whole it does it mostly right and has very few real issues, definitely nothing game breaking that's for sure dood.Okay ya'all here? Good so on the surface Wolfstride is a comedic RPG mecha battle game strewn with a few fun minigames here and there, some of which are hilarious but ironically as much as I came to enjoy the combat the game has a veeeery strong story element, the humour is on point but it also cuts deep, real deep and takes it to places even I didn't expect it to, it had me wanting more and it always delivered, lot's of fully voiced lines at that, very rare exceptions to that and quite the diverse cast I might add in terms of how they all sounded dood.So I talked about the story and I did it first which is rare for me, shows how much I appreciated it but now let's get onto the gameplay, you typically have an arena with varying amounts of space between you and the other mech, each panel can have + or - attacks on them and if you push them to the back you can deadlock them, allowing you to go to town on them in terms of damage but of course they too have this ability making it a real push of war at times doodEach mech has four key parts, the head, both arms and the chest, all of which can have an armour stat to decrease damage of incoming attacks and of which with the right attacks can shred that armour, arms account for damage but also your attacks in general so losing one will take away an attack you may have, head I believe accounts for AP this is what allows you to attack often and chest? Chest is your life blood, you get that destroyed? It's game over, off to the junkyard dood!Of course there's actually more parts than just those outside of combat and a variety of pieces you can equip to your mech, wanna be a long range specialist? Here's parts with more ammo and better ranged damage, wanna be a melee god? here's parts with more damage and armour, the games got ya covered, there are also parts to improve movement and AP so you can go back and forth around the field like nobodies business and push more than ever which helps because that costs two movement points dood.So about combat and why it's slow at the start, as the game progresses you learn more and more attacks and skills, both defensive and offensive, at the start? You uhhh are quite frankly pathetic and that's being extra nice, you're gonna be in for a rough ride, but between the shop, minigames and certain side things you can do you can qui-well in a reasonable time make your mech a God among mechs but here's the hitch, you keep unlocking things as you go along so it's hard to judge when the best time for that is, I grinded out a very specific item to get some super good stuff but honestly? I should have done some of it later when I had more attacks dood.That said the game is not all that hard of you get the right parts and play smart, the hardest thing to start is limitations but eventually you'll be able to make each fight seem almost too easy as long as you aren't dumb enough to try and be too fancy in your tactics, the game will definitely punish you for that and yet despite that it get's quite fun and tactical to play with some fun little visuals for the attacks dood.Bad things about the game? Let's see there's a lot of walking and that would be fine but the issue is you never know what may be new in an area or not, to the devs I suggest maybe markers in each area if something new is there to find or someone has something new to say, I always wanted to find all the things and not miss out on them but it meant a loooot of walking, by the way you usually go everywhere and the only things you may miss are jukebox discs, no achievement for that either, you're welcome lol and anything else is usually in such plain site you'll not miss it so feel free to concentrate on conversations or even events at times dood.Final words? This game is different and in a lot of good ways, both story wise and gameplay wise, the mechanics are surprisingly deep once you've unlocked everything and I'd love to see more games done like this, especially if they do one in the future with the end segment, that's as much of a spoil as you'll get from me on that ;) could they do more? What game can't do more? But what's here? Is a game I won't be forgetting anytime soon and I'd love to see the devs do more of these kinds of games, it doesn't even have to be mechs or the same world but as long as the storywriting is as good and they took on board all the good of the game I would play the heck out of a new game! (On that note in case the devs read a post game would be a good idea for all the new moves I never really got to use as much as I'd have liked for future games if you keep this formula) Thank you for reading and I hope you enjoy the game as much as I did dood! ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride feels like it's an underrated gem, yet the reviews are very positive for it (this, of course, being another positive review to add to the pile).The gameplay is split into two parts: a No More Heroes-esk roam around the town and do odd jobs to get money to pay for mech parts and other items loop, and a turn based combat loop where each mech has (most of the time with a single-digit number of exceptions) four parts that allow the mech to do different kinds of offensive and/or defensive moves.What's kinda crazy is how the game melds 2d pixel art, really stylized non-2d art, and a (mostly) voice acted story with multiple characters (none of the voices are one person doing multiple voices from what I noticed).At first the story might not seem like it's worth seeing to the end, but it is.Oh, and choose the Black Door.

_childDocuments_.review: "What a piece of crap!"Story - absolutely fantasticArt direction - very goodEverything else - good to "wHy?"  As in: Why do the pineapple social links exist? Is it because Persona did it? Now is it? All it does is pad out playtime. Doesn't even give additional story content.  The previous point leads into the second one. Why are the minigames the only way to get half the damn pineapples or more? There are four of them and out of four of them only two are completed in reasonable time, making Hog your only helper on the grind. It still takes a stupid amount of time to complete, and you still have to pay attention the entire time. I wish I could just purchase pineapples 10k a pop.   And speaking of money, the aforementioned grind leaves you with heaps of cash so Why is arcade so damn pointless? You invest to get time-based income, but it is limited to 2k a day. Why??? You can make over 2k over 2 rounds of junk mining if you sell drops. So 2k are absolutely worthless.  Why do you need the pineapple grind if it ruins your monetary system, doesn't provide story content and demolishes story pacing for the completionists?   Mech combat is good, could be more dynamic, but the amount of changes that some fights provide is good enough.   Not nearly enough 1AP moves worth using, not enough moves that aren't a pain in the ass to set up, no melee armor breaking attacks which locks you into having to keep at least some gun attacks + reload.  Head is not worth going for most of the time.  Basement is disappointing despite providing the best parts, simply because it is so short and doesn't impact the story at all.  Also most mechs are missing one of their legs, and it would be fine if we were not able to see it, game devs don't need to draw things that the players can't see, but it is very clearly visible and distracting. Give Trinket and Killer their own game, it seems like what they were doing in the background was interesting enough.Recommended to everyone

You have to walk around everywhere. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty damn great, but horribly pacing in the beginning is basically catastrophic. Tip below to get past the beginnning then proper review.Tip: Just speedrun the first 10 days, do your tasks and all that and remember that the first 2 fights are plot fights instead of real ones, but just try and get to day 9 or 10 when the game opens up a lot more, cause that's when it starts to actually feel good instead of drag on, plus Junk Hunt gives plenty of money if you want to grind it, so don't worry at all about the biking minigame, and no from the start you can't make it to the end of the minigame.Note: I'm at end of act 3 of the game as of writing (having 24 hours in at that point isn't that showing of how long the game is. I just really liked the mech combat so did a ton of that, and did a lot of money grinding. That doesn't effect my discussion on the pacing though as most of my money grinding was after the first 10 days where the pacing is horrible)Now for the proper review: Art: Clearly its pretty incredible. Probably the best part of the game. It makes having to walk through many areas a lot better, and it definitely leaves a nice atmosphere. (but the game could still use fast travel past the inbetween streets)Characters: This is  so far to me the 2nd best part of the game. Early on the dialogue is pretty cringey with overreliance on basic swearing and toilet level humor. Especially the introduction of fifth member of the crew: , but with time the characters started to show more, and their personality really start to connect with you. There are side characters of clearly lesser importance but they can be fun and the main cast for the most part are really fun to hang out with and talk to. The game can also get really silly too, but when not using toilet level humor it can be really funny and charming.Music: It's pretty good I'd say. It may not always be my taste, but I can see people really liking it. I don't have the know how to go any deeper than that.Gameplay: Walking and Talking - it's pretty standard and alright. The biggest annoyance is that the character has a changing direction left or right bit of art that pauses instead of automatically taking them to the other direction. It just feels unnecessarily slow and is a bit annoying for the Junk Hunt mini game. The in-between streets while atmospheric and have some fun descriptions, can be grating to walk through after a while and no descriptions update. A fast travel would have been great after a few times through.Gameplay: Mech Combat - this part feels great. Sadly buying new parts doesn't give much aesthetic difference, but it's still quite fun seeing small changes when mixing and matching moves. You have only so many squares left or right to move your mech, and have to position yourself to correctly use your weapons and have as much bonus damage as possible, and leave your enemy with as little as possible. Good combinations, strategies, and some special items let you beat enemies definitely stronger than you from quite early in the story. From acts 2-3ish you can defeat even some of the stronger later game enemies if you plan and work through it right. Sometimes it can be annoying dealing with stuff you haven't seen before since there's nothing to prepare you for it other than just losing, but soon enough you've seen enough to prepare for fights ahead. I personally think of the fights are better thought of as puzzles with when you haven't bought a ton or gotten a ton of items, you may not have tons of wiggle room. and when fighting things above your intended level you definitely have to think it through. It's incredibly satisfying though to see a good plan come to fruition.Starting Pacing: Its utterly horrible. There's a reason that this game only has half of its people go through the first act, and that probably goes towards whoever structured the first 10 days or so. It feels very slow meeting everyone, the biking game when its the ONLY way to get money and you don't know how much stuff will cost later, and only slowly having more and more options of what to do around the city. Not to to even mention the 2nd fight of the game is also not one you're meant to win for basically no reason other than you didn't have the ability to buy upgrades to your mech, nor did you have the ability to helpfully get info on the mech and plan around what it could do. (BTW: Mech info when given to me is honestly pretty useless with how shallow it is. It gives you the barest idea on what's to come. Knowing their moves and maybe getting a round or two to see their opening movement from x or y position would actually make enemy info feel useful at all. Or even the first part of that at the very least.) It's like they thought people would be willing to sit through a persona intro length, without knowing how many people dislike their long intros already, and how those who do like it (like even me) know enough with previous games to know that what comes ahead is worth it. But for a new game like this? It practically kills it and it's pretty clear to see with the low rate of getting past chapter 1. Just speed past the first 10 or so days as fast as you can to get to the real good stuff.Once you're past that though you're past what I feel to be so far is the worst part of the game, and the great parts of it really start to show itself. This game is ABSOLUTELY worth it, but it really makes it hard to see it from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Cant believe this isn't meta scored it deserves somewhere between 70 and 80. I prize this for the story line, characterisation and plot delivery. The art style and and turn based battle sequences are also very good, though ill avoid elaborating here for the sake of brevity. The main thing I want to mention is on the quality of the story and so on. The story revolves around misfit characters who have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up their lives and are now trapped in lively hood of scraping by, the main character shade has on openly troubled past that you're made aware pretty early on, and his past is given the proper attention it deserves. At first glance this game is humorous but underneath and especially when you get to the ending you realise that it covers very seriously the themes of suicide, life's hardship and the kind of general philosophical views that could be held by individuals contemplating suicide. The game will not have a dark and gloomy mood throughout most, so you will not realise this straight away. It will feel more like a faux-noir with slapstick and cheerful comedy. But that is precisely the brilliance of the game. The dialogue writing and the voice acting are both excellent and really pulls the whole thing together.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite interesting but unfortunately I can't recommend it. Pros:-Despite it being in black and white (for the most part) the characters are quite colorful. You get attached to them and want them to succeed.Cons:-The combat is poorly balanced. Even the final tournament was pretty easy-There's so many interesting plot points that could have been explored, but ultimately ends up going nowhere. This could have easily been avoided since there's a lot of "open" days throughout the game. Maybe they initially ran out of money and can correct this with DLC/updates.-The game relies to much on "and then things kinda happened" to push the main narrative along.-Due to a combination of the voice acting and writing, some of Shade's internal monologue is extremely pretentious and unnecessarily edgy. They went too hard on the tragic hero angle.-Why was the final mech fight with the Soviet even necessary? Previously the player had just fought the final boss that's been hyped up throughout the game. Then all of a sudden this guy shows up in an unwinnable fight. That's just bad story design.I know it seems like I listed a lot of Cons, and the game is definitely rough around the edges. It's still decently fun and very stylish. If you can get it on a deep sale then definitely go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rather interesting, and if you are a fan of older styles of turned base combat with some giant robot flare, this is the game for you. The game itself is short, but packs in a lot of character development for the main cast. Though the combat is simple, some fights you do have to work out what moves is best in slot for the match up. (However, if you intend to do everything and get all that you can before the end of the main story, there is a way to cheese the fights, but I won't say how.) Simply put, this is an enjoyable game and I kind of would like to see more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I learned of this game because I saw news that It'll come to the Switch. I purchased and binged the game since I got it. What I:-Loved is the non-pixelated art (like the mechs and character portraits). I have a bias to bold and thickly drawn art style. It's also noteworthy that almost all of the dialogue has good voice acting, which in my opinion, carried the game's narrative. Some dialogues are also funny, with some pop culture references added to the mix.-Likedis the combat. Though the animations tend to be repetitive at times.  The difficulty is a hit or miss IMO since I think I was able to focus in one style and it kinda carried me through the whole game. I only needed to upgrade parts if I find myself not being able to defeat enemies, so not much tactics were involved. I wish there were more animation and visual variety. -Hatedis that you needed to tediously walk ALL THE TIME if you want to go anywhere. In this game, you go through a menu to select a general area where you want to go, and walk 2 screens before you get to where you want. With the limited locations the game has, it's tedious to see the same scene time and time again, without anything happening. I don't see the reason why another menu was not used for it. While I don't pay attention to the story that much, the ending is kinda confusing as well.Summary:Game looks good with great ideas for it's game play. It's not the best game, but for the price I paid, I am satisfied. Should this get a sequel, it's probably a day-1 purchase for me. I totally agree with one of the reviews that said: “Wolfstride is an obvious labor of love that manages to be much more than the sum of its gameplay and presentation parts.”

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks. From it's aesthetic, to it's gameplay, to it's writing. Yes, there are some typos and grammatical errors in the text - That aside a lot of the writing doesn't feel forced,  and with it being 95% voiced,  this game proved to be an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gem.The story is great, from wacky moments - to /some/ cringe moments (Looking at the introduction to PeePoo) - to some genuinely unexpected twists and banging storytelling.If you have 15 dollars, buy this game. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: To me, this is more of a Visual Novel than an RPG, and it's a fun ride if you're looking for a story. As the mech fights can devolve into a one-sided beatdown in your favor the moment you unlock some stuff. My biggest gripes are how time consuming traveling is, and how there's no indication for new dialogue in zones.If you're looking for an RPG experience, you're probably not going to find what you want here. But I truly feel the writing is what carries the experience, so if you're looking for a story, you might like what you get here.And for the love of God, don't try to unlock everything. The story is linear, grinding minigames for all the unlocks will not change the ending. Spending 1-2 minutes per minigame for a chance of getting an item to progress bonus unlocks is not worth your time when it doesn't affect the story.----I absolutely adore this game. I rock with the aesthetic, the writing is fun, and the voice acting really brought the script to life. To me, the game is more of a Visual Novel about mech fighting and the RPG is secondary to that. As in my playthrough, which had some early minigame grinding so I could see some unlocks, simply keeping your mech parts "up to date" and figuring out a rotation for combat resulted in the endgame fights being filler for the story.But of course, there are things that I didn't like. Like how there's no fast travel between the major zones, or anything that tells me that there's new dialog in an area (as I feel the writing is the big highlight of the game). When you're traveling around, a one-way trip is like this:1. Menu2. Area3. "Hallway"4. Arrive at your destination, NPC you're looking for might be on the complete other side of the areaSo if you're doing daily rounds to see if anybody has anything new to say, it takes a good couple minutes just running around. And at certain points, some characters either just repeat the same dialogue, or just have no dialogue whatsoever, making checking on them a waste of time. And in the endgame, if you're doing a certain side thing, it'll take you A LOT of walking just to repair your mech between fights.Also, the minigames are your primary source of Pineapples, which are used to improve your relations with certain characters, and unlock bonus items which make minigames easier, new moves, and parts. You honestly don't need to grind for too many, and I highly advise you don't. Either I can't figure out their drop rate, or my luck is just that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Being someone who played their fair share of Mecha Flash games growing up, I have to say that Wolfstride ended up being a wonderful sub-20 hour experience. a. Story & Characters: One that needs time to growWhilst some of the characters are initially rather off-putting (looking at you Mr Tiny Robot), I found that over the course of the game that many of their characters arcs turned out to be rather quite satisfying - if a bit unresolved by the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Story - 9/10A pretty good-written story with some twists. The side plotlines are a bit cut in my opinion.Visuals - 9/10Nice simple style, very high quality.  Though some parts are missing - many scenes lack close-up faces, mostly in the 2nd half of the game.Gameplay - 7/10The battles are...me(c)h. I mean, if your objective is to specifically not hit the torso and the target does not hide behind a shield, it is pretty straightforward. Still fun to see how characters interact during the fight.The mini-games are sort of dull and for their quality I would expect more quantity, at least in the next part.The visual novel/travelling part was the most annoying though. _childDocuments_.review: The game took just about 22 hours to beat and I did pretty much everything, I'm only missing 2 achievements and one of them is grinding the battlepass in the in-game video game to max.It is very very heavily story focused, everything and everyone is voice acted. The mecha battles are mandated by story progression, not a freeform tournament or anything you go through at your own pace.The writing and the voice work is quite good for every character and that's really the main focus, though there are a few eye-rolling moments when things get a bit too emo or edgy. Even the robot who has a stupid high pitched voice and says PEEEEE as a censor, grew on me by the end. The "real" story is only told in tiny bits and pieces with foreshadowing until the very very end, you're really here for the characters and their journey through this mecha tournament, with the backstories of everyone as a side focus, I feel like. The battle system is pretty simple but engaging enough, but once you get the hang of it the story battles are never challenging. After each story battle you have a chance to go grind for money to buy the best parts for your mech if you feel like it, probably so you cant get stuck.You can target specific body parts of your opponents to disable their attacks using that part and move left/right in a line grid battlefield. Getting your opponent (or yourself) locked in the corner gives a damage buff.There's 2 sets of optional challenge fights you can do that can be tough depending on how well equipped you are at the time, but once you're geared and have a good basic strategy they aren't that hard either.The art is really nice when its there, for character portraits or mechs with the occasional full screen art piece. Otherwise most everything is done in pretty simple pixel art.I was expecting it to have some super robot anime tropes where there's some grand power up or world changing event (ala Gurren Lagann and such) but honestly it stays very grounded.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: It's a VN on the most part. With additional mini-games and JRPG style turn-based mecha combat. Weebs and mecha fans will find a lot of references and easter eggs.Plot is all over the place yet fits comedy/parody style with some drama inserts almost perfectly. A lot is going on simultaneously, political struggle of superpowers unleashes in background, subplots (sometime ridiculous) develop in your town while you are just trying to make ends meet and fix/upgrade your mech for the next fight. Devs left a lot of loose ends so sequel seems quite possible.Humour and jokes vary especially from character to character so I think everyone will find something to laugh at.Voice acting is quite solid though I think they overact at some TEH DRAMA points but it's quite subjective.The biggest fault: grindy as hell and a lot of running around the town map that simply wastes time and annoys. But maybe it's just my play style of searching every nook and cranny.Overall: recommended to mecha/VN/turn-based combat lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: How to make a cool game with anime qualities - Take mechas & a bit of over-the-top artstyle from Tengen toppa Gurren Lagann, mix in a dash of strong characters with interesting backstories from something like Cowboy Bebop, pepper it with strong language, then wrap it up in basic premise from Redline to kick off the story.AND YOU HAVE A WINNER LADIES AND GENTLEMEN!I cannot stress enough how much I enjoyed this game. The main turn-based combat system is fun, it is nicely animated to convey the brutal oil-spilling action, and it feels great to slowly upgrade your mecha. The minigames are a nice distraction. The music is just brilliant and often I would just chill in the hangar, enjoying the atmosphere. But the well written, fully voiced (SO DAMN WELL VOICED) characters and great story really made this one of my instant all time favourite games.My only complaint would be too much unnecessary running around the city, looking for new events at every location, EVERY DAY. Often I would run all the way somewhere to find that nothing has changed from the day before. But still, it was all worth it for me in the end.Now... I just sit here with a void in my heart after finishing the game, wishing for more. Best mark of quality in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: As Ota Imon Studio's debut game, they absolutely knocked it out of the ball park.Wolfstride is an indie masterpiece, filled with gorgeous art, colorful characters, and a great story to wrap it all up. At its core, it's a story-rich linear narrative game with mecha fights sprinkled along the way. Characters have unique and humorous personalities, and the voice acting is superb. The story is over-the-top dramatic and the game is very self-aware about it. There will be small subplots you can piece together over the course of the game by visiting locations often, but its mostly "hidden" dialogue and have no huge impact on the main story. The game is separated into days, and new events can occur on every day minus Free Roam days, where you can do whatever you want. The fighting aspect of the game is great! you maneuver around a battlefield separated into sections with buffs and debuffs to your damage. There are a huge variety of mecha to fight against, although the COWBOY will be your only ride throughout the game, as it is central to the story. New parts make your mecha stronger, watching movies gives your pilot new stances (gives bonuses doing certain actions, like blocking, pushing, etc), and your trainer robot can sell you new moves. Of course, upgrading your mecha will cost money. While winning fights does pay prize money, most of your cash will be earned grinding out short minigames scattered throughout Rain City. if you over prepare and grind way too much cash, it might get boring, but in my experience I never really had to grind that much. Some minor nitpicks:-large amounts of backtracking, visiting old locations. Can't be helped since Rain City is a pretty small place.-minor bugs that the developers will no doubt patch in the future. -For those looking for a pure mecha brawler turn based strategy game, sometimes that aspect takes a backseat compared to the main story. However, later unlocks in the game allows you to do just that with non stop battles. -Some humor is a hit or miss depending on the audience. I enjoyed it because I didn't take it too seriously, but other people might find it way too dramatic.Game length is about 20 hours or so give or take.For the price this game is at and the amount of love the devs fit in its little 3.4ish gigabyte body, this is a steal. Definitely check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic turn based strategy game. Classic anime style artwork. A unique style of combat with many different strategies. The story is deep and developed, and you can tell the developers put a lot of effort into this game.If I had to rate this game I would give it 10/10.Seriously, if you like turn based combat, this is THE game to play.

Honestly I was initially put off by the trailer, something about it just didn't vibe well with me.As I'm sure you can tell by my play time, it has done anything but put me off. I adore this game. _childDocuments_.review: So I just completed what I believe is a 100% playthrough (all achievements at least) and I enjoyed the game for the most part.Pros:-Mech battle system is very fun. I enjoyed the positioning mechanics, and it felt like a great medium for storytelling.-Characters are enjoyable. There are many archetype subversions that I found enjoyable. (looking at you Oyabun and Boss Hog)-Artistically very fun. Black and white worked. Shockingly well. Pixel art + fleshed out portraits was great.Cons:-Battle system feels unfinished. There's a very clear way to build a mech, and deviating from that will meet you with disappointment. I'd love to have changed my mech for who I was fighting, but doing that only seemed to make my mech weaker compared to a generalist build.-Not enough parts for the mech. I felt like I got no real new options past day 30ish, which is roughly the halfway point. That was kinda a bummer.-Stances and a fair amount of systems are a bit unbalanced.-Pineapples? I'm still not 100% sure if they change the story or not, but they felt kinda pointless. I was hoping for more bonus dialogue, or something for getting everyone all the pineapples. They kinda just give things to make jobs easier.-Ending felt bad. Without giving any spoilers, the narrative ended up feeling circular and counter to the growth moral the rest of the story pushes.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth a playthrough if you like mechs, or you like story.The Story - It could be a little cringey/corny at times but overall I loved it. It took some time getting used to how quick the tone shifts and the story's focus changing but after a while I got used to it.Voice actors - The voices were awesome. They did an amazing job. Enough said.Gameplay - Gameplay was split into 3 sections: Overworld, minigames, and mech battles. Overworld: It reminded me of the later persona games with you wandering around and talking to npcs. So if you know how those are, you get the idea.Minigames: These were quick and easy ways to get some cash and earn some new parts (after a while you do outpeform anything you can be given from these but they are easy cash so big deal). There were 4 major minigames that I remember. When you play them you need to learn them on the fly (they give you very little warning when they start). But you can repeat them as much as you want with no downside.Mech battles: These are similar to fencing, with both mechs on a line. Depending on where you are on the line, you can get bonuses or penalties to attacks (simple plus or minus damage values). You have 4 options to you during combat: movement, attack, defense, and one thats a bit of spoilers so you'll have to play to see. Theres some more stuff I could go into but if you like any of this, give it a try. You won't regret it.TLDR: Games good, play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: The game is better than the demo. Full voice acting by folks with chops, a soundtrack with longer cues, a great script that paces things out way more than back-to-back fights - it's a big step up.This is a fantastic game being held back by some rough edges. While art, music, writing and animation are all good to great... in order to go somewhere, you have to walk through a street zone before reaching the real zone. There is nothing to do in this street zone and it doesn't seem to change. Good for mood? Maybe? It's hard not to read this as padding out the game length.You're able to go to a hospital at any time. So you head that way and you walk aalllll the way down the street. Then your protag helpfully says "there's nothing to do there". And you walk aaallll the way back. You can talk to people, but you can't tell if you're about to listen to a new conversation or hear an older one repeated. You can go anywhere, but your protag has ideas about where to go first, and won't tell you what they are until you're halfway there. There's a lot of time being wasted here. It feels like this game should have been a visual novel but really, really wanted to be No More Heroes, tried to pull it off on a more modest budget, and was ultimately hurt by the attempt.Again, I want to stress, I do recommend this game. It has a lot going for it! Get in there! I just wish they'd taken a hard look at some elements in those final editing passes.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best experiences I had with indie games this year, an easy 9/10 and the developers of this game should be proud of what they made it.Incredible Artstyle and just style in general.10/10 voice action and really surprised me with how much of this game was voice acted, I really can't think of anything in the game that is not voiced, from random conversation or background NPC, everyone has a voice that fits and its well performance.Really fun combat, just wish the last couple fights in the story itself was a little harder. Of the final 4-5 gauntlet fights I was able to win 3 of the on the first turn and another on the second, but the fight with queen took some more time and it was really fun.Biggest problem with the game was probable the amount of time you spend walking around, I feel like you could had cut the screen you had to talk before you reach your destination and it would had being fine, hell I would even make the second screen shorter and disable the running to compensate, or maybe its just my love for the walking animation talking, really the walking animation looked really good.Aside from that there was some small thing I would change like how some transitions from scene to scene were just the game going to black and all the sound cutting, a little jarring where you just finish a sad/important scene and don't really had time to absorb it.Also, some bugs and softlock, but I'm sure the developers of this game love their project and are going to patch it.But anyway, this game could probably cost more than double and I would still give it high praise and say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn does this game makes an entrance. I am at work right now, but I stayed up till almost 4 am just so I could play this a little longer and I haven't been more excited to go back and play a game in a while. I will update my review when i get farther in the game, but I felt it deserved a thumbs up already.The love child of Cowboy Bebop, Gurran Leggan, and Red Line. This game oozes style and personality. Every character is rich with charm and I have really enjoyed the pacing. Some people might find it slow (in the first few hours there is only three fights, but honestly I really liked that. When a fight happens, it feels epic because its been built up through the story)The music is on par, the voice acting is really good, and I don't even have to mention the art direction but I am constantly baffled by how cool and unique each new character I meet looks. They also each have several portrait drawn for their different emotions, some of which completely changes their entire look and its awesome.It really is a time to be alive, seeing so many games that are influenced by anime, but aren't actually anime, which allows them avoid tropes and put new spins on things. I HIGHLY recommend this game.

At this point if it was just a pure VN I'd probably dig it, just because the atmosphere, the animations, the voice acting...they've just nailed it.I hope for the continued success of this production group, because the talent and creativity they've shown here is sorely lacking in many creators today. Just sick stuff boys, keep it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game that outright shows how much care was put into it. Nearly all lines are voiced, animations for characters do show their general vibe, music that is catchy and fitting to the scenes. Great balance of story and actual game elements makes it more than just a visual novel. Both the character portrait art and the pixel art overworld are beautiful. Only negative thing I have to say about it is that there's a ton of running back and forth, with transition maps taking up a good chunk of time, they are nice, add to the atmosphere, but nth time running through a road to the bar and back from it with nothing really happening on the way does wear on the player a bit.tl;dr It's as if Redline met Megas XLR. Give it a chance to suck you in

If those tournament arcs were the hottest ♥♥♥♥, if you're a sucker for a good underdog story, then buy it now. Also consider getting the OST, it's pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: The consistency and precision with which this game hits its vibe is honestly ridiculous, every time I thought it couldn't evoke another reference or callback or hit that sweet 90s mecha style again it DID. The music, the visuals, the dialogue, all of it is so perfectly accurate to what I wanted after I played the demo. There are a few road bumps and flaws but overall a thoroughly enjoyable game.As I'm the type of person to look for the negatives in reviews more often than the positives, I'll list those here:- The "map" is a simple location selector, but in order to get to the main point of interest for each location you have to run through an extra street before actually arriving at the important part of the area. It can get a little annoying and repetitive.- I found the battles generally pretty easy, especially with how money becomes very easy to grind making it all the easier to have the best equipment available.- One particular resource is extremely grindy to get but essential to getting some of the best gear in the game.Once again, for effect, thoroughly enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, trash! So you need to give this baby some time, eh? The build-up will be slow and sometimes cheesy also tedious but maaaan, if you have the patience and will to survive the first few hours, that's where the real game begins... Once you can upgrade your Mech, your piloting skills, and have the option to fight virtual battles, the whole thing suddenly opens up. Too bad it took so long. - Traveling between locations is a slow and unnecessary process (which hurts the pace quite often), a fast travel option would have been very welcome. The mini-games are more funny and cheesy than entertaining or useful, but thankfully there aren't too many of them. - The story seems interesting, it's just as confusing and muddled as your regular anime storyline, but that's probably intentional. (And I'll probably update this section when I finished the game!). - The dialogue is mostly great, sometimes it is a little too "cool" and edgy for its own good, which hurts the otherwise quite nice character development arks. - The art design is amazing (and unique!), the music is excellent and the voice-acting is exceptionally good, although some of the recorded lines don't really match the facial expressions of the characters which can be off-putting.- The Mecha fight side of the game is solid and tactical, deep enough to really make you think, but not hardcore in difficulty, so you're unlikely to be stuck on a boss for too long and you won't need mathematical formulas to win.- For all its faults, this game has a real personality and a SOUL, which is perhaps the most important aspect, because all other "issues" are mostly a matter of taste, and most of them can be corrected with some fine-tunings, patches, updates, etc. So, again: Give this baby time and patience, because it will reward you with love, and you'll have a heck of a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: I never bother to write reviews, but this game is so good I have to make an exceptionThe artstyle (Both pixel art and detailed character art), writing and story is all superb. The voice acting is great and fits and makes the characters so much more enjoyable to listen too. One of the few RPG's where I don't actually skip dialogue as I read and instead just let it all play out.While some might not like the running around the game has you doing, it isn't that bad, and while it can feel like padding, events happen enough to always keep you interested. The actual combat is simple yet interesting with a good amount of tactics and thinking required.I don't really know what else to say other than, buy the game, play if for two hours, and if you aren't hooked by then, ask for a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review:
Wolfstride is a role-playing game about three former partners-in-crime coming to a turning point in their lives. When they inherit a junkyard mecha called Cowboy, they reunite to enter the planet's most elite mecha competition: the Ultimate Golden God Tournament.

Each member of the team lends their unique experience as they prepare to outwit the best mecha opponents from around the world. Between dog-mechanic Duque, mecha pilot Knife Leopard, and jack-of-all-trades Dominique Shade, the core crew's got just about everything covered.

That is... until their simple mission to make money unfolds into a deep, slow-burning exploration of their complex lives, the dark choices of their past, and their inevitable fate

name: Stray
detailed_description: Lost, alone and separated from family, a stray cat must untangle an ancient mystery to escape a long-forgotten city. Stray is a third-person cat adventure game set amidst the detailed, neon-lit alleys of a decaying cybercity and the murky environments of its seedy underbelly. Roam surroundings high and low, defend against unforeseen threats and solve the mysteries of this unwelcoming place inhabited by curious droids and dangerous creatures. See the world through the eyes of a cat and interact with the environment in playful ways. Be stealthy, nimble, silly, and sometimes as annoying as possible with the strange inhabitants of this mysterious world. Along the way, the cat befriends a small flying drone, known only as B-12. With the help of this newfound companion, the duo must find a way out. Stray is developed by BlueTwelve Studio, a small team from the south of France mostly made up of cats and a handful of humans.
