_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a game whose idea is much better than the implementation. If you just see "cyberpunk" and "cats" and buy the game - like I did - you might be expecting something a bit more than than this is. This isn't Deus Ex seen through the eyes of a street kittie. This is more of a janky indie linear narrative that features elements of better games and doesn't really nail any of them.The controls are the first thing you'll notice sucking. For a cat, you move very clumsily. The things you are are allowed to jump on are very limited and only appear as jumpable on certain angles, which makes navigating an exercise in futzing around with the camera till the magical jump icon appears. So you think you're gonna get parkour, but it's parkour minus the joyous, free movement of Mirror's Edge.Then you think maybe you're gonna get a relaxing walking sim, which you do get for about 10 minutes, until suddenly you are chased by swarms of facehuggers that hatch from glowing eggs AND KILL YOU. Yes, this game features death mechanics and checkpoints. No difficulty slider as far as I can determine, so you just have to die and repeat and die and repeat until you eventually pick the path with the least aliens and make it to another checkpoint. Extremely frustrating. I almost rage quit a couple of times.Later in the game you pick up a weapon that allows you fight back, but that turns it into even more of a gross-out, ultra-violent splatter-fest than it already was. Weird. Then you clear the bugs and get the obligatory stealth game section, hiding or running from drones THAT KILL YOU. And because the controls are so twitchy, all of these die and repeat sections are far more irritating than they should be.Meanwhile the story is sweet but predictable. You're not walking around a heavily-populated cyberpunk city. It's just two or three neighborhoods in an empty post-apocalypse world with a handful of characters in each one. There are a couple of meaningless collectables, but mostly you're just following signs to fetch the next item and unlock the next door. There is no big reveal, no character arcs, you know exactly what is going to happen from the start.And probably if I'd read some of the reviews before blindly buying because "cats" and "cyberpunk" I would've had lower expectations. Or maybe not, since the reviews are mostly meme reviews that don't tell you anything about the actual game. It's not a bad game. It's fine. It's passable. But is it worth the price? There are cheaper indie games and cheaper classic GOTYs that provide a better story, better parkour, better stealth, better everything... except you don't get to be a cat. So unless you really, really want to be a cat, wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I guess cats are great, but I just don't mesh with this game. I dislike pretty much everything about the gameplay: camera position, navigation, puzzles, stealth missions... And the story isn't anything I haven't seen a million times before. Only with a cat. The problem with the cat, however, is that I don't see WHY does it behave like a sentient being. So, it fell into some strange underground world. A normal cat would either die or adjust and live there, it would not seek Outside. Why is our cat hero different? The game provides no answer. It's a normal cat, otherwise, but it sure has strange motivations...Anyway, I had very little fun with this title. Possibly not because it's bad, but because it's not a genre I like. But still a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute.  It's weird.  It's sometimes heartwrenching.  Yes, it's a short game.  But it's not about the length of the experience, it's about the experience.  And from the moment you get out of the intro...and you'll know it when that happens...you're going to be so hooked on the story of this adorable little catto's journey that you won't want to stop until you see where it goes.  And then you can replay it and go for the goofy achievements.  There's one for sleeping an hour (yes, real time) in game.  Peak feline experience.Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the year.EDIT : Finished the game, I'll stand by it. Bold choices all around; a shorter adventure, simple but powerful characters and events (should give a lesson to the "character building" clique, sometimes less is more), casual - in a good way - gameplay and puzzles that don't require a walkthrough  to solve, atmospheric music and setting . Price is fine too.My congratulations to the team for their hard work.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed with this game.I love cats and lived with many different cats in my life, each with its own personality, from lazy fat apartment cats to semi-feral very energic cats that are used to hunting. Maybe I was expecting a cat more in like with the later, given the implications of being a stray cat in the apocalyptic wasteland.Thus, I miss being able to sprint much faster in small bursts of energy: in the game, I run for my life from zurks like a playful kitty running from mommy, not like a crazed cat who, at 2 AM, saw a ghost and is doing ninja wall jumps at 12 m/s.I miss the ability to hiss and growl, stand on my side facing forward and erect my spine and tail fur to appear bigger to intimidate the zurks.I miss the ability to violently fight back when overwhelmed by zurks, and the ability to kill them with my claws and fangs when one caught wandering alone. I mean 10 zurks are trouble for a cat, but 2 or 3 should not be.I wanted to be able to lurk unnoticed behind a zurk, shake my butt and stealth pounce kill.I understand the this would make it a different kind of game, at least in the action sections, but when it was announce I would play as a cat, I expected to be able to play with one of nature's deadliest predators.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is definitely a lot better than I expected it to be. The environments are extremely detailed and really nice to explore. The characters are interesting and fairly unique too. The main cat in the game is also fairly detailed and realistic. The story is pretty good too and there's a few nice side quests too.There's a lot of care and polish placed into this game. The only issues I had was a bug where I couldn't unlock the Scratch achievement, but that was fixed a few hours after launch. Another issue I had, might be specific to my setup, was that the mouse freaked out sometimes and that there was a bit of stuttering sometimes.This is definitely a game I would recommend and there's a lot of things to explore and look at if you're willing to put the time in to do so. The developer even sneaked their name in as the little robot helping you out during the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a short game, the story is wonderful. My first playthrough took me just under 6 hours. I was missing a lot of B-12's memories and some of the badges. As I'm writing this, I just finished my 2nd playthrough. There's still some achievements for me to get, but I got all of B-12's memories this time and all of the badges and just hit 10 hours of total playtime. I will most definitely play it again at some point. My only negative thing I have to say about it is that Doc got stuck and I had to reload on both playthroughs, but that's such a small thing that it really doesn't even bother me that much. I would love another game like this. Perhaps a 2nd Stray would be too much to ask for, but that's just how much I love this game :')
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I devoured this game. It probably is one of my quickest play-throughs/100%s and I was eager for more gameplay. The world is  amazing, the concept is brilliant, and the whole thing is just fun. Could have spent hours roaming a bigger world, and I really hope to see these guys make something like this again in future. It's one of those atmospheric games that make you feel like you could move in and live there. Also bonus points because who doesn't like playing as a cat?

_childDocuments_.review: Steam needs an "In-between" rating. Can I recommend this game? Sure. But for $29.99? No. I spent $23.99 and that is still too much for a game so short. I'm all for short and sweet games sometimes and not everything needs to be an 80 hour adventure, but think of all the other Steam games you can get for cheaper, that are better and longer. Granted, any longer and the game would have gotten stale. I felt in the short 5-6 hours or so it could have done more. To make my point, Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons ,I got for less than 2 bucks and that game was was around the same length, but was more creative and  overall a better game, even moreso for that price.But I digress. _childDocuments_.review: While technically a very basic platformer, what this game lacks in variety of mechanics or gameplay, it makes up for in a beautifully told story, making for a short, but emotional journey. If you haven't been a cat lover up to now, you will be after this one. The gaming equivalent of a feel good movie. Wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Got it at a sale price. Totally worth it. It's quite polished for an "indie game". The world is super detailed and interesting to explore and they totally nailed the "cat physics" as care as controlling a cat goes. Super cute. Interesting world and storyline that you uncover as you go. Gameplay becomes a bit typical at one point in a "fetch this" / "deliver that" kind of way, but it's tolerable.I'll also point out that it plays well through Steam Link streaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I love exploring as a cat. The dodge runs through bad guys can be hectic but I like the story. I started over once to see what I missed with a different choice, wasn't worth restarting. The game ends up going in the same direction later anyway. I do like the scratching posts and being able to crawl into a pile of books and take a nap. Not an essential part of the game, although it might be an achievement, but I love the attention to detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best game of 2022. Everything about this game; the fact that pratogonist is a cat, the lore, the atmosphere, the environment, the gameplay, controls, everything was perfect and so smooth. I enjoyed the whole time i've spent in this post apocalyptic world. And the fact that this was only a indie game makes it even more admirable. Although i must say, the ending was pretty bitter-sweet and did not totally satisfied what i expected, the whole game was dark so it was actually fitting. This is not a cute game, our little orange furball shouldn't confuse you. Also thanks for the developers for adding a lot of language options. Even big studios don't bother themselves to do that. I hope this game receives the credit it deserves. Lastly, thanks my boyfriend for buying me this game as my birthday present <3

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty much exactly what it looks like, which is good, and it's a bit more. For only taking 4-5 hours for most people, it's money well spent.While some games are good at giving you a lot of gameplay for not much, games like Stray are good for giving you a lot of value while being considerate of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too far into the game yet, but I'm in love with it.Of course playing as the cat is cute and endearing, but even more than that: the game is just gorgeous. The colors are amazing. The designs of the robots are super cool. The soundtrack slaps. The story and lore is compelling. There's a ton of cute and extra content around every corner. _childDocuments_.review: Whats better than petting the cat? BEING THE CAT! Got this so both me and my gf could play it, especially cus she doesn't normally play games! I seriously feel like watching someone play it doesn't do it justice of actually playing it as there is something so nice about doing it yourself, as being the cat! Jumping around the place in an amazingly and beautifully crafted world is so incredibly fun. So easy to just stop and stare every chance you get, which is quite a lot! Hugely inspirational with the art direction! Seriously, so many shots look like stuff ive scene in beautiful illustrations and concept pieces I always love! I also personally think that this is one of those games to really pull off the sewer levels, as often times, theyre very dreaded by players, me included, but legit, they were able to make them feel really cool and mysterious! Absolutely love the game!

_childDocuments_.review: the art, the story, the emotional bond you create with the NPC's is purely beautiful. its a really easy puzzle game with lots of parkour and mystery, just because its easy doesn't mean its bad. its a great comfort game to get into on a rainy evening. i highly recommend spending 4-5 hours in this breathtaking game.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game on 100% now, both ingame as well as steam achievements - because I love it so much and wanted to play it to the very last drop. That's a rare thing, at least for me. But anyhow - the gameplay is smooth, both the controls as well as the difficulty of the riddles. You have to think about it a bit, but not for too long that it would frustrate you.The worldbuilding, however, is what really sucked me in. I love the way we learn bits and pieces over the memories and have to puzzle the full picture together in our mind; imagining of what was and will be eventually. The more time you give yourself to explore, the more hints to the world you'll find - and god. I wish I could read a book about this world or something, because it really intrigued my interest and I want to know *more* than is possible.Big recommendation from my side. This game truly deserves all the love it gets at the moment.EDIT: While I still recommend the game, I had to realise that the localisation to German was most likely just rushed through Google Translate. It's bad - *really* bad. Which is a shame, because the game feels so refreshingly polished otherwise for todays standards in the industry. Please invest in an actual localisation team next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game for it's premise, the world, honestly just about everything. BUT without giving out any spoilers, I wish there was multiple endings to it! Although I know what they where going for (you'll know when/if you get there) the point still stands! Overall a beautiful game, objectives can be a little unclear at times but it's not crazy hard. But I really like it because you can tell how much time, effort and love went into it! And yes, it'll probably make you cry 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a game where you play as a cat! 🐈At first I didn't know what to expect from this game, but simply being able to play as a cat made me fall in love with the idea! The dialogues in this game are very minimal, with the story being told mostly through pictures, music, ambience and other abstract imagery and even then, most of the plot details need to be uncovered by solving puzzles that you'll find if you take the time to explore the incredibly detailed and gorgeous map this game has to offer.It's a game you can play from start to finish in a day, or take your time by doing cat things like napping or playing with toys. Simply exploring the rooftops in this game with your cat-parkour abilities is a ton of fun on its own.There are a few bugs here and there: At one point I got stuck inside a piece of furniture and couldn't get out, I had to restart from a previous checkpoint and find some collectibles all over again. But it was ok, it did not bother me because I could just go straight to them without losing practically any time, meaning the experience I got by exploring the map could not be taken away by a simple game glitch.If you like relaxing games where exploring and imagining is its own reward, then this will be one of the most rewarding games you could play and I would highly recommend it to you! 😺
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend for a casual gamer and cat lover.The graphics are pretty good. Not jaw dropping but the aesthetic of the world itself and the design is amazing.I really loved the story around this world. I would say it's a bit cliche, but there's nothing wrong with cliches; in fact they're nice from time to time. It's a very simple game so it's easy to play. The music although is a very good pick me up! Really love the vibes it sets.For the price, I'd say I'm 50/50. Although its a nice game and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I don't think full price is worth it. Graphics are okay, simple game play, simple story and can be finished in under 2 hrs. But I really took my time with it and enjoyed what I feel is almost a therapeutic game; the music really bumps it up.I will definitely jump back in and go for a full completion run!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Creative. Polished. I liked the game play, though a little linear. Great perspective-a cat. Couple puzzles. No skills or puzzles very challenging, makes a relaxing but compelling to play game. My negative review is that it only lasts a weekend, one day not looking in every corner  even. Would be positive review for a $15 or $20 price.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: The Quality is the best youll find around for any game really. The Cat concept is amazing aswell and incorporates the behaviors of cats into the game like scratching things, sleeping, the jumping, meowing, and it may sound logical that those things are in there but it really does improve the QoL. On top of the story line being super cool aswell. My only pet-peeve is that quests tend to have no guidance.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it in one day. About 9 hours. Playful, very cute, well thought out. Puzzles are decent. Not stupid hard, but enough to make you hmm for a bit. While there are jumps and things required for the puzzles, they are on the rails so you can't fall off of things and have to repeat the puzzle several times because of a mistimed jump.The action is heart poundy but infrequent. There are places to rest inbetween most action scenes in case you need a minute to chillax.  Autosaves are super generous in this game, Even after I failed a few times, I still wasn't *frustrated* like in other games.I got just shy of half the achievements without a guide or anything in the first play through. Not sure about replay value, but I thoroughly enjoyed it on the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unlike anything I've ever played before. The story is very unique and you get so attached to the characters in an emotional way. The atmosphere is so amazing in this game and the story and setting leaves so much for the imagination, something that very few games manage to do. I would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie story game with plenty of reading and a few puzzles and scavenger hunts in there, I personally wouldn't really even consider this a platformer bc the platforming doesn't require any skill. The game is a very cool concept. Cool visuals. Very cool world building. The gameplay was just too one dimensional for me personally. I really appreciate a game like this coming out, just wish there was more to it from an interactive gameplay standpoint. There wasn't much in the game that got my heart racing or challenging other than maybe one or two moments throughout the whole game.  I also don't like how you couldn't go back to get the memory objectives that you missed. Its not a bad game at all, just wouldn't recommend it the type of gamers that are in my circles. This game seems perfect for kids or people that want to play a game that does not take any effort to get through it.

Also there are no cloud saves, the steam cloud files basically do nothing.I'm going to say this again: There are no cloud saves, the steam cloud files basically do nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a simple cat story set in an interesting and beautifully crafted world. Playing as a cat means the actions/controls are limited, making the game easy to learn and play. You can probably get through Stray much quicker but the game, in my opinion, encourages slow exploration, which is why my first play-through took much longer. _childDocuments_.review: What a fun adventure game with platforming elements. For sure it doesn't bring anything novel gameplay wise, but it does everything solid and has a tight narrative. The strength of the narrative is that it never feels forced. Even where there isn't shocking twists and turns, there doesn't need to be since the goals and motivations of characters are plain and the unfolding simple. That said, the story will stay with you if you became invested enough in the world, which is not hard to do. The devs managed to make the environments feel alive and rich staying true to its atmospheric tagging. Everything from the artwork and advertisements on the walls to the ambient music absorbs you into the world in such an organic way, it's honestly refreshing. Part of the charm and the ease comes from playing as a cat. You are able to take in all the scenes you come upon in a sweeping panorama, like viewing city art in motion. The stretch of urban life on display - and its decay - make the game worthy of its association with the Cyberpunk genre, especially with the visual and narrative references to consumerism. No doubt this is one of the more polished and complete game releases this year and deserves the praise it receives. Excited to see what the developers will do next!

That's just too short in my opinion. * Most of the dialogs don't accomplish anything. It doesn't move the story forward, doesn't reveal the character. Nothing. Except for filling time.* Useless actions like scratching carpet. I see it may be fun to do it the first time. But after a few times it just become visual distraction from actually important items.* There are many confusing places where it seems like you can go there, but you don't.* Robots feel like robots. _childDocuments_.review: Stray is part point-and-click adventure, part physics-based puzzle platformer, part interactive story, part 3D adventure, but is far more than the sum of it's parts.The writing is incredible; it's a wonderful example of a "show don't tell" narrative. There is little-to-no exposition. The story unfolds through environmental cues and some "lore" items in such a natural way that I can't think of any games that are even close to the level of brilliance Stray displays.The art direction is amazing; It's dystopian cyberpunk with a twist. The entire journey so far has been an absolute joy to behold. Around every corner and across every rooftop, the sprawling decay stretches into the distance and lends a very real sense of weight to the narrative.Sound design is likewise perfectly done. The ambience created between the visual and aural components creates a truly enthralling and immersive experience.Game play is surprisingly hard to define, but if you imagined a top-tier point-and-click from the 90's (I Have No Mouth and I Must Scream, The Monkey Islands, etc.) re-imagined as a 3D physics puzzle-platformer, you'd be part way there.I really can't express how quickly and hard I fell in love with Stray. It's a true work of art in every sense, and one of the most impressive feats of story telling in a game I've ever had the privilege to experience.The entire development team should feel a deep sense of pride here; they've created something beautiful, strange, and above all, compelling.P.S.You can totally do cat stuff. Clawing furniture? Yep. Knocking things off things? Totally. Getting your head stuck in a paper back? Absolutely.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray

_childDocuments_.review: Best cat game where you get to cat!On a more serious note, and just so you know, Stray is an honest-to-goodness point-and-click adventure game. It may not be "point-and-click" in the strictest sense, but the way traversal works is very hot-spot-hunt-y. You will collect inventory items, and try to use them on puzzles or show them to NPCs for progression hints, with an occasional switch puzzle thrown in here and there. None of this will present much challenge to anyone versed in classic adventure gameplay, but thankfully, challenge isn't Stray's vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: The simple pleasure of being a cat getting into cat mischief is enough to make Stray enjoyable, but the game overall is not really outstanding.On the plus side, the quality of the animations took my breath away. Every vault, leap, and trot is unbelievably natural and fluid. There's amazing attention to detail, down to the way your cat will arch its back as you inch close to a ledge. The movement in game is also very intuitive and consistent, and as viewing the world as a cat becomes second nature, it becomes a lot of fun to use your feline agility to explore. Finally, there's a great cinematic feel to the game, and the various locales are well designed and memorable.For the downsides, the world, as pretty as it is, is quite shallow in terms of the amount of interaction you can have with it. Interactions with the various characters is short and stilted, and if you try to poke beneath the surface by, for example, showing items to different NPCs, you get a lot of recycled dialogue. As a result, even though the environments are interesting the game does feel a little bit empty and soulless. The story also obviously bites off more than it can chew, and it's upsetting how many characters and plot points and introduced and quickly discarded to accommodate the short game length. Finally, for better or worse, the game is extremely linear and almost completely devoid of challenge. The puzzles are so facile that I wonder why they bothered including them at all.In conclusion, while Stray is a well designed game it does feel a little soulless and sorely lacks gameplay novelty. Whether the "Cat score bonus" is enough to shift this game into the worth-it zone will be up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost, alone and separated from family, a stray cat must untangle an ancient mystery to escape a long-forgotten city.Stray is a third-person cat adventure game set amidst the detailed, neon-lit alleys of a decaying cybercity and the murky environments of its seedy underbelly. Roam surroundings high and low, defend against unforeseen threats and solve the mysteries of this unwelcoming place inhabited by curious droids and dangerous creatures.See the world through the eyes of a cat and interact with the environment in playful ways. Be stealthy, nimble, silly, and sometimes as annoying as possible with the strange inhabitants of this mysterious world.Along the way, the cat befriends a small flying drone, known only as B-12. With the help of this newfound companion, the duo must find a way out.Stray is developed by BlueTwelve Studio, a small team from the south of France mostly made up of cats and a handful of humans.

_childDocuments_.review: My disappoinment is immeasurable and my day is ruined.There is no gameplay to speak of whatsoever, all actions that aren't meaowing, even jumps, are bound to object interactions!But at least you get to play as a cat, right? Right? Not at all!.There's only one button to meow and it has several expressions that are completely unrelated to anything except the time you pressed the button in succession for. Which is undoubtedly wrong, because you wouldn't bind all of your expression on a single button and then make it give them at random anywhere, even in a single game. You would at least make it in context. And cats are extremely expressive beasts, having in their range, in addition to meaowing, chittering, chirping, purring... And yet even the sounds they make when playing the playing animations are wrong - just as the animations themselves are wrong. The part of the animations that's supposed to show affection doesn't make the proper positions of the tail, for the most glaring example.The last straw that make me to refund this game in first 24 minutes is the claw sharpening interaction with a rug. That's just wrong - rugs are there to knead, not just sharpen the claws on, unless you have nowhere else and are in dire need of getting rid of old claws. And there is no such need, just like there aren't any gameplay mechanics whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: A real treasure of an adventure game. Reminds me of the old point and click era, especially in later sections- disable camera to get a casette tape to put in a boombox to distract a guard so you can steal a hat.Graphics and music are well done. Best part for me is, there is no platforming, no timed jumps. Good for a casual romp in a strange city.The story falls flat by its own making though.When you meet a significant robot character, you bond, then *gasp* he can't go with you to the next level. Go find the next important robot!Ok... find the next important robot. You bond then *gasp* they can't go with you to the next level!The game literally conditions you to find a character then leave them. To the point where late in the game, you are trying to find a key to help out a robot, I thought it was some random robot until I realized far later than I should that it was one of the named robots that are important to your adventure. But yet again, that one can't go with you. It's supposed to be an emotional moment, but for me it was just like all the others the game had trained me to just leave behind and was met with an unenthusiastic "meh, ok."

_childDocuments_.review: In this captivating game, players are transported to a beautifully detailed futuristic city through the eyes of a stray cat. From the moment you start exploring, the vibrant world, rich with neon lights and towering skyscrapers, draws you in. The city is teeming with life, offering a unique blend of exploration and puzzle-solving that is both engaging and immersive.The storyline, while simple, is deeply emotional and poignant. It follows the stray cat's quest to return to its family, and the narrative is woven seamlessly into the gameplay, making each discovery and interaction feel meaningful. The game excels in environmental storytelling, using its surroundings to convey the history and atmosphere of the city without the need for lengthy exposition.Gameplay is intuitive yet innovative, leveraging the cat's natural agility to navigate obstacles and solve puzzles. The developers have done a remarkable job capturing the essence of feline behavior, from the way the cat moves to its interactions with the environment. This attention to detail makes the experience feel authentic and adds a layer of charm that is hard to find elsewhere.Graphically, the game is stunning. The art style is a beautiful mix of realism and stylization, creating a visually striking world that is both immersive and enchanting. The lighting and textures contribute to a vibrant and atmospheric cityscape, while the character animations bring the stray cat to life in a way that is both endearing and realistic.The soundtrack and sound design further enhance the experience, with a hauntingly beautiful score that complements the game's tone perfectly. The ambient sounds of the city, from distant chatter to the hum of machinery, add to the immersion and make the world feel alive.In terms of pacing, the game strikes a good balance between exploration, puzzle-solving, and narrative progression. The puzzles are clever and challenging without being overly frustrating, and the story unfolds at a steady pace that keeps players engaged without overwhelming them.Overall, this game is a memorable and heartwarming journey that stands out in the gaming landscape. It offers a unique perspective and a fresh take on the adventure genre, delivering an experience that is both emotionally resonant and visually captivating. Whether you're a fan of exploration games, puzzles, or simply enjoy a good story, this title is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh i could start telling you it's lovely to play as a cat, to have a dedicated button to meow and to be able to jump and throw things off surfaces.. and well, it's what i just did :) But this game is way more than that. it's a harrowing depiction of a post-cyberpunk world where things went awry in a sad, realistic way. So no humans, few animals, and a world populated by machines. it's not all gone though. In this intricate daedalus of a city, that I wouldn't call a ruin given the strong yet artificial living populating it, life keeps pulsating in different forms, from the most archaic to the quasi-philosopical. Colors and lights are few of the little things left to express oneself in the city, and that gives us an extraordinary palette of vibrant, electric colors. The price of this game might be a bit steep for the amount of hours required to complete it, but it's absolutely fascinating and you'll love every second of it. Except the Zurks. Just nuke those little pests already.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst, low effort cash grabs on Steam - at least when a scammer flips some store-bought assets in a weekend they only charge a few bucks for it.  Stray sounds like it has a lot of promise, but once you get through the first few minutes into the actual game, it reveals itself to be extremely shallow and poorly made.  Your 'platforming' is locked to designated paths, all interactions are either pointless or one-note, and the game burns through every gimmick imaginable very quickly.  There are autorunning segments, 'puzzles' where you push a platform to a spot where you can jump off it, and even tedious stealth sections.  Much is made of the ingenious decision to let you play as a cat, but the cat in question feels cumbersome, is animated sloppily, and all of the 'cat-like behavior' animations are locked to specific context prompts.  There are optional collectables but they do nothing but waste more of your time, there's story and dialogue and cutscenes that add nothing, and there's no personality to the robots or the world they live in.  It's just a big sewer level where all the NPCs have CRT faces.  Don't buy the hype, because what you're getting is a student project that needed another semester of work.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly thought this game being hailed as game of the year and having such good reviews would make it a worthwhile purchase. I was under the impression there would be a lot of interesting gameplay and exploration here, with a captivating story about a cat in a sci-fi setting (I love the idea of both of these things).But as it turns out, Stray was just inherently disappointing. Don't get me wrong, I had fun playing the game, the visuals were nice and it was really relaxing to explore the areas, jump around and figure things out about the setting. However, do know one thing before buying this: it really is just a badly written story centered around a cat. The best game mechanic in the game completely disappears within like an hour of using it, and there are no good mechanics to replace it. The characters are much more boring than I'd have anticipated from a game of such high renown, (warning spoiler about the characters and the role they play in the story) More interesting than the main characters are actually all the side characters you can talk to and watch as you walk through the game. I honestly found that to be one of the most fun things about this game. Watching the things the people were doing and hearing small tidbits about their life, good, but definitely not something I'd expect to pay £25 for, and most definitely not game of the year.Having a cat be the main character does not make a game good. I'm honestly extremely surprised I could write a bad review about a story driven game because I honestly love almost every story driven game, I'm one of those people that are too naive and oblivious about tropes to really predict major plot points like other people I know, but even with that, I still predicted many many major plot points of Stray's story because it's just done in the most boring way (see the spoiler above for more info) I usually LOVE any story driven games for whatever story they have, even if there's no real "fun" gameplay. I LIKE walking simulators, but Stray has such a poor story that I felt like I really had to get this review out there, I honestly cannot believe a game got voted game of the year just for having the main character be a cat.I seriously do regret buying this game, it's better if you experience the story blind by watching a youtuber play it rather than buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a puzzle game, I don't reject puzzle game unless the puzzles are too basic like finding key objects here and there, then solving puzzle becomes a tedious chore, so I stopped playing after 1 hour and watched a video telling the story of the full game, the story is actually clichéd as I can guess the ending from the very beginning, nothing surprises me in terms of the plot.The atmosphere and music is good for the 1 hour play, but overall I think it's greatly overrated and overhyped. I have a feeling that so many people love this game so much is just because the protagonist being a cat.If you like basic puzzle games or you love cat protagonist, you may try, but for most people who wanna get through this game because of its popularity, I think watching a 15 min video should be enough.BTW, it's also overpriced, $30 for 4 hours walking and basic puzzle solving is way too expensive, $10 should be a fair price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty great game, with just a few flaws. I avoided looking into this game since I knew I was going to buy it and I was expecting a game where you played AS a cat rather than one where you just LOOK like a cat. It's kind of weird talking to people and doing normal puzzle game stuff as a creature that shouldn't rightly know how to do any of it. That's not one of the flaws, it's just funny to think about as you play. "Oh, you want me to take this key, go through this house and open the door for you from the other side? Buddy, I'm a cat. Freaking meow.".The main issue I had was the erratic auto-save. The game auto-saves on triggers which are sometimes often but other times are few and far between so you might want to quit but you're stuck playing until the game saves since there's no way to do so manually. In the Slums you can hold onto music sheets because giving one to the robot that wants them triggers an auto-save but the rest of the game can be problematic, especially Midtown. When I got to Midtown, I talked to a TON of people, I found a few memories, I did a quest to get an item and not once did it save. I wanted to quit the game but had to play another 30 minutes before finally triggering an auto-save. Kind of annoying.Other than that, though, everything is pretty great. The visuals, the cat animations, the music and the story are all really well done. The puzzles are all pretty simple and straight-forward, more like speed bumps than roadblocks, but that's fine. The game has a pretty chill atmosphere and rich environments so it's enough to just explore around. Overall, fantastic game. I enjoyed my time with it. Check it out if you love cats. >=3

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of this game and the review is only negative cause I think this game deserves to be a bit lower on the pole as it is not as "Great" as it appears to be.To start with the biggest glaring issue you should be aware of when purchasing this game: everyone is right, this game is technically over priced, there is no way to argue otherwise. Simultaneously the developers 100% poured their heart and soul into this game's graphics; what you were expecting me to say animation and all the other stuff?As if, animations are janky, sound is hit or miss; could be bug related. Don't get me started about compatibility, I conveniently work with someone at my work who has wanted this game to work for them and it fails everytime due to hardware/driver incompatibility. Also take a VERY close look at the cat, do you see how Uncanny-Valley it is for a cat? It may fool your cat, but it doesn't me; and probably a few other people who are very attune to their cat's body language/behavior.Oh and the gameplay? Yeah it is basically a button prompt simulator. There is no challenge or gameplay to be had, you just press prompts when told; this extends to all aspects of the game. The part that makes this tolerable is the puzzle-navigation-platforming; yes the entire game is all about figuring out how to navigate. The puzzles are, as previously mentioned, all about "navigating" them not solving them which is why people say the puzzles are easy.And now the story, yes there will be spoilers, even though the plot is so contrived and predictable that if you've seen ANY sort of dystopian show/movie you already know the ending to this tale:Stray is a spectacular game that allows you to be immersed in a world with a POV as a cat and perform some cat like behaviors, although it doesn't allow you to get FULLY immersed as a lot of animations can stutter and be slightly off. At the end of the day it is definitely worth 30$, IF you look past the fact that this game is literally a rip off as you are paying about 10$ per hour of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try my best to give a proper review..I absolutely loved this game. I got this game because of, well "cat", but it truly exceeded my expectations. _childDocuments_.review: Stray is my second favorite game of 2022 and a game I would recommend to cat lovers, casual gamers and gamers looking to try something new and innovative. It's a cyberpunk-themed, light platformer/puzzle game that you can complete in a single sitting, but one with an excellent narrative and the best soundtrack of the year (sorry Elden Ring). Sprinkled between the puzzles and platform sections are fast-paced chased sequences to give a light dose of excitement.None of these core gameplay sequences are particularly challenging or complex, but you get some variety for a 6-7 hour game. In addition to these shorter levels and their sequences are two larger levels that allow for some exploration and collection hunting that may give you a reason for a second playthrough. To avoid spoilers, I'll say that the themes of Stray's narrative are rather ambitious for such a small, novelty game. It very much asks questions about what makes us human and our relation to A.I, art and animals. Stray is a surprisingly profound, fun game and I sincerely hope if kicks off a new era for ambitious indie games much like Journey did back in 2012.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is the ultimate cat game.  The atmosphere is a 10/10, it was incredible. Everything from the visuals to the sound and music are just amazing. _childDocuments_.review: Oh, let me tell you about Stray, the game that's made for cat lovers like me! It's not just an adventure RPG; it's a heartwarming journey that tugs at your emotions. You play as a cute little kitty in a cyberpunk world, and your mission is to get home or die trying. Yeah, it sounds intense, but the emotional investment is real when you love cats.From the start, you'll be captivated by the lifelike movements and behavior of your feline protagonist. The game's about sneaking, evading, and escaping rather than combat, which suits a cat's nature perfectly. But be warned, there are some heart-wrenching moments when you encounter vicious creatures and perilous parkour sections.The cyberpunk setting is a mix of awe and decay, reminiscent of Hong Kong's urban landscape, which adds an interesting layer to the game. And the attention to detail in the visuals, from rundown interiors to vibrant neon signs, is fantastic.Stray's emotional design hits hard, making you care deeply for your little in-game buddy. As a cat owner, I couldn't help projecting my own cat onto the protagonist, adding to the emotional ride. The game doesn't shy away from mortality and endings, which is something all pet owners dread, but it handles it gracefully.In the end, Stray may not bring anything entirely new to the table, but its masterful manipulation of our love for cats makes it a unique and touching experience. It's a triumph for the sly cat people who developed it. And as a cat lover, I couldn't be happier with the heartfelt journey this game took me on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very quickly skyrocketed to the top of my favorite games ever. The graphics are beautiful, the gameplay is immersive, and the characters are SO well-written. It was impossible for me to not get insanely emotionally attached to each of the robots, ESPECIALLY the Outsiders! There were so many moments I stopped to just stare at the city scenery in awe and just take in how amazing it all looked. _childDocuments_.review: I once knew someone who pirated this game when it came out. They told me that they did this for most games, to "try them out before they wasted money on something they'd regret". They beat the whole game, even using a guide get all the collectibles, (not shaming). When I asked them what they thought, they told me that they were glad that they never bought it. Claiming that the game devs were insane to charge $40 for such a short game with barely anything in it. "The whole selling point of the game is that you get to play as a cat," they said "People are stupid if they spend money on this, there's nothing else in this game."When I bought Stray much later and played it for myself, I can see THEY didn't like it. They're shallow person, with no appreciation for art and only see value in games with swathes of "content".Stray is a beautiful, hand crafted gem that I believe everyone should experience. Every single part of this game shows the clear love, talent, and dedication of the developers to create something they were truly passionate about. Every part of this world feels lived in. The attention to detail in the environments and the NPCs are truly amazing, showing so much personality in the art design, so that every character you interact with and building you enter fells unique and alive. I loved simply exploring the game world, buildings a lit with neon and filled various trinkets, walls covered with grime and art, and the NPCs going about their days, looking for secrets and talking to everyone, and not once did I feel like the game fell short. Even the infested areas felt real and threatening, making me feel uncomfortable like I had entered an alien world filled with dangers.The animations are purrfect, especially with the cat. The way they move, jump, and interact with the world feels real, and shows just how much the devs cared and hard work they put in to make it feel just right. And finally, the writing is beautiful. Every dialogue with the various characters is filled with personality and charm that adds to the world building and story. I never had a bad experience talking to anyone, and they all felt believable, whether they were casually going about the routines or voicing their complaints. The story is surprisingly tragic, and tells a beautiful tale of desperation, adversity, friendship, and hope that I have very seldom experienced before, and I'm unafraid to say I teared up multiple times throughout.I don't regret purchasing this game in the slightest, anyone who says that it has nothing in it, clearly needs to reevaluate their Idea of "content". I loved every part of Stray and I can absolutely see myself playing this again in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst playing as a cat in a game is nothing new, Stray manages to take full advantage of this concept as part of a compelling cyberpunk narrative. The verticality and freedom of movement in the environments is all possible because you're playing as a cat. It's a fresh perspective when you consider most story experiences involve playing as a humanoid.Without spoiling the story, the approach the game has to world building is nothing short of incredible. Ambiguity is an underrated story element. Sometimes it is necessary to provide exposition in subtle ways, rather than trying to explain everything at once. Finding 'memories' that piece together elements of the story is how Stray chooses to do this. This system also gives the game replayability, as you can go back to previous chapters to find all the memories.The game runs smoothly enough (it is running on Unreal Engine after all), though I did have some trouble launching it on Steam. The fix was fairly straightforward however.My only other criticism is the checkpoint system. It's fine when doing the main story, but if you are doing side quests for residents or finding collectibles, the game will not save until you progress the main story. Considering I'm going back through the game again to collect everything, I really hope this won't be too much of a nuisance!Nitpicks aside, the hype this game is getting is very much justified. It's a fun cyberpunk adventure, made even better by the fact you're a cat!8/10Oh, also, the soundtrack.... S L A P S

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is visually engaging, the gameplay is a little repetitive and fetch-questy; but this game is way more than just its technical qualities and mechanics.  Folks who enjoy levels, gear, stat points, and skill tress may find themselves quickly bored with Stray.  However, for those who enjoy a pensive, individual gaming experience heavy on world discovery, light puzzling, and simple detective work, Stray is an incredible joy.  One does not need to be a power gamer of any stripes to complete the tasks, and is wonderfully accessible for it's lack of needing to memorize a bunch of button combinations or study exploits to combat situations.  The little direct conflict in the game is dealt with in truly feline fashion: running away fast and hiding.The root story—while familiar in theme and flavor—is truly original, and is central to the gameplay.  The narrative is straightforward and simple, but is not basic; the events and consequences of the story really pull the player into the world of the post-human city.  The central cat character is not used as a gimmick for internet cat points, but instead you can feel that the developers really love cats.  The anti-authoritarian sentiments and visualization of class divides are not played for simple tropes, but instead make thoughtful, poignant commentary on our politically and environmentally deteriorating world.  Much is said about videogames as art, and as a medium for storytelling.  Many of the major, best-selling games these days put so much into the content and playtime numbers, but seem to forget that an engaging narrative—the why—is important to leaving a lasting impression on the player.  In that regard, it is my opinion that Stray is an excellent game as work of art, in the way of telling a story.  I hope there will be a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: As with most of Annapurna's titles, a charming little game that works from a simple concept: You are a cat. Just an ordinary cat, albeit one with a vaunted intelligence that some owners like to attribute to their pets. And this works very well, possibly because through this simple platform you can experience the rich and immersive sci-fi/cyberpunk world that has been delightfully constructed and filled with small details (like two robots playing mahjong in a picturesque little ramshackle town deep in the underbelly of the game world). It's a bleak world without being too dark and serious, and the robotic denizens give a great sense of levity, in their interactions with each other and the protagonist, primarily through their pixelated facial expressions. And the game encourages you to stop and play, leaning into the concept of the cat protagonist - giving you the ability to bat things off of shelves, scratch carpets and doors, and even giving you a dedicated meow button that I admit I used far more than I should have.Typically the gameplay switches between platforming elements and simple puzzle solving, the different areas and challenges of the game are different enough to keep this feeling fresh throughout, and despite the simple concepts driving the game I felt like it was varied enough to keep me entertained throughout the duration of my playthrough.It's a short-ish game, so this is something to bear in mind. I took my time with my playthough, tried to find collectables, explored quite extensively, and at one point left my protagonist sleeping on a pillow while I went to get something to eat, and my overall playtime was just under 8 hours. This felt about right in terms of length - some games tend towards tedium if they're overstretched. I'm sure that at some point I'll revisit the game in the future, if nothing else just due to its atmosphere and the unique concept that it was built upon.All in all I would highly recommend this title. Especially if, like me, you enjoyed other Annapurna games.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of Stray as a project is a fairly interesting one. The project was presented as “Project HK” back in 2015 with a few pictures and tweets, the most interesting part was that they also had a few pipe UE4 blueprint videos for the game, which at the time already had the current elements of what would become STRAY. 5 years later, Annapurna Interactive took the project to publish it - It’s now 2022, 7 years after the initial picture of Project HK we got the game, STRAY is finally here. Is it worth your time? Did it deliver a good experience? Let’s find out.Rusty pipes, cracked concrete and wild vegetation. This is the first thing we see through the eyes of our feline protagonist, perhaps an abandoned structure? We don’t care because we are a wild cat with our pack until one day, exploring the decaying structure we fall into a dark pit.Defendless, scared but still curious we wake up inside the structure, a dead city. No one to be found but we follow the signals that ask for our help, is somebody there? It won’t take long before we encounter strange life forms on those empty streets and a few disconnected robots but soon we discover who is asking for help, B12, a sentient AI that will need your help and will go with you in this adventure. This is an unknown world with tons of secrets to discover like what happened, what’s going on and most importantly, how do we return with our pack.Make no mistake, there’s a story behind this game. While it might seem that the narrative aspect of the game is merely formulaic, it presents a very interesting premise in which AI and their robotic bodies started evolving by creating a language, imitating human life and even started to have feelings and emotions. I won’t spoil the story because I consider it an important part of the game but sooner rather than later we will find out we are in the distant future in which, apparently, there are no longer human beings in this city but instead there are quite a few charismatic robots that will open new branches of this enigmatic place. If there’s a topic from the game I want to share with you is that our planet is precious and we should take care of it, it’s our home.Remember when I said “our feline protagonist” well, I made that distinction because I consider B12 as “our robotic protagonist”. Both characters do have an important role together in this story, kitty serves as a transport and as a way of keep going through the story while B12 is the narrative element of our duo, the one that will open fractions of the past and present and the one that will help kitty to get to the surface. In this case I think it’s fair to say that this ain’t a story about a cat, it is a story about a cat and an AI. The more you traverse these streets and the further you go, the more you will learn about your companion.There are quite a few more characters during this adventure like Momo and the rest of The Outsiders, the Slums and midtown people and while it’s interesting to talk with them (sometimes they share some cool tidbits about the world) they lack depth, which isn’t bad per say, it’s just that they merely have a narrative purpose and that’s it, they are not meant to be extremely detailed.When it comes to details I think about the world and its visuals.STRAY is absolutely gorgeous. The game’s city is based on the walled city of Kowloon, a piece of land in Hong Kong where jurisdiction was under a different administration and as so, buildings were able to be built in ways that were impossible to do under regulated areas, the result? A big city in which buildings were built one above the other and it has served as inspiration for countless fictional products like STRAY.You will notice that there’s a decaying cyberpunk feeling on the streets. Dark corners, water drops everywhere and neon lights, tons of neon light. Buildings are extremely detailed, you can see how nature is reclaiming the space it lost and how the parasitic creatures are spreading, there’s beauty in all scenarios waiting to be explored. At a graphical level STRAY sometimes looks like an animation movie.Kitty is extremely well done, robots have a lot of personality and a really cool design. In general there has been a lot of effort into making this a really meaningful visual experience.Something I wanted to mention before I jump into the gameplay loop. The more you look at the game, the smaller it seems to be and that’s right, STRAY is quite contained but at the same time it feels enormous thanks to the small size of our feline character. The size illusion makes it look like the city is huge while in reality it is us who are small. This is actually really clever and the fact that the city is so detailed (as said previously) makes it even more impressive because it lets you explore quite a lot of it.And here comes the gameplay part which is extremely simple but surprisingly engaging. There are a few basic actions, jump, run and talk (exactly, meow!) but the fun part begins here. The way you traverse the multiple levels of the city is by acting like a real cat jumping from roof to roof, throwing some things or interacting with objects to see the reaction. Do not expect combats nor deep interactions, it’s simple but effective. Thanks to this combatless or, let’s say, liviane situations you can do funny things with kitty.Movement feels natural most of the time and interactions are well done, while sometimes it might do some weird things, the overall experience is delightful. It is lovely how they portrayed this cat’s behaviour to feel so natural, like for example, putting a paper bag in your head or scratching a surface, the results are hilarious.They also did a great job with music and sound effects. In general, there isn’t a lot of music, however, it has this semi-chip effect that makes it sound futuristic while at the same time it feels intriguing. It helps a lot building an atmosphere in which you feel immersed.There’s also this guitar folk at the slums, you might want to give him the music sheets, some pieces are really cool.Finally I think it is time to talk about performance. Much like in my latest review, I played this game entirely on my Steam Deck and performance was good, extremely good I would say. It’s already verified so there’s no point talking about which Proton version I did use, however, I must say that I have been playing with medium settings at 60% resolution scale at 800p and the visual quality was impressive at the 7inch screen.There were performance dips at each new level but once it loaded the section, it didn’t stutter nor drop in performance, overall I would say that pre-cached shaders did a really great job, so there’s that.And that’s it, STRAY delivered exactly what I expected, a great cat experience exploring an unknown city and surprised me with a story I wasn’t expecting at all with sci-fi touches that weren’t shown previously. If you are looking for a visually appealing experience, a relaxing walking game or a cat and robot adventure, I think you will likely enjoy the game. It took me around 7 hours to finish by doing most of the side stuff (I’m going to 100% it) so keep that in mind but I think it was well worth the money they ask for.In general Annapurna published titles doesn’t disappoint me and this wasn’t the exception, STRAY was a really great game and easy to recommend, I thought it was an engaging little adventure and sometimes that’s exactly what you need, an adventure.I hope you all enjoy STRAY as much as I did. Have fun and congrats for the developers for the successful release.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray gives you more than you would expect.It is a well made story-rich adventure game. It isn't just the story of a stray cat separated from its family in to the city full of robot, finding the way back home. Besides the protagonist is a cat (that's 8 out of 10 already), the story turned out to be greater than I expected.Discovering the past of the city by collecting collectibles and talking with robots make the world feel alive. And it also implement this idea of this version of cyberpunk future very well. And another thing that make the story really great is the relationship between B12, the robot companion and the cat. In only about 5-6 hours long of the whole game, it can create such a strong bond between them which is incredible. And other relations with other npcs are not feel pointless as they are just supporting characters as well.I played the game on pc and it doesn't require a lot of system requirements, at least in my opinion, yet the visual of the game is stunning and it run smoothly. The world design, lighting, art style and everything combined creates the beautiful world of cyberpunk perfectly. This including the soundtrack which hits in the right spot every time, whenever you enter the different areas of the city or in the action scenes.It is true that the puzzle is not challenging but at least it is not too straight forward, I would say it's around easy to almost medium difficulty. And some stealth also pointless because you could just run through it. But as I said, the foremost points of the game in my opinion is the story and beautiful the scene, and those little gameplay flaws didn't change my thought at all.As I said from the beginning, Stray gives you more than you would expect. At first I bought this game just because I love cat and cyberpunk theme. And I like game that has collectibles to collect, I didn't even expect the story would be this great until I finished the game. I'm not a  fan of a story game, normally I would watch it on Youtube, but I'm glad I did play it myself. I recommend people like me to try to open up with this game, and if you are a fan of story game, this is a must play.P.S. Although the is kinda short, but considering the price and quality, I think it's still worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and surprisingly challenging! It's one of those games that just feels so unique and in a category all to itself. You play as a cat trying to find your way in a new world after losing your way. The game is filled with creative world-building, fun characters, interesting puzzles, and terrifying blob creatures that would very much like to eat you. I thought I was getting a slightly more relaxing gameplay experience, so this is just a heads-up if you thought the same thing. Took me about 8hrs to complete and I'd give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The best cat game in human history the fun i had with the game and being a cat was over the roof it deserves the most Independent Game  , Game of the Year , Best Game Direction ,  Best Debut Indie Game. , Most Innovative Gameplay ,and PlayStation game of the year  at the 40th Golden Joystick Awards. The story, is well-crafted, is pleasant to play It takes the best parts of games like Limbo and Untitled Goose Game, and then blends them together with a simple but effective gameplay pattern. There's a lot of love that's gone into crafting this game and Stray deserves its plaudits. This is a fantastic game and easily one of the best in 2022. Stray is not a difficult game by any means, and the stakes are low: You have an infinite number of lives, and there's no fall damage. Even still, it has no trouble establishing tension during its more action-packed sequences. Stray takes about 5 HoursWhen focusing on the main objectives, If you're a gamer that strives to see all aspects of the game, you are likely to spend around 9½ Hours to obtain 100% completion. There are almost 2 million copies on Steam alone! And this is already more than God of War, which was sold on Steam “in circulation” of approximately 1.5-1.7 million copies. Impressive result, well done BlueTwelve Studio and Annapurna Interactive!

_childDocuments_.review: Still on the fence about the meow meow game? Cos hey it'll just be some gimmick for toxoplasmosis YouTubers and their catlady like-smashers, right? Cutesy meme crap that won't stack up against the chest-high wall of Proper Gaming?Hold up then, because you might well enjoy this one more than you'd think. I'm not gonna tell you Stray's perfect or anything adjacent. But there's more here than meets the tapetum lucidum.Cats' eyes glint like that when the light hits them because they've got a reflective layer at the back. It blurs the image a little but gives them a second bite at the light on its way back. Subtle and acute, yet somehow hazy, this shadowy trade-off seems emblematic of cats. The best way I can explain the bright heights Stray hits at its best is through chiaroscuro. This game:How can Stray be that good when there's so much wrong with it? These aren't things you can just hotfix out. The fundamentals of its gameplay are deeply flawed and there is a tentative lack of confidence to much of the game that maybe trudges along beside innovation. But Stray is also a fiercely intelligent game that develops timely and unorthodox themes with a subtle bravery that's worthy of its protagonist. Without rubbing your nose in its cleverness, Stray considers how humans, absent yet hauntingly present in its apocalyptic setting, remain entangled to the end with their environment, and asks what would be left of us without our companions and works on Earth. Cats emerge from the shadows as indivisible elements of who we were and will be, with a gentle suggestion: somehow, through all those terabytes of papyrus and digital video we devoted to them, we underestimated them all along.Stray is a game that finds hope in the utter desolation we're facing. It's a game that communicates remarkably complex ideas about co-evolution, mutual influence and the transmission of memory, and does that best when it's not using dialogue at all. It's a game with a cool reference to Another World on the Amiga, and it's even pretty damn fun in a nerve-shredding way towards the end.In conclusion, this game is important as hell and deserves to stand as an inspiration. Meow meow.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a third-person cat adventure game set amidst the detailed, neon-lit alleys of a decaying cybercity and the murky environments of its seedy underbelly. Roam surroundings high and low, defend against unforeseen threats and solve the mysteries of this unwelcoming place inhabited by curious droids and dangerous creatures.See the world through the eyes of a cat and interact with the environment in playful ways. Be stealthy, nimble, silly, and sometimes as annoying as possible with the strange inhabitants of this mysterious world.I can't speak about the story without getting into spoilers. I recommend you play the game without knowing too much about it!This is obviously a major thing in games, You are playing as a cat (obviously). The developers seems to have made the controls as realistic as possible without making it not fun etc. You press left alt to "meow", You cannot jump on command, You are forced to go near a ledge or somewhere you can climb up to be able to jump. I personally like this, I dislike the idea of being able to jump whenever you want as it would make the game look very goofy.I am really enjoying the game so far, It's very calming when you are exploring, The music adds to the exploration and it can be pretty enjoyable doing puzzles and trying to find items in the game!The game is very good looking, I was blown away at how good the game looked. The smallest details can be seen in this game. Looks like the developers had fun making the game and put lots of love into the game.So far. This game to me is honestly the best i've seen so far this year. I'm mentioning again that the developers have put in a LOT of effort to this game. I appreciate the effort they put in. I'm going to rate it a solid 10/10. Amazing work, The feelings at the end after progressing through everything just wowed me.I'm not going to "cry" about bugs here, I'm only mentioning them so others can be aware of them. Includes spoilers, So be warned!

_childDocuments_.review: Purr-fect, totale Versenkung in das Spiel, und das als Katze. Nicht nur für Katzenliebhaber ein must-have. Schon auf den ersten Metern, die noch als Anleitung dienen, kann man dem Stubentiger echtes Leben einhauchen, indem man am Baum sein Revier markiert. Weiter im Spiel darf man auch anderen Vorlieben einer Katze frönen wie dem stundenlangen Powernapping. Atmosphärisch ist das Spiel einfach ein Kracher, so detailreich liebevoll und mit Herzblut ist das Abenteuer gestaltet. Der Soundtrack paßt gut zum Spiel, die Kameraführung ist meist genau passend. Stray ist ein ungewöhnliches Spiel, da man als Katze spielt und sich auch ungehemmt so verhalten kann wie ein Stubentiger. Also mach Katzenkram! Es lohnt sich, eine Katze zu sein ;) Das Spiel sollte auf deiner Wunschliste stehen oder im Einkaufskorb liegen ;)Möchtest du Kekse dazu?Purr-fect, total immersion in the game, and that as a cat. A must-have, not just for cat lovers. Already on the first few meters, which still serve as a guide, you can breathe real life into the house cat by marking its territory on the tree. Further on in the game you can also indulge in other cat preferences like hours of power napping. In terms of atmosphere, the game is simply a blast, the adventure is designed with so much love and passion. The soundtrack goes well with the game, the camera work is mostly spot on.Stray is an unusual game because you play as a cat and can also behave uninhibitedly like a cat. So do cat stuff! It pays to be a cat ;)Have some cookies?Cute Kitty CookiesIngredients    1/2 cup butter, softened    1/4 cup shortening    1 cup sugar    2 eggs    1 teaspoon vanilla extract    2-1/4 cups all-purpose flour    3/4 teaspoon baking powder    1/2 teaspoon salt    1 cup quick-cooking oats    2 ounces unsweetened chocolate, melted and cooled    Semisweet chocolate chips    Red-hot candies    Shoestring black licorice, cut into 1-1/2-inch piecesDirections    In a large bowl, cream butter, shortening and sugar until light and fluffy. Spread 2 cups meat sauce into an ungreased 13x9-in. baking dish. Layer with 3 noodles and a third of the ricotta mixture. Sprinkle with 1 cup mozzarella cheese and 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese. _childDocuments_.review: I know this review will be lengthy, but I hope you stick around to read the reason why I adore this game, as it is very personal to me.Firstly, a game like this is the last kind of game someone like me would buy. I'm not big on puzzle games, chill games and the like, certainly not games where I play as a cat. I like the action, shooter, strategy kind of stuff. So why would someone like me buy a game like this?Well, let me start by saying something even weirder: I'm not a cat person. Or at least, there was a time I wasn't. Then one day at work, in the auto detailing shop I work in, a stray cat wandered into our shop, pregnant with a litter. My mom managed to catch her, bring her into one of the rooms of our shop, and turn it into a place to take care of her kittens until they were able to be given away. We designated the mama cat "Mama Kitty", and eventually called her "Mama" for short. After we got them homes, we got her fixed so she couldn't have kittens anymore. During this time, I was going through a lot of depression problems, and once again, the last thing I expected was a cat would be a companion in this time, but Mama Kitty became just that.After her kittens were all gone, she fell into a deep depression, and was alone in that room. I watched her, and my heart sank. For her, her kittens all moved on, were given new homes, and she was left here, alone. I related to exactly how she felt, feeling like everyone around you was moving on with life but you couldn't. We tried to get her a home, but it didn't work out. She just wasn't an indoor cat. So what happened? She ended up staying in our shop, literally making the whole shop her home. She followed me almost everywhere I went, and for two years, I would come into work and there was Mama Kitty waiting for me to feed her, and fill her day with love, affection and joy. She found a home, and she found peace at our shop, and for me, helping her move on with her life, no longer needing to worry about kittens, and getting to just be a free-spirited cat, was all I needed to help me with my own depression. She fit in so well. She would literally just find a spot in the shop, lay there and watch you work, and occasionally want so much attention, she'd interrupt your work, demanding you pet her, or feed her.Why do I speak in past tense? About five or six months ago, Mama Kitty disappeared. One Friday she was there, on Saturday gone. She had gone off many times before, but was always back by the end of the day, and she had this little makeshift bed in a bush that she slept in every night, and napped in every day. She was just gone, and I have never seen her since. The Monday after she disappeared was the hardest day of them all. It was the first day coming back to work and she was not there waiting for me. I didn't want to be there, falling apart, trying not to let people see me an emotional, pitiful mess. My little Mama Kitty was gone. I miss her meow (which the cat you play as in this game reminds me so much of), her playfulness, and just how spoiled she was.I don't know where Mama Kitty is, or if she is even still alive. By now, I'll never know what happened to her unless she miraculously turns back up at the shop. Cats have been known to do that, particularly strays. The other day I caught myself wondering if she wandered off for the last time, got herself into serious trouble, and then died all alone, without me to be there with her in her last moments, and it eats me up to think about. I loved that cat with all my heart. But I know at least I can have the peace of mind that I did everything I could to give her a wonderful life while she had it, even if it was two short years.  I don't regret it, and I pray she'll come back to that same life.That's why this game hits me on a personal level that no game does. When I heard about this game, I was immediately reminded of Mama Kitty, and just had to get it. For the first time in my life, a game has reached me on an intimately emotional level. Thank you to these developers for making this game. I bought this game for Mama Kitty, in remembrance of her and how much she helped me as I did my best to give her the best little life I could. This game is a joy to my heart, helping me with the memory of my own cat, a little stray, whom I had the privilege of loving.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's short. But only if you zoom through the game at lightning speed. There is so much to explore and relax doing. I'm 6 hours in and have 'beaten' the game but there is much more lore to discover and dwell on, as well as little areas I missed exploring.You get to be a cat, and I mean that short of making people uncomfortable licking your privates, you are a cat. Your movements, behavior, everything is pure cat. And many moments, if you're a cat owner, will have you laughing quite heartily at how well they nail said behavior.  What this game does best is give a fantastic narrative through the eyes of a small cat in a semi-open world setting, I was invested and connected to this world and in such a short time. What this game could do better is a touch more world building and cohesion. There are some elements that seem out of place or unnecessary when viewed as the whole of the story. Certain environment details seem unexplained and out of place. Certain explained elements seem inconsistent with the explaination. As well as little details, that while somewhat unimportant, would have made for a nice touch in the end.What this game does poorly? It doesn't let you pick your cat color. And what a minor thing that is in the grand scheme of things. I hope they give quite a bit of DLC for this game as the story felt as though it's easy to expand upon. I know the price seems steep but it was well worth it for me, it's the first game I simply couldn't wait to keep playing in a long time and such a nice break from typical games. I also experienced zero graphical errors and relatively little bugs (the only one was robot clothes sans the robot) even with running it while streaming.
