_childDocuments_.review: A few days ago, I left a negative review for this game, citing terribly imprecise controls that resulted more often than not in cheap, artificial failures. It was one of the few times that I have been genuinely disappointed in a game.Since then, the developers have put out an update. There is now an option to turn off the sliding mechanic when Alex stops moving, allowing for a greater degree of control and ownership of one's mistakes. The trade-off is that certain parts of the game are now harder to access, since they relied on the sliding mechanic to reach them. However, the developers have wisely chosen to make this feature optional, as some players will be happy to slide.So, of course I jump back in. The idea that it had been improved was too good to pass up.I got a few levels in and Alex died a bunch of stupid, avoidable deaths, eventually leading to a game over screen. Every time, it was my fault, and it felt amazing.I have nothing but praise for game developers who take on criticism, with the aim to improve their product, and I will reward this by changing my review to a positive one. It's now mostly everything I could want in a remake.Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: First of all:I'm a huge Alex Kidd fanboy (perhaps to be guessed by the avatar). I regularly play the Sega Ages version on the nintendo switch. On a good day, I can play through Alex Kidd in a good 20 minutes. (Record at 17mins). So I claim to know the game Alex Kidd in Miracle World very well and therefore to be able to assess how much the remake has captured the flair of the original...and the truth is: hardly at all. I had already bought the game for the Switch back then and was moderately enthusiastic...but now I bought it again for 3€ on steam because of the ccheap price and the controls update.I still find the new graphics very coherent. The choice of what Alex should munch on at the end of a level is great (Hamburger4Life) but that's where the fun ends. The controls are still spongy. When Alex jumps onto stones, the height is corrected again after his hit collision, which just feels awkward. The hit collision with enemies is a bad joke.The reset points after dying are completely pointless and unlike in the original game, where you continue where you die. Despite the “Control Update”, it is still not possible to jump out of the upper edge, which would be important in the castles or on the island, for example.The Ring-Ghost-Extralife Rotation is completely weird...most probably because due to the changes to the reset pointsIf you lose all your lives, you have the option to restart the level... but lose all your money...which makes the forest the final boss, for example...especially in combination with the spongy controls and the creepy final boss fight. (in the original you could by a continue for 400Gold)Helicoptercontrols are still way offThe new levels are meh...I have no idea what the makers of this reimagination tried to archieve...they took a game which has the (unfairly) reputation of being way to hard...and made it even harder...but with less fun...Yeah I get, that the boss fights (StoneScissorsPaper and the final bosses) are the weakest points of Alex Kidd, but the new Bossfights are not one bit more exciting...The new level feel completely out of place...would have been better they were making a few levels as epilogue and didn't touch the original level order...But the worst thing is still the physics (not even so much the controls) The physics feel so off, that it's almost another game...I would only recommend this game if you have nostalgic memories of this game, but haven't played it in 30years. And then for not more than 5€...
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: This remake of the original Alex Kidd game is as hard as it was back in the day, but now, with a lot more polish on the surface.The aesthetic is gorgeous. The characters look cartoony and lively, the lighting effects are beautiful, and the animation is so fun to watch.Interestingly enough, the game allows you to switch back to the old look of the game at the click of a button. It makes you appreciate just far we've come, and how much great work the devs put into creating an atmosphere and unique look to each level.The music is fun, although nothing to write home about. It had my head bopping, and it accompanied the levels well.Now the most important point: gameplay.Platforming and jumping feels totally fine. Unfortunately, because this is a faitfhul recreation of the game, it comes with a lot of the flaws the original game has too.I found that the level design in this game is a bit uninspired. Most of the level consists of breakable blocks, which includes obstacles, and some that contain powerups.Sometimes it can be fun trying to figure out the mini puzzle of which order to break the blocks to get some extra money in your pocket, however I found that after a while this quickly became a bit tedious.Your basic attack is very short ranged, so you need to go right up to each one, and there are just SO MANY BLOCKS TO BREAK!Obviously you can skip them if you'd like, but it's fun to collect stuff, and you do want to gather enough money to buy items later on in the game.Moving on to enemies, most of them die in one hit, although there are a few that take a bit more of a beating.You, however, will take one hit to die. And combine that with a short range melee attack, and sometimes unfair-feeling hitboxes, this can lead to a bit of frustration. There is still a lives system, and if you run out of them all, you will be put back at the beginning of the level. Thankfully, for those interested, you can enable infinite lives in the options, if you think the mechanic is outdated.Some levels begin with a shop, where you can purchase items, whose function you have absolutely no idea. They will be consumed upon use, so you have to just hope you used them in the right situation.These range from temporary invincibility, ranged attacks, or a small orb that deploys small Alex Kidds that march out, Lemming-style and hurt enemies they touch.I think they're fun and interesting, but the whole shop system feels a bit random. I just buy every single item at every single shop, and if it's a vehicle... The vehicle levels are awesome. However, if it's your first time playing a level, good luck keeping your vehicle alive for more than 5 seconds.On most of them, I would crash into a block or enemy that I didn't expect, only to be left stranded in a vehicle level, on foot. Which, can be a bit underwhelming.Finally, the boss levels.There are normal bosses, which are fun enough to figure out and defeat.There are however, also Rock, Paper, Scissors  bosses too.The first one was quite frustrating. Your fate is left to the Gods of RNG if you'll be coming out alive. Thankfully, the bosses do use the same "hand" every time you fight them, so you can memorize that and outsmart them, but it just feels like a waste of time.Later on you can get an upgrade that lets you see what they will play. and you just have to react fast enough to beat them.All that, is to say that I can't quite complain about a game's mechanics that came out in 1986. I am actually happy the devs kept it as annoying and frustrating as the original. (Although maybe some more quality of life changes like the infinite lives would have been nice as a toggleable option. Maybe a difficulty setting you can choose from the beginning).There are definitely platformers out there that have aged better, at least in my opinion, but I think this is still a fantastic remake. If you enjoyed the original, then I'd highly recommend picking this up. It's just a better version.And if you didn't play the original, then I'd say really give some gameplay a look. If I could give the game a neutral review, I would.I had mixed emotions throughout my playthrough, while some elements were frustrating, there was still enjoyment to be had in other areas. Overall, it's a decent game!
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: My mom would always tell me how growing up, she would play Alex Kidd on her Sega Master System when she was a lil' kid. Being the only game she had plus Astro Warriors, she grew very fondly of the game. Fast forward to 2017, my mom taught me all about the game from the Sega Ages version on Switch, how you can kill the octopus to get into a secret room and get a bunch of money, the crouch-sliding trick, the motorcycle, etc. And with this game being announced and releasing, we were both SUPER excited to get it and play it together taking turns once again. While my mom prefers to play on the Retro Visuals mode (And so do I, frankly), I have to say that the spritework is absolutely STELLAR, all the expressions and colors truly pop and catch the vibes of each level. The music in this game is catchy as the original, with the modern remixes being nice guitars. The new levels and music are very welcoming, truly expanding this game to be in my opinion the DEFINITIVE way to play this classic game.Theres even a bunch of stuff to do after playing and beating the game, and although the Boss Rush is a little barren bones and easy, the Classic mode and the advanced extras are truly a nice touch. I totally recommend this game to experience this classic in a modern age.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: My experience at the moment of this review:- 3000+ hours in the original game- 28 hours played on DX 48 hours after his release++:- New graphics are magnificent.- Alex Kidd movements are nearly similar to the orignal and at the same time more dynamic. The best of the two worlds.- The original counts 17 levels, in this one you have 5 more and 1 completely remade. These news levels don't just bring more hours of gameplay they also bring new enemies and new environnements.- The capsule B (shield) item has been remade too. It's better now.- Bosses have been remade (more fun now and also more new content).- New modes: Boss rush (fun but quick), classic (i don't like it, just play the original game).- The infinite lives option shut the mouth of all the persons reviewing badly this game and telling he is too difficult. Go play Mario.--:- In the over way i found the hitboxes of some enemies really weird (like frogs). A patch would be great but it's manageable.- Only one save so if you press new game your save is erased (can be fixed copying you savestate in another file and the game is short).To conclude: Perfect symbiosis between keeping the old stuff we like and making new. 18/20
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake of this unappreciated gem from the old days.The obvious thing are the graphics, everything looks beautiful, plenty of attention to detail went into the new sprites, a lot more variety... the music is also great, many new tracks to replace the same main theme repeating pretty much every level. The game is still short, but this remake has a few new levels, and they are pretty decent. Could have been a few more, but at least the few we got are interesting and unique. We also get collectibles that have some cheeky references.Pretty much all of the classic level design and secrets were kept, even the questionable ones, but it also changes stuff, specially the bosses. Also what they did with the Jan-ken-pon fights is adorable, it doesn't allow you to skip the little jingle, which is a minor inconvenience when you lose the match, but it's still super charming. Also, there are A LOT of new sprites for the 8bit mode too, which is a very nice touch, definitively worth playing the game over again with the 8 bit mode.I'd say the only thing this really lacks is leaderboards, stuff like time attack and speedrun mode, maybe even one for most money collected, like the leaderboards on the Sega Ages port of the game... considering the game is short, giving more arcade-ish options like that would go a long way in incentivising replayability. Also, compared to the remake of Wonder Boy, I'd say that game has a better artstyle, but that's up to preference. I was worried I wouldn't enjoy the artstyle they went with for this, but it grew on me and I definitively enjoy it.To finish, it's a great remake, must-have if you are an Alex Kidd fan, and if you are new to it, give it a shot, it's definitively a unique blend of gameplay and level design that no other main platformer franchise has. If it's short length bother you, I'd say wait for a sale, but do still get it, it's worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: alex kidd in miracle world is one of my most nostalgic games from when i was a "kidd". i was psyched to hear when they announced this remaster. now i've played it a bit and its awesome. love the new pixel graphics, the comfort features and the infinite lives mode. and when i'm feeling really nostalgic i can switch to the original graphics/soundtrack at the click of a button. alex controls A LITTLE BIT more floaty i feel than in the original, which caused me to die once or twice because it deviated from my muscle memory.highly recommended for those that are nostalgic for this game, and those who enjoy really old school platformers. well done devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Good News: It's Alex Kidd, just like you remember it, and now it looks and sounds just as you saw it in your mind's eye, the beautiful graphics could almost be called "nostalgia vision." (also, it has Wonderboy 3's gimmick that allows you to flip between new and original game).Bad News: It's Alex Kidd, with its frustrating, unfair gameplay, floaty jumps, and awful hitboxes.Silver lining: The devs introduced extra options (hit ALT in the options screen) to make things better: Infinite lives, non-floaty jumping, and better hitboxes.All in all, if you belong to the game's target demo (hardcore old Sega fans in their mid 40s), you'll love and cherish this piece of nostalgia (even if you get a guide with all the jan ken pon sequences and use infinite lives in the last stage, like I admittedly did).
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: While it looks great visually it didn't take long for me to notice that the smoother animations didn't account for the hit box of both the player character and enemies in turn giving the visual feedback that you're getting hit by nothing, for a game that kills you in one hit that kind of issue makes it instantly less fun for me I'm sure for people who enjoyed it in the past this is a real gemFor me coming in new to Alex Kidd i just can't recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: 90s-ass hitboxes and jumping physics, no wonder I couldn't get past the last level as a kid. _childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this ever since the announcement trailer. This was the first game I ever owned. I've been playing it for decades via Master System II and Emulation, and... this remake absolutely destroys the game balance, progression and pace thanks to totally pointless changes.Simply put there is a reason why the bosses in the original game were easy to defeat. If you wanted to change them you should have fixed the controls but instead you put much harder boss encounters in a high-risk platform game where you cannot afford to die, with no save mechanic which has some of the most slippery controls ever created. Controls that are hopelessly unsuited to the precise movement needed to make for enjoyable, or even fair boss-fights.If I wanted challenging combat and boss fights (as opposed to a 2d platformer, which is what I thought this was supposed to be) I'll play Ghosts 'n Goblins. it has good controls that are designed for it. Alex Kidd does not. Trying to shoe-horn such content into the game without fixing the controls ruins it completely. It's a painful experience now that feels frustratingly difficult because it's lazy and badly made as opposed to the carefully crafted challenge of the original, which I'll note was already an extremely difficult game.It's sad.The animations are nice, the sprites are nice, the backgrounds are nice, and the music is absolutely fantastic. I am confused at how this took so long to make and the asking price (gouging aside) to be blunt though given how basic a remake it is. Aside from the stuff they ruined it's basically a carbon copy. The only thing that's both new and amazing, and they really knocked this out of the park, is the music.But that doesn't save it.Would have been happy to own it, for nostalgia alone, if only the devs had fixed the controls to suit their changes, or just left out the changes. As it stands I'll just continue to play the non-broken version.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I have a deep attachment to this title, since it was the first video game I've ever played.I tried it, I liked it.I knew it was coming out, but I've never seen trailers, so I was pleasantly surprised to see some new levels and mechanics;other than that, the game is pretty much as I remembered it, including the infamous spot underwater, with the spears, which is pretty much a dead end if you haven't bought the right item.It must be said that, for someone who hasn't tried it in his childhood, this game may seem trivial, or not be understood (And now that I think about it, why the heck would I have to fight guys playing paper, scissor, stone, It's beyond my mind), but it's worth a try.I loved being a small dumb child again for a day.Now I'm just a insignificant dumb adult, and that's not so funny. But that's another story.EDIT:
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh yes… the game that taught me rock, paper, scissors as a kid. Alex Kidd on the master system is where my journey with gaming began… a simple but better time.As a 7 year old I could easily get to the last castle back in the day, now 27 years later I’m finding it tough to do the first few levels. It’s hard as s*it but I will always love it.Alex Kidd will always hold a special place in my heart. It was the first game I beat, and I kept bragging about it to total strangers and adults who couldn't care less. My mom was so good at the rock, paper, scissors boss fights, that I called her on a work number that was supposed to be for emergencies to ask her for advice.My mother still keeps an old cookbook where we wrote down the final symbol sequence (we played together). Cherished memories that will live with me forever.Well, if you liked Alex Kidd in Miracle World you'll almost definitely adore this.The gameplay itself can take a little adjustment to get used to as Alex himself is pretty slippy, and one hit deaths aren't something people are used to these days.Fortunately they have added an Infinite Lives mode which bypasses the difficulty for those not used to retro hard platforming, but equally you don't need to use it.I genuinely really like it to the point I've played it through about 15 times now, but I feel it's hamstrung a bit by trying to keep the feel of the original mechanics and design as close to the original as possible and sometimes that works against it making sense to a modern audience.However, it's a catch-22 because if it wasn't faithful, people would complain. I feel the addition of the option to use tight controls and fixed hitboxes in the options is a great workaround though.Visually and audibly the game is a true joy to behold, and it's full of easter eggs for fans of the series whilst simultaneously adding neat additions like more personality into some of the characters and additional NPCs making the world of Radaxian feel more alive.I'm not sure if it'll be bringing too many new fans in as the control is a little unusual for a platformer and one hit deaths are brutal, but I think this is probably the most accessible version of Alex Kidd in Miracle World to date thanks to the Infinite Lives and very generous checkpoint options, both of which are very useful anti frustration quality of life changes.Would recommend highly checking out.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Power off Steam. Remove any game in the cartridge input slot. Turn on the power base again and enjoy this agonisingly bright and chirpy lesson in the evils of collision detection... back from the days when nobody knew what any of those things were.It's sweet agony. And the revised rework is excellent. And when you play Classic it saves your progress... just imagine that back in the day, games might have been finishable without investing years! :DThe first Japanese thing in any media that any of us learned is that Rock, paper, scissors is called Janken. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up on the original and still plays it regularly to this day, I think this is a pretty good remake. I think it's gorgeous and the new music tracks are great. The new levels are fun and reasonable. The updated boss fights took some trial and error at first, but I managed to figure it out without a game over.The handling of the game itself is  faithful to the original. It's not drastically different, but different enough that I needed some getting used to. There are also some minor changes in the levels and the ? block system that sometimes make the game easier and other times harder.Overall, if you played the original Alex Kidd in Miracle World, I recommend this one. If you haven't, please go in expecting a very unforgiving game that handles in a very peculiar fashion. Think about how the original Castlevania handles very differently from modern platformers. We're talking that kind of difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I never had the chance to play the original but I can see how it looked like by switching in real time to the old graphics which is a nice feature to have.Even without the "nostalgia goggles" all I can say it's that it's a solid platform with solid controls, simple but challenging like Super Mario was .Easy to see why it's considered a classic.Recommended to both people who played the original and first timers like myself who want a solid old school platform,  even though the choice of having a rock paper scissor mechanic to "fight" some of the bosses is questionable to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up, I was a Nintendo kid, so I missed out on playing Sega titles at that time. Later in life, I did try an Alex Kidd game and thought it sucked, as his attacks were so close-range they were useless. A remade version of Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX (AK) wasn't exactly stellar news to me, but it had decent reviews, so it made me curious if this fixed some of the flaws of the old school original.Even if some improvements were made to the visuals, they could have made other changes while doing a remake. For example, the level design can be lackluster, with cheap enemy placement. Plus, if you restart a stage against a boss, you have to beat them at rock paper scissors again, instead of being able to skip it. Another area that hasn't changed is that pitifully short attack range, as his fist barely extends beyond his body. It makes almost all interactions with enemies treacherous, because touching them anywhere is an instant-death. Due to how easily you die, were AK to abide by the old-school rule of getting a game over and returning to the first level, I imagine very few people would make much progress in this game. Thankfully, they weren't cruel enough to keep that around. Despite only having three lives, if you lose them all, it just restarts you at the beginning of the level. That isn't much of a problem on shorter levels, which makes up a decent portion of the game. Other ones aren't nearly so forgiving, with the last castle being a real slog. I got frustrated and turned on infinite lives, since it was such a pain.Many gamers complain about underwater levels, and they can certainly be hit or miss for me. The way they're handled in AK really puts it into the unfavorable side, as he constantly floats upward unless you're holding the down button. Some of the vehicles he uses might take some time to adapt to, but I think their controls work well. Overall, I'm fairly content with the controls, although the way his jump handles is a bit different than what I'm used to. In a certain sense, the plot of AK is stereotypical. A lost prince returns to his people, goes on a quest to retrieve an important object, saves important figures, and vanquishes the great evil that threatened the peaceful landscape. Fairly standard stuff. Placing the story on another world, where invading forces have giant hands for heads, and face off in duels determined by rock paper scissors, is more on the unusual side.One positive about this game is that the levels take place in a wide array of locations, and the artists took that opportunity to create areas that look very distinct from each other. Volcanic areas are more moody with blacks, purples, and reds, whereas the sea is calming with blues and greens. However, not everything worked that well. Some platforms and ceilings blended into the background, as I didn't originally notice them. It should always be obvious what's just for decoration or interactive. Plus, some of the blocks and balls look out of place in the environment. When first starting the game, I recognized the theme, which is something positive about the original. The music was pretty catchy, and it's only been improved with modern sound capabilities. A stand out element for me was the prominent guitar notes, as they caught my attention while I was playing. From what I observed, quite a few songs would stress one or two instruments in particular, making them the star of the tune. Normally I'd be more concerned about an OST being made up of short songs, but many levels aren't that long, so it's not such an issue here.🌟 You can turn on infinite lives and it'll only disable one achievement, but it is the one for beating the game. This would make unlocking others, such as not using the shop or getting all the collectibles, easier though. However, those have to be completed in a single playthrough.🌟 At any time you can switch to the old school visuals, which would be nice for people with nostalgia for AK.❌ Quite a few people have indicated they've re-opened the game and found their save data missing. Despite being mentioned a few times over the years, no permanent solution has been worked out yet, so it could happen to you too.❌ The screen won't scroll backwards, unless you're in a maze level. Not that you'd often want to go back, but I expect that basic feature in any game not older than I am.❌ They could have made larger speech bubbles that'd fit a character's full sentences, but instead they'll continue onto the next one. It looks sloppy.❌ It's a short game for $20. Even when trying to clear it with only 3 lives, it took me less than 2 hours.🔍 This is a classic Sega game, so there's no level select available. Technically, you're able to play any level you want after beating it, but it'll override your current save, and doesn't let you maintain your progress. For example, if you're gathering the collectibles, it'll keep resetting you to having none. That's not what people have in mind when they think of that feature.🔍 There's one part of the last level that looks utterly impossible, as you have to swim through a series of spikes. However, defying all logic, especially in this game, your head can bump up against the bottom part of them without any problem.Maybe I'd appreciate AK more if it was completely bug free, but during my playthrough, I encountered a handful of glitches. Despite theoretically being fixed on PlayStation, I died on a desert level, and then lost all my lives while respawning on top of a cactus. You're supposed to be invincible at that time too! In the last castle, with the room of boiling water, the game lagged and threw off my controls, when it was never a problem elsewhere. Other players have earned the Radaxian Protector achievement by replaying the Homecoming stage from the level select, but it didn't work for me.For those of us who didn't grow up with AK, we don't know the tricks for easily slipping past certain obstacles, or what all of the power-ups are for. A quick tutorial or outline of the controls and items might have been helpful, since I also didn't know there was a way to slide under blocks. That actually kind of shocked me because nothing even hinted at that mechanic. This game seemed to have the design philosophy of repeatedly killing the player to artificially lengthen its playtime, as many areas were pretty easy to get past, while others could be excruciating. AK might be an improvement on the original, which I don't think is saying much, but I still wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game briefly in 92 and remember continually dying at the first frog. Bought it for a bit of nostalgia. It's a good remake with awesome music. Would recommend in the options menu selecting 'Reworked Controls' as this makes the game a ton easier by making Alex less slippery when you move him aroundA solid remake
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted this game to be good. I've been anticipating it since it was teased, and as a fan of the original SEGA games, I was wondering what improvements would be made to the Alex Kidd formula to modernize the game a bit. Sadly, outside of a new coat of paint, it's not much of an improvement. In fact, there were aspects that made it worse than the original game. I noticed a lot of input lag in this game, where Alex would not move right away, or would continue moving after the joystick was released. In a difficult game like this that requires a lot of precision and skill, a flaw like that makes it literally unplayable. There are also areas of the game that were notoriously unfair, such as the acid near the end, that players used a glitch to pass. Well, the glitch is gone in this remake, but the acid hazard was not tweaked either. Even jumping a little bit in that room (which you need to, to hit the block) brings you death. There's a lot of trial and error and stuff that's not introduced to a new player in a controlled environment the way, let's say, a Megaman game might. However this is in the spirit of the original game, so your mileage may vary.Worst of all, when I got to the final castle and decided to save it for the next day since it was late at night, I opened the game the next day to see that my save had been completely wiped. Why even make it saveable if it will just wipe itself out at the most important part of the game?I know these developers are really passionate about Alex Kidd, so I am hoping that improvements will be made to make the game better. As it is now, I can't recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: My first game as it was built into my master system II. Never finished it but I always found myself playing it, even on emulation.Controls feel more slippery in this version and Alex's punch hit-box feels smaller compared to the enemy's hit-box which seems a little easy to touch and die.Lastly, I live in Japan and have played Janken daily with my students for more than 10years; never has anyone said Jan Ken 'Pon'. It's said and spelled (in Romaji) as Jan Ken 'Poi'('Hoi' for some pronouciation). My Japanese wife, who tried the game, also asked why it says 'Pon', I told her it's bad translation. Though, Everytime I enter a boss battle I shudder when I hear 'Pon'
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: The original Alex Kidd is a fun colorful platformer that's notorious for being difficult, but it's still a lot of fun. I grew up with the Sega Master System in the 80's. Alex Kidd was like my Super Mario Bros. So I'm very familiar with it. This remake has cartoony graphics and great artwork. As well as backgrounds which the original never had. The controls feel similar to the original but with better precision. If you make a mistake it's your fault. The Rock, Paper Scissor game is back as well and it's been improved with a more Japanese style flavor. The underwater levels were always hard with Alex Kidd bobbing up and down, but with tighter controls and a hit detection that's now more forgiving you'll have a little easier time with them.The original game had just a short synopsis on the story in the manual, but here we get fun anime style cut scenes that tell the story. You'll also meet characters after finishing a level and talk to them via text and also run into friends that were turned into statues during some levels and react to them via text. The motorcycle and flying levels can still be hard but now with better controls they're more fun to play. The world map between levels showing your location has been improved with much better graphics, The music has all been redone and it's fun hearing the new arrangement of each classic tune and sound. It's all really well done. The difficulty makes a return as well which is both a good and bad thing depending on how you look at it. Good because it's faithful to the original but bad because it's still frustrating, but you can't say it's not challenging. Why is this game so hard? Well it mostly has to do with the fact that it's a one hit and game over style game. Yep, no life bar and you only get 3 lives and there's no continue. Good news though, now if it's game over the game no longer goes to the title screen. You start at the beginning of the level you're playing in and boss fights will continue right at the start of the boss fight unless you reach the retry screen. Then it takes you back to the beginning of the level. Thankfully though there's now an option for infinite lives. A nice feature is that the game let's you switch between classic Alex Kidd in Miracle World and DX on the fly anytime during the game. There's also two modes to unlock, Classic Mode which I won't spoil. As well as Boss Rush mode where you fight all the bosses. In conclusion this is a fantastic remake that captures the spirit of the original game while adding new life with it's colorful updated graphics and wonderful animations. It's very faithful to what Alex Kidd is all about and I'm very grateful to the developers who worked so hard to make the best remake possible for Alex Kidd. This is a must buy for fans or anyone looking for a fun classic style platformer.Here's my Review of Alex Kidd In Miracle World DX for Steam on youtube
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are pretty but the controls, collisions and "level design" are garbage.The punch often fails to break the blocks or properly hit enemies, the level design is often awkward with weird jumps, gaps that Alex doesn't fit through or traps in odd unpredictable or with unfair placement. I had to quit the game in the last castle where the spikes are all over the water-filled room, the water physics kept pushing me towards the spikes and it was getting really annoying.This game is a prime example as to why if you remake an oldskool game, it's okay to change or improve some things that were annoying back then and will be 10x more annoying now.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: The first game i ever played, the start of my adventure into the deep dark pits of gaming and my job. Ain't it funny how it works? I never was supposed to take this step. My brother wanted a Game Boy at the time, instead got a bulky Master System, i got some Barbie dolls and stuff but that weird looking thing that hooks up to a TV got more of my attention. It came  with this game (and he got Ghostbusters because as my dad said "you both like the movie, so it was a logical choice") Anyway, i took me some time before i conquered Miracle World, i think i both finished Lost Stars and Shinobi World, the two good sequels of this horribly threaten franchise before i conquered the Miracle World. Once you get behind the quirky Janken matches and ths slippery controls (the original master system controllers really were bad), you will find a pleasant, easy game. Even at my advanced age i can run through it just fine in 50-55 minutes, knowing the secret level and all the quirks and hidden shortcuts by heart. So we come to this reboot, remake, something in between. It takes the original game, gives it a graphical overhaul, which i really like. I looks really great overall. The music is also remixed, although i don't really like it a 100%, it's a bit too latin and spanish sounding, which doesn't really work i think. It's just too strange to generally have the original music in your ear and hear this new interpretation, like a not so great cover version of your favourite hit. It's not horrible, but it's just not really working. Graphically, it's awesome though. It looks amazing, the animations are great (Alex got two fists now! He finally realized he has two arms) and except for the two or three times something moves into the foreground and blocks your view (like in the forest stage) it's great all around. I do have mixed feelings about everything else. The original game had a story going on, told through a few characters and text files, which for 1986 was pretty great, this game tries to expand on it with characters everywhere that have something to say, but usually don't add anything to the lore. Like in the first Castle there suddenly is a knight who pretty much tells you "Oh, you're the prince of radaxian, super, go on" and it makes me wonder why this even was added. It doesn't make the game any better or the lore any deeper. The new levels are interesting. They don't add anything new to the lore and in fact are sometimes weirdly placed, like the first new one comes after Level 6, so the original Level 7 is Level 8 now, but stills has the number 7 made out of rocks at the start. Also quite a fewi things are changed like the battle with the Ox, in the original game, you just had to punch him a couple time on the nose, here it workd completely different and i lost a life because it surprised me. I do like those little changes, they caught me off guard and it's neat to see a new interpretation. Now you can switch back to the "original version", though that's still a remake of how the original felt, it's not 100% correct but for example, the Ox battle is just like it was back then, you ca do that on the fly and just compare everything instantly.My biggest pet peeve at the moment are the hit boxes. You die a lot because Alex's hitbox is bigger than his reach with the fist and enemies will just kill you even though you punched them. This is especially noticeable at Lake Fathom were you try to hit the Octopus to reach the secret level. In the original version you can just float above his head and hit the tentacle. This isn't possible here, so  you have to tackle him from the front and the hitboxes are so screwed it kills you relatively easily. Since the game is really short in it's original form (it takes 50-60 minuts to get through, shorter if you really know everything, take all shortcuts and equipment) this remake also features a boss rush and additional features, which are unlocked after beating the game. A welcome addition. I was really excited about this game overall but now that it's released i'm not 100% into it, it's just not the awesome remake like Wonder Boy: Dragon's Trap was and it doesn't really add anything to the world of Alex Kidd like Ian's awesome Alex Kidd in Miracle World 2 did (if you never heard about it or never checked it out: DO IT NOW! I may never agree with him about wrestling games on the Master System, but he created a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece there!)I do enjoy the game overall, especially thanks to all the nostalgia but i just expected something more. I still give it a thumbs up because overall it's fun and the developer is active in the community, so the hit boxes and other quriks may get fixed in the future. Edit: Despite promises to fix issues, nothing has happened so far. The developer has gone  completely AWOL in this :( Might turn it into a thumbs down if it remains that way
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Instant win for us Sega Master System fanboys who grew up on this stuff when anytime anyone properly revitalizes a classic.  The devs did great work bringing back Alex Kidd in Miracle World back to life in all departments but one.  The rearranged music misses the mark a bit.  The original soundtrack just popped, but the reworked version is a bit too subdued; muffled, almost muted.The new graphics and animations are vivid and crisp, but the foregrounds can obstruct enemies and pitfalls sometimes.  No problem since you can switch between the original graphics and the new ones on the fly with the press of a button.The new stages, albeit few and short, are a very welcome addition.  They're nothing outlandish.  Just feel like some things that were cut out of the original.  They feel completely organic.Here's hoping that the devs bring back other early SMS games back to life like the other ones in the Alex Kidd series, Teddy Boy, or pretty much anything else that was presented in the SMS foldout posters that were included in every case.  The devs did a more than respectable job here by properly respecting a classic as fans and for its fans.  👍
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: They say you should always start with something positive...So...Yeah, I think the developers had quite some courage releasing this... thing.Also the graphics look kinda cool and better than back in 1986 (what an achievement!).On the other hand: There's nothing else positive about it.Janky controls, your hitbox feels like double the size of the model, sometimes you respawn inside enemies killing you again (so it makes no sense playing without infinite lives) and the level design is still 1986.I got it for a few Cents and still regret spending time and money on this. :-(
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: As my naming source i had to get this game mostly due to nostalgia reasons.And that is exactly where i technically have to split the review.Here is the review for the non-nostalgia buyers (lets asume new players, not familiar with the classic).It has/ It is:- hard as nails platformer (tight jumps)- somewhat jankie controls (for modern standards)- can be beaten in 2-5 Hours depend on level clearing speed- option for endless lifes (-> But using this will only allow you to get the "unfinished" ending)-  story is not of the deepest kind but is nicely narrated and re-told a bit more extensively than the classic- Often Spawning enemies (but not randomly; so technically you could finish the game damageless by memorizing all enemy spawn positions and pulling off dozens of hard/fast jumps)-  ALSO it is a game where one touch of nearly anything seamingly dangerous kills you - There are items and vehicles which can be optained in shops or in the levels themself and can be used at will even cross-levels (but you can not hold multiple ones of the same kind and vehicles are allways insta-used from the shop you bought it)Bottom Line:A well made game if you are into hard platformers like "Super Meatboy" or "I wanna be the guy"(but instead of sadistic kills you get own faulty controlling kills)The review for the nostalgia folks:In my opinion a very well made oldschool remake of the game.The devs kept close to the original although i think at some movement mechanics they showed some mercy and adjusted the intesity of button presses to not insta-accelerate you to full speed for somewhat more controlability. But this is a very subtle change which even veterans will hardly recognize. The respawn mechanic got a bit toned down (you usually spawn very close to your last kill point or a save zone nearby) instead of further away or at the beginning of the level.Grafics and soundeffects got way better and softer(i often got frustrated back then because the sound effects where highly annoying imo).And finally, due to quality of live features that have been added, i ones made it through the whole game (even though on endless live-mode so i only got the unfinished ending) and even had a good lough as the trailer mentions this because a lot of people never finished the old one. Also in this regards you can now play on multiple sessions because the game saves your level-progress not forcing you to start all over on every fresh start of the game.Final Bottom Line :Awesome remake of an oldschool gem and i would wish for more devs of oldschool games to remake in this fashion (keep true to your old material but put in some quality of life features and tone down the arcade-coin-grabber mechanics).But this review might not be the most neutral one because i am litteraly depicting the main character :D
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: A fine revival of a nostalgia-scented game. An infuriating game, to be sure, but absolutely the best in the Alex Kidd series. I thought some of the new levels were a little obnoxious here and there, and having to do janken matches before each boss in Boss Rush mode was a pain, but Alex Kidd's difficulty originally came from obnoxious design in the first place. Altogether it's a faithful recreation of a classic. I'd recommend it (after first having cooled off and done some deep-breathing exercises).
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Alex Kidd in the Miracle World DX is an extended remake of the 1986 Sega Master System classic game, which has been weighed down by the years in its gameplay and level design.+ The game has 20 linear levels, most of them so short that they do not reach 1 minute of gameplay.+ Repeated bosses, you have to face 3 of them 2 times, the 1st time the "combat" is limited to a game of rock-paper-scissors and the rest consists of mashing the hit button.+ The mechanic to "kill" enemies is to hit them head on, forget the classic jump on top of any other platform game.+ The controls and physics are not very precise, so much so that there is an option in the settings to improve them. Why is it optional?+ The collision system does not work properly, you will "die" multiple times before the enemies touch you. There is also an option in the settings to improve it. Again, why is it optional?With all this I can see why Alex Kidd only had games from 1986 to 1990 while other franchises like Sonic and Super Mario have far surpassed it.In conclusion, unless you really liked the original Sega Master System version and want a version with improved graphics, don't buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are AWFUL. The "improved controls" option was done without much thought by the dev, which leads you to have to turn it on and off several times during the game in order to access specific areas. The game's default controls have NOTHING to do with the original, even though the dev insists that controls suck because the original sucked. Jumping feels completely different! The SMS original was not frustrating at all.Default hitboxes are also absolutely horrendous, but the fix works well for that.Difficulty is completely unstable - there are some unforgiving levels that precede absolutely ridiculously easy ones.  All bosses vary from "quite difficult" to "ridiculously easy" depending on whether you have the bracelet equipped. If you really want to buy it, wait for a huge sale - Took me around 2h from start to finish once I figured out that I needed to enable improved controls and turn off vsync for the game to be playable. Not worth it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: In 1991, my father came home with a box. Then I (6) have no idea what a game console is. I have some Tomy Handheld toys and I play with them all day. Caveman speeder space vs.We installed it with my father and connected it to the TV. My father did not buy a game, of course, there is one game in the console. Yes, as you guessed, that game is Alex Kidd's miracle world.My mind was blown at the beginning of the game. I said what is this game?It didn't take long for me to get used to it, and I made my way through my mother's cries of "it's enough, sleep now". I came to the first boss, of course, at that time I did not know that his name was boss. I call it punch man paper head or something.When my father comes home from work, I tell him about my progress that day. Things got different the second time I came to punch man, the boss fight became difficult, of course I gave it to my father and he took my place.Then I played I played I played I played more I'm dying I'm starting over vs vs vs vs I came to the last tower. In the last tower I spent the time I spent in the game until that day.And that day came, after I found the Rock paper scissors solution in the final boss (I solved all the mysteries in the game, all the boss tactics myself), it was time to fight the boss. first few hands-on time and then baaam. I had spent so much time on the game until that day that I never hesitated in that boss fight. My fingers got used to it.And yes, I finished. I went up to the princess, my hands were shaking. I finished. It was the first game I finished in my life. The princess was telling me to take the crown. A few more chapters. I entered a secret room. Symbols on the ground. first I pressed a random two, the ghost came out and killed me I said it's not like that. While navigating the menu, I thought of the tablet. I applied the one there, I died again, it turns out I applied it in reverse :DWhen I applied it correctly, the crown came out and I don't remember that I had such a hard time take it. I had it smack. and black screen text entered then credits. That day I felt the sense of achievement to my bones.I finished it many times after, breaking every stone, searching every mystery etc etc.I had reached such a level that I started to finish it without ever dying.I was very happy when I heard that a remake of this game was coming out. I bought it the day it came out and the moment I entered the first game, I had the excitement of cutting that last boss.It took me about 5 hours to finish the game:D I'm rusty and I can't tell you how rusty I am. I finished the game and classic mode was opened at that moment I said, "Hakan stop."I went and set up the sega master system, it took a few connectors to connect it to the new generation TVs, but soon I will start the game I finished first on my first console.Thank you so much for reminding me of my childhood.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I had a SMSII when growing up.Alex Kidd was built into it.While I never did manage to beat the game when I was young(between homework and parents wanting me off TV and being less skilled) I do remember a lot of the original fondly.I remember all the boss battles and the tricks needed to beat each one.Even how if you had enough speed with the bike you could kill the bear in the dark forest with in a few seconds.The boss battles have some changes made to them it that was a pain but i adapted.I dislike how the top of the screen(in open areas) is has collision and you can no longer jump above the screen like you could in the original version, this makes it harder to jump from blocks that are near the top of the screen.Stopping you from doing this was not really needed IMO.Controls feel a tad odd, not sure why(not locked to FPS like SMS version?)I do like the Retry function so you do not need to start from the start when you die.Not played the emulated version with in the game fully yetCould be nostalgia but the added levels dont jive with meBut all in all, I loved it

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovingly crafted remake of the original Master System classic. This game's brilliant new soundtrack, new graphics and art, and a world of fixes to controls and gameplay make overlooked 1980s adventure game a modern masterpiece. Toggle retro style graphics with one button is a cute gimmick and I won't lie, and unlocking new play modes by beating the game actually had me coming back to this title even after beating it. Don't forget to look in the options menu to see the new options for gameplay fixes; this game was made at the dawn of console platforming, they didn't get it quite right at first.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a review from somebody who played Alex Kidd in the original Master System the entire childhood:So far, I've only made it until the forest, so bear in mind that when reading this review.This adaptation is very good, but it's not perfect. The new graphics are beautiful, but they make the game more difficult several times, such as in the cavern and in the forest stages. I actually had to turn to the original graphics because in the new ones it's impossible to discern the background from the roof or wall at times, and at the forest now there are huge vines blocking a good chunk of the  view!About the songs and audo effects: very good! Love all the new songs! I only miss the 'buda' punch.(when I was a child, I thought Alex Kidd used Buddah's power, because his punches sounded like buddah) Overall: only buy it if you are a hardcore fan like me. And bear in mind the "enhanced" graphics need to be fixed!And another thing: it's annoying that the top of the screen act as an invisible ceiling. I could swear in the original game the top did not limit your movements.Here's hoping for patches to fix these issues. Better graphics should enhance the game, and not make it worse, after all!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times where a mixed review option would be handy... Recommended for established fans of the series, but it won't impress new players. The new graphics didn't resonate with me nor the new music arrangements, personally I feel like this stylized design went in the wrong direction. Additionally, it has a strange system where you can play through the new version with graphics influenced by the original but not exactly so it continually looks kind of off... You have to beat the game to unlock the real original (which isn't actually the real original, just has more tweaks to be closer but still misses the mark). Quite pricey for what it is, even on a pretty deep sale, and for that reason I'm saying not recommend for now. Pick it up if it is around $2.49.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a MIXED review but felt I needed to write this so people know that this game can be very FRUSTRATING  It's a game for hardcore fans of the original, while new players will find it unforgiving and unnecessarily old-school in it's controls and gameplay I really feel like the developers put a lot of effort into this remake. The art is great and so is the music. So it pains to have to give it a negative review. This is one of the most frustrating playthroughs I've ever had. The controls are very floaty, I never end up where I feel like I'm supposed to land. The improved controls make you stop on a dime, which feels very clunky as well. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes for enemies are very hard to figure out, I can be nowhere NEAR the enemy and instantly die.. This happens on normal enemies and bossfights. Meanwhile the Player's punch box is very small, so you have to get close to enemies... I often die because I try to attack an enemy but I'm too far away, so I move 1 step closer and die. Some levels have checkpoints that are inside enemies, so if you die, you instantly die AGAIN before you take control..  (I played with the Infinite Lives mod, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game can be unfair)I feel like these types of Remakes all share the same issues. Games evolve, we have better user-friendly designs today, better controls, better hitbox-detection etc.. but when these Remakes add the Original game into the game as well (~1:1) they have to stay true to the flaws of the original.. I just don't see how this is beneficial for anyone. If we want to play the original, we can still do so with emulators. I think new Remakes should keep the spirit of the Original, but apply a modernized/improved gamedesign to it (not only audio/visually). Wonderboy Remakes have the same issues. (Yes I've played the Originals as a kid, so much of the critique is of the design of the original games, they simply don't hold up to today's platforming standard imo)
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, very hard recommend, but I will appreciate how the old look can be toggled on, so you can essentially play the original, which is cool. If you never played it before, probably fiddle around with the assist options so the game can be a little less frustating. The visuals and soundtrack are great, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I love Alex Kidd and grew up playing it on Sega Master System II. When I found out about this remake, I was really excited and hopeful that they could pull off the amazing success that Lizardcube had when they remade Wonder Boy III: The Dragons Trap. Unfortunately, this remake falls far short of what it could have been.The controls and mechanics are wildly different from the original game, and make Alex a nightmare to control. He is too slippery, making precise platforming incredibly difficult. He will also now slide off platforms or clip through them slightly, which has caused me no end of frustration. The hitbox for Alex with the remastered graphics feel a little off; I have died several times from being too near an enemy even though I made no contact. The projectiles from both the ring and from the peticopter feel far smaller than in classic mode, and almost never make contact with the enemies. I had to play the peticopter levels in classic mode to be able to finish it. The duck and slide mechanic has become almost impossible to pull off. Some levels have been altered altogether; on the Secret Island in the original game, you could break the bottom row of blocks at the beginning of the level and walk under the rest, but now you need to break both rows.Aside from the mechanical issues, there are a lot of disappointing design choices. The music is off in a number of levels and it doesn't capture the original well at all. The most egregious change is the complete rewrite of all in game text. This was devastating for me, because the huge text boxes and the original dialogue were some of the most charming elements of the game. To see this new script pushed into the classic mode just felt really gross and awful.I do like some elements that have been introduced. The infinite lives is a nice addition and the diet option gave me a good chuckle. But overall, this is a very poor remastering of a classic and well loved game. I will keep at it and give it more time to see if any changes are made, but suffice to say I am really disappointed. This could have been brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Like so many remakes the main reason you'll be after this is if you've already played it and are just looking for a prettier/more accessable version on your preferred platform. But this isn't just a lick of fresh paint on an old game, the DX version of Alex Kidd has new levels and reworked bosses, which is nice given how braindead the original versions of the bosses are. But there are also some less than fun changes like losing all your items, money and powerups when you continue after dying. Given that most players familiar with the game know to save certain items for later in the game (flying cane to skip the infamous underwater spike room) the fact that you lose them with no chance of getting them back is a pain, especially given that the controls are still as awful as in the classic version. But probably the worst part is that you can now lose the telepathy ball, you know the thing you kinda need to beat the rock/paper/scissors boss battles, yes the solutions are the same each time and you can just use the solutions you remember from back in the day but it sucks if you happen to be a new player.And for new players, well I already said the games controls are ass. Its pretty standard for games from this time but it would be nice if amongst the other improvements the controls had been tightened up a bit, for anyone worried it wouldn't feel true to the original, you can play that game inside this game and better controls would make unlocking this mode easier. And of course theres the dumbest aspect of the game, the rock/paper/scissors thing. Each battle begins with a RPS battle no skill just chance, this is made somewhat bearable by the fact that bosses always throw the same hands so you memorize their patterns, its a trademark of the game but still kinda dumb design (I still love it but thats because this was the 2nd ever game I played).So yeah if you've already played the old school version you know what you're in for and you'll probably have a good time, but as for new players its not really that great without the nostalgia attached.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely poorly done platformer game where your characters movement is slippery for the sake of being “hard”. One little move and your character slips like on ice. Also some of the blocks put in this game that you need to pass doesn’t make sense and they are very annoying to pass. Don’t even try to play this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever had the chance to play the Master System console, chances are you know this game – it was usually built into the memory; the character Alex Kidd was SEGA's first attempt at creating a mascot for the brand. It worked for a while, but then the company aimed to create a character with more appeal to a younger and rebellious audience, leading to the development of Sonic. This ended up making poor Alex practically doomed to oblivion, only remembered now and then when he shows up as a selectable character in some releaseBut let's get back to the game. Let's say this was SEGA's first shot at leveling up a platform adventure compared to its rival, Mario from Nintendo. However, I think comparing these two titles might be a bit rushed, especially if you consider some fundamental differences in mechanics and even level developmentUnlike the mustachioed plumber who jumps on enemies, Alex Kidd prefers to handle things with a good old punch. However, since he can't eat mushrooms or use magic flowers, any contact with an enemy means instant death. The game is not generous at all when it comes to difficulty, demanding absurd precision for some jumps, along with cat-like reflexes on occasionTo be honest, the game's story is kinda crazy, where King Janken decides out of the blue to turn everyone into stone (in the best Medusa style) and tries to take the kingdom's crown for himself. Your mission is basically to put an end to this crazy plan and restore the royal object to its rightful place. As you travel through the world, you'll have the chance to explore various scenarios and face enemies. While most of them can be defeated with punches or special accessories, the main bosses also have to be defeated in a deadly game of Rock-Paper-Scissors. Yeah, if you actually lose, you're simply turned to stone and die (no kidding)This new DX version not only presents updated graphics and a well-done soundtrack but also features modifications to some additional levels, enemies, and even boss mechanics, bringing even more challenge to the game. Other novelties include collectible items along the way and infinite continues. One attraction that can't be left unmentioned is the achievements, which usually add even more value to the experienceAll in all, it's great to see games from the nostalgic Master System being re-released here on Steam, and it would certainly be fantastic if others showed up here too
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! Kinda wish people would stop leaving negative reviews because of the punch mechanic. There's literally a shop at the beginning of so many levels that sells the power ring that shoots a projectile when you punch, making the game MUCH easier to play. The power ring is also all over every single level in the mystery boxes. So there's no general excuse other than the fact that they're bad at the game (which isn't a bad thing, they should just practice.)There's also a Unicopter thing (unicycle+helicopter hybrid) and a bike you can buy at the shops, which make the game easier too. Theres also a powerup that you can get at the shop that acts as a shield, and another that summons minions who kill enemies/damage the bosses at the cost of time. The money in the levels arent there to look pretty. They have a purpose. Y'all are just angry because it's not a press right to win game. Get good:)Graphics: 10/10Gameplay: 8/10 (could use a little bit more mobility and make running slightly less responsive.PLEASE make an Enchanted Castle remake!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't handle much like the original game, the classic mode doesn't have the same sound effects or has distorted audio. Certain tricks that you could do in the older game are no longer possible, for example in the first level when you punch the question mark block for the ghost to appear, in the old game you would run and hit two money boxes and it would disappear; this is no longer possible. _childDocuments_.review: I play the original a couple of times a year, I'm very familiar with the game. This is not that. Artificially increased input delay makes this an awful experience, and even playing on the original graphics feels terrible; it's not just a graphical overhaul, it's an attempt to recreate the original game in a new engine, and it's not a good experience at all. Play the original.

_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: This game comes SO close to what it's trying to be, but by that same token, it unfortunately comes just short. It's still Alex Kidd in Miracle World at heart, which is a brutally punishing game from a different era. Not to mention the offensive accessibility options, purposefully tucked away to artificially increase the game's difficulty while also locking you out of achievements. Although it does have its fair share of qualities such as its wonderful presentation, the game is caught between an awkward limbo of trying to improve its source material while still attempting to retain its original spirit: both the good AND the bad parts.+ Phenomenal presentation in visuals, incredible acoustic soundtrack, and (mostly) responsive controls+ Improved visual variety and world-building from the original game- Cracks show from the original game's design such as one-hit deaths and slippery controls- Mean accessibility options that lock you out of achievements for enabling
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: My first console of choice was the Sega Master System. It's easy to deduce that I would have naturally had this game. Though I was more into the arcade style games like Action Fighter, Space Harrier, and Kenseiden, I hated Super Mario Brothers (and Zelda), especially the music, so I glossed over this SMS gem and continued with Phantasy Star and R-Type. Like everyone alive, I got nostalgic for some classic gaming because being 40+ sucks, so why not make it better. I did not like the game. The controls are way to floaty and haphazard. collision detection is horrible, and you simply die whenever they feel like you need to. I admit that's a bit of a stretch to claim, but I'm feeling dramatic. Yes, it's a fun game. It looks amazing. Pure, vivid, and evocative. I just hate the controls. I kept dying. Over and over. Finishing it wasn't too hard, I just needed to come back after a day of dying over and over by some spikes, a boss you can't get to close to due to the awful collision detection, or that one jump you can't make. The slide feature is impossible to do. I can not figure it out. It's simple to do on the SMS, but not here.I changed the control response at their recommendation and noticed an improvement. I didn't die before I made it to the water. I need to go through the game again and see how it goes, but this game is quite nice to look at. Some play features are fun, but the slippery controls stop the flow. Not the best SMS game, but an important one with much better music, game play ideas, and look than any SMB game.Thank you, Sega!
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I know there's only half an hour here, but I played many hours of the original SMS game, as I'm sure a lot of you others have too. Alex feels mostly the same, but some mechanics have changed ever so slightly in this version: Alex can't jump out of the bounds of the screen like he could on the SMS (makes jumping from a higher platform pretty impossible if I'm being honest), and other things like "sitting on the back of the octopus and punching like mad" to kill it just isn't a viable option anymore (making killing that octopus to get to the secret island a bit more difficult than it used to be!). I may be misremembering things on how to get rid of a ghost if you punch one out of a ? block but i'm pretty sure it used to be "punch three money blocks and it'll disappear" - not anymore? Also the "JAN KEN PON screens" during the janken battles - "JAN KEN NO" - i don't like it. It distracts from the actual game. Despite all this, I'd still recommend this game to people as the original is a classic and this provides some nice updates to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alex Kidd in Miracle World was one of the first console games I remember playing on the SEGA Master System. At the time, it was a thing of wonder. A colourful platformer, with fantastic gameplay and imaginative boss fights. I was smitten from the start.  Back in the mid 1980s, SEGA was looking for a mascot to rival Mario. Sonic was still a twinkling. And so, Alex Kidd was their throw of the dice. It had considerable success, particularly in Europe, and spawned several sequels, but, sadly, never made it past the SEGA Genesis era.  So, here we are, over 30 years later, looking at a HD remake of the very first game in the series. Published by Merge Games, Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX, attempts to do something similar to what Lizardcube and Dotemu did with the 2017 remake of Wonderboy III – The Dragon’s Trap.  And for the most part it’s a success. Like Wonderboy III, the developers provide the option to switch between the original graphics and a striking new 16-bit art style by the press of a button. It’s a neat feature that caters to fans wanting nostalgia and those looking to play the game for the first time. I spent most of my time playing the new graphics mode, and only really switched to the original graphics for comparison now and again. Whilst the look of the game gets a huge overhaul, gameplay feels very similar to the original – and this seems primarily for things to mirror across the two graphical modes. And this will please some, but potentially frustrate others – particularly modern gamers. Controlling Alex Kidd is simple. You have a jump button and a punch – and that’s it! Remaining faithful to the original, jumping is not so precise, feels a bit ‘floaty’, and requires some getting used. It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but, even from an Alex Kidd veteran, it took me a while to adjust. Navigating a spike pit and a couple of platforms is often more difficult than it looks. It does add to the challenge, as the levels themselves are not very long – and respawn points are fair, as long as you have lives remaining.  You don’t have a crawl move, but are able to get under blocks, if you time a run and duck perfectly – and then keep pressing jump to shuffle your way underneath it. It seems pretty bizarre now, but it is what it was.  The remake features plenty of content, including new levels, reimagined and remastered music, a ‘Classic Mode’ and a ‘Boss Rush’ mode. Bosses remain true to the original. You play games of rock, paper, scissors, with the winner being the best out of three. Again, this seems rather dated compared to modern platformers, but it is a pretty unique mechanic.  All in all, I think it’s a wonderful way for modern gamers to see a game that clearly inspired many platformers that followed. Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX is as true to the original as you could possibly get – and like the 80s classic, requires both patience and perseverance to see it through to the end.  Whilst not in the same league as the reimagined ‘Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom’ from a couple of years ago, it’s a retro experience well worth taking.  And who knows, if this remake does well, we may see Alex Kidd return in an all-new adventure in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just started it and I can already recommend it. Alex Kidd in Miracle World is the game that got me into gaming as a young kid in the early 90s...being able to play the same game with a new graphical sheen is simply amazing. The way you can change to classic mode at a touch of a button and back to the remake to see the differences is an excellent touch. And the music is just so well done as well. Hats off to the guys who made this and a huge thank you from me to allow me to relive my nostalgia without plugging in my old Sega Master System.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. I tried to like it. It looked like a fun platformer. I even beat it.But it's just not a good game. And I'm not saying it's a bad remake, I'm saying that the original game is bad.The slippery controls feel like you're constantly walking on ice which causes you to hit enemies very easily.Yes, you can turn on the modernized controls but that's not the "true experience." The game looks andsounds really nice but the gameplay is horrible. The other thing I didn't like was the rock-paper-scissors bossbattles. They're plain old trial and error, take a long time and are not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX is an accomplished remake built around a core that's admittedly creaking with age. It’s difficult to brainstorm anything extra that I wish the development team had added, beyond perhaps more new levels, although at that point the line between remake and sequel would surely begin to blur. Some of the quality-of-life changes will probably prove contentious, but the kid in me from 30 years ago just wishes they’d been there from the start. And that’s probably as good a sign as any that the developers handled this remake well.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought this game with one thing in mind: being able to beat it playing exactly like I've been playing for 30 years, just with a prettier version paying homage to the original one - just a good old nostalgia trip. But I died in the first fishman spitting bubbles because my ancient strategy - breaking the lowest brick, getting in and punching around until it died - simply didn't work anymore because now the bubbles can get me in that spot. I know it seems like a small thing - because it is - but this kind of "change" happened like 5 times in the first level. If they wanted to do a completely different game, I'd be on board with the changes, but these feel more like mistakes than anything else - and turned out to be too annoying for me. TL;DR If you can always beat the original in the first try, that doesn't mean anything here

_childDocuments_.review: This game is OKAY to me, I suppose the gameplay is exactly like the classic, never seem to change any controls whatsoever, its the same and the only difference is the enhanced graphics which you also have the ability to switch between modern or classic graphics.As for gameplay overall, the only reason why the game is so "difficult" is because of poor controls which makes platforming very hard. Both movement and air control is very poor, but combat is somewhat good. On the bright note, the bosses arent that difficult if you know how to dodge, as well as knowing well how to play rock, paper, scissors.Its a hard game to play, play it if you are up for a challenge. Ignore if you want a casual platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Alex Kidd In Miracle World was one of if not the first game I ever played. It was brutal in it's difficulty and was a test of endurance, problem solving and wits. This remake is all of that but has some things added that makes it better in every way. 1- The art style is absolutely gorgeous + you have the ability to switch between the original and updated one on the fly.2 - If you game over you will lose your items and money but you no longer go back to the very beggining of the game.3 - The new levels feel like an extention of the land of Radaxian and could've very much been included in the original game.Only problem I have with the remake is the fact that there's not much to keep you coming back once you've completed it, but overall if you enjoyed the original game on the Master System or are looking to see what the game is like I recommend picking it up if you can. 8.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've wanted to revisit this game for years and years, having grown up playing the master system in the mid 80s.  This is a faithful recreation of the game and enough to satisfy that desire, and enjoyable enough to play through twice right away.A few things to note... If you are looking for a full overhaul like another vendor did with Dragons Trap, this isn't that.  It is more of a 16 bit upgrade sort of scenario, but the price is set accordingly.  While the upgrade works flawlessly, to date the classic mode (dedicated, not just the new version with the old graphics overlaid) has a bug where you can not exit the shops.  Be it keyboard or gamepad play, the "up" to exit the shop is broken, so if you want to play through, you will not be able to use the shops.Also if you're like me and was annoyed near to death by the difficulty of the last castle, there is a wimp mode that allows you to continue indefinitely, but you will lose your steam achievements from that point on as well as your ability to resume the game after exiting.  A small price to pay though for me, as I always seem to have difficulty making it through they last castle on the given lives.All in all it's a great way to reminisce and kill two hours for under twenty bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't convinced by the looks and music. But after half an hour I started to love it. It has lots of extra content that the original game didn't have and I'm just enjoying it a lot. Can't wait to 100% it. If you liked the original game or played it as a child, give it a try, you won't be disappointed! Also I'm playing it like old school, when I game over I restart from the beginning, but there are a lots of options to make the game easier if you find it challenging! Personally I also love the original controls <3 but you can switch to less slippery if you prefer. Honestly, if you played this is a child, you don't have an excuse to try this excellent remake!
