_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar perhaps most resembles the Quake games.It's a solid FPS, with a dash & bullet time.There will be plenty of moments where you will enter a room and die (or lose most of your health) almost instantly because you had the wrong gun out for the situation, or encountered one of those flying hitscan enemies that you couldn't have known was there, or got bum rushed by something nasty.  In other words; unless you have the reactions of Neo from the Matrix, you are going to have a fair few unforseeable deaths, and can do better the next time knowing what is around that corner.  Fortunately checkpoints are pretty frequent, and you aren't heavily punished, which makes this entirely bearable to me.The game lets you augment your weapons, though i found myself just adding basic + damage +ammunition type stuff, and it wasn't until about 3/4 through the game that I got to really play with the cool upgrades that would change how the guns function.  Levels have plenty of secrets in them, some of which are cumulative, as in: you find might find 3 secret items on a level which can be used somewhere to uncover a bigger secret, or lead you to a secret level.  Some secrets will reward you with parts you can use to upgrade your weapons, so there is quite an incentive to try and find them unlike most other FPS's.In terms of polish;  I encountered a crash a couple of times in the same place.  The game has its fair share of invisible walls/boundaries.  It seems like they didn't polish up the later episodes much at all when it came to these, which really put a dent in the exploration, it in fact discouraged me from looking for sneaky ledge jumps i might be able to do to track down secrets, because i expected to smack my face into an invisible wall and plummet to my death.Music is a mixed bag.  On the one hand, the tracks are great, mostly a mix of slow thrashy/industrial metal and dance techno.  On the other, well hearing the same track for 90 minutes, no matter how good it is can get a bit too much.  The game needs more tracks!If you don't go in expecting anything groundbreaking, and were happy with the level design in games like the Quake series, you should have a good time.  The greater rewards for finding secrets is something I want to see in more FPS games.  Dread Templar is one of the better retro FPS's to come out and for me a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok in general, but each episode after the second feels a bit less polished than the previous. "Dread Templar" incorporates a lot of things that could have been done better: enemies that are a tad too spongy, invisible walls, instantly killing falls, some of which are not properly indicated, and so on..
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: In the - still rolling - wave of throwback-shooters, this one has its spot not far from the crown. Fast, gory, fun. Yes, the look is OG Quake-y, if that rubs you the wrong way, better stay away. If you don't mind that or even - like me - appreciate it, you're in for quite the treat. From what is on display so far - this is still early access mind you - there's little to complain and a lot to love.Weapons are mostly variations of your standard FPS-arsenal, but they all look and sound just the way you want it (the shotty feels good, and if you nail that, you're a winner in my book), the enemies are diverse and creative, the level design is intricate enough to not be boring but not so much as to confuse the player too much.Apart from your regular rootie-tootie point-and-shooties you're equipped with three timed abilities, a dash - which is solid, a katana-throw - which is fun when I remember that I have it, and bullet-time - which I somehow never use. It's not bad, it's just that I never feel the need for it and eventually forget about it.Saving your game is done at fixed savepoints in the level which aren't too far between; the system feels fair.There's also an upgrade system for your weapons and abilities in place which could feel a bit more impactful, especially on the damage side of things.If you're a fan of the genre and feel like playing a mash-up of Prodeus and Wrath - buy this. If you feel uncomfortable with shelling out coin for unfinished products, you can make an informed decision by checking the roadmap on this here steam page to see what's already there and what's to come. (There's also the option of getting this game in the "This is my Boomstick Bundle" by publisher 1C, which also includes the brilliant Viscerafest and Forgive Me Father. Just saying.)

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar (AKA Hell Hunt) has been a game I've been following for quite some time ever since the beginning of the decade when this got announced. I was very excited for it, but after many disappointments in the Boomer Shooter market, many of which I've talked about my problems with in previous reviews of this sub genre, I was a bit weary if I was truly going to like this especially with many people complaining that it's a very generic game altogether. Yes, it might be a bit on the unoriginal side of things, but that doesn't mean the game is not fun, because it actually is! And Dread Templar improves upon many aspects that many other games have implemented in it's design.First off, I want to get my only real negatives out of the way first. Like most Boomer Shooter games, the story here is hot garbage. It's edgy nonsense that thinks it's so cool when it really isn't. It's grating and annoying. The main character of the Templar sounds like if Postal Dude was trying too hard to be edgy and cool. Thankfully, all the cutscenes can be skipped which is always nice so you can just get into the action immediately. Aside from some immersion breaking things like how the Templar has two different pitched sounds when getting hit and jumping (which is mostly a nitpick but I really do care about being immersed in games nowadays) and Episode 4 being a bit on the easy side, everything here is solid.This is a hardcore styled shooter in the same vein of Doom Eternal. I thought I was going to have another Turbo Overkill situation where the game was just overly hard for no reason and copied the hardcore shooter style without getting why, but thankfully, Dread Templar's difficulty takes notes from Doom Eternal and makes some massive improvements to what that game did as well. One of the best things about the game is the weapon management. It's by far the best I've played in a Boomer Shooter recently. Every gun has it's use for one reason or another and nothing went to waste. Weapon combos to defeat enemies from a double shotgun to a regular shotgun blast is very satisfying and with the right mouse button being to switch to different weapon variants. The developer here has done a great job at this and should be commended for understanding Boomer Shooter/Old School game mechanics and putting a modern feel to them.As for the gameplay, it's a super fast twitched base style that works extremely well here. Dread Templar takes notes from Doom Eternal yet again and by being a challenging but never cheap game. Even if you don't get something at first or die for reasons unknown, you'll know immediately how to deal with the situation next time. The gunplay is nothing extraordinary but can still be solid when facing multiple enemies at once. Another thing this game does well is it's upgrade system. Again, this is the best I've seen in the Boomer Shooter market, tons of diverse upgrades, easy to find and unlock them, whether it be in the open or going through side areas and all having different effects that you can stack up on top of each other. When Doom eventually returns, I hope they take notes from this game here. Because this is the best of the best I've seen in a long time when it comes to upgrades.Some other quick notes to make are the graphics. While the game does have a similar style to Quake and early 3D Shooters, it's never an eyesore and is never uncompelling. The graphics here are excellent and the replication of the old school shooter is tasteful and effective. The boss fights are also very challenging as well. The final boss does take some time to understand how to defeat him, but I found a nice plan on how I used my weapons to be effective in battle. The side areas are also quite fun as well. Some are combat oriented while some are challenge oriented. The Mine Cart Area and Boulder Slope area were some of the most interesting of the game and the side areas do get better as you go along despite most of them being combat oriented.Finally, Dread Templar has a pretty kick ass soundtrack. The songs here take on different styles each fitting the respective area and episodes of the game. There is never a bad song and it fits with the action nicely, even if nothing will truly stick out in the coming weeks. Another thing as well is the campaign can be beaten in about 6.5/7 Hours total, making it unusually lengthy for an FPS Game. This might be nice to some who want more playtime, but I felt a more tighter, 4-5 Hour length would have made the game sturdier. It overstayed it's welcome by the end and I just wanted it to be over despite me enjoying the game.So I did enjoy Dread Templar. Boomer Shooter fans will find lots to like and admire here as it improves upon many gameplay and design aspects of recent Boomer Shooters and Old School Shooters good and bad. I never found myself frustrated with it totally and it does a good job at replicating the hardcore style difficulty of Doom Eternal well enough. It's not the most original game of the bunch, but that's just a thing that's lacking currently in the Boomer Shooter market at the moment. Overall, a worthy FPS that you should definitely check out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of content here for an Early Access title. Dread Templar is very challenging with good level design and a plethora of enemy types. The gunplay is amazing and the soundtrack kicks ass. With weapon and skill customization to boot this really does feel like Doom Eternal in the Quake engine. Some of the most fun I've had in a shooter. It really feels like the developers built upon the best in retro-shooters these past few years and put it all in one package. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing that happened to so called boomer shooter revival was DUSK. that game set the standards high and that was just the perfect thing because this game and some others I played are not even close to that standard. I played most of the 90's shooters so I like to think I know a thing or 2 about these kind of games.I don't like doing this, writing a bad review for an indie title is really not my thing.So most of negative reviews say that this game is ok, average, mid etc and yet only 2.8 % reached the middle of the game and 2.8 % finished the game. I finished it on hard and here are some of my thoughts.I will start with the positives first. The guns are ok, the upgrade system is ok, 10 % levels are well designed, some secrets smartly hidden.Now, the first thing that I want to say is that this game is not finished, you can run through enemies, get stuck in enemies, there are glitches, bugs.... Look, I would get over bugs and glitches but running through enemies like they are ghosts and getting stuck in enemies is unacceptable. Most of the levels are just copied and each chapter feels like one level, large open levels and they are badly designed. The other thing I can't stand are invisible walls and there are a ton of them in this game so how about an idea - build a visible wall - ! Overall poor level design.The music is heavy metal of course but only one track is playing on repeat on every level so just turn it off. One thing that I almost never complain about are graphics, you can go through my 400 + reviews and you can find only a few. This game looks mostly crappy and I am being polite. Quick save , no reloading are not included so you will have to save manually on save stations OMG and reload of course,Look, I thumbed down Ion Fury ( and that game doesn't look bad at all after playing Dread Templar ) so I have no problems when I say that this game is not good. It lacks identity, has poor level design and it could use 10-15 patches. I wasted my time so you don't have to.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this during its final playtest just over a month ago and left a scathing review. Let me just say, this is the largest improvement I have ever seen in a game in such a short span of time. The massive jump in quality, and the implementing of player feedback bodes well for this game being in early access. I absolutely loved this game. _childDocuments_.review: Hi there!Yeah, yeah, we're here again. Steam nominations and all that stuff. The time of the year where hundreds of forced reviews show up haha. Ok I'll keep this rather brief I think and will put a TL;DR right at the start here:Great action FPS game with a lot of nods to classic/retro/Boomer-Shooters with a pumping "industrial death metal"-soundtrack (no vocals) and fast gameplay (although you can play it slower too if you like). It features unlockable skills, diverse environments, different enemies and some huge bosses. Also lots of secrets in every level. No quicksaving - but save spots!So yeah, if you grew up playing all those boomer shooters, you might feel right at home. Although not all of our ancient shooters featured a high tempo like this game offers. And not all offered a story too. Yes, this game has a story but it doesn't bother you too much if you just wanna jump right in it. To keep things short: you are a/the Dread Templar and you are on a quest for revenge. Your "quest" if you want to label it as such takes you through different times and places and lots of killing will take place. All along the way you'll improve your powers and weaponry with artifacts called "blood gems" and runestones.That's cool and all but what about your arsenal? Your first weapon is the (dual) katana which you can use to melee or combine to a spear you can hurl at your foes. You don't have to run to your "improv spear" to pick it up as it is tied to a skill with a cooldown. After a while, it will reappear in your hand ready to switch to melee mode or take your shot at another throw again.Then there's different kinds of pistols, a single and double barreled shotgun, some kind of "electrical mine thrower", rocket launcher and more. You'll even be able to use the "inferno gauntlet" which kind of is like this games BFG9000. Some weapons also feature alternate variants for specific playstyles or targeted towards different situations.And what about those skills? No way that I'll spoil it for you and list all there is, but... here's a little "teaser": some skills decrease cooldown timers for various weapons, like the cooldown of the "spear katana" to return to your hand. Pretty self explanatory. Then there's of course possible damage boosts or increasing the maximum amount of ammo you can carry. And then there's kinda "ultimate upgrades"; for example, your shotgun can become the "frost-banshee" - hitting normal foes will freeze them or your pistols will be their "inferno" variants with higher rate of fire to bathe your enemies in a whirlwind of bullets. Mind the ammo consumption though.Movement isn't limited to walking and running, you can also dive (I think there's no air timer you have to watch for in this game) and dash while in the air and on ground. No double jump though except I just haven't unlocked that yet (I still have to finish the last episode)."Ok, what about the levels?" you may ask. Ok, I have to be honest here, caves, tunnels, dungeons, ancient sites and hellish mines are somewhat prevalent. But there's still variety, like a wintry landscape containing an small archaic town with wooden houses and the almost expected well. There's giant libraries. There are some huge contraptions and buildings to explore. Excavation sites, frozen caves, some supernatural stuff (one level is called "Soul Melting Factory" FYI lol). Everything is garnished with pillars, chests, demonic statues, switches, elevators, platforms and on top of that each level features a good deal of secrets and one super secret. What's a super secret? Well, you might have a clue if you played Blood. Usually there's something exceptionally hidden or different objects you have to find and return to a specific location and your reward most of the time is worth the trouble. On top of that: of course there's easter eggs included which I won't spoil here.EDIT:Each level usually also has a side-area with additional loot and monsters if you want to go for the 100% run.Since you can't quicksave wherever you please, how's the save system set up? You can only save your game at specific "save spots" (glowing blue symbols scattered around the maps). In my opinion they're close enough to each other as to not make this game too hard or frustrating.Your enemies? Puh, some are rather weird. I don't actually know how to describe some of those... Cenobyte-Zombies? The usual host of demonic and occult looking beasts, ice ... insects? Acid pus flinging lovecraftian blobs? Bomb throwing ogres? Body horror crawlies with big eyeballs? These are just some words that come to mind and might give you a general idea of the enemy roster.The music I described as "industrial death metal" was done by John S. Weekley from PRIMEVAL Music. It features lots of electronic sounds layered with distorted, down-tuned electric guitars and a pumping drumset with these powerful "80s snare sound". I guess one could also drop the word "djent" here or there, although it doesn't go overboard too much with it. And sometimes there's a bit of "ethno" sound to the songs too (listen to E4M1/E4M2 for example). You won't have any real vocals, no growling here - but there's the occasional supporting "choir" sample. If you liked the modern Doom games soundtracks by Mick Gordon or music made by Andrew Hulshult, chances are you'll be a-ok with this too.Sound FX wise there's not too much to complain in my book. I think the shotgun could've used a beefier sound, something close to the inferno revolver but it doesn't sound as weak as the single barrel shotgun in Quake. You remember that one? You got one jumping sound, lots of booms and bangs with your whole arsenal but honestly, I'd like to keep the music in the foreground. As you'd expect, enemies react to you and the world with their own samples. All in all I'd say the soundwork is well done (and will definitely benefit if you have a subwoofer lol), although nothing exceptional comes to mind.Performance-wise I never had a problem with my 1080 Ti and 12700k CPU, it was always running super smooth. And it rarely crashed. In about 30 hours of playtime I had when I was writing this review, I only had few and I might've provoked those because I was doing stuff in the background.All in all, I'm having a blast with this game. Well done T19 Games & Fulqrum Publishing.If you should have any unanswered questions regarding this game, feel free to ask. And remember: this game has no toilets.

_childDocuments_.review: yes, but dont expect a masterpiece, theres some jank here and there and some strange enemy behaviour, but the gunplay is fun if you use the following weapons, pistols, mac's, shotgun, inferno rocket launcher, inferno revolver, and the 2nd gauntlet that drains all around you (kind of like a BFG 10000 from Quake II but without the projectile, it just channels on everything you see as long as you hold the button)The secrets are fun to run around and find, i think the upgrade system is interesting, but could perhaps be better, the level design compared to other indie games is definitely more vertical (ive seen too many games going for the wolfenstein 3D route, i.e; flat) so that gets a big plus.Again i think the guns i listed are a ton of fun to use and i especially like the alignment they have, they dont cover 40% of the screen like waaaaaay too many games do these days, probably the best gun alignment ive seen in a long ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time, so that gets the biggest plus. my favorite is probably the shotgun, i used that up until the point where things needed 5 shots to take an enemy down, but thats when the upgrades swoop in to save it, the frost upgrade for it was the saviour. probably used the shotgun 75% of the entire games playtime which is a bout 9 hours, (less if you rush ofc). the super shotgun... it was not good, felt like a wet fart in comparison to its single shot counterpart.The bosses were interesting, but some of the movements they did requires you to slow down reality in real life to react to, cause even with the bullet time mode in game, their swings are still lightning fast.Some of them had fun mechanics, where my favorite might have been the fire boss.overall i'd give it a 73%, i found some enjoyment, but some things annoyed me.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another boomer shooter to keep track of. Dread Templar was at first an early access title that became available in around August 2021. Unlike some early access titles though, it didn't take this game too long to leave that state and now it gets to enjoy the status of a full release as of 26th of January 2023.I enjoyed my time with Dread Templar, I would consider it above average in quality as far as the scene goes, however, I still think it still falls slightly short when it comes to games like Dusk and Amid Evil, which are the gold standard for these types of games. Dread Templar features 5 episodes that explore different 'biomes', and features various callbacks and easter eggs to classic shooter and action games. As you explore the levels, the game will reward you with  you need to upgrade your character and weapons. First are the blood gems, important for unlocking upgrade slots, and the second are runes, which are the upgrades for your character and weapons. It's a pretty straightforward upgrade system but some of the cooler rare runes can drastically change the appearance and functionality of your guns. Some of the secret hunting isn't obvious though, and for this you may need to consult a guide.Quick swapping between guns is generally as fun as in any of these games but I found character movement to be quite slow, even with your character's dash ability it feels a little slower than I'd like but thankfully the levels aren't too large for this to be a deal breaker. Another aspect to mention is the enemy AI, it is better than your typical boomer shooter as some of your enemies will move from left to right to avoid attacks but admittedly there's still plenty of enemies who will mindlessly rush you.Dread Templar is not 'genre defining' but still generally better than your typical game of this niche.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like to leave negative reviews for small games, especially since I bought it a few years ago when it was still in early access and looked very promising. I really tried to enjoy this one, but simply couldn't, no matter how hard I tried.Dread Templar is another one of the so called boomer shooters. Unfortunately, the likes of DUSK, Amid Evil etc., set the bar so high, it makes this one look and play really bad in comparison. The soundtrack was clearly inspired by Mick Gordon's DOOM and DOOM Eternal soundtrack, but without the punch. There aren't many tracks and it gets repetitive very fast. It's not bad, but not great either.There is a story of some sort, but to be honest I didn't pay any attention to it.An upgrade mechanic is also included where you have to collect runes scattered across each level that boost your weapons' stats slightly, but it's nothing significant and the game would likely be better off without it. Also, there is no sprinting. Instead, you get a dash. I like that.There are no quicksaves in the game. You can only save in specific points in the levels and sometimes the game autosaves for you. Not a big deal since the levels aren't long anyway, so worst case you lose a few minutes of progress.Your loadout is pretty standard. Melee, pistols, shotguns, rocket launcher and the "BFG". The weapons lack impact, which is a shame. The only weapons I used were the bow, throwing katana, revolver and the double-barreled shotgun. The rocket launcher was a joke that did almost no damage, or at least it felt like that.The first two episodes were boring. Really boring. It couldn't get any more generic. Episode three looked and played a bit better, but it still didn't click for me and I couldn't play any longer. The level design itself reminds me of community-made levels rather than actual developers working on a fully-fledged game. I got stuck in a lot of places and had to reload. Sometimes I dropped through the floor. Sometimes the enemies got stuck and ran straight into a wall. Overall, the AI isn't great and the pathfinding is as simple as it gets. They just run in your direction.One good thing I can say about the game is the amount of secrets each level has. It really is the best thing about the game.To sum it up, it's not a terrible game. It's their first game and it shows, but at least it's playable. Is it worth 19,99€ though? In my opinion, no. There will be more than enough people that'll enjoy this game, but not me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: First Impressions count a lot, especially in a genre as crowded as Retro/Throwback/Boomer/Whatever shooters, and Dread Templars wasn't the most positive, with a decidedly "cheap" feel, from the unimaginative levels and janky animations to the terrible soundtrack and generic weapons. Things quickly improve, though, and by the time the second episode rolls around, Dread Templar begins to reveal itself as a perfectly competent, if decidedly generic Retro FPS.It has its fair share of flaws though. Most notably, the way the enemies were designed generally doesn't lend itself to the kind of fast-paced, consequences be damned combat style the genre has become known for. See, enemies in Dread Templar mostly come in two flavors, melee enemies, many of whom are noticeably faster than the player, and ranged enemies, who will happily start shooting you from halfway across the map, often with homing projectiles. What this means is that it's almost never advisable to face hordes of enemies head on instead of picking them off from a distance or simply running backwards while holding down the fire button. The slow motion ability attempts to remedy this, but its duration, even after a handful of upgrades, is generally too short to have much on an impact.The biggest failing of Dread Templar however, is that it just doesn't have much of an identity of its own. Everything it does has been done elsewhere and often better. The levels can at times look fairly impressive, but quickly start to blend together, the weapons are fine, but lack any true standouts and the boss fights are somewhat anticlimactic, as well as often easier than the levels surrounding them.A slight recommendation to fans of the genre then, but if you're just getting into it, maybe try something like DUSK first.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished this early access build, and I gotta say DO NOT make more levels like the last 2, in episode 3 (the ice cave ones)... I don't know if the team got rushed but those two levels make a fresh and fun experience plummet into repetitiveness and frustration. Every single encounter it's literally the same - 4 ice scorpion/bugs that slow you to a crawl if they bite you, 2 huge ice xenomorph aliens and 2 mages that spawn enemies. Add to that an uninspired bland environment and it just doesn't fit with the previous levels of the game.The game itself (aside from ep 3) is awesome. Fast paced shooter with proper mechanics, powerups with a cool arsenal making it fun to decimate enemies. There is also an upgrading system in the game which allows you to upgrade weapons and powerups with upgrade tokens you find around the level, giving a good incentive to explore the interesting and detailed environments. Amazing game however it falls flat on episode 3
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Make it past the first 10 minutes of slog and it's a great game.Quick switching guns is fun and snappy, especially shotgun to double shotgun and back. There is a good amount of enemy variety to keep things interesting. Good roster of weapons, as mentioned in other reviews the trap shooter feels weird, maybe make it a usable like bullet time instead of a dedicated weapon. Maps have some cool visuals.It's good. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Such a delight to play though, fast-paced setting, has that old school feeling which i love, secrets, really does feel like doom in a way and it feels good playing through it all the way.Really can't wait for this to come out of Early Access, they deserve the support because i can see something great coming out of this.For sure something i will be coming back to often, i only now finished it on normal difficulty and will for sure try to beat the other difficulties in my spare time. If you want to just chill, kill/slash some demons, this game is great, it deserves muuuch more recognition.Fingers crossed full release will blow it up ;)Happy slaying! :D(p.s. the "Last level" in the EA is everything i've ever wanted... no spoilers but, its great, you really get to let loose.)
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game provides everything it says on the tin. It's a great action-shooter with some customizable weapon upgrades, a well-implemented Bullet Time system, dope weapons, and exciting boss fights. My main complaint is that the Level 3 tier upgrades are far more interesting and apparent then the others. I like how getting the cooler upgrades rewards exploration, but I wish that gap was smaller.There's a cool character in the game art, but there's no real story to see at all. The game gives you Quake-Style text entries between episodes. These could still be cool, but they need a writing facelift (At least if the game plans on not having cutscenes), getting all DND with it and writing some atmosphere into these texts can still give the game some excitement between levels. Another thing I note is the environments in Episode 2 are far more interesting than the first. The second is a trip through a very colorful version of hell, while episode 1 has some, kinda boring crypts, to run through. But these are nitpicks and very subjective. This game is a great time and I'm excited for the full release!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say, I really like it so far.The Bow and Katana are really nice, and the dash is addictive. Weapons overall feel great and the upgrade system is really cool - especially the ability to reset everything encourages experiments.It feels good exploring the levels and hunting for secrets.If there is one thing I would love to see it would be enemy collision. Especially with weapons like the Katanas it feels strange that I can just run through enemies.Other than that I think this could become an excellent entry in this retro FPS market.Congratulations to the Devs, I think you're onto something here!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I expected it to be and more. Fast paced, awesome music, and fantastic weapon design. Dread Templar is bound to be one of my favorite retro styled FPS games whenever it leaves Early Access. I definitely recommend playing this game if you are into games like DUSK, Amid Evil, or Doom.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; If you like retro shooter gameplay, and would like to have fun, buy it now!I will just start listing what comes to mind, that makes me love this game, then write some experiences from my first 8 hours of playing on the hardest difficulty so far. Smooth movement with air controll using the mouse, running feels similar to classic doom (taking a short time to reach full speed), satisfying meaty gun sounds and very good feedback with lots of gore, build variety that actually changes gameplay, bullet time, stylish awesome visuals, amazing soundtrack, atmosphere, very good enemy and level design, exploration with rewarding secrets to find, weapon swapping combos combined with positioning during combat.I started my first playthrough on the hardest difficutly, witch is called Hell. I died a lot, but as i kept going, i got familiar with the enemy types, and my weapon combos, thus increasing my damage output, started using bullet time sparingly, for short periods of time at the most needed moments, improvede my tactics about using the wrist gun to stun the most dangerous enemies, and got good at dodging different attacks. The game gave me a huge sense of adapting and learning through progression. I also never found ANY of the weapons useless, i kept using pistols kimbo for sniping when my bow was on cooldown and i didnt want to waste revolver ammunition, and the super shotgun did not replace the normal shotgun, because even if i skipped the reloading animation momentarily for the super shotgun, it had to be finished later, so after i fired it, i had to stick with the basic shottie for higher maintained dps. I used them in the following tradition: one shot from the normal, followed by a super shotgun blast, and again a normal, then either swapped to dual smgs, or kept unloading the simple shotgun. All in all, i just find myself replaying the whole game, and i am having so much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A five star boomer shooter experience. Plenty of cool weapons and enemies to blast apart. Many cryptic secrets. All I need to enjoy the chunky campaign.    At least it would be five stars, if not for a few issues.The metal soundtrack is great but it's also an incessant cacophony. Exploring a map for secrets for 30 minutes: still thumping along like you're in the thick of it. I would appreciate downtime in the soundtrack when not acting out a killing machine. The quality of the maps start to deteriorate somewhat in Episode three, and definitely the last two. There's mostly a lack of detail and polish I saw in the beginning, and while the game gets better with more weapon upgrades, some of the environments were so bland to look at it got a tad repetitive going from enemy wave to enemy wave. With New Game+, "horde" mode, a secret difficulty, and how awesomely fun the core shooting is, I would absolutely recommend Dread Templar to FPS fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A big juicy "boomer shooter", with a few rough edges here and there, but it's engaging, rewarding, and packed with well hidden secret areas in decently designed levels, including very rewarding "super secrets" which grant amazing rewards. I particularly like the Rune system, which reminds me of Painkiller's Tarot Cards since Dread Templar also has Silver and Gold variants of these upgrades you can equip and change at any time with these statues. Silver upgrades are minor but easier to find, often passive bonuses, and gold upgrades are amazing and will often result in changing your guns into more powerful versions! Some of the best secrets in Dread Templar involve references to other retro shooters, such as a big secret involving a certain man who "lived again", whatever that means. ;)I just wish that Dread Templar's difficulty was more consistent and rose at an expected rate. You will fight a boss at the end of an episode that feels very much like a final boss, then suddenly your journey will continue which isn't unwelcome since I wanted more. Just, expect way more episodes than just 3, this is a juicy game to get into! Eventually, you will hit the final boss for real, and the difficulty is as challenging as you'd expect.The only real problem is that the gunplay isn't as satisfying as I'd like. The game relies more on screen shaking and view tilting rather than a nice sense of recoil and weapon power, makes the character feel sort of like they are floating around just a bit and not quite as grounded. It isn't THAT bad, the gunplay, and I still enjoyed blasting hordes of demons into giblets!We are truly in a golden age of retro shooters. It's funny, because I grew up with these kinds of games too, being born on 1987 and growing up in the 90s. It's awesome to see a renewed appreciation for sprawling level design, secret areas, and carrying WAY TOO MANY guns for your own good!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, when compared to games in the same genre, Dread Templar sucks.I originally started playing this back when it first released in EA and shelved it down because just it wasn't good. I figured I'd pick it back up 3 years  later and see if it felt any better, and I think it somehow feels worse. That could just be me, though, because I've played nearly every good boomer shooter to release in that time frame. Your character is incredibly slow with a dash that recharges incredibly slowly while you fight enemies that are faster than you (some of which when they hit you slow you down even more) and do a ton of damage in very basic, relatively flat combat arenas. Enemies hit you hard, so you'll always be low on health, mostly because you move so slowly you can't really avoid damage.  The dev realized how BS most of the fights were and put save stations roughly 3 minutes apart in most areas. And it shouldn't be like that. Your game should be hard enough to have some kind of tension to it, but not so hard as to encourage save scumming every 3 minutes. Most of the encounters I had during the 3rd chapter went like this: Save, die, respawn, die, WIN, save at the next point which is on the other side of the arena, die, respawn, die, respawn, die, respawn, WIN, save at the next save point. And from what I remember, this was the first 2 chapters as well. You rarely ever feel, as the description puts it "the scariest thing in hell and beyond." The scariest thing about this game is that sinking feeling you get when you have 2 HP and realize you haven't saved in 30 minutes because constantly stopping at save points ruins the flow of the game and you decided it was a good idea to just pass up the saves. The bullet time is all but useless. You have to kill enemies to charge it, which is easier said than done because most of the enemies are just bullet sponges. After you charge it, you get roughly 3 seconds of it before it runs out. At that point, just remove the mechanic because, as I said, it's all but useless. Circling back to being slow, the maps are huge. Your character feels like he's moving at a snail's pace. Exploration IS NOT fun. The game wants you to explore for all of these secrets and side areas, but you move so slowly that it just drags on and on and on. And the worst part? If you don't explore, you don't get upgrade tokens. If you don't get tokens, you become quickly underpowered. You become underpowered, everything beats you into a bloody mess (faster than they already do). See the pattern? Speaking of the upgrade system: It is unique.  You NEED upgrades to do anything meaningful in this game. I think that might also be a reason that I think so lowly of this game, because if you just played the game like a normal person and didn't secret hunt every area for every little thing, you'd be horribly underpowered. The soundtrack is fine, but nothing to write home about and feels very generic for this kind of game. Nothing spectacular.Enemies are varied, but mostly bullet sponges that do a ton of damage very quickly and will very quickly outpace you and kill you before you can really do anything if you don't catch them in time. If you do decide to play it, pick it up on sale or just watch someone play it on Youtube. I promise, you're not missing out on much.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is a mixture of old and new shooter elements. Having a chunky, pixelated art style and level designs inspired by Doom, Heretic, HeXen, Amid Evil, and many others, it is a wonderful blend of those games.The story is there, but not the focus, but still a nice touch to the overall experience. The weapons and game play are smooth, fast, and chaotic. As you unlock more of your arsenal and get upgrade runes, it is at its best. All of the weapons feel unique and fill a specific purpose in combat and quick swapping is encouraged as the switch animation is so short and can interrupt reloads so the demons stand no chance.The music is probably my favorite aspect of the game as it is a blasting metal OST with different themes for each episode that melds well with the atmosphere of each level. The enemies are quite varied and most are fun to fight. The bosses aren't too bad, maybe a bit hard to dodge some attacks. Everything is executed quite well and a fun experience for those that enjoy older shooters and possibly the newer ones. Beyond that, I had a few bugs which weren't game breaking, but annoying. Occasionally enemies shoot projectiles through walls, sometimes reloading can mess with the end of level stats like secrets you found then died or something and reload and the counter is incorrect. Besides that, I would recommend this game to fans of Dusk, Amid Evil, Ion Fury, Doom, Heretic, HeXen, Blood, Shadow Warrior, Quake, and the countless other greats.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is an incredible fast-paced first-person shooter made by a solo dev (damn dude).You should definitly give it a try if you like the genre (old-school classics like DOOM or more recently New Blood games).The OST also is amazing. Truly, one of the best I have heard in a game like this!Can't wait to see more over Early Access...
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: They are a lot of old-school FPS out-there, I tried many of them, this one is among the best. Very equilibrated even in “Hard+” difficulty. You will need to know how to attack and move in each situation. Map and artwork design also very pleasant. However, I don’t like how they implemented the secrets, you LITTERALY need to wall-glitch to find some of these secret rooms, which gives powerful and sometimes essential weapons. They are a few bugs here and there, but no game-breaking bugs, and this is still alpha so no worries there. I’d say it’s worth the 15 bucks even at this stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is pretty damn fun game, albeit rather rough around the edges. By the end I truly enjoyed the frantic pace of the combat and swapping to various weapons of the game, all of which are tremendously useful throughout the game. Though the game took me a bit to truly enjoy because I did not understand the importance of secret hunting, since this is where the bulk of weapon upgrades will come from. Before this had clicked with me I found the difficulty of the game to be pretty random, and punishing due the game only allowing saves at certain spots. But once you settle into the groove of collecting all the secrets you can and upgrading the weapons to powerful variants the game really its its stride and proves to be a very enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like fast paced shooters with weapons that are fun to use and responsive? Do you like it when combat in a shooter keeps you on your toes and forces you to make quick decision as well as fight fast and hard to survive? Do you like having lots of enemies to shoot and kill? yes? Then buy this game. It's that simple. Even in it's EA state I definitely think it's worth the mere asking price of $15(USD). Combat is probably best compared to Doom Eternal. It even has the fast weapon switching of Eternal. In terms of aesthetics and presentation I think it's like a mix between Quake and Killing Floor. Enemy type and behavior is more in line with Quake I'd say. It's got flying enemies that shoot stuff at you (i.e. Scrag), enemies that shoot grenades (i.e. Ogre), and enemies that rush into melee (i.e. Knights/Death knights). The look and presentation of the enemies is more like something you'd see in Killing Floor. The melee enemies look very similar to the Gorefasts in that game for example. The OST is certainly reminiscent to something you would hear in Kiiling Floor.I would recommend playing on hard if you want to get the best experience. I found normal to be too easy at least in the early levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  This is an awesome retro shooter designed like the games I grew up with in the 1990's.  Smooth action, nice weapons and skills and great fun around a group of enemies.  If you loved the FPS titles from the 1990's like Hexan and Heretic, this is a must have.  Buy it today, or at least ask me to buy it for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I heard it put perfectly, If Dusk if a 5 star restaurant experience, this game is a takeaway Maccas experience. Quick, dirty and nowhere near as good as a restaurant quality meal. In saying that, like a Maccas meal, its still enjoyable and satisfying at the time. Rough around the edges and leaves you desiring more though.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the game started very strongly, but I was pretty board by the end of episode 2.  I don't think it's a bad game and wish Steam has a middle ground between recommend yes or no.  It's still a solid fps, but something was missing for me in this current state.  I don't really like the upgrade system, as many of the upgrades seemed to make little difference.  Also, none of the weapons really felt memorable.  I think there are much better old school shooters, but if you need more this is worth checking out.With all this being said, I am excited to check this out again once there is a final release.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is game definetly inspired by 90's shooters and it's a good one...but not perfect. Positives +-Well done level design; -Intresting and disgusting enemies;-Very good soundtrack;-A very good arsenal to play with;-Bullet time;-Upgrade system with a lot of unclockables and abilities to choose;-A lot of secrets-Very challenging and scalable difficulty.Negatives --The game is challenging but the bosses are insanely hard, probably unbalanced even on normal (except maybe for the third one);-The music is good but repetitive after a while, maybe they should alternate more between silence\ambient and the metal OST;-The main character sounds weird, it seems male for the most parts but when it jumps sounds like a female;-A map could be useful because some levels are quite intricate;-The story is narrated with a black screen and few words...maybe a little drawing in the background explaing the scene could be a nice touch because for now it's not a very good way of storytelling.For an early access it's good but it could be much better, i hope to see patches in the future that correct the issues i've found so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome old school fps. But not as good as the best of the genre (like Dusk, Amid Evil, Iron Fury or Postal Braindamaged) mainly because of the lack of quicksaving. I really don't get why some of the new old school fps are doing this (also Wrath or Prodeus). The reason can't be to avoid save scumming because you can still do it most of the time, you just have to backtrack to the last save point. And btw. on the highest difficulty you pretty much have to play like this as enemies deal an insane amount of damage and for some reason devs thought it would be a good idea to take away almost all health items on that difficulty. On the other hand the game givey you way too much ammo imo. Especially considering that you have two strong weapons (Katana which you can throw and the bow) each one recharging ammo over time.The skill system motivates you looking around for secrets and playing around the different skills can be fun. BUT there are some skills which are pretty much useless while others are overpowered, like one making boss fights a joke and even though you can find that one quite late you can still use it for the last two bosses. And in general it's not the case that you find the weak ones early and the OP ones late, it's often the other way around. So yeah, the balancing of that system could be better imo. (Oh and the rocket launcher is also a bit weak.)A bit weird and kinda annoying for achievement hunters is that you have to play through the game twice, because for some reason the achievements for beating the game for the two highest difficulties do not stack.But the overall level design, gunplay, different enemy types, weapons and the soundtrack is all pretty good. If you are a fan of the genre, this one is for you even though I wouldn't consider it a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been on my wishlist since launch of early access.  I always hesitated to get it due to thinking it was going to blend in with other boomer shooters on my backlog.  Finally I tried it out and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game has some stellar combat and ideas.  The game starts off pretty slow but as soon as finish the super secret on mission one you will start to realize how you are supposed to play the game.  Secrets may seem optional but finding them grants you with upgrade shards and emblems that drastically change how a weapon functions and how a player will face encounters.My main complaints with the game are the player noises.  The jump noise is sucks and is the worst "hut" I've heard in a boomer shooter.  The health pickup is just gross sounding and I hope it will be changed.

_childDocuments_.review: The music for every level is great; a constant upbeat metal. All the guns feel very chonky. Gameplay feels very smooth and satisfying (apart from when enemies occasionally shoot you through walls). The bosses are also really fun to fight. Also nice to have a game like this avoid the cliche of spawning enemies directly behind you or just out of nowhere. Def recommend if you enjoy fast paced shooters without a bunch of extra gimmicks.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A solid FPS in the vein of Quake. Movement is fast, as are the enemies. It's on the hard side, I'd say, in a good way. The enemies hit pretty hard but the bosses aren't much to write home about. Some great music sets the scene. I do wish there were more weapons that would inflict status effects. I loved the projectile blade weapon. Good stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: If "Quakelike" isn't a thing yet, I'm declaring it right now. I don't mean "pixelated boomer shooter", I specifically mean that horror aesthetic. Otherworldly, uncanny if not nightmarish environments to kill hellish monstrosities in, while sitting on a solid foundation of a boomer shooter gameplay loop. What I mean, is a lightning-fast power fantasy which wants you to earn it and when you do, you're death incarnate. With that rocking music on top, an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun retro shooter! The weapons are mostly satisfying (I didn't get much use out of the bow and trap launcher), the monsters have nice variety and are well-designed, and the boss battles are unique but not too much of a slog (I finished most of them on the first try, maybe the second).  The level design is a lot of fun, with lots of unexpected and unusual sights. Secrets can be quite hard to find: I think I only found 1 or 2 on every level, though I went out of my way to find the items needed to unlock "super-secrets." I played through the incomplete game on early access, and went back to play the complete campaign after full release, if that tell yo something about how much I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: The first two acts are fine, after that it becomes just frustrating to play. - Claustrophobic arenas, with enemies that use ranged attacks on you at close range, that you can't dodge. - It doesn't matter how many damage upgrades you put into your guns, they are all way too weak.  What's the point of finding a triple rocket launcher, when it can't even kill small enemies? - Upgrades do absolutely nothing. Example: Flying enemies take two hits to kill with the standard bow, and when I put three damage upgrades into it, ...they still take two hits to kill. - Why is ammo so damn scarce, that half the time I'm just waiting for the bow arrows to regenerate so I have anything to shoot with at all? Why did that damn bow timer need to be so slow. Even with both speed upgrades, it still takes something like 30 seconds for your 5 arrows to regenerate.- Hitboxes are EXTREMELY wonky. You often line up your shot perfectly and still miss because it just doesn't get registered.- There is way too few variety in the enemies and the AI is too basic. It's either rush or spam you with seeking ranged attacks.- The enemies have a great visual design, but otherwise are extremely basic. Weak points are just the heads. There is no strategy besides gunning them down. You'd think at least the giant mortar enemies with big gas bubbles on their backs would have a weak point there that they try to protect and can be burst. No. There is none of that sort of stuff.- The later levels feel rushed. The save points there are too far apart, the design seems lackluster.That said, there is some good here and some fun to be had. But ultimately the strong first two acts don't make up for the frustrating final acts. Giving a thumbs down with a heavy heart, as this game does many things right but the bad overweights.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This is kind of a loose recommend. The gameplay overall is tight and responsive, very light RPG elements in the form of upgrade runes, a decent soundtrack, slo-mo mechanics that work fairly well, but there's not much to unpack here.Overall it's solid and doesn't lack in the areas these kinds of games are known for, but simultaneously there's nothing much here to really call attention to itself. Gunplay is solid, I like the different upgrades you can find in the levels but the enemy variety isn't much to write home about. Basic charging/ranged enemies, stronger versions of those, and some bosses that are basically bullet sponges but not enough so to detract from the fun.Level design is fine, nothing really stands out in terms of locale or setting. Sound design is fine across the board, my biggest complaint is you'll go through 5 levels at times and those 5 levels will have the same soundtrack. It got old for me rather quick.I'd pick it up on sale if you decide to at all, other than that you're not really missing much here. There's nothing that this game offers that others don't already.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread templar is one of the best shooters I played in 2021 and it makes you have hope in Early access games. It's fast and bloody, the soundtrack is one of the best I ve ever heard. I love how you can switch guns on the same category with right mouse button which allows you to create some combos and deal more damage in combat. There are a lot of secrets to find which I barely found because I suck at secret hunting and an upgrade system that is kinda cool and allows you to experiment different combinations depending on which guns you like and your playstyle, although if you really want to upgrade everything look for all the secrets. Finally there is a bullet time mechanic that recharges when you kill enemies, I didnt use it that much but its useful  for getting out of a dangerous situation. My only complain with this build are the bosses, the second and last one. The second boss spawns way too many enemies and there is little room for movement, the last boss isn't that bad but you can barely damaga him because he is constantly doing a special attack where he has a shield and throws sime kind of lasers at you.         In conclussion, Dread Templar is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing game and you should buy it right now, its not really long. Your first playthrough should take you between 3 and 4 hours depending if you want the secrets and do the side areas. I suggest playing this game on hard, to me it  felt like a balanced challenge aside from the annoying bosses. Hope my review is useful.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Completely fumbles its weapon upgrade system. You go through levels and find both perk emblems and red gems to unlock perk slots for you and your weapons. Gold emblems can radically change each weapon and make combat more unique and strategic. Except the red gems needed to unlock the perk slots are bizarrely scarce and more hidden than the perk emblems. Worst of all, unlock progress is tied to the difficulty. You can retry levels with a guide to find missing items but cant keep them on other difficulties. So no collecting on Normal to prep for a full Hard run.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun so far. Great soundtrack and atmosphere, guns are fun to shoot and sound great. Really like that Blood secret btw. Overall, can't really complain about much, I stumbled upon this completely by chance but I'm glad I did. I expect this game to land on *Insert boomer shooter channel*'s review list sometime soon. HOWEVER. Small but very annoying thing the devs need to address; You are completely vulnerable while saving, during cut scenes, and while upgrading. I can't begin to tell you how annoying it is to be upgrading and figuring out what I want to do with my stuff only to immediately die upon exiting because an enemy was attatcking me, with no audio cues as well. Also, I think they should remove the character moan upon picking up health. Little annoying and loud, a simple beep like a heart monitor or something would be nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I've played tons of boomer shooters, and this one felt like such wasted potential. Gorgeous visuals, interesting weapons, fantastic music, but it's held back by poor visual/audio feedback and unbalanced fights. Often you'll be low on health and suddenly die without knowing why because enemies give you very poor indication that they're attacking.Movement somehow feels soft.Last boss was an absolute nightmare. Unbalanced attacks and absolutely awful accessibility (transparent red attacks on a red background with a red boss isn't something you should expect players to be able to read and dodge). I think you're supposed to unlock secrets in the previous levels to make the fight easier, but I don't think it should be so unbalanced if you didn't unlock them.Last chapter in general felt like a chore, which is a shame because the first 4 were pretty fun.Would recommend if not for the last few levels + boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ok. It's Doom-like but it doesn't get you hyped like DOOM does. The soundtrack is kinda meh. The player moves fine but jumping is weird. When you're close to an edge you wont jump, you'll just run off the cliff. Flick shots don't work/register. And if they do they aren't doing much damage. Strafing doesn't really help you dodge enemy attacks from guns. You watch enemies spawn right in front of you.  The upgrade menu could use some work. Map layouts could be better. It's cheap and it's ok in short burst.

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar asks "What if we made a pure old school shooter but layered a bullet time mechanic and every lesson Doom Eternal taught on top of it?" And the answer is "that would be awesome."weird that this game doesn't have "Overwhelmingly Positive"reviews. Over the last 5 or 6 years FPS fans have been treated to a resurgence of the genre. The stagnation of the CoD clone era died and developers started finally looking back to what made FPS games so engaging in the first place. Movement, pacing, level design, enemy design. At every budget we've gotten great FPS games. From the Metro series to the incomparable Doom reboots all the way down to the indie gems Amid Evil, Dusk, Ultrakill, Project Warlock and others.If there is one legitimate complaint to level against the brilliance of games like Ion, Dusk and Amid Evil it's that they might stick a bit too closely to the classic formula. This year we got Ultrakill which is one of the very best shooters ever made and a legitimately innovative game unlike any other shooter out there and here we have a game that sticks very closely to the formula but has one crucial element that elevates it to excellence. For the most part this is an EXCELLENT retro shooter. Fast paced, smartly designed, tight and polished, it has perfectly balanced enemies, sprawling levels that are big enough to act as places to explore but never so big it gets frustrating, and a great arsenal of guns. This is the foundation of every great shooter from HalfLIfe to Doom Eternal. Dread Templar brings this perfect core design together by adding a light progression system into the mix. Even on hard it doesn't feel like this is crucial to beat the game but it IS an fantastic incentive for fully exploring levels.Dread Templar is basically Dusk with a dash dodge, a progression system, and a kind of "slayer gate" system where you can find "side areas" that are difficult arenas or platforming challenges that award extra progression items, runes and ammo. If you're the kind of person who likes exploration but thinks just finding "secrets" ultimately feels hollow, this game is for you. If you love old school shooters AND Doom Eternal, you are 100 percent going to love Dread. It's one of the best FPS games of the current era. An absolute steal.

_childDocuments_.review: It was hard to decide whether to recommend or not.On one hand, the game has tight controls, satisfying shooting, fun weapon upgrade system, and some interesting locations.On the other, it has some bad game design decisions (or technical flaws). Enemies often attack you right after you come around the corner, so you have no chance to react and evade the projectile. There are also enemies that can jump on you, and oftentimes they jump from behind a corner or even through a wall.Finally, there are various issues with collisions, specifically enemy projectiles (or maybe camera?). More often than not it looks like a projectile is going to move just past your character, but it still hits and damages you. I played every major shooter since Wolfenstein 3D and never had this issue. Considering all enemies in the game use projectile attacks (no hitscanners, thank god!), this is a huge issue.I finished the game on hard, and died so many times because of these issues desribed above. Honestly, enemies on hard here have much lower reaction times than in Quake or Doom on Nightmare (talking about 1993 Doom).The game has slow mo, and it looks like it was put as an afterthought so the players can have a chance against these monsters with insane reaction times. However, it doesn't work that well, because unless you know there's an enemy there, you won't have time to activate slo mo, and if you would activate it before each corner, you would run out of charge very quickly.As I said, it was hard to decide whether to recommend or not, but the final episode made the choice easy. It has extremely lackluster level design (basically, intestine-like corridors with tons of enemies) and the final boss is very lame. You have to fight a red colored boss in a red arena while avoiding red projectiles and red aoe effects. And the boss has so much HP that it takes almost all your ammo (all weapons combined) to defeat him. Extremely frustrating encounter and a very unsatisfying ending to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: Yes, it's another boomer shooter. However this one has a few things going for it that I enjoy. First off the level design is pretty good and interesting. Secrets are well hidden but with a bit of tenacity and common sense you will find most of them and it is recommended that you do considering you can get power runes and currency to use said runes by finding secrets. This game also has some good weapons that can be further powered up by the runes you find. The line up of weapons I have come across have mostly been standard such as Pistols, Bow, Shotgun, etc. But there are a few that stand out such as a trap launcher that can damage and stun enemies and a gauntlet that can shoot a powerful beam to stop even the strongest monsters in their tracks. All weapons can be enhanced by runes but even the most common of weapons can be turned into something more interesting. For example, I found a rune that allows me to use my pump action shotgun from long distances without the damage or spread degrading too much. Pair that up with a damage increase and weapon fire rate plus runes and you have yourself one mean ass shotgun that rivals the best of them. The game moves smoothly and has a simple slow motion feature and dash mechanic. You will use the former to help lay waste to enemies and the latter to helping traverse the map and find items and secrets. The enemy roster is quite basic feeling but there are a few that stand out (much like the weapons) and this game also has boss fights. It's a pretty solid title that has offered me plenty of fun so far.Sound/Music: A lot of these games have great sound effects. I feel some of the explosions don't pop enough but the bullet weapons sound really good. Something about the SMG's just really makes me happy. This game also goes for the "heavy metal" stock option for music. However I don't mind this music as it just sounds awesome. The riffs are pretty wicked. By far my favorite metal soundtrack from the pack.Controls: Movement can be customized and your character is nice and fast. The game feels loose and that's a good thing. The action can get a little hectic but remember to use your slow motion. You will move in normal speed while your enemies are slowed to a crawl. Sometimes traversing small spots that you need to crouch in is awkward and you can even get stuck unless you keep holding down the crouch button. I didn't see a crouch toggle option and am hoping they add one in the future.Graphics: It's done in the Unity engine and looks and feels a lot like Quake. Minus all the brown. It's a compliment.In conclusion I highly suggest getting this one. It has me hooked and I can't wait to run through it again on a harder difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I could say a lot, but it won't be read due to how Steam buries older, edited reviews of once Early-Access products. I'll just say this: The game is great. It has some shortcomings, but assuming you're playing on Nightmare(+), the general flow and feel of combat is something unique and visceral. Enemies react very quickly. Enemies deal tons of damage. Health is limited. Sometimes, an enemy capable of killing you instantly spawns right in front of you - and yet it's completely fair. With instant weapon switching, a non-spammable dash function to reserve for kneejerk reactions, a refillable bullet time meter, and one or two means of disabling enemies, you're given the ability to address any threat as it comes, without ever trivializing fights.The combat is predictable, yet brutal, and therefore satisfying. If you play methodically, you win. If you know how to utilize your set of tools and react on the fly, you stand a good chance of winning. If you refuse to use all of your weapons, or slip up and eat more than a couple of hits, you'll probably die. There is a definitive moment-to-moment rhythm to the moving and shooting, which you can break as needed to power through scenarios, and yet doing so never devalues the lethality of the enemies. Death is always looming over you, and yet you can tell it to ♥♥♥♥ itself. This is proper power fantasy.Think Serious Sam, but the enemies are twice as strong, and the enemy count is as low as Quake. Then add some of Nu-Doom's features without all of the fluff like glory kills and loot pinatas. Then sprinkle a bit of Painkiller's atmosphere and aesthetics into the mix. That's this game. I like it very much.

_childDocuments_.review: - - Dusk at home: ...Jokes aside, Dread Templar is not a bad game, it's enjoyable for the most part, but it has some glaring design issues.For the positive side, I liked the fluidity of the combat, the fast-paced weapon switching and the ability to upgrade and modify your weapons. The music kicks ass! Slow time is cool too, but it feels more like a spectacle than a useful mechanic.But let me address some issues with the game:- Minimap. There is none. Why?- The weapons. There are too many of them. Yes, I said that. Its really clunky to juggle a dozen weapons all the time, and they don't even have a secondary attack, which is a huge missed opportunity in my opinion. Remember Painkiller? It has like 4 weapons, all with distinctive secondary attacks - it was easy and fun to use. The lesson is: quality over quantity. Also, the Trap Launcher is a utility weapon, which I pretty much need to use all the time, why doesn't it have its own dedicated button? Why does it need to occupy the 5th slot, which everyone knows that belongs to the rocket launcher (or any other explosive weapon)?- No weapon wheel. Ties to the previous problem.- Level design. Some maps are fine, but some are just dreadful (hah). Episode 1 is kinda meh. I like Episode 2 and 4, but I really, REALLY hate Episode 3. It looks like crap, has the most annoying enemies, and really hard to navigate. And when I found out that enemies can pop up from the ice cubes randomly, instantly and without any indication or ways to prevent that (like pre-firing them or something) I wanted to break the keyboard on the head whoever came up with that bullsh!t. Episode 5 looks like diarrhea and it's very short - feels really rushed. There are invisible walls everywhere, which really defeats the whole purpose of exploring the maps for secrets.- I can barely see the projectiles. There are no hitscanning enemies, which is great, but its really hard to spot the projectiles that enemies are shooting at me. How should I effectively kill  enemies shooting  projectiles in a  environment? It's a huge problem most of the time. Also, they make almost no sound. Sometimes I just minding my own business, then die randomly from some projectile shot from a hundred miles away. No sound cue when enemies die either. The enemy attacks and deaths should to be telegraphed much better.- Balance. Huge difficulty spikes randomly. A lot of times there is not enough health and armor in the maps. Maybe in secret places, but they are REALLY obscure. I know secrets should be hard to find, but come on! I don't want to carefully examine every pixel of the map to find some really needed health, armor or upgrade shard. It breaks up the flow, and its not fun at all. Well, the minimap would have helped in this, too.- Annoying enemies. There are three types of enemies: bullet sponges that rush to you face, bullet sponges that rush to your face AND shoot projectiles, and bullet sponges that fire projectiles from a million miles away (which I cannot really see). I'm sure you can see the problem here. Also, I expected a completely new enemy roster in every chapter, but they are recycled from previous chapters (sometimes they doesn't even fit into the environment). It's really disappointing. Better enemy variety would have helped.- Bosses. They are either trivial and laughably easy or freaking impossible.Other minor annoyances:- For the love of DOG, please remember my katana setting, when I reload a game! It's annoying that I have to change to throw mode every time, because the game just forgets it.- The music. As I said, it's good. But my main problem is that it NEVER lets up. There are no ambient tracks and no dynamic music which ramps up when the action starts, just constant blasting of metal music, which gets really tiring after a while. Especially when you need to comb the map for secrets for half an hour.- I don't really get the need for this save system. Auto-saves at random AND fixed save points? Why? Just give me a quicksave at F5, and thats it. Every old-school shooter does that.- Clipping and collision issues.I'd give this game a  at this stage. I can cleary see the effort put in, but some issues just need to be fixed to this be an above average shooter and a fun time. I give it a thumbs up for support, but I'd give a mixed one if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10I can see the potential here at making a retro shooter and I love me a good retro shooter, but there a lot things holding it back. Now before you tell me, yes, I get that it's in early access and that it could improve. But, if previous early access games like Amid Evil, Dusk and Ion Fury are anything to go off of, the Early Access build should leave you satisfied enough, not a sour taste in your mouth. Dread Templar especially leaves a sour taste when talking about its negatives. So as is, I recommend playing Amid Evil, Dusk, Hellbound and/or Ion Fury instead.+ Good soundtrack.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.- No quick saves. If your game is balanced enough to not need it, then sure, but this game clearly isn't.- Bad boss fights. They tend to lean on spawning other enemies in corners or giving the boss near unavoidable attacks. That's not my idea of fun.- Controls feel clunky. They may be better than the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games, but that doesn't excuse Dread Templar. Granted, it's hard to put my finger on it, but I certainly get a sense of input delay whenever I perform certain actions.- Bad level design moments. There's one point before the second boss, where they throw more than a dozen enemies in a large arena surrounded by lava, some of which can throw fireballs that do massive splash damage. What were they thinking?

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Good, fast-paced retro shooter, with great audio tracks, but riddled with all types of bugs. I do tentatively recommend that, as while the bugs are annoying, if you are aware of them, the game is really enjoyable.Dread Templar is fast-paced, classic rendition of a retro shooter. Like most of these games, the story is not really interesting, as it feels that its only just to get the game going. Pros:- Esthetic is really good, and I feel that most level design is really great- Love the inclusion of "Super Secrets", although it is a fact that most of them require more than just exploration of the map to find them- The music track for most of the levels is really great- A small thing that i always like - the maps are designed in a way, that in nearly all levels you can backtrack to the start. This in most cases prevents being locked out of goodies or secrets- Weapon design is also good, and i personally feel that the balance is great. Unfortunately, for the classic weapons it took a long time to start "feeling" them- Enemies are quite varied, though most of their AI is simple at best.Cons:- The upgrade system, while at its core is great, it is very poorly presented. For most upgrades you have little information what it actually does. For example: "Increases damage level 1" doesn't tell you if it's major or minor buff. 5% damage might be completely useless, but 50% would be something you'd always want.- Bugs. Bugs again. I'll do a short list of them, which you can encounter as early as the tutorial* The icon for Dash recharge uses Black Bow icon* Katana Slaughter 3 is named "2" in the tooltip* This one is big: Enemies may shoot through walls, including with explosive projectiles* Related to above, explosions can damage through walls* Monsters may walk into the player* Some monsters/attack seem to be missing audio. Which is extremely sad, as audio is one of the best parts of this game.* Weapon audio is always interrupted with weapon switching - this does affect immersion

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely repetitive. Weapons do NOT feel very powerful because enemies are so tanky for some reason. Level design is very meh. Some cool ideas, but I constantly feel like I'm just barely strong enough to smash enemy hoards. Game seems to tell me the katanas and slow motion are useful, but everytime I use them, no matter how I spec, I still feel weak. I'm a very competent FPS player, so the game feels fairly easy to me, but my point is that the game doesn't make me FEEL powerful. Doom Eternal succeeds in forcing you into a specific gameplay loop to conserve ammo, health, etc. This game just makes me lose ammo and arbitrarily switch weapons until I can find more for the weapons I actually want to use.tl;dr many interesting ideas, nearly all of them feel half-baked.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my Steam for years, yet it's never clicked with me until now.Dread templar is a retro FPS that in its atmosphere reminds me of Dusk a lot, however unlike that game I believe that you have to power through a few bad levels before the game really gets going. First few maps are merely fine, featuring some really boring theming and design. Thankfully, later episodes, especially 3-5 go way harder on creating memorable enviroments.This game has slight RPG experience in that you find runes to equip. Each weapon, and yourself, have 2 rune slots for silver runes, and one for a golden one. Silver runes are plentiful and usually will power you and the weapons up, upgrading ammo, reload speed, damage, and the like. However, it's the gold runes that really make the exploration interesting, as they can change the behavior of your weapons entirely. For example, I really didn't care for Trap Launcher weapon, but finding a rune that would summon a creature on my side when I would fire it helped immensely.I think exploration-wise it's one of the better retro FPS games out there: the levels are short enough, but contain quite a few secrets, and usually a mega secret which requires either a sequence of events or a short questline to complete. Unfortunately, what doesn't help with exploration is that the game feels very janky. It's got plenty of invisible walls, sometimes in places that you really feel you should go through. It's also got a few issues with readability: some ledges aren't meant to stand on, and some pits that you feel like you can go into will just kill you. This prevented me from fully immersing myself in exploration, especially since the game's got a strange save system where you can only save with special crystals. I don't get that system at all. Each level has 3-4 save points and you can just go back to them at any time, so the lack of a quick save is just a timewaster.The arsenal and enemy roster are solid, with every enemy feeling like a threat but not many being overly tanky. Your weapon selection also has quite a few toys with most being familiar to any FPS player with a few exceptions. My favorites were shotgun, which I modded to be way better at range, and the bow with constantly replenishing ammo.I think Dread Templar has a few issues, but I'd say 80% of it is great, with the rest merely being "good". It starts off fairly slow, but quickly finds its footing.
