_childDocuments_.review: Boy, oh boy, Where to start?Welp, I loved the game for the first two chapters or so, the levels, the enemies, the design, and the gunplay, were all pristine; it was fun to get new weapons, the gunplay was great and meaty, the enemies kept melting whilst I would use all of the repertoire of my arsenal; it was a darn good time... And then, the damn game turns into a slog fest with a complete unbalanced level of difficulty...This happens for two reasons: First, the game has health pickups, no regen; which is fine, it's a "boomer shooter" after all, but here's the thing; the pickups aren't well scattered nor well given to the player... Some areas have more pickups than others, sometimes they're arbitrarily scattered through some of the later levels, it's very messy...Then there's the second reason, perhaps the worst of them all...The game isn't properly balanced... At first is excellently balanced, the first two chapters are great, but as soon as I hit the third the problems started, sometimes you get into areas where the game keeps throwing enemies at you, other times the game chooses to lock you into very small areas filled with huge enemies giving you a very small room to maneuver; Worst of all? The damn game has a mechanic in which you're slowed down when getting hit by an enemy for some strange reason; you can change it and by getting an upgrade but...You have to find this upgrade, they're runes that you can find throughout the level which can give you higher damage, fire rates, or even cool things like removing this obnoxious mechanic; but you have to find these items first they're not just given to you for the most part... Not only that, but to actually equip them, you have to spend blood crystals, which is a type of currency -also-, scattered throughout the levels.In the end you're left with two choices to push through these issues; you either persist despite how frustrating the game can get, or you drop down the difficulty and deal with how boring the game becomes...So in the end, because of this, sadly this isn't a recommended game for me.It's such a shame too, because I really, really liked the game at the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - It's a good game, it could be improved a lot though. I like the level design of this game a lot, music is also very good. The boss fights are cool, they have actual mechanics which isn't that common in FPS games.Unfortunately I feel like the game falls off a lot in the second half, the first half of it is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, up to an 8/10 level game, but then its just starts to go downhill. The biggest problem is the weapons. They literally feel the same, within their effective range most weapons do very similar damage. This would make some sense if this was a multiplayer game, but it is not, so...Enemies are very bulletspongy, and the weapons makes this feel ever worse. Like it takes 3 close range shots with the sawed off shotgun to kill a regular enemy, rocket launcher is the exact same but to mid-long range. This is the most limp ♥♥♥♥ rocker launcher I have used in recent memory, it is more of a threat to yourself due to splash damage than it is to the enemies. Like 3 direct rocket launcher hits to kill a regular ass enemy? Thats just not good. There is the glove weapon that really stands out being the most powerfull but you barely get to use it because there is no ammo for it.There is some upgrades but whenever I got a new one, it didn't feel like anything has changed at all. Like give me a slight boost to one of the weapon classes but in the same time the enemies get stronger too so it's like absolutely nothing has changed.If they would change the weapons to feel different it would immediately improve this game a lot. There is a bunch of things they could do to make them better. I would either remove reloading, or make it much, much faster. This would also make weapon comboing much more effective. Adjust the damage numbers to separate weapons a lot more, adjust available ammo accordingly or raise enemy numbers or make them more aggressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Having now played through all five episodes (normal difficulty), I can say that Dread Templar is a good game. It has very smooth controls, the gunplay feels great and the perk mechanic goes well with the otherwise oldschool gameplay. What´s missing here in my opinion is a good story / more background information about the character (he stays very bland) and the game world. I really don´t expect cutscenes like in Turbo Overkill, but at least a story which holds the episodes together would have been nice. It still feels you are thrown in different settings just for the sake of some variety, but it´s not very believable. I think the devs recognized that at the end of episode 5 and therefore threw some "Dusk"-horror in, but this just feels out of place at the end.Same goes for the levels - while some of them show a lot of creativity (e. g. the pirate ship in episode 2), others are kind of generic and repetitive (especially episode 4). Check out Cultic, Turbo Overkill, Dusk or Hrot and you will see what I mean. Anyway, in terms of pure gameplay, Dread Templar gets a clear recommandation from me for all fans of oldschool FPS - even if it´s not a game to come back to after the first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished it yet so this might get updated when I do.Cons: - It's a bit darker than I would like and I'm not sure if it's intentional or not - Lack of map (the level design is very well thought out, but I would say in this case is more like nice thing to have since I do have some occasions that I get a bit confused, but nothing major)Pros: - Gameplay is smooth, responsive and fast - Music is great and goes well with the flow - Some of the weapons are interesting and the others are basically in every boomer shooter, but if it works don't change it and I like we have headshot system (makes the bow quite useful) - I love secrets and this game has a ton of them and some are really well hidden (super secrets) - Maps have this horror diablo like theme to them and I like it. The layout of the maps is also well done and there were some small occasions I got...well not lost, but a bit confused, but I would say nothing major.Overall I really love me some good boomer shooters and this one satisfies that itch quite nicely and I totally recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Dusk.Nearly everything about this game is sheer perfection in my experience. It is to the point where I struggle to find anything negative to say about the game. Weapons feel satisfying to use. Soundtrack is amazing. Every single weapon litteraly feels useful, and the whole rune upgrading system works brilliantly, giving you options to try out different playstyles. Want to rely on bullet time more? Use the upgrade that grants you more bullet time per kill and combine it with the "Neo" rune, allowing you to mow down tons of enemies with the basic pistols. Want to rely on oneshotting monsters with the infernal revolver? Pick the fatality rune for it and along with the Lucky rune to grant it a 55 percent chance of oneshotting everything except bosses. Or build the Infernal revolver around dealing double damage to stunned enemies, which other runes give synergy to... Just an amazing and very well thought out system. Dusk has nothing at all like this. Another interresting and unique thing this game does with the "normal" shotgun and supershotgun is that you have to reload the SSG inbetween shots, so you cant just quickswitch like crazy inbetween the 2. You haft to reload it, switch to normal shotgun fire, then shoot the SSG and quickly fire off the regular shotgun, allowing you to fire 3 shots almost instantly. There is even a rune that buffs the damage of firing the shotgun like this with quickswitching.Your basic katana serves as a recharging throwing weapon, that you will often be switching to in order to save ammo, instantly killing a demon while instantly switching to another weapon. The quick weapon switching on this game suits this gameplay loop with the katana well. Katana also gets its own rune slot.The super secrets in this game are brilliant. All of them are fun and satisfying to find, and grants you much needed runes and blood gems. Game rewards you for exploring everything, rather than punishing you for "wasting time". The side areas are also fun. Absolutely worth doing. There was even one of them that had the layout of de_dust1 from CS which was great. The game is also filled with references to other games.Sounds in this game are particularily satisfying. Everything from the monsters, weapons and other enviromental sounds are exellent. I think the main reason I like this game so much has to do with the sound design. Level design is great, not that many problems getting lost.I have some very minor complaints, mainly about a specific enemy that sometimes outranges you so much that none of your weapons can even reach it except the bow. This happens very rarely, but it was a minor annoyance. The bosses on this game are... good, but I would not say they are amazing. I think they are better than the boss fights in Dusk tho, as both games kinda lack a good boss fight, but Dread Templar comes out with the better fights here imo.I think this is the best boomer shooter I played so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: While the first stages were not very interesting to me, the game got progressively better and I have really enjoyed episodes 2 and 3. As you advance, you have more options regarding weapons and upgrades, enemies get harder to deal with (though ambushes/hordes can be a bit too much), and in my opinion the setting of the levels gets better (in the sense that the graphic elements follow a theme closer, and scenery is more spectacular and it seems like it has more work behind it). The slowing time mechanic was very nice too. Just don't expect an interesting and deep story, that's not a point of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little boomer shooter. The difficulty spikes pretty hard in the final episode with some of the most annoying enemies I've ever seen. The weapons are all mostly useful due to the "rune" system. Pretty promising early access title.Update: Game just hit 1.0 and the last episodes are alright but nothing too special. The voice-acting is just as retarded as ever. I wouldn't recommend buying this for full price, the combat gets gimmicky later-on with the focus on precise head-shots. I'd probably give this a 6/10 at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: It's too bad this game makes such a "meh" first impression, because it absolutely BANGS. Episode One is mind-numbingly easy, kinda ugly, and weirdly balanced (breaking destructible objects leaves you absolutely SWIMMING in ammo). Also the bare-bones story is presented in the most boring way possible: literally just text on a black screen.That said, once you get to Episode 2 the enemy roster gets MUCH better and the challenge starts to ramp up. The visuals get nicer as you move out of samey crypts and into wide-open outdoor areas. It keeps escalating to a boss battle that legit had me sweating.And then episode 3 hits and GOT DAMN. It's beautiful, it's challenging, the music is better than ever...it's almost like a completely different game! The finished version is going to have 5 episodes and it's already worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and generally great Boomer Shooter, It's upgrade system adds an insane amount of replayability and it's one of the few Retro Shooters where you can make your own full unique builds. I'd give this like a solid 9/10 just some super high quality shooting with no glaring flaws in my eyes, though I feel balance on some upgrades could be changed a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Even at this stage you get a great experience for a fair price. Movement and shooting itself feel great and the upgrade system provides an incentive for further playthroughs. Level design and the themes present really sell the mood well and music fits with everything and cranks up the rush of gameplay. Cannot wait for the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it from that Humble Bundle sale a ways back and finally got to it.Episodes 1 and 2 easily put me in a trance state where my jaw goes slack because the gameplay loop was just that tight. Episode 3 broke me out of it cause they went with much bigger/intricate level design that didn't really work for me. What really really matters for classic shooters is the movement and weapons which were still great even in weaker levels. It was still good but the hooks were slipping out of my brain during EP3. Love the perk system and how hard they go with some of the level 3 ones. As-is DT's pretty great overall and I look forward to the full release.And good aesthetics and music and vibes yadda yadda it's good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Petty cool little boomer shooter, if you skip all the secrets the game is only like 4 hours long but even so its super fun with cool weapons to choose from and a bit of character customisation to do with perks.The game isn't too hard to 100% either so if you're looking for a pretty ez but fun game to 100% this is it.Its def worth the asking price already but if its on sale you shouldn't have a reason not to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! Looking forward to what more is to come. My only real criticism is the score could really use some work. Parts of it are good but I turned it off during the first level and never turned it back on. I really like the genre of music but it just sounds like a couple cords on loop constantly,  it could use some variety, maybe ramping up when you're fighting and when you're exploring maybe have some calmer music. Also is it just me or does the bow, the jump / jump dash and revolver REALLY feel familiar.. that's all I'll say about that.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: So, I originally played this hidden gem of a game after it was brought onto Steam in 2021 for a Beta test. I initially went into the game thinking it would pretty much be a poor knock off of Doom, but it has surprised me.While it definitely takes more than a few of it's inspirations from the early Doom games, it's still really enjoyable. The movement is really simple and easy to get the hang of, the weapons are also relatively easy to use and great fun, and the sword is a great little addition and option for when you absolutely have to YEET something at the one spider that's gunning for you. I mean, you'll be running and gunning. That's all this game in really. Think Devil Daggers with less ominous void.The levels are very well designed with enough hidden or secret areas to keep you guessing and questioning all the walls, doors and buttons you can find, and the enemies are pretty good at keeping you moving and shooting. The music is great, and definitely makes you feel more like a demon slaying monster, although even as a lifelong metalhead I have to admit it can be a little repetitive at times.Regardless of anything else, this is a delightful little game that really makes you feel like a kid again, and I would highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Don't sleep on this title in particular if you like Quake or modern FPS games.There's something about the fine mix of the classic quake FPS experience and style mixed with modern mechanics like upgrades and special weapon abilities like head-shots and reloading that I absolutely adore. I understand that reloading in a boomer shooter isn't the most welcome design decision but I personally don't mind it because reloading seems cool, dunno how to explain it really and plus the reloading isn't necessary for all weapons and even when it is necessary it's not that disturbing. There are 11 weapons and only 4 need reloading by default: Pistols, SMGs, SSG and the revolver.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: First game I consider to be a decent successor to Quake 1. Of course it's still quite different and there a few flaws that need to be ironed out (much smaller team!) but this has soul! Most weapons especially the basic guns, shotgun and bow feel amazing but the rocket launcher lacks oomph. Good enemy variety and great mix of level design with ambushes, secrets and traps though the first episode has a pretty slow start with a lack of surprises and challenges. Bunch of bosses, even hidden optional bosses and lots of abilities to unlock for your weapons. One of my favorite aspect is that there's quite good worldbuilding with several levels having a theme and fun bits of visual storytelling as well as "super secrets" in each level that often take the form of mini side quests with items to use to reveal paths. Lots of love's been put into this.Last but not least: The OST by Primeval absolutely slaps!!! New track every couple level and even several boss themes. It goes all in!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: +great setting+fun powerful punchy weapons+good upgrade system+you can throw your katana. need i say more.+full secret optional areas. not just secrets. basically mini levels hidden inside of the main levels+fun gameplay loop+great level design and sense of direction+awesome ost+varied enemy types+good checkpoint system that doesn't hold your hand but is still somewhat generous. good balance.-upgrade tokens are too infrequent -no ammo pickups on some boss fight arenas-movement options are lacking-no cheats without mods
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addicting. One more level. One more level. The soundtrack is killer; crunchy and motivating. Often found myself just chillin' and listening to the riffs.Love how each chapter has a different theme and different enemies.The guns all serve a purpose, no redundancies. All fun to make a mess out of monsters with.Recommend if you like to feel like a badass.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking for a retro shooter with an amazing metal soundtrack?If your answer is yes, then I can only recommend this game, it isn't your run and gun shooter, some encounters do require a little thought process unless you want to die ofc.Which is one of the things I love about this game, plus it just feels and looks like the good old shooters from an era where shooters, weren't full of regenerating health and what not, and ammo wasn't just thrown at you like money at a stripper who knows what she is doing. So if you are a true retro fan, this is a game you should not miss out on.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: overall the game is fun, graphics are great, the weapons feel good and you can get satisfying gibs. people say its more like doom or quake but i disagree, its way more like serious sam. not much unique movement aside from the one dash and in one of the episodes, you'll find yourself backpedaling and dashing away from enemies who run straight towards you. level design is okay, its really easy to get lost in some parts because you didn't realize you had to press E on something when you weren't told to interact with anything6.5/10 for people who like id games, 7.5 if you like serious samgood buy if its on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty awesome, it takes the starting-to-get-stale boomer shooter formula and takes some risks with it, adding a ton of customization options, snappy and responsive movement, a large arsenal that can be modified to your taste and lots more. It has a ton of content already and I'm excited to see where it goes during early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I can play this game for about 15 minutes at a time. It's just boring. The gunplay is fine, but it's a snooze of a game. The level design is bland, the enemies are repetitive, and the guns are mostly uninspired. The music is great, but the soundscape feels so lifeless. I really wish there was voice acting or something to make the game feel more alive. I also am tired of boomer shooters having no story at all. That's not fun or interesting. At least something to breaking up the monotony of shooting the same 8 enemies for hours on end. Something other than puzzles so easy a cat could do them and slow ass moving platforms.It's not a bad game, it's gunplay and music really do carry a lot of the game. There's a lot of room for improvement. I really think the soundscape needs to be one of the top priorities.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: If you like "old school" fast FPS like Quake, Doom, Dusk, Blood, Shadow Warrior, etc. you should enjoy this one.The feeling of the weapons and movement is really good.Levels are really well designed, especially the 1st two episodes.Music really goes well with the action.Secrets everywhere & even puzzles!What do we ask for? More!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic retro-FPS.The level design is spectacular (and there's no backtracking which can get annoying in these games).The music is phenomenal.Pacing is just right.The mechanics are great - very similar to the widely celebrated Dusk.The only downside is that it's still in Early Access so it ends too soon, about 4-5 hours, but hopefully more content will be added.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I get that this is an Early Access game and unfinished as of EA release.  I get the "artistic style" that is being presented.  But comon', it's not the 1990's or early 2000's... the game-play could be a bit better with modern elements (just a few more).  The animations need work.  Especially the "lever" animations or rather lack there of.Titles like DOOM and Quake can be modded up to exhibit better game-play features and those games [modded up] are at least a decade old.  So why can't developers duplicate all the game-play features and advancements of the game(s) that the are emulating BEFORE (not after or during) releasing to Early Access?  So, yeah, another EPA (early access potential) that I'll play some other day.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Fun combat. I regret not purchasing earlier and did so on latest update 6. With fairly big open maps it doesn’t have a claustrophobic feeling. It is dark but not in a way you can’t see. Shadow warrior gameplay feel with the katanas and dashing and demon monster mobs. Enemies get taken down pretty easily which doesn’t make them bullet sponges and has the old school vibe of blasting through! But with head shots included also it makes it somewhat skilful and more satisfying *thumbs up*
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: As part of the Humble Boomer Shooter Bundle, Dread Templar promised loads of old-school FPS gameplay and it did not disappoint.Dread Templar is a lovingly crafted homage to Quake, borrowing a lot of its design to the point where it plays like a Quake expansion. That is never a bad thing as I loved Quake and its remaster.The gameplay is fast and fluid, the maps are expansive and packed with secrets, the art style is gorgeous and draws a lot of inspiration from Quake's expansions, the guns are fun to play with and have a lot of variety, the enemies also have a lot of variety and are fun to fight and the soundtrack is killer.My only real flaws are the overabundance of ammo right before a boss fight, the ineffective Black Bow, the repetitive soundtrack in Episode 1 and the easy final boss for Episode 3. Aside from that the game is a pitch-perfect boomer shooter.The developer is still working on the game, and we currently have 3 out of the 4 planned episodes. I had a blast with the first 3 and I eagerly await the 4th. I'll update this review once I've played the 4th episode.I give Dread Templar a 4/5. It promised fast-paced, run n' gun gameplay that evokes 90's FPS games and it absolutely delivered.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game feel and combat. Love the references to Blood and seemingly Dark Souls 2? I think that it front loads the levels with generic elements and the really good stuff is saved until later. I will say as well, I hated the soundtrack. So if you can turn off the music and boot up your own playlist, you'll have a good time shooting and slicing your way through enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, quick boomer shooter. I don't know how they pulled it off, but every gun is meaty and satisfying.I really like the bullet time, bow and spear abilities. They make this particular boomer shooter stand out in a sea of very similar doom clones. The levels could be better, they don't seem to have any structure, just a level after level. Gunplay is amazingly fun, if you're good at these games. The soundtrack is alright, nothing memorable but it gets the job done. I'd like to praise the upgrade system in the game. You can choose which weapons you want to be better, and there are upgrades that can alter them completely a la doom eternal. It allows you to make specific builds and definitely adds replayability. This game has the best bow i've seen in any game ever, so there's that. Perfectly timed, high damage, super satisfying. Oh, and the infernal revolver is a weapon that could kill god and it's the best revolver i've seen in a game. Also, the devs made a pretty good save system which avoids save scumming, and that's usually a huge issue in boomer shooters. In terms of bigger cons, the game very much needs polish, but it's expected in an early access game. PLEASE LET US DISABLE CUTSCENES. They play every time you open a gate, it's infuriating. Any sense of flow you had, it just dies. I can understand it being there for new players, but for real boomers, just say "a gate has opened somewhere" and let us go on. Oh, and chapter 3 kinda sucks D for now, hopefully it gets better in the next updates.In conclusion, it's a very fun boomer shooter, which innovates the otherwise stale formula for these games with cool abilities and upgrades. It has potential, and I think it's worth the price even now. Def play if you're into these sort of games
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: G L O R I O U SI really love level design, challenge scaling, secrets and progression system. Every weapon feels powerful, you'll even use your melee weapon on higher diffculties as it deals insane damage if used properly. Movement is responsive. When you'll die (and for sure you will die a lot on hell/nightmare) you'll be put right back into the action in moment's notice. This game makes me want to look carefully for secrets because it really is rewarding giving you useful upgrades for your weapons and character. For sure i'll complete it few times before full release. Could use multiplayer, but hell, this game dont needs one. I can't really point out any cons during my 5 hours with this game. Levels are kinda short, but I play on nightmare diffculty, so I get punished a lot. TL;DR Shotgun got it's punch, get this game
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fantastic. Worst thing about it is the music, which is kinda grim repetitive metal. Gameplay is fast and solid... flows like Quake, feels like similar physics. Cool modern ideas like skill cooldowns for a couple weapons and a dash instead of run (and air dash, at that). Decent level design that isn't entirely to my liking. Figuring out some of the weapons, like the LMB RMB LMB for a quick triple shotgun barrage, is fun to do. Ammo goes fast for your pistol slot weapons and you'll usually fight bosses that eat up most ammo, so there's a LITTLE bit of the frantic weapon hopping of Doom Eternal without being quite so extreme. You can clear an encounter with shotguns exclusively without much problem, so it's more if you try to be a pistol main. Most other weapons besides pistol and shotgun feel kinda situational, which is good I think... I rarely felt the need to use the inferno rocket, and the inferno revolver was incredible but had pretty limited ammo. Black Bow was a great sniper weapon I used to pick off distance enemies regularly, but the AI is aggressive so only a couple enemies will actually stick around while you poke em. Inferno fist was a fun BFG style weapon but only found a couple uses for it. Bottom line, if you've already beaten Dusk and Amid Evil, this is probably the next of the boomer shooters I would give a shot. Episode 1 and 2 are pretty tame, and 3 only has two missions currently, but it's a good experience. Well worth supporting for 15 bucks... much better than Prodeus.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: There are loads of these "90s style" shooters around now, gods be praised, and this is one of the best ones I've played recently. What makes it stand out is the shameless splattery and bloodiness, the interesting selection of weapons and a nice feature where levels have an alternative, more difficult, route through parts of them with extra rewards for those who fancy the challenge. The chuck-able katana is also cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this game convinced me. It's pretty damned good. this was always the one of the new boomer shooters that I never really cared about buying. It came in a bundle, so I thought I'd try it out. The first half of the first chapter was so boring to me  because I was still going into this game thinking it was gonna play just like the classics. The first few levels really aren't the greatest, but it definitely picks up! The weapon and character perk system is so nice. It reminds me of DOOM 2016, but without having to do those challenges for the final upgrade. I don't like all of the music for this game, but the songs that hit, hit HARD. There are a lot of bangers in this OST! The overall feel of the movement is decent. You have your dash (which is on a cooldown timer), and your jump. The cooldown for the dash feels just a tad too long by default. There's a perk to reduce the cooldown though so it's whatever I guess. I wish there was a little bit of momentum based movement though. The graphics are really clean, but I feel that the basic shotgun enemies, and runners lack inspiration in design. They just look basic. Not a big deal though. The game definitely makes up for that early design later on with a lot of awesome enemies! Overall this game is in a really good place right now, with a dev who is seems to be really honing in on their craft throughout the project, and it shows!  To think that only 2 chapters have been finished...insane!So far: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Short (cause it's still in development) and fun. I love the shotgun, the revolver and the gaunlet. Feels GREAT to use them. The movement is also top tier and the bullet time is so fun and makes you feel powerful.But all the other guns are kinda hit or miss (at least for me). I still recommend it and I will be waiting for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty standard, yet fun retro-styled FPS. You've got your enemies and weapons you would usually find in these kinds of games. However, the biggest system that this game has is the upgrading system.As of now, upgrades are collectibles found within levels with which you can spend a currency to open up slots for your character or specific weapons. These upgrades include your typical increased damage, ammo, speed, cooldown reduction on certain abilities, etc. Furthermore, the last slot of an upgrade tree is pretty much where the unique abilities are. For example, I found an upgrade that changes the look of my dual pistols to demonic "Hellscream" pistols that adds punch through to projectiles. The system is pretty bare bones as of now. Simple numerical buffs to your arsenal just isn't that interesting, but since the game is in Early Access the developers can work more on it to provide unique abilities for fun builds, allowing more diversity in play style.Overall, I had a really awesome time with the game. Can't wait for the full release!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun.  Really liked the weapon upgrade system and I really hope there's an upgrade for the fist that lets you dash forward with it.  I was kinda disappointed that there seems to be no way to maintain the momentum you get from dashing but dashing around the levels and using it to solve environmental puzzles was a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I didn't know much about this game. Took a chance with it and I absolutely love it! The guns are fantastic, top to bottom. The pump shotgun is punchy and powerful, same with the double barrel counterpart. The pistols manages to break the curse of a last desperation weapon; even after you get the SMGs (which are very satisfying). The bow is tight and does a great job of not being pushed aside by the other high-accuracy weapons. The infernal weapon set is amazing. I won't go too much into them because they are really the showcase and includes the BFG of the game which is introduced perfectly. The featured Katana is balanced amazingly. Though I mostly used it as a javelin and reserved melee for crates and vases.There is only one critique I have about the weapons. But this does come with a caveat: I have not upgraded this particular weapon, so it definitely could just be on my end of things. Will edit if I find my experience changes: But, I hardly used the trap gun. I think it is a good weapon for the game but there's something missing that is hard to describe. It is not very interesting as far as the feel for it goes. The other aspect of it is that the game doesn't have situations that encourage it above anything else. Like, there are a few instances I know it would have made life easier, but it never stood out as the solution above strafing and gunning.Not a huge issue, but worth mentioning. Beyond that, I love everything about the weapons. I love that if it shares the same ammo type, you can right click to change between them. This is fast and responsive. Won't leave you in a panic of a pinch. Ease of use that I love.Upgrades are interesting, though it isn't anything that will massively change the game play. Mostly typical more ammo, more damage, faster fire-rate, etc. With exception of gold emblems which do give you a more interesting perk for each weapon. It is apparent how useful these upgrades (silver or gold emblems) can be, regardless. An interesting addition to this retro-shooter. Though it does take a little foresight how you choose to distribute them. Because you have to open slots. This costs crystals you find through out the levels. Mostly in side areas (but I will talk about this more when I talk about level design). Even then they are not abundant. And with how it increases cost per slot in each weapon, you will want to save them up. With that said, I think the spread is fairly balanced, all things considered.As for level design, I think this game is as solid as a rock! They're memorable and I never got lost once while playing. I love how levels tend to wrap around or at least give you an easy way out if you don't want to do tedious back tracking. No level feels samey or repetitive. Each one has a very distinct feel or philosophy put into it. And if you find yourself pulling a lever that activates something not in the immediate area, the game will give you a very short clip showing what you just opened and doesn't kill the flow at all.There are your typical switches and keys but it isn't disruptive. You aren't bombarded with a level full of switches or a key to open a door so you can get a key to open a door, etc. It uses it sparingly and effectively. To the point where it is actually kind of exciting to find one of the keys.Like most games of its ilk, it has secrets. And like most retro-shooters, some secrets are satisfying, some are questionably secrets, while some I am sure I will never ever find on my own. But, along with those, there is the addition of side areas and I absolutely LOVE this idea. It is a whole other section of the level that tends to be focused on a unique sense of difficulty. Whether it ramps up the enemies, gives you a tight lay out to move around or just a trap-ladden hell hole, these areas bring a supremely unique aspect to not only each individual level but to the game as a whole. Find a glowing red crack in the wall and blow it open for a whole other area. Not only do these areas give a satisfying reward of -red crystals and upgrade emblems, but they are very interesting and fun to play. If I have gotten through the level and have found I haven't gone through the side area, I have to go back. Such a brilliant concept of optional difficulty which I hope gets adopted into more games that wish to find a way to challenge their players without getting more novice players trapped into the cruelty.Enemy placement is pretty good and exciting. At least on the normal difficulty which is pretty fairly balanced. It feels really solid and not dickish. The pacing of new enemies is solid and they tend to be introduced fairly well. The enemies themselves are great and have very distinct styles and attacks which do a great job of forcing you to think about your movement. Though, most of the time if you run back and shoot, you will be fine. Which isn't terrible.The bosses themselves can be hit or miss so far. It is a simple set up. An arena with not much in terms of surroundings. Mostly just you and the boss...Which is where the first problem comes in. Both the spider and the heart, I beat on the first try by circle strafing and emptying my ammo into them. The heart is cool in design and so I won't complain too much about it, but I'll be honest, the spider boss is not very good. It is half of the arena, not an interesting pattern of attack, and the hardest thing about it is the spawn it brings into to fight you as well. Overall it is a very boring boss fight. The Heart is more interesting. It takes up less room, it looks cooler and the attacks are a little bit more interesting, but still not too engaging as long as you circle strafe and don't let its minions build up too much.The third boss, the knight. THAT was a great and challenging boss! Still a bit of circle strafe and shoot but it has attacks that creates a lot more interesting movement. The attacks are awesome, the design is cool and the level leading up to it was a tour-de-force that was so satisfying to beat. It matches the tone and excitement of the rest of the game so well and it was a lot of fun to beat. The aesthetic of the game is very solid as well. It is kind of like Quake meets Hellraiser, with a little bit of Pain Killer as well. The monsters are revolting and interesting to look at. They have a unique style while not being entirely alien. You worry sometimes with a lot of these grim-dark shooters that take such huge inspiration from Quake, that the oppressive and dark mentality of it will be samey. And for a lot of games, it is. I won't say Dread Templar re-invited the wheel of art direction but it definitely keeps things unique and varied. Though there is definitely an Ogre variant in here. The levels aesthetic themselves might not feel the most unique but it uses it very well where it doesn't feel bland at all. It embodies its tone amazingly.Overall this is a great solid game. It might not break the glass ceiling past New Blood but I have a hard time thinking you'll be disappointed if you are looking for another great 'boomer-shooter'. It is a blast to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't like it. Levels felt sparse due to being really spacey, and the enemies were damage-sponges. Overall it just lacked speed and intensity and did not encourage playing with tactics in its moment-to-moment gameplay.On the plus side, I liked the weapons and the level design was pretty true to oldschool design.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Great sign when I don't realize the game is still in Early Access and get majorly disappointed when it ends early. Soundtrack kicks ass and the environments for all their low poly pixelation are impressive and atmospheric. The enemies could use a bit of tuning in my opinion. I played on Hard and if I wasn't constantly alert I'd be turned into mist. _childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on the boomer shooter bundle over at Humblebundle.  I already had several of the games, but of the ones i didn't already have this is my favorite so far. I'm a couple levels into episode 2 at the moment. Similar art style or "visual feel" to Wrath: Aeon of ruin, both of which have a gritty Quake 1-ish vibe. With the weapon upgrade system and dashing you could draw comparisons to doom eternal or doom 2016.  The pistol  even upgraded gets overlooked once I have the SMG.  Super shotgun vs pump still has the same mechanic as the classic doom - pump for saving ammo and quicker refire for sweeping a room full of weaker enemies, SSG for blasting somethings face off in one or two shots.    The sword felt kinda weird at first, but its good for smashing boxes and the jars/breakables for items/ammo  and at least for the first  episode a slower-but effective means of killing stuff and saving ammo.  The sparta throw is great for  early "sniping" of enemies far off. I kind of feel like darkness in the maps was abused a bit to hide some secrets or to maybe waste your time a bit when secret hunting. Secrets are plentiful, some are pretty easy to find if you see or notice something that seems empty or a room that doesn't really seem to have a purpose other than killing a couple enemies and some ammo that is all to itself. I haven't found them all as far as i know yet - so some are hid pretty well.    I'm dealing with an inner ear infection so i can't really comment on sound/music  as i'm nearly deaf at the moment.   Whatever little bit i could hear in the first episode seemed to have a pretty good rhythm that was suited well for run&gun. Easter eggs-  i found calebs grave and two "missing" secrets, and the dusk dudes sickles just kinda chilling on a ledge. Texture work could be better in a few areas, some of the cave/dungeon sort of areas look kinda "samey" due to the same texture being used a lot in certain areas.  Aside from that,  level layout/design is pretty great, even the puzzley/backtracking sections don't drag on too long that its annoying.    Some of the level design reminds me of the quake mod arcane dimensions. Performance - Game runs well on my laptop with intel graphics,  so I would suspect this would run like greased lightning on about any dedicated gpu made in the past 5 years.   even though its still in development  the  feel of the gameplay is good, in fact quite a bit better than some "finished" games. if you like boomer shooters, or a moderately challenging fast paced shooter - this is definitely worth grabbing.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with it.Starts out rough, exemplified by the first real boss, the spider. The main reason the first few levels and the boss are a pain is because you don't have most of your tools yet, meaning you're operating on a limited set of ammo pools and lots of enemies. The boss in particular likes to spawn ads at several points, so you're usually better off ignoring/dodging them and emptying everything into the boss as fast as possible.As said, it's rough, but once you get more weapons and runes to empower them with, the kit really starts to feel like your own and you seem more in control of the situation. Near the end of the EA my death count reduced drastically and I was doing more of that typical boomer-shooter resource management where I remember where some large ammo pickups are for later because I'm 98% full on it at the moment. That kinda stuff.Much like it how it looks on the tin, the weaponry and atmosphere is very edgy. However, I found that a lot of that edge had actual function. Yeah, it's cool you can attach your katana's together and chuck them, but there's actual purpose to it. The katana's pierce in flight, and there's a cooldown before it comes back, meaning it can be part of a routine as you switch between weapons to rain hellfire with. In fact, anything with a cooldown has a devoted icon for it. The impression really is that these cooldown-based weapons are meant to part of your combat routine.Tidbits like that stand in contrast with the initial impression that this is just another boomer shooter with an edgy coat of paint. Having gotten through the EA, it stopped feeling like that.There are shooters of the genre that are in EA/releasing at around the same time period that do Dread Templar's combat better, but it's not a slouch. Worth paying attention to if boomer shooters are your thing.

_childDocuments_.review: (Video review at the bottom)Dread Templar, developed by T19 and published by 1C Entertainment, who haven’t been involved in anything that I’ve heard off, Oh hey, Alekhine’s gun! The first thing you hear when you boot up is this *music* oh yeah, it’s one of those games.This game sees you step into the shoes of a Dread Templar who enters hell in order to find revenge on whoever, the plot is paper-thin but it honestly doesn’t matter as this is just early access, focused purely on the gameplay. We go through a tutorial and learn how to jump, dash and swim. We also learn how to use bullet time, a classic mechanic from several titles, ranging from John Woo’s Stranglehold and the Max Payne trilogy, it runs out pretty fast but recharges as you kill things. Throughout the game you come across a whole cast of demons, such as ghouls, ghouls with shotguns, bomb boys and these… things. You are given a whole arsenal of demon killing tools, ranging from dual pistols, dual Uzi’s which are insanely satisfying to use, a shotgun, a bow and arrow? what? there’s also these infernal weapons, which are extremely powerful and saved my skin more than once. There’s red barrels that naturally, blow up. You can have a pair of katanas which you can attach to one another in order to throw it at some unsuspecting demon. You’re able to find Templar Emblems and Blood Gems which you can use to power up weapons at Upgrade Altars, each weapon allowing up to three Emblems, some of these come with a stronger variant later in the game. Emblems can do things like give you higher damage, increase your ammo capacity and give you a faster firing rate. Each weapon has up to 3 upgrade slots which need to be unlocked by using these Blood Gems with each additional slot requiring an additional Gem.The level design harkens back to the old Doom games, mazelike dungeons with several paths to take, no map either because this is a real man’s game. There’s a bunch of secret areas in every level so if you see some weird looking textures, just hit E on it and you’ll probably be rewarded. There’s also Side Areas which are harder than the base difficulty but they do come with extra rewards such as strong health pickups, better Templar Emblems and additional Blood Gems. The current early access version includes 2 entire chapters with 5 levels and a boss each with the final release having 5 chapters and 25 levels in total.The game plays very well, the movement is fluid and smooth as the rapid weapon switching, reload times and heaps of enemies being thrown at you make for a very chaotic experience. Graphics are overall good and enjoyable to look at, very familiar to anyone who’s played anything from the 90’s, which is where this game draws most of its inspiration from. The sound design is good enough to make every gun feel weighty, making it pack quite the punch in combat. The old school graphics style makes it so that basically anyone with a computer can play this game and still run it at a solid fps count. Yeah, this early access game didn’t crash once, nor did it ever drop any frames, so that’s a giant plus if you see the state that some triple A games come out in.The two already released chapters took me just over 3 hours to complete, that being said I missed out on a whole bunch of the secret areas mostly because I’m an impatient ♥♥♥♥ so if you’re down to 100% it could probably take over 5 hours. I assume that the entire release, currently scheduled for Fall of 2022 should run anywhere between 8 to 10 hours in total. The game currently costs 15 dollars but the devs have stated that it will go up when they fully release the game. So, if you think that everything I’ve said sounds like your cup of tea, or if you liked Quake or DOOM: Eternal I’d recommend picking it up and hopping in now to save yourself some money, you’d also be helping the development of an insanely fun indie title that definitely delivers in the genre that its set itself in. I was pretty surprised to not have seen Dave Oshry, king of Boomer Shooters tweet about it atleast 23 times in the week of its release. So yeah, that’s all I’ve got to say about Dread Templar, it’s fun, it’s fast, and its excellent.Video Review -

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access Review:Dread Templar is a good game, in fact it is really good. Is it great? Well not yet but it certainly seems to be heading in the right direction. The game blends the visuals of a quake era type game with action more akin to the recent Doom Eternal. In a way you can think of it was a retro styled Doom Eternal Lite. The gun play is fast and slick and the upgrade system is interesting in giving you some variety. The levels overall are well designed and complex enough to keep you busy but not so complicated you get lost easily. The enemy roster is also nicely varied while providing a fun challenge. You will find yourself switching weapons and combat styles to prioritize and take our different foes at different times.Right now what is keeping the game from greatness is that both the skill tree and the weapons are lacking a certain something for me. While the weapons have some unique stand outs there is nothing that really wowed me. Likewise the skill tree is good and the higher tier stuff has some interesting effects but I would like to see some wilder options in the full release (maybe even a health decrease for a massive damage buff, or something equally stupid).My only other minor grip is that the levels, while good looking and fun can start to feel a little samey by the end of the currently included content. I am hoping further episodes will change up the aesthetic a little so this can probably be discount.Overall i am looking forward to seeing this develop further. It's really is a very good game and the devs seem dedicated to making it even better. If you like fast paced, skill based retro shooters this is one to buy/watch.

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar asks "What if we made a pure old school shooter but layered a bullet time mechanic and every lesson Doom Eternal taught on top of it?"  And the answer is "that would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great."Odd that this game doesn't have "Overwhelmingly Positive".  Over the last 5 or 6 years FPS fans have been treated to a resurgence of the genre.  The stagnation of the  CoD clone era died and developers started finally looking back to what made FPS games so engaging in the first place.  Movement, pacing, level design, enemy design.  At every budget we've gotten great FPS games.  From the Metro series to the incomparable Doom reboots all the way down to the indie gems Amid Evil, Dusk, Ultrakill, Project Warlock and others.If there is one legitimate complaint to level against the brilliance of games like Ion, Dusk and Amid Evil it's that they might stick a bit too closely to the classic  formula.  This year we got Ultrakill which is one of the very best shooters ever made and a legitimately innovative game unlike any other shooter out there and here we have a game that sticks very closely to the formula but has one crucial element that elevates it to excellence.  For the most part this is an EXCELLENT retro shooter.  Fast paced, smartly designed, tight and polished, it has perfectly balanced enemies, sprawling levels that are big enough to act as places to explore but never so big it gets frustrating, and a great arsenal of guns.  This is the foundation of every great shooter from Half LIfe to Doom Eternal.  Dread Templar brings this perfect core design together by adding a light progression system into the mix. Even on hard it doesn't feel like this is crucial to beat the game but it IS an fantastic incentive for fully exploring levels.Dread Templar is basically Dusk with a dash dodge, a progression system, and a kind of "slayer gate" system where you can find "side areas" that are difficult arenas or platforming challenges that award extra progression items, runes and ammo.  If you're the kind of person who likes exploration but thinks just finding "secrets" ultimately feels hollow, this game is for you.  If you love old school shooters AND Doom Eternal, you are 100 percent going to love Dread.  It's one of the best FPS games of the current era.  An absolute steal.  I haven't encounterd one thing that made me think, "Why game?  You were doing so well."  And I'm one of the most nit picking, snobbish, critical jerks around.This is a great shooter.  The only real issue is some bad boss design, with final boss being particularly poor.  Developers, please understand boss immunity phases are garbage and movement slowing mechanics in games that are all about movement feel terrible.  I hope the final boss is looked at again.  Aside from that, i's near perfect and accomplishes everything it sets out to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Typical boomer shooter fps. Has very smooth movement control and a great range of weapon. The game also has a upgrade system with perks which give incentive to revisit old level, find secret to get those perks. Best part of the game. The music is lit, the gun sfx is powerful and satisfying. Crispy Quake-style graphic, with good color choices.Improvement: - I suggest that we have a way to double-bind weapon to same button. Like we have dual-uzi and dual piston bind to the same key 2, super shotgun and pump shotgun bind to same key 3. This way my left hand don't have to stretch all the way to the right to get the infernal revolver or the gauntlet.- In addition, I think the game should add an option where press the right mouse button will attach the dual katana and throw them immediately, instead of right click and left click to throw them.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Super sleek and fun boomer shooter. The melee combat actually feels pretty intuitive, the katanas are a fun weapon. The weapon combination feels balanced and the enemies are varied and challenging. Movement feels fluid, although strafe jumping feels a little more sluggish than in a game like Quake or Dusk. Totally worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed what is currently available in the Early Access.I purchased this game during Realms Deep 2021 and what caught my attention was how "Quake-like" it looked. The game surprised me by also adding modern FPS mechanics into the mix, making it feel a lot more like the fabled "Quake 2016". The game is fast and very action packed. The gun selection is varied and no weapon feels out of place or useless. The gameplay feels GREAT AND SMOOTH with how the Quick-Switching, Slowed Time and Dash mechanic are implemented. The downtime between combat, puzzles and upgrade zones are fairly paced and you never feel like you are spending TOO much time in just one zone. I did get lost from time to time on some of the early levels but, that's probably just me.The only thing that I didn't like and that almost led to my death, was that in the first level, as you emerge from the catacombs, the trees' hitboxes felt too big the first time I played through it. Granted, in subsequent playthroughs I never encountered that same problem so this is just a small nitpick which I bet could trouble a new player coming in to the game only to get stuck and suffer a slow and painful death.Overall, the game feels fantastic and frankly, I can't wait to see what next content will this game push forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: this game takes me back to the old classic shoot em all style games with secret areas and lots of enemies.if you are familiar with "Serious Sam" and "Doom" this is a mix of both with a touch of unique weapon and character upgrade mechanism.I highly recommend this game to those 90's kids that want a taste from the past :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Really love the game and the vibes it gives! Super satisfying to 1shot stuff with the Bow. My favorite weapon so far. But the weapons in general and the diversity in gameplay they bring is really really fun and that's something that makes it more enjoyable longterm than Dusk for example (for me at least). Also love the weapon enhancement system. Music is decent aswell, although it isn't nearly as good as with Doom Eternal (but I doub't thats possible anyway). Only thing I really don't like about it is the fact that it doesn't end. I'd like to have a break from the music from time to time and rather have it only during combat go wild. Having it play nonstop is making it less special and less enjoyable for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is a solid retro shooter. It's very much a mashup of all the best game play features from Hexen and Quake. The movement is extremely smooth and fast paced. Weapons are hard hitting. Level design is unique and secrets can be difficult to find which is a nice touch. The atmosphere and lighting choices are very cool. Generally I'm not a background music fan I prefer the ambient noises minus music but I have to say the metal hesher soundtrack on this is pretty rad. Parts of it reminded me of the BGM from the zombie level on Metal Slug 3 which is kinda hip. My only gripe with this so far is the lack of levels. Yes, I get it this is an early release and it's off to a very promising start. But this truly requires ~50 levels not 25 as a finished game when that release is completed. I'd like the devs to consider extending the game's episodes and creating a longer arc of maps to explore and brawl through. Dread Templar is worthy of this extra effort. Or open it up for community created maps which will inevitably add a lot of replay value. If you are a fan of early FPS games because you remember when these were new or if you have not played the genre before consider giving Dread Templar a try. It's damn good.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Just realized that the full release happened, and I am happy to say that I am thoroughly enjoying this game. I enjoyed it in early access as well, but now it feels much more polished and I'm stoked that I can play from start to finish. Good music, tight controls, and who doesn't love the aesthetic? Come on.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: 1C Entertainment is killing it again.  They partnered with 3D Realms to make Wrath: Aeon of Ruin and Graven.  Both great games (Graven still has a way to go whereas Wrath is almost at the finish line.)Im quite surprised this isnt also a 3D Realms game.  The movement and combat is extremely satisfying and compelling.  (There is one issue I hope the dev fixes and that is, no enemies seem to have collision at the moment.)  This game plays like Duke Nukem 3D when it comes to handling and smoothness overall.  The story has not been revealed, but it follows your basic 90s FPS tropes (as far as Ive seen, mind you the games is still in pretty early access.  You will get to complete 2 episodes as of now, each with 5 levels each.)I really just cant get over how satisfying everything about this game is.  The developer seems to be fresh, but its 1C publishing and they dont usually release garbage.  In this game, expect fast paced first person shooting in the classic 90s style of skill based. You wont find any hit scanners here.  You can dodge and move and staying still is a death sentence. There are many games like this but this one definitely stands apart with its unique upgrade system.  You can tailor your character to your playstyle and this also leads to good replayability, Ive completed the entire game as of now and I find its artstyle and tight controls so gripping.  You can also unleash "bullet time".  yeah.All in all, this is definitely one to wishlist or go ahead and buy it.  I find it worth the price because I know theyll finish it and right now, the replayability for me is great.  I keep replaying it on harder difficulties to unlock the level to be played as a one off.TLDR;  its good, get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a lot of the new boomer shooters that have come out in the wake of Dusk/Amid Evil, and this one really stands out to me.I played the original demo when it was still called Hell Hunt and knew it had a lot of potential and it has vastly improved since then.The gameplay is fast, frantic and extremely fun. The weapons all feel great to use, and the upgrade system really allows you some options in how you use them. (Shout out to the inferno pistol and sniper shotgun upgrade)The music is fantastic and sets the tone for the demon slaying perfectly. The level design is great with a lot of rewarding secrets and references to classic shooters both old and new to find, as is typical in these kinds of games you have to hunt hard to find them all.The only gripes i have are certain quality of life things such as a secret/enemy counter but these could easily be added in future. Overall Dread Templar is a fantastic boomer shooter and shouldn't be overlooked with the current influx of games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Needs some oil on the ol' cogs but overall a very enjoyable experience for anyone that fancies Quake or Doom Eternal. While at first the weapon choice and enemy variety in the early game can be a bit of a slow drag, towards the latter half off this Early Access build, I found myself enjoying the combat and management of its mechanics thoroughly!
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Even in early access this game feels very solid. The level design, movement, and guns all feel polished and well made. I've yet to fully explore the content available but if it's anything like what I've played so far I wont have any complaints. If you want a game that already has the movement and guns ironed out then I would pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: HelloI can recomend this game so far, especially to fans of Quake (especially the first one) and Killing Floor.I am saying "so far" because this game is still in Early Acces. Hopefully the development of the gamewill go on smoothly and without any lapses in quality.But the game is still not flawless (not only because of the Early Acces tag)- the video options are quite bare, allowing only to change resolution, turn off/on bloom, turn on/off Vsync (dreaded me that name), change FOV,adjust brightness and adjust the size of the reticle. Unfortunately the video options don't allow deeper graphical customization- like lowering quality of graphic effect or quality of the graphics themselves. I would perosnally really like those deeper graphic customization to be added, mainly to boost performance and to turn off the graphic effects of the slow motion power. The warping blur of this effect is quite neat stylisticly, but it is a distraction and tends to cause some performance hickups (talking from a rather low end laptop)I also hope bugs will be fixed- I encountered 2 major ones. On 2 occasions loading back from the checkpoint killed me for no reason and I had fallen under the map a couple of times, not only after loading in from the checkpoints.But, asside from Early Acces, lacking graphics options and the 2 notible bugs, the game is really playable and with the mechanics being quite polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Have now finished the game after 2.0 release, and it was very good. Not perfect, but very good. For essentially a lone developer, pretty amazing. I feel like the game suffers in its general reception because the start looks quite generic. The middle episode especially the nautical themed levels are by far the best, the last couple of episodes released at 1.0 are good but a but drawn out. Definitely worth buying for fans of this genre.------------Orig reviewThis is an amazing retro FPS, maybe destined to become the best. When I saw the first trailer it looked like an average doom/quake ripoff but while certainly inspired by those games it is so much more than that. Great modern mechanics like dash along with the fast paced combat you'd expect of old school, interesting weapons, good un-intrusive upgrade system, killer soundtrack and really memorable enemies especially the bosses. Can't wait for more content to be released through early access. At the moment I'd put it ahead of prodeus, amid evil, wrath and ion Fury in terms of the first few levels and only dusk ahead of it in the retro FPS hierachy mostly for its greater personality and more interesting premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Story:What's happening?Just like prodeous, I don't really know what's happening, and while it's not a huge problem, it still bothers me somewhat. Hopefully we'll get more story in the future.Graphics:Feeling like a mix of Dusk and Wraith: Aeon Of Ruin, it's great to look at, but it's undoubtly retro. Reminds me of Quake a lot. The Gore reminds me of Blood.Gameplay:Oh boy this is beautiful. Each gun feels great, and the game just reminds me of Doom Eternal, with the weapon switching and the combos you can do. Just like Amid Evil, every weapon has it's use, and they all feel great. Only complaint is that when you switch immediatly after shooting the Double Barrel, it doesn't automatically reload like Doom Eternal.Music:Whoever made this should be proud. It feels like something Mick Gordon would make, and that is the highest praise I can give this soundtrack. Hope it makes a release on steam or spotify!Enemies:They all have cool designs, and they all challenge you in different ways. They're cool.10/10Thanks Jarek

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar is a very welcome birth into the family of modern boomer shooters.The game as a whole feels polished despite being in early access. The guns feel and sound neat. The movement is simple but precise, with the humble dash being a good friend in combat.The level design is also on point. You'd be hard-pressed to get lost, the atmosphere is well done, and the secrets, although well-hidden, are still findable if you search with effort.The combat does not feel cheesy. Many enemies fling projectiles with travel times or use melee attacks, so you can avoid the bulk of incoming bitchslaps with good movement and by keeping your distance.The Early Access version of the game contains 10 levels. They're all good, but now I am eager for more demon-punishing adventures.Solid game, hats off to the dev(s).Oh, and the music slaps like a dungeon mistress. I'd gladly buy the composer a beer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic addition to the new wave of retro FPS games that have been coming out lately.Gameplay is very fast paced with a great selection of weapons and fun enemies to fight. Level design is solid, with some of the more enjoyable secret hunting I've experienced.Being early access there's plenty of content missing (mostly the remaining 15 levels) and some things that are a little rough around the edges, but overall it's easy to recommend. At the very least it's one to keep an eye on until the full release.

I also hope the open area before the final boss in the EA is just a place holder because that area is unimaginative and unbalanced. These can all be ironed out as the game gets updated. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice blend of new and old shooters. I enjoyed the game so far, it took me about 2 hours to finish the content so far. My only complaint is every time you pull a lever it never opens a door nearby. For some reason they decided to make a door open across the map each time. _childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Its probably the weakest of the boomer shooters Ive played during the past few years. The maps are way too big and the weapons feel under powered, even with upgrades. You can at least shotgun swap for big damage but most of the time your just juggling your weapons. Also there are save spots you have to manually save in and you have to do it often which takes away the flow of the game. Why not make those save points into checkpoints that auto save. That would have a been a way better idea. Its just there to prevent you from restarting the entire map but really unnecessary and interrupts the game a lot.The game at its core is great, but with all these annoyances just takes the fun away.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes what's good from the likes of Doom and Killing floor, merges them in to one and then adds it's own spin on things for good measure.Seems to be really well put together, great visuals, fun gameplay and the soundtrack is really quite something.Jarek4's review on Youtube sparked my interest and made me aware of this game. Thought i'd take the plunge and try the game for myself. No regrets
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar has come a long way since it first released as an Early Access title. While Episode 1 is a pretty standard "quake-inspired FPS", good but nothing that really stands out, EP2 starts showing a bit more color and more creative choices, ends on a high note and then throws you off when EP3 starts.This is probably my favorite part of the game, not only the enemy & level design/variety improves a ton, but the music becomes way better as well. Changing tempo and not being non-stop metal all the time (while still being that at its core). The last 3 levels are amazing.E4 starts in the desert, my least favorite setting in any kind of media. I don't like the aesthetic and music in most games that use it, but BY FAR this game knocks it out of the park. Seriously, just go listen to E4M1's song and tell me it's not a perfect blend of metal & egypt.I'm not gonna talk about E5 because of spoilers, but it fits nicely as an ending chapter, clearly inspired by DUSK's final levels. We have upgrades and weapon "mods" that you can buy and swap at specific stations spread across each level, with save points for manual saving as well as checkpoints. Some of the mods are underwhelming or, at least, inferior to others that just feel way more fun and effective. The upgrades (runes) and points (blood gems) can be found most of the time inside secrets, which are very well hidden, so you'll want to explore the levels or use a guide because otherwise you're gonna miss out on some juicy things. There's also an optional, challenging side-area in most levels with some rewards as well.It has a decent amount of Bosses but nothing that you can't kill by circle strafing while shooting, except maybe the final boss, who kicks ass.Overall, you'll have a good time with this game! Especially if you go past E1. It also comes with 5 difficulty modes, a wave-based Guardian Mode, and New Game+! So you can't get tired of it easily
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I was nearly fooled by the menu and lack of options to think that it would be a sub-optimal game.I was wrong.My only poor critique about this game is that it wouldn't have many replay-ability opportunities with it's upgrade system.The game runs very smoothly with good mechanics. The gameplay is simple, but very enjoyable. Execution is great.The fact that this is early access is what most games similar to this development should strive to be. A very passable, enjoyable game that has a lot of upside with further development and feature-additions.I can see a world where a Dread Templar 2 would be amazing if they improved from this title. UI, Gameplay Options and an overhauled progression system.Excellent addition to the genre at a good price point. 8.5/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: What started as a nice little Quake-like demo last year and evolved into a behemoth of a retro-fps title. The enemies, weapons, and level design are top-tier. This is one of those games where you think you've seen all it has to offer not far into it, but it keeps expanding and adding to what is on offer. It never stops being fun, and my jaw was on the floor towards the end of what is currently available in the EA build. This deserves to be regarded as one of the great modern retro shooters along with titles like Dusk, Amid Evil, and (hopefully when it's done) Wrath. Really looking forward to seeing what else comes from T19 and Dread Templar, but even in it's current state it is well worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Templar

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a TON when they offered the free demo a while ago and had a blast. There was enough there to convince me that grabbing this thing as soon as it hit EA was a must. I don't usually buy EA titles (early access, I never buy games from EA :) ), but for my money, there is already enough there to justify $15. Obviously YMMV. I will say that the combat, weapons, movement, MUSIC(!), level design, and visuals are all spot-on and the gameplay is fast run-n-gun like Quake & Dusk. Add in options to upgrade yourself and your weapons, and optional side-areas and you've got a wonderful, bloody, savage time on your hands. Oh, and the katana throw. Oh my, the katana throw...

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Templar hits a lot of good notes—notes essential for a well-crafted boomer shooter. The first thing that impressed me right away was the sound design. Sound design is integral to any good FPS game. For one, the guns should sound powerful. The first gun you receive in Dread Templar (or guns, rather) are pistols that you duel-wield. These wicked twins are total beasts and sound the part. These pistols have one of, if not the most, satisfying gun sounds I've heard in a long time. With these, you'll be slinging lead like Revy from "Black Lagoon" and be just as menacing. Roughly 3 hours of content (as you can see from my hour count, that's how long it took to beat) but a damn good time it was! I can't wait to see more. Want to hear more? _childDocuments_.review: It is the 15th of August as of writing this review. I have beaten  of this game that contains the first two episodes. Will update this later.Pros:- Gameplay is quite fun! Nice fast pace and switching between weapons during encounters is satisfying. Weapons feel pretty good too.- Interesting visual style.- Doors and interactables are labeled with noticeable symbols, which definitely helps with making exploration less confusing. On top of that, unlocking certain doors shows a little cutscene (which you can actually skip).- You can assign different upgrades to different weapon classes, allowing for a bit of customization. The upgrades are super simple (increased damage, ammo capacity, fire rate, etc.), but it's something. You can also upgrade yourself. Maybe the upgrades will become more interesting later. The game does mention the weapons possibly changing appearance depending on upgrades.- The two bosses of episode 2 are quite interesting!Cons:- Sound design needs serious work. Every single pickup uses the same sound effect. Picking up a brand new weapon plays the same sound effect as when you pick up some ammo for your starting pistols. Picking up a brand new weapon should be a triumph, not part of a routine. You get the same feeling when picking up a nice piece of armour because of the lack of memorable and distinguishable sound effects. Finding a secret does not play any sound effect either. Taking damage should also feel more punishing, but it doesn't because all you get is a very subdued "oof" from the main character.- On the topic of taking damage not feeling punishing, there is very little visual indication of it too, as in basically none. Generally, UI elements appear to be missing. Picking up a new weapon not only does not play a noticeable sound effect, but as far as I can tell, there is zero visual indication telling you what you picked up. This actually goes for everything. I am sure every single classic shooter shows a little text indicating what the player has picked up, but apparently not this one.- The music is bad and REALLY grating. Not fitting for a game where there is light exploration going on. Just a constant cacophony of weird-sounding metal. I would go as far as to say it doesn't really fit the visuals of the game.- You can get hurt and even killed when you are in the upgrade menu, but there is zero indication. Upon exiting the menu, all of the attacks you have been hit by will have their sound effects play AT THE SAME TIME. It's not right.- Actually, you can get hurt during cutscenes too I think.- The missions don't have names. For a game taking inspiration from classic shooters, that is inexcusable. It doesn't even show what mission you just beat when you reach the level ending screen.- The bosses of episode 1 are quite boring.A decent amount of complaints, but this game definitely has the fundamentals down. That might seem like not much of a compliment, but there are a ton of games that are not fundamentally fun to play, indie or triple A. Looking forward to the next update!

Dread Templar is a fast-paced first-person shooter that combines elements from both modern retro shooters and classics from the 90s. 

You are a Dread Templar seeking his revenge deep in the evil realm. Explore the levels and solve puzzles to find hidden weapons and upgrades. Face hordes of demons and bloodthirsty fiends using ninja equipment, firearms, and infernal weapons that will make YOU the scariest thing in hell. Gain Dread Powers and customize your skills according to your playstyle, as they will help you in your battle against the dark forces.
