name: Sumire
detailed_description: Sumire is an indie narrative adventure, featuring a one-day journey through a picturesque Japanese village. In this enchanted place, a disenchanted girl named Sumire meets a mischievous spirit who makes her a deal to fulfill her most desired wish. But in order to see this wish come true, she must complete a series of tasks in return, before night falls and this special day reaches its end. A Narrative Quest-Driven Adventure Follow Sumire on a series of quests both big and small, given by charming forest creatures, quirky townspeople, and Sumire's own heartfelt needs. Take or refuse them, but be wary: as the day progresses, your path will change and you may never get the same chance again. Discover collectibles, bonus items, tests of skill, and other challenges -- some hidden, some not. Explore a variety of lush, beautiful environments rendered in a painterly style. A one day time limit. With the sky changing from the promise of morning to the soft twilight, all choices are finished when the sky turns to violet. Between the Magical and the Mundane For a single day, the magical world crosses with ordinary life for Sumire. Within this ambiguous time, be extra mindful of words, choices, and actions taken. What awaits at the end of the day...? A Day to Remember, and Choices to be Made Guide Sumire through her reality, her dreams, and her memories. As the sky changes throughout the day, Sumire too must come to terms with the changes that have affected her life, as well as those around her. How Sumire ultimately addresses these matters is influenced by the player's guidance, seeking to turn a life unlived into a final dream come true.

The story is pretty short, but eventually ask you to run it few times to own every achievements.It leaves a little bit of something once you reach a certain point of the game, seeing really what you did makes a difference even if it's small and only to the people you know in the town ; you think about what you try to do and sometimes regrets not choosing the other option (or not lmao).I still wish we could pet the cat. Such a chubby cute cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a japanese indie game. Sumire means violet, it can also refer to flowers like the one that protagonist has in her hair. You can see how it looks like by searching スミレ in google images. It's not voiced, everything is told through text accompanied by beautiful soundtracks. It has multiple endings, and choices you can make, hence it encourages multiple playthroughs. For the price tag on sale It's very much worth it, despite the fact that one playthrough lasts 3 hrs or so. It's a sad, beautiful title, playing through it feels like cleansing your soul. Some words were simplified in english since they only exist in japanese like ランドセル = backpack (It's a very specific kind of backpack that elementary school children use, which suggests that sumire is 6-12 years old) はんてん = small coat ( google 半纏) Which is to be expected. The background text was also left untranslated. Simple stuff like sign "ポイすて禁止" no littering, items in the stationary shop, poem in sumire's house on the wall. I feel like it does make it more charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really weak to emotional narratives, I get too involved with the characters or the story, and they sneak into the corners of my soul. Sumire is a proposal that aims to pull at the heartstrings, whether with beautiful and adorable moments, or sad ones that come to feel more like stabs. Presented with some really beautiful visuals, a calm but at times energizing soundtrack, and a protagonist that one can't help but want to protect, it was a game that left me pleasantly surprised.The story follows Sumire, a little girl who hooks us from the start with a theme of loneliness and grief. Her mother pays no attention to her, ever since she plunged into a void of hopelessness after her separation with her husband, and her best friend has grown distant and no longer knows how to reconcile with her. One can't help but feel sorry for Sumire, as these are very mundane feelings and ones that most of us can relate to.Fortunately, something will change on the night the game starts. After dreaming about her grandmother and not being able to interpret the meaning behind it, a seed falls from the sky, and from it sprouts a beautiful and magical flower. It explains to Sumire that it has only one day to live, and wants her to take it to spend the best possible day, being more of a gift for the girl than for the flower. It is then that they both set off on the adventure, with no fixed destination but with a clear goal: to make it an experience to remember.As we advance we’ll find different situations, where we can make Sumire choose between two options, and we’ll shape our ending depending on our actions. Basically, there is a karma system, and we’ll have to behave well or take the girl down a darker path. The second one hit me much harder and I recommend doing it first in any case, as it deals with the characters in a different way.It's a plot full of morals and situations that several of us are familiar with. Loneliness, loss, the search for understanding, all intertwine in a very touching way. Besides, some Japanese traditions are explored, they show us for example the steps to follow to pray in a temple and some other little details, adding a cultural touch that I personally like.On the other hand, each action we take will make a petal fall from our flower, giving us a visual representation of the progression, and a notion of our current karma depending on the color it takes. At the same time, we’ll have a to-do list, where Sumire will write down the things she wants to do that day, further clarifying the objective of the adventure. It should be noted that it is not mandatory to do everything, it is at the player's discretion.In terms of gameplay, it is very accessible for all types of players, as it has no difficult sections or hair-pulling puzzles. It is a very quiet journey in that aspect, with some mini-games and mostly conversations. The visuals are what stands out the most along the story, in my opinion, stylized as watercolors or brushstrokes that fascinated me, especially in some environments that are simply beautiful. The accompanying tunes set up a nice ambient, and some have vocals that elevate the experience even more.All in all, Sumire is a short, but beautiful game. It seeks to evoke different feelings in us, immerse us in a colorful world to guide our protagonist along the path that feels right. The absence of complicated mechanics only serves to make the spiritual journey more pleasant, full of touching and bittersweet moments. Needless to say, I liked it a lot, and it's usually very cheap on sale, so it would be criminal not to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful adventure game with a unique and gorgeous art style, supported by equally great music that progresses along with the story. And it's an extremely soulful, touching story. The emotional themes are pretty blatant, but the storybook nature lends itself well to that, whereas this might be a criticism of mine against other games. Can't deny I had tears in my eyes. As for the gameplay, it's simple though perfectly aligned with the story. To stay fresh throughout the three hours, there are some minigames that nicely complement the usual flow of walking around and talking to people/things. Last note, this game lets you make a bunch of karmic decisions. I felt obligated to help everybody I could and be nice, so I can't speak to how different the game plays out if you're a rotten brat or refuse to help anybody, if it's significantly different. One of the only times I did something bad (small spoiler ahead)  Still, despite being satisfied with my overall good karma, having ways to personalize your experience is appreciated. A smaller example are the coins acquired by exploring and doing favors. You can purchase cute, mostly cosmetic items with them. But there are only so many coins. That's deliberate of course, and it's part of why I love this game.If I had any gripes, they're minor ones. The few loading screens aren't seamless. Everything loads instantly so it's not a fundamental problem, but seeing the screens at all slightly taints the storybook-style presentation. Another gripe had to do with some of the dialogue. All in all it's a very well-written game--however, I couldn't help noticing there were several lines that started with "Anyway . . ." in close proximity to each other, which felt repetitive. Again, very minor things most players won't care about, just thought I'd mention them for the sake of future games by the developers. When you're mindful of stuff like this, I believe it leads to an even better and intricately polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short narrative game that plays like an interactive storybook enriched with various gaming elements. If you are looking to pick your brains through puzzles or a very long experience, this is not for you. However, if the screenshots caught your attention and you want to get immersed in this beautifully painted world, please read on. is about spending a very special day in the life of, well, the titular Sumire, a Japanese girl experiencing the transition phase between childhood and adolescence. She just lost the only stable anchor of her life: her grandmother. Everything is changing around her, and her relationships with others are getting complicated. So far, she has been putting a lid on her feelings, and she prefers to leaves things unsaid. And then, suddenly, a magical flower appears, claiming that he only has one day to live and he would like to see Sumire take that day to accomplish all that she wishes for. The time constraint pushes her out of the comfort zone of her isolated home atop the hill, and she will interact with the local wildlife as well as the residents of the nearby city. The player’s choices will take Sumire’s day in several possible directions.Our main character is moved with WASD or a controller’s left stick rather than pointing and clicking. It is immediately apparent that although the screen scrolls left or right like a platformer, it is also possible to slightly explore depth to move closer or farther away from the camera: the world is a 3D environment, and it is used for great visual effects. The curvature of the edges feels like a tiny round earth, and some sequences are about moving toward the depth of the screen rather than sidescrolling. The result is gorgeous. Combined with the painted backgrounds and sprites, ’s world is absolutely delightful to explore. Some of my screenshots have already been selected as my new Windows wallpaper! Despite how short the game is, it is full of variety. There are quests to accomplish for other characters, and also several mini-games that range from avoiding evil crows to playing a card game. The quests are never difficult to accomplish, but the way you talk to the characters or the way you solve problems will impact Sumire’s karma and change small events or even the ending.The heart of the game is in Sumire’s dialogues and interactions with others. She tends to be very assertive with non-humans and extremely shy with other human beings, but the player can influence her behavior. For example, Sumire can confront people or not, she can forgive or get revenge, and so on. Her body language, her way to express herself, as well as the idiosyncrasies of the Japanese language translated into English, made her a very cute and compelling character. She is so well written that I was looking forward to every single line of dialogue… and this is coming from someone who usually doesn’t care about stories in video games and frowns at cutscenes. I even played the game twice, once with positive karma and once with negative karma. My first run took between 2 to 3 hours. I am still considering a third run to change a few interactions, that is how rich the game is despite its apparent simplicity.Notwithstanding my comment about changing interactions, the overall structure of the game is quite linear, as specific cutscenes are necessary to move to new locations, and the next step is always made obvious. You won’t get lost or left clueless about a puzzle. Yet, you have enough freedom in your actions not to feel constrained by a linear adventure: the developers at GameTomo Team struck a nice balance. There is also a fine balance between magic/fantasy creatures and the humans in Sumire’s life, both impacting each other subtly and gracefully. If I had to find one single nitpick, I would say that one of the songs that played in the background with acoustic guitars was repetitive. That’s truly all I can find to complain about…Navigating ’s gorgeous painted world and the changes in her life left me utterly charmed. This game is short and simple, and yet it offers richness in terms of gameplay with a soft blend of 2D and 3D, as well as a variety of minigames and situations that offer multiple outcomes. This game is like an enhanced storybook, combining the best of both worlds: an enchanting story, gorgeous pictures, great writing, interactivity, and player choice. If you like the screenshots and you don’t mind playing as a little girl within a game that is both short and easy, I heartily recommend . You might even find it touching.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm. Cute and relaxing story-driven game with beautiful visuals, exploration, peaceful quests... This game checks my boxes. And yet... Let's say, if you liked the writing in  or  then you're probably going to love this one and can stop reading this. Personally I found these games surprisingly shallow considering the serious topics they take on, and that they are trying to be deep and meaningful. I was still going to recommend Sumire, but then I saw that the only negative review so far is some kind of weird joke, so I'll write this for people looking for something more balanced. My plus side is, the game is pretty and I did enjoy it a bit. I liked the art, the music (though a bit repetitive sometimes), the journal thingy, doing quests, oh and definitely that card minigame and the interactions with the NPC while playing it. I didn't click with the story, though. It was sometimes confusing, I think there were a few loose ends, and it was so full of platitudes. I couldn't really relate to any character. I missed deeper conversations, and more sensitivity for the topics the game addressed (like bullying and mental illness). Also, heads-up that for a "cute and relaxing" game, a lot of the NPCs are intentionally annoying and mean to you, and there are some mildly scary and hectic elements. All that talk about a "perfect day" honestly didn't make sense to me - that girl must have had a terrible life or been absolutely bored out of her mind if she thought that day was great, even with the best possible outcome. The minigames were mostly meh. The game tries to put some time pressure on you, but AFAIK it doesn't really make a difference (except maybe for some achievements). Ah yeah, I don't think it's so cute that some achievements require you to be a jerk. I don't know if you can let your character actively harm NPCs, but it looked like it. I also found the controls a bit annoying, and - oh, for ♥♥♥♥'s sake it's NOT "Point & Click" as tagged (most likely by ignorant users, not the devs), but it really should have been. Please correct me if it's a Linux issue, but I had zero mouse support so no pointing or clicking ANYWHERE. All in all, this should be a "neutral" review. I don't really regret playing this game, but I can't say that I got much out of it either. Other people loved it though. Read their glowing reviews and decide if you're more like them or like me. If you'd like a well-written beautiful and emotional game about a young girl dealing with personal issues, (mild spoiler and perhaps content warning for both games)  and trying to achieve something, I'd warmly recommend . * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: A colorful bittersweet adventure with a touching story and a deep underlying message.⠀Bought on a whim, I truly fell in love with this game. It's hard to pinpoint what exactly attracts me the most but I guess it's a combination of things that make Sumire better than the sum of its parts. The art direction is fantastic, the music gave me shivers and is probably the most beautiful I've heard in any game! Finally, I really enjoyed the story and the message it passes on. Sumire is all about dealing with the hardships life throws at us, the capacity for love and forgiveness and how it's important to see beauty in the little and seemingly insignificant things. Not everyone will relate to this but if you are a kind soul, it will undoubtedly resonate with you.⠀In my opinion, too many playthroughs are required to get all the achievements and I can't understand why some of them are related to how bad a person you can be. _childDocuments_.review: Sumire, a young girl who is dealing with some issues, has recurring dreams about her recently passed away grandmother. She feels like her grandmother is trying to tell her something, but she isn’t sure what. She wakes up to visit the shrine of her grandmother when she hears a glass shattering sound. A little seed from a magical place that came through the window, laying there on the floor. A seed that will sprout a very special flower. A flower with only one simple wish, to have a perfect day as it will have to return to the place it came from when the sun set. So Sumire’s adventure, with the flower on her side, begins.The gameplay, a story driven adventure, mostly exists out of exploring and ticking off your ‘perfect day’ list. Which isn’t that hard as it’s part of the story. There are also small fetch side quests you can do, where you help humans, animals, a scarecrow and even a stone statue.All with a pinch of consequences, better known as karma. Your actions and choices will have a positive or negative effect. Just not as much as I hoped for as I’ll tell you in my final word.There is a fair amount of walking and running around but at one point you unlock fast travel.As a small extra bonus, one of the mini games that is a card game unlocks after your first play-through, ready to be revisited if you like. At least I’m fairly sure it wasn’t there when I started up for the first time.A tad magical and whimsical. From the water painted like art style to the colour pallet used. The depth of the game as you can walk back and forth along with the small curve of the globe. Or how the scenery changed. I liked all those little things and details.Beautiful. Each location has its unique theme that is very fitting. Relaxing or uplifting when needed and a bit catchy with moments.Controller or keyboard, your choice. I played with my xbox for pc controller and it was smooth and easy. Thumb stick to run around, B too run, Y to open your backpack and left/right bumper to scroll through it, A as action button. Which the game all explains as you put your first steps in the game.The movement was sometimes a tiny bit awkward but for me personally not that big of an issue and easily forgivable.The dialogue and story were sometimes a bit confusing, not sure if this is a me thing or…If you want all the achievements, then it can get repetitive as multiple playthroughs are required.It’s a short game that picks up on heavy topics such as grief, bullying, depression, divorce but also touching ones like love, new friendship, learning how to give grief a place, the choice to help others. Paired with underlying message(s). Message(s) of which I drew my ownconclusions as I believe it’s open for interpretation and everyone will draw their own thing out of it. Whether it be a form of comfort, a new view on things or a lesson/multiple lessons.I enjoyed my first playthrough and was satisfied with the ending I got, perhaps I should have left it at that.Of course me being me and being curious as can be I sped through another one. Trying to get worse karma and picking the most rotten answers/actions, which in all honestly really didn’t feel good, just to compare to the story and ending I just had of which I believed was mixed karma.There the game disappointed me a little as there wasn’t that much, just a tiny little bit, change in the overall story and no different ending. Maybe my karma still wasn’t horrible enough?But I’m willing to give it a, borderline -doubted a long time which way to swing-, thumbs up cause it was a nice experience to have gone through, one that I don’t regret in the end.Just be cautious if you pick it up and be aware you’re in for multiple plays if you want all the achievements.With love,Tchii

_childDocuments_.review: Well crap. I haven't been this emotionally ruined by a game since Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons. And, like that game, I loved every moment of it, but I will never play it again. You just can't have an experience like that twice. Running through again just to grab all the achievements would cheapen it.Sumire (the game, not the titular character) is proof that a story doesn't have to be 2deep4u to say some very profound things. Despite its absolutely gorgeous children's storybook visuals, it doesn't sugarcoat the uglier side of life: sometimes you have to go through fear and pain to see better times, some people are just awful no matter how nice you are to them, and once someone's gone, they're gone. Like all the best and truest stories, it is extremely bittersweet, equally tragic and hopeful. Just the way I like it.Sumire (the titular character, not the game) is wonderfully depicted, as are all the characters: even in spite of the relatively simple animations I couldn't help but feel her sadness. Especially considering that the relationship between my own parents is... yeah. Although perhaps even more painful than her overt sadness was Sumire trying to convince herself that she *wasn't* sad, although that does eventually turn around. If you want catharsis, you've come to the right place.And ultimately, this game serves as a good guide for getting over grief IRL: get out there, allow yourself to be vulnerable, help people out and make new connections. By making someone else's life better, you share in their happiness. There's no rule saying you can't be sad and happy at the same time.I hope you'll get as much out of this game as I did. It's definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful and artistic adventure game about making the most of every day and keeping in touch with the ones you love. Despite the talking plants and animals, it's a very down-to-Earth story about Sumire coming to terms with her grandmother's passing and her depressing life and then taking steps to improve her situation and relationships with the help of her new flower friend. The moral of the story is to not procrastinate - reach out to people and work toward your goals today, not tomorrow, because tomorrow might be too late.I don't have a single bad thing to say about this game. It delivers exactly what it intended to and it does so skillfully and beautifully. I can't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: What You Should Know Before Buying: Positives and NegativesPros:+Thought-provoking dialogue told through unpretentious conversations about big topics involving life, love, dreams, hope, and death+Captures the feeling of childlike wonder perfectly; nearly everything around you can be interacted with, and interacting with them spurs charming dialogue that builds up the characters and world+Puzzles reward you for paying attention to people and the environment+Soothing OST with incredible sound design (excellent-sounding reverb)+Hardly any loading screens in the entire gameCons:-There's not as much replay value as I'd like. I expected two different routes to the storyline depending on if you were kind or not, but the story largely remains the same with a few dialogue line changes. The ending is, however, fairly different depending on if you were kind or unkind-The storyline has some fantasy elements, and the amount of representation or explanation for these elements is very uneven. Even after experiencing both a good and bad day, I still felt there were some unanswered questions-The game is very short. My playtime reflects two playthroughs, one for a good day with near max completion of all help requests and one of a bad day. The map screen gives you the impression of the game being longer, but the final few areas are much shorter than the first half, making this impression false-One puzzle (involving the rabbit) was a bit obscure, in that I couldn't tell what actions could cause good consequences or if any action would be badAt the end of the day, you can ignore everything I said above and just know that when I took my first step outside in this game, the world felt like it opened up to me, and life could be better, richer, than I knew it before. For that feeling alone, this game is worth much more than it's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: StorySumire tells the story of a little girl with a lot on her plate. You will follow her journey, make lots of small and big decisionsand you will witness how these decisions impact the people around her and herself.You can help those around her or focus on her goal alone. Will you seek revenge or go the path of forgiving?Will you be a helpful, kind-hearted spirit or isolate yourself and be self centered?Will you be able to face the darkness inside you? GameplayThe controls are very simple and intuitive.There are many possibilities to interact with your environment.You can get different endings depending on your decisions. „Cutscenes“ aren't skippable except one.When replaying multiple times you can't fast skip the text. You basically need to button smash and this can lead to picking a decision you didn't want.The game autosaves after every decision, you can't make a save manually.MusicThe music really complements the game.It's soothing and compelling.And when necessary it gives you chills.It's not overpowering and really just fits.It supports the story-telling really well.I, for myself, am in love with the soundtrack.ArtThe animation definitly fits the narrativ.I liked how they went with a water color design.In my opinion it looks really nice.At times I cought myself just gazing at the backroundor just watched Sumire walking towards the screen. It's adorbale. VerdictEven with it's at times serious themes this game always found a way to make me smile and a First off you might not want to play it when you, yourself, are in a dark mindset. Otherwise:I suggest this game to everyone who likes deeper plot with dark sparks in it.But also tons of wholesame content when taking the good route. To people who want to play something simple and not too challanging. And to the ones who like to explore every inch and find every interaction. They are worth it. I really hope more people find there way to this game.It definitely deserves more attantion. And I think it's highly underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing narrative experience with beautiful art style and soundtrack! Written well and the whole game has clearly been crafted by talented people and with great passion! A true hidden gem that I'm glad I bought with this year's accumulation of Steam Trading Card earnings.Sumire is an emotional story-driven 2.5D (?)  game that feels really Ghibli-esque in atmosphere. You play as a little girl with family troubles and embark on a magical journey to discover who you are as a person. There are many choices along the way that feel meaningful and impactful. As well as some minor choices that affect little things here and there. I've only played the game through once so I don't know exactly how much things would've changed if I had chosen differently in the more impactful choices, but I could see several things being completely different had I chosen otherwise.The story and narrative is written well, is loaded chock-full of emotion and keeps you hooked through the full journey. Everything from the settings to the characters are presented in a believable manner. This is especially important in a game, which tackles very heavy and deep philosophical and life issues. It's very easy to make them sound hollow or cheesy but this game makes me truly care and think about the topics that are explored. Gameplay consists mostly on normal story-driven adventure game stuff including talking to NPCs and exploring. While the game is basically a sidescrolling adventure, there's 3-dimensional depth. Though the towards/away from camera movement is often quite limited, it offers depth and a better sense of freedom and exploration than a flat 2D sidescroller would offer.Mostly you'll be traveling to left, finding points of interests, coins, sidequests or NPCs to talk to. Almost every character has an errand for you to run and you usually have at least 2 ways you can handle the request if you accept the fetch quest. Basically you can do it the nice way or some less nice way. This will affect your karma, which I will touch on a bit further down. In some cases you will not be able to complete the quest if you choose the naughty option.There are a couple of mini-games throughout the game and they are pretty cleverly tied to the narrative as the characters might converse while they are playing some mini-game. That adds to the mini-game experience and makes them more immersive in my opinion.As mentioned earlier, the game has a karma system, which is your typical Good/Evil point system. It's based on your choices. As far as I understood, the game did not require you to 100% good or evil as I was able to get an achievement for finishing the game with good karma. Despite getting bad karma at least 2 times. The evil choices were often faster solutions and seemed less of a hassle but you could choose to do things the correct way. Even if it is more troublesome.The graphics are a clever blend of 2D and 3D graphics, giving the game a unique style and depth. Paired with a vibrant watercolour painting art style and excellent art direction, There's a really great attention to detail throughout the game world. It has been crafted with much love and care, that is clear. You will see many beautiful areas and vistas along your journey. Animations are generally done really well. Though the main character's walk and run animations feel a bit off. Left and right direction animation especially. Weirdly the harder angle (towards/away from camera) angles worked better and were actually done rather well.usually these type of adventure games would use something like pixel graphics and the kinda 45 degree "top-down" angle (think RPG Maker games) and while I personally like those type of games, having the side angle with gorgeous watercolour art mixed with 3D elevates the experience and makes it look really stunning.Just simply beautiful music and soundscape. It's mostly acoustic guitars with some vocals here and there. Some more traditional japanese style music in the mix too. Every piece of music fits the scene or area it's being used and just enhances the experience tenfold. Can't find anything to complain other than maybe in few game sections the songs could've been longer and looped less.Sound effects are also on point. Fits the general style of the game perfectly.These are the kind of hidden indie gems I always hope to stumble upon. Exactly why I started the tradition of always finding one game to play on New Year's Eve that I can afford with just my steam trading card earnings for the year. It forces me to look at games I would probably normally miss. Anyone who likes well-written adventure games with a lot of heart and soul should give this game a try.

They both have magic and touching stories - I recommend playing both over a couple of days because it's one heck of an emotional rollercoaster.   It's one day that can either be amazing or totally the opposite of that.  You deal with a lot of social issues like bullying, mental health, friendships in school, young love, parental separation, the rich vs. poor girl idea, and losing loved ones.  It was so very moving and very sad especially with Flower and the girl's grandma but especially with Flower.  I totally cried while playing this game and I liked the ending.  This game seems to me to be really fun and touching but some aspects of it can be disturbing and I am definitely touched but more deeply disturbed than many of the darker and more horror-oriented games. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of games like Ib and Yume Nikki (Dream Diary), for the setting and atmosphere. To be honest, I don't have the patience for story-heavy games anymore, but this game caught my eye and I decided to try the demo. I liked the setting and music. Couldn't stop thinking about it after the demo. So I bought it, knowing that it's only a few hours long.I was a little surprised by how much the game opens up after the demo, with more areas and side quests than I'd expected. Even some mini-games. I think this game has a good sense of world, despite its short length.There are lots of morality-based choices. For this kind of story-heavy game, I'd usually say "it would've been better as a movie/animation", but I think there are so many meaningful choices and interactive elements in this, that I feel it works better as a game.I played through the entire thing in one sitting. I'm not sure what kept me hooked, aside from the lovely music. Maybe it's because I strongly relate to many parts of the story. Or maybe because the characters are believable, interesting and well-written. Maybe it just appeals to me in all the right places.I generally avoid English localizations because they tend to be poor quality, so I played in Japanese. But I later discovered that this game originated from someone who visited Japan (ie. not a Japanese local), and that the developer team is roughly 50/50 Japanese and not. That's quite interesting. I think they did a good job.Overall, it was a nice experience and I enjoyed it. That probably means a lot coming from someone like me who can't stand 99% of modern games. Some parts were quite scary though, at a level that I think would probably traumatize children, so I'm not sure who the target audience is supposed to be.I think I'll probably replay it later just to experience the world again. But I don't think I can bring myself to pick the bad choices.Oh... one last thing. I almost didn't buy this because it advertises itself with review scores. When I'm trying to decide if I want to buy a game or not, the last thing I want to see plastered all over the game is vague numbers from random nobodies. Especially not at the end of the demo. I already finished the demo myself. I don't need review scores to tell me how to think.9/2021 edit: Still listening to the music months later. Really, really nice soundtrack. Also recently realized/remembered that Sumire is the same internet name a Japanese acquaintance used before they unexpectedly passed away in a tragic accident a few years back. So this game has added meaning for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little modern-fantasy narrative game about a girl dealing with a variety of tween crises (first crush, her former best friend turning on her, grandmother's death, parents separated, etc.) with the aid of a magical flower. Has a few tropes you might recognize from other tearjerker games of this sort, but still a charming, touching, and short play.A bit surprised to see the preponderance of Western names in the credits, given the very Japanese art direction and setting (apparently, the studio was founded by Western expats in Tokyo). _childDocuments_.review: Sumire is such a heartwarming game where we get to tag along with Sumire and her flower on a special journey that lasts just one day. And if you thought one day wasn't enough time for a game or in our busy lives, think again – this game is about to prove you wrong!Set in a charming Japanese countryside, you'll be right there with Sumire and her flower, striving to make this day absolutely perfect, just as we promised. With its stunning art style and captivating music, get ready for a rollercoaster of emotions – from happiness to anger, anger to sadness, sadness to fear... It's a complete emotional rollercoaster that we are going to be experiencing together with Sumire. During this single-day journey, you'll witness so many events that might seem a bit cheesy (like childhood crushes), or they might bring back painful memories from the past that you thought were locked away, or remind you of unfinished business that you might have left in the back of your mind. There are plenty of life events in this game that I'm sure many people can relate to, and loads of valuable life lessons to learn from it too.And on top of all the emotional journey, the game also treats us to several fun mini-games that are so well-made they could have been their own games! Sumire feels like a real hidden gem, and I absolutely recommend giving it a try if you're up for a journey filled with beautiful art, music, and life lessons.Who knows, maybe after playing this game, you'll realize that sometimes, all it takes to change our lives is just to have one perfect, courageous, and forgiving day ✨

_childDocuments_.review: Short, heartfelt, rather melancholy but with undertones of sweetness and hope - and hauntingly beautiful. These are some words that begin to describe Sumire. I wouldn't describe it as entertainment, exactly, so much as a work of art which evokes feelings in the person experiencing it.Pretentious? It may sound that way, but it can only be accurately called such if the description is not wholly accurate, yes? There is no pretense if something is actually art, actually emotional. Will it affect you? Who knows, your mileage may vary, but a lot of the themes are fairly universal so it seems likely. Do you currently need this experience? Quite possibly yes, quite possibly no. Decide for yourself.It won't be a super light experience, nor a constantly humorous one, and there is not a huge amount of gameplay besides exploring a vividly imagined world and getting to know the people and other beings who inhabit it. But if you're looking for something to make you feel things, give it a go.Lightly recommended for those who think it sounds like something they want to experience. Not so much for anyone who's already sad and/or lonely, though there is a fairly good (if slightly bittersweet) ending available - you probably won't get that if you do nasty things the whole game, so bear that in mind.

(it conveys the depressing mood of the main character but is not memorable as a result)It's over all a well though game with an interresting take on the visuals.Maybe something with a more uplighted story would be nice to see next. The concept works well for young children and its much better than popular things around VN.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special, everything in it is special, the art is gorgeous, the music is one of the best and the story is beautiful, it's difficult to say something about a game so perfect as this one, This game made me happy, sad, and even made me cry, this is surely a hidden gem in steam, Gametomo did such a great job on this one, and i certainly can consider Sumire one of the best games i have ever played in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I wasn't expecting to have my heart ripped out and be in tears, but here we are. This game is BEAUTIFUL. The art, the soundtrack, the story... just everything. Be prepared to feel all of the feels. If you're even remotely mentally fragile, skip this game unless you want to destroy your soul. 10/10 will be playing again to get all of the endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: A truly touching and heartwarming experience, that you should probably know as little as possible beforehand to experience it fully. It's not often that a game manages to make me tear up or make me want to change my life, but Sumire managed to do both things. The artwork is beautiful, especially towards the end and in a section within a house that i won't spoil. It goes surprisingly deep at points and encourages multiple playthroughs. Also loved the card game ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I've cried a lot when was playing this game, 'cause it reminds me a lot of my life's situations i had to pass through. I've lost most of my friends and feel of loneliness following me through many years. Like Sumire I saw how my family had tore apart and now i no more feel i am a part of it. Every people need to be loved and Sumire passing through her one-day path searching for her love trying to get it from a boy who used to be her friend but now... I dont think they're good friends now, more then classmates. Their relationships are unclear, that's why I'm confused about their kiss (both Sumire and Kenji can suggest it).Anyway, there is the story about what we can do with our lifes, but sometimes it's just about rely on destiny. People can be unfair and cruel, but you can choose to hate or forgive them. And there is no right answer for that. Sometimes you can't make someone happy - it's up to them. But sometimes it's enough to be beside them, support them. This game is reminder of the unpleasent reality, where we can do not much in many situations. But I think, it's better to live with that fact, then with blind hope.Sorry for some mistakes there could be. English is my second language. But thank you for reading ^_^**В игре не очень сложная лексика и даже со средним знанием языка её можно пройти без словаря/переводчика  <33
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: (Ignore my playtime, I might have left the game running when I was away. For a whole day. A couple of times. A normal playthrough should be 3-4 hours long.)Sumire is a mechanically simple adventure game. You mostly walk around, explore, talk and play mini-games. It also has some choices to make that may or may not change the relations of the main character with others or even affect the ending.The story follows a lonely, somewhat depressed girl, Sumire, who wishes to meet her late grandmother one more time. A magical talking flower, who can only exist in this world for one whole day, promises to fulfil that wish.The game's strength lies mainly in its atmosphere: emotional, melancholic and subtly sad, but at the same time warm and comfy. This is emphasised further by the beautiful visuals and music. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: While it seems like a short, simple game, it is much more than that. The art and music in this game is so cleansing. Making choices, either good and bad, feels like your actually impacting the story. Not gonna lie, almost cried at this game as well. Perfect for fans of visual novels and make your own choice games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game that can be enjoyed in one sitting!My first impression was fairly middling, but I was wholly won over by an incredibly thoughtful and gorgeous game. The writing is just right, exploring the ideas of life, identity, and relationships very well and offering interesting alternatives for both good and bad karma outcomes (though this distinction is, often, just aesthetic)Go listen to the incredible acoustic OST if you're interested!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! 7/10BEAUTIFUL artstyle, well-made drawings. Detailed.Lovely OST, adaptive music!Simple gameplay, very guided. Easy to follow while still keeping the sense of freedom; especially of choice in which each one definitely felt like they have consequences.Just wished I saw the post-happenings of the day with an epilogue, to give a more lasting impact to the story/character based choices we did.Nothing groundbreaking, but definitely an experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: What a visually-stunning game and more!! Although it only took about 3 or so hours to complete it, it was well-worth it! Gorgeous 2D hand-drawn graphics, beautiful and calming music, and so full of emotions, life lesson and good morals. If you are an empathetic person who feels so much, then this game will definitely connect with you on a deeper emotional level. I absolutely recommend playing this if you like all of those in one. The gameplay itself taught me about friendships, family, trust, bullies and standing up to them, loss and grief, experiencing first love, and trying to be a good person, but not a doormat, no matter what the world turns against you. I really hope there will be another game like this, or even a sequel, because if there will be, I'll definitely buy it! Moral of the story though....so many events, connections and feelings can happen in just one day, and it's down to you to decide what you want to do and when, depending on the situation and how much time you have left of the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: One Day, One Life. What a gem, this game is healing and really fun. It makes you realize what wonderful things you could do in one day given the choices you make in every step, and reflect on the actions you take as they can greatly affect one another. I'm so glad I get to experience such a game. The art style and the music is also good. Kudos to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play through of this game and I will definitely be doing another to see how different decisions impact the final result. Not only are the visuals stunning but the story is quite deep for such a "cute" game. Great point and click option with an interesting array of puzzles/side quests.Would recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Novel-like Interactive GameAbout 2h 8/108/10Sumire is a very short interactive novel-like game. There is not very much reading you need to do – it is fairly balanced between reading and exploration. To be honest I was a bit misled by the trailer: I thought it will be a puzzle game. However, the puzzles in this game are very simple. It’s more about talking to people and interacting with the environment.About the story: Sumire is a girl, who has lost everything.  She gets a chance to change her fate for the best or worse by doing the things she really wants to do for one day. Right, it’s basically the player’s choice how her life will play out in the future. A bit of a hard task… and in the end I chose to not finish the “worst ending”. Regarding the gameplay, you are just walking most of the time and interacting with NPCs – be it humans or animals.  There is some amount text to read in this game, but it’s not comparable to visual novels. Usually, it’s only a short dialogue between the main character and the NPC and it also depends on whether you choose to interact with the NPC or not. However, the dialogue is not skippable. The best you can do is set the text speed on the highest setting and spam “c”, but for me it still got a bit annoying (on my third playthrough). Plus, the game is kind of “forgiving” means you can’t get the bad ending if you have at least done one good deed. And no quick save options available either, so if you mess things up you have to replay the whole thing. Honestly, even though the whole not skippable part kind of annoyed me, I found the game to be overall enjoyable. It feels more like a “rough diamond” than a jewel though – the ideas were nice, but the delivery was a bit lacking. Sumire is in no way a bad game, but I felt something was missing. It felt like things were left undone, even though in the game they were “done”. I disliked also the impact of some of the things. It felt somehow like the world is black and white in this game:  All in all, I felt like multiple situations were “unsatisfying” and a bit childish. The whole game gives off a childish vibe like it is especially written for children because the solutions to the situations seem so simple (well, duh, Sumire is a kid though). I’d wish that the game had dealt with those situations more seriously though.All in all, while this game was enjoyable, it still gets an 8/10 from me because I was not satisfied with some parts of it. Lastly, my favourite part of the game:  I think this is a very valuable lesson for everyone out there because usually people tend to regret especially these things.

_childDocuments_.review: you guys....i cannot possibly explain how much i love this game with words. its so beautiful. the artwork is breathtaking and the story is so touching and moving. i enjoyed every single bit of this game. it actually helped me with my own mental health too!! everyone ive recommended it to loved it also. i cried so much lol 1000/10 absolutely play this lovely and tragically underrated masterpiece
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game over the course of three sessions. It can be done in one if you want to as it only took me in total a little over 3hrs to complete. But what's here is golden. If you're looking for a loving tale with mature nuances, it's right here, and I'm personally coming back to this game eventually. When I hit a time where I need this kind of reminder, this kind of embrace.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a nice and relaxing game.Despite the sometimes quirky control it has some really cool features like Bo's card game or Kenji's story arc.It also is a decision-driven game so what you decide will determine what ending you get. That means you can have different endings and intermediate results and the replayability is really high.And the artwork (and music) is awesome. If they sold posters I would put them on my walls :) If you decide to grab this game during a Steam sale you definitely won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very simple, beautiful game that you can play in some hours (3-4 hours).I've played the demo, before it was released, and I got interested. But I'm glad I only got it on a sale, tbh.I think the only good mark in here is really the visuals, the story is also okay but when it comes to more sensitive topics it doesn't explore them in a more deep way, especially in terms of social issues.It tries to be something else, but stays on the surface!Also, you can play it on Steam Deck, but it's not fully supported. When it comes to the mini-games parts, you just get a black screen on deck...It's an okay game to pass some time, you won't get that much emotionally envolved with the characters, and that's what's lacking in here -- more depth in the writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a really cute and wholesome game which you can play in about one less than 5 hours session.It has a good story, some intriguing minigames and a wonderful morale.Let yourself be transformed and learn a lesson for life: to be kind to others, strive for your goals and live the day as best as you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes it's nice to bask in the sunThat's the kind of feeling it left me withA perfect little gem for ages Sumire and up!Recommended.  Great artwork.  Good music.  Characters, story; all well done.  There were some interesting choices to be made as well.  Though I didn't go back to try the alternative... because I already had my perfect day.  I am content...
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful chill game that confronts you sometimes more subconciously, sometimes more direct with past trauma.But not sure if these are bugs or if I missed something: I couldn't help the stone and I couldn't help the turtle (I checked on them a billion times every time of the day. Also I couldn't find coins (I am guessing those where the sparkly parts of the ground? I couldn't interact with them and I couldn't find a shovel or anything like that.).I will definitely play through this at least one more time to fix the parts where I messed up, maybe a third time to get the bad achievements. Hopefully I can help the stone and turtle and find coins this time......
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: A good game about growing over a spectrum of relatable life problems with strong morale and phylosophy. Bad ending has some decent twist to it as well if a bit weakly written in comparison to the good one.My japanese friend told me that Sumire is actually the name of certain purple flower. There might be more symbolism to it than I comprehended.The only thing I felt off was the dice game which seemed kind of too heavily RNG-depended. But beating it was not required for the story and for an achievment one can simply grind it by restarting.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect this game to make me bawl my eyes out.The game doesn't even lay it on that thick with the emotions, but it tells it's story in such a believable and relatable way, it just hit me in the right places it seems.Sumire is a game about moving on and letting go of your anger, asking yourself what it means to be friends and deciding what you want your family to be.You play as the titular Sumire, a girl with a broken family and no friends, who suddenly finds a magic, talking flower one day.The Flower wants you to make it's day a special one, as it only gets to live for one day, in turn encouraging Sumire to take steps towards deciding on what she wants to do about all the loose ends she's left in her life.Will you make up with a past friend or will you hurt them like they did to you?These are the choices you will have to make and which will decide how Sumire's life will look like after the day is over.The gameplay is very simple, as it consists mainly of walking around the gorgeous town and it's various points of interest, meeting a bunch of cute animals and characters and helping them out with what troubles them if you want to.Even though this is pretty casual i did enjoy it a lot and with a short play time of 2-3 hours i think this is the perfect length to not get dull.A lot of praise also goes to the art of Sumire.I thought the game looked pretty okay in the screenshots here, but it looks so much better when playing in my opinion. The backgrounds are especially, gorgeous.The only thing standing out is some of the character animations looking a bit stiff, but that doesn't really detract from the overall pretty visuals.The soundtrack also is so much better than i would have expected.Each area has it's own theme and each is such a joy to listen to.I could just stand around admiring a new area and vibing to the music for a little while.All in all, i highly recommend you check out Sumire if you've got 2-3 hours to kill and enjoy emotional, story driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much. I'm feeling very emotional right now having finished the game. The game helped me remember that it's possible to be open and compassionate, to live in a gentle and openhearted way. I felt the emotions of the characters. I loved Sumire, Flower, Mom and Grandmother and felt for them. The art and music were so beautiful and helped me gradually let go of trying to rush, and instead to slow down and enjoy the moments. I'm going through a difficult time in my life and my family is going through a difficult time, and this game has helped me to process and attend to my emotions, and helped me to bring a compassionate and gentle light on the dark and difficult situations I am going through. Oh, and I loved how this game explored darkness, anger, hatred, pain, fear. The game expressed something I experience - negative emotions, anger, darkness - without shaming it, and without making it easier, and it helped me to have compassion towards that while also seeing the way to heal.

The graphics and music was gorgeous. I loved the little message at the end of the game too.I would love this maybe see a part two maybe in Kenji's or Bo's perspective and a longer version of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Just. Excellent.Loved the art and music.And there is a wonderful story which can help you consider something in your life ;)Short (2.5 hours, but replayable) and sweet :)The one thing that bugging me though: give more hints to the player about gameplay. But song is beautiful, cannot deny that ;)Other than thatMasterpiece 11/10Edit: Just replayed it the second time.Got almost all achievements and looked almost all variants of outcomes (you can get all of them on 3-rd playthrough, or on 2-nd if you watched someone's walkthrough ;)2-nd playthrough is also 2x times faster! (because you can skip all the dialogue and all unnecessary details)Loved the references to Japanese culture (if you watched lots of anime you will understand what I mean ;)Also, at the game with Kenjo I thought that he DELIBERATELY wanted to fail so that girl can kiss him! _childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute!!!♥ It is very cute. The story is so much better than I thought it would be, though I wish there were more social options for other NPCs, I played almost entirely good karma route, and I'll be working on a bad karma route.  Though the game is really interesting to me, that also comes with hoping or expecting more out of any possible 2nd games, updates or spinoffs. I really hope this isn't where it ends with Sumire.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful atmosphere and pretty calming and relaxing gameplay. Going around and helping the townspeople and hearing their stories and advice really helped me out of a tough time. I think this game has good messages and it really makes me want to go out and enjoy every moment i have left and be a better person.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: At its heart, Sumire is a game about flowers.Sumire ("Violet" in English) is a girl coping with loss and everyday life. Dad isn't around anymore, and Mom has withdrawn into a sad inner world. The protagonist takes up talking to inanimate objects and imaginary friends, and that would be heartbreaking... if the soundtrack wasn't so amazing, the art style wasn't heartfelt and whimsical, and the entire thing didn't come across as a beautiful little storybook, which it does. I can't tell you whether this purchase will be worth its price to you, but I can say for certain this is a game in which we get to watch a flower grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming game. At first, I was afraid it would contains the same flaws as Majora's Mask had, which is to be forced to play the game not only in real-time, but to have to repeat it until we finish the game. But from what I've seen on the Internet, it's thankfully not that, and is a peacefull experience that make players think about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very sweet.  A touching game that really tugs at the heartstrings.  I finished it in around 5 hours, but it was the perfect amount of time to tell the story.With a talking flower at her side, it has a magical feel, yet deals with real world emotions of mourning, loss, grief, courage, and hope.  In a way that doesn't seem preachy.  Sumire is a young girl learning to navigate the world despite losing everything, and you may discover a little bit of your own magic along the way.There are a bunch of optional side quests that yield helpful rewards, and in certain places you have a choice whether to do good or ill.  Some may affect the outcome of the game (I haven't tried, I find it difficult to purposefully play Darkside, to use SW parlance) but it helps you empathize with Sumire.You also don't have more than one save slot so - just like life - you have to live with the consequences of your actions (unless you re-start from the beginning).I found everything about the game to be quite lovely, from the graphics where the background moves smoothly as you stay at the centre of the screen, to the vibrant, and sometimes gloomy characters who inhabit Sumire's world.  And Sumire herself, whose expressions changed depending on the situation.I highly recommend this game to anyone who is dealing with loss (you may cry a little, but in a good way), or simply wants to play a game with beautiful graphics and a heartfelt story.  ^-^
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there is anything I can say about this game that has not already been said in other more eloquent reviews for this game. Frankly I just want to give this game one more thumbs up among the thousands more that it truly deserves. This is one of the most beautiful experiences I have had playing games in 2021. The look of the game is so lush and vibrant, it's like jumping into a watercolor painting that swirls endlessly around you. The soundtrack jumps from catchy and smile-inducing to solemn and introspective. The storyline is simple enough that anyone can follow it but deep enough to really awaken an emotion in anyone who ponders its themes. More important than anything, this game made me feel something real. That every day we live is a lifetime of opportunity. That you always need to say what you have in your heart because you never know when it will be too late. I care for Sumire, and I wish the best for that little girl. If you want something to sink into for a few hours, or just need a good cry, please buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that makes me wanna relive my childhood and retake those decisions which I should've taken in order to my life a bit better.. The movement in this game feels like you're in a picture book. The artstyle is cute and wholesome and the some of the characters are quite intriguing as well, especially the boy who plays a yugi-oh cards with you.. That moment did remind me of Gwent in Witcher for a second.. Anyways, highly recommend buying this..
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story, art, and music all coming together with great characterization that tells so much in such a short amount of time.  Was a bittersweet experience that I don't want to go into without revealing story elements, but if you're ok with that (and I get a kick out of that type of stuff) then I recommend trying it out.I don’t usually play visual novels, I don’t much like the walking simulators I’ve played, graphic adventures can keep my attention with the puzzles.  Sumire is very graphic-adventure lite, so it better have an amazing story to captivate me.  Well the story, the mood, the writing and dialog get a strong endorsement from me.  The music, just seems to fit, as if someone is reading the room and playing an instrument as you’re progressing, it’s not something I see in games much compared to some passive media where the scene and pacing is controlled.  To add to that, it’s very cohesive across tracks, flowing from one to another perfectly throughout the entire playthrough.Now getting into the story, I enjoyed it, I don’t want to alter someone’s expectations going into it, so I’ll leave it at that.  However, once I finished the game, I looked at my playtime of 2.7 hours and was surprised, I thought 4 hours had passed, it was so dense in delivery with character exposition.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, it's bittersweet, it's sad - but uplifting. A really moving story that might bring you to tears. Beautiful art and cutscenes with a dynamic soundtrack including some vocals that set a strong mood. Treat the price of admission like a movie ticket for a double feature film and you'll have no buyer's remorse if you're worried about the playtime. I think the game was the perfect length for what it was and the story it wanted to tell. The bonus card game is pretty fun too. The extra character interactions you get during it are nice. I'm so glad I found this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: An  absolutely lovely game about love, chances and about moving on. Love the artwork and music - breathtaking!  Trasnslation / writing? Could use a little more polish but it's a thoroughly lovely game with good premise. I care for the characters and the story. It's just beautiful1 Even the credits are wonderful, so warm-hearted. A game with a heart! Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a beautiful game, and I mean that in every sense it’s possible to interpret that phrase. It looks wonderful, it sounds amazing, it tells a delightful story through some exquisitely written dialogue… and it will grab hold of your heartstrings and tug like there’s no tomorrow until you are an emotional wreck of a human being.I knew the game was going to be something special when I had the good fortune to try its demo in the Steam Game Festival back in February of 2021. And I was delighted to discover, upon playing the full version, that the final product not only met, but exceeded my expectations considerably. This game is an absolute work of art, and should be considered an absolute must-play if you have the slightest interest in narrative-centric games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: WoW..... It's been so long since i really played a great heart felt game that teaches about life when you become blind in your ever day tasks. The scenes are just pure beautiful, the text could be a little bit better but i knew what they were saying, The music is wonderful.For me i give this a 9/10. Just because of the art, the music but most importantly the impact it shows within about life. if you love 2D Adventure games with a great story line then i highly suggest it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a short but beautiful game by its cute art, amazing ost and its touching story. The story is the main point of the game, they're many moment where you can make some mistake without realise it and you will sometimes feel guilty afterwards. Sumire was a memorable and unique experience and I recommend this game at everyone !
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review:
One Day, One Life. Embark on a mysterious journey to help Sumire achieve her deepest wishes, before the day ends and the sky turns to twilight. Sumire is an indie narrative adventure, featuring a one-day journey through a picturesque Japanese village. In this enchanted place, a disenchanted girl named Sumire meets a mischievous spirit who makes her a deal to fulfill her most desired wish.
But in order to see this wish come true, she must complete a series of tasks in return, before night falls and this special day reaches its end.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

name: Operation: Tango
detailed_description: FRIEND PASS About the Game Join our Discord Server NOTES: - This game is online co-op only and requires a microphone. - Thanks to the Friend Pass, any of your friends can play with you for free. - Cross-platform play enabled Operation: Tango is an espionage-themed cooperative adventure challenging you and a friend to complete dangerous missions across the globe in a high-tech near-future world. As an exclusive team of two, you and your partner will become AGENT and HACKER, working in tandem to bring a high-tech global menace to its knees. With only your voice to link you, teamwork is crucial, and communication is key! Now with a FREE CONTENT UPDATE - The Challenge mode introduces a new area to explore, new puzzles to solve, and new robots to hack. Game features: CO-OP PUZZLE SOLVING - Combine skill sets from different points of view to overcome challenges focused on communication, not difficulty. These missions cannot be completed alone. THRILLING ESPIONAGE - Investigate, hack and infiltrate while executing missions across the globe. Live out your ultimate “Hollywood” spy fantasy! HI-TECH TOOLS - Experience the visual splendor and technological advances of a hyper-connected world built around augmented reality. FRIENDLY BANTER - Constant communication makes for both heartfelt and hilarious moments. It’s all about sharing your voice. Multiplayer options: FRIEND PASS - If you own Operation: Tango, any of your friends can play with you for free. All they need to do is download the Operation: Tango Friend Pass on their platform of choice. It takes two to save the world, but it only takes one to pay for it. CROSS-PLATFORM PLAY - Operation: Tango can be played with a person who’s not playing on the same platform as you. It just works.

_childDocuments_.review: This will likely serve as more of a PSA than a review: Because purely in a gameplay sense, Operation Tango is definitely one of the highest quality "Hacker + Infiltrator" Coop games I've played. Lot of varying interactions required between players, minigame reuse is fairly rare, and each of the levels have wildly varying styles and objectives to them. The Hacker side has got to be the best visualization of the role in any game of this genre (Of which there are very few, to be fair) I've played. It's fast to navigate, completely changes depending on the context of each mission, and often goes as far as entering full first person control for some puzzles. It's a significant improvement over the usual 2D, lazily designed menu driven gameplay that the majority of games like this provide.But that's unfortunately where the praise ends, because we couldn't make it any further than Mission 3.The online for this game is utterly . My coop partner and I are in the same building, on the same local network. And yet from the moment we even started the tutorial, we were sitting at an average ping of 200ms. It fluctuated wildly throughout our entire experience, often spiking to highs of . The game was still somewhat playable, but desyncs in minigames became very irritating.But the final nail in the coffin was the full Disconnects for no reason. In only 80 minutes of play, we fully lost connection no less than 9 times. No fault with our internet or connection, the game just dropped us. The levels are generous with their checkpoints, but it was still frustrating getting instantly booted back to the menu constantly. And when four of those times were midway through a timed sequence of puzzles without checkpoints, we had to give it up.I can see a lot of positive reviews around, which shows that most were able to have a good experience. But we have Gigabit Ethernet throughout our house and decent internet: None of this is our own connection's fault. I can only expect that the developers only have a single set of servers in one region, and your experience will depend entirely on whether you're close to it or not. The Community Forums also have several topics from people suffering with ping issues.It's extremely disappointing, because from what we did play, the game is really fun and clearly well made. We were genuinely disappointed that we had to stop! But in the end we just couldn't play any further, the servers are inadequate.I'd say you could check the Demo to see how it'd perform, but it seems that the levels cause more network issues the further you go... Buy it cheap on sale, and be prepared to refund if you get a bad connection.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those asymmetric co-op games where you should not see the other person's screen, and are meant to communicate clearly in order to make it through.The game does a great job at changing up the puzzles, so you're always doing something different and interesting. Sometimes some puzzles are recycled and built upon, but every level feels fresh for the most part.Both roles are equally fun and have moments to shine throughout.The game is quite short. We beat it in about 4 hours. The asking price is quite cheap to begin with though, which is good. I feel it's worth the asking price. There are some super memorable moments if you enjoy co-op games.Although we didn't find the game that difficult, the game comes with a hint system. At any point in time, you can both agree to see a hint for the puzzle you're working on. That's something I appreciated, as it eliminates the need for an external walkthrough. Overall though, we found the difficulty to be just right.We didn't run into any bugs throughout our playthrough, except the final level. It broke on us 3 times, and we were wondering if we were just missing something, or if it was glitched. Upon restarting the game, the issues were fixed every time. Still, frustrating.In the end, if you have a friend and enjoy games like Keep talking and nobody explodes,  Exorcise the Demons, or We were here, this is a strong recommendation! A super fun game!

In 6 different missions, you are supposed to clear all kind of puzzles while having to rely on each other. Communication is a big point of this game and the concept was actually nice. With some nice graphics and especially the "free friends pass" like "It Takes Two" had, we had big expectations. Unfortunately the praise already ends there though. Many puzzles are quite boring, sometimes annoying and overall not designed well.  The worst part is the price tag though of about $20 (depending on your country) for barely 3hour of gameplay. A real cooperative experience that allows one of you to be a agent working a case, while the guy gets to be the guy in the chair typing away, and providing the agent critical information. _childDocuments_.review: This is a well polished though short co-op game (it took my friend and I about four hours to complete the campaign once).  The challenge mode presumably gives it some more replay value though we haven't dove into that yet, and of course swapping roles and playing again would effectively double the play time.  The presentation/visual style is distinct and fun and the "hacking" has some very inventive mini games that avoid a lot of the stale and repetitive "hacking" simulation cliches that have pervaded gaming for decades now so kudos to the devs for being able to put a new spin on it.The fact that it has a friend pass means you don't have to talk someone else into buying it which is a great feature, though be aware a player using a friend pass won't unlock any achievements so if that's a big deal to them they should buy it.If you're looking for a co-op game with a different spin than just another shooter I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, quick co-op adventure. The asymmetry of it makes for some very fun communication exercises. My partner and I enjoyed it very much, but the lack of content left us craving more after we'd done all the game had to offer.I do highly recommend it for a fun couple evenings of asymmetrical co-op goodness, but do be aware of how short the game actually is - It won't give a lot of replay value for your money if you're on a tight budget, but you'll deeply enjoy what it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: So, we did have a game-breaking sync issue between PC and PS5 on launch day. My hopes and prayers are to see it patched very quickly. :)But what does it say when I'm still going to give it a positive review?It's innovative, engaging, finding a random player to play with took a few minutes and we had a superb time up until the softlock. We were coming up with unique ways to communicate for different puzzles. Fully immersive.I think after a couple of playthroughs I'll need something more to bring me back, but for 18 quid - best purchase i've made all year.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a light "Recommend" for me, because the game is honestly amazing and fun - but it's just so short, that it's genuinely hard to recommend the 20$ price tag on it. I'll be taking my second playthrough with a friend to complete the other "Half", but the game is pretty easy to complete in a single evening. You're going to have a few times where you might feel a lack of direction from the game - but that's part of the fun of doing these sorts of puzzle games. The communication needed is on point, and it's never too complex to the point of being unable to properly coordinate information to one another. Whenever a timer appears, you feel the pressure, but it's never too much to easily overcome, and the checkpoint system and retries make it genuinely forgiving. I wouldn't mind a challenge mode for achievements to complete each mission in an Ironman-style mode to do it in one try. I give it a recommend because even at 20$, it's still fun. I just wish it was longer, and getting hit with what felt like an advertisement for more games at the end felt a little bit frustrating learning there wasn't another set of missions. Both of us said, in unison, "That's it?" when we realised there wasn't more to come. You'll have fun when you're playing, and ultimately, that's going to leave you dissapointed at the end when there just isn't enough 'meat' to the game.
