_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, and the asymmetric nature of the game means at the very least you get a play through on each character with the same partner and the game is quite different. Some of the communication challenges are a bit confusing for a while before it's clear what the players need to do. Fortunately failing one of the mini games, or getting caught as the agent is a quick reset and back to the action so learning what to do does not feel too punishing.My partner and I had a lot of fun playing through and look forward to doing so again in reverse roles.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Quite fun asymmetric co-op game. If a little short... Only 6 missions, which is maybe 5 hours playtime, plus time trials mode postgame. One player plays the hacker, using computer UI. Occasionally you end up in first-person in a virtual world representation of the computer systems you're hacking.One player plays the agent, in first-person view, infiltrating places to execute missions.You can switch roles between every mission if you want to.Both players seek to gain info and gain access to the next area, and deal with emergencies that crop up. A voice call is required since you will be passing information back and forth constantly.(You do not have to buy two copies of the game.)The story and setting is this world where everyone is hooked into technology in a deep way, and the cybercrimes you have to stop are nuanced at first, growing to become outlandish. The game also pulls out absurd techno logic, like being able to download a physical EMP grenade that your partner sends to you over the net. It's all outlandish and absurd in a way that hit my partner's funny bone in the right way.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: While some instructions aren't as clear as i would like after some tries you will get the hang of it.As of now a friend of mine and i finished the first round of the story mode. Cant wait to switch roles and play it again.- You need to talk and communicate giving each other information and synchronize your actions- You need to challenge your brain a bit. So no relaxed couch gaming, but that makes it fun- Fair price (15€). Played ~5h and didnt touch the challenge mode with 10 extra levels + can play story mode with reversed roles.- ++++ Only one needs the game, the other can join for free -> so 8€  (friend an i bought it too support the game but you dont have to, which is nice)Overall a thumbs up...... if you have a friend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool co op game, the puzzles are enjoyable to figure out and the game has a lot of variety for it´s runtime, which is about 2-4hrs for one playthrough and maybe a couple more for challenges or re doing it as the other character, it is a pretty short game for it´s price, but only one person needs to have brought it so I would recommend you get it on a sale
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a fantastically unique concept that was also well executed. A co-op game that requires verbal communication skills to relay information and solve puzzles together from 2 completely different perspectives. The co-op aspect is enjoyable and collaborative. The puzzles are not overly complicated but still satisfying to complete through teamwork. The execution of the "spy" theme feels so right over voice that where you constantly bombard each other with fancy tech and spy terms like "mainframe", "decryption" and of course - my personal favorite: *LOUD KEYBOARD CLACKING HACKY NOISES*. The immersion into the "agent/hacker experience" is on point for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Among asymmetrical co-op games in which two people with different roles attempt to work together, Operation Tango is by far the best implementation by far. Yes, as you'll read in other reviews as well, it is fairly short (2-3 hours), but make no mistake, these are quality hours.It's impossible to review this genre without referencing Keep Talking, so let's get it out of the way. This is the better game. Keep talking is fine, simple, and streamlined, but the variety of puzzles, challenges, and new ways you and a friend will have to communicate data, ideas, and other information keeps the game fresh throughout the entire 2-3 hours. In essence, Keep Talking is one very well designed level while Operation Tango is many well designed levels. The two roles are so vastly different that I found particular enjoyment when I watched another set of friends attempt the same puzzle but from the opposite side.Beyond that the artwork and world building are solid, making it a pleasant experience visually.I believe we'll continue to see evolution in the asymmetric co-op experience, but at the time of writing this and having played (to my knowledge) all the previous PC games with this mechanic, Operation: Tango is the current leader and a must play for anyone looking to be challenge their friendships in what ultimately amounts to a trust exercise taken to extreme limits.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing else I play with friends will come close to this experience I've had. It's wonderful to bring in Friends with the sick free pass and seeing your friends excitement never gets old. The only thing that does get a bit old is that every activity in the missions are essentially the same just with a few different digits. That's not really a bad thing since now my friends and I are hoping to speedrun!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great time with a friend. You both work together to solve a variety of puzzles, some shamelessly taken from other games. It was a blast the entire time! But, it is so short it only took me and my friend 3 hours to beat. At 20$ you could buy a more robust co-op game on the market. Granted only one player needs to buy it but I would say this game is worth 10$ for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a long game. My friend and I are about 3 hours in, and have two missions left (I believe). That includes us going back and swapping roles for the first two missions to get both experiences. That said, it's a lot of fun and we are enjoying the hell out of it. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but way too short for 17€.We finished it in 2.5h without any hints.The challenge mode could be fun, but it seems to reuse every single tools you have already used in the main campaign, which makes it pretty boring.I would have preferred for them to sell a new campaign for ~5€ instead of these challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, it's very fun, it's creative, it has memorable moments, and it's especially good when you want to put your communication skills to the test.But... I just had MAJOR issues.SPOILERS AHEAD:In my most recent playthrough with a friend, we managed to get softlocked TWICE.In the forth mission, where the agent has to open a gateway to let the hacker through, the "open" button loads really quickly before letting you actually opening the door.We failed, because my friend didn't know how quickly he fell, so we restarted, upon restarting, the Open button was stuck PERMANENTLY loading, so we couldn't open the door no matter how long we waited, we even tried killing ourselves again to try and fix it, but it didn't work. It was frustrating, because of how deep the point in the mission is, it just wasted time.In the final mission, where you go through a hotel to find the cords for the bomb, the game EXPLICITLY told me where the cords were, but the little screens didn't show us the cords, so we couldn't even get past the EASY part of the mission.I played this game multiple times and NEVER had these issues until last night and the time this review is up, which is heartbreaking because I LOVE this game to bits, but I can't in good conscious recommend a game that has these recent bugs.Until these bugs are fixed, I can't recommend a game, even if it is fantastic.But hey, maybe I'm alone here, you'll probably never have these issues come up, hence why I'm posting this as a positive review.Provided you don't have my experience, this is probably some of the most fun you'll have with a friend recently.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Has some keep talking and nobody explodes elements to the game. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with really well thought out puzzles, levels and difficulty. Communication is key to passing each level, and the different perspective for the Agent and Hacker is really excellent and done in a way that's balanced and fun to play as either role. This also adds a kind of  reason to play the game a second time. But as others have pointed out the game is super short. There's only about 10 missions and then simple challenges after that, so the length of the game was a huge disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Clever Plays for the friend pass system. Other devs *please* take this approach going forward. I want to play your indie 2 player coop game, but convincing another player to buy a game just so they can play it with you is frequently a deal breaker. Operation Tango is good evening's worth of entertainment, but it is just that. The game is short, it took me about 45 mins per mission and there are 6 missions. There is no replay value here, it's a one and done deal. However, for your money, you are getting a fun, stylish asymmetric coop puzzle game, dense with variety and invention. The game throws a new mini puzzle at you every few seconds with minimal repetition. The focus is on keeping forward momentum going and minimising frustration, so the puzzles are relatively easy and checkpoints are plentiful. If Clever Plays continue this format with a sequel or DLC I will be back.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a 2-player co-op game where one plays as an Agent and another as a Hacker. You both have different tasks to complete but they are interlinked with each character which makes communication so important in this game. The puzzles in this game are fun and easy to solve. They are also lenient on failures and there are unlimited checkpoints after every puzzle. A must play for 2-player co-op games. Definitely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to We Were Here and had intense elements like in Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. I absolutely loved the game and it is worth it to replay it a second time as the other character. The art style is very pretty and the missions were immersive and fun. We encountered a few bugs here and there but nothing that completely ruined the game for us. The game was short but a lot of similar co-op games have even shorter play times. One of the best two-player co-op games I've played. I hope they add more missions because I really want to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If we are not taking price into account the game is a solid experience with fun little puzzles, its not really difficult or complex but results in a fun and interesting time with the theme. Problem is you will beat it in one sitting. There is a challenge mode which drops most of the theme and leaves just the puzzles with a time frame that almost doubles the length. But the length is still unbelievably short. So if your willing to pay 20 dollars for a couple hours then yeah its worth it but, if don't have a lot of money save your money.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, it was so fun to play with my boyfriend. We played through all the missions as both Agent and Hacker and got all the achievements minus the challenges. I did almost call him a pr*ck though at one point because in the first mission as the hacker I struggled with the one task in the vault and we were on it for ages. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: clocks in at about 6 hours of play (I see many others completed it in around 4 hours, so maybe we're just slow). There's a lot of great asymmetrical co-op fun to be had here, with one person playing the field agent, infiltrating and navigating various locations, and the other playing "the guy in the chair", hacking systems and databases and helping the agent get where she needs to be. As is typical of the genre, patience and communication are key.What's nice for a change is that the hacker role gets to do some limited first person action in the form of a virtual environment he has to navigate to achieve various goals. It's a nice change of pace from a strictly supportive role.Absolutely minor pet peeve: IP addresses that are out of valid ranges. They did  on this for the first half of the game that we actually commented on how refreshing it was, but then out of the blue all the ranges went wacky and into the high hundreds. Oh, well.There was also one puzzle in particular that didn't make a lot of logical sense, but we figured out the gist of it even if it seemed less puzzle and more arbitrary hunting. It was a little unimaginative, but again, that's a minor quibble in an otherwise high quality game.Overall,  is a fun entry that I can easily recommend. There are interesting puzzles, some tense moments, and a great opportunity to work on your communication skills. ;)Watch for the Asymmetrical Co-Op Bundle to go on sale and you can get several worthy co-op games a great discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a barrel of laughs, Had a lot of fun, it's short but definitely worth $20 for two people, our completion playtime was around 3 hours, with 6 missions, loved every second of it, especially mission 4. Would highly recommend this, since it costs about the same price as a movie ticket and it's twice as fun. I really hope that the developer decides to make DLC or make more missions, would definitely pay more for more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great asynchronous gameplay, interesting puzzles.  Sometimes the game doesn't quite give you enough information to work with but I don't mind that, it makes you figure it out on your own.  If you pick this one up do yourselves a favour and don't use the hint feature or any online walkthroughs.  The only real downside to this is that the main game only has 6 levels and you can get through them in just a few hours.  There are challenge missions but they pale in comparison to the 6 main levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great game just wish it would be longer. There are 6 missions in total which is quite short for it's price. You can play as an agent or a hacker and have the option to choose roles for each mission. Both roles are enjoyable, recommend finishing the game as both. Also only one person needs the game the other person can use friend pass for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: First a nice touch : you can have two people playing with only 1 version of the game. (the other install demo version and that's it)Also, the game is simple enough that almost anyone can play and it's a good idea to have 2 players cooperating on the same puzzle each with their specific control, UI and set of information.Unfortunately, UI is often inconsistant (what is interactive...what's not...), some mini games are lacking polish and balancing and overal the game is already starting to feel redundant after 3 hours.Buy it in special to spend a few evenings of cooperation.A simple game that can be as fun as it can be frustrating at time. (did they test the game?)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Me and my son had too much fun playing this game.  It promised fast paced challenges, and it delivered well.  Some of the movement mechanics felt clunky at times, but the overall experience was fluid and engaging.  I highly suggest playing with someone you know, the friend pass is an amazing feature worthy of praise alone.  However, even if you can't find someone to play with, they have a discord for player to find partners in.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun to play with friends. Really shows you how hard it is to communicate some visual cues haha. It didn't take too long to 100% but almost everything changes every time you play so you can replay with friends or with the same person for better times and it's still fun.EDIT: took a bit under 10 hours to get 100% in the game. That is playing through the entire campaign and the post campaign content with both agents and getting good enough times plus some other random stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Takes about 2 hours to complete, depending on the competency of your friend (If you have one that is.)I'd say the game is worth it if you manage to get it at a lower price, at current price it is a bit too expensive. (I managed to get the game on Humble with this months choice bundle) Games value increase if you intend to 100% the achievements, or play as both characters, which I suspect would take around 4-8 hours to complete.Game itself is very fun, I found some of the puzzles very satisfying, especially if you finish them without failing. (You better make sure your friend knows how to use a compass in head, and knows basic directions) We didn't contract any bugs during our session, game ran smoothly.Personally didnt like the FOV, as it felt very low for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but VERY short. 6 missions plus a challenge mode but there's some replayability since you can play each mission from either the Agent or the Hacker's perspective. Also, keep in mind that this is 100% a puzzle game so despite the theme, don't expect any shootouts or frantic gameplay. At most, you're partner will be helping you avoid some security drones.If you go in knowing what this game is, it's a good time. $20 may be a bit steep for how little content there is but especially if it's on sale and this kind of game is your jam, it's absolutely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: First look at Operation: Tango, I thought it was intriguing but I was unsure if it would meet my expectations; or meet how the game play had been explained, however; I was keen as hell because I do love a good co-op game to play with my best friend, there really isn't many co-op games being made opposed to multiplayer.  From the very first mission, through to the last it was great. Everything from the main menu, lobbying, the AI, explaining your goals and missions step by step, it all worked perfectly and I can't fault it. There was no bugs, no glitches, nothing that was out of order. Graphics were nice, ran stable and smooth, overall it's a really, really good game and I recommend it to anyone who loves co-op/communication based games. I finished it with my friend in about 3 hours, we are currently swapping roles to get all of the achievements; and It's a game that I could play a few times over and not get bored of. I do hope this game gets a lot of attention, I really hope/am looking forward to further updates and additional missions/seasons/dlc etc. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: What's there is great, there's just... not enough of it. Hardly a couple hours' worth, really. It sucks, because the asymmetric hackerman/infiltrator gimmick is fantastic and pretty well-executed.I'm ignoring the time-padding DLC sections here; they're just copypasted levels with compounding objectives.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly the greatest co-op experience I've ever had in any game ever. The fact that both characters have entirely different mechanics that coenside, I don't think I looked more forward to playing this game again as the other character. Both are entirely different from one another which kept the game fresh at every moment. The hacker literally has a new set of visuals and mechanics every level keeping that role interesting as well. Playing from the hacker to the agent was kinda funny cause me and my friend beat the game way faster than we anticipated even though we never saw each others roles before but the puzzles were just in our brain so it was like a speedrun. I hope to buy the sequel if one is ever made because I absolutely adore this game, especially if it becomes a series.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun asymmetrical co-op! Both roles were fun but I enjoyed the agent more! Got 100% Achievements in about 6.6hrs.There were a few game breaking glitches that needed to be resolved with either a checkpoint reload or by verifying the file integrity through steam which was slightly inconvenient but not a huge deal. I would have liked another set of missions since there's not much replayability after you clear the 6 missions with both roles.Praying that the devs make some new missions in like a DLC or something in the near future! Maybe add in more randomness.Overall definitely worth picking up and playing with a buddy!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Bunch of fun to play. Very stylised, and doesn't take itself too seriously, which adds to gags and humour, as well as the overall experience. There's an excellent foundation here, so despite my criticisms of the puzzles generally being too easy, this can be fixed with more content / DLC adding to the complexity / challenges the base game presents.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely great, I had 5 awesome hours with it with my friend, both roles are super fun, I hope they keep adding missions and new ways to play, maybe some more variation in the variables of the puzzle? it was a bit similar the second time around, but all around, excellent co-op experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a 10/10 game which left me and my mate wanting more. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - the game is OK if you want to solve quite easy mostly abstract puzzles with someone else. Beyond that there's not a lot to write home about.I would give this a "maybe" if I could. It's OK. Asymmetric 2 player puzzle games are few and far between, and if you really need something to fill that gap this will fill it... But it's very just OK. The good:Everything works well multiplayer implementation wise. Voice chat isn't ideal but also not terrible if you don't have anything else. Puzzles are pretty varied, you do get some 'stepping up' from one puzzle to a more advanced version later, but it remains quite fresh through what I've seen.The fine:The visual design, music, characters, story, etc, are all thoroughly middle of the road. There's nothing particularly original or interesting about it though. The puzzles are generally very easy, although there were some interesting ideas here that I haven't seen before.The bad:The puzzle design is completely disconnected from what you are supposed to be doing, ESPECIALLY for the 'hacker' player. You are apparently hacking into servers and the like... But usually this involves some very cheezy l33t h4x0r "going into the matrix" nonsense where you have to navigate through virtual worlds. This is true to a lesser extend for the other player - you're doing tasks that don't really make sense outside of being a thin veil over what is quite obviously an abstract puzzle design. There is the barest of connections between what you are actually doing, and what the story/world is telling you.And the world itself... Is lifeless. Outside of a few moments there isn't really anything in the world that even moves. Characters on a train just sit there - even while you walk around "scanning" them or whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow wow wow, what do we have here? Quite the little gem. Let's begin with a hearty round of applause for the ethical concept of only requiring one player to own the game in order to delve into this mandatory co-op adventure. Somewhere, one of EA's shareholders just died of a heart attack from the imbalance of karma. More devs like this please and fewer triple A studios.Heroic financial decisions aside, the game itself is also really good. Many games have tried this kind of asynchronous experience before but few pull it off so well. It's not just about relaying information to each other but also about how to correlate that information and the unique experience/interaction with your environment. It's like "Keep Talking" if you could leave the room with the bomb and interact with other stuff while the other guy is plugged into the matrix. So whilst short (~4 hrs), you really can go back through as the other character and deal with an entirely different experience. Honestly, I had a great night playing this with one friend and I'm definitely going through it with another (and then back the second way with the first friend) for maximum enjoyment. I think I got my money's worth, the price point seems just about right. One minor glitch was literally patched while we were playing. I think we're onto a winner. If you have many friends that will likely play a free game with you, you're gonna get a lot of mileage out of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is an asymmetrical co-op game (similar to a game like We Were Here) where one player plays as an agent and the other as a hacker, and you must communicate with each other to progress through the game. I generally found the missions to be interesting and challenging, with parts of one or two missions being a bit unclear what you were supposed to do (even after having completed it as both the agent and hacker!). There are 6 missions and 10 challenges, with the missions taking about 6-7 hours to complete, and the challenges taking 3-4 hours to complete at the highest level. The game's overall aesthetic and UI is nice, and I enjoyed the music. I personally think the price is a little steep, though only one person needs to own the game (the other person can use a friend's pass to join) and 10 hours to complete the entire game is a decent amount of game time. Therefore, if you can get it on sale, I think it is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright listen up folks. This game? This game right here? Think of it as Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes' next evolutionary step. This is a game of high intensity scenarios where you and a good friend are gonna scream, laugh, and bust your ass for hours. The game itself only needs one copy to be played which means send your pal 10 bucks, split that game 50/50 and get yo self some co-op spy action. The premise is you and your friend are two top tier spies, one a legendary hacker, the other a daredevil boots on the ground professional. You use your words (usually poorly) to try to solve a series of different puzzles in order to save the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ world. Is it cheesy? ♥♥♥♥ yeah, and that makes it all the more fun to roleplay and ♥♥♥♥ around in. There are plenty of parts you can just do something stupid and screw over your partner for a laugh, and others where your blood is pumping so fast you forget that you're supposed to be listening. It's short but I imagine there will be more content in the future and even if not I got 3.5 hours of gameplay out of just trying the hacker out. I assume knowing the tasks a little bit will make the next run through a bit shorter, but it probably ends up being about 5-6 hours with one of your best pals for a nice 50/50 split of $20, which to me is plenty worth it for the memories and the fun you're gonna have. Definitely recommend this if you and a friend are looking for a way to have a fun time for a night and it's cheaper than seeing a 007 film anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a handful of escape rooms played out as a separated-playspace co-op puzzler that applies a somewhat silly  narrative to sell all the arbitrary pattern-finding and code-breaking. Thankfully, there were only a few stressful time-sensitive scenarios, and even then the checkpoints were super forgiving. Despite the secret agent theming, the game is pretty light on stealth segments and mostly consists of asking your partner if there’s anything about an ‘x’ or ‘y’ code/symbol anywhere on their screen. However, when sneaking is required, having a second person on the cameras makes the process more interesting. The game is definitely at its weakest when it reuses or overuses the same mini-games, but this doesn’t happen too often and there are plenty of unique spy-esq scenarios to play through.Operation Tango is an overall satisfactory distraction. While it's not the most possible fun you can have with a dedicated two-player co-op game, it's about the right level of challenge and a good tool for practicing clear communication. Having a Friend Pass is a nice touch too.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T WAIT TO BUY THIS GAME.I didn't think three hours could go by in the blink of an eye like it did. What drew me to this game first was the art style and the concept of having to communicate with another person but not being able to see what they are seeing. I bought the game but didn't have anyone to play it with for a long while until a good friend of mine said they'd be interested! We both stream on twitch, so we got together, went live and now have 3 hours of memories to go back and laugh at again. I was laughing so hard I was in stitches!! So much to pay attention to, so much to describe, and the music is amazing to boot!We've only played through 4 missions so far, and I don't know how many are left, but I'm so excited to be able to play with them again and laugh that hard. 13/10 you should get this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Some co-op games are about telling stories. Operation Tango is about solving puzzles. Each one beautifully veiled as a high-tech caper, where one player hides behind a computer terminal as a hacker, while the other infiltrates. Both have very different experiences and entry points, and are wholly dependent on the other’s skillset. Often, the challenge here is to correlate intel from two different points of views into something that makes sense. Like the hacker looking at a solitary PIN-code, but nowhere to punch it in until the other guy discovers a code panel. Information won’t always make sense to you alone, so sharing it will more often than not result in some collective -moments where all the disparate pieces suddenly click in place. In a way, it’s a game all about talking. Or at least one that highly encourages it, and recognizes how important dialogue is for cooperative play. The missions themselves are pretty compact and to the point, usually with a gimmick or theme running through them. One mission sees you identifying targets on a train based on the apps they’ve installed on their phone. Another might have you sneaking around, dodging flying sentries as you triangulate the position of a bomb. None of them feel derivative, or even like they emerged from a common blueprint. Highly recommended if you enjoy solving challenges with a friend, and love games like Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the  not too long ago, I ended up developing a crave for more short co-op experiences. This brought me to  an asymmetrical co-op game where one person plays as an agent and the other plays as a hacker. It looked like an expanded version of  and that's essentially what it is, although it's far from perfect in execution.I like the style of this game quite a lot. The HUD design in particular is a highlight, as it's slick and it's very easy to keep track of what's going on. I also really like how the story of the game is presented in a comic book style, which really helps maintain the classic spy feel the game is going for. The environments and character designs aren't anything to write home about, but I still liked them well enough. More than anything though, this game succeeded in establishing the feel it was going for, and that was probably the most important part here.I had a ton of fun with this game. At the time of writing this, I've only played through the game as an agent, but I had a lot of fun with her. My friend, who played the hacker, also really enjoyed the game, so it seems that both characters are very fun to play either way. It's a fairly casual experience, and not one that's taken too seriously. You're given plenty of opportunities to screw your partner over and it made the game significantly funnier as a result. I found the puzzles, which make up the bulk of the game, pretty enjoyable overall, although I do think a couple towards the end were repetitive and presented in an overly-complex fashion despite having a simple solution. I found the game was at its best during the train mission where you had to identify a terrorist among the passengers () and the "heist" mission where you need to identify a suspect by cross-referencing information between you and your partner. There were a few points where I felt the agent was just a hacker-lite, and simply had to "hack" things on the ground, which I found slightly disappointing, but missions like the ones I mentioned were great examples of striking a balance between the two characters and giving each person time to shine through their distinct roles and the other missions were still pretty fun and unique in their own right. I think the big issue, however, are some of the technical issues we experienced in our playthrough. We ended up being softlocked multiple times during the playthrough, and we had to restart the game multiple times in order to fix them, and it was especially frustrating at certain points because we couldn't tell if it was part of the puzzle or an actual glitch. Thankfully, restarting the game didn't mean restarting the mission, and we were brought right back to where we were when reloading our game, which definitely made the issues a little more tolerable. Overall, the game was fun to play and did what it set out to do. It didn't really exceed expectations (outside of the train and heist missions), but it's still a good time either way and I was pretty happy with it.The story isn't anything to write home about. It's your typical "stop a terrorist and save the world" affair that doesn't really try to do anything unique with it, but I do appreciate that they let the story take a backseat for most of the game (only ever being brought up during brief dialogue bits or cutscenes in between missions), since the appeal of the game was just doing cool spy stuff with your friend. And occasionally deleting them from the system while they're trying to hack something.  If nothing else, it has charm, and it works for what it is.Again, just like the story, it's passable. There's absolutely nothing notable here, from the music, to the voice acting, to the sound design, but it never really got in the way of anything. I have nothing else to say here.Where I think  really falters, however, is in the content value, and that's mainly because this game is way too short. I finished it in a little over 4 hours, and that's considering the time I spent restarting the game and struggling through puzzles because I'm terrible at them. I normally don't mind shorter experiences, but there's so much potential in the gameplay loop they've created that only having six missions that take around 30 minutes (and upwards of 60 minutes for the last few missions) each was definitely a little disappointing. I hope the developers find time to add more levels, because I think there's still plenty of room for more content. It's not all bad, as there's definitely a little replay value in playing as the other character, though I'm unsure of the extent to how randomized puzzle solutions are. For $20, I think the price works if you and your friend split the price and each pay $10, but otherwise it might be safer to wait for a small discount for this one. At least you only need to purchase it once! That's a big plus no matter how you look at it.Overall, I enjoyed my time with  It's not an absolutely stellar experience, but I had a lot of fun navigating through different puzzles and timed situations, and it will definitely scratch your co-op game itch. There's a ton of potential in a sequel or DLC, if the folks at Clever Plays decide to go that route, but what's here is still a very fun and charming experience, even if it's a little too short and a little too buggy. - 7.5/10 - 8.5/10 - 7.0/10 - 6.0/10 - 6.0/10+ Charming art style+ HUD design looks great+ Very fun gameplay loop+ Only needs to be purchased once to play with a friend- Game-breaking technical issues- Extremely short- Agent feels  underutilized

_childDocuments_.review: Having experience with many other asymmetrical co-op games, Operation Tango is just as good as genre hits like the We Were Here series, and maybe even better.A majority of the game is talking though puzzles with you co-op partner, while each of you only has half the information. The most appealing part of the game is the spy theme, where you'll defuse bombs, and evade guards. Timers put you on the clock, and they pressure the Hacker into sifting through the information faster to keep the Agent alive. Though there's no punishment for failing and the checkpoints are generous. If that sounds fun then the game is for you.Compared to We Were Here (the second one), the game is a similar length (3-4 hours), and has a similar complexity. None of the puzzles were harder than We Were Here, and there's a hint system in case you get stuck. I would have liked to see Operation Tango utilise the Agent role more, as it plays very similar to We Were Here's roles. You don't shoot anyone or platform about, and your never get tested on your movement skills, but that's not much of a downside and makes the game accessible to older, younger, and disabled gamers.The game was buggy at launch for about 6 hours which explains the inflated amount of negative reviews. When we experienced bugs and quit, the bug fixes were ready to download. The Devs had already updated them within 6 hours of launch.A sequel or more DLC would be greatly appreciated,.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough game, got about 4 hours of play for $20, even while milking a lot of the missions. I wish there were more options to customize levels/sabotage your partner (heh). The first level had fun easter egg type things like customizing the elevator message and adding themes, which I didn't see in most of the other levels. The puzzles were pretty easy and relatively low key. Even if you messed up, you get dropped back right before your "mistake" when you "accidentally" killed your partner.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game if you have a friend to play it with.I didn't expect much when I first started it but had a lot of fun almost immediately.The puzzles didn't feel too difficult so far and very doable.We had some minor issues on one puzzle due to high ping but it was still completable.Definitely give it a try, only one person has to buy the game due to the Friends Pass! It's Amazing.Try not to spoil the surprise and go in without watching Videos!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice game that is a little like "Keep Talking and nobody explode" but it's for 2 players and each one has a very different role. Arround 4h to finish the story (and the level feels very different, even if some puzzle type are reused between level). You can then try again the game by switching role, and also do some additionnal challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Me and a friend were struggling to find things to do together and we had come across this.  As soon as we began It gave a great first impression with beautiful but simple graphics and very understandable mechanics.  The elevator at the very beginning serves as a fun tutorial on how you can both help, and screw with your partner.From start to finish it was an extremely memorable experience for me and my friend, and we then replayed it as the other character, which is an entirely different experience. It was very immersive.As we got deeper into the game some minor annoyances popped up. Examples below, marked as spoiler.Spoilers:The Cyberspace missions, especially the one with the multiple levels caused problems trying figure out how it worked.There were some minor Desync issues aswell which would often affect our performance. Another not-really-a-issue is that there is no replayability after your second round though as the other character. The only reason I take umbrige with this is I actually want to spend more time in this world.For any and all criticisms here though I must say they are minor irritations at worst and I genuinely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't like spending more than $10 on a game people refer to as "short" in the reviews, but I did so cause this game was obviously made with love.The art style is simple and beautiful instead of relying on realistic free assets we've all seen hundreds of times. The puzzles are unique in my experience and sometimes annoying to control even if you don't find them challenging. I doubt I'd play this game for more than 1 playthrough but I'm glad I got to experience something like this; and I will keep an eye out for similar games like this in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game with my BFF, it was so fun and difficult, I loved the game so much, both the puzzles and the way the game itself unfolds. And the best thing, only 2 roles and is enough for a cheering experience.I'd like obviously more missiones and cases, I know it still a "new" game but, you know, In about 6 six hours (with a lot of effort) we beat the game.I'd like particular places, I mean underwater, in-air missions and important hacking places (Russia, EEUU, China)I'd like ONLY IF YOU CAN, more roles, don't get me wrong, i mean 2 roles it's good, but if you can add more roles, it would be quite fine.It's a great game with a great potential, and I think is fun for play it for an afternoon. Please add more content soon and I'll give it a higher score.8.5/10 !!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal, stylish co-op experience that is incredibly reliant on you and your partner being able to communicate well. Both modes are remarkably distinct, and some missions were so thrilling that we'd immediately replay to see the other operative's perspective. There are some puzzles that might seem obtuse on the first go, but the game is incredibly forgiving  for mistakes.Solidly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, some puzzles are a bit too far out there. Mostly it's the ones where the hacker is running around and the agent is giving instructions. There are a couple of great puzzles, that also require you to think a bit. But most importantly, the tasks vary enough and they don't become boring before the game ends. Except for the challenge mode, where you just repeat everything you did during the campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, it pains me to give this a NOT RECOMMENDED.The game has a solid concept and good execution, but all that is ruined when the game stability is unreliable. I think on mission 4, we got through half way, when my screen started ghosting during one of the sections followed by freezing up... We were a little peeved that we had to start the mission over, but we powered through. Unfortunately this time, we got through like 90% of the mission when the game disconnected or crashed. It's unacceptable for a game that is so sensitive to network blips, to not have a RESUME level functionality. Or at the VERY least, a Resume Checkpoint feature.Both computers were connected via LAN, but that doesn't matter since the game forces you to play via their server, so your progress is at the mercy of them paying their internet bill. This kind of system might be needed to enable for cross console play, but should not be the _only_ option allowed.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed my first play through with my brother, and I was very pleased. The levels are all fun, and I'm looking forward to play again to experience each level with both characters. The levels give me the impression that they could be more difficult or have more to explore, but despite that, the cooperation aspect is really enjoyable. I definitely felt like I got my money's worth, and the free friend pass is such a plus. I hope they add more content at some point or do a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Encountered 2 game breaking bugs during my go: frozen rendering and irreversibly hidden UI elements. The hidden UI element can be fixed by purposely failing a puzzle, but I had to force close the program when the the game stopped rendering e.g. the screen was a still image but my mouse could move.For a coop-puzzler, this game is very short for its price and quality. Considering its bugs, it doesn't give you the best value for your money. Otherwise, the puzzles were a fun (not very difficult) test of communication.If you get this game, remember to kill your partner at least once for an achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Recently discovered this solid co-op game. Really enjoyed running through it as the Agent. Will have to do a second run as the Hacker. Single run through the campaign took about 4 hours. There are additional challenge levels to play through after the main campaign is done. Graphically minimalist but intentionally so, and looks great in the chosen art style.Puzzles are good and were decently varied, although there are some repeats.Really hope to see more from Clever Plays either in the form of additional DLC or more games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a co-op puzzle game where you play as two spies, an Agent and a Hacker, who break into places and steal important things that danger humanity in some shape or form. The story is pretty straightforward. You start off with what seems to be a routine heist on a well-secured facility, but this then spirals into a more engaging story featuring various individuals who are involved in the overarching plot. The gameplay is pretty involved for a game of this length and utilizes its co-op-focused mechanics greatly. The Hacker and Agent both excel in their own areas, and the game makes sure that the gameplay of either option is unique even when playing the same mission. Some portions are entirely reliant on the Hacker, some on the Agent, and most of the time, it's a blend of both. It's a surprisingly seamless use of the co-op nature of the game, and it's really nice. Each level also introduces a different setting with different mechanics, so nothing ever feels too stale or repetitive. There are also enough levels to feel fulfilled with what the game has to offer while also not feeling like the game is overstaying its welcome. Unfortunately, this game has a few bugs that sometimes forces you to restart sections of a mission or the entire mission itself, so that is also something you should be aware of.The art and sound design is pretty standard. It isn't anything that stands out, but it isn't anything bad. Overall, this is a solid co-op game with fun mechanics that don't get too old and stay for just the right amount of time. I recommend giving this game a try, but only if you have a friend to play it with!

The hacking puzzles do get a little repetitive over time but it does not get boring. Overall great coop experience :)

One get's to roam around the world like Kim Possible and the other gets to play her trusty hacker Wade. _childDocuments_.review: This is a really tight experience, not too long but extremely fun every step of the way. I'd say it's well worth the price, especially considering that your co-op partner can grab the free version and join in for the whole game. This game deserves more attention, and I hope it gets popular enough for the devs to consider expansions!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best Co-Op games out there, especially since as the game says: "It takes two to save the world, but it only takes one to pay for it". The friend pass is likely the best thing the devs could've done to this game. I could easily convince my friend to play this since he didn't have to pay, so we tried it and we really liked it. The game features a very interesting story line, and every mission is worth replaying twice from each perspective. Really reccomend, completely worth the 17€ or if you find it on discount even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Played this and beat both parts and fully completed game in about 5 hours or so. It's a really fun game and the biggest disappointment is that there isn't more than 6 chapters. It's taken some inspiration from Keep Talking Nobody Explodes and put it's own spin on it and it's beautiful. It's similar to first playing We Were There and thoroughly enjoying the suspense and mystery behind it all. Really enjoyed the game and if you play it with someone you know you'll absolutely enjoy itPros:Friend Pass - Game is 15 euro which is a bit expensive for being so short but the friend pass easily makes up for that.Mechanics - It changes things up inside missions and between missions enough for both the hacker and the agent that you never get bored.It's fun1Cons:Playing the game as the other character feels a lot easier and not much of a challenge - but to be fair we almost played them back to back.A few weird syncing issues. We were sitting in the same room but had multiple desynchs on our first play through where one of our screens would just freeze and it wouldn't save our progressIt's shorter than you'd like, especially when you've just gotten a feel of things.All around it's a game that deserves to be bought at full price. I'd love to see DLC added to the game and I'd love to see some replayabilty added as well. Chapter 4 could be an endless mode that would be kind of fun. If you're looking for a game to play with someone that you'll both enjoy no matter your skill level then get it, it's a ton of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the few good asymmetrical co-op puzzle games out there. I really recommend it due to multiple reasons. There are different kind of puzzles that quite increase in difficulty throughout the story. There is a nice balance between what the two players have to do. You do not feel that the game is one sided. The graphics are simplistic but very appealing in my opinion. The story feels a bit short, but technically you should play it twice once with each character. The main downside is that the game may crash from time to time, but it is not that problematic. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun to play with your partner.  Some replay value repeating the missions in the other role (coupled with "OH, THAT'S WHY YOU WERE CONFUSED" when you see the other point of view)Would love to see more content and missions, though.  We finished the main story twice in around 7-8 hours with the second play through in the other role that went much faster. We found the visual style beautifully done, with great sound.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Fully finish the game at this point and have unlocked all the Achievements. I wholly loved the game. The story line is rather silly, but it has lots of humor and fun. It is really short, so I'm looking forward to the possibility of further expansions.  The hint mechanic wasn't needed at all, if you're at all used to puzzle solving games. I can see how it would be helpful for younger players, but my friend and I only used the hint mechanic to get the final achievement unlocks. If I could ask for anything in the future, it would be for more levels that are like the 5th mission vault scene.Looking forward to more content at some point.

Updating steam manually seems to have resolved those issues (steam auto update did not work).Aside from a few bugs, like requiring a low screen resolution for lock picking puzzles to be doable, the game is fun to play. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango gave me the opportunity to live out my fantasy of being a hackerman and constantly saying "I'm in" to the annoyance of my co-op buddy. The game provides about 6 hours of gameplay, that includes doing all challenges and story missions as both the hacker and agent. It's not all that challenging, so if you and your friend are looking for a bunch of head scratching puzzles maybe give it a miss. However, I had an overall enjoyable time, moments can get pretty tense and exciting which does get that heart pumping.If I played this before the addition of the Challenge mode I'd be less willing to recommend it, however seeing that the developers appear to be providing more content for the game I'll give it a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It’s fantastic! It’s not the longest game in the world, as you’ll see in most of the negative comments, but we’re talking still hours of co-op Agent/Hacker goodness. I will be playing again with other friends as soon as I can get them to sit still long enough haha

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazingly good, mechanics are nice and engaging and its perfect to play with a friend/SO to escape boredom ot waste some time. The game is indeed really short (around 4 hours depending how fast you manage to deal with the levels) but thats not necessarily a bad thing. Its something really fresh amongst all new releases.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game for co-op playing.Pros:* This is very short, but enough to take a couple of funny evenings.* Every mission is different* A lot of unique puzzles. Repeatable puzzles are repeated only in repeatable situations (like hack the door or IP address) and this happens not so much time.Cons:* Sometimes I want to have more interactions with the environment. I played as an agent and my partner thinked about a clue or asked me to wait for some second. In that time I just run from one point in the level to another. It will be cool if I can order coffee in the coffee machine or change the TV channel or do any other useless interaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A game that takes Clandestine, and turns it into a co-op puzzle game without sacrificing the intensity of a spy game (which is actually impressive since the spy doesn't have a gun).  There is at least a stage that highlights the role of the spy and a stage that highlights the role of a hacker/cracker where they truly shine, and makes you want to play both roles to experience the fun in their respective stages.Voice chat implemented in the game is appreciated as it's an absolute requirement, given how there are also stages where vision is impaired.  I actually dislike those puzzles as it's difficult to relay in real-time on how to progress when danger becomes a variable.  But then there's challenging time-based, yet fair puzzles where failing them offers a chance to continue progress by completing an emergency task, preventing disruption in gameplay and its intensity.It helps to have great sound design too, making everything seem more dramatic.  I highly recommend this game, especially with DLC that increases its replayability, given the overall short campaign.  Just remember that you can't play this game alone, but cross-platform multiplayer helps make this more accessible.  Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is one of the best co-op game ever! My brother and I recently embarked on this cooperative adventure, and we've been utterly hooked from the very start. The adrenaline rush of completing a mission together is simply unparalleled. One of the standout features of Operation Tango is its ingenious asymmetrical gameplay. As partners in crime-solving, my brother and I were forced to rely on each other's expertise and communication skills to progress through a series of challenging missions. The game's puzzles and challenges are wonderfully designed, while you're infiltrating a high-tech facility, hacking into secure systems, or defusing a bomb, you feel the enjoyment and tension at the same time. If you have a friend you should definitely try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best co-op puzzle games I've played. Wish it was longer or they just made a sequel. One of the roles (hacker) can be a tad less interesting because they're behind the scenes most of the time and not interacting with the physical game world, so my suggestion is to switch roles every chapter. On a second playthrough—even though most of the allure is gone since you know pretty much what to do from the start—it's still fun to go over the game again and get to see how the other side perceived things as you were going through it the first time around. The game didn't overstay its welcome at all even while going for 100% achievements, which isn't too hard and helps you maximize the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as engrossing as A Way Out (which I highly recommend) but this is still an engaging and enjoyable coop game and good for those who played that title. A big plus is the friend's pass which allows a friend to download a free copy of the game to play online, but only to join the host who owns the game. The only downside would be the small amount of missions that other reviewers have mentioned but hopefully this opens up more content to be released later, perhaps thru DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little game that is sure to be a blast for those who enjoy playing co-op games that hinge on extensive communication with one's teammatePros:1) Well-designed puzzles that actually immerse you in the experience of being an agent/hacker.2) A charming art-style that is simple yet pleasing, and is quite complimentary to the game's overarching aesthetic.3) The fact that any of your friends can join in by downloading the free 'friend pass' is fantastic.Cons:1) The game is quite short. It allows for a second playthrough (Once as Angel and once as Alistair); but even so, don't expect to get more than 6-ish hours of gameplay. I personally am okay with this, but I can see this being a potential issue for others.

As fun as the core gameplay is, I can't really recommend a game that we can't finish because of serve issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Asymmetrical games is a genre that hasn't been done much. This is an Asymmetrical Coop game and it proves how much potential these kinds of games have when done right.The way this game works is that two people are basically playing entirely different games (in terms of gameplay/interface). One person plays a first-person view and another plays a "hacker" role. Now saying that this games hacking system is unrealistic is a massive understatement. But it also proves that that's not a bad thing. It's actually really fun despite how comical it is. (And also the levels after the first one do provide a bit of a challenge if you arnet the best at explaining things or reacting to information quickly)Theres a free demo to check it out and see if you have anyone on your list who is also willing to play. It has the first level which is easy but still fun.Plus not only can people who bought the game play with demo users (essentially meaning only one person needs to buy the game), but so far it features crossplay! Havent gotten to use it yet since I dont have console friends but from what ive heared the devs are working hard to support this feature and its not just a PR stunt.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, I would love if there was multiple story campaigns.But, I am also very disappointed, this game soft-locked, glitched and straight up crashed very very frequently, at least two-three times per mission. The soft-locking seemed to occur when I was playing as hacker and my co-op bud playing the spy lady would initiate a hack and you had to do those co-operative key unlocking sections. My screen would go black behind the mini game and when we had finished, I couldn't do anything and had to relaunch the game. The other big issue was huge, huge ping spikes, which doesn't make sense at all as I've never had issues with ping in any other games I've played, and certainly has never entered the thousands. I'm glad for the frequent checkpoints but it did still very much break my immersion and frustrate us to the point we had to take a break in the middle of a rather short game that would ordinarily take us one sitting to finish. Still very much liked the game. I just wish these game breaking bugs were fixed, especially when the game is 2-3 years old now and still not very functional.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is a very unique coop experience. Fun new mechanics and riddles. Enjoyed it a lot! Nice graphics aswell! Sadly only around 5-6 Hours of play time for a heafty price tag of 16,99€. But still in my opinion worth the money for a great game, supporting very talented game developers. +++ Great for 100% Achievements (very simple to complete with your friend). +++ 5 Steam Cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game works perfectly on a Steam Deck! Since you need a second player (using the free Friend Pass), it means you need 2 PCs so most people will play with a friend online. For me, playing on the Deck meant that I could install the Friend Pass on my laptop and ask my non-gamer girlfriend to play with me! Gameplay is simple enough that she was able to understand everything by herself on her side of the game (that's kinda important because I absolutely did not want to see her screen). We played by the bonfire on a camping trip and had a lot of fun, the puzzles were reasonably difficult and we both think it was satisfying to beat them. 10/10Disclaimer: I got a copy of this game for review by the developer and it's not changing my opinion about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Not a unique take in the co-op puzzle game genre, but many of the missions do have me and my partner at the edge of our seats, then taking a stale breath of relief after figuring it out. Some missions require a lot of patience, which is key here. While some co-op puzzle games put you on a timer, though this game does have a few, Operation: Tango is more of a take your time and learn the steps to figure things out. Really puts the whole agent-hacker dynamic into use.Very fun. I'd love to see more cases in the game, and if they come out as DLCs I would definitely buy them.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game and struggling through the challenges together with a friend is a blast. I don't really want to spoil anything about the gameplay since it would just devalue your experience. So at this point, just take my word for it that the game is well worth its price. Oh, one last thing only one person needs to buy it, the other one can just download the free friend pass and get a code from the buyer to join them, thanks for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly stellar experience. We may have been too dumb for some parts but the hint system is really a godsend. More Coop games should be THIS intertwined! If you have a friend whom you KNOW cant work well under pressure THIS is the game for you! ;)Graphis and Artstyle: Insanely stylish, super polished and overall a incredibly recognizeable artstyle. Cant wait to see more from this studio!Story: Classical Spy themed adventure. it may be on the shorter side but its DEFINETLY worth the asking price. We just unlocked challenge mode and are looking forward to what that may bring.Gameplay: One word: Varied!I have only played the Agent so far but it was a insanely fun experience to see my friend open doors for me, manipulate the environment and even explore 3D space himself. The way you are forced to communicate is DEFINETLY inspiring!Verdict: 9.9/10 simply because i wished it was longer ;) But thats something you could fix with some DLC?~
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game bills itself as a coop puzzler, but it's more of a "coop minigames" game.  The difficulty in nearly all of the "puzzles" is not figuring out what you need to do or how to do it; rather, the difficulty is in actually executing what you need to do.That said, this is not a bad game at all. The art and sound design were , and the minigames were reasonably fun.  My brother and I had fun playing through it. There's about 3 hours of content, with a bit of replayability if you decide to switch sides and play again.Overall I think this is worth getting on sale, with the caveat that you should  go in expecting a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially for you and one friend to play together. Only one person has to own it, while the other can install the free launcher for the game (found a bit lower on the store page from the purchase option), and I think that's pretty darn cool. This game is highly reminiscent of the "We Were Here" games, though it is a spy theme and felt more exciting to me. I also found the puzzles to be less vexing in this game, and I spent a lot more time communicating with my team mate to solve the puzzles in this game than just silently thinking up the solutions like I did in We Were Here.Another cool thing in this game which I liked much more than in the We Were Here games is that the two playable characters feel so different to play as, with one doing the more "physical" spy work in office buildings and public places, while the other deals with computer apps and providing remote guidance to the partner. I played through the game twice with my friend; with each of us switching roles after completing our first playthrough (and all of the challenge missions). I got every achievement and just had a really good time with the game. It's fairly short, but I had a lot more fun with this game than I did with so many other popular games. I highly recommend this game if you like some puzzles and have at least one good friend you like voice chatting and gaming with.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Don't usually do a lot of reviews for games and especially a co-op for that matter! But here goes!First off! I was introduced about this game from a friend that has been bugging me about it for quite some time. After thinking real hard on it and we didn't have a game to play for the mean time! Sure! Why not! Let me go ahead and purchase Operation Tango! Now! The best feature I'll give this developer that me personally I haven't seen from any other is having your buddy install the "Friend Pass"! Which includes them installing the game on their end without paying out of pocket. Especially if that individual is a bit hesitant for trying it out. No biggie! We all have people that are a bit edgy nowadays for paying a full price game and not expecting what we're hoping for! I'll say this now! It was worth my $20!Second! As much as I adore my friend! Please for the sake of your sanity and theirs. Make sure they don't get highly too upset over the littlest things! Ha, ha, ha! Some areas of the game can be a bit frustrating and take a bit of thinking! At the same time know! The rewards you reap for each mission are very satisfying! Take it from me!Third! Communication is key in this game! Whether you're doing this over Discord (which we did), or VOIP in the game! There's no way you're going to bypass this without having a microphone on standby! You've been forewarned! I won't spoil any particular mission in this section, but I'll say the one we had to do together. It "really" took a lot of initiative from the both us to push through together without falling apart and rage quitting the game! We just kept on b***hing at each other until we finally got through! 😂We prevailed!Can't really say much about the graphics on the game! Since I was playing as the hacker and didn't really get to see what the Agent saw from her POV, but I'll probably give it around an 7.5/10! Granted! There were some areas as the hacker that looked impressive! At this point. I'm probably just too spoiled with the 4k graphics on some games (*cough* Series X *coughs)! Guess what know?! Sometimes the graphics don't make up for a good game! At the end of the day! It's the core of the game play mechanics that make up for what it is and, again, this game did just that!Now for the game play and keeping it brief! For me to play as the Hacker (hopefully I don't have to go in great lengths to explain what the role does) and supporting my fellow Agent! Oh man! I had a blast! Like I stated earlier above! There were definitely some frustrating moments when my friend screwed me over (Sorry Martin)! 😂 To me frankly it felt like a chore to keep him in line, but at the end of the day. Once we figured out how our roles played. Cake walk! Being zapped into the Matrix (Ceez moment btw)! Thanks for the fond memories, brother! Lol! Helping your teammate impersonate a Mission Impossible task etc.! I won't go into great detail, but you generally get the idea!Overall! If you're looking for a good, new co-op to sink your teeth into! Please! By all means! Try it out! You won't be disappointed! I wasn't! ;D
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful Co-op game where you really have to communicate with your partner to not fail!I'd recommend this to anyone who wants to play Agent and Hacker with their Friend or just randomly hook up with other people over their official discord server. The community is really lovely so even if you don't have a friend to play it with, you will find a match.It's great that this has friend's Pass - meaning only one of you needs a copy of the game! The replayability value is nice as well since the view of the characters is completely different.All in all I am hoping and WAITING! for a hopeful DLC with more missions in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't pick this game up for full price as it's only six missions, done in a couple of hours, but picked it up on sale for £10 and then it's worth it. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is short, my friend and I beat it in about 5-6 hours this is not a bad thing as it is a good solid experience. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice short co op experience with decent puzzles that require verbal communication to solve. Its nice when played with someone you know and is enjoyable throughout. That said this game is very short, only 6 missions long. Playing through each mission once in each role and getting the secret achievements took only 6 hours, and within that time my friend and I encountered game breaking glitches that we had to relaunch the game completely to fix.I would recommend getting this game if it goes on sale or is in a bundle (that's how I got it) but not for its full £15.49 price tag as there simply isn't enough content to justify that price.Overall, apart from those aforementioned glitches, the game ran smoothly with a consistent frame rate. The gameplay combined with the stylised graphics and the nice music lets me confidently say that this is a good game but it is sadly lacking in content.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun coop, some tasks are quite intense as you have to multitask. The game keeps you engaged to the end. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this game with my son and absolutely LOVE the game.The game play is great.  Difficulty of puzzles can vary depending on skill level of players involved.Full communication is KEY in this game.  There were times we got triggered with each other as we either didn't hear or ask enough questions of what each of us saw or had access to.Some people are saying game is too short. _childDocuments_.review: Sure it's fun to play coop, but this game is not fun. Stressful and short are the most fitting description. _childDocuments_.review: I mean, what if I don't get along with people, humm? You've got games like "Tale of two brothers" which revolves around Co-Op gameplay, but doesn't necessarily force you to have someone else playing your partner... And then you've got Operation Tango, in which you basically can't even launch the game without having someone on the other end.Operation Tango is an exclusively CO-OP game where you play as either an Agent or a Hacker, playing as one or the other entails going for specific objectives, like activating turrets with the hacker, or building a bridge and the agent is actually in place, doing the looting and the smashing (not the one you're thinking about). That's about it... Also, worth mentioning that the game is super short, so chances are if you don't have friends you'll do it by having another laptop.The only good thing about the game is that your partner doesn't have to own the game, they can log into your session by downloading the free demo of the game... That's pretty wholesome, so I was playing agent and hacker at the same time by switching frequently to my laptop and I hated every single second of it. That's why I'll rate "Operation Tango" a solid , I didn't have to buy it for my other account, but playing in two PCs was lame as hell. The game is like "Well, it sucks that you don't get along with other people and we don't care!", F YOU TOO, DEVS lol!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Its kind of like a cross between it takes two, and the we were here series.It's got a little bit of the technical and movement skills from it takes two, and its got a little bit of the puzzle aspects from we were here, mixed into a spy thriller in a technologically advanced society.It's a well polished, well rounded game where the devs set out to make an enjoyable game and have achieved in doing that.Other then that, it's not anything ground breaking.Oh, and you can break peoples ankles with a S P E E D Y cleaning bot, which is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I was SOOOOO hyped for this but ended up disappointed. Here's why:- 6 missions can be played in 3-4 hours, you can replay them as the other character for maybe 2-3 more hours- the challenge mode is horrible and absolutley no fun, even with doing the level quickly and with no mistakes we missed the gold mark by 15 seconds and just didn't care enough after that to grind even longer for a better score.- one of the characters is a lot less fun to play (hacker)- navigating as hacker is a pain in the a** especially when you have to be quick about it- even though this game is all about communication, it lacks instructions (we often struggled with what we were meant to do even though we talked about what we were seeing etc), puts you under a lot of stress because many things happen at the same time/ you have to be quick/ have no idea what to do or where to get what you need). many "puzzles" are so unintuitive that they are just no fun to fingure out. even after completing some of them we didn't understand how we were supposed to know what to do.- this game was worse for my relationship than risk/ monopoly/ yugi-oh and mario kart combined, we ended up b*tching at each other because we were both so frustrated with the levels- some maps are designed quite well, other not so much. the train level is lovely, the deep dive almost made us quit completelyThe only good thing that i am taking from this game is that the "keep talking and nobody explodes" parts were fun and i will look into playing that game instead.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I just played through this over the course of 4ish hours; a great little communication/teamwork game where you and a friend take on the roles of an Agent and Hacker respectively and solve puzzles, navigate networks and do espionage-flavoured things against a colourful comic book-esque art style backed by well fitting music. If you enjoyed We Were Here, this scratches a similar itch albeit coming from a more asymmetrical angleThe campaign consists of six Missions following your relatively typical spy-movie plot, typically tasking the Agent with on-site duties like slinking through security systems and sneaking into office computers to provide IPs, passwords and network details to the Hacker who then opens doors, manipulates elevators, and generally Trons about the place. Players can change characters between missions but we played through the whole thing in our roles and will probably go again to try out the other side in a year or two.Overall a punchy, stylish experience that doesn't overstay its welcome nor feel too thin for the $10 we paid - and, thanks to the friend pass, you only need one copy! I would wholly recommend this to any gaming couples looking for some silly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great, but be careful how you choose your roles. If you don t like the game the first time, try again as the other role. Been there, done that. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango
