_childDocuments_.review: Fun first-person co-op action puzzler.  The co-op elements are well done, with lots of communication and close timing required between the players.  There's even a SpaceTeam style game at one point that was funny.  It's a bit expensive for a game that only lasts 4 hours, but there are not a lot of good co-op games out there.  It Takes Two and the We Were Here series are my favorites, but is a solid entry in the category and worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to other co-op games that I have played, such as We Were Here or Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes, I really liked the fact that the puzzles were not one sided. There are two roles to play, agent and hacker. But unlike those other co-op games, both sides get to describe a puzzle to the other person, which makes the game feel a lot more "co-op" than other games. Not to mention the fact that you can replay levels with your roles swapped to get a different experience, which gives this short game some replayability. The game isn't super long, but for the price of admission, I thought that it was just long enough to not overstay it's welcome. The puzzles do end up getting slightly repetitive, but they do also keep getting more challenging so I didn't think that was a problem. If you have been looking for a co-op game to play with a friend, I would definitely recommend giving this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but with some problems. We had to stop playing on multiple occasions during our play session due to bugs soft-locking us (this happened about 4 times in our 5 hour playthrough). Also, I felt like the game was only just starting to pick up, as if we had only just been cut loose after tutorial just to have the game end.Saying that though this game was a lot of fun. Both sides are completely different so it is replayable and interesting to see from each side. Big positive that this game comes with a friends pass! Only one of us had to buy it and the other downloads the free friends pass. All in all I'd definitely recommend the game. Bugs are irritating but we just restart the mission and it didn't ruin the experience entirely.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah, this game is really fun! I played it with my friend, and we had a lot of good laughs. However, panic attacks and anger issues may arise pretty soon. Communication with your friend is key. You can play as both an agent and a hacker. Each side offers a different perspective on the game. With six missions in total, you can switch roles with your partner, allowing you to experience the same mission from a different angle. Additionally, after completing the story, you can tackle challenges, which are really enjoyable. As always, I completed 100% of the achievements. See you in the next game, fellas!"
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Like Don't Talk and Nobody Explodes but actually fun. Like DTNE, Tango can bring out issues in your relationship when you can't communicate properly, but when you know exactly how each other thinks it works like a well-oiled machine. The feeling you get when you synchronize with each other isn't something a lot of other co-op games offer, and you really depend on your partner as much as they depend on you; which can be incredibly frustrating or rewarding. A lot of fun for a co-op adventure and I think it's great for couples and good friends who want to test the strength of their relationship
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun, if you enjoyed games like We Were Here, would highly recommend. It's more technology based than WWH which makes it more unique. It's made by a small company but you would never know from how much love was put into the game. They plan on adding more missions if the game is received well, so absolutely buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent 2 player co-op game. You and your partner take on 2 asymmetric roles: Hacker and Field Agent. Hacker is mostly dealing with an informational interface and helping the Field Agent navigate obstacles. The Field Agent role primarily involves a first person view and moving around in the 3D world.Each task involves communicating information not available to the other in order to complete the puzzle. With several tasks requiring coordinated and timely actions, which are typically the most difficult. Tasks range from Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes type bomb defusal, to solving a maze or cross-referencing criminal information across different databases.Pros:- heavily communication based, no progression without teamwork, exactly how a co-op should be.- failure will reset the team back to the last checkpoint (no more than 1 minute of lost time)- on point old-school spy aesthetic- lovely visuals- 100% replayable as the other agentCons:- a little short (completed one role in ~5 hours)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a great co-op experience. Everything is set up for two players to play together. You can't even start the game alone, but thanks to the Friend Pass, it's enough if one of the two players buys the game.In effect, one player plays an agent and the other a hacker. Together you must stop the propagation of a dangerous virus (Covid 19?). You need to communicate successfully so that everyone can solve their tasks with the help of their partner. The tasks are very fun, exciting and sometimes even challenging. Especially in the missions where you are under time pressure, your brain is working at full speed. Nevertheless, all the tasks are, in my opinion, quite easy. My friend and I got through the game relatively quickly and played through the entire campaign (6 missions) in only 3 hours. Now we have switched roles so that everyone experiences the other perspective (after all the gameplay is completely different).The story itself is quite boring and stereotypical. There is also no real character development. But that's not half bad. I didn't buy this game to hear a good story, but because the co-op gameplay interested me a lot.The art style is also very appealing, the graphics are great, and the Secret Agent ambience is great. The soundtrack is also good.A great co-op experience that partly reminded me of "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes".
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a Coop Game similar to the We Were Here Series for example, i can definitely recommend this one.But it is a bit expensive for my taste. We are looking a a total of 8 to 10 hours estimated to complete it 100%, which means playing the campaign as both classes and completing challenge mode. My first playthrough of the campaign took about three hours.If its on sale, definitely get it! If not, Maybe wait for the next discount!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice asymetrical Co-Op game. Communication in the game is key. You and your partner will fail at first. But you will get better as you figure out how to give information to each other quickly. The art style is rather enjoyable as well.In a few missions there are some puzzles, which are just strange or maybe unfair given the tight timing needed. At a few other points there were some issues with the color scheme. I had issues differentiating certain colors from each other or from the background. Thus making the puzzles harder. A larger cursor might have helped as well. There were a few issues with network latency the last time I played it. So you need a stable connection.I still recommend this game. Especially if you enjoyed games like "We were here" or "Keep talking and nobody explodes".Score: 7/9
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful two player co-op experience. Strong "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes" influences with plenty of unique interactions that take full advantage of the Hacker/Spy duo themes.The vast majority of the difficulty comes from the communication challenges rather than traditional videogame inputs and timing. Generous and frequent checkpoints really help to keep the difficulty low. Play with someone to put your collective communication (and patience) to the test!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast! Asymmetric information, escape-the-room style puzzles, a great theme and awesome visuals. My wife and I played it over the course of a few nights, and every mission was an awesome time. The friend pass support makes this game a steal.Highly recommended co-op game. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the prettiest asymmetric co-op puzzlers I've played, and the gameplay offers a solid couple of hours of good fun. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good. A bit short, but a decent experience for the money. However across the 3 hours it took me to complete the game, we ran into bugs about 5 times. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A really great co-op game to play with a friend. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Game is short (about 4 hours for the main playthrough). However, it is quite fun with good puzzles. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: My review system works with a 10 point score. 0 = bad and 10 = good.I have 5 criteria on which I decide. Each can give 0 - 2 points.Below that I will explain my decisions.Operation Tango is the type of game this world needs far more of!Honestly, I haven't had this much fun playing a coop game with friends in a long while.Every level of the game has its unique and tricky puzzles which are perfectly in balance between not too easy to be boring but also not too hard to be frustrating. Also, the game actually makes you feel like the two people playing really depend on one another.The whole game has a toon-ish style which is perfectly matched with the graphics and sound design. Both give you a feeling like "The Incredibles" film. And the best thing is you can experience each level twice. Unlike other coop games, choosing one of the two characters really makes it a completely different experience.Story wise, the game is nothing special. But what the devs  did, they did good. It's funny, straight to the point, and it was all I needed.In my opinion, Operation Tango is a must-play for every coop lover, and I would gladly pay for more content. So grab a good friend, buy this game and enjoy a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a co-op puzzle heist game that has you working with a friend to save the world from cyber terrorism. Playing through this game was a ton of fun. Each level is different and brings unique challenges to work through. Succeeding relies a lot on communication, and doing so effectively is surprisingly not easy. I feel like it was more than a game to play with a friend; it strengthened my relationship with the people close to me, and it's rare a game can do that. Since only one copy of the game is needed to play online co-op, this is an easy pick for gaming with anyone. Both roles are enjoyable in their own way, and neither felt better than the other. Overall, I loved this game and the memories I made while struggling through it, and I would easily recommend it to anyone looking for a good co-op challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: really great use of asymmetrical co-op system, pretty well-polished, with a nice variety of mechanics/puzzle types to test communication. developers should be proud of this.HOWEVER, i nearly gave it a negative review because it's very short and can be completed in under 3 hours. also, given that this is the case, it might have been better to make the finale harder to make it more intense, as some other parts of the game definitely nailed the frantic intensity aspect better (there's one part where you and your partner have to juggle a few different things while using both your hands which felt very good)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The first four missions were fun - unfortunately in the fifth mission my friend encountered a black screen bug so we had to restart and continue. This apparently desynced the random number generators in the mission such that the password I found and the password he was supposed to put into the system was no longer the same, so we could either restart from the very beginning or just try the other 9999 different possible combinations. Fortunately we could skip to the final mission, but in that mission I got the black screen every time we messed up, and had to restart from the beginning every time. Eventually, we just gave up because it just wasn't very fun anymore.It's disappointing when these kinds of gamebreaking bugs stay in the game despite the game being out for 2 years - I probably wouldn't have bought the game knowing that after slightly more than 2 hours of fun the game would just stop working properly. It's a short game, but it's even shorter when you only get to play the first 4 missions, especially when the first mission is basically just a tutorial. A shame, but can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Both the hacker and the agent both feels like they're part of the game, so even if you're the hacker and thus a more supportive role, you STILL feel like you're actually part of what's going on, being able to manipulate stuff for the agent to progress.The stages are fairly short (if you know what you're doing, anyway - going through them blind, you'll probably look at about 40-60 minutes/stage due to the puzzles - time might vary, depending on how good you and your partner are at puzzles).You can and will fail puzzles multiple times. Thankfully, there are PLENTY of checkpoints, allowing you to easily continue the game from where you left off if you die.Cons:A bit short, with only 6 stages. I really hope they'll add more in the future as it's a really fun game.Some of the puzzles are more tedious than actually hard. Disclaimer: the following two things are bugs that I hope gets fixed. The first a minor annoyance at best, but still bad. The latter one is pretty annoying.For some reason, on stages 2-5 if you're playing as the Hacker, you can't see the end credits - the game just turns slightly dark and while you'll still hear the end credit sequence play out, you won't actually get to see it. Nothing game breaking, thankfully.The second bug is on stage 2. Slight spoilers ahead.As the agent, you have to avoid two drones but for some reason, the game will sometimes make you respawn inside one of the rooms where you're trying to hide from the drones, only to end up being instantly caught by the drone again, forcing yet ANOTHER reset. Other times, the drones will be somewhere else on the path, allowing you more free reign.Overall, I find the game very fun and I hope that they'll add more stages in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best co-op games you can get. The gameplay is amazing and requires timing, coordination, and using your brain. While there isn't too much content in the main campaign, challenge mode also gives you some extra content for you and your friend to do. Another thing that I haven't see developers do before is allow friends to get the game for free and only one person has to actually buy the game. It makes playing co-op games a lot easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I spoke with my partner at length after completing the game in 2 sittings, and below will be the points we discussed. But for those looking for a short answer: Yes it's good fun, and we need more games like this.For the record, I played as the Hacker.It does need to be said; the game is short. Very short. Every level honestly felt like we just got the tutorial sample of what was possible, but it was over before we knew it. That doesn't mean the experience wasn't fun or worthwhile, but that we needed MORE with the tools we've now learnt to use. We were hoping to use all our new experience in less linear-based level design moving forward. Sadly, it was already the end.Don't stress too much about which character to play, as you'll both experience elements of each others default style in some form or another. The game revolves mostly around information gathering and sharing it clearly between each other to progress. This is mostly happening both ways throughout the game.We were a little confused at the decision for the theme of the story. We're supposed to be badass top agents, but the immersion wasn't really there as we're chaotically thrown into our levels with no real clue what's happening. In this casual and chaotic style of gameplay, it would've made more sense that we were like the worst agents on record, but everyone else was unavailable for some reason, and it was up to us screw ups to save the world. If you wanted a more badass tone, I personally would've preferred a proper planning phase before a mission starts, to get an understanding of what we'll be doing and to some degree, and how. The unexpected twists can still happen of course, but the cutscenes just lacked any real conveyance of how we're actually going to accomplish our task.This style of game is quite rare, and definitely worth the experience, but the point I want to make here is that this game just barely scratches the surface of whats possible for this genre. This game has great example of all the tools and creative ideas for puzzles and missions, but you'll rarely ever use a single mechanic twice. Which I mean, hats off to them for being unique and creative for every level. But imagining now using each of these mechanics, solving mysteries, and completing difficult objectives under more 'free-roam' environments...Let's just say this game represents the tip of the iceberg for what's possible in the future. I wish the developers all the best and would even go so far as to beg them for a sequel that's extensively deeper. Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: After far too many B Grade crime investigation shows I had always dreamed to be a hacker.Much like the shows, there were many times I just mashed the keyboard and hoped for the best.I now feel I am fully equipped to hack turrets, robots or entire buildings should the situation ever arise. My Agent was by all accounts a cut above the rest...and by this I also mean half cut most of the time.This may have increased performance but it also increased the sass.I was the eyes and the ears of the operation, this required a lot of navigation, timing and remembering components, so naturally that went about as well as a knife in a toaster. I feel getting your partner killed on occasion only adds to the beauty of the game. The game it's self was a little short, but I think you should only push a friendship so far... so perhaps its for the best.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Possibly one of the best puzzle-solving co-op experiences you can have in the modern era, assuming you and your second agent are capable of sentient thought (you'd be surprised). There's about three hours of content per agent, meaning the worst critique I could level to this game is that there isn't more of it to digest.Visual presentation and art style are top notch, with a lot of clarity in User Interface elements. The visually distinct stages for the Agent and the well-polished interfaces for the Hacker have this cartoon-ish postmodern vibe that are all kept different over the course of play. My personal level, the Moving Train, is awesome to experience from either Hacker or Agent side, full of good twists and panic moments throughout the level's 20 minute long run time. The game has a lot of flair and passions put into it, from the polished light to the just-right sound effects really letting you experience the perspectives of the agents. A review should never say "It really makes you feel like X" (unless ironically) but this is one of the moments where I felt extreme gratification after finishing a level, like finally putting the pieces together in the detective sequence, or finally completing the ending of mission six with mere seconds between victory and obliteration.Not many puzzles or content are re-used, aside from the lock picking experiences which are kept consistent and expanded upon constantly. After playing both sides for myself, the difference in game play between the two agents is shocking; it makes other games of this principle look like they're slacking off by comparison. In Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, the other players besides the one tinkering with the bomb just get to read a manual for several minutes. In Operation Tango, that "Manual" Is a highly interactive second game that the Hacker is peeling through to get you openings or advantages. I'm baffled in hindsight that this isn't a more common idea.Since I got into this game on patch 1.01, I experienced an extremely minimal level of glitches. I played Cyberpunk 2077 on release and liked it; nothing this game can hit you with is even NEAR that. If you cannot stomach the idea of spending thirty Australian dollars on this short-but-ever-so-sweet experience, then you might want to wait until they either add more content or until the game goes on sale. I can say, personally that I'd rate this above games like Trine or even Portal 2's coop.

One player is the Field Agent, infiltrating a location and sneaking through laser grids. The other plays the Hacker who breaks through mainframes to unlock doors, hijack turrets and more to help the Field Agent complete their task. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: While short, if you're thirsting for asymmetric co-op, it delivers. The price seems a little much for around 3 hours of content, but I think it's actually quite reasonable when you realize that your friend can play with you for free - it really only costs half as much, if you think about it like that.The game itself is somewhat of a mix of concepts in other co-op games - A mix of We Were Here and Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes.  Something I appreciated was that there was no penalty for failing other than moving back to the last checkpoint. While it's nice to be challenged, I'd rather not have spats with friends because of bad feelings over not understanding each other.I'm absolutely desperate for more content, honestly, and dearly hope there's DLC or other content down the line. There's a small storyline in this game that holds up on its own, but the game is really begging for additional 'episodes.'Being a co-op game that releases the same year as It Takes Two must be rough, but this one definitely carves out a niche for itself with gameplay I really would like to see more of, either within Operation Tango itself or just in the game genre in general.Final thoughts: Slightly pricy for the length of the game, but zero regrets on my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is a phenomenal asymmetric co-op puzzle game. The premise (a spy and a hacker work together to stop Bad Mystery Man from blowing up the internet or something) is just enough to carry the game forward. It isn't original, there's no big "twist," and the puzzles make no sense in context. Which is good, because if Operation: Tango tried to be dramatic or realistic, it would be a mess. Instead it's just the best co-op game I've ever tried.I've played a few other asymmetric co-op puzzle games but this? This is something else. Your teammate has a completely different screen, with a completely different UI, and completely different controls. It isn't just about solving clever puzzles, it's also about finding a way to communicate to your ally what you need from them, without being able to explain where or how to find it. The game frequently takes full advantage of this...disadvantage, by making the spy avoid detection, hide from someone hunting them, and finish a long series of tasks before time runs out.You may have seen a complaint from other reviews that the game is too short. With only six missions and 3-5 hours of gameplay (if you only play it as one side), it can be played in an evening or two without much trouble. But here's the thing. Every mission in Tango is unique and memorable (especially the train mission, that one was incredible). It's a bit like Titanfall 2: I'll take a shorter campaign that was worth every minute than a long campaign of white-walled test chambers that I barely remember any of.Except O:T goes one VERY big step further and makes the game free for Player 2. ANY Player 2. You spend $20 (and $20 is a reasonable price, in my opinion), and you can play the game with anyone else, without them spending anything. It is an incredibly generous move by the developers.I very highly recommend Operation: Tango. It's great. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I just 100 percented the game and it's really cool, among the best 2-player-asymmetric-coop I've played. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun! There are a couple of missions, and recently they have added a few special challenges, which are like small missions in a training facility.The game is not too difficult, it is rather accessible, and it's not really an action game. It is more of akin to the We were here games.A really cool feature is that, while the two players do need to have the game installed on their PC, one of the players can just install the Friend Pass version (free) if the other player owns the game.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Its a great cooperative puzzle solver. Very good if you want something casual to play with a friend. Its not without it's issues, First of all its very short, At the time of this review I've beaten this game 3 times, twice as the field agent and once as the hacker, and gotten gold on all the challenge maps, all within 10 hours of play time. So its a bit hard to recommend at the $20 price point. Aside from that, we also experienced a few network issues, and a game bug where the game was saying an access code was being reported as incorrect. It was fixed after we restarted the game but it had us confused for a little while. But other than that the game is great, it has beautiful minimalist graphics, fantastic lighting and level design  and a wide variety of puzzles that are fun to work through as a team. The puzzles tend to be pretty easy but progress is satisfying.Finally I have a few thoughts I'd like to tack on to the end of this review:Although its super short the two sides of the game play completely differently, so you have to play it through at least twice before you get the full experience. Second, if you have friends who want to play with you, they dont have to buy a copy. They can play free as long as a game owner gives them a lobby key, so in a way you're kind of buying a game for a friend as well.And finally, this game was made by an indie dev, I like to support this type of work, so I think that modifies my opinion of the price a bit. From a pure gameplay to dollar value comparison, $20 might be a bit much, but if youre looking for a coop game, its definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game if you are looking for a puzzle co-op. Each players screens are different (Hacker and Spy) so trying to describe things to each other is the right amount of frustrating and fun. My friend and I had a hard time putting this game down. You get double game play if you wanna switch characters and for $13 and a free friend pass it's hard not to recommend. Just zelle a buddy 6 dollas and you get to be James Bond, hell yeahThe only issue we had was at one mission there you need to unlock a key by doing this dot box mini game. One player can move the dot up and down, the other player can move it left and right. Basically get the dot in the goal and don't hit the lines or you start over. It ranged from easy to moderate. The very last one was a pain in the ass to beat, it was stupid hard and you would have to be a 'total masochist' to want to keep pushing through it. Which apparently I am lmaooo but my friend is not.We even met in person and I controlled both sides on two laptops and it was still hard to beat. But I think there should be an option that lets you bypass certain challenges or just specifically take that one mini game level out. Other than that, I love the concept. I love the challenges and say it's a pretty decent game if you are into puzzles/co-op/spy themes/escape rooms/ or just pissing off your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome communication based co-op game. You can also play with random people online although I'm not sure how fun that would be, as communication is key. The main play through is super short (about 3 hours), so I wouldn't pay anymore than £10 for this game. There are extra challenges at the end, but I didn't really enjoy these as they're the same puzzles found in the main game, except you're timed. Achievements are a bit of a grind as you have to play through the game/challenges on both roles to get 100%. Overall, a really fun puzzle game to play with a friend - recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Coop game for two players in which one of you is a secret agent in the field and the other one a hacker supporting her from behind the scenes. It's reminiscent of games like the bomb defusing simulator "Keep talking and nobody explodes" in how it requires both of you to check the information and tools available to you to solve the tasks at hand together: So there is a corridor full of invisible lasers that the agent can't see, but the hacker with his camera access can? Sounds like he should tell her where to step to make it through safely. Other tasks include picking door locks, finding out the identity of a person of interest and hacking into highly secure servers. All in all, some tasks repeat, but you also constantly get new ones that differ from mission to mission, keeping the gameplay fresh and surprising.The game's difficulty is just right. It can be quite tricky in spots (especially those were you have to control the same moving dot together), but in the end, everything was doable.What I appreciated was that when we had a disconnect, the game allowed us to continue in the middle of the mission where we had left off. Another big plus: Only one of you needs to buy the game. The second player can use the free demo version as his "friend pass".

_childDocuments_.review: This game kinda builds on the ideas of games like the “We Were Here” series. Take those sort of core concepts - intimate 2 player coop, puzzles that require information split between the two players - and put them in a futuristic setting with hackers and agents and you have kinda the base idea of what the game is. For “We Were Here” fans I think that’s probably already enough to sell you. The fact that it has a friend pass system is a nice plus. For people who tried the “We Were Here” games and didn’t like them, although I think this game sort of improves the formula, I’m not sure that it’s different enough that this will click for you when “We Were Here” didn’t. If you don’t know about “We Were Here” and just want a cool coop game that you and a friend can play, I think this is definitely worth a shot. And like I pointed out before, your friend doesn’t have to buy the game, if they download the friend pass they can join your game for free.

_childDocuments_.review: Teamwork is the key! From now on it's one of my favourite co-op games I ever played, anyone who loves Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, We Were Here series and other cooperative games would love it too. The gameplay is simple, but still interesting since almost all players' actions are tied to the partner ones, which gives you a 'pure co-op' experience. The graphics are very colourful and quite pretty, but I think optimization could be a little bit better with this style.The only drawback is that the Operation: Tango is very short, but I hope devs will release more cases to solve soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Played this through in one sitting with my partner through one of the roles, took about 3.5 hours to get through all six missions. We had fun, its just short enough for one sitting, but feels like there should be more than just the one "case." I'm not counting the challenge modes, as that isn't really our thing. I would say, as our first asymmetrical co-op game that this was a good start, Its forgiving enough when you mess up, but with enough difficulty to not feel like a complete cakewalk. Just because I was the "Hacker" role the whole time didn't mean I just clicked buttons, and just because my partner was the "Agent" role didn't mean all they did was run around and go where I told them to. There were a few points where we had to stop and talk it through since we think very differently (planning, directions, etc.) but the game allows for this with time and safe spots in almost every place. I only had one crash, and when we reconnected it brought right back to the end part of the level, so we didn't have to do the whole thing over again (thankfully). A lot of the puzzles have multiple iterations, so multiple playthroughs are viable (even though the story overall will be the same.)My biggest gripe is the time vs. price ratio, and what offsets it. My general rule is 50 cents/hour (I'm cheap, sorry) but since only one person needs a copy, I'd raise it to $1/hour. If you run through both sides like we plan to do, it'll probably equal out at 6-7 hours total, which at $20 is a fair ways short. I'm still recommending it, as on sale at around $10 I'd say its worth it to have a couple playthroughs with different folks and see how each of you thinks, and try again in a few months with roles swapped. I would absolutely look forward to any DLC for this, but as of writing this review its been two years, so I wouldn't hold out hope.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An online co-op spy game. Operation: Tango is similar to the We Were Here series.  Two players try to complete spy missions in enemy territory.  One player will be a field operative, and the other plays a hacker, though both characters will have a variety of tasks that they will need to collaborate on to work their way through each mission.   The game requires online play but only needs one copy of the game and the expectation is the only communication between the players is verbal, with no way to see each other’s screens. Operation: Tango should be played by friends, random players won’t be as good for this.  But a bigger problem is that Operation: Tango is a single experience.  Once players get through the entire game, the same experience won’t be as special.  I forgot to record footage, and this is the second playthrough of the same level.  Even swapping characters didn’t change the experience.  There are only 6 missions and while there are ten additional challenges in a new free DLC, this isn’t the longest experience.   Pick this up if you have someone to play with, if you get the game, this is enjoyable, and with the right partner, it’s something else.  The reason I forgot to record the footage was that I was having an amazing time playing the game, but we also got through two out of the six original missions already, so, as I said, it’s not going to be that long. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I felt the need to return to this review after completing the entirety of Operation Tango, but most of my opinion will stand - this game is not worth full price. On initial appearance and reviews I was very excited to play this with a close girl friend of mine. We both bought it without telling the other, but we didn't ask for a refund because we wanted to support the creators. It was also for a sale price, probably about $10 or so. This is a somewhat fair price, but I'd even go so far unfortunately to say The reason that premise is so unfortunately short is the story is laughable. Me and my friend tried really hard to understand the plot and story but it's pretty boring overall. On our first playthrough I was the Hacker and she played the Agent. We had a bit of fun and seriousness- that lasted at best an hour. The Hackers perspective can go from boring to aggravating, and the Agents is uninteresting and lackluster. We agreed that on both playthroughs the Agent had it worse since when you think of Agent you think of more action sequences or such. There were a few moments of stealth and absolutely 0 combat sequences, which was a slight let down to the already incredibly short game. The puzzles range from hand holding through an empty mall to drilling a golfball sized hole through your cranium. It took a third friend to help figure out some of them and they weren't there until the second playthrough meaning the first run around we just managed to squeak by. This game one full game completion is about three hours. There are 6 story missions to complete before you beat the game, and then unlock challenges for aftergame content. Most of the challenges were laughably easy, taking 2-4 tries to gold tier. They aren't meant to take long either so we spent perhaps a 1/2 hour to an hour on that. We both agreed the last mission is our least favorite, simply because it's the most nothing out of them all; says a lot considering it's the LAST mission. In this mission  After that we had 100% completed the game and uninstalled it immediately. My opinion has not changed- do not buy this game more than once, allow a friend with the friend pass. Don't get this game for more than $10 because it's laughably short and lacking. My cardinal rule is whatever price you buy the game for you should get double the time out of it. I barely have 9 hours and I 100% completed it, more upset then triumphant. I respect the company that made this, but I and my friend were left upset and disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be one of my first reviews but I feel I have to mention the excellence of this game. A brilliant asymmetrical co-op experience that insentivises clear communication in order to be the eyes for your other agent and deal with obstacles in your way.A unique introduction into the co-op genre that has many positives going for it. Such as affordable (£15) and with only one of the two needing to purchase my brother and I split the difference to play this game together.  It has great style. Unique puzzles and challenges that are evolving as you progress through the game. Every level offers different challenges and obstacles for Angel (Field Operative) and Alistair (Hacker) to navigate which means running through each mission is a blast.However, the game is not without its flaws. Namely that it is rather short, my brother and I managed to beat it in under 4 hours when I just played Angel and he played Alistair so if you are looking for an epic then this game will not be for you. Additionally, though there is story it is nothing special but simply serves a purpose for you to navigate to the next level. Finally, there is little character development between Angel and Alistair. It would have been lovely to hear the two communicate in some way in cutscenes or during downtime within the game, but I do understand the company is small and good VA is not cheap, therefore, I will not be too harsh with this criticism.Overall, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking to play a styalistic and unique take on co-op that challenges your communication in fun and interesting ways. I do hope they release more content for this world, either with DLC, a sequel or a different game focussing on Angel or Alistair respectively. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Buy it, it's an exceptional co-op puzzle game. You don't even need two copies because of the friend pass, so actual price is 10 bucks if you split with a friend. Albeit a bit short, you'll have a lot of fun.Honestly, one of the best co-op puzzle games out there. It seems that half of its puzzles are the We Were Here type (i.e. lower intensity but slightly more complex) and the other half are Keep Talking and Nobody Explode's style (i.e. frantic, usually relying on some sort of "is X this?" and symbol matching puzzles). Of course, the range of puzzles is much more vast than I'm describing, but this is just a simplification to give you a taste of what to expect. None of them very hard, of course. All the puzzles are well paced, so you won't get bored with only doing one type.As for the game itself, it's clear that a lot of love and soul was poured into it. The artstyle and character design is unique, the settings are gorgeous (even the hacker ones!), and a lot of thought was put into what each character's role is. Simply put, you won't just be solving puzzles as a hacker and providing the clues as an agent. The two roles are often reversed during gameplay, with both the agent and the hacker serving as guides to the other.Honestly, its only fault is that it's too short! I need more! As it stands, it takes about 3 hours to complete the campaign with one character, and apparently 5.4 to completely finish the game. However, devs say DLC is (maybe) in the works. I honestly can't wait for more missions!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously brilliant.  It's short, yes.  But it's brilliant.  No word of a lie, I loved it so much I held off on reviewing so I could make it my review #200. I wanted this to be significant.This is a game about being spies.  One of you is an infiltrator, sneaking around in buildings and being subtle AF.  The other is a hacker, in the very spirit of being a netrunner in Cyberpunk 2020 or a William Gibson novel.On the surface, it looks like it follows the template laid out by an older game, Clandestine:  the spy, the hacker, the teamwork.  Except it's very extremely not that game.  That's like saying smoked salmon and buffing compound are the same thing because they look kinda dark red.  They're radically different.In Operation Tango, the game is really more about communications and problem solving.  In the midst of hacking a network, or infiltrating an office tower, or whathaveyou, somebody is going to get stymied by a lock, or a missing password, or something similar.  The other may have access to that very thing, but needs to go find it, and/or communicate to the partner how to find it.  Sometimes you can see what they're up to, but indirectly--a drone camera, some digital readout, etc.  From that frame of reference, you'll have to direct your partner.So this is very much a game about communication.  A partner is mandatory.  A partner you can communicate well with is mandatory.  Even still, failures will happen, but the game is extremely generous with its savepoints, very polite with failure messages, and extremely forgiving.  If communications aren't happening, luck and patience might see you through.But again, this isn't hard.  There's a bit of sneaking, "cyberspace" "hacking", bomb defusing, and so forth.  It totally nails the feel of being a movie spy, or a scifi hacker.  It's a game that brings you the *experience*.Now, it's a short game.  I played through the whole campaign as the hacker in four hours.  I might go back and play the campaign as the infiltrator.  Let's say another four hours.  But the thing is this:  My partner didn't buy a copy.  Only I did.  One person plays for free.  Effectively divide that price point in two, because both of you are paying for the price you see.  And that's a heck of a steal.This game is brilliant.  I have only one regret:  It's that I waited this long to play it.  I bought it pretty much on the day of release, and I sat on it for awhile, because that's what I do.This will be great fun to go through with my wife, as we've rigged up a picture-in-picture way of showing what she's doing on my own stream.  We'll surely give this a spin soon, again.  And if you made it here, you're my kind of person and I hope you pop in and say hello.  .Oh yeah.  And totally buy this game and get your buddy to grab the free coop partner download.

_childDocuments_.review: Take space team, combine it with keep talking and nobody explodes, then make it a two player game and you get Operation: Tango.The good: There seems to be a decent amount of "polish" to the game in terms of looks and sounds. The co-op gameplay is asymmetrical. Only one person needs the game (the other can use friends pass), which is a great system that works really well. Setting up a game over the internet is relatively painless.  The bad: The game's puzzles aren't particularly engaging. Basically they consist of one person explaining what needs to be done to another. This could be trying to describe some abstract symbol, passing on a string of numbers, giving instructions that the other person is missing, or working on interactive 2D puzzles together.The ugly: It's short, only 6 missions long. If you play both roles that extends the game time slightly.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Definitely play this if you like playing co-op with a friend.Operation Tango does a great job of capturing the feel of the spy movie tropes we've become accustomed to. The hacker manipulating the environment to help the agent reach an objective and ultimately escape the mission area.Some of the puzzles can get sufficiently tense, but you're never punished for failing a puzzle.  This might be the only shortcoming I can identify for the game.  Maybe allowing the players to select a difficulty which might give failing some more weight on higher difficulties.That being said, it doesn't detract from the joy of working together with a friend in a remote location that sees something completely different to yourself.I'd recommend this game over and over to anybody who has a friend who's up for starring in your own spy movie.In terms of playtime, we finished the game at around 3 hours and spent another 3 with reversed rolls.  Even though on the second playthrough you now know what the other player is seeing, it's still fun to see the whole picture after experiencing both parts.People expecting more replayability out of this game other than switching rolls once, have a skewed view of what this genre, and by extension, this game should be.It's meant to be played once from each viewpoint and having fun while doing so.As mentioned, definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, its one of the best coop experiences I've played, an easy recommendation at full price even. That does, in part, from having free friend pass. Gameplay-wise this is an asymmetrical cooperative puzzle game that revolves around good communication and teamwork.  As one player explores the world as an agent, they are supported by the other players hacking skills.  Each player has half of the clues and half of the puzzles and you need to solve it, and only by sharing information can you make progress.It takes best the best parts of "Keep Talking and No one Explodes" and expands this into a far deeper and more rewarding experience.  There is a good combination of low stress puzzles and high stress timed panic modes. With each stage taking a new approach to things and introducing new puzzle elements... it never got old.It's a relatively short game, but I'd also say it didn't outstay its welcome. It had a good buildup, a good pace, and I felt the ending was absolutely satisfying. If, unlike me, you need more... they now have a series of challenge puzzles to master.   Considering one purchase is all you need to play through with a friend... it's more than worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best asymmetrical co-op game I've played, Operation Tango is a true masterpiece to enjoy with family, friends, and work colleagues alike. It's fast-paced, innovative and polished puzzles make for a fun time where communication is key and failure is no set-back as checkpoints are plenty and well-placed.The narrative design is spot-on and blends well with the gameplay and game objectives, and while the game does not penalize the player for any mistakes made during the campaign, the challenges in Operation Tango do make up for that and could provide a challenge for the more ambitious players, especially when aiming for the gold medals.I'd definitely recommend Operation Tango for both players who seek a more relaxed experience and for players who are aiming for a more challenging experience. It's a unique game best enjoyed with a friend! ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: As a hacker you piece together the information.As an agent you gather the information.You wont make it on your own. Clear or chaotic communication is the key. It was a blast. After you complete the story you shall unlock the chalange mode, which I have not played yet.A lot of love went into this game and if you want something to distract yourself along with a friend. This is a great pick. Plus only one of you has to buy the game the other one can just download the friend pass from steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

Plus you can play it either as agent or as hacker  so there is a certain replay value.For me this game gets 9 out of 10 points and I seriously hope there will be a DLC or "Operation Tango 2"!!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

More variation would be welcome, or depth on puzzles to make them more challenging after the first time through, or general length.Also worth noting is the friend pass model, which I respect.  Only one person has to own the game, the other can grab the demo and play for free the whole way.Not worth the 15 they're asking for.  I've played much better for such a price and if you haven't played Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes yet, that game is more worthy of your library and certainly a similar tone.  On a sale though, worth a look.  If more is added post release, that might be worth a revisit.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat collection of random mini games wrapped in cool spy aesthetics.Took us four hours to play through the six main missions once, looking forward to replay with the roles swapped, and there's also ten shorter (time) challenge levels. The puzzles and mini games are usually intuitive if you communicate well, there was only one that we couldn't figure out. There's also a hint option, never tried that though. (Completely forgot it existed, oops.) Quite a few puzzles require speed/timing though nothing suuuuper fast. Check points are also very generous, basically saving after every puzzle. Big thank you for that, devs!For the most part the mini games are literally just random puzzles and have no connection to the tech they represent irl. Although one thing that made me chuckle is  , The story didn't seem to be a large focus of the game, but it did do a great job of setting the vibe of the futuristic world it's set in. As are little details scattered about, like being able to read random emails and the beautiful art.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game for 2 people. I think this game has the potential to be bigger and a bit deeper in the missions while keeping the mood, the friendly art style, and the atmosphere.It's a very good game to play with someone who is not very used to playing video games, but it is necessary to play from different computers or devices, so, not very good to play with the family.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm doing my due diligence to tell both the devs and gamers that this was a REALLY good time--I only wish there were more of it.This is possibly one of my favorite co-op games of this genre. While the solutions to the puzzles aren't terribly difficult in themselves, the bulk of the challenge and fun comes from your attempts to relay valuable information and convey nonsense symbols, sometimes in a timely manner. There's something so incredibly gratifying when you and your partner are trying to figure out exactly how to get something done, and then something clicks in your head--"wait, that thing you said? I actually need that. Oh, you need help getting into that room? I can help you with that."There were moments that felt like we were going through the escape rooms of the "We Were Here" series and others that had the same intensity as "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes". If you loved those games or just plain co op games, I think you'll find something to love in Operation: Tango.At the time of writing, my friend and I have put in 3.8 hours, having completed 1 run-through, and we plan on replaying the campaign again with the roles reversed. $20 bucks for 3.5 to 4 hours might sound a bit steep, but the devs were kind enough to offer a Friend Pass so you really only need one copy between 2 players.That being said, the devs have said they'd make more missions depending on the demand of the community. So I'll end this review by saying that this was a solid time and PLEASE MAKE MORE MISSIONS AND DLC!!![EDIT]: THEY ADDED FREE DLC!!!!!!!!!!!!10/10 experience. The agent x hacker fanfics practically write themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its similarities to others in the co-op genre, Operation: Tango is an incredibly unique spy game that gets so much right about its story, gameplay, and visual/audio prowess. With it being so short, it feels akin to a small basket of incredibly good, well-seasoned fries. You won’t be chewing away at it for long, but that time you do will feel oh so amazing. It definitely has its rough edges here and there (including a few game-breaking glitches), but other areas make up for it to some extent. If you and a friend are looking for an incredibly good experience akin to Hazelight’s titans of the genre, Operation: Tango has plenty of co-op excitement, hilarity, and nostalgia to go around.If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Clever Plays for providing a review copy.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game for 4.5hrs of playtime (100% - pre-challenge update, see note below), I wish there were additional levels or more dynamic changes of challenges within a level to support more replay-ability. Once I did the storyline as one role my friend and I re-did the campaign in opposite roles, but the challenges are the same or have very minor changes that made it easy for us to breeze through a second run. Definitely some unique puzzles and interesting ways the hacker/infiltrator are linked together which I hope future updates or other games expand upon.EDIT: New content added that took about 2 hours to complete playing both sides (Challenge/Training Mode - 10 missions in total). Both players see different things and need to communicate with each other to complete tasks. It's fairly similar to the We Were Here series except it feels more like mini games for each puzzles rather than each player having a puzzle to solve. There's some funny moments you'll have as you get each other killed. The nice thing is only one person needs to buy the game. _childDocuments_.review: Its so hard to find any co-op games like this one and I have to say as we really like the genre my mate and me had some fun playing the game, but some decisions by the devs/design choices make me not recommend this unfortunaly.First of all, the game isn't made for people who like a decent challenge or want to scratch their heads for a bit before they find a solution. If you don't know how to proceed you'll be asked to use a hint pretty much straight away. You can obviously choose not to use it, but it sets the direction for all puzzles. The only slight challenge in any puzzle was multi-tasking, so the game giving you multiple simplistic things to do and expecting you to maybe fail in one of them - and even that was very easy (and this is coming from somebody who thinks of himself as someone who isn't able to multitask very well). Many puzzles looked pretty cool and seemed like a nice idea in general, but were way too simple and accordingly rather disappointing and very short (lock-picking is a great example for this. A fun mechanic with way too easy solutions). If you fail at a task the game restarts right where you died, but any currently active "objective-timer" also gets reset. This a huge design error, because it took out any challenge of certain areas the moment we died for the first time as we gained additional time/rescources without having to start from the beginning. You can pretty much not loose/fail at all during these tasks (the overheating cooldown being reset in the shaft f.e. Its the only "challenging" aspect of this section, resetting it completely but allowing you to start where you died is beyond boring and eliminated all fun from this part).Also, the final chapter is pretty much taken 1:1 from "Keep talking and nobody explodes". Not because of the bomb defusing in general, but of the way the defusing works. "If a wire has this colour do this with that other wire, if not proceed to.. - How many batteries does the bomb have? - How many letters in the serial number?" I mean come on guys, this is so obvious and almost embarrassing.In addition, we both did not like the pricing and the way this game is sold on steam. Please hear me out: Do I think this game is worth around 8€ per player or maybe even just 5-6€ per player on sale? Yes I do, thats a more or less fair price. But here is the problem: My guess is at least 90% of all players buy this game knowing who they want to play it with. That means you talk to your buddy beforehand and ask him/her if he/she wants to play it with you. Then you might want to share the price, as you obviously get the more or less same experience and time out of it. It would be so much easier (and way more fair!) for each player to buy their own copy or a bundle of 2 copies if you want to gift it to your friend. In theory you could share the price for the game outside of steam or (like in my case) just buy it as a sort of "gift" for your mate. But my mate does not own the game, he isn't able to play this at all without me and he didn't get any achievements while he was playing with me as he played the free "Friend Pass Edition" of this game which is actually labeled a "demo". So I didn't really gift anything to him, I just spent too much money on an overpriced product and kinda let him play with me. Why on earth would you not make the pricing 10€ per copy and offer a bundle with 2 copies for lets say 16€, so 8€ each? This way both players would have the full game, you'd be encouraged to buy more than one copy because of the bundle-discount and you still wouldn't rip off solo-players or the ones that might want to play it with someone who already played the game. Because lets say my friend now tells someone else that he knows a nice co-op game and as you can experience the story from 2 different perspectives he might want to play it with another mate. But he doesn't own the game, he does not own anything. Now he has to convince this friend to spend 17€ on this title or spend that amount of money himself in order to play it again. And thats ridiculous and I'm very convinced the devs miss out on many sales because of their choice on how to sell copies and make half of their playerbase not own the game at all. Because as much as I think something between 6-9€ is more or less fair for this game, 16,99€ definitely isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolute blast with Operation: Tango, so much so that I roped multiple friends into playing it again with me, despite the fact I knew exactly what I had to do in each level. Gameplay works off of telling each other what you have available to you and figuring out which elements of information you have that your partner needs to progress. There’s a degree of randomness in the execution of puzzles (i.e. the specific combinations to finish them change), but you’ll know exactly which puzzle type is coming next each time.Nothing’s overly challenging as long as both players are conveying all the information they have to their partner. Nothing requires particularly fast reflexes, though occasionally you’ll need to be calm under pressure. There're one or two puzzles that're a little obtuse as to what is required, though there's a hint system if you get stuck.Definitely feels a little short if you enjoy the concept a lot, but I think the developers smartly knew that there’s only so much that they could do with the premise while staying within their resources, and I think significantly more content could’ve led to the game outstaying its welcome or the quality dropping (I’d argue the last mission starts to show the ideas beginning to run thin).Overall, a well crafted game that comes with the kicker of the friend pass, which is a genius and commendable offering to help the game work without making the purchase burden too onerous.Incidentally, some sections are almost direct copies of game design from Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes so if you enjoyed Operation: Tango then it might be worth looking that up to extend your fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A casual co-op puzzle game following a pair of agents on their quest to apprehend a cyber-criminal.In Operation: Tango, you and a partner take on the role of either Angel, a spy infiltrating various field locations, and Alistair, a hacker providing support through the use of various technology, respectively. You're given various missions, tasking you with snooping out locations and extracting intel without being caught. All missions are connected by a light story, which does a decent job at setting up a spy thriller setting, but is too vague and basic to be a driving force for playing.On every mission, each player is given distinct tasks, which build on one another and most of the time require teamwork to complete. Just like the missions overall, these activities are quite varied, providing an engaging experience throughout the game's runtime without much repetition. The main challenge of these tasks is found in understanding what has to be done and effectively communicating with each other, with things rarely becoming difficult to solve.Overall, Operation: Tango does a decent job at keeping both players busy throughout, which I very much appreciated. Given the very different natures of both characters' activities, the game also lends itself very well to being replayed with switched roles. Providing further replayability beyond this is a challenge mode, in which your given training missions much smaller in scope to those found in the main campaign. These challenge you with competing them in a set amount of time, making things a bit more tense and giving an opportunity for high score hunting.As for its presentation, Operation: Tango goes for rather cartoonish visuals, with flat textures, simple models and overall exaggerated features like proportions. Shading is used to great effect, with the game managing a good-looking and genuinely atmospheric look. Sound-wise, the game comes with some decent if not too memorable background music as well as similarly average sound design, both of which fit in well.In conclusion, I enjoyed my time with Operation: Tango. While it's not exceptional on any level, it provides a good co-op experience that's great fun with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable two-player puzzle game with a focus on communication and cooperation, Operation Tango puts players into the shoes of two agents working together to save the world from a supervillain.The game is rather short; in fact, you can easily complete it within an afternoon if you're good at it, though it obviously depends on how good you are at solving the puzzles.The classic spy vibe is really charming, though the character designs are an interesting choice, but certainly easy to recognize, even in a crowd.The puzzles require communication via voice chat programs such as Discord or Teamspeak. In addition, only one player needs to pay to access the full game; player two is allowed to play the game using the Friends Pass. Woo!The gameplay itself differs depending on whether one plays the hacker or the agent.The agent has to move around the level and find specific information they can then give to the hacker, who then tries to use said information to help the agent reach their goal. As such, the hacker's gameplay mostly consists of using hacking tools to open doors and disable/warn the agent about surveillance cameras/drones, as well as providing information to allow the agent to proceed, whereas the agent's gameplay tends to contain a bit more navigating the level and solving more physical puzzles, which, of course, require information given by the hacker to solve.However, the game does its best to shake things up and make sure that no particular type of puzzle is used too much. In addition, it also has a decent difficulty curve, as later levels can be rather tricky if you don't already know the solution.The story is nothing too special; the protagonists are just trying to stop a bad guy who wants to cause global mayhem. You're tasked with finding said bad guy and bring him to justice. That's all I'll say without getting too much into it.The frequent changes in puzzle types do a successful job of keeping the game from getting stale and for the most part, the players have all the time in the world to figure out the solution. Sometimes, though, the game will put you on a time limit, forcing you to think fast and stay on your toes.From a technical point of view, I don't really remember experiencing any great issues with the game, which is commendable. Also, it has cross-play with other platforms, so you can send an invite code to your friend on, say, the PS4 version! As long as one of two players owns the game, nothing stops you from playing together!...aside from problems with the connection and paid online on consoles, perhaps.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good coop game, with interesting asymmetry regarding if you are playing agent (which has a lot more first person view and movement) or hacker (which has you more navigating interesting and varied computer user interfaces).  Therefore I would say there is an element of replayability.The puzzles you need to solve together are mostly a wide variety of mini games, and the goals are not always immediately apparent until you verbally communicate what you see to your partner. Then comes the playing of the mini-games:  Many are timed in some way and therefore require some reflexes or learning to communicate efficiently with your partner e.g. coming up with short hands for the things you must communicate verbally. However, in the first 3 chapters we've played so far, nothing impossibly hard after a few tries and figuring out the most efficient way to communicate.. The mini-games are challenging enough that it feels satisfying to complete, more so because of the required teamwork. The game has a groovy 60s spy movie esthetic and appropriate sound track. The technical aspects of the online co-op (including built-in voice communication) also works very smoothly and reliably.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE & WARNING: The first time I played through this, I was able to complete the game, but hit some obnoxious disconnect errors on the lock picking puzzles in later levels that necessitating switching who hosted the game and verifying the game files again. However, on my second playthrough, this workaround no longer seemed to fix it. As this may potentially render the game unplayable for some if the host-swap workaround doesn't work, I cannot in good conscience recommend it as a purchase even if I was able to complete it once. The rest of my review below still stands though.While I found O:T enjoyable, it was not what I was expecting, and I think it's important that a review makes this clear up front. This is an asymmetrical-information-based two-player puzzle game at its core, along the lines of the "We Were Here" games, or the Rusty Lake co-op puzzle games. It is strictly linear and the puzzles have strictly one resolution. With a very few exceptions, you are not exercising creativity or strategy here. You are solving puzzles with an espionage theme laid over them. The asymmetry comes in with one player playing the Agent, who handles physical infiltration and boots-on-the-ground tasks, and the other as a remotely located Hacker. The latter seems to have more to do. The Agent's role seems to mostly be just having eyes on providing the hacker with various numbers and IDs. But it's only a slight imbalance.There's no matchmaking as far as I know. If you want to play, you will have to find a partner out of game. At full price, at time of writing, that would put you and your partner out $20 each, which might be hard to justify for a game that's extremely short. You can complete the main story in under eight hours easily.There are some serious glitch problems as well. I encountered an error where initiating a collaborative lock-picking minigame would consistently crash the game. Switching who was hosting did alleviate it for some reason, FYI, but this bug has been known since last year with no apparent fix.The chief intended appeal of the game appears to be in orchestrating situations that force you and your partner to talk to each other like spy drama characters. It's definitely at its best when it has players shouting "I need an access point! Try ID 8675309!" at each other. There should be an achievement for resisting the urge to say "I'm in!" when playing the hacker, too. There's almost no story to speak of - it's not just so perfunctory you could jot it on a bar napkin, but much of what's there makes no sense. There are no real characters to speak of - only the mission-giver NPC ever even talks. But there is at least a good sense of visual flair in the design.I was expecting something more like a simulation game, where I can make strategic choices and collaborate on-the-fly with my partner. Instead it's a pretty relaxed affair, generally with no real time limits, simply teasing apart puzzles (some lifted outright from other games like Space Team, or Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes). But the puzzles are fun enough to still generally merit a recommendation from me, and there's a little replay value in switching characters for a second (invariably much shorter) playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, considering the price tag of about 10 dollars per player (assuming you, as the owner of the full game, don't wish to play it with more than 1 partner), I would say you get what you pay for in terms of content.I'm not the only review saying this game is short, only  missions, 4 hours on my record which included looking through graphics options, leaving the game idle while me or my friend took a quick break, messing up the puzzles over and over again.Also without giving out too much info, just as a warning of a buggy interaction in the game... Roomba's don't like walls, or going up ramps especially, apparentlyHowever, it's pretty good.  Left me hoping for more, either through update or DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth every penny of its £15.49 asking price. Especially when your friend can join you for free. I spent 3 hours testing my friendship with a good friend of mine and we made it out the other side relatively unscathed! The puzzles are fun and interesting, the storyline was relatively fun. There were moments of hysterical laughter, shouting at each other and utter confusion as to what we were meant to be doing. It took us 4 hours to stagger through this game with our incompetence and they were 4 hours well spent.Pros:Good puzzles (Except the tile path they can go jump off a cliff)Interesting but basic storylineReplayability as you go back to change perspectiveGood length (not too long or not too short as frustration mounts)ConsWill destroy some friendshipsControls aren't as tight as I would preferMore content for when you've completed the two perspectivesAll in all this was a really fun game and I would recommend it highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, although the game is quite short currently for the price, although the ending suggests more content coming later on. Completed the game completely as Hacker, planning on playing a second time as Agent later. Had 2 major bugs which were fixed via a restart of the mission, both on the last mission; Agent spawned outside of the map and the latter part of the mission did not allow me to interact with nodes as the Hacker.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It takes two to save the world in this Asymmetrical Spy Thriller. Pair up with a friend as a special agent or elite hacker, and work together to bring a high-tech global menace to its knees.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

name: Floodland
detailed_description: THE TEAM BEHIND Vile Monarch was founded in 2015 by Kacper Kwiatkowski and Grzegorz Mazur, both of whom worked on ‘This War of Mine’ – before starting a studio that created titles such Weedcraft Inc, Oh...Sir! and Growing Up, securing a number of awards. - Kacper Kwiatkowski and Grzegorz Mazur, founded Vile Monarch and worked on Floodland after being the co-creators of This War of Mine at 11 Bit Studios. - The art director, Konrad Czernik, had a lead position on Dying Light - Kuba Pałyska, our head of design was among the key staff of Hard West - Piotr Musiał, composed the soundtrack for Floodland, he is notoriously famous for his work on This War of Mine, Frostpunk and dozens of other games! - Other musical credits include Neil Haverty and Misha Bower of Bruce Peninsula! - Those are only some big shots that worked on Floodland but we also counted on the help of dozens of passionate gamedevs at Vile Monarch! The studio is now 80 persons strong, working on 3 different titles and continues to expand, with teams working in both Warsaw and Wrocław. About the Game Update 1.2 – NEW TIDE Floodland has been relaunched with a complete code overhaul fixing all major reported bugs, PLUS some awesome new content, leaving you with a new world ready to build! As well as core fixes, we’ve also introduced three new starting islands, bringing the total to four. These will randomly spawn when you start the game, making each experience different. As you progress through the resource tree you’ll also find a new building - the Mushroom Picker Hut is the perfect way to continue develop you food supply. There’s more! Law system updates, 10 new events, a new achievement on steam and 8 new clans all come to this game overhaul. Dive in and start building your post apocalyptic worlds! Unite Humanity - Shape Society The climate change was a catalyst for a succession of events that led to the destruction of our world; rising sea levels have inundated the coasts. Only you can help humanity survive by leading your band of survivors on a path to redemption. Starting with a lost bunch of survivors, you need to scavenge resources, rediscover technology and maintain the peace between differing factions as you strive to rebuild society. Explore and Exploit The world - as you know it - has gone, replaced by islands, swamps and isolated groups of survivors. Gathering scarce resources, you need to explore the world - island by island - helping those you can and dealing with those who do not share your vision of the future. Grow Your Colony There's more to a city than just people. Food, shelter, water, health, security - the list is long and varied. Technology to be researched along a branching Tech-Tree, buildings upgraded and specialists to train. It's down to you to make sure all these needs are fulfilled; a job made all the harder with limited resources, space and labour to complete these tasks. You Are the Law A society is only as good as its laws; it's up to you to define them. Will you usher in a new utopian age of equality or is your future a benign dictatorship? Not every group shares your vision and the choices you make can have a profound impact on the future of your settlement. A common goal will make your society more productive than one at loggerheads with itself; you need to define and choose your legal evolution and which route to follow on the Law-Tree but - as with all things - there are always consequences. Unlimited Playthroughs Each game is different; maps, events and make up of the world are randomly generated, allowing unique playthroughs every time.
