short_description: A society survival game set in a world destroyed by climate change. Explore, scavenge and build a city to unite the clans. Conflicting cultures and limited resources mean you need to make tough choices; have you got what it takes to lead your people into a new era of humanity?

_childDocuments_.review: Start to end, this game (80% achievements) took me 4 hours. My first Frostpunk run was about 7 hours, and I felt like I didn't touch the surface with that one. You can read other reviews to see why this game isn't great, but I will add a few personal points of pain:- This is NOT early access, but feels like it should be. It's not finished.- The game loop becomes incredibly boring once you have a stable second island. - The same "events" happen over and over, in a row. This means you'll get shellfish issues 15 times in a row, then water issues 8 times in a row, then fish issues a few times, and back to shellfish issues.- The game looks pretty, but on my RTX 4090 (!) and i9 13900KF after the first two hours, lags on double or triple speed becomes jarring.- You will run out of resources. There are many non re-newable resources. There is plenty on the map to finish the story, but it means you are FORCED to use the SINGLE exploration boat to find more resources.- Sustainable food is so complex (as in amount of steps) that it's not worth it to set up. I didn't need a single bread bakery mushroom thing. You can get comfortably to the end without buidling any of these.- There are bugs with resources not being delivered or buildings not being built or upgraded. The solution is always to delete the building completely.Buy when 10 EUR or less, but don't expect a masterpiece. This is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough.At first, the reviews confused me. Mixed? This game is great! It's FUN. But one review said that the game consistently crashes. And I can confirm this. Towards the end of a run, there will be consistent crashes, usually just before the next autosave. I am unable to complete the story, because the game cannot handle its own complexity anymore. Keep in mind, I have a PC that handles triple-A games at highest graphic settings without any issues at all. This is an explicit software problem.I really want to recommend the game. Sure, there are some minor game design choices I take issue with (scrap metal can only be scavenged, advancing technology is NOT compatible with renewable sources, I have NOT found an island where I can use highest stage woodcutters without it depleting the forests, micromanaging the clans becomes irrelevant at some point, you can't swipe notifications away, etc.) but overall it's a great experience. As said; I had fun with this.But the crashes at endgame mean that I HAVE to start the game over, even though I'm close to beating the game. It means that if I try another run, I need to be aware that I'm not just playing against the environment, I'm playing against the software itself to BEAT the game, never mind complete it. Because if the map gets too big, if I have too many people, if too much is going on, it WILL crash.It's a tough decision, recommend or not? It's fun and I really enjoyed it! But I've decided that the crash at endgame is too serious an issue to ignore. As such, I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I am not having the issues that others are having with the game being unplayable. My game runs just fine. There are a few occasional lags when trying to save, but no more than Civ 6 or other games do as well.However, the reason I don't recommend the game still is actually because I just did not enjoy it very much. I played for a while, and I really dislike controlling all 4 factions at the same time when their world views, etc., are constantly clashing. At the start of the game, you choose a group to control and make decisions for, so why choose between the 4 if I end up controlling all 4 eventually anyway? It's too much micromanagement, and I really dislike feeling like I am constantly behind / trying to catch up so that I can make everyone happy. I would recommend adding features such as:1) Population increases - such as access to clean water and stable food sources increasing population steadily over time2) Option to play as one faction and one faction only (random members of other factions do not just randomly join)3) There is a lot of multiplayer potential here, but perhaps I am a hopeful Civ player. TLDR: Game works, but just isn't very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: It's been over a year since my last review. I'm still alive! It takes a lot to encourage me to write a review these days; I almost didn't, but given the mixed views on this, I wanted to share my point of view. I've forgotten how to style a review nicely so you get a wall of text.If Frostpunk and This War of Mine had a baby, it would be Floodland. It's a post apocalyptic resource and colony management simulator. It's heavy on the micro management and excruciating on some of the detail, figuring out how to do it right and survive can be brutal and will take some time. Considering both Frostpunk and This War of Mine are in my top 10 favourite games, it's no wonder that I love Floodland too. There's so much to learn, so many mistakes to make - but very rewarding when you actually get that ah-ha moment of realizing you do know how to do something, until you're eventually one step ahead of the game.In my current game I'm still in crisis management mode at the moment, my colony is struggling, I've not got enough workers, I rescued an old lady who gave my settlement the plague and I've got clans of people who hate each other and I'm trying to get them to play nice before all out riots break out. There's a massive world to explore but to be honest, I'm still trying to manage my tiny little island. And it's fun for me. There's atmosphere and there's story and there's meaningful choices to agonize over.I did read quite a few of the negative reviews before playing and I think that going in to the game you do need to realize how brutal it is, how much reading of text and minute details, how much micro management and strategizing there is, and yes, how frustrating it can be too. Not everyone is going to find that fun. I've never sworn as much at a game as Frostpunk on hard mode, but that didn't mean it wasn't a good game. Perhaps it meant I wasn't a good enough gamer. But trying, and dying, is still a lot of fun. Floodlands strikes me as the same; a game that'll keep me swearing at it for quite a long time to come.I will say that there are currently some optimization problems. I know a lot of people are having crashes when I write this. The game runs pretty good for me until it gets to day 100 or so, then the saving gets longer and longer and eventually it starts crashing after a save game and I need to restart. If I run autosave (which you kinda want to do in a game like this) I tend to need to restart it once an hour just to keep it happy, but hopefully this gets fixed in future patches. Obviously I understand the frustration of people who've paid for a game they can't play, but I do feel it's a bit unfair to write negative reviews within the first few weeks of release purely about optimization, without seeing if there are prompt fixes.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys Frostpunk, They are Billions, Rimworld etc, I was pretty hyped for this game, even after playing the demo. Unfortunately, it doesn't really lend itself to new players. The resources are finite, a la frostpunk, but it's easy to hit the resource wall in early game and be unable to progress. Restarted twice due to this. This would probably be less of an issue once you knew exactly how you wanted to progress in early game (Plastic into wood into rubble, wait I'm out of research points already, no more artifacts to be found on my island but no way to get points to research boats to go find more...)  But new players don't know the system well enough to plan for this, and it's frustrating to brute force your way into this knowledge through restarts. While misuse of resources will kill your settlement in Frostpunk or Rimworld, it's sort of a slow painful slide into death which gives you time to learn more than one thing before your next restart, so when you do actually restart it's exciting because 'I'm gonna do things WAYYY different this time....', and then you make significant progress each time.It's a shame, because the game has some really cool ideas, a great aesthetic, and could have been an excellent addition to my post-apocalypse-settlement-management games collection. But I just can't spend restart after restart pushing through stops which feel like frustrating softlocks to get to the enjoyment - which I'm sure is there! Just beyond my reach.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game abandoned with bugs and poor optimization never fixed.  Sadly, it could have been a good game.  Worth at best, $5.This game is barely beta quality. There are many game breaking bugs that have not been addressed in months. Limited gameplay, lack of direction, and an extensive lack of polish make this game pointless. Every game is literally just the same exact islands, but with their locations changed. Save your money, don't buy it.Some of the game breaking bugs I have run into:1) Saves getting stuck and failing to load. Doesn't happen all the time, but when it does, it sucks. I can get a lot done in a short amount of time, so I lose a lot of progress. Yes there is autosave, but if you don't mind your game locking up for a little bit every time it does it, maybe this will lessen the blow. I don't like having to redo crap, no matter how much.2) Quest line getting stuck because of over zealous requirement to bring electricity to every single person. I've electrified every building. Every, single, building. Which you have to do manually. Just why? Even double checking by deconstructing all habitats and replacing with new does absolutely nothing.3) Vanishing barges with people on them... I mean seriously?4) Banish that clan? Buggy as all hell. Sometimes they don't all leave, then you lose the option to banish them. Sometimes they leave, only to come back. Again, no option to banish them returns.5) Pathing and basic logic. Workers live too far away!! Even when there are four habitable buildings sitting empty right next to their workplace. Hampered even further by an overly limited range.6) Your pathfinder party even with no additional people and plenty of supplies, will just starve to death. Rare, but have had it happen twice in my last two playthroughs.7) Some buildings when you deconstruct them will get stuck at 100%, but not vanish. You have to reload the game for it to complete. There is no option to cancel the deconstruction or take any other method to remedy.8) Some buildings will not upgrade, they just sit at 0%, maybe reloading the game will get them to go, but faster to just destroy and rebuild. You can also just cancel the destruction and leave it.Limited Gameplay and Lack of Polish:1) The UI bogs down late game, many options are redundant. Tech screen and Build screen category order are inverted.2) Tech tree is an absolute mess.  Lacking extensively.3) Not all places can be connected. Even though you can climb and dive everywhere, your people can't do a lot of basic things. Like having rope bridges, for places where you can not build pathways or stilted platforms.4) Some buildings can be deconstructed, but some can not, for no reason at all.5) Can not remove renewable resources like Trees, etc.6) Fences can not be restored or deconstructed, but some you can build over?7) Housing is, an afterthought. The whole system was not well made.8) Pathways blending in with the ground making it hard to see where you have placed them. Then deconstructing them isn't always a sure thing.9) Vastly limited ranges on things that should not have limited ranges.10) Places that should have limited ranges, having no range indicator.11) Going from Medium to Large storage giving you barely any additional space.12) Reclaimed buildings having barely more capacity than your generic options, yet taking up a lot more ground space.13) Same islands, just in a different spot.  If you've played it once, that's it.  14) Notifications just fly off the screen.15) Game drags you away from what you are doing for certain quest/scenario events.I could probably go on and on, more than I already have. Why am I so upset with this game? Because I feel that it likely went on sale as a last ditch cash grab for a game that probably isn't getting fixed.  The last word from the devs was nearly 5 months ago.UPDATE 5/11/2023:  The long awaited update with all the fixes dropped yesterday!!  Updated the game. loaded it up and.... none of the previous saves will load.  Fine, expected this might happen.  Deleted all previous saves and started a new game.  Played around for a very short bit, saved the game and logged out.  Went to play the game today and it won't load the save.  Same as before.  Gets to about 95% and just hangs.  Again, same as before.  This team says you can send a save into their discord and maybe they can fix it for you, but with as often as this happens, this is ridiculous.  And with how they approach updates and "hotfixes", I am guessing it will be another 6 months before they throw out an attempt.  It's kind of funny though, because when I saw the release notes the part about the saves really stuck out.   Saving your progress and hoping to continue should not be a gamble.  Yet here we are.Update 4/27/24:  Havent't played this game in a long while, waiting on bug fixes that were promised and never delivered.  Game had potential, but it is clearly abandoned.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, I have playtested this game for two months as of writing and was able to witness how much work they put into polishing the really well working basic concept of the game.One of the easiest comparison as a game style is definitely Frostpunk, to give you a rough idea of what to expect. If you are not familiar with it: You manage a small settlement of people and grow it into a civilization. You will meet other clan members with different visions then your own, you have to do a lot of decisions which will upset everyone, and you can constantly optimize supply chains.I really love the artwork in the game, it continuously makes me excited to play more. The music is top notch and it has a great replay value for me.I can wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is beautiful and fun. Other reviews have it as very similar to Frostpunk, and I agree (which is great in my opinion.) However, I can't really recommend the game because of how often it crashes and loses all progress, without any noticeable reason as to why. It is incredibly frustrating, especially in a game where it can be very detailed with what you're doing from moment to moment. Even after the promised big update and for a couple of hotfixes and it's just as bad as it was. The specific issues regarding pathfinding camps and shacks not upgrading etc. do appear to be fixed, but each of these were either very annoying or completely halted all progress as they came up, and now that they shouldn't be an issue, there's still the crashing. So frustrating. I should be rage quitting a game like this because of the challenges, not because I just lost another 30 minutes of progress. (And regularly saving doesn't help, because oftentimes that's what triggers the crash). So disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Summarized in 3 pointsGame is very poorly optimized. I would recommend 24GB RAM for a smooth experience. Till mid game it consumes more than 10GB RAM alone. Yes, we don't see that many games which are bottle necked by RAM.Play style mimics  by almost 99%. Go for Frostpunk for a smoother gameplay.The concept, design and music of the game is really nice. The game looks beautifully colorful. The gameplay is addictive. You wouldn't want to leave it if you enjoy city builders or survival or management. I continued playing it at 10-15 FPS towards the endgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve been playing for some time and grown a nice large settlement. Now, whenever I´m trying to save, the game crashes to desktop without saving. So, since I cannot save anymore, the game has become completely useless. This is a game-breaking and very severe bug. I am surprised that the issues with the game crashing upon saving have apparently not been fixed although the game is on the market for quite some time now. Very disappointing!
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Was on the fence about picking this up because of the mixed reviews. In the end I got it on sale and ended up getting so into I I played it until 2am.It definitely has Frostpunk vibes in its mechanics, art style, setting, even a few of the music queues. Ultimately it feels a lot more optimistic, and its even possible to have quite a successful run where you can balance everyone's concerns and not make anyone too miserable. My jam is narrative based survival city builders this really scratched that itch for me.As for performance issues - right at the end of the campaign when I had grew my settlement and explored most of the map it started to get a little choppy, but that was easy to ignore and was only the last couple of hours or so for me.It ran on my PC - I7 1070k, RTX 3070 with 16GB RAM and 970 EVO SSD just fine.Not a single crash in my 20 hours play time either!Hopefully this encourages someone to take a punt on this - I guess there is always the refund window if it doesn't work on your device.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was really excited for this game, placing it even on my "must-buy"-wishlist for christmas. Even bigger the letdown.Now don't get me wrong, the game is great - I love the art, the world, even the mechanics (though sometimes you might wonder "Now how exactly am I supposed to do that?" - the game tells you a few minutes later xD)I'm not much of a civilization-guy, I don't normally play games like these as they quickly get boring, but this one interested me enough for me to buy it.But the bugs are terrible. Yesterday I started my first game, had auto-saving on - the first time it tried to save something shut down and the game crashed. Don't know what, it just told me that it stopped working and thus - GAME OVER. Tried again, I wasn't that far in the game yet, nothing I couldn't do again in a few minutes. Everything was fine, I had auto-saving turned off and saved manually instead. I got even as far as too send out my first search-party for the scouts.Then a few hours later I went to play again - and forgot to save as I was trying to get that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ epidemic to end. A few in-game days after it ended a pop-up-box pops up for just a moment - I could only read "unity" so big chance something stopped working. Next second game doesn't react again, I have to turn it off - losing all my made progress.I was frustrated for the day and didn't want to play again but today I thought: "If I just remember saving, it should be fine." No, it wasn't. 5 Minutes in and after going back from the Knowledge Tree Window to my settlement, everything flickers black and blue. Fortunately I don't suffer from epilepsy otherwise I would've died literally and not just emotionally.I won't be playing this game again until it's fixed. Also; I'm gonna go and play Frostpunk now. Let's see if that game works.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a lot of potential! Unfortunately, after having to start over multiple times due to game-breaking bugs, abysmal lag, and pushing through long freeze times. I have come to the final quest line to start the power plant. I have stocked up somehow over the total limit of Steel by 1,200 units. in order to start the power plant you need to clear it out of loot. Since I wasn't able to take in any more steel (even though I was over the very small limit of 270 units by 1,200 units, with each stockpile only holding 15 steel each) I was in effect, locked out of completing the game due to something that has never happened to me in a video-game ever... I had too many resources.With no way to effectively get rid of that much Steel. i was ♥♥♥♥♥♥. building Storage was useless at 15 max storage and limited rubble and space. Building Dynamite only helps until you reach that limit as well. the highest-cost steel building cost 20 steel and had no space for that many buildings!I find it hard to believe this could make it past any reasonable play testing.Please allow a feature to possibly get rid of some of your resources or something, and fix the lag times and save times and this would be a solid game.But for now, it is a clunky survival city sim where I feel like I'm just trying to make the game survive until I can reach an end I was too good of a hoarder to reach.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: So I have a love/hate relationship with this game. You might see me put more hours into the game after I post this review because it scratches an itch I have for these types of games. It certainly brings a lot to the table as far as top down resource/strategy games go. I will start with the positives first..Pros:This game is gorgeous and has a beautiful art style and soundtrack. The music really sucks you into the game and time seems to fly by very fast whilst you are playing. The upgrading/research trees and UI are interesting and very well done. They can seem a bit overwhelming and difficult to understand at first but once you do, they work great. The buildings and mechanics involved around gathering resources and improving the lifestyle of your citizens are cool and interesting. Cons:The optimization and performance of this game is absolutely terrible. Even with the render distance turned down I still manage between 40 and 70 fps 6 hours into the game and I have a 4070 ti. This is after having several settlements on 3 separate islands. As far as progression through the game at this point I feel like I was only about halfway. There would be too much to manage and with the performance issues that I would get frustrated and start over. Also having multiple factions on the same settlement is extremely frustrating as no matter what you seem to do, they never get along and will progressively become more hostile with each other. As far as the laws you establish to try and help each of your factions (Some of them require you to establish certain laws) almost none of them will all agree on the same law and therefore causing more internal conflict than beneficial. I get that the devs made it this way as to seem more realistic, but it detracts from the fun by adding another layer to manage (A frustrating layer at that). Lastly, this game does crash from time to time and it can be annoying resetting some of your progress. It has blue screened my computer once. The devs have been inactive for some time so one could consider this game abandoned. If for some miracle they release a huge patch that fixes most of the performance problems and re-balances the game I will update my review.Conclusion:This game has immense potential and does have some fun mechanics, however I cannot recommend it due to the performance issues that makes everything pointless once you see the flaws. It is worth buying and trying out, but only on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not fit for purpose. It lets you play ok for a few hours and as soon as your map gets a bit bigger it crashes constantly. I had hoped that the recent patch had fixed it, so despite all the reviews warning about it, I gave it a chance. I wish I hadn't. It crashes while you play, it crashes when you save, it seems totally random. Steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wasted occasion.The game is really nice, it's easy to pick up, charming, fast-paced, original, very enjoyable.Why can't I recommend it? Because the support is abysmal.It is incredibly unstable. I've been playing it for some days and never managed to go more than an hour, often less than half, without crashing. From a quick look to the reviews and discussions, it's a problem that has plagued the game since release, and the developers never managed to get it under control. This should already be unacceptable, but I decided to give the game the benefit of the doubt, since it's quick to crash but it's also very quick to launch again.However, after not even 10h of gameplay I've run into a game-breaking issue: the game crashes SYSTEMATICALLY on save. Auto save, quick save, manual save, it's impossible to save your game. For a game that can't exactly be finished in a single go - not just because of length, but mostly because of the continuous crashes, not being able to save means that the game is completely unplayable. It seems that the bug was introduced with the last hotfix in the middle of June, the devs asked for save games to help them investigate it immediately after, and since then there has been no news.Three months with no fix and not even news on a game-breaking bug are not acceptable in any form or shape and clearly denote scarce professionality and commitment from the development team.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the art style and the gameplay is alright but the game is majorly stunted by some aspects. First off, the game runs terribly. Despite the seemingly simple graphics and inability to zoom in far enough to make out any details on the population, my Nvidia 2070s was struggling to hit 50fps with my little colony. I also got some weird vibes from the political element of the game. I thought it was a joke but legalizing gay marriage is actually an option at the end of a tech tree, it gives a slight mood boost to liberal citizens for 3 days. I'm not sure if it's intentional but this implies that all 4 clans in the game outlaw gay marriage until near the end of the game. That's a really odd choice for a post-apocalyptic game and it just shouldn't be there in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a maybe for me right now.I've got a sour taste in my mouth, and stopped playing because I'm having difficulty with worker placement, and housing.  Have expanded to a second base, explored past the water line and rescued a stranded group (scientists), and they've come to join with me (the firefighters), they keep all their beliefs from before SO I assigned them science jobs, built some new shelters, and watched for two days as people complained. I hope it'll get better, because I really don't understand why the game wouldn't auto assign shelter to the closest workplace (like Frostpunk). The biggest difference is in Frostpunk you're dealing with hundreds of people, with Floodlands you only have 20-40 people early on, so every person matters. _childDocuments_.review: It's good. It's like.... really good. Although this comes with some MAJOR asterisks, I think this studio might be going places, so I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt. In fact I have a very personal reservation here, and yet I still believe this is fundamentally quite a good game.The core game is fairly pleasant. Some cool ideas around the core management experience. It has a pretty Disco-Elysium reminiscent art style, and a jaunty RimWorld-reminiscent music (some lyrics in the music too, which was actually nice and atmospheric).But what I almost gave the game a red rating for is the law tree. Some socio-political concepts were arbitrarily grouped into what which side might support. E.g. the more "leftist" (in all but name) clans are against any kind of policing. It rings of somebody having learned about some of these concepts from American TV shows and YouTube comments.And now the more personal gripe: as a gay man living in the developer's country - Poland, I am particularly dismayed by the inclusion of Same-sex marriage in that tree, at the end of one of the "liberal" paths. First of all, in my opinion, it has no business being there. It's a post-future-disaster setting, the depicted struggles should relate to community organisation, they don't need to litigate just a single minority issue (e.g. neither race nor gender got the same treatment). Then again in our country, lots of people believe gay marriage would cause floods, so even having the option in is some kind of progress, maybe an overcorrection by a studio with worldwide ambitions.So the fact I'm giving this a thumbs up, despite that huge, very personal reservation, speaks volumes. That I even found out this is a Polish studio, also responsible for some other titles I enjoyed, because I was waiting for information about a game breaking bug, eager to continue playing, rather than uninstalling it and moving to the rest of my games backlog is just another tangible proof of how much I'm enjoying the game.Twitter says a patch will drop soon. Hope it's the fix I'm waiting for!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has not updated since this review came out, so don't expect anything mentioned in this review to be fixed.If you're really into building and management, I would avoid this game. It'll probably only cause head aches, but it's generally fine otherwise for other players who don't play for these aspects if you can ignore the lack of player-friendly tools and severe late-game performance issues. If you try to play it long-term like City Skylines or other in-depth building and management games, you will run out of things to do quickly. The game is shallow, but that's not a bad thing. It's just important to know what the game is before you get into it.Game has potential, but it's got some pretty annoying flaws in my opinion. Before the flaws, the positives. I like the setting. The level design and the islands are exactly what I wanted from a game about recovering from the collapse of the world. Aside from the below issues, the core mechanics of the game in general play fine. I have no complaints about the ideas the game works on. I love the scavenging aspect. Sending a team out to explore the ruins of an office complex feels really cool, and there's no shortage of loot they give you. I really like the laws tree and the fact that it gives you different ways to approach the game. I can't speak much on the story because I spent all of my time building and finishing the tech and law trees instead of progressing. The game is basically fully playable without progressing through the story. There aren't many hard roadblocks I've seen except for electricity, which really isn't needed. The art style is beautiful as well, and I really like the Disco Elysium-esque portraits.The factions can seem a bit copy-paste. The only unique thing about each faction is the story bits (the little paragraph about their backstory, their leader, and their icon), which don't affect the gameplay. So if you get two factions with the same oversimplified "political compass" leaning (ie. new world and liberty), they are functionally identical and have no unique interactions or decisions in my experience. There are different levels of leanings and extremes, but they only really affect how impactful an event is on their reputation with your main faction. It doesn't give them any different answers or change anything else from my experience. The system gives "political compass" vibes, but the depth of each faction's beliefs are just as 2-dimensional. There are a wide range of factions to find (more than you can select when you start a game), but this variation is kind of made irrelevant because any faction of the same leaning is functionally the same. The game even acknowledges this through random events where a smaller faction of the same leaning will get absorbed into a larger one, and there's nothing you can do about that. You can get some factions making some really silly choices, or having some really silly dislikes. For example, the Commune's leader went to the gym a lot prior to the end of the world and it's still a big part of her aesthetic, but the faction dislikes when you give them gyms. Because factions have to side with choices you make, the factions kind of feel like immature children with some of the decisions they are upset by because the choices you are posed with feel so minute sometimes. Ultimately though, I don't think it's too big of an issue, I would've liked to see more unique factions though.Firstly, the performance tanks hard once you get to filling the first island. It nearly crashes every time it autosaves when you get further into your run. During the day or when I'm deconstructing or building a lot, it becomes a slideshow. I don't think the game was meant for playing long-term on a save. I would recommend entirely avoiding building out with the floating platforms in any substantial amount.Second, there's a ton of bugs. Sometimes structures you place or find can't be deconstructed for some reason, or plans for a building stay despite construction being canceled, blocking you from building somewhere. Sometimes you cannot click on structures, particularly the floating platforms, and instead will click on another building somewhere off your cursor.The game moves resources by assigning workers to a storage building, and those workers go out and collect resources in range. The issue is, you can only assign a current priority. You can't designate anything beyond that, like prioritizing certain buildings. You can't blacklist anything from the queue making it virtually impossible to manage because the storage building's range will almost always cover an entire island, especially at higher upgrades. The daily +/- numbers next to each resource aren't to be trusted. They don't account for issues or bottlenecks with the above so it can be very misleading and it may tank your settlement if you don't catch it. There is no indication of how many resources you are consuming daily, only your net positive. There have been several times where I have been producing excess food or water, only to find that I can't build a supply and suddenly I have a crisis and fifty people die.There are too many resources and they will overflow from the top bar once you discover most of them. You have no control over which resources stay on the screen and which you push to the overflow menu, meaning you can accidentally ♥♥♥♥ yourself over if you didn't catch you're bleeding a resource.There's no mass-cancel or mass-deconstruction for anything besides paths, which makes it very annoying to rebuild, especially if you're using the floating platforms. Each item you order to deconstruct creates a particle effect on each that obliterates your game, at least on fast speed. There's not even a keybind for deconstructing or canceling. The floating platforms are a cool concept, but their execution leaves more to be desired. They hardly ever match the terrain they are placed next to, and you can't change their elevation. This means that sometimes you will build a section of floating platforms only to find some of them raised higher than others, blocking you from building anything in that area. The paths are very hard to see as well, as they often clip through the terrain they are placed on.You can't turn off certain notifications like in Stellaris for example. You will get pinged A LOT. If an issue isn't solved, you'll get a ping for it the next day. And you get a ping PER STRUCTURE. This issue is a detriment to the game's performance, I feel.Not the biggest issue, but when there's one tree stubbornly preventing you from using that space, it gets a bit frustrating. Or if you're not using a resource, you have to forfeit the space. For example, in my run I only used farms, mills, and bakeries as my food source, so mushrooms and fish were useless for me and only really took up space.

_childDocuments_.review: I've done two playthroughs and have really enjoyed it on the whole. Great visuals, music, and story. I think the law system and the clan politics are really cool -- something new in survival city building. Now, some gripes: while lot of the bugginess mentioned in other reviews has been addressed in hotfixes over the last couple of weeks, there are two game-breaking bugs still happening to me: 1) I had an expedition party member starve and the expedition never returned to base -- so I lost the ability to do expeditions for the rest of the game; and 2) I sent some survivors from one district to another and the ferry just stopped on the way and never arrived. At the end of the game's main story, you have to provide electricity for all of your people. I got power to 180 of them with no problem, but the 20 people who were lost at sea counted against me, so I couldn't finish the quest, or the story.  Very frustrating.But check this game out, maybe after an update or two -- it has a very cool post-apocalyptic setting, interesting mechanics, and challenging survival gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun post-apocalyptic builder w/ classic resource management meeting the needs of different societies (clans).Lot's of research and civil options.  Could use a little more clues as to how to make respective clans increase happiness, and sometimes the result of a policy has the opposite effect that you think it should... but... ok.Need the ability to toggle recreation buildings - the gym and the art studio consume WAAAY too many resources... and the only option is to destroy the buildings.  I had two full time, fully manned, fully upgraded recycling centers producing paint and the art studio (a single one!) was constantly out of paint.  That needs to be fixed.  Definitely some frame rate issues as more of the map is revealed (being fixed).  And that auto-save... seems to take an increasingly long time to save which can disrupt game enjoyment and makes me wonder if a crash is incoming (it never crashed on me once).Could use better re-homing of citizens to optimize production, but later in the game there is a fully auto-mode for district management (I didn't like that mode, but it suggests the devs *could* auto-re-home ppl to better locations).Kind of grinds near end of the game (could use even more research unlocks at this point - like unlocking more scouting parties or increase their load capacity etc.).  I also think that for a game focused on the "event", there are a startling lack of events.  Come on guys, you teased us with the contaminated oil drums... we need more!.  Calamities.  Satellite debris falling on us.  Contaminated cruise ships being washed up.  Cemeteries releasing their bloated cargo causing plague.  Droughts or insect-collapse or soy bean fungus.  There are SO many stressors that could be added to the game to increase variety and re-playability.  I love the look and feel of the graphics and there are some surprise audio tracks that are quite delightful. Given the sheer number of negative comments, I was hesitate to play... but it is definitely worth the cost of admission and is a nice addition to my post-apo builder library!Some simple fixes for optimization of consumption vs. production rates are needed - but that is trivial.  The frame rate issue is being explored but isn't game breaking.  The slow reveal of the event was nice and simple and enjoyable.  A neat mashup of raft meets flotsam meets frostpunk.  Oh - and don't make me electrify EACH house... make some hotkeys guys.  That part annoyed me.(played over the course of a week, loading my saves each night w/o ever a problem).

_childDocuments_.review: It's disheartening to see so many people giving a thumbs down and appearing to just not understand how to play the game. My entire experience with Floodland so far has been a single playthrough of the demo, which is limited to a given number of days, and a single playthrough (meaning I beat the main story) of the released version. I didn't hit any specific soft-locks or death spirals. I hit a couple of issues that you'd expect to encounter in this type of game:- A large population (50) joins the settlement, so food and water are suddenly in short supply- An expedition brings back a severe virus that takes days to recover from - A specific food source runs out, so you have to adjust and build something more sustainable and varied- Having to research new tech to keep progressing (How is this an issue? What else would you expect?)I think the game is fantastic and it's disheartening to see people not "getting it" because I'm sure they'll convince the devs to change the formula, which will likely ruin it and just make it a clone of whatever other games people are comparing this to. Oh well. I got to have some fun before that at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the only time I'd recommend this game is if you played Frostpunk and really, REALLY needed to play a game that went in the exact opposite direction in terms of tone and mechanics. I was pretty impressed to see that in a world face ecological catastrophe (but only an aesthetic one,) every faction you can play approaches the situation with hope and a spirit of community. That optimism is charming, but it isn't enough to save the game from its flaws.There are people for whom micromanaging the clans across multiple settlements, waiting on scouting parties (which can only leave from one island) to arrive where you send them so that you can manually direct them to anything worth scavenging, and then balancing way too many resources while being unable to lock down where they're all disappearing to is exciting. I am not one of those people, so I found all of those tedious. Which is a shame, because that's the core of this game.But otherwise? Just play Frostpunk. Everything this game does, it does better. The art and optimism does not make up for all the things it does badly.

_childDocuments_.review: I did quite like this game. (just played it through once so far, completing the main story)It's atmospheric, with beautiful and surprisingly colourful visuals. Haunting music, a little like country-and-western meets trance. Surprising you with songs when you hit a milestone in the story.The mechanics are smooth and reasonably intuitive, although there are a few cases (interactions of the various clans) where I ended up gritting my teeth and throwing solutions at problems. The tech trees (4 of them) make a certain amount of sense, and the occasional folk popping up to request laws, request old favourites (bread!) or just puzzle you (hey, we found this doll....) add to the sense of being a puzzled community leader. Downsides: it's slow. I spent quite a while playing it on highest speed so my one team of foragers could trek across the map, grab the stuff, trek back, get it processed through my tiny factories, and repeat. Taking a good week or so gametime, luckily about 1 min of play. I'm not sure if it's possible to play random maps. I hope so. I don't know if this game is ever getting upgrades; again, I hope so. As it is, this is a lovingly made work of art, and good fun for the first 15 hours or so. Beyond that, i suspect it gets a little repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: If overpriced Starfield can get 71% positive reviews even though it's an absolute pile of steaming bugs, despite being published by a massive rich company, then this game should be reviewed much better. It's not a huge studio. It's an indie game. I haven't found bugs here as much as huuuge FPS drops by the end of the game. AND this definitely feels like the endstate of the game - there haven't been updates in months. But I did not get a single crash and I'm having a lot of fun, hoping they'll make a more polished sequel.Maybe I'm enjoying this game so much because it's simple and lacks most of the "spend 100h learning the mechanics" aspects of most strategy games, a genre which I usually dislike. Maybe its setting is something that speaks to me, but I tried Frostpunk afterwards and I found the controls too unintuitive to enjoy it as much as this game. Maybe I just vibe with this game for some reason, but I really, really like it.If you looked at this game and went "huh it sounds interesting" but are put off by the reviews, give it a shot. You always have 2h to refund. Trust me, you'll know if you like this game within this time frame. I found myself saying "just one more hour" until it was 3am.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite similar to Surviving the Aftermath.Sadly it is way worse than that game. (And i did not have a good oppinion of Surviving the Aftermath neither!) It has a lot of "visual effects" that actually do not add anything to the game beside draining resources. In Surviving the Aftermath you had a map where you could build your stuff and a world map, where districts were present and where you could loot, build outposts and the like.Here there is no world map, instead there are districts in the "build map". You need to unlock the technology to build districts, to build PATHS (which actually do not really matter), to explore, to be able to explore more thouroughly and such. By the time you get your third island(district) up and running you will notice that the game will start to slow down. Very noticeably. I had to turn off the autosave function as it is a known cause of crashing.(I myself experienced it 5 times.) By the time i reached the end game as to say, i often had to reissue commands as the game did not register them, the game quite often "hung" as in loading, so there are terrible performance issues. The technology menu seemed interesting, until it turned out that for some reason sometimes it does not want to expand, and you need to repeatedly click on it pull down and right and hope that this time you can finally unlock farms, as it will be visible.The game also overdoes micromanageing. Just the call it specializing.The two most important non-renewable resources are rubble and screws. You will be constantly on the lookout for them, and they will be the main reason for you to settle multiple islands. (So build an academy for each clan:P)There is a "clan" system introduced, which is basicly a form of different beliefs and customs for groups, but it is just annoying, and you are better off shipping everyone to their own island, as when the clans live under the same roof they usually just end up hating each other. Due to this a legislative system is also introcuded with buildings tied to them, and mutually exclusive laws. But basicly...it is just a bad ripoff from Frostpunk.I was quite excited for this game when i saw it first, but it failed to deliver quite hard. I bought it for 6 euros as it was on sale, and it was BARELY worth that price. The game is not really interesting, the gameplay is boring and repetitive, the story is way below average, and the performance issues are just terrible. Overall a 42/100.Edit: I played the game with a PC that is over the recommended system requirements. I managed to finish the game with medium settings. So basicly if you are below the recommended settings do not even try the game, as with even low settings you might experience constant crashes not letting you get past a certain point. Which you will most likely encounter after about 4-5 hours of gameplay.Edit2: The game has stopped receiving updates, so most of the issues that are there, including the terrible performance issues will persist. Currently the game for many will be therefore unplayable. (Even on the recommended computer.) I can only suggest not to buy this AT ALL.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing. I'm giving it a thumbs up. But I gotta say, it's because they set out to do what they wanted to do.This is one of those difficult, lots of micromanaging, sometimes depressing kind of colony simulator games. A lot of decisions need to be made. A lot of micromanaging is involved. The game is unforgiving and punishing. _childDocuments_.review: I first played this game as a demo during Steam's Next Fest sometime last year. I was hooked from that little teaser of content and had every intention of buying this game as soon as it was available. I believed this game would be something special and new, and I was very excited for it. After reading reviews and watching updates, I'm glad I didn't end up buying the game until recently, but I don't regret buying the game now and can absolutely recommend it to others.Altogether, the game is... good, but not great. I wouldn't have been satisfied to buy this for $60, but I think $30 or less on sale is very reasonable for the enjoyment I got out of the game. It still has bugs, there are some strange interface and progression choices I'm surprised haven't been edited considering how long the game has been out, and there are aspects that I feel needed more polish or were just plain not good and needed some fixing, but it was overall a fun and meaningful experience. The art and music was amazing and the devs absolutely nailed the ambiance and setting, the gameplay is novel, and the story and progression has a way of drawing you in and making you feel for the people you manage.Floodland felt different than any other survival/city-builder type game I've ever played (yes, including Frostpunk). The game has layers of challenge and often makes you prioritize one problem over another; are you dangerously low on food or water, is there an epidemic, is your main island too crowded, do you need more people, are there not enough jobs, do you need more research to learn to build something to fix a crisis, do you have to placate your people so they stop stealing resources because they hate eachother, or is it finally time to advance the story? There is a story that you are working to finish, but your path through the game is not linear. You are making the decisions on what to do next, not the game. I found myself wishing there was more pressure to continue the main story, as being allowed to take all these problems at my own pace with infinite time to spare took away some of the fun of the challenge, but at the same time this lack of a time limit or overarching threat of some kind made me focus on the people and actually made me feel the purpose of my role as the leader of the settlement. Balancing your people's needs and wants is the challenge here, not the secondary objective only there to put pressure on you, and Floodland executes this challenge frustratingly well.The game is as much a political sim as it is a city-builder. Your people are not so kind as to overcome their differences for the sake of the future; these are stubborn people that devoutly stick to their political beliefs and will do everything they can to convince you to follow their ideals. When you have clans in your settlement that are on complete opposite ends of the political axis it gets downright frustrating to try and figure out what laws you should pass, and if you decide you don't want to pass any extreme laws the clan leaders will pester you about it the whole game. Some clans staunchly believe that laws that only benefit you gameplay-wise are horrible and contrary to everything they believe in, and much like real life, there are laws that are meant to improve society or foster understanding between the people that clans will still argue over. This system by itself is immensely frustrating, but it serves to enhance the severity of every other crisis and makes the game feel different than other games in the same genre.The way Floodland presents its resources and exploration also felt novel to me. All the nonrenewable resources seem so plentiful in the beginning and there's so many ruins with an assortment of useful resources, so in my first few games this lulled me into complacency and I failed to set up a reliable renewable resource system before a crisis brought everything crashing down. Renewable resources are not infinite and seem to replenish so slow that they don't seem all that important in the beginning; why spend resources on slow income when you can just expand to a new island and take those resources now? Expanding your settlement has its own risks and isn't always viable, and many times in my attempts I found myself running out of food and water and unable to expand, thus collapsing everything. It was frustrating at first to restart, but very satisfying to learn how to be better next time.Floodland required some patience and learning for me, and it wasn't always fun, which might seem strange for a video game, but I always found myself excited to come back for more and felt proud to overcome the many problems it thew at me. Now, as for the negatives... I experienced pretty minor lag and only a few bugs up until ~23 hours, shortly before I actually finished a run. I thought at first all the crashes I had heard about were just others' computers not being very good, but I did eventually start experiencing problems. I had a bug that killed one of my earlier runs where 120 or more people suddenly decided they no longer wanted to work because I gave them autonomy and I was not going to manually reassign them one by one for the rest of the game. The game started crashing during auto and manual saves (though thankfully it successfully saved manually) and I started to experience lag more commonly with a settlement of ~370 people across four islands and a large portion of the map revealed. Considering the game that gives you infinite time, it would've been nice to try and explore all of the available map and invite every available person into the settlement, but it seems like the game can't handle very large settlements.Recreation made absolutely no sense. I simply never passed recreation laws, and the game never made this into an actual problem, it just bugged me about it the whole time. You expect me to place very large and rather expensive buildings, some of which use up vital resources on a daily basis, in a place close to as many houses as possible (but you're not necessarily supposed to cluster houses up, the game tells you over and over and over again to put houses near workplaces!), many of which individual clans hate and grow angry over their existence and the passing of the laws required to build them, to improve the relationship of clans? The solution to clans hating each other is segregating them, not recreation anyhow or anyway, which is really strange considering a major part of this game is about making these people get along despite their differences.There are no hotkeys for rapidly switching between buildings of the same type. When you have many houses you want to upgrade or provide electricity for, you have to click on each individual little house and click the upgrade button or the dropdown menu and then click again for electricity mode. I've never used hotkeys much but there are cases like these where it's borderline necessary to have something to speed the process up/make it easier.The notifications are terrible. It's hard to tell sometimes if something actually important is happening in the settlement because I'm constantly getting spammed with messages of "your people live too far from the workplace!" or "X buildings have no resources to gather in range!" or "X clans hate each other even more now!" Most of the game these notifications were complete redundant.You can't tear down some old buildings that take up vital space on your small islands despite having the resources to destroy other far more complex buildings. It's one thing to say the sunken ruins of stone and concrete that don't take up land space aren't necessary to destroy, but you can neither destroy nor re-purpose some collapsed wooden buildings fully on land? You can't tell me these people can blow up old gas stations but can't tear down a little old wood.

_childDocuments_.review: While I would love to recommend this game - I can't.The concept of a strategy game set in an ecological disaster post-apo was really enticing and was - for the first hours - really interesting.The whole concept of scarcity, sociology & politics alongside a deep and profund skill tree really talked to me. However, the game quickly becomes painful with the expansion. Not only very difficult to handle but really, really painful. Aside the regular crash when the map expand ; the concept of "exploration" quickly limits you to your small island and you have to send expeditions that requires micromanagement in addition to a lot of ressources ; taking you away from what the game should become overtime : macromanagement. Gone the foreseeing of the politics & research. You are suddenly stuck in gathering enough ressources (that are taken away from your main camp) to send an expedition that will take 6 days to move forward on the story, only to learn you need to do it 5 more times to have the chance to move a step further and finally set up a camp on the other side on the tiny river. The game is itself is full of amazing ideas - but the result is sadly underwhelming. I kinda want a Floodland 2 though... with all the improvements done.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game and quite enjoyable on Easy Mode. I have not gone into that harder modes because I prefer a more casual play, but I have played a few games already, and I have some notes.It is not procedurally generated, but think of each discoverable area as a tile. There is water inbetween, and you have to go through "tech trees" to be able to proceed farther, etc.There is a "story" to the game as well, and it doesn't seem to change that much, so I kinda wish there were some more modes or variations available. Replayability is not that strong for this game, because the "tiles" or  islands are the same, so you can kinda figure out how best utilize the space. I would love to see more. You can "win" but can keep playing (like with Civ), but here there is very little reason to keep playing after getting the last bit accomplished.Bottom line, an enjoyable game, definitely worth $20 if you just play easy mode and play casually. _childDocuments_.review: I have to agree with most of the other bad reviews, unfortunately. I find the general gameplay quite enjoyable, there are some neat new details, but there's nothing groundbreaking new either. My biggest problem is the performance. I have a pretty powerful system, but I can see the framerate degradation in the game, even in the early stages. I start at a full 75 FPS (limited for my specific monitor) with a GPU load of about 75 to 80%. The more I expand the colony, the more the framerate drops, but the GPU load stays at about 80%. We're talking a solid 10 FPS loss per hour, so you won't get very far before hitting 25 FPS and below. To me, it looks like the game is very poorly optimized and it's a shame that the developers brag about what they've worked on before (like "this war of mine") and then release such obviously poor quality. Maybe there is a reason why they don't work on "this war of mine" anymore? ;)Update: Please also refer to the developers' update notes on the latest update (Nov 16, 2022), where you can read the following section:We also have a "low performance guide" for you:We'll be constantly optimizing the game in the following updates of which this is the 1st.In fairness, please don't expect miracles - if you have a low-end machine, play at lower resolution and reduce visual effects. Please check the suggested specs below.Our "Painterly" art style doesn't automatically mean it's "cheaper" performance-wise. There's plenty of detail, lighting and effects that will keep the GPU busy.The game's complexity also naturally means that the more buildings/people you have, the more power it demands, which is especially visible on fast forward (more calculations in a time frame).Interestingly, neither my CPU, GPU nor RAM are close to their limits. The game is complex? Sure, if you say so. Is that the problem? No, the problem is that developers are not able to effectively utilize the capacities of a system. There are indie games that are much more complex and offer better performance, and there are games with much more graphical detail that run much better. All I'm saying is that even if the statement sounds like you (the player) are the problem, you are not.Take care!

Just to SUMMARIZE there are just alot of little things that can doom like this if you let them add up. And that's does not even cover the 8 or so clans that disagree on culture....that right culture. Stuff like how a body is buried to who chooses the loved ones the community or the leader to just letting the water take it. Many of you may think it's stupid but this is a real problem in the world today and I personally find it fascinating the bs people argue about in the game. AND THIS is why the game is not for everybody as struggling to feed, build and expand is the most common problem to not building it all efficiently is that the people may just kill each other over bs. _childDocuments_.review: I was waiting to see whether I would feel the pull to return to this game before writing a review and honestly I do not because this game feels more like a chore than deriving any sense of fun. I do enjoy resource-management sim games and was intrigued by the different philosophies of each faction and challenging choice-based research tree in a post-apocalyptic world, but this game goes too far in the need to manage resources, rival factions, penalties, etc without providing quality of life structures that would bolster the enjoyment of these things in the game. You're often left hitting a resource wall and waiting for replenishment or scouring for things (or unable to scout for things) and then when other factions start joining the communit(ies) and hating each other, there is no easy way to disentangle multiple groups from different jobs/tasks. This game thus becomes far too tedious a way to spend my time. When I logged in last and realized that the stack building I was tasked at finding was in the far corner of the map and that it would take several more hours of basically the same boring loop to get there, I logged out. There are better games in the genre out there that care more about their players.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game overall, but there is definitely some room for improvement.1. I wish there was just a sandbox mode that didn't have a story line tied to it. Would be great to play a bit in that mode before jumping into the campaign. My reason for this is that the first time I started a campaign, I researched the wrong technologies and focused a lot of workforce on buildings that don't actually do much, like the shellfish station. 2. The randomness in the campaign is alright, but can really screw you over early on. For example - On my first run, the second clan I found was diametrically opposed to everything my first clan wanted. They pretty quickly became upset to the point where theft ruined me. I couldn't get the tech to separate them soon enough to avoid this.3. Storage for food & water seems to be a little low. It does add to difficulty, but makes it hard to adjust quick enough when you bring a 30 person clan in and need to have the wiggle room to incorporate them.4. Auto-saves are an issue in late game. Saving in general takes much longer than it should, and by the time you've expanded to several extra islands, it is taking several minutes to finish a save. I had to disable auto-save because of this.5. Performance in general should be improved. I'm running a 3080ti, 32gb ram & a i5-13600K, but have noticed drops happening. This shouldn't be the case on a game like this.6. Clan relationship mechanics are poorly explained and seem pretty nebulous. You can be absolutely ruined early game by happening to encounter a clan that isn't compatible with your first clan. The reasons why your clans lose relationship 'points' is also poorly explained. It might help to have some type of mechanic to spend resources to improve relations.All that said, I am enjoying the game. There are some unique mechanics that I like, and the game has the building blocks of something really neat. I just hope that the devs continue support for the game and expand on the base of what is here.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 3/10 DONT BUY every run is practically the same. If you grow too much the game cannot handle it. (crashing, frame loss) Finite resources tedious to gather. Segregation is basically the only way to manage clans. Electricity addition later in the game feels lazy and tacked onPlayed on Ryzen 7 3800x - 32GB ram - Asus 1080 - dropped resolution too 720p -- played on second highest difficultyThe map is technically random, but really its just the same map with the islands shuffled around. The starting island is the same every time including the resources. Story events are pretty boring. Far enough in they are just people asking for policies that dont really do anything. The game seems to be incapable of handling more than 150-200 people, I got over 300 and it was a coin toss every day cycle if the game would crash. Finite resources are not hard to get but annoying to get. Need scrap? building often cost 400-600 some even more, you can either send a scouting party to take a raft to an area, gather material (they can only hold 750) then leave. and repeat that basically non stop to meet demand. The other way is too either set up a proper expansion near scrap piles usually only 3-4 piles worth about 250 each. after that they are gone. The third and most annoying but something you'll have too do is set up an expansion, ferry over some extra workers, gather the piles (which you can only do at a base and not with the scouting party) then once the piles are gone, dismantle the base and ferry your people back. Very annoying when you need thousands of scrap and rubble to progress with metal and concrete. Managing the different clans with differing world views seems interesting, until you learn that you'll be spending all of your time trying to build a glass tower just so they dont turn to crime and screw you entire economy. The only way i found to stop them from spiraling into chaos was too just give any clan with separate views their own district where that cant interact with another clan. As for the laws and policies, they are essentially pointless. any buffs they provide to make people get along are either too late to be useful or too minor to make a difference. All the other provide boring unnoticeable changes ie eat 10% more food, 25% lower chance for sickness to turn lethal.----------- ELECTRICITY... IS.... boring... very, very boring. minor spoiler ahead -----------You fix the power plant. good job. you can pretty much only use that power on that island, likely far from your main base, and chances are your island aren't close enough to one another too build a bridge that would connect them to make them one district.... So you need to build your own power plants. rather, a coal plant or a wind turbine... that's it..... turbines are very cost inefficient. So coal power it is. you can make an infinite amount of coal so you never need to worry about fuel. but scrap... remember that, the material that's super annoying to get. your going to need a ♥♥♥♥ ton of it too make metal too then make the coal plants.... Great, you've made the metal got the coal plants, now too put those electrons to work...... but hitting a toggle on all your building and giving them a 10%ish boost to its production..... good job. that's its... all doneOverall, this game feels like it fails to achieve any wins at anything its trying too be. too basic too be a city builder. really only one strategy, only emphasized by the map being the same. Not a very engaging story. (regardless of your opinion of climate change) any choice you do make is practically predetermined by your main clan worldview.DONT BUY, 3/10 i guess. there are far better games, probably on sale right now

_childDocuments_.review: very reminiscent of frostpunk in terms of gameplay. like frostpunk, the interface here is fairly straightforward and easy to use unlike the cluttered menus of many city-builders. the designs of the buildings are quite fun, and the setting itself is great if you like post-apocalyptic kind of put-together building style. it's as if fallout 4's settlement making was it's own cute game. really nicely designed--the character designs and art direction is really refreshing. the music is quite good as well, with relaxing sounds and even a vocal track that actually rules and got stuck in my head! i haven't experienced any save file corruption issues like some reviewers. the game runs perfectly fine for me at max settings on a decently high end PC.my only complaints are that i wish the regular speed was slower or that there was option to slow down because it kind of looks very silly seeing everyone running around quickly while the sun moves at breakneck speed and the shadows cast by everything are moving so fast. epidemics are annoying as well because even though you've done everything you can, your leaders will still moan and groan that you're not doing anything. maybe i haven't played long enough to experience any other game-breaking things, but it's cute and decent so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a thumbs-up, but I give it with some big caveats which I will list below. What this game has going for it is style, aesthetic and a basic concept. You get to build a city in a watery post-apocalypse, explore the ruins and build a thriving community. You are rewarded for utilizing what you find in the most efficient manner possible, and for planning ahead well. I had a good bit of fun with the early and mid game here, and if the devs support the game properly, it may yet realize its full potential. If you like city-builders and find the setting cool and interesting, it might be worth your money and time.Now for the big pro/con lists.The Good:- Unique "trashpunk" postapocalyptic setting, complete with creatively designed factions- Technological advancement from sticks and stones back to electricity is meaningful- Exploration feels rewarding and fun- Player freedom in terms of choosing your own path, creating synergiesThe Bad:- Inexplicably a very hardware-heavy game despite the smol indie studio feel- Poor optimization causes big framerate drops, saving the game takes forever and crashes can occur (optimization issues may yet be fixed by patches and hotfixes from the devs post launch)- Performance becomes even worse as you get more people and settle more islands- UI is very rudimentary and rough. Resource inventory is displayed in a single bar across the top of the screen, not grouped into structured categories- Warning messages are displayed for too many things unnecessarily- Exploration limited to only one 3-person-team being sent out at a time even in the late game- Lack of a diplomacy system or trading with AI controlled factions. It feels strange when no other groups of survivors are doing anything in this post-apocalypse- Seemingly strange balancing with resource production generally leaves the player very short of the materials needed- Late game seemingly consists of an extended grind for research and advanced resources which is tedious, especially with being limited to only 1 explorer team to go out and find stuff

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a reviewer but I'll do my best: Coming from the tiny windward island of Wai'tu kubuli, and seeing the amount of sarrgassum washing up on our shores from climate change... Knowing that we will some day end up under water with only our mountains surviving the fall... Being the only country on Earth known for its nature more than even our Native Kalinago people... It can go without saying I've been waiting for a game like this for a while. This is a refreshing, low-key mix of Tropico and that other game with the British frozen people (I'm lazy and don't wanna look the name up idc), except the tropes aren't Amerikan takes of our leaders and are more like down-to-earth representations of actual ideologies we come by on a day to day basis, jettisoned out into the nearish future, and given the task of surviving amongst each other. It makes this interfactional connection as important as resource management and gives you an evolving puzzle that changes from game to game (I failed badly twice so I would know despite not having beat it yet lol). What makes this game unique is its potential to give you a true choice in taking these ideologies and making the pressures a leader would face in making them work for everyone's "benefit", which you also decide despite there being a somewhat linear story for the faction you start with. The backstory is literally littered around the map, so if you plan on focusing on exploration, you will be in for a spicy treat. You'll find surprises you can't guess re: factions. I did lost over 30 pops to disease at one point, but I felt more ashamed than depressed (XCOM) or pissed (that frozen British people game). You could also just build a lot of farmland and grow a bunch of crops but that doesn't really mean much without money existing, and naturally occurring resources taking time to grow like IRL, making your infinite-growth dreams impossible (also like IRL). There are contradictions being heightened and conflict at every corner to be managed or to let happen for whatever end goal you please. It almost feels like an experiment. The art is beautiful. Watercolors and pseudo-caricatures fill a believable world that reminds me a lot of Disco Elysium. The music is heavily reactive to what's happening as you play. I'll probably come back to add more as I play but definitely get this game if you're even slightly curious about one very possible future we may be facing as a planet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels utterly held together by tape and string. The balancing is beyond backwards and nothing makes sense. I am sad that at this point I have played past the point of refund, so please take heed and avoid this game at all cost. I mean where do I even start? Everyone hates each other. Like to a unbelievable degree. You have to FORCE people of different "clans" to live together. How can the same people of the same settlement be different clans? No idea, but hey ignore that and suffer.  Shove them all into the same tents and public places and pray its enough to keep them from actively murdering each other. Probably wont. Research is just stupid and based off a resource you have to find. You know how humans just couldn't invent the wheel until they found the manual? Or how throughout history the majority of innovations came when we found a cool looking doodad and suddenly learned how to fish? Or how yelling at each other in a room sparked the idea of how to cook bread? No? Cause it didnt happen. Get rid of the dumb system and just let me actually research technologies. Get ready to collect some 1000 pieces of scrap to create one tent. Or cut down two entire forests to make a single dock. The resource requirements for buildings, like so many other things, is just terribly balanced. You will be staring at unbuilt projects for days on end despite having a fifth of your manpower collecting that one resource. Worst still is most, if not all, resource nodes collected by dedicated buildings are considered "renewable". This is a lie. Your tier one crappy wood cutting station can, and will, consume every tree around it within days. It will then be running on quarter efficiency as the game tries to "renew" these resources by offering you a pittance a day. I will literally have my stations running with one singular person in it and still have all resources consumed by noon. But hey, better get that building to tier three, how else can you keep up with demand right? Just everything, and I mean  feels so badly designed! It goes beyond annoying, this game is a rage game hiding as a normal city builder! You will be slowly pinpricked by nuisance after nuisance until your very sanity is in tatters. Until the devs tear this game apart and build it from the ground up again, just avoid. Not even worth getting on sale, which I did. I feel  for having played this game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack, nice atmosphere and a pretty complex tech tree. It also has an interesting law system (which probably could be expanded/improved) and clan system. The story is interesting as well, with events occuring occasionally and you have to make decisions. It's fun and interesting to explore the flooded environment. The game is pretty chill and there's no combat (not so far at least), but I don't feel that is necessary in this game. I strongly recommend it. Feels a bit like Civilization, on a smaller/micro scale.The game could perhaps have been a bit longer, maybe with a bigger tech tree and spanning over a period in time, and it would be nice if you could remove/move cars earlier in the game, they are a bit in the way when you construct your settlement.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Frostpunk you're going to like this game too. Floodland is a climatic city-builder survival game with emphasis put into relationships between different factions in the community. This game does so many things well. Visual design is creative, soundtrack is relaxing and memorable and user interface is convenient. To progress through the game you have to complete quests, expand your settlement,  resolve disputes between factions, discover new technologies, make difficult desicions and many more. The gameplay is a pretty standard for the genre with no major innovations and it is not a bad thing. It is just a brilliant game setting idea paired with a great execution.However, the game is not flawless. If you are a type of player who permanently needs 60 FPS regardless of the game you play, you are going to have a hard time here. Once your village expands you can start feeling performance issues. My specs for the game were RTX2060 + Ryzen 5 2600 and at a later stage it was hard to keep even 20 FPS. This is not that big of a problem because it is a city builder after all but be warned. On the bright side, the game never crashed and I never encountered any game-breaking bugs. Creating paths and bridges feels very clunky though.All in all, despite performance issues, I can highly recommend this game.
